Retaining the original multiplicities, the channel sum therefore contributes $$ (\pi N)^{R/2}\prod_i(C_{i,N}-\pi i\epsilon_i)^{-1/2}(1+o(1)). $$ Here $C_{i,N}$ is evaluated at the exact finite critical radius and tends to a positive geometric value $C_i$. The factor cannot vanish. The estimate is relative throughout a window wider than $\sqrt N$, and the proof controls both its intermediate and macroscopic tails. ![The two constant-face directions and the neighboring original physical heads that give a primitive transverse slice.](../figures/face-potential-rank.png) ## How far this is from the requested knot theorem The complete signed source now has a global equality. The remaining general problem is passage to independently long fillings: | Required extension | What is available | What still needs proof | | --- | --- | --- | | Local deformed source | The whole original source has the geometric volume limit in a near-complete corridor at any set of untwisted ports; one varied signed port is covered by an explicit local curvature test | Interacting signed ports and their disconnected reflection subsets | | Whole filling transform | Exact filling transform and geometric long-filling threshold | A bound for the entire complementary color region and its aliases, retaining all small-color terms | Internal deficits $s_i=N-1-2a_i$ and external filling-color deficits $h_i=N-j_i$ are different variables. The [fixed complex core theorem](../../notes/actual_complete_core_complex_packet.md) now controls the complete-image term with $\boldsymbol\chi=\mathbf h/N$ in a fixed complex neighborhood: $$\frac{F_N(N\boldsymbol\chi)}{F_N(0)} =e^{N(S_N(\boldsymbol\chi)-S_N(0))} \sqrt{\frac{\det K_N(0)}{\det K_N(\boldsymbol\chi)}} \bigl(1+O(N^{-1})\bigr).$$ Here $S_N$ is the selected joint critical action and $K_N$ its nonsingular Hessian. The square root is fixed at $\boldsymbol\chi=0$. The theorem proves nonvanishing uniformly and $S_N\to S$ holomorphically. The [geometric deformation theorem](../../notes/actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.md) identifies this limiting action on the actual marked peripheral branch: $$2\pi\operatorname{Re}S(\boldsymbol\chi) =\operatorname{Vol}(\rho_{\boldsymbol\chi}) +\frac12\sum_i\operatorname{Re}U_i\operatorname{Im}V_i, \qquad U_i=-2\pi i\chi_i.$$ Thus for small **real** $\boldsymbol\chi$, the exact complete-core polynomial has rate $\operatorname{Vol}(\rho_{\boldsymbol\chi})$. At zero this is the complete augmented-link volume. For complex meridians the displayed boundary correction is necessary. The relative asymptotic still retains $S_N$; convergence alone does not justify substituting $S$ in its exponential. The [finite-level action transfer](../../notes/general_long_filling_varying_action_transfer.md) now proves that the filling calculation can retain $S_N$ throughout and take its limit at the end. Its remaining hypotheses are the full mixed-source estimates. The [external reflection theorem](../../notes/actual_external_circle_reflection_and_cusp.md) gives an exact interface. An original color $N-h$ circle is a cosine-weighted complete circle plus a literal color $h$ circle. The complete term has a proved Fourier limit for $h=z\sqrt N$, and its coefficient matches the primitive cusp shape: $$\frac{F_N(\sqrt N\,\mathbf z)}{A_{D,N}^{\boldsymbol\epsilon}} =\exp\!\left[-\sum_i\frac{\pi^2z_i^2}{Z_i}\right](1+o(1)), \qquad \tau_{\mathrm{geom},i}=\frac{2\pi i}{Z_i},\quad Z_i=C_i-\pi i\epsilon_i.$$ This holds uniformly for bounded complex $\mathbf z$, with fixed derivatives. It is a theorem about the specified complete term. The full mixed source also contains small-color terms, and the complete term has a full-size opposite-end alias. At that endpoint the small-color term cancels it exactly. A proof for the filling transform must retain this cancellation and control the entire combined source. ![Two actual cusp rectangles fix the primitive longitude factor of two and the normalization of the mesoscopic Fourier Gaussian.](../figures/cusp-gaussian.png) The [source-divisor transfer](../../notes/general_long_filling_source_divisor.md) explains the final quantifier: a nonzero analytic amplitude germ gives a result outside an exceptional divisor, while all independently long slopes require the stronger unit or coordinate-monomial condition. The established complete core has a unit amplitude. To use it for the original filled invariant, the other terms and the color complement must still have a proved gap. ## The exceptional edge now has an exact algebraic description The [finite Fourier-period theorem](../../notes/actual_positive_face_fixed_fold_packet.md) gives an exact four-component difference equation for the original complete-circle core. Its shift range is bounded independently of $N$. It retains the actual finite polynomial solution, both fold endpoints, the Fourier gauge and the full classical determinant factors. Its selected local characteristic is an explicit palindromic quartic. After the shared-face extraction, the equation couples neighboring face coefficients; a scalar equation for the whole knot has not yet been derived. The [exponential interpolation theorem](../../notes/actual_positive_face_exponential_fold_interpolation.md) improves the original fixed-real estimate to an exponentially accurate comparison on the actual channel grid, uniformly for complex face radii. Analytic iterations on nested disks and contraction of the actual finite recurrence establish that comparison. The complete-core theorem then converts the finite channel grid by exact cotangent contours and evaluates the joint saddle. This closes the fixed-neighborhood analytic step for the complete term. The [coupled polynomial system](../../notes/actual_whole_source_coupled_face_difference_system.md) retains every shared-face coefficient and the exact fold-selection relation. It matches the ordered classical momenta on regular charts. At a triangle with two marked zero faces the local quadratic has a double root. The [marked circle-pattern theorem](../../notes/actual_marked_deformed_circle_pattern.md) recovers the shared strip, all source-stationary face radii, and selected eigenline germs directly from a nonsingular finite geometric system. The [primitive collar calculation](../../notes/actual_deformed_circle_primitive_collar.md) then fixes the actual disk word, half-twist shear and line-face limit. Its single side pairing has multiplier $E_bE_c/D$; the double-reflection word has its square. Keeping that distinction and the actual eigenflag lets the global theorem verify every group relation and the regulator differential. ## What the remaining small-color terms now reduce to The [exact small-circle operator](../../notes/actual_small_circle_polynomial_face_insertion.md) preserves the face polynomial ring after summing all original paths. Its apparent negative powers cancel because the physical endpoint coefficients vanish. The original total-degree argument then excludes every whole-level Fourier alias. At fixed positive radii, a color $h$ insertion costs at most $C^{h-1}$ in the weighted coefficient norm. The [simultaneous correspondence](../../notes/actual_simultaneous_small_circle_face_correspondence.md) now covers **every untwisted subset with connected identity smoothing**, including protected outgoing faces and cyclic dependencies between operators. Its proof checks polynomiality separately in each merged-face component, while retaining all other formal path choices. It needs no global elimination order. The earlier [ordered construction](../../notes/actual_ordered_small_circle_face_insertions.md) remains a useful special case. Disconnected identity smoothings have a different exact conclusion. If the inserted colors satisfy $$2\sum_{i\in J}(h_i-1)<N-1,$$ their entire original subset contribution is **zero**. The ordinary face targets require more degree than the retained Laurent terms can supply. This includes the mesoscopic window at both level parities, with every remaining complete-circle phase retained. Deleted ports carrying a half twist are still outside these results. For the required geometric gap, the [smoothing-capacity theorem](../../notes/actual_matching_smoothing_angle_capacity.md) supplies a sufficient angle-flow and entropy condition when an untwisted color-one circle is deleted. The polynomial operator carries any compatible strict gap to small colors, at the stated $C^{h-1}$ cost. It does not supply the gap itself. The [fixed-radius criterion](../../notes/actual_smoothing_fixed_radius_gap.md) gives another sufficient bound without requiring a regular smoothed minimizer. Its explicit certified matched-graph family shows that the corresponding capacity test can fail when only the merged face varies. A source-coverage correction distinguishes that functional example from an original flat-plat source counterexample: the latter would need a presentation adapter that has not been proved. The graph geometry and capacity calculation remain valid. The [capacity decomposition](../../notes/actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md) now handles those boundary limits. Compact angle duality remains exact even when the positive-radius infimum is not attained. Loops give an infeasible angle problem; separating two-edge cycles split the capacity into an additive sum. Each nontrivial simple block has a constructed circle packing and an actual convex ideal right-angled polyhedron, with $$\Phi_{\mathrm{smoothed}}=\sum_B\frac{\operatorname{Vol}(Q_B)}{\pi}.$$ Double-triangle blocks contribute zero. The formula is independent of each block's adjacent marked pair; it does not move the quantum mark or factor the finite quantum source. The [strict representation-volume theorem](../../notes/general_representation_volume_kernel_strictness.md) supplies the strict comparison when the smoothed source is itself certified hyperbolic. Its actual filling quotient kills an essential meridian. An independently checked natural-map argument proves that a representation with such a kernel has strictly smaller absolute volume. Thus the connected regular smoothing has a strict capacity gap, and the simultaneous operator estimate transfers it to small colors. A simple smoothed white triangulation supplies its required polyhedron by the block construction. The [actual block representation](../../notes/actual_smoothed_block_representation_volume.md) now closes the nonzero degenerate-block case. It retains the original cuts and face pairings, including matching cuts whose shaded pairings run between blocks. Compatible finite horospherical corners and a uniform short-edge tetrahedron bound identify the regulator with the sum of block volumes. The representation kills the deleted meridians, so the strict-volume theorem applies. No geometric decomposition of the whole smoothed exterior or finite quantum factorization is assumed. Combining that strict gap with the exact subset identities proves a **general untwisted color corridor**. For any fixed set $E$ of untwisted varied ports, the other ports staying complete with their original signs, there are $\delta(D),\gamma(D)>0$ such that $$\left|A_N(N-\mathbf h_E,N_{\mathrm{else}})-F_N^E(\mathbf h)\right| \leq N^{K(D)}e^{N(\operatorname{Vol}(Y_D)/(2\pi)-\gamma(D))}, \qquad 0\leq h_i\leq\delta(D)N.$$ The [whole-source corollary](../../notes/general_untwisted_mixed_source_volume_corridor.md) combines this gap with the zero-free core. After shrinking the corridor, their ratio is $1+O(e^{-cN})$. Consequently, for any physical integer sequence $\mathbf h_N/N\to\boldsymbol\chi$ in that corridor, $$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log\left|A_N(N-\mathbf h_{N,E},N_{\mathrm{else}})\right|=\operatorname{Vol}(\rho_{\boldsymbol\chi}).$$ This is a limit for the **whole original mixed source**, with the actual marked geometric representation on the right. It holds at arbitrary fixed width and both level parities. A complete metric on a filled knot is a further assertion, and the full filling transform still needs its complementary-color estimates. For a signed varied port, the [exact crossing kernel](../../notes/actual_signed_small_circle_face_kernel.md) preserves the original confluent Casimir data. Its weighted coefficient norm can grow exponentially even at color one. The same calculation nevertheless gives a sufficient one-port criterion at the original packing: $$g_i=F(x_i,b_i,y_i)+F(x_i,c_i,y_i)-G(b_i,x_i,y_i,c_i)>0.$$ Here $F$ is the original triangle potential and $G$ is the explicit four-variable entropy maximum in that note. The criterion assumes connected identity smoothing and four positive, suitably unmarked face curvatures. It gives a signed one-port corridor with every other port complete and its sign retained. A curvature ratio below $2.807257219\ldots$ is one sufficient local test. This is an inequality on the local curvature data; it is not a claim that every such quadruple occurs in a rigid labeled packing. Interacting signed ports require a separate simultaneous estimate. ![A schematic slice of external colors: the untwisted corridor, the sufficient signed one-port estimate, and the remaining full color complement.](../figures/external-color-corridor.png) The [positive Newton calculation](../../notes/actual_positive_newton_capacity_obstruction.md) explains why the far-color problem cannot be reduced to a presumed universal entropy comparison on all certified matched graphs. Its exact local kernel has nonnegative coefficients, but an explicit shared-face feasible state gives a capacity above the geometric complete value. The coefficient lower bound retains the true Newton weights. The graph family has not yet been adapted to the original flat-plat compiler, so this remains a polynomial-capacity obstruction, not a claimed flat-plat source counterexample. In the actual alternating expansion the omitted sign changes a critical equation. A proof using that expansion must retain the sign. The remaining general source problems are interacting signed near-complete terms and the entire complementary color region, including their combined opposite-end aliases. The [near-maximal-volume theorem](../../notes/general_representation_volume_peripheral_gap.md) gives a general geometric criterion for the latter problem. For a fixed finite list of marked peripheral words, keeping any $|\operatorname{tr}^2\rho(\mu_i)-4|$ bounded away from zero forces a uniform positive volume gap. Its proof derives convergence to the marked complete representation from near-maximal volume. Using this criterion for the quantum source still requires a bound on the actual full period; a characteristic equation or the complete-image term alone does not provide that bound. The previous operator and torsor approaches remain available. The exceptional operator is the original normalized Casimir polynomial, with its [general character relation](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_polynomial_geometric_action.md) and [exact resolvent period](../../notes/actual_matching_edge_continuant_operator_period.md). The original marked transport, genuine quantum normals, odd framing source, logarithmic class and relative boundary currents are preserved in the [source and torsor routes](../library.html). The new coefficient identity and signed Gaussian resolve the complete contraction without assigning an arbitrary relative cycle. The global knot quantum A-operator and its selected period have not been derived from this identity. The coefficients and source relations provide a concrete finite object for that work; they are not being renamed the knot A-polynomial. ## Existing knot results and preserved alternatives The [results chapter](results.md) retains the internally reviewed pretzel, belt-stack and signed Conway filling theorems with their original hypotheses. They do not exhaust arbitrary plats. The cube, Fourier, weighted-Cauchy, Karamata-inspired and torsor arguments remain in the [research library](../library.html), including failed intermediate estimates and their corrections. The current route adds a general exact coefficient and a whole-source augmented-link result without discarding those ideas.

title: Notation and conventions
text: # Notation and conventions The technical notes were developed over time and sometimes reuse letters. This guide uses the conventions below; each linked proof remains authoritative for its own definitions. | Symbol | Meaning in this guide | | --- | --- | | $N$ | Quantum level; the diagram and filling slopes are fixed before $N\to\infty$ | | $q=e^{\pi i/N}$ | Principal root used in the displayed symmetric quantum integers | | $\zeta$ | Generic parameter before root specialization | | $[r]_\zeta$ | $(\zeta^r-\zeta^{-r})/(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})$ | | $d=N-1$ | Top physical color index; some notes call it $D$ | | $j_e$ | Integer spin in the folded scalar theorem | | $A,B,C,D$ | Integer highest weights in the general four-port theorem; these can represent half-integral spins | | $E,G$ | Intermediate highest weights for the two four-port pairings | | $K_N$ | The specified original reduced or marked invariant, with convention stated in its theorem | | $W_N$ | Positive face-normalized local Racah scalar; not the full knot invariant | | $Z_{E,N}$ | Whole positive source of the specified Conway expression $E$ | | $v_3,v_8$ | Volumes of the regular ideal tetrahedron and regular ideal octahedron | ## Three distinctions that matter **A generic normal versus a level asymptotic.** A derivative in $\zeta=q\exp(t)$ keeps $N$ fixed and differentiates the genuine generic source. It is not the same operation as taking another term in a large-$N$ expansion. **A source normal versus a zero root value.** A factor such as $[2N]$ vanishes at $q$ but has a nonzero derivative. Removing it before the prescribed normal is taken can change the invariant. **Complete versus filled volume.** The augmented complement and a complement obtained by Dehn filling generally have different volumes. The filling theorem compares the deformed original source with the actual filled geometry, using its specified peripheral slopes. The longitude variable $L$ in an A-polynomial, a complete-circle operator called $L_N$, and a recoupling coefficient denoted $L_{G,E}$ are distinct objects. Likewise, a genuine turn and an inverse recoupling matrix can both be called $R$ in older notes. Consult their typed definitions before combining formulas.

title: Reproducing and reading the audits
text: # Reproducing and reading the audits ## What is being checked The repository contains written arguments, exact finite algebra audits, numerical diagnostics, and recorded outputs. These are different kinds of evidence. An exact symbolic identity can verify a stated algebraic step for independent formal variables. A finite-field counterexample can refute a proposed exact identity when the reduction is valid. A successful list of finite levels alone does not prove a uniform asymptotic theorem. Floating-point growth plots need their own error control before they can support a rigorous estimate. Each technical note specifies its proof and the narrower role of its audit. The archive keeps scripts and result files accessible together. ## A focused starting set From the repository root, install the core research dependencies in an environment of your choice: ```sh python3 -m pip install -r requirements-core.txt ``` These checks cover the current finite source and variational inputs: ```sh python3 experiments/audit_actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_positive_conway_variational_limit.py ``` Read the corresponding result's `scope` field before interpreting `PASS`. There is no assertion that every historical diagnostic forms a single passing application test suite. Some optional geometry checks require SnapPy, Regina, Sage, or other packages listed by the particular script. The arbitrary-plat advance has a separate focused set: ```sh python3 experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_selected_complex_action.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_uniform_complex_amplitude.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_magnetic_complex_corridor.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_regular_geometric_phase_chart.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_channel_hessian.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_small_channel_generic_normals.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_physical_partner_normal_bound.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_racah_positive_scalar.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_marked_four_port_block.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_completed_projector_block.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_native_projector_energy.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_magnetic_energy_profile.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_native_magnetic_energy_local_geometry.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_shrinking_fold_native_energy.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_fourier_coefficient_variational.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_matching_graph_shared_cycle_fourier_compiler.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_matching_graph_positive_fourier_partition.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_positive_fourier_radial_geometric_obstruction.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_physical_generic_jet_bound.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.py python3 experiments/audit_general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.py python3 experiments/audit_actual_planar_three_port_reflection_double.py ``` The root, complex-action and amplitude notes contain their analytical proofs; root finding and large-level comparisons are regressions. The magnetic audit also tests the original finite Casimir equation and the exact joint rational formula, retaining the difference between Gaussian and positive sine binomials. The character and regulator audits check exact rational identities in formal variables. The marked gluing audit uses an actual three-cusp triangulation; the critical-scheme audit checks local inverses and 24 incidence graphs. The reflection and graph audits replay actual finite sources. None of these checks proves the missing general global asymptotic. The joint determinant audit checks the source polynomial before continuation, its three-term recurrence and positive principal minors. The joint amplitude audit compares the literal finite sum with its determinant and asymptotic, including both derivative corrections at folded channels. The framing audit verifies the stated equivalences and local construction; it does not search for or prove a favorable common frame for every plat. The generic-normal audits compare the original generic columns and derivatives, including the exact large-partner collision tail and nonzero extra-pole residues. The right-angled obstruction audit checks reflection signs, polarization identities and exact two-facet examples. Its general conclusion rests on the separate proof of the literal Morse-prefix dictionary and convex incidence, not on extrapolating those examples. ## The exceptional-period checks The current period argument has focused audits for the generic Casimir polynomial, its root location and positive endpoint convolution, the actual inverse-turn character relation, and the full resolvent with its normal poles. The strict-prefix and Green-action audits check original matrix entries and selected logarithms. The rectangle audit verifies the actual primitive words for all three half-twist cases. Each note links its script and recorded output. The endpoint resolvent proof uses a unitary congruence and exact Schur denominator; it does not claim a Hermitian similarity or a polynomial bound for individual spectral projectors. Numerical rate samples supplement the written asymptotic proofs. None of these local or endpoint checks establishes a contributing contour or the general source asymptotic. ## Rebuilding this guide and its figures The guide is generated from `book/chapters/` and the published notes. Its static HTML uses native MathML and local CSS and JavaScript; reading it requires no account or external math service. ```sh python3 tools/build_book.py python3 tools/check_book.py python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory docs ``` The build requires Pandoc. TikZ sources and their compiled PNG/PDF figures are retained in `book/figures/`. To regenerate the figures, install a TeX distribution with TikZ and the optional Python package PyMuPDF, then run: ```sh python3 tools/render_figures.py python3 tools/build_book.py ``` The main README is deliberately short. The long research log, all existing technical note paths, and audit imports are preserved. The physical paired-normal audit checks the original Casimir entries, weighted Dirichlet identity, double-node reflection and actual generic derivative. Its polynomial estimate is proved on the physical grid; it is not a complex-neighborhood or whole-source theorem. The near-fold complex audit retains the full large generic source and checks the resonant recurrence on a small complex circle. Its subexponential theorem requires shrinking scaled channel windows. The matching-edge audits reconstruct the actual generic four-port matrices, pivotal signs, root first jets and original row measure. They retain unequal partner derivatives and do not infer a completed positive matrix norm from the scalar formula. The full physical packet audit tests the new cone determinant, finite boundary zeros, generic matrix lifts and actual amplitudes outside the old central wedge. The physical generic-jet audit retains both forward and backward q recurrences and nonzero higher divided-pair jets. The localization audit checks the exact low/high flag formulas; its general conclusion is the separately reviewed continuation and geometric argument. None establishes a contributing global cycle. The completed-projector audit independently checks the categorical norm, full generic operator identities, actual cyclic turn, paired cluster jets and complete original-measure cancellation. It retains the nilpotent contribution and unequal scalar derivatives. Its finite checks support the written identities; they do not bound the native projectors or establish a global volume limit. The native-energy audit checks the actual generic high-degree adapter, dual measures, residue and completed-projector jets, and exact rank-one norms. The exponential midpoint-energy rate has a written Riemann-sum proof; its numerical sequence only illustrates that proof. The theorem retains the energy rather than asserting polynomial projector norms. The energy-profile audit checks actual Fourier norms, vanished unused nodes, canonical midpoints, both-parity endpoint source formulas and the selected dilogarithm constant. Its even finite full-norm samples concern the nilpotent operator; the completed projector's rate follows from the separate polynomial comparison. The local geometry audit checks original phases, measures, parity factors and all four tetrahedron shapes, without inferring global phase matching. The shrinking-fold audit checks the actual source formula outside complete support as well as its endpoint and measures. The coefficient audit checks log-concavity, tilted modes, literal complex-radius normalization and interior coefficient rates. The shared-cycle audit compares against original Morse contractions, including the first-failure zeros, both-parity carrier cancellation, exact Kirchhoff support and marked charge. The resulting global Cauchy comparison remains an upper bound. The positive-partition audit reconstructs the original endpoint and white scalars, the high-degree Chevalley adapter, and full phase-bearing sums before checking their Cauchy bound. The radial-obstruction audit checks the finite phase derivatives, adapters and cup/mark relation; its general geometric conclusion uses the separately proved common-frame obstruction. Neither audit claims a global rate gap or volume equality.

title: Figure gallery
text: # Figure gallery These diagrams introduce the objects and constructions used in the guide. The geometric drawings are combinatorial projections; their captions state what the colors and highlighted faces mean. Each figure can be opened at full resolution or downloaded as SVG, PDF, or editable TikZ. ## The route to volume equality Exact source formulas, joint local complex amplitudes and the marked geometric branch are now available at arbitrary fixed width under their stated hypotheses. The diagram highlights the remaining global selection and estimate problem. The [frontier](chapters/frontier.md) states the precise gap; the [results chapter](chapters/results.md) states the families already covered by the recorded proofs. ![The general research route: exact source, local action and actual geometric volume, with the remaining global theorem highlighted.](figures/research-map.png) ## The joint local domain The blue region shows the limiting [full strict physical domain](../notes/actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) in the real parts of the two wire coordinates. Both the pair degree and magnetic coordinate may vary complexly. The seam and outer boundary are excluded. At finite level the proved zero-free region also excludes a band of width $1/(2N)$ on each side of the seam. Every fixed compact in the limiting domain is covered eventually. ![The full strict physical domain in two wire coordinates, with low and high adapters and the necessary finite-level seam correction.](figures/joint-kernel-domain.png) ## Two exceptional factors at arbitrary bridge width Under the geometric strip conditions, the common framing flags determine a line through the convex hull of the normalized white face normals. A generic line meets exactly two facets. The [framing obstruction and localization](../notes/actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) prove that these are exactly the two local factors failing strict physical support. The two facets can be prescribed, including those at both ends of one crossing-circle matching edge. The [selected-factor theorem](../notes/actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md) now puts every other ordinary factor on the selected full physical packet. The later [positive coefficient and signed-source proof](../notes/general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md) resolves the complete contraction. The exceptional operator route is preserved for deformations and generic normals. ![Schematic planar section of the white-normal convex hull, with two facet exits locating the exceptional factors.](figures/two-exceptional-factors.png) ## Two framing directions and a primitive transverse slice For the certified original matching graph, the finite boundary cores equate all quadratic white-face potentials. The two constant-prefix faces leave exactly two flat directions. The marked physical head and one neighboring original physical head detect them with determinant $\pm1$. The [rank and curvature theorem](../notes/actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.md) therefore gives a uniformly invertible transverse Hessian. This is a choice of source coordinates. The [positive face coefficient theorem](../notes/actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md) uses the same connected graph to establish its global saddle; the [signed Gaussian theorem](../notes/general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md) also controls the complete channel sum. External filling colors remain separate. ![Two constant-face potentials and the neighboring original physical heads that give a primitive transverse slice.](figures/face-potential-rank.png) ## The cusp rectangle and the Fourier Gaussian The [external reflection and cusp theorem](../notes/actual_external_circle_reflection_and_cusp.md) places the exact complete-circle cosine term on the same primitive cusp normalization as the geometry. One polyhedral rectangle has width $W$ and height $H$; two rectangles give a meridian of length $H$ and a longitude of length $2W$. Thus $C=\pi H/W$ and the retained half-twist Gaussian has $Z=C-\pi i\epsilon$ and primitive cusp shape $\tau=2\pi i/Z$. The Fourier limit is proved on the scale $h=z\sqrt N$. The full mixed-color source and fixed-color filling packet still require additional estimates. ![The primitive cusp basis from two rectangles and its exact factor of two in the folded Gaussian normalization.](figures/cusp-gaussian.png) ## The marked faces share one strip The [marked circle-pattern theorem](../notes/actual_marked_deformed_circle_pattern.md) keeps the two zero-curvature faces as actual parallel lines. Main incidences stay tangent; matching incidences acquire the prescribed inversive cosine. A finite system with $3R-1$ equations reconstructs every center and radius, and its Jacobian is invertible at the complete pattern. The resulting curvatures solve the original source's face-stationary equations. The diagram shows the shared strip and the selected fixed points at two marked triangles; the theorem applies to every certified diagram, with no restriction to this illustrated configuration. ![Two finite circles in the same marked strip, with main tangencies, deformed matching intersections, and selected fixed points that collide at completeness.](figures/marked-circle-strip.png) ## External colors and the remaining filling estimate The blue square schematically represents the proved [whole-source untwisted corridor](../notes/general_untwisted_mixed_source_volume_corridor.md); its size depends on the fixed diagram. Along the indicated axis, one varied signed port has a [sufficient local curvature criterion](../notes/actual_signed_small_circle_face_kernel.md). The complement remains a problem for the full original source. The complete term has an opposite-end alias, which the small-color term cancels; a bound for the complete term alone cannot replace the combined estimate. The diagram shows two external color coordinates, not two bridge strands or a quantitative value of the corridor width. ![External-color regions and the scope of the current source estimates.](figures/external-color-corridor.png) ## The exceptional operator and its selected scalar action The scalar polynomial and original resolvent have different analytic roles. All polynomial zeros lie above $2$, while the physical Casimir nodes lie in $[-2,2]$. The actual geometric target is at most $-2$ under the marked complete certificate. The exact contour retains both factors and their generic normals. Endpoint estimates at $+2$ do not prove the global saddle contribution or settle a parabolic target at $-2$. See [the current critical path](chapters/frontier.md#the-exceptional-edge-now-has-an-exact-algebraic-description). ![The exact polynomial-resolvent period and its spectral regions, with the contributing global period still open.](figures/exceptional-period.png) ## The exact support boundary The prescribed geometric frame puts the exceptional edge beyond physical bandwidth. The [support calculation](../notes/actual_matching_edge_geometric_support_zero_chamber.md) identifies the failed inequality exactly. The [entire finite kernel](../notes/actual_matching_edge_entire_operator_kernel.md) cancels its apparent poles while retaining every physical lattice zero. The [joint deficient packet](../notes/actual_q_hahn_joint_deficient_degree_packet.md) now controls its selected asymptotic on a complex neighborhood of the actual geometric frame. The later positive coefficient theorem establishes the complete-source contribution; this local picture by itself does not control external-color deformations. The axis depicts the folded limiting channel, not the finite-level bandwidth endpoint $a/N$; the geometric packet has complex magnetic coordinates. ![The limiting physical bandwidth, the selected complex geometric packet, and the remaining global period problem.](figures/support-wall.png) ## A change of pairing Four external colors stay fixed while the internal channel changes. This is the local operation used to transport the source through a diagram. The [mechanism chapter](chapters/mechanism.md) explains the normalization and why local control must be assembled into a global estimate. ![Four-port recoupling: internal channel E in the first pairing becomes G in the turned pairing.](figures/four-port.png) ## The cube experiment The four blue rungs are summed in the proved packet, while the eight orange cycle labels remain fixed. The [cube discussion](chapters/results.md#cube-sectors-are-kept-separate) records the conclusions and the remaining full-source problem. ![Cube channels, with four summed blue rungs and eight fixed orange cycle edges.](figures/cube-channels.png) ## The local geometric cell The blue triangles are polar truncation faces. The hyperbolic metric is specified by the face Gram matrix, not by the Euclidean proportions of this drawing. See [the local geometric argument](chapters/geometry.md#a-local-tetrahedron-is-a-genuine-geometric-result). ![A truncated hyperideal tetrahedron shown in a combinatorial projection, with blue truncation faces.](figures/truncated-tetrahedron.png) ## The Conway cells The source leaf is an ideal quadrangular pyramid and multiplication gives an ideal triangular prism. Blue quadrilateral ports carry the matching data; the shaded leaf triangles retain the crossing-disk pairing. The [global geometry chapter](chapters/geometry.md#the-conway-maximum-now-builds-the-actual-complement) explains their assembly into the actual complement. ![Conway source cells: the ideal leaf pyramid and multiplication prism, with their ordered quadrilateral ports.](figures/conway-cells.png) ## Peripheral marking and the torsor The left panel draws a primitive filling curve on a schematic torus fundamental domain. Opposite sides are identified; the amber segments join into one loop in class $\mu+2\lambda$. The drawing does not prescribe a Euclidean cusp shape. The right panel shows the local sheets of the square-root cover $\ell^2=L$, the branch selected by the source, and the integral monomial shear on that cover. It is a local picture, not a claim that the torsor splits globally. The [peripheral geometry discussion](chapters/geometry.md#half-twists-preserve-the-marked-action-through-a-shear) explains why the primitive marking must be retained through filling. ![A primitive cusp filling slope and the selected local sheet of the peripheral square-root torsor.](figures/peripheral-torsor.png)

title: A-polynomial volume limits and torsors: current status
text: # A-polynomial volume limits and torsors: current status Active sharp-bound attack, 28 October: follow the [full-source plan](full_source_volume_bound_attack_plan.md). The new [two-anchor contour bound](actual_coefficient_minimax_upper.md) retains cancellations and has polynomial transport cost; [arrangement orders](charged_arrangement_boundary_orders.md) isolate bounded-deficit boundary strata; and [actual meridian transport](actual_bounded_quantum_meridian_transport.md) is uniformly bounded in N for every fixed signed word. The first two results do not impose full clock criticality. The last does not yet impose the original closure or joint atomic regulator on its compact physical support. The broad-class upper bound and geometric survival remain open; these qualifications are part of the current proof status. The subsequent [original plat source theorem](actual_plat_cup_cap_gram_support.md) does impose the bottom/top meridian relations on the respective compact cup/cap supports. Unrescaled overlap limits obey both sets of relations, but may be the zero measure. This supplies a source-specific support statement, not the missing exponential overlap or regulator estimate. Latest forced-flow theorem, 28 October: the [actual critical graph equation](charged_critical_flow_and_chambers.md) and strict source-cut inequalities bound ALL regular anchor critical radii in a residual core by a polynomial in N. Balance forces the critical points onto the original unit torus, and chamber concavity then supplies a genuine selected-coefficient theorem under a sign gap. But [an all-level original-source calculation](actual_alternating_balanced_source.md) proves that every nonzero figure-eight clock sector has an individual defect >=(N-1)/2 in these coordinates. Pointwise sublinear defects are not its leading support. The jet strategy must first retain or exactly cluster this macroscopic forcing. Properness alone does not force geometric selection, as [explicit unit-cyclotomic source examples](charged_torus_critical_selection.md) demonstrate. No full-clock volume theorem follows yet. Latest general reduction, 28 October: the actual nilpotent source now allows [all knot closure adapters to contract](actual_general_flow_fusion.md) through arbitrary exteriors, with the original pivot substitutions. Balanced trivalent stars have an exact triangle replacement. Its [retained defect polynomial](charged_star_triangle_defect_jets.md) has subexponential normalized coefficient norm for every e=o(N), with the explicitly calibrated TWO-tetrahedron scalar rate. [Cut/flag jets](charged_source_cut_jets.md) give exact global boundary factorizations and canonical residual flow cores. The original [underclock feedback](actual_clock_feedback_normal_form.md) is also an explicit, necessary finite Gaussian operation. These facts do not show that the whole source lies in the controlled defect regime or that its geometric contribution survives the final pairing. Latest whole-period source, 28 October: the [global charged-flow identity](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md) is exactly K_N=(chi_N/N) sum_h W_h [product X_a^(N-1)]P_h. Each event is a homogeneous degree-(N-1) form, each anchor has one terminal denominator, and every nonzero cyclic alias is excluded by total degree. All closure adapters, pivots and the original cut remain. Anchor contours can move through arbitrary finite radii in this POLYNOMIAL presentation, without finite full-Psi/Cauchy seams. This does not continue the remaining discrete clock variables. The [fixed-level source algebra](actual_charged_socle_and_fermat_source.md) is finite flat over all Fermat centers, with an exactly constant, unimodular Frobenius pairing. Its regular-grid residue and nilpotent jet socle functional give the same original period with fixed normalization. Complete Q-orbits of pair factors give exact source annihilation. Neither fixed-level flatness nor that pairing proves growth across N. The [actual bridge phase and complementary-charge rule](actual_bridge_charge_phase.md) retain every phase and give a further exact projector: a tuned original remaining-wire fiber is zero unless r+H>=N-1. It eliminates the demonstrated oversized post-bridge entropy family. This is actual source selection, not yet selection of the geometric period for a broad class. The surviving charged coefficient/h-sum remains the critical path to the volume estimate. Latest bridge theorem, 28 October: the [original physical port interpolation](actual_fourier_port_polynomials_and_profiles.md) proves [simultaneous signed overbridge unwinding](actual_signed_overbridge_unwinding.md). All interior overbridge sums close exactly by a root degree-complement identity, for arbitrary signs, width and regular spectator parameters. The surviving clocks decrease along each overbridge; the product lengths telescope to at most N-1 and the binomials to a q-multinomial. Original spectator-dependent crossing normalizers and the full source are retained. The resulting period still couples the remaining labels; there is no automatic second underbridge pass or volume lower bound. [Critical-path Section 23](critical_path_to_original_volume_conjecture.md#23-simultaneous-exact-elimination-of-arbitrary-signed-overbridge-interiors) records the exact advance and next actual source problem. Latest exact whole-source result, 28 October: the [balanced four-full-Psi kernel](actual_balanced_fourier_crossing_kernel.md) equals the ORIGINAL crossing operator at the complete color. The original E-coproduct identity and injectivity on high-degree blocks eliminate the formerly allowed degree-N aliases exactly. Thus the [whole-word comparison](regular_balanced_fermat_word_source.md) retains arbitrary fixed-root insertions, both signs, the full marked source and every scalar. This is not an off-root meridian-jet theorem. [Propagated regular frames](propagated_balanced_frames_and_boundary_source.md) eliminate every interior Fourier adapter for any open signed braid, leaving at most one closure adapter per head. The [original rational co-source and toric residue](whole_fermat_toric_residue_and_wire_source.md) have exact grid and wire-pole Jacobians. The [explicit deck characters](balanced_crossing_deck_characters.md) retain the off-grid bulk logarithmic seams. Removing interior adapters does NOT identify the full source with the positive geometric cycle. An exact unequal-radius slide inserts transfer weights, and a wire-pole pushforward can restore the old beta/Rogers current. These are checked limitations of the proposed global simplifications. The local operator/source comparison is therefore genuinely stronger, but the broad-class geometric coefficient, volume-rate lower bound and sharp total upper bound remain open. The distance assessment remains: at least one major conceptual advance is needed, rather than routine assembly of the proved local identities. Preceding complete-crossing result, 28 October: the [Rogers source](actual_rogers_sink_opposite_beta_source.md) now follows exactly from opposite-root Newton reversal, with its off-balance norm and relative current. This completes the actual local source formulas. Their shared opposite face cancels as a FULL function with central factor 1-w^N, before taking asymptotic symbols. The [complete sourced gluing equation](actual_crossing_shared_face_fourier_source.md) has three explicit endpoint blocks. At completeness exact finite cancellation makes its entire right side polynomially bounded: operator norm N-1 for N>=3, sqrt(2) for N=2. The [signed Green identity](signed_green_antiunitary_transport.md) uses the SAME balanced flat metric for both signs. For any fixed r-crossing word, [whole tensor transport](whole_word_ground_green_transport.md) and its inverse have bounds N^r and 2^r, and the original co-source is retained. These are ambient bounds, not a lower bound on its restriction to a geometric sector. The complete ground data include the original crossing entries by isometric reindexing; their bulk exponential weights and possible scalar cancellation remain. The [exact full-function deck characters](actual_full_psi_frobenius_deck_gluing.md) give the marked Frobenius gluing equations. The [current extension](actual_beta_current_connection_and_monodromy.md) shows why a generic quotient killing the currents also kills the geometric section. A balanced base change has a nonzero local section, but the original global source has not been shown to factor through it. Thus no new broad knot class or general volume limit is asserted. Latest selected-source theorem, 28 October: the ORIGINAL trivalent source now has an [exact beta decomposition](actual_trivalent_quantum_beta_source.md) into a nonzero balanced geometric residue and its retained central current. The [normalizer is fixed exactly](actual_trivalent_beta_normalizer.md) by descent to z=u^N, exclusion of finite poles, and the two end bounds that make its ratio holomorphic on P^1. The answer includes u^N; q-periodicity alone would not determine or bound that factor. The full-function symbol and a uniform Barnes bound prove actual local geometric selection with coefficient one on an explicit open norm-gap chamber. An independent [positive Fourier norm identity](actual_sink_source_convolution.md) proves the balanced source's nonvanishing without oscillatory estimates. This is a concrete realization of the requested torsor/rigidity idea for the actual source. Its composition with the whole exterior knot source, and hence the broad volume conjecture, remain unproved. Latest exact source advance, 28 October: an [atomic-window resolution](atomic_window_total_source_resolution.md) removes every compact artificial Cauchy cluster, including dependent circuits, by a coefficient-independent identity of the ORIGINAL whole source. Its full-Psi/interval normal block has determinant -1; finite regular atomic endpoints cannot be stationary. The source can use fixed head radii. This is stronger than estimating the previously retained pole currents separately. An [actual quantum Pachner relation](actual_quantum_pachner_source_saturation.md) now supplies an explicit fixed-degree Q-1 correction to the saturated middle-face polynomial. The correction is a compulsory original source current, retained by a polynomial unipotent extension. This does not authorize a raw classical quotient of the faithful source. Global geometric selection, true zero ends and dilogarithmic degenerations remain unproved; no new broad volume-limit class follows. Latest general theorem, 28 October: the actual nine-atom scalar phase has the [original representation regulator](actual_wall_critical_regulator.md) at every regular full critical point, including integer cut marks. An independent [finite-tetrahedron averaging proof](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md) bounds each value by the hyperbolic volume in absolute value. The [joint saturated critical closure](saturated_critical_regulator_compactification.md) retains that bound at every degenerate shape limit and has finitely many regulator values. Regular finite cap-endpoint values are zero. These assertions require no knot-by-knot saddle computation. The original whole relative cycle now has an [exact scalar cut-wall pushforward](actual_full_psi_cut_wall_pushforward.md). The aggregate correction current remains present. A whole-period growth bound still requires controlling its singular and non-full endpoint strata; the geometric coefficient remains unproved. The critical-value theorem does not close those two remaining tasks. Latest, 28 October: the [all-Hardy forest](actual_hardy_forest_residue_reduction.md) now has an exact original-source residue pushforward of degree +1. Its negative current branches cannot return to the original finite source. [Coupled interval caps](actual_coupled_caps_interval_source.md) remove the spurious endpoint stationary equations, recover the actual inverse framed meridians, and admit exact endpoint-fixed paths through complex geometric clocks. A regular source endpoint forces the knot's PSL2 representation to be trivial; singular and escaping endpoints are not covered by that exclusion. The [full modular function and its exact moment source](actual_modular_dilog_circle_and_boundary_source.md) give a different necessary bridge: both full angular cut choices have an explicit radial correction preserving every original coefficient. At radius one these correction operators have polynomial bounds. The full function has a nonzero uniform dilogarithm symbol throughout its selected angular strip, on either side of the unit circle. This agrees with the [all-radius reference cycle](all_radius_angular_geometric_cycle_and_polarization.md), whose geometric maximum has a strict boundary gap; the original relative cycle has not yet been carried to that reference cycle. An [actual marked pentagon](actual_marked_full_phi_flag_pentagon.md) now exists at the physical root, with its cup-selected integer degree and exact coefficient sqrt(N) exp{i*pi[1/4-(N+N^(-1))/12]}. The apparent norm-root singularity is removed by the full degree gauge, not by deleting its scalar. The literal five-point factorial gauges also have full-function relative moments. All three classical certificate patterns and their global source transport remain to be realized. These results remove specific local/cycle barriers, but do not prove general geometric survival, a lower bound, or a sharp global volume bound. Latest, 28 October: the [cyclic-dilogarithm/continuous-Gaussian period](actual_continuous_gaussian_cyclic_network.md) now represents the ORIGINAL whole signed word by the literature norm-one cyclic functions, Hardy Cauchy kernels and ordinary Gaussian weights, with its specified source, initial cycle and all original scalar factors. Ordered factorial support kills every internal upper-projector branch and makes the added cyclic Taylor tails invisible to the complete original contraction. The Gaussian moment removes the last finite scalar kernel, using an explicit fibered torus with a proved integrable bound. This is an exact whole-function replacement with uniform initial-cycle leading symbols, not an inferred equality of scalar asymptotics. Its initial cycle has not been transported to the geometric Rivin cycle. The independent [cut-strand peeling theorem](original_source_cyclic_variation_peeling.md) proves, path by path in the ORIGINAL Kashaev coordinates, that the cut strand stays zero. It removes that strand with explicit q-Pascal boundary operators and the original pivotal scalar. The [charged-simplex action](original_crossing_winding_convexity.md) is concave on every supported winding face; strictness on that face has an explicit linear-algebra criterion. Ambient four-angle strictness alone is insufficient, since the actual source forces lower-dimensional faces. The absolute model is also crossing-sign blind, so the retained quadratic phase and the global cycle are still essential. The [actual shared-flag theorem](actual_shared_quantum_flags_and_charged_exchange.md) supplies finite quantum Hurwitz, cleared cross-ratio and mixed cyclic/nilpotent two-to-three identities on the original heads. It retains the even-level wrap sign and the actual cap's unit pairing on v=Q. The missing local equality is the realization of the three classical five-point certificates with this collision source; generic localization at their nilpotent flag difference annihilates the finite module. Latest, 28 October: the [paired source theorem](tame_paired_fermat_source_transport.md) gives an exact whole-word pointed frame with subexponential bounds. The actual charge D+1=N projects two original Fermat cap heads together. Their factorial profiles cancel by root reflection, and their explicit paired value is G=R(2-epsilon)/(1+delta), a known algebraic unit. A rank-two change of the identity maps the original corner to this source and transports the co-source and ALL currents. Its inverse is explicit. It preserves the original arbitrary-plat period pointwise with every G^-1 factor retained. The frame, inverse and fixed source-jet extraction have bounds independent of N on one fixed central disc. On the real slice its marked paired projector is orthogonal. This is not the exponentially conditioned independent-head Fermat frame, and it does not change the original operator's central character. The new crossing still lacks a positive geometric kernel identification; no geometric noncancellation or broad volume theorem is inferred. Latest source/geometry audit, 28 October: the [cap-residue quad theorem](cap_wall_fermat_quad_residue_transport.md) extends the actual arbitrary-plat corner through the Fermat cusps, with its scalar divisor, dual shift and central Jacobian retained. The [Ward-current theorem](ward_cyclic_wall_contraction_and_marked_augmentation.md) identifies the exact canceled currents and the nonzero augmented source left behind. A [physical two-head contraction](actual_two_head_ward_polynomial_contraction.md) costs at most max(1,|x|)N^2/4 at every degree; an algebraic holomorphic version is polynomially bounded on the scaled meridian tube. These statements do not establish simultaneous many-head compatibility or the geometric image of the original whole word. The [full four-line Fermat frame](actual_four_line_fermat_crossing_and_conditioning.md) has an explicit cap-compatible inverse and actual crossing kernel. Its norm, inverse norm, and selected corner norms nevertheless have positive exponential rate. Polynomial coefficients on individual quad lines are not a subexponential full-frame theorem; the computed dilogarithm action must be retained. The [positive alias counterexample](positive_geometric_alias_volume_counterexample.md) is a decisive scope correction: even on a positive complete ideal triangulation of 5_2, a nonnegative angle locus of an ACTUAL integer alias, with the complete marked meridian retained, contains a point of volume 3.76403...>Vol(5_2)=2.82812.... Universal domination of such faces by Rivin's original maximum is false. This is not a counterexample to the conjecture: no nonzero original source coefficient on that face is asserted. It makes exact source support and cancellation necessary in any argument that uses this triangulation and these alias loci. Latest, 28 October: the [original 5_2 selected-period theorem](five_two_selected_volume_proof.md) now proves the actual scalar asymptotic with a nonzero coefficient, all source corrections controlled, and exact marked Bloch calibration. Its whole-meridian finite identity and two exact quadratures are independently proved; 1,832 outward-rounded Arb cells certify the remaining one-variable connector inequalities. This establishes the previously missing survival of an oscillatory geometric contribution for this known prototype. It does not establish a broad knot class, a general selected geometric A-factor, or a general torsor rigidity theorem. Those remain the main goal. The [critical-path audit](critical_path_to_original_volume_conjecture.md) measures progress against the original conjecture. Exact quantum reconstruction and the local geometric branch/action are proved. The final selected geometric image, subexponential coefficient control and sharp global norm remain open. Auxiliary frame classification is not counted as completion of those gates. 28 October: the original full root meridian family now has an [exact marked cyclic-dilogarithm period](actual_whole_word_cyclic_dilog_resolvent_period.md), with all factorials inside its local cover factors and every original source and peripheral factor retained. An [explicit Hankel cut cycle](actual_cyclic_dilog_hankel_cycle.md) represents the same period, with polynomial rational-source upper bounds and an unconditional exponentially small far-radial tail. This is a quantum period realization compatible with the existing actual meridian action, not an identification of the classical A-curve or its selected Bloch period. The angular noncancellation and geometric source coefficient remain the central open problem. The subsequent [actual cyclic sewing](exact_quantum_quad_source_transport.md) and [regularized cut theorem](cyclic_sewing_regularized_cut_cycle.md) make the source correction explicit: only two boundary-sewing terms per transfer carry the original small-circle period, and their new cyclic poles require retained residues or order-two endpoint finite parts. The [bulk radial symbol](full_cut_geometric_coupling.md) is an explicit strictly accretive Gamma quotient. Its coefficient-level inverse is uniformly bounded; the remaining angular and pivotal contraction can still cancel. The [rigidity audit](cyclotomic_rigidity_selected_period.md) requires the actual divided meridian source, since a regular scalar comparison on the raw central fibre already fails for the original figure-eight family. No selected geometric-period theorem is inferred from these new comparisons. The [whole-word Euler completion](actual_crossing_euler_completion_and_weight_source.md) and [prefix source-jet transport](prefix_euler_source_jet_torsor.md) now give an exact Euler presentation of the actual signed braid word, its currents and every fixed normal-jet order. The comparison group has bounded nilpotent depth at fixed braid index and jet order; its dimension, coefficients and norms need not be bounded with N.
