A nonzero reduced period must retain a relative boundary source or equivalent regularized data; the exact model period is (t_1-t_0) integral dlog A_cut. Nilpotence of this centralizer alone does not select that relative class. The [actual cut-residue/density calculation](actual_cut_residue_and_principal_density.md) now identifies the cut co-source exactly: the original normalized average is a residue against dlog A on its canonical polynomial representative. Its Mobius transform retains the complete root pole packet, the excluded A=1 frame point, and a compensating pole. Multiplication and normal differentiation have an explicit cyclic carry; forgetting the representative would change the functional. An explicit source reweighting can remove A=1 while preserving the unchanged invariant, with its new normalization. At the principal level, each original crossing amplitude is its mixed-Hessian half-density times a momentum coboundary and color factor. These telescope on every marked critical braid closure. The remaining pivot corrects the ambient holonomy volume to a form invariant under the regular-meridian centralizer. A finite linearized Hurwitz complex gives a rational framing-invariant torsion when its explicitly stated rigidity condition holds. Its Gaussian determinant comparison and the selected relative class still need identification. Neither an equality of those determinant lines nor a regulator norm is inferred from the ambient volume identity or the finite cut normalization. The [crossing fundamental-cycle proof](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) now closes the complete rational Bloch-lift comparison. The actual five-term crossing expressions reduce, by a three-five-term certificate, to an oriented four-tetrahedron diagram cycle. Its universal face pairing and degree-one cusp cycle identify the relative fundamental class, with the specified representation. Thus at the complete geometric point beta_cross=beta_T and D(beta_cross)=Vol(M). The generic M correction and its different eigenflag choices are recorded explicitly rather than discarded at M=1. This supplies the marked complete Bloch--Wigner target on the actual coefficient side. Integral flattenings, the full complex period, and the quantum selected-period comparison remain additional work; the original volume limit is not proved. The [exact longitude/action proof](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md) then fixes a compatible geometric action of these actual coefficients. A meridian shift is an exact rational insertion in the unchanged finite state, with cancelled whole terms at the ideal color. Integral stationary windings are removed by a character equal to one at every actual lattice state. With H=Log(q^2), u=Log M and v=Log L_intr, dS_flat=2v du, Im S_flat=D(beta)+2 Re u Im v, R_intr=S_flat-u v. (5.2) The full geometric peripheral rows are m=M^2,l=L_intr^2. Thus R_intr has exactly the connection and invariant norm in (1.1)--(1.2). At completeness Im S_flat=Vol(M), with no free imaginary additive constant. The geometric action's regulator norm is now identified. A full complex-period comparison retains phase and integral-lift data. The nonzero contribution of this action to the actual quantum period, and control of the remaining contributions, are still unproved. There is now an exact intrinsic scalar on the quantum side for this norm comparison. In squared-meridian coordinates let U=Y^N and t_N=(1/N)Tr_(C(Y)/C(U))(Y F_N(Y))|_(U=1). The [regular-period theorem](regularized_kashaev_period.md) proves t_N=R_N(1) and K_N=N*t_N+O(N^b), where b is any fixed knot braid strand count. The entire polar contribution to the full ADO value at completeness has size O(N^(b-1)). It also gives the positive norm H_N=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1)|F_N(Q_N^j)|^2 =|K_N|^2/N+O(N^(2b-2)). For positive hyperbolic volume the target (5.1) is equivalently the same regulator limit for (4/N)log|t_N| or (2/N)log H_N. These are exact consequences of the pointed state and its controlled ordinary colors. They do not supply the still-missing norm estimate. For the operators satisfying the normal-period theorem's hypotheses, this last norm problem is an exact inverse-matrix pairing. In the specified cyclic trace metric, K_N=-N e_0^* B_0^+ B_1 v_0, ||B_1||=O(1/N), ||v_0||=O(sqrt(N) D_N), where v_0 is fixed by the ordinary colors. A checked Weyl reciprocity restricts the inverse to its -1 sector, whose source and complete functional have the required parity. The full phase and the normal factor 1/N are retained. Estimating this inverse together with its actual source coupling remains necessary; a small singular value alone is not a volume theorem. There is an exact reason to keep this distinction. A nonzero rational root-level solution gives a module map to (C(x),sigma), on which sigma^n=1. It follows that H-1 is not invertible, hence D_n(u,1)=0. The rational ADO states have this central v=1 sector. It is not automatically the geometric classical branch. Retaining the original q-family and its selected period is essential. The requested volume statement, with all constants fixed, is (4/N)log|F_N(1)|-log||P_hyp|| -> 0. (5.1) By (1.2) and (4.1), this is exactly (2pi/N)log|<K>_N| -> Vol(S^3 minus K). It is not proved here. For the intended torsor proof, the missing work is to identify the selected all-level quantum-A period with the calibrated geometric action period, preserving the peripheral lattice and its realization across levels. This also requires justifying the relevant geometric factor's survival in the actual summed operator. The action's classical peripheral marking and regulator norm are now proved, but no comparison of the full pointed quantum period objects has been constructed here. What Hilbert 90 proves is the comparison of the algebraic modules once their central data match. It does not identify the two central curves, select the regulator lift, or bound the remaining scalar across unrelated levels. For example a central unit (u/2)^n fixes an unpointed root-level module and changes a period at u=1 by 2^(-n). This illustrates missing comparison data, not freedom to alter the already normalized Kashaev invariant. The reference anchor above removes this scalar freedom on the Kashaev fiber once a common rational solution line and its anchored comparison are established. It does not prove that a proposed geometric period belongs to that line or has the required residue. Without the rank-one hypothesis, the all-level theorem supplies the actual quantum period by finite fixed-color pointing instead. Its uncontrolled growth is now explicitly in the long operator product and its whole germ; it is not an arbitrary initial normalization. The comparison of that expression with the marked regulator remains unproved. A useful sufficient normalization control is proved: a fixed nonzero meromorphic or algebraic Puiseux germ c(q) at q=1 satisfies log|c(exp(2pi*i/n))|=O(log n), provided evaluation is defined and nonzero. Factor c(q)=(q-1)^a h(q), h(1)!=0. Such a comparison factor cannot change the volume rate. Producing that controlled comparison for the actual quantum-A period is part of the missing theorem. The [central specialization theorem](algebraic_central_normalization.md) strengthens this normalization control. A factor on a fixed finite algebraic cover of (q,t,M,z), specialized by t=1/N, q=exp(c/N), z=M^(kN), has at most polynomially growing nonzero whole-germ value at M=1. This includes the exact ADO factor, including its specified root. It controls known algebraic comparisons; it does not construct the unknown comparison to the geometric period. No alternatingness assumption is used in these structural lemmas. This does not establish the volume conjecture for all hyperbolic or alternating knots. The work above identifies explicit torsors, an algebraic regulator connection, and the exact remaining compatibility.

title: Volume limits constructed from the A-polynomial
text: # Volume limits constructed from the A-polynomial Research note, 26 October 2026. This is an auxiliary classical A-polynomial volume identity. The intended full route starts with Kashaev's own quantum A-module or torsor and uses its structure to prove the invariant's volume growth. This classical construction calibrates the geometric period; it does not replace that actual invariant. Jones is separate. Here is a direct classical construction. It produces marked roots of integer polynomials built from the A-equation by finite-algebra norms, with a proved volume limit on the stated connected geometric class. The remaining choices are a marked curve, path and sampling. No standard quantum A-state is claimed for this construction. It is a discretization of the existing classical regulator, not a claim to have proved the original Kashaev conjecture or to have discovered the regulator identity. ## 1. Conventions and the relative period Use the squared peripheral functions m,l of [the marked regulator note](boundary_regulator_period.md). In SL_2 eigenvalues M,L these are m=M^2,l=L^2, with the recorded orientation of the longitude. Write the corresponding geometric A-equation as A(m,l)=0. It is obtained from the ordinary eigenvalue A-polynomial by its stated finite monomial image, not by renaming M as M^2 without elimination. Let C be a connected marked algebraic curve of representations or a finite augmented cover, containing the geometric and conjugate complete points p_+,p_-. Let beta be its rational crossing or triangulation Bloch class. The already proved boundary identity and complete fundamental-class values are delta beta=-(1/2)m wedge l, D(beta)(p_+)=Vol(X), D(beta)(p_-)=-Vol(X). (1.1) They follow from the actual [boundary-wedge calculation](marked_braid_holonomy.md#8-a-global-boundary-wedge-and-complete-frame-regulator-rigidity) and [fundamental-cycle calculation](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md). No selected quantum state is a premise. Put eta=log|l| darg m-log|m| darg l. The elementary Bloch--Wigner derivative is dD(z)=log|z|darg(1-z)-log|1-z|darg z. Applying it to (1.1) gives dD(beta)=eta/2. Consequently every piecewise C^1 path gamma from p_- to p_+, avoiding the finite shape and coordinate divisors, has integral_gamma eta=4 Vol(X). (1.2) The normalized complete places must be retained: their peripheral coordinate pairs can coincide even though their regulator values differ. This fixes the absolute volume by two specified endpoints, without a zero-volume reference. If C is finite over a normalized A-component, its real primitive descends. Pass to a connected Galois closure. A deck transformation changes the primitive by a constant, since it fixes eta. Its finite order makes that constant zero. Thus the primitive is invariant and descends on the common regular open curve. This is an elementary finite-cover descent argument; it does not concern a quantum state. ## 2. Integer products of A-roots Parametrize gamma on [0,1]. Choose continuous argument lifts theta=arg m, phi=arg l along it. For large N put r=floor(sqrt(N)), h=2pi/N, t_j=j/r. For each interval choose an algebraic point q_(N,j) on C within N^(-2) of gamma((j+1/2)/r), in a fixed finite collection of regular coordinate charts. Such points exist: use a local finite algebraic projection and approximate its regular value by an algebraic number. Avoid its finitely many ramification and coefficient exceptions. Set m_j=m(q_(N,j)), l_j=l(q_(N,j)), a_j=nearest_integer((theta(t_(j+1))-theta(t_j))/h), b_j=nearest_integer((phi(t_(j+1))-phi(t_j))/h), Z_N=product_(j=0)^(r-1) l_j^(a_j) m_j^(-b_j). (2.1) Fix either convention at a rounding tie. These are finite algebraic evaluations with integer exponents; no volume value occurs in their definition. All pairs satisfy the A-equation, with the branch specified by gamma. **Theorem.** Under Section 1's connectedness and marking hypotheses, lim_(N->infinity) [pi/(2N)]log|Z_N|=Vol(X). (2.2) **Proof.** Logs of the moduli are bounded on the compact path. Integer rounding changes h log|Z_N| by O(r/N). Replacing the midpoint values by their algebraic approximants changes it by o(1); the total argument variation is bounded. The remaining sum is the midpoint Riemann sum for integral eta. Its error tends to zero for a piecewise C^1 path. For a C^2 path the total error is O(r^(-1)+r/N+N^(-2)), hence O(N^(-1/2)). Equation (1.2), and h/4=pi/(2N), prove (2.2). The limit is independent of the allowed path, samples and rounding choices because eta has the stated real primitive. The finite values need not be independent of those choices. ## 3. A polynomial defined by norms, not just an informal root product Here is an explicit polynomial containing the marked value Z_N. Let F_N be a number field containing the coefficients of A and the sampled meridians m_j. Require only that the leading and constant l-coefficients at each sample are nonzero; finite exceptional sample points can be avoided. Normalize each A(m_j,L_j) to be monic and form E_N=tensor_(j,F_N) F_N[L_j]/(A(m_j,L_j)). It is a finite algebra. Each L_j is a unit. Let H_N=product_j L_j^(a_j)m_j^(-b_j) in E_N, Q_N(T)=det(T-Mult_(H_N)) in F_N[T], P_N(T)=primitive_integer_multiple of Norm_(F_N/Q)(Q_N(T)). (3.1) All operations are polynomial remainders, multiplication matrices, determinants and number-field norms. Equivalently one can use successive resultants. Evaluation L_j->l_j sends H_N to Z_N, so Q_N(Z_N)=P_N(Z_N)=0. Thus (2.2) is a marked-root limit for explicitly A-generated integer polynomials P_N. The chosen root is essential. A field norm or the largest root over all independent sheet choices can combine other periods. No formula for such an unmarked choice is asserted. This construction is a classical polynomial period, with an existing algebraic norm definition; it is not a new definition of the literature quantum A-operator. ## 4. Cover transfer is exact before taking the limit For a peripheral monomial map m'=m^a l^b, l'=m^c l^d, k=ad-bc>0, use the same sampled marked points upstairs and transfer the integer increments by a'_j=a a_j+b b_j, b'_j=c a_j+d b_j. Then ordinary multiplication proves exactly product_j (l'_j)^(a'_j)(m'_j)^(-b'_j)=Z_N^k. (4.1) Thus this algebraic period has the correct degree law before any asymptotic argument. For a connected one-cusped manifold cover, k is the manifold degree. Laurent elimination gives the upstairs geometric A-factor as in [the cover calculation](regge_period_covers_and_a_curves.md). Independent rounding upstairs changes the scaled log by o(1), so it gives the same limiting law. ## 5. A connected infinite class from the twist presentation Here is an independent algebraic connectedness argument, which avoids assuming an irreducibility theorem from the literature. Use the signed twist convention G_k=<a,b | a w^k=w^k b>, w=ab^(-1)a^(-1)b. Reading a full pair in the twist box conjugates by w; after k pairs the clasp closes by a w^k=w^k b. For k=1 the relation reduces to aba=bab. The hyperbolic twist members have k<=-1 or k>=2. The independently certified families in [the twist topology note](twist_topology_and_peripherals.md) have parameters p=-k-1 (even family) and p=k-2 (odd family), respectively. Their geometry is supplied by the explicit positive face/angle proof, rather than a cited character-variety irreducibility theorem. On the nonabelian meridian chart use A=[M 1;0 M^(-1)], B=[M 0;-u M^(-1)], s=M^2+M^(-2), W=AB^(-1)A^(-1)B, z=Tr(W)=u^2+(2-s)u+2. Direct multiplication gives A W-W B=(s-u-1)(A-B). Let S_(-1)=0,S_0=1,S_(j+1)=z S_j-S_(j-1), extended to all integer indices, and put S=S_(k-1),T=S_(k-2). Cayley--Hamilton gives the single relation (s-u-1)S-T=0. (5.1) Consecutive S,T have no common root. Also S(2)=k, T(2)=k-1. Set v=s-u-1; then z=2+u(1-v). On (5.1), S!=0 and v!=1: otherwise z=2 and S-T=1 would contradict (5.1). Hence every point of this chart is given by the rational parametrization v=T/S, u=(z-2)S/(S-T), s=z-1/[S(S-T)]. (5.2) The last equality uses S^2+T^2-z S T=1. This proves absolute irreducibility of the relevant (s,u) curve. The squared meridian m=M^2 gives the double cover m^2-s(z)m+1=0. (5.3) It is also absolutely irreducible. For k>0, D=S(S-T) has degree 2k-2, so (z-2)D-1 has odd degree 2k-1, is coprime to D, and has an odd-order zero. Thus s(z)^2-4 cannot be a square in C(z). For k=-h<0, take the largest real root z_0 of S_h, which lies in [0,2). At that point T=0, S^2=1, D=1, so s(z_0)=z_0-1 is strictly between -2 and 2. The real rational function s(z)^2-4 is negative there and positive for large real z, since s(z)~z. A real rational function that is a square in C(z) is either a real square or minus a real square: conjugating its square root gives the same root up to sign. Such a function cannot change sign on its real regular locus. This proves (5.3). Consequently this real irreducible marked eigenvalue curve contains both conjugate complete holonomies. The preferred squared longitude is a rational function on it, obtained from its peripheral word; its A-image is nonconstant and the map to that curve is finite on regular open sets. The complete volume values and boundary differential are (1.1). Therefore the polynomial limit theorem applies to every hyperbolic member of this twist family. The rational parametrization and connectedness are the additional algebraic checks here. The full hyperbolic geometry and preferred-peripheral certificates are the previously reconstructed ones; their conventions still have to be kept when writing a numerical A-polynomial. ## 6. A simpler cone product when a zero-volume endpoint is available This gives a useful direct numerical test, independent of the rounded two-endpoint construction. In ordinary SL_2 coordinates take the expanding longitude L(alpha), with M(alpha)=exp(i alpha/2), 0<=alpha<=Theta, along a geometric cone family ending at volume zero. Schlaefli gives Vol(X)=integral_0^Theta log|L(alpha)| d alpha. If M_E=exp(i Theta/2) is algebraic, choose q_N^N=M_E on that arc and L_j the continued A-root at M_j=q_N^j. Then lim_(N->infinity) (Theta/N) log|product_(j<N) L_j|=Vol(X). (6.1) The proof is the Riemann-sum theorem, including continuous or integrable logarithmic endpoint singularities. The geometric cone and zero-volume endpoint are hypotheses, not consequences of alternatingness. The earlier [cone-transfer note](quantum_a_volume.md) supplies this geometry and its quadratic A-factor for the figure-eight. Here the left side is the algebraic root product itself; no transfer-state dominance assumption is required. ## 7. Scope and coverage The classical regulator/volume framework is existing work. [Guilloux--Marche, 1804.01395](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01395) studies exact polynomials, their volume functions and Mahler measures. Its abstract was checked for coverage; its proofs are not premises for the arguments above. A bare Mahler measure is a different observable from the marked product here and can collect several volume contributions. [Hoste--Shanahan, math/0311051](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0311051) provides adjacent coverage of twist-character recursions. The matrix, Chebyshev and irreducibility arguments above are independent of that proof. This is a proved classical marked polynomial-period limit, with an explicit broad connectedness criterion and the twist family application. Its finite sampling is not canonical. Constructing a preferred sequence from an existing quantum A-definition, and proving its volume limit, remains a further goal. Recovering Kashaev directly is its own subsequent objective, as distinguished from a relation with Jones. ## 8. Relation to the actual Kashaev torsor program The intended quantum route uses the A-structure attached to Kashaev itself to prove its volume growth. Its comparison with the previous repo is in [the primary status, Section 0](a_polynomial_torsor_status.md#0-comparison-with-the-previous-work-in-this-repo). The finite classical products above are not already that invariant. A direct small-level calibration is instructive: for the figure-eight at N=2 the cone product in Section 6 is 2+sqrt(3), whereas the original enhanced Kashaev crossing gives 5. The audit evaluates the latter directly from its W-symbol and pivotal closure, without a Jones evaluation. This only distinguishes this particular classical product from the finite invariant. It is not an obstruction to the invariant's own quantum A-torsor route. There is already a direct operator-period mechanism in [the all-level A-period note](all_level_a_period.md): a specified actual quantum annihilator and finitely many fixed initial periods recover Kashaev exactly by a companion product and whole-germ root evaluation. Its verification uses the original cut and quantum-group quotient modules. Jones need not be a definition or a proof input there. There is no need to reconstruct the invariant from the bare classical polynomial alone. The intrinsic route already starts with its actual annihilator and pointed source. Its geometric classical support and selected regulator norm are the missing conclusions. The classical product identity above supplies neither conclusion for that quantum object. A comparison to Jones is additional. [Audit](../experiments/audit_a_polynomial_volume_limits.py). [Results](../experiments/a_polynomial_volume_limits_results.json).

title: Exact boundary reduction of the original quantum-A energy
text: # Exact boundary reduction of the original quantum-A energy 28 October 2026. This implements the proposed boundary-to-interior strategy at the level of the ORIGINAL pointed operator. A regular interior with a weighted symbol gap can be eliminated with controlled cost. Its entire effect is an explicit positive operator on the retained boundary packets. This operator retains the original source, turning regions, endpoint resonance and selected observable. The reduction is proved below. A sharp estimate for its selected boundary response is not proved. In particular, uniqueness does not supply that estimate: a concrete two-endpoint example in Section 4 has an excellent interior gap and an exponentially small boundary eigenvalue. The complementary [interval propagation theorem](actual_pointed_a_interval_observability.md) gives a controlled whole-line Green extension and exponential inward decay from both retained endpoint packets, including shrinking symbol gaps. This note identifies the exact positive operator that determines those packets in the original global source. A subsequent [macroscopic actual-source estimate](actual_macroscopic_a_spectral_upper_bound.md) does now bound the whole original value by a classical spectral integral, under its explicit actual-operator and classical-order hypotheses. Comparing that rate with volume remains open broadly. For the proposed stepwise energy mechanism, the [pointed metric calculation](actual_pointed_metric_transport_and_crossing_obstruction.md) shows precisely what source and endpoint costs must be retained and why tame full-space metrics can lose coherent phase cancellation. ## 1. Eliminate only an interior whose estimate has been proved Use the full bounded-jet system and weights in [the actual bulk energy theorem](actual_pointed_a_bulk_agmon_energy.md): L u=f, P=L* L, g=L* f, beta=f* f. (1) Here * means Hermitian transpose. The actual source consists of the fixed initial identity rows. Choose the remaining column set B to contain their colors, the complete color, and every turning, end or other exceptional packet. Write I for the regular interior columns. Thus g_I=0 exactly. No color or normal jet in B is removed. Suppose the full-output estimate on vectors supported in I gives mu ||v||^2 <= <v,P_II v>, ||P|| <= C, mu>0. (2) For example a fixed weighted symbol gap eta gives mu=eta^2/4 for large N by the proved localized Plancherel estimate. Several regular intervals are allowed: keep enough exceptional columns between them that the full banded operator does not couple their supports, or apply that same estimate to their union with its uniform gap. The operator in (2) retains ALL output rows meeting I. Set A=P_II, H=-A^(-1)P_IB, S=P_BB-P_BI A^(-1)P_IB, E v=(H v,v). (3) Then the exact original solution obeys u_I=H u_B, S u_B=g_B. (4) Moreover 0<=S<=P_BB, ||H||<=C/mu, ker P=E ker S. (5) Proof. Complete the square, for arbitrary v_I,v_B: <v,Pv>=<v_I-Hv_B,A(v_I-Hv_B)>+<v_B,Sv_B>. (6) This proves positivity, the Schur bound and the kernel assertion; the normal equations P u=g with g_I=0 prove (4). Conversely (4) implies the normal equations. Since the original system is consistent, their solutions also satisfy L u=f: their residual is perpendicular to the range of L while belonging to that range. Thus no spurious boundary solution has replaced the original source. For a weighted complete-color projection T_B, its value is T_B u_B. The original unweighted value is exp(-N phi(1)) times that value. For any full observable R u, its exact boundary observable is R_eff=R_I H+R_B, R u=R_eff u_B. (7) The fixed-jet pointing theorem gives ker P subset ker R for the selected constant-color observables (including their weighted versions). Consequently ker S subset ker R_eff. Higher-jet nonuniqueness is retained and does not change the observable. The estimates in (5) show that bulk elimination itself costs at most a power of N whenever mu^(-1) does. ## 2. The residual boundary period is positive and source-exact Let nu=dim ker S, equal to dim ker P and hence bounded by the original fixed jet budget. Define the two polynomials Q_B(lambda)=det(S+lambda I), D_B(lambda,z)=det[ S+lambda I+z R_eff* R_eff g_B; g_B* beta ]. (8) Then the SAME original selected energy is exactly ||R u||^2=[lambda^nu z]D_B/[lambda^nu]Q_B. (9) The denominator is positive; all coefficients of both polynomials are nonnegative real numbers. In particular (9) keeps the boundary source, rather than substituting a maximum eigenvalue or arbitrary boundary vector. Here is a direct proof. Since (1) is consistent, (4) gives beta=<u,Pu>=<u_B,S u_B>=g_B* S^+ g_B. (10) The matrix [S,g_B;g_B*,beta] is positive semidefinite: it is the Schur complement of A in the Gram matrix [P,g;g*,beta]. Factor it as Z* Z. Appending rows sqrt(lambda)[I,0] and sqrt(z)[R_eff,0] gives the matrix in (8). Expanding its determinant as squared minors proves coefficient nonnegativity. The same argument applies to Q_B. Decompose the boundary space orthogonally into ker S and its orthogonal complement. Both g_B and R_eff vanish on the kernel in the appropriate sense. Thus D_B has a factor lambda^nu. On the complement, S is positive definite and (10) makes its bordered Schur complement zero at z=0. Its derivative in z at lambda=0 is g_B* S^(-1) R_eff* R_eff S^(-1) g_B=||R_eff u_B||^2. Multiplication by det(S on (ker S)^perp) proves (9). This is a smaller exact period whenever I occupies most colors. With finitely many exceptional windows of width o(N), its matrix size is o(N), although its entries may retain exponentially small transport information. The latter qualification is essential. Auxiliary regulator weights need not themselves be algebraic; they are an estimating metric, not a new definition of the quantum invariant. Undoing the weight gives the original period exactly. ## 3. Regular interior coupling decays with distance Assume the block bandwidth of P is w and its norm is at most C>0. The proof of (2) gives mu<=C. In the original color distance, the interior Green blocks satisfy ||(A^(-1))_(jk)|| <= mu^(-1) exp[-mu |j-k|/(2 C w)]. (11) If w=0 the inverse is block diagonal instead. To prove (11), expand A^(-1)=(2C)^(-1) sum_(n>=0) (I-A/(2C))^n. The norm of the n-th power is at most (1-mu/(2C))^n. Its (j,k) block vanishes for n<ceil(|j-k|/w), even when I has gaps. Summing this tail and using 1-a<=exp(-a) gives (11). This is a direct banded-matrix proof, independent of diagonalizing the classical transfer. For widely separated boundary columns j,k, (3) therefore gives ||S_(jk)|| <= C' mu^(-1) exp[-c mu (|j-k|-2w)] when |j-k|>2w. (12) Only finitely many P neighbors of j and k occur in the product in (3). The analogous formula u_I=H u_B gives a sum of exponentially decaying contributions from the retained boundary data. If those data and the inverse gap are controlled, the regular interior carries their estimate with polynomial loss. It does not generate an additional volume exponent. The estimate is on the exact response, including all jets. ## 4. Why the residual boundary estimate is necessary Consider a simple, fully rigid sourced recurrence on j=0,...,n: y_0=b, y_(j+1)-2 y_j=0. (13) Its weighted gap with weight zero is |exp(i theta)-2|>=1. Its interior Gram matrix on I={1,...,n-1} has diagonal 5 and off-diagonal -2, so A>=I for every n. Keep B={0,n}. Eliminating I minimizes the energy |y_0|^2+sum_(j=0)^(n-1)|y_(j+1)-2y_j|^2 for prescribed endpoints. Since y_n-2^n y_0=sum_(j=0)^(n-1)2^(n-1-j) (y_(j+1)-2y_j), Cauchy--Schwarz, with equality attained by proportional residuals, gives D_n=sum_(j=0)^(n-1)4^j=(4^n-1)/3, <y_B,S y_B>=|y_0|^2+|y_n-2^n y_0|^2/D_n, S=[1+4^n/D_n, -2^n/D_n; -2^n/D_n, 1/D_n]. (14) The retained source is g_B=(b,0), beta=|b|^2. Solving S y_B=g_B gives y_0=b and y_n=2^n b, exactly as in (13). Yet ||S|| is bounded, det S=1/D_n, and its smallest eigenvalue is asymptotic to 3*4^(-n)/4. Thus a uniformly controlled bulk, a two-dimensional boundary space, and uniqueness still allow exponential source amplification. In (9) the selected period is exactly 4^n |b|^2. This example is a logical test of the propagation inference, not a knot counterexample. It explains why the actual boundary Schur operator and its selected source must be estimated rather than deleted. ## 5. The exact remaining geometric target For the actual complete-color observable, (9), together with undoing the weight, reduces the desired upper bound to a selected boundary response estimate. One may also seek a source-compatible transport flag or an exact boundary factorization which proves (15) without bounding S^+ on irrelevant channels. The regulator must retain its source anchor: phi(0)=0 fixes the initial source scale, and a bound on absolute branch regulators alone controls their differences by at most 2 Vol. Neither (3) nor (9) removes that issue. The local physical-face fillings give possible information for the exceptional packets, but their identification with this complete boundary response still requires an exact source comparison. The independently proved ordinary-color bound concerns the CONSTANT color components j<N. It does not bound the normal jets in B. Those jets are necessary at singular recurrence steps, and (3)--(9) retain them. Replacing the complete boundary packet by its constant-color projection would therefore be an additional unproved inference. This is a constructive boundary-to-interior reduction, valid for the actual original operator wherever its stated bulk gap is verified. No broad sharp whole-source bound or geometric survival theorem is claimed. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_a_boundary_schur_transport.py): four actual figure-eight source elimination identities, an exact rank-deficient rational fixture for the selected coefficient ratio, and four exact recurrence Schur complements. title: Adaptive Fermat sampling preserves the entire original crossing source
text: # Adaptive Fermat sampling preserves the entire original crossing source 28 October 2026. The internal root-orbit source may be placed on its exact Fourier resonance without changing the ORIGINAL finite crossing operator. Its sampling point is allowed to depend on the input/output heads. The old degree-zero restriction is replaced by two explicit physical source walls. This is not an unsupported central base change or a modification of one homogeneous summand. The resulting source-flat family has a first-normal-jet reconstruction at resonance, with jet order independent of N. It fixes the whole finite state, including its currents. It does not prove a global geometric coefficient is nonzero. ## 1. Complete Laurent kernel and its only alias Put Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), d=N-1, retain the actual color x and scalar kappa, and use the COMPLETE positive crossing polynomial K(t)=B_N(t/z_1,x^(-1)t/z_0) R_N(z_6/z_0,x^(-1)z_6/t) B_N(x^(-1)z_7/z_6,x^(-2)z_7/t). (1) The physical crossing is its ORIGINAL finite input/output block, with kappa retained. This is the proved Gaussian-absorbed complete kernel; no original Gaussian was deleted from a separated sector. Expand the three factors with indices (i,j),(r,k),(h,l), respectively, each nonnegative pair having sum<N. One term has input demands a=j+r, b=i, output degrees c=r+k-h, e=h+l, t exponent p=i+j-k-l, c+e-a-b=-p. (2) In particular input powers are nonpositive, second-output degree is at most d, both output degrees are at most d, and -2d<=p<=d. For any nonzero sampling root t_0, (1/N)sum_(j=0)^d K(t_0 Q^j) =CT_t K+t_0^(-N)[t^(-N)]K. (3) There is exactly one possible alias. This identity is an equality of the COMPLETE finite Laurent kernel before any source split. ## 2. A source-flat adaptive family, including exact resonance Let A be an independent scalar source parameter. Choose the algebraic sampling root by t_0^(-N)=z_1^(-N)-A z_7^(-N). (4) The normalized symmetric root average is independent of which Nth root is chosen. Equations (3)--(4) show its two errors explicitly: z_1^(-N)[t^(-N)]K-A z_7^(-N)[t^(-N)]K. (5) The FIRST term demands incoming second index at least N, since K has no positive powers of z_1. The original finite INPUT space kills it. The SECOND term has negative second-output degree, since K has z_7 degree at most d. The original finite OUTPUT block kills it. Therefore the adaptive average has EXACTLY the original finite crossing operator, for EVERY A, not merely its closed trace. This is stronger than the earlier total-degree alias argument. The root t_0 has overall head degree one, so that argument alone would not apply. The two physical index walls in (5) are the replacement. No alias deletion is asserted for a separately continued full-Psi homogeneous/current sector. The symmetric average is linear in t_0^(-N). It consequently extends regularly across z_1^(-N)-A z_7^(-N)=0, even though the individual sample points then go to infinity. One first takes the COMPLETE symmetric average and the original finite block, not a value of a single divergent sample. In the all-homogeneous one-Psi field, the full-turn multiplier is (z_7/z_1)^N[1-(z_1/t_0)^N]=A. (6) Thus A=1 is precisely its exact Fourier resonance. It is reached inside an actual source-flat family, rather than by imposing A=1 inside the old co-source. The normalized finite-orbit/Fourier formula then has zero FINAL closure current and its explicitly known nonzero resonant coefficient. The pre-existing B/R currents must still be kept unless a further proved source map removes them. The stronger independent external-frame construction in [the balanced crossing theorem](actual_balanced_fourier_crossing_kernel.md) also balances all three B/R sources. That theorem is compatible with the present head-adaptive source map; it is not assumed in its proof. ## 3. Both signs and whole original words At complete color x=-q^(-1), the exact balanced relation is R_-=P overline(R_+)P, with the common scalar conjugated to kappa^(-1). Apply this relation to the COMPLETE polynomial source, with opposite root Q^(-1) and the formal two heads exchanged. Its adaptive negative sampling is t_(0,-)^(-N)=z_0^(-N)-A z_6^(-N). (7) The errors now demand first INPUT index at least N or have negative first OUTPUT degree. Both are removed by the SAME original physical finite blocks. Hence any number of crossings in ANY original signed braid or plat may be replaced simultaneously. Their finite matrices agree entrywise, and the original cups/caps, pivot, marked row, Cartan and zero-framing lines are unchanged. Arbitrary bridge count is allowed. The unsplit cyclic inhomogeneous equation The COMPLETE state has a concrete cyclic connection, not only the one-function homogeneous equation. Put u_0=t/z_1, v_0=x^(-1)t/z_0, a=x^(-1)z_7/z_6, c=z_6/z_0, w=x^(-1)z_6/t, B_0(t)=B_N(u_0,v_0), F(t)=B_N(a,a w)R_N(c,w), Y(t)=B_0(t)F(t)=K(t), D_0=1-u_0^N+v_0^N, H_pair=D_B R_N(c,w)+a D_R B_N(a,Qa w). (10) At A=1 the left side vanishes. Since the whole original state is regular on this chart, differentiating the ACTUAL source family gives Y|_(A=1)=-d_A(G_A eta)|_(A=1). (11) Thus the entire resonant finite state is fixed by the first normal jet of its explicit unsplit source, with jet order ONE independent of N. This is a source identity, not an instruction to divide by 1-A and separately evaluate a vanishing numerator. For an explicit homogeneous coefficient choose a holomorphic branch omega=A^(1/N) near one and the periodic cyclic gauge g_j(A), g_0=1, b(t_j)g_(j-1)=omega g_j. All b(t_j) are nonzero at resonance. Write tildeY_j=Y_j/g_j and tildeeta_j=eta_j/g_j. Averaging their equation yields mean(tildeeta)=(1-omega)mean(tildeY). Consequently its zero-clock homogeneous projection coefficient is mean(tildeY)|_(A=1) =-N*d_A mean(tildeeta)|_(A=1). (12) The normalized homogeneous vector g_j at resonance is the actual Fermat/cyclic full-Psi vector with the independently fixed Fourier normalizer. Equation (12) constructs its comparison coefficient from the original source, rather than assuming that coefficient exists or is nonzero. Its possible vanishing and its geometric overlap after exterior contraction still have to be checked. For a fixed word with m internal orbit variables, apply (10) to each complete tensor factor before the original finite contraction. The whole original period is thereby a mixed FIRST normal derivative in each of m independent source parameters at their Fermat values. The required jet order depends on the fixed word, not on N. These derivatives include the moving root and all source terms; differentiating only a homogeneous block would not be the same operation. ## 6. Scope The adaptive sampling and normal-source formulas are exact, source preserving and valid for all original signed finite words. They close an actual internal circle on its resonant algebraic multisection and give a prescribed normal-jet pointing there. Neither the one-dimensional homogeneous space nor its nonzero local Fourier vector by itself proves survival of the final geometric period. title: The genuine adjacent observable algebra and its macroscopic source filtration

# The genuine adjacent observable algebra and its macroscopic source filtration 29 October 2026. Two ACTUAL adjacent interval Casimirs already generate the full matrix algebra on the complete three-head source multiplicity. This narrows the older arbitrary-coupon quotient obstruction to a small physical moment-map algebra. Its proof is constructive and retains the original nilpotent normal source. The associated filtration is equally important: bounded-degree source tests see zero until an integer traversal of length N-1. A single original crossing has precisely that macroscopic observable degree. Thus full matrix generation does not disprove a filtered or microlocal geometric reduction, and low-degree source-null identities do not by themselves control its norm. ## 1. Original matrices, sources and charts Let N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, rho=q-q^(-1). On the COMPLETE original W=(V tensor V)_(degree d), use e_j=|j,d-j>. The actual interval Casimirs A=Omega12 and B=Omega23, in the left highest chart, are \[ A_{j,j}=q+q^{-1}-q(1-Q^j)^2-q^{-1}(1-Q^{j+1})^2, \qquad A_{j-1,j}=A_{j,j-1}=-(1-Q^j)^2, 	ag{1} \] \[ Be_j=c_je_j+b_je_{j-1},\qquad c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1},\quad b_j=Q^j+Q^{-j}-2. 	ag{2} \] All off-diagonal coefficients in (1) are nonzero. Put c*=q+q^(-1). The ORIGINAL cup and ordinary cap are \[ p_j=Nx^{j-d},\qquad \ell_j=x^{-j}Q^{-j}/N=x^j/N. \] The complete anti-Pascal chart J satisfies the exact source identities \[ JB=AJ,\quad JAJ^{-1}=B^{\mathsf T},\quad Jp=Nx^{-d}e_d,\quad \ell J^{-1}=(x^d/N)e_0^{\mathsf T}. 	ag{3} \] These are the original coproduct and actual cap identities from [the complete source theorem](actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md), not a semisimple replacement. In particular all N multiplicities, both members of every colliding Casimir pair, and even levels remain. ## 2. A tame nilpotent source operator generates all channels The monic characteristic polynomial of A is \[ \mathcal P_N(z)=\prod_{j=0}^d(z-c_j)=2T_N(z/2)+2. \] Its roots have multiplicity two, except the simple root -2 when N is odd. At N=2 it is z^2, so the following construction also applies. The irreducible Jacobi matrix A has cyclic endpoint vectors; hence its minimal polynomial is this full degree-N polynomial. Set Q0(z)=P_N(z)/(z-c*)^2. Define the explicit degree-d observable \[ \Xi_0(A)= rac{(A-c*)Q_0(A)}{Q_0(c*)}. \] Then \[  oxed{\displaystyle \Xi_0(A)=	heta p\ell,\qquad 	heta=(-1)^Nho^2
e0.} 	ag{4} \] Here is a proof not assuming a Jordan basis. At all other Casimir nodes the polynomial has the full required vanishing multiplicity. At c* it has value 0 and derivative 1. The eigenspace of an irreducible Jacobi matrix is one-dimensional, so its range is the original eigenline Cp and its row is the original eigenrow Cell. The coefficient is fixed by its (0,d) entry. Lower matrix powers cannot connect d to 0, and \[ (A^d)_{0,d}=\prod_{j=1}^d[-(1-Q^j)^2]=(-1)^dN^2. \] The elementary Chebyshev differential equation at the double zero gives Q0(c*)=N^2/(4-c*^2)=-N^2/rho^2. Since p0 ell_d=1, the coefficient in (4) is theta. This proves its normalization, including the exceptional N=2 case. In the original positive physical norm, \[ \|\Xi_0(A)\|_{m op}=N|ho|^2\leq4\pi^2/N. 	ag{5} \] Indeed ||p||^2=N^3 and ||ell||^2=1/N. This rank-one normal source is polynomially controlled; it is not an exponentially conditioned projector. It is nonzero even though it is square-zero, because ell p=0. For 0<=r,s<=d, \[ B^r\Xi_0(A)B^s=	heta(B^rp)(\ell B^s). 	ag{6} \] By (3), the columns B^r p are a basis: their J images are a nonzero constant times A^r e_d, which are triangular endpoint Krylov columns. The rows ell B^s are also a basis, since their products with J^(-1) are a nonzero constant times e0^T A^s. Therefore the N^2 operators in (6) are a basis of End(W). In particular \[  oxed{\displaystyle \mathbb C\langle A,Bangle =\operatorname{Mat}_N(\mathbb C).} 	ag{7} \] No arbitrary Borel-relative matrix coupon is needed for (7): A and B are the two actual adjacent interval observables. ## 3. Consequence for an exact positive or invariant quotient Suppose a linear quotient q0:W->H is compatible with these two observables: q0 A=A' q0 and q0 B=B' q0. Its kernel is invariant under (7), and is therefore either 0 or all of W. If it preserves the original source and its inserted observable values it cannot be the zero quotient, since \[ \ell B^d p=(-1)^dN^2
e0. 	ag{8} \] Thus it is injective. Equivalently, a positive semidefinite packet Gram whose nullspace is invariant under BOTH actual observables cannot remove a source channel: its nullspace is 0 or it kills the entire original source representation. A multiplicative quotient imposing a nonzero relation on this actual observable algebra is likewise impossible while retaining all source insertions. In particular setting the rank-one normal (4) to zero generates the whole matrix ideal by (6). This is a restriction on an EXACT observable-compatible quotient, not a no-go theorem for a nonmultiplicative Ward pushforward, a current-complex reduction, or a geometric comparison after taking semiclassical asymptotics. Nor does it preclude a faithful embedding of W into a larger positive angle space satisfying additional edge constraints. Such an embedding need not be a smaller quotient of this observable representation. The same statement applies to a reflected double IF both copies of the actual observable algebra are retained independently: (7) then gives the full matrix algebra on W tensor conjugate(W). It is not asserted for a construction that retains only synchronous diagonal braid action and no independent copy observables. ## 4. The exact source filtration: degree N-1 is essential Define \[ \mathcal F_m=\operatorname{span}\{p,Bp,\ldots,B^mp\}, \qquad0\leq m\leq d. \] The endpoint Jacobi calculation and (3) give EXACTLY \[ J\mathcal F_m=\operatorname{span}\{e_{d-m},\ldots,e_d\}, \quad\dim\mathcal F_m=m+1, \quad A\mathcal F_m\subset\mathcal F_m, \quad B\mathcal F_m\subset\mathcal F_{m+1}. 	ag{9} \] The A statement uses JAJ^(-1)=B^T, which is LOWER bidiagonal, and therefore preserves the displayed terminal coordinate subspace. Also \[ \ell|_{\mathcal F_{d-1}}=0,\qquad \ell B^m p=0\ (m<d),\qquad \ell B^d p=(-1)^dN^2. 	ag{10} \] More generally EVERY mixed word with fewer than d occurrences of B has zero original pairing ell w(A,B)p, independently of the number of A factors. In the J chart each B can lower the integer index by at most one, each A preserves or raises it, and the source travels from d to 0. Thus there is no cyclic shortcut. At the first detected degree the complete associated-graded source is explicit. For any nonnegative integers a0,...,ad, \[  oxed{\displaystyle \ell A^{a_0}B A^{a_1}B\cdots B A^{a_d}p =(-1)^dN^2\prod_{j=0}^d c_j^{a_j}.} 	ag{11} \] With exactly d lowering opportunities, every B must use its lowering Jacobi entry and every A its diagonal entry. This proves (11) as a unique finite path, with all original source constants cancelling as (Nx^(-d))(x^d/N)=1. In particular, for N>=3 and 1<=r<=d-1, \[ \ell B^{d-r}(A-c*)B^rp =(-1)^dN^2(c_r-c*)
e0. 	ag{12} \] The local cup relation (A-c*)p=0 therefore cannot be reimposed after an arbitrary legitimate exterior. Its first detectable exterior has macroscopic observable degree, not bounded degree. For the selected normal (4), the exact factorization (6) implies that an exterior on BOTH sides needs at least d B occurrences on each side before the original scalar can detect it. Its retained response is nevertheless explicitly local, rather than an unspecified lost normal direction. For ANY allowed exteriors U,V, \[ \ell U\Xi_0(A)Vp=	heta(\ell Up)(\ell Vp). 	ag{12a} \] This is the actual cup--cap rank-one surgery (4), with its known normalization; it does not define a metric from an unknown closed period. The individual factors still require their own estimates. With r such normals the exact correction is \(\ell U_0\Xi_0U_1\cdots\Xi_0U_rp =	heta^r\prod_{j=0}^r(\ell U_jp)\). All factors are in the SAME original cap/cup normalization; converting them to separately normalized knot periods retains their individual known external lines. No inequality between their volumes is implied. ## 5. A fixed braid already reaches the macroscopic degree This degree distinction is not permission to ignore it for fixed knot diagrams. The actual adjacent crossing is R23=kappa r_N(B), a polynomial of degree<N. Its coefficient at B^d has EXACT modulus N^(-2): \[  oxed{\displaystyle [B^d]R_{23}= rac{\kappa(-1)^d x^{-d}}{N^2}.} 	ag{13} \] To prove it directly from the original crossing, highest-chart extraction forces one finite transfer and gives (R23 p)_j=kappa p_j F_(d-j). Therefore \[ \ell R_{23}p=\kappa x^{-d} \sum_{k=0}^d Q^{k+1}F_k=\kappa x^{-d}. 	ag{14} \] The last sum telescopes, Q^(k+1)F_k=F_k-F_(k+1), with F_N=0. All lower polynomial degrees pair to zero by (10), proving (13). In particular the original crossing really has degree d, at every level, and its first detected source coefficient is polynomially large rather than exponentially suppressed. A fixed number of actual crossings can therefore expose the normal even though low-degree observable tests cannot. From (12a),(14), \[ \ell R_{23}\Xi_0(A)R_{23}p =	heta\kappa^2x^{-2d}=	heta x^{-d}
e0, 	ag{14a} \] of exact modulus |rho|^2. This is a polynomial-sized normal current between TWO original crossings. It must not be set to zero in an exact source identity, but it is compatible with a filtered construction that explicitly retains and estimates polynomial normal counterterms. These statements concern the specified complete source sector; no rank-one formula is asserted on an unrestricted larger multiplicity space without its actual charge projector. For any polynomial f of degree<d, (14) also gives the elementary operator-norm separation \[ \|R_{23}-f(B)\|_{m op}\geq1/N, 	ag{15} \] since the original source has dual product ||ell|| ||p||=N. This does not preclude a polynomial-error approximation at a specified order or an exponentially normalized upper comparison. It does show that fixed-degree truncation does not preserve even the first nonzero original source value automatically. The viable filtered alternative must therefore state how its fixed-degree Ward equations act on these degree-N crossing packets, including the retained normal source and the norm of the resulting counterterms. Low-degree tests against the bare cup are identically zero, so they cannot alone certify a nonzero geometric component or a polynomial-cost positive reduction. No sharp global energy estimate or obstruction to a properly controlled microlocal quotient follows from (7) alone. ## 6. Original braid algebra at prime levels For completeness there is an actual-word strengthening along every prime level. At an odd prime N, the nodal eigenvalues nu_j=(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)] coincide only at the paired indices j+l=d. Indeed equality implies N divides (j-l)(j+l+1); for distinct indices primality forces j+l+1=N. At every double Casimir node r_N' is nonzero. Finite Hermite interpolation therefore recovers A as a polynomial in R12, and B as the same polynomial in R23. Hence \[ \mathbb C\langle R_{12},R_{23}angle=\operatorname{Mat}_N \quad	ext{for every prime }N. 	ag{16} \] N=2 has a single double node and nonzero derivative, so it also satisfies (16). For composite levels additional braid-phase coincidences can occur; (16) is not asserted there. The all-level observable statement (7) has no such restriction. The interpolation degrees and inverse norms in (16) are not claimed uniform or tame. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_adjacent_observable_source_filtration.py) reconstructs the original coproduct Casimir and physical highest intertwiner, checks the normal operator and full Krylov bases, all-level filtrations and source values, and the literal full-Cartan crossing coefficient. It does not infer a geometric norm from algebra dimension or from a finite numerical rank fit. title: Exact adjacent-twist character coupling with its physical source
text: # Exact adjacent-twist character coupling with its physical source 28 October 2026. Adjacent original twist blocks have an exact coupled quantum-character algebra, not independent spectral phases. The identities below give a denominator-free braid recursion, fix the nearest-neighbor spectral phase ratios, and impose a **strict integer spectral window** on the original generic-meridian family. (4) No division by delta, rho, a clock determinant, or a nilpotent face is needed to state (3)--(4). Here is a reproducible algebraic proof, separate from finite-level numerical checks. Take independent quantum tori Z_i S_i=q^2S_i Z_i, and independent formal meridians M_i. Substitute K_i=-M_i q^(-1)Z_i^(-1), F_i=S_i(1-q^2 Z_i), Ecal_i=S_i^(-1)(M_i Z_i^(-1)-M_i^(-1)). A,B,C,D have respectively 14,14,62,34 Laurent terms before those identities are expanded. This is an exact generic-q polynomial certificate, not a sample at roots or an imported q-Racah theorem. It applies to the original finite nilpotent heads too. Indeed the single-head algebra with fixed Casimir has normal forms K^aF^b and K^aEcal^c; the mixed product FEcal is its fixed nonzero Laurent polynomial in K. The torus realization (5) is faithful on those normal forms: distinct F/Ecal degrees have distinct S powers, and the remaining nonzero Laurent factor cannot kill a Laurent polynomial in Z. Thus the certified identities hold in that central quantum-group quotient and then in its finite-head representations. This argument does not add the generic cyclic E endpoint to the original module. ## 3. Taking its ordered traces gives the exact identities, for equal colors (a_1=a_2=a_3=a, alpha=beta=gamma=a^2+aD), Ad(R_12):(A,B,C) -> (A,q alpha-qBA-q^2C,B), Ad(R_23):(A,B,C) -> (C,B,q alpha-qCB-q^2A). The complete adjacent-block transport is B_(t+1)=-q B_t A-q^2 B_(t-1)+q alpha, B_0=B, B_(-1)=C. (7) This formula holds at every signed integer t and every N, with the whole physical boundary and original source unchanged. It retains the q-phase; replacing it by a real modulus recurrence is not valid. On the genuine generic-meridian family the first pair has distinct Casimir nodes and original eigenvalues c_j(Y)=q^(-1)YQ^(-j)+qY^(-1)Q^j, lambda_j(Y)=nu_jY^(-j), nu_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j+1)), 0<=j<N. (8) The normalized physical fusion/projector formulas in [the factorial-frame theorem](actual_twist_block_factorial_frame_bound.md) realize these operators with their actual normalizers. In particular the two homogeneous multipliers of (7) at A=c_j(Y) are -Q^(j+1)Y^(-1)=lambda_(j+1)/lambda_j, -Q^(-j)Y=lambda_(j-1)/lambda_j. (9) These are precisely the neighboring ratios of the ORIGINAL twist phases, not independently selected semiclassical characters. ## 4. A strict spectral window, rather than a cyclic replacement Let E_i(Y) denote the meromorphic actual pair-Casimir projectors, extended by the third head. For i!=j, project (7) between E_i and E_j. The central forcing disappears, and its scalar characteristic equation is (lambda_i/lambda_j)^2 +q c_j(Y)(lambda_i/lambda_j)+q^2=0. By (9), equality as a meromorphic function of Y forces the exponent of Y in lambda_i/lambda_j to be +1 or -1. Therefore E_i(Y) B E_j(Y)=0 unless i=j or i=j+1 or i=j-1 (10) as INTEGER indices in [0,N-1]. For N>=3 the apparent cyclic neighbor (0,N-1) is excluded. Casimir nodes alone are cyclic, but the original braiding eigenvalues (8) have a nontrivial endpoint norm character; discarding it would incorrectly allow that extra edge. The diagonal is fixed as well: (delta+c_j(Y)) E_j B E_j=E_j alpha E_j. (11) This follows from Ad(R_12)C=B and the diagonal part of (6). It is stated without dividing at a zero of the factor on the left. Equations (10)--(11) are the actual finite three-term spectral coupling underlying a q-Racah overlap. They remain identities of whole meromorphic germs at completeness; the colliding projectors cannot be independently evaluated or replaced by a semisimple root basis. For an adjacent sequence R_12^ell R_23^m, its exact kernel is obtained by composing the actual C_T E_i C_T^(-1) projector matrices with their lambda_i^ell and lambda_j^m factors, then applying the original co-source. Formula (10) supplies the coupling recurrence rather than treating those spectral labels as independent or modulo N. It does not yet evaluate the resulting multidimensional contour. ## 5. The original cup port gives the parabolic total character At completeness let p be the ORIGINAL cup on heads 1,2. Its actual Hopf identities E_tot p=F_tot p=0 and K_tot p=p imply that both two-head coproduct triangular matrices are identity on p. Consequently (D+2I)(p tensor v)=0 for EVERY third-head vector v. (12) Every actual word in R_12 and R_23 commutes with D, so (12) remains true on the entire transported cup-generated subspace. Spectator heads may be included. An original ordinary cap and full marked row can be left untouched: inserting D+2 into that original whole network gives zero by (12), with no change of co-source or division by a knot period. This is a forward source restriction, not an assertion that the unrestricted marked row is an invariant covector. One may NOT impose D=-2 on an arbitrary three-head port which has already interacted with outside heads. At such a port the full D in (2)--(7) must be retained and sewn to its actual exterior source. On a commutative principal chart, (4) at a_i=-2 becomes the usual four-punctured character cubic. On the actual cup slice D=-2 it is A^2+B^2+C^2+ABC-8(A+B+C)+28=0, (X+Y+Z)^2+XYZ=0, X=A-2,Y=B-2,Z=C-2. (13) This identifies the coupled trace support and its original parabolic source. It does not establish that the original spectral cycle has a nonzero intersection with its geometric place, or bound every complex boundary phase by knot volume. ## 6. Audit and remaining analytic problem python3 experiments/audit_actual_adjacent_twist_character.py The certificate checks nine generic Laurent identities with three independent formal meridians, including the cubic, centrality and both ordered Hurwitz trace reductions. Separate actual finite matrices test complete and generic M, four iterates of (7), and the original cup restriction with the FULL marked four-head plat closure. Both level parities and N=2 are included. [Saved results](../experiments/actual_adjacent_twist_character_results.json). What remains is an analytic/source theorem for the **joint** q-Racah overlap period: retain (8)--(11), its endpoint and meridian currents, and prove a contour bound or nonzero geometric coefficient after full closure. Character support and correct local phase ratios alone do not prove that estimate. No sharp-volume conclusion is claimed here. ## 7. A specific obstruction to leaving the spectral contour real At completeness the original spectral nodes are c_j(1)=2cos((2j+1)pi/N), and their real-angle limit lies in [-2,2]. On a regular physical classical chart, A is the actual trace of the product of its two based parabolic meridians, by (1). A nontrivial element in a discrete faithful hyperbolic manifold group cannot have real trace strictly between -2 and 2: such a matrix is elliptic, whereas the manifold's deck group acts freely and discretely on hyperbolic space. Thus a regular discrete-faithful pair-product trace cannot occur in the interior of this real spectral interval. A loxodromic pair product requires either a nonreal trace or a real trace outside that interval. Parabolic/central pair products belong to the turning values +/-2 and need their own retained boundary analysis. Consequently a proposed real-spectral-angle stationary proof cannot simply identify its real optimizer with a regular geometric pair whose product is loxodromic. The q-Racah spectral variable must undergo a complex deformation, or one must perform another actual polarization change with its source. This criterion is local and applies at any width; it is not a knot census or a disproof of a complex-contour route. Real eigenvalues of a nonnormal finite Casimir do not exclude complex principal characters in the original physical polarization. The claim concerns leaving THIS diagonal spectral contour real. This is why the coupled trace identities above still do not turn the local block bound into a sharp volume estimate: the actual complex spectral contour and its endpoint/normal source currents remain to be transported and bounded. They have not been selected by the algebraic cubic alone.

title: The normalization clock disk is not uniformly tame on the physical head
text: # The normalization clock disk is not uniformly tame on the physical head 29 October 2026. The selected original normalization scalar has a tame clock disk, but its ALL-INPUT physical operator does not. The distinction can be proved at the first normal jet, with the actual sources and full Cartan factor retained. This gives an explicit physical Ward current which a gluing theorem has to cancel coherently. The result does not assert exponential growth of a closed knot scalar, or failure of the source-specific shrinking-arc construction. It rules out promoting its selected scalar estimate to a uniform physical-head operator estimate. ## 1. The literal open-head normalization operator Let N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, F_j=(Q;Q)_j, s_j=|F_j|, and kappa=q^(d^2/2). Let R be the FULL original positive crossing on the physical pair degree-d block W, and set L=kappa^(-1)R. Keep the original cup and ordinary cap. The all-input cup slide exposes the operator \[ \mathcal C_N(t)=(\ell_{12}\otimes I_3) (I_1\otimes R^2)t^{J_2}(I_1\otimes p_{23}), \qquad J|a\rangle=a|a\rangle. \] Here R^2 acts on the degree-d subspace of the last physical pair; the full original physical crossings restrict to this block and the first head is its untouched spectator. This is the same actual local normalization slot as in [the mesoscopic-current theorem](actual_mesoscopic_clock_packet_currents.md#4-why-the-scalar-packet-does-not-already-solve-physical-gluing). The remaining physical input is arbitrary. Integer degree makes the operator diagonal, with EXACT entries \[ C_a(t)=x^{-a}Q^{-a}\sum_{n=0}^d(L^2)_{d-a,n}(xt)^n. \tag{1} \] Indeed the three factors are the cup coefficient N x^(n-d), the original crossing square kappa^2(L^2)_(d-a,n), and the cap x^(-a)Q^(-a)/N. The identity kappa^2=x^d gives (1). The apparent all-input source freedom is therefore fixed, not chosen by a favorable scalar period. At t=1 every entry is x^d=kappa^2. Write u(t)_j=(xt)^j and v(t)=L^2u(t). Because x^2=Q^(-1), \[ C_a(t)=x^a v_{d-a}(t),\qquad \max_a|C_a'(1)|=\|v'(1)\|_\infty. \tag{2} \] ## 2. The exact finite Ward register before the second crossing For 0<=i<=d define \[ D_i^+(s)=F_i^2\sum_{b=0}^i \frac{Q^{b^2}s^b}{F_{i-b}F_b^2}. \] Let D_i^-(s) denote the same polynomial with Q replaced by Q^(-1). All factorial indices are below N. Finite Durfee convolution gives D_i^+(1)=D_i^-(1)=1. Directly from the original crossing entries, \[ \boxed{\displaystyle (Lu(t))_i=x^i t^d D_i^-(1/t).} \tag{3} \] For clarity, the intermediate finite coefficient is \[ (Lu(t))_i=x^{-i}Q^{i(d-i)}t^{d-i}F_i^2 \sum_{k=0}^i\frac{(-1)^kQ^{k(k-1)/2}t^k}{F_kF_{i-k}^2}. \] Replace k by i-b and use (Q^(-1);Q^(-1))_b=(-1)^b Q^(-b(b+1)/2)F_b to obtain (3). This is an all-port factorial identity, not an adjoint/unitarity claim. The finite polynomials obey \[ D_i^+(s)=(1+Q-2Q^i+Q^{2i-1}s)D_{i-1}^+(s) -Q(1-Q^{i-1})^2D_{i-2}^+(s). \tag{4} \] One elementary derivation uses formal series through degree d: U(z)=sum z^k/F_k has U(Qz)=(1-z)U(z), and W(z)=sum Q^(b^2)s^b z^b/F_b^2 satisfies W(z)-2W(Qz)+(1-sQz)W(Q^2z)=0. Compare coefficients of U(z)W(z). This proves (4) at the root without using any denominator F_N. Let P_i be the ORIGINAL Green register, \[ P_0=1,\qquad P_i=(1-Q^i)^2P_{i-1}+Q^i. \] Differentiating (4) at s=1 and factoring the resulting first difference gives the exact normal current \[ (D_i^+)'(1)-(D_{i-1}^+)'(1)=Q^iP_{i-1}. \tag{5} \] The base case is (D1^+)'(1)=Q. Equivalently, set w=Lu'(1); (3) gives w_i=x^i[d-(D_i^-)'(1)]. Therefore \[ \boxed{\displaystyle x^{-i}w_i-x^{-(i-1)}w_{i-1} =-Q^{-i}\overline{P_{i-1}},\quad1\leq i\leq d.} \tag{6} \] This is the retained physical normal current. It is not zero at a normalization leaf merely because its value at t=1 is a scalar. ## 3. The source endpoint forces a large interior current The all-parity ORIGINAL source endpoint has the independently derived quadratic-Gaussian asymptotic \[ P_d=N^{3/2}\exp\!\left[i\pi\left(\frac14-\frac N{12} +\frac1{4N}\right)\right]+O(\sqrt N). \tag{7} \] Its proof retains the complete pivotal derivative source, including the odd simple node: [the endpoint Gaussian theorem](actual_normalization_endpoint_gaussian_asymptotic.md). In particular |P_d|>=c N^(3/2) for all sufficiently large N. No volume asymptotic or fitted saddle branch is assumed. The exact backward Green identity from [the terminal capacity proof](actual_terminal_green_capacity_bound.md) is \[ P_t=F_t^2\left(\frac{P_d}{N^2} -\sum_{b=t+1}^d\frac{Q^b}{F_b^2}\right). \tag{8} \] Choose i nearest 5N/6, with 1<=i<=d, and t=i-1. For large N, s_t>N. The sine-factorial sequence increases up to its high peak and then decreases to s_d=N. Consequently s_b>=N for every b>t, so the tail in (8) has absolute value at most1/N. It follows from (7) that \[ |P_{i-1}|\geq c_1 N^{-1/2}s_{i-1}^2. \tag{9} \] Put J(s)=integral_0^s log(2sin(pi*u))du. Uniform sine-factorial asymptotics give \[ \log|P_{i-1}|\geq\frac{v_3}{\pi}N-O(\log N), \tag{10} \] since J has maximum v3/(2pi) at 5/6, where v3 is the regular ideal tetrahedron volume. The lower bound is a coherent source result: the complex tail in (8) is estimated only AFTER the actual nonzero endpoint has been evaluated. ## 4. A quantitative all-input obstruction after the second crossing The literal original NEGATIVE crossing supplies \[ |(L^{-1})_{r,j}|= \begin{cases} \displaystyle\frac{N^2}{s_r^2s_j^2s_{d-r-j}},&r+j\leq d,\\ 0,&r+j>d. \end{cases} \tag{11} \] No conjugate-transpose inverse is used. Define the exact row mass B_r=sum_j |(L^(-1))_(r,j)|. Since w=L^(-1)v'(1), (6) implies the FINITE inequality \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \max_{a\geq i-1}|C_a'(1)| \geq\frac{|P_{i-1}|}{B_i+B_{i-1}}.} \tag{12} \] The color restriction follows from the two strict supports in (11), not from an imposed geometric color. It is enough to control the operator on its upper sixth of physical inputs. The global factorial minimum is log s_j>=-N v3/(2pi)-O(log N), and for r=i or i-1, log s_r^2=N v3/pi+O(log N). Hence (11) gives \[ \log(B_i+B_{i-1})\leq N\left(-\frac{v_3}{\pi}+\frac{3v_3}{2\pi}\right)+O(\log N) =\frac{v_3}{2\pi}N+O(\log N). \] Combining this with (10) proves a positive explicit exponent: \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\max_a|C_a'(1)| \geq\gamma:=\frac{v_3}{2\pi}>0.} \tag{13} \] The numerical value gamma is about0.16153. It is a rigorous LOWER bound, not the claimed exact jet exponent. Every C_a is a polynomial. Cauchy's derivative inequality now gives, for EVERY fixed c>0, \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \liminf_N\frac1N\log \sup_{|t-1|\leq c/N}\|\mathcal C_N(t)\|_{\rm op} \geq\gamma>0.} \tag{14} \] The same assertion holds for any disk radius r_N<=1 with log(1/r_N)=o(N). It is therefore not repaired by choosing a smaller polynomial clock disk. This is a statement about the ALL-INPUT physical operator, not about the selected scalar row. This particular obstruction is independent of a choice of positive inner product on the SAME physical input/output head. The C_a(t) are the actual eigenvalues of the diagonal operator, so every such operator norm is at least max_a|C_a(t)|, even for N- and t-dependent metrics. A change between DIFFERENT input and output metrics has additional interfaces and is not covered by that observation. ## 5. The missing moment constraint is an actual normal Ward defect For a=d the original source packet is still C_d(t)=x^(-d)P_N(t), in the notation of the mesoscopic-current theorem. Its first derivative is x^(-d)Q conjugate(P_d-1), polynomial in N; the whole selected c/N disk is polynomially bounded by the original clock-disk proof. There is no contradiction with (13): the large normal response occupies other physical inputs. It can also be stated directly as a failure of the untwisted Hopf moment condition. The original single-head F acts by F|a>=(1-Q^(a+1))|a+1>. Therefore \[ [F,\mathcal C_N'(1)]|a\rangle =(1-Q^{a+1})(C_a'(1)-C_{a+1}'(1))|a+1\rangle. \tag{15} \] The terminal C_d' is polynomial, while (13) is exponential. Telescoping the physical differences and using |1-Q^(a+1)|>=4/N proves \[ \liminf_N N^{-1}\log\|[F,\mathcal C_N'(1)]\|_{\rm op} \geq\gamma. \tag{16} \] The same holds for Ecal, whose relevant coefficient magnitudes agree. Thus a polynomial-norm same-head correction cannot make this jet an intertwiner: its commutator would have to cancel (16). The required normal current is explicitly (5)--(6), not an unproved abstract error. The exact all-input tensor Ward identity identifies the omitted two-color insertion more directly. Put S=I tensor p and A_cap=ell tensor I, and let U=I tensor R_phys^2 act on the FULL physical pair space, not only its degree-d block. Define \[ \mathcal J_F(t)=A_{\rm cap}U K_1^{-1}F_2 t^{J_2}S,\qquad \mathcal J_E(t)=A_{\rm cap}U E_{{\rm cal},2}t^{J_2}K_3S. \] The actual coproduct and cup/cap intertwinings give \[ [F,\mathcal C_N(t)]=(1-t)\mathcal J_F(t),\qquad [E_{\rm cal},\mathcal C_N(t)]=(1-t^{-1})\mathcal J_E(t). \tag{17} \] Indeed only the middle-head term in the total coproduct fails to commute with t^(J2). In particular [F,C_N'(1)]=-J_F(1) and [Ecal,C_N'(1)]=J_E(1). The F insertion goes through pair degree d+1 and the E insertion through degree d-1. Replacing either by a shift of the recording register inside the degree-d scalar packet would omit that sector. Equations (16)--(17) prove that these ACTUAL physical normal-current operators have exponential norm; no polynomial operator correction may simply erase them. A full exterior may cancel it with neighboring clock/crossing currents or may retain a source projection excluding these inputs. Such a cancellation must be shown in its actual tensor slot, with the marked source unchanged. Replacing (1) by the selected value C_d(t), imposing a lowest-color projection on an internal head, or declaring the clock insertion a Hopf map omits the defect above. This proves the requested uniform physical operator extension FALSE. It leaves a source-compatible correlated/mesoscopic gluing theorem open. Tensoring a spectator identity does not change the lower bound; no claim about a general correlated whole-knot scalar or a one-dimensional unit-circle arc follows solely from the disk inequality (14). [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_all_input_normalization_clock_obstruction.py) checks the original full R/cup/cap operator, the finite Ward recurrence, the exact derivative current, literal inverse row masses, and finite inequality (12). The endpoint Gaussian input has its separate all-level proof and original-source audit. Fresh replay: PASS twelve literal all-input physical normalization operators at N=2,...,12,14, their exact root Ward jets and Hopf commutators; ten complete complex current/lower-bound families through N=96. Numerical jet rates are recorded only as diagnostics, not used to infer the positive lower exponent (13).

title: Full first-normal bounds for all supported Racah partners
text: # Full first-normal bounds for all supported Racah partners 29 October 2026. This proves a uniform polynomial relative bound for the ACTUAL first generic-q normal at every one of the 64 reflected branches of a supported folded sextuple. The new step is a positive finite presentation of the full generic source on face-supported branches, including branches whose seven-factorial formula has a live `[2N]` current. The already proved Fourier partner involution and exact first- normal Ward equation then cover the remaining branches. Every fixed generic normal order is controlled on the face-supported branches. The general 64-branch conclusion is FIRST ORDER ONLY. No completed physical recoupling norm or global volume equality follows merely from this local scalar theorem. ## 1. Statement and source convention Fix `N>=3`, `D=N-1`, `q=exp(pi i/N)`, and integer folded labels `j=(a,b,c,d,e,f)` in `[0,D/2]`, with all four face sums at least `D`. Use the SAME actual generic seven-factorial sum and normalization as in [the reciprocal source theorem](actual_racah_partner_reflection_identity.md): K_B(zeta)=[N]^2 S_B(zeta)^2 product_faces Delta_B^2, k(B)=D_log(zeta) K_B(q). Here B records any subset of the six changes `j -> D-j`. The original actual source prefactors, peripheral factors and marking are not changed. The proved root-value identity gives `K_B(q)=W_N^2>0` for all branches. There is an absolute constant C such that max_B |k(B)| <= C N^2(1+log N) W_N^2. (1) The local analytic square root positive at q, and the first inverse jets of K and its square root, have corresponding relative bounds. Every implicit constant below is independent of the supported labels, level parity and compositeness. A set of high bits is called face-supported if it is contained in one of the four faces (a,b,e), (c,d,e), (a,d,f), (b,c,f). For every such branch, and every fixed r, the stronger conclusion is |D_log(zeta)^r K_B(q)| <= C_r N^(c_r) W_N^2, (2) with the analogous local square-root and inverse bounds. An opposite pair of high bits is not face-supported; that two-bit case is tail- free and is already covered by the positive-core theorem. ## 2. A root-unit presentation of the FULL generic source A tail-free branch already has all fixed-jet bounds. Consider a live face-supported branch, so all three opposite sums exceed `2D`. Choose an opposite pair with maximal label sum, and use tetrahedral relabeling to call it `(e,f)`, with f its high-bit edge and e its low-bit edge. This is possible: the largest opposite sum exceeds D, whereas an opposite pair with both bits low has sum at most D. A face contains at most one edge of each opposite pair. In this labeling, e<=D/2<=f, e+f>=max(a+c,b+d), min(a,b)<=D/2, min(c,d)<=D/2. (3) For the last assertion, the two remaining possible high edges are in the face containing f. Each of the two faces containing e therefore has at most one high external edge. The same assertion is immediate when there are fewer than three high bits. Set p=min(a+d,b+c), s=a+b+c+d, h=max(|a-b|,|c-d|), t0=s-2p, rA=a+b-h, rC=c+d-h, n=p-f, t=p+f-D. (4) The exact elementary identity p+h=max(a+c,b+d) (5) follows by expanding the difference of the maximum and minimum: its four possibilities are `a-b,b-a,c-d,d-c`. The true triangle conditions give `n>=0` and `h<=e`. Equations (3),(5) imply n<=e-h, h+e+n<=2e<=D, n<=t. (6) Furthermore 0<=n<=rA,rC<=D, 0<=t<=D, 0<=t0, t0+n<=D. (7) Indeed `rA,rC<=D` follows from (3), and `n<=e-h` together with `e<=a+b,c+d` proves their lower bounds. The upper bound on t follows from `p+f<=2D`, since both relevant face sums are at most `2D`. Finally `t0+n=max(a+d,b+c)-f` is a face deficit and belongs to `[0,D]`. All these are literal integer inequalities, including walls. Write `Q=zeta^2`, `alpha=zeta^(2h+1)`, `z=zeta^(2e+1)`. The already proved [actual generic source conversion](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md#6-exact-conversion-to-the-seven-factorial-sum-including-its-phase) is the exact identity S=S0 (V_n/C_n) G_n, G_n=sum_(k=0)^n (Q^-n,Q^(-p-f-1),alpha z,alpha/z;Q)_k Q^k /(Q,Q^(t0+1),Q^-rA,Q^-rC;Q)_k. (8) This is the actual finite generic series BEFORE specializing q. By (6),(7), every numerator and denominator factor of every term in (8) is a root unit. For the second upper parameter use `p+f+1=N+t`; its root exponents are those of `Q^-t`, and `k<=n<=t`. For the two spectral factors, their exponent ranges are h+e+1,...,h+e+k in [1,D], h-e,...,h-e+k-1 in [-D,-1]. (9) Thus there is no disappearing generic summand and no singular Pochhammer denominator in this presentation. ## 3. Every summand has positive root value Let `s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2sin(pi u/N)` and `c_j=2cos((2j+1)pi/N)`. Direct conversion of each finite Pochhammer in (8) to sine factors gives its kth root summand as A_k product_(i=0)^(k-1)(c_(h+i)-c_e), A_k= s_n/s_(n-k) * s_t/s_(t-k) * s_(rA-k)/s_rA * s_(rC-k)/s_rC * s_t0/[s_k s_(t0+k)] >0. (10) For clarity this is the same finite phase calculation as in the proved folded spectral formula; it only requires the inequalities (6),(7), not that every external label is folded. The residual monomial phase is `q^(Nk)` and the residual sign is `(-1)^k`, so both cancel. The spectral factorization uses (alpha z,alpha/z;Q)_k = product_(i<k) alpha Q^i (c_(h+i)-c_e) at the root. Since `h+i<e<=D/2` whenever `i<k<=n`, every displayed cosine difference is strictly positive. The term at k=0 is one. Hence the ENTIRE true generic series has a positive common phase at q and a nonzero value `G_n(q)>0`. Each term in (8) is a product of a bounded number of finite unit Pochhammers of lengths O(N), with integer exponents O(N). On the uniform disk |log(zeta/q)| <= c/[N^2(1+log N)], (11) every such term divided by its positive root value remains in a small sector about one. This is the elementary unit-factor harmonic estimate proved in the positive-core note: sum the logarithmic changes using `|sin(pi u/N)|>=2 dist(u,N Z)/N`. The bounded number of products, including negative exponents and exponents up to `2N`, only changes the absolute constant. Their positive sum obeys the same estimate. Cauchy inequalities therefore bound every fixed jet of G_n and its inverse relative to their root values. ## 4. Actual prefactor cancellation retains the generic normal It remains essential to check the prefactor in (8). Positivity of a substituted polynomial alone would not prove the source theorem. Choose `(a',b',c',d')=(a,b,c,d)` if `a+d<=b+c`, and `(b,a,d,c)` otherwise. The actual source formula gives R=(c+d-e, a+b-e, t0, a'-b'+e, d'-c'+e), S0=(-1)^s [s+1]!/product_(u in R)[u]!, V_n=zeta^n (Q^(-p-f-1);Q)_n /[(Q;Q)_n(Q^(t0+1);Q)_n(Q^(-s-1);Q)_n], C_n=alpha^n (Q^(-p-f-1);Q)_n /[(Q^(t0+1);Q)_n(Q^-rA;Q)_n(Q^-rC;Q)_n]. (12) Every entry of R is in `[0,D]`: these are face deficits, together with t0, bounded by (7). Because the branch is live, 2N<=s+1<3N, 0<=s+1-2N<n. (13) The second inequality follows from `max(a+d,b+c)+f<=2D`. Consequently `[s+1]!` contains exactly `[N]` and `[2N]`, while `(Q^(-s-1);Q)_n` contains exactly one zero factor, namely `1-zeta^(-4N)`. All other factors in (12) are root units by (6),(7). Cancel the common Pochhammers in V_n/C_n GENERICALLY. Then cancel the indicated zero factor using the exact identity [2N]/(1-zeta^(-4N))=zeta^(2N)/(zeta-zeta^-1). (14) If a superscript circle means omitting exactly the indicated factor, the result is the explicit analytic unit identity (-1)^D S/[N]=A(zeta) G_n(zeta), A(zeta)=(-1)^(D+s) zeta^(2N-2hn)/(zeta-zeta^-1) * [s+1]!^(omit N,2N)/product_(u in R)[u]! * (Q^-rA,Q^-rC;Q)_n /[(Q;Q)_n (Q^(-s-1);Q)_n^(omit -2N)]. (15) Every denominator in (15) is now a root unit. No term proportional to `[2N]` in the original seven-factorial sum has been dropped: (15) is an equality of the original generic germs, obtained from the exact finite source transformation and exact cancellation (14). The same unit-factor estimate applies to A and its inverse; the additional monomial has exponent O(N^2), and the extra quantum integer denominator is a root unit. Combining it with the positive G_n gives fixed relative jet bounds for the entire original regular source `(-1)^D S/[N]`. Its root value is the positive original core C, so A(q)>0 as well. The four regularized face factors are analytic units with the already proved uniform relative jet bounds. Therefore (2), its inverse version and its local square-root version follow on the SAME polynomial disk (11). ## 5. Cover all first normals using exact source relations The [first-normal Ward theorem](actual_partner_first_normal_ward_reduction.md) proves, for each opposite pair and every choice of the other bits, k(00)-k(01)-k(10)+k(11)=0. (16) Apply it independently to the three opposite pairs. Every branch is a signed sum of at most 27 branches having at most one high bit in each opposite pair. Thus it remains to handle high sets of size at most three, with no opposite pair. Sets of size zero, one or two are face-supported. A three-edge set with one edge of each opposite pair is either a face or the complement of a face, namely a three-edge star. Face sets satisfy (2). Consider a star set. If the branch is tail-free, use the positive-core theorem. If its maximal face sum is repeated, use the proved coherent Fourier bound. Otherwise use the exact controlled first-normal difference from the [Fourier source involution](actual_coherent_racah_tail_fourier_residues.md#6-the-residual-is-an-exact-partner-involution): |k(B)-k(B*)| <= C N^2(1+log N) W_N^2, (17) where B* flips the three edges outside its unique largest face. The unique maximal face cannot be the all-low face complementary to the high star. Every other face shares one of its low edges and replaces its two remaining low edges by their high partners; its sum is at least that of the all-low face. Equality everywhere would also contradict uniqueness. Therefore the maximal face contains two high edges and one low edge.
