Its complementary flip turns the third high edge low and turns its other two low edges high. In terms of opposite pairs, B* has one pair in state `00` and two pairs in state `11`: a tetrahedral face contains exactly one edge from each opposite pair. Apply (16) to those two `11` pairs. This expresses k(B*) as a signed sum of at most nine branches with at most TWO high bits, all already controlled by (2). Equation (17) controls the star branch. Finally the initial 27-term interpolation proves (1) for every original partner, with constants independent of N, labels and parity. The estimates are on the actual full generic first normals. The proof has not replaced a normal by the root core, differentiated a root-value identity, or imposed the first-order Ward equation on higher orders. The original coherent tail itself now has a uniform bound on EVERY partner branch: |T_B(q)| <= C(1+log N) C_B(q). (18) For a tail-free branch T is zero. Otherwise write the exact germ as `K_B=U_B(C_B+[2N]T_B)^2`, where U_B is the product of the four regularized face factors. The logarithmic derivatives of U_B and the positive core C_B are `O(N^2(1+log N))`. Divide the first normal by `K_B(q)=U_B(q)C_B(q)^2` and use (1). This bounds `[2N]'(q) T_B(q)/C_B(q)` by the same order. Finally |[2N]'(q)|=2N/sin(pi/N)>=2N^2/pi, which proves (18). Thus the contribution of the actual retained tail to the first normal is controlled through an exact positive source presentation; no absolute estimate of its alternating summands was substituted. ## 6. Precise remaining scope This closes the local ALL-PARTNER FIRST-NORMAL scalar gap. Fixed higher normals are proved here for face-supported and tail-free branches. The exact first-normal Ward equation does not extend homogeneously to second order: its cluster trace contributes there. Thus arbitrary higher partner normals, the positive completed physical change-of-frame metric, shared global source constraints, and geometric overlap remain separate problems. Audit: [literal generic source transformation and support checks](../experiments/audit_actual_all_partner_first_normal_bound.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/actual_all_partner_first_normal_bound_results.json). Independent root review checked the maximal-opposite-pair presentation, all root-unit ranges, the exact generic prefactor cancellation and the star-to-Ward covering argument. Fresh replay passed 79,649 supported face-bit classifications, 2,384 live face branches, 430 complete generic presentations through four Taylor coefficients, and 13,852 star routes. The analytic bounds follow from the proof; the finite checks supplement the source and incidence identities.

title: One explicit divided-current kernel for every original plat source
text: # One explicit divided-current kernel for every original plat source 29 October 2026. The source-specific six-port kernel extends to EVERY fixed plat width. This supplies a concrete, proper original-source restriction before a coherent metric is chosen. It does not infer a sharp energy estimate from a small coefficient in an algebraic projector. ## 1. The actual regular divided currents Use the generic balanced original V_d, d=N-1, and the original coproducts from [the six-port normal-current proof](actual_six_port_divided_power_source_kernel.md). For an ordered block of 2r physical heads let H be its unrolled total weight. The regular first-normal operators are J_E=[Ecal_(2r)^N/(1-zeta^(2N))]_(zeta=q), J_F=[F_(2r)^N/(1-zeta^(2N))]_(zeta=q). (1) These are defined by generic division before specialization. Their ordered divided-coproduct formula is finite, with every nonzero local factorial index<N. They change H by +2N and -2N, respectively. Their normalization and all Cartan signs are those of the literal original matrices, not an abstract replacement representation. Consider the full physical K_total=1 sector Lcal=direct_sum_(k in Z) (V_N^tensor(2r))_(H=2Nk). (2) The source degree space is just its H=0 summand. Sector(2) is NOT being identified with the much smaller Hopf invariant space. ## 2. An ordinary sl2 action is an exact consequence of the normal Ward The generic divided commutation identity gives, at a vector of weight H, E^[N] F^[N]=sum_(t=0)^N [H choose t]_zeta F^[N-t]E^[N-t]. For H=2Nk, EVERY integer k, the root coefficients are [2Nk choose t]_q=0 (0<t<N), [2Nk choose N]_q=2k(-1)^N. (3) Here is a proof including negative k. In the finite product for the last Gaussian, the numerator contains [2Nk]; every other nonzero numerator factor specializes to [-j]=-[j], 1<=j<N. The zero ratio [2Nk]/[N] has derivative ratio -2k at q. Thus its value is (-1)^(N-1)(-2k)=2k(-1)^N. For t<N the numerator zero has no denominator zero. At k=0 the finite product is identically zero, consistent with(3). No semisimple or tilting theorem is used. The exact scalar connecting (1) with divided powers is alpha_N=N q^[-N(N-1)/2]/(1-Q)^N, alpha_N^2 rho^(2N)=N^2(-1)^(N-1), rho=q-q^-1. Consequently on(2) [J_E,J_F]=-N H. (4) Put e=J_E/N, f=-J_F/N, h=H/N. Equations(1),(4) give EXACTLY [e,f]=h, [h,e]=2e, [h,f]=-2f. (5) This is a finite-dimensional ordinary sl2 action on a KNOWN physical sector, derived from the first normal of the actual quantum operators. It is not a statement that the physical braids are positive-unitary, and no Hermitian condition on e,f is assumed. ## 3. A finite explicit right inverse, with no complete-reducibility premise On the h=2 subspace define R=sum_(j>=0) (-1)^j f^(j+1)e^j/[(j+1)!(j+2)!]. (6) The sum is finite. Since |H|<=2r(N-1)<2rN, terms j>r-2 vanish. For r<2 this h=2 space is zero. On a vector v of weight2, (5) gives e f^(j+1)e^j v =f^(j+1)e^(j+1)v+(j+1)(j+2)f^j e^jv. Successive terms in eR cancel, and the first coefficient is 2/(1!2!)=1. Therefore e R=I on the ENTIRE weight2 space. (7) Thus J_E maps its weight0 space onto its weight2 space at every N and width. This argument proves the needed surjectivity directly; it does not import complete reducibility of a classical module. ## 4. The source is exactly that kernel at arbitrary width For an original 2k-head plat put r=k-1 and C=r d. The complete root invariant theorem identifies all invariants with W_r=(V_N^tensor(2r))_(degree C). Its literal coefficient extraction and original turns are those of [the complete source module](actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md), section5. The target of J_E is the physical degree C-N space, call it L_r. If C-N<0 interpret it as zero. Let S_N^(2k) be the saturated specialization of GENERIC invariant tensors inside V_d(zeta)^tensor(2k), as in [the deformable-source construction](actual_six_port_deformable_source_and_recoupling.md). Every generic invariant is killed by the regular divided current. Extraction of its last two colors(0,d) gives ext(S_N^(2k)) subset ker(J_E:W_r->L_r). (8) The extraction proof is unchanged at arbitrary prefix width: fifth in the six-port argument is now head 2k-1. If that head has input c>0, its c ordinary lowerings leave E_prefix^(N-c) E_prefix^c=0 at the root; c=0 retains the full divided prefix operator. Last head color d forces zero lowering there. Thus no endpoint or derivative source is removed. It remains to compare exact dimensions. Write S(z)=1+z+...+z^d, a_j=[z^j] S(z)^(2r), a_j=0 outside its actual support. The full root space has dimension a_C and L_r has dimension a_(C-N). Over generic q, the invariant dimension in 2k heads is the weight-zero dimension minus the weight-two dimension: rank S_N^(2k)=[z^(kd)](1-z) S(z)^(2k). This follows either from the elementary generic highest-vector tensor decomposition, or by observing that each nontrivial even highest weight has one weight0 and one weight2 while the trivial module has only weight0. Using (1-z)S(z)^2=(1-z^N)S(z) and coefficient symmetry a_(C+j)=a_(C-j), its value telescopes to rank S_N^(2k)=a_C-a_(C-N). (9) Surjectivity(7) says the kernel on the right of(8) has exactly the SAME dimension. Saturation makes the specialization injective, so (8) is an equality: BOXED: ext(S_N^(2k))=ker(J_E:W_r->L_r). (10) In the full 2k-head root invariant space this is equivalently the kernel of its total J_E; adjoining total J_F changes nothing because all generic invariant lifts are killed by both. This is a VALUE source theorem: derivatives of the whole source still obey their differentiated inhomogeneous Ward equations, not a falsely homogeneous version of(10). ## 5. A completely explicit all-width source projector On W_r=weight0, (6)--(7) give the algebraic projection I-Re. In the original normal-current normalization its finite formula is P_source=I+sum_(m=1)^(r-1) J_F^m J_E^m/[N^(2m) m!(m+1)!]. (11) For r<=1 the sum is empty. Its range is exactly(10), and it is the identity there; P_source^2=P_source follows from eR=I. For six heads r=2 this reduces to I+J_F J_E/(2N^2), with the previously proved right inverse J_E J_F=-2N^2 I on L_r. All original regular generic braids, interval Casimirs and polynomial circle coupons preserve the source subspace. Therefore (11) may be inserted between their reduced gates on an ORIGINAL source orbit without changing any literal exterior co-source. It need not commute on the larger unrestricted root module, and a root-only Hopf coupon with no regular generic lift is not covered by this assertion. The operator(11) is generally oblique. Its polynomial coefficients in N do NOT make its norm polynomial: J_E and J_F themselves may have exponentially large entries in a specified frame. If a positive metric is needed, the orthogonal projector onto the SAME explicit kernel has norm one. In the physical W_r coordinates, the exact original boundary data satisfy ||w0||=N^[3(k-1)/2], ||lambda||=N^[-(k-1)/2], ||w0|| ||lambda||=N^(k-1). Orthogonal compression does not increase that boundary cost and retains the literal marked cap only after its proved whole-invariant reduction. This does not yet estimate the coherent word energy on(10). ## 6. Consequence for the first genuinely non-tree source block At six heads, the full root module has dimension(2N^3+N)/3, whereas the actual deformable source has dimension(N^3+N)/2. A generic 6j construction belongs on this latter saturated module. It must keep its complete confluence/normal coefficients, and must NOT be equated to the larger raw-root invariant space or to three free scalar circle registers. Formula(10) supplies its missing normal source equation explicitly; formula(11) provides an actual algebraic insertion enforcing that equation before positivity. The sharp analytic task remains the coherent Clebsch/Racah contraction on this constrained source, including its complex corridor and global complement. Neither dimension compression nor the ordinary sl2 relation is a sharp hyperbolic-volume estimate. No additional knot/link equality is claimed here merely from this source theorem.

title: Balanced anchors and the actual alternating-knot source
text: # Balanced anchors and the actual alternating-knot source 28 October 2026. In the exact charged source of an alternating one-component diagram, vanishing of every individual anchor defect forces all overcrossing clocks to be equal. This is a topological incidence statement, not a knot census. For the ORIGINAL figure-eight state the resulting diagonal clock sectors are ALL annihilated, at every level. More strongly, every nonzero clock sector has an anchor defect of size at least (N-1)/2. Thus individual sublinear-defect star estimates, or a positive balanced-anchor chamber alone, cannot cover this actual source. Further clustering/fusion may transport these defects; no statement that such a global method is impossible is made. ## 1. Alternation determines the defect equations Use the exact [charged source](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md) and [source closure contraction](actual_general_flow_fusion.md). Put d=N-1. In a strictly alternating diagram, each maximal overbridge is a single crossing. After contracting the original closure-adapter forest, its anchors are the physical oriented segments between successive OVER encounters. Each such segment contains exactly ONE UNDER encounter. Let crossing i be its first over encounter and j its next over encounter. If its under encounter has clock h_l, the three contributions to the anchor's incident linear-factor count are h_i from the first over-output block, d-h_j from the final over-input block, (d-h_l)+h_l=d from the spectator under encounter. A self-loop is counted twice, since it contributes a factor of that anchor at both ends. Phase rescalings from the retained pivots do not change these counts. Hence the EXACT incidence and defect are S_(i->j)=2d+h_i-h_j, delta_(i->j)=S_(i->j)-2d=h_i-h_j. (1) The successor relation on over encounters is one cycle for a one-component knot. Therefore all delta=0 iff all crossing clocks h_i=H. (2) For a link the same conclusion is componentwise. Formula (1) is valid independently of crossing signs. It uses physical over/under roles and survives the exact signed source gluing, rather than identifying successive braid positions with successive physical strand encounters. ## 2. The actual figure-eight cut forces its first clock to zero Take the original signed word [1,-2,1,-2], with clocks (h_0,h_1,h_2,h_3). We retain the original averaged pivotal scalar. The initial use of INTEGER degree conservation to write it as (1/N)Tr[(I tensor g tensor g)W] (3) is made before decomposing into clock sectors, as in the charged source theorem. No Schur lemma or marked-row substitution is applied to an individual h-sector afterward. For the support calculation choose fixed cyclic Fourier grids on head i with root x^(i-1), x=-exp(-pi*i/N). At a positive adjacent crossing these roots differ by x. The outgoing first propagated root is Q^(-1) times its fixed root; the other outgoing root is unchanged. Thus if (a,b;c,e) are its fixed-grid input/output colors, the actual overclock at the first +sigma_1 crossing is h_0=[b-c-1], (4) where brackets mean the representative in 0,...,d. The same-grid crossing is the exact finite Fourier transform of the ORIGINAL R, even where its old raw four-Psi presentation was singular. The closed polynomial port formulas extend there; their normalizer is a nonzero monomial. These clock dictionaries are unchanged by the propagated prefixes. If a positive under-input root has offset Q^v from its fixed position root, its under-output root has offset Q^(v-1), since it is x times the input root. The difference of the two label offsets therefore still gives b-c-1. For a negative understrand the offsets are Q^v and Q^(v+1), giving e-a-1. Thus resetting the grid labels does not silently replace the actual clock variables. Here is its elementary support dictionary. Put u=[b-a-1], v=[a-c], t=[c-e], z=[e-b]. The two positive Pochhammers are nonzero exactly when u+v+t+z=d, h_0=u+v. (5) For example the first Pochhammer says u<=h_0 and then v=h_0-u; the second says z<=d-h_0 and then t=d-h_0-z. The negative table gives the same support equation, with its overclock u+z instead. Equivalently supported crossing colors have cyclic lifts b<=e_lift<=c_lift<=a_lift=b+[a-b]. (6) For clarity, the cut-support argument is recalled here. For fixed sentinels L,R define V(x)=[L-x_1]+sum_i[x_i-x_(i+1)]+[x_b-R]. The cyclic interval (6) makes V nonincreasing at every supported crossing: the two outside triangle inequalities have defects which are nonnegative multiples of N, and their middle intervals sum to [a-b]. The trace source (3) has input (A_1,[A_2+1],...) and output (A_1,A_2,...), because the actual pivot is a nonzero scalar times the cyclic shift. Choose L=A_1 and R=[A_b+1]. The endpoint difference of V is zero if A_2=A_1 and -N otherwise. Thus A_2=A_1 and V is constant along every supported source path. Translate colors by -A_1; this changes none of the support tests. The first head begins and ends at zero. The left triangle equality at position1 gives [0-c]=[0-a]+v. Its nonnegative increments must sum to zero, so v=0 at every position1 crossing and that head stays zero. Before the FIRST such crossing the second head stays one: its distance [0-x_2] is nondecreasing and begins at its maximum d. Thus at that first crossing a=0,b=1, so u=v=0. This proves pointwise, for EVERY cut color in the averaged source, nonzero fixed-clock source sector implies h_0=0. (7) This is the same support argument independently proved in [the original cyclic-cut theorem](original_source_cyclic_variation_peeling.md), with its mapping (4)--(5) to the present clocks made explicit. It does not require intertwinement of separately split sectors. The center-independent homogeneous source theorem transports this support calculation back to its original regular frames. ## 3. A second support inequality in the actual reduced polynomial There is also a direct regular-Fermat test of the full reduced four-anchor polynomial. Up to a nonzero scalar, rescale its two anchors B,D by x^(-1), and call the four new variables A,B,C,D. Choose all four new variables to be Nth roots of one. This is permitted by the exact finite-flat source theorem, not a change of invariant or a pointwise replacement of the old raw kernel. The eight actual blocks have the following lengths and root starts: | tail -> head | length | start exponent p in (tail-Q^p head;Q)_L | | --- | --- | --- | | B -> C | d-h_0 | 0 | | C -> A | h_0 | 1 | | D -> A | d-h_1 | h_1+1 | | A -> B | h_1 | -h_1+h_2+1 | | C -> B | d-h_2 | h_0+h_2+2 | | B -> D | h_2 | -h_2-h_3-1 | | A -> D | d-h_3 | -h_1 | | D -> C | h_3 | 0 | This table includes all original closure pivot substitutions. It is a direct application of the actual graph metadata and full-block source contractions. No new graph or exterior coupon is introduced. Let a,b,c,e be the root-grid color indices of A,B,C,D. If a grid summand is nonzero, the D->A block forces r=[e-a] in [0,h_1]. The A->D block forces [a-e+h_1] in [d-h_3,d]. Since r<=h_1, the left representative is the ordinary integer h_1-r. Hence h_1-r>=d-h_3, h_1+h_3>=d. (8) The endpoint cases with an empty block give the same (possibly vacuous) inequalities. If (8) fails, EVERY point on this regular Fermat grid has polynomial value zero. Its exact source coefficient is therefore zero. Thus (8) is necessary for a nonzero h-sector, not merely an absolute-envelope or stationary-point condition. There is an independent pathwise check of (8), in the same cyclic coordinates as Section2. With first cut color zero, the source-cut support forces the four intermediate states to have the form initial (0,1,B+1), after first (0,D,B+1), after second (0,E,F), after third (0,0,F), final (0,0,B), all colors interpreted cyclically. The fourth negative crossing has current clock h_3=[B-1]. If B=0 it is d, proving (8). If B>0, its cyclic interval forces 1<=F<=B. At the second negative crossing h_1=u_2+z_2 with u_2=[B-D]>=0, z_2=[F-B-1]=N+F-B-1>=N-B. Thus h_1+h_3>=(N-B)+(B-1)=d. This argument uses only actual supported paths before summation. The grid offsets just checked show that h_1,h_3 here are the present propagated overclocks, not renamed old-corner variables. ## 4. Balanced diagonal sectors vanish, and defects must be macroscopic For this alternating one-component diagram, (2) makes every balanced clock sector (H,H,H,H). But (7) would force H=0, while (8) would require 2H>=d. As d>=1, these are incompatible. Therefore lambda(P_(H,H,H,H))=0, EVERY N>=2 and EVERY H in 0,...,d. (9) There is no asymptotic qualifier: the WHOLE fixed-H coefficient vanishes exactly in the actual original source. More generally, any nonzero sector has h_0=0 and max_i h_i>=d/2 by (8). Its cyclic clock range is therefore at least d/2. Along the physical four-overencounter cycle, total variation is at least twice the range. In fact the actual physical successor is (3,0,1,2), so the four defects are exactly (-h_3,h_1,h_2-h_1,h_3-h_2). Using (8) gives the stronger explicit bound sum_anchors |delta_i|>=d, max_anchors |delta_i|>=max(h_1,h_3)>=(N-1)/2. (10) Thus no sequence of nonzero figure-eight clock sectors can have all individual anchor defects o(N) in this representation. The positive balanced-anchor maximum principle and the retained sublinear local defect jets are consequently insufficient by themselves for its actual volume contribution. This does not rule out cluster reductions: full-kernel fusion can add opposite defects, and exact phase-aware fusions can change the remaining source variables. Equation (10) must be respected before such a further operation; it does not prove that a macroscopic defect core can never be reduced or analyzed geometrically. ## 5. Reproducible audit python3 experiments/audit_actual_alternating_balanced_source.py The audit verifies the sign-independent physical successor and incidence formula on actual alternating signed words after all original closures, the local cyclic-support dictionary directly against both ORIGINAL R matrices, the general reduced figure-eight block table, and exact zero of every diagonal sector at multiple levels. It separately checks the regular-grid support implications without replacing them by coefficient-modulus estimates.

title: Exact radial compactification and sublevel transport of strict-Hall source cores
text: # Exact radial compactification and sublevel transport of strict-Hall source cores 28 October 2026. For the ORIGINAL fixed-clock unit-factor source, every strict-Hall core admits an explicit radial retraction which never increases the modulus of its masterfunction. The retraction is piecewise monomial, has uniformly bounded logarithmic differential, and puts every sublevel cycle in a logarithmic box of radius O(log N). In addition, the complete logarithmic metric gives a global horizontal-lift proof that ordinary critical values are the ONLY nonzero finite bifurcation values of this product masterfunction. Consequently the original coefficient torus can actually be homotoped into every sublevel above all its regular critical moduli. This is not yet the polynomial-mass theorem: the horizontal flow in the bounded box need not have a proved uniform complexity or Jacobian bound. The clocks are fixed throughout. Their full coupled critical equations and the original volume bound do not follow from this result. ## 1. The actual source and its strict cores Let k>=2 and f(X)=gamma product_(e=1)^M(alpha_e X_(u_e)-beta_e X_(v_e)) / product_i X_i^(q_i), (1) where u_e!=v_e, |alpha_e|=|beta_e|=1, gamma!=0, q_i are integers, and sum_i q_i=M. All original scalar, pivot and feedback factors which have already been extracted remain in gamma or in the separate clock weight. Loops are evaluated as their exact scalar monomials before (1). For a nonempty proper anchor set I, let m_I count the factors internal to I, C_I its crossing factors, and e_I=q(I)-m_I. Assume 1<=e_I<=C_I-1 for EVERY such I. (2) The source cut theorem gives exactly these strict inequalities in each nontrivial residual SCC after tight cuts and forced factors are removed. They imply C_I>=2 and M>=2. They concern endpoint support, not the nonvanishing of the selected complex coefficient. The function (1) is invariant under common complex scaling. We work on the quotient torus T=(C*)^k/C*, using X_k=1 when a concrete coordinate system is needed. Its original source is the positive generator I=(2*pi*i)^(-(k-1)) integral_(|X_1|=...=|X_(k-1)|=1) f(X) dlog X_1 ... dlog X_(k-1). (3) The divisor f=0 is allowed in this coefficient cycle: the form in (3) is holomorphic there. It is removed only when discussing horizontal lifts over the nonzero base. ## 2. An exact OFF-critical cut derivative Put rho_i=log|X_i|, r_i=|X_i|, and delta_i=S_i-2q_i, where S_i counts the incident linear factors. At any point with f!=0, partial_(rho_i) log|f| =delta_i/2 + (1/2) sum_(e incident i) (r_i^2-r_j^2)/|alpha_e X_i-beta_e X_j|^2. (4) The sign in the numerator always uses i as the first endpoint, irrespective of the displayed orientation of the factor. This follows from Re[a/(a-b)]=(1+(|a|^2-|b|^2)/|a-b|^2)/2. Suppose every radius in I is at least exp(g) times every radius outside I, where g>0. Internal edge terms cancel after summing (4). Also (r_i^2-r_j^2)/|alpha_e X_i-beta_e X_j|^2 >=(r_i-r_j)/(r_i+r_j)>=tanh(g/2). Since delta(I)=C_I-2e_I, the exact high-cut direction V_I=sum_(i in I) X_i partial_(X_i) satisfies Re[(V_I f)/f] >=(C_I-2e_I+C_I tanh(g/2))/2. (5) In particular, for L=log M, (2) gives the uniform quantitative bound g>=L ==> Re[(V_I f)/f]>=1/(M+1). (6) Indeed tanh(L/2)=(M-1)/(M+1), so the right side of (5) is C_I M/(M+1)-e_I >=1-C_I/(M+1)>=1/(M+1). This is an identity and inequality away from the zero divisor, not an evaluation of the critical equations alone. ## 3. Explicit simultaneous gap clipping Order the logarithmic radii rho_(s1)<=...<=rho_(sk), and let g_j=rho_(s(j+1))-rho_(sj). Replace each g_j by min(g_j,L), preserving all arguments. Reconstruct the radii from these new adjacent gaps and then divide all coordinates by their kth coordinate to restore X_k=1. Call the resulting map C:T->T. The reconstruction is independent of the choices among equal radii, so C is continuous across order walls. A semialgebraic homotopy is obtained by interpolating the RADIUS RATIOS, not by using arbitrary real powers. For R_j=exp(g_j), set R_j(s)=(1-s)R_j+s min(R_j,M), 0<=s<=1. (7) Reconstruct as above to obtain C_s, with C_0=identity and C_1=C. Every changing gap stays at least L. Its derivative is nonpositive, and changing gap j is exactly translation in the high-cut direction I_j={s(j+1),...,sk}, modulo common scaling. Therefore (6) implies d/ds log|f(C_s X)|<=0, |f(C_s X)|<=|f(X)|. (8) At a zero of f, a zero factor has equal endpoint radii and equal phased arguments. Its endpoints remain at equal radii throughout (7), so that factor stays zero. Thus (8) extends across f=0 by continuity. Conversely no new zero factor is created: an originally positive radius gap remains positive because L>0, and arguments never change. The same homotopy therefore preserves the arrangement complement as well. Every output gap is at most L. Hence max_i log|C(X)_i|-min_i log|C(X)_i| <=(k-1)log M. (9) The map fixes this clipped region pointwise. It is thus a genuine strong deformation retraction of EVERY sublevel {|f|<=R} onto its intersection with the compact projective box (9). In the X_k=1 gauge, all log radii then have absolute value at most (k-1)log M. The endpoint map C is piecewise monomial in the positive radii. The pieces are indexed only by the k! orders and 2^(k-1) clipped-gap choices. On each piece, its logarithmic radial differential has integer entries bounded by 2; the argument map is the identity. Thus, in the standard Euclidean metric on (rho_1,...,rho_(k-1),theta_1,...,theta_(k-1)), its Lipschitz constant is at most 4k. The same bound holds throughout (7): the derivative of log R_j(s) with respect to log R_j lies in [0,1]. In particular, clipping increases Euclidean logarithmic (k-1)-mass by at most (4k)^(k-1). This statement uses the full real logarithmic metric; it does NOT claim such a comparison with only the absolute holomorphic wedge |dlog X_1 wedge ... wedge dlog X_(k-1)|, which can vanish on a real tangent plane before a nonholomorphic map is applied. Using auxiliary positive r_i with r_i^2=X_i conjugate(X_i), the maps C and C_s have semialgebraic graphs of degree bounded solely in k on each piece (the coefficient M is retained). Images of chains whose algebraic support degrees and multiplicities are polynomial in N therefore still have polynomial support complexity after clipping. No such complexity claim for the INTERIOR horizontal flow is inferred here. ## 4. Complete horizontal lifts: no hidden finite escape Give T its complete flat logarithmic metric. Let J be a compact subset of C* disjoint from all regular critical values of f. Write l_i=(X_i partial_(X_i) f)/f. Their sum is zero by homogeneity, so they define the logarithmic cotangent vector on the quotient. Outside the box (9), there is an adjacent gap greater than L. Equation (6) implies ||dlog f|| >=c_k/(M+1). (10) Here one may take c_k=1/(2sqrt(k)), a conservative quotient-coordinate constant. Inside the box, the set f^(-1)(J) is compact. A factor cannot approach zero there while f stays in J: the denominator is bounded away from zero, all other factors are bounded, and J stays away from zero. There is also no ordinary critical point there by the choice of J. Thus ||dlog f|| has a positive minimum on this compact set. For a piecewise C^1 base path w(t) in J, the standard logarithmic Hermitian dual gives the explicit horizontal vector field dZ/dt=(w'(t)/w(t)) conjugate(l(Z))/||l(Z)||^2, (11) in any orthonormal logarithmic quotient coordinates. Its defining identity is dlog f/dt=w'/w. Its norm is bounded on f^(-1)(J), by (10) outside and the compact positive minimum inside. Local uniqueness and completeness of the logarithmic metric therefore extend its flow for the whole finite path time. Indeed a bounded-speed finite-time path is Cauchy at a hypothetical endpoint; its limit remains in T, and f stays in J, so the ordinary local ODE existence theorem extends it. The same argument applies to every initial point, with smooth dependence on it and on the base path. Lifting a short base contraction and its reverse gives a local smooth trivialization over J. No finite nonzero bifurcation values occur outside the ordinary critical-value set. The outside bound (10) is uniform in N; the compact INSIDE minimum is only proved positive at each fixed N and has no polynomial lower bound here. ## 5. An actual homologous sublevel cycle for the original source There are finitely many regular critical VALUES. The critical locus is algebraic with finitely many irreducible components, and f is constant on each connected component of its regular critical locus. Put Mcrit=max_regular_critical |f|, using zero if that set is empty. Fix R>Mcrit. Over |w|>=R the horizontal lift (11) is complete on every finite closed radial base interval. Choose a smooth radial base homotopy which fixes |w|<=R and moves each point with |w|>R toward modulus R (or toward R+epsilon, followed by a limit). Lifting it wherever |f|>R and using identity elsewhere yields a deformation of T into {|f|<=R+epsilon}; the cutoff can be chosen so that it is the identity at the joining level. Only the compact range of |f| on the original coefficient torus is needed for its transported cycle, so there is no assertion of a uniform infinite-time lift. This produces a cycle Gamma_(R,epsilon) homologous in T to the ORIGINAL torus (3), with |f|<=R+epsilon. Compose it with the explicit clipping map C to put it in (9), preserving that sublevel and its homology class. The holomorphic coefficient form is closed on all of T, so its integral over the resulting cycle is exactly I, including its original scalar. This is a global existence theorem for the required sublevel homotopy, not a selection theorem for any individual critical point. It improves the earlier sufficient macrodeficit condition e_Z>B: strict Hall support alone gives the needed complete logarithmic lift for these PRODUCT masterfunctions. It does not assert that every critical stratum of an arbitrary compactification is regular; a topological horizontal lift on T is the exact conclusion needed here. ## 6. The quantitative step which this proof does NOT supply The endpoint clipping has fixed-dimensional semialgebraic complexity and bounded logarithmic mass distortion. The preceding interior horizontal flow need not be semialgebraic, and no uniform bound for its Jacobian or for the multiplicities of a replacement algebraic chain has been proved. Thus it is not yet valid to combine cycle existence with the earlier polynomial logarithmic-mass lemma and announce |I|<=poly(N) Mcrit. Effective triangulation of the sublevel SET alone would not prove that bound either: one must control a representative of the particular original integral homology class, including its coefficients. The present proof isolates that remaining mass/complexity issue inside an explicit compact logarithmic box, rather than leaving radius escape or asymptotic bifurcation as additional hypotheses. For the knot problem, every claim above still fixes the integer clocks. Their exact feedback, factorial weights and original finite source must remain when constructing the full phase cycle. Neither full critical Hurwitz support nor a general-knot exponential upper bound follows by taking absolute values over these fixed-clock cores. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_anchor_sublevel_radial_transport.py): actual source residual cores, exact off-critical cut derivatives, strict-Hall bounds, modulus-monotone simultaneous gap clipping, and horizontal right-inverse identities. The audit supplements the uniform proof; it does not estimate the unresolved interior flow mass.

title: The endpoint channel Hessian is the inverse primitive cusp shape
text: # The endpoint channel Hessian is the inverse primitive cusp shape 30 October 2026. The actual normalized augmented-plat phase has a nondegenerate channel block at every regular complete geometric point. After eliminating its two local q-Hahn variables on their recorded critical sheets, ALL channel/magnetic mixed second derivatives vanish at the complete channel endpoint. The diagonal entries are exactly H_(xi_i,xi_i)=-4pi i/tau_i, (0) where tau_i is the ACTUAL oriented primitive crossing-circle cusp shape, longitude translation divided by meridian translation. Hence each entry has strictly negative real part. This is a source theorem for every original augmented plat admitting the stated regular complete geometric chart, at any fixed width, with any retained half-twist pattern. The proof identifies the cusp shape directly from the actual meridian and longitude MATRICES. It does not infer that marking by matching a Hessian. It also does not assert that the remaining magnetic Hessian is nondegenerate after removing framing directions, or that a finite source cycle contributes a nonzero Gaussian amplitude. ## 1. A local critical reduction must keep its integer characters Use the fully normalized local phase Theta_epsilon and its rational critical map from [the actual character calculation](actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md). Write y for the magnetic variables (tau,u,v), xi for the folded channel, and alpha,beta for the two internal q-Hahn variables. The high physical degree chart uses its proved affine adapter; its phase remains the same function of these LOW coordinates, not the same function with the physical pair product substituted for T. At a regular complete point J=exp(2pi i xi)=-1, both internal critical quadratics have simple roots. The holomorphic implicit-function theorem gives their chosen continuations alpha(y,xi), beta(y,xi) in a small logarithmic neighborhood. The exponentiated equations alone give Theta_alpha=2pi i n_alpha, Theta_beta=2pi i n_beta, with locally constant integers on these roots. Retain these characters and put Theta_tilde=Theta-2pi i(n_alpha alpha+n_beta beta). Then its two internal derivatives are EXACTLY zero. Define the root-reduced phase Theta_bar(y,xi) by substituting these roots into Theta_tilde. Envelope differentiation now gives exp(partial_xi Theta_bar)=R_epsilon =R0(-J)^epsilon. (1) Reducing an unadjusted phase whose internal derivatives are nonzero integer characters would add spurious alpha_xi and beta_xi terms. No choice of these local characters is, by itself, a proof that the corresponding Poisson sector contributes to the original finite sum. ## 2. Endpoint tangential derivatives vanish identically The actual source identities hold on the ENTIRE endpoint root chart: R0|_(J=-1)=1, C=I+bH, H=P+I, H^2=0, (dR0/dJ)|_(J=-1)=2b. (2) The derivative in (2) follows the implicit internal roots, holding the magnetic variables fixed. In particular it is not a derivative taken with their exponential coordinates Z,W incorrectly frozen. The scalar b is recovered from the actual ordered input/output meridians by b=Tr([H,A_in] A_out)/32. The endpoint regulator note's [rational chart](actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.md), with Z=(a-1)/(a+1), W=(b0-1)/(b0+1), gives explicitly b=(2Ta b0-Ta-Tb0+a+b0-2) /[2(T+1)(a-1)(b0-1)]. (3) Here b0 is a chart parameter, not the transport coefficient b. Formula (3) holds in both physical degree charts. The audit differentiates the original general-J rational expression for R0 using Z_J=-P_J/P_Z and W_J=-P_J/P_W, and checks (2) exactly over Q(T,a,b0). Because (-J)^epsilon=1 at J=-1, equation (1) implies partial_xi Theta_bar(y,1/2)=2pi i n_xi (4) for one LOCALLY CONSTANT integer n_xi on each connected marked endpoint chart. It does not automatically imply that this derivative is zero. Nevertheless differentiating (4) in ANY magnetic tangent direction gives partial_y partial_xi Theta_bar=0. (5) This is an identity along the whole endpoint chart, not a numerical vanishing at the geometric point alone. Finally dJ/dxi=-2pi i there, so (1),(2) give partial_xi^2 Theta_bar =-2pi i(2b-epsilon) =-4pi i(b-epsilon/2). (6) The high-degree adapter is independent of xi. Therefore (5),(6) remain valid in the actual high physical coordinates. ## 3. The primitive cusp translations fix the factor and sign The collar is the ORIGINAL threading word [2,1,1,2], followed by the retained main half twist R^epsilon. The [proved endpoint reconstruction](actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.md), section 3, supplies its raw trace -2 auxiliary meridian C_aux,raw=-[I+(epsilon/2-b)H]. (7) Thus the actual trace +2 meridian is mu=I+(epsilon/2-b)H. The actual disk-framed preferred longitude is P=BA, with no meridian power inserted. Since P=-I+H, its centered trace +2 representative is lambda_centered=-P=I-H. (8) Changing a matrix by its central minus sign changes no projective translation. Conjugate their common parabolic fixed point to infinity. The nonzero nilpotent H then has form [[0,h],[0,0]], h!=0. Equations (7),(8) say that the actual translations are translation(mu)=(epsilon/2-b)h, translation(lambda)=-h. Both primitive paths retain their original collar orientations. Therefore tau_geom=translation(lambda)/translation(mu) =1/(b-epsilon/2). (9) This proves the inverse cusp relation DIRECTLY at the complete point; no nearby deformation theorem or guessed cusp potential is used. With the positive orientation I(mu,lambda)=1, Im tau_geom>0. Substituting (9) into (6) proves (0), including Re(-4pi i/tau_geom) =-4pi Im(tau_geom)/|tau_geom|^2<0. (10) As a sign check, an actual rectangular crossing-circle cusp with c=cot(pi x)>0 has, in the SOURCE half-twist convention, tau_epsilon=2ic/(1-epsilon ic), b=1/(2ic), H_xixi=-2pi/c+2pi i epsilon. (11) Source epsilon=-1 is the geometric '+' collar of the matching-graph geometry note; the two notations should not be silently interchanged. The parameter x in (11) is a geometric rectangle parameter and is not being identified with a general Newton source coordinate. ## 4. The full original plat retains this diagonal block Sum the root-reduced phases of all original circle coupons, together with the original cup, cap, marking and exterior phases. Eliminate only the affine physical-wire degree equations, using coordinates independent of the channel variables. Denote the resulting local phase by F(y,xi_1,...,xi_r). The remaining y coordinates are the original magnetic degrees of freedom; no assertion about their Hessian or framing quotient is made. Cups/caps and the degree constraints introduce no additional channel dependence. At the full endpoint xi_i=1/2, equations (5),(6) give exactly F_(xi,y)=0, F_(xi_i,xi_j)=-delta_ij 4pi i/tau_i (12) at a regular complete geometric point. Off-diagonal channel terms vanish because each local reduced coupon contains only its own channel. The mixed block remains zero under the actual affine degree restriction. In particular the channel block is invertible with negative definite REAL PART in these actual channel coordinates, independently of any magnetic degeneracies. For clarity this statement concerns the marked phase. The integers in (4) remain locally constant, and the original normal equation becomes stationary only in the corresponding specified Poisson sector. Equation (12) does not choose that sector's coefficient in the finite source. ## 5. A local channel elimination, with the color normalization retained There is a limited but useful implicit-function consequence. Subtract the recorded constants 2pi i n_i xi_i from F, and add the actual positive cosine-branch color coupling -2pi i sum_i (xi_i-1/2) chi_i. (13) At chi=0 every point y of a sufficiently small endpoint chart has the channel stationary solution xi_i=1/2. By (12) and continuity, the holomorphic implicit-function theorem solves all CHANNEL equations uniquely for xi=xi(y,chi), near the geometric point. This eliminates only those variables. It does not solve the remaining y equations. At the complete geometric point, partial xi_i/partial chi_j=-delta_ij tau_i/2. (14) The resulting channel-eliminated phase f(y,chi) obeys f_(chi_i,chi_j)=delta_ij pi i tau_i, f_(chi,y)=0, (15) at chi=0. Replacing the cosine sign changes both first derivatives and leaves (15) unchanged. For the displayed positive cosine branch the physical similarity logs are U_i=-2pi i chi_i and V_i=4pi i(xi_i-1/2), so (14) also gives V_i/U_i=tau_i to first order, with the original inverse-meridian sign. The transfer convention writing f''=2pi i tau_packet therefore has tau_packet=tau_geom/2, as already required in the explicitly solved Conway sources. There is no additional factor of two in (0) or (15). What this removes is a genuine local obstruction: the folded channel normal is nondegenerate, its sign is controlled, its mixed second-order coupling to the magnetic coordinates vanishes, and its peripheral coefficient is correctly normalized. What remains includes the magnetic critical scheme and its genuine gauge directions, a selected complex magnetic branch, the physical support/Poisson cycle, boundary and alias estimates, and a nonzero amplitude. The physical channel endpoint is still an endpoint of the finite folded summation domain; this theorem does not turn it into an interior finite-state saddle. Audit: [exact cusp and channel calculation](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_channel_hessian.py), [results](../experiments/actual_augmented_plat_channel_hessian_results.json). Independent character/current review: full analytical read and fresh audit PASS. The review checked the retained internal integer characters, implicit root derivatives, actual primitive cusp orientation and signed shear, both physical adapters, the channel-independent affine degree restriction and the channel-only implicit-function theorem. Six cusp cases and three rectangle/color-Hessian checks passed. No magnetic quotient rigidity, physical cycle or global source estimate is inferred.

title: The actual Casimir plat phase and its marked representation germ
status: Classical geometric branch; quantum selection open
text: # The actual Casimir plat phase and its marked representation germ 30 October 2026. On a regular chart at a complete geometric point, the constrained critical scheme of the ORIGINAL augmented-plat phase is isomorphic to the actual marked representation germ modulo one diagonal framing scale. This includes local Artin test rings, rather than only complex points or tangent dimensions. The proof reconstructs shared wire momenta from the event-incidence equations and supplies an inverse which is regular at the parabolic channel endpoint. The phase is the actual normalized Casimir/q-Hahn phase. This is not an application of the older braid-cut scheme claim with its different boundary state. Every original cup, ordinary cap, the unrestricted marked cap after its permitted whole-source degree restriction, and both physical degree adapters occur below. No quantum source quotient or asymptotic selection is asserted. ## 1. Objects and the precise local statement Fix a literal augmented plat, its retained half twists epsilon_v, and its actual outside wires. Its event graph has a vertex for each cup, cap or two-input/two-output circle coupon, and one directed edge for each physical wire between successive events. Identity segments are included in that wire. Let B be its oriented incidence matrix, with +1 at an incoming half-edge and -1 at an outgoing half-edge. The leading degree constraints are B x=b, b_cup=-1, b_cap=1, b_coupon=0. (1) Each connected component has equally many cups and caps, by counting its incoming and outgoing half-edges, so its entries of b sum to zero. The graph can have arbitrary cycles and width. We state the representation quotient for a CONNECTED event graph. The incidence construction below works componentwise without that assumption. A disconnected projection is a split diagram; contracting the connected local crossing-circle boxes does not change that connectivity. Thus the connected case includes an essential nonsplit augmented-plat diagram. Choose one of the actual low/high degree adapters at each coupon and a regular complete geometric point as in [the generic magnetic chart](actual_augmented_plat_regular_geometric_phase_chart.md). Fix its affine logarithmic lift of (1), its simple internal q-Hahn roots, and all logarithmic characters. All displayed local-map denominators, prefix diagonals, main K+1, and the chosen total F charts are units. We work in the corresponding formal neighborhood over C. The internal roots are eliminated by the exact marked critical reduction in [the channel-Hessian theorem](actual_augmented_plat_channel_hessian.md), not by substituting roots into an unadjusted phase. For each auxiliary circle retain its longitude eigenvalue J_v near -1 and prescribe its physical meridian eigenvalue m_v near 1. The channel equation is the ORIGINAL one R_(epsilon_v)=m_v^(-2). (2) The complete fiber has m_v=1. Equivalently the positive cosine branch uses m_v=exp(-pi i chi_v) and adds 2 Log(m_v)(xi_v-1/2) to the phase, with J_v=exp(2pi i xi_v). Let Crit be the formal scheme given by magnetic criticality on ker B and (2), with the retained integer characters. Let Rep be the actual Morse/ crossing-disk representation germ with the same peripheral marking: main meridians have their exact unipotent eigenvalue +1, auxiliary meridians have selected eigenvalue m_v, and the raw ordered disk product has selected eigenvalue J_v. All the same regular chart conditions hold. The main flag means the kernel of mu-I, NOT an arbitrary invariant line of a trace-two Artin matrix. The auxiliary flag is the selected J_v eigenline of its noncentral disk product. Then there is an isomorphism of formal functors Crit = Rep / T_diag, (3) where T_diag acts by simultaneous projective diagonal conjugation. The quotient has a concrete local slice: set the momentum S on one chosen physical wire to 1. Every such S is a unit. No reductive-quotient existence theorem or reduction of a nonreduced ring is needed for (3). Sections 2--6 give mutually inverse constructions over every local Artin C-algebra with the specified residue point. ## 2. Incidence criticality reconstructs all wire momenta Use physical half-edge variables before imposing (1). At a low coupon take the following ambient extension of its root-reduced phase: s=x_in,1+x_in,2, u=x_out,1, v=x_in,1, f_v=Theta_bar(s,u,v,xi). The second output is recovered by degree conservation. Write D, Y_in, Y_out for the ACTUAL derivatives in the local character note. The four exponentiated half-edge derivatives of this extension are incoming: (D Y_in,D), outgoing: (Y_out,1). (4) For a high coupon use the actual affine function Theta_bar(2-s,u-s+1,v-s+1,xi). Formula (4) remains true with D_high=1/(D Y_out Y_in) and the physical high head coordinates. Thus there is no separate high-degree gauge assumption. Let p_(v,e) be the local derivative of the chosen ambient extension and c_e=exp(sum_(v incident e) p_(v,e)). Magnetic criticality means product_e c_e^(l_e)=1 for every l in ker_Z B. (5) The integer cycle lattice is the full kernel: an oriented graph incidence matrix is saturated. A direct construction is enough here. Choose a spanning tree and one vertex value t_v0=1. Solve along its edges c_e=t_tail(e)/t_head(e). (6) Every non-tree edge satisfies (6) precisely because its fundamental cycle satisfies (5). This constructs unit vertex values over ANY commutative test ring. They are unique up to one common unit per connected component; no extraction of roots is involved. Now define the momentum at each incident half-edge by S_(v,e)=t_v exp(B_(v,e) p_(v,e)). (7) Equation (6) says exactly that the two definitions of S on a wire agree. At a coupon (4),(7) give S_in=(t_v D Y_in,t_v D), S_out=(t_v/Y_out,t_v). (8) This is the ORIGINAL local kernel formula with g=t_v D. Conversely shared momenta satisfying that formula give (7), hence (6),(5). Choosing another ambient extension changes its derivatives by a local multiple of the degree row and merely changes t_v, leaving S unchanged. In additive logarithmic language, (5) is grad F=B^t lambda after keeping the fixed integral character, and t_v=exp(-lambda_v). On a formal Artin neighborhood the exponential is injective on nilpotents. Thus the exponentiated equations and the exactly marked critical equations have the same infinitesimal scheme, not just the same complex zero set. The spanning-tree construction also proves the asserted saturation and the absence of hidden finite scale choices. ## 3. The actual boundary maps have precisely the inverse-pair relation On their actual forced degree fibers, the leading cup, ordinary cap and marked cap phases are respectively pi i(x_1-1), pi i x_1, pi i x_2. (9) The marked restriction x_1+x_2=1 follows only after all other actual caps and degree-preserving coupons act; it is not a local replacement of an unrestricted mark in a degree-changing source. Apply (7) with B=-1 at a cup and B=+1 at a cap. The two momenta are (-t,t) for the cup and ordinary cap, and (t,-t) for the marked cap. All three therefore give X_1 X_2=1, S_1/S_2=-1. (10) For an actual physical head use K=-1/X, F=S(1-X), E=(X^(-1)-1)/S, Lminus=[[1,0],[-KF,K]], G=[[K,E],[FK,FE+K^(-1)]]. (11) It has determinant one and trace -2. Its exact -1 eigenline is spanned by (1,S). Since K+1 is a unit, this kernel line is unique over the Artin ring; no nilpotent invariant-flag freedom is silently added. Equation (10) is equivalent to the actual based pair product P=I. For the converse, K_total=1 gives X_2=X_1^(-1), while F_total=(1-X_1)(S_1+S_2)=0 forces S_1=-S_2 because 1-X_1 is a unit. These are identities over the test ring. The ordinary and marked phases differ on the degree fiber by pi i-2pi i x_1; this retained integral character has the same exponentiated relation (10), but must not be deleted from the action. ## 4. A regular parabolic inverse for each actual coupon The local critical map reconstructs actual ordered pair matrices from (X,S), preserves their ENTIRE product P, and fixes Tr P=J+J^(-1). Conversely, given regular incoming and outgoing heads with that product, their ratios S_in,1/S_in,2 and S_out,2/S_out,1 determine their internal q-Hahn roots by the rational inverse (5) of the local map. The Jacobi equation is the actual trace equation, so these roots satisfy the two internal critical equations. Total-F preservation gives the exact D and therefore (8); the regular high adapter gives the same conclusion in the other physical chamber. The chosen simple roots eliminate any additional local root choice in this formal neighborhood. At J=-1 one MUST NOT divide by J-J^(-1) in an Artin ring. Here is an explicit replacement for the local conjugator formula. Put Q=P-J^(-1)I, A=A_in, A'=A_out, c=Tr([Q,A](A'-A)) / Tr([Q,A](Q A-A' Q)), C=I+cQ. (12) At the complete point Q=H=P+I and A'=A+b[H,A]-4b^2H. The denominator in (12) is Tr([H,A]([H,A]-4bH))=32, (13) using Tr([H,A]^2)=32 and Tr([H,A]H)=0. It is a unit throughout the formal neighborhood. The original generic conjugator identity now extends in this regular expression and gives C A C^(-1)=A', [C,P]=0, det C=R0=1+c(J-J^(-1)). (14) For precision, these rational identities hold on the smooth localized internal-root chart before imposing the global critical equations; their specialization therefore holds on nonreduced Artin test rings as well. This is not cancellation by a nonunit in such a test ring. Specify the selected auxiliary eigenvalue m and let h_J=J^(-1)-1, which is a unit near J=-1. The actual physical auxiliary meridian is C_aux=m R0 h_J^(-epsilon) C^(-1)(P^(-1)-I)^epsilon. (15) It has selected J-flag eigenvalue exactly m and det C_aux=m^2 R0(-J)^epsilon=1 (16) by (2). All inverses in (12),(15) are units. At completeness (15) is I+(epsilon/2-b)(P+I), exactly the original primitive collar matrix. Its inverse followed by the retained Hurwitz half twist induces C on the main pair. Thus the auxiliary is the literal disk-framed meridian, not a centralizer chosen only from its eigenvalue ratio. Conversely an actual auxiliary meridian with that eigenvalue commutes with P. Its inverse, composed with the retained half twist, transports the pair. Normalize this projective conjugator to have eigenvalue one on the J^(-1) flag. This divides by a unit even at the endpoint, because the commutant of the noncentral P is the free span of I,P. The normalized matrix is (12), and its eigenratio gives (2). The normalization and the conjugator are unique: at the complete pair a matrix commuting with P=-I+H has form aI+bH; commuting also with A forces b=0 since [H,A] has a unit entry. The same unit linear minor proves this assertion in the whole formal neighborhood. ## 5. Assemble the actual marked representation, and invert it From a critical point, section 2 supplies shared physical heads (11). At every horizontal slice prefix-transport them by their actual lower triangular matrices. The local coupon preserves P, and each cup/cap has P=I, so prefixes outside the event remain unchanged. Physical wires therefore carry the same based meridian at both ends. At each circle, (15) satisfies exactly the original threading relation [2,1,1,2] and the retained main Hurwitz move. These are the literal van Kampen relations of the drilled box; inverse-pair caps close the outside plat. They construct a representation of the actual marked augmented link. For the reverse construction start with that representation and its recorded Morse basepaths. If H_1,...,H_m are the raw trace -2 main meridians at a slice, let P_i=H_i ... H_1, P_0=I and use Bminus(P)=[[1,0],[-P_21,P_11]], G_i=Bminus(P_(i-1)) H_i Bminus(P_(i-1))^(-1), K_i=(P_i)_11/(P_(i-1))_11, X_i=-1/K_i, S_i=(G_i)_21/(K_i+1). (17) All denominators are units by the same regular chart. This is the explicit inverse of the actual prefix factorization. It remains valid over the Artin ring. The selected channel eigenvalue fixes the actual trace equation and its unique regular eigenline; the rational inverse from section 4 recovers the internal roots. The local maps then recover (8),(10), and section 2 gives magnetic criticality. No root is chosen by an order, norm, or independent semiclassical convention. Both constructions are inverse before quotienting, except for the one common scale in (6). Multiplying all momenta by t conjugates every matrix by diag(1,t) projectively: upper entries divide by t and lower entries multiply by t. The prefix construction respects that same conjugation. Setting one wire momentum to 1 removes exactly this freedom and proves (3) over all local Artin test rings. ## 6. Consequences and limits of the statement On the complete fiber m=1, (2) fixes J=-1 locally, scheme-theoretically. Indeed R_epsilon-1 vanishes identically on J=-1 and its J derivative there is 2b-epsilon=2/tau_geom, a unit at the actual complete cusp. The formal implicit-function theorem therefore gives J+1=0. This uses the primitive cusp normalization of the channel-Hessian theorem, not a semisimple endpoint quotient. At an irreducible geometric representation, changing the common projective frame supplies the PGL2 orbit; the diagonal scale above has already been quotiented. With the convention rho_g=g rho g^(-1), that scale acts on g by LEFT multiplication. Its two-dimensional local T_diag\PGL2 framing directions therefore remain in the critical scheme. Equation (3) identifies all its additional infinitesimal directions with actual marked representation deformations. This source equivalence alone does not exclude those additional deformations. The following corollary uses a separately checked geometric input. ## 7. With an actual positive certificate, the magnetic radical is exactly framing Assume additionally an ACTUAL marked positive complete ideal gluing certificate for this augmented exterior. The [multi-cusp marked rigidity theorem](general_marked_multicusp_gluing_rigidity.md) identifies its decorated representation germ modulo PGL2 with a smooth germ whose coordinates are the primitive peripheral eigenvalue logs. It proves this identification on Artin rings, with the exact main eigenvalue conditions used above. Fix all main eigenvalues to +1 and fix the auxiliary eigenvalues m. The unframed germ is then a point. The complete geometric representation is irreducible, so its framed germ is a smooth PGL2 orbit. Equation (3) and its explicit one-scale slice therefore prove Crit at fixed m is smooth of dimension two. (18) This assertion holds formally over nearby auxiliary eigenvalue parameters as well. The dimension comes from the actual T_diag\PGL2 framing quotient, not from deleting two presumed redundant equations or counting variables and equations. At completeness write F for the root-reduced phase after its affine degree restriction, in free magnetic coordinates y and channels xi. The scheme Crit is the zero scheme of its EXACTLY marked derivatives. Consequently its Zariski tangent space is the kernel of Hess F, even before any reducedness assertion. Equation (18) now proves that this kernel is precisely the two-dimensional framing tangent space. The independently proved channel calculation gives Hess F = [[F_yy,0],[0,diag(-4pi i/tau_geom,i)]]. (19) The channel diagonal is invertible. Hence the two framing directions are purely magnetic, and ker F_yy = tangent(T_diag\PGL2), dim ker F_yy=2. (20) There are no further magnetic infinitesimal null directions on this regular positive geometric germ. A local slice transverse to these actual frame directions has a nondegenerate holomorphic quadratic form. This supplies a classical normal form; it is not a computation of an actual source density, a finite quantum gauge factor, or a Gaussian coefficient on the physical summation cycle. ### A nearby classical stationary branch and its absolute action There is now also a holomorphic CLASSICAL stationary branch. Choose a local slice transverse to the two framing directions and keep the geometric sheet's integer Poisson characters fixed. The marked geometric implicit-function theorem solves the representation uniquely on that slice for m_i=exp(-pi i chi_i) near 1. Its critical value phi(chi) is independent of the transverse framing slice. Along the connected local framing orbit all internal derivatives vanish, so the value of the same marked phase is constant. This statement does not reset any additive period or change an integer mark. The auxiliary-color normalization can be checked directly in the [exact entire core](actual_augmented_plat_entire_core_color_packet.md). Its full-algebra identity centers (-1)^h T_h into cos[pi(N-2j-1)chi]. On the positive cosine branch the order-N coupling is EXACTLY pi i(1-2xi)chi. The finite -1 contributes exp(-pi i chi) to the amplitude, not a new term in the principal phase. The actual main cups/caps, kappa^epsilon factors and original exterior line have no auxiliary chi dependence in this packet. Their known leading constant phases are retained. In particular there is no additional order-N exterior color character to discard or calibrate by the volume. Envelope differentiation and the proved literal peripheral marking give partial_i phi=pi i(1-2xi_i), U_i=-2pi i chi_i, V_i=4pi i(xi_i-1/2), d(2pi i phi)=(1/2) sum_i V_i dU_i. (21) Here U,V are the centered projective meridian and preferred-longitude logs. The negative cosine sign requires the simultaneous reciprocal eigenflag convention stated in the local character note; it gives the same primitive differential with those consistently marked logs. An independently changed exterior color character would change the corresponding linear action/log mark and is not covered by silently reusing (21). The [absolute endpoint regulator comparison](actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.md) now applies to the complete point of this FULL stationary branch and fixes its value: 2pi Re phi(0)=Vol(Y_D). (22) Finally (21) and dV_i=tau_geom,i dU_i at completeness, or equivalently the channel elimination calculation, give phi_(chi_i,chi_j)(0)=delta_ij pi i tau_geom,i. (23) Thus the general transfer's parameter is tau_packet=tau_geom/2. These are statements about the actual marked PRINCIPAL action on its geometric sheet. They do not prove continuation from the locally lattice-selected q-Hahn roots, a nonzero finite-source cycle coefficient, or a uniform quantum packet with this action. The branch is called geometric here, not source-selected. ## 8. Scope This is a formal classical equivalence. It neither quotients the finite quantum coupon algebra nor replaces its co-source. It does not locate the point in a physical support chamber, continue the source-selected local branches to it, choose its Poisson coefficient, compute a nonzero amplitude, or bound any competing source. title: The actual augmented-plat endpoint action has its diagram regulator
text: # The actual augmented-plat endpoint action has its diagram regulator 30 October 2026. At the complete channel endpoint, the fully normalized q-Hahn coupon phase has the SAME Bloch–Wigner regulator as its original crossing-circle diagram, for every retained half twist. This is an absolute comparison: an exact rational wedge calculation gives a constant regulator difference, and a connected real chart proves that constant is zero. It is not an inference from matching peripheral derivatives. Consequently any regular, correctly marked geometric critical point of the assembled endpoint phase has critical rate equal to the volume of the actual augmented link. Existence of such a point on the source's required logarithmic sheet, a contributing cycle, and a nonzero controlled amplitude are separate questions. This note does not prove a source asymptotic. ## 1. The complete normalized endpoint symbol Use the ORIGINAL phase Theta_epsilon from [the local character calculation](actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md), equation (1), with its inverse-measure factor H, both q-Hahn columns, and the retained half twist epsilon in {0,+1,-1}. Write T=exp(2pi i tau), U=exp(2pi i u), V=exp(2pi i v), Z=exp(2pi i alpha), W=exp(2pi i beta). At xi=1/2, J=exp(2pi i xi)=-1 and J0(1/2)=0. Adding H to the two column factorial actions cancels the terms J0(tau-1/2). The remaining factorial part is J0(u)+J0(tau-u)+J0(v)+J0(tau-v) -2[J0(alpha)+J0(1/2-alpha)+J0(beta)+J0(1/2-beta)] -J0(u-alpha)-J0(tau-u-1/2+alpha) -J0(v-beta)-J0(tau-v-1/2+beta). (1) The retained polynomial phase is pi i [(u+v)/2+(tau-1/2)(alpha+beta) +tau+3(epsilon-1)/4]. (2) On the original factorial branch, 2pi i J0(s)=-Li2(exp(2pi i s)) +pi^2(s^2-s)+Li2(1). (3) One verifies (3) by differentiation from 0<s<1 and the common value at s=0, then analytically continues with the recorded logarithmic marks. Thus the Bloch symbol of 2pi i Theta_epsilon is B_H=B(U,Z)+B(V,W), B(X,z)=-[X]-[T/X]+2[z]+2[-1/z]+[X/z]+[-Tz/X]. (4) The half-twist term in (2) contributes a REAL constant to 2pi i Theta, so it contributes no regulator. It does still change the actual auxiliary meridian needed to realize the same main-input/main-output relation. Neither that change nor the coefficient 2 in (4) may be discarded. ## 2. A rational chart for the endpoint critical correspondence Both actual internal q-Hahn equations at J=-1 are rationally parameterized by Z=(a-1)/(a+1), U=T(a-1)^2/(Ta^2+1), W=(b-1)/(b+1), V=T(b-1)^2/(Tb^2+1). (5) Indeed a=(1+Z)/(1-Z), and direct substitution gives the quadratic P(U,Z)=0 of the local character calculation; the same holds for V,W. Every regular endpoint root is represented by this chart away from the listed denominators. The chart has coordinates (T,a,b) in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of C^3. A common nonzero magnetic scale can be fixed at one: it simultaneously conjugates the head matrices and does not change any crossing symbol below. For clarity all reconstructions use the actual physical head matrices K=-1/X, F=S(1-X), E=(X^-1-1)/S, Lminus=[[1,0],[-KF,K]], G=[[K,E],[FK,FE+K^-1]]. (6) Put Y(X,z)=-(1-X)(Tz+X)/[(X-z)(T-X)], D=ZW(T-U)(T-V)/[(TZ+U)(TW+V)]. (7) In the low physical degree chart the input heads (X,S) are (V,Y(V,W)), (T/V,1), and the output heads are (U,1/[D Y(U,Z)]), (T/U,1/D). (8) Let A=G1, B=Lminus1^-1 G2 Lminus1, P=BA, H=P+I. Then H is nonzero nilpotent and the endpoint transport is C=I+cH, c=(2Tab-Ta-Tb+a+b-2) /[2(T+1)(a-1)(b-1)]. (9) This follows either by multiplying the explicit matrices or by c=Tr([H,A]A_out)/32. In particular C A C^-1=A_out. The full ordered product P, including its Borel frame, is preserved. For the HIGH physical degree chart one must use the actual affine index adapter, rather than substitute the physical pair product into (4). Its input and output heads are respectively (V/T,Y(V,W)), (1/V,1), (U/T,D Y(V,W)), (1/U,D Y(U,Z)Y(V,W)). (10) The low variables in (4),(5),(7) remain unchanged. The exact finite high-block identification has no extra phase or scalar. Formula (6) with (10), followed by c=Tr([H,A]A_out)/32, gives exactly the same coefficient (9) in the high physical chart. The executable certificate checks it independently with the same original crossing rule below. ## 3. Reconstruct the actual auxiliary meridian and every crossing The positive Hurwitz half twist on a trace -2 pair is simultaneous conjugation by P^-1-I. At P=-I+H its projective normalization is I+H/2. Therefore the raw, trace -2 auxiliary meridian for the original coupon R^epsilon L_N is C_aux,raw=-[I+(epsilon/2-c)H]. (11) This sign is its actual complete raw lift; the corresponding physical meridian has trace +2. The literal threading word [2,1,1,2] transports the main pair by C_aux^-1 and closes the auxiliary because it commutes with P. Composing its main half twist gives total conjugator I+cH. This uses the [proved original peripheral word](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md), not an assigned auxiliary longitude. To recover the actual THIRD Gauss head from (11), let L=Lminus2 Lminus1 and set G3=L C_aux,raw L^-1. Its coordinates are K3=(G3)11, E3=(G3)12, F3=(G3)21/K3. (12) Now execute chronological adjacent crossings [2,1,1,2], and then the signed main crossing R^epsilon if epsilon is nonzero. All maps here are rational. For two input heads (k,e,f),(l,g,h), the original positive crossing, with d=1-eh, is (ld, [dg+e(dl-l^-1)]/k, kh/d), (k/d, e/(ld), l[df+h(d/k-k)]). (13) With physical clocks A0=-1/k, B0=-1/l its five-dilog symbol is [B0]+[1/d]+[1/A0]-[B0/d]-[1/(dA0)]. (14) The original negative crossing has c0=1-(B0/A0)gf and outputs (lc0, kg, f+h/k-f/(l^2c0)), (k/c0, le+g-k^2g/c0, f/l), (15) with symbol [A0]+[c0]+[1/B0]-[A0c0]-[c0/B0]. (16) Call the sum of these FOUR or FIVE actual symbols B_disk,epsilon. Direct rational substitution checks all nine final Gauss coordinates: the first two heads are exactly (8) or (10), and the auxiliary head is exactly (12) again. Thus this is the actual original closed circle, not an abstract centralizer with a missing closing/pivot convention. The closing pivot is a monomial; its complete leading contribution and the main marked cup/cap phases are included in (2) and the global source characters. They contribute no extra dilogarithm symbol. A monomial can still change an action value off stationarity; section 5 treats that point explicitly. ## 4. Exact wedge identity and absolute real normalization With delta[z]=z wedge (1-z), the following identity holds over the rational function field Q(T,a,b), for BOTH physical degree charts and all epsilon in {0,+1,-1}: delta(B_H-B_disk,epsilon)=0. (17) Here is a finite algebraic certificate for (17), including its procedure so no fitted regulator or floating point identity is involved. Use (5) in (4); construct B_disk by (6)--(16); factor every argument and its complement into irreducible polynomials over Q. For an argument z write v_z for its integer exponent vector, retaining positive rational prime factors as well as polynomial factors. Then expand sum_(coefficient n, argument z) n (v_z v_(1-z)^t-v_(1-z) v_z^t). (18) The matrices from (4) and (14),(16) are identical. Only the torsion sign -1 is removed in this rational exterior square; factors such as 2 are kept. The accompanying audit performs precisely (18), symbolically, and records every rational argument and the empty difference matrix. It also independently checks (9)--(13) and the complete auxiliary closure. Thus (17) is an identity of rational functions, not evidence from a finite sample of shapes. One compact form of the COMMON wedge, useful for checking the expansion without comparing two large symbol lists, is as follows. Put A_r=2Tr-T+1, B_r=Tr-r+2, F_r=Tr^2+1. Then BOTH sides expand to 2 T wedge (T+1) +sum_(r=a,b) [ A_r wedge T - A_r wedge F_r +2 A_r wedge (r-1) + B_r wedge F_r -2 B_r wedge (r-1) + F_r wedge r +2 r wedge (r-1) ]. (18a) There are exactly fifteen nonzero coefficients in this polynomial-factor basis. In particular the mixed factors involving both a and b from the actual four-crossing diagram cancel; this is a global identity for the whole coupon, not equality of independent crossing maxima. For any Bloch symbol B the differential of its Bloch–Wigner regulator factors through delta B: dD(z)=log|z| dArg(1-z)-log|1-z| dArg z. Therefore (17) makes D(B_H-B_disk,epsilon) constant on its regular complex parameter chart. This chart is connected: it is obtained from C^3 by deleting finitely many proper polynomial hypersurfaces, and two generic points can be joined by complex lines avoiding their finitely many excluded intersection points. Every rational expression has real coefficients, so the chart contains a generic real point. At that point every argument is real and every Bloch–Wigner value is zero. Consequently D(B_H)=D(B_disk,epsilon). (19) This is the required ABSOLUTE regulator identity. Wedge equality alone would not prove it. Nor does (19) claim equality of integral Bloch classes, flattenings, or complex periods: rational wedge zero can retain information not measured by D. Changes of logarithmic sheet must continue to carry the original integer marks in the action. ## 5. Assemble the actual diagram and the critical action Apply (19) at every original twist-region coupon. The actual disk words and retained half crossings, with the actual outside wires and caps, form the original augmented-link diagram. The crossing-block proof in [the marked fundamental-cycle calculation](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md), sections 2--4, is componentwise: its local octahedral balls, arc-strip face identifications, and degree-one cusp truncation apply to this multi-component diagram as well. No step joins different components or replaces their preferred peripheral paths. The knot-only shortcut H2(M)=0 is NOT used: for a compact connected oriented link exterior H3(M)=0, so the exact sequence makes H3(M,partial M) -> H2(partial M) injective. The displayed degree-one cycle on EACH oriented cusp is precisely the boundary of the relative fundamental class, and hence fixes the relative class uniquely. Accidental developed crossing degeneracies can be avoided by adding their finitely many divisors to the generic frame exclusions, or handled by the continuous extension D(0)=D(1)=D(infinity)=0. Thus at the complete geometric representation sum_regions D(B_H)=Vol(actual augmented link). (20) One can use an actual positive gluing certificate to supply that geometric representation; (20) does not assume convexity of a particular source polytope or independently maximize individual regions. To pass from a Bloch symbol to the ORIGINAL action value, keep the full stationarity condition. In logarithmic variables z=rho+i theta the assembled action G=2pi i phi has the form G=sum n_j Li2(exp(a_j dot z+i pi nu_j)) +(1/2)z^t C z+i k dot z+c0, with real a_j,nu_j,C,k and Im c0=0, and C symmetric. This follows directly from (1)--(3), the original monomial cup/cap phases, and the retained integer logarithmic characters. For matching branches the exact identity is Im G-sum n_j D(exp(a_j dot z+i pi nu_j)) =rho dot Im(gradient G). (21) It follows by expanding Im Li2, the real quadratic, and the imaginary linear term; the full proof is in the repo's [wall regulator calculation](actual_wall_critical_regulator.md), section 3. At a FULL stationary point on the recorded marked sheet the right side vanishes. If the channel is held at its endpoint rather than varied, its logarithm is log J=i pi modulo 2pi i and has rho_J=0, so its unsolved normal derivative contributes nothing to (21). All remaining free magnetic and internal variables still require their actual stationary equations. A constrained endpoint extremum in some other complex variable is not enough. Therefore, whenever the complete geometric character is realized by a regular correctly marked full critical point of this actual endpoint phase, 2pi Re phi(0)=Im G(0)=Vol(actual augmented link). (22) The original exterior framing factors of unit modulus add real constants to G and preserve (22). Equation (22) fixes the complete-volume ANCHOR needed alongside the proved primitive differential dG=(1/2) sum_i V_i dU_i. It does not prove a global lift to the required source sheet, a quantum cycle coefficient, a nonzero leading amplitude, a bound on competing or singular regions, or a mixed-color complex corridor. In particular no source limit or general long-filling theorem follows from (22) alone. Audit: [exact six-chart regulator comparison](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator.py), [recorded results](../experiments/actual_augmented_plat_endpoint_regulator_results.json). Independent character/current review: full analytical read and fresh audit PASS for both physical degree charts and all three retained half-twist choices (six exact cases, 54 final Gauss coordinates, six rational wedge identities and eighteen Bloch–Wigner checks).
