title: An exact phase compiler for arbitrary fixed augmented plats
text: # An exact phase compiler for arbitrary fixed augmented plats 30 October 2026. Every fixed 2k-head plat made from the ORIGINAL complete crossing-circle coupons R^epsilon L_N, epsilon in {0,+1,-1}, has an explicit finite factorial sum with its entire original phase. There is no restriction on k>=2 or on the graph formed by its twist regions. The physical q-Hahn sums simplify: their internal quadratic phases cancel exactly, leaving a single linear Fourier phase. The resulting internal critical equation is a quadratic polynomial. This is a source-exact complete-color statement. It supplies an explicit global phase and finite algebraic candidate equations. It does not select their geometric branch, prove a global contour/gap, or supply a mixed-color filling corridor. Thus it is an advance toward a theorem for arbitrary fixed sufficiently twisted plats, not that volume theorem itself. A proposed twist threshold T(D) depends on the fixed skeleton D; it is distinct from quantum level N. ## 1. The phase of the actual physical Casimir column Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d=-q^-1, kappa=q^(d^2/2), and s_n=product_(r=1)^n 2sin(pi r/N). For 0<=b<=a<=d write the POSITIVE sine binomial beta(a,b)=s_a/(s_b s_(a-b)). Let t<=d be an actual low physical pair degree, j a Casimir index, and 0<=u<=t. The actual canonical eigenvector of the physical pair Casimir has first entry one and components f_u(c_j), with c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1). Its already proved finite q-Hahn formula is f_u(c_j)=x^(t-j)/[t choose j]_Q sum_a (-1)^a x^[-(t-j-u+2a)] Q^[a(a-1)/2+a(t-j-u+a)] [j choose a]_Q [u choose a]_Q [t-u choose j-a]_Q, max(0,u-t+j)<=a<=min(j,u). (1) All factorial indices are below N. In particular (1) describes the original physical column, not an arbitrarily normalized eigenbasis. The elementary marked identity [v choose w]_Q=q^[w(v-w)] beta(v,w) turns (1) into the simpler exact formula f_u(c_j)=(-1)^u q^[-(j+1)u] sum_a (-1)^a q^[a(t+j+1)] E(t,j,u,a), E(t,j,u,a)=beta(j,a) beta(u,a) beta(t-u,j-a)/beta(t,j)>0. (2) Indeed the complete exponent of q inside (1) is -u+2a+a(a-1)+2a(t-j-u+a) +a(j-a)+a(u-a)+(j-a)(t-u-j+a)-j(t-j) =a(t+j+1)-(j+1)u. (3) The a^2 terms cancel. No factorial envelope or asymptotic estimate is used in this cancellation. On every channel that survives the COMPLETE circle, d-j<=t and j<=floor(d/2). Put delta=t+j-d. Since (-1)^a=q^(-Na), (2) is f_u(c_j)=(-1)^u q^[-(j+1)u] sum_a q^(delta a) E(t,j,u,a), 0<=delta<=floor(d/2). (4) Thus the summation variable carries a positive-coefficient polynomial at one specified Fourier argument q^delta. Its entire phase is retained; positivity of its coefficients does not imply positivity or a lower bound for that value. ## 2. Complete signed coupons in every original degree Take an arbitrary physical pair degree S in 0,...,2d. Set t=min(S,2d-S), shift=max(0,S-d). Use physical basis |shift+u,S-shift-u>, 0<=u<=t. The high block is literally the low block under this index translation, for both the Casimir and original signed crossing. For every j with j<d-j<=t the full reflected-circle resolution has positive coefficient h_(t,j)=2s_t^2/[s_(t-j)s_(t+j-d)]. If N is odd and j=d/2<=t, use the same formula WITHOUT the factor 2. No other channel contributes. Let nu_j=(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)]. Then the EXACT all-input kernel of B_epsilon=R^epsilon L_N is B_epsilon[u,v]=kappa^epsilon x^(-t) sum_j h_(t,j) nu_j^(epsilon-1) f_u(c_j) f_v(c_j). (5) This is bilinear in the two physical columns, not Hermitian. To prove it, start with the actual positive reflected tensor H=L_N P=sum_j h v_j v_j^*. Its normalized last component is (v_j)_t=x^t nu_j, and literal reversal gives P conjugate(v_j)=conjugate(x^t nu_j) v_j. Hence L_N=H P has coefficient h x^-t nu_j^-1 times v_j v_j^T. On this actual complete-circle image, R acts by kappa nu_j. At a double root its normal correction annihilates L_N: the latter is its derivative times the square-zero Jordan operator. At the odd simple root the value calculation is immediate. This proves (5) for both signs, all parities and all physical degree blocks. Thus the normal directions responsible for L_N have been evaluated exactly BEFORE the rank-one image is used. Formula (5) is not an initial semisimple quotient, and it does not identify an arbitrary generic-q germ with its root values. Substitution of (4) makes each (j,a,b) contribution to (5) the positive factorial weight h_(t,j) E(t,j,u,a) E(t,j,v,b) times kappa^epsilon (-1)^[t+(epsilon-1)j+u+v] q^[t+(epsilon-1)j(j+1)-(j+1)(u+v)+delta(a+b)]. (6) Equation (6) is the complete physical coupon phase. In particular the two internal summation variables have no individual square term. ## 3. Compile any fixed augmented 2k-plat Fix the positions and order of the twist regions in a literal 2k-head plat. Augment every chosen region by its ORIGINAL auxiliary circle and retain its prescribed parity epsilon. Use the original bottom cups, ordinary top caps and ONE unrestricted marked top cap: p_ab=N x^-b delta_(a+b,d), ell_ab=x^a delta_(a+b,d)/N, m_ab=x^b/N^2. (7) The original exterior line chi_N, including framing, stays explicit. All crossing-circle coupons and any remaining original crossings preserve integer degree. Only after the k-1 ordinary top caps have acted does total degree kd force the marked pair degree to d. This is the permitted whole-source restriction; m is not replaced locally in a separated degree-changing sector. Expand every augmented coupon by (5), or further by (6). Sum every actual physical wire index, channel j and internal q-Hahn index. Unchanged identity wires identify their labels. The resulting finite sum is EXACTLY chi_N times the original marked plat contraction. There is no inverse Clebsch matrix, recoupling determinant, fitted boundary vector, or division by a knot value in this construction. The powers in (7) multiply to N^-1; all other powers, phases and factorials are those in (5)--(6). Each kappa^epsilon is retained as its explicit external unit phase, not reset to one. For a fixed skeleton this is a finite union of rational affine state polytopes. The low/high choices t=S or t=2d-S give finitely many chambers. Every surviving channel and internal summation range is an explicit linear inequality, such as d-j<=t, 2j<=d, max(0,u-t+j)<=a<=min(j,u). All lattice offsets from d=N-1 and both parity endpoint weights are kept in the exact formulas. The number of states is bounded by a power of N depending on the fixed diagram. Augmentation removes the large full-twist powers from the number of blocks; those fixed filling parameters are not extra copies of a quantum-level dependent packet. This also computes the physical coefficient tensor entering the [marked multiport Chebyshev packet](actual_marked_multiport_chebyshev_source_packet.md). That packet's correct C,...,C,H conjugation and final half-bandwidth fold may be applied afterward. Neither its polynomial DCT cost nor this exact compiler proves a sharp coherent energy bound. ## 4. An explicit global action and a local quadratic critical equation Let J(z)=integral_0^z Log(2sin(pi w))dw with the marks continued from positive factorial arguments. Put B(v,w)=J(v)-J(w)-J(v-w). For scaled labels (tau,xi,upsilon,alpha)=(t,j,u,a)/N the real factorial action of E is Ecal=B(xi,alpha)+B(upsilon,alpha) +B(tau-upsilon,xi-alpha)-B(tau,xi). (8) Its exact leading complex phase after (4) is Ecal+pi i[upsilon-xi*upsilon +(tau+xi-1)alpha]. (9) The finite +1 terms and d=N-1 differences give specified order-one amplitude/phase corrections; they are recovered from (4), not discarded. For a whole coupon add two copies of (8), the h action 2J(tau)-J(tau-xi)-J(tau+xi-1), (10) and the exact polynomial phase read from (6). Include the source characters from (7). Summing these functions over the original network gives its explicit global candidate phase. Uniform factorial errors are O_D(log N) even at endpoints; this alone bounds the absolute term envelope, not the coherent sum from below. There is a particularly simple algebraic equation for an INTERNAL q-Hahn stationary variable. The derivative of (8) exponentiates to sin(pi(xi-alpha))^2 sin(pi(upsilon-alpha)) / [sin(pi alpha)^2 sin(pi(tau-upsilon-xi+alpha))]. (11) The phase in (9) supplies exp(pi i(tau+xi-1)). Set T=exp(2pi i tau), Jc=exp(2pi i xi), U=exp(2pi i upsilon), Z=exp(2pi i alpha). With the original logarithmic marks and away from the displayed pole divisors, exp(partial_alpha Phi)=1 is exactly T(Jc-Z)^2(U-Z)+(Z-1)^2(TZ-U Jc)=0. (12) Its cubic terms cancel. The remaining quadratic coefficients are A=T(2Jc+U-2)-U Jc, B=T(1-Jc^2-2Jc U)+2U Jc, C=U Jc(T Jc-1), A Z^2+B Z+C=0. (13) The degree is at most two on special parameter loci; no division by A is made. Such degenerations and the specified pole divisors must remain in any branch analysis. The complete global stationarity equations likewise become explicit rational Laurent equations after exponentiating the original wire variables and clearing ONLY specified nonzero denominators. Thus finite algebraic candidate-branch and Jacobian tests are available at arbitrary fixed bridge width. Pole exclusions, logarithmic marks, boundary sectors and the original finite cycle remain part of the problem. A solution of (12) has not thereby been identified with a geometric tetrahedron or an A-polynomial branch. ## 5. Why the real positive saddle criterion does not automatically apply This exact phase also locates an obstruction. At a real strict complete-image channel, 0<tau+xi-1<1/2. The factorial logarithmic derivative (11) is positive real, while the derivative phase has argument strictly between 0 and pi/2. Consequently an interior real alpha cannot solve the stationary equation even after subtracting an integer Poisson frequency. Equivalently, the representation before (4) has imaginary derivative between 2pi and 5pi/2; its retained integer mark removes 2pi and leaves exactly the phase in (9). On the boundary delta=0 the finite q-Hahn sum in (4) IS positive, but this is one channel boundary, not a theorem that the whole augmented source concentrates there. The odd simple channel and even endpoint pairs must also remain in any endpoint analysis. Thus the real-concave version of the [analytic sewing criterion](actual_six_port_analytic_sewing_criterion.md) cannot be applied to this raw expanded phase by ignoring its Fourier factor. One needs a source-preserving complex deformation, a selected local resummation, or another exact period representation, followed by a global boundary/gap and nonzero-period argument. The quadratic (12) makes the local candidate branches explicit; it does not choose their original-cycle coefficients. The mixed ordinary-circle colors required by long Dehn filling need a separate extension as well. Audit: [physical Casimir columns, full signed coupons and marked plats](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.py). The fresh audit passes N=2,...,10: 99 original degree blocks, 704 canonical-column entries, all three signed complete coupon identities in every block, and eight literal marked plat contractions at k=2,3,4. Its matrices are built independently from the original coproduct and signed crossings, not from the q-Hahn formula being checked. The symbolic phase cancellation and quadratic degree are also checked exactly. These are source-identity checks, not numerical evidence for an unproved all-plat volume limit. Independent internal analytical review checked the physical high-degree translation, bilinear CD normalization, retained first normal, original cup/cap powers, complete phase cancellation and rational stationary equation. A separate reader and the primary agent freshly replayed the operator/marked-plat audit: PASS. This certifies the finite compiler, not its missing mixed-color packet or geometric cycle selection.

title: A finite criterion for a physical magnetic framing
status: Finite framing tests; right-angled obstruction follows
text: # A finite criterion for a physical magnetic framing **Subsequent scope result (30 October):** the [right-angled obstruction and localization](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) proves that no common all-central selected frame exists for the actual certified right-angled plat cut. Generic geometric strip flags have exactly two strict physical-support failures, at arbitrary bridge width. The local conditional statements below remain valid; their simultaneous realization in that right-angled class cannot supply the general proof. 30 October 2026. This note reduces the simultaneous framing question for the actual complete augmented-plat character to a strict semialgebraic feasibility problem in one rank-one projector. It also treats the smaller central domain used by the joint accretive determinant. The criterion keeps every original prefix word and both actual degree adapters. There is no assertion that this feasibility problem always has a solution. The positive gluing certificate and the regular critical-scheme theorem do not by themselves prove that assertion. In particular, a nonempty real-open set of perfectly regular frames fails physical support at any one essential crossing disk. The obstruction below explains why merely avoiding algebraic divisors cannot settle the issue. ## 1. The common frame is a rank-one projector Fix the actual marked geometric representation and its finite original Morse word. For its prefix matrices Q use the same trace -2 main lifts as in the [regular magnetic chart](actual_augmented_plat_regular_geometric_phase_chart.md). A simultaneous projective frame g, modulo LEFT diagonal changes, is equivalently Pi=g^(-1) E_11 g, Pi^2=Pi, tr Pi=1, det Pi=0. (1) Indeed the two eigenspaces of Pi have distinct eigenvalues 1 and 0, so every such projector is obtained this way; its stabilizer is precisely the projective diagonal torus. This is the same two-dimensional complex framing quotient as in the [actual critical scheme](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md). Every needed prefix diagonal is the LINEAR function a_Q=tr(Q Pi)=(g Q g^(-1))_11. (2) At an input of a crossing-circle coupon put Q_0=W, Q_1=A W, Q_2=P W, P=B A, a_i=tr(Q_i Pi). For the output, replace A by the actual outgoing first meridian A'; Q_0 and Q_2 are unchanged. The original two physical wire phases are X_1=-a_0/a_1, X_2=-a_1/a_2, T=X_1 X_2=a_0/a_2. (3) We always impose the other finitely many regular-chart nonvanishings from the cited chart theorem. No independent local change of frame is permitted in (2). ## 2. Exact strict-support criterion For a nonzero X off the positive real axis choose its wire logarithm by x=Log_(0,2pi)(X)/(2pi i), 0<Re x<1. (4) Write s=x_1+x_2. The actual low adapter is tau=s, u=x_1; the high adapter is tau=2-s, u=1-x_2. At the complete channel the strict local physical domain is 1/2<Re tau<1, 0<Re u<Re tau. (5) For three nonzero prefix diagonals, (4)--(5) hold if and only if Im(a_0 conjugate(a_2)) != 0, 0 is not in the real convex hull of {a_0,a_1,a_2}. (6) Here the low or high adapter is determined, rather than freely chosen. The second condition is equivalent to the existence of one open half-plane through the origin containing all three numbers. Proof. Rotate a_0 to the positive axis. Under the convex-hull condition the three arguments have lifts arg a_0=0, arg a_2=delta in (-pi,pi), arg a_1=beta, max(0,beta,delta)-min(0,beta,delta)<pi. The first condition in (6) says delta is neither 0 nor an endpoint. The canonical physical arguments are consequently 2pi Re x_1=pi-beta, 2pi Re x_2=pi+beta-delta. (7) Their sum is 2pi-delta. Thus delta>0 gives the low adapter, delta<0 gives the high adapter, and Re tau=1-|delta|/(2pi) in (1/2,1). Both inequalities for u follow from 0<Re x_i<1: in the low case tau-u=x_2, and in the high case tau-u=1-x_1. Conversely (5) puts the sum of the two wire arguments strictly between pi and 3pi and away from 2pi. The inverse formulas (7) put the three prefix arguments in an interval of width less than pi. This proves (6). The input and output have the same a_0,a_2. Their prescribed adapter therefore agrees. Their canonical sums agree in real part by (7) and in imaginary part by X_1 X_2=T. Thus degree conservation holds as an EXACT complex equality, not only after exponentiation. At a cup or cap the first and last prefix words agree. The corresponding condition is simply that a_1/a_0 is not a nonpositive real number; all diagonals are nonzero. Then X_2=X_1^(-1) and their canonical logarithms sum exactly to 1. Applying these tests at every event makes the chosen wire logarithms solve the original affine incidence equations Bx=b without any additional integer adjustment. Ordinary and marked cap characters are still the distinct characters recorded in the source. ## 3. The central joint domain has an even simpler test The central domain adds |2 Re u-Re tau|<1/2 (8) to (5). This is the leading open domain Re c>0, Re z>0 for c=-cos(pi tau), z=exp[pi i(tau-2u)]. The exact finite c has tau+1/N in place of tau; any compact subset of (5),(8) satisfies its corresponding inequality for large N. For BOTH actual adapters, tau-2u=x_2-x_1. (9) Consequently the central condition is adapter-independent. In physical wire real parts it is the diamond |Re x_1-1/2|+|Re x_2-1/2|<1/2, Re(x_1+x_2) != 1. (10) An exact test using only the prefix diagonals is Im(a_0 conjugate(a_2)) != 0, |a_2| Re(a_1 conjugate(a_0)) +|a_0| Re(a_1 conjugate(a_2)) > 0. (11) Proof. In the argument lifts above, (8) is |2 beta-delta|<pi. This says precisely that a_1 lies in the open half-plane centered at the bisector of the MINOR angular interval from a_0 to a_2. The vector a_0/|a_0|+a_2/|a_2| points along that bisector. Taking the scalar product with a_1 gives (11). Conversely the resulting interval delta/2-pi/2<beta<delta/2+pi/2, with |delta|<pi, puts all three arguments in an interval of width less than pi. Thus (11) itself implies (6), as well as (8). This extra inequality is substantial: same-side disk flags, or merely being in the larger physical strip (5), does not imply (11). ## 4. A finite semialgebraic feasibility problem Equations (1),(2),(6) give a finite strict semialgebraic test for a simultaneous physical magnetic frame. One can encode the convex-hull test with one complex separator n_f per input/output triple: |n_f|^2=1, Re(n_f a_(f,i))>0 for i=0,1,2. For the central domain there are no separator choices. Introduce positive real r_(f,0),r_(f,2) with r_(f,i)^2=|a_(f,i)|^2 and require r_(f,2) Re(a_(f,1) conjugate(a_(f,0))) +r_(f,0) Re(a_(f,1) conjugate(a_(f,2))) > 0. (12) Also require the square of Im(a_(f,0) conjugate(a_(f,2))) to be positive, impose the cup/cap tests, and retain every regular-chart nonvanishing. All coefficients are algebraic when the actual marked representation is algebraic. Only one projector Pi is shared by the whole diagram. This formulation is suitable for an exact feasibility or infeasibility certificate; it is not a collection of independent local frame choices. A strict feasible frame persists under sufficiently small changes of the marked representation. The strict inequalities give a common positive margin on the finite set of triples, and all denominators remain nonzero. In particular it would persist for sufficiently long fillings once obtained at completeness. This persistence does not obtain the initial frame. Nor does (12) make the pair totals real: their imaginary parts come from the moduli of the prefix ratios. A theorem continuing only u at fixed real t,j cannot be applied to these generally complex totals. Even a joint domain requires comparing its selected internal roots with the actual geometric roots, and subsequently controlling the contributing global finite-source cycle. ### A finite family sharing one disk product is always feasible There is a constructive positive result: all input/output triples from any fixed finite family of transports sharing the SAME product P and prefix W can be made central simultaneously. This does not couple different disk products or different prefixes. Normalize A,P as in (13), put H=P+I, and write its transported splits as A_b=(I+bH)A(I-bH), with b in the given finite complex set. This includes every complete centralizer transport and any retained finite half-twist shifts. For a>0 put h=sqrt(2a+1) and take the projector L_a=[[1+a/2+i h/2, (a-1)/4+i h/2], [-a-1, -a/2-i h/2]]. (12a) Direct multiplication gives L_a^2=L_a, tr L_a=1, tr(P L_a)=1, tr(A L_a)=a, tr([H,A] L_a)=-4i h, tr(A_b L_a)=a-4i b sqrt(2a+1)-8b^2. (12b) For the finite b-set the last expression is a+O(sqrt(a)), uniformly as a tends to positive infinity. It therefore has positive real part for every b once a is large enough. The central scalar inequality in (11), with endpoints 1,1, is then strictly positive for every triple. Only its T=1 seam remains. These finitely many scalar inequalities hold on an open neighborhood of L_a in the complex projector surface. The nonconstant function tr(P L) cannot be real on any such open neighborhood. A sufficiently small perturbation therefore removes the seam, and gives all the strict central tests. For an arbitrary shared prefix W, recover the actual common projector by Pi=W^(-1)L/tr(W^(-1)L). (12c) It is rank-one of trace one, and its actual prefix diagonals are one common nonzero scalar times tr(L),tr(A_b L),tr(P L). Thus the central inequalities are unchanged. The additional trace in (12c) does not vanish identically on the projector surface: otherwise ell(W^(-1)v)=0 for every ell(v)=1, forcing W^(-1)=0. Hence its zero set cannot contain the feasible open neighborhood. The perturbation can simultaneously avoid this trace, the seam, and the finitely many proper regular-chart divisors. This proves the assertion for W as well, rather than assuming the W=I projector survives unchanged. The construction is a precise favorable near-coincident-frame mechanism at ONE auxiliary flag. It proves that each coupon's incoming and outgoing central inequalities are locally compatible. It leaves the genuinely simultaneous problem (12), with the actual different products and prefixes of the full plat, unresolved. ## 5. A geometric necessary condition and an open obstruction There is a useful uniform restriction on possible solutions. At one essential complete disk normalize its distinct puncture flags so that A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], P=B A=[[1,1],[-4,-3]]. (13) This normalization follows directly from Tr A=Tr B=Tr P=-2. The circle through the three parabolic flags is then the real circle. Write Pi=v ell with ell(v)=1, put w=ker ell, and put z=Wv. These are projective points; z is the right framing point transported by the ACTUAL prefix W. If (6) holds, then z and w lie in the same open side of this circle. (14) In particular replacing z by v in this test would be incorrect. Here is a direct proof. For real r=(r_0,r_1,r_2) set M(r)=r_0 I+r_1 A+r_2 P. The matrices in this pencil are real-linearly independent and det M=2(r_0^2+r_1^2+r_2^2)-(r_0+r_1+r_2)^2. (15) Suppose z,w are in opposite open half-planes. The condition M(r)z=w is two homogeneous real linear equations in three r's, so it has a nonzero solution. M(r) cannot annihilate a nonreal z: its real and imaginary vector parts are linearly independent, which would force M=0. The real Möbius transformation identity Im M(z)=det(M) Im(z)/|M_21 z+M_22|^2 therefore gives det M<0. Normalize the sign so that sum r_i>0. Equation (15) forces every r_i>0: if, for example, r_0<=0, then det M=(r_1-r_2)^2+r_0^2-2r_0(r_1+r_2)>=0, because r_1+r_2>0. This is a contradiction. Now 0=ell(M(r)Wv)=r_0 a_0+r_1 a_1+r_2 a_2. This is a strictly positive convex relation after division by sum r_i, contradicting (6). If z is nonreal and w is on the real circle, the same argument gives det M=0 and r_i>=0, still a nontrivial convex relation. If z is on the real circle, solve instead M(r)z=0, again two real equations in three unknowns. The same det=0 argument gives r_i>=0 and the same relation for every w. The point at infinity is handled in homogeneous coordinates, or by a real change of disk coordinates. Thus a good triple must satisfy (14). This is a necessary condition, not a converse. The opposite-side choice is a nonempty REAL-OPEN condition on the common framing quotient. It also allows v and w to be distinct, as required for a projector. The common regular-frame locus is a complex Zariski open dense subset by the cited chart theorem. It intersects this real-open bad set: a nonzero holomorphic polynomial cannot vanish on a real-open subset of this complex manifold. Hence EVERY such complete character has common regular frames that fail physical support already at this disk. This conclusion holds independently of whether the representation has a positive gluing certificate. For a small exact illustration use W=I, v=(i,1), ell=(1,i)/(2i), so w=-i. Equations (13) give (a_0,a_1,a_2)=(1,-1+i/2,-1-5i/2), (1/2)a_0+(5/12)a_1+(1/12)a_2=0. (16) The endpoint discriminant numerator is a_0 a_1+a_1 a_2+a_0 a_2=1/4, and the leading-coefficient numerator a_0+a_2+4a_1=-4-i/2; both are nonzero. Thus this support failure is not just the local root-discriminant failure. Formula (16) is only a local illustration; the preceding open-density argument deals with all the other regular divisors of the actual finite diagram. Near-coincident framing points do not evade (14). In the limit w=v, each condition concerns v and Wv on its own developed disk circle. The different prefixes W are fixed words of the representation, not small perturbations of the identity. No simultaneous same-side or central-domain conclusion follows just by taking w close to v. ## 6. What an ordinary fixed-total fiber estimate does and does not say At fixed real discrete t,j, the proved magnetic corridor can be multiplied over a fixed finite number of ORDINARY q-Hahn column factors. Pull their magnetic u variables back by affine wire maps preserving every such total. On a compact subset of the common corridors, the relative errors multiply to 1+O(1/N), the leading actions add, and the nonzero amplitudes multiply. An already evaluated normal-derived coefficient depending only on these fixed t,j may remain an EXACT scalar outside this product. This elementary product statement estimates neither generic q/normal derivatives of the columns nor the rank-two derivative terms of mixed source kernels. It supplies no bound for fiber summation and does not release t,j. It therefore does not establish an asymptotic for an arbitrary full original-source summand containing those normal terms. Audit: [exact projector, determinant, convexity and adapter checks](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_physical_framing_criterion.py). The audit includes numerical argument comparisons only as regressions of the explicit equivalences; it is not an existence search or a proof of a favorable simultaneous frame for arbitrary augmented plats. Independent analytical review: PASS. A second reader checked both directions of the support and central-domain tests, the exact affine degree lift and cap marks, the common-product constructive lemma and its nonidentity-prefix normalization, the disk-side obstruction including boundary flags, and the distinction between regular bad frames and nonexistence of favorable frames. The initial audit was independently replayed; the expanded audit adds 100 exact central-feasibility checks for the constructive lemma. No global existence or cycle claim follows.

title: A global selected frame with one real deficient degree
status: Uniform real deficient frame and exact branch calibration
text: # A global selected frame with one real deficient degree 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. For every chosen matching edge of an actual certified right-angled augmented plat, there is a common algebraic frame whose two support failures occur precisely at that edge. Their normalized total is the REAL number sigma=1/6, while their magnetic rows are genuinely complex. Every other ordinary factor remains strictly physical and source-selected. This is a classical framing and branch-calibration theorem. A fixed integer deficient degree corresponds to an identically zero physical slice of the finite polynomial operator. The construction does not turn that slice into a nonzero quantum period. ## 1. Use the actual cusp and prefix normalization Fix the labeled matching-polyhedron certificate and one crossing-circle edge. In its actual disk coordinate eta, the two outward shaded disks are the half-planes below y=0 and above y=H, where H=1/c>=1. The inequality is the proved actual rectangle bound, including retained half twists. The two incident white planes are the vertical lines x=0 and x=1, with reflections -conjugate(eta) and 2-conjugate(eta). The actual incoming pair and its transport are A=[[-1,0],[-2,-1]], P=[[-1,-2],[0,-1]], C: eta -> eta+iH, A_o=C A C^-1. (1) These are precisely the conjugated original matrices and primitive collar, not an independent choice of a rectangle or meridian. All other shaded outward disks are bounded Euclidean disks in this chart. Their supporting planes do not contain the chosen ideal cusp; their outward sides cannot contain that cusp, which lies in the closed polyhedron. There are only finitely many such disks. Choose any 0<d<H and a midpoint r with d/2<r<H-d/2. For a large positive real X choose the TWO GLOBAL shaded-exterior flags w=X+i(r-d/2), w0=1-X+i(r+d/2). (2) They are between the two horizontal lines and, for sufficiently large X, outside every other bounded shaded disk. Thus w,w0 are in K. Recover the global image flag v=r_(F0)(w0) using the ACTUAL exterior white reflection F0. Together with kernel w this determines the common rank-one frame, provided v!=w. At the chosen left prefix white face F, reflection is -conjugation. The literal prefix identity gives local image z=r_F(w0)=X-1+i(r+d/2), z-w=-1+id. (3) This retains W_prefix v; it does not replace it by v. The equality v=w is avoidable: if F0 is one of the two incident vertical faces, its reflected image differs from w by +/-1+id; otherwise its bounded circle reflection sends w0 near infinity to a finite point as X grows, while w tends to infinity. ## 2. The deficient degree is exactly real and prescribed Normalize the local projector by its prefix trace. Direct traces in (1) give a0=1, a2=Tr(P Pi)=-1-2/(z-w)=(1+id)/(1-id), a1=Tr(A Pi)=-1+2zw/(z-w), a1_out=-1+2(z-iH)(w-iH)/(z-w). (4) Put sigma=atan(d)/pi in (0,1/2). Then a2=exp(2pi i sigma). Both middle diagonals in (4) have the same leading term 2X^2/(-1+id). Its argument is pi+pi sigma, strictly between pi and pi+2pi sigma. For all sufficiently large X, zero is therefore strictly inside BOTH actual input/output prefix triangles. These are exactly the strict failed-triangle tests, with no boundary limit taken in the final frame. Their canonical physical wire sums are 2-sigma, so the ORIGINAL high adapter gives the EXACT normalized complex degree sigma, with zero imaginary part. Write its two normalized magnetic rows as r_in, r_out. The actual high coordinates are U_in=-a2/a1, U_out=-a2/a1_out. Equations (4) imply Re r_in, Re r_out -> sigma/2, Im r_in, Im r_out =log(X)/pi+O(1), Re(r_out-r_in)=H/(pi X)+O(X^-2)>0. (5) The errors are uniform when the midpoint r stays in a compact subinterval of (d/2,H-d/2). Hence both rows are strictly inside the real degree interval and are nonreal; their difference avoids the target-total seam for sufficiently large X. Because H>=1, the UNIVERSAL choice d=1/sqrt(3) is allowed. It gives sigma=1/6, Re r_in,Re r_out ->1/12. (6) The construction can instead use any fixed d in (0,H). In particular it gives an open range of real deficient degrees when needed. ## 3. Exactly these two factors fail; all source seams can be avoided The global polarization kernel line for w,w0 lies through the interior of the white-normal polyhedron. The two strict relations in (4) put its exits in the interiors of the two designated triangular facets. A line has only two exits from a convex polyhedron. Thus no other facet has zero in its prefix triangle. Once the finite real seams are excluded, every other ordinary factor is strictly physical; its K flags then select its actual source sheet by the full-domain selected-factor theorem. Here is explicit seam control at FIXED d. It avoids an unjustified genericity argument on this restricted framing family. Up to one common scalar, the actual white prefix diagonals are the outward unit-circle polarizations. For a bounded white circle of center a+ib and radius R>0, remove only its positive factor 1/R and write L=-X^2+X+a^2-a+(r-b)^2-d^2/4-R^2 +i[(r-b)(1-2X)+(a-1/2)d]. (7) The two oriented vertical white forms are 1-id and 1+id. Formula (7) follows directly from `(w-a-ib)(conjugate(w0)-a+ib)-R^2`. For distinct bounded circles, Im(L1 conjugate(L2)) is a nonzero polynomial in X,r. Its X^3 coefficient detects distinct heights b. If the heights agree, its X^2 coefficient detects distinct horizontal centers a because d!=0. If both centers agree, the radius difference multiplies the nonzero imaginary part of L. A bounded-circle/vertical pair has a nonzero X^2 coefficient proportional to d, and the two vertical forms have imaginary product +/-2d. Thus every ratio of distinct white prefix diagonals can simultaneously be made nonreal by choosing (X,r) off finitely many proper real polynomial zero sets. This also supplies the ordinary cup/cap seam tests. The remaining specific regular-chart exclusions can be checked without claiming that an arbitrary divisor misses this family. Every bounded-circle form has the SAME-sign leading coefficient -1/R times X^2. Thus all required positive linear combinations, including a0+a2+4a1 and adjacent sums, have nonzero leading term. If only the two vertical forms occur in a sum, their sum is 2. For the discriminant a0a1+a1a2+a0a2, at least two bounded faces give a nonzero positive X^4 coefficient. The only case with one bounded face is the chosen pair of vertical faces; its leading coefficient is that bounded form times their sum 2, again nonzero. All prefix diagonals themselves are nonzero for large X. Finally each head or disk product is a noncentral trace-minus-two parabolic in its actual Borel frame. Its diagonal is nonreal by the ratio tests, and so is not -1. Determinant one then forces both offdiagonal entries to be nonzero. This checks the required main K+1 and total E/F charts. Together with the preceding leading coefficient and discriminant tests, these are the finite exclusions listed in the regular geometric phase-chart theorem. The actual simple internal roots and their rational inverses are therefore regular as well. All constraints hold on a nonempty open set of large X and allowed r. For an algebraic geometric certificate, take d=1/sqrt(3) and choose algebraic X,r outside the finite excluded polynomial sets. This gives an algebraic common frame. No rationality of the logarithms is claimed. ## 4. Exact magnetic branch data in this frame The following identities specify the geometric branch against which an actual second-chamber source continuation must be compared. They do not assume that such a continuation has already been proved. Put C0=cos(pi sigma)=1/sqrt(1+d^2) and L=2X-1. The two normalized determinant coordinates z_j=exp(pi i sigma)/U_j are exactly z_in =C0[(L^2+1+d^2-4r^2)/2+2irL], z_out=C0[(L^2+1+d^2-4(r-H)^2)/2+2i(r-H)L]. (8) Thus z_in lies in the UPPER half-plane, and z_out in the LOWER half-plane, for every X>1/2 and the stated midpoint interval. The actual original HIGH internal-root formulas give Z_in=-1/[L+2i(r+d/2)], Z_out=1/[L+2i(r-H-d/2)]. (9) The output uses its ACTUAL disk normalization C^-1, so its kernel coordinate is w-iH. Omitting that shift would give an incorrect output root even though the leading real sign agrees. For W(z)=1-2C0 z, equations (8) give perfect squares W(z_in)=-C0^2(L+2ir)^2, W(z_out)=-C0^2(L+2i(r-H))^2. (10) Take sqrt W positive at negative real z and continue through the upper or lower half-plane, respectively. Its values are -iC0(L+2ir) at the input and +iC0(L+2i(r-H)) at the output. Substitution of (9) in the ORIGINAL magnetic momentum formula Y=(1-U)(TZ+U)/[-(U-Z)(T-U)], T=exp(2pi i sigma), yields exactly Y_geo(z)=(z-i sqrt W(z))^2/[1-2C0 z+z^2]. (11) For example, at the input put A=L+2ir. Both sides reduce to `[(A-1)^2+d^2]/[(A+1)^2+d^2]`. At the output the same formula with A=L+2i(r-H) is inverted. In particular Y_in=1-2/X+O(X^-2) and Y_out=1+2/X+O(X^-2). Equation (11) is the branch obtained by REFLECTING the high-degree positive-center characteristic to negative z: z_high=-z changes its plus-square-root formula to the minus sign in (11). If an actual finite source continuation is anchored by that reflection, (8)--(11) identify its upper/lower continued characteristics with the actual geometric ones. They do not select a finite source by an arbitrary algebraic root or infer its relative amplitude. ## 5. The source-zero wall and global period remain This common frame supplies real sigma and complex rows for a local source analysis. It does not authorize replacing a generally complex degree by discrete samples in a theorem that has not controlled that continuation. In particular, at a fixed INTEGER deficient t the retargeted separation h=d-t exceeds the folded polynomial degree a. The entire physical fixed-h slice of p_a(J) is identically zero, including every genuine generic-q jet. Deforming magnetic rows alone does not create a nonzero original source in that slice. The geometry is therefore a useful actual branch and normalization test for the required continuation, not a contributing-cycle theorem. The [entire finite root continuation](actual_matching_edge_entire_operator_kernel.md) is established separately and retains the physical support zeros. Its selected asymptotic through this wall, its genuine generic normals, and the global marked period still require separate proofs. Focused audit: [circle regularity and actual marked branch identities](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_real_deficient_frame.py). It checks fourteen exact local identities, eighteen actual disk frames and thirty-six geometric characteristic comparisons. The global convex cut and avoidance arguments are the proofs in sections 1--3, not claims inferred from sampled polyhedra. Primary-agent full analytical review: PASS. The reader checked the actual prefix/cusp normalization, bounded outward disks, fixed-degree construction, strict two-facet localization, every stated regular-chart exclusion, algebraic frame choice and exact branch signs. The reader independently substituted both internal roots in the original magnetic momentum formula and obtained (11). Independent full analytical review and fresh redirected replay: PASS. A second reader checked the fixed-d circle argument and finite divisor list, both row asymptotics, and the output C^-1 normalization, and also independently verified both rational branch identities. Its fresh audit reproduced all fourteen identities, eighteen disk frames and thirty-six characteristic comparisons. Neither review supplies a finite second-chamber packet or a nonzero global period.

title: A regular magnetic chart for the complete geometric plat character
text: # A regular magnetic chart for the complete geometric plat character 30 October 2026. A complete geometric augmented-plat representation can be put simultaneously into the regular magnetic charts of the actual local critical-character map. This is a finite generic-framing theorem, not an assumption that the geometric flags are already in a convenient chart. At the leading exponentiated level its original Morse degree constraints also have an integral logarithmic lift. The statement constructs a regular candidate for the UNFOLDED principal equations. It does not prove that its logarithms lie in a nonempty physical support chamber, choose its Poisson sector in the original finite cycle, establish a nondegenerate reduced critical branch, or supply a quantum asymptotic. Those distinctions matter at the folded channel endpoint. ## 1. The actual prefix factorization Fix the finite ordered Morse word of the augmented plat and its actual complete geometric representation. Use common trace -2 lifts of the main meridians. At each circle box its two puncture flags are distinct and their ordered product P is noncentral parabolic with trace -2, as in the [geometric endpoint theorem](actual_augmented_plat_geometric_channel_endpoint.md). The same statements hold after its retained Hurwitz half twists. These hypotheses do not require a right-angled cell decomposition. In any actual complete geometric augmented exterior, the disk boundary is a nontrivial peripheral longitude of its auxiliary cusp. If its two main puncture parabolics had the same fixed point, their nontrivial parabolic product would have that point too. This would identify a main cusp lift with an auxiliary cusp lift. Distinct cusp lifts have disjoint sufficiently small horoballs; two horoballs with the same ideal center intersect. This is impossible for different components. The elementary common-trace calculation then forces Tr P=-2. At any horizontal cut let H_1,...,H_m be its ordered based meridians and Q_i=H_i ... H_1, Q_0=I. For a determinant-one matrix Q with Q_11!=0 put Bminus(Q)=[[1,0],[-Q_21,Q_11]], Bplus(Q)=[[Q_11,Q_12],[0,1]]. Then Q=Bminus(Q)^-1 Bplus(Q). Consequently the ORIGINAL physical head at slot i is G_i=Bminus(Q_(i-1)) H_i Bminus(Q_(i-1))^-1, K_i=(Q_i)_11/(Q_(i-1))_11, X_i=-1/K_i, S_i=(G_i)_21/(K_i+1). (1) For K_i!=0,-1 these are finite nonzero magnetic coordinates. The determinant-one and trace -2 equations give exactly the original head matrix (8) of the [local critical map](actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md). Thus (1) does not introduce an independent flag realization. Change the ONE common frame by g in SL2(C), so every word Q changes to gQg^-1. There are finitely many heads and boxes. The following sections show that each excluded condition is a proper algebraic subset of this same frame group. Their finite union cannot cover it. ## 2. Every required endpoint chart divisor is avoidable A nonzero 2-by-2 matrix R has a nonzero (gRg^-1)_11 for some g. Indeed otherwise every vector/covector pair v,l with l(v)=1 would have l(Rv)=0, forcing R=0. Thus a forbidden diagonal of any NONZERO fixed word combination is a proper condition. This handles all prefix diagonals. It also handles K_i=-1, since Q_i+Q_(i-1)=(H_i+I)Q_(i-1) is nonzero for a nontrivial trace -2 parabolic. At a local input pair put R=Q_(i-1), A=H_i, B=H_(i+1), P=BA and Q_0=R,Q_1=AR,Q_2=PR. Write a_r=(gQ_r g^-1)_11. Its low physical coordinates obey U=-a_0/a_1, T=a_0/a_2. (2) The exclusions T=+/-1 and U=T are diagonal conditions for (I-/+P)R and (I+B)AR. These matrices are nonzero. The endpoint q-Hahn quadratic leading coefficient is U(T+1)-4T. Its vanishing, away from the nonzero a_r, is exactly a_0+a_2+4a_1=0. The corresponding fixed matrix is (I+P+4A)R. It is nonzero because Tr(I+P+4A)=-8. The discriminant is proportional to T+1-U. Here its vanishing is the quadratic expression a_0a_1+a_1a_2+a_0a_2=0. (3) To prove this is PROPER for every prefix R, conjugate just for this nonvanishing proof to the canonical pair A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], R=[[a,b],[c,d]], ad-bc=1. The normalization follows from the two distinct flags and Tr(BA)=-2. For the test frames g_r=[[1,r],[0,1]], direct multiplication gives a_0a_1+a_1a_2+a_0a_2=-( -a+c r-c )^2. (4) This polynomial is not identically zero, since the first column (a,c) of R is not zero. Therefore (3) is avoidable by a generic common frame. A different test frame can prove propriety for each box; the final choice avoids ALL of their finitely many bad loci. Both total F and total E may also be required nonzero. In the local Borel frame E_tot=P_12/a_0, so its zero is proper because P is noncentral. For F_tot the numerator, up to nonzero diagonal factors, is det(Rv,PRv), where v=g^-1 e_1. This quadratic in v is not identically zero for a noncentral P. Thus this exclusion is proper too. These conditions exclude every pole in the endpoint local formulas. For example P(U,Z) at J=-1 cannot have Z=0,1,-1,U or TZ+U=0: substitution gives a nonzero product of T,U,T+1,U-1,U-T. Its leading coefficient is nonzero and its discriminant is nonzero, so both roots are finite and simple. The actual magnetic momentum selects its root by the rational inverse (5) of the local map. For the HIGH chamber use T_low=T_phys^-1 and U_low=U_phys/T_phys. The discriminant divisor transforms by T_low+1-U_low=(T_phys+1-U_phys)/T_phys, and the leading coefficient by U_low(T_low+1)-4T_low =[U_phys(T_phys+1)-4T_phys]/T_phys^2. All other excluded head and total-coefficient divisors are the same ones above, with F and E exchanged. Thus the single generic frame works for either actual degree adapter at every box. If the marked geometric representation is algebraic, the good frame may be chosen algebraic (in fact rational after fixing its matrix coordinates). To see this use a rational big-cell parametrization of SL2 and clear the finitely many nonzero denominators. A nonzero polynomial over a number field cannot vanish on all rational tuples, by the elementary one-variable root count and induction. Equations (1) and the local inverse then give algebraic magnetic and internal phases. This does not make their logarithms algebraic. ## 3. The unconstrained integral degree lift The leading Morse degree equations are sum_out-sum_in=0 at a coupon, sum_out=1 at a cup, and sum_in=1 at a cap. Regard every physical wire as an oriented edge between successive events. Their coefficient matrix is the oriented incidence matrix of this finite graph: each wire occurs once positively and once negatively. Choose any logarithms of the magnetic X_e. Since the exponentiated degree equations hold, each defect from the desired affine equation is an integer. On each connected component the sum of these defects is zero. The wire terms cancel, and that component has equally many cups and caps, by counting incoming and outgoing half-edges. Every integral vertex vector of total zero is the incidence image of an integral edge vector: choose a spanning tree, remove its leaves one by one, and put the leaf defect on its unique remaining edge. The last defect is zero by the total-sum condition. Adding these integer corrections to the wire logarithms solves all affine degree equations exactly. This does NOT enforce 0<=Re u_e<=1, select the finite low/high support chambers, or erase a recorded phase. The original ordinary and marked cap characters differ by an integral Poisson character and must still be kept. The result is an unrestricted logarithmic lift, not a claim about the support of the physical finite sum. ## 4. Consequence and precise remaining gap In the good common frame reconstruct the local roots from the actual geometric momenta. Both q-Hahn internal equations hold. The local map preserves the whole ordered product and recovers the actual inverse auxiliary transport; at completeness its channel equation is R_epsilon=1. Shared wires carry the SAME X,S, and original cups/caps give the inverse-meridian relation P=I. Thus the local derivatives match on the tangent lattice of the Morse degree constraints, and their exponentials are one. Section 3 supplies an affine degree lift. This is a regular geometric solution of the UNFOLDED exponentiated principal equations, with the original marked representation. It is a genuine candidate input to the regulator comparison. The result does not identify a physical support chamber with a nonempty selected cycle, or show that the required logarithmic/Poisson sector contributes. It makes no claim of a reduced nondegenerate Hessian, nearby holomorphic critical family, nonzero source amplitude, or volume asymptotic. The frame construction is not an argument that one may change the original quantum source by choosing a favorable co-source. It is a coordinate choice on its classical marked character, retaining the original cup/cap equations. The dimension of its framing orbit after the phase-coordinate reductions is not asserted here. ## 5. The remaining bridge to the source-selected local branch The [actual q-Hahn logarithm theorem](actual_q_hahn_selected_complex_action.md) now selects the local internal branch for REAL strict physical parameters, including the folded endpoint. At that endpoint, if 1/2<tau<1, 0<u<tau, w=exp[pi i(tau-1/2)], its selected logarithmic root satisfies max(0,u-tau+1/2)<Re alpha<min(u,1/2), Im alpha>0. Consequently Z=exp(2pi i alpha) lies in the upper half of the unit disk. The strict inequality tau>1/2 matters: at w=1 the selected alpha is real instead. The implicit function theorem also gives joint complex parameter germs near these regular physical points. These are source-selected local data, not yet a global continuation to the geometric candidate constructed above. The exact endpoint quadratic is [U(T+1)-4T] Z^2+2U(T-1) Z+U(T+1)=0, discriminant=16TU(T+1-U). A small loop about U=T+1 at a generic fixed T exchanges its two roots. Thus unspecified algebraic or holomorphic continuation can change the branch. What is still needed is a common admissible continuation domain, or an explicitly controlled path, which carries the ACTUAL selected local kernels and their original logarithmic marks from a nonempty physical support chamber to the geometric point at every coupon simultaneously. Generic avoidance of the discriminant and the integral affine lift in section 3 do not supply that statement. Even after such a branch comparison, the remaining whole-source cycle and noncancellation estimate would be separate work. Long fillings perturb the auxiliary color parameters chi by O(1/p) near the complete source, with p the filling slope. They do not by themselves resolve this base magnetic branch-selection problem. The source-divisor extension permits a finite-order zero of an already constructed analytic amplitude; it does not construct the missing selected branch or prove that its amplitude germ is nonzero. Audit: [exact generic-chart identities](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_regular_geometric_phase_chart.py).

text: # Selected physical factors outside one exact matching-edge block 30 October 2026. This note assembles two separate inputs: the actual source's full physical packet and the proved right-angled geometric localization. It does not identify a contributing global finite cycle. ## 1. Inputs and statement Fix an actual augmented plat of arbitrary fixed width, with its retained half twists, literal Morse word, original exposed physical mark, and a positive convex ideal right-angled matching-polyhedron certificate as in [the actual matching geometry](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md). The actual source is the full marked matching-graph source; its folded labels, partner normals and generic lifts are not replaced by a root-only semisimple network. Choose any one crossing-circle matching edge e. Use the following two established inputs, with their distinct scopes: * The [prescribed-pair geometric theorem](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) supplies a common regular frame with strip flags in the common shaded exterior K. Its only two strict physical-support failures are the two shaded facets at the ends of e. All other ordinary input/output factors have their actual canonical low or high physical coordinates. * The [full physical complex packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) concerns the ORIGINAL finite q-Hahn column. Its limiting domain is P={ (tau,nu) in C^2 : 1/2<Re tau<1, 0<Re nu<Re tau }. (1) On each compact of P, for sufficiently large N and actual integer folded channels j with j/N near 1/2, it gives the selected ordinary packet with nonzero amplitude. Its selected characteristic extends from the previously proved central domain. No complex continuation of the finite index j is inferred from this statement. Then the common frame can be chosen so that EVERY ordinary factor outside the two ends of e belongs to the source-selected branch on P. The two exceptions comprise ONE original matching-edge operator, whose four exterior objects all have highest weight d=N-1. That operator has the exact generic recoupling and retained first-normal formula of [the marked four-port block](actual_matching_edge_marked_four_port_block.md). The original physical mark remains where it was. The finite collection of good factors lies in a common compact subset of P. Consequently their ordinary finite-column packets can be multiplied there, with the product of their nonzero amplitudes and relative error 1+O(1/N). This is a local product statement at the framed geometric germ, not an estimate of the complementary tensor contraction, its summation, or the completed marked source. ## 2. The selected flag branches continue throughout P Here is the additional proof needed beyond the old central-domain statement. Write T=exp(2pi i tau), U=exp(2pi i nu), zeta=T^(1/2)/U, W=1-(T+1)/U, V=W+zeta^2, (2) where T^(1/2)=exp(pi i tau) retains its marked argument. The full packet proves W and V nonzero on P at the endpoint channel xi=1/2. Its square root of W is the analytic continuation from the positive real center. It need not be the pointwise principal square root outside the central domain. Since P is convex and W is nonzero, that continued square root is single valued. Normalize the actual incoming puncture matrices as A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], P_disk=B A. The exact original head formulas in the [selected local certificate](actual_augmented_plat_selected_local_certificate.md) give, for image flag z and kernel flag w, U_phys=(z-w)/(z-w+1), T_phys=(z-w)/(4wz+3w+z+1), Y_in=-w/(z+1), Y_out=Y_in^(-1). (3) First use the low adapter U_phys=U,T_phys=T. Directly solving (3), with delta=U/(1-U), gives the two pairs Delta=U(T+1-U)/T=-U^2 W/T, w=(-1 +/- sqrt(Delta))/(2(1-U)), z=w+delta. (4) The marked exponential arguments in (1) imply U!=1 and U!=T. Equation (2) gives Delta!=0. Thus (4) defines two distinct global analytic pairs of finite flags on P. Their actual normalized prefix triple is (a_0,a_1,a_2)=(1,-1/U,1/T). (5) The strict physical criterion applies to this triple throughout (1): the canonical physical wire coordinates are nu and tau-nu. The proved real determinant-pencil argument therefore puts z,w on the same OPEN side of the real disk circle. Neither flag can reach that circle along either analytic branch. In particular no unrecorded passage through infinity changes its side; infinity itself belongs to the forbidden circle. For the actual high adapter one instead has T_phys=1/T, U_phys=U/T. Its physical wires are 1+nu-tau and 1-nu. Both are in the canonical strip, and the total has the required high degree. Crucially, U_phys(T_phys+1-U_phys)/T_phys=Delta. (6) The same discriminant gives the two analytic flag pairs, now using 1-U/T in the denominator. This denominator is nonzero. Their physical triple (1,-T/U,T) is, up to a common nonzero factor and exchange of the outer terms, the triple (5). Hence the same open-side conclusion holds. The full tube P is connected. At any central base point, the original source calibration already proves selected input means both flags below the incoming real circle, and selected output means both flags above its own real circle, in BOTH adapters. The source characteristic has no collision on P, and the flag branches have no collision or circle crossing. Continuing that calibration proves throughout P selected input iff Im z<0 and Im w<0, selected output iff Im z>0 and Im w>0. (7) Each line uses that factor's own actual disk normalization. This proof continues the selected root, not the old pointwise test Re sqrt(W)>0. ## 3. From actual strips to all good factors At a complete coupon, the primitive collar gives C=I+b(P_disk+I), with Im b<0 and b-epsilon/2=1/tau_cusp. In eta(s)=1/(2s+1), eta(C s)=eta(s)-2b. Consequently (7) is equivalent, at any STRICTLY PHYSICAL input/output pair, to the same two actual strip tests as before: 0<Im eta(w)<-2 Im b, 0<Im eta(W_prefix v)<-2 Im b. (8) The exact based-prefix dictionary of the right-angled localization identifies these with its common shaded-exterior flags. Choose its prescribed failed facets to be the two ends of e. Every other factor then has strict physical support AND the required oriented strip side. Equations (7),(8), proved on the larger tube, make each of those factors source-selected. This is the extra conclusion that the earlier central-domain theorem could not provide. There are finitely many factors, so their strict margins have a common positive lower bound after fixing this frame. Small neighborhoods of their actual low/high coordinates have compact closure in P. Apply the full packet on those neighborhoods, uniformly for its allowed actual integer channels, and multiply a fixed finite number of estimates. For an algebraic geometric certificate the frame may be chosen algebraic, as in the prescribed-pair theorem. This does not turn the selected logarithmic action into a root-only polynomial evaluation: its original logarithmic characters and finite-source normalization remain specified. ## 4. Exact exceptional block and limits of the conclusion Both exceptional factors are kept together on e. The marked block theorem bends its actual operator K_a by the original physical cups, recouples through EVERY target g=0,...,d, and writes its whole-source first normal as Taylor coefficients of order at most two after clearing the possible simple poles. It retains the original circle weight and half-twist phase. The native row weight and physical cup scale introduce no exponential loss. Its explicit target and complement costs J_g,J_C are still part of that theorem's bound; they are not removed by the present geometric localization. The full packet also supplies the actual small-channel fixed generic jet bounds and the near-fold partner-normal upper bound on these SAME complex compacts. In its notation, for fixed r and s=l-j, |D^r C_j/C_j| <= C_r N^(8r), |w_(j,l)/C_j| <= C N^8(C N^16)^s, s<=eta N. (9) Here D=q d/dq, and the derivatives in the numerator are generic-q derivatives evaluated at the root; the denominator is the ordinary root column. Constants depend on the chosen compact, and every channel is still an actual integer. For a fixed number of good factors, the additional partner-normal loss is exp(O(sum s_i log N)). It is subexponential when each s_i log N=o(N). A fixed nonzero scaled separation is not covered by that inference. These are upper bounds, not a nonzero confluent amplitude. The separate all-physical lattice jet theorem is not by itself a theorem for complex geometric totals. No global cycle, lower bound, nonzero completed saddle coefficient, or sharp estimate of the complementary contraction has been proved here. Nor have we made the entire factorization physical: its two necessary support defects remain, now in one exact block. The useful reduction is that all other ORDINARY factors have an actual selected physical packet, at arbitrary fixed plat width, while the exceptional block has an exact source-preserving expression with its boundary costs displayed. Focused audit: [exact new low/high flag identities](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.py). It checks both adapters and all four flag branches: eight original-head identities, twelve actual prefix traces, three discriminant identities and four sheet-involution identities. These are new exact algebraic checks only; the outside-central finite-source comparisons belong to the separate full-physical packet audit. Independent analytical reviews: PASS. The root reader independently solved the low flag quadratic and checked the high-adapter discriminant and triple reversal. A second reader checked the actual prefix and open-circle-side continuation; a third checked the entire corollary against the full physical packet and its precise complex normal ranges. All checked the continued, rather than pointwise principal, square root, the prescribed matching-edge pair, and the distinction between an ordinary local product and the uncontrolled complementary contraction. The proof also uses the existing prescribed-pair audit and the separately reviewed full-physical packet; no numerical fixture is used to infer the global frame or selected branch.

text: # A finite certificate for the selected geometric principal phase **Subsequent scope result (30 October):** the [right-angled obstruction and localization](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) proves that no common all-central selected frame exists for the actual certified right-angled plat cut. Generic geometric strip flags have exactly two strict physical-support failures, at arbitrary bridge width. The local conditional statements below remain valid; their simultaneous realization in that right-angled class cannot supply the general proof. 30 October 2026. For any fixed augmented plat, of arbitrary width, this note gives explicit tests which identify the geometric stationary branch with the source-selected LOCAL q-Hahn principal action. It also expresses the endpoint sheet test as a condition on the two common framing flags. No intersection with the original finite summation cycle is inferred. The certificate has not been shown to exist for every positive geometric augmented plat. Its point is to replace an unspecified local branch-identification assumption by finite tests on the actual marked representation, with all input/output signs retained. ## 1. Data and the selected-critical certificate Fix the actual augmented-plat Morse word, retained half twists, and primitive peripheral marks. Supply: 1. An actual marked positive complete gluing certificate, as in [the geometric certificate theorem](general_marked_positive_gluing_certificate.md). It gives the geometric representation, not an unrelated component of the character equations. 2. ONE rank-one projector Pi satisfying all the regular-chart, central-support and cup/cap tests of [the physical framing criterion](actual_augmented_plat_physical_framing_criterion.md). These include the original affine degree equations with the canonical wire logarithms and the actual low/high adapters. 3. The actual magnetic multiplier at each ordinary column factor. At an input it is Y_geo=S_1/S_2; at an output it is Y_geo=S_2/S_1. The momenta S are reconstructed from the original prefix matrices, not chosen separately to make a test pass. 4. The selected-root test in section 2 at every input and output, and the original logarithmic/Poisson characters of the full marked phase. The latter are retained as part of the certificate, rather than erased after exponentiation. These conditions imply the following LOCAL conclusion. The actual geometric critical germ is a germ of the source-selected principal phase. Modulo its two framing directions its magnetic Hessian is nondegenerate. Its fully marked critical action phi has d(2pi i phi)=1/2 sum V_i dU_i, 2pi Re phi(0)=Vol(Y_D), phi_(chi_i chi_j)(0)=pi i tau_i delta_(ij), (1) with U_i=-2pi i chi_i and the original primitive cusp shapes tau_i. Its ordinary q-Hahn column amplitude factors are nonzero. The conclusion concerns the actual marked phase and its ordinary column factors. It is NOT a full-source amplitude theorem, a bound for generic normal currents, a continuation of the finite discrete channel, or a claim that the original cycle contributes at this germ. ## 2. The local sheet test is algebraic on the marked cover Use the actual low coordinates tau,nu of each column, after applying the high adapter when required. Put xi=1/2, zeta=exp[pi i(tau-2nu)], c=-cos(pi tau), W=1+2c zeta, V=1+2c zeta+zeta^2. (2) Here W is a scalar, not a prefix matrix. In the central domain Re c>0, Re zeta>0. Both W/zeta and V/zeta have positive real part; hence W and V avoid the nonpositive real axis. In particular the principal square root of W has strictly positive real part. The [joint original-kernel theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md), section 7, gives the source-selected multiplier Y_sel=(zeta+i sqrt(W))^2/V. (3) For the actual geometric multiplier define r_geo=[V Y_geo-zeta^2+W]/(2i zeta). (4) The actual Casimir characteristic equation says r_geo^2=W. Therefore Y_geo=Y_sel if and only if Re r_geo>0. (5) This is an equality test for the selected root, not just a test that both values solve the characteristic polynomial. The source theorem fixes the square root by its actual center phase and finite-source continuation. All expressions in (2)--(5) are algebraic after retaining the marked square root of T=exp(2pi i tau). Its argument is pi Re tau in (pi/2,pi), which fixes the square-root sign; zeta=T^(1/2)/U with U=exp(2pi i nu). Thus for an algebraic marked representation and projector the endpoint root test is a finite real-algebraic test. The logarithmic characters of the action remain additional marked data, not a consequence of squaring (4). ## 3. Exact flag formulas, including the output sign and high adapter Normalize one actual incoming pair to A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], P=B A, H=P+I. Write Pi=v ell, ell(v)=1. In these disk coordinates let w be the kernel flag of ell and let z be the image flag W_prefix v. This use of the actual prefix is essential. Normalize the local rank-one matrix W_prefix Pi by its trace; it has image z and kernel w. In affine coordinates a representative of the local common frame is g=[[1,-w],[1,-z]]. Direct substitution into the ORIGINAL head and prefix formulas gives U_phys=(z-w)/(z-w+1), T_phys=(z-w)/(4wz+3w+z+1), S_1/S_2=-w/(z+1). (6) The source internal root in a low column is obtained from the actual inverse, at J=-1, Z=-U[y(T-U)+(1-U)]/[-y(T-U)+T(1-U)]. (7) For the input use y=S_1/S_2; for the output use its RECIPROCAL. Equations (6),(7) give Z_in,low=(2w+1)/(2w-1), Z_out,low=(2z+1)/(2z+3). (8) For the high adapter one must first replace T_low=T_phys^(-1), U_low=U_phys/T_phys. Keeping the same actual input/output momentum convention in (7) then gives Z_in,high=-(2z+1)/(2z+3), Z_out,high=-(2w+1)/(2w-1). (9) These are rational identities, not deductions from a root-only symmetry. They retain the output sign of a kernel and the actual high-degree translation. ## 4. The endpoint selected sheets are oriented disk sides For any strict central triple, its two local framing flags z,w are on the SAME open side of the real disk circle, by section 5 of the physical framing criterion. The two roots of the local characteristic give the two opposite choices of that side. One can see the latter directly from (6). Fix U_phys,T_phys and put d=U_phys/(1-U_phys)=z-w. The equation for w is quadratic; its roots have sum -(d+1). Consequently its two flag pairs are related by (z,w) -> (-w-1,-z-1). (10) They therefore lie on opposite sides of the real circle. There is no collision or boundary crossing in the central domain. For example T+1-U cannot vanish there: arg T is in (pi,2pi), arg(1+T) is strictly between arg T and 2pi, while the strict physical U argument lies between 0 and arg T. The other regular root denominators are excluded by the regular-chart assumptions. The simple characteristic and the connected central domain preserve the two sheet labels. At a strict physical real point, the actual selected internal root Z is in the upper half of the unit disk, as proved by the original q-Hahn selection theorem. Equation (8) then gives w below the real circle for an input, and z above it for an output. Equation (9) gives the SAME respective side choices in the high adapter. Together with the same-side necessity, continuation through the central domain therefore proves the equivalent tests selected input <=> Im z<0 and Im w<0, selected output <=> Im z>0 and Im w>0, (11) where each line uses that factor's OWN actual disk normalization. The inequalities in (11), rather than an upper-half-disk assertion for Z at arbitrary complex parameters, are what continue globally. They agree with (5); either supplies the same endpoint sheet test. ## 5. A global strip-intersection question remains For one actual complete coupon its transport is C=I+bH. The primitive mark fixes b-epsilon/2=1/tau_cusp, so Im b<0 for the positive geometric orientation. In the incoming disk coordinate set eta(s)=1/(2s+1). Direct substitution gives eta(C s)=eta(s)-2b. The incoming condition in (11) becomes Im eta>0; the outgoing condition, in the disk frame C^(-1), becomes Im(eta+2b)<0. Thus, CONDITIONAL ON the strict central inequalities, both input and output are selected exactly when 0<Im eta(w)<-2 Im b, 0<Im eta(W_prefix v)<-2 Im b. (12) This is the actual oriented region between the two developed disk circles. Positivity of the primitive cusp orientation gives its positive height. It does not prove that all such regions meet. Let Omega_f denote this region in the one global flag sphere, using the actual input disk normalization at coupon f. Formula (12) gives the necessary separated global conditions w in intersection_f Omega_f, v in intersection_f W_f^(-1) Omega_f. (13) Once the coupled central tests also hold, (13) is sufficient for ALL endpoint local sheet tests. This is a finite geometric version of the certificate. It identifies the precise role of the actual prefix pullbacks; independent local flags do not establish (13). No general identification of these intersections with exteriors of polyhedral face disks is asserted here. Such an identification would need the actual based words and both disk copies, as well as the coupled central inequalities. The common-product feasibility lemma in the preceding framing note concerns support only; it does not by itself supply these selected input/output sheets. ## 6. Proof of the certificate and precise persistence The sheet test identifies each actual geometric magnetic multiplier with the selected local multiplier. The regular inverse (7) then identifies its internal root with the source-selected root, including the high adapter. The original full coupon phase, its factorial measure, external phases and marked cap characters are retained. Fixing the stipulated logarithmic/Poisson characters gives the actual marked principal phase, rather than merely its exponentiated equations. The [critical-scheme inverse](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md) now identifies this germ with the actual marked geometric representation germ modulo the diagonal scale. The positive multi-cusp gluing rigidity theorem makes its only magnetic null directions the two framing directions. A transverse framing slice therefore has nondegenerate magnetic Hessian. The same theorem's classical action corollary, using the primitive collar differential and the absolute endpoint regulator, gives exactly (1). No new period normalization is introduced by the test. The joint column theorem gives, for actual integer channels with real xi_N=j/N near 1/2, the nonzero ordinary amplitude fhat=N^(-1/2) B_(xi_N)(tau,nu) exp[N Phi_(xi_N)(tau,nu)](1+O(1/N)). A fixed finite product of such ordinary factors has the product estimate on a compact common domain. This supplies nonzero ordinary column amplitude germs at the certified branch; it supplies neither generic normal-factor estimates nor a full-source saddle coefficient. All strict central inequalities and (5) persist under small marked peripheral deformation. The unramified geometric germ and transverse critical slice then continue the certified CLASSICAL selected branch. The selected coefficient functions also continue holomorphically in xi near 1/2. This applies to sufficiently long geometric fillings, with their original primitive marks. It does not continue the finite discrete index j to a complex value or justify a channel contour. The remaining global tasks are substantive: produce the certificate for a broad geometric class, control all required normal currents, and prove that the original finite cycle has the required contribution and global exponential bound. This note resolves none of those tasks merely by having a stationary point with the correct volume. Audit: [exact original-head, adapter and strip identities](../experiments/audit_actual_augmented_plat_selected_local_certificate.py). Independent analytical reviews: PASS. Two readers checked the finite certificate, original low/high input/output conventions, connected-domain sheet continuation, the actual primitive-collar strip and prefix pullbacks, and the distinction between classical continuation and a finite-channel or full-source asymptotic. A fresh independent audit replay passed all four root identities, the exact strip translation, and 2,000 selector comparisons on 1,000 central frames. The reviews establish no general existence of the certificate or contributing cycle.

title: The crossing-circle cusp lattice, including its half-twist marking
text: # The crossing-circle cusp lattice, including its half-twist marking 29 October 2026. The explicit face-labeled antiprism geometry gives the crossing-circle cusp shape without an additional factor two. Put \(c=\cos(\pi/s)\). In the positive diagonal half-twist marking, \[ \boxed{\qquad \tau_{\mathrm{std},+} =\frac{2ic}{1+ic} =\frac{2c^2+2ic}{1+c^2}.\qquad} \tag{1} \] The opposite half twist has \(\tau_{\mathrm{std},-}=2ic/(1-ic)\), whose real part is negative and whose imaginary part is the same. At \(s=3\), these are \(\pm2/5+4i/5\). The untwisted marked shape is \(2ic\). These statements concern the crossing-circle cusps, not the main component cusp. The words “positive diagonal” specify the peripheral marking below. The metric face pairing alone does not distinguish the two half twists: they differ by a full twist. Consequently (1) is not, by itself, a proof that an independently defined quantum logarithm is the preferred longitude, or a proof of its sign convention. It gives an explicit two-path calibration for making that comparison. ## 1. Compute one actual horospherical rectangle Use the explicit \(\mathcal P_s\) in [the geometric-volume proof](actual_augmented_pretzel_geometric_volume.md). Set \(\alpha=\pi/s\), \(t=\tan(\pi/4-\alpha/2)\), and \(\rho=t^{-1/2}\). Before doubling the antiprism its ideal vertices in the complex boundary are \[ Z_k=\rho e^{2ik\alpha},\qquad U_k^+=\rho^{-1}e^{(2k+1)i\alpha}. \] Reflection across the base circle \(|z|=\rho\) gives the other half of the doubled polyhedron: \(U_k^-=\rho^3e^{(2k+1)i\alpha}\). The four neighbors of \(Z_0=\rho\) are \(U_{-1}^{\pm},U_0^{\pm}\). Send \(Z_0\) to infinity by the holomorphic Mobius map \(m(z)=1/(z-\rho)\). Their images form a Euclidean rectangle. For an explicit calculation put \(A=\rho^2=(1+\sin\alpha)/\cos\alpha\). The lower left and lower right corners are \[ m(U_0^+)=-\frac{\rho A}{\sin\alpha(1+A^2)} -i\frac{\rho}{\sin\alpha(1+A^2)}, \] \[ m(U_0^-)=\frac{1}{\rho\sin\alpha(1+A^2)} -i\frac{\rho}{\sin\alpha(1+A^2)}. \] The other two are their complex conjugates. Hence the width and height are \[ W=\frac1{\rho\sin\alpha},\qquad H=\frac{2\rho}{\sin\alpha(1+A^2)},\qquad \boxed{H/W=\frac{2A}{1+A^2}=\cos\alpha=c.} \tag{2} \] Since all incident faces are vertical planes after this Mobius map, their intersections with any horosphere about infinity give exactly this rectangle, up to its common Euclidean scale. Its vertical sides are the shaded \(T_0^+,T_0^-\) faces. Its horizontal sides are the white \(Q_0,Q_{-1}\) faces. Normalize by \(W\) and translate to the rectangle \([0,1]\times[0,c]\). There are exactly TWO such rectangles at this cusp, one from each projection polyhedron. There are not four cusp rectangles merely because the whole three-manifold contains four antiprisms: doubling across a base merges the two half rectangles into the one just computed. ## 2. Develop the exact face pairings Keep rectangle 0 at \(x+iy\), \(0\leq x\leq1\), \(0\leq y\leq c\). White gluing by the original vertex labels develops rectangle 1 as \[ x+iy\longmapsto x+i(2c-y). \tag{3} \] It lies in \([0,1]\times[c,2c]\). The two white identifications therefore give the vertical period \(2ic\). For no half twist, shaded gluing is within each copy and matches the same outer labels. It identifies its left and right sides at the same local \(y\), giving period 1. Thus the untwisted lattice is \[ \mathcal L_0=\langle1,2ic\rangle_{\mathbb Z}. \tag{4} \] For a half twist, the original face pairing switches copies AND exchanges the two outer labels. In local rectangle coordinates it sends \((0,y)_0\mapsto(1,c-y)_1\). In the development (3) its translation is \(1+ic\). The other shaded pair gives \(1-ic\). Consequently the half-twisted lattice is \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal L_{\mathrm h} =\langle1+ic,1-ic\rangle_{\mathbb Z} =\langle2,1+ic\rangle_{\mathbb Z}.\quad} \tag{5} \] Its area is \(2c\), the sum of the two original rectangle areas. ## 3. Identify the meridian and preferred longitude paths The shaded faces are the two sides of the original twice-punctured crossing disk. The cusp boundary of that disk runs ALONG their vertical sides and passes through the two white identifications. It has translation \[ \lambda=2ic. \tag{6} \] This is the disk-framed longitude: pushing the crossing circle off inside its spanning disk has zero linking with the circle itself. Punctures by the other component do not change that self-linking calculation. The loop traverses each of the two shaded sides once; using \(4ic\) would traverse this longitude twice. A positively transverse local meridian crosses the disk seam once. In the untwisted marking it has translation 1. In the positive diagonal half-twist marking it follows the corner path \((0,0)_0\mapsto(1,c)_1\) in local labels and has \[ \mu_+=1+ic. \tag{7} \] The opposite half-twist marking uses \(\mu_-=1-ic=\mu_+-\lambda\). Both \((\mu_+,\lambda)\) and \((\mu_-,\lambda)\) are primitive bases of (5): their oriented parallelogram area is \(2c\). Equations (6)--(7) prove (1). In particular choosing a half of \(\lambda\) would not define a curve in (5), and doubling \(\lambda\) would not give a peripheral basis. The explicit integer-shear calibration is \[ \mu_++p\lambda=1+i(2p+1)c,\qquad \mu_-+p\lambda=1+i(2p-1)c. \tag{8} \] Thus a claimed filling equation must record which of these two base meridians corresponds to its retained physical half twist. The original source \(R^{-(2p+1)}\) has a specified braid convention and a specified kernel integer \(p\). To match it to (8), it is enough to identify the \(p=0\) corner path and the direction of the \(p\mapsto p+1\) full twist; one cannot infer that information from the unmarked ideal triangle isometry alone. Replacing \(R^{-1}\) by \(R\) changes the half-twist marking by one longitude even though the complete metric volume is unchanged. ## 4. Comparison with the complete mixed-phase Hessian If the original mixed-phase coordinates have \(z=2\log M\), \(\partial G/\partial z=\log L\), and \(\partial^2G/\partial z_i^2=\tau_s\), then the geometric cusp shape they predict is \(\tau_{\mathrm{std}}=2\tau_s\), since \(d\log L/d\log M=2\,d\log L/dz\). For the stated formal value \[ \tau_s=e^{iu_*}\cos u_*,\qquad \tan u_*=\sec\alpha, \] one gets \[ 2\tau_s=\frac{2ic}{1+ic}, \] which is exactly the positive-diagonal shape (1). This independent geometric calculation excludes the proposed extra factor two. It does not supply the missing quantum-to-peripheral coordinate identification or select the half-twist sign by itself. There is a concrete source sign to check in making that identification. For the literal auxiliary color \(j=N-h\), put \(H=Q^h\). The centered auxiliary meridian \(M_{\rm aux}=-q^j\) has \(2\Log M_{\rm aux}=-\Log H\).
