Moving F through the unsummed network generally produces currents in those remaining flow coordinates. Their exact finite boundary, canonical carries and normal source must be retained to identify its complex with W. ## 4. Actual coproduct symbols and the two cut-framing currents There is a direct principal-symbol comparison, using the already proved actual moment-map identity. On the tensor product put K_tot=Delta^(b-1)K, Ecal_tot=rho^2 Delta^(b-1)E, F_tot=Delta^(b-1)F, rho=q-q^(-1). In balanced wave coordinates A=Q^a and S f(A)=f(QA), their local input matrices have symbols K=x/A, e=(1-x^2/A)p/x, f=(1-A)/p. The actual finite Ecal is the truncated matrix, including its rank-one endpoint subtraction; only its interior symbol is used in this display. The actual coproducts are Delta K=K tensor K, Delta Ecal=Ecal tensor K+1 tensor Ecal, Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F. Writing the classical prefix product as P=[a b;c d], its exact Gauss factorization gives symbol(K_tot)=a, symbol(Ecal_tot)=b, symbol(F_tot)=c/a. (4.1) Indeed the upper triangular products multiply their off-diagonal entries by E_1K_2+E_2, while the lower triangular product gives F_1+K_1^(-1)F_2. Taking B_-^(-1)B_+ gives P with precisely the three entries in (4.1). For simultaneous conjugation A xi and the actual symplectic form, [the uniform moment-map calculation](quantum_source_bridge_extension.md) proves iota_(A xi) Omega=(2u da+v dc+w db)/a, xi=u h+v e_sl+w f_sl, where h=diag(1,-1), e_sl=E_12, f_sl=E_21. With the convention iota_(X_H)Omega=dH, equation (4.1) therefore yields X_logK=A(h/2), X_F=A(e_sl-(c/(2a))h), X_Ecal=A(a f_sl). (4.2) The cut stabilizer is ker ell, ell(h,e_sl,f_sl)=(2,1,-1). Thus K,F alone describe a different Borel. Its actual cut basis h+2f_sl, e_sl+f_sl is instead obtained from A(h+2f_sl)=(2/a)(X_K+X_Ecal), A(e_sl+f_sl)=X_F+(c/a^2)X_K+(1/a)X_Ecal. (4.3) These relations also give literal quantum Ward identities with a specified operator order. For any full tensor endomorphism J commuting with the actual coproduct generators, both W_1(J)=2 K_tot^(-1)([K_tot,J]+[Ecal_tot,J]), W_2(J)=[F_tot,J]+F_tot K_tot^(-1)[K_tot,J] +K_tot^(-1)[Ecal_tot,J] (4.4) vanish exactly. Their first commutator symbols divided by H=Log Q give the two vector fields in (4.3). No quantum Log K is needed. The coefficients in (4.4) multiply on the left; interchanging their order introduces genuine additional quantum terms. Equations (4.3)--(4.4) identify the principal cut-framing currents, but are not by themselves a quantum representation of the cut Borel Lie algebra. The Hopf-adjoint presentation below removes their variable-coefficient ambiguity at the finite matrix level. ### The Hopf adjoint gives constant conjugation fields For h in the actual quantum group define its actual action on matrices by ad_h(C)=sum rho(h_1) C rho(S h_2). The displayed coproduct and antipode formulas give, exactly, (ad_K-I)(C)=[K,C]K^(-1), ad_Ecal(C)=[Ecal,C]K^(-1), ad_F(C)=[F,C]+K^(-1)[K,C]F. (4.5) In the tensor formulas K,Ecal,F are their actual total coproducts. The first commutator symbols divided by H are therefore (ad_K-I)/H -> A(h/2), ad_Ecal/H -> A f_sl, ad_F/H -> A e_sl. (4.6) For F, the extra term contributes (c/a)X_logK, canceling the h component in (4.2). Thus 2(ad_K-I)+2ad_Ecal, ad_F+ad_Ecal (4.7) are literal quantum Ward operators with principal fields A(h+2f_sl), A(e_sl+f_sl). They use the actual truncated E, including its endpoint, and no logarithm of K. The conventional opposite sign of fundamental conjugation vector-field brackets agrees with the Ecal-to-f_sl and F-to-e_sl correspondence. No exact two-generator Lie or coideal presentation is being inferred solely from these first symbols. The K,F Hopf Ward rows and the rows in (1.1) are related by an invertible exact row operation: X_H=X K^(-1), Z_H=Z+K^(-1)X F, X=X_H K, Z=Z_H-K^(-1)X_H K F. (4.8) Hence (1.4) transfers to the Hopf Ward complex by substituting the second line of (4.8) into h. Its cut homotopy is Phi-p=-Tr(K B_cut (ad_K-I)(C)), (4.9) with B_cut from (2.1). This is an actual cochain row transformation. ### Pivotal partial trace is an exact Hopf-adjoint chain map For two actual modules V,W let ptr_W(C)=Tr_W((I tensor g_W)C), g_W=K_W^(1-N). Then for every matrix C, not only for invariant intertwiners, ptr_W(ad_h C)=ad_h(ptr_W C). (4.10) One exact proof identifies End(V tensor W) with V tensor W tensor W* tensor V* and contracts W tensor W* by the actual right pivotal cap w tensor phi |-> phi(g_W w). This cap is a Hopf map by the checked antipode identities. The resulting contraction is literally the displayed weighted partial trace. There is also a generator check with no categorical premise. For K, cyclicity of the W trace and commutation of g_W with K_W give the assertion. For Ecal, expand [Ecal_V K_W+Ecal_W,C] * (K_V K_W)^(-1). The V terms give the right side, and the two W terms cancel because K_W^(-1)g_W is central. For F, expand the third formula of (4.5) for F_tot=F_V+K_V^(-1)F_W. Again the V terms give the right side; the W terms cancel by K_W F_W g_W K_W^(-1)=g_W F_W, which follows from the same centrality. The generator identities extend by composition to every h. Iterating gives every original pivotal closed-strand contraction. Thus the degree-zero map ptr and its rowwise degree-one map give an exact map from the full finite tensor Hopf-Ward complex (using its actual image as degree one) to the cut Hopf-Ward complex. The scalar contraction and the actual cut homotopy are now attached to that finite diagram. This does not yet identify scalar partial Gaussian elimination with that operator-valued diagram. It must transport the E endpoint, the diagonal K poles, cumulative F carries, and the chosen normal source. A remaining flow index is not automatically an open matrix index. That is the remaining algebraic comparison, rather than a consequence of Schur scalarity or (4.10). ## 5. Uniform size and regularity of the actual contraction For the prescribed unit-circle root, |Q^(-a)-Q^(-b)|>=4/N for a!=b, |1-Q^(r+1)|>=4/N. These follow from sin(pi/N)>=2/N. With the maximum entry norm, ||H_K(X)|| <= N ||X||/(4|x|), ||H_F(Z)|| <= N(N-1)||Z||/4. (4.1) The coefficients in (1.2) each have modulus at most one, giving the second bound. Hence the actual Ward contraction is regular at M=1 and has polynomial bounds in N on compact meridian sets away from zero. This estimate does not involve d_N(M); that separate marked line keeps all its original divisors and jets. Polynomial control of a projection does not imply that its value on a given nonzero vector has a nonzero exponential rate. Its kernel contains many nonzero matrices. The bound is useful only after the actual source class has been shown to survive the map. ## 6. What this does and does not settle about the geometric block The partially summed actual family has a nonzero transverse formal geometric block and an actual bulk operator with geometric support, as proved in [the partial support construction](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md). The remaining two-index framing functional has not thereby been identified with the contraction (1.4), nor with the sourced centralizer transgression. That identification requires explicit Ward currents from the local R coproduct identities after partial elimination, and a map retaining the chosen source and normal row. If a nonzero formal geometric class were proved to map into ker delta as a nonzero endomorphism, then its cut would be nonzero algebraically: ker delta=k I and Phi(I)=1. This is a precise reduction of the needed normalization problem, not a proof of that embedding or its nonzero scalar coefficient. Ward identities plus unknot normalization alone cannot prove that coefficient is nonzero for every knot: arbitrary scalar families C_K=c_K I satisfy both commutator equations, with c_unknot=1 and c_K=0 allowed elsewhere. The missing source map must supply more information than the universal commutant calculation. No global cycle, Stokes, or volume inference is made here. The [cyclic Ward completion](cyclic_ward_norm_adapter.md) also computes the missing raising edge, its full Frobenius determinant character, and a literal quantum-factorial affine source equation. This retains the complete d_N(M) adapter. It is a further exact source datum for the missing Gaussian/adjoint comparison, rather than a replacement for that comparison. ## 7. Subsequent currents and an exact divided-normal realization of the cut The [literal local R currents](local_r_ward_transfer_currents.md) now give the unsummed E and F Ward divergence formulas with the full missing-edge source and inserted moments. Their ordinary closed wall source cancels exactly, so a locally nonzero wall entry cannot by itself certify the global geometric contribution. On the genuine complete integral-color lift there is a different specified normal operator: the [true divided Hopf adjoint](divided_adjoint_marked_edge_pairing.md) J_ad=[(ad_Ecal)^N/(1-Q^N)]_root. For the literal missing edge W=E_(N-1,0), direct calculation gives J_ad(W)=-N sum_(a=0)^(N-2) E_(a,a+1), Phi(J_ad(W))=-(N-1). Therefore the normalized row Phi_div(C)=-Phi(J_ad(C W))/(N-1) has Phi_div(I)=1 and obeys the exact all-matrices homotopy Phi_div-Phi=(Phi_div-Phi)h delta. It returns the original invariant on every actual closed tangle. Generic pivotal naturality before division also gives an explicit full-network realization, with the ordered insertion T(W_cut tensor I) retained. This supplies an actual divided-normal cut, rather than a conjectural scalar normalization. The [complete-color theorem](complete_color_divided_ward_and_fusion.md) keeps its q-normal distinct from the fixed-root meridian normal, and retains the pivot and framing derivatives. Its one-sided fusion correction is a finite exponential with nilpotence bounded by tensor length. The opposite divided Ward actions contain an SL_2 block, so a nilpotent whole gauge group is not asserted. The Gaussian/source comparison and selected volume norm remain the additional theorem. The [subsequent complete-color residual theorem](residual_gaussian_ward_currents.md) now computes the dual cut rows explicitly and transports their currents through the actual nondegenerate transverse Gaussian. Their two compensated framing fields have precisely the source covariance of Omega_cut, and their formal ideal is the flat line of that actual Gaussian amplitude. This supplies an all-order interior formal ideal, while preserving the distinction from the whole finite relative-source complex. The [finite-cut source audit](finite_cut_euler_source_obstruction.md) shows explicitly why such local formal closure alone cannot prove nonzero selected source survival. [Exact matrix audit](../experiments/audit_actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction.py). [Results](../experiments/actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction_results.json).

title: Uniformly bounded physical quantum meridians through every actual braid
text: # Uniformly bounded physical quantum meridians through every actual braid 28 October 2026. The particular Heisenberg meridian matrices of the ORIGINAL quantum crossing are uniformly bounded in N along any fixed signed braid word, despite the possible exponential condition number of its crossing matrices. The reason is the EXACT quantum Hurwitz law: their conjugates are fixed Nielsen words in the initial meridians, whose inverses have a bounded polynomial formula. Their entries and adjoints asymptotically commute in operator norm. Consequently every positive Gram moment limit has compact, honest SL2 free-group/braid-graph support, including Gauss-chart boundaries. This does NOT impose the original knot closure on such a positive state or identify singular atomic shape phases with that support. Those are explicit remaining requirements for a sharp upper bound. ## 1. The original complete-head observables form a bounded star family Use the actual balanced factorial basis, N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=-q^(-1), rho=q-q^(-1). Put K=x Z^(-1), e=q rho^2 E, f=F, Z w_a=Q^a w_a. These are the ORIGINAL finite quantum-group matrices. Explicitly f w_a=(1-Q^(a+1))w_(a+1), a<d, f w_d=0, e w_(a+1)=(x^(-1)-xQ^(-a))w_a, a<d. In the actual flat positive head metric, ||K||=||K^(-1)||=1, ||e||,||f||<=2, K^*=K^(-1), e^*=x f, f^*=x e. (1) The last identities follow entrywise using xQ=x^(-1). They do not assert unitarity of the original braiding or positivity of its pivotal closing, both of which have separate exact obstructions. The scaled relations are Ke=QeK, Kf=Q^(-1)fK, [e,f]=(Q-1)(K-K^(-1)), fe=c-QK-K^(-1), c=x^(-1)+Qx. (2) Thus commutators among e,f,K,K^(-1) and ALL their adjoints have norm O(|Q-1|)=O(1/N). Different heads commute exactly. There is no inverse rho or factorial in these estimates. ## 2. Bounded matrices and polynomial inverses On an auxiliary two-dimensional space define the actual L matrices L_+=[[K,e],[0,I]], L_-=[[I,0],[-Kf,K]], L_-^(-1)=[[I,0],[f,K^(-1)]], G=L_-^(-1)L_+=[[K,e],[fK,fe+K^(-1)]]. (3) All L matrices and their inverses have norm at most 3: each is a unitary block diagonal plus an off-diagonal block of norm at most 2. Consequently ||G||,||G^(-1)||<=9. The exact quantum identity already proved from the original entries is G^2-cG+QI=0, G^(-1)=Q^(-1)(cI-G). (4) It supplies an alternative polynomial inverse, without choosing a Gauss face denominator or inverting a nilpotent root shift. For b heads set P_(j-1)=L_(-,j-1)...L_(-,1) and H_j=P_(j-1)^(-1)G_j P_(j-1), 1<=j<=b. (5) These are the actual based meridians (the physical SL2 lift is -H_j). Before any braid action, ||H_j||,||H_j^(-1)||<=9^j<=C_b, C_b=9^b. (6) All entries are fixed-degree polynomials in the head observables (1), with coefficients bounded uniformly in N. Their inverse entries also have this property by (4). ## 3. Exact all-word Heisenberg transport and its uniform bound Let B_i be the ORIGINAL checked crossing on heads i,i+1, with its full common Cartan scalar either included or retained in the unchanged external line. The direct finite proof in [the shared quantum flags](actual_shared_quantum_flags_and_charged_exchange.md) gives the exact two-head identities. They extend to (5) as Ad_(B_i) H_i=H_(i+1), Ad_(B_i) H_(i+1)=H_(i+1)H_iH_(i+1)^(-1), Ad_(B_i) H_j=H_j for j!=i,i+1. (7) Indeed the earlier prefix commutes with B_i. For later heads the two adjacent L_- factors in the prefix have their product preserved by the same original Hopf intertwining; thus the later prefix is unchanged. The inverse crossing gives Ad_(B_i^(-1)) H_i=H_i^(-1)H_(i+1)H_i, Ad_(B_i^(-1)) H_(i+1)=H_i. (8) No inverse of B is estimated by its operator norm. Repeatedly substituting (7)-(8) expresses, for EVERY actual signed prefix W of length m, W H_j W^(-1)=w_(W,j)(H_1,...,H_b), (9) where w is the explicit free-group Nielsen word. Its unreduced length is at most 3^m; free cancellation can only improve it. Therefore, uniformly for all levels N, ||W H_j W^(-1)||, ||(W H_j W^(-1))^(-1)|| <=C_b^(3^m). (10) The bound is intentionally coarse and may be large in the fixed diagram. Its point is independence of N. All full Cartan/framing/ peripheral scalars remain those of W; its scalar line cancels only in this genuine conjugation identity. Each entry on the right of (9), and its adjoint, is a fixed-degree bounded polynomial in (1). Leibniz expansion of a commutator and (2) now prove, for ANY two such entries at ANY two prefixes, ||[A_N,B_N]||, ||[A_N,B_N^*]||<=C_(b,W)/N. (11) Thus the full finite family of transported physical meridian observables is uniformly bounded and asymptotically commuting as a star family. A general Heisenberg conjugate of an arbitrary coupon does not enjoy (10); the exact Nielsen relation is essential here. ## 4. What every positive Gram limit actually supports Take ANY positive trace-class Gamma_N of trace one on the initial b-head Hilbert space. This could be a normalized Gram of a specified annotated network if that construction is available; no positive pivotal closing is being assumed. For the fixed family above every polynomial moment is uniformly bounded, so a subsequence has all moments convergent. Equation (11) lets these limits be regarded as a functional on the COMMUTATIVE polynomial star algebra of the limiting entries. It is positive because for every polynomial p, lim Tr(Gamma_N p_N^*p_N)>=0. It has a compact representation. To see the needed boundedness directly, use real and imaginary coordinate operators. Each has norm at most a fixed C. Thus in its polynomial GNS inner product, multiplication by each real coordinate is a commuting selfadjoint operator of norm at most C: positivity of C^2-X_N^2 passes to the limit. Their joint spectrum is compact and represents the moments by a positive measure. This uses the actual operator bounds, not normalized expectations of a nonpositive source. At any character of that commutative algebra let k,e,f denote a head's values. Equations (1)-(2) imply |k|=1, f=-conjugate(e), ef+k+k^(-1)=-2. The commuting matrix g from (3) therefore has determinant one and trace -2. Its based versions h_j in (5) are genuine SL2 matrices, including the central value -I. All their inverses remain regular. The exact identities (7)-(9) show that the time-indexed character matrices are precisely the honest free-group Hurwitz braid graph. This statement persists when a local Gauss coordinate or flag cross-ratio chart degenerates. It does not require a bounded inverse of that chart's denominator. For example, if a SPECIFIED positive annotated state additionally obeyed the actual closed-meridian matching equations in mean square, its limiting measure would be supported on honest knot representations. For a polynomial matrix constraint F, the statement follows from Tr(Gamma_N F_N^*F_N)->0 and positivity. Establishing that property for the ORIGINAL relative closing is a remaining theorem, not a consequence of (10) or an assertion of this note. ## 5. Why final cut vectorization does not supply those constraints The actual assembled knot cut is C_K=f_(K,N)I. When it is nonzero, its normalized vectorized Gram is EXACTLY |vec C_K><vec C_K|/||C_K||_HS^2 =|vec I><vec I|/N. (12) It is the same cut state for every knot. The scalar norm stores the unknown period; the normalized state by itself contains no interior meridian or atomic-shape data. Such data must be added as a specified bounded observable/source lift, rather than inferred from (12). Retaining all internal coupon moments is possible algebraically, but the original closing is not a positive multiplicative compression: its canonical nilpotent Pi satisfies ptr_g(Pi)=I and Pi^2=0, while ptr_g(I)=0. The [actual positivity obstruction](actual_quantum_source_positivity_obstruction.md) therefore remains relevant. The polynomial norm of that extension helps retain it; it does not automatically make its positive Gram impose all original closure equations. Finally, honest physical braid-graph support alone does not identify the JOINT atom-shape limit at singular face denominators. A boundary comparison must retain those shapes and their regulator, not merely bounded physical matrices. The saturated critical compactification theorem already bounds the regulator on the genuine critical joint closure; this note does not prove that every source boundary belongs to that closure. The unconditional advance is (9)-(11): the specific physical Heisenberg meridians need no uncontrolled braid-condition-number estimate. No sharp whole-period upper bound is asserted here. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_bounded_quantum_meridians.py): literal original signed prefixes, all based quantum matrices, exact Nielsen substitution, polynomial inverses and direct complex star/ commutator bounds. It retains both crossing signs and original Cartan factors in the matrix comparisons.

title: The actual braid transport has a semisimple sector
text: # The actual braid transport has a semisimple sector Research note, 26 October 2026. The finite-by-Heisenberg result for ideal shape ordering does not extend to the full actual braid-source transport. At every level the latter has a connected subgroup with an SL_2 quotient. We prove this from the prescribed crossing, using a nonzero exact pivotal moment and an ordinary-trace identity with definite sign. Finite-index restriction cannot remove that sector. This suggests a relative approach: retain the semisimple central/spectral algebra and study its normalization or period extension. We give an explicit rank-four algebra for the two unipotent generators, and show how the already computed actual two-channel source splits on a quadratic spectral cover. Neither construction identifies its spectral coordinate with the geometric A-curve or proves the volume conjecture. ## 1. Fix the actual crossing and its phase Let N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), and use exactly the actual color V=V_(x_0), x_0=q^(N-1)=-q^(-1). Write B for the checked crossing with the common Cartan scalar removed, as in the original ADO cut. Its zero-framing scalar is theta=x_0^(1-N), theta^(2N)=1. Replacing B_i by theta^(-1)B_i gives the same zero-framed word evaluation and is still a braid representation. Thus the pure braid powers below are the actual normalized ones: U_1=B_12^(2N)=I+X, U_2=B_23^(2N)=I+Y, J=B^(2N)-I, X=J tensor I, Y=I tensor J. (1.1) For the full universal crossing the common scalar and twist cancel in this same normalization. No peripheral or modified dimension factor is changed. The [independently proved Casimir interpolation](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md#3-the-actual-crossing-has-a-unique-confluent-polynomial) has double nodes c_k=q^h+q^(-h), h=2k+1<N, with r_N(c_k)=nu_k=(-1)^k q^(k(k+1)), r_N'(c_k)/nu_k=-(N-h)/[2(q^h-q^(-h))]. The one possible simple node has the same root-of-unity property nu_k^(2N)=1. Since B=r_N(Omega), (1.1) obeys J^2=0, X^2=Y^2=0. (1.2) The claim follows by evaluating the value and derivative of (r_N^(2N)-1)^2 at every double node; both are zero. The same polynomial vanishes at the simple node. This is a statement about the actual matrices, not a formal leading symbol or a spectral projector substituted for a crossing. ## 2. An exact nonzero pivotal moment Keep the original K and pivot g=K^(1-N)=(-1)^(N-1)K. The already proved closing functional on the Casimir algebra is ptr_K f(Omega) =[-sum_(h odd, 0<h<N) (c_h f(c_h)+(q^h-q^(-h))^2 f'(c_h)) + simple-node contribution] I. For f=r_N^(2N)-1 its node values are zero and its double-node derivatives are -N(N-h)/(q^h-q^(-h)). Therefore, exactly, ptr_K J=Phi_N I, Phi_N=N sum_(h odd, 0<h<N)(N-h)(q^h-q^(-h)) =-2N^2/rho !=0. (2.1) For the last equality multiply the sum by rho and use rho(q^h-q^(-h)) =(q^(h+1)+q^(-h-1))-(q^(h-1)+q^(-h+1)). The weighted sum telescopes; q^N=-1 and the Q-geometric sum give -2N, for either parity of N. Thus no exceptional level or unverified noncancellation hypothesis enters (2.1). With the actual pivot the corresponding scalar is L_N=(-1)^(N-1) Phi_N. Sequentially closing strands 3 and 2 in XY gives t_reduced,W(XY)=L_N^2, mathfrak_t_W(XY)=d_N(1)L_N^2 !=0, d_N(1)=i^(N+3)/N. (2.2) These are the actual cut and its full modified normalization. This test uses the pure-braid source operators; the braid powers depend on N. It is not the fixed-knot volume limit. ## 3. A negative ordinary trace forces a semisimple quotient For a pair matrix use the total integer degree a+b. The actual B and J preserve that degree, so the ordinary partial traces A=Tr_1 J, C=Tr_2 J are diagonal. We claim C=-conjugate(A). Here is a direct proof retaining the original Cartan order. Write B=P D Theta, where P is the swap and D_(a,b)=x_0^(-a-b)q^(2ab). In this color E_j=[j]_q^2 is real and F is the real unit shift. Complex conjugation of the finite Euler coefficients gives Theta^(-1), while conjugation gives D^(-1) on D. The finite inverse identity is the ordinary Euler convolution on its nilpotent argument. Hence conjugate(B)=D^(-1) P B^(-1) P D, conjugate(J)=-D^(-1) P J P D. (3.1) The second equation uses J^2=0. On diagonal entries the D factors cancel. Summing the diagonals gives C=-conjugate(A). Consequently on W=V^(tensor 3), Tr_W(XY)=Tr(A C)=-sum_a |A_aa|^2 <0. (3.2) The strict inequality has a proof, not a numerical assumption: Tr(A K)=Tr[J(I tensor K)]=N Phi_N !=0. Indeed (2.1) computes this trace by closing the other factor. As |K_aa|=1, it also gives the quantitative bound -Tr_W(XY) >= N |Phi_N|^2=4N^5/|rho|^2. (3.3) Now XY has a nonzero eigenvalue lambda. Choose v with XYv=lambda v and put w=Yv. Then Xv=0, Xw=lambda v, Yv=w, Yw=0. The vectors v,w are independent. Their plane is invariant under U_1,U_2, with matrices U_1|=[1 lambda;0 1], U_2|=[1 0;1 1]. (3.4) Their cyclic powers are Zariski dense in the respective one-parameter upper and lower unipotent groups, since the characteristic is zero. Those two groups generate SL_2: elementary upper/lower row operations give its open Gaussian cell and its remaining matrices. Thus the closure of the subgroup generated by U_1,U_2 has an SL_2 quotient on this plane and lies in the identity component of the full braid image closure. In particular that identity component is not solvable, and is not nilpotent. Every finite-index subgroup of the original braid group contains positive powers of both pure braids. The same plane argument applies with their two nonzero parameters rescaled. Thus no such restriction removes this connected semisimple sector, at any N>=2. The invariant plane here is selected from an eigenvalue of XY; it is not asserted to be the two-cup corner. That corner is not generally preserved by the full braid powers. Nor does this theorem compute the difference-Galois group of the minimal quantum A-operator or identify its selected geometric branch. It tests the full retained braid transport, which is stronger data than a normalization line. ## 4. The two-square-zero algebra has an explicit spectral center There is nevertheless a useful reduction. In the universal algebra on X,Y with X^2=Y^2=0, put c=XY+YX. It commutes with both generators. Every alternating word reduces to a C[c]-linear combination of 1,X,Y,XY; for example (XY)^k=c^(k-1)XY and XYX=cX. These four elements are independent, as the following model over C[c] shows: X=[0 1;0 0], Y=[0 0;c 0], XY=[c 0;0 0]. Its commutator equations also show that the center is exactly C[c]. After c is inverted the algebra is Mat_2(C[c,c^(-1)]), with matrix units e_11=XY/c, e_22=YX/c, e_12=X, e_21=Y/c. (4.1) Thus on a simple nonzero spectral component the comparison problem reduces to a line. Replacing a source module by only its scalar center still loses its multiplicity, lattice and period functional; those remain specified data. At c=0 the flat abstract fiber is the four-dimensional exterior algebra X^2=Y^2=0, YX=-XY. Its augmentation ideal has cube zero, and [1+sX,1+tY]=1+2stXY is central. This is the two-step nilpotent fiber. The ambient two-by-two matrix specialization of the displayed model is not faithful there; using it alone would lose the flat source directions. A finite field extension cannot send a nonzero spectral value c to this zero fiber. For the actual X,Y of (1.1), (3.2) proves that nonzero spectral components occur. The spectral center is for this pair of pure powers. It is not claimed to commute with the original B_12,B_23, or to give their entire knot-period decomposition. ## 5. The actual cap source detects its matrix sector There is also a completely calibrated source test. Use the actual adjacent cups and caps from [the source normal form](adjacent_source_normal_form.md#1-adjacent-cups-and-caps-give-opposite-source-matrix-units). Their operators Pi_1,Pi_2 have square zero and obey Pi_1 Pi_2 Pi_1=Pi_1, Pi_2 Pi_1 Pi_2=Pi_2. Their common corner is two copies of V. On it they are E_12,E_21, with the actual full modified trace d_N(1) times the ordinary two-by-two trace. Let A_s=I+s Pi_1, B_t=I+t Pi_2, C_(s,t)=A_s B_t A_s^(-1) B_t^(-1). On the corner det C=1 and Tr C=2+s^2t^2, and it is the identity on the complementary source. Therefore, exactly, mathfrak_t_W(C_(s,t)^m-I) =d_N(1)[T_m(2+s^2t^2)-2], (5.1) T_0=2, T_1=z, T_(m+1)=zT_m-T_(m-1). This follows from the actual rectangular trace calibration, not from choosing a new scalar trace. For s=t=1 the trace argument is 3, so the right side detects the semisimple matrix dynamics. These localized source units need not be braid words; (3.4) supplies the separate genuine-braid theorem. Growth in m in (5.1) concerns word length at a fixed N, not growth of a fixed knot as the level changes. ## 6. A cover can split the spectral algebra instead of killing it The original meridian source already has the appropriate quadratic deformation. Its two numerators satisfy t_1^2=delta t_1, t_2^2=delta t_2, z=t_1t_2+t_2t_1-delta(t_1+t_2) central. On the actual charged two-copy block, delta=rho(M^2-M^(-2)), A_N=(-1)^N rho(M+M^(-1)) *(qM^2-q^(-1)M^(-2))/(M^N+M^(-N)), z=A_N^2-delta^2. (6.1) All functions are the previously calibrated actual ones. In particular the peripheral denominator is retained. More generally pass to the quadratic cover A^2=z+delta^2. Where A and z are units, the identities e_11=(t_1t_2-delta t_1)/z, e_22=(t_2t_1-delta t_2)/z, e_12=(t_1-delta e_11)/A, e_21=(t_2-delta e_22)/A (6.2) are matrix units, directly splitting this rank-four algebra. The actual mark is A=A_N, and at completeness A_N=(-1)^N rho^2 is nonzero. Thus the meridian source is on the matrix-algebra locus at each fixed level, rather than at its nilpotent fiber. Once these source generators and the charged simple module are matched, their simultaneous comparison is a scalar line. This is a useful finite-cover reduction of a torsor problem. It preserves the semisimple algebra, its integral source and its trace, while making the remaining comparison rank one. It does not prove that the same central functions and cut are realized on the geometric triangulation or A-curve. This statement concerns the integral numerators t_i. It does not supply a common finite lattice for both unscaled projectors t_i/delta; their double-pole trace obstruction from the adjacent-source note remains in force. ## 7. Consequence for the Regge and cover strategy The [finite Regge/ordering result](regge_period_covers_and_a_curves.md) and its Heisenberg period kernel remain valid. The present theorem rules out extending that nilpotence claim to the whole actual braid-source group. A finite cover can still choose roots, split a spectral algebra and make scalar comparison possible, as (6.2) shows. The target must keep the semisimple source and seek a controlled period extension or marked quotient over it. Such a relative viewpoint has existing coverage in [Hain's relative Malcev theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9607019). Also, the stated homological model of [De Renzi--Martel, 2212.10940](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.10940) uses Heisenberg coefficients for quantum mapping-class-group representations. A nilpotent coefficient group does not assert that the represented mapping class or braid image is nilpotent. [Karvounis, 1909.11162](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.11162) already treats projective quantum-sl2 braid representations and nontrivial central action. Only their stated coverage was consulted; none of their proofs is used above. We have not identified the SL_2 plane of (3.4) with hyperbolic holonomy, built the requisite relative completion of the selected quantum A-period, or proved its regulator norm. The original conjecture remains unproved. [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_semisimple_transport.py) checks the genuine pure powers, the conjugation and pivotal identities, full original source closings, and the spectral matrix-unit and commutator formulas. [Results](../experiments/actual_semisimple_transport_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_actual_semisimple_transport.py

text: # The actual braided residual-framing current 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. After a legitimate coherent functional fixes the first cut, the actual Hopf adjoint gives an exact current in the second cut. Its coefficients are two routed OFF-DIAGONAL bands of the original tensor. They are not reconstructed from the diagonal two-cut array. The identity holds at arbitrary width, with actual finite endpoints and every genuine quantum jet. This is a finite-source integration-by-parts identity. Its closed flux is zero; no nonzero relative framing residue or selected global cycle coefficient is inferred from that fact. ## 1. The source, coherent first cut, and actual generic generators Use the [braided source adapter](actual_braided_two_cut_source_adapter.md). Fix d=N-1 and zeta=q0 exp(epsilon). At the two actual Morse cuts let V=V_d^tensor b, W=V_d^tensor c, with b,c>=1, and let A:W->V and B:V->W be the original covariant maps. Original cups, caps and all scalar/peripheral factors remain in A,B. The partial closure P_V uses the actual generic pivot g=(-1)^d K on the closed heads. Let U be the recorded braid carrying the chosen W head to its first position. Thus in the parallel convention U=R_1...R_j, with R_j acting first. Define the WHOLE band operator C_(p,q)=P_V[A U^-1(E_pq tensor I)U B], J_(a,l)=(C_(l,l))_(a,a). (1) Indices outside 0,...,d are zero ACTUAL matrix entries. No Fourier wrap or continued endpoint is substituted for that zero. By actual integer degree conservation C_(l,l) is diagonal, although the nearby band operators in (1) need not be. Closing the identity cut gives sum_l C_(l,l)=z(epsilon)I. For t distinct from 0,1 put beta_a(t)=binom(d,a)t^a(1-t)^(d-a), e_t=beta(t) 1^T, Tr e_t=sum_a beta_a=1. (2) This is the existing coherent boundary functional with w=1 and z_coh=t/(1-t). It is source-preserving on the WHOLE exposed scalar: Tr(e_t zI)=z, exactly, including the fixed d=N-1. It is not an additional normalized state on the second identity edge. All formulas below also hold for any specified quantum-independent vector beta of sum one; (2) is the legitimate coherent localization used here. Write the actual generic generator entries as k_a=zeta^(d-2a), f_a=1-Q^(a+1), 0<=a<d, e_a=zeta^(-N)(1-Q^(N-a)), 1<=a<=d, Q=zeta^2. (3) Their missing endpoint arrows are ZERO. In particular f_d=e_0=0 as matrices, even though the untruncated expressions in (3) need not vanish there at generic zeta. The Hopf adjoints are ad_K C=K C K^-1, ad_E C=[E,C]K^-1, ad_F C=[F,C]+K^-1[K,C]F. The residual combination is D_c=ad_F-ad_E-2(ad_K-I). (4) Its proved principal framing field is partial_r in the actual F(r,s) chart, with the first cut clock A_cut=(1+s)^-1 fixed; see [the actual Ward fields](actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction.md). Multiplication by s gives s partial_r. We do not identify a finite translation with this infinitesimal field merely from its symbol. ## 2. A source-defined flux using the two neighboring bands For 0<=a<d define L_a=f_a beta_a+(e_(a+1)/k_(a+1)) beta_(a+1), L_-1=L_d=0. (5) Define the actual band pairing and its second-head flux by T_t(p,q)=Tr(e_t C_(p,q)), M_l=f_l T_t(l+1,l) +(e_(l+1)/k_(l+1)) T_t(l,l+1), 0<=l<d, M_-1=M_d=0. (6) Every C_(p,q) contains the full U and U^-1 and all original contractions. In particular (6) is not a choice of interpolation for J. The source identity is M_l-M_(l-1) =sum_(a=0)^d (L_a-L_(a-1)) J_(a,l) =sum_(a=0)^(d-1) L_a[J_(a,l)-J_(a+1,l)], 0<=l<=d. (7) Here is a direct proof. Generic pivotal partial closure is an exact Hopf-adjoint map, and A,B,U intertwine the actual coproduct. Therefore applying D_c to C_(l,l) is the same as replacing its inserted E_ll by the corresponding adjoint in W. Since E_ll commutes with K, the spectator terms cancel, and the inserted matrix is exactly f_l E_(l+1,l)+(e_(l+1)/k_(l+1))E_(l,l+1) -f_(l-1)E_(l,l-1)-(e_l/k_l)E_(l-1,l), (8) tensored with the spectator identity and conjugated by U. Its pairing is the left side of (7), with all four bands and their actual order. On the first cut the dual rows are, literally, e_(t,K)=K^-1 e_t K-e_t, e_(t,E)=K^-1 e_t E-E K^-1 e_t, e_(t,F)=e_t F-K F e_t K^-1. The K row has zero diagonal. Direct multiplication gives (e_(t,F)-e_(t,E)-2e_(t,K))_(a,a) =f_a beta_a-f_(a-1) beta_(a-1) -(e_a/k_a) beta_a+(e_(a+1)/k_(a+1)) beta_(a+1) =L_a-L_(a-1). (9) Only these diagonals pair with C_(l,l). This proves the first equality in (7); finite summation by parts gives the second. The proof applies to rectangular A,B and arbitrary fixed width. It uses the actual routed bands, not a scalar Ward operator assigned to an unrelated residual index. For clarity, the generic interior coefficient in (5) is e_(a+1)/k_(a+1)=zeta[Q^(a+1-N)-1]. At the root (5) becomes L_a=(1-Q^(a+1))[beta_a-q0 beta_(a+1)]. This shorter root formula must NOT be differentiated as the generic current: the omitted term is zeta Q^(a+1)(Q^-N-1) beta_(a+1), whose first derivative at zero is -2N q0 Q^(a+1) beta_(a+1). Equation (5) retains it and all higher genuine derivatives. ## 3. Finite-head integration by parts, with the interval ends Let R_l denote either expression on the right of (7), and let h_l be any specified finite-head weight. On EVERY actual subinterval 0<=L<=R<=d, sum_(l=L)^R h_l R_l =h_R M_R-h_L M_(L-1) +sum_(l=L)^(R-1)(h_l-h_(l+1)) M_l. (10) In particular a window's two current ends are retained. On the whole head interval the actual endpoint arrows make M_-1=M_d=0. For h=1 this says sum_l R_l=0. It also follows from sum_l J_(a,l)=z and sum_a(L_a-L_(a-1))=0. Neither proof says that the current has zero period on an arbitrarily selected relative subchain, or that one of its two ends contributes nontrivially. The identity is generic before any specialization. It may be differentiated to any fixed quantum order, with the derivatives of the actual U, inverse route, generator entries, pivots, coupons and any moving h retained. The same holds for a specified finite sum of channel assignments with its original coefficients. The original closed normalization remains F=D_N z and z(0)=F'(0)/nu_N, with D_N=(-1)^d[N]_zeta. No extra derivative per band or per vertex is introduced by (7). ### The complete Fourier endpoint of the same actual channel At completeness let S be the cyclic physical-head shift and X_j its original Fourier projectors, (X_j)_(r,s)=Q^[j(s-r)]/N, eta_j=Q^j, j mod N. For the ROUTED first-slot channel C(X)=P_V[A U^-1(X tensor I)U B], the [complete Fourier source theorem](universal_resonant_fourier_source_completion.md) applies: A U^-1 and U B are still actual covariant maps. Thus C(X_j)=z X_j. Its proof uses the actual root adjoint equations and C(I)=zI and also applies to the rectangular maps above. Since 1^T X_j=delta_(j,0)1^T, the legitimate first coherent functional still gives Tr(e_t C(X_j))=z delta_(j,0), exactly for every t. The actual cyclic generator formulas give D_c X_j=(eta_j-q0 eta_j^-1+2)X_j +(q0^-1 eta_j^-1-2)X_(j+1)-Q^-1 eta_j X_(j-1). (10a) Consequently this SAME sourced residual current has the exact three-node Fourier endpoint distribution Tr[e_t C(D_c X_j)] =z[(3-q0)delta_(j,0)+(q0-2)delta_(j,N-1) -delta_(j,1)]. (10b) Overlapping labels are added when N=2. The total of (10b) is zero. It is a statement about the original complete root source, not its generic normal, and no off-root cyclic endpoint is added. It locates the current at the complete resonance rather than at regular-node principal samples. Its coefficient remains the UNKNOWN whole scalar z; homogeneous Ward equations alone cannot determine it or show that the selected geometric component survives there. ## 4. The specified moving-period realization and its boundary chain There is a source-preserving residue realization of the coefficients in (6), not a new interpolation of those finite values. Expand their ORIGINAL generic tensors, including the routed crossings, in the specified finite white/cup/cap presentation. For U and U^-1 this is the FULL generic spectral expansion of each original crossing, with both small and large partner channels and their actual spectral denominators. It is not the restricted regular complete-circle sector sum. Use the actual large white polynomials and moving-period factorial with P=pi i/Log zeta. Keep every fixed generic spectral scalar and every integral character; clear a known intermediate scalar pole before taking the required higher jet. This is the source class of the [actual tensor connection](actual_tensor_source_finite_jet_connection.md). For each admissible assignment and each off-diagonal band retain its own primitive affine head lattice and ORIGINAL finite support. The band source has a fixed integral charge offset. At every allowed integer point its moving-period coefficient is the actual generic matrix entry. Its small product-cotangent torus therefore gives that same entry. Summing those tori reproduces T_t(p,q), and the displayed combinations reproduce M_l and (7), with no omitted normal. An original constant forbidden stratum remains zero rather than being assigned a 0/0 continuation. The first head may be left as the exact finite coherent sum (2). There is no need to invent a meromorphic interpolation of beta_a. For the remaining free coordinates x of an individual band let S(epsilon,x) be its specified meromorphic summand, Gamma its actual ordered residue cycle, and c(x)=product_j pi cot(pi x_j). For an integral translation v and an analytic retained weight w, change of variables gives the EXACT chain identity integral_Gamma c w (S_v-I)S =integral_Gamma c (S_-v w-w)S +integral_(Gamma+v-Gamma) c (S_-v w)S. (11) All periods use (2pi i)^(-n_free). The only fact used about c is its integer periodicity. When the last cycle difference is filled by an allowed annular chain, its value is the sum of the actual crossed source residues, with their orientations. All other crossed divisors, and any remaining relative ends, stay in that formula. At a coincident source/cotangent pole one must use the full finite part and complement derivative, as in the [actual degree-wall theorem](actual_matching_edge_degree_cycle_boundary.md). It is not enough to multiply a cup's simple residue by an assigned geometric scalar. Equation (7) is proved AFTER the original finite internal period contraction. The subsequent [common-band theorem](actual_matching_graph_common_band_ward_current.md) supplies its meromorphic interior Ward assembly on one primitive free-head lattice, with the actual charged insertions and full routed source. Its different original support cycles are still retained. Equation (10) keeps the exact finite-head ends of this contracted current, and (11) transports EACH specified band summand with those cycle differences. These formulas do not replace Gamma+v by Gamma merely because the source has a moving-P quasiperiod. The latter has its nontrivial rational gauge, characters and divisors even at finite normal order. ## 5. The literal source between Fourier nodes The actual routed channel has more information than its cyclic samples. Its genuine integral source preserves UNWRAPPED integer charge: if an inserted matrix is supported on row minus column equal to n, its output has that same charge. This follows before root specialization from the original crossings, cups, caps and typed degree equations. The fixed weight differences of rectangular A and B cancel. A bare root K-eigenvalue, which would identify n and n+N, is not used here. Put T_n=sum_(r-s=n)E_rs, with -d<=n<=d. Then X_j=N^-1 sum_n eta_j^(-n)T_n. Separating the DISTINCT output matrix diagonals in C(X_j)=zX_j proves C(T_n)=zT_n, -d<=n<=d, X(p)_(r,s)=p^(r-s)/N, C(X(p))=zX(p), p in C*. (12) In fact the j=0 identity suffices. X(p) is a specified finite rank-one matrix, not an interpolation assigned to contracted source values. Every physical position and every unwrapped band remains. Pairing with the same first coherent functional (2) gives exactly Tr[e_t C(X(p))]=z b_N(t,p), b_N(t,p)=(1-p^N)/[N(1-p)] (1-t+t/p)^(N-1). (13) The factor at p=1 is its removable value one. This formula follows by separately summing p^r and beta_s p^(-s), so it keeps the actual coherent degree d=N-1 and the original p=eta^-1 orientation. Whenever b_N(t,p)!=0, dividing THIS specified functional by b_N returns exactly the original root scalar z. This licenses that finite band-momentum boundary family; it does not license a general second diagonal functional or simultaneous evaluation of two heads. There is an exact whole-source absorption of this insertion. Let H=C(I)=P_V[AB]=zI, with the ORIGINAL pivots and all other source factors. Equation (12) gives Tr[e_t C(X(p))]/b_N(t,p)=Tr[e_eff H], e_eff=e_t X(p)/b_N(t,p), (e_eff)_(a,c)=beta_a(t)p^(-c)/(1-t+t/p)^d. (13a) Thus the right side is evaluated on the original white-cut network, without the extra U and U^-1 insertions. This is an identity AFTER the whole root contraction, not a local rule for moving X(p) through one crossing or moving a bare mark. No pivot has been added or removed. Moreover e_eff is exactly the existing normalized coherent kernel with z_coh=t/(1-t) and w=p^-1. Put D_p=diag(p^a). Directly, D_p^-1 e_eff D_p=e_(t_eff), t_eff=t/[p(1-t)+t]. (13b) The [original common diagonal gauge](compact_framing_gauge_and_boundary_residue.md) preserves t_eff and removes this common momentum p. Its one-cut physical map forgets the residual centralizer coordinate. Therefore the absorption supplies no additional pin of that coordinate: the two apparent parameters are one coherent position and the already present common diagonal gauge. The canceled formula for e_eff may extend across a Fourier zero of b_N, but this is not a generic-q removal of that zero or a contour transport statement. The source therefore has an exact boundary-scale test. In the first-slot chart r=1/(1-p)-b0 s, retain c0=b0 s and set p_N=1-1/(N rho+c0). For rho in a fixed compact subset of C*, and t,c0 in fixed compacts, direct expansion of the FINITE factor in (13) gives b_N(t,p_N)=rho(1-exp(-1/rho))exp(t/rho)+O(N^-1). (14) The error is uniform and absolute, including its limiting zeros. On a compact avoiding those zeros it is relative, and b_N and its inverse have bounded size for large N. At the exact Fourier nodes p=Q^-j, j!=0, (13) instead vanishes exactly. Their limiting positions rho=1/(2pi i j) are precisely the zeros in (14). At rho=infinity the displayed limiting factor tends to one. No pointwise substitution of p into the whole internal source is used to prove these facts. In the absorbed one-cut expression, t_eff=t+t(1-t)/(N rho)+O(N^-2). Thus this scaling gives a small coherent-position tilt, not an independent centralizer condition. All of (12)--(14) is ROOT-ONLY. For the original moving-q channel write Delta(epsilon,p)=C_epsilon(X(p))-z(epsilon)X(p). Although Delta(0,p)=0, its genuine first quantum derivative need not vanish. The focused original-matrix checks below exhibit nonzero derivatives, including after the coherent pairing. They retain the actual route, endpoint arrows and generic pivot. Thus differentiating (13) would discard a source term. If a quantum-dependent p is used, the additional p derivative of Delta(0,p) is zero; it does not remove the genuine defect. All required normals still use the original generic channel and the source currents (5)--(11). More explicitly, for the SAME actual generic A,B,U and pivot, the identity retaining every quantum correction is Tr[e_t C_epsilon(X(p))]/b_N =Tr[e_eff H_epsilon]+Tr[e_t Delta(epsilon,p)]/b_N. (14a) Every genuine jet differentiates the full right side. The second term cannot be discarded by the root absorption (13a). Equation (14) is a matching condition for any proposed contracted hard-edge calculation. Its coefficient is the UNKNOWN whole z. Local nonzero white packets do not determine how their transverse periods and charged support cycles reproduce that coefficient. ## 6. What covariance fixes in the genuine normal There is an exact freedom at every N. Write tau_e(X)=Tr(g_e X), D_e=tau_e(I), with the ORIGINAL generic pivot, and put B_e(X)=D_e X-tau_e(X)I. (15) Cyclicity of trace gives tau_e(ad_E X)=tau_e(ad_F X)=0 and tau_e(ad_K X)=tau_e(X) for the actual adjoints above; I is invariant. Thus B_e is a regular covariant channel, made from the straight channel and pivotal evaluation and coevaluation. It has B_e(I)=0. At the root tau_0(T_n)=0 for every unwrapped band, including T_0=I since D_0=0. Adding c(e)B_e therefore preserves C_e(I)=z(e)I and every root identity (12), for any holomorphic c. Nevertheless the constant diagonal of X(p) gives EXACTLY B_e(X(p))=D_e[X(p)-I/N], B'_0(X(p))=nu_N[X(p)-I/N], Tr[e_t B'_0(X(p))]=nu_N[b_N(t,p)-1/N]. (16) Except at the displayed zeros, this changes the retained coherent normal without changing z. This is freedom in the linear span of actual covariant tensor channels; it does not assert that every such linear combination is a single connected augmented plat. For the original routed channel, charge conservation also implies that Delta(e,p) has zero diagonal at every e: its charge-zero input is I/N and C_e(I)=z(e)I. A diagonal first functional consequently kills this defect, but also kills every nonzero off-node band. That is a zero constraint, not a determination of a boundary coefficient. The freedom is visible in an exact family of connected source words. At N=2 retain q as the generic quantum parameter, eta=q^(1/2) with eta_0=exp(pi i/4), and the original positive crossing and pivot R=eta Rhat, Rhat=[[1,0,0,0],[0,0,q^-1,0], [0,q^-1,1-q^-2,0],[0,0,0,1]], g=diag(-q,-q^-1), D=-q-q^-1. (17) These are the d=1 specialization of the original highest-weight R and pivotal closure. For any odd k>=3 choose A=R^(k-1), B=U=R. The actual routed channel is C_k(X)=ptr_g[R^(k-2)(X tensor I)R^2], C_k=eta^k Chat_k, z_k=eta^k zhat_k. Set lambda=-q^-2, u_j=sum_(r<j)lambda^r and v_j=1-u_j. The middle block of Rhat has roots 1,lambda, so its kth power is u_k times that block plus v_k I. The two literal pivotal terms of Chat_k(E10) are -q u_(k-1) and -q^-3. It follows that zhat_k=-q-q^-1 v_k, psihat_k=Chat_k(E10)_(1,0)-zhat_k =(q^-1-q^-5)u_(k-2), Chat_k(X)=(zhat_k+psihat_k)X-psihat_k tau_q(X)I/D. (18) For the last formula, the actual generic adjoint module End(V_1) splits as C I plus ker tau_q; the latter is generated by E10 and its E-adjoint ladder and has dimension three. Equivalently (18) follows by multiplying the displayed middle-block powers. Its apparently singular quotient denotes the regular literal source. Since tau_q(X(p))=D/2, the actual defect is exactly eta^k psihat_k[X(p)-I/2]. At q=i, zhat_k=-ki, psihat_k=0, partial_e psihat_k=-4i(k-2), [partial_e Delta_k(E10)]_(1,0)/z_k(0)=4(k-2)/k. (19) Here Delta_k(E10) means C_k(E10)-z_k E10. The Cartan factor eta_0^k is restored in both numerator and denominator; its derivative multiplies psihat_k(i)=0. Any retained nonzero regular exterior framing scalar has the same cancellation in this ratio. The ratios are 4/3 for k=3 and 12/5 for k=5. In particular C_5-(5/3)eta_0^2 C_3 has root scalar zero but nonzero extreme-band normal (-16i/3)eta_0^5. Both individual words are original connected odd two-braid closures with the same cut, pivot and route. For t=2/3,p=2, b_2=1 and the paired defect is HALF the extreme-band coefficient, giving ratios 2/3 and 6/5 instead. Covariance does identify the extra datum. For ANY regular covariant N=2 channel with C(I)=zI and the root identities (12), the same generic adjoint decomposition gives (18) with a scalar psi vanishing at the root. Since D'_0=-2i and g_0[0,0]=-i, C_0(E00)-z_0 E00=-psi'_0 I/2, Delta'_0(X(p))=psi'_0[X(p)-I/2]. (20) Thus this normal is determined by an additional ROOT open-diagonal source period, not by the whole-source scalar z. More generally the defect is independent of the regular covariant lift when the FULL root channel is fixed. Suppose C_e and Ctilde_e use the SAME actual generator family and fixed highest weights, are regular covariant, preserve unwrapped charge, and C_0=Ctilde_0 as maps on End(V_d). The quotient L_e=(C_e-Ctilde_e)/e is then regular, covariant and scalar on I. The proof in Sections 3--4 of the [universal root theorem](universal_resonant_fourier_source_completion.md) applies to this quotient: it uses only linearity, root adjoint covariance and L(I)=zI. Our actual root generators are precisely its M=1 generators, with BOTH missing endpoint arrows zero. Its K row, highest-input E recurrence and physical F induction therefore give L_0(X_j)=(z'_0-ztilde'_0)X_j; its Fourier-row basis gives the full matrix identity. No realization of L_e as one closed word is needed. Unwrapped charge separates the T_n as in (12), so Delta'_0(p)=Deltatilde'_0(p). (21) This requires equality of the whole open root map, not merely its scalar closure, nor equality of individual small/large root columns. Equations (15)--(21) rule out determining it from covariance and root absorption alone. They neither refute the hyperbolic conjecture nor show that the additional period cannot be controlled on the selected geometry. ## 7. The remaining equation at the framing diagonal The new ingredient relative to the old formal Ward ideal is the source-defined M_l in (6), including the off-diagonal routed bands and its finite endpoint chain. Its principal D_c field is the residual centralizer direction. A stationary pushforward would have to send THIS current and THIS chain, with the coherent first head and original complement, to the residual framing current. In particular neither the finite values J_(a,l) nor the nonzero local stationary density determine the residue at the framing diagonal. No continuous second-head current has been defined by interpolating (7). To obtain the desired framing coefficient one must identify the pushforward of the prescribed band periods (6) and the endpoint/divisor chain (10),(11) with that diagonal current, and compute its actual relative coefficient. A global cycle or nonzero endpoint intersection is not proved here. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_braided_residual_framing_current.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_braided_residual_framing_current_results.json) check 19 actual braid/complete-circle sources, including rectangular one-to-three-head birth/death cuts: 326 original routed band value/first jet coefficients, 134 flux coefficients, 334 weighted interval/jet identities, and 48 nonzero retained generic-normal corrections. Separate original-matrix checks verify 1177 full Fourier-projector channel entries and 67 three-node complete current values. The off-node extension checks 2087 unwrapped Toeplitz entries, 801 literal rank-one source entries and 57 coherent pairings. It retains 588 nonzero genuine first-normal entries and 54 nonzero coherent normal defects. Twelve boundary-scale checks include a limiting Fourier zero. The whole-source absorption has 114 actual root/first-jet checks and 801 effective coherent-gauge entries; 139 symbolic kernel identities, 139 gauge identities, six trace normalizations and the first position tilt are checked independently. The genuine-normal extension additionally checks the literal N=2 crossing and pivot jets, the factorized arbitrary-k channel identity, and the full generic channels, restored normal ratios and open-diagonal adapter for five odd braid powers. These finite checks accompany the all-k block-power proof (18), rather than replacing it. Symbolic checks verify the universal integer-shift chain rule and its resonant cotangent finite part. They do not audit an off-grid Ward identity or a stationary framing pushforward. Independent validation: the primary and coherent-source readers fully checked the actual generic adjoint, four routed bands, coherent dual row, endpoint arrows, rectangular maps, and finite interval identity; both freshly replayed the full focused audit, including the added complete Fourier corollary. The geometry reader independently checked the principal residual field, complete-source normalization, cotangent change-of-chain rule and all three resonant coefficients. These reviews retain the explicit distinction between finite contracted currents, off-grid Ward assembly and an original geometric-period coefficient. The added off-node section 5 received independent full primary and coherent-source reviews. The latter freshly replayed the extended audit, including the true generic defects and limiting Fourier zero. Those reviews cover the literal finite rank-one source, unwrapped charge proof and root boundary profile; they do not determine z, differentiate its root factor, or identify a selected transverse period. The subsequent whole-source absorption (13a),(13b),(14a) also received independent primary and coherent-source reviews of its exact kernel, gauge orientation, position tilt and retained generic defect. Its conclusion is reduction to the existing one-cut coherent family, not an independent localization of the residual framing direction. The genuine-normal section 6 also received an independent full coherent-source review of (15)--(21), including a fresh symbolic check of the original N=2 family and its arbitrary-power identity. The primary reader independently checked the original crossing, pivot, restored Cartan factor and general free pivotal channel. These reviews distinguish tensor-span freedom from the two actual connected source words, and full-root-map lift independence from determination by the scalar z. No geometric-period obstruction is inferred from the counterexample.

title: A braided second-cut co-source with its actual pivotal weights
status: Exact braided change of cut with genuine pivotal derivatives
text: # A braided second-cut co-source with its actual pivotal weights 30 October 2026. Reviewed finite-source theorem. The literal second identity cut cannot be replaced by another normalized boundary state, or even by an untransported pivotal marginal. There is an exact repair: retain the actual braid carrying the selected wire to the exposed position. Its conjugated matrix-unit insertion gives a second co-source for the SAME whole marked scalar. The original pivot, all exchange bands, and all genuine quantum derivatives remain explicit. This is a global finite-source identity. It does not prove that this co-source has a nonzero coefficient on the selected geometric framing fiber, or replace the two-cut tensor by simultaneous point evaluation. ## 1. The genuine generic source and its original first cut Fix N, d=N-1, q0=exp(pi i/N), and zeta=q0 exp(epsilon). Use the original ordinary highest-weight-d module and the ACTUAL generic physical cup. Its pivotal matrix is g(epsilon)=(-1)^d K(epsilon), g_a(epsilon)=(-1)^d zeta^(d-2a), D_N(epsilon)=Tr g=(-1)^d[N]_zeta. (1) At the root this is the original K^(1-N), on every physical index. Away from the root the latter frozen power is a different germ. In particular the derivative in (1) is (d-2a)g_a, not (1-N)(d-2a)g_a. All assertions below use (1). Take an actual parallel physical level with b ordered heads and write the cut word as A B, with matrices composing right to left. Cups and caps elsewhere are their original maps. On the complete source use the regular Hopf lifts of its root complete-circle sectors, or the proved exactly equivalent literal polynomial presentation WITH all its moving scalar adapters. A bare root-value substitution is not a generic lift. Let G=g tensor ... tensor g, P(C)=Tr_(heads 2,...,b)[(I tensor g tensor ... tensor g)C]. The exposed endomorphism is H=P(A B)=z(epsilon)I. This follows from the actual generic Hopf covariance and the distinct K weights and nonzero interior F arrows. Its root marked value is z(0), while the ordinary closed source is F=Tr(G A B)=D_N z, z(0)=F'(0)/nu_N, nu_N=2N(-1)^N/(q0-q0^-1). (2) This is the same original exposed mark and trace normal as in the [full source theorem](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md). The retained exterior normalization and peripheral factors multiply both sides; they are not changed here. The formulas also apply at an actual Morse level after transporting its oriented objects with their literal duality maps. A braid route between different ordered boundary objects then includes those maps. The following displayed parallel-head formulas specify the simplest case; one must not replace a typed route by an unclocked permutation. ## 2. What the literal second identity cut does not satisfy Insert E_bb on a chosen intermediate wire and keep the original first cut open. With the second index renamed j to avoid confusion with the number of heads, set J_(a,j)=[P(A E_jj^(slot) B)]_(a,a). (3) Summing the actual identity edge gives sum_j J_(a,j)=z, (1/N)sum_(a,j)J_(a,j)=z. (4) It follows that the first head can be fixed at ANY actual physical a0, giving z=sum_j J_(a0,j), with no new scalar. But the column sums need not be constant, and multiplying the first index by g_a does not fix that defect. The old exposed marked row is not a Hopf cap on an arbitrary partially summed tensor. For a concrete exact example, use the original three-positive-crossing two-strand word at N=3, cut after its first crossing and select its second wire. In the audit's cyclotomic field F_1009, with every original pivotal factor retained and the common exterior scalar omitted on both sides, its row sums are (227,227,227), while its column sums are (758,555,377). With g=(374,1,634), its pivotal column sums are (903,221,894). Thus neither proposed second marginal is a source identity. These examples only distinguish the formulas; the correct identity is proved next at every generic parameter and every level. ## 3. The actual braided projector and its two exact marginals Number the selected wire by j=0,...,b-1. Let R_i be the actual generic crossing between slots i-1 and i. Choose the recorded route U=R_1 R_2 ... R_j, U^-1=R_j^-1 ... R_2^-1 R_1^-1. (5) Thus R_j acts first and the selected wire moves left one position at a time. A different specified signed braid route is allowed with its literal inverse; the route is data. Every crossing and its full scalar is retained. Put X_l=U^-1(E_ll tensor I)U, J^U_(a,l)=[P(A X_l B)]_(a,a). (6) The X_l are actual mutually orthogonal idempotents with sum I. They are GENERALLY NOT local matrix units on the selected wire. Their full exchange and prefix bands are indispensable. The universal identities are J^U 1=z 1, g^T J^U=z g^T. (7) For the first, sum X_l=I and use H=zI. For the second define C_new=U B A U^-1. It is an actual Hopf intertwiner, so P(C_new)=z_new I. Every factor commutes with the total pivot G. Cyclicity of the FULL ordinary trace therefore gives D_N z_new=Tr(G U B A U^-1)=Tr(G B A)=D_N z. Cancel the nonzero generic function D_N before root specialization. Both open endomorphisms are regular, so z_new=z through epsilon=0. For each l, the same trace calculation now gives sum_a g_a J^U_(a,l) =Tr(G A X_l B) =Tr[G U B A U^-1(E_ll tensor I)] =g_l z. (8) This proves (7) with the actual order of U and its inverse. It uses the whole closed trace, not movement of a bare root mark. Since g_l is always a unit, it supplies the exact second co-source z=g_l^-1 sum_a g_a J^U_(a,l) (9) at any physical l. The original first-cut source remains z=(1/N)sum_(a,l)J^U_(a,l). The formula is valid for arbitrary fixed complete-channel assignments and their finite sum, with their original signs and scalar weights. Differentiating it retains the actual U, U^-1, g and coupon derivatives; no unproved generic normal is suppressed. The two cuts need not have the same Morse width. More generally let V=V_d^tensor b and W=V_d^tensor c, with b,c>=1, and use the actual rectangular covariant maps A:W->V and B:V->W. The selected route U and X_l act on W; use P_V in (6). Covariance gives G_V A=A G_W and G_W B=B G_V. The entire trace step is then Tr_V(G_V A X_l B)=Tr_W(G_W B A X_l). The ordinary partial closures P_V(A B) and P_W(U B A U^-1) are scalar on the same exposed simple object. Cancelling the SAME generic D_N proves (7)-(9) unchanged. This includes actual intervening births and deaths, with their original cups, caps and typed duality transport; it introduces no new pivot on the second identity edge. At the root g^T1=D_N(0)=0. Thus (9) is an essentially canceling pivotal co-source, not another positive normalized row. Equations (7) do not determine the individual entries of J^U: perturbations Z satisfying Z1=0 and g^T Z=0 remain. This kernel has dimension (N-1)^2: it is precisely Hom(C^N/span(1),ker(g^T)). It cannot be removed by two independent point evaluations. ## 4. Root characters and the change of cut-density line There are two distinct continuations to complex magnetic indices. The finite generic matrix pivot in (1) is defined on physical integer a. The specified actual CUP continuation instead gives, by its literal ratio p_d(a,d-a)/p_d(d-a,a), ghat(epsilon;a)=(-1)^d exp(2pi i a) zeta^(d-2a). (10) It agrees with (1) at every physical integer a and every epsilon. At the root, for complex a, it is exactly the marked literal power q0^[(1-N)(d-2a)]. Consequently ghat(0;a)/ghat(0;l) =exp[2pi i(a-l)] A_l/A_a, A_a=exp(2pi i a/N), A_l=exp(2pi i l/N). (11) A_l is the clock of the new FIRST head after the recorded braid U; it is not automatically the clock of the old bare selected wire. The integer-linear character is one on the physical grid, but not on a continued complex magnetic chart. Nor may the root power in (11) be differentiated as if it were the generic cup germ (10). This distinction is independent of the matrix identity (8). The actual geometric cut forms have the corresponding algebraic line transition: writing the conjugation-invariant form on the ordered-flag surface as Omega=-Tr(Pi dPi wedge dPi), their fixed-cut forms are Omega_cut,i=-A_i Omega. Their ratio is A_l/A_a. Thus the algebraic factor in (11) is exactly the expected change of cut-density line, WITH its source character still present. This does not identify the whole continued tensor, its integration cycle, or its boundary residues merely from equality of that ratio. ## 5. Remaining fiber and source problem The braided correction (6) is a concrete finite source operation; it neither normalizes away the kernel in (7) nor supplies an asymptotic bound for that kernel. Its added routes are actual matrices and may carry substantial magnetic growth before contraction. A geometric framing reduction must still transport this entire co-source, including the exchange bands, into the residual centralizer fiber and its original relative ends. The nonzero unit g_l^-1 in (9) is an exact normalization of the whole scalar, not a proof that a particular local geometric block survives this functional. Existing two-cut current identities retain the relevant band and endpoint data; no replacement by a trace-one state on the second identity edge is made. The focused [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_braided_two_cut_source_adapter.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_braided_two_cut_source_adapter_results.json) check 16 original braid/complete-circle sources at parallel widths two and three, 476 actual adapted entry value/first-jet coefficients, and 116 weighted column value/first-jet coefficients. They also retain the failed literal second marginals, check the original generic crossing intertwiners and their inverses, and verify the whole-source trace normal. These finite checks supplement the generic proof; they do not test a geometric fiber integral. Independent validation: root fully reviewed the generic proof, pivot germ, ordered route and rectangular trace extension, and freshly replayed the focused audit (16 sources, 476 entry coefficients, 116 weighted column coefficients). The coherent-source reviewer independently read the parallel-width proof and source/character scope and freshly reproduced the same audit. The geometry reviewer independently checked the ordered trace argument, residual kernel, actual cup character, and the cut-line transition in Sections 3-5. These reviews do not assert survival of the selected geometric fiber under the retained co-source.

title: Exact charged bridge phase and a further original-source selection rule
text: # Exact charged bridge phase and a further original-source selection rule 28 October 2026. After exact signed overbridge elimination, all quadratic interior-clock phases telescope. The COMPLETE bridge is one charge-d cyclic beta product with explicit linear weights. This gives its full marked complex action. Positive absolute entropy does not automatically make that action stationary. An actual post-elimination 5_2 source fiber has nonzero phase flux at its unique conditional absolute maximum. More constructively, its remaining finite Fourier sum vanishes EXACTLY on that entire high-entropy clock region. The vanishing is a new complementary charge constraint, not a discarded small term or a counterexample to the volume conjecture. ## 1. Exact normalization and complete phase telescoping Use the original signed bridge theorem and its full normalizers in [the source-preserving unwinding note](actual_signed_overbridge_unwinding.md). Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=-q^(-1). A bridge has m encounters, signs sigma_j, monotone clocks h_1>=...>=h_m, and original port parameters a_j,b_j with a_j b_j=Q^2 x. Let u_j be the spectator output, z6 for a positive encounter and z7 for a negative one. The signed table gives EXACTLY c_j=kappa^(sigma_j)/N *a_j^(-h_j) q^(-h_j^2+(1+sigma_j)h_j). (1) For a positive encounter u_j=Q^(-h_j)/(x a_j); for a negative one u_j=Qx/a_j. Substituting either in the proved original c_j gives (1), including every sign and half-step. Combining all c_j, link monomials and Gaussian phases, the complete non-Pochhammer/non-binomial prefactor is kappa^w/N *Zin^(-h_1) *product_(j<m) a_j^(-(h_j-h_(j+1))) *a_m^(-h_m) *(-1)^(sum_(j=2)^m h_j) *q^(-h_1^2+h_1+sum_j sigma_j h_j), w=sum_j sigma_j. (2) All interior quadratic clocks have cancelled, not been dropped by taking absolute values. Define NONNEGATIVE integer charges n_0=d-h_1, n_j=h_j-h_(j+1) (1<=j<m), n_m=h_m, sum_(r=0)^m n_r=d, w_r=sum_(j=1)^r sigma_j. Put t_0=1, t_r=(-1)^r q^(2+w_r)/(Zin a_r), 1<=r<=m, z_0=b_1/Zin, z_r=a_r b_(r+1)Q^(-1)=x^(-1)a_r/a_(r+1), 1<=r<m, z_m=a_m Zout. Then the ENTIRE original conditioned bridge coefficient is B_gamma=kappa^w product_(r=0)^m [(z_r;Q)_(n_r)/F_(n_r) *t_r^(n_r)], F_n=(Q;Q)_n. (3) This identity includes every original N factor. To prove it, the telescoping q-binomial product is F_(h_1)/[F_(h_m)product F_(h_j-h_(j+1))]. Reflect F_(h_1)F_(d-h_1)=N(-1)^(h_1)q^(h_1(h_1+1)). Its N cancels the 1/N in (2), its quadratic cancels -h_1^2, and its sign combines into (-1)^(sum_j h_j). Finally sum_j h_j=sum_(r>=1)r n_r and sum_j sigma_j h_j=sum_(r>=1)w_r n_r. This proves (3). The exact parameters obey z_(r-1)t_(r-1)=Q^(epsilon_r)t_r, epsilon_r=(1-sigma_r)/2, z_m t_m=Tend=(-1)^m q^(2+w) Zout/Zin. (4) These are source identities, not an imposed balancing condition. ## 2. The full leading COMPLEX bridge action Write T_r=n_r/N, U_r=exp(2pi*i*T_r). The exact charge is sum T_r=1-1/N; its leading equation is sum T_r=1. On a fixed nondegenerate logarithmic cell the marked complex action is W_gamma=sum_r [Li_2(z_r)-Li_2(z_r U_r) -Li_2(1)+Li_2(U_r) +Log U_r Log t_r]. (5) The full coefficient has exp[N W_gamma/(2pi*i)] times its specified subexponential density, with kappa^w still EXACTLY outside. If one expands the original complete kappa as well, its leading action is the known real constant -pi^2 w. It changes no stationarity equation. The q^(2+w_r) factors in (3) remain in the exact source and its finite-level phase; they affect (5) at subleading order for fixed word length. Branches in (5) mean the continuation of each actual finite Pochhammer arc. Equivalently define its leading logarithm by integrating Log(1-z exp(2pi*i*t)) along that arc; do not give the endpoint dilogarithms unrelated principal branches. The factorial starting at 1 has its usual integrable endpoint. The full differential, before imposing actual spectator-flow dependencies, is dW=sum_r { Log[t_r(1-z_r U_r)/(1-U_r)] dLog U_r +Log[(1-z_r U_r)/(1-z_r)] dLog z_r +Log U_r dLog t_r }. (6) Thus the Gaussian/monomial source has not disappeared from the action. It is now the explicit Log U Log t coupling. If the bridge parameters a_r are independent while its charges vary, constrained charge criticality requires t_r(1-z_r U_r)/(1-U_r)=Lambda, U_r=(Lambda-t_r)/(Lambda-z_r t_r). At leading order (4) gives z_r t_r=t_(r+1). Hence product U_r=(Lambda-1)/(Lambda-Tend). The charge equation product U_r=1 therefore requires Tend=1 for a finite regular interior critical point. Generic endpoint data do not satisfy it. This is a conditional phase-flux test, not a global knot critical equation: the actual anchored flow makes some a_r depend on other charges and supplies the extra terms in (6). There is an exact finite counterpart. If the a_r really are held independent during summation over all charges, write U_z(v)=sum_(n=0)^d (z;Q)_n v^n/F_n. Then sum_(sum n=d) B_gamma =kappa^w [v^d] U_Tend(v) product_(sigma_r=-1)(1-t_r v)^(-1). (7) Proof: modulo v^N the finite quantum binomial theorem is U_z(v)=P(zv)/P(v), with the original finite Euler P. Using P(Qv)=P(v)/(1-v), equations (4) telescope the product. This independent-parameter sum must not be applied to a whole knot while ignoring the actual spectator-flow dependencies. ## 3. Real angular entropy and phase, with every sheet retained On the original fixed-central grids, |z_r| and |t_r| differ from one by O(1/N). Write their leading arguments as z_r=exp(2pi*i*alpha_r), t_r=exp(2pi*i*tau_r). Let J(s)=-D(exp(2pi*i*s))/(2pi), periodic, and let chi(s)=({s}^2-{s})/2. The leading logarithmic modulus per N and phase per N are E_gamma=sum_r [J(alpha_r+T_r)-J(alpha_r)-J(T_r)], Theta_gamma/pi=sum_r [chi(alpha_r+T_r)-chi(alpha_r)-chi(T_r)+2T_r tau_r]. (8) The phase includes the c_j monomials and original Gaussian phases through tau_r. The omitted kappa phase is label-independent and specified above. Equation (8) is a piecewise quadratic real phase on every actual support cell, not a positive weight. At the usual nonzero radial grid regularization the errors are O(log N) in log magnitude; on endpoint-free cells the neighbor phase derivatives converge with O(1/N) error. On a positive arc 0<alpha_r<alpha_r+T_r<1, (8) reduces to Theta_gamma=pi sum_r T_r(alpha_r+2tau_r). Choosing the actual lifted relation alpha_r=tau_(r+1)-tau_r there gives Theta_gamma=pi sum_r T_r(tau_r+tau_(r+1)). Its internal phase derivative is pi(T_(r-1)+T_r), strictly positive when the adjacent charges are positive. A real absolute optimizer is therefore not automatically a complex stationary point. The corresponding absolute entropy is the sum of twice the ideal tetrahedron volumes with angles pi*T_r, pi*alpha_r, pi*(1-alpha_r-T_r). These form a genuine positive concave angle chart, but the retained phase remains. ## 4. A new complementary-charge rule for an actual remaining wire Consider an actual under-output followed by a reduced overbridge-input on the SAME ordinary wire. Suppose its full dependence is g(Z)=Z^(r-H)(aZ;Q)_(d-r)(b/Z;Q)_(d-H), ab=Q, 0<=r,H<=d. (9) Then the exact remaining constant term is CT g=(-1)^(d-r) a^(H-r) *Q^[(d-r)(d-r-1)/2-H(d-H)] *[r choose d-H]_Q. (10) In particular it is ZERO unless r+H>=d. No geometric norm is divided out in (10). This is a new source-support selection in addition to overbridge monotonicity. Here is an elementary proof, without assuming a q-Chu theorem. Put t=aZ, L=d-r, K=d-H. Reflect the second product: (Q/t;Q)_K=(-1)^K Q^(K(K+1)/2)t^(-K) (tQ^(H+1);Q)_K. Thus CT g is a^(H-r)(-1)^K Q^(K(K+1)/2) times [t^L](t;Q)_L(tQ^(H+1);Q)_K. If r+H<d, the product is (1-t^N) times a polynomial of degree<L, so this coefficient vanishes. If r+H>=d it is (1-t^N)/(tQ^L;Q)_(H-L+1). Finite q-Pascal gives its t^L coefficient Q^(L^2)[H choose L]_Q. Root factorial reflection turns the result into (10); the parity factor is exactly Q^(N(N-1)/2)=(-1)^(N-1), also at even N. For r+H<=d-1 the stronger root-circle identity is g(Z)=(-1)^(d-H)a^(-(d-H))Q^((d-H)(d-H+1)/2) *Z^(r-d)(1-(aZ)^N) *(Q^(H+1)aZ;Q)_(d-1-r-H). (11) On the original grid the norm 1-(aZ)^N is a fixed nonzero scalar. Its remaining Fourier powers lie from r-d through -H-1, entirely negative and strictly above -N. Thus the original N-point SUM, not merely a formal constant term, is exactly zero in this region. ## 5. Whole ORIGINAL post-reduction sanity check: 5_2 Use the independently identified original word [1,1,1,2,-1,2] and its actual averaged cut and two pivots in the [post-bridge source audit](../experiments/audit_bridge_reduced_absolute_envelope.py). Its overpaths are [0],[1],[2,3],[4],[5]; wire 8 has already been eliminated in the genuine two-crossing bridge. Keep the audit's rational labels, but change label6/N from 9/10 to 89/100. Then the underclock of crossing1 is r/N=1/100, while the first reduced overbridge clock is H/N=59/100 and the second is 35/100. The nontrivial bridge inequality is strict. The remaining wire5 occurs only in the under-output of crossing1 and the input of that reduced bridge. Their actual parameters satisfy ab=Q: a=Q^(r+1)/z3 and b=z6/x, while z6=x z3 Q^(-r). Every other crossing, reduced bridge factor and ORIGINAL boundary coupon is independent of wire5. Thus (9)--(11) apply to the ENTIRE remaining source, with its full scalar. The label5/N=1/10 lies at the unique conditional global absolute maximum in this fiber. Indeed its one remaining Pochhammer has asymptotic length 1-r/N-H/N=2/5; the two endpoints are conjugate there. Yet its phase flux under label5 -> label5+1 tends to pi(1+r/N-H/N)=21pi/50 !=0 modulo 2pi. (12) The complete reduced entropy at this supported source point is 2.546436873747266..., much larger than the geometric knot-volume rate. This does not refute the volume conjecture: (11) shows its conditional source sum is EXACTLY ZERO. The large real envelope is removed by a further source constraint, not by a norm estimate. For a direct phase calculation on this cell, the whole source's leading phase obeys (1/pi) partial_(label5/N) Theta =xi3-2xi6+xi7+1=21/50. The original cap/pivot factor is nonzero and independent of wire5; common kappa/framing phases are retained and cancel from this neighbor ratio. The audit compares the whole actual finite-source ratio with (9), not a newly chosen co-source or a pre-elimination summand. The lesson is constructive. Exact bridge reduction gives a positive entropy chart, but no automatic real saddle. One must also perform or control the remaining anchor contractions. Equation (10) proves one actual new complementary-charge selection; its condition ab=Q is typed and must be checked before applying it elsewhere. No claim that all remaining seams have this form is made. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_bridge_charge_phase.py) checks the exact charged identity, its optional independent-parameter height sum, the complementary seam for every clock, and the whole original post-bridge phase/source fiber.

title: Actual cap residues at the Pachner norm wall
text:
# Actual cap residues at the Pachner norm wall 28 October 2026. The actual source and co-source give an explicit residue functional at the simultaneous norm wall of [the last-move calculation](oversized_alias_last_pachner_wall.md). For a full holomorphic product it retains its original matrix corner. For split meromorphic terms it retains a finite list of source jets, with bounds uniform in the level. The cap is not a projector onto geometric edge winding one. The results below use exactly the source frames and residue constants of [the cap-wall theorem](cap_wall_fermat_quad_residue_transport.md). They do not replace an invariant or assign an arbitrary source to the geometric triangulation. The original geometric exterior still needs its typed comparison with these local matrix coordinates.
