The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_cap_pachner_wall_charge.py) checks 148 direct finite-product identities in cyclotomic fields, the generic first and second central jets, and the uniform-bound constants. Its [saved results](../experiments/actual_cap_pachner_wall_charge_results.json) separate central-meromorphic, fixed-cover-pole, and global-source scope. For the original word, its Ward corner is used only after the full intertwining contraction has been assembled. These residue formulas do not authorize applying that Ward replacement separately to a cyclic/sewing sector whose full original marked row is different. ## 1. Coincident residues reproduce the original corners Fix $N\ge2$, $d=N-1$, $Q=e^{2\pi i/N}$ and put $$ \varepsilon=a^N,\quad \delta=(1-\varepsilon)^{1/N},\quad u_0=\delta,\quad u_d=Q\delta, $$ with the branches equal to $1$ at $\varepsilon=0$. For $s,t\in\{0,d\}$ use the ORIGINAL Fermat frames $$ P_n^{s}(a)=  rac{a^n}{\prod_{j=1}^{n}(1-u_sQ^j)},\qquad L_m^{t}(a)= a^{-m}\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}(1-u_tQ^j). 	ag{1} $$ Their original residue constants are $$ \alpha_0= eta_0=1,\qquad \alpha_d=1-Q,\qquad eta_d=N. $$ Write $\sigma_0=	au_0=0$, $\sigma_d=1$, $	au_d=d$, and $D_{ts}=\sigma_s+	au_t$. For any matrix $O(a)$ holomorphic at zero, $$  oxed{\quad  rac1{\alpha_s eta_t} \operatorname{Res}_{a=0} a^{D_{ts}-1} L^t(a)O(a)P^s(a)\,da =\langle e_t,O(0)e_sangle. \quad} 	ag{2} $$ Indeed $P^d_d=(1-Q)a^{-1}+O(a^{N-1})$, while $P^d_n=O(a^n)$ for $n<d$. Also $L^d_d=Na^{-d}+O(a)$ and $L^d_m=O(a^{-m})$ for $m<d$. At the zero corner $P^0_0=L^0_0=1$, whereas $P^0_n=O(a^n)$ and $L^0_m=O(a^{N-m})$ for $m,n>0$. Thus exactly $(m,n)=(t,s)$ has the maximal required pole; every other term has at least one additional power of $a$. Multiplication by a holomorphic $O(a)$ cannot create another residue. For $s=t=d$, (2) is specifically $$  rac1{N(1-Q)} \operatorname{Res}a^{N-1}L^d(a)O(a)P^d(a)\,da =O_{dd}(0). 	ag{3} $$ This equals the actual independent input/output cap residues. It is an equality of residue functionals on the stated class, not a pullback of two differential forms to their diagonal. For individually singular factors the order of regularization must therefore still be proved; it cannot be inferred by substituting the same parameter into two residue formulas. Taking $O=I$ in (3) gives exactly one. The marked wall has its original unit augmentation. ## 2. Exact source jets for meromorphic split terms Suppose now $O=O(\varepsilon)$ is meromorphic, with pole order at most a fixed integer $p$: $$ O(\varepsilon)=\sum_{r=-p}^{\infty}O_r\varepsilon^r. $$ Let $m(n)=n+t-s mod N$, valued in $0,\ldots,d$. The residue functional in (2) is exactly $$ \mathcal R_{ts}(O) =\operatorname{CT}_{\varepsilon=0} \sum_{n=0}^{d}H^{ts}_n(\varepsilon) O_{m(n),n}(\varepsilon). 	ag{4} $$ All factors in this formula are retained. Direct telescoping in (1) gives the following kernels: | Input $s$ | Output $t$ | Kernel | |---|---|---| | $0$ | $0$ | $H_0=1$; for $n>0$, $H_n=(1-\delta)/(1-Q^n\delta)$ | | $d$ | $d$ | $H_n=\varepsilon(1-Q\delta)/[N(1-Q)(1-Q^{n+1}\delta)]$ | | $d$ | $0$ | $H_d=(1-Q\delta)/(1-Q)$; for $n<d$, $H_n=(1-\delta)(1-Q\delta)/[(1-Q)(1-Q^{n+1}\delta)]$ | | $0$ | $d$ | $H_0=\varepsilon/[N(1-\delta)]$; for $n>0$, $H_n=\varepsilon/[N(1-Q^n\delta)]$ | The quotients at $\varepsilon=0$ are their removable values. Every kernel is holomorphic there and $H^{ts}_n(0)=1$ exactly when $n=s$, and is zero otherwise. If $H^{ts}_n=\sum_{r\ge0}H^{ts}_{r,n}\varepsilon^r$, then $$  oxed{\quad \mathcal R_{ts}(O)= \sum_{r=0}^{p}\sum_{n=0}^{d} H^{ts}_{r,n}(O_{-r})_{m(n),n}. \quad} 	ag{5} $$ Thus a full regularized product uses only its original corner. Its singular summands can also use $H_1,H_2,\ldots,H_p$. Those terms disappear only when their corresponding pole coefficients cancel in the complete product or source current. For the marked $d	o d$ corner, write $K=H^{dd}$. At $n
e d$, $$ K_{1,n}= rac1{N(1-Q^{n+1})},\qquad K_{2,n}= rac{Q-Q^{n+1}} {N^2(1-Q)(1-Q^{n+1})^2}. 	ag{6} $$ At $n=d$, $$ K_{0,d}=1,\quad K_{1,d}= rac{Q}{N(1-Q)}- rac{N-1}{2N},\quad K_{2,d}=- rac{N^2-1}{12N^2}. 	ag{7} $$ The second-order coefficient includes the cubic expansion of $\delta$ before the removable denominator is divided. ## 3. Uniform bounds: no exponential source-jet cost Take $ho=1/16$. On $|\varepsilon|\leho$, $$ |\delta-1|\le rac{2|\varepsilon|}{N}. $$ For a nontrivial root $Q^r$, put $\ell=\operatorname{dist}(r,N\mathbb Z)\ge1$. The elementary sine bound gives $|1-Q^r|\ge4\ell/N$, and hence $$ |1-Q^r\delta|\ge rac{3\ell}{N},\qquad \left| rac{1-Q\delta}{1-Q}ight|<2. 	ag{8} $$ All nonexceptional entries of the table are therefore bounded by $(4/3)|\varepsilon|/\ell$. The two removable quotients use $$ A(\varepsilon)= rac{\varepsilon}{N(1-\delta)} = rac{1+\delta+\cdots+\delta^{N-1}}N, \qquad |A|\le1+ho. $$ In particular $$ K_d=A+ rac{\varepsilon Q}{N(1-Q)},\qquad |K_d|\le1+ho+ho/4<2. $$ The remaining wrap value $(1-Q\delta)/(1-Q)$ is also bounded by two. Consequently, for **all four actual cap channels**, all $N\ge2$, and all indices, $$ \sup_{|\varepsilon|\le1/16}|H^{ts}_n(\varepsilon)|\le2, \qquad |H^{ts}_{r,n}|\le2\cdot16^r. 	ag{9} $$ For example, in the original flat Euclidean matrix basis, $$  oxed{\quad |\mathcal R_{ts}(O)| \le2N\sum_{r=0}^{p}16^r\|O_{-r}\|_{\mathrm{op}}. \quad} 	ag{10} $$ The factor $N$ can be replaced by a trace-norm bound on each selected cyclic diagonal. Independent source variables tensor: for a fixed word and fixed pole orders their combined extraction has polynomial cost in $N$. This is a bound relative to the actual Laurent coefficient norms. It does not turn exponentially large input currents into small ones without their exact cancellation. Nor is the norm asserted unchanged under an exponentially conditioned fusion frame. The [actual sewing theorem](cyclic_sewing_regularized_cut_cycle.md) retains at most second-order poles per Euler variable. When such an actual matrix term is expressed in the stated central local coordinate, (5)--(10) give its exact cap correction and a bound for the finite source-jet pushforward. They do not authorize dropping the sewing poles or their finite-part prescription. ### Fixed pole order on the Fermat cover, without central descent There is a complementary statement for an actual matrix that is meromorphic in $a$ itself. Put $$ \widehat P_s=a^{\sigma_s}P^s/\alpha_s,\qquad \widehat L_t=a^{	au_t}L^t/ eta_t,\qquad J_{ts}(a)=\widehat P_s(a)\widehat L_t(a). $$ These are the regular ORIGINAL cap frames. The uniform cap-wall estimate gives an absolute $C$ such that their Euclidean norms are at most $C$ on $|a|\le1/(16N)$. Consequently the rank-one kernel has trace norm at most $C^2$ there. If $O(a)=\sum_{\ell=-p}^{\infty}A_\ell a^\ell$, then exactly $$ \mathcal R_{ts}(O)= \sum_{r=0}^{p}\operatorname{tr}(A_{-r}J_{ts,r}), \qquad \|J_{ts,r}\|_1\le C^2(16N)^r. 	ag{10a} $$ This follows from the original formula $\operatorname{Res}\widehat L_tO\widehat P_s\,da/a$ and Cauchy's coefficient estimate in trace norm. Thus $$ |\mathcal R_{ts}(O)| \le C^2\sum_{r=0}^{p}(16N)^r\|A_{-r}\|_{\mathrm{op}}. 	ag{10b} $$ For $0<r<N$ the actual endpoint jets are especially explicit. Writing $F_r=(Q;Q)_r$ and $F_r^-=(Q^{-1};Q^{-1})_r$: $$  egin{array}{c|c|c} &r=0&0<r<N\ \hline [a^r]\widehat P_0&e_0&e_r/F_r\ [a^r]\widehat P_d&e_d&e_{r-1}/F_r\ [a^r]\widehat L_0&e_0^t&e_{N-r}^t/F_r^-\ [a^r]\widehat L_d&e_d^t&e_{d-r}^t/F_r^- \end{array} 	ag{10c} $$ The first central correction to $\delta$ has degree $N$, which proves this table directly from (1). These are genuine source and co-source derivatives, with all original normalizations. A fixed pole order on the cover and a fixed pole order in the central variable are different hypotheses: a central pole of order $p$ has cover order $Np$. Estimate (10) is strong precisely because it uses central descent and exact cyclic-diagonal telescoping. Estimate (10b) applies without descent only when the cover pole order is bounded. Neither is a uniform assertion for arbitrary separated Puiseux factors with growing pole order. ## 4. Monodromy selects the physical cap charge Under $a\mapsto Qa$, $\delta$ is fixed and $$ P^s(Qa)=ZP^s(a),\qquad L^t(Qa)=L^t(a)Z^{-1},\qquad Ze_n=Q^ne_n. $$ The total residue weight is $Q^{D_{ts}}$. Deck averaging keeps precisely matrix entries with $$ m-n\equiv t-s\pmod N. $$ The zero jet of (4) further selects the actual corner $(t,s)$. For $d	o0$ and $0	o d$ this is the WRAPPED entry of the corresponding cyclic diagonal, with coefficient one. Thus actual cap residues require, rather than delete, a retained cyclic boundary charge. In particular the compatible root monodromy $(Q,Q^{-1},Q)$ of the last Pachner wall cannot by itself be read as a projector onto geometric edge winding one. It gives a finite root/deck charge. The geometric integer lift has not been identified with the original integer-degree/carry data. ## 5. The literal primitive cap retains the generic local wall There is also a direct local nonvanishing statement. Express the primitive normalized pentagon in a common clock/shift basis $$ X=\mu Z,\quad Y=\eta S,\quad ZS=QSZ, \quad \mu(0)=Q,\quad \eta^N=x_0, $$ and take the actual $d$ input and output cap corners in that basis. At a generic exceptional direction, $x_0
otin\{0,1\}$ and $y_0=1-x_0$. The regular two-atom side is $$ O_0=D(Y;b)\,D(bX;h),\quad b^N=y_0,\quad h^N=x_0. $$ The second factor is diagonal with every entry nonzero. Write the first as $\sum_{n=0}^{d}c_nS^n$. Its exact cyclic difference equation gives $$ (Q^n-b)c_n=\eta Q^{n-1}c_{n-1}, 	ag{11} $$ with indices cyclic. Since $\eta
e0$ and $b^N=1-x_0
e1$, every coefficient is nonzero: one zero would propagate around the entire cycle and make the invertible matrix zero. Therefore $$  oxed{\quad (O_0)_{dd}=c_0\,D(bX;h)_{dd}
e0.\quad} 	ag{12} $$ Formula (3) says that the actual paired cap retains this local wall. It is not killed by operator regularity, by a norm-root zero, or by deck averaging. This does **not** identify this primitive cap placement with the exterior of the specific oversized $5_2$ face. The actual crossing's atom order and commutator orientation must be matched; an equation between central sums alone does not establish that embedding. No global excessive-face coefficient is computed here. The result is the explicit original-cap local charge and the finite uniformly bounded extraction map that an eventual typed exterior comparison must preserve.

title: Four-channel actual cap pushforward with signed deck characters
text: # Four-channel actual cap pushforward with signed deck characters 28 October 2026. This extends the exact central-meromorphic [actual cap extraction](actual_cap_pachner_wall_charge.md) to bounded SIGNED Puiseux characters. The source, co-source, residue weights and 0/d corner indices are the original ones. Fixed negative characters cost a power of N. Arbitrary bulk characters are not covered by this polynomial bound. ## 1. A single exact formula for every actual endpoint channel Put d=N-1, epsilon=a^N, delta=(1-epsilon)^(1/N), delta(0)=1. Use the original Fermat sources P^s and L^t, s,t in {0,d}, and alpha_0=beta_0=1, alpha_d=1-Q, beta_d=N. Set sigma=1_(s=d), D=sigma+t, R=(1-Q delta)/(1-Q), E_j=product_(h=0)^(j-1)(1-delta Q^h), E_(j+N)=epsilon E_j. The last identity extends E_j to ALL signed integers j as a meromorphic germ. It retains, rather than resets, the full central norm. Let O(a)=a^ell O_ell(epsilon), ell any integer. The exact cap functional [alpha_s beta_t]^-1 Res_(a=0) a^(D-1) L^t(a) O(a) P^s(a) da is the central constant coefficient of sum_(n=0)^d H_n^(ts,ell)(epsilon) [O_ell(epsilon)]_(m(n),n), m(n)=(n+t-s+ell) modulo N, where h=n+sigma and H_n^(ts,ell)=B_t R^sigma E_(h+ell)/E_(h+1), B_0=1-delta, B_d=epsilon/N. (1) Here the representative m(n) is always in 0,...,d. The epsilon powers in (1) include the corresponding integer carry exactly. To prove (1), express every source product in the common E frame: denominator(P^0_n)=E_(n+1)/(1-delta), denominator(P^d_n)=E_(n+2)/[(1-delta)(1-Qdelta)], numerator(L^0_m)=E_m, numerator(L^d_m)=E_(m+1)/(1-delta). The prefactor in the residue contributes a^(D+ell+n-m). Since D+ell+n-m is a multiple of N, this is precisely its integer power of epsilon. Apply E_(j+N)=epsilon E_j. All long products cancel, leaving exactly (1). This proves the operator indices, normalization and deck charge simultaneously. At ell=0 it is the four-channel table in the earlier theorem. No assumption that an arbitrary singular matrix descends to epsilon has been made: its chosen character a^ell is part of the input. Summing the actual character decomposition preserves the original matrix operator. A character may not be deleted because its central norm later has a numerical specialization. ## 2. Bounded signed characters have polynomial source cost For ell>=1 the quotient in (1) is the SHORT numerator product E_(h+ell)/E_(h+1) =product_(j=h+1)^(h+ell-1)(1-delta Q^j). (2) For ell=-k, k>=1, it is the SHORT reciprocal product E_(h-k)/E_(h+1) =1/product_(j=h-k)^h(1-delta Q^j). (3) Take rho=1/16 and N>k. In (3) the interval contains at most one exceptional factor 1-delta. If it occurs, B_0 cancels it exactly, while B_d cancels it by epsilon/[N(1-delta)]=(1+delta+...+delta^(N-1))/N. Thus the kernel is holomorphic at epsilon=0. All other factors have absolute value at least 3/N on |epsilon|<=rho; also |R|<2. The actual uniform bounds are ell=0: sup_n |H_n| <=2, ell>=1: sup_n |H_n| <=4rho 3^(ell-1)/N, ell=-k<0: sup_n |H_n| <=2(1+rho)(N/3)^k, N>k. (4) For (2), use |1-delta Q^j|<=3 and |B_t|<=2rho/N. For (3), cancel the exceptional factor when present; otherwise use that same B_t estimate. This proves (4), not merely a coefficient estimate at one root value. For an actual central Laurent matrix with fixed pole order p, O_ell(epsilon)=sum_(r=-p)^infinity A_r epsilon^r, Cauchy's estimate and (4) give the exact finite pushforward cap(O)=sum_(r=0)^p sum_n [epsilon^r]H_n (A_(-r))_(m(n),n), |cap(O)| <=N C_ell(N) sum_(r=0)^p16^r||A_(-r)||_op, (5) where C_ell(N) is the corresponding bound in (4). Thus fixed signed characters and fixed central pole orders have polynomial cost. For ell=-k the asymptotic requirement N>k is explicit; smaller levels use the same exact formula (1), after retaining its additional integer epsilon carry. Fixed finitely many small levels do not alter the volume-rate assertion. This is not a bound for unrestricted ell=ell(N). The bulk-sector example derived in the all-sector analysis has exponential source cost despite fixed central pole order. Its actual support must be checked in a singular Pachner operator before applying (5). ## 3. Arbitrary meromorphic operators on the cap cover There is also a separate statement that needs no central descent. Define the ORIGINAL normalized source frames p_hat_s=a^sigma P^s/alpha_s, l_hat_t=a^t L^t/beta_t. They are holomorphic with respective values e_s,e_t^t at zero, and have uniformly bounded Euclidean norms on |a|<=1/(16N), by the explicit cap-frame estimate. If O(a)=sum_(j=-p)^infinity A_j a^j is any actual matrix Laurent germ with fixed COVER pole order p, the exact cap residue is CT_a l_hat_t(a) O(a) p_hat_s(a). The rank-one source kernel has trace norm bounded by an absolute constant C on that circle. Cauchy on its coefficients proves |cap(O)| <= C sum_(j=0)^p(16N)^j||A_(-j)||_op. (6) Thus every such actual cover-meromorphic operator has a polynomial finite-jet extraction, even if it is not invariant under a->Qa. Fixed central pole order and fixed cover pole order are different: an epsilon pole of order p has cover order Np. Formula (6) must not be substituted for (5) while hiding that growth. For 0<=r<N, the four normalized cover jets are explicitly | Endpoint | r=0 | 1<=r<N | |---|---|---| | input0 | e_0 | e_r/F_r | | inputd | e_d | e_(r-1)/F_r | | output0 | e_0^t | e_(N-r)^t/F_r^- | | outputd | e_d^t | e_(d-r)^t/F_r^- | Here F_r^-=(Q^-1;Q^-1)_r. These follow by canceling the unique vanishing factor and using full factorial reflection; they include the wrapped channels. They independently fix the indices in (1). ## 4. Actual-network scope The source functionals in (1), (5) and (6) are the actual normalized 0/d corners used simultaneously by the original pair-fused plat. The original Cartan, framing, turn and peripheral lines multiply the same expressions. Independent source variables tensor with the displayed constants. For a fixed word and bounded pole orders and signed-character support, the total extraction cost is a fixed power of N relative to the ORIGINAL Laurent-coefficient norms. These are the specified relative-head coordinate norms. No equality with the physical tensor metric across a nonunitary fusion is asserted, and an exponentially large coefficient matrix remains exponentially large in these bounds. An equality of complete actual typed meromorphic operators on the same marked cover remains an equality after this finite extraction. This supplies the regularized residue rule for a typed Pachner identity when its actual exterior maps and common cover have been specified. It does not supply that exterior comparison merely from a classical five-term identity, nor equate the character label with a geometric edge winding. Singular factors must first be composed with their actual maps, or all their finite source jets and integer carries must be retained term by term in a common Laurent expansion. The coincident residue is not a silent pullback of independent differential forms across a singular diagonal. [Exact original-source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_cap_signed_deck_pushforward.py). ## 5. Sharp scope: a bulk character has exponential cap extraction The bounded-character hypothesis above cannot be removed from the original SINGLE-HEAD d-to-d cap functional. For N>=7 set L=ceil(N/6), U=floor(5N/6), n=L-2, r=U-n, m=U, O(a)=a^r epsilon^-1 |m><n|. All indices lie in the original head range and 1<=r<N. The exact d-to-d positive-character kernel from (1)--(2) gives cap(O)=[epsilon]H_n^(dd,r) =(1/N) product_(j=L)^U(1-Q^j). (7) This can also be read directly from the literal normalized cap frames: their relevant leading components are (p_hat_d)_n=a^(n+1)/F_(n+1)+higher central powers, (l_hat_d)_m=a^(d-m)F_m/N+higher central powers. The coupon contributes a^(r-N). The total power is zero since m=n+r and d+1=N, leaving F_U/[N F_(L-1)], exactly (7). Thus the example retains the actual cap normalization and indices; it is not a redefinition using an unknown knot period. The elementary Riemann sum on the nonsingular interval [1/6,5/6] proves lim_N (1/N)log|cap(O)| =integral_(1/6)^(5/6) log(2sin(pi t))dt =Vol(4_1)/(2pi)>0. (8) On every fixed circle |epsilon|=rho in (0,1), however, ||O(a)||_op=rho^(r/N-1)<=rho^-1, uniformly in N. Its central pole order is exactly one; the deck character r grows proportionally to N. Thus neither bounded central pole order nor bounded inserted-coupon norm alone makes the SINGLE-HEAD actual cap extraction tempered over all characters. This is an original cap with an INSERTED auxiliary coupon. It is NOT an original knot counterexample, and the coupon does NOT intertwine the actual degree/Cartan charge: it changes the head degree by r. In particular extending it trivially on the other head gives zero between the paired D=d charge projections. The [tame paired source](tame_paired_fermat_source_transport.md) uses that actual charge and is not contradicted by (7)--(8). The example explains why that paired-charge improvement and the explicit deck-support hypotheses are substantive.

title: Complete ordinary-cap trees have one positive angle-simplex energy
text: # Complete ordinary-cap trees have one positive angle-simplex energy 29 October 2026. An arbitrary binary tree of the ORIGINAL ordinary-cap reassociation packets contracts exactly. Its internal factorials telescope, its actual phases remain explicit, and its full squared kernel is ONE positive angle-simplex weight. After its known row normalization the complete boundary packet is a coisometry; overlaps between any two such normalized cap trees are contractive. This holds at arbitrary fixed width, including all endpoint indices and arbitrary adjoining tensors. This is a constructive boundary contraction theorem. It does not say that a knot's interior operator preserves these source packets, that complete-channel Racah matrices are contractive, or that the remaining marked cap is an ordinary cap. No new whole-knot volume estimate follows from this theorem alone. ## 1. The literal node and its source type Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=-q^-1, F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a|, and the physical gauge B_a=N^(1/4)/sqrt(s_a). Let A=(C'_23)^(-1)C'_12, with the original finite Euler maps. The [proved original pivotal-cap identity](actual_pivotal_cap_reassociation_angle_packet.md) uses ellhat=sqrt(N)ell, where ell is the LITERAL original ordinary cap including its pivot. Its gauged map Khat=(ellhat_12 tensor I)A is Khat_(n;(a,b,c)) =delta_(b,d)delta_(n,a+c<=d) q^[a(n-N-1)] sqrt(w_d(a,c,d-n)), w_d(i,j,k)=1/(s_i s_j s_k). (1) The b=d selection is the result of the COMPLETE pivotal q-Pascal sum, not a discarded input channel. In the ungauged physical coordinates and with the literal ell the same node is Kraw_(n;(a,b,c)) =delta_(b,d)delta_(n,a+c<=d) N^(-1) p(a) F_n/(F_a F_c), p(a)=(-1)^a Q^[a(a-1)/2]. (2) The original Cartan/framing/peripheral lines on any exterior are unchanged. Equation (2) uses x=-q^-1; the full unreduced meridian factors in the local theorem must instead be retained off completeness. ## 2. A source-exact complete tree, with every phase retained Choose any planar binary tree T with l>=1 ordered leaves. Its original physical input has 2l-1 heads: l active leaves, and one separator head between each two successive leaves. At an internal node, first contract its left and right subtrees, then apply the three-head node (1) to their two outputs and the original separator between them. Each separator is used once. These are ordinary compositions of the specified actual maps. Every nonzero input has ALL l-1 separator indices d. If the active indices are a_1,...,a_l, its root index is n=sum_i a_i<=d. Conversely every such input is allowed: all intermediate subtree sums are at most n. There is exactly one intermediate root index at every node. Therefore no unperformed internal summation or cyclic alias remains. For an internal vertex v write n_v for its subtree sum and n_L(v) for its left-subtree sum. The complete normalized-cap, quarter-gauged kernel is Khat_T(n;a_1,...,a_l; separators) =delta_(separators,d)delta_(n=sum a_i<=d) N^(-(l-1)/2) sqrt(s_n/product_i s_(a_i)) q^(Theta_T), Theta_T=sum_(v internal) n_L(v)(n_v-N-1). (3) Proof. Replace each square root in (1) by N^(-1/2)sqrt(s_(n_v)/(s_(n_L)s_(n_R))), using s_j s_(d-j)=N. Every internal s cancels between its output and its parent's input. The phases multiply to exactly the displayed sum. They have NOT been replaced by one, nor asserted to cancel on a cycle. There is an independent exact polynomial form for the LITERAL original cap tree before physical gauging: Kraw_T=N^(-(l-1)) F_n/(product_i F_(a_i)) product_(v internal) p(n_L(v)). (4) This follows by the same cancellation using (2), and specifies every original root phase. In particular it is not a norm-only construction. The literal gauged cap tree equals N^(-(l-1)/2)Khat_T: each use of ellhat in (3) restores its stated ell=ellhat/sqrt(N) factor. All input and output B gauges are explicit, and their internal inverse factors cancel under composition. No separator-state norm is silently substituted for its actual physical coordinate. ## 3. Exact positive simplex incidence and all-width energy By reflection, the squared surviving entry (3) is |Khat_T|^2=N^(2-l)/[s_(d-n) product_i s_(a_i)]. (5) Thus its true nonnegative integer charges are (a_0,a_1,...,a_l), a_0=d-n, sum_(i=0)^l a_i=d. (6) This is a bijection, not a relaxation: every composition in (6) is one allowed input/root combination of the complete tree. The internal subtree charges are its specified partial sums. All zero angles and zero-length slots are retained by s_0=1. Let E_(l,n)=N^(-(l-1))s_n sum_(a_1+...+a_l=n) product_i s_(a_i)^(-1). Different root rows have disjoint input-degree support, hence EXACTLY Khat_T Khat_T^*=diag(E_(l,0),...,E_(l,d)), ||Khat_T||_op^2=max_n E_(l,n), ||Khat_T||_HS^2=N^(2-l) Z_(l+1,N), Z_(m,N)=sum_(a_0+...+a_(m-1)=d) product_i s_(a_i)^(-1). (7) These quantities are independent of the binary tree. Equations (3)--(7) are an exact controlled contraction for the entire ordinary-cap tree, not independent Cauchy bounds at its nodes. For fixed l>=2 put Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log(2sin t)dt. The uniform factorial estimate at ALL 0<=a<N gives log||Khat_T||_op^2=log||Khat_T||_HS^2+O(log N) =N (l+1)Lambda(pi/(l+1))/pi+O_l(log N). (8) Here the first equality follows directly from the N rows in (7). To prove the second, the continuum objective on (6) is sum_i Lambda(pi a_i/N). On the simplex of nonnegative angles summing to pi its unique maximum, for m=l+1>=3, is m Lambda(pi/m). For completeness its Hessian on the interior is -diag(cot theta_i). If all angles are below pi/2 it is negative on sum-zero vectors. If one angle exceeds pi/2, put S=sum of the other angles<pi/2. Weighted Cauchy and sum tan(theta_i)<tan S=-tan(theta_big) show the same strict negativity on the sum-zero tangent. Equality at pi/2 follows directly from the positive remaining cotangents. Thus the function is strictly concave; symmetry fixes its maximum at equal angles. Continuity includes the boundary. Rounding an equal composition to the integer sum d gives the lower bound at every sufficiently large level; there are only polynomially many compositions and all factorial errors are O_l(log N), giving the upper bound. No lattice progression is needed. For l=1 the map is identity, E_(1,n)=1, and its energy exponent is zero. There is a stronger UNIFORM root-conditioned formula. For every 0<=n<=d, including both endpoints, put t=n/N. Then log E_(l,n)=(N/pi)Phi_l(t)+O_l(log N), Phi_l(t)=l Lambda(pi*t/l)-Lambda(pi*t). (9) The constant is independent of n. For fixed sum of the l leaf angles, at most pi, the concavity argument just given places their maximum at equal values. The case l=2 at total pi may have additional maximizers, without affecting this value. For the lower estimate, distribute the integer n among l parts differing by at most one. Each angle changes by O_l(1/N), whose Lambda error is O_l(log N/N) uniformly even at zero or pi. There are at most (N+1)^(l-1) compositions. Applying the uniform factorial estimate to every term in E_(l,n), and to s_n, therefore proves BOTH sides of (9), with the stated uniform error. For l>=2 and 0<t<1 the explicit boundary action satisfies Phi_l'(t)=pi log[sin(pi*t)/sin(pi*t/l)], Phi_l''(t)=pi^2[cot(pi*t)-(1/l)cot(pi*t/l)]<0. (9a) Indeed x cot x is strictly decreasing on (0,pi), since its derivative has numerator sin(x)cos(x)-x<0. Its unique maximum is t=l/(l+1). Using Lambda(pi-theta)=-Lambda(theta), the maximum is exactly (l+1)Lambda(pi/(l+1)), giving (8). Formula (9) also includes a prescribed root tending to t=1, with rate l Lambda(pi/l)/pi. For l=1, E_(1,n)=1 and Phi_1=0 identically. ## 4. Exact coherent packet overlaps are contractive Every E_(l,n) is positive and known without a knot value. Define R_T=diag(E_(l,n)^(-1/2)) Khat_T. Then R_T R_T^*=I_N. Consequently P_T=R_T^*R_T is a specified orthogonal projection on the full physical input space, including its literal separator-d selection. For ANY two planar binary trees on the same ordered heads, R_T R_U^* is diagonal and ||R_T R_U^*||<=1. (10) The diagonal entry is the ACTUAL mixed phase sum of the two root rows, divided by E_(l,n); Cauchy proves its modulus at most one. This retains the off-diagonal leaf copies inside P_T and the full phases Theta_T. An arbitrary finite sequence of these packet overlaps is contractive. No artificial dephasing, ordinary positive pivotal trace or favorable choice of unknown source has been introduced. For a specified remaining row z on the root, its complete original boundary-functional norm remains exactly ||z Khat_T||^2=sum_n |z_n|^2 E_(l,n). (11) One may not drop these root weights, replace a marked row by an ordinary cap, or normalize z using an unknown period. For literal caps multiply the energies by N^(-(l-1)) as stated after (4). ## 5. What this gives for global gluing This proves a genuine positive angle incidence for a complete tree source: (6), including all its internal actual partial sums. It is a single angle simplex. It is NOT yet the edge/peripheral incidence of a knot ideal triangulation. The identity applies to arbitrary fixed width and to any polynomial or matrix exterior because it is an actual boundary-operator identity. The complete-channel Racah transition on an interior port has additional channels beyond these ordinary-cap packets. It is not the compression R_T R_U^*. Nor is an arbitrary interior R word proved to preserve P_T. The full marked packet in the local theorem must also remain. Thus (10) is a constructive boundary-tree overlap estimate; using it as a unitary or complete projection on an arbitrary knot interior would be an extra unproved step. The original full-source goal still needs the corresponding complete-channel or source-specific interior control. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_cap_tree_angle_energy.py): original coproduct-derived reassociation with the literal ordinary cap, all middle-index cancellations, exact complete tree q-factorial/phase formula, angle-simplex bijection, row energies, and coherent overlaps. Fresh replay: PASS five levels of literal original cap/reassociation matrices and complete tree phases, and twenty all-tree-shape families checking metric kernels, positive simplex incidence, full mixed overlaps and retained arbitrary root co-sources. Python compilation passes.

title: The original operator period has a controlled closing region at two
text: # The original operator period has a controlled closing region at two 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. A whole right half-disk at the spectral endpoint has vanishing exponential cost as its radius tends to zero. The bound is uniform over EVERY physical degree and every original matrix entry, including the Jordan blocks. Fixed genuine generic-q and spectral derivatives of the resolvent have the same vanishing-rate property. Combined with the separately proved canceled Sears bound for the actual scalar polynomial, it controls the full original integrand and its fixed generic normals throughout that region. The same estimates extend to a fixed angular slit cone on both sides of that half-disk, avoiding the spectral poles on the left real ray. The statement is an upper estimate. It does not select a contributing contour or give a nonzero saddle contribution. The scalar normal input to the final assembly is proved in its linked companion theorem. ## 1. Uniform finite statement Use the original physical matrix J_t, q=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, N>=3, and 0<=t<=d. Define f(r)=sqrt(r) log(2+1/r), r>0, and f(0)=0, H_N(r)=C N^3 exp[C N f(r)+C(log N)^2]. (1) There is an absolute C such that for every 0<=r<=1/4, ||(zI-J_t(q))^-1||op<=H_N(r), Re z>=2, |z-2|<=r. (2) The same holds for the actual high-degree blocks, by their exact generic adapter. For fixed nonnegative integers j,k, with R_t(h,z)=(zI-J_t(q exp(h)))^-1, one also has on this region ||partial_h^j partial_z^k R_t(0,z)||op <=C_(j,k) N^j max(1,H_N(r))^(j+k+1). (3) These are genuine generic derivatives of the original matrix, with its distinct moving upper and lower entries. In particular lim_(r down 0) limsup_(N->infinity) N^-1 log sup_(t,z) ||partial_h^j partial_z^k R_t(0,z)||op <=0. (4) Here z ranges over the half-disk in (2). Replacing a zero norm by max(1,norm) gives the equivalent nonnegative-rate formulation. More generally fix 0<gamma_0<pi/2. All these statements hold, with constants depending on gamma_0, throughout K_(r,gamma_0)={2} union {z=2+rho exp(i phi): 0<rho<=r, |phi|<=pi-gamma_0}. (4a) This includes parts of the disk to the LEFT of two, but excludes a fixed angular neighborhood of the left real ray containing the poles. ## 2. Every prefix has a small positive determinant rate Put theta=pi/N. The exact ground-state congruence in the [endpoint theorem](actual_casimir_endpoint_resolvent_bound.md) gives, for any leading prefix of size 1<=m<=t, |det(J_[m]-zI)|=|det(L_m+(z-lambda_0)V_m)|, lambda_0=2cos(theta), |(V_m)_(r,r)|=1. (5) L_m is the real Dirichlet path matrix with conductances a_r=4sin((t-r)theta)sin((r+1)theta), 0<=r<t, (L_m)_(r,r)=a_(r-1)+a_r, a_(-1)=0, (L_m)_(r,r+1)=-a_r. (6) The final term a_(m-1) is retained as a Dirichlet boundary spring. The principal minors are positive, so expansion in the diagonal perturbation, term by term in absolute value, yields |det(L_m+(z-lambda_0)V_m)| <=det L_m det(I+s L_m^-1), s=|z-lambda_0|, det L_m=product_(r=0)^(m-1) a_r. (7) The following estimate holds uniformly in ALL t,m,N and 0<=s<=2: log det(I+s L_m^-1) <=C N f(s)+C(log N)^2. (8) Here is a direct path proof, including the two small-conductance endpoints. Let h_r=min(r+1,t-r). Since t<=N-1, both integers r+1 and t-r, and their distances from N, are at least h_r. The elementary sine lower bound therefore gives a_r>=16 h_r^2/N^2. (9) The exact inverse-trace formula for L_t then gives Tr L_t^-1=sum_(r=0)^(t-1)(r+1)/a_r<=C N^3. (10) In particular its smallest eigenvalue is at least c N^-3. Partition the rows of L_t into consecutive dyadic blocks from the left and right endpoints towards the middle. There are O(log N) blocks, with a bounded number of each dyadic length, apart from at most two shorter remainder blocks. On a block of length ell, every internal conductance is at least c ell^2/N^2 by (9). Remove the springs between blocks and the final Dirichlet spring. The resulting block-diagonal Neumann operator is smaller than L_t as a quadratic form. A constant-conductance Neumann path of length ell has eigenvalues 4 a sin^2(pi k/(2ell)), 0<=k<ell. Consequently each such block contributes at most 1+C min(ell,N sqrt(lambda)) eigenvalues at most lambda. Summing the dyadic lengths gives the counting estimate n_t(lambda)<=C log N +C N sqrt(lambda) log(2+1/lambda). (11) For clarity, with x=N sqrt(lambda), the sum of lengths below x is O(x), while the larger blocks contribute O(x[1+log(N/x)]). If x<1, their contribution is O(x log N), which is bounded by the second term in (11). For large lambda the trivial bound n_t<=N is stronger. Prefix interlacing gives n_m(lambda)<=n_t(lambda) and the same lower eigenvalue bound as in (10). For positive eigenvalues mu, integrate the identity log(1+s/mu)=integral_mu^infinity s/[lambda(lambda+s)] d lambda. The C log N term of (11), starting at cN^-3, costs O((log N)^2). The other term has integral at most C N f(s): set lambda=s y and use the integrability of y^-1/2(1+y)^-1 and the same function times |log y|. This proves (8), with s=0 immediate. No inverse bound for a long complex Casimir prefix was assumed. Only the real positive path L_m enters this comparison. ## 3. Exact cancellation controls all original Green entries For u<=v the original continuant identity expresses R_(u,v) as the leading prefix determinant of size u, the trailing determinant of size t-v, and the product of original upper entries between them, divided by the full characteristic polynomial. At the root the trailing prefix is the reflected conjugate of a leading prefix; the magnitudes a_r in (6) obey a_(t-1-r)=a_r. Thus the conductance products from the two bounds (7) and the middle Green product telescope EXACTLY to product_(r=0)^(t-1) a_r=s_t^2, s_t=product_(r=1)^t 2sin(r theta). (12) The root matrix is symmetric, so the same estimate holds for u>v. Its exact characteristic polynomial has real roots below two: chi_t(z)=product_(r=0)^t[z-2cos((2r+1)theta)]. For Re z>=2, each factor has magnitude at least its value at two. The already proved exact product inequality is |chi_t(z)|>=chi_t(2)>=4s_t^2/N^2. (13) Equations (7),(8),(12),(13) therefore bound EVERY entry by (N^2/4) exp[2C N f(|z-lambda_0|)+2C(log N)^2]. (14) Empty prefixes have determinant one and cause no exception. For t=0 the scalar bound follows directly from 2-lambda_0>=4/N^2. Finally |z-lambda_0|<=r+delta with delta=2-lambda_0 comparable to N^-2. The elementary inequality f(a+b)<=f(a)+f(b) gives N f(r+delta)<=N f(r)+C log N. The function f is increasing: its derivative has the sign of log x-2+4/x for x=2+1/r>=2, whose minimum is log 4-1>0. Multiplying the entrywise bound by the dimension at most N proves (2). In particular the proof includes t=N-1 and long prefixes; no compact restriction on physical degree is needed. ### The angular slit-cone extension The same numerator estimate applies at any complex z. Only the full characteristic lower bound changes outside Re z>=2. Write x_h=2-2cos((2h+1)theta)>0, |chi_t(2+rho exp(i phi))/chi_t(2)| =product_(h=0)^t |1+rho exp(i phi)/x_h|. (14a) For |phi|<=pi-gamma_0 and every y>=0 one has |1+y exp(i phi)|>=sin(gamma_0). Split the factors in (14a) at x_h=2rho. To count them, put v_h=min(h+1/2,N-h-1/2). The complete list 0<=h<N satisfies 16 v_h^2/N^2<=x_h<=4pi^2 v_h^2/N^2. There are O(N sqrt(rho)+1) factors with x_h<=2rho, so their total logarithmic loss is at most C_(gamma_0)(N sqrt(rho)+1). For the other factors, y=rho/x_h<1/2 and log|1+y exp(i phi)|>=log(1-y)>=-2y. The two displayed comparisons, followed by the convergent tail sum of v_h^-2, give sum_(x_h>2rho) rho/x_h<=C(N sqrt(rho)+1). Bounding the entire list also bounds every degree sublist. Hence |chi_t(z)/chi_t(2)| >=exp[-C_(gamma_0)(N sqrt(rho)+1)] (14b) on (4a). The additional loss is absorbed in N f(r)+O(log N). This proves (2),(3),(4) on the full cone (4a). The cone has a useful literal overlap with the earlier strict-prefix action domains. For any fixed strict pair of prefix angles beta_1, beta_2<pi, choose gamma_0 smaller than both (pi-beta_i)/2. Points z=2-rho exp(+/-i gamma_0) then lie in BOTH selected-prefix halfplanes. Thus the estimate reaches potential joining points for those actual integrand charts. No contour deformation or saddle contribution follows from this overlap alone. ## 4. Actual generic normals remain controlled For each fixed j>=1 the displayed ORIGINAL generic matrix satisfies ||partial_h^j J_t(q exp(h)) evaluated_(h=0)||op<=C_j N^j. This follows directly from its fixed bandwidth and finite products of monomials with exponents O(N). Differentiating the inverse identity retains the exact moving matrix: partial_h R=R(partial_h J)R and partial_z R=-R^2. Each mixed derivative is a finite sum of products with at most j+k+1 resolvent factors and total h-derivative order j on the intervening J factors. Bound them by (2) to obtain (3). This argument includes every moving eigenvalue and Jordan-current term, and differentiates no root-only reflection. ## 5. The root scalar integrand also has vanishing closing rate The actual polynomial p_a(q,z), 0<=a<=floor(d/2), has only simple roots strictly above two. Its normalization makes p_a(q,x)>0 for real x<2. Therefore the factorization into its actual roots gives the exact estimate |p_a(q,z)|<=p_a(q,2-r), |z-2|<=r. (15) This remains true on the part of the disk crossing the scalar's LIMITING cut: the finite source is a polynomial there and (15) does not select or continue a logarithm through its zeros. For a/N->alpha in (0,1/2], the proved slit action gives N^-1 log p_a(q,2-r)->Psi_alpha(2-r) at every fixed r>0. Its explicit real formula has Psi_alpha(2-r)->0 as r decreases to zero. Indeed its maximizing t_* satisfies sin^2(pi t_*)=A r/(r+4A), A=sin^2(pi alpha), so t_*=O(sqrt(r)); the sine-log integrals in that formula tend to zero, including their integrable endpoint logarithms. Thus (2),(15) prove lim_(r down 0) limsup_(N->infinity) N^-1 log sup_(Re z>=2,|z-2|<=r) ||p_a(q,z)(zI-J_t(q))^-1||op <=0, (16) uniformly over every physical degree t. The actual face factor is one at the root. The same conclusion holds with any fixed generic or spectral derivative placed on the RESOLVENT factor alone, by (3). Consequently a closing arc of bounded length contained in this half-disk has the upper rate (16). This is a genuine estimate on the entire closing region, rather than an inference from a tiny endpoint disk. This root-factor argument does not itself estimate generic derivatives of the scalar polynomial on that whole region; Section 6 uses the separate scalar theorem for them. Neither argument estimates the rest of an enclosing contour, its deformation or intersection numbers, or the coherent surrounding state. A contributing geometric saddle and noncancellation remain separate requirements. All conclusions in this section also hold on the slit cone (4a), with its fixed gamma_0-dependent constants. The scalar estimate (15) already holds on the whole disk, and (14b) supplies the only extra resolvent cost. ## 6. Assembly for the full original integrand and its generic normals The independently proved [canceled-Sears closing theorem](actual_matching_edge_polynomial_closing_region_bound.md) supplies the scalar factor on the WHOLE complex disk, including its genuine generic-q normals and the actual face scalar. Combine it with (2),(3),(4a). For I_(N,a,t)(h,z)=D_a(q exp(h))^-1 p_a(q exp(h),z)(zI-J_t(q exp(h)))^-1, every fixed j,k>=0 satisfies sup_(z in K_(r,gamma_0)) ||partial_h^j partial_z^k I_(N,a,t)(0,z)||op <=C_(j,k,gamma_0) r^-k N^(4j+3k+3) exp[C_(j,k,gamma_0) N f(r) +C_(j,k,gamma_0)(log N)^2]. (17) This holds uniformly in ALL 0<=a<=floor((N-1)/2), ALL 0<=t<=N-1, both level parities and 0<r<=r0, for a sufficiently small fixed r0. The angular exclusion gamma_0 remains fixed and positive. No limit a/N->alpha is required in (17). Here are the finite costs in the pure Leibniz argument. Put i of the j generic derivatives and l of the k spectral derivatives on the scalar factor. Its companion bound costs at most N^(3i) r^-l exp[C N f(r)+C log N], since p_a(q,2)<=1. The remaining resolvent derivatives cost, by (3), C N^(j-i) H_N(r)^(j-i+k-l+1). The resulting power of N is 4j-i+3k-3l+3<=4j+3k+3, and r^-l<=r^-k. Summing the finitely many Leibniz terms proves (17). The inverse face scalar and all its q jets are already part of the scalar companion theorem; none is discarded. In particular, let r_N decrease to zero at ANY rate and let an arc Gamma_N lie in K_(r_N,gamma_0), with length at most a fixed power of N. Hold that arc fixed while taking generic-q derivatives. For every fixed j, the integral over Gamma_N of partial_h^j I(0,z) has norm at most exp[o(N)]. This uses k=0 in (17), so there is no r_N^-k loss. It includes the actual finite source normals needed by the exceptional operator period, not just its root value. This cap estimate does not prove a deformation of the remainder of the original contour, its saddle intersection number or a nonzero geometric contribution. In particular it leaves the surrounding complement and its coherent contraction explicit: multiplying this block by an uncontrolled environment is not a completed volume bound. Audit: [dyadic path comparison, all-prefix determinants and original Green entries](../experiments/audit_actual_casimir_closing_region_bound.py). Independent review of Sections 1--5: the root and geometry agents checked the full analytical proof, including the angular cone and its strict-prefix overlap. The geometry agent freshly replayed the audit: 128 dyadic partitions and deleted-spring matrices, 6,951 block scales, 1,089 all-prefix congruences and positive determinant comparisons, 5,445 original Green entries and exact product cancellations, 264 characteristic half-plane comparisons, 12 first and 12 second genuine q-resolvent identities, 24 spectral identities, 254 node-distance bounds and 2,025 angular characteristic-product bounds passed. The finite spectral-count samples are explicitly diagnostics; the uniform estimates are proved above. The Section 6 assembly uses only the two independently reviewed bounds and the displayed Leibniz count. The root and source agents independently checked that assembly, including the actual face factor, conservative power of N, arbitrary shrinking radii for k=0, fixed angular exclusion and the explicit surrounding-environment limitation: PASS. No new numerical test is needed for this finite Leibniz consequence.

title: The full original Casimir resolvent is polynomial at the spectral endpoint
status: Full physical endpoint resolvent and genuine jets
text: # The full original Casimir resolvent is polynomial at the spectral endpoint 30 October 2026. The original physical Casimir has a uniformly polynomial resolvent at z=2, including all degrees, both level parities and its Jordan blocks. Fixed genuine generic-q and spectral derivatives have polynomial cost on an explicit shrinking neighborhood. This addresses a finite endpoint of the exact operator contour; it does not prove dominance of a geometric saddle or control an entire contour segment merely from its endpoint. ## 1. Uniform statement Put q=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, N>=3, and use the ACTUAL generic physical matrix J_t(zeta) from the [original jet theorem](actual_q_hahn_physical_generic_jet_bound.md). For every 0<=t<=d there is an absolute constant C such that ||(2I-J_t(q))^-1||op<=C N^17. (1) The exponent is a conservative uniform bound, not an optimal rate. The same bound holds for every high-degree block, by the exact generic high-degree adapter, and for their full orthogonal direct sum. For sufficiently small absolute c>0, on the bidisk zeta=q exp(h), |h|<=cN^-19, |z-2|<=cN^-18, the resolvent exists and has norm at most 2C N^17. Consequently its mixed Taylor coefficients satisfy ||[h^r(z-2)^s](zI-J_t(q exp(h)))^-1||op <=C_(r,s) N^(17+19r+18s). (2) These are the original matrix normals, with distinct generic upper and lower entries. No semisimple projection or root-only reflection is differentiated in (2). ## 2. The exact ground-state congruence Write theta=pi/N, lambda_0=q+q^-1, delta=2-lambda_0=4sin^2(theta/2). The original normalized channel-zero vector is f_r=(-q^-1)^r. The root offdiagonal and its positive magnitude are A_r=-a_r q^(2r+1-t), a_r=4sin((t-r)theta)sin((r+1)theta)>0, 0<=r<t. The exact row identity proved in the [off-spectrum prefix theorem](actual_casimir_off_spectrum_prefix_action.md) is D_r=lambda_0+q^-1 A_r+q A_(r-1), with A_(-1)=0. For a leading m-by-m prefix, m<=t, let F=diag(f_0,...,f_(m-1)) and let L_m be the REAL weighted Dirichlet matrix with diagonal a_(r-1)+a_r and offdiagonals -a_r, retaining the right boundary conductance a_(m-1). Then exactly F(J_[m]-lambda_0 I)F=-q^-t L_m, F(J_[m]-2I)F=-q^-t(L_m+delta V_m), V_m=diag(q^(t-2r)). (3) This is a unitary congruence, not a unitary similarity. Its left and right factors nevertheless preserve singular values and determinant magnitudes. Thus it can be used for inverse norms without claiming that J is Hermitian. The positive matrix L_m has the elementary exact formulas det L_m=product_(r=0)^(m-1) a_r, tr L_m^-1=sum_(r=0)^(m-1)(r+1)/a_r. (4) Indeed L_m=B^T diag(a_r)B, where (Bv)_r=v_r-v_(r+1) and v_m=0. The inverse of B has ones above its diagonal; (4) follows directly. ## 3. Both halves are controlled, even when t approaches N-1 Suppose 1<=m<=floor(t/2)+1 and m<=t. Every argument (t-2r)theta in V_m lies in [0,t theta], and t theta<=pi-theta. Rotation by exp(-it theta/2) therefore gives Re[exp(-it theta/2)(L_m+delta V_m)] >=cos(t theta/2)(L_m+delta I). Since cos(t theta/2)>=sin(theta/2)>=1/N and delta>=4/N^2, ||(J_[m]-2I)^-1||op<=N^3/4. (5) This remains uniform at the folded physical endpoint t=N-1. For these same half-prefixes one has a_r>=4(r+1)^2/N^2. (6) For r=0 use sin(t theta)>=sin theta>=2/N. For r>=1, r<=t/2 and t<=N-1 put t-r in [r,N-r-1]. Both sine factors in a_r are at least 2r/N, giving a_r>=16r^2/N^2 and hence (6). Equations (4),(6) show delta tr L_m^-1<= (pi^2/4)(1+log N). Expansion in the diagonal perturbation gives an especially simple determinant bound: all principal minors of L_m are positive, and every diagonal entry of V_m has modulus one. Therefore |det(L_m+delta V_m)|<=det(L_m+delta I) <=det L_m exp(delta tr L_m^-1) <=C N^3 product_(r=0)^(m-1) a_r. (7) This is an upper bound for the ACTUAL determinant; no estimate on individual nonorthogonal spectral projectors was used. The trailing half at the root is the reflected conjugate of a leading half, so (5),(7) apply to it too. Only these root norm statements use reflection. ## 4. The exact full determinant prevents a small Schur denominator The actual characteristic polynomial gives chi_t(2)=det(2I-J_t(q)) =product_(r=0)^t [2sin((r+1/2)theta)]^2>0. (8) Let s_t=product_(r=1)^t 2sin(r theta). Then product_(r=0)^(t-1)a_r=s_t^2, chi_t(2)/s_t^2>=4/N^2. (9) Here is an elementary uniform proof of the second inequality. The positive sequence H_t=product_(r=0)^t 2sin((r+1/2)theta)/s_t has successive ratios sin((t+1/2)theta)/sin(t theta). They are first at least one and then at most one, so its minimum occurs at an endpoint. The cyclotomic products give H_(N-1)=2/N, while H_0=2sin(theta/2)>=2/N. Squaring proves (9). For t>=1 split J_t-2I between its two middle rows. Its diagonal blocks B,C have sizes floor((t+1)/2), ceil((t+1)/2), so (5),(7) apply. Let A be their single connecting root offdiagonal and a=|A|<=4. In (7) the connecting conductance occurs in BOTH Dirichlet halves. Consequently |det B det C|<=C N^6 a s_t^2. The two-by-two bridge correction has determinant Delta=1-A^2(B^-1)_(last,last)(C^-1)_(first,first) =det(J_t-2I)/(det B det C). Using (8),(9) and a<=4 yields |Delta|>=c N^-8. (10) Every entry of its adjugate is bounded by C N^3 by (5). Its inverse therefore has norm at most C N^11. The rank-two resolvent formula, with two diagonal-block inverse factors of norm at most C N^3, gives C N^(3+3+11)=C N^17 for the whole inverse. This proves (1). The case t=0 is the scalar inverse delta^-1<=N^2/4. This argument controls the actual full Jordan resolvent; it does not bound it by a sum of exponentially large individual projector norms. ## 5. The original generic normals and the contour qualification Every exponent in the displayed original generic matrix entries is O(N), and the bandwidth is fixed. On |h|<=c/N the matrix perturbation has operator norm at most C N|h|, uniformly in physical t. Combining this with (1), the two perturbations h and z-2 on the stated bidisk have relative inverse norm less than 1/2 for sufficiently small c. The Neumann resolvent formula proves the uniform bidisk bound; two-variable Cauchy gives (2). This argument starts from the genuine generic matrix and so retains all moving-node and moving-projector contributions automatically. The endpoint matters because the largest root Casimir node tends to 2, while the source-polynomial zeros approach 2 from above. A fixed contour enclosing all nodes cannot remain a fixed compact of the scalar limiting slit plane. Equations (1),(2) provide uniform finite control at 2 and on the displayed shrinking neighborhood. They do not alone estimate the path connecting that neighborhood to a fixed contour, establish a steepest-descent deformation, or show that the geometric contribution is nonzero. Focused audit: [actual ground-state congruence, halves and full endpoint resolvent](../experiments/audit_actual_casimir_endpoint_resolvent_bound.py). Primary and independent analytical reviews: PASS. The independent read checked the unitary congruence rather than a claimed similarity, the two half-block bounds uniformly through t=N-1, the duplicated bridge conductance, exact characteristic-product lower bound and full Schur denominator, and the genuine generic perturbation. A fresh independent replay passed 187 original full blocks, 5,030 congruence entries, 251 half-inverse, positive-determinant and trace checks, 187 characteristic products, and 170 exact Schur determinants. The numerical full norms are diagnostics; the stated uniform exponent comes from the proof. No contour deformation or geometric contribution is included in these reviews.

title: The actual Casimir prefix has a selected off-spectrum action
text: # The actual Casimir prefix has a selected off-spectrum action 30 October 2026. This is a theorem for the original physical Casimir matrix, with an arbitrary spectral variable. It supplies a forward/backward Green-kernel ingredient for the exact exceptional-block contour. It does not continue a finite color or a magnetic index, evaluate the full polynomial operator by its symbol, or prove that a geometric saddle contributes to the source contour. ## 1. Statement and the strict half-prefix condition Use the original root matrix J_t of the [physical generic-jet theorem](actual_q_hahn_physical_generic_jet_bound.md), with q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, 0<=t<=N-1. Let J_[m] be its first m rows and columns. Suppose t/N -> tau, m/N -> nu, 0<nu<tau/2, 0<tau<1. All convergence below is uniform when the two real parameters stay in compact subsets of this strict domain. Put beta=pi(1-tau+2nu) in (0,pi), H_beta={z: Re[exp(-i beta/2)(2-z)]>0}. On every compact subset of H_beta, the actual matrices J_[m]-zI are invertible for all sufficiently large N, with a uniformly bounded inverse. In particular this includes every fixed compact set of real spectral parameters z<2. The bound does not hold here at a central prefix nu=tau/2; that endpoint is deliberately excluded. There is a canonical analytic logarithm of the determinant, selected from negative real infinity, for which N^-1 Log det(J_[m]-zI) -> S_(tau,nu)(z), (1) locally uniformly on H_beta, with every fixed z derivative. Write A(x)=-4 exp(i pi(2x-tau)) sin(pi(tau-x))sin(pi x), w=2-z. The limiting action is the explicit single integral S_(tau,nu)(z)=integral_0^nu Log[(w+2A(x)+sqrt(w(w+4A(x))))/2] dx. (2) The square root and logarithm in (2) are selected at large positive w and continued in H_beta. They are not pointwise principal choices of a determinant or discriminant. Formula (1) is a leading action, not a relative-amplitude expansion. ## 2. An exact Dirichlet decomposition of the original matrix The actual root entries, with U=Q^r and T=Q^t, are D_r=U/T [2(q^-1+qT)-(q+q^-1)U], A_r=(U-T)(1-q^2 U)/T. Put A_(-1)=0. Direct algebra gives BOTH identities D_r=q+q^-1+q^-1 A_r+q A_(r-1), (3) R_r:=D_r-2-A_r-A_(r-1) =-U(q-1)^2(Tq^2-Uq^2-Uq-U+1)/(Tq^2). (4) Hence |R_r|<=C/N^2, uniformly over all physical r,t. The unitary diagonal sign matrix changes the offdiagonals of J_[m] to -A_r. After this conjugation, (4) says exactly J_[m]-2I=L_A+diag(R_r), (5) where L_A has diagonal A_(r-1)+A_r and adjacent entries -A_r. For v_m=0 its sesquilinear form is <v,L_A v>=sum_(r=0)^(m-1) A_r |v_r-v_(r+1)|^2. (6) The term r=m-1 is the retained Dirichlet boundary term. At the other endpoint A_(-1)=0 exactly; no omitted boundary term is being estimated. The original coefficients also have the exact polar form A_r=-4 exp(i(2r+1-t)pi/N) sin((t-r)pi/N)sin((r+1)pi/N). For 0<=r<m, both sine factors are positive and their marked arguments obey 0<Arg A_r<=beta_N:=pi+(2m-1-t)pi/N<pi. (7) In the strict scaling range beta_N tends to beta<pi. If w=2-z, rotation of wI+L_A by exp(-i beta_N/2) gives Re <v,exp(-i beta_N/2)(wI+L_A)v> >=Re[exp(-i beta_N/2)w] ||v||^2. (8) The perturbation (4) costs at most C/N^2 in (8). Every compact of H_beta has a positive margin in its right side; (5)--(8) therefore give the claimed uniform inverse bound for the ORIGINAL prefix. The sign conjugation is unitary and does not alter determinants. ## 3. Determining the actual logarithm, without an assumed WKB solution For a finite N, restrict first to Re[exp(-i beta_N/2)(2-z)]>2C/N^2. There the rotated matrix in (8) is strictly accretive. Its principal matrix logarithm defines Log det(J_[m]-zI) :=i m beta_N/2 +tr Log[exp(-i beta_N/2)(J_[m]-zI)]. (9) This agrees with m Log(-z)+O(m/|z|) as z tends to negative real infinity. These halfplanes exhaust every compact subset of H_beta. The logarithm in (9), rather than the principal logarithm of the scalar determinant, retains the actual accumulated phase. The inverse bound gives |N^-1 partial_z Log det(J_[m]-zI)|<=C_K m/N. At one sufficiently negative fixed real z, the uniformly bounded entries and fixed bandwidth give a bounded normalized logarithm by its convergent trace series. The derivative bound then gives local boundedness throughout H_beta. These analytic functions form a locally bounded normal family there. It remains to determine its limit on a nonempty open set. For each fixed integer k, multiplication of the tridiagonal matrices gives a finite sum over nearest-neighbor closed paths. Paths within k rows of an endpoint contribute O(k/N) after normalized trace, since their entries are uniformly bounded. On all other paths, the slowly varying entries may be replaced by their common local limits with error O_k(1/N). Thus N^-1 tr(J_[m]^k) -> integral_0^nu (1/pi) integral_0^pi [2+2A(x)+2A(x)cos(phi)]^k dphi dx. (10) The coefficient of the zero Laurent power in the local tridiagonal symbol is precisely the inner integral in (10); this proves the path count directly. For |z| sufficiently large, the uniformly convergent logarithmic trace series and (10) show that (1) has limit integral_0^nu (1/pi) integral_0^pi Log[w+4A(x)cos^2(phi/2)] dphi dx. (11) For every x in [0,nu], A(x) is zero or lies in the cone of (7). The argument of the logarithm in (11), after rotation, has strictly positive real part for z in H_beta. Consequently (11) is analytic on H_beta with the branch selected by negative infinity. The identity theorem and the normal-family bound make every subsequential limit equal to (11), proving convergence of the full sequence. Cauchy's formula proves convergence of all fixed spectral derivatives. Finally integrate the elementary logarithmic symbol. For large positive w, expansion in A/w (or differentiation in w followed by its value at infinity) gives (1/pi) integral_0^pi Log[w+4A cos^2(phi/2)] dphi =Log[(w+2A+sqrt(w(w+4A)))/2]. (12) Both sides continue analytically on H_beta. Indeed w and w+4A lie in the same rotated right halfplane; the selected product square root is nonzero there. The selected numerator in (12) is nonzero as well: a zero would force A=0 after squaring, whereas then it equals 2w. Equation (12) proves (2) with its source-selected branch. ## 4. What this gives to the exceptional-block problem The forward resolvent numerator is exactly det(zI-J_[m]); it differs from the determinant in (1) by (-1)^m, whose marked logarithm must be retained. The actual trailing prefix is the reflected conjugate root matrix, so it has the conjugate statement with its own corresponding halfplane and branch. Thus suitable strict forward/backward portions of the original Green kernel have a selected off-spectrum leading action, including all real geometric target traces below 2. This does not yet control prefixes reaching or crossing their midpoint, complex magnetic continuation, a relative nonzero amplitude, or the resolvent contour's intersection with a geometric steepest-descent cycle. No large-degree polynomial has been replaced by scalar symbol evaluation in this theorem. The moving generic-q normal also remains the one in the exact contour formula; (1) concerns spectral derivatives of the root prefix, not generic-q derivatives of the whole source. Focused audit: [original prefix, exact row residual and selected action](../experiments/audit_actual_casimir_off_spectrum_prefix_action.py). Primary and independent analytical reviews: PASS. The independent review checked the retained Dirichlet endpoint, exact residual, rotated halfplane, matrix-log branch, closed-path trace argument, normal-family continuation and selected integral. A fresh independent replay passed both symbolic row identities, 577 original prefix entries, 18 Dirichlet forms and 54 rotated inverse checks. Eighteen selected-log and eighteen trace-moment diagnostics agree with the proved limits; their finite tolerances are not a proof of those limits. The strict half-prefix, root-spectral-derivative and leading-action scopes were checked explicitly. No relative amplitude or source-cycle contribution is included in either review.

title: Exact central black, ordinary-white and marked contractions
text: # Exact central black, ordinary-white and marked contractions 29 October 2026. At the ODD simple Steinberg triple the actual ordinary white covector is a genuine pivotal dual of the black tensor, with an explicit scalar. It is nonzero, yet its closed magnetic pairing with black is ZERO. The original marked closure instead gives an explicit positive scalar after all magnetic indices are contracted. This is a coherent source calculation, not a norm-square replacement of the vertex. It explains why the [full-black CD norm obstruction](actual_trivalent_full_cd_normalization_and_magnetic_growth.md) does not determine the growth of a sewn scalar. Only this odd central sector and the specified actual two-vertex contraction are evaluated. No paired/even analogue, arbitrary graph recoupling estimate or global volume statement is inferred. ## 1. Original duality fixes the ordinary white tensor Use N=2m+1, d=2m and the exact central W,pi,Theta,A_N of [the actual odd source](actual_trivalent_steinberg_central_anchor.md). Thus pi=W^dagger P, pi W=I, and the unscaled black tensor is U=pi^tensor3 J_source=s Theta, s=N^2 q^(-m^2) A_N, Theta=(W tensor I)p. (1) The ORIGINAL physical cup/cap matrices are p_(a,b)=N x^(-b)delta_(a+b,d), ell_(a,b)=x^a/N delta_(a+b,d), p ell=ell p=I. For a map T:V->V tensor V its genuine right dual, after identifying the dual objects by these SAME maps, is D(T)=p^T T^T(ell^T tensor ell^T)P_ord. (2) P_ord reverses abstract dual tensor order; it is not an inserted R. For an invariant column v in V^tensor3 the right-dual covector is D(v)=v^T(ell^T)^tensor3 Rev_3. (3) These are bilinear pivotal duals. Complex conjugation is not part of D. Both formulas follow by the ordinary evaluation index sums, with every N factor retained. The actual simple-channel Hom space is one-dimensional, so D(W) is a scalar multiple of pi. Evaluate row0,column(m,0) in(2), using W_d(d,m)=q^(m^2). It gives EXACTLY D(W)=gamma pi, gamma=q^(3m^2)/N. (4) In particular gamma is nonzero. Dualizing pi W=I and using the same one-dimensional Hom space gives D(pi)=gamma^(-1)W. The nested matching (16),(23),(45) is preserved by reversal, and its right dual is precisely the ORIGINAL three ordinary caps ell^S. Therefore, with Lambda=ell^S W^tensor3, D(U)=gamma^(-3)Lambda, Lambda=gamma^3 s D(Theta). (5) Both U and Lambda are nonzero at every odd N, since A_N is the proved nonzero quartic scalar. The original ordinary white packet V in the unscaled W coordinates satisfies conjugate(V)=N^6 Lambda. This proves its precise dual relation; it does not assume V=U or V=Vm. ## 2. The ordinary closed pairing is zero, despite nonzero vertices Write Theta_c and lambda_c for the third magnetic slices of Theta and D(Theta). Let T_(s,t)=sum_(a,b) Theta_(a,b,s)D(Theta)_(a,b,t). Integer H=0 support makes T diagonal. The ordinary E equations for the invariant column and covector imply, for 1<=r<=d, k_r lambda_r E_12=-e_r lambda_(r-1), k_(r-1) E_12 Theta_(r-1)=-e_r Theta_r. Here k_r=xQ^(-r) and every e_r is nonzero. Pairing these identities gives T_rr/T_(r-1,r-1)=k_(r-1)/k_r whenever interpreted as the cleared equality. Hence K T is scalar, with NO division by T_rr. Its scalar can also be computed finitely. The top-edge Clebsch identity is W_(d-a)(d,m-a)=q^(m^2)h_a, 0<=a<=m. (6) To prove it, start at W_d(d,m)=q^(m^2), apply the actual E relation at first physical color d, and use factorial reflection. The resulting factor is Q^(ma)F_m F_(d-a)/(F_(m-a)F_d); its root phase converts it exactly to h_a. There is no new scalar connection constant. Equations(2),(4),(6) give T_dd=gamma x^(-d)q^(-m^2) sum_a x^a beta(m,a)^2 =gamma x. The last sum is the finite Vandermonde sum N/F_m^2. Since k_d=x^-1, K T=gamma I, D(Theta)Theta=Tr T=gamma Tr(K^-1)=0. (7) Consequently Lambda U=0 exactly. This is the ordinary q-dimension zero in its actual magnetic contraction, not a claim that either vertex vanishes. Replacing it by a positive Euclidean contraction would destroy this cancellation. The open tangle obtained by cutting that third edge is K T in these left/right duality conventions. The K factor is the recorded pivotal clock from the same snakes; (7) also verifies directly that the open map is a Hopf endomorphism. Its normalized marked closure is gamma, since the original marked unknot has value one. ## 3. Transfer the physical mark through the actual simple projector Let E_St=W pi be the FULL isolated -2 Casimir projector. The actual central circle is L_St=N E_St. Its appropriately oriented ordinary partial traces are sum_b K_b (E_St)_(a b;c b)=delta_(a,c), sum_a K_a^(-1)(E_St)_(a b;a e)=delta_(b,e). (8) Here is a root-safe proof, rather than a guessed positive resolution. Lift only this projector to the ordinary generic highest-weight-d pair. Its central summand is again the highest-weight-d module. The Casimir projector is regular at the odd root: its eigenvalue -2 collides with no other pair eigenvalue, so every projector denominator is a unit there. Its typed partial trace is a Hopf endomorphism of V_N, hence scalar. Taking the generic full pivotal trace gives scalar [N]_q=[N]_q, so the scalar is one away from the root and remains one by regular specialization. This proves(8) with the original root duality. The same argument shows equality of the root scalar obtained by cutting a physical V_N component or its embedded central V_N edge: the generic quantum dimensions are IDENTICAL, and all relevant coupons have a regular lift. No arbitrary modified-trace axiom is assumed. At odd root the usual generic pivotal maps specialize to the recorded ones, since K^N=I on V_N and K^(1-N)=K. Root marked closure of an open scalar t I is exactly t, by the direct identity m p=1 with m_(a,b)=x^b/N^2. This is the actual unrestricted marked source, not a replacement by an ordinary cap. This generic lift proves a FIXED-ROOT identity only. It does not identify the original moving-q normal germ of the complete circle with a value-only projector or authorize differentiation of it. Other Casimir channels and their original normals remain separate. ## 4. Exact marked two-vertex central scalar Use the actual two-vertex, three-edge source of the branching note, with one original marked cap and all three edge circles projected to their odd simple Steinberg summand. Contract EVERY magnetic index before estimating. The open effective scalar of U and Lambda is, from(1),(5),(7), gamma^4 s^2=q^(10m^2)A_N^2=|A_N|^2. (9) Indeed A_N=q^[m(2-m)]S_N with S_N positive, and the remaining phase is q^[8m^2+4m]=q^(4mN)=1. Each of the three actual central circles contributes N, while(8) transports the original marked cut without an extra dimension. Thus the ORIGINAL raw marked central contribution is EXACTLY Z_St=N^3 |A_N|^2 =(1/16)exp(2Nj0)[1+O(1/N)]. (10) For edge twists R^(e_i)L_St multiply(10) by the literal full-Cartan unit phase omega_m^(e_1+e_2+e_3). Any recorded external line chi_N stays outside. Equation(10) is not the full graph source with the other joint channels removed by fiat: it is the explicitly specified central sector of an original source decomposition. This is a concrete coherent contraction that removes the extra magnetic growth of the black CD norm. It does not make the original marked WHITE tensor equal to the black tensor, or furnish a sharp norm bound for arbitrary six-port sewing. The paired/even analogue still needs its own normal-current calculation. A complete graph also retains all other channels, phases and possible cancellations. The [focused exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_central_black_white_marked_contraction.py) passes seven odd levels N=3,...,15: literal right-dual Clebsch maps, nonzero ordinary white rows and zero closed pairing, both typed physical partial traces, the complete magnetic cut operator, and the unrestricted original marked contraction. Nine direct physical signed full-Cartan matrix contractions independently reproduce(10). Four labeled high-precision checks calibrate its scalar prefactor. The duality and regular-projector arguments above prove the general identities; the finite range is supplementary.

title: What simplifies at the geometric endpoint, and a magnetic gauge obstruction
text: # What simplifies at the geometric endpoint, and a magnetic gauge obstruction 30 October 2026. At every ODD level, fixing all complete-circle channels to the genuine simple endpoint makes each retained half twist an explicit scalar. The local q-Hahn critical equation also has no saddle collision on its physical endpoint domain. Nevertheless the actual central black spin tensor cannot be made entrywise positive by separate nonzero gauges on its three magnetic legs, already at N=3. The obstruction is an exact gauge-invariant six-entry ratio. It does not rule out a larger coherent resummation or a positive final scalar. It identifies why selecting endpoint channels and adjusting separate leg phases is not itself a general positive-source proof. ## 1. All retained half twists become known endpoint scalars Let N=2m+1, d=2m, q=exp(pi i/N), x=q^d and kappa=q^(d^2/2). The complete-circle node c_m=-2 is SIMPLE. Its physical summand is the actual intertwiner W:V_N->V_N tensor V_N of the [central Clebsch theorem](actual_trivalent_steinberg_central_anchor.md), with genuine dual pi=W^dagger P and pi W=I. Its projector is E_St=W pi, and L_(N,m)=N E_St, E_St^2=E_St, R E_St=omega_m E_St, omega_m=kappa (-1)^m q^[m(m+1)], |omega_m|=1. (1) Therefore for any original fixed ordered plat or source-certified matching circuit, its simultaneous endpoint contribution satisfies Z_endpoint(epsilon)=omega_m^(sum_i epsilon_i) Z_endpoint(0), (2) before the independently specified exterior framing line is restored. All cups, caps, the original unrestricted marked cut and wire ordering are unchanged. Equation (2) is just an all-input scalar identity on each actual endpoint image; it does not use positivity or replace a structural crossing elsewhere in the diagram. At even N the last folded node is DOUBLE and L_N is nilpotent there. Equation (1) must not be copied to that level as a projector identity. Its actual first-normal source is required, as in the existing even central black/white calculations. ## 2. The endpoint local saddle roots do not collide For the raw physical q-Hahn phase in the [augmented-plat compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md), put T=exp(2pi i tau), U=exp(2pi i upsilon), and let Z be the exponentiated internal summation variable. At the continuum endpoint xi=j/N->1/2, its Jc=exp(2pi i xi) equals -1. The exact candidate quadratic from that LEADING phase simplifies to [U(T+1)-4T]Z^2+2U(T-1)Z+U(T+1)=0. (3) Its discriminant is Delta=16TU(T+1-U). (4) On the entire real physical domain 1/2<=tau<=1, 0<=upsilon<=tau, one has |T+1-U|>=1, hence |Delta|>=16. Indeed, with phi=2pi tau and psi=2pi upsilon, |1+exp(i phi)-exp(i psi)|^2-1 =4cos(phi/2)[cos(phi/2)-cos(psi-phi/2)]>=0. (5) Here cos(phi/2)<=0, while |psi-phi/2|<=phi/2<=pi makes the second factor nonpositive. The quadratic coefficient also has modulus at least 4-|T+1|>=2. Thus both roots remain simple; no division by a vanishing quadratic coefficient or hidden branch collision occurs on this domain. At tau=1/2 a root can be zero, so a logarithmic chart there still needs its boundary treatment. This removes one possible local obstruction. It does NOT select which root the actual finite q-Hahn sum carries. For an interior endpoint state with 1/2<tau<1, its internal Fourier derivative still has argument pi(tau-1/2), strictly between zero and pi/2. Hence the raw summation does not have a real interior saddle. A complex source deformation or an exact resummation is still needed. ## 3. An exact N=3 obstruction to positive magnetic leg gauges Use the ACTUAL endpoint invariant Theta=(W tensor I)p, Theta_(a,b,c)=N x^-c W_(d-c)(a,b), a+b+c=3m, (6) with the original cup p. The central black vertex is a known NONZERO scalar times Theta, as proved by its finite quartic transform. No scalar is inferred here from an unknown graph evaluation. At N=3, m=1, q=(1+i sqrt(3))/2 and x=q^2. The actual highest vector is W_0=|0,1>+q|1,0>; its descendants are W_r=F_pair W_(r-1)/(1-Q^r), F_pair=F tensor I+K^-1 tensor F, F|a>=(1-Q^(a+1))|a+1>, K|a>=x Q^-a |a>. These finite equations and (6) give the six NONZERO entries | Magnetic triple | Actual Theta entry | |---|---:| | (2,1,0) | 3q | | (1,2,0) | 3 | | (0,2,1) | -3 | | (0,1,2) | 3q^2 | | (1,0,2) | -3 | | (2,0,1) | 3 | Consequently Theta_210 Theta_021 Theta_102 / (Theta_120 Theta_012 Theta_201) =q^-1=(1-i sqrt(3))/2, (7) which is not real. Under ANY separate nonzero leg gauges Theta_abc -> A_a B_b C_c Theta_abc, the numerator and denominator of (7) contain exactly the same multiset of labels on EACH leg. Every gauge factor therefore cancels. A common vertex scalar cancels too. If every nonzero coefficient could be made positive real, (7) would be positive real, a contradiction. This obstruction allows arbitrary nonzero complex diagonal gauges, not just unit phases. Reversing or conjugating the displayed ratio does not make it real. Thus the actual central BLACK tensor already prevents the proposed independent-leg positive normalization. The known endpoint half-twist scalars in (2) do not change this ratio. No information about the marked white tensor was suppressed to obtain the obstruction. ## 4. What this does and does not rule out The actual ordinary white and marked white packets are distinct from the black tensor and must stay in the complete source. The source- certified two-vertex contractions have already been resummed to positive expressions at both parities; those proofs sum additional indices and retain the original mark. They are fully consistent with (7), which concerns entrywise magnetic positivity before such sums. For an arbitrary fixed matching graph or plat, the next step is a COHERENT resummation of its original contracted endpoint tensors, or a controlled complex saddle with that source. A full non-diagonal basis change could also be investigated, but its actual inverse, exponential norm and transported marked source would need estimates. Neither the local no-collision statement (4) nor endpoint half-twist scalarity (2) supplies that global comparison. In particular (7) does not disprove an arbitrary-plat volume limit, positivity of a resummed scalar, or a possible geometric period. It excludes one precise proposed shortcut while retaining the actual root phases and source normalization. The displayed counterexample concerns N=3: it rules out an all-level independent-leg normalization, but by itself does not classify the larger levels or exclude an asymptotic normalization with a controlled phase error. title: The actual endpoint q-connection, clock feedback and its source extension
text: # The actual endpoint q-connection, clock feedback and its source extension 28 October 2026. The charged polynomial has a flat rank-one q-connection whose numerator and denominator degrees are bounded by the diagram valencies, independently of N. Macroscopic lengths Q^L are retained. Its correct source Ward identity uses a specified endpoint-DELETED polynomial. It is not a polynomial annihilator of the top-degree state obtained by simply multiplying the cleared equation by that state. The original clock feedback has an exact compatible mixed transport. These identities retain all macro defects and peripheral factors, but they do NOT imply a nonzero selected geometric component. We locate precisely the information lost by localizing the actual nilpotent source. ## 1. Exact bounded-degree endpoint connection Use the original charged source, before or after its exact closure contractions, with d=N-1 and Q primitive of order N. Write its fixed-clock polynomial, including every extracted nonzero scalar, as P_h=gamma_h product_i X_i^(mu_i) product_e B_(L_e)(X_(u_e),X_(v_e);a_e), B_L(U,V;a)=product_(r=0)^(L-1)(U-Q^r aV). (1) Nonloop blocks have u_e!=v_e, 1<=L_e<=d. Actual self-loops have been evaluated as their exact scalar times X_i^L; a zero scalar means the actual sector is zero and is not localized. All gamma_h, original clock factors W_h, chi_N, pivots and Cartan/framing phases remain. The original functional is lambda(P)=[product_i X_i^d]P. Let tau_i shift X_i to QX_i. The literal block ratios are B_L(Q U,V;a)/B_L(U,V;a) =Q^L (U-Q^(-1)aV)/(U-Q^(L-1)aV), B_L(U,Q V;a)/B_L(U,V;a) =(U-Q^L aV)/(U-aV). (2) Define D_i=product_(u_e=i)(X_i-Q^(L_e-1)a_e X_(v_e)) *product_(v_e=i)(X_(u_e)-a_e X_i), N_i=Q^(mu_i+sum_(u_e=i)L_e) product_(u_e=i)(X_i-Q^(-1)a_e X_(v_e)) *product_(v_e=i)(X_(u_e)-Q^(L_e)a_e X_i). (3) Then EXACTLY in the ordinary polynomial ring, D_i tau_i P_h=N_i P_h. (4) Each degree is the number of incident nonloop BLOCKS, not the sum of their lengths. It is bounded for a fixed diagram. The Q^L coefficients are not replaced by one when L is proportional to N. Self-loops contribute the displayed Q^mu, rather than being counted twice in (2). On the regular locus these ratios define a flat rank-one connection: R_i=N_i/D_i=tau_i P_h/P_h, (tau_j R_i)R_j=(tau_i R_j)R_i, product_(r=0)^(N-1) tau_i^r R_i=1. (5) These are actual identities with a specified global section P_h. Flatness by itself is not new knot holonomy or a source nonvanishing theorem. In particular (5) has no extra condition on Fermat centers. ## 2. The NONTRIVIAL original source current Every factor of D_i in (3) is the last factor of an outgoing block or the first factor of an incoming block. Therefore D_i divides the ordinary polynomial P_h, with multiplicities as specified by its factorization. Put P_(h,i)^del=P_h/D_i. (6) This is an endpoint-deletion operation on the proved polynomial, not an inverse in the nilpotent algebra. Equation (4) is equivalently tau_i P_h=N_i P_(h,i)^del. Since lambda(tau_i P)=Q^d lambda(P), the exact source current is lambda((N_i-Q^d D_i)P_(h,i)^del)=0. (7) For a Laurent-polynomial insertion F its retained version is lambda(F N_i P_(h,i)^del) =Q^d lambda((tau_i^(-1)F) P_h). (8) The coefficient here is the specified Laurent-residue source whenever F has negative exponents. No claim that arbitrary such insertions are original finite-head coupons is needed. At F=1 equation (7) preserves the original charge and is already nontrivial. In contrast, lambda((N_i-Q^dD_i)P_h)=0 is normally VACUOUS: the inserted homogeneous numerator has positive degree and P_h is already at the total top degree. Confusing it with (7) loses the actual endpoint source extension. Equation (7) survives multiplication by the full W_h and summation over the actual clocks, with its h-dependent coefficients and endpoint-deleted state retained. ## 3. Exact mixed clock transport with the actual underhistory Use the independent coefficient C_h(R)=[Y^h]F_N^0(R,Y) and actual matrix T of [the feedback theorem](actual_clock_feedback_normal_form.md). For a crossing j at position r in its overbridge, increasing h_j by one decreases n_(r-1) by one and increases n_r by one. At independent primitive parameters the finite binomial recurrence gives C_(h+e_j)(R)=b_j(h,R) C_h(R), b_j=(t_r/t_(r-1)) *(1-Q^(n_(r-1)))/(1-z_(r-1)Q^(n_(r-1)-1)) *(1-z_rQ^(n_r))/(1-Q^(n_r+1)). (9) Use its cleared form if a displayed numerator or denominator vanishes. Inside the monotone simplex the factorial denominators are units; the original boundary support remains part of the statement.
