No cyclic continuation across h=0,d is inferred from a zero-over-zero recurrence. For S_h(R)=C_h(R Q^(T h)) define the primitive parameter shift Sigma_j R_i=R_i Q^(T_(ij)). The ACTUAL transport is S_(h+e_j)(R) =b_j(h,R Q^(T(h+e_j))) S_h(Sigma_j R). (10) It is not multiplication of S_h at the old parameters by (9). Equation (10) changes the other event endpoints, bridge parameters and closure source exactly by the actual underclock column T_(.,j). It follows by substituting RQ^(T(h+e_j)) in (9). Thus the joint anchor/clock connection is the exact pullback of the independent one, with all causal histories and negative self-clock shifts retained. Its compatibility is an identity of the actual functions, not an assumption that the a_j are independent physical clocks. For a regular leading coefficient action S_0, this produces the feedback term T^T partial_(log R)S_0 in clock stationarity, as derived in the feedback note. The anchor equations obtained from (3) likewise retain the macro endpoint Q^L. Those are necessary equations for a regular stationary contribution; they do not determine its intersection with the original relative source. There is also a source-level affine mark which its exponentiated classical equation alone cannot read. On a regular branch with log P_h=N S+o(N), equation (2) has leading ratio exp(2*pi*i X_i partial_(X_i)S). The original coefficient contour has the stationary equation X_i partial_(X_i)S=1, since d/N tends to one. But Q^d tends to one, so the bounded-degree leading q-equation retains only exp(2*pi*i X_i partial_(X_i)S)=1. Its integer lift has to be fixed by the original charge window and source, not by this equation alone. The exact homogeneous alias theorem fixes that window on the WHOLE finite coefficient; it does not authorize replacing every classical integer branch by its required lift before the period is compared. ## 4. Why localization does not select the nilpotent source The actual source algebra at its jet fiber is A_0=K[X_1,...,X_k]/(X_1^N,...,X_k^N). Every positive-degree linear form, and hence every nonconstant D_i, is nilpotent in A_0. Localizing A_0 by such a D_i gives the ZERO ring. This follows directly from D_i^M=0: after adjoining its inverse one gets 1=0. Therefore the rational connection R_i cannot simply be restricted as an invertible connection to the original jet source. The endpoint-deleted polynomial (6) is still a legitimate specified lift in the ordinary ring. It is not determined by division of the class of P_h in A_0, where D_i is a zero divisor. Keeping (6) is the minimal extension needed by the actual cleared current (7). There is an additional exact loss of data if the source is taken first. The homogeneous degree-kd class is [P_h]=lambda(P_h) Omega, Omega=product_i X_i^d. On this line tau_i acts as the constant Q^d, independent of L_e, a_e and their macro limits. Also N_i[P_h]=D_i[P_h]=0 whenever their degree is positive. Thus the geometric endpoint information in (3) lives BEFORE the socle projection, in its stated factorized source extension, not in a nontrivial localized connection on that one line. Generic nonzero Fermat fibers avoid this localization problem and have the exact same original period. But invertibility of P_h or of its endpoints there does not imply that its specified Fourier/residue coefficient is nonzero. The next actual example retains macro defects. ## 5. Actual hyperbolic-source sector with macro defects and zero period Use the original figure-eight braid [1,-2,1,-2] and its actual clocks h=(d,0,0,0). After the exact three closure contractions, write its four remaining anchors as X_0,X_4,X_5,X_6. Up to the retained NONZERO scalar, its actual polynomial consists of the four full blocks B_d(X_5,X_0;Q), B_d(X_6,X_0;q^(N+3)), B_d(X_5,X_4;q^(N+1)), B_d(X_0,X_6;q^(N-1)). (11) Its incidence defects S_i-2d are +d at X_0, -d at X_4 and zero at X_5,X_6. Thus this test does NOT assume small or vanishing defects. Its original selected coefficient is zero for EVERY N. The first full block contracts X_5=X_0. The third then contracts X_0=xX_4, since q^(N+1)Q^(-1)=x. The other two become B_d(X_6,X_4;Q) and a nonzero scalar times B_d(X_4,X_6;1). Contracting the first gives X_6=X_4; the remaining block contains X_4-X_4 and is zero. Every contraction is the actual arbitrary-exterior source identity, with its scalar retained. No bare geometric quotient or unknown knot period is used. This is also a special case of the separately proved first-cut clock support in [the alternating-source theorem](actual_alternating_balanced_source.md); the contraction above is included as a diagnostic of the connection, not as a new knot-specific selection mechanism. Nevertheless the polynomial in (11) is nonzero in the ordinary ring. Choose generic independent nonzero Fermat centers so that C_u!=a_e^N C_v for every edge. Then ALL its factors, endpoint denominators and P_h itself are units on that semisimple fiber. Its flat rank-one connection (5), actual T feedback and original source currents remain exact, while its selected period is still zero by center independence of the original homogeneous source. This is not a counterexample to a geometric-sector theorem: the full knot sum has other clocks, and no geometric contribution is claimed for (11). It proves that a nonzero actual section, a regular flat bounded-degree connection, source Ward equations and retained macro defects do not ALONE force nonzero source projection. ## 6. Critical-path conclusion The endpoint connection and mixed clock transport are exact tools for the ORIGINAL state, with bounded endpoint complexity and full macro coefficients. They do not yet prove anything stronger about geometric selection than the previously known regular critical correspondence. In particular there is no new broad-class volume lower bound here. A successful further argument must preserve the endpoint extension (6)-(8), the clock windows and T transport (10), and compute a nonzero projection of their WHOLE original relative class to the marked geometric branch. Specializing or localizing the socle first destroys precisely the data which that comparison needs. The example (11) prevents replacing the missing computation by rank-one flatness. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_charged_connection.py) checks the actual endpoint identities and source currents, original primitive clock recurrences and feedback, and the all-N macro-defect source annihilation (11). No literature proof is used as a premise.

title: The actual charged source has the same residue on Fermat and nilpotent fibers
text: # The actual charged source has the same residue on Fermat and nilpotent fibers 28 October 2026. The whole-source coefficient proved in [the charged bridge-flow theorem](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md) has a canonical finite-flat algebraic realization. At each fixed level, its cyclotomic-grid residue and its nilpotent jet evaluation are exactly the SAME functional, with no unknown scalar or chosen asymptotic branch. The pairing remains nondegenerate when all Fermat centers vanish. This makes a part of the proposed algebraic-period/jet viewpoint literal. It does not identify residues at different levels, select the geometric regulator, or prove a volume limit. The algebra and the state class both depend on N. ## 1. A fixed-level finite-flat Frobenius algebra Fix N>=2, d=N-1, the actual primitive Q and the coefficient field K containing Q, the original half-root and source scalars. For k anchors put R=K[C_1,...,C_k], A_N=R[X_1,...,X_k]/(X_i^N-C_i, all i). (1) Its basis over R is X^a with 0<=a_i<=d. Reduction by the monic relations is unique, so A_N is free of rank N^k; in particular it is flat even when some or all C_i vanish. Define lambda_C(P)=[X_1^d ... X_k^d] (P reduced in (1)). (2) For two basis monomials the EXACT multiplication pairing is lambda_C(X^a X^b)=product_i delta_(a_i+b_i,d). (3) Indeed a_i+b_i<=2d. If reduction by X_i^N occurs, its remaining exponent is at most d-1, so it cannot contribute to (2). Thus the Gram matrix is an anti-diagonal permutation matrix, INDEPENDENT of every C_i, with determinant a unit. This proves A_N -> Hom_R(A_N,R), f -> (g -> lambda_C(fg)) (4) is an isomorphism of A_N-modules on every fiber. This is a specified Frobenius functional, not an unspecified nonzero linear form. Generators of this dual module form a torsor under A_N^units; the original source fixes the generator (2). ## 2. The selected Fermat residue extends to the actual nilpotent jet When every C_i is nonzero, the roots are simple. The Jacobian of f_i=X_i^N-C_i is N^k product_i X_i^d. Direct evaluation gives lambda_C(P) =Res_(all f_i=0) P(X) dX_1...dX_k/(f_1...f_k) =1/N^k sum_(X_i^N=C_i) P(X)/product_i X_i^d. (5) The residue means the sum of normalized local product-circle integrals. It agrees with (2) on every basis monomial, hence on all polynomials modulo (1). The coefficient and the Jacobian fix its sign and normalization. At C=0 the algebra is A_N(0)=K[X_1,...,X_k]/(X_1^N,...,X_k^N). (6) Its socle, the elements annihilated by all X_i, is exactly the one-dimensional line generated by Omega=product_i X_i^d. The same lambda is its top-coefficient functional, lambda_0(Omega)=1, or equivalently the local residue P dX/product_i X_i^N at zero. Formula (3) proves that the source pairing has NOT degenerated, although the fiber has become a nonreduced jet algebra. For a homogeneous polynomial P of total degree kd there is the stronger exact identity lambda_C(P)=[X^d]P=lambda_0(P), for EVERY C. (7) Any use of one monic relation reduces total X-degree by N; such a term cannot reach the top monomial of total degree kd. This is the algebraic version of the whole-source alias argument, and includes polynomials with large degrees in individual anchors. The ORIGINAL invariant therefore has the identical descriptions K_N=chi_N/N sum_(h over-monotone) W_h lambda_C(P_h) =chi_N/N sum_(h over-monotone) W_h lambda_0(P_h). (8) All clock weights, closure adapters and pivots are those already proved in the charged-flow theorem. No raw full-Psi continuation is substituted for this polynomial. Equation (8) is an equality of algebraic periods at each level, rather than an inference from a limit or an arbitrary choice of a quantum source. ## 3. A general cyclotomic annihilation rule for the actual source Let i!=j and alpha,beta be nonzero. In the nilpotent fiber, product_(r=0)^(N-1)(alpha X_i-Q^r beta X_j) =alpha^N X_i^N-beta^N X_j^N=0. (9) Consequently, if the actual event polynomial P_h contains a complete Q-orbit of linear factors on a pair of anchors, its entire selected coefficient is ZERO. This is an exact rule on the actual class, not an absolute-value estimate or a generic quotient killing a geometric full-function section. By (7) the same selected value vanishes on EVERY original regular Fermat grid. At nonzero centers the product in (9) equals the scalar alpha^N C_i-beta^N C_j rather than zero. There is no contradiction: its remaining polynomial has degree kd-N, and lambda_C kills that lower degree. Thus applying (9) to the selected period is justified by the whole homogeneous source, not by declaring that scalar zero in an individual grid summand. For the actual event factors, coefficients are explicit half-root phases. Group factors by their unordered anchor pair and their ratio modulo Q. Covering all N phases of one Q-orbit detects (9) before coefficient expansion. This is a sufficient vanishing test; failure of this test is NOT a nonvanishing theorem. More complicated cycle cancellations and the remaining h sum are still present. The recently proved two-crossing winding selection in [the bridge-phase theorem](actual_bridge_charge_phase.md) uses the same full-cycle polynomial 1-t^N in its one-variable coefficient calculation. The multianchor rule (9) does not require that local bigon presentation, but it also does not exhaust the source kernel. ## 4. What rigidity does and does not establish The source line is fixed across the finite-flat family (1), and the full original polynomial classes have center-independent periods. This resolves the ambiguity of transporting that source from regular cyclotomic points to its nilpotent jet fiber. It does NOT imply that the original class has a nonzero projection to a geometric period. The perfect pairing (3) allows many nonzero elements with lambda=0; (9) gives source-relevant exact cancellations. Also N^k, the socle degree k(N-1), the clock domain, and P_h all vary with N. Fixed-level flatness or the source torsor alone therefore supplies no cross-level growth estimate. A comparison with the marked Bloch regulator and a nonzero selected geometric coefficient are still required for the volume conjecture. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_charged_socle_and_fermat_source.py): exact Frobenius pairings, grid/nilpotent residue normalization, homogeneous center independence, and complete-cycle vanishing tests on original charged bridge polynomials.

title: Exact underclock feedback and charge elimination in the ORIGINAL source
text: # Exact underclock feedback and charge elimination in the ORIGINAL source 28 October 2026. This note promotes the independent-parameter bridge generating function to an exact whole-word identity, retaining the actual UNDER clock feedback. The additional operation is an explicit diagonal root-of-unity Gaussian, equivalently a normalized finite Fourier kernel. The bridge charges can then be eliminated with their fugacities retained. This does not prove geometric selection or a volume lower bound. In particular, ordinary evaluation of the independent generating function before this feedback changes the original scalar. We prove the precise failure rather than treating its parameters as independently adjustable. ## 1. Original source and the actual feedback matrix Use the complete original root family N>=2, d=N-1, Q=q^2=exp(2*pi*i/N), x=-q^(-1). The original external dimension/framing factor is chi_N; every crossing still contains its original kappa factor. For any signed braid word W on b heads, take the overbridge/closure events and k=B+b anchor segments of [the whole charged source](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md). The original scalar source is its equation (1), not a newly chosen functional. Denote the anchor on a segment by X_s. At crossing j of sign sigma_j, with overclock h_j, the UNDER transport is z_out=x^(sigma_j) z_in Q^(-sigma_j h_j). (1) For a port v let P_v list earlier UNDER encounters on its segment and S_v=sum_(ell in P_v) sigma_ell. Then literally z_v=x^(S_v) X_(s(v)) Q^(-sum_(ell in P_v) sigma_ell h_ell). (2) Let P_j,S_j denote these data at the UNDER INPUT of crossing j. The actual conditioned overbridge parameter a_j is alpha_j/u_j, where u_j is the UNDER OUTPUT and alpha_j=Q^(-h_j)/x, sigma_j=+1, alpha_j=Qx, sigma_j=-1. Substituting (1) and (2) gives the exact formula a_j=Q^(delta_j) x^(-S_j) X_(s(j))^(-1) Q^[sum_(ell in P_j) sigma_ell h_ell-epsilon_j h_j], delta_j=(1+sigma_j)/2, epsilon_j=(1-sigma_j)/2. (3) Thus the positive a_j has no self-clock dependence, while the negative one has the compulsory factor Q^(-h_j). Both signs retain all earlier UNDER clocks. These facts follow by cancellation of alpha_j with its own transport; no geometric central relation has been imposed. Introduce independent primitive Laurent variables R_i consisting of one A_j for each a_j and one Z_v for every event endpoint port. Equations (2)-(3) have the uniform form R_i(actual)=rho_i X^(v_i) Q^((T h)_i). (4) The integer matrix T and the monomials rho_i X^(v_i) are diagram data. For A_j the row is rho_j=Q^(delta_j)x^(-S_j), v_j=-e_(s(j)), T_(j,ell)=sigma_ell for ell in P_j, T_(j,j)=-epsilon_j, all other entries zero. (5) For an endpoint Z_v its row has rho_v=x^(S_v), v_v=e_(s(v)), and entries -sigma_ell for ell in P_v. No future UNDER crossing enters (5). Closure ports use their whole actual segment prefix, as in (2). ## 2. Independent event polynomials with charge fugacities Put F_n=(Q;Q)_n and define the finite formal series U_z(v)=sum_(n=0)^d (z;Q)_n v^n/F_n. (6) Take one overbridge e with crossings j_1,...,j_m in its physical order, signs sigma_r, and independent primitives A_r=A_(j_r), V=Z_in, W=Z_out. Define w_r=sum_(s<=r) sigma_s and t_0=1, t_r=(-1)^r q^(2+w_r)/(V A_r), z_0=Q^2x/(A_1 V), z_r=x^(-1) A_r/A_(r+1) for 1<=r<m, z_m=A_m W. Let Y_(e,r)=product_(s<=r) Y_(j_s), Y_(e,0)=1. The independent, event-normalized generating polynomial is E_e^0(R,Y)=N kappa^(w_m) [v_e^d] product_(r=0)^m U_(z_r)(v_e t_r Y_(e,r)). (7) The coefficient of Y^h is N times the entire actual bridge formula with independent parameters: n_0=d-h_1, n_r=h_r-h_(r+1), n_m=h_m. Indeed the exponent of Y_(j_s) is sum_(r>=s)n_r=h_s. This is exactly equation (3) of [the complete bridge-phase proof](actual_bridge_charge_phase.md), with every scalar, sign, Gaussian phase and endpoint retained. For a closure event on head i use its ORIGINAL numerator kernel, including its denominator and pivot but omitting only the explicit 1/N: C_i^0=eta_i Z_in^(-d) sum_(a=0)^d Z_in^(d-a)(t_i Z_out)^a, (eta_1,t_1)=(1,1), (eta_i,t_i)=(x/x^N,Q^(-1)) for i>1. (8) Set F_N^0(R,Y)=product_e E_e^0 product_i C_i^0. Each crossing clock occurs once and has range 0,...,d. Its coefficient remains a Laurent polynomial in the independent primitives R. No clock is yet summed after falsely freezing the actual spectator variables. ## 3. Exact source-preserving feedback theorem Define on Laurent monomials the linear operator G_T(R^nu Y^h)=Q^(nu^T T h) R^nu Y^h. (9) For every signed braid word and its original source, K_N=chi_N/N * CT_X [G_T F_N^0(R,Y)]_(Y=1, R_i=rho_i X^(v_i)). (10) In particular the full normalization is fixed by the original period, not by division by an unknown knot invariant. Proof. On its Y^h coefficient, (9) is exactly substitution (4) in every primitive monomial. Equation (7) then gives the actual bridge, and (8) gives the actual boundary event. There are k events and each has its original factor 1/N. Every original anchor orbit sum gives N times its constant term: after clearing the single event-input denominator, the numerator is nonnegative of total degree kd. If an orbit kept exponents e_s-d=N l_s, then e_s>=0 gives l_s>=0 and homogeneity gives sum l_s=0. Thus all aliases vanish, exactly as in the whole-source theorem. Its N^k cancels the k event factors 1/N. The remaining 1/N in (10) is the original averaged first-cut source. This proves (10), for links as well as knots and at arbitrary bridge number. It does not make sectorwise replacements of the marked row. The feedback has an exact finite Fourier realization. If m is the number of crossings, then for any polynomial with these clock ranges [G_T F(R,Y)]_(Y=1) =N^(-m) sum_(lambda,eta in (Z/N)^m) Q^(-lambda dot eta) F(R_i Q^((T eta)_i), Y_j=Q^(lambda_j)). (11) For a monomial the lambda sum enforces eta=h modulo N. Since h_j is already in 0,...,d, it gives its actual value, and the remaining phase is precisely (9). This verifies both the exponent and N^(-m), rather than N^(-2m). There are no hidden central or peripheral normalizers. On the coefficient basis G_T is diagonal unitary. That observation controls its coefficient norm only; the actual charged evaluation and clock sum can still cancel. ## 4. The bridge charges can be eliminated with feedback retained Formula (11) does allow the bridge charge sums to be performed exactly, but it requires ALL the Fourier fugacities. Choose the representatives 0<=lambda_j<N, put Y_j=Q^(lambda_j), and on a bridge write Y_r=product_(s<=r)Y_(j_s), Y_0=1, T_end=(-1)^m q^(2+w_m) W/V. Then its v-series in (7) is, modulo v^N, EXACTLY product_(r=0)^m U_(z_r)(v t_r Y_r) =U_(T_end Y_m)(v) product_(r=1)^m (v t_r Y_(r-1);Q)_(lambda_(j_r)) /(v t_r Y_(r-1);Q)_(epsilon_r). (12) The denominators in (12) have constant term one and hence a unique inverse modulo v^N. Equation (12) leaves just one coefficient [v^d] per bridge, together with the explicit Fourier feedback (11). It is a uniform charge elimination, not a knot-specific summation identity. Proof. For the finite Euler series P, U_z(v)=P(zv)/P(v) modulo v^N, and P(Qv)=P(v)/(1-v). The actual bridge parameters obey z_(r-1)t_(r-1)=Q^(epsilon_r)t_r, z_m t_m=T_end. Cancel consecutive P factors while retaining Y_r/Y_(r-1)=Q^lambda. Their remaining ratio is P(Q^epsilon w)/P(Q^lambda w)=(w;Q)_lambda/(w;Q)_epsilon, which proves (12). Lambda=0 recovers the independent-parameter telescoping, but the full original source requires (11), not that single Fourier fiber. ## 5. A precise obstruction to pre-feedback telescoping Evaluation at Y=1 is NOT a quotient respected by G_T. Whenever T_(ij) is nonzero modulo N, [(Y_j-1)R_i]_(Y=1)=0, [G_T((Y_j-1)R_i)]_(Y=1)=(Q^(T_(ij))-1)R_i !=0. (13) Thus the actual feedback does not descend to the ideal (Y_j-1). This is a direct obstruction to replacing the independent bridge generating function by its pre-summed Y=1 value, then attempting to restore the spectators afterwards. The audit below also checks that this omission changes full original pivotal scalars, rather than merely an arbitrary auxiliary observable. Although the histories in (5) are causal, the operation is not nilpotent transport: the phases in (9) have order up to N. Causal ordering therefore does not supply a uniform finite unipotence argument for the original clock sum. The exact conjugation laws are G_T R_i G_T^(-1)=R_i Q^(sum_j T_(ij) E_(Y_j)), G_T Y_j G_T^(-1)=Y_j Q^(sum_i T_(ij) E_(R_i)), (14) where E is the integer exponent operator. They make the missing coupling explicit. In a regular semiclassical chart, write nu/N=v, h/N=H. Feedback contributes the full phase exp(2*pi*i*N*v^T T H). Equivalently it shears logarithmic coordinates log R -> log R+2*pi*i*T H, log Y -> log Y+2*pi*i*T^T v. (15) For example, if F_N^0 has a smooth leading log action S_0 and the finite Fourier sum admits a critical description, its internal stationary equations are exactly H=partial_(log Y) S_0, Lambda=T^T partial_(log R) S_0, log Y=2*pi*i*Lambda, log R=log R_base+2*pi*i*T H. (16) The charged CT also imposes sum_i (v_i)_a partial_(log R_i)S_0=0 at every anchor. These are the feedback/implicit equations with the actual source. They contain the terms omitted by varying bridge charges with independent spectators. Equations (15)-(16) are a stationary interpretation of the exact (10)-(11), not a proof that the original contour meets a particular geometric branch. ## 6. What is proved and what remains The original whole period now has (i) an explicit clock-independent integer feedback matrix, (ii) a normalized Fourier realization, and (iii) an exact charge-eliminated bridge formula at every Fourier fiber. The coupled phase has not been replaced by its absolute value or by the zero-feedback fiber. No unknown multiplier has been introduced. This does not fix the selected geometric coefficient. In particular, the known surviving nonflat anchor cycles in [the exact fusion note](anchor_phase_cycles_and_exact_fusion.md) prevent a blanket argument that the remaining phase is a vertex gauge. Regular critical equations may still be compared with the previously proved holonomy/calibration equations, but neither (10) nor their implicit stationary form proves a nonzero original geometric period. No new knot is claimed to satisfy the volume conjecture here. Generic q-Weyl/determinant and quantum MacMahon approaches to knot invariants already occur in the literature; this note makes no novelty claim for that general architecture. Coverage references are [Huynh-Le](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0503296), [quantum MacMahon](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0303319), and [noncommutative Jones](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0411505). Their proofs are not premises of the identities above. ## 7. Reproducible checks [audit_actual_clock_feedback_normal_form.py](../experiments/audit_actual_clock_feedback_normal_form.py) constructs (3)-(5) without using any clock values, then independently compares the whole substituted polynomial, every primitive port, and the charged coefficient with the actual bridge-flow implementation. It sums all allowed clocks and compares with original signed R matrices and the original pivotal averaged cut. Five whole sources are checked at N=2,3. At least one changes if feedback is suppressed. The same audit checks the normalized finite Fourier delta for N=2,...,9 with positive and negative primitive exponents, and 96 complete fugacity-preserving telescopes (12), including negative crossings and the extreme residues lambda=0,N-1. These numerical checks audit the all-N proofs; they do not replace them.

title: A uniform closed route in the original Pascal-cell source
text: # A uniform closed route in the original Pascal-cell source 29 October 2026. The exact positive angle cells of the actual divided fusion maps have a simultaneous, source-admitted closed route at every crossing of ANY signed braid. Its energy is exponential. In particular, the phase-free path partition of these cells cannot itself be the sharp geometric angle partition for the figure-eight knot. Coherent contraction of the physical maps is essential before such a geometric comparison. This is about the original averaged-trace presentation AFTER its authorized whole-word degree reduction. It is not a statement about every possible pointed presentation or a surviving coherent clock sector. ## 1. Exact physical alphabet and original source Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, and x=-q^(-1). The exact [physical fusion and crossing theorem](actual_reassociation_angle_kernel.md) gives C=C'_12 and its literal inverse with entries C_(a-r,b+r;a,b)=x^(-r)[b+r choose r]_Q, C^(-1)_(a-r,b+r;a,b) =(-1)^r Q^(r(r-1)/2) C_(a-r,b+r;a,b), 0<=r<=min(a,d-b). (1) Write C_21=Flip C Flip and D_2|a,b>=(-1)^b Q^(b(b-1)/2)x^(-2b)|a,b>. The FULL original checked crossings are R_+=kappa C D_2 C_21 C^(-1), R_-=kappa^(-1) C C_21^(-1) D_2^(-1) C^(-1). (2) No physical cutoffs or common Cartan scalars have been removed. All displayed diagonals, kappa and original closing pivots have unit modulus at completeness. Both signs are included below with their actual order. For the whole original knot word W, integer total-degree conservation first gives the exact source K_N=chi_N/N Tr[(I tensor g tensor ... tensor g)W]. (3) This is [the original charged-source theorem](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md#1-use-the-original-scalar-source-before-splitting). It is used BEFORE expanding W into fusion paths. It is not a sectorwise replacement of the full marked row, nor a rule for arbitrary insertions. The original dimension/framing line chi_N remains outside (3). The physical quarter gauge G_a=N^(1/4)/sqrt(s_a), s_a=|(Q;Q)_a|, commutes with the closing pivots. Thus its tensor similarity preserves (3) exactly. The squared entry of either C or C^(-1) in this gauge is |Chat_entry|^2=N^2 w_d(r,a-r,d-a)w_d(r,b,d-b-r), w_d(i,j,k)=1/(s_i s_j s_k), i+j+k=d. (4) The operator C_21 has the same formula with the two physical heads exchanged. The inverse phases in (1) remain in the coherent word. ## 2. One closed route works for all signs and all braid positions Put N=3r+1, d=3r, r>=1, and choose the PHYSICAL initial trace state a_star=(2r,r,2r,r,...). (5) Every adjacent pair is either (2r,r) or (r,2r). At each crossing use the following transfers, listed in operator ACTION order: | input pair | right C^(-1) | middle C_21 or C_21^(-1) | left C | output pair | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | (2r,r) | r | r | 0 | (2r,r) | | (r,2r) | 0 | r | r | (r,2r) | For a negative crossing its D_2^(-1) is between the right and middle maps; for a positive crossing D_2 is between the middle and left maps. It is diagonal and never changes this route or its nonzero modulus. Each intermediate pair is (2r,r) or (r,2r), so all physical bounds in (1) hold as ORDINARY integers. Inverse maps have exactly the same support and modulus as the forward maps. Each row therefore returns the pair to its initial value. Applying the indicated row at every crossing keeps the complete physical state (5) fixed after EVERY complete R. It supplies a closed route for any braid width and any signed word, regardless of crossing order. Its original pivotal factor in (3) is nonzero and of modulus one, and its single cut factor is 1/N. This is an admitted expanded route of the complete original source, not an isolated entry without boundary gluing. ## 3. Exact energy and its uniform growth Every active transfer in the table sees a high input head 2r and a low input head r in the orientation of that C. Both triples in (4) are EXACTLY (r,r,r). Each zero transfer contributes the two triples (0,a,d-a) and (0,b,d-b), with w_d(0,a,d-a)=1/N. Thus its squared entry is exactly one. There are two active C maps per crossing, giving four regular cells. For a word with m crossings, the product of squared, quarter-gauged path entries is exactly E_route=N^(4m) w_d(r,r,r)^(4m)=N^(4m)/s_r^(12m). (6) All internal gauge factors telescope, since the route is closed. Equation (6) is therefore also its ungauged squared modulus; no endpoint gauge or source normalizer is missing. Including the literal cut coefficient changes (6) by N^(-2), and including chi_N multiplies it by |chi_N|^2. These known external factors remain explicit. Let Z_path be the positive sum of squared entries over all closed physical paths in the alphabet (2), with the original trace boundary conditions. Then Z_path>=N^(4m)w_d(r,r,r)^(4m). (7) With Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log(2sin t)dt and v_3=3Lambda(pi/3), the uniform endpoint factorial estimate gives log s_r=-(N/pi)Lambda(pi*r/N)+O(log N), lim_(N=3r+1) (1/N)log E_route=4m v_3/pi. (8) This is an exact all-r family with a proved rate, not extrapolation from a few levels. Every cell has the correct affine sum d and every physical head-flow/source constraint is satisfied. For the original figure-eight word [1,-2,1,-2], m=4 and its geometric volume is 2v_3 (two regular ideal tetrahedra). The lower rate in (8) is 16v_3/pi, whereas a sharp angle ENERGY partition has rate 2v_3/pi. Hence neither a polynomial normalization nor bounded polynomial multiplicity can identify the complete phase-free Z_path with that sharp positive geometric fiber. In particular the actual shared-spin relations alone do not imply the required geometric edge equations. ## 4. What has to remain coherent The route is NOT claimed to survive summing its internal C channels. For example, for R_+ at input (r,2r), the diagonal physical entry is zero: the literal positive R requires output first head b+k with k>=0, so returning it to r is impossible. Its nonzero expanded routes cancel exactly. For R_- the analogous statement holds at (2r,r). This is a constructive reason to perform the available complete crossing contractions before assigning an angle partition, not a new obstruction to doing so. It also prevents misidentifying (6) with an already coherently summed, nonzero original clock sector. The exact positive cells and coherent Gram remain useful. What fails is the shortcut of imposing the original physical head/source support on their phase-free path expansion and inferring a sharp geometric edge fiber from that support alone. An additional source-preserving coherent regrouping, such as complete-channel recoupling with its full mixed Gram, is necessary. This theorem does not rule out that route or a different global inner product. [Focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_closed_pascal_route_energy.py): original coproduct-derived C and inverse, full positive and negative R, both path orders, quarter metric and all regular/boundary cells, original pivotal trace conversion, and nonzero closed routes at arbitrary adjacent positions.

title: Actual Racah cluster projectors cannot share an orthogonal positive metric
text: # Actual Racah cluster projectors cannot share an orthogonal positive metric 29 October 2026. This is an exact obstruction to one proposed shortcut for higher generic normals. Even the COMPLETE analytic root clusters of the two physical Casimirs need not be orthogonal projections for any common positive Hermitian form. A seven-level source example has rank-two cluster projectors P,Q with trace(PQ)>33. The bound would be at most two for orthogonal projections in any positive metric. This does not refute the proved all-partner first-normal estimate, higher scalar bounds, or a suitably weighted nonorthogonal transport estimate. It rules out obtaining those conclusions by declaring the two actual cluster decompositions simultaneously orthogonal. ## 1. The second normal retains an actual cluster overlap Use the same generic source as the [all-partner first-normal theorem](actual_all_partner_first_normal_bound.md). For a pair of complementary internal channels write e*=N-1-e, f*=N-1-f, d_j=[2j+1], and K_ij=[N]^2 S(e_i,f_j)^2 product_faces Delta^2, e_0=e,e_1=e*, f_0=f,f_1=f*. The proved exact source-projector identity is sum_(i,j=0,1) d_(e_i)d_(f_j) K_ij =[N]^2 tr(E_e^S E_f^T), (1) where E_e^S and E_f^T are the ANALYTIC complete cluster projectors on the actual saturated invariant lattice. Each has rank two when its two channels are distinct. The trace in (1) is the ordinary local multiplicity-space trace from the source identity; the original marked exterior has not been replaced by a trace invariant. Let t=log(zeta/q), and let [t^r] denote Taylor COEFFICIENTS, rather than unnormalized derivatives. If d_(e_i)d_(f_j)=a_ij,0+a_ij,1 t+a_ij,2 t^2+..., K_ij=W_N^2+k_ij,1 t+k_ij,2 t^2+..., [N]=c_N t+O(t^2), then the second coefficient of (1) is EXACTLY sum_ij(a_ij,0 k_ij,2+a_ij,1 k_ij,1+a_ij,2 W_N^2) =c_N^2 tr(E_e^S(q) E_f^T(q)). (2) Consequently the homogeneous first-normal Ward equation cannot simply be imposed at second order. The additional overlap is a real physical source quantity, rather than a removable convention. ## 2. An exact seven-level example Take N=7, D=6, q=exp(pi i/7), a=b=c=d=2, e=f=2, e*=f*=4. The ordinary invariant channel range is 0,1,2,3,4, so the saturated invariant lattice has rank five. The root eigenvalue of channel 2 coincides precisely with that of channel 4. None of channels 0,1,3 shares it. Thus the complete selected cluster has rank two in EACH pairing. Its projector is analytic at q by the proved cluster theorem. Set r=q+q^-1=2cos(pi/7). In its real cyclotomic subfield, r^3-r^2-2r+1=0, W_7^2=(1+r)^2. (3) Literal expansion of the FOUR actual seven-factorial germs in (1) gives [t^0] sum_ij d_(e_i)d_(f_j) K_ij =0, [t^1] sum_ij d_(e_i)d_(f_j) K_ij =0, [t^2] sum_ij d_(e_i)d_(f_j) K_ij =3444-5180r-6440r^2. (4) The leading quantum-integer coefficient is equally explicit: c_7=-14/(q-q^-1), c_7^2=-28-28r-56r^2. (5) For an independent check of the division, ordinary polynomial reduction modulo the cubic in (3) gives (-28-28r-56r^2)(24r^2+20r-11) =3444-5180r-6440r^2. (6) Equations (1),(4)--(6) therefore prove the EXACT source identity tr(E_2^S(q) E_2^T(q))=24r^2+20r-11. (7) Since pi/7<pi/3, one has r>1. Hence (7) is strictly greater than 33, in particular strictly greater than two. No numerical rounding, large-level extrapolation, or conjectural asymptotic is used. The audit evaluates (4) directly in Q[q]/Phi_14(q), retaining the actual generic t-series. In this example every individual Racah range is tail-free, because the untouched opposite sum a+b+c+d=8<=12. This makes the finite coefficient certificate especially short; it does not substitute a semisimple root value for the source germ. The calculation uses three Taylor coefficients of the root-unit factorial products after canceling their actual common [7] zero. ## 3. Why this excludes every common orthogonal positive metric Suppose H were a positive definite Hermitian form making BOTH P=E_2^S(q) and Q=E_2^T(q) self-adjoint. They are idempotents, so in an H-orthonormal basis they would be ordinary orthogonal projections. For an orthonormal basis u_1,u_2 of the range of P, tr(PQ)=tr(PQP)=sum_(j=1)^2 <Q u_j,u_j>_H, 0<=<Q u_j,u_j>_H<=1. Thus tr(PQ)<=2. This contradicts (7). Trace is invariant under simultaneous change of basis, so allowing a different physical gauge or a nondiagonal positive form does not repair the contradiction. This excludes simultaneous positive self-adjointness of the ACTUAL complete cluster projectors, already at one finite level. It does not exclude a positive form in which those projectors are nonorthogonal, a metric adapted only to one pairing, a weighted source/dual energy bound, or a direct bound on the scalar generic germs. The exact generic bilinear source metric remains a separate, valid statement; a transpose identity must not be turned into a Hermitian orthogonality identity. ## 4. Consequence for the higher-normal proof path The first-normal bound uses exact positive generic presentations on face-supported branches and first-order Ward/Fourier relations. A higher-order extension must retain the overlap in (2), together with its derivatives at subsequent orders, or find a different exact positive presentation. The actual cluster projectors cannot be made jointly orthogonal to bypass these terms. This is an obstruction to that proposed METHOD, not a counterexample to the general volume limit or to polynomial higher-normal scalar bounds. Those bounds remain open outside the already proved face- supported and tail-free branches. Audit: [exact cyclotomic source calculation](../experiments/audit_actual_cluster_projector_positive_metric_obstruction.py) and [recorded certificate](../experiments/actual_cluster_projector_positive_metric_obstruction_results.json). Primary-agent analytical review checked the complete-cluster ranks, second-Taylor-coefficient Ward normalization, exact real-cyclotomic division and the positive-projection trace contradiction. Fresh replay of the exact N=7 certificate passed. This excludes the stated common orthogonal metric shortcut, not a general volume conjecture.

title: A polynomial-cost critical-value upper bound for two-anchor source cores
text: # A polynomial-cost critical-value upper bound for two-anchor source cores 28 October 2026. A genuine minimax deformation is available for any two-anchor residual core of the actual unit-factor source. Its original coefficient is bounded by its largest regular critical modulus times an explicit polynomial in its degree. No positivity, accessible highest saddle, nonzero thimble coefficient, or lower bound on critical values is assumed. This is an upper bound only. It does NOT prove the knot upper bound. These anchor critical points are conditional on the remaining integer clocks; they are not automatically FULL critical points of the knot's coupled phase. The sharp regulator theorem cannot be applied to them without that step. ## 1. Statement with its original coefficient normalization After extracting the actual scalar and any monomial factors, a two-anchor core with strict Hall support has the form f(z)=gamma z^(-q) product_(j=1)^m (z-u_j), |u_j|=1, gamma!=0, 1<=q<=m-1, I=CT_z f(z)=(1/(2*pi*i)) integral f(z) dz/z. (1) Here m and q can depend on N. Repeated roots and arbitrarily close unit roots are allowed. All extracted source scalars remain in gamma. This is exactly the homogeneous two-anchor coefficient after removing its common scale. Put p=m-q and M=max_(f'(z)=0, z!=0, f(z)!=0)|f(z)|, with M=0 if the regular critical set is empty. Then |I| <=4 m^2 log(m+1) M. (2) In particular m=O(N) gives only polynomial transport cost. If a separate argument bounds EVERY such full-source critical modulus by exp(N V+o(N)), (2) would give the same exponential upper bound. It is not inferred here that these conditional critical values have V=Vol(knot)/(2*pi). ## 2. The critical-value contour exists without selecting its saddle Fix R>M. The Laurent polynomial f is a proper finite map from C* to C: its only poles on the sphere are 0 of order q and infinity of order p. There is no finite asymptotic value at either pole. Over {|w|>R}, f has no critical point. Every component of its preimage is therefore an unramified finite cover of an annulus. Such a component is an annulus with one end over infinity. It contains exactly one of the two pole ends. Thus there is one component around 0 and one around infinity, of degrees q and p. The finite boundary Gamma_R of the component around 0 is a smooth closed level curve |f|=R. It winds once around 0, and so represents the ORIGINAL positive generator in (1). This proves |I| <= R/(2*pi) integral_(Gamma_R)|dz/z|. (3) The assertion is not that the source reaches every critical point. The contour uses a level above all critical values; an inaccessible highest point is entirely compatible with (3). For completeness the annular-cover statement can be read locally and topologically. A connected finite cover of the punctured disk at infinity corresponds to a finite-index subgroup of Z, hence is again a punctured disk. Filling its puncture adds one pole. It cannot contain both poles or a third component without a pole. Its regular level boundary is an embedded circle. No transport norm has yet been assumed; it is estimated next. ## 3. A uniform logarithmic length estimate The level equation is a real algebraic curve of degree 2m: |gamma|^2 product_j |z-u_j|^2-R^2 |z|^(2q)=0. Every radial ray meets it at most 2m times: along a fixed ray it is a nonzero real polynomial of degree 2m in the radius. Every circle meets it at most 2m times: the restriction is a nonzero trigonometric polynomial of degree m. It cannot vanish identically on a circle, since its highest harmonic has the nonzero product of the leading and constant coefficients of product(z-u_j). The elementary one-dimensional coarea/total-variation count therefore gives, writing r_min,r_max for the extreme radii of Gamma_R, integral |dArg z| <=4*pi*m, integral |d log|z|| <=2m log(r_max/r_min). Since |dz/z|<=|dArg z|+|d log|z||, integral_(Gamma_R)|dz/z| <=4*pi*m+2m log(r_max/r_min). (4) These are bounds on a single component by the number of intersections of the whole level curve. Tangencies affect a set of measure zero and do not invalidate the total-variation estimate. ## 4. Unit roots prevent an exponential transport constant Put A_+(R)=max(0,log(R/|gamma|)+m log2). For |z|>=2, |f(z)|>=|gamma| 2^(-m)|z|^p, and for |z|<=1/2, |f(z)|>=|gamma| 2^(-m)|z|^(-q). Hence on the level curve log(r_max/r_min) <=2log2+A_+(R)(1/p+1/q). (5) This does NOT require a lower bound on M/|gamma|. If that ratio is extremely small, the positive-part expression clips to zero once its logarithm is below -m log2. Root clustering causes no hidden log(1/M) transport factor. The exact two-anchor critical-flow equation bounds every regular critical radius between 1/m and m; it is the two-vertex case of [the cut maximum principle](charged_critical_flow_and_chambers.md). It also follows directly by comparing the real parts of sum_j z/(z-u_j)=q inside and outside the unit circle. Thus, for M>0, M/|gamma| <=(m+1)^(2m). Take R down to M in (3)--(5), without deforming through the critical level. Since 1/p+1/q<=2, |I|/M <=2m+(m/pi)[2log2+2(2m log(m+1)+m log2)] <=4m^2 log(m+1). This proves (2). If M=0, use any R>0 and let R decrease to zero in the same estimates; the bounded positive-part expression gives I=0. The proof is uniform in the unit-root positions and their multiplicities, with no assumption of a fixed saddle Hessian. ## 5. The precise higher-dimensional issue The one-variable proof uses a proper map C*->C. A Laurent polynomial on a torus of dimension at least two is generally NOT a proper map to C, even when every ordinary critical radius is bounded. Nonzero finite asymptotic values and critical values on boundary restrictions must be included before repeating the annular fibration argument. In the original source these are not removed merely by saying the torus generates its absolute homology. The [exact cut/flag jets](charged_source_cut_jets.md) retain coordinate boundary currents and bound their small-deficit normal cost. They do not bound the remaining core periods or force a constrained boundary stationary point into the saturated genuine critical variety. The [critical regulator compactification](saturated_critical_regulator_compactification.md) controls limits of FULL genuine critical points, not arbitrary such restricted boundary points. Those distinctions are essential for extending (2) to the complete clock-coupled knot period. Thus (2) supplies an actual polynomial-cost minimax estimate for a source class to which it applies. The missing general upper-bound theorem is still to prove that the FULL phase, with all its retained relative boundary strata, has no larger relevant stratified critical value. No new knot or broad knot class is proved here. ## 6. A rigorous logarithmic-mass estimate for a prospective global chain There is one higher-dimensional quantitative step which can be proved without assuming a controlled gradient flow. Let an oriented real r-cycle Gamma in (C*)^r be a finite sum of semialgebraic pieces Gamma_a with integer multiplicities c_a. Suppose each piece is contained in a real algebraic support whose complexification has dimension r and degree D_a. Suppose also |log|z_i||<=B on the chain. Then integral_Gamma |dlog z_1 wedge ... wedge dlog z_r| <=4^r (B+pi)^r sum_a |c_a|D_a. (8) Lower-dimensional strata have zero r-dimensional integral. Supports can be split into their regular pieces without changing their total degree bound. Singular pieces of full real dimension r require their own r-dimensional support; an arbitrary algebraic superset of larger dimension does not satisfy the hypothesis. Proof. Write dlog z_i=d rho_i+i d theta_i. The absolute r-form is bounded by the sum of the 2^r real wedge forms obtained by selecting rho_i or theta_i at every coordinate. For each corresponding projection, the area formula integrates its absolute Jacobian by counting fibers. A fixed rho_i imposes the quadratic equation Re(z_i)^2+Im(z_i)^2=exp(2rho_i); a fixed theta_i imposes one real linear equation, with an extra ray inequality. At a regular fiber point these equations cut the complexified r-dimensional support in an isolated point. Bezout's inequality bounds their number by 2^r D_a. This remains a bound on the isolated points even if an unrelated positive-dimensional complex intersection is present; the singular/projection-critical locus has image measure zero. If s radial coordinates were selected, the projection box has volume at most (2B)^s(2pi)^(r-s). Sum these bounds over all coordinate choices and over the chain pieces. The result is 2^r sum_a|c_a|D_a * (2B+2pi)^r, which is (8). Angular seams are omitted sets of measure zero and the absolute-Jacobian count includes all windings. Consequently an ACTUAL homologous sublevel representative with polynomial sum|c_a|D_a and polynomial logarithmic radius range would have polynomial log-form mass. Bounding its exponential integrand would then give the desired upper estimate without a hidden exponential transport constant. This is a proved mass lemma, not a claim that an effective semialgebraic triangulation constructs that representative. Construction with the original relative source, and control of its full stratified critical values, remain separate. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_coefficient_minimax_upper.py): exact source normalizations, complete regular critical sets for root families including repeated roots, the critical radius and level-radius bounds, the explicit polynomial prefactor, and the inaccessible-highest example as a check that an upper estimate does not assert selection.

title: The original filling kernel is an exact centered Gaussian with a normal source
text: # The original filling kernel is an exact centered Gaussian with a normal source 29 October 2026. The full original twist, including every projective Casimir jet, is an exact centered Gaussian in the pair eigenlogarithm. Its finite Fourier coefficients have an exact Poisson/Fresnel formula with a retained INTEGER LINEAR charge weight. No coprimality or parity restriction is needed. The representation gives actual nonzero local Gaussian charge channels near real complete color for fixed |p|>=2. It does not prove that their exterior pairing survives in a filled knot. ## 1. Full-Hermite Gaussian, not a value-only Gauss sum Use the original N,d=N-1,q=exp(pi i/N),Q=q^2, kappa=q^(d^2/2), and hbar=2pi i/N. The node eigenlogs are UNWRAPPED: x_k=pi i(2k+1)/N, w_k=exp(x_k), 0<=k<N. For an integer P, the actual twist2P data in the [complete Fourier-Hermite theorem](actual_twist_circle_fourier_kernel.md) are h_k=nu_k^(2P), d_k=-P(d-2k)h_k. They satisfy EXACTLY \[ \boxed{h_k=\kappa^{-P} \exp\{P(x_k-\pi i)^2/\hbar\},\qquad d_k=\left.\partial_x\left[\kappa^{-P} e^{P(x-\pi i)^2/\hbar}\right]\right|_{x=x_k}.} \tag{1} \] Indeed the derivative multiplier is P(2k+1-N), and expanding the square gives precisely Q^(P k(k+1)). Its difference is a full integer turn, not an omitted even-level sign. The centered square is invariant under x->2pi i-x, so it has the compatible paired values, opposite derivatives, and zero derivative at the odd simple node x=pi i. Every original normal jet is present. There is also a source-independent matrix form avoiding any sum over auxiliary colors. The function K(z)=arccosh(-z/2)^2 has the branch analytic on C minus[2,infinity), with its removable continuation at z=-2. On the nodes, K(c_k)=(x_k-pi i)^2. The actual finite Casimir has all its eigenvalues below2. Full holomorphic/Hermite functional calculus therefore gives \[ \boxed{R^{2P}=\kappa^P\exp\{P K(\Omega)/\hbar\}.} \tag{2} \] This equality uses BOTH (1) conditions and the FULL polynomial P_N=2T_N(z/2)+2. It is not an assertion that R is Euclidean unitary; its nilpotent exponential is retained. For the filled odd box the exact formula is \[ \mathscr R(R^{-(2p+1)}) =\kappa^{-p}\mathscr R\{R^{-1} e^{-pK(\Omega)/\hbar}\}. \tag{3} \] The actual turn map mathscrR is linear, not multiplicative. Formula (3) does not move the exponential through a turn as a new local operator or discard a source-normal direction. ## 2. A coherent all-color finite Gaussian kernel The exact marked transforms are H_n=N^(-1)sum_k h_k w_k^(-n), D_n=N^(-1)sum_k d_k w_k^(-n), a_n=[D_n+(N-n)H_n]/N, 0<=n<N. (4) At n=0, D_0=0 so (4) includes a_0=H_0. These a are the actual first-kind Chebyshev coefficients, not freely chosen Fourier values. For an arbitrary original mixed-circle exterior A_j, where A_j multiplies L_(j+1), put eta_n=(-1)^n(A_n-A_(n-2)), A_negative=0. Then the FULL filling/source identity is \[ \kappa^{2P}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\beta_j A_j =\frac{\kappa^{2P}}{N^2} \sum_{n,k=0}^{N-1}h_kw_k^{-n} [N-n-P(d-2k)]\,\eta_n. \tag{5} \] It holds for scalar, Hilbert-valued or operator-valued exteriors in their original order. Taking a difference on the exterior retains the two finite color endpoints; no periodic substitute for that finite difference is made. For completeness the normal transform can be recovered coherently from the value transform alone, with its compulsory full finite Hilbert kernel: \[ D_n=-iP\sum_{m\ne n}\frac{H_m}{\sin(\pi(m-n)/N)}. \tag{6} \] Derive this by the elementary DFT of k: its nonzero-frequency coefficients are -1/(1-Q^(-l)), and its mean is d/2. That mean cancels the -PdH_n term exactly. The matrix in (6) is Hermitian and has norm |P|d. This does NOT allow one to discard D when H_n vanishes at a particular color: it mixes all retained colors. All gcd/parity behavior is already exact in (4). For P!=0 put g=gcd(|P|,N), L=N/g. The value H_n is zero unless g divides n. After that reduction it has modulus L^(-1/2) for odd L. For even L it is zero unless (P-n)/g congruent to (P/g)L/2 modulo2, and otherwise has modulus sqrt(2/L). These statements follow by grouping the quadratic sum into g cosets and expanding its squared modulus; the latter leaves only the shifts0, and L/2 if L is even. They include L=1 by its trivial sum. Their PHASES remain the actual finite Gaussian sum in (4); none is divided out as a nonzero normalizer. For P=0, H_n=delta_(n,0),D_n=0, exactly. In particular arithmetic zeros of the value Gauss sum do not determine support of the full-Hermite filling kernel. ## 3. Exact finite-window Poisson representation and endpoint current Set t_k=(k+1/2)/N. For P real integer define the entire finite coefficient interpolation \[ a(n)=\frac{\kappa^{-P}}N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} [2P(t_k-\tfrac12)+1-n/N] e^{2\pi i PN(t_k-1/2)^2-2\pi i n t_k}. \tag{7} \] It is exactly (4) on the physical n=0,...,N-1. It is a specified interpolation of the FILLING COEFFICIENT, not a new assertion about an arbitrary nonintegral ordinary-color exterior. Define \[ I_{P,N}(b)=\int_0^1 e^{2\pi i PN(t-1/2)^2-2\pi i bt}\,dt, \quad J_{P,N}(n)=\frac{e^{\pi i PN/2}(1-e^{-2\pi i n})}{2\pi i N}. \] The all-N, all-parity exact formula is \[ \boxed{a(n)=\kappa^{-P} \sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z}^{\rm symmetric}(-1)^\ell \{(\ell+1)I_{P,N}(n+N\ell)-J_{P,N}(n)\}.} \tag{8} \] The SUM IS PAIRED symmetrically in ell. Each paired tail is O(ell^(-2)) on compact n sets for fixed N,P; the series is then locally uniformly convergent. The endpoint current J is essential off the integer lattice. No unsupported absolute summation of its constant pieces is intended. Here is a direct proof. Apply midpoint Fourier sampling to the periodic extension of the smooth finite-window integrand in (7). Its Fourier coefficient at frequency N ell acquires (-1)^ell. The periodic extension may jump at its endpoints, but its Fourier series converges to each interior t_k. Its paired Fourier aliases converge as stated, by two integrations by parts; their leading odd1/ell terms cancel. In that coefficient put b=n+N ell. The amplitude equals [2P(t-1/2)-b/N]+(ell+1). The first bracket is the phase derivative divided by 2pi i N. Its integrated endpoint is EXACTLY -J_(P,N)(n). This proves (8) and specifies the original side current rather than assuming it vanishes under a later complex-color deformation. For physical INTEGER n, J=0 and (8) simplifies to \[ a_n=\kappa^{-P}\sum_\ell^{\rm symmetric} (-1)^\ell(\ell+1)I_{P,N}(n+N\ell). \tag{9} \] Thus the integer linear charge weight is exactly the retained NORMAL data in (4), not an optional phase-space amplitude. In particular ell=-1 is killed on the original integer color grid. Off that grid its term is -J and may NOT be dropped. The zero charge is therefore not deleted from a deformed source by fiat. When P!=0, each integral in (8) is explicitly a finite Fresnel difference. With b arbitrary complex, \[ I_{P,N}(b)=e^{-\pi i b-\pi i b^2/(2PN)} \int_{-1/2-b/(2PN)}^{1/2-b/(2PN)}e^{2\pi i PN v^2}\,dv. \tag{10} \] The integration segment is the translated original interval, and the integrand is entire. For P=0 use its elementary Fourier integral instead. Thus no division by a Gauss sum or a coprimality assumption has entered any formula. ## 4. Exact odd-filling operator and its classical charge equation Put B_j=mathscrR(R^(-1)L_(j+1)), and eta_n^B=(-1)^n(B_n-B_(n-2)), B_negative=0. Substituting P=-p into (5),(9) gives an ALL-INPUT identity for the filled box: \[ \boxed{\mathscr R(R^{-(2p+1)}) =\kappa^{-p}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\eta_n^B \sum_\ell^{\rm symmetric}(-1)^\ell(\ell+1) I_{-p,N}(n+N\ell).} \tag{11} \] All exteriors and original modified/peripheral factors are kept when this is inserted in a diagram. Multiple boxes can be replaced simultaneously before their original marked closure, by ordinary linearity. Formula (11) is the coherent surgery kernel, rather than an absolute sum over independently normalized circle invariants. To state its local symbol precisely, let a=n/N, b/N=a+ell, y=2pi i(t-1/2), mu=2pi i(a-1), and c=ell+1. Stationarity of the Gaussian integral in (9) gives \[ 2P y-\mu=2\pi i c. \tag{12} \] For the actual negative odd filling, P=-p, this is mu+2p y=-2pi i c. It is the canonical FULL-TWIST charge relation with the half twist already in B_j. The exact physical auxiliary color is j=n+1, whose squared-meridian log near completeness is mu_phys=2pi i((n+1)/N-1)=mu+hbar. Thus the finite equation has the corresponding retained Weyl shift, and (12) is its leading classical form. Identifying y with a chosen topological longitude also requires the actual peripheral chart, not an inference from a classical A-polynomial alone. For the actual low mixed pretzel core the sign can be checked directly. Put H=Q^h for auxiliary color j=N-h. Its literal coefficient has the identity a_(h,v)x^v/N^2=q^(h^2)F_(2v)/[F_v^2F_(v-h)F_(v+h)]. Thus its phase replaces 4Li2(X) by 2Li2(X)+Li2(X/H)+Li2(XH), and includes +(Log H)^2/2. Differentiation at a regular internal saddle gives dG/dLogH=LogH+Log(1-X/H)-Log(1-HX) =Log[(H-X)/(1-HX)]=Log L_H, with its continued integer mark. Here mu_phys=-LogH, rather than LogH. In the circle kernel the factor (-1)^(j-1) cancels the Gaussian linear action -pi i mu_phys, leaving (LogH-2pi i c)^2/(4p) up to real constants for P=-p. Its combined stationary equation is therefore LogH+2p LogL_H=2pi i c. This is a calculation from the original factorial and normal-source phases. It still does not assert the actual exterior contour selects that stationary point. ## 5. Exact first-order transport of the FULL filling coefficient There is an additional useful source Ward identity for a(n). Shifting the original periodic chirp index k->k+1 gives, on integer n, \[ H_{n-2P}=Q^{n-P}H_n, \quad D_{n-2P}=Q^{n-P}(D_n-2P H_n+2Pq^{-n}). \] The boundary term 2P is the retained jump of the original LINEAR normal weight at k=N-1. Substitution in (4) cancels the homogeneous H terms and proves \[ \boxed{a(n-2P)=Q^{n-P}a(n)+\frac{2P}{N}q^{n-2P}, \quad n\in\mathbb Z.} \tag{12a} \] Outside 0<=n<N this uses the specified finite interpolation (7), not an extension of missing Chebyshev coefficients by zero. For complex n the EXACT retained current is \[ a(n-2P)-Q^{n-P}a(n)-\frac{2P}{N}q^{n-2P} =\frac{(e^{-2\pi i n}-1)q^{n-2P}}{N^2} [N-n+P(N+1)]. \tag{12b} \] Thus the physical coefficient recurrence is affine, not an illicit homogeneous theta recurrence after complex-color deformation. For P!=0, define g_n=q^(n^2/(2P))a_n, with the original log q. Equation (12a) says g_(n-2P)-g_n=(2P/N)q^(n^2/(2P)-n). Every physical coefficient packet is therefore a sum of at most 2|P| homogeneous quadratic chirps and explicit INCOMPLETE finite quadratic sums. For instance along n_j=n_0+2Pj in the actual window, j>=0, \[ a_{n_j}=q^{-n_j^2/(2P)} \left[q^{n_0^2/(2P)}a_{n_0} -\frac{2P}{N}\sum_{t=1}^j q^{n_t^2/(2P)-n_t}\right]. \tag{12c} \] The anchors are explicit finite Gaussian data (4), bounded by 1+|P|. No anchor is a knot period. Equation (12c), or the exact Fresnel representation (8), supplies the endpoint function with its actual source rather than approximating D by a Gaussian value. Polynomially small errors in this endpoint function cannot simply be discarded against an exponentially smaller filled rate. ## 6. The actual circle difference cancels its current and folds EXACTLY The current J in (8) is periodic in n with period1. It therefore cancels TERMWISE in the ORIGINAL circle-basis difference. Define the canonical ENTIRE extension b_ext(j)=exp(pi i(j-1))[a(j-1)-a(j+1)], K_P(h)=b_ext(N-h). The physical circle coefficient for color j is beta_(j-1). For 1<=j<N it equals b_ext(j); for the last color, \[ \beta_{N-1}=\tfrac12 b_{\rm ext}(N). \tag{12d} \] The half is compulsory: the original aliases give a(N)=0 and a(N+1)=-a(N-1), while the missing actual coefficient a_(N+1) was extended by ZERO in the finite circle-basis conversion. There is an exact ENTIRE Weyl symmetry, not only an equality on the color lattice: \[ \boxed{K_P(h)=K_P(-h),\qquad h\in\mathbb C.} \tag{12e} \] To prove it without discarding a current, put y_k=x_k-pi i and use the finite Gaussian expression (7). Directly \[ K_P(h)=\frac{2(-1)^{N-1}}{N^2}\sum_k h_k e^{hy_k} [(h+2Py_k/\hbar)\sinh y_k+\cosh y_k]. \tag{12f} \] The k,d-k pair has y mapped to -y and h_k unchanged. Its sum is even in h. The odd simple y=0 term is even as well. Equivalently, the exact alias identities H(-n)=e^(2pi in)H(n), D(-n)=-e^(2pi in)D(n), together with antiperiodicity at n+N, give (12e), including its necessary exp(pi i(j-1)) factor. For ANY even core exterior C_h=C_(-h), scalar or operator-valued, and any integer H with 0<=H<N, the literal physical-color sum therefore obeys \[ \boxed{\sum_{h=0}^H\beta_{N-h-1}C_h =\frac12\sum_{h=-H}^H K_P(h)C_h.} \tag{12g} \] This keeps the physical half weight at h=0. In the actual pretzel core, C_h is even on the physical grid by its finite Chebyshev relation. Its symmetric finite-factorial continuation keeps the pair F_(v-h)F_(v+h) and q^(h^2), and is even as well; a new one-sided exp(pi i h) continuation must not be substituted for it. Thus the fold applies before the original marked closure and with arbitrary spectator boxes. It iterates over several color ports. The remaining high bands/aliases and any cutoff at +/-H remain their actual source terms; (12g) makes no global tail assertion. The current-inclusive Poisson formula becomes especially simple for this folded kernel. With c=ell+1 and b=Nc-h, \[ K_P(h)=\kappa^{-P}e^{\pi i(N-h-1)} \sum_\ell^{\rm symmetric}(-1)^\ell c [I_{P,N}(b-1)-I_{P,N}(b+1)]. \tag{12h} \] There is NO omitted J in this equation: J(j-1)=J(j+1) cancels exactly for all complex j. The charge c=0 is thus truly absent from the full circle kernel, even off lattice. This stronger conclusion holds after the actual circle difference, not for an individual a(n) in section3. Reflection (h,c)->(-h,-c) preserves each paired contribution in (12h). Indeed I(-b)=e^(2pi ib)I(b) by t->1-t; its factor e^(-2pi ih) cancels the reflected prefactor and the two odd signs cancel. Thus +/-charge folding keeps the EXACT endpoint Fresnel functions too. The h=0 endpoint is removed by a genuine whole-source identity, not by comparing two formal saddle heights. ## 7. An actual nonzero LOCAL Gaussian charge, and the remaining gate Fix |P|>=2 and 0<=h/N<=delta<1/2, with physical n=N-1-h. For each c=+1 or -1, the stationary point of the labeled integral with ell=c-1 stays strictly inside [0,1], uniformly for large N. The exact Fresnel integral therefore has \[ I_{P,N}(n+N\ell)= \frac{e^{i\,\operatorname{sgn}(P)\pi/4}}{\sqrt{2|P|N}} e^{-\pi i(n+N\ell)-\pi i(n+N\ell)^2/(2PN)} +O_{P,\delta}(N^{-1}). \tag{13} \] This follows by the elementary full real Gaussian integral and one integration by parts on its two nonstationary omitted tails. It is uniform and NONZERO for sufficiently large N. The original normal charge factor c is nonzero on both channels. No unknown cycle coefficient occurs INSIDE this labeled real Gaussian integral. For P=0 or |P|=1, the exact formulas remain valid; uniform endpoint asymptotics are not substituted for (13). For the circle difference itself the corresponding leading charge term is, with b=Nc-h and ell=c-1, \[ \frac{2i\kappa^{-P}e^{i\operatorname{sgn}(P)\pi/4}} {\sqrt{2|P|N}} (-1)^{(N+1)\ell}c\sin\frac{\pi b}{PN} \exp\{-\pi i(b^2+1)/(2PN)\}. \tag{13a} \] This follows by subtracting the two actual Gaussians at b-1,b+1. Its c=+/-1 amplitudes are nonzero in a fixed sufficiently small real complete-color corridor for |P|>=2. Under (h,c)->(-h,-c), the sine and c both reverse and all remaining factors agree. Thus the two geometric-charge halves ADD at h=0; the apparent half-line endpoint is not an independent positive-height error. One must still retain exact endpoint corrections until their exterior pairing is estimated to the needed exponential accuracy. This is a local source-channel result, not yet nonzero filled-knot pairing. The complete sum in (11) retains all charges; arithmetic Gauss cancellations can and do occur. A complex geometric color deformation must retain the full current-inclusive kernel before using the proved difference cancellation, all exterior/source data, and its endpoint transport. Neither (13) nor the formal relation (12) proves survival after that original exterior contraction. The subsequent [exact source Fourier estimate](actual_filling_source_fourier_endpoint_gap.md) retains those endpoint currents and proves a uniform high-charge gap. Combined with the original analytic mixed source it now yields [nonzero survival of the entire truncated cusp-color sum](actual_pretzel_cusp_corridor_filling_survival.md) for independently large fixed signed fillings. That theorem still retains the complementary physical color region as an open whole-source gate; it does not infer its absence from the local Gaussian above. ## 8. The wrapped normal current is an explicit original source The endpoint function also has a finite operator Ward identity. It identifies its forcing term without discarding it. Let f_P be the degree-<N Casimir polynomial for r_N^(2P), so that R^(2P)=kappa^(2P)f_P(Omega). Define a LINEAR map on Casimir polynomials by \[ (\mathcal T f)(w+w^{-1}) =f(Qw+Q^{-1}w^{-1})+f(Q^{-1}w+Qw^{-1}). \tag{14} \] The symmetric Laurent expression is a polynomial: its constant Chebyshev coefficient is doubled and its nth coefficient is multiplied by Q^n+Q^(-n). Products on the following left side are evaluated in the FULL Casimir algebra, with reduction modulo P_N where necessary. Write rho=q-q^(-1). Then, for every integer P and every N>=2, \[ \boxed{\mathcal T f_P(\Omega) -Q^P\,2T_{2P}(\Omega/2)f_P(\Omega) =\frac{2PN}{\rho}\,\Xi_0(\Omega) =2PN(-1)^N\rho\,p\ell.} \tag{15} \] Here T_(-n)=T_n and Xi_0 has value zero at every node, derivative one at c_0=q+q^(-1), and derivative zero at the other double nodes. The literal original cup and ordinary cap p,ell have precisely the normalizations used throughout this note. To prove (15), put G(x)=kappa^(-P)exp(P(x-pi i)^2/hbar). Its exact shifts satisfy G(x+/-hbar)=Q^P exp(+/-2Px)G(x). The interpolating Laurent polynomial g(x)=f_P(e^x+e^(-x)) has the same value and x derivative as G at every original node x_k. Consequently both sides of (15) have zero node values. All their normal derivatives agree except when a shift crosses the original logarithmic window. At x_0 the derivative defect is +2PN, and at x_d it is -2PN; the shifted endpoint value is one in both cases. Dividing by dc/dx=rho and -rho, respectively, gives the SAME Casimir derivative 2PN/rho at the paired node c_0. At the odd simple node no extra normal condition is imposed. Full Hermite uniqueness proves the first equality, including even and composite levels. For the second equality use the [normalized original source observable](actual_adjacent_observable_source_filtration.md), Xi_0=(-1)^N rho^2 p ell on the degree-d block. This identity extends to the entire physical pair: both sides are Hopf intertwiners, and the degree-d block generates the whole pair by the actual E/F maps, as proved in the [full pair commutant theorem](actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md). There is no unrecorded projector onto that block. Most usefully, the exact endpoint forcing becomes a scalar when placed in its ACTUAL odd-box turn. Indeed R^(-1)p=kappa^(-1)p and the genuine unscaled turn obeys mathscrR(p ell)=I. Therefore \[ \boxed{\mathscr R\!\left[ R^{-1}\{\mathcal T f_P-Q^P 2T_{2P}(\Omega/2)f_P\}\right] =2PN(-1)^N\rho\,\kappa^{-1}I.} \tag{16} \] Its scalar modulus is at most 4pi|P|, uniformly in N. This is an all-input original-source reduction, not just a formal critical value statement. It can be inserted with arbitrary spectators in this typed slot. In a composed source the displayed current removes that box and leaves its explicitly known scalar factor. Equations (15)--(16) do not bound the inverse Ward transport, nor identify a general Fresnel endpoint remainder with this one term. The map mathcalT is the specified linear Casimir q-shift, not a physical gate that may be relocated through other boxes. A global filled-knot estimate must still control the resulting actual source and any iteration of this identity. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp.py) tests original full physical signed twists and odd filled boxes, all-node Gaussian values AND derivatives, finite Hilbert normal data, gcd/parity selection, the current-inclusive Poisson/Fresnel identity, the uniform nonzero labeled charge asymptotic, and the full physical endpoint Ward (15) with its scalar turned source (16).

title: Coherent complete-belt stacks with arbitrary signs and outer twists
text: # Coherent complete-belt stacks with arbitrary signs and outer twists 29 October 2026. The complete-circle boundary packet removes the balance restriction from the original quantum source of the literal octahedral belt stacks. No ordering, parity or residue subsequence is selected. A fixed extra signed crossing power is retained exactly; its literal geometric collar certificate is linked separately below. ## 1. The exact original source and its nodal crossing phase Use the genuine full checked crossing R, the complete ordinary auxiliary-circle operator L_N and the unscaled physical turn of [the original stack construction](actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md). Write z=z_N, z^sharp for its literal reflected polynomial, and f_+=z^sharp R^(-1), f_-=Rz, n=p+q>0, e=q-p, Phi_(p,q,a;N)=phi(L_N R^a product_i f_(epsilon_i)), where the fixed word epsilon has p plus and q minus pieces, and a is any fixed signed integer. The whole pair commutant is the FULL Hermite algebra, so the exact all-port identity is Phi_(p,q,a;N)=phi(L_N R^(e+a)(z^sharp)^p z^q) =N sum_(j=0)^(N-1) R(c_j)^(e+a) conjugate(z(c_j))^p z(c_j)^q. (1) The second equality is the proved original complete-belt sewing functional; the repeated Casimir normal source has not been replaced before closure. Its derivative pairing gives precisely the displayed N-weighted nodal sum. The all-port equality in the first line includes the normal directions and is stronger than the final nodal formula. Put d=N-1, q_root=exp(pi i/N), kappa=exp(pi i d^2/(2N)) and theta_j=(2j+1-N)pi/N, c_j=-2cos(theta_j). The literal crossing has R(c_j)=kappa(-1)^j q_root^[j(j+1)]. Consequently, at EVERY node and both parities, R(c_j)=kappa^(1/2) exp[iN theta_j^2/(4pi)], kappa^(1/2) HERE MEANS exp[pi i d^2/(4N)]. (2) There is no principal-square-root convention. The two exponent formulas differ by -2pi i j, exactly. Since the two indices of a double node give the same eigenvalue, (2) is compatible with all multiplicities in (1). In particular |R(c_j)|=1. ## 2. The nonzero all-parity coherent Gaussian The [source-exact boundary packet](actual_complete_circle_boundary_packet.md) gives, uniformly for small real theta, z(-2cos theta)=exp(-i pi d/4) a(i theta) exp[Nj(i theta)] [1+O(1/N)], j(i theta)=j_0-theta^2/(4pi)+O(theta^4), a(0)=2^(-9/4) exp(i pi/8), j_0=v8/pi. (3) Both a(i theta) and j(i theta) are even analytic; j(i theta) is real. Every fixed neighborhood of theta=0 has an exponential gap on its complement for the literal polynomial. The twist in (2) has unit modulus, so it preserves that entire-source gap. Combining (1)--(3), the local exponent is EXACTLY, to quadratic order, nN j_0 - N[n-i(e+a)]theta^2/(4pi). Its real quadratic part is positive because n>0, even for arbitrarily large FIXED signed a. The nodal grid has step2pi/N and shift0 for odd N, shift1/2 for even N. Its complex Gaussian sum is sum_j exp[-N(n-i(e+a))theta_j^2/(4pi)] =sqrt(N)/sqrt(n-i(e+a)) [1+O(exp(-cN))]. Here and below sqrt has positive real part. This follows directly by Fourier transforming the Gaussian: all nonzero frequencies are bounded by exp[-pi N Re(1/(n-i(e+a)))], at either lattice shift. The two tails outside the fixed local window are exponentially small as well. Taylor expansion of the even analytic amplitude and quartic exponent has relative error O(1/N); dominated Gaussian integration makes that estimate uniform on the actual lattice. The resulting FULL original source is Phi_(p,q,a;N) =N^(3/2) 2^(-9n/4) kappa^(a/2) exp[-ie pi/8+ie pi/(4N)] /sqrt(n-i(e+a)) * exp[nN j_0] [1+O(1/N)]. (4) The fixed constant in the error can depend on p,q,a. There is no claim uniform in a growing with N. To check the phase explicitly, the constant factors BEFORE simplification are kappa^((e+a)/2) exp[-ie pi d/4] exp[ie pi/8]. Since d^2/N-d=-d/N, these equal precisely those in (4). This retains the original crossing scalar kappa, not only its modulus. No source phase, normal or winding coefficient is dropped. The leading factor in (4) is nonzero at EVERY sufficiently large level, without a prime-level, parity or congruence restriction. In particular lim_N (2pi/N) log|Phi_(p,q,a;N)|=2n v8. (5) For p=q=k and a=0, (4) reduces to the earlier retained-belt constant N^(3/2)2^[-(9k+1)/2]/sqrt(k), providing a normalization check. The excluded n=0 case has no positive localized packet and is not covered by this theorem. ## 3. Actual links and the precise geometric scope For a=0 the literal octahedral stack proof already constructs the ACTUAL complement for every fixed sign word of length n>=1. Its complete regular-cell metric has volume2n v8, without a balance hypothesis. Its original source is exactly (1). The original reduced single-cut Kashaev normalization differs only by the recorded unit phases (and the stated single1/N in the modified convention), so (5) proves the full original volume limit for EVERY such sign word. Thus unbalanced stacks, including a single positive or negative piece, are now included. This is an actual link-family extension, not a new claim about arbitrary bridge graphs or independently filled crossing circles. Its possible containment in previously known Whitehead-chain families retains the earlier coverage caveat. For a!=0, (1)--(5) retain the literal original outer R^a insertion with all of its source scalars. The independently reviewed [outer-collar puncture permutation/isometry certificate](actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md#3a-any-fixed-integer-outer-crossing-power) identifies its ACTUAL complement with the same complete regular-cell gluing, of volume2n v8. Its component count is n+3 for even a and n+2 for odd a. Thus the original volume equality holds for every fixed sign word and every fixed integer outer twist a. The topological assertion comes from that literal collar certificate, not from the quantum rate. Audit: [full original sign-word/outer-twist sources, high-precision nodal phase checks and coherent Gaussian calibrations](../experiments/audit_actual_coherent_octahedral_belt_stack_asymptotic.py). Fresh replay PASS: seven full physical levels,210 all-sign word operators and490 complete original outer-twist closures;860 100-digit all-parity nodal phase checks; six growing-N families of complete coherent Gaussian calibrations. The phase identities themselves are proved algebraically above; the phase checks and profiles supplement the analytic proof and are not its noncancellation premise. Independent analytical check: the global critical-path auditor re-derived (2), the exact imbalance/Cartan phase in (4), and the complex Gaussian at both lattice shifts. The pointwise source error is controlled after summation by its absolute real Gaussian, with fixed factor depending on n,e,a. Thus no parity cancellation or unestimated residue current is being assumed away.

title: A finite Fourier identity for coherent Racah normal tails
text: # A finite Fourier identity for coherent Racah normal tails **Later result, 29 October 2026:** the [all-partner first-normal theorem](actual_all_partner_first_normal_bound.md) now bounds every actual coherent tail, including the symmetric component left undetermined by the involution below. It uses a positive presentation of the full generic source in addition to these Fourier identities. Higher general normal orders remain open. 29 October 2026. This is an own finite algebraic identity for the actual retained `[2N]` current. It gives a uniform logarithmic relative bound when the largest face sum occurs at least twice, including genuinely nonempty high-partner tails. For arbitrary partner labels the identity retains a second alternating sum. No general bound on that residual, higher normal jets, or completed physical transport is asserted. ## 1. The actual tail and its positive core Use the symmetric quantum-factorial convention and the exact generic sum of [the supported normal theorem](actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.md). Put `D=N-1`, `theta=pi/N`, `q=exp(i theta)`, `Q=q^2`, and s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2 sin(u theta), s_0=1. For any partner of a supported folded sextuple let `F_i` be its four face sums and `Q_k` its three opposite sums. Assume the tail is live: `min Q_k>2D`. Define a_i=2D-F_i, b_k=Q_k-2D, c_k=D-b_k=3D-Q_k. The exact face-deficit inequalities give 0<=a_i<=c_k<=D-1 for EVERY i,k, sum_k c_k-sum_i a_i=D. (1) Indeed `c_k-a_i=D-(Q_k-F_i)>=0`; the equality follows from `sum F_i=sum Q_k`. Order the four `a_i` as A=a_1<=B=a_2<=a_3<=a_4. The true positive core, indexed by `z=2D-v`, is C=sum_(v=0)^A C_v, C_v=(1/N) product_k s_(c_k-v) /[s_v product_i s_(a_i-v)] >0. (2) This is the same `C(q)` appearing in the ACTUAL generic identity (-1)^D S/[N]=C(zeta)+[2N] T(zeta). (3) The true root current is T(q)=-2 sin(theta) N^2 sum_(k=0)^(D-c_max-1) (-1)^k s_k / [product_i s_(a_i+1+k) product_j s_(D-c_j-1-k)]. (4) All displayed factorial arguments are between zero and `D`. No invalid factorial has been assigned a value or silently removed. ## 2. Exact coherent Fourier reduction Write H_r=sum_(u=1)^r cot(u theta), H_0=0, J_v=H_v+sum_k H_(c_k-v)-sum_i H_(a_i-v). Then the following identity is exact at every level, of either parity: T(q)=-sin(theta) sum_(v=0)^A C_v J_v +(2 sin(theta)/N) sum_(v=A+1)^B (-1)^(A+v) E_v, (5) where E_v=s_(v-A-1) product_k s_(c_k-v) /[s_v product_(i=2)^4 s_(a_i-v)] >0. (6) An empty last sum is zero. In particular it is absent when `A=B`, equivalently when the largest face sum occurs at least twice. The second sum is essential. For `N=5` and partner labels `(a,b,c,d,e,f)=(2,2,3,3,2,2)`, one has the ordered arrays `a_i=(0,1,1,2)`, `c_k=(2,3,3)`. The first sum in (5) is zero, whereas the retained residual gives `T(q)=-1`. Dropping it would incorrectly assert zero current. ## 3. Own finite algebraic proof This proof only uses polynomial division, finite sums of roots of unity, and the elementary sine-factorial reflection `s_r s_(D-r)=N`. Let R(x)=product_k product_(u=1)^(c_k)(1-Q^u x) / product_i product_(u=1)^(a_i)(1-Q^u x), f(x)=x R(x)/(1-x), K=sum_k c_k(c_k+1)/2-sum_i a_i(a_i+1)/2, beta=(2 sin(theta)/N) i^(N-2) q^(-K). In (4) put `j=k+1` and use the sine-factorial reflection on its three descending denominators. Converting every remaining sine by `2 sin(u theta)=i q^(-u)(1-Q^u)` gives exactly T(q)=beta sum_(j=1)^(D-c_max) f(Q^j). (7) The phase is important: the alternating sign and the degree difference in (1) leave `q^(2j)=Q^j`, the numerator `x` in `f`. After cancellation, `f` has SIMPLE poles precisely at r_v=Q^(-v), 0<=v<=A. For `1<=u<=A` the numerator has three factors `1-Q^u x` and the denominator has four. Above `A` there are no poles because every `c_k` is at least every `a_i`. Its polynomial part has degree at most `D=N-1`: the numerator degree minus denominator degree is `D`. Let B_v=[(1-x/r_v) f(x)]_(x=r_v), L_v(x)=(1-x/r_v) f(x). Ordinary partial fractions give a polynomial `P` of degree at most `N-1` with f(x)=P(x)+sum_v B_v/(1-x/r_v). Since `f(0)=0`, one has `P(0)=-sum_v B_v`. Sum this identity over all `N`th roots except its pole set. For a nonconstant monomial of degree less than `N` the full root sum is zero, and sum_(x^N=1,x!=r_v) 1/(1-x/r_v)=(N-1)/2. The finite regular parts at the other omitted roots cancel the corresponding partial-fraction corrections. Thus sum_(x^N=1,x not a pole) f(x) =sum_(v=0)^A [r_v L_v'(r_v)-(N+1)B_v/2]. (8) For example, the finite regular part of `f` at `r_v` is `-r_v L_v'(r_v)`. This also checks the constant `(N+1)/2` in (8).
