Direct conversion of the unit factors gives, for EVERY `v`, B_v=i^(-D) q^K N C_v, r_v L_v'(r_v)/B_v=(N+1)/2-(i/2)J_v. (9) Here is an explicit verification rather than an assumed residue sign. For `v>=1`, set `(Q;Q)_r=product_(u=1)^r(1-Q^u)`. Cancelling the three numerator and four denominator zero factors gives B_v=(-1)^v Q^[v(v-1)/2] product_k (Q;Q)_(c_k-v) /[(Q;Q)_v product_i (Q;Q)_(a_i-v)]. Converting these factorials to sines leaves the phase `i^(-D) q^(K-vN)(-1)^v=i^(-D)q^K`, proving the first part of (9). For `v=0` it is immediate from `R(1)`. The logarithmic derivative of a unit factor is -Q^w/(1-Q^w)=1/2-(i/2)cot(w theta). After removing the pole, the signed number of unit factors is `N-1`, and the leading factor `x` contributes one. The real part is therefore `(N+1)/2`. The negative indices `1-v,...,-1` and the factor `1-x` contribute `H_v`, while the remaining positive indices contribute the other seven sums in `J_v`. This proves the second part of (9). Since `beta B_v=-2i sin(theta) C_v`, (8) contributes exactly the first term of (5). It remains to compare (8)'s root set with (7)'s ACTUAL finite range. For roots `x=Q^(-v)` outside the range in (7), cancellation shows: * `0<=v<=A`: these are precisely the omitted poles; * `A<v<=B`: the regular value can be nonzero; * `B<v<=c_max`: the regular value is zero. The last assertion follows by counting factors: above `B`, at most two denominator factors remain while at least three numerator factors remain up to `a_4`; beyond `a_4`, no denominator factors remain, and at least one numerator factor remains up to `c_max`. For the middle range the exact unit-factor conversion gives beta f(Q^(-v))=(2 sin(theta)/N)(-1)^(A+v+1) E_v. (10) One can verify (10) before conversion using f(Q^(-v))=(-1)^(A+1) Q^[vA-A(A+1)/2] (Q;Q)_(v-A-1) product_k (Q;Q)_(c_k-v) /[(Q;Q)_v product_(i=2)^4 (Q;Q)_(a_i-v)]. Subtracting these extra regular nodes from (8) proves (5), including its residual sign. This is a finite proof for all arrays satisfying (1), not an inference from finitely many knots or levels. ## 4. A proved nonempty-tail first-normal bound Suppose `A=B`. Since `H_r=H_(D-r)` and positive cotangents obey `cot(u theta)<=1/(u theta)` for `u<N/2`, 0<=H_r<=(N/pi)(1+log N), 0<=r<=D. Equations (2),(5) therefore give the uniform coherent bound |T(q)| <= 8(1+log N) C(q). (11) Unlike an estimate of the absolute summands in (4), this uses the actual cancellations. The factor 8 is deliberately nonsharp. Together with the existing positive-core jet estimate and the exact normal derivative dot G(q)=dot C(q)+4N/(q-q^-1) T(q), G=(-1)^D S/[N], dot=D_(log zeta), it proves, with an absolute constant `C_*`, |dot G(q)| <= C_* N^2(1+log N) C(q). (12) Indeed the sharper form before `sin(theta)<=pi/N` is applied in (11) cancels the denominator in `4N/(q-q^-1)` directly. The analytic face factors have the same unit-factor logarithmic bound. Hence for this entire repeated-maximal-face class, the ACTUAL normalized squared scalar and its local positive square root satisfy K(q)=W_N^2, |dot K(q)| <= C_* N^2(1+log N) W_N^2, H(q)=W_N, |dot H(q)| <= C_* N^2(1+log N) W_N. (13) Their first inverse jets have the corresponding reciprocal bounds. This conclusion includes live `[2N]` currents; it does not extend to higher generic normal orders merely by differentiating (5), which is an identity on the fixed cyclotomic fiber. ## 5. The former all-high diagnostic is now a theorem Take `N=3m+1` and all six high spins equal to `2m`. Then `a_i=0`, `c_k=m`, `A=B=0`, and `C=s_m^3/N`. Equation (5) proves EXACTLY T(q)/C(q)=-3 sin(theta) sum_(u=1)^m cot(u theta). (14) More generally, every live partner array with all four faces equal `2D` has `a_i=0`; (14) becomes T(q)/C(q)=-sin(theta) sum_k sum_(u=1)^(c_k) cot(u theta). Thus the finite Fourier proof is not confined to the equilateral sequence. The former numerical observations remain archived as their historical record; (14) now follows from the own uniform identity. ## 6. The residual is an exact partner involution For a unique minimum `A<B`, define new arrays a*=(A,D-c_1+A,D-c_2+A,D-c_3+A), c*=(D-a_2+A,D-a_3+A,D-a_4+A). (15) They again satisfy (1), have the SAME unique minimum `A`, and applying (15) twice returns the original arrays up to permutation. Substitute `v=A+1+k` in the residual in (5), and apply `s_r s_(D-r)=N` to its three numerator factorials. The three factors of `N` cancel its prefactor exactly. The result is the ACTUAL tail formula (4) for `(a*,c*)`, with no extra factor or sign. Therefore T(a,c)-T(a*,c*)=-sin(theta) sum_(v=0)^A C_v J_v. (16) Moreover the same factorial reflection proves C*_v=C_(A-v), C*=C, J*_v=-J_(A-v). (17) The last equality also follows directly from `H_(D-r)=H_r`. Thus the difference in (16) is logarithmically bounded relative to `C`, whereas this involution alone leaves the average of the two currents undetermined. Repeated application is not a contraction. For the actual tetrahedral labels, this is an actual PARTNER move, not just a transformation of abstract factorial arrays. If the unique largest face is `F_1=a+b+e`, retain those three edges and replace its complementary edges by (c,d,f) -> (D-c,D-d,D-f). (18) The unchanged face sum is `F_1`; the other new face sums are the three numbers `2D-Q_k+F_1`, and the new opposite sums are `2D+F_1-F_i` for `i!=1`. These are exactly (15). They again have the same unique largest face, because the original tail is live. The other choices follow by tetrahedral relabeling. In particular (16) controls a difference of the full ACTUAL first normals, not merely a difference of bare root tails. Both core germs have polynomial logarithmic derivatives, their root cores agree by (17), and the four face factors also have polynomial logarithmic derivatives. Differentiating (3) for each branch therefore gives |dot K_B(q)-dot K_(B*)(q)| <= C_* N^2(1+log N) W_N^2. (19) No equality of the two generic normal germs is asserted. Combining these controlled three-edge differences with other exact source relations is a possible next step; (16) by itself does not fix the common first-normal component. ## 7. What the general residual still requires For a unique largest face, the last sum in (5) is still alternating. No polynomial relative bound on its absolute envelope has been proved here. Positivity of the residues does not authorize replacing this residual by its absolute sum. The exact formula exposes the partner involution and proves the repeated-maximal-face class, but it does not close the general first-normal transport problem. The transformed summation interval need not be shorter than the original one. The identity holds for abstract arrays (1) as well as actual partner branches. Applying it to a source retains all original generic normalization, peripheral factors and marked exterior data through the already proved coefficient theorem. It does not alone supply a positive completed recoupling metric or identify a global complement. Audit: [exact finite-field Fourier and tail checks](../experiments/audit_actual_coherent_racah_tail_fourier_residues.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/actual_coherent_racah_tail_fourier_residues_results.json). Independent full analytical review of the Fourier residue identity, phase conversion, retained residual and first-normal scope passed. The exact audit freshly replayed 13,132 balanced arrays and 32 all-high identities. The uniform proof is the algebraic argument above; these finite checks are supplementary.

title: A coherent bridge has a pointed metric potential and a coercive source-fixed optimization
text: # A coherent bridge has a pointed metric potential and a coercive source-fixed optimization 29 October 2026. The six-head bridge and the COMPLETE terminal packet can be composed before an operator norm is taken. Eliminating the bridge is exactly a POINTED diagonal potential on the terminal INPUT; the terminal Green/Newton interference remains intact. Its best all-input constant in the actual pair-degree bias family is a coercive log-convex finite-dimensional optimization. Minimizers stay in a fixed compact interval uniformly in N. They obey an exact physical charge-balance equation, with no exponential cost at the original paired sources. This gives a quantitative local metric step with arbitrary spectator inputs. It does not bound the preceding biased word or prove that such steps telescope across overlapping bridges. No sharp knot-volume bound or new geometric-edge identification is asserted. ## 1. The SAME original maps and physical metric Keep the original root N>=2,d=N-1,Q=q^2,x=q^d, F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a| and all kappa/source factors. Let W_2=(V^tensor4)_(degree2d), W_1=(V^tensor2)_(degree d). Use the physical source-fixing coordinate gauge G_a=s_a/sqrt(N) on each input/output head. It fixes original cups and ordinary caps pointwise, since G_aG_(d-a)=1. The whole marked closure is kept by the complete invariant-source theorem. Write L for the gauged POSITIVE bridge map L=(ell_12 tensor I_34) R_23:W_2->W_1 from [the exact open bridge theorem](actual_terminal_bridge_operator_reduction.md). For input |a,b,c,e> it forces k=d-a-c, u=b-k=d-e, a+c+k=d, 0<=k<=d-u. (1) Its full coefficient includes the original phase; in this gauge its magnitude is N/(s_a^2 s_c^2 s_k). All through-head feedback is the actual strict shift and unitary clock, not a scalar substitution. Let T:W_1->C^N be the ORIGINAL complete terminal packet. It has [the closed all-input kernel](actual_terminal_packet_closed_kernel.md), including its partial factorial Green register P_t. On W_1 the physical product gauge is one. Thus that literal T matrix is unchanged. The full six-head terminal bridge is K=TL, with every spectator port retained. Its row sum is the original source row by the cap/Hopf identity, not by a new boundary functional. Define the genuine pair-degree bias on W_2 by A_delta|a,b,c,e>=exp[delta(a+b-d)]|a,b,c,e>, L_delta=L A_delta^(-1), delta real. (2) It is obtained by the SAME coordinate factor exp(delta(j-d/2)) on heads1,2. It fixes every original paired cup/cap. Equation (1) gives a+b-d=u-c, so its exact coefficient change is exp[delta(c-u)]. In particular the original initial vector w_0=p_12 tensor p_34 obeys A_delta w_0=w_0. No knot value or unknown solution defines this bias. ## 2. Exact coherent composition reduces to a pointed potential Rows of L_delta have disjoint spectator e=d-u. Consequently its COMPLETE row Gram is exactly L_delta L_delta^*=diag(E_delta(u)), E_delta(u)=N^2 sum_(k=0)^(d-u) sum_(a+c=d-k) exp[2delta(c-u)]/(s_a^4 s_c^4 s_k^2). (3) All its original phases were retained before taking this Gram. The complete composition therefore satisfies the operator identity (T L_delta)(T L_delta)^* =T diag(E_delta(u)) T^*=:M_N(delta). (4) It is not necessary to replace E_delta by its largest row. In particular (4) keeps its THROUGH-COLOR dependence and all the Green/Newton/R interference inside the terminal T. Here u is a PHYSICAL degree-basis index of W_1, not a Casimir node. The terminal Gram T^*T still mixes distinct Casimir nodes; (4) does not return to the disproved nodewise Cauchy budget. Define the exact constant C_N(delta)=lambda_max(M_N(delta))>0. (5) It is the SMALLEST all-input constant in the typed inequality ||T L w||^2 <=C_N(delta)||A_delta w||^2, EVERY w in W_2. (6) This follows from T L=(T L_delta)A_delta and the largest singular value. It remains true with an arbitrary Hilbert spectator tensor, including matrix-valued exterior columns; no spectator coefficients have been commuted. Optimality is an actual singular-value statement on the COMPLETE module, not an independently estimated path sum. Equivalently the conditional bridge cost is exact: if v is a specified output of L_delta, its minimum input norm squared is sum_u |v_u|^2/E_delta(u), since L_delta has full row rank. Thus (4) is the actual pointed input metric for the terminal packet. For clarity, the known ordered factorization of T is T=N^(-1) D_out U^(2) D_in P(J) Rev (kappa^(-1)R). Substituting it in (4) leaves the middle operator R diag(E_delta) R^* between Rev and the two Green factors. It does NOT allow P(J), Rev, R and E_delta to be reordered. The terminal singularity P_1=0 at N=6 causes no difficulty: T need not be invertible anywhere in (4)--(6). For the unchanged scalar source, the exact terminal row factorization also yields |chi_N sum_n (T L w)_n|^2 <=|chi_N|^2 N C_N(delta)||A_delta w||^2. (7) The N is the known number of coherent packets. The full positive completion by exp(-N^2)I from the terminal Gram theorem still has polynomial dual cost; no boundary source is normalized by a period. The full positive completion can be kept throughout. Put H_epsilon=(TL)^*(TL)+epsilon I on the COMPLETE W_2, and consider its exact norm after the same input bias. Its optimal constant C_(N,epsilon)(delta) satisfies C_N(delta)<=C_(N,epsilon)(delta) <=C_N(delta)+epsilon exp(2|delta|d). (7a) This follows by conjugating H_epsilon with A_delta^-1 and using the exact input charge range[-d,d]. For epsilon=exp(-N^2), the difference is superexponentially small on every bounded bias set. No channel in ker(TL) is removed. Log convexity and the coercive bounds below apply to this completed norm too: apply the same column exponential-sum proof to the fixed stacked matrix (TL,sqrt(epsilon)I)A_delta^-1. The tiny regularizer is therefore compatible with the complete positive inner product, not an assumed inverse of T or L. ## 3. The local metric optimization is genuinely coercive Let t_u=T e_u be a COMPLETE terminal input column. Equations (3)--(4) give the positive matrix exponential sum M_N(delta)=sum_(u,k,a+c=d-k) N^2 exp[2delta(c-u)]/(s_a^4 s_c^4 s_k^2) t_u t_u^*. (8) For any fixed unit output vector z with T^*z!=0, z^*M_N(delta)z is a positive sum of exponentials in delta. Its logarithm is convex by the elementary log-sum-exp Hessian. Vectors in the common nullspace give zero and are ignored in the Ritz supremum. Since log C_N is that supremum, delta -> log C_N(delta) is convex. (9) There are ACTUAL opposite extreme charges, not just a formal convex hull assumption. The bridge states (a,c,k,u)=(0,d,0,0) and (d,0,0,d) each have squared coefficient N^-2 before the bias. The closed terminal entries give |T_(0,0)|=1/N, |T_(0,d)|=1. Their rank-one positive contributions imply, for ALL real delta, C_N(delta)>=N^-4 exp(2delta*d), C_N(delta)>=N^-2 exp(-2delta*d). (10) Thus log C_N tends to infinity at BOTH ends and attains a finite global minimum. Neither uniqueness nor positivity of every terminal eigenvalue is required. Moreover all minimizers are uniformly bounded as N varies. The uniform sine-factorial estimate bounds s_a and s_a^-1 by N^C exp(CN), with constants independent of a. The explicit closed T entry consists of a bounded number of such ratios, a sum of at most N terms, and |P_t|<=(4^(t+1)-1)/3. Therefore ||T||<=N^C exp(C_T N). The independently proved pointed bridge profile gives max_u E_0(u)<=N^C exp(Nv_8/pi). Hence log C_N(0)<=C_0N+C_1log N. (11) At a minimizer delta_N, C_N(delta_N)<=C_N(0). Combining (10) with (11), and d=N-1>=N/2, proves |delta_N|<=C_2 (12) with an explicit finite constant obtainable from those factorial bounds, independent of N. Thus the optimal local typed metric does not require a bias growing with N or an unknown solution. Its exponential coordinate conditioning is the controlled physical degree weight in (2); original paired boundary norms remain fixed. ## 4. Its optimality equation is an exact physical charge balance If the largest eigenvalue in (5) is simple at a minimizing delta, let z be its unit eigenvector. Differentiating the finite matrix sum (8) gives EXACTLY sum_(u,k,a+c=d-k) (c-u) N^2 exp[2delta(c-u)]/(s_a^4 s_c^4 s_k^2) |z^*t_u|^2=0. (13) For a multiple largest eigenvalue, the same equation holds with |z^*t_u|^2 replaced by Tr(rho t_ut_u^*), for a positive trace-one rho supported on that largest eigenspace. To see this, the left and right derivatives of the largest eigenvalue are the minimum and maximum quadratic forms of M_N' on the top eigenspace. At a minimum they enclose zero; a convex mixture gives rho. All weights in (13) are nonnegative and sum to C_N(delta) after dropping (c-u). Thus the maximizing output-energy ensemble has zero mean ACTUAL pair-degree charge, a+b-d=u-c. The true bridge angle sum a+c+k=d and cutoff k<=d-u are retained simultaneously. This is a concrete local metric-duality constraint, not an assertion of a complete hyperbolic gluing equation or a peripheral parameter. It concerns the all-input norm optimizer, not automatically the selected original-source distribution. The exact negative-bridge analogue uses the dual physical gauge G^-1, complementary angles and the corresponding E_-(u) profile. The same matrix-potential construction applies. Changing between the two physical gauges retains the actual G^2 interface; it is not a free contraction in this optimization. ## 5. Why it does not yet telescope through an arbitrary prefix For an ORIGINAL preceding braid B and its original source w_0, (6) is the genuine pointed bound ||T L B w_0||^2 <=C_N(delta)||A_delta B w_0||^2, A_delta B w_0=(A_delta B A_delta^(-1))w_0. (14) The conjugated prefix and all its original coefficients remain. A_delta commutes with generators contained in input pair12 or34, but not with the overlapping bridge R_23. Its matrix entries gain the exact pair-degree difference of their physical input/output. Thus one cannot optimize (5) and then keep the untransformed preceding word. This is the retained interface to be controlled in a sequence of bridge eliminations. The new result is an exact, coercive ALL-input step relative to the fixed terminal Gram, preserving all spectator operators and known sources. It improves on a free octahedral maximum by retaining the pointed potential and a physical degree-balance condition. It does not prove a global telescoping potential, a knot-volume upper bound, or geometric survival. No additional presentation counterexample is needed or claimed by this local optimization theorem. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_coherent_terminal_bridge_metric.py): eleven levels N=2,...,12. The code constructs L directly from the ORIGINAL R and cap, T from its independently verified closed kernel, and tests (4) on all open columns, arbitrary two-column spectator states, exact paired-source invariance, both coercive bounds, log convexity and the minimizing charge equation. Finite numerical optimization supplements the all-level convex/coercivity proof.

title: When the compact physical star locus can contain hyperbolic geometry
text: # When the compact physical star locus can contain hyperbolic geometry 28 October 2026. The compact Gram intersection is not automatically a real-form locus of zero-volume representations. It CAN contain a discrete-faithful representation: an explicit algebraic figure-eight example is given below. There is also an all-width feasibility criterion, including a necessary common-circle condition on the chosen bridge eigenflags. Thus real compact accessibility depends on the actual bridge marking; it cannot be assumed for a broad knot class. The original cap has an exact nonzero coefficient on every matched product packet, with no asymptotic normalization ambiguity. That computes the cap half of a weighted geometric overlap. It leaves the original braid transition amplitude, and possible cancellation in the full overlap, unproved. ## 1. The compact cap locus is an explicit bridge-generator real form Use the original complete source and the bounded physical meridians of [the cup/cap Gram theorem](actual_plat_cup_cap_gram_support.md). A compact head character has |k|=1, e=-conjugate(f), k+k^(-1)+ef=-2, G=[[k,e],[fk,k^(-1)+fe]]. (1) An ordinary adjacent cap relation is H_2 H_1=I. By the triangular factorization, it says L_(-,2)L_(-,1)=L_(+,2)L_(+,1). One is lower triangular with top-left one; the other is upper triangular with bottom-right one. Consequently BOTH are I. All earlier paired L_- prefixes therefore reset after each cap. The chosen top bridge generators are precisely G_1,G_3,..., with their partners inverse. Conversely for ANY G with data (1), the partner k_2=k^(-1), e_2=-k^(-1)e, f_2=-k f (2) also satisfies the compact star conditions, and its two L products are I. Thus the compact top-cap locus is exactly the product of these explicit bridge-generator sets, with based partners inverse. This also includes G=-I, but a discrete-faithful meridian is noncentral. Let a representation of a fixed k-bridge plat be given, and let mu_r be its CHOSEN oriented top bridge meridians, with trace two. It lies, up to simultaneous conjugation, in the compact physical intersection IF AND ONLY IF there exists one g in PGL2(C) such that, for EVERY r, G_r=-g mu_r g^(-1)=[[a_r,b_r],[c_r,-2-a_r]], |a_r|=1, c_r=-a_r conjugate(b_r). (3) Necessity is (1) and the prefix reset. For sufficiency put k=a_r, e=b_r,f=c_r/a_r, construct all partners by (2), and use the given plat representation relations. They are exactly the bottom Nielsen cap constraints. The same common conjugation, not independently chosen frames at the bridges, is essential. Formula (3) is a finite real-algebraic feasibility test at ANY width. ## 2. Equivalent common Hermitian-matrix criterion There is a useful coordinate-free version of (3). It is equivalent to the existence of Hermitian matrices B,J such that B>0, signature(J)=(1,1), J B^(-1) J=B, mu_r^* J mu_r-J =-(1/2)(mu_r-I)^* B(mu_r-I), every r. (4) These are actual matrix conditions on the specified meridians. They do not require an arbitrary choice of a geometric action normalization. Proof in the compact frame. Put J_0=diag(1,-1), B=I. If G is (1), write N=G+I. A noncentral N has null image/kernel line (1,t), |t|=1, and takes the form N=a [[1,-t^(-1)],[t,-1]], a=1+k, |a-1|=1. (5) Direct multiplication gives N^*J_0 N=0 and N^*J_0+J_0N=N^*N/2. Hence G^*J_0G-J_0=-N^*N/2, which is (4), since mu=-G. Conversely for a noncentral trace-minus-two G satisfying that equation, apply it to a nonzero v in ker(G+I). It forces v^*J_0v=0. Thus v=(1,t), |t|=1. In (5), the same equation forces |a|^2=2 Re a, equivalent to |a-1|=1. This recovers (1). The central case is G=-I and is included directly. Under a common conjugation g set B=g^*g and J=g^*J_0g. These satisfy (4). Conversely J B^(-1)J=B makes B^(-1/2)J B^(-1/2) a Hermitian involution of signature (1,1). A unitary diagonalization therefore produces g with precisely those B,J, reducing back to the compact frame. This proves equivalence. ## 3. A genuine all-width obstruction: bridge flags must be concyclic Every noncentral compact G has its unique eigenflag (1,t) in (5), with |t|=1. Consequently ALL chosen bridge eigenflags of a compact representation must lie on ONE generalized round circle before conjugation. For four distinct flags every cross-ratio must therefore be real. Equivalently they must be null for one indefinite Hermitian form J. This is a necessary condition at arbitrary bridge number; it is not claimed sufficient without the amplitude conditions (4). Thus a discrete-faithful representation whose chosen bridge flags have a nonreal four-point cross-ratio is absent from that particular compact physical star intersection. It could still contribute to the original scalar through a complex analytic saddle. Ordinary real Gram moment support would miss that exponential mechanism. The criterion concerns the ACTUAL chosen bridge generators. A change of bridge presentation can change the set of flags. It is not a claim that a given knot has no other compactly accessible presentation. ## 4. Complete two-bridge criterion: an explicit cardioid For two noncommuting noncentral trace-two parabolics put tau=Tr(mu_1 mu_2)-2 !=0, phi=Arg tau in (-pi,pi]. Then (3) holds IF AND ONLY IF phi!=pi, 0<|tau|<=16 cos^2(phi/2). (6) In particular a nonzero negative real tau is excluded. To prove this, write the two compact matrices using (5), with a_j=1+k_j and unit flags t_j. Their trace invariant is exactly tau=a_1 a_2(2-t_1/t_2-t_2/t_1) =4 a_1 a_2 sin^2(delta/2), a_j=2cos(alpha_j)exp(i alpha_j), -pi/2<alpha_j<pi/2, alpha_1+alpha_2=phi. Since cos(alpha_1)cos(alpha_2)<=cos^2(phi/2), this proves necessity. Conversely choose k_1=k_2=exp(i phi), a_1=a_2=1+exp(i phi), and t_1=1,t_2=exp(i delta), where sin^2(delta/2)=|tau|/[16cos^2(phi/2)]. These give the prescribed invariant. Two irreducible trace-two parabolics are determined up to simultaneous conjugation by tau: use their distinct fixed eigenvectors as a basis, obtaining [[1,s],[0,1]] and [[1,0],[t,1]], then diagonally normalize s=1; the remaining parameter is st=tau. This proves sufficiency for the original pair, not only for some abstract representation. ## 5. Exact discrete-faithful prototype inside the compact intersection Use the independently checked figure-eight Riley pair A=[[1,1],[0,1]], B=[[1,0],[u,1]], u^2-u+1=0, u=exp(i*pi/3), from [the marked holonomy proof](marked_braid_holonomy.md). Set a=1+u, z=(5+i sqrt(11))/6, z+z^(-1)=5/3, G_1=[[u,-a],[a,-2-u]], G_2=[[u,-a/z],[a z,-2-u]]. (7) Both matrices satisfy (1), and Tr(G_1G_2)-2=u. There is an explicit conjugation, not just matching dimensions: F=[[a(z-1),1],[a(z-1),z]], F A F^(-1)=-G_1, F B F^(-1)=-G_2. (8) Its determinant is nonzero. The identity for B uses a^2=3u and 3(z-1)^2+z=0. Thus this is the SAME discrete-faithful representation, at the recorded geometric embedding. All algebraic identities hold at BOTH Riley embeddings. Conjugating u,z and every displayed matrix gives the conjugate discrete-faithful place, including the positive-volume convention used in the earlier regulator calibration. Compact accessibility is therefore not confined to the opposite volume orientation. With top meridians (G_1,G_1^(-1),G_2,G_2^(-1)), the actual Nielsen word for the four-plat [2,-1,2,2] satisfies BOTH bottom inverse-pair relations exactly. Symbolically their common Riley factor is u^2-u+1. After the top pair substitutions the remaining free-group relator is a cyclic permutation of the usual figure-eight relation a b^(-1) a^(-1) b a=b a b^(-1) a^(-1) b, so this is the same two-bridge presentation. Consequently the complete compact star intersection can contain a discrete-faithful point. It is not uniformly a trivial, unitary-group or zero-volume representation locus. This is a prototype diagnostic of the GENERAL criterion, not a new figure-eight asymptotic proof or a broad accessibility claim. ### The same prototype has NO wholly real compact source-to-source transport There is an exact limitation even in this accessible case. The top compact point above does NOT imply that the actual incoming cup point pulled through W is also compact. In fact no simultaneous frame makes both endpoints compact for this discrete-faithful plat. The other bottom bridge generator of [2,-1,2,2], in the canonical A,B frame, is C=A^(-1) B A^(-1) B^(-1) A =[[2,u],[u-1,0]]. The three distinct fixed flags of A,B,C are 0,infinity,u-1 in the column-ratio coordinate. Their unique generalized circle has, up to a nonzero real scalar, Hermitian form J_0=[[0,2-u],[1+u,0]], det J_0=-3. Direct exact multiplication gives A^*J_0A-J_0=diag(0,3), B^*J_0B-J_0=diag(3,0), C^*J_0C-J_0=0. (8a) Any common compact frame for A,B,C would, by Section 3, have this same null circle. But (4) forces a NONZERO negative rank-one defect for every noncentral bridge meridian and every B>0. The last identity in (8a) contradicts it for C, regardless of the scale/sign of J_0. Thus the bottom Nielsen cap equations in the weak Gram intersection are weaker than demanding that its transported input variables obey the same physical star real form. This is allowed because the original W is nonunitary: Ad_W does not preserve adjoints. The geometric source-to-source transition here must be treated by complex analytic propagation, not by a positive real canonical map between the two compact cup loci in this fixed physical polarization. New frame adapters could change that question, but would have to retain their source and exponential normalization. This explicitly locates a mechanism by which weak Gram support can fail to see the exponential geometry, even when its necessary intersection contains that representation. ## 6. The original cap packet weight is nonzero EXACTLY The cap half of an admissible real compact overlap can also be computed without a formal Gaussian approximation. The ORIGINAL normalized cup has coefficients phat_(i,j)=x^(-j)delta_(i+j,d)/sqrt(N). For ANY unit vector v in C^N define its actual reflected dual by (J_x bar v)_j=x^(-j) conjugate(v_(d-j)). It is a unit vector and direct summation gives <v tensor J_x bar v, phat>=N^(-1/2). (9) For k cups choose arbitrary unit v_r and put z_0=tensor_r(v_r tensor J_x bar v_r), z=G_top^* z_0, phihat=G_top^* uhat. With ALL original pivot phases retained, <z,phihat>=N^(-k/2). (10) In particular cup-compatible localized product packets have a known nonzero cap coefficient, uniformly in their centers and N. This is the actual positive cap state fixed in the source theorem; it is not a new favorable cap or a division by the knot period. There is an exact whole-source decomposition. Choose ANY orthonormal basis {v_(r,a)} on the first head of each pair and form the matched packets z_a above. They are orthonormal and phihat=N^(-k/2) sum_a z_a, P_N=chi_N N^(k/2-1) sum_a <z_a,W uhat>. (11) Thus every cap coefficient in this complete decomposition is the same positive polynomial factor. A single chosen packet may be included by extending its v_r to an orthonormal basis. The individual projector-weighted term is exactly chi_N N^(k/2-1)<z,W uhat>. For (7) this includes localized packets at the geometric compact point. On each odd head take a Gaussian of width sqrt(N), center N/3-1/2, and phase exp(-i Arg(t_r)j), with t_1=1,t_2=z; normalize on j=0,...,d and use the exact reflected dual above on its partner. The K,e,f mean-square errors relative to (7) and (2) are O(1/N): the clock varies by O(N^(-1/2)) across the packet, the shift error is O(N^(-1/2)), and the endpoint tails are exponentially small. Applying the specified G_top^* changes the shift phase only by Q, so the same leading geometric point is retained. Its cap coefficient is STILL exactly (10), rather than merely a formal Gaussian unit. At the conjugate Riley place the same construction has center 2N/3-1/2 and the conjugated t_r; the source root and pivots remain the original ones. Equation (11) does NOT say that its braid transition amplitudes have the same phase or that the geometric one is nonzero. Those amplitudes still contain the original whole W and can cancel in their sum. The bounded Nielsen constraints control their classical support, not their action-normalized coefficients. No exponential overlap estimate has been proved here. In particular one may not infer that a geometric point satisfying (3) has positive mass in the actual ket Gram limit. The exact criterion (3)-(6) and cap amplitude (9)-(11) locate the next missing quantity: the original braid transition to a geometric matched packet, with its actual analytic cycle, and its cancellation against the other transitions. Weak real Gram support alone cannot supply it; when (3) fails it cannot see that geometric point at all. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_compact_geometric_bridge_criterion.py): exact algebraic compact figure-eight data and literal four-plat Nielsen equations, common Hermitian identity, the two-bridge cardioid construction, and exact original cup/pivot packet coefficients.

title: What the original compact trace does not localize
text: # What the original compact trace does not localize 28 October 2026. Independent lower-bound audit. The exact compact coherent source is a genuine normalized matrix trace. That fact does not make the original crossing a pullback along a map of the compact source, and it does not make its total-normalized selected functional a rational trace on the geometric critical field. The two failures below concern the specified original operators and source, rather than arbitrary replacement periods. They exclude an exact finite-graph Lefschetz shortcut. They do not exclude a semiclassical Fourier-integral or derived-correspondence construction with its own source transport theorem. ## 1. Every original crossing level has a full-rank coherent endpoint Use the balanced factorial basis of the [compact source](compact_coherent_source_period.md), d=N-1, Q=exp(2 pi i/N), x=-exp(-pi i/N), F_k=(Q;Q)_k, F_0=1. Let B be the ORIGINAL checked positive crossing, with its common nonzero Cartan scalar retained externally. In these actual balanced coordinates its coefficient for |a,b> -> |b+k,a-k> is (-1)^k x^(-a-b-k) Q^[ab+(a-b)k-k(k+1)/2] {b+k choose k}_Q (Q x^2 Q^(-a);Q)_k. (1) This is the original coefficient followed by its literal two head factorial changes, as independently specified by `MixedEntries.direct` in the [whole-source audit](../experiments/audit_figure_eight_whole_source.py). No cup or co-source is replaced here. Because Q x^2=1 and Q^(-d)=Q, (1) gives B |d,0> = sum_(k=0)^d c_k |k,d-k>, c_k=(-1)^k x^(-d-k) Q^[d k-k(k+1)/2] F_k. (2) Every c_k is nonzero. Thus the two-head coefficient matrix is anti-diagonal with nonzero determinant: its Schmidt rank is exactly N. There is an equally useful transpose statement: B^t |d,0> = sum_(k=0)^d t_k |k,d-k>, t_k=x^(-d-k) Q^(-k) F_d/F_(d-k). (3) For (3), apply (1) to input (k,d-k) and transfer k, and use (Q^(-k);Q)_k=(-1)^k Q^[-k(k+1)/2] F_k. All t_k are again nonzero. These formulas are valid at every N>=2; neither a numerical asymptotic nor a particular knot is involved. The independent original E/Cartan evaluator also checks both formulas exactly over the existing prime-field realizations for N=2,...,13. ## 2. No exact single-graph pullback, even on a dense rational chart The coherent evaluation embedding for one head is the degree-d Veronese curve P^1 -> P(H^0(P^1,O(d))^*). For two heads its image lies in the rank-one locus for the tensor product of the two head spaces. The endpoint |d,0> is such an evaluation tensor; the binomial normalizations do not alter that endpoint or tensor rank. A weighted composition operator on sections along a rational map f:(P^1)^2 -->> (P^1)^2 has the following necessary property wherever it is defined: T^t ev_p = h(p) ev_(f(p)). (4) It therefore maps coherent evaluation tensors to rank-one tensors on a dense open set. Every two-by-two minor expressing rank at most one is a polynomial in the evaluation coordinates. If it vanishes on that dense open set it vanishes everywhere. If T is invertible its image never vanishes, so indeterminacy at a special endpoint cannot evade this test. Equation (3) contradicts (4). Consequently the actual B is not a weighted pullback on this compact source, even along a rational map defined only generically. Constant changes of frame on individual heads preserve tensor rank, so separate head frame changes do not repair the obstruction. More generally, suppose T is a sum of r weighted graph pullbacks on a common dense open set. Then T^t ev_p is a sum of r rank-one tensors, so it has matrix rank at most r there. The rank-at-most-r locus is closed, hence that bound holds at the endpoint as well. Equation (3) forces r >= N. (5) Thus an exact graph-pullback expansion of bounded branch number cannot be the sought fixed finite geometric Lefschetz model. A genuine quantized canonical correspondence is a different object: it need not act by pointwise composition on holomorphic sections. None of (2)--(5) rules out such an object or its eventual stationary localization. ## 3. The original selected leading source need not descend as a field trace There is a second, independent obstruction to applying [irreducible critical trace nonvanishing](irreducible_critical_source_and_whole_norm.md) without constructing its actual comparison map. Use the exact original positive figure-eight state, with its literal monomial insertions: mu_N(f)=sum_(n=0)^(N-1) |(Q;Q)_n|^2 f(Q^n), mu_N(1)=K_(4_1,N)>0. (6) This is the same source as in the [actual quotient obstruction](actual_source_quotient_and_critical_relation.md). Its continuous rate is H(s)=2 integral_0^s log(2 sin(pi t)) dt. The logarithmic endpoint singularities are integrable. Comparing the monotone endpoint pieces and ordinary interior Riemann sums gives log |(Q;Q)_n|^2=N H(n/N)+O(log N) uniformly in n. The unique global maximum of H on [0,1] is s=5/6. Indeed H'=2 log(2 sin pi s) has zeros 1/6 and 5/6, with the former a minimum; H(0)=H(1)=0 and H(5/6)>0. Thus for any fixed neighborhood U of 5/6 the normalized mass outside U is exponentially small. For every fixed Laurent polynomial f, positivity and continuity give mu_N(f)/mu_N(1) -> f(z_*), z_*=exp(-pi i/3). (7) In particular the actual leading normalized first moment is z_*. On the critical algebra K=Q[Z]/(Z^2-Z+1) this selected limiting functional is one complex embedding. It is not a Q-valued field trace: its value on Z is nonrational. After extension to C the algebra splits as C x C and the functional in (7) has weights (1,0), up to the order of its two embeddings. Its moment matrix has rank one. This is compatible with the exact finite source and with every nonzero weight in (6). The trace-duality theorem itself remains correct. Its hypothesis is an F-valued functional on an irreducible finite extension over F. The total-normalized selected functional in (7) does not have that rational descent. Taking F=C instead splits the critical algebra and removes irreducibility. Finite normalized matrix trace faithfulness does not supply the missing descent. This does NOT disprove rational descent of a separately action-normalized, multi-sector critical module. Division by the dominant total period automatically suppresses any lower-action sector, even if that sector has a nonzero rationally descended coefficient before this division. Thus (7) excludes identifying this particular limiting functional with a rational field trace; it does not show that the conjugate sector's own coefficient vanishes or that a suitable per-sector construction is impossible. Equation (7) is a diagnostic of the already specified original source, not a definition of a new source by dividing an unknown invariant. In particular it is not an adapter proposed for a general knot. ## 4. Consequence for the lower-bound strategy The exact compact trace supplies the original cycle and a faithful finite matrix pairing. It supplies neither the graph hypothesis of ordinary holomorphic Lefschetz localization nor rational descent of the total-normalized leading functional. Both shortcuts have concrete failures above. The separately action-normalized microlocal comparison is not decided by these tests. An action-normalized microlocal correspondence could still solve the problem, but it must construct the geometric summand and prove that the ORIGINAL source has nonzero image there. Rewriting its conclusion as a positive rank in a critical field does not bypass that step. No new broad-class exponential lower bound is proved by this audit.

title: Complementary root arcs preserve the source, but change its relative cycle
text: # Complementary root arcs preserve the source, but change its relative cycle 28 October 2026. A long actual root arc can be replaced exactly by the inverse complementary arc on a regular Fermat fiber. The central norm is compulsory. For a homogeneous original source, the resulting complementary period has an explicitly determined central divisor. Its scalar numerator is the SAME original selected coefficient. There is also an exact global cycle check: after any nonempty set of these complements, its bare ordinary product-torus integral, enclosing all the Fermat roots, is ZERO. The original nonzero source is carried by additional short-arc relative residue cycles. Thus center freedom does not justify substituting a bare convex torus for the original selected cycle. A construction retaining those relative cycles remains possible; it is not supplied by the complement identity. ## 1. Exact complementation with its original source normalizer Use the actual charged polynomial source with d=N-1, I_N(h)=lambda_C(P_h), K_N=chi_N/N sum_h W_h I_N(h), deg P_h=k d, lambda_C=[X_1^d ... X_k^d] mod(X_i^N-C_i). All W_h, pivots and chi_N remain. The equality between lambda_C and the specified Fermat residue, and its center independence at this degree, were proved in the [actual source theorem](actual_charged_socle_and_fermat_source.md). Let a genuine two-anchor block be B_L(X_i,X_j;a)=product_(r=0)^(L-1)(X_i-Q^r a X_j). For every 0<=L<=N, set D=B_(N-L)(X_i,X_j;aQ^L), F_i=X_i^N-C_i, K_ij=C_i-a^N C_j. Then the ordinary polynomial identity is B_L D=X_i^N-a^N X_j^N=K_ij+F_i-a^N F_j. (1) If K_ij!=0, D has no zero on the Fermat fiber and is a UNIT in its finite algebra. Its inverse is exactly B_L/K_ij. Thus replacing B_L by K_ij/D is a source-exact identity. There is no numerical normalization chosen by the value of a knot invariant. A nonunit tail coefficient alpha contributes its retained factor alpha^L; loops have already been evaluated as scalar monomials instead. Choose any fixed collection S of block slots, with r=|S|>=1, and write P_h=E_h product_(e in S)B_e. Define the rational representative R_h=E_h product_(e in S)D_e^(-1), K_S=product_(e in S)K_e. On the regular central domain where all K_e!=0, lambda_C(R_h)=I_N(h)/K_S. (2) The left means the SAME selected sum of local grid residues, not an unspecified contour integral of the rational representative. Equation (2) follows from (1) in the finite algebra and the original center independence of lambda_C(P_h). It fixes its central divisor exactly; its remaining scalar is the original period I_N(h). Knowing that divisor does not establish that this scalar is nonzero. For the actual bridge blocks a is a diagram-dependent power of x times an integer power of Q: the h-dependence enters only the latter. Consequently a^N=(x^N)^integer is a signed diagram datum, independent of the clocks. For a fixed choice of potential block slots, even when a length is zero, the same K_S can be retained through the full clock sum. The normalized complementary whole period is then exactly K_N/K_S. Choosing only the long blocks separately in each sector is also legitimate, but its norm product must remain inside that sum. ## 2. The bare source torus of the complemented form is exactly zero Define the rational k-form Omega_comp=K_S R_h(X) dX_1...dX_k/product_i F_i. (3) Take any ordinary product torus T with each radius larger than |C_i|^(1/N), and assume that no D_e vanishes anywhere on T. Such radii always exist: for unit arc coefficients any unequal endpoint radii avoid that edge's roots. The normalization of integrals is (2*pi*i)^(-k). Then EXACTLY integral_T Omega_comp=0. (4) Proof. Complementing one block changes its homogeneous X-degree from L to -(N-L), a decrease of N. Thus deg R_h=k(N-1)-rN. Dilate all radii of T by the same positive factor t>=1. No F_i pole is crossed, since all its roots were inside the original coordinate circle. The D_e are homogeneous, so their zero set cannot cross this common dilation either. Holomorphic top-form Stokes therefore makes the integral constant in t. On the dilated torus the k-form has size O(t^(-rN)): the numerator, dX and the Fermat denominators contribute respectively t^(k(N-1)-rN),t^k and t^(-kN). Its integral tends to zero. This proves (4), without an asymptotic exchange in N. For comparison, the original polynomial form Omega_poly=P_h dX/product_i F_i integrates on this same torus to lambda_C(P_h)=I_N(h). Thus the chosen sum of small grid-residue tori is not homologous to T in the complement of the NEW short-arc divisors unless that source value happens to vanish. Every nonzero original source requires an additional relative residue cycle in this presentation. The statement includes complementing a zero-length block: in the finite algebra 1=K_ij/(X_i^N-a^N X_j^N). This exact unit insertion still creates new off-fiber poles and a zero bare-torus integral. One cannot infer a selected geometric cycle merely from the poles of a chosen rational representative. ## 3. The missing source currents are explicit For one complemented block let P_h=E B_L and write F_other=product_(ell notin {i,j})F_ell. Equation (1) gives the EXACT identity of meromorphic forms Omega_poly-Omega_comp = E/D *[1/(F_j F_other)-a^N/(F_i F_other)] dX. (5) Each term has lost one Fermat denominator. It has zero local product residue at every original grid point because D is regular there. That explains why (1) preserves lambda_C. It does NOT make these currents zero on an enlarged torus: the short-arc divisors can supply the missing pole. Combining (4)--(5) gives I_N(h)=integral_T E/D *[1/(F_j F_other)-a^N/(F_i F_other)]dX. (6) Thus these explicitly retained currents carry the ENTIRE selected source on that torus. They cannot be declared subleading from the complement identity or from central regularity. With several complements, expanding each K_e+F_i-a^N F_j gives the corresponding finite collection of mixed source currents; dependent intersections must remain jointly regulated if they are converted to contour residues. ### A literal unit source cell The actual full closure/reproducing block is B_d(X,Y;Qt)=sum_(j=0)^d X^(d-j)(tY)^j. With the permitted exterior Y^d its original selected coefficient is EXACTLY one. Its complement is D=X-tY and K=C_X-t^N C_Y. On every product torus enclosing both Fermat root grids and avoiding X=tY, its complemented bare integral is zero by (4), while the two currents in (5) have sum one. This is the original reproducing source normalization, not an auxiliary quantum invariant. Both unpivoted t=1 and actual pivotal t=Q^(-1) cases retain these values. ## 4. A constructive finite forest residue formula The additional relative cycles have an exact algebraic decomposition. Choose ANY nonempty forest of actual two-anchor block slots and orient each edge from a child i to its parent p(i). Reverse a block when necessary using its exact identity B_L(X,Y;a)=(-a)^L Q^[L(L-1)/2] B_L(Y,X;a^(-1)Q^(1-L)). Every such scalar and the original gamma,W_h,chi_N remain. Write the oriented selected blocks as B_(L_i)(X_i,X_p;a_i), and put m_i=N-L_i, S_i=B_(m_i)(X_i,X_p;a_i Q^(L_i)), H_i=F_i S_i for a nonroot, H_r=F_r for a forest root, R=(product_i K_i) E. Here P_h=E product_i B_(L_i) includes the actual orientation scalars. Assume generic nonzero centers so ALL path norms C_i-(product_(edges on i->ancestor) a_e^N) C_ancestor are nonzero. This is stronger than merely checking each adjacent K_i. For the actual unit-root phases, a_e^N=+1 or -1, so pairwise distinct centers up to sign suffice. The result extends rationally wherever the corresponding joint residue is defined, but colliding residues must not be split independently. The triangular monic system H=0 has simple zeros. At a nonroot choose either F_i=0, or a short root X_i=a_i Q^(L_i+r_i)X_p, 0<=r_i<m_i. (7) Every component of chosen short edges has one root satisfying its original Fermat equation. This lists ALL zeros of H, not only an assumed geometric branch. With standard Grothendieck orientation, sum_(all H zeros) R(X)/det(partial H/partial X)=0. (8) Here is a direct proof of the zero. H_i is monic in its child variable, of degree N+m_i; a root equation has degree N. Their coefficients depend only on parents. Consecutive monic division in child-to-parent order gives a basis with child exponent <N+m_i and root exponent <N. Every reduction preserves or decreases TOTAL degree: the highest part is homogeneous and the central term decreases degree by N. The global sum of residues equals the coefficient of the top basis monomial. This follows inductively from the elementary one-variable identity that, for monic h, sum_(h(x)=0)A(x)/h'(x) is the highest coefficient of the remainder of A modulo h. The required top degree is sum_i(deg_(X_i)H_i-1)=k(N-1)+sum_nonroot m_i, whereas deg R=k(N-1)-sum_nonroot L_i. Their difference is exactly N times the number of forest edges, which is positive. The top coefficient therefore vanishes, proving (8). Equivalently the leading homogeneous system has no projective zero: start with each root and propagate zero to its children. There is no omitted residue at infinity. For the EMPTY choice of short edges every F_i vanishes. At those points R/product S_i=P_h, so their sum of residues is EXACTLY I_N(h). Consequently I_N(h)=-sum_(nonempty selected-short subsets) sum_(their explicit zeros) R/J_H. (9) All relative cycle coefficients in this complete decomposition are fixed, with no unknown knot scalar. For fixed diagram size its number of points is polynomial in N: it is at most product_roots N product_nonroots(N+m_i). This is a finite canonical residue presentation once the actual forest and orientations have been specified, not a positivity assertion about its terms. The triangular Jacobian is completely explicit. Its factor at i is N X_i^d S_i(X) if F_i=0, (X_i^N-C_i) partial_(X_i)S_i if S_i=0, and at an original forest root it is N X_r^d. At the short root (7), partial_(X_i)S_i =(a_i Q^(L_i)X_p)^(m_i-1) *(-1)^r_i Q^[r_i(m_i-1)-r_i(r_i+1)/2] *F_(r_i) F_(m_i-1-r_i), F_j=(Q;Q)_j. (10) This is obtained by splitting the other roots at r_i. Every factor is nonzero under the stated genericity; its possible exponential size is retained. For an entirely selected SPANNING tree, X_i=beta_i X_r. Homogeneity of E cancels all powers of X_r against (10) and the root Jacobian. The N identical root labels cancel its 1/N exactly, leaving an explicit sum of products of the factorials in (10), the evaluated remaining actual blocks E(beta), and the retained central path norms. This is an exact full-source channel, but it is generally only ONE part of (9). The mixed subsets must not be discarded. More generally, grouping a selected component into one root gives source charge d+sum_selected_internal(d-L_i), which can exceed N-1. Its remaining regular-Fermat root sum has genuine winding sectors. It cannot be called the ordinary top coefficient, or simplified by dropping cyclic aliases, before the stated component sums or a further source identity have been performed. ## 5. An arbitrary-block contraction, with its changed source charge The one-edge case also has a direct ordinary-coefficient formulation. Put m=N-L, b_r=aQ^(L+r), and w_r=1/product_(s!=r)(b_r-b_s), 0<=r<m. For ANY polynomial exterior E and all other original charges equal to d, there is the exact source identity [X_i^d X_j^d X_other^d] B_L E =sum_(r<m) w_r [X_j^(2d-L) X_other^d] E(X_i=b_r X_j). (11) Its ordinary parent charge is 2d-L=d+m-1, and must be retained. The root sum is essential; its individual regular-Fermat channels need not have the same ordinary coefficient. Proof. The Lagrange sums sum_r w_r b_r^p vanish for p<m-1 and equal h_(p-m+1)(b) for p>=m-1. Their generating function is sum_(k>=0)h_k(b)t^k =product_(s=0)^(L-1)(1-aQ^s t)/(1-a^N t^N). Only p<=2d-L can contribute to the coefficient on the right, hence k<=d. In that range h_k is exactly the kth coefficient of the displayed numerator, including its zero range L<k<N. These are precisely the coefficients of B_L needed on the left. This proves (11), without choosing an unknown normalization or a geometric cycle. For subsequent charges larger than d, the same short-root formula cannot simply be iterated: the next complete homogeneous index may reach N, where the denominator above produces aliases. For example N=3,L=2,E=X_i^3, with tail charge 2 and parent charge 3, gives zero on the original side but a nonzero short-root evaluation. The full forest formula (9) retains the necessary mixed channels; further charge/jet reductions require an additional explicit source identity. ## 6. Consequence for a geometric cycle construction Complementation itself is fully authorized by the existing actual source and preserves every normalization. It can replace long arcs by shorter inverse factors and may provide useful geometric charts. But its selected relative cycle has to be transported as well. Equations (4)--(6) show precisely why a bare torus replacement loses the original source, even with arbitrary regular Fermat centers. Large N-dependent centers need extra care: K_e can itself carry an exponential action. It is retained in (1)--(6), and fixed-center tame Fourier-frame estimates do not extend automatically to it. Conversely on fixed compact central domains these factors may be tame, but the relative currents still need not vanish. A successful Rivin comparison would therefore have to map the FULL grid/short-arc relative cycle, or the explicit currents (5), to a source-compatible convex chain and compute its geometric coefficient. Its starting value is not determined by the known central divisor (2). No broad volume upper or lower bound follows from the present complement identity alone. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_complementary_source_transport.py): actual charged polynomials after closure contraction, ALL triangular forest zeros and mixed short subsets, original scalar/orientation/path norms, factorial Jacobians and the spanning-tree root cancellation, a whole original signed pivotal scalar, and the original unit closure cell's zero bare integral versus nonzero source currents.

title: Complete augmented-link source normalization: no hidden exponential factor
text: # Complete augmented-link source normalization: no hidden exponential factor 29 October 2026. At the ORIGINAL boundary-parabolic complete color, the marked raw augmented-link period differs from its reduced zero-framed quantum/Kashaev evaluation only by a unit phase. The full one-cut ADO modified evaluation has the additional EXACT factor i^(N+3)/N. This is not an assertion about a generic meridian germ's size. It follows by retaining and then specializing that whole normalization germ and all actual turns. ## 1. Which scalar is raw, reduced, or modified Fix N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d and kappa=q^(d^2/2). The raw source here is the one in the [literal augmented pretzel diagram](actual_odd_pretzel_augmented_transfer_source.md): every full physical crossing has its original common Cartan, the crossing circles are the exact auxiliary pivotal traces L_N, and the main component has k genuine cups, k-1 ordinary caps and ONE original marked cap. Their balanced entries are p_ab=Nx^(-b)delta_(a+b,d), ell_ab=x^a delta_(a+b,d)/N, m_ab=x^b/N^2. The [direct turn/source calculation](quantum_bridge_cap_source.md) proves that these are precisely the original left/right duality and the selected cut projector. Specifically, with g=K^(1-N), e=psi phi, psi_a=1,phi_a=1/N and D=g^(-1)e, \[ \operatorname{Tr}(gDC)=\operatorname{Tr}(eC),\qquad m p=1. \tag{1} \] Each cup contributes its actual N, each ordinary cap 1/N, and the single marked cap 1/N^2. Their net scalar is EXACTLY 1/N, the original cut average. There is no other cut normalization waiting outside this raw tensor contraction. Balanced factorial changes cancel by exact basis covariance on every internal wire; their potentially exponential condition numbers are never estimated as an external scalar. At completeness the original twist is \[ \theta_d=q^{(d^2+2(1-N)d)/2}=q^{-d^2/2}=\kappa^{-1}. \tag{2} \] Therefore any recorded change from the actual diagram's framing to the chosen component framings is a product of integer powers of theta_d, and has modulus one. For a braid normalization using total writhe w it is theta_d^(-w)=kappa^w. If individual component self-framings are prescribed instead, their difference from this convention is a linking/framing character, again a unit phase. Mutual crossings are not silently called self-writhe; only the modulus statement is independent of that convention. Let A_raw be the actual tensor scalar and F_red the reduced zero-framed evaluation with the same chosen marked component. With its explicitly recorded framing character zeta_(N,L), \[ F_{\mathrm{red}}(L)=\zeta_{N,L}A_{\mathrm{raw}}(L), \qquad |\zeta_{N,L}|=1. \tag{3} \] This applies to the original auxiliary-circle diagram before or after its exact finite L_N contraction. Each closed auxiliary circle uses an ORDINARY pivotal trace already in L_N, with no added1/N, no division by its zero quantum dimension, and no extra modified dimension attached to it. Modifying every component independently would define a different normalization from the original one-cut source. ## 2. The modified dimension is specialized as a WHOLE germ At fixed root q, use the original meridian M=-q q^alpha=e^u, so alpha=d+u/Log q. The given modified dimension is \[ d_N(\alpha)=-q^{N(1-N)/2} \frac{q^{\alpha+1}-q^{-\alpha-1}} {q^{N\alpha}-q^{-N\alpha}}. \] Substitution, retaining both numerator and denominator, gives the ENTIRE specified local meridian function \[ d_N(e^u)=i^{N+3}\frac{\sinh u}{\sinh(Nu)},\qquad \boxed{d_N(1)=\frac{i^{N+3}}N.} \tag{4} \] This is a removable value, not a cancellation of two separately evaluated zeros. The full one-cut modified invariant, by its original definition, is d_N(M) times the reduced selected tangle scalar. Consequently \[ \mathcal N_N(L;M=1)=\frac{i^{N+3}}N F_{\mathrm{red}}(L), \qquad |\mathcal N_N|=\frac1N|A_{\mathrm{raw}}|. \tag{5} \] There is ONE such factor, on the marked component. The other components were closed by the ordinary trace in section 1. No claim about q-transverse derivatives is made: (4) is the actual meridian germ at a fixed root, not a substitution of a generic-q ordinary pivot for the full modified source. Equations (3)--(5) prove, in the respective two normalizations, |chi_red|=1, |chi_full|=N^(-1), (1/N)log|chi_red|=(1/N)log|chi_full|+log(N)/N=0. In particular the previously unspecified common external chi_N has zero exponential rate at THIS complete pointing. It need not have polynomial size on an arbitrary moving peripheral germ. ## 3. The enhanced Kashaev comparison extends to a link The original comparison note states its conclusion for knots. The local matrix identities used there also suffice for the present multicomponent source; no quotient-color argument is needed. Here is the missing connectivity check. Let a b-strand braid be colored by the full original V_N and close every head but the chosen first one with the actual pivot. The resulting cut matrix C commutes with E,F,K. This follows by partial trace of the explicit Hopf coproduct identities. For the K-pivot convention, tracing [A,E_prefix K_last+E_last] ordinarily over the last head yields commutation with E_prefix. For F, use K conservation and cyclicity to obtain Tr_last K_last[A,K_prefix^(-1)F_last]=0. Multiplying the original pivot by its complete scalar sign leaves this intertwining assertion intact. Repeating the argument closes all other heads, regardless of how many link components their permutation has. On the remaining V_N, K has N distinct weights and all internal F coefficients are nonzero. Thus C is a SCALAR matrix, at all even and composite N as well. Connectivity of the closed link was not used. The selected Tr(eC) is that scalar. The exact original Fourier/diagonal comparison in [the crossing calculation](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md) therefore works unchanged on this link cut. The large factorial similarities on traced factors cancel by cyclicity; the one on the open factor cancels because C is scalar. The local equality gamma alpha_q=alpha_K cancels all writhe factors. This compares the enhanced Kashaev period with the ordinary quantum-group enhancement with unknot value1, without any exponential gauge. To fix the dual/primal convention explicitly, the crossing note uses the dual pivot K^(-1). The original matrix B v_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j-N)) v_(d-j) in [the complete pointing comparison, section 2](kashaev_ado_pointing.md#2-exact-specialization-to-the-original-kashaev-period) intertwines that dual module with the primal one, conjugates its pivot to K, and satisfies R^T=(B tensor B)R(B^(-1) tensor B^(-1)). Those are direct generator and finite-crossing identities. The same full cut scalarity cancels this open-factor conjugation as well. Thus the primal K in the next display and the dual K^(-1) in the enhanced crossing comparison refer to identical scalar evaluations, with no additional normalization character. There is one useful sign when the latter is instead expressed with the ADO pivot/twist. At completeness g_ADO=(-1)^d K, theta_ADO=(-1)^d alpha_q. For a b-strand closure of total writhe w, the trace and framing ratios multiply to (-1)^(d(b-1-w)). If that closure has c components, its permutation gives w congruent to b-c modulo2. Hence \[ F_{\mathrm{red}}^{\mathrm{ADO}}(L) =(-1)^{d(c-1)}\langle L\rangle_N \tag{6} \] in those two explicitly specified enhanced-framing conventions. Other recorded choices of individual zero framings add only their already described unit twist character. In particular \[ \boxed{|\langle L\rangle_N|=|F_{\mathrm{red}}(L)| =|A_{\mathrm{raw}}(L)|.} \tag{7} \] For the odd-pretzel complete augmented diagram there is one main component and s genuine auxiliary circles, so c=s+1. The sign in (6) is (-1)^(ds); it is immaterial to the exponential rate but is not asserted to be one. The local full Cartan and the exact half-twist phases remain IN A_raw and in its proved leading constant. They are not counted a second time in chi. ## 4. What this closes, and its precise limit For the ORIGINAL one-cut enhanced Kashaev link evaluation, the full raw-period asymptotic has EXACTLY the same absolute value and exponential rate. For the full modified ADO evaluation it has the factor1/N and the phase in (4); its leading N-power must be adjusted accordingly. This closes the external normalization gate at the complete augmented source. It does not identify its action with a manifold volume without the geometric face-gluing calibration, and it proves no Dehn-filling or fixed-knot statement. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.py) compares original enhanced Kashaev matrices, ordinary quantum matrices, and the actual ADO pivot/twist through full cuts of both knots AND multicomponent links. It checks scalarity, the component-dependent sign, and the entire modified-dimension germ. It does not replace a link by a knot on the basis of an invariant.

title: Complete actual Casimir packets and their recoupling measure
text: # Complete actual Casimir packets and their recoupling measure 29 October 2026. Every physical integer-degree block has an explicit complete Casimir frame, including all confluent derivative columns. Its inverse is determined by a closed bilinear Christoffel--Darboux measure. That measure has explicit sine-factorial profiles; at degree N-1 all its double-node weights are polynomial. No tame eigenframe is inferred from tame spectral jets. The adjacent complete-channel change has an explicit all-entry product formula before restriction to a total-three-head multiplicity module. Its entries admit finite angle-factorial envelopes, with every inverse normalizer accounted for. The original cup and both cap rows are kept. The remaining marked-source norm and coherent overlap action are not asserted to have the sharp volume bound. ## 1. Literal Jacobi blocks and the high-degree mirror Put `q=exp(pi*i/N)`, `Q=q^2`, `d=N-1`, `x=q^d=-q^-1`. Use the original balanced F,Ecal,K and tensor Casimir Omega as in [the source Hermite theorem](actual_tame_c0_hermite_source_frame.md). For total degree `0<=T<=d`, write physical states `|u,T-u>`, `0<=u<=T`, and set `v=T-u`. The block J_T of Omega is COMPLEX SYMMETRIC tridiagonal. Its offdiagonal from u to u+1 is A_u=Q^(-v)(1-Q^v)(1-Q^(u+1)), 0<=u<T. (1) Its diagonal is D_u=(Q^(-u)-1)xQ^(-v)(1-Q^u) +(Q^(-v)-1)x^(-1)Q^u(1-Q^v) +q x^2Q^(-T)+q^(-1)x^(-2)Q^T. (2) Both formulas are direct application of F_tot E_tot and the actual Cartan. Every A_u is nonzero. The product is especially simple: B_T=product_(u=0)^(T-1) A_u=(-1)^T s_T^2, s_a=|(Q;Q)_a|. (3) For `T>d`, put `K=2d-T`, `a0=T-d`. Its block is the SAME J_K after translating the physical first index by a0. One proof uses the actual root Chevalley matrix `W|a>=(-1)^a|d-a>`: `W F W^-1=Ecal`, `W Ecal W^-1=F`, `W K W^-1=K^-1`. Chevalley followed by tensor flip commutes with Omega, and its coefficient is constant on a fixed integer degree. Thus the high blocks introduce no additional frame cost or missing channels. The same comparison follows from direct entries (1)--(2). ## 2. Explicit polynomial columns and generic-q confluence Define continuants p_0(z)=1, p_1(z)=z-D_0, p_(u+1)(z)=(z-D_u)p_u(z)-A_(u-1)^2 p_(u-1)(z). For `0<=u<=T` put f_u(z)=p_u(z)/(A_0...A_(u-1)), f_0=1. (4) The characteristic polynomial is P_T(z)=p_(T+1)(z)=product_(j=0)^T(z-c_j), c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1). (5) There are only simple or double nodes; a collision is exactly `j+l=d`. The self-paired node j=d/2, when integral, is simple. At a simple node take the column f(c_j); at a double node take BOTH f(c_j), f'(c_j). (6) The last-row recurrence gives `(J_T-z)f(z)=-P_T(z)e_T/B_T`. Hence (6) is the exact Jordan chain `(J_T-c)f'=f` at a double node. These are normalized ACTUAL Clebsch columns and their generic-q divided differences, not an arbitrarily supplied Jordan basis. To see this, vary q to zeta near q with ordinary highest weight d. Its highest vector at degree j has coefficients b_0=1 and b_a=(-1)^a x^(-a) Q^[a(j-1)-a(a-1)/2] (Q^(N-j);Q)_a/(Q^(N-a);Q)_a, (7) where in (7) `Q=zeta^2`, `x=zeta^d`. The E equation directly gives its successive ratio. Its divided descendant `F_tot^(T-j)h_j/(Q;Q)_(T-j)` has eigenvalue `zeta^(2N-1-2j)+zeta^(-2N+1+2j)`. Its first physical component is `x^(-(T-j))[T choose j]_Q`, nonzero near the root because `T<N`. Thus normalizing that component to one gives the unique first-row recurrence solution f(zeta,lambda_j(zeta)). This proves (5) by generic distinctness and dimension T+1. For colliding j,l the divided difference of these two normalized columns converges to f'(c); the common zeta derivative cancels. The eigenvalue gap has logarithmic derivative `2N` times `q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1)`, up to its order sign, and is nonzero. All denominators in (7) and in these low-degree descendants have factorial indices at most d. Exact generic-q duality is retained; no fixed-q meridian splitting is imposed on an exact dual cap. ## 3. The complete inverse, including every derivative normalizer Let V_T have the columns (6), grouped by distinct nodes. Different nodes and their chains are orthogonal for the BILINEAR pairing `u^T v`, because J_T is symmetric. This is not a Hermitian positivity assertion. Define `nu_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j+1))`. At a simple node c_j, the bilinear block is the nonzero scalar sigma_j=x^T nu_j P_T'(c_j)/B_T. (8) At a double node c=c_j=c_l, put `Q_j(z)=P_T(z)/(z-c)^2` and let r'_j be the derivative of the ORIGINAL normalized crossing polynomial at c. Its exact block is K_j=[[0,sigma_j],[sigma_j,sigma_j eta_j]], sigma_j=x^T nu_j Q_j(c)/B_T, eta_j=r'_j/nu_j+Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c). (9) In particular `sigma_j` never vanishes. The full frame and inverse are V_T^T V_T=K_T=directsum K_j, V_T^(-1)=K_T^(-1)V_T^T, K_j^(-1)=sigma_j^(-1)[[-eta_j,1],[1,0]] (10) for a double block; a simple block has inverse `sigma_j^-1`. This proves completeness and gives the ENTIRE inverse, without a condition-number guess or loss of a Jordan channel. Proof of the normalizers. Christoffel--Darboux for the continuants is sum_(u=0)^T f_u(z)f_u(w) =[P_T(z)p_T(w)-p_T(z)P_T(w)]/[(z-w)B_T^2]. Its simple-node specialization gives `P_T'(c)p_T(c)/B_T^2`. At a double node it gives `Q_j(c)p_T(c)/B_T^2` for f^T f', and `[Q_j(c)p_T'(c)+Q_j'(c)p_T(c)]/B_T^2` for f'^T f'. The first physical row of the ORIGINAL checked R in degree T has only the last column, with coefficient `kappa x^-T`. Therefore f_T(c_j)=x^T nu_j, f_T'(c_j)=x^T r'_j at a double node. Since `p_T=B_T f_T`, these formulas prove (8)--(9), including all phases. The actual full Cartan kappa cancels in this argument; it remains on R itself. ## 4. Exact sine-factorial measures, all parities and all degrees Write `a_j=|1-Q^(2j+1)|`. For a simple UNPAIRED j (`j<d-T`), |sigma_j|=s_(T-j)s_(T+j+1)/(s_T^2 a_j). (11) For a double pair `j<l=d-j<=T`, |sigma_j|=N s_(T-j)s_(T+j-d)/(s_T^2 a_j^2). (12) For the simple SELF-paired node `j=d/2<=T` at odd N, |sigma_j|=N s_(T-j)^2/s_T^2. (13) Every index lies in `0,...,d`. To prove these, factor each nonzero node difference into |c_j-c_k|=|1-Q^(j-k)| |1-Q^(j+k+1)|. The first product gives `s_j s_(T-j)`, deleting the partner factor when present. The second is the circular interval j+1,...,j+T+1: delete its self factor, and its unique root-zero partner if present. Root complementation `s_d=N` gives exactly (11)--(13). No separate factorwise N^O(N) bound is used. At T=d this simplifies to |sigma_j|=1/|1-Q^(2j+1)|^2 for EVERY double node, |sigma_(d/2)|=1 at the simple odd-level node. (14) Thus the full degree-d channel MEASURE is polynomial; this does not say the Clebsch frame or its Hermitian inverse is tame. For all double blocks, nonzero node gaps are at least `16/N^2` and the independently derived actual jets obey `|r'_j/nu_j|<=N^2/8`. Consequently `|eta_j|<=C N^3`. The inverse block in (10) has no additional exponential factor beyond its explicit `1/|sigma_j|`. ## 5. Explicit q-Hahn sums and a quantitative angle profile For `T<=d`, set `r=T-j` and `I={max(0,u-r),...,min(j,u)}`. At the actual root the value column is f_u(c_j)=x^r/[T choose j]_Q * sum_(a in I) (-1)^a x^[-(r-u+2a)] Q^[a(a-1)/2+a(r-u+a)] [j choose a]_Q [u choose a]_Q [T-u choose j-a]_Q. (15) This follows by expanding the actual highest vector (7) at the root, then applying the divided coproduct descendant. All three binomial factors retain their true root phases. In particular it is a closed finite Clebsch/q-Hahn sum, with no unknown knot period. Let beta denote the positive sine-binomial magnitude and put E_(T,j,u)=sum_(a in I) beta_(j,a)beta_(u,a) beta_(T-u,j-a)/beta_(T,j). (16) Then `|f_u(c_j)|<=E_(T,j,u)`. For a double pair j,l, |f_u'(c_j)|<=C N^2(1+log N) [E_(T,j,u)+E_(T,l,u)]. (17) For (17), differentiate the ACTUAL generic-q sums before their confluence. Each factorial has index below N and `|D_logzeta log F_a|<=N^2(1+log N)` at the root. There are a bounded number of factorial ratios and quadratic monomials in every summand and its endpoint normalizer. The eigenvalue-gap derivative has modulus at least eight. Thus differentiation costs only the displayed polynomial times the SAME positive factorial profiles. No exponential frame factor is put into the error term. Every beta in (16) is `N w_d(k,L-k,d-L)`, with exact sum d. Equivalently E is `N^2` times a finite sum of THREE such positive cell weights divided by the known boundary weight `w_d(j,T-j,d-T)`. Their charges and the range I are literal integer Clebsch incidence; the denominator is a compulsory boundary metric. Equations (10)--(13),(16)--(17) give a quantitative profile for the entire frame AND inverse, including every Jordan derivative. They are bounds, not assertions that the q-Hahn phases can be deleted at the sharp exponent or that these cells already form geometric edges. For high physical T extend the notation by `E_(T,j,u)=E_(2d-T,j,u-(T-d))`, and use the corresponding low-block measure sigma; inadmissible physical indices have value zero. ## 6. Complete adjacent-channel kernel at arbitrary width Lift the block frames to the full physical pair, preserving total T. Before restricting the THREE-head total Casimir, its complete pair coordinate change has the following exact entry. For input pair degree T, channel gamma (value or derivative type), and third physical index c, choose an output first physical index u. Put b=T-u, T'=b+c. If the physical indices are admissible, the output pair channel delta has coefficient Rcal_((u,T',delta);(T,gamma,c)) =V_T[u,gamma] (V_T'^(-1))[delta,b]. (18) Otherwise it is zero. Here high blocks use the unitary index translation from Section1. Equation (18) is simply the two ACTUAL pair frames sewn at the shared physical index; no complete channel or derivative row has been suppressed. Its entries are products of the finite q-Hahn columns and explicit inverse rows (10). For a double channel use `Ebar=E_j+E_l`, and for a simple channel use E_j. Equations (10),(16)--(17) give, uniformly in all admissible ports, an all-channel estimate of the form |Rcal|<=C N^5(1+log N)^2 Ebar_(T,gamma,u) Ebar_(T',delta,b)/|sigma_delta|. (19) All exponential factors on the right are the stated sine-factorial angle profiles. Restricting (18) to a fixed total-three-head Casimir or a source-generated Hom space is the subsequent genuine Racah contraction; it cannot be assumed from (18) alone. This distinction avoids a spurious tensor-multiplicity assertion at the root. The original signed pair crossing in these frames is exactly kappa times blocks `nu_j` at simple nodes and `[[nu_j,r'_j],[0,nu_j]]` at double nodes; its literal inverse retains the inverse derivative. Thus twist phases remain coherent when (18) is used in an arbitrary original braid. This is an all-exterior operator/source coordinate change, not a replacement invariant. The original pivot, framing, modified-dimension germ and peripheral line are transported unchanged. None is divided by the spectral measure sigma or selected afterward from the knot value. ## 7. The original source and the remaining estimate At degree d the c_* block may be replaced, by its explicit two-by-two adapter, with the uniformly conditioned p,t source frame of [the source Hermite theorem](actual_tame_c0_hermite_source_frame.md). If g_0=x^-d, its columns in the canonical f,f' coordinates are p=N g_0 f(c_*), t=-(mu_N/gamma_N)p+(g_0/gamma_N)f'(c_*). (20) This retains the ORIGINAL cup, ordinary cap and marked row. Ordinary caps vanish on other Casimir blocks and select the corresponding source derivative row; the cup lies in the source value channel. The marked row does NOT vanish on arbitrary other channels. Its complete coefficients are the explicit sums `m V_T`; in an assembled original plat integer degree forces the final marked pair to degree d, as before. No sectorwise marked-corner substitution is made here. For example a positive spectral packet metric can be specified by giving each canonical simple/double block the positive scalar `|sigma_j|` times identity, with the source block (20) handled in its actual p,t frame. This defines a full positive Gram by pullback through the COMPLETE frame. Its original marked dual norm and its adjacent overlap energies are explicit via (10),(15),(18), but no polynomial or sharp-volume bound for them is asserted. The new result supplies the actual all-channel frame, inverse measure and factorial/angle envelopes needed to ask that question. The remaining sharp step is a coherent estimate of (18) after its actual source-generated restrictions and closure, rather than separate absolute maximization of (16) or of twist eigenvalues. The subsequent [source-generated complete module](actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md) and [positive-source Gram calculation](actual_complete_channel_positive_gram.md) do give polynomial BOTH boundary norms after the actual J recoupling. However its fixed canonical positive-channel energy is [nonsharp already for the original figure-eight](actual_figure_eight_complete_channel_energy.md). This does not invalidate the frames or measures above; a sharp norm estimate must retain a more selective coherent packet, such as the [source-exact terminal construction](actual_terminal_packet_positive_gram.md), and control its general propagation. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.py): original generator-built blocks, all nodes and derivative columns, full inverse/bilinear measures and phases, finite Clebsch sums, high-degree mirror and original signed crossings/source adapters.

title: Positive complete-channel Grams with the original source
text: # Positive complete-channel Grams with the original source 29 October 2026. The complete source-generated N-dimensional module has an explicit positive Gram, independent of the braid word and its unknown value. All Casimir value AND derivative channels are retained. The original incoming cup and outgoing cap have polynomial norms in this metric. Their exact weighted norms below provide an honest Cauchy inequality for the ORIGINAL reduced scalar. This independently checks the full source formulas in [the complete multiplicity theorem](actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md#4a-a-complete-positive-hermite-metric-with-both-original-sources-polynomial). It also identifies the natural positive CD-weighted metric, distinct from the simpler unweighted channel metric. They are polynomially equivalent, so neither changes the exponential target. The unresolved step is an upper estimate on the COHERENT channel energy, not a missing boundary normalization. ## 1. Physical, right and channel coordinates Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d. Let w be the physical degree-d two-head vector representing the COMPLETE actual three-head Hopf intertwiner I_w. The original source module has actual recoupling J, original pair cup p, and ordinary cap ell, with EXACT identities Jp=Nx^(-d)e_d, ell J^(-1)=(x^d/N)e_0^T. (1) The module contains every intermediate Casimir Jordan channel. An original signed word W acts on it as W_mult. Its genuine reduced open-strand scalar, with its assigned external line chi_N, is K_N=chi_N ell W_mult p. (2) Equation (2) is the already proved whole-source opening of the marked cut: the exterior is the original Hopf braid, its remaining V map is scalar, and the actual cut functional has value one on I_V. It is NOT a local substitution of an ordinary cap for the unrestricted marked row in an arbitrary exterior. The full marked operator is retained when an exterior is not a Hopf intertwiner. Let V=V_d be the canonical COMPLETE Casimir/Hermite frame from [the all-channel theorem](actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md). The three coordinate systems are physical w, right y=Jw, channels z=V^(-1)y. Put F=V^(-1)J. For ANY explicitly assigned positive channel matrix D, G_D=F^* D F, u=Fp, b=ell F^(-1)=ell J^(-1)V, W_ch=F W_mult F^(-1). (3) G_D is positive definite of full rank N. It depends on the specified actual module and D, not on W or K_N. Exactly K_N=chi_N b W_ch u, ||p||_(G_D)^2=u^*D u, ||ell||_(G_D^(-1))^2=b D^(-1)b^*. (4) The two choices considered here are D=I and the positive CD measure `D_CD=directsum |sigma_j| I_(multiplicity j)`. The bilinear CD matrix itself is not being called positive. The complete original Cartan, framing, modified dimension and peripheral line remain in W and chi_N, exactly as assigned before the change of coordinates. ## 2. Exact cancellation in the complete source At a double node c=c_j let `Q_j(z)=P_N(z)/(z-c)^2`, `P_N=T_N+2`, and let nu_j be the original crossing eigenvalue. The canonical frame has endpoints (f_d(c),f_d'(c))=x^d(nu_j,r_N'(c)), K_j=sigma_j[[0,1],[1,eta_j]], eta_j=r_N'(c)/nu_j+Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c). Applying its EXACT inverse to (1) gives u_double=(-N nu_j sigma_j^(-1) Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c), N nu_j sigma_j^(-1)), b_double=(x^d/N,0). (5) The potentially large crossing derivative cancels in the first component. It has not been dropped: its cancellation uses the full value/derivative inverse, not an independent semisimple evaluation. At a simple node `u=N nu_j/sigma_j`, `b=x^d/N`. There is an exact elementary simplification. The Chebyshev polynomial defined by its recurrence obeys (4-z^2)P_N''-zP_N'+N^2(P_N-2)=0. It follows either by differentiating `T_N(2cos t)=2cos Nt`, or by induction in that recurrence. At every double root, Q_j(c)=N^2/(4-c^2), Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c)=c/(4-c^2), sigma_j=(-1)^d x^d nu_j/(4-c^2).
