(6) Thus (5) is simply u_double=N(-1)^d x^(-d)(-c,4-c^2), b_double=(x^d/N,0). (7) At the odd-level simple node c=-2, sigma=x^d nu, u=Nx^(-d), b=x^d/N. (8) All phases, parity and N factors are fixed. Neither original source has an exponential hidden normalization in these FULL coordinates. ## 3. Unweighted channel metric: the simpler Cauchy prefactor For D=I, let S_N=||u||_2^2 and T_N=||b||_2^2. Then exactly T_N=ceil(N/2)/N^2, S_N=N^2[sum_double(c_j^2+(4-c_j^2)^2)+1_(N odd)]. (9) The notation T_N here denotes a source norm, not the Chebyshev polynomial of Section2. Explicitly, S_N=N^2(4N-1), N odd, S_N=4N^3, N even and N>=6, S_4=192, S_2=64. These are the source formulas proved in the multiplicity note. They also follow directly by summing second and fourth powers of `2cos((2j+1)pi/N)` and pairing the repeated nodes. In particular S_N T_N<=4N^2, EVERY N>=2. (10) With the explicitly known unit source `u_0=u/sqrt(S_N)` define `E_I(W)=||W_ch u_0||_2^2`. Genuine Cauchy--Schwarz gives |K_N|^2<=|chi_N|^2 S_N T_N E_I(W) <=4|chi_N|^2 N^2 E_I(W). (11) There is no contraction to K_N in the definition of this Gram: F is the whole N-channel frame, u_0 has the explicit components (7)--(8), and W_ch is the full original matrix word with every mixed channel, phase and derivative retained. A useful balanced scalar normalization is G_bal=F^*F/N, E_bal(W)=||W_mult p||_(G_bal)^2 =||W_ch u||_2^2/N. (11a) Then the EXACT original outgoing dual norm is `||ell||_(G_bal^(-1))^2=ceil(N/2)/N<=1`, while the incoming norm squared is `S_N/N=O(N^2)`. In particular |K_N|^2<=|chi_N|^2 [ceil(N/2)/N] E_bal(W). (11b) This version needs no additional polynomial Cauchy loss: it uses the ORIGINAL unnormalized incoming cup. It is the same positive Gram up to its specified scalar, not a different source. ## 4. Positive CD measure: exact weighted source norms For D=D_CD, each double block has weight `(4-c_j^2)^(-1)`; the odd simple block has weight one. Let A_N=u^*D_CD u, B_N=b D_CD^(-1)b^*. Equations (7)--(8) give the exact finite formulas A_N=N^2[sum_double((4-c_j^2)+c_j^2/(4-c_j^2)) +1_(N odd)], B_N=N^(-2)[sum_double(4-c_j^2)+1_(N odd)]. (12) In closed form, A_N=N^4/4+N^3/2, B_N=1/N, N even>=4, A_N=N^2(N^2+3N+8)/6, B_N=(N+1)/N^2, N odd, A_2=16, B_2=1. (13) For a direct proof put theta_j=(2j+1)pi/N, so `4-c_j^2=4sin^2 theta_j`. The sum of reciprocal sine squares over odd indices is `N^2/4` at even N and `(N^2-1)/6` at odd N before the factor 1/4. These follow by subtracting even from all root reciprocal-square sums, or pairing the odd and even indices when N is odd. Also `c^2/(4-c^2)=4/(4-c^2)-1`. The first sine-square sum is a finite geometric sum; N=2 is its stated resonance. This proves (13) at composite and even levels without a modular half inverse. In particular `A_N B_N<=2N^3` for every N>=2. With `u_CD=u/sqrt(A_N)` and `E_CD(W)=||W_ch u_CD||_(D_CD)^2`, |K_N|^2<=|chi_N|^2 A_N B_N E_CD(W) <=2|chi_N|^2 N^3 E_CD(W). (14) This is a different natural positive metric from D=I; its source normalizers must not be mixed with (9). Both metrics retain the same complete channel source and original scalar. For the similarly balanced metric `F^*D_CD F/N`, the original outgoing dual norm squared is `N B_N<=2`; its incoming norm squared is `A_N/N=O(N^3)`. Its corresponding unnormalized-cup energy obeys the same bound as (11b), with coefficient `N B_N`. ## 5. One remaining coherent-energy assertion The two channel metrics are polynomially equivalent: I/4<=D_CD<=max(1,N^2/16) I. (15) The corresponding normalized-source energies E_I,E_CD therefore have the same exponential rate, whenever that rate or limsup is considered. No exponential conditioning is hidden by changing between these two explicitly related channel measures. The physical maps V and J themselves need not have polynomial norms. The right-frame generators are the FULL Hermite block matrix `D_braid=kappa r_N(Jordan(A))` and its complete conjugate `C D_braid C^(-1)`, where `C=V^(-1)JV`. Derivative rows remain. A single repeated-generator power costs polynomially, but C can carry exponential energy and phase cancellation. For this fixed positive Gram, the sufficient energy statement would be limsup_N (pi/N)log E_I(W)<=Vol(K), (16) or the stronger specified positive-geometric-partition comparison `E_I(W)<=exp(o(N)) Z_geo,N`. Equation (11) would then give the sharp original upper bound. It is not implied by positivity, the unit spectral values, a Krein conservation law, or polynomial boundary norms. Equivalently one may use E_bal of (11a): it differs from E_I by the explicit polynomial initial factor S_N/N. The subsequent [exact original energy calculation](actual_figure_eight_complete_channel_energy.md) shows that (16) is FALSE for this fixed candidate Gram already on the true figure-eight word `[2,-1,2,2]`. The odd-level simple channel has the exact coefficient proved in [the finite quadratic transform](actual_half_color_quadratic_source_transform.md), forcing `liminf_odd (pi/N)log E_bal>=v_8>Vol(4_1)`. The source/Cauchy theorems above remain exact; this particular positive norm retains more exponential energy than the final period. Both D=I and the polynomially equivalent CD metric have this problem. A [specified terminal packet Gram](actual_terminal_packet_positive_gram.md) provides a different source-preserving metric on the SAME complete module and recovers the sharp figure-eight energy. Its kernel is positively completed, not discarded. A general sharp prefix bound for that terminal construction is still unproved. This theorem solves the complete boundary-norm problem on the actual three-head Hom module (hence the original four-plat source), not the global coherent q-Racah growth problem. At larger bridge width the actual complete multiplicity reduction is known, but a compatible complete-channel positive metric still has to be constructed. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_channel_positive_gram.py): original coproduct-built complete source module and endpoint identities, full Hermite inverse and parity, both positive metrics/source norms, and original signed open-strand periods with the prescribed source.

title: The complete original circle has a complex packet through the quarter transition
text: # The complete original circle has a complex packet through the quarter transition 29 October 2026. The actual complete-circle polynomial z_N has a uniform nonzero asymptotic on a FIXED complex neighborhood of c=-2. The source is continued coherently through the quarter-index modulus crossing, using an exponentially accurate analytic diagonalization, a genuine high-index source anchor, and an explicit negative cumulative action for the unwanted channel. No phase-sector assumption is made. This is a fixed-root spectral/color-coordinate theorem. Its parameter below is NOT declared to be a peripheral meridian or an independently changed auxiliary-circle color. Such a source identification requires its own exact transform. All physical Casimir normal derivatives remain in the same original polynomial. ## 1. Statement and original finite source Keep N,d,q,Q,kappa,M,F_r,s_r and the exact A_r,D_r,U_r of [the coherent inner source](actual_pretzel_coherent_inner_gauss_elimination.md). Set u=pi r/N, nu_r=(-1)^r q^[r(r+1)] and define the EXACT chirp-normalized source on its physical grid by W_(N,r)=kappa^(-1)e^(i pi d/4)U_r/nu_r. The original Newton coefficient is EXACTLY b_(N,r)=e^(-i pi d/4) [s_(2r)/s_r^6] W_(N,r), z_N(c)=N^2 sum_(r=0)^M b_(N,r) product_(a<r)(c_a-c). (1) This follows by inserting D_r and the original factorial phases; no absolute value replaces the inner sum. The established source formula on strict high-index compact sets is W_(N,r)=w_0(u)[1+O(1/N)], w_0(u)=e^(iu/2)sqrt(sin u), u>pi/4. (2) There is eta_0>0 such that UNIFORMLY for |eta|<=eta_0, z_N(-2cosh eta)=e^(-i pi d/4)a(eta)exp[N j(eta)] [1+O(1/N)], (3) u_*(eta)=atan(cosh(eta/2)), T=2cosh eta, a(eta)=e^[i u_*(eta)/2]/[2((T+2)(T+6))^(1/4)], j(eta)=Psi(u_*(eta),eta), Psi(u,eta)=[-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u)]/pi +(1/(2pi))integral_0^(2u)Log(T+2cos v)dv. All branches are continued from real u=pi/4, eta=0; Lambda denotes its holomorphic local continuation in the displayed regular arguments. The amplitude is nonzero. Both a and j are even holomorphic functions of eta, so (3) is equivalently a holomorphic statement on a fixed disk in c=-2cosh eta about -2. It includes all fixed-order normal derivatives on a smaller disk by Cauchy's estimate. ## 2. The exact direction of transport and a source barrier The original backward Ward for U gives W_r=a_N(u)W_(r+1)+b_N(u)W_(r+2), (4) a_N=Q^(-1)(2Q^3Y^2+Q+1)/(1-QY)^2, b_N=-Q^(-1)(1-Q^3Y^2)(1+Q^2Y) /[(1-QY)^2(1-Q^2Y)], Y=e^(2iu). Thus X_r=(W_r,W_(r+1))^T propagates from HIGH r to LOW r: X_r=T_N(u_r)X_(r+1), T_N=[[a_N,b_N],[1,0]]. Its principal eigenvalues in this direction are lambda_slow=1, lambda_fast=-cot(u)^2. (5) They are distinct and nonzero near pi/4, including at the modulus crossing. That fact alone is insufficient for a selected-source claim. Use the [proved analytic diagonalization lemma](actual_local_analytic_transport_action_barrier.md) on a fixed complex neighborhood of pi/4, with the shift direction in (4). The same proof with the reversed shift supplies bounded V_N=V_0+O(1/N), nonzero diagonal d_s,d_f and R_N=O(exp(-sigma N)) such that EXACTLY V_N(u)^(-1)T_N(u)V_N(u+pi/N)=diag(d_s,d_f)+R_N. (6) The hypotheses here are explicit rational functions, not an unknown solution bound. On |Re u-pi/4|,|Im u|<=pi/32 the sine and cosine are bounded away from zero. The supplied eigenframe has columns (1,1)^T,(-cot^2u,1)^T; it and its inverse are bounded. One may use conservative bounds K=20, nonzero-root/gap bounds1/4 and eventual diagonal bound M=20, after rescaling x=u/pi and taking stadium radius 1/256. The rational coefficients have T_N-T_0=O(1/N) there, directly from Q-1=O(1/N) and their nonzero denominators. Hence the lemma gives a COMPUTABLE fixed sigma>0. Constants may be coarse; no optimal conversion exponent is needed. Choose a fixed sufficiently small delta>0, h=delta/4, and a high anchor grid point u_b=pi/4+2delta+O(1/N). Require delta<pi/4096 and 16delta^2/pi<sigma/4. Propagate(6) over [pi/4-h,u_b]. The cumulative REAL logarithmic action of the fast channel relative to the slow one is A_f(u)=pi^(-1)integral_u^(u_b)2log cot v dv. (7) This is the sign appropriate to HIGH-to-LOW transport, not its inverse. On this interval the total diagonal action width is at most 16delta^2/pi+O(1/N). For every target |u-pi/4|<=h the action in(7) is at most -gamma_0 for a fixed gamma_0>0. For example -8<=d(2log cot v)/dv<=-4 on the small window; the negative contribution from pi/4 to pi/4+2delta exceeds the possible positive contribution from pi/4-h to pi/4 by a fixed multiple of delta^2. At the high anchor, the ACTUAL source vector from(2) is w_0(u_b)(1,1)^T+O(1/N). Its slow component in V_N is bounded away from zero, and its fast component is O(1/N). Both entries are literal finite original U sums. In the interaction picture, all off-diagonal terms in(6) are bounded by exp[-N(sigma-width)]. Their product is I+O(N exp[-N(sigma-width)]). Equations(2),(7) therefore give, on the whole target grid, the selected slow solution with error O(exp(-gamma N)), for some fixed gamma>0. The other actual source component and every conversion term have been estimated, not deleted. There is no assumed adiabatic survival across a long crossing interval. ## 3. A holomorphic interpolant of the SAME selected grid packet The slow diagonal has d_s=1+O(1/N), holomorphically. Apply optimally truncated Euler--Maclaurin to the sum of Log d_s from u to u_b and multiply by the first component of V_N and its EXACT source coefficient at u_b. Construct it first on a fixed smaller complex tube containing the ENTIRE interval [pi/4-h,u_b], and then restrict to a still smaller tube around |u-pi/4|<=h. This defines a zero-free holomorphic function W_hat_N(u); its high-anchor value is part of the same interpolant, not an independent continuation constant. The usual analytic remainder is explicit: Cauchy bounds on a tube of radius a give a remainder bounded by C N[K/(pi aN)]^(2K); choose K=floor(cN). Thus, after shrinking the tube once, W_(N,r)=W_hat_N(pi r/N)+O(exp(-gamma' N)) (8) on its physical grid. This construction uses known coefficient functions and the finite source anchor; its normalization is not defined using the unknown closed circle value. The same EM formula at u and u+pi/N gives its diagonal shift relation with an exponential holomorphic residual. Together with(6) this makes W_hat_N satisfy(4) with an exponential residual throughout the tube. It and its derivatives are uniformly bounded: Log d_s=O(1/N), its sum is O(1), and the slow eigenvector component stays near1. Its leading amplitude is explicit, not a new connection constant. Expanding(4), using a_0+b_0=1, gives W_hat_N'/W_hat_N =-2i [partial_Q(a_N+b_N)]_(Q=1)/(a_0+2b_0)+O(1/N) =iY/(Y-1)+O(1/N). The denominator is -4Y/(1-Y)^2, so is nonzero. The high source anchor(2) fixes the solution of this first-order transport on the whole anchor-to-target tube. Integration on the fixed complex tube proves W_hat_N(u)=e^(iu/2)sqrt(sin u)[1+O(1/N)] (9) UNIFORMLY and holomorphically on the smaller tube, now through BOTH sides of pi/4. The exponential grid residual in(8) is separate from the inverse-N leading-amplitude error in(9). ## 4. Coherent outer sum, retained residuals and the full complex saddle At eta=0 the old ALL-index envelope of the exact source is J_1(u)+E(u), where J_1'=4log cot u/pi and E'=-2log cot u/pi below pi/4, E=0 above it. Hence its unique maximum is j_0=v_8/pi at pi/4. Every index outside the fixed window in(8) has a strict exponential gap. This includes all lower indices; they have not been set to zero. The same gap holds uniformly for sufficiently small complex eta. One can bound the Newton factor on its fixed enclosing Bernstein ellipse. Its continuum logarithm converges uniformly to the eta=0 logarithm as the ellipse shrinks: the only endpoint singularity is the integrable log(2+2cos v). Thus first choose the r-window/gap, then the fixed eta disk. The polynomial all-index prefactors do not affect the gap. On the retained window use(8), with the actual half-shift Newton product and sine factorials. These have zero-free holomorphic interpolants with exponentially small RELATIVE grid residuals. For the sine factorial, separate log(sin v/v), keep Gamma(k+1) exactly, and apply the same optimal EM bound to the regular factor. For the Newton product apply midpoint EM to Log(T+2cos v); its leading prefactor is ONE. All arguments here lie in regular compact strips. The discarded indices and ALL grid interpolation residuals are bounded absolutely by poly(N)exp[N(j_0-g)] for some fixed g>0, uniformly on a sufficiently small complex eta disk. This is not a claim inferred from pointwise O(1/N) continuation. The exact interpolant is used before its leading approximation, just as in the previous mixed-color source. For the retained finite r-sum choose half-grid vertical endpoints. Its exact cotangent rectangle has vertical |cot(Nu)|<=1. Their source phases have a fixed endpoint gap. At fixed height d_0 the horizontal cotangent errors are O(exp(-2Nd_0)), while the complete phase increases by at most C d_0^2 at eta=0. Choose d_0 small, then shrink the complex eta disk again. All four residual currents are strictly below the nearby saddle. The two constant cotangent parts give the same analytic integral with density N/pi; no integer residue or endpoint term has been discarded. The exponent is Psi in(3). At eta=0 its unique saddle is pi/4, with Psi_uu=-8/pi. Its analytic continuation is u_*(eta), and stays in the fixed interpolation tube. Ordinary analytic Gaussian expansion, with its fixed nonzero source density from(9), gives(3). Inserting the explicit sine-factorial prefactor gives exactly the stated a(eta). The external exp(-i pi d/4) and the unchanged Cartan normalization are already in(1), at both parities. Alternatively, this analytic leading coefficient is fixed uniquely by its agreement with the already proved real eta>0 formula on the nonempty overlap where the saddle lies strictly above pi/4. This identifies its continuation through eta=0 without an extra endpoint or parity factor. ## 5. Nodal concentration, original normals, and a retained-belt corollary The new packet has j(0)=j_0, j''(0)=1/(2pi), a(0)=2^(-9/4)e^(i pi/8). For real theta near0 this yields the whole original nodal packet z_N(-2cos theta)=e^(-i pi d/4)a(i theta) exp[Nj(i theta)][1+O(1/N)], j(i theta)=j_0-theta^2/(4pi)+O(theta^4). (10) There is also an exponential nodal gap outside every fixed theta neighborhood. For a root c_a in[-2,2], the factor at a unit w obeys |c_a-w-w^(-1)|<=|c_a-Rw-(Rw)^(-1)| for R>1. Apply the established same-angle circle envelope and let fixed R decrease toward1. Its continuum arc-convolution profile is continuous, has a unique maximum at(theta,u)=(0,pi/4), and has strictly smaller endpoint values. Compactness proves the gap. This uses the coherent U envelope, not a sector claim. For precision, the convolution is over the symmetric arc[-2u,2u] of g_1(t)=log|1-e^(it)|, centered at pi+theta. For0<u<pi/2, g_1 is strictly increasing with circular distance from0, so this arc integral has its unique maximum at theta=0. At u=0 or pi/2 it is constant in theta, but the resulting all-index actions are strictly less than j_0. Moreover ||g_R-g_1||_(L^1(S^1))->0, which bounds the difference of ALL these arc integrals uniformly in both u and theta. Thus the limiting argument uses a uniform integral bound, not pointwise logarithmic convergence at a root. Equation(3) is holomorphic in c, so the original first-normal source is retained by differentiating it on a smaller disk. For example z_N'(-2)/z_N(-2)=-N/(4pi)+O(1). Nothing is replaced by a value-only semisimple trace. The [exact complete-belt source](actual_complete_circle_nodal_energy_and_belt_sewing.md) therefore has, for every fixed integer k>=1, the nonzero ALL-parity asymptotic phi(L_N(z_N^sharp z_N)^k) =N^(3/2) 2^[-(9k+1)/2]/sqrt(k) exp(2kNj_0)[1+O(1/N)]. (11) Indeed its exact source is N sum_(a=0)^(N-1)|z_N(c_a)|^(2k). The nodal angles around -2 have step2pi/N, with shift0 for oddN and1/2 for evenN. The Gaussian in(10) gives the same leading sum at both shifts; all other nodes have the proved exponential gap. The derivative source producing this exact belt trace remains literal. This establishes a genuine complete-circle boundary packet and a whole original retained-belt amplitude. An independently changed ordinary auxiliary color, a filling transform, or a branched six-port sewing must still be identified with this packet by an exact source map. They are not inferred merely from the spectral parameter eta. Audit: [literal finite circle coefficients, quantum recurrence/chirp and boundary Gaussian](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_circle_boundary_packet.py), fresh replay PASS: eleven literal all-parity full sources and first normals, exact symbolic chirped recurrence/transport, and six growing-N complex-packet/normal/retained-belt calibrations. The analytic proof, not those finite calibrations, establishes the fixed neighborhood and the exponential current bounds. Independent review: the global critical-path auditor reread the exact transport direction, source barrier and anchor, holomorphic EM/cotangent argument, uniform angular gap and Gaussian constants, then freshly replayed the finite audit; PASS. This review concerns the stated spectral packet and complete retained-belt source, with the physical color/filling identification still separate.

title: A sharp complete-circle nodal energy from the original source
text: # A sharp complete-circle nodal energy from the original source 29 October 2026. The actual complete-circle packet has the sharp physical-node exponent \(v_8/\pi\). This follows from an exact discrete Chebyshev identity and the already proved NONZERO finite-source asymptotic on each fixed Bernstein ellipse. It needs no assertion about the phases of all Newton or monomial coefficients. Consequently a retained complete belt gives a positive original source, with an exact rate for every fixed reflected power. This is an all-channel source theorem. Its interpretation as a family of geometric belted sums requires a separate literal disk-gluing certificate; it is not inferred from the rate. ## 1. The unchanged packet and the actual complete belt Use \(N\geq2,d=N-1,q=e^{\pi i/N},Q=q^2\), and \[ M=\lfloor d/2\rfloor,\qquad c_a=2\cos((2a+1)\pi/N),\quad 0\leq a<N. \] These are the actual pair-Casimir nodes. Write \(m_c=2\) at each double node and \(m_{-2}=1\) at the odd simple node, so \(\sum_{c\ \mathrm{distinct}}m_c=N\). Let \[ z_N=\mathscr R(R^{-1}L_N),\qquad z_N^\sharp=\mathscr R(RL_N),\qquad j_0=v_8/\pi. \tag{1} \] Here \(R\) is the FULL original checked crossing, \(L_N\) its literal ordinary auxiliary-circle trace, and \(\mathscr R\) the genuine unscaled turn. The sharp sign is coefficient conjugation in the real Casimir variable, realized by the stated actual reflected diagram. The [complete polynomial proof](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md) gives \(\deg z_N=M\), at every parity, including every Casimir normal. The [full-circle sewing theorem](general_augmented_graph_source_extension.md#7-complete-circle-connectors-a-coherent-channel-sum-not-independent-blocks) proves on the FULL root algebra \[ \phi(L_Nfg)=N\sum_{c\ \mathrm{distinct}}m_c f(c)g(c). \tag{2} \] The positive weights in (2) come from the retained derivatives of \(L_N\) at its double zeros. Thus (2) does not discard the original nonsemisimple normal source. In particular the complete belt has not been replaced by a value-only trace with different normalization. ## 2. Exact discrete Chebyshev sampling, with both endpoint parities Let \(T_k(\cos\theta)=\cos(k\theta)\). For \(0\leq k,l\leq M\), \[ \frac1N\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}T_k(c_a/2)T_l(c_a/2) =\begin{cases}1,&k=l=0,\\1/2,&k=l>0,\\0,&k\ne l.\end{cases} \tag{3} \] Indeed \(\sum_a e^{in(2a+1)\pi/N}=0\) for \(0<|n|<N\), and \(k+l\leq2M<N\). Product-to-sum proves (3). Replacing the sum over \(a\) by the distinct-node sum with weights \(m_c\) is EXACT. The odd endpoint \(-2\) has weight one; there is no duplicated simple node or omitted even middle node. For any complex polynomial \(f\) of degree at most \(M\), write \[ f(z)=\sum_{k=0}^M a_kT_k(z/2),\qquad b(f)=\max_{c\ \mathrm{distinct}}|f(c)|. \] Equation (3) gives \[ a_0=\frac1N\sum_cm_cf(c),\qquad a_k=\frac2N\sum_cm_cf(c)T_k(c/2)\quad(k>0). \] Hence \(|a_0|\leq b(f), |a_k|\leq2b(f)\). For fixed \(\eta>0\), \[ \boxed{\quad |f(-2\cosh\eta)|\leq(2M+1)e^{M\eta}b(f) \leq N e^{M\eta}b(f). \quad} \tag{4} \] This uses \(T_k(-\cosh\eta)=(-1)^k\cosh(k\eta)\), not an extrapolation of numerical root values. It is stable at all levels. ## 3. Sharp maximum on the actual physical nodes The [proved finite-source circle theorem](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md), equations (9),(13)--(15), supplies for EVERY fixed \(\eta>0\) \[ z_N(-2\cosh\eta) =e^{-i\pi d/4}a(\eta)e^{Nj(\eta)}(1+o(1)), \qquad a(\eta)\ne0, \tag{5} \] \[ \limsup_N\frac1N\log\max_{|w|=e^\eta} |z_N(w+w^{-1})|\leq j(\eta),\qquad \lim_{\eta\downarrow0}j(\eta)=j_0. \tag{6} \] These are estimates for the literal finite polynomial, not a formal critical value or an unspecified contour. In particular (5) has a proved nonzero source amplitude. The limiting value in (6) follows from the displayed Lobachevsky formula there: \(j(0)=8\Lambda(\pi/4)/\pi=v_8/\pi\). Put \(b_N=b(z_N)\). The segment \([-2,2]\) lies inside every fixed Bernstein ellipse \(z=w+w^{-1},|w|=e^\eta\). The maximum principle and (6) give \[ \limsup_N N^{-1}\log b_N\leq j(\eta). \] Conversely (4),(5), and \(M/N\to1/2\) give \[ \liminf_N N^{-1}\log b_N\geq j(\eta)-\eta/2. \] Let \(\eta\downarrow0\) AFTER these limsup/liminf inequalities. No estimate uniform in a shrinking ellipse is required. We obtain \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log \max_{c\ \mathrm{distinct}}|z_N(c)|=\frac{v_8}{\pi}.} \tag{7} \] This does not assert that the maximizing node is always \(-2\), or that \(z_N(-2)\) has a nonzero limiting prefactor. In particular it does not require a special odd-level simple-node argument. ### A reusable bandlimited cyclotomic source criterion The same proof applies to ANY sequence of actual two-port source polynomials \(f_N\) of degree at most \(\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\). Suppose that for each fixed \(0<\eta<\eta_0\) an actual finite-source estimate proves \[ \liminf_N N^{-1}\log|f_N(-2\cosh\eta)|\geq j(\eta), \qquad \limsup_N N^{-1}\log\max_{|w|=e^\eta}|f_N(w+w^{-1})| \leq j(\eta), \tag{7a} \] where \(j(\eta)\to j(0)\in\mathbb R\) as \(\eta\downarrow0\). Then the exact DCT and the maximum principle give \[ \lim_N N^{-1}\log\max_c|f_N(c)|=j(0),\qquad \lim_N N^{-1}\log\phi(L_N f_N^\sharp f_N)=2j(0). \tag{7b} \] For the second assertion use (2), with \(N\max_c|f_N(c)|^2\leq\phi(L_N f_N^\sharp f_N) \leq N^2\max_c|f_N(c)|^2\). Thus (7a) is a concrete sufficient source/Fourier criterion for this complete-belt energy. It requires an actual selected-source lower estimate, not only a classical algebraic curve or a formal principal symbol. The verified packet \(z_N\) supplies (7a) by its finite-source central Gaussian, with no new assumption. The degree/nonaliasing hypothesis is essential. There are only \(M+1\) distinct physical nodes. Their product polynomial \(G_N(z)=\prod_c(z-c)\), of degree \(M+1\), is nonzero in the FULL Casimir algebra but vanishes at every physical node. Consequently its retained-belt energy is zero. At even \(N=2L\), explicitly \(G_N(z)=2T_L(z/2)\), so it has the nonzero radial exponential rate \(\eta/2\) while its sampled maximum vanishes identically. Its normal directions have not vanished in the full algebra; it is the exact complete-belt functional that pairs them to zero. Neither an arbitrary degree-near-\(N\) packet nor a saturated classical curve can be substituted into this bandlimited theorem. ## 4. Exact positive energies for arbitrary fixed reflected powers For any FIXED integer \(k\geq1\), define the literal complete-belt source \[ \mathcal B_{k,N} =\phi\!\left(L_N(z_N^\sharp z_N)^k\right) =N\sum_cm_c|z_N(c)|^{2k}>0. \tag{8} \] Strict positivity at every \(N\) follows already from the exact nonzero degree-\(M\) polynomial: it cannot vanish at all \(M+1\) distinct physical nodes. No asymptotic lower estimate is needed for this finite-level assertion. All the ports before the final closure remain those of the original two-strand tangle. Equation (8) consists of \(2k\) actual turned circle boxes in series, with ONE retained auxiliary complete circle around their two physical strands, and the original marked closure. It is not a metric defined from its final scalar. At every fixed \(N\) \[ N b_N^{2k}\leq\mathcal B_{k,N}\leq N^2 b_N^{2k}. \] Consequently \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \lim_N N^{-1}\log\mathcal B_{k,N}=2k\frac{v_8}{\pi}, \qquad \lim_N\frac{2\pi}{N}\log\mathcal B_{k,N}=4k v_8.} \tag{9} \] More generally let \(F_N=R^{e_N}z_N^a(z_N^\sharp)^b\), where \(a,b\geq0\) are fixed, \(a+b>0\), and \(e_N\) is ANY integer. The physical nodal values of \(R\) have modulus one, including even/composite levels. Therefore, EXACTLY, \[ \phi(L_NF_N^\sharp F_N) =N\sum_cm_c|z_N(c)|^{2(a+b)}, \tag{10} \] and its exponent is \(2(a+b)j_0\), independently of the twist. This is a source-preserving statement at this particular retained complete-belt seam. It is not a claim that arbitrary filled exterior volumes ignore twists: the complete belt cusp is still present. For the cut box \[ f_N=z_N^\sharp R^{-1} \] of the verified two-octahedron base, \(f_N^\sharp f_N=z_N^\sharp z_N\) in the FULL actual algebra, so (8) is also its genuine reflected complete-belt sewing. Its quantum cut differs from the Newton reflection cut used to prove that original base's rate. The one-cut reduced normalization and its recorded component/frame characters are those of the [complete-point comparison](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md). They have modulus one, or the stated single \(N^{-1}\) in the one-cut modified convention. They do not alter (9). No extra modified dimension is assigned to each auxiliary circle. ## 5. The remaining geometric gluing condition The [two-octahedron cut certificate](actual_reflected_two_circle_octahedral_base.md) supplies a concrete base and its actual twice-punctured crossing disks. The [literal stack and outer-collar theorem](actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md) now matches (8) with these actual geodesic pants gluings and proves its balanced complete-link volume equality. It also gives the metric for arbitrary fixed sign words and fixed integer outer collars; the nonzero asymptotic in that broader case uses the separate [coherent source Gaussian](actual_coherent_octahedral_belt_stack_asymptotic.md), not the positive-energy argument alone. General tangle or branched graph sewings do not inherit this particular collar certificate. In particular (8) must NOT be reinterpreted as a tree of scalar Frobenius vertices. Such a tree inserts \(L_N^{|E|}\) and vanishes at every even level when \(|E|\geq2\), as the exact earlier source calculation shows. A branched physical vertex has six open legs and its original saturated source kernel; (7) does not replace that kernel or prove its geometric energy bound. A general graph/filling volume conjecture remains open here. Audit: [full physical belt sources and exact discrete sampling](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_circle_nodal_energy_and_belt_sewing.py). Independent analytical reviews rederived the weighted DCT, both endpoint parities, the fixed-ellipse order of limits, the exact full-normal complete-circle trace, and the arbitrary-twist nodal identity. The focused audit was independently replayed: seven physical levels and 21 entire reflected powers, 40 complex sampling levels and six rate diagnostics passed. These checks do not supply a geometry or arbitrary-six-port extension beyond the stated seam.

title: The actual complete circle as a positive face polynomial
text: # The actual complete circle as a positive face polynomial 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. The complete ROOT circle, with its original weight and literal W/pi cup normalization, has an exact homogeneous polynomial factorization in its four face diagonals. For EVERY original folded channel that polynomial has nonnegative coefficients. Its local zeros enforce the original unwrapped channel support on a modular physical-head grid. Both level parities are included. This is local source algebra. The global face-grid measure, marked coefficient, stationary angle balance and original relative period are separate statements. ## 1. Exact local variables, lifts and scalar Put N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, and keep an actual integer 0<=a<=floor(d/2). Write m=d-a, s=d-2a and beta_a=S_(2a)/S_a^2, S_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N), k_a=1 if s=0, otherwise k_a=2. Let x,b,c,y be the outer, incoming-middle, outgoing-middle and final face diagonals, respectively. Choose their logarithms and use the literal centered physical heads S=d/2+N(Log x-Log b)/(2pi i), R=d/2+N(Log x-Log c)/(2pi i), sigma=d+N(Log x-Log y)/(2pi i). (1) The other physical heads are sigma-S and sigma-R. The auxiliary row is r=sigma-m, with its actual complement 2a-r. Thus Q^S=-q^-1 x/b, Q^(sigma-S)=-q^-1 b/y, Q^R=-q^-1 x/c, Q^(sigma-R)=-q^-1 c/y. The physical half-index and the auxiliary finite color are not confused. Define, using the ORIGINAL Hermitian matrices H_-,H_+, D_a(x,z,y)=det[z I+(x/2)H_-+(y/2)H_+], Ptilde_s(x,y)=product_(j=a+1)^(d-a)(x-Q^j y). (2) The empty determinants and products are one. Then the full coefficient of the specified regular root complete-circle source is EXACTLY h0_a W_a pi_a =k_a beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y) D_a(x,c,y) Ptilde_s(x,y)/(bc)^(d/2). (3) This is the fixed-root Hopf lift from the [original source envelope](actual_original_network_resonant_source_envelope.md), not a newly chosen off-grid continuation of a canceled exceptional kernel. A retained half twist multiplies (3) by its original fixed scalar omega_a^epsilon. Every power in (3) uses the logarithms in (1). If one adds literal N-lifts to R,S,sigma, the multiplier is (-1)^[d(n_R+n_S)]. The degree lift n_sigma cancels. It is identically one at odd N; at even N it must be retained or canceled by a proved global source-character calculation. Formula (3) makes no independent wrapping of an out-of-basis head. ## 2. Proof from the literal large white and cups At the root the actual white and dual are W_a(i,j;r)=(-1)^m q^[-dr+di-m(m-1)] H_m^1(Q^i,Q^j)/F_m, i+j=m+r, F_m=(Q;Q)_m, pi_a(r;i,j)=gamma_a^-1 p_(2a)(2a-r) W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r)/[pV(d-j)pV(d-i)]. Here gamma_a=q^(2-a^2)/N^2 is FIXED, h0_a=k_a N beta_a, pV(z)=N q^(-d^2+dz), and no paired norm pi_a W_a is inverted. The exact Chevalley factor is W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r)=q^[s(a-r)]W_a(i,j;r). Let T=Q^sigma and P_s(T)=product_(j=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^j). The exact root reflection of the SPECIFIED factorial section gives p_(2a)(d+a-sigma) =F_s q^[2m(d+a)] T^-a/P_s(T). (4) Indeed p_(d-s)(z)=F_s exp(pi i z)q^[(s-1)z] /product_(j=1)^s(1-Q^(z+j)); substitute z=d+a-sigma and retain exp(pi i z)=q^(Nz) literally. This proves (4) before canceling its possible poles. The root identities H_m=H_a P_s and H_a(U,V)=V^a K_a det[I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+], K_a=q^(a^2) beta_a, are source-exact finite polynomial identities. For comparison with the previously normalized entire circle C_a, substitution in the preceding literal W/pi expression gives the same head factor q^[d(R+S-2sigma)]/P_s(T) as in C_a. Its remaining scalar ratio is one: use F_j=(-i)^j q^[j(j+1)/2] S_j, S_(d-j)=N/S_j. The ratio reduces to q^[-2N(-2N+a+3)]=1. This proves h0_a W_a pi_a=C_a as the specified meromorphic root functions, not just at physical nodes. It does not identify their moving-q germs with a different generic lift. Now use the exact original normalized coefficient C_a=k_a V_a(d-sigma) q^[d(R+S-sigma)-2a^2] H_a(U_o,V_o)H_a(U_i,V_i)/T^a, V_a(h)=product_(j=a+1)^m 2sin(pi(h+j)/N). On the logarithms (1), direct factorization gives V_a(d-sigma)=Ptilde_s(x,y)/(xy)^(s/2), H_a(-q^-1 x/z,-q^-1 z/y)=(-q^-1)^a K_a y^-a D_a(x,z,y), q^[d(R+S-sigma)]=(xy/(bc))^(d/2). (5) For the first identity, the scalar in the sine product is i^s q^[-sum_(j=a+1)^m j]=i^s q^(-sN/2)=1. The remaining powers of xy cancel because d=2a+s, and K_a^2 q^(-2a^2)=beta_a^2. This proves (3) with its exact scalar. The same formulas show that additional N-lifts contribute (-1)^[d(n_R+n_S)+(s-d)n_sigma]=(-1)^[d(n_R+n_S)], since s-d=-2a. ## 3. Coefficient positivity and homogeneity D_a is homogeneous of degree a in x,z,y and has NONNEGATIVE REAL coefficients. This follows directly from the actual positive matrices, without assuming their entries are real. Factor H_-=B_-B_-* and H_+=B_+B_+*, and apply Cauchy--Binet to the rectangular matrix [sqrt(z) I, sqrt(x/2) B_-, sqrt(y/2) B_+]. Its determinant expansion is a sum of squared absolute minors times the indicated monomials, hence has the claimed coefficients. Since all three source matrices I,H_-,H_+ are positive definite, every homogeneous monomial of degree a in the three variables in fact has positive coefficient: subtract a sufficiently small positive multiple of I from each matrix, then select the three identity parts in the same Cauchy--Binet expansion. This is a coefficient statement for each fixed N,a; no uniform lower coefficient bound is claimed. More strongly, the retained forced product has the exact positive expansion for EVERY original folded label: Ptilde_s(x,y)=sum_(j=0)^s [S_s/(S_j S_(s-j))] x^(s-j)y^j. (7) To prove it, multiply its finite linear factors, or induct on their number, to obtain the coefficient (-1)^j Q^[(a+1)j+j(j-1)/2] [s choose j]_Q. The exact finite Gaussian coefficient is [s choose j]_Q=q^[j(s-j)] S_s/(S_j S_(s-j)). The remaining q exponent is j[2a+2+j-1+s-j]=j(2a+1+s)=jN. Its factor q^(jN)=(-1)^j cancels the displayed sign. This proves (7), whose coefficients are strictly positive because s<N. It also retains both maximal-fold parities: Ptilde=1 at odd simple fold and Ptilde=x+y at even maximal fold. No quarter-channel restriction is needed. The numerator in (3) is consequently a homogeneous polynomial of degree 2a+s=d with nonnegative coefficients in the four face variables. The monomial denominator and all finite logarithmic carries are still part of the source. Evaluating some face variables at complex values does not preserve positivity of the resulting specialized coefficients. ## 4. Local modular support retains one forced zero Take physical heads i,j in {0,...,d}, sigma=i+j. In the original white the unwrapped auxiliary row is r=sigma-m, so its actual allowed range is 0<=r<=2a, equivalently m<=sigma<=d+a. (6) At U=Q^i,V=Q^j, every Newton summand of H_a has factors forcing k<=i and a-k<=j. Therefore H_a(Q^i,Q^j)=0 if sigma<a. Exact root complementation sends the pair to (d-j,d-i), proving the same vanishing if sigma>2d-a. The complete circle retains ONE factor P_s(Q^sigma) after (4) cancels one of the two factors from its large numerators. Hence: * If sigma<m, either sigma<a and the small numerator vanishes, or a<=sigma<m and the retained P_s vanishes. * If sigma>d+a, either sigma>2d-a and the complementary small numerator vanishes, or sigma-N belongs to [a,m-1] and P_s vanishes. These are zeros of the canceled entire root coefficient, not an assignment of a value to an unexplained 0 times infinity. Thus a modular auxiliary residue outside its original support is killed locally even though its individual continued channel cup may have a pole. If both physical pairs of a circle survive and their totals agree modulo N, both totals lie in the SAME interval (6), containing only 2a+1<=N integers. They therefore agree exactly. The auxiliary row is then the original unwrapped row. The complementary physical cup also adds no modular states: i+j congruent to d modulo N with 0<=i,j<=d forces i+j=d, since d-N<0 and d+N>2d. This local check supplies the missing support input for a possible global face-grid transformation. The global primitive measure, even-level coset and carry phases, original marked-cap monomial and coefficient-extraction identity still require their own proof. Focused audit: [literal circle, coefficients and support](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial_results.json). At 85 digits it checks 94 literal LARGE-white/dual/cup circle identities and 22 retained N-lift characters, with maximum source error below 4.6e-83. Independent continuant expansions check 79 original D polynomials and their 823 strictly positive coefficients; 522 forced-product coefficients check the all-label sine-binomial formula. Exact finite-field checks retain 6910 forbidden physical-pair zeros, 28211 circle zeros for unequal totals congruent modulo N, 5274 supported unwrapped pairs and 150 original physical-cup modular support identities. Three symbolic calculations check the phase, outer degree and centered mark exponents. No numerical global source transformation is asserted by this audit. Independent full analytical local/source review: PASS. The reviewer checked the exact root Hopf normalization and both-parity carry sign, all-label sine-binomial positivity, and local modular support after ONE forced factor remains following the actual cup cancellation. Independent primary full analytical review and fresh redirected replay: PASS. The primary reader checked the full scalar and head powers, q-binomial phase cancellation, positive mixed determinant coefficients, and every unwrapped-support interval case. The fresh audit reproduced all reported counts and errors. Both reviews retain the local source scope; the global face-grid, marked coefficient and rate remain separate.

title: The complete positive circle quotient has ordinary channels and an exact source metric
text: # The complete positive circle quotient has ordinary channels and an exact source metric 29 October 2026. The positive reflected complete-color circle has an explicit ordinary-channel quotient, with a once-power affine-angle normalization. Its original ordinary and marked co-sources have exact polynomial dual costs. This gives a positive all-width Cauchy form with the ORIGINAL whole source, rather than an ordinary positive trace. The quotient does not erase the circle's nilpotent data: its inclusion and projection do NOT compose to the identity. Whole-block braiding is well typed on these channels, whereas a crossing that splits the pair need not descend. The remaining macroscopic reassociation estimate and the global geometric edge equations are not proved here. ## 1. The actual positive form and its star Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^-1 and the original complete physical V=V_N with H weights d-2a. Let E denote Ecal, so E|a>=(Q^(-a)-1)|a-1>, F|a>=(1-Q^(a+1))|a+1>, K|a>=q^d Q^(-a)|a>. Missing endpoints are zero. In the original positive Euclidean metric, E=-F^dagger and K^dagger=K^-1. On V tensor V let E_t,F_t,K_t be the actual coproducts, Omega=F_tE_t+qK_t+q^-1K_t^-1, and P the LITERAL exchange of the two physical legs. The complete ordinary circle is L=(-1)^d U_d(Omega/2), with its full auxiliary pivot and Cartan. The [positive reflection theorem](actual_complete_circle_reflection_positive.md) proves C=P L>=0, H=L P=P C P>=0, rank C=floor((N+1)/2)^2, ker C=ker L. (1) No positive pivotal trace is asserted. The actual adjoint identities are E_t^dagger P=-P F_t, F_t^dagger P=-P E_t, E_t^dagger C=-C F_t, F_t^dagger C=-C E_t, K_t^dagger C K_t=C, Omega^dagger C=C Omega. (2) For the first line expand E_t=E_1K_2+E_2 and F_t=F_1+K_1^-1F_2, then exchange the legs. The next line uses that L is an actual Hopf intertwiner. Thus ker C is a Hopf submodule, and Q_C=(V tensor V)/ker L, <[v],[w]>_C=v^dagger Cw (3) is positive definite, with E^dagger=-F and unitary K. This is a single-object star statement. Taking a tensor coproduct still reverses order under adjoints; product metrics are not thereby a positive monoidal source theory. The actual reflection/leg wiring remains. ## 2. The quotient is a complete sum of odd ordinary modules Put M=floor(d/2) and c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1), 0<=j<=M. These nodes are distinct and real. The exact Hopf decomposition is Q_C = orthogonal direct sum_(j=0)^M V_(2j+1). (4) Here V_l means the genuine l-dimensional ordinary highest-weight module, not its semisimplification. At odd N the last summand is the Steinberg V_N; it is retained. To prove (4), first use the equivalent Hopf module im L. At a paired Casimir node c_j, L has one nonzero image vector in precisely the physical integer degrees T=d-j,d-j+1,...,d+j. This follows from the complete pair Jordan blocks: a derivative can survive exactly when both members j and d-j are present. At odd N the simple Steinberg node has the SAME range. A nonzero image vector in the first degree is killed by E_t, since the preceding image weight space is zero, and has highest H weight 2j. Its F_t descendants are nonzero through order 2j, because E_t F_t^r v=rho^2 [r]_q[2j-r+1]_q F_t^(r-1)v, and every displayed q-number is nonzero. They span V_(2j+1). The dimensions sum to floor((N+1)/2)^2, the full rank in (1), so no extension or remaining channel is missing. Distinct real Casimirs are orthogonal by (2). ## 3. A canonical basis has explicit affine-angle weights Let E_j(z) be the ordinary Lagrange VALUE polynomial on the distinct nodes c_0,...,c_M, and set T_j=d-j, w_j=E_j(Omega)|0,T_j>, w_(j,r)=F_t^r w_j/F_r, 0<=r<=2j, F_r=(Q;Q)_r, s_r=|F_r|. The classes [w_(j,r)] form an orthogonal basis of Q_C. Value interpolation suffices modulo ker L; no generalized direction is deleted before the complete circle is applied. Their EXACT norms are ||[w_(j,r)]||_C^2=g_j beta(2j,r), beta(n,r)=s_n/[s_r s_(n-r)], (5) where g_j=2N beta(2j,j), 2j<d, g_(d/2)=N, 2j=d (odd N). (6) Here is a normalization proof. In degree T_j the positive CD resolution of L P has its j-th weight 2s_(d-j)^2/s_(d-2j), with weight s_(d/2)^2=N at the odd simple node. The first component of the reflected normalized eigenvector has modulus one. Projecting |0,T_j> to the quotient's c_j-channel thus gives this norm. Reflection s_a s_(d-a)=N gives (6). Finally (2) gives the descendant norm product product_(h=1)^r[-rho^2[h]_q[2j-h+1]_q]. Dividing by s_r^2 reduces it exactly to beta(2j,r), proving (5). These are once-power angle factors. With w_d(a,b,c)=1/(s_a s_b s_c), a+b+c=d, beta(2j,r)=N w_d(r,2j-r,d-2j), g_j=2N^2 w_d(j,j,d-2j) for paired nodes. (7) The odd Steinberg node has half that paired prefactor. All zero indices, scalar factors and true integer charges remain. Equations (5)--(7) do not identify a geometric triangulation's edge rows. In an orthonormal quotient basis the ladder coefficients have modulus 2sqrt(sin(pi(r+1)/N)sin(pi(2j-r)/N)). Consequently ||F||_Q, ||E||_Q<=2, ||K||_Q=1. (8) ## 4. Circle sewing retains the normal source instead of semisimplifying Let pi:V tensor V->Q_C be the quotient map in the orthonormal basis (5), so pi^dagger pi=C. Define iota=P pi^dagger. Both pi and iota are actual Hopf maps, by (2), and L=iota pi, pi iota=0 on every paired-node V_(2j+1), pi iota=N I on the odd Steinberg V_N. (9) Indeed pi L=(pi iota)pi and the induced circle on Q_C is its Casimir value, zero on the paired nodes and N at the odd simple node. Thus two complete circles sew to ZERO at every even level; at odd levels they retain precisely the genuine Steinberg channel. This is the full interior face contraction, including the normal directions, not an orthogonal identity resolution. Treating iota pi as an ordinary semisimple summand projector would lose the original nilpotent source. For the original cup p and normalized Hermite t, pi p=0, pi t=sqrt(2N^3)e_(0,0), iota e_(0,0)=sqrt(2/N)p, L t=2N p. (10) Thus the nonzero normal source is explicit even though the incoming cup itself is null. No radical is silently deleted from a physical input before its actual circle insertion. ## 5. The complete original boundary has a positive Cauchy form The original ordinary cap and restricted marked cap satisfy ell=pi_(0,0)/sqrt(2N^3), m_d=ell P/N=(pi P)_(0,0)/sqrt(2N^5). (11) The marked cap therefore uses H, not C. Their exact dual costs are 1/(2N^3) and 1/(2N^5). These statements follow also from the canonical highest norm g_0=2N and ell w_0=1/N. They retain the original turns; in particular m does not descend to Q_C because m p=1. The associated twist isometry is correspondingly typed: C uses R, whereas H uses the leg-exchanged R#=P R P, so R#^dagger H R#=H. No unexchanged R^dagger H R=H is presumed. Actual diagram reflection or duality must supply that leg exchange before using this transport. For an original 2k-head plat let v=W p^tensor k, with every full signed crossing, and retain its external line chi_N. After the k-1 ordinary caps, the original integer-degree conservation forces the last marked pair to degree d. Only THEN replace its unrestricted row by m_d. Put G_top=C^tensor(k-1) tensor H, Lambda=ell^tensor(k-1) tensor m_d. Tensoring the genuine local positive inequalities proves Lambda^dagger Lambda <= 2^(-k)N^(-(3k+2)) G_top, |K_N|^2<=|chi_N|^2 2^(-k)N^(-(3k+2)) v^dagger G_top v. (12) The dual cost is exact on the supported quotient. Adding exp(-N^2)I makes this a full positive metric with no larger dual cost; the added energy is negligible for a fixed word by the original coarse physical norm bound. This metric uses fixed operator/source data, not K_N. Its SHARP GEOMETRIC ENERGY BOUND is not proved. The marked restriction in (12) cannot be used for arbitrary non-degree-preserving exteriors. ## 6. Which overlap maps are well typed The whole-block braid R12 R23 carries L12 to L23 by the actual coproduct/naturality identity. It therefore maps Q_C tensor V to V tensor Q_C, preserving j, and is the literal mixed universal braiding of V_(2j+1) with V_N. The unrolled highest weight is exactly 2j, so no new half-Cartan mark or scalar is introduced. On an ordinary channel l=2j+1 the finite universal R and its inverse obey, in these positive single-object metrics, ||R_(l,N)^plusminus||<=sum_(r=0)^(l-1) 4^r/s_r. (13) The Cartan and checked flip are unitary. Each nilpotent coefficient has modulus1/s_r in the actual Ecal,F conventions; (8) proves (13). For l<=N/2 this is at most l[eN/(l-1)]^(l-1), with value1 for l=1, since s_r>=(4/N)^r r!. Hence every SUBLINEAR ordinary channel l=o(N) has exp(o(N)) block-braiding cost. The macroscopic channels retain their genuine angle energy rather than a claimed polynomial cost. A crossing which SPLITS the paired block is different. The original p12 tensor V lies in ker L12, yet its R23 image has nonzero ordinary cap kappa x^(-d)I. The cap inequality then implies that this image is not in ker C12. Thus a single split-pair R23 cannot propagate the same quotient. Actual reassociation must retain its full coupled ordinary-channel map and source interfaces; the local kernel cannot be discarded. This is the same concrete overlap test as [the cap-Ward source lemma](actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md#4b-a-local-cap-ward-quotient-does-not-propagate-through-an-adjacent-crossing), now for a genuine positive circle quotient. The quotient's integer labels and (7) are constructive inputs to an angle comparison. They do not prove the global full-2N edge character 2d, a coherent norm bound for arbitrary split-pair faces, or the sharp whole-source knot-volume bound. Those remain the substantive gluing problem, rather than a consequence of positivity of C alone. ### The first genuine split-pair face has a specified complete source module For an actual pair of overlapping COMPLETE circles the internal map is T_face=(I_V tensor pi)(iota tensor I_V): Q_C tensor V -> V tensor Q_C. (14) This is a Hopf map with the physical legs in their displayed order. It follows by factoring L23 L12, so it is valid with every exterior and all normal/source data. It is not an asserted unitary associator. The complete V_N source multiplicities on each side have dimension M+1. In the balanced quotient basis of (5), their highest vectors are h_j=sum_(r=0)^j alpha_(j,r)[w_(j,r)] tensor |j-r>, alpha_(j,r)=Q^(jr) F_j F_(2j-r)/[F_(j-r)F_(2j)], and on the right their coefficients are x^(-r)alpha_(j,r), with physical |j-r> first. These are actual unrolled highest-weight d vectors. The coproduct E recurrence determines them; its j equations on j+1 coefficients have all necessary nonzero arrows, so there is exactly one such vector per j. F^N=0 supplies its unique V_N lift. Thus no incomplete Clebsch source space is substituted. Their positive squared norms are exactly sum_(r=0)^j |alpha_(j,r)|^2 g_j beta(2j,r). (15) Equation (14) therefore reduces on the COMPLETE source to an explicit (M+1)-square ordinary-channel Racah packet with these fixed metrics. It carries the nontrivial macroscopic face estimate still needed for global geometric gluing. In its trivial-to-trivial channel there is already an exact source-coherent contraction: T_face[0,0]=2N I_V, (16) because pi_0=sqrt(2N^3)ell, iota_0=sqrt(2/N)p and the original snake is (I tensor ell)(p tensor I)=I. Thus both the same-pair sewing (9) and the source channel of the first overlapping face are polynomially controlled, with their full original factors retained. No polynomial norm is claimed for the remaining macroscopic Racah entries, and (15) is not identified with the geometric edge partition. ## 7. Audit [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_circle_positive_quotient.py) checks the actual image-module decomposition and all ladder endpoints, the positive quotient's orthogonal metric (5), the complete sewing operator (9), both original cap types and the full-source positive inequality (12). It uses the original finite generators and crossings; no unknown scalar period selects the basis or metric. Fresh replay: PASS seven exact original Hopf quotient families N=2,...,8, their complete highest Hom spaces in BOTH leg orders; seven full positive angle-metric and sewing families; five complete mixed-block braidings N=2,...,6, including both signed norm bounds; and nine original signed plat source inequalities through six physical heads. The mixed-block audit identifies the induced physical braid entry by entry with the ordinary-channel universal R, including its full Cartan. Whole-block braid naturality is separately checked on all input columns at N=2,...,5. The finite tests supplement the all-level proofs and make no macroscopic split-pair or global geometric-energy assertion.

title: The complete crossing circle is positive after the literal face reflection
text:
# The complete crossing circle is positive after the literal face reflection 29 October 2026. The ORIGINAL complete-color crossing-circle operator has a positive reflected tensor at every level and in every physical integer-degree block. Its original ordinary cap has an exact polynomial dual cost in this semidefinite form. Same-pair signed twists are exact isometries. None of these statements identifies an arbitrary augmented link contraction with a positive norm, or proves an open cusp-color geometric-survival corridor. ## 1. Actual operator, reflection, and complete channels Put (d=N-1), (q=e^{\pi i/N}), (Q=q^2), (x=q^d), and \[ s_a=|(Q;Q)_a|,\qquad s_0=1,\qquad 0\leq a\leq d. \] On the two ORIGINAL complete physical heads let \(\Omega\) be the coproduct Casimir, including the original Cartan normalization. The [literal mixed-circle calculation](actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md) proved, with the actual auxiliary pivot and no new color average, \[ L_N=(-1)^d U_d(\Omega/2),\qquad \mathcal P_N(\Omega)=0,\qquad \mathcal P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2. 	ag{1} \] Here the scalar polynomial \(U_d\) has \(U_0=1,U_1(z/2)=z\). Let \(P|a,bangle=|b,aangle\) be the LITERAL tensor flip. It is a face reflection, not an added crossing or a braid half-twist. For total degree \(0\leq T\leq d\), use \(|u,T-uangle\), \(0\leq u\leq T\). The original block \(J_T\) is complex symmetric, and direct conjugation of its displayed entries in the [complete channel theorem](actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md) gives \[ P\overline{J_T}=J_TP. 	ag{2} \] Its nodes, with multiplicities retained, are \[ c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1},\quad 0\leq j\leq T, \qquad 
u_j=(-1)^j q^{j(j+1)}. \] Let \(v_j=f(c_j)\) be its canonical eigenvector with first component one, as defined by the original continuant recurrence. Its last component is \((v_j)_T=x^T
u_j\). Thus uniqueness of its eigenline, (2), and its first component give \[ P\overline{v_j}=\overline{(v_j)_T}\,v_j. 	ag{3} \] All formulas below use this specified physical normalization, not a rescaled abstract Jordan basis. ## 2. Positive rank-one resolution in EVERY physical block The exact theorem is \[  oxed{\quad H_N=L_NP\succeq0,\qquad C_N=PL_N=PH_NP\succeq0.\quad} 	ag{4} \] In a low block \(T\leq d\), its full nonzero rank-one resolution is \[ H_N ig|_T=\sum_{\substack{j<d-j\leq T}}  rac{2s_T^2}{s_{T-j}s_{T+j-d}}\,v_jv_j^* +\mathbf1_{N\ \mathrm{odd},\ d/2\leq T}  rac{s_T^2}{s_{T-d/2}^2}\,v_{d/2}v_{d/2}^*. 	ag{5} \] Every displayed coefficient is STRICTLY positive. Unpaired simple nodes are killed. For \(T>d\), set \(K=2d-T\); translation of the first physical index by \(T-d\) identifies the block with the low block \(K\), including its literal reversal \(P\). Thus (5) covers all \(N^2\) physical pair states. In particular \[ \operatorname{rank}H_N =\operatorname{rank}C_N=\lfloor(N+1)/2floor^2. 	ag{6} \] Proof, including the signs. At a double node \(c=c_j=c_{d-j}\), write \(Q_j(z)=\prod_{k\leq T,k
e j,d-j}(z-c_k)\) and \(B_T=(-1)^T s_T^2\). The exact bilinear CD measure is \[ \sigma_j=v_j^{\mathsf T}f'(c) =(v_j)_T Q_j(c)/B_T. \] Since \(L_N(c)=0\), its entire Jordan contribution, including its normal part, is \[ L_N ig|_{c}= rac{L_N'(c)}{\sigma_j}v_jv_j^{\mathsf T}, \qquad L_N'(c)=(-1)^d rac{2N}{4-c^2}. 	ag{7} \] Equation (3) converts the reflected contribution to \[ (L_NP) ig|_c = rac{L_N'(c)B_T}{Q_j(c)}v_jv_j^*. 	ag{8} \] There are exactly \(d-T\) unpaired nodes; all lie above every paired node on the real line. Other paired factors in \(Q_j(c)\) are squares, and a possible self-paired node \(-2\) lies below it. Consequently \(\operatorname{sign}Q_j(c)=(-1)^{d-T}\). Together with \(\operatorname{sign}B_T=(-1)^T\), this proves strict positivity in (8), including even levels. The exact magnitude from the sine-factorial CD formula is the first coefficient in (5). At odd \(N\), the self-paired simple node \(-2\) has \(L_N(-2)=N\). The same argument uses \(\mathcal P_T'(-2)\) in place of \(Q_j(c)\); its sign is \((-1)^{d-T}=(-1)^T\), since \(d\) is even. Its exact coefficient is the second in (5). At any other simple node \(L_N(c_j)=0\). This proves (4)--(5). Counting the paired nodes, with both physical high/low blocks, gives (6). At the selected total degree \(T=d\), (5) simplifies particularly: \[ H_N ig|_d=N\sum_{j\ \mathrm{distinct}}m_jv_jv_j^*, \qquad m_j=2\ \mathrm{at\ double\ nodes},\quad m_j=1\ \mathrm{at\ the\ odd\ simple\ node}. 	ag{9} \] ## 3. Exact ordinary-cap cost and same-pair isometries Keep the original cup \(p\), ordinary cap \(\ell\), and normalized Hermite normal \(t\) from the [source frame theorem](actual_tame_c0_hermite_source_frame.md). They satisfy, with their literal scalar normalizations, \[ \ell=p^*P/N^2,\quad \ell t=1,\quad L_Np=0, \quad L_Nt=2Np. \] Therefore \[ C_Nt=2N^3\ell^*,\qquad  oxed{\quad \ell C_N^+\ell^*= rac1{2N^3},\qquad \ell^*\ell\preceq rac{C_N}{2N^3}.\quad} 	ag{10} \] Here \(+\) is the positive Moore--Penrose inverse. The first display explicitly puts \(\ell^*\) in the range of \(C_N\); any inverse solution differs from \(t/(2N^3)\) by its kernel, which \(\ell\) annihilates. Positive Cauchy then proves the second formula. This is an ALL-INPUT inequality on the physical pair, extending by zero outside degree \(d\) on its left and by the positive blocks on its right. No inverse of \(L_N\) is used. Tensoring (10), and tensoring with arbitrary spectator identities, gives for every physical \(2r+1\)-head vector \(\psi\) \[ |(\ell^{\otimes r}\otimes\langle d|)\psi|^2 \leq(2N^3)^{-r}\, \langle\psi,(C_N^{\otimes r}\otimes|dangle\langle d|) \psiangle. 	ag{11} \] It applies to the ORIGINAL marked scalar when the already proved whole-intertwiner theorem converts that scalar to this specified ordinary-cap matrix element. Arbitrary inserted marked exteriors retain their actual marked row. In particular \(p\) lies in the radical of \(C_N\), while the marked row has \(mp=1\); the marked row is NOT bounded in this seminorm by an illicit local replacement. The literal original same-pair crossing \(R\) satisfies \(R^*PR=P\) and commutes with \(L_N\). This holds on every physical block: (2) gives \(\Omega^*P=P\Omega\), and the actual polynomial \(r_N\) has unit values and purely imaginary logarithmic derivatives at the real double nodes. Thus \(\overline{r_N}r_N-1\) vanishes with the full multiplicity of \(\mathcal P_N\). Its functional calculus proves the assertion, with the original unit Cartan factor retained. Hence \[ (R^a)^* C_N R^a=C_N,\qquad a\in\mathbb Z. 	ag{12} \] Thus every signed same-pair twist is an exact isometry on this positive quotient. No invariance under an overlapping pair crossing is asserted. There is also a quantitative ordinary-color transmission bound on this SAME inserted-circle quotient. Since \(\Omega^*C_N=C_N\Omega\), its induced operator on \((V_d\otimes V_d)/\ker C_N\) is selfadjoint. At a double node its nilpotent value vector is in the radical, so the quotient has one ordinary eigenline; at the odd simple node it has the ordinary line. Every quotient eigenvalue is therefore one of the real \(c_j\). For \(c=2\cos	heta\), \(|U_{j-1}(c/2)|\leq j\), hence \[ L_j^*C_NL_j\preceq j^2C_N,\qquad 1\leq j\leq N. 	ag{12a} \] If \(\gcd(j,N)=1\), its retained nodal values are all nonzero and have modulus at least \(\sin(\pi/N)\geq2/N\). The possible odd simple node is interpreted by its removable value \(L_j(-2)=j\). Thus the inverse on this quotient has norm at most \(N/2\), and \[  rac4{N^2}C_N\preceq L_j^*C_NL_j\preceq j^2C_N \quad (\gcd(j,N)=1). 	ag{12b} \] These operator inequalities tensor with arbitrary spectators. They bound a transmission inserted on an existing complete-circle form; they do NOT express replacement of its defining \(L_N\) insertion by \(L_j\). That distinction is essential at the original cup below. ## 4. A once-power positive angle coefficient and a nonzero local channel For a paired node put \[ A=T-j,\quad B=T+j-d,\quad D=d-T. \] These are nonnegative ACTUAL integer indices with \(A+B+2D=d\). The coefficient in (5) is exactly \[ h_{T,j}= rac{2N^2}{s_As_Bs_D^2}. 	ag{13} \] The odd simple coefficient has the same formula without the factor 2 and with \(A=B\). This uses \(s_Ts_{d-T}=N\); it is a positive once-power four-angle factorial weight. It is not asserted to give the full edge incidence of an augmented-link triangulation. One original physical corner can be calculated without a Clebsch envelope, since every \((v_j)_0=1\): \[ (H_N|_T)_{0,0} =s_T^2\sum_{a=0}^{2T-d} rac1{s_as_{2T-d-a}}, \quad 2T\geq d, 	ag{14} \] and it is zero for \(2T<d\). The full sum over both members of a double pair supplies its factor2; the odd simple midpoint is counted once. Consequently the corner is strictly nonzero on every admitted physical block. The uniform all-index factorial estimate and midpoint maximization give, with \(	au=T/N\), \[ \log (H_N|_T)_{0,0} = rac N\pi\left[-2\Lambda(\pi	au) +2\Lambda igl(\pi(	au-	frac12) igr)ight] +O(\log N),\qquad 2T\geq d. 	ag{15} \] The formula is uniform through the endpoints, with the continuous odd extension of \(\Lambda\) if \(	au=1/2-1/(2N)\). To verify midpoint maximization, at fixed sum \(s\leq1\) the function \(\Lambda(\pi a)+\Lambda(\pi(s-a))\) increases up to \(s/2\) and decreases after it: its derivative has the sign of \(\sin(\pi(s-a))-\sin(\pi a)\). Selecting a nearest integer midpoint gives the lower bound; summing at most \(N\) terms gives the upper bound. Integer shifts by \(d=N-1\) cost only \(O(\log N)\). The bracket in (15) has its unique maximum at \(	au=3/4\), equal to \(4\Lambda(\pi/4)=v_8/2\). Thus \[ \log\max_T (H_N|_T)_{0,0} =Nv_8/(2\pi)+O(\log N). 	ag{16} \] This is a quantitative, positive, nonzero ORIGINAL local circle channel at all levels. It is not a nonzero geometric coefficient of an arbitrary assembled augmented-link source. ## 5. The open color corridor still requires an actual source argument The positivity is special to the COMPLETE circle. For any \(1\leq j<N\), the reflected ordinary circle \(PL_j\) is Hermitian but INDEFINITE already on the original source plane. Indeed \[ L_jp=\lambda_jp,\qquad \lambda_j=(-1)^{j-1} rac{\sin(\pi j/N)}{\sin(\pi/N)}
e0. \] In the basis \(p,t\), its Hermitian quadratic form has top-left entry zero and off-diagonal entry \(N^2\lambda_j
e0\), so its two-by-two determinant is negative. Thus a nonzero geometric coefficient on an OPEN cusp-color corridor cannot be inferred by continuing local positive-semidefiniteness. It may instead follow from a source-preserving contour and analytic continuation, but that requires its own original-cycle and Stokes/boundary estimates. Likewise local positivity does not identify a whole planar augmented network with a squared norm: all reflected leg identifications, ordinary pivots, the sole modified cut and any extra complete components have to match in the global tensor contraction. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_circle_reflection_positive.py) checks every physical block, the exact CD positive resolution, original cup/ordinary/marked typing, same-pair actual signed twists, and the positive corner/profile, with separate literal mixed-circle checks. Fresh replay: PASS six literal mixed universal/pivotal circles at \(N=2,\ldots,7\); eleven complete physical PSD/CD/source/twist families at \(N=2,\ldots,12\), including every high-degree mirror; four uniform positive-corner profiles through \(N=128\).

title: A fixed complex external-color packet for the original complete core
text: # A fixed complex external-color packet for the original complete core 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed and frozen. This note assembles the exponentially accurate local interpolation into the actual shared-face period. The theorem applies to each fixed certified augmented plat at arbitrary fixed bridge width. Its object is the exact complete-image term in color reflection. The other reflected terms remain part of the long-filling problem. Subsequent geometric identification: the [marked deformation theorem](actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.md) resolves the boundary reconstruction dependency stated below, retaining the primitive collar and the complex regulator boundary correction. It does not remove the ordinary-color subsets from the full source. ## 1. The finite object and theorem Fix a connected labeled convex ideal right-angled augmented source D covered by the [signed complete-source theorem](general_signed_augmented_source_volume.md). Retain its actual two marked faces, exterior normalization, and a vector of half twists epsilon_i in {0,1,-1}. Let R be its number of crossing circles and n=R-1 the dimension of the finite-face logarithmic torus after fixing scale. All constants below may depend on this fixed labeled diagram. Its bridge number and matching graph are otherwise unrestricted within that geometric certificate. Set d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), s0=d-2M, and delta_min=s0/(2N). The [exact color reflection](actual_external_circle_reflection_and_cusp.md) specifies the complete-image core F_N(h), before any asymptotics, by multiplying each complete channel a_i by cos(pi h_i(d-2a_i)/N). In particular F_N(0) is the original signed complete augmented source. Cosine makes F_N(h) an entire function of its external variables h. No interpolation of an unspecified sequence is being chosen here. The following holds on a fixed complex polydisc |chi_i|<rho, where chi=h/N. There are holomorphic critical actions S_N(chi), and nonsingular symmetric Hessians K_N(chi) of dimension m=2R-1, such that F_N(N chi)/F_N(0) = exp[N(S_N(chi)-S_N(0))] sqrt[det K_N(0)/det K_N(chi)] [1+O(N^-1)]. (1) The error is uniform on a smaller closed polydisc. The square root is the holomorphic branch equal to1 at chi=0. Thus the actual core is nonzero throughout that closed polydisc for all sufficiently large N. Both parities and composite quantum levels are included. The functions S_N converge holomorphically to S, and S(0)=Vol(Y_D^epsilon)/(2pi)=Vol(Q_D)/pi, lim (2pi/N) log|F_N(N chi)|=2pi Re S(chi). (2) The second equality is a locally uniform limit. The factor (1) retains S_N in its exponential: holomorphic convergence S_N -> S alone does not permit replacing exp(N S_N) by exp(N S). Only the COMPLETE VALUE of S in (2) is identified here with the actual hyperbolic volume. Identifying its whole germ with the marked geometric regulator requires the boundary reconstruction described in section7. The theorem also does not estimate the nonempty ordinary-color subsets in the original reflection identity. ## 2. Exact reflected period and analytic local factors Write B_(N,a)(x,b,c,y) = beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)P_(d-2a)(x,y). The [exact polynomial reflection](actual_positive_face_fixed_fold_packet.md) extends this original polynomial from 0<=a<=M to 0<=a<=d by B_(N,d-a)=B_(N,a); the half-twist eigenvalue obeys the same reflection. Consequently the original multiplicities k_a and cosine weights unfold to one full finite sum, with no omitted endpoint: F_N(N chi)=chi_(D,N) N^R product_i omega_M^epsilon_i *(2pi)^(-n) integral_(face torus) sum_(delta in Lambda_N^R) product_i B_(N,a_i)(r exp(i theta)) /product_(finite faces) (r_f exp(i theta_f))^d *exp[pi i N sum_i epsilon_i(delta_i^2-delta_min^2) +2pi i N sum_i chi_i delta_i] dtheta. (3) Here delta_i=(d-2a_i)/(2N), a_i=0,...,d. Lambda_N is the physical integer or half-integer lattice of mesh 1/N in the finite interval [-d/(2N),d/(2N)]. At fixed scale one theta coordinate is zero. The two marked face variables remain zero. Equation(3) is the literal marked coefficient measure, including its N^R factor and framing unit. Use r=r_N, the positive critical radius of the all-M coefficient. The [coefficient theorem](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md) gives r_N -> r_geom, transverse Hessian cN<=H_face,N<=CN, and fixed logarithmic derivatives O(N) on a common face neighborhood. Positive-matrix preconditioning makes the determinant factors nonzero on a fixed complex neighborhood, including the actual zero patterns. The [exponential interpolation theorem](actual_positive_face_exponential_fold_interpolation.md) supplies even holomorphic functions Phi_i,N(delta;w)=-H_i,N(delta;r_N exp w)/N on fixed complex delta and face neighborhoods, with Phi_i,N(0;w)=0, B_(N,a)(r_N exp w)/B_(N,M)(r_N exp w) = exp[-N(Phi_i,N(delta;w)-Phi_i,N(delta_min;w))] [1+O(exp(-cN))]. (4) This comparison holds on the actual REAL channel grid and for COMPLEX face variables w. Uniform holomorphic derivatives and comparison with V_i(delta;r_N exp w) hold on smaller neighborhoods; these functions converge to V_i(delta;r_geom exp w). In particular, at the finite radii, partial_delta^2 V_i(0;r_N exp w)=2C_i(r_N exp w), C_i=pi(sqrt(b_i(x_i+y_i)+x_i y_i) +sqrt(c_i(x_i+y_i)+x_i y_i))/(x_i+y_i)>0 at positive real radii. The comparison error in (4) is exponential, which is essential when the Fourier transform itself has an exponential decay. A relative O(N^-1) grid estimate would not suffice. ## 3. Excluding the original complement Choose small fixed cutoffs delta0,theta0 inside the neighborhoods of (4). If some |delta_i|>delta0, the original all-channel shared-radius bound gives an exp(-cN) gap relative to the complete scale. This is the bound proved from the literal determinant and forced polynomial in the [channel-rate theorem](actual_positive_face_channel_rate.md), together with the strict maximum at the fold. The external weight in (3) costs at most exp(pi N sum_i |Im chi_i|). A sufficiently small fixed chi polydisc preserves the gap. There are only polynomially many channels. For all |delta_i|<=delta0 but |theta|>theta0, apply the exact positive matrix contraction to every original determinant. Its pair-trace lower bounds cN are uniform for a/N in [1/2-delta0,1/2]. Indeed the bulk Cholesky-square bounds in the coefficient theorem use a fixed compact index interval strictly below N/2; choose delta0 so that every matrix under consideration contains that same macroscopic interval. The one-variable boundary factors need no pair trace. The remaining actual pair graph is connected and primitive, exactly as in that theorem. Thus, uniformly over these channels, |product_i B_(N,a_i)(r_N exp(i theta))| <= product_i B_(N,a_i)(r_N) *exp[-cN dist(theta,0)^2]. (5) Each forced polynomial has nonnegative coefficients and cannot increase the torus modulus. This is a global angular estimate on the actual physical summands, not on their local interpolants. Shrinking chi again preserves its fixed gap outside theta0. Both discarded parts of (3) are therefore bounded by a polynomial times exp[N(f_N-c)], where f_N=N^-1 log[product_i B_(N,M)(r_N)/product_f r_N,f^d]. Any polynomial factor is absorbed by reducing c for large N. ## 4. The selected joint critical point On the retained face box put w=i theta and define the marked logarithms psi_N(w)=N^-1 log[product_i B_(N,M)(r_N exp w)] -(d/N) sum_f log(r_N,f exp w_f), Psi_N(theta,delta;chi)=psi_N(i theta) -sum_i[Phi_i,N(delta_i;i theta)-Phi_i,N(delta_min;i theta)] +pi i sum_i epsilon_i(delta_i^2-delta_min^2) +2pi i sum_i chi_i delta_i. (6) All logs continue the original positive factors. The even-level anchor delta_min is retained. The framing and omega_M factors stay outside this phase. At chi=0, evenness makes every delta derivative vanish exactly at delta=0. Also d_theta psi_N(0)=0, and the anchor contributes only O(N^-2), with the same bound for fixed derivatives. The joint critical point therefore lies O(N^-2) from (theta,delta)=(0,0). The negative Hessian there has the blocks N^-1 H_face,N + O(N^-2), diag_i[2(C_i(r_N)-pi i epsilon_i)]+o(1). (7) Mixed theta/delta blocks vanish exactly at delta=0. The real quadratic part on real integration directions is uniformly positive. All fixed holomorphic derivatives of Psi_N are bounded independently of N. The analytic inverse-function argument now gives a unique nearby joint critical point z_N(chi) on a fixed small complex polydisc. One direct uniform construction is Newton iteration after multiplying by the inverse Hessian at chi=0: its norm is bounded, and the bounded third derivatives give a common contraction ball. Define S_N(chi)=Psi_N(z_N(chi);chi), K_N(chi)=-d_z^2 Psi_N(z_N(chi);chi). (8) The Hessian stays nonsingular and its real quadratic part stays positive along the translated real contour. S_N(chi)-f_N is uniformly small when chi is small. The neighborhood can therefore be chosen so that the preceding fixed complement gaps remain gaps relative to the selected critical value, not just relative to f_N. ## 5. Finite lattice to contour integral, with exponential errors Use (4) only on the retained physical grid. Its accumulated error in (3) is at most exp[N(f_N-c)] on a smaller fixed chi polydisc: the finite count is polynomial, the model is bounded by the original real scale up to the small complex Fourier cost, and (4) has a fixed exponential rate. For one channel write its lattice as z=alpha_N+j/N. Enclose its retained nodes in a rectangle whose vertical sides are halfway between the last retained node and the first deleted node, and whose horizontal sides have heights +/-eta. For a holomorphic f the exact residue identity is (1/N) sum_(retained nodes) f(z) =(1/(2i)) integral_(rectangle) cot(pi N(z-alpha_N)) f(z) dz. (9) On the upper and lower sides cot approaches -i and +i respectively, with errors O(exp(-2pi eta N)). On the vertical sides it is bounded because their real coordinates are lattice midpoints. The constant upper/lower terms deform to the real interval integral. The vertical closing segments are exponentially small by the original quadratic channel gap and its analytic continuation. Here are the estimates needed for that last assertion and for the horizontal errors. On the small box, the real Hessian bound from (7) and the bounded derivatives imply, for real theta and real channel coordinates x with imaginary shifts y, Re Psi_N(theta,x+i y;chi) <= f_N+C/N^2-c(|theta|^2+|x|^2) +C|y||x|+C|y|^2+C|chi|(|x|+|y|). For complex deficits the explicit peripheral boundary correction is retained. This note does not estimate the ordinary-color subset terms of the full mixed source or prove the long-filled knot limit. ## 1. (4) With m_i=exp(-pi i chi_i), this says m_i^2 R0_i(-J_i)^epsilon_i=1. Thus the input and output products are the same P_i. The collar C_i in (3) gives their actual simultaneous conjugacy. For a retained half twist put h_J=J_i^-1-1, a unit near completeness. The original physical auxiliary meridian is the regular matrix M_i=m_i R0_i h_J^(-epsilon_i) C_i^-1(P_i^-1-I)^epsilon_i. (6) This is exactly the original collar/Hurwitz expression from [the literal Morse presentation](actual_augmented_plat_critical_scheme.md), section 4. Its selected J_i-line eigenvalue is m_i, while det M_i=m_i^2 R0_i(-J_i)^epsilon_i=1. It commutes with P_i. Its inverse followed by the recorded Hurwitz half twist induces C_i on the main pair. The selected algebraic peripheral germ There is also a finite algebraic description of the representation germ, distinct from its analytic action. The actual cup and ordinary cap become opposite endpoint coordinates after that recoupling. The original Hermite source packet also has a polynomially conditioned recoupled frame, although the full recoupling matrix can have exponential norm. The same construction reduces the COMPLETE original even plat at arbitrary fixed width to a central-degree multiplicity space. The full marked cap is evaluated only after this whole invariant-tensor identification; its resulting source row and vector have explicitly polynomial norms. Every reduced signed generator is given below. No sharp whole-word norm, geometric coefficient, or complete-channel contractivity is inferred from this exact reduction. ## 1. Original finite modules and conventions Put N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d=-q^(-1), rho=q-q^(-1), F_a=(Q;Q)_a. On the original balanced V=V_d use F|a>=(1-Q^(a+1))|a+1>, Ecal|a>=(Q^(-a)-1)|a-1>, K|a>=xQ^(-a)|a>, H|a>=(d-2a)|a>, 0<=a<=d. (1) Missing endpoint arrows are zero. The ORIGINAL coproduct is F_12=F_1+K_1^(-1)F_2, E_12=Ecal_1 K_2+Ecal_2, K_12=K_1K_2. (2) Use these iterated coproducts on every physical prefix. All their N-th E and F powers vanish: the individual terms Q-commute, and the root q-binomial makes their N-th power the sum of the individual N-th powers. We retain the unrolled H, not only K=q^H. The original turns, including all N powers and the pivot, are p_(u,v)=N x^(-v) delta_(u+v,d), ell_(u,v)=x^(-u)Q^(-u)/N delta_(u+v,d), m_(u,v)=x^v/N^2, WITHOUT a degree delta. (3) The cup p and ordinary cap ell are literal Hopf maps. They satisfy the two snake equations, ell p=0 and m p=1. The marked row m is not an invariant cap and is never replaced by ell. The common Cartan kappa=q^(d^2/2), original framing, modified dimension and external scalar chi_N remain on the original crossing/source line. Write Omega=F_tot E_tot+qK_tot+q^(-1)K_tot^(-1). The original crossing is kappa r_N(Omega_pair), including its [confluent value AND derivative data](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md). Its inverse is the literal inverse polynomial. No semisimple root evaluation is substituted for a double channel. ## 2. A complete three-head Hom space from an explicit highest lift Let W=(V tensor V)_(integer degree d), with basis e_j=|j,d-j>, j=0,...,d. For EVERY w in W set H_L(w)=sum_(c=0)^d (-xQ)^c E_12^c w/F_c tensor |c>, I_w|a>=F_123^a H_L(w)/F_a, 0<=a<=d. (4) Then I_w is an actual unrolled Hopf intertwiner V -> V^tensor3. Moreover EVERY such intertwiner occurs exactly once. In particular Hom_Hopf,H(V,V^tensor3) is isomorphic to W, dim Hom=N, dim sum_w image(I_w)=N^2. (5) Here is a direct proof including endpoints. A highest vector of the required weight has integer degree d. If its last-head-c component is z_c, its E equation gives z_(c+1)=-xQ E_12 z_c/(1-Q^(c+1)), with the action interpreted as in (4). Thus the c=0 component w determines it and gives exactly H_L. The final c=d equation is E_12^N w=0. Conversely this proves the E equation for every w. Its total K and H are precisely the highest K=x,H=d of V. The quantum-group commutator then gives, along its F string, E_tot I_w|a>=(Q^(-a)-1)I_w|a-1>. The last F arrow is zero by F_tot^N=0. This proves the full intertwiner, not only a highest-weight kernel comparison. For each a<N, applying E_tot^a to I_w|a> returns a NONZERO scalar times H_L(w). Distinct a have different unrolled degrees. Consequently the N copies of V in (5) are independent. The proof also gives an inverse: restrict the highest vector to last color0. No complementary Clebsch channel or internal excursion was dropped. Both original adjacent signed braids commute with the entire Hopf action and H. They therefore act exactly on this complete module. The source cup intertwiner is w=p: E_12 p=0 gives H_L(p)=p tensor |0>, I_p(v)=p tensor v.
