(6) The generalized source vector t from the [tame Hermite theorem](actual_tame_c0_hermite_source_frame.md) must be lifted as H_L(t). The bare vector t tensor |0> is generally not highest and must not replace it. ### The total-character slice has no missing generalized extension The center identity follows directly by multiplying the N shifted factors FE=Omega-qK-q^(-1)K^(-1): T_N(Omega)+K^N+K^(-N)=0, T_0=2,T_1=z,T_(n+1)=zT_n-T_(n-1). (7) Indeed product_(r=0)^(N-1)[z-(uQ^r+u^(-1)Q^(-r))] =T_N(z)-u^N-u^(-N), with u=qK and q^N=-1; F^NE^N=0. On three heads K_tot^N=(-1)^d. The root Omega=-2 of T_N(z)+2(-1)^d is SIMPLE, since T_N'(-2)=(-1)^(N-1)N^2. Thus total-character extensions at -2 are not being silently removed. In fact ker(Omega_123+2) is exactly the N^2-dimensional image (5). Any highest vector in it has K=x, hence degree d modulo N. Degree d is covered by (4). The only other possible physical degree is 2N-1. A highest vector there would have a nonzero F string of length N, by the same coefficients in (1), ending outside the available degree range0,...,3d; so it is zero. Applying E repeatedly to an arbitrary vector in the kernel and using E^N=0 therefore places it in the strings (4). The intermediate pair Casimirs DO have their size-two Jordan channels, and all of those remain below. ## 3. Actual complete recoupling is an anti-Pascal matrix There is a second complete highest chart, H_R(w')=sum_(a=0)^d (-1)^a/F_a |a> tensor E_23^a w', whose inverse is first physical color0. The factor follows directly from the E equation: on its degree-d slice the K_23 factor at the next step is Q^(a+1), canceling the Q^(-(a+1)) in Ecal|a+1>. Define J by H_L(w)=H_R(Jw). Its exact coefficients are J_(i,j)=(-xQ)^(d-i)x^j Q^[i(i+1)/2-d(d+1)/2] [d-j choose i]_Q, i+j<=d; zero otherwise. (8) To prove (8), extract physical first color0 from (4). It requires c=d-i and exactly j first-head lowering arrows in E_12^c. The q-binomial expansion with E_1K_2 and E_2 gives the displayed Gaussian coefficient. The remaining exponent simplifies to i(i+1)/2-d(d+1)/2; no modular half inverse is used. The opposite antidiagonal is nonzero, so J is invertible. Thus this is a complete frame change including all colliding intermediate channels. Put A=Omega_12 restricted to W. It is the literal actual symmetric tridiagonal degree-d pair Casimir, with explicit entries A_(j,j)=q+q^(-1)-q(1-Q^j)^2-q^(-1)(1-Q^(j+1))^2, A_(j-1,j)=A_(j,j-1)=-(1-Q^j)^2, 1<=j<=d. On W the OTHER pair Casimir is B e_j=c_j e_j+b_j e_(j-1), c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1), b_j=Q^j+Q^(-j)-2, 1<=j<=d. (9) Direct extraction in (4) proves (9): only c=0,1 can reach last color0. Their F_2 E_2 terms cancel exactly; the remaining off diagonal is b_j. The right-chart calculation similarly gives J^(-1) A J=B, J A J^(-1)=B^T. (10) Consequently BOTH complete original signed braid generators are R_12=kappa r_N(A), R_23=kappa r_N(B)=J^(-1)R_12 J, (11) with their literal inverses for negative signs. The derivative conditions of r_N at every colliding c_j are essential in (11). The polynomial has degree<N and supplies the full matrix, not only its eigenvalues or its two-dimensional source restriction. Equivalently the entries of f(B) are products of the b_j times the confluent divided differences f[c_i,...,c_j]. The ordinary tridiagonal A has nonzero adjacent coefficients at all j=1,...,d. Hence e_d is cyclic for A. Since Jp=Nx^(-d)e_d, p is cyclic for B on ALL N multiplicities. This establishes complete source generation by the actual character/Ward algebra. It is distinct from claiming cyclicity under one braid alone: at composite levels distinct Casimir nodes can have the same R eigenvalue, and no reduction based only on those eigenvalues is authorized. ## 4. Exact original boundary source and a tame Hermite recoupling The same finite q-binomial identities in (8) give Jp=Nx^(-d)e_d, J e_0=p/N, ell J^(-1)=(x^d/N)e_0^T. (12) For example row0 of J is x^(-d)(1,x,...,x^d), whereas ell_j=x^j/N. Thus the cap identity is literal, including its pivot. For EVERY word W in the two original signed crossings, (ell_12 tensor I) W (p_12 tensor I) =[ell W_mult p] I_V, ell W_mult p=e_0^T [J W_mult J^(-1)] e_d. (13) The first equality follows from the actual Hopf intertwiner and Schur calculation on the explicitly simple V: commuting with H makes a matrix diagonal and commuting with F makes it scalar. All actual common Cartan and external framing factors remain. Any originally prescribed cut functional with value1 on I gives that same scalar; arbitrary inserted nonintertwining exteriors must instead retain their literal transported functional. The original degree-d marked row m and ordinary row ell are coordinate duals to p,t on their source Hermite plane. Their full physical use is distinct: for arbitrary w the unrestricted marked contraction is the matrix M(w)_(beta,a)=sum_(u,v) x^v/N^2 [I_w|a>]_(u,v,beta). (14) This matrix, not just m restricted to W, is retained if the actual exterior asks for a marked row on that pair. No scalar replacement of (14) is asserted for arbitrary exteriors. There are useful quantitative bounds BEFORE any ambient recoupling estimate. Let g_r=F_12^r|0,0>/F_r; every one of its r+1 nonzero components is the unit phase x^(-second color). The original Hermite t obeys (A-c_*)t=theta p, theta=(-1)^N rho^2. Since F_12 is injective in degree d-1, this gives exactly E_12^c t=theta N q^(c-1)F_(c-1)/(1-Q^d) g_(d-c), 1<=c<=d. (15) The subsequent E coefficients are q(1-Q^j), giving the product in (15). The distinct last colors in H_L(t) are orthogonal. Using the finite root reciprocal-square identity therefore gives <H_L(p),H_L(t)>=0, ||H_L(p)||^2=N^3, ||H_L(t)||^2=||t||^2+N^3|rho|^2(N^2-1)/24, N^3/4<=||H_L(t)||^2<=pi^2 N^3/3. (16) Thus the two embedded highest SOURCE columns have condition at most2 at EVERY N. This concerns those source columns, not all N multiplicities or arbitrary descendants of t. The full recoupled source frame is also explicit: (Jt)_j=Nx^(-d)(-q)^j(1-Q)/(1-Q^(j+1)), 0<=j<d, (Jt)_d=t_0. (17) Indeed (B^T-c_*)Jt=theta Nx^(-d)e_d; its first coordinate is fixed by ell t=1 and (12). The recurrence in the remaining coordinates has ratio -q(1-Q^j)/(1-Q^(j+1)), proving (17). Its last coordinate follows from the last row of J. Writing alpha=Nx^(-d), remove the e_d component of Jt. The remaining vector z is orthogonal to Jp and satisfies exactly N^2<=||z||^2=N^2|rho|^2(N^2-1)/12<=pi^2 N^2/3. The removed scalar is t_0/alpha=(-1)^N rho Hbar, where Hbar=N^(-1)sum_u sum_(j<=u)(1-Q^j)^(-1). Its absolute value is at most pi(1+log N). Hence [Jp,Jt] has condition at most (pi/sqrt(3))[1+pi(1+log N)]^2. This is a proved tame recoupling of the ORIGINAL two-dimensional source packet into the complete multiplicity module, not an ambient q-Racah bound. For arbitrary complete multiplicities there are specified coherent positive Grams, without a choice depending on the unknown braid: G_high=sum_c (E_12^c)^* E_12^c/|F_c|^2, G_full=sum_a (F_123^a H_L)^*(F_123^a H_L)/|F_a|^2. (18) These give EXACTLY ||H_L(w)||^2 and ||I_w||_HS^2. The right chart Grams satisfy G_left=J^*G_right J. Formula (18) retains all mixed copies; it does not claim polynomial conditioning of the complete Gram or that both braids are contractions in it. The explicit q-Pascal entries (8) can carry angle energy. ## 4a. A COMPLETE positive Hermite metric with both original sources polynomial There is a useful non-diagonal Cauchy metric on ALL N channels, not just the source plane. Use the [complete physical degree-d Hermite frame](actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md) V for A: at a double node c=c_j=c_(d-j) take f(c),f'(c), normalized by f_0(z)=1; at a simple node take f(c). Its entire inverse is the bilinear Christoffel--Darboux inverse, not a Hermitian orthogonality assumption. Write nu_j=(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)]. For a double node let Q_j(z)=P_N(z)/(z-c)^2. Its exact block is V^T V=K, K_j=sigma_j [[0,1],[1,eta_j]], eta_j=r_N'(c)/nu_j+Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c), V^(-1)=K^(-1)V^T, f_d(c)=x^d nu_j, f_d'(c)=x^d r_N'(c). (18a) The single-node formula is V^T V=sigma_j on that block. At degree d the exact normalizers satisfy |sigma_j|=1/|1-Q^(2j+1)|^2 at a double node, |sigma_j|=1 at the possible simple node. (18b) These follow by the Jacobi continuant CD identity: its endpoint residue is Q_j(c) f_d(c)/product offdiag, while its next derivative adds f_d'(c) and Q_j'(c). Thus the inverse and every normalizer in (18a) are fixed by the original Jacobi matrix; no selected knot value or favorable metric is used. The TRUE complete source-multiplicity Racah matrix is C=V^(-1) J V. (18c) This is already restricted to the N-dimensional actual Hom space. It is not the larger physical adjacent-frame product before total-character restriction. In RIGHT channel coordinates z=V^(-1)Jw the complete positive inner product is ||w||_ch^2=||V^(-1)Jw||_2^2. (18d) It is full rank, includes every Hermite derivative channel, and depends only on N and the specified original module. The exact positive Hermitian matrix is G_N=J^*(V^(-1))^*V^(-1)J. Thus ||p||_(G_N)=||u||_2 and the exact dual norm of ell is ||a||_2; the bilinear CD matrix K is not itself being called positive. The exact generators are D=kappa r_N(Jordan(A)) and C D C^(-1), with their literal inverses. The first consists of the known unit-value and polynomial first-jet blocks; the second retains the FULL coherent Racah transport. Both ORIGINAL sources in this metric are polynomial. Put u=V^(-1)Jp and a=ell J^(-1)V. From the exact endpoint source (12) and CD inverse (18a), their entries at each double node are (u_value,u_derivative) =(-N nu_j sigma_j^(-1) Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c), N nu_j sigma_j^(-1)), (a_value,a_derivative)=(x^d/N,0). (18e) At a simple node they are u=N nu_j/sigma_j and a=x^d/N. In particular the original full Cartan phase is retained in the generator matrices; the source scalar cancellation is exactly (12). For clarity, the potentially large crossing derivative cancels in u_value: applying sigma^-1[[-eta,1],[1,0]] to the endpoint vector x^d(nu_j,r_N') leaves -x^d nu_j sigma^-1 Q_j'/Q_j in the first entry. This is an exact SOURCE cancellation; replacing Hermite columns by independent spectral values would miss it. There is an exact simplification, stronger than a polynomial gap estimate. P_N=T_N+2 satisfies the Chebyshev equation (4-z^2)P_N''-zP_N'+N^2(P_N-2)=0. At a double node, this equation and its derivative give Q_j(c)=N^2/(4-c^2), Q_j'(c)/Q_j(c)=c/(4-c^2). The original offdiagonal product of A is (-1)^d N^2, so CD gives sigma_j=(-1)^d x^d nu_j/(4-c^2). Hence the exact complete source (18e) is simply (u_value,u_derivative)=N(-1)^d x^(-d)(-c,4-c^2), (a_value,a_derivative)=(x^d/N,0), (18f) at every double node. At the simple node, present only at odd N, sigma=x^d nu and u=Nx^(-d), a=x^d/N. All constants and phases in these formulas are retained. Thus the source norms are explicit. Put n_distinct=ceil(N/2). Then ||a||_2^2=n_distinct/N^2, ||u||_2^2=N^2[sum_double(c^2+(4-c^2)^2) +1_(N odd)]. The first n_distinct formula here uses the ACTUAL number of distinct nodes: n_distinct=N/2 at even N and (N+1)/2 at odd N. The sum is elementary: ||u||_2^2=N^2(4N-1), N odd, ||u||_2^2=4N^3, N even, N>=6, ||u||_2^2=192 at N=4, 64 at N=2. Indeed the full list c_j=2cos((2j+1)pi/N) has sums sum c_j^2=2N and sum c_j^4=6N except the resonant levels2,4. Pairing j with d-j and treating the simple c=-2 separately gives the displayed formula. Direct substitution proves both exceptional levels. In particular the UNIFORM source product is ||u||_2 ||a||_2<=2N, for EVERY N>=2. (18g) Thus the COMPLETE positive Gram (18d) has polynomial BOTH original boundary norms, exactly as required for an honest Cauchy--Schwarz estimate. For every original three-head word, |chi_N ell W_mult p| <=|chi_N| ||a||_2 ||W_ch u||_2 <=2|chi_N| N ||W_ch||_op. (18h) One need not replace the source energy by a full operator norm: with E_N(W)=||W_ch u||_2^2 the stronger pointed bound is |chi_N ell W_mult p|^2 <=|chi_N|^2 n_distinct/N^2 E_N(W). (18i) Here E_N is a specified positive doubled energy built from the actual coherent matrices D,C, the complete initial vector (18f), and every mixed channel. It is not a sum of independently squared paths or a new chosen boundary state. This is a complete source-preserving positive-metric statement, not a metric pulled back from the unknown word. The subsequent [exact full-source test](actual_figure_eight_complete_channel_energy.md) proves that its coherent energy is NONSHARP already for the actual figure-eight, despite (18g). A single D has polynomial norm, but coherent transport through C creates the displayed excessive channel. The [terminal packet Gram](actual_terminal_packet_positive_gram.md) constructs a different positive metric on this same complete module with the sharp benchmark rate; general-prefix energy remains unproved. No individual absolute q-Hahn path or diagonal clock majorant is substituted for W_ch. ## 4b. A local cap-Ward quotient does not propagate through an adjacent crossing There is a minimal ORIGINAL-source test for quotienting currents before taking a positive norm. Set D=A-c_*I on the complete W above. Since ell D=0, the ordinary-cap row descends to the LINEAR quotient Q_cap=W/im D. This is a state/current quotient, not a quotient of the full observable algebra. Nevertheless it cannot be propagated unchanged through even one adjacent original R_23. The exact source-Hermite relation (15) gives p=D(t/theta), theta=(-1)^N rho^2!=0, [p]=0 in Q_cap. The primitive has polynomial norm O(N^(7/2)), by the proved tame source frame and |rho|>=4/N. Thus no large-current asymptotic is needed for this test. On the other hand the literal original crossing gives (R_23 p)_j=kappa p_j F_(d-j), ell R_23 p=kappa x^(-d) sum_(r=0)^d Q^(r+1)F_r =kappa x^(-d)!=0. (18j) The sum telescopes by Q^(r+1)F_r=F_r-F_(r+1), F_N=0. Therefore R_23(im D) is not contained in im D, so there is no induced map R_23:Q_cap->Q_cap. A local quotient would send the original cup to zero before this crossing and lose the exact unit source (18j). Equivalently the missing overlap current is explicitly nonzero: ell [R_23,A](t/theta)=kappa x^(-d). All kappas and boundary normalizations are the original ones, and (13) identifies this pairing with the original whole marked source. This argument uses one actual source and crossing; it does not rely on the separate full-observable-algebra no-quotient theorem. A GLOBAL equation/source quotient can still retain the transported current and its boundary term. Positive Schur/minimum-energy reduction is legitimate after those complete compatible variables have been assembled. The local calculation above supplies no geometric bound on that global quotient energy. In particular, a polynomial boundary Riesz norm or a polynomial primitive for one Ward current does not prove a sharp energy estimate across arbitrary overlapping crossings. ## 5. All odd-head Hom spaces and every even-plat source The same endpoint argument works at arbitrary fixed width. Put b=2r+1 and D=r d. Let W_r=(V^tensor(2r))_(integer degree D), H_r(w)=sum_(c=0)^d (-xQ)^c E_(2r)^c w/F_c tensor |c>, I_w|a>=F_b^a H_r(w)/F_a. (19) Then restriction to last color0 proves an exact bijection W_r=Hom_Hopf,H(V,V^tensor(2r+1)), dim W_r=[z^(rd)](1+z+...+z^d)^(2r). (20) The E recurrence and E_prefix^N=0 prove both directions exactly as in (4). The highest H and K are d,x, and the complete F string gives the whole V map. For fixed r>=1 this dimension is O_r(N^(2r-1)); r=0 means the one-dimensional scalar Hom. No internal channel between successive braid gates is projected. Now take an ORIGINAL 2k-head plat, r=k-1, b=2k-1. Define Phi_w=(I_w tensor I)p =N sum_(a=0)^d x^(a-d) F_b^a H_r(w)/F_a tensor |d-a>. (21) These are EXACTLY all invariant tensors in V^tensor(2k). For a direct inverse expand an invariant tensor by its last head. Its last-color-d component is highest on the first b heads. The F equation then determines every other component by psi_(d-a-1)=x F_b psi_(d-a)/(1-Q^(a+1)). This is precisely (21), and the last endpoint holds by F_b^N=0. Its inverse on w is the coefficient of last TWO colors(0,d) multiplied by x^d/N. The E equation supplies the same highest constraint; there is no unperformed normal/source condition. Both signed original braids preserve these COMPLETE invariant tensors. Therefore every original plat word has an exact reduced operator B_word on W_r, computed by (21), the actual physical word, and that specified coefficient extraction. In particular this is a strict all-word representation, not the upper corner of a nonmultiplicative truncation. Most importantly the FULL original top source is retained. Set w_0=p^tensor(k-1), lambda=ell^tensor(k-1) on W_r. Then Phi_(w0)=p^tensor k, and EXACTLY (ell^tensor(k-1) tensor m) Phi_w=lambda(w), ORIGINAL plat scalar=chi_N lambda B_word w_0. (22) To prove it, compose I_w with the first k-1 ORDINARY caps. This is a Hopf map V->V and hence scalar. Its highest matrix entry is lambda(w), because those caps require prefix degree D and therefore select c=0 in (19). Composing this scalar map with the LAST literal marked cap on the original cup gives m p=1. This is a whole invariant-tensor identity. It does not replace m by an ordinary cap on arbitrary physical sectors. The reduced source norms in the stated orthonormal W_r basis are ||w_0||=N^[3(k-1)/2], ||lambda||=N^[-(k-1)/2], ||w_0|| ||lambda||=N^(k-1). (23) Thus no exponential boundary cost is hidden in this complete all-width reduction. At k=2 these are precisely the source p and ordinary row ell in (12)--(13). The actual common external chi_N is unchanged and is not asserted to have polynomial size. ## 6. Every induced generator has an explicit actual Casimir Write the even prefix in (19) as A_prefix tensor B_head, with 2k-3 and one physical head respectively. On its degree D slice put H_boundary=q x K_B+q^(-1)x^(-1)K_B^(-1) -x E_A F_B K_B, O_prefix=F_prefix E_prefix+qK_prefix +q^(-1)K_prefix^(-1). (24) The ordering F_B K_B is part of the formula. The full induced positive braid generators on W_r are physical R_i restricted to W_r, i<=2k-3, kappa r_N(H_boundary), i=2k-2, kappa r_N(O_prefix), i=2k-1. (25) Their negatives are the literal inverses. For k=1 the prefix is trivial and only the final value r_N(q+q^(-1)) occurs. Here is an extraction proof, rather than an assumed spectral matching. For the penultimate pair only last colors0,1 in (19) contribute to its output color0. The c=0 part gives xF_B E_B plus the Cartan terms in (24). The c=1 part is -x F_B(E_A K_B+E_B). The F_BE_B terms cancel, leaving exactly H_boundary, with no omitted endpoint term. Polynomial functional calculus then gives the middle formula (25). For the last pair, its coproduct Casimir can be moved through the invariant tensor (21) to the complementary even prefix. This keeps the same Casimir because the actual antipode fixes it: S(FEcal)=Ecal F, and Ecal F=FEcal+rho(K-K^(-1)) cancels the shifted Cartan terms. This is the literal cup duality (3), so no transpose framing factor or new norm character is inserted. It proves the last formula (25); specializing the same polynomial gives the full R, including all Jordan derivatives. Physical generators inside the prefix commute with its total E/F and give the first formula. These formulas implement the entire original scalar in a coherent source-generated module of polynomial dimension at fixed width. They do NOT establish a sharp bound for products of the two noncommuting boundary Casimir polynomials. The remaining task is their complete-channel/coherent angle-energy estimate, with the source (22), rather than any phase-free path majorant. ## 7. Verification and scope [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.py) uses an independent original finite-root E/F and signed R implementation. Fresh replay: PASS seven complete three-head families N=2,...,8, all descendants, both full signed braid matrices, all sources, anti-Pascal phases, Casimir cyclicity, ordinary and unrestricted marked contractions. Ten further full-source plat families include 2,4,6 and8 physical heads, every signed generator, the exact Casimirs (24)--(25), and full original word/source comparisons. The audit also checks the exact full-channel Racah and BOTH source profiles (18e), and twelve Hermite source-embedding/recoupling norm families through N=128. The proof above establishes the all-level/all-width statements; finite tests are supplementary. Original kappas and turns are retained. The same fresh replay checks the cap-current primitive and the exact nonzero adjacent-crossing overlap in Section4b at all seven complete three-head levels; no arbitrary coupon algebra is used for that test. This is different from the auxiliary classical Clebsch memory in [the degree-elevation dilation](clebsch_memory_dilation_and_actual_r_excursions.md). Here we use complete ACTUAL Hopf Hom spaces and invariant tensors, not a chosen upper subchannel with discarded R excursions. It is also stronger than retaining only the c_0 Jordan source plane: all intermediate channels (8)--(11),(24)--(25) are present. Their nontrivial norms and the geometric global estimate remain open.

title: A sharp capacity for two coherently composed original bridge packets
text: # A sharp capacity for two coherently composed original bridge packets 29 October 2026. The terminal packet with its adjacent inverse and the open signed bridge can be estimated TOGETHER, with their common physical color retained. Their exact operator norm has a strictly smaller exponent than the product of their separate sharp norms. The resulting constant is the unique maximum of an explicit strictly concave angle function. This is a sharp all-input norm theorem for an actual four-crossing terminal block, and gives a quantitative bound for the full original source with arbitrary prefixes and arbitrary plat width. Its constant is a block capacity, not asserted to be the volume of the closed knot. The requested sharp knot-volume estimate remains open. ## 1. The actual coherent block and its exact row Gram Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, F_j=(Q;Q)_j, s_j=|F_j|. Let R be the FULL original checked crossing on the pair degree-d multiplicity W_1. Put P_0=1, P_t=(1-Q^t)^2 P_(t-1)+Q^t, H=T R^(-1)=N^(-1) diag(x^n) R diag(P_(d-u)). (1) Here T is the complete original terminal packet, with all cap and Cartan factors retained. The exact formula, endpoint cancellation, and uniform bounds are proved in [the original Green estimate](actual_terminal_green_capacity_bound.md): |P_t|<=N+4s_t^2, P_t=1/(2-Q^t)+O(1/N) uniformly when t/N is in a compact subset of (1/6,1/2). (2) Let L:W_2->W_1 be the POSITIVE open bridge (ell_12 tensor I_34)R_23, in the source-fixing physical coordinate gauge g_j=s_j/sqrt(N). This gauge fixes every original paired cup and ordinary cap. The whole marked closure is retained through the complete invariant-source theorem. Its exact row Gram is LL^*=diag(E_N(u)), E_N(u)=N^2 sum_(k<=d-u) s_k^(-2) sum_(a+c=d-k) s_a^(-4)s_c^(-4). (3) Thus the COMPLETE coherent block C=HL satisfies CC^*=H diag(E_N) H^*. (4) No exterior coefficient or Green factor is commuted in (4). Both sides can be tensored with an arbitrary Hilbert spectator space. The actual source row is 1^T C. Its Cauchy cost is at most N, also for the positive completion C^*C+exp(-N^2)I. The [pointed row theorem](actual_terminal_bridge_operator_reduction.md) gives, uniformly in u including the endpoints, log E_N(u)=(N/pi)h(u/N)+O(log N), h(t)=v_8, 0<=t<=1/2, h(t)=8 Lambda(pi*t/2)-2 Lambda(pi*t), 1/2<=t<=1, (5) where Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log(2sin s)ds and v_8=8Lambda(pi/4). The transfer restriction k<=d-u is part of (3); taking independent free maxima would lose it. ## 2. The sharp answer On 0<=alpha,beta<=pi/2, with gamma=pi-alpha-beta, define F(alpha,beta)=4Lambda(alpha)+6Lambda(beta)+2Lambda(gamma) +8Lambda((pi-beta)/2). (6) Let C_* be its maximum. It is attained at a UNIQUE point with 0<alpha_*<pi/2, pi/6<beta_*<pi/2, sin(gamma_*)=2sin(alpha_*)^2, sin(gamma_*)cos(beta_*/2)^2=sin(beta_*)^3. (7) The sharp all-level operator estimate is log ||H L||_op^2=(N/pi) C_*+O(log N). (8) In particular v_8+3v_3<C_*<2v_8, C_*=6.930886593131580854..., alpha_*/pi=0.243487774973153603..., beta_*/pi =0.347871118966627868... . (9) Here v_3=3Lambda(pi/3). The decimal values only describe the analytically specified unique maximum; the proof does not infer the rate or its strict gaps from numerical fitting. ## 3. The Green remainder has a strictly smaller exponent The actual crossing support is i+u>=d. With h_0=i+u-d, |R_(i,u)|=s_i^2 s_u^2/(N^2 s_(h_0)). (10) By (2), pointwise on this support, |H_(i,u)|<=|R_(i,u)|+4N|R_(i,u)|/s_u^2. (11) Multiply each column by sqrt(E_N(u)). The operator norm is bounded by the Hilbert--Schmidt norm, and (11) bounds that norm by the sum of the two Hilbert--Schmidt norms of the displayed nonnegative entry majorants. This is used only AFTER the actual coherent P_t endpoint cancellation which proves (2). Write J(t)=integral_0^t log(2sin(pi*s))ds=-Lambda(pi*t)/pi. For the second majorant the squared exponential profile is at most h(u/N)+pi[4J(i/N)-2J((i+u-d)/N)]<=v_8+3v_3. (12) Indeed max J=v_3/(2pi) and min J=-v_3/(2pi). Polynomial N factors and the uniform factorial errors cost O(log N). This argument includes all physical endpoints and every parity. The first majorant has squared profile h(u/N)+pi[4J(i/N)+4J(u/N)-2J((i+u-d)/N)]. (13) If u/N<=1/2 then J(u/N)<=0, so (12) bounds (13) too. For u/N>=1/2 put alpha=pi(1-i/N), beta=pi(1-u/N). Replacing the exact offset d=N-1 by N changes the action by O(log N/N), uniformly, using the modulus |Lambda(a)-Lambda(b)|<=C|a-b|(1+|log|a-b||). This includes the thin support strip where the limiting gamma would otherwise be between -pi/N and zero; adjust the angles by O(1/N) into the closed simplex before applying the formula. The limiting expression (13) is precisely (6), with beta<=pi/2. An alpha>pi/2 cannot maximize it: then 0<gamma<pi/2 and swapping alpha and gamma raises 4Lambda(alpha)+2Lambda(gamma) by 2[Lambda(gamma)-Lambda(alpha)]>0. Hence its maximum is C_*. Finally C_*>v_8+3v_3. Evaluate (6) at alpha=pi/4,beta=pi/3. Its excess over v_8+3v_3 is -4Lambda(pi/4)+5Lambda(pi/3)+2Lambda(5pi/12)>0. Strict concavity of Lambda on (0,pi/2), with Lambda(pi/2)=0, gives Lambda(5pi/12)>Lambda(pi/3)/2 and Lambda(pi/3)>2Lambda(pi/4)/3. Combining them proves the displayed strict inequality. Thus the remainder in (12) cannot control the sharp exponential rate, and the upper half of (8) follows. ## 4. Strict concavity, the unique optimizer, and the lower bound Inside the rectangle 0<alpha,beta<pi/2 put a=cot(alpha)>0, b=cot(beta)>0, g=cot(gamma)=(1-ab)/(a+b). The negative Hessian of (6) is [[4a+2g, 2g], [2g, 6b+2g+2tan(beta/2)]]. (14) Its first principal minor is positive. If g>=0 this is immediate; if g<0, then g>-ab/(a+b)>-a, so 4a+2g>2a. Before its last positive diagonal term, the determinant is 24ab+8ag+12bg=8+16ab+4bg>0. For g>=0 the first expression is positive. For g<0, bg=(1-ab)b/(a+b)>=1-ab, so the second is at least12+12ab. The extra term in (14) increases the determinant. Thus F is STRICTLY concave throughout this convex rectangle. The alpha derivative tends to +infinity at alpha=0, and at alpha=pi/2 it is 2log(cos(beta)/2)<0. The beta derivative at beta=pi/2 is 2log(cos(alpha)/2)<0. At beta=pi/6 it is 2log(2sin(gamma))+4log(2cos(pi/12))>0, since gamma ranges from pi/3 to5pi/6. Concavity then excludes every beta<=pi/6 from the maximum. These statements give the unique interior optimizer and the range in (7). Setting the two first derivatives to zero gives exactly its trigonometric equations. The upper gap C_*<2v_8 is also strict without decimals. The separate crossing squared profile has maximum v_8 only at alpha=beta=pi/4. The row profile h has maximum v_8 only for u/N<=1/2, i.e. beta>=pi/2. They cannot attain both maxima together. Continuity on the compact angle domain therefore gives a strict gap for their sum. For the lower bound in (8), take integers i,u nearest N(1-alpha_*/pi), N(1-beta_*/pi), with the exact support retained. The Green index t=d-u satisfies t/N->beta_*/pi in (1/6,1/2), so (2) gives a nonzero limiting P_t. Equations (5),(10) then imply log(|H_(i,u)|^2 E_N(u))=(N/pi)C_*+O(log N). Equation (4) has norm at least this single squared entry of H diag(sqrt E). Conversely its Hilbert--Schmidt bound costs at most N^2 terms. This completes (8), including odd, even and composite levels and all original normalization factors. ## 5. A full-source consequence at arbitrary plat width For a six-head plat the actual terminal block has action order [2,-3,4,4]. First R23 couples the first ordinary cap to the remaining pair, then the inverse R34 is retained, and finally R45^2 meets the terminal cap. The exact cap identities give C=HL on W_2. Thus for ANY preceding original braid B, |K_N|^2<=|chi_N|^2 N ||HL||^2 ||B w_0||_g^2. (15) The input metric g is the specified source-fixing physical factorial metric. Its original paired source w0=p tensor p has polynomial norm. The preceding operator is transported in that metric; its cost has not been dropped from (15). The same terminal block can be placed at the last five odd heads of a 2k-head plat for ANY k>=3, with action order [2k-4,-(2k-3),2k-2,2k-2]. All earlier ordinary caps commute with this terminal block and can be contracted exactly. Their product norm is polynomial. This leaves the same complete W_2 input and the SAME HL estimate. The preceding braid may use every head, including the last marked partner: its complete invariant-tensor inverse is (x^d/N) times extraction of the last two colors (0,d), not an unjustified odd-head cut replacement. The gauges of those two colors multiply to one. For reference each original physical signed crossing in the common gauge g_j=s_j/sqrt(N) has Hilbert--Schmidt norm exp[Nv_8/(2pi)+O(log N)]. (16) Its nonzero modulus is s_(b+k)^2/(s_b^2 s_k) for the positive sign, and s_(a+k)^2/(s_a^2 s_k) for the negative sign. With three nonnegative complementary variables the limiting action is 2Lambda(alpha)+2Lambda(beta)+Lambda(gamma); its maximum is v_8/2, at alpha=beta=pi/4,gamma=pi/2. The strict physical support admits nearest lattice points, and its O(N^3) entries cost only log N. Consequently an arbitrary fixed m-crossing prefix in this all-width family satisfies the actual bound |K_N|<=|chi_N| N^C exp{N[m v_8+C_*]/(2pi)}. (17) The exponent C depends only on the fixed word and width. This saves more than two crossing capacities compared with separately charging the FOUR terminal crossings; it also improves the two separate packet capacities 2v_8. It is a bound for the whole original source, with chi_N retained. It is not a claim that m v_8+C_* equals or is at most the hyperbolic volume. Further coherent global constraints and geometric survival remain to be proved. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_composed_bridge_capacity.py) checks the actual finite operator product, its exact row Gram, the unique angle optimizer and growing-level capacity bounds. Fresh audit: PASS four full original marked sources through ten heads, seven complete finite compositions including both signed physical crossing formulas, the optimizer equations, and five growing-level norm sandwiches. An independent analytic review checked the strict Hessian, boundary exclusion, remainder gap and lower bound. The finite support strip is accounted for explicitly in Section 3.

title: The original source has an exact cyclic-dilogarithm and ordinary-Gaussian period
text: # The original source has an exact cyclic-dilogarithm and ordinary-Gaussian period 28 October 2026. The remaining finite marked Gaussian in [the exact cyclic/Hardy network](actual_cyclic_hardy_dilog_network.md) can also be removed. The original knot period is an exact integral of the literature cyclic dilogarithm and its inverse, ordinary Cauchy kernels, and ordinary continuous Gaussian weights. There are no finite Dirichlet, finite Euler, or finite Gaussian scalar kernels in this presentation. The cycle is a specified **fibered torus over real Gaussian variables**, with Gaussian-dominated absolute convergence. It is not a fixed product of circles interchanged formally with an unbounded Gaussian integral. All original source, peripheral, Cartan and framing factors are retained. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_continuous_gaussian_network.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_continuous_gaussian_network_results.json) check 660 exact both-sign phase identities, eight whole original pivotal word matrices with joint Gaussian moments and no finite Gaussian kernel, ten real-Gaussian quadratures, and the fibered radius bounds. ## 1. The exact Gaussian moment, with both signs fixed Put $h=2\pi i/N$, $Q=e^h$. For the original equal-color Gaussian, $$ d_a=(-1)^a x^{-2a}\exp\{h(a^2-a)/2\}. $$ For $s\in\{+1,-1\}$ set $$ c_s=-x^{-2s}e^{-sh/2},\qquad \alpha_s=\sqrt{\pi}(1+is),\qquad \alpha_s^2=2\pi is. \tag{1} $$ Then exactly $$ \boxed{\quad d_a^s= \sqrt{\frac{N}{2\pi}}\int_{\mathbb R} e^{-N\xi^2/2} (c_se^{\alpha_s\xi})^a\,d\xi. \quad} \tag{2} $$ Indeed the centered Gaussian of variance $1/N$ has complex moment $\exp(\alpha_s^2a^2/(2N))=\exp(sh a^2/2)$. Multiplication by $c_s^a$ gives the original linear phase and meridian powers. For $s=-1$, the sign is still $(-1)^a$, as required by the inverse Gaussian. For a typed unequal-color crossing replace $x^{-2s}$ by $(xy)^{-s}$ in (1). Nothing else changes. No common Cartan factor is incorporated into this replacement. For every polynomial $f$, (2) gives an exact operator identity $$ \mathsf D_sf(z)= \sqrt{\frac{N}{2\pi}}\int_{\mathbb R} e^{-N\xi^2/2} f(c_se^{\alpha_s\xi}z)\,d\xi. \tag{3} $$ Each integrand is a dilation, so it preserves polynomial degree. Before every original Gaussian its active head lies below $N$. Thus (3) equals the original finite marked Gaussian on every actual input. This is an equality of whole operators on those inputs, not an assumed selected Gaussian branch. The active scalar Cauchy kernel for the dilation is $$ \frac1{1-c_se^{\alpha_s\xi}z/w}. \tag{4} $$ All spectator heads retain their ordinary Hardy kernels. There is one independent $\xi$ for each original Gaussian factor, hence one for each signed crossing in the specified strict presentation. ## 2. A common fibered cycle Retain the norm-one literature functions $$ \mathcal V_N(t)=(1-t^N)^{(N-1)/(2N)} \prod_{\ell=1}^{N-1}(1-Q^\ell t)^{-\ell/N}, \qquad \mathcal U_N(t)=\mathcal V_N(t)^{-1}, \tag{5} $$ on their branches equal to one at zero. All non-Gaussian kernels and reflected monomials are exactly those in the previous theorem. Choose $\rho=1/16$. On a fixed color chart choose $0<\lambda\le1$ with $\lambda\le|x_j|$ and choose $$ C_c\ge\max(1,\sup|x_j|^2,\sup|x_j|^{-2}). $$ The same bound covers the typed products $(x_jx_{j+1})^{\pm1}$. Insert a Hardy identity-reset layer before every elementary factor. Given preceding output radii $R_j$, first put $r_j=\rho R_j/2$. Before a transfer decrease its numerator radius, if needed, so $r_{\rm num}/r_{\rm den} \le\rho\lambda/2$. For the factor's output radii use $$ s_j=\rho r_j/2 $$ except at a positive factorial, where $s_i=2r_i/\rho$, and at a Gaussian, where use $$ \boxed{\quad s_i=\frac{\rho}{2C_c}e^{-2|\xi|}r_i. \quad} \tag{6} $$ Since $\operatorname{Re}\alpha_s=\sqrt\pi<2$, $$ |c_se^{\alpha_s\xi}|\,s_i/r_i \le\frac\rho2e^{\sqrt\pi\,\xi-2|\xi|} \le\rho/2. \tag{7} $$ Thus every cyclic atom argument and every Cauchy-kernel argument has modulus at most $\rho/2$. At a positive factorial the reflected argument has modulus $|Qw_i/z_i|=\rho/2$; its full scalar kernel is still $N(z_i/w_i)^{N-1}\mathcal V_N(Qw_i/z_i)$. These inequalities hold simultaneously for every $\boldsymbol\xi\in\mathbb R^m$. The number of layers is fixed by the word. There is no inequality closing terminal radii back to initial radii, because the fused source is monomial. The construction uses no $N$-dependent radius constant on the fixed color chart. For each $\boldsymbol\xi$, take the product of the positively oriented circles of these radii and its uniquely anchored lift through (5). Denote it by $\Gamma(\boldsymbol\xi)$. The full integration chain is the union of these tori over the oriented base $\mathbb R^m$. The radii are continuous and piecewise smooth because of the minima and absolute values. Their strata glue without additional internal boundary. When the logarithmic torus volume form is wedged with all $d\xi_j$, its $d\log r(\boldsymbol\xi)$ terms vanish. Equivalently one integrates the fibers with their usual $dz/(2\pi iz)$ measure. There is **no extra radius Jacobian**. ## 3. Absolute convergence on the full fibered chain The following bounds are uniform in $N$ and in the real Gaussian variables; constants depend on the fixed word and color chart. First, all radii can be chosen at most one. A positive factorial's increase after its reset never exceeds its preceding radius. If $L$ is the number of elementary factors, put $$ c_{\rm reset}=\min(\rho/2,\rho^2\lambda/4),\qquad c_* =c_{\rm reset}\rho/(2C_c)>0. $$ An induction gives, at every layer, $$ -\log r_j\le C_{\rm word} +2\sum_{\ell=1}^{m}|\xi_\ell|. \tag{8} $$ One may take $C_{\rm word}$ to be a fixed multiple of $L|\log c_*|$. Minima in the radius construction only replace one radius by a fixed constant times another; they do not introduce products of previously accumulated logarithms. Second, the exact logarithm of (5) gives on $|t|\le\rho$ $$ |\log\mathcal V_N(t)|,\ |\log\mathcal U_N(t)| \le-\frac N4\log(1-\rho). \tag{9} $$ Here $|Q^r-1|\ge4/N$ for every nontrivial root, and the resonant logarithmic coefficients cancel exactly. All Hardy and Gaussian-dilation kernels are bounded by $(1-\rho)^{-1}$. Every reflected factorial contributes its ORIGINAL factor $N$ and a monomial whose radius ratio is fixed at $2/\rho$. Every source exponent has magnitude at most $N-1$. Consequently the absolute scalar density, apart from the unchanged external line $\chi_{\beta,N}$ and the normalized Gaussian measure, is bounded by $$ C N^B \exp\left\{C_0N+C_1N\sum_\ell|\xi_\ell|\right\}. \tag{10} $$ Thus the full pullback is dominated by $$ C N^B \exp\left\{C_0N+C_1N\sum_\ell|\xi_\ell| -\frac N2\sum_\ell\xi_\ell^2\right\}. \tag{11} $$ This is integrable for every $N$. With the normalized Gaussian measures its integral is at most $C'N^B e^{C_2N}$. We make no additional growth assertion about the retained external $\chi_{\beta,N}$. These estimates prove Fubini and the disappearance of Gaussian boundary terms at real infinity. ## 4. Exact original-source identity, with no finite scalar kernels Let $\mathcal H_{\ell,N}(\boldsymbol\xi)$ be the kernels of the cyclic/Hardy network with each finite Gaussian replaced by (4). Let $m$ be their Gaussian count. The ORIGINAL full fused-plat period is exactly $$ \begin{split} P_{\beta,N} ={}&\chi_{\beta,N}N^{1-k} \left(\frac N{2\pi}\right)^{m/2} \int_{\mathbb R^m} e^{-N\|\boldsymbol\xi\|^2/2}\\ &\quad\cdot \int_{\Gamma(\boldsymbol\xi)} (z^0)^{a_{\rm in}}(z^L)^{-a_{\rm out}} \prod_{\ell=1}^{L} \mathcal H_{\ell,N}(\boldsymbol\xi) \prod_{\ell,j}\frac{dz_j^\ell}{2\pi iz_j^\ell} \,d\boldsymbol\xi . \end{split} \tag{12} $$ Every source exponent, factor $N$, monomial, norm root, half-character and original external scalar is retained. No finite $\Gamma_{\pm,N}$, finite Euler polynomial, or finite Dirichlet numerator occurs in its scalar integrand. For a fixed $\boldsymbol\xi$, the torus contraction is the original completed polynomial word with its Gaussian factors replaced by independent dilations. Each head is still polynomial and all previous support/barrier arguments remain valid. The contraction is a finite sum of products of the dilation moments. Integration of each independent variable gives (2), in its original operator order, and therefore the exact original word. Estimate (11) also justifies this as an equality of absolutely convergent multiple integrals, rather than only an iterated polynomial calculation. The full original Ward corner is fixed BEFORE expanding the Gaussian factors. A fixed-$\boldsymbol\xi$ word need not be a Hopf intertwiner. We do not reapply the Ward corner reduction to such an individual word or replace its transported co-source by a newly chosen cap. Linearity of the already proved full-source functional is what is used in (12). Any specified root-specialized quantum A-annihilator of the original meridian function therefore annihilates (12) as well. No identification of a classical symbol or selected geometric component is inferred. ## 5. Uniform leading symbols on the INITIAL cycle There is now a direct uniform phase comparison for the actual scalar functions on this cycle, without a finite Taylor-remainder sector. For every fixed $\rho<1$, $$ \begin{split} \mathcal V_N(t) &=(1-t)^{1/2} \exp\{\operatorname{Li}_2(t)/h\} (1+O_\rho(N^{-1})),\\ \mathcal U_N(t) &=(1-t)^{-1/2} \exp\{-\operatorname{Li}_2(t)/h\} (1+O_\rho(N^{-1})). \end{split} \tag{13} $$ The normalized errors are analytic and admit the same bound with any fixed number of derivatives on smaller disks. All logarithms are the anchored branches. For a direct proof split the logarithmic series $\log\mathcal V_N(t)=\sum_{N\nmid m}t^m/[m(Q^m-1)]$ at $m=N/2$. On the lower range, $$ \frac1{e^{hm}-1}=\frac1{hm}-\frac12+O(|h|m). $$ For example the remainder bound on $|hm|\le\pi$ follows from the elementary sine/cotangent formula, with its removable value at zero. Summation gives $O_\rho(1/N)$. The upper range is exponentially small in $N$, using $|Q^m-1|^{-1}\le N/4$. The omitted resonant coefficients are exponentially small too. Thus $$ \log\mathcal V_N(t) =\operatorname{Li}_2(t)/h+\tfrac12\operatorname{Log}(1-t) +O_\rho(N^{-1}), $$ and Cauchy estimates give the derivative version. The exact Gaussian weight in (12) is $e^{-N\xi^2/2}$. On the original color charts, the remaining $q$ phases shift the small cyclic arguments by $e^{\beta h}$ for fixed half-integer or integer $\beta$. Their change is an explicit nonzero amplitude: $$ \mathcal V_N(e^{\beta h}t) =(1-t)^{1/2-\beta}e^{\operatorname{Li}_2(t)/h} (1+O_\rho(N^{-1})), \tag{14} $$ with the inverse formula for $\mathcal U_N$. The dilation Cauchy kernel has the same type of uniform nonzero density correction, since its argument stays below $\rho$. Thus (12) has actual dilogarithm/Gaussian leading symbols and a specified nonzero leading density on its INITIAL fibered cycle. This is a pointwise integrand comparison. It does not imply a relative asymptotic for a cancelling total period, geometric dominance, or a nonzero intersection with a Rivin critical cycle. ## 6. The remaining global theorem The finite scalar endpoints have been replaced by global anchored functions and a specified convergent cycle, with exact equality to the original invariant. Their boundary information has not been discarded: it is carried by that cycle, the norm-root branches, the original affine charges and the Cauchy pole data. To prove a broad volume theorem one must still transport this cycle to the geometric ideal-angle chain, retaining norm-divisor residues, compatible root frames, Cauchy-pole contributions and the original pointed source. The oversized weak alias example shows why an unmarked choice of every nonnegative angle locus would be incorrect. No global transport or volume limit is claimed here.

title: Coupled crossing gauges: an exact optimizer and a twist-block improvement
text: # Coupled crossing gauges: an exact optimizer and a twist-block improvement 28 October 2026. The original endpoint-preserving gauge program can be implemented as a finite convex optimization, with its full original paired source retained. For a broad explicit alternating-sign class, flat gauges are its **exact finite-N global minimizers** at the single-crossing Hilbert--Schmidt partition. Even replacing HS norms by operator norms cannot improve its exponential crossing envelope. Thus this particular optimization does not produce the Rivin volume. There is a constructive improvement after coherent block contraction: an entire repeated-crossing twist block has a uniform exponential norm bound independent of its length. It improves the crossing bound for every repeated-generator block of length at least five in the specified original braid word, at arbitrary width. No conversion of an arbitrary unoriented diagram twist region is assumed. This is not the sharp knot-volume bound or a lower bound. ## 1. The implemented original program and its entropy dual Use the source-preserving gauge program in [the weighted Fourier energy theorem](actual_weighted_fourier_plat_energy.md#3-a-computable-positive-energy-upper-bound-hierarchy). The width is 2k; every original cap/cup pair is adjacent. On every physical wire edge e choose arbitrary real logs s_e(a), 0<=a<N. At each endpoint the only restrictions are s_(odd,a)+s_(even,d-a)=0, d=N-1. (1) These make the endpoint gauges fix the ORIGINAL paired cups, ordinary caps, and the marked cap after its legitimate whole-degree restriction. All scalar, pivotal and framing lines stay as before. An internal wire has a single gauge on its entire segment between incident gates. For a crossing v let i=(a,b), o=(c,e). Put Phi_N(s)=(1/2)sum_v log sum_(i,o) |R_v(o,i)|^2 exp(2s_out(o)-2s_in(i)). (2) The sums use the original physical crossing support, not a cyclic completion. Positive entries are exactly R_+(a+b-e,e;a,b) =kappa x^(-b-e)Q^(eb) F_(a+b-e)F_a/[F_(a-e)F_bF_e], (3) with 0<=e<=a<N and a+b-e<N. The negative moduli are obtained by swapping both input and output heads, from the proved actual antiunitary identity. The common kappa is a retained unit phase. Thus no knot scalar is input to the objective. The resulting rigorous bound is |P_N| <= |chi_N|N^(k-1) exp(inf_s Phi_N(s)). (4) The implementable objective (2) is convex log-sum-exp. The new script eliminates (1) with a signed union-find and supplies its analytic gradient to L-BFGS. It keeps separate intermediate wire gauges and the independent top and bottom source gauges; it does not optimize each crossing in isolation. There is a useful dual characterization. At every crossing choose a probability p_v on its actual nonzero entries. Require identical one-head marginals at the two ends of every internal wire and require reflected odd/even marginals at each paired boundary. Such probabilities annihilate every gauge linear term in (2). The elementary entropy identity log sum_i exp(l_i)=max_p [sum_i p_i l_i-sum_i p_i log p_i] therefore gives the lower certificate inf_s Phi_N(s) >= (1/2)sum_v [sum p_v log|R_v|^2-sum p_v log p_v]. (5) If the maximizing constrained probabilities are strictly positive, Lagrange multipliers give p_v proportional to the exponentials in (2), and equality holds. Indeed the entropy has infinite inward derivative at a zero coordinate whenever a strictly positive feasible point exists, so its maximum is interior. Its derivative annihilates the constraint tangent space, hence is a linear combination of the constraint rows, which gives precisely those multipliers. This is a finite-dimensional entropy/flow duality with actual R weights. It does not identify those flows with geometric angle structures. The subsequent [joint projector-profile bound](actual_twist_block_projector_barrier.md) sharpens the block constant below to 4v_3+2v_8 while retaining the same original source, frame and meridian-circle proof. The valid coarser estimates here are unchanged. ## 2. Exact optimum for alternating signs by generator position Suppose the word has the sign pattern sign(sigma_i)=epsilon*(-1)^(i+1), epsilon=+1 or -1, (6) at every occurrence of generator i. Its index sequence is arbitrary, as are its length and even width. The theorem applies whenever its plat closure is the desired one-component knot; no knot-specific calculation enters. It is not a claim that every alternating knot presentation automatically has (6). **Exact optimizer theorem.** For every N>=2, inf_s Phi_N(s)=m log||R_+||_HS. (7) Thus the fully coupled single-crossing HS gauge program is already minimized by s=0, including all endpoint gauges allowed in (1). Proof. Normalize the squared moduli of the positive crossing: p_+(o,i)=|R_+(o,i)|^2/||R_+||_HS^2. The literal matrix (3) is symmetric: R_+(o,i)=R_+(i,o). It follows that its input and output first-head marginals coincide, as do its second-head marginals. Let them be p_H and p_L. Root factorial reflection gives a second exact modulus symmetry, |R_+(c,e;a,b)| =|R_+(d-e,d-c;d-b,d-a)|. (8) Indeed the new transfer difference is still a-e=c-b, and |F_j||F_(d-j)|=N cancels all reflected numerator/denominator factors in (3). Consequently p_H(a)=p_L(d-a). For the negative crossing the two head marginals are interchanged. Under (6), any given odd physical head therefore has the same marginal at ALL its incident crossings, and every even head has the reflected marginal. Which of the two is called H depends only on epsilon. Assign these same marginals to untouched wire segments too. All internal wire constraints and all boundary reflection constraints in Section 1 are satisfied. The strictly positive probabilities p_v=|R_v|^2/||R_v||_HS^2 are thus feasible in (5). Their entropy value is exactly sum_v log||R_v||_HS=m log||R_+||_HS. The same value is attained by s=0 in (2), proving (7). Equivalently, the entire projected gradient at s=0 vanishes, not merely the gradients of individually balanced crossings. Convexity then certifies the global minimum without any numerical convergence assumption. This is why some randomly initialized large-N numerical optimizations converge slowly in gauge-null directions; the exact stationary certificate avoids confusing that with a smaller optimum. ## 3. Even operator-norm gauges retain the crossing exponent Let a_N+b_N=d with a_N/N ->3/4 and b_N/N ->1/4. When epsilon=+1, put the fixed indices (a_N,b_N,a_N,b_N,...) on the physical heads; reverse them for epsilon=-1. At a positive crossing this gives the diagonal entry R_+(a_N,b_N;a_N,b_N). At a negative crossing it gives the head-swapped diagonal entry with the same modulus. This is a single physical index path through the WHOLE network, and its paired endpoint charges are exactly d. Every gauge in (1) is one on each of these endpoint states. Along the path the interior gauge ratios telescope. Bounding each local operator norm by this one entry therefore gives, for ANY N-dependent choices of positive diagonal wire gauges, product_v ||G_out,v R_v G_in,v^(-1)||_op >= |R_+(a_N,b_N;a_N,b_N)|^m. (9) This is a lower bound on the norm-based upper-bound program, not on the actual scalar period; other state paths can cancel that scalar. The uniform factorial estimate shows log|R_+(a_N,b_N;a_N,b_N)| =N[2J(3/4)-J(1/2)-2J(1/4)]+O(log N) =N v_8/(2pi)+O(log N). Flat gauges have that same operator-norm exponent by the original crossing theorem. Hence the best single-crossing operator program, as well as (7), has the exact exponential rate inf_gauge sum_v log||R_v,gauge|| =m N v_8/(2pi)+O_word(log N). (10) This decides the proposed finest local scaling route for the class (6), at arbitrary width. It cannot by itself lower the crossing envelope to the smaller hyperbolic knot volume. A genuinely coherent block contraction is necessary. ## 4. A uniform twist-block improvement from the actual Casimir Such contraction does yield a quantitative general improvement. Let B be either original complete crossing on two physical heads, with its original unit Cartan/framing factors retained. For every integer ell and every N>=2, ||B^ell||_op <=32 N^2(1+|ell|) c_*^N, ||B^ell||_HS <=32 N^3(1+|ell|) c_*^N, c_*=7+5sqrt(2). (11) The exponential constant is independent of twist length. No spectral condition number or unproved semisimplicity is hidden in (11). Here is a direct norm proof from the already independently derived [actual Casimir crossing polynomial](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md#3-the-actual-crossing-has-a-unique-confluent-polynomial). Use Ecal=rho^2 E and the actual complete physical matrices. They obey ||F||,||Ecal||<=2, K unitary, F Ecal+qK+q^(-1)K^(-1)=-2I. On the tensor product put Omega=F_tot Ecal_tot+qK_1K_2+q^(-1)K_1^(-1)K_2^(-1), F_tot=F_1+K_1^(-1)F_2, Ecal_tot=Ecal_1 K_2+Ecal_2. Expanding and using the single-head Casimir identity gives Omega=-2(K_2+K_1^(-1)) -(q+q^(-1))K_1^(-1)K_2 +F_1 Ecal_2+K_1^(-1)Ecal_1 F_2K_2, so ||Omega||<=14 in the ORIGINAL flat balanced metric. Let P_N(z)=T_N(z)+2, T_0=2,T_1=z,T_(n+1)=zT_n-T_(n-1). The proved actual polynomial identity is B=lambda_0 r_N(Omega), |lambda_0|=1, with P_N(Omega)=0. Its roots c=2cos(pi h/N), h odd, 1<=h<N are double. When N is odd there is additionally the simple root -2. At every double root r_N(c)=nu, |nu|=1 and |r_N'(c)|=(N-h)/(4 sin(pi h/N))<=N^2/8. (12) The simple root value has modulus one. These spectral jets, including their derivatives, follow from the defining finite R by confluent generic-q highest-weight interpolation; no diagonalizability at the root is used. For an explicit bounded Hermite basis set Q_c(z)=P_N(z)/(z-c)^2, A_c=Q_c(c)=N^2/(4sin^2(pi h/N)), alpha_c=Q_c'(c)/A_c=c/(4-c^2), e_c(z)=Q_c(z)[1-alpha_c(z-c)]/A_c, j_c(z)=(z-c)Q_c(z)/A_c. These polynomials have respectively the jets (1,0) and (0,1) at c, and zero jets at all other roots. At a possible simple root -2 use e_-(z)=P_N(z)/[(z+2)P_N'(-2)], with |P_N'(-2)|=N^2. Consequently the exact polynomial representing B^ell/lambda_0^ell is f_ell(z)=sum_double [nu^ell e_c(z) +ell nu^(ell-1)r_N'(c) j_c(z)] +sum_simple nu^ell e_-(z). (13) This formula works for negative ell too: r_N is a unit modulo P_N. For completeness the constants can be controlled explicitly. Integrate around |z|=R=14+1/N. The resolvent norm is at most N by its Neumann series. Put r(R)=(R+sqrt(R^2+4))/2. The Chebyshev recurrence gives |T_N(z)|<=2r(R)^N, and |P_N(z)|<=5 c_*^N, |z-c|>=12, A_c>=N^2/4, |alpha_c|<=N^2/8. The first inequality uses N[log r(14+1/N)-log r(14)]<=1/sqrt(200). It follows on that circle that |e_c(z)|<c_*^N/3, |j_c(z)|<=5c_*^N/(3N^2), |e_-(z)|<=5c_*^N/(12N^2). Together with (12), the at most N interpolation conditions bound |f_ell(z)| by N(1+|ell|)c_*^N. Cauchy's matrix functional calculus therefore gives ||f_ell(Omega)||<=R N^2(1+|ell|)c_*^N, which is stronger than the operator inequality (11). The HS inequality costs at most sqrt(N^2)=N. Thus no exponentially conditioned eigenbasis has entered the proof. ## 5. Whole-word consequence at arbitrary width Partition any fixed original knot word into maximal repeated-generator twist blocks of lengths ell_t, leaving other crossings as blocks of length one. Perform these actual matrix contractions first, preserving the original source and all common phases. Combining (11) with the ordinary crossing bound gives the unconditional whole-source estimate limsup_N (2pi/N)log|P_N| <=sum_t min(|ell_t|v_8, 2pi log(7+5sqrt(2))). (14) The factors 32N^3(1+|ell_t|), spectator dimensions and all complete source normalizations contribute only O_word(log N). The same holds for the reduced original Kashaev scalar. This applies to arbitrary width and sign patterns, not just the twist-knot family. There is also a direct finite-N source justification which includes ODD braid width and does not require passing to an even plat. For a b-strand knot cut use its original complete pivot g, which is unitary, and retain the unit-modulus zero-framing line in W. The exact actual cut is C=Tr_env[W(I tensor g^(tensor(b-1)))]=K_N I. Every partial trace of a unitary-weighted operator has norm at most the environment dimension times its operator norm. Thus, with every normalization still original, |K_N| <= N^(b-1)||W||_op <= N^(b-1) product_t min( ||B_sign(t)||_op^|ell_t|, 32N^2(1+|ell_t|)(7+5sqrt(2))^N). (14a) At completeness the full ADO modified dimension is its known root phase divided by N, so it does not change the exponential bound. This proof uses the actual original pivotal cut, not a new positive closing trace. It supplies the source estimate for (14) at every braid width. Since 2pi log(7+5sqrt(2)) < 5 v_8, every repeated-generator block of length at least five gives a strict improvement over its separate-crossing bound. The displayed numerical comparison can be verified by elementary convergent series for sqrt(2), log and Catalan's constant; it is not used for (11) or (14). The constant is deliberately coarse, so (14) is not asserted to equal or be bounded by Vol(S^3-K). It establishes a real quantitative gain from coherent block contraction in the specified braid word after the finest gauge program has been shown ineffective on the alternating-sign class. ## 6. Reproduction and numerical scope python3 experiments/actual_convex_gauge_block_energy.py python3 experiments/actual_convex_gauge_block_energy.py --full The script uses exact finite factorial moduli in logarithmic form; the only floating operations in the objective are ordinary positive log-sum-exp and its gradient. It checks the transpose/reflection marginals through N=32 and optimizes complete coupled wire gauges at width four and six. In the class (6), the independently verified zero gradient is the global certificate, so starting at that point does not rely on slow optimization in null directions. Nonalternating examples are diagnostics; finite-iteration results there are feasible upper bounds and are not claimed exact optima. The block tests independently construct the bounded physical Omega, check its actual polynomial crossing identity, and evaluate positive and negative twist powers through N=10. The all-N bound is the analytic Hermite/resolvent proof above, not extrapolation from those powers. [Saved results](../experiments/actual_convex_gauge_block_energy_results.json).

title: Arbitrary widths in the actual Conway seed grammar
text: # Arbitrary widths in the actual Conway seed grammar 30 October 2026. The restriction to the seed h^3 is unnecessary. Let A_s=h^s for any fixed integer s>=3, using s separate original complete-circle coupons and their actual stack product. Expressions may use any finite mixture of these seeds, literal turns, and products. Every retained C(FG) with two such expressions has the same strict source geometry and signed mixed-source estimates as the original three-leaf grammar. The proof below checks the changed seed hypotheses; it does not infer them just from an expression name. There is also an extension to the isolated cylinder C(A_s) for s>=4. The isolated C(A_3) remains outside the whole mixed-color gap proved here. All sizes, trees, signs and filling slopes are fixed before the level tends to infinity. No uniform estimate over unbounded diagrams is asserted. ## 1. Full finite support and an interior optimizer The full Newton coefficients of h_N are positive at every index 0<=r<=M=floor((N-1)/2), including its constant coefficient N^2. For N>=3, A_3 already has strictly positive coefficients at EVERY index 0,...,N-1. Since Bhat_r Bhat_0=Bhat_r, multiplication by h preserves that full strict support. Thus A_s=A_3 h^(s-3) has full support for all s>=3 and every N>=3. This is the actual repeated-root algebra identity, including its normal directions. The old N=2 exception is unchanged. Here is the continuous strict-feasibility argument, separately from the finite support. A strict state of a seed has leaves in (0,1/2) and, at every gate (x,y)->z, max(x,y)<z<x+y<1. (1) A_3 admits such a state at every prescribed output b in (0,1). Given this property for A_(s-1), choose 0<c<min(b/2,1-b,1/4), t=b-c/2. Use its strict state at output t and a last leaf c. The gate (t,c)->b obeys (1). This proves feasibility for every A_s. At a macro-product choose both child outputs in (b/2,min(b,1/2)); at a turn use the child output 1-b. Hence every proper expression admits a strict state at every interior output. For C(FG), delete only the forced last gate: its inputs sum to 1 and its exact finite coefficient equals one. Choose both child outputs 1/2 to obtain a strict state of the reduced problem. For C(A_s), s>=4, choose its last leaf c in (0,1/2) and the preceding A_(s-1) output 1-c. Again every retained atom is strict. The boundary barrier is unchanged but is worth making explicit. The leaf atoms are (x,1/2-x,1/2), twice; with p=z-x,q=z-y,r=x+y-z,w=1-x-y the gate atoms are (y,x,w), (p,q,2r+w), (p+q,r,r+w). (2) Every nonvertex-flat atom (0,a,1-a), 0<a<1, has positive infinite directional derivative toward the constructed strict state. A vertex-flat atom has a finite derivative and cannot cancel it. A proper endpoint wire propagates down through turns and products until either a product has interior inputs summing to one, or a leaf equals zero. Both exhibit a nonvertex-flat atom. A leaf at 1/2 does also. With every proper wire interior, any equality in (1) displays such an atom directly in (2). Therefore no boundary state maximizes the action. Each positive tetrahedron is strictly concave in its independent angles. The retained angle maps recover every leaf and product wire; turns then recover their wires too. The removed last gate adds no free tangent direction. Thus the reduced Hessian is negative definite, the optimizer is unique and strict, and every fixed proper-output profile is real analytic on (0,1). This proof uses no special property of the number three after constructing a strict seed state. ## 2. Exact open seed ports for every width For the optimized output b set B=cot(pi b), kappa=exp(-f'(b)), X=sqrt((1+B^2)/(1+kappa)), Y=sqrt(kappa) X. Then X^2+Y^2-B^2=1. The actual product stationarity equations give one common X for its two inputs and output, and B_out=(B_left B_right+X^2-1)/(B_left+B_right), Y_out=Y_left Y_right/(B_left+B_right), B_left+B_right>0. (3) A leaf has B=X=cot(pi a)>0 and Y=1. Consequently every optimized A_s has the SAME a at all its s leaves. Iterating (3), with no restriction placed on the finite source labels, gives B_s=T_s(X)/U_(s-1)(X), Y_s=1/U_(s-1)(X), (4) where T and U are the usual Chebyshev polynomials. These are formulas for the optimizer, not a reduction of the original sum to equal labels. For example the open optimum is on the algebraic branch T_s(X)-cot(pi b) U_(s-1)(X)=0. (5) The output b here is the Newton coordinate, not a renamed physical meridian. The branch and its inequalities follow directly from the positive denominators in (3). If 0<X<1 put alpha=arccos X and h0=sin alpha. Induction gives B_j=h0 cot(j alpha), Y_j=h0 csc(j alpha), 0<j alpha<pi, 1<=j<=s. (6) Indeed B_j+X=h0 sin((j+1)alpha)/(sin(j alpha)sin alpha). Starting at alpha in (0,pi/2), positivity forces the next angle to remain below pi; it cannot skip the entire negative-sine interval. Thus X>cos(pi/s). At X=1 the limit is B_s=Y_s=1/s. For X>1, put beta=arcosh X and h0=sinh beta; then B_s=h0 coth(s beta), Y_s=h0 csch(s beta). (7) In every case, for s>=2, -Y_s<B_s<X. (8) For (6), the upper inequality is strict monotonicity of cotangent and the lower is cot(t)+csc(t)=cot(t/2)>0. For (7), B_s>0 and coth(s beta)<coth beta; X=1 is immediate. This proves the entire seed input needed by the old macro-port argument. ## 3. Closure gives a stronger leaf interval at larger widths The inequality -Y<B<X is preserved by a turn (B,X,Y)->(-B,Y,X) and by every stationary macro-product. For X<1, write its child ports as (B_1,Y_1)=(h0 cot u,h0 csc u), (B_2,Y_2)=(h0 cot v,h0 csc v). The inequalities give u,v>alpha=arccos X and (3) gives u+v<pi. The output has angle u+v, so (8) persists. For X>=1, (8) forces both child B's positive and between sqrt(X^2-1) and X. Therefore 0<X-B_i<1 and B_out-X=[(X-B_1)(X-B_2)-1]/(B_1+B_2)<0; its lower inequality follows from B_out>0. In a closed C(FG) the two root ports are (B,X,Y) and (-B,X,Y). Applying (8) to both gives |B|<min(X,Y), hence X,Y<1. These bounds propagate down every macro-product: its common X<1 is fixed, and Y_out<1 implies u+v<pi-alpha, while u,v>alpha. Hence each child has alpha<u,v<pi-alpha and therefore Y_child<1. Turns exchange X,Y. Stop this induction at a seed, not at its individual leaves, whose Y equals one. At a proper A_s seed, (6) and Y_s<1 say sin(s alpha)>sin alpha, 0<alpha<s alpha<pi. Equivalently (s+1)alpha<pi. Its complete leaf label thus satisfies cos(pi/(s+1))<X<1, 1/4<a<atan(sec(pi/(s+1)))/pi <=atan(sqrt(2))/pi=:a0. (9) In particular every leaf is in the strict high-index source regime, and the old universal alias tangent margin applies. Increasing the seed width strengthens the upper bound; it does not degrade it. The isolated cylinder C(A_s) is explicit. Its final flat relation gives B_(s-1)=-X. Formula (3) excludes X>=1; formula (6) then gives s alpha=pi. Thus X=cos(pi/s), a=atan(sec(pi/s))/pi. (10) For s>=4 this belongs to (1/4,a0], so all required inequalities hold, including the endpoint a=a0 when s=4. For s=3 it is atan(2)/pi>a0; that isolated cylinder is still excluded here. ## 4. The actual source and geometry interfaces extend The extension of the existing signed long-filling proof now follows by its explicit interfaces, rather than by changing its vocabulary. * Exact source: every leaf is still the original T(R^epsilon L_j), epsilon in {0,+1,-1}. Full Newton multiplication, turns, ordinary caps and the exposed mark are unchanged. * Whole-source bounds: at every complete leaf in (9) or (10), the proved tangent inequality dominates the full alias profile by c0=2 Catalan/pi-(3/4)log 2>0. The all-color core majorant, actual gate concavity and affine-wire cancellation are unchanged. This proves the same gap for every alias subset and the physical color complement, including the isolated s=4 endpoint. * Exact complex packet: its leaf finite functions and selected changed actions are unchanged. Strictness and the negative Hessian provide its fixed window. With H actual leaves the full primitive grid still has dimension 2H-3, with every D=N-1 offset retained. Its power is N^(3-H+(2H-3)/2)=N^(3/2); equal optimal seed labels do not reduce that dimension. The same nonzero odd amplitude and exponentially controlled interpolation residual apply. * Geometry: the seed is the literal stack of the same pyramids and prisms. The existing local convex gluing and FREE/CAP angle induction apply at each one of its gates. Strictness supplies all their required inequalities. Their ordered corner maps are the original stack maps, so the closed bowtie cut is unchanged. Every complete edge is a leaf bowtie edge, and the same pure/odd edge words and canonical rectangle decorations prove completeness. * Marked deformation: its rational white/prism/turn identities and actual signed shaded maps are local. The strict critical branch therefore assembles them with the same primitive peripheral paths, U=-2pi i chi and V=-2 partial_chi Phi. No new slope or phase convention is introduced by a larger seed. Consequently the quantum and geometric inputs of the [signed long-filling assembly](actual_odd_conway_long_filling_volume.md) hold for these enlarged classes. For every fixed signed coupon pattern and independently sufficiently long signed integral full-twist fillings of any selected auxiliary circles, the same original-source limit equals the actual filled hyperbolic volume. The source normalization, both level parities and the marked peripheral filling equation are exactly those of that assembly. ## 5. Constructive knot parity for every width Use the original endpoint pairings I,U,X. A pure leaf has U, an odd leaf X, and the only loop-creating stack choice is U times U. An odd-length seed can realize {U,X} without loops: use exactly one pure leaf or use all odd leaves. An even-length seed realizes {I,U} without loops by the same two choices. Thus every seed supplies at least two loop-free types. Turns permute I,U,X; the already checked set-product table preserves at least two choices under every product. Backtracking a root choice U or X gives one main component after the cylindrical closure. Full-twist fillings preserve that connectivity. Therefore filling all auxiliary circles produces a constructive knot subfamily for every allowed fixed expression, including isolated C(A_s) with s>=4. Partial fillings retain one main component together with the unfilled auxiliary components. This is still a specified diagram grammar, not a claim covering all arborescent or alternating knots. Audit: [seed recurrences, support and interval certificates](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_arbitrary_width_seeds.py). The proof for unbounded fixed seed widths is the induction and trigonometric argument above; a finite list of widths does not prove it. Independent internal review: separate source and geometry readers checked the all-width strictness/port argument, isolated s=4 endpoint, full primitive lattice, signed packet interfaces, actual bowtie/cusp reconstruction and loop-free knot parity choices. The primary agent checked the displayed recurrences, boundary argument and extension scope and replayed the focused audit: PASS. The claim remains the stated grammar, not all k-bridge or alternating knots.

title: Boundary coefficient limits and the algebraic relation selected by the source
status: Full boundary limit and algebraic relation
text: # Boundary coefficient limits and the algebraic relation selected by the source 29 October 2026. Every coefficient of the actual positive Conway operator has a full-sequence volume profile, including coefficients approaching either endpoint at any rate. At every interior output the optimizer is unique and strictly positive. Its profile supplies one selected algebraic boundary relation and a relative Bloch boundary formula. The boundary coordinate here is the original Newton index. It has NOT been identified with the meridian eigenvalue of a knot, or with a literature quantum A-operator. This extends the closed-source theorem rather than replacing its normalization. In particular its endpoint b=1 is the original marked closure, while b=0 is the actual turned closure. ## 1. The full boundary profile For a fixed robust expression E write its ACTUAL full-normal operator E_N=sum_(r=0)^d e_(E,N,r) Bhat_r, d=N-1. Every coefficient is positive for N>=3. Use the wire polytope from [the Conway variational theorem](actual_positive_conway_variational_limit.md), but leave its final output free. Call this compact rational polytope P_E, its output coordinate b, and its sum of ideal-tetrahedron volumes V_E. Every slice P_E(b), 0<=b<=1, is nonempty. Indeed the constructive integer witnesses give every output r at every level d>=2; their normalized limits supply every real b. Define the boundary profile v_E(b)=max_(x in P_E(b)) V_E(x). (1) Then v_E is finite, continuous and concave on the CLOSED interval [0,1]. Concavity follows by taking convex combinations of maximizing states and using concavity of V_E. Compactness makes (1) upper semicontinuous. Interior continuity follows from finite concavity; at either endpoint concavity gives the reverse lower-limit inequality by interpolation with one fixed interior point. This proves endpoint continuity as well. **Boundary limit theorem.** For EVERY sequence of integers 0<=r_N<=N-1 such that r_N/(N-1)->b, lim_(N -> infinity) (2pi/N) log e_(E,N,r_N)=2v_E(b). (2) No parity restriction, fixed-denominator subsequence, interior saddle, or speed of convergence of r_N/(N-1) is required. ## 2. Exact-output integer approximation The existing uniform factorial estimate applies to every state before fixing its output: log(weight)= (N/pi) V_E(labels/d)+O_E(log N). (3) The number of states is polynomial in N. For the upper bound in (2), choose a largest state. Any convergent subsequence of its normalized labels has output b and lies in P_E(b), by compactness and the closed linear constraints. Equations (1),(3) prove the upper bound. The lower bound needs states with the EXACT prescribed output r_N. The additive semigroup property alone, without the following output correction, would not suffice. First let 0<b<1 and choose a maximizing x_* in P_E(b). Fix a small epsilon>0. Choose a rational point y in P_E sufficiently close to x_* that its output b_0 also satisfies (1-epsilon)b_0 < b < (1-epsilon)b_0+epsilon. (4) This is possible because at b_0=b both inequalities have strict margins. Let D y be integral and put k=floor((1-epsilon)d/D), l=d-kD, R=r_N-kD b_0. For all sufficiently large N, (4) gives 0<=R<=l and l>=2. The constructive full-support theorem gives an integer state a_l at level l with exactly output R. Consequently n_N=kD y+a_l is feasible at level d and has output EXACTLY r_N. Its normalized distance from y is at most (l/d) times the bounded diameter of P_E. Taking epsilon and the distance from y to x_* arbitrarily small, uniform continuity of V_E makes its value arbitrarily close to (1). That single positive state proves the required lower bound. For b=0 choose y rational in the rational face P_E(0), as close to x_* as desired, and let D y be integral. Choose the smallest l>=r_N+2 with l=d modulo D. Then l=o(d), l>=2, and the anchor of level l with output r_N gives the same construction with k=(d-l)/D. For b=1, choose y in P_E(1) and instead take the smallest l>=d-r_N+2 with l=d modulo D. Its required anchor output is l-(d-r_N), which lies in [0,l]. Again l=o(d). These constructions prove (2) at both endpoints, including sublinear but unbounded deviations from them. ## 3. The exact composition laws survive in the entire profile Let R denote the genuine physical turn and let m be the already proved Newton product action: m(x,y,z)=L(x+y)+L(z)-L(x)-L(y) -L(z-x)-L(z-y)-L(x+y-z), L(t)=integral_0^t log(2sin(pi u))du. The exact turn and multiplication of the original coefficients imply the following identities on the whole closed domains: v_(R E)(b)=v_E(1-b), v_(EF)(z)=max_[max(x,y)<=z<=x+y<=1] (v_E(x)+v_F(y)+pi m(x,y,z)). (5) They also follow directly from the source polytopes, keeping all internal variables and shared outputs. In particular v_(EF)(0)=v_E(0)+v_F(0), v_(EF)(1)=max_(0<=x<=1)(v_E(x)+v_F(1-x)). (6) The last product gate is flat in both cases. The first identity is the exact cap-sum decomposition; the second is the full cylindrical pairing and does not assert a connected-sum factorization. ## 4. Every robust interior profile has a unique strict optimizer Fix b in (0,1). There is a feasible state with EVERY leaf label in (0,1/2) and every product gate satisfying p,q,r,w>0, where p=z-x, q=z-y, r=x+y-z, w=1-x-y. Here is a constructive induction. For a product of two robust expressions choose their input labels x=y in (b/2,min(b,1/2)) and use the induction inside both children. A turn uses the child's output 1-b. For the seed h^3 choose a small positive c<min(b/2,(1-b)/2,1/4), put t=b-c/2, and choose a in (t/2,min(t,1/2)). Give its first two leaves label a, their product output t, and its last leaf label c. Both product gates are strict, all leaves are strict, and the final output is b. Now join a maximizing state to this strict state by a straight segment. An ideal atom with boundary angles (0,a,1-a), 0<a<1, has directional derivative +infinity toward the strict state: its zero-angle term is -epsilon c log epsilon+O(epsilon), c>0. At a simplex vertex (0,0,1), the epsilon log epsilon terms cancel, leaving a finite derivative. Positive atoms also have finite derivatives. Thus no nonvertex-flat atom can occur at a maximum. No wire can have value 0 or 1 there. A product output 0 forces both children to be 0. A product output 1 either has two interior children summing to 1, giving a nonvertex-flat first atom, or has an endpoint child. A turn interchanges the endpoints. Descending through endpoint children must reach a leaf: value 1 is infeasible there and value 0 gives its nonvertex-flat atom (0,1/2,1/2). A leaf value 1/2 gives the same obstruction with the angles exchanged. All wires are consequently interior. At a product, w=0 then makes the first atom (y,x,0) nonvertex-flat, and r=0 makes the third atom (z,0,1-z) nonvertex-flat. If p=0 and q>0, the second atom is (0,q,1-q); if p=q=0, the third is (0,x,1-x). The q=0 case is the same. Therefore every product is strict at the maximum. Finally the Hessian has no kernel in the affine wire space. A zero of its negative quadratic form leaves every positive atom angle unchanged. Leaf angles first fix their wire variations to zero; the product angle p=z-x then fixes the output variation, inductively through the tree. Turn variations follow their child. This proves negative definiteness, both with b fixed and with b varying. It follows that the optimizer is UNIQUE for every b in (0,1), and the implicit function theorem makes it real analytic throughout that interval. The Schur complement of the negative definite wire Hessian gives v_E''(b)<0. There is no maximizing-face change in the interior for this robust compiler. Endpoint degenerations are still allowed and are covered by the full limit theorem (2). ## 5. The algebraic boundary branch and its scope Choose a face F of P_E whose projection to b is nonconstant, and a point in its relative interior which is stationary in the internal directions at fixed b. Delete the atoms identically flat on F. Choose rational affine coordinates (y,b) on F and remove the rational kernel of the internal angle map. The remaining positive angles are alpha_jr=a_jr+sum_l B_jrl y_l+C_jr b. (7) All coefficients are rational; weights w_j are positive rational. The Conway case has w_j=1. The negative internal Hessian is positive definite by the [quotient-Hessian theorem](positive_source_algebraic_volume_period.md). Therefore the stationary point continues as a unique real analytic branch y(b), with positive atoms, for b in a small interval. It is the maximum on that face's fixed-b slice. It represents the FULL profile v_E only where this face remains globally maximizing; the argument does not assume away a change of maximizing face. For the robust Conway compiler, section 4 proves that F is the whole wire polytope and that the selected positive branch represents v_E throughout (0,1). Thus the following algebraic relation applies to its entire interior profile. Uniqueness and the nonsingular internal Jacobian continue the same selected component along that interval; there is no exchange of stationary branches on the positive place. Choose an integer Q clearing the denominators of B and C, and put U_l=exp(pi i y_l/Q), M=exp(pi i b/Q), t_jr=exp(pi i a_jr) product_l U_l^(Q B_jrl) M^(Q C_jr), s_jr=(t_jr-t_jr^-1)/i. The s_jr are Laurent polynomials over a cyclotomic number field, and are strictly positive at the selected real branch. For an integer H clearing the denominators of w_j B_jrl and w_j C_jr, internal stationarity is exactly product_jr s_jr^(H w_j B_jrl)=1, for every l. (8) Keep U,M and every s nonzero when clearing negative exponents. The internal Jacobian of these equations, in y, is -(H/pi) Hess_y V and hence invertible. It follows that the selected component is locally etale over M and its function field is finite algebraic over a number field's rational function field in M. This can also be seen from differentials: (8) expresses every dU_l in terms of dM; M is a local parameter, so the component has exactly one transcendence degree. This is a selected local branch statement, not a claim that every component or every point is unramified. Define the exact boundary multiplier P=product_jr s_jr^(H w_j C_jr). (9) It belongs to that algebraic function field. Thus there is a nonzero polynomial relation A_F(M,P)=0 over a number field, with a selected positive real place. On the real branch P>0, and the envelope identity gives the absolute differential normalization d v_F/db=-(pi/H) log P.
