(10) Internal derivatives disappear by (8); no unproved differentiation of a quantum asymptotic is used. If there are no internal variables, the same statements follow directly from (7),(9). The symbol A_F denotes THIS source boundary relation. It is not called the knot A-polynomial: M exponentiates the Newton output, and P is its variational conjugate. An actual peripheral interpretation is still required before identifying them with knot holonomy variables. Earlier geometric boundary constructions start with a marked gluing variety; here the original coefficient problem produces its own algebraic relation before that geometric comparison. The subsequent [actual Conway cell construction](actual_positive_conway_hyperbolic_volume.md) now supplies a geometric meaning throughout the robust interior: v_E(b) is the volume of an explicit convex ideal polyhedron with one quadrilateral port, and its ordered modulus is kappa_E(b)=exp(-v'_E(b)/pi), P=kappa_E(b)^H. Thus the boundary conjugate in (9) is an actual face modulus. The output phase M records its specified port-edge angle; this still does not identify M and P with a knot's peripheral eigenvalues. ## 6. The relative Bloch boundary fixes the period normalization Work in the selected algebraic function field, enlarged by the needed roots of unity, and tensor multiplicative groups with Q. For each positive atom define two algebraic shapes z_j=t_j1 s_j2/s_j3, z_j^dagger=t_j1^-1 s_j2/s_j3. On the real branch dagger is complex conjugation. For complex parameters it is the displayed algebraic companion; no unproved conjugation involution of the selected function field is assumed. The sine identity gives both 1-z_j=t_j2^-1 s_j1/s_j3 and 1-z_j^dagger=t_j2 s_j1/s_j3. Therefore the exact wedge calculation from [the source Bloch theorem](actual_positive_source_bloch_regulator.md) applies in the function field as well. With beta_F=(1/2)sum_j w_j([z_j]-[z_j^dagger]), it gives delta beta_F=(Q/H) M wedge P. (11) Indeed the internal phase wedges vanish by (8); the sole remaining row is Q M wedge sum_jr w_j C_jr s_jr, which is (Q/H)M wedge P by (9). This is a rational identity with the chosen exponent scaling visible. It makes no integral torsion or peripheral-framing claim. At any algebraic real specialization, the actual regulator is D(beta_F)=v_F(b). (12) Applying the regulator differential to (11), using |M|=1, arg M=pi b/Q and P>0, gives precisely (10). Thus the algebraic boundary relation, relative Bloch boundary and actual source-volume derivative have one consistent normalization. The closed-source theorem at b=1 remains valid even where a stationary branch degenerates. This note does not infer that it is obtained by unramified continuation of one interior branch. Nor does it identify the relative class with the marked geometric class of a complement. ## 7. An exact normalization check For the single positive angle family (y,b,1-y-b), with 0<b<1, the internal maximum has y=(1-b)/2. Here Q=H=1 and the equations are U^2 M=-1, P=2sin(pi b/2), P^2=2-M-M^-1, z=1-M^-1, z^dagger=1-M. (13) Thus both the algebraic boundary relation and its positive real place are explicit. Since P^2=-(1-M)^2/M, direct wedge expansion gives delta(([z]-[z^dagger])/2)=M wedge P, as required by (11). This is a check of the normalization, not an identification of this single-atom family with an actual knot source. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_boundary_volume_relation.py) checks exact full-output anchors and prescribed-output semigroup corrections for robust expression trees, including sublinear endpoint sequences. It also checks (13) and its relative wedge identity exactly. The all-sequence and algebraic-branch conclusions are proved above; sampled large-level growth is not used to infer them. Independent analytical review checked the arbitrary prescribed-output and endpoint constructions, closed-profile continuity, the full strict optimizer barrier, Hessian injectivity, selected algebraic branch and relative boundary normalization. Fresh audit passed 3,000 full-output anchors, 1,392 interior corrections, 1,312 sublinear endpoint corrections, 1,592 exact strict interior assignments and the symbolic normalization. The knot-peripheral A-operator comparison is not asserted by this review.

title: The actual closed Conway cut from its bowtie ribbon graph
status: Corrected closed cut and marked cusps
text: # The actual closed Conway cut from its bowtie ribbon graph 29 October 2026. This supplies a direct CLOSED-diagram identification for the complete Conway geometry. It also corrects an overstatement in the earlier explanation of the open cells: the quadrilateral port of a single leaf pyramid must not simply be called half of the physical four-punctured tangle boundary. The closed identification can and should be proved without that assertion. The proof below reconstructs the actual projection cut from literal main-wire connections and the original crossing disks. It compares EVERY colored face cycle and its ribbon order with the stationary polyhedron. Matching only component counts or volume is not used. ## 1. Why the open-port description needs qualification For a leaf pyramid the port is Q=(C0,C1,C2,C3), while its shaded faces are (O,C1,C2) and (O,C3,C0). Restoring the crossing disk pairs C1 with C0 and C2 with C3. In particular it identifies the two CAP edges of Q within each copy. The two FREE edges are joined across copies through the white faces. The two remaining quadrilateral faces consequently have four paired edges and TWO ideal vertex classes. Their compactification has Euler characteristic 2-4+2=0; it is not the usual two-quad cellulation of a four-punctured sphere, whose four punctures remain four distinct vertices. Thus an open metric port is useful auxiliary cut data. Its ordered cross ratio and its gluing identities are valid, but those facts do not identify it by itself with the physical four-punctured boundary or determine that boundary's full holonomy representation. In particular one cannot infer a deformed peripheral representation from port cross-ratio matching alone. This observation does NOT give a counterexample to the closed hyperbolic-volume theorem. The closed theorem has the following independent projection-cut proof, which avoids the open-port claim. ## 2. Compile the original main segments without using prisms Expand the robust expression into h leaves, actual turns and stacks. At leaf i label its four main half-segments C_i0 bottom-left, C_i1 bottom-right, C_i2 top-right, C_i3 top-left. These are the pieces from the leaf's crossing-disk punctures to its four physical ports. Its two original main arcs join 0 to 1 and 2 to 3, each crossing its own disk once. The half-segments on opposite sides of that puncture are kept DISTINCT in the projection polyhedron; the shaded face pairing will restore the main arc. An open expression has four exposed, still unpaired half-segments. The literal rules for these four labels are: * A turn replaces (C0,C1,C2,C3) by (C1,C2,C3,C0). * In a lower F, upper G stack, pair F2 with G1 and F3 with G0. The four exposed labels become (F0,F1,G2,G3). * The final cylindrical closure pairs C0 with C3 and C1 with C2. Each pairing joins exactly the two ends of one actual main segment between successive crossing disks. A structural induction shows that each exposed label is still unpaired, and every removed label is paired exactly once. Therefore a closed expression with H leaves has 2H such segment pairs, not an unspecified equivalence relation deduced from a quantum polynomial. Make one ideal vertex for each paired segment, and one further vertex O_i for each upper crossing-circle semicircle. At leaf i place the two SHADED triangles (O_i,C_i1,C_i2), (O_i,C_i3,C_i0). (1) Here each C now denotes its actual paired-segment vertex. These are the original two sides of that leaf's half crossing disk. Their six edges are the complete bowtie at that leaf. All pairings are the physical identity wires, with no auxiliary circle omitted. ## 3. Ribbon order determines all white faces Use the orientation of the original projection sphere. At O_i the cyclic neighbor order is (C_i0,C_i1,C_i2,C_i3). Both shaded triangles in (1) have their displayed positive cyclic order in the local projection chart. At an outer corner of a shaded triangle, list its outgoing next neighbor followed by its incoming previous neighbor. This ordered pair records the shaded sector; the complementary sector is white. When an actual identity segment joins two such corners, concatenate their two ordered shaded sectors. This is the cyclic order at the resulting four-valent vertex. It follows by taking a thin planar regular neighborhood of the actual joining arc: the two shaded sectors remain on its two sides and the white sectors connect through the two sides of that neighborhood. No strand crosses another during this contraction. Consequently the source's literal planar matching gives a complete oriented ribbon graph, including every shaded sector. A facial walk arriving along the dart (u,v) leaves v along the neighbor preceding u in that cyclic order. The walks (1) are exactly the shaded faces; all the remaining walks are WHITE faces. Thus all white polygons are fixed by the actual diagram, not guessed from face counts. The graph is embedded in the original projection sphere: quarter- turns rotate its charts, and products join the two matching ports by the two actual disjoint identity wires. This construction records nesting and cyclic order as well as abstract incidence. An unembedded graph or a linking matrix would not supply the same information. ## 4. This is the genuine cut of the closed link exterior Put the compiled untwisted main diagram in its projection sphere. Every auxiliary circle is the original small perpendicular circle with its recorded twice-punctured spanning disk. Those disks lie in disjoint leaf boxes, and remain disjoint under every actual turn and stack. In each projection ball, the upper or lower semicircle of an auxiliary component is boundary parallel by its literal half disk. Drill these disjoint semicircles and cut along those same half disks. This returns a ball: drilling one boundary-parallel arc introduces one handle, and opening its recorded bridge disk cancels that handle in the explicit collar of the arc. The collars are disjoint, so this cancellation can be performed for all arcs. The main segments lie on the projection boundary; removing their small neighborhoods makes ideal ends and does not add an interior handle to this cut ball. The ideal vertices of the cut ball are precisely the upper semicircles O_i and the main segments between disk punctures. Flattening each half disk exposes exactly its two triangles (1). At its punctures, the main-segment sides occur in the order of section 3. The remaining boundary pieces are the original planar projection regions, whose cycles are exactly the white facial walks of that ribbon graph. This gives a reversible cut with all faces labeled. The two balls glue across white faces by their projection labels. Within each ball, the two shaded faces of disk i are paired fixing O_i and matching C_i1 to C_i0 and C_i2 to C_i3. These restore the two original arcs through that disk. Reversing all cuts therefore recovers the ACTUAL original link exterior, with its retained auxiliary circles and component/mark paths. ## 5. The stationary polyhedron has exactly this ribbon boundary The geometric construction uses the same local shaded triangles (1). At a product its explicit prism maps are F:(C0,C1,C2,C3) -> (v0,v1,P,infinity), G:(C0,C1,C2,C3) -> (infinity,P,v2,v3). They make precisely the two segment pairings F2=G1 and F3=G0, and leave exposed corners (F0,F1,G2,G3). A turn cyclically rotates these exposed labels. The final face gluing j->3-j makes the remaining cylindrical pairings, exactly as in section 2. The right/flat angle table proves that every edge not belonging to a shaded leaf triangle is a flat WHITE/WHITE seam and is removed when those two white pieces are merged. No edge of a shaded triangle is removed. Hence the final nonflat boundary graph is precisely the union of the leaf bowties (1) under the actual segment pairings. The local orientation check in the displayed prism maps concatenates the shaded sectors exactly as in section 3; the maps are the left/right identity stack, not a reflection of one selected child or an unrecorded mutation. Flat white merging does not change any remaining cyclic order. Therefore the geometric polyhedron and the actual projection cut have the SAME oriented ribbon graph, the SAME two shaded triangles for every disk, and the SAME complete list of white face cycles. Their boundaries are labeled cellulations of a sphere. A map of the matched cells extends over the two balls by radial extension after choosing interior points. Together with the matched white and shaded gluing maps, this gives a homeomorphism of the assembled geometric manifold to the actual link exterior. This is the closed topological identification needed by the volume theorem. The independent audit below implements section 2--3 directly from the original wires, WITHOUT constructing any prism. It then compares every colored face cycle with the separately implemented stationary cell compiler. This is a stronger check than component counts or the numbers 3H,6H,3H+2; the proof itself is the local ribbon-order argument and reversible disk cut above. ## 6. Every actual crossing-circle cusp is explicitly marked The closed-cut identification also gives a general complete-cusp formula. The apex O_i retains the four original neighbors of its leaf pyramid, even after all white merges. In its original local upper-half-space coordinate they are C0=1, C1=E, C2=-1, C3=-E, E=exp(2pi i x_i), 0<x_i<1/2. On a horosphere at O_i=infinity these form a rectangle. Its FREE (white) sides have length W=2sin(pi x_i); its CAP (shaded) sides have length H=2cos(pi x_i). The complete cusp has TWO rectangles, one from each projection ball. Their original disk and projection pairings give the primitive lattice mu=E-1, lambda=-2(E+1), tau_geom=lambda/mu=2i cot(pi x_i). (2) One direct path check fixes the marking. The meridian is the inverse shaded map, fixing O and sending C3 to C2 and C0 to C1. Thus at completeness it is exactly z->z+(E-1). The longitude crosses the bottom white face to the other copy and returns through the top white face. Its translation is -2(E+1). This runs along the two sides of the original crossing disk, and is its disk-framed preferred longitude. It traverses those sides once, not twice. The parallelogram has area 2WH, the total area of the two rectangles, so these paths form a primitive peripheral basis. The sign convention agrees with a positive imaginary cusp shape. Equation (2) is a statement about ACTUAL crossing-circle meridians and longitudes. The Newton wire x_i is used to compute their shape; it is not itself renamed as a meridian logarithm. In the general source filling convention phi_titi(0)=2pi i tau_packet,i, the packet parameter is HALF this geometric ratio: tau_packet,i=i cot(pi x_i), dV_i/dU_i=2 tau_packet,i=tau_geom,i. Matching this Hessian is a useful necessary check, but a full deformed marked representation must still be supplied before the general quantum filling transfer can identify filled volumes. Audit: [literal bowtie ribbon faces and complete cusp paths](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut_results.json). This repairs the closed cut interpretation; it does not assert that the single open quadrilateral port is a physical four-punctured boundary, or that arbitrary deformed port matches already solve the full peripheral gluing equations. Independent internal reviews: the local-cell and coherent-source agents separately read the full closed ribbon and disk-cut argument and the primitive cusp marking, and reported PASS. The coherent-source agent also independently replayed the strengthened 69-case audit. The audit additionally fixes one global sphere orientation and compares every oriented face cycle and every vertex cyclic order, rather than allowing independent reversal of faces. Primary-agent analytical review checked the direct closed disk cut, actual segment matching, oriented ribbon induction, and primitive cusp marking. Fresh replay passed all 69 oriented face/rotation comparisons. The former open-port overstatement has been replaced in the complete geometry note; no deformed representation is inferred from this correction.

title: Exact cap-sum reduction of the source and its volume problem
text: # Exact cap-sum reduction of the source and its volume problem 29 October 2026. There is a general topological reduction of the actual positive Conway class, before any hyperbolic gluing problem is attempted. A cap closure of a stack is a componentwise connected sum of its cap closures. Its ORIGINAL full-normal quantum source factors exactly, and its entire angle polytope and volume functional factor with it. This does not turn a Conway four-punctured sphere into a rigid pair of pants. The separating surface used here is an explicitly different sphere: it crosses only the TWO wires between stacked boxes, after the outer cap closure has been made. The result applies to arbitrary boxes in the actual Conway algebra, not just to a pure run of circles. ## 1. Two closures and the exact source identity Use the physical boxes, genuine turn R, Newton basis Bhat_r, and original pointed functional phi of the [actual Conway compiler](actual_positive_complete_circle_conway_trees.md). Put d=N-1. For a box F write C_N(F)=phi(F), D_N(F)=phi(R F). The first is its ordinary two-strand cylindrical closure. Rotating the second diagram back to the original position of F identifies it with the cap closure: the two upper ports are joined to each other and the two lower ports are joined to each other. The same actual cups, caps, and single mark are retained. This is a description of a literal closed diagram, not of an extra functional invented for the proof. For F=sum f_r Bhat_r the established actual turn gives C_N(F)=f_d, D_N(F)=f_0. The full repeated-root multiplication rule has only ONE contribution at coordinate zero: i=j=k=0, with coefficient one. Therefore for ANY two actual boxes in this algebra, D_N(FG)=D_N(F)D_N(G). (1) There is no positivity hypothesis in (1); no root normal, auxiliary color, or framing scalar is removed. All factors are the raw sources of their recorded diagrams. Framing conversions, if desired, retain their separately recorded unit characters. This equality is proved in the actual full Newton algebra, not by citing a multiplicativity theorem for a different link invariant. For the robust positive class, D_N(F),D_N(G)>0 for N>=3. Iterating (1) gives an exact product for every finite cap-closed stack. The two turns also satisfy C_N(RF)=D_N(F) and D_N(RF)=C_N(F), because R reverses all Newton coordinates. At the level of unmarked closed diagrams, these last relations are realized by rotating the whole closed diagram; when a point is recorded, it must be transported with that rotation. The supplied source identities already specify their marks. They do not assert that arbitrary choices of a marked component of an arbitrary link have been proved equivalent. ## 2. The actual separating sphere and its component labels Put the lower box F and upper box G in disjoint balls, and connect their two interface ports by two short vertical arcs in an otherwise empty collar. Perform the cap closure outside the two boxes: the lower pair of F is capped, as is the upper pair of G. Every auxiliary component stays in its own box. Choose a horizontal disk through the middle of the interface collar. Closing that disk around the lower ball and its lower cap in the empty exterior gives a sphere S which meets the link in exactly the TWO interface arcs, once each, and no other component. Cut along S and cap its two punctures on each side by a trivial arc. The lower resulting link is exactly the cap closure of F: the newly inserted arc is its upper cap. The upper resulting link is exactly the cap closure of G: the inserted arc is its lower cap. This is a reversible construction, with the original ribbon framing inherited by each arc. Thus, as an actual unmarked link, cap(FG)=cap(F) #_(upper cap of F, lower cap of G) cap(G). (2) The subscript is essential. A general cap-closed box can have its upper and lower caps on DIFFERENT main components. Equation (2) does not silently choose an arbitrary distinguished component in either factor. Nor does the proof use a linking matrix to recognize the link: the empty collar and its two-punctured sphere exhibit the connected sum directly. If c(F) counts all components in cap(F), then c(FG)=c(F)+c(G)-1. (3) All components other than the two named cap components remain intact. For more than two factors, use parallel interface spheres, obtaining a tree of componentwise connected sums with the cap labels retained. The original marked point can be followed through this construction; (1) is independently the exact identity for the compiler's specified marked source, so no change-of-mark theorem is needed to infer it. This reduction is special to the cap closure. An ordinary cylindrical closure of FG has an outside return running across the same cut and does NOT give this two-punctured sphere. Its exact source is instead the full pairing sum_i f_i g_(d-i), which in general does not factor. ## 3. The entire variational problem splits, including its boundary For any fixed robust expression F, let P_F^0 be its wire polytope from the [whole-source variational theorem](actual_positive_conway_variational_limit.md), but with final output 0 instead of 1. Let V_F^0 be the SAME sum of leaf and multiplication tetrahedral volumes, restricted to this face. Equivalently these are the polytope and volume function for R F with its final turn wire deleted. Thus the proved full-sequence limit is lim_N (2pi/N)log D_N(F)=2 max_(P_F^0) V_F^0. (4) For the cap-closed product FG, the final product has output z=0. The exact constraints max(x,y)<=z<=x+y force x=y=0. Its product weight is exactly one at every level, and its continuous product action is m(0,0,0)=0. More explicitly, the three product angle triples are all (0,0,1), so the entire final gate is flat. Deleting the forced wires therefore gives the literal affine identity P_(FG)^0 = P_F^0 x P_G^0, V_(FG)^0 = V_F^0 + V_G^0. (5) These equalities hold on the whole CLOSED polytopes, not just near a saddle. They include boundary maxima and every shared wire inside each factor. Consequently max V_(FG)^0 = max V_F^0 + max V_G^0. (6) At the exact integer level the state sets have the same Cartesian product and the weights multiply. Thus (5) is stronger than deriving additivity after taking a limit: both its quantum and angle versions come from the same forced zero-coordinate conservation law. The stationarity equations for nonflat atoms split into the two independent systems as well. Any claim of a single nondegenerate geometric critical point for the unreduced whole expression must first remove this forced-flat gate and respect the topological decomposition (2). Uniqueness or algebraicity of the two reduced optima does not erase the connected-sum sphere. ## 4. A general boundary reduction procedure Retain a closure flag C or D alongside the actual expression tree. At a turn, switch the flag and retain the child's diagram and mark. At a product with flag D, split into the two children, each with flag D, and record the sphere and its upper/lower cap labels from section 2. At a product with flag C, stop at that factor. Leaves are retained. This terminates since each step removes at least one expression vertex. It yields simultaneously: * an exact product of original source scalars; * an exhibited componentwise connected-sum decomposition of the unmarked closed diagram, with transported marked data recorded; * a Cartesian product decomposition of its reduced angle polytopes, and an additive decomposition of their volume functions. No assertion of primeness is attached to the factors at which this procedure stops. A four-punctured Conway seam inside such a factor still needs its actual incidence and completeness proof. This is an exact boundary reduction, not a complete JSJ algorithm. ## 5. Positive exponential growth can come from several hyperbolic pieces Let A=h^3 be the robust seed and set, for k>=1, E_k=R((R A)^k). The whole original scalar satisfies, at EVERY N>=3, C_N(E_k)=C_N(A)^k. (7) This follows from (1) and R^2=1 on the actual algebra. In this particular family there is no ambiguity about the connected-sum component: A has U main pairing and two internal main circles; R A has through pairing and the same two internal circles. In its cap closure the upper and lower caps therefore lie on ONE main component. Every interface sphere in section 2 joins those components. Rotating the closed factor back identifies it with the actual theta closure C(A), including the transported point on that component. The [theta-link geometry](actual_marked_theta_link_and_angle_geometry.md) already proves that this factor is the literal untwisted six-component augmented theta link, has four regular ideal octahedra, and satisfies the original-source limit 4v8. Consequently E_k is an actual componentwise connected sum of k such theta links and has number of components = 5k+1, lim_N (2pi/N)log C_N(E_k)=4k v8. (8) For k>=2 its complement is not a complete finite-volume hyperbolic manifold. Here is a group proof which avoids inferring topology from the scalar. The explicit sum sphere gives, by cutting collars and van Kampen, an amalgam of the two summand groups over the infinite cyclic subgroup generated by the glued component's meridian mu. Each theta summand is already proved complete hyperbolic, so its cusp group injects as Z^2. Choose a longitude lambda_1 and lambda_2 in the two adjacent summands. Each commutes with mu, and neither lies in <mu>. The amalgam normal-form argument says that their commutator lambda_1 lambda_2 lambda_1^-1 lambda_2^-1 is nontrivial: its four letters alternate between the factors and none lies in the amalgamated cyclic subgroup. Their images remain nontrivial after further sums by the same normal form. In a torsion-free orientation-preserving hyperbolic manifold group, the centralizer of a nontrivial parabolic is abelian. To see this directly, conjugate that parabolic to z->z+1. A commuting Mobius map must fix infinity, hence has form z->az+b; commutation forces a=1. All such translations commute. Here mu would be the meridian of an actual cusp and hence a nontrivial parabolic, contradicting the two noncommuting longitudes in its centralizer. This proves the stated nonhyperbolicity. Equation (8) is therefore equality with the SUM of the volumes of the exhibited hyperbolic summands, not the volume of a nonexistent complete hyperbolic structure on the whole complement. No general simplicial-volume or JSJ-identification theorem is needed or claimed for this statement. It supplies a necessary scope check for any proposed universal Conway volume theorem, while preserving the exact whole-source and variational information. ## 6. What remains after the reduction This result supplies a general topology-compatible reduction rather than a new primitive hyperbolic equality. It strengthens the earlier pure cap-run example: the obstruction persists with arbitrary positive rates and with genuine complete hyperbolic factors, so a nonzero variational maximum is not a hyperbolicity certificate. For each retained cylindrical factor, the outstanding task remains the actual global face/edge/peripheral dictionary for its nonflat angle functional. The two-punctured sum spheres above can be removed before that task. An internal four-punctured seam cannot be removed by the same argument. Audit: [exact full-source, support, and component checks](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_cap_sum_reduction.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_conway_cap_sum_reduction_results.json). The finite calculations supplement the uniform algebraic identity, explicit sphere construction, and variational Cartesian-product proof; they are not numerical manifold recognition or a proof for unreduced primitive factors. Independent internal review: the primary agent read the full literal two-wire sphere construction, cap-component labels, exact zero-output polytope factorization, and amalgam-centralizer proof, and reported PASS. A fresh primary-agent replay of the complete audit also passed. The review retains the distinction between these connected sums and an unreduced primitive hyperbolic complement.

title: A uniform complex packet for the actual positive Conway core
text: # A uniform complex packet for the actual positive Conway core 29 October 2026. A fixed rectangular window about the unique strict complete optimizer gives an EXACT separately-even holomorphic packet for the original positive auxiliary-color core. Its complex asymptotic has a nonzero analytic amplitude at every level parity. The proof keeps the finite lattice window, its endpoint currents and all nonzero cotangent modes. It is not an inference from a real-grid asymptotic. This note concerns the core packet and its comparison with the WHOLE positive core on real physical colors. Signed alias estimates and a geometric peripheral interpretation are additional inputs; they are not supplied by the complex Laplace argument itself. ## 1. The actual lattice and a fixed strict window Fix one retained cylindrical robust Conway factor. Expand its seed blocks into h leaves and products, and let H be its number of leaves. The expanded expression tree has H-1 products. Delete only the final forced-flat product, whose exact multiplication coefficient is one, and impose its exact input relation i+j=D, where D=N-1. The remaining H leaves and H-2 products have a unique strict complete optimizer by the existing boundary-barrier theorem. Every leaf index lies strictly between zero and D/2, and every retained product's four strict inequalities hold there. There are exactly d=2H-3 (1) free integer wire coordinates. Indeed the H leaf outputs and H-1 product outputs give 2H-1 variables before the final closure. Turn outputs are eliminated one at a time by r_out=D-r_in. Fixing the root output and its final input-sum relation removes two variables. The last relation involves variables of disjoint child subtrees with coefficients +1 or -1, so one can solve it integrally. There is no parity-dependent lattice index or omitted congruence class. Choose the remaining physical wire indices k_1,...,k_d as coordinates and put x=k/N. Every other physical wire has the exact form r_w=N ell_w(x)+delta_w, (2) where ell_w is integral affine and delta_w is a fixed integer. The constants delta_w retain every occurrence of D=N-1. They are not silently replaced by zero. Let x_0 be the strict complete optimizer in these coordinates. Choose a sufficiently small closed rectangular box B centered at x_0, entirely inside the strict source domain. Let chi_l=h_l/N be the auxiliary-color deficit of leaf l. At physical colors h_l>=0, its exact positive core coefficient is A_(N,r_l)(h_l)=N^2 s_(2r_l) /[s_(r_l)^2 s_(r_l-h_l)s_(r_l+h_l)]. (3) On a small fixed complex chi polydisk, replace every sine factorial in the SAME leaf and product weight by the [canonical marked interpolation](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md) G_N. Define the packet Z_N^win(chi)=sum_(k in Z^d, k/N in B) I_N(k/N,chi), (4) where I_N is the product of the H interpolated factors (3) and the H-2 actual interpolated Newton multiplication coefficients. After shrinking B and the chi polydisk, every scaled factorial argument has real part in a fixed compact subinterval of (0,1), on a fixed complex thickening of B. Thus I_N is holomorphic and nonzero there. For large N, EVERY lattice point in (4) is an actual admissible core state at every physical color in the chosen real chi window. No support indicator changes inside this box. Formula (4) is finite and separately even in every chi_l, by the two factors r_l+-h_l in (3). ## 2. Exact normalization of the interpolated summand Write every factorial argument as N alpha_nu(x,chi)+c_nu, with integer c_nu, and let sigma_nu be its signed multiplicity. The canonical uniform expansion gives G_N(N alpha+c) =sqrt(2N sin(pi alpha)) exp[N J(alpha)] (2sin(pi alpha))^c [1+O(N^-1)], J(alpha)=integral_0^alpha Log(2sin(pi u))du. (5) Its marks are continued from positive real arguments. The remainder and its fixed derivatives are uniform on smaller complex compact sets. Equation (5) follows directly from the canonical expansion at alpha+c/N; its shift factor is ESSENTIAL when c is nonzero. Define f(x,chi)=sum_nu sigma_nu J(alpha_nu(x,chi)), b(x,chi)=2^(3-3H) product_nu sin(pi alpha_nu)^(sigma_nu/2) (2sin(pi alpha_nu))^(sigma_nu c_nu). (6) All square roots and powers are continued from the positive real complete window. A leaf has one numerator and four denominator factorials, with its extra N^2. A retained product has two numerator and five denominator factorials. Consequently sum_nu sigma_nu=-3H-3(H-2)=6-6H, I_N(x,chi)=N^(3-H) b(x,chi) exp[Nf(x,chi)] [1+O(N^-1)]. (7) The leading amplitude b is nonzero and positive on the real complete window. It contains all D=N-1 offset factors from (2); there is no unknown periodic normalization. At chi=0, f is exactly the complete source action V_E/pi in the selected free wire coordinates. For general chi it is the sum of the actual product actions and g_chi(x_l)=J(2x_l)-2J(x_l) -J(x_l-chi_l)-J(x_l+chi_l) (8) over the leaves. Here x_l=ell_l(x) is its limiting leaf coordinate. ## 3. A finite-window complex lattice Laplace lemma The following elementary argument applies to (7), and more generally to a fixed-dimensional analytic summand N^a b_N exp(N f), provided: * f is holomorphic on a fixed complex thickening of B and a parameter polydisk, real on the real slice at zero; * at zero it has its unique strict nondegenerate maximum x_0 in B, with negative definite real Hessian; * b_N=b+O(N^-1) uniformly holomorphically, with b(x_0,0)>0; * the source sum uses the entire rectangular integer lattice window. Shrink the box if necessary so the real Hessian stays uniformly negative definite throughout it. The implicit-function theorem gives one holomorphic critical point x_*(chi) near x_0. Put phi(chi)=f(x_*(chi),chi), A(chi)=-f_xx(x_*(chi),chi). Then uniformly on a fixed smaller complex parameter polydisk, sum_(k/N in B) N^a b_N(k/N,chi) exp[Nf(k/N,chi)] =N^(a+d/2) (2pi)^(d/2) b(x_*(chi),chi)/sqrt(det A(chi)) exp[Nphi(chi)] [1+O(N^-1)]. (9) The determinant square root is positive at zero. Here is a proof that explicitly controls the discrete nonzero modes. For each coordinate enclose its retained integer interval by a rectangle whose vertical sides are halfway between consecutive lattice points, and whose horizontal sides have fixed imaginary heights +-eta. The endpoints differ from B's endpoints by O(1/N). The product residue formula with kernels pi N cot(pi N z_j) is EXACTLY the original finite sum. On a vertical half-grid side |cot(pi N z_j)|<=1. On a horizontal side, cot(pi N(x+i eta))=-i+O(exp(-2pi N eta)), cot(pi N(x-i eta))= i+O(exp(-2pi N eta)). (10) At parameter zero the real part of f changes by O(d eta^2) under these imaginary shifts, because its first derivatives are real. The same bound holds with a small additional parameter error after shrinking the parameter disk. The real boundary of B has a fixed strict gap below f(x_0,0). Choose eta first, small enough that O(d eta^2)<pi eta and small enough to retain half the boundary gap. Then choose the fixed parameter disk sufficiently small to retain both inequalities, relative to Re phi(chi). Every contour piece with a vertical side is exponentially below the critical value. Every nonconstant cotangent-error term in the product expansion has at least the factor exp(-2pi N eta); the possible phase increase is smaller than exp(pi N eta). Polynomial prefactors cannot remove these strict exponential gaps. The 2^d constant horizontal kernel terms have coefficient N^d/2^d and the same orientation. Deforming their horizontal boxes to the real box only adds vertical connectors with the already established boundary gap. Thus the exact sum equals N^d times the ordinary analytic integral over B, up to a uniform exponentially smaller error. Replacing the real half-grid rectangle B_N by B changes only O(1/N)-wide boundary strips, which have the same strict exponential gap. This is the finite-window counterpart of suppressing all nonzero Poisson modes; no infinite-lattice replacement was made. Finally deform that integral to x_*(chi)+(B-x_0). This translation remains inside the same holomorphic tube. Its endpoint connectors have the boundary gap. On the translated box, Re(f(x_*+u,chi)-phi(chi))<=-c|u|^2 uniformly for real u, since A(chi) remains close to a positive definite real matrix. Taylor expansion and Gaussian integration give the stated determinant. The nominal N^-1/2 corrections are odd in u and integrate to zero on the symmetric Gaussian domain; truncation errors are exponentially small. The remaining relative error is O(N^-1), including the uniform b_N-b error. This proves (9) for the exact finite packet, not merely for real parameter values or a selected subsequence. ## 4. The Conway packet and its color Hessian Apply (9) with a=3-H and d=2H-3. There is a fixed complex chi polydisk on which Z_N^win(chi)=N^(3/2) a_E(chi) exp[Nphi_E(chi)] [1+O(N^-1)], (11) a_E(chi)=(2pi)^((2H-3)/2) b(x_*(chi),chi)/sqrt(det A(chi)). (12) The amplitude is nonzero and a_E(0)>0. This is the raw source normalization in the stated free integer coordinates. Any separately recorded enhancement or framing phase must still multiply it; (11) does not remove such a factor from an invariant. All statements hold on the whole sequence of sufficiently large N, including both parities. The upper leaf cutoff floor((N-1)/2) lies outside the fixed strict window. Half-grid endpoint choices affect only exponentially small boundary terms, and (2) has no parity- dependent lattice density. The canonical factorial normalization has fixed the actual square roots and the offset factors in (6). The phase and amplitude are separately even in each chi_l. Indeed f and the summand have this symmetry, and uniqueness of the local critical branch gives the same symmetry for x_*. At completeness, phi_E(0)=max V_E/pi, partial_(chi_l) phi_E(0)=0, partial_(chi_l)partial_(chi_m) phi_E(0) =-2pi cot(pi x_(l,*)) delta_lm. (13) To verify the last formula, f_(x chi_l)(x,0)=0 IDENTICALLY in x, because each leaf factor is even in its own parameter. Hence the usual critical-point Schur-complement correction vanishes here. The direct second derivative of (8) is -2pi cot(pi x_l). Every x_(l,*) is in (0,1/2), so this Hessian is strictly negative. Uniformity on a complex disk also supplies every fixed color parameter derivative by Cauchy estimates on a smaller disk. ## 5. Comparison with the positive core, and the remaining interfaces For physical real deficits in a sufficiently small fixed window, the positive core outside B is exponentially smaller than the complete source at chi=0. Indeed each exact deformed core coefficient is at most its complete counterpart, the product coefficients are positive, and the complete action has a strict compact support gap outside B. The polynomial number of states and the uniform global factorial estimates preserve that gap. Therefore |Z_N^core(h)-Z_N^win(h/N)| <=poly(N) exp[N(phi_E(0)-gamma)] (14) with gamma>0. Shrink the real color window so phi_E(h/N) stays above phi_E(0)-gamma/2. Equations (11),(14) then give exponential relative accuracy for the WHOLE positive core. A separate uniform estimate for the signed alias sectors can be combined with (14); the present proof does not assume such sectors are absent. Nor does the complex window argument identify chi with a geometric meridian or establish the Dehn-filling contour. It supplies the exact even analytic core packet, its nonzero marked amplitude, its all-parity normalization and its uniform complex saddle expansion, which those later steps require. ## 6. An explicit three-leaf calibration, including the integer shift For the retained seed C(h^3), use the three original leaf indices i,j,k as free coordinates. The surviving gate output is EXACTLY t=D-k. Thus its limiting output is z=1-x_3, but its interpolated factorials have the additional shift -1 in t. The limiting phase is F(x_1,x_2,x_3)=sum_l g(x_l)+m(x_1,x_2,1-x_3). Its unique maximum occurs at all three x_l=a=atan(2)/pi. Directly, sin(pi a)=2/sqrt(5), sin(2pi a)=4/5, sin(pi(3a-1))=2/(5sqrt(5)), g'(a)=m_z(a,a,1-a)=-log4, m_x(a,a,1-a)=m_y(a,a,1-a)=log4. These give stationarity in the actual three free coordinates. The negative Hessian and its positive determinant square root are A=(25pi/4)(I_3+1 1^T), sqrt(det A)=125pi^(3/2)/4. (15) Each unshifted leaf amplitude in (5) is sqrt(10)/8; the unshifted gate amplitude is 5sqrt(10)/16. The actual output t=N(1-x_3)-1 adds the factor exp(-m_z)=4. Equivalently its seven factorial shifts are 0,-1,0,0,-1,-1,+1 in the displayed numerator/denominator order of the exact Newton coefficient mu_(N;i,j,t)=s_(i+j)s_t /[s_i s_j s_(t-i)s_(t-j)s_(i+j-t)]. Thus b(a,a,a,0)=(sqrt(10)/8)^3 (5sqrt(10)/16) 4=125/512, a_(h^3)(0)=(2pi)^(3/2)b/sqrt(det A)=sqrt(2)/64. (16) Omitting D=N-1's shift would give a leading amplitude four times too small. This makes the shift convention in (2),(5) testable. The phase is F_0=3g(a)+m(a,a,1-a)=2v_8/pi, using the already proved [whole three-leaf seed evaluation](actual_positive_conway_variational_limit.md). Hence the theorem above and the positive-core comparison give Z_(h^3,N)=(sqrt(2)/64)N^(3/2)exp(2Nv_8/pi)(1+O(N^-1)). (17) The audit derives the gradient, Hessian, determinant and amplitude from the individual signed factorial arguments using exact rational and radical arithmetic. It also evaluates the original positive sum sum_(0<=i,j,k<=M; i+j+k>=D) a_(N,i)a_(N,j)a_(N,k) mu_(N;i,j,D-k). For N=5,8,20,40,80 its ratios to the leading term of (17) are 1.44279, 1.26530, 1.10276, 1.05067 and 1.02515. Additional levels 21,41,81 check the odd sequence. These finite values are diagnostics of the independently proved normalization, not an extrapolation argument for (17) or the complex-window theorem. Audit: [exact calibration and finite positive sums](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_complex_window_laplace.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_conway_complex_window_laplace_results.json). Independent internal analytical review: the source-transport agent checked the full lattice count, integer-offset amplitude, tensor cotangent orientations and errors, complex saddle deformation, and positive-core comparison, and reported PASS. The root agent separately reviewed the full proof and derived the calibration (15)--(17); the present exact audit independently reproduces its constants. These proof reviews do not replace the separate source-algebra or alias audits. Primary-agent full analytical review and fresh calibration audit: PASS. The review checked the primitive integer coordinates, D=N-1 offset factors, finite tensor-cotangent contours and all boundary/mode gaps, uniform complex Gaussian remainder, and the exact H3 prefactor. title: Full-twist fillings of the positive Conway class remain links
text: # Full-twist fillings of the positive Conway class remain links 29 October 2026. The robust positive Conway grammar cannot produce knots by filling all its auxiliary circles with the existing integral FULL-TWIST kernel. If a compiled expression contains S occurrences of its seed A=h^3, every such filled diagram has at least 2S+1 main components. In particular the smallest seed still has at least three. This is a literal connectivity obstruction, independent of any asymptotic estimate or geometric deformation. It does not contradict the complete retained-circle volume theorem. It prevents presenting a future filling theorem for this unchanged class as a knot theorem. ## 1. The two internal circles in every seed The original unrotated complete circle L_N threads two through main arcs, with identity endpoint pairing. The genuine quarter-turn h=Rturn L_N has the planar U pairing: its two bottom main ports are joined to one another, as are its two top main ports. Stacking two U boxes creates one closed internal main component between the upper cap of the lower box and the lower cup of the upper box. It leaves U pairing on the four external ports. Therefore A=h^3 has exactly TWO closed internal main components and U external pairing. This is an actual tangle calculation, not a decomposition into quantum channels. A quarter-turn rotates a tangle and preserves all its already closed components. Stacking two tangles also preserves every closed component in each: identity wires are attached only to their exposed ports, so they cannot connect an existing closed component to another one. A stack can create additional closed components, but cannot destroy those present before it. Induction on E ::= A | Rturn E | E E consequently gives internal main components of E >= 2S(E), where S(A)=1, S(Rturn E)=S(E), and S(EF)=S(E)+S(F). Closing the four exposed ports adds at least one further main component. Hence every actual closed expression has c_main(E) >= 2S(E)+1. (1) Both cylindrical and cap closures satisfy this lower bound. All 3S(E) auxiliary components are counted separately. ## 2. The exact filling kernel preserves that connectivity The original auxiliary-color filling identity replaces a retained complete circle by the literal full twist R^(-2p), with p an integer, and its separately recorded scalar. A full twist has the IDENTITY permutation of its two main endpoints for every sign and magnitude of p, including p=0. Thus the replacement has the same main pairing as the original unrotated L_N. After the same physical quarter-turn, each replaced leaf has the same U pairing as h. All subsequent identity stacks, rotations and closures therefore have exactly the SAME main-component connectivity as the unfilled expression. In particular every one of the seed's two internal main circles persists after these fillings. If I is any subset of the auxiliary circles, the filled link has c_total(E,I)=c_main(E)+3S(E)-|I|, c_total(E,I) >= 5S(E)+1-|I|. (2) Filling every auxiliary component gives c_total=c_main>=2S+1>1. The threshold "sufficiently long" does not change this conclusion. Neither a sign choice nor arbitrarily large full-twist powers can change an even braid permutation into an odd one. ## 3. What a knot extension actually requires To reach knots one must change the original source topology, for example by retaining an ODD half-twist coupon at selected auxiliary ports before performing the full-twist fillings, or by using another seed whose exposed main connections can join these components. Such a change has its own exact quantum source. The present positive Newton coefficients and whole-source theorem cannot silently be reused after changing those coupons. The existing odd-pretzel knot construction does retain the required odd half twists, which is why its connectivity differs from the pure h grammar here. Volume invariance of an unmarked complete half-twist partner does not identify its finite quantum source or prove its long-filled asymptotic. The general complete Conway construction and any verified full-twist extension of it therefore provide a broad LINK theorem. A broad KNOT theorem remains a separate critical-path task. Audit: [literal pairings and full-twist permutation checks](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_full_filling_component_obstruction.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_conway_full_filling_component_obstruction_results.json). The proof of (1)--(2) is the all-expression component-preservation induction, not an extrapolation from the finite samples. Primary-agent analytical review checked the two permanent internal main circles in every seed, their preservation under turns/stacks, and the identity permutation of every full-twist filling. The resulting link-only scope is independent of source asymptotics.

title: Complete half-twist partners and a general knot-connectivity construction
status: Complete partners and constructive knot patterns
text: # Complete half-twist partners and a general knot-connectivity construction 29 October 2026. Every fixed half-twist pattern on the leaves of a retained robust Conway factor has an actual complete hyperbolic augmented-link complement, with the SAME volume as its pure partner. This follows from explicit changed face pairings of the already proved polyhedron, including their pointwise edge words and complete cusp links. No unmarked half-twist invariance theorem is imported. Moreover EVERY robust expression has a constructible half-twist pattern whose main strands form ONE component, before or after any integral full-twist fillings. Thus the grammar has genuine arbitrarily branching knot candidates. The required odd-source mixed-color estimates and marked DEFORMED geometry remain separate from the complete theorem here. ## 1. The actual local cut after one half twist Use the original closed bowtie cut and its labels S0=(O,C1,C2), S1=(O,C3,C0). Superscripts + and - distinguish the two projection balls. Without a half twist the shaded gluing stays within each ball, fixing O and matching C1 to C0, C2 to C3. The white faces pair the two balls by their original projection labels. To insert a literal half twist, cut at that leaf's original twice- punctured crossing disk and rotate one side through +pi or -pi around its normal. In coordinates on the disk this is (y,z)->(-y,-z), with the projection line z=0 and the two punctures at y=+a,-a. It exchanges the punctures AND the upper and lower half disks. Consequently the new shaded pairings are S0+ -> S1-: O+->O-, C1+->C3-, C2+->C0-, S1+ -> S0-: O+->O-, C3+->C1-, C0+->C2-. (1) The reverse pairings are their inverses. The white maps are unchanged. These are maps across copies; making the same puncture swap within one copy would give the wrong boundary orientation. This is a literal reversible local cut of the original odd leaf T(R^epsilon L_N), epsilon=+1 or -1. Quarter-turning its one-crossing main tangle gives the opposite pairing (0,2),(1,3), exactly as (1). All original turns and identity strips outside this disk remain in place. The closed bowtie proof therefore identifies the resulting face quotient with the actual half-twist partner exterior. The two signs have the same boundary half-rotation and hence the same unmarked face pairing. Their collar paths differ by a full twist, which changes the primitive crossing-circle meridian by one disk longitude. Complete volume does not depend on this marking, but a future filling equation must keep the chosen sign and collar path. ## 2. Exact odd edge holonomy Keep the complete stationary polyhedron of the pure source. At this leaf set E=exp(2pi i x), 0<x<1/2, and normalize its ordered port to Q=(0,infinity,1,R), R=(1+E)^2/(4E), O+=(1+E)/2, O-=(1+E)/(2E). The four actual white/completion maps are the matrices W0,...,W3 in [the marked pure-deformation proof](actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md), equation (8). At the COMPLETE point the cross-half map in the first line of (1) is T=[[R,-R],[1,ER-1-E]]. (2) It sends infinity to R, 1 to 0 and O+ to O-. The second map is T'=bar(T)^(-1), where bar(E)=E^-1 and bar(R)=R. Direct multiplication gives all three pointwise odd edge words: W0^(-1) T' W2^(-1) T = identity, W2^(-1) T' W0^(-1) T = identity, W1^(-1) T' W3^(-1) T = identity. (3) The first two are the two pairs of bowtie sides incident to O; the third is the CAP-base pair. The reverse edge words are their inverses. Each word visits four distinct copies of an edge. Each corner still has dihedral angle pi/2, so its total is 2pi. Equation (3) additionally rules out translation or dilation along that edge; the angle count alone would not suffice. Every edge belongs to one leaf bowtie. An arbitrary mixture of even and odd leaves therefore uses the already checked pure edge word or one of (3), independently at that leaf. All white/white auxiliary seams remain the original pointwise identities. This proves every edge relation for an arbitrary fixed pattern, not just one isolated half-twist example. ## 3. Complete cusps and unchanged actual volume Use the complete right-angled polyhedron's canonical horosphere decoration: at each ideal vertex scale its rectangular link so that both opposite shaded sides have length one. They have equal length because they are opposite sides of a rectangle. The same decoration is placed in the other copy. Every ideal shaded triangle then has the same length-one horocycle at each of its three corners. Both the original shaded maps and the changed cross-half maps (1) preserve these horocycles, including their corner permutation. White maps preserve the copied rectangular links. Hence the new cusp links are finite Euclidean rectangle gluings without a dilation defect. Their corner angles sum to 2pi by the four-edge cycles. The literal link-exterior topology makes each connected link a torus. They give complete flat cusp tori and complete horoball ends after a uniform shrink. All finite points are smooth by (3). Thus the quotient of the two original polyhedra is the complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the ACTUAL half-twist partner. Its oriented volume is exactly twice the unchanged polyhedron volume: Vol(S^3 minus L_E^epsilon) =2 Vol(P_E)=2pi phi_E(0). (4) Combined with the independently proved whole complete odd-source asymptotic in [the original Newton transport theorem](actual_odd_conway_newton_transport.md), this identifies its full-sequence exponential rate with the actual half-twist partner volume, for every fixed ±/0 pattern. This is a COMPLETE statement. The mixed pure-cell construction with opposite apex flags cannot be reused unchanged in (1): the odd cross-half equations and the correct meridian marking must be solved for the odd source's own deformed action. ## 4. The two primitive half-twist markings The complete crossing-circle cusp can also be computed directly. In its original local upper-half-space coordinate, (C0,C1,C2,C3)=(1,E,-1,-E), O=infinity. The lower and upper white maps to the reflected copy are B0(z)=-z/E+(E+1)/E, B2(z)=-z/E-(E+1)/E. The two cross-half shaded maps in (1) are T0(z)=-z/E+(E-1)/E, T1(z)=-z/E-(E-1)/E. (5) The disk-framed longitude still crosses the bottom white face and returns through the top, giving lambda=B2^(-1)B0=-2(E+1). The two signed meridian collar paths give translations mu_+=-2, mu_-=2E, mu_+-mu_-=lambda. (6) For example the elementary shaded/white paths B0^(-1)T0 and B0^(-1)T1 translate by 2 and 2E; reversing the first gives mu_+. Which collar is called + is the geometric positive-diagonal convention. Identifying it with the chosen quantum R or R^-1 requires retaining that braid convention; it is not inferred from the unmarked metric. Put c=cot(pi x)>0. Relative to the pure meridian mu_0=E-1, mu_+=mu_0+lambda/2, mu_-=mu_0-lambda/2, tau_+=lambda/mu_+=2ic/(1+ic)=1+E, tau_-=lambda/mu_-=2ic/(1-ic)=-1-E^-1. (7) These relations compare Euclidean translation vectors; lambda/2 alone need not be a loop of either cusp lattice. Each pair (mu_+,lambda) or (mu_-,lambda) has area 4 sin(2pi x), exactly the total area of the two original rectangles, so each is a primitive peripheral basis. This checks the complete marking rather than merely the isometry type of an unmarked cusp. ## 5. Literal main connectivity Ignore auxiliary circles only for counting the main components. For the four ports (bottom-left,bottom-right,top-right,top-left) write I=(0,3)(1,2), U=(0,1)(2,3), X=(0,2)(1,3). A pure leaf has pairing U. An odd leaf has pairing X by (1). A turn swaps I and U and fixes X. The literal stack table is | lower / upper | I | U | X | |---|---|---|---| | I | I | U | X | | U | U | U plus one internal circle | U | | X | X | U | I | This is obtained just by following the original two identity wires. The ONLY operation creating a new internal main circle is U times U. Once an internal component exists later operations cannot remove it. The cylindrical closure of I has two components; those of U and X have exactly one. At a robust seed h^3 choose either: * all three leaves odd: its pairing is X, with no internal circle; * exactly one leaf pure and the other two odd: its pairing is U, with no internal circle. Thus the seed can realize the set C={U,X} without loops. A turn permutes the three pairing types. To see that arbitrary branching never destroys the needed choices, put A={I,U}, B={I,X}, C={U,X}, D={I,U,X}. When the forbidden loop-creating choice U times U is excluded, the products of the three two-element sets are | lower / upper | A | B | C | |---|---|---|---| | A | A | D | C | | B | D | B | D | | C | C | D | A | In particular at least two feasible pairing types survive every product. The statement remains true if a child already offers D. Induction proves that EVERY robust expression offers at least two types with no internal main circles. At least one is U or X. Choose that root type and backtrack the finite choices in the table: its cylindrical closure has one main component. This is a linear-time constructive parity prescription for arbitrary fixed branching and turn depth. One may choose either sign on every odd leaf; only parity affects connectivity. Subsequent full twists have even endpoint permutation and preserve it. Therefore after filling ALL auxiliary circles by any integral full-twist parameters, the resulting diagram is a KNOT in S^3. With some auxiliary circles retained it has one main component and those auxiliary components. The complete augmented partner is hyperbolic by sections 1--3. The odd mixed source estimates and the correctly marked deformed branch are separate inputs. They are now supplied in the [long-filled knot and link assembly](actual_odd_conway_long_filling_volume.md) for C(FG) with robust children. That mixed-color filling theorem continues to exclude C(A), although the complete theorem here covers it. Audit: [exact odd edge words, cusp paths and constructive knot patterns](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_half_twist_partner_geometry.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_conway_half_twist_partner_geometry_results.json). PASS for all three generic odd edge words, both primitive diagonal markings and their two-rectangle areas, all nine products of pairing sets, 69 literal expression witnesses and 483 signed full-twist checks. Independent internal review: the local-cell/source agent read the full actual half-disk cut, all three pointwise edge words, the complete rectangle decoration and primitive collar markings, and reported PASS. Its independent fresh audit replay also passed. Primary-agent review and fresh symbolic/topological audit: PASS. The closed half-disk cut, cross-copy orientation, complete cusp decoration, primitive marking areas, matching-set induction and preservation under full twists were checked. Complete geometry alone is not used to claim a filled quantum theorem.

title: Long-full-twist volume equality for every retained robust Conway factor
text: # Long-full-twist volume equality for every retained robust Conway factor 29 October 2026. The complete quantum hypotheses of the general long-filling transfer theorem now hold for EVERY retained cylindrical robust Conway factor. This gives a full original-source limit after independently sufficiently long fixed signed integral full twists, with a nonzero leading coefficient and both level parities retained. Its rate is the ACTUAL hyperbolic volume of the correctly marked filled link complement. The [marked deformation theorem](actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md) constructs the required representation and fixes its absolute regulator. These pure robust sources remain LINKS after the indicated fillings; they do not give a new knot family. ## 1. Exact scope and source normalization Let C(E) be C(A), A=h^3, or C(FG) with F,G robust expressions generated by A, the actual quarter-turn and actual product. Fix the entire compiled diagram, its retained auxiliary circles and original mark. Choose a subset I of the auxiliary circles. At each i in I substitute the ORIGINAL full twist R^(-2p_i) through its exact Fourier--Hermite auxiliary-color kernel. Unfilled colors stay at their complete value; they are not assigned p_i=0. Let K_(E,N)(p) denote this actual scalar with its separately recorded original enhancement/framing factor chi_N, where log|chi_N|=o(N) and chi_N is nonzero. The result applies first to the literal raw one-cut source and then to any stated normalization with this property. No new normalization depending on the unknown completed invariant is introduced. The principal analytic inputs are now proved: * The [mixed-leaf identity](actual_pure_conway_auxiliary_color_leaf.md) retains the full repeated-root algebra, positive core and signed square-zero radical. * The [uniform whole-source gap](actual_conway_uniform_mixed_source_gap.md) bounds every propagated alias and the ENTIRE complementary physical color cube after arbitrary finite turns and branching. * The [finite complex packet](actual_conway_complex_window_laplace.md) has a uniform, separately-even, nonzero asymptotic on a fixed complex neighborhood, with its actual integer lattice and D=N-1 offsets. These facts supply hypotheses (2)--(5) of the [general original-source transfer theorem](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md). Its already proved exact contour and charge argument therefore applies. No source assumption is inferred merely from geometric existence. ## 2. The actual packet and its selected action Use chi_i=(N-j_i)/N for each chosen auxiliary color. Let y denote the free wire coordinates of the reduced strict source problem. Define f_E(y,chi)=sum_leaves g_(chi_l)(x_l(y)) +sum_retained_products m(x,y,z), g_chi(x)=J(2x)-2J(x)-J(x-chi)-J(x+chi), J(x)=integral_0^x Log(2sin(pi t))dt, (1) where chi_l=0 for unfilled circles, the source marks are continued from the positive complete chamber, and all true product/turn relations remain in the affine wire maps. There is a unique holomorphic critical branch y_*(chi) near the strict complete optimizer. Put phi(chi)=f_E(y_*(chi),chi). (2) The exact finite packet has asymptotic N^(3/2) a_E(chi) exp[N phi(chi)](1+O(N^-1)), with a_E nonzero and a_E(0)>0, uniformly in a fixed complex polydisk. Both phi and a_E are separately even. If x_(i,*) is the complete maximizing leaf label, then phi(0)=max V_E/pi, phi''(0)=-2pi diag(cot(pi x_(i,*))). (3) Thus the transfer theorem's parameters are tau_packet,i=i cot(pi x_(i,*)), with positive imaginary part. They are HALF the actual complete geometric cusp ratios tau_geom,i=2i cot(pi x_(i,*)); this factor is required by the recorded full-twist/peripheral convention. ## 3. The unconditional original-source limit For independently sufficiently large fixed signed integers p_i, let chi_*(p) be the unique small solution of partial_i phi(chi)+(pi i/p_i)(chi_i-1)=0 for i in I. (4) Existence and uniqueness follow by the implicit-function theorem in the small independent parameters 1/p_i. Define S_p(chi)=phi(chi)+(pi i/2)sum_(i in I)(chi_i-1)^2/p_i. (5) Then the FULL original invariant has a nonzero asymptotic of the form K_(E,N)(p)=chi_N kappa^(-sum_i p_i) N^(3/2) D_E(p) exp[N S_p(chi_*(p))](1+O_p(N^-1)), D_E(p)!=0, (6) with the explicit retained unit Cartan/framing factors of the transfer theorem. In the pure positive mixed-circle chart its packet phase eta_N is one. In particular lim_N (2pi/N)log|K_(E,N)(p)| =2pi Re S_p(chi_*(p)). (7) To check (4)--(5) directly against the transfer conventions, its Fourier critical equations are partial_i phi(chi)+2pi i z_i=0, chi_i-2p_i z_i=1. Thus z_i=(chi_i-1)/(2p_i); substituting into phi(chi)+2pi i chi.z-2pi i sum(p_i z_i^2+z_i) gives exactly (5). The nonzero prefactor and the addition of the minimal signed charge sectors are those proved in the transfer theorem, not an inference from a positive real maximum before filling. All ordinary auxiliary colors, projective normals, paired endpoints and nonminimal Fourier charges are accounted for by that theorem and the whole-source gap. There is no prime-level, odd-level, equal-slope or same-sign restriction. The number of circles and every slope are fixed before N tends to infinity. ## 4. The actual filled hyperbolic volume At zero inverse slope the source anchor is 2pi phi(0)=2max V_E=Vol(S^3 minus L_E), (8) by the complete geometry and its [corrected closed projection cut](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md). The source rate in (7) tends to this actual complete volume as all |p_i| tend to infinity. For example its quadratic decrease is 2pi Re S_p(chi_*) =2pi phi(0)-sum_i pi^2/[2p_i^2 cot(pi x_(i,*))] +O(||p^(-1)||^3). (9) This follows by inserting chi_*,i=-i/[2p_i cot(pi x_(i,*))]+O(||p^(-1)||^2) in (5). Its geometric interpretation uses the full marked construction below, not merely agreement with the complete cusp Hessian. The [marked deformation proof](actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md) now supplies an actual bounded framed representation near the complete one, with the ORIGINAL peripheral marking and full action differential. Here U,V are logarithms of projective similarity multipliers, equivalently squared SL(2,C) peripheral eigenvalues: G=2pi i phi+recorded real constant, U_i=-2pi i chi_i, V_i=-2 partial_i phi. (10) All white and shaded edge words are pointwise identities, every main cusp stays parabolic, and the auxiliary paths are the primitive disk meridian and longitude. With the complete regulator anchor, (4) gives U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i exactly. Unfilled auxiliary cusps also remain parabolic. The existing general geometric completion theorem therefore applies, and the absolute regulator identity proves lim_N (2pi/N)log|K_(E,N)(p)|=Vol(S^3 minus L_E(p)). (11) This uses the actual group representation and every peripheral mark; it does not infer geometry just from matching open-port cross ratios. ## 5. These fillings do not produce knots If E contains S robust seeds, it already contains at least 2S internal main circles. Closing its exposed strands adds at least one more. Full twists have even endpoint permutation and preserve these components. The [literal component theorem](actual_conway_full_filling_component_obstruction.md) therefore gives at least 2S+1 main components after filling every auxiliary circle. Consequently (11) is a broad actual LINK volume equality, with arbitrary fixed branching and turn depth. A new knot theorem needs different source connectivity, such as suitable retained odd half-twist coupons, with its own phase and source estimates. The filled-volume identification does not remove that requirement. Independent internal analytical review checked the exact filling substitutions, all source hypotheses, the lattice and framing normalization, critical equations, quadratic rate expansion, and the distinction between packet and primitive cusp ratios. The subsequent marked deformation supplies the actual geometric interface used in the final theorem. Completion of the geometric interface: both independent agents and the primary agent reviewed the actual marked deformation proof and replayed its exact rational-function audit. The resulting representation, primitive unit filling equation, and absolute regulator establish (11); the original quantum proof (1)--(7) is unchanged. The later [signed half-twist extension](actual_odd_conway_long_filling_volume.md) changes the original leaf connectivity and proves its separately selected source and peripheral geometry. For C(FG) with robust children it gives long-filled knot and link families at arbitrary fixed diagram branching and turn depth. The pure component obstruction in section 5 remains unchanged.

title: The actual marked deformation of every retained Conway factor

text: # The actual marked deformation of every retained Conway factor 29 October 2026. This constructs an actual framed representation of the original closed link exterior for the mixed-circle critical source. All face-pairing relations hold as PSL(2,C) identities, including the white seams and the full four-step shaded-edge holonomies. The primitive crossing-circle logarithms are U_i=-2pi i t_i, V_i=-2 partial_i phi(t). Thus the existing source filling saddle is the actual marked filling equation. The conclusion concerns the broad robust LINK class. Even full-twist fillings of these pure sources do not produce knots. The proof uses the [actual closed bowtie cut](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md). An open metric quadrilateral is an auxiliary chart, not an asserted physical four-punctured boundary. No representation is inferred merely from matching quadrilateral metrics. ## 1. The analytic branch to be represented Fix a retained cylindrical factor C(A), A=h^3, or C(FG), where F,G belong to the robust turn/product grammar. Delete its final forced-flat product and retain the exact relation between the two final wire labels. For its free wire coordinates y and independent auxiliary parameters t_i write the ORIGINAL mixed-core action f(y,t)=sum_i g(x_i(y),t_i)+sum_products m(x,y,z), g(x,t)=J(2x)-2J(x)-J(x-t)-J(x+t), J(a)=integral_0^a Log(2sin(pi u))du. (1) The logarithms are continued from the strict complete positive chamber. The complete wire Hessian is negative definite. Hence there is one holomorphic critical branch y_*(t) near zero, and phi(t)=f(y_*(t),t). (2) Uniqueness and the separate evenness of (1) imply that every wire label and phi are separately even in all t_i. For small real t, all cell angles used below remain strict. Stationarity still says that ordered quadrilateral metrics match under the original stack corner maps. ## 2. The mixed leaf and its two actual flags Put E=exp(2pi i x), H=exp(2pi i t). A mixed leaf is the ideal pyramid with apex infinity and cyclic base C0=1, C1=E/H, C2=-1/H, C3=-E. (3) The consecutive half-arc lengths of its unit-circle base are (x-t, 1/2-x, x+t, 1/2-x). Triangulating the base gives volume pi g(x,t). Indeed the intermediate diagonal angles cancel, and J(2x)-2J(x)=-2J(1/2-x). Its ordered base cross ratio is kappa=sin(pi(x-t))sin(pi(x+t))/cos(pi x)^2 =exp(-partial_x g). (4) Normalize its ordered base to (0,infinity,1,R), where R=1/(1+kappa)=cos(pi x)^2/cos(pi t)^2 =H(1+E)^2/[E(1+H)^2]. (5) In this chart the plus-t apex is zeta_+=(1+E)/(1+H). The minus-t leaf has the SAME ordered base metric and its normalized apex is zeta_-=H zeta_+. These are the two roots of zeta^2-(1+E)zeta+ER=0. (6) For the second projection ball use the reflected MINUS-t cell, not the reflection of the plus-t cell. Its apex is zeta_+/E. Its main segment vertices remain the same real ordered base vertices. In the actual bowtie cut the shaded map takes (O,C1,C2) to (O,C0,C3). In the normalized chart its projective matrix is S=[[0,-ER],[1,-1-E]]. (7) It fixes both roots in (6). This follows by substitution, rather than by naming an unmarked eigenvalue of the Newton boundary relation. ## 3. Four universal boundary transport matrices For an ordered auxiliary port Q=(0,infinity,1,R) of wire label b, put E=exp(2pi i b). The following matrices send a plus chart to its reflected minus chart: W0=[[1,0],[0,E]], W1=[[1,E-1],[0,E]], W2=[[E-R,R(1-E)],[E-1,1-ER]], W3=[[R,0],[1-E,ER]]. (8) Wj fixes the two endpoints of port edge j,j+1. All equalities between matrices below are projective. The FREE edges are 01 and 23; CAP edges are 12 and 30. For the mixed leaf, W0 and W2 are its ACTUAL white triangle maps: they fix the relevant two main vertices and send zeta_+ to zeta_+/E. For W2 the last assertion follows from (6). The matrices W1,W3 are completion-plane maps: at a leaf they describe the white pieces attached on the other side of its shaded CAP edges, not extra leaf white faces. One useful geometric description of (8) is that Wj followed by complex conjugation is reflection in a plane through the corresponding port edge. Its angle with the port plane is pi b on FREE edges and pi(1-b) on CAP edges, with the side fixed by the ordered chart. These are virtual planes for the mixed leaf; its actual white planes need not be their fixed planes. Equation (8), rather than an assumption of planarity of the deformed white polygons, is the transport data. ### The product identities Use the literal prism coordinates and child maps from [the local-cell proof](actual_newton_ideal_prism_and_associativity.md): lower Q=(v0,v1,P,infinity), upper Q=(infinity,P,v2,v3), output Q=(v0,v1,v2,v3). (9) The white prism triangles are T_top=(P,v1,v2) and T_bottom=(infinity,v0,v3). Call their actual maps to their reflected copies B_top,B_bottom. Transport each set of matrices (8) to the common prism coordinate. Then direct substitution gives ALL the needed identities: W_lower,1=W_upper,1=W_output,1=B_top, W_lower,3=W_upper,3=W_output,3=B_bottom, W_lower,2=W_upper,0, W_output,0=W_lower,0, W_output,2=W_upper,2. (10) Here the three E parameters are exp(2pi i x), exp(2pi i y), exp(2pi i z), and each R is the actual ordered-port value. These identities can also be checked by the plane description: the CAP/input angles complement each other; the common two-input FREE seam has angle w+x+y=1; the two output FREE angles are p+x=z and q+y=z. The maps are equal on entire planes, including their translations, since their ordered edge endpoints and reflection planes agree. No mere equality of absolute cross ratios is used. For a wholly algebraic check of (10), put A=exp(2pi i p), B=exp(2pi i r), C=exp(2pi i q). The prism coordinates are v0=1, v1=A, v2=AB, v3=ABC, P=1+A-A[AB(1+C)-1-A]/[A^2 B^2 C-A], (11) and the three E parameters are BC, AB, ABC. Conjugation replaces A,B,C by their reciprocals. If T sends an ordered port to (0,infinity,1,R), its world-coordinate matrix is bar(T)^(-1) Wj T. Inserting (11) gives (10) by cancellation of rational functions. The accompanying audit checks these identities symbolically with independent indeterminates A,B,C. ### Turns and final cylindrical closure A turn replaces E by E^-1, R by 1-R. The coordinate change is T(z)=(R-1)/(z-1), and exact substitution in (8) gives T W_(j+1)(E,R)=W_j(E^-1,1-R) T. (12) For the final ordered gluing j->3-j the two wire labels add to one and their kappas are equal. The normalized coordinate change is C(z)=(z-R)/(z-1), and C W_j(E^-1,R)=W_(2-j)(E,R) C. (13) Thus every original turn and the actual cylindrical closing map retain the complete transport matrices, not only their port metrics. ## 4. All original white face maps exist Build both halves using the prescribed metric quad maps. For real t, the plus and minus source wire values are equal. Every prism is therefore the same before reflection, and all corresponding main vertices have the same normalized port coordinates. Only auxiliary apices select the opposite roots (6). Induct on the actual expression. At a leaf its two white triangle maps are W0,W2. At a product the CAP pieces already white in a nonleaf child match the attached prism maps by (10). If the child is a leaf, its CAP face is shaded and the prism supplies precisely its completion map W1 or W3. The two-input FREE seam matches by the middle identity in (10). The remaining boundary pieces have exactly the output maps in (8). Equations (12),(13) perform every turn and final closure. Consequently any two triangular pieces belonging to the SAME original white face have EXACTLY the same Mobius map. This statement continues through all the white/white seams, including those whose deformed pieces are no longer coplanar. Their two-step edge holonomy is the identity. The original closed bowtie ribbon graph fixes which pieces belong to each white face; no open-port topology is being assumed. ## 5. Shaded edge relations and actual representations Write bar(S) for (7) with E replaced by E^-1; R is unchanged. Direct matrix multiplication gives W0 S=bar(S) W0, W2 S=bar(S) W2, W3 S=bar(S) W1. (14) The first two equations are the two pairs of bowtie sides incident to O. The last equation is its CAP-base pair. They are precisely the four-step edge words: shaded in the first half, white to the second, inverse shaded there, and inverse white back. Every such word is POINTWISE the identity in PSL(2,C), including any possible dilation or translation along its ideal edge. The [closed cut](actual_conway_bowtie_projection_cut.md) supplies two actual topological balls and the labeled white/shaded gluings. Choose one of the face transitions to join their frames. The remaining face transitions generate the fundamental group; its edge relations are exactly the two-step white seams and four-step bowtie words just proved. Equivalently subdivide the balls and their faces and use the standard dual two-skeleton presentation, whose two-cells are these edge words. Thus these matrices define an ACTUAL representation of the original link group. This argument does not need the deformed half-ball image to remain an embedded convex polyhedron. At t=0 the construction is the proved complete geometric holonomy. The finitely many face matrices and cusp flags vary analytically and stay in a bounded framed neighborhood of it. Extend to complex t by holomorphic continuation: the second half means the Schwarz-reflected minus branch, with conjugated coordinate coefficients, rather than antiholomorphic dependence on t. Every identity above is holomorphic and holds for small real independent t, hence on a complex polydisk. ## 6. All main cusps remain parabolic At a main corner Cj the two original white sectors give its small meridian: cross one white face and return through the other. In its local port frame the resulting map is W_(j-1)^(-1) Wj, or its inverse according to the orientation. Both factors fix Cj. Their derivatives there are equal: at C0,C2 they are E^-1, and at C1,C3 they are E, using the finite local coordinate at infinity. Thus the multiplier of this actual meridian is one, IDENTICALLY in the deformation. The meridian is nonidentity at the complete point and remains so after shrinking the neighborhood. It is therefore parabolic. The actual longitude commutes with it, so it too is a translation in the common flag frame and has multiplier one. This proves parabolicity of the entire main peripheral groups, not only a trace equation at one flag. ## 7. Primitive auxiliary holonomies and their source derivatives Use the same primitive paths as at completeness in the closed-cut note. The crossing-circle meridian is the inverse shaded map. In the original leaf coordinate (3) it sends C3 to C2, C0 to C1 and fixes infinity: mu(z)=H^-1 z+(E-1)/H. Hence its small centered similarity log is exactly U=-Log H=-2pi i t. (15) The disk-framed longitude crosses the bottom white face and returns through the top. In the normalized chart it is W2^-1 W0, fixing zeta_+. Its multiplier in the flag-at-infinity coordinate is exp(V)=[(zeta_+-E)/(zeta_+-1)]^2 =[(1-EH)/(E-H)]^2 =[sin(pi(x+t))/sin(pi(x-t))]^2. (16) One can check the first equality directly: a Mobius map fixing a finite flag has flag-at-infinity multiplier reciprocal to its ordinary derivative there. Use (6) when differentiating W2^-1 W0. Continue the logarithm from V=0, obtaining V=2Log[sin(pi(x+t))/sin(pi(x-t))] =-2 partial_t g(x,t). (17) The paths are the primitive meridian and disk-framed longitude already calibrated by the two-rectangle complete cusp; no doubled longitude or unrecorded change of slope is inserted.
