Their continuations cannot change integral marking in a small connected neighborhood. Internal criticality and the envelope rule now give for every circle U_i=-2pi i t_i, V_i=-2 partial_i phi(t). (18) An unfilled auxiliary color has t_i=0. Separate evenness makes V_i=0 there as well, so it remains a complete parabolic cusp. In particular dV_i/dU_i at zero =2i cot(pi x_(i,*)), in agreement with the primitive complete lattice, while the packet parameter in phi_ii=2pi i tau_packet,i is half this ratio. ## 8. Algebraic marked peripheral equations This construction also supplies finite algebraic equations for the ACTUAL peripheral branch. Exponentiate every internal stationarity equation, retaining all port variables and excluding the strict denominators. The product cross ratios are rational functions of their angle phases, and (4) is rational in E,H. Include M_i=H_i^-1, L_i=[(1-E_i H_i)/(E_i-H_i)]^2. (19) Here M_i=exp(U_i), L_i=exp(V_i) are the centered PROJECTIVE similarity multipliers. An SL(2) eigenvalue convention takes their square roots on the local marked branch, retaining its original central signs. No SL(2) spin is silently identified with one in (19). Here M_i,L_i are the PSL(2,C) similarity multipliers, equivalently the squared SL(2,C) peripheral eigenvalues. An SL lift and its spin would need to be retained before changing to unsquared variables. All equations are over Q after choosing the finitely many phase variables clearing the rational wire coefficients. Select the branch through the complete positive solution and retain its actual marking. The nondegenerate internal Hessian gives the analytic branch already used above. Thus (19) is a marked gluing presentation of an actual peripheral representation branch. Elimination may introduce extra components or factors; no irreducibility or equality with an entire classical A-polynomial is asserted merely by eliminating variables. More precisely, near the selected complete point the exponentiated stationarity Jacobian in the internal wire phases is nonsingular: on its continued logarithmic sheet it is the invertible wire Hessian times invertible phase-coordinate factors. Hence this algebraic solution branch is locally etale over the auxiliary H coordinates. Its marked peripheral image is the analytic graph L=L(M) given by (19). Equation (20) below implies sum_i dU_i wedge dV_i=0, so this actual H-dimensional peripheral germ is Lagrangian. The source action is its calibrated local primitive, not a period attached to an unidentified algebraic curve. ## 9. Absolute regulator and actual long-filled volumes Put G=2pi i phi, with any explicitly recorded real action constant retained. Equation (18) gives the full differential dG=(1/2)sum_i V_i dU_i. (20) At zero the actual oriented fundamental-chain volume is Im G(0)=2pi phi(0)=Vol(S^3 minus L_E), by the complete cell theorem and the closed bowtie cut. This anchors the SAME oriented representation family, not a possibly unrelated Bloch cycle of equal regulator. For completeness, the marked fundamental-chain differential is dVol(rho)=(1/2)sum_i[Re V_i dIm U_i-Re U_i dIm V_i]. It follows by differentiating each ideal tetrahedron's Bloch--Wigner volume; internal face/edge terms cancel, and a primitive meridian and longitude on a boundary torus have the signed intersection pairing. With eigenlogs U/2,V/2 the boundary pairing is -2, giving precisely the factor 1/2 displayed here. Distinct tori have zero cross pairing. This is the diagram-independent marked-chain calculation proved in [the general regulator theorem](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md), section 6. Applying (20) and the complete anchor yields the ABSOLUTE identity on the connected small branch Vol(rho_t)=Im G(t)-(1/2)sum_i Re U_i Im V_i. (21) Now choose any subset of auxiliary circles and sufficiently long fixed signed integral full twists p_i. The actual original-source filling saddle is phi_i(t)+(pi i/p_i)(t_i-1)=0. By (18) this is exactly U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i, in the primitive disk marking. Unfilled main and auxiliary cusps stay parabolic. The actual nearby framed representation therefore satisfies every hypothesis of the general geometric completion theorem. It gives a smooth complete hyperbolic metric on the correctly marked filled link exterior. Using Re U_i=-p_i Re V_i at the saddle in (21) gives Vol(L_E(p))=2pi Re[phi(t)+(pi i/2) sum_i(t_i-1)^2/p_i]. (22) The already proved [whole original-source transfer](actual_conway_long_filling_source_limit.md) has exactly the right side of (22) as its full-sequence exponential rate. Hence it is the ACTUAL filled hyperbolic volume for every fixed retained robust factor and all independently sufficiently long signed integral fillings of any chosen subset. Its original normalization, normal terms, level parities and nonzero prefactor are those of that source theorem; geometry does not replace them with another state. This is a general branching LINK theorem. The [component obstruction](actual_conway_full_filling_component_obstruction.md) still gives at least 2S+1 main components for S robust seeds after all even full-twist fillings. A knot extension needs different connectivity and its separately checked quantum source, such as retained odd twists. Audit: [exact peripheral and transport matrices](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation_results.json). PASS for all nine generic prism identities over Q(A,B,C), all four turn identities, all four cylindrical closure identities, the three pointwise shaded-edge identities, and every main/auxiliary peripheral matrix check. No sampled phase values are used in this audit. Independent internal review: the coherent-source agent read the full closed-cut representation construction, main meridian topology, opposite-root/holomorphic continuation, primitive auxiliary logs, absolute regulator and filling sign, and reported PASS. Its independent replay of the exact symbolic audit also passed. The local-cell/source agent independently read the full proof and replayed the audit with PASS. It additionally recomputed the two white slopes in the original leaf coordinate and their longitude composition, recovering the complete translation -2(E+1) and the multiplier (16). Primary-agent full analytical review and fresh symbolic audit: PASS. The review checked ordered child-port metrics, plus/reflected-minus world frames, all prism/turn/closure and shaded-edge identities, the actual closed-cut group presentation, both main peripheral multipliers, primitive auxiliary paths, holomorphic continuation, and the boundary-corrected absolute regulator.

title: Every complete robust Conway leaf lies strictly above one quarter
text: # Every complete robust Conway leaf lies strictly above one quarter 29 October 2026. For every retained cylindrical robust factor, the unique complete source optimizer satisfies x_l>1/4 at EVERY h leaf. This follows from the actual g,m stationarity equations and a preserved port inequality. No circle-packing estimate is assumed. The result is about the existing positive complete source; replacement by a different quantum coupon still requires its own local and global source estimates. ## 1. Positive port variables from the actual source derivatives For a proper robust expression E at output b in (0,1), let f_E(b)=v_E(b)/pi be its strictly optimized source action. Put B=cot(pi b), kappa=exp(-f'_E(b)), X=sqrt((1+B^2)/(1+kappa)), Y=sqrt(kappa) X. (1) Thus X,Y are positive and X^2+Y^2-B^2=1. The already proved strict maximum theorem makes these derivatives legitimate at every proper macro-port of the complete optimizer. A literal turn sends (B,X,Y) -> (-B,Y,X). (2) At a product F G with strict input/output x,y,z, write U=cot(pi x), V=cot(pi y), Z=cot(pi z), and D=(U+V)Z-UV+1>0. The strict inequality x+y<1 gives U+V>0. Directly differentiating the SAME seven-factorial action m gives kappa_F=exp(m_x)=(U+V)(U-Z)/D, kappa_G=exp(m_y)=(U+V)(V-Z)/D, kappa_out=exp(-m_z)=(U-Z)(V-Z)/D. (3) Here the first two signs use f'_F=-m_x and f'_G=-m_y at the inner maximum. Since 1+kappa_F=(1+U^2)/D, 1+kappa_G=(1+V^2)/D, 1+kappa_out=(1+Z^2)/D, all THREE ports have the same X=sqrt(D), and Z=(UV+X^2-1)/(U+V), Y_out=Y_F Y_G/(U+V). (4) The positive square root in the last identity is fixed by U+V>0. These are exact algebraic consequences of stationarity, not new gluing assumptions. ## 2. A strict inequality preserved by the entire robust grammar Every proper robust port satisfies -Y < B < X. (5) First check A=h^3. At a leaf the actual action has g'(a)=2log cot(pi a). Therefore its coordinates are B=X=cot(pi a)>0, Y=1. The common-X identity (3) makes the three stationary seed leaf coordinates equal. Composing twice using (4) gives B_2=(2X^2-1)/(2X), Y_2=1/(2X), B_A=X(4X^2-3)/(4X^2-1), Y_A=1/(4X^2-1). (6) The second product has B_2+X>0, so X>1/2. Consequently X-B_A=2X/(4X^2-1)>0, B_A+Y_A=(2X-1)(X+1)/(2X+1)>0, which proves (5) for every interior seed output. Equation (2) preserves (5), because its two inequalities exchange. It remains to check a product of two ports satisfying (5). If the common X>=1, the identities Y_F^2=1+U^2-X^2 and U>-Y_F force U>0; similarly V>0. Also U<X, V<X and U>sqrt(X^2-1), V>sqrt(X^2-1). Hence 0<X-U<1 and 0<X-V<1 (also at X=1). Equation (4) gives Z>0 and Z-X=((X-U)(X-V)-1)/(U+V)<0. Thus -Y_out<Z<X. If 0<X<1, put h=sqrt(1-X^2), and write uniquely U=h cot alpha, Y_F=h csc alpha, V=h cot beta, Y_G=h csc beta, 0<alpha,beta<pi. With alpha_0=arccos X, the upper inequalities U<X,V<X say alpha,beta>alpha_0. The actual U+V>0 says alpha+beta<pi. Equation (4) is now exactly Z=h cot(alpha+beta), Y_out=h csc(alpha+beta). (7) Thus Z<X since alpha+beta>alpha_0, while Z>-Y_out follows from cot t+csc t=cot(t/2)>0 for 0<t<pi. This proves preservation of (5), and hence proves it for all robust expressions. ## 3. Closure and downward propagation For a retained factor C(FG), its two proper children F,G are robust. After deleting the final forced-flat gate, their outputs are b,1-b. Stationarity of f_F(b)+f_G(1-b) gives equal derivatives and therefore equal kappa. Their port data are consequently (B,X,Y) and (-B,X,Y). Applying (5) to both gives |B|<min(X,Y). Since X^2+Y^2-B^2=1, this implies 0<X<1, 0<Y<1 (8) at both root child ports. These two strict bounds propagate down the ROBUST macro-tree. They are preserved by a turn. At a product, X is common, hence already below one. Use (7). Its parent Y_out<1 means alpha_0<alpha+beta<pi-alpha_0. Each robust child already has alpha,beta>alpha_0 by (5), so each also lies below pi-alpha_0. Therefore sin alpha,sin beta>h, which gives Y_F,Y_G<1. Thus (8) holds at every robust seed port. STOP this propagation at A: its individual leaf ports have Y=1, so (8) is not asserted for those ports. Instead use (6): all three seed leaves share the seed's X. Since this X is strictly below one, cot(pi x_l)=X<1, hence x_l>1/4. (9) The remaining retained factor C(A) is equally explicit. Its two closing children are h^2 and h; their cotangents are opposite. The same root matching again makes X common. Thus B_2=-X in (6), forcing X=1/2 and x_l=atan(2)/pi>1/4 for all three leaves. This proves (9) for every retained cylindrical robust factor. For each FIXED expression there is a positive minimum margin above 1/4 because it has finitely many leaves. No uniform margin across all expressions is claimed or needed here. The theorem locates the whole positive-source optimizer in the strict local regime required by the proposed odd-half-twist packet. It does not itself identify that packet with the pure source or prove survival of its summed complex amplitude. Primary-agent independent analytical review: PASS. The product identities were derived directly using D=(U+V)Z-UV+1; the seed inequalities, both X>=1 and X<1 preservation cases, closure inequalities, macro-only downward propagation, and separate C(A) endpoint were checked. No uniform margin over all expressions or odd-coupon source theorem is inferred.

title: A uniform mixed-color source gap for arbitrary robust Conway expressions
text: # A uniform mixed-color source gap for arbitrary robust Conway expressions 29 October 2026. The positive complete-circle Conway source controls its ENTIRE original auxiliary-color packet. The signed radical contributions are uniformly exponentially smaller than the complete source, even after arbitrary finite branching and turns. For every retained cylindrical factor there is also a strict gap outside any fixed small complete-color corridor. These are whole-source estimates, not bounds on selected colors. The complex corridor packet and the marked geometric peripheral interpretation remain separate statements. No Newton output is declared to be a meridian. ## 1. Exact source and conclusions Use the original pure leaf h_j=Rturn(L_j), with actual auxiliary color 1<=j<=N. Put D=N-1, M=floor(D/2). The [mixed-leaf theorem](actual_pure_conway_auxiliary_color_leaf.md) gives h_j=C_j+R_j, C_(N-h)=sum_(v=h)^M N^2 s_(2v)/(s_v^2 s_(v-h)s_(v+h)) Bhat_v for 0<=h<=M, C_j=0 for j<=floor(N/2). (1) Every C_j has nonnegative Newton coefficients bounded coefficientwise by h_N. Every R_j lies in the square-zero nilradical J_N=span{Bhat_v:v>=ceil(N/2)}, J_N^2=0, (2) and each coefficient has absolute value at most N/2. These are identities in the full repeated-root algebra, including its original normal data. Let E be any fixed robust expression generated by A=h_N^3, actual turn, and product. Give every individual circle leaf an independent ordinary color j_l. Let A_(E,N)(j) be its ORIGINAL marked cylindrical scalar, C_(E,N)(j) the same circuit with each leaf replaced by C_j, and Z_(E,N)=A_(E,N)(N,...,N)>0. **Uniform radical-gap theorem.** There are gamma>0 and N_0 such that for all N>=N_0 and ALL physical auxiliary-color choices, |A_(E,N)(j)-C_(E,N)(j)|<=exp(-gamma N) Z_(E,N), 0<=C_(E,N)(j)<=Z_(E,N). (3) The analogous coefficientwise estimate holds for the OPEN operator at every output. It is preserved under further positive Conway composition, not only by the final closure. For a retained cylindrical factor C(A), or C(FG) with F,G robust, write F0=max A_E, where A_E=V_E/pi is the complete source action after removing only the forced flat final product gate. For every sufficiently small fixed delta>0 there is gamma_delta>0 such that, for large N, max_(some N-j_l>delta N) |A_(E,N)(j)| <=exp[N(F0-gamma_delta)]. (4) Both parities and composite levels are included. The expression and delta are fixed before N tends to infinity. The gaps are proved below; no numerical profile is used to infer their existence. ## 2. The two-leaf profile has its free maximum at output 1/2 Set J(x)=integral_0^x log(2sin(pi u))du, g(x)=J(2x)-4J(x), 0<=x<=1/2, m(x,y,z)=J(x+y)+J(z)-J(x)-J(y) -J(z-x)-J(z-y)-J(x+y-z). The product domain is max(x,y)<=z<=x+y<=1. The proved ideal-atom decompositions make g and m concave on their closed domains, with a negative definite Hessian on their effective interior variables. Define F2(t)=max [g(x)+g(y)+m(x,y,t)], 0<=t<=1, (5) with x,y<=1/2 and the product constraints retained. It is finite, continuous and concave on [0,1]. For 0<t<1 a strict feasible point is x=y in (t/2,min(t,1/2)). The nonvertex-flat inward barrier and negative Hessian give a unique strict optimizer and a strictly concave analytic profile on (0,1). Its free maximum occurs at t=1/2, x=y=a=(1/pi)atan(sqrt(2)). (6) Indeed, in the strict domain, exp(m_x)=sin(pi(x+y))sin(pi(z-x)) /[sin(pi x)sin(pi(x+y-z))], exp(m_z)=sin(pi z)sin(pi(x+y-z)) /[sin(pi(z-x))sin(pi(z-y))], g'(x)=2log cot(pi x). At (6), cos^2(pi a)=1/3, exp(m_x)=exp(m_y)=2, g'(a)=-log 2, and exp(m_z)=1. Thus all three derivatives vanish. Concavity and strictness prove the unique global maximum and hence F2'(t)>0 for 0<t<1/2. (7) ## 3. A radical leaf cannot maximize a three-leaf seed Let F3(b) be the complete h_N^3 coefficient profile, normalized as log(coefficient)/N. Exact positive associativity and its variational limit give F3(b)=max [F2(t)+g(y)+m(t,y,b)], (8) with 0<=y<=1/2. Every b in (0,1) has a unique strict optimizer. At b=1 the final gate is forced flat, but the three leaves and preceding gate are strict at the unique maximum. These are purely variational facts from the [boundary profile proof](actual_conway_boundary_volume_relation.md) and its cylindrical endpoint argument; no complement identification is needed here. An alias leaf has output y>=1/2 and polynomially bounded coefficient. Its relaxed envelope inside the three-leaf seed is G(b)=max [F2(t)+m(t,y,b)], y>=1/2, max(t,y)<=b<=t+y<=1, 1/2<=b<=1. (9) F3 and G are continuous on this closed interval. For G, convex combination of feasible states proves concavity; compactness gives upper semicontinuity and endpoint interpolation gives the opposite inequality. **Key claim: every maximum in (9) has y=1/2.** Take 1/2<b<1 and suppose a maximum had y>1/2. There is a strict feasible point with y>1/2: choose y in (1/2,b) and then t in (b-y,min(b,1-y)). Joining to it excludes every flat prism boundary by the nonvertex-flat inward volume barrier. At t=0, y=b and the atom (b,0,1-b) supplies the same barrier. F2 has no negative infinite inward derivative. Therefore the supposed maximum has a strict prism, 0<t<1-y<1/2, and stationarity gives m_y=0, F2'(t)+m_t=0. (10) The first equation yields exp(m_t)=sin(pi y)sin(pi(b-t)) /[sin(pi t)sin(pi(b-y))]>1. (11) The numerator minus the denominator is exactly sin(pi b)sin(pi(y-t))>0. Equations (7),(11) contradict the second equation in (10). This proves the claim for 1/2<b<1. At b=1/2 the constraint y<=b forces y=1/2. At b=1 the constraints force t+y=1, the last product action vanishes, and (7) makes F2(t) maximal at t=1/2, again giving y=1/2. Since g(1/2)=0, (9) is thus the restriction of the complete problem (8) to the boundary leaf y=1/2. The strictness and uniqueness in (8), including b=1, imply F3(b)>G(b) for every b in [1/2,1]. Consequently gamma_*=min_(1/2<=b<=1) [F3(b)-G(b)]>0. (12) This uses continuity and compactness, not finitely sampled outputs. ## 4. Uniform exact seed comparison Expand the ORIGINAL three-leaf seed: h_(j1)h_(j2)h_(j3) =C_(j1)C_(j2)C_(j3) +sum_(i=1)^3 R_(ji) product_(k!=i) C_(jk). (13) Terms with two aliases vanish EXACTLY by (2), including their normals. Commutativity of the actual pair algebra puts the remaining alias last inside this seed. No operator is moved through a turn or another box. By positivity the coefficientwise absolute value of each summand in (13) is bounded by the corresponding coefficient of (N/2) [sum_(v=ceil(N/2))^D Bhat_v] h_N^2. (14) It is zero at outputs r<ceil(N/2). For any sequence of remaining outputs r/D->b, endpoint-uniform factorial estimates and polynomial state counts give limsup_N (1/N)log coefficient_r(14)<=G(b). (15) To verify (15), select a largest summand and pass to convergent scaled indices. Their limits satisfy the closed constraints in (9), and the two complete leaves give (5). The alias has zero exponential cost. Replacing scale N by D changes the exponent by O(log N), also at sine zeros. This argument includes b=1/2 and b=1. For the complete seed coefficient a_(N,r), the exact-output boundary limit says, along EVERY such output sequence, (1/N)log a_(N,r)->F3(b). (16) This is the proved prescribed-output theorem, not an assumption that rounded real optimizers have the correct output. Compactness and (12),(15),(16) now imply, uniformly over all outputs and all colors, |mixed_seed_r-core_seed_r| <=exp(-gamma_* N/2) a_(N,r) (17) for sufficiently large N. Otherwise a sequence of failures would have a convergent output subsequence contradicting the strict gap (12). The factor three in (13) and polynomial factors are absorbed by halving the gap. Outputs below ceil(N/2) have identically zero error. ## 5. Arbitrary turns and branching preserve the gap Let S be the fixed number of seed occurrences. The actual turn permutes Newton coefficients; multiplication has nonnegative structure constants; the marked closure extracts one coefficient. Thus absolute coefficientwise inequalities propagate through every operation. Each seed is its nonnegative core plus an error bounded by epsilon_N times the complete seed, with epsilon_N=exp(-gamma_*N/2). Each core is itself bounded by the complete seed. Expanding multilinearly in seed errors, without moving a turn, bounds the error at every open output by [(1+epsilon_N)^S-1] times the complete coefficient. (18) This proves the open version of (3), and then its marked closure. Turns do not preserve the nilradical; the entire propagated radical was bounded, not removed by passing to a semisimple quotient. ## 6. The whole physical color complement has a strict gap For a retained cylindrical factor the reduced complete angle problem has a unique strict maximum x_*. Every leaf lies in (0,1/2), and every unforced prism is strict. The complete variational theorem gives log Z_(E,N)=NF0+o(N). If some j<=floor(N/2), the core circuit is zero and (3) proves (4). Otherwise put chi_l=(N-j_l)/N. For a leaf with output x>=chi, its core action is g_chi(x)=g(x)-Delta(x,chi), Delta(x,chi)=J(x-chi)+J(x+chi)-2J(x)>=0. (19) For 0<x<1/2 and 0<chi<=x, this loss is strictly positive. Differentiate in chi<x: partial_chi Delta =log[sin(pi(x+chi))/sin(pi(x-chi))]>0, and use continuity at chi=x. The loss may vanish at x=1/2, so the strict COMPLETE optimizer is essential. Take the compact joint domain of feasible complete states and parameters 0<=chi_l<=x_l with at least one chi_l>=delta. Its deformed action is at most F0. Equality would require x=x_* and every loss zero, impossible at the selected interior leaf with chi_l>=delta. Hence the maximum on this joint domain is F0-c_delta for some c_delta>0. Uniform factorial estimates and polynomial state counts bound the entire positive core outside the corridor by exp[N(F0-c_delta/2)] for large N. Combining this with (3) proves (4). All physical auxiliary colors, signed radical terms and original normal directions are covered. ## 7. Remaining steps toward a filled-knot equality These estimates apply to an arbitrarily branched fixed robust Conway source. The [general original-source filling theorem](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) additionally requires the specified finite holomorphic corridor packet with a uniform nonzero complex saddle asymptotic, and an actual marked peripheral representation whose regulator is its action. Neither is inferred just from the gap or from naming a boundary curve an A-polynomial. Audit: [finite source expansion and analytic identities](../experiments/audit_actual_conway_uniform_mixed_source_gap.py). Its checks supplement the analytic proof, not an extrapolation of exponential rates from finitely many levels. Independent internal analytical review by the cluster/source agent checked the free two-leaf critical point, the strict alias-boundary argument including both output endpoints, compactness of the exact- output seed comparison, arbitrary turn/product propagation, and the whole physical color-complement loss. A fresh independent replay of the audit passed all 4,347 full-polynomial mixed seeds and both symbolic stationary identities. No claim about a complex packet or peripheral representation was used in this review. The separate interfaces are now supplied by the [uniform complex packet](actual_conway_complex_window_laplace.md) and [actual marked deformation](actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md). Together they give the [full long-filling hyperbolic volume equality](actual_conway_long_filling_source_limit.md) for the retained robust link class.

title: Correlated neighboring bands of the original boundary source
status: Correlated adjacent-band errors and the normalized finite-clock quotient
text: # Correlated neighboring bands of the original boundary source 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. The exact ratio of two neighboring charged source products is rational in their actual clocks. On the original six-type resonant boundary chart, their root packet errors are correlated strongly enough to divide by the odd-source normalization of size N^-1. The resulting model is an explicit FINITE quotient. Its classical limit, a transverse Gaussian reduction, and its coefficient in the original period are not evaluated here. ## 1. One original product and one integral band path Use the labeled right-angled matching polyhedron, actual cut and original white-prefix dictionary of the [common chart](actual_original_network_resonant_boundary_chart.md). There is one main component. Let N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2. Fix the actual folded labels a_i, m_i=d-a_i and deficits s_i=d-2a_i. The number of original tensors is fixed. Initially one can require sum s_i<=S0, independently of N; the proof below is uniform also for 0<=s_i<=eta N, with a sufficiently small fixed eta. After the two ACTUAL cuts, use the primitive common head chart of the [charged-current theorem](actual_matching_graph_common_band_ward_current.md). The component charge conditions must hold. Fix its free coordinates and the two input heads at the common boundary assignment. Its three bands are restrictions of the SINGLE affine family h(delta)=h_N+delta v, (1) where v is the recorded integral charge path. Its entries are bounded independently of N. All original vertex equations, reversed dual heads and cup complements hold for complex delta. In particular delta=+1 and -1 are not independent head assignments or independently selected asymptotic branches. Their original physical supports remain different. Let S_N(delta) be the actual charged ROOT product s_delta of the common-band theorem: original whites, literal pi duals, the remaining cups/caps, turns and fixed root channel weights, before any internal head sum or exposed coherent functional. The ordinary scalar cap at the exposed cut has been REMOVED. Its replacement is the literal off-diagonal coherent row after the two bands are assembled. Keeping that old diagonal cap would annihilate a nonzero charged band. For all remaining local tensors we use the specified continuation in the [original source envelope](actual_original_network_resonant_source_envelope.md). This is not its closed charge-zero product S_F. In particular its charge-zero complementary mark/cap formula Xi_N is NOT used for delta=+/-1. The coherent binomial row is applied after this statement; its input head is fixed along (1), so its common factor can also be retained on both sides of the pointwise ratio. The hypothesis is on this actual source presentation: each numerator must be one of the original six types 200,002,220,022,202,222. Unspecified routed R or U factors can introduce 000 or 020. Their inclusion is NOT justified by the theorem, even if their contracted root channel has the same scalar. No off-grid equality between such presentations is assumed. Take r_frame=N rho, rho in a positive real compact, and the first-cut angle in a fixed sufficiently small positive compact of the common chart. For some c>0 independent of N, (1) extends to |delta|<cN: each clock is multiplied by exp(2pi i v_e delta/N), a small bounded complex perturbation. The scaled escaping clocks remain in compact subsets of C*, the finite negative clocks stay in a small neighborhood of the negative ray, and 202 totals stay near their positive ray. The 200/002 Bessel factors stay uniformly away from zero. Shrink c once for the finite network. The exact head lifts and all half-index offsets are kept; this extension does not assert finite-a stationarity. ## 2. Rational source quotients before asymptotics The actual large white is W_a(i,j;r)=(-1)^m q^[-dr+di-m(m-1)] H_m^1(U,V)/F_m, i+j=m+r, U=Q^i, V=Q^j, F_m=(Q;Q)_m. For ANY integral u,v its exact meromorphic quotient is W_a(i+u,j+v;r+u+v)/W_a(i,j;r) =q^(-dv) H_m^1(Q^u U,Q^v V)/H_m^1(U,V). (2) The same identity holds before specialization with q replaced by zeta and the actual H_m^(Q^-N). Thus (2) is not obtained by differentiating a root collision. It retains the internal Casimir label m. For the specified cup, L<N fixed, p_L(x)=exp(pi i x) q^[x(L-x-1)] Fhat_N(x)Fhat_N(L-x)/F_L, the factorial recurrence gives, for u>0, p_L(x+u)/p_L(x) =(-1)^u q^[u(L-2x-1)-u^2] product_(j=1)^u(1-Q^(x+j)) /product_(j=0)^(u-1)(1-Q^(L-x-j)). (3) Negative shifts are the reciprocal formula at the shifted base head. Caps use the literal complementary argument and inverse. Physical cup scales are constant in x. Formula (3) also holds for the specified generic moving-period factorial, before taking the root. For estimates at the ROOT, an exact simplification is essential. Write L=d-s and use the PROVED root reflection with the moving-factorial section specialized only now. It gives the meromorphic identity p_(d-s)(x)=C_(N,s) exp(pi i x) q^[(s-1)x] /product_(j=1)^s(1-Q^(x+j)), C_(N,s)=N(-1)^s Q^[s(s+1)/2]/F_(d-s). (4) Explicitly, the reflection is Fhat_N(x)Fhat_N(d-x)=N q^[x(x-d)]. Apply the unit recurrence s times to its second factor. The removed product is product_(j=1)^s(1-Q^(-x-j)); factoring each negative power gives exactly (4). Also C_(N,s)=F_s by the finite root factorial identity. In particular p_d(x)=exp(pi i x)q^-x, and p_(d-s)(x+1)/p_(d-s)(x) =-q^(s-1)(1-QU)/(1-Q^(s+1)U), U=Q^x. (5) The exp(pi i x) in (4) is literal. It is not set to one off the integer lattice. The physical scale N q^-d^2 and every other source character remain. Equation (4) cancels the quadratic factorial gauges BEFORE estimating derivatives; estimates for their separate absolute logs, which can be of size N log N, are unnecessary. For clarity, the literal dual is still pi_a(r;i,j)=gamma_a^-1 p_(2a)(2a-r) W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r)/[pV(d-j)pV(d-i)], (6) with FIXED root gamma_a and the actual reversal. Equations (2),(3) applied to (6), together with the recorded turn and peripheral characters, prove that S_N(+1)/S_N(-1) is an explicit rational function of the base clocks. No norm pi_a W_a is inverted. Apparent denominators are kept, or canceled as meromorphic factors; the boundary chart below avoids them. This proves the rational identity BEFORE any asymptotic replacement or normalization by the odd source. ## 3. The finite model and a bounded neighboring quotient Here are explicit choices of numerator model B_(m,N)(U,V). All finite clocks in the formulas co-vary along (1). Put a=d-m, s=m-a, P_s(T)=product_(r=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^r), K_a=[2a choose a]_Q, M(U,V)=I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+, M0(U)=I-(qU/2)H_-. Below S_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N), S_0=1, is the sine factorial; it is distinct from the channel deficit s. The matrices are the actual positive Hermitian source matrices from the [complementary packet](actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge.md). The following are finite expressions, including their source phases: * 200: E_m(U,V) J_0(2sqrt(K)), where E_m=(-1)^m Q^{m(m+1)/2}(UV)^m product_(r<m)(1-Q^r/U), K=sin^2(pi m/N)(V-1)/(pi^2(U/N^2)V). The Bessel series specifies this expression without a square-root ambiguity. * 002: product_(r<m)(V-Q^r) J_0(2sqrt(K0)), where K0=N^2 V sin^2(pi m/N)(1-U)/pi^2. * 220: V^a K_a det M0(U) P_s(UV). The actual large-partner product is retained exactly. * 022: (UV/A0)^m times the 220 model at (A0/V,A0/U), A0=Q^d. This is the literal generic reciprocity restricted to the root. * 202: A_a(UV)P_s(UV), where A_a(T)=(-1)^a Q^[a(a-1)/2] sum_(k=0)^a [S_a/(S_k S_(a-k))]^2(QT)^k. * 222: V^a K_a det M(U,V) P_s(UV). This model is the EXACT root numerator; no determinant is frozen at its limiting clocks. The first two and the relative 202 estimate are proved in the [root hard-edge theorem](actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.md). The 220 comparison is proved in the complementary packet; multiplying both sides by the SAME P_s changes no relative error. The 022 model uses its exact reciprocity. The 222 zero exclusion and its uniform finite-clock neighborhoods are proved by [positive determinant domination](actual_q_hahn_negative_clock_boundary.md). Replace each numerator of S_N(delta) by its displayed model, and keep EVERY other factor exactly. Call the resulting nonzero product B_N(delta). Uniformly on |delta|<cN, S_N(delta)=B_N(delta)(1+R_N(delta)), |R_N(delta)|<=C/N, (7) where R_N is holomorphic. This follows by the finite product of the uniform holomorphic root estimates on the indicated complex compact domains, not by extending estimates known only on a real ray. The first two limiting Bessel factors are nonzero on the common chart; continuity gives the required smaller complex neighborhoods. For 202 and 222, P_s has roots on the unit arc near -1 when eta is small, whereas the total lies near a positive compact. For the mixed outer-degree types its total tends to zero or infinity, and the reciprocity above retains the corresponding nonzero partner factors. We also need the two-sided bound |B_N(+1)/B_N(-1)|+|B_N(-1)/B_N(+1)|<=C. (8) Here is a direct proof, with no assumption on an absolute logarithm of B_N. Write D=partial_delta; each varying clock Z obeys D Z=(2pi i n/N)Z for a fixed bounded integer n. For (4), all factors Q^(x+j), 1<=j<=s, either remain uniformly separated from 1 in a compact negative-clock neighborhood, or tend uniformly to zero or infinity. Thus D log p_(d-s)(x) =v_x[pi i+(s-1)pi i/N] +(2pi i v_x/N) sum_(j=1)^s Q^(x+j)/(1-Q^(x+j)) is O(1+s/N). Physical cups have s=0. This also controls inverse cups and the reversed arguments in (6). The actual common-chart factorial-domain proof ensures these assertions for the auxiliary heads, including 202/202 and both maximal-fold parities. No escaping Gamma factor remains to estimate after the EXACT identity (4). Each original white/turn/peripheral character has a linear head exponent with coefficient O(N) in a power of q or Q (and the retained bounded integer character in (4)); therefore its logarithmic delta derivative is O(1). No arbitrary added character with an unbounded logarithmic delta derivative is covered by (8). Fixed root weights, factorials, gamma and K_a have derivative zero. In the 200/002 models the degree-m monomials and endpoint products have bounded logarithmic derivative: each finite linear factor has logarithmic derivative O(1/N), while m=O(N). The Bessel factor has derivative O(1/N), since its argument varies by O(1/N) and it stays away from zero on a fixed complex compact. For 220, H_- is positive. Its eigenvalue product proves |U partial_U log det M0(U)|<=C a on the negative-clock neighborhood. For 202 the negative real roots of its positive-coefficient polynomial give |T partial_T log A_a(T)|<=C a near the positive ray. Each partner factor gives an additional O(1/N) delta derivative, uniformly under the separation just stated. The 022 expression has the same bounds after its literal reciprocal substitutions and exact monomial. Finally, for 222 fix the nearby negative raw clocks as a reference. For M_ref=I+alpha H_-+beta H_+, alpha,beta>0, conjugation by M_ref^-1/2 puts both positive summands below I. A small complex clock neighborhood leaves the normalized inverse bounded and bounds M_ref^-1/2 (D M) M_ref^-1/2 by C/N. Hence |tr(M^-1 D M)|<=C a/N. This controls the exact finite determinant uniformly at the fold. Combining the finitely many factors yields |D log B_N|<=C on |delta|<=2, with its continuous local logarithm. Integration between -1 and +1 proves (8). ## 4. Correlation survives the small odd-source denominator Apply Cauchy's formula to the SAME R_N in (7) on the delta disk. For |delta|<=2 it gives |D R_N|<=C/N^2. Therefore S_N(+1)/S_N(-1) =[B_N(+1)/B_N(-1)](1+O(N^-2)). (9) The improved error is a correlation statement. Two unrelated relative O(N^-1) estimates would not prove it. All source and model quotients are nonzero here for sufficiently large N. Let t range in a fixed real compact subset of (0,1), and retain the EXACT normalization of the [source-preserving odd insertion](actual_source_preserving_odd_framing_period.md), kappa_N(t)=1-q-t^d+q(1-t)^d. Its proved lower bound is |kappa_N|>=1/N. Equations (8),(9) give [S_N(+1)-q S_N(-1)]/[kappa_N S_N(-1)] =[B_N(+1)/B_N(-1)-q]/kappa_N + O(N^-1). (10) In particular this theorem retains the exact q, rather than replacing it by one before a cancellation of order N^-1. The entire finite model quotient, every cup character, internal channel label, clock correction and half-index offset remains on the right of (10). The constants are uniform for bounded total deficit, both parities, and also in a sufficiently small fixed near-fold label neighborhood 0<=s_i<=eta N. Thus they apply to the shrinking window sum_i s_i log N=o(N). This is a ROOT ratio result and does not expand the previously proved generic-normal window. No assertion is made that the right side of (10) has a nonzero limit, or even stays bounded. In particular replacing its finite label dependence by the complete parabolic stationary value would require an additional argument. Formula (10) supplies an explicit model with an absolute O(N^-1) error relative to S_N(-1), even when its leading finite quotient has not been evaluated. ## 5. What contraction would additionally require This is a theorem about the ORIGINAL uncontracted products on a common affine band path. Their coherent first-cut weight, the original internal head measure and the two original support cycles have not been removed. A ratio of sums or periods is not the sum or period of the pointwise ratio in (9). Uniform pointwise relative errors alone do not control the relative error of a complex integral with cancellation. A Gaussian-reduced version would need one common holomorphic transverse reduction, its full coarea/Hessian factor, controlled common cycles and ends, and a nonzero model pushforward with a uniform relative remainder. If such a reduction itself supplies (7) on a cN disk and (8), the same Cauchy proof gives (9),(10) for that reduced family. This implication is conditional; those analytic and cycle hypotheses are not proved by the present uncontracted calculation. Nor is a routed source with uncontrolled 000/020 factors covered by removing its routing only after contraction. Focused audit: [original shifts and correlated local packets](../experiments/audit_actual_correlated_boundary_band_ratio.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_correlated_boundary_band_ratio_results.json). It checks 649 actual white neighboring quotients and 649 literal dual neighbors through the first genuine quantum jet, 68 generic cup shifts, 58 root reflection-reduced cups and two symbolic source exponents. At 160 digits it compares 48 original finite Newton sums with the six model formulas, then checks 384 packet values, 96 paired W-pi source quotients and their normalized odd errors, 192 complex head-neighborhood values and 48 exact escaping-cup logarithmic derivatives. Both level parities and fixed neighboring folded labels are retained. The local signed fixtures cover all six types, including an explicitly supplemental 202/202 face pair; they are not a numerical global-network proof. Independent full analytical geometric/model review: PASS. The reviewer rederived the root cup reflection and character, literal dual and reciprocal scalar, checked every model on the cN complex head disk, the positive-total forced-root separation through the fold, and the exact finite-clock 222 determinant. The first logarithmic derivative bounds, correlated Cauchy estimate and normalized absolute error were checked. The review retains the uncontracted, controlled-presentation scope and supplies no Gaussian reduction or period coefficient. Independent primary full proof review, focused audit code review and fresh redirected replay: PASS. The reviewer checked the actual charged product with its exposed scalar cap removed, the omission of the charge-zero Xi_N formula, every exact quotient and cup character, all six co-varying finite models, uniform divisor separation and first logarithmic derivative bounds, and the Cauchy/normalization argument. The fresh replay reproduced all reported counts and errors. No contracted, arbitrary routed, or model-limit conclusion is included in that validation.

title: What all-face collars do not supply: source homology and a gluing criterion
text: # What all-face collars do not supply: source homology and a gluing criterion 28 October 2026. The physical-face collars and quantitative regular gradient estimate are compatible local analytic ingredients. They do not alone prove a low-action deformation of the ORIGINAL scalar. There is an exact source-homology obstruction to applying that argument as one ordinary contour homotopy of its undecomposed holomorphic summand. The obstruction occurs for the SAME hyperbolic knot after ordinary signed Markov stabilizations; it is not a hypothetical phase counterexample. Source-specific current cancellation, exact normalization pruning or a pointed-operator reduction can evade it. Thus this does not rule out all contour or boundary-to-interior methods. A sufficient quantitative gluing criterion is given below; its source-compatibility premise is not yet proved for the full cotangent atlas. ## 1. A precise individual-evaluation homology lemma Let F_N be holomorphic on the swept region Omega_N in C^r. Let Gamma_0 be the original product residue contour around the finite integer box in the independent ORIGINAL source coordinates. For every valid state p in that box, the ordinary product Cauchy kernel gives F_N(p)=(2pi*i)^(-r) integral_(Gamma_0) F_N(z) dz_1...dz_r/product_j(z_j-p_j). (1) Suppose a closed deformed current Gamma_N, including all its retained components and multiplicities, is homologous to Gamma_0 in Omega_N minus UNION_(j,n) {z_j=n}, (2) where the removed set includes ALL coordinate integer divisors met by the original source. In particular every form in (1) stays holomorphic on the deformation complement. Equation (1) holds with Gamma_N too, independently of whether it was originally obtained using a cotangent kernel. Define its individual Cauchy mass M_(p,N)=(2pi)^(-r) integral_(Gamma_N) |dz_1 wedge ... wedge dz_r|/product_j|z_j-p_j|. Then EXACTLY |F_N(p)| <= M_(p,N) sup_(Gamma_N)|F_N|. (3) Consequently, if log M_(p,N)=o(N), a deformation in this homology class cannot place the undecomposed density below the exponential rate of that original individual state. Subexponential geometric mass plus subexponential inverse distance to these Cauchy kernels is a sufficient hypothesis on M. An arbitrary deformation with uncontrolled near-divisor mass is not covered. This is a statement about ordinary homology preserving ALL individual evaluation tests. It deliberately excludes source-specific crossings of canceled divisors, dropping exact zero pairings only for the selected source, current recombination, and distinct transports of meromorphic phase sectors whose compensating poles must be paired. Such operations can change these extra tests while preserving the original period. They are possible escapes, not contradictions to (3). ## 2. An actual same-knot family with arbitrarily high individual states Use the original complete physical head, with Q=exp(2pi*i/N), x=-exp(-pi*i/N), d=N-1, F_a=(Q;Q)_a, g_b=theta Q^(-b), theta=x^(1-N), kappa=exp(pi*i*(N-1)^2/(2N)). For a positive crossing, a DIAGONAL original matrix element has a=b+k and exact value r_+(a,b;k)=kappa x^(-2b)Q^(b^2) F_a^2/[F_k F_b^2]. (4) The original negative crossing on the reversed pair has the conjugate value, including conjugate kappa. For N divisible by four take A=3N/4, B=N/4, k=N/2. The actual endpoint-uniform factorial estimate, or its elementary interior Euler--Maclaurin proof, gives |r_+(A,B;k)|=|r_-(B,A;k)| =(2N)^(-1/2) exp[N v_8/(2pi)](1+O(1/N)). (5) Indeed I(3/4)=-I(1/4)=Catalan/(2pi), I(1/2)=0 and v_8=4 Catalan. The factorial square-root prefactors give precisely (2N)^(-1/2). Both actual half-root and full Cartan phases are retained in (4); they have modulus one. Start from ANY fixed one-component braid diagram of ANY hyperbolic knot K. Its closed state with every head A and every original transfer zero is valid. Every original crossing then has modulus one, at either sign, and all original pivots also have modulus one. Append signed Markov stabilizations, starting with a positive one and then alternating signs. The new last head values are B,A,B,A,..., and every appended transfer is k=N/2. Each new crossing is diagonal: (A,B) is unchanged by the positive crossing and (B,A) is unchanged by the negative crossing. Thus this is an EXACT valid closed original state at every stage, with no mod-N routing or reset. With s such stabilizations, its absolute value is (2N)^(-s/2) exp[s N v_8/(2pi)](1+O_s(1/N)), (6) up to the retained label-independent external line, which has no exponential modulus at the original complete normalization. The single original averaged-cut factor 1/N also changes only a power of N. No additional average is attached to each new head. ### Independent check of the whole original Markov normalization The exact original partial trace of the new head is Tr_new[(I tensor g)R_+]=kappa theta I, Tr_new[(I tensor g)R_-]=kappa^(-1)theta^(-1)I. (7) Here is a direct proof without assuming an external invariance theorem. For the positive case its a-th cut diagonal, divided by kappa theta, is F_a^2 sum_(b=0)^a Q^(b^2)/(F_(a-b)F_b^2)=1. (8) The rational identity follows by decomposing a partition with largest part at most a by its Durfee square of side b: the square contributes Q^(b^2), the part to its right is a b by (a-b) rectangle, with generating polynomial {a choose b}_Q, and the part below has largest part at most b, contributing 1/F_b. This is a bijection, so 1/F_a=sum_b Q^(b^2){a choose b}_Q/F_b as a formal power series and hence as a rational identity. All root denominators satisfy b<=a<N. There is no first-partial-trace off-diagonal by exact degree support. For the negative trace put A'=d-a and replace b by d-r. Exact factorial reflection at Q^(-1) and the SAME identity (8) give, before its final Cartan simplification, the scalar kappa^(-1)theta x^(2a) Q^[-a^2+1+A'(A'+1)]. Since x^2=Q^(-1), A'+a=N-1 and theta^2 Q=1, this is exactly the second value in (7), with no parity exception. Both are unit scalars. The original zero-framing line cancels precisely these actual Markov factors. Partial tracing the new head in a whole word uses its original pivot and NO factor 1/N; the sole original average in (2) of the cardinal source stays unchanged. Thus every stabilized diagram has the SAME original knot invariant and the same volume, while (6)'s individual-state rate is arbitrarily large as the fixed number s increases. This independently checks every new pivot and normalization relevant to the example. ## 3. Consequence for the proposed global dynamics For the cardinal completion, F_N is holomorphic on the stated joint box and equals the exact original summand at every valid integer state. Therefore (1)--(6) apply to that ACTUAL source. Choosing s with s v_8>Vol(K) rules out an undecomposed low-|F_N| cycle with subexponential Cauchy mass in the homology class (2), at the desired knot-volume level. All proper physical faces of that diagram still have the proved outward action coefficient, and its genuine regular critical values still have the representation-volume bound. This pinpoints a compatibility which those local results alone do not establish. One must use the selected source, not silently prove an equally strong estimate for every individual-state evaluation. The already proved exact Markov pruning DOES evade this example; it contracts a complete source cell before absolute estimation. It is part of the remedy, rather than a contradiction to the theorem. Additional source-specific relations can likewise evade the extra evaluation tests. The example does not prove that a pruned diagram still has the same obstruction, nor that all sector/current contour methods fail. ## 4. A sufficient quantitative gluing criterion and its power count The following criterion isolates what a valid boundary-to-interior construction would have to add. It is local-current data rather than an assumption that the unknown whole period already has a low-action representative. Suppose the finite physical-face atlas is supplied with SOURCE-specific chain homotopies on the complete marked sector/current complex, with all these properties: * Their boundary formulas include all overlap curtains, valid cotangent residue currents, and paired artificial pole currents. The formulas glue on overlaps and preserve the selected original period. They need not preserve the additional tests (1). * A common marked height H is used. A face operation, including its outgoing current pieces, lowers H by at least g_N=c N^(-alpha)log N, up to a smaller overshoot O(N^(-beta)log N), beta>alpha. No unmatched side current is left at arbitrary height. Already low-height terminal pieces are allowed. * After the leading height is accounted for, each operation has a bounded number of pieces and log mass cost at most C log^C N+C N^(1-beta)log^C N. The exact collar Gamma bounds can provide this type of local estimate; their leading negative action must not be counted again as a positive amplitude loss. * Regular gradient segments preserve the same source class and have cumulative log mass at most N^(B epsilon)log^C N, with B epsilon<1. All ends either enter another covered patch or the target sublevel. If the initial relevant height range is O(log^C N), these properties give the desired exp(o(N)) total transport cost. In fact the number of face operations is at most J_N=O(N^alpha log^C N), because each spends at least a fixed fraction of g_N in height. Their combined log mass is consequently bounded by O(N^alpha log^C N+N^(1+alpha-beta)log^C N)=o(N), (9) provided alpha<1 and beta>alpha. Fixed branching adds only O(J_N). The regular-flow cost is also o(N). A transported chain ending in H<=Vol(K)/(2pi)+eta then gives the upper bound by triangle inequality; letting eta decrease gives the sharp limsup. This proves the criterion. The not-yet-verified part for the actual global cotangent atlas is precisely the first two source-compatible gluing properties, including valid interior residue currents and overlap heights. Finite face count, endpoint action drop and a regular flow bound do not imply them. In particular source-universal chart identities alone preserve the individual tests behind (3); state-specific normalization/Ward or pointed-A information must enter where that barrier is exceeded. ## 5. Independent audit of the source-specific A-boundary alternative I independently read [the actual A-boundary Schur theorem](actual_a_boundary_schur_transport.md) and reran its audit: **PASS**. The initial weighted identity-row source gives g_I=0 exactly when those colors are retained in B. Completing the square gives H=-P_II^(-1)P_IB and the positive Schur operator S with ker P=E ker S. Consistency gives beta=g_B^* S^+ g_B, not an independently chosen border normalization. I checked the positive bordered Gram and the selected coefficient formula [lambda^nu z]D/[lambda^nu]Q, including the retained kernel: g_B and the selected observable vanish on it, so the kernel factors off as lambda^nu and the z derivative is the exact squared selected boundary response. The banded Neumann-series inverse decay and the rigid two-endpoint recurrence example also check, including lambda_min(S)~3*4^(-n)/4. No source or weight correction was needed. The fresh audit passed four actual pointed-source eliminations, the exact one-dimensional retained-kernel fixture and four rational rigid boundary recurrences. This construction can escape (3): it estimates the ACTUAL selected source response, not every holomorphic state evaluation. Its remaining boundary energy estimate is not supplied by uniqueness or the good interior gap. [Independent original-source normalization audit](../experiments/audit_actual_cotangent_homology_stabilization.py) checks (4)--(8), both crossing signs and every new pivotal trace.

title: Exact coupled cap sources and their regular meridian boundary relation
text: # Exact coupled cap sources and their regular meridian boundary relation 28 October 2026. Every terminal pair source can be peeled by exact coefficients before taking a critical-point limit. The resulting source is a coupled geometric polynomial, including at the ORIGINAL marked cap. An exact interval identity retains its complete numerator and gives a regular complex Lagrangian on which the actual framed meridians are inverse. This supplies the classical cap equation missing from treating the two terminal monomials as independent saddle variables. The retained interval endpoints are disjoint from every regular noncentral geometric critical branch for a one-component knot. It does not compute the intersection of the original interval/torus cycle with a hyperbolic thimble. In particular, a generic geometric clock is complex, while the initial interval parameter is real. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_coupled_caps_interval_source.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_coupled_caps_interval_source_results.json) check the literal duality matrices, all fused boundary coefficients, whole original four-head words, interval identities on their logarithmic charts, and the actual framed meridian product. ## 1. Physical pair sources, with their original normalization Put N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), F_a=(Q;Q)_a, y=x^(-1)Q^(-1), K_i=x_i B_i^(-1). Use the existing balanced factorial basis and the actual oriented dual in [the pivotal-duality proof](relative_pivotal_duality.md). On the physical basis vector indexed by (a,b), the cup and ordinary right cap are cup_x(a,b)=N x^(a-d) delta_(a+b,d), cap_x(a,b)=N^(-1) y^a delta_(a+b,d). (1) The ORIGINAL averaged marked right cap, before any Ward-corner replacement, is mark_x(a,b)=x^b/N^2, 0<=a,b<N. (2) Here is a direct normalization check. In the original unbalanced basis, J_x e_b=c_b e_(d-b)^*, c_b=(-x)^b Q^(b(b+1)/2), and the pivot is g_a=x^(-d)Q^(-a). The balanced reflection identity is F_b F_(d-b)=N(-1)^b Q^(b(b+1)/2). Thus the balanced cup is F_a F_b/c_b on a+b=d; the ordinary cap is c_b g_a/(F_a F_b). These give (1). Writing D_F=diag(F_a), the actual averaged defect is D_F^(-1)g^(-1)e D_F, e_(a,b)=1/N. Its cap row is (D_F^(-1)g^(-1)e D_F)^t g J_x before balancing, which gives (2) at EVERY pair (a,b), not just on the invariant fiber. For a k-pair plat, the cup degree is k d. Each ordinary cap forces degree d on its pair. The actual word and every Gaussian dilation sector preserve total integer degree. Consequently, after the k-1 ordinary caps, (2) is paired only with the marked fiber a+b=d. On that fiber it is mark_x(a,d-a)=x^(d-a)/N^2. (3) This restriction uses degree, not a Ward identity applied separately to a Gaussian sector. Finite head support and all external scalar lines are retained. If one first uses the already assembled Ward corner, reversing that corner after decomposing into Gaussian sectors is not justified; start from (2) instead. Let K_N(r)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1) r^a. With the coefficient-source convention that a row at (a,b) contributes z_1^(-a)z_2^(-b), the exact coupled kernels are Cup_x(z_1,z_2)=N x^(-d) z_2^d K_N(x z_1/z_2), Cap_x(z_1,z_2)=N^(-1) z_2^(-d) K_N(Q^(-1)z_2/(x z_1)), Mark_x(z_1,z_2)=x^d N^(-2) z_2^(-d) K_N(z_2/(x z_1)). (4) The last line is precisely (2) on its forced degree fiber. Its normalization is different from the ordinary cap. The phase Q^(-1) in the ordinary cap is retained. ## 2. Exact terminal-factor peeling These kernels can also be recovered by peeling the terminal factors in [the all-Hardy residue graph](actual_hardy_forest_residue_reduction.md). For the actual inverse fusion C_x^(-1)=F_2 F_1^(-1) V_- F_2^(-1), the ordinary fused row is N^(-1)<0,d|. The terminal F_2 extracts F_d=N, while the first-head reciprocal factorial at output 0 extracts 1. The remaining exact coefficient is [b^d] U_N(b/z_2) V_N(b/(x z_1)) =z_2^(-d) (t;Q)_d/N =z_2^(-d) K_N(Q^(-1)t)/N, t=z_2/(x z_1). (5) Only the first N jets of U_N,V_N occur. The first equality is the finite q-binomial theorem; the second follows from (t;Q)_d=(1-t^N)/(1-Q^(-1)t). Both numerator and denominator are retained, with the ratio extended as its polynomial. For completeness, the fused ORIGINAL marked row m_x=mark_x C_x on the same degree fiber has m_x(r,d-r)=x^(d-r)(-1)^r Q^(-r(r+1)/2) F_r^2/N^2. (6) Indeed the explicit fusion coefficient gives sum_(a=0)^r F_(d-a)/F_(r-a)=N, by the finite q-binomial theorem and the reflection identity. This yields (6). Peeling its adjacent complete inverse fusion gives m_x C_x^(-1)=mark_x, not a new selected row. There is no division by the knot value and no requirement that it be nonzero. Equations (4)--(6) eliminate all terminal monomial/factorial caps and their redundant fusion-frame variables by exact coefficients. They do not discard a terminal source endpoint: that information is in K_N. ## 3. Replace K_N by its exact interval source On a chosen logarithmic chart write L=Log r and put A(r)=Log r/(r-1), K_N(r)=N A(r) integral_0^1 exp(N s Log r) ds. (7) This is an exact elementary integral, since its right side is (r^N-1)/(r-1). On the sheet L=0 at r=1, A extends analytically with A(1)=1 and is nonzero nearby. The two interval endpoints remain present; (7) does not replace their difference by one exponential. On a different logarithmic sheet at r=1 the individual factors in (7) have a compensating pole and zero. The combined function is still the polynomial K_N, but the factors must not be continued separately through that point. On any compact logarithmic chart avoiding those points, the interval integrand is bounded and ordinary Fubini applies. A full angular circuit is treated as a lifted cut chart with its matched ends. Substituting (7) into (4) gives the exact boundary kernels Cup_x=N^2 x^(-d) z_2^d A(r_cup) integral_0^1 exp(Ns Log r_cup)ds, Cap_x=z_2^(-d) A(r_cap) integral_0^1 exp(Ns Log r_cap)ds, Mark_x=x^d/N z_2^(-d) A(t) integral_0^1 exp(Ns Log t)ds, r_cup=x z_1/z_2, r_cap=Q^(-1)t, t=z_2/(x z_1). (8) In particular the original marked normalization is x^d/N after introducing its one interval, not 1. These formulas can be inserted in the ORIGINAL whole physical word. They are exact scalar source identities, including with its continuous Gaussian variables. Concretely, if W_beta is the ORIGINAL physical word on 2k heads, its original selected scalar is the pairing of W_beta with k copies of (1) as input, k-1 ordinary cap rows, and the one row (2), times the unchanged external scalar line chi_beta,N. Equations (3)--(8) replace only those sources. Each of the 2k turns contributes one interval coordinate, independently of N. The boundary fusion frames can all be removed; the unshortened all-Hardy graph now has 6m+2k complex coordinates for m crossings, together with its m real Gaussian coordinates and the 2k interval coordinates. This count is before any further coefficient or residue simplification. The source numerator is encoded by the retained ends of these intervals, not deleted. For a source-compatible initial cycle one may ensure that every boundary ratio has modulus different from 1. Initial cup radii can be chosen freely. At a terminal touched head the last active factorial is positive: its output radius can be enlarged arbitrarily while keeping its reflected cyclic argument small. If it is the first head of its last crossing, the only subsequent transfer lowers that head and increasing this radius also makes the transfer argument smaller. The second-head terminal factorial has no subsequent transfer. Thus the final radius of each touched head can be enlarged independently; for each terminal pair choose a sufficiently large common scale giving |t|=1/2. An untouched head has its free source radius. This preserves the previous small-atom chamber and gives fixed positive separation of the boundary ratios from 1. The logarithmic radius bounds remain C(1+sum|xi|), so the original Gaussian domination still applies. Initial cup ratios can be perturbed off 1 if an untouched pair fixes their reciprocal ratio. ## 4. The regular complex boundary relation Let h=2*pi*i/N and define a clock by B=exp(p), where p is the logarithmic semiclassical momentum. In (8), stationarity in the interval interior requires Log t=0 at leading order (or Log r_cup=0 for the cup). The resulting paired relation is z_2=x z_1, B_1=exp(2*pi*i*s), B_2=B_1^(-1). (9) The cup and covector orientations give opposite source momenta and the same physical constraint. For the ordinary cap Log r_cap=Log t-h; its extra factor exp(-2*pi*i*s) is nonzero and is kept in the amplitude. At the exact position t=1 its already-integrated kernel has K_N(Q^(-1))=0, and the ordinary cap--cup bubble remains exactly zero. The nonzero density asserted below is the JOINT (head,s) density before integrating s, not a claim that this integrated kernel is nonzero at t=1. The original marked bubble is instead one. Both normalizations are checked by the audit. Integrating out s can produce cancellation and must not be mistaken for a proof of selected noncancellation. The exact degree d=N-1 gives the affine constraint D+1=N, and the leading clock lifts in (9) have p_1+p_2=2*pi*i. It is not a zero-charge constraint produced by forgetting the half-step. At finite N the source monomial has p_1+p_2=h d and hence B_1 B_2=Q^d=Q^(-1); together with the actual dual color xy=Q^(-1) this gives K_tot=1 exactly. The principal constraints (9) are its Q-to-1 limit. No exact finite clock identity B_1 B_2=1 is asserted. For fixed x the set (9), with z_1 nonzero and B_1 nonzero and different from 1, is nonempty, regular, and Lagrangian: dlog B_2=-dlog B_1 and dlog z_2=dlog z_1 cancel the two symplectic terms. The factor A has value 1 on its selected local sheet at the stationary relation. Interval orientation is +1. Thus the local source density there is nonzero, with its original scalar and Gaussian determinant still retained. This statement is about a boundary relation and local density, not a computed geometric-thimble multiplicity. ## 5. These are the actual inverse peripheral meridians Use the commuting principal symbols of the actual balanced generators: K_i=x_i/B_i, f_i=(1-B_i)z_i, e_i=z_i^(-1)(x_i^(-1)-x_i/B_i), x_1=x, x_2=x^(-1). On (9), direct substitution gives K_tot=K_1 K_2=1, f_tot=f_1+K_1^(-1)f_2=0, e_tot=e_1 K_2+e_2=0. (10) At completeness x=-1, (9) reads z_2=-z_1. These are exactly the classical equations of the actual dual pair, not equations of a newly assigned boundary invariant. To check the based meridians, retain the actual Gauss convention L_(+,i)=[[K_i,e_i],[0,1]], L_(-,i)=[[1,0],[-K_i f_i,K_i]], G_i=L_(-,i)^(-1)L_(+,i), H_1=G_1, H_2=L_(-,1)^(-1)G_2 L_(-,1). Then the exact classical matrix multiplication is H_2 H_1=(L_(-,2)L_(-,1))^(-1)(L_(+,2)L_(+,1))=I. (11) The last equality follows from (10): both triangular products are I. Raw G_2 G_1 is generally NOT the correct based product. These H_i are the same framed meridians whose exact quantum Hurwitz transport was proved in [the actual shared-flag note](actual_shared_quantum_flags_and_charged_exchange.md). Thus the boundary branch in (9) is compatible with an actual knot representation's oriented cup/meridian relation. Conversely, H_2 H_1=I makes the upper triangular product L_(+,2)L_(+,1) equal the lower triangular product L_(-,2)L_(-,1). Their diagonal and off-diagonal entries force exactly (10). On the regular locus B_1 different from 1, K_tot=1 gives B_2=B_1^(-1), and f_tot=(1-B_1)(z_1-z_2/x)=0 gives z_2=x z_1. Thus (9) is precisely the regular physical cap locus, not only a sufficient special family. At x=-1, this chart covers the Zariski-open part of the nontrivial trace -2 parabolic class with G_(11) different from 0,-1. Explicitly B=-1/G_(11), z=(-G_(11)-1)/G_(12). The determinant and trace equations force G_(12)G_(21)=-(G_(11)+1)^2, so z is nonzero there. For finitely many nontrivial parabolic meridians, a simultaneous generic SL(2,C) conjugation avoids all these finitely many proper closed conditions: each is proper on a parabolic conjugacy class, and SL(2,C) is irreducible. Hence a supplied geometric knot representation with inverse meridians at its paired turns has a simultaneous regular boundary chart. At each turn the second physical factor is recovered by (10)--(11), giving B_2=B_1^(-1), z_2=-z_1. In a list of adjacent paired turns the preceding paired triangular products are I by (10), so the first meridian of the next pair is in the same based frame; a separate independent frame per cap is not being assumed. This is a classical simultaneous framing statement. It does not supply a quantum cycle map implementing that conjugation. This does not assert that every INTERNAL factorization chart of the word is regular in that frame. Further five-term/relative-chart transport may still be needed there. For example, substituting the regular physical cap into the inverse fusion chart gives K=V, A=UK=1 and J=V/K=1. This intrinsic terminal auxiliary degeneration is why adjacent boundary factors were peeled by coefficients rather than declared regular independent saddles. There is also an exact agreement with the literal five-flag source mark. Put R=x z_1/z_2 and X=x z_2/z_1, as in the [marked full-Phi flag calculation](actual_marked_full_phi_flag_pentagon.md). At the complete root x^2=Q^(-1), so X=Q^(-1)/R. The source branch R=1 therefore has precisely the mark X=Q^(-1). In the original finite typed source, the independently proved equality is X cup=Q^(-1)cup. This marking match does not impose X^N=1 on the unwrapped scalar coordinate; the latter remains a variable until an actual source/cycle map supplies that specialization. ## 6. Complex cap clocks have an exact endpoint-fixed source deformation Initially s is the real interval [0,1]. Its interior clocks lie on the unit circle. A generic geometric B is any nonzero complex value; its logarithm gives a complex s modulo integers. No claim is needed that a single frame puts every B on the unit circle. There is instead an exact source-preserving deformation. For fixed Log r, the function exp(Ns Log r) is ENTIRE in s. Consequently, for any compact piecewise smooth path gamma from 0 to 1, integral_gamma exp(Ns Log r) ds =integral_0^1 exp(Ns Log r) ds. (12) This follows from its entire primitive, also at Log r=0. Given a regular geometric clock B, choose any s_g=Log B/(2*pi*i) and an endpoint-fixed path through s_g. Equation (12) proves exact equality of the original source pointwise in every other variable. It holds for all caps simultaneously by taking the product paths. The endpoints are unchanged; there are no residues or omitted source corrections in this s-only deformation. One may prescribe a nonzero local tangent at s_g as well. If useful, a single generic classical frame can also avoid the positive real ray for all the finitely many B. Each B is a nonconstant holomorphic function of that frame; its positive-ray inverse image has empty interior by the open mapping theorem. On this additional dense open real-analytic choice, use 0<Arg B<2*pi, giving 0<Re s_g<1. This is not required for (12), but places the desired complex point directly above the interior of the initial interval strip. On a fixed compact path family, |s| is bounded. The additional absolute factor is at most exp(CN|Log r|); the initial radius estimates make this at most exp(C'N(1+sum|xi|)). Thus the original Gaussian majorant still justifies the joint path deformation and Fubini. The marked logarithmic charts in r, including their matched angular ends, remain as in Section 3; entireness in s is not a license to discard those data. Therefore the theorem removes the spurious separate-terminal-monomial critical equations and supplies a regular actual meridian boundary Lagrangian with nonzero density. The boundary interval paths can be deformed through its desired complex clocks exactly. This does not yet prove that the bulk head-variable cycle reaches the same geometric branch with nonzero whole-cycle intersection, or that its endpoint/alias contributions have smaller exponential rate. ## 7. A regular interval endpoint cannot carry a noncentral knot representation At either retained interval endpoint s=0 or 1, the principal source clocks are B_1=B_2=1. Stationarity in s is not imposed at an endpoint, so this does NOT require z_2=x z_1. Nevertheless, at x=-1 the actual classical generators have e_i=f_i=0, K_i=-1 for every finite nonzero z_i. Hence each physical G_i=-I, and the framed H_i is also -I. Suppose a complete stationary solution is in regular charts where the actual Hurwitz laws and paired boundary equations define a representation of a ONE-component knot group. All its oriented meridians are conjugate, up to inversion. If one is -I, every meridian is -I; since meridians generate the knot group, the induced PSL(2,C) representation is trivial. Thus no noncentral geometric representation occurs at a regular source interval endpoint. In particular, choose a regular geometric critical point and small coordinate neighborhoods of its finitely many interval coordinates s_g. Each s_g is different from 0 and 1, since its meridian is not central. The neighborhoods can be chosen with positive separation from both endpoints. Every endpoint stratum has empty intersection with this neighborhood of the geometric critical branch. Thus the localized geometric stationary germ, including its Gaussian block, has no contribution from a cap interval endpoint. This removes an endpoint cancellation of THAT local block; it does not compute the original whole-cycle coefficient of that block. This is a source-support exclusion on the regular representation locus. It is not an estimate for endpoint periods on singular norm divisors, escaping flags, or extra integer phase aliases. Those are precisely the cases where a regular representation argument alone supplies no bound. ## 8. Uniform regular-geometric exclusion of physical cutoff walls The same argument applies to fixed signed endpoint-clock projectors in the actual five-term/flag moves, including the explicit E_0(Z) in [the marked full-Phi flag calculation](actual_marked_full_phi_flag_pentagon.md). The clock here must be a PHYSICAL actual head clock, or an explicitly tracked exact Hurwitz conjugate of one; arbitrary fusion-relative clocks are not covered. For Z^N=1 define its original spectral projector E_j(Z)=N^(-1)sum_(r=0)^(N-1) Q^(-jr)Z^r. Exactly, (Z-Q^j)E_j=0. Let j range over a fixed finite set of signed integers as N grows, so the top index d is j=-1. Their principal characteristic wall is B=1. At complete color the corresponding actual physical meridian is G=-I, as proved above. A regular actual Hurwitz solution for a one-component knot on ANY such wall therefore has trivial induced PSL(2,C) representation. This gives a uniform LOCAL statement near a compact regular geometric critical branch. There are only finitely many tracked clocks, and their B values differ from 1. Choose delta>0 such that |B-1|>=delta throughout a sufficiently small compact neighborhood. For all large N, |B-Q^j|>=delta/2 for every one of the finitely many signed j. More explicitly, suppose a wall component admits a regular formal WKB expansion exp(S/h)(a_0+h a_1+...), h=2*pi*i/N. A physical clock acts with leading multiplier B=exp(partial_(log z) S). Its annihilating relation (Z-exp(jh))f=0 first gives (B-1)a_0=0. Since B-1 is invertible on this neighborhood, a_0=0. At each subsequent order the lower coefficients already vanish, leaving (B-1)a_r=0; hence EVERY a_r=0. Exact Hurwitz conjugation transports both the annihilating equation and this regular symbol argument. A bounded fixed number of clock shifts only changes the finite signed set of j. Thus physical endpoint-projector corrections have zero regular formal geometric block in these charts. They cannot cancel a nonzero localized geometric Gaussian block there. This is neither an analytic bound on the full root-level correction nor a proof that such a Gaussian block is selected by the original whole cycle. Two limitations are essential. First, a bulk index j_N/N tending to a nonzero angle has principal B=exp(2*pi*i*lim j_N/N), not 1, and is not excluded. Second, relative fusion clocks A=J=1 can occur on a REGULAR physical cap, as the explicit inverse-fusion calculation in Section 5 shows. A projector in such a relative clock must not be called a physical meridian cutoff without its actual clock map. No finite Ore localization is being performed. Inverting all the shifted factors 1-Q^r Z at fixed N would invert their product 1-Z^N=0 and destroy the whole finite module. Formal regular-geometric exclusion at bounded signed shifts does not authorize this globally invalid operation, or deleting any original finite source/projector. ## 9. Finite physical-projector stationary strata have action zero There is also a critical-VALUE statement, including the missing normal equation of an endpoint projector. It applies to a network of actual canonical crossing relations, the original inverse-meridian turns, and finitely many explicitly tracked PHYSICAL signed-endpoint projectors. Require finite nonzero physical position coordinates. At every crossing the shape tuple must be regular, or a genuine joint limit of its regular actual rational graph; an arbitrary cleared auxiliary chart is not sufficient. Stationarity is imposed in all remaining phase directions. The following argument does not assume stationarity in a projector's fixed clock normal. First, a general finite unit-wall calculation extends the action identity. Write the full leading phase, with all original logarithmic marks retained, in the form W(Z)=sum_j epsilon_j Li_2(exp(a_j.Z+i phi_j)) +Z^t C Z/2+i kappa.Z+c, where C is real symmetric, a_j,phi_j,kappa are real and Im c=0. Restrict it to a stratum of linear logarithmic constraints A Z=i theta_0, A and theta_0 real. (15) Thus A Re Z=0. Dilog terms identically equal to Li_2(1) on the stratum are real constants, with their consistent integer marks, and are omitted from its derivative. If this restricted finite phase is stationary, the gradient of its remaining expression is conormal to (15). Its contraction with Re Z consequently vanishes. The off-critical defect identity from [the actual regulator calculation](actual_wall_critical_regulator.md) therefore gives EXACTLY Im W=sum_j epsilon_j D(exp(a_j.Z+i phi_j)). (16) This also covers dependent linear unit-wall constraints, after using a basis of their conormal space. It avoids assigning a finite value to a singular normal derivative: remove the constant Li_2(1) terms before differentiating on the stratum. Equivalently their possible normal limits are bounded by rho log|rho|, which tends to zero. All Gaussian/cap variables and pure-imaginary integer logarithmic terms remain in this calculation. An unrelated constrained maximum of the real part of W does not satisfy this stationarity hypothesis. Next the ORIGINAL physical projector kernel is, in the actual position frames, (F_out E_j F_in^(-1))(zout,zin) =N^(-1)(zout/zin)^j. (17) For a bounded signed index choose its representative j_N in [0,d]. Its leading clock lift h j_N, h=2pi*i/N, is either 0 or 2pi*i; the latter integer logarithmic phase in (17) is retained. In either case its characteristic correspondence is B_in=B_out=1, positions zin,zout arbitrary. (18) Thus a projector can allow a position/flag jump. It does NOT permit a physical MERIDIAN jump: at B=1 the original finite-chart formulas give K=-1,e=f=0 and G=-I, independently of that position. Based conjugation preserves -I. All the other crossing, wire and turn relations therefore glue physical meridian matrices through this projector just as through an ordinary wire. They define a representation of the SAME one-component knot group, even though the auxiliary position need not be periodic at that wire. One meridian is -I by (18); every knot meridian is conjugate to it, up to inversion. Hence ALL meridians are -I. In these finite charts every physical clock equals one. The original direct five-symbol crossing regulator is consequently zero at EACH crossing: its arguments are A=B=C_plus=C_minus=1. The nine-symbol value has the same limit whenever the specified joint actual graph limit exists. Cups, caps, Gaussians and the retained projector marks add no Bloch terms. Equation (16) proves Im W=0 (19) for every such stationary physical-projector stratum. This extends the local geometric exclusion of Section 8 to a value bound for finite physical-wall stationary blocks, despite their omitted clock-normal equations. It is not an analytic bound on the sum or mass of those blocks. Auxiliary fusion clocks, escaping positions, arbitrary cleared-graph branches and bulk indices j_N/N not tending to 0 or 1 remain excluded. Nor does (19) apply to an unidentified TRANSFER-index endpoint: its zero-transfer Cartan-flip branch need not force any physical meridian to be central. Those boundaries require their own exact source grouping.

title: Original crossing-circle sources and the complete twist-filling packet
text: # Original crossing-circle sources and the complete twist-filling packet 29 October 2026. A crossing-circle source can be calculated from the ORIGINAL mixed universal crossings and pivotal trace. Its complete-color operator is generally noninvertible and is nilpotent at even levels. Therefore a fixed N-colored augmented-link scalar is not, by itself, an all-port filling state for the original knot. The constructive replacement is the COMPLETE auxiliary-color packet. Its N loop operators form a polynomial basis including all confluent Casimir jets. The explicit Fourier--Hermite kernel then reconstructs each original full-twist block at polynomial coefficient cost. This gives an exact arbitrary-width source formula over mixed-color augmented diagrams, with the original marked cut unchanged. It does not prove a nonzero geometric coefficient at a fully augmented base, or transport such a coefficient through long fillings. Those require the selected mixed-color base period, not just its operator basis or a positive geometric reference chain. ## 1. The literal encircling operator Put N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^-1. The two physical targets are the original complete V_d heads. Their Casimir is Omega=F12 Ecal12+q K12+q^-1 K12^-1, Ecal=rho^2 E. For 1<=j<=N let A_j be the ordinary j-dimensional highest-weight auxiliary module, with H weights j-1-2a, 0<=a<j. Use the literal mixed universal R, including q^(H tensor H/2), and close the auxiliary strand with g_j=K_j^(1-N). There is NO new 1/j or 1/N in this auxiliary trace. The main modified/marked source stays where it was. Define L_j on the two physical targets by the actual block-braiding monodromy. With the auxiliary strand initially in position3 this is the typed braid [2,1,1,2], followed by the original pivotal trace of strand3. Intermediate crossings use their actual changing strand dimensions. Write T_n(z)=2cos(n theta) and U_n(z/2)=sin((n+1)theta)/sin(theta) when z=2cos(theta). These are polynomial conventions: T_0=2,T_1=z,T_(n+1)=zT_n-T_(n-1), U_0=1,U_1=z,U_(n+1)=zU_n-U_(n-1). Then the exact all-input circle identity is L_j=(-1)^(j-1) U_(j-1)(Omega/2). (1) The notation U_n(Omega/2) means the displayed recurrence U_1=Omega. In particular L_1=I and L_2=-Omega. ### Independent proof, including the root specialization First work at generic q with ordinary finite highest-weight modules and the standard pivotal trace K_j. Block braiding is obtained by the actual coproduct identities of the finite universal R, proved coefficientwise in the [ordinary-color audit](actual_ordinary_color_comparison_audit.md).
