title: The actual cut residue and its principal density
text: # The actual cut residue and its principal density Research note, 26 October 2026. The previous turn identified a commutative regular-meridian torsor and its cut two-form. Here we identify its logarithmic cut co-source directly in the original finite boundary pairing. We also factor both original crossing amplitudes into a mixed-Hessian determinant and an explicit momentum coboundary. The latter cancels along every closed braid. These are uniform identities, independent of alternatingness or a particular knot example. The actual quantum period is unchanged. These statements do not yet transport its internal relative class to a geometric triangulation or establish its regulator norm. ## 1. The unchanged finite cut is a logarithmic residue Use the [marked braid boundary](marked_braid_holonomy.md): Q is primitive of order N, F_a=(Q;Q)_a, and the basis w_a=v_a/F_a has the constant input vector psi=1 and covector phi=(1/N)sum_a. Let C_N=k[A]/(A^N-1), f_tilde(A)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) f_j A^j. The tilde denotes the unique representative of degree <N, not an arbitrary Laurent representative. Root orthogonality proves the following exact identities: phi(f)=(1/N)sum_(a=0)^(N-1) f(Q^a)=f_0 =Res_(A=0) f_tilde(A) dA/A =-Res_(A=infinity) f_tilde(A) dA/A. (1.1) Equivalently put omega_N=A^(N-1)dA/(A^N-1) =(1/N)dlog(A^N-1). Every root has residue 1/N. The sum of its finite root residues after multiplication by f_tilde is (1.1). At infinity omega_N=dA/A+O(A^(-N-1))dA; since deg f_tilde<N the correction has zero residue there. This gives an independent residue-theorem proof of (1.1). The normalized source projector is also explicit. If (S f)(A)=f(QA), then e=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1) S^j=psi phi, e^2=e, Tr(e)=1, phi C psi=Tr(e C) (1.2) for every linear operator C. For the actual zero-framed knot cut C=F_N(M)I, so this is exactly the reduced ADO evaluation, with its original normalization. No new state has been defined by the residue formula. ## 2. The cut-coordinate change retains the entire pole divisor For M!=0 make the rational boundary coordinate change A=M/(M+s), s=M(A^(-1)-1). This is also the cut-coordinate map on the classical critical chart in [the regular-meridian note](regular_meridian_centralizer.md). The finite identity here is a change of boundary coordinate; it does not define a finite-q framing variable r. Direct substitution gives omega_N=M^N ds/[(M+s)((M+s)^N-M^N)], (2.1) beta=dlog A=-ds/(M+s). The N simple roots are s_a=M(Q^(-a)-1), with residues 1/N. The additional pole s=-M has residue -1. Infinity is regular for omega_N. The representative f_tilde(A(s)) is regular at infinity and has pole order at most N-1 at s=-M. Hence (1.1) becomes phi(f)=-Res_(s=-M) f_tilde(M/(M+s)) beta = Res_(s=infinity) f_tilde(M/(M+s)) beta. (2.2) This is an exact finite-level pairing with the same beta which contracts the classical framing two-form. It identifies the cut co-source, rather than replacing omega_N by beta on a fixed cycle: beta has a pole at infinity, while omega_N does not. Pole divisors and representatives remain part of the comparison. At completeness A=1 corresponds to s=0, which is excluded from the invertible framing chart Delta=s!=0. Its cut contribution is exactly f(1)/N. Deleting that point without its source changes the pairing. Its coefficient follows from partial_s[(M+s)^N-M^N]|_(s=0)=N M^(N-1). For the actual contracted cut C psi=F_N(M)1, each cut point contributes F_N(M)/N. These internal state indices are distinct from the ordinary meridian-color evaluations. In particular no polynomial bound on ordinary colors bounds this deleted internal contribution. It is permissible to change the cut presentation explicitly: any weights w_a with sum w_a=1 give sum_a w_a (C psi)_a=F_N(M). (2.3) For example averaging the N-1 points A!=1 with normalization 1/(N-1) preserves the invariant exactly. Its boundary source and its stationary presentation change; (2.3) alone does not prove that a particular geometric normal block survives. ## 3. Canonical representatives carry a normal source The representative condition in (1.1) is indispensable: A^N and 1 agree in C_N but have different residues against dA/A at zero if used without reduction. The section obeys A f_tilde - (Af)_tilde =f_(N-1)(A^N-1). (3.1) Thus multiplication has a specified boundary carry. More generally in the flat algebra C_U=k[U,A]/(A^N-U), write f *_U g=sum_(i,j<N) f_i g_j U^floor((i+j)/N) A^((i+j) mod N). Its first normal product at U=1 is exactly partial_U(f *_U g)|_1 =sum_(i+j>=N) f_i g_j A^(i+j-N). (3.2) Let D=A partial_A on the canonical representatives and reduce products at U=1. Checking each monomial pair gives D(f *_1 g)-(Df)*_1 g-f *_1(Dg) =-N partial_U(f *_U g)|_1. (3.3) This makes precise why an ordinary derivation cannot simply be imposed after cyclic specialization. On the full family, the vector field A partial_A+N U partial_U preserves A^N-U; at U=1 the separate normal term remains necessary. The formulas are compatible with, but do not replace, the previous actual carry lattices and meridian normal jets. The cut-point coefficient 1/N and the earlier peripheral inverse-power correction 1/u_N(M) are distinct factors. Their product is the already computed paired source scalar Gamma_N=1/[N u_N(M)] from the [cyclic source calculation](cyclic_source_connection_and_resonant_flags.md). Identifying these scalar evaluations does not identify the corresponding full quantum modules. ## 4. Both actual crossing amplitudes have a canonical factorization Use the actual balanced coefficients and their principal transport amplitudes in [the normal-period note](actual_geometric_normal_period.md). Write Y=M^2=x^2 at the classical symbol. Then a_+^2=AB (1-BC)(1-Y/A)/[(1-B)(1-C)(1-YC/A)], a_-^2=C/(AB) (1-AC)(1-Y/B)/[(1-A)(1-C)(1-YC/B)]. These are variable principal amplitudes. Their fixed product normalizations, root phases and boundary 1/N are retained separately, exactly as in that note. Put a=log A, b=log B, c=log C, tau=a+b. For a positive crossing the first output coordinate is u=b+c; for a negative crossing it is u=b-c. View its generating phase S as a function of a,u at fixed tau. Its mixed Hessian is V_+=partial_a partial_u S_+=1/(1-C), V_-=partial_a partial_u S_-=C/(1-C). (4.1) These follow by differentiation, with no stationary equation for the transfer imposed at an individual crossing. For example the positive directional vectors in (a,b,c) are (1,-1,1),(0,0,1); the negative ones are (1,-1,-1),(0,0,-1). Applying them to the actual Hessian gives (4.1). Let p_1,p_2 be the input balanced momenta and p'_1,p'_2 the output momenta. Their exact classical shift relations are p'_2/p_1=BC/x * (1-Y/A)/(1-YC/A), p'_1/p_2=A/(Cx) * (1-BC)/(1-B) (+), p'_2/p_1=x/B * (1-AC)/(1-A), p'_1/p_2=x/A * (1-Y/B)/(1-YC/B) (-). Multiplying these two relations and cancelling factors proves a_+^2=Y V_+ (p'_1 p'_2)/(p_1 p_2), a_-^2=Y^(-1) V_- (p'_1 p'_2)/(p_1 p_2). (4.2) Thus the departures from the mixed-Hessian half-density are an explicit momentum coboundary and the color factor. This is an identity from the original coefficients, not an assumption about a semiclassical quantization. ## 5. The momentum coboundary cancels for every knot braid Take a b-strand braid of writhe w on its marked critical correspondence. Multiply (4.2) over all crossings. Every internal momentum cancels between an output and its next input. At a closed strand the two remaining momenta agree; at the specified constant cut both are one. Therefore product_crossings a_sign^2 =Y^w product_crossings V_sign. (5.1) The original pivot and zero-framing variable amplitude is M^(b-1-w)/product_(j=2)^b A_j. Consequently the complete variable amplitude has the identity a_beta^2=(product_(j=2)^b K_j^2) product_crossings V_sign, K_j=x/A_j. (5.2) This is uniform in the braid word and retains the actual pivotal factor. Square-root signs and base-only phase lines remain marked; an identity of squares does not choose them. ## 6. The same pivotal factor corrects the ambient holonomy volume On a fixed-trace SL_2 conjugacy class write G=[K e;Kf K^(-1)+ef], K+K^(-1)+ef=t, nu=dK wedge de/e. The form nu is conjugation invariant. One proof regards the class as the quadratic surface in the three traceless matrix coordinates: conjugation preserves its equation and has determinant one, so its residue two-form is invariant. This can also be verified on upper, lower and diagonal generators. Balanced phase coordinates have A=x/K, p=e x/(1-xK), omega=dlog A wedge dlog p=-nu/K. (6.1) The prefix Gauss transformation to marked holonomies is H_j=B_(j-1)^(-1) G_j B_(j-1). It is triangular in j. On its diagonal it is a fixed conjugation, preserving nu. Hence wedge_j nu(G_j)=wedge_j nu(H_j). For P=H_b...H_1, Gauss multiplication gives P_11=product_j K_j. Combining these identities yields (product_(j=2)^b K_j) wedge_j omega_j =(-1)^b/K_1 wedge_j nu(H_j). (6.2) The right side is invariant under simultaneous conjugation centralizing the first meridian: its K_1 is fixed and all nu(H_j) are invariant. On the cut critical chart K_1=-(M+s). This gives exactly the residual (M+s)^(-1) factor in the centralizer/cut form. It supplies a general geometric explanation for that divisor, beyond its earlier figure-eight check. Equation (6.2) is an identity of ambient top forms. It has not yet been promoted to an identification of the reduced Gaussian determinant line or the actual internal relative cycle. That reduction must retain its kernel, dual source, square-root phase and the normal terms in Section 3. ### An invariant finite-dimensional complex for the reduction There is a natural algebraic candidate for its determinant line. Let X be the product of the b noncentral fixed-trace meridian conjugacy classes, F the Hurwitz braid map, and rho a fixed point. Write P=H_b...H_1 and use left trivialization for its product derivative. There is a complex 0 -> sl_2 --a--> T_rho X --D--> T_rho X --m--> sl_2 -> 0, a(xi)=([xi,H_j])_j, D=dF-I, m(v)=dP(v)P^(-1). (6.3) Both compositions vanish: equivariance gives D a=0 and product preservation gives m D=0. These identities hold for every braid and every fixed representation. If rho is irreducible, a is injective and m is surjective. For the latter claim, use the nondegenerate trace pairing on sl_2. An element annihilating m first commutes with H_b. The preceding term then makes it commute with H_(b-1), and induction gives commutation with every H_j. Its trace zero common centralizer is zero. This proves surjectivity. Assume additionally ker D=im a, meaning that the fixed-trace representation is infinitesimally rigid modulo conjugation. Rank-nullity then makes (6.3) acyclic. This is an explicit regularity hypothesis; it is not supplied by this complex or silently inferred from a reduced set of fixed points. Choose columns V completing a to a basis of T_rho X and a right inverse W of m. Then D V,W also form a basis, and the scalar determinant ratio is T_beta(rho)=det[a,V]/det[D V,W]. (6.4) The same tangent-coordinate basis is used in both middle terms. Changing V multiplies numerator and denominator by the same determinant; changing W adds D V columns. Thus (6.4) is independent of those choices. It is invariant under simultaneous conjugation: d(conjugation) changes both middle bases equally, and Ad(g) changes the two sl_2 bases equally. It is a rational nonzero scalar on the regular representation locus and descends along the framing torsor. This constructs an invariant torsion directly from the linearized actual holonomy map. Identifying its determinant line with the Gaussian reduction in (5.2), including the cut co-source, remains a separate required calculation. No equality with an established topological Reidemeister torsion or with the selected quantum period is asserted. The subsequent [uniform Markov reduction](pointed_markov_reduction.md) now proves invariance of this scalar under braid conjugation, braid relations and either stabilization, on the stated regular representation locus. Its proof gives explicit chain maps and an acyclic rank-two summand. The actual geometric Gaussian complex has its own explicit rank-one reduction under the same move, with determinant canceled by the original coefficient amplitude. A full comparison of the two determinant lines is still required. ## 7. What remains for the selected period The finite cut co-source is now exactly the logarithmic residue in (2.2). The original principal coefficients have the uniform determinant/coboundary form (4.2), and their pivotal correction gives the invariant ambient form (6.2). These remove an arbitrary choice of boundary measure from the proposed torsor comparison. The next reduction must send the actual internal class, with its normal carry, to the centralizer contraction of that form. At M=1 the framing two-form is exact on the specified chart in ordinary de Rham cohomology; a relative or regularized source is essential. The residue normalization alone does not prove this pushforward or nonvanishing on the geometric block. The selected regulator norm across levels, and thus the original Kashaev volume conjecture, remain unproved. ## 8. Coverage and verification Root traces, residues, polynomial remainder carries and mixed-Hessian half-densities are existing algebra and semiclassical constructions; no novelty is claimed for them. The identities here concern the fixed actual boundary and coefficient conventions. For adjacent existing scope, [McPhail-Snyder, 2005.01133](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.01133) relates a quantum holonomy construction at q=i to twisted Burau representations and nonabelian torsion. [The holonomy-braiding paper, 2509.02354](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02354) advertises a four-dilogarithm factorization. Only their abstracts were consulted for coverage; neither proof is used here, and neither statement is taken to identify the present selected geometric period at all levels. [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_cut_density.py) checks the exact residue and normal-carry identities, both original principal amplitudes, the ambient volume factors, and the original finite cut matrices. [Results](../experiments/actual_cut_density_results.json).

title: The original quantum period has an explicit convergent cut cycle
text: # The original quantum period has an explicit convergent cut cycle 28 October 2026. The whole-word cyclic-dilogarithm construction now admits an exact deformation from its marked small circles to radial branch cuts. By choosing the opposite-root realization of every u factor, all factors are inverse cyclic dilogarithms. Every cut integral converges at both ends, with no omitted contribution at infinity. The resulting cycle and its nonzero local-system jump coefficients are specified for the ORIGINAL quantum state. This is not yet a proof that their full contraction has a nonzero geometric critical contribution. In particular the complex integrand is not made positive by the sine weights below. ## 1. The actual marked covers Let N>=2, Q=exp(2pi i/N), and epsilon=+1 or -1. On the t-plane put D_epsilon(t)=product_(k=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^(epsilon k)t)^(k/N), A_epsilon(t)=D_epsilon(t)^-1. The branches start with D_epsilon(0)=1. Their algebraic cover is y^N=product_(k=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^(epsilon k)t)^k. The factor with k=1 shows that the cover is connected: its divisor valuation is one, so the defining right side cannot be a p-th power for any prime p dividing N. Equivalently the local monodromy about that root generates all N sheets. We use its normalization. The actual first N Taylor coefficients of A_epsilon are c_(epsilon,a)=(-1)^a Q^(epsilon a(a-1)/2) /(Q^epsilon;Q^epsilon)_a, 0<=a<N. (1) This follows from the logarithmic coefficient identity for D and the finite Euler inversion. In particular, for T^N=0, the corresponding v polynomial is exactly v_(epsilon,N)(T)=(1/(2pi i)) integral_(|t|=rho) A_epsilon(t)(tI-T)^-1 dt, (2) where 0<rho<1 and the small circle is lifted from the marked sheet. The resolvent is a finite Laurent polynomial in t^-1. No spectral choice or unknown knot normalization is involved. Every original u factor has a realization of this form as well: u_(Q,N)(T)=v_(Q^-1,N)(Q^-1 T). (3) Indeed (Q^-1;Q^-1)_a=(-1)^a Q^(-a(a+1)/2)(Q;Q)_a. The auxiliary root orientation changes in (3); the physical knot parameter Q, its source and its Gaussian factors do not change. The [whole-word construction](actual_whole_word_cyclic_dilog_resolvent_period.md) also realizes every factorial diagonal by an inverse-D coefficient functional. Thus it uses only (2) and the nonnegative coefficient orders in Section 3 below. ## 2. Exact boundary values and the oriented cut identity The distinct cuts are L_(epsilon,j)={Q^(-epsilon j)r : 1<=r<infinity}, 1<=j<N. Their complement contains zero and carries the marked branch. Define for r>1 h_(epsilon,j)(r)=(r-1)^(-j/N) product_(k!=j)(1-r Q^(epsilon(k-j)))^(-k/N). (4) For each k!=j, continue its logarithm radially from r=0. It never crosses its zero on this path; equivalently use the corresponding principal logarithm. The remaining real power in (4) is positive. Let + denote the side obtained by a small counterclockwise rotation of the outward ray, and - the clockwise side. The j-th factor then has logarithms log(r-1)-i pi and log(r-1)+i pi, respectively. Hence (A_epsilon)_+=exp(+pi i j/N)h_(epsilon,j), (A_epsilon)_-=exp(-pi i j/N)h_(epsilon,j), (A_epsilon)_+-(A_epsilon)_- =2i sin(pi j/N)h_(epsilon,j). (5) The sign is independent of epsilon: both sides refer to the actual complex orientation of the t-plane. Let a>=0. Cauchy's theorem on the plane with the rays and a small zero disk removed gives [t^a]A_epsilon(t) =sum_(j=1)^(N-1) sin(pi j/N)/pi * Q^(epsilon j a) *integral_1^infinity h_(epsilon,j)(r)r^(-a-1)dr. (6) To check the orientation, a positive contour around an outward slit runs inward on its + side and outward on its - side. The small zero circle equals the large outer contour minus those slit contours, which gives the + minus - jump in (6). All limits in this deformation are justified at fixed N. Near the j-th endpoint the integrand is O((r-1)^(-j/N)), which is integrable because j<N. At infinity A_epsilon(t)=O(|t|^(-(N-1)/2)) on every slit sector. The outer arc integral with t^(-a-1) is therefore O(R^(-a-(N-1)/2)) and tends to zero. The finitely many sectors have fixed marks. This argument does not require a single-valued branch on an entire large base circle, including when infinity ramifies. The small endpoint circles also tend to zero. On the normalized cover the apparent endpoint singularity is even more transparent. Set g=gcd(N,j), t-t_j=s^(N/g). Then A_epsilon is a unit times s^(-j/g), and its product with dt has order (N-j)/g-1>=0. Thus the lifted differential is holomorphic at that ramification point. The slit description simply records the marked combination of its sheet paths. For N=2, (6) gives [t^a](1+t)^(-1/2) =(-1)^a/pi * integral_1^infinity (r-1)^(-1/2)r^(-a-1)dr, including the value one for a=0 and -1/2 for a=1. This checks both the orientation and the full normalization. ## 3. Matrix transport and the whole original source Expand the finite resolvent in (2) and apply (6) coefficientwise. For every T^N=0, exactly v_(epsilon,N)(T) =sum_(j=1)^(N-1) sin(pi j/N)/pi *integral_1^infinity h_(epsilon,j)(r) (rI-Q^(epsilon j)T)^-1 dr. (7) This retains all original finite-head walls inside the NILPOTENT matrix T. It does not replace T by an invertible Laurent shift. There is no pole of this resolvent on r>=1. The same proof applies to a matrix coefficient source sum_(a=0)^(N-1)B_a t^(-a-1): its cut kernel is sum_a B_a Q^(epsilon j a)r^(-a-1). Apply (7) in the original order to every factor of the full 9m-variable construction for an m-crossing braid. The Gaussian diagonals, original caps, pivots, Cartan scalars, framing and peripheral line are retained. The original scalar becomes a sum over j_1,...,j_(9m) in {1,...,N-1} of integrals over [1,infinity)^(9m). Its scalar jump weight is product_l sin(pi j_l/N)/pi, (8) and its matrix/rational source is precisely the unchanged ordered network with the cut kernels of (7). The upper endpoint and infinity estimates above dominate every finite matrix entry by a product of integrable one-variable functions at fixed N. Thus Fubini and multilinearity justify the whole substitution, not only its isolated scalar atoms. This is an exact source-preserving global cycle deformation for every original word. It does not assume geometricity, positivity of an ideal triangulation, a nonvanishing Kashaev value, or a large-level asymptotic. All original normalization factors remain in the original source; no factor is chosen to fit a volume limit. ## 4. What this settles about cycle selection, and what it does not The marked quantum cycle is now a completely specified convergent combination of sheet paths on actual cyclic-dilogarithm covers. Every local jump coefficient in (8) is nonzero. For indices whose j_l/N stay in a compact subinterval of (0,1), these coefficients are bounded above and below independently of N. Even over all indices their loss is at worst polynomial at fixed braid length. These statements control ONLY the local-system jump coefficients. The remaining functions h, the ordered matrix source and their full contraction are complex and may cancel. The number of cut summands grows with N. None of these facts proves that a marked geometric critical point lies on the selected deformation, that its full derived coefficient is nonzero, or that the sum of all other pieces has a smaller exponential rate. The task is therefore no longer to invent a quantum cycle or to guess its local branch weights. The remaining comparison must carry this explicit whole cut cycle to the positive geometric chart, preserving its matrix source and all branch orientations. The positive-chart maximum and the actual-atom analytic regions are available inputs; a global identification with the marked Bloch regulator period is still unproved. [Numerical sign and coefficient audit](../experiments/audit_cyclic_dilog_hankel_cycle.py). The Cauchy deformation and estimates above, rather than those finite diagnostics, prove (6)-(8) for all N. ## 5. Exact radial localization and a whole-word bound on infinity escape The radial variables in this ACTUAL cycle have a uniform bound, not merely fixed-N convergence. Put u=j/N, g_(epsilon,j)(r)=(r-1)^u h_(epsilon,j)(r), G_j=|g_(epsilon,j)(1)|, C_j=(N-1)/4-u/2. The endpoint magnitude G_j is independent of epsilon. For r>1 and |w|=r the elementary identity d_(Log r) Log|1-w| =Re[w/(w-1)] =1/2+(r^2-1)/(2|1-w|^2)>1/2 applies to every non-endpoint factor of g. Consequently |g_(epsilon,j)(r)|<=G_j r^(-C_j), |h_(epsilon,j)(r)|<=G_j (r-1)^(-u)r^(-C_j). (9) Here C_j>=c_N:=(N-1)(N-2)/(4N)>=0. Euler's beta integral gives the exact normalization sin(pi*u)/pi * integral_1^infinity (r-1)^(-u) dr/r=1. Thus for EVERY nonnegative coefficient order a and R>=1, sin(pi*u)/pi * integral_1^infinity |h_(epsilon,j)(r)|r^(-a-1)dr <= G_j, sin(pi*u)/pi * integral_R^infinity |h_(epsilon,j)(r)|r^(-a-1)dr <=G_j R^(-C_j). (10) This controls all cuts, including indices approaching either end of the index range. No lower bound on a jump weight is needed. The endpoint weight is itself explicit: G_j=|(Q;Q)_j|/N^(j/N+1/2). (11) For a direct verification put L_l=Log|1-Q^l|. Reindex k-j modulo N in the product defining g(1), retaining the absent k=0 factor with coefficient zero. Use sum_(l=1)^(N-1)L_l=Log N, sum_(l=1)^(N-1)l L_l=(N/2)Log N, L_(N-l)=L_l. It follows that Log G_j=-(j/N+1/2)Log N +sum_(l=N-j)^(N-1)L_l, which is (11). Thus the endpoint is an ORIGINAL quantum-factorial weight, with its complete polynomial normalization retained. For the full all-inverse construction set s=9m. At |M|=1 the [actual rational-source bound](actual_whole_word_cyclic_dilog_resolvent_period.md) is |R_(beta,N)(t)|<=N^(b-1+6m) product_l |t_l|^(-1), |t_l|>=1. (12) Its proof uses the literal truncated shifts, unitary root Gaussian and pivotal diagonals, and the original averaged source. It does not absorb the external dimension or framing line. Apply (10) variable by variable to the absolute value of the whole cut integral, and use a union bound for the s radial variables. If P_tail(R) denotes the contribution with max_l r_l>=R, |P_tail(R)| <=|chi_(beta,N)| s N^(b-1+6m) R^(-c_N) (sum_(j=1)^(N-1)G_j)^s. (13) The same bound without s R^(-c_N) bounds the full absolute integral. This is a bound on the original whole source; it is not a termwise claim about a substituted positive knot model. Write J(v)=integral_0^v Log(2sin(pi*t))dt. The uniform endpoint-aware factorial estimate already proved in [the full-atom note](full_euler_atom_dilog_and_endpoint_regions.md) gives Log G_j=N J(j/N)+O(Log N) uniformly for 1<=j<N. Its maximum occurs at v=5/6 and is max J=Lambda(pi/6)/pi=v_3/(2pi), where v_3 is the volume of a regular ideal tetrahedron. At M=1 the original external line chi has polynomial size. Since c_N/N tends to 1/4, (13) proves the unconditional whole-word escape estimate limsup_(N->infinity) (1/N)Log|P_tail(R)| <=s v_3/(2pi)-(1/4)Log R. (14) In particular any fixed R>exp(4s v_3/(2pi)) makes this whole infinity tail exponentially small in ABSOLUTE size. The required R depends on the fixed word, not on N. Thus escape to infinity can be excluded as a competing positive exponential contribution in this representation. For smaller radial collars, (13) controls the tail relative to the stated endpoint ABSOLUTE envelope. It does not imply localization on an O(1/N) collar relative to the ACTUAL selected period: cancellation may make that period much smaller than the envelope. The angular/source coupling and a nonzero geometric contribution remain unresolved. None of (9)-(14) replaces that remaining lower-bound theorem. [Radial and endpoint audit](../experiments/audit_actual_cut_radial_localization.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_cut_radial_localization_results.json). The subsequent [bulk radial theorem](full_cut_geometric_coupling.md) evaluates each original coefficient moment with an explicit nonzero Gamma symbol, uniformly in the actual coefficient order. The [cyclic sewing comparison](exact_quantum_quad_source_transport.md) instead splits the nilpotent transfers into cyclic resolvents and mandatory boundary terms. For that split representation, use the [regularized cut rule](cyclic_sewing_regularized_cut_cycle.md), which retains its new endpoint finite parts and cyclic-pole residues. The ordinary unsplit Hankel formula must not be applied to its terms without those corrections.

# An exact scalar cyclic-dilogarithm network for the original knot source The subsequent [continuous Gaussian theorem](actual_continuous_gaussian_cyclic_network.md) completes this construction: its exact original-source period has ordinary Gaussian weights and no finite Gaussian scalar kernel either. The intermediate construction below retains the finite Gaussian while proving the cyclic/Hardy support and initial-cycle identities. 28 October 2026. For every actual signed braid word, the scalar Euler/Gaussian Cauchy representation can be replaced by one using **the literature norm-one cyclic dilogarithm, its inverse, ordinary Hardy Cauchy kernels, and the full finite marked Gaussian**. All finite Dirichlet numerators and all scalar finite Euler polynomials are absent from this presentation. The original period, including its source and peripheral/framing line, is exactly unchanged. This is an exact function-and-cycle representation, not a replacement of the invariant by a positive model or an asymptotic substitution. The initial cycle and every norm root are specified below. Moving that cycle to a geometric Rivin chain remains unproved. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_cyclic_hardy_dilog_network.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_cyclic_hardy_dilog_network_results.json) check the full literature normalization, nonzero added cyclic tails, both actual signed crossings, and sixteen original whole-word pivotal contractions. Exact rational radius chambers are checked independently of those finite-field identities. ## 1. Fix the literature normalization as a function Let $Q=e^{2\pi i/N}$, $N\ge2$. Use precisely the alternate literature cyclic dilogarithm from [four_cyclic_atoms.md](four_cyclic_atoms.md): $$ \mathcal V_N(t)= (1-t^N)^{(N-1)/(2N)} \prod_{\ell=1}^{N-1}(1-Q^\ell t)^{-\ell/N}, \qquad \mathcal U_N(t)=\mathcal V_N(t)^{-1}. 	ag{1} $$ Every power is the analytic branch equal to one at $t=0$. In particular the full factor $(1-t^N)^{(N-1)/(2N)}$ is retained. This is the normalized function $\mathfrak d_N$, not the unnormalized weighted product often denoted $D_N$. Even-level half roots use this same anchor. On $|t|<1$ its convergent logarithm is exactly $$ \log\mathcal V_N(t)= \sum_{\substack{m\ge1\N
mid m}}  rac{t^m}{m(Q^m-1)}. 	ag{2} $$ Indeed $\sum_{\ell=1}^{N-1}\ell Q^{\ell m} =N/(Q^m-1)$ at nonresonant degrees. At $m=Nk$ the norm factor in (1) cancels the resonant logarithm of the weighted product. Thus $$ \prod_{j=0}^{N-1}\mathcal V_N(Q^jt)=1 	ag{3} $$ on the anchored component. For the ACTUAL finite Euler polynomials $$ u_N(t)=\sum_{h=0}^{N-1}t^h/F_h,\quad v_N(t)=\sum_{h=0}^{N-1} (-1)^hQ^{h(h-1)/2}t^h/F_h, $$ comparison of their nilpotent logarithms gives $$ \mathcal U_N(t)-u_N(t)\in t^N\mathbb C[[t]],\qquad \mathcal V_N(t)-v_N(t)\in t^N\mathbb C[[t]]. 	ag{4} $$ This finite-jet observation alone is not a period theorem. The ordered support argument below proves where ALL the additional coefficients disappear in the actual source. ## 2. Three different support mechanisms Work on nonnegative polynomial heads and use the Hardy Cauchy kernel $K_+(t)=1/(1-t)$, as in [the exact Hardy replacement](actual_hardy_cauchy_network.md). Keep the original strict crossing order and original coefficients. ### Transfer atoms Before EVERY transfer in the strict actual crossing and boundary fusion words, both active indices lie in $0,\ldots,N-1$. For a transfer $J_-\otimes J_+$, every added power of order $h\ge N$ lowers the first index below zero. Hardy projection annihilates it. The reversed transfer has the same property on its second index. Therefore $$ \mathcal U_N(x^{-1}J_-\otimes J_+),\quad \mathcal V_N(x^{-1}J_-\otimes J_+) $$ act exactly as the original finite transfer atoms on these actual inputs. The infinite series terminates on each such input by its LOWERING head; no upper truncation is imposed. ### Reciprocal factorial diagonals The scalar kernel $u_N(z/w)$ is replaced by $\mathcal U_N(z/w)$ at $|z/w|<1$. It now has genuinely nonzero diagonal coefficients at indices above the original head. However, the active input of every reciprocal-factorial diagonal in the strict word is already in the head: - the initial second head of inverse fusion is in the head; - after its lowering transfer the first head is still in it; - in the final fusion, the central transfer has only lowered its second head. Thus none of the added diagonal coefficients is ever used. ### Positive factorial diagonals The actual factorial kernel is $$ \sum_{a=0}^{N-1}F_a t^a=N t^{N-1}v_N(Q/t). $$ Replace it by the full Laurent function $$ \mathcal F_N(t)=N t^{N-1}\mathcal V_N(Q/t), \qquad |t|>1. 	ag{5} $$ Its powers $t^a$ for $0\le a<N$ have exactly the original coefficients $F_a$. It has NO power $t^a$ with $a\ge N$. All added terms have $a<0$. In a diagonal Cauchy contraction, a term $t^a=(z/w)^a$ can pair only with input index $a$. Nonnegative polynomial inputs therefore do not see any of the added negative powers. Consequently (5), despite being a different scalar function, acts **exactly as the original finite factorial diagonal on all nonnegative polynomial inputs**. In particular it still kills every upper overflow. All factors $N$ and $t^{N-1}$ in (5) are retained. ## 3. The support induction is simultaneous, not a circular assumption Let $\mathcal F$ denote the operator represented by (5), and let $\mathcal F^{-}$ be the operator with scalar kernel $\mathcal U_N(z/w)$. On head inputs use the completed fusions $$  egin{split} \mathcal C&=\mathcal F_2\, \mathcal U_-(x)\,\mathcal F_1\,\mathcal F_2^{-},\ \overline{\mathcal C}&=\mathcal F_2\mathcal F_1^{-} \mathcal V_-(x)\,\mathcal F_2^{-}. \end{split} 	ag{6} $$ Starting from a head input, the first reciprocal diagonal in $\overline{\mathcal C}$ has a head input. Its transfer lowers the first index, so all added powers vanish and the first index remains in the head. The next reciprocal diagonal is therefore also exact. The last positive factorial kills any second-index overflow. This proves $$ \overline{\mathcal C}i=iC^{-1}. 	ag{7} $$ For $\mathcal C$, its first reciprocal diagonal is exact on a head second index. The positive factorial on head one enforces that head's support BEFORE the transfer. The transfer is then exactly finite, and the last positive factorial kills its possible second-head overflow. Moreover $\mathcal C$ kills any nonnegative input outside the head pair: an oversized first index is killed before transfer; an oversized second index can only increase before the final factorial kills it. Hence $\mathcal C=P\mathcal CP$ and $\mathcal Ci=iC$. The central transfer in either signed crossing receives a head input by (7); its added high powers vanish. Its possible first-head overflow is killed by $\mathcal C$. The full marked Gaussian is kept exactly as before. Therefore the two completed signed operators satisfy $$  oxed{\qquad \mathcal R_\pm i=iR_\pm. \qquad} 	ag{8} $$ The same proof applies to the typed unequal-color formula, using the original input/output fusions and its prescribed Euler argument. No common Cartan scalar is reset. By induction, for EVERY signed word, with any original finite-head coupons BETWEEN complete crossings, $$ \mathcal W( eta)i_b=i_bW( eta). 	ag{9} $$ This includes the full original source and Hopf Ward pairings. It does not authorize arbitrary insertions between factors inside (6), nor infer a source identity for an independently chosen cyclic/geometric sector. ## 4. A simultaneous, explicit initial radius chamber The scalar kernels in this representation are: $$  egin{array}{c|c} 	ext{factor}&	ext{active scalar function}\ \hline 	ext{transfer}& \mathcal U_N(x^{-1}w_j/w_i) 	ext{ or }\mathcal V_N(x^{-1}w_j/w_i)\ 	ext{reciprocal factorial}&\mathcal U_N(z_i/w_i)\ 	ext{positive factorial}& N(z_i/w_i)^{N-1}\mathcal V_N(Qw_i/z_i)\ 	ext{Gaussian}&\Gamma_{\pm,N}(z_i/w_i) \end{array} 	ag{10} $$ Every spectator contributes $K_+(z_j/w_j)$. Transfers also have Hardy kernels on their active heads. The complete finite Gaussian is retained, with its marked meridian powers and chirp; it is not replaced by a guessed Gaussian branch. Fix $0<ho<1$, for example $ho=1/16$, and a positive lower bound $\lambda$ for all active color moduli on the selected meridian chart. Insert one identity Hardy layer before EACH elementary factor. This preserves the exact polynomial operator. Let $R_j>0$ be the preceding output radii, $r_j$ the reset layer's output radii, and $s_j$ the factor's output radii. The finite set of required inequalities is $$  egin{array}{c|l} 	ext{reset}&r_j/R_j<ho\quad	ext{for all }j\ 	ext{transfer}&r_j/r_i<ho\lambda,\quad s_h/r_h<ho\quad	ext{for all }h\ 	ext{reciprocal factorial on }i& s_h/r_h<ho\quad	ext{for all }h\ 	ext{positive factorial on }i& r_i/s_i<ho,\quad s_h/r_h<ho\ (h
e i)\ 	ext{Gaussian on }i& s_i>0,\quad s_h/r_h<ho\ (h
e i). \end{array} 	ag{11} $$ They always have a simultaneous solution. Inductively put $r_h=ho R_h/2$. Before a transfer, decrease its numerator radius further, if needed, to $$ r_j\le rac{ho\lambda}{2}r_i. $$ Put $s_h=ho r_h/2$ except at an active positive factorial, where set $s_i=2r_i/ho$, and at an active Gaussian, where set $s_i=r_i$. Every inequality in (11) is then strict. The construction proceeds forward in word time; there is no terminal-to-initial Hardy inequality. All cyclic atom arguments are in $|t|<ho$, so their branches are exactly those of (1). The reflected factorial is expanded at its specified infinity sector. Every scalar series is uniformly absolutely convergent on the compact product tori. Termwise constant-term extraction and composition are justified. Thus the operator proof yields a genuine compact Cauchy-cycle identity, not only a formal equality of jets. For a fixed meridian compact chart with nonzero colors, these radii and strict margins can be chosen independently of $N$. The number of reset layers and integration variables depends on the fixed word and bridge count, not on $N$. ## 5. The original fixed charged period Use the existing full fused-plat source $$ P_{ eta,N}=\chi_{ eta,N}N^{1-k} \langle e_{m out},B_ eta e_{m in}angle, $$ with its specified $(d,0)$ input pairs, $(0,d)$ ordinary output pairs and $(d,0)$ marked output pair. The full-word Ward corner is used only after assembly, as in its original proof. Expand $B_ eta$ into the actual factors, replace them by (10), and insert the reset identities above. If the resulting scalar kernels are $\mathcal K_\ell$, the same ORIGINAL period is exactly $$  oxed{\quad P_{ eta,N}=\chi_{ eta,N}N^{1-k} \operatorname{CT} (z^0)^{a_{m in}}(z^{L})^{-a_{m out}} \prod_{\ell=1}^{L} \mathcal K_\ell(z^\ell,z^{\ell-1}). \quad} 	ag{12} $$ Its contours are the product circles just constructed, with the anchored lifts from (1). All original peripheral, Cartan, pivot and framing factors are included exactly once. The equality holds at all primitive levels, even or composite, and in the original root-meridian family. Consequently any specified root-specialized quantum A-operator annihilating that original meridian period also annihilates (12), with its full peripheral factors. This is equality of the selected function, not a new assertion identifying an operator's classical symbol with the geometric A-polynomial. There are no scalar finite $u_N/v_N$ truncations and no finite Dirichlet numerator factors in (12). This does not erase boundary information: it specifies which global functions and initial cycle reproduce that information. Their norm divisors and matched residue/branch corrections must be retained in any subsequent contour transport. The integer source charge is unchanged: total plat degree is $k(N-1)$, and after the ordinary caps the remaining pair has $D+1=N$. That is the actual cap charge. Equation (12) does not identify an unassigned geometric Pachner edge with that class. ### An exact internal three-index charge is already available There is also a genuine internal affine charge in this particular network. In (5), a nonnegative head index $a$ and the selected cyclic Taylor index $r$ satisfy exactly $$ a+r=N-1,\qquad a+r+1=N. 	ag{13} $$ The $+1$ is forced by the original reflected monomial $t^{N-1}$, not chosen by a flattening convention. For an actual fusion coefficient write $$ h=a-u=v-b,\qquad r_1=N-1-a,\qquad r_2=N-1-v. $$ The two positive-factorial kernels in that fusion then give $$  oxed{\quad (u+1)+h+r_1=N,\qquad (b+1)+h+r_2=N. \quad} 	ag{14} $$ All entries are nonnegative, and the first entry of each triple is positive. Interior routes with $h,r_i>0$ give strictly positive triples. The inverse fusion retains the second equation, from its positive output factorial. Thus actual fusion-network clocks can form an exact three-index charge-one sector, with its original affine shift. This is a more specific dictionary than total-degree conservation alone. It does not yet identify either triple in (14) with the three angles around the last geometric Pachner edge. Such an identification must come from the typed five-term/source map, not from renaming these index variables. The remaining conjectural step is therefore genuinely global: transport this marked scalar cyclic-dilogarithm/Gaussian cycle to the positive ideal geometric chain, with all norm divisors, compatible root frames and original source charges retained, and prove its geometric coefficient and dominance. No such transport or volume limit is inferred from the exact identity (12). In the stronger continuous version just linked, the Gaussian is also an ordinary integral over a specified fibered Cauchy cycle. Joint absolute convergence and uniform initial-cycle leading symbols are proved there. The remaining global-cycle statement is unchanged; a finite Gaussian endpoint sector is no longer an unresolved part of the scalar representation.

text: # The primitive collar of the actual deformed circle pattern 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. The deformed marked circle pattern supplies the flags that the limiting source quadratic loses at a two-line triangle. This note calculates its ORIGINAL ordered crossing-disk sidepairing, including the primitive meridian, half twist and selected eigenflag. The result uses the specified sidepairing, not the product of two shaded reflections. Global representation assembly and the full regulator identification remain separate. ## 1. Keep the original order and corners Use the actual labeled pattern of [the marked reconstruction](actual_marked_deformed_circle_pattern.md). At one matching edge its input triangle is (x,b,y), and its output triangle is (x,c,y); the letters denote the curvatures of their actual white circles. First calculate a finite-circle model with the specified side signs. Section 5 verifies the signs and limits for the actual marked pattern; positivity of the radii alone does NOT fix those signs. Put delta=1/2-mu, s=sin(pi delta), c0=cos(pi delta), A=x+y, D=A^2-4xy s^2, T_b=sqrt[bA+xy+b^2s^2], B_b=A+2bs^2, E_b=B_b+2sT_b, and similarly for the middle circle c. Roots are positive at complete positive data and continued holomorphically near delta=0. Thus E_b(delta)E_b(-delta)=D, R0=E_b E_c/D. (1) These are precisely the continuant roots and channel ratio of the [original coupled source](actual_whole_source_coupled_face_difference_system.md), with input b and output c, including its original beta and forced polynomial normalization. Write r_f for reflection in white circle f in this paragraph only. The actual prefix convention is explicitly proved in [the original white-prefix dictionary](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md), section 3: A_in=r_b r_x, B_in=r_y r_b, P=B_in A_in=r_y r_x, A_out=r_c r_x, B_out=r_y r_c. (2) It is not the reversed product r_x r_y. The original corner labels are C1=x tangent b, C2=b tangent y, C0=x tangent c, C3=c tangent y. The actual even disk glues the shaded b-side to the c-side by C1->C0 and C2->C3, as in [the labeled cut quotient](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md), section 4, equation(3). These corners, not an unlabeled metric rectangle, fix the sidepairing used below. ## 2. Exact shaded-circle radii For small real delta>0 put the outer centers at 0,L on the real axis, with radii r_x=1/x,r_y=1/y and L^2=(r_x+r_y)^2-4r_xr_y s^2=D/(x^2y^2). Their intersections are P_plus=u+iv and P_minus=u-iv, where u=(L^2+r_x^2-r_y^2)/(2L), v=2r_xr_y s c0/L=2s c0/sqrt(D). (3) The input middle circle lies on the positive side of the outer center line. Its center p_b+iq_b and radius r_b=1/b obey p_b=u+r_b(r_x-r_y)/L, q_b=2c0 T_b/(b sqrt(D))>0. The output middle circle uses the negative side, with the same formula for p_c and q_c=-2c0 T_c/(c sqrt(D)). These are the oriented model's two shaded sides. The signed variant and its actual complete-word calibration are retained in section 5. The circle orthogonal to the three input white circles has center u+i t_b and squared radius t_b^2-v^2. Orthogonality to the middle circle gives exactly t_b=[r_x(r_x+r_b)-u p_b]/q_b =c0 B_b/[sqrt(D) T_b]. (4) The output shaded circle has t_c=-c0 B_c/[sqrt(D) T_c]. These formulas follow by subtracting squared center-distance equations; in particular they retain the actual side signs. The identity B_b^2-4s^2 T_b^2=D verifies their normalizations. Use the Möbius coordinate w=(z-P_plus)/(z-P_minus). Both outer circles become straight lines through 0 and infinity. On the shaded circle with center u+it, its equation gives |w|^2=(t-v)/(t+v). Consequently the INPUT and OUTPUT shaded circles become concentric circles of radii rho_b,rho_c with rho_b^2=(B_b-2sT_b)/(B_b+2sT_b)=D/E_b^2, rho_c^2=(B_c+2sT_c)/(B_c-2sT_c)=E_c^2/D, rho_c/rho_b=E_b E_c/D=R0. (5) The square roots in (5) are positive in this real configuration. Equation(5) is an algebraic identity with the stated selected branches; it continues holomorphically on the small complex parameter germ. ## 3. The primitive sidepairing and its selected flag The two transformed middle circles are tangent to the same two outer lines and lie in the SAME selected wedge. To check the latter rather than assume it, as delta tends to zero the coordinate w tends to1 at every original point away from the outer tangency. Both entire middle circles are separated from that tangency, and their transformed circles are therefore small circles near1 in the same wedge. This persists for sufficiently small positive delta. In one such wedge, a circle tangent to both boundary lines has center on its fixed angle bisector. Its center distance and radius are fixed positive multiples of the radius of its concentric orthogonal circle. Hence the POSITIVE dilation C_w(w)=R0 w (6) maps the entire input middle circle to the output middle circle, and the shaded b-circle to the shaded c-circle. It preserves EACH outer circle and sends their respective contact points C1->C0 and C2->C3. This is exactly the original even shaded sidepairing. The alternative negative dilation moves the middle circle to the opposite wedge and does not give this corner pairing. The reverse disk path gives C^-1. This argument also distinguishes the primitive map from a doubled one. Reflection in |w|=rho is w->rho^2/conjugate(w). Thus the composition of the TWO shaded reflections has multiplier R0^2, not R0. The original disk pairing (6) is a single sidepairing within its projection copy; it must not be replaced by that doubled reflection word. For the order (2), the actual determinant-one outer product is P=1/(r_x r_y) [[r_y^2-L^2, L r_x^2], [-L, r_x^2]]. (7) It has trace -2cos(2pi delta). At P_minus its eigenvalue is J=-exp(-2pi i delta), whereas at P_plus it is J^-1. Indeed the lower row evaluated on (P_minus,1)^T gives [-L P_minus+r_x^2]/(r_xr_y)=-cos(2pi delta)+i sin(2pi delta). The coordinate w sends the J-line to infinity. Therefore (6) has eigenratio R0 ON THE ORIGINAL J-LINE, as required by the source. Reversing the product in (2) would exchange this ratio with its inverse. In the original coordinate the projective map (6) is exactly C=I+(R0-1)/(J-J^-1) (P-J^-1 I). (8) It has eigenvalues R0 and1 and determinant R0. Because it preserves the two outer circles and maps b to c, the original ordered meridians satisfy C A_in C^-1=A_out, C B_in C^-1=B_out. (9) Thus (8) is the geometric sidepairing with the SAME full ordered character map as the original source; trace matching alone was not used to identify it. All formulas first hold for small positive real delta and positive circle data, then as holomorphic identities. At completeness put Cscalar=pi(T_b(0)+T_c(0))/(x+y). Then R0=1+2Cscalar delta+O(delta^2) and J-J^-1=4pi i delta+O(delta^3). The apparent quotient in (8) is removable, and its limit is C=I+(Cscalar/(2pi i)) (P+I). (10) This is the nontrivial parabolic collar already fixed by the actual complete rectangle. It is not inferred to be identity from R0=1. ## 4. Primitive meridian and the retained half twist The actual crossing-disk threading word is [2,1,1,2]. Its original Hurwitz calculation in [the local critical-character map](actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md), section 4, gives pure physical transport by C_aux^-1, with disk longitude P=BA and no auxiliary meridian detour. Equation(9), with its checked original corner order, therefore identifies C with that pure transport in the untwisted case. Normalize its SL2 lift by sqrt(R0), selected to equal1 at completeness. On the J-line the primitive auxiliary meridian eigenvalue is then M_aux=R0^-1/2. The actual positive main Hurwitz move is (A,B)->(A^-1 B A,A). It is simultaneous conjugation by P^-1-I, whose eigenratio on the J-line is -J^-1. Retaining the source half twist epsilon in {0,+1,-1} thus gives the SAME original convention as the source equation: M_aux^-2=R0(-J)^epsilon. (11) No unrecorded half-longitude loop is inserted. The square root defining M_aux is selected by the original complete meridian lift; reversing the selected eigenflag or the collar path reverses the indicated logarithms, rather than changing this convention silently. On the logarithmic branches centered at completeness, U_aux=2Log M_aux=-Log R0-epsilon Log(-J), V_long=2Log(-J)=-4pi i delta. (12) In particular dV_long/dU_aux at zero is 2pi i/(Cscalar-pi i epsilon), the independently proved primitive rectangle modulus. This is a consequence of the ordered calculation; it is not used as a substitute for it. ## 5. Common marked-line limit The [marked pattern theorem](actual_marked_deformed_circle_pattern.md) has already constructed the TWO marked lines, the common strip width, and their selected matching eigenline germs. They provide the geometric data absent from a collapsed 200 source root. We use those data here; no finite Bessel logarithmic derivative is interpreted as a classical eigenflag. There is one explicit regularization for the whole finite pattern. In its normalized strip 0<Im z<1 take real t->0 and g_t(z)=z/[1-t z+i t/2]. (13) Its pole 1/t+i/2 lies between the two marked halfplanes and outside every finite white disk for sufficiently small t. Every transformed outward disk is therefore bounded, with positive radius. In particular both marked curvatures are positive and O(t^2); every other curvature has its original positive limit. The same g_t transforms ALL circles, original contact labels, sidepairings and selected flags, and g_t->Id. It is not a collection of independent local conjugations. An important signed correction is necessary here: making all disks bounded does NOT imply that the input and output middle centers lie on opposite sides of their outer center line. If their actual side signs are sigma_b=sign(q_b) and sigma_c=sign(q_c), the same calculation gives rho_f=(sqrt(D)/E_f)^sigma_f, R_signed=(E_b/sqrt(D))^sigma_b (E_c/sqrt(D))^(-sigma_c). (13a) For example both centers can lie on the negative side after a common Möbius transformation. Equation(13a), not an unsigned application of (5), is used at every finite regularization parameter. Here is the actual planar and word calibration. At completeness all transformed disks are bounded and disjoint. Each straight tangency edge between their centers lies in its two disks, so these edges give the original planar rotation system. The bounded center triangles have its consistent orientation; only the outer triangle has the opposite orientation. The pole in (13) is in a far-end gap of the original strip. Every one-line/two-finite gap has bounded horizontal extent, while the two unbounded gaps are precisely the triangles containing BOTH marked line faces u,v. Thus the exceptional outer triangle is a uv triangle. Its matching edge is not uv, since uv is MAIN, so its limiting source type is 200 or002 and its T_f tends to zero. On that triangle E_f/sqrt(D) tends to1, whichever side sign occurs. The global choice of the remaining orientation is fixed by the ORIGINAL complete collar word, rather than by a desired sign for (1). The direct primitive translation calculation in [the channel-Hessian note](actual_augmented_plat_channel_hessian.md), section 3, together with the actual rectangle in [the external reflection note](actual_external_circle_reflection_and_cusp.md), section 4, gives C_complete=I-i(P+I)/(2c_geom), c_geom=(x+y)/(T_b(0)+T_c(0))>0. (13b) ALL curvatures and T terms in (13b) refer to the ORIGINAL MARKED-STRIP LIMIT after t->0, not to arbitrary finite g_t curvatures. At finite t one must keep (13a), including its possible flipped sign. First take the signed complete-collar coefficient back to the marked strip, and only then compare it with (13b). The first identity is the literal threading/longitude translation calculation there, independent of its subsequent Hessian conclusion. The signed model (13a) has limiting coefficient -i[sigma_b T_b(0)-sigma_c T_c(0)]/[2(x+y)]. Comparing with (13b) forces sigma_b=+1 whenever the MARKED limiting T_b(0)>0 and sigma_c=-1 whenever the marked limiting T_c(0)>0. A zero limiting T term has no sign constraint and contributes nothing. Reversing the copy or collar path reverses both the ordered word and this calibration; it is not an independent local choice. The signs remain constant for small real delta. Indeed the squared height of every finite center triangle is the strictly positive 4cos^2(pi delta) T_f^2/[f^2 D], so no nondegenerate center triangle can reverse along this deformation. The exceptional uv triangle has T_f=0 in the actual line limit for every delta. Thus (13a) converges to EXACTLY R0 in (1) for small real delta. The regular three-point map below then supplies its holomorphic extension; no separate uniform square-root assertion at the disappearing T term is required. Conjugating the SIGNED finite-circle sidepairing back by g_t and letting t->0 therefore gives (8),(9) for the actual line pattern. The limit is regular: the three original labeled points C1,C2 and the selected matching fixed point are distinct at completeness, as are their images C0,C3 and that fixed point. Their unique Möbius map is holomorphic on a common neighborhood. A point equal to infinity is handled in homogeneous coordinates. It is precisely the sidepairing already determined in section 3. This also proves existence of the common-conjugated limit, rather than selecting a root of a boundary polynomial after the fact. No matching edge has both outer faces equal to the two marked faces: their common edge is MAIN and the white sphere is simplicial. Thus A=x+y remains positive at every matching edge, even at a two-line triangle. The functions D,E_b,E_c and R0 therefore have the stated nonzero holomorphic limits near delta=0. For a 200 triangle T_b=0, take E_b=A exactly. Its missing flag has already been supplied by the marked line geometry and the common-conjugated map. The actual upper and lower line eigenflag adapters are those of the marked pattern theorem, with no independent reflection of a source head. The resulting identities extend to small complex delta by holomorphy in the constructed pattern. The geometric configuration, not the collapsed scalar root alone, is what justifies that extension. ## 6. Scope This proves the actual local primitive collar, its ordered meridian transport, selected flags, half-twist and logarithmic normalization on the marked deformed pattern. The matching ratio is exactly the source ratio E_b E_c/D, including the marked zero-face limits. Global representation relations, comparison with the chosen marked geometric deformation, and integration of the full regulator still require the separate assembly. Ordinary-color subsets and the full filled-source gap also remain outside this local theorem. Focused [collar audit](../experiments/audit_actual_deformed_circle_primitive_collar.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_deformed_circle_primitive_collar_results.json): author PASS. It checks 11 exact radius/selected-flag identities, 60 ordered-product and eigenflag identities, 24 literal contact pairings, 12 primitive-versus-double-reflection factors, 36 actual threading/half-twist words and their primitive eigenvalues, 18 marked 200 maps/flags, and 24 common circle regularizations at 80 digits. Twelve regularizations genuinely flip the center triangle: the signed formula passes while the unsigned finite formula fails. These checks retain the marked-line correction rather than hiding it in a limiting sample. Independent root full analytical review, audit-code review and fresh 80-digit replay: PASS. The final proof explicitly takes the signed regularization back to the original marked-strip limit before applying the complete-word sign calibration; it does not apply the unsigned formula to a flipped finite compactification. Independent geometry full analytical review and fresh redirected 80-digit replay: PASS. This includes the original ordered P/J flag, literal corner pairing, primitive-versus-double-reflection distinction, threading/Hurwitz word, signed regularization and regular three-point line limit. All stated audit counts were reproduced. These reviews establish the local collar theorem with its marking; global assembly and the source qualifications in section 6 are unchanged.

title: The actual cap has affine winding one and a degree-blind unit carry wall
text: # The actual cap has affine winding one and a degree-blind unit carry wall 28 October 2026. The ORIGINAL cap has an exact charged winding equation D+1=N, with the affine +1 forced by its actual dual color. Its signed carry current is nevertheless identically zero. The original marked cap detects the canonical cyclic/noncyclic wall with the nonzero WHOLE meridian value -x/N. The two individual wall charges each have marked augmentation one; total degree sees only their difference. This does not identify the last oversized geometric edge with an actual quantum head or prove its coefficient zero/nonzero. It fixes the affine charge and augmented wall class that comparison must carry. The existing common-tree carry lattice and cyclic sewing identities are not re-proved or called new here. The new point is the actual dual condition, four-atom degree calculation, and original marked source evaluation together. ## 1. The source fixes the cyclic wrap ratio Use the ORIGINAL semicyclic heads V(x,phi), with K v_a=xQ^-a v_a, F v_a=v_(a+1) (a<d), F v_d=phi v_0, d=N-1, k=x^N. The actual dual is V(y,psi), with y=x^-1 Q^-1, psi=-k phi. (1) These are the proved [actual oriented duals](relative_pivotal_duality.md), not freely chosen cyclic directions. In particular the total F center on their cup is phi+k^-1 psi=0. For phi!=0 form the actual four-atom monomial A=F_1^-1 tensor F_2. Let W_d have basis b_a=v_a tensor v_(d-a), 0<=a<N. It is stable under A, whose exact restriction is A b_a=b_(a-1) for a>0, A b_0=-k b_d. (2) The ratio psi/phi=-k cancels phi. Consequently (2) has a canonical phi-independent extension to the nilpotent source. Let T be the nonwrapped part, T b_0=0 and T b_a=b_(a-1). The source's missing edge is exactly A-T=-k B, B=|b_d><b_0|, A^N=-k I, T^N=0. (3) The central -k is retained, not replaced by a complete numerical value. This is the canonical carry limit of the genuine cyclic monomial, rather than an arbitrary added wrap. ## 2. The total degree current is zero on that actual fiber Let J_i have the literal integer eigenvalues 0,...,d and D=J_1+J_2. On the full two-head space, let P_1 project to first index 0 and P_2 project to second index d. The EXACT cyclic degree identity is [D,A]=N A(P_1-P_2). (4) Indeed lowering the first index changes J_1 by -1 except at its wrap, where it changes by N-1; raising the second changes J_2 by 1 except at its wrap, where it changes by 1-N. This proves (4) with the actual nonzero wrap coefficients as well. For the four genuine crossing monomials in [the four-atom factorization](four_cyclic_atoms.md), m_i=c_i A S_1^(b_i), b_i=(-1,0,0,1), c_i=(-Qx,x^-1,Qx,-x^-1), the same equation holds with A replaced by m_i, since the integer degree commutes with each clock S_1. Thus the physical total degree records a DIFFERENCE of the two wrap charges. On W_d, exactly D=d I, P_1=P_2=P_0=|b_0><b_0|. (5) The degree current (4) therefore vanishes identically, although the common deleted edge (3) is nonzero. Any spectral projector depending ONLY on D is either zero or identity on this whole fiber. It cannot remove the cyclic wall while retaining its noncyclic source. Thus the signed carry CURRENT alone does not identify the common augmented class. The degree VALUE, in contrast, carries a precise affine winding. The actual dual color has xy=Q^-1, so on the entire two-head space K_total=Q^(-1-D). Consequently its eigenvalue-one subspace is exactly W_d: since 0<=D<=2N-2, the only possible multiple of N for D+1 is N. Every actual invariant cup therefore obeys D+1=N, W_cap=(D+1)/N=1. (5a) This is an exact integer equation, not a choice of log lift or only an asymptotic statement. The affine +1 is forced by the original dual K root. It excludes total degree zero on this channel. The same conclusion holds for the remaining pair after the other ordinary caps of any actual plat are contracted. What remains unproved is that a new Pachner edge's three angular indices give THIS charged D+1. A zero Euler-transfer route in the actual crossing does not disprove (5a): its cup input can be (d,0), so that zero transfer still has charged degree N. Individually the two degree equations retain an affine term: [J_1,A]=-A+N A P_0, [J_2,A]= A-N A P_0. Since A is invertible on this fiber, the winding cochain is P_0=(I+A^-1[J_1,A])/N, Tr(P_0)=1. (6) Its unit augmentation disappears on summing the two degree currents. The signed total-degree carry is a coboundary with zero cyclic sum; the single common wall retains the fundamental unit cyclic class. An edge-winding comparison needs this augmented class, not just D. ## 3. The ORIGINAL marked source detects the missing class Use the balanced basis w_a=v_a/F_a only to display the actual source simply. From [the exact bridge cap](quantum_bridge_cap_source.md), write b_a^bal=w_a tensor w_(d-a), distinct from b_a in Section 1. cup coefficient at b_a^bal =N x^(a-d), marked_cap(b_a^bal)=x^(d-a)/N^2. (7) These include the original averaged cut, pivot and marked defect. Their product at EACH a is 1/N, so the full marked bubble is one. The change from v to w has equal factorial products at b_0 and b_d, hence it leaves the edge coefficient -k in (3) unchanged. For the original functional Phi(O)=marked_cap O cup, exactly Phi(I)=1, Phi(P_1)=Phi(P_2)=Phi(P_0)=1/N, Phi(P_1-P_2)=0, Phi(A-T)=(-k) x^-d/N=-x/N !=0. (8) Thus each individual wall has N Phi(P_0)=1, while total degree sees zero. The canonical carry coupon has a nonzero original source value on the ENTIRE meridian family. At completeness it is q^-1/N, but (8) has been obtained before that specialization. No peripheral factor has been reset. At the complete self-dual color, the bare four-atom monomial wall values in this common source frame are respectively (1,-1,-1,1)/N. This follows by multiplying (8) by the c_i and using S_1^(b_i)b_0=b_0 and Qx^2=1. Their sum is zero, but none is zero. This is a common-frame COUPON calculation; it does not replace the differently transported exterior source at each separate factor of the full crossing. The [Ward augmentation theorem](ward_cyclic_wall_contraction_and_marked_augmentation.md) and [cap-residue theorem](cap_wall_fermat_quad_residue_transport.md) give complementary forms of the same obstruction: the marked unit wall and its actual residue survive, while some signed Ward currents can be contracted. Equation (8) supplies the literal whole-meridian source value for the dual-cup carry. ## 4. The actual cap forces a four-atom norm wall The precise bare ratio in the four-atom crossing is r=phi_2/phi_1. At a true dual cap it is fixed by (1): r=-k. At completeness k^2=1 and the source color is self-dual. To inspect the local normal direction perturb r=-k+epsilon, keeping that complete color fixed. The four displayed transported atom centers are exactly 1-k epsilon, 1-k/epsilon, 1-k/epsilon, 1-k epsilon, with norm-root powers k epsilon, (k epsilon)^-1, (k epsilon)^-1, k epsilon. (9) Thus their compatible root valuations are (1/N,-1/N,-1/N,1/N). The actual cap is already on this mandatory wall; setting a zero norm factor to zero cannot delete it. Full common-frame products and the original relative source are required. This links the old abstract fusion-wall condition to the literal four-atom factors. There is also a FULL, uninserted original-source test at this wall, rather than only the coupon test (8). The strict actual crossing core from the bridge theorem satisfies R_+ C_x|d,0>=kappa C_y|d,0>, because its Euler shift kills |d,0> and its Gaussian there is one. At completeness y=x, so the original marked one-bridge plat evaluates the whole crossing to exactly its retained nonzero common Cartan scalar kappa. The original zero-framing adapter gives the unknot value one. Equivalently this follows directly from the physical output (0,d): only original input (d,0) and zero transfer contribute, fixing the scalar. Thus the mandatory four-atom norm wall has nonzero coupling to the FULL original source; no auxiliary source vector has been chosen. This remains a test of the actual cap wall (9), not an assertion that it is the last geometric Pachner wall in the oversized example. A tempting but invalid shortcut is to match two displayed centers whose sum is one. The first two actual bare monomials satisfy m_1 m_2=Q m_2 m_1. The two-factor side of the retained primitive pentagon is D(Y)D(bX), with XY=QYX, so its first/second bare commutation is Q^-1. The actual first pair also DIVIDES the second center by its first norm, whereas that pentagon side MULTIPLIES it. Center matching alone therefore does not put that Pachner move inside this actual word; an additional typed quad/shear/source map is necessary. The two commutation phases differ for N>2; at N=2 they coincide, but the transported norm factors still require the same explicit typed check. ## 5. Consequence for the oversized winding-zero face The [last Pachner-wall calculation](oversized_alias_last_pachner_wall.md) shows that the geometric positive angular branch needs internal edge winding one, and the weak oversized face has winding zero. The present theorem neither admits nor removes that face from the original cycle. It supplies the exact cap-side mechanism: the charged degree is N, while the signed carry current has lost the common augmentation (8). Plain exponentiated edge gluing or the current alone would omit different parts of this data. What is now required is a literal chain/source map from the new Pachner edge to this AUGMENTED cyclic class, with the compatible log/angle lift and all three new face sources. A claim that the new integer angles sum to N must prove that map, including any affine charge. It cannot be inferred from unwrapped total-degree conservation or from the exponentiated edge equation alone. For clarity, the elementary angular criterion such a map could use is uniform: if nonnegative integer angles n_j have a positive fixed affine charge c, satisfy sum n_j+c=0 modulo N, and 0<sum n_j+c<2N, then sum n_j+c=N. A zero-charge equation admits the collapsed all-zero branch. Equation (5a) proves c=1 on the actual cap channel. It has not proved c=1 on the new Pachner edge; that is the precise remaining local chain-map target. The generic primitive pentagon, carry-tree lattice and local atom order do not yet supply this missing identification. No new source-preserving geometric 2↔3 theorem or volume claim is asserted by (1)--(9). ## 6. Exact original-matrix checks The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_degree_cap_winding.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_degree_cap_winding_results.json) pass 44 original dual-cap families at N=2,...,12, with complete and generic meridians and two nonzero semicyclic parameters. They construct caps, cups, marked defect and pivot from the original duality matrices, then check (4)--(8), the exact charged K_total eigenspace, all four bare monomial currents/centers, and the FULL mixed crossing source using independent original E and Cartan coefficients. The retained complete Cartan and twist give zero-framed value one. Thirty-three exact perturbed four-atom norm charts check (9) and both level parities. The proofs establish all N; these checks verify the original source conventions and transported scalar factors. ## 7. The paired Fermat completion has local cyclic source equations This section checks the projected paired source proposed in the [tame paired-source construction](tame_paired_fermat_source_transport.md). It is a source FRAME family; its parameter is not identified with the semicyclic phi or the meridian normal. Literal conjugation of the whole currents and word is required when using it away from zero. Its endpoint is the original relative pair |d,0>. Put epsilon=1-delta^N, with delta=1 at epsilon=0, and define V_j=epsilon/[(1-Q)(Q^2 delta;Q)_j (Q delta;Q)_(d-j)], W_j=(Q delta;Q)_j(delta;Q)_(d-j)/N, 0<=j<N. (10) These are regular at the marked epsilon=0 after whole cancellation, with V(0)=e_d and W(0)=e_d^t. For generic epsilon the consecutive ratios are EXACTLY V_(j+1)/V_j=(1-delta Q^(-j-1))/(1-delta Q^(j+2)), W_(j+1)/W_j=(1-delta Q^(j+1))/(1-delta Q^(-j-2)), (11) where indices are CYCLIC. For j<d these follow by cancelling one factor. The wrap uses the whole endpoint identities V_0=(1-delta)/(1-Q), V_d=(1-delta Q)/(1-Q), W_0=epsilon/[N(1-delta Q^-1)], W_d=epsilon/[N(1-delta)]. Thus (11) holds also at j=d; no endpoint source has been omitted. Let A have eigenvalues Q^j and let T act on COMPONENTS by (Tf)_j=f_(j+1 mod N), so TA=QAT. The bounded-complexity source and CO-SOURCE equations are [(1-delta Q^2 A)T-(1-delta Q^-1 A^-1)]V=0, W[(1-delta Q^-1 A^-1)T^-1-(1-delta QA)]=0. (12) The second is a right row action: the coefficient of its jth component is W_(j+1)(1-delta Q^(-j-2)) -W_j(1-delta Q^(j+1)). In particular W is not a left kernel of the FIRST operator. The original marked co-source must not be changed into an ordinary adjoint cap by that substitution. On a regular classical chart with Q,delta tending to one, both symbols describe p=-A^-1, respecting the source/co-source orientations. Their Gaussian phase is the cancellation of the two individual dilogarithmic head actions. The exact endpoint A=1 still requires the original pointed normalization in (10). ## 8. Its normalized diagonal source is an exact discrete Poisson measure Let G=sum_j W_jV_j and R=V_d. Finite-product cancellation gives W_jV_j=R epsilon(1-delta)/ [N(1-delta Q^(j+1))(1-delta Q^(-j-1))], G=R(2-epsilon)/(1+delta). (13) For the sum, the exact partial-fraction identity gives sum_(n=0)^d 1/[(1-delta Q^n)(1-delta Q^-n)] =N(1+delta^N)/[(1-delta^N)(1-delta^2)]. This follows by summing 1/(1-delta z)+1/(1-delta/z)-1 over z^N=1 and dividing by 1-delta^2; the single sums are N/(1-delta^N). Substitution proves (13), with its actual nonzero scalar. Normalize w=W/G. The diagonal weights pi_j=w_jV_j are pi_j=epsilon(1-delta^2)/ [N(2-epsilon)(1-delta Q^(j+1)) (1-delta Q^(-j-1))], sum_j pi_j=1. (14) For real 0<epsilon<1 and the marked real delta=(1-epsilon)^(1/N), these are STRICTLY POSITIVE discrete Poisson weights: the denominator product is |1-delta Q^(j+1)|^2. This is a positive DIAGONAL boundary functional. It does not make the full transformed braid kernel positive. All its clock moments are explicit. For 0<=m<=N, sum_j pi_j Q^(m(j+1)) =(delta^m+delta^(N-m))/(1+delta^N). (15) For |delta|<1, expand the two denominator factors in geometric series and sum the root characters. Only exponent differences congruent to m survive; the root-summed denominator is N/(1-delta^2) times (delta^m+delta^(N-m))/(1-delta^N). Multiplying by the prefactor in (14) proves (15), with the same formula at m=0,N. Algebraic continuation gives the general marked identity. Moments of A itself have the additional retained factor Q^-m. Thus the paired source has a local cyclic operator, its true co-source operator, a normalized positive real slice, and exact finite moments. It retains the charged origin j+1 and tends to the actual d-corner at epsilon=0. It does not identify the Pachner edge's angular variables or prove geometric global noncancellation. The current/frame transport and relative source must still accompany the whole word. ### The real paired source is a positive rank-one density In fact the real-slice positivity is stronger than its diagonal. Put A_scalar=epsilon/[N(1-delta)]>0 and R=V_d. Exact root complement reflection gives W=(A_scalar/conjugate R) V^dagger, ||V||_2^2=|R|^2(2-epsilon)/[(1+delta)A_scalar], w=W/G=V^dagger/||V||_2^2. (16) For j<d, write A_m=(Q delta;Q)_m. Then conjugate A_(j+1)=epsilon/[(1-delta)A_(d-j-1)] and conjugate A_(d-j)=epsilon/[(1-delta)A_j]. Substituting in V_j gives conjugate V_j=conjugate R (1-delta)^2 A_j A_(d-j-1)/epsilon, while W_j=(1-delta)A_j A_(d-j-1)/N. At j=d, W_d=A_scalar and V_d=R directly. This proves the first equation; (13) proves the others. Thus E_pair=Vw is an ORTHOGONAL rank-one projector for real 0<epsilon<1, and its diagonal is exactly (14). Its norms stay uniformly controlled on every real epsilon<=rho<1: use 1-epsilon<=A_scalar<=1, |R|^2=delta+(1-delta)^2/[4sin^2(pi/N)], N(1-delta)<=-log(1-epsilon). This gives positive upper and lower bounds in (16), independent of N. It does not make a general oriented braid operator positive or establish a lower bound for its complex matrix coefficient. The same exact audit checks 33 paired cyclic parameters, both wraps and operator orders, the normalization (13), and every moment m=0,...,N. Eighteen positive real-slice diagnostics check the orthogonal-density and norm identities (16). Independent proof review checked (10)--(15), including the retained Q^-m factor for the unshifted clock.

title: Actual divided Ward closure keeps a whole Green cap current
text: # Actual divided Ward closure keeps a whole Green cap current Research proof, 27 October 2026. Actual pivotal closure gives a global current map for every finite weighted braid word and every integral divided generator. The map retains the actual coupling moments, the marked cut row, and the whole ordinary/frozen pivot adapter. Its endpoint is an explicit inserted current, rather than an inference from scalarity of the unweighted knot matrix. This does not identify the resulting finite current with the two internal geometric Gaussian currents. In particular the [memory-Borel wall](degree_elevation_complement_bockstein_wall.md) is not declared to be a quantum-group coproduct generator. The high-color statements also do not identify its whole normal jets with those of the original low color; only the previously proved root scalar comparison may be used for that purpose. ## 1. The actual divided coproduct and adjoint Use the generic integral Weyl family and the conventions Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E, Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F, K E K^(-1)=Q E, K F K^(-1)=Q^(-1) F, S(E)=-E K^(-1), S(F)=-K F, Q=q^2. Put E^(a)=E^a/[a]_q! and F^(a)=F^a/[a]_q!. Their matrices are integral Gaussian matrices on every actual integral color. They are retained before root specialization. Direct expansion of the two q-commuting summands gives Delta E^(n)=sum_(k=0)^n q^(k(n-k)) E^(n-k) tensor E^(k) K^(n-k), Delta F^(n)=sum_(k=0)^n q^(-k(n-k)) K^(-k) F^(n-k) tensor F^(k). (1.1) For example AB=Q BA for A=E tensor K, B=1 tensor E. The coefficient of B^k A^(n-k) is the ordinary Q-Gaussian; dividing by [n]_q! changes it to q^(k(n-k)). This proves (1.1) without a root-level division. Iteration retains every multiindex of total size n, including mixed ordinary/divided terms. The adjoint on matrices is A_h(C)=sum h_1 C S(h_2). In particular A_(E^(n))(C)=sum_(k=0)^n (-1)^k q^(-k(n-1)) E^(n-k) C E^(k) K^(-n), A_(F^(n))(C)=sum_(k=0)^n (-1)^k q^(k(n-1)) F^(n-k) K^(-k) C K^k F^(k). (1.2) The antipode factors in (1.2) follow by multiplying S(E)=-E K^(-1) and S(F)=-KF. At n=N the terms 1<=k<N are essential. Replacing (1.2) by a plain commutator with the individual divided matrix loses them, even when that individual matrix vanishes on a small color. Write D_h=A_h-epsilon(h)I. All matrices in (1.1)--(1.2) and their actual normal coefficients are regular on the integral color lattice. Full Cartan, framing and peripheral scalar factors remain part of every operator below. ## 2. An explicit integral current for every actual crossing Write either signed actual checked crossing, with its literal unwrapped transfer, as R_t(w)=sum_(k>=0) w^k R_(t,k), R_t(1)=R_t. The sum is finite. The color list is switched after the crossing; rho_in and rho_out denote its actual iterated coproduct matrices. For any integral h define Xi_(h,t,k)=rho_out(h) R_(t,k)-R_(t,k) rho_in(h), J_(h,t)(w)=sum_(k>=1) (1+w+...+w^(k-1)) Xi_(h,t,k). Actual R intertwining says sum_k Xi_(h,t,k)=0. Therefore rho_out(h)R_t(w)-R_t(w)rho_in(h) =(w-1)J_(h,t)(w). (2.1) This is an explicit polynomial division by w-1. It neither divides by [N]_q! nor chooses a root primitive. Hence it applies directly to h=E^(N),F^(N) with (1.1), to both crossing signs, and to every whole normal jet. Every transfer endpoint is present. For h=E,F it is the generating transform of the literal [crossing-transfer currents](local_r_ward_transfer_currents.md). The same construction applies to a cut or component-position weight w^J: its value at w=1 is the identity intertwiner. For a link retain one such initial-position weight per component. Let W(w)=R_m(w_m)...R_1(w_1), including any position weights as additional factors. All actual tensor spectators are included in rho_t(h). The elementary telescoping identity gives Xi_h(W)=sum_t (w_t-1) W_>t J_(h,t)(w_t) W_<t. (2.2) To pass to the true Hopf adjoint use the exact identity D_h(W)=sum_(h) Xi_(h_1)(W) rho_0(S h_2). Thus (2.2) gives specified whole matrix currents B_(h,t) with D_h(W)=sum_t (w_t-1) B_(h,t)(w), B_(h,t)=sum_(h) W_>t J_(h_1,t)(w_t) W_<t rho_0(S h_2). (2.3) All coproduct and antipode factors occur in their displayed order. Equation (2.3) is a global finite-word current identity. It uses actual matrices, rather than assigning a coproduct to the memory Cartan or to a projected highest-spin corner. ## 3. The ordinary pivotal cap and its marked source row For an actual closed tensor factor let P_o(C)=Tr_W[(I tensor K_W)C]. This is an exact intertwiner of the Hopf adjoints on ALL matrices: P_o D_h=D_h P_o. (3.1) For E the two internal terms cancel because K_W^(-1)K_W=I; for F they cancel because K_W F_W K_W^(-1)=Q^(-1)F_W. K is immediate by cyclicity. The identities extend to products; alternatively (1.1)--(1.2) give a direct integral check for every divided generator. Apply the generic identity first and then specialize its regular matrices. This is the actual divided-cap argument of [the marked-edge note](divided_adjoint_marked_edge_pairing.md), now applied to the coupled currents (2.3). Let Phi_A(C)=Tr(A C) be the ORIGINAL cut row, allowing its whole q-dependent source, pivot and normalization. Its exact dual row is D_h^vee(A)=sum_(h) rho(S h_2) A rho(h_1) -epsilon(h)A. Cyclicity, not invariance of A, gives Phi_A(D_h C)=Tr[D_h^vee(A) C]. (3.2) Consequently pivotal closure of (2.3) is the source-sensitive map Tr[D_h^vee(A) P_o W] =sum_t(w_t-1) Phi_A(P_o B_(h,t)). (3.3) The original coherent cut, uniform interval cut and normalized trace are distinct A's in (3.2)--(3.3). They may not be substituted for each other on the wall. In particular their values on the normalized Frobenius wall E_(N,0) remain respectively 2^(-N), 1/(N+1), and zero. ## 4. Actual Green moments leave a finite difference of the moment Put E_t=w_t partial_(w_t) and let p be any actual index-moment polynomial. Define its forward finite difference by Delta_t p(x)=p(x+e_t)-p(x). Apply p(E) to (3.3) and only then put every w=1. The exact product rule p(E)(w_t f)=w_t p(E+e_t)f proves Tr[D_h^vee(A) P_o p(E)W]_(w=1) =sum_t Phi_A[P_o (Delta_t p)(E) B_(h,t)]_(w=1). (4.1) Thus a constant moment has zero current endpoint. A nonconstant Green moment has the SPECIFIED lower-moment current on the right; unweighted Schur scalarity does not make it zero.
