The same failure occurs inside the macroscopic source tail at Y=-i, not only at Y=i. This is a local statement in a specified classical eigenframe. A superadiabatic change of frame can remove the first-order off-diagonal terms; no impossibility of a different global source-retaining connection is asserted. ## 1. A pure amplitude map cannot be silently made bistochastic Let C be an invertible square matrix. Suppose a completely positive trace-preserving map Phi has, for every pure input psi, a pure output on the line C psi. Then C^*C is a scalar matrix, and Phi is the corresponding unitary channel. This includes a claimed equality with C psi psi^* C^* up to one common scalar, as well as the normalized pure-output prescription. Proof. Write Phi(X)=sum_a K_a X K_a^*. Positivity and the rank-one output imply K_a psi is on the line C psi for every psi and a. Thus C^(-1)K_a preserves EVERY vector line. Applying it to basis vectors and their pairwise sums gives C^(-1)K_a=c_a I. Trace preservation yields (sum|c_a|^2)C^*C=I. Since C is square, its scalar normalization is unitary; unitality follows as well. Agreement on ONE selected pure state is much weaker and does not imply this conclusion. Introducing a dephasing, a Kraus completion, or a state-dependent postselection normalization changes the original coherent map unless the extra source contributions are retained. ## 2. Exact original connection and its normalized eigenframe Use the exact coefficients and original source of [the actual regulator-weighted transfer](actual_regulator_weighted_a_transfer.md): w_(j+1)=T_Q(Y)w_j+f_Q(Y), Q=exp(i tau), tau=2pi/N, T_Q=[-c0/c+, -c-/c+; 1,0], f_Q=(D/c+,0)^t. No affine source is set to zero in this note. In a classical modal frame S(Y) its exact update is z_(j+1)=K_N(Y)z_j+g_N(Y), K_N=S(QY)^(-1)T_Q(Y)S(Y), g_N=S(QY)^(-1)f_Q(Y). (1) On a hyperbolic interval put P=Y^2+Y^-2-Y-Y^-1-2, lambda+lambda^-1=P, V=[lambda,lambda^-1;1,1], Lambda=diag(lambda,lambda^-1). Choose the real negative expanding root lambda<-1 and normalize EACH eigenvector column in the Euclidean norm: S=V diag(n1,n2), n1=(lambda^2+1)^(-1/2), n2=-lambda n1. This is a fixed, tame modal energy convention. Its columns need not be mutually orthogonal in the original companion coordinates. Factor the known one-step diagonal propagation on the LEFT and call C_N=Lambda^(-1)K_N its instantaneous connection. This is a factorization of (1); the source g_N stays in (1) and, if the output is divided by Lambda, must be divided by Lambda there as well. Put s=sqrt(3). At Y=i, P=-4 and lambda=-2-s. The exact quantum subprincipal term AND moving-frame derivative give C_N=I+tau E+O(tau^2), E=[ -5/12 (s-1)/6; -(s+1)/6 -5/12 ]. (2) Here is a direct derivation from the previously checked connection. In the unnormalized frame V, K_N=Lambda+hB+O(h^2), h=i tau, with B12=i(s-1)/6 and B21=-i(s+1)/6. The full first-order matrix Lambda^(-1)iB is [ (s-1)/6 (3s-5)/6; -(3s+5)/6 -(s+1)/6 ]. Column normalization conjugates it by diag(1,2+s), and subtracts diag(d_theta log n1,d_theta log n2). At Y=i, d_theta log n1=1/4+s/6, d_theta log n2=1/4-s/6, since d_theta P=2. This proves every entry of (2). Omitting the moving normalization would give different diagonal terms. ## 3. The polar test fails for the diagonal regulator observable Equation (2) gives C_N^*C_N=I+tau[ -5/6 -1/3; -1/3 -5/6 ]+O(tau^2). (3) The off-diagonal term is nonzero, so no common scalar normalization makes this pure amplitude map unitary for all sufficiently large N. The lemma in Section 1 excludes a bistochastic channel agreeing on all pure inputs with this specified connection. Its polar decomposition C_N=U_N H_N does have a unitary part: U_N=I+tau(s/6)[0,1;-1,0]+O(tau^2), H_N=I+tau[-5/12,-1/6;-1/6,-5/12]+O(tau^2). (4) For a nonconstant diagonal calibrated regulator R=diag(r1,r2), (U_N^* R U_N-R)_12 =tau(s/6)(r1-r2)+O(tau^2). (5) Thus the natural polar unitary is bistochastic but NOT regulator-fixed. Dropping H_N is not the actual amplitude evolution. Its off-diagonal positive part also fails to commute with R. Both errors are polynomial, whereas the exponential action gauge requires the stronger control in the majorization theorem. This rotation cannot be removed by a positive diagonal rescaling of the same classical eigenlines. Such a rescaling with ratio t>0 changes the off-diagonal generator entries to a t and -b/t, where a=(s-1)/6,b=(s+1)/6. The polar skew entry has modulus (a t+b/t)/2>=sqrt(ab)=1/(3sqrt(2))>0. Diagonal phase marks change its phase but cannot make it vanish. This statement is about the specified instantaneous eigenlines, not arbitrary nondiagonal frame corrections. Conjugation gives the actual SOURCE-TAIL point Y=-i, x=3/4: C_N(-i)=I-tau E+O(tau^2), (U_N(-i)^* R U_N(-i)-R)_12 =-tau(s/6)(r1-r2)+O(tau^2). (6) The geometric/conjugate figure-eight regulators are different there. From the midpoint zero anchor they agree at x=2/3, while on 2/3<x<1 one eigenvalue has |lambda|>1 and its reciprocal has modulus less than one. Their regulator derivatives have opposite nonzero signs, so the gap at x=3/4 is nonzero. Hence (6) is a test on the relevant restarted half orbit as well. The affine source is present in BOTH modes. At either Y=i or -i, f_0=(2,0)^t and S^(-1)f_0=(-sqrt(lambda^2+1)/s, sqrt(lambda^2+1)/((-lambda)s))^t. (7) Both entries are nonzero. Neither the polar part nor a regulator projection may be substituted into (1) without its transformed source and the corresponding energy cross term. ## 4. An actual conserved flux, and its limitation The exact rational functions -c0/c+, -c-/c+ and D/c+ are REAL when |Q|=|Y|=1: conjugation Q->Q^-1,Y->Y^-1 fixes each one. This follows by direct factor cancellation, not just at the classical limit. On a regular arc where det T_Q>0 put J=[0,i;-i,0]. For every real 2 by 2 matrix T, T^* J T=(det T)J. (8) Thus T_Q/sqrt(det T_Q) preserves this Hermitian indefinite Wronskian form EXACTLY. Similarly C_N is real with positive determinant, so its polar U_N is a real rotation and fixes J exactly. This gives an actual fixed Hermitian observable, but it is not the diagonal geometric regulator: its eigenvectors are the circular superpositions of the two real modal lines. The form has eigenvalues +1,-1 and provides no positive norm bound. Moreover the actual ordinary figure-eight values and source are real on the root orbit, so their J flux is identically zero; the affine cross current vanishes on such real vectors too. Large real solutions can have zero flux. This conserved observable cannot replace the required positive regulator energy. It also does not establish an identity on the tiny COMPLEX-q source circle. ## 5. The source-specific route remains possible The explicit failure above does not exclude an exact global flag after a nontrivial source-retaining change of coordinates. Already locally an O(h) nondiagonal correction can kill the O(h) mixing: if K=Lambda+hB, choose X_ik=-B_ik/(lambda_i-lambda_k), i!=k, and use V_new=V(I+hX). The transformed off-diagonal starts at O(h^2); the affine source transforms by the same inverse frame. The previously proved analytic iteration improves this locally to an exponentially small remainder, with an explicit action barrier. The actual [pointed Newton--Green factorization](pointed_newton_green_barrier.md) also supplies a stronger global source estimate for this prototype, without proving this local bistochastic description. These tests neither rule out nor construct a different source-selected global flag. What does not follow from the Ward identities or the eigenvalue curve alone is the proposed bistochastic, regulator-fixed description in the instantaneous classical frame: (2)--(7) are exact obstructions to that literal claim. A global coherent/normal source reduction, its nodal connection matrices, and their exponential costs still need a separate proof for a broad class. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_regulator_channel_test.py) verifies the exact constants, rational reality, both actual orbit points, polar and regulator defects, retained source components, and the Wronskian alternative.

title: A complete positive Fourier--Hermite filling Gram and an actual source discriminant
text: # A complete positive Fourier--Hermite filling Gram and an actual source discriminant 29 October 2026. The full crossing-circle kernel gives an explicit positive, full-rank coherent Gram, independent of the unknown period. Its filling-source dual norm is exactly 1+ell^2(N^2-1)/(12N^2). It retains every confluent Casimir jet. The same construction has a precise limitation: its energy is polynomially equivalent to the whole mixed-color packet energy, so it does not automatically see the smaller filled volume. ## 1. Complete data and the positive metric Use the ORIGINAL kernel and conventions of [the Fourier--Hermite theorem](actual_twist_circle_fourier_kernel.md). For an integer crossing power ell let h_k=nu_k^ell, d_k=-ell(d-2k)h_k/2, w_k=q^(2k+1), d=N-1. Put \[ H_n=N^{-1}\sum_kh_kw_k^{-n},\qquad D_n=N^{-1}\sum_kd_kw_k^{-n}. \] Their exact marked aliases are H_(N-n)=-H_n, D_(N-n)=D_n, D0=0. For n<N/2 write m=N-n and r=n/N. Define N orthonormal compatible-data coordinates \[ y_0=H_0,\qquad (y_{n,H},y_{n,D})=(\sqrt2H_n,\sqrt2D_n/N), \] with the additional y_mid=D_(N/2)/N when N is even. At that index H_(N/2)=0. Odd N has no middle coordinate; its simple Casimir node has only a value, with logarithmic derivative zero automatically. Let a be the first-kind Chebyshev coefficient vector. The exact alias inverse a=K y is \[ a_0=y_0,\qquad \begin{pmatrix}a_n\\a_m\end{pmatrix} =\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1-r&1\\-r&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}y_{n,H}\\y_{n,D}\end{pmatrix}, \qquad a_{N/2}=y_{\rm mid}. \tag{1} \] Define the real difference matrix S by \(\beta_j=(-1)^j(a_j-a_{j+2})\), with a_N=a_(N+1)=0, and set B=S K. The original all-input filling identity is \[ R^{\ell}=\kappa^{\ell}\sum_{j=0}^d\beta_jL_{j+1}, \qquad\beta=B y. \tag{2} \] Every L_(j+1) is the literal ordinary auxiliary-circle operator, with its full Cartan and pivot and no added color average, by [the original circle-source proof](actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md). For a complete mixed-color exterior packet A=(A0,...,Ad)^T put z=B^T A and \[ \boxed{\quad E_N(A)=\|z\|^2=A^\dagger G_N A, \qquad G_N=\overline B B^{\mathsf T}>0.\quad} \tag{3} \] B is real in these coordinates, but the conjugation in (3) makes the complex Riesz convention explicit. There is a particularly simple direct formula. Set eta_n=(-1)^n(A_n-A_(n-2)), A_negative=0. Then z0=eta0, and for n<m, \[ z_{n,H}=((1-r)\eta_n-r\eta_m)/\sqrt2,\qquad z_{n,D}=(\eta_n+\eta_m)/\sqrt2, \] with z_mid=eta_mid when present. Thus the energy keeps explicit cross-color interference, not just separate squared color values. Marked Fourier Parseval gives the EXACT source cost \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \|y_\ell\|^2=\frac1N\sum_k(|h_k|^2+|d_k/N|^2) =1+\frac{\ell^2(N^2-1)}{12N^2}=:c_{N,\ell}.} \tag{4} \] Here sum_k(d-2k)^2=N(N^2-1)/3. Since B is invertible, this is also the exact dual norm beta^T G_N^(-1) conjugate(beta), not just an upper bound. For the original scalar, with its actual external line chi retained, \[ |\chi\kappa^{\ell}\beta^{\mathsf T}A|^2 \leq|\chi|^2c_{N,\ell}E_N(A). \tag{5} \] The pairing is y^T z; its Hilbert Riesz vector is conjugate(y). No unknown closed invariant defines the metric. Equations (3)--(5) also apply to Hilbert-valued packets. For arbitrary operator-valued exteriors A_j, preserving their original order, they give the all-input positive inequality \[ (\sum_j\beta_jA_j)^\dagger(\sum_j\beta_jA_j) \preceq c_{N,\ell}\sum_r Z_r^\dagger Z_r. \tag{6} \] All original Casimir jets are retained. This is a genuine positive filling port, not an inverse of the possibly nilpotent complete-color circle alone. ## 2. Polynomial conditioning and simultaneous fillings Each two-by-two block in (1) has norm at most sqrt(3/2) and inverse norm at most sqrt6. Also ||S||<=2 and ||S^(-1)||<=N, by finite summation along each parity chain. Therefore \[ \boxed{\displaystyle (6N^2)^{-1}\|A\|^2\leq E_N(A)\leq6\|A\|^2, \qquad\operatorname{cond}(G_N)\leq36N^2.} \tag{7} \] For s specified twist boxes use the tensor product transform B^T on the s color registers, AFTER retaining their entire original mixed-color exterior. The dual cost is exactly product_i c_(N,ell_i), and the Gram is positive full rank with polynomial conditioning for fixed s. Physical boxes may overlap in time; the original operator order in each packet entry is not changed. This does not assume independent physical contractions. For full twists ell_i=2p_i, the cost is at most product_i(1+p_i^2/3), independent of N. It is subexponential whenever sum_i log(1+|p_i|)=o(N). All source, framing, and peripheral factors remain the exact ones outside the filling identity (2). ## 3. A complete actual source discriminant Use the original four-plat multiplicities, cup p, cap ell and full crossings R1,R2 from the source theorems. Define ONE fixed base packet \[ A_j=\ell R_2^2L_{j+1}(\Omega_{12})R_1R_2p,\quad0\leq j<N. \] The raw filled period with slope p is F_p=ell R2^2 R1^(2p+1) R2 p=kappa^(2p) beta_(2p)^T A. The original normalization/cup slide and whole figure-eight source give the EXACT values \[ F_0=A_0=x^d=\kappa^2,\qquad F_{-1}=Z_N:=\sum_{a=0}^d|(Q;Q)_a|^2. \tag{8} \] No augmented geometric saddle is assumed. The second value is the literal original [figure-eight whole-source identity](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md); the first is the actual [all-input normalization tangle](actual_terminal_source_normalization_packet.md). Apply (5) with ell=-2. Since c_(N,-2)<=4/3, \[ \boxed{\displaystyle E_N(A)\geq\frac34 Z_N^2.} \tag{9} \] At p=0 the exact dual cost is 1 and the filled raw scalar has modulus one, yet the SAME coherent positive energy has positive exponential rate. This is a fully contracted original packet, not an expanded absolute-value path or a guessed augmented invariant. It also quantifies the requirement on a different color metric H. The bound ||B||^2<=6 and (4) give ||beta_(-2)||^2<=8. Hence ||A||^2>=Z_N^2/8. The p=0 source is beta0=e0, so its Cauchy budget under ANY positive H satisfies \[ (A^\dagger H A)(e_0^\dagger H^{-1}e_0) \geq Z_N^2/[8\operatorname{cond}(H)]. \tag{10} \] A zero-exponent sharp budget for this normalization therefore requires exponential metric anisotropy, or actual coherent pruning before the energy is formed. Polynomial-conditioned changes of the complete Fourier--Hermite norm cannot supply it. Exponential anisotropy is allowed; (10) is a necessary quantitative condition, not a no-go theorem for all coherent metrics. ## 4. The same defect persists in a hyperbolic final knot There is a source-exact all-width insertion, not merely a scalar coincidence. Let M_j be the physical one-input/one-output tangle whose complete source entry is A_j. Each crossing, original turn, and auxiliary pivotal loop is a Hopf map. Thus M_j commutes with K and F on the original complete V_N. Its K eigenvalues are distinct, so it is diagonal; every interior F coefficient is nonzero, so all diagonal entries agree. Consequently M_j=A_j I at EVERY N. The p=0 tangle is topologically the straight unframed strand. Here is the local move proof, separately from its scalar evaluation: slide the free strand past the neighboring cup (the oriented cup-slide Reidemeister-II isotopy), leaving the two crossings directly above that cup. Each is a removable Reidemeister-I kink on the same arc. The remaining cup/cap cancels by the snake isotopy. No closed component remains. In the actual framed tensor calculation the two kinks have the retained unit factor kappa^2, as (8) verifies on every input; the prescribed zero-framing line is kept when this tangle is inserted into a diagram. Insert it into a strand of any original knot J. The raw mixed-color packet is multiplied by its original cut scalar, and after retaining the original external line its energy is |K_N(J)|^2 E_N(A), up to the displayed unit framing phase. All such phases remain in the exact scalar identity and do not change this norm. The unframed p=0 filled knot is still J. By (9), \[ E_N^{\rm inserted}(J)\geq\frac34|K_N(J)|^2 Z_N^2. \tag{11} \] For the independently proved benchmark J=4_1, K_N(J)=Z_N, so this Gram has energy at least 3Z_N^4/4 while the final knot has squared scalar Z_N^2. Its energy exponent is at least DOUBLE the correct figure-eight squared-volume exponent. This counterexample uses a redundant normalization augmentation and the p=0 filling. It does NOT exclude a properly reduced fully augmented diagram or a long-filling subclass. It proves that exact filling, complete jets, and a polynomial dual source cost do not by themselves imply the filled-volume energy bound. Normalization pruning or a source/slope-dependent geometric norm remains substantive. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_filling_fourier_hermite_gram.py) checks the full marked aliases and positive Gram, exact source dual costs, all-input operator inequality, original mixed-color scalar tangles, and the two actual source fillings (8). No geometric energy bound is inferred from interpolation or from coefficient mass. Fresh replay: PASS seven complete positive Grams with49 signed dual-source costs; five literal all-input mixed-circle packets N=2,...,6; six complete original two-filling energy discriminants.

title: A source-specific Fourier gap for the exact filling endpoints
text: # A source-specific Fourier gap for the exact filling endpoints 29 October 2026. The full finite filling kernel, including its linear normal weight, has exponentially small endpoint-frequency strips when paired with an analytic source having a strict complete-color maximum. This is an estimate on a truncated ORIGINAL color corridor. It does not bound colors outside that corridor or prove survival of the remaining filled saddle. No Fresnel endpoint remainder is replaced by a polynomial error. ## 1. An exact finite Fourier lemma with its source hypotheses Let H=floor(delta N), d_N=(H+1/2)/N. Suppose a physical packet c_h, -H<=h<=H, has a holomorphic interpolation f_N(z), for |Re z|<=2delta and |Im z|<=sigma_0, satisfying \[ \|f_N(x+iy)\|\le C N^B \exp\{N(F-a x^2+C_0 y^2)\},\qquad a>0, \tag{1} \] \[ \|c_h-f_N(h/N)\|\le C N^B e^{N(F-\gamma)},\qquad\gamma>0. \tag{2} \] These are hypotheses on the specified source, not on arbitrary holomorphic test functions. Scalar or finite-dimensional vector/operator packets with the displayed norm bounds are allowed. All constants are independent of N. For any fixed phi_0>0 and fixed nonnegative integer r, there are g>0 and C',B' such that \[ \boxed{\left\|\sum_{h=-H}^Hh^r c_h e^{i\phi h}\right\| \le C'N^{B'}e^{N(F-g)},\quad \operatorname{dist}(\phi,2\pi\mathbb Z)\ge\phi_0.} \tag{3} \] The distance is at most pi; the assertion is empty if phi_0>pi. In particular no number-theoretic restriction on N is involved. Here is an exact contour proof retaining the finite endpoints. Reduce phi modulo2pi into [phi_0,2pi-phi_0], which changes no physical value. For a fixed small sigma>0 use the rectangle in the UNWRAPPED variable z whose vertical sides have Re z=+/-(H+1/2) and whose horizontal sides have Im z=+/-sigma N. Then \[ \sum_{h=-H}^H h^r f_N(h/N)e^{i\phi h} =\frac1{2\pi i}\oint z^r f_N(z/N)e^{i\phi z} (\pi\cot\pi z-i\pi)\,dz. \tag{4} \] Every enclosed integer has residue one. The subtracted entire term -i pi changes no residue and is essential for simultaneous upper and lower decay. Indeed pi cot(pi z)-i pi=2pi i/(exp(2pi i z)-1). On the upper horizontal side its product with exp(i phi z) is at most 4pi exp(-phi sigma N); on the lower side it is at most 4pi exp(-(2pi-phi)sigma N), for all sufficiently large N. On either vertical half-integer line the sharper exact bound is |exp(i phi z)(pi cot(pi z)-i pi)| <=2pi exp[-phi_0 |Im z|]<=2pi. Choose sigma<=sigma_0 so that C_0 sigma^2<=min(a delta^2/8,phi_0 sigma/2). For large N, d_N>=delta/2. The horizontal exponent in (4) is at most F-phi_0 sigma/2, and the vertical exponent is at most F-a delta^2/8. Its contour length and z^r cost only powers of N. Equation (2) contributes at most C N^(B+r+1)exp[N(F-gamma)] on the physical grid. Thus one may take g=min(gamma,a delta^2/8,phi_0 sigma/2)>0. (5) This proof neither discards a vertical current nor assumes that a universal residue rewrite lowers the maximum of arbitrary source values. Its input is precisely the state-specific analytic bound (1). ## 2. Apply the lemma BEFORE any Gaussian approximation to the filling Use the original q,Q,kappa and the exact full-jet kernel from [the coherent filling theorem](actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp.md). For t_k=(k+1/2)/N and y_k=2pi i(t_k-1/2), write \[ K_P(h)=\frac{2(-1)^{N-1}}{N^2} \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}h_k e^{hy_k} \left[(h+2Py_k/\hbar)\sinh y_k+\cosh y_k\right]. \tag{6} \] Here |h_k|=1 for every integer P and real physical data. The original normal derivative has not been dropped: 2Py_k/hbar is its unwrapped linear weight, and the h term comes from the same exact circle difference. Every factor outside exp(hy_k) is at most polynomial in N for fixed P, uniformly over k. Here beta and K_P are the coefficients of the NORMALIZED power f_P=r_N^(2P), exactly as in the filling theorem. The actual box R^(-1)R^(2P) multiplies every color pairing below by the known unit phase kappa^(2P). In particular the actual prefactor corresponding to kappa^(-P) in (10)--(11) is kappa^P. This original phase is kept; it does not change any norm estimate. Let K_P^end retain any subset of the original k values with |t_k-1/2|>=eta_0>0. For a physical EVEN core c_h=c_(-h), the original half-color convention gives the exact truncated pairing sum_(h=0)^H beta_(N-h-1)c_h =(1/2)sum_(h=-H)^H K_P(h)c_h. (7) In (6), phi_k=2pi(t_k-1/2) belongs to [-pi,pi], and dist(phi_k,2pi Z)>=2pi eta_0 on the retained endpoint strips. Apply (3) for r=0,1 and sum the N original k values. It follows that \[ \boxed{\left\|\frac12\sum_{h=-H}^H K_P^{\rm end}(h)c_h\right\| \le C_P N^{B_P}e^{N(F-g)}.} \tag{8} \] This is a bound on the EXACT finite endpoint part, with both parities, all gcd cases and the normal source retained. There is no infinite charge tail to estimate, and no O(1/N) Fresnel error against an exponential target. The bounded current of section8 in the coherent filling note is consistent with (8), but (8) does not assume that every endpoint remainder equals that one Ward forcing. ## 3. The actual mixed-source input and its precise remaining scope The EXACT finite packet in [the analytic original-source theorem](actual_pretzel_exact_analytic_color_packet.md) provides (1)--(2) for a mixed pretzel period at fixed odd s>=5, on a sufficiently small complete-color corridor. Here the other physical cusp colors may be fixed in a sufficiently small corridor. To specify the interpolation, retain a fixed regular high Newton-index window in each box, use its canonical paired factorial continuation Fhat(v-h)Fhat(v+h) and q^(h^2), and apply the UNCHANGED Hermite functional Phi_2. The lower index windows and the full nonempty alias sets are their proved exponentially smaller physical source errors. Its separate exact-interpolation bridge must be retained; a pointwise relative O(1/N) approximation on the color lattice alone does NOT imply (2) with an exponentially small Fourier error. This construction is even in the continued color, rather than an arbitrary exp(pi i h) extension. The resulting nonzero analytic leading phase, composed with chi=pi z, is even in the color variable z=h/N. Its real second derivative at zero is strictly negative, uniformly for the other sufficiently small physical colors. Taylor's formula and the elementary inequality 2|xy|<=epsilon x^2+y^2/epsilon give Re Phi(x+iy)<=Re Phi(0)-a x^2+C_0 y^2. The analytic amplitude is uniformly bounded by a polynomial in N. The exact high-window finite-source interpolation error and the alias bound supply (2), after shrinking the corridor so that its height stays within gamma/2 of the complete height. Thus (8) removes a genuine class of endpoints of this original mixed-source corridor. Aliases need not be even and are estimated before folding. Directly from the original finite H,D data, |a_n|<=1+|P| for 0<=n<N and |beta_j|<=2(1+|P|). Their entire corridor pairing therefore costs only another factor 2N(1+|P|) times the proved alias error. The exact normal forcing and the vertical color sides in (4) are both retained. This does not estimate physical colors h>H. It does not discard the central k strip, establish a nonzero filled critical pairing, or identify its action with a preferred topological longitude. A fixed-large-filling proof still requires those three steps, including the peripheral sign convention. The present source-conditioned estimate is not an all-input operator norm bound for a free exterior. ## 4. The combined source is a total derivative, with exact paired charges There is a useful exact representation for the remaining coherent packet, avoiding the separate interpolation of any a_n. For ANY physical even core in (7), set \[ \mathcal F_N(z)=\sum_{h=-H}^Hc_h e^{2\pi i h z},\qquad U_N(z)=e^{2\pi iPNz^2}\sinh(2\pi i z)\mathcal F_N(z), \qquad z_k=(k+1/2)/N-1/2. \tag{9} \] The literal entire-normal filling kernel (6) gives EXACTLY \[ \boxed{\sum_{h=0}^H\beta_{N-h-1}c_h =\frac{(-1)^{N-1}\kappa^{-P}}{2\pi iN^2} \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}U_N'(z_k).} \tag{10} \] Indeed differentiating U multiplies its sinh term by 2pi i(2PNz+h) and differentiating sinh supplies 2pi i cosh. These are precisely BOTH linear normal contributions in (6). This holds with operator-valued c_h in their unchanged exterior order. In particular U_N(1/2)=U_N(-1/2)=0, and U_N'(1/2)=U_N'(-1/2) =-2pi i exp(pi iPN/2)sum_h(-1)^h c_h. The periodic extension of U_N' is continuous, with piecewise smooth derivative. Its Fourier series is absolutely convergent (two integrations by parts bound its nonzero coefficients by a constant times frequency^(-2)). Exact midpoint Fourier selection and one integration by parts therefore prove \[ \boxed{\sum_{h=0}^H\beta_{N-h-1}c_h =(-1)^{N-1}\kappa^{-P} \sum_{m\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}} (-1)^{m(N-1)}m\int_{-1/2}^{1/2} e^{2\pi iN(Pz^2-mz)}\sinh(2\pi i z) \mathcal F_N(z)\,dz.} \tag{11} \] The series is absolutely convergent for each N. Its constants can depend on the actual source; no uniform asymptotic tail estimate is silently inferred. The zero charge vanishes EXACTLY from the two original endpoint zeros of U_N, not by discarding a Fresnel current. Because the core is even, mathcalF_N is even and U_N is odd. The integrals at -m and m are opposites, so their weighted contributions in (11) are equal. Thus the +/-m channels ADD exactly, at every parity and level, before any saddle approximation. For the source obeying (1)--(2), mathcalF_N and its fixed derivatives are exponentially small on any fixed real strip eta_0<=|z|<=1/2, by (3). Equations (10)--(11) therefore provide a source-faithful central phase problem with exact normal charge m. The finite-k endpoint bound (8) is already quantitative. Passing between a restricted central integral and (11) must still retain the new side currents at its artificial cutoff; absolute convergence at fixed N alone is not a uniform exponential bound on all charges. The uniform infinite-tail bound is proved separately below; a central-saddle conclusion is not inferred from fixed-N convergence. ## 5. A uniform exponential high-charge tail, with its paired current Under (1)--(2), the large-|m| part of (11) is exponentially smaller than exp(NF). This is a UNIFORM estimate; absolute convergence at each fixed N alone would not suffice. For fixed integer P there are M_P>0 and finite B_P,C_P, independent of N, such that \[ \boxed{\sum_{|m|>M_P} \left\|m\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}U_N(z)e^{-2\pi imNz}\,dz\right\| \le C_P N^{B_P}e^{N(F-g_*)}.} \tag{12} \] The positive gap g_* and the contour width below depend ONLY on the source hypotheses, not on P. This matters for independently large fillings with no comparability between their lengths. First, (3), for a small real neighborhood of +/-1/2 in z, extends to a FIXED small complex strip. In its exact rectangle proof, an extra Im z=v in the Fourier variable costs at most exp(2pi delta |v|N) on the physical source support. The same argument applies to fixed derivatives of mathcalF_N, by taking r larger in (3). Thus for some fixed sigma_1,g_1>0, ||mathcalF_N^(j)(+/-1/2+iv)|| <=poly(N)exp[N(F-g_1)], |v|<=sigma_1, j=0,1,2. Fix a smaller sigma>0 using ONLY this source strip. On either endpoint line, at height -v, the chirp costs at most exp(2pi|P|Nv), and its first two derivatives cost powers of N and P. Keep that v-dependent cost; do not bound it by exp(2pi|P|sigma N) and then shrink sigma as the filling length grows. For m>0 shift its Fourier integral DOWN by sigma. On the lower horizontal side the elementary physical-grid estimate ||mathcalF_N(x-i sigma)|| <=poly(N)exp[N(F+2pi delta sigma)] gives an upper bound poly(N)exp{N[F-2pi sigma(m-|P|-delta)]}. (13) Crucially the two vertical currents must be paired. Their common Fourier endpoint phase is (-1)^(mN), and their difference is V_N(v)=U_N(1/2-iv)-U_N(-1/2-iv), 0<=v<=sigma. The ORIGINAL integer Fourier polynomial mathcalF_N is periodic. Together with the sinh zeros this gives V_N(0)=V_N'(0)=0 exactly, as already checked before (11). The source derivative bound on the two vertical strips, with the chirp cost explicitly retained, gives ||V_N(v)||<=poly(N,P)v^2 exp[N(F-g_1)+2pi|P|Nv]. Consequently the paired vertical contribution obeys \[ \left\|m\int_0^\sigma e^{-2\pi mNv}V_N(v)\,dv\right\| \le\frac{\operatorname{poly}(N,P)m}{(m-|P|)^3N^3} e^{N(F-g_1)},\quad m>|P|. \tag{14} \] For m>M_P>=2|P|+2delta+2 this is at most a fixed multiple of poly(N,P)m^(-2)N^(-3)exp[N(F-g_1)], which is summable. The horizontal bounds (13) have an exponentially convergent geometric sum with gap at least 2pi sigma, independent of P. Take g_*=min(g_1,2pi sigma)>0. The upper shift for negative m is identical; for an even core it also follows from the exact +/-m identity. This proves (12). Neither individual vertical current is set to zero. Here is the precise multiport justification. Leave all remaining z_j variables REAL until their tails have been removed. On the entire source U=exp(2pi iN sum P_i z_i^2) product_i sinh(2pi i z_i) mathcalF_N(z), define the commuting COLOR-register functionals D_i U=(2pi iN^2)^(-1)sum_k partial_i U(z_(i,k)), I_(i,m)U=(-1)^(m(N-1))m integral_[-1/2,1/2] U dz_i, D_i^lo=sum_(0<|m|<=M_i) I_(i,m), D_i^tail=D_i-D_i^lo. Midpoint Poisson and the matched endpoint values prove D_i=sum_m I_(i,m) exactly. These operations act linearly on scalar color registers; they do NOT commute or reorder physical Hopf boxes or matrix-valued exterior coefficients. Exact telescoping gives \[ \prod_iD_i-\prod_iD_i^{\rm lo} =\sum_i\left(\prod_{j<i}D_j^{\rm lo}\right) D_i^{\rm tail}\left(\prod_{j>i}D_j\right). \tag{14a} \] For fixed M_j, the real-integral functional D_j^lo has supremum norm at most sum_(0<|m|<=M_j)|m|=M_j(M_j+1). The original D_j uses N samples and one derivative. Its mixed derivatives on U cost powers of N and P_j: all remaining chirps have modulus ONE at real z_j, while differentiating them supplies only P_j N. Differentiating mathcalF_N supplies integer powers of h_j, bounded by powers of N. The endpoint Fourier bound and (14) are uniform in these remaining real spectators AND in every mixed derivative just described. To see this directly, sum the other physical h_j in absolute value using the original source bound exp[N(F_0-a sum x_j^2+C sum y_j^2)]. Their sums and fixed powers of h_j cost only powers of N; no positive exponential is introduced. The contour shift and paired vertical current occur ONLY in the tail coordinate i. Thus each term of (14a) is bounded by poly_(s,p)(N)exp[N(F_0-g_*)], with g_* fixed by the source and independent of the largest slope. There is no uncontrolled infinite charge sum in a spectator coordinate. Later central saddle-contour motions are made only AFTER (14a) has removed the tails. Equations (8),(11),(12) leave a FINITE set of nonzero coherent central charges for every fixed collection of integer fillings. Their source Fourier saddle is made explicit next. Comparing the remaining charge actions and bounding colors outside the chosen corridor are separate tasks. ## 6. A nonzero central Fourier packet from the EXACT analytic source This step uses the stronger, proved input from the exact color packet: on a fixed complex polydisk, with r color ports, C_N(pi x)=N^(3/2)e^(-i s pi d/4) A(pi x) exp[N phi(x)](1+O(1/N)), phi(x)=Phi_s(pi x), phi(0)=F_0, phi''(0)=2pi i tau_s I, tau_s=(1+exp(2iu_s))/2, Im tau_s>0. (15) The exact function C_N, not just this leading expression, has the complex Gaussian bound (1) in all continued coordinates. The case needed for filling all boxes is r=s. Define the ENTIRE finite packet mathcalF_N(z)=sum_(|h_i|<=H) C_N(pi h/N) exp(2pi i h dot z). (16) It is exactly even in every z_i. For a fixed sufficiently small complex z-polydisk, the holomorphic implicit-function theorem defines grad phi(xi(z))+2pi i z=0, Psi(z)=phi(xi(z))+2pi i xi(z) dot z. Then, UNIFORMLY on a smaller fixed complex polydisk, \[ \boxed{\mathcal F_N(z)=N^{(r+3)/2}e^{-i s\pi d/4} B(z)e^{N\Psi(z)}(1+O(1/N)),\quad B(z)=\frac{(2\pi)^{r/2}A(\pi\xi(z))} {\sqrt{\det[-\phi''(\xi(z))]}}.} \tag{17} \] The Gaussian square root is fixed at zero by the positive real part of -phi''(0). In particular B(0)=A(0)(-i tau_s)^(-r/2) !=0, xi(z)=-z/tau_s+O(||z||^3), Psi(z)=F_0-i pi sum_i z_i^2/tau_s+O(||z||^4). (18) Both Psi and B are even in each z_i and B is nonzero on a smaller polydisk. All phases in (15) remain in (17). Here is the finite-source proof of (17). Apply exact half-integer cotangent rectangles in the h coordinates to (16). The two constant cotangent parts give the ordinary integral with density N^r. The nonconstant parts cost exp(-2pi sigma N) on its horizontal sides; the extra factor exp(2pi iN x dot z), the quadratic complex-source growth and the small complex z displacement cost strictly less after choosing sigma first and then the z-polydisk. The vertical h sides keep their strict endpoint gap from (1). This proves mathcalF_N(z)=N^r integral_[-d_N,d_N]^r C_N(pi x)exp(2pi iN x dot z)dx +poly(N)exp[N(F_0-g)], g>0. (19) Slightly changing the half-integer endpoints of the integral is exponentially harmless, and all corresponding side currents are in the displayed error. This is a statement about the EXACT holomorphic source; a pointwise real-grid O(1/N) error would not imply (19). Deform the ordinary integral locally to the parallel real contour through xi(z). Its end connectors retain their strict gap for small z. The real part of phi'' remains negative definite, uniformly near zero. The elementary multivariate Gaussian integral and the uniform analytic amplitude in (15) therefore give (17); its exponentially small cotangent remainder stays below the saddle after shrinking the z-polydisk. This also proves the required uniformity BEFORE any later z-contour motion. No original-cycle coefficient has been assigned. For completeness, apply (11) successively in all r filled ports. The actual R powers restore their phases as explained above. The exact corridor source is \[ (-1)^{r(N-1)}\kappa^{\sum_iP_i} \sum_{m_i\ne0}(-1)^{(N-1)\sum_i m_i}\prod_i m_i \int_{[-1/2,1/2]^r} e^{2\pi iN\sum_i(P_i z_i^2-m_i z_i)} \prod_i\sinh(2\pi i z_i)\mathcal F_N(z)\,dz. \tag{20} \] All original normal charges and the full original source are kept. Every coordinate reflection (m_i,z_i)->(-m_i,-z_i) preserves its term, so the 2^r all-unit charges have exactly equal contributions, including the even-level signs. There is no charge with m_i=0. The large-charge remainder is controlled by (12) before any Gaussian approximation; the real endpoint-frequency strips are controlled by (8). Equations (17),(20) therefore give an actual nonzero analytic source amplitude for the remaining finite central phase problem Psi(z)+2pi i sum_i(P_i z_i^2-m_i z_i). (21) The comparison of its finite charges, its legitimate local saddle contours, and the physical color complement are not replaced by formal stationarity. In particular (20) alone is not a theorem for an entire filled knot. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_filling_source_fourier_endpoint_gap.py) checks the exact finite-k normal-weighted decomposition, its retained half-color source and endpoint split, the contour equality (4), and the quantitative estimates on explicitly controlled analytic packets, and the combined-source total derivative and exact paired-charge Fourier selection in (10)--(11). The actual mixed-source hypotheses are proved in the linked source notes; finite tests alone do not establish them.

title: Exact unit-mass transport for phase-flat charged block cores
text: # Exact unit-mass transport for phase-flat charged block cores 28 October 2026. An additional constructive case of the fixed-clock mass problem covers UNBALANCED biconnected cores with any fixed number of anchors. The hypothesis is the flatness of their actual positive-binomial block connection, not balance of their individual binary-factor incidences. It is checked from the original block metadata. No finite source is changed. The conclusion is stronger than existence of a semialgebraic replacement: one constant-radius source torus has normalized logarithmic mass ONE. There is also an explicit polynomial lower bound relative to its positive capacity. This is a fixed-clock theorem. Flatness is not automatic on surviving knot sources, and this note supplies no general full-clock volume estimate. ## 1. Original blocks and a precise phase test Let Q=exp(2pi*i/N), q=exp(pi*i/N), and take the actual residual block source P(X)=gamma product_e product_(r=0)^(L_e-1) (alpha_e X_(u_e)-Q^r beta_e X_(v_e)), f(X)=P(X)/product_i X_i^(a_i), 1<=L_e<=N-1, |alpha_e|=|beta_e|=1, sum_i a_i=sum_e L_e=M. All extracted original normalizers and clock factors remain outside or in gamma as previously specified. Loops and tight cuts are treated by their exact source rules before taking this residual connected core. Assume its strict Hall inequalities: for every nonempty proper vertex set I, 0<a(I)-m_I<C_I. (1) The block coefficient identity from [the actual phase calculation](anchor_phase_cycles_and_exact_fusion.md) is product_r(alpha X_u-Q^r beta X_v) =alpha^L sum_(j=0)^L c_(L,j) w_e^j X_u^(L-j)X_v^j, c_(L,j)=|[L choose j]_Q|>0, w_e=-(beta_e/alpha_e)q^(L_e-1). (2) Assume there are unit phases eta_i such that w_e=eta_v/eta_u on every edge. Equivalently every oriented block-cycle holonomy is one. This is a finite spanning-tree test, including every parallel edge and original closure block. For actual root phases it is exact integer arithmetic modulo 2N, rather than a numerical small-phase test. Substitution X_i=eta_i^(-1)Y_i transforms the ENTIRE polynomial to P(eta^(-1)Y)=Gamma P_+(Y), P_+(Y)=product_e sum_j c_(L_e,j)Y_u^(L_e-j)Y_v^j, Gamma=gamma product_e alpha_e^(L_e)eta_u^(-L_e). Consequently the original coefficient has the exact pointing [X^a]P=Gamma product_i eta_i^(a_i) [Y^a]P_+. (3) The factors in (3) are known source factors; they are not chosen from the unknown period. Their modulus is |gamma|. ## 2. An actual regular critical point and a unit-mass sublevel torus Set G(rho)=log P_+(exp rho)-sum_i a_i rho_i. For each block use its normalized positive weights proportional to c_(L,j) exp((L-j)rho_u+j rho_v). Differentiation gives Hess G=sum_e Var_e(j)(e_v-e_u)(e_v-e_u)^t. (4) Every variance is strictly positive. Connectivity therefore makes G strictly convex modulo the common scale. It is coercive on that quotient. To see this without a capacity theorem, order the rho_i and write their successive gaps as g_j, with high vertex sets I_j. Choosing the larger endpoint of every block gives an endpoint monomial of coefficient at least one, and hence G(rho)>=sum_j [C_(I_j)-(a(I_j)-m_(I_j))]g_j >=max rho-min rho. (5) The last inequality uses the integral strict Hall condition (1). Adding the constant log|gamma| would restore the outside scalar. Thus a unique minimizer rho_* exists modulo scale. Its positive value Cap=|gamma| exp G(rho_*) is an ACTUAL regular complex critical modulus of f at X_i=eta_i^(-1)exp(rho_*,i). Holomorphic differentiation agrees with the real logarithmic derivative there, and every block is nonzero because its transformed coefficients and arguments are positive. The existing radial cut theorem in addition bounds its radius ratios by (M-1)^(k-1). On the shifted source torus X_i=eta_i^(-1)exp(rho_*,i+i theta_i), the triangle inequality in (2) gives |f(X)|<=Cap. This torus is homologous to the original coefficient torus in (C*)^k/C*, by ordinary finite changes of radii and angles; its normalized absolute logarithmic top-form mass is exactly one. Therefore |[X^a]P|<=Cap<=Mcrit(f). (6) This bypasses the unknown complexity of interior gradient transport for this entire class, including its unbalanced biconnected members. It does not assert that Cap is the largest of all complex critical moduli. ## 3. A source-exact polynomial lower bound Let B be the number of nonempty blocks. At rho_*, choose independent integer random variables J_e with probabilities p_e(j)=c_(L_e,j)exp((L_e-j)rho_u+j rho_v)/Z_e. The mean endpoint assignment is a, by criticality. Expanding P_+ gives the EXACT identity |[X^a]P|/Cap=Prob(endpoint degrees equal a). (7) The sequences p_e are log-concave. Indeed their successive ratios, apart from a positive tilt, are sin(pi(L-j)/N)/sin(pi(j+1)/N). These decrease because the sum of the two relevant cotangents is sin(pi(L+1)/N) divided by positive sine factors. For L=N-1 the ratios are constant, so the same conclusion holds. Extend log p_e affinely between integers, obtaining a concave function phi_e. If mu_e=E J_e, Jensen and the entropy bound give phi_e(mu_e)>=sum_j p_e(j)log p_e(j)>=-log(L_e+1). (8) There is an integral endpoint flow j_e with the SAME required degrees and with sum_e phi_e(j_e)>=sum_e phi_e(mu_e). Here is an elementary rounding proof. Confine each coordinate to [floor mu_e,ceil mu_e]; every phi_e is affine on this box. The nonintegral edges of a feasible flow have no degree-one vertex, since the required incidence imbalance is integral. They therefore contain an undirected cycle. Move in both directions along that cycle until an edge becomes integral. The current flow is a convex combination of the two endpoints, so at least one endpoint does not decrease the affine objective. Repeat; an integral feasible flow is reached after at most B steps. This is the usual network-flow rounding proved here with its source degrees retained. The probability of that ONE integral flow, using (8), is at least product_e(L_e+1)^(-1). Equation (7) now proves Cap/product_e(L_e+1) <= |[X^a]P| <= Cap. (9) For a fixed original diagram B is bounded independently of N, so the lower factor is polynomial in N. This is actual selected-coefficient noncancellation in a fixed sector, not a conclusion from a nonzero ambient module or a guessed local saddle. ## 4. What must still be checked for a whole knot The phase test must hold for the ACTUAL surviving block graph, after every proposed exact fusion, with all original closure and clock factors. The existing nonzero 6_3 family has a macroscopic curved bulk cycle, so the test is not automatic for alternating diagrams or arbitrary widths. No arbitrary-width hyperbolic-knot class satisfying it in every sector has been established here. An original full clock sum may also cancel between the known phases in (3) and its retained W_h. There is a finite way to certify UNIFORM anchor flatness, if a diagram class supplies the needed identities. For the original metadata each block gain is q^(b_e N+c_e+sum_j a_ej h_j), with integer coefficients. On a stratum where the nonempty blocks and chosen source fusions are fixed, spanning-tree propagation makes each cycle exponent an affine integer function of (N,h). Uniform flatness is exactly its vanishing modulo 2N on that stratum's integer clock lattice. Check its values on one lattice point and on generators of the difference lattice. The constants and linear coefficients are explicit, so this avoids an all-level numerical extrapolation. The unit-block-preserving source fusions used here only multiply or divide unit gains and impose affine charge/length equalities; their finite anchor-decreasing order gives finitely many such strata for a fixed diagram. This is a certification procedure, not a proof that the test succeeds on any new knot class. Including the clocks as extra coefficient variables would require an exact nonnegative-coefficient, phase-flat presentation of their FULL feedback and factorial weights. The anchor Ward equations alone do not provide this: their critical points are not critical in h. Equations (6)--(9) therefore cannot be assigned the knot regulator bound without that missing joint comparison, and no nonflat sectors are discarded. For the general nonflat mass problem, semialgebraic complexity of one sublevel set still does not control the particular transported source class. Effective local trivializations over a polynomial number of base intervals cannot simply be composed while retaining polynomial degree or multiplicity. This note avoids that issue only by constructing the constant-radius torus above. A bare quotient by the critical ideal is not an alternative finite-source argument. Already for f=z+z^(-1), its critical derivative z-z^(-1) has CT[z(z-z^(-1))]=-1. Thus the original coefficient functional does not annihilate the critical ideal. A toric-residue comparison must retain the differential source or construct its exact adapter, not replace this functional by evaluation on critical points. An independent proof review and fresh audit replay verified the phase normalization, strict-Hall coercivity, covariance Hessian, original coefficient/probability identity, log-concavity and source-preserving cycle rounding. The hypothesis L_e<=N-1 is essential: a length-N Fermat block has missing interior coefficients, so strict Hall alone would not imply the lower bound (9). No full-clock or knot-class conclusion is added by this review. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_flat_block_sublevel_transport.py): root-Pochhammer phases, unbalanced strict-Hall examples, convex critical points, original complex coefficients and the polynomial probability bound. These computations supplement the uniform proof above; no knot class or full-clock volume theorem is inferred from the examples.

title: Forced physical overbridges and charged full-block source fusion
text: # Forced physical overbridges and charged full-block source fusion 28 October 2026. This gives two constructive reductions of the ORIGINAL source, at every N, arbitrary braid width and arbitrary crossing signs. First, the exact bridge contractions continue through the actual closure pivots. A marked-cut extreme therefore removes a whole physical overbridge, including pieces on opposite sides of the braid cut. Second, full blocks remain exactly contractible after earlier fusions lower the source charges. All such contractions terminate, with explicit charge redistribution, scalars and clock feedback retained. This does not identify the remaining source with that of a smaller knot, make its defects sublinear, or establish geometric noncancellation. In particular the actual figure-eight macrodefects are transported into the reduced source, not removed by changing its definition. ## 1. Continue bridges through the original source Write d=N-1, Q=exp(2 pi i/N), x=-exp(-pi i/N). The [signed bridge theorem](actual_signed_overbridge_unwinding.md) gives, with the opposite physical pair fixed on its actual grids, M_j(Zout,Zin)=c_j Pout_j(Zout) Pin_j(Zin), Pin_j(Z)=Z^(-h_j)(b_j/Z;Q)_(d-h_j), Pout_j(Z)=(a_j Z;Q)_(h_j). (1) Every original c_j is the explicit signed scalar in that theorem, including kappa, the phase Q^(+/-h_j(h_j+1)/2), the spectator monomial, and 1/N. None is discarded here. Let an identity or original pivotal wire continue the first output to the next input. In the physical finite basis its operator is diag(eta t^a), 0<=a<=d. Thus t=1, eta=1 at the unpivoted marked continuation, whereas t=Q^(-1), eta=x^(1-N) (2) at an ordinary closing pivot. The whole original averaged marked row is converted to this unpivoted continuation with the SINGLE exterior factor 1/N **before** splitting crossings into clocks. This is the integer-degree source theorem already used in the [global charged state](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md). No sectorwise scalar-endomorphism or Schur argument is used. For arbitrary endpoint Fourier frame roots the exact continued wire is sum_(k,l) Pin_next(z_l) E_(l,k) Pout_prev(w_k) =N eta CT_Z Pout_prev(t Z) Pin_next(Z). (3) Indeed E=G_next diag(eta t^a) G_prev^(-1). The first matrix product recovers precisely the polynomial eta Pout_prev(t Z), since its degree is at most d. Multiplication by Pin_next has frequencies in [-d,d]. The remaining finite root sum is therefore N times its constant term, with no nonzero cyclic alias. This proves (3) even when the two old central frame parameters differ. It uses the finite interpolation source, not a bare full-Psi seam deformation. The old complementary identity consequently gives N eta (-a_j t)^h_next Q^(h_next(h_next-1)/2) *[h_j choose h_next]_Q *(a_j t b_next Q^(-1);Q)_(h_j-h_next), (4) when h_j>=h_next, and zero otherwise. Thus the same monotone clock simplex and q-multinomial compose across ALL closure continuations. The only changes are the displayed t and eta factors. Select every physical over-output-to-over-input continuation, including closure continuations, and freeze all unselected under and endpoint labels. These selected paths are disjoint. A directed cycle would be an entire link component with no under encounter. For a one-component knot with at least one crossing this is impossible: both encounters of each self-crossing lie on that component. Thus the selected components are genuine finite paths. Applying (3)--(4) to every such path gives exact simultaneous contraction of all TRUE physical overbridge interiors, independent of where the braid was cut. After homogenizing, each physical overbridge still has total block length exactly (d-h_first)+sum(h_j-h_next)+h_last=d. (5) The finite multinomial, every c_j, every closing eta and all t shifts remain. There is one factor 1/N per bridge, canceled by its anchor root sum as in the global charged theorem. The single exterior marked factor 1/N remains. In particular the number of polynomial bridge events may be reduced from the number of open-braid paths to the number of physical diagram overbridges. No cup, marked row or nonordinary turn is moved in this assertion. ## 2. A whole overbridge is forced to an extreme source face Use the actual finite cyclic-source support theorem from [the cut peeling proof](original_source_cyclic_variation_peeling.md) and its [current-clock dictionary](actual_alternating_balanced_source.md). For either sign, put u=[b-a-1], v=[a-c], t0=[c-e], z=[e-b]. A supported local crossing has u+v+t0+z=d. The actual overclock is h_plus=u+v, h_minus=u+z=d-t0. (6) The whole original source forces at its first position-1 crossing u=v=0, and at its last position-1 crossing v=t0=0. These are actual pathwise statements, for every cut color, before coefficient sums. They apply after the whole source replacement preceding (3). Suppose the first position-1 crossing is positive. It is an OVER encounter at the first cut head, and (6) forces h=0. After the exact bridge sums, monotonicity forces every subsequent clock of this physical overbridge to be zero. If the cut lies inside the bridge, the preceding encounter at that cut head must be the last negative position-1 crossing: only the negative OVER output is on that head. Equation (6) forces its clock d. Monotonicity forces the entire pre-cut portion of the same physical overbridge to have clock d. The bridge therefore has either all clocks zero (if the cut is its initial endpoint), or the form d,...,d | 0,...,0, (7) where the bar is precisely the marked continuation. Dually, if the last position-1 crossing is negative, the distinguished bridge has an all-d terminal portion, and an all-zero portion beyond the marked continuation if that continuation is inside the bridge. Consequently its homogeneous source kernel has exactly ONE nonzero-length block, and that block has length d: the input block, output block, or the single internal d-to-0 jump. All its other Pochhammer lengths vanish and its multinomial is one. The FULL bridge, of arbitrary length and signs, is thus a reproducing block against the complete remaining exterior, to which Section 3 applies. The propagation in this paragraph is a statement about the EXACT SUMMED clock sector. It is not a pointwise restriction on each unsummed cyclic path. For example at N=2 the word [1,2,-1,-2] has a supported original path with clocks (0,0,1,1); its increasing overbridge clocks cancel under (4). Only the initial clock extreme itself is the pointwise cut restriction. This applies to arbitrary signed words having first position-1 sign positive or last position-1 sign negative, with no alternation, twist-family or bridge-width hypothesis. A whole-word cyclic recut may put any positive position-1 occurrence first; if none exists, the last such occurrence is negative. Such a recut uses the original knot invariant's whole braid-conjugacy equivalence before decomposition, and is not an identification of its individual clock sectors. The exact source reduction itself needs only the stated first/last sign condition and the local support proof above. All feedback of the removed bridge remains explicit. In particular its under continuation is z_out=x^sigma z_in when h=0, z_out=x^sigma Q^sigma z_in when h=d. (8) The second line is Q^(-sigma d)=Q^sigma, not the first line. The original integer charge d and its phase must not be discarded as if this were a zero clock. Remaining bridge parameters still depend on all surviving clocks through the proved feedback matrix. ## 3. Full blocks fuse arbitrary relative source charges Write B_d(X,Y;a)=product_(r<d)(X-Q^r aY), s=aQ^(-1). Root complementation gives B_d=sum_(j=0)^d X^(d-j)(sY)^j. For ANY polynomial exterior F and ANY 0<=q_X,q_Y<=d, [X^q_X Y^q_Y] B_d(X,Y;a) F(X,Y,U) =s^(d-q_X) [Y^(q_X+q_Y-d)] F(sY,Y,U). (9) The right side is zero when its source charge is negative. This is an exact coefficient identity, without a bound on the degree or valency of F. To prove it, the term X^r of F contributes only j=d-q_X+r. The left side thus includes r<=q_X. On the right, every omitted r>q_X has Y-degree at least d-q_X+r>d>=q_Y in the unshifted source, and cannot contribute. Its scalar is exactly s^(d-q_X), as displayed. Equivalently the substituted exterior is needed only modulo the actual remaining source charge plus one. The new anchor charge is q_new=q_X+q_Y-d. (10) It stays at most min(q_X,q_Y), and is nonnegative precisely when the saturated pair has enough charge to support its d internal factors. Thus a full block never stops being contractible merely because earlier fusions lowered its endpoint charges. Equation (9) extends the previous q_X=q_Y=d source reproducing identity. All scalar monomials generated by the substitution remain. For a loop of ANY length L, B_L(X,X;a)=X^L (a;Q)_L. (11) Extract its displayed scalar and lower the charge of X by L; negative charge means zero. In particular a full loop requires q_X=d and then removes X by evaluating the entire exterior at X=0. Its scalar is (a;Q)_d=G_N(aQ^(-1)), G_N(t)=sum_(j=0)^d t^j. (12) At unit root phases this is the retained resonant value N, zero, or 2/(1-q^m) already computed in the general fusion theorem. For partial loops, (a;Q)_L can have exponential size and MUST remain; no tame-modulus claim is made for (11). A zero-charge anchor is also eliminated exactly by evaluating its whole incident polynomial at zero. Each outgoing B_L(X,Y;a) then contributes (-a)^L Q^(L(L-1)/2) Y^L; each incoming block contributes its other endpoint to the power L. These monomials lower the neighboring source charges by L, retaining their exact coefficients. A negative resulting charge gives another exact zero. It follows that loop extraction, zero-charge evaluation and all full-block contractions form a TERMINATING reduction for every original clock sector, with no branching sum or omitted current. Each loop step removes an edge, each other step removes an anchor, and no block length increases. The residual source is loop-free, has all charges between 1 and d, and has no length-d block. It is an exact charged polynomial exterior, not automatically the source of another knot diagram. ## 4. Defect transport and the full-block topology Let S_v count all incident factor lengths, with loops counted twice, and define delta_v=S_v-2q_v. Under a nonloop full contraction, S_new=S_X+S_Y-2d, q_new=q_X+q_Y-d, delta_new=delta_X+delta_Y. (13) Thus opposite macrodefects can cancel when the actual full-block adjacency permits their fusion. Other macrodefects can add. Partial loop extraction removes 2L from S and L from q, so preserves delta. A zero-charge evaluation distributes its removed incident lengths as precisely the charge loads just described. These are actual source transformations, rather than a declaration that the shell has become balanced. There is also a useful topology-only zero test. If a connected full-block subgraph has m vertices and r full edges, its internal degree rd cannot exceed sum q_v in a nonzero source coefficient. Since every q_v<=d, r>=m+1 forces zero. If r=m, all its q_v must equal d. Hence the full-block graph of a nonzero sector is a PSEUDOFOREST. Its trees reduce by (9) to charge q_C=sum_(v in C) q_v-(m-1)d. (14) A unicyclic component reduces to the explicit full-loop scalar and evaluation of its complete exterior at its surviving anchor zero. This gives exact outward monomial loads. A component with q_C<0 vanishes. Different spanning-tree elimination orders give equal complete source pairings because every step is the ordinary coefficient identity (9); the retained gauges and scalar phases can of course be expressed in different coordinates. Balanced star--triangle fusion is now available wherever the reduced actual anchor still has charge d, exactly three incident blocks, and total length 2d. These conditions are explicit and testable. The forced bridge alone does not ensure them. The [all-N figure-eight support theorem](actual_alternating_balanced_source.md) already shows why setting the remaining defects to zero would discard the original source. Repeating the new reduction does terminate, but termination at a positive geometric core or a nonzero leading scalar remains to be proved. ## 5. Reproducible audit python3 experiments/audit_actual_forced_source_fusion.py The audit checks identity and original pivot continuations between different finite Fourier frames at N=2,...,10, all relative charges and arbitrary monomial exteriors at those levels, twelve arbitrary sign/width physical-bridge support problems (including bridges crossing multiple closure heads), and eight COMPLETE original signed word sources. Every clock sector of each whole-source test is reduced by (9)--(12), compared with its unreduced exact source, then summed with the original feedback weights and compared with the original crossing matrices and pivotal cut. The N=3 tests include surviving reduced sources with charges strictly between 0 and d. These checks validate the formulas; the general proofs are the coefficient and support arguments above.

title: A full-source tree channel exceeds the hyperbolic volume rate
text: # A full-source tree channel exceeds the hyperbolic volume rate 28 October 2026. The short-complement forest representation is exact, but its individual source channels do not automatically satisfy the hyperbolic-volume bound. This failure already occurs for the ORIGINAL figure-eight source AFTER its forced full block has been contracted. An explicit all-short spanning-tree term has rate -5 J(1/5)=0.79366964575974769..., J(s)=integral_0^s log(2 sin(pi t)) dt, (1) whereas Vol(4_1)/(2 pi)=0.32306594721945051.... All central norm factors, short-root Jacobians and the extracted source loop are included. Thus direct absolute estimation of this exact tree representation cannot give the conjectured sharp upper bound. The statement concerns this representation and its absolute envelope; it does not exclude a further phase-aware regrouping of its channels. There is a separate algebraic limitation: if ordinary parent charges larger than N-1 are retained during iteration, jets only at the short roots can require order proportional to N, even at two anchors. Bounded anchor count alone does not bound that local jet depth. ## 1. The actual source after the forced full block Use N=5r+1, r>=1, d=N-1=5r and the actual overclocks of the figure-eight word [1,-2,1,-2] h=(0,v,w,t)=(0,3r,2r,4r). (2) The [actual finite block table](actual_alternating_balanced_source.md) gives its entire closure-contracted source, after the displayed unit coordinate gauges, as [A^d B^d C^d D^d] B_d(B,C;1) B_(d-v)(D,A;Q^(v+1)) B_v(A,B;Q^(-v+w+1)) B_(d-w)(C,B;Q^(w+2)) B_w(B,D;Q^(-w-t-1)) B_(d-t)(A,D;Q^(-v)) B_t(D,C;1), (3) with Q=exp(2 pi i/N) and B_L(X,Y;a)=product_(j<L)(X-Q^j aY). All original external and clock scalars remain; they have unit modulus or polynomial size at complete color in these singleton overbridges and do not alter the rates below. Contracting the first, genuinely forced full block sets B=Q^(-1)C. The middle C-to-B factor becomes a loop. Consequently (3) is EXACTLY Q^(-w) L_w [A^d C^w D^d] E(A,C,D), L_w=(Q^(w+1);Q)_(d-w)=F_d/F_w, (4) where F_k=(Q;Q)_k and E=B_(d-v)(D,A;Q^(v+1)) B_v(A,C;Q^(w-v)) B_w(C,D;Q^(-w-t)) B_(d-t)(A,D;Q^(-v)) B_t(D,C;1). (5) The factor Q^(-w) is the tail normalization of B_w(Q^(-1)C,D;...). The source charge of C is w, rather than d. To apply the original ordinary-d forest residue formula one equivalently uses [A^d C^d D^d] C^(d-w) E. (6) This monomial source padding is compulsory and is retained below. Equations (3)--(6) are ordinary coefficient identities, preserving the original source. No new boundary functional has been chosen. ## 2. A specified original relative-residue channel Choose the two actual tree edges A -> C: length v=3r, root coefficient Q^(-r), D -> C: length t=4r, root coefficient 1. (7) Their SHORT complementary polynomials are S_A=product_(i=0)^(2r)(A-Q^(2r+i)C), S_D=product_(j=0)^r(D-Q^(4r+j)C). (8) Take regular fixed centers C_C=1, C_A and C_D distinct from 0 and 1 and from each other. In the complete forest formula of [the original complementary source](actual_complementary_source_transport.md), the ALL-SHORT component contains every pair of roots in (8), with the original relative-cycle coefficient. Select precisely i=r, j=0: A=Q^(3r) C, D=Q^(4r) C, C^N=1. (9) This is not an assumed geometric critical point; it is one explicit nonzero term of the exact original relative residue formula. The two central factors in its numerator are K_A=C_A-1, K_D=C_D-1. At (9) their original Fermat denominators are 1-C_A and 1-C_D. They cancel EXACTLY, with product sign +1. Thus there is no omitted central multiplier, large-center choice or inverse central norm affecting this term. The remaining Jacobian is S_A'(A) S_D'(D) N C^d. (10) The numerator has total degree 3d-v-t, equal to the total degree of this Jacobian. Therefore the N root labels of C have identical values. Their sum cancels the N in (10) exactly. The whole selected channel, including the source loop (4), is, up to the fixed relative orientation sign, T_r=Q^(-w) L_w E_rest(Q^(3r),1,Q^(4r)) /[S_A'(Q^(3r)) S_D'(Q^(4r))], (11) where E_rest is (5) with the two selected long tree blocks removed. There is no factorial normalizer or root-label average suppressed in (11). An individual ungrouped C root has magnitude |T_r|/N; this has the same exponential rate. ## 3. Exact magnitude and its entropy All factors in (11) are nonzero. Directly splitting the short-root derivatives gives |S_A'|=|F_r|^2, |S_D'|=|F_r|. (12) The three remaining long products have respective root intervals 2r+1,...,4r; 3r+1,...,5r; 3r+1,...,4r. Their product magnitude is |F_(4r)/F_(2r)| * |F_(5r)/F_(3r)| *|F_(4r)/F_(3r)|. Together with |L_w|=N/|F_(2r)|, this gives |T_r|=N^2 |F_(4r)|^2 /(|F_(2r)|^2 |F_(3r)|^2 |F_r|^3) =N^2/|F_r|^5. (13) The final equality uses the exact root reflection |F_k F_(d-k)|=N at k=r and 2r. It is not an asymptotic estimate. The uniform factorial estimate log|F_k|=N J(k/N)+O(log N) now proves (1), since r/N tends to 1/5. The strict comparison with the figure-eight volume does not require decimal diagnostics. Since sin(pi s)<=pi s, -5J(1/5)>=1-log(2pi/5)>=2-2pi/5>26/35. The calibrated figure-eight volume is 2D(exp(pi i/3)), and the dilogarithm series gives D(exp(pi i/3))<=sum_(n>=1)1/n^2=pi^2/6. Hence its volume rate is at most pi/6<11/21<26/35. The actual rates are the decimals in (1). Thus the triangle-inequality envelope of this tree representation is too large even after the genuine source-forced full contraction. Its currents and root channels must undergo further cancellations or exact regrouping before a sharp Rivin-volume estimate is possible. We do not assert that (2) is a leading surviving clock sector, or that an individual residue rate is the rate of its complete source. The finite audit certifies nonzero complete clock-sector coefficients at several levels as an additional check, not an all-r hypothesis. ## 4. Short-root jets can require macroscopic depth The obstacle here is algebraic and has arbitrary degree. Let 1<=m<N, L=N-m, and put B=B_L(X,Y;a), S=B_m(X,Y;aQ^L), q_X=d, q_Y=2d, s<=floor((d+m-1)/m). Define the allowed homogeneous exterior H_s=X^d S(X,Y)^s Y^(d+m-1-ms). (14) Its degree is 3d-L=2d+m-1, precisely the exterior degree required by this pair of source charges. It vanishes to order s at EVERY short-root branch S=0. In particular all normal jets of order strictly less than s are zero there. Nevertheless [X^d Y^(2d)] B H_s =B(0,1) S(0,1)^s !=0. (15) Indeed the exterior factor X^d forces every other factor to its X-constant term. All their Y-degrees sum to 2d and their constants are nonzero for a!=0. For fixed m, s can be proportional to N. Already m=2, L=d-1 excludes the full blocks removed in (4). Therefore no unrestricted interpolation of these larger ordinary source charges using ONLY short-root jets of depth bounded by anchor count is valid. This does not obstruct retaining the original Fermat-root/mixed-current channels, or derivatives on a complete finite-Frobenius presentation. Such channels contain source data which short-root evaluations alone have lost. Nor is (14) claimed to be a new original-knot source: it refutes the unrestricted arbitrary-exterior interpolation needed for such a proposed closure. ## 5. Audit python3 experiments/audit_actual_forced_source_tree_entropy.py The audit verifies the actual figure-eight block table, the full source/loop reduction, the exact nonzero central-norm cancellation and ALL C-root labels of the specified relative-residue channel. It checks (13) independently by complex products and reflection, the actual fixed-clock source over finite cyclotomic fields, and the short-root-jet obstruction including m=2. It imports no volume proof; the rate comparison is the elementary argument above.

title: The actual four-line Fermat crossing and its unavoidable exponential action
text: # The actual four-line Fermat crossing and its unavoidable exponential action 28 October 2026. The compactified cap sources form an explicit full head frame with an exact inverse and the ORIGINAL basis as its normalized cap value. This gives a four-Fermat-line formula for the actual crossing. The full frame and EACH selected corner have a sharp positive exponential norm on fixed-log root charts, although the separate quad-line coefficients are polynomial. That action must be retained in a geometric comparison. The cyclic conjugation and existence of dilogarithmic gauge action are already established in the [actual Hilbert-90 gauge](actual_hilbert90_gauge_dilogarithm_action.md) and [controlled cyclic source](controlled_cyclic_euler_source.md). They are not counted as new here. The new content is the full dual frame, its cap-compatible four-leg actual kernel, the selected sharp norm scale, and an all-N support obstruction for independent frames. No positive geometric crossing identity or volume limit is claimed. ## 1. The full coherent frame has an explicit dual Use N>=2, d=N-1, q,Q,Z,S,P,L from [the cap-residue theorem](cap_wall_fermat_quad_residue_transport.md). Thus u^N+v^N=w^N, uvw!=0, and P_n=v^n/product_(r=1)^n(w-uQ^r), L_n=v^-n product_(r=0)^(n-1)(w-uQ^r). The N-column coherent frame is M_(n,j)=P_n(uQ^j,v,w), 0<=n,j<N. (1) It has the EXACT inverse (M^-1)_(j,n) =v^N Q^n L_n(uQ^j,v,w) /[N(uQ^j)^(N-1)(w-uQ^j)]. (2) Indeed the columns are eigenvectors of A=Z^-1(wI-vS), with distinct eigenvalues uQ^j. The corresponding left eigenvectors are L(uQ^j,v,w)Z. Different eigenvalues are orthogonal, while their diagonal pairing is L(uQ^j,v,w)Z P(uQ^j,v,w) =N(uQ^j)^(N-1)(w-uQ^j)/v^N. (3) To compute it, sum (w-uQ^j)Q^n/(w-uQ^(j+n)) and use the logarithmic derivative of w^N-u^N. Every factor in (3) is a unit on the chart. This proves (2), including its output clock. ## 2. A cap-normalized circulant, with exact inverse Set w=1 and take u=(1-v^N)^(1/N), u(0)=1. Order the columns by k=-j modulo N. Multiply column k>=1 by v^(N-k)/F_(N-k), and leave column k=0 unchanged. Call the result K(v). The all-cusp residue formulas prove K(0)=I. (4) Extend p_n=P_n(u,v,1) periodically. Put H_(n,k)=p_(n-k), r_0=1, r_k=(uQ;Q)_(N-k)/F_(N-k), 1<=k<N. Then exactly K=H diag(r_k). (5) For P_n(uQ^-k)=p_(n-k)/p_(-k) and p_(-k)=v^(N-k)/(uQ;Q)_(N-k), proving (5). All r_k tend to one, with r_k-1=O(v^N). Thus the FULL head frame, not only one vector, extends invertibly through the actual cap wall. The circulant has an especially simple inverse. For general homogeneous u,v,w, define kappa=v^N/[N u^(N-1)(w-u)], h_n=kappa (v/Q)^n/product_(r=1)^n(w-uQ^-r). Then H^-1_(n,k)=h_(n-k). (6) For a proof, (2) at j=0 gives the zeroth row of the inverse circulant; finite-product reflection gives exactly h_n. Thus (6) is a finite cyclic beta-convolution identity with its WHOLE rational scalar. At the cap branch kappa→1 and H→I. The apparent 0/0 has this prescribed regular extension. The associated known cyclic Weyl shear is exactly H^-1 S H=S, H^-1 Z H=u^-1(wI-vS)Z. (7) It follows from u H(QS)=(w-vS)H(S) and ZH(S)=H(QS)Z. The new clock's Nth power is one precisely because w^N-v^N=u^N. Its compensating root u must not be dropped. ## 3. The original crossing in four Fermat lines Let R be either ORIGINAL mixed crossing, with its original Cartan scalar inside R or in the specified external line. Choose Fermat triples f_i on its two incoming and two outgoing heads. Define R_F=(M_3^-1 tensor M_4^-1)R(M_1 tensor M_2). Equations (1)--(3) give its explicit four-line kernel: (R_F)_(j3,j4;j1,j2) =v3^N v4^N / [N^2 (u3Q^j3)^(N-1)(w3-u3Q^j3) (u4Q^j4)^(N-1)(w4-u4Q^j4)] *sum_(n1,n2,n3,n4) Q^(n3+n4) L_n3(u3Q^j3,v3,w3)L_n4(u4Q^j4,v4,w4) R_(n3,n4;n1,n2) P_n1(u1Q^j1,v1,w1)P_n2(u2Q^j2,v2,w2). (8) The original crossing support reduces this to three independent finite indices. There is no asymptotic substitution or new cap. One can instead use the cap-normalized K frames, or H with the explicit r factors in (5). The four external kernels are then p and the reflected cyclic sources h in (6). At all four cap walls this identity specializes back to the original crossing MATRIX by (4). In a whole plat every interior inverse frame cancels; actual rows, columns, coupons and scalar lines all move. There are two distinct applications. For the original PHYSICAL head R in (8), cups and caps remain their original balanced arrays, transported by these frames; they are not replaced by corner vectors. The literal cup is C_x|d,0>, so the physical transformed cup keeps (K_1^-1 tensor K_2^-1)C_x|d,0>. Alternatively first use the proved pair-fused corner presentation, then apply these head frames to its RELATIVE heads. Its within-pair crossing has four such lines, while its between-pair kernel acts on four relative heads and has eight external lines. The formulas apply to both presentations, but they must not be conflated. The transported Hopf currents are also explicit. On a balanced head of color x, K_head=xZ^-1 and F_head=S(1-QZ); their H images follow by (7). At completeness the original scaled E is the exact cyclic expression S^-1(Z^-1-1). At other colors its original bottom projector must also move. No bare current is left in the old relative frame. Equation (8) is an exact four-line ACTUAL identity. Arbitrary independent f_i are not thereby geometric shared-face data. ## 4. Sharp exponential norms include every selected corner Take canonical unit roots and compatible fixed logarithms u=exp(a/N), v=exp(b/N), w=1, exp(a)+exp(b)=1. Assume the central values stay away from zero and the logarithms in a fixed compact set. Define gamma_*=-integral_0^(1/6)log(2sin(pi t))dt >0. Then lim (1/N)log||H||_2=lim (1/N)log||H^-1||_2=gamma_*, lim (1/N)log cond_2(H)=2gamma_*. (9) The same holds for the cap-normalized frame K. For EVERY corner j=j(N), uniformly in that choice, lim (1/N)log||K e_j||_2=gamma_*, lim (1/N)log||e_j^t K^-1||_2=gamma_*. (10) In the existing figure-eight normalization, gamma_*=Vol(4_1)/(4pi); the integral definition alone suffices. These are the standard Euclidean norms of the explicitly chosen head basis. When used on the actual relative corner presentation, they concern its original corner sources. A further nonunitary physical fusion change needs its own comparison and may not be ignored in a whole physical norm estimate. Here is a complete proof. The elementary marked root-product comparison gives, uniformly in n,k, N^-C/|F_n| <= |p_n|, |h_n| <= N^C/|F_n|, N^-C <= |r_k| <= N^C. (11) For each product the relative logarithmic errors are O(1/min(j,N-j)); their sum is O(log N). The finitely many endpoint ratios have nonzero limits, because the marked central value of u differs from one. For h use (6), the identical inverse-Q factorial magnitude, and the nonzero bounded kappa. The r assertion is the same comparison in (5). The elementary uniform factorial estimate proved in [the full-Euler estimate](full_euler_atom_dilog_and_endpoint_regions.md) is log|F_n|=N J(n/N)+O(log N), J(s)=integral_0^s log(2sin(pi t))dt. Its minimum is J(1/6)=-gamma_* and its maximum is J(5/6)=gamma_*. Consequently max_n 1/|F_n| has rate gamma_*. The norm of an N by N matrix is between its maximum entry magnitude and N times that magnitude. Applied to H and H^-1, this proves (9). Every circulant column is a permutation of p, and every inverse row a permutation of h, so their Euclidean norms have the same rate. The polynomial r factors in (5) prove both claims for K and (10). In particular e_j^t K^-1 K e_j is EXACTLY one, while the product of its selected row and column norms has rate 2gamma_*. This is selected source cancellation, not merely poor conditioning of an unrelated auxiliary module. The polynomial quad-LINE coefficients do not make the FULL frame subexponential. This dilogarithmic action has to enter the geometric phase calculation. There is no contradiction with the cap theorem's fixed-log line bounds: a full raw frame includes uQ^j with bulk j, whose marked logarithms need not stay bounded. Even for fixed-log selected lines, a polynomial transition COEFFICIENT compares two vectors which can both have exponential norm. For comparison, the UNNORMALIZED coherent frame M in (1) is even worse: lim (1/N)log||M||_2 =lim (1/N)log||M^-1||_2=2gamma_*, lim (1/N)log cond_2(M)=4gamma_*. Its largest entry is exactly max|p_n|/min|p_n|, since M_(n,j)=p_(n+j)/p_j. In (2), the inverse entries equal p_j/p_(n+j) times a uniformly polynomial factor, using L_n P_n=(w-u)/(w-uQ^n). The factorial profile proves the displayed limits. The cap column factors in (5) therefore remove part, but not all, of the exponential condition number. Both normalizations must remain explicit in a four-face comparison. ## 5. What tetrahedral variable the principal shear needs For fixed-log roots u,v→1, let the input clock be A, output clock U, and let p be their common wavefunction momentum. S has symbol p^-1. Equation (7) has the principal graph t=U/A=1-p^-1. (12) Its generating action is Li_2(t)-Li_2(1), with the branches inherited from the cyclic product. Differentiation gives p_out=p_in=(1-t)^-1. If p is in the upper half-plane, t is its positive quad rotation. The variable needing a geometric mark is the BULK ratio U/A, not the central Fermat value u^N. The actual momentum has a holonomy meaning. In the existing Gauss coordinates K=x/U, e=(1-x^2/U)p/x, f=(1-U)/p, G=[[K,e],[Kf,fe+K^-1]], direct multiplication gives G(1,p^-1)^t=x^-1(1,p^-1)^t. (13) Thus p^-1 is the selected meridian eigenflag in that frame. The other three reference flags must still be identified with the actual shared developing flags to make (12) a geometric tetrahedron. A single eigenflag/source ratio does not establish that four-face comparison. The action's existence is already known; its exact four-leg source and scale (9)--(10) are the new comparison information here. ## 6. Independent line frames cannot be one basic tetrahedron There is an all-N support obstruction to a naive reading of (8). Take four INDEPENDENT cap parameters z_i with u_i=(1-z_i^N)^(1/N), v_i=z_i, w_i=1 and H frames. Every entry of (H_3^-1 tensor H_4^-1)R(H_1 tensor H_2) is a NONZERO algebraic germ. For input (a,b) and output (c,e), let r=-a mod N and s=-b mod N in the head range. The coefficient of z_1^r z_2^s z_3^c z_4^e is uniquely the original route with both intermediate R indices (0,0). It equals R_(00,00) (-1)^(c+e)Q^[c(c-1)/2+e(e-1)/2] /[F_r F_s F_c F_e], (14) which is nonzero with the original Cartan line retained. Each degree is less than N, so no central correction to u_i enters. The four cyclic shifts fix both intermediate indices uniquely, which proves (14) with no possible cancellation. The basic matrix tetrahedron kernel instead has strict support delta i+j=l modulo N, hence only N^3 potential nonzero entries. Independent diagonal face gauges and Weyl index permutations preserve that support count. Therefore this generic four-line actual kernel cannot be a SINGLE such tetrahedron under those changes. Coupled shared-face parameters, additional shears, or several tetrahedra are necessary. This does not exclude a genuine four-face geometric identity. It states precisely what (8) alone lacks. Proving actual shared developing-flag relations, with their full source and phase, remains the next comparison; no broad volume claim follows here. ## 7. Reproducible checks The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_four_line_fermat_crossing.py) and [saved output](../experiments/actual_four_line_fermat_crossing_results.json) pass 56 full coherent/circulant frames at N=2,...,8, including the dual inverse, exact nonlinear clock transport and all column normalizations. They check 56 mixed positive/negative ORIGINAL crossing entries by an independent sum using the literal E and Cartan coefficients, with the full four-line kernel retained. The 8,771 support witness coefficients are nonzero at every matrix position in these levels. Five norm-scale diagnostics through N=256 approach the limits in (9)--(10); the limits are proved by the uniform product estimates, not those samples.
