Independent proof review and rerun checked the exact dual, reflected inverse, all conditioning rates, actual kernel order, full-support witness, and physical-versus-relative source scope.

title: The saturated four-port factorial action is a hyperideal tetrahedron volume
text: # The saturated four-port factorial action is a hyperideal tetrahedron volume 29 October 2026. The positive FACE-NORMALIZED Racah partition has an explicit local geometric action. Six folded Casimir labels determine the six dihedral angles of a truncated hyperideal tetrahedron; the four supported face sums are precisely its four vertex-angle conditions. The optimized action equals its actual hyperbolic volume divided by pi. This is proved here from a Lorentz Gram construction, finite rational identities and a direct first-variation calculation. No asymptotic 6j volume theorem is an input. The face normalization is essential. This note does not identify an arbitrary physical recoupling energy with that normalization, discard high partners/normals, or infer a global knot triangulation from one local tetrahedron. The actual four-port source kernel and its weighting must be matched separately. ## 1. The exact local angle dictionary and positive scalar action Order the six colors as (a,b,c,d,e,f). The four vertex triples and three opposite quadrilateral sums are F=(a+b+e, c+d+e, a+d+f, b+c+f), Q=(a+b+c+d, a+c+e+f, b+d+e+f). (1) For the geometric theorem first take real scaled colors in 0<a,b,c,d,e,f<1/2, every F_i>1. (2) Put alpha_a=pi-2pi a, and similarly for the other five. These angles are in (0,pi), and at each of the four indicated vertices sum_incident alpha=3pi-2pi F_i<pi. (3) Thus each vertex will be hyperideal, with a geodesic polar truncation triangle of area pi-sum alpha=2pi(F_i-1). All triangle deficits F_i-2(color in that face) are strictly between 0 and 1. The source-compatible quantum scaling is EXACTLY a=(j_a+1/2)/N, alpha_a=pi-(2j_a+1)pi/N, c_(j_a)=q^(2j_a+1)+q^(-2j_a-1)=-2cos alpha_a. (4) If the six folded integer labels are <=floor((N-1)/2) and every face sum is >=N-1, then (3) is at most pi-pi/N. Its truncation triangle area is (2pi/N)(faceSum-(N-1)+1/2). The only zero edge angles are the odd simple Steinberg labels. They are treated by continuous limiting geometry, not as strictly positive interior tetrahedral angles. These are internal Casimir angle coordinates; (4) is not an auxiliary-meridian identification. Let L(t)=integral_0^t log|2sin pi u|du, with period 1. On the interval max F_i<Z<min Q_k define A(Z)=L(Z-1)-sum_(i=1)^4 L(Z-F_i) -sum_(k=1)^3 L(Q_k-Z), M=(1/2)sum_faces [sum_(edges in face)L(F_i-2edge)-L(F_i-1)], Psi=max_Z A(Z)+M. (5) The interval is nonempty: every Q_k-F_i is a positive triangle deficit from one of the other faces. It lies in (1,2). For reference the finite positive scalar producing (5) is R_N=N sum_(max faceSum<=z<=min quadSum) s_(z-(N-1)) / {product_faces s_(z-faceSum) product_quads s_(quadSum-z)}, D_face=product_(edges in face)s_(faceSum-2edge) /[N s_(faceSum-(N-1))], W_N=R_N sqrt(product_faces D_face). (6) All factors in (6) are positive. It is the root of the explicitly normalized squared generic factorial expression, not the bare Racah sum. The phase-coherent root sum follows because its numerator has exactly one [N] zero and its seven denominator indices are <N. The finite phase/metric statements are proved in [the supported Racah theorem](actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.md). For the shifted scaled variables (4), use Z=(z+7/4)/N: Z-F_i=(z-faceSum+1/4)/N, Q_k-Z=(quadSum-z+1/4)/N. Uniform all-index factorial estimates then give (5) as the limiting logarithmic action, with O(log N) endpoint errors. The geometric identification of this action is independent of a proposed source normalization. At six colors 1/3 the bare optimized A is 3v3/pi, whereas Psi=v3/pi; omitting M would already give the wrong volume. In these conventions log W_N/N has action Psi; the SQUARED weight W_N^2 has action 2Psi. That factor must be retained in a later energy or doubled-source comparison. ## 2. An own existence/uniqueness construction of the tetrahedron Number the vertices by the four triples in (1). The edge endpoints are a:13, b:14, c:24, d:23, e:12, f:34. Let n_i be its four outward face normals, face i opposite vertex i. Their prescribed Lorentz Gram matrix is G_ii=1, G_12=-cos alpha_f, G_13=-cos alpha_c, G_14=-cos alpha_d, G_23=-cos alpha_b, G_24=-cos alpha_a, G_34=-cos alpha_e. (7) We prove that G has signature (3,1), rather than assuming an angle realization theorem. Every three-by-three principal minor corresponds to three angles A,B,C at a vertex, A+B+C<pi. Its determinant is -4 cos((A+B+C)/2)cos((A+B-C)/2) cos((A-B+C)/2)cos((-A+B+C)/2)<0. (8) Its two-by-two minors are sin^2(alpha)>0, so that block has signature (2,1) and can be realized in Lorentz three-space. Its inverse has all entries negative: its off-diagonal cofactors have numerator cos C+cos A cos B>sin A sin B>0 and its determinant is negative. If the three inner products of the fourth normal with this block are nonpositive, its projection to the block has nonpositive square. Adding a new spacelike coordinate makes its square one, with a nonzero fourth component. This constructs G with signature (3,1). Otherwise choose a nonacute dihedral A>=pi/2 among these products and call its two normals n_0,n_1. At most two dihedrals can be nonacute, and two such edges must be opposite, because any two meeting at a vertex have sum <pi. The other products of n_0 are -cos B,-cos C, and those of n_1 are -cos D,-cos E. The three old normals have last mutual angle F, with D+E+F<pi. The vertex conditions imply B+D<pi-A, C+E<pi-A. In n_1-perpendicular Lorentz space define m_2=(n_2+cos D n_1)/sin D, m_3=(n_3+cos E n_1)/sin E, <m_2,m_3>=-(cos F+cos D cos E)/(sin D sin E)<-1. Write n_0=(-cos A)n_1+sin A u. The two required products of u with m_2,m_3 are both <-1: for example <u,m_2>=(-cos B-cos A cos D)/(sin A sin D)<-1. The inverse Gram matrix of m_2,m_3 has every entry negative. Thus their prescribed negative-product projection of u has negative square. An additional spacelike coordinate again makes u^2=1 and constructs the fourth normal independently. This proves det G<0 throughout (2), including the possible two opposite obtuse edges. Let C=adj(G). Its diagonal entries are negative by (8), so the dual vectors v_i=-sum_j(G^-1)_ij n_j have positive squares. Their off-diagonal products are strictly negative. Indeed Jacobi's minor identity gives (G^-1)_ii(G^-1)_jj-(G^-1)_ij^2 =sin^2(alpha_complement)/det G<0. No off-diagonal inverse entry can therefore vanish. The angle domain is convex and connected, and at a small regular angle all those entries are negative; continuity fixes their sign everywhere. Normalize the v_i to square one. Every pair has product <-1, so their projective edge crosses the Klein ball. Their sum is timelike, and has negative product with every v_i. It supplies an interior point of the four face halfspaces AND the four vertex-polar halfspaces. Cutting the six projective edges by those polar planes gives twelve finite hyperbolic vertices. Each lies strictly on the proper side of the other two polar planes, by the negative products. The result is a compact convex truncated tetrahedron, with four triangular polar faces and four right-angled hexagonal original faces. Its six original dihedrals are (7); every new truncation edge is right-angled. There are no assumed end or completeness conditions in this compact local construction. Its ordered face-normal Gram fixes it up to isometry. For an explicit compactness check, suppose a remaining point were ideal and write it in the vertex cone as x=sum_i t_i v_i, t_i>=0. The polar inequalities <x,v_i><=0 and x^2=0 force <x,v_i>=0 on every active coefficient. This would put the nonzero active vector t in the kernel of its principal vertex Gram block. All such blocks are nonsingular: their determinants are complementary principal minors of G divided by det G (size one and two were checked above; size three uses G_ii=1). Thus no ideal point remains after truncation. The length along original edge a, between its polar truncations, is ell_a=arccosh[ C_13/sqrt(C_11 C_33) ]>0. (9) The cofactor in (9) is positive since det G<0 and (G^-1)_13<0. The formula follows by restricting to the Lorentz plane spanned by its two normalized hyperideal endpoints. Other edges are obtained by vertex relabeling. ## 3. The optimized derivative is EXACTLY that truncated edge length Here is a finite rational certificate for the derivative, with all branches fixed by the positive interval. Set u_a=exp(2pi i a), etc., P=product_edges u. Let U_i be the four products of u on the faces in (1), and V_k the three products on the quads. Then product U_i=product V_k=P^2. Write n=exp(2pi i Z). The stationarity equation A'(Z)=0 is exactly (n-1)product_k(n-V_k)-product_i(n-U_i) =n(A2 n^2+A1 n+A0)=0, A2=sum U_i-1-sum V_k, A1=sum_(k<l)V_kV_l+sum V_k-sum_(i<j)U_iU_j, A0=sum_(i<j<l)U_iU_jU_l-P^2-sum_(k<l)V_kV_l. (10) Expansion gives the independent identity A1^2-4A2A0=16P^2 det G. (11) In (11), G has off-diagonals cos(2pi color), which is exactly (7). Also A0=P^2 conjugate(A2) and A1/P is real. Thus the two roots of (10) are distinct and on the unit circle. A2 cannot vanish, since that would make (11)/P^2 a nonnegative real square instead of 16det G<0. The function A' tends to +infinity at the lower positive interval endpoint and to -infinity at the upper one. It is continuous inside, and (10) permits at most two simple critical points there. The number is odd, so there is EXACTLY one, Z_*. It is a strict global maximum, with nonzero negative second derivative. This also fixes a smooth selected branch on the entire connected domain (2). For edge a let B(n)=u_c (n-U_1)(n-U_3)/[(n-V_1)(n-V_2)], R_a= sin pi(a+e-b)sin pi(a+b-e) /[sin pi(b+e-a)sin pi(F_1-1)] *sin pi(a+f-d)sin pi(a+d-f) /[sin pi(d+f-a)sin pi(F_3-1)]. All displayed sines in R_a are positive. Differentiating (5) at its selected stationary Z_* gives E_a:=exp(partial_a Psi)=B(n_*)sqrt(R_a)>0. (12) To verify (12), the bare derivative is the ratio of the two sin(Z-F) factors to the two sin(Q-Z) factors incident to a. Their canceled phase is u_c. The four face derivatives give R_a. Let n_+,n_- be the two roots of (10). Direct rational products give B(n_+)B(n_-)=1/R_a, B(n_+)+B(n_-)=C_13/(2K_a), K_a=sin pi(a+e-b)sin pi(a+b-e) sin pi(a+f-d)sin pi(a+d-f), sqrt(C_11 C_33) sqrt(R_a)=4K_a. (13) These are uniform algebraic identities, not tests at selected colors. For an explicit cleared-polynomial verification, put A=-A1-A2(U_1+U_3), B=A2 U_1U_3-A0, C=-A1-A2(V_1+V_2), D=A2 V_1V_2-A0, Den=C^2 A0-CD A1+D^2 A2. The sum/product of the two B(n) are respectively u_c[2AC A0-(AD+BC)A1+2BD A2]/Den, u_c^2[A^2 A0-AB A1+B^2 A2]/Den. With edge variables written a,...,f temporarily for u_a,...,u_f, the claimed product is (be-a)(abe-1)(df-a)(adf-1) /[(ae-b)(ab-e)(af-d)(ad-f)], and the claimed sum is 8a^2bdef C_13 /[(ae-b)(ab-e)(af-d)(ad-f)]. Substitute (10), multiply these explicit denominators, and expand: both polynomial differences are identically zero in six independent variables. The final identity in (13) is the elementary three-face Gram determinant (8), with its sine factors. The accompanying audit performs these symbolic zero checks; no interpolation is involved. Consequently the two possible E_a values are reciprocal and have sum 2C_13/sqrt(C_11C_33). They are exp(+ell_a), exp(-ell_a). Near the regular ideal limit all colors approach 1/3 from above; the metric factor in (12) diverges while its bare ratio remains finite and positive. Thus the selected E_a is the positive-length branch there. It cannot change branch on (2), since ell_a never vanishes. By connectedness and tetrahedral relabeling, partial_edge Psi=ell_edge for all six edges. (14) ## 4. An elementary volume-variation proof and its constant For completeness the needed first variation can be derived directly. On the hyperboloid the coordinate vector restricted to a totally geodesic face satisfies Delta_face x=2x. It follows by differentiating the usual cosh/sinh coordinates on H^2. A face with moving outward unit normal n has normal speed -<dot n,x>. The divergence theorem within that face therefore gives dot V=-(1/2)sum_faces sum_edges integral_edge <dot n,nu_edge> ds. For an edge between face normals n_i,n_j and angle alpha, the outward conormal within face i is (n_j+cos alpha n_i)/sin alpha. Adding its two face contributions uses d<n_i,n_j>=sin alpha d alpha, and gives dV=-(1/2)sum_edges ell_edge d alpha_edge. (15) The new truncation edges have fixed angle pi/2, hence contribute zero. Using alpha=pi-2pi color, (15) becomes dV=pi sum ell_edge d(color). Equations (14),(15) show that V-pi Psi is constant on the connected domain (2). Calibrate at the regular ideal boundary a=...=f=1/3. Then F_i=1, Q_k=4/3, Z_*=7/6, and A(Z_*)=-6L(1/6)=3v3/pi, M=6L(1/3)=-2v3/pi, Psi=v3/pi. (16) The Lobachevsky duplication identity gives Lambda(pi/6)=(3/2)Lambda(pi/3), so (16) has no numerical calibration. The Gram construction converges to the regular ideal tetrahedron, whose volume is v3=3Lambda(pi/3). One can justify volume convergence here without a realization or rigidity theorem. For the regular family take fixed Euclidean regular tetrahedral unit vectors t_i with mutual products -1/3 and use n_i=(T,S t_i), T^2=(3cos alpha-1)/4, S^2=1+T^2. At alpha=pi/3 their Klein faces have distance 1/3 from the center, giving the four ideal vertices -t_i. The finite polar truncation vertices converge to those same vertices. Here are exact uniform end inequalities. Set c=cos alpha, t=T/S and rho=3t=sqrt((9c-3)/(c+1))>1. The projective hyperideal vertex at -t_i is rho(-t_i). In a fixed upper-half-space frame sending w=-t_i to infinity, its polar cut is |z|^2+y^2<=(rho+1)/(rho-1). For every incident j!=i, t_j dot w=1/3. Its original face inequality therefore gives exactly 2(t_j)_perp dot z <=(t+1/3)+(t-1/3)(|z|^2+y^2) <=2(rho+1)/3. The three fixed perpendicular normals surround the origin at angles 120 degrees. Hence |z|<=C uniformly as rho decreases to 1. The cross-sectional area is bounded, and its volume above y=Y is <=C/Y^2. Do this in the four disjoint ideal-end frames; the remaining compact regions converge. This proves volume convergence to the ideal tetrahedron and fixes the constant in (15), with no O(epsilon) end estimate left as an assumption. We have therefore proved the LOCAL GEOMETRIC IDENTITY pi Psi(a,b,c,d,e,f)=Vol(truncated hyperideal tetrahedron). (17) Both sides extend continuously to the closed angle chamber. For Psi this follows directly from continuity of L and maximization on a continuously varying compact interval. The corresponding geometric extension is the limit from the interior; no assertion that every boundary point retains a nondegenerate truncated-tetrahedron cell is needed. In particular at six colors 1/2, Z_*=7/4 and Psi=v8/pi; the six original edge lengths tend to zero at the escaping ideal corners. The limiting cell is the regular ideal octahedron, not a tetrahedron with positive edges. One can check its geometry directly: G=2I-J and its four normalized polar normals are m_i=-n_i+(1/2)sum_j n_j. Then distinct n_i,n_j and distinct m_i,m_j have product -1, while <n_i,m_j> is -2 for i=j and zero otherwise. These are exactly the eight regular-octahedron face normals (1,sigma_1,sigma_2,sigma_3)/sqrt(2), partitioned by the product of the three signs. Thus the octahedral constant is attached to an explicit geometric cell, not only a limiting dilogarithm number. ## 5. Exact stationarity data, and what a global source still needs The local action supplies more than a constant fit. The colors give the actual face-normal Gram (7), its polar triangle areas are (3), and the optimized derivatives are the six metric edge lengths (14). For a specified gluing of such cells, (15) gives its first variation on EVERY allowed dihedral-angle tangent, not merely on a chosen one-parameter source family. In particular variations exchanging two angles around one fixed total-angle edge force equality of their corresponding truncated lengths. More generally a linear constraint matrix C gives the exact stationarity condition length vector in image(C^T). (18) If the ONLY angle constraints are sums around actual common edges, (18) forces one common length per glued edge. Three such matched alternating lengths determine a right-angled hexagon by elementary hyperbolic cosine laws, so the prescribed original hexagonal faces then match isometrically. Actual angle sums, link degree/winding, boundary markings and end completeness must still be checked. Additional source constraints can reduce the tangent space, and then stationarity in that smaller space does not imply this full metric gluing. No global strict-concavity or complete-manifold maximum theorem is asserted solely from the local derivative identity. There is a concrete obstruction to using just the four support inequalities as a complete volume-maximization certificate. Equation (14) gives partial_edge Psi>0 at every strict point. Increasing any color preserves those four inequalities. Along the line toward six colors 1/2, Psi therefore increases to v8/pi. By continuity that is the maximum over the CLOSED support chamber, and there is NO interior stationary point under only these inequalities. A geometric interior critical point for a larger graph needs the actual additional edge constraints, boundary potentials or their full source counterparts; the local face supports alone do not supply them. The [generic actual four-port theorem](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md) now gives an explicit separable row/column gauge relating its literal inverse kernel L_(G,E) to the seven-factorial sum S. Its four Delta face factors give exactly the normalization in (6) after root-zero removal. Thus this finite scalar/generic normalization is explicit; it is not being taken from a named 6j evaluation. But identifying the resulting weight with a useful FULL marked-source Cauchy energy still requires controlled gauge transport, complete colliding partners and root normals, and the graph's actual port/edge incidence in (18). No individual partner value or semisimple normalization may replace that comparison. The bare Racah term is already wrong at the regular ideal tetrahedron by the factor in (16). ## 6. Uniform local quantum-volume theorem, including moving boundary colors The geometry identity has the following UNIFORM finite-level consequence. There is an absolute constant C such that, for EVERY N and every six folded integer labels satisfying all four face sums >=N-1, the positive normalized scalar W_N in (6) obeys |log W_N-(N/pi)Vol_ext(T(a_N))|<=C log(N+1), a_(N,edge)=(j_edge+1/2)/N. (19) The domain is empty at any level with no supported sextuple. The symbol Vol_ext is the continuous geometric extension of (17); at strict angles it is the ordinary compact truncated-tetrahedron volume, while zero-angle boundary cells are interpreted by their geometric limits. Constants in (19) do not depend on a distance from any face, edge, corner or the octahedral endpoint. Both level parities and composite N are included. Here is the full uniform estimate. Write F_i^int,Q_k^int for the integer forms (1), z_-=max F_i^int and z_+=min Q_k^int. All true factorial indices are in [0,N-1]. The elementary uniform estimate log s_n=N L(n/N)+O(log(N+1)), 0<=n<=N-1, has an absolute constant. Applying it to the fixed eight factorials in each positive R_N term changes its logarithm by O(log N). At its actual point Z_z=(z+7/4)/N, the action arguments differ from those true indices divided by N by exactly numerator: 3/(4N), each of seven denominators: 1/(4N). For a face metric the three deficits and its excess differ by exactly 1/(2N). The shifted and original arguments are all in [0,1]. The uniform modulus |L(t+epsilon)-L(t)| <=C0 |epsilon|(1+|log|epsilon||) therefore changes N times these actions by O(log N), including when an original factorial index is zero. The explicit N factors in R_N and D_face add only O(log N). The geometric maximization interval is I=[(z_-+3/2)/N,(z_++2)/N], whereas the true grid runs from (z_-+7/4)/N to (z_++7/4)/N in steps 1/N. Its first and last points are inset by exactly 1/(4N) from the two respective endpoints. Every point of I is within 1/N of a true grid point, even when z_-=z_+. The same modulus of L, now for its eight action terms, shows that the continuous maximum and the true-grid maximum differ by O(log N/N), uniformly. There are at most N positive terms: z_+-z_-<=N-1 by the complementary triangle-deficit bounds. The largest term bounds their sum from below, and N times it bounds the sum from above. Thus log W_N=N Psi(a_N)+O(log N) with one universal error constant. Equation (17) proves (19). No nonzero Hessian, separation from a boundary, selected complex cycle or asymptotic interpolation of an unobserved normal was used in this argument. In particular ANY convergent supported color sequence a_N->a in the closed chamber satisfies lim (pi/N)log W_N=Vol_ext(T(a)). (20) This is a genuine broad LOCAL quantum-volume theorem for the explicitly gauged scalar/residue. Its squared weight has twice the logarithmic action. It does not turn (19) into a full marked recoupling norm or authorize replacing a partner germ by its positive value core; those source requirements in section 5 remain. Audit: [universal rational certificates and local geometry](../experiments/audit_actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume.py), with [recorded results](../experiments/actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume_results.json). It verifies four symbolic identities in six independent edge variables, all six derivative/Gram lengths in regular, unequal and opposite-obtuse chambers, three independent direct regular geometric volume integrals, and the exact half-step angle ranges at eight full physical levels. Finite profiles check normalization; the uniform proof is the Gram construction, symbolic identities and first variation above. The range audit also verifies all shifted factorial arguments, exact quarter-grid endpoint insets and the <=N positive-term count in (19). Independent internal review: root read the full argument and supplied the exact regular-end cap inequalities used in section 4. The crossing/source agent independently read the complete analytical proof and replayed the permanent audit: PASS, including the selected positive-length sheet, compactness, ideal calibration and source scope. These are internal research audits, not external peer review or a general four-port/graph energy theorem. The uniform scalar consequence (19) was additionally checked against the supported Racah theorem by the source agent, including its exact half-step shifts and boundary-uniform constants. It does not extend that theorem's low-fold jet estimate to the retained partner current.

title: What a Tauberian argument would need from the original positive Fourier energy
text: # What a Tauberian argument would need from the original positive Fourier energy 28 October 2026. The positive Fourier energy is the right actual object for testing an Abelian/Tauberian approach. It permits elementary, self-contained statements about its Laplace transform and its exponential rate. Positivity alone identifies a limsup, however; it does not force the volume limit or suppress exceptional low levels. The results below give a precise additional cross-level condition that WOULD turn a critical Laplace singularity into the full original volume limit. No such cross-level condition or sharp singularity has yet been derived from the actual A-source. This is a criterion and a source-scope audit, not a proof of the conjecture. ## 1. The exact original energy and its existing bound Use the ORIGINAL unitary color Fourier transform and original reduced normalization from [the independently audited Plancherel identity](ordinary_color_plancherel_bound_audit.md). For every fixed knot presentation, E_N=sum_k |chat_(N,k)|²=|K_N|²+R_N, 1<=R_N<=N^B, N>=2, (1) with a fixed constant/power allowed in the upper bound. Every pivot, Cartan and framing factor is retained. The ordinary-color remainder is the original remainder, not a positive replacement model. Thus log E_N=log(1+|K_N|²)+O(log N). (2) For any fixed lambda>0, log E_N/N ->lambda iff (2pi/N)log|K_N| ->pi*lambda. (3) In particular the desired energy exponent is lambda=Vol/pi. The [direct ordinary-color coefficient bound](actual_regular_fast_color_elimination.md) gives, for an ell-crossing b-braid, ||C_j||_1<=j^(ell+b-1)4^(ell*j). Taking j=N and using (1) proves E_N<=exp(CN) for a fixed C. This provides an actual nonempty convergence half-plane for the positive Laplace series Z(s)=sum_(N>=2) E_N exp(-sN). (4) It does not identify its sharp convergence boundary geometrically. ## 2. The abscissa gives exactly the exponential limsup Put lambda*=limsup_N log(E_N)/N, finite and nonnegative. Then (4) converges for real s>lambda* and diverges for s<lambda*. Indeed, for s>lambda*, choose epsilon<(s-lambda*). Eventually E_N<=exp((lambda*+epsilon)N), so comparison with a geometric series proves convergence. For s<lambda*, infinitely many terms satisfy E_N>=exp((s+epsilon)N), so the terms of (4) do not even tend to zero. The convergence boundary itself can be convergent or divergent. Consequently a source-derived proof that Z(s) is finite for every s>Vol/pi would give the sharp original exponential UPPER bound. Locating its abscissa at Vol/pi would identify the corresponding limsup. Positivity makes these implications exact, but does not compute the abscissa. Merely naming the abscissa is not an estimate. ## 3. A power singularity gives a genuine cumulative Tauberian conclusion Here is a special case sufficient to explain the Karamata-type idea, proved independently rather than assumed. Suppose, for lambda>0, alpha>0 and C>0, an actual calculation establishes Z(lambda+t) ~ C t^(-alpha), t down to0. (5) Then A(x):=sum_(2<=N<=x) exp(-lambda N)E_N ~ C x^alpha/Gamma(alpha+1). (6) Proof. Write a_N=exp(-lambda N)E_N>=0 and define finite positive measures on x>=0 by nu_t=(t^alpha/C) sum_N a_N exp(-tN) delta_(tN). For each integer k>=0 their Laplace moments satisfy integral exp(-kx)dnu_t =(t^alpha/C)Z(lambda+(k+1)t)->(k+1)^(-alpha). (7) Under y=exp(-x), these are ordinary polynomial moments on [0,1]. The candidate limit has x-density exp(-x)x^(alpha-1)/Gamma(alpha); its moments are exactly (7), by the defining Gamma integral. Polynomial moment convergence implies convergence against every continuous function on [0,1]: Bernstein polynomials approximate such a function uniformly, since uniform continuity and the binomial variance bound force the approximation error to zero. The measures' total masses tend to one, so the uniform approximation error is uniform in t. This proves the claimed weak convergence without a separate Tauberian theorem. The bounded function y^-1 times the indicator y>=exp(-1) has just one jump, at a point with zero limit mass. Approximate it from above and below by continuous functions. Hence (t^alpha/C)A(1/t) ->integral_0^1 x^(alpha-1)/Gamma(alpha)dx =1/Gamma(alpha+1), which proves (6). An immediate useful consequence is that HIGH-ENERGY LEVELS OCCUR IN EVERY FIXED MULTIPLICATIVE WINDOW: for each delta in(0,1), A(n)-A((1-delta)n) ~ C[1-(1-delta)^alpha] n^alpha/Gamma(alpha+1)>0. (8) Thus no fixed proportional interval can avoid all near-rate levels. Also the UNTILTED cumulative energy S(n)=sum_(N<=n)E_N obeys log S(n)/n ->lambda. (9) For the upper bound S(n)<=exp(lambda n)A(n). For the lower bound, use (8) and exp(lambda(1-delta)n), then let delta decrease to zero. Equations (6),(8),(9) are stronger than a bare limsup. They still do not prove log E_N/N->lambda for every individual N. ## 4. An operative cross-level condition completing the implication The following one-sided source-transport condition suffices. Suppose there are fixed delta0>0, L>=0 and A0>=0 such that, for every large n, E_(n-r)<=n^A0 exp(Lr) E_n, 0<=r<=delta0*n. (10) It prevents an exponentially deep drop from preceding nearby levels; it does not assert positivity of the original unsquared period. An exact source-preserving map between the relevant positive Fourier spaces, with norm at most n^(A0/2)exp(Lr/2), would prove (10). Then the cumulative exponential law (9) implies log E_n/n ->lambda. (11) To prove it, fix 0<delta<delta0. Since lambda>0, (9) gives S(n)-S((1-delta)n)=exp(lambda n+o(n)). By (10) this difference is at most n^(A0+1)exp(L delta n)E_n. Hence liminf log E_n/n>=lambda-Ldelta. Let delta decrease to zero; the upper bound E_n<=S(n) proves (11). Combining (3),(5),(10) therefore proves the ORIGINAL volume limit with V=pi*lambda. An O(1) bound on each negative neighboring log-increment implies (10). In contrast, a polynomial comparison at ONE neighboring step, E_(n-1)<=n^A E_n, accumulates to exp(O(r log n)); it does not imply (10). Such a weak comparison allows narrow exponentially deep dips. It cannot be substituted into this proof without further control. The power singularity (5) is itself a substantial averaged asymptotic. It is stronger information than the convergence abscissa. Neither (5) nor (10) is being inferred from positivity or from an algebraic classical characteristic. ## 5. What the current actual source does and does not supply The available exact A-equation transports COLOR j at a fixed q: sum_i a_i(q,-q^j) C_(j+i)(q)=0. The energy E_N changes the color range, the Hilbert-space dimension, AND the parameter q_N when N changes. The fixed-q recurrence does not provide an operator from the level n-r Fourier space to the level n Fourier space. The quantum-group coproduct is also at fixed q. Connected-sum multiplication changes the KNOT at a fixed level; it is not a submultiplicative relation in the LEVEL N. The verified cross-level polynomial rigidity of the color family identifies that family, but gives no norm estimate of the form (10). There is a concrete actual-source reason not to replace this missing level map by uniform continuity of a fixed-color polynomial in q. For 4_1, its exact Newton formula gives C_N(q_(N+1))=1 for EVERY N: at that root the evaluation node Q^N+Q^-N equals the first node Q+Q^-1, so all positive Newton indices vanish. The same fixed color at q_N is K_N. Thus a q-displacement of order N^-2 can cross the entire high-color boundary response. This does not disprove (10) for the COMPLETE level energies E_N,E_(N+1); it shows why fixed-q pointing and low-color derivative estimates do not supply it. Likewise each exact pointed Gram ratio is positive at its own level. It has not been rewritten as the moments of one fixed positive transfer operator across levels, nor as a positive renewal equation with a specified spectral edge. Either construction, with the original source and nonzero edge weight verified, could supply Tauberian input. The existing level-dependent Gram identity does not. There is even a small exact ORIGINAL hyperbolic-source warning against assuming cross-level moment/log-convex structure for raw E_N. For 4_1, the independently proved whole-source formula gives K_2=5, K_3=13, K_4=27, R_2=1, R_3=2, R_4=3, E_2=26, E_3=171, E_4=732. Thus E_2 E_4-E_3²=-10209<0. (12) So positivity within each Fourier space does not imply positivity of the cross-level Hankel matrix, or a raw positive moment representation of E_(n+2). This does not exclude an eventual inequality, a known polynomial normalization, or a different source-derived transfer. It simply prevents assuming that structure from Plancherel alone. ## 6. A minimal counterexample to positivity-only inference For any lambda>0, let E_N=exp(lambda N) at even N and E_N=1 at odd N. This is NOT a knot counterexample. Its purpose is to check the exact logical strength of the proposed Tauberian inference. It satisfies Z(lambda+t)~1/(2t), A(x)~x/2, log S(n)/n->lambda, but log E_N/N alternates between lambda and0. It violates (10). Thus even the pure-pole singularity and positivity leave an individual-level survival condition to establish. The useful next target is consequently a SOURCE-DERIVED positive Laplace/renewal description or a cross-level comparison such as (10). Neither is currently available. A Tauberian argument can use those inputs efficiently; it cannot create them or resolve the geometric branch coupling by itself. Reproduce the exact source warning and the positive-sequence checks: ```sh python3 experiments/audit_actual_fourier_energy_tauberian.py ``` Coverage only: this is the classical positive-measure Tauberian setting; see [Michael Taylor, Karamata's Tauberian Theorem](https://mtaylor.web.unc.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/16915/2020/07/karamata.pdf). Section 3 supplies its own moment proof for the precise power-law case used here; no quoted theorem supplies the missing knot-source inputs.

title: Actual Fourier polarization gives a nonzero geometric normal block
text: # Actual Fourier polarization gives a nonzero geometric normal block Research theorem, 27 October 2026. Fourier-transforming the SECOND physical cut, while retaining the original first-cut rank-one row, gives an exact new partial family for the original root state. Its specified proper finite-array lift has a nonzero geometric formal Gaussian block. The two external coordinates are the first physical position and the second Fourier label. They correspond to (A,p_e), which is birational on the complete discrete-faithful framing torsor. The displayed source is the ACTUAL finite sum over both external labels. A subsequent root Ward reduction fixes the first input and retains only the Fourier-label sum, as described below. Neither source is the residue eta=0 of the old band variable. No selected global geometric contribution or volume conjecture follows from the existence of this local block. ## 1. Exact finite polarization and the unchanged selected source Use the literal four-port tensor T_(c,d;a,b) from [the two physical cuts](actual_two_cut_framing_port_reconstruction.md). All original pivots, caps, Cartan/framing lines, meridian marks and the full peripheral factor stay in T or its recorded external line. The second cut is an identity wire, with no new pivot. At level N put Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N) and V_(j,b)=Q_N^(jb), (V^-1)_(b,j)=Q_N^(-jb)/N, T^V=(I tensor V)T(I tensor V^-1). Keep the ORIGINAL first-cut row: define the RAW partial array Jtilde_(a,j)=sum_c T^V_(c,j;a,j). (1) Then finite basis invariance of the identity closure proves EXACTLY P_N(M)=(1/N)sum_(a,j=0)^(N-1) Jtilde_(a,j). (2) The first factor 1/N is the original cut average. The inverse Fourier matrix contributes another 1/N INSIDE Jtilde. Neither is silently removed or treated as a second physical pivotal trace. Here P_N denotes the originally selected scalar with its chosen reduced/full external line; the original pointing at completeness and every external d_N factor are unchanged on the two sides. For a conserving tangle c+d=a+b, put q=d-b. Formula (1) becomes Jtilde_(a,j)=(1/N)sum_(b,q) Q_N^(jq) T_(a-q,b+q;a,b). (3) All four original head bounds are retained by zero extension. Crucially c is summed in (1), not set to a. A double diagonal at BOTH cuts would impose q=0 and lose the new Fourier label. The [whole Vandermonde construction](actual_two_cut_fourier_polarization_and_cap.md) retains the actual generic inverse, source, normal connection and endpoint carries. For the stationary construction here specify also the proper ROOT LIFT obtained from (3) by using Q^(jq)/N off root. It equals (1) at every original root. Off root this kernel is generally DIFFERENT from V(Q)^-1, and its total external sum need not equal the original whole q-germ. This distinction is retained; no equality of their higher q-normal source jets is inferred. ## 2. The open phase is made from the original finite coefficients Let the braid have m crossings. The old two-position array has external labels (a,b) and r=m-1 remaining cycle flows u. Opening the two ports with balanced offset (-q,+q) adds one boundary-flow parameter. A spanning tree in the connected remaining graph gives an integral particular flow linear in q; the same internal cycle coordinates u remain. No lattice index or hidden determinant occurs. Every original position/transfer is consequently an integral affine function of (a,b,q,u). Substitute these functions into the original finite factorial/Cartan coefficients. Their compact formal expansion therefore defines a genuine open phase germ S_open(a_log,b_log,t,u_log), t=Hq, a_log=Ha, b_log=Hb, H=Log Q, and the actual nonzero amplitude with all half-step and source lines. The variable compact arguments must stay in the established regular shape chart. At t=0 this is exactly the old closed coefficient model. This construction uses its WHOLE finite-product expressions, not an unjustified summation of fixed-offset asymptotic formulas. The actual boundary proper-ratio calculation in the two-cut theorem gives on the closed geometric critical surface partial_t S_open=Log p_e. (4) The balanced exchange lowers the first output and raises the second; the first-cut wave momentum is one in its original constant boundary frame. Hence (4) has the stated sign and contains the original factorial-boundary adapter. Flattened logarithms and peripheral signs are those of the original marked critical correspondence. Put v=Hj. The proper lift (3) has the exact additional monomial Q^(jq)=exp(vt/H), Phi=S_open+vt. (5) The new external variables are (a_log,v). Its internal variables are x=(b_log,u_log), together with t, of dimension m+1=r+2. ## 3. A complete discrete-faithful framing torsor has birational (A,p_e) The following proof supplies a nonempty regular polarization chart for EVERY complete discrete-faithful knot representation in the actual geometric model. It does not assert this for arbitrary reducible or nondiscrete representation components. Normalize the cut meridian J=[[1,1],[0,1]] and retain F(r,s)=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], s nonzero, A=1/(1+s). For the chosen actual physical second edge retain its developed PREFIX words U,V. The actual inverse clock is k=ell_U/ell_V, ell_W=d_W+(a_W-d_W)r+b_Ws+c_W r(1-r)/s. (6) An independent second physical position exists by the actual two-position theorem, so k depends nontrivially on r. Here U,V are group words, UV^-1 is a nontrivial parabolic meridian, and det U=det V=1. Let t_W=Tr W, h_W=a_W-d_W and sigma=(-1)^ell for its actual prefix strand position ell; the Fourier sample label is still j. The exact prefix/momentum identities give, with u_p=p+p^-1 and v_p=p^-1-p, A_0=c_U+s t_U, A_1=c_V+s t_V, u_p=sigma(A_0-kA_1)/[s(k-1)], D=-sigma s(k-1)v_p, D=c_C+s h_C-2c_Cr, C=U-kV. (7) First, every UPPER TRIANGULAR word W of this discrete torsion-free projective group has diagonal entries a,a^-1 with a^2=1, hence h_W=0. Indeed if |a| differs from one, suitable conjugates W^n J W^-n are nontrivial translations converging to the identity. If |a|=1 and a^2 has infinite order, choose a^(2n) tending to one; then W^n J W^-n J^-1 is a nontrivial translation tending to the identity. Both contradict discreteness. If a^2 has finite nontrivial order, the upper triangular W is diagonalizable with projectively finite order, contradicting torsion-freeness. This proves the assertion without a stabilizer classification theorem. Suppose p were independent of r. Since k_r is nonzero, differentiating the Mobius expression in (7) forces A_0=A_1 as functions of s. Thus c_U=c_V and t_U=t_V. Now C_0=U-V has c=0, trace zero and determinant zero, so C_0=b E_12. It is nonzero because UV^-1 is a nontrivial meridian. Equality of the two determinants forces b c_V=0, hence c_U=c_V=0. Both U,V are upper triangular; the previous paragraph gives h_U=h_V=0. Equation (6) then makes k independent of r, a contradiction. Therefore (A,p) is etale on a nonempty open of the complete geometric framing torsor. The same upper-word argument shows c_U,c_V are not both zero. On the open set with the displayed denominators units, (7) has the explicit rational inverse s=(1-A)/A, k=(s u_p+sigma A_0)/(s u_p+sigma A_1), C=U-kV, D=-sigma s(k-1)v_p, r=(c_C+s h_C-D)/(2c_C). (8) Thus the function field of the framing torsor equals its field in (A,p): no new framing cover is introduced by this polarization. Any existing marked representation, SL2-sign or half-density cover is still retained. This is a birational assertion on the indicated open sets, not a global compactification or cycle identification. At a generic old position-projection caustic p=+1 or -1, k_p=0 but differentiating (8) gives r_p=-sigma s(k-1)/c_C !=0. (9) Thus the new chart resolves those old two-position caustics when the other displayed units and original shape chart remain regular. The exact geometric two-form is Omega_cut=-ell_V(k-1)/(A_1-A_0) dlog A wedge dlog p. (10) This is the prefix density in its new rational coordinates, not a claim about the old finite band cap variable. It is regular at the generic caustics in (9). ## 4. The ACTUAL new stationary block is nondegenerate At t=0 let x=(b_log,u_log). Fixing the first physical position in the old geometric Morse--Bott model leaves one framing tangent xi. Hence H_0=partial_x^2 S_open has rank r and radical span(xi). Let c=partial_x partial_t S_open and gamma=partial_t^2 S_open. Differentiating (4) along the critical framing gives mu=c dot xi=dlog p_e(xi), which is nonzero precisely on the new etale polarization chart. The internal Hessian of (5) is the actual bordered matrix H_new=[[H_0,c],[c^t,gamma]]. (11) It is invertible. If H_new(delta_x,delta_t)=0, pairing its first row with xi gives mu delta_t=0, hence delta_t=0. Then delta_x lies in the old radical, and the last equation gives delta_x=0. No invertibility of an old two-position transverse minor is used. Thus this proof also applies where that old minor is singular. For each new external pair with eta=exp(v), eta p_e=1, the old closed geometric point at t=0 solves all new internal critical equations. The formal implicit-function theorem for (11) makes it the UNIQUE critical germ there. In particular all the old closed equations still hold, and Phi_critical=S_geo, (12) with exactly the same marked regulator action and retained base characters: the new term vt vanishes at t=0. The comparison is now an actual Fourier partial-family critical construction, not substitution into the old band-generating cap. The regular marked representation/gluing branch has the meridian as a local coordinate. Nonzero mu and det H_new persist in that meridian deformation germ. Thus the same construction supplies the geometric formal normal line and action S_geo(M) there. The birational function-field statement of Section 3 was specifically at completeness; it is not promoted to a global statement over every peripheral point. On an old regular (A,B) chart, choose xi with xi_b=1 and first contract u. If H_perp is the old r-by-r transverse Hessian, its remaining Schur block in (b,t) is [[0,mu],[mu,gamma_eff]], det H_new=-mu^2 det H_perp. (13) The formula is independent of gamma_eff. At an old projection caustic xi_b may vanish, so that normalization and old minor are not used; the direct kernel proof of (11) remains valid. ## 5. Fourier normalization and the remaining actual source The amplitude at the new critical point is the SAME original nonzero coefficient amplitude at q=0. The Fourier character is one there. Equations (11)--(13) therefore give a nonzero formal normal block, with algebraic coefficients on the new chart and the original square-root/phase mark retained in its Gaussian line. The two extra discrete sums b,q contribute their logarithmic measure H^-2, while the inverse Fourier matrix contributes 1/N. On the physical sequence H_N=2pi*i/N their product is EXACTLY (1/N)H_N^-2=1/(2pi*i H_N). (14) This is the normalized two-variable formal Fourier pairing. With the explicit convention that its cross Gaussian exp(zt/H) has pairing one, composition after the old transverse contraction gives numerical leading coefficient a_perp/mu for that declared ordered cross pairing. The oriented external two-form has an additional minus sign: v=-Log p implies db/dv=-1/mu, consistently with (10). This is a FIXED ordered- Fourier phase, not a variable source correction. Another ordered Gaussian square-root mark carries its corresponding fixed phase in the recorded base line. Neither the original physical 1/N in (2) nor any peripheral character is absorbed into an unspecified variable unit. The resulting amplitude has the same exponential action (12); no new exponential factor is generated by the Fourier pair. This is a formal, coefficientwise statement from the original proper finite-array model. It asserts neither analytic stationary-phase asymptotics for its growing sums nor survival of this block in the final selected contraction. In particular the CORRECT new final source is still the finite sum in (2). Its Fourier label j takes all original N head values. It has not become eta=0, a choice of one momentum boundary, or an unmarked sum over the old quadratic framing sheets. A global comparison must transport that finite source, its endpoint carries and the actual whole-V versus proper-root-lift distinction above. [Exact bordered-Hessian and rational-polarization checks](../experiments/audit_actual_fourier_polarized_normal_block.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_fourier_polarized_normal_block_results.json). They pass four exact bordered-Hessian identities, 548 rational forward/inverse and density-Jacobian cases, and 120 old-caustic cases with nonzero new momentum derivative, including both prefix parities. Finite-field cases check the rational identities; the discrete-faithful argument in Section 3 is a separate direct proof. The [Fourier partial support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md), Section 7, applies the global finite-array certificate to the specified proper root lift and this SAME formal block. It retains the full first-cut sum, the two exterior labels, the original and Fourier factors 1/N, and the distinction from whole-V normal jets. Its geometric A-factor assertion concerns that actual all-level ROOT partial family, rather than an asserted off-root q-normal equivalence or the final sourced scalar sum. The [subsequent one-index source theorem](actual_one_index_fourier_source_and_ward_reduction.md) and [its independent audit](one_index_fourier_source_independent_audit.md) use actual ROOT scalarity of the fully reclosed cut to fix ANY first input a while retaining the original sum over its outputs. Thus the selected scalar is sum_j Jtilde_(a,j), with no remaining outside 1/N and with its internal Fourier 1/N unchanged. A fixed good root-of-unity phase sequence retains a nonzero geometric normal block. Section 8 of the partial support theorem gives the corresponding nonzero operator on each finite residue class. The unresolved global pushforward can therefore be formulated as ONE exterior Fourier-label sum. Whole q-normal source defects remain explicit; root scalarity is not extended off root. The [rank-one prefix calculation](mobius_fourier_framing_and_intrinsic_norm_pole.md) now simplifies the fixed-A rational inverse to an explicit Möbius map of projective lines and computes its single intrinsic density pole. The [actual cancellation theorem](actual_fourier_source_cancellation.md) provides an important scope test: an actual port current with zero final source still has a nonzero block of the same geometric action on this chart. Consequently this local block and its partial A-factor do not, by themselves, prove selected survival.

title: Exact physical port polynomials and global conditional angular profiles
text: # Exact physical port polynomials and global conditional angular profiles 28 October 2026. The ORIGINAL four-full-Psi crossing has exact finite-band Laurent-polynomial interpolants in each port, while the other three ports stay on their specified correlated grids. These are the actual finite Fourier interpolants, with their entire source normalization fixed by a known local kernel entry. Their apparent full-Psi poles cancel after the exact fixed-grid period factors and integer aliases are retained. This proves a nonzero analytic symbol for a single actual finite Fourier adapter on a compact positive crossing chart. It also gives the unique GLOBAL angular modulus maximum on the whole conditional port circle. It does not justify moving several unrelated ports simultaneously or suppressing a whole knot's boundary sectors. ## 1. Actual kernel, grids, and the two integer chamber labels Use the EXACT original operator and source of [the balanced Fourier theorem](actual_balanced_fourier_crossing_kernel.md). Write q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, h=2pi*i/N, d=N-1, x=-q^(-1), X=pi*i-h/2. The marked grids have z0=r0 Q^i, z1=r1 Q^j, z6=x r1 Q^k6, z7=x r0 Q^l, r0^N=A, r1^N=B, A B(B-x^N A)!=0. Retain a,b,c,d0 for their logarithms and define k=the representative of l-i modulo N in {1,...,N}, m=the representative of k6-j modulo N in {1-N,...,0}. Choose the corresponding matched logarithmic lifts so that d0-a-X=k h and c-b-X=m h. The whole-turn characters are one at the original balanced grids, so this does not change M or discard its compensating central factors. The positive octahedral chamber has 1<=k<=N-1, 2-N<=m<=0. (1) Indeed its positive angle sums are, up to the recorded half-step, theta1+theta3=2pi*k/N and theta2+theta3=2pi*(N+m-1)/N. These are both between zero and 2pi. The EXACT polynomial statements hold for all those cyclic representatives, including k=N and m=1-N. Only the positive-chart estimates need the strict ranges in (1). Let M be the actual normalized Fourier matrix entry, including its original kappa and every fixed central factor. It is explicitly the four-full-Psi expression (14) of the linked theorem; every grid entry is nonzero on its regular torus. ## 2. The exact ORIGINAL finite-band interpolants Write (v;Q)_L=product_(r=0)^(L-1)(1-Q^r v). For a single variable Z and all other ports fixed on the ORIGINAL grids, define the following Laurent polynomials: P0(Z)=Z^m (z1/(xZ);Q)_(N+m-1), P1(Z)=(Q^(k+1)x z0/Z;Q)_(N-k), P6(Z)=Z^(N-k)(Q^(1-k)Z/z0;Q)_(k-1), P7(Z)=(Q^m Z/(x z6);Q)_(-m). (2) P0 and P7 use m in {1-N,...,0}; P1 and P6 use k in {1,...,N}. They have the exact physical spectra | Port | Powers | Physical frequency indices | | --- | --- | --- | | input z0 | negative | -m,...,N-1 | | input z1 | negative | 0,...,N-k | | output z6 | positive | N-k,...,N-1 | | output z7 | positive | 0,...,-m | Every coefficient inside the stated interval is nonzero. Each interval is contained in the ORIGINAL head band 0,...,N-1. Choose any fixed grid value Z_* for the port under consideration. Then its exact original Fourier interpolation is g_port(Z)=M(Z_*) P_port(Z)/P_port(Z_*). (3) This preserves the full ORIGINAL scalar. M(Z_*) is a known explicit local four-full-Psi value, not an unknown knot period. P_port(Z_*) is nonzero since its root central argument is not one. No new normalization is introduced by (3). Equation (3) agrees with M at EVERY old grid point. Since its physical frequency interval lies in 0,...,N-1, finite Fourier uniqueness makes it the actual original finite-band interpolation. It therefore holds for every complex nonzero Z, with no omitted residues or approximate projection. At the two cyclic endpoint cases the table is literal: k=N gives P1=1 and P6 of degree N-1; m=1-N gives the input monomial P0=Z^(1-N) and P7 of degree N-1. There is no degree-N norm polynomial substituted for a constant grid row. ## 3. Full-function proof, including every period and alias factor In the exact kernel use beta=b-a-X, f=d0-c-X, rho=c-a, lambda=d0-b+2pi*i, G=d0-a-X, J=b-c+X. Its full-function part is Psi(beta)Psi(h-f)Psi(lambda+2pi*i+h)/Psi(rho). First use the EXACT whole-turn identity Psi(lambda+2pi*i+h) =Psi(h+d0-b)/(1-exp[N(d0-b)])^2. (4) On the old grids exp[N(d0-b)]=x^N A/B, and R=exp(Nrho)=x^N B/A. Thus the central density R(1-R)^2 in kernel (14), divided by (1-1/R)^2 from (4), is exactly R^3. For interpolation, these are the fixed old-grid constants. They are retained in the normalizer in (3). This qualification matters: substituting a moving Z into the RAW four-Psi expression changes those Nth powers. That meromorphic continuation is generally NOT the finite Fourier interpolation. For example (4) creates moving double poles at (z7/Z)^N=1; they are absent from the polynomial (3). No contour is moved across such artificial poles by the present theorem. For input z0, rho-beta=c-b+X=(N+m-1)h. Hence Psi(beta)/Psi(rho)=(exp beta;Q)_(N+m-1). The exact Gaussian in kernel (14) has a-dependent power exp(m a). This gives P0 after the fixed central factors are retained. For input z1, beta+(d0-b)=G=kh. Full inversion gives Psi(beta)Psi((k+1)h-beta) =zeta exp[pi*i*(sqrt(N)beta/(2pi)-c_b)^2] *(Q^(k+1)exp(-beta);Q)_(N-k). Combining its Gaussian with the ORIGINAL kernel Gaussian leaves exp(-N beta), times a factor independent of b. On the old grid exp(-N beta) is a known fixed central scalar. Retaining that scalar gives precisely P1. This is the integer alias +N b; it is compensated by its known old-grid value. For output z6, h-f=rho+(1-k)h, so Psi(h-f)/Psi(rho)=(Q^(1-k)exp rho;Q)_(k-1). The original Gaussian power is exp[-(N+k)c]. Its fixed-grid alias exp(-2N c) is retained as a central scalar, leaving exp[(N-k)c] and giving P6. For output z7 put t=h-f. Then t+(h+d0-b)=(N+m+1)h. The same full inversion gives a polynomial of length -m, with argument Q^m z7/(xz6). Its Gaussian combines with the original one to give exp(3N d0), independent of the remaining polynomial. This is again a known old-grid central scalar and gives P7. All displayed Gaussian cancellations are exact, including the affine logarithmic marks and half-step in X. Thus the integer aliases +N b,+2N c,-3N d0 are NOT discarded phases: their known central values are in (3). Nonzero coefficients in (2) follow from the finite q-binomial theorem, since all factorial indices in its lengths are less than N. There is also a genuine TWO-port result. With b,c fixed on their original grids, the physical interpolant factors exactly: M_interp(Z0,Z7)=M(z0_*,z7_*) *P0(Z0)P7(Z7)/[P0(z0_*)P7(z7_*)]. (3a) With a,d0 fixed, the analogous formula uses P1(Z1)P6(Z6). To prove this, kernel (14) on the original grids separates into an a-only factor times a d0-only factor when b,c are fixed: its Gaussian has no a*d0 term, and its full functions and central factors split. The other pair splits likewise. Every two-by-two conditional minor is zero. Tensor-product finite Fourier uniqueness then proves (3a) for BOTH free complex variables, with the complete original scalar. This is a paired polynomial identity, not the assertion that the raw four-Psi formula is the same off-grid function. ### The pair scalar is explicit and tame The reference value in (3a) can be eliminated altogether. Use the [uniform signed role table](actual_signed_overbridge_unwinding.md) and write the paired kernel as c_sigma Pout Pin, with the physical over/under clock h in 0,...,d used there. Then c_(+,over)=kappa/N *(-1)^h Q^(h(h+1)/2) z6^h, c_(+,under)=kappa/N *(-1)^h Q^(h(h+1)/2) z0^(-h), c_(-,over)=kappa^(-1)/N *(-1)^h Q^(-h(h+1)/2) z7^h, c_(-,under)=kappa^(-1)/N *(-1)^h Q^(-h(h+1)/2) z1^(-h). (3b) These retain the ENTIRE original crossing scalar and phase. Their magnitudes lie between c_K/N and C_K/N on fixed nonzero central compacta, uniformly in every spectator label and h. Their explicit Gaussian and monomial phases can still carry a leading oscillatory action; tameness is not positivity. Here is an independent all-level proof directly from ORIGINAL coefficients. For the positive over-pair extract over-input physical frequency h and over-output frequency zero. Since the chosen Pin starts with Z^(-h) and Pout with 1, this coefficient is exactly c. The original sparse crossing gives c=kappa/N^2 z6^h F_h sum_(t=0)^(d-h) [h+t choose t]_Q Q^(-ht). Root complementation turns its summand into (-1)^t Q^(t(t+1)/2)[d-h choose t]_Q. The finite q-binomial theorem makes that sum F_(d-h). Finally F_h F_(d-h)=N(-1)^h Q^(h(h+1)/2). This proves the first line. For the positive under-pair extract input frequency zero and output frequency h; the same original coefficient sum appears, multiplied by z0^(-h). The exact negative mirror conjugates kappa and Q and swaps ports, proving the other lines. Reversing a Q^(-1) product only reorders its factors and introduces no further scalar. All steps hold for even and composite levels as well. This improves merely specifying the scalar by a known local value: no hidden exponential magnitude is left in the pair normalization. It also fixes the normalization of every source-preserving bridge contraction in the linked theorem. ## 4. Actual adapter action and a nonzero analytic symbol For an outgoing positive-band port the exact finite adapter F(r')F(r)^(-1) acts on the sampled polynomial by g(r Q^j) -> g(r' Q^j). (5) For an incoming port the inverse/contravariant adapter has the same evaluation statement with the matching direction and the negative powers in (2). This is finite Fourier interpolation, not a formal pseudodifferential assertion. Take r'/r=exp(delta/N) with delta in a fixed compact set. On a compact positive octahedral chart every factor in the corresponding Pochhammer arc stays uniformly away from zero. The arc connects two nonreal positive-orientation endpoints without crossing 1. Its length is at most N. Thus log[g(Z exp(delta/N))/g(Z)] =delta p_port(Z)+O_K(1/N), p_port=(1/N) Z partial_Z log P_port. (6) The estimate is uniform, with derivatives: the second logarithmic derivative of each factor is bounded, so the sum of N such derivatives is O_K(N). Equation (6) follows by Taylor expansion through a displacement delta/N. Ordinary Riemann sums on the zero-free arc give p_port's explicit classical limit with another O_K(1/N) error. The resulting adapter symbol is exp(delta p_port), nonzero and bounded above and below on compact data. The sign convention in (6) is the Laurent power of the kernel: physical incoming momentum is -p_port, whereas physical outgoing momentum is +p_port. The REAL parts of its physical incoming/outgoing momenta, after the just-proved fixed aliases, are p_in,0=1-(theta2+theta3)/(4pi), p_in,1=1/2-(theta1+theta3)/(4pi), p_out,0=1-(theta1+theta3)/(4pi), p_out,1=1/2-(theta2+theta3)/(4pi). (7) Every one belongs to (0,1), uniformly away from its ends on every compact positive chamber. At the regular octahedron they are (3/4,1/4;3/4,1/4). This agrees with the ORIGINAL finite-head indices, not an independently selected wave packet. Equivalently, the exact global linear alias of the original action is 2pi*i(b+2c-3d0), with inverse scalar compensation by exp[-N(b+2c-3d0)]. On the original grids this scalar is known and bounded for fixed central data. Its derivative puts all four momenta in the physical band without changing any actual matrix value or original source. ## 5. Unique GLOBAL fixed-port angular maxima Assume additionally |A|!=|B|, as in the fixed regular choice A=2,B=3i. Along each original port circle all Pochhammer roots are radially separated by a constant times 1/N. Uniformly on the ENTIRE conditional angular circle, sum_(j=0)^(L-1) log|1-e^((gamma+i phi)/N) e^(i theta)Q^j| =N integral_0^(L/N) log|1-e^(i(theta+2pi t))|dt +O_K(log N). (8) Here gamma ranges in a compact set bounded away from zero, L<=N, and phi is bounded. To prove (8), regularize the periodic logarithmic singularity at radial distance |gamma|/N. Its total variation is O_K(log N), giving that Riemann-sum error; its integrated change from the boundary logarithm is O_K(log N/N). This also proves the endpoint uniformity. Known monomial and source constants do not depend on theta. Let L(theta)=D(exp(i theta)). On a fixed positive crossing chart the four angles sum to 2pi. A conditional port varies only one of the following two FULL-circle profiles, up to constant and reversal of its angular coordinate: H_delta(theta)=L(theta)-L(theta+delta), J_delta(theta)=L(theta)+L(delta-theta), 0<delta<2pi. (9) For input z0 and output z6 use H with the sum of the two other relevant positive angles; for input z1 and output z7 use J with the fixed sum of their two varying positive angles. By (8) these are the true leading logarithmic modulus profiles of the ORIGINAL finite polynomials on the whole circle. Explicitly, (2pi/N)log|g_port| equals its H_delta or J_delta profile, plus an angularly constant normalization and O_K(log N/N). The profile itself is not divided by 2pi. All quantum whole-turn factors are already in the fixed source normalization from Section 3. The maxima in (9) are UNIQUE and GLOBAL: max H_delta=2L(pi-delta/2), theta_*=pi-delta/2, max J_delta=2L(delta/2), theta_*=delta/2. (10) For H, differentiation gives H'=log|sin((theta+delta)/2)/sin(theta/2)|. Its only stationary points are theta_* and theta_*+pi. The former is the strict global maximum; the latter is the strict minimum. At shape-1 points the derivative is logarithmically infinite with the same monotone direction on both sides, so no extra endpoint maximum is concealed. For J the same computation gives its maximum theta_* and minimum theta_*+pi. The curvatures at the maxima are -tan(delta/4) and -cot(delta/4), respectively. At these maxima the two varying positively oriented tetrahedron angles are equal. If the other pair was positive, the maximum lies in the positive chamber. Every other sheet or endpoint on this conditional circle is strictly lower. On compact delta ranges, excluding a fixed neighborhood of theta_* gives a UNIFORM gap. This is a conditional statement. The other ports are held fixed. Its maximum is not automatically the complete global geometric point after sewing the original knot. ## 6. Composition scope and the remaining global source issue The exact formulas may collapse ONE adapter, or the paired adapters of (3a), while the untouched opposite ports remain on their correlated original grids. Nothing here permits applying the other pair's formula after arbitrary movements of the first pair. In particular a general geometric complex deformation can destroy its integer relation. The exact [deck-character calculation](balanced_crossing_deck_characters.md) makes the obstruction explicit. If the first pair moves so that D!=sA, then the other input port has mu_b-1=(sD-A)/(A-sB), generically nonzero. The physical FOUR-variable Laurent polynomial remains single-valued; the raw four-Psi continuation does not. Known fixed-grid constants and integer alias multipliers alone cannot turn that raw continuation into a simultaneous equality. An asymptotic comparison in a complex neighborhood may still be possible, but it needs the additional seam terms or their actual bounds, beyond the one-pair theorem. Known phase oscillation is not removed by the modulus maxima. On the positive real-angle chamber the mixed input-output Hessian of the retained leading REAL action is partial_(theta_out) partial_(theta_in) Re W =-(1/2) I_2. Head-only or input/output-only gauges do not remove it. The exact one-port adapter result (5)--(7) controls its local Fourier action; it does not make the entire sewn original scalar a positive Laplace integral. Global cycle selection, compatible elimination order, and the retained cap/boundary source still need a proof. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_fourier_port_polynomials.py) checks (2)--(3) against independently evaluated ORIGINAL crossing matrices and their Fourier transforms, every allowed k/m frequency support and scalar normalization, and the analytic adapter and profile estimates.

title: An actual zero-source Fourier current retains a geometric formal block
text: # An actual zero-source Fourier current retains a geometric formal block Research theorem, 27 October 2026. The last Fourier-label source has an explicit, uniformly tame cyclic current complex. A literal Cartan port current of the ORIGINAL knot tensor lies in its zero-source subspace, retains the actual highest-input one-sided support, and on the proved regular geometric chart has a NONZERO formal block with the SAME regulator action. Thus nonzero geometric partial support, root scalarity, the pointed boundary line and one-sided support do not by themselves prove survival in the selected sum. This is an actual current/source obstruction, not a replacement state or a proposed positive model. The geometric formal assertion below uses the regular good-A chart; it does not assert that chart extends to the highest-input boundary A=1. ## 1. A literal whole Cartan current has zero selected source Let T_(c,d;a,b) be the original two-cut tensor, with every original cap, pivot, scalar and peripheral line retained. Put B=diag(Q^b) on the SECOND physical wire and define W(T)=[(I tensor B)T(I tensor B^-1)-T]/(Q-1). (1) Its literal band coefficient is W(T)_(c,b+q;a,b)=[q]_Q T_(c,b+q;a,b), [q]_Q=(Q^q-1)/(Q-1). (2) For every integer q this is a Laurent polynomial in Q, including negative q; it has a regular Q=1 continuation. Formula (1) is a specified actual position/Cartan PORT current. It makes no assumption about an untwisted total Hopf action on a reshaped tensor. Partial trace on the second identity wire is invariant under this conjugation. Therefore the ENTIRE reclosed first-wire matrix obeys ptr_second W(T)=0 (3) as a WHOLE finite-matrix identity, including all q-normal derivatives. No root scalarity is used in (3). The first input/output source, highest vector, Whittaker row and external dimension line remain exactly the originals. The multiplier (2) changes no index or support. If T is charge zero and the first input is a, its band interval is [a-(N-1),a]. At the highest input a=0 it remains the original nonpositive interval. In particular the actual endpoint defects 1-Q^N and M-M^-1 of [the highest boundary](actual_highest_whittaker_boundary_and_moving_walls.md) have not been discarded or replaced by cyclic off-root formulas. ## 2. The exact root Fourier current complex Let J_j be the RAW Fourier partial array with fixed first input, including its inverse-Fourier 1/N. Its selected source is Sigma J, where Sigma J=sum_j J_j, with NO outside 1/N. At Q=Q_N the actual Fourier transform sends (1) to J_W,j=(J_(j+1)-J_j)/(Q_N-1), (4) with cyclic j modulo N. This follows from (2) and Q_N^(Nq)=1, or by the actual cyclic companion matrix at the root. Thus Sigma J_W=0, in agreement with the stronger whole identity (3). Put D=(S-I)/(Q_N-1), S J_j=J_(j+1), and P J=(Sigma J/N)1. Over the root coefficient field, ker D=constant vectors, im D=ker Sigma. (5) There is an explicit centered inverse h on the zero-source space. For f put g=f-Pf and (h f)_j=(Q_N-1){sum_(k<j)g_k -(1/N)sum_(ell=0)^(N-1)sum_(k<ell)g_k}. Direct telescoping, including the cyclic last endpoint, proves D h=h D=I-P, h P=0, Sigma h=0. (6) This is a strict finite cyclic source/current contraction, with section i(c)=c1/N. It is not an assertion that the actual port clock remains a cyclic shift off root. At whole Q its Vandermonde companion has the previously proved last-row carry, and (3), not an uncorrected cyclic formula, is the normal-source identity. This image statement also lifts to literal highest-input port tensors, rather than only abstract sequences. For any g with Sigma g=0 put f_(-b)=sum_j g_j Q_N^(jb), 1<=b<N, and take R_(b,0;0,b)=f_(-b)/[-b]_(Q_N), with every other entry zero. All arrows are in the original head, the tensor is charge zero, its highest band support is one-sided, and its reclosed matrix is zero. The highest Fourier family of W(R) is EXACTLY g. Every divided coefficient here is a nonzero head unit. Thus every zero-source highest Fourier array has an explicit actual-port Cartan primitive. In the flat root metrics, Parseval and |[-b]_(Q_N)|>=1 give the tame bound ||R||_HS<=sqrt(N)||g||_2. This concerns the linear actual port/ current category; it does not assert that arbitrary R is a new uninserted knot word. In the flat complex root metric the cyclic Fourier basis is unitary. For nonzero mode k the inverse h has multiplier (Q_N-1)/(Q_N^k-1), whose modulus is at most one. Hence EXACTLY ||h||_2<=1, ||J||_2^2=|Sigma J|^2/N+||(I-P)J||_2^2, |Sigma J|=sqrt(N) dist(J,im D). (7) Thus the selected norm measures distance from actual zero-source currents, rather than the size of the partial array. There is no positive lower bound for that distance from ||J|| alone. These are norms of this specified finite source complex, not estimates for the full knot word or a uniform q-normal neighborhood. For a literal ACTUAL example, the two-cut unknot is the flip tensor. At first input zero it has F_0(eta_F)=sum_(b=0)^(N-1) eta_F^-b, J_j=delta_(j,0), J_W,j=[delta_(j+1,0)-delta_(j,0)]/(Q_N-1). The last array is nonzero, one-sided before Fourier transformation, and its selected source is zero at every N>1. Its source and actual moving endpoint operators are precisely the originals. ## 3. The same actual current has nonzero geometric normal support Now use the proved good first-position phase, not the unproved highest-boundary extension. The actual proper root lift and its nondegenerate Fourier Gaussian give Z(v,H)=C(H) exp(S_geo/H)[A_0(v)+H A_1(v)+...], eta=exp(v), p_e=eta^-1. Here S_geo is independent of v; all original base, peripheral, half-density and Fourier phase marks stay in C and the chosen line. Multiplication of the actual open coefficient by (2) is EXACTLY the external shift identity Z_W(v,H)=[Z(v+H,H)-Z(v,H)]/(exp(H)-1). (8) Equation (8) uses the specified proper root lift of the partial family; it does not equate that lift's q-normal jets with the whole-Vandermonde family. It follows coefficientwise, rather than by a growing-band analytic limit. Hence Z_W=C(H) exp(S_geo/H)[partial_v A_0+O(H)]. (9) The leading derivative is NOT identically zero. Indeed the uniform actual Gaussian/holonomy density and its Fourier Jacobian show at fixed good A that A_0(v)=c(M,A) partial_v r(eta), (10) up to the retained fixed ordered Fourier phase. Here is the needed frame-independence justification, rather than a free normalization: the [actual uniform density theorem](quantum_source_bridge_extension.md) gives Omega_beta^2=(-T_beta/2)Omega_cut^2. Its determinant ratio T_beta is invariant under simultaneous representation framing; the frame-change determinants in its two chain maps cancel and det Ad(g)=1. On the marked half-density cover the square of Omega_beta/Omega_cut is therefore frame-constant. Differentiating that square in characteristic zero makes the marked ratio itself frame-constant. The exact Fourier Jacobian then gives (10), with a nonzero c depending only on M,A and the retained base mark. At completeness r(eta) is the nonconstant rational inverse of the actual birational (A,p_e) chart. If partial_v A_0 vanished, eta partial_eta r would be a constant d. Then dr=d deta/eta. A derivative of a rational function has zero logarithmic residue at eta=0, so d=0, forcing r constant. This contradicts that birational chart. Thus partial_v A_0 is nonzero on a dense regular open. The result persists on the marked meridian deformation germ. Equations (3) and (9) prove the advertised obstruction: an ACTUAL zero-source port-current family has a nonzero formal geometric block with the same marked action as the knot. For its certificate use a common LEFT multiple, rather than assuming this insertion has unit principal amplitude: its multiplier vanishes at t=0 and contains H^-1. Let D(eta) be the already constructed meridian certificate for the original partial array and its SAME formal block, with eta the physical Fourier character Q^j. Then D(Q eta) annihilates the externally shifted array J(Q eta) and formal block Z(Q eta). The meridian shift fixes Q,eta. A nonzero common left multiple of D(eta) and D(Q eta), over the indicated localized Ore field, consequently annihilates their difference divided by Q-1, BOTH for actual root arrays and for the exact formal difference (8). Clear its denominators and remove its common q-1 power. Its leading symbol has the geometric factor because (9) is a nonzero formal block with the same longitude action. This avoids applying the unit-amplitude coefficient theorem directly to a vanishing insertion. The [original certificate theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md) supplies D and its formal identity. The selected scalar of this current family is nevertheless identically zero, whose minimal scalar annihilator is one. This is an explicit mechanism by which geometric partial support is lost in the final source pushforward. This does NOT say the uninserted knot's selected geometric contribution is zero, nor establish an actual exponential norm for the current arrays. It says that taking a nonzero local WKB line alone is not a faithful map on the actual source quotient. Any global comparison must carry the current/relative class and its marked cycle, not merely its action or leading local solution. ## 4. Compatibility with the first-cut highest moment decomposition There is a complementary exact first-port description in [the rank-one moment/orbit theorem](actual_rank_one_multiplicative_moment_and_orbit_source.md). With A_j[c,a]=T^V_(c,j;a,j), it proves J_whit,j=P_N/N+beta_K(D_K A_j), beta_K(X)=sum_(c=1)^(N-1) X_(c,0)/(Q_N^-c-1). The equality is entrywise: D_K multiplies that entry by Q_N^-c-1. The highest moment row c=0 forces q=0 in the uninserted conserving tensor and is constant in j at the root. Its exact beta norm is sqrt((N^2-1)/12). This decomposition retains the ORIGINAL orbit row and its Ward sector; it does not compute the unknown scalar P_N or move the regular good-A geometric block to A=1. Together with (5)--(9), it identifies the extra requirement sharply: the selected scalar class must be determined in the cyclic/current quotient, including boundary and normal data. Scalar root closure, pointing, algebraicity of the geometric optimizer and a nonzero partial A-factor do not supply that determination by themselves. The [flat cyclic source-frame theorem](flat_cyclic_source_frame_and_scalar_period.md) is consistent with this: it fixes the aligned whole clock/source frame before jets, but the scalar of the supplied closed word is separate. Here its actual cyclic-source kernel and a nonzero geometric formal current in that kernel are both explicit. [Exact current/source and cyclic-complex audit](../experiments/audit_zero_source_fourier_current.py) and [saved results](../experiments/zero_source_fourier_current_results.json). The checks pass seven root levels with all 8,771 port units, 119 highest-input conserving units, 35 cyclic homotopy basis vectors, eight checks of the proved norm bound, and the exact whole-Q two-cut unknot. The latter detects the nonzero off-root carry missed by treating the root cyclic difference as a whole companion formula. [The intrinsic Mobius-pole calculation](mobius_fourier_framing_and_intrinsic_norm_pole.md) makes r(eta) and its pole explicit. Its root norm factor 1-lambda^N explains why sampling the rational principal density is not automatically a uniform source comparison. In particular the actual figure-eight principal pole meets the sampling grid at N divisible by six, while its finite arrays remain regular.

title: Actual Frobenius endpoint periods and the normal current correction
text: # Actual Frobenius endpoint periods and the normal current correction Research proof and independent audit, 27 October 2026. The actual paired Frobenius source has an explicit Serre-dual relative interval with the required geometric endpoints. Its original whole quantum source gives a rational relative-period deformation of this interval. The normal connection required by that deformation is computable; it is already different from a naive divided-Borel generator at first order. Endpoint norm growth is also explicit. This is a source-level relative-period map. It does not identify the full braid network's residual Gaussian currents with it. ## 1. The canonical interval is an actual finite unipotent source Use the actual Sym^N source and dual from [the marked Borel construction](actual_unprojectivized_frobenius_borel_torsor.md). Write \[ \psi_\alpha=\alpha^N\sum_{k=0}^N v_k,\qquad \lambda_m(v_k)=\alpha^{-N}\binom Nk \left(\frac{1+m}{2}\right)^{N-k} \left(\frac{1-m}{2}\right)^k . \tag{1} \] The source pairing is one. These formulas include the missing finite-u chart point m=-1 (u=infinity); no inverse flag coefficient is introduced there. Take D=0 in the framing map, so \[ s=C\alpha^2,\quad r=(1+m)/2,\quad A=(1+s)^{-1},\quad \tau=r/s=\frac{1+m}{2C\alpha^2}. \] The geometric marked interval tau=0 to 1 has the EXACT endpoints \[ m_0=-1,\qquad m_1=-1+2C\alpha^2. \tag{2} \] Put L=C alpha^2 and n=h+f-e, where e,f,h are the original root divided Frobenius matrices. Direct calculation in the actual module gives \[ n\psi_\alpha=0,\quad n^{N+1}=0,\quad \partial_m\lambda_m=\tfrac12\lambda_m n, \quad\lambda_\tau=\lambda_0\exp(\tau L n). \tag{3} \] Equivalently, \[ \lambda_\tau(v_k)=\alpha^{-N}\binom Nk (L\tau)^{N-k}(1-L\tau)^k . \tag{4} \] Thus the interval co-source is a specified finite expression, \[ \mathcal I=\int_0^1\lambda_\tau\,d\tau =\lambda_0\sum_{j=0}^N\frac{(Ln)^j}{(j+1)!}, \qquad \mathcal I Ln=\lambda_1-\lambda_0. \tag{5} \] No inverse of n is used. Every original matrix insertion B satisfies \[ \mathcal I[Ln,B]\psi_\alpha =(\lambda_1-\lambda_0)B\psi_\alpha. \tag{6} \] This retains both endpoints and their alpha-dependent displacement. Since Omega_cut=d tau wedge dlog A, integrating its source kernel along this marked interval gives precisely the co-source (5) times dlog A, with that orientation. An arbitrary translation tau_0(A) moves both endpoint rows; it does not erase them. At L=1, the beta integral in (4) gives \[ \mathcal I(v_k)=\frac{\alpha^{-N}}{N+1}. \tag{7} \] For alpha=C=1 this is the original uniform Frobenius co-source. Thus exponential endpoint norms do not imply an exponential scalar period: the full integrated row, including cancellations, matters. ## 2. Serre residue preserves the same actual endpoint rows Use the exact convention \[ v_k\longmapsto\binom Nk z^k\in H^0(\mathbb P^1,O(N)), \quad c_\lambda(z)=\sum_{k=0}^N \frac{\lambda(v_k)}{\binom Nk}z^{-k-1}. \] The second expression is a Cech representative for H^1(O(-N-2)); its pairing is Res_(z=0) c_lambda f dz. These conventions and all actual normal operators are developed in [the global Frobenius Cech source](global_frobenius_cech_source_and_endpoints.md). For the interval (4) the representative is explicitly \[ c_\tau(z)=\alpha^{-N}\sum_{k=0}^N (L\tau)^{N-k}(1-L\tau)^k z^{-k-1}. \tag{8} \] It is polynomial in tau, has the fixed allowed Cech exponents, and retains both endpoints in (2). Residue, interval integration, and the finite matrix action commute exactly. Hence (5)--(6) hold as Serre-dual cohomology identities, not only scalar coincidences. The residue pairing alone supplies no identification of n with the network's full actual Hopf-adjoint current. ## 3. An original whole-source rational period retains ALL normal jets Fix a residue string s of the original high integral color. Let F_s(q), E_s(q) be its actual divided matrices, with the original root sign included in E_s, so their root values are f,e. Write \[ B_k(q)=[\exp F_s(q)v_0]_k,\qquad A_k(q)=[v_0^*\exp E_s(q)]_k . \] The exponentials are finite because these matrices are strictly triangular. Their root values are B_k=1 and A_k=binom(N,k).
