Define ORIGINAL whole source and homogeneous dual \[ \begin{split} \psi(q)&=\alpha^N\sum_k B_k(q)v_k,\\ \widetilde\lambda(q,m)(v_k) &=\alpha^{-N}A_k(q) ((1+m)/2)^{N-k}((1-m)/2)^k,\\ U_s(q,m)&=\widetilde\lambda(q,m)\psi(q),\qquad \lambda(q,m)=\widetilde\lambda(q,m)/U_s(q,m). \tag{9} \end{split} \] These are the actual divided-source germs, expressed homogeneously; the normalization is their ACTUAL pairing. No root binomial weight is differentiated in place of that pairing. In particular \[ U_s(q_N,m)=1 \tag{10} \] for every finite m, including both endpoints. Consequently the whole interval co-source \[ \mathcal I_s(q)=\int_0^1 \lambda(q,-1+2L\tau)\,d\tau \tag{11} \] is a rational relative-period integral on the tau line with the zeros of U_s deleted and endpoints 0,1 retained. For fixed N it is analytic near q_N on a small neighborhood where the compact path has no U_s zero. Equivalently it exists coefficientwise in the completed actual quantum normal ring. Every coefficient of the inverse of U_s is polynomial in m because its constant coefficient is one; normal expansion and the compact interval integral commute. The same applies to its Serre representative (8), replacing lambda by (9), and to every original whole matrix insertion B(q). For each finite normal truncation this is an explicit algebraic calculation followed by a relative rational period. It imposes no uniform-in-N neighborhood, metric bound, or geometric-saddle claim. It is generally a period, rather than a rational function of q: integrating a rational row with moving poles can produce logarithms. There is also an exact source-pair current connection. Put \[ P_0=\psi_0\lambda_0(\tau),\quad P_q=\psi(q)\lambda(q,\tau), \quad G=\psi(q)\lambda_0+(I-P_q)(I-P_0). \] Its root is I, so it is an invertible rational germ; directly G psi_0=psi(q) and lambda(q)G=lambda_0. Define \[ K_q=G(Ln)G^{-1}-(\partial_\tau G)G^{-1}. \tag{12} \] Since psi(q) is tau-independent, the exact identities are \[ K_q\psi(q)=0,\quad\partial_\tau\lambda(q)=\lambda(q)K_q, \] and for every insertion, including tau-dependent ones, \[ \partial_\tau[\lambda(q)B(q,\tau)\psi(q)] =\lambda(q)([K_q,B]+\partial_\tau B)\psi(q). \tag{13} \] Integration gives the ACTUAL endpoint rows with all normal coefficients retained. Formula (12) constructs a source connection; it does not assert that the network's Hopf current equals K_q. That comparison requires an actual intertwining calculation. ## 4. A literal actual first-normal defect forbids the naive lift The distinction in the last sentence is already necessary at N=3, r=3, residue string s=1 of the original high color 12. Use epsilon=log(q/q_3), q_3=exp(pi i/3), and include the actual root sign tau=(-1)^(Nr-1)=+1 in e(q). Direct integral Gaussian coefficient differentiation gives \[ e(q)=e+\gamma\epsilon e+O(\epsilon^2),\quad f(q)=f+\gamma\epsilon f+O(\epsilon^2),\qquad \gamma=1-2q_3=-i\sqrt3. \tag{14} \] For example the first divided coefficient is, including its constant beta sign, [4]_q/[1]_q; the sign does not affect its logarithmic derivative, which at q_3 is 3(q_3+q_3^{-1})/(q_3-q_3^{-1})=gamma. The remaining entries give the same gamma, as the exact audit checks independently using integral Gaussian polynomials. The naive whole divided generator \[ n(q)=[e(q),f(q)]+f(q)-e(q) \] therefore satisfies \[ n(q)\exp(f(q))v_0 =-2\gamma\epsilon f\psi_0+O(\epsilon^2)\ne0. \tag{15} \] Indeed psi_1=gamma f psi_0, n_1=gamma(2h+f-e), [n,f]=-2f-h, and n psi_0=0. This proves (15) without numerical approximation. The endpoint current (12) kills the actual whole source; hence it differs from L n(q) already in this first normal. The extreme residue strings s=0 and s=N-1 have vanishing first derivative here, so testing only them misses the defect. This is a source/connection defect, not a claim about failure of the actual quantum-group relations. ## 5. A sharp endpoint metric obstruction and its limitation The actual root Frobenius coherent metric in this divided basis is g_k=binom(N,k). Then \[ \|\psi_\alpha\|^2=|\alpha|^{2N}2^N,\qquad \|\lambda_m\|_*^2=|\alpha|^{-2N} ((1+|m|^2)/2)^N. \] Thus the normalized rank-one source coupon satisfies EXACTLY \[ \|\psi_\alpha\lambda_m\| =(1+|m|^2)^{N/2}. \tag{16} \] Any translated geometric interval of length one at fixed s has endpoint displacement m_1-m_0=2s. The triangle inequality gives max(|m_0|,|m_1|)>=|s|, hence \[ \max_{j=0,1}\|\psi_\alpha\lambda_{m_j}\| \ge(1+|s|^2)^{N/2}. \tag{17} \] At the regular anchor s=-2,A=-1 this is at least 5^(N/2), for EVERY translation of the marked interval. The unshifted endpoints are m=-1,-5, giving 2^(N/2) and 26^(N/2). This rules out an automatic tame UNITARY endpoint comparison in the specified actual Frobenius coherent metric. It does not rule out the integrated period or cancellations: (7) is an exact counterexample to that inference. A transported metric, a contour comparison, or retained character compensation needs its own proof. Neither Serre duality nor a root Borel isomorphism supplies that proof by itself. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_frobenius_relative_endpoint.py) checks the finite unipotent/interval identities, Serre residues, the actual integral Gaussian first-normal defect, and the metric formulas. No volume asymptotic is assumed.

title: The finest crossing bound is unchanged by arbitrary matrix wire gauges
text: # The finest crossing bound is unchanged by arbitrary matrix wire gauges 29 October 2026. Allowing off-diagonal matrices on individual physical wires does not improve the existing alternating-sign crossing bound. This extends the earlier diagonal optimizer theorem to every positive definite one-wire matrix, with the original paired source fixed. The proof uses the full one-head density matrices, not only their diagonal entries. It does NOT exclude entangled metrics on several wires, coherent clock packets, or norms formed after block contraction. ## 1. Exact source-preserving matrix gauges Use the original balanced crossing matrices and paired plat source of [the weighted energy theorem](actual_weighted_fourier_plat_energy.md). At the bottom a cup pair is, up to its retained scalar, vec(U), where U is an anti-diagonal unitary matrix. At the top the ordinary or marked co-source similarly has an anti-diagonal unitary coefficient matrix; the ordinary pair includes its actual pivot. The marked pair is used only after the already proved whole-degree reduction. No source is changed on a separately dephased state. On each physical wire segment choose an arbitrary positive matrix P_e=exp(H_e), H_e Hermitian. At a bottom pair require P_o U P_e^T=U, H_e=-U^T H_o^T bar(U). (1) The second identity is equivalent to the first, by the unique Hermitian matrix logarithm. At a top pair apply the same formula to the conjugate of its actual cap matrix. These relations fix the actual input vector and output covector. In particular their diagonal entries obey (H_e)_(b,b)=-(H_o)_(d-b,d-b), d=N-1, (2) regardless of the off-diagonal entries or the retained root phases. Bottom and top gauges can be chosen independently subject to their own source relations. Untouched wires keep the same matrix at both ends. For a gate v define C_v=(P_out,1 tensor P_out,2) R_v (P_in,1 tensor P_in,2)^(-1), F(P)=sum_v log ||C_v||_HS. (3) All interior gauges cancel in the full original product. Equations (1) retain its endpoint source, so the standard whole-source bound using (3) remains valid, with the same external polynomial factors. ## 2. The full one-head densities are diagonal Every literal R_v preserves total INTEGER head degree. Therefore R_v R_v^* and R_v^*R_v commute with the sum of the two degree operators. Taking either partial trace shows that EACH one-head reduced density commutes with the simple one-head degree operator. It is consequently diagonal. This is an exact matrix statement, including the complete-color endpoint and its nilpotent source. Normalize these reduced matrices by ||R_v||_HS^2. For R_+, symmetry R_+^T=R_+ makes its input and output first-head densities equal, and likewise for its second head. Denote their diagonal probabilities by p_H and p_L. The literal factorial reflection gives p_H(a)=p_L(d-a). (4) For R_- the two one-head densities are exchanged. These are the same exact coefficient identities proved in [the diagonal gauge theorem](actual_convex_gauge_block_energy.md), now supplemented by the off-diagonal vanishing above. The common Cartan/framing scalar is a unit phase and remains external. ## 3. Convexity along every Hermitian gauge ray proves the optimizer Assume the actual signed word has sign(sigma_i)=epsilon*(-1)^(i+1), epsilon=+1 or -1, (5) at each occurrence of generator i. Its index sequence, number of crossings and even width are otherwise arbitrary. When its plat is a one-component knot, all original source identifications above apply. For ANY collection H satisfying (1), set P_e(t)=exp(t H_e). The endpoint relations hold at every real t. Vectorizing a gate gives vec(C_v(t))=exp(t K_v) vec(R_v), K_v=H_out,1+H_out,2-H_in,1^T-H_in,2^T, (6) where each term acts on its own tensor leg. Thus K_v is Hermitian. By its finite spectral decomposition, log ||C_v(t)||_HS =one_half log sum_j w_j exp(2t lambda_j), w_j>=0. (7) Its second derivative is twice the variance of lambda_j under the displayed normalized weights, hence nonnegative. No assumption that different H_e commute is used: the four operators in (6) act on separate legs. F(P(t)) is therefore convex in t. At t=0 its derivative is the sum, over every outgoing wire, of Tr(H_e rho_out,e), minus the corresponding incoming terms. Under (5), every odd physical wire has the same normalized one-head density at all its incident gates, and every even wire has its reflected density. All interior terms cancel. At a paired boundary the remaining terms cancel by (2),(4). Off-diagonal H entries contribute zero because the full densities are diagonal. Therefore dF(P(t))/dt at t=0 =0. (8) Convexity on the ray from identity to any prescribed P proves the EXACT finite-level theorem inf_{all positive matrix wire gauges preserving source} F(P) =m log ||R_+||_HS, (9) where m is the number of crossings. Flat gauges attain the right side. This is a proof for all admissible matrices, not numerical optimization over a chosen finite set of off-diagonal perturbations. The same conclusion holds if invertible complex one-wire gauges are allowed. Write each as U_e P_e by polar decomposition. At every gate the outer unitary factors do not change its HS norm. The positive parts preserve the unitary paired source too: if A U B^T=U, then B=U^T A^(-T)bar(U), whose positive polar factor is U^T P_A^(-T)bar(U). The analogous cap formula follows from A^T L B=L with its unitary L. Thus (9) applies to their positive parts. ## 4. Operator norms and the actual scope Each crossing acts on N^2 dimensions, so ||C_v||_HS/N <= ||C_v||_op <= ||C_v||_HS. Consequently the optimum product of operator norms differs from the HS optimum by at most a power N^m. The already proved crossing factorial asymptotic gives, for all these matrix wire gauges, inf sum_v log ||C_v||_op =m N v_8/(2pi)+O_word(log N). (10) This is a limitation of the finest local norm estimate, not a lower bound on the knot invariant. It leaves all cross-gate interference outside the norm, which is precisely what the desired coherent Gram must recover. The normalized-star identities and the new Pascal packet metric act on coupled boundary/coefficient data; they are not excluded by (9). Neither a general tensor-product wire metric nor a diagonal clock metric can by itself supply the sharp geometric bound for the alternating-sign class (5). The original source and degree hypotheses are explicit. This theorem does not apply an ordinary positive pivotal trace at color N, nor does it assert that every alternating knot presentation has pattern (5). [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_full_matrix_wire_gauge.py): literal positive/negative crossing reduced densities, original cup/cap matrix gauges, zero derivatives and finite off-diagonal gauge rays at several widths. The proof of the all-matrix optimizer is (6)-(9).

title: Exact pole pushforward with the original scalar cut-wall current retained
text: # Exact pole pushforward with the original scalar cut-wall current retained 28 October 2026. The absolutely convergent [full-Psi flow cycle](actual_full_psi_scalar_flow_cycle.md) can be pushed to a bare full-function head period PLUS an explicit scalar current on the negative-ray atomic cut walls. The current is an oriented tubular boundary of a specified radius homotopy; all wall intersections are retained with a common regularization. It is not an unknown matrix normalization or an asserted zero correction. This supplies an allowed exact cycle deformation and locates its additional chains. It still does not prove geometric survival or a sharp global bound on those chains. A cycle passing through a regular critical point does not determine its Lefschetz intersection number. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_full_psi_cut_wall_pushforward.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_full_psi_cut_wall_pushforward_results.json) check full-function Cauchy pushforwards for both signs and a coupled two-atom source with two distinct angular cuts. The latter explicitly has a nonzero correction; bare-circle substitution fails. ## 1. A scalar full-function Cauchy identity Use the exact moment chain M_(epsilon,R) of (3) in the flow note. For 0<|A|<R off the negative real ray, M_(epsilon,R)[1/(1-A/t)] =Psi_epsilon(Log_principal A). (1) This is an ordinary cut-disk Cauchy formula, not a formal coefficient expansion on its radial piece. For epsilon=+1 integrate Psi(Log t)dt/(t-A) around the disk cut on the negative axis, with an inner circle of radius delta. Its inner-circle integral tends to zero since Psi tends to 1 and A is fixed nonzero. On the two cut lips, Psi_lower=(1-t^N)Psi_upper. Their difference gives exactly the negative-ray term in M. The residue at t=A is Psi(Log A). Conjugate reflection gives epsilon=-1, including its orientation. Equation (1) cannot be applied to the original flow cycle with fixed head variables without moving that cycle: its head radii depend on the moment radii. That move is the source of the current below. ## 2. A global target head torus with no hidden large source First perform the exact HEAD Hardy-forest contraction from Section 8 of the flow note. Its continuous flow polytope is unchanged, and its reduced whole-source period is absolutely convergent. The remaining head-dependent poles are ONLY D_j: 1-A_j(z,xi)/t_j=0. (2) Every A_j is a primitive ratio of distinct retained head segments, times its explicit color/Gaussian coefficient. In particular it is not a constant self-loop. Choose finite outer moment radii R_j>=1 and target head log radii lambda_*(xi), independent of all t_j, such that |A_j|<=a_j^max<R_j, |lambda_*|<=C(1+sum|xi|). (3) Such a target exists by the original reduced small-argument radius construction with moment radii set to one. More generally it may be chosen to have ANY prescribed finite head radii at a fixed Gaussian tuple xi_g: use that prescribed vector in a compact xi neighborhood, the small-argument construction outside it, and a log-convex smooth interpolation. Enlarge the finitely many R_j to cover the compact modified neighborhood. All bounds in (3) remain uniform in xi. The flow proof extends verbatim from R_j=1 to any fixed finite R_j: replace -log|t_j| in its bound by its positive part; on 1<=|t_j|<=R_j all extra radial powers are bounded by R_j^N. Thus the original source still has an absolute Gaussian majorant with explicit exp(C_word N) constants. No discarded exterior-radius estimate is being substituted for the exact ray chain. At the target, integrate each full moment chain first. Equation (1) gives the bare product of Psi_epsilon(Log_principal A_j), with exactly the original monomials, Gaussian and coupled K_N sources. This target period is well-defined as an ordinary angular cut period. Its moment form is locally absolutely integrable even where a radial pole meets the head torus: integrate its real radial distance first to obtain at most a logarithm of the angular distance to Arg A_j=pi. Products of finitely many such logarithms are integrable. Indeed Holder's inequality reduces this to finite powers of one logarithm of a nonzero torus character, whose Haar integral is finite. Each radial variable is separate even if some atomic angular characters coincide. Condition (3) prevents circle-pole intersections. The head source contributes at most exp(CN(1+sum|xi|)) times a fixed power of N. All A_j stay in a bounded disk, where the selected principal-log full function is bounded at each N, including its continuous limit at zero. Therefore the target period is jointly absolutely convergent with its Gaussian variables as well. ## 3. The exact global homotopy and its correction current Let lambda_0(t,xi) be the reduced flow-dual radii, and use the single angle-INDEPENDENT homotopy on the FULL head-angle torus lambda_s=(1-s)lambda_0+s lambda_*, 0<=s<=1. (4) There is no restriction to an isolated angular box whose side prisms would be omitted. The form is the original scalar full-function form, first with the exact K_N cap kernels integrated as polynomials. Source interval versions can be reinserted using their exact relative derivative on logarithmic seams. On every moment circle, both endpoints of (4) have |A_j|<R_j. Log-convex interpolation preserves this, so no D_j is crossed on circle pieces. On a moment ray t_j=-r_j, a crossing of D_j requires A_j=t_j<0. (5) These are the only extra pole loci in the head-radius homotopy. All head angular boundaries are paired globally. If one instead partitions into angular chambers, their side prisms MUST be included; they cancel pairwise off (5), with the remaining pole tubes retained. For complete precision, truncate every radial variable at a common delta>0, truncate the Gaussian box, and remove a common small tubular neighborhood of the union of (2) from the homotopy (4). Apply Stokes to its complement. Retain the ENTIRE induced tubular boundary, including all its matched intersections/corners; do not replace it by independent unsupported simple residues. Denote its integral, with the complement's boundary orientation, by W_(delta,epsilon). The matched full-Psi logarithmic lips are exactly those in M, so their outer endpoints cancel using the original monodromy. On a fixed radial end face the full form has dt_j=0. Gaussian end faces vanish in the limit by its majorant. One obtains P_original=P_bare+W, W=lim_(delta->0,epsilon->0) W_(delta,epsilon), (6) with the SAME common regularization for all tube pieces. The sign is fixed by the complement's boundary orientation. This aggregate limit exists because the initial and target periods just proved absolute have their corresponding limits and Stokes gives their difference. Separate periods for individual intersecting or divergent tube pieces are not assigned. The non-pole source-prefactor bound during (4) follows from convexity of its support function J: J(lambda_s)<=(1-s)J(lambda_0)+s J(lambda_*) <=d sum_j max(0,-log r_j)+CN(1+sum|xi|). Away from a fixed logarithmic pole tube the rational kernels are bounded. This justifies the finite-cutoff homotopy and its Gaussian limit, while the common tube regularization retains every pole term. No statement that W is small or zero is part of (6). ## 4. The simple-wall formula fixes the retained source and sign For one primitive head coordinate u=A and a Laurent test F(u), assume no other pole is crossed. If its initial radius obeys |u|<rho|t| and the target radius is a<R, the negative-ray pole u=t is crossed for 0<r<a. The head kernel has residue Res_(u=t) F(u)du/[u(1-u/t)]=-F(t). The resulting correction in (6) is exactly W=-epsilon/(2*pi*i) integral_0^a Psi_epsilon(log r+i epsilon pi) (-r)^N F(-r) dr/r. (7) Taking F(u)=u^(-b), 0<=b<N, gives precisely the original coefficient identity v_b=C_b-J_b. Thus this pushforward does not silently discard the low Cauchy moments of t^N Log t. For multiple atomic poles (6) retains their common tubular boundary, with (7) as its simple stratum. ## 5. Actual wall geometry, and what remains on the critical path A simple wall retains the explicit charge A_j^N. Its leading action is W_0+2*pi*i Log A_j. Regular transverse iterations give integer sums of these marks. The exponentiated actual canonical/Hurwitz equations and the original caps are unchanged. The independently proved [regular critical-regulator theorem](actual_wall_critical_regulator.md) shows that EVERY regular FULL interior critical point of such a wall action has its actual boundary-parabolic representation volume. The atom argument on the cut is flat; it need not be a physical degenerate meridian clock. Normalization ray cells can still carry the full geometric rate and must be grouped exactly. There is also an exact branch formula on the specified principal angular domain. If epsilon Arg A<0, then Psi_epsilon(Log A) =(1-A^N)Psi_epsilon(Log A+epsilon*2*pi*i). (8) The shifted logarithm is in the selected epsilon strip. Otherwise the principal logarithm already is in that strip. On compact angular cells away from the real rays, the uniform full-Psi symbol therefore applies to an EXACT finite integer-mark expansion. This does not assert that arbitrary Stokes branches in other domains are exhausted; positive-ray interfaces and all cut/corner chains remain part of the source. The Gaussian contour may also be shifted by any bounded constant imaginary vector, or a bounded endpoint-fixed deformation through a prescribed finite complex tuple. Apply the exact scalar source identity first: its remaining Gaussian integrand is a finite sum of entire exponential moments, with Gaussian decay on horizontal lines. The adapted flow radii satisfy the same bound with bounded imaginary parts, so this is an allowed full scalar cycle deformation, not an assumption that a fixed-circle Gaussian interchange is valid. Consequently a regular target head/Gaussian/cap chart can be specified through a given finite geometric point. The exact price is the current W in (6), not an unspecified comparison factor. Neither passing through that point nor the unit normal residue proves that the resulting whole cycle has nonzero geometric-thimble coefficient. Global growth near singular real-axis interfaces, non-full endpoint strata, approximate critical escape and the selected geometric lower bound still require proof. Equation (6) locates these issues in explicit scalar chains; it does not resolve them by notation.

title: Exact full-Psi deck characters and central gluing
text: # Exact full-Psi deck characters and central gluing 28 October 2026. The full functions in the ORIGINAL source and its new beta residue factors have an exact algebraic deck character. Products and integral monomial gluing carry this character without an unknown central normalizer. Its triviality equations are the marked exponential gluing equations in Frobenius coordinates. This constructs central data of the actual specified full-function components. It does not assert that the original invariant is only one such component, or that its complete relative source lies on the character-one locus. The [actual beta deck extension](actual_beta_current_connection_and_monodromy.md) shows why those additional assertions would be false without source and cycle control. ## 1. A full-function identity on the logarithmic cover Put h=2*pi*i/N, N>=2. Use precisely the two original functions Psi_epsilon, epsilon=+1,-1, with Psi_epsilon(L+epsilon*2*pi*i) =Psi_epsilon(L)/(1-exp(NL)). (1) For every integer m, meromorphic continuation gives Psi_epsilon(L+2*pi*i*m)/Psi_epsilon(L) =(1-exp(NL))^(-epsilon*m). (2) This includes negative shifts and all divisor multiplicities. An identity across a zero or pole is understood after cross-multiplication; no vanishing norm factor is separately inverted on the source. Let Z=(Z_1,...,Z_d) be marked logarithmic coordinates. Take integer row vectors a_j, a symmetric integer matrix C, constants ell_j and a specified linear term b_N. The constants may include actual colors and exact h or h/2 shifts. Consider the SPECIFIED component F_N(Z)=P_N(exp Z) exp[(Z^t C Z/2+b_N^t Z)/h] product_j Psi_(epsilon_j)(a_j.Z+ell_j), (3) where P_N is single-valued meromorphic in exp Z. It can contain the original integer powers, factorial constants and boundary polynomials; it is not assumed small. Write X_k=exp(NZ_k), Xi_j=exp(N ell_j), A_j=Xi_j product_k X_k^(a_jk), gamma_k=exp(N b_N,k+pi*i*N C_kk). Direct substitution in (2)--(3) gives EXACTLY F_N(Z+2*pi*i e_k)/F_N(Z)=chi_k(X), chi_k=gamma_k product_l X_l^(C_kl) product_j(1-A_j)^(-epsilon_j a_jk). (4) All half-step phases are present in Xi_j and gamma_k. In particular an h/2 shift contributes -1 to Xi_j and cannot be dropped before taking the Nth-power norm. The factor pi*i*N C_kk is also necessary. For example the bare Gaussian exp(-eta^2/(2h)) has character (-1)^N exp(-N eta), (5) not exp(-N eta). Such signs can cancel an actual half-step elsewhere in a complete kernel, but may not be removed from individual factors. For any winding n in Z^d, F_N(Z+2*pi*i*n)/F_N(Z) =exp[N n^t C Z+pi*i*N n^t C n+N b_N^t n] product_j(1-A_j)^(-epsilon_j a_j.n) =product_k chi_k^n_k. (6) The last equality uses n^t C n-sum_k n_k C_kk in 2Z. Thus the complete deck action is an algebraic character on the central torus, not only an infinitesimal semiclassical relation. Formula (6) fixes the integer Gaussian cocycle as well as its first generators. If a later elimination produces rational C or rational linear coordinates, (4) must be used on the corresponding integral cover or before that elimination. Clearing a common denominator and restricting to its integral deck sublattice is sufficient. This does not identify different logarithmic sheets of the original source. ## 2. The character-one equations are marked Frobenius gluing On a selected central logarithmic chart Y=Log X define W_cent,N(Y)=sum_j epsilon_j Li_2(Xi_j exp(a_j.Y)) +Y^t C Y/2+sum_k Log(gamma_k)Y_k. (7) The logarithms of gamma keep their specified marks from (4). Differentiation gives exp(partial_(Y_k) W_cent,N)=chi_k(X). (8) Consequently chi_k=1 is precisely the EXPONENTIAL marked gluing equation for this component. Its logarithmic lifts differ by the recorded multiples of 2*pi*i. This is an exact central identity at every N, before making a saddle approximation. The central variables X=exp(NZ) and the ordinary semiclassical shape variables exp Z are different. Equation (8) is not a convergence theorem between their evaluations, and does not put the selected source on chi=1. It specifies the Frobenius copy of the same monomial/dilogarithmic equations, with its actual norm and Gaussian marks retained. ## 3. The actual beta residue verifies the complete formula For the proved original trivalent section, put l=Log u, k=Log v. Its exact form is S_N=(N/phi_N)u^N exp[(l^2-kl)/h] Psi_+(k-l) Psi_+(h-l). (9) Here C=[[2,-1],[-1,0]], both atom signs are positive, and their rows are (-1,1),(-1,0). The exact h shift has central value one. The factor u^N is single-valued and stays in P_N; it has a genuine exponential rate but no deck character. Let U=u^N,V=v^N,A=U-V. Formula (4) becomes chi_u=A(U-1)/V, chi_v=1/A. (10) These are the independently derived exact beta deck multipliers. They are also the exponential derivatives of the classical marked phase after substituting the central variables. At chi_u=chi_v=1, the finite nonzero torus condition is simply A=1. The factor u^N is INVISIBLE in (10); its correct value was established by the separate original-source rigidity proof. Thus even this exact character calculation alone would not normalize the period. The untouched full-Psi atoms in the original scalar crossing obey (2) individually. The reflected factorial monomials have integral exponents N-1 and no additional deck character. The original continuous Gaussian of sign s is exp[-s eta_s^2/(2h)] with eta_s=sqrt(2*pi*i*s)xi; its character is (-1)^N exp(-sN eta_s). Equation (5) displays the positive case. In these respective coordinates the dilation atom rows remain integral. The new beta residue has precisely (9), including its rational prefactors after exact Q-tag shifts. Therefore all these actual components are covered by the SAME character rule before their original external integration. No alternative knot state is introduced. ## 4. Integral head gluing carries the characters exactly Suppose local component i has logarithmic arguments Z_i=L_i T+c_i, where L_i is an integer matrix describing its actual head and boundary monomials. Include all untouched atom, Gaussian and source factors. If T_k makes one full turn, factor i makes the integer winding L_i e_k. Therefore the geometric product has chi_total,k=chi_external,k product_i product_a chi_(i,a)^(L_i[a,k]). (11) This follows from exact meromorphic identities, so it does not require pairwise independence of monomial arguments, a nonsingular B block, or a saddle determinant. Equivalently substitute Z_i in (3): C_total=sum_i L_i^t C_i L_i and the atom incidence rows pull back by L_i. The linear terms include C_i c_i as well as the original b_i. Formula (4) for this substituted function is identical to (11), including the parity constants in (6). For the literal eligible crossing star u=z_4/z_1, v=x^(-1) z_4/z_0, its three head characters are z_4 turn: chi_u chi_v=(U-1)/V, z_1 turn: chi_u^(-1)=V/[A(U-1)], z_0 turn: chi_v^(-1)=A. (12) Their product is one, as required by invariance under simultaneous scaling of its three heads. They are generally not individually one. The central color x^N remains inside V; it is not specialized to a clock value merely because the finite head has dimension N. For a finite collection of pairwise disjoint eligible sink stars, the sink source has the tensor product presentation of the beta rank-two extensions, with its original exterior pairing. Formula (11) computes the character of the full selected component. The finite sink pointing product_i B_i, which also contains the current sectors, is invariant in its boundary monomials. Untouched full functions still have their own characters and matched relative cycles. Invariance of the sink pointing does NOT imply that its all-residue sector, or that sector times untouched fields, has character one. ## 5. What the central equations establish and what they do not On any stated actual phase graph, (8) and (11) provide the exact central norm equations whose classical gluing description has already been checked. An A-polynomial elimination must keep the same regular graph, peripheral marks and saturation divisors. Arbitrary denominator-cleared components are not restored by calling these equations Frobenius gluing. The theorem does not identify an eliminated curve with the selected minimal quantum A-operator or prove that its geometric branch contributes to the original scalar. The current extension and original relative integration class remain indispensable. In particular, the exact current can gain a nondegenerate geometric residue under a deck turn. Killing every current is not a source-preserving quotient even when a product character is one. The constructive output is explicit: the entire residue product's deck character and its character-one variety are known from the actual monomial incidence and Gaussian data. The missing global step concerns the selected marked relative class on that variety, not an unspecified central multiplier for each local beta section. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_full_psi_frobenius_deck_gluing.py) checks direct complete-function turns with both orientations, mixed integer Gaussian matrices, arbitrary integer windings, half-step and odd-Gaussian signs, the actual beta characters, and the literal three-head pullback. Finite checks supplement the exact identities (2)--(6), not a source-selection assertion. Cap factors are used as their complete finite polynomials or with their matched relative interval seams. No scalar character is assigned to an isolated fractional interval-density summand.

title: An absolute scalar full-Psi cycle for the original whole source
text: # An absolute scalar full-Psi cycle for the original whole source 28 October 2026. The actual physical word, its continuous Gaussian factors and ALL original cups/caps admit one explicit scalar relative period using the full literature dilogarithm. No finite matrix resolvent or finite Euler polynomial is present. The missing analytic step in combining coefficient moments with the untruncated scalar Hardy network is supplied by a continuous-flow duality lemma: its fibered head radii make every retained radial source absolutely integrable, jointly with the Gaussian and the coupled caps. This does not justify bare substitution of Psi for the cyclic function on fixed Laurent tori. The radial chains below are compulsory. The regular all-moment-pole action has the actual meridian/cap equations; the whole relative cycle's geometric intersection and dominance remain unproved. An artificial exponential gap for every individual ray term is specifically not asserted. The [rational audit](../experiments/audit_actual_full_psi_scalar_flow_cycle.py) and [certificates](../experiments/actual_full_psi_scalar_flow_cycle_results.json) check 189 individual all-N atom capacities before and 189 after the Hardy-forest contraction, and 25 whole-network primal/dual radius solutions, with rational checks of every constraint and exact objective equality after recovery. These audit the general flow proof below; they are not a knot-family proof by examples. ## 1. The actual scalar kernels to which the theorem applies Subsequent exact simplification: [the cut-wall pushforward](actual_full_psi_cut_wall_pushforward.md) removes the remaining moment resolvents in favor of a bare full-Psi head period PLUS its explicit aggregate scalar cut-wall current. Every original radial source is retained by that identity; the current's global growth and geometric selection remain open. Use the strict ORIGINAL physical crossing order in [the literal Euler network](actual_euler_gaussian_cauchy_network.md), the [continuous Gaussian](actual_continuous_gaussian_cyclic_network.md), and the ORIGINAL physical boundary sources in [the coupled-cap theorem](actual_coupled_caps_interval_source.md). Insert scalar Hardy identities before/after elementary gates, in the same harmless initial chamber as before. All head variables are z_v. Each scalar atomic kernel is a positive/negative Euler coefficient generating kernel with a monomial argument. All can be expressed using v_(epsilon,N), with epsilon=+1 or -1: v_N(A)=v_(+,N)(A), u_N(A)=v_(-,N)(Q^(-1)A), F^(-1) diagonal: v_(-,N)(Q^(-1)z/w), F diagonal: N(z/w)^d v_(+,N)(Qw/z), d=N-1. (1) Thus a moment atom has argument A_j=kappa_j z^(v_j), where v_j has one +1 and one -1. The reflected factorial also has its original prefactor N(z/w)^d. The Q shifts are exact. Gaussian dilation kernels are ordinary Hardy kernels with coefficient g_s(x,y,xi)=-(xy)^(-s)exp(-s h/2) exp(sqrt(pi)(1+i s)xi), h=2*pi*i/N, s=+1 or -1. (2) They carry the exact Gaussian weight sqrt(N/(2*pi))exp(-Nxi^2/2). Every other spectator/reset is 1/(1-z_out/z_in). The physical cup/ordinary cap/ORIGINAL marked cap are exactly (4) of the coupled-cap note, including their distinct powers of N and color. The full marked row is restricted to D=d only by whole integer degree, as proved there; no Ward identity is reapplied to a summand. ## 2. Full-function moment chains, with no finite resolvent Let Psi_epsilon be precisely the full rational Faddeev function fixed in [the full-function source theorem](actual_modular_dilog_circle_and_boundary_source.md). For R>0 define the scalar functional M_(epsilon,R)[f]= (1/(2*pi)) integral_(-pi)^pi Psi_epsilon(log R+i epsilon theta) f(R exp(i epsilon theta)) dtheta -epsilon/(2*pi*i) integral_0^R Psi_epsilon(log r+i epsilon pi)(-r)^N f(-r) dr/r. (3) The indicated logarithmic lift on the negative ray is retained. For every 0<=a<N, the independently proved shifted-keyhole identity is M_(epsilon,R)[t^(-a)]=v_(epsilon,a). (4) On its negative ray, exactly |Psi_epsilon(log r+i epsilon pi)|=sqrt(1+r). (5) In the scalar network replace every v_(epsilon,N)(A_j) by the moment kernel M_(epsilon,R)[1/(1-A_j/t_j)]. (6) Expression (6) is NOT defined as a standalone function with a fixed head-variable circle on its radial piece. Its meaning is the jointly fibered scalar cycle specified in Sections 4--5. The untruncated geometric kernel has no numerator 1-(A_j/t_j)^N and no matrix source. ## 3. Coefficient-independent continuous support Expand every ordinary Hardy kernel in nonnegative powers. A reflected factorial contributes diagonal index a=d-r, r>=0; a following Hardy identity forces a>=0. Hence it retains the upper barrier a<=d, entirely independently of the numerical coefficient assigned to r. The complete strict crossing has the following ordered barriers. * In C^(-1), its transfer lowers head one. Its following reciprocal first-head diagonal therefore sees an index at most d. The reflected second-head diagonal kills a second-head overflow before the central transfer. * The central transfer only lowers head two and may overflow head one. The reflected first-head diagonal of the final C kills this overflow BEFORE its lowering transfer can return it. * The final transfer lowers head one; the final reflected second-head diagonal kills its second-head overflow. The incoming second-head reciprocal diagonal of each inverse fusion sees the finite incoming head. All Gaussian indices are likewise in [0,d]. Every nonzero original whole-source route therefore has 0<=r_j<=d at EVERY moment atom. (7) This argument uses inequalities and degree conservation only. It holds for REAL nonnegative flows, not only integer paths, and for arbitrary coefficient values at the atoms. All intermediate nonnegative head indices are bounded by the fixed total degree k d of a k-pair plat. The scalar flow polytope is consequently bounded. Its source cup and cap variables range over [0,d]. It is nonempty: take every transfer order zero and match the cup and cap head labels, with the diagonal indices then fixed. Numerical coefficients of different routes may cancel, but this feasible nonnegative continuous route exists independently of those values. ## 4. Exact toric-flow duality supplies the joint radii Write a geometric kernel as 1/(1-exp(ell_e) z^(v_e)). Its v_e is the incidence vector of an oriented edge: one +1, one -1. Atomic edges have ell_e=log|kappa_e|-log|t_j|; Gaussian edges include log|g_s|; other Hardy edges have ell_e=0. Let gamma=d gamma_0 be the total head-monomial exponent from reflected factorials and the cup/cap prefactors. A cup/cap K_N is a bounded edge c with index a_c in [0,d] and log coefficient ell_c. All original scalar factors outside head monomials are kept separately. For fixed t,xi choose head log radii lambda_v. Impose the strict geometric-kernel constraints, for a fixed eta>0, ell_e+v_e.lambda <= -eta. (8) There is a common feasible chamber for every positive set of |t_j|: the previous gate-order reset construction works with its atomic threshold rho replaced by rho |t_j|. No terminal Hardy edge closes the time paths. Finite cap polynomials impose no radius constraint. On this chamber the head source/monomial growth is bounded by J(lambda)=gamma.lambda +d sum_c max(0,ell_c+v_c.lambda). (9) The dual of minimizing (9) subject to (8) is EXACTLY maximize sum_e f_e(ell_e+eta)+sum_c a_c ell_c, gamma+sum_e f_e v_e+sum_c a_c v_c=0, f_e>=0, 0<=a_c<=d. (10) For clarity, the second term of (9) is the support function of [0,d]. Insert a_c in that interval, add the multipliers f_e of (8), and minimize in lambda; its coefficient must vanish, giving (10). Strong equality is finite polyhedral duality: introduce u_c>=0 and u_c>=ell_c+v_c.lambda to make (9) linear. A separating hyperplane between its attainable objective epigraph and a smaller objective value gives exactly the nonnegative multipliers in (10). Feasibility of (8) and boundedness of the continuous route polytope give a finite attained optimum on both sides. Thus no integer-only inference or asymptotic convexity is being used. Every f_e in (10) is precisely a nonnegative head or atom flow of Section 3. At R=1, put tau_j=-log|t_j|>=0 on radial pieces; tau_j=0 on circle pieces. The moment contribution is sum_j r_j tau_j. By (7), and since every other flow is at most k d, min J <= d sum_j tau_j+C_word N(1+sum|xi|). (11) Color moduli on a fixed nonzero meridian chart are included in C_word. Equation (11) is the required simultaneous bound, rather than a possibly divergent independent choice of a radius at each atom. The incidence/capacity matrix and the normalized charges gamma_0 are fixed by the word. An optimal basic solution, after fixing harmless componentwise radius gauges, has |lambda| <= C_word(1+sum tau_j+sum|xi|). (12) One can use piecewise affine solutions on their finitely many polyhedral parameter cells. To obtain a genuine fibered chain, glue different solutions by log-linear head-radius prisms on cell walls; (8) is convex, so no pole is crossed. These prisms have zero period: the scalar form contains ALL base moment/Gaussian differentials, whose pullback has deficient rank on a base cell wall. Equivalently use a continuous smoothed choice with a smaller fixed margin; (11) changes by only C_word N. No source term is lost by the radius selection. ## 5. Absolute convergence, including every original coupled cap Under (8) every geometric kernel has modulus at most (1-exp(-eta))^(-1). The bound |K_N(r)|<=N exp(d max(0,log|r|)) is exactly the source support function already present in (9). All scalar N powers are the original reflected-factorial and cap normalizations. Thus the head integrand is bounded by C N^B exp(C_word N(1+sum|xi|)) prod_radial r_j^(-d). (13) The full-Psi radial measure in (3), using (5), has modulus sqrt(1+r) r^(N-1)dr/(2*pi). Since d=N-1, its product with r^(-d) is uniformly integrable at r=0. The circles are compact and their selected full functions have no poles. The Gaussian weight dominates exp(C_word N sum|xi|), so all variables are jointly absolutely integrable at every N. This proves the required Fubini; it is stronger than declaring a finite matrix-coefficient sum first. The exact interval sources of the coupled-cap theorem may be included as well. Choose principal Log r on its cut plane. Uniformly there, with its removable value at 1, |Log r/(r-1)| <=C(1+|log|r||) exp(-max(0,log|r|)). (14) Near 1 this follows from removability; for |r|>=2 or <=1/2 it is immediate, and the remaining compact annulus is bounded. On ANY fixed compact cap path with 0<=Re s<=1, |exp(Ns Log r)|<=exp(N max(0,log|r|)+C_path N). The one power lost in (14) changes N back to d=N-1. Hence the interval source obeys (13), up to a fixed product of logarithmic factors bounded by powers of 1+sum tau+sum|xi| using (12). Radial integrals of those logarithms still converge. Thus the real intervals and the compact complex cap paths inside the vertical strip have the SAME absolute convergence theorem. The generic simultaneous classical framing in the cap note puts all desired s_g in that strip. Source logarithmic cuts are matched exactly, rather than discarded. If L changes to L+2*pi*i, the difference of the two interval densities N L exp(NsL)/(exp L-1) is d_s { [exp(Ns(L+2*pi*i))-exp(NsL)]/(exp L-1) }. The primitive vanishes at both s=0 and s=1. Thus the seam is an exact relative interval derivative with fixed ends; it produces no extra period. This is the explicit scalar cut gluing needed when using the principal source chart in (14). ## 6. Exact equality with the original selected scalar If the interval presentation is used, first evaluate those intervals to recover their exact cap polynomials; the joint absolute bound permits this order. Then integrate the head circles in the convergent chamber. Expansion of their rational geometric kernels is absolutely convergent. By Section 3, only indices 0<=r_j<N survive the original source, so this head integral is a FINITE Laurent polynomial in the moment t_j^(-1). Apply (4) separately at every atom. Equations (1) recover the original finite Euler/factorial coefficients exactly, with all Q shifts and N factors. The joint Gaussian moments give the exact original Gaussian diagonal. All original Cartan, pivot, framing, modified-trace and peripheral lines remain attached once. Consequently, for every fixed signed physical word and its original selected plat source, P_(beta,N)=chi_(beta,N)(N/(2*pi))^(m/2) integral_R^m exp(-N||xi||^2/2) (tensor_j M_(epsilon_j,1)) [ integral_head_tori R_(beta,N)(z,t,xi) prod_v dz_v/(2*pi*i z_v) ] dxi. (15) Here R is the explicitly specified product of ordinary scalar Hardy kernels, original reflected monomials and the coupled sources, or their exact interval forms. Its number of variables is determined by the word and bridge count, independently of N. Equation (15) is a single tensor-product scalar RELATIVE cycle. Writing it as circle/ray pieces is optional bookkeeping, not a selection of a new invariant. In particular no exponentially large unspecified matrix source is hidden in (15). All possible exponential factors are explicit: full Psi functions, Gaussian weights, original monomial/interval phases, and the retained radial powers (-r)^N. Their cancellations are still part of the original problem. ## 7. What the pole pushforward does and does not prove The new atomic rational poles are t_j=A_j(z). Each is primitive and has scalar normal form dt_j/(t_j-A_j). With its induced orientation its residue is +1; their normals are independent because every t_j occurs in its own pole equation. The ordinary head Hardy poles have the already proved forest normal degree +1. At a regular local chart where these residue operations are allowed, the ALL-CIRCLE atomic residue branch has density the product of the full functions Psi_epsilon(Log A_j), with exactly the original reflected monomials, Gaussian and coupled caps. The complete relative source also has its retained ray-weighted pole and cut currents. Its full residue is not being identified with this single bare-function product. Using the uniform full-Psi symbol on its selected strip, its leading action is therefore the SAME signed sum of Li_2 and monomial/Gaussian terms computed in the Hardy-forest note. The exact Gaussian canonical graph and the actual fusion graphs give the actual framed Hurwitz holonomy. The cap equations are precisely the inverse-meridian locus proved in the coupled-cap note. This is a statement about the regular all-pole critical scheme, not existence of a global geometric cycle. The full functions are regular across the apparent interior cyclotomic roots on their selected strip; a positive geometric argument may have ANY modulus. Local residue/chart deformations may use that regularity while retaining every negative-ray and source-cut face in (3). Enlarging an outer radius is an exact moment-chain deformation, but its extra ray segment must be kept; for R>1 it need not be small. The known ordered support theorem can push the HEAD Hardy forest on every radially truncated cycle r_j>=delta>0, with all source-null negative currents retained first. Section 8 below proves the stronger fact that the reduced whole-source flow polytope is unchanged. Thus the reduced full-source cycle itself has the same absolute radial bound, without needing a new divergent-piece prescription. This does not permit deleting atomic ray/cut currents or independently assigning a period to a divergent separated negative-current component. Bare substitution remains false. For example the ordinary full-turn moment at a<N differs from the original v_a by its nonzero radial source E_a(R). Its small-radius leading term is E_a(R)=epsilon R^(N-a)/(2*pi*i*(N-a))+O_N(R^(N-a+1)|log R|). The logarithmic term t^N Log t has nonzero low Cauchy moments. It is not an integer high-degree tail annihilated by a head barrier. The explicit relative cycle (3), plus the flow-controlled radii, is the proved correction to that substitution. A further global pole pushforward must transport this whole relative class. Normal degree one of the all-pole graph does not determine its geometric-thimble coefficient and does not prove noncancellation of the original period. ## 8. The full-Psi cycle remains absolute after Hardy-forest contraction Contract all head-Hardy edges at their pole equations, including the Gaussian edges with their full g factors. Their graph is the forest already proved in the Hardy-reduction note. In a component, write z_v=c_v z_root, where c_v is its nonzero product of Gaussian dilation factors. Every remaining moment argument is still a primitive ratio of two DIFFERENT retained head segments. A transfer connects different heads; an active factorial connects the two segments it separates. Thus no atomic argument becomes a constant self-loop. There is an exact equality of CONTINUOUS route polytopes: reduced atom/cap flows <--> original atom/cap/head-Hardy flows. (16) Here the reduced constraints only require atom orders nonnegative and cup/cap orders in [0,d]; omitted head currents are not assumed nonnegative. To prove (16), first reconstruct the omitted currents as SIGNED real numbers. On each forest component, the contracted balance equation is exactly the compatibility condition for a unique solution of its tree incidence equations; solve from the leaves. These numbers are precisely the signed head indices in the ordered physical word. Suppose a reconstructed index first becomes negative. A diagonal preserves the index, and Gaussian dilation does too, so a lowering transfer must create it. There are only the following possibilities. * In C^(-1) it is the first head, whose following reciprocal first-head factorial forces the index to be nonnegative. * In the central transfer it is the second head, which the incoming reciprocal second-head factorial of C forces nonnegative before another transfer touches it. * In the final transfer of C it is the first head. At the next touching crossing it is either the second head, killed immediately by the incoming reciprocal factorial, or the first head, lowered before that crossing's reciprocal first-head factorial. An untouched negative head is incompatible with the final finite cap. These are inequality statements for real indices. They do not use integrality, coefficient cancellation, or a finite matrix norm. The initial cup and final cap indices are in [0,d]. Hence no reconstructed negative current is possible. All omitted head currents are nonnegative and (16) follows. The upper barriers of Section 3 then give atom order at most d and all head currents at most k d. The g factors introduce only explicit costs. If delta_v=log|c_v|, the reduced atomic coefficient log is ell_e+v_e.delta, the source monomial has its additional fixed term gamma.delta, and a cap edge has the same substitution. After reconstructing a flow, these costs sum to the original Gaussian/color costs by the tree balance equations. Their bound is still C_word N(1+sum|xi|). Apply exactly the duality of Section 4 to this reduced incidence matrix, now with ONLY atomic geometric kernels. Equations (11)--(14) hold unchanged. The graph has b+6m complex head coordinates, its original m continuous Gaussian variables and its original coupled sources. It has NO head-Hardy/reset kernels. The pure full-Psi moment cycle on this reduced graph is jointly absolutely convergent. For exact equality, perform the original forest annulus argument at every common radial cutoff delta>0. All nonempty negative-current components have zero original head/source pairing, by the same coefficient-independent signed-index proof. The initial and reduced whole-source cycles both satisfy the absolute bound above, so take delta to zero in those cycles. No separate convergence of an individually source-null annulus component is required or asserted. The audit contracts the literal time-layered head forest, drops ALL of its nonnegativity constraints, maximizes each reduced atom order, and reconstructs the unique omitted tree currents exactly. It finds 189 rational all-N certificates with every omitted current nonnegative, plus ten reduced strict-radius certificates. The proof (16), rather than those examples, establishes this for all words.

title: Exact fusion relates the right Euler operator to physical clocks
text: # Exact fusion relates the right Euler operator to physical clocks Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual two-leg fusion kernel gives an exact polynomial operator relation between the RIGHT lowering coefficient and physical/relative clocks. All nilpotent endpoints are retained. This provides a concrete coordinate relation for the Euler cap rather than guessing that its argument is a physical Fourier momentum. It does not yet supply a geometric period map or a selected geometric sector. ## 1. The actual finite kernel Use the [actual Borel fusion](actual_borel_regular_fusion_and_divided_cap_period.md) on two nilpotent heads. Their highest K eigenvalues x,y are invertible. Set F_j=(Q;Q)_j, with Q of exact order N. Relative basis vectors are f^a e_j, where f is the TOTAL physical lowering operator acting on the LEFT. Their images under the actual fusion C are f^a(e_0 tensor e_j). In the physical basis (u,v), the kernel is exactly \[ C_{u,v;a,j}= \begin{cases} x^{u-a}\displaystyle\frac{F_aF_v}{F_{a-u}F_j}, &0\leq u\leq a,\quad v=j+a-u<N,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \tag{1} \] To prove (1), write f=A_0+B_0 with A_0=F_1 and B_0=K_1 inverse F_2. Then B_0 A_0=Q A_0 B_0. In the q-binomial expansion of f^a, the term with u first-leg lowering steps has coefficient F_a/[F_u F_(a-u)]. Acting on the source gives F_u from the first leg, x^(u-a) from the K_1 inverses, and F_v/F_j from the second leg. Terms exceeding the second nilpotent head vanish. This gives (1) with no asymptotic step. In the ordering by a on the relative side and u on the physical side, C is upper block triangular. Its diagonal blocks are F_a times the identity. They are units, so C is invertible. The kernel depends on x, but not on y. Let D_a and D_j be the relative diagonal clocks Q^a and Q^j. Let U,V be the physical diagonal clocks Q^u and Q^v. Equation (1) immediately gives \[ C D_aD_j=UV C. \tag{2} \] ## 2. Right lowering and its exact clock equation Right multiplication R_f in the coefficient algebra is \[ R_f(f^a e_j)= \begin{cases}f^{a+1}e_{j-1\bmod N},&a<N-1,\\0,&a=N-1. \end{cases} \tag{3} \] This is different from physical total lowering, which is LEFT multiplication in the fused module. Define the transported operators \[ A=C D_a C^{-1},\qquad J=C D_j C^{-1},\qquad f_R=C R_f C^{-1}. \] Then the following are exact finite matrix identities: \[ \boxed{\quad x(1-U^{-1}A)f_R=(1-QA)(1-J),\qquad AJ=UV. \quad} \tag{4} \] They are not assertions merely about interior matrix entries. Before conjugating, the first identity reads \[ x C R_f-xQ U^{-1}C R_fD_a=C(1-QD_a)(1-D_j). \tag{5} \] For j>0 and a<N-1, use (1) at consecutive relative labels: \[ \frac{C_{u,v;a+1,j-1}}{C_{u,v;a,j}} =x^{-1}\frac{(1-Q^{a+1})(1-Q^j)}{1-Q^{a+1-u}}. \tag{6} \] The polynomial equation obtained by clearing the denominator in (6) is valid even when that denominator is zero. At the new support u=a+1, the left coefficient vanishes and the old kernel entry is zero. At any other excluded row both sides vanish. For j=0, R_f sends the second label to N-1. Its new kernel support is ONLY u=a+1,v=N-1. The left coefficient 1-Q^(a+1-u) is then zero, and the right side is zero because 1-Q^j=0. This is an actual wrapped endpoint, not a discarded row. For a=N-1 the left side is zero by (3), while the right side has factor 1-Q^N=0. These observations establish (5) on every matrix entry. Finally R_f D_a=Q^(-1)D_a R_f, so conjugating (5) gives the ordered equation in (4). Also, exactly, \[ [A,J]=0,\qquad A f_R=Q f_R A,\qquad J f_R=Q^{-1}f_R J. \tag{7} \] These follow directly from the relative basis, including its cyclic j endpoint, at the root Q^N=1. ## 3. The apparent denominator is nilpotent at the actual root It would be incorrect to divide the first equation in (4) by 1-U inverse A as an actual finite operator. In fact \[ (1-U^{-1}A)^N=0. \tag{8} \] Indeed C is upper block triangular with scalar diagonal blocks F_a. Conjugating D_a by C yields an upper block triangular A with diagonal blocks Q^u. Therefore U inverse A is upper block triangular with every diagonal block equal to one. Its difference from one is strictly upper block triangular, which proves (8). Thus (4) is an exact polynomial transport identity through this endpoint, not a rational inverse formula for f_R. It retains a singular clock divisor that a prospective period transform must handle. No scalar normalization removes (8). ## 4. A useful prospective principal relation, with its scope The [actual cap](actual_euler_cap_cauchy_boundary.md) uses the Euler argument x f in the RIGHT coefficient algebra. On a commutative principal-symbol chart associated with (4), that argument would satisfy \[ z(1-A/U)=(1-A)(1-J),\qquad AJ=UV. \tag{9} \] Where 1-A/U is invertible this can be written \[ z=\frac{(1-A)(1-J)}{1-A/U}. \tag{10} \] Equations (9)-(10) specify the algebraic symbol relation forced by the exact kernel. They do not prove that a particular semiclassical symbol chart exists for the full selected word, that it is symplectic, that z equals a geometric Fourier momentum, or that its divisor is traversed by the original source class. In particular (10) is NOT the finite root matrix equation, because of (8). This still makes a concrete step beyond the former unspecified right-Euler/physical-clock relation: the actual finite kernel and all its endpoint terms are now explicit. A geometric comparison must use this relation and the original cap, rather than silently replacing the cap argument by another momentum. ## 5. Truncated generic-Q kernel exposes a top-degree defect For a Q not satisfying Q^N=1, retain the SAME finite formula (1), provided F_1,...,F_(N-1) are units, and the SAME nilpotent shift (3). These are well-defined matrices, without claiming they form the actual generic-q word module. Let Pi_top project to a=N-1. The exact finite-kernel identity is now \[ \begin{aligned} x C R_f-xQ U^{-1}C R_fD_a &=C(1-QD_a)(1-D_j)\\ &\quad -(1-Q^N)C(1-D_j)\Pi_{\rm top}. \tag{11} \end{aligned} \] The same entry proof applies away from a=N-1, including j=0. At a=N-1 the left side vanishes by truncation. The correction in (11) subtracts exactly the nonzero right side there. Consequently the root identity has a visible normal endpoint term before root specialization. Dividing (11) by 1-Q^N and discarding its last term would change the kernel calculation. This is only a statement about this explicit finite kernel; it does not provide a moving-q extension of actual braid intertwining, fusion of divided powers, or the original whole q-normal source. Those further comparisons remain necessary. ## 6. Exact checks The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_fusion_right_euler_clock.py) and [saved output](../experiments/actual_fusion_right_euler_clock_results.json) pass at N=2,...,9 with unequal x=3,y=7. At each actual root they compare (1) to the literal coproduct fusion matrix and check (2), (4), (7), (8). Eight additional generic-Q kernel cases check the full nonzero endpoint correction (11). The all-level entry proofs above establish the theorem; these exact checks verify its conventions and endpoints.

title: A selected actual gauge period evaluates fixed observables at the algebraic point 2
text: # A selected actual gauge period evaluates fixed observables at the algebraic point 2 27 October 2026. An actual source period now gives a direct local instance of the proposed quantum-period-to-algebraic-point mechanism. For the canonical primitive gauge g_N, its top-coefficient period, normalized by its EXPLICIT Gauss period, converges on every fixed polynomial observable to evaluation at z=2. Its universal moment recursion and finite cyclic source are exact. This is a proved selection statement for this local gauge period, rather than only the construction of a formal critical branch. The observable degree must be independent of N. The transformed full knot word does not satisfy that restriction automatically. This does not identify the knot's quantum A-module or prove a new knot-volume limit. It supplies one fully sourced local comparison which a whole-word construction may try to extend. ## 1. The actual period and its known normalization Let Q=exp(2pi*i/N), N>=2, and let g_N(z)=sum_(r=0)^(N-1)c_r z^r be the CANONICAL nilpotent polynomial of the primitive source gauge v_N(z)v_N(Qz), as in [the actual gauge theorem](actual_hilbert90_gauge_dilogarithm_action.md). For a polynomial P define the actual linear period I_N(P)=[z^(N-1)] P(z)g_N(z), c_N=I_N(1)=c_(N-1). (1) The [exact resonant calculation](actual_primitive_gauge_resonant_endpoint.md) proves, including all endpoint terms, c_N=(1/N)sum_(r=0)^(N-1)(-1)^rQ^(r(r-1)/2) =omega_N/sqrt(N)+O(1/N), omega_N=exp[-pi*i*(N+1)/4-pi*i/(4N)]. (2) Thus c_N is nonzero for all sufficiently large N and its modulus is polynomially bounded above and below. Normalizing by c_N uses this evaluated universal Gauss period. It does NOT divide by the unknown knot invariant or choose its exponential normalization. This is a sourced period of the same actual coefficient algebra. For example it is realized by the original two-leg Euler cap with its explicit insertion b=J_Q(z)^-1 P(z)g_N(z), apart from the already specified cap scalar and the conversion f=z/x. No new invariant is defined by (1). ## 2. An exact period Ward identity and a two-generator module The UNREDUCED polynomial identity is (1-z)(1-Qz)g_N(Qz)-g_N(z) =-(2/N)z^N+c_N z^(N+1). (3) Multiplying by any polynomial P and extracting degree N-1 kills the right side. Rescaling the coefficient variable therefore gives the exact source identity I_N[Q^-1 P(Q^-1z)(1-Q^-1z)(1-z)-P(z)]=0. (4) Put i_m=I_N(z^m), using the UNWRAPPED nonnegative degree m. Then (4) is the N-independent recursion i_(m+2)=(1+Q)i_(m+1)+(Q^(m+2)-Q)i_m, i_0=c_N, i_1=(1+Q)c_N-2Q/N. (5) The second initial value follows from the degree-N relation in (3). Degrees m>=N give i_m=0, consistently with (5); no cyclic identification of that degree has been made. Define universal integer polynomials H_m(Q),R_m(Q) by H_0=1, H_1=1+Q, R_0=0, R_1=-2Q, F_(m+2)=(1+Q)F_(m+1)+(Q^(m+2)-Q)F_m (6) for either F=H or F=R. Induction in the exact recurrence gives I_N(z^m)=H_m(Q)c_N+R_m(Q)/N (7) for EVERY m>=0. Thus every fixed polynomial period is an explicit linear combination of TWO known source periods, c_N and 1/N. The coefficients in (6) are independent of level. This is stronger than a purely formal large-N moment calculation. An independent coefficient proof can be useful. For 0<=m<N, the root factorial reflection gives c_(N-1-m)=(1/N)sum_(r=0)^(N-1-m) (-1)^r Q^(r(r-1)/2)(Q^(r+1);Q)_m. Expanding its finite product and using t_r Q^(sr)=(-1)^s Q^(-s(s-1)/2)t_(r+s) gives H_m(Q)=sum_(s=0)^m Q^s {m choose s}_Q, |I_N(z^m)-H_m(Q)c_N|<=m 2^m/N. (8) For the last estimate compare each shifted Gauss interval with the full interval: at most m terms are missing, all of modulus one. The Gaussian binomial has nonnegative integer polynomial coefficients with total binomial(m,s), so its modulus on |Q|=1 is at most that number. Equations (5)-(8) agree exactly. ## 3. The selected leading symbol is evaluation at 2 At Q=1 the universal coefficients obey H_m(1)=2^m, R_0(1)=0, R_m(1)=-2^m for m>=1. (9) For a FIXED polynomial P, with coefficients independent of N, (7)-(9) and Q_N=1+O(1/N) therefore imply I_N(P)=P(2)c_N+[P(0)-P(2)]/N+O_P(N^(-3/2)), (10) I_N(P)/I_N(1)=P(2)+O_P(N^(-1/2)). (11) The constants may depend on that fixed polynomial. In particular P(2)!=0 proves nonvanishing for all sufficiently large N. If P(2)=0 and P(0)!=0, the boundary period 1/N is instead leading. If both vanish, (10) only gives the indicated smaller-order bound; it is not a nonvanishing claim. The classical limit of the actual Ward relation (4) is ((1-z)^2-1)P(z)=z(z-2)P(z). Its two algebraic support points are 0 and 2. The ACTUAL Gauss normalization and moments select the point 2. Consequently the map in (11) is asymptotically multiplicative on every fixed polynomial window: both P and PR are evaluated at 2. No regular map from the nilpotent finite algebra to that point is asserted. This is a genuinely nonlocal period selection: the coefficient degree increases with N. Directly specializing the finite nilpotent generator to the scalar 2 would be invalid. The period calculation supplies the comparison instead. The exact rational endpoint observable (1-z)^-1, interpreted by its Taylor expansion at zero before coefficient extraction, also fits this picture in this particular case: I_N((1-z)^-1)=g_N(1)=2/N-c_N. Its leading value is -1=1/(1-2). This assertion follows from the separately proved exact endpoint identity, not from extending (11) to every rational function without a new estimate. ## 4. The leading period also intertwines ordered gauge meridian steps Let q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2. For any FIXED integer r use the actual primitive gauge increment D_r(z)=g_N(q^r z)/g_N(z) in z^N=0. (12) All quotients are units in that algebra, with canonical normal forms. Positive r gives the ordered product of the actual M->qM gauge increments; negative r uses their genuine inverses. The [whole-word gauge theorem](whole_word_primitive_source_gauge.md) proves the r=1 increment before any endpoint evaluation. Exactly, I_N(P D_r)=q^(r(N-1)) I_N(P(q^-r z)). (13) Indeed D_r g_N=g_N(q^r z) modulo z^N; multiplying by a polynomial P and extracting degree N-1 gives (13) by rescaling the variable. The source phase q^(r(N-1))=(-1)^r q^-r is retained. It cannot be replaced by one before evaluation. Combining (11) with (13) gives the sourced meridian relation I_N(P D_r)/c_N -> (-1)^r P(2). (14) This extends to every fixed finite Ore observable Ahat=sum_r P_r(q,z) T^r, Tz=qzT, T(g_N)(z)=g_N(qz), where the r range and polynomial degrees in z are independent of N, and the coefficient functions are regular at q=1. Define its actual period by I_N[(Ahat g_N)/g_N]. Then I_N[(Ahat g_N)/g_N]/c_N -> sum_r (-1)^r P_r(1,2). (15) The limit is a character of the commutative symbol algebra at (z,T)=(2,-1). Products of any two such fixed observables stay in the same class, and the Ore coefficient shifts q^r z tend to z, so the leading evaluation is multiplicative as well. This is an actual local period/connection comparison, not only moment evaluation. The meridian steps here are the GAUGE PART of the knot's transport. Fusion, actual word coefficients and the full peripheral line remain separate data. The gauge wave equation itself has the fixed operator [(1-z)(1-Qz)T^2-1]g_N=0 modulo z^N, whose unreduced source is (3). Its classical symbol is (1-z)^2 T^2-1; the selected character (2,-1) lies on it. It is not the knot's quantum A-polynomial. ## 5. The moment recursion has a retained cyclic source For reference set X_m=Q^m and let E raise m. Then EX=QXE, and (5) is the actual local source recursion P_cap=E^2-(1+Q)E+Q(1-QX). (16) Its ordinary commutative symbol is (E-1)^2-X. At X=1 the two roots are 0 and 2; the selected branch in (11) is the unit root 2. This is a recursion of the universal cap-gauge moments. The index m is observable degree, NOT the knot's meridian color, and P_cap is not identified with its quantum A-polynomial. Folding i_0,...,i_(N-1) into a cyclic array changes (16). The exact cyclic residual is (P_cap i)_m=c_N delta_(m,N-2) -(2Q/N)delta_(m,N-1). (17) For m<N-2 use (5). At m=N-2 the wrapped i_N contributes c_N in place of zero. At m=N-1 the wrapped i_(N+1) and i_N give i_1-(1+Q)i_0=-2Q/N. This proves (17), also at N=2. The finite cyclic source cannot be erased by calling (12) an unpointed homogeneous spectral equation. The Gauss period and its smaller boundary term are its specified source data. ## 6. Its root norm curve is exactly its classical curve, with the source retained The moment recursion in (16) has companion matrix C(X)=[[0,1],[-Q(1-QX),1+Q]], V_(m+1)=C(Q^m X)V_m. Let H_N(X)=C(Q^(N-1)X)...C(X) be its forward cyclic monodromy. Its characteristic polynomial is EXACTLY det(v-H_N)=(v-1)^2-U, U=X^N, (18) at every level. This is the same polynomial as the classical symbol of (16), after identifying its central variables with the classical variables. No conjectural norm-curve equality is used to obtain it. Here is a direct proof. The determinant is the full product det H_N=product_(j=0)^(N-1)Q(1-Q^(j+1)X) =1-X^N. The trace is invariant under X->QX by cyclic conjugacy wherever C(X) is invertible, hence as a polynomial identity. In a closed walk contributing to the trace, each occurrence of the X-dependent lower-left edge must be paired with an upper-right edge. Thus the trace has degree at most floor(N/2)<N. A Q-invariant polynomial of that degree is constant. At X=0 the companion has eigenvalues 1,Q, so its Nth power has trace 2. This gives (18), including composite levels and all determinant zeros. The selected finite source still matters. At X=1 its nonzero initial vector is V_0=(c_N,(1+Q)c_N-2Q/N)^t. The exact unwrapped moments give V_N=(i_N,i_(N+1))=0, so H_N(1)V_0=0. (19) It is in the central v=0 kernel, while the leading fixed-degree period in (11) selects the classical point z=2. The two facts refer to different selections: finite cyclic monodromy of the sourced state and the leading local observable period. They cannot be identified merely because the two defining curves in (18) agree. The singular orbit and the source in (17) must be retained. In particular the generic invertible norm-torsor description alone does not extend through this v=0 fiber. This is an explicit, fully evaluated local example of both norm-curve compatibility AND its limitations for selected periods. It is not an assertion of either compatibility or a particular central character for the knot's own quantum A-module. ## 7. The selected action and prefactor have a marked dilogarithm calibration The exact Gauss proof identifies the period, its phase and its nonzero prefactor. There is a compatible classical critical-action calibration. For coefficient extraction I_N(1) the relevant action in the logarithmic coordinate x=Log z is S(z)=2Li_2(z)-2pi*i Log z. Continue from the unit disk to 2 through the upper half-plane. Then Log(1-2)=-pi*i, and the elementary dilogarithm reflection identity gives Li_2(2+i0)=pi^2/4+pi*i log 2, S(2)=pi^2/2, D_z S(2)=0, D_z^2 S(2)=-4. (20) Here D_z=z partial_z. The phase exp[S(2)/h], h=2pi*i/N, is exactly exp[-pi*i*N/4], the leading phase of c_N in (2). The measure also matters: [z^(N-1)] is the Cauchy measure dz/z^N, so choosing the above action leaves amplitude z dx, with value 2 at the saddle. A quadratic Fresnel calculation with that amplitude and Hessian -4 gives exp[-pi*i*N/4] exp[-pi*i/4]/sqrt(N), again the actual leading Gauss prefactor. Omitting the amplitude z would lose a factor two. This is an independently matched action/density calibration. The Gauss argument proves selection and the asymptotic directly; no unproved deformation of an analytic dilogarithm contour beyond the established small-disk chart is used as its proof. At this real shape 2 the Bloch--Wigner value is zero: its Li_2 imaginary part cancels Log|2| Arg(1-2). Thus this local source comparison has zero volume rate and does not introduce a knot's hyperbolic volume by interpreting a gauge-chart value as that volume. ## 8. Scope for the general torsor program This proves the requested kind of algebraic leading-period mechanism in a real local part of the original source: a quantum Ward module, a selected period, an algebraic critical point and a nonvanishing criterion P(2)!=0, with known polynomially sized normalization and all cyclic source terms retained. It does not prove that the FULL transformed word, whose degree and number of entries grow with N, has such a fixed presentation. It does not intertwine the knot's meridian insertion with this degree recursion. It does not identify the point 2 with a geometric knot holonomy or assign it a positive hyperbolic volume. The leading hyperbolic action and global sector cancellation remain the original open problem. Nor may (11) be naively extended to Laurent observables: the formal coefficient of z^-1 g_N at degree N-1 is zero, rather than (1/2)c_N. Rational localization needs a sourced period construction; it is not inversion of a nilpotent finite matrix. Even rational expressions regular at 2 need their actual source lattice. For example (3) gives EXACTLY I_N(J_Q)=Q^-1 c_N, I_N((1-z)^-2)=c_N+(1-Q)g_N(Q). The second identity follows by differentiating (3) at z=1 and using I_N((1-z)^-2)=N g_N(1)-g_N'(1). These rational functions have the same classical expression (1-z)^-2 but different quantum pole arrangements. The displayed additional endpoint term is not controlled by the fixed-polynomial theorem. Its vanishing or size cannot be assumed from pointwise convergence of the two rational expressions away from their poles. [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_gauge_critical_evaluation.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_gauge_critical_evaluation_results.json) check the exact moment, two-period and cyclic-source equations at finite-field roots. High-precision fixed-degree samples diagnose the proved algebraic evaluation limit. A separate agent independently verified the reflection/q-binomial moment proof and its error estimate before this note was written.

title: The actual Gauss-wall co-source and its relative cut-current map
text: # The actual Gauss-wall co-source and its relative cut-current map Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual coherent kernel determines both anchored Gauss-wall co-sources explicitly. Their difference is the original selected trace class, not zero. The two corresponding finite cut-current maps have a shared binomial wall row and two literal endpoint corrections. They glue exactly on every actual zero-extended Green array. This constructs an actual finite relative current map for the cut direction. It also identifies a definite nonzero boundary class which two Weyl charts cannot erase. It does not identify the internal Gaussian images of the remaining currents with these finite co-sources, or select a geometric global contribution. ## 1. The literal coherent kernel has two anchored wall primitives Let N>=2, n=N-1, and use the actual compact source with T=v a, Omega_0=dv wedge da=-dT wedge dlog v, f_C(v,T)=sum_(i,j=0)^n C_ij binom(n,j) v^(i-j)T^j(1-T)^(n-j). (1) This is the actual matrix symbol, written on v!=0. It includes the full weighted-word and Green-current matrices before any scalar projection. The normalized compact period is Tr(C)/N. On the resolved framing threefold retain nu_cut=-(d eta/eta) wedge Omega_0/(1-eta v), D_cut={1-eta v=0}, E={eta=0}. On the Gauss wall, eta=1/v, so D_cut=C^*_v times A^1_T, Res_(D_cut)(f_C nu_cut)=-f_C(v,T)dT wedge dlog v. (2) Here f_C nu_cut is the explicit source-kernel lift of the known principal framing form. It is not silently identified with an internal Gaussian current. Define the two actual anchored primitives on D_cut by zeta_C^+=-sum_(i,j) C_ij binom(n,j)v^(i-j) [integral_0^T t^j(1-t)^(n-j)dt]dlog v, zeta_C^-=+sum_(i,j) C_ij binom(n,j)v^(i-j) [integral_T^1 t^j(1-t)^(n-j)dt]dlog v. (3) Polynomial antiderivation proves `d zeta_C^+=d zeta_C^-=(2)`. The lower primitive is marked to vanish at T=0 and the upper one at T=1. Their difference is exactly zeta_C^--zeta_C^+ =(1/N)sum_(i,j) C_ij v^(i-j)dlog v. (4) Indeed `binom(n,j) integral_0^1 t^j(1-t)^(n-j)dt=1/N`. Every off-diagonal term in (4) is exact on C^*, with primitive `C_ij v^(i-j)/[N(i-j)]`. Therefore its full boundary class is [zeta_C^--zeta_C^+] =(Tr(C)/N)[dlog v] in H^1(D_cut). (5) This is a concrete Cech obstruction to choosing a common anchored primitive. For the actual closed knot cut C=F_N(Y)I, it is exactly `F_N(Y)dlog v`. This is nonzero as a whole meridian family at every level, since the original ordinary-color anchor gives F_N(Q_N)=1. A particular complete value K_N can still vanish. Two Weyl charts alone cannot turn (5) into zero while retaining the actual selected source class. ## 2. The wall co-sources are exact positive finite matrix rows On the intersection loop of the actual radial normal homotopy, T=1/2 and v=exp(i phi), integration of (3) gives integral_C zeta_C^+=-c lambda_N^+(C), integral_C zeta_C^-=+c lambda_N^-(C), c=2pi*i. (6) The two functionals are literal diagonal matrix rows lambda_N^+(C)=sum_(j=0)^n w_(N,j) C_jj, w_(N,j)=binom(n,j)integral_0^(1/2)t^j(1-t)^(n-j)dt =[1/(N 2^N)]sum_(r=j+1)^N binom(N,r), lambda_N^-(C)=Tr(C)/N-lambda_N^+(C). (7) The finite binomial identity in (7) follows by differentiating the indicated binomial tail in its upper limit; its value at zero fixes the integration constant. Thus no unknown knot period is used to define these co-sources. All weights are positive and lambda_N^+(I)=lambda_N^-(I)=1/2, w_(N,n-j)=1/N-w_(N,j). (8) Let W_M be the actual root Weyl operator, with its retained diagonal coefficients and index reversal. Conjugation reverses the diagonal entries, so exactly lambda_N^+(W_M C W_M^(-1))=lambda_N^-(C). (9) This functional identity holds generically and extends on the paired fractional source lattices at a resonance. It does not assert that W_M acts on every coherent coordinate by a classical Mobius transformation. Off-diagonal angular weights in (6) have been integrated explicitly. Every full-head Gamma/frame comparison in the current source theorems is diagonal. Its conjugation commutes with both weight matrices in (7), so both co-sources are invariant under it on all matrices. The bounded Gamma source comparison transports the wall charge; it cannot discard it. For the actual closed knot they return F_N(Y)/2 each, including the original full external phase and modified dimension if it is restored. ## 3. A literal cut difference has a shared degree-elevated wall row Let J_j be any finite zero-extended actual cut-current array, and take the literal shift `(S J)_j=J_(j+1)`. Define the degree-elevated wall co-source B_N(J)=[1/(N2^N)]sum_(j=0)^N binom(N,j)J_j. (10) The j=N value is retained. It lies outside the original head and can occur in the shifted currents even though the original state is supported in 0,...,n. Extend the head rows (7) by zero outside that interval. Direct summation by parts gives lambda_(N,head)^+((S-1)J)= B_N(J)-J_0/N, lambda_(N,head)^-((S-1)J)=-B_N(J)+J_N/N. (11) For example the backward difference of the positive head weights is the binomial row, except for the additional -1/N at j=0. This proves (11) including all shifted endpoints. Equivalently use the explicit finite relative extensions lambda_(N,rel)^+(J) =lambda_(N,head)^+(J)+(1/N)sum_(j<0)J_j, lambda_(N,rel)^-(J) =lambda_(N,head)^-(J)+(1/N)sum_(j>=N)J_j. (12) The sums are finite on the actual Green arrays. They agree with (7) on every original head-supported state and satisfy lambda_(N,rel)^+((S-1)J)=+B_N(J), lambda_(N,rel)^-((S-1)J)=-B_N(J), lambda_(N,rel)^++lambda_(N,rel)^- =(1/N)sum_(all j). (13) Thus the two chart currents glue exactly through the SAME wall row. Their endpoint counterterms are specified by (11), not assigned by a generic relative-cohomology existence theorem.
