Substituting (6),(7) in p+b+m-S gives the IDENTICALLY ZERO rational function of q,t,H,V,Y. The diagonal of the second identity in (5) fixes products P_c=p_c m_(c+1) by the first-order recursion [2lambda_c-(Q+Q^-1)lambda_(c+1)]P_c +[2lambda_c-(Q+Q^-1)lambda_(c-1)]P_(c-1) =rho^2[delta alpha-gamma b_c-delta^2 lambda_c +lambda_c b_c^2]. (9) Its forward coefficient is nonzero generic, and P_(h-1)=0. Substitution of (7) in (9) is a SECOND identically zero rational function in those five independent variables. The accompanying symbolic certificate clears each denominator and verifies zero. These two identities determine the actual coefficients uniquely: at h, m_h=0 and the row-sum gives p_h; then (9) fixes P_h, so m_(h+1)=P_h/p_h, and the next row-sum fixes p_(h+1). Continue. All interior proposed p_c are nonzero generic; their only physical endpoint zeros are c=a+b or c=d. Thus induction proves (7) at every channel, including the endpoint, without an undetermined sign. If b=0 the space has one dimension and the statement is immediate. ## 4. The source is a coefficient COLUMN, with literal bend normalization Use the actual generic maps T=(I_V tensor W_(V,Qa)^V)W_b, L_c=(W_c tensor I_Qa)W_(Qc,Qa)^Qb. The right map T has Omega_23 eigenvalue H0 on ALL input colors, since its positions23 factor through the actual V_d. Its left-basis expansion is T=sum_c R_Hom(c) L_c, R_Hom(c)=J_c B_abc, J_c=(-1)^(d+c) zeta^ER F_r1 F_r2 F_(d-a)F_(d-c)F_(2c+1) /[F_a F_d F_(d+c+1)], ER=-2a^2-5c^2+2ac+2bc+ad+3dc-c+d. (10) The full source-independent map proof, using only cups and Clebsch maps, is in [the literal generic tetrahedral bend](actual_generic_tetrahedral_source_as_recoupling.md). In brief, bend the b output of (DW_a tensor DW_b tensor DW_c)(p16 p23 p45). The resulting map is simultaneously a known multiple of W_(Qc,Qa)^Qb and (DW_c tensor I)(I tensor Wtilde_a)W_b. The latter bent Wtilde_a is its actual first-entry-one mixed Clebsch map times its explicitly computed cup scalar. Composing DW_c W_c=n_c then proves (10). It is a map identity before scalar extraction, not a scalar fit. The third-color-zero coefficient of L_c is nu_c v_c, where nu_c=(-1)^r2 zeta^[r2(2c-4a+r2-1)] F_(2a)F_r/(F_r1 F_(2c)). Thus in the f_c basis the RIGHT coordinate column of T is y_c=J_c nu_c phi_c B_abc. (11) This is not the inverse coefficient obtained by applying a left eigenrow to v_c. Confusing them changes the transpose and invalidates the recurrence. Define a nonzero generic gauge by K_c=(-1)^(d+b+c) zeta^P F_a F_(N+a)F_(2b)F_(d-a+b) /[F_(J+1)F_(a-b)F_r F_b F_(d-a)F_r1F_(d-c)], P=2a^2-b^2+3c^2-2ac+2bc-d(a+b+2c+1)+b+c, g_c=B_abc/K_c, sigma_c=J_c nu_c phi_c K_c. (12) All factorial indices here are nonnegative on C. From the explicit products, its successive ratio is sigma_(c+1)/sigma_c =-Q^(c-h)(1-Q^(c+h+1))(1-Q^(2c+3)) *(1-Q^(a+b-c))(1-Q^(d-c)) /[(1-Q^(2c+1))(1-Q^(N+c+1)) *(1-Q^(J+2))(1-Q^(c-h+1))]. (13) Successive ratios are used only when both indices belong to C; outside C the corresponding term is its actual endpoint zero. There is an exact source endpoint: at c=h the source Euler formula has r=0 and directly gives B_abh=K_h. Hence g_h=1. No unknown endpoint residue or source coefficient is supplied as an assumption. ## 5. The exact finite eigenproblem is our own AW polynomial operator Put X=Q^N. For c in C define u_c=(1-Q^(h+c+1))(1-Q^(c+1)) *(1-Q^(c-a-b))(1-X^-1Q^(c+1)) /[(1-Q^(2c+1))(1-Q^(2c+2))], v_c=(1-Q^(h-c))(1-Q^(-c)) *(1-Q^(-a-b-c-1))(1-X^-1Q^(-c)) /[(1-Q^(-2c-1))(1-Q^(-2c))], Lambda_b=(Q^-b-1)(1-X^-1Q^-b). (14) At c=0 the second formula has its removable value after canceling (1-Q^(-c))/(1-Q^(-2c))=1/(1+Q^(-c)). Direct rational substitution of (7),(13) gives b_c=H0-kappa0(Lambda_b+u_c+v_c), p_c=kappa0 v_(c+1) sigma_(c+1)/sigma_c, m_c=kappa0 u_(c-1) sigma_(c-1)/sigma_c. (15) These are also checked identically over the five-variable rational field. Since y is the coefficient COLUMN, its Casimir equation is H0 y_c=p_(c-1)y_(c-1)+b_c y_c+m_(c+1)y_(c+1). Equations (11),(15) therefore give the exact source recurrence u_c(g_(c+1)-g_c)+v_c(g_(c-1)-g_c) =Lambda_b g_c. (16) Equivalently the gauged physical matrix is H0 I+kappa0(L_AW-Lambda_b I), with L_AW the difference operator on the left of (16). Its physical Casimir eigenvalue is H0, NOT lambda_b. The latter is the affine difference-operator eigenvalue only. Our independently proved [finite symmetric polynomial operator](finite_balanced_sears_operator_proof.md) applies with base Q and parameters A0=zeta Q^(a-b), B0=zeta, C0=zeta^(-1)Q^(-a-b), D0=zeta/X, z_c=zeta Q^c, degree n=b. Its forward/backward coefficients are exactly (14). Thus the finite polynomial calculation in that note proves that G_c=4phi3(Q^-b,X^-1Q^-b,Q^(a-b-c),Q^(a-b+c+1); Q^(a-b+1),Q^-2b,X^-1Q^(a-b+1);Q,Q) (17) satisfies (16). The sum has length b; no denominator reaches zero in its generic physical range, since d>=a>=b. At c=h one numerator is one, so G_h=1. Also v_h=0, u_maxC=0, and every interior u_c is nonzero generic. Consequently the scalar three-term recurrence with its ACTUAL endpoint g_h=1 determines all its values uniquely. It follows that B_abc=K_c G_c, for a>=b, c in C. (18) This is the decisive source-selection step. It is a finite exact recurrence argument; no semiclassical branch or noncancellation assumption is made. ## 6. Own Sears conversion gives the single sum First suppose a=max(a,b,c) and d>=b+c. Write z=d+a+k in (2). The factorial ratios give the balanced finite long series H=4phi3(Q^-r,Q^(N+a+1),Q^-b,Q^-c; Q^(N-b-c),Q^(a-b+1),Q^(a-c+1);Q,Q). Its prefactor is the k=0 term of (1). Apply our OWN finite Sears identity, taking termination length b, retained parameter Q^-r, d_S=Q^(a-b+1), e_S=Q^(a-c+1). Extending the sum to length b is legitimate since Q^-r already kills all k>r. It gives H=(Q^(b+1),X^-1Q^(a-b+1);Q)_b /(Q^(a-c+1),X^-1Q^(c+1);Q)_b *G_c. Here the k=0 prefactor of (1) is explicitly R0=(-1)^(d+b+c) zeta^D [a]![N+a]! /([J+1]![d-b-c]![a-b]![a-c]![r]!). Reverse the two negative-start Pochhammers in the Sears factor. That factor becomes Q^[b(h-c)] F_(2b)F_(d-h)F_(a-c)F_(d-b-c) /[F_b F_(d-a)F_r1 F_(d-c)]. All four latter factorials cancel those in R0 as displayed in (12). For the phase, converting R0 to F factorials gives exponent D-T(a)-T(N+a)+T(J+1)+T(d-b-c)+T(h)+T(a-c)+T(r), where T(n)=n(n-1)/2. Adding 2b(h-c) gives exactly P in (12). Thus their product is K_c with its full sign and phase, not merely its square. Equation (18) proves (1) in this region. To remove the temporary size restriction, fix ordinary a=max(a,b,c). The independently proved [generic source polynomial reduction](generic_trivalent_bilinear_racah_port.md), section3a, normalizes the ACTUAL B to R_SRC(X), degree at most r, after the explicit factor (XQ^-a)_(2a+1). The proposed single sum normalizes to the explicit R_TGT(X) of that same degree. Their normalizations and constants were derived by finite products there. For every real 0<zeta<1, the preceding argument proves equality at ALL X=Q^(d+1), d>=b+c. These are infinitely many distinct points. Thus the two finite polynomials agree identically. Their rational coefficients in Q then agree generically as well. Substitute X=Q^(d+1) for ANY physical d>=a. If a term would have d-b-c+k<0, its finite product (XQ^(-b-c+k);Q)_(J+1) contains 1-Q^0 and is EXACTLY zero. This restores precisely the correct lower limit z>=J. Therefore the same identity covers d<b+c and every high-partner range. No nonzero factorial is assigned to a negative index. Finally remove the ordering restriction by genuine cyclic duality. For the canonical physical cup, P_d(d-u)/P_d(u)=(-1)^d zeta^(-d+2u). Cycling the three consecutive physical PAIRS in p16 p23 p45 gives exactly the inverse K on the moved pair. Intertwining transports it to the moved ordinary object. Hence U_bca(r_b,r_c,r_a)=K_a^(-1)(r_a)U_abc(r_a,r_b,r_c). The ordinary Theta coefficient needed to extract the new canonical corner is computed by its finite two-term E recursion, first along third color zero to second color 2b, then keeping that second color maximal. It is Theta_abc(0,2b,r2) =zeta^Et F_(2b)F_r2/(F_r1F_(2c)), Et=-2(a^2-ab-a+bc-c^2). Substituting the ACTUAL source-corner prefactors (9) of the generic six-head theorem cancels every factorial and sign, leaving B_bca=zeta^[D(b,c,a)-D(a,b,c)]B_abc. (19) Every triple can be cyclically rotated so its largest label is first. The factorial prefactor and the finite sum in (1),(2) are symmetric. Thus (19) proves (1) for ALL ordered ordinary triangles. ## 7. Root normals, scope and audit There is also a useful EXACT closed-trace corollary. With the original ordinary closure T_abc from (11) of the generic six-head theorem, T_abc=(-1)^d product_(j=a,b,c)[2j+1] *[r]![r1]![r2]!/[J+1]! *product_(j=a,b,c)([j]!^2[d-j]!/[N+j]!) *S_abc^2. (20) This is a square of the generic scalar, not a Hermitian absolute square. It keeps the genuine ordinary dimensions. To verify all normalization factors directly, insert (1) for B_abc and B_cba in that source trace and replace F_n by zeta^[n(n-1)/2](1-Q)^n[n]!. The powers of 1-Q cancel. Writing T(n)=n(n-1)/2, the remaining exponent is the identically zero polynomial E+D(a,b,c)+D(c,b,a)+T(r)+T(r1)+T(r2)+T(J+1) +sum_(j=a,b,c)[T(d-j)-T(N+j)+2j]=0, where E is the actual trace exponent in the six-head theorem. This also proves (20) without importing a tetrahedral trace normalization. Equations (1),(2) now give a single factorial sum for each generic branch in the full <=8-branch marked cluster formula. This identity holds before specialization, so it retains the derivative tails that are lost by imposing Q^N=1 first. For low-fold principal-root labels, one can extract the known single [N] factor and recover the proved positive root partition. High partners and terms crossing N retain their actual zero orders; they must be combined as prescribed by the generic cluster formula before a marked normal is taken. The proof has NOT yet established a polynomial bound for every lower marked moment divided by the positive top moment. Such a bound requires estimates for the explicit factorial sums and their bounded normals; it does not follow merely from (1). Audit: [universal symbolic recurrence and literal source checks](../experiments/audit_actual_generic_trivalent_racah_source_identity.py). The two Fricke/boundary rational certificates and the transpose/AW gauge certificates have identically zero cleared numerators in five independent parameters. The supplementary original-matrix audit passes eleven generic families, 489 all-vector Jacobi recurrences, full highest-source column/endpoint checks, and cyclic source covariance. These are exact checks supporting the uniform proof, not an inference from numerical polynomial fitting. Independent internal review: both the global audit agent and the crossing/source agent completed full analytical reads and fresh replays, including the exceptional c=0 actual cup projection, literal source-column bend and transpose, generic high-partner continuation, cyclic source phase and closed-trace exponent cancellation. No conditioning or asymptotic conclusion was included in either verdict.

title: The actual coefficient model has a nonzero geometric normal period
text: # The actual coefficient model has a nonzero geometric normal period Research note, 26 October 2026. This derives the first transport amplitude from the original crossing coefficients and proves a uniform Morse--Bott statement at the complete hyperbolic representation. After transverse formal contraction, the resulting actual-coefficient normal connection is formally gauge equivalent to the marked geometric one. This is a comparison of local normal stationary blocks. It is not a construction of the selected global finite-state cycle, an identification of its quantum-A annihilator ideal, or a volume-conjecture proof. ## 1. The actual state and its independent flow variables Keep the original reduced state F_N(M), q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q_N^2, x=-M/q_N and Y=M^2. Use exactly the factorial boundary frame of [the marked critical-correspondence proof](marked_braid_holonomy.md). Its cut vector is constant and its covector is the normalized average. The reduced period is still F_N(M); the factor 1/N is retained. Take a b-strand knot braid with m crossings, read in the actual operator-action order. Start with integer positions a_0,...,a_(b-1) and one transfer k_t for each crossing. The position update is (a,b) -> (b+k,a-k) for a positive crossing, (a,b) -> (b-k,a+k) for a negative crossing. Closing strands 1,...,b-1 gives b-1 independent integral equations. Their matrix on the initial positions is a cofactor of P-I for the braid permutation P. Because the closure is a knot, P is one cycle; this cofactor has determinant +1 or -1. Thus all positions except a_0 are solved integrally in terms of a_0 and all m transfers. The total-index conservation gives the remaining closure as well. There are exactly d=m+1 (1.1) independent phase variables, on an integral flow lattice with no unrecorded determinant. This counts variables of the actual cut sum, not a substituted geometric state. ## 2. The principal amplitudes retain the color half-step Write H=Log Q, A=Q^a, B=Q^b, C=Q^k. The balanced positive crossing has exact variable product P_Q(QB)P_Q(QC)P_Q(Y/A) /[P_Q(QBC)P_Q(YC/A)P_Q(Q)], (2.1) with the already proved Gaussian factor. The negative product replaces B by A and Y/A by Y/B, with its different Gaussian. The cancellation Qx^2=Y is important in (2.1): the last two variable arguments are not Q-shifted arguments. For the existing compact product, Log P_Q(z)=Li_2(z)/H+(1/2)Log(1-z)+O(H), Log P_Q(Qz)=Li_2(z)/H-(1/2)Log(1-z)+O(H). Every higher variable coefficient is rational in z. Also Log x=Log M+pi*i-H/2 on the specified sheet. Its contribution to the Gaussian amplitude is sqrt(AB) positively and sqrt(C/(AB)) negatively. Therefore the squared variable principal amplitudes of the actual coefficients are a_(+,0)^2=AB (1-BC)(1-Y/A) /[(1-B)(1-C)(1-YC/A)], a_(-,0)^2=C/(AB) (1-AC)(1-Y/B) /[(1-A)(1-C)(1-YC/B)]. (2.2) All five shape arguments are nonzero and different from one on the established geometric chart, so these are units there. Their square-root covers and original phases are retained. This includes the exact local transport. For example the three positive internal shift ratios are R_a=BC/x * (1-Y/(QA))/(1-YC/(QA)), R_b=A/(Cx) * (1-QBC)/(1-QB), R_k=-A/(QBCx) * (1-QBC)(1-YC/A)/(1-QC). (2.3) The negative ratios are R_a=x/B * (1-QAC)/(1-QA), R_b=x/A * (1-Y/(QB))/(1-YC/(QB)), R_k=1/x * (1-QAC)(1-YC/B)/(1-QC). (2.4) They follow by cancelling finite factors; no asymptotic knot identity is used. If S is the actual local leading action, each equation verifies [H]Log R_i=(1/2)S_(ii)+partial_i Log a_0. (2.5) For the actual meridian half-step M->exp(H/2)M, its ratios are R_M^+=(ABC)^(-1/2)(1-YC/A)/(1-Y/A), R_M^-=(AB/C)^(1/2)(1-YC/B)/(1-Y/B). (2.6) They have zero first H correction and satisfy S_(uu)/8+partial_u Log a_0/2=0. The half-step and its original square-root character are therefore checked independently. The closed pivot and zero-framing factors contribute principal amplitude M^(b-1-w)/product_(j=1)^(b-1) A_j, where w is the writhe and A_j are initial closed positions. Their leading phases and base-only constants remain the ones in the [actual action calculation](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md). Thus the complete variable amplitude is nonzero on the chart. Neither the fixed P_Q(Q)^(-m) nor the boundary normalization 1/N has been evaluated separately at a root or discarded. ## 3. The geometric critical scheme is smooth with two framing directions The actual crossing calculation gives an isomorphism of open critical schemes with framed augmented knot representations, with its inverse meridian eigenflag fixed to the cut flag 1. Its formulas and inverses have unit denominators on the chosen chart, so this includes Artin rings, not just complex points. The framing group is B_1=Stab_(PGL_2)(1), of dimension two. The geometric representation is irreducible and its projective centralizer is trivial; the framing torsor is explicitly split by three developed flags, as already constructed in that note. Here is why the unframed geometric germ is smooth with meridian as coordinate, without importing a deformation-rigidity proof. Use the positive triangulation and invertible marked gluing Jacobian in [the geometric rigidity note](geometric_rigidity_and_cyclic_source.md). The development construction identifies its germ with the augmented representation quotient. This identification also works over Artin rings: three distinct vertex flags give the unique face transformation; their differences stay units. The product around an edge fixes its two distinct endpoints and has multiplier the edge shape product, hence is identity when that product is one. The dual two-skeleton therefore constructs a flat representation. Conversely a representation and peripheral flag give the developed cross-ratios. Normalizing one ordered triple makes these two constructions inverse. The fixed SL2 lift is retained on its etale sign cover. The marked gluing germ is etale over the meridian. Consequently the actual framed critical germ at fixed M is a smooth open part of its two-dimensional B_1 torsor. The actual inverse cut flag can be compared by (U,V)->(-U,-V); both peripheral signs are changed together, preserving the regulator differential. It follows that the Hessian of the flattened actual phase has kernel=T(B_1), rank=d-2=m-1. (3.1) Indeed the local gradient ideal is the logarithm of the exponentiated critical equations. Its Jacobian is the Hessian, and smoothness of this very critical scheme gives rank d-2. This is a Morse--Bott assertion for the actual coefficient phase. Alternatingness is not required; the positive geometric input is the already audited one for hyperbolic knot exteriors. ## 4. A nonzero transverse formal block of the actual coefficients Choose two actual position/transfer coordinates chi whose differential on the framing torsor is invertible. Their level set is an algebraic transverse slice. Restriction of the symmetric Hessian to the remaining d-2 coordinate directions is nondegenerate, because those directions complement its radical. Let this restriction be H_perp. Formal Gaussian contraction on the slice now yields a nonzero normal block, with variable leading term A_(perp,0)=a_(beta,0)/sqrt(det(-H_perp)), (4.1) up to the retained coordinate half-density. The numerator is a unit by Section 2 and the denominator is a unit by (3.1). Subtract the full constant and quadratic phase before Wick contraction; all remaining vertices have degree at least three. At each formal H order there are finitely many contractions. All coefficients are algebraic functions of the critical representation and framing, regular at the complete chart. Before selecting a framing section, the result is a formal two-form density on B_1. If r,s are coordinates on that torsor, then its squared leading coefficient is a_(beta,0)^2 det(partial chi/partial(r,s))^2 /det(-H_perp). (4.2) This formula changes correctly under a different transverse coordinate choice. It does not perform the remaining framing period. Replacing that period by evaluation at an arbitrary framing section would change the selected global construction. ## 5. Formal normal difference transport agrees with the geometric line Let K be a common algebraic function field for the geometric gluing branch and its rational framing section, adjoining the recorded half-density roots. The actual normal block has form Z_act^perp=C_beta(H) exp(S_act/H) A_act(M)(1+sum_(j>=1)H^j A_j(M)). (5.1) C_beta(H) denotes its recorded base-only normalization line, including the fixed product and cut-average constants and powers of H. If a constant Li_2(1) is moved from the phase into this line, that move is recorded on both sides. No value of an individual compact factor at a root is assigned. All variable amplitudes in (5.1) belong to K, and A_act is a unit on the complete chart. The positive triangulation's dual local formal period in the geometric rigidity note has the same property. Its leading action satisfies the same preferred-longitude differential as S_act, and both complete imaginary values equal Vol(M). Their leading difference is therefore an M-constant real phase, retained in the comparison line. Use epsilon=H=2h, h=Log q, throughout. After retaining those base-only lines, the ratio of the two normal amplitudes is an explicitly recursively computable g(M,h) in K[[h]]^times. (5.2) It is their quotient of formal Gaussian series. The leading term is the ratio of the algebraic unit amplitudes; every higher coefficient follows by finite division in K. Thus, for their actual meridian-step ratios with sigma(M)=exp(h)M, a_act^perp=a_geo * sigma(g)/g. (5.3) Equivalently their formal period connections differ by h dLog g, with all leading longitude and lift characters matched. This proves a formal normal-connection comparison to all orders. It is not merely a comparison of leading dilogarithmic symbols. The full ADO factor d_N(M), including its root-central difference constant, remains the original one. It is not absorbed into the coefficientwise formal unit (5.2). Its local nodal density comparison is the separate exact result of the preceding note. ## 6. What this does and does not select The normal block comes from the actual coefficient model and has nonzero principal amplitude. The remaining framing density and its boundary source have not been paired with the actual finite cut cycle. Equation (5.3) consequently does not identify the quantum-A module of the selected finite sum, its root monodromy eigenline, or its complete value with this normal block. In particular no conclusion about a geometric factor of the minimal summed operator follows just from the nonzero normal block: taking the remaining relative period can kill a class. The whole selected root source and its lattice still have to be transported, including all polar intersections and caps. Nor are the formal series assumed to converge or to control their selected value along h=pi*i/N. The volume-norm theorem is still required for the original F_N(1). There is a concrete check against a tempting simplification. The raw normal framing density is not automatically a constant Haar form. At the figure-eight algebraic critical point over F_97 with Riley root 36, frames (r,s)=(2,3),(3,2) give squared two-form coefficients 92 and 77. Multiplication by s^2 gives 52 and 17, and multiplication by s^4 gives 80 and 68. Thus neither dr ds/s nor dr ds/s^2 is the raw coefficient density up to a frame-independent multiplier. A global framing comparison needs its specified quantum adapters and boundary source, not an assumed group-volume factor. There is also an exact characteristic-zero calculation on the full framing chart. Put t=(1-sqrt(-3))/2 and tau_cusp=2-4t. The squared coefficient of dr ds in the same normal two-form is f_perp(r,s)^2=-tau_cusp/[6 s^2(s+1)^2]. (6.1) The [full two-variable audit](../experiments/audit_full_framing_density.py) retains both framing derivatives and checks the two Hessian null vectors in Q(sqrt(-3))(s,r). Exact polynomial arithmetic proves independence of r on this figure-eight chart. [Results](../experiments/full_framing_density_results.json). The [regular meridian centralizer](regular_meridian_centralizer.md) now explains the additional (s+1) divisor. Its invariant two-form adapted to the actual cut coordinate is Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(s+1)], so (6.1) says exactly Omega_perp^2=(-tau_cusp/6)Omega_cut^2. Contracting the latter with its centralizer vector s partial_r gives dlog A_cut, A_cut=1/(1+s). This identifies the geometric quotient form; it does not yet prove that the original finite source and its selected cut implement this contraction. Neither the formula for every knot nor that period comparison is assumed. The subsequent [actual cut-residue/density calculation](actual_cut_residue_and_principal_density.md) now derives the logarithmic cut co-source directly from the original finite average. Both original crossing amplitudes have a mixed-Hessian/momentum-coboundary factorization; the momentum factors cancel on every critical closure and leave the original pivot. The corrected ambient phase volume is invariant under the regular-meridian centralizer. A linearized fixed-point complex supplies an invariant torsion under a stated rigidity hypothesis. Identifying that determinant line with this normal Gaussian density and transporting the selected internal source remain work. ## 7. Precisely where the ideal triangulation theorem enters The positive triangulation theorem supplies more than a numerical expression for volume. Its geometric shapes produce the marked Bloch representative beta_T, with D(beta_T)=Vol(M); Section 3 uses positivity to prove an invertible marked gluing Jacobian. Development then transports this rigidity to the actual critical scheme. Sections 4--5 consequently construct a nonzero transverse formal block from the original crossing coefficients and compare its connection with the geometric regulator line. These implications use the ideal triangulation theorem at the geometric realization and rigidity step. They do not assert that the theorem supplies a quantum source, a selected relative period, or a quantum comparison along arbitrary changes of triangulation. In particular, the algebraically split framing torsor does not fix a pairing of (4.2) with the original cut cycle. Selecting an ordinary algebraic frame and selecting a horizontal pointed relative period are different operations. This gives a precise route for the next theorem. Transport the actual relative source, its integral lattice, and its full cut through a tetrahedral presentation to the positive triangulation. Retain the marked meridian, longitude lift, and peripheral factors throughout. The selected resulting relative class must pair nontrivially with the normal block above. The required comparison concerns this class and its period, rather than just the critical equations or the existence of an unpointed module isomorphism. Control of that selected period's regulator norm across levels is additional to the local formal comparison. ## 8. An exact obstruction for a proposed source comparison When the two proposed source objects admit specified equal-rank affine presentations over the same difference field (F,sigma), write them as sigma(v)=C_K v+c_K, sigma(w)=C_T w+c_T. (8.1) This is a conditional comparison criterion; neither the existence of a global geometric inhomogeneous factor for every knot nor a selected triangulation source is assumed to have been proved. A change w=Gv+t with G invertible intertwines (8.1) exactly when sigma(G) C_K=C_T G, (sigma-C_T)t=c_T-sigma(G)c_K. (8.2) The first equation compares the homogeneous connections. Once it is solved, the remaining obstruction is the explicit additive class [c_T-sigma(G)c_K] in F^d/(sigma-C_T)F^d. (8.3) Indeed, with H_aug=[G t;0 1] and U_i=[C_i c_i;0 1], the identity sigma(H_aug)U_K=U_T H_aug is exactly the two equations (8.2). Thus this obstruction concerns the horizontal affine extension, not the existence of points on its underlying affine space. The geometric gluing germ does not determine (8.3). For an elementary demonstration take F=C(q,M), sigma(M)=qM and C=1. The sources c=0 and c=1 have the same homogeneous connection, but are inequivalent: sigma(t)-t=1 has no rational solution. Expand any t in C(q)((M)); the constant Laurent coefficient of sigma(t)-t is zero, whereas that of 1 is one. This proves the claim without a growth argument. It does not model a hyperbolic knot; it isolates the additional datum any comparison must retain. Even a solution of (8.2) over a completed field is only a formal extension comparison. To identify actual selected periods one must also transport the source-one section p, the meridian lattice Lambda, and the augmented cut functional lambda: p_T=H_aug p_K, Lambda_T=H_aug Lambda_K, lambda_T H_aug=lambda_K. (8.4) Whenever these identities hold in the actual whole-germ period realization, they give lambda_T(p_T)=lambda_K(p_K), including at a marked specialization where the common lattice makes the period regular. Equation (5.3) solves only the homogeneous formal normal comparison; it does not establish (8.2)--(8.4) for the actual relative source. Finite-cover descent alone cannot fill this gap, as the trace argument in the [affine-source note](affine_quantum_a_period.md) shows. This is the explicit source-compatible comparison for which the positive ideal triangulation supplies the geometric target. ### When the source comparison also determines the period There is a useful conditional reduction at a root. Work over a coefficient field E with sigma of finite order n; for the actual M coordinate and q_N this can be n=2N. Suppose both specified source extensions in (8.1) have nonresonant cyclic monodromy, det(I-H_K)det(I-H_T)!=0. Their rational horizontal source-one sections are unique, by the cyclic descent proof in [the affine-source note](affine_quantum_a_period.md): v_K=(I-H_K)^(-1)s_K, v_T=(I-H_T)^(-1)s_T. Iterating the actual affine comparison (8.2) around the orbit gives G H_K=H_T G, s_T=G s_K+(I-H_T)t. Substitution therefore proves exactly v_T=G v_K+t. Thus an independent choice of rational horizontal section is unnecessary under these hypotheses. When the specified selected sections belong to this rational solution space and the cut and lattice are also transported, their scalar periods agree, including a common regular complete specialization. Nonresonance may fail at the complete point: the equality is first an equality of rational whole germs, then is evaluated on the specified common lattice. This is not a proof of those hypotheses for the actual geometric source. In a resonant block homogeneous rational sections remain, and the original pointing must still be supplied. Nor does a separately chosen root-level affine gauge control the comparison across levels: a nonresonant extension always has a rootwise rational splitting. A fixed generic comparison, or another proved uniform realization with its normalization, is still required. The triangulation theorem supplies the geometric chart on which to seek that comparison; it does not construct the gauge or prove the selected period's regulator norm. The subsequent [common period-space construction](common_frobenius_regulator_period_space.md) now records this geometric action line together with the actual Frobenius and Tate marks over one logarithmic Heisenberg connection. Its phase and norm identities are exact. A source-cohomology retraction shows why that enlargement alone cannot split an existing generic source. It does not prove (8.2)--(8.4) for the actual knot period or control the selected realization of the formal amplitude (5.2). The subsequent [actual cut-wall source calculation](cut_wall_and_cyclic_source.md) now identifies a local part of this comparison. The normalized actual cut has consecutive wall factors p,sigma(p); its regularized dual presentation and the geometric cyclic lattice have the same point source. An explicit regular formal unit calibrates the geometric collision to the actual wall, including its residue. The full ADO common frame is retained. This is a comparison of local presentations over S, not a solution of (8.2)--(8.4) for the actual global source and selected knot section. ## 9. Exact checks and coverage [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_normal_stationary_period.py) verifies all six exact internal first-transport identities and both meridian half-step identities symbolically from (2.3)--(2.6). Twenty-four independent geometric charts use both algebraic Riley roots over F_97,F_193,F_601 and four different regular frames per root. The Hessian is constructed from the actual phase, while its null vectors are differentiated from independent representation matrices. Each five-variable Hessian has rank three and precisely the two framing null directions. Every selected transverse determinant and actual principal amplitude is nonzero. The meridian deformation tangent satisfies the mixed Hessian equation, and the reduced second derivative is twice the independently computed marked longitude derivative. These are validations of the uniform scheme and Gaussian arguments, not volume experiments. The additional univariate function-field certificate proves (6.1) and checks both framing null vectors before the stated restriction. [Results](../experiments/actual_normal_stationary_period_results.json). Critical-point existence and optimistic-limit potentials have the coverage already recorded in the marked-braid note. Formal stationary phase and formal difference connections likewise have existing coverage in the earlier comparison notes. No published proof is assumed here and no novelty claim is made. The result added here is the particular normal-block comparison in the original coefficient conventions, with the actual subprincipal color, pivot and half-step factors retained. The subsequent [uniform density theorem](quantum_source_bridge_extension.md) now gives the intrinsic variable principal coefficient for arbitrary knot braids: its parity-normalized square is -T_beta Omega_cut^2/2. The Gaussian kernel and self-dual cokernel are explicitly matched to the endpoint cut complex. Thus the determinant identification is no longer limited to the two prototype knots. Its base-only quantum normalization and selected global period remain unproved. Reproduce the finite and symbolic first-transport diagnostics with: python3 experiments/audit_actual_normal_stationary_period.py

title: The whole original source as an exactly charged bridge-flow coefficient
text: # The whole original source as an exactly charged bridge-flow coefficient 28 October 2026. After the exact simultaneous overbridge reduction, ALL remaining understrand anchor sums can also be performed exactly. The result is a finite charged coefficient, with one charge N-1 at every anchor. There are no extra cyclic alias sectors in this whole coefficient. This follows from nonnegative polynomial degree and global homogeneity, with the original closed-braid source retained. This is a larger closed algebra than the isolated complementary Pochhammer class. Its coefficients remain coupled and oscillatory. It does not prove a positive state, geometric selection or scalar noncancellation. ## 1. Use the original scalar source before splitting Put N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), x=-exp(-pi*i/N), s=x^N. Let W be ANY original complete signed braid word on b heads, in the balanced factorial basis. Every actual crossing preserves total INTEGER head degree. The original closed-head pivots are diagonal, g_a=(x/s)Q^(-a). Therefore the original one-cut partial trace is diagonal on its remaining head. The original averaged marked row, with every entry 1/N, has exactly the same scalar pairing as I/N on this already assembled diagonal matrix. Hence the actual scalar is K_N=chi_N/N *Tr[(I tensor g tensor ... tensor g) W]. (1) The external ORIGINAL dimension/framing line chi_N remains. This uses integer-degree conservation BEFORE any Fourier or bridge decomposition. It is not a sectorwise replacement of the marked row, a claim about arbitrary inserted currents, or an extra pivotal trace. Put W in the exact regular propagated frames. This removes every interior Fourier adapter. At closure head i retain its exact adapter, including the pivot when i>1. If Z is its final-grid input and Y its initial-grid output, the kernel is E_i(Y,Z)=eta_i/N *Z^(-d) C_i(Z,Y), C_i(Z,Y)=sum_(a=0)^d Z^(d-a)(t_i Y)^a, (eta_1,t_1)=(1,1), (eta_i,t_i)=(x/s,Q^(-1)), i>1. (2) This is the finite Fourier sum, including its removable values. Its numerator is a homogeneous d-form. Equivalently C_i(Z,Y)=product_(r=1)^d (Z-Q^r t_i Y). (3) Every nontrivial boundary adapter stays in (2). Matching incompatible central grids or replacing it by an identity is unnecessary. ## 2. Each reduced overbridge is a homogeneous d-form Use the exact [signed overbridge theorem](actual_signed_overbridge_unwinding.md). An overbridge e has m encounters in physical strand order, signs sigma_j, clocks d>=h_1>=...>=h_m>=0, and spectator UNDER outputs u_j. Its conditional crossing parameters can be written a_j=alpha_j/u_j, b_j=beta_j u_j, alpha_j=Q^(-h_j)/x, beta_j=Q^(h_j+1), sigma_j=+1, alpha_j=Qx, beta_j=Q, sigma_j=-1. In either case alpha_j beta_j=Q^2x. Write Delta_j=h_j-h_(j+1), and f_sigma(h)=(-1)^h Q^(sigma*h(h+1)/2). Define the explicit factor Gamma_e=kappa^(sum_j sigma_j) *product_j f_(sigma_j)(h_j) *product_(j<m) [(-alpha_j)^(h_(j+1)) Q^(h_(j+1)(h_(j+1)-1)/2)] *F_(h_1)/[F_(h_m) product_(j<m)F_(Delta_j)], F_r=(Q;Q)_r. (4) Every factorial index in (4) is at most d. All crossing normalizers are now explicit. In particular the powers N from the internal strand sums and the factors 1/N at crossings leave precisely 1/N for this ENTIRE bridge. Let Zin and Zout be its overstrand endpoint variables. Directly clearing the denominators in the exact bridge formula gives B_e=Gamma_e/N *Zin^(-d) P_e(Zin,Zout,u_1,...,u_m), (5) P_e= product_(0<=r<d-h_1)(Zin-Q^r beta_1 u_1) *product_(j<m) product_(0<=r<Delta_j) (u_j-Q^(r-1)alpha_j beta_(j+1)u_(j+1)) *product_(0<=r<h_m)(u_m-Q^r alpha_m Zout). (6) The three collections have lengths d-h_1, sum Delta_j, h_m. Their total is EXACTLY d. Thus P_e is a homogeneous degree-d polynomial with no negative powers, even when spectator variables later coincide or particular coefficients vanish. Equation (5) has only ONE denominator, at the overbridge input. For example each link denominator u_j^(Delta_j) is canceled by the corresponding spectator powers of the closed crossing scalar and link monomial. The last spectator power clears the last output Pochhammer; the input endpoint becomes Zin^(-d). This is an exact polynomial identity, not a modulus estimate. ## 3. Understrand clocks and a global bijection At a signed crossing the overclock from the actual port table is label_under,out=label_under,in-sigma*h (mod N), z_under,out=x^sigma z_under,in Q^(-sigma*h). (7) The label equation holds for both signs, with the table's physical over/under conventions. The root equation also uses the actual propagated roots, not an independently imposed meridian value. Regard every compressed overbridge and every retained closure adapter (2) as an event with one physical input and one output. Cut the oriented strand at these events. Between successive events the remaining encounters are exclusively UNDER encounters. Untouched head identities have already been suppressed. If there are B overbridge events, there are k=B+b events and exactly k intervening directed segments. The closure adapter events break any directed cycle of under encounters, even on a link component which is always under in the open braid. Assign one anchor variable X_a to the first grid port on each such segment. Starting there, (7) gives EVERY port on the segment as z_v=zeta_v(h) X_a, zeta_v=x^(sum_previous sigma) Q^(-sum_previous sigma*h). (8) For fixed clocks the map from the segment anchor label to its port labels is a cyclic translation. Conversely a collection of the old segment labels determines each h by (7) and its initial anchor label. Thus the change from all remaining port labels to the crossing clocks h and k anchor labels is a BIJECTION, of counting Jacobian one. No congruence sectors are thrown away. Every anchor segment ends at the input of exactly one event. Thus, after (8), it acquires exactly ONE denominator X_a^d, from (2) or (5). The phase zeta_event,input^(-d) is retained in the event factor. All event output and spectator variables in their numerators are also substituted by (8). No selected-overbridge variable reappears. Write P_h(X) for the product of these k substituted event numerator polynomials, and W_h=product_overbridges Gamma_e *product_closure eta_i *product_events zeta_event,input^(-d). (9) The root substitutions in each event polynomial preserve degree, so P_h has nonnegative exponents and TOTAL degree k d. Its coefficients and W_h are fully explicit functions of Q,x,kappa,h; they do not depend on an unknown knot period or on the initial Fermat centers. The latter only specify the anchor sampling grids. ## 4. Exact disappearance of EVERY cyclic anchor alias The complete source (1), after the bijection and simultaneous overbridge reduction, is K_N=chi_N/N *N^(-k) sum_(h over-monotone) W_h sum_(X_a^N=C_a, all a) [product_a X_a^(-d)] P_h(X). (10) Each C_a is the actual fixed nonzero central value at its segment anchor. It need not be one. Every event contributes its exact 1/N; there are k events. Expand a monomial X^e in P_h. Root sampling can keep it only if e_a-d=N l_a, for integers l_a, all a. But e_a>=0 and d=N-1 imply l_a>=0. Global homogeneity gives sum_a N l_a=sum_a e_a-kd=0. Therefore ALL l_a are zero. The argument includes arbitrarily large single-variable degrees: there is no omitted high-degree positive alias, because it would require a negative alias elsewhere, which the lower bound -d excludes. Consequently, termwise in h, sum_(X_a^N=C_a) [product X_a^(-d)]P_h(X) =N^k [X_1^d ... X_k^d]P_h(X). (11) There are no powers of the C_a on the right. This proves exact frame-center independence of the WHOLE anchored coefficient at each clock assignment, without deleting a separate current sector. Substituting into (10) gives the final original-source identity K_N=chi_N/N *sum_(h over-monotone) W_h [X_1^d ... X_k^d]P_h(X). (12) All k finite anchor sums have been evaluated. Their N^k cancels the N^(-k) event normalizations EXACTLY. The remaining 1/N is the original averaged first-cut source in (1), not a guessed normalization. ## 5. The resulting charged flow algebra and its scope Every event polynomial is a product of d explicit linear differences of anchors; closure uses (3). Expanding these factors chooses an endpoint anchor for each factor. The coefficient in (12) keeps exactly d choices at EACH anchor. Thus it is a finite nonnegative integer-charge flow problem, with a complex unit-phase weight on each choice. The overbridge clock domain is the independent product of monotone simplexes, equivalently the compositions (d-h_1,Delta_1,...,Delta_(m-1),h_m), all >=0, sum=d. The polynomial coefficient algebra is closed under further anchor elimination: taking one degree-d coefficient preserves nonnegative polynomial exponents and lowers total degree by d. It does not preserve the isolated two-Pochhammer factorization. It is in this larger EXACT charged algebra that the understrand elimination closes; no tuned Vandermonde identity or discarded boundary term is required. ### Exact anchor-cycle transport and charged source currents For every FIXED h the period in (12) is the specified Laurent polynomial form (1/(2*pi*i)^k) integral P_h(X) product_a dX_a/X_a^(d+1). (13) It has no finite noncoordinate poles. Consequently the product circle radii can be changed to ANY finite positive radii, with the original coefficient and source unchanged. This is a literal torus homotopy in (C*)^k; it does not use the raw off-grid four-Psi continuation. Its linear-form zeros are zeros, not residue divisors. No discarded Phi seam, Cauchy collision or unretained cyclic carry is needed for this anchor-radius transport. Escape to zero/infinity is not part of the assertion. The exact charged Ward current at each anchor is [X^d](X_a partial_(X_a)-d)P_h=0. (14) More generally the integral of X_a partial_(X_a)[F P_h product_b X_b^(-d)] against product_b dX_b/X_b is zero, for a Laurent-polynomial test F. After multiplying by the FULL W_h and summing h it is still zero. This is a current of the proved charged representation, not a claim that arbitrary new matrix coupons preserve its previous root-grid support theorem. If none of the linear forms L_r vanishes, the finite-N stationary anchor equations of (13) in logarithmic coordinates are explicitly sum_r c_(r,a) X_a/L_r(X)=d, all a, L_r(X)=sum_a c_(r,a)X_a. (15) Thus the stationary current is a rational charge-balance equation. Each form contributes total one, so the sum of (15) is the known identity kd=kd. One common scale is redundant. Exactly, without an asymptotic argument, [X_1^d...X_k^d]P_h(X) =[Y_1^d...Y_(k-1)^d]P_h(Y_1,...,Y_(k-1),1). (16) This follows from total degree kd. It removes the common C* scale from the actual source period. Neither (15) nor (16) by itself identifies its stationary scheme with the knot A-curve; the remaining clock equations and their actual source selection must also be proved. ### The exact grouped graph connection Let q=exp(pi*i/N). A block of length 0<=L<=d has the form product_(r=0)^(L-1)(alpha X_i-Q^r beta X_j). Its coefficient with j-charge a is alpha^L S_(L,a) w^a X_i^(L-a)X_j^a, w=-(beta/alpha)q^(L-1), S_(L,a)=product_(r=1)^L sin(pi*r/N) /[product_(r=1)^a sin(pi*r/N) product_(r=1)^(L-a) sin(pi*r/N)] >0. (17) This follows from [L choose a]_Q=q^(a(L-a))S_(L,a), together with the q-binomial expansion. Thus the phase is LINEAR in the block charge after a fixed block phase is removed; it is not a quadratic approximation. For the actual blocks in (6), after the undertransport (8), the connection phases are exactly input: w=q^(sigma_1*h_1) zeta_(u_1)/zeta_(Zin), link j: w=q^(sigma_(j+1)*h_(j+1)-sigma_j*h_j) zeta_(u_(j+1))/zeta_(u_j), output: w=q^(-sigma_m*h_m) zeta_(Zout)/zeta_(u_m), closure: w=t_i zeta_(Zout)/zeta_(Zin). (18) For closure the first argument in its length-d block starts at Q, as in (3), which makes its residual phase exactly the actual pivot t_i=1 or Q^(-1). No extra half-turn is hidden in (18). Within one bridge, (18) telescopes using the local potentials q^(sigma_j*h_j)zeta_(u_j) and the unshifted endpoint potentials. That fact alone is not global flatness: distinct spectator ports u_j can belong to the SAME under-anchor segment and have different local potentials. A gauge test must use the actual grouped graph and differences of FEASIBLE charge flows, including its capacities, rather than an unsupported abstract cycle. The audit exposes this graph through graph_blocks(H,S,h). Its metadata records every block's anchor endpoints, length, event type, and exact integer q-exponents for alpha,beta,w, modulo 2N. It also records the baseline outgoing degree at each anchor. If a block chooses head charge a_e in [0,L_e], the exact charge equations are sum_(head=i) a_e-sum_(tail=i) a_e =d-sum_(tail=i)L_e. (19) These metadata reproduce the whole polynomial coefficient, with (17) and all fixed block phases retained. They do not assert that the connection has trivial holonomy on the feasible-flow lattice. Equation (12) is stronger than retaining a generic higher hypergeometric remainder at every underbridge. It supplies the complete source charge at all anchors and removes all cyclic carry ambiguity from those sums. It does not make the remaining h/flow sum positive. The phases in (4), (8), and the linear forms remain; they can produce cancellation. Identifying a global geometric critical branch and its selected coefficient is still required. No broad scalar volume limit follows solely from (12). For literature COVERAGE only, quantum-determinant presentations of the Kashaev invariant were already reported by [Huynh--Le, *On the Colored Jones Polynomial and the Kashaev invariant*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0503296). The abstract also proposes comparing that determinant with a determinant expression for hyperbolic volume. No determinant formula or analytic proof from that paper is used here, and no novelty claim for coefficient/determinant reformulations in general is intended. The independent statement proved above is the exact original-source clock bijection, event charge and absence of cyclic anchor aliases. The proof is for the ORIGINAL complete braid word and its stated scalar source. An inserted degree-changing coupon need not permit (1) and would need its own charged source form. The theorem does not discard such a coupon or claim the same charge automatically. ## 6. Reproducible audit python3 experiments/audit_actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.py The audit verifies the signed undertransport and event/segment bijection, pointwise homogeneous bridge forms with all original normalizations, the alias-free root-grid coefficient identity, and the full formula (12) against ORIGINAL signed physical word matrices and their actual averaged pivotal scalar, including its external framing/dimension line.

title: A source-exact full half-clock dilation of the physical head
text: # A source-exact full half-clock dilation of the physical head 28 October 2026. At complete color the ORIGINAL N-dimensional head is an invariant orthogonal window in an explicit 2N-clock representation. The weighted cyclic shifts have zeros at both window boundaries. The unrolled H, full half-Cartan, genuine dual, N-normalized turns, original pivot and selected cut all lift exactly. For a one-component knot, the selected cut forces the physical window around the entire component, so the full extended contraction is the original scalar. This supplies a legitimate unitary 2N Fourier ambient space. It does not supply the global triangulation edge character required by the [positive-angle majorant](positive_angle_majorant_and_integer_winding.md). The new ambient clock dilates the old window; its conserved physical charge is already present in the original unrolled degree equations. ## 1. Exact complete-color generators Put q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, x=q^d=-q^-1, and c=q-q^-1. Use the ORIGINAL balanced basis w_a=v_a/(Q;Q)_a. The original head is H w_a=(d-2a)w_a, K w_a=x Q^-a w_a, F w_a=(1-Q^(a+1))w_(a+1), E w_a=(Q^-a-1)/c^2 w_(a-1), 0<=a<N, (1) with the nonexistent endpoints set to zero. Indeed the original unbalanced E coefficient is [a]_q[N-a]_q=[a]_q^2 and [a]_q^2/(1-Q^a)=(Q^-a-1)/c^2. No factorial metric change is being made in this note: (1) is the already used balanced presentation. On W=C^(2N), with orthonormal basis u_J, define T u_J=q^J u_J, X u_J=u_(J+1 mod2N), F_W=X(1-Q T^2), E_W=X^-1(T^-2-1)/c^2, K_W=x T^-2, H_W u_J=(d-2J)u_J. (2) Here TX=qXT; Q is still q^2 of order N. The zeros of F_W occur at J=d,2N-1 and those of E_W at J=0,N. Hence W=W_0 direct_sum W_1, W_0=span(u_0,...,u_d), W_1=span(u_N,...,u_(2N-1)) (3) is an orthogonal decomposition into invariant unrolled modules. Under u_(N epsilon+a) <-> w_a, E,F,K are the original matrices, and H is shifted by -2N epsilon. In particular W=V_d direct_sum V_(d-2N), E_W^N=F_W^N=0. (4) The first-window inclusion i and p=i^* are isometric and satisfy p i=I. Any prescribed original head metric can instead be copied orthogonally to both summands; the inclusion remains isometric. Unitary ordinary DFT statements below use the balanced flat metric. The unrolled quantum relations follow on each summand from (1). For example [H,E]=2E and [H,F]=-2F hold at the cyclic wraps because the corresponding weights are ZERO, not because H was made cyclic. Replacing H by a residue class would lose this justification. ## 2. The full Cartan and the genuine dual Use the ORIGINAL finite universal crossing, in its original order, Rcheck=Flip q^(H tensor H/2) sum_(n=0)^d q^[n(n-1)/2] c^n/[n]_q! E^n tensor F^n. (5) Formula (5), and its actual inverse, are well defined on W. Every denominator has n<N and is nonzero. Since each summand in (3) is invariant, a crossing transports its two summand labels with the physical strands. On the selected W_0 tensor W_0 its restriction is EXACTLY the original Rcheck, including the common Cartan scalar kappa=q^(d^2/2). No kappa was stripped or replaced by a 2N scalar. The full Cartan is not the bare cyclic phase Q^(ab). On the original window it is q^[(d-2a)(d-2b)/2] =kappa q^[-d(a+b)] Q^(ab). (6) On W_epsilon tensor W_eta its ratio to the original Cartan is (-1)^[d(epsilon+eta)]. This is a unit phase; it follows by expanding the two unrolled H shifts before taking q powers. The restriction statement itself does not require dropping this phase elsewhere. Use the GENUINE dual W^*, with the ORIGINAL antipode and pivotal duality. It is V_d^* direct_sum V_(d-2N)^*. In the copied original dual basis u_(N epsilon+a)^vee its H weights are H_Wvee=d+2N epsilon-2a. (7) In particular, its second dual summand is not assigned the naive weight d-2(N+a). Those two expressions differ by 4N, which is invisible to q^H but not to unrolled H as an operator. The true dual is what justifies the cups, caps and half-Cartan identities. Write the original pivotal matrix as g_a=x^(1-N) Q^-a. The root parameter is still N: the pivot on W is K_W^(1-N), not K_W^(1-2N). Copy this exact matrix to both summands. In the original unrolled convention the twist at highest weight alpha is q^[(alpha^2+2(1-N)alpha)/2]; its values at d and d-2N agree, since their ratio is q^(2N^2)=1. Thus the original zero-framing correction also lifts with its exact scalar. The original left turns, in the original factorial boundary frame, lift as coev_L^W=sum_(epsilon=0,1) sum_(a=0)^d N x^-a u_(N epsilon+d-a) tensor u_(N epsilon+a)^vee, ev_L^W(u_(N epsilon+a)^vee tensor u_(N eta+b)) =delta_(epsilon,eta) x^a/N delta_(a+b,d). (8) The right turns have the SAME original pivot factors; for example coev_R^W=sum_(epsilon,a) N x^-a g_(d-a)^-1 u_(N epsilon+a)^vee tensor u_(N epsilon+d-a). (9) These are the direct-sum genuine turns, not new normalization choices. They use N and 1/N, not 2N and 1/(2N). Restricting every leg to the first summand gives the literal original turns. The ordinary cap is still not declared to be the Hermitian adjoint of the cup; this dilation does not change the pivotal trace's positivity. ## 3. Exact original one-component source Let P_0=i p be the first-window projector. If the original closed-braid source is the normalized averaged cut, retain it literally as (1/N) Tr_(W cut)(P_0 C_W), (10) with every original closed pivot and zero-framing factor retained. If the original source is a specified cut matrix entry, retain that entry in W_0 instead. These choices agree for the uninserted scalar knot endomorphism; they are NOT interchanged for arbitrary inserted exteriors. In a plat retain its actual marked coupon g E_00 and its prescribed pivotal side, extended in W_0. No replacement by I_W/(2N) is made. **Source theorem.** Replace every physical head by W, every dual by W^*, and use (5),(8),(9) and their actual inverse/right versions. For ANY one-component knot presentation, its original selected scalar is unchanged. Proof. Expand the extended contraction by summand labels epsilon. Each crossing transports the two labels with their physical strands; each cup or cap matches the label on its two incident physical legs. Thus the label is constant along each physical link component. The original selected cut forces label0 on its component. Since there is only one component, every nonzero term lies in W_0 on every physical leg. Each local restriction is exactly the original coupon, including Cartan, pivot, boundary and framing constants. Therefore the entire sum equals the original scalar, not merely its modulus or its leading exponent. This proof also retains literal original insertions which preserve or are lifted inside the selected summand, provided their original cut functional is kept unchanged. It does not apply a scalar-knot trace conversion after inserting new coupons. For a multi-component link, each component must carry its specified selected projector if this same statement is wanted. Leaving another component unselected permits its other summand and is a different source. Likewise arbitrary new offdiagonal summand-changing coupons are outside the theorem. The construction is an exact COMPLETE-COLOR lift. At generic color the direct sum V_alpha direct_sum V_(alpha-2N) still gives an exact isometric module lift, but the simple E polynomial in (2) no longer gives its boundary values: endpoint projectors are then required. No unproved whole-meridian polynomial-weight extension is inferred from the complete-color q-number zeros. The original full modified dimension remains an external normalization line throughout. ## 4. What full-clock information actually follows On W and its genuine dual the copied half-clock is T u_J=q^J u_J. Although their unrolled H lifts differ, both satisfy T=q^(d/2) q^(-H/2). (11) The dual second-summand difference4N contributes q^(2N epsilon)=1. Unrolled total-H conservation therefore gives the EXACT identity [Rcheck,T tensor T]=0. (12) On every full turn, J+Jvee=2N epsilon+d, so (T tensor Tvee)coev=q^d coev. (13) The corresponding cap has the same affine charge. Consequently a full q-character average is legitimate at these PHYSICAL vertices. The charge in (12) is not only modulo N: on the original window, the conserved unwrapped total lies in[0,2d], whose width is <2N, so its modulo2N equation is equivalent to exact integer equality. However, (12)--(13) already hold on the original N-window. They are its existing integer flow and inverse-meridian pairing laws, now realized in a full-clock ambient space. The quantum factorial still has base Q=q^2 and length N; the nilpotency order in (4) is still N. Nothing has changed it to a 2N-dimensional cyclic dilogarithm. There is an explicit limitation for the OLD unweighted N-cyclic shift used in cyclic-atom factorizations. Its exact blockwise lift is not X. Put P_wall=|d><d|+|2N-1><2N-1|, S_hat=X(I-P_wall)+X^(1-N)P_wall. (14a) Then S_hat is the direct sum of the two ORIGINAL N-cyclic shifts, so S_hat^N=I. Directly on every basis vector, T^2 S_hat=Q S_hat T^2, T S_hat-q S_hat T=-2q X^(1-N)P_wall T. (14b) The right side is a nonzero rank-two wall current, of norm2 in the flat metric. The two weights in (2) kill their respective endpoint terms, which is why the complete original R lifts cleanly. An old cyclic-atom factorization, however, must use S_hat and retain (14b) if its old Q-Weyl relation is refined to a q relation. Replacing its unweighted S_N by X without this correction changes its physical restriction. Thus the dilation does not automatically upgrade the old cyclic shape algebra to a free full-q Weyl algebra. The small rank alone supplies no bound after arbitrary factorial conjugations. Let F_(2N) be the unitary 2N discrete Fourier transform. The physical window becomes the rank-N projector (F_(2N) P_0 F_(2N)^*)_(rs) =(1/(2N)) sum_(a=0)^d q^[a(r-s)]. (14) Its diagonal is1/2. For r!=s its entry is zero if r-s is even and 1/[N(1-q^(r-s))] if r-s is odd. Thus the selected Fourier source is not an independent uniform full-clock source: it retains this exact projector, or its propagated equivalent under the full contraction. Plancherel preserves it rather than deleting it. To apply the positive affine-angle theorem one must STILL construct the actual source map to tetrahedral nonnegative angles with sum d, identify the geometric edge-incidence rows, and prove the full edge character Ek=2d modulo2N with subexponential comparison norm. Physical head conservation (12) is not that global geometric edge equation. Joint noncommuting quantum shapes are not automatically positive angle labels either. This dilation resolves the cyclic-wrap issue for the physical head; it does not close those geometric/source gates. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_half_clock_source_dilation.py): literal generators and unrolled relations, full Cartan/crossings, genuine dual turns, physical affine charge, Fourier projector and selected original one-component braid sources. Finite checks are supplementary to the direct-sum and component-label proof above.

title: A finite half-color quadratic transform for the original source
text: # A finite half-color quadratic transform for the original source 29 October 2026. This proves the exact simple-channel coefficient of the ORIGINAL figure-eight four-plat in the complete Casimir frame. The finite proof uses one terminating q-Chu identity, proved below by finite binomial expansion. It retains all root phases, common Cartan factors and the actual original cup/cap opening. The resulting coefficient is a positive sine-binomial square sum times its known phase. It tests the pointed energy of the complete channel Gram, not the value of the invariant after its final cap. ## 1. A reusable odd-root quadratic transform Let `N=2m+1>=3`, let Q have exact order N, put `F_r=(Q;Q)_r` and `a=Q^(-m)=Q^(m+1)`. All factorials below have index at most 2m and are nonzero. Define S_m=sum_(k=0)^m Q^[-k(m-k)] [m choose k]_Q^2. Then EXACTLY sum_(t=0)^m Q^t (a;Q)_t^3/F_t^2 =(-1)^m Q^[-m(3m+1)/2] S_m. (1) This is a finite 3-parameter-to-2-parameter quadratic source transform. It is valid at composite odd levels as well as prime ones, with no square-root choice or root-zero denominator. Proof. Expand the THIRD Pochhammer by the finite binomial theorem, put `t=k+j`, `n=m-k`, and retain the other two factors. The left side becomes sum_(k=0)^m (-a)^k Q^[k(k-1)/2+k](a;Q)_k^2/F_k^2 *sum_(j=0)^n Q^j (aQ^k;Q)_j^2 /[F_j(Q^(k+1);Q)_j]. Apply terminating q-Chu to the inner sum with terminating length n, `b=Q^-n=aQ^k`, `c=Q^(k+1)`. It is Q^(-n^2)(Q^(m+1);Q)_n/(Q^(k+1);Q)_n =Q^(-n^2)(a;Q)_n F_k/F_m. (2) Here the ODD ROOT relation `Q^(m+1)=a` is essential. Substitute (a;Q)_r=(-1)^r Q^[-mr+r(r-1)/2]F_m/F_(m-r). Each k-th term is now `(-1)^m Q^[-m(3m+1)/2-k(m-k)] [m choose k]_Q^2`. This proves (1), including every sign and exponent. ## 2. Elementary finite q-Chu and Durfee identities The finite identity used in (2), whenever its denominators are units, is sum_(j=0)^n (Q^-n;Q)_j(b;Q)_j Q^j /[F_j(c;Q)_j] =b^n(c/b;Q)_n/(c;Q)_n. (3) No published summation proof is a premise. Here is a direct finite proof. First the binomial theorem gives sum_(s=0)^n (Q^-n;Q)_s Q^s/F_s *(cQ^s;Q)_(n-s) =(-c)^n Q^[n(n-1)/2]. (4) To check (4), expand the last Pochhammer. Its c^r coefficient contains `(Q^(1-(n-r));Q)_(n-r)`, zero unless r=n. Only that last coefficient survives, giving the right side. Multiply (3) by `(c;Q)_n`, expand `(b;Q)_j`, and extract b^r. Set `j=r+s` and apply (4) with length n-r and parameter cQ^r. The result is (-c)^(n-r) Q^[(n-r)(n-r-1)/2][n choose r]_Q, the b^r coefficient of `b^n(c/b;Q)_n`. Thus (3) is a rational identity before specialization and holds at the stated roots. Its useful finite Durfee consequence is sum_(r=0)^t Q^(r^2)/(F_r^2 F_(t-r))=1/F_t^2. (5) Indeed take n=t, b=Q^-t, c=0 in (3), multiply by Q^(t^2), and reverse its summation index. This proves (5) by the same finite algebra, without an infinite-product interpretation. ## 3. The actual complete-channel coefficient Now use the principal `q=exp(pi*i/N)`, `Q=q^2`, `d=2m`, `x=q^d=Q^m`, `nu_m=(-1)^m q^[m(m+1)]`. Let R_1,R_2 be the two ORIGINAL generators on the complete source multiplicity module, including their common Cartan kappa. The TRUE four-plat action order is `[2,-1,2,2]`, hence W=R_2^2 R_1^(-1) R_2. Let V be the complete physical Casimir/Hermite frame, J the actual anti-Pascal recoupling, and p the original cup. Define the COMPLETE right-channel output z=V^(-1)J Wp. At odd N the node c=-2 is simple, with normalized eigenvector `f_0=1`, crossing value nu_m and bilinear norm `sigma=x^d nu_m`. Its exact coefficient is z_simple=N Q^[m(m+1)] F_m S_m. (6) At the principal root `S_m=sum_(r=0)^m |[m choose r]_Q|^2>0`. Thus (6) is not an expanded path or a guessed saddle surviving selection; it is the ENTIRE actual channel after all its sums. ## 4. Source reduction to the quadratic transform The actual J is symmetric: its anti-Pascal formula and `F_jF_(d-j)=N(-1)^jQ^[j(j+1)/2]` give `J_(i,j)=J_(j,i)`. Put `y=Jf`, `h=R_2p`, `v=R_1^(-1)h`. The lower bidiagonal equation for y, with endpoint `y_d=f_0=1`, gives exactly y_i=0 for i<m, y_(m+r)=Q^[-r(m-r)][m choose r]_Q^2. (7) The successive ratio is the square of `|1-Q^(m-r)|/|1-Q^(r+1)|`; its complex factorial form in (7) keeps the phase identity at arbitrary primitive Q. The FIRST original R_2 on the cup highest lift has a forced final third-head color zero. In the literal positive crossing the transfer must equal that second input color. Its coefficient simplifies to `kappa F_(d-i)`, using `x^2=Q^-1`. Therefore h_i=kappa p_i F_(d-i), p_i=Nx^(i-d). (8) The literal original inverse crossing then gives v_i=x^(i-d)(-1)^i Q^[i(i+1)/2-d] F_(d-i)/F_i *sum_(b=i)^d Q^b F_b^3/F_(b-i). (9) For example (9) follows directly by the finite inverse-R transfer sum and the SAME reflection identity; the common kappa in (8) cancels the prescribed inverse kappa. No external normalization has been changed. Multiply (9) by (7), put `i=m+r`, and interchange `b=m+t` and r. Using (5) gives y^T v=C sum_(t=0)^m Q^(m+t) F_(m+t)^3/F_t^2, C=(-1)^m x^(-m) Q^[m(m+1)/2+1]. (10) This intermediate reduction is a finite identity with the original source; in particular no extension beyond the true finite ranges has been made. Since `F_(m+t)=F_m(a;Q)_t`, (1) evaluates (10): y^T v=Q^[-2m^2+m+1]F_m^3 S_m =F_m^3S_m=N nu_m F_m S_m. (11) The remaining exponent is `(1-m)(2m+1)`, a full root period. The last equality is the full reflection identity `F_m^2=N nu_m`. Finally the simple inverse channel row is `f^T/sigma`. Moving the two terminal R_2 factors through J and selecting that simple channel gives z_simple=(kappa^2 nu_m^2/sigma)y^T v =nu_m y^T v. Here `kappa^2=x^d` for the actual odd-level full Cartan. Substituting (11) proves (6), with all source and common-line phases retained. ## 5. Scope for the proposed positive energy For the balanced complete-channel Gram `G=(V^(-1)J)^*(V^(-1)J)/N`, the original pointed energy is `E_N=N^(-1)||z||_2^2`. Equation (6) implies EXACTLY E_N>=N^2 S_m^2, (12) because `|F_m|^2=N`. The asymptotic consequence is developed in the companion energy audit; it concerns THIS particular positive Gram. It does not contradict its exact Cauchy inequality, and it does not rule out a different source-preserving coherent terminal Gram that contracts more of the actual tensor before squaring. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_half_color_quadratic_source_transform.py): the finite q-Chu/quadratic transform and the literal full original four-plat simple-channel coefficient, at odd composite and prime levels, with all common Cartan and source constants.

title: Exact Hardy replacement of the internal finite-head projectors
text: # Exact Hardy replacement of the internal finite-head projectors 28 October 2026. The original scalar Euler/Gaussian network admits an exact simplification: **every internal finite Dirichlet kernel can be replaced by an ordinary Hardy Cauchy kernel**, provided its existing finite factorial and Gaussian kernels are retained. This holds for every signed braid word and its full original source. With the proved fused plat source, the boundary is monomial as well. Thus the Dirichlet numerator branches are unnecessary in this presentation of the complete word. This does not remove the actual finite Euler/Gaussian endpoint sectors. Their support is essential to the proof. Nor does the theorem identify a new geometric edge's three indices with a charged degree. The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_hardy_cauchy_network.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_hardy_cauchy_network_results.json) check the full original signed crossing matrices and original whole-word pivotal cuts while allowing nonzero intermediate indices beyond the head. ## 1. The actual operators, extended without an upper head projection Let $\mathcal P=\mathbb C[z]$, and let $H_N$ be its subspace of degree below $N$. On $\mathcal P$ use the unilateral shifts $$ J_+z^a=z^{a+1},\qquad J_-z^a=\begin{cases}z^{a-1}&a>0,\\0&a=0.\end{cases} $$ They have no upper cutoff. Define the ORIGINAL finite polynomials $$ u_N(t)=\sum_{h=0}^{N-1}\frac{t^h}{F_h},\qquad v_N(t)=\sum_{h=0}^{N-1} \frac{(-1)^hQ^{h(h-1)/2}t^h}{F_h}, \qquad F_h=(Q;Q)_h. $$ On a pair put $$ U_-^\infty=u_N(x^{-1}J_-\otimes J_+),\quad V_-^\infty=v_N(x^{-1}J_-\otimes J_+), $$ and define $U_+^\infty,V_+^\infty$ by reversing the two shifts. Only the lower polynomial wall is imposed. Extend each existing finite diagonal kernel by zero outside its ORIGINAL active-head support: $$ \begin{split} \mathsf Fz^a&=F_az^a,\quad \mathsf F^{-}z^a=F_a^{-1}z^a &&(0\le a<N),\\ \mathsf Fz^a&=\mathsf F^{-}z^a=0 &&(a\ge N). \end{split} \tag{1} $$ The superscript minus here is the zero-extended finite inverse diagonal, not an inverse on $\mathcal P$. Likewise retain $\mathsf D,\mathsf D^{-}$ with their original nonzero entries for $0\le a<N$ and zero entries above the head. Spectator heads are identities on all nonnegative indices. No new cutoff has been added to (1): these are exactly the finite scalar kernels already present in the [literal network](actual_euler_gaussian_cauchy_network.md). ## 2. The support lemma removes the internal upper projections Let $P$ project onto $H_N\otimes H_N$ and put $$ C^\infty=\mathsf F_2U_-^\infty\mathsf F_1\mathsf F_2^{-}, \qquad \overline C^\infty= \mathsf F_2\mathsf F_1^{-}V_-^\infty\mathsf F_2^{-}. \tag{2} $$ These are the original strict fusion and inverse-fusion words. Their support has the following exact properties: $$ C^\infty=PC^\infty P,\qquad \overline C^\infty=P\overline C^\infty,\qquad C^\infty|_{H_N^2}=C,\qquad \overline C^\infty|_{H_N^2}=C^{-1}. \tag{3} $$ For the first operator the two right diagonal factors kill inputs outside the head. Its transfer only lowers the first index, so that index stays in the head; the left $\mathsf F_2$ kills every second-index overflow. For the second operator the two left diagonals enforce its output support. On a head input, an overflow generated by $V_-^\infty$ is precisely the second-index overflow killed by $\mathsf F_2$. These are the same coefficient sums as the finite fusion and its finite inverse. Keep the original Cartan scalar $\kappa$, and define $$ \begin{split} R_+^\infty&=\kappa C^\infty \mathsf D U_+^\infty\overline C^\infty,\\ R_-^\infty&=\kappa^{-1}C^\infty V_+^\infty\mathsf D^{-}\overline C^\infty. \end{split} \tag{4} $$ Then for the actual inclusion $i:H_N^2\to\mathcal P^2$, $$ \boxed{\qquad R_\pm^\infty i=iR_\pm.\qquad} \tag{5} $$ Indeed $\overline C^\infty i=iC^{-1}$. The transfer $U_+^\infty$ or $V_+^\infty$ can overflow only its first index. Before the next transfer, $C^\infty$ applies its input support $P$, which kills that overflow. Its surviving part is exactly the truncated $U_+$ or $V_+$ in the original strict factorization. The two extensions in (4) need not be inverses on the whole polynomial space. Their restrictions to the original head are the prescribed signed inverse crossings. That is sufficient for an arbitrary signed word. The proof is unchanged for unequal colors in the actual [typed strict formula](actual_rogers_bridge_transport.md): $C_x^{-1}$ on input, $C_y$ on output, the original $D_{x,y}$, and the stated $x^{-1}$ or $y^{-1}$ Euler argument. Their coefficients change; the support argument does not. All unrolled common Cartan and external normalization lines multiply the same two realizations. ### Every nonempty upper-tail branch vanishes in the complete crossing One may replace ANY subset of the original internal finite projections by Hardy projections, not merely all of them at once. To see this, follow the three transfer stages in (4), in traversal order. 1. The inverse-fusion $V_-^\infty$ can overflow only head two. The following $\mathsf F_2$ kills that overflow before the central transfer. 2. The central $U_+^\infty$ or $V_+^\infty$ can overflow only head one. The input $\mathsf F_1$ of the final fusion kills it before the final $U_-^\infty$ transfer. 3. The final $U_-^\infty$ can overflow only head two, which the last $\mathsf F_2$ kills. The remaining factors between these barriers are diagonal; they cannot return an overflow to the head. Spectator heads remain in their original finite heads. Earlier killing by any additional finite projection therefore removes only paths that the barrier would already kill. On Laurent inputs the exact decomposition is $$ \Pi_N=\Pi_+-\Pi_{\ge N},\qquad \Pi_{\ge N}(z,w)=\frac{(z/w)^N}{1-z/w}. \tag{5a} $$ In the nested Hardy chamber, expand the original finite projection factors using (5a). **Every term containing at least one upper-tail factor has zero full-crossing action on the original head.** The same assertion holds for boundary fusion factors and for every original full word by (6). This is an ordered barrier identity. It is not an assertion that an arbitrary endpoint coupon or Ward current is zero. Inserting a new operator between a transfer and its barrier can invalidate it. ## 3. Whole-word and source identity For $b$ heads write $i_b:H_N^{\otimes b}\to\mathcal P^{\otimes b}$. Embedding the two-head operators of (4) at every letter gives for EVERY signed braid word $$ \boxed{\quad W^\infty(\beta)i_b=i_bW(\beta).\quad} \tag{6} $$ This follows by induction from (5); no intermediate finite-head projector is used. Every original input/output entry, pivotal partial trace, marked source, peripheral function and external framing line is consequently preserved. The same inclusion intertwines any original finite-head coupon inserted BETWEEN complete crossings, provided its extension restricts to that coupon on the head. This includes the original Hopf currents, so the full Ward identities and their original source pairings are preserved. It does not assert the same statement for an arbitrary coupon inserted between the elementary factors of one crossing. The original closed-braid boundary still has its prescribed finite pivotal sum. Alternatively use the already proved full fused $2k$-plat formula $$ P_{\beta,N}=\chi_{\beta,N}N^{1-k} \langle e_{\rm out},B_\beta e_{\rm in}\rangle. \tag{7} $$ Here every input pair is $(d,0)$; every ordinary output pair is $(0,d)$; the marked output pair is $(d,0)$. Expand $B_\beta$ into its actual pair fusions, signed crossings and retained original scalar lines. Apply (3)--(6). The result is exactly (7) on the polynomial space, with monomial input and coefficient-extraction output. The Ward corner in (7) is the theorem for the FULL assembled intertwining word. It is not applied separately to a Hardy, cyclic, or sewing summand. ## 4. The scalar integral has no finite Dirichlet numerators Let $$ K_+(t)=\frac1{1-t},\qquad |t|<1. $$ This is the Hardy reproducing kernel for nonnegative powers. For example the transfer kernel on two heads is now $$ \prod_j K_+(z_j/w_j)\, u_N(x^{-1}w_2/w_1), \tag{8} $$ with $v_N$ and the reversed argument for the other transfers. The diagonal kernels are exactly the existing finite ones: $$ \mathsf F^{-}:u_N(z/w),\qquad \mathsf F:N(z/w)^{N-1}v_N(Qw/z),\qquad \mathsf D^{\pm}:\Gamma_{\pm,N}(z/w). \tag{9} $$ Their spectators contribute $K_+$ instead of $K_N$. Thus **all internal factors $(1-t^N)/(1-t)$ are replaced by $1/(1-t)$**, without approximating or discarding a period. The proof is the complete ordered support identity above, not replacement of one split reproducing residue in isolation. For monomial boundary data $e_a,e_c$ and a word with $L$ elementary factors, its entry is $$ \operatorname{CT}_{z^0,\ldots,z^L} (z^0)^a(z^L)^{-c} \prod_{\ell=1}^{L}K^\infty_\ell(z^\ell,z^{\ell-1}). \tag{10} $$ Choose nested positive radii $|z^\ell_j|<|z^{\ell-1}_j|$. Every Hardy series converges there; every other factor is a finite Laurent polynomial. The CT is consequently a literal rational Cauchy integral. There are a fixed number of variables for a fixed plat, independent of $N$. No cycle made solely of Hardy inequalities is being imposed: the boundary in (10) is monomial. The initial/final finite indices and every scalar in (7) remain the original ones. ## 5. Exact gain and the remaining geometric charge This eliminates a specific exponential branch family from the original scalar Cauchy presentation: the finite Dirichlet numerators and their artificial split poles. Nonzero intermediate overflow routes are allowed and then killed by the support of the original diagonal kernels. The earlier source-visible coupon $X_-X_+$ has no intervening finite diagonal barrier: an upper excursion can return before it is tested. Its nonzero endpoint correction is therefore consistent with this theorem. Likewise the cyclic-sewing and Fermat-cap walls are different relative terms and have not been deleted here. It does not eliminate the finite endpoints of $u_N,v_N$ or $\Gamma_{\pm,N}$. The diagonal support in (1) is essential; replacing those kernels by unrelated nonfinite symbols is outside the theorem. The Hardy poles in (8) are also genuine reproducing poles; contour transport must retain their actual residues. All elementary transfers preserve total INTEGER degree. Hence (10) retains the original total plat degree $k(N-1)$, and after ordinary caps the remaining pair has the exact affine charge $D+1=N$ from [the charged cap theorem](actual_degree_carry_and_cap_winding_obstruction.md). The theorem does not impose that pair charge at every intermediate slice: crossings between pairs move degree between them. What is still missing is the source-preserving identification of a geometric Pachner edge's three angle clocks with that augmented charged class. The Hardy replacement supplies a simpler exact whole-word integral on which to seek it; it does not prove $h_1+h_2+h_3=N$ for an unassigned geometric edge or select the hyperbolic critical cycle.

title: Exact Hardy-forest residue reduction of the original selected cycle
text: # Exact Hardy-forest residue reduction of the original selected cycle 28 October 2026. All Hardy/reset variables in [the continuous-Gaussian cyclic period](actual_continuous_gaussian_cyclic_network.md) admit a simultaneous ordinary-residue reduction. The surviving cycle is specified explicitly. Every other annulus component is retained first and then proved zero against the ORIGINAL source by a one-way negative-index barrier. The normal residue coefficient is exactly $+1$. This is the coefficient of the Hardy pole graph, **not** a computed intersection number with a hyperbolic thimble. The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_hardy_forest_residue.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_hardy_forest_residue_results.json) check eight original whole-word pivotal matrices with no intermediate Hardy/head projection, 360 signed head columns, 812 negative-current subsets, nonzero surviving negative outputs before the original source, the pole-forest Jacobian, and reduced radius chambers. ## 1. Hardy poles form a forest Keep the fully telescoped physical braid word, with its boundary pair fusions and original monomial input/output. Every Hardy factor connects consecutive variables of ONE head in word time: $$ K_e=\frac1{1-g_e z_{\rm out}/z_{\rm in}}. $$ Here $g_e=1$, except at an actual Gaussian dilation where $g_e=c_se^{\alpha_s\xi}$. Transfer multiplication does not identify different heads. An active factorial kernel breaks the path; its input and output variables remain independent. The monomial source adds no closing Hardy edge. Thus the Hardy pole graph is a forest of head-time segments. Choose one terminal variable per segment and set $$ u_e=\frac{z_{\rm in}}{g_ez_{\rm out}}. \tag{1} $$ The logarithmic incidence matrix is triangular/unimodular. Using path normals followed by the terminal coordinate gives determinant one with the induced orientation. The base-only $d\log g_e$ terms vanish when wedged with all Gaussian $d\xi$ variables. Consequently $$ K_e\,\frac{du_e}{2\pi i u_e} =\frac{du_e}{2\pi i(u_e-1)}. \tag{2} $$ Every normal pole is now independent, with residue $+1$. No scalar $g_e$, determinant root, meridian factor, or Gaussian Jacobian is removed. Such factors remain in the substituted source and cyclic arguments. ## 2.
