A reduced cycle before taking the residues The pole graph sets $u_e=1$: $$ z_{\rm in}=g_ez_{\rm out}. \tag{3} $$ After imposing it, retain one complex variable per head-time segment and every real Gaussian variable. Equivalently, one may retain the initial coordinate of each head and a new coordinate after each active factorial. Moving the retained coordinate within a segment multiplies it by a known nonzero product of $g_e$; its logarithmic Jacobian is one. There are $b+6m$ complex coordinates for the displayed strict $m$-crossing physical word on $b$ heads. The two boundary pair-fusion frames of a $2k$-plat add $6k$, giving $6m+8k$ in the unshortened presentation. Further exact simplifications may reduce this count. All counts are independent of $N$. ### Explicit radii without resets Take $\rho_0=1/64$ and $0<\lambda\le1$ below all active color moduli. The following construction works for every fixed Gaussian tuple and every signed word. For one crossing, let its input head radii be $R_1,R_2$, and put $G=|c_se^{\alpha_s\xi}|$. The inverse-fusion part is realized by $$ \begin{split} b&=\min(\rho_0R_2/2,\ \rho_0\lambda R_1/2),\\ a&=\rho_0R_1/2,\\ c&=\max(2b/\rho_0,\ 2aG_*/(\rho_0\lambda)), \end{split} \tag{4} $$ where $G_*=1$ for the positive crossing and $G_*=\max(1,G)$ for the negative crossing. The first reciprocal factorial updates head two to $b$. Its following $V_-$ transfer has argument modulus at most $\rho_0/2$. The reciprocal factorial on head one updates it to $a$, and the positive factorial on head two updates it to $c$. Positively, the central transfer uses radii $a,c$, then the Gaussian graph changes head two to $c/G$. Negatively, that Gaussian graph comes first and the central transfer uses $a,c/G$. Formula (4) makes its argument small in either order. For the final fusion choose $$ e=\min(\rho_0(c/G)/2,\ \rho_0\lambda a/2),\quad f=2a/\rho_0,\quad q=2e/\rho_0. \tag{5} $$ Its reciprocal second-head diagonal updates to $e$, its positive first-head factorial to $f$, its $U_-$ multiplier leaves these coordinates unchanged, and its final factorial updates head two to $q$. Every cyclic argument has modulus below $\rho_0$. Spectator coordinates are simply identified, rather than being constrained by an extra radius inequality. For a boundary fusion use its three diagonal updates and the same preparation of its one transfer; no Gaussian compensation is needed. The inverse boundary fusion is handled in the same way. The full complex Gaussian relation in (3), including its phase, is imposed; (4)--(5) give its radii. All logarithms of the chosen radii satisfy $$ |\log r_j|\le C_{\rm word} \left(1+\sum_\ell|\xi_\ell|\right). \tag{6} $$ Indeed each update is a minimum/maximum of one preceding logarithm plus a fixed constant and, at most, a term $\pm\log G$. There is no multiplicative recursion of logarithms. This gives a specified reduced fibered torus cycle, not separate incompatible local circles. ## 3. An exact simultaneous annulus decomposition Let $H$ be the number of Hardy edges. Starting from the reduced radii above, choose $$ \eta=\frac{\log2}{4(H+1)}. $$ In the normal coordinates (1), allow $e^{-\eta}\le|u_e|\le e^\eta$ independently. Each unreduced head coordinate is a retained coordinate times a product of path normals and Gaussian factors. Each cyclic argument therefore changes in modulus by at most $e^{2H\eta}<\sqrt2$. Since its reduced value is below $1/64$, it remains below $1/16$ throughout this complete polyannulus. In particular NO cyclic norm divisor is crossed. Every cyclic root has its original anchored lift. Only the explicit independent poles $u_e=1$ occur in these annuli. The outer torus $|u_e|=e^\eta$ has every Hardy argument strictly below one. It can be reached from the original reset-cycle chamber without crossing a pole or norm divisor: all radius constraints are affine strict inequalities in logarithmic radii, so interpolate linearly. Both cycles have cyclic arguments below $1/16$ and Hardy arguments below one. Estimate (6) and the Gaussian majorant hold uniformly in this homotopy. Now apply the ordinary annulus identity in each independent $u_e$: $$ \int_{|u_e|=e^\eta}\frac{F\,du_e}{2\pi i(u_e-1)} =F|_{u_e=1} +\int_{|u_e|=e^{-\eta}} \frac{F\,du_e}{2\pi i(u_e-1)}. \tag{7} $$ The other variables are retained. Iteration gives a finite sum of $2^H$ relative components: the full pole graph and all possible nonempty sets of inner circuits. Nothing is shrunk to zero or infinity. Any information inside an inner circuit, including possible distant branch divisors, is still represented by that circuit. The assertion below is that its ORIGINAL source pairing is zero, not that it is zero in unpointed twisted homology. On each inner circle, $$ K_e=-\sum_{a<0}(g_ez_{\rm out}/z_{\rm in})^a. \tag{8} $$ It is precisely the negative-Laurent current at that head-time edge. Residue edges implement ordinary coordinate identification/dilation. All these series converge absolutely in their stated chambers. Every branch cycle has the same type of joint bound $$ C N^B\exp\{C_0N+C_1N\sum|\xi_\ell| -N\|\boldsymbol\xi\|^2/2\}. $$ For the absolute coefficient expansion, bound cyclic coefficients on a slightly larger disk still below one; the resulting absolute series has the same exponential-in-$N$ bound. Hardy series have a fixed geometric ratio $e^{-\eta}$. Thus Fubini/Tonelli and coefficient routing are justified, including the noncompact Gaussian base and the radius homotopy. ## 4. Every nonempty inner-current component is source-null Use signed integer head indices; do NOT impose a Hardy projection. The exact scalar kernels have these elementary support properties: - a reciprocal factorial has only nonnegative diagonal coefficients, so it kills a negative active index; - a positive factorial has only diagonal indices at most $d=N-1$; its negative Laurent coefficients are retained and may be nonzero; - a transfer has order $h\ge0$ and changes indices by $(a,b)\mapsto(a-h,b+h)$ or $(a+h,b-h)$; - a Gaussian dilation preserves every signed index. Consider the actual fully ordered crossing $C\,D\,U_+\,C^{-1}$ or $C\,V_+\,D^{-1}C^{-1}$. 1. In $C^{-1}$, a new negative first index is lowered further before the reciprocal first-head factorial kills it. A negative second input is killed immediately by its first reciprocal second-head diagonal. 2. A negative second index created by the central transfer survives any dilation, then is killed by $C$'s first reciprocal second-head diagonal. 3. The last $U_-$ in $C$ can emit a negative FIRST head. Its other head is nonnegative and at most $d$ after the last positive factorial. At the next crossing touching the negative head, that head is killed in $C^{-1}$: immediately if it is second, or after further lowering if it is first. An untouched negative head cannot heal. Diagonal negative Laurent coefficients never change an index and therefore cannot repair it. This proof uses no cancellation of coefficients and is independent of colors or Gaussian values. The original cup input is nonnegative. A boundary fusion applied to $(d,0)$ produces no negative survivor, since its last positive factorial requires $h\le d$. The terminal inverse-fusion frames kill any negative head. Alternatively, an original finite nonnegative output coefficient or pivotal cut kills any untouched negative output. Thus there is NO supported route from any nonempty negative-current component in (7) to the original output source. Its exact pairing is zero. Arbitrary Laurent-healing coupons inserted inside the word are outside this statement; original finite coupons may be extended by zero outside their heads. This is a route-support proof on the actual kernels, not reconstruction and evaluation of an entire prefix polynomial. Infinite cyclic tails are handled by the convergence argument in Section 3. Combining (7)--(8), the original selected period equals the **pure all-pole graph integral with coefficient exactly $+1$**. All other circuits have been retained and explicitly proved source-null. ## 5. Explicit reduced scalar phase and cycle coordinates After the residues: - each transfer is multiplication by its cyclic function in the two current head coordinates; - every spectator/reset coordinate is identified; - an active factorial retains a new complex coordinate and its cyclic convolution kernel; - a Gaussian identifies its input/output by $w=g_s(\xi)z$, and its ordinary Gaussian variable remains integrated on $\mathbb R$. There are no rational Hardy poles left. The surviving cycle is exactly the fibered product of circles in (4)--(5), with the anchored cyclic roots, not an arbitrary positive-angle chain. Here is the variable-dependent leading phase of one positive crossing explicitly. Let its input coordinates be $z_1,z_2$, its six successive active factorial output coordinates be $u_1,\ldots,u_6$, and put $g=-(xy)^{-1}e^{\sqrt{\pi}(1+i)\xi}$. The output coordinates are $u_5,u_6$. With limiting marked colors $x,y$ and phase convention $\exp(W/h)$, $$ \begin{split} W_+={}&-\operatorname{Li}_2(u_1/z_2) +\operatorname{Li}_2(u_1/(xz_1)) -\operatorname{Li}_2(u_2/z_1) +\operatorname{Li}_2(u_1/u_3)\\ &-\operatorname{Li}_2(u_2/(xu_3)) -\operatorname{Li}_2(gu_4/u_3) +\operatorname{Li}_2(u_2/u_5) -\operatorname{Li}_2(u_4/(yu_5)) +\operatorname{Li}_2(u_4/u_6)\\ &+2\pi i\left[ \log(u_3/u_1)+\log(u_5/u_2)+\log(u_6/u_4) \right]-\pi i\xi^2 . \tag{9} \end{split} $$ For a negative crossing use $g=-(xy)e^{\sqrt{\pi}(1-i)\xi}$ and replace its central term $-\operatorname{Li}_2(u_2/(xu_3))$ by $+\operatorname{Li}_2(gu_2/(yu_3))$. All other terms follow the same strict order. The full word phase is the sum of these local phases and boundary-fusion phases, together with $2\pi i$ times the original initial-minus-terminal source logarithms. The original external $\chi_{\beta,N}$ is retained separately. Exact $q$ half-steps and the difference between $N$ and $N-1$ contribute the specified nonzero amplitude; they are not discarded normalization. All logarithmic marks in (9) come from the original reflected factorial monomials and source. Norm roots retain the continuation from the small-argument cycle. ## 6. Actual classical coordinates, rather than unnamed auxiliaries Let $p$ be the momentum conjugate to $\log z$, so $B=e^p$ is the physical clock $Q^a$. The reduced elementary phase relations give: $$ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{kernel}&\text{canonical input/output relation}\\ \hline \mathcal U(z/w)& B_{\rm out}=B_{\rm in}=B,\quad z=w(1-B)\\ N(z/w)^d\mathcal V(Qw/z)& B_{\rm out}=B_{\rm in}=B,\quad z=w/(1-B)\\ \text{Gaussian}& B_{\rm out}=B_{\rm in}=B,\quad w=c_sB^s z \end{array} \tag{10} $$ The positive-factorial momentum lift includes its retained $2\pi i$. The transfer multipliers change the momenta by the derivatives of their dilogarithms. For example a $U_-$ multiplier with $t=x^{-1}z_2/z_1$ sends $$ B_1\mapsto B_1/(1-t),\qquad B_2\mapsto B_2(1-t), $$ and leaves the two position coordinates unchanged. The Gaussian relation follows from $\partial_\xi W=-2\pi i\xi+\alpha_s p=0$ and $\alpha_s^2=2\pi is$. This identifies concrete parts of the known actual fusion chart. For a full $C_x$ put $A=B_1,J=B_2$ and $$ K=1-\frac{z_2}{xz_1}(1-A)(1-J). $$ Composition of the elementary relations gives $$ \begin{split} U&=A/K,\qquad V=JK,\\ z'_1&=z_1/(1-A),\qquad z'_2=z_2(1-J)/(1-JK). \tag{11} \end{split} $$ With $$ p_A=z_1^{-1},\quad p_J=z_2^{-1},\quad p_U=(z'_1)^{-1},\quad p_V=(z'_2)^{-1}, $$ equation (11) is EXACTLY the previously proved [actual rational fusion graph](fusion_canonical_chart_and_retained_source_wall.md), including its inverse. Thus the remaining coordinates are actual cotangent/head variables. There is also a literal shared-flag dictionary on the unwrapped Laurent realization: $$ Z_i=B_i,\quad S_i=z_i,\quad X=xz_2/z_1,\quad Z=B_1,\quad XZ=QZX. \tag{12} $$ At the complete color, $$ (Q-B_1^{-1})X=q\,\mathcal E_1z_2. $$ This is the actual tetrahedral factor in [the middle five-point wall calculation](actual_middle_five_point_wall_factorization.md). However $X^N=x^Nz_2^N/z_1^N$ is still a variable central multiplication; no typed $X^N=1$ has been imposed by renaming variables. At $M=1$ the classical generators are $F=(1-B)z$, $\mathcal E=z^{-1}(B^{-1}-1)$ and $K=-B^{-1}$. Up to its specified scalar lift, the actual shared meridian matrix is the usual unipotent Gauss chart with $A=B$ and flag coordinate $z^{-1}$. This gives an explicit comparison with known classical flag variables, not a conclusion that the reduced cycle is already a positive Rivin-angle cycle. ## 7. What remains unproved The selected auxiliary Hardy cycle has now been pushed forward exactly, with its normal degree $+1$, all inner currents accounted for, and an explicit reduced phase and cycle. The unreduced Hardy normal directions are no longer being treated as ordinary geometric stationary variables. The reduced cycle is still the small-argument anchored cycle above. Its transport through cyclic norm divisors and the actual five-term flag atlas to a regular hyperbolic chart has not been proved. Neither the normal residue degree nor the existence of a geometric critical representation computes its geometric intersection number. In particular no volume conjecture or hyperbolic noncancellation is claimed here.

title: The actual highest-input / Whittaker-output boundary retains two walls
The actual primitive Hilbert-90 gauge has a dilogarithm action and exponential norm
text: # The actual primitive Hilbert-90 gauge has a dilogarithm action and exponential norm 27 October 2026. The explicit cyclic source gauge in [the actual Fourier twisted-trace theorem](actual_source_fourier_twisted_traces.md) has a rigorously computable exponential scale, even in the flat right-regular metric. This is an ACTUAL gauge from the original source construction, not an arbitrary central rescaling of a state. It proves why solving its norm-one transport equation does not by itself give a subexponential comparison to a geometric period. The result also identifies a concrete dilogarithm action of this source gauge on a regular chart. It does not identify that chart with the marked geometric A-component or its Bloch regulator. ## 1. The specified actual gauge Let q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, h=2pi*i/N and z^N=0. The primitive k=1 source sector has the unique scalar-polynomial gauge with constant term one g_N(z)=v_N(z)v_N(Qz) =[u_N(z)u_N(Qz)]^-1, (1) u_N(z)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1) z^a/(Q;Q)_a, v_N=u_N^-1 in the nilpotent algebra. It solves g_N(Qz)/g_N(z)=1/[(1-z)(1-Qz)], eliminating the corresponding inner twist of the source automorphism. The constant-term and transport equation make it unique: a quotient of two gauges would be Q-invariant, hence constant in degree<N. The full matrix comparison can have other choices; no uniqueness claim for all matrix gauges is made. The CANONICAL polynomial representative of (1), of degree<N, is exactly the Taylor polynomial through degree N-1 of exp(L_N(z)), where L_N(z)=sum_(a=1)^(N-1) (1+Q^a) z^a/[a(Q^a-1)] =-i sum_(a=1)^(N-1) cot(pi*a/N) z^a/a. (2) Indeed the logarithm of v_N in the nilpotent algebra is sum z^a/[a(Q^a-1)]. Adding its shifted logarithm gives (2). This establishes the relation to the ACTUAL finite gauge before using analytic estimates. It is not an unproved resummation of quantum jets. ## 2. Uniform asymptotics of the actual polynomial on a fixed disk For |z|<=1/4 one has, uniformly as N grows, g_N(z)=exp[(2/h) Li_2(z)+O(1/N)]. (3) The same statement with the opposite sign holds for the canonical degree-<N representative of g_N^-1. In particular these finite polynomials have no zero on that disk for all sufficiently large N. Here is a proof that retains the truncation error. First, on every fixed disk |z|<=rho<1, L_N(z)=(2/h)Li_2(z)+O(1/N). (4) For a<=N/2 use the uniform elementary estimate cot(t)=1/t+O(t) on 0<t<=pi/2. Dividing its error by a gives O(1/N) per coefficient, whose sum against rho^a remains O(1/N). For a>N/2, the inequality |cot(pi*a/N)| <= N/[2 min(a,N-a)] gives a tail O(rho^(N/2) log N), and the omitted tail of Li_2 is smaller. This proves (4) with both root endpoints accounted for. Put G_N=exp(L_N) as an ordinary analytic function. On |z|=1/2, the coarser |cot(pi*a/N)|<=N/2 gives |L_N(z)| <= (N/2)log 2, |G_N(z)| <= exp[(N/2)log 2]. Cauchy's coefficient bound and the degree-N Taylor tail therefore give, throughout |z|<=1/4, |G_N(z)-g_N(z)| <= 2 exp[-(N/2)log 2]. (5) Meanwhile (4) gives |G_N(z)| >= exp[-N Li_2(1/4)/pi-O(1/N)]. For example Li_2(1/4)<=13/48, so Li_2(1/4)/pi is strictly smaller than log(2)/2. Thus (5) is exponentially small RELATIVE to G_N on the entire disk. Combining it with (4) proves (3) for the actual canonical polynomial. Replacing L_N by -L_N proves the inverse statement by the identical estimate. The Taylor-tail estimate is essential. Nilpotent equality alone would not justify evaluating its analytic exponential away from zero, as the nonzero endpoint carry in [the meridian half-step theorem](actual_euler_meridian_half_step.md) explicitly demonstrates. ## 3. A positive exponential lower bound for this comparison gauge Take w=i/4 and set c=Im Li_2(i/4)/pi > 0. The alternating power series proves Im Li_2(i/4) >= 1/4-(1/4)^3/9=143/576. Equation (3) gives the precise scalar-gauge rate log|g_N(i/4)|=c N+O(1/N). (6) To pass from this polynomial value to an ACTUAL finite operator, use the flat right-regular basis f^a e_j. The operator R_f is a truncated shift with unit coefficients. For |x|=1, its argument xR_f has norm one, and the powers applied to a degree-zero basis vector are orthogonal. If g_N(z)=sum c_a z^a, this gives ||g_N(xR_f)|| >= (sum |c_a|^2)^(1/2) >= sqrt(15/16)|g_N(i/4)|. (7) The second inequality is just Cauchy--Schwarz for evaluation at |w|=1/4. Multiplication by x^a changes no coefficient norm. Thus this specified comparison gauge has exponential operator growth, with liminf N^-1 log||g_N(xR_f)||>=c. Applying the inverse version of (3) at -i/4 proves the same lower bound for its inverse. Its condition number therefore has liminf logarithmic rate at least 2c. All these operators are unipotent: their diagonal entries and determinants are one. The source transport is cyclic and obeys its exact norm-one equation. Those algebraic facts coexist with the exponential norm in (7). This result concerns the flat coefficient metric. A nonunitary physical fusion change requires its own metric comparison. ## 4. Implication for the intended torsor proof The primitive source transport is explicitly SOLVED at each level, and its gauge action is the specified dilogarithm in (3). Its comparison is not tempered. A proof may carry this action into the marked regulator rather than try to discard the gauge as a normalization. Which combination of actions and source sectors is selected by the original knot word remains to be proved. This establishes neither a counterexample to the volume conjecture nor an exponential estimate for the knot invariant. The number c above is a gauge-chart value, not a knot's hyperbolic volume. It does not rule out a different whole comparison with controlled norm. It does rule out inferring such control for this actual primitive gauge solely from Hilbert 90, finite cyclicity, unipotence or determinant one. The rigorous uniform normal-form estimate (3) is the new local period/action comparison here. The nonzero selected geometric image and global sector/cancellation estimates remain open. Subsequent direct source calculations now distinguish that operator norm from selected local periods. The [canonical resonant endpoint](actual_primitive_gauge_resonant_endpoint.md) is an explicit Gauss period of size N^-1/2. The [normalized top-coefficient period](actual_gauge_period_selects_algebraic_point.md) selects the algebraic point 2 on fixed polynomial observables and intertwines fixed ordered gauge meridian steps. Thus this specified source has an evaluated local leading period, not just an exponential operator estimate. Its full knot-word coupling and selected hyperbolic action remain unproved. [The high-precision diagnostic](../experiments/audit_actual_hilbert90_gauge_action.py) and [saved output](../experiments/actual_hilbert90_gauge_action_results.json) compare the literal finite v_N(z)v_N(Qz) polynomial with exp(L_N) and its dilogarithm action. The theorem rests on the uniform proof above; numerical rate samples are not used as a proof. Another agent independently checked its source-gauge orientation, the Cauchy remainder, both coefficient tails and the operator lower bound.

title: An interior five-point wall cannot be relocated by bare cut cyclicity
text: # An interior five-point wall cannot be relocated by bare cut cyclicity Research note, 28 October 2026. This tests a possible simplification of the retained wall in [the literal middle five-point calculation](actual_middle_five_point_wall_factorization.md). At the marked endpoint that wall contributes a known polynomial scalar. The same assertion is **false for an untransported interior wall**. An original one-crossing cup and an original figure-eight network give explicit incompatible relocation factors. The result concerns the original actual source, not a hypothetical state model. It does not exclude a Ward-completed relocation with additional currents and its full relative co-source. It proves which additional data cannot be discarded. ## 1. Fix the original wall and source conventions Take N>=2, Q=exp(2pi*i/N), complete color x=-q^(-1), lambda=x^(-1)=Qx, d=N-1, k=x^N=(-1)^(N-1). Use actual balanced heads K=xZ^(-1), e=q rho^2 E, f=F, and cyclic marks S_1^N=mu, S_2^N=k mu, X=x S_2S_1^(-1), W=E_d(Z_1)X. Equivalently, W=x mu^(-1)|d><0| tensor S_2. (1) The original cup and full averaged marked cap are p=N sum_(a=0)^d x^(a-d)|a,d-a>, m|a,b>=x^b/N^2, mp=1. (2) Let B be the original positive checked crossing, with its unchanged common scalar Cartan line kappa external. Thus the full crossing is kappa B and Bp=p. All framing and peripheral factors below multiply the same expressions; none is reset to a new numerical value. The endpoint identities, already proved in the preceding note, are Xp=Q^(-1)p, mWp=Q^(-1)/N. For any actual knot cut C_N=K_N I, a defect on that marked endpoint therefore gives mW(C_N tensor I)p=Q^(-1)K_N/N, m(1-W)(C_N tensor I)p=(1-Q^(-1)/N)K_N. (3) The second multiplier has modulus between 1/2 and 3/2, so this endpoint correction preserves every normalized volume exponent, without a volume conjecture premise. Equations (3) alone do not relocate an interior two-head coupon. ## 2. The exact naturality/current condition fails The coupon (1) acts on two physical heads. Cutting its two ends does not leave a one-strand knot endomorphism. Moreover it is not a Hopf intertwiner. For the actual total lowering current F_tot=f_1+K_1^(-1)f_2, direct multiplication gives [K_1K_2,W]=0, [F_tot,W]=(Q^(-1)-1)mu^(-1) |d><0| tensor S_2^2 !=0. (4) Indeed f_1W=Wf_1=0. The two remaining products are mu^(-1)|d><0| tensor Q^(-1)f_2S_2 and mu^(-1)|d><0| tensor S_2f_2; their difference is (4). The defect is nonzero at every N>=2 and every nonzero mu. Thus weight zero is insufficient for naturality. If a single-head coupon D is an actual Hopf intertwiner, then commuting with the distinct K eigenvalues and all nonzero consecutive F arrows forces D=cI. Such a coupon can be relocated along that strand with the original normalizations. For a multi-head coupon, block naturality requires its actual tensor-object intertwining equations, and its closing functional is not automatically a scalar one-strand cut. Coupon (1) does not even pass (4). More generally, moving an inserted coupon through a typed crossing R must retain the exact discrepancy Delta_R=R D_in-D_out R. (5) An admissible relative Ward comparison may remove (5) only after exhibiting its actual typed current homotopy and checking its pairing with the full marked co-source. Vanishing of an unmarked scalar or a cyclic matrix trace does not provide that check. The existing [Ward co-source homotopy](ward_cyclic_wall_contraction_and_marked_augmentation.md) makes the issue explicit: if mu-ell=nu F on the relevant fiber, then with an inserted W the omitted term is nu F(AWBp). For original intertwining exteriors and Fp=0, this contains the term nu A[F,W]Bp. Equation (4) supplies the literal current that must be transported here. ## 3. Two ordinary partial traces lose the actual source Retain the original pivot g=x^(1-N)Z^(-1). Both ordinary pivotal partial traces vanish: Tr_2[(1 tensor g)W]=0, Tr_1[(g tensor 1)W]=0. (6) This follows directly from (1): both |d><0| and the cyclic shift S_2 have zero diagonal. Nevertheless mWp=Q^(-1)/N is nonzero. Consequently an ordinary partial trace or an argument dividing by the ordinary quantum dimension cannot give the original marked evaluation. Indeed Tr(g)=0 at the same color. The original modified/relative source is essential, rather than an optional normalization of (6). Modified-trace cyclicity is a statement about its specified categorical morphisms. Extending it to all arbitrary linear coupons while retaining this marked functional would be false, as the next calculation shows. ## 4. An all-level one-crossing identity Define the actual finite Euler value U_Euler,N(1)=sum_(j=0)^d 1/F_j, F_j=(Q;Q)_j. This is the Euler polynomial of the original crossing, not the differently named meridian norm adapter u_N in other notes. Then exactly m W Bp=Q^(-1)/N, m B Wp=Q^(-1)U_Euler,N(1). (7) To prove the second identity note Wp=NQ^(-1)|d,0>. The original crossing coefficient from (d,0) to (h,d-h) is r(d,0,h)=N x^(-d-h)Q^(-h)/F_(d-h). Multiplication by m contributes x^(d-h)/N^2. Since x^(-2)=Q, the product with NQ^(-1) simplifies to Q^(-1)/F_(d-h). Summing h proves (7). The first identity uses the original Bp=p. Thus no published modified-trace proof or unknown scalar is involved. At N=2, Q=-1, x=i, these marked values are mWBp=-1/2, mBWp=-3/2. (8) The full original crossing changes these to -kappa/2 and -3kappa/2, with identical exterior factors. They are still unequal. This is an actual one-crossing source counterexample to bare cyclic relocation. ## 5. A scalar multiplier cannot repair all exteriors Use the actual three-braid figure-eight word T=B_1 B_2^(-1)B_1 B_2^(-1). Keep the global typed wrap marks (1,k,1), rather than resetting them independently at each insertion. Close heads 2 and 3 with the original pivots. The marked first cut uses the full functional N^(-1)sum_(a,b)C_(a,b) in the balanced basis, exactly as in the original Gauss source. For the uninserted scalar cut this is the original invariant. After inserting a nonintertwining coupon it is kept fixed and is not replaced by a highest entry. At N=2 the uninserted cut is 5I. Insert W on heads 1,2 at each of the five displayed word gaps, from left to right. Their original marked values are (-5/2,-3/2,-5/2,5/2,5/2). (9) These are exact complex-root values. The word has writhe zero, so the common scalar crossing factors cancel in the same way in all five expressions. Its original full peripheral normalization is also the same throughout. The gap-0 to gap-1 relocation is through the same local positive crossing as in (8). In (8) its ratio is 3; in (9) its ratio is 3/5. Consequently there is no scalar c_N(M), depending only on that local crossing, the root and peripheral color, that repairs this untransported wall move in every original exterior. A phase or a factor such as 1+M^n cannot fix this environment dependence. A larger current/source state must be retained. ## 6. Consequence for the remaining proof The marked endpoint wall in (3) is controlled by a known nonzero scalar and costs no exponential uncertainty. That result survives. What fails is moving an arbitrary interior wall to that endpoint while keeping its bare formula and then applying (3). A possible valid route is to transport W together with its current (4) and the original co-source homotopy, including all residues and normals. The discrepancy (5) then has a precisely stated relative pairing to check. Neither ordinary trace cyclicity nor a local scalar adjustment supplies that transport. The computations here do not prove that the required completed currents cannot cancel across a full five-point move. They show that such cancellation is a genuine missing theorem. No sharp upper or lower bound relative to a selected geometric period follows from these relocation tests. In particular the exact endpoint polynomial factor does not select a geometric saddle of the interior period. ## 7. Independent exact audit Run python3 experiments/audit_actual_interior_wall_cut_relocation.py The audit uses original E/Cartan crossing coefficients and the original pivots. It checks twelve complete/wrap families for (4), (6), (7), and twelve original figure-eight gap families through N=7 over exact prime fields. A separate exact SymPy calculation at Q=-1,x=i proves (8)--(9), including the uninserted cut 5I. Highest-entry diagnostics are recorded separately and are never used to replace the full marked source after insertion.

title: An original-source zero-side patch across an isolated shape-one divisor
text: # An original-source zero-side patch across an isolated shape-one divisor 28 October 2026. A single transverse A=1 exit of a DIRECT full-Psi factor is locally removable. The actual function is holomorphic on the entire shrinking patch, including all its accumulating zeros. After crossing to its zero side, its outgoing current is the exact sum of TWO regular selected-strip currents. The whole norm factor 1-A^N, its logarithmic mark and every original side current are retained. For a fixed finite patch this costs exp(o(N)). With a normal collar chosen smaller than the background regularity scale, both outgoing phase sectors are downhill. This does not bound the global number of visits, sum an arbitrary set of simultaneous signed collisions, or estimate the remaining original side currents by knot volume. ## 1. Precise local source hypotheses Let u=Log A be a genuine complex normal coordinate to A=1 in the INTEGRATION variables, with u=0 on the divisor. In the actual monomial phase charts this is a fixed real integral linear combination of the log coordinates; complete it by fixed linear coordinates y. The coordinate change has N-independent condition number. A purely external meridian specialization is not an available normal contour direction. The argument A includes every ORIGINAL Q/q/color tag of that full-Psi factor. If its classical signed monomial differs by an O(1/N) logarithmic shift, keep that shift in u exactly. It moves the collision center by O(1/N), which is inside the collar since alpha<1; the uniform estimates are unchanged. In particular its N-th power need not be one for a half-root tag. The exact factor 1-exp(Nu) below retains that character and is not replaced by the untagged 1-A_classical^N. This applies to an actual source chart before singular elimination: use the [atomic-window whole-source resolution](atomic_window_total_source_resolution.md) and keep its finite-window interval sources and original coupled caps. The finite window is an entire polynomial in its argument; its exact interval prefactor Log r/(r-1) has its removable value at r=1. Near a lone atomic t=1, these sources therefore introduce no new normal pole. Their N-dependent exponential monomials stay in G, with interval variables and endpoints fixed by the local normal translation. The remaining rational/head exclusions must still be checked on the chart. This does not assume an eliminated current with an apparent inverse norm is holomorphic term by term. Suppose the original scalar differential form on this chart is omega_N=Psi_epsilon(u) exp(G(u,y)/h) a_N(u,y) du wedge dy, h=2pi i/N, epsilon=+1 or -1, (1) where a_N and the FULL original relative co-source are holomorphic in the normal tube being used. All other actual full-Psi factors, fixed Gaussian/interval phases and N-dependent monomial factors are retained in G and a_N. Their own shape and quantum-pole exclusions remain valid. The unexpanded original ray currents and boundaries remain part of the same relative chain. No bare reciprocal full function or unpaired norm denominator is assumed holomorphic by definition. For the quantitative estimates, assume the other regular factors obey the slowly expanding window bounds with L=N^epsilon_0. In the fixed normal coordinate these imply |partial_u G|<=C_0+C_1 epsilon_0 log N (2) when their logarithmic marks stay bounded. For downhill alone it is enough to impose this bound on |Re partial_u G|: arbitrary retained integer wall marks have purely imaginary normal derivative and do not affect that bound. The rational/half-density amplitude is bounded by a fixed power of N, or more generally by exp(o(N)), on this tube. The tube is ISOLATING: no other dilogarithm shape-one divisor, source pole, cap singularity or quantum pole is crossed. These are substantive local hypotheses. In particular the lemma cannot be applied separately to two current summands whose apparent norm poles only cancel in their sum. One must first use their actual holomorphic aggregate. Set delta=N^(-alpha), with 0<alpha<1. The patch below lies in |Re u|<=delta, -3delta<=epsilon Im u<=delta. By isolation, all other factors remain regular throughout this patch. N is sufficiently large that Ndelta>=2pi and a fixed multiple of delta is small. ## 2. Uniform full-function bound on the ENTIRE collision collar Use the exact quantum shift, with its original logarithmic lift, Psi_epsilon(u+epsilon h_0) =Psi_epsilon(u)/(1-exp u), h_0=2pi i/N. (3) Choose a FIXED integer m=O(Ndelta) large enough that every u in the patch has delta<=epsilon Im(u+epsilon m h_0)<=Cdelta. Iteration gives the literal function identity Psi_epsilon(u) =Psi_epsilon(u+epsilon m h_0) product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-exp(u+epsilon j h_0)). (4) The shifted factor is holomorphic and nonzero in its selected strip. Every product factor is entire; its size is at most Cdelta on the patch. Equation (4) proves that Psi itself is holomorphic there and retains the simple zeros u=-epsilon j h_0; no pole or residue is created by crossing them. The argument uses the actual full function, not the norm-one cyclic atom. At the shifted point the shrinking-strip estimate applies. The local dilogarithm expansion Li_2(exp w)=pi^2/6+O(w(1+|Log w|)) gives sup_patch |Psi_epsilon(u)| <=exp[C Ndelta(1+|log delta|)+O(log N)] =exp(o(N)). (5) The constant pi^2/6 contributes unit modulus in the prescribed h_0 phase. This upper bound is uniform through every zero; no lower bound for Psi or its logarithm across those zeros is claimed. The variation of the other leading phase across this normal patch is O(delta log N) by (2). Thus relative to the same tangential base phase at u=0, the entire local integrand changes its exponential scale only by exp(O(Ndelta log N)+o(N)). Fixed-dimensional translations and their sweeps have at most polynomial mass cost. ## 3. Exact outgoing selected-strip sectors Translate the normal variable by H_t(u,y)=(u-2i epsilon delta t,y), 0<=t<=1. (6) For incoming |u|<=delta the output u'=u-2i epsilon delta satisfies -3delta<=epsilon Im u'<=-delta. The exact FULL-turn identity is Psi_epsilon(u') =(1-exp(Nu')) Psi_epsilon(u'+epsilon 2pi i). (7) The shifted factor now lies in its original selected strip with margin at least delta. Hence the outgoing differential form is exactly the sum omega_out,0 = Psi_epsilon(u'+epsilon 2pi i) exp(G(u',y)/h_0) a_N(u',y) du' wedge dy, omega_out,1 = -exp(Nu') omega_out,0. (8) Their leading actions are W_0=epsilon Li_2(exp u')+G(u',y), W_1=W_0+2pi i u'. (9) The dilogarithm and logarithm in W_0 are on the shifted selected strip, not reset to an unrelated principal value. The factor 1-exp(Nu') has NOT been divided out or replaced by a number. It records the entire outgoing zero lattice and the original integer norm/ray mark. There are exactly two currents here, independent of N, with coefficients +1,-1. ## 4. Genuine downhill transport on nested collars The singular leading action is epsilon Li_2(exp u). Along a vertical normal translation its derivative satisfies, on any continued local sheet away from u=0, d/ds Im W(u-i epsilon s,y) =-epsilon Re(partial_u W) =log|1-exp u|-epsilon Re(partial_u G). (10) This real derivative is independent of the logarithm branch. It is locally integrable through u=0 itself. Since |u|<=Cdelta on the patch, (2) gives d/ds Im W <=-(alpha-C_1 epsilon_0)log N+C. (11) Choose C_1 epsilon_0<alpha<1. (12) For large N this is uniformly negative. Thus the normal patch is genuinely downhill, not merely of subexponential amplitude cost. The background exponent epsilon_0 may first be chosen small enough to permit (12). If the SAME exponent is used for both collars and the arbitrary background bound is only O(log N), strict downhill does not follow automatically; the upper bound (5) still does. For incoming points in the selected side, continue its classical action along (6) without silently changing sheets. On Re u'<0 it agrees with W_0 at the outgoing point and W_1 has smaller imaginary part. On Re u'>0 it agrees with W_1 and W_0 has smaller imaginary part. This is the usual local Li_2 monodromy difference 2pi i u'; both continuations agree at u'=0. The statement holds for either epsilon by conjugate reflection. Therefore max(Im W_0,Im W_1) <= Im W_in-c delta log N (13) on a complete translation of length 2delta, under (12), for some fixed c>0. Retained integer logarithmic marks only add a constant 2pi m Re u along each vertical path, so the same downhill conclusion holds with those marks included. The two-sector split does not introduce an uncontrolled leading action. ## 5. The original chain identity, INCLUDING side currents Let Gamma be any fixed finite-dimensional original chain portion in the isolating tube, with its original source and logarithmic marks. Let S=H_*([0,1] times Gamma) and S_side=H_*([0,1] times partial Gamma), with the product orientation. Since partial S=Gamma_out-Gamma-S_side, holomorphy of the FULL differential form in (1) proves exactly integral_Gamma omega_N =integral_(Gamma_out,0) omega_out,0 +integral_(Gamma_out,1) omega_out,1 -integral_(S_side) omega_N. (14) No additional residue is produced at u=0 or at the lower neighboring cyclotomic zeros. The original radial/logarithmic boundaries are carried by the same homotopy or left outside its support; they are not deleted by (14). If the chart has to be split along a logarithmic seam, the two original seam currents are matched using the exact identity (7), rather than assuming the classical Li_2 branch is single valued. The whole norm factor in (7) is retained. The side current in (14) is compulsory. It vanishes for a closed chain piece, cancels on a common face of two pieces using the SAME homotopy, or remains as an explicit original relative boundary term. Normal side faces with |Re u|=delta already lie outside the shape-one divisor and are regular. Boundaries from other coordinates remain their original exit currents; this theorem does not estimate them by knot volume. All finite patch sweeps have exp(o(N)) local cost relative to the retained tangential phase, by (5), (2) and their bounded translation Jacobians. This removes the isolated shape-one divisor as a local analytic barrier and returns its outgoing contribution to REGULAR full-Psi charts with explicit integer sectors. It does not prove a global bound on the number of patches, revisits or accumulated branching. ## 6. Several independent divisors, and the limitation For a fixed number p of INDEPENDENT normal coordinates u_j, direct factors product_j Psi_(epsilon_j)(u_j), an isolating polydisc and background satisfying the corresponding bounds, the translations in (6) commute. Their exact outgoing factor is product_j (1-exp(Nu_j')) product_j Psi_(epsilon_j)(u_j'+epsilon_j 2pi i). Thus a fixed simultaneous patch has 2^p regular outgoing sectors, with every integer mark retained, and the same exp(o(N)) bound. Under nested collars satisfying (12) in each direction, the actions are downhill coordinate by coordinate. Product-chain side currents are retained by the same Stokes formula. This is a fixed finite independent-normal statement, not a cancellation theorem. Dependent signed normals can prevent a common zero-side translation; oppositely cooriented copies of the same divisor are the simplest example. Balanced collisions, simultaneous source poles, nontransverse normal maps, and arbitrary collision circuits are excluded. No automatic cancellation or sharp whole-knot estimate is inferred there. ## 7. Reproduction and scope of the checks python3 experiments/audit_actual_isolated_shape_one_patch.py The exact finite-product checks are made at Re u<0 so their logs are on the original convergent anchored branches; no floating branch unwrapping is assumed. They compare both signs of (4),(7), retaining the norm factor, through N=256 and both level parities. Separate phase calculations test both outgoing sectors with adverse polynomial background derivatives. Fresh result: **PASS**, 36 exact normal-chart transitions and 48 signed two-sector downhill checks. [Saved results](../experiments/actual_isolated_shape_one_patch_results.json). The theorem and its uniform estimates follow from the analytic proof above. The checks do not establish a global patch-count bound, a simultaneous dependent-collision theorem or a geometric lower bound.

title: The original clock source under the factorial LENGTH gauge
text: # The original clock source under the factorial LENGTH gauge 29 October 2026. The full original clock co-source has polynomial Riesz norm in the proposed factorial length frame, provided every crossing is first kept as a singleton over-event. Each crossing then supplies a complementary pair of lengths. This is an exact source embedding for arbitrary signed braid width, including the original cut, pivots, clock feedback and external scalar. After an overbridge has been unwound, its factorial Gamma is no longer a harmless phase. In the same length frame its exact norm is a positive angle-simplex partition. The two descriptions are consistent: unwinding has moved a genuine weight from the tensor network into the clock co-source. It must be retained there or assigned back to a specified bulk tensor. This note concerns the LENGTH registers, not a replacement metric on physical heads. It does not establish a positive geometric state or a sharp knot bound. ## 1. The actual singleton presentation Put q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, x=-q^-1 and F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a|, L_a=s_a^2/N, A_a=L_a^(1/8), D_a=A_a^2=s_a^(1/2)/N^(1/4). (1) The exact reflection s_a s_(d-a)=N gives D_a D_(d-a)=1, D_d=N^(1/4). (2) For a binary block B_l(X,Y;a)=product_(r<l)(X-Q^r aY), use the proposed normalization b_l=B_l/D_l. Its coefficients, phases and spectator dependence are otherwise unchanged. All original LENGTH SLOTS are retained, including l=0: D_0=N^-1/4 and b_0=N^1/4. A raw empty factor B_0=1 can be omitted, but after normalization its scalar must then be recorded. The complementary products below include those zero-length slots. In [the original charged source](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md), one may choose EVERY crossing as a singleton over-event: no identity requires compressing a maximal overbridge. For a word with m crossings on b heads there are then m+b anchor events. At crossing j its two binary blocks have lengths (d-h_j,h_j), 0<=h_j<=d. (3) All m clocks are independent. Their feedback into spectator ports is the same exact signed integer map as in the global source theorem; it is not suppressed or untwisted. The m crossing Gamma factors are now just kappa^(sigma_j)(-1)^h_j Q^[sigma_j h_j(h_j+1)/2], of modulus one. Every other factor in W_h is a power of x,Q or an original pivotal phase. Thus |W_h|=1. The original complete dimension/framing line is denoted chi_N and remains outside. Every closure block has length d. Therefore the whole block normalizer is EXACTLY, and independently of every clock, product_edges D_(length)=N^(b/4). (4) There is no factorial action hidden in (4): each pair in (3) cancels by (2). If f_h is the ACTUAL normalized b-network coefficient, the exact scalar is K_N=(chi_N/N) N^(b/4) sum_(h in{0,...,d}^m) W_h f_h. (5) The original cut factor1/N has not been absorbed into an invented boundary normalization. The f_h can be exponentially large and oscillatory. Equation(5) makes no assumption about their size. ## 2. Exact source norm and a real full-source Cauchy inequality Give the clock space C^({0,...,d}^m) its standard orthonormal basis. The Riesz norm of the co-source in (5) is EXACTLY ||ell_N||=|chi_N| N^(b/4+m/2-1). (6) Indeed there are N^m entries, all of the same modulus. This gives the genuine original-source inequality |K_N|^2 <= |chi_N|^2 N^(b/2+m-2) sum_h |f_h|^2. (7) For fixed word and the known complete scalar line, the source factor is polynomial. This is an exact Cauchy--Schwarz theorem, not a proposed positive pivotal trace or a favorable cut. Equivalently, the length-register inclusion |h_1,...,h_m> -> tensor_j |d-h_j,h_j> tensor |d>^(tensor b) (8) is isometric before the diagonal D frame. Applying D on every length leg leaves every clock pair fixed and multiplies the closure legs by N^(b/4), exactly as in (4). Arbitrary diagonal unit-phase clock/flow feedback commutes with this length frame; its actual phases remain in the network. It supplies no additional Riesz cost at the boundary. No relation between a length leg and a physical head index is presumed. There is a slightly cleaner equivalent source. Contract the b original closure blocks by the exact source reproducing law BEFORE taking a norm. Each normalized full block contributes the retained scalar D_d^-1=N^-1/4, canceling (4). The remaining clocks are still independent and the new weights W'_h have modulus one. For a one-component presentation with at least one crossing, the closure edges form the proved forest, so no unexplained full-loop factor is introduced. The resulting literal co-source has K_N=(chi_N/N) sum_h W'_h f'_h, ||ell'_N||=|chi_N|N^(m/2-1). (9) The original pivots survive as their exact root phases in f'_h and W'_h. Equations(6),(9) use their own typed bulk families; one must not keep (6)'s family while deleting its closure scalar. These polynomial SOURCE norms do not estimate the positive energy sum|f_h|^2. In particular they do not identify that energy with the geometric angle partition. A large energy is compatible with an exact Cauchy inequality. Global angle support, edge characters and coherent normalized-block gluing are additional requirements. ## 3. The exact cost after overbridge unwinding An m_e-encounter bridge has r=m_e+1 composition lengths n_0=d-h_1, n_j=h_j-h_(j+1), n_(r-1)=h_(m_e), n_i>=0, sum_i n_i=d. (10) The original Gamma in the bridge theorem satisfies EXACTLY |Gamma_e|=s_(h_1)/(s_(h_m) product_j s_(h_j-h_(j+1))) =N/product_(i=0)^(r-1) s_(n_i). (11) No normalization is chosen by dividing by the knot value. Under the SAME b=B/D convention its transformed co-source coefficient has modulus |Gamma_e product_i D_(n_i)| =N^(1-r/4) product_i s_(n_i)^(-1/2). (12) Thus its exact squared Riesz norm, on the orthonormal composition basis, is N^(2-r/2) Z_(r,N), Z_(r,N)=sum_(n_i>=0,sum n_i=d) product_i s_(n_i)^(-1). (13) For a collection of compressed bridges, after the closure forest has been contracted, independence of their monotone clock domains gives the WHOLE original co-source norm ||ell_comp||^2=|chi_N|^2/N^2 product_e [N^(2-r_e/2) Z_(r_e,N)]. (14) The feedback phases can couple the bulk coefficients but do not change this norm: their moduli are one. Keeping a normalized coefficient family and declaring its Gamma source unit would change the original source. For r=2, reflection gives Z_(2,N)=1 EXACTLY. Consequently (13) is N, agreeing with the singleton source norm in (9). For r>=3, the source weight really can have exponential scale. If Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log(2sin u)du, then log Z_(r,N)=N r Lambda(pi/r)/pi+O_r(log N). (15) In particular r=3 is the positive tetrahedral angle energy of rate v_3/pi. This is useful geometric weight, not an unrecorded error or a claim of geometric knot gluing. Proof of(15). The uniform factorial estimate gives log s_a=N J(a/N)+O(logN), with J(t)=-Lambda(pi*t)/pi, including a=0,d. There are polynomially many compositions and changing their total d/N to1 changes the maximum by O(logN/N), using the integrable logarithmic endpoint modulus of continuity. It remains to maximize sum_i Lambda(pi*x_i), x_i>=0,sum x_i=1. For r>=3 a maximum cannot lie on the boundary: adding a small positive coordinate increases the sum by a positive -delta log delta term, except at a pure vertex; there, distributing delta equally among two zero coordinates gives a positive delta log2 term. At an interior maximum no coordinate can be at least1/2: each of the other coordinates is strictly smaller than its complement, so shifting mass to one of them increases the function by the derivative -pi log(2sin(pi*x)). On the remaining region all coordinates are below1/2, where this function is strictly concave. Its unique maximum is therefore the uniform point x_i=1/r. Rounding that point to a composition of d gives the matching lower bound with O(logN) loss. This proves(15). An isometric complementary-pair encoding cannot erase the Riesz norm(13): isometries preserve it. It may instead KEEP the positive simplex weight as a bulk/source tensor. That is exactly the weight(12), and its global geometric incidence must still be proved. The polynomial singleton source and the weighted compressed source are two exact organizations of the SAME state. ## 4. What this settles for the proposed special inner product The original clock source is not an uncontrolled exponential boundary factor in the uncompressed length frame: (6)--(9) give its exact polynomial norm at arbitrary width. The original clocks, phases, closure and full external line are explicit. This does not mean that a contracted normalized b-network scalar has polynomial norm, nor that its anchor coefficient functional has polynomial dual norm in every proposed polynomial metric. For example, with the half-factorial metric ||X^a||^2=s_a, a valence-v anchor's exact dual norm squared is sum_(sum a_i=d, a_i<=l_i) product_i s_(a_i)^(-1). Complementary valence2 is tame; higher valency carries another positive simplex weight when its capacity constraints allow it. Those gluing weights must be retained in a global Cauchy/angle calculation. These are typed source and dual norms. They do not replace every trivalent tensor by a positive sum-d vertex with complementary pairings on every edge: a closed such network would require both Vd=Ed and 3V=2E, which are incompatible for d>0,V>0. In the actual binary blocks the two flow powers sum to the BLOCK LENGTH l, not d; the remaining length registers and oriented dual source charges are essential. A geometric edge-incidence theorem cannot be inferred by forgetting those types. No geometric coefficient or lower bound follows from this source norm alone. The useful next question is whether the COMPLETE normalized state energy, with these exact source and gluing weights, has the desired geometric edge support and volume bound. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_length_gauge_clock_source.py): uncompressed original signed source identities, complementary normalization, complete bridge Gamma and Riesz partition formulas.

title: Exact length-normalized stars and their doubled Gram
text: # Exact length-normalized stars and their doubled Gram 29 October 2026. The original charged star admits an exact factorial length normalization which removes its exponential scalar. Its doubled boundary Gram changes by exactly `1/N`. Contiguous parallel fusion then supplies the square root of the positive affine-angle weight. These are source-preserving tensor identities, with all phases retained. The length frame has a polynomial original clock co-source, as proved in [the independent source calculation](actual_length_gauge_clock_source.md). This does not estimate the norm of the completely contracted clock state. Indeed [a complete figure-eight sector](actual_figure_eight_clock_gram_obstruction.md) shows why a diagonal norm on those clocks is insufficient for the sharp volume comparison. ## 1. The typed length frame Set `q=exp(pi*i/N)`, `Q=q^2`, `d=N-1`, and F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a|, L_a=s_a^2/N, A_a=L_a^(1/8), D_a=A_a^2=s_a^(1/2)/N^(1/4). Root complementation gives, exactly, s_a s_(d-a)=N, A_a A_(d-a)=1, D_a D_(d-a)=1. (1) For an actual root interval put B_l(X,Y;a)=product_(r=0)^(l-1)(X-Q^r aY), b_l(X,Y;a)=B_l(X,Y;a)/D_l. (2) The index `l` is an interval LENGTH. Equation (2) is not permission to apply a physical-head diagonal gauge to a fusion-relative index. For a fixed charged graph it is a scalar normalization of each actual polynomial block, so its effect on the full source is unambiguous. In particular `D_0=N^(-1/4)` and `b_0=N^(1/4)`: zero-length slots are retained, or their exact scalar is explicitly compensated. An empty unnormalized block may be omitted; its normalized version is not one. If `P_G` is a graph polynomial, let `D(G)=product_edges D_l`. Then P_G=D(G) P_(b,G). (3) Every original graph prefactor is multiplied by `D(G)` when the blocks are changed to `b`. For varying lengths this is a diagonal change of frame on explicit length registers. Interior inverse changes cancel; the actual source and all its length constraints must be transported. For singleton over-events every crossing has lengths `(d-h,h)`, so its factor in (3) is one. The original closure blocks contribute only `D_d=N^(1/4)` each; their exact source contractions cancel these factors in the closure-contracted presentation. Thus the original singleton clock co-source is polynomial, including its original feedback, pivots, framing and peripheral line. No knot value is used to choose this frame. ## 2. The normalized balanced star, including its full phase Take nonnegative `k_1+k_2+k_3=d`, put `l_i=d-k_i`, and assume `|a_i|=1`. The [proved actual star identity](actual_general_flow_fusion.md#3-balanced-star--triangle-identity) has outer triangle B_(k_3)(X_1,X_2;Q^(k_2+1)a_1/a_2) B_(k_1)(X_2,X_3;Q^(k_3+1)a_2/a_3) B_(k_2)(X_3,X_1;Q^(k_1+1)a_3/a_1). Define `T(k)=k(k-1)/2` and w(k)=1/(s_(k_1)s_(k_2)s_(k_3)), u(k,a)=(-1)^(k_1+k_3) *Q^[T(k_1)+T(k_3)-k_2]*q^(k_1 k_3) *a_1^(k_2)a_2^(k_3)a_3^(k_1). (4) Here `|u|=1`. The sine-binomial identity [l choose r]_Q=q^[r(l-r)] s_l/(s_r s_(l-r)) and (1) give the original star scalar `N w(k) u(k,a)`. Changing all six interval blocks according to (2) therefore gives [Z^d] product_i b_(d-k_i)(X_i,Z;a_i) =N^(-1/2) u(k,a) product_triangle b_k. (5) Indeed the normalizer ratio is product_i D_(k_i)/D_(d-k_i) =product_i D_(k_i)^2 =1/[N^(3/2)w(k)]. (6) This proves (5) at every level, including zero lengths and coincident outer variables. It is a polynomial identity, valid inside ANY polynomial exterior paired by the original socle coefficient. There is no change of selected period and no positive-trace assumption. More generally the normalization `B_l/A_l^theta` changes the scalar to N^(1-3theta/4) w(k)^(1-theta/2) u(k,a). (7) Thus `theta=1` gives `N^(1/4) sqrt(w) u`, while the frame (2), `theta=2`, makes the star scalar polynomial and independent of the angles in modulus. Formula (7) explains precisely where the full binomial is moved; it has not been discarded. Let `v_old,v_new` be the boundary coefficient vectors of (5) in ANY common positive Hermitian boundary metric `H`. Then <v_old,H v_old>=N^(-1)<v_new,H v_new>. (8) The stronger rank-one Gram equality follows as well. The same `H` must be used on the typed outer boundary on both sides; replacing it by unrelated positive metrics would require their actual adapters. ## 3. Parallel fusion produces the positive angle weight For `L+M<=d` the ordered intervals concatenate exactly: B_L(X,Y;a) B_M(X,Y;aQ^L)=B_(L+M)(X,Y;a). In the same frame (2), b_L(a)b_M(aQ^L) =N^(1/4) sqrt(|[L+M choose L]_Q|) b_(L+M)(a) =N^(3/4) sqrt(w_N(L,M,d-L-M)) b_(L+M)(a), (9) where `w_N(a,b,c)=1/(s_a s_b s_c)` and `a+b+c=d`. The local identity `|[a+b choose a]_Q|=N w_N(a,b,c)` is exact. All interval roots and reversal phases remain in their stated places. In particular (9) is a genuine square-root positive-angle amplitude, not an identification of an unnormalized star with its square root. For a full block, `b_d=N^(-1/4)B_d`. Its arbitrary-exterior reproducing contraction therefore has polynomial cost `N^(-1/4)` times the original unit monomial. A saturated full-block loop retains its exact finite geometric sum; short loops are not declared tame. A fixed valid reduction program made from (5), (9), full-block contractions and explicit interval reversals has scalar equal to a power of `N`, a retained unit phase, and the product of the square-root angle weights from its parallel fusions. A tame terminal pairing and a proved geometric incidence certificate would turn such a program into a sharp comparison. Existence of that program and certificate for all original clock graphs, or for a broad knot class, is not proved here. ## 4. A compatible anchor metric and its compulsory dual weight One useful coefficient metric on a single anchor is ||X^a||^2=m_a=s_a/sqrt(N). (10) The coefficient of `X^(L-r)Y^r` in `b_L(X,Y;a)`, for `|a|=1`, has squared norm in the tensor product of (10) N^(-1/2) |[L choose r]_Q| =sqrt(N) w_N(r,L-r,d-L). (11) This follows by multiplying its squared coefficient by `m_r m_(L-r)`; no phase is changed. Its sum over `r` is therefore an actual positive affine-angle partition up to a power of `N`. The trivalent anchor co-source `lambda_d(X^aY^bZ^c)=delta_(a+b+c,d)` has squared dual coefficient weight 1/(m_a m_b m_c)=N^(3/2)w_N(a,b,c), a+b+c=d. (12) Equations (11)--(12) must both be retained. Merely using (11) and declaring the anchor contraction a unit functional loses its dual angle weight. The metric `m_a=s_a` instead changes only the displayed powers of `N`. It does not remove the exponential weight. These exact local Gram identities provide a concrete special inner product for the user's Cauchy proposal. The remaining requirement is a coherent GLOBAL estimate of the normalized network energy with its actual dual contractions. The complete clock-sector example linked above rules out obtaining that estimate from a diagonal clock norm alone; it does not rule out a non-diagonal Gram retaining cancellation. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_length_normalized_star_gram.py): full normalized polynomial stars and phases, parallel fusion, and both coefficient/dual angle-weight identities.

title: Analytic transport through a regular modulus crossing
text: # Analytic transport through a regular modulus crossing 28 October 2026. This gives a local marked-action upper bound for a holomorphic recurrence at a modulus crossing where its eigenvalues are DISTINCT and nonzero. The proof constructs an exponentially accurate diagonal form by elementary matrix identities and Cauchy estimates. It needs no exact solution, source overlap, formal WKB summation theorem or pointwise dominance assumption. The sufficient condition compares a COMPUTABLE analytic remainder barrier with the width of the marked classical actions. It always holds on a sufficiently short regular crossing window. Extending it over a whole knot orbit still requires a global action-barrier comparison; mere single-valued calibration of an action does not prove that. Actual real ramification and singular leading coefficients are outside this local theorem. ## 1. Explicit analytic data Write epsilon=1/N and x_(j+1)=x_j+epsilon on a fixed real interval I. Let U_R denote its complex stadium of radius R. Suppose T_N and T_0 are holomorphic on U_(2R), uniformly bounded, and ||T_N-T_0||_(U_(2R))<=C_0 epsilon. (1) Assume T_0 has a supplied holomorphic eigenbasis V_0 there: V_0^(-1)T_0V_0=D_0=diag(lambda_1,...,lambda_d), ||V_0||,||V_0^(-1)||<=K, |lambda_i|>=m>0, |lambda_i-lambda_k|>=delta>0. (2) These are bounds on specified coefficient functions. For a classical companion, V_0 has columns (1,lambda_i,...,lambda_i^(d-1))^t, so all data are directly checkable on its normalized spectral branches. An actual recurrence as in [the whole-source spectral theorem](actual_macroscopic_a_spectral_upper_bound.md) satisfies (1) on any such regular fixed domain, uniformly on its small complex-q source circle. An unverified classical polynomial alone does not supply that actual quantum premise. After the exact change by V_0, put B_N(z)=V_0(z+epsilon)^(-1)T_N(z)V_0(z). Cauchy's estimate gives B_N=D_0+O(epsilon) on U_R. Initially set D=diag B_N, R_N=B_N-D. The diagonal gap is at least 3delta/4 for large N and ||R_N||<=C epsilon. All constants below are uniform. ## 2. Exponentially accurate diagonalization, with its proof There are explicitly bounded constants sigma>0,C and holomorphic V_N,D_N,R_N on U_(R/2), with D_N diagonal, such that EXACTLY V_N(z+epsilon)^(-1)T_N(z)V_N(z)=D_N(z)+R_N(z), ||V_N-V_0||+||V_N^(-1)-V_0^(-1)||<=C epsilon, ||D_N-D_0||<=C epsilon, ||R_N||<=C exp(-sigma N). (3) The shifted identity is asserted where both z and z+epsilon belong to that neighborhood; this includes every real step across I. The one-dimensional case has no off-diagonal part and is immediate. Here is a constructive proof with quantitative constants. Maintain ||D||<=M and diagonal gap g=delta/2; take M larger than twice the initial diagonal bound. If R is off diagonal with norm eta, solve [D,X]=-R, diag X=0, X_(ik)=-R_(ik)/(D_(ii)-D_(kk)), ||X||<=a eta, a=d/g. On a stadium narrowed by Delta>=2epsilon, Cauchy gives ||X(z+epsilon)-X(z)||<=2a eta epsilon/Delta. With X^+=X(z+epsilon), (I+X^+)^(-1)(D+R)(I+X)=D+F, F=(I+X^+)^(-1)[(X-X^+)D+R X]. (4) This is an exact identity. If a eta<=1/2, its new off-diagonal norm is bounded by eta_new <=[8Ma epsilon/Delta+4a eta] eta. (5) Its diagonal change is O(eta^2). To see the latter without losing a derivative, (X-X^+)D is off diagonal. Its contribution to diag F therefore requires the extra factor (I+X^+)^(-1)-I=O(eta). The other term RX already has size O(eta^2). Choose a fixed c<=min(R/8,R/(128Ma)), p=floor(cN), Delta=R/(2p). For sufficiently large N the starting eta is at most 1/(32a). Equation (5) then decreases eta at least by a factor 1/2 at EVERY step. The accumulated diagonal change is O(sum eta^2)=O(epsilon^2), so the stated bound M and gap g persist. The p domain losses total R/2 and Delta>=4epsilon, so all exact shifts are legitimate. The basis is the product of I+X at each step. Since sum ||X||<=2a eta_0=O(epsilon), it and its inverse are I+O(epsilon). The final off-diagonal is O(epsilon*2^(-p)). For example one may use sigma=(c log 2)/2. (6) All bounds are derived from (1)--(2), not an unknown solution. They are conservative, not optimal conversion exponents. The same construction is holomorphic in additional parameters wherever those uniform premises hold, including the actual tiny complex-q circle. ## 3. A checkable action-width criterion Normalize the real marked actions at the left endpoint a of I: A_i(x)=integral_a^x log|lambda_i(t)| dt, W=max_(x in I)[max_i A_i(x)-min_i A_i(x)]. (7) Suppose W<sigma. Then the EXACT product P_N of T_N across I satisfies limsup (1/N)log||P_N||<=max_i A_i(b), (8) where b is its right endpoint. Every specified input and output with subexponential norms has the same upper bound. This is a product bound, not merely a prediction from formal critical points. Proof. Let d_(i,j) be the diagonal entries of the actual D_N(x_j), and put G_0=I, G_(j+1)=D_N(x_j)G_j, all diagonal. Uniformly in j, log |(G_j)_(ii)|=N A_i(x_j)+O(1), (9) by (3), nonvanishing in (2), and the ordinary uniform Riemann estimate. The remaining EXACT recurrence after G_j has factors I+E_j, E_j=G_(j+1)^(-1)R_N(x_j)G_j. Equations (3), (7), and (9) give ||E_j||<=C exp[-N(sigma-W)]. There are O(N) steps, so their product is I+O(N exp[-N(sigma-W)]). Consequently P_N=V_N(b) G_n [I+O(N exp[-N(sigma-W)])] V_N(a)^(-1). This proves (8) and gives an exponentially small relative matrix remainder after the explicitly marked diagonal propagation. The exponential anisotropy of G_j is RETAINED and estimated by W; it is not asserted to be a tame positive full-space metric. In fact the same proof pins down the WHOLE singular-value vector. Let A_(1)(b)>=...>=A_(d)(b) be the sorted endpoint actions. Under the stated barrier, bounded invertible endpoint frames and the I+o(1) middle factor give, for every k, log sigma_k(P_N)=N A_(k)(b)+O(1). (9a) Use the elementary singular-value inequalities for multiplication by a bounded invertible matrix on both sides of the diagonal G_n. Thus all partial sums satisfy the corresponding asymptotic log-majorization, and every fixed continuous convex function of the normalized log singular values has the endpoint-action limit. This conditional pinching is stronger than a convexity estimate. It does not make the barrier follow from Karamata, and does not prove a nonzero overlap for the selected scalar source. For finite N there is a more flexible certificate: construct (3) and the diagonal G_j, compute bounds e_j>=||G_(j+1)^(-1)R_NG_j||, and use ||P_N||<=||V_N(b)|| ||V_N(a)^(-1)|| max_i |(G_n)_(ii)| product_j(1+e_j). (10) Proving sum_j e_j=o(N) suffices. These quantities use only the explicitly constructed local diagonalizers and scalar diagonal products, not the unknown exact vector solution or its final scalar. ## 4. A distinct-root modulus crossing is locally harmless For two branches suppose |lambda_1(x_*)|=|lambda_2(x_*)|, while the eigenvalues themselves stay separated as in (2). On I=[x_*-ell,x_*+ell], let |d/dx log|lambda_1/lambda_2||<=L. Then |A_1(x)-A_2(x)|<=L ell^2 throughout I. Thus L ell^2<sigma is a sufficient condition for (8), even if the larger modulus switches at x_*. The bound applies also to distinct REAL roots of opposite sign. No positive real weights are introduced. The analytic data may be fixed on a neighborhood of x_* first; sigma is then independent of the shortened ell. Hence a sufficiently short crossing window always meets this condition. For more than two regular branches use W<=2ell max_(i,k) sup_I|log|lambda_i/lambda_k||. All quantities are checkable from a specified classical curve and actual analytic recurrence. For a simple root of F(x,L), partial_x Log lambda=-F_x/(lambda F_L), which bounds L. A calibrated Bloch/peripheral action may supply the A_i, but (7) still requires the explicit quantitative width comparison. This does not contradict the [Gaussian conversion example](analytic_two_channel_conversion_counterexample.md). On its whole interval the conversion has positive gain even though the complete branch actions vanish. Its global width cannot satisfy the sufficient barrier comparison. On a sufficiently short regular window the theorem gives precisely the local estimate (8). An exponentially small local conversion can still grow after a long external propagation; it cannot be discarded in later gluing. ### A verified action-coordinate radius can replace the Euclidean one The proof also works in a supplied univalent holomorphic coordinate w=zeta(z). Assume the transformed matrices and basis obey (1)--(2) on an action-plane neighborhood of radius R_w, and the EXACT shifted coordinate map f_epsilon(w)=zeta(zeta^(-1)(w)+epsilon) is holomorphic there with |f_epsilon(w)-w|<=V epsilon. In (4) set X^+=X(f_epsilon(w)). Cauchy's estimate changes (5) only by replacing epsilon/Delta with V epsilon/Delta. Hence one may use c<=min(R_w/(8V),R_w/(128MaV)), sigma=c log2/2. (11) The actual sampled recurrence and the real actions (7) are unchanged; no continuum substitution for a discrete step is made. This follows from a verified analytic coordinate and shift map, not a formal replacement of the independent variable. At a distinct-root crossing, an appropriately marked zeta(z)=integral Log(lambda_i/lambda_k) dz has nonzero derivative unless that MARKED logarithm vanishes. It is therefore a valid local coordinate on a sufficiently small domain. Its analytic inverse may be bounded by excluding its actual action-plane critical values and singularities. This gives a CHECKABLE action-domain version of the remainder barrier. It does not identify the optimal barrier with the nearest calibrated collision action, or show that a zero regulator jump implies the global width inequality. Those stronger connection statements are still unproved. ## 5. What finite gluing additionally requires On overlapping regular domains with the SAME marked V_0 and the same iteration (4), two truncation depths give compatible frames: their ratio is I+O(exp[-min(sigma_1,sigma_2)N]) on a smaller overlap. Indeed their factors are literally the same up to the smaller depth; every additional X is already exponentially small there. This proves an actual overlap statement without choosing an unspecified exact WKB solution. It does NOT justify resetting every local action to zero and then freely splicing its best endpoint. In global action coordinates, each off-diagonal error and overlap correction acquires its FULL factor exp[N(A_k-A_i)]. A sufficient finite-gluing condition is a strict positive margin between each domain's exponential remainder barrier and those globally calibrated action differences, including the overlap locations. More flexibly, one may verify the weighted finite-N certificate (10) on the full assembled blocks. Across genuine spectral ramification V_0 and its inverse need not be bounded, so (1)--(6) no longer apply. Equality of absolutely calibrated regulator values at a ramification point is useful geometric information, but does not itself prove a quantum connection estimate. An action-coordinate refinement controlling that connection, rather than the conservative Euclidean sigma, remains necessary for the proposed general endpoint theorem. Thus the proved local result is (3)--(8), including regular modulus crossings and an explicit analytic barrier. No general two-bridge or whole-knot geometric bound is claimed until the actual operator, boundary source and global conversion margins are verified. The original-source Cauchy recovery remains exactly that of the macroscopic spectral theorem. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_local_analytic_transport.py) checks the exact iterative identity, separated-root contraction, bounded frame and weighted product reconstruction on analytic model matrices. These are supplementary checks, not an actual quantum-operator or global ramification calculation.

title: Independently long fillings of signed octahedral belt stacks
text: # Independently long fillings of signed octahedral belt stacks 29 October 2026. Root and independent global full-proof reviews passed. This records the precise theorem and its proved quantum, peripheral, regulator and geometric inputs together; the review statement describes the internal proof audits, not external peer review. ## 1. The actual family and statement Fix n>=1, a word epsilon of length n in {+,-}, and an integer a. Use the two literal mirror/reversed pieces D_+,D_- of the [octahedral stack construction](actual_balanced_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md), with ONE retained outer complete circle and the actual outer R^a. Denote this ACTUAL augmented link by B_(epsilon,a). It has n inner crossing circles and one outer belt. Its complement is complete hyperbolic of volume2n v8, by its exact regular-cell/collar proof. Choose ANY subset I of those n+1 auxiliary circles. For each i in I use its preferred meridian and crossing-disk longitude to fill the primitive slope mu_i+p_i lambda_i, for fixed nonzero integers p_i. Equivalently perform the literal1/p_i surgery/full-twist substitution in the original oriented diagram. Circles outside I remain components with their literal color N/L_N; this is NOT p_j=0, which would meridionally fill and remove them. Denote the resulting link in S^3 by J_(epsilon,a,I)(p). There is a source-dependent finite P such that, whenever min_(i in I) |p_i|>P, the actual filled complement is hyperbolic and its ORIGINAL single-cut reduced Kashaev evaluation satisfies lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|K_N(J_(epsilon,a,I)(p))| =Vol(S^3 minus J_(epsilon,a,I)(p)). (1) For I empty this is the already proved COMPLETE stack theorem, with no filling threshold. For nonempty I the threshold may depend on I; for a fixed stack take the maximum over its finitely many subsets if desired. The limits include every parity and composite level. The slopes may have independent signs and arbitrarily unequal lengths. They are fixed before N tends to infinity. No numerical value of P, uniformity as n or a grows with N, or arbitrary branched-graph theorem is claimed. Full twists preserve the main permutation. When ALL n+1 circles are filled, J is a KNOT for odd a and has TWO components for even a. For a proper subset its unfilled auxiliary circles remain: the total is n+2-|I| for odd a and n+3-|I| for even a. ## 2. Whole ORIGINAL quantum source, not a formal critical value The exact color expansion inserts every R^(-2p_i) using the original ordinary mixed circles L_j and the complete Hermite filling coefficients. It retains the marked cut, original pivot, full half-Cartan and all dimension endpoints. Coefficient mass is polynomial for each fixed slope. No closed auxiliary component is assigned an extra modified dimension. The [inner auxiliary-color theorem](actual_belt_stack_auxiliary_color_inner_packet.md) proves source-fixed nonzero analytic packets through the quarter- index transition, for the ACTUAL colors j_i=N-h_i. Its exact finite factorial completion agrees with the actual physical low core on the grid, with a quantitatively retained exponential replacement error in a faithful norm containing every first Casimir normal. The nonzero RP band and the ENTIRE physical inner-color complement have strict gaps, for every fixed n>=1. The [outer squared-kernel theorem](actual_outer_color_squared_kernel.md) retains the actual full-Hermite outer ordinary color. Its exact double-pole kernel kills the dangerous false h≈N Fourier alias; it proves the remaining outer-color complement gap, together with a fixed-complex-neighborhood, separately even packet for ALL n+1 circle colors. This is not a spectral eta=meridian guess. Write p and q for the numbers of plus and minus pieces and m=q-p+a. In x_i=h_i/N its local source action has phi(x)=n v8/pi - pi x_0^2/[n-im] +(pi/2)sum_(i=1)^n(-1+i sigma_i)x_i^2+O_4, sigma_i=+1 for z, -1 for z^sharp. The real quadratic part is strictly negative in every color. The ENTIRE source cube complement is gapped, not just the individual box coefficients. Thus the hypotheses of the [general original-source long-filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) hold. Restrict every unfilled color literally to h_j=0/L_N and apply only the original filling functionals indexed by I. The exact complex packet, nonzero amplitude, negative real Hessian and entire-cube complement gap restrict to these coordinates. It proves a NONZERO full-source asymptotic, and the selected point tends to the complete source point as min_(i in I)|p_i|->infinity. The empty subset instead uses the already proved nonzero complete-stack asymptotic directly. Fixed normal jets, endpoint currents and all nonleading charge sectors are controlled by that proof before its conclusion. ## 3. The selected point is an actual marked representation The [typed character composition](actual_belt_stack_typed_character_composition.md) supplies the group/flag lift which is essential after the source estimate. Its input is the source-selected internal critical root, not an arbitrary branch of a trace polynomial. The local pair matrices a,b,A=ba remain bounded and irreducible through A's parabolic trace -2. The selected inner box, its sharp type and every actual bare R interface satisfy their literal threaded Hurwitz equations and ordinary-pivot flag conditions. At the outer seam, TWO original nested main-head snakes reverse dual tensor order and invert the main meridian paths. Every incident mixed crossing is transported through the SAME original Hopf duality, including its full Cartan and nilpotent factors. The auxiliary cut/pivot and unrestricted marked co-source stay on their original side. This proves the actual outer disk word P_0=A^(-1), not a word selected from a matching cusp derivative. Irreducibility uniquely gives C_0=K_tot at closure. All complete white and BOTH inner shaded face maps match the regular octahedron certificate, as full three-vertex maps. The actual signed pants collars and outer R^a match too. The outer generator is then uniquely forced by closure to be the geometric one. Consequently the ENTIRE complete representation is the positively oriented holonomy of the ACTUAL B_(epsilon,a), not only a representation with matching flags, trace coordinates or Hessian. Let z_i=Log H_i and G be the actual logarithmic source primitive, with its real Cartan/spin constant retained. The preferred flagged peripheral data at ALL n+1 auxiliary circles are exactly M_i=exp(-z_i/2), lambda_i=-exp(-ell_i), ell_i=partial_(z_i)G. (2) For the outer circle ell_0=eta=Log(-w). The preferred minus sign is fixed by the original ordinary pivot and the disk framing. Simultaneously inverting both generators and swapping their common flag is equivalent; inverting only one is not. All surviving main meridians are noncentral parabolic, so BOTH small logs at each unfilled main cusp are zero, including the merged odd-a cusp. ## 4. The source action is the absolute regulator Keep the spin term in Gbar=G-pi i sum z_i. The actual source and preferred peripheral data give u_i=-z_i/2, v_i=pi i-ell_i, dGbar=2 sum_i v_i du_i, D_src=Im G-sum_i Re z_i Im ell_i. (3) The developed fundamental chain for the SAME marked representation has Bloch boundary -2 sum M_i wedge lambda_i. Its elementary Bloch--Wigner differential equals dD_src, including its factor2. Both sides have complete value2n v8 by the full geometric anchor. They therefore agree on the connected selected germ. No equality of an unproved transformed dilogarithm list is assumed. The exact source filling equations are z_i+2p_i ell_i=2pi i m_i, m_i=+1 or -1, i in I, z_j=0, j not in I. (4) Separate exact evenness gives ell_j=0 for every unfilled auxiliary coordinate, even as all the other colors vary. Its actual peripheral group remains noncentral parabolic near completeness. Its kept quadratic chirp is sum_(i in I)(z_i-2pi i m_i)^2/(4p_i). On(4) its imaginary part equals -sum_i Re z_i Im ell_i. Hence the imaginary FULL filled source action is exactly the marked representation volume D_src. This establishes the volume normalization, not just a numerical quadratic/cusp comparison. ## 5. Primitive completion supplies equality with hyperbolic volume The small geometric squared-eigenvalue logs are U_i=-z_i, V_i=-2ell_i, U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i m_i, i in I, U_j=V_j=0, j not in I. (5) Thus the filled slope has its actual primitive2pi angular period. The preferred SL longitude sign in(2) is kept before passing to these small geometric logs. A mere exponentiated PSL identity would not establish this unit winding. The actual selected representations and peripheral flags tend to the now identified complete geometric ones as the chosen slopes become independently long. For each filled coordinate separate evenness implies ell_i divisible by z_i, so z_i=0 would contradict (4). The full geometric completion theorem therefore applies to these source-selected representations. Its explicit logarithmic torus/tube construction adds a smooth core at each primitive slope, with no missing axis sheet.
