The compact core and every unfilled main AND auxiliary cusp remain positive and complete. This constructs the COMPLETE hyperbolic metric on the actual filled topology; it is not merely a nearby incomplete metric. The oriented fundamental class and the two-way Gromov-volume comparison identify its regulator with the actual hyperbolic volume. Combining this with the NONZERO whole-source asymptotic and (3)--(4) proves(1). ## 6. Scope and review ledger The theorem expands a cyclic one-belt source family. It does not assert an arbitrary six-port tensor estimate, arbitrary branched augmentation, or the volume conjecture for every fixed bridge number. The possible overlap of these actual belt-stack diagrams with known Whitehead-chain families remains a coverage caveat; no novelty claim about a literature family is used in the proof. Underlying independent replays: complete boundary packet; full inner mixed-color packet and gap; exact outer squared source; literal all-sign/outer-twist stack matrices and geometric collars; all white and shaded local face maps; exact nested main snakes with transported signed full-Cartan mixed coupons; primitive log completion and spin-preserving regulator. The detailed typed/marked proof is the linked composition note. Root and independent global full-proof reviews passed, including the any-subset restriction: unfilled colors remain literal L_N, their two geometric logs vanish by exact separate evenness, and the primitive completion leaves those cusps complete. These are internal independent analytical audits and exact finite checks, not a claim of external peer review.

title: The source point is the Casson--Rivin maximum for the actual filling
text: # The source point is the Casson--Rivin maximum for the actual filling **Current scope and direct geometric input.** The [whole-color improvement](actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.md) lowers the odd-width threshold to s>=9. The [direct ideal-chart certificate](actual_pretzel_positive_ideal_angle_certificate.md) constructs a compatible positive ideal subdivision of the ACTUAL half-twisted cells and verifies the full edge/peripheral rank. Thus the variational proof for this class no longer requires a general ideal triangulation existence theorem. The [general source certificate](source_volume_casson_rivin_certificate.md) and [independent tangent audit](source_angle_stationarity_critical_audit.md) isolate precisely why stationarity holds on the entire angle slice. 29 October 2026. This records the variational equality argument requested by the user. The relevant volume is Vsrc_s(p), not the larger complete augmented volume V_s. The angle constraints must be those of the actual filled slopes. A maximum for the unfilled cusp problem would not prove the desired equality. The geometric completion inputs are the [positive-core construction](actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md), the [primitive angle certificate](actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.md) and the [log-link/tube lemma](long_pretzel_equality_critical_audit.md). Their proofs and independent reviews now accompany this note; stationarity is not substituted for smooth end completion. The [completion audit](long_pretzel_volume_equality_completion_audit.md) records the full original-source equality and its exact scope. ## 1. The essential established quantum inputs For each fixed odd s>=9 and independently sufficiently large fixed signed integers p_i, the [whole original source theorem](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md) with the subsequent [width improvement](actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.md) gives Kraw_N=N^(3/2) exp[-is*pi*(N-1)/4] kappa^(-sum p_i) D_s(p) exp[N A_s(p)] (1+O_(s,p)(1/N)), D_s(p)!=0. The original reduced Kashaev invariant has the same absolute value. Thus its limit already exists and equals Vsrc_s(p)=2pi Re A_s(p). The steps that matter for this conclusion are: 1. Exact source transformations retain the original marked derivative channels, all colors, peripheral factors and Cartan phases. 2. The inner sums are combined coherently before estimating them. The global alias/core gap controls every color outside the cusp corridor. 3. The corridor has an exact complex analytic packet, not merely a pointwise real-grid approximation. This permits the contour estimates. 4. The exact filling transform retains every endpoint current. Its zero charge vanishes and its minimal nonzero signed charges add. This establishes the nonzero coefficient for the entire source. 5. The [literal port lift](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md) and [marked regulator comparison](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) supply an actual representation rho_p of the filled knot group and the absolute identity Vsrc_s(p)=Vol(rho_p), with the complete oriented augmented holonomy as anchor. Neither Cauchy alone nor existence of a classical stationary point establishes steps2--4. They are already supplied by the linked analytic proofs. The present task is the classical equality for this selected representation. ## 2. Obtain a positive ideal angle point from the selected source Let Y_s be the original complete augmented link complement. Choose a fixed positive geometric ideal triangulation T of Y_s. The [direct subdivision certificate](actual_pretzel_positive_ideal_angle_certificate.md), sections 1--3, supplies it from the actual face-labeled polyhedra: normalized light lifts are preserved by every white and shaded face pairing, and a finite compatible affine subdivision gives nonflat ideal tetrahedra. This uses no general triangulation existence theorem. Here "positive" means every oriented tetrahedron has shape in the upper half-plane; it is stronger than a topological ideal triangulation. The direct finite-center completion proof does not depend on this all-ideal existence input, but it supplies the customary Casson--Rivin angle presentation used in this note. Transport the finitely many developed ideal vertices of T using the actual source representation rho_z and its selected peripheral flags. At z=0 this is exactly the geometric developing configuration. A peripheral flag tends continuously to its noncentral parabolic flag: in a bounded matrix frame the eigenspace kernel has rank one at the limit, so it admits a local continuous, indeed holomorphic, choice. Every vertex orbit is well defined because its peripheral stabilizer fixes the chosen flag. All cross-ratios of the finitely many tetrahedra therefore vary continuously from strictly positive shapes. Shrink the parameter neighborhood once so every shape remains positive and nondegenerate. The actual representation identities telescope to the complex edge gluing equations. The edge angular sums are continuously close to 2pi and are integral multiples of 2pi, hence are exactly 2pi. The marked peripheral products are the actual eigenvalue multipliers. The selected filling points approach z=0 uniformly as max_i |p_i|^(-1) tends to zero. One threshold therefore puts ALL independently signed sufficiently long tuples in this fixed positive shape neighborhood. No comparability between different slopes is used. Denote their positive angle points by theta_p. ## 3. The correct affine volume problem includes the filled slopes For each tetrahedron write its positive angles as alpha,beta,gamma, with alpha+beta+gamma=pi. Let V_T(theta)=sum_t [Lambda(alpha_t)+Lambda(beta_t)+Lambda(gamma_t)], Lambda'(a)=-log(2sin a). The edge constraints are the usual linear equations with sum2pi at each edge. Fix their original angle and peripheral log lifts, continued from the complete triangulation. In projective geometric coordinates the actual auxiliary logs are U_i=Log(M_i^2)=-z_i, V_i=Log(lambda_i^2), centered at completeness,=-2ell_i. Their imaginary parts are affine real-linear functions of the tetrahedral angles in this fixed marking. The old SL longitude sign is retained in the quantum/regulator comparison; it is not an extra geometric rotation here. By the primitive-angle certificate the selected all-positive unit charge has U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i. (1) Other minimal signed charges replace the right side by -2pi i m_i, |m_i|=1, on their corresponding eigenflag marks. It suffices to use the all-positive charge, whose nonzero contribution is already proved. Define A_p to be the positive angle polytope satisfying the tetrahedral and edge equations, the REAL linear filling-angle constraints Im U_i+p_i Im V_i=-2pi, i=1,...,s, (2) and Im U_0=0 on a chosen primitive meridian of the remaining main cusp. The latter cusp is actually fully parabolic in rho_p, so U_0=V_0=0. The source point theta_p belongs to the INTERIOR of this affine slice. The full nonlinear holonomy equations are not being imposed as convex constraints. Only their imaginary, angle-linear parts define A_p. The real parts will give stationarity of volume. ## 4. The source equations imply stationarity on the entire angle slice Set x_t=Log z_t and y_t=Log z_t'', z_t''=1-z_t^(-1), with Im x_t=alpha_t and Im y_t=gamma_t. The sine rule gives Re x_t=log(sin beta_t/sin gamma_t), Re y_t=log(sin alpha_t/sin beta_t). For EVERY infinitesimal angle variation, not merely a variation through geometric solutions, direct differentiation gives dV_T(delta theta)=sum_t [Re x_t delta gamma_t -Re y_t delta alpha_t]. (3) Let E be the real space of edge Hamiltonians in the standard shape symplectic space Omega=sum dx_t wedge dy_t. Both the real logarithmic shape vector of a gluing solution and any tangent satisfying the edge angle equations lie in E^perp. The already established [boundary pairing](bloch_lift_and_boundary_torsor.md), summed over the boundary tori, reduces Omega there to Omega_red=-(1/2)sum_i dU_i wedge dV_i. Distinct tori have zero intersection pairing; on each torus the primitive peripheral rows have pairing -2. Thus at theta_p equation(3) becomes the boundary formula for arbitrary angle tangents dV_T(delta theta) =(1/2)sum_i [Re V_i delta Im U_i -Re U_i delta Im V_i]. (4) This is not obtained by restricting the derivative to the smaller variety of full complex gluing solutions. The coisotropic pairing justifies its use for every tangent of A_p. For each filled cusp, the real part of(1) says Re U_i=-p_i Re V_i. Its contribution to(4) is therefore (1/2)Re V_i [delta Im U_i+p_i delta Im V_i]=0 by(2). The main cusp contributes zero because U_0=V_0=0. Consequently dV_T(theta_p)|_(T_theta_p A_p)=0. (5) This is the full constrained critical-point condition requested in the Casson--Rivin argument. It uses the actual filled slopes and their centered integer angles, rather than the unfilled cusp maximum. ## 5. Strict concavity makes this the unique global maximum On one tetrahedron, in coordinates alpha,gamma with beta=pi-alpha-gamma, the negative Hessian is [[cot alpha+cot beta, cot beta], [cot beta, cot gamma+cot beta]]. (6) Its determinant is1. Its first diagonal entry equals sin(gamma)/(sin(alpha)sin(beta))>0. It is positive definite on the entire positive angle simplex. Summing proves strict concavity of V_T on every affine angle slice, including A_p. For any other point of the closure of A_p, the straight segment from theta_p stays positive until its possible final endpoint. Along it the first derivative starts at zero by(5), and the second derivative is strictly negative unless the point is unchanged. Continuity of Lambda at the boundary then gives V_T(theta)<V_T(theta_p), theta!=theta_p. (7) Thus the source point is the UNIQUE global maximizer of the full filled-slope angle polytope, including its boundary. No gradient-flow convergence assumption or numerical maximum is required. ## 6. Smooth completion identifies the maximum with hyperbolic volume The value of the positive developed fundamental triangulation is V_T(theta_p)=D(beta(rho_p))=Vsrc_s(p). (8) Here the absolute marked regulator comparison fixes the constant; one is not defining an unknown source action to be volume. For completeness, the geometric content behind the generalized Casson--Rivin conclusion is proved directly by the companion notes. The positive finite-center deformation supplies a local hyperbolic metric on the same compact core. Its auxiliary cusp links are positive Euclidean similarity tori. After placing their chosen flags at infinity, the second common affine fixed point q escapes to infinity near the complete structure. The finite link development avoids q. Therefore Log(dev-q) gives a nonsingular translation structure on a COMPACT torus. Its flat metric is complete, so its universal developing map is the whole complex plane, with its actual rank-two period lattice. The end contains a full punctured hyperbolic tube. The [primitive-angle certificate](actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.md) proves that its actual meridian period is exactly -2pi i, not that integer merely modulo2pi. Hence the tube completes to a smooth solid torus with the specified primitive slope. The main cusp stays complete. The [tube lemma](long_pretzel_equality_critical_audit.md) proves both the degree-one statement and the finite-volume completion. The resulting complete oriented metric g_p is on the ACTUAL filled knot complement. Its holonomy is rho_p. This supplies the geometric equality certificate that strict concavity or scalar PSL holonomy alone would not provide. The user's Gromov-norm observation gives a short final comparison. Apply the independently proved [sharp representation-volume inequality](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md) with the specified hyperbolic metric g_hyp as domain and g_p holonomy as target. Then reverse their roles using the same oriented topological marking. Fundamental chains have degree one in both directions, so Vol(g_p)<=Vol(g_hyp), Vol(g_hyp)<=Vol(g_p). No separate unproved equality case of the norm inequality is invoked. These two inequalities prove Vsrc_s(p)=max_(theta in A_p) V_T(theta) =Vol(g_p)=Vol(S^3 minus K). (9) ## 7. Quantum conclusion and quantifiers Combining(9) with the whole-source asymptotic and the independently audited positive-core, primitive-period and tube certificates proves the requested original-invariant equality: lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|<K>_N|=Vol(S^3 minus K). With the later whole-color improvement, the class is each fixed odd width s>=9, all independently sufficiently large fixed signed p_i, the original boxes R^(-(2p_i+1)), and the standing hyperbolicity assumption. The common threshold may increase to place the selected source points inside the fixed geometric neighborhood. There is no upper bound on width across the class, no comparability or common-sign condition on the slopes, and no restriction to prime levels or one parity. This note does not assert the quantum limit for all hyperbolic knots or for slopes growing with N. ## 8. Literature coverage, not a proof premise The [Futer--Gueritaud survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.0440) describes Casson--Rivin's critical-volume characterization of hyperbolic structures. That classical variational framework is established territory; this note does not claim to invent it. The contribution needed for this project is verifying its hypotheses for the point selected by the ENTIRE original quantum source, with the actual filled slopes and marked logarithms. Equations(3)--(7) and the companion geometric completion arguments are proved here rather than imported from the survey. The geometric ideal-triangulation input used for this angle presentation is the previously audited argument of [Ge, version1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27635v1); the independent finite-center completion route avoids making that input necessary for the final volume equality itself.

title: A nonzero asymptotic for the whole original long-pretzel source
text: # A nonzero asymptotic for the whole original long-pretzel source **Width extension, 29 October.** The [varying-radius alias estimate](actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.md) now supplies the full-color gap for every fixed odd s>=9. All local packet and filling inputs used here already hold there, so the theorem and its geometric equality extend to those widths without changing the invariant or signed-slope quantifiers. The older s>=25 argument below remains as the original assembly with its coarser sufficient bound. 29 October 2026. The full original source, with ALL auxiliary colors and original normal terms, now has a nonzero selected asymptotic for every fixed odd pretzel width s>=25 and every independently sufficiently large fixed signed twist tuple. This is a quantitative whole-source survival theorem. Its rate is specified by the exact source action. The separate [geometric completion theorem](actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md) now proves that this rate equals the filled hyperbolic volume. Its [Casson--Rivin presentation](actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) identifies the source point as the unique filled-slope volume maximizer. The equality uses these geometric proofs, rather than naming a formal source action a volume. ## 1. The unchanged invariant and the statement Use the literal original diagram, turns and marked cap from [the odd-pretzel source theorem](actual_odd_pretzel_augmented_transfer_source.md). There are s boxes R^(-(2p_i+1)), where s is odd. Its connectivity calculation proves that this is a one-component pretzel diagram. Let Kraw_N(p) be its original marked tensor contraction, including the full physical Cartan factors on every crossing. Its exact filling identity is Kraw_N(p)=kappa^(-2 sum_i p_i) sum_(j_1,...,j_s=1)^N [product_i beta_(j_i-1)^(-p_i)] A_(s,N)(N-j_1,...,N-j_s). (1) Here beta^(P) is the full Fourier--Hermite coefficient of r_N^(2P), and kappa=q^((N-1)^2/2), q=exp(pi i/N). The upper auxiliary bands and the Casimir normal derivatives are part of A and beta in (1). There is no replacement of this finite source by a positive model. For every fixed odd s>=25 there exists an integer p_s>0 such that for every FIXED tuple of integers |p_i|>=p_s, Kraw_N(p)=N^(3/2) exp[-i s pi(N-1)/4] kappa^(-sum_i p_i) D_s(p) exp[N A_s(p)] (1+O_(s,p)(1/N)), (2) with D_s(p) NONZERO. The action and amplitude are the explicit holomorphic functions defined in section2 of [the cusp-corridor filling theorem](actual_pretzel_cusp_corridor_filling_survival.md). The slopes can be positive or negative and can have arbitrarily different magnitudes. They are fixed BEFORE N tends to infinity. Both parities and all composite levels are included. The [original normalization calculation](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) applies here to the actual one-component marked diagram as well: its reduced Kashaev evaluation differs from Kraw only by its recorded unit framing character. In particular its absolute value is |Kraw|. The full one-cut modified ADO convention instead contributes the retained whole-germ value i^(N+3)/N at the main complete color. There is one such factor, not a new factor for each auxiliary color used in (1). Thus (2) specifies the original reduced invariant's growth, and not just an unnormalized comparison sum. ## 2. Exact assembly of the global and local estimates Write F0=V_s/(2pi) for the already calibrated COMPLETE augmented source rate. Choose a fixed sufficiently small corridor 0<=h_i=N-j_i<=H=floor(delta N) for which the exact analytic-packet and cusp-corridor theorems hold. The [global full-color theorem](actual_pretzel_global_alias_and_colored_source_gap.md) gives gamma>0 and a sequence epsilon_N->0, uniform over the ENTIRE complement of this color corridor, such that |A_(s,N)(h)|<=exp[N(F0-gamma+epsilon_N)]. (3) Replacing delta by a slightly smaller positive value handles the integer floor without changing this statement. The theorem includes every intermediate color, the even-level middle color j=N/2, the whole RP band, and the original value-plus-normal source functional. Its sufficient width condition is V_s/(2pi)>(s-1)v_8/pi + (1/2)log(4+sqrt(15)), which is proved for all odd s>=25. No small-color unitarity claim is used: the alias itself can grow exponentially, but its proved rate is small enough for (3). The exact full-normal filling coefficients satisfy sum_(j=0)^(N-1) |beta_j^(-p_i)|<=2N(1+|p_i|). Apply this to the complement in (1), BEFORE any limiting operation. All its kappa factors have modulus one. Its absolute contribution is therefore at most product_i[2N(1+|p_i|)] exp[N(F0-gamma+epsilon_N)]. (4) Inside the corridor the independently proved source-preserving filling theorem supplies exactly (2), with nonzero coefficient, for all independently sufficiently large |p_i|. In that theorem all color and Fourier endpoint terms have fixed positive source gaps. The high-charge estimate has a gap independent of the largest slope; this is essential when the |p_i| are not comparable. The exact source includes no zero Fourier charge. Its 2^s all-unit signed charges add, and all other local charges have a strict gap. The same theorem gives Re A_s(p)->F0 uniformly as all |p_i| tend to infinity. Increase the common threshold p_s so that Re A_s(p)>F0-gamma/2 whenever every |p_i|>=p_s, and so that the fixed corridor theorem also applies. For each such fixed tuple, (4) is exponentially smaller than its nonzero corridor asymptotic. Adding it cannot cancel the leading coefficient, and its relative error is eventually O(1/N). This proves (2) for the WHOLE original finite sum (1). ## 3. The rate and its subsequent geometric equality Define only as notation Vsrc_s(p)=2pi Re A_s(p). Then the theorem proves an actual limit for the original invariant: lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|<Pretzel(2p_1+1,...,2p_s+1)>_N| =Vsrc_s(p). (5) The displayed knot notation uses the source's crossing convention R^(-(2p_i+1)); globally mirroring the convention changes phases but does not change this absolute-value statement. Let tau_s=(1+exp(2iu_s))/2, u_s=atan(sec(pi/s)). The exact action calculation gives Vsrc_s(p)=V_s-2pi^2 Im(tau_s) sum_i |1+2p_i tau_s|^(-2) +O_s(sum_i |p_i|^(-4)). (6) More fundamentally, A_s is the value of the analytic source phase Psi(z)-2pi i sum_i(p_i z_i^2+z_i) at its selected nondegenerate critical point, with Psi the explicitly defined Fourier Legendre transform of the actual mixed-color action. Formula (6) is a consequence, not a substitute for that exact action. The subsequent geometric completion proves Vsrc_s(p)=Vol(S^3 minus Pretzel(2p_1+1,...,2p_s+1)). (7) The [geometric comparison and completion](actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md) match the actual auxiliary meridian and preferred longitude, construct the filled-knot representation rho_p, and prove Vsrc_s(p)=Vol(rho_p)=Vol(S^3 minus K). The positive core and primitive2pi tubes give a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric with holonomy rho_p. This closes equality(7), not merely the earlier upper-bound checkpoint. The actual fundamental-chain regulator and smooth completion, rather than agreement of one cusp derivative, establish it. Neither an uncontrolled complementary color sector nor an assumed nonzero cycle coefficient remains in(2). The separate geometric argument is explicitly linked so that equality(7) is not hidden in the name of the source action. ## 4. Verification and its scope The global complement proof and the corridor proof have each passed independent analytic reviews, including signed unequal slopes, the even-level middle color, and the paired high-charge endpoint currents. The assembly above has also passed an independent review. Fresh root replays of all four supporting audits passed: - `audit_actual_pretzel_global_alias_and_colored_source_gap.py`: exact physical band identities, normal coefficients, spectral ellipse, frozen blocks, binomial sum and the rational width bound. - `audit_actual_pretzel_exact_analytic_color_packet.py`: actual marked-source decompositions and exact complex packets. - `audit_actual_filling_source_fourier_endpoint_gap.py`: full-normal kernels, exact contour currents and charge transforms. - `audit_actual_pretzel_cusp_corridor_filling_survival.py`: original filling coefficients and signed Gaussian density/phase calibrations on controlled analytic packets. The analytic-packet calibrations in the last audit are not numerical proofs of the pretzel asymptotic. The actual-source hypotheses and uniform asymptotic estimates are proved in the linked notes. None of these finite checks alone supplies geometric equality(7); that conclusion uses the separate geometric completion proof.

title: Positive geometric deformation and smooth filling of the selected source
text: # Positive geometric deformation and smooth filling of the selected source **Subsequent quantum scope extension.** The [improved full-color bound](actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.md) lowers the required odd width to s>=9. The geometric argument below already applies there and is unchanged. Its diagram-independent generalization is [the general geometric theorem](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md). 29 October 2026. The selected long-filling representation is realized by a complete, positively oriented finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the ACTUAL filled pretzel complement. The construction starts with the explicit four-antiprism cellulation and uses finite face and cell centers. It does not assume that an arbitrary ideal topological triangulation has a positive geometric realization. Together with the already proved full original-source asymptotic and marked regulator comparison, this gives full hyperbolic-volume equality for every fixed odd width \(s\geq25\), with all signed twist parameters independently sufficiently large and fixed before \(N\to\infty\). The proof below identifies the selected representation geometrically; a representation-volume UPPER bound or convergence of its volume alone would not prove this conclusion. ## 1. The precise geometric and source inputs The [explicit augmented geometry](actual_augmented_pretzel_geometric_volume.md) constructs the original half-twisted augmented link from two convex ideal polyhedra \(\mathcal P_s\), each the double of an ideal right-angled antiprism. Its labeled face pairings, edge cycles and cusp tori are those of the original source, and the complete volume is \(V_s\). The [literal port and anchor theorem](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md) supplies a family \(\rho_z\) of representations of that ACTUAL augmented-link group, with its specified main and auxiliary peripheral eigenflags. It proves: * \(\rho_0\) is the positively oriented complete geometric holonomy, by every white and both shaded face maps; * the main meridian stays noncentral parabolic; * the auxiliary meridians and preferred disk longitudes are \(C_i,P_i\), with a common specified eigenflag and the retained SL sign; * the selected source filling point approaches this complete point uniformly as \(\max_i|p_i|^{-1}\to0\), and kills exactly the primitive slopes \(\mu_i+p_i\lambda_i\) in PSL(2,C). This family is a direct verified group/peripheral construction, not an inference from a scalar eigenphase or an unspecified character-variety component. The original cap order and the orientation-preserving reverse traversal are retained. The [primitive-period theorem](actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.md) fixes the continuous LOG SIMILARITY holonomies near completeness: \[ U_i=\Log M_i^2=-z_i,\qquad V_i=\Log\lambda_i^2\text{ centered at completeness}=-2\ell_i, \] \[ U_i+p_iV_i=-2\pi i m_i,\qquad |m_i|=1. \tag{1} \] The source's selected all-unit charge, not just its exponentiated relation, is used in (1). The SL longitude sign is not counted as an additional uncentered \(2\pi i p_i\). ## 2. A fixed positive triangulation of the ACTUAL complete cellulation Choose a finite point \(O_P\) strictly inside each of the two convex complete polyhedra. For every paired original face, choose one finite point \(F\) in the relative interior of one face and put the center of its partner at the point prescribed by that face isometry. This is one choice per face ORBIT, not two unrelated choices. Each original face is a convex ideal polygon. Join its center to every ideal edge, and cone every resulting triangle to \(O_P\). The resulting finite tetrahedra have vertices \[ (O_P,F,v_j,v_{j+1}), \tag{2} \] with two finite and two ideal vertices. Every tetrahedron is strictly positive with its cell's induced orientation: \(F\) is interior to its face, \(v_jv_{j+1}\) is an edge, and \(O_P\) is strictly on the inner side of that face plane. Convexity makes these face fans and cones a decomposition of the original polyhedron. The paired face fans match EXACTLY, including shaded outer-label exchanges. There are \(24s\) tetrahedra in the two polyhedra. Their only ideal vertices are the original cusp lifts. This is a geometric triangulation of the actual complete manifold, allowing finite vertices. No assertion about a positive all-ideal subdivision is needed. Finite centers may, for example, be chosen by normalized positive Lorentz sums of ideal vertex lifts in a chosen face/cell and then transferred to a paired face by its isometry. All choices are fixed before deformation. ## 3. Equivariant deformation gives a locally hyperbolic core Work in the topological universal cover of this fixed triangulation. Choose one representative of each FINITE vertex orbit and give it its old finite point, or any continuous nearby point. For every other lift define its position by \(\rho_z\)-equivariance. Finite vertices have trivial deck stabilizer, so this assignment is well defined. Assign each ideal vertex its specified peripheral fixed flag, and propagate it equivariantly. This is well defined because its entire peripheral subgroup fixes that flag. The preferred flags vary continuously, indeed analytically on the marked chart, at the complete point. For the auxiliary cusp the given eigenvalue is \(M_i=H_i^{-1/2}\); its eigenspace is the kernel of \(C_i-M_iI\), a rank-one matrix even at the complete NONCENTRAL unipotent limit. Thus no singular diagonalizing frame is used. The same statement holds for the noncentral main parabolic meridian. There are finitely many tetrahedra, faces and local stars modulo the deck group. Only finitely many group words occur in their vertex assignments. Their developed vertices are consequently uniformly close to the old ones for \(z\) in one fixed sufficiently small neighborhood. Every tetrahedron in (2) stays strictly positive and nondegenerate. Straighten it to the convex geodesic tetrahedron with its assigned vertices. Shared faces match by EXACT hyperbolic isometries: their three vertices are the same equivariant points, including every finite face center. In a fundamental-domain description the transition is precisely the corresponding \(\rho_z\) face word. Positivity and closeness keep the two tetrahedra on opposite sides of a common face. Thus there is no fold in a face interior. Here are the remaining local checks; positivity alone would not justify ignoring them. **Edges.** Develop the finite cyclic star of a nonideal edge into \(\mathbb H^3\). It returns to the SAME developed face and edge point because its contractible edge-loop word is the identity in the actual manifold group, hence also under \(\rho_z\). More precisely the ENTIRE face-transition product telescopes to \(\rho_z(1)=1\); this is stronger than merely returning one edge endpoint or one normal ray. There is no residual translation or dilation along the edge. In a normal disk, its positive sectors therefore have total angle \(2\pi k\), with integer \(k\). Their angles depend continuously on the finitely many developed vertices. At completeness \(k=1\), so it remains one in the chosen neighborhood. This includes finite--finite, finite--ideal and ideal--ideal edges; dihedral angles are constant along each geodesic edge. The full edge star is an ordinary hyperbolic neighborhood, without a cone or screw defect. **Finite vertices.** The finite topological vertex link is a 2-sphere. Its positive spherical triangles glue isometrically, and the preceding edge check gives angle \(2\pi\) at every link vertex. Its development is therefore a local isometry to the unit sphere. Compactness and geodesic path lifting make it a covering of that sphere. Since the sphere is simply connected, it is one-sheeted. Hence the vertex star is an ordinary hyperbolic ball; no hidden branched spherical link occurs. It follows that every finite point of the ideal-vertex-deleted manifold has a genuine oriented metric of curvature \(-1\). Its holonomy is the original \(\rho_z\), by construction. This proves the required local developing geometry directly, without assuming a deformation or local-rigidity theorem. ## 4. The actual ideal stars have positive similarity links Send a selected cusp flag to infinity by a Mobius frame chosen continuously near its complete frame. In each incident tetrahedron, the three faces through infinity are vertical planes. The horizontal projections of the three remaining vertices form a NONDEGENERATE Euclidean triangle, because the tetrahedron is positive. They give its horospherical link triangle. The face transitions fixing infinity are orientation-preserving complex similarities \(\zeta\mapsto a\zeta+b\). Thus these positive triangles form a similarity structure on the compact topological cusp torus. At its vertices the same developed edge star has winding one and angle \(2\pi\), so this is a local Euclidean coordinate structure even at those vertices. There is no cone or branch point in the affine link. In the continuously chosen flag frame, all vertices of a fixed finite fundamental union of link triangles remain finite and uniformly bounded. The finite-center vertices stay finite; the other ideal vertices remain distinct from the chosen flag. Their projected triangles and any fixed meridian/longitude edge paths consequently have uniformly bounded developed images and Euclidean lengths. This verifies the geometric input used to identify the small logarithmic periods in the primitive-period theorem, including for independently unequal filling lengths. The opposite face of an incident tetrahedron is not vertical: otherwise it would also contain the ideal point at infinity and all four vertices would be coplanar. It is a hemisphere, so over each projected link triangle the tetrahedron contains a vertical ray above a bounded lower height. These finitely many epigraphs provide the ACTUAL end, not merely a formal link at infinity. ## 5. Primitive tube completion, with no hidden covering multiplicity Apply the proved [compact-log and tube-completion lemma](long_pretzel_equality_critical_audit.md), sections2--4, to the similarity links just constructed. Its argument is recalled to specify every needed input. At an auxiliary end a meridian has affine form \(d\mapsto a d+b\), with \(a\to1\) and complete \(b\to W(1+ic)\ne0\). At the selected finite filling \(a\ne1\): separate evenness gives \(V_i=\tau_i(z)U_i\), while (1) excludes \(U_i=0\), and the logs are small. The common second fixed point \(q=b/(1-a)\) therefore exists and escapes to infinity near completeness. The bounded fundamental link triangles miss it; equivariance then shows that the ENTIRE link development misses it. On the simply connected link cover take \(f=\Log(d-q)\). The form \(df\) is invariant under deck translations and is everywhere nonzero. Hence \(|df|^2\) is a nonsingular flat metric on the COMPACT link torus. It is complete. Lifting straight Euclidean segments makes \(f\) a global isometry of its universal cover onto \(\mathbb C\). Its periods form an INJECTIVE rank-two lattice, rather than an unspecified covering of a punctured plane. After translating \(q\) to zero, \(d=e^f\). The actual epigraphs in section4 contain \(y>A|d|\), for some finite \(A\), because their lower heights divided by \(|d|\) are bounded on a finite fundamental link domain. The deck similarities multiply both by the same positive number. In cylindrical coordinates about the axis \(0\)--\(\infty\), this is the WHOLE punctured tube \[ 0<R<R_0,\qquad ds^2=dR^2+\cosh^2R\,dX^2+\sinh^2R\,d\theta^2. \tag{3} \] A logarithmic period \(L\) acts by \((X,\theta)\mapsto(X+\Re L,\theta+\Im L)\). The period of the primitive filled slope is exactly \(\pm2\pi i\) by (1) and the primitive-period theorem, NOT merely an exponentiated value one. Choose that primitive slope and a complementary longitude as a torus basis. The latter has nonzero real period because the lattice has real rank two. Adding \(R=0\) to (3) is therefore a smooth hyperbolic solid torus: its angular period is exactly \(2\pi\), and its core has the nonzero loxodromic screw period. Its meridian is precisely \(\mu_i+p_i\lambda_i\). There is no factor \(|m_i|>1\) producing a branched core, no zero winding, and no extra framing longitude. At the unfilled main cusp both affine multipliers are one. Its positive link is an ordinary flat translation torus; compactness again makes its development the Euclidean plane. Its end contains a full horoball quotient and is complete with finite volume. ## 6. A complete finite-volume metric on the original filled topology Choose all slopes sufficiently long that their selected source parameters lie in the fixed positive geometric neighborhood of sections2--4. The source solution is holomorphic in all \(\epsilon_i=1/p_i\) near zero, so a common threshold works whenever every \(|p_i|\) exceeds it, with either sign and NO comparability requirement. The source parameters are fixed before the quantum-level limit is taken. Complete every auxiliary end as in section5. The underlying topological operation is exactly Dehn filling by its prescribed primitive slope, and leaves the original complete main cusp. This is the actual pretzel knot with boxes \(R^{-(2p_i+1)}\), by the literal tangle and preferred-peripheral certificates. All original cap, spin and marking data agree. The resulting Riemannian metric is smooth of curvature \(-1\). Its complement of the standard ends is compact; the added solid tori are compact at bounded tube radius and the main horoball quotient is a complete cusp. Thus the whole metric is complete. Its volume is finite: there are finitely many finite-volume partially ideal tetrahedra, standard finite-radius tubes, and one finite-volume cusp. Its holonomy is exactly \(\rho_{\boldsymbol p}\). The complete simply connected developing cover is \(\mathbb H^3\). Indeed geodesic path lifting for a complete local isometry gives a covering of \(\mathbb H^3\), which is simply connected. Hence the developing map is a global isometry and the holonomy is discrete and faithful. This conclusion has been PROVED from the positive core and primitive tube; it was not inferred from killing a peripheral word or from proximity of two volumes. There is no need for a separate character-variety local-uniqueness theorem. The actual source critical solution is already the unique analytic selected solution in its marked small parameter chart. For that fixed holonomy the completed structure is \(\mathbb H^3/\rho_{\boldsymbol p}\), so changing auxiliary finite centers cannot produce a different complete metric. No assertion that all algebraic character components are this branch is used. ## 7. Hyperbolic-volume equality and the original invariant The [marked regulator comparison](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) and the finite compatible filling-chain argument prove \[ 2\pi\Re\mathcal A_s(\boldsymbol p) =\operatorname{Vol}(\rho_{\boldsymbol p}). \] Since the constructed complete metric has that holonomy and the same oriented fundamental chain, its geometric volume is precisely this value. If one starts with another complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the same oriented filled topology, apply the independently proved sharp representation-volume inequality in BOTH directions, with the identity-marked holonomies. The two inequalities force equal volumes. Thus no additional unproved volume-rigidity assertion or imported Mostow theorem is needed to identify this with the usual topological hyperbolic volume. Finally the [whole original-source asymptotic](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md) has a nonzero leading coefficient at BOTH level parities and all composite levels, with the actual original normalization. Combining it with the geometric completion gives \[ \boxed{\quad \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N} \log\left|\langle\operatorname{Pretzel} (2p_1+1,\ldots,2p_s+1)\rangle_N\right| =\operatorname{Vol}\bigl(S^3\setminus \operatorname{Pretzel}(2p_1+1,\ldots,2p_s+1)\bigr). \quad} \tag{4} \] Here \(s\geq25\) is any fixed odd integer, and the independently signed integer slopes are all sufficiently long and fixed before \(N\to\infty\). The construction itself proves hyperbolicity in this sufficiently long range. No statement for short slopes, smaller widths, growing width, or arbitrary knots is inferred. This completion is a geometric equality certificate. A Casson--Rivin ideal-angle interpretation requires its own positive ideal shape chart and modified filling constraints; it cannot be obtained by maximizing the old unfilled cusp slice. The direct positive finite-center metric and primitive end completion above do not need that additional chart. ## 8. Independent completion review Both independent companion reviewers read sections1--7 in full and reported PASS. Their checks included the finite face-orbit centers, strict tetrahedral positivity, the FULL identity edge transition (hence no axial dilation), spherical-link degree one, positive similarity-link triangles, bounded generator paths and actual epigraph ends. The primitive-log and compact-log/tube proofs were also independently read against these exact inputs. These are analytical proof checks; no finite numerical sample is substituted for positivity in a fixed neighborhood or the degree-one argument.

title: The selected long-pretzel filling has primitive angle 2pi
text: # The selected long-pretzel filling has primitive angle 2pi 29 October 2026. The actual unit-charge equation gives a primitive 2pi geometric meridian, not merely scalar PSL holonomy. The uncentered SL longitude log would give the WRONG angle. This note fixes the small geometric logs from the actual cusp development, proves their exact oriented core-length formula for independently signed slopes, and identifies the normal rotation without a hidden integer. The positive compact-core deformation and the resulting global tube completion are supplied by their separate geometric lemmas; scalar holonomy alone would not supply them. ## 1. Center the projective geometric logs before forming the slope The literal mixed-circle certificate fixes M_i=exp(u_i)=H_i^(-1/2), u_i=-z_i/2, lambda_i=-L_i^(-1), v_i=Log lambda_i=pi i-ell_i, z_i=Log H_i, ell_i=Log L_i, with all z_i,ell_i zero at the complete geometric point. The preferred longitude has SL eigenvalue -1 there. Its PROJECTIVE multiplier is nevertheless one. In a coordinate whose infinity is the selected peripheral eigenflag, the actual affine holonomy multipliers are M_i^2 and lambda_i^2. Their continuously small logs are therefore \[ U_i=2u_i=-z_i,\qquad V_i=2(v_i-\pi i)=-2\ell_i. \tag{1} \] Both vanish at completeness. This centering is fixed ONCE by the complete affine translation cusp, independently of the slope. It is not an opportunistic logarithm reset at the filling point. The positive original diagonal marking is mu_i=W_i(1+i c), lambda_i=2ic W_i, c=cos(pi/s), W_i>0, in its complete Euclidean cusp coordinate. Thus (dV_i/dU_i)(0)=2tau_s=2ic/(1+ic), Im(2tau_s)>0. (2) The basis is primitive: it is the actual meridian and boundary of the crossing disk, not half or twice that boundary. The retained R^(-1) is already in this mu_+ marking; no additional meridian shear is allowed. For the ACTUAL source equation of charge m_i, z_i+2p_i ell_i=2pi i m_i, equation (1) gives EXACTLY \[ \boxed{U_i+p_iV_i=-2\pi i m_i.} \tag{3} \] In contrast u_i+p_i v_i=pi i(p_i-m_i) is an UNCENTERED SL eigenlog. Its p_i*pi i term is the old longitude spin, not geometric winding about a new core. Doubling that expression and calling it a cone angle would be incorrect. Likewise using undoubled eigenlogs would incorrectly give pi instead of 2pi. ## 2. A uniform exact core-length and orientation identity Separate evenness of the original analytic source action implies ell_i=z_i a_i(z_1^2,...,z_s^2), a_i(0)=tau_s. Hence the ratio t_i(z)=V_i/U_i=2a_i(z_1^2,...,z_s^2) is holomorphic through z_i=0. On a fixed sufficiently small complex source neighborhood, Im t_i>=b>0. This remains true for the simultaneous selected fillings, regardless of the signs or relative magnitudes of their large p_i. Combining V_i=t_iU_i with (3), for REAL nonzero p_i, gives the exact formulas \[ U_i=\frac{-2\pi i m_i}{1+p_it_i},\qquad V_i=\frac{-2\pi i m_i t_i}{1+p_it_i},\qquad \boxed{\operatorname{Re}V_i =\frac{2\pi m_i\operatorname{Im}t_i} {|1+p_it_i|^2}.} \tag{4} \] The denominator cannot vanish because Im t_i>0. Thus each nonzero charge gives U_i,V_i nonzero and a genuine LOXODROMIC core generator: Re V_i has the sign of m_i. In particular it cannot be a nontrivial elliptic with an accidentally killed eigenvalue. At the selected unit charges the positive core length is length_i=|Re V_i|=2pi Im t_i/|1+p_i t_i|^2>0. There is no comparison between different slope sizes in this proof. The oriented logarithmic lattice is also fixed: \[ \operatorname{Im}(\overline U_iV_i) =|U_i|^2\operatorname{Im}t_i =2\pi m_i\operatorname{Re}V_i>0. \tag{5} \] Thus the two period directions are linearly independent over R, with the SAME orientation as the positive complete cusp. Reversing the unit charge jointly reverses U_i,V_i and the core orientation; it does not mirror the hyperbolic structure or change the slope. ## 3. The small source logs ARE the geometric angular lifts Here is the precise local lemma needed to exclude a hidden extra 2pi winding. Its input is the genuine positive similarity cusp-link deformation supplied by the positive-core construction, not an abstract representation with prescribed eigenvalues. Choose the moving peripheral eigenflag as infinity by a frame continuous at the complete cusp. Let the developed similarity cross-section have holonomy mu: w -> exp(U)w+A, lambda: w -> exp(V)w+B. On the complete limit A->W(1+ic), B->2icW, both nonzero. Develop the two primitive generator paths using a fixed finite cusp triangulation and a fixed basepoint. Their images and their Euclidean lengths stay uniformly bounded near completeness: each comes from finitely many continuously varying positive triangles. Call a common image bound R and length bound L. These are bounds in the continuous cusp frame, not a singular diagonalizing frame. For U!=0 sufficiently small, the common finite affine fixed point is k=A/(1-exp(U)). Commutativity makes it the fixed point for lambda too. Since A has a nonzero limit, |k| tends to infinity as U tends to zero, uniformly in all the other small parameters. In particular |k|>2R. Along either generator path the analytic logarithmic coordinate T=Log(dev-k) can be continued in the ball of radius R, which misses k. Its variation satisfies the elementary bound \[ |\Delta T|\le L/(|k|-R)\longrightarrow0. \tag{6} \] The endpoint affine holonomy gives exp(Delta T)=exp(U) or exp(V). Therefore Delta T-U or Delta T-V is an integer multiple of 2pi i. Both quantities tend to zero. For all sufficiently small parameters the ONLY possible integer is zero: \[ \boxed{\Delta_\mu T=U,\qquad\Delta_\lambda T=V.} \tag{7} \] This is pointwise quantitative; no connectedness of a punctured parameter domain or arbitrary lift choice is used. It rules out an added integer for EACH primitive generator before multiplying one by the large p. Because the finite source/port frame and the cusp triangles vary on one fixed neighborhood, the argument is uniform for independently signed large slopes. If only a PSL character were given without this geometric cusp-link development, the conclusion (7) would not follow from eigenvalues alone. The log-link/tube theorem uses precisely these periods. Its compact translation torus has no extra wrapping index because the primitive generators have periods U,V generating its full rank-two lattice. One must not infer a period lattice solely from the multiplier equations without the small-increment argument (6). ## 4. Primitive slope, actual angle, and the absence of branching The filled primitive curve is sigma=mu+p lambda: its first coefficient is one, so it is primitive in the ACTUAL torus basis. Take lambda as the complementary core curve. This is an integral basis change of determinant one. From (3),(7), its exact developed displacements in T are Delta_sigma T=-2pi i m, Delta_lambda T=V, Re V!=0. (8) For the angle normalization use H3 around the vertical axis above k. In upper-half-space coordinates set horizontal=k+exp(t)tanh(r)exp(i theta), height=exp(t)sech(r). Direct differentiation gives ds^2=dr^2+sinh(r)^2 dtheta^2+cosh(r)^2 dt^2. At fixed r, T=t+Log tanh(r)+i theta, so its periods ARE the axial/rotational displacements (Re T,Im T). Equation (8) has zero axial translation and angular displacement -2pi m. A small normal circle therefore has circumference 2pi |m| sinh(r)=2pi |m| r+O(r^3). (9) For |m|=1 the axis has the ordinary smooth 2pi neighborhood. For |m|=2 it is a 4pi branched neighborhood, although both cases have scalar PSL meridional holonomy. This is the rigorous discriminant that the scalar group relation alone cannot supply. In particular the selected |m|=1 channels give a smooth primitive filling. For m=1 the displayed meridian angle is -2pi; reversing the orientation of the SAME primitive filling curve gives +2pi. This is the usual orientation-reversing boundary attachment of a solid torus, not a reversal of ambient volume. Formula (5) keeps the positive cusp lattice orientation for either choice of signed slope. More explicitly, for either unit sign choose meridian_tube=-m sigma, core_tube=m lambda. Their angular period and axial length are respectively +2pi and |Re V|. Relative to the original oriented (sigma,lambda) basis the change has determinant -m^2=-1, exactly the boundary-orientation reversal required to glue an ORIENTED solid torus. This works for both signs of p without changing the orientation of H3. The exact holomorphic reversed-cap isometry jointly inverts both peripheral generators; it interchanges m=+1 and -1 and preserves (9). No mu_+ -> mu_- framing shear occurs. The ORIGINAL coherent source has no zero charge, and all 2^s unit signed charges were proved to add. Thus it is exactly the quantum selected channels, rather than an imposed primitive filling, that meet the smooth-angle condition. ## 5. Scope and the direct geometric lemmas used for completion The result proves the actual peripheral lift, loxodromic core orientation and primitive smooth-angle calibration, using the positive geometric cusp-link deformation near the established complete anchor. It does NOT infer a hyperbolic metric from a bare PSL representation. The independent [finite-center positive-core proof](actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md) now supplies the face-compatible local metric and these cusp links. The [log-link/tube completion proof](long_pretzel_equality_critical_audit.md) identifies the ENTIRE end with a standard punctured tube before adding its smooth core. Both constructions have passed this note's independent analytical review; no imported Dehn filling theorem is being assumed correct without proof. The final completion review checks the finite face-orbit centers and cell cones, exact identity of each contractible edge-star holonomy (including zero axis dilation), winding-one continuity, finite-vertex spherical covering degree one, ideal similarity links and actual vertical epigraphs. It also checks the signed surgery convention: straightening mu+p lambda uses phi'=phi-p theta and inserts -p full turns, so the original retained R^(-1) becomes R^(-(2p+1)). Thus the completed oriented manifold is the actual source's filled knot. Combined with the independently proved complete log-link and whole-source/regulator theorems, this is a FULL equality certificate on the unchanged class: each fixed odd s>=25 and independently sufficiently large FIXED signed p_i, with the full N sequence, both parities and composite levels. No slope comparability or all-ideal triangulation assumption is needed for this completion. It makes no assertion for small widths, short slopes, N-dependent slopes/width, or arbitrary hyperbolic knots. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.py) checks the exact spin/angle distinctions, signed independent core length and orientation identities, the small affine logarithmic increments, and the Fermi metric/circumference normalization.

title: The hyperbolic-volume upper bound for the full original long-pretzel invariant
text: # The hyperbolic-volume upper bound for the full original long-pretzel invariant **Subsequent equality, 29 October.** The [geometric completion proof](actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md) now proves rho_p is the holonomy of a complete positively oriented metric on the actual filled knot. The upper inequality below is therefore an equality on the SAME sufficiently long fixed signed class. See the [Casson--Rivin equality proof](actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) and [full completion audit](long_pretzel_volume_equality_completion_audit.md). This note retains the intermediate upper-bound argument as a dependency. 29 October 2026. This assembles the whole-source asymptotic, the literal representation/peripheral lift, and the marked regulator comparison. The upper bound uses the ACTUAL filled hyperbolic volume, with coefficient one. The equality required by the full volume conjecture is distinguished explicitly below. ## 1. Statement and scope For every fixed odd integer s>=25 there is an integer p_s>0 with the following property. Let p_1,...,p_s be independently chosen fixed signed integers satisfying |p_i|>=p_s, and let K be the original odd pretzel knot with boxes R^(-(2p_i+1)). Assume its complement is hyperbolic, as in the standing project hypothesis. Then the ORIGINAL normalized Kashaev invariant satisfies lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|<K>_N| =Vol(rho_p) <= Vol(S^3 minus K). (1) Here rho_p is an explicitly constructed boundary-parabolic PSL2(C) representation of the ACTUAL filled knot group. The limit exists, and its leading source coefficient is nonzero. Both level parities and all composite levels are included. The fixed slopes need not have comparable sizes or the same signs. The class has no upper bound on its number of twist regions, and each sufficiently long twist parameter varies independently. It is not a fixed-width twist family or a finite list of tested knots. No assertion for small widths or short slopes is inferred from (1). The hyperbolicity assumption is explicit. The proof below does not use an unproved claim that every displayed diagram is hyperbolic, or require a faithfulness theorem for rho_p in order to establish the upper bound. ## 2. The full original source supplies a nonzero limit The [whole-source survival theorem](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md) proves, including the ENTIRE original color cube, Kraw_N=N^(3/2) exp[-i s pi(N-1)/4] kappa^(-sum p_i) D_s(p) exp[N A_s(p)] (1+O_(s,p)(1/N)), D_s(p)!=0. (2) Its global bound includes all ordinary color bands, the even middle color, and every Casimir normal derivative. Its coherent filling estimate retains the zero-charge cancellation, all nonzero charges, paired endpoint currents and the exact original half-color weights. The unit charges add rather than being assigned an assumed cycle coefficient. All these statements are quantitative source estimates, not consequences inferred from classical stationary equations. The actual framing/cut normalization gives |<K>_N|=|Kraw_N|. The optional full one-cut modified convention contributes the kept factor i^(N+3)/N, with the same exponential rate. It follows that the left side of (1) exists and equals 2pi Re A_s(p). ## 3. Its selected point is an actual filled-knot representation The [source-selected mixed lift](actual_pretzel_mixed_regular_character_lift.md) derives the regular internal coordinates from the literal finite recurrence and verifies their stationary rational identities. The [full port and geometric-anchor theorem](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md) then constructs actual parabolic main meridians and auxiliary matrices C_i,P_i, with [C_i,P_i]=1, M_i=H_i^(-1/2), lambda_i=-L_i^(-1) on the same eigenflag. It verifies every original cap in the actual right-to-left multiplication order. The common w and the outer equation product_i U_i=1 close the full original diagram. This is a representation of that diagram's group, not a trace variety introduced independently of the source. The [preferred-longitude certificate](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md) proves that P_i is the disk-framed longitude, with no unrecorded meridian power. The minus in lambda_i is forced by the original auxiliary pivot. With continuous z_i=Log H_i and ell_i=Log L_i, the actual unit-charge filling equation is z_i+2p_i ell_i=2pi i. It gives C_i P_i^(p_i)=(-1)^(p_i-1)I, as a MATRIX identity on the regular nearby branch. Thus it kills the primitive filled slope in PSL2 and defines rho_p on the actual knot group. A particular SL2 lift may require a mod-two character change; no SL2 descent is needed for the PSL2 representation-volume bound. The main meridian remains noncentral parabolic, so its commuting peripheral image is boundary-parabolic. At the complete augmented point the same representation agrees with every white and shaded face pairing of the four-antiprism geometric construction. The absolute auxiliary translations also match the primitive disk longitude and positive diagonal meridian. The reversed cap traversal is accounted for by an explicit orientation-preserving holomorphic isometry, not by taking a mirror. This supplies the oriented geometric anchor V_s. ## 4. The source action is the absolute regulator of rho_p The [marked regulator comparison](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) keeps the preferred SL sign before centering. If G is the source action with G_(z_i)=ell_i, put u_i=-z_i/2, v_i=pi i-ell_i, Gbar=G-pi i sum_i z_i. Then dGbar=2 sum v_i du_i, and the marked regulator is Dsrc=ImGbar-2 sum Reu_i Imv_i =ImG-sum Rez_i Imell_i. (3) The actual fundamental Bloch boundary is -2 sum M_i wedge lambda_i. Its elementary differential agrees with (3), and the complete geometric anchor fixes their SAME absolute constant V_s. Thus Dsrc is the regulator of the representation constructed above throughout the selected connected local branch. The ORIGINAL Gaussian filling action is W=G+sum_i (z_i-2pi i)^2/(4p_i). At its critical point, Re z_i=-2p_i Re ell_i. Consequently 2pi Re A_s(p)=ImW =ImG+2 sum_i p_i Reell_i Imell_i =Dsrc. (4) No peripheral or endpoint correction is omitted in (4): the quadratic is precisely the one in the source-preserving filling formula, and the spin terms cancel only in their complete paired regulator expression. Finally compare the augmented and filled fundamental chains using one finite compatible triangulation of the truncated core and the attached solid tori. The proved axis-cusp homotopy first replaces the OLD filled-boundary data by an axis-valued map without changing the augmented regulator. Assign those boundary vertices and every new solid-torus vertex equivariantly to that SAME invariant axis. The killed primitive slope makes the assignment descend through the solid-torus fundamental group. Every added tetrahedron is collinear and has zero volume. The core plus solid-torus chain therefore computes the filled boundary-parabolic representation volume with no new constant. This proves 2pi Re A_s(p)=Vol(rho_p). (5) The boundary replacement uses the explicit O(Y^(-2)) homotopy estimate in [the general peripheral volume proof](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md), sections1--2. Merely assigning NEW vertices an axis flag while leaving arbitrary old boundary data would not justify (5). ## 5. Apply the independent sharp representation-volume estimate For an oriented complete finite-volume hyperbolic manifold X and a boundary-parabolic representation rho, the independently proved [representation-volume theorem](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md) gives |Vol(rho)|<=Vol(X). (6) Its proof averages finite regular tetrahedra, cancels all four face-homotopy errors by Haar invariance, and lets their volumes increase to the maximal ideal-tetrahedron volume. It does not assume a quantum volume conjecture or faithfulness of rho. Apply it to the actual hyperbolic filled complement and rho_p. Equations (2),(5),(6) prove (1). Thus the requested sharp full-original-source UPPER-BOUND milestone holds for the stated broad class. Equality in (1), and hence the full volume conjecture for that class, additionally requires proving that rho_p is the positive geometric Dehn-filling representation (or an equivalent equality argument). This theorem does not count that remaining geometric completion as already proved. It also makes no assertion for all hyperbolic or all alternating knots.

title: A whole-source spectral upper bound from macroscopic ordinary-color pointing
text: # A whole-source spectral upper bound from macroscopic ordinary-color pointing 28 October 2026. The actual source can be restarted at a positive fraction of the color orbit, rather than only at fixed small colors. This gives a quantitative upper bound for the FULL original Kashaev value in terms of the classical roots of a specified actual all-level operator. All root singularities and nearly singular steps are retained. There is no unproved lower bound on a nonzero cyclotomic denominator in this argument. The bound is proved below under an explicit classical-order condition. It is sharp geometrically when its displayed classical spectral integral is at most the hyperbolic-volume rate. That classical inequality, and verification of the relevant operator for a broad knot class, remain separate tasks. No broad volume-conjecture theorem is asserted here. ## 1. Actual inputs and the theorem Fix a k-bridge presentation with k>=2, and use the ACTUAL reduced colors C_j(q), q_N=exp(pi i/N), C_N(q_N)=K_N. The [positive macroscopic color window](ordinary_color_macroscopic_normal_jet_window.md) uses the original colored plat and its normalization. It bounds the colors up to J_N=1+floor((N-1)/k). (1) In addition to its polynomial fixed-jet bounds, the elementary complex arc argument in Section 2 below gives, for any fixed A>4, sup_(|s|<=2N^(-A)) |C_j(q_N exp(s/N))|<=N^C for 1<=j<=J_N. (2) Constants depend on the fixed diagram and A, not j,N. A fixed scalar multiple of N^C is harmless in every displayed polynomial bound. Choose a specified ACTUAL all-level annihilator, retaining its original peripheral factors and conventions: sum_(i=0)^d a_i(q,-q^j) C_(j+i)(q)=0, a_i in C[q^(+/-1),M^(+/-1)], d>=1. (3) Its fixed coefficients may lie in a number field; fix the intended complex embedding. The identity is the original polynomial color identity, not a conjectured quantization of a classical curve. Remove a common q-1 power if needed. The additional classical-order condition used here is a_d(1,M) is not identically zero. (4) Assume also that at least one a_i(1,M), i<d, is not identically zero. This excludes an identically nilpotent classical companion; no semisimplicity or generic eigenvalue separation is required. Let T(x) be the d by d classical companion, with shift rows and last row -a_i(1,M(x))/a_d(1,M(x)), where M(x)=-exp(pi i x), rho(x)=max{|L|: sum_i a_i(1,M(x))L^i=0}. (5) The finitely many leading-coefficient zeros are interpreted by improper integration. Then limsup_(N->infinity) (1/N) log |K_N| <= integral_(1/k)^1 log rho(x) dx. (6) More generally any actual family with polynomial complex source packets at colors j/N->a satisfies the same result with lower endpoint a. The bridge theorem supplies a=1/k without knowing K_N or any high normal jet. An identically zero K_N is assigned logarithm minus infinity. The exact Fourier energy E_N=|K_N|^2+O(N^C) consequently satisfies limsup (pi/N)log E_N <=2pi max(0, integral_(1/k)^1 log rho(x) dx). (7) The ordinary-color remainder used here is the independently proved original positive trace estimate. Formula (6) is already a scalar whole-source bound; (7) introduces no replacement model. ## 2. A tiny complex source disk from the real positive arc For j in (1), the actual 2k-plat gives the real-arc bound |C_j(exp(i theta))|<=j^(k-1), pi/(2N)<=theta<=pi/N. (8) At equality k(j-1)+1=N the upper endpoint follows by scalar Laurent polynomial continuity from below. One does not differentiate a singular path basis at the endpoint. The actual integral crossing formula bounds the Laurent degree of C_j in q^(1/2) by D<=C_K j^2. For zero-framed ordinary colors it is also harmless to use any fixed common angular denominator; the following estimates change by fixed constants. Here are details of the needed complex estimate. Put z=exp(i theta/h) for that fixed integer denominator h, so the function is Laurent in z with exponents between -D and D. Center the real arc at theta_c and write t=tan((theta-theta_c)/(2h)), z=exp(i theta_c/h)(1+i t)/(1-i t). Then p(t)=(1+t^2)^D C_j(z^h) is a polynomial of degree at most 2D. The symmetric real t interval is [-tau,tau], tau comparable to 1/N. Its supremum is at most (1+tau^2)^D j^(k-1)<=C_K j^(k-1). (9) Expand p(tau v) in Chebyshev polynomials. Each coefficient has modulus at most twice the supremum, by its elementary cosine integral. For a complex v with dist(v,[-1,1])<=delta<=1, |T_l(v)|<=exp(C l sqrt(delta)). (10) Indeed solve w+w^(-1)=2v, choose |w|>=1, and use T_l(v)=(w^l+w^(-l))/2. The elementary quadratic formula, compared with a point of [-1,1], gives |w|<=1+C sqrt(delta). For q=q_N exp(s/N), |s|<=2N^(-A), the complex angle differs from the upper arc endpoint by -i s/N. Thus the normalized v is within O(N^(-A)) of that endpoint. Equations (9)--(10) give |p(t)|<=C_K(2D+1)j^(k-1) exp(C_K D N^(-A/2)). (11) Since D=O(N^2) and A>4, this is polynomial. Also |t|=O(1/N), so |(1+t^2)^D| and its inverse are bounded by fixed constants. This proves (2). This argument bounds the ACTUAL entire initial color functions on the complex disk; it does not replace them by truncated Taylor series. That distinction will matter below. A Taylor approximation at s=0 need not cancel poles at OTHER nearby zeros of a leading coefficient. Using the original analytic source retains those exact cancellations. ## 3. One small circle avoids every tail denominator with polynomial cost Collect the s_0 distinct monomials of a_d(q,M). For a color j with j larger than a fixed constant, its restriction to the complex orbit is g_(N,j)(s)=a_d(q_N exp(s/N),-(q_N exp(s/N))^j) =sum_(l=1)^s_0 c_l (-1)^(b_l)q_N^(a_l+b_l j) exp[(a_l+b_l j)s/N]. (12) The frequencies lambda_l=(a_l+b_l j)/N are real and uniformly bounded for j<=N. They are distinct once j exceeds the q-exponent span: a collision of different M powers would force j to be bounded. Their pairwise differences have modulus at least 1/N. The first s_0 derivatives at zero form a Vandermonde matrix applied to coefficients whose moduli are the fixed nonzero |c_l|. The determinant is at least N^(-s_0(s_0-1)/2) in modulus and its adjugate is bounded. Consequently, for a fixed C_0, N^(-C_0)<=max_(0<=r<s_0)|g_(N,j)^(r)(0)|<=C_0. (13) Normalize g by this maximum. All normalized functions solve a constant coefficient ODE product_l(partial_s-lambda_l)g=0 with bounded coefficients and initial jet norm one. The first-order system form and its exponential series show that this is a compact family of entire functions, uniformly on compact disks. Every limit has initial jet norm one and is nonzero. We record the elementary local consequence carefully. There exist rho_0,c>0, depending only on s_0 and the frequency bound, such that each normalized function has at most s_0-1 zeros in |s|<4rho_0 and, after factoring all zeros zeta_l in |s|<3rho_0 with multiplicities, |g_normalized(s)|>=c product_l |s-zeta_l| for |s|<=rho_0. (14) For the zero count, otherwise take radii tending to zero and a compactly convergent sequence with at least s_0 zeros in each disk. The nonzero limit would have zero of order at least s_0 at the origin, contradicting its initial jet norm one. Shrink a resulting uniform radius to obtain 4rho_0. For the quotient bound, pass to a subsequence of the bounded number of zeros. On a circle between rho_0 and 2rho_0 avoiding their limits, the quotients converge uniformly, and hence inside by Cauchy's formula. A zero of the limit quotient inside rho_0 would, by the argument principle on a small surrounding circle, force an additional zero of the original functions there. All such zeros were factored. This contradicts a quotient minimum tending to zero. The possible zeros crossing |s|=3rho_0 stay away from the disk being estimated. Compactness therefore gives the positive uniform c in (14). There are at most (s_0-1)N zeros to avoid over ALL tail colors. For each remove a radial interval of radius N^(-A-2) around |zeta_l|. Their total length is O(N^(-A-1)), smaller than the length N^(-A) of [N^(-A),2N^(-A)]. Choose a radius r_N outside this union. Equations (13)--(14) prove, simultaneously for every tail color and every point on this ONE circle, |g_(N,j)(s)|>=N^(-C_A), |s|=r_N. (15) No Diophantine estimate on g_(N,j)(0) is used. A nonzero zero may lie arbitrarily close to zero inside the circle; the original source will cancel its apparent pole. Exact zeros at s=0 are retained as well. ## 4. Transfer through the entire tail and its singular regions Start at j_0=J_N-d+1. The initial companion vector consists only of colors j_0,...,j_0+d-1 covered by (2), and j_0/N->1/k. At every point on the circle in Section 3, propagate the exact companion for (3). Denote the individual matrices by T_(N,j)(s). Their entries have a polynomial bound from (15). Away from the finite zeros of a_d(1,M(x)), they converge uniformly, also uniformly in s on the circle, to T(x). On a fixed closed regular interval, a direct positive metric gives limsup (1/N)log ||product T_(N,j)(s)|| <=integral log rho(x) dx, (16) uniformly in s. To verify this without diagonalization, fix epsilon>0 and use H_epsilon(x)=sum_(n>=0)(T(x)^*)^n T(x)^n/ (rho(x)+epsilon)^(2n). On a compact matrix family this series converges uniformly (bound the powers by a resolvent on an intermediate circle), is continuous, and lies between I and C_epsilon I. In its norm a step costs at most rho(x)+epsilon+o(1); neighboring metric changes are 1+o(1), uniformly. Summing logarithms proves (16) after epsilon tends to zero. Include any isolated zero of rho in the exceptional set first. This argument is valid for repeated roots and nonnormal companions. We must also bound the steps near exceptional points, rather than delete them. Let m be a bound on the orders of the classical leading zeros. Outside distance N^(-epsilon_0) from them, with epsilon_0>0 sufficiently small, the coefficient error O(1/N) is less than half the classical denominator, and ||T_(N,j)(s)||<=C dist(j/N,Z)^(-m). (17) Here A>4 makes the extra s perturbation smaller than O(1/N). Inside those shrinking neighborhoods there are O(N^(1-epsilon_0)) steps; their polynomial bound from (15) costs exp(o(N)) in total. Between that neighborhood and a fixed radius delta, summing the logarithm of (17) costs at most C N delta(1+|log delta|)+o(N). (18) This follows by comparing the monotone logarithm with its integral on the color mesh; the shrinking core removes any near-grid anomaly. Isolated zeros of rho with nonzero leading coefficient have bounded matrix norm and cost O(N delta). Thus all exceptional neighborhoods have a rate tending to zero as delta decreases. Finally log rho is integrable. Upper root bounds use the rational companion coefficients. For a fixed nonzero lower coefficient a_i, the elementary-symmetric root formula gives rho^(d-i)>=|a_i/a_d|/binom(d,d-i). Orders of zeros of the fixed analytic functions on the compact arc are finite, so both upper and lower logarithmic bounds are integrable. Combining (16)--(18) and sending delta to zero gives the full-tail product bound with integral from 1/k to 1. ## 5. Recover the exact complete value, with every cancellation retained On the chosen circle the generic recurrence identity gives C_N(q_N exp(s/N)) =e_d^t [product_(j=j_0)^(N-d) T_(N,j)(s)] (C_(j_0)(q(s)),...,C_(j_0+d-1)(q(s)))^t. (19) The right side uses the original source. Although its factors may have poles INSIDE the circle, their full product in (19) is the actual Laurent polynomial on the left and is holomorphic there. Therefore ordinary Cauchy evaluation gives K_N=(2pi i)^(-1) integral_(|s|=r_N) C_N(q_N exp(s/N)) ds/s. (20) Its absolute value is at most the supremum on the circle. The initial packet is polynomial by (2), and the transfer product has the rate proved in Section 4. This proves (6). No source overlap, root-fiber inverse bound, or assumption that normal data at color N are small has entered the proof. ## 6. What is now a classical geometric question A sufficient, independently checkable condition for the sharp upper bound for a given actual operator is 2pi integral_(1/k)^1 log rho(x) dx<=Vol(S^3 minus K). (21) Together with (3)--(4), this implies the desired original-source limsup, not merely an auxiliary positive-state bound. Condition (21) is NOT asserted for an arbitrary annihilator: multiplying by extra operator factors can enlarge rho, and an actual operator's classical support has to be determined rather than assumed to be the geometric A-polynomial. For k=2, a possible geometric proof of (21) is a continuously selected dominant peripheral branch whose regulator starts at zero at x=1/2 and ends with absolute value at most Vol. One must verify its dominance throughout the interval, including any changes at the unit circle; switching freely between different regulator primitives is invalid. The estimate (6) itself requires none of those geometric assertions. This replaces an unspecified quantum boundary amplification by an explicit classical spectral integral, under the stated order condition. It does not yet verify (21) for a broad knot class or prove geometric survival. ### A verified limitation of the scalar envelope The independently derived [6_1 longitude quartic](six_one_classical_spectral_envelope_obstruction.md) has a certified transverse modulus crossing at x=5/6 between DISTINCT expanding eigenvalues. Hence rho is locally obtained by switching analytic branches; it cannot be identified throughout that interval with one fixed geometric branch. Its numerical half-integral has 2pi-scaled value about 3.44499, while the continued expanding branch integrals are about 3.16396 and 1.41511. These integral values are diagnostics, not certified volume comparisons or an actual quantum operator calculation. A separate [coherent classical-matrix diagnostic](classical_six_one_coherent_transfer_diagnostic.md) has rates well below the scalar envelope at increasing levels. This directs the next estimate toward phase-aware products and continuously marked branch actions. It does not license replacing the safe envelope in (6) by an unproved smaller number. In particular, proving (21) for ALL two-bridge curves by asserting one dominant branch would be an invalid next step. A further [exact analytic conversion example](analytic_two_channel_conversion_counterexample.md) shows that even replacing the scalar envelope by the maximum of complete marked-branch actions is NOT a general adiabatic theorem. With distinct nonzero roots, uniformly bounded analytic eigenframes and an O(1/N) coupling, both individual actions can be zero while the actual selected product has a positive exponential rate. The proof is a finite Gaussian sum with an exact Fourier expansion. A separate [polynomial-clock example](algebraic_clock_conversion_counterexample.md) has an exact binomial proof. Neither example is a knot operator. They show why a sharper bound must establish the actual source's conversion cost, rather than infer it from the classical roots and slow variation. ## 7. Checks and coverage [The actual-source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_macroscopic_a_spectral_upper_bound.py) propagates the original figure-eight colors from the midpoint around five tiny complex-q circles, through the full homogeneous recurrence, and compares every output with the independent finite color product. It also checks Cauchy recovery, the exact classical factor, and the nearby-pole example explaining why the entire initial source is needed. The general sparse-ODE zero argument is the proof in Section 3, not a conclusion from those finite examples. An independent agent reread the complete argument and freshly reran the audit: PASS. Its review specifically checked the compact ODE-family quotient bound, the common radius, the shrinking exceptional cores, the nonnormal metric estimate, logarithmic integrability, and Cauchy recovery with the original entire source. The scope qualifications in Sections 1 and 6 remain part of that verdict. Its separate 5_2 diagnostic computes a classical cubic from the actual Newton coefficient curve by the previously proved canonical map. The half-interval integral numerically equals its known volume rate, but that diagnostic does NOT certify an actual quantum operator or the classical geometric comparison. It is labeled accordingly. Coverage only: recurrence asymptotics and their connection with the volume problem are established research topics; see [Aptekarev--Dudnikova--Tulyakov (2021)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1134/S1995080221110056). Their introduction records earlier regularity hypotheses excluding colliding and zero roots; their paper also discusses the nonregular knot examples. This note makes no novelty claim and assumes none of their proofs. Its source-window, small-circle, singular-region and whole-value estimates are given above independently.

title: The actual marked line-circle pattern near the complete source
