title: Genuine scalar normals have vanishing exponential cost near the closing point
text: # Genuine scalar normals have vanishing exponential cost near the closing point 30 October 2026. The original Casimir polynomial and every fixed genuine moving-q derivative have an absolute upper bound of vanishing exponential rate on an ENTIRE small complex disk about z=2. This is larger than the shrinking zero-free disk of the [endpoint theorem](actual_matching_edge_polynomial_endpoint_control.md). Zeros may occur in the present fixed disk; no relative lower bound or canonical logarithm is asserted there. Use N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), zeta=q exp(epsilon), Q=zeta^2 and `0<=a<=floor(d/2)`. All polynomials and face factors are the original generic ones, before extracting any source normal. ## 1. All spectral denominators cancel in the finite Sears expression In the exact generic endpoint formula put z=Z+Z^-1, A=zeta^-1 Z^-1 Q^-d, B=zeta^-1 Z Q^(-d-a). The two spectral-dependent series denominators there are EXACTLY C=zeta Z Q^(d+1-a)=A^-1 Q^(1-a), zeta Z Q^(-d-a-1)=B. For the kth term, finite product reversal gives (A;Q)_a/(C;Q)_k =(-1)^k A^k Q^[k(2a-k-1)/2](A;Q)_(a-k), (B;Q)_a/(B;Q)_k=(BQ^k;Q)_(a-k). Consequently the exact source polynomial is the finite sum p_a(zeta,Z+Z^-1)=sum_(k=0)^a T_k(zeta,Z), T_k=(-1)^k A^k Q^[k(2a-k+1)/2] *(Q^-a;Q)_k^2 (zeta Z;Q)_k^2 *(A;Q)_(a-k)(BQ^k;Q)_(a-k) /[(Q;Q)_k^2(Q^-d;Q)_a(Q^(-d-a-1);Q)_a]. (1) The exponent of Q is an integer. Every denominator in (1) depends ONLY on Q and is a root unit in this actual range. Thus (1) is valid even when an uncanceled spectral denominator in the preceding Sears presentation vanishes. Each T_k is a Laurent polynomial in Z of degrees between -a and a, with regular generic-q coefficients. The full sum is the already proved polynomial in z; this assertion does not require any symmetry of an individual summand. At zeta=q,Z=1 the exact endpoint convolution says T_k(q,1)=b_k^2 b_(a-k)^2>0, b_n=product_(r=1)^n sin((r-1/2)pi/N)/sin(r pi/N), sum_k T_k(q,1)=p_a(q,2), 1/(4a+1)<=p_a(q,2)<=1. (2) ## 2. A uniform absolute bound on a fixed small disk There are absolute constants c,C,r0>0 such that for 0<r<=r0, |p_a(q exp(epsilon),z)| <=p_a(q,2) exp[C N sqrt(r) log(2+1/r)+C log N], |epsilon|<=c N^-3, |z-2|<=r. (3) In particular the upper exponential rate in (3) tends to zero as r decreases to zero, uniformly in the original row and both parities. Here is the estimate from the actual finite terms. Choose a solution of Z+Z^-1=z with `|Z-1|<=C sqrt(r)`, and take r0 small enough that |Z-1|<1/2. No holomorphic choice of this root over the disk is made. The identity (1) is pointwise valid for either solution. The denominators, Q-only numerator factors and q monomials in (1) have relative logarithmic change `O(N^2(1+log N)|epsilon|)`. Their factors have nonzero root exponent distances, and the harmonic bound is the same one proved for the endpoint unit products. A factor with Z dependence in its NUMERATOR instead satisfies |1-zeta^m Z^e|/|1-q^m| <=1+C N (|Z-1|+N|epsilon|)/dist(m,2NZ), where e=+1 or -1 and |m|<=4N. At the base point these distances are the nonzero odd distances 1,3,... in consecutive intervals. They occur with uniformly bounded multiplicity. The separate factor Z^-k costs at most exp(CN|Z-1|). For v>=0 the elementary integral comparison gives sum_(j=1)^N log(1+Nv/j) <=N[log(1+v)+v log(1+1/v)] <=C N v log(2+1/v), (4) with value zero at v=0. The first inequality uses the decreasing integrand log(1+Nv/x) on (0,N]. Apply (4) with `v=C(|Z-1|+N|epsilon|)`. The extra N|epsilon|<=cN^-2 costs at most O(log N); the same is true of the Q-only changes. We obtain a bound for EACH term, uniform in k, |T_k(q exp(epsilon),Z)| <=T_k(q,1) exp[C N sqrt(r) log(2+1/r)+C log N]. (5) Summing (5) uses the exact positive endpoint weights in (2). There is no replacement by a separately maximized summand, and no additional number-of-terms cost is required. This proves (3), including points where numerator factors vanish. Lower bounds away from z=2 are not part of this argument. ## 3. Genuine q jets and fixed spectral derivatives For each fixed nonnegative integer m, Cauchy on the SAME generic epsilon disk proves sup_(|z-2|<=r) |partial_epsilon^m p_a(q exp(epsilon),z)|_(epsilon=0) <=C_m N^(3m) p_a(q,2) exp[C N sqrt(r) log(2+1/r)+C log N]. (6) This differentiates (1), an identity of the original generic source. It does not differentiate a root-only positive replacement. For any additionally fixed spectral order s, applying Cauchy on a disk of radius r inside |z-2|<=2r gives sup_(|z-2|<=r) |partial_epsilon^m partial_z^s p_a|_(epsilon=0) <=C_(m,s) r^-s N^(3m) p_a(q,2) exp[C N sqrt(r) log(2+1/r)+C log N], (7) after changing C and restricting r<=r0/2. For fixed r, the factor r^-s has zero N-exponential rate. The tiny-endpoint theorem remains available if a chosen r itself shrinks so quickly that (7) is not the useful form of the bound. The original face scalar D_a and its inverse remain uniformly bounded on this epsilon disk by their canceled root-unit product estimate. Thus (3),(6),(7) also apply to the actual normalized scalar `D_a^-1 p_a`, with adjusted constants and the corresponding genuine product derivatives. ## 4. The bound is for a closing region, not for a contributing cycle The estimates allow the scalar factor and all fixed required normals to be bounded throughout a small closing region, rather than just at the point 2 or on a fixed compact of its limiting slit plane. They make no claim that this region is zero-free: the scalar roots are above 2 and can enter a fixed disk as N grows. The actual resolvent still has its own nearby spectral poles. Any bound on a closing part of the ORIGINAL contour must combine (6) or (7) with its actual resolvent estimate and retain the permitted contour and all residues. The present theorem by itself neither selects that contour nor proves geometric saddle dominance or a nonzero source contribution. Focused audit: [canceled original Sears terms, removable spectral denominators and genuine joint jets](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_polynomial_closing_region_bound.py). Primary-agent full analytical review: PASS. The reader checked the exact prefactor cancellations and exponents, all remaining root-unit denominators, the positive endpoint comparison, pointwise spectral lift, and genuine q/spectral Cauchy estimates. Independent full analytical review and fresh redirected audit: PASS. The second reader checked sections 1--4 and reproduced 168 generic identities, 224 removable-denominator cases, 108 genuine joint four-jet comparisons, 180 positive endpoint terms and 84 fixed-region samples at 100-digit precision. Neither review infers a zero-free fixed disk or a contributing contour.

title: Polynomial control through the target spectral endpoint two
status: Positive endpoint convolution and generic jets
text: # Polynomial control through the target spectral endpoint two 30 October 2026. The actual exceptional Casimir polynomial has a positive finite convolution at z=2. Its value is between an explicit reciprocal polynomial and one. An exact generic Sears representation then controls the whole polynomial, including its genuine moving-q derivatives, on a shrinking joint neighborhood of this endpoint. No contour deformation or saddle contribution is proved. Use the original polynomial p_a(zeta,z) from the [generic source identity](actual_matching_edge_geometric_target_polynomial.md), with N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), theta=pi/N and `0<=a<=floor(d/2)`. Every occurrence of a moving-q derivative below means zeta=q exp(epsilon), with the spectral variable z held fixed. ## 1. An exact positive endpoint convolution Define b_n=product_(r=1)^n sin((r-1/2)theta)/sin(r theta), b_0=1. Then the actual root polynomial satisfies p_a(q,2)=sum_(k=0)^a b_k^2 b_(a-k)^2. (1) In particular 1/(4a+1)<=p_a(q,2)<=1. (2) Here is a finite proof retaining the source normalization. At the root, the polynomial's generic 4phi3 becomes, at z=2, 4phi3(Q^-a,Q^(a+1),q,q; Q,Q,Q; Q,Q), Q=q^2. Apply the proved finite Sears identity with length a, retained parameter q, and d_S=e_S=Q. The result has numerator parameters `(Q^-a,Q^-a,q,q)`, denominators `(Q,qQ^-a,qQ^-a)`, and prefactor (q,qQ^-a;Q)_a/(Q,Q^-a;Q)_a=b_a^2. All denominators are units; the half-integer sine factors are never zero. The kth transformed term is [(b_(a-k)/b_a)b_k]^2. All q powers and signs cancel, giving exactly (1). This is an identity of the actual source polynomial, not a lower estimate based on a different factorial model. Since `sin x/x` decreases and sin x increases on (0,pi/2), (r-1/2)/r <= sin((r-1/2)theta)/sin(r theta)<=1. Thus `b_a>=product_(r=1)^a(r-1/2)/r`. The square of that last product is at least `1/(4a+1)`: induction uses (2a+1)^2(4a+5)-(2a+2)^2(4a+1)=1. Keeping k=0 in (1) proves the lower bound in (2). The upper bound follows from the already proved simple roots `rho_h>2`, since p_a(q,2)=product_h (rho_h-2)/(rho_h-2cos theta)<=1. ## 2. An independent quantitative separation of the roots The source Jacobi theorem gives J_a-2I=2 H D_a H+2sin^2(theta/2)D_a, where D_a is its positive matrix and H its sine diagonal. The D_a here is a MATRIX, not the scalar face factor. Its inverse has exact entries, indexed 1<=k,l<=a, (D_a^-1)_(k,l)=(-1)^(k+l) sqrt[sin((2k-1)theta)sin((2l-1)theta)] *sum_(m=max(k,l))^a cot(m theta). (3) For a direct proof, the elementary LDL^T pivots and lower entries are delta_m=sin(m theta)/[cos(m theta)sin((2m-1)theta)], L_(m,m-1)=sqrt[sin((2m-3)theta)/sin((2m-1)theta)]. Their inverse products telescope. Substituting them into `L^-T diag(delta_m^-1)L^-1` proves (3). Summing its diagonal and using `sum_(k=1)^m sin((2k-1)theta)=sin^2(m theta)/sin theta` gives Tr D_a^-1=sin(a theta)sin((a+1)theta)/(2sin^2 theta) <=1/(2sin^2 theta). Hence every source-polynomial root satisfies the uniform separation rho_h-2 >= 4sin^2(theta/2)sin^2 theta >= c N^-4. (4) The case a=0 has no roots. Equation (4) is useful by itself, but it does not supply a moving-q estimate; that requires the actual generic representation below. ## 3. A generic positive-at-the-root representation Keep zeta generic and put Q=zeta^2, z=Z+Z^-1. The ORIGINAL polynomial is the finite series with numerator parameters `(Q^-a,Q^(a+1),zeta/Z,zeta Z)` and denominator parameters `(Q,Q^-d,Q^(d+2))`. Apply the same own Sears identity, now retaining zeta Z and choosing d_S=Q, e_S=Q^-d. It gives the exact GENERIC identity p_a(zeta,Z+Z^-1)=P_a(zeta,Z) *4phi3(Q^-a,Q^-a,zeta Z,zeta Z; Q,zeta Z Q^(d+1-a),zeta Z Q^(-d-a-1);Q,Q), P_a=(zeta^-1 Z^-1 Q^-d,zeta^-1 Z Q^(-d-a);Q)_a /(Q^-d,Q^(-d-a-1);Q)_a. (5) At zeta=q,Z=1, the terms INCLUDING P_a are the positive summands of (1). The identity is generic before taking any normal. In particular its derivatives are not obtained by differentiating the root convolution. There are absolute constants c,C>0 such that, uniformly in every allowed a,N, |p_a(q exp(epsilon),z)/p_a(q,2)-1|<=1/2 if |epsilon|<=c N^-3 and |z-2|<=c N^-4. (6) Here is an explicit estimate. Each nonzero factor in each summand of (5) is `1-zeta^m Z^e`, with |m|<=4N and e in {-1,0,1}, or the unit monomial Q^k. At the base point its distance from zero is at least a constant times its distance in exponent from 2NZ divided by N. The half-integer factors in the Q notation correspond to ODD integer powers of zeta; they stay separated from every even multiple 2N. All other factors in the finite range also avoid those multiples. Summing logarithmic changes along each consecutive product gives |change log(summand)| <=C[N^2(1+log N)|epsilon|+N(1+log N)|Z-1|]. (7) This includes the prefactor, not merely the residual series. The bound uses a harmonic sum of reciprocal nonzero exponent distances; the product multiplicities are uniformly bounded. Taking `|epsilon|<=c N^-3`, `|Z-1|<=c N^-2` and decreasing c makes every summand a relative perturbation of its positive root value by, say, one quarter. Their sum obeys the same relative bound, without paying the number of terms or allowing cancellation of large terms. For every `|z-2|<=c' N^-4`, one solution of Z+Z^-1=z satisfies `|Z-1|<=c N^-2`, since `(Z-1)^2/Z=z-2`. Apply the preceding pointwise estimate to it. The polynomial is already holomorphic in z; a global choice of this square root is neither needed nor made. This proves (6), after adjusting the absolute constants. ## 4. All fixed genuine jets have polynomial endpoint cost Multivariable Cauchy applied to (6) proves, for every fixed r,s>=0, |partial_epsilon^r partial_z^s p_a(q exp(epsilon),z) evaluated_(0,2)| <= C_(r,s) N^(3r+4s) p_a(q,2). (8) The same bound holds on a fixed smaller joint disk with an adjusted constant. By (2), the function and its inverse therefore have only polynomial cost there, and a holomorphic logarithm exists on that product disk. The actual scalar face factor D_a is a product of root units after its displayed [N] zero is canceled, and D_a(q)=1. The same harmonic product estimate bounds D_a and its inverse on the WHOLE epsilon disk in (6), which is contained in their earlier uniform unit disk of radius c/[N^2(1+log N)]. Thus the statement also applies on the same joint disk to the original normalized scalar `D_a^-1 p_a`. These bounds cover the polynomial through the endpoint z=2 while the Casimir poles approach it. They retain both level parities and every original generic coefficient. The resolvent factor in the exact operator period, its own poles and normals, and the actual contour contribution still require their respective estimates. Neither (6) nor (8) moves a contour or proves dominance of its geometric saddle. Audit: [original endpoint convolution, generic Sears germ and joint disk](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_polynomial_endpoint_control.py). It passes 426 exact generic Sears comparisons, 210 joint root four-jet identities, 1,679 actual endpoint/convolution/lower-bound comparisons, eight inverse-trace and root-gap matrices, and 104 genuine generic joint-disk samples at 100 digits. The uniform bounds follow from the displayed finite formulas and harmonic estimates, not from those samples. Root full analytical review: PASS. The review checked the exact Sears normalization and positive convolution, elementary lower induction, LDL inverse/trace/root separation, every generic root-unit factor, the harmonic epsilon/Z bounds and pointwise Z lift, and multivariable Cauchy with the full face-unit disk retained. Independent geometry-agent full proof review and fresh redirected audit: PASS. The reviewer independently rederived both finite transforms, the convolution and lower bound, the telescoping matrix inverse and quantitative root gap, and the joint generic disk without a holomorphic square-root assumption. All 426/210/1,679/8/104 audit counts were reproduced. The note and focused audit are frozen; neither review includes contour deformation or source-saddle dominance.

title: Exact polynomial action away from a physical endpoint
status: Exact generic continuant action on explicit rows
text: # Exact polynomial action away from a physical endpoint 30 October 2026. The original exceptional Casimir polynomial acts by its scalar value on a genuine forward or backward continuant in an explicit part of the physical block. The identity is finite and generic, so it retains the actual q normals. It does not say that the surrounding selected boundary state is such a continuant or is supported in that part of the block. ## 1. Original matrix, continuants and endpoint residual Fix N, d=N-1 and a physical low degree 0<=t<=d. Let J_t(q) be the ACTUAL generic Casimir matrix of the [physical generic-jet theorem](actual_q_hahn_physical_generic_jet_bound.md), with diagonal D_u, upper entries A_u^+ and lower entries A_u^-. These entries are the original coproduct entries before root specialization; their generic upper and lower values are different. For an arbitrary spectral parameter z define C_0(z)=1, C_u(z)=det(zI-J_[u](q))/product_(r=0)^(u-1) A_r^+, 1<=u<=t, (1) where J_[u] is the first u rows and columns. Equivalently these are the normalized forward recurrence with C_-1=0. They are polynomials in z with rational generic-q coefficients. Every A_r^+ is a root unit when 0<=r<t, so (1) is holomorphic near the actual root for every z, including z outside the physical spectrum. The recurrence gives EXACTLY (J_t-zI)C(z)=r_t(z)e_t, r_t(z)=-det(zI-J_t)/product_(r=0)^(t-1) A_r^+. (2) The empty product has value one. Thus C(z) is an exact solution on every row except the final row. For an eigenvalue, its residual vanishes and this is the actual normalized eigenvector; at an arbitrary z it is an endpoint-residual vector, not an invented complex-color eigenvector of the finite matrix. The backward vector C^back(z), normalized to value one at u=t, is defined from the reversed ACTUAL generic matrix. It similarly satisfies (J_t-zI)C^back(z)=r_0(z)e_0. (3) No root-only conjugation symmetry is differentiated to obtain (3). ## 2. Finite propagation for the original exceptional polynomial For any scalar polynomial p of degree at most a, put h_z(X)=(p(X)-p(z))/(X-z), deg h_z<=a-1. Polynomial division and (2) give the exact vector identity p(J_t)C(z)-p(z)C(z)=r_t(z) h_z(J_t)e_t. (4) A tridiagonal matrix can move the support of a vector by at most one row in one multiplication. Consequently h_z(J_t)e_t is supported in rows u>=t-a+1. Therefore [p(J_t)C(z)]_u=p(z)C_u(z), 0<=u<=t-a. (5) The backward version is [p(J_t)C^back(z)]_u=p(z)C^back_u(z), a<=u<=t. (6) For a=0 both equalities hold everywhere. A negative upper limit or an excessive lower limit denotes an empty window. These are exact finite identities, independent of any limit or positivity. In particular take the ORIGINAL degree-a polynomial p_a of [the geometric target theorem](actual_matching_edge_geometric_target_polynomial.md). For 0<=a<=floor(d/2), all of its displayed generic coefficients are root regular. Its actual completed exceptional operator is D_a^-1 p_a(J_t), with the same regular scalar D_a. Multiplying (4)--(6) by D_a^-1 therefore proves the same finite identities for that completed operator. They hold as generic-q germs before specialization, hence after EVERY fixed generic derivative, with all continuant and scalar derivatives retained. They neither discard the nilpotent term nor replace a q derivative by a spectral one. They also hold for a chosen holomorphic z(q). The high physical block has total degree T>d. Use the already proved GENERIC adapter t=2d-T and u'=u-(T-d). Its matrix is exactly J_t(q), so (5),(6) apply to u'. No new high-degree convention or root-only reflection is introduced. The windows are generically sharp. If a>=1 and t>=a-1, the first possibly affected forward row is u=t-a+1. In (4) only the leading term of h_z can reach that row from e_t, giving [p(J_t)C-p(z)C]_(t-a+1) =r_t(z) lead(p) product_(r=t-a+1)^(t-1) A_r^+. (7) It is nonzero whenever the three displayed factors are nonzero. The corresponding backward statement uses the lower entries. Thus one cannot generally extend (5) through the remaining rows by merely observing that z is a classical geometric trace. ## 3. Exact Green-column formulation When z is outside the actual finite spectrum, (2) also gives (zI-J_t)^-1 e_t=-C(z)/r_t(z). (8) Equations (4),(8) are an exact resolvent-column identity. It can be used in a functional-calculus or boundary-state representation without assigning an artificial noninteger color. For example, any row functional ell supported on 0<=u<=t-a satisfies ell p_a(J_t)C(z)=p_a(z) ell C(z). (9) An actual representation of the surrounding state as such a vector, or a controlled integral of such vectors, remains additional input. An arbitrary row functional, dense mark or boundary tensor is not declared to have the support in (9). All physical bends, pivotal turns and the exposed mark remain the original ones. ## 4. Macroscopic windows and the remaining interface In scaled low coordinates, a/N->xi, t/N->tau, the two safe regions are respectively nu<=tau-xi, nu>=xi. (10) At the folded row xi=1/2 and a strict physical degree tau<1, their union leaves the central interval (tau-1/2,1/2). The existing selected-factor localization proves a physical packet outside the exceptional matching edge. It does not prove that the target environment equals (1), or that its output belongs to (10). Moreover (5),(6) are statements at ACTUAL integer physical rows. Evaluating them at complex geometric magnetic coordinates would require a proved continuation of these continuants and their boundary identity. The ordinary packet alone, whose channel stays real and discrete, does not supply that off-spectrum continuation. The exact identity consequently identifies a concrete sufficient interface for scalar evaluation, while preserving the unresolved environment, continuation and source-cycle questions. It is not a degree-O(N) functional-calculus approximation. Focused audit: [actual generic Casimir propagation and sharp boundary defects](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_polynomial_finite_propagation.py). Primary-agent full analytical review: PASS. The reader checked the forward/backward endpoint signs, generic root units, actual high adapter, first affected row, resolvent-column identity, and the precise missing environment and complex-row continuation assumptions. Independent full analytical review and fresh focused replay: PASS. A second reader checked the original upper/lower continuant normalization, polynomial division, sharp path factor and retained generic jets, and reproduced 104 continuants, 1212 safe-row four-jet identities, 260 nonzero first defects and 104 endpoint determinants, totaling 4848 retained jet coefficients. Neither review identifies an arbitrary boundary state with a continuant or infers a whole-source asymptotic.

title: The selected scalar polynomial generates the actual recoupled transport
status: General local character relation; operator contribution open
text: # The selected scalar polynomial generates the actual recoupled transport 30 October 2026. At the complete original channel, the canonical leading action of the actual target Casimir polynomial has exactly the derivative required by the ACTUAL inverse cyclic four-port turn. Its additive scalar constant is fixed by a positive finite-source anchor. This is a classical marked-transport comparison with an actual scalar asymptotic, not an asymptotic theorem for the polynomial operator acting in the surrounding contraction. The exact finite operator and all its original generic normals remain those in [the geometric target polynomial theorem](actual_matching_edge_geometric_target_polynomial.md). The actual selected scalar branch comes from the [root-location and slit-domain theorem](actual_matching_edge_racah_root_location.md), not from choosing a solution of a formal characteristic equation. ## 1. Follow the actual inverse turn Use the original trace-minus-two incoming meridians A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], P=BA, H=P+I, C=I+bH, Aout=C A C^-1, Bout=C B C^-1. The proved physical bend has tuple `(Aout,Bout,B^-1,A^-1)`. Its target pairs the middle objects. To write the target as an ordinary two-head operator one applies the INVERSE of the original pivotal turn R. Its based tuple, up to one common conjugacy, is (Bout,B^-1,A^-1,Aout), (Ain_target,Bin_target)=(Aout^-1,A), (Aout_target,Bout_target)=(Bout,B^-1). (1) Here is a direct basepath check of the cyclic order. If L_i are the four original local lower Borel factors, their total product is I for the invariant tensor. Rotating their local order from (1,2,3,4) to (2,3,4,1) rotates their four based meridians and conjugates all of them by L_1. Thus it has precisely the common-conjugacy effect just stated. The finite pivotal clock in R is still present in the operator identity; it gives no extra leading magnetic-momentum factor, since its ratio under one physical index shift is q^-2 -> 1. Its actual constant phase is NOT removed from the finite source. The target ordered product is T=B^-1 Bout=A Aout^-1, Tr T=2+16b^2. (2) Set alpha=8b^2-4b+1. Direct calculation gives the genuine target conjugator D=T-alpha I, D A D^-1=B^-1, D Aout^-1 D^-1=Bout, [D,T]=0, det D=-64b^4. (3) In particular (3) retains WHICH ordered meridian is sent to which; it is stronger than matching the target trace alone. ## 2. The physical rectangle determines its eigenratio For the certified complete geometry the actual primitive marking gives `b=-i/(2c)`, independently of the retained half-twist sign. Suppose first `0<c<=1`, and write c=sech eta, eta>=0, Tr T=-2cosh(2eta), J=-exp(-2eta)=exp(2pi i xi), xi=1/2+i eta/pi. (4) This specifies the target eigenflag. On the two T-eigenlines the conjugator D has eigenvalues J-alpha and J^-1-alpha. Its selected eigenratio is therefore R_target=(J-alpha)/(J^-1-alpha) =(1+i sinh eta)/(1-i sinh eta) =exp(2i atan(sinh eta)). (5) The opposite eigenflag inverts (5). Both (3) and the chosen expression in (5) extend through eta=0. In the normalization that gives eigenvalue one on the other flag, the parabolic limit is D_normalized=I+(i/2)(T+I) at eta=0. (6) This coefficient is a target transport parameter; it is not an independently introduced crossing-circle cusp shape. In particular there is no reason to assign it the orientation inequality of an original auxiliary cusp. ## 3. The actual scalar source fixes the generating derivative Let a_N/N->1/2 in the original folded range. The root-location theorem proves local uniform convergence of the actual canonical logarithms N^-1 Log p_(a_N)(z) -> Psi_(1/2)(z) on C minus [2,infinity). Define the scalar action along the actual target trace by F(eta)=Psi_(1/2)(-2cosh(2eta)). (7) For eta real and nonnegative, the positive finite-product proof gives F(eta)=max_(0<=v<=1/2) integral_0^v log[cos^2(pi s) *(cosh^2 eta-sin^2(pi s))/sin^4(pi s)] ds. Its unique maximum is `v=atan(cosh eta)/pi`, the actual rectangle parameter. Differentiation at the maximum gives an elementary exact formula. In c=sech eta coordinates, dF/dc=-2/c * integral_0^(atan(1/c)/pi) ds/(1-c^2 sin^2(pi s)) =-2 arccos c/(pi c sqrt(1-c^2)). Using `dc/deta=-c tanh eta` proves F'(eta)=2 atan(sinh eta)/pi. (8) The limit at eta=0 is zero. Its additive constant is fixed by the ACTUAL positive source evaluation at z=-2: F(0)=4 integral_0^(1/4) log cot(pi s) ds =4 Catalan/pi=v8/pi. (9) Thus no arbitrary period constant or logarithm winding was selected: F(eta)=v8/pi+(2/pi) integral_0^eta atan(sinh r) dr. (10) These formulas hold holomorphically on `|Im eta|<pi/2`, with the branch continued from eta=0. Indeed `-2cosh(2eta)` avoids [2,infinity) on that strip. The analytic arctangent in (8) is its continuation from zero; its derivative is `1/cosh eta`, with no pole inside the strip. The identity theorem extends the real calculation. One must not substitute a pointwise principal inverse trigonometric value after leaving the real axis. Because `xi=1/2+i eta/pi`, equation (8) is precisely partial_xi Psi_(1/2)(J+J^-1) =-2i atan(sinh eta), exp[-partial_xi Psi_(1/2)(J+J^-1)]=R_target. (11) The sign in (11) is the actual spectral-multiplier sign. Let Theta be the original fully normalized algebraic two-column generating phase. We use it here as the already proved classical character relation, not as a new asymptotic for a column at the complex target color. Its algebraic critical-character map says `exp(partial_xi Theta)=R_target`. Multiplication by the scalar source polynomial adds `Psi_(1/2)(J+J^-1)` to that phase. Target-channel stationarity is therefore exp(partial_xi[Theta+Psi])=1, exactly (11). It is NOT `R_target=exp(partial_xi Psi)`. This calculation uses the original inverse turn (1), the physical ordered matrices (3), and the canonical scalar branch (7). ## 4. General input color gives the actual four-parabolic character relation The same comparison holds for EVERY fixed real INPUT parameter `0<alpha<=1/2`, not only the complete input alpha=1/2. Keep it distinct from the TARGET parameter `xi=1/2+i eta/pi`. Put lambda_input=2cos(2pi alpha), s=sin(pi alpha), z=J+J^-1=-2cosh(2eta), F_alpha(eta)=Psi_alpha(z). Here Psi_alpha is again the actual selected scalar limit proved by the finite polynomial root theorem. For eta>0 its positive variational formula has unique maximum satisfying sin^2(pi v_*)=s^2 cosh^2 eta/(s^2+cosh^2 eta). Differentiate its original integral at that maximum. With `t=tan(pi v)`, the integral of `1/(cosh^2 eta-sin^2(pi v))` is elementary. It gives partial_eta F_alpha =(2/pi) atan[s sinh eta/sqrt(1+(1-s^2)sinh^2 eta)] =(2/pi) asin(s tanh eta). (12) Both inverse functions in (12) are continued from zero; for positive real eta their values lie in `(0,pi alpha)`. For example the equivalence follows by squaring the tangent and using `1+sinh^2 eta=cosh^2 eta`. Thus the selected scalar multiplier gives the eigenratio R_alpha=exp[-partial_xi Psi_alpha(J+J^-1)] =exp[2i asin(s tanh eta)], R_alpha+R_alpha^-1 =2-(2-lambda_input)(z+2)/(z-2). (13) This is precisely the ACTUAL four-parabolic trace equation in the inverse-turn convention (1), as can be proved without importing a character-variety formula. Diagonalize the target product `T=diag(J,J^-1)` and write its second incoming meridian as B_t=[[b11,b12],[b21,b22]], Tr B_t=Tr(B_t^-1 T)=-2, det B_t=1. The two trace equations give b11=-2J/(J+1), b22=-2/(J+1), b12 b21=-(J-1)^2/(J+1)^2. (14) For a target centralizer with eigenratio R, take `D=diag(R,1)`. The original input product is, BY THE ACTUAL INVERSE TURN, `(D B_t D^-1)^-1 B_t`. Therefore lambda_input=Tr(D B_t^-1 D^-1 B_t) =2-[(J-1)^2/(J+1)^2](2-R-R^-1). (15) Since `(J-1)^2/(J+1)^2=(z-2)/(z+2)`, equations (13) and (15) are identical. This proves the generating relation for general input trace, not just the number of its roots. At alpha=1/2 the explicit physical collar computation (3)--(5) fixes WHICH of the two inverse eigenratio branches is the marked one. Continuing that branch in alpha gives (13); no new arbitrary sign is selected at each input value. The expressions extend on `|Im eta|<pi/2` using the same scalar slit branch. The parabolic target eta=0 has the finite normalized limit D_normalized=I+(i s/2)(T+I). Its source trace is `2+16(i s/2)^2=lambda_input`, as it must be. This is a classical parabolic limit, not a substitute for an actual generic-q normal. For the analytic rectangle parameter c>1 one may take `eta=i arccos(1/c)` inside the same strip; the continued marking agrees with the real physical target in the preceding theorem. This statement does not assert that any finite real-color contour can be moved there without poles or without additional contributions. The additive value of each general-input scalar action is already fixed by its actual positive finite-source limit at any z<-2, followed by the slit-domain continuation. What has and has not been compared The target trace, the ordered target conjugator, its selected eigenratio, and the entire scalar generating derivative now agree with the actual recoupled geometry. title: A positive tail-free Racah scalar at one actual matching edge
status: All-target positive scalar; fixed generic jets
text: # A positive tail-free Racah scalar at one actual matching edge 30 October 2026. This is a specialization of the actual generic four-port coefficient theorem to the two halves of ONE crossing-circle matching edge. Its four outside objects are all the original physical V_(N-1). The scalar is positive after the retained single root zero is removed, including every new high recoupling channel and both level parities. All fixed generic scalar jets have polynomial relative cost. Each full recoupled tensor term has at most one pole, so its first normal needs Taylor order two after clearing that pole. This theorem controls the explicitly stated scalar and Laurent budget. It does not estimate the native boundary change-of-frame costs, the completed Hermite operator, or the surrounding coherent contraction. ## 1. The full actual channel range is uniformly saturated Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), and fix 0<=a<=floor(d/2), (A,B,C,D)=(d,d,d,d), E=2a, G=2g, 0<=g<=d. (1) The G range in (1) is the ENTIRE generic four-port recoupling range. No high partner is discarded. These are the four-port highest-weight conventions of [the actual coefficient theorem](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md). The corresponding six spins are (d/2,d/2,d/2,d/2,a,g). Its faces and opposite sums are F=(d+a,d+a,d+g,d+g), Q=(2d,d+a+g,d+a+g). (2) Every face is at least d, and all its triangle deficits are among k,k,d-k for k=a or g. They lie in [0,d]. All four faces and three opposite sums are INTEGERS, also when N is even and the four physical spins d/2 are half-integral. Consequently the true Racah range is d+max(a,g)<=z<=min(2d,d+a+g), (3) and all seven denominator factorial indices are in [0,d]. Every numerator [z+1]! contains exactly one [N] and contains NO [2N]. Thus this special physical block is tail-free even when g>d/2. This is not a claim that arbitrary high recoupling partners are tail-free. For the genuine generic symmetric factorial at zeta define S_ag(zeta)=sum_(z in (3)) (-1)^z [z+1]! / ([z-d-a]!^2 [z-d-g]!^2 [2d-z]! [d+a+g-z]!^2), G_ag(zeta)=(-1)^d S_ag(zeta)/[N]_zeta. (4) The division in (4) is performed in every original summand before root specialization. It is an analytic germ at q, not a derivative of a root-only replacement. ## 2. An exact positive squared-trinomial formula Set s_k=product_(v=1)^k 2sin(pi v/N), s_0=1. The elementary identity s_(d-k)=N/s_k gives the explicit root scalar R_N(a,g)=G_ag(q) =sum_(r=max(0,a-g))^(min(a,d-g)) [s_(g+r)/(s_(g+r-a)s_r s_(a-r))]^2 >0. (5) To verify every factor, put k=z-d. The removed-numerator formula is N sum_k s_k / [s_(k-a)^2 s_(k-g)^2 s_(d-k) s_(a+g-k)^2]. Replace s_(d-k) by N/s_k and then set r=k-g. All indices in (5) are between 0 and d. The signs of the factors [N+1],...,[z+1] combine with (-1)^(d+z) to give +1. No half-spin phase was omitted: A+B+C+D+E+G=4d+2a+2g is even. The full high partner has the SAME root scalar: R_N(a,g)=R_N(a,d-g). (6) This is termwise: replace g by d-g and r by a-r, and use s_(d-k)=N/s_k in the numerator/first-denominator ratio. The actual ranges in (5) are carried onto one another. Equation (6) is proved at both parities and does not discard any generic normal. The face metric is especially simple. For a face (d/2,d/2,k), put Delta_k^2=[k]!^2[d-k]!/[d+k+1]!, D_k(zeta)=(-1)^k [N]_zeta Delta_k^2. (7) All D_k are analytic and nonzero at q, and D_k(q)=s_k s_(d-k)/N=1. (8) There are two faces of each kind k=a,g. The generic normalized scalar therefore has the single-valued form H_ag(zeta)=G_ag(zeta)D_a(zeta)D_g(zeta), H_ag(q)=R_N(a,g). (9) Its branch-independent identity is the exact actual scalar convention H_ag^2=[N]^2 S_ag^2 product_(four faces) Delta^2. (10) All powers and signs in (10) are the original ones. A scalar diagonal gauge relating (10) to the physical recoupling matrix is still required; root value 1 of the face factors alone does not make that matrix unitary. ## 3. Every fixed generic scalar jet has polynomial relative cost There are universal c,C>0 such that, for ALL labels in (1), on zeta=q exp(t), |t|<=c/[N^2(1+log N)], (11) G_ag/G_ag(q), D_a, D_g and H_ag/H_ag(q) are holomorphic and remain in a fixed small disk about 1. In particular they are nonzero. For every fixed m>=0 this implies |partial_t^m G_ag(0)|+|partial_t^m H_ag(0)| <=C_m [N^2(1+log N)]^m R_N(a,g). (12) The same relative estimate holds for their inverses. For clarity, the proof applies to the COMPLETE generic germ in (4). After the one [N] factor is canceled, each summand and each face metric is a quotient of factors zeta^u-zeta^(-u), 1<=u<2N, u!=N, with fixed factorial multiplicities. Its logarithmic change on (11) is bounded by C N^2(1+log N)|t|, using |sin(pi u/N)| bounded below by a constant times dist(u,NZ)/N and the finite harmonic sum. At the root every summand of G_ag is positive by (5). On a sufficiently small common disk these summands remain in one narrow sector, so their sum has the same uniform relative bound. Equations (7),(8) give it for D_a,D_g. Cauchy's estimate proves (12). This is the direct supported-scalar argument, with (2),(3) proving its hypotheses for the entire present range, including half-integral physical spins and high g. In particular no missing [2N]T normal survives here: such a numerator factor is absent from every term before differentiation. The result does not say that a normal equals the derivative of the positive root expression (5); (4) remains the differentiated source. ## 4. The actual physical coefficient has only a simple pole Let L_(2g,2a) be the actual inverse Racah coefficient, with its original pivotal turn and first-highest-entry-one Clebsch bases. The exact source formula is L_(2g,2a)=chi_E X_E/(b_G J_n S0 V_n) S_ag, n=d-g, S0=[2d+1]!/([d-a]!^2[a]!^2), V_n=zeta^n (Q^(-d-g-1);Q)_n / [(Q;Q)_n^2 (Q^(-2d-1);Q)_n], Q=zeta^2. (13) The four prefactors chi_E,X_E,b_G,J_n are root units. This follows from their actual boundary product formulas: E=2a<N; their physical endpoint factorial indices are all in [0,d]. No first-normal channel norm is divided out. S0 has exactly one root zero. The numerator of V_n has a single root zero exactly when 2g<d. (14) Indeed its negative exponents run from -(d+g+1) to -(2g+2), and the only possible root multiple is -N. Its denominator factors are all units: the negative product starts at -(2N-1) and has length d-g, ending strictly before -N. The two (Q;Q)_n factors have n<N. By the strict positivity in (5), S_ag has exactly one root zero. Thus the ACTUAL coefficient orders are ord_q L_(2g,2a)=-1 for 2g<d, ord_q L_(2g,2a)= 0 for 2g>=d. (15) This includes a=0 and all endpoints. It does not assert positivity or regularity of the uncompleted physical coefficient matrix. Let T_(2g) be the actual generic target invariant tensor. Its Clebsch entries have the regular canceled physical coproduct formulas; the only possible pole is the canonical intermediate cup, with denominator (Q;Q)_(2g). Hence T_(2g) is regular for 2g<N and has at most a simple pole for 2g>=N. These two ranges never overlap the pole range in (15). Consequently pole_order [L_(2g,2a) T_(2g)] <=1 (16) for EVERY channel and level parity. The fixed source tensor S_(2a) is regular, so the simple poles on the right of its exact recoupling identity cancel in their full sum. After multiplication by a local parameter t, each recoupled term is holomorphic. Its contribution to the first normal of the regular whole contraction is extracted from Taylor coefficient t^2. Thus this special block has a uniform first-normal budget TWO, improving the general all-port budget four. If a regular surrounding contraction is present, it must be included when extracting that coefficient; its derivatives are not discarded. ## 5. Relation to the geometric pair localization The [prescribed-facet corollary](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) allows the two physical-support exceptions to be placed at the two halves of any chosen crossing-circle matching edge. Their four outside objects are then all V_d, so the present specialization applies regardless of the ribbon order of the other matching edges. A physical MAIN edge does not have that automatic property: its two channel legs can be adjacent instead of opposite in the actual cyclic order. The exact typed bend from the original W_a pi_a block to S_(2a), its fixed gamma factor, and the unchanged physical mark belong to the separate source interface. The normal must be extracted from the complete generic contraction, with all channels in (1) retained. Even after that interface, this is not a sharp completed block norm or a bound on the full source. Its scalar gauge factors can carry nontrivial boundary cost; the other local columns are not automatically in the central domain; and a global selected cycle and coherent bound remain necessary. The theorem makes the exceptional matching block an explicit tail-free scalar/finite-jet problem, without declaring those remaining tasks solved. Audit: [exact matching-edge scalar, original recoupling and normal budget](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_racah_positive_scalar.py). It passes 21,772 support/phase/pole cases, ten independently reconstructed generic source tensor families with all 47 recoupling coefficients, 529 retained root germs, 1,257 termwise partner checks, and 1,058 exact face-unit jets. In 406 comparisons the partners have the same root value but DIFFERENT generic first derivatives. The audit retains that distinction; its finite cases test conventions, while the written harmonic-product argument proves the uniform jet bound. Independent source-transport review and fresh audit replay: PASS. The reviewer independently specialized the actual boundary prefactors, including the pure-phase highest endpoint, and checked every root-unit and zero interval. The positive squared formula, half-integral physical spin phase, face roots, full generic sector argument, disjoint coefficient and target-cup poles, and Taylor-order-two budget all passed. The fresh replay reproduced all reported exact counts, including the unequal partner derivatives. Root analytical review: PASS. The review separately checked a=0, the actual scalar gauge convention, full generic fixed-jet bounds, all boundary product units, and coefficient extraction with a regular surrounding contraction. Neither review infers a native matrix norm or a whole-source estimate from the face metric's root values.

title: The source-normalized Racah polynomial has all its zeros above two
status: Roots above two; selected scalar action
text: # The source-normalized Racah polynomial has all its zeros above two 30 October 2026. For EVERY folded original channel, the exact matching-edge Casimir polynomial has simple real zeros strictly greater than 2. A positive matrix factorization proves this, including maximal channels at both level parities. Its canonical logarithm and leading action consequently continue to the whole slit plane C minus [2,infinity), including every real geometric target below 2. No continuation of a finite target color g is required. This theorem concerns the actual scalar polynomial. It does not prove a relative amplitude, control moving-q normal derivatives, estimate the complementary tensor contraction, or select a global source cycle. ## 1. The exact original polynomial at the root Use the generic source identity proved in [the geometric target polynomial theorem](actual_matching_edge_geometric_target_polynomial.md). Its normalization is D_a G_ag D_g=p_a(lambda_g), lambda_g=zeta^(2g+1)+zeta^(-2g-1), with all generic source factors retained. Put q=exp(pi i/N), theta=pi/N, d=N-1, 0<=a<=M=floor(d/2), and specialize to q. Let s_k=product_(r=1)^k 2sin(r theta), and set lambda_r=2cos((2r+1)theta), phi_k(x)=product_(r=0)^(k-1)(lambda_r-x). The generic terminating formula becomes EXACTLY p_a(x)=sum_(k=0)^a c_(a,k) phi_k(x), c_(a,k)=s_(a+k)/(s_(a-k)s_k^4). (1) Indeed [d-r]=[r+1] and [d+r+2]=-[r+1] at q, so the generic alternating signs cancel. Also [g-r][g+r+1]=(lambda_r-lambda_g)/(4sin^2 theta), product_(r<k)(lambda_r-lambda_a)=s_(a+k)/s_(a-k). These identities yield (1) without changing the original spectral variable. In particular p_a(lambda_0)=1 and its leading coefficient is kappa_a=(-1)^a s_(2a)/s_a^4. (2) All displayed denominators are nonzero for 2a<N. For a=0 the polynomial is identically one. ## 2. An own three-term recurrence For 0<=n<M define A_n=-4sin^4((n+1)theta) /[sin((2n+1)theta)sin((2n+2)theta)], B_n=2/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], C_n=-4sin^4(n theta)/[sin(2n theta)sin((2n+1)theta)], C_0=0. Then the finite polynomials (1) satisfy x p_n(x)=A_n p_(n+1)(x)+B_n p_n(x)+C_n p_(n-1)(x). (3) Here is a direct coefficient proof. Since x phi_k=lambda_k phi_k-phi_(k+1), the coefficient of phi_k on the left is lambda_k c_(n,k)-c_(n,k-1). The required ratios are c_(n+1,k)/c_(n,k)=sin((n+k+1)theta)/sin((n-k+1)theta), c_(n-1,k)/c_(n,k)=sin((n-k)theta)/sin((n+k)theta), c_(n,k-1)/c_(n,k) =4sin^4(k theta)/[sin((n+k)theta)sin((n-k+1)theta)]. (4) Substitution in (3), followed by the sine addition identities, gives equality. More explicitly the identity after division by c_(n,k) is lambda_k-4sin^4(k theta)/[sin((n+k)theta)sin((n-k+1)theta)] =A_n sin((n+k+1)theta)/sin((n-k+1)theta) +B_n+C_n sin((n-k)theta)/sin((n+k)theta). It is a rational identity in exp(i theta), exp(i n theta) and exp(i k theta); clearing its displayed denominators gives zero. The top coefficient k=n+1 is A_n=kappa_n/kappa_(n+1). The case n=0 follows directly from p_0 and p_1. Thus no presumed orthogonality or external q-Racah recurrence enters the proof. Set P_n=p_n/kappa_n, the monic polynomials. Equation (3) becomes P_(n+1)=(x-B_n)P_n-e_n^2 P_(n-1), e_n^2=A_(n-1)C_n =4sin^6(n theta) /[cos^2(n theta)sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]>0. (5) Consequently P_a(x)=det(xI-J_a), where J_a is the real symmetric Jacobi matrix with diagonal B_0,...,B_(a-1) and adjacent entries e_1,...,e_(a-1)>0. ## 3. The positive shift by two Let Dpos_a be the previously proved positive q-Hahn matrix; the distinct scalar face factor retains its original name D_a: (Dpos_a)_(n,n)=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], (Dpos_a)_(n-1,n)=sqrt(beta_n), beta_n=sin^2(n theta) /[cos^2(n theta)sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. For completeness, its leading principal minors are det Dpos_m=2^m product_(r=1)^m sin(r theta) /product_(r=m+1)^(2m)sin(r theta)>0. This finite formula was proved by the determinant recurrence in [the original q-Hahn determinant theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.md#4-a-positive-definite-real-part). Every factor is positive because 2m<N, so Dpos_a is positive definite also at a=M. Put H=diag(sin((n+1/2)theta))_(n=0)^(a-1), s0=sin(theta/2). There is the exact matrix factorization J_a-2I=2 H Dpos_a H+2s0^2 Dpos_a. (6) The diagonal identity is sin^2((n+1/2)theta)+sin^2(theta/2) =1-cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta). The adjacent identity is sin((n-1/2)theta)sin((n+1/2)theta)+sin^2(theta/2) =sin^2(n theta). These are precisely the entries in (5),(6). The right side of (6) is positive definite. Therefore EVERY eigenvalue of J_a is strictly greater than 2. The nonzero adjacent entries also imply simple spectrum: an eigenvector is determined by its first coordinate through the tridiagonal recurrence, and that coordinate cannot vanish. Hence ALL zeros of p_a are simple, real, and strictly greater than 2. (7) This is uniform in the folded channel, with no restriction to odd levels or to channels bounded away from the fold. ## 4. The canonical logarithm and its uniform derivative bounds Write the zeros as r_1,...,r_a>2. Since p_a(lambda_0)=1, p_a(x)=product_(h=1)^a (r_h-x)/(r_h-lambda_0). On Omega=C minus [2,infinity), define Log p_a(x)=sum_h Log((r_h-x)/(r_h-lambda_0)), (8) where each logarithm is continued from its positive real value at any x<2. Equivalently its argument has the principal logarithm in each individual factor. This is a single holomorphic branch on Omega, real on the whole interval x<2. For m>=1, |partial_x^m Log p_a(x)| <=(m-1)! a/dist(x,[2,infinity))^m. (9) Thus the original scalar itself, rather than a complexly continued finite color g, supplies a canonical selected branch at every geometric real target x<2. ## 5. Leading source action continues through the physical endpoint Here the scalar leading limit can also be proved directly. Let a_N/N tend to alpha in (0,1/2]. For a real x<-2, every term in (1) is positive. Uniform sine-factorial estimates and Riemann sums give N^-1 log p_(a_N)(x) -> max_(0<=t<=alpha) E_alpha(t;x), E_alpha(t;x)=J(alpha+t)-J(alpha-t)-4J(t) +integral_0^t log(2cos(2pi u)-x) du, J(v)=integral_0^v log(2sin(pi u)) du. (10) The endpoint logarithmic singularities in the sine factorials cost O(log N), uniformly in their integer indices. The final integrand in (10) is smooth and positive-argument for x<-2. The number of summands is at most N, so maximum-term comparison proves (10), including sequences approaching the folded channel. The maximum is unique and interior. Put A=sin^2(pi alpha), v=2-x and z=sin^2(pi t). Its derivative is partial_t E=log[(A-z)(v-4z)/(4z^2)]. For x<-2 this strictly decreases from +infinity to -infinity. The critical equation is linear after cancellation of its z^2 terms, and gives z_*=A v/(v+4A), t_*=pi^-1 arcsin(sqrt(A v/(v+4A))). (11) Now fix an anchor x0<-2. The bounds (9), divided by N, make N^-1 Log p_(a_N) a locally bounded normal family on the connected slit domain Omega: its value at x0 is bounded by (10), and its derivative is uniformly bounded along any fixed compact path. Every subsequential holomorphic limit agrees with (10) on the real interval x<-2. The identity theorem therefore makes the limit unique. Consequently N^-1 Log p_(a_N)(x) -> Psi_alpha(x) (12) locally uniformly on ALL of Omega, with every fixed x derivative. This is the actual source logarithm (8), not a formally chosen solution of a characteristic equation. On the entire real interval x<2 the continuation is explicitly Psi_alpha(x)=E_alpha(t_*(x);x), (13) with (11). Indeed 0<z_*<min(A,v/4), so all logarithms in the integral up to t_* have positive arguments. Formula (13) is real analytic on x<2 and agrees with (10) on x<-2, proving the claimed continuation. In particular the passage through x=-2 is regular. There is no claimed uniformity at the removed boundary x=2. The result proves a leading selected SCALAR action. It does not turn the original tensor contraction into a scalar evaluation, or justify discarding its generic first normals. Those distinctions remain essential to the global volume problem. Audit: [original root values, the own recurrence and positive matrix shift](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_racah_root_location.py). Independent review: the root agent and cluster/source agent checked the complete proof, including the original polynomial normalization, all recurrence endpoints, positive matrix shift, simple spectrum, canonical logarithm, and connected-slit normal-family argument. The cluster agent freshly replayed 3 formal identities, 6,984 original source values, 1,904 recurrence coefficients, 304 leading coefficients, 25 matrix factorizations and 24 actual continued-rate diagnostics. This review concerns the scalar polynomial and its leading action; it does not substitute that scalar for the contracted operator.

title: A real exceptional target cannot preserve the selected global complement
text: # A real exceptional target cannot preserve the selected global complement 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. The [real-target classification](actual_matching_edge_real_target_frames.md) constructs local real cross-central frames for every strict geometric target c<1. They cannot also preserve the selected physical ordinary complement in the present one-matching-edge reduction of a certified right-angled link. This is a precise frame obstruction for that route, not a rate gap or a contradiction to the source invariant or conjecture. ## 1. Statement and retained hypotheses Fix an actual labeled right-angled matching-polyhedron certificate, its literal Morse prefixes, retained half twists, primitive markings, and original source. Choose one matching edge as the exceptional four-port block. Assume its actual rectangle satisfies 0<c<1; the parabolic case c=1 is not treated here. There is NO common regular frame with all the following properties: * Every original input/output factor outside this edge lies in the strict physical domain on its source-selected complete geometric sheet, as in the selected-factor localization theorem. * After the ACTUAL inverse pivotal turn, both target magnetic rows and the normalized total are real and strictly physical, in either degree adapter. The two limiting target rows are distinct. * The limiting target row distance is positive and at most 1/2, the folded polynomial bandwidth. In particular this includes any strict candidate for a nonzero real exceptional matrix entry. The real-target classification shows that such rows must be on its minus anti-diagonal branch. The key additional fact proved below is that undoing the turn puts BOTH original factors at this edge in the strict physical domain on their selected sheets as well. The geometric white-normal argument then excludes the resulting all-factor frame. ## 2. Undo the actual turn before testing the disk strips Retain the original incoming pair and transport A=-[[1,1],[0,1]], B=-[[1,0],[-4,1]], P=BA, C=I+b(P+I), b=-i/(2c), A_o=C A C^-1, B_o=C B C^-1. The target input/output pair is (A_o^-1,A) and (B_o,B^-1), with target product T=B^-1 B_o=A A_o^-1. Let Pi be the ORIGINAL frame, and Pi_t its inverse-turn frame. The actual basepath change is Pi_t=A_o Pi/Tr(A_o Pi). (1) Here Pi is the prefix-normalized local projector `W Pi_global/Tr(W Pi_global)`, followed by the common local normalizing conjugacy. Its flags are the actual prefix image Wv and the same global kernel w. This notation does not choose a new independent frame at the edge. In the target notation, let E=e^2, e=exp(+/-pi i tau), and q=rho+i sqrt(1-rho^2), q_out=conjugate(q), rho=rho_-<0, k=sinh^2 eta, c=sech eta. First use the displayed ordering; exchanging q and its conjugate will be included below. Since q is unit, the target prefix equations and (1) give the EXACT original prefix diagonals Tr(A Pi)=e/q, Tr(A_o Pi)=e^-1/q, Tr(P Pi)=q^-2. (2) Indeed Tr(A_o^-1 Pi_t)=1/Tr(A_o Pi), while T A_o=A and B_o A_o=P. These identities fix the basepoint and all ratios; (2) is not obtained by identifying Pi with Pi_t. Write the original image and kernel flags in the disk coordinate eta(s)=1/(2s+1) as z and w. Put H=1/c=sqrt(1+k). In this coordinate A=[[-1,0],[-2,-1]], P=[[-1,-2],[0,-1]], C acts by eta -> eta+iH, A_o=[[-1-2iH,-2H^2],[-2,-1+2iH]]. (3) For Pi represented by these flags, Pi=[[z,-zw],[1,-w]]/(z-w). Direct traces in (3) give Tr(P Pi)=-1-2/(z-w), Tr(A Pi)=-1+2zw/(z-w), Tr(A_o Pi)-Tr(A Pi) =[-2H^2-2iH(z+w)]/(z-w). (4) Use q+q^-1=2rho and (2) in (4). It follows that z-w=-q/rho, z+w=iH+(e^-1-e)/(2iH rho). (5) The second term in the sum is REAL for both target adapters. Hence Im z=[H-sqrt(1-rho^2)/rho]/2, Im w=[H+sqrt(1-rho^2)/rho]/2. (6) Exchanging the trace signs exchanges these heights. They are finite: rho_- is strictly negative. Both flags lie strictly in the ACTUAL original disk strip 0<Im eta<H precisely when |rho|>1/sqrt(k+2). (7) For rho_-=(-sqrt(k+2)-c0)/(1+k), inequality (7) is equivalent to c0>-1/sqrt(k+2). This is exactly the lower inequality in the strict physical interval already required by the real-target classification. Thus every viable real minus-branch target satisfies its original disk's selected strip test, including when tau<1/2. The real plus branch fails (7), but it is already excluded from a direct nonzero folded entry by its exact row distance greater than 1/2. No source support is discarded in this argument. ## 3. Both original factors are also strictly physical Let q=exp(i alpha), pi/2<alpha<pi, and set delta=1-alpha/pi in (0,1/2), u=(tau-delta)/2, v=(tau+delta)/2, 0<u<tau/2<v<tau<1. These are the target low and high rows. The original physical coordinate dictionary applied to (2) is U_in=-q/e, U_out=-q e, T_original=q^2. (8) For q in the upper half-plane, the original two factors have total degree tau_original=alpha/pi=1-delta in (1/2,1), and their magnetic rows are u and 1-v, in one order or the other depending on the target adapter. Their physical wire pairs are (u,1-v) and (1-v,u). Every entry is strictly between zero and one, and their sum is tau_original. Thus both factors lie strictly in the ordinary complete-channel physical domain. For q in the lower half-plane, the actual physical total is instead 1+delta, with physical magnetic rows v and 1-u. Applying the ORIGINAL high-degree adapter subtracts delta from those rows and reverses the total. The normalized total and rows are again 1-delta, u and 1-v. (9) This explicitly covers both trace orderings and both target adapters. There is no implicit assumption that the normalized target total tau itself exceeds 1/2. Combine (6),(7) with (9). The selected-sheet continuation throughout the full strict physical domain, proved in [the selected-factor theorem](actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md), identifies these strip tests with the actual source-selected input and output sheets. Therefore BOTH original factors at the chosen edge are now physical and selected, in the same original frame Pi. ## 4. Why the geometric global obstruction applies beyond its old headline The original [white-normal obstruction](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md) was initially stated for an all-central source frame. Its geometric sections 4--5 prove a stronger conditional assertion: simultaneous STRICT physical support and the oriented disk-strip tests are impossible in one common frame for the literal certified cut. Here is the precise use, with no extension of an unproved source sheet outside its domain. Write Pi_global=v ell, let w=ker ell and w_0=r_(F_0)(v). The literal prefixes are Q_i=r_(F_i)r_(F_0). Each adjacent white reflection preserves the two disk halfspaces. Consequently all input/output strip tests imply w,w_0 belong to the common shaded exterior K. In the white-normal polyhedron C, K lies strictly inside C on its unit sphere. Actual prefix diagonals are positive normal rescalings of the polarized real-linear forms L_n(w,w_0). Their real kernel meets int C. Following a line in that kernel to a triangular boundary facet gives a nonnegative relation among the three actual prefix diagonals of that facet. Thus zero lies in their real convex hull. This contradicts that original factor's strict physical-support criterion. The proof includes coincident flags and nongeneric facet-edge intersections; it does not require exactly two generic failures or an all-central hypothesis. By assumption every factor outside the selected matching edge is physical and source-selected; the full-domain theorem supplies its strip test. Sections 2--3 supply both properties on the edge as well. The preceding geometric contradiction proves the stated obstruction. ## 5. What must change in the proposed method The exact real-row Green action and real exceptional operator packets remain valid local theorems. The new conclusion is that this real slice cannot contain the complete geometric point while retaining the currently selected physical ordinary complement in a single common frame. Within that one-block setup, a geometric contraction must use complex target coordinates or change which grouping or complementary source description is controlled. No numerical exponential gap, vanishing of the invariant, absence of a geometric contribution on another cycle, or impossibility of a different source-preserving resummation is inferred. The parabolic target c=1, boundary support, and exact limiting row coincidences remain outside the strict local classification used here. Focused audit: [actual inverse-turn flags and both physical adapters](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_real_frame_global_obstruction.py). Primary-agent full analytical review: PASS. The reader checked the actual projector pullback, strip heights, all original low/high logarithms and the precise reuse of the geometric strict-support obstruction. Distinct limiting target rows are explicitly required. Independent full analytical review and fresh redirected replay: PASS. A second reader reproduced seventeen matrix/trace identities, seventy-two actual frames, 144 strip flags and 144 normalized original factor checks. Both reviews retain the explicit local-prefix projector and make no conclusion about a different global source route.

title: Which actual geometric target frames have real magnetic rows?
text: # Which actual geometric target frames have real magnetic rows? 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. This is a local classification for the ACTUAL inverse-turn target, not a common-frame existence theorem for the whole link. It supplies a real cross-central frame for every strict certified target c<1. Its total degree can be below 1/2; the existing Green theorem allows that range. One other apparently favorable branch is killed by the exact finite-source bandwidth, including all generic-q normals. ## 1. Keep the actual ordered target and both degree adapters Use the marked inverse turn of [the polynomial generating-action theorem](actual_matching_edge_polynomial_geometric_action.md). For a certified crossing-circle rectangle with 0<c<1, write c=sech eta, eta>0, k=sinh^2 eta, J=-exp(-2eta), T=diag(J,J^-1), R=(1+i sqrt(k))/(1-i sqrt(k)), D=diag(R,1). After a centralizer normalization, its first target input and output are A=[[a,1],[kappa,d]], A_out=D A D^-1, a=-2J/(J+1), d=-2/(J+1), kappa=-(J-1)^2/(J+1)^2. (1) The second input is T A^-1. These are the actual inverse-turn pair, whose product trace is 2-4/c^2, and its actual conjugator eigenratio. In particular D is not chosen to fit magnetic coordinates. The [rectangle bound](actual_matching_circle_rectangle_bound.md) proves c<=1 in the certified class; the parabolic equality c=1 is excluded from the present diagonalization argument. A physical frame is represented by a rank-one trace-one projector Pi. Let the normalized target degree be real, 0<tau<1. The low adapter has E=Tr(T Pi)=exp(-2pi i tau), e=exp(-pi i tau). The high adapter instead has E=exp(+2pi i tau), e=exp(+pi i tau). In BOTH cases put c0=-cos(pi tau) in (-1,1), and write Pi=[[p,q],[r,1-p]], p=(E-J^-1)/(J-J^-1), X=r/e, Y=kappa q/e, K=(c0^2+k)/(4k^2), d0=-c0/k. The determinant-zero condition and the two actual prefix traces are exactly XY=K, z_in=Tr(A Pi)/e=d0+X+Y, z_out=Tr(A_out Pi)/e=d0+R X+R^-1 Y. (2) For example the diagonal trace in (2) follows from `k=-(J+1)^2/(4J)` and `c0=-(e+e^-1)/2`; the same substitutions give `kappa p(1-p)/e^2=K`. Here z_in,z_out denote normalized traces, not tetrahedron shapes. In the low adapter the physical coordinate is U=-1/Tr(A Pi), so the centered exponential is U/exp(pi i tau)=-1/z_in. In the high adapter the actual dictionary is T_phys=1/T_low, U_phys=U_low/T_low, and U_low/exp(pi i tau)=-1/z_in again. The output is identical with A replaced by A_out. Thus in both adapters the two rows are REAL if and only if |z_in|=|z_out|=1. Their strict physical support is equivalent to Re z_in<c0, Re z_out<c0. (3) Indeed the centered magnetic argument has the unique marked lift in (-pi tau,pi tau), and z=-exp[-2pi i(nu-tau/2)]. This proves (3) also for tau<1/2; that range must not be discarded merely because an ordinary complete-channel column needs a larger total degree. The present exceptional operator is the polynomial p_a(J_t). ## 2. All strictly physical real solutions are anti-diagonal Since K>0, parameterize every solution of XY=K by X=sqrt(K) exp(sigma+i phi), Y=sqrt(K) exp(-sigma-i phi), sigma,phi real. Put beta=atan sqrt(k), chi=phi+beta, and L=2sqrt(K). Then z_in =d0+L[cosh(sigma)cos(chi-beta) +i sinh(sigma)sin(chi-beta)], z_out=d0+L[cosh(sigma)cos(chi+beta) +i sinh(sigma)sin(chi+beta)]. (4) Their squared-modulus difference factors as |z_in|^2-|z_out|^2 =4L sin(chi)sin(beta) [d0 cosh(sigma)+L cos(beta)cos(chi)]. (5) If sin chi=0, the two traces are complex conjugates. To exclude the other possibility from strict support, put M=cosh^2 sigma and use the vanishing of the bracket in (5). The common unit-modulus equation then gives M=k/(1-c0^2)+1/(1+k), cos^2 chi=c0^2 M(1+k)/(c0^2+k). (6) Consequently Delta=1-c0^2(k+2)>=0 is necessary. Directly computing the mean and difference of the two real parts gives (c0-Re z_in)(c0-Re z_out) =-Delta [c0^4(k+2)-2c0^2+k^2+k+1] /[(1-c0^2)^2(1+k)^2]. (7) The bracket is strictly positive: Delta>=0 implies c0^2<=1/(k+2)<1/2, so already 1-2c0^2>0 and all other terms are nonnegative. Thus (7) is nonpositive, contradicting BOTH strict inequalities (3). This also excludes the equality Delta=0. It follows that every strictly physical real pair is conjugate. Write z_in=rho+i sqrt(1-rho^2), z_out=conjugate(z_in), allowing their exchange. Substitution in (2) gives precisely [(1+k)rho+c0]^2=k+2, rho_+=(sqrt(k+2)-c0)/(1+k), rho_-=(-sqrt(k+2)-c0)/(1+k). (8) The value rho=-1 gives the common central row; strict cross-central rows require -1<rho<c0. Conversely every branch of (8) with this inequality supplies an actual projector: solve the two linear equations (2) for X,Y, set r=eX and q=eY/kappa, and (8) gives XY=K. The linear determinant is nonzero because R!=R^-1 for k>0. Both target prefix traces are units. No purely formal independent choice of the input and output rows is involved. The two marked row coordinates are nu_low=(tau-1)/2+acos(rho)/(2pi), nu_high=tau-nu_low, 0<nu_low<tau/2<nu_high<tau. (9) For the displayed upper-half-plane z_in, the INPUT is nu_high and the OUTPUT is nu_low. Exchanging the signs of both trace imaginary parts swaps input and output. Their exchange has the same support and distance. This proves the classification in BOTH actual degree adapters. ## 3. Exact bandwidth selects only the minus branch The original target matrix J_t(zeta) is tridiagonal at generic zeta. The exact matching-edge operator is a scalar normalization times p_a(J_t), where p_a has degree a. Therefore EVERY generic entry with |u-v|>a vanishes identically. This remains true after taking any fixed generic-q derivative, clearing its scalar normalizers, or combining the retained partner normal. It is not a semiclassical estimate. For (9) the row distance is delta=nu_high-nu_low =1-acos(rho)/pi=1/2+asin(rho)/pi. (10) The plus branch is strictly physical precisely when c0>1/sqrt(k+2). It always has rho_+>0. Thus delta>1/2, and for actual folded degrees a/N->1/2 every sufficiently nearby integer matrix entry is IDENTICALLY ZERO. Its real frame cannot serve as a direct nonzero exceptional kernel. The finite-propagation identity for a whole continuant vector does not contradict this entrywise fact. The minus branch has rho_-<0, hence delta<1/2. It avoids this exact support obstruction. This does not by itself prove a nonzero matrix element, an asymptotic, a contributing spectral saddle, or absence of cancellation in the full marked contraction. ## 4. Real cross-central local frames exist for every strict target The minus branch is strict cross-central and physical exactly when -1/sqrt(k+2)<c0<min(1,k+1-sqrt(k+2)). (11) The interval is nonempty for EVERY k>0, since k+1-sqrt(k+2)+1/sqrt(k+2) =(k+1)(1-1/sqrt(k+2))>0. Choose any c0 in this open interval and set tau=acos(-c0)/pi. Equations (2),(8) construct a common local frame with the strict real cross-central rows (9) and distance below 1/2. It therefore lies in the real parameter range of the [cross-central Green action](actual_matching_edge_cross_central_green_action.md). That theorem allows every 0<tau<1, so no additional tau>1/2 hypothesis is needed for this local application. There IS a useful limitation if one insists on tau>1/2: then c0>0, and (11) has a solution precisely when k>(sqrt(5)-1)/2, c<sqrt((sqrt(5)-1)/2). (12) For larger rectangles the required real total must be below 1/2. The already certified isolated cylinders C(h^s), s>=5, have c=cos(pi/s) above this threshold by [the arbitrary-width seed theorem](actual_conway_arbitrary_width_seeds.md). They illustrate why imposing the ordinary complete-column domain on the exceptional Green operator would falsely create an obstruction. No theorem about a universal global choice of frame follows instead. ## 5. The original selected frame is still an additional constraint The inverse pivotal turn changes the basepoint. With A_old,out the original first output meridian, the projectors obey Pi_target=A_old,out Pi_old/Tr(A_old,out Pi_old), Pi_old=A_old,out^-1 Pi_target/Tr(A_old,out^-1 Pi_target). (13) For a direct check, the actual first lower factor is L_1=[[1,0],[-G_21,G_11]], and L_1^-1 E_11 L_1=G E_11/G_11. Conjugating back gives (13). The denominator in the inverse formula is the nonzero first target prefix trace, so the local projectors constructed here pull back. The selected-strip conditions for EVERY other disk must be imposed on this Pi_old and its actual prefixes. They are not conditions on independently selected target diagonals. The present classification neither proves nor disproves their simultaneous compatibility with (11). In particular it does not replace the global prescribed-pair theorem by a real-slice assertion, identify the complementary state with a continuant, or infer that a real spectral saddle contributes. Focused audit: [actual target traces, classification and bandwidth](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_real_target_frames.py). Primary-agent full analytical review: PASS. The reader checked the rank-one trace equations, both physical adapters, exclusion of the nonconjugate branch, both exact roots and their support intervals, the generic bandwidth argument, and the inverse-turn pullback. The input/output ordering in (9) is explicit. Independent full analytical review and fresh redirected replay: PASS. A second reader reproduced eight formal identities, thirty-six actual local frames, seventy-two adapter row checks, thirty nonconjugate support failures and 222 exact generic bandwidth entries. Neither review infers compatibility with the other disks of the link.

title: The full real native cost throughout every shrinking fold window
status: Full real norm rate in shrinking fold windows
text: # The full real native cost throughout every shrinking fold window 30 October 2026. Let j_N/N tend to 1/2, with 0<=j_N<=floor((N-1)/2). The FULL physical completed projector and, when paired, its actual nilpotent have exponential norm rate 5v3/pi. No restriction such as (N-1-2j_N)log N=o(N) is needed here. This concerns real integer physical degrees and magnetic indices, their Euclidean operator norms, and fixed generic-q jets. It does not extend the complex-normal corridor, supply a confluent complex amplitude, or estimate a marked whole-network contraction. ## 1. Statement and the exact source interfaces Put d=N-1, j=j_N, l=d-j and s=l-j. If j<l, let Q_j and M_j be the ACTUAL completed target pair in the [native projector theorem](actual_matching_edge_native_projector_energy.md). If j=l, retain the ordinary isolated midpoint projector Pi_j. Then, for every sequence j/N->1/2, N^-1 log ||Q_j||op ->5v3/pi, N^-1 log ||M_j||op ->5v3/pi (1) on its paired subsequence, and the same limit holds for Pi_j on its simple subsequence. All statements remain true for the Hilbert--Schmidt norm. Every FIXED generic-q jet of these operators has upper exponential rate at most 5v3/pi; equality is not asserted for a derivative that can vanish. We prove the paired claim; the isolated midpoint is already covered by the [full folded profile](actual_matching_edge_magnetic_energy_profile.md). Here s/N->0, while s itself can tend to infinity at any sublinear rate. All original physical degrees are retained. For complete degrees l<=t<=d, the exact Parseval comparison is N/(j+1) Z_(t,j) <= E_(t,j) <=N Z_(t,j), Z_(t,j)=|fhat_j(t/2)|^2/|sigma_(t,j)|. (2) The exact center source and double CD measure give Z_(t,j)=A_(N,t,j) R_j(1;c_t)^2, A_(N,t,j)=a_j^2/N *s_(2j)^2/s_j^4 *s_(t-j)/s_(t-l), c_t=-cos(pi(t+1)/N), a_j=|1-q^(4j+2)|. (3) All factorial indices lie in 0,...,d. The monic determinant R_j is the original source determinant, not an auxiliary positive replacement. It is increasing at z=1 for real c>=0. In (3), c_t ranges from cos(pi j/N) to 1, so this monotonicity applies. Let J(x)=integral_0^x log(2sin(pi y))dy on [0,1]. Its continuity, J(0)=J(1/2)=J(1)=0, and the uniform factorial estimate give sup_(l<=t<=d) |N^-1 log A_(N,t,j)| ->0. (4) Indeed the factorial part divided by N is 2J(2j/N)-4J(j/N) +J((t-j)/N)-J((t-l)/N)+O(log N/N). The first two terms tend to zero. The last two arguments differ by s/N->0, uniformly over t, so their difference tends to zero by uniform continuity. The remaining a_j and N factors have logarithms O(log N), since a_j>=4/N at a nonself-paired node. Thus (2)--(4), at the endpoint and throughout the complete range, prove max_(l<=t<=d) E_(t,j)=R_j(1;1)^2 exp(o(N)). (5) This is a maximum over one genuine physical degree. It does not maximize independently over degrees of adjacent network coupons. ## 2. The actual endpoint selects the same cubic limit Put u=floor(d/2), v=d-u and w_N=q^j. At t=d the positive coefficient polynomial appearing in the ORIGINAL physical column is P_N(w)=sum_(a=0)^j beta(j,a)beta(u,a)beta(v,j-a) w^a, C_j(d,u)=q^((d-j)u) P_N(w_N). (6) The denominator beta(d,j) is exactly one. The finite negative-root theorem applies to this original polynomial. Uniform factorial estimates and j/N,u/N,v/N->1/2 give uniformly over the whole support N^-1 log[beta(j,a)beta(u,a)beta(v,j-a)] =-3[J(a/N)+J(1/2-a/N)]+o(1). (7) Replacing j/N by 1/2 uses only uniform continuity of J, including both endpoints. There is no assumed bound on s log N here. For every positive real w, (7) gives the same strict real Laplace action as in the full folded theorem. Its selected saddle is alpha(w)=pi^-1 arctan(w^(1/3)). The actual negative-root product bound makes N^-1 Log(P_N(w)/P_N(1)) a normal family on the slit plane. Uniqueness from the positive real axis therefore gives the same holomorphic action for this whole sequence of actual polynomials. In particular at w_N->i, N^-1 log |C_j(d,u)| ->5v3/(2pi). (8) This is the selected complex rate, not a conclusion from comparing positive coefficients at w=i. The exact constant was computed from alpha(i)=1/4+i log(3)/(4pi) and D(i/sqrt(3))=5v3/6 in the preceding theorem. At degree d the magnetic polynomial has all j roots negative real. If u differs from d/2 by one half, its root-product formula gives cos(pi/(2N))^j <= |C_j(d,u)|/|fhat_j(d/2)| <=1; (9) if d is even the ratio is one. Finally the exact center scalar is |fhat_j(d/2)|=R_j(1;1) s_(2j)/s_j^3. (10) Its normalized logarithm tends to zero, since J(2j/N)-3J(j/N)->0. Equations (8)--(10) prove N^-1 log R_j(1;1)^2 ->5v3/pi. (11) ## 3. The incomplete band is smaller, using its own actual formula It remains to control j<=t<l, where the completed pair contains only its simple physical branch. The complete-range Fourier factorization is NOT assumed in this band. Instead start with the original generic finite column. Its highest-vector factor at the root is exactly F_(N-j+a-1) F_(N-a-1)/(F_(N-j-1)F_(N-1)) =Q^(a(a-j)) [j choose a]_Q. (12) This follows by complementing each factor 1-Q^(N-r)=-Q^(-r)(1-Q^r). Every denominator index is below N; (12) is valid for ALL 0<=j<=t< N, not just complete channels. Since [n choose k]_Q=q^(k(n-k)) beta(n,k), substitution into the original divided-descendant sum gives the exact identity C_j(t,u)=q^((d-j)u) sum_a E(t,j,u,a) q^(a(t+j-d)), E=beta(j,a)beta(u,a)beta(t-u,j-a)/beta(t,j), max(0,u-t+j)<=a<=min(j,u). (13) To check its phase directly, the Gaussian-binomial phases, divided-descendant powers and root highest ratio leave a(t+j-1)-ju before the factor (-1)^a x^(-2a). Combining that factor with x^u and q^N=-1 gives precisely (13). Thus its real positive envelope is an authorized bound for this ACTUAL root source outside the complete chamber. Set r=t-j<s=o(N). Every allowed a satisfies 0<=u-a<=r. Uniform factorial estimates, j/N,t/N->1/2, and that inequality imply N^-1 log E(t,j,u,a) =-J(x)-J(1/2-x)+o(1), (14) uniformly throughout the incomplete band and its full support. Here x can be chosen as min(u/N,1/2). The possible excess of u/N above 1/2 is o(1), so this harmless clipping and all arguments of J are justified by its uniform continuity. In detail the beta(j,a) term supplies the displayed profile, while beta(u,a), beta(t-u,j-a), and the denominator beta(t,j) each have normalized logarithm tending uniformly to zero because their complementary indices are at most r. There are at most N summands in (13). A triangle bound therefore gives the uniform upper estimate from (14). This step is used only in the collapsing boundary band and claims no selected oscillatory rate for an interior column. The simple CD measure there is |sigma_(t,j)|=s_(t-j)s_(t+j+1)/(s_t^2 a_j). Its normalized logarithm tends uniformly to zero: its three factorial arguments tend respectively to 0,1,1/2. Summing the squared column bound over at most N magnetic indices yields max_(j<=t<l) E_(t,j) <=exp[N(v8/(2pi)+o(1))]. (15) The smaller constant comes from the strict maximum at x=1/4 of -2J(x)-2J(1/2-x). This estimate retains endpoints and all source phases until the explicitly stated upper-bound step. ## 4. Assemble the real operator and retain the scope The exact generic high adapter duplicates the same physical low blocks. On each complete block M_j has norm E_(t,j); it is zero on the incomplete band. Hence (5),(11) give its full operator and Hilbert--Schmidt rate in (1). On a complete block M_j=(J_t-c_j)Q_j, with uniformly bounded J_t-c_j, providing the matching lower bound for Q_j. The native projector theorem gives its upper bound by a polynomial times the maximum or square sum of ALL energies. Equations (11),(15), and v8/(2pi)<5v3/pi prove the other claim in (1). Fixed generic-q derivatives add only the uniform polynomial factors already proved there. Thus every shrinking SCALED fold window has the same explicit real boundary cost, even when s log N is not o(N). The stronger width here comes from positivity and real physical norms, not from a larger joint complex domain for paired normal currents. No fixed nonzero scaled-width assertion or whole-source volume conjecture follows from this corollary. Audit: [original incomplete-band formula and shrinking-fold source](../experiments/audit_actual_matching_edge_shrinking_fold_native_energy.py). Primary-agent analytical review: PASS. The reader checked the exact center/CD scalar and uniform continuity estimates, original endpoint polynomial and selected negative-root continuation, half-step and center normalizations, all-j highest-factor and phase conversion, incomplete-band support collapse and simple measure, and full Q/M comparisons. The review retains real physical indices and does not enlarge the complex-normal corridor or assert a whole-source limit. Independent analytical review and fresh redirected audit: PASS. The reviewer checked the same center/CD cancellation, actual cubic endpoint selection, half-step comparison, original all-j phase and incomplete-band support, uniform real profiles, and full operator assembly. The replay passed 3,756 original phase identities, including 1,791 incomplete-band values, 202 highest-factor complements, 202 general complete center scalars, and six endpoint polynomial/half-step comparisons. Numerical samples are convention checks; the continuity, root-product and operator arguments prove the stated unrestricted shrinking real window.

title: The original shared Fourier source has an explicit centered quadratic phase
text: # The original shared Fourier source has an explicit centered quadratic phase 30 October 2026. In the exact positive Fourier partition, every Clebsch endpoint phase and every ordinary cup/cap constant cancels explicitly. The remaining original phase is a quadratic form in the shared integer labels, with the original half-twist phases and marked Fourier charge retained. This is an exact source identity, not a claim that its stationary point contributes to the finite sum. ## 1. Exact paired endpoint phase Use the original definitions in [the positive Fourier partition](actual_matching_graph_positive_fourier_partition.md). Put q=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, r=a+w, t=d-|w|, and B_N(a,w)=k_a N s_(a+|w|) /(s_a^2 s_|w|^2 s_(a-|w|)).
