Use the orientation factor epsilon/(2*pi*i). By (3), the inner vertical integral tends to v_(epsilon,a), since its error is O_N(r^(N-a)(1+|log r|)). The paired radial integral converges at zero for precisely the required indices a<N. Equation (7) justifies continuation through R=1 and arbitrary positive R. This proves (9) with its sign and every scalar fixed. Thus the coefficient source is a relative cycle consisting of one lifted circle and one paired radial edge. It is not the circle alone. ## 4. Exact radial modulus and a uniform boundary bound For 0<t<1, conjugate-pair the finite factors in V_epsilon. This gives |V_epsilon(t)|^2=(1-t)(1-t^N)^(-1/N). The remaining modulus in (1) is (1-t^N)^((N+1)/N); the explicitly imaginary logarithmic and dilogarithmic terms have modulus one. Hence |Psi_epsilon(log t)|^2=(1-t)(1-t^N). (10) In fact (10) holds for all t>0. For t>1 its two factors are both negative. To check this extension without choosing fractional powers across the zero, take the real part of (7). On the real radial line, the paired finite terms give d_(log t) log|Psi_epsilon| =-t/[2(1-t)]-N t^N/[2(1-t^N)]. This is the logarithmic derivative of the positive square root of |(1-t)(1-t^N)|. The simple zero at t=1 fixes the same multiplicative constant on both sides by continuity of its nonzero first derivative. For 0<R<=1, (10) gives the UNIFORM estimate |E_(epsilon,a)(R)| <=1/(2*pi) integral_0^R t^(N-a-1) sqrt((1-t)/(1-t^N)) dt <=R^(N-a)/[2*pi*(N-a)]. (11) This includes a=N-1 and R=1; no fixed-distance-from-the-endpoint condition is needed. For R>1 the same calculation yields the explicit bound |E_(epsilon,a)(R)| <=1/[2*pi*(N-a)] +1/(2*pi) integral_1^R t^((N-1)/2-a) dt. (12) Here t^N-1 >= t^(N-1)(t-1). In particular an exterior-radius radial term need not have polynomial size. Its possible exponential rate is retained in (12), rather than discarded in a geometric deformation. If T^N=0 and ||T||<=1, define B_epsilon(T) and E_epsilon(T) using the finite resolvent (tI-T)^(-1). Equivalently sum (8) times T^a. Then (9) and (11), at R=1, give v_(epsilon,N)(T)=B_epsilon(T)-E_epsilon(T), ||E_epsilon(T)|| <= H_N/(2*pi), H_N=sum_(j=1)^N 1/j. (13) This bound is on the FULL source correction, not on its logarithm. The nilpotent resolvent retains the finite original head and introduces no unknown scalar normalization. ### 4a. The shifted full turn and its exact negative-ray source There is a second useful coefficient cycle for the SAME full function. Write Psi=Psi_+ and v_a=v_(+,a). For every R>0 and 0<=a<N put C_a(R)=1/(2*pi) integral_(-pi)^pi Psi(log R+i theta)(R exp(i theta))^(-a) dtheta, J_a(R)=(-1)^(N-a)/(2*pi*i) integral_0^R Psi(log t+i*pi) t^(N-a-1) dt. Then, with the indicated logarithmic marks, exactly v_a=C_a(R)-J_a(R). (13a) The shifted rectangle is holomorphic even though it contains zeros: in the lower half-strip, a cyclotomic point z=-2*pi*i*j/N has residues -j/N and 1+j/N in (7), hence a simple zero of Psi, not a pole. The upper half-strip has the cancellations already proved. Thus the rectangle with imaginary endpoints -pi and pi requires no additional pole residues. Its paired rays satisfy Psi(log t-i*pi)=(1-(-t)^N)Psi(log t+i*pi). Substituting this into the same rectangular argument as Section 3 cancels the central denominator in its radial difference. The phase of (t exp(-i*pi))^(N-a) is exactly (-1)^(N-a), giving (13a). The inner circle tends to v_a for the same reason as before. The selected upper negative ray has the particularly simple EXACT modulus, for ALL t>0, |Psi(log t+i*pi)|^2=1+t. (13b) Indeed in (7) put exp z=-t. Pairing the finite terms gives real part (1/2)[N(-t)^N/(1-(-t)^N)+t/(1+t)]. The second term of (7) cancels its first summand because Re(1+i(log t+i*pi)/(2*pi))=1/2. The remaining logarithmic derivative is t/[2(1+t)]. The anchor Psi->1 at t->0 fixes the constant. When N is even and t=1, the apparent terms cancel at a regular interior-strip point, so the same identity extends through it. Consequently |J_a(R)| <= (1/(2*pi)) integral_0^R sqrt(1+t)t^(N-a-1) dt <=sqrt(1+R) R^(N-a)/[2*pi(N-a)]. (13c) At R=1 this again gives a polynomial original-head bound: the nilpotent unit-shift correction has norm at most sqrt(2)H_N/(2*pi). For R>1 the factor R^(N-a) is retained; no exterior polynomial bound is asserted. The epsilon=-1 identity is the conjugate-reflection of (13a)-(13c). Thus BOTH full angular choices [0,2*pi] and [-pi,pi] have exact original coefficient cycles. In particular the cut prescribed by [the all-radius angular maximum theorem](all_radius_angular_geometric_cycle_and_polarization.md) need not be imposed as a new source choice: its matching ray is specified by (9) or (13a). This fixes the local coefficient cycle, not its whole-word geometric dominance. Carrying those ray terms through the actual positive chart, and proving their total contribution cannot cancel the geometric term, remains necessary. ## 5. Application to every original crossing and its boundary factors At the complete unit meridian the actual transfer shifts have norm at most one in the standard balanced head metric. Their scalar color factors have modulus one. For the actual Q=e^(2*pi*i/N), exactly u_(Q,N)(T)=v_(-,N)(Q^(-1)T). (14) This is the finite factorial reflection, not an asymptotic equality. Equations (9), (13), and (14) therefore treat both types of actual transfer with the literature full function and their retained radial sources. In particular no reciprocal full function with a divergent radial endpoint is needed to represent u. All original factorial diagonals have the same coefficient realization: 1/F_a=Q^(-a) v_(-,a), F_a=N Q^(N-1-a) v_(+,N-1-a), 0<=a<N. (15) At R=1 the radial-error operator norms for these DIAGONAL kernels are, respectively, at most 1/(2*pi) and N/(2*pi). These are maxima of the coefficient bounds, not sums. The positive factorial's original factor N and phase are retained exactly. Insert (9) and (14)-(15) in the strict original signed crossing word. Keep its Gaussian, Cartan, framing, peripheral and original input/output functionals. Expanding the finite product gives an EXACT finite sum over choices of circle or radial source at each atom. The number of choices is fixed by the word, independently of N. Each term is an ordinary full-dilogarithm relative period with the original finite rational kernel/source. Absolute convergence at each fixed N follows coefficientwise from the finite nilpotent resolvents and (8)-(10). This applies to the full original knot scalar, not just an unpointed operator. It does not require a nonzero knot value or division by one. The previous ordinary-Gaussian replacement can also be retained: its diagonal acts on the same finite degrees and the initial domination argument is unchanged. This construction is distinct from the [Hardy forest reduction](actual_hardy_forest_residue_reduction.md). It supplies full-function relative moments on the original finite heads; one must not replace every scalar atom in the unwrapped Laurent graph by (1) and assume that its nonanalytic logarithmic tails are source-null. The radial terms in (9) are exactly what such a substitution would miss. ## 6. What this changes on the path to the geometric period The cyclic atom's accumulating root divisors are not intrinsic barriers to the selected full-function transport. Equations (1), (7), and (9) give the full dilogarithm and its exact coefficient cycle, with an explicit locally polynomial correction at radius one. The independently proved Fourier and pentagon identities for that full function can now be tested against this specified source, rather than against an unspecified state integral or an assumed equivalence of formal jets. Two conclusions do NOT follow. First, a positive geometric change of coordinates must carry the radial edges and finite resolvents as well as the circle integrand. Second, a polynomial norm bound for one radial factor does not make its whole-word contraction exponentially small: the remaining factors and their source can still carry the volume rate. The nonzero geometric image and the global comparison with the marked Rivin period remain unproved. Those, rather than a further choice of local quantum-dilogarithm normalization, are the next required steps. ## 7. Reproducible checks [The main audit](../experiments/audit_actual_modular_dilog_circle.py) checks 30 exact shift/monodromy/modulus instances, 16 entire circle-plus-radial moments, 14 original diagonal/reflection families, and 12 full-strip phase instances at interior, unit, and exterior radii. The moments use the full function, not its truncated polynomial; the bare circle is explicitly checked to give the wrong coefficient. [Results](../experiments/actual_modular_dilog_circle_results.json). [The shifted-circle audit](../experiments/audit_actual_modular_shifted_circle.py) separately checks the negative-ray formula and its exact modulus. These checks supplement the all-level proofs above. Neither audit computes a geometric cycle coefficient or verifies a volume limit.

title: Moving-period factorial normals along logarithmically escaping heads
status: Actual factorial normals for logarithmically escaping heads
text: # Moving-period factorial normals along logarithmically escaping heads 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed source estimate. The marked Gamma factorial remains controlled when a head has imaginary part of order N log N. This is a bound for the actual factorial factors and fixed quantum jets. It does not provide a packet for a polynomial whose critical points merge, or cross an original zero or pole divisor. ## 1. The precise source factors and growing charts Use EXACTLY the interpolant Fhat_P and its logarithmic mark in [the moving-period factorial theorem](actual_moving_period_factorial_normals.md), with P=pi i/(pi i/N+epsilon), d=N-1 fixed. Put L_N=1+log N. Fix positive constants delta,C. The new interior arguments satisfy delta <= Re(z/N) <= 1-delta, |Im(z/N)| <= C L_N. (1) An exterior argument may instead have |Re(z/N)|<=C and delta<=|Im(z/N)|<=C L_N. Choose a fixed integer shift k_N=O(N) which puts its real part in a smaller interior strip, and use the original unit recurrence for that SAME function. The shift stays fixed when epsilon moves. Fixed physical integer arguments 0,...,d are also allowed, by their exact finite factorials. For a fixed finite number of these arguments, there are constants c,C_1, independent of N and the arguments, such that on |epsilon| <= rho_N=c/[N^2 L_N^2] (2) every factor is holomorphic and nonzero, and its relative value and inverse are bounded by C_1. In particular, for every fixed j, |partial_epsilon^j Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)|_(epsilon=0) <= j! C_1 (C_1 N^2 L_N^2)^j |Fhat_N(z)|. (3) The same assertion holds for products and inverses of a fixed number of those factors, their normalized local square-root gauges, and retained powers zeta^E with |E|<=C N^2 L_N^2. All exponential root values and integer-linear characters remain part of the source. ## 2. A direct differentiated Gamma-product bound The convergent product defining G_P gives, at FIXED z, partial_P Log G_P(z)=-z/P +sum_(k>=1) { k psi(Pk+z+1)-k psi(Pk-z) -(2z+1)/P }. (4) It suffices first to work on |P-N|<=c/L_N. All Gamma arguments have positive real part there. Their real parts are at least c_delta N for k=1 and comparable to Nk for k>=2. Take K=ceiling(C_2(1+|z|/N)), C_2 sufficiently large. For k<=K, the uniform right-half-plane digamma expansion psi(w)=Log w+O(1/|w|) applies. Both arguments have size at least c_delta N. Their modulus ratio and the difference of their marked arguments are bounded uniformly: the large imaginary parts enter with opposite signs, and the real-part distance to the strip endpoints is fixed. Hence |psi(Pk+z+1)-psi(Pk-z)|<=C_delta, and the first K terms of (4) have total size O(K^2+K L_N)=O(L_N^2). This includes the case that z stays bounded in scaled coordinates. For k>K, |z+1|/|Pk|<1/4. Expanding the two digammas about Pk shows that their 1/(Pk) term is (2z+1)/(Pk), while their 1/(Pk)^2 terms are EQUAL and cancel. More explicitly the latter coefficient of psi(w+a) is -a^2/2+a/2-1/12, which has the same value at a=z+1 and a=-z. The uniform next remainder gives |k[psi(Pk+z+1)-psi(Pk-z)]-(2z+1)/P| <=C(1+|z|)^3/(N^3 k^2). (5) One may obtain (5) directly by differentiating the convergent Gamma-ratio expansion on a fixed larger relative P disk; the same 1/k cancellation and uniform |z/(Pk)|<1/4 give its bound. Summing (5) costs O((1+|z|/N)^3/K)=O(L_N^2). The initial -z/P term is smaller. Therefore |partial_P Log G_P(z)|<=C L_N^2. (6) The marked elementary exponential converting G_P to Fhat_P has P derivative -pi i z(z+1)/(2P^2), also O(L_N^2). Since |P'(epsilon)|=O(N^2), |partial_epsilon Log Fhat_P(z)|<=C N^2 L_N^2. (7) Disk (2) lies inside the P neighborhood just used. Integrating the actual logarithmic derivative along that disk proves the two-sided relative bound, and Cauchy's formula gives (3). No principal logarithm is reset, and no root-only reflection is differentiated. For completeness, the digamma estimates used here follow from the same uniform complex-sector Stirling expansion used to construct the original product. The Gamma arguments lie in the right half-plane, so its fixed sector can include angles up to pi/2. The finite sum and tail bounds above make explicit their dependence on the growing imaginary argument; a compact-set estimate is not silently reused. ## 3. Exterior rows, fixed endpoints and original gauges For an exterior row the O(N) fixed unit shifts introduce factors 1-exp[2(z+j)Log zeta]. Their scaled imaginary parts remain at least delta/2 on (2). Thus |exp[2(z+j)Log zeta]/(1-exp[2(z+j)Log zeta])|<=C_delta. Each logarithmic epsilon derivative has size O(N L_N), so the whole shift product costs O(N^2 L_N), within (7). Large or small absolute magnitudes of individual factors are NOT bounded away: only their relative variation is being estimated. These magnitudes and all phases remain in the root value. For a fixed physical integer n<=d, the original finite product has logarithmic derivative O(N^2 L_N), including n=d. Its known relative disk contains (2). This keeps the endpoint N-1 fixed rather than replacing it by P-1. Combining the bounds proves the statement for any fixed product, ratio and locally normalized square root. A marked monomial zeta^E has logarithmic derivative E, so it has precisely the additional cost claimed after (3). Consequently the actual moving-factorial cup and cap factors at heads of size O(N log N) have polynomial fixed-jet cost whenever their arguments obey these hypotheses. The same is true of their specified boundary gauges. This does not give a relative estimate for a SUM of white-polynomial terms, and does not replace the actual large generic white by its root-colliding small partner. ## 4. What this resolves at the resonant framing boundary For an actual clock X(r) asymptotic to c r^(2e), e=+1 or -1, on a marked ray r=N R with R in a compact set avoiding zero, its head z=Log X/(2Log q0) has |Im(z/N)|=O(log N). On a fixed logarithmic sheet with bounded real part it falls into the nonreal exterior class above for all sufficiently large N. Thus its large imaginary lift by itself is tame for the actual factorial normals. No bounded-lift hypothesis is falsely invoked. In contrast, a clock tending to one can give a factorial argument approaching an integer zero or pole. Nor does this theorem control a white numerator's endpoint saddle or its resonant coefficient sum. Those need their own exact small-argument products or turning analysis. The original finite support, generic normal, cotangent measure and selected global period remain unchanged and unproved by this estimate. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_moving_period_factorial_logarithmic_escape.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_moving_period_factorial_logarithmic_escape_results.json) retain 12 independent Gamma-tail comparisons, 48 two-sided relative disk checks, 12 genuine fixed-index normals, 12 exact marked unit recurrences and 12 actual opposite-head cup gauges, at 85 digits. The maximum identity error was 2.18e-75. These are diagnostics of the specified function; the uniform estimate is proved above. Independent parent and geometry reviews passed the full proof, including the growing Gamma domain, near/tail cancellation, nonreal shift nonvanishing, fixed endpoint and marked quadratic gauges. Both freshly replayed the focused audit successfully. Their scope is the relative factorial/cup estimate and its genuine fixed jets, not an absolute magnitude, turning packet or global period.

title: The exact factorial interpolant with a moving quantum period
status: Exact two-period section and finite unipotent jet transport
text: # The exact factorial interpolant with a moving quantum period 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. The existing convergent Gamma product extends to the ACTUAL moving quantum parameter. It matches every original finite integer factorial, including the fixed endpoint d=N-1, before taking derivatives. On specified complex index charts it has uniform relative bounds and polynomial cost for every fixed genuine q derivative. The index d stays N-1 when the analytic period moves; no root reflection is differentiated as though d were the moving period minus one. ## 1. The same convergent product at a complex period Fix N>=3, q0=exp(pi i/N), and let zeta=q0 exp(epsilon), P=pi i/Log zeta=N/[1+N epsilon/(pi i)], Q_P=exp(2pi i/P)=zeta^2. (1) The logarithm of zeta is the local one pi i/N+epsilon. Use the analytic Log P near the positive number N and Log(Pk)=Log P+log k. Define, initially where all Gamma arguments have positive real part, G_P(z)=(2pi/P)^z Gamma(z+1) *product_(k>=1) Gamma(Pk+z+1) /[Gamma(Pk-z)(Pk)^(2z+1)], Fhat_P(z)=exp[pi i z(z+1)/(2P)-pi i z/2]G_P(z). (2) This uses the infinite Gamma product from the [exact interpolation theorem](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md), not its finite Barnes product whose number of factors was an integer. The log of the kth factor is locally uniformly O(k^-2), with leading term -z(z+1)(2z+1)/(6P^2 k^2). Its 1/k coefficient vanishes. The Gamma-ratio expansion therefore proves local uniform convergence, including P and z derivatives. The function is holomorphic and nonzero on the initial domain and G_P(0)=1. The Gamma functional equation and the convergent sine product give EXACTLY G_P(z+1)/G_P(z)=2sin(pi(z+1)/P), Fhat_P(z+1)=[1-Q_P^(z+1)]Fhat_P(z), Fhat_P(0)=1. (3) They also define its meromorphic continuation in z. Consequently, with n a fixed nonnegative integer, Fhat_P(n)=(zeta^2;zeta^2)_n. (4) In particular (4) holds for EVERY 0<=n<=d=N-1 on a neighborhood of the original root. This is equality of generic analytic germs, not merely of their root values. The marked power Q_P^z is always exp(2z Log zeta). There is also an exact SECOND difference equation, G_P(z+P)=-2sin(pi z)G_P(z), Fhat_P(z+P)=[1-exp(2pi i z)]Fhat_P(z). (4a) To prove its constant, first take -1<Re z<0, so both z and z+P are in the defining Gamma domain. The quotient of the products truncated at k=K is (2pi/P)^P/[Gamma(z+1)Gamma(-z)] *Gamma(P(K+1)+z+1)Gamma(PK-z) /[P^(2PK)Gamma(K+1)^(2P)]. The last ratio tends to (2pi)^(1-P)P^P by the same uniform complex-sector Stirling formula, with all powers marked by Log P. The Gamma reflection identity then gives -2sin(pi z); equivalently that elementary Gamma identity follows from its convergent product and the sine product already used in (3). Meromorphic continuation proves the first equation globally. The exponential in (2) has P-shift quotient i exp(pi i z), proving the second equation with the displayed scalar ONE. The complex-P reflection is consequently exact as well: G_P(z)G_P(P-1-z)=P, Fhat_P(z)Fhat_P(P-1-z) =P exp[pi i z(z-P+1)/P]. (4b) Indeed the z derivative of the first logarithm, truncated at K, telescopes to psi(PK+z+1)-psi(P(K+1)-z), which tends to zero. Its constant is G_P(P-1). Differentiating (4a) at z=0 gives G_P'(P)=-2pi. Differentiating (3) at z=P-1 gives G_P'(P)=-(2pi/P)G_P(P-1), hence the constant is P. The marked exponentials in (2) then give the second equation of (4b). ## 2. The complex-period asymptotic is uniform Let K be a compact subset of 0<Re x<1. Uniformly for z=Nx, x in K, and P in a sufficiently small relative complex disk about N, put y=z/P. On a slightly smaller disk y stays in a fixed compact of the same strip. The DIRECT Stirling proof in the interpolation theorem then gives Log G_P(z)=P J(y)+(1/2)Log(2P sin(pi y)) +pi cot(pi y)/(12P)+O_K(|P|^-3), (5) where J'=Log(2sin(pi y)) has its original mark, continued from 0<y<1. Formula (5) is proved for complex P term by term: the Gamma arguments z,Pk+z,Pk-z remain in fixed right-half-plane sectors; the kth Stirling remainder is O_K(|P|^-3 k^-3). Summing it is uniform. The sine product sums the leading terms and the cotangent identity sums the 1/P terms just as before. This argument does not interpolate an identity known only at integer periods. The remainder is holomorphic on a larger relative P disk, so its P derivative at FIXED z is O_K(N^-4) by Cauchy's formula. The derivative of the leading term is partial_P[P J(z/P)]=J(y)-y J'(y). The two elementary exponential factors in (2) also have bounded P derivatives on this chart. Thus |partial_P Log Fhat_P(z)|<=C_K. (6) Since |P'(epsilon)|=|P|^2/pi=O(N^2), (6) implies |partial_epsilon Log Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)|<=C_K N^2 (7) for fixed marked z=Nx in this interior chart. The logarithm here is the relative one at epsilon=0. There is no principal-root or dilogarithm reset when epsilon varies. ## 3. Fixed integer shifts cover the nonreal exterior rows Let K be any compact scaled-index set with |x|<=M, |Im x|>=delta>0, z=Nx. (8) Choose on each of finitely many smaller charts an integer k_N, FIXED as epsilon moves, with |k_N|<=C_K N and (z+k_N)/N in a compact subset of 0<Re x<1. Such charts cover K by shifting the real part into the middle of the strip. For k_N>=0, use the exact formula Fhat_P(z)=Fhat_P(z+k_N) /product_(j=1)^(k_N)(1-Q_P^(z+j)); (9) for k_N<0 use the reciprocal-direction finite product. These are evaluations of the SAME meromorphic function by (3), not new independent factorial choices. For epsilon on the disk used below, all intermediate (z+j)/P have imaginary part bounded away from zero. Their real and imaginary parts remain bounded. Therefore each finite sine or Pochhammer factor in (9) and its inverse is bounded by constants depending only on K. Its logarithmic epsilon derivative is -2(z+j) zeta^[2(z+j)]/[1-zeta^[2(z+j)]]=O_K(N). There are O_K(N) factors. Combining this with (7) proves the same O_K(N^2) logarithmic derivative for these exterior rows. In particular negative rows and rows above N are controlled when their scaled imaginary parts stay away from zero. The statement does NOT give a bound across their real integer zeros or poles. Those are retained by the exact interpolation. ## 4. The fixed endpoint and all physical factorials For every original fixed integer 0<=n<=d, use (4) itself. On a sufficiently small disk about epsilon=0, partial_epsilon Log Fhat_P(n) =sum_(j=1)^n -2j zeta^(2j)/(1-zeta^(2j)). (10) At the root |1-q0^(2j)|>=c min(j,N-j)/N. Perturbing epsilon by at most c/[N^2(1+log N)] keeps every denominator comparable to its root value. Summing the displayed elementary bounds gives |partial_epsilon Log Fhat_P(n)| <=C N^2(1+log N), (11) UNIFORMLY in n, including n=d=N-1. No asymptotic estimate at the endpoint x=1 is being inferred from an interior compact. The finite index n, and specifically d, is fixed throughout. At the root one may use the already proved exact identity with N-1-z for evaluating root values. It is NOT an identity with that same fixed endpoint after P moves. For example its generic integer factorial factors have the nonzero logarithmic derivatives (10). Replacing the fixed d by P-1 during differentiation would change the source and is not part of this construction. The second period also supplies an exact normal-transport equation. Put H_N(z)=partial_epsilon Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)|_0, with z FIXED. Since P'(0)=iN^2/pi, differentiating (4a) gives H_N(z+N)=[1-exp(2pi i z)]H_N(z) -(iN^2/pi)partial_z Fhat_N(z+N). (11a) The undivided identity remains meaningful at the physical zeros. The last term is essential: the left argument in (4a) moves with P. Thus actual generic normals do not obey a root-only N-shift rule obtained by omitting that index derivative. More generally put Delta=N-P and c(z)=1-exp(2pi i z). There is the exact local analytic identity Fhat_P(z+N)=exp(Delta partial_z)[c(z)Fhat_P(z)]. (11b) Indeed z+N=(z+Delta)+P, so this is just (4a) at z+Delta. Modulo epsilon^(J+1), Delta belongs to the ideal (epsilon), and the exponential in (11b) is the FINITE differential operator sum_(j=0)^J Delta^j partial_z^j/j!. On a chart where c is a unit, divide by the root multiplier and write U=c^-1 exp(Delta partial_z)c =exp[Delta(partial_z+c'/c)]. The conjugation identity follows by applying partial_z to c times a test function. Its logarithmic connection has explicit simple poles at the integers. On the order-J jet module, U-I raises the epsilon filtration and therefore (U-I)^(J+1)=0. Its inverse is the finite geometric series in -(U-I). This is an actual unipotent transport of finite quantum jets, with the differential correction (11a) at order one. The localization excludes the original c-divisors; the statement does not remove physical support zeros, prove convergence of an infinite jet expansion, or select a global degree cycle. The two exact shifts themselves form a flat rank-one difference connection. With a_P(z)=1-exp[2pi i(z+1)/P], one has a_P(z+P)=a_P(z) and c(z+1)=c(z), so applying the unit shift and the P shift in either order gives the same multiplier. At P=N, their compatibility includes the literal cyclotomic norm product_(j=1)^N(1-exp[2pi i(z+j)/N]) =1-exp(2pi i z). The Gamma product (2) chooses a section of this connection. These equations alone do not establish global uniqueness of a section: a factor periodic under both shifts preserves them. Nor do they determine the original source period or its cycle. ## 5. Uniform relative disks and genuine normal bounds Consider a fixed finite list of factorial arguments, each either * a fixed original integer between 0 and N-1; * z=Nx in a fixed compact of the interior strip; or * z=Nx in a fixed compact satisfying (8), continued by (9). All indices are held fixed when the generic parameter varies. Affine O(1) offsets are allowed by enlarging the compacts slightly. For sufficiently small c_K>0, on |epsilon|<=rho_N=c_K/[N^2(1+log N)] (12) every listed factorial is nonzero and holomorphic, and C_K^-1 <= |Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)/Fhat_N(z)| <= C_K. (13) The same holds for any fixed finite product or quotient of the listed factors. Equations (7),(9),(11), integrated along the epsilon segment, prove (13), with a consistent relative logarithm. Cauchy's formula on (12) proves for every fixed j |partial_epsilon^j Fhat_(P(epsilon))(z)|_0 <=C_(K,j)[N^2(1+log N)]^j |Fhat_N(z)|. (14) Inverse factorials have the corresponding relative bound. In particular the entire assertion holds on the smaller actual normal disk |epsilon|<=c N^-10, at cost at most C_(K,j)N^(10j). The marked factors exp(pi i z), zeta^[z(L-z-1)] and the original physical cup scalar N zeta^(-d^2) cause no further difficulty: L and all indices are O(N), so the epsilon derivative of their logarithms is O_K(N^2), and higher derivatives follow on (12). Thus the original continued cups and inverse cups formed from these factors also satisfy (13),(14). No unit phase is discarded. One can specify the formerly ambiguous off-grid symmetric gauge as well. For a fixed integer L<N, set b_L(epsilon,z)=zeta^[z(L-z)] Fhat_P(z)Fhat_P(L-z)/Fhat_P(L), g_L(epsilon,z)=[b_L(epsilon,z)/b_L(0,z)]^(1/2). (15) Use the analytic square root equal to 1 at epsilon=0. Whenever the two index arguments satisfy the preceding hypotheses, (13) on a smaller disk makes this a specified holomorphic unit with the same relative jet bounds. It is symmetric under z->L-z and agrees with the original physical gauge at every admissible integer index. Its continuation is now fixed by (2), rather than inferred from bounded values on a finite integer set. At epsilon=0 the displayed phases cancel exactly, giving b_L(0,z)=G_N(z)G_N(L-z)/G_N(L). The already proved FIXED-root reflection therefore gives b_d(0,z)=1 meromorphically, also at noninteger z. This is useful for evaluating the root cup. It does not say that b_d(epsilon,z) is constant when P moves. In fact (4b) gives the exact fixed-endpoint correction b_d(epsilon,z)=P/Fhat_P(d) *exp[pi i z(N-P)/P] *Fhat_P(d-z)/Fhat_P(P-1-z). (16) The final quotient retains the difference between the ORIGINAL fixed d=N-1 and the moving endpoint P-1. Formula (16), or its derivative, may be used for boundary transport; replacing that quotient by one away from the root changes the genuine normal. ## 6. Application scope at the slightly nonreal geometric degree For the actual channel cup, the needed arguments are r=a-h and 2a-r, while the physical cups use v,d-v,l,d-l. In the joint deficient geometric corridor take a small but fixed NONZERO imaginary part of the degree. Then r/N and (2a-r)/N lie in nonreal exterior compacts, with opposite imaginary signs; the physical cup arguments have real parts strictly inside (0,1). The remaining factorials F_a,F_m,F_(2a),F_d have fixed integer indices below N. The lemma therefore controls all these explicit boundary factors and their genuine generic derivatives together. It does not justify crossing their real degree poles, deform the original support cycle, or prove a nonzero geometric contribution. Source assembly must still use the actual large-partner white columns and all original tensor marks. The present result is the moving-period analytic input for that assembly, not a replacement for its finite tensor identity or its global period argument. ## 7. Independent checks and review scope The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_moving_period_factorial_normals.py) and its [results](../experiments/actual_moving_period_factorial_normals_results.json) check the actual generic integer factorials, independent Gamma/Barnes evaluations, relative disks, fixed-endpoint derivatives, exterior gauges, second-period and complex-period reflection identities, and fixed-N first and second normal transport. Its largest relative identity error at 85 digits was below 5.3e-82. These finite checks support, and do not replace, the proofs above. Independent analytical reviews by the root, cluster-source and geometry agents passed the moving-period construction and its stated bounds. The geometry agent freshly replayed the base audit; the root freshly replayed the entire augmented audit, including the transport block. The root and cluster-source agents also checked the exact second-period, moving reflection and fixed-N normal formulas; the root checked the finite-jet corollary. The review does not assert global degree transport across the retained divisors or a contributing quantum cycle.

title: Actual multichannel Newton transport beyond the tame figure-eight source
text: # Actual multichannel Newton transport beyond the tame figure-eight source 28 October 2026. The actual five-crossing Newton source does NOT have a polynomially bounded coefficient vector. This can be proved directly, without using its volume theorem: a uniformly dominated initial transfer branch forces exponential growth of a genuine Newton coefficient. Consequently a polynomially bounded source-preserving comparison to the previous tame UL response cannot exist in this universal Newton basis. There is nevertheless a source-exact two-channel replacement. Both endpoint source vectors have polynomial norms. Forward and backward Green transport therefore give a strictly sharper coefficient barrier than the one-sided largest-root bound. Combining it with the ORIGINAL complete evaluation, and then the audited root-color Plancherel identity, gives an unconditional quantitative upper bound for this full source. Its barrier is about 0.57776, whereas the selected invariant's known rate is about 0.45011. The remaining outer phase cancellation has not been eliminated. The matrix estimate in Section 4 applies to fixed-channel recurrences generally. No new knot class or general volume bound is claimed. ## 1. The original coefficients and their exact monic recurrence The independently proved WHOLE-source transform in `five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md` gives, at every primitive root, F_N(Y)=sum_(n=0)^(N-1) C_n T_n(Y), T_n(Y)=product_(r=1)^n(Y+Y^-1-Q^r-Q^-r), C_n=(-1)^n t^(n(n+3)/2) J_n(t), t=Q^-1, J_n(t)=sum_(j=0)^n t^(j(j+1)){n choose j}_t. (1) All original turns, Cartan scalars and framing are included in that identity. No coefficient is chosen to fit an unknown scalar. The phases preceding J_n have modulus one at the specified root. The coefficients satisfy, GENERICALLY in t, J_0=1, J_1=1+t^2, J_n=(1+t-t^n+t^(2n))J_(n-1) -t(1-t^(n-1))J_(n-2). (2) Here is an elementary derivation. Put F_n=(t;t)_n and, formally, E(z)=sum_(k>=0)z^k/F_k, G(z)=sum_(j>=0)t^(j(j+1))z^j/F_j, H(z)=sum_(n>=0)J_n z^n/F_n=E(z)G(z). Coefficient comparison gives E(tz)=(1-z)E(z) and G(z)-G(tz)=t^2 z G(t^2z). Eliminating E yields (1-z)(1-tz)H(z)-(1-tz)H(tz)-t^2zH(t^2z)=0. Its n-th coefficient is (2). This is a formal identity before root specialization; at n<N no vanishing factorial is divided out. With w_n=(J_n,J_(n-1))^t, n>=1, the actual transfer is w_n=M_(N,n)w_(n-1), M_(N,n)=[[1+t-t^n+t^(2n), -t(1-t^(n-1))], [1, 0 ]]. (3) Its leading coefficient is ONE, so there is no singular forward division. Its determinant is t(1-t^(n-1)), nonzero for 2<=n<=N-1. ## 2. The terminal source is known and polynomial too At t^N=1, root reflection gives {N-1 choose j}_t=(-1)^j t^(-j(j+1)/2). Thus J_(N-1) is the explicit quadratic Gauss sum sum_(j=0)^(N-1)(-1)^j t^(j(j+1)/2), of modulus at most N. Likewise {N-2 choose j}_t={N-1 choose j}_t (1-t^(-1-j))/(1-t^-1). Since |1-t^-1|>=4/N, (1) proves |J_(N-2)|<=N^2/2. Therefore both w_1 and the ACTUAL terminal w_(N-1) have polynomial norms. These endpoint bounds are finite coefficient identities, not an assumption that the desired Kashaev value is small. ## 3. A direct all-level obstruction to a tame UL coefficient response For x=n/N let z=exp(-2pi i x). The continuous transfer limit is M(x)=[[2-z+z^2, -(1-z)], [1,0]], p(z,L)=L^2-(2-z+z^2)L+1-z. (4) For 0<=x<=1/32, |z-1|<=pi/16<1/5. Hence |2-z+z^2-2|<1/5 and |1-z|<1/5. On |L-2|=1/2, the unperturbed |L(L-2)| is at least 3/4, whereas the perturbation is at most (1/5)(5/2)+(1/5)=7/10. Rouche's argument gives a single analytic root L_+ in that disk, so |L_+|>=3/2. The other root has modulus at most (1/5)/(3/2)=2/15. The eigenvectors (L_+,1) and (L_-,1) give a uniformly smooth, invertible eigenframe on this interval. In that frame each finite step (3) equals diag(L_+,L_-)+O(1/N), uniformly, including the frame change at adjacent x. Its initial vector w_1 tends to (2,1), the L_+ eigenvector at x=0. The ratio of the second component to the first is O(1/N) initially and remains O(1/N): the offdiagonal entries are O(1/N), while |L_-/L_+|<=4/45<1. Induction therefore keeps a fixed O(1/N) cone. The first component is multiplied at each step by L_+(x)+O(1/N), and the resulting product error is bounded above and below by constants on this fixed-length x interval. The original first coordinate J_n has the same exponential rate. For n=floor(N/32), this proves the unconditional lower estimate liminf_N (1/N)log||C^(N)||_2 >=log(3/2)/32>0. (5) The tame fixed-window UL theorem has polynomial coefficient response. Equation (5) therefore rules out representing THIS actual coefficient vector by that response under a comparison whose map AND inverse have polynomial norms and preserve the pointed source. In particular a diagonal unitary phase gauge cannot fix it. This statement does not rule out a different metric, a genuine multichannel transport, or later source-exact fusion; their exponential evaluation cost must stay. ## 4. A uniform two-boundary matrix estimate Let T_(N,n) be a fixed-size matrix family converging uniformly to continuous T(x). Suppose rho(T(x)) and rho(adj T(x)) are positive on the parameter interval, and every actual determinant in its interior is nonzero. For a specified solution with polynomial endpoint norms, forward and backward propagation give (1/N)log||w_n|| <=min{ H_f(n/N), H_b(n/N)}+o(1), (6) uniformly in n, where H_f(x)=integral_0^x log rho(T(s))ds, H_b(x)=integral_x^1 log rho(adj T(s))ds -lim (1/N)sum_(ell=n+1)^(N-1)log|det T_(N,ell)|. An endpoint factorial product or leading-germ identity must justify the last limit uniformly; it is not silently inferred at an exact zero. To prove the numerator estimates, fix epsilon>0 and use the positive Lyapunov metric H_eps(x)=sum_(k>=0)(T(x)^*)^k T(x)^k /(rho(T(x))+epsilon)^(2k). For bounded matrices of fixed size this converges uniformly, is continuous, is at least I and bounded above. In its norm, a step costs at most rho(T(x))+epsilon+o(1); neighboring metric changes cost 1+o(1). Products over ANY prefix therefore obey the integral bound uniformly in the prefix endpoint. Apply the same argument to adj T in reverse order, and use the EXACT identity T^-1=adj T/det T. The polynomial endpoint norms cost o(N). Let epsilon decrease to zero. Positivity of the continuous spectral radii makes the logarithmic limit uniform. This proves (6), with the original endpoint vectors retained. It is a source-sensitive bound on a specified solution, not a claim that the entire inverse norm is controlled or that every growing channel couples to the source. ## 5. Actual two-channel barrier and the full Fourier energy For (4), write R(x)=rho(M(x)) and H(x)=integral_0^x log R(s)ds, J(x)=integral_0^x log(2sin(pi s))ds. The eigenvalues are explicit: L_±=(2-z+z^2 ± z sqrt(z^2-2z+5))/2. (7) The square root has its principal analytic branch here, since its argument has real part at least 7/2 on the unit circle. R is continuous and positive; for example |2-z+z^2|^2>=7/8 gives R>=sqrt(14)/8. For a two-by-two matrix, rho(adj M)=rho(M). The determinant product in backward propagation is exactly product_(ell=n+1)^(N-1)|det M_(N,ell)| =|F_(N-2)|/|F_(n-1)|. (8) The endpoint-uniform factorial estimate and |F_(N-2)|=O(N^2) give its logarithm as -N J(n/N)+O(log N), uniformly for n>=1. Thus (1/N)log|C_n| <=h(n/N)+o(1), h(x)=min{H(x), H(1)-H(x)+J(x)}. (9) Retain the ORIGINAL complete evaluation T_n(1)=|F_n|^2 in (1). The triangle bound on this exact sum, now with its n-dependent coefficient transport retained, gives limsup_N (1/N)log|K_N| <=B_2:=max_(0<=x<=1){2J(x)+h(x)}. (10) By the independently audited ordinary-color theorem, the full root-color Fourier energy E_N=|K_N|^2+poly(N) consequently satisfies limsup_N (pi/N)log E_N<=2pi max(0,B_2). (11) This use of Plancherel keeps the actual cancellations of ordinary rows; bounding every entry of the Newton evaluation matrix separately would lose that information and give a larger estimate. There is a useful exact simplification of (10). R(1-x)=R(x), J(1-x)=-J(x), and d/dx[2H(x)-J(x)] =log(|L_max(x)|/|L_min(x)|)>=0. The switch in (9) is therefore at x=1/2. Since J<=0 on [0,1/2], B_2=max_(0<=u<=1/2){H(u)-3J(u)}. (12) This is a completely specified one-variable positive-norm barrier, not the desired volume inserted as a hypothesis. The audit bounds it rigorously between 0.5775 and 0.5780; its numerical value is approximately 0.57776062097. It improves the one-sided envelope, approximately 0.94608, but is above the known selected rate 0.45010961003. Hence even these two exact endpoint sources do not eliminate the remaining outer phase. ### 5.1 A certificate for the global norm barrier The location of the maximum in (12), and the quoted interval, can be verified without an unproved plot. Put v=4sin^2(pi u), so 0<=v<=4. The derivative of H-3J has the sign of log[R/v^(3/2)]. For v<1, R>=sqrt(|1-z|)=v^(1/4)>v^(3/2), so the derivative is positive. For v>1 use the quadratic Schur test on L^2-A L+B, with A=2-z+z^2 and B=1-z. Its roots lie inside radius r precisely when |B|<r^2 and |r^2 A-B conjugate(A)|<r^3-|B|^2/r. To prove this test, normalize r=1 and subtract b times the reversed conjugate polynomial from w^2+a w+b. On the unit circle the subtracted term has modulus |b| times the original. Rouche's argument reduces the root count to w[(1-|b|^2)w+a-b conjugate(a)], giving the stated inequality. Here r=v^(3/2). The first condition is exactly v>1; squaring the second and using z+z^(-1)=2-v reduces it to P(v)>0, where P(v)=v^10-2v^9+6v^8-9v^7+9v^6-6v^5 -2v^4+5v^3-4v^2+1. (12a) The identities used in this reduction are |A|^2=4-5v+2v^2 and conjugate(B)A^2+B conjugate(A)^2=v(v^3-5v^2+9v-4). The exact Euclidean Sturm sequence for P has sign variations 4 at v=1 and 3 at v=4, omitting zero terms. It also has variations 4 and 3 at 57/50 and 29/25 respectively. Thus P has exactly one root v_* in (1,4), with 57/50<v_*<29/25. Since P(1)<0 and P(4)>0, the derivative changes from positive to negative there. This proves that u_*=asin(sqrt(v_*)/2)/pi is the UNIQUE global maximizer in (12). The audit computes the exact Sturm signs and verifies the polynomial reduction before any numerical integration. On 0<=u<=u_* the larger-modulus root is L_+ in (7). Indeed equality of root moduli would force A^2/B real. Its imaginary part can vanish, away from the endpoints, only if 4c^3-6c^2+5c-1=0, c=cos(2pi u). For c>=2/5 that polynomial is positive, since its derivative is 12(c-1/2)^2+2 and its value at 2/5 is positive. Here c>=1-v_*/2>2/5, so no root-modulus crossing occurs before u_*. For the actual rigorous interval in the audit, isolate v_* to a rational width below 10^(-35), use interval arithmetic for u_*, and integrate log|L_+| by 4096 interval RANGE cells on [0,u_*]. Every cell's whole image is enclosed, so this is a rigorous integral bound without a quadrature error assumption. The log-sine primitive is evaluated by J(u)=-Im Li_2(exp(2pi i u))/(2pi), also with complex interval arithmetic. The resulting enclosure lies strictly between 0.5775 and 0.5780. ## 6. The same two-channel system retains the geometric algebra The failure of polynomial coefficient growth does not sever the source from the geometric curve. Before taking absolute values, the coefficient phase in (1) changes its consecutive ratio to -z L. Complete Newton evaluation contributes -(1-z)^2/z. Thus the joint complex stationary equation is L(1-z)^2=1. Eliminating L from this and (4) gives exactly -z^2(z^3-4z^2+7z-5)=0. (13) The nonzero cubic has discriminant -23 and is the already identified five-crossing geometric critical field. Equation (13) is an algebraic coupling calculation, not a new thimble-selection or cancellation proof. It makes precise what the wider mechanism must retain: the non-tame coefficient channel together with the evaluation phase, rather than separate positive norm maxima. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_multichannel_newton_green.py): generic finite identities, all-index actual root coefficients, both polynomial endpoint vectors, exact determinant products, dominated initial branch, two-sided propagation diagnostics, certified barrier, and cubic elimination.

title: The native highest-weight energy has a geometric action
status: Local energy cells; global phase gap retained
text: # The native highest-weight energy has a geometric action 30 October 2026. The exponential native projector cost is already geometric in a simple physical block. Its exact normalization also shows why a general comparison cannot assign a positive volume to every normalized magnetic summand or discard the phases at a maximum. ## 1. Exact highest-weight energy, both parities Put q=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, s_r=product_(h=1)^r 2sin(pi h/N), and choose 0<=j<=floor(d/2). In the physical degree t=j the original normalized column is a highest vector. Its exact entries are f_u=C_j(q;j,u)=q^(ju) s_j/(s_u s_(j-u)), 0<=u<=j. (1) This follows directly from the original generic highest-vector ratio: at the root its negative-index Pochhammer factors give q^(u^2) [j choose u]_(q^2), and the Gaussian binomial has phase q^[u(j-u)] and positive magnitude s_j/(s_u s_(j-u)). The generic source is specialized only after this calculation. The actual Christoffel--Darboux measure of this simple degree block is |sigma_(j,j)|=s_(2j)/s_j^2. (2) For 2j<d, cancel the last factor in the original formula s_(2j+1)/(s_j^2 |1-q^(4j+2)|). For the odd simple midpoint 2j=d, the separately retained measure N/s_j^2 is the same expression, since s_d=N. No zero denominator is evaluated in this cancellation. Therefore its native rank-one projector norm is exactly E_(j,j)=sum_(u=0)^j W_N(j,u), W_N(j,u)=s_j^4/[s_(2j)s_u^2 s_(j-u)^2]. (3) For j<d-j this is the degree-t=j block of the completed cluster projector, not the singular individual projector on larger degrees. For 2j=d it is the degree-t=j block of the isolated midpoint projector. Formula (3) does not maximize over the other physical degrees of either operator. ## 2. Its complete local variational profile Let J(x)=integral_0^x log(2sin(pi y))dy. The endpoint-controlled factorial estimate log s_r=N J(r/N)+O(log N), uniform for 0<=r<N, gives, with xi=j/N and x=u/N, N^(-1)log W_N(j,u)=e(xi,x)+O(log N/N), e(xi,x)=4J(xi)-J(2xi)-2J(x)-2J(xi-x). (4) This is uniform on 0<=x<=xi<=1/2, with continuous endpoint values. For fixed 0<xi<=1/2 the action is strictly concave in 0<x<xi: e_x=2 log[sin(pi(xi-x))/sin(pi x)], e_xx=-2pi sin(pi xi)/[sin(pi x)sin(pi(xi-x))]<0. (5) Its unique maximum is x=xi/2. The actual discrete support contains a point within 1/N of this maximum, and has at most N points. Bounding (3) between its largest summand and N times that summand therefore proves, whenever j/N tends to xi in [0,1/2], lim N^(-1)log E_(j,j)=m(xi), m(xi)=4J(xi)-J(2xi)-4J(xi/2). (6) This statement includes both level parities. Moreover m'(xi)=2 log[cos(pi xi/2)/cos(pi xi)]>0 (0<xi<1/2), m(0)=0, m(1/2)=-4J(1/4)=v8/(2pi). (7) For even N=2h and j=h-1, the actual measure in (2) is 1/sin(pi/N); for odd N=2h+1,j=h it is one. This polynomial difference does not change the common folded limit (7). Thus the native exponential obstruction is not restricted to odd levels. ## 3. Four actual ideal tetrahedra at the folded color Write Lambda(a)=-integral_0^a log|2sin b|db, so J(x)=-Lambda(pi x)/pi. At xi=1/2, (4) becomes 2pi e(1/2,x) =4[Lambda(pi x)+Lambda(pi(1/2-x))] =4 Vol T(pi x,pi(1/2-x),pi/2), 0<x<1/2. (8) The tetrahedra in (8) have positive angles summing to pi. They also glue to an explicit convex ideal octahedron O_x. In the upper half-space boundary take its six ideal vertices to be 0, infinity, 1, -1, zeta, -zeta, zeta=exp(2pi i x). (9) The four unit-circle vertices form a Euclidean rectangle. Their unit-hemisphere plane separates the other two vertices. The upper half is the ideal quadrangular pyramid with apex infinity; reflection in that hemisphere gives the lower half with apex zero. Split the base along the diameter from 1 to -1. The two upper tetrahedra have the Euclidean triangle (1,zeta,-1), or (1,-zeta,-1), as a horospherical triangle at infinity. Each has angles pi x,pi(1/2-x),pi/2, up to permutation. Reflection gives two more tetrahedra of the same volume. These four tetrahedra fill the convex hull in (9). One can check the supporting planes directly: the vertical halfspace over each rectangle edge contains the origin, because the rectangle contains its center. It therefore contains ALL six vertices. Reflecting that halfspace in the unit hemisphere fixes the four rectangle vertices and exchanges zero and infinity, so the four lower face halfspaces contain all six vertices as well. Their eight triangular faces form the octahedral boundary. Along a shared rectangle edge, the two interior dihedral angles sum to either 2pi x or pi-2pi x, both strictly less than pi. The remaining pyramid edges have angle pi/2. Thus the joined boundary is locally convex; equivalently its eight triangular face planes support all six vertices. There is no hidden negative-volume piece. It follows that 2pi e(1/2,x)=Vol(O_x). At x=1/4 its eight faces form the regular ideal octahedron and its volume is v8. Equation (5) gives this as the unique maximum in this family. This is a geometric interpretation of ONE native degree-block energy, not a claim that this octahedron is already a cell in the supplied link complement. ## 4. The compulsory face subtraction away from the fold The same interpretation is signed for other colors. The elementary duplication identity Lambda(2a)=2Lambda(a)-2Lambda(pi/2-a) converts (4), for 0<x<xi<1/2, to 2pi e(xi,x) =4 Vol T(pi x,pi(xi-x),pi(1-xi)) -4Lambda(pi(1/2-xi)). (10) The second term is forced by the original measure (2). It is positive before its subtraction, since Lambda is positive on (0,pi/2). At x=0 the tetrahedron flattens and e(xi,0)=-(2/pi)Lambda(pi(1/2-xi))<0. (11) Consequently no representation of EVERY CD-normalized magnetic summand's action as a sum of nonnegative ideal-cell volumes can be correct without additional boundary terms or cancellations. This does not prevent the completed energy from having a positive geometric maximum: (6),(7) prove that its maximum is strictly positive. It identifies a necessary normalization in any such argument. ## 5. What a shared-variable action must retain For general physical degree and channel, the exact local energy is sum_u |C_j(t,u)|^2/|sigma_(t,j)|. On strict compacts where the selected ordinary packet applies, its summand has the action 2 Re Phi_xi(tau,nu)-kappa(tau,xi), (12) where kappa is the leading logarithm of the ACTUAL measure. Here tau, nu and xi are real admissible scaled physical indices; the complex packet supplies their selected action, not a different complex-degree operator norm. In the two chambers supplied by its factorial formulas, kappa=J(tau-xi)+J(tau+xi)-2J(tau), tau+xi<1, kappa=J(tau-xi)+J(tau+xi-1)-2J(tau), tau+xi>1. (13) The odd self-paired endpoint has the corresponding limit 2J(tau-1/2)-2J(tau). Polynomial factors in the finite measures do not contribute to (13). Formula (12) describes a normalized summand; the sum over u and the sum over physical degree are still to be taken. If a positive comparison energy is constructed by sewing these actual columns, its candidate action is the SUM of (12), together with the remaining original boundary weights, restricted to the SAME magnetic wire variables and exact affine degree constraints used in that sewing. Taking separate maxima in tau or nu before sewing changes that variational problem. Neither the existence of such a useful global comparison nor its equality with the manifold's angle-volume problem is proved here. The selected geometric framing generally gives COMPLEX magnetic coordinates. The localization theorem puts them in the selected physical tube, but does not put them on the real grid defining this positive energy. An identification with a real angle polytope, or a justified deformation of the original sum, is therefore an additional step; the local complex packet alone supplies neither. There is a further exact local warning about stationarity. Equation (1) has the marked highest-weight action Phi_high(xi,x)=J(xi)-J(x)-J(xi-x)+pi i xi x. At the energy maximum x=xi/2, partial_x Phi_high=pi i xi, exp(partial_x Phi_high)=exp(pi i xi). (14) At the folded value this multiplier is i, although the real energy derivative vanishes. Real-energy stationarity constrains the modulus of a transport multiplier; it does not by itself impose its marked phase or a full complex gluing equation. In a real link network those phases may cancel through the actual shared incidence and boundary characters, but that requires a separate proof. This example does not assert that an open column ought to have trivial boundary momentum. Thus the missing global bridge is precise: construct the actual sewn energy with its signed face terms and shared variables, and prove that its stationarity, INCLUDING the retained phase and peripheral conditions, gives the degree-one geometric gluing. The local octahedral volume and the correctly normalized summands alone do not establish that bridge or a nonzero original quantum period. ## 6. The larger full folded cost is twice an ideal cube volume The separate [full magnetic-energy theorem](actual_matching_edge_magnetic_energy_profile.md) now computes the full folded operator rate as 5v3/pi, with effective volume 10v3, for the odd simple projector and the actual even completed pair. This maximizes over physical degree and is strictly larger than the highest-weight block cost in (8). Here is an explicit local polyhedron with that larger two-copy volume. In Minkowski coordinates with form (-+++), let V_epsilon=(sqrt(3),epsilon_1,epsilon_2,epsilon_3), epsilon_i in {+1,-1}. These null vectors project to the eight Klein vertices of the cube [-1/sqrt(3),1/sqrt(3)]^3. The four vertices with product epsilon_i=+1 form a regular ideal tetrahedron: every distinct pair has the same Lorentz product, and the signed coordinate symmetries permute its vertices. Its face opposite V_epsilon has normal n_epsilon=(1,-sqrt(3)epsilon_1, -sqrt(3)epsilon_2,-sqrt(3)epsilon_3), <n_epsilon,n_epsilon>=8, <V_epsilon,n_epsilon>=-4sqrt(3). Reflection in that face sends the opposite vertex to V_epsilon-2<V_epsilon,n_epsilon>n_epsilon/8 =2V_(-epsilon). (15) Thus the four adjacent corner tetrahedra are also regular ideal tetrahedra, congruent to the central one. They fill the cube without overlap. Indeed the central tetrahedron has the four Klein inequalities epsilon dot x>=-1/sqrt(3), for sign triples of product +1. Inside the cube, two such inequalities cannot fail simultaneously: adding them would violate one coordinate bound of the cube. The part failing one inequality is precisely the tetrahedron with its opposite cube corner and the three neighboring central vertices. This gives the usual central tetrahedron and four corner tetrahedra as an actual geometric partition. Each original cube edge lies in one regular tetrahedron and has dihedral angle pi/3. Along each triangulated square-face diagonal, three tetrahedral angles add to pi. This is the regular ideal six-square-faced cube, with its stated angle data. Consequently this regular ideal cube has volume 5v3, and TWO copies have volume 10v3. This is an exact geometric interpretation of the local full folded COST. It supplies no face pairing, cusp marking, degree-one chain, or volume upper inequality for the original link complement. Attaching the local cube to a source diagram remains a separate shared-incidence problem. Focused audit: [original highest vectors, CD measures and ideal shapes](../experiments/audit_actual_native_magnetic_energy_local_geometry.py). It verifies 817 original finite highest-vector entries with their phases, 167 bilinear measures, 23 even/odd folded measure formulas, and all four actual tetrahedron cross ratios. The global sewing and phase-matching problem is not a conclusion of these checks. The cube addition also checks all four Lorentz reflections (15) exactly. Independent analytical reviews of sections 1--5: PASS. The root reader checked the original highest-vector phase, both parity measures, uniform local action and its strict maximum, the eight supporting planes and four tetrahedra, the compulsory signed term, and the distinction between real-energy and complex-phase stationarity. A second reader independently derived those formulas and freshly replayed the focused audit, reproducing all 817 source, 167 measure, 23 parity and four shape checks. Both reviews retain the degree-block scope and infer no cells in the actual source complement, real-grid geometric saddle, or global volume equality. Section 6 review: a second reader independently checked the four Lorentz reflections, central/corner partition and regular ideal tetrahedra, and freshly replayed the enlarged audit including all four cube reflections. The resulting cube volume is a local boundary-cost interpretation only; no identification with the right-angled matching polyhedron is inferred. The primary reader also independently verified the Lorentz reflection, the impossibility of two failed central halfspaces, all five regular tetrahedra, the cube-edge and face-diagonal angle sums, and the exact 5v3 single-cube volume, with the same topology limitation.

title: The actual graph complement from one rectified core and octahedra
text: # The actual graph complement from one rectified core and octahedra 29 October 2026. This is a general GEOMETRIC theorem for the literal ordered noncrossing (NC) cubic sources. It gives the actual complete hyperbolic volume, rather than a scalar-vertex volume surrogate. Its input is a finite positive right-angled ideal core certificate. It does not prove the growing-color quantum asymptotic. Let Gamma be a connected plane cubic graph in the original NC source class, with b black and b white vertices and E=3b edges. Keep a crossing circle on each physical edge box. Suppose Q is a convex right-angled ideal polyhedron with the following labeled medial incidence: * Its ideal vertices x_e are the edges e of Gamma. * At every vertex v of Gamma there is a triangular face T_v with the three incident edge labels. * At every face f of Gamma there is a polygon F_f following its edge boundary. Every polyhedral edge separates a T_v from an F_f. The certificate includes the labeled oriented face cycles and positive supporting-plane inequalities. In particular a matching unlabeled polyhedron or cusp count is not sufficient. Such a Q will be called the ideal rectified core; this term means the ideal medial polyhedron, not the untruncated projective polyhedron used in some literature. Then the ACTUAL retained-circle source link L_Gamma(e), with any fixed signed edge twist integers e, has a complete hyperbolic metric and Vol(S^3 minus L_Gamma(e)) = 4b v8 + 2 Vol(Q). (1) The topology and peripheral crossings in this assertion are those of the original cups, caps and edge boxes. No quantum twist has been removed. Equation (1) is the target for an eventual full-source limit, not a proof of that limit. ## 1. A finite explicit octahedron on an ideal triangle Use the Lorentz product of signature (-,+,+,+). Normalize the three future null lifts a,b,c of a triangular face so that their pairwise products are -1. This is possible uniquely by positive rescaling: the three scale products are prescribed positive numbers. Let n be its outward unit spacelike normal. The regular ideal octahedron on the OTHER side of this face has three further vertices a' = b+c+sqrt(2)n, b' = c+a+sqrt(2)n, c' = a+b+sqrt(2)n. (2) These are future null vectors. Opposite pairs (a,a'), (b,b'), (c,c') have product -2 and every other pair has product -1. Thus the six vectors are Lorentz isometric to the standard regular ideal octahedron: four independent vectors determine an isometry by their Gram matrix, and the remaining two satisfy the same linear equations. The choice of +n places its interior outside Q. The three octahedral faces adjacent to the attaching face merge with the corresponding F_f faces. Indeed their third vertices have the form a+b+sqrt(2)n. If m is the normal of F_f along the edge ab, then <m,a>=<m,b>=<m,n>=0, the last equality being the right-angle condition. Thus all three vertices lie in that same supporting plane. The remaining boundary faces are an opposite WHITE triangle (a',b',c') and three SHADED triangles S_(v,e_a)=(a,b',c'), and cyclically. (3) Their outward unit normals are respectively n_white=2n+(a+b+c)/sqrt(2), n_a=n+sqrt(2)a, and cyclically. (4) Their incident products vanish. Equations (2)--(4) prove directly that all the surviving boundary dihedral angles are right angles. Attach an octahedron along EVERY T_v. This is an abstract gluing of convex cells along full ideal faces. The union is topologically a ball: the attaching triangles have disjoint interiors, and the same statement holds after small cusp truncation. We do not need to assume that all developed octahedra in a chosen global drawing have disjoint interiors. The intrinsic cell metric and the actual face identifications below are enough to construct the complete manifold. Flat boundary seams are merged only as intrinsic coplanar faces. Each original F_f is an ideal polygon. An attached coplanar triangle lies outside one of its sides, with its third ideal vertex on the empty ideal-boundary interval between that side's endpoints. Different sides have disjoint such intervals. These attachments therefore form an embedded ideal polygon with twice as many vertices. This also justifies the merged white-face isometries used below. ## 2. The complete labeled bowtie cell Call the resulting ball P. It contains Q and exactly 2b octahedra, with disjoint interiors in its intrinsic cell decomposition. Hence Vol(P)=Vol(Q)+2b v8. (5) It has 3E ideal vertices: E original x_e and three new vertices for each of the 2b original graph vertices. Its shaded faces are the 2E triangles S_(v,e). Its white faces are the 2b opposite octahedral triangles and the b+2 expanded old face polygons, hence E+2 in total. Every boundary edge separates a white and a shaded face. The boundary has 6E edges and Euler characteristic 2. For each edge e=vw, the two shaded triangles S_(v,e),S_(w,e) meet at x_e. They are precisely the two sides of its retained crossing disk. Their other vertices correspond to the two physical strand arcs at that end of the box. At each trivalent graph vertex the three original nested cup/cap arcs connect the three incident disks in a triangle. Consequently the white-face and cusp incidence is exactly the Fisher expansion T(Gamma), as independently traced in [the actual boundary construction](actual_six_pants_boundary_torsor_and_sewing.md). This is a reversible topological cut: shrink each opposite white triangle toward the original vertex cup/cap matching; trace each expanded F_f along the original planar region; restore each pair of shaded triangles as its crossing disk. It recovers the literal NC diagram. In particular it does not use an arbitrary incidence permutation in place of the original ordered ports. Take two copies P^0,P^1 with opposite orientations. Glue each WHITE face across the copies by its labels. At e=vw an even box twist glues S_(v,e) to S_(w,e) within each copy, fixing x_e and matching the actual two strand positions. An odd twist uses the opposite copy and exchanges these two outer strand positions. These are exactly the disk maps from the original two-strand box; the same orientation rule is written explicitly for theta in [the marked-theta geometry](actual_marked_theta_link_and_angle_geometry.md). Because every shaded face is an ideal triangle, each prescribed vertex bijection is an isometry. Around every actual boundary edge the alternating white and disk maps give four right angles. At an old flat seam the two copies supply two angles pi. Internal attaching faces already have smooth neighborhoods. Thus all finite edge and face neighborhoods in the glued cell metric are hyperbolic. ## 3. Simultaneous horospheres and completeness Completeness requires more than the angle sums. At an original ideal vertex x_e the Q link is a Euclidean rectangle. Its two opposite sides belong to T_v and T_w, and have equal length on EVERY horosphere. Normalize its horosphere so that this length is 1. Do this independently at each original ideal vertex. On each triangular T_v, all three corner horocycle segments now have length 1: they are its canonical mutually tangent decoration. Equality of opposite rectangle sides shows there is no incompatibility between the two triangles at x_e. Equip each attached regular octahedron with its canonical decoration having side length 1 at every cusp square. Its three old vertex horospheres then agree with those just chosen on Q. Its new vertices use that same canonical decoration. Every S_(v,e) consequently has the canonical decoration at ALL THREE corners. Every shaded face pairing, including an outer-vertex exchange, preserves it. White pairings preserve decorations because they join identical copies. After uniformly shrinking these horospheres, they are disjoint and the complement of their ends is compact. The ideal links glue as compact nonsingular Euclidean surfaces. They are orientable, and the reversible link cut identifies them as the link's cusp tori. There is no dilation holonomy. Their ends are complete standard hyperbolic cusps. This proves completeness and finite volume of the literal link complement, with volume twice (5), establishing (1). Further full twists are crossing-disk collar homeomorphisms while the circle remains drilled. They change the preferred peripheral marking by the actual integral shear. They do not change the unmarked complete volume. The quantum twist phases and any later filling slopes must still retain that shear. ## 4. Algebraic input and an explicit nondegenerate example The input is finite real-algebraic data: future null vertex lifts, spacelike outward face normals, incidence equalities, strict supporting inequalities, the labeled convex face cycles, and vanishing Lorentz products at adjacent faces. A finite convex-hull/incidence check certifies the stated Q. Formulae (2)--(4) use only arithmetic and positive square roots. No limiting geometric realization or a choice of formal peripheral series is needed for this complete anchor. For the cube graph, the core is explicitly the convex hull in the Klein ball of (±1,±1,0)/sqrt(2) and their coordinate permutations. (6) Its six square planes are ±X_i=1/sqrt(2). Its eight triangular planes are ±X_1±X_2±X_3=sqrt(2). The corresponding Lorentz normals have norms squared 1/2 and 1, respectively; each incident square/triangle pair has product zero. Every vertex is ideal, and the strict nonincident supporting inequalities check directly. Thus it is a positive ideal right-angled cuboctahedron with the required cube labels. Here b=4 and Vol(actual augmented cube link)=16v8+2Vol(Q_cube). (7) The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_nc_graph_rectified_core_geometry.py) checks this certificate and all eight octahedral attachments, their merged supporting planes, right angles and the actual resulting 36-vertex/72-edge/38-face bowtie incidence. The general proof is the cell construction above, not extrapolation from this example. The theta graph has a degenerate triangular core rather than a positive three-dimensional Q. Its separately proved four-octahedron construction has volume 4v8; it is not being passed through the strict hypothesis here. ### The input class is closed under actual vertex grafts Two such positive cores can be glued along triangular faces by the specified three-port bijection, putting their interiors on opposite sides of the common plane. The adjacent white polygons merge because their dihedral angles add to pi. The resulting union is convex. For an explicit proof, the two convex cores lie in opposite closed halfspaces and intersect exactly in the common triangle T. If x,y are in different cores, minimize d(x,z)+d(z,y) over z in T. This function tends to infinity when z escapes to an ideal end, so a minimum is attained at a finite point. Every finite seam point is locally convex because the right angles add to pi; T has no finite vertices. The minimizing broken path therefore straightens locally across the seam to the ambient geodesic. It is a single geodesic, contained in the union. Points in the same core are already joined there by a geodesic. This proves convexity. Its ideal end vertices and the remaining right-angled boundary faces have exactly the medial incidence of the planar three-edge vertex sum of the two graphs. The canonical unit decorations agree at the seam. Volumes add, and the finite certificate is transported by the explicit face isometry. This gives a constructive closure operation on the geometric input class, not an existence assumption for every planar graph. When the operation uses the ordered interval/outer-face graft of [the NC cube insertion](actual_nc_spin_one_flow_order_certificate.md), it also retains the actual original source topology. In particular, start with the literal cube and repeatedly insert an ordered cube at any allowed interval vertex. Equivalently take the theta source followed by k>=1 such cube insertions. The resulting genuinely branching family has b=1+3k and a core formed from k copies of Q_cube. Its actual hyperbolic volume is Vol(S^3 minus L_Gamma(e)) =(4+12k)v8+2k Vol(Q_cube). (7a) The choices include arbitrary finite ordered binary branching trees. This establishes positive core existence and actual geometry throughout that family. The fixed-level spin-one theorem does not yet provide its all-N quantum limit. ## 5. The precise remaining quantum target For every graph satisfying the input certificate, the desired equality now has a geometrically specified right side: lim_N (2pi/N)log |K_N(L_Gamma(e))| =4b v8+2Vol(Q). (8) The exposed-mark first-normal source formula is exact, but it does not yet prove (8). The shared Q contribution is a global graph term; independent theta scalars cannot supply it. Growing-label control of the full magnetic first normal, coherent noncancellation, and the outer-color packet needed for fillings remain to be proved. For coverage only, the ideal medial polyhedron appears as the truncated rectification in [Belletti's paper](https://msp.org/agt/2025/25-2/agt-v25-n2-p01-p.pdf). Fully augmented right-angled cell decompositions and octahedral subclasses are discussed in [Purcell's exposition](https://users.monash.edu.au/~jpurcell/papers/expos-auglinks.pdf). No proof or quantum-invariant identification from those sources is used in the construction above, and no novelty of the geometric operation is asserted. Independent analytical review: the global audit agent checked the construction through sections 1--4, including all vertex formulas, canonical horospheres, actual Fisher incidence and odd-parity face maps. The exact cube audit additionally identifies its six square faces from the literal NC source's opposite black/white ribbon orders. The vertex-graft closure paragraph received a separate independent review; its minimizing-path proof includes the exact common triangle and excludes escape to an ideal end.

title: An exact first-normal reduction for arbitrary original NC Morse graphs
text: # An exact first-normal reduction for arbitrary original NC Morse graphs 29 October 2026. Every fixed graph in the actual noncrossing Morse class has a source-exact reduction to an ordinary magnetic spin network with ONE retained generic-q normal. This includes a distinct boundary term when the sole marked white vertex has an unsaturated root source. The original unrestricted mark remains on the physical V_N strand. No Euclidean norm, semisimple root quotient, scalar Frobenius vertex, or vanishing source normal is substituted for it. This is an exact finite source theorem at arbitrary fixed width. It does not establish a norm bound, noncancellation, a stationary cycle, or a geometric volume for a general graph. ## 1. The graph is an original ordered Morse diagram Use precisely the class in section5 of the [literal trivalent vertex theorem](actual_trivalent_complete_circle_vertex_kernel.md). There are b black and b white vertices and E=3b ordered edge slots. Each color class partitions {0,...,E-1} into sorted triples; each partition is noncrossing. At a triple (a,b,c) the actual matching is (2a+1,2c+2), (2a+2,2b+1), (2b+2,2c+1). Removing innermost adjacent arcs gives an original nested cup/cap Morse word. There is no free incidence permutation or unrecorded braid. Choose a white vertex v* whose outer cap is EXPOSED: it is not contained in any other top cap. Mark that arc; all other caps are ordinary. Its row is the original UNRESTRICTED m. Equivalently, all ordinary top caps can be removed by innermost removals without passing over the marked arc. Every noncrossing partition has such a top-level block, so this leaves the arbitrary graph class intact while restricting its bare pointing. Replacing a NESTED cap by the same bare m is not covered. A genuine cut at that location requires pivotal transport through the enclosing caps, which is not a local unmodified m replacement. Fix labels 0<=j_e<=M=floor((N-1)/2) and signed integer exponents e_e. The edge coupon is the actual full-normal sector R^(e_e)L_(j_e)=omega_(j_e)^(e_e) h0_(j_e) W_(j_e) pi_(j_e), pi_j=G_j^(-1)W_j^dagger P, G_(j,r)=s_(2j)/(s_r s_(2j-r)), h0_j=k_j N s_(2j)/s_j^2, k_j=2 if 2j<d, k_j=1 if 2j=d, omega_j=kappa(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)]. (1) Here d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, kappa=q^(d^2/2), F_u=(Q;Q)_u, s_u=|F_u|. The paired coupon is nilpotent; pi_j W_j=0 there. Formula(1) includes its first normal BEFORE passing to an ordinary object. All external original line/framing factors remain outside the raw scalar Z_Gamma defined here. ## 2. Explicit local regular lifts and canonical ordinary tensors Set zeta=q exp(t). Every prime below means d/dt at t=0. Let V_N(t) be the generic highest-weight d module in the same balanced basis. Its physical cup has highest coefficient N zeta^(-d^2): pV_(u,d-u)(t)=N zeta^(-d^2)(-1)^u zeta^[u(d-u-1)] F_u(t)F_(d-u)(t)/F_d(t), ellV(t)=pV(t)^(-1). (2) It specializes exactly to p_(u,v)=N x^(-v)delta_(u+v,d) and ell_(u,v)=x^u/N delta_(u+v,d). On the ordinary object Q_j of highest weight 2j choose pQ_j with highest coefficient ONE, using the same formula with d replaced by 2j and the leading scale omitted. The physical Clebsch map W_j(t) starts at degree l=d-j with h_u(t)=(-1)^u zeta^(-du) Q^[u(l-1)-u(u-1)/2](Q^(j+1);Q)_u F_(d-u)/F_d, W_(j,r)(t)=F_pair(t)^r h(t)/F_r(t), 0<=r<=2j. (3) All displayed factorial denominators have index <N and are units. The direct highest recurrence and E,F commutator prove covariance; the last F endpoint follows because E_pair is injective above degree d. These facts were proved explicitly in the [all-channel marked calculation](actual_trivalent_all_channel_marked_contraction.md), section3. No generic decomposition theorem is required. Keep the ROOT constants h0_j, omega_j and gamma_j=q^(2-j^2)/N^2 fixed as t varies. Define the chosen regular lift pi_j(t)=gamma_j^(-1)D_t(W_j(t)), D_t(W_j)=pQ_j(t)^T W_j(t)^T [ellV(t)^T tensor ellV(t)^T]P. (4) At t=0 this is precisely the actual pi_j in(1). Direct cup matrices and K covariance give D_t^2(W_j)=W_j. This is a lift of the fixed-root coupon, not an assertion about the full moving-q germ of the original circle, pivot, or framed R. Constant omega_j^(e_e) in the lift is legitimate because(1) is an exact all-normal root equality. At any triangle triple (a,b,c), let Theta_abc(t) be the genuine ordinary invariant in Q_a(t) tensor Q_b(t) tensor Q_c(t), normalized by Theta_abc(2a,b+c-a,0)=1. (5) It is an explicit regular finite tensor. Put J=a+b+c, r=b+c-a, r1=a+b-c. Its third-color-zero slice is Theta_abc(2a-k,r+k,0) =(-1)^k zeta^[k(2a+1-k)] F_(r+k)F_(2a-k)/(F_r F_(2a)), 0<=k<=r1. (6) All other slices are forced by v_u=-K_c(u-1)/E_c(u-1,u) E_ab v_(u-1). (7) Every denominator in(6),(7) is a unit at the root. The corresponding integer-H invariant space is one-dimensional. Outside the ordinary triangle range it is zero, by the rectangular lowest F equation. Define the LOCAL source coefficient by the finite original index sum s_abc(t)=<2a,b+c-a,0| [pi_a(t) tensor pi_b(t) tensor pi_c(t)]J_source(t), J_source(t)=pV_16(t)pV_23(t)pV_45(t). (8) Then the whole black tensor is U_abc(t)=s_abc(t)Theta_abc(t). At the root its value is explicitly s_abc(0)=N^3 A_N(a,b,c)/G_(b,b+c-a), (9) where the [proved positive source formula](actual_trivalent_all_channel_positive_scalar_and_regular_cubes.md) includes its original phase. Thus s_abc(0)!=0 exactly when J>=d within the triangle range; it is zero for J<d. The derivative in(8) is a retained local source current, not determined merely by(9). ## 3. The exact ordinary spin network and all root constants Keep each vertex's actual increasing edge order. At a black vertex v with incident labels (a,b,c), place Theta_abc(t), and put s_v(t)=s_abc(t). At a white vertex with the SAME displayed incident order place D_t(Theta_cba(t)), and put s_v(t)=s_cba(t). The dual reverses the abstract object order, so its resulting row is again indexed in (a,b,c) order. No same-order adjoint may be substituted. Contract equal magnetic edge indices, with their dimensions 2j_e+1, to obtain the explicitly specified finite spin network Xi_Gamma(t). It contains the genuine ordinary 3j tensors and cups; it is not defined by the original unknown closed scalar. All its factors and their first derivatives are given by(2),(6),(7). Define the EXACT fixed root factor C_Gamma=product_edges [h0_j gamma_j omega_j^(e_e)], S_Gamma(t)=product_vertices s_v(t). (10) The h0_j and G_j can have factorial exponential growth. They have not been declared polynomial or suppressed. A single gamma_j occurs per edge, because that edge meets exactly one white vertex. Let F_Gamma(t) be the ordinary closed ORIGINAL physical graph with the regular lifted coupons (1),(4), and with an ordinary cap also at the eventually marked arc. Genuine local duality gives Lambda_abc(t)=gamma_a gamma_b gamma_c D_t(U_cba(t)). Substitution at every vertex is therefore the all-width index identity F_Gamma(t)=C_Gamma S_Gamma(t) Xi_Gamma(t). (11) This does not require a factorization of Xi_Gamma into vertex norms or source-independent inverse frames. The magnetic contraction is retained in full, on the actual graph wiring. ## 4. The original marked scalar is exactly the first normal Remove all other caps in their actual innermost Morse order. Exposure ensures that this leaves the two marked legs as a genuine generic invariant physical column. Bend with the SAME pV(t). Every remaining map is then a generic Hopf map; hence the resulting open map on V_N(t) is a scalar z_Gamma(t)I. To prove scalarity directly, its generic K eigenvalues are distinct and all its interior F arrows are nonzero, so commuting with K,F forces a scalar matrix. Every entry is regular at t=0, by(2)--(4); thus z_Gamma is holomorphic. The physical closing trace, including the cup's sign, is exactly ellV pV^T=(-1)^d K_V, F_Gamma(t)=D_N(t) z_Gamma(t), D_N(t)=(-1)^d[N]_(q exp(t)), D_N(0)=0, nu_N:=D_N'(0)=2N(-1)^N/(q-q^(-1))!=0. (12) The original unrestricted root marked row has m pV(0)=1. Thus the original marked source is z_Gamma(0), with no extra component factor: Z_Gamma=C_Gamma/nu_N *[S_Gamma'(0)Xi_Gamma(0) +S_Gamma(0)Xi_Gamma'(0)]. (13) Only the chosen physical trace quotient is differentiated. The mark has never been transported through a paired image or replaced by an ordinary cap. In particular (13) retains the current that would be lost by first specializing the generic ordinary graph to its root zero. The factor 1/nu_N has magnitude sin(pi/N)/N; this alone gives no bound for the differentiated tensors or their source coefficients. The answer is independent of the chosen regular Hopf lift. Two such lifts with the same original root coupons give the same root open map, hence the same z_Gamma(0). Their ordinary closures differ by D_N(t) times a holomorphic scalar vanishing at t=0, so their first normals agree. Individual local source and spin-network derivatives may change with the lift; their complete combination in(13) does not. ### 4a. Why an inner bare mark is not a movable pivotal cut The exposure hypothesis is necessary for the bare row used here. On the ordered cube at N=3, give all twelve edges label j=1 and zero twist.
