Fixed endpoint insertions still have a finite Gaussian certificate Keep a(s)=(1-2s)sin(2pi s), epsilon=k mod2, and s_l=(2l-epsilon)/(2k), as in [the actual twist endpoint theorem](actual_twist_endpoint_gaussian_certificate.md). For every FIXED k>0 and FIXED h>=0, set G_(k,h)(N)=sum_(0<s_l<1)(-1)^l a(s_l)sin(pi s_l)^(2h) exp[-i pi N(l-epsilon/2)^2/k]. (5) This is algebraic and periodic in N modulo8k. With C_(N,k) exactly the phase in that theorem, the ORIGINAL source obeys phi(r^k Bhat_h) = C_(N,k) N^(3/2+2h)/(pi^(2h)(h!)^2) G_(k,h)(N) +O_(k,h)(N^(1+2h)). (6) For odd k the error is O_(k,h)(N^(1/2+2h)). Negative k follows by coefficient conjugation. The statements concern fixed h<N as N tends to infinity; h may not be sent to a fraction of N here. An own proof retains the full source derivative. Its exact folded form is phi(r^k Bhat_h)=(-1)^(d+1)/2 sum_j nu_j^k { Bhat_h(c_j)[c_j-(k/2)(d-2j)A_j]+A_j^2 Bhat_h'(c_j)}. (7) Uniformly with all fixed-order s derivatives, Bhat_h(2cos(2pi s)) =N^(2h)sin(pi s)^(2h)/(pi^(2h)(h!)^2)+O_h(N^(2h-2)). This follows directly from its h factors and s_h^2=(2pi/N)^(2h)(h!)^2[1+O_h(N^(-2))]. Insert this into(7) and apply the proved half-grid Gaussian argument to the leading a(s) term. The remaining source terms have no extra N factor and are O(N^(1/2+2h)), except the possible even-k endpoint contributions already bounded by O(N^(1+2h)). This proves (6), including normals. For each specified k,h, nonvanishing of(5) is a FINITE cyclotomic test; a zero leading coefficient is not silently discarded. For k3, G_(3,h)=4^(-h)G_(3,0), and for k4, G_(4,h)=2^(-h)G_(4,0). Both are nonzero on every N residue class. For k5 the two paired weights are a_1 sin(pi/10)^(2h), a_2 sin(3pi/10)^(2h). At h0 the first is larger; at every integer h>=1 the second is larger: a_2/a_1=cos(pi/5)>1/2 and sin(3pi/10)/sin(pi/10)=(3+sqrt5)/2>2. Their strict difference gives a uniform triangle lower bound exactly as in the scalar theorem. Thus fixed endpoint insertions for powers3,4,5 all have nonzero leading terms, with no parity restriction. The exceptional powers have exact fixed-root boundary data instead: phi(Bhat_h)=delta_(h,d), phi(r Bhat_h)=(-q)^(d-h), phi(r^2 Bhat_h)=(-q)^(d-h)F_(d-h). (8) Negative powers are their conjugates. These follow from the literal r and r^2 source columns and the full Frobenius pairing. Thus the vanishing leading Gaussians at k0,1,2 leave no unknown endpoint data. ## 3. Every fixed twist power has nonzero resolved Gaussian boundary modes There is a stronger UNIVERSAL vector statement even when the scalar Gaussian sum cancels. Fix any k>=3, put epsilon=k mod2 and rho=floor((k-1)/2), and define s_j=(2j-epsilon)/(2k), t_j=sin(pi s_j)^2, 1<=j<=rho, 0<t_1<...<t_rho<1, w_j(N)=2(-1)^j(1-2s_j)sin(2pi s_j) exp[-i pi N(j-epsilon/2)^2/k]. (9) Then, for EVERY integer N, G_(k,h)(N)=sum_(j=1)^rho t_j^h w_j(N). (10) To prove it, pair the stationary index j with k+epsilon-j. Their positions are s and1-s, their a values and sin(pi s)^(2h) agree, and their (-1) signs agree. Their quadratic phase difference is pi N(k+epsilon-2j), an even integer multiple of pi. The remaining middle position s=1/2 has a=0. Thus every pair adds, proving(10). Moreover |w_j(N)|=2(1-2s_j)sin(2pi s_j)>0 (11) independently of N or any coprimality condition. Let V_(h,j)=t_j^h, 0<=h<rho. This fixed Vandermonde is invertible: its determinant is product_(i<j)(t_j-t_i)!=0. Form from the ACTUAL source entries the normalized vector b_(h,N)=pi^(2h)(h!)^2 phi(r^k Bhat_h)/(C_(N,k)N^(3/2+2h)). Equation(6) is uniform over this fixed finite vector. Consequently V^(-1)b_N=(w_j(N))_j+O_k(N^(-1/2)), (12) with O_k(1/N) error for odd k. Every individual resolved coefficient therefore has a uniform positive lower bound for all sufficiently large N. Negative powers give its conjugate statement. One may use an EXACT algebraic normalization at every root instead: btilde_(h,N)=s_h^2 phi(r^k Bhat_h) /(4^h C_(N,k)N^(3/2)). (12a) Since s_h^2/4^h=pi^(2h)(h!)^2 N^(-2h)[1+O_h(N^(-2))], the same conclusion(12) holds with btilde. All its finite-level normalizing factors, and the Vandermonde entries, are algebraic. The normalizations and V inverse are explicit, depend on k, and have only polynomial cost in N. They do not use an unknown knot invariant. Thus scalar residue-class cancellations do NOT leave unknown source incidence if one retains the full fixed-rank endpoint vector. These are resolved GAUSSIAN endpoint modes. Identifying them with a chosen interior Ward branch requires the exact boundary-to-Ward projection and a propagation estimate on the domain in question. Neither follows from the names or from nonzero individual entries; a finite endpoint projection alone does not control subsequent mode conversion. ## 4. What this gives a finite-depth source criterion For any fixed m and any proposed finite-rank Ward recurrence for v_m, (2)--(7) specify its endpoint vectors by finitely many exact Gaussians and known N powers/phases. A dominant-eigenprojection test can therefore be made against actual source data. It must retain a possible linear combination/cancellation between those finite coefficients; nonzero individual entries do not imply a nonzero projection. The repeated run is modularly PARABOLIC and conjugate to one twist. Its unbounded count of displayed turns is not a new general bridge family. The reusable result here is the actual finite boundary-data formula; it is not counted as completion of the broad source problem. The next m4 vector and its exact rank-three inhomogeneous Ward are already displayed in the endpoint theorem. Its forward source has an interior modulus switch; distinct roots alone cannot select one branch. The data here remove an unknown boundary value from that problem, rather than asserting that the remaining conversion or global source gap has been solved. All statements are ROOT-VALUE identities in the actual original source. Bhat insertions encode endpoint coordinates and full Casimir Hermite normals. They are not Taylor derivatives in q of an arbitrary generic turn family. No recorded Newton clock is promoted to a peripheral deformation or an additional actual knot coupon without its own proof. Audit: [full original endpoint matrices and finite Gaussian data](../experiments/audit_actual_twist_endpoint_gaussian_certificate.py). Its modal-residue checks use exact primitive cyclotomic-root images in finite fields, with the prime and image recorded in the results. They supplement the all-k pairing/Vandermonde proof above; a successful specialization is not itself a proof of an identity over the complex cyclotomic field. Independent analytical reviews passed for the exact all-m endpoint identities, full fixed-h Hermite fold/asymptotic, and the universal paired Gaussian/Vandermonde nonvanishing theorem. The expanded audit passes eleven full original source families,360 coefficient checks, 42 Gaussian profiles and1656 exact cyclotomic modal residue vectors. These finite checks supplement the universal pairing proof; they do not extrapolate it from the tested twist powers.

title: A positive Newton metric for genuine original tangle turns
text:
# A positive Newton metric for genuine original tangle turns 29 October 2026. The genuine quarter-turn of ANY original two-head Hopf box is a unitary reversal in an explicit full-dimensional Newton packet. Both original marked closures have dual norm ONE. Signed crossings have an explicit adjoint in this same metric, so a specified class of reflected rational/arborescent circuits is an exact positive norm of its coherent half-network. This is not positivity for an arbitrary fully augmented diagram, and no general sharp energy or new volume-equality class is inferred. ## 1. Actual operators and the normalized Newton packet Keep the full original algebra and source of [the pair commutant theorem](actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md) and [the circle sewing theorem](general_augmented_graph_source_extension.md): \[ \mathcal H_N=\mathbb C[z]/P_N,\quad P_N=2T_N(z/2)+2,\quad c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1},\quad d=N-1,\quad Q=q^2 . \] All \(c_j\) are real, with \(c_{d-j}=c_j\). Let \[ F_r=(Q;Q)_r,\quad s_r=|F_r|,\quad B_r(z)=\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}(c_j-z),\qquad \widehat B_r=B_r/s_r^2,\quad 0\leq r\leq d . 	ag{1} \] Here \(s_0=1,\ s_d=N,\ s_rs_{d-r}=N\). The basis (1) is a CASIMIR Newton basis, distinct from earlier normalized homogeneous interval/length blocks. In particular its zero slot is exactly \(1\). The original marked functional and genuine UNSCALED turn are \[ \phi(f)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d](f mod P_N),\qquad (\mathscr R f)_{(a,b);(c,e)} =x^{a-e}f(\Omega)_{(d-a,c);(b,d-e)}. 	ag{2} \] The turn preserves the full Hopf algebra, satisfies \(\mathscr R^2=I\), and includes both actual cup/cap factors; it is not the scaled \(Z\) and is not multiplicative. ## 2. Full physical proof of the Newton turn identity For the physical degree block \(W_t\), \(0\leq t\leq d\), the Casimir is an irreducible tridiagonal matrix with characteristic AND minimal polynomial \[ \prod_{j=0}^t(z-c_j). 	ag{3} \] The characteristic formula follows by the explicit generic highest-weight/descendant triangular decomposition before regular specialization, as in the pair commutant proof. The root offdiagonal entries are nonzero; hence a boundary vector is cyclic, and (3) is the minimal polynomial even when some \(c_j\) coincide. Thus \(B_r\) annihilates \(W_t\) whenever \(t<r\), INCLUDING its Jordan normals. Every degree block of \(B_r(\Omega)\) has first-color bandwidth at most \(r\). In (2) the difference of its first colors is \((d-a)-b=d-(a+b)\). Therefore \(\mathscr R B_r\) annihilates every physical degree \(t<d-r\). Applying (3) at \(t=d-r-1\) shows that its representing polynomial is divisible by \(B_{d-r}\); when \(r=d\) this assertion is vacuous. For the reverse degree bound, use the middle block \(A=\Omega|_{W_d}\). Its turned first column is \[ (\mathscr R B_r(A))_{a0} =x^{a-d}(B_r(\Omega))_{(d-a,0);(d-a,0)} . \] This vanishes for \(a>d-r\), by (3). A polynomial of degree \(k<N\) in the irreducible tridiagonal \(A\), applied to \(e_0\), has nonzero component \(k\) from its unique outermost path. Hence \(\deg(\mathscr R B_r)\leq d-r\). It follows that \(\mathscr R B_r=C_rB_{d-r}\). The scalar comes from ONE literal physical entry: \[ (\mathscr R B_r)_{(0,d-r);(d-r,0)} =(B_r)_{(d,d-r);(d-r,d)}=s_r^2 . \] For clarity, in the latter high-degree block the unique \(r\)-step path increasing the first color has entries \[ Q^{j-r}(1-Q^{r-j})(1-Q^{j+1}),\quad0\leq j<r . \] Multiplying and including the leading coefficient \((-1)^r\) gives \((-1)^rQ^{-r(r+1)/2}F_r^2=s_r^2\). Similarly the unique decreasing path for \(B_{d-r}\) in the LOW block of degree \(d-r\) gives \(s_{d-r}^2\). All turn monomials in this chosen entry equal one. Consequently \[  oxed{\quad \mathscr R B_r= rac{s_r^2}{s_{d-r}^2}B_{d-r}, \qquad \mathscr R\widehat B_r=\widehat B_{d-r}. \quad} 	ag{4} \] This proof works for all \(N\geq2\), all \(r\), and all repeated Casimir nodes. It uses physical matrix support and full minimal polynomials, not an equality only on distinct eigenvalues. ## 3. Positive Gram, all ports open, and the exact original source The full Frobenius pairing in this basis is especially simple: \[ \phi(\widehat B_i\widehat B_j)=\delta_{i+j,d}. 	ag{5} \] For \(i+j<d\) use degree. For \(i+j=d\) use its leading coefficient and \(s_is_j=N\). If \(i+j\geq N\), the product is divisible by \(P_N\): indeed \(B_N/B_j=B_{N-j}\), since \(c_{d-k}=c_k\), and \(B_i\) is divisible by \(B_{N-j}\). This is polynomial divisibility with FULL multiplicities, so (5) retains all normals. Write \(f=\sum_r\alpha_r\widehat B_r\) and let \(f^\sharp(z)=\overline{f( ar z)}\). All basis polynomials in (1) have real coefficients. Equations (4)--(5) prove the positive definite all-input identity \[  oxed{\quad \langle f,gangle_{m Newt} :=\phi(f^\sharp\mathscr Rg) =\sum_{r=0}^d\overline{\alpha_r} eta_r,\qquad \|\mathscr R f\|_{m Newt}=\|f\|_{m Newt}. \quad} 	ag{6} \] The metric is prescribed independently of any knot or exterior. It is not the canonical unweighted Hermite-channel Gram whose energy was excessive in a previous figure-eight test, nor the terminal \(T^*T\) metric. Its change of frame can have exponential condition number. The exact packet transform is \[ \alpha_r=(-1)^rs_r^2 f[c_0,\ldots,c_r], 	ag{7} \] with confluent divided differences at repeated nodes. Thus it is explicit and invertible on the COMPLETE algebra and retains every first derivative, including even/composite levels. Equivalently let \(B\) be the ACTUAL complete source-Hom bidiagonal Casimir \[ Be_j=c_je_j+b_je_{j-1},\qquad b_j=Q^j+Q^{-j}-2=-|1-Q^j|^2 . \] Its cyclic column obeys \(f(B)e_d=(\alpha_d,\ldots,\alpha_0)^T\). This follows either from its confluent divided-difference formula or from \(\widehat B_r(B)e_d=e_{d-r}\). Consequently \[ \phi(f\,\mathscr Rg)=(f(B)e_d)^T(g(B)e_d),\qquad f(B)e_d\mapsto P_{m rev}f(B)e_d 	ext{ under }\mathscr R . 	ag{8} \] The ORIGINAL closures, with unrestricted marked cap and actual pivot, are \[ m f(\Omega)p=f(c_0)=\alpha_0,\qquad \phi(f)=\alpha_d . 	ag{9} \] Their proof and original \(N\) factors are in the circle sewing note, section 3. Both are unit coordinate rows in (6), so have dual norm EXACTLY one. No arbitrary local marked cap was replaced by an ordinary cap. Any physical exterior can still be attached before using (4); it is a full operator identity. ## 4. Explicit twist matrices, their physical star, and coherent sewing In Newton coordinates multiplication by \(z\) is the real LOWER bidiagonal matrix \[ Z_{rr}=c_r,\qquad Z_{r+1,r}=-|1-Q^{r+1}|^2,\qquad Z^T=P_{m rev} ZP_{m rev}. 	ag{10} \] Every literal signed crossing power acts by \[ T_p=R(Z)^p,\qquad R=\kappa r_N,\quad \kappa=q^{d^2/2}. 	ag{11} \] Its nodal values and first derivatives are the original complete ones, with no Jordan term omitted. In particular its all-entry form is \[ (T_p)_{ij} =\left(\prod_{k=j+1}^i b_kight) R^p[c_j,\ldots,c_i]\quad(i\geq j); \qquad (T_p)_{ij}=0\quad(i<j). 	ag{12} \] One can also use the entirely finite Newton alphabet \[ R=\kappa\sum_{r=0}^d(-q)^r\widehat B_r,\qquad R^{-1}=\kappa^{-1}\sum_{r=0}^d(-q)^{-r}\widehat B_r . 	ag{13} \] These follow from the literal cup-slide \(R_{23}^{-1}p=N\kappa^{-1}e_d\), equivalently \(R_{23}e_d=\kappa p/N\), and (8); that original-source identity is proved in [the normalization packet](actual_terminal_source_normalization_packet.md). Equations (11)--(13) retain the common Cartan scalar. There is a simpler ALL-ENTRY one-crossing kernel. Define the positive sine Gaussian \( eta_{ij}=s_i/(s_js_{i-j})\), \(0\leq j\leq i\leq d\), and \(
u_j=(-1)^jq^{j(j+1)}\). Then \[  oxed{\quad (T_1)_{ij}=\kappa
u_j(-q)^{i-j}{i rack j}_Q =\kappa(-1)^iq^{\,i(j+1)} eta_{ij},\qquad (T_{-1})_{ij}=\overline{(T_1)_{ij}}\quad(i\geq j), \quad} 	ag{13a} \] with zero entries above the diagonal. This includes ALL confluent channels; it is not an eigenline expansion. Here is an independent finite proof. Call the first displayed triangular matrix \(C\). Its first column is \(\kappa(-q)^i\), exactly \(R(Z)e_0\) by (13). For \(i\geq j\), Gaussian factorial cancellation gives \[ b_i rac{C_{i-1,j}}{C_{ij}} =-q^{-1}Q^{-i}(1-Q^i)(1-Q^{i-j}),\qquad b_{j+1} rac{C_{i,j+1}}{C_{ij}} =q^{-1}(1-Q^{j+1})(1-Q^{i-j}). \] Their difference is \(-(c_i-c_j)\), so \(CZ=ZC\). The boundary terms vanish by their displayed factors. Since \(e_0\) is cyclic for the irreducible lower-bidiagonal \(Z\), two commuting matrices that agree on \(e_0\) agree on the whole space. Thus \(C=R(Z)\), with no separation of repeated nodes. Finally \({i rack j}_Q=q^{j(i-j)} eta_{ij}\) proves the second expression in (13a), and \(R^\sharp=R^{-1}\) proves the inverse. Thus an arbitrary genuine rational circuit has an explicit alphabet: unitary reversal, the lower sine-binomial kernel (13a), and its coefficient conjugate. Its oscillation is the ORIGINAL half-clock \(q^{ij}\); replacing it by \(Q^{ij}\) would change the source. Its absolute entry also has the exact angle identity \[  eta_{ij}=N\,w_d(j,i-j,d-i),\qquad w_d(a,b,c)= rac1{s_as_bs_c},\quad a+b+c=d. 	ag{13b} \] This follows from \(s_is_{d-i}=N\). It supplies one actual angle-simplex amplitude with its phase and incidence labels. It is the amplitude \(Nw_d\), NOT its square root. Any proposed square-root-energy comparison must still prove its metric and source compensation rather than silently replacing (13a). Two adjacent crossings have a further COHERENT all-input elimination: with \(m=i-j\), \[  oxed{\quad (T_2)_{ij}=\kappa^2
u_j^2(-q)^m {i rack j}_Q (Q^{j+1};Q)_m =\kappa^2
u_j^2(-q)^m  rac{F_i^2}{F_j^2F_m}, \quad i\geq j .\quad} 	ag{13c} \] The negative two-crossing kernel is its coefficient conjugate. To prove it, expand the actual product \(T_1T_1\), use \({i rack k}_Q{k rack j}_Q ={i rack j}_Q{m rack k-j}_Q\), and set \(r=k-j\). The remaining sum is exactly \[ \sum_{r=0}^m {m rack r}_Q (-1)^rQ^{r(r-1)/2}(Q^{j+1})^r=(Q^{j+1};Q)_m . \] This finite identity follows by inserting the last Pochhammer factor and the Pascal recursion. Every index is below \(N\). Its cancellations are retained BEFORE taking an absolute value. Thus the all-entry magnitude is \(s_i^2/(s_j^2s_{i-j})\), not a sum of positive one-crossing path magnitudes. Equivalently, for \(D_F=\operatorname{diag}F_i\) and \(D_
u=\operatorname{diag}
u_i\), \[ T_2=\kappa D_F T_1D_F^{-1}D_
u . 	ag{13d} \] This is a typed packet identity preserving arbitrary adjoining input and output arrays. Its factorial gauge is on the NEWTON register; it is not an unrecorded physical-head gauge. Although its endpoint factors at \(0,d\) are only \(1,N\), its interfaces with a turn must remain explicit: \(P_{m rev}D_FP_{m rev}=ND_
u D_F^{-1}\). Consequently (13d) alone is not a polynomial-cost global replacement of every twist/turn network. At a real node the original ratio \(R'(c)/R(c)\) is purely imaginary, and its value has modulus one. Hence full Hermite uniqueness gives \(R^\sharp=R^{-1}\), not only equality of distinct nodal values. For ANY multiplication coupon \(M_f\), its exact adjoint in (6) is \[ M_f^\dagger=\mathscr R M_{f^\sharp}\mathscr R . \] Indeed the Frobenius pairing is symmetric and (4)--(5) imply its turn is selfadjoint and orthogonal. In particular \[  oxed{\qquad \mathscr R^\dagger=\mathscr R,\qquad T_p^\dagger=\mathscr R T_{-p}\mathscr R . \qquad} 	ag{14} \] The turn is unitary; the crossing is GENERALLY NOT. Its real bidiagonal Casimir is nonnormal and has repeated-node derivative channels. Thus unit nodal phases do not bound a whole twist/word norm polynomially. Formula (14) is the required typed interface, not an assertion that every plane-reflected diagram supplies it. For an arbitrary genuine two-port word \(W\), starting with \(1\), the original numerator closure now has the exact source Cauchy bound \[ |m\,W(1)(\Omega)p|^2\leq\|W(1)\|_{m Newt}^2 . 	ag{15} \] All internal turns in this energy are the fixed unitary reversal and all twist kernels are the known matrices (12). No terminal word or unknown invariant is used to define the metric. ## 5. An exact positive class with genuine extra turns Let \(A\) be ANY finite typed word in genuine turns and signed crossing multiplications. Form its ADJOINT WORD by reversing the order and using the exact replacements (14). It is again a literal rational tangle circuit with the original turns and signed crossings. The ORIGINAL numerator closure of its doubled circuit satisfies \[  oxed{\qquad m\,[A^\dagger A(1)](\Omega)p =\langle1,A^\dagger A1angle_{m Newt} =\|A1\|_{m Newt}^2>0 . \qquad} 	ag{16} \] All generators of \(A\) are invertible, so the strict inequality holds at EVERY level. A recorded outer framing or component enhancement unit may multiply this raw positive scalar; its modulus is unchanged. This class includes words with arbitrary numbers of genuine internal turns, for instance \(A=T_p\mathscr R T_q\). Its doubled word is \(\mathscr R T_{-q}\mathscr R T_{-p}\mathscr R T_p\mathscr R T_q\), with no unjustified crossing/turn commutations. Thus the positivity is for an actual specified entire source circuit, not one expanded crossing state or an arbitrary positive model. As a calibration, the normalization packet's exact \(R_{23}p\) formula gives \[ R^2=\kappa^2\sum_{r=0}^d(-q)^rF_r\widehat B_r . \] Taking \(A=T_2\) in (16) therefore gives \(\sum_rs_r^2\), the already proved whole-source figure-eight scalar. The general statement (16) is not inferred from that one example. For longer \(A\), the energy in (16) retains coherent cancellations INSIDE \(A1\); the norm only reflects the second half afterwards. Bounding it by independent absolute-entry capacities would lose the very coupling this construction preserves. A sharp Rivin-constrained bound or a nonzero geometric saddle for these arbitrary half-networks is still needed for a new volume-equality family. This note proves the all-exterior positive kernel and a genuine full-source noncancellation operation, not that remaining geometric estimate. ## 6. A complete-circle reflected source with a proved exponent The known complete packet \(z_N=\mathscr R(R^{-1}L_N)\) now gives an ENTIRE positive original source with an explicit exponential rate: \[ E_N:=\phi(z_N^\sharp\mathscr Rz_N)=\|z_N\|_{m Newt}^2, \qquad  oxed{\ \lim_{N	o\infty} rac1N\log E_N= rac{v_8}{\pi}\ } . 	ag{17} \] In particular the original quantum scaling gives rate \(2v_8\). This uses the already proved actual finite coefficient/endpoint theorems, rather than a guessed positive envelope. Write \[ z_N=N^2\sum_{r=0}^{M} b_{N,r}B_r,\quad |b_{N,r}|= rac{s_{2r}}{s_r^6}|U_r|,\quad M=\lfloor d/2floor. \] The exact norm is \[ E_N=N^4\sum_{r=0}^{M} rac{s_{2r}^2}{s_r^8}|U_r|^2 . 	ag{18} \] The [all-index original-source estimate](actual_pretzel_all_index_backward_envelope.md) gives \(|U_r|\leq CN^B\exp[N\mathcal E(\pi r/N)]\), with \[ \mathcal E(u)= rac2\pi\int_u^{\pi/4}\log\cot v\,dv \quad(0\leq u<\pi/4),\qquad \mathcal E(u)=0\ (u\geq\pi/4). \] Uniform sine-factorial bounds, INCLUDING both endpoints, give the remaining exponential profile \[ T(u)=\{8\Lambda(u)-2\Lambda(2u)\}/\pi,\qquad T'(u)=4\log\cot u/\pi . \] Hence \(T+2\mathcal E\) is exactly constant \(j_0=v_8/\pi\) below \(\pi/4\), and \(T\) decreases above \(\pi/4\). The polynomial number of summands and their uniform polynomial errors prove the upper bound in (17). For each FIXED \(u\in(\pi/4,\pi/2)\), the nonzero coherent high-index asymptotic in [the complete packet theorem](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md), section 2 equation (3), gives \(|U_{\lfloor Nu/\pifloor}|^2 	o\sin u>0\). Its one positive summand proves a lower rate \(T(u)\). Let \(u\downarrow\pi/4\) AFTER the quantum limit to obtain (17). Both parities and all composite levels are covered. The actual raw diagram is specified without an unverified link name: \[  oxed{\qquad E_N=\phi\!\left(\mathscr R(RL_N)\,R^{-1}L_Night). \qquad} 	ag{19} \] Here \(\mathscr R\) commutes with coefficient reflection by (4), and \(L_N^\sharp=L_N\); thus (19) follows from the literal signed boxes, not a replacement by a positive model. It has two ordinary complete crossing-circle components. Deleting those two components leaves the genuine diagram \(\phi(\mathscr R(R)R^{-1}) =\phi(R^{-2})\): the quarter-turn of the single crossing is the opposite single crossing, and the two-strand closure has two main components. Thus the complete reflected diagram has FOUR components. It must not be identified with the three-component Borromean rings merely from the numerical value \(2v_8\). The separate [literal octahedral certificate](actual_reflected_two_circle_octahedral_base.md) now identifies its complement by a reversible projection/disk cut, the actual labeled face table, and four complete torus links. This proves that (17) equals the actual volume of that specified link. The original single-cut normalization comparison changes only the recorded unit phase (or the optional one-cut modified factor \(1/N\)), so it does not alter (17). title: Exact Newton twist equations, original source, and the parabolic Fricke graph
text: # Exact Newton twist equations, original source, and the parabolic Fricke graph 29 October 2026. The actual Newton crossing has a denominator-free finite Weyl system. Its classical map is the genuine parabolic braid/Fricke map, with the original four-plat cup and cap retained by an explicit matrix intertwiner. Arbitrary rational words therefore have an actual complete- meridian character gluing description without an unknown 6j frame. The Newton clock is NOT the knot meridian or the Casimir eigenvalue. This does not construct a generic-meridian A-curve or prove a sharp asymptotic/survival theorem for all rational words. The exceptional cup boundary and its normal source cannot be replaced by a regular torus point. Those distinctions are made explicit below. ## 1. The exact kernel and its actual generic normalization Use the [full Newton packet](actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md): q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, kappa=q^(d^2/2). The actual full crossing kernel is C_ij=kappa(-1)^i q^(i+j^2) [i choose j]_Q, 0<=j<=i<=d; C_ij=0 above the diagonal. (1) It is multiplication by the ORIGINAL checked R, including its common Cartan, all Jordan derivatives, and the true q^(ij) half-clock phase. The actual turn is the reversal P_rev and both original closures are coordinate rows. None of these facts is an independent-eigenline model. There is a useful analytic generic-q extension of(1), but its physical scalar must remain. For zeta near q, put Q=zeta^2 and s_r^2(zeta)=(-1)^r zeta^[-r(r+1)](Q;Q)_r^2, c_j(zeta)=zeta^(2j+1)+zeta^(-2j-1), kappa(zeta)=zeta^(d^2/2). The normalized Newton basis uses these s_r^2; multiplication by z is the lower bidiagonal Z with diagonal c_j and subdiagonal b_j=Q^j+Q^(-j)-2. The generic matrix (1) commutes with this Z by the same finite Gaussian identities, and its diagonal is kappa nu_j, nu_j=(-1)^j zeta^[j(j+1)]. The literal generic highest-weight-d physical braiding, however, has at the Casimir node c_a the highest-vector eigenvalue lambda_(d-a)=(-1)^(d-a) zeta^[d^2/2-(d-a)(N+a)] =kappa gamma_N(zeta) nu_a, gamma_N(zeta)=(-1)^d zeta^(-Nd). (2) Consequently its Newton matrix is gamma_N C, not just C. Generic distinctness and equality of all nodal values prove the matrix identity; regular specialization retains the full confluent polynomial. At the root gamma_N(q)=1, but its normal derivatives are NONZERO. All q-normal calculations must keep(2). This generic q deformation is not a deformation of the knot meridian. The inverse of the finite Gaussian kernel is also explicit: (C^-1)_ij=kappa^-1(-1)^i q^[j^2-2ij-i] [i choose j]_Q. (3) This follows from the finite q-Pascal inverse and equals coefficient conjugation of(1) at the original root. The physical generic inverse has the additional scalar gamma_N^-1. ## 2. Finite Weyl equations, including the actual normal wall Let X=Q^i,Y=Q^j on the kernel. Direct adjacent-factor cancellation gives (QX-Y) C_(i+1,j)=qY(1-QX)C_ij, (QY-1) C_(i,j+1)=q(X-Y)C_ij. (4) These equations are CROSS-MULTIPLIED; they include the triangular diagonal and its zero neighbors. One must not divide their vanishing coefficients to change the support. For the finite zero extension C_(N,j)=0, the first equation has the explicit generic last-row current (QX-Y) C_(i+1,j)-qY(1-QX)C_ij =-qY(1-Q^N) delta_(i,d) C_(d,j). (5) It vanishes at the root, but its first q-normal coefficient does not. Multiplying by gamma_N preserves(4)--(5), with that scalar retained. The backwards-j version is globally valid without another source: (Y-1)C_ij=q(X-Q^-1Y)C_(i,j-1), C_(i,-1)=0. (6) Together with triangular support and C_(i,0)=kappa(-q)^i, these are finite pointed equations determining the actual kernel. They do not identify an arbitrary cyclic-shift solution with the original one. For strict forward shifts S f_i=f_(i+1), (6) gives the exact matrix identity X C S=C Y S+q^-1 C(Y-I). (7) The first equation similarly gives a cleared operator relation with the wall(5). Inverting its factor S+q(1-QX) at the root is invalid: that factor has a zero last diagonal entry. The finite source is part of the operator identity, even when studying a regular classical chart. ## 3. The regular canonical graph and its preserved Casimir For i/N=x,j/N=y in 0<y<x<1 the leading exponent of(1) is Phi(x,y)=J(x)-J(y)-J(x-y)+pi i(xy+x+1/2), J'(x)=log(2sin pi x). The common Cartan produces the displayed pi i/2; the remaining known subleading phase is retained in the finite kernel. Put X=exp(2pi i x), Y=exp(2pi i y), U=exp(Phi_x), V=exp(-Phi_y). The negative sign in the INPUT momentum is essential for composing kernel critical equations. Equations(4) give precisely X=Y+(Y-1)/V, U=-Y(1+V), equivalently XV+U+1=0, Y(V+1)+U=0. (8) It preserves dlog U wedge dlog X. Indeed 2pi i Phi is a generating function with differential log U dlog X-log V dlog Y. The same graph comes from the exact cleared equations, not merely a guessed phase. The actual Newton multiplication-Casimir symbol is A(X,U)=X+X^-1+(X+X^-1-2)/U. (9) Substitution in(8) proves A(output)=A(input). The turn has the exact root clock relation P_rev X P_rev=Q^-1 X^-1 and interchanges strict forward and backward shifts. Its principal graph is (X,U)->(X^-1,U^-1). Thus the second trace symbol is B(X,U)=X+X^-1+(X+X^-1-2)U. With {log X,log U}=-1, define the ordered third trace C(X,U)=(8-AB+{A,B})/2 =2-(X-1)^2(U+1)^2/U. (10) Direct algebra gives the ACTUAL parabolic Fricke equation A^2+B^2+C^2+ABC-8(A+B+C)+28=0. (11) On these trace coordinates, the active point map(8) is (A,B,C)->(A,C,8-AC-B). (12) The inverse occurs on observables: Ad(R) is pullback by the inverse state map. Thus(12) agrees with the actual positive braid formula Ad(R):(A,B,C)->(A,8-AB-C,B), rather than reversing a physical crossing based on an isolated eigenphase. ## 4. Actual quantum trace matrices and original source matching This graph has an exact physical source realization. In the already audited three-head complete multiplicity basis let A_phys=Omega_12, B_phys e_j=c_j e_j+b_j e_(j-1). A_phys is the original symmetric tridiagonal matrix with (A_phys)_jj=4qQ^j-q(1+Q)Q^(2j), (A_phys)_(j-1,j)=(A_phys)_(j,j-1)=-(1-Q^j)^2. (13) The actual R_23 is C^T, by multiplication functional calculus in the upper-bidiagonal B_phys. Finite Gaussian cancellation gives the FULL matrix identity R_23^-1 A_phys R_23=B_phys^T. (14) For an entrywise proof substitute(1) transposed in A_phys C^T=C^T B_phys^T. On the interior the needed three ratios are U_(i-1,j)/U_ij=q^(-2i+1)(1-Q^i)/(1-Q^(j-i+1)), U_(i+1,j)/U_ij=q^(2i+1)(1-Q^(j-i))/(1-Q^(i+1)), U_(i,j+1)/U_ij=-q(1-Q^(j+1))/(1-Q^(j-i+1)). Cross multiplication proves the identity, including the adjacent zero diagonal. The end terms vanish by b_0=b_N=0 and (1-Q^N)^2=0 at the root. No nodal or semisimple substitution is used in(14). Set the explicit source intertwiner S_source=P_rev R_23^-1. Then EXACTLY S_source B_phys S_source^-1=Z_lower, S_source A_phys S_source^-1=Z_upper=Z_lower^T. (15) The original cup slide gives R_23^-1 p=N kappa^-1 e_d. Moreover ell_i=x^i/N, x=q^d=-q^-1, and the finite q-binomial identity gives ell R_23=(kappa/N)e_0^T, S_source p=N kappa^-1 e_0, ell S_source^-1=(kappa/N)e_d^T. (16) For the first formula the j-th component is kappa(-q)^j/N times sum_i [j choose i]_Q(-1)^iQ^[i(i-1)/2], namely kappa(-q)^j(1;Q)_j/N. It is zero for j>0. Thus the original N and kappa factors cancel in the WHOLE marked four-plat scalar: ell W_phys p=e_d^T W_Newton e_0, W_Newton=S_source W_phys S_source^-1. (17) The original enhancement/framing line multiplies both sides unchanged. In the complete four-head invariant reduction, physical generators1 and3 use A_phys and generator2 uses B_phys. Therefore they become P_rev T_1 P_rev and T_1, respectively, with literal signed inverses. This is a complete source-exact alphabet for ANY original four-plat word, including all composite/even levels and all Casimir normals. No unknown Racah eigenframe is present. The exact quantum trace triple in these coordinates is Z_lower,Z_upper, and the tridiagonal matrix(13). Expanding its band entries gives the denominator-free quantum Fricke identities from [the actual adjacent-trace theorem](actual_adjacent_twist_character_and_source.md) with single/total Casimirs -2 and central coefficients8. In particular it is the actual physical character slice, not an arbitrary surface inferred only from(11). Equation(14), or its transpose, fixes the braid orientation on the full matrices. At N=2 no division by q+q^-1 is allowed; the same explicit matrix identities still hold. ## 5. The original cap is an exceptional curve, not a torus point Both exact boundary vectors in(17) have the correct source eigencondition: Z_upper e_0=c_0 e_0, e_d^T Z_upper=c_d e_d^T=c_0 e_d^T. (18) Consequently their reduced classical cap is B=2. The Fricke equation then gives C=4-A on its reduced locus, but has a NONREDUCED normal there. The exact finite source(16)--(18) retains that normal data. Naively putting X=1 with finite nonzero U in(9)--(10) collapses all three traces to2. It loses the real cup family. To retain a finite free A!=2 one must resolve the actual corner by U ~ (X-1)^2/[X(A-2)] as X->1. Then B->2 and C->4-A. Thus the correct cap is an exceptional divisor of the Newton chart. It cannot be removed from an endpoint estimate by calling it a regular stationary point on (C*)^2. There is a direct group certificate on this cap. For z=A-2 use mu_1=-[[1,1],[0,1]], mu_2=-[[1,0],[z,1]], mu_3=mu_2^-1, mu_4=mu_1^-1. (19) Their total product is identity, all meridian traces are -2, and their trace triple is (A,2,4-A). For z!=0 it is irreducible. Actual Hurwitz propagation of(19) gives the trace dynamics(12), with its direction fixed by the finite conjugation identities. On an irreducible four-punctured representation, a terminal cap trace2 forces the actual inverse pair matrices: if their product were a nontrivial unipotent, both meridian pairs would share its flag and the whole representation would be reducible. This is the four-port case of [the faithful cap certificate](actual_parabolic_cap_trace_certificate.md). Thus any REGULAR irreducible intersection of the transported cap with the closing cap is an actual representation of the ORIGINAL rational word closure. This is global parabolic character gluing for arbitrary rational words, not merely a formal cubic at each isolated crossing. Reducible and escaping/normal intersections are not discarded, and their source contributions require separate analytic control. This also gives a finite univariate character test for any specified word. Start with the four literal matrices(19), apply the corresponding signed Hurwitz substitutions (with the source adapters in(15)--(17)), and impose the SAME closing inverse-pair matrix equations as the cap pattern(19). Matrix inverses are adjugates since determinant is1, so these are polynomial equations in z. Saturate by z and any denominators introduced by a chosen auxiliary chart; the irreducible solutions are the zeros of an explicit ideal in C[z]. It can be computed by a gcd and, for reduced character support, its square-free part. This retains the actual group/peripheral marking without a generic-meridian A-polynomial elimination. The original nonreduced quantum source is still(16)--(18); taking this reduced ideal does not replace it in the finite period or prove a nonzero geometric coefficient. ## 6. Exact limits of the statement The Newton clock X is exp(2pi i times a NEWTON INDEX/N). The spectral Casimir is the function(9), and the geometric eigenvalue w is obtained only by solving w+w^-1=A. Neither is the physical meridian M. This theorem fixes the actual COMPLETE-meridian slice M=1, with meridian trace-2 and the original source framing. It does not create the generic M-dependent quantum A-module. That requires the actual meromorphic color/dual/turn family and its peripheral currents; the generic q scalar(2) is not a substitute for that meridian deformation. The older [actual-color Newton transform](newton_actual_source_canonical_transform.md) uses different nodes Q^j+Q^-j and the knot's meridian variable. The two Newton transforms must not be identified by their names. The reversal identity is exact at the original root. Its actual generic-q turn family need not be the same reversal matrix off the root, so whole normal derivatives of a turned circuit must retain that family. Likewise(5) is not deleted in a q-normal recurrence. Finally actual character support and an explicit source alphabet do not prove that the geometric branch is accessible, noncanceling, or largest in the complete finite source. A sharp coherent action bound and a nonzero full-source coefficient remain necessary. This result provides the exact finite recurrence, actual braid graph and pointed boundary data for that next analysis; it does not infer a new universal volume equality from a principal curve alone. ## 7. What the universal local dilogarithm does identify There is a precise useful boundary-symbol statement. On the logarithmic lift of the regular triangle, put S=2pi i Phi. Directly from the actual factorial ratio in(1), its leading action is S=-Li_2(X)+Li_2(Y)+Li_2(X/Y)-Li_2(1) +(Log Y)^2/2+pi i Log X-pi^2. (19a) The last real constant is the leading original kappa, not a chosen imaginary calibration. The q^i factor in(1) is subleading and remains in its exact amplitude. Differentiation gives the same actual graph: partial_(Log X) S=Log U, partial_(Log Y) S=-Log V. Thus the rational pre-Bloch symbol of this local phase is beta_Newt=-[X]+[Y]+[X/Y], delta beta_Newt=-X wedge U+Y wedge V. (19b) For an elementary verification, ignore the torsion class of -1, write a=1-X, b=1-Y, c=X-Y, and expand the wedge of U=Ya/c and V=-b/c. Bilinearity gives exactly the boundary of the three displayed dilogarithms. The Bloch--Wigner identity also gives D(beta_Newt)=Im S-log|X| Arg U+log|Y| Arg V, (19c) on compatible logarithmic branches. Regular composed seams telescope in(19b); a turn preserves X wedge U. This does NOT yet identify the resulting closed symbol with the topological fundamental class. Boundary wedges do not fix a closed Bloch period, and the actual cap lies on the exceptional corner in section5, where a regular seam-telescoping argument cannot replace its normal source. A chain-level comparison with the actual signed crossing blocks and marked boundary is still required. Such a global comparison is already proved for the ORIGINAL factorial crossing symbols in [the fundamental-cycle note](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md), for arbitrary diagrams and their regular complete representations. It supplies the classical regulator bound, not the missing global source estimate. In particular(19b) alone neither supplies a generic meridian nor proves access or noncancellation for any new word class. ## 8. Focused verification [The new exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_newton_twist_canonical_graph.py) passes symbolic symplectic/Fricke/inverse-Hurwitz and resolved-cap group identities; six generic physical families using the literal full-Cartan universal R and its gamma_N scalar; and seven original root families N=2,...,8. The latter include every finite Weyl boundary equation, the physical three-head Hom action, all quantum Fricke relations/cubic, the source intertwiner, and twenty-one full marked four-plat words using all three physical braid generators. Finite-field arithmetic is exact. These checks supplement the all-entry proofs and do not claim an asymptotic or a meridian deformation from finite tests.

title: A coherent two-twist/turn source packet with a sharp norm rate
text: # A coherent two-twist/turn source packet with a sharp norm rate 29 October 2026. Set A=T_2 P_rev T_2 in the COMPLETE original Newton metric. The whole source vector A1 has an exact second-order Ward recurrence, an exact reflected boundary equation with an inhomogeneous current, and a sharp all-level norm exponent. The proof uses both actual source endpoints and never assumes that distinct spectral roots alone prevent conversion. It does not identify the reflected circuit with a hyperbolic link or prove the rate for arbitrary longer reduced words. ## 1. Exact original coefficient and Ward equation Use the original N,d,q,Q,kappa,F_i,s_i of [the Newton metric](actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md). Define W_i=F_i^2 sum_(j=0)^i (-1)^j Q^[(3j^2+j)/2]/(F_j^3 F_(i-j)), H_i=F_i W_i, 0<=i<=d. The all-entry T_2 formula and F_j F_(d-j)=N nu_j give the exact SOURCE vector, with no phase or endpoint discarded, (A1)_i=kappa^4 N(-q)^(i+d) W_i. (1) Indeed T_2 1 has entries kappa^2(-q)^j F_j. Apply the genuine reversal and then T_2; its inner j coefficient is nu_j^3 Q^(-j), exactly (-1)^j Q^[(3j^2+j)/2]. The whole-index recurrence is (1-Q^i)W_i=(1+Q-3Q^i)W_(i-1) -Q(1-Q^(i-1))^2 W_(i-2), H_i=(1+Q-3Q^i)H_(i-1) -Q(1-Q^(i-1))^3 H_(i-2), (2) H_0=1, H_1=1-2Q. At i=1 the second coefficient is ZERO; no H_(-1) is needed. These equations hold for every physical index i<=d and all N>=2. For an own derivation, put a_j=(-1)^jQ^[(3j^2+j)/2]/F_j^3, G_i=sum_j a_j/F_(i-j), and use formal generating series modulo z^N. The shift T:f(z)->f(Qz) gives (1-T)^3 a(z)=-Q^2 z T^3 a(z), E(Qz)=(1-z)E(z), E(z)=sum z^k/F_k, G=aE. Consequently (1-z)(1-Qz)G(z)-3(1-Qz)G(Qz) +3G(Q^2z)-G(Q^3z)=0. Coefficient extraction gives (1-Q^i)^3G_i=(1+Q-3Q^i)G_(i-1)-QG_(i-2), hence (2). This argument can first be made at generic Q and then specialized coefficientwise below degree N. It never divides a zero root factorial. The physical source identification (1) uses the root complementation identity. A generic-Q continuation of this displayed scalar recurrence is not thereby identified with the actual generic-q tangle/source germ. All estimates here use its exact physical root values. ## 2. The second source endpoint is exactly the known Gaussian Let P_d be the ORIGINAL normalization endpoint, with its already proved identities and all-parity Gaussian asymptotic: P_d=N^2 sum_(j=0)^d Q^j/F_j^2 =sum_(j=0)^d F_j =N^(3/2) exp[i pi(1/4-N/12+1/(4N))]+O(sqrt N). See [the endpoint proof](actual_normalization_endpoint_gaussian_asymptotic.md). In particular cN^(3/2)<=|P_d|<=CN^(3/2) for all large N. Root factorial complementation in the actual sum gives W_d=N sum_j Q^(j^2)/F_j^2 =(Q/N)sum_j Q^j F_j^2=conjugate(P_d)/N, H_d=conjugate(P_d). (3) The penultimate coefficient is also fixed, not a free backward datum: (conjugate(F_1))^3 H_(d-1) =(1-2/Q)H_d+Q^(-1). (4) For completeness set C(t)=sum_j F_j^2t^j. Its exact finite Ward is (1-t)C(t)+2Qt C(Qt)-Q^2t C(Q^2t)=1. At t=1 this evaluates C(Q^2) from C(Q); substituting the complemented finite expression for H_(d-1) gives (4). Define J_0=0,J_1=1 and evolve J by (2) only for i>=2. Direct reversal of (2), with g_k=conjugate(F_k)^3 H_(d-k), now proves g_k=H_d conjugate(H_k)+Q^(-1)conjugate(J_k), 0<=k<=d. (5) The corresponding PHASED source coefficient, useful before any future color-contour deformation, is exactly (A1)_(d-k)=kappa^4 Q^(-1) q^(k^2)/s_k^2 [H_d conjugate(H_k)+Q^(-1)conjugate(J_k)]. (5a) Indeed W_(d-k)=nu_k g_k/(N s_k^2); the actual factor (-q)^(2d-k)nu_k=Q^(-1)q^(k^2) gives (5a). The constant term Q^(-1) in (4)--(5) is a retained original boundary current. It is not set to zero. The independent J solution does not satisfy the resetting i=1 source equation, which is why that current cannot be absorbed into a second homogeneous source at the endpoint. ## 3. A regular gapped half-circle and a uniform envelope Put u=pi i/N and Y=exp(2iu). The classical monic transfer has roots mu_±(u)=[2-3Y ± Y sqrt(4Y-3)]/2. (6) Choose the square root continuously from +1 at u=0. On 0<=u<=pi/2, the minus root mu is nonzero and dominant until the terminal equality of moduli; write rho(u)=|mu(u)|. The eigenvalue difference has modulus |sqrt(4Y-3)|>=1, so its eigenframe and first derivatives are uniformly bounded on this entire closed half-circle. Here is a direct modulus check. For a=2-3Y, b=(1-Y)^3 and 0<u<=pi/2, a^2/b=(9+16sin^2u)/(8sin^2u) -i cos(u)(1-16sin^2u)/(8sin^3u). Two roots of lambda^2-a lambda+b have equal modulus exactly when a^2/b belongs to [0,4]. The imaginary part vanishes only at sin u=1/4 or cos u=0. The first gives 20, outside that interval; the second gives25/8. Thus the only modulus equality is u=pi/2. At u=0 the roots are -1,0 and the source selects -1. Let I(u)=pi^(-1)integral_0^u log rho(v)dv. Uniformly for all physical i with 0<=i<=d/2, the exact transfer matrix differs by O(1/N) from its classical matrix. In the bounded moving eigenframe, each normalized step has norm at most rho(u_i)(1+C/N). Hence |H_i|+|J_i| <= C exp[N I(pi i/N)]. (7) The constants do not deteriorate at the terminal modulus equality: the eigenVALUES remain separated. The sum-to-integral error is O(1). On every smaller interval 0<=u<=u_0<pi/2 the source is sharper: log|H_i|=N I(pi i/N)+O_(u0)(1), |J_i/H_i|<=C_(u0). (8) To justify the nonzero statement, write h_i=H_i/H_(i-1). The exact Riccati map is h_i=a_i-b_i/h_(i-1). Its derivative at the dominant classical root is mu_other/mu, of modulus uniformly less than one. An O(1/N) disk around the smooth nonzero dominant root is therefore invariant under every step, by induction. The literal reset H_1=1-2Q starts inside that disk. Thus every h_i is nonzero and h_i=mu(u_i)+O(1/N). Summing logarithms proves (8)'s first assertion. For the second, the difference of successive J_i/H_i has consecutive ratio b_i/(h_i h_(i-1)), uniformly less than one; its first difference is1/H_1. This proves the uniform bound. No claim of adiabatic survival is made across the modulus crossing. ## 4. Sharp whole-source norm from the two actual endpoint solutions For the first half, (7) and the uniform sine-factorial estimate give log|W_i| <= N[I(u)+Lambda(u)/pi]+O(log N). For the second half put k=d-i, u=pi k/N. Equations (3),(5), and s_i s_k=N give |W_i|=|g_k|/(N s_k^2), log|W_i| <= N[I(u)+2Lambda(u)/pi]+O(log N). (9) These bounds cover EVERY index, including the middle and endpoints. Since Lambda(u)>=0 on [0,pi/2], the backward profile dominates the forward one. Write B(u)=I(u)+2Lambda(u)/pi. For each fixed u in(0,pi/2), (3),(5),(8) also give the matching lower rate in(9): the J term is relatively O(N^(-3/2)) and cannot cancel the main term. There is a unique maximizer u_* of B. Indeed B'(u)=pi^(-1)log[rho(u)/(2sin u)^2]. For 2sin u<1, rho>=|b|^(1/2)=(2sin u)^(3/2)>(2sin u)^2. For u>=pi/6, an equality rho=(2sin u)^2 can occur only when z^3-4z^2+3z-1=0, z=4sin^2u. (10) One can verify this without choosing a root phase: impose |mu|^2=z^2 in mu^2-a mu+b=0 and its conjugate. The resulting equality is z(1-z)^2=1-2z+2z^2, exactly (10); here |conjugate(b)a-conjugate(a)z^2|^2=z^3(1-2z+2z^2)>0. The polynomial has a unique root z_* in[1,4], in fact in(3,4). At pi/6 the ratio rho/(2sin u)^2 is greater than one, whereas at pi/2 it is1/sqrt2<1. Continuity and uniqueness therefore prove the claimed strict maximum, with u_*=arcsin(sqrt(z_*)/2). Using (1), the polynomial number of positive norm terms and a rounded index near the backward maximizer now prove the ALL-LEVEL estimate log||T_2 P_rev T_2 1||_Newt^2 = N L+O(log N), L=(2/pi)[integral_0^(u_*)log rho(v)dv+2Lambda(u_*)]. (11) Numerically L is approximately .9060724478038353. This number is only a calibration; formula (11) is the proved constant. It comes from the fully coherent source vector before taking its positive norm. ## 5. Scope and reuse The actual adjoint-word closure of A^dagger A is the original numerator source ||A1||^2, with the unrestricted marked cap and kappa retained. Thus (11) is a new coherent estimate for an ENTIRE specified original source circuit, not an expanded positive path. Its link topology, hyperbolicity and regulator identification are separate questions; no volume equality is asserted from its numerical rate. This proof offers a checkable recurrence mechanism beyond distinct eigenvalues: an exact resetting source endpoint, a regular half-domain modulus gap, an independently evaluated nonzero opposite endpoint, and a reflection identity retaining the inhomogeneous current. Those inputs allow the two gapped solutions to be estimated separately. There is no unsupported propagation through a general modulus crossing. The [modular reduction](actual_newton_coherent_turn_reduction.md) removes arbitrarily many redundant turns; genuinely longer reduced mixed words still require their own coherent packet/current estimate. Audit: [literal original matrices, exact sums/recurrences/endpoints and norm calibration](../experiments/audit_actual_newton_two_twist_interaction_packet.py). Independent analytical review and fresh replay passed: the reflection indices/current, endpoint normalization, separated-frame bound through the midpoint, strictly gapped Riccati lower bound, and cubic maximum were each rederived. The finite profiles supplement that proof; they are not its justification.

title: The nilpotent Mobius action is not the actual framing Ward action
text: # The nilpotent Mobius action is not the actual framing Ward action 28 October 2026. A common fractional-linear change of the charged nilpotent anchors is an exact algebra automorphism. Its effect on the ORIGINAL source is computable. However, it does not provide a second geometric framing integral: invariance of a homogeneous top-degree state is automatic, while the ordinary common action fails covariance with an ORIGINAL crossing. Its source-preserving weighted lift also has the wrong nilpotent Jordan type to be the actual Hopf current on a head. This rules out that specific identification. It does not rule out a coupled quantum dressing which transforms clocks, crossings and source currents together, or the independent positive selection theorem for a network already satisfying its stated hypotheses. ## 1. Exact automorphism and source Jacobian Put d=N-1 and A_N=K[X]/(X^N), in characteristic zero. The source is the ORIGINAL functional lambda(P)=[X^d]P. For a!=0 define phi_(a,c)(X)=aX/(1+cX) mod X^N. (1) The inverse is X/(a-cX), so this is an algebra automorphism. Its SOURCE formula, valid for EVERY polynomial exterior, is lambda(P(phi_(a,c)(X))) =lambda(P(X) J_(a,c)(X)), J_(a,c)(X)=a(a-cX)^(N-2). (2) Proof. In the specified residue lambda=Res P(X)dX/X^N, make the formal invertible change Y=aX/(1+cX). Then X=Y/(a-cY) and dX/X^N=a(a-cY)^(N-2)dY/Y^N. This proves (2) with its exact scalar and exponent. For k anchors the source factor is the product of the k displayed J factors. At a=1, its infinitesimal identity is lambda(-X^2 partial_X P)=-(N-2)lambda(XP). (3) Thus ordinary Mobius substitution does NOT preserve the original source on arbitrary exteriors. The coefficient norm of its source multiplier at a=1 is exactly ||(1-cX)^(N-2)||_1=(1+|c|)^(N-2). (4) At fixed nonzero c this is exponential in N. This is a norm statement about the full normal source, not a claim that the original scalar acquires that factor. ## 2. Why homogeneous-source invariance is automatic For k original charged anchors let Omega=product_i X_i^d. The top homogeneous piece of A_N^(tensor k) has degree kd and is the ONE line K Omega. Every actual whole-source P_h is homogeneous of that degree before projection, including after the proved closure contractions. Under common (1), each variable starts with aX_i and all remaining terms have strictly higher degree. Since no degree above kd survives, phi_(a,c)(P_h)=a^(kd) P_h in A_N^(tensor k). (5) In particular c-invariance at a=1 holds for EVERY top-degree state, whether its selected coefficient is nonzero or zero. The induced c-action on this socle line is trivial. It therefore contains no information identifying a geometric relative period or selecting a nonzero second framing fiber. This is the same original homogeneous socle, not a substituted favorable source. It remains possible to retain lower-degree normal classes and the full Jacobian (2). Their covariance must actually be proved; (5) cannot replace it. ## 3. The exact source-preserving lift has the wrong Ward generator There is a specified weighted action preserving lambda on ALL states: U_(a,c)P(X)=a^(-d)(1+cX)^(N-2)P(phi_(a,c)(X)). (6) Indeed (2), or direct substitution in it, gives lambda(U P)=lambda(P). At a=1 its infinitesimal generator is L=(N-2)X-X^2 partial_X, L X^j=(N-2-j)X^(j+1). (7) For N>=3 its Jordan blocks are N-1 and 1: it acts in one full chain on 1,X,...,X^(N-2), and kills the separate socle X^d. At N=2 it is zero. The UNWEIGHTED substitution generator -X^2 partial_X likewise has blocks N-1 and 1, with the separate constant line instead. The ORIGINAL complete quantum E and F on one physical head have a single Jordan block of size N. For F its consecutive coefficients in the actual balanced basis are 1-Q^(j+1), 0<=j<=N-2, all nonzero. The corresponding E coefficients are also nonzero along their whole chain. Consequently no invertible head gauge conjugates (7), or its unweighted version, to the actual E or F. Nilpotent Jordan type is unchanged by any such gauge. One can instead use the ordinary coherent weight (1+cX)^d, obtaining the regular classical generator dX-X^2 partial_X. But then the source is NOT fixed; exactly lambda((1+cX)^d P(X/(1+cX))) =lambda(P(X)/(1-cX)). (8) Moreover the primitive two-head coherent generator has nilpotency index 2N-1, whereas the actual root Hopf coproduct has its N-th power zero. Thus even this alternative is not a factorwise identification with the actual quantum tensor action. Its source and tensor adapter would have to be constructed and retained separately. ## 4. A literal original crossing fails common Mobius covariance This is also visible without a representation classification. Let B be the ORIGINAL positive checked crossing in the actual balanced factorial basis and retain its common Cartan scalar kappa. Complete color means x=-q^(-1), Q=q^2, hence x^(-2)=Q. Its k=0 entries give [|0,1>] B |1,0>=kappa x^(-1), [|0,2>] B |2,0>=kappa x^(-2). (9) For N>=3 put D=-X^2 partial_X and D_tot=D_1+D_2. Then [|0,2>] [B,D_tot] |1,0> =kappa(x^(-1)-x^(-2)) !=0. (10) To see the two terms, D_tot|1,0>=-|2,0>; after B only its k=0 term can yield |0,2>. Conversely B|1,0> has |0,1> coefficient in (9), and D_tot sends it to -|0,2>. This proves (10), with no lost factorial, source normalization or Cartan scalar. At the actual half-root x^(-1)=-q and x^(-2)=q^2, so the difference is -q(1+q), nonzero for every N>=3. Therefore the common ordinary Mobius action cannot be slid through the unchanged actual crossing. Full E/F Ward identities do not supply that missing covariance, since they concern the different Hopf action in Section 3. At N=2 the unweighted Mobius substitution is already the identity on K[X]/X^2 and supplies no framing direction at all. ## 5. Consequence for the proposed second framing fiber The [nilpotent source](actual_charged_socle_and_fermat_source.md) and [closure contractions](actual_general_flow_fusion.md) are exact. The ordinary common Mobius changes do not add a selected nonzero fiber to them. On the original top-degree state they act trivially by (5). On general exteriors they require the source multiplier (2), and on the fixed actual network they have the explicit covariance defect (10). This leaves a precise constructive possibility: a COUPLED quantum framing transformation, including the underclock feedback, Hopf tensor factors and boundary co-source, might have a controlled nonzero relative fiber. It cannot be identified with the common automorphism (1) merely from nilpotent-source invariance. The existing warning about ordinary coherent Mobius action versus actual quantum dressing in [the Springer boundary note](springer_centralizer_boundary_source.md) is consistent with, and now has the explicit selected-source and crossing calculations (2)-(10). No broad knot-volume lower bound or nonzero global geometric coefficient is proved by this test. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_nilpotent_mobius_source.py): exact source Jacobians and inverse maps, both weighted source actions, their Jordan indices, original quantum E/F chains and the full original crossing witness (10), with kappa retained.

title: Projected nodes, actual local periods, and the surviving Ward source
text: # Projected nodes, actual local periods, and the surviving Ward source 28 October 2026. A collision of two preferred-longitude values need not be a collision of the original critical points. On two disjoint regular Morse charts of the ORIGINAL coefficient density, the local periods have a bounded separating insertion frame even at that projected node. Internal shift identities have explicit exponentially small relative-boundary errors on these charts. No inverse longitude difference is used. This does not prove that the selected finite knot source splits into these local periods with a bounded connection. The exact original figure-eight Ward equation below shows why the missing source step cannot be replaced by the classical separating projectors. The distinction concerns a projected node, not a genuine collision on the full normalized character scheme. ## 1. Actual density and the analytic hypotheses Keep the actual whole coefficient array, integral closure lattice, cut average, pivots, Cartan/framing constants and peripheral line of [the geometric normal-period theorem](actual_geometric_normal_period.md). Fix its two framing coordinates on a transverse slice. Write the remaining scaled internal coordinates as z in C^r and u=Log M. The preferred meridian half-step is u -> u+pi*i/N. Use the exactly normalized factorial interpolant, equivalently [the exact full-Psi quotient](actual_factorial_full_psi_identity.md), with the original affine arguments and their marks. Denote this holomorphic density on a regular chart by omega_N(u,z). No new finite-state values or co-source are assigned. Here are the analytic premises needed below. They are more than a formal stationary series. On fixed neighborhoods of two sections z_p(u), p=1,2, suppose omega_N = chi_N(u) N^beta exp[N Phi(u,z)] a_N(u,z) dz_1...dz_r, (1) a_N=a_0+O(1/N), a_0(u,z_p(u)) != 0, uniformly holomorphically, with all fixed derivatives on smaller neighborhoods. The external normalization chi_N is retained as a line; it is not assumed tame or dropped. Phi=S/(2pi*i) is the actual marked action. Suppose partial_z Phi(u,z_p(u))=0, det partial_z^2 Phi(u,z_p(u)) != 0, z_1(u) != z_2(u). (2) All bounds and separations are uniform after shrinking the u-disk. When a separating actual monomial is used below, the two exponentiated critical configurations must also be distinct; different logarithmic lifts of the same configuration are not enough. For the reduced coefficient density chi_N is nonzero and holomorphic on the chosen chart. If the full ADO dimension is included, its possibly meromorphic line stays external: analyticity and nonvanishing below refer to the normalized sections Z_p,N/chi_N, and scalar ratios are asserted on the regular locus of that line. No fixed-size pole-free disk for the full ADO dimension is assumed. For a finite product of original factorial interpolants, (1) follows from the proved uniform complex Stirling estimate whenever every scaled factorial argument stays in a compact subset of 0<Re s<1. The powers N^beta and scalar marks are literal ones. Other regular full-Psi charts can be used only where their marked uniform symbol has actually been established. The formal normal theorem alone does not establish (1) on an arbitrary continued chart. If an exact cotangent or window factor is included in a chosen local source presentation, (1) must hold for that factor too, with its retained mode/action. A bare coefficient estimate is not automatically an estimate for every relative source sector. The [actual critical correspondence](marked_braid_holonomy.md) identifies (2), on its full regular locus, with distinct framed knot representations. The nondegenerate transverse Hessian is supplied at the geometric branch by the normal-period theorem. Its conjugate has the same algebraic nondegeneracy. A projected coincidence L_1(u_0)=L_2(u_0) (3) does not invalidate either of these full critical charts. ## 2. Analytic local periods have a bounded frame at the node **Local theorem.** Under (1)--(2), after shrinking the u-disk, there are disjoint truncated Gaussian cycles Gamma_p(u) and exact analytic periods Z_p,N(f;u)=integral_(Gamma_p(u)) f(u,z) omega_N(u,z), (4) such that Z_p,N(1;u)=chi_N(u) N^(beta-r/2) exp[N phi_p(u)] [b_p,0(u)+O(1/N)], phi_p=Phi(u,z_p), b_p,0 != 0. (5) The cycles in (4) are specified local relative cycles for the unchanged actual density. They are not asserted to be summands of the selected finite lattice cycle. Choose a holomorphic insertion theta with |theta(u,z_1(u))-theta(u,z_2(u))| >= delta > 0. For distinct exponentiated critical configurations such a theta is a fixed linear combination of the actual internal monomials: each distinct pair excludes only a proper hyperplane of choices. For the two literal insertions 1,theta, form M_N(p,0)=1, M_N(p,1)=Z_p,N(theta;u)/Z_p,N(1;u). (6) Then uniformly on a smaller disk, M_N(p,1)=theta(u,z_p(u))+O(1/N), ||M_N||+||M_N^-1|| <= C. (7) In particular, (3) does not cause an insertion-frame singularity. The normalized sections Z_p,N/chi_N are nonzero for all sufficiently large N, as are the scalar periods on the regular nonzero locus of the external line. The exact diagonal meridian ratios in this LOCAL period object are b_p,N(u)=Z_p,N(1;u+pi*i/N)/Z_p,N(1;u). (8) After retaining chi_N's exact ratio, they have the actual marked leading longitude ratio. Indeed N times the action increment tends to partial_u S_p/2=Log L_p. The common prescribed external scalar line must be included in whichever longitude convention is used. Proof. A parameter-dependent holomorphic Morse coordinate y exists near each section, with Phi(u,z(y,u))=phi_p(u)-(y_1^2+...+y_r^2)/2. One elementary construction first solves partial_1 Phi=0 for z_1 by the implicit-function theorem, completes that square using the analytic square root of its nonzero coefficient, and repeats on the Schur complement. A fixed complex linear change makes the needed pivots nonzero at the base point. Shrinking the disk keeps these pivots and square roots holomorphic and bounded. This proves the asserted coordinate without an asymptotic summability premise. Take the image of the real cube [-eta,eta]^r with its fixed orientation. The two images remain disjoint. In these coordinates ordinary Gaussian integration, a Taylor expansion on a smaller cube and an exponentially small outside tail give (5). Its leading coefficient is (2pi)^(r/2) times the original a_0 and the marked Morse-coordinate Jacobian. Every factor is nonzero. The same calculation with theta gives (7). Analyticity follows by integrating over a fixed cube in y; the exponentially small tails are analytic as well. Formula (8) is then an exact analytic ratio. This proof does not divide by L_1-L_2 or solve a scalar companion eigenvector problem at the projected node. For clarity, transporting a LOCAL branch vector in the insertion frame produces the matrix M_N(u+pi*i/N)^t diag(b_1,N,b_2,N) M_N(u)^(-t). (9) Its frames are bounded by (7). This is a statement about the direct sum of the specified local periods. Equation (9) is not identified with the global finite-source companion, nor is it an explicit new all-level operator. Such an identification would require the source pushforward which is still missing. ## 3. Exact local Ward errors are relative-boundary currents There is a source-relevant quantitative refinement. Let v be one actual internal integer shift, scaled as delta_N=v/N (with the corresponding convention if logarithmic coordinates are used). The original factorial functional equations give EXACTLY omega_N(u,z+delta_N)=R_v,N(u,z) omega_N(u,z), (10) on the common regular chart, including the original Gaussian and all characters. Let f be holomorphic on that common chart. Let H_p,N be the translation cylinder of Gamma_p by delta_N, and B_p,N the cylinder of its boundary. With consistent boundary orientations, holomorphic Stokes gives the exact identity Z_p,N(R_v,N f(u,z+delta_N)-f(u,z);u) = integral_(B_p,N) f omega_N. (11) There are c>0,C,B independent of N for which the right side satisfies |integral_(B_p,N) f omega_N| <= |chi_N(u)| C N^B ||f|| exp[N(Re phi_p(u)-c)]. (12) Here ||f|| is the supremum on a fixed neighborhood of the cylinder. To prove it, the unshifted boundary has |y|>=eta and hence an action drop at least eta^2/2. Its O(1/N) translation changes Re Phi by O(1/N), uniformly by holomorphy. Thus a fixed positive fraction of the drop remains. The cylinder's volume and Jacobians have uniform polynomial bounds; (1) proves (12). No discarded boundary term is set to zero. Relative to its own nonzero local period, this error is at most C N^B exp(-cN). Consequently the full regular phase has separate analytic quantum blocks with exponentially accurate local Ward relations even when the scalar longitude roots coincide. Genuine complex collisions of the FULL critical points, a vanishing Hessian, a source pole crossing, or continuation outside these neighborhoods are excluded. Also, an external action gain can amplify (12). The comparison of its c with the full action width is an extra estimate, just as in [the local analytic transport barrier](actual_local_analytic_transport_action_barrier.md). ## 4. An exact original-source test at an actual projected node The original figure-eight identity gives, at M=1 and EVERY level, K_N=sum_(n=0)^d w_n, w_n=|(Q;Q)_n|^2, mu_N(f)=sum_n w_n f(Q^n), d=N-1. (13) This is the complete reduced source with its original pointing, not an arbitrary normal-state co-source. Its two classical critical clocks are z_+=(1+i sqrt(3))/2, z_-=(1-i sqrt(3))/2, the distinct geometric/conjugate character lifts with the same complete preferred longitude. The two saddles of the exact sine interpolant G_N(Ns)^2 lie at s=1/6,5/6. Its phase is 2J(s), with nonzero second derivatives +2pi sqrt(3),-2pi sqrt(3), respectively. Thus this is an actual source example satisfying the local analytic premises: the two full critical points are regular while their peripheral projection is nodal. Their calibrated regulators have opposite signs. The real positive finite source is not replaced by the sum of both local Gaussian cycles. The full finite Ward equation retains an endpoint. Put A(Z)=2-Z-Z^-1, (B_Q f)(Z)=A(QZ) f(QZ). The exact weights satisfy w_(n+1)=A(Q^(n+1))w_n, w_0=1,w_N=0. Therefore, for EVERY Laurent polynomial insertion, mu_N((I-B_Q)f)=f(1). (14) Now take the classical separating functions e_+(Z)=(Z-z_-)/(z_+-z_-), e_-=1-e_+. They separate the two classical critical points, but [B_Q,e_+]f =(Q-1) Z A(QZ) f(QZ)/(z_+-z_-), (15) mu_N((I-B_Q)e_+)=z_+/(z_+-z_-) != 0, mu_N((I-B_Q)e_-)=-z_-/(z_+-z_-) != 0. (16) These are exact original-source identities, not asymptotic errors. The pointwise commutator is O(1/N) on the unit clock grid, but it is not zero. Such algebraic smallness cannot alone establish an exponential conversion barrier. Moreover e_+ and e_- are not exact idempotents in C[Z,Z^-1]/(Z^N-1); their idempotent defect is proportional to Z^2-Z+1. In the SAME source, N mu_N((Z^2-Z+1)(Z^-2-Z^-1+1))/K_N -> 2pi sqrt(3), (17) as proved in [the source-quotient theorem](actual_source_quotient_and_critical_relation.md). Thus the positive paired insertion of that idempotent defect still has the full geometric exponential rate. The exact global source cannot be replaced by the reduced critical projectors while discarding only exponentially smaller terms. This does not show harmful node conversion occurs in this knot. It shows exactly which source identity a proposed exact separation would have to improve. In fact this prototype has a separate positive whole-source proof; (14)--(17) explain why the node's local classical idempotents are not that proof. ## 5. The remaining quantum test The [pointed commutant theorem](actual_pointed_commutant_and_critical_observable.md) already proves that every horizontal endomorphism preserving the raw Mellin source lattice acts scalarly on its selected source. Its partial insertion module supplies formal critical observables, with a covariant rule rather than a zero commutator. The local analytic construction above strengthens the regular-node statement but does not evade that exact source obstruction. To exclude harmful nodal conversion for the original whole period, one must still do one of the following with the ORIGINAL source: identify a bounded analytic pushforward to these separated local periods and bound all the currents in (11), or construct a different covariant multioperator module whose actual connection has the necessary equal-calibrated-action support/exponential barrier. Classical sheet separation and a nondegenerate full Hessian supply neither identification automatically. A formal direct sum alone cannot detect a nonzero exponentially small entry. In particular, this note proves a regular projected node introduces no LOCAL Morse or insertion-frame singularity. It does not prove that the actual global connection contains no conversion there, that the geometric coefficient of the selected cycle is nonzero, or a sharp whole-knot upper bound. [Finite audit](../experiments/audit_actual_node_source_ward.py): exact original cyclic weights, affine Ward endpoint, classical separating commutator and nonzero two-node source values over finite fields. The analytic statements above are proved by the uniform Morse and side-cylinder estimates, not inferred from the finite audit.

title: A source-exact quotient for normalization boundary currents, including normal jets
text: # A source-exact quotient for normalization boundary currents, including normal jets 29 October 2026. There is a genuine class of singular relative-source components that can be eliminated before positivity: the zero-pointing part of a complete visible Markov normalization cell. This is an operator identity with spectators retained. It composes through any fixed forest of such cells at arbitrary braid width, even when the spectator coefficients are not scalar or mutually commuting. For the original full-Psi radial current, even at radius one, every normalized Mellin Taylor coefficient of its pointed scalar is at most N/(2pi). The entire radial operator on a nilpotent contraction has normalized coefficients bounded by H_N/(2pi). On a fixed radius below one, oscillation gives the sharper bound C r! log(eN)^r for raw pointed derivatives. Thus these actual logarithmic normal currents have no additional exponential normalization cost after contraction. This extends the known normalization-cell evaluation and its tame radial value to an operator-valued relative-current quotient with a quantified normal germ. It does not eliminate internal head/cap alias currents, identify Mellin order with the knot meridian, or prove a sharp bound for the remaining knot period. ## 1. The exact selected cell, with all original scalar factors Use the literal positive equal-color factorization and pivot of [the Markov source proof](actual_markov_ray_normalization_and_pruning.md): R+=kappa C D U C^-1, g_b=x^(-d) Q^(-b), d=N-1, alpha=kappa x^(-d). For every diagonal function r of the second RELATIVE channel, Tr_new[(I tensor g) kappa C D U (I tensor r) C^-1] =alpha r_0 I. (1) The trace has NO additional 1/N. The original sole cut average, turns, marked row and full peripheral/framing line are unchanged. Zero framing cancels the original alpha only when the complete original Markov cell is contracted. A current with r_0 != 1 keeps that extra factor. For completeness, the direct finite coefficient proof of (1) computes the k-th channel's cut diagonal as alpha x^(-2k) Q^(-k) (1;Q)_k = alpha delta_(k,0). Its intermediate q-binomial identity is sum_(j=0)^s (-1)^(s-j) Q^[j(j+1)/2] (Q^(a-j+1);Q)_s/[F_j F_(s-j)]=(-1)^s. Expand the Pochhammer as a polynomial in Q^a. All its positive-degree coefficients contain (Q^(1-ell);Q)_s and vanish; the constant is the right side. A second finite binomial sum gives (1). This proof retains the forbidden-index zeros of the original finite head and works at all levels, including even and composite N. ## 2. Operator-valued pointing and exact cancellation of its kernel Let S be ANY spectator space. Replace r_k by arbitrary operators A_k on S, acting at the same relative-channel slot in (1). Then Tr_new[(I tensor g tensor I_S) kappa (C D U tensor I_S) (sum_k I_cut tensor |k><k| tensor A_k) (C^-1 tensor I_S)] =alpha I_cut tensor A_0. (2) To prove (2), expand in any basis of End(S) and apply (1) to every coefficient. No positivity, simultaneous diagonalization or assumption about an exterior knot value enters. In particular A_k may be coupled to arbitrary tensors outside the cell, but not silently moved through the cut head or the inside of C. Define the pointing map epsilon(A)=A_0. The difference A_k-A_0 for every k (3) is annihilated by the COMPLETE cell. Thus a source-current packet may be replaced by its pointing after the whole cell has been assembled. It is not necessary for the norms of its individual channels to be small. Equation (2) remains valid after arbitrary exterior composition and the original full marked functional. The same statement holds coefficientwise for a holomorphic or meromorphic normal germ A_k(sigma), on a common domain where the cell expression is defined. If epsilon(A(sigma)) is identically zero, ALL its normal Laurent/Taylor coefficients pair to zero. A pole in separated channel pieces is canceled only after their common complete packet is formed; (2) is not a prescription to drop those poles first. Now suppose a fixed tensor diagram contains a forest of visible cells: each leaf has the precise form (2), and after contracting a leaf the next prescribed cell has that form. Contract leaves in this order. Induction proves that every zero-pointing leaf packet disappears exactly, and each surviving cell is replaced by its specified A_0, in the ORIGINAL operator order. This is an all-width source theorem, not a claim that every braid admits such a pruning or that arbitrary internal projectors can be slid to a cap. ## 3. The actual radial current and its Mellin-normal germ Fix a real 0<R<1, independent of N. Let Psi be the fully normalized positive function from [the original circle/ray source](actual_modular_dilog_circle_and_boundary_source.md). The actual positive atom's radial part in the displayed cell has channel coefficients r_k(0)=-N Q^(d-k) E_(d-k)(R)/F_k, where E_a(R)=1/(2pi*i) integral_0^R Psi(log t)/(1-t^N) * t^(N-a-1) dt. Consequently its pointed scalar is EXACTLY h_N(0)=-N Q^-1 E_d(R). (4) It must be retained: the original ray group is h_N(0) times the whole exterior invariant, and need not have a smaller exponential rate. The circle group is (1-h_N(0)) times that same exterior. There is a natural logarithmic normal of this specified relative radial current: multiply its radial integrand by t^(-sigma). For Re sigma<1 set h_N(sigma)=-N Q^-1/(2pi*i) integral_0^R Psi(log t)/(1-t^N) * t^(-sigma) dt. (5) This is holomorphic there, by integrable domination on compact sigma-sets. Its derivatives are the literal insertions (-log t)^r in the ORIGINAL radial current. At sigma=0 (5) is (4), with the original phase and coefficient, not a rescaled boundary state. Sigma is a Mellin-normal coordinate of this atom source. It is NOT being identified with the knot's meridian parameter or with a normal Cartan coupon elsewhere in the word. ## 4. Uniform normal currents through radius one The exact real-ray modulus, with the complete central factor retained, is |Psi_epsilon(log t)|^2=(1-t)(1-t^N), 0<t<=1. Consequently its quotient has modulus A_N(t)=sqrt((1-t)/(1-t^N))<=1, A_N(1)=1/sqrt(N). (6a) There is no pole at t=1. This proves, for EVERY 0<R<=1 and r>=0, |h_N^(r)(0)|/r! <=N/(2pi*r!) integral_0^R A_N(t)(-log t)^r dt <=N/(2pi). (6b) For Re sigma<1 it also proves |h_N(sigma)|<=N/[2pi(1-Re sigma)]. (6c) All normal coefficients are those of the actual Mellin current (5). No fixed-distance-from-one assumption, separated root branch, or pointwise phase approximation enters (6a)--(6c). There is an operator version BEFORE the normalization cell is closed. For a literal nilpotent contraction T on its supplied finite relative head, T^N=0 and ||T||<=1, retain the full source correction E_sigma(T)=epsilon/(2pi*i) integral_0^R Psi_epsilon(log t)/(1-t^N) * t^(N-sigma-1) sum_(a=0)^d t^(-a)T^a dt. (6d) It is a holomorphic operator germ for Re sigma<1 and includes every original finite resolvent coefficient. Differentiation and (6a) give || E_sigma^(r)(T)|_(sigma=0) /r! || <=(1/(2pi)) sum_(j=1)^N j^(-r-1) <=H_N/(2pi), r>=0. (6e) The first inequality uses integral_0^1 t^(j-1)(-log t)^r dt=r!/j^(r+1). Similarly, for |sigma|<=rho<1 the whole operator germ is at most [1/(1-rho)+H_N]/(2pi). (6f) This applies in the stated nilpotent-contraction metric. No assertion is made that every conjugated interior atom is a contraction in one common physical metric; changing that metric or composing with an unrestricted exterior still requires its actual estimates. The first Mellin pole at the other endpoint is also explicit. The actual small-t expansion starts with Psi(log t)=1+O(t), up to higher logarithmic terms which do not affect this first pole. Therefore Res_(sigma=1) E_sigma(T)=-epsilon T^d/(2pi*i), Res_(sigma=1) h_N(sigma)=N Q^-1/(2pi*i). (6g) Subtract the constant term in the a=d coefficient of (6d); the remaining integral is holomorphic through sigma=1. Every other coefficient is already integrable there. This proves (6g), with its sign and full original normalization. It is a retained source current, not zero. For a fixed ordered collection of such atom endpoints the iterated residues are the corresponding ordered products of T_j^d; their norm is at most one in the supplied contraction metrics. After the displayed normalization-cell pointing their scalar cost is polynomial in N. No reordering of noncommuting atoms is used. For a fixed normalization forest, (6b) bounds an independent normalized multijet by (N/(2pi))^L. If all cells share one normal coordinate, the order-r coefficient has the additional count binom(r+L-1,L-1). Thus even growing normalized jet orders cost only a polynomial in N and r for this fixed forest. These coefficients may be nonzero; they are retained scalar source factors, not declared negligible. ### Sharper pointed estimate at a fixed interior radius There is C_R, independent of N, such that sup_(|sigma|<=1/log(eN)) |h_N(sigma)| <= C_R. (6) Here is a direct proof, including the t=0 endpoint. The exact small-disk full-Psi expansion, with one fixed derivative, gives Psi(log t)/(1-t^N)=a_N(t) exp[-iN phi(t)], phi(t)=Li2(t)/(2pi), ||a_N||_(C^1[0,R])<=C_R, 0<c_R<=phi'(t)<=C_R, |phi''(t)|<=C_R. (7) It follows from the normalized full function, including its central period; the proof and two-derivative version are given in the Markov source note. The finitely many small levels can be absorbed in C_R. Split the integral at 1/N (or at R if R<1/N). On the first interval, with rho=1/log(eN), N integral_0^(1/N) |t^(-sigma) a_N(t)| dt <=C_R N^(Re sigma)/(1-Re sigma)<=C_R. On [1/N,R], integrate the oscillatory exponential once by parts, keeping BOTH endpoint terms. Multiplication by N cancels its 1/N. The endpoint terms are bounded since N^(Re sigma)<=e and R is fixed. The derivative of a_N/phi' gives a bounded integral. The only remaining term is bounded by C_R |sigma| integral_(1/N)^R t^(-Re sigma-1) dt <=C_R |sigma| log N max(1,N^(Re sigma))<=C_R.
