This proves (6). No claim of pointwise smallness of the original ray has been used, and its lower endpoint contribution is not discarded. In particular Cauchy's formula on that normal disk gives |h_N^(r)(0)| <= C_R r! log(eN)^r, r>=0. (8) For a fixed forest of L cells with independent normal coordinates, the resulting pointed scalar germs are products in the specified operator order. In the scalar radial case their multijets satisfy |partial^nu product_(j=1)^L h_(N,j)(0)| <=C^L product_j(nu_j!) log(eN)^(|nu|). (9) For fixed L and fixed total order this is polynomial (indeed polylogarithmic). Raw derivative orders with |nu| log((|nu|+1)log(eN))=o(N) still cost exp(o(N)); normalized Taylor coefficients need only |nu| log log(eN)=o(N). The conjugate radial integral has the same analytic estimate. The operator-valued pointing assertion here is for the displayed POSITIVE cell. A negative cell may be contracted as its complete original normalization, but no unstated negative arbitrary-channel formula is assumed. In particular no original pivot is replaced by a fresh average. ## 5. Scope for the global contour question This is a source-specific cancellation before positivity, valid with all original spectators and marked data. The full radial current is not thrown away: its pointed scalar and its controlled normal germ remain. The zero-pointing part vanishes as a complete original-source pairing, without assuming a thimble comparison. The operation can remove normalization boundary components even when separate circle/ray pieces individually carry the whole knot rate. It changes individual-state evaluation tests and so evades the genuine obstruction to a UNIVERSAL cotangent chart homotopy. Its hypothesis is the literal visible-cell/forest structure, not merely a rational spectral relation or a matching character value. For genuinely internal head, transfer and alias clusters that structure has not been proved. Their complete currents may not lie in this pointing kernel. No sharp upper bound for the remaining pruned period, no all-face descending cycle, and no original-source lower bound follow from (1)--(9). Extending source-specific contraction to those internal clusters remains substantive work. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_normalization_boundary_current.py) checks the operator-valued all-input identity with original crossings, ordinary pivots and marked exteriors, and independently evaluates the full-Psi Mellin current and its first logarithmic normal derivatives.

title: A source-specific backward Ward estimate on shrinking clock disks
text: # A source-specific backward Ward estimate on shrinking clock disks 29 October 2026. The exact normalization packet identified in [the original cup-slide calculation](actual_terminal_source_normalization_packet.md) has a polynomial bound on a disk of radius 1/N about its original clock. This controls the entire clock germ, not only its value. The proof uses an exact backward recurrence; its contraction product cancels the exponential size of the original factorial coefficients. More generally the packet is subexponential on EVERY shrinking disk. This supplies a genuine sharp, zero-exponent estimate for this actual normalization source and for specified sublinear-frequency exterior couplings. It does not prove the hyperbolic-volume bound for an arbitrary braid, or a uniform bound on a different open physical head. ## 1. The original finite polynomial and its exact Ward equation Put N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), F_j=(Q;Q)_j, s_j=|F_j| and H_N(t)=sum_(j=0)^d F_j t^j. (1) Every statement below also holds with Q replaced by its conjugate. Since F_j=(1-Q^j)F_(j-1), and F_N=0 exactly, the polynomial satisfies (1-t)H_N(t)+t Q H_N(Qt)=1. (2) This is an identity of the original finite function. No endpoint remainder, coefficient, or peripheral factor has been discarded. Let k=floor(N/6). The elementary sine sequence obeys min_(0<=j<N) s_j=s_k, s_j s_(d-j)=N, max_j s_j=N/s_k. (3) For the first assertion use s_j/s_(j-1)=2sin(pi*j/N): this ratio is at most one up to N/6, at least one from N/6 to 5N/6, and then at most one. The final value s_d=N exceeds s_0=1. Reflection follows from F_d=N and the complementary conjugate factors, and proves the last assertion, including ties and small N. In particular, for any t with |t-1|<=c/N, |H_N(tQ^r)| <= exp(c) N^2/s_k (4) for every integer r. This coarse bound uses absolute values and is exponential by itself. The next step retains a coherent recurrence before using it. ## 2. Exact backward propagation cancels that exponential Iterate (2) from tQ^(-k) to t. With empty products equal to one, H_N(t)=sum_(r=0)^(k-1) (-1)^r t^(-r-1) Q^[r(r+1)/2] product_(j=1)^r(1-tQ^(-j)) +(-1)^k t^(-k)Q^[k(k-1)/2] product_(j=1)^k(1-tQ^(-j)) H_N(tQ^(-k)). (5) This follows by substitution, so phases as well as moduli remain specified. For k=0 it is simply the original polynomial. Assume 0<c<=N/2 and |t-1|<=c/N. For 1<=j<=k, 4j/N <= |1-Q^(-j)| <= 1, |1-tQ^(-j)| <= |1-Q^(-j)|+c/N. Consequently product_(j=1)^k |1-tQ^(-j)| <=s_k product_(j=1)^k(1+c/(4j)). (6) Also |t|^(-k)<=exp(c/3). For an intermediate product in the sum of (5), its modulus is at most (1+c/N)^r<=exp(c/6). Thus the whole forcing sum has modulus at most 2k exp(2c/3). For b=c/4 and k>0, a decreasing-function integral estimate gives sum_(j=1)^k log(1+b/j) <=integral_0^k log(1+b/u)du =k log(1+b/k)+b log(1+k/b) <=b[1+log(1+k/b)]. (7) Since k/b<=2N/(3c), the combination of (4)--(7) bounds the remainder by exp(19c/12) N^2 (1+2N/(3c))^(c/4). (8) The decisive cancellation is the factor s_k in (6) against 1/s_k in (4). There is no estimated adiabatic eigenbranch or untracked mode conversion in this first-order finite identity. Adding the forcing sum, and treating k=0 directly by (4), proves the uniform, all-level bound SUP_(|t-1|<=c/N) |H_N(t)| <= B_(N,c):=2 exp(2c) N^2 (1+2N/(3c))^(c/4), 0<c<=N/2. (9) A simpler bound sufficient when c is fixed is SUP |H_N(t)| <=2 exp(2c) N^(2+c/4). (10) For (10), use sum_j log(1+c/(4j))<=c H_k/4 and H_k<=1+log(k+1), with k+1<=N, directly in (6). At t=1 the same argument is sharper and especially elementary: |H_N(1)|<= k+N^2. (11) All forcing products then have modulus at most one, and (6) is exactly s_k. Thus this independently bounds the original endpoint sum without a spectral trace formula or a saddle argument. ## 3. Whole shrinking germs and their derivatives If c_N=o(N), equation (9) gives log SUP_(|t-1|<=c_N/N) |H_N(t)|=o(N), (12) as an upper bound: c_N log(1+N/c_N)=o(N), and log N=o(N). More explicitly, the logarithm is at most log 2+2log N+2c_N+(c_N/4)log(1+2N/(3c_N)). (13) For a fixed c>0, ordinary complex Cauchy on this actual holomorphic disk gives, for EVERY integer r>=0, |H_N^(r)(1)|/r! <= B_(N,c) (N/c)^r. (14) The bound is polynomial in N at every fixed normal order. It is also an explicit quantitative estimate when r grows; no claim of subexponential cost is inferred for arbitrary r=O(N). ## 4. The exact original source packet to which the theorem applies The complete physical cup slide gives R12 R23 p=N e0. After the specified terminal R23^2 and actual cap, its recorded rows are b_j=x^(-d) Q^(-j) conjugate(F_j) =x^(-d) Q[conjugate(F_j)-conjugate(F_(j+1))], x=Q^(d/2), conjugate(F_N)=0. (15) Here x has its ORIGINAL mark x=q^d, q=exp(pi*i/N); the notation Q^(d/2) retains that mark. Every full crossing scalar and source factor in (15) is the one in the linked original-source proof. Define Hbar_N(t)=sum_j conjugate(F_j)t^j. The exact phase-generating function of these rows is f_N(t)=sum_j b_j t^j =x^(-d) Q[(1-t^(-1))Hbar_N(t)+t^(-1)]. (16) Its apparent pole at zero is removable. In particular f_N(1)=x^(-d)Q has unit modulus, whereas the full-circle packet energy sum_j|b_j|^2=sum_j s_j^2 is exponential. Thus (9) resolves an actual full-source normalization test that the flat packet norm fails, not merely an arbitrary polynomial example. On the disk of (9), |f_N(t)| <=2+(2c/N) B_(N,c). (17) For the weighted Cayley-arc energy of [the exact Cauchy metric](actual_shrinking_arc_cauchy_metric.md), put t=(1+i a s)/(1-i a s), -1<=s<=1. Then |t-1|<=2a. Choose c=2Na (for large N so that c<=N/2). Equations (12),(17) and (1+a^2s^2)^d<=exp(Na^2) show log E_arc(f_N)=o(N) whenever a=a_N->0. (18) The equality of the exponential rate to zero also uses the exact evaluation lower bound E_arc>=|f_N(1)|^2/kappa_d>=1/N. For a<=C/N the upper bound is polynomial. All fixed derivatives of f_N at one are polynomially bounded as well, by (17) and Cauchy. The original external scalar chi_N, if used, multiplies f_N and its squared energy by chi_N and |chi_N|^2 respectively. It remains explicit. The raw source identity above already retains all common crossing phases; no auxiliary positive invariant is substituted. ## 5. Precise scope of the exterior and global problem For an exposed recorded packet with operator-valued diagonal exterior A_j(t)=sum_(|ell|<=D_N) A_ell(t) Q^(ell*j), its actual contraction is sum_ell A_ell(t) f_N(tQ^ell), with the original order of each spectator operator retained. Since |tQ^ell-1| <= (c_N+2pi D_N)/N, (9),(17) give subexponential norm whenever c_N+D_N=o(N) and sum_ell||A_ell(t)||=exp(o(N)) uniformly. Fixed degrees and fixed polynomial spectator costs give polynomial bounds. This is a statement about the specified exposed RECORDING slot. It is not automatically a uniform estimate for every physical input color of the open normalization tangle. Inserting physical raising or lowering operators can expose a different two-color packet and requires its literal source calculation. Likewise a general original crossing has degree N-1 in the adjacent observable; it is not a sublinear-frequency perturbation covered by this result. For a general exterior sequence A_j the exact Ward equation instead retains the forcing term (1-t)H_A(t)+t Q^(-1)H_A(Q^(-1)t) =A_0+sum_(j=1)^d conjugate(F_j)(A_j-A_(j-1))t^j, H_A(t)=sum_(j=0)^d conjugate(F_j) A_j t^j. (19) Equation (19) follows coefficientwise from the ORIGINAL recurrence. Dropping its finite differences would lose genuine spectator feedback. Controlling this forcing for complete interior crossings, with the geometric exponent, remains part of the broad goal. The present theorem proves source-specific cancellation at a nontrivial normalization germ, not a general hyperbolic knot-volume estimate. ## 6. Where the excessive full-circle energy actually resides The same exact Ward equation also bounds all root samples, so its nonlocal energy is not an unspecified error. Write H_k=H_N(Q^k), H_0=H_N(1), m=floor(N/6). Then H_1=Q^(-1), |H_k|<=N+2N s_(k-1), 1<=k<N. (20) For k<=m+1, forward propagation of (2) from H_1 uses only factors |1-Q^j|<=1 and proves |H_k|<=k. For k>=m+1, backward propagation from H_N=H_0 gives exactly the modulus bound |H_k|<=s_(k-1)[|H_0|/N+sum_(r=k)^d 1/s_r]. (21) After its minimum at m, the sine factorial rises to its unique maximum interval and then decreases to N. Hence min_(r>=k)s_r>=min(s_(k-1),N). Substituting (11) into (21) yields (20). All inverses here have indices strictly between zero and N; no zero root factor is divided out. For the actual normalization polynomial (16), reflection now gives |f_N(Q^r)| <=1+2N+4N^2/s_r, 1<=r<N, |f_N(1)|=1. (22) Indeed Hbar_N(Q^r)=conjugate(H_N(Q^(-r))), and s_(N-r-1)=N/s_r. Thus the full macroscopic clock cost has the uniform leading envelope log |f_N(Q^r)| <= N max{-J(r/N),0}+O(log N), J(u)=integral_0^u log(2sin(pi v))dv. (23) This uses the already proved uniform sine-factorial estimate; at a zero of f it is simply an upper bound. The function -J has its unique maximum c_*=v_3/(2pi) at u=1/6. Finite Plancherel for the ORIGINAL coefficients (15) is exact: sum_(r=0)^d |f_N(Q^r)|^2 =N sum_(j=0)^d |F_j|^2 =exp(2c_*N+O(log N)). (24) Consequently, for every fixed delta>0 small enough to give a proper neighborhood of 1/6, there is eta_delta>0 such that [sum_(|r/N-1/6|>=delta)|f_N(Q^r)|^2] /[sum_r |f_N(Q^r)|^2] <= N^C exp(-eta_delta N). (25) To prove it, use the strict gap of the continuous envelope in (23) off that neighborhood and (24). There are only N samples. No pointwise lower estimate for an individual root sample is needed. Thus the excessive ROOT-SAMPLED Fourier energy of this literal normalization source is concentrated away from t=1, near phase exp(pi*i/3). This discrete concentration statement alone does not prove a corresponding continuum-arc concentration statement. Equations (9),(18) control the original phase neighborhood and its normal germs by a separate uniform complex-disk argument, while (22)--(25) describe the sampled large-phase energy quantitatively. No analogous concentration or local bound is inferred for a general hyperbolic source. There is also a sharp reason to retain the frequency restriction in Section 5. Choose r_N maximizing |f_N(Q^r)|. Equations (23)--(25) and the average in (24) imply r_N/N ->1/6, log |f_N(Q^(r_N))|=N v_3/(2pi)+O(log N). (26) The inserted diagonal clock Q^(r_N j) is UNITARY in the recording space, yet produces this exponential scalar on the known packet. It is an additional observable, not the original closed knot value. Thus mere norm-one control of an arbitrary diagonal exterior cannot replace the sublinear-frequency or geometric conditions in the source estimate. The [independent audit](../experiments/audit_normalization_clock_disk_independent.py) checks exact finite recurrences, all backward phases, factorial reflection and the product/integral bounds at ten levels through N=192, as well as three noncommuting spectator-mode packets. Its 1,152 complex-disk samples supplement the all-disk proof; they are not a numerical supremum certificate. The original physical source identification is separately checked on every input column by the [cup-slide audit](../experiments/audit_actual_terminal_source_normalization_packet.py). Two independent analytic reviews verified the displayed constants, the k=0 case, the endpoint, and the growing-bandwidth limit. The expanded audit also checks nine complete root-sample profiles through N=192, including all exact sample bounds and Plancherel, while explicitly distinguishing discrete from continuum concentration.

title: The original factorial endpoint has a nonzero Gaussian leading term
text: # The original factorial endpoint has a nonzero Gaussian leading term 29 October 2026. The endpoint in the exact normalization/Green source has the following all-level asymptotic, with its phase fixed: \[ P_{N-1}:=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(Q;Q)_j =N^{3/2}\exp\!\left[i\pi\left(\frac14-\frac N{12} +\frac1{4N}\right)\right] +O(\sqrt N),\qquad Q=e^{2\pi i/N}. \tag{1} \] The implied constant is independent of every integer N>=2; no parity or residue class is omitted. In particular |P_(N-1)|>=N^(3/2)/2 for all sufficiently large N. This is a polynomial endpoint lower bound, not a positive hyperbolic-volume rate. Its use below is to keep a nonzero coefficient in an actual neighboring-crossing Green current. ## 1. A finite original-source formula Write d=N-1, q=e^(pi i/N), F_j=(Q;Q)_j. The original source identity already proved in the [terminal Green calculation](actual_terminal_green_capacity_bound.md) is P_d=-q Phi_N(r_N^3), with its full Cartan and pivotal factors. For k=0,...,d put \[ c_k=q^{2k+1}+q^{-2k-1},\quad A_k=q^{2k+1}-q^{-2k-1},\quad \nu_k=(-1)^kq^{k(k+1)}. \] The literal spectral-jet source gives the exact finite formula \[ P_d=\frac q2\sum_{k=0}^{d}\nu_k^3 \left[c_k-\frac32(d-2k)A_k\right]. \tag{2} \] To verify the fold, at every double node the original contribution is -nu_k^3[c_k-3(d-2k)A_k/2] to Phi_N(r_N^3). The index d-k has the SAME c and nu, and the opposite A and d-2k. Thus (2) counts each double contribution exactly once. When N is odd the remaining node has c=-2 and A=0; its half-sum contribution to Phi is precisely nu_k^3, the original simple-node term. N=2 is included. This uses the exact [spectral-jet source proof](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md#8-the-actual-closing-trace-is-a-spectral-jet-functional), not a chosen semisimple trace or a fitted endpoint value. Set s_k=(k+1/2)/N, and define fixed smooth functions on [0,1] \[ a(s)=(1-2s)\sin(2\pi s),\qquad b(s)=\cos(2\pi s),\qquad S_N(A)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}A(s_k)e^{i\pi N(3s_k^2+s_k)}. \] Since nu_k^3=-i exp[-3pi i/(4N)] exp[i pi N(3s_k^2+s_k)], (2) becomes EXACTLY \[ P_d=e^{i\pi/(4N)}\left[-\frac{3N}{2}S_N(a)-iS_N(b)\right]. \tag{3} \] In particular every phase needed in (1) is specified before taking a limit. The external original period line, if present, remains external; it is not used to change the finite endpoint (2). ## 2. An elementary half-grid quadratic-sum lemma For a fixed smooth A on [0,1] with A(0)=A(1), finite Fourier inversion of its periodization gives \[ S_N(A)=N\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}(-1)^m I_{m,N}(A),\qquad I_{m,N}(A)=\int_0^1 A(s) e^{i\pi N[3s^2+(1-2m)s]}\,ds. \tag{4} \] Indeed the periodized function A(s)exp[i pi N(3s^2+s)] is continuous at its endpoints, since exp(4pi iN)=1. Its piecewise smooth derivative has bounded variation, so its Fourier coefficients are absolutely summable: integrating twice, with the possible derivative jump retained, gives O_N((1+|n|)^-2). Summing its Fourier series at s_k keeps exactly the coefficients n=Nm, with factor exp(pi im)=(-1)^m. This proves (4), including the half-grid sign. The following estimates are uniform in m and N and justify its asymptotic use. Only m=1,2,3 have stationary points in (0,1), namely \[ s_m=(2m-1)/6,\qquad 3s^2+(1-2m)s=3(s-s_m)^2-(2m-1)^2/12. \tag{5} \] There is no omitted endpoint resonance: the endpoint derivatives are the odd integers 1-2m and 7-2m, never zero. The endpoint PHASES still matter, and agree exactly at every integer N as used below. If m is outside this set, the phase derivative has absolute minimum delta_m>=c(1+|m|)>0. Two integrations by parts give \[ |I_{m,N}(A)|\le \begin{cases} C_A/(N^2\delta_m^2),& A(0)=A(1)=0,\\ C_A/(N\delta_m^2),& A(0)=A(1). \end{cases} \tag{6} \] For clarity, the first boundary term in the second case is exactly A(0)/(i pi N) times [1/(7-2m)-1/(1-2m)]. Both endpoint phases are one, so this difference is O(delta_m^-2), rather than an unsummable O(|m|^-1). If A vanishes there, that term is zero; the next boundary and integral terms have the stronger N^-2 bound. All derivatives of A in (6) are fixed. Summing the nonstationary terms in (4) therefore costs O(1/N) in the first case and O(1) in the second. At each of the three stationary points choose a fixed smooth cutoff inside (0,1). Completing the square gives \[ I_{m,N}(A)=\frac{e^{i\pi/4}}{\sqrt{3N}} A(s_m)e^{-i\pi N(2m-1)^2/12} +\begin{cases}O(N^{-3/2}),& A(0)=A(1)=0,\\ O(N^{-1}),& A(0)=A(1). \end{cases} \tag{7} \] Here is an elementary error proof. For a compactly supported smooth amplitude B in the centered variable, Fourier inversion and the damped Gaussian integral give \[ \int B(u)e^{3\pi iNu^2}du =\frac{e^{i\pi/4}}{\sqrt{3N}} \int\widehat B(\xi)e^{-i\pi\xi^2/(3N)}d\xi. \] Subtracting B(0)=integral Bhat and using |exp(iv)-1|<=|v| bounds the error by C N^-3/2 integral xi^2|Bhat(xi)|dxi. This integral is finite. The identity follows first with Gaussian damping and then by its limit; compact support and rapid Fourier decay justify that passage. The portion outside the cutoff has no stationary point; the same integrations by parts as (6) give O(N^-2) for zero endpoints and O(N^-1) otherwise. This proves (7) without assuming a selected WKB branch or an asymptotic theorem for a knot invariant. Combining (4),(6),(7), when A has zero endpoints one obtains \[ S_N(A)=e^{i\pi/4}\sqrt{N/3} \sum_{m=1}^3(-1)^m A(s_m)e^{-i\pi N(2m-1)^2/12} +O(N^{-1/2}). \tag{8} \] For a smooth amplitude with matching nonzero endpoints the same formula has error O(1); in particular S_N(A)=O(sqrt N). ## 3. The two surviving Gaussian terms reinforce at every level For a(s) above, \[ a(1/6)=a(5/6)=\sqrt3/3,\qquad a(1/2)=0. \] The half-grid signs for m=1 and m=3 are BOTH minus. Their phases coincide at every integer N, since their quotient is exp(-2pi iN)=1. Thus (8) simplifies to \[ S_N(a)=-\frac23\sqrt N\, e^{i\pi/4-i\pi N/12}+O(N^{-1/2}). \tag{9} \] The function b has matching endpoints, so S_N(b)=O(sqrt N). Substitution in the exact source equation (3) proves (1). There is no parity cancellation between the two leading points, and the possible odd simple node was already retained in (2). ## 4. A quantitative consequence for the actual Green current The original first-order current obeys \[ P_t=F_t^2\left[\frac{P_d}{N^2} -\sum_{r=t+1}^d\frac{Q^r}{F_r^2}\right]. \tag{10} \] If t/N stays in a compact subinterval of (1/2,1), with t<=d, the tail in (10) is O(1/N^2) uniformly. To see this, reflect r=d-k: it is Q^-1/N^2 times a partial sum of Q^-k conjugate(F_k)^2. Here k runs only up to (1/2-delta)N. Its k=0 term is one, and the rest is uniformly bounded: up to a small fixed fraction of N the factorials decrease geometrically, while on a fixed interval below 1/2 they are exponentially small. Thus the partial absolute sum is O(1). This argument needs no cancellation in that reflected short tail. Together with (1), this proves on every such compact interval \[ P_t=\frac{F_t^2P_d}{N^2}\,[1+O(N^{-3/2})],\qquad |P_t|=N^{-1/2}|F_t|^2[1+O(1/N)]. \tag{11} \] The endpoint source in (1) therefore supplies a nonzero polynomial coefficient of the interior factorial current. It does NOT justify dropping that current or bounding it by its tame endpoint. This is the coefficient needed in an all-physical-input neighboring-crossing test; it does not assert that the full closed knot has a positive volume contribution from this sector. ### A sharp all-input normal current of one complete original crossing There is a direct local consequence, with an ordinary ORIGINAL pivotal closure and arbitrary outside spectators retained. Put g_b=theta Q^(-b), theta=x^(1-N), x=q^d, kappa=q^(d^2/2), and define \[ \mathcal M_\pm(t)=\operatorname{Tr}_2[(I\otimes g\,t^J)R_\pm], \qquad J|b\rangle=b|b\rangle . \] This partial trace has NO extra factor1/N. Literal integer-degree conservation makes it diagonal on the remaining physical head. Its complete original coefficients are \[ \mathcal M_+(t)=\kappa\theta\,\operatorname{diag}(D_a(t)),\qquad D_a(t)=F_a^2\sum_{b=0}^a\frac{Q^{b^2}t^b}{F_{a-b}F_b^2}, \tag{12} \] \[ \mathcal M_-(t)=\kappa^{-1}\theta^{-1} \operatorname{diag}\!\left(t^dD_{d-a}^{\overline Q}(t^{-1})\right). \tag{13} \] The superscript in (13) replaces every Q coefficient by Q^(-1). Both known scalar Markov factors have modulus one. For (12), a diagonal positive R coefficient has transfer a-b and value kappa x^(-2b)Q^(b^2)F_a^2/(F_(a-b)F_b^2). The original pivot cancels x^(-2b)=Q^b. The negative formula follows from its literal inverse coefficient by b->d-b and factorial reflection; theta^2Q=1 retains its displayed phase. Thus these are full crossing/source identities, not new favorable traces. They tensor with every spectator identity. The actual finite packets close under a second-order Ward recurrence: \[ D_0=1,\quad D_1=1-Q+Qt,\qquad D_a=(1+Q-2Q^a+Q^{2a-1}t)D_{a-1} -Q(1-Q^{a-1})^2D_{a-2}. \tag{14} \] One coefficient check proves this including all endpoints. For b<a, divide by the nonzero t^b coefficient in D_(a-1), and set u=Q^(a-b), v=Q^b. The required identity is \[ \frac{(1-uv)^2}{1-u} =1-2uv+u+\frac{u^2(1-v)^2}{1-u}. \] The top coefficient b=a is Q^(a^2) on both sides. Initial values therefore show D_a(1)=1 at EVERY physical a. At the other source endpoint, root reflection gives an exact whole-polynomial identity \[ D_d(t)=Qt^d H_N(Q/t),\qquad H_N(z)=\sum_jF_jz^j. \tag{15} \] Its apparent inverse powers cancel, so it is a polynomial. The Ward equation for H_N at one gives Q^2H_N'(Q)=P_d-1, whence \[ u_a:=D_a'(1),\qquad u_0=0,\quad u_d=N-P_d,\qquad u_a-u_{a-1}=Q^aP_{a-1}. \tag{16} \] To verify the last equality directly, differentiate (14); its successive difference obeys v_a=Q(1-Q^(a-1))^2v_(a-1)+Q^(2a-1), v_1=Q. The original Green recurrence identifies v_a=Q^aP_(a-1) exactly. The retained current in (16), rather than a dropped exterior forcing, is what a neighboring crossing generates. The original finite bound |P_j|<=N+4s_j^2 gives \[ \max_a|u_a|\le N^2+4\sum_js_j^2,\qquad |u_a|\le4N^3(1+s_a^2)\quad\hbox{for every }a. \tag{17} \] Here is a source-aware proof of the pointwise version. Let p=d-floor(N/6) be a factorial maximum index. If a-1<=p, sum (16) forward. The largest factorial on that prefix is at one of its endpoints, so |u_a|<=N^2+4N max(1,s_(a-1)^2). Use s_(a-1)<=N s_a/4. If a-1>p, sum (16) BACKWARD from the literal endpoint u_d=N-P_d; the remaining factorials decrease, giving |u_a|<=N+|P_d|+N^2+4Ns_a^2. The proved bound |P_d|<=N^2+floor(N/6) implies (17), with the generous constant displayed. The negative normal current has the corresponding bound with s_(d-a), by (13). No exponentially conditioned eigenframe is used. Conversely choose p/N->5/6 with p+1<=d. Equation (11) and (16) give \[ \max_a|u_a|\ge\tfrac12|u_{p+1}-u_p| =\tfrac12|P_p|\asymp N^{-1/2}s_p^2. \] The uniform factorial estimate in (17) now proves the SHARP all-input first-normal norm for BOTH original signs: \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \log\|\mathcal M_\pm'(1)\|_{\rm op} =\frac{v_3}{\pi}N+O(\log N).} \tag{18} \] At phase one the same complete operators are only the known scalar Markov units. Nevertheless Cauchy's derivative inequality implies that a uniform subexponential bound on a c/N COMPLEX disk, for every physical input, is impossible. More generally its supremum is at least exp[Nv_3/pi-o(N)] on every radius exp[-o(N)]. This does not contradict the [specific normalization-clock disk theorem](actual_normalization_clock_disk_bound.md): that theorem keeps one specified recording/source packet, not every physical input of an opened normalization tangle. It also does not contradict a bound with the explicit factorial energy (17), a coherent multi-crossing reduction, or a statement on the actual fixed marked source trajectory. No off-phase change of the chosen cut is made here. ## 5. Audit [The independent finite audit](../experiments/audit_actual_normalization_endpoint_gaussian.py) checks the original factorial sum against the complete spectral-jet formula, the full centered quadratic sum and all source phases. It also checks the nonzero leading normalization and the reflected Green tail on growing levels. These tests supplement the uniform proof in Sections2--3; no lower bound is inferred from a fitted numerical rate. Fresh replay: PASS nine literal full-R-cubed original pivotal sources N=2,...,10, including every open-cut column and the full Cartan scalar; 768 literal signed twisted-Markov polynomial coefficients at ALL physical inputs, their exact Ward recurrences and normal endpoints; thirteen exact quadratic-source/Green/current levels through N=768; and three finite-integral Poisson boundary checks. The latter use an exact finite Gaussian-erf formula with both endpoints, independently checked against direct integration before testing truncated Poisson sums. Another agent independently reread the complete analytic proof and found no gap in the parity, endpoint, Gaussian error or reflected-tail calculations.

title: An actual positive central-sector period for the primitive cube
text: # An actual positive central-sector period for the primitive cube 29 October 2026. For every odd level the all-Steinberg sector of the ORIGINAL ordered cube source is an explicit strictly positive Newton period, times its recorded edge-twist phase. The physical mark, all circle factors and all root normals are retained. The reduction is a generic pivotal contraction followed by a regular specialization; it does not replace the marked source by a Euclidean spin-network norm. This evaluates ONE specified joint channel of the cube. It does not identify the whole color sum with this sector, prove its dominance, handle even levels, or establish a full cube volume conjecture. ## 1. The original cube, its pointing and the statement Put N=2m+1>=3, d=2m, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, and s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2sin(pi u/N), s_0=1, beta(m,r)=s_m/[s_r s_(m-r)], S_N=sum_(r=0)^m beta(m,r)^4, A_N=q^[m(2-m)] S_N, omega_m=kappa(-1)^m q^[m(m+1)], kappa=q^(d^2/2). The exact A_N is the [original odd black source](actual_trivalent_steinberg_central_anchor.md). Use this actual ordered, noncrossing cube, with increasing port orders: black 0:(0,1,2), 1:(3,4,11), 2:(5,9,10), 3:(6,7,8), white 4:(0,10,11), 5:(1,8,9), 6:(2,3,7), 7:(4,5,6). The original unrestricted mark is on the EXPOSED outer cap of white vertex 4. A nested bare mark is not substituted for it. On every edge retain the actual complete-circle sector with j=m, and a fixed signed crossing exponent e_l. This sector is R^(e_l)L_St=omega_m^(e_l) N E_St. Let H_N=C[z]/P_N, P_N=2T_N(z/2)+2, be the complete physical pair commutant, including its double-node normals. Its full original functional and genuine turn are denoted phi and Rturn. Define E_St=the isolated c_m=-2 pair projector, h_N=Rturn(E_St). Then the original RAW marked central-sector cube contribution is Z_cube,St=N^12 S_N^8 phi(h_N^4) omega_m^(sum_(l=0)^11 e_l), (1) and phi(h_N^4)>0 (2) at every odd N>=3. External line/framing normalizations, if present in the original invariant, remain external to (1). No factor depending on an ordinary root quantum dimension is divided out after it has been specialized to zero. ## 2. The generic cups, cyclic clocks and the literal rung reduction All generic statements in this section use zeta before root specialization, with Q=zeta^2 and F_r=(Q;Q)_r. On highest weight L use the canonical cup with FIRST coefficient one: P_L(u)=(-1)^u zeta^[u(L-u-1)] F_u F_(L-u)/F_L, p_L(u,L-u)=P_L(u), ell_L=p_L^(-1). The actual physical highest-d cup is instead pV(u,d-u)=N zeta^(-d^2)P_d(u). (3) It specializes exactly to the recorded root physical cup. Both its factorials and its overall scalar are retained. In particular the genuine generic turn of a pair map A is (Rturn_zeta A)_((u,b);(v,e)) =pV(d-e)/pV(d-u) A_((d-u,v);(b,d-e)). (4) Its root simplification x^(u-e) is NOT continued generically. The global scalar in (3) cancels in (4), but its factorial ratios do not. Let W:V_d->V_d tensor V_d be the generic ordinary Clebsch map of spin (m,m;m), whose first highest entry is one. Put eta=D(W)W, where D is the genuine bilinear pivotal dual, with reversed abstract dual order. The finite unequal-Clebsch norm calculation in [the four-port kernel](actual_ordinary_four_port_recoupling_kernel.md), equations (4)--(6), gives eta_m=(-1)^m zeta^[-m(3m+1)] F_(3m+1)/(F_m F_(2m+1)). That calculation is the coefficient of a single contiguous product of reciprocal finite Pochhammers, not a fitted norm. Write a_m=(-1)^m zeta^[-m(m+3)], Theta=(W tensor I)p_d/a_m, e_m=W D(W)/eta_m, c_m=eta_m/a_m^2. (5) Thus Theta(2m,m,0)=1, exactly the canonical ordered invariant used in the first-normal source theorem. Equations (3)--(5) involve two uses of the same highest-d object: its ordinary canonical cup in Theta, and its scaled physical cup in the original source. These are not conflated. The scale cancels in the turn and every closed cup/cap snake, while the physical source factors are kept below. Moving the last magnetic leg to the front by the ACTUAL snakes gives (C Theta)(a,b,c)=K(a)Theta(b,c,a), K(a)=zeta^(d-2a), C Theta=Theta. (6) The clock follows directly from ell_d^T p_d=K^(-1), since d is even. For the scalar in (6), C^3 is K_total and hence is identity on integer H=0 invariants. The generic invariant line has dimension one. At a real positive generic zeta the scalar is real, so its cube being one forces it to be one. All entries are rational functions of zeta; therefore this is a rational identity. Dualizing gives the matching white rotation, with inverse clock. No plain permutation of the three magnetic legs is substituted for (6). Here is the explicit prism cut in the ordered cube: top cycle (0,4,1,6), edges (0,11,3,2), bottom cycle (5,2,7,3), edges (9,5,6,8), rung pairs (0,5),(4,2),(1,7),(6,3), rung edges 1,10,4,7, respectively. (7) Apply (6) only to put each indicated rung into the cup/evaluation slot. On a rung, substitute Theta=(W tensor I)p_d/a_m and its actual dual. The two intermediate cup/cap matrices cancel, and the surviving map on its four side legs is W D(W)/a_m^2=c_m e_m. (8) This is an all-side-legs-open identity: D(W)W=eta_m I is used only to identify the normalized projector e_m. For example the elementary sum in (8) is W_(ab,r)D(W)_(r,ce)/a_m^2; when a side leg is brought around a bend its p_d and ell_d are the same inverses in (6). The opposite cyclic move contributes K^(-1), so no residual independent clock is removed. This proves the rung replacement before doing the four-side contraction. After the four replacements, (7) is precisely the cyclic four-box pretzel closure with e_m in each box. Its two strand orientations are the ones supplied by the preceding snakes. Writing its edge indices as a_u,b_u (u modulo 4), the remaining contraction is sum_(a_0,b_0,...,a_3,b_3) K(a_0)K(b_0) product_(u=0)^3 (Rturn_zeta e_m)_((a_u,b_u);(a_(u+1),b_(u+1))). This is Tr[(K tensor K)(Rturn_zeta e_m)^4]. Equivalently its entry in terms of the unturned box is exactly the ratio pV(d-b_(u+1)) / pV(d-a_u) in (4); it is the generic physical ratio, not a root monomial. Denoting the unmarked ordinary cube spin network by Xi, the result is the generic rational identity Xi_cube=c_m^4 F_4(e_m), F_4(e_m)=Tr[(K tensor K)(Rturn_zeta e_m)^4]. (9) For an explicit index check of this last closure, let t_i be the four top edges in (7), and b_i its four bottom edges, indices modulo 4. The four rung contractions, in that order and after removing c_m, are exactly K(t_3)^(-1) e_((t_3,t_0);(b_3,b_0)), K(t_0) e_((b_1,b_0);(t_1,t_0)), K(t_1)^(-1) e_((t_1,t_2);(b_1,b_2)), K(b_2) e_((b_3,b_2);(t_3,t_2)). (9a) For the last row, the initial clock is K(b_3)^(-1)K(r)^(-1); the black vertex's H=0 condition makes it K(b_2). The other three rows follow directly from (6), putting the black rung in its third slot and the white rung in its first slot, then applying (8). The full pivotal self-duality of the channel projector reads e_((a,b);(c,e)) =P_d(d-b)P_d(d-a)/[P_d(d-e)P_d(d-c)] *e_((d-e,d-c);(d-b,d-a)). (9b) It follows by dualizing W D(W)/eta (or directly from the nested pair cup); it includes both reversed tensor order and both cup ratios. Apply (9b) to rows 2 and 4 of (9a). In the four turn factors of (9) make the bijective index substitution (a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3)=(d-t_3,t_0,d-t_1,t_2), (b'_0,b'_1,b'_2,b'_3)=(b_3,d-b_0,b_1,d-b_2). Their four e entries are now exactly those in (9a). Their scalar ratios agree by P_d(d-u)=K(u)^(-1)P_d(u) and the e entry's cleared weight equality K(t_3)K(t_0)=K(b_3)K(b_0). The remaining clocks are precisely K(a_0)K(b'_0), the pivotal trace in (9). This proves (9) by finite substitution, without a picture-dependent cyclic trace. The vertex orders, rungs and clocks in (6)--(9b) are the source certificate. An unlabeled cube or a product of closed theta values would not establish (9). ## 3. Regular specialization preserves the original physical mark At the odd root c_m=-2 is isolated from EVERY other pair node. Consequently the generic e_m has a regular spectral-projector lift, and specializes to the full E_St. This assertion includes its zero first normals on the OTHER double nodes; it is stronger than matching values at distinct nodes. Formula (4) is regular there as well. The generic ordinary trace of the four-box closure is [N]_zeta times its open scalar, because d is even. The original exposed physical mark extracts exactly the root of this scalar: m pV=1. Equivalently, with t=Log(zeta/q), nu_N=(d/dt)[N]_(q exp t)|_(t=0) =2N(-1)^N/(q-q^(-1)), F_4(e_m)'(0)/nu_N=phi(h_N^4). (10) This is the genuine marked closure of the [full pair source algebra](actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md). It is legitimate to choose the regular projector lift here: the root open scalar depends only on the root coupon. A change of lift alters the unmarked closure by [N] times a scalar vanishing at the root, and hence does not alter (10). It does NOT say that E_St is the original moving-q complete-circle germ. Since F_4(e_m)(q)=0, differentiating (9) retains no c_m' term. The finite ratio in (5) gives at the root c_m(q)=(-1)^m q^[-m^2+5m]=q^[-3m^2+4m]. (11) Indeed F_(3m+1)/(F_m F_(2m+1)) reduces, after removing its COMMON root zero, to product_(u=1)^m(1-Q^(N+u))/F_m=1. No vanishing F_N is canceled by a value-only substitution. In the full original source reduction at this central label, h0_m=N, gamma_m=q^(2-m^2)/N^2, s_mmm=N^3 A_N, G_(m,r)=1. There are twelve edge factors h0 gamma and eight source coefficients. The [exposed first-normal theorem](actual_nc_morse_graph_first_normal_source_reduction.md) and (9)--(11) therefore give Z_cube,St=(N gamma_m)^12 (N^3 A_N)^8 c_m(q)^4 phi(h_N^4) product_l omega_m^(e_l). Its magnitude prefactor is N^12 S_N^8. The entire residual phase is q^[24-32m^2+32m]=q^[-8N(2m-3)]=1. This proves (1), including its absolute normalization and original marked cut. ## 4. A full-root positive polynomial, with every nodal value explicit Use the real Casimir Newton basis of [the genuine turn theorem](actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md): c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1), Bhat_r(z)=product_(j<r)(c_j-z)/s_r^2, Rturn Bhat_r=Bhat_(d-r), phi(Bhat_i Bhat_j)=delta_(i+j,d). (12) The full isolated projector is E_St=Bhat_m^2. To see this without losing normals, its polynomial has degree d, a DOUBLE zero at every paired node, value one at -2, and product_(j<m)(c_j+2)=N=s_m^2. Thus it is the full Hermite projector. The proved positive multiplication formula followed by (12) yields h_N(z)=sum_(r=0)^m beta(m,r)^2 Bhat_r(z). (13) Its half degree and all its first normal coefficients are fixed by this genuine polynomial identity. For every distinct node j<=m, direct sine factorization gives Bhat_r(c_j)=0, r>j, Bhat_r(c_j)=s_(j+r)/[s_(j-r)s_r^2], r<=j. Consequently h_N(c_j)=sum_(r=0)^j s_(j+r)/[s_(j-r)s_r^2] beta(m,r)^2 =P_(N,j)>0. (14) This is EXACTLY the positive all-node factorial sum in [the actual one-leg source](actual_trivalent_one_channel_source_packet.md), with its own source phase kept there. Equation (14) identifies the polynomial values with that sum; the stronger full-normal statement is (13). In particular h_N(-2)=S_N and h_N(c_0)=1. For clarity the positive multiplication coefficients are, when i+j<N, mu_(i,j,k)=s_(i+j)s_k / [s_i s_j s_(k-i)s_(k-j)s_(i+j-k)]>0, max(i,j)<=k<=i+j; the product vanishes in the FULL algebra if i+j>=N. Write h_N^2= sum a_k Bhat_k. Then a_k=sum_(i,j<=m, max(i,j)<=k<=i+j) beta(m,i)^2 beta(m,j)^2 mu_(i,j,k)>0, phi(h_N^4)=sum_(k=0)^d a_k a_(d-k)>0. (15) The last strictness holds at EVERY k, since one can choose i+j=k with i,j<=m. This uses the original functional, so the first normals that define phi have not been discarded. No assertion that Rturn(h_N^2)=h_N^2 is needed. In fact the analogous square-turn identity is false generically with the full cups (3); the audit explicitly records this failed stronger premise. ## 5. What the positive period does and does not settle At N=3, h_N=(4-z)/3 and phi(h_N^4)=11. Formula (1) then gives 108^4 times 11 in the zero-twist central sector, agreeing with the independently derived exact spin-one cube source. The geometric target for the full retained-circle cube source is Vol(actual augmented cube)=16v8+2Vol(Q_cube), where Q_cube is the explicitly labeled ideal right-angled cuboctahedron of the [rectified-core geometric theorem](actual_nc_graph_rectified_core_geometry.md). The period in (15) is the remaining correlated-core contribution; it is not a product of four independent theta-block norms. The [positive cuboctahedral period theorem](actual_positive_newton_cuboctahedral_period.md) now proves lim_(N odd) pi log(phi(h_N^4))/N=Vol(Q_cube). Combining it with S_N=(1/4)N^(-3/2)exp(Nv8/pi)(1+O(1/N)) and (1) proves that THIS central sector has rate 16v8+2Vol(Q_cube), the actual cube-link volume. It does not control the other joint sectors, their interference or even levels. The accompanying profile calculation tests the more precise candidate phi(h_N^4) ~ C_4 N^(-9/2) exp(N J_4), J_4=(16/pi)[Lambda(3pi/8)+Lambda(pi/8)], C_4=4^(-3) sin(pi/4) cos(pi/4)^(-1/2)/2. These growing-level values are labeled as prefactor calibrations, not used as a proof of this asymptotic in the present note. The exact source reduction (1) and strict positivity (15) are unconditional. Audit: [original generic cups, full-root kernels and literal marked cubes](../experiments/audit_actual_odd_central_cube_reflection_packet.py), with [recorded results](../experiments/actual_odd_central_cube_reflection_packet_results.json). It checks six generic cyclic/rung families at zeta=2,3; six odd full physical root kernels including all polynomial normals; eight literal marked cube sources with signed edge powers; and five multiprecision positive-period prefactor calibrations. Finite checks supplement the pivotal and full-polynomial proofs above; they do not establish a whole-color or all-parity source limit. Independent internal review: the crossing-period agent read the full analytical proof, including the clocked rung table (9a), full generic cup/projector identity (9b), exposed physical trace quotient and complete root polynomial, and independently replayed the focused audit: PASS. This records a separate proof check, not external peer review or a whole-source cube equality theorem.

title: The exact complex color packet for arbitrary signed Conway coupons
status: Exact complex packet and selected shear
text: # The exact complex color packet for arbitrary signed Conway coupons 29 October 2026. For every retained C(FG), with F and G robust, and every fixed choice of pure or signed odd-half-twist coupons, the ORIGINAL mixed-color source has the finite analytic packet required by the general filling theorem. Its uniform complex asymptotic has power N^(3/2), a nonzero marked amplitude, and both level parities. The changed odd action is explicitly identified with a local shear of the pure action; it is not replaced by the pure colored action. The representation and primitive peripheral interpretation of that shear are a separate geometric statement. This note proves the exact source packet, its phase, Hessian, and whole-source error estimates. ## 1. An exact finite definition in original Newton coordinates Fix the actual expression and epsilon_l in {0,+1,-1} at each of its H individual circle leaves. The physical coupon is T(R^epsilon_l L_(N-h_l)), with t_l=h_l/N. Put D=N-1, M=floor(D/2), q=exp(pi i/N), kappa=q^(D^2/2), with the original half-Cartan mark. Let G_N be the canonical sine-factorial completion, G_N(r)=s_r, and put A_N(v,t)=N^2 s_(2v)/ [s_v^2 G_N(v-Nt)G_N(v+Nt)], 0<=v<=M. (1) For a retained high Newton index r define the EXACT finite functions d_N^0(r,t)=A_N(r,t), d_N^epsilon(r,t)=kappa^epsilon sum_(v=r)^M (-1)^v q^[epsilon v(r+1)] [v choose r]_q A_N(v,t), epsilon=+-1. (2) Here [v choose r]_q=s_v/(s_r s_(v-r)). These are the coefficients of the literal transported core, by the [full Newton half-twist identity](actual_odd_conway_newton_transport.md). For physical integers h<r, (2) is EXACTLY that coefficient in the full repeated-root algebra, including its normal directions. For complex t near zero it is its specified factorial continuation. All functions in (1)--(2) are holomorphic and even in t. Remove only the explicit common unit phase: ell_N^epsilon(r,t)=exp(-i epsilon pi D/4)d_N^epsilon(r,t), eta_N=exp[(i pi D/4)sum_l epsilon_l]. (3) The positive coupon is the Schwarz reflection of the negative one, including its original q and kappa phases. For complex parameters this means ell_N^+(r,t)=overline(ell_N^-(r,overline(t))); it does not mean conjugating a variable inside a holomorphic function. The [strict leaf interval](actual_conway_strict_leaf_quarter_bound.md) places all complete leaf coordinates strictly above 1/4. Choose a small fixed rectangular window B about the unique complete optimizer in the d=2H-3 free integer wire coordinates of the [pure finite-window construction](actual_conway_complex_window_laplace.md). All leaf indices in this window lie in one compact subinterval of (1/4,1/2); all retained product inequalities are strict. The last forced-flat product has exact coefficient one and is removed using its actual input relation i+j=D. Every other wire index has the exact form r_w=N L_w(y)+delta_w, with fixed integer offsets delta_w. The remaining lattice is primitive Z^d. Define C_N^epsilon(t)=sum_(k in Z^d, k/N in B) product_leaves ell_N^(epsilon_l)(r_l,t_l) product_retained_gates mu_N(r_left,r_right,r_out). (4) The mu_N are the ORIGINAL positive Newton multiplication coefficients, not their asymptotic equivalents. Thus (4) is a finite, explicit, separately-even holomorphic function. For all sufficiently large N, each state in its fixed window is an actual admissible core state for every physical small deficit. No support cutoff moves with t. ## 2. The selected local action and amplitude Use t=h/N throughout; the older mixed-source note uses pi t for its second variable. Put Y=exp(2pi i x), H_t=exp(2pi i t) and D_t=(1-Y/H_t)(1-Y H_t). The source-selected quadratic is mu^2-p_0 mu-q_0=0, p_0=-Y^-1[(H_t+H_t^-1)Y^2+2]/D_t, q_0=-Y^-2(1-Y^2)^2/D_t^2, mu(x,0)=-Y^-1. (5) On a fixed complex neighborhood of the high x interval and a small fixed t disk this root is nonzero, analytic and dominant in the actual high-to-low source transport. Define S(x,t)=integral_x^(1/2) Log mu(u,t)du, C(x,t)=sqrt(mu(x,t)) exp[integral_x^(1/2) nu(u,t)/mu(u,t)du]. (6) The logarithm and square root equal zero and one respectively at x=1/2. The correction nu is computed from the exact source recurrence: nu=[p_1+q_1/mu-q_0 mu_x/mu^2]/[1+q_0/mu^2]. (7) Here p_1,q_1 are the 1/N derivatives of the EXPLICIT rational recurrence coefficients in the [selected mixed-inner theorem](actual_pretzel_mixed_inner_source_wkb.md), with its color variable replaced by pi t. Its terminal source is U_M=1; C is therefore normalized by that finite source. In particular S(x,0)=i pi(1/2-x)^2, C(x,0)=sqrt(sin(pi x))exp[-3pi i(1/2-x)/2]. (8) Let g(x,t)=J(2x)-2J(x)-J(x-t)-J(x+t), f_0(x,t)=g(x,t), f_-(x,t)=g(x,t)+S(x,t)-S(x,0), f_+(x,t)=overline(f_-(overline(x),overline(t))). (9) The three functions all equal g(x,0) at t=0, but their color derivatives differ. Their local leading amplitudes are b_0(x,t)=sqrt(sin(2pi x))/ [2^(3/2)sin(pi x)sqrt(sin(pi(x-t))sin(pi(x+t)))], b_-(x,t)=b_0(x,t) exp[i pi(3/4-x)] C(x,t), b_+(x,t)=overline(b_-(overline(x),overline(t))). (10) All marks continue from the positive complete factorial branches. They are nonzero after shrinking the fixed domains. At completeness, b_epsilon(x,0)/b_0(x,0) =sqrt(sin(pi x))exp(-i epsilon pi x/2), epsilon=+-1. (11) These formulas include the source's quadratic color phase. Indeed the literal finite sum is A_(h,r)=D_(h,r)U_(h,r), and the canonical factorial marks give exactly q^(h^2)D_(h,r)/D_(0,r) =G_N(r)^2/[G_N(r-h)G_N(r+h)]. (12) The apparent q^(h^2) has thus combined with the factorial phases; it has not been discarded as an external unit factor. ## 3. Exponentially accurate joint interpolation of the finite grid This step is necessary before using a complex wire saddle. A merely O(1/N) coefficient approximation on the real grid would not suffice. The selected mixed-source theorem supplies a holomorphic E_N(x,t), on a fixed joint neighborhood, satisfying U_(Nt,r)=exp(E_N(r/N,t))[1+O(exp(-sigma N))], exp(E_N(x,t))=C(x,t)exp[N S(x,t)][1+O(N^-1)]. (13) Both estimates are uniform in the specified complex t disk. The first compares the ACTUAL finite source with its interpolation on the physical high-index grid. Its proof uses the exact endpoint zero in the continued fraction followed by optimally truncated analytic Euler--Maclaurin; no homogeneous solution is substituted. The remaining chirp must use a fixed analytic lattice mark. Take nu_N(z)=exp[-i pi z+i pi z(z+1)/N], P_N(x)=kappa^-1 exp(i pi D/4)/nu_N(Nx). At integer r, nu_N(r)=(-1)^r q^(r(r+1)) exactly. Moreover P_N(x)exp[N S(x,0)] =exp[i pi(3/4-x-1/(2N))]. (14) This fixes the continuous chirp before the lattice contour estimate. Replacing exp(-i pi r) by an arbitrary off-grid branch would move a whole lattice frequency and is not done here. For complex x define the exact pure interpolation A_N^hol(x,t)=N^2 G_N(2Nx)/ [G_N(Nx)^2G_N(N(x-t))G_N(N(x+t))]. (15) A joint analytic interpolant of the NEGATIVE normalized coefficient is I_N^-(x,t)=A_N^hol(x,t) P_N(x)exp(E_N(x,t)). (16) At the physical high grid it agrees with ell_N^- up to the relative exponential error in (13). Formula (12) proves that this is the same finite coefficient (2), including its phase. For the positive sign use its Schwarz reflection, and for the pure coupon use (15) itself. Equations (8),(13)--(16) and the canonical factorial expansion give I_N^epsilon(x,t)=N^(1/2)b_epsilon(x,t) exp[N f_epsilon(x,t)][1+O(N^-1)] (17) uniformly holomorphically on a smaller fixed joint neighborhood. The factor exp(-i pi/(2N)) in (14) belongs to the displayed error, not to an omitted constant or parity phase. ## 4. Exact identification of the changed action as a shear There is a useful equivalent expression for (9). For each epsilon in {0,+1,-1}, solve near s=0 the implicit equation t=s-epsilon g_s(x,s)/(2pi i). (18) Its derivative in s at completeness is 1-epsilon i cot(pi x), which is nonzero. Then EXACTLY f_epsilon(x,t)=g(x,s)-epsilon g_s(x,s)^2/(4pi i), partial_x f_epsilon=g_x(x,s), partial_t f_epsilon=g_s(x,s). (19) The last two identities follow by differentiating (18); what needs proof is that (19) is the action selected by the original source. For epsilon=-1 put E=exp(2pi i x), H=exp(2pi i t), T=exp(2pi i s). Exponentiating (18) gives H=T(E-T)/(ET-1), T^2+E(H-1)T-H=0, T=1 at H=1. (20) The pure ordered-port quantity K=exp(-g_x(x,s)) is -(1-E/T)(1-ET)/(1+E)^2. Eliminating T from (20) gives K^2(1+E)^2+K[(H+H^-1)E^2+2]+(1-E)^2=0. (21) On the other hand, differentiating the ACTUAL selected action (9) in x and using (5) gives exp(-partial_x f_-)=E mu D_t/(1+E)^2, which obeys precisely (21). At H=1 the polynomial factors as (K+1)[K(1+E)^2+(1-E)^2], and both constructions take the branch K=tan(pi x)^2. Their x derivatives therefore agree, with the logarithms fixed at t=0. Their difference could only depend on t. Both actions tend to zero as x tends to 1/2: S(1/2,t)=0 and J(1/2+t)=-J(1/2-t); the implicit shear has s=t and g_s=0 there. This fixes that remaining function to zero. Schwarz reflection proves the positive case, and epsilon=0 is immediate. Thus the half-twist source really implements this action change; matching its Hessian alone was not used to identify it. ## 5. The finite packet's uniform complex saddle Let y be the primitive free wire coordinates. With all exact turn relations retained in their affine limiting maps, put F_epsilon(y,t)=sum_l f_(epsilon_l)(x_l(y),t_l) +sum_retained_gates m(w_g(y)). At t=0 it is the pure complete action. Its wire Hessian is negative definite, so it has one holomorphic critical branch y_*(t) near the strict complete optimizer. Set Phi_epsilon(t)=F_epsilon(y_*(t),t). (22) To specify the amplitude without losing integer offsets, write r_w=N L_w(y)+delta_w. Use the leaf amplitudes (10), the usual positive gate amplitude b_mu(x,y,z)=2^(-3/2) sqrt[sin(pi(x+y))sin(pi z)/ (sin(pi x)sin(pi y)sin(pi(z-x))sin(pi(z-y)) sin(pi(x+y-z)))], and multiply their product by the EXACT leading offset factor exp[sum_l delta_l partial_x f_(epsilon_l) +sum_g grad m(w_g) dot delta_(w_g)]. (23) Call the resulting holomorphic nonzero function b_E(y,t). In (23) the changed f_epsilon is essential at nonzero colors; one must not reuse a pure colored offset factor. Define a_epsilon(t)=(2pi)^(d/2)b_E(y_*(t),t)/ sqrt(det[-F_(epsilon,yy)(y_*(t),t)]). (24) The determinant square root is positive at completeness. All factors are fixed by the original grid and its canonical factorial marks. Then, uniformly on a fixed smaller complex color polydisk, C_N^epsilon(t)=N^(3/2)a_epsilon(t) exp[N Phi_epsilon(t)][1+O(N^-1)]. (25) Proof with the finite errors retained. Replace the grid leaf factors in (4) by (16), (15), or their reflected versions, and use the canonical interpolation for each unchanged gate. The total grid error is bounded by poly(N)exp[N(F0+C||t||^2-sigma)], because (13) is relative at each original state and all local actions are even perturbations of the complete real action. Shrink the fixed color disk until this is exponentially below Re Phi_epsilon(t). This estimates the error BEFORE any oscillatory saddle cancellation. The interpolated summand has amplitude N^(3-H)b_E and phase F_epsilon, uniformly holomorphically on the same fixed wire tube. Apply the finite tensor-cotangent rectangle proof from the pure window theorem: vertical half-grid sides retain a boundary gap; each nonconstant horizontal kernel term loses exp(-2pi N eta), dominating the O(eta^2) complete phase increase and sufficiently small complex-color perturbation. The constant horizontal terms give N^d times the ordinary integral, including all orientations. Replacing half-grid endpoints by the fixed rectangle costs only exponentially small boundary strips. Translate that integral to its nearby complex critical point. The endpoint connectors retain their gap, its real tangent Gaussian is uniformly nondegenerate, and the odd first corrections integrate to zero. This gives relative O(N^-1), with power N^(3-H+d/2)=N^(3/2). Adding back the already bounded exponential grid residual proves (25) for the EXACT finite function (4). Neither parity changes the lattice density or any displayed phase. ## 6. Nonzero amplitude, color Hessian and the whole physical source The functions Phi_epsilon and a_epsilon are separately even. At zero, Phi_epsilon(0)=F0, a_epsilon(0)=a_pure(0) product_(epsilon_l!=0) sqrt(sin(pi x_(l,*)))exp(-i epsilon_l pi x_(l,*)/2), (26) which is nonzero. Since F_(y t_l)(y,0)=0 identically by evenness, the critical-point Schur correction vanishes. With c_l=cot(pi x_(l,*)), partial_(t_l)partial_(t_m) Phi_epsilon(0) =[-2pi c_l/(1-epsilon_l i c_l)] delta_lm =2pi i tau_l delta_lm, tau_l=i c_l/(1-epsilon_l i c_l), Im tau_l>0. (27) For epsilon=-1 this is tau=(1+exp(2pi i x))/2; for epsilon=+1 it is -(1+exp(-2pi i x))/2. The pure value is i cot(pi x). These are the packet parameters; the corresponding geometric cusp ratios are twice these numbers in the original full-twist convention. At the level of the exact local action (19), if U_old=-2pi i s and V=-2g_s, then U_new=-2pi i t=U_old-epsilon V/2. Identifying these as the primitive paths on a changed half-twist partner requires its literal geometric cut, not just this generating-function equation. The negative-definite real part of the diagonal Hessian and separate evenness give, after shrinking the fixed complex polydisk, |C_N^epsilon(u+iv)|<=poly(N) exp[N(F0-a||u||^2+B||v||^2)], a>0. (28) The bound concerns the finite packet itself by (25); imaginary quadratic cross terms are absorbed by completing squares. Finally the [whole mixed-source gap](actual_odd_conway_uniform_mixed_source_gap.md) controls all actual aliases. On real physical colors, the omitted core states outside B have a fixed gap from the common concave majorant and its unique complete maximizer. Therefore, uniformly for 0<=h_l<=delta N, |Z_N(h)-eta_N C_N^epsilon(h/N)| <=poly(N)exp[N(F0-gamma)], (29) for some fixed delta,gamma>0. The full physical color complement has its separately proved gap as well. Thus (25),(27)--(29) supply ALL quantum source hypotheses of the general long-filling transfer for the changed coupons, with mu=3/2 and eta_N exactly as in (3). The actual peripheral geometry remains its distinct hypothesis. ## 7. The same action transformation holds on the entire source branch Let Phi_0(s) be the optimized PURE colored action, with all its actual wire equations retained. Since f_(epsilon,x)=g_x in (19), the changed critical wire state is precisely the pure critical wire state at the corresponding local s parameters. The global action identity is consequently t_i=s_i-epsilon_i partial_i Phi_0(s)/(2pi i), Phi_epsilon(t)=Phi_0(s) -sum_i epsilon_i [partial_i Phi_0(s)]^2/(4pi i). (30) The first map has invertible diagonal derivative 1-epsilon_i i cot(pi x_(i,*)) at zero. It therefore fixes a unique small analytic branch. Differentiation gives partial_(t_i)Phi_epsilon=partial_(s_i)Phi_0 exactly; mixed source couplings are retained in this global map. At a full-twist filling saddle with charges +1, this implies the action identity S_epsilon,p = S_0,p_eff, p_eff,i=p_i-epsilon_i/2, (31) at their corresponding critical points. This is an equality of selected analytic ACTIONS, not a replacement of the actual filled manifold by a pure rational-slope filling. Multiplying the pure half-integral slope equation by two would also double its rotation charge, so primitive geometric completion does not follow that way. The original changed meridian and its physical filling equation must still be used. Audit: [finite coefficients, action shear and color normalization](../experiments/audit_actual_odd_conway_complex_color_packet.py). The [recorded results](../experiments/actual_odd_conway_complex_color_packet_results.json) pass 18 exact finite transported-source comparisons, 12 continuous chirp/parity checks, the symbolic selected-port, implicit-derivative, Hessian and effective-slope identities, and eight complex amplitude calibrations across both parities. These computations check finite normalizations; the uniform estimates and their error bounds are proved above. Independent analytical review checked the finite source phases, continuous chirp, both endpoint parities, all integer offsets, the N^(3/2) power, and the conversion of the relative interpolation residual into an absolute bound before the complex saddle. A fresh replay of the audit passed all 18 finite-source, 12 chirp and eight complex-amplitude checks. The primary-agent review independently confirmed the original coefficient phase and the exact cancellation of q^(h^2) against the shifted factorial phases. Primary-agent analytical review and fresh audit replay: PASS. The review independently derived the cancellation of the quadratic color phase, the continuous lattice chirp, the selected action shear and endpoint constant, the exact finite-packet comparison before oscillatory cancellation, integer offsets, nonzero amplitude and the negative-definite real part of the color Hessian. No finite calibration is used to infer complex uniformity.

title: Signed half twists and long fillings of arbitrarily branching Conway factors
status: Full signed long-filled knot and link equality
text: # Signed half twists and long fillings of arbitrarily branching Conway factors 29 October 2026. The original marked quantum invariant has its full hyperbolic-volume limit for every fixed signed half-twist pattern on C(FG), where both children are robust, after independently sufficiently long fixed signed integral fillings of any auxiliary subset. Every such expression has a constructible pattern giving a KNOT when all auxiliary circles are filled. No fixed diagram width, branching depth, turn depth, level parity, or prime-level condition is imposed. This research proof assembles the independently checked full-source gap, finite complex packet, actual marked representation, and primitive geometric completion. It is not a theorem for arbitrary hyperbolic knots. The exact grammar and the excluded minimal case are below. ## 1. The class and theorem Start with the original retained crossing-circle leaf h and seed A=h^3. Let F and G be any fixed finite expressions generated by A, literal quarter-turns, and stacking. Use the actual cylindrical closure C(FG). At each individual leaf l choose epsilon_l in {0,+1,-1}, replacing h_j by the actual T(R^epsilon_l L_j). Keep all original auxiliary circles, marks, and normalization. This includes arbitrary finite branching, arbitrary turn depth, and independent half-twist signs. Let Y^epsilon be this augmented-link exterior. Choose any subset I of auxiliary circles and independently sufficiently large fixed signed integers p_i. Fill by the original disk-framed full twists R^(-2p_i). The resulting literal crossing power at a filled leaf is epsilon_i-2p_i. Unfilled auxiliary colors remain complete; p_i=0 is not used to represent an unfilled cusp. Then Y^epsilon(p) is the actual complete hyperbolic filled exterior and lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N) log|K_(E,N)^epsilon(p)| =Vol(Y^epsilon(p)). (1) Both level parities and composite levels are included. The diagram, half twists, filling subset, and slopes are fixed before N tends to infinity. The threshold may depend on the fixed diagram and signs; it does not require the slopes to have the same sign or comparable magnitudes. The invariant is the original marked one-cut scalar, with its explicit nonzero enhancement factor of subexponential modulus. For the reduced enhanced Kashaev invariant this outer factor has unit modulus. For the full one-cut modified normalization it has modulus 1/N, once rather than once per auxiliary circle. These facts follow from the [original normalization comparison](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) and the independently derived [Kashaev crossing comparison](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md). The minimal C(A) is excluded from this mixed-color filling statement. Its complete half-twist volume equality is a separate proved result. No equality for all alternating, arborescent, or hyperbolic knots is claimed simply from the name of this expression grammar. ## 2. The actual complete source and the whole-source gap The [full Newton transport theorem](actual_odd_conway_newton_transport.md) retains every repeated-root normal coordinate and the original Cartan phase. Its complete-source leading coefficient is nonzero for every fixed epsilon pattern. The complete critical point is the pure one; every complete leaf lies strictly above one quarter. The [supporting-plane theorem](actual_odd_conway_uniform_mixed_source_gap.md) proves a uniform gap for every alias subset and the entire physical color complement on C(FG). Its mechanism is uniform across this grammar: each proper-seed leaf lies between 1/4 and atan(sqrt(2))/pi, and the tangent to its complete action dominates the full alias profile by a fixed positive amount. Product tangents cancel by stationarity under the actual affine wire relations. No separate estimate is needed for each expression or for each number of aliases. The [half-partner geometry theorem](actual_conway_half_twist_partner_geometry.md) constructs the actual complete augmented complement by changed shaded face pairings. All pointwise edge words and complete horosphere links are checked. Its volume is 2pi times the same complete source action. The [finite complex-color packet](actual_odd_conway_complex_color_packet.md) is separately even and has a uniform complex asymptotic with power N^(3/2) and nonzero leading amplitude. The fixed finite grid, all D=N-1 offsets, and the exponentially small interpolation residual are retained. The [marked odd deformation](actual_odd_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md) constructs the actual near-complete link-group representation and the primitive peripheral coordinates of that SAME selected action. Together these results supply every hypothesis of the [general original-source filling theorem](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md). ## 3. The global peripheral shear Let Phi_0(t) be the already proved pure critical action, with all auxiliary colors allowed to vary near completeness. Write a_i(t)=partial_i Phi_0(t), U_i^0=-2pi i t_i, V_i^0=-2a_i(t), G_0(t)=2pi i Phi_0(t). (2) The exact changed-source/geometry correspondence is chi_i=t_i-epsilon_i a_i(t)/(2pi i), Phi_epsilon(chi)=Phi_0(t) -sum_i epsilon_i a_i(t)^2/(4pi i). (3) At zero, Phi_0''=-2pi diag(c_i), c_i=cot(pi x_(i,*))>0. The Jacobian of t->chi is diag(1-epsilon_i i c_i), hence invertible. Equation (3) defines a unique holomorphic branch t(chi) near zero. The local selected-source identity is proved in the complex packet by its exact Ward quadratic and the zero-action endpoint x=1/2. Its global extension is elementary. At fixed wire coordinate x the implicit local relation is chi=t-epsilon*g_t(x,t)/(2pi i), and f_epsilon(x,chi)=g(x,t)-epsilon*g_t(x,t)^2/(4pi i). Differentiation at fixed chi gives f_epsilon,x=g_x; differentiation at fixed x gives f_epsilon,chi=g_t. Thus the complete network wire equations are exactly the old pure equations at the hidden colors t. At their critical point g_t=partial_i Phi_0. This proves (3), including all interactions between distinct cusps and all turns and products. The same computation gives partial_i Phi_epsilon=a_i(t), U_i^epsilon=U_i^0-epsilon_i V_i^0/2=-2pi i chi_i, V_i^epsilon=V_i^0=-2 partial_i Phi_epsilon, G_epsilon=G_0-sum_i epsilon_i (V_i^0)^2/8, dG_epsilon=(1/2)sum_i V_i^epsilon dU_i^epsilon. (4) Its packet cusp ratios are tau_i^epsilon=i c_i/(1-epsilon_i i c_i), Im tau_i^epsilon=c_i/(1+epsilon_i^2 c_i^2)>0. (5) For epsilon=-1 this is (1+exp(2pi i x_(i,*)))/2; for epsilon=+1 it is -(1+exp(-2pi i x_(i,*)))/2. The geometric primitive cusp ratio is twice the packet ratio, as required by the original full-twist convention. Equations (3)--(5) are used together with the actual selected finite packet and the original odd-link primitive paths. Neither the algebraic shear alone nor a match of Hessians is used to infer the asymptotic. ## 4. Filling stationarity and an exact action simplification The general original-source filling theorem uses the unique small critical point chi_*(p) of S_epsilon,p(chi)=Phi_epsilon(chi) +(pi i/2)sum_(i in I)(chi_i-1)^2/p_i. (6) In the original normalization it proves the stronger asymptotic K_(E,N)^epsilon(p)=Xi_N eta_N kappa^(-sum_(i in I)p_i) N^(3/2) D_(E,epsilon)(p) exp[N S_epsilon,p(chi_*)] *[1+O_p(N^-1)], eta_N=exp[(i pi (N-1)/4)sum_l epsilon_l], D_(E,epsilon)(p)!=0. (6a) Here Xi_N is the already recorded enhancement/framing factor, not another copy of a factor inside the raw source. The nonzero D is the explicit Gaussian-and-sinh prefactor of the general transfer. Its minimal signed charge sectors add. Every original color, alias, normal term, endpoint current, and nonminimal charge is controlled before taking this limit. In particular (6a) is a full-sequence statement and is not obtained by taking the modulus term by term. Its saddle equation gives the primitive filling condition U_i^epsilon+p_i V_i^epsilon=-2pi i. (7) The regulator anchor is the actual complete volume, and the marked volume identity is Vol(rho_chi)=Im G_epsilon(chi) -(1/2)sum_i Re U_i^epsilon Im V_i^epsilon. At (7) this equals 2pi Re S_epsilon,p(chi_*). The [general geometric completion proof](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md) applies to the actual nearby bounded framed representation, with all unfilled cusps parabolic and the primitive small logs in (7). It constructs the smooth complete hyperbolic metric on the intended filled topology. Combining its volume with (6a) proves (1). There is also a useful exact simplification. At the saddle put P_i=p_i-epsilon_i/2 and substitute (3). Then a_i(t)+(pi i/P_i)(t_i-1)=0, S_epsilon,p(chi_*)=Phi_0(t_*) +(pi i/2)sum_(i in I)(t_i-1)^2/P_i. (8) For an unfilled cusp, chi_i=0 implies t_i=0 on the local branch: separate evenness factors a_i=t_i Q_i(t), and its coefficient remains nonzero near completeness. Thus it contributes no extra term in (8). Equation (8) is an identity of selected actions, not an assertion that the odd link is the pure link with a rational filling. At an odd leaf multiplying U_i^0+(p_i-epsilon_i/2)V_i^0=-2pi i by two produces the primitive pure-cusp slope (2,2p_i-epsilon_i) with total logarithmic angle -4pi i. Ordinary smooth pure-link Dehn filling therefore cannot replace the marked odd-link completion in (7). ## 5. The constructive knot subfamily The [literal connectivity theorem](actual_conway_half_twist_partner_geometry.md#5-literal-main-connectivity) gives a linear-time parity assignment for EVERY robust expression. The allowed endpoint matchings are I,U,X; a seed realizes U or X without internal circles, a turn swaps I and U, and stacking has only one circle-creating pair, U times U. Every subtree retains at least two feasible matching types, so the root can be chosen U or X. Its cylindrical closure has one main component. Either sign can be used at every odd leaf. Full-twist fillings preserve the resulting endpoint permutation. Filling all auxiliary circles therefore gives knots for arbitrary fixed branching and turn depth. Equation (1) applies to this entire constructible knot subfamily. No fixed diagram width or turn depth is imposed; a statement about the knots' intrinsic minimal bridge numbers is not needed here. ## 6. A-structure scope The relevant marked branch is algebraic. With E=exp(2pi i x), T=exp(2pi i t), H=exp(2pi i chi), and Q=(E-T)/(ET-1), the local equations following from (3)--(4) are H=T Q^(-epsilon), M=H^(-1), L=Q^(-2), kappa=-(1-E/T)(1-ET)/(1+E)^2. (9) Together with the actual product and turn equations these describe the selected auxiliary peripheral branch. All multipliers here are projective similarity multipliers (squared SL eigenvalues), with the original centered logarithms retained. The pole divisors are excluded and the complete oriented branch is specified. The calibrated primitive G_epsilon and the source-selected nonzero period carry information beyond the elimination ideal. No whole classical knot A-polynomial, generic-main-meridian quantum operator, or automatic dominant-period selection is inferred from elimination. Those general extensions remain part of the larger active objective. The half-integral notation has a simple algebraic explanation. Over the peripheral torus with coordinates M,L, retain ell with ell^2=L. This finite etale double cover is a mu_2 torsor in characteristic zero. On it the change is the INTEGRAL monomial map (M^0,ell) -> (M^0 ell^(-epsilon),ell). (10) The source branch supplies ell=Q^(-1)=exp(V/2), continued from ell=1. Thus the internal algebraic data trivialize the pulled-back torsor locally. With several cusps the cover has group (mu_2)^b. Forgetting this marked square root loses the information needed to distinguish the physical odd meridians. It does not justify a half-integral change of primitive basis on the same cusp torus. On the logarithmic cover, the primitive changes by G_epsilon=G_0-sum epsilon_i V_i^2/8, as in (4). This is an explicit algebraic correspondence together with its calibrated action change. Neither the elementary torsor nor its trivialization alone proves the asymptotic: selection and survival of the period are supplied by the finite-source packet and the whole-color bound. ## 7. Verification and limits The new source gap and selected complex packet, complete and deformed geometry, and this assembly received independent internal analytical reviews. The general transfer and explicit geometric completion were also rechecked at the application-specific interfaces. The primary agent read the new proofs and replayed the full transport, geometry, complex-packet and six-leaf audits. These are internal research reviews, not external peer review. The [independent six-leaf certificate](../experiments/audit_actual_odd_conway_six_leaf_calibration.py) checks C(A A) beyond the old three-leaf examples. It proves the nine stationary gradient equations and positive Hessian exactly, retains the D=N-1 multiplier 4/3, and gives the pure leading amplitude 3^(5/4)/32768. Its 36 signed complete-source and 18 mixed-color finite-level comparisons are explicitly numerical diagnostics; they are not premises of the general convergence proof. [Literature coverage](positive_conway_literature_coverage.md) is kept separate from the own proofs. The result retains its literal grammar, long-slope quantifiers, and original invariant. The active general objective remains open beyond classes with these source and geometry certificates, including arbitrary knot diagrams and the full generic quantum A-operator formulation.

text: # Actual mixed peripheral geometry for arbitrary odd/pure Conway patterns 29 October 2026. Every fixed signed odd/pure coupon pattern on a retained robust Conway factor has an actual marked representation family realizing its selected mixed-source action. The odd shaded gluings satisfy their full pointwise edge words away from completeness. The physical auxiliary meridians and preferred disk longitudes obey U_i=-2pi i chi_i, V_i=-2 partial_i phi(chi). (1) The source phase changes by an explicit canonical shear. It is not the pure packet with the same color variables. In particular the complete half-twist marking is retained in every filling equation. This supplies the geometric input for the whole original-source long-filling transfer. Its analytic source hypotheses must be supplied by the separately proved odd-coupon gap and complex packet. The present proof works for arbitrary fixed turn depth, branching and coupon signs; it is not a cyclic or pretzel-only construction. ## 1. An exact change of the physical color coordinate Write the pure leaf action as g(x,t)=J(2x)-2J(x)-J(x-t)-J(x+t), J(a)=integral_0^a Log(2sin(pi u))du, v=g_t=Log[sin(pi(x-t))/sin(pi(x+t))]. (2) The continued marks are those of the complete positive chamber. For a coupon epsilon in {0,+1,-1} define the hidden pure parameter t=t_epsilon(x,chi) and transformed action by chi=t-epsilon*v/(2pi i), f_epsilon(x,chi)=g(x,t)-epsilon*v^2/(4pi i). (3) For epsilon=0 this is simply the original pure leaf. At t=0 the derivative of the first equation with respect to t is 1-epsilon*i cot(pi x), which is nonzero for 0<x<1/2. Thus (3) determines one holomorphic branch near every complete leaf. The function t is odd in chi; f_epsilon is even. Direct differentiation, including the implicit t dependence, gives EXACTLY df_epsilon=g_x dx+v dchi. (4) Thus the internal wire derivative remains g_x evaluated at the hidden parameter, while the derivative in the PHYSICAL color is v. ## 2. This is the action selected by the original odd source The exact finite mixed half-twist source has the selected analytic action, for epsilon=-1, f_src(x,chi)=g(x,chi)+S(x,pi chi)-S(x,0), S(x,a)=integral_x^(1/2) Log mu(s,a)ds, (5) where mu is the source-selected root of the explicit quadratic in [the mixed finite-source theorem](actual_pretzel_mixed_inner_source_wkb.md), with mu(x,0)=-exp(-2pi i x). This formula keeps the original q^(h^2) term: in the normalized physical coefficient its phase cancels exactly against the two shifted factorial phases, as in that theorem. No order-N phase has been dropped from (5). Put E=exp(2pi i x), H=exp(2pi i chi), K=exp(-partial_x f_src). With D=(1-E/H)(1-EH), the source quadratic and its selected root give K=E mu D/(1+E)^2, K^2(1+E)^2+K[(H+H^-1)E^2+2]+(1-E)^2=0. (6) At H=1 this polynomial factors as (K+1)[K(1+E)^2+(1-E)^2]. The SOURCE selects K=tan(pi x)^2, not K=-1. On the fixed high-index interval x>1/4 its selected eigenvalue is simple; the same regular branch continues for small complex chi. Now let T=exp(2pi i t) in (3). Since exp(v)=(E-T)/(ET-1), its epsilon=-1 equation is H=T(E-T)/(ET-1), T^2+E(H-1)T-H=0, (7) with T=1 at H=1. The pure ordered port value is K=(E-T)(1-ET)/[T(1+E)^2]. (8) Eliminating T between (7),(8) gives precisely (6). Its branch agrees at H=1, so (4) and the selected source have the same x derivative. This fixes the derivative, not yet the possible chi-dependent constant. That constant is fixed at x=1/2: both (5) and (3) tend to zero there, because S(1/2,a)=0, g(1/2,t)=0 and g_t(1/2,t)=0. Continue the common high branch to that endpoint. Therefore f_src=f_- EXACTLY on the selected neighborhood, with the original complete mark retained. The positive coupon is the Schwarz conjugate of the negative finite source. Conjugating (3), including i->-i, proves f_src,+ = f_+. In particular (3) is an identification with the selected finite source, not a newly proposed definition of its quantum phase. ## 3. Universal port data with either shaded pairing For arbitrary nearby complex E,R normalize a port to (0,infinity,1,R). Choose a leaf flag Z satisfying Z^2-(1+E)Z+ER=0. (9) In the first half use apex Z, and in the second half apex Z/E. For the hidden pure parameter this means Z=(1+E)/(1+T), R=T(1+E)^2/[E(1+T)^2]=1/(1+K). (10) Use the same four white/completion matrices as in the pure proof: W0=[[1,0],[0,E]], W1=[[1,E-1],[0,E]], W2=[[E-R,R(1-E)],[E-1,1-ER]], W3=[[R,0],[1-E,ER]]. (11) W0,W2 send Z to Z/E by (9). The pure shaded map is S=[[0,-ER],[1,-1-E]], pairing the two shaded triangles within one half. At an odd leaf use instead the ACTUAL cross-half pairings (Z,infinity,1) -> (Z/E,R,0), (Z,R,0) -> (Z/E,infinity,1), whose matrices are A=[[R,-R],[1,ER-1-E]], B=[[R/E-1-1/E,R],[-1,R]]. (12) The second is the inverse of the first with E replaced by E^-1 and R retained. Equation (9) checks both apex correspondences. These are the same local puncture and copy permutations proved by the literal half-disk rotation in [the complete half-partner proof](actual_conway_half_twist_partner_geometry.md). They are not a change of the original main-wire compiler. Crucially, the three odd edge relations hold for INDEPENDENT E,R: W0^-1 B W2^-1 A=identity, W2^-1 B W0^-1 A=identity, W1^-1 B W3^-1 A=identity. (13) These are rational 2-by-2 matrix identities. No complete relation R=(1+E)^2/(4E), unit-modulus condition, or equality of edge angles is needed. The reverse words are their inverses. Thus all odd side and CAP-base edge words remain pointwise trivial, including translations and dilations, throughout the mixed deformation. ## 4. Assemble actual representations for the whole grammar At each leaf use (3),(10), and retain the original multiplication action m and every actual turn/final closing relation. Let F(y,chi)=sum_leaves f_epsilon(x_i(y),chi_i) +sum_products m. At zero it is the pure complete action. Its wire Hessian is therefore negative definite there. The implicit-function theorem gives its one holomorphic critical branch y_*(chi), and phi(chi)=F(y_*(chi),chi). By (4), internal stationarity is exactly the old ordered port cross-ratio matching, with each pure g_x evaluated at its own hidden t_i. The nine prism transport identities, all turn identities and the final cylindrical identities from the pure marked-deformation proof are rational identities, so they continue unchanged. They supply a SINGLE Mobius map on every original white face, even if its deformed triangular pieces are not coplanar. For complex source parameters the construction uses holomorphic charts: the second prism's coordinates invert its angle phases, as in the rational transport identities. The normalized port value R remains the same in its two charts, and the leaf apex pair is specified directly by (9). No antiholomorphic operation on the physical parameters is being used. Three-point charts are regular near the complete anchor; stationarity matches their fourth points. Use the exact pure shaded words at pure leaves and (13) at odd leaves. The actual closed bowtie quotient, with the changed local half-disk pairings, supplies the labeled fundamental-group presentation. All its face-edge words are now identities. Thus the matrices give an ACTUAL representation of the original half-twist partner link group, in a bounded framed neighborhood of its complete holonomy. The small meridian around a main segment still crosses its two white sectors and is W_(j-1)^-1 Wj at that corner. Their derivatives at the common flag are equal, so this meridian is exactly parabolic; it stays nonidentity near completeness. Its peripheral commutant consists of translations.
