The audit passes 2,680 literal local meridian shifts, 1,268 open paths in 44 genuine signed-word/cut families, 20 generic/root scaled-Vandermonde matrices with 9,096 full port-source units, 60 root cyclic-packet isometries, 56 exact window branch carries, 812 optional source Ward rows, 588 independent alias-power cases, 42 periodic/antiperiodic principal filters and 72 checks of the proved unit-arc source metric estimates. Generic q and root q cases are kept separate.

title: Adaptive resonant sampling of the actual source and the raw-quotient obstruction
text: # Adaptive resonant sampling of the actual source and the raw-quotient obstruction 28 October 2026. There is a constructive EXACT adaptive Fermat sampling which puts the complete original finite source on the resonant divisor; Section 5 proves it entrywise for either crossing sign. This is a genuine base change before the original finite windows. It evades, rather than contradicts, the fixed-scalar raw-quotient obstruction proved first below. No arbitrary exterior coupon, renormalized invariant, or generic oscillatory countermodel is involved. Other original Newton/Rogers currents remain compulsory after this sampling. ## 1. The closure character is invisible to the complete finite crossing Keep the ports and complete signed Laurent kernels of [the actual trivalent crossing](actual_trivalent_layer_crossing_source.md). Inputs are z0,z1 and outputs are z6,z7. Put d=N-1. For fixed t0!=0, independent of the head variables, the character in [the exact resonant Fourier source](actual_crossing_shared_face_fourier_source.md#11-an-exact-resonant-fourier-source-including-its-closure-current) is A=(z7/z1)^N-(z7/t0)^N, D=1-A. (1) For the positive crossing it is exactly exp(N lambda)(1-exp(N z)), with the retained marks lambda=Logz7-Logz1+2pi*i and z=h+Logz1-Logt0. Equation (1) is a Laurent polynomial, so its monodromy notation does not introduce an additional choice here. Let K_sigma(t) be the COMPLETE raw signed kernel, including all finite Newton/Rogers factors and the original shared negative Gaussian when sigma=-. Let Pi_phys extract the ORIGINAL finite input/output block. Then, identically before taking the t constant term, Pi_phys[A K_sigma(t)]=0, Pi_phys[D K_sigma(t)]=Pi_phys[K_sigma(t)]. (2) This also holds after the exact finite root-orbit average, for every N, every original color, and either crossing sign. The proof is the actual finite output support. In the positive layer the last Newton factor is B_N(x^(-1)z7/z6,x^(-2)z7/t), and in the negative layer the last Rogers factor is R_N(g_- z7/t,x^(-1)z7/z6). Every monomial in either has second-output exponent e between 0 and d; none of the other factors contains z7. Both monomials of A contain z7^N. They therefore force second-output exponent at least N, which the ORIGINAL finite output window excludes. The first monomial also raises the required second input by N, but that additional exclusion is not needed. Gaussian integration changes coefficients and cannot change these exponents. The same proof works term by term on any fixed scalar root orbit. This proves (2) without assuming that the meromorphic homogeneous/current pieces separately have finite support. More generally Pi_phys[A^k K_sigma]=0 for every k>=1. If a polynomial f(A) is inserted directly on this complete local kernel, its finite physical projection is f(0) times that of the uninserted kernel. ## 2. This is an exact statement for the whole original knot source Apply (2) at any physical crossing of an actual signed word, retaining all original input/output barriers, pivots, markings, and framing. The physical local operator is unchanged if it is multiplied by D. Consequently its contraction with the original source is unchanged. This applies to nonzero hyperbolic-knot periods as well as to general words; for example the independently proved original figure-eight source is K_N(4_1)=sum_(n=0)^d |(Q;Q)_n|^2>0. (3) Thus there is no exact raw restriction of this original source to A=1 which retains the COMPLETE inserted crossing and its D-inserted source pairing: restriction would send D K_sigma to zero, whereas its original pairing is the nonzero quantity (3). This does NOT authorize the opposite algebra quotient A=0. Equation (2) is a statement about a specified finite projection of a specified complete kernel. The finite projection is not multiplicative on the Laurent algebra: A has a factor z7^N, while multiplication first by z7^(-N) can return those exponents to the physical output window. An arbitrary later operator/coupon need not retain (2). Accordingly the precise assertion is the actual insertion-functional identity (2), not an algebraic support statement for the whole coupon algebra. Nor can (2) be applied separately to the meromorphic S/I sectors. Those sectors are not finite Laurent kernels; their continued high Fourier modes are exactly what restore the original finite source in their sum. ## 3. What the orbit and deck equations do determine The root-orbit map proves equality of the COMPLETE original sourced functional with its finite-orbit version. The only unwanted orbit alias has positive integer degree N, and the original closure kills every nonempty alias selection. Invariance under changing the fixed scalar t0 is therefore exact. These are consequences of the original finite degree/source data; they are not new constraints forcing A=1. Likewise the local exact formula T_N=H_N F_ref+Psi_+(z)(1-A) I_- has a completely normalized, nonzero reference coefficient H_N on the regular part of A=1. Its compulsory current restores the source away from that divisor. Equation (2) shows why one cannot obtain the original global geometric coefficient by setting that current to zero through a raw multiplicative restriction of the complete source. Beyond the adaptive map in Section 5, the wanted additional structure is a SOURCE map to an action-normalized geometric vanishing-cycle/formal block, including the finite window and its currents. One must calculate the image of the actual marked class there and show that its coefficient is nonzero with subexponential normalization. This would be a genuinely derived or microlocal source comparison; its local resonant residue cannot simply be substituted for the complete finite pointing. ## 4. Exactly what compact divisor rigidity would and would not prove If two meromorphic sections of the same line on a connected compact normal variety have the SAME complete divisor, their ratio is a nowhere zero global holomorphic function, hence constant. One exact nonzero value fixes that constant. This is a valid rigidity principle. Its present application is missing two pieces of actual data: a globally defined geometric component with its full divisor, and the map of the original source/cosource to that component. Known local homogeneous divisors and total deck invariance do not supply either piece. The complete section includes currents with different divisors and different continued homogeneous components. Even uniqueness of the COMPLETE exact section would not by itself compute its decomposition into action-normalized geometric periods. The obstruction (2) is stronger than an abstract caution: the original finite pointing already pairs nontrivially with the closure defect which raw resonant restriction would erase. Therefore a successful global compact-torsor rigidity argument must explicitly transport that pointing, rather than infer its balanced support from the fixed-scalar orbit map. The following adaptive construction does transport it to a balanced sampling of the COMPLETE finite kernel. ## 5. A constructive adaptive Fermat sampling evades the obstruction Define a head-dependent orbit radius by the algebraic equation t0^(-N)=c(z1,z7):=z1^(-N)-z7^(-N). (4) On c!=0 choose any of its N roots and sample the COMPLETE raw kernel on the orbit t=t0 Q^j. The finite sum is independent of that root choice. Since K_sigma(t) has t exponents in [-2d,d], its average is exactly CT_t K_sigma+c(z1,z7) C_sigma, C_sigma=[t^(-N)]K_sigma. (5) Now apply the ORIGINAL physical windows. Every monomial of C_sigma has incoming second exponent -b with b>=0 and outgoing second exponent e with 0<=e<=d. The first term z1^(-N)C_sigma in (5) requires incoming second index b+N>=N, and the second term z7^(-N)C_sigma has outgoing second exponent e-N<0. Both are excluded. Therefore, ENTRYWISE, Pi_phys [(1/N)sum_(j=0)^d K_sigma(t0 Q^j)] =Pi_phys CT_t K_sigma. (6) This is true at either sign and every original color, with the same continuous Gaussian retained for a negative crossing. It consequently preserves every original whole-word source, without needing a global degree argument to cancel residual local aliases. Its scalar and all finite barriers are unchanged. By (4), the actual character (1) is identically A=1 on this algebraic sampling. Thus the local resonant Fourier comparison has its exact reference coefficient H_N and no additional closure current. This closes a source-balancing step which a fixed scalar orbit did not close. The construction does not erase the OTHER original B/R current sectors created before that one-function comparison. An additional balanced external Fourier-frame completion can remove those local currents too. Its degree proof must be performed before the original whole source is applied; it is not a consequence of (6) alone. That construction is now proved in the [local balanced Fourier theorem](actual_balanced_fourier_crossing_kernel.md) and the [whole-word source theorem](regular_balanced_fermat_word_source.md). It uses independent regular local grids and retains the exact rational Fourier adapters. The remaining geometric source problem concerns that explicit sewn network, rather than an unidentified local normalizer. At c=0 an individual sampled radius tends to infinity. The COMPLETE finite average nevertheless has the explicit Laurent-polynomial extension (5), and its physical projection has the extension (6). Separated homogeneous/current expressions require their matched joint continuation there; one cannot infer separate finite limits from (5). There is no contradiction with (2): substituting (4) before projection changes the head dependence of the moment variables. It is not an A-linear restriction of the fixed-scalar inserted source. Algebraic base change and the physical projection do not commute. This is the precise mechanism by which the adaptive source map evades the no-go. ## 6. The remaining adaptive local norms form a two-generator boundary ideal There is a concrete algebraic target for that additional transport at complete color. Write a=z0^N, b=z1^N, c=z6^N, d=z7^N, s=x^N, s^2=1, T=t0^N=bd/(d-b). On the regular torus, the first Newton, final Newton, and middle Rogers norms in the ORIGINAL positive layer are, respectively, D_first=T[1/(s a)-1/d], D_B=d[1/b-1/(s c)], D_R=1-c/a-c/(s T) =-(s c/T)D_first-(c/(s d))D_B. (7) The last equality uses only 1/T=1/b-1/d and s^2=1. Thus the THREE norms generate exactly the two boundary-exchange relations d-s a and b-s c after localization at the displayed nonzero coordinates. They vanish jointly precisely when c=s b, d=s a. (8) Keep the source-selected decompositions B0=S0+D_first I0, R=T_R+D_R J, Bf=Sf+D_B If, with all logarithmic marks. Their complete scalar kernel obeys the exact aggregate identity B0 R Bf-S0 T_R Sf =D_first[I0 R Bf-(s c/T)S0 J Bf] +D_B[S0 T_R If-(c/(s d))S0 J Bf]. (9) It follows by expanding in the stated order and then substituting (7). This reduces the remaining local current transport to TWO specified boundary relations, rather than three unrelated local normalizers. It does not assert that the raw finite projection annihilates each meromorphic term of (9). Regular balanced external sampling can impose (8) before the finite projection, and must retain its Fourier changes of frame when the local blocks are sewn. [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_orbit_closure_source_obstruction.py) checks the full raw signed finite layers, the actual physical R matrices, nonzero discarded terms, finite-orbit aliases, and original pivotal whole-word source identities. The grading/output-support proof above is uniform in N.

title: Ordered small-circle insertions and the original marked face
text: # Ordered small-circle insertions and the original marked face 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed and frozen. This note extends the exact polynomial insertion to several untwisted ports in a specified literal Morse class. The operators act in reverse source order, including on all coefficients created by later ports. It also supplies a one-port adapter when the outgoing middle face is the original marked or exterior face. No mark is moved and no generic-q transpose identity is inferred. The general subset with several protected outgoing faces or disconnected smoothing remains outside the statement below. ## 1. Literal face births, not an arbitrary operator order Use the flat 2k-plat sweep and actual region labels of the [marked face coefficient theorem](actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.md). Number boxes in their original bottom-to-top order. At box i write (x_i,b_i,c_i,y_i) for the outside, input-middle, output-middle and final faces. Only its middle gap changes. The output region is created at this box and remains in that gap until its next box or the top cap. Only the top exterior gap identifications can identify such a new region with a region already present earlier: those identifications all give the exterior face u. Every bounded output face c_i is therefore a distinct face with a unique birth i. In particular c_i does not occur as ANY face of a box j<i. This includes outer faces, not only the two middle positions. A bounded middle face is distinct from the two outer faces at its incident box; the outer faces may coincide with one another. The other protected face v is the bounded face of the original marked cap. Choose a set S of ports such that epsilon_i=0 and c_i not in {u,v}, for every i in S. (1) The input b_i may equal u. All other physical turns, the mark and the retained half twists outside S are unchanged. No one-main-component assumption is made. The relations c_i=b_i, i in S, form a forest directed from an older face to a newer one. Each c_i has one birth and at most one such incoming edge. A directed cycle would contradict the strict birth order, and an undirected cycle would have a newest vertex with two incoming edges. Neither protected face is eliminated. In the flat plat one can also see this forest as consecutive deleted segments in the original gaps. Each even gap retains its last box, whose outgoing face is u; connectedness of the original plat requires a box in each internal even gap. Thus the identity-smoothed projection remains connected. The marked gap retains its last box if it has one, so the two original marked faces remain distinct. For clarity, this is a source-coordinate class with a proved order. It is not a claim that an arbitrary untyped graph or a differently routed collection of coupons has this triangular incidence. ## 2. The exact reverse-ordered polynomial Retain N,d,q,Q and the operators T_h(x,c,y) of the [one-port theorem](actual_small_circle_polynomial_face_insertion.md). They preserve polynomials and total degree; their coefficients retain the full source phase q^(pd), where p is output-minus-input first head. Each h_i is an actual integer in 1,...,N. Let P_rem be the product D_a D_a Ptilde_s over all ports outside S, in ALL original face variables before any identifications. Starting with this polynomial, process i in S in STRICTLY DECREASING original Morse order. At step i apply T_(h_i)(x_i,c_i,y_i) to the CURRENT polynomial, then substitute c_i=b_i everywhere. Apply the same region identification to the remaining notation. Call the result Q_S. This instruction acts on every factor created at preceding steps. For example an earlier output c_i may occur as an outer variable in a later port's operator. Its q-shifts must then act on that operator's coefficients as well. Commuting the operators or applying them only to the initial product is not the stated formula. Why this order is exact can be checked before any coefficient extraction. Keep the original finite physical paths at every small port. For the latest pending port i, its bounded output c_i occurs in no earlier pending port, by section 1. Thus summing its paths and eliminating c_i=Q^(-p_i)b_i acts ONLY on the current remaining source polynomial; the other pending port weights are independent of c_i. The true factor q^(p_i d) is unchanged because the eliminated face c_i has the ordinary exponent -d, whereas b_i is retained. The local path calculation is therefore exactly T_(h_i), followed by the merge. Repeating proves the algorithm. If later eliminated faces were merged into c_i, all their factors already occur in the current polynomial and are shifted along with it. This is precisely the cross-shift contribution required by the original paths. Let r=R-|S|, and let F_sm be the r faces other than u,v in the identity-smoothed diagram. Then Q_S is homogeneous of degree dr and the actual fixed-sector source is A_(N,a;h_S)=N^r product_(i not in S) [k_(a_i)beta_(a_i)^2 omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i] [product_(f in F_sm)L_f^d] Q_S(L)|_(L_u=L_v=0). (2) All physical endpoint factors remain those of the original Casimir. Each elimination reduces the primitive grid by exactly one variable; there are N^(r+1) final grid points and the unchanged single N^-1 marked factor. All exponents in Q_S are nonnegative integers, so its degree dr excludes every whole-N alias exactly as in the one-port proof. Neither positivity of Q_S nor independent periodicity of a local half-integer source factor is needed. ## 3. Uniform cost at an actual compatible smoothing radius Choose fixed positive values l on the final smoothed faces, including both marked faces. Give each old face the value of its merged class. For each i put C_i(l)=3+4(l_(x_i)+l_(y_i))/l_(c_i) +4l_(x_i)l_(y_i)/l_(c_i)^2. (3) These use the literal old incidences followed by the final region map. The weighted polynomial norm in the one-port theorem applies at every step; merging variables of equal weight cannot increase it. Therefore |[L^(d F_sm)]Q_S| <= product_(i in S) C_i(l)^(h_i-1) P_sm(l)/product_(f in F_sm) l_f^d, (4) where P_sm is the original positive polynomial obtained by identity smoothing all ports in S. This includes all dependence of later operator coefficients on earlier shifted faces. The original scalar factors in (2) are retained outside (4). A proved strict coefficient-rate gap at the SAME positive smoothed variables thus survives with only O(sum_i h_i) added logarithmic cost. This is subexponential for a fixed number of ports with h_i=O(sqrt N), and preserves a fixed strict gap for sufficiently small h_i<=delta N. An optimized or fixed-radius gap is a separate geometric/capacity input; none is asserted for every smoothing by this algebra. ## 4. A one-port adapter at the original mark or exterior There is a useful boundary extension that does not require moving the mark. The original root Casimir is TRANSPOSE-SYMMETRIC in the balanced physical basis. Indeed its true coefficients satisfy A_+(U,V)=A_-(Q U,Q^-1 V), (5) including the endpoint zeros, and its diagonal is unchanged. Hence L_h^T=L_h at the root. This is ordinary transpose, not Hermitian conjugation and not a statement about its genuine generic-q jet. For ONE port suppose its middle faces b,c are distinct, at least one is unmarked, and the identity smoothing is connected with u,v still distinct. Eliminate an unmarked middle face. If it is c, use the original T_h in c. If instead c is protected and b is unmarked, use (5), regard the outgoing pair as input for this local calculation, apply the SAME T_h(x,b,y) to P_rem, and then set b=c. The displacement is now S-R and the exact source phase is q^((S-R)d), because the eliminated variable b has exponent -d. All other variables and the actual original mark are retained. Formula (2) with |S|=1 and bound (4) follow without changing the marked functional. If the incoming b is protected and outgoing c unmarked, no transpose is required: the q^(pd) computation only uses that the ELIMINATED face c is unmarked. Its merged target is then zero rather than d, as required by the same original mark. The degree/alias argument again applies with the two protected faces retained. In a flat plat a middle gap has fixed parity. The exterior belongs to even gaps and the marked-cap face belongs to an odd gap, so they cannot be the two distinct middle faces of one box. A nondegenerate certified port has distinct middle faces. Thus every such single untwisted port whose smoothing stays connected admits this adapter, irrespective of which actual top cap was marked. This one-port transpose does NOT justify arbitrary compositions of forward and reverse eliminations. A reversed elimination can act on earlier pending port weights, unlike the ordered class in section 1. Several protected outgoing ports, disconnected smoothings, and retained R^epsilon at the small ports remain separate source problems. ## 5. Original-source verification and reviews The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_ordered_small_circle_face_insertions.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_ordered_small_circle_face_insertions_results.json), checks 81 original Morse charts, 1,143 bounded output births, 9,056 earlier-face exclusions, 243 deleted forests and connected literal smoothings, and 1,836 genuine cross-coefficient incidences. It compares 27 whole original multiport contractions and 122 original one-port mark/exterior adapters with the stated coefficients, retaining the other half twists, actual cups and unrestricted mark. The root transpose check uses 4,659 original coproduct entries. All 86 surviving modular targets are the asserted unique coefficients. An explicit original source gives a different answer when the reverse order is replaced by forward order. Coincident outer labels are also tested literally. Two independent full analytical reviews checked the source births, ordered summation including coefficient shifts, scalar/primitive-grid normalization, weighted norm and protected-face transpose adapter. The second reviewer freshly replayed the full audit with redirected output and reproduced every count. A third targeted source-geometric review independently checked the literal sweep, older-face forest, last-even-gap connectedness and retained marked-gap assertions in sections 1--2. None of these reviews extends the theorem to arbitrary mixed-direction subsets, disconnected smoothings or signed small ports. The note, audit and saved results are frozen.

title: Independent audit of the ordinary-color identification
text: # Independent audit of the ordinary-color identification 28 October 2026. This checks the two representation comparisons needed before applying the positive path trace in [the regular-period note](regularized_kashaev_period.md#2-a-positive-trace-bounds-all-the-ordinary-colors). Neither comparison assumes a published colored-Jones or ADO comparison proof. They are exact finite-matrix statements, including the Cartan scalar and zero framing. The positive path trace itself is a separate algebraic step. The conclusion is that, for a **one-component** zero-framed closure of a fixed b-strand braid and every 1 <= j < N, F_N^M(-q^j) = F_N^Y(Q^j) = C_j(q), C_j(q) = theta_j^(-w) tau(P rho(cable(word)) P)/[j], q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, theta_j=q^((j^2-1)/2). (1) The coordinate superscripts in (1) are essential. In `root_orbit_pointing.md`, the reduced family is a function of M=-q x=-q^(alpha+1); here it is denoted F_N^M(M). In `regularized_kashaev_period.md`, the symbol F_N denotes its even descent to Y=M^2; here that function is denoted F_N^Y(Y). Thus F_N^M(M)=F_N^Y(M^2), alpha=j-1 <=> x=q^(j-1), M=-q^j, Y=Q^j. In particular one must NOT insert -q^j into the Y-coordinate function. The complete point is M=1, Y=1. All these are reduced periods; the full modified-dimension factor can have poles at the ordinary orbit points and is not asserted polynomially bounded there. For an independent check that this descent is legitimate, use the actual stripped Laurent crossing formulas. Under x -> -x, a transfer of order h contributes (-1)^(u+v+h) for either crossing sign, where u,v are its inputs. Modulo two this is (-1)^(c-u), with c its first checked output: c=v+h for a positive crossing and c=v-h for a negative one. Conservation of the integer pair sum makes c-u the negative change of the sum of index times strand position. Its total is zero on every diagonal cut state. The remaining pivot/framing sign is (-1)^((N-1)(b-1-w))=1 for a knot. Hence the reduced Laurent family is even in x, equivalently in M. Since it is Laurent polynomial, it descends uniquely to a Laurent polynomial in Y=M^2. This proof uses the original reduced framing; the unreduced/full state has the separate sign line and pole factors described in the pointing notes. Here tau is the algebraic fundamental pivotal closure trace, P is the product of the actual Jones--Wenzl idempotents p_(j-1), and every crossing in rho is the full fundamental matrix, with its common Cartan scalar. The usual value of q^(1/2) is exp(pi*i/(2N)). The source is the original reduced cut; the modified-dimension line is not divided out in a new way. ## 1. The invariant quotient is genuinely the ordinary color At alpha=j-1 the original N-dimensional unrolled color V has H v_a=(j-1-2a)v_a, K v_a=q^(j-1-2a)v_a, E v_a=[a][j-a]v_(a-1), F v_a=v_(a+1). All missing vectors are zero. The subspace U=span(v_j,...,v_(N-1)) is invariant: its only possible downward escape is E v_j, whose coefficient is zero. H,K,F preserve it as well. The quotient V/U has basis v_0,...,v_(j-1), with exactly the ordinary j-dimensional highest-weight matrices. At j=1 this quotient is the trivial color. The actual uncheck R is R=q^(H tensor H/2) sum_(h=0)^(N-1) c_h E^h tensor F^h, c_h=q^(h(h-1)/2)(q-q^(-1))^h/[h]!. (2) Every summand preserves U on each input strand separately, as does the Cartan factor. The inverse has the same preservation property, either from its finite inverse formula or from invertibility of its induced diagonal blocks. Its induced quotient is the defining ordinary R: all terms h >= j vanish there. The checked R exchanges the two typed strands; it does not exchange the status of a strand with an unrelated one. The quotient maps consequently satisfy, for both crossing signs, (pi tensor pi) B_N = B_j (pi tensor pi). (3) The pivot and twist preserve U. There is no singular factorial in this calculation: h < N in (2), and h < j on the quotient. ## 2. Why quotienting only the open strand quotients the entire knot This is the essential one-component trace lemma. Choose a basis adapted to U and V/U on every physical strand. Along each underlying oriented strand segment, attach status 1 to a basis vector in U and status 0 to a quotient-basis vector. For every nonzero crossing coefficient, status can change from 0 to 1, but cannot change from 1 to 0. This is exactly preservation of U by each uncheck factor, with the strand types followed through the check permutation. The diagonal pivot preserves status, and a closing partial trace identifies the status at the two ends of each traced strand. To calculate the induced open cut on V/U, its two open ends both have status 0. If the closed braid is a knot, there is one underlying component, and it passes through those ends. Following that entire component from its open input to its open output, a status-1 segment could never return to the final status 0. Therefore **every** segment of every contributing state has status 0. The contributing summands are precisely those obtained by replacing every color by V/U and taking the same cut trace there. This proves the all-strands color comparison; Schur's lemma alone would not prove it. This argument is termwise and works for arbitrary positive/negative words and any number of strands. It does not require a splitting V=U direct-sum W into modules. The original reduced cut on V is scalar even at this reducible color: it commutes with K and F, K has N distinct eigenvalues, and every internal arrow of F has coefficient one. Thus its scalar is the same scalar found on the nonzero quotient. The component assumption cannot be omitted. For the identity two-strand braid, a separate closed N-color component has pivotal trace zero, whereas replacing it by the trivial quotient gives trace one. Our audit checks this failure as well as the knot identities. No analogous unqualified statement for links is used. ## 3. Pivotal, framing and half-root scalars Write m=j-1 and epsilon_j=(-1)^m. On the quotient, K^(1-N)=epsilon_j K, theta_ADO=epsilon_j theta_j, theta_j=q^(m(m+2)/2). (4) Indeed K^N=q^(Nm) I=epsilon_j I, since the other weight term is q^(-2Na)=1. Also theta_ADO/theta_j=q^(-Nm)=epsilon_j from the defining ADO twist q^((alpha^2+2(1-N)alpha)/2). For a cut of a b-strand knot with writhe w, the b-1 traced pivots and the framing correction therefore produce the total factor epsilon_j^(b-1-w)=1. (5) The braid permutation is a b-cycle, so w and b-1 have the same parity. This proves the first equality in (1) without an unspecified phase. The same bookkeeping can be performed in the stripped matrices used by the exact audits. The common positive Cartan scalar is q^(m^2/2), and its inverse occurs at a negative crossing. After removing it, the ordinary residual twist is theta_j/q^(m^2/2)=q^m=x. The ADO residual twist is x^(1-N)=epsilon_j x. Both conventions give (5). In particular no half-root factor is silently rounded to an integer q power. The proof covers even N and both parities of j. ## 4. The fundamental cable is the literal colored R This comparison is needed to use a positive fundamental path trace for the actual j-color; calling a cable a color is not a proof. Work first over rational functions of q^(1/2), and retain the coproducts Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E, Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F. Formula (2), now as a locally finite operator on highest-weight modules, has the directly verifiable identities (Delta tensor 1)R=R_13 R_23, (1 tensor Delta)R=R_13 R_12. (6) For detail, put Q=q^2 and h=r+s. The finite q-binomial expansion gives (Delta E)^h = sum_(r+s=h) {h choose r}_Q E_1^r E_2^s K_2^r, (Delta F)^h = sum_(r+s=h) {h choose r}_Q F_2^r K_2^(-s) F_3^s, c_h {h choose r}_Q = Q^(rs)c_r c_s. (7) For the first identity of (6), move the R_23 Cartan factor left through E_1^r F_3^r in R_13. It supplies K_2^r; moving it past E_2^s supplies Q^(rs). This is exactly the first expansion in (7). For the second identity, moving the R_12 Cartan factor through the R_13 nilpotent term supplies K_2^(-s), and ordering it with F_2^r again supplies Q^(rs). The second expansion in (7) follows. These coefficient identities prove (6), including the Cartan scalar; they do not assume a tensor-category comparison theorem. The q-binomial identities themselves follow by induction from AB=QBA. Let V_f be the fundamental two-dimensional module. In V_f^(tensor m) put J_m(v_r)=(Delta^(m-1)F)^r(v_0 tensor ... tensor v_0), 0 <= r <= m. (8) The coproduct relations give E J_m(v_r)=[r][m-r+1]J_m(v_(r-1)), F J_m(v_r)=J_m(v_(r+1)), K J_m(v_r)=q^(m-2r)J_m(v_r). The endpoint at r=m+1 is zero. There is a nonzero vector at every weight for m < N, so J_m is an injective intertwiner at the roots under consideration. Repeated use of (6), followed by naturality under this explicitly verified intertwiner, proves B_fused (J_m tensor J_m)=(J_m tensor J_m) B_j, (9) where B_fused is the ordinary m-by-m crossing cable with its m^2 fundamental crossings. The inverse identity follows by invertibility. Equivalently (9) follows by expanding the two sides with (7). The highest-highest entry on each side is q^(m^2/2), so no additional central scalar is available or required. On fundamental 01,10 the operator U=q I-q^(1/2)B_f has block [[q,-1],[-1,q^(-1)]] and is zero on 00,11. The kernel of all adjacent U_i in a fixed weight has dimension one: each adjacent exchange fixes the q-ratio between the two coefficients, and exchanges connect all binary words of that weight. It is the vector in (8). Thus the common kernel has dimension m+1 and is exactly im J_m. The Jones--Wenzl recursion used in the regular-period note has image this common kernel: its image is annihilated by the U_i, and it acts as identity on every common-kernel vector, by induction. Consequently its actual tensor image is precisely the j-color. All specializations in this paragraph are regular for m <= N-2. The recursion uses only [1],...,[m], which are nonzero, and the ordinary R uses only [h]!, h <= m. No projector on a color of zero quantum dimension is used in the bound. The constant-color j=1 case is the empty tensor power and is immediate. ## 5. The trace identification and bound The fundamental coproduct pivot is K^(tensor m), and (8) identifies its restriction with the ordinary pivot K_j. For any operator preserving the idempotent image, finite matrix trace on that image equals Tr(K^(tensor m) p_m A). Applying this to every block of (9) gives the second equality in (1). The framing scalar theta_j is exactly the one in (4). It also follows directly from the positive crossing's pivotal partial trace: its highest-input entry has just the zero-transfer, zero-closed-index summand q^(m^2/2)q^m=theta_j. The fundamental trace obeys tau_(l+1)(A tensor I)=(q+q^(-1))tau_l(A), tau_(l+1)((A tensor I)U_l)=tau_l(A). The second equation is the literal partial pivotal trace of the displayed 2-by-2 block of U. These recursions identify it with the path trace whose local positivity is audited separately. At the principal root q=exp(pi*i/N), that trace is positive, the fundamental braid is unitary, and p_m is an orthogonal projection there. Its trace is [j], and the b-fold projection has trace [j]^b. Therefore |F_N^M(-q^j)|=|F_N^Y(Q^j)|=|C_j(q)| <= [j]^(b-1) <= sin(pi/N)^(1-b) <= (N/2)^(b-1). (10) This applies to every j<N uniformly, with the original one-component source and framing. At j=N the quantum dimension vanishes, so the division in (1) and the positive-color argument do not apply. ## 6. Independent exact audit [The new audit](../experiments/audit_actual_ordinary_color_comparison.py) constructs the defining full colored R independently, builds the fundamental coproduct highest-weight embedding (8), constructs the literal crossing cable, and tests both signs of (9). It also assembles the tensor-basis Jones--Wenzl projector, checks its image, generator intertwining and quantum trace, and restores the full Cartan/twist factors. The quotient tests use a separate original N-dimensional matrix construction and compare all colors j<N through complete knot cuts, including four-strand words and non-highest open inputs. A separate closed-component failure is checked explicitly. Fresh result: **PASS**, seven quotient levels N=2,...,8, 228 whole-knot quotient-cut comparisons, and 22 literal signed-cable families through N=9, including boundary colors j=N-1 and both level parities. An additional 28 exact cut comparisons at generic x and -x, away from the integer-color orbit, independently check the even M descent used to pass to the Y-coordinate. No full-state pole is evaluated. [Saved results](../experiments/actual_ordinary_color_comparison_results.json). The checks supplement the all-level arguments above. The result is a verification of the ordinary-color polynomial bound's input, not a volume estimate for the Kashaev color or a claim of reflection positivity of its modified source.

title: An actual generic four-port Clebsch recoupling kernel
text: # An actual generic four-port Clebsch recoupling kernel 29 October 2026. This gives a finite factorial kernel for a typed four-port recoupling, with the ordered unequal-pair norm and pivotal cyclic turn derived directly. All intermediate channels are retained, including high root partners. The coefficients are bilinear ribbon coefficients, not a unitary or positive 6j matrix. No quoted recoupling formula is a premise. Single-sum completion: the independent source construction below is now evaluated by the [generic all-port single Racah theorem](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md), including its exact seven-factorial prefactor, half-integral-spin cyclic sign and retained root normals. The two-sum formula here is preserved as an independent actual-source proof and audit input; it is no longer the final unresolved summation gate. The construction supplies an exact local identity before root specialization. Its explicit pole bookkeeping retains the normal data needed in the original marked source. A positive or asymptotic estimate for the primitive cube remains a separate question. ## 1. Generic unequal Clebsch maps Write Q=zeta^2, F_r=(Q;Q)_r. The highest-weight L object has the actual balanced matrices K|u>=zeta^L Q^-u|u>, F|u>=(1-Q^(u+1))|u+1>, Ecal|u>=zeta^(-L-1)(1-Q^(L+1-u))|u-1>. Its canonical cup has first coefficient one: P_L(u)=(-1)^u zeta^[u(L-u-1)]F_u F_(L-u)/F_L, p_L(u,L-u)=P_L(u), ell_L=p_L^(-1). (1) Take physical highest weights A,B, target C=A+B-2m, with 0<=m<=min(A,B). The first-entry-one highest vector in V_A tensor V_B has entries at (s,m-s) h_s=(-1)^s zeta^[s(A-2B+2m-s-1)] F_(B-m+s)F_(A-s)/(F_(B-m)F_A), 0<=s<=m. (2) The direct highest equation gives h_(s+1)/h_s=-zeta^(A-2B)Q^(m-s-1) (1-Q^(B-m+s+1))/(1-Q^(A-s)). Let W_AB^C[r]=Delta(F)^r h/F_r, 0<=r<=C. Its full finite entry is W_AB^C[r](i,j)=F_i F_j sum_s h_s zeta^(-A t) Q^(st) /[F_s F_(m-s)F_t F_(r-t)], i+j=m+r, t=j-m+s. (3) All indices are required to be physical: 0<=s<=m, 0<=i<=A,0<=j<=B,0<=t<=j,0<=r-t<=i. Otherwise the term is zero. Formula(3) is the direct finite coproduct binomial, with F_r canceled BEFORE specialization. If A,B<N, every denominator in(2),(3) has index<N, even if C or r is >=N. Thus W itself has no root pole. The final F endpoint follows from the commutator and injectivity of E above the physical middle degree, exactly as for the previously proved equal-pair Clebsch map. This proves generic covariance without assuming a decomposition or a semisimple root replacement. ## 2. The ordered bilinear norm, by finite convolution The right dual of W_BA^C is a map on the ORIGINAL A,B order: D(W_BA)=p_C^T W_BA^T(ell_B^T tensor ell_A^T)P_AB, where P_AB changes the displayed A,B input to B,A. The actual norm is D(W_BA^C) W_AB^C=n_AB^C I, n_AB^C=(-1)^m zeta^[-AB+m(m-1)] F_(A+B-m+1)/(F_m F_(C+1)). (4) Using D(W_AB) without reversing the object labels is not a typed composition when A!=B. Equation(4) is a rational generic identity; its zeros and any canceled factors are retained. Here is an own finite derivation. The lowest F recurrence gives W_BA^C[C](B-m+s,A-s) =ell_BA zeta^[(B-A)s] h_AB(s), ell_BA=zeta^[-AB+3Bm-2m^2] F_(B-m)F_A/(F_(A-m)F_B). (5) At s=0 the coproduct entry reduces to sum_u(-1)^u Q^[u(u-1)/2] F_(B-u)/(F_u F_(m-u)F_(B-m-u))=Q^[m(B-m)]. This is the elementary finite second Chu identity, proved by finite binomial expansion in the earlier source calculations; all endpoint powers give exactly(5). The recurrences then prove the entire slice. Schur's K,F equations make the composition in(4) scalar. In its highest entry substitute(1),(2),(5). The only remaining convolution, with X=B-m,Y=A-m, is sum_s Q^[-(X+1)s] [X+s choose s]_Q[Y+m-s choose m-s]_Q =Q^[-(X+1)m][X+Y+m+1 choose m]_Q. (6) It is the coefficient of u^m in 1/[(uQ^(-X-1);Q)_(X+1)(u;Q)_(Y+1)], a single contiguous reciprocal product. Its elementary finite-product coefficient formula proves(6). The factorials cancel to those in(4); the sign is (-1)^m and the remaining zeta exponent is -AB+m(m-1). The equal case A=B=d is exactly the independently proved physical norm of the generic six-head tetrahedral source. The generic projectors are consequently Pi_AB^C=W_AB^C D(W_BA^C)/n_AB^C. (7) Different generic Casimir eigenvalues make them mutually orthogonal, and the dimension identity sum_C(C+1)=(A+1)(B+1) proves completeness. This generic identity is not a claim that the individual projectors are regular or orthogonal positive projections at the root. ## 3. Four-port columns and the actual cyclic turn Now use integer spin labels a,b,c,d, with external highest weights 2a,2b,2c,2d. Let e range over I_S=[|a-b|,a+b] intersect [|c-d|,c+d] in integer steps. Write W_ab^e for (2),(3) with highest weights 2a,2b,2e. Define the actual invariant column Psi_e^S=(W_ab^e tensor W_cd^e)p_(2e). (8) The first canonical cup has to be kept, including its possible root pole. It is not replaced by a Euclidean Bell vector. For the other pairing let f range over I_T=[|b-c|,b+c] intersect [|d-a|,d+a]. First form Psi_f in the order B,C,D,A. Bring its last A leg to the front by the GENUINE pivotal cyclic map: Psi_f^T(u,v,w,z)=K_a(u) [(W_bc^f tensor W_da^f)p_(2f)](v,w,z,u). K_a(u)=zeta^(2a-2u). (9) To prove the clock, moving a first highest-L leg to the end by the actual cap/cup has matrix ell_L^T p_L=(-1)^L K_L^(-1). The inverse move multiplies by (-1)^L K_L. Here L=2a is even, giving(9). It is an invariant-column identity; a plain cyclic permutation would give a different kernel. Let Psi_e^rev be (8) with external order d,c,b,a, and dualize it with those actual four cups and reverse the abstract dual order. The exact diagonal norm is D(Psi_e^rev) Psi_g^S=delta_(e,g) N_e, N_e=n_ab^e n_cd^e [2e+1]_zeta. (10) Indeed each ordered pair composition is(4), and the surviving cup and cap give their actual pivotal quantum dimension. No norm square or conjugation is used. All N_e are nonzero generic rational functions. ## 4. A finite all-entry recoupling kernel The complete kernel and all-entry source identity are R_(e,f)=D(Psi_e^rev) Psi_f^T/N_e, Psi_f^T=sum_(e in I_S) R_(e,f) Psi_e^S. (11) Equations(1)--(3),(8),(9) make every entry an explicit terminating factorial sum, with no quoted 6j formula. Weight conservation removes one external magnetic sum. More specifically, for external colors u,v,w,z with u+v+w+z=a+b+c+d, the S column has the single product Psi_e^S(u,v,w,z)=W_ab^e[r](u,v) P_(2e)(r) W_cd^e[2e-r](w,z), r=u+v-(a+b-e). (12) The T column has the analogous product from(9). The dual in(11) uses the reverse complementary external colors and division by their canonical cup coefficients. All those entries are given in(1)--(3). For completeness, the S columns span the generic four-port invariant space: resolve the first pair by(7). The remaining invariant couples that target to the second pair; its homogeneous highest recurrence allows exactly the matching target e, once. Thus the dimension is |I_S|=|I_T| and the diagonal pairing(10) proves(11). It follows that the local four-port invariant tensor can be replaced by(11) against ANY exterior row, including a source-dependent row. A planar source disk with incoming ports is first bent using its actual cups; the inverse bends are retained when using(11) in the original network. ## 5. Root partners and the necessary higher normals Suppose now 0<=a,b,c,d<=M=floor((N-1)/2). All W entries in(3) are holomorphic at q. The cup p_(2e) is regular for e<=M and has at most a simple pole for e>M. The exact norm factors give the following orders, without treating high partners as low ordinary simple modules. For a PAIRED low node 2e<N-1, including e=M at even N, put e*=N-1-e. Then ord_q n_ab^e =1 if e* is in [|a-b|,a+b], else0. The same holds for c,d. At the odd simple 2e=N-1, each n is a unit and [2e+1] has a simple zero. At e>M the zero in the numerator and denominator factorial of(4) cancels, so each n and [2e+1] are units. Thus the low N_e can have order TWO, the odd simple N_e has order one, and high N_e have order zero. These are actual source zeros. In particular each coefficient in(11), and each summand R_(e,f)Psi_e^S, has a pole of order at most THREE. For low e its dual column is regular and N_e has at most two zeros; the input f has at most one pole. For high e the dual and input have at most one pole each, N_e is a unit, and the extra output column supplies at most one more. The odd simple case is smaller. Therefore a local Laurent identity(11) can be checked through its first normal by retaining Taylor ORDER FOUR (five coefficients, degrees0 through4) after multiplication by the cube of a local root parameter. This is a pole-order bound, not a magnitude bound. The pair spectral projector also has at most one pole: only its partner eigenvalue can collide, and that eigenvalue gap has a simple zero away from the odd self-paired node. Summing complete colliding clusters, or retaining the Laurent terms in(11), is necessary BEFORE specialization. Dropping high channels, taking only nodal values, or bounding each singular term separately changes the normal source. The finite kernel does not yet make R unitary or sign-coherent at the principal root. Factorial coefficients and confluence frames can be exponentially large. A primitive cube reduction must retain its entire recoupling sum and original fixed normal, rather than infer positivity from a diagonal norm or real spectral values. ## 6. An explicit highest-chart kernel with just two terminating sums The four-port coefficient can also be evaluated without the full four-color magnetic pairing. Put H=a+b+c-d and use the highest chart w_i=Psi(i,H-i,0,2d), max(0,H-2b)<=i<=min(2a,H). (13) Bending the last leg by the actual canonical cup makes this the third-color-zero slice of a highest-weight-2d three-object vector. The original highest recurrence recovers all its other slices, then the ordinary F descendants recover the entire four-port column. Thus this chart is injective; it is not an arbitrary packet truncation. The MIDDLE-pair Casimir on a valid highest chart is the upper-bidiagonal operator B e_i=lambda_i e_i+b_i e_(i-1), lambda_i=zeta^(2d-2a+1)Q^i+zeta^(-2d+2a-1)Q^-i, b_i=-zeta^(2b+2c-2a-1)Q^(i-H) (1-Q^(2a+1-i))(1-Q^(H-i+1)). (14) To derive it, lift w into the third object using its actual highest recurrence. In the third-color-zero extraction of Omega_bc only third colors0 and1 can contribute. Their F_b E_b terms cancel, leaving -zeta^(2c)F_b E_a K_b plus the two Cartan terms, which is (14). If c=0 the absent color1 is not introduced; the same formula agrees on the valid kernel E_ab w=0. Thus (14) is always used on the actual highest-source subspace. For f in I_T put i0=a+f-d, and define the generic left eigenrow ell_f(i)=0 for i<i0, ell_f(i0)=1, ell_f(i)=product_(j=i0+1)^i[-b_j/(lambda_j-lambda_i0)]. (15) The row equation directly proves ell_f B=c_f ell_f. For the T_f column, (9) shows its chart is zero when i>i0. Its value at i0 is the following explicit NONZERO normalization: beta_f=zeta^(2a-2i0) h_bc^f(b+c-f) *(-1)^(d+a-f) *zeta^[-4da+4d(d+a-f)-(d+a-f)(d+a-f+1)]. (16) The last factor is the lowest physical endpoint of W_da^f; it follows by substituting s=m in(5). There is no unspecified eigenvector scale. For the S_e chart, put u_e=c+e-d. Its exact scalar is w_e(i)=chi_e W_ab^e[u_e](i,H-i), chi_e=(-1)^u_e zeta^[u_e(2e-u_e-1)-2c(d-c+e)] F_(u_e)F_(2d)/(F_(c+d-e)F_(2e)). (17) This is the unique s=0 coproduct contribution at the external colors (third=0,fourth=2d) in (12). Hence the INVERSE recoupling has the explicit finite formula Psi_e^S=sum_(f in I_T) L_(f,e)Psi_f^T, L_(f,e)=chi_e/beta_f *sum_(i=i0)^min(2a,H) ell_f(i) W_ab^e[u_e](i,H-i). (18) There is one displayed magnetic sum, and each W entry is the single finite factorial sum(3). All remaining factors are finite products. To prove (18), eigenrows with different generic c_f kill the other right channels; the support just noted gives ell_f(w_f)=beta_f. Injectivity of the highest chart then proves the ALL-ENTRY identity. Equivalently the matrices in(11),(18) are inverse. This is a concrete finite two-sum Racah kernel derived from the original operators, not a quoted hypergeometric recoupling coefficient. It also exposes cancellations hidden in the diagonal norm. At the principal root beta_f is a unit: all its factorial indices are external physical indices <N. Chi_e has at most one pole, precisely from F_(2e) on a high channel. In ell_f there can be at most one colliding denominator, from f*=N-1-f; its zero is simple, and it is absent for a high f or an odd self-paired node. Therefore each coefficient in (18) has pole order at most TWO. The cyclically interchanged formula gives the same bound for(11). Its product with an output column still has at most three poles, so the fixed-normal instruction in section5 is unchanged. No pole is discarded by evaluating an individual partner at the root. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_ordinary_four_port_recoupling_kernel.py) passes 44 exact unequal Clebsch/norm channels, 61 four-port external families and all185 recoupling entries, the separate highest-chart two-sum inverse at all61 families/185 entries, and eight full-partner/root families N=2,...,9. The latter construct high-channel W by(3) without dividing by the vanished F_N, check their actual E,F,K covariance, and compare the uncanceled norm-factor zero count with the exact partner condition. Both even central PAIRED and odd central SIMPLE nodes are included. These checks supplement the finite proofs, not a growing-color asymptotic or conditioning assertion.

title: The original marked boundary source and its transverse stationary point
status: Marked stationary force and absolute volume
text: # The original marked boundary source and its transverse stationary point 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. This concerns the specified original six-type boundary source, at fixed real integer channel labels approaching the fold. Its actual marked cap cancels the limiting linear magnetic force. This gives a nearby transverse stationary point and a constructed local period. It does not identify their coefficient in the original support cycle. An independent coning calculation below identifies its absolute leading real rate with Vol(Q)/pi, where Q is the actual right-angled half-polyhedron; it does not use a finite-r sheet assertion. The logarithmic source coordinates, exact scalar factors and original mark are part of the statement. No additional winding character is introduced in the marked-source conclusion. ## 1. The literal regular circle lift has no extra root character Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, 0<=a<=floor(d/2), m=d-a, s=d-2a, and F_j=(Q;Q)_j. Write S_j for the positive sine factorial and beta_a=S_(2a)/S_a^2. Retain the original constants h0_a=k_a N beta_a, gamma_a=q^(2-a^2)/N^2, P_s(T)=product_(j=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^j). All heads in this section use the specified moving-factorial continuation of the [regular original source](actual_original_network_resonant_source_envelope.md). Let sigma=i+j, r=sigma-m, x=2a-r=d+a-sigma, T=Q^sigma. At the root its ordinary channel cup is exactly p_(2a)(x)=F_s q^[2m(d+a)] T^(-a)/P_s(T). (1) This is a meromorphic identity, including its removable specializations. Indeed the fixed-root factorial reflection first gives p_(d-s)(x)=F_s exp(pi i x) q^[(s-1)x] /product_(j=1)^s(1-Q^(x+j)). At x=d+a-sigma its denominator is T^(-s)P_s(T), and exp(pi i x)q^[(s-1)x]=q^(2mx). This proves (1) with its literal logarithmic character. The actual generic reversal, specialized only after it is used, gives W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r)=q^[s(a-r)] W_a(i,j;r), pV(d-j)pV(d-i)=N^2 q^(-d sigma). Thus the literal categorical dual is retained in the product. For an output row R and input row S at the same total sigma, substitute W_a(R,sigma-R;r) =(-1)^m q^[d(R-sigma)+m(a+1)] H_m(Q^R,Q^(sigma-R))/F_m and the same formula for S. Use the exact root collision H_m=P_s(T)H_a and H_a=q^(a sigma)K_a R_a, where K_a=F_(2a)/F_a^2 and R_a has its actual monic normalization. The remaining head dependence of h0_a W_a pi_a is q^[d(R+S)-2m sigma] P_s(T) R_a(q^(sigma-2R);c_sigma)R_a(q^(sigma-2S);c_sigma). The entire coefficient C_a in the [absolute regulator normalization](actual_matching_edge_deficient_packet_regulator.md) has precisely this dependence, because its residual sine product obeys V_a(d-sigma)=q^(-sd-s sigma)P_s(T). The ratio of the two scalars, retaining gamma_a and h0_a, reduces by F_j=(-i)^j q^[j(j+1)/2]S_j and S_j S_(d-j)=N to q^[-2N(-2N+a+3)]=1. Consequently, as the SPECIFIED root continuations, h0_a W_a pi_a = C_a. (2) This uses both actual LARGE numerators and the actual dual cups. It does not differentiate a root collision, identify moving-q germs, or replace the separately recorded bare canceled/turned continuation by this one. The retained half twist is a fixed-channel scalar on both sides and changes no magnetic derivative. There is a useful exact homogeneous form, valid for EVERY folded label; the [positive face-polynomial theorem](actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.md) gives its independent local proof, both-parity carry convention, full coefficient positivity and the physical support-zero audit. Define D_a(x,b,y)=det[bI+(x/2)H_-+(y/2)H_+], Ptilde_s(x,y)=product_(j=a+1)^(d-a)(x-Q^j y). For positive formal face diagonals x=L0, y=L2 and the two middle diagonals b,c, use the marked raw clocks -x/b,-b/y and -x/c,-c/y. Then (2) is exactly h0_a W_a pi_a =k_a beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)Ptilde_s(x,y) /(bc)^(d/2). (2a) Indeed H_a=(-q^-1)^a K_a D_a/L2^a and P_s(Q^sigma)=q^(-2s)L2^(-s)Ptilde_s. Substitute these into the calculation above. Its remaining scalar phase is (-1)^d q^[d-sd-2s-2a]=(-1)^(d+s)=1. In this computation q^sigma=-q^-1 sqrt(x/y) and the two negative physical raw clocks have their canonical argument pi. The identity extends with those marked half powers; at odd N the powers are integral. This is not a replacement of an even-level marked square root by an unrecorded principal branch. The numerator in (2a) has degree 2a+s=d. ## 2. Source coordinates and the local angle-force input Fix the labeled certified diagram and the common boundary sample r_frame=N rho, s_frame=exp(-2pi i alpha)-1. The parameters range in the compact sets of the [common boundary chart](actual_original_network_resonant_boundary_chart.md). Keep the actual physical half-index shifts, auxiliary integer offsets, all original turns, the ordinary or marked exposed cap, and fixed labels with S=sum_i(d-2a_i)=o(N). Use LOGARITHMIC CLOCK potentials Z_f, not normalized head potentials. Their homogeneous physical variations are delta h_e=N(delta Z_left-delta Z_right)/(2pi i). (3) The [literal face-lattice theorem](actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.md) proves that the integer face differences give the original primitive homogeneous lattice. A common additive constant is immaterial. Exactly two faces have constant prefixes; write Qcal for the other, quadratic faces. The actual sample has Z_f=Log L_f with all source marks retained. For clarity the local analytic input needed here is stated explicitly. At an ordered white triangle with faces f0,f1,f2, let theta_j be the angle at the center of its j-th circle in the tangent-circle triangle. A constant-prefix line has limiting angle zero. At the common sample, the normalized logarithmic derivative of its literal W numerator and white monomial tends uniformly to sum_(j=0)^2 theta_j dZ_fj/(2pi) - dZ_f1/2. (4) The theta sum is pi. This statement is obtained from the actual finite cores, not from a finite-r identification of their sheets with the geometric critical branch. For 222, with alpha_*=a_f0/(2a_f1), beta_*=a_f2/(2a_f1), its derivatives are theta_0/(2pi)=atan(2alpha_*/sqrt(2alpha_*+2beta_*+4alpha_*beta_*))/pi, theta_2/(2pi)=atan(2beta_*/sqrt(2alpha_*+2beta_*+4alpha_*beta_*))/pi. The actual H Ward equations and positive finite determinant select these angles. The 220 and 022 formulas are their one-line limits. The 202 positive polynomial gives theta_0=2atan(sqrt(T_raw)) and theta_2=pi-theta_0. The 200 and 002 top terms give respectively (theta_0,theta_1,theta_2)=(pi,0,0) and (0,0,pi). All root partner products and near-fold cup corrections are retained; their normalized first-derivative errors tend to zero when S=o(N). Here are source proofs of the force limits, including the boundary cases. Put p=N^-1 partial_logU Log H and r=N^-1 partial_logV Log H. The exact two white Ward equations, the O(N) second-log-derivative bounds, and Q=exp(2pi i/N) give at the fold (1-U)t_U+U(1-V)t_V=1+UV, (1-U)/t_U+U(1-V)/t_V=1+UV, t_U=exp(2pi i p), t_V=exp(2pi i r). (4a) The errors before taking the limit are O((s+1)/N) on a 222 compact. Its positive matrix gives p,r in a compact subset of (0,1/2): each relevant positive trace has a bulk lower bound, as does its complement. For U=-u,V=-v the unique upper-semicircle solution is p=atan(u sqrt(v)/sqrt(1+u+uv))/pi, r=atan(sqrt(v(1+u+uv)))/pi. Its triangle discriminant is positive and separated from zero on the specified compacts. Thus it gives uniform derivative convergence, not just an identity satisfied by a putative geometric saddle. The elementary circle cosine law makes these exactly the angles in (4). For 220 the determinant-rate theorem extends to its zero second coefficient uniformly using H_+<=2H_-+8I. Its fixed holomorphic logarithmic bounds give derivative convergence. At the fold the derivative integral is integral_0^(1/2) [1-cos(pi t)/sqrt(cos^2(pi t)+u)]dt =atan(sqrt(u))/pi. The last equality follows by y=sin(pi t). The other H force tends to 1/2. Exact reciprocity gives 022. For 202 the positive coefficient ratios give the mode equation tan(pi kappa)=sqrt(T_raw)sin(pi a/N) /[1+sqrt(T_raw)cos(pi a/N)]. The already proved Gaussian weight bound and variance O(N) imply mean/N-kappa=O(N^-1/2), uniformly. This tends to the stated atan formula. Finally the exact top terms of 200/002 have H forces (m/N,m/N)+O(N^-1) and (0,0)+O(N^-1), respectively. Their nonzero Bessel remainders have bounded logarithmic derivatives. Multiplication by the original white monomial subtracts d/(2N) from the second H force. The large partner and root cup corrections cost O((s+1)/N) in normalized first derivatives, using the actual separated factors. These arguments prove (4), locally uniformly with its marked phases. No uniform quantitative rate beyond o(1) is needed below. ## 3. The integer covector is computed from the original turns At a literal physical cup or cap write its first-head variable as its actual signed face difference plus the affine offset. The exact root cup pV(x)=N q^(-d^2)q^(dx), and its ordered inverse cap, contribute in the normalized limit one half of a SIGNED face difference. Let epsilon_(b,f) be that signed incidence for the original turn b. This is read from the cup or cap entry; it is not chosen afterward. Let chi_f be the integer face-incidence vector of the retained marked versus ordinary cap character. For the specified mark this follows directly from Xi_N(x)=N^-1 q^(-d^2)Q^(dx). Here x is the SECOND ordered cap head: the original cap and mark are q^(di)/N and q^(dj)/N^2 at (i,j)=(d-x,x). If u is the cap's outside face and v its inside face, the raw second clock is -L_v/L_u; the mark therefore contributes +1 at v and -1 at u. A retained literal cyclic turn is treated by its actual monomial in the same way. Let M_f count the middle white corners at the trivalent vertices. Then the limiting normalized logarithmic derivative of the original full root product S_N is the explicit covector nu_f=1_(f in Qcal)-M_f/2 +(1/2)sum_b epsilon_(b,f)+chi_f. (5) The angle contribution is 1 on a bounded circle because the consecutive tangent-circle triangles sweep its full 2pi angle. It is zero at each of the two constant-prefix lines. This is the actual circle-packing incidence, not a sum of independently optimized vertices. Every nu_f is an INTEGER. To prove this in the original uncontracted Morse graph, traverse the closed boundary of a white face and record whether its direction agrees with the source-edge orientation. At a middle corner the two main legs are both incoming or both outgoing, so this agreement flips. At a main-matching corner one leg is incoming and one outgoing, so it does not flip. It flips at a literal cup or cap. Returning to the start implies that M_f plus the number of turns at f is even. The sign of a turn is irrelevant modulo two, proving the integrality in (5). This argument is unchanged by the literal pi reduction. Before that reduction dualization reverses all THREE ports; each adjacent face meets two of these local turns. Deleting them preserves turn parity. Algebraically its cup/physical-inverse-cup ratio has no leading magnetic derivative at the fold: when 2a=d its q exponent is d[(d-r)-(2d-i-j)]=d(m-d), which is label-only. The exact near-fold remainder is not deleted. Thus the parity calculation and the reduced two-W calculation of (4) refer to the same source. Also sum_f nu_f=0. There are 2R white vertices and R quadratic faces; the total middle count is 2R, while every turn and mark incidence has sum zero. Hence (5) defines an integral covector on face potentials modulo their common constant. For the ORIGINAL flat-plat presentation the signed count is stronger. At a horizontal slice let the gaps between its 2k ordered heads carry the actual white-region labels. A box in slot a removes the old middle gap a+1 at its pi vertex and introduces a new one at its W vertex. Each odd gap begins at a bottom cup and ends at a top cap. Every bounded segment of such a region has exactly two endpoints: middle vertices or inside cups/caps. The internal even gaps begin and end in the exterior. Each must be met by at least one box: otherwise the plat separates across that gap, contrary to the one-main-component hypothesis. Its bounded intermediate segments have two middle endpoints. Thus, with the LITERAL cup signs, every bounded face has M_f-turn_f=2, turn_f=sum_b epsilon_(b,f). The exterior has M_out=2(k-1) and turn_out=2k, hence index -2. An inside cup/cap contributes -1 to turn and its outside contributes +1; this follows directly from its raw first-head ratio -L_out/L_in. Consequently the exact physical monomial after (2a) is L_out^d product_(bounded f) L_f^(-d). (5a) The two constant faces are precisely this exterior and the inside face of the marked cap. The mark contributes -d at the former and +d at the latter. In fact its scalar is exactly Xi_N=N^-1 (L_in/L_out)^d, (5b) since q^(-d^2)(-q^-1)^d=(-1)^d q^(-Nd)=1. This proves nu_f=0 for EVERY face of the original marked source. (5c) The ordinary closed source instead has the two charges +1 at the exterior and -1 at the other constant face. They are canceled by the actual mark, not by an invented winding choice. For the specified compact parameter sets, (4) therefore implies (1/N)d Log S_N(Z_N) = o(1) (6) uniformly for shrinking folded deficits. Fixed-channel h0, gamma and half-twist phases have zero magnetic derivative but stay in S_N. ## 4. Retained normalization and the distinction from a winding change The preceding signed count also records the complete formal-face normalization. On the positive face-log branch each original bottom cup has scalar N q^(-d^2/2), and each ordinary top cap has scalar N^-1 q^(d^2/2); their k pairs cancel. Equation (5b) supplies the remaining 1/N. Hence the uncontracted original marked sector is N^-1 product_i[k_(a_i) beta_(a_i)^2 omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i] * product_i[D_(a_i,in)D_(a_i,out)Ptilde_(s_i)] /product_(quadratic f)L_f^d. (7) The original exterior framing line remains separate and unchanged. The identities extend with the specified source marks. Formula (7) does not itself convert a physical finite sum to an unrestricted face torus, or settle its support and alias conditions. For comparison, if one keeps the ordinary cap, or uses another already proved presentation with the integer cochain (5), an exact lattice-one winding change can be specified as follows. This comparison is NOT used to obtain (5c). Choose an INTEGER affine source origin h^0 for the fixed labels and support stratum. Its corresponding potential origin Z^0 includes the actual half-index constants. Every original integer source state has Z-Z^0=(2pi i/N)n, n integral modulo constants. The entire character C_nu,N(Z)=exp[-N sum_f nu_f(Z_f-Z_f^0)] equals one at every such state. Multiplying the original summand by this displayed character preserves its original finite sum, and all residues on its original small node tori. It does not equate differently transported support chains. The affine-origin factor exp(N nu dot Z^0) is retained, even when its real logarithm has leading size. Define the particular sector logarithm g_N(Z)=Log S_N(Z)-N nu dot(Z-Z^0). (8) For the original MARKED source nu=0 and g_N=Log S_N exactly. For the comparison presentation its normalized gradient at the boundary sample tends to zero after the displayed explicit correction. The subtracted character can change the real off-grid action. Accordingly (8) is a specified winding representative, not an assertion that the original global cycle selects this representative or that its critical value is the marked geometric volume. The exact identity (2) prevents an additional accidental circle character; it does not compute an unproved global winding coefficient. ## 5. Local transverse critical point and a constructed local period Fix the two neighboring original physical heads from the primitive slice theorem. Equivalently take its fixed integral complementary log-clock basis C and write Z=Z_N+Cw, w in C^n, n=R-1. The existing rank theorem and [finite core curvature](actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature.md) give, in this basis, a real positive reference Hessian bounded between cN I and CN I. The exact finite clocks and near-fold corrections change it by o(N). On a fixed complex neighborhood all fixed derivatives of order at least two are O(N). These statements include both parities. Set e_N=|N^-1 partial_w g_N(0)|, so e_N tends uniformly to zero by (6). The Hessian divided by N has inverse bounded uniformly, and its derivative is bounded on a smaller fixed ball. Newton's contraction, using that Hessian at zero, therefore gives a unique zero w_N in a ball of radius C e_N. Explicitly the Newton remainder is at most C|w|^2, so the map sends that ball into itself and has contraction constant at most C e_N for sufficiently large N. Thus partial_w g_N(w_N)=0, |w_N|<=C e_N=o(1). (9) This is a transverse sector-critical point; it does not assert that the finite-label geometric sample itself is stationary. Nor does it assert that the two remaining finite framing forces vanish. Without a quantitative rate for (6), the head displacement is only o(N). Let H_N be the w Hessian at w_N. Its real part remains at least cN I. For fixed sufficiently small eta>0 the oriented local contour w=w_N+i x, x in [-eta,eta]^n, obeys Re[g_N(w_N+i x)-g_N(w_N)]<=-cN|x|^2. Taylor's theorem proves this from the Hessian and O(N) third derivative. The standard rescaling x=N^-1/2 y can here be verified directly: the cubic correction is odd and integrates to zero on the symmetric box against the even complex Gaussian; the quartic correction and square of the cubic have relative size O(N^-1), and the remaining tails are exponentially small. Uniform higher derivative bounds give integral_(w_N+i[-eta,eta]^n) exp(g_N(w)) dw = i^n (2pi)^(n/2) exp(g_N(w_N))/sqrt(det H_N) *[1+O(N^-1)]. (10) The square root is the continuation from the positive reference matrix. All source scalars and the affine-origin character remain in the displayed exponential. If the chosen flat source measure is the actual unscaled free-head measure, the exact coordinate Jacobian contributes (N/(2pi i))^n. Any cotangent kernels or additional boundary currents must be retained separately; they are not implicitly replaced by that flat measure. Equation (10) is a nonzero explicitly constructed LOCAL period. No intersection with the original finite-support cycle, residue transport, mixed-color comparison, or asymptotic for the fully contracted source is inferred. ## 6. The absolute rate from the actual coned polyhedron This section supplies an absolute geometric normalization without identifying the finite-r selected sheets with a geometric critical branch. The potential and coning identities themselves require only the connected certified right-angled graph and a marked main edge; they do not require that all main strands form one component. The one-main-component hypothesis remains in the earlier finite-r six-type boundary-chart and local-period assertions. Let a_f>0 be the actual curvatures of the bounded white circles in the marked coordinate p=infinity, and set a_f=0 at its two white lines. A common positive scale is immaterial. For one shaded triangle write its three curvatures as (x,b,y), and let F(x,b,y)=lim_(a/N->1/2) N^-1 Log D_a(x,b,y). The limit and its first derivatives follow from the actual finite determinant rate and the preceding boundary limits. It is homogeneous in the logarithmic sense F(tx,tb,ty)=F(x,b,y)+(1/2)log t. For three positive curvatures set Delta=sqrt(xb+by+yx), theta_j=2atan(a_j/Delta). These are the center-triangle angles, their sum is pi, and (4) says partial_log a_j F=theta_j/(2pi). Consequently V_tri=2pi F-sum_j theta_j log a_j has differential -sum_j log(tan(theta_j/2))dtheta_j. The common log Delta disappears because sum_j dtheta_j=0. Define the usual Lobachevsky function by Lambda(t)=-integral_0^t log|2sin u|du. Direct differentiation now gives V_tri=2 sum_j[Lambda(theta_j/2) +Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2)] + constant. (11) The constant is ZERO, with the source normalization still retained. Indeed at (x,0,0), D_a=(x/2)^a det H_-. The exact original LDL pivots give det H_-=product_(n=1)^a sin(n pi/N)/[cos(n pi/N)sin((2n-1)pi/N)]. Their normalized logarithm tends to (1/2)log2, by the elementary log-sine Riemann sum. Thus F(x,0,0)=(1/2)log x and V_tri=0. This is also the continuous boundary value of the determinant rate: set the second matrix coefficient to zero by H_+<=2H_-+8I, then let the identity coefficient tend to zero in its explicit rate integral. After subtracting (1/2)log alpha its integrand is dominated by C+2|log cos(pi t)| and tends to -log2-2log cos(pi t). The right side of (11) tends to zero at (pi,0,0). This fixes the absolute constant and includes all one-line degenerations. The actual facets identify the sum in (11) with volume. Cone the marked ideal vertex p=infinity to every nonincident facet of the convex Q. These positive pyramids partition Q, as in the existing positive polyhedron triangulation. For a WHITE ideal polygon on a finite circle, let delta_j be its consecutive central arcs. Its cone volume is sum_j Lambda(delta_j/2). To verify this, triangulate the actual cyclic polygon from one of its vertices. Each ideal tetrahedron with fourth vertex infinity contributes the three Lobachevsky values of its Euclidean triangle angles. Internal diagonals occur with complementary half-arcs t and pi-t, and cancel by Lambda(pi-t)=-Lambda(t). Only the boundary half-arcs remain. No new ideal vertex or unsigned overlapping decomposition is introduced. At a shaded triangle the consecutive contact arcs on a neighboring white circle are exactly its center angle theta_j. Orthogonality of the white and shaded circles gives two right angles in the quadrilateral of their centers and their two intersections. Hence the shaded arc between those intersections is pi-theta_j. The shaded ideal triangle coned to infinity therefore has volume sum_j Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2). Summing the white pyramids and shaded tetrahedra over their ACTUAL facet incidences proves Vol(Q)=sum_(shaded triangles) sum_j [Lambda(theta_j/2)+Lambda((pi-theta_j)/2)] =(1/2)sum_(shaded triangles) V_tri. (12) The two incident white lines have zero cone volume. Incident shaded triangles give the (pi,0,0) limiting angles and contribute zero as well. Thus (12) retains the marked cusp and every actual facet; it is not a separately maximized local-polyhedron comparison. Evaluate the homogeneous source polynomial at these curvatures, with the two constant faces set to zero. Its limiting normalized real log, including the target monomial of (7), is Phi=sum_(shaded triangles)F(a_f0,a_f1,a_f2) -sum_(quadratic f)log a_f. The angle sums at every bounded white circle are 2pi. Equations (11),(12) therefore give the ABSOLUTE identity 2pi Phi=sum_tri V_tri=2Vol(Q), Phi=Vol(Q)/pi=Vol(actual augmented complement)/(2pi). (13) The remaining original fixed-channel scalars have not been discarded. For shrinking folded deficits, N^-1 log beta_a^2 tends to 2J(2a/N)-4J(a/N), hence to zero because J(1)=J(1/2)=0. The positive root forced product has logarithmic size O(s) on these curvature compacts, including a zero endpoint curvature; its normalized rate also tends to zero. The factors k_a and 1/N are polynomial, and the retained half-twist powers have modulus one at actual integer labels. Their exact values stay in (7). The original finite-r face diagonals have one common quadratic scale (b_ref/s_frame)N^2 rho^2 and relative error O(N^-1); their two constant diagonals divided by that scale tend to zero. Total homogeneity of degree dR cancels this common complex scale against the target monomial EXACTLY. The six source packets, with their retained top monomials and nonzero Bessel factors, then give the same normalized real rate (13). Their finite transport factors are not reset to one; they have zero normalized logarithmic rate. The nearby critical displacement in (9) changes N^-1 Re g_N by o(1), so it has the same value (13). This proves the absolute rate of the original marked boundary sample and of the constructed local transverse period. It still does not prove that an original finite-support period contains that local contour with nonzero coefficient, or control cancellation in the full auxiliary-label sum or in external filling colors. ## 7. Focused source and absolute-normalization checks The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_original_boundary_stationary_character.py), with [recorded results](../experiments/actual_original_boundary_stationary_character_results.json), checks 34 literal marked-cap ratios and 34 physical cup/cap scalar pairs, 60 actual Morse charts with 810 signed face indices and zero marked forces, 48 original LARGE-H Ward identities in all six boundary regimes, 40 original LDL products, nine reciprocal-radius circle-angle identities, three absolute determinant-rate/Lobachevsky comparisons, and seven cyclic-polygon fan cancellations. The arithmetic is at 90 digits. Twenty-four finite force errors are retained as convergence diagnostics, not substituted for the uniform derivative proof. The Morse region compiler is shared with the independently audited full marked coefficient transformation. The local all-label circle identity has its separate original-white/dual/cup audit in the positive face-polynomial theorem. No new source-cycle assertion is attached to these numerical checks. Independent primary full analytical review: PASS. The reader checked the six source-force branches, signed Morse index and literal mark, uniform implicit-function and Gaussian constants, absolute LDL anchor, actual facet coning, and all source/connected-geometry scope distinctions. Independent full peer analytical review: PASS. The reader independently rederived the literal circle and mark scalars and all six force limits, then checked the local transverse proof and the absolute factor 2Vol(Q). A fresh redirected replay reproduced every reported count at 90 digits. The original cycle and full auxiliary-label sum remain separate.

text: # The original boundary source has exactly two flat face directions 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. On the labeled original right-angled matching graph, the finite boundary models detect every homogeneous magnetic direction except two explicit face potentials. Two neighboring ORIGINAL physical heads give a primitive slice for those directions.
