text: # The original marked source is one positive face coefficient 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed and frozen. For every fixed folded channel assignment, the literal complete-circle plat source equals one coefficient of an explicit homogeneous polynomial with nonnegative real coefficients, times its known scalar and retained half-twist phases. The proof retains the original marked cap, finite support, primitive measure and both level parities. It does not substitute a newly chosen period for the physical source. The identity below is finite and exact. It does not yet estimate that coefficient, prove it nonzero for every channel assignment, or establish a hyperbolic-volume asymptotic. ## 1. Literal source and polynomial Fix a connected 2k-plat projection, k>=2, with all crossings in R recorded two-strand boxes. The exterior contains the actual k bottom cups and k top caps, one of the latter carrying the ORIGINAL unrestricted mark. Retain each box's half twist epsilon_i in {0,+1,-1}. The source is the [original complete-circle contraction](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md), not a routed replacement. Any separately recorded exterior framing line multiplies both sides of the identity below and is not erased. Remove half twists only in the planar graph used to name its regions; their exact scalars omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i remain in the source. The plane matching graph Delta has R+2 white faces. Let u be the exterior face and v the bounded face inside the actual marked top cap. These are the two faces adjacent to the marked physical edge. Write F_* for the other R faces. The geometric certificate is not needed for the finite identity; when it is present these are exactly the two constant-prefix faces of the resonant chart. Connectedness here concerns the planar source graph, not the number of main link components. Multiple main components are allowed. In particular the all-untwisted standard 2k-plat generally retains k main components; the positive untwisted specialization is a statement about that augmented LINK source, not automatically a family of k-bridge knots. Put N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2. For each actual integer label 0<=a_i<=floor(d/2), set s_i=d-2a_i and beta_a=S_(2a)/S_a^2, S_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N), k_a=1 if s=0, and k_a=2 otherwise. Use the exact local factors proved in the [positive-circle theorem](actual_complete_circle_positive_face_polynomial.md): D_a(x,z,y)=det[z I+(x/2)H_-+(y/2)H_+], Ptilde_s(x,y)=sum_(j=0)^s S_s/[S_j S_(s-j)] x^(s-j)y^j. At box i let (f0,fin,fout,f2) be its ORIGINAL outer, input-middle, output-middle and final white regions. Define P_(N,a)(L)=product_i D_(a_i)(L_f0,L_fin,L_f2) D_(a_i)(L_f0,L_fout,L_f2) Ptilde_(s_i)(L_f0,L_f2). (1) Repeated region labels, if the actual plane diagram has them, are substituted literally. Every coefficient of (1) is nonnegative real, and its total degree is sum_i(2a_i+s_i)=dR. Define C_(N,a)=[product_(f in F_*) L_f^d] P_(N,a)(L) evaluated at L_u=L_v=0. (2) The fixed-channel contribution A_(N,a)^epsilon to the original marked root source is EXACTLY A_(N,a)^epsilon =N^R product_i[k_(a_i) beta_(a_i)^2 omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i] C_(N,a). (3) Thus C_(N,a)>=0, with zero allowed. The full original source is the finite sum of (3) over its original folded labels. In particular the untwisted terms have a positive coefficient description; signed half twists retain their actual channel phases. No cancellation between different half-twisted channels is ruled out by (3). ## 2. A signed face index in the original flat-plat sweep Use the actual bottom-to-top order of physical heads and adjacent boxes. Number the gaps between strands by g=1,...,2k-1. Odd gaps start inside a bottom cup and end inside a top cap. Even gaps start and end in the exterior. A box on zero-based slot a replaces ONLY the region in gap g=a+1: its old middle region ends at the input pi vertex, and its new middle region starts at the output W vertex. All other gap regions continue through the box unchanged. Let M_f count these middle corners in face f. Let T_f be the signed ordinary physical turn incidence: each original cup or cap contributes +1 to its outside face and -1 to its inside face. These signs are the literal source signs: both cup and ordered ordinary cap have the same positive first-head monomial q^(d i) on i+j=d. In particular a top cap does not acquire an independently reversed sign. Every bounded segment in an odd gap has two ends, each either a middle corner or an inside cup/cap. Every bounded segment in an even gap has two middle ends. Therefore M_f-T_f=2 for every bounded face. (4) Connectedness forces at least one box in each internal even gap: an unused such gap would separate the source projection into two disjoint plat blocks. Each of the k-1 even gaps therefore contributes two middle ends to the exterior, whereas all 2k cups/caps contribute their outside incidence there. Hence M_u=2(k-1), T_u=2k, M_u-T_u=-2. (5) This is the signed Euler turning identity in the literal Morse convention. Equivalently, middle corners and inside turns contribute +1 to twice the tangent winding of a face boundary; outside turns contribute -1. The sweep proof specifies all signs without selecting an arbitrary face orientation. The literal pi dualization does not invalidate (4). It reverses all three ports, and each adjacent face sees two of these local reversals. More directly the exact complete-circle factor already combines its auxiliary cup and two inverse physical cups, leaving precisely the two middle denominators with exponent d/2. There are no unrecorded turns to add after applying that exact factorization. ## 3. The original mark gives exactly the two missing face exponents Use centered face logarithms. For an ordered physical pair with outside face x, middle face z and final face y, i=d/2+N(Log L_x-Log L_z)/(2pi i), j=d/2+N(Log L_z-Log L_y)/(2pi i). (6) On each actual cup/cap y=x. The exact complete-circle expression is its scalar k_a beta_a^2 times its numerator in (1), divided by the product of its two middle variables to power d/2. Thus the ordinary whole-source face monomial has exponent (d/2)(T_f-M_f). Equations (4),(5) give L_u^d product_(f != u) L_f^(-d). (7) This holds also at EVEN levels: d/2 may be half-integral locally, but the assembled exponents in (7) are integers. Every local logarithmic lift is retained until this assembly. The mark sign is fixed by the original ordered matrices. At its cap with first head i and SECOND head j=d-i, ordinary cap(i,j)=N^-1 q^(di), mark(i,j)=N^-2 q^(dj). The original mark is unrestricted before contraction. The k bottom cups fix total physical degree kd, every actual box preserves that integer degree, and the other k-1 top caps use degree (k-1)d. Thus the two surviving marked endpoints necessarily have i+j=d. This is a consequence of whole-source conservation, not an early diagonal replacement of the marked tensor. Their ratio is N^-1 q^(-d^2)Q^(dj). The second head is the one whose raw face clock is -L_v/L_u. On the centered lift (6), the ratio is N^-1 (L_v/L_u)^d. (8) Using the first head in (8) would reverse the marked character and give an incorrect target coefficient. Equation (8) changes exponent +d to zero at u, and exponent -d to zero at v. All other exponents remain -d. No integral character has been selected anew or discarded. For completeness, the source constants also agree exactly. There are k cups N q^(-d^2)q^(di), k-1 ordinary caps N^-1 q^(di), and one marked cap N^-2 q^(dj). Each centered physical head contributes the constant q^(d^2/2); these 2k constants cancel the k cup factors q^(-d^2). Their total scalar is therefore precisely N^-1. Consequently the assembled meromorphic root product is N^-1 product_i[k_(a_i)beta_(a_i)^2omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i] P_(N,a)(L) product_(f in F_*) L_f^(-d). (9) The local root cup poles have been canceled by the proved complete-circle identity before (9) is used. No generic-q cancellation is inferred. ## 4. Primitive face grids at both parities and exact physical support The centered homogeneous source lattice is the cycle lattice of Delta. Its integral identification with face-potential differences modulo a constant is proved in [the original rank theorem](actual_original_boundary_transverse_rank.md), section 1. Fix the exterior face potential to zero. There are R+1 independent integral face potentials, with no finite-index Jacobian. At ODD N, d/2 is integral. Set L_u=1 and let every other L_f range independently through mu_N={Q^p:0<=p<N}. Formula (6) gives integral heads. At EVEN N there is an exact specified coset. Give each main edge the Z2 value1 and each matching edge the value0. Every shaded triangle has two main edges and one matching edge, so this cochain sums to zero on each triangle of the dual sphere. It integrates to face values t_f in Z2, unique after setting t_u=0. In the literal plat sweep this is simply the parity of the gap in which a region is born; the exterior has parity0. In particular t_v=1. Use the grid L_f=q^(t_f) Q^(p_f), p_f in Z/N, L_u=1. (10) On a main edge, d+t_left-t_right is even, so (6) is integral. On a matching edge, its auxiliary row is a plus a face-potential difference; the matching parity0 makes that integral too. The physical cup complements and all channel equations hold on the chosen affine lifts. The number of grid points is exactly N^(R+1) at either parity. There are no extra physical states hidden in this modular grid. Reduce physical heads to 0,...,d. The local support theorem proves that a surviving circle has BOTH physical totals in the actual interval [d-a,d+a], which contains at most N integers. Their congruence modulo N therefore forces equality as UNWRAPPED totals, with the original auxiliary row in [0,2a]. Unsupported pairs are killed by the small white or by the ONE forced factor retained after the cup cancellation. This is a zero of the entire root circle, not an undefined zero times a pole. Cups/caps similarly have unique physical total d in their congruence class. Thus every nonzero grid point gives an actual allowed state. Conversely every allowed state defines one grid point by the primitive face-potential isomorphism. Distinct allowed states cannot differ by N times a nonzero flow, since every head lies in an interval of length less than N. The actual allowed states are therefore exactly the possibly nonzero grid points, with zero points harmlessly included. Finally retain the even-level carry signs rather than canceling them locally by fiat. A surviving canonical state and its chosen affine lift differ by N times an integral CLOSED source flow. By the integral face-potential theorem this is N times integral face shifts. The full expression (9) has integer face exponents and is unchanged by such shifts. Hence the product of the local recorded carry multipliers is one. This proves the global carry cancellation in the actual source; it does not assert independent periodicity of each physical tensor. ## 5. A unique alias and the exact measure Write the nonnegative-coefficient polynomial as P_(N,a)=sum_n c_n product_f L_f^(n_f), with n_f>=0 and sum_f n_f=dR. In (9), the target exponents are0 at u,v and d at the R other faces. Averaging independently over (10) annihilates a monomial unless n_v=0 modulo N, n_f=d modulo N for f in F_*. Because 0<=d<N, nonnegativity forces n_v>=0 and n_f>=d. Their minimum total already equals dR. Homogeneity therefore forces n_u=n_v=0, n_f=d for every f in F_*. There is exactly ONE possible alias, namely the actual coefficient (2). At that exponent the even coset multiplier is1. The normalized face average equals C_(N,a), and the unnormalized source sum multiplies it by N^(R+1). Together with the single N^-1 in (9), this proves (3). No second boundary average or matching-edge trace factor is inserted. The same calculation also checks the original unmarked ordinary root closure. Its monomial is (7), so every one of the R+1 bounded faces would require polynomial degree at least d. This exceeds the total degree dR. Its whole root sum is consequently zero, as required by the original trace-normal identity. The mark is essential to the nonzero admissible target, not an optional renormalization. ## 6. Scope and review Formula (3) is the original fixed-channel ROOT contraction, not merely an equality of off-grid interpolants or local density values. It uses the proved canceled root circle and its exact modular-support zeros. It does not replace genuine generic-q lifts or their normal derivatives. The source weights h0 already include the actual complete-circle normal. The finite formula is valid at both parities and composite levels. All folded labels occur. A positive geometric certificate supplies additional candidate angle data but is not inferred from positivity of the polynomial. Estimating (2), proving a sharp full-channel bound with retained signed phases, and identifying the filled mixed-color limit remain separate tasks. No volume conjecture is asserted here. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.py), with [recorded results](../experiments/actual_original_marked_face_coefficient_results.json), checks 735 signed flat-plat sweeps and 15,386 exact marked face exponents. It compares 17 original fixed-sector W/pi matrix contractions, including the unrestricted original mark, with the independently built determinant coefficient. Its full face-grid checks cover 19,737 assignments: 2,179 supported states, 17,558 forbidden states, and 117 nontrivial even-level carry cancellations. Both level parities and composite levels occur; ordinary root closure zero is checked separately. These are finite identities over exact cyclotomic finite fields, not numerical evidence for an asymptotic or a nonzero coefficient in every sector. Independent primary full analytical review and fresh redirected replay: PASS. The reader checked the signed sweep, second-head mark, exact N^-1 scalar, primitive parity-coset grids, global carry cancellation, local support interval, unique alias and original ordinary-closure zero. Every focused-audit count was independently reproduced. Independent peer full analytical review and fresh redirected replay: PASS. The reader independently checked the original unrestricted mark and whole-degree restriction, both-parity measure, retained forced factor and finite support, and exact coefficient extraction. Every focused-audit count was reproduced, including the nontrivial even carries. The connected multi-main-component scope and the absence of an asymptotic or a nonzero-coefficient assertion were retained.

The first-cut phase is small and positive, and the boundary parameter rho is positive real. No independent local conjugations, reference changes or optimized heads are used. This is a statement about the original white numerators sampled from the COMPLETE geometric representation. It is not a finite-channel stationarity theorem, a generic-normal theorem, or a selected-period calculation. The full source still retains its cups, measures, marks, band sums and original support cycles. ## 1. Actual data and the common chart Fix the labeled positive right-angled matching-polyhedron certificate, the original exterior spine and white-prefix dictionary, and a fixed retained-half-twist pattern for which the main strands form ONE component. Auxiliary crossing circles remain present. The statement applies to every original input and output white factor with that dictionary; it does not label an arbitrarily routed extra band by an original face. All constants below may depend on this fixed diagram. Use its original exposed primitive meridian J=[[1,1],[0,1]], with fixed point infinity, and its incident reference face F_ref. Retain the actual reflection lifts of the [signed-prefix theorem](actual_right_angled_resonant_prefix_signs.md): H_f=[[a_f,b_f],[bar b_f,d_f]], det H_f=-1, Q_f=J_f bar J_ref, (Q_f)21=-a_f bar b_ref, a_f>=0, with equality precisely at incident faces. (1) There is a useful further consequence of this ORIGINAL meridian normalization. The other adjacent white face at its ideal vertex has actual prefix -J^epsilon, epsilon=+1 or -1, according to the recorded orientation. Its diagonal gives b_neighbor=-b_ref. Its upper-right entry then gives b_ref(d_ref+d_neighbor)=epsilon. Both d entries are real, and |b_ref|=1. Hence b_ref=+1 or -1. In particular the common phase in (1) is REAL in this specified global normalization. This does not choose new signs for individual lifts. In the actual two-parameter frame F(r,s)=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], put s=exp(-2pi i alpha)-1, r=N rho, alpha>0 small, rho>0. For each prefix Q_f=[[A,B],[C,D]], its diagonal is exactly L_f=Tr(Q_f F E11 F^-1) =-C r^2/s+(A-D+C/s)r+D+Bs. (2) The complete cusp-stabilizer argument in the [original boundary theorem](actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.md) gives the following two alternatives: a_f=0: Q_f=e_f[[1,z_f],[0,1]], L_f=e_f(1+z_f s), e_f=+1 or -1; a_f>0: L_f=(a_f b_ref/s)r^2[1+O(1/r)]. (3) There are finitely many such constants. Since s=-2pi i alpha+O(alpha^2), every constant L_f tends to e_f as alpha tends to zero. Thus one alpha_0>0 makes all constant prefixes nonzero for 0<alpha<alpha_0. The frame is invertible since s is nonzero. All subsequent uniform statements mean alpha in a fixed compact subinterval of (0,alpha_0), rho in a fixed compact subset of (0,infinity), and N sufficiently large depending on those compacts and the diagram. The coefficients and errors in (3) are then uniform. No limit taking alpha to zero together with N is asserted. ## 2. Simultaneous signs and canonical logarithmic lifts At each original half disk use its ACTUAL ordered faces and clocks X=-L_0/L_1, Y=-L_1/L_2, T_raw=XY=L_0/L_2. (4) The input and output share their outer prefixes, but may have different middle prefixes. The original auxiliary longitude and the marked main cusp are distinct, so 000 and 020 are excluded by the signed-prefix theorem. Keep every other possibility, independently at the two halves. For transitions between a quadratic and a constant prefix, (3) gives X/N^2 -> -a_f b_ref rho^2/[s e_g(1+z_g s)] for a quadratic-to-constant transition; N^2 X -> -e_f s(1+z_f s)/(a_g b_ref rho^2) for a constant-to-quadratic transition. (5) Because b_ref and e_f are real signs, their leading imaginary parts as alpha tends to zero are nonzero: of order alpha^-1 in the first line and alpha in the second. Shrinking alpha_0 once therefore keeps every one of these finitely many limiting coefficients off the real axis, simultaneously. Finite-r corrections preserve this separation for large N. In particular no escaping physical clock is on its positive-ray logarithmic seam. Ratios of two quadratic prefixes give the strict signs already proved from positive face normals. Ratios of two constant prefixes in an original 200 or 002 box have the primitive forms proved by the one-main-component corollary: the corresponding puncture is -J^epsilon, not an arbitrary cusp translation. Their finite clock is (1+z0 s)/(1+(z0+epsilon)s) =1+2pi i epsilon alpha+O(alpha^2). (6) It also avoids the positive-ray seam and the value one for sufficiently small positive alpha. The resulting simultaneous table is | Pattern | Limiting data and applicable root model | | --- | --- | | 200 | X/N^2 nonzero, Y finite nonzero; last-term Bessel packet | | 002 | X finite nonzero, N^2 Y nonzero; first-term Bessel packet | | 202 | X/N^2 and N^2 Y nonzero, T_raw positive; relative full-polynomial packet | | 220 | X negative finite, Y/N^2 nonzero; complementary determinant packet | | 022 | N^2 X nonzero, Y negative finite; its exact reciprocal packet | | 222 | X,Y negative finite; positive determinant with retained trace correction | The negative limits stay off the positive seam too. Hence every physical head in these original factors has its canonical logarithmic lift x=Log(X)/(2pi i) with 0<Re x<1. The original cup/cap inverse clocks then have complementary canonical lifts. The physical finite index is i=Nx-1/2, so its ACTUAL white argument is Q^i=q^-1 X, with q=exp(pi i/N) and Q=q^2. Do not drop this half-index factor. The input/output totals agree EXACTLY, not just modulo N. To see the required carry, all original two-head canonical argument sums lie in the SAME open interval (pi,3pi). For 222 and 202 they tend to 2pi. For 220/022 one argument tends to pi and the other stays strictly between zero and 2pi. For 200, the primitive formulas in the signed-prefix corollary give an escaping argument 3pi/2+O(alpha) when epsilon=+1 and pi/2+O(alpha) when epsilon=-1. The corresponding finite argument from (6) is O(alpha)>0 or 2pi-O(alpha), respectively. Their sums are therefore 3pi/2+O(alpha) and 5pi/2+O(alpha). The 002 formulas give the same two alternatives. Shrink alpha_0 and then take N large so all these statements have a uniform strict margin. The two halves have EXACTLY the same product T_raw. Their complex logarithmic sums can differ only by 2pi i times an integer, and their argument sums lie in an interval of length 2pi; hence they are equal. This proves their auxiliary matching rows agree after the physical half-index shift. It does not assume independently reset local degree logarithms. These are the PHYSICAL input/output rows of the matrix coefficient. The underlying literal dual white instead has heads (d-j,d-i), total 2d-sigma and row 2a-r0. Its exact source reflection is retained: with A0=Q^d, the numerator transforms by H_m(A0/V,A0/U)=A0^m(UV)^(-m) H_m(U,V), and the full white by W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r0)=q^[(d-2a)(a-r0)] W_a(i,j;r0). These are the recorded generic source identities, with their marked affine heads. The dual white rows are not asserted to equal r0. For 202, the two escaping limiting clocks are nonreal and have a positive product. Their canonical arguments in (0,2pi) therefore add to 2pi. At finite N their product lies near the positive ray, and continuation gives the exact marked choice q^(sigma+1)=-sqrt_near_positive(T_raw), sigma=i_1+i_2, Q^sigma=Q^-1 T_raw. (7) Here sqrt_near_positive is the branch positive on the limiting ray. Equation (7) is forced by the two original head lifts; it is not a freely chosen total square root. The same conclusion holds for 222, whose limiting two canonical arguments are both pi. There is NO exclusion of a 202/202 pair, of a rectangle with c=1, or of T_raw tending to one. The argument is applied to both actual middle prefixes and uses only the same finite set of original faces. ## 3. What the root-numerator packets now imply At every matching edge retain its actual integer channel 0<=a<=floor((N-1)/2), put m=N-1-a, and define the auxiliary row by the original equation i_1+i_2=(N-1-a)+r0. No universal physical -1/2 offset is assigned to auxiliary heads. Thus all finite degree constraints hold, but these samples of the complete parabolic representation are NOT asserted to solve the deformed finite-a stationary equations, especially when m/N is away from one half. Suppose each actual m/N stays in a fixed compact subset of (0,1). For the allowed folded channels this also keeps a/N away from zero for large N. The same geometry identifies the actual factorial domains. Every physical head i and d-i has real part divided by N in a fixed compact subset of (0,1), and imaginary part divided by N of size O(log N). Exactly, r0=a+N(x+y-1), 2a-r0=a-N(x+y-1). For 202/222, x+y=1-i log(T_infinity)/(2pi)+O(1/N), so both auxiliary real parts are a+O(1), in an interior factorial strip. For mixed outer degrees, their imaginary parts have opposite signs and absolute values divided by N equal to (log N)/pi+O(1), with bounded real parts divided by N. They are nonreal exterior arguments. The literal dual exchanges these auxiliary complements and reflects physical heads by d; it preserves the stated margins. Fixed integer factorials F_m,F_(2a),F_d have indices at most d. Thus these arguments meet the hypotheses, including divisor avoidance, of the already proved [logarithmic-factorial theorem](actual_moving_period_factorial_logarithmic_escape.md). This identifies source-factor domains; it does not replace a full regular-lift normal estimate. The finite list of numerator parameter limits in the table lies in the compact domains of the already proved root theorems: * The [200/002 theorem](actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.md) has the same limiting Bessel parameter at every such box, K=s^2 sin^2(pi m/N)/(4pi^2 rho^2), independent of its primitive orientation. Choose alpha_0<1/2. The corresponding J_0 argument s sin(pi m/N)/(pi rho) is nonreal and its value is nonzero by the radial energy identity in the signed-prefix corollary. On the fixed parameter compacts these values are uniformly bounded away from zero. * The same source theorem's 202 packet keeps its full small-channel polynomial and the exact large-partner product. Its total is near a positive compact, away from the negative polynomial-root ray. Since a/N is separated from zero, the forced partner factors stay uniformly away from their unit-arc zeros, even if T_raw tends to one. * The [complementary packet](actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge.md) applies to every 220 box. Its exact reciprocity, including the scalar and marked head lifts, transports every 022 box to that domain. * The [negative-clock theorem](actual_q_hahn_negative_clock_boundary.md) applies to every 222 box. Its O(1/N) clock perturbations retain the order-one trace term; replacing the finite clocks by their limits without that correction is not asserted. These models give nonzero root numerators for all sufficiently large N and uniform relative errors O(1/N) after their stated exact scalar, endpoint-product and trace normalizations. There are only finitely many original factors. Their literal product therefore has the product of these normalized root models with relative error 1+O_D(1/N). This is only a finite product statement for these specified numerator values; it does not estimate a sum over the original shared head variables. Every model retains its actual finite clocks and total, as specified in its source theorem. The limiting signs select its domain; they do not license replacing a degree-O(N) polynomial by its limiting-argument value. The positive-rho chart is also compatible with the actual off-node family in the [braided current theorem](actual_braided_residual_framing_current.md): set p_N=1-1/(N rho+b0 s). Its known coherent boundary factor tends to rho(1-exp(-1/rho))exp(t_coh/rho), which is nonzero. The coherent variable t_coh is not identified with alpha, and the whole-source scalar multiplying that factor remains unknown. No source-to-framing degree or nonzero relative-cycle coefficient follows from the common numerator chart. Focused audit: [actual simultaneous charts and source packets](../experiments/audit_actual_original_network_resonant_boundary_chart.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_original_network_resonant_boundary_chart_results.json). Two original main references of the signed ideal right-angled cuboctahedron cover all six patterns and both primitive orientations. Its cube matching retains the spherical ribbon order and has a literal one-main-component parity witness (0,1,1,1). A supplemental actual octahedral pair tests 202/202 and total one; that supplemental reference is NOT asserted to be a main edge in the one-main-component class. The audit keeps this distinction rather than assuming such pairs away. At 100 digits it passes 288 exact paired-total checks, 1152 physical head/cup checks, 3456 auxiliary-factorial domains, 320 marked square-root checks, 576 simultaneous half-disk domains, 1152 finite-r clock checks, and 288 literal root packets with 288 full dual numerator/white-turn identities. The largest paired-total error is below 3e-101, the largest dual identity error below 1.9e-91, and max N times packet relative error is 0.01491. These are focused finite checks; the written proof supplies the uniform existence and error claims. Independent full analytical review: PASS. The coherent-source reader checked the real reference coefficient, common small-phase seam exclusion, primitive orientation signs, exact (pi,3pi) total-carry argument, physical and auxiliary offsets, both marked total branches, every root-numerator domain and the finite-product error. This review includes 202/202 and c=1; it does not supply a generic bound, finite-color critical point or global relative-cycle coefficient. The primary reader independently passed the common-chart proof, including the real reference normalization, simultaneous seams and exact total carry. The source reader additionally checked the literal dual total, auxiliary complement, generic reciprocal factor and full white-turn monomial, then freshly replayed the complete focused audit: PASS. text: # A finite original-network source envelope at the resonant boundary 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. Fix the labeled positive right-angled matching-polyhedron certificate, actual cut and original white-prefix dictionary of an augmented diagram with one main component. On its single common boundary chart, the actual complete ROOT tensor summand is nonzero. Its specified regular complete-circle Hopf lift has fixed-quantum-jet upper bounds of polynomial cost times (CN^C) to the sum of the channel deficits. This includes all six original numerator types, both folded parities, 202/202 pairs and c=1. A positive triangulation alone does not supply the required polyhedron and prefix data. This is an UNCONTRACTED finite-network theorem. It retains the exact first-normal identity for the original complete source, but supplies no bound or noncancellation statement for its contracted finite sum or relative period. The generic lift is the regular W pi lift already proved for that identity, not the exceptional K/E germ and not the entire moving-q germ of a complete crossing circle. ## 1. Specify the original generic tensor summand Fix the original marked 2k-plat D with R complete-circle boxes and retained half-twist signs epsilon_i. Put N>=3, d=N-1, q0=exp(pi i/N), zeta=q0 exp(epsilon), Q=zeta^2. Fix actual folded labels a_i, 0<=a_i<=floor(d/2), and write m_i=d-a_i, s_i=d-2a_i, S=sum_i s_i. Use EXACTLY the regular Hopf lift from [the full matching-graph source](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md), sections 3--4. Its channel weights are held at their ORIGINAL root values h0_a=k_a N s_(2a)/s_a^2, omega_a=q0^(d^2/2)(-1)^a q0^[a(a+1)], k_a=1 if 2a=d and k_a=2 otherwise, gamma_a=q0^(2-a^2)/N^2. (1) They are all nonzero, including both maximal folded parities. In particular h0_M=N at odd N and h0_M=2N/sin(pi/N) at even N. Gamma_a is a FIXED root constant, not a generic norm to invert. The original generic white has the specified finite continuation W_a(i,j;r)=(-1)^m zeta^[-dr+di-m(m-1)] H_m^(Q^-N)(Q^i,Q^j)/F_m, i+j=m+r, F_m=(Q;Q)_m. (2) It is the actual LARGE source, m=d-a, in both physical degree halves. For a fixed highest weight L<N define the original continued cup p_L(x)=exp(pi i x) zeta^[x(L-x-1)] Fhat_P(x)Fhat_P(L-x)/F_L, pV(x)=N zeta^(-d^2)p_d(x), P=pi i/Log zeta. (3) Here Fhat_P is the specified moving-period Gamma product, agreeing with the exact generic finite factorial at its admissible integer arguments. The ordered cap is 1/p_L(L-x), with the same physical scale when L=d. The complete-circle retraction is literally pi_a=gamma_a^-1 p_(2a)^T W_a^T (ellV^T tensor ellV^T)P_rev. (4) An explicit coefficient, useful for retaining every orientation, is pi_a(r;i,j) =gamma_a^-1 p_(2a)(2a-r) W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r)/[pV(d-j)pV(d-i)]. (5) The exact generic Chevalley identity also gives W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r)=zeta^[(d-2a)(a-r)]W_a(i,j;r). Thus (5) retains the original channel cup, TWO physical inverse cups, reversed tensor order and gamma_a. It divides by no paired root norm: pi_a W_a=0 at a paired node is not a denominator in this theorem. Expand every original coupon with (2),(4), and use the original physical cups/caps and cyclic turns. Impose their literal integral affine head constraints on an admissible stratum, with any primitive free-lattice chart h=h0+A x. Let S_F(epsilon,h) be this ordinary CLOSED tensor summand, including product_i h0_(a_i)omega_(a_i)^epsilon_i and an ordinary cap at the exposed marked arc. At admissible integer heads it is the actual finite summand of this specified regular Hopf lift. No head is wrapped, and no support inequality is removed. Constant forbidden strata retain their original zero value rather than being assigned a meromorphic 0/0 continuation. ## 2. The one common geometric head assignment Use the [original common boundary chart](actual_original_network_resonant_boundary_chart.md), with r_frame=N rho, rho in a positive real compact, and s_frame=exp(-2pi i alpha)-1, alpha in a fixed sufficiently small positive compact. Every physical head has its ACTUAL canonical lift i=Nx-1/2, X=exp(2pi i x), 0<Re x<1. The input/output two-head argument sums lie in the SAME interval (pi,3pi), so their totals agree exactly, not just modulo N. Cups have complementary lifts summing to d. Auxiliary heads are defined by r0=i+j-(d-a), and both ends of each matching edge agree after the recorded cup/dual reversal. Therefore h_N lies in the original complex affine head chart. These are samples of the complete geometric representation, not assertions of finite-a stationarity. Require the shrinking-fold range S log N=o(N). For the estimates it is enough first to assume each 0<=s_i<=eta N, for a sufficiently small fixed eta. Then a_i/N stays in a fixed interior neighborhood of one half and all the following margins are uniform. Every physical i and d-i has real part divided by N in a fixed compact subset of (0,1), with imaginary part divided by N of size O(log N). For auxiliary heads put sigma=i+j. Exactly, r0=a+N(x+y-1), 2a-r0=a-N(x+y-1). (6) For 202/222, the canonical total gives x+y=1-i Log(T_infinity)/(2pi)+O(1/N), T_infinity>0. Both auxiliary real parts are consequently a+O(1), within an interior factorial strip. For mixed outer degrees 200/220 and 002/022, the two auxiliary arguments have opposite imaginary parts with absolute value divided by N equal to (log N)/pi+O(1); their real parts divided by N remain bounded. They lie in the nonreal exterior factorial domain. Fixed integer offsets and all actual reversed arguments preserve these margins. The only fixed integer factorials are F_m,F_(2a),F_d and their original finite products, with indices<N. Thus every factor and inverse in (2)--(5) satisfies the [logarithmic-factorial theorem](actual_moving_period_factorial_logarithmic_escape.md). The actual root and nearby generic factors avoid its poles and zeros. This includes 202/202 and either folded parity; no physical-head half-index offset is assigned to an auxiliary head. ## 3. Nonzero root product, with every exact factor retained At the common chart every original white numerator has one of the six proved boundary models. The source-normalized 200/002 Bessel factors are nonzero: their common argument is s_frame sin(pi m/N)/(pi rho), which is nonreal. The 202 whole polynomial lies near its positive total ray, with its actual large-partner product retained. The 220/022 determinant packets are nonzero on their actual negative finite-clock rays. The 222 positive determinant retains its finite clock perturbation and order-one trace correction. No202/202 pair or c=1 case is excluded. Let B_v,N denote the exact scalar times normalized root model specified by the applicable numerator theorem, evaluated at the ACTUAL finite clocks. Keep every non-numerator factor of S_F(0,h_N) exactly, and replace each H_m only by its B_v,N. Denote the resulting finite product by B_F,N. Then S_F(0,h_N)=B_F,N[1+O_D(N^-1)], B_F,N!=0. (7) In particular the uncontracted original root summand is nonzero for large N. The original h0_a, gamma_a, omega_a, white monomials, factorials, cups, pivotal clocks, half-index shifts and every integral character remain in B_F,N. They are not normalized to modulus one. Some have exponential or N log N size individually. Equation (7) retains their exact joint product rather than bounding them separately. The finite-clock determinant in 220 and the trace correction in 222 cannot be replaced by their limiting-clock values without their specified order-one factors. At the original exposed root mark, degree conservation after the other caps forces complementary indices (d-x,x). The literal ratio of that marked row to the ordinary cap is Xi_N(x)=N^-1 q0^(-d^2) Q0^(d x), Q0=q0^2. (8) Consequently the actual marked root summand on this same affine chart is S_M(0,h_N)=Xi_N(x_N)S_F(0,h_N), and has the corresponding nonzero packet Xi_N(x_N)B_F,N. The character in (8) is retained as written: Q0^(dx)=exp(2pi i x)Q0^-x on a literal complex head, not merely Q0^-x. No bare root mark is moved through a cap or promoted to a generic covariant tensor. For the chosen original first-cut chart its exposed physical clock is A=(1+s_frame)^-1=exp(2pi i alpha), or the recorded complementary clock according to the cap orientation. Thus x_N is real, equal to N alpha-1/2 or N(1-alpha)-1/2, and |Xi_N(x_N)|=1/N. (9) This modulus statement is specific to that chosen real-alpha boundary chart. It is not a claim that the marked character is harmless on an arbitrary complex framing chart. ## 4. Every fixed generic jet of the specified lift There are constants c_D,C_D and, for each fixed k, C_(D,k) such that on |epsilon|<=c_D N^-10, |S_F(epsilon,h_N)/S_F(0,h_N)| <=C_D(C_D N^40)^S, (10) and hence |partial_epsilon^k S_F(0,h_N)| <=C_(D,k) N^(10k)(C_D N^40)^S |S_F(0,h_N)|. (11) The derivative holds EVERY marked head h_N fixed. Its common geometric construction is not rerun as epsilon varies. Here is the proof from the actual factors. The genuine 200/002 theorem gives bounded relative numerator variation on this smaller disk when the nonzero Bessel factor is retained. The [paired220 theorem](actual_q_hahn_paired_resonant_circle_packet.md) gives cost C(CN^20)^s for 220; exact GENERIC reciprocity gives the same for 022, including its marked complement and scalar. The [positive-total theorem](actual_q_hahn_positive_total_boundary_normals.md) gives that bound for 202/222, including possible zero single root edges. Each matching edge has TWO original white numerators after (5) is expanded. Their total cost is at most C_D(C_D N^20)^(2 sum_i s_i)=C_D(C_D N^40)^S. The factorial domain verification in section 2 gives bounded two-sided relative variation for every cup factor, its inverse and fixed factorial on the larger disk c/[N^2(1+log N)^2]. All monomial exponents have size O_D(N^2(1+log N)^2), so their ratios are bounded on our smaller disk. Gamma_a, h0_a and omega_a are the fixed root constants of the specified lift and have relative ratio one. There are only finitely many factors for fixed D. This proves (10) and its holomorphy directly in the original regular factors. Cauchy's formula proves (11). Thus the cost is polynomial for bounded total deficit S, including maximal folded channels at both level parities, and subexponential whenever S log N=o(N). No fixed nonzero scaled channel-width estimate is asserted. Nor is a nonzero leading normal amplitude inferred from this relative UPPER bound. ## 5. The unchanged original first-normal identity and its limit Let A_D,N be the original complete root source before its separately recorded exterior framing line. On each label sector the specified regular Hopf lift has ordinary closed value F_a(epsilon)=D_N(epsilon)z_a(epsilon), with D_N(epsilon)=(-1)^d[N]_(q0 exp(epsilon)), nu_N=D_N'(0)=2N(-1)^N/(q0-q0^-1)!=0. The exact source theorem therefore remains A_D,N=nu_N^-1 sum_a sum_(h in original support(a)) partial_epsilon S_F(0,h). (12) All sums in (12) are finite and retain their original affine constraints, support, parity and mark. The full paired-circle first normal is already contained in h0_a W_a pi_a at the root. No paired norm is inverted, and no Hermite sector is removed. The regular lift need not be the whole moving-q circle: any two regular generic Hopf lifts with the same root coupon give the same marked scalar, because their closed difference is D_N times a holomorphic open scalar vanishing at zero. Combining (9),(11) with |nu_N|=N/sin(pi/N) gives the local bound |nu_N^-1 partial_epsilon S_F(0,h_N)| <=C_D N^9(C_D N^40)^S |S_M(0,h_N)|. (13) This retains the actual first-normal normalization and the actual mark ratio. It is still a bound at the sampled complex head assignment. Equation (12) is NOT evaluated by replacing its finite supported summands by (13), moving their cycles to this chart, or identifying the regular lift with the exceptional K/E germ. A contraction can vanish although every local boundary factor in (7) is nonzero. The original coherent band cycles, their boundary residues and the global relative framing coefficient remain to be determined. Focused audit: [literal regular source normalization and retained normals](../experiments/audit_actual_original_network_resonant_source_envelope.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_original_network_resonant_source_envelope_results.json). It compares (5) against 307 original categorical-dual coefficients and their first jets, including 100 high-total coefficients. It retains 15 paired zero retractions and three simple retractions, checks 54 nonzero root scalars, six maximal-fold formulas and 33 actual mark/cap ratios. All 307 tested coefficients detect the wrong first jet if the fixed gamma_a is replaced by its tempting moving-q monomial. Two original four-box plats, at opposite level parities, verify 32 retained sector trace normals and both exhaustive full-color source sums. The N=4 full source in that finite-field fixture is zero; no noncancellation assertion is attached to the local envelope. Six symbolic checks retain the affine offsets, reversed dual indices and marked character. The common-chart, individual-packet and factorial bounds have their separate focused audits. The finite-network inequalities here follow by the displayed exact factorization and Cauchy's formula; they are not a numerical estimate of a global period. Independent full analytical review and fresh focused replay: PASS. The source reader checked the literal reversed categorical dual (5), actual LARGE white, fixed root gamma/h0/omega, both folded retraction types, the retained physical trace normal and mark ratio, all six numerator domains, and the two-large-factor deficit cost. The fresh replay reproduced every reported coefficient, scalar, retraction, mark and whole-source check, including the zero full-source fixture. Independent geometric/source-domain review: PASS. The geometric reader checked every physical and auxiliary moving-factorial argument, the exact dual offsets, the real exposed first-cut head, the nonzero root product with its finite-clock factors, and the N^9 normalization in (13). Both reviews retain the specified regular-lift, uncontracted-product and relative-upper-bound scope; neither asserts a global period coefficient. Independent primary proof review: PASS. The primary reader checked the literal complementary dual rows, fixed root weights, two-numerator deficit cost, all moving-factorial domains, normalized mark and N^9 factor. The focused source replay is recorded separately; this proof review supplies no global contraction or relative-cycle conclusion.

title: The original outer color has a squared Fourier kernel
text: # The original outer color has a squared Fourier kernel 29 October 2026. The full original Hermite source cancels the dangerous outer-color alias exactly. A finite contour with a SQUARED denominator then turns a coherent spectral packet into a genuine auxiliary-color packet, with a strict bound on every complementary physical color. This is a source identity and estimate, not an identification of a Casimir coordinate with a meridian. ## 1. Actual color, values, and normals Let N>=2, d=N-1 and theta_j=(2j-d)pi/N, 0<=j<N. The actual Casimir nodes are c_j=-2cos(theta_j). Use the literal circle L_j=(-1)^(j-1)U_(j-1)(Omega/2) and original functional phi from [the full physical trace theorem](actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md). For a full Hermite element f set F(theta)=f(-2cos(theta)). For each ACTUAL auxiliary color N-h, 0<=h<N, that trace gives exactly A_N(h)=phi(L_(N-h) f) =sum_j [(N-h)cos(h theta_j)F(theta_j) -sin(h theta_j)F'(theta_j)]. (1) Here the prime is the theta derivative. In particular it retains the first Casimir normal at every double node. At the odd simple node theta=0 its contribution is (N-h)F(0), as required. To derive (1), sin(theta)L_(N-h)(-2cos(theta))=sin((N-h)theta). The double-node trace is twice (-1)^d times the theta derivative of that last sine times F. At a node cos(N theta_j)=(-1)^d and sin(N theta_j)=0. Combining the two equal terms at theta and -theta gives (1). The simple node is checked by its removable value. No generic-q derivative is substituted for this fixed-root normal. An even analytic function F may replace the polynomial on any symmetric set of nodes if it has the SAME values and theta derivatives there. Symmetry of those nodes then also gives A_N(h)=sum_j exp(i h theta_j)[(N-h)F(theta_j)+i F'(theta_j)]. (2) ## 2. The exact Fourier alias that disappears Write F(theta)=sum_k Fhat_k exp(i k theta), with Fhat_k=Fhat_(-k). For a polynomial f the sum is finite. Since sum_j exp(i k theta_j)=N(-1)^(d ell) if k=ell N, (1) gives the exact all-normal formula A_N(h)=N^2 sum_(ell in Z) (1-ell)(-1)^(d ell) Fhat_(ell N-h). (3) If f has degree less than N, every noncentral possible alias is killed and A_N(h)=N^2 Fhat_h, 0<=h<N. (4) Thus the physical auxiliary-color vector is precisely the Fourier coefficient vector of the FULL Hermite representative of f. Reducing f modulo P_N is allowed here; reducing only its values is not. Most importantly, ell=1 has coefficient ZERO in (3). For h near N this would otherwise be the low frequency N-h, with the complete source growth. The normal term in (1) removes it. This is why an unweighted node sum is inadequate for the whole-color gap. For a nonperiodic analytic representative of the same node jets, one must not assume the separately weighted infinite Fourier aliases are absolutely summable. The finite contour below avoids this issue. ## 3. A finite residue identity, with its entire boundary retained Choose a symmetric rectangle [-b_N,b_N]+i[-eta,eta], with vertical sides halfway between physical theta nodes. Thus E(theta)=(-1)^d exp(iN theta)=-exp(-N Im theta) on either vertical side. Assume F is even and holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed rectangle. Put K_N(theta)=iN/(E(theta)-1). Its poles at the enclosed physical nodes have residue one. Apply residues to (2) and integrate F' by parts around the CLOSED contour. This is an exact identity: sum_(|theta_j|<b_N) exp(i h theta_j) [(N-h)F(theta_j)+iF'(theta_j)] =(1/(2pi i))oint exp(i h theta)F(theta) [-iN^2/(E(theta)-1)^2]dtheta. (5) Indeed K_N'=N^2 E/(E-1)^2 and N K_N-iK_N'=-iN^2/(E-1)^2. Equivalently the squared pole has principal part i/(theta-theta_j)^2 +N/(theta-theta_j); its residue is exactly the expression on the left. Every vertical and horizontal piece of the contour remains. For 0<=h<=N the oscillatory part of the kernel has these bounds: * upper side: at most C N^2 exp(-h eta); * lower side: at most C N^2 exp(-(2N-h)eta); * vertical sides: at most N^2, because exp(-h y)/(1+exp(-Ny))^2<=1 for every real y. The lower-side frequency is 2N-h, rather than N-h. This is the finite-contour version of the missing alias in (3). ## 4. A uniform physical-color theorem Here are explicit sufficient inputs, independent of any knot class. Let f_N be an actual full Hermite source. Suppose it has an even holomorphic representative F_N on a fixed rectangle |Re theta|<=2b, |Im theta|<=eta_0, and constants a,B,gamma>0 such that |F_N(u+iv)|<=C N^C exp[N(F0-a u^2+B v^2)]. (6) On the enclosed physical nodes require that F_N and its first theta derivative approximate the ACTUAL f_N node jets with error poly(N)exp[N(F0-gamma)]. On the complementary physical nodes require the actual values and first theta derivatives to have the same strict exponential gap (with possibly another fixed positive gamma). These are quantitative source assumptions; a principal symbol alone does not imply them. Choose halfway endpoints b_N=b+O(1/N). For every fixed delta>0, there is g_delta>0 such that max_(delta N<=h<N)|phi(L_(N-h) f_N)| <=poly(N)exp[N(F0-g_delta)]. (7) Proof. The approximation and omitted-node errors in (1) cost only powers of N. In (5) choose a fixed small eta with B eta^2<min(a b^2/16,delta eta/2,eta/2). For large N, b_N>=b/2. The upper and lower edges then lose at least delta eta/2 and eta/2 respectively; the vertical edges lose a fixed fraction of a b^2. There are finitely many edges of bounded length. This proves (7) uniformly through h=N-1, without an infinite charge-tail argument. There is also an exact specified analytic corridor interpolation: C_N(t)=N^2/(2pi) integral_(-b_N)^(b_N) F_N(theta) exp(iNt theta)dtheta. (8) It is even and entire in t. For 0<=h<=delta_0 N, with delta_0 fixed and small, |A_N(h)-C_N(h/N)|<=poly(N)exp[N(F0-g)] (9) for a fixed g>0. To see this, on the upper edge of (5) write the kernel as -iN^2+O(N^2 exp(-N eta)). The constant part, with the counterclockwise upper-edge orientation, is N^2/(2pi) times the upper translated integral in (8). Move that integral to the real segment and retain its two vertical connectors. They are gapped by (6); the upper remainder and lower side are gapped as above. The same actual node-jet errors are then added. This proves (9) for the exact finite integral, before any asymptotic expansion. The argument is uniform over additional REAL physical parameters satisfying these source estimates. If F_N is holomorphic and separately even in their complex continuations, (8) has the same properties. For that continuation an additional C||Im y||^2 in the exponent is allowed; (6) with the unchanged F0 is not asserted on a full complex parameter disk. Shrink this disk so its growth spends less than the fixed endpoint/current gap before using the complex saddle below. No analyticity of a merely pointwise error on the physical color lattice has been assumed. ## 5. The nonzero complex corridor saddle Suppose additionally on the fixed local rectangle and parameter disk F_N(theta,y)=eta_N N^mu b(theta,y) exp[N varphi(theta,y)] (1+O(1/N)), uniformly holomorphically, where b(0,0)!=0, varphi is even in theta and separately even in y, varphi(0,0)=F0, and varphi_theta,theta(0,0)=-D/(2pi), Re D>0. (10) Keep the known nonzero unit eta_N outside C_N. The implicit equation varphi_theta(theta_*,y)+it=0 has a unique small holomorphic solution. After shrinking the fixed disks, contour translation within the same rectangle and the gapped endpoint connectors give eta_N^(-1) C_N(t,y) =N^(mu+3/2) B(t,y) exp[N Phi(t,y)](1+O(1/N)), Phi=varphi(theta_*,y)+it theta_*, B=b(theta_*,y)/sqrt(2pi[-varphi_theta,theta(theta_*,y)]). (11) The square root continues the convergent Gaussian at t=y=0. It is nonzero. The local quadratic bound gives an integrable Gaussian majorant; outside a fixed saddle neighborhood (6) and the retained connectors give a strict gap. Taylor expansion and Gaussian moments prove the displayed uniform error. The analytic O(1/N) source error is bounded on this same contour. Both Phi and B are separately even. At the complete point, Phi(t,0)=F0-pi t^2/D+O(t^4), B(0,0)=b(0,0)/sqrt(D). (12) Since Re(1/D)>0, the physical outer-color curvature is strictly negative. Equations (7)--(12) are exactly the outer source gap and fixed complex color corridor needed in the general filling theorem. They do not yet assert that this action is a marked Bloch regulator. ## 6. Application to actual octahedral belt stacks [The inner physical-color theorem](actual_belt_stack_auxiliary_color_inner_packet.md) supplies the exact analytic inputs to this result for every fixed nonempty sign word of n pieces and every fixed outer crossing power a. Let sigma_i=+1 for a z_(N,h_i) piece and -1 for its typed reflection, e=sum_i sigma_i, and m=e+a. Its local representative is the actual product of finite inner packets times q^(m d^2/4) exp[iNm theta^2/(4pi)]. (13) The literal q^(m d^2/4) is used, not a principal square root. The original crossing and (13) have the same node values AND theta normals: partial_theta log R=iN theta/(2pi). The inner theorem retains exponentially small full-Hermite replacement errors and the strict angular complement bound. It also bounds every physical color tuple with an inner color outside its corridor, for ANY physical outer color. Consequently the WHOLE (n+1)-color original stack has an exact separately even complex corridor, a nonzero leading amplitude and a strict bound on its entire complementary physical color cube. Writing x_i=h_i/N, its action is Phi(x)=n j0-pi x_0^2/[n-i(e+a)] +(pi/2)sum_(i=1)^n(-1+i sigma_i)x_i^2+O(||x||^4), j0=v8/pi. (14) Thus in the notation Phi''(0)=2pi i diag(tau_i) of [the long-filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md), tau_0=i/[n-i(e+a)], tau_i=(sigma_i+i)/2, Im tau_i>0. (15) All analytic source hypotheses of that theorem now hold for these stacks, at every fixed n>=1. It supplies their nonzero original long-integral-filling asymptotic with the stated analytic critical action and original normalization. There is no width threshold in this source assertion. Width, a and all filling slopes are fixed before N tends to infinity; both level parities are retained. The independent geometric requirement is the ACTUAL deformed peripheral map and absolute regulator comparison for this SAME mixed packet. Matching (15) to cusp derivatives alone would not prove it. The [typed global lift](actual_belt_stack_typed_character_composition.md) now supplies that map, all complete face/collar checks and the absolute regulator. Combined with the source theorem above, it gives the [any-subset long-filling volume equality](actual_long_filled_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md). The spectral-to-color transform alone is not used to infer that equality. Independent full proof review rederived the exact alias cancellation, squared kernel, all boundary bounds, Gaussian normalization and the joint real/complex parameter quantifiers. The focused audit checks the polynomial identity with exact arithmetic, literal physical marked traces over finite fields, and separately labeled high-precision Gaussian examples. Such examples do not prove the analytic source hypotheses for an unrelated diagram.

title: A macroscopic clock current surviving exact source fusion
text: # A macroscopic clock current surviving exact source fusion 28 October 2026. Fixed overclock sectors cannot separately be bounded by the regulator of the closed knot, even after exact closure/full-block fusion. This is an all-level calculation in the ORIGINAL enhanced source. It identifies a remaining macroscopic current whose coherent clock sum is essential. It does not establish a new hyperbolic case or obstruct a source-specific upper bound after that sum. ## 1. Exact original source and its clock sectors Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, and exactly the enhanced crossing/pivot conventions of [the original crossing audit](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md): mu=-q S and alpha=-q. Take the positive two-strand word [1,1,1], with its original fixed first cut. The exact cyclic-source peeling proof gives K_N=Q^(-1) (T_+^3)_(0,1). (1) Here K_N is the original reduced enhanced period with unknot value one. In the full modified-trace convention multiply EVERY sector and both sides of the subsequent identities by its original known external line. That common line is retained and has no exponential modulus at completeness; it is never replaced by an unknown scalar. The factor Q^(-1)=(-q)^(-2) includes the ORIGINAL closing coefficient and full writhe correction. No new average, source or normalization is introduced. The entries of this actual boundary operator are T_(0,j)=Q^(1-j), T_(k,0)=0 for k>0, T_(k,j)=(-1)^(j-1) Q^[k+(j-1)(j-2)/2] [k-1 choose j-1]_Q, 1<=j<=k<=d. (2) All other entries vanish. These are the directly proved q-Pascal entries of the original crossing, including T_(0,0)=Q. Every supported cut path has first head zero throughout. At a positive crossing its actual overclock is h=[b-a-1]+[a-c]=[b-1]. Thus its three clocks are (0,H,J), with H,J in 0,...,d, and its intermediate second-head values are i(H)=H+1 if H<d, i(d)=0; i(J)=J+1 if J<d, i(d)=0. (3) There is exactly ONE such peeled path for each supported clock pair. The positive-index triangular block and the wrap row in (2) give K_(N;H,J)=0, H>J, K_(N;H,J)=(-1)^H Q^[1+H(H+1)/2] [J choose H]_Q, H<=J. (4) This is an identity of actual original clock contributions, not an arbitrary inserted coefficient. For J<d it follows by multiplying T_(i(H),1), T_(i(J),i(H)) and T_(0,i(J)) and the factor Q^(-1). For J=d it follows from [d choose H]_Q=(-1)^H Q^[-H(H+1)/2], which is exact factorial reflection. This also includes H=J=d and the absorbing wrap state zero. There is no excluded parity or prime level and no division by F_N. ## 2. The same current after all charged full-block reductions The source of (4) is also visible in the [whole charged bridge coefficient](actual_global_charged_bridge_flow.md). After its three full contractions and one loop extraction, put X,Y for the two surviving anchors. Up to the explicitly retained unit root phases its clock sector is (Q^(-J);Q)_J [X^d Y^(d-J)] B_(d-H)(Y,X;Q) B_H(X,Y;Q^(J+1)) B_(d-J)(X,Y;Q^(H+J+1)), (5) where B_L(U,V;a)=product_(r<L)(U-Q^r a V). The two parallel X-to-Y intervals concatenate to length d+H-J. If H>J this contains a FULL N-orbit, hence vanishes in the actual nilpotent source X^N=Y^N=0. This recovers the exact support condition in (4). If H<=J, the degree-complement identity at charge d fuses the two remaining edges. Its binomial is [d-H choose J-H]_Q. Its last loop has scalar (Q^(J+1);Q)_(d-J)=N/F_J, while the first loop in (5) has modulus |F_J|. Therefore the COMPLETE charged coefficient has modulus N |[J choose H]_Q|. (6) The N is canceled by the original single exterior 1/N. The other original W_h, kappa, pivot, framing and normalization factors are retained; in this alternating singleton-bridge diagram they have unit modulus, up to the common tame source line. Thus the large sector survives the existing full-block/zero-charge/loop reduction. Equation (4) independently supplies its exact normalized phase. ## 3. Two successive macroscopic cancellations Choose H=floor(N/3), J=floor(2N/3). The uniform actual factorial estimate gives log |[J choose H]_Q| =N[v_3/pi]+O(log N)>0, (7) where v_3 is the regular ideal tetrahedron volume. Indeed, with I(s)=integral_0^s log|2sin(pi*t)| dt, the rate is I(2/3)-2I(1/3)=v_3/pi. This is the figure-eight volume rate, despite the present closed word being the trefoil, whose volume is zero. No figure-eight asymptotic theorem is a premise of (7). The FIRST coherent sum is itself an exact general q-binomial identity inside this actual source: sum_(H=0)^J K_(N;H,J)=Q F_J, F_J=(Q;Q)_J. (8) Use the finite q-binomial theorem with argument Q. This collapses the entire H current before estimation. It lowers its maximal rate, but does not make it polynomial: at J=floor(5N/6), log |F_J|=N[v_3/(2pi)]+O(log N)>0. (9) Thus even the partially summed current in (8) cannot be assigned the closed knot's zero regulator or dropped as a small boundary. The complete original scalar is exactly K_N=Q sum_(J=0)^d F_J. (10) The last sum has polynomial size. This follows independently from the already derived ACTUAL spectral-jet closing functional, not a named torus-knot asymptotic. Write its normalized crossing as r_N. At double nodes c=q^a+q^(-a), a odd, 0<a<N, it obeys r_N(c)=nu, |nu|=1, r_N'(c)/nu=-(N-a)/[2(q^a-q^(-a))]. The original pivotal functional is Phi(f)=-sum_double [c f(c)+(c^2-4)f'(c)] + one simple-node value if N is odd. For f=r_N^3, each first term has modulus at most 2 and each derivative term at most 3N, because c^2-4=(q^a-q^(-a))^2. The possible simple-node term has modulus one. The full writhe factor is (-q)^3, of modulus one. Hence, at EVERY level, |K_N|<=3N^2. (11) All node derivatives and the original pivotal source are retained in this bound. These formulas were independently proved from the finite R and its generic tensor specialization in [the spectral source note](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md). They do not rely on semisimplicity at the root. ## 4. Consequence for the next source-specific operation The first fusion (8) is constructive and exact, but a second macroscopic cancellation is still needed. A bound on individual fixed-h charged coefficients, or even on the first fused current at each J, cannot equal the closed knot regulator. Those currents are not separately honest closed-knot representation periods. The new physical-face outward estimates can control their actual endpoint continuations; they do not remove the internal coherent sum exhibited by (8)--(11). A proposed broad source fusion must retain and use that final clock connection, rather than fixing the clocks and then applying a knot-volume bound. This is an explicit failure of that sectorwise route, not a no-go for phase-aware fusion of the entire original source or the volume conjecture. No arbitrary consecutive-run or arbitrary-width positive-kernel extension is claimed here. The theorem is restricted to the actual source and exact current proved above. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_overclock_sector_obstruction.py) checks every sector against the literal original crossing, both coherent sums, the original spectral normalization, the fully reduced charged coefficients and the displayed exponential rates.

title: The full physical pair commutant, true box rotation, and its marked trace
text: # The full physical pair commutant, true box rotation, and its marked trace 29 October 2026. Every endomorphism commuting with the ORIGINAL two-head E,F,K action is a polynomial in its Casimir, at EVERY level N>=2. No generic semisimplicity or omission of projective normals is needed. The literal bent pretzel boxes remain in this full algebra. Their original source is one explicitly weighted Hermite-Casimir period. This is a finite exact reduction, not a volume or asymptotic theorem. ## 1. The actual module and a generating middle weight Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, rho=q-q^(-1). On the original balanced physical V_N use E=Ecal: E|a>=(Q^(-a)-1)|a-1>, F|a>=(1-Q^(a+1))|a+1>, K|a>=x Q^(-a)|a>, 0<=a<=d, with outside-basis arrows omitted. The actual pair coproduct is \[ E_t=E_1K_2+E_2,\qquad F_t=F_1+K_1^{-1}F_2, \qquad K_t=K_1K_2, \qquad\Omega=F_tE_t+qK_t+q^{-1}K_t^{-1}. \tag{1} \] Let W_T have the physical basis |a,T-a>, max(0,T-d)<=a<=min(d,T). The K_t eigenvalue there is x^2Q^(-T)=Q^(d-T). Its eigenvalue ONE occurs ONLY on W_d: the other possible degrees d+N and d-N lie outside [0,2d]. Thus an arbitrary E_t,F_t,K_t intertwiner preserves W_d, even if integer-degree preservation was not assumed. The following surjections are literal bidiagonal matrix facts: \[ E_t:W_{T+1}\twoheadrightarrow W_T\quad(0\leq T<d), \qquad F_t:W_T\twoheadrightarrow W_{T+1}\quad(d\leq T<2d). \tag{2} \] For the first use domain columns a=0,...,T and target rows a=0,...,T. The second-head E entry has nonzero diagonal Q^(-(T+1-a))-1; the other E entry is strictly off that diagonal. For the second use source a=T-d,...,d-1 and target a+1. The first-head F entry has diagonal 1-Q^(a+1), all nonzero, and the second-head term is off diagonal. These prove the two maximal ranks, including every composite and even N. Consequently \[ V_N\otimes V_N =\sum_{r=0}^d E_t^r W_d+\sum_{r=1}^d F_t^r W_d. \tag{3} \] This is generation by a specified physical weight space, not a claim that some abstract projective generator exists. ## 2. Exact commutant theorem, with all Jordan derivatives retained The middle block J=Omega|_(W_d) is the original complex symmetric tridiagonal matrix, with offdiagonal J[a,a+1]=J[a+1,a]=-(1-Q^(a+1))^2, 0<=a<d. All these entries are nonzero. In the vectors e_0,J e_0,...,J^d e_0, the k-th vector has last possible nonzero component k, equal to the nonzero product of the first k offdiagonals. They are a basis. Hence any X_d commuting with J is a UNIQUE polynomial f(J), deg f<N: choose f by X_de_0=f(J)e_0 and commute with J on this cyclic basis. Now let X commute with E_t,F_t,K_t. It preserves W_d by section 1 and commutes with Omega. Choose that f and put Y=X-f(Omega). Then Y annihilates W_d and commutes with E_t,F_t. Equation (3) forces Y=0 on the ENTIRE pair. We have therefore proved \[ \boxed{\operatorname{End}_{E_t,F_t,K_t}(V_N\otimes V_N) =\mathbb C[\Omega],\qquad \dim\mathbb C[\Omega]=N.} \tag{4} \] It follows in particular that every such endomorphism preserves full integer degree and is complex symmetric in the original pair basis. The actual Casimir is symmetric on every physical block. The familiar complete characteristic polynomial can also be recovered without a representation-theoretic endomorphism assertion: \[ P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2 =\prod_{j=0}^{d}(z-c_j),\qquad c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1}. \tag{5} \] For example continue the explicit highest-weight N-module in q; its generic pair highest weights 2d-2j give these limiting middle-block eigenvalues. The middle characteristic polynomial is (5). The cyclic basis makes it also the minimal polynomial, and (3) propagates its vanishing to the full pair. Alternatively its original continuant recurrence gives the same polynomial. Thus the only simple root is -2 for odd N; every other distinct root is DOUBLE. Equality (4) is the full Hermite algebra C[z]/P_N, not the algebra of values on its distinct roots. In particular projective first derivatives survive. ## 3. Literal turn rotation agrees with the charge-block formula Keep the actual pair turns, with their ORIGINAL scalars: p_ab=N x^(-b) delta_(a+b,d), ell_ab=x^a/N delta_(a+b,d). They are the original invariant cup and cap; E_t p=F_t p=0, K_t p=p and the corresponding cap identities follow directly from their displayed entries. They obey the two snake identities. For an actual Hopf box B, define its genuine bend by \[ \mathcal R(B)=(I^{\otimes2}\otimes\ell) (I\otimes B\otimes I) (p\otimes I^{\otimes2}). \tag{6} \] Composition of the just specified intertwining matrices makes this an E_t,F_t,K_t intertwiner. The cup adds integer degree d and the cap removes d. No separate quantum-group covariance hypothesis on an arbitrarily framed head is used. Direct contraction gives \[ \mathcal R(B)_{(a,b);(c,e)} =x^{a-e} B_{(b,d-e);(d-a,c)}. \tag{7} \] By (4) the original B is symmetric. Its degree support and a+b=c+e turn (7) into the concrete source-normalized rotated box \[ \boxed{(Z_B)_{(a,b);(c,e)} =x^{c-b-d}B_{(d-a,c);(b,d-e)},\qquad Z_B=x^{-d}\mathcal R(B)\in\mathbb C[\Omega].} \tag{8} \] The scalar x^(-d) is retained; it is part of the source port convention. Both original N factors cancel in (6). Formula (8) is injective as a reshuffling of all four indices, so it is a linear automorphism of the N-dimensional algebra (4). It is NOT an algebra homomorphism. For example \[ Z_I=x^{-d}p\ell,\qquad Z_{R^{-1}}=x^{-d}R. \tag{9} \] For the second identity use the literal original inverse R^(-1)=P conjugate(R) P and factorial reflection F_(d-a)=N(-1)^a Q^(a(a+1)/2)/F_a. After these substitutions the factorial ratio is exactly the original positive crossing ratio. Writing k=a-e=c-b, the residual Q exponent, before reducing modulo N, is b(e+1)-(b+k)N. The remaining Cartan/x factors use kappa^2=x^d and x^2=Q^(-1), giving precisely (9), without a parity or normalization exception. In the pretzel notation T=d+h, I_h=[max(0,h),min(d,d+h)], put S_h=diag_(a in I_h)x^a and let P_h reverse a to T-a. For the literal transfer M_B in the [original all-width source](actual_odd_pretzel_augmented_transfer_source.md), equation (8) says EXACTLY \[ Z_B|_{W_{d+h}}=P_hS_hM_B^hS_h^{-1}P_h. \tag{10} \] This fixes the true turn conjugation rather than identifying a reshuffled positive tensor with a physical crossing by analogy. The same four-index formula also supplies its exact inverse: \[ Z_{Z_B}=x^{-2d}B. \tag{10a} \] Indeed the two exponents in the composition add to -2d and all four original indices return. Consequently Z_R=x^(-d)R^(-1) and Z_(p ell)=x^(-d)I as well. These are coherent full-Hermite Fourier identities; the rotation is still not multiplicative. ## 4. The ORIGINAL fixed-root trace is an explicit Hermite period Let g=K^(1-N) be the ORIGINAL physical pivot and define \[ \phi(f)=\frac1N\operatorname{Tr}_{V_N\otimes V_N} [(I\otimes g)f(\Omega)]. \tag{11} \] At this root K^N=(-1)^d I, hence g=(-1)^d K EXACTLY. For each distinct double node c in (5), retain both f(c) and f'(c). Then \[ \boxed{\phi(f)=(-1)^d\sum_{c\ {\rm double}} \{(4-c^2)f'(c)-c f(c)\} +\mathbf1_{N\ {\rm odd}}f(-2).} \tag{12} \] Here is an independent finite-matrix derivation, including its germ scope. Use a generic variable z near q and the explicit ordinary highest-weight N-module with K_a=z^d z^(-2a), F_a=1-z^(2a+2), and E_a=z^(-N)-z^N z^(-2a), missing endpoints omitted. It specializes to the original module. Its K-pivotal partial trace of f(Omega_z) is a scalar C(z) I. This follows directly from the coproduct: tracing [f(Omega_z),E_1K_2+E_2]=0 over head2 yields [C,E_1]=0; the F equation, K conservation and cyclicity of the head2 trace yield [C,F_1]=0. Distinct K weights and nonzero internal F entries make the partial trace scalar. No generic Schur assertion at the root is used. Explicitly K conservation gives A K_1^(-1)=K_1^(-1)K_2^(-1) A K_2 for A=f(Omega_z), so Tr_2 K_2[A,K_1^(-1)F_2] =K_1^(-1) Tr_2(A K_2F_2-K_2F_2 A)=0. Tracing the F coproduct commutator now gives [C,F_1]=0 directly. For generic z, solve the bidiagonal highest-weight equations and take their F descendants. They give one summand of highest weight 2d-2j for each j=0,...,d; their dimensions sum to N^2 and their distinct generic Casimirs prove independence. Their K traces are [2d-2j+1]_z. Taking one further K trace therefore gives \[ C(z)=\frac{\sum_{j=0}^d[2N-1-2j]_z f(z^{2N-1-2j}+z^{-2N+1+2j})}{[N]_z}. \tag{13} \] The actual finite matrices make C(z) regular at z=q. Keep f fixed and differentiate this removable ratio in log z. The denominator derivative is -2N/rho. At a pair with r=2j+1 and m=2N-r, the dimension weights cancel at the root; their derivatives sum to 2Nc/rho. The sum of weight times the node derivative is 2N(c^2-4)/rho. Their ratio is (4-c^2)f'(c)-cf(c). At the odd self-paired m=N, the removable ratio contributes f(-2). Finally multiply by (-1)^d to replace K by the ACTUAL fixed-root g. For odd N this sign is one. This proves (12). This use of a generic K trace COMPUTES A FIXED-ROOT FUNCTIONAL. It does NOT differentiate the original whole q-dependent source g(z)=K(z)^(1-N), and does not identify that source germ with a generic K-pivotal germ. Any such q-normal-jet assertion requires its own pivot derivative. It is unnecessary for (11)--(12). In particular phi(1)=0, phi(L_N)=N^2 and phi(R)=kappa x^(-d), with the actual crossing and auxiliary-circle normalizations. Also phi(p ell)=1. The trace weights in (12) have only polynomial size: \[ |\phi(f)|\leq (N+1)\max_c|f(c)|+2N\max_{c\ {\rm double}}|f'(c)|. \tag{14} \] There is no exponentially costly hidden source conversion in this period. This does not control the actual rotated nodal values or their phases for a given family of boxes. There is a useful exact endpoint form of the SAME functional. If r_f is the degree-at-most-d remainder of f modulo P_N, then \[ \boxed{\phi(f)=(-1)^dN^2[z^d]r_f(z) =(f(J))_{0,d},\qquad J=\Omega|_{W_d}.} \tag{14a} \] To see the coefficient identity directly, at a double c the factor Q_c=P_N/(z-c)^2 has Q_c(c)=N^2/(4-c^2), Q_c'(c)/Q_c(c)=c/(4-c^2), as follows by differentiating the elementary Chebyshev equation. Thus the residues of f/P_N, multiplied by (-1)^d N^2, are exactly (12). At odd N, P_N'(-2)=N^2 supplies the simple-node term. Their sum for the proper fraction r_f/P_N is its coefficient of z^(-1) at infinity, namely [z^d]r_f. Finally the tridiagonal path from 0 to d has length at least d, and its sole length-d coefficient is product_(a=1)^d[-(1-Q^a)^2]=(-1)^d N^2. This proves the last identity in (14a). It is the original selected endpoint matrix element; it is not a positive trace or permission to select only one logarithmic/Fourier winding of a residue formula. ## 5. All-width pretzel reduction, including the original mark The original source theorem gives the transfer trace with D_h=diag x^(2a). Under (10), P_h D_h P_h=x^d (I tensor g)|_(W_(d+h)). Conjugating the PRODUCT of all transfers by the SAME S_h,P_h and retaining its original prefactor x^((s-1)d)/N proves \[ \boxed{\mathcal A_{s,N}(B_1,\ldots,B_s) =x^{sd}\phi(Z_{B_1}\cdots Z_{B_s}).} \tag{15} \] This uses every h=-d,...,d and the unrestricted original marked row until the already proved whole-degree restriction. Its original external chi_N is multiplied afterwards without modification. There are two convenient normalization conventions for this same rotation. For the unscaled genuine quarter-turn mathscrR(B)=x^d Z_B, equation (15) is equivalently phi(product_i mathscrR(B_i)), with NO external x phase. The explicit polynomial z_N in the [complete-base calculation](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md) uses this unscaled mathscrR convention. Thus its source-normalized Z_B polynomial here is x^(-d)z_N. These scalar conventions must not be mixed. Writing Z_(B_i)=z_i(Omega), (12) makes (15) an explicit finite sum: at each double c, its derivative is sum_i z_i'(c) product_(k!=i) z_k(c), alongside the value product; the odd simple node contributes its full product. Thus all s boxes couple through the same actual Casimir channel, with the original normal source retained. No independent summation of unphysical channel maxima, deletion of a zero value's derivative, or assumed positive pairing is involved. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.py) uses original finite generators to check the full E/F/K commutant, the middle cyclic basis and both generating surjections, literal rotations of a complete polynomial basis, source-normalized crossing rotation, fixed-root trace on values AND derivatives, and the marked all-width product identity. The general geometric growth estimate for the rotated channel packets remains a separate task.

title: Faithful parabolic cap certificates on the complete original character support
text: # Faithful parabolic cap certificates on the complete original character support 29 October 2026. The complete three-head source cubic has an elementary finite representation atlas, including its pair-trace endpoints. Its source line imposes the LITERAL cap relation on every irreducible point. At larger plat width a pair trace and a total trace do not suffice. A finite list of cubic witness traces, inherited from the original matrix cap relation, is faithful on the irreducible locus. Nilpotent normal directions are explicitly distinguished from this statement about the reduced geometric support. There is also a uniform bounded-representative construction from bounded pair traces. For a one-component knot it gives an elementary quantitative separation from the all-parabolic reducible character. These are genuine geometric support/compactness results. They do not estimate the quantum Racah transport or the positive word energy. ## 1. Unipotent trace tests All matrices below lie in SL2(C). Write a trace-two unipotent as mu=I+N, where tr N=0 and N^2=0. A nonzero N has rank one and its image equals its kernel, the fixed flag of mu. For two NONCENTRAL trace-two unipotents, Tr(mu nu)=2 iff they have the same fixed flag. (1) Indeed N=u phi, M=v psi with phi(u)=psi(v)=0. The extra trace is phi(v)psi(u). In dimension two either factor vanishes precisely when the two fixed lines agree. Central matrices are included separately. Suppose mu_1,mu_2,mu_3 have trace two and Tr(mu_2 mu_1)=2, Tr(mu_3 mu_2 mu_1)=2. (2) If their tuple is irreducible, then mu_2 mu_1=I. To prove this, put P=mu_2 mu_1. If P!=I, (1) implies that mu_1,mu_2 and P share one fixed flag, also when one input is central. P is a noncentral trace-two unipotent. The second equation in (2), together with (1), makes mu_3 share that flag or be central. The tuple is reducible, a contradiction. This proof has no affine-position or finite shear assumption on an individual flag. ## 2. The actual three-head cubic, and both original caps For the original complete heads set mu_i=-H_i, so Tr mu_i=2. The full source Hom module has D=Tr(H_3H_2H_1)=-2, hence Tr(mu_3mu_2mu_1)=2. Write A=Tr(mu_2mu_1), B=Tr(mu_3mu_2), C=Tr(mu_3mu_1), X=A-2, Y=B-2, Z=C-2, S=X+Y+Z. The [actual character cubic](actual_adjacent_twist_character_and_source.md) is F(X,Y,Z)=S^2+XYZ=0. (3) Every finite point except the origin has an explicit irreducible representative. On X!=0 use mu_1=[[1,1],[0,1]], mu_2=[[1,0],[X,1]], mu_3=[[1+S/X,Y/X],[Z,1-S/X]]. (4) Its determinant minus one is -F/X^2, its trace is two, its pair traces are exactly A,B,C, and the triple trace is exactly two. The first two flags are distinct. Cyclically permuting the meridians supplies the other pair-coordinate charts and preserves the triple trace. The only missing point is X=Y=Z=0: all pair traces are two, so (1) makes every such tuple reducible. This proves the finite atlas without assuming a character variety reconstruction theorem. The actual initial ordinary-cup source has A=2. On the irreducible locus (2) therefore gives mu_2mu_1=I. Its reduced source line is explicitly (A,B,C)=(2,2-t,2+t), t!=0, mu_1=[[1,1],[0,1]], mu_2=mu_1^(-1), mu_3=[[1,0],[t,1]]. (5) At X=0 equation (3) is (Y+Z)^2=0. The square is important: the reduced line is honest inverse-pair geometry, while its polarization has a quadratic normal ramification. It is not permission to remove the actual c_0 Hermite derivative source. Every actual Hurwitz word preserves the ordered total product mu_3mu_2mu_1 and irreducibility. Applying (2) at both ends shows: an irreducible character on the initial A=2 source and final A=2 source has BOTH literal inverse-pair caps. Preservation of the total product then matches the remaining meridian as a matrix, not merely by its trace. Following the actual crossing assignments and these cap identifications therefore gives an honest representation of that original one-component cup--braid--cap knot. This applies to the complete source support, not just its geometric branch. Finite intermediate pair traces A=+/-2 or B=+/-2 do not invalidate (4)--(5): another nonzero pair coordinate supplies a chart, unless the entire character is reducible. This statement is about finite characters, not about ignoring a polar spectral-coordinate Jacobian. ## 3. A faithful witness certificate at arbitrary plat width For a tuple mu_1,...,mu_b of trace-two unipotents and a selected cap pair, put P=mu_v mu_u. On the irreducible locus the following finite trace conditions are EQUIVALENT to the literal matrix relation P=I: Tr P=2, Tr(mu_k P)=Tr mu_k=2, every k=1,...,b. (6) The reverse implication is immediate. For the forward implication, if P!=I it is a noncentral unipotent. Every noncentral mu_k shares its fixed flag by (1), making the whole tuple reducible. This proves the equivalence at arbitrary fixed width, with no chosen flag chart. These are genuine source witnesses, not new favorable constraints. The exact original cup obeys the framed matrix identity (H_v H_u-I)p=0, as proved in [the original plat source theorem](actual_plat_cup_cap_gram_support.md).
