This also fixes the sign convention and normalization in (3). ## 2. The algebraic data selected by the source maximum Use the notation of the algebraic maximum theorem. The compact rational polytope carries positive rational weights w_j and rational affine ideal-angle triples alpha_j. Let F be its smallest face containing all maxima. On F discard the atoms which are identically flat, and call the remaining set I. Those positive atoms have the SAME angle triples at every maximum. After removing their common rational flat kernel, choose rational coordinates y_l in which the positive angles read alpha_jr=a_jr+sum_l b_jrl y_l, a_jr,b_jrl in Q. The proved algebraicity theorem supplies an optimum y_* for which the phases, sine values and positive shapes are algebraic. More explicitly choose a positive integer B clearing the b denominators, and put u_l=exp(pi i y_*l/B), t_jr=exp(pi i alpha_jr), s_jr=2sin(pi alpha_jr)>0. Then t_jr=eta_jr product_l u_l^(B b_jrl), eta_jr=exp(pi i a_jr), (4) where eta_jr is a root of unity. Choose K to contain these finitely many algebraic numbers and their conjugates. It is a finite number field stable under the given complex conjugation. No assertion that K is the trace field of a manifold is being made. All positive angles are interior in their simplices at a relative- interior maximizer of F. Constrained stationarity in EVERY quotient tangent y_l gives sum_(j in I,r) w_j b_jrl log s_jr=0. (5) For an integer C clearing the rational exponents, (5) gives the exact algebraic relation product_(j,r) s_jr^(C w_j b_jrl)=1. (6) There is no winding ambiguity here: the s_jr are positive real numbers, and (6) is derived from the selected real maximum. Its image in U_K, divided by the nonzero rational C, is sum_(j,r) w_j b_jrl ell(s_jr)=0. (7) Equations (4) and (7), not merely the algebraicity of the shapes, are the reason the regulator has a Bloch-cycle lift. ## 3. The antisymmetric shape boundary For a positive angle triple (a,b,c), a+b+c=1, set t_a=exp(pi i a), s_a=2sin(pi a), and cyclically, z=t_a s_b/s_c. The Euclidean angle sine rule, or an elementary sine identity, gives 1-z=t_b^-1 s_a/s_c. (8) For the elementary check multiply (8) by sin(pi c): it says sin(pi c)=exp(pi i a)sin(pi b)+exp(-pi i b)sin(pi a). The imaginary parts cancel and the real part is sin(pi(a+b)), which equals sin(pi c). In particular Im z>0 and z has the prescribed ordered ideal angles. Write T_r=ell(t_r), S_r=ell(s_r). Since s_r is positive real, conjugation fixes S_r and sends T_r to -T_r. Also T_a+T_b+T_c=ell(-1)=0 in U_K. Using (8) to expand both shape boundaries therefore gives the exact identity delta([z]-[bar z]) =2(T_a wedge S_a+T_b wedge S_b+T_c wedge S_c). (9) For clarity, the individual unsymmetrized expansion is delta[z]=-T_a wedge T_b +T_a wedge(S_a-S_c)+T_b wedge(S_b-S_c) +S_b wedge S_a-S_b wedge S_c-S_c wedge S_a. The phase-phase and sine-sine terms are unchanged by conjugation; only the two middle phase-sine terms change sign. Their difference is (9). Thus the proof does not assume that the unsymmetrized sum of positive shape symbols already has zero boundary. ## 4. Stationarity kills the complete rational boundary Define the source class beta=(1/2) sum_(j in I) w_j([z_j]-[bar z_j]) in P(K)_Q. (10) By (4), after torsion has been removed, T_jr=B sum_l b_jrl U_l, U_l=ell(u_l). Equations (9) and (7) now give delta beta =sum_(j,r) w_j T_jr wedge S_jr =B sum_l U_l wedge (sum_(j,r) w_j b_jrl S_jr) =0. (11) Hence beta is in B(K)_Q. It is anti-invariant under complex conjugation and its regulator is EXACTLY R_K(beta)=sum_(j in I) w_j D(z_j)=max_P V. (12) There is no undetermined additive multiple of a volume constant in (12): the symbols use their actual positive shapes and the regulator uses actual ideal-tetrahedron volume. If there are no positive atoms, beta=0 and the maximum is zero. If there are no quotient tangent variables, (4) makes every T_jr zero and the same proof works directly. This construction includes rational weights and affine constants of arbitrary denominators. Passing to Q coefficients removes the roots of unity in (4), the factor ell(-1) in (9), and the cleared exponent in (6). The argument does NOT remove that torsion integrally. No integral K-theory, integral Bloch boundary, or integral peripheral normalization is asserted. The ordered positive triples are uniquely selected by the maximum, even when some original wire coordinates are free. Thus (10) does not depend on choosing values for those flat coordinates. It is unchanged as a displayed symbol expression by a rational change of quotient coordinates; the coordinates are used to prove (11), not to define its shapes. There is also an elementary descent which removes the auxiliary phase field. Put F_shape=Q(z_j,bar z_j : j in I) subset K. The displayed expression beta already belongs to P(F_shape)_Q. The inclusion F_shape^times -> K^times is injective; tensoring with Q preserves that injection. Exterior squares of vector spaces preserve injections as well (extend a basis of the smaller space to a basis of the larger one). Thus exterior^2 U_(F_shape) -> exterior^2 U_K is injective. The image of delta beta is zero by (11), so its boundary was zero over F_shape itself. Consequently beta belongs to B(F_shape)_Q. This descent uses neither a presumed injection of Bloch groups nor a Galois or Hilbert-90 theorem. The phase coordinates merely provide a finite algebraic field in which the boundary calculation is transparent. For an empty atom list the class is zero over Q. ## 5. The full original quantum limit is a Bloch regulator For EVERY fixed robust actual positive Conway expression E, the [whole-source variational theorem](actual_positive_conway_variational_limit.md) and the algebraic maximum theorem yield, along all levels and both parities, lim_(N -> infinity) (2pi/N)log Z_(E,N) =2 max_(P_E) V_E =R_(F_shape)(B_E), B_E=sum_(j in I_E)([z_j]-[bar z_j]) in B(F_shape)_Q. (13) The weights here are all one and B_E=2 beta. Although its displayed symbol expression has integer coefficients, its proved zero-boundary statement is rational; possible integral torsion has not been checked. Z_(E,N) is the entire original source, with all colors and repeated-root normal directions retained. The class is selected by that exact source's positive variational problem, not by choosing an arbitrary branch of an A-polynomial. The [cap-sum reduction](actual_conway_cap_sum_reduction.md) is compatible with this construction. At a cap-closed product, the maximizing polytope is a Cartesian product, its final gate is flat, and the positive atom list is the union of the two lists. Thus, in a common number field, B_(cap FG)=B_(cap F)+B_(cap G). This agrees with the literal componentwise connected sum and exact source multiplication. It also shows why a nonzero Bloch regulator alone cannot certify a single complete hyperbolic complement. ## 6. The remaining geometric question is now more precise We have an actual source-selected RATIONAL BLOCH CLASS, and its regulator is the full quantum limit in (13). What is still missing for a broad hyperbolic-knot theorem is a proof that this regulator is the volume of the actual complement, for example by identifying the class with its marked geometric Bloch class or by supplying a source-compatible complete gluing certificate with the same volume. The vanishing in (11) is algebraic and global, but it is not a face pairing, an edge winding count, a cusp completeness equation, or a fundamental-class degree computation. It also does not identify K with a trace field, construct a generic-meridian A-torsor, or show that a formal source cycle is the preferred geometric representation. Those statements must not be inferred from the word "Bloch". Audit: [formal wedge and stationarity certificates](../experiments/audit_actual_positive_source_bloch_regulator.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_positive_source_bloch_regulator_results.json). The identities are uniform symbolic exterior-algebra calculations; finite numerical volumes are not used in their proof. Independent internal review: the primary agent read the full proof, independently expanded the conjugate-shape boundary and stationarity factorization, checked the five-term differential normalization and rational field scope, and replayed the symbolic audit successfully. The additional descent to the conjugation-stable shape field was checked separately: it uses exterior-square injectivity, not an unproved assertion that Bloch groups inject under field extension. The review leaves the marked manifold-class comparison open.

title: A uniform all-index bound for the actual coherent pretzel inner packet
text: # A uniform all-index bound for the actual coherent pretzel inner packet 29 October 2026. The exact original-source Ward recurrence, together with its proved high-index source anchor, bounds EVERY remaining inner index. The estimate retains both classical characteristic branches, every endpoint factorial and both parities. Its prefactor is polynomial in N, uniformly even at r=0. No rational first-order factorization or choice of a single growing branch is assumed. ## 1. Literal selected packet and theorem Use N>=2, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, M=floor((N-1)/2), and F_a=(Q;Q)_a. In the EXACT original rotated box, reversing the two finite sums gives the inner packet \[ A_r=\sum_{v=r}^M Q^{-vr}\frac{F_{2v}}{F_v^3F_{v-r}}, \qquad D_r=Q^{-r^2}\frac{F_{2r}}{F_r^3}, \qquad U_r=A_r/D_r,\quad 0\leq r\leq M. \tag{1} \] All D_r are nonzero, including r=0 and r=M. These are the same packets in the [actual coherent inner elimination theorem](actual_pretzel_coherent_inner_gauss_elimination.md), not an arbitrary solution of their recurrence. That finite source transformation proves, at BOTH parities, \[ |U_r|\leq2N,\qquad \lceil N/4\rceil\leq r\leq M. \tag{2} \] Only this upper bound is needed here; its nonzero amplitude and phase are not substituted into a different index range. The same theorem proves the full selected Ward equation, with Y=Q^r, \[ QY^2(1-Q^2Y)A_{r+2} +Y(2Q^3Y^2+Q+1)A_{r+1} -Q(QY+1)(QY^2-1)A_r=0, \tag{3} \] and actual endpoints A_M=D_M, A_(M+1)=0. Define the continuous nonnegative envelope \[ E(u)=\begin{cases} \displaystyle\frac2\pi\int_u^{\pi/4}\log\cot v\,dv, &0\leq u\leq\pi/4,\\ 0, &\pi/4\leq u\leq\pi/2. \end{cases} \tag{4} \] The integral is finite at zero. The explicit uniform bound is \[ \boxed{|A_r|\leq8e^{128}N^{129}|D_r| \exp\{N E(\pi r/N)\}, \quad N\geq12,\quad0\leq r\leq M.} \tag{5} \] The constants are deliberately coarse and independent of N,r. In particular the exponential error after this full two-branch envelope is uniformly o(N). This is a bound for the literal finite packet BEFORE the original outer Newton sum and Hermite source; no boundary packet or original current has been dropped. ## 2. Exact factorial cancellation in the normalized recurrence The adjacent diagonal ratio is \[ \frac{D_{r+1}}{D_r} =Q^{-1}Y^{-2}\frac{(1-QY^2)(1+QY)}{(1-QY)^2}. \tag{6} \] The factors 1-QY^2 and 1+QY are EXACTLY those in the backward coefficient of (3). Cancelling them algebraically, rather than estimating inverse factorials separately, gives \[ U_r=p_N(Y)U_{r+1}+q_N(Y)U_{r+2}, \tag{7} \] \[ p_N(Y)=-\frac{Q^{-2}Y^{-1}(2Q^3Y^2+Q+1)}{(1-QY)^2}, \quad q_N(Y)=-\frac{Q^{-4}Y^{-2}(1-Q^3Y^2)(1+Q^2Y)} {(1-QY)^2(1-Q^2Y)}. \tag{8} \] For r=M-1 the numerator of q_N vanishes at BOTH parities: 1-Q^(2M+1)=0 for odd N, or 1+Q^(M+1)=0 for even N. Thus (7) extends to that last step with any assigned U_(M+1), for example zero. This is an exact cancellation of the terminal factorial zero, not division by D_(M+1). The proof below initializes instead at two genuine high-index U values in (2), so it needs no choice of a value beyond M. ## 3. Shifted classical matrix and a globally conditioned frame Put R=ceil(N/4), delta=pi/N, and for 0<=r<R use Z=Q^(r+1)=exp(2iu), u=(r+1)delta. The shifted classical backward matrix is \[ T_0(u)=\begin{pmatrix}p_0&q_0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad p_0=-\frac{Z^{-1}(2Z^2+2)}{(1-Z)^2},\quad q_0=-\frac{Z^{-2}(1+Z)^2}{(1-Z)^2}. \tag{9} \] On the unit circle its eigenvalues are mu_1=-Z^(-1), mu_2=Z^(-1)c, c=cot(u)^2, rho(u)=max(1,c). They remain DISTINCT even where their moduli meet. Use the normalized right eigenvector matrix \[ V(u)=\left( \frac{(-Z^{-1},1)^{\mathsf T}}{\sqrt2}, \frac{(Z^{-1}c,1)^{\mathsf T}}{\sqrt{1+c^2}} \right). \tag{10} \] Its column correlation is (1-c)/sqrt(2(1+c^2)), whose modulus is at most1/sqrt2. Therefore, UNIFORMLY for 0<u<pi/2, \[ \|V(u)\|_2<\sqrt2,\qquad \|V(u)^{-1}\|_2<2, \qquad \|V'(u)\|_2\leq4. \tag{11} \] For the derivative, write the second column as (e^(-2iu)cos theta,sin theta), theta=atan(tan(u)^2). If t=tan u, then theta'=2t(1+t^2)/(1+t^4)<=2, since 1+t^4-t-t^3=(t-1)^2(t^2+t+1)>=0. Its squared derivative norm is at most8; the first column's is2. Thus the Frobenius bound is sqrt10<4. This controls the frame all the way toward u=0; there is no hidden exponentially ill-conditioned change of basis. ## 4. The exact matrix has only a harmonic RELATIVE error Let T_N(r) be the companion matrix from (7). In the shifted Z coordinate, its coefficients are \[ p_N=-\frac{Z^{-1}(2Z^2+1+Q^{-1})}{(1-Z)^2},\qquad q_N=-\frac{Q^{-2}Z^{-2}(1-QZ^2)(1+QZ)} {(1-Z)^2(1-QZ)}. \tag{12} \] For N>=12 and r<R, u<=pi/3 and u+delta<pi/2. In particular |1+Z|^2>=1 and |1-QZ|=2sin(u+delta)>=2sin u>=4(r+1)/N, |Q-1|<=2pi/N. The difference in p is exactly -Z^(-1)(Q^(-1)-1)/(1-Z)^2. For q use the elementary numerator identity \[ (1-QZ^2)(1+QZ)-(1+Z)^2(1-QZ) =(Q-1)Z(2+Z-QZ^2). \tag{13} \] Dividing by rho>=c=|q_0| gives the uniform estimates |p_N-p_0|/rho<=2pi/(r+1), |q_N-q_0|/rho<=6pi/(r+1). Hence \[ \|T_N(r)-T_0(u)\|_2\leq\frac{8\pi}{r+1}\rho(u). \tag{14} \] Large absolute entries near r=0 have NOT been called small. They are controlled relative to the full eigenvalue envelope, whose large second branch is kept. Combining (11), (14) and the step u->u+delta proves \[ \|V(u)^{-1}T_N(r)V(u+\delta)\|_2 \leq\rho(u)\left(1+\frac{128}{r+1}\right). \tag{15} \] Indeed the frame change contributes at most8pi/N; the error term contributes at most16sqrt2*pi/(r+1). Their sum is less than 128/(r+1). This argument uses a full operator-norm bound and therefore allows arbitrary mixing of the two characteristic branches; it does not posit adiabatic survival of either one. ## 5. Selected high-index boundary to all-index estimate Write X_r=(U_r,U_(r+1))^T and X_r=T_N(r)X_(r+1). For N>=12 both R and R+1 are within the high range in (2). Thus ||X_R||<=2sqrt2 N. Iterating (15), using (11) at both ends, gives \[ |U_r|\leq8N \prod_{j=r}^{R-1}\rho((j+1)\pi/N) \left(1+\frac{128}{j+1}\right). \tag{16} \] The second product is at most exp(128 H_N)<=e^128 N^128. The logarithm of the first is the RIGHT Riemann sum of the nonnegative decreasing function max(0,2log cot u). Even for r=0 it is bounded ABOVE by its finite improper integral: sum_(j=r)^(R-1) log rho((j+1)pi/N) <=(N/pi) integral_(pi*r/N)^(pi/4) 2log cot u du =N E(pi*r/N). This proves (5) for r<R. Equation (2) proves it for r>=R. The argument is uniform at all indices, with no epsilon-dependent unstated endpoint constants. In particular, after the existing uniform sine-factorial estimate for D_r is applied, the whole coherent inner packet has precisely the two-branch upper envelope. Its lower-index excess is E(u); it is NOT assumed to be zero. Whether the positive outer Newton profile absorbs that excess is a separate variational inequality. This theorem supplies the source-faithful estimate needed for that comparison; it does not alone prove augmented-base survival, a volume LOWER bound, or a filling theorem. ## 6. Validation The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_all_index_backward_envelope.py) checks the original finite sum, selected Ward boundaries, exact normalized recurrence and endpoint cancellation, both high-range anchors, shifted coefficient differences, uniformly conditioned moving frame and its one-step bound, and the full coherent all-index envelope at both parities. Tests never replace the selected solution by an arbitrary recurrence branch.

title: A varying-radius alias estimate lowers the proved width threshold to nine
text: # A varying-radius alias estimate lowers the proved width threshold to nine 29 October 2026. The original short RP band admits a stronger global bound when its TRUE sine-binomial coefficients and its varying monic spectral radius are kept together. The uniform rate is B_*=(1/pi) integral_0^(pi/2) log rho(u) du < 81/100, instead of the previous (1/2)log(4+sqrt(15)). This proves the ENTIRE original-color source gap for every fixed odd width s>=9. All color endpoints, the even middle color, and the original Hermite normal jets remain. The previously proved corridor/filling and geometric-completion arguments therefore apply unchanged at those widths. This does not remove every width restriction: s=3,5,7 remain outside the present global alias argument. No assertion for them is obtained by naming this positive envelope a sharp source asymptotic. ## 1. Keep the exact original short-band coefficients Use q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, s_a=|(Q;Q)_a| and the monic physical middle continuants p_l. The exact identity in [the original global alias theorem](actual_pretzel_global_alias_and_colored_source_gap.md) is (-1)^(N+h-1) P_(N,h)(z) =sum_(l=0)^(h-1) (-1)^l q^(3l^2+4l+1-2hl-h) [h+l choose 2l+1]_Q bar p_l(z). (1) It holds for EVERY 1<=h<=floor(N/2), including h=N/2 at even N. All Gaussian factorial indices are below N. The actual alias is R P_(N,h), not P alone and not a semisimple truncation. The monic recurrence has p_(l+1)=(z-D_l)p_l-a_(l-1)^2 p_(l-1), D_l=4qQ^l-q(1+Q)Q^(2l), a_(l-1)=-(1-Q^l)^2, (p_0,p_(-1))=(1,0). (2) The finite root phases in (1) are retained. Only after this exact identity will absolute values be taken. In particular no conjectural Laurent positivity or ordinary-color unitarity is needed. ## 2. Exact pointwise maximal frozen radius Freeze u=pi l/N in [0,pi/2]. After a unit phase change the two frozen roots obey lambda^2-d_z lambda+a^2=0, d_z=z exp(-2iu)-4+2exp(2iu), a=4sin(u)^2. (3) For z=-2 define t=sqrt(1+8sin(u)^2), rho(u)=(t+1)/2 * [2+sqrt((t+1)(3-t))]. (4) This is EXACTLY the larger root modulus in (3), not a numerical fit. For a derivation put y=1-cos(2u), so a=2y, d_(-2)=-4+4i sin(2u). Then |d_(-2)|^2=16(1+2y-y^2), |d_(-2)^2-4a^2|=16sqrt(1+4y). If the root moduli are rho and a^2/rho, their squared sum is (|d|^2+|d^2-4a^2|)/2. Solving this quadratic and taking its positive square root gives (4). Equivalently set t-1=2sin theta; then rho(u)=(1+sin theta+cos theta)^2, 0<=theta<=pi/2. In particular rho is continuous, positive, rho>=a, and 4<=rho<=3+2sqrt(2). It is the POINTWISE maximum over all real z in [-2,2]. Indeed at z=2 the roots both equal -a. For fixed a, a root of modulus r>=a makes d_z lie on the ellipse d=r exp(i theta)+(a^2/r) exp(-i theta). Its closed interior is exactly the region where both roots have modulus at most r. For r=rho(u), the z=-2 endpoint lies on the ellipse and the z=2 endpoint lies inside. Convexity covers their entire affine z-segment. The two endpoints u=0,pi/2 follow directly from (3); no inverse eigenframe is used there. ## 3. A uniform varying-product estimate for the actual polynomials Put I(v)=integral_0^v log rho(pi t) dt, 0<=v<=1/2. The exact companions of (2), divided at their l-th step by rho(pi l/N), converge uniformly to a bounded continuous family whose root moduli are at most one, uniformly for z in [-2,2]. Their coefficients have no singular root endpoint. The frozen-block Cayley--Hamilton argument therefore gives max_(z in[-2,2]) |p_l(z)| <=exp[N I(l/N)+epsilon_N N], max_(0<=l<=floor(N/2)) epsilon_N ->0. (5) For clarity this is an actual product bound, not an adiabatic claim. For a fixed block length L, the exact normalized block differs uniformly by o(1) from its frozen power. A bounded 2x2 matrix with root moduli at most one has ||B^L||<=CL by Cayley--Hamilton, also at a double root. First choose L to make log(CL)/L small, then N large, and concatenate blocks. Uniform continuity of log rho turns the scalar product of radii into N I(l/N)+o(N), uniformly in l. The initial vector is exactly (1,0). This proves (5) through BOTH index endpoints without a conditioned eigenvector factor. ## 4. The entire sine-binomial envelope has an exact global maximum Let J(x)=integral_0^x log(2sin(pi t)) dt, 0<=x<=1. The already proved UNIFORM factorial estimate gives, with alpha=h/N and beta=l/N, log |[h+l choose 2l+1]_Q| =N[J(alpha+beta)-J(2beta)-J(alpha-beta)]+O(log N). (6) The index shifts by one cost O(log N), uniformly even at zero and N-1. This estimate is applied only to actual indices below N. Combining (5),(6), the possible term rate in (1) is at most F(alpha,beta)=J(alpha+beta)-J(2beta)-J(alpha-beta)+I(beta), 0<=beta<=alpha<=1/2. (7) Its maximum is EXACTLY B_*=I(1/2). Here is an elementary proof. For 0<beta<alpha<1/2, partial_alpha F=log[sin pi(alpha+beta)/sin pi(alpha-beta)]>=0, because their difference is 2cos(pi alpha)sin(pi beta)>=0. Thus maximize first at alpha=1/2. At that boundary, d/d beta F(1/2,beta) =log[rho(pi beta)/(4sin(pi beta)^2)]>=0, using rho>=a in section2. Therefore the maximum occurs at (alpha,beta)=(1/2,1/2). Since J(0)=J(1)=0, its value is B_*. All boundary cases follow by continuity of J and I. No unsupported interior saddle or numerical optimization is being used. Sum the at most N terms in (1). The polynomial degree is h-1<=N/2; complex Markov on [-2,2] controls N^(-2) times its first derivative at every actual node with only the same fixed factor as before. The actual crossing R has faithful Hermite norm at most9/8. Hence limsup_N (1/N) log max_(1<=h<=floor(N/2)) ||R P_(N,h)||_H <= B_*. (8) Thus (8) retains ALL original source normal jets and the actual crossing. It is not a bound for an unrelated positive comparison model. ## 5. A finite rigorous upper certificate and the width-nine margin The bound B_*<81/100 has a direct finite interval-arithmetic certificate, described explicitly here so it is reproducible as a proof rather than as sampled evidence. In variable t in[1,3], put u(t)=asin sqrt((t^2-1)/8). For a rational interval [a,b] in[1,3], (t+1) is increasing and sqrt((t+1)(3-t)) is decreasing. Therefore rho(u(t)) <= K(a,b) =(b+1)/2 * [2+sqrt((a+1)(3-a))]. Divide [1,3] into512 equal rational intervals. This gives the EXACT analytical upper sum B_* <= (1/pi) sum_[a,b] [u(b)-u(a)] log K(a,b). (9) Outward-rounded Arb evaluation at100-bit precision encloses the right side in [0.80908894192172909372913834 +/- 5e-26] <81/100. Only a fixed finite sum of square roots, asin, log and pi is evaluated; no large-N experiment enters this certificate. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.py) reconstructs the upper sum and proves the strict comparison by its enclosing interval. For the complete augmented rate A_s=V_s/(2pi), put j_0=v_8/pi. Its exact alias margin is g_s=A_s-(s-1)j_0 =j_0-(2s/pi) integral_0^(pi/s) (pi/s-v)sec(v)dv. (10) For alpha=pi/s<1, cos v>=1-v^2/2 gives g_s >= j_0-pi/s -pi^3/[12s^3(1-pi^2/(2s^2))]. (11) Use pi<22/7 and the first32 alternating terms of G=sum_(k>=0)(-1)^k/(2k+1)^2 as a rational LOWER bound for Catalan's constant; j_0=4G/pi. At s=9 the resulting rational lower bound is greater than0.812633708, hence greater than13/16 and81/100. The loss in (11) decreases with s>=9. Consequently g_s>B_* for EVERY odd s>=9. (12) This strictly improves the previous threshold25. The same constants do not prove the condition at s=3,5,7. ## 6. Transfer to the ENTIRE actual source and the remaining widths Every original auxiliary color is already covered by the exact two-band identities: high colors are c_(N,h)+RP_(N,h), low colors are pure (-1)^N RP_(N,j), including even j=N/2. The global coherent core bound remains j_0, with a strict macroscopic-color contraction. Every term containing m>=1 aliases therefore has upper rate (s-m)j_0+mB_* <=(s-1)j_0+B_* < A_s for odd s>=9. The full value-plus-normal functional costs only a polynomial, and the fixed subset count2^s is harmless. The all-core term outside a fixed cusp corridor has its separately proved strict gap. This proves the SAME entire-color-cube source gap as the old global theorem at EVERY odd s>=9. All subsequent analytic inputs were already proved for every fixed odd s>=5: the exact even complex high-window packet, whole filling Fourier endpoint/current bounds, nonzero unit-charge sum, original normalization, and the actual geometric filling construction. Thus they transfer unchanged once their long-slope threshold is increased as necessary. The original full volume equality consequently extends to every fixed odd s>=9 with all independently sufficiently long fixed signed slopes. No width or slope is allowed to grow with N. For s=5 and7 the present phase-free per-alias margin test remains insufficient; at s=3 the old limiting margin is exactly zero and its local corridor alias estimate was also only proved for s>=5. Those are TWO distinct remaining gates. Extending the theorem there needs a stronger coherent alias/source estimate, not a changed declaration of the existing condition. No fabricated all-width conclusion is inferred from (8). ## 7. Why another constant improvement in this termwise route is insufficient The monic bound used above is exponentially sharp at the actual endpoint z=-2. This identifies exactly which ABSOLUTE-TERM step must be replaced to reach the remaining widths; it is not a claim that the full coherent alias P_h has this rate or that the whole source fails to cancel. For l=floor(N/2)-1 one has log|p_l(-2)|=N B_*+O(1). (13) Here is a direct uniform proof. Use tau=l/N and epsilon=1/N in the literal companion (2), and write it as T_epsilon(tau). Its leading eigenvalues lambda(tau),sigma(tau) can be chosen smoothly on the WHOLE closed interval[0,1/2], with lambda(0)=-4, sigma(0)=0, |lambda(tau)|=rho(pi tau)>=4, |sigma(tau)|<=|lambda(tau)|, |lambda(tau)-sigma(tau)|>=4. (14) The last inequality follows from the explicit discriminant in section2. There is no equality of the two eigenvalue moduli in the open interval: for u>0 and u<pi/2 the normalized d_(-2) has nonzero imaginary part, whereas two roots of equal modulus and positive real product would have real sum. Their moduli meet only at the terminal endpoint, where their eigenvalues remain distinct. Thus the branch starting at -4 is the dominant branch throughout; no hidden exchange of expanding channels is used. Take the uniformly invertible eigenframe S(tau)=[[lambda,sigma],[1,1]]. Taylor expansion of the explicit smooth companion gives S(tau+epsilon)^(-1)T_epsilon(tau)S(tau) =diag(lambda,sigma)+epsilon A(tau)+O(epsilon^2), with all coefficients and two derivatives uniformly bounded. An explicit bounded off-diagonal matrix X, determined by X_ij=-A_ij/(D_i-D_j), makes the near-identity change I+epsilon X diagonal through first order. The resulting matrix is diag(lambda+epsilon A_11,sigma+epsilon A_22)+O(epsilon^2). Divide each step by d_1=lambda+epsilon A_11. Its normalized form is diag(1,r_tau)+O(epsilon^2), with |r_tau|<=1+Cepsilon. All normalized products therefore have uniformly bounded norm. The original initial vector (p_0,p_(-1))=(1,0) has first eigen-coordinate -1/4+O(epsilon). At the first step the second coordinate is O(epsilon), because sigma(0)=0. Over at most N/2 steps the O(epsilon^2) residual changes the first coordinate by O(epsilon), and keeps the second O(epsilon). The first physical coordinate consequently has a uniformly nonzero bounded prefactor times product d_1. Finally log|product d_1|=sum_j log rho(pi j/N)+O(1) =N I(l/N)+O(1). This proves (13), including the endpoint of equal moduli without an inverse eigenvalue-modulus gap. The proof applies equally to bar p_l. Now choose the ACTUAL h=floor(N/2) and the top term l=h-1 in (1). Its Gaussian coefficient is EXACTLY [2h-1 choose 2h-1]_Q=1, and its other displayed coefficient is a unit phase. Therefore any termwise-absolute estimate of the expansion (1) has rate at least B_* already from this single EXACT monic term. Since g_7 and g_5 are both smaller than B_*, this specific route cannot remove those widths by a sharper frozen-radius constant or a better estimate of that term. That comparison can also be certified without a numerical limiting fit: rho>=4 everywhere and rho>=5 on[pi/6,pi/3]. The latter follows from its displayed unimodal (1+sin theta+cos theta)^2 expression and the two explicit endpoint values, both greater than5. Hence B_* >= (log5)/6+(log4)/3 > .73. On the other hand sec v>=1 in (10) gives g_s<=j_0-pi/s. The elementary bounds G<11/12 and pi>157/50 give j_0<1.17, so g_5,g_7<1.17-157/350<.73. The finite interval audit checks the two endpoint and logarithmic comparisons with outward rounding. This is an obstruction to the STATED ABSOLUTE-TERM METHOD, not to the actual source. A further improvement must combine the P_h terms coherently, or pair the complete alias with the other boxes and the original Phi_2 functional before estimating. The exact Frobenius/ circle-source pairing under investigation is eligible for that task; deleting the alias or a normal jet is not. ## 8. Parity of the number of boxes: the even-width link statement The same proof applies to every fixed INTEGER s>=9, if even widths are stated as LINKS rather than knots. This is a source/parity audit, not an inference that a link is a knot. The exact unwrapped-degree and Phi_2 product identities use the original cups, ordinary caps and ONE marked cap and hold for any integer box count. The only use of oddness in their topological conclusion is the component count: following the main strand advances its box label by2 modulo s. Thus there are gcd(s,2) main components. With all crossing circles present the augmented diagram has s+gcd(s,2) components; after their prescribed fillings it has gcd(s,2) main components. In particular an even s gives a two-component pretzel link. The analytic checks are likewise independent of oddness of s: * The complete polynomial is the SAME z_N and the source is the SAME full-Hermite Phi_2(z_N^s). The coherent inner bounds have no s in them. The enclosing-circle saddle has s j'(eta_s)=1 and alpha=pi/s in(0,pi/2) for every integer s>2. Its two Gaussian constants are nonzero and the higher winding bound is unchanged. * The mixed packet remains exactly even in EACH color. The complex saddle Hessian and the real color curvature are nonzero for s>2. Local source replacement uses a strictly positive alias margin; (12) supplies it for all integer s>=9. * The exact filling formula is applied once per port. Under every unit charge reflection both m_i and its sinh factor change sign. Its level character is (-1)^((s+sum_i m_i)(N-1))=1, because sum_i m_i is congruent to s modulo2. This conclusion does not require s odd. All endpoint/tail estimates depend on the fixed number of ports and continue verbatim. The original LINK normalization is already proved in [the complete source-normalization theorem](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md), section3: a cut partial trace is a scalar Hopf endomorphism of the remaining simple V_N regardless of connectivity. Thus the same single-cut reduced Kashaev link value has the modulus of the raw source. Its enhancement sign is (-1)^((N-1)(c-1)) with the ACTUAL component count c. There is still only one modified dimension if that optional convention is used, not one per main component. The literal port matrices, reversed-cap ordering, shaded/white face geometry, and primitive auxiliary filling equations also do not use oddness. For even width the two main-component meridians remain noncentral parabolic. The general geometric completion theorem keeps BOTH unfilled cusps complete; it does not collapse them to one. Consequently, with the same sufficiently long independently signed fixed twists, the source and volume equality extend to the ORIGINAL single-cut reduced two-component pretzel LINK for every fixed even s>=10. The knot conclusion is the odd s>=9 part. No assertion for a normalization that modifies every component independently is made. The even widths4,6,8, like the odd widths3,5,7, are not supplied by the present full-color gap. The audit includes literal even-width full marked sources against the unwrapped transfer and exact rotated Phi_2 product; numerical checks supplement the parity-independent derivations above.

title: Actual pretzel circle sewing: a coherent positive factorization and a half-twist test
text:
# Actual pretzel circle sewing: a coherent positive factorization and a half-twist test 29 October 2026. For the specified arbitrary-width pretzel port graph, the complete circle has an exact source-preserving Kraus/Cauchy factorization. The half twists remain diagonal unitary channel phases. The original marked cap produces TWO explicit boundary states; local positivity alone does not identify them. A level-three exact calculation rules out a literal positive norm-square identity for the half-twisted base, even after multiplying by any unit root framing phase. A separate untwisted calculation shows that the two source states remain different in the complete positive-circle quotient itself. This excludes their automatic identification by a choice of positive factor or consistent unitary duality gauges. It does not rule out another global reflection pairing for the genuinely untwisted base or a sharp positive majorant. ## 1. Specified original port graph Let s>=3 be odd, with boxes on adjacent head pairs (1,2),(3,4),...,(2s-1,2s). The bottom matching and top matching are S={(1,2s),(2,3),(4,5),...,(2s-2,2s-1)}. The outer top pair (1,2s) has the ORIGINAL marked row m; all other top pairs have the original ordinary cap ell. Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, and retain the original common Cartan kappa=q^(d^2/2). Use the original physical pair operators R and L=L_N. Each box considered here is \[ B_i=R^{e_i}L,\qquad e_i\in\mathbb Z. 	ag{1} \] The [literal all-width port/source calculation](actual_odd_pretzel_augmented_transfer_source.md) fixes this graph and its signs. Its augmented odd-pretzel base has e_i=-1. The genuinely untwisted circle graph has e_i=0. These are different graphs; removing the half twists is not a scalar framing operation. Let p_S be the tensor product of the genuine cups p_ab=Nx^(-b) delta_(a+b,d), placed on S in its displayed order. Let P_o swap each ordinary-cap pair (2,3),(4,5),... and leave the marked outer pair alone. Let P_b swap every box pair. Both are literal permutations of tensor legs, not added physical crossings. All boxes preserve total INTEGER physical degree. Thus the total incoming degree sd and the ordinary caps force the final marked pair to degree d. Only on this assembled source the top row is \[ \Lambda_S=N^{-(2s+1)}p_S^\dagger P_o. 	ag{2} \] Indeed ell=p^dagger P/N^2 and m_d=p^dagger/N^3 on their respective pairs. The unrestricted marked row has not been replaced locally on an arbitrary exterior. Consequently the full raw source scalar, before its existing external framing/peripheral factor chi_N, is \[ Z_N=N^{-(2s+1)}p_S^\dagger P_o (B_1\otimes\cdots\otimes B_s)p_S. 	ag{3} \] This graph identity is the source input; no geometric triangulation or hyperbolic volume formula is assumed. ## 2. Full physical coherent channel factorization Use the canonical full physical positive resolution [of the original complete circle](actual_complete_circle_reflection_positive.md). For every physical degree T and admitted distinct Casimir node j, let v_(T,j) have first component one, embedded in its actual degree block, and let h_(T,j)>0 be its exact positive CD coefficient. Form a rectangular matrix F with columns sqrt(h_(T,j)) v_(T,j). Then \[ FF^\dagger=H=LP,\qquad R F=F\,\operatorname{diag} (\kappa
u_j),\quad 
u_j=(-1)^j q^{j(j+1)}. 	ag{4} \] Every high physical block is retained by the explicit low-block mirror; both even paired nodes and the odd simple node are included. This is not a value-only replacement of a root Jordan block. The original circle has already selected its entire image, with its actual normal source, before (4) is used. Since |kappa nu_j|=1, define the diagonal unitary U_i=diag((kappa nu_j)^(e_i)). Equations (1) and (4) prove the ALL-INPUT factorization \[  oxed{B_i=F U_i F^\dagger P.} 	ag{5} \] This retains every half twist and its full Cartan phase. It does not use the false assertion that the original R is an H-isometry; the isometry on H would instead involve the correctly leg-exchanged R. Put F_s=F^(tensor s), U=U_1 tensor...tensor U_s, and define the two source packets \[ u=F_s^\dagger P_b p_S,\qquad v=F_s^\dagger P_o p_S. \] Inserting (5) in (3) gives the exact coherent formula and its positive Cauchy estimate: \[  oxed{Z_N=N^{-(2s+1)}v^\dagger Uu,\qquad |\chi_N Z_N|^2\leq |\chi_N|^2N^{-(4s+2)} \|v\|^2\|u\|^2.} 	ag{6} \] The two energies are explicit positive original-source contractions: \[ \|u\|^2=p_S^\dagger C^{\otimes s}p_S,\qquad \|v\|^2=p_S^\dagger P_oH^{\otimes s}P_op_S. 	ag{7} \] All original integer labels, cap constraints and CD factors are kept before these contractions. The local once-power angle coefficient is the exact h_(T,j), not its independent maximum. Formula (6) works at arbitrary s and for arbitrary signed e_i; neither packet is defined by the unknown closed scalar. For e_i=0, the middle U is the identity, but v and u are still different specified source packets. A global reflection theorem must supply an additional relation between them, or another controlled pairing. This does not follow from FF^dagger>=0 or from a consistent dual-object basis change. In particular (6) is a structural positive comparison, not a sharp geometric energy estimate. For clarity, the equivalent literal transfer entries retain the phases as follows. If h is the conserved input-left minus output-left charge, I_h=[max(0,h),min(d,d+h)], T=d+a-a', then \[ M_i^h[a,a']=x^{-2a+h} \sum_{j\ {m admitted\ at}\ T} h_{T,j}(\kappa
u_j)^{e_i} v_{T,j}(a-h)\overline{v_{T,j}(d-a')}. 	ag{8} \] The total physical degree T varies with the two open transfer indices. It cannot be replaced by a common fixed degree before contraction. ## 3. Exact half-twisted source certificate at N=3 Take N=3, s=3 and every e_i=-1. Build the literal original factorial R, the actual coproduct Casimir Omega, and L=Omega^2-I. The complete source contraction (3), or equivalently the already specified transfer trace, gives exactly \[  oxed{Z_3=-189+81i\sqrt3=27(-7+3i\sqrt3).} 	ag{9} \] This calculation includes kappa=q^2 and the original marked N factors. The exact transfer trace used to verify it is \[ Z_3= rac{x^4}{3}\sum_{h=-2}^2 \operatorname{Tr}\{D_h(M^h)^3\},\qquad D_h=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in I_h}x^{2a}. \] The five traces, in order h=-2,-1,0,1,2, are 270+243 i sqrt3, 27-351 i sqrt3, 2781/2+(189/2) i sqrt3, -540+162 i sqrt3, -999/2+(27/2) i sqrt3. Moreover \[ Z_3/\overline{Z_3}=(11-21i\sqrt3)/38. 	ag{10} \] This cannot be a root of unity: its rational field trace is 11/19, whereas a root of unity is an algebraic integer and a rational trace of an algebraic integer must be an integer. Thus multiplying (9) by ANY unit root framing phase cannot make it real. In particular the original half-twisted scalar is not a positive norm square times the retained framing phase and a positive scalar normalization. This is an obstruction only to that literal norm-square identity. The positive comparison (6) remains valid. The certificate is not an upper-volume counterexample and does not identify a hyperbolic knot or link from a numerical invariant. The graph without the half twists (all e_i=0) instead has Z_3=270, consistent with the still-open genuinely untwisted reflection question. No extrapolation from this calculation settles arbitrary untwisted fully augmented diagrams. ### 3a. The untwisted source mismatch survives the positive-circle quotient There is a stronger, source-exact check than merely observing that the two permutations in Section 2 are different. Set N=3, s=3, and every e_i=0, with the ORIGINAL cups and the one marked cap as in Section 1. For ANY factor F satisfying FF^dagger=H, the actual packet Gram is \[  oxed{\quad  egin{pmatrix} u^\dagger u&u^\dagger v\v^\dagger u&v^\dagger v \end{pmatrix} =3^{10} egin{pmatrix}18&10\10&119\end{pmatrix}. \quad} 	ag{11} \] This is an exact quadratic-field calculation directly in the original physical modules. One can verify it without choosing square roots or CD columns: put \[ p_{a,b,c}=27x^{-(d-a+d-b+d-c)},\qquad (i_1,\ldots,i_6)=(a,b,d-b,c,d-c,d-a), \] for a,b,c in {0,1,2}. These are precisely the 27 nonzero entries of p_S. Permute them by P_b or P_o, and contract the two resulting vectors against H tensor H tensor H. The literal coproduct Casimir gives L=Omega^2-I and H=LP; their entries, and all the displayed source coefficients, lie in Q(sqrt(-3)). The three resulting finite contractions are respectively 18,10,119 times 3^10. The audit performs these operations in that exact number field, separately from the numerical CD tests. In particular \[ \|u-v\|^2=117\,3^{10}>0,\qquad \det\operatorname{Gram}(u,v)=2042\,3^{20}>0. 	ag{12} \] The difference therefore survives the actual image quotient: it is not a radical vector discarded by the positive complete circle. The packets are not even collinear. The original closed value and the two proposed canonical packet norms are \[ Z_3=3^{-7}v^\dagger u=270,\qquad 3^{-7}\|u\|^2=486,\qquad 3^{-7}\|v\|^2=3213. 	ag{13} \] Every equality (11)--(13) is independent of the Kraus factor: its Gram depends only on H. Replacing a minimal F by another such factor applies a common isometry to its channel space and cannot change it. Consistent unitary physical duality changes, with the original sources transformed at their ports, likewise leave these closed contractions unchanged. Consequently removing the half-twist phases and transporting the true dual objects do NOT turn formula (6) into either canonical norm square. This is deliberately a limited obstruction. It does not exclude a different projection-plane cut, a nontrivial global pairing with its own proved source normalization, or coherent elimination before taking a norm. The untwisted value in (13) is positive. What fails is the specific proposed inference that the original marked source identifies the two positive-circle boundary states after quotienting. In particular this calculation does not replace a genuine six-port junction by a two-port Frobenius multiplication. ## 4. Validation and remaining estimate The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_circle_coherent_reflection.py) constructs the full original generators, crossings, complete circle, actual marked/cup source and canonical CD columns. It compares (3) directly to (6), with all physical box ports still open before their literal source contraction. A separate exact quadratic-field calculation reconstructs (9) from the original matrices rather than from guessed channel phases. It also computes (11) exactly from H and the literal 27-term original cup state; positivity, noncollinearity, and the quotient-level mismatch are consequences of that exact Gram matrix. The remaining sharp task is a bound for the ACTUAL constrained packets (7), or a stronger coherent pairing than their product. Independent local capacities do not establish this. Neither polynomial duality transport nor the complete-circle local PSD theorem supplies the missing global geometric incidence or selected-source energy estimate.

title: Coherent circle control and the full original augmented pretzel period
text: # Coherent circle control and the full original augmented pretzel period 29 October 2026. The analytic proof and its full two-branch recurrence estimate have passed independent proof audits. The statement below concerns the COMPLETE augmented pretzel source, with every crossing-circle color equal to N and every retained half twist equal to the original R^(-1). It is a link-source theorem at arbitrary fixed odd box count s, not a theorem for its fixed Dehn fillings or for an arbitrary alternating knot. ## 1. Statement, including the original phase and leading constant Use the [literal complete-base polynomial](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md) z_N and the unchanged marked functional Phi_2. For each fixed odd s>=3 put alpha=pi/s, eta=2 asinh(tan alpha), R=exp(eta), T=R+R^(-1)=4 sec(alpha)^2-2, u_*=atan(sec alpha), d=N-1, V_s=8s[Lambda(pi/4+alpha/2)+Lambda(pi/4-alpha/2)], C_s=(R-R^(-1)) exp(i s u_*/2) /[sqrt(s cos alpha) 2^s ((T+2)(T+6))^(s/4)]. Here Lambda(t)=-integral_0^t log|2 sin v|dv. The asserted full-source asymptotic is A_(s,N)=Phi_2(z_N^s) =N^(3/2) exp(-i s pi(N-1)/4) C_s exp[N V_s/(2pi)] (1+o(1)). (1) In particular C_s is nonzero. The formula treats both parities of N with their actual original Cartan factors, and includes all repeated Casimir nodes and normal derivatives through Phi_2. Any external normalization must still be applied explicitly; no unexamined factor is declared harmless. The [explicit face-gluing and tetrahedron calculation](actual_augmented_pretzel_geometric_volume.md) identifies V_s with the complete augmented link volume. This assertion concerns the specified RAW marked source A_(s,N); an external chi_N is not implicitly set to one or assigned a growth rate. The [complete-point normalization proof](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) now checks that the ORIGINAL reduced Kashaev link evaluation has |<L_s>_N|=|A_(s,N)|. Its framing and component-dependent enhancement characters have modulus one. Thus (1) proves the actual link statement lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|<L_s>_N| =Vol(S^3 minus L_s)=V_s. (1a) The full one-cut modified ADO convention instead multiplies the reduced value by i^(N+3)/N at completeness. That changes the leading N-power from N^(3/2) to N^(1/2), and preserves (1a)'s exponential rate. ## 2. The coherent Newton coefficients and the permitted envelope Write q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, M=floor((N-1)/2), F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a|, and c_a=2cos((2a+1)pi/N). Set B_r(w)=product_(a=0)^(r-1)(c_a-w-w^(-1)), A_r=sum_(v=r)^M Q^(-vr)F_(2v)/(F_v^3 F_(v-r)), D_r=Q^(-r^2)F_(2r)/F_r^3, U_r=A_r/D_r. The finite source identity is exactly z_N(w+w^(-1)) =N^2 sum_(r=0)^M b_(N,r) B_r(w), b_(N,r)=kappa^(-1)(-1)^r q^(2r^2+r) A_r/F_r^3. (2) Consequently |b_(N,r)|=(s_(2r)/s_r^6)|U_r|. The [coherent finite inner transformation](actual_pretzel_coherent_inner_gauss_elimination.md) proves |U_r|<=2N for r>=ceil(N/4), and, uniformly on compact subintervals of 0<u=pi r/N<pi/2 lying above pi/4, b_(N,r)=exp(-i pi d/4) (s_(2r)/s_r^6) sqrt(sin u) exp(iu/2) [1+O(1/N)]. (3) The error is complex, uniform, and relative to the nonzero displayed amplitude. This formula is the same for BOTH parities. It follows from the exact half-shift phases before taking their asymptotics. The [all-index backward estimate](actual_pretzel_all_index_backward_envelope.md) retains the entire lower range and gives constants C,B independent of r,N such that |U_r|<=C N^B exp[N E(pi r/N)], E(u)=(2/pi) integral_u^(pi/4) log(cot v)dv, 0<=u<pi/4, E(u)=0, pi/4<=u<=pi/2. (4) This estimate expressly ALLOWS the second recurrence branch to grow. No assertion that |U_r| is polynomial below N/4 is needed. ## 3. A uniform circle estimate for each original Newton factor Fix R>1 and write w=-R exp(i theta), rho=R^(-1), g(t)=log|1-rho exp(it)|, eta=log R. The exact factorization gives log|B_r(w)|=r eta +sum_(a<r)[g(pi+theta+(2a+1)pi/N) +g(pi+theta-(2a+1)pi/N)]. (5) This is a midpoint sum on the symmetric arc [-2u,2u], u=pi r/N. Its difference from N/(2pi) times the integral is O_R(1), uniformly in r,N,theta. Indeed the total variation of g on one circle is 2log((R+1)/(R-1)); on each cell the midpoint error is at most half the variation on that cell. For any 0<=a<=pi, the function I_a(theta)=integral_(-a)^a g(theta+t)dt has its maximum at theta=pi: its derivative is g(theta+a)-g(theta-a), which is nonnegative on [0,pi], since cos(theta+a)-cos(theta-a)=-2sin(theta)sin(a)<=0 and g decreases as a function of cos. For 0<a<pi the maximum is unique modulo2pi. It follows in particular that max_(|w|=R)|B_r(w)| <=((R+1)/(R-1))^2 B_r(-R). (6) The right side is positive because every c_a>-2 and R+R^(-1)>2. This is a bound for the ORIGINAL finite Newton factor; no positivity of its monomial coefficients or unproved root-location assertion is used. ## 4. The second-branch envelope stays below the geometric maximum Uniform sine-factorial summation, including the endpoints, gives log s_k=-(N/pi)Lambda(pi k/N)+O(log N), 0<=k<N. Equations (2),(4),(5) therefore bound each term by a fixed polynomial in N times exp[N(H_R(u,theta)+E(u))], where H_R(u,theta)=(-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u))/pi+u eta/pi +(1/(2pi)) integral_(-2u)^(2u)g(pi+theta+t)dt. At theta=0 put J_R(u)=H_R(u,0). Equivalently, with T=R+R^(-1), J_R(u)=(-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u))/pi +(1/(2pi)) integral_0^(2u)log(T+2cos v)dv. (7) It has the derivative J_R'(u)=(1/pi)log[(T+2cos(2u))cos(u)^2/(4sin(u)^4)]. In t=tan u its zero is 4t^4-(T-2)t^2-(T+2)=0, tan(u_*)^2=(T+2)/4. The other algebraic root is -1. Thus J_R has a unique strict global maximum at u_* in (pi/4,pi/2). In the entire lower range, (J_R+E)'(u) =(1/pi)log[(T+2cos(2u))/(4sin(u)^2)]>0, 0<u<pi/4. (8) Hence max_(u<=pi/4)(J_R+E)=J_R(pi/4)<J_R(u_*). This is the essential quantitative comparison: the allowed growth from switching recurrence branches never reaches the geometric maximum of the OUTER original sum. The exact diagonal/interior equality in the old two-variable presentation is handled coherently by (2), not ignored. It follows that, with j(eta)=J_(exp eta)(u_*(eta)), limsup_N (1/N)log max_(|w|=R)|z_N(w+w^(-1))|<=j(eta). (9) There is also a stronger local bound needed for the full period. For some c,epsilon,delta>0 and finite B,C depending only on R, |z_N(-R exp(i theta)-R^(-1)exp(-i theta))| <=C exp[Nj(eta)] [exp(-cN theta^2)+N^B exp(-delta N)], |theta|<=epsilon, (10) and the same expression with only C N^B exp[N(j-delta)] holds on epsilon<=|theta|<=pi. To prove it, first use (8) and compactness to remove the lower range and all u outside a small neighborhood of u_*. At that maximum the real mixed derivative H_(u theta) vanishes, while H_(uu)=J_R''(u_*)=-(T+6)^2/[pi(T+2)^(3/2)]<0, H_(theta theta)=-sin(2u_*)/[pi(T+2cos(2u_*))]<0. Thus H<=j-c[(u-u_*)^2+theta^2] locally. On this compact u range, (3) and the uniform sine-product expansion give a summand prefactor O(N^(-5/2)); the outside factor N^2 and the discrete Gaussian sum O(sqrt N) give O(1). This proves (10). Away from theta=0, the strict arc inequality in section3 supplies the missing global gap; u=0 and u=pi/2 are already below j by section4. ## 5. A nonzero central Gaussian from the actual finite sum For complex zeta near real eta>0 define Psi(u,zeta)=(-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u))/pi +(1/(2pi)) integral_0^(2u) Log(2cosh zeta+2cos v)dv. (11) The logarithm is analytic in a fixed neighborhood, since its argument is positive at real eta. In a compact neighborhood of u_*, s_(2r)/s_r^6 =(2N)^(-5/2) sqrt(sin(2u))/sin(u)^3 exp[N(-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u))/pi][1+O(1/N)], and the midpoint expansion of B_r has leading prefactor one. These follow respectively by factoring sin(pi k/N)/(pi k/N) before ordinary Euler--Maclaurin, and by the smooth midpoint rule. Both are uniform in the neighborhoods in use. Insert (3) and set zeta=eta+i t/sqrt N, u=u_*+x/sqrt N. Taylor's formula in the REAL index x gives N Psi=N j+i sqrt N Psi_eta t +(1/2)Psi_uu x^2+i Psi_(u eta)xt -(1/2)Psi_(eta eta)t^2+o(1). (12) For bounded x,t this is uniform. The Gaussian bound (10), together with its index-level proof, justifies summing (12) by dominated Riemann sums and removing the remaining x tails. The resulting Fourier transform of a real Gaussian has coefficient j''(eta)=Psi_(eta eta)-Psi_(u eta)^2/Psi_uu>0. No contour deformation of the r sum or assertion about an unknown cycle is being made. The exact finite-sum asymptotic is, uniformly for bounded real t, z_N(-exp(eta+i t/sqrt N)-exp(-eta-i t/sqrt N)) =exp(-i pi d/4) a(eta) exp[Nj(eta)] exp[i sqrt N j'(eta)t-j''(eta)t^2/2](1+o(1)), a(eta)=exp(iu_*/2)/[2((T+2)(T+6))^(1/4)]. (13) The displayed constant comes directly from the index Gaussian: 2^(-5/2)pi^(-1)sqrt(2pi/|Psi_uu|) times sqrt(sin(2u_*))/sin(u_*)^(5/2). In particular it is nonzero. At t=0, (13) also turns (9) into equality. Elementary differentiation under the integral in (11) yields j'(eta)=alpha(eta)/pi, alpha(eta)=atan(sinh(eta/2)), j''(eta)=1/[2pi cosh(eta/2)]=cos(alpha)/(2pi). (14) For example j' follows by substituting tan(v/2) in its integral and using tan(u_*)=cosh(eta/2). Also j(eta)-eta/2 tends to zero as eta tends to infinity. Integrating (14), or differentiating the Lobachevsky expression with this boundary value, gives j(eta)-alpha eta/pi =(4/pi)[Lambda(pi/4+alpha/2)+Lambda(pi/4-alpha/2)]. (15) ## 6. The original marked residue has a surviving leading term The exact full source, including its normal coefficients, is A_(s,N)=(-1)^d N^2/(2pi i) integral_(|w|=R) z_N(w+w^(-1))^s w^N(1-w^(-2))/(1+w^N)^2 dw. (16) This is the proved coefficient/partial-trace identity for Phi_2, not a newly defined period. Choose eta=2asinh(tan(pi/s)), so that s j'(eta)=1. Parametrize w=-R exp(i theta). Uniformly on this circle, the rational factor is w^(-N)(1-w^(-2))[1+O(R^(-N))]. The error is exponentially smaller by (9),(10). In the central window theta=t/sqrt N, the original factor (-1)^d cancels the exact sign of w^(1-N). Equations (13),(14) cancel the linear Fourier phase as well. The remaining Gaussian is exp[-s j''(eta)t^2/2]. Bound (10) permits dominated convergence in this final integral; its complement is exponentially negligible. Consequently A_(s,N)=N^(3/2) exp(-i s pi d/4) [(R-R^(-1))a(eta)^s/sqrt(2pi s j''(eta))] exp[N(sj(eta)-eta)](1+o(1)). (17) Equations (14),(15) are precisely the constant and exponent in (1). The double-pole factor 1-w^(-2) is nonzero at -R and has been kept. Equivalently, all higher positive windings in the exact source have an extra R^(-(m-1)N) factor on this same circle; none was dropped before estimating it. Together with the independently proved finite-source and backward-envelope lemmas, this proves survival of the specified original raw period with its stated normalization. The bounds and local expansion used above are all at fixed s. No uniform assertion as s grows with N, no fixed Dehn-filling theorem, and no general-knot volume conjecture follows from (1). ## 7. Independent checks and the normalization boundary Two independent analytical audits checked the midpoint maximum, the lower-index envelope comparison, the all-parity coefficient phase, the two real Gaussian integrations and the marked residue constant. The explicit harmonic-error backward proof was separately audited before use. The [finite audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.py) checks the exact stationary polynomial/Hessian, literal Newton-circle factors, and the predicted full complex leading constant against the original value-plus-normal period at N=32,33,64,65,128,129 and s=3,5,7,9. Those samples are calibration of the proof, not a replacement for its estimates. The original pretzel source theorem keeps a peripheral/framing line chi_N outside A_(s,N). Formula (1) has NOT silently absorbed that line. The [normalization proof](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) retains the whole modified-dimension meridian germ before evaluating it: |chi_red|=1 and |chi_full|=1/N at THIS complete point. It also checks that the exact enhanced Kashaev comparison extends to this multicomponent link, with component-dependent sign (-1)^(d(c-1)). No polynomial-size assertion for an arbitrary moving peripheral germ is inferred. The fixed filled-knot source also contains the ENTIRE coherent auxiliary-color sum; taking only its complete-color value is not a filling theorem. ## 8. The requested special inner product is an explicit Fourier norm Write the SAME finite Laurent polynomial as z_N(w+w^(-1))^s=sum_(k=-sM)^(sM) a_k w^k. For N>=3 use the positive inner product on its coefficient space <a,b>_R=sum_k conjugate(a_k)b_k R^(2(k-N)), Z_(s,N)=||a||_R^2 =R^(-2N)/(2pi) integral_(-pi)^pi |z_N(-R exp(i theta)-R^(-1)exp(-i theta))|^(2s)dtheta. (18) The equality is finite Fourier--Plancherel. It retains all coherent inner sums BEFORE squaring. The exact original source functional is b_N(a)=(-1)^d N^2 sum_(m>=1)(-1)^(m-1)m (a_(mN-1)-a_(mN+1)), (19) with coefficients outside the finite support equal to zero. Its squared dual norm is bounded explicitly by ||b_N||_(R,dual)^2 <=N^4(R^2+R^(-2)) sum_(m>=1) m^2 R^(-2(m-1)N) =N^4(R^2+R^(-2))(1+x)/(1-x)^3, x=R^(-2N). (20) There is no index overlap for N>=3. Omitting absent coefficients can only decrease this bound. Cauchy--Schwarz therefore proves EXACTLY |A_(s,N)|^2<=N^4(R^2+R^(-2))(1+x)/(1-x)^3 Z_(s,N). (21) This metric is specified by the polynomial source and the geometric radius; it does not use the unknown contracted value A_(s,N). Equations (10),(13) additionally prove, at the radius in section1, Z_(s,N)=[|a(eta)|^(2s)/sqrt(2s cos alpha)] N^(-1/2) exp[N V_s/pi](1+o(1)). (22) Thus for this complete augmented source the original question is literally Cauchy in a specified inner product, AND its positive energy has now been independently estimated at the sharp volume rate. The additional Gaussian argument in section6 proves the lower bound/survival that Cauchy by itself cannot supply. For an external normalization chi_N, (21) retains |chi_N|^2 on its right. There is also an exact way to separate the upper-bound question from survival. Let D_(s,N) be the ACTUAL squared dual norm of (19) on the finite coefficient space, and let v be its Riesz vector for (18). Then |A_(s,N)|^2 = D_(s,N) Z_(s,N) cos(theta_N)^2, cos(theta_N)^2=|<v,a>_R|^2/(||v||_R^2 ||a||_R^2). (23) Here theta_N denotes the Hermitian angle, so cos(theta_N) is defined as the nonnegative normalized absolute overlap. For each fixed s>=3, both first-winding indices N-1,N+1 eventually lie in the coefficient space. Consequently D_(s,N)=N^4(R^2+R^(-2))(1+O(R^(-2N))). For fixed odd s>=3, equations (1) and (22) now give the quantitative survival statement cos(theta_N)^2 ~ [(R-R^(-1))^2/(R^2+R^(-2))] sqrt(2/(s cos alpha)) N^(-1/2). (24) Thus Cauchy's upper estimate loses only a polynomial factor for this particular original source. The nonzero-overlap asymptotic (24) uses the independently proved original-period asymptotic (1); it is not inferred from positivity or Plancherel. For a general filled source, the geometric energy estimate and exclusion of exponentially small overlap remain separate requirements.

title: Exact coherent inner elimination for the original pretzel polynomial
text: # Exact coherent inner elimination for the original pretzel polynomial 29 October 2026. Reversing the TWO ACTUAL finite sums in the complete pretzel box gives a balanced terminating finite transformation. It retains the half shift and proves a nonzero, uniformly tame inner packet throughout the geometric range r>=N/4, at BOTH parities. An explicit nonzero leading amplitude follows on compact subintervals of 1/4<r/N<1/2. No stationary-cycle assumption is used for this inner sum. The remaining outer sum and the all-r upper bound are separate. The exact all-r recurrence below retains the same original source, including the part below N/4 which has NOT been discarded. ## 1. The unchanged source and a generic finite identity Use q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), F_a=(Q;Q)_a. In formula (11a) of [the original complete box](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md), interchanging the FINITE v,r sums gives exactly kappa z_N(z)/N^2 =sum_(r=0)^M (-1)^r Q^(r(r+1)/2) P_r(z) A_r/F_r^3, A_r=sum_(v=r)^M Q^(-vr)F_(2v)/(F_v^3 F_(v-r)), P_r(z)=(qw;Q)_r(q/w;Q)_r, z=w+w^-1. (1) This retains every original coefficient, all half-twist and Cartan phases, and the full polynomial BEFORE its marked Hermite period. There is no removal of boundary r=v. Put n=M-r and D_r=Q^(-r^2)F_(2r)/F_r^3, U_r=A_r/D_r. Then U_r=sum_(k=0)^n (qQ^r;Q)_k(-qQ^r;Q)_k(-Q^(r+1);Q)_k Q^(-rk) /[F_k(Q^(r+1);Q)_k^2]. (2) Exactly one of the three numerator parameters is Q^(-n): -qQ^r at odd N, and -Q^(r+1) at even N. All denominators are nonzero throughout the TRUE finite ranges. Here is the finite transformation used in both cases. For generic parameters with nonzero displayed denominators, sum_(k=0)^n (Q^-n;Q)_k(a;Q)_k(b;Q)_k (cdQ^n/(ab))^k/[F_k(c;Q)_k(d;Q)_k] =(c/a;Q)_n/(c;Q)_n *sum_(j=0)^n (Q^-n;Q)_j(a;Q)_j(d/b;Q)_j Q^j /[F_j(d;Q)_j(aQ^(1-n)/c;Q)_j]. (3) This is proved here by finite summation, not assumed from a named transformation theorem. The terminating identity sum_(j=0)^k (Q^-k;Q)_j(t;Q)_j Q^j/[F_j(d;Q)_j] =t^k(d/t;Q)_k/(d;Q)_k (4) was proved by two finite binomial expansions in [the elementary q-Chu proof](actual_half_color_quadratic_source_transform.md#2-elementary-finite-q-chu-and-durfee-identities). Its balanced version is sum_(j=0)^k (Q^-k;Q)_j(a;Q)_j(cQ^k/a)^j /[F_j(c;Q)_j]=(c/a;Q)_k/(c;Q)_k. (5) For completeness, reverse the summation in (5). After its last term is factored out, the remaining sum is (4) with parameters t=Q^(1-k)/c and d=Q^(1-k)/a. The factorial reversal (Q^(1-k)/a;Q)_k=(-a)^(-k)Q^(-k(k-1)/2)(a;Q)_k cancels that last-term factor and gives (5). To prove (3), expand (b;Q)_k/(d;Q)_k =(b/d)^k sum_(j=0)^k (Q^-k;Q)_j(d/b;Q)_j Q^j/[F_j(d;Q)_j] using (4), interchange the finite k,j sums, and put k=j+l. The l sum is (5) with parameters Q^(j-n),aQ^j,cQ^j and argument cQ^(n-j)/a. It equals (c/a;Q)_(n-j)/(cQ^j;Q)_(n-j). Cancel (c;Q)_j(cQ^j;Q)_(n-j)=(c;Q)_n and use (c/a;Q)_(n-j)/(c/a;Q)_n =(-c/a)^(-j)Q^(-nj+j(j+1)/2) /(aQ^(1-n)/c;Q)_j. All remaining powers combine to Q^j. This proves (3) exactly, and rational continuation gives every root specialization used here. ## 2. Odd levels: a coherent quarter-phase series Let N=2M+1, n=M-r. Substitution in (3) gives U_r=(q;Q)_n/(Q^(r+1);Q)_n *sum_(j=0)^n (Q^(2r+1);Q^2)_j(-1;Q)_j Q^j /[(Q^(2r+2);Q^2)_j F_j]. (6) Every summand on the second line is EXACTLY i^j h_j, h_j>0. Its consecutive positive magnitudes obey, with delta=pi/N, h_(j+1)/h_j =sin((2r+1+2j)delta)/sin((2r+2+2j)delta) *cos(j delta)/sin((j+1)delta). Thus the high-index Newton packet has a common quadrant at a real z<-2, with no macroscopic phase cancellation. An exact all-r source Ward equation There is nevertheless a low-order equation controlling the ENTIRE remaining sequence, including the lower-index range. With Y=Q^r, QY^2(1-Q^2Y) A_(r+2) +Y(2Q^3Y^2+Q+1) A_(r+1) -Q(QY+1)(QY^2-1) A_r=0, (14) A_M=Q^(-M^2)F_(2M)/F_M^3, A_(M+1)=0. Here A_r=0 for r>M. The sum telescopes: g(Q^r)=0 and t(M+1,r)=0 by its literal root factor. Finally t(v,r+1)/t(v,r)=z^-1-Y^-1, so its first two moments are A_(r+1)+Y^-1 A_r and A_(r+2)+(1+Q^-1)Y^-1A_(r+1)+Y^-2A_r. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_coherent_inner_gauss_elimination.py) checks (3) at independent generic parameters, both literal root sums for EVERY r, their exact phases, the all-input source Ward endpoints, the uniform high-index inequalities, and the explicit amplitude limits. ## 6. For odd N, factorial phases and (7) give exactly b_(N,r)=kappa^(-1)q^(M^2) [s_(2r)/s_r^6] B_(N,n) Srev_r. The leading Srev_r in (9) is sqrt(cos beta)exp(-i beta/2), where beta=n pi/N=pi/2-pi/(2N)-u and u=pi r/N. Since kappa=q^(d^2/2), M=d/2, its total leading phase is EXACTLY kappa^(-1)q^(M^2)exp(-i beta/2) =exp(-i pi d/4)exp(iu/2). At even N the prefactor in (10) has exact phase q^(n(n+1/2)); the remaining factorial phases give kappa^(-1)q^(M^2+M/2)q^(r/2). The first two factors are EXACTLY exp(-i pi d/4), since d=2M+1. Together with (12) this proves, uniformly on every compact 1/4<r/N<1/2 at BOTH parities, b_(N,r)=exp(-i pi d/4)[s_(2r)/s_r^6] sqrt(sin u)exp(iu/2)[1+O(1/N)]. (15) No parity-dependent sign or unknown root phase remains in (15). Fix a real T>2, eta=arcosh(T/2), R=exp eta, and define J_T(u)=[-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u)]/pi +(1/(2pi)) integral_0^(2u)log(T+2cos v)dv, u_*=atan(sqrt(T+2)/2). Its derivative is pi^(-1)log[(T+2cos(2u))cos(u)^2/(4sin(u)^4)]. The difference of the numerator and denominator in this logarithm has the sign of T+2-(T+6)sin(u)^2. Hence u_* is the unique strict maximum on 0<=u<=pi/2, and u_*>pi/4. Direct differentiation gives J_T''(u_*)=-(T+6)^2/[pi(T+2)^(3/2)]. The original sine-factorial and smooth midpoint products give uniformly near this maximum s_(2r)/s_r^6=(2N)^(-5/2) sqrt(sin(2u))/sin(u)^3 *exp{N[-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u)]/pi}[1+O(1/N)], product_(a<r)(c_a+T) =exp{N/(2pi) integral_0^(2u)log(T+2cos v)dv} *[1+O(1/N)]. All other high indices have a strict profile gap, using (8),(11) and the uniform logarithmic endpoint factorial estimate. The real discrete Laplace sum has step du=pi/N. Inserting (15), its Gaussian prefactor is 2^(-5/2)pi^(-1)sqrt(2pi/|J_T''(u_*)|) *sqrt(sin(2u_*))/sin(u_*)^(5/2) =1/[2((T+2)(T+6))^(1/4)]. (16) It also has a uniform central-window extension without deforming its index contour. Let j(eta)=J_(2cosh eta)(u_*(eta)), and let tau be bounded real. Taylor-expand the analytic midpoint logarithm at eta+i tau/sqrt N and the REAL index u=u_*+x/sqrt N. Its quadratic part is Nj+i sqrt N j' tau +(Psi_uu/2)x^2+i Psi_(u eta)x tau -(Psi_(eta eta)/2)tau^2. (17) The error is uniform for bounded tau. The displayed limiting Gaussian and a(eta) are nonzero, so the error is relative as written. This is an actual finite-sum calculation with every coherent inner factor; it does not assert an unknown r-cycle incidence. To replace z_N^hi by the FULL z_N requires the independent all-index upper envelope and its strict lower-range profile gap. The [whole-period assembly](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) states that additional gate explicitly before applying (17) to the original marked residue. title: Coherent radial capacity of the original augmented pretzel source
text: # Coherent radial capacity of the original augmented pretzel source 29 October 2026. These diagnostics evaluate the exact polynomial and original source in [the complete-base theorem](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md). They retain all nodal derivatives and all true winding channels. They do not prove an asymptotic limit, a global circle supremum, or geometric survival. ## 1. A genuine full-source finite Cauchy bound Let \(z_N\) be that explicit half-degree polynomial and let \(R>1\). The exact enclosing residue, with the original source normal terms, immediately gives \[ |\mathcal A_{s,N}| \leq N^2\frac{R+R^{-1}}{(1-R^{-N})^2} R^{-N}\max_{|w|=R}|z_N(w+w^{-1})|^s. \tag{1} \] No inner factorial sum is replaced by absolute values. Its only maximum is the coherent actual polynomial on the specified circle. For each fixed \(R,s\) the prefactor is polynomial in \(N\). The classical candidate circle for the primitive winding is \[ c_s=2-4\sec^2(\pi/s),\qquad R_s=\frac{-c_s+\sqrt{c_s^2-4}}2. \] The compared classical action rate is \[ V_s/(2\pi)=\frac{4s}{\pi} \left[\Lambda\left(\frac\pi4+\frac\pi{2s}\right) +\Lambda\left(\frac\pi4-\frac\pi{2s}\right)\right]. \] The identification and accessibility of that classical critical point are separate from the finite inequality (1). ## 2. Coherent values, with precision replay The capacity column below is \(s\log\max_{|w|=R_s}|z_N(w+w^{-1})|/N-\log R_s\), before the polynomial prefactor of (1). The period column is the FULL original \(\log|\mathcal A_{s,N}|/N\), calculated with the source derivative terms, not only the largest spectral value. | Boxes | N | Coherent capacity rate | Original period rate | Candidate action rate | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 3 | 128 | 2.282542848771 | 2.358391191770 | 2.332487232247 | | 3 | 256 | 2.307490060173 | 2.349466791768 | 2.332487232247 | | 5 | 128 | 5.113656771500 | 5.175096842135 | 5.180738545635 | | 5 | 256 | 5.147131188299 | 5.181900345453 | 5.180738545635 | | 7 | 128 | 7.617877073877 | 7.673538626889 | 7.707108672092 | | 7 | 256 | 7.662390577692 | 7.694267916927 | 7.707108672092 | | 9 | 128 | 10.031081747751 | 10.083088667235 | 10.143508359858 | | 9 | 256 | 10.087158750074 | 10.117206848457 | 10.143508359858 | The apparent circle maximum is near the negative real axis, with a finite-level angular shift of order \(1/N\). At \(N=256\), its angles divided by \(\pi\) are respectively 0.998640430, 0.999300037, 0.999527662, 0.999641617. Evaluation exactly on the negative axis changes the reported rates by less than \(2.2\cdot10^{-6}\). The grid used \(\max(256,4N)\) angles followed by local golden-section refinement at every sampled local maximum. This is a numerical search, not a certified global bound. The \(N=128\) calculation was repeated at 128 and 256 decimal digits; \(N=256\) was repeated at 256 and 512 digits. All rates reproduce the displayed twelve decimal places. The finite Cauchy prefactor is included when checking (1); its omission from the capacity column explains why finite capacity rates can lie below finite period rates. ## 3. Exact remaining analytic step These values support trying to prove a uniform coherent circle bound at \(R_s\), including all competing branches and boundary currents. The original period then still needs a selected saddle with a nonzero coefficient for a LOWER/survival theorem. Formal stationary values, convergence of these samples and positivity of the coefficient \(b_v\) do not prove either assertion. [Diagnostic program](../experiments/diagnose_pretzel_coherent_radial_capacity.py). Its four JSON outputs record the base levels, two precision replays, and the high level independently. All diagnostic processes completed; no background calculations remain.

title: An explicit half-degree Casimir polynomial for the original augmented pretzel base
text: # An explicit half-degree Casimir polynomial for the original augmented pretzel base **Subsequent analytic theorem.** This exact source now feeds the [full coherent period asymptotic](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md), which proves a nonzero leading coefficient and the actual augmented link volume rate at arbitrary fixed odd width. The formulas below retain their role as independently checked finite algebraic inputs. 29 October 2026. The COMPLETE mixed-circle base of every odd pretzel has a single, explicit pair-Casimir polynomial. Its degree is at most \(\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\). Its coefficients in the physical continuant basis are positive finite cosine/factorial products, with the actual half-twist phase retained. This yields all nodal values AND first normal jets, and an original one-variable coefficient source for every odd number of boxes. No geometric saddle or noncancellation theorem is inferred from this exact reduction. ## 1. Literal quarter-turn, not a partial transpose of a positive form Use the original \(N,d,q,Q,x,\kappa,p,\ell,m,R,L_N\) of the [pretzel source theorem](actual_odd_pretzel_augmented_transfer_source.md). For any two-head box define its actual rigid quarter-turn by \[ (\mathscr R B)_{(u,b);(v,e)} =\sum_{r,t}\ell_{u,r}B_{(r,v);(b,t)}p_{t,e} =x^{u-e}B_{(d-u,v);(b,d-e)}. \tag{1} \] This is a linear tangle rotation using the ORIGINAL turns. It is not a multiplicative map for vertical box composition and is not asserted to preserve matrix positivity. The original crossing rotation/snakes give \(\mathscr R(R^{-1})=R\), with full Cartan retained; also \(\mathscr R(I)=p\ell\), rather than the identity matrix. The charge transfer in the pretzel theorem makes this rotation source exact. On degree \(T=d+h\), if \(S_h=\operatorname{diag}(x^a)\) and \(P_h\) is physical reversal, then \[ (\mathscr R B)|_T=x^dP_hS_hM_B^{(h)}S_h^{-1}P_h. \tag{2} \] Under this conjugation \(D_h\) becomes the clock \(Q^{-b}\) of the second physical head. Its factor relative to the original pivot \(g_b=x^{-d}Q^{-b}\) cancels every remaining phase in the pretzel source. Precisely, \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \mathcal A_{s,N}(B_1,\ldots,B_s) =\Phi_2\bigl((\mathscr R B_1)\cdots(\mathscr R B_s)\bigr), \quad\Phi_2(X)=\frac1N\operatorname{Tr}_{V\otimes V} [(I\otimes g)X].} \tag{3} \] This is the same original marked source, not a new \(2N\) average. ## 2. Why the rotated box is a SINGLE full pair polynomial An actual pair intertwiner rotates to another pair intertwiner by the Hopf cup and cap equations. Work first at generic nearby \(q\), with the ordinary finite highest module of dimension \(N\), its genuine dual turns, and the literal mixed-circle polynomial. These data specialize regularly to the displayed root source: all turn factorials have indices below \(N\). Generic pair decomposition is multiplicity-free, with \(N\) distinct Casimir nodes, so every rotated box here is a unique polynomial in the generic pair Casimir of degree less than \(N\). These polynomial coefficients have NO root pole. Indeed the middle degree block of the Casimir is tridiagonal, and all its adjacent entries remain nonzero at the root. The map from its first \(N\) polynomial coefficients to its first physical row is triangular with these nonzero products on the diagonal. Its inverse is regular. Consequently the polynomial identity specializes on the ENTIRE physical pair, including high-degree blocks and all Jordan normals. It is not only a statement about distinct root eigenvalues. Apply this to \(B_*=R^{-1}L_N\), using the generic ordinary circle with its standard pivot before specialization. At the root its \((-1)^d\) pivot factor is exactly the original auxiliary pivot. Thus \(\mathscr R B_*=z_N(\Omega)\) for one degree-\(<N\) polynomial. ## 3. Explicit positive coefficients and the half-degree truncation Let \(A=\Omega|_{\deg d}\) in physical order \(|u,d-u\rangle\). Write its diagonal as \(D_u\) and adjacent entry as \(a_u=-(1-Q^{u+1})^2\). Define its canonical continuant polynomials \[ f_0(z)=1,\quad f_1(z)=(z-D_0)/a_0, \] \[ f_{u+1}(z)=\frac{(z-D_u)f_u(z)-a_{u-1}f_{u-1}(z)}{a_u}. \tag{4} \] Tridiagonality gives \(e_0^Tf_u(A)=e_u^T\). Thus the first physical row determines the polynomial by this specified basis. Put \(M=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\) and \[ C_L=\prod_{r=0}^{L-1}2\cos\frac{\pi(2r+1-L)}{2N}, \qquad C_0=1, \] \[ b_v=\frac{s_{d-v}^2 C_{d-2v}}{s_{d-2v}}>0, \qquad 0\leq v\leq M. \tag{5} \] At exactly these lengths the cosine product simplifies further: \[ C_{d-2v}=\frac{F_{d-v}}{F_v}=\frac{N}{s_v^2},\qquad \boxed{\quad b_v=\frac{N^2s_{2v}}{s_v^4},\quad b_vx^v=N^2\frac{F_{2v}}{F_v^4}.\quad} \tag{5a} \] Indeed \(-q^{1-(d-2v)}=Q^{v+1}\), so the product is precisely the interval \((Q^{v+1};Q)_{d-2v}\). Root factorial complementation gives the real positive value displayed. All integer lengths are below \(N\); this retains the exact root phases, rather than taking absolute values inside an unknown sum. Then the COMPLETE original base polynomial is \[ \boxed{\displaystyle z_N(z)=\kappa^{-1}\sum_{v=0}^{M}b_v f_v(z).} \tag{6} \] Proof of its first row. Equation (1), restricted to the middle degree, gives \((\mathscr R B_*)_{0,v}=x^{v-d}(B_*)_{(d,v);(d,v)}\). In the high block of physical degree \(d+v\), the original \(R^{-1}\) has only its first column in its last row, with coefficient \(\kappa^{-1}x^{d-v}\). Therefore the two phases cancel exactly and \[ (\mathscr R B_*)_{0,v} =\kappa^{-1}(H_N|_{d-v})_{0,0}. \tag{7} \] The [positive reflected-circle theorem](actual_complete_circle_reflection_positive.md) proves that this corner vanishes if \(2v>d\), and otherwise equals \[ s_{d-v}^2\sum_{a=0}^{d-2v}\frac1{s_as_{d-2v-a}}. \] The finite sum FACTORIZES. At any \(0\leq L<N\), the finite q-binomial theorem and \(F_a=(-i)^a q^{a(a+1)/2}s_a\) give \[ \sum_{a=0}^L\frac1{s_as_{L-a}} =\frac{(-q^{1-L};Q)_L}{s_L}= rac{C_L}{s_L}. \tag{8} \] In the middle expression the product is real and positive: its individual phases sum to zero, and all its cosine factors are positive. This proves (5)--(7), including the exact truncation. In particular the top coefficient of \(z_N\) is nonzero. For odd \(N=2m+1\), it has the especially simple exact value \[ [z^m]z_N(z)=\kappa^{-1}q^{-m(m+1)}, \tag{9} \] of modulus one. No absent leading channel is being supplied by a normalization choice. At even \(N=2m\), its degree is \(m-1\) and the top coefficient has modulus \(8/s_1\), also polynomial and nonzero. ## 4. All nodal values and normal jets without a large crossing matrix For every original node \(c_j=q^{2j+1}+q^{-2j-1}\), define \[ \lambda_j=\kappa^{-1}\sum_{v=0}^M b_v f_v(c_j),\qquad \xi_j=\kappa^{-1}\sum_{v=0}^M b_v f'_v(c_j). \tag{10} \] These give the FULL node values and first derivatives of the actual rotated base box. Paired nodes have exactly the same data. At the possible odd simple node only the value is required. Differentiate (4) to compute every derivative with no divided zero: \[ f'_{u+1}= \frac{f_u+(z-D_u)f'_u-a_{u-1}f'_{u-1}}{a_u}, \quad f'_0=0,\quad f'_1=1/a_0. \tag{11} \] For a formula entirely in finite q-factorials, use the actual q-Hahn value formula in the [complete physical packet](actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md), Section5, at \(T=d\): each \(f_v(c_j)\) is its displayed finite sum of three Gaussian binomials and an explicit quadratic \(Q\) phase. Equation (10) with (5) is therefore a finite factorial/quadratic-phase formula, not an unspecified eigenvector or a spectral fit. Equations (4),(11) retain all normal data even at even and composite levels. There is a shorter polynomial factorial formula. Define \[ P_r(z)=\prod_{a=0}^{r-1}(1-qQ^a z+Q^{2a+1}),\qquad P_0=1. \] Direct substitution in the explicit recurrence (4), coefficient by coefficient in this product basis, gives \[ f_v(z)=x^v\sum_{r=0}^v \frac{(Q^{-v};Q)_rQ^r}{F_r^3}P_r(z), \] \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \frac{\kappa z_N(z)}{N^2}= \sum_{v=0}^M\frac{F_{2v}}{F_v^4} \sum_{r=0}^v\frac{(Q^{-v};Q)_rQ^r}{F_r^3}P_r(z).} \tag{11a} \] This is an OWN finite polynomial identity: its proof uses the coefficient recurrence (4), the root relation \(x=-q^{-1}\), and \(P_{r+1}=P_r(1-qQ^r z+Q^{2r+1})\). It does not assume a named orthogonal-polynomial transformation or an asymptotic formula. More explicitly, with \(C_{v,r}=x^v(Q^{-v};Q)_rQ^r/F_r^3\) and zero coefficients outside \(0\leq r\leq v\), the coefficient identity to check is \[ a_vC_{v+1,r}=(c_r-D_v)C_{v,r} -q^{-1}Q^{1-r}C_{v,r-1}-a_{v-1}C_{v-1,r}. \] It follows by inserting the finite products and clearing their nonzero factorial denominators; the initial coefficients are those of \(f_0,f_1\). This also specifies all boundary terms of the check. Writing \(z=w+w^{-1}\) factors \(P_r=(qw;Q)_r(q/w;Q)_r\), so all node values for \(0\leq j\leq M\) have the explicit quadratic sum \[ \frac{\kappa\lambda_j}{N^2} =\sum_{v=0}^M\sum_{r=0}^{\min(v,j)} \frac{Q^{r(r-v-j)}F_{2v}F_{j+r}} {F_v^3F_{v-r}F_{j-r}F_r^3}. \tag{11b} \] The NORMAL source must not truncate the same way. For every double node let \(w_j=q^{2j+1}\), and \[ A_{v,r}=\frac{F_{2v}(Q^{-v};Q)_rQ^r}{F_v^4F_r^3}, \quad B_{j,r}=(Q^{j+1};Q)_r(Q^{-j};Q)_r. \] For \(r\leq j\) put \[ D_{j,r}=\sum_{a=0}^{r-1} \left[\frac{Q^{a-j}}{1-Q^{a-j}} -\frac{Q^{a+j+1}}{1-Q^{a+j+1}}\right]. \] Every denominator in this expression is nonzero. Differentiating the full polynomial BEFORE specializing gives the exact normal \[ \frac{\kappa\xi_j}{N^2} =\frac1{w_j-w_j^{-1}}\sum_{v=0}^M \left[\sum_{r=0}^{\min(v,j)}A_{v,r}B_{j,r}D_{j,r} +\sum_{r=j+1}^v A_{v,r}(-1)^jQ^{-j(j+1)/2} F_{j+r}F_{r-j-1}\right]. \tag{11c} \] The second sum is essential. For \(r>j\), the value of \((q/w;Q)_r\) vanishes at \(w_j\), but its logarithmic derivative does not: removing its unique zero gives exactly \((-1)^jQ^{-j(j+1)/2}F_jF_{r-j-1}\). Thus (11c) keeps the first-normal source terms which are invisible in the terminating node-value sum (11b).
