At the odd simple node \(w=-1\), no first normal is required; the safe polynomial derivative (11) remains available if desired. The audit checks (11a)--(11c) against the original full physical Hermite blocks. ## 5. The unchanged one-variable source and what it does not prove The actual pair source has the exact expression \[ \Phi_2(f(\Omega))= (-1)^d\sum_{j<d-j} [(4-c_j^2)f'(c_j)-c_jf(c_j)] +\mathbf1_{N\ \mathrm{odd}}f(-2). \tag{12} \] This follows directly from the generic ordinary pair decomposition and original pivotal partial trace, not from an imported polynomial invariant. At generic angle \(\theta\) the coefficient is the ratio \(\sum_j\sin(n_j\theta)f(2\cos n_j\theta)/\sin(N\theta)\), where \(n_j=2N-1-2j\). At \(\theta=\pi/N\) numerator and denominator vanish. Differentiate: a paired pair has \(n_j+n_{d-j}=2N\), giving the summand in (12). The unpaired \(n_j=N\) gives \(f(-2)\). The original root pivot differs from the ordinary \(K\) pivot by \((-1)^d\), exactly the displayed sign. The actual partial trace is regular, so this computes its value rather than a new derivative source. Equivalently, reduce \(f\) modulo the FULL \(\mathcal P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2\), retaining its double roots. Then \[ \Phi_2(f(\Omega))=(-1)^dN^2[z^d](f\bmod\mathcal P_N). \tag{13} \] For a direct verification, put \(w_k=q^{2k+1}\). The right side of (12) is \(-(-1)^d\sum_k(w\partial_w)[(w-w^{-1})f(w+w^{-1})]/2\). For degree below \(d\), root Fourier orthogonality annihilates it; at degree \(d\), the coefficients at \(w^{\pm N}\) give \((-1)^dN^2\). This proves (13). Consequently the COMPLETE raw augmented pretzel base at every odd number of boxes is \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \mathcal A_{s,N}(N,\ldots,N) =(-1)^d\sum_{j<d-j} [(4-c_j^2)s\xi_j\lambda_j^{s-1}-c_j\lambda_j^s] +\mathbf1_{N\ \mathrm{odd}}\lambda_{d/2}^s =(-1)^dN^2[z^d](z_N(z)^s\bmod\mathcal P_N).} \tag{14} \] The literal original marked cut, all half-twist phases and all normal channels remain. For \(N=2\) the polynomial has degree zero and the base is exactly zero. For \(N=3\), (6) is \(z_3(z)=q^2z-1-5i\sqrt3\); (14) at \(s=3\) recovers exactly \(-189+81i\sqrt3\). There is also an exact ORIGINAL one-variable residue and its finite integer windings. For any \(R>1\), parametrizing the enclosing \(z\)-ellipse by \(z=w+w^{-1}\) gives \[ \mathcal A_{s,N} =\frac{(-1)^dN^2}{2\pi i}\int_{|w|=R} z_N(w+w^{-1})^s \frac{w^N(1-w^{-2})}{(1+w^N)^2}\,dw. \tag{15} \] Indeed the coefficient in (13) is the enclosing residue of \(z_N(z)^s/\mathcal P_N(z)\), and \(\mathcal P_N(w+w^{-1})=w^{-N}(1+w^N)^2\). Expanding on the ACTUAL outer circle yields the finite coefficient identity \[ \boxed{\displaystyle \mathcal A_{s,N}=(-1)^dN^2 \sum_{m=1}^{\lfloor(sM+1)/N\rfloor}(-1)^{m-1}m \left([w^{mN-1}]-[w^{mN+1}]\right) z_N(w+w^{-1})^s.} \tag{16} \] Coefficients outside the Laurent degree range are zero. The \(m\) weight is exactly the double-pole/normal source from (12); it must not be dropped. For \(s=3\) only \(m=1\) can occur. This gives a fixed finite set of true winding channels at each fixed \(s\), not an identification of independent logarithmic aliases. No separation of the unit-circle poles or omission of the \(w=0\) Laurent behavior is used: (15) is an exact parametrization of the original enclosing residue, and (16) is its convergent outer Laurent expansion. The source in (14) is oscillatory. Positive \(b_v\) do not make the \(f_v(c_j)\) real positive, and taking separate absolute values of the nodal terms need not give the sharp antiprism volume. A selected asymptotic evaluation retaining these phases and integer Fourier marks is still required. No nonzero geometric coefficient, open cusp-color corridor or simultaneous long-filling survival is claimed by this exact finite reduction.

title: An exact cusp-color split with a controlled original normal-source remainder
text: # An exact cusp-color split with a controlled original normal-source remainder 29 October 2026. For every \(j=N-r\) with \(0\leq r\leq\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\), the literal rotated pretzel circle box has a positive half-degree core plus an ORIGINAL crossing times a degree-\(r-1\) polynomial. The entire second band, including every Casimir normal jet, has norm at most \(56^r\) in a faithful source-compatible Hermite norm. Thus it costs \(\exp(O(\delta N))\) on a fixed cusp-color corridor \(r\leq\delta N\), and subexponentially when \(r=o(N)\). No term is deleted. This is not yet a geometric survival theorem. The low core still requires its selected asymptotic analysis; estimates of a remainder do not prove that the whole original coefficient is nonzero. ## 1. The entire rotated polynomial, with its two support bands Use the original conventions and actual rotation \(\mathscr R\) of [the complete-base polynomial theorem](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md). Let \(f_v\) be the physical middle-degree continuant polynomials, \(s_a=|(Q;Q)_a|\), \(M=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\), \(d=N-1\). Then \[ \mathscr R(R^{-1}L_{N-r})=z_{N,r}(\Omega),\qquad z_{N,r}(z)=\kappa^{-1}\sum_{v=0}^d a_{r,v}f_v(z), \] \[ \boxed{\quad a_{r,v}=s_{d-v}^2q^{r^2-v^2} {2v\brack v-r}_Q.\quad} \tag{1} \] The Gaussian coefficient is its finite polynomial, not an invalid factorial ratio at a root. A negative lower index gives zero. For the displayed cusp corridor its support and all phases are exactly \[ a_{r,v}=\frac{s_{d-v}^2s_{2v}}{s_{v-r}s_{v+r}}>0, \quad r\leq v\leq M, \tag{2} \] \[ a_{r,N-t}=(-1)^{N-t-r} \frac{s_{t-1}^2s_{t+r-1}}{s_{2t-1}s_{r-t}}, \quad 1\leq t\leq r, \tag{3} \] and it is zero elsewhere. In particular the middle band is exactly zero. For \(r=0\), (2) is the positive complete-base coefficient \(b_v=N^2s_{2v}/s_v^4\), and there is no upper band. Proof by a finite resolvent, not a semiclassical approximation. In the low block of degree \(K=d-v\), the first-to-last entry of \((I-tJ_K+t^2I)^{-1}\) is \[ \frac{t^K B_K}{\prod_{k=0}^K(1-q^{2k+1}t)(1-q^{-2k-1}t)}, \qquad B_K=(-1)^Ks_K^2. \] Its \(t^{j-1}\) coefficient is the first-to-last entry of \(U_{j-1}(J_K/2)\). The full two-copy root orbit factors the inverse denominator as \[ \frac{(q^{1-2v}t;Q)_{2v}}{(1+t^N)^2}. \] The needed remaining coefficient has degree \(v-r<N\), so the denominator contributes exactly 1. The finite q-binomial theorem, the original circle sign \((-1)^{j-1}\), and the literal \(R^{-1}\) last-row coefficient give precisely (1). This derivation retains both the actual pivotal circle normalization and its half twist. If \(2v<N\), the Gaussian phase in (1) cancels, giving (2). If \(2v\geq N\) and \(v-r<N\), split one whole root orbit from the finite q-binomial product. Its factor has no coefficient in degrees \(1,\ldots,N-1\). Thus \({2v\brack v-r}_Q={2v-N\brack v-r}_Q\), which is zero unless \(v+r\geq N\). Taking its explicit phase and complementing the remaining sine factorials gives (3). This proves the exact bands without division by a vanished factorial. ## 2. The upper band is an original crossing times a SHORT polynomial Let \(\bar f_l\) mean coefficient conjugation at the specified principal root. Reversing the physical Jacobi recurrence gives \[ f_{d-l}(\Omega)=f_d(\Omega)\bar f_l(\Omega), \qquad f_d(\Omega)=x^d r_N(\Omega). \] Indeed \(e_0^Tf_d(A)=e_d^T\) and \(e_d^T\bar f_l(A)=e_{d-l}^T\); the cyclic first row proves the polynomial identity modulo the FULL \(\mathcal P_N\), including every double root. Since \(x^d=\kappa^2\), define \[ c_{N,r}(z)=\kappa^{-1}\sum_{v=r}^M a_{r,v}f_v(z), \quad P_{N,r}(z)=\sum_{t=1}^r(-1)^{N-t-r} \frac{s_{t-1}^2s_{t+r-1}}{s_{2t-1}s_{r-t}} \bar f_{t-1}(z). \] The exact ALL-INPUT identity is \[ \boxed{\quad z_{N,r}(\Omega)=c_{N,r}(\Omega) +R P_{N,r}(\Omega).\quad} \tag{4} \] For \(r=1\) its remainder is \((-1)^N R\). Thus the short sector is not identically zero, and it cannot be removed by restricting to the original cup or by retaining only the complete-circle quotient. ## 3. Uniform quantitative bound WITH every original normal jet On \(\mathbb C[z]/(\mathcal P_N)\) use the faithful Hermite norm \[ \|f\|_{\mathrm H}= \max\left\{\max_{c\ \mathrm{double}} (|f(c)|+N^{-2}|f'(c)|),\quad |f(-2)|\ \mathrm{if\ }N\mathrm{\ is\ odd}\right\}. \tag{5} \] It includes values and ALL first-normal coefficients; the simple node has only its value. It is submultiplicative. The literal crossing has \(\|R\|_{\mathrm H}\leq9/8\), by its original unit nodal values and \(|r_N'/r_N|\leq N^2/8\). The original source has \[ |\Phi_2(f)|\leq3N^3\|f\|_{\mathrm H}. \tag{6} \] This follows immediately from the exact source values and derivatives in the complete-base theorem. In particular this norm does not discard the nilpotent source as an ordinary semisimple quotient would. There is a constant independent of \(N,r\), explicitly \[ \boxed{\quad \|R P_{N,r}\|_{\mathrm H}\leq56^r, \qquad 1\leq r\leq M.\quad} \tag{7} \] Here is a direct proof of the bound, including the cancellation of small factorial denominators. Write the MONIC physical continuant as \(p_l=(a_0\cdots a_{l-1})f_l\), so \(|a_0\cdots a_{l-1}|=s_l^2\). On \(|z|\leq2\), its recurrence has \(|z-D_l|\leq12\) and \(|a_{l-1}^2|\leq16\). Induction gives \[ |p_l(z)|\leq14^l,\qquad |p_l'(z)|\leq l14^{l-1}. \] The coefficient in (3) divided by \(s_{t-1}^2\) has magnitude \[ \frac{s_{t+r-1}}{s_{2t-1}s_{r-t}} =\left|{t+r-1\brack 2t-1}_Q\right| \leq {t+r-1\choose 2t-1}\leq4^r. \] The first inequality follows from the nonnegative integer coefficients of the finite Gaussian polynomial (or its elementary Pascal induction), since its argument has modulus one. Therefore the \(s_{t-1}^2\) CANCELS the full denominator of \(\bar f_{t-1}\) before estimating any normal derivative. Summing the geometric series in \(14^{t-1}\), and multiplying by \(9/8\), proves (7) with room to spare. No \(N^{O(r)}\) loss occurs. There is also a full physical operator bound \[ \|P_{N,r}(\Omega)\|_{\rm op}\leq120^r, \qquad \|R P_{N,r}(\Omega)\|_{\rm op} \leq120^r\|R\|_{\rm op}. \tag{8} \] Indeed every physical \(\Omega\) block has norm at most18; the same monic recurrence is bounded by \(30^l\) when evaluated at this operator. The preceding factorial cancellation proves (8). The factor \(\|R\|\) cannot be discarded: already \(r=1\) the remainder is the whole original crossing. Thus (7), which is the faithful normal-source bound needed here, is stronger than a claim of uniform physical contraction would be and has a different scope. ## 4. Exact simultaneous original-source error accounting For arbitrary fixed \(s\), substitute (4) at every augmented pretzel box BEFORE applying the original source. The difference between the complete mixed-color period and its low-core product is exactly the sum over nonempty subsets of the retained remainder boxes. Equations (5)--(7) give the explicit bound, with \(\epsilon_0=0\) and \(\epsilon_r=56^r\) for \(r\geq1\), \[ \left|\Phi_2\left(\prod_i z_{N,r_i} -\prod_i c_{N,r_i}\right)\right| \leq3N^3\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subset\{1,\ldots,s\}} \prod_{i\in S}\epsilon_{r_i} \prod_{i\notin S}\|c_{N,r_i}\|_{\mathrm H}. \tag{9} \] For \(r_i\leq\delta N\) the individual retained source remainders have rate at most \(\delta\log56\); for \(r_i=o(N)\) that rate is zero. This is an independently quantified actual source term. It does not make the TOTAL right side negligible relative to the geometric period without estimates of the coherent core and its selected action gap. No open-corridor noncancellation or long-filling survival is asserted from (9) alone.

title: Survival of the original filling sum restricted to a cusp-color corridor
text: # Survival of the original filling sum restricted to a cusp-color corridor 29 October 2026. For every fixed odd box count s>=5 there is a fixed complete-color corridor in which the ENTIRE original coherent filling sum has a nonzero selected asymptotic, for all independently sufficiently large signed integer slopes. This includes all physical normal jets, the actual half-color weight, every Fourier charge and the original marked source. It does not estimate the complementary physical colors, and therefore is not yet a theorem about the whole filled knot. ## 1. The precise truncated ORIGINAL scalar Use q,Q,kappa,d and the original mixed marked source A_(s,N)(h). For an integer P let beta_j^(P) be the ACTUAL circle-basis coefficient of r_N^(2P); the full R^(2P) includes the factor kappa^(2P). Choose a sufficiently small fixed delta>0 and H=floor(delta N). For fixed nonzero integers p_i define \[ \mathcal K_{N,\delta}^{\boldsymbol p} =\kappa^{-2\sum_i p_i} \sum_{h_1,\ldots,h_s=0}^{H} \prod_i\beta_{N-h_i-1}^{(-p_i)} A_{s,N}(h_1,\ldots,h_s). \tag{1} \] This is the indicated physical color corridor of the actual boxes rotation(R^(-(2p_i+1))). It is not a single color term. No new modified dimension is placed on the ordinary auxiliary loops. There is p_0(s,delta) such that for EVERY FIXED tuple |p_i|>=p_0, with no comparability condition between slopes, (1) has \[ \boxed{\mathcal K_{N,\delta}^{\boldsymbol p} =N^{3/2}e^{-is\pi d/4}\kappa^{-\sum_i p_i} D_s(\boldsymbol p)e^{N\mathcal A_s(\boldsymbol p)} (1+O_{s,\boldsymbol p}(N^{-1})),} \tag{2} \] where D_s is explicitly specified below and is NONZERO. This holds at both parities and all composite levels as N tends to infinity. The slopes are fixed before this limit; no claim uniform in growing slopes is made. ## 2. The source action, actual Fourier amplitude and leading constant Let C_N be the EXACT finite packet in [the analytic color-source theorem](actual_pretzel_exact_analytic_color_packet.md). It has the SAME original full-Hermite Phi_2 functional. Its uniform complex asymptotic supplies A_s(chi),Phi_s(chi), with F_0=Phi_s(0)=V_s/(2pi), A_s(0)=C_s !=0, phi(x)=Phi_s(pi x), phi''(0)=2pi i tau_s I, tau_s=(1+exp(2iu_s))/2, Im tau_s>0. The exact Fourier-packet theorem in [the source Fourier estimate](actual_filling_source_fourier_endpoint_gap.md), section6, gives holomorphic even functions xi(z),Psi(z),B(z): grad phi(xi)+2pi i z=0, Psi(z)=phi(xi)+2pi i xi dot z, B(z)=(2pi)^(s/2) A_s(pi xi)/sqrt(det[-phi''(xi)]). Thus Psi=F_0-i pi sum z_i^2/tau_s+O(||z||^4), and B is nonzero near zero. These are defined by the original selected packet, not an arbitrary classical branch. Put T_m(z)=Psi(z)-2pi i sum_i(p_i z_i^2+m_i z_i). For sufficiently large |p_i| the all-unit charge m=(1,...,1) has the unique nearby critical point z_*=z_(1,...,1). Define \[ \mathcal A_s(\boldsymbol p)=T_{\boldsymbol1}(z_*),\qquad D_s(\boldsymbol p)= \frac{2^s(2\pi)^{s/2}B(z_*)\prod_i\sinh(2\pi i z_{*,i})} {\sqrt{\det[-T_{\boldsymbol1}''(z_*)]}}. \tag{3} \] Every square root is the one from the actual translated real Gaussian contour. Equivalently it is the analytic Gaussian branch on complex symmetric matrices with positive definite real part, fixed positive on real positive matrices. This retains the signed slope Gaussian phases, rather than choosing their moduli. The [local charge theorem](actual_pretzel_long_filling_charge_selection.md) proves that every z_(star,i) is nonzero, |z_(star,i)|<1/4, and the Hessian is nondegenerate. Consequently every factor in (3) is nonzero. In particular D_s is not a postulated cycle coefficient. The actual critical action has Re A_s(p)=F_0-pi Im(tau_s) sum_i |1+2p_i tau_s|^(-2)+O(sum_i |p_i|^(-4)), where the exact holomorphic action in (3), not this truncation, is used in (2). Its geometric peripheral interpretation is separate. ## 3. Exact source replacement and finite charge reduction The source theorem proves, on the physical grid in (1), |A_(s,N)(h)-C_N(pi h/N)| <=poly(N)exp[N(F_0-gamma)], gamma>0. Since |beta_j^(-p)|<=2(1+|p|), replacing A by C in the WHOLE truncated sum costs poly_(s,p)(N)exp[N(F_0-gamma)]. The upper color aliases need not be even and are estimated here, BEFORE folding. No full physical source is analytically continued by fiat. The exact C_N is even in each color. Apply the physical Weyl half weight and the full normal kernel in every coordinate. With mathcalF_N(z)=sum_(|h_i|<=H) C_N(pi h/N)exp(2pi i h dot z), the SAME truncated packet is exactly \[ (-1)^{s(N-1)}\kappa^{-\sum_i p_i} \sum_{m_i\ne0}(-1)^{(N-1)\sum_i m_i}\prod_i m_i \int_{[-1/2,1/2]^s} e^{-2\pi iN\sum_i(p_i z_i^2+m_i z_i)} \prod_i\sinh(2\pi i z_i)\mathcal F_N(z)\,dz. \tag{4} \] The source Fourier theorem proves a UNIFORM exponentially gapped tail outside |m_i|<=M_i, where one may take M_i>=2|p_i|+2delta+2. Its gap depends only on the SOURCE, not on the largest slope: the paired vertical current keeps its growth exp(2pi|p_i|Nv), which the larger charge absorbs. Shrinking the contour as 1/|p_i| would not give the needed independent-slope conclusion. Its multiport use is exact telescoping of commuting COLOR-register functionals, not a physical operator relocation: remove one high charge with every remaining coordinate still on its original REAL finite grid or in a FINITE real charge integral. Those spectators have unit-modulus chirps, and their fixed derivatives/sums cost only powers of N. Formula (14a) in the source Fourier note gives the precise identity and uniform mixed-derivative estimate. No other port is moved to a complex saddle until all such tails are removed. The same theorem shows that mathcalF_N and its fixed derivatives are exponentially small whenever any real |z_i|>=eta for fixed sufficiently small eta>0. Thus only a finite set of nonzero charges and a fixed central real z-cube remain, with original side currents already included in the errors. On a fixed complex neighborhood of that cube, the EXACT Fourier packet has its nonzero, uniform asymptotic with exponent Psi and prefactor N^((s+3)/2)B. This is established BEFORE moving any central charge contour. ## 4. Nonlocal finite charges have a fixed gap Choose the local charge scale t_0 from the local charge theorem much smaller than the central analytic z-window. If some |m_i/p_i|>=t_0, split its REAL coordinate into |z_i|<=t_0/4 and its complement. The complement has a fixed source Fourier gap, regardless of the other real coordinates. On the inner interval, m_i+2p_i z_i has the sign of m_i and magnitude at least |p_i|t_0/2. For sufficiently large |p_i| the bounded normal derivative of Psi cannot change that sign. Shift z_i by -i sigma sign(m_i) for a fixed small sigma>0. The real part of the filling phase decreases along the entire translation, including BOTH endpoint connectors. The real part of the chirp derivative is controlled because p_i is real, with either sign; its imaginary normal derivative depends on the combination m_i+2p_i Re z_i. The exact analytic Fourier packet remains within its proved complex neighborhood. At the connectors' starting points the source Fourier gap already holds. On the translated inner segment the phase drops by a fixed positive amount when |p_i| is large enough. This gives an absolute bound poly_(s,p)(N)exp[N(F_0-g_0)] for every such finite charge, with g_0>0 independent of the particular large slopes. The number of finite charges depends on p but not on N. No finite-order integration-by-parts error is substituted for this exponential gap. ## 5. Local finite charges: actual contour and noncancellation For |m_i/p_i|<=t_0 the local charge theorem gives a unique saddle z_m, with z_(m,i)=-m_i tau_s/(1+2p_i tau_s)+O(|p_i|^(-1)||m/p||^3), |Im z_(m,i)|<=C |p_i|^(-1)|m_i/p_i|. The second estimate is COMPONENTWISE: it follows from the exact separate-evenness factorization (12) in the local charge theorem, not merely its coarser multivariate Taylor remainder. It is what allows unrelated filling lengths in the next contour estimate. Translate the small real integration cube to the parallel real cube through Im z_m. Its saddle has real coordinates strictly inside that cube. The endpoint connectors stay below the selected height: their original source Fourier gap is fixed, while |p_i Im z_(m,i)|<=C t_0 and |m_i Im z_(m,i)|<=C t_0^2. Taking t_0 sufficiently smaller than the cube width controls these changes uniformly for independently unequal signed slopes. On the translated cube the REAL Hessian of T_m is the real Hessian of Psi; the quadratic filling chirp has purely imaginary Hessian. It is uniformly negative definite. The critical point is therefore the unique real maximum on that translated contour and its ends have a strict Gaussian gap. Holomorphic Gaussian expansion of the EXACT packet, with its uniform complex asymptotic, yields the nonzero contribution N^(3/2)e^(-is pi d/4) kappa^(-sum p_i) parity(m) (2pi)^(s/2) B(z_m) [product_i m_i sinh(2pi i z_(m,i))] exp[N T_m(z_m)]/sqrt(det[-T_m''(z_m)]) *(1+O_(s,p)(1/N)). Here parity(m)=(-1)^((s+sum_i m_i)(N-1)) is unchanged by every coordinate reflection. The factor N^(s/2) from the source Fourier packet cancels the z Gaussian N^(-s/2); the original N^(3/2) marked-source factor remains. For fixed slopes, all nonminimal local charges have a strict gap below the unit charges: Re T_m(z_m)<=Re T_1(z_*) -(b/8)sum_i(m_i^2-1)/p_i^2, b>0. This is the exact monotonicity theorem, not a quadratic guess. The minimal charges m_i=+/-1 have identical contributions by the EXACT reflected source integral. Their parity factor is one, and their products m_i sinh are unchanged under reflection. Their 2^s contributions ADD and give precisely (3). Finally, Re A_s(p) tends to F_0 as all |p_i| tend to infinity. Choose p_0 large enough that its deficit is smaller than half every fixed source, high-charge and nonlocal-charge gap above. This absorbs all absolute source errors. For each fixed tuple the remaining local nonminimal gap may be small, but is strictly positive and is exponential in N. The leading coefficient (3) is nonzero, so (2) follows. ## 6. The remaining whole-source gates This theorem is a source-preserving result for the PHYSICAL color corridor in (1). It retains every normal mode and does not discard the color complement h_i>H. That complement could still alter or cancel this contribution unless separately bounded. Nor is the identification of A_s(p) with a preferred filled hyperbolic action assumed: the auxiliary meridian and preferred-longitude sign must still be matched. Neither condition follows from local stationarity or from Cauchy alone. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_cusp_corridor_filling_survival.py) checks the full normalized-source chirp, signed Gaussian branches, N^(3/2) density and parity pairing on explicit analytic packets. The actual pretzel source hypotheses are the independently proved finite-packet and charge theorems linked above. Fresh replay: PASS 44 exact original full-normal coefficient families N=2,...,12, both signs; ten complete coherent analytic-packet asymptotic calibrations through N=513, including even/odd levels and unrelated signed slopes. The source Fourier companion also passed 21 exact normal/spectator splits, 12 finite side-current contour identities, 32 quantitative Fourier bounds, three exact paired-charge packets, three paired high-charge contours and 12 central complex Fourier calibrations. These checks supplement the proofs; the analytic-packet samples do not replace the actual pretzel source construction. Independent proof reads checked the source Fourier tail, central density, original phases and local assembly.

title: An exact analytic color packet carrying the original mixed pretzel source
text: # An exact analytic color packet carrying the original mixed pretzel source 29 October 2026. Fix an odd s>=5. There is an EXACT finite, holomorphic, separately even color packet C_N(chi_1,...,chi_s), defined using the original factorial coefficients and the full marked Hermite functional. It approximates the physical mixed-color source with a uniform, explicitly retained exponential gap in a fixed cusp corridor. The packet ITSELF, rather than merely its leading expression, satisfies a complex Gaussian growth bound. This is the source input needed before applying a Fourier/cotangent endpoint estimate. The theorem does not remove the rest of the physical color cube or identify a filled-knot volume. Those remain separate source terms. ## 1. Definition by actual finite coefficients and the original mark Use N,d,q,Q,kappa,M and the original f_v,P_r,Omega as in [the exact complete polynomial](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md). Let eta_s=2asinh(tan(pi/s)), R_s=exp eta_s, u_s=atan(sec(pi/s)), and F_0=V_s/(2pi). Choose FIXED numbers 1/4<a<u_s/pi<b<1/2, I_N={ceil(aN),...,floor(bN)}. For sufficiently large N this is a nonempty physical index window. Shrink a fixed complex chi disk so that |Re chi|/pi<a/2 and all arguments below lie in regular compact scaled factorial substrips. Put h=N chi/pi, and define the finite holomorphic function Ahat_(N,r)(chi)=sum_(v=r)^M Q^(-vr)F_(2v) /[F_v F_(v-r) Fhat_N(v-h)Fhat_N(v+h)], r in I_N. Here F_a=(Q;Q)_a at the physical integers, and Fhat is the canonical whole factorial completion with its ORIGINAL marks. Define the polynomial c_N^win(z,chi)=N^2 sum_(r in I_N) b_(N,r)(chi) B_r(z), b_(N,r)(chi)=kappa^(-1)q^(h^2)(-1)^r q^(2r^2+r) Ahat_(N,r)(chi)/F_r^3, B_r(z)=product_(v=0)^(r-1)(c_v-z), c_v=q^(2v+1)+q^(-2v-1). (1) The powers q^(h^2)=exp(iN chi^2/pi) and the full kappa are KEPT. They are not replaced by absolute values or a fitted period scale. This polynomial is a finite explicit function, not an asymptotic definition. It has degree at most floor(bN)<M+1 and is even in chi. Its coefficients are holomorphic on a fixed complex disk, uniformly in the sense of domains, since each denominator Fhat(v+/-h) is nonzero there. Use the ORIGINAL full-Hermite marked functional Phi_2(f)=(-1)^d sum_(c double) [(4-c^2)f'(c)-c f(c)] +1_(N odd)f(-2), where the double and possible simple nodes are those of P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2. The exact packet is C_N(chi_1,...,chi_s)=Phi_2(product_i c_N^win(z,chi_i)). (2) It is holomorphic and even in EACH color. Every original Casimir normal derivative remains in (2). No positive quotient, ordinary semisimple trace, or modified dimension for auxiliary components is substituted. An external original normalization, if required, is still multiplied separately with its already proved value. Equivalently, for ANY fixed R>1, the SAME exact packet is C_N=(-1)^d N^2/(2pi i) integral_(|w|=R) product_i c_N^win(w+w^(-1),chi_i) w^N(1-w^(-2))/(1+w^N)^2 dw. (3) This is the established residue formula for the actual marked source. It keeps all finite windings, including the double-pole normal weight. Formula (2), or (3), is the definition of C_N; no unknown scalar knot period defines its metric or amplitude. ## 2. Exact relation to the physical mixed source and its residual At an actual integer deficit 0<=h<aN/2, Fhat(v+/-h)=F_(v+/-h) for every v>=r in I_N. Thus (1) is EXACTLY the indicated Newton window of the physical low core c_(N,h). The finite source identity proves z_(N,h)=c_(N,h)+R P_(N,h), with the actual nonzero upper band retained separately. Put A_N(h)=Phi_2(product_i z_(N,h_i)). The exact residual is A_N(h)-C_N(pi h/N) =Phi_2(product_i z_(N,h_i)-product_i c_(N,h_i)) +Phi_2(product_i c_(N,h_i) -product_i c_N^win(pi h_i/N)). (4) There is a fixed corridor 0<=h_i<=delta_s N and gamma_s>0 such that, uniformly on this physical color grid, |A_N(h)-C_N(pi h/N)| <=poly(N)exp[N(F_0-gamma_s)]. (5) Here are the two bounds, so neither residual in (4) is silently discarded. The first is the proved [uniform original RP-band source gap](actual_pretzel_mixed_alias_source_gap.md) for odd s>=5. For the second, use the REAL-color all-index bound from the mixed-source theorem and the original circle estimate at R_s. The complete positive Newton profile J_R+E has its unique maximum at u_s, so g_I=j(eta_s)-max_(u/pi outside(a,b))(J_R(u)+E(u))>0. Every removed r-summand has circle height at most j(eta_s)-g_I+C chi^2, and every retained or full core has height at most j(eta_s)+C chi^2, with polynomial prefactors. Telescope the product of s cores and use the EXACT source-circle bound from (3). This gives |second residual|<=poly(N) exp[N(F_0-g_I+C sum_i chi_i^2)]. First fix the index window and its gap, then shrink delta_s to preserve at least half this gap and the independent RP gap. This proves (5). The underlying sums in (4) remain the actual source terms. The estimate is absolute, so it remains usable before a subsequent filling sum with its known polynomial coefficient mass. It is not an assertion that those terms vanish. No complex continuation of the FULL physical low-index or upper-band source is needed for (5). Only the EXACT packet (2) is continued. ## 3. The exact packet has a uniform complex-color asymptotic After shrinking its fixed chi disk, the packet ITSELF satisfies C_N(chi)=N^(3/2)exp(-i s pi d/4) A_s(chi)exp[N Phi_s(chi)](1+O(1/N)), (6) UNIFORMLY on a fixed closed complex polydisk. The analytic functions are those in the [mixed-cusp construction](actual_pretzel_mixed_cusp_period_survival.md), and A_s is nonzero there. This statement is stronger than a pointwise approximation to the original real-grid full source. It follows by applying that construction to (2) as follows. First, the high-window coefficients are the natural COMPLEX-color factorial source. The literal endpoint wall makes their continued fractions exact on every physical r-grid, even when chi is complex. The source theorem supplies a uniformly analytic action interpolant, and its original-grid residual is relatively O(exp(-cN)), uniformly in that complex color disk. The analytic Newton factor has its proved prefactor ONE with all the original logarithmic marks. Second, use the EXACT finite half-grid cotangent rectangle for the r-window. Its vertical sides have |cot(Nu)|<=1 and a fixed endpoint gap. Its horizontal remainders are O(exp(-2Nd)); their complete phase grows only O(d^2) under that fixed vertical displacement. Choose d first, then the fixed complex eta,chi neighborhoods. All these remainders, INCLUDING the retained grid residual, are exponentially below the complex saddle. The two constant cotangent parts give the same analytic saddle integral with total density N/pi. Uniform analytic Gaussian expansion gives the nonzero box amplitude a(eta,chi), with the original exp(-i pi d/4) factor. This proves the local box asymptotic for the EXACT high-window polynomial at complex eta,chi. Third, control the rest of the w circle WITHOUT invoking real-color estimates on an off-grid source. The high-window WKB and canonical factorial ratio imply, directly on the physical r-grid, |b_(N,r)(chi)|<=poly(N)[s_(2r)/s_r^6] exp(CN|chi|^2). The finite Newton factor B_r(w) has the old strict angular envelope away from w=-R_s, uniformly for a<=r/N<=b. Thus the exact packet's noncentral circle parts have a fixed exponential gap for all small COMPLEX chi. These estimates concern only the explicit finite packet, whose domain contains that entire complex color polydisk. Finally insert the analytic box asymptotic into the ORIGINAL source contour (3). The nearby eta saddle has nonzero Hessian, stays in Re eta>0, and is reached by a local contour shift with gapped end connectors. No pole of (3) is crossed. The original sign and normal kernel give exactly N^(3/2) and the amplitude A_s in (6). The exact packet's exponential interpolation remainders stay below this saddle after a fixed further shrink of the color disk. This proves (6) uniformly in complex colors; it is NOT inferred by analytic continuation of a pointwise real-grid error estimate. ## 4. A genuine complex Gaussian growth estimate for C_N itself Write u_s=atan(sec(pi/s)) and a_0=sin(2u_s)/(2pi)>0, b_0=(1+cos(2u_s))/(2pi). The actual source curvature is Phi_s(chi)=F_0+(-a_0+i b_0)sum_i chi_i^2+O(||chi||^4). For chi=x+i y, the real quadratic part is -a_0||x||^2+a_0||y||^2-2b_0 sum_i x_i y_i <=-(a_0/2)||x||^2 +(a_0+2b_0^2/a_0)||y||^2. Shrink the fixed complex polydisk until the quartic remainder is at most (a_0/4)(||x||^2+||y||^2). Then (6), with bounded A_s, proves an ACTUAL uniform inequality |C_N(x+i y)|<=C_s N^(3/2) exp{N[F_0-a_s||x||^2+B_s||y||^2]}, (7) a_s=a_0/4, B_s=5a_0/4+2b_0^2/a_0. The constants and the color domain are independent of N. The uniform relative O(1/N) error in (6) changes only C_s. In particular (7) is a bound on the EXACT source function (2), not on A_s exp(N Phi_s) after discarding a polynomially small error. For Fourier estimates in the physical variable h/N, substitute chi=pi h/N; both quadratic constants are multiplied by pi^2. Because the packet is exactly even in every color, the actual complete-color coefficient retains its physical half weight under the proved Weyl fold. No extra 2N average, ordinary trace, or one-sided exp(pi i h) completion is introduced. ## 5. Precisely what can now be combined with filling The [Fourier endpoint lemma](actual_filling_source_fourier_endpoint_gap.md) may be applied to the exact packet C_N, or to a slice of it with the other colors retained, using (7). The physical error (5) is still a separate explicit source term and must be multiplied by the actual filling coefficient mass before estimating it. For fixed twists that mass is polynomial, so its fixed gap is preserved. This handles only the displayed small cusp-color window. The complement of that physical color window, its upper RP bands, other Fresnel charges and the geometric identification of the filled critical action require their own proofs. Neither (5) nor (7) licenses deletion of those parts of the original filling source. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_exact_analytic_color_packet.py) checks the literal finite polynomial/source definition, its marked phases, exact evenness and retained physical source decomposition; complex growth diagnostics supplement the uniform proof above. Fresh replay: PASS six original physical source families N=5,...,10, each with five genuine boxes, retained color deficits, all E/F/R normalizations and the full marked transfer. The same packet is independently evaluated by the full physical pivotal trace and the Hermite coefficient-residue functional. Its low-index and RP residuals are checked as exact separate source terms. Four further canonical complex-color families verify separate exact evenness and the unchanged derivative source. These diagnostics do not establish an exponential estimate from finite samples; bounds (5),(7) follow from the proofs above.

title: Literal pretzel coefficient phase, marked geometric saddles, and their action
text: # Literal pretzel coefficient phase, marked geometric saddles, and their action **Subsequent global proof.** The [full coherent period asymptotic](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) now establishes complete augmented-source survival by a finite inner transformation, a global two-branch bound and real Gaussian estimates. The local symbol audit below remains a separate verification; it is not being promoted to a survival proof by itself. 29 October 2026. This independently checks the leading phase from the EXACT finite factorial coefficients, its branch marks, all regular stationary equations, and the nonzero full Hessian. The geometric action has an explicit Lobachevsky formula. These are symbol and local saddle statements only: no deformation of the original finite source, nonzero thimble coefficient, or asymptotic dominance is proved here. ## 1. The actual finite term fixes the phase Use the original complete-base polynomial [with its source normalization](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md): \[ \frac{\kappa z_N(w+w^{-1})}{N^2} =\sum_{0\leq r\leq v\leq M}t_{v,r}(w),\quad t_{v,r}=\frac{F_{2v}}{F_v^4} \frac{(Q^{-v};Q)_rQ^r}{F_r^3} (qw;Q)_r(q/w;Q)_r, \qquad M=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor. \tag{1} \] Here F_a=(Q;Q)_a, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, and the original kappa=q^((N-1)^2/2) is retained. On the interior physical index triangle put X=Q^v, Y=Q^r. In a regular product-log chart the leading exponent of the normalized term is N S/(2pi i), where \[ \begin{split} S={}&-6\operatorname{Li}_2(1)-\operatorname{Li}_2(X^2) +4\operatorname{Li}_2(X)+\operatorname{Li}_2(X^{-1}) -\operatorname{Li}_2(Y/X)\\ &+\operatorname{Li}_2(w)+\operatorname{Li}_2(w^{-1}) -\operatorname{Li}_2(wY)-\operatorname{Li}_2(Y/w) +3\operatorname{Li}_2(Y). \tag{2} \end{split} \] For example log F_v has leading N[Li2(1)-Li2(X)]/(2pi i). The first quotient in (1) gives -3Li2(1)-Li2(X^2)+4Li2(X). The terminating Pochhammer gives Li2(X^(-1))-Li2(Y/X), F_r^(-3) gives -3Li2(1)+3Li2(Y), and the two remaining products give the four w terms in (2). This is the product-log primitive continued from the physical triangle, not a separately chosen favorable potential. The factor Q^r is subleading in this scaling; the half-step q in the last two products affects subleading amplitudes. The full original z_N additionally contains kappa^(-1), whose unwrapped leading contribution to S is +pi^2, a REAL constant per box. No imaginary action or stationary equation is lost by recording it separately. There is a check avoiding all primitive choices. The EXACT adjacent finite term ratios are \[ \frac{t_{v+1,r}}{t_{v,r}}= \frac{(1-Q^{2v+1})(1-Q^{2v+2})}{(1-Q^{v+1})^4} \frac{1-Q^{-v-1}}{1-Q^{r-v-1}}, \] \[ \frac{t_{v,r+1}}{t_{v,r}}= Q\frac{(1-Q^{r-v})(1-qwQ^r)(1-qQ^r/w)}{(1-Q^{r+1})^3}. \tag{3} \] Their regular limits are exactly exp(S_x), exp(S_y), for x=log X,y=log Y below. These identities retain the root phases before taking a limit. They do not extend an interior assertion to the terminating boundary r=v or to any collision divisor. ## 2. All regular sheets and the inner source marks In logarithmic coordinates x,y,t=log w, differentiating (2) gives \[ e^{S_x}=\frac{(1+X)^2}{(X-1)(X-Y)},\qquad e^{S_y}=\frac{(1-Y/X)(1-wY)(1-Y/w)}{(1-Y)^3},\qquad e^{S_t}=\frac{wY-1}{w-Y}. \tag{4} \] A regular dilogarithm sheet change adds 2pi i times an INTEGER linear form in x,y,t, plus a real multiple of 4pi^2. This follows directly by continuing dLi2(z)=-Log(1-z)dLog z; every argument in (2) is an integer monomial. Thus (4) and the Hessian are sheet independent. A stationary PHASE also retains the corresponding integer Fourier/Poisson marks; exponentiating alone forgets them. When a sheet is changed those marks change by the same integer linear form. The combined marked phase has unchanged imaginary action. No choice of a different sheet may silently delete this compensating source mark. For an s-fold power in the actual positive winding m from the finite enclosing residue, the explicit regular geometric branch below uses PRINCIPAL dilogarithms. There one has S_x=0, S_y=2pi i, S_t=2i alpha, alpha=pi m/s. Consequently its locally stationary marked phase is \[ \mathcal F=\sum_{i=1}^s [S(X_i,Y_i,w)-2\pi i\log Y_i] -2\pi i m\log w. \tag{5} \] The inner y mark is compulsory on this sheet. It happens to change only the REAL action at the geometric point because |Y_i|=1; that does not justify dropping it before stationarity or continuation. On the conjugate/reciprocal branch its y mark is -1 instead. The exact finite winding weights, their double-pole multiplicities, and the original common Cartan are still those of the source formula. Equation (5) does not select a winding or a cycle for it. ## 3. Nondegenerate geometric solutions and the excluded factor In the regular locus, the first two equations e^(S_x)=e^(S_y)=1 imply \[ X=\frac{Y-1}{Y+3},\qquad w+w^{-1}=6-\frac{16Y}{(1+Y)^2}. \tag{6} \] Factors Y=0, Y=1, X=0, X=1 and all zero denominators must be excluded before using these rational equivalences. For the outer condition put U=exp(2pi i m/s). Then Y=(Uw+1)/(w+U), and exact substitution in the second equation of (6) yields \[ \frac{(w-1)^2}{w(w+U)^2} \{(1+U)^2(w^2+1)-2(U^2-6U+1)w\}=0. \tag{7} \] For U!= -1, the factor w=1 gives Y=1, a collision rather than a regular geometric saddle. It may not be retained as a nondegenerate stationary branch. On the regular branch, \[ w+w^{-1}=2-\frac{16U}{(1+U)^2} =2-4\sec^2\alpha. \tag{8} \] For 0<m<s/2, define \[ \eta=2\operatorname{arsinh}(\tan\alpha),\quad \beta=\arctan(\sec\alpha),\quad w=-e^\eta,\quad Y=e^{2i\beta},\quad X=\frac{i\sec\alpha}{2-i\sec\alpha}. \tag{9} \] These satisfy (4)--(8) and the marked derivatives in section 2. All their dilogarithm arguments remain regular for fixed alpha in (0,pi/2). This is the outside-|w| branch appropriate as a candidate for the actual enclosing-circle representation. The other regular solution for this U is obtained by w->1/w and (X,Y)->(conjugate X,conjugate Y); its imaginary action is the negative one. Neither statement proves a contour reaches either point. For fixed odd s, the positive finite-source windings are m=1,...,(s-1)/2 once N is sufficiently large, all within this range. The principal integer marks can be verified without numerical argument tracking. Put tau=sec(alpha)>1, A=atan(1/tau), B=atan(2/tau). The four principal arguments in S_x are respectively pi/2+A-2B, A-B, A, pi-A, with coefficients 2,-4,1,-1; their sum is exactly zero. For S_y, Arg(1-Y/X)=pi-A and Arg(1-Y)=-A. Both 1-wY and 1-Y/w lie in the upper half-plane, the latter in its right half. Their product, using (4), has principal argument pi-2A. Their argument sum is in (0,3pi/2), so it equals pi-2A without a full turn. Thus S_y has argument (pi-A)+(pi-2A)+3A=2pi. Finally S_t has imaginary part the difference of these last two positive arguments, which is in (-pi/2,pi). Equation (4) fixes it to 2alpha in (0,pi). The real parts vanish by the same rational equations. These prove the asserted 0,1,m/s marks on the entire connected branch. At s=3,m=1, (9) is exactly w=-7-4sqrt3, X=(-1+i)/2, Y=(-3+4i)/5. ## 4. The FULL saddle Hessian is nonzero Write the one-box Hessian in the logarithmic variables as \[ H_3=\begin{pmatrix}a&b&0\\b&d&e\\0&e&f\end{pmatrix}, \] where \[ a=\frac{2X}{1+X}-\frac X{X-1}-\frac X{X-Y}, \quad b=\frac Y{X-Y}, \] \[ d=-\frac Y{X-Y}-\frac{wY}{1-wY}-\frac Y{w-Y} +\frac{3Y}{1-Y}, \quad e=-\frac{wY}{1-wY}+\frac Y{w-Y}, \quad f=-1-\frac{wY}{1-wY}-\frac Y{w-Y}. \tag{10} \] After the first relation in (6), its determinant is exactly \[ \det H_3=-\frac{Y(Y-1)(Y+3)^2(w^2-6w+1)} {4(w-Y)(Y+1)^2(Yw-1)}. \tag{11} \] On the second relation of (6), the inner two-by-two block K_2 has \[ \det K_2=-\frac{Y^2(Y+3)^2(w-1)^2} {(w-Y)(Y+1)^3(Yw-1)}. \tag{12} \] Both are NONZERO at (9). In particular checking only three collective coordinates has not missed the antisymmetric modes of the s actual copies. The full (2s+1)-variable Hessian of (5) has \[ \boxed{\det\operatorname{Hess}\mathcal F =s(\det K_2)^{s-1}\det H_3\ne0.} \tag{13} \] This follows by its exact block Schur complement. Its effective outer entry, before summing the s copies, is det H3/det K2=i cos(alpha) on the expanding branch. It changes sign on the reciprocal branch. This is a local saddle fact, not a global maximum or a statement about the original integration-cycle intersection. For the FULL power z_N^s there are also mixed regular inner branches, which must not be suppressed. At a common negative w<-1 the two inner solutions are the plus solution (9) and its conjugate. Their outer characters are U and U^(-1), respectively, and their inner y marks are +1 and -1. With k plus copies, put n=2k-s. Since s is odd, n cannot vanish. On the principal product chart the positive winding condition is n>2m, alpha=pi m/n for the outside-|w| solutions. These are all regular stationary possibilities in this chart for a positive source winding: the inner quadratic has only its reciprocal Y pair; the outer product is U^n=1, and the regular elimination (7) then fixes negative real w. The zero-winding possibility U=1 is not part of the exact source sum, whose windings start at 1. In particular it need not be treated as a selected saddle of that source. The reciprocal-|w| solutions have a majority of conjugate copies and negative action. The exact mixed Hessian has outer Schur entry n i cos(alpha) and \[ \det\operatorname{Hess}\mathcal F =(\det K_2)^k(\overline{\det K_2})^{s-k} n i\cos\alpha\ne0. \tag{13a} \] This retains every one of the 2s independent inner variables. The binomial number of arrangements is finite for a fixed source width; it is not an additional exponential multiplicity as N grows. ## 5. The real imaginary-action formula Define Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log|2sin t| dt. For (9), the fully marked phase has \[ \boxed{\operatorname{Im}\mathcal F =8s\{\Lambda(\tfrac\pi4+\tfrac\alpha2) +\Lambda(\tfrac\pi4-\tfrac\alpha2)\}.} \tag{14} \] Here is a derivation that does not assume a known antiprism volume or the survival of this saddle. Set V(alpha)=Im S(X,Y,w)-2alpha eta. Along (9), y=2i beta and t=eta+i pi. The derivatives in section 2 give d(Im S)/dalpha=2alpha eta', V'=-2eta=-4arsinh(tan alpha). The right side of (14), divided by s, has the SAME derivative, since sin(pi/4+alpha/2)/sin(pi/4-alpha/2) =sec alpha+tan alpha, whose logarithm is arsinh(tan alpha). The common integration constant is zero at alpha->pi/2. To check the latter directly, X,Y tend to -1 and all bounded dilogarithms have vanishing imaginary limits. The only unbounded pair is Li2(w)-Li2(wY). The elementary inversion identity, proved by differentiation and evaluation at -1, Li2(z)+Li2(1/z)=-pi^2/6-(1/2)Log(-z)^2, shows that its imaginary part is 2beta eta+o(1). As beta-alpha=O(pi/2-alpha), 2(beta-alpha)eta tends to zero. Hence V tends to zero, as does the Lobachevsky expression. This proves (14). For s=3,m=1, triplication of Lambda gives the exact value 4v8, where v8=8Lambda(pi/4). The same formula for other s is the formal four-antiprism action with the stated winding alpha. This identification of a REAL formula does not assume that the original augmented link's invariant has this growth, or identify a filled knot from that action. The original-cycle/boundary and possible multi-winding cancellation questions remain outside this theorem. For completeness, the mixed branch with effective n in (13a) has the SAME formula with s replaced by n and alpha=pi m/n. This follows since the two inner actions are complex conjugates at negative real w; their imaginary parts subtract. All such mixed outside actions are strictly below the all-plus n=s action at the same m. Indeed V(alpha)>0 and V'(alpha)<0 for 0<alpha<pi/2, so \[ \frac d{dn}\{nV(\pi m/n)\}=V(\alpha)-\alpha V'(\alpha)>0. \tag{15} \] The all-plus action in turn strictly decreases with the positive winding m. Hence m=1 and n=s give the UNIQUE largest regular imaginary action among these actual positive-winding stationary systems, apart from identical labeling of equal copies. This is an interior critical-value gap, NOT a contour-height or boundary gap. In particular the equal-height diagonal collision boundary in the independent boundary analysis is not ruled out here. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_geometric_symbol.py) checks the literal finite ratios, exact elimination and Hessian identities, every positive winding at several odd widths, both reciprocal branches, the actual integer inner marks, and the full Lobachevsky action. It does not numerically estimate a selected cycle coefficient.

title: A global alias bound and the full original colored-source gap
text: # A global alias bound and the full original colored-source gap 29 October 2026. The entire original \(RP\) band has the uniform faithful-Hermite upper rate \[ B=\tfrac12\log(4+\sqrt{15}) <j_0=\frac{v_8}{\pi}. \tag{1} \] The proof uses the exact short-band coefficients, monic physical continuants, and an elementary spectral ellipse for their recurrence. It retains the value AND first normal coefficient at every double Casimir node. It requires no ordinary-color unitarity, Laurent positivity conjecture, or discarded endpoint sector. Combining this bound with the [proved global low-core bound](actual_pretzel_global_core_spectral_gap.md) gives a strict original-source gap outside every fixed complete-color corridor, over the ENTIRE auxiliary-color cube, for every fixed odd width \(s\geq25\). More generally the exact sufficient condition is \(A_s>(s-1)j_0+B\). This supplies a global-color input for long fillings; the selected cusp-corridor filling asymptotic and its peripheral identification remain separate. ## 1. Rewrite the exact short band before estimating it Use \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(M=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\). Let \(p_l\) be the MONIC physical middle-degree continuant: \[ p_0=1,\quad p_{-1}=0,\qquad p_{l+1}(z)=(z-D_l)p_l(z)-a_{l-1}^{\,2}p_{l-1}(z), \tag{2} \] \[ D_l=4qQ^l-q(1+Q)Q^{2l},\qquad a_{l-1}=-(1-Q^l)^2. \] Thus \(p_l=(a_0\cdots a_{l-1})f_l\). A bar on a polynomial denotes coefficient conjugation at this root. For \(1\leq h\leq\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), define the literal short polynomial by the same finite formula as the cusp split: \[ P_{N,h}= \sum_{t=1}^{h}(-1)^{N-t-h} \frac{s_{t-1}^2s_{t+h-1}}{s_{2t-1}s_{h-t}} \bar f_{t-1}. \tag{3} \] The endpoint \(h=N/2\) at even \(N\) is allowed in (3): the largest factorial index is \(2h-1=N-1\). It is needed for the actual middle auxiliary color, which has no low core. All small denominators in (3) cancel in the following exact polynomial identity: \[ \boxed{\quad (-1)^{N+h-1}P_{N,h}(z)= \sum_{l=0}^{h-1}(-1)^l q^{3l^2+4l+1-2hl-h} {h+l\brack 2l+1}_Q\,\bar p_l(z). \quad} \tag{4} \] Indeed \(s_a=i^a q^{-a(a+1)/2}F_a\). In the term \(t=l+1\), the factorial ratio not containing \(s_l^2\) becomes its Gaussian coefficient with the indicated phase. Also \(F_l^2\bar f_l=(-1)^lQ^{l(l+1)}\bar p_l\). These two phase simplifications give (4), including its sign. No factorial index in (4) reaches \(N\), and the Gaussian can equivalently be regarded as its finite polynomial. ## 2. A uniform monic-continuant bound with all source endpoints The required estimate is \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\ \max_{0\leq l\leq M}\ \frac1N\log\left(6^{-l} \max_{z\in[-2,2]}|p_l(z)|\right)\leq0. \tag{5} \] The initial vector in (2) is exactly \((p_0,p_{-1})=(1,0)\). Its coefficients have no singular endpoint. They are uniformly smooth functions of \(u=\pi l/N\), \(0\leq u\leq\pi/2\), with uniform \(O(1/N)\) error from their frozen classical values. Put \(V=e^{2iu}\). The eigenvalues of the frozen companion are \(V\lambda\), where \[ \lambda^2-d_z\lambda+a^2=0, \qquad d_z=zV^{-1}-4+2V,\qquad a=4\sin^2u. \tag{6} \] Both roots lie STRICTLY inside \(|\lambda|=6\), uniformly for \(0\leq u\leq\pi/2\), \(-2\leq z\leq2\). Here is an elementary verification, avoiding a chosen eigenbasis. For fixed \(a\leq4<6\), a root on \(|\lambda|=6\) makes \(d_z=\lambda+a^2/\lambda\), the ellipse with semiaxes \(6+a^2/6\) and \(6-a^2/6\). Both roots at \(d_z=0\) are inside that disk. The same segment-continuity argument used for the mixed-source ellipse therefore puts both roots inside whenever \(d_z\) is in the interior of this ellipse. The point \(d_z\) is affine in real \(z\), so convexity reduces the check to \(z=\pm2\). For \(z=2\), \(d_2=-2a\), and \(2a<6+a^2/6\) because \(a<6\). For \(z=-2\), put \(y=1-\cos(2u)\in[0,2]\), so \(a=2y\), \(d_{-2}=-4+4i\sin(2u)\). The ellipse condition is \[ \frac{36}{(9+y^2)^2} +\frac{36(2y-y^2)}{(9-y^2)^2}<1. \tag{7} \] After multiplication by \((81-y^4)^2>0\), its positive slack factors exactly as \[ (y^4+12y^2-36y+27)(y^4+24y^2-36y+135). \] The first factor equals \((y-1)^2(y^2+2y+3)+12(y-4/3)^2+8/3>0\). The second equals \(y^4+24(y-3/4)^2+243/2>0\). This proves the uniform strict root bound, including both index endpoints. For completeness, this spectral statement genuinely bounds the varying product in (2). Divide each frozen companion by 6. On the compact \((u,z)\) set the matrices are uniformly bounded and their eigenvalues have modulus at most 1. Cayley--Hamilton gives \(\|B^L\|\leq L\|B\|+L-1\leq C L\), including double roots. An exact block of fixed length \(L\) differs from the frozen power by \(O_L(1/N)\), uniformly in \(u,z\). Choose \(L\) large to make \(\log(CL)/L\) arbitrarily small, then choose \(N\) large and concatenate the blocks. The two incomplete blocks have bounded cost. This proves (5) uniformly in \(l,z\), without adiabatic eigenvector transport or an uncontrolled endpoint factor. ## 3. A global bound for the entire alias, including the normals At a unit root the finite Gaussian satisfies \(|{h+l\brack2l+1}_Q|\leq{h+l\choose2l+1}\), by its elementary Pascal polynomial expansion with nonnegative integer coefficients. Consequently (4)--(5) give a sequence \(\epsilon_N\to0\), independent of \(h\), with \[ \max_{[-2,2]}|P_{N,h}| \leq e^{\epsilon_NN} \sum_{l=0}^{h-1}{h+l\choose2l+1}6^l =e^{\epsilon_NN}U_{h-1}(4). \tag{8} \] The identity follows from the generating function \(\sum_{h\geq1}\sum_{l<h}{h+l\choose2l+1}K^l t^{h-1} =[1-(K+2)t+t^2]^{-1}\). The actual short polynomial has degree \(h-1\leq M\). Complex Markov on \([-2,2]\) therefore bounds its derivative by \((h-1)^2/2\) times its supremum. In the ORIGINAL faithful Hermite norm, with normal scale \(N^{-2}\), this costs at most \(9/8\). The literal crossing also has norm at most \(9/8\). Thus the whole original alias obeys \[ \boxed{\quad \|R P_{N,h}\|_{\mathrm H} \leq\frac{81}{64}e^{\epsilon_NN}U_{h-1}(4) \leq\frac{81}{128\sqrt{15}}e^{\epsilon_NN} (4+\sqrt{15})^h. \quad} \tag{9} \] It includes every value and every first normal coefficient. In particular, uniformly for \(1\leq h\leq\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), \[ \limsup_N\frac1N\log\|RP_{N,h}\|_{\mathrm H} \leq B=\tfrac12\log(4+\sqrt{15}). \tag{10} \] This is a source-compatible upper bound, not a claim that the alias is polynomial, nor an asserted sharp asymptotic for it. ## 4. Every original auxiliary color is covered For \(j>N/2\), put \(h=N-j\leq M\). The exact box is \(z_{N,h}=c_{N,h}+RP_{N,h}\), with a zero alias at \(h=0\). For \(1\leq j\leq\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), factorial complementation in the literal high band gives \[ \mathscr R(R^{-1}L_j)=(-1)^N RP_{N,j}. \tag{11} \] This includes \(j=N/2\) at even \(N\). Thus no middle color, normal channel or color endpoint is absent. The [global core theorem](actual_pretzel_global_core_spectral_gap.md), followed by complex Markov and the limit of its fixed radius \(R\downarrow1\), gives the uniform bound \[ \limsup_N\frac1N\log \max_{0\leq h\leq M}\|c_{N,h}\|_{\mathrm H} \leq j_0. \tag{12} \] Apply (9),(12) to the ORIGINAL source \(|\Phi_2(f)|\leq3N^3\|f\|_{\mathrm H}\). Any product term with a nonempty alias set of size \(m\) has uniform upper rate \[ (s-m)j_0+mB\leq(s-1)j_0+B, \tag{13} \] since \(B<j_0\). This applies across the ENTIRE original color cube, including low colors whose boxes are pure aliases. Let \(A_s=V_s/(2\pi)\). Whenever \[ \boxed{\qquad g_s:=A_s-(s-1)j_0>B,\qquad} \tag{14} \] all alias-containing original-source terms have a fixed exponential gap from the complete geometric period. The finite subset expansion costs at most \(2^s\), with \(s\) fixed. Condition (14) holds for EVERY odd \(s\geq25\). Indeed the previous elementary bound is \(g_s\geq j_0-\pi/[s\cos(\pi/s)]\). Here is a rational check at the smallest stated width: use \(\pi<22/7\), \(G>1-1/9+1/25-1/49+1/81-1/121\), \(\cos(\pi/25)>1-(22/175)^2/2\), and \(B<31/30\). These give a strictly positive rational lower margin greater than 0.00139. The last logarithmic bound follows by the first ten terms of the exponential series at \(31/15\): their sum is greater than \(4+\sqrt{15}\). Finally \(s\cos(\pi/s)\) increases with \(s\). ## 5. The full off-cusp original-source theorem Fix an odd \(s\geq25\) and any \(0<\delta<1/2\). There is \(\gamma_s(\delta)>0\) such that, uniformly over ALL actual auxiliary colors \(1\leq j_i\leq N\) with at least one \(j_i\leq N-\delta N\), \[ \boxed{\quad \limsup_N\frac1N\log \left|\mathcal A_{s,N}(j_1,\ldots,j_s)\right| \leq A_s-\gamma_s(\delta). \quad} \tag{15} \] The limsup includes the maximum over those color tuples. To prove it, if some color is at most \(N/2\), every term contains an alias, so (13)--(14) give the gap. Otherwise all boxes have the exact core-plus-alias split. Alias terms have the same gap; the all-core term has a strict source gap by the global core theorem because at least one deficit is at least \(\delta N\). Taking the smaller of the two positive gaps proves (15). In the exact original simultaneous filling sum, each fixed signed twist kernel has polynomial total coefficient mass \(\leq2N(1+|p_i|)\). Thus its ENTIRE off-cusp color contribution is bounded by \[ |\chi_N|\prod_i2N(1+|p_i|) \exp\{N[A_s-\gamma_s(\delta)+o(1)]\}. \tag{16} \] All original \(\kappa\) factors are unit phases, and the original \(\chi_N\) is displayed rather than absorbed. The estimate is before any asymptotic deletion of filling normal data; their exact Fourier--Hermite kernel is used with its proved total mass. Equation (16) does not yet prove a filled-knot asymptotic. One must still analyze the original coherent cusp-corridor sum, identify its peripheral marking, and prove its selected contribution. The present theorem removes the global-color obstruction for the stated broad fixed-width family; it does not replace those remaining tasks by a positive comparison invariant.

title: A global color gap for the actual coherent low core
text: # A global color gap for the actual coherent low core 29 October 2026. The literal mixed-source recurrence has a global two-branch upper envelope no larger than the complete-color envelope. Every macroscopic nonzero color deficit gives a STRICT contraction on a fixed high-index interval, uniformly even at the repeated-root color. Together with the proved coherent circle profile, this yields a strict circle and original-source gap for the low cores at all colors \(0\leq h\leq\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\) outside a fixed complete-color corridor. This is a theorem about the **actual low core**. The original nonzero crossing-times-short-polynomial band \(RP_{N,h}\) remains separate. Its global macroscopic-color bound is not supplied here. Thus the theorem does not yet bound the full mixed-color filling sum. ## 1. Exact recurrence and a bounded source at its literal wall Use the notation of [the selected mixed-inner source theorem](actual_pretzel_mixed_inner_source_wkb.md). Put \(M=\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\), \(H=Q^h\), \(\chi=\pi h/N\), and normalize by the COMPLETE diagonal: \[ V_{h,r}=q^{h^2}A_{h,r}/D_{0,r},\qquad0\leq r\leq M. \] The exact selected Ward identity gives, with \(Z=Q^{r+1}\), \[ V_{h,r}=p_{h,N}(r)V_{h,r+1}+q_N(r)V_{h,r+2}, \] \[ p_{h,N}=-\frac{Z^{-1}[(H+H^{-1})Z^2+1+Q^{-1}]}{(1-Z)^2}, \quad q_N=-\frac{Q^{-2}Z^{-2}(1-QZ^2)(1+QZ)} {(1-Z)^2(1-QZ)}. \tag{1} \] This holds at EVERY physical \(r\), including \(r<h\). At \(r=M-1\), \(q_N=0\) at both parities. Thus one may start the recurrence at the actual \(V_{h,M}\), assigning the auxiliary \(V_{h,M+1}=0\); no nonexistent factorial is divided out. The terminal source is especially well controlled: \[ |V_{h,M}|=\frac{s_M^2}{s_{M-h}s_{M+h}} =\begin{cases}1,&N\text{ odd},\\ \cos\chi,&N\text{ even}. \end{cases} \tag{2} \] For odd \(N=2M+1\), complement the two denominator factorials. For even \(N=2m\), \(M=m-1\), one has \(s_M^2=N/2\) and \(s_{M-h}s_{M+h}=N/(2\cos\chi)\). This proves (2) uniformly for all physical colors \(0\leq h\leq M\). The endpoint is the original finite source, not a chosen solution of an annihilator. ## 2. An elementary spectral ellipse controls all colors Freeze \(u=(r+1)\pi/N\) and let \(Q\to1\) in (1), keeping \(Z=e^{2iu}\) and \(H=e^{2i\chi}\). Write \(T_0(u,\chi)\) for its \(2\times2\) companion. Its eigenvalues are \(Z^{-1}v\), where \[ v^2-bv-c=0,\qquad c=\cot^2u, \quad b=(c-1)\cos^2\chi-2i\sqrt c\sin^2\chi. \tag{3} \] For every \(0<u\leq\pi/2\), \(0\leq\chi\leq\pi/2\), \[ \boxed{\qquad \rho(T_0(u,\chi)) \leq\rho_0(u):=\max(1,\cot^2u).\qquad} \tag{4} \] Moreover the inequality is strict when \(\chi>0\) and \(u\ne\pi/4\); it also holds strictly at \(u=\pi/2\). Here is a direct proof, including collisions. For \(0<c<1\), a root on the unit circle gives \(b=v-c/v\), the ellipse \[ \left(\frac{\Re b}{1-c}\right)^2+ \left(\frac{\Im b}{1+c}\right)^2=1. \] The displayed \(b\) has the left side \[ \cos^4\chi+\frac{4c}{(1+c)^2}\sin^4\chi\leq1, \tag{5} \] strict for \(\chi>0\). Both roots at \(b=0\) have modulus \(\sqrt c<1\). The segment from zero to an interior point of this convex ellipse cannot cross the unit-root locus. Continuity therefore puts both roots inside the disk; limiting boundary points give the non-strict assertion. For \(c>1\), apply exactly this argument to \(v/c\), with parameter \(1/c\). At \(c=1\), the roots of \(v^2+2i\sin^2\chi\,v-1\) lie on the unit circle. At \(c=0\), the roots are \(0,-\cos^2\chi\). These computations prove (4), with no root-label selection. In particular, for fixed \(\chi_0>0\) and any fixed interval \(I\subset(\pi/4,\pi/2)\), compactness gives \[ \sup_{u\in I,\ \chi_0\leq\chi\leq\pi/2} \rho(T_0(u,\chi))\leq\theta<1. \tag{6} \] At \(\chi=\pi/2\) the two roots coalesce throughout this interval. Their common modulus is \(\sqrt c<1\). No eigenbasis or gap between the two roots will be used. ## 3. Frozen blocks turn the spectral bound into a uniform source bound Define \[ E(u)=\begin{cases} \displaystyle\frac2\pi\int_u^{\pi/4}\log\cot v\,dv, &0\leq u<\pi/4,\\ 0,&\pi/4\leq u\leq\pi/2. \end{cases} \] The following are actual uniform estimates, not an adiabatic assumption: \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\ \max_{0\leq h,r\leq M} \left\{\frac1N\log|V_{h,r}|-E(\pi r/N)\right\}\leq0, \tag{7} \] and for every fixed \(\delta>0\), \(0<\beta<1/2\), there is \(\gamma=\gamma(\delta,\beta)>0\) such that \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\ \max_{\delta N\leq h\leq M,\ 0\leq r\leq\beta N} \left\{\frac1N\log|V_{h,r}|-E(\pi r/N)\right\} \leq-\gamma. \tag{8} \] We take \(\log0=-\infty\). If \(\delta\geq1/2\), the range is eventually empty, so only \(0<\delta<1/2\) matters. Proof. First fix a small lower cutoff \(a>0\). On \(a\leq u\leq\pi/2\), all coefficients of (1), and their first \(u\) derivatives, are uniformly bounded, independently of \(h,N\). The normalized exact matrix \(B_N(r)=T_N(r)/\rho_0(u_r)\), \(u_r=(r+1)\pi/N\), differs from the Lipschitz family \(B(u_r,\chi)=T_0(u_r,\chi)/\rho_0(u_r)\) by \(O_a(1/N)\). For a bounded \(2\times2\) matrix \(B\) with both eigenvalues in the closed unit disk, Cayley--Hamilton gives directly \[ \|B^L\|\leq L\|B\|+L-1\leq C_a L. \tag{9} \] Indeed its divided-power coefficient is \(\sum_{k=0}^{L-1}\lambda_1^{L-1-k}\lambda_2^k\), whose modulus is at most \(L\); this formula also covers the repeated root. If both roots instead have modulus at most \(\theta<1\), the same proof gives \(C_aL\theta^{L-1}\). Choose a fixed block length \(L\). A telescoping expansion of a block of adjacent exact normalized matrices differs from the frozen \(B(u_r,\chi)^L\) by \(O_{a,L}(1/N)\), uniformly in \(\chi\). For any prescribed \(\varepsilon>0\), choose \(L\) so large that \(C_aL<e^{\varepsilon L}\), and then choose \(N\) large. Partition the product into such blocks. Two incomplete end blocks cost a constant. This bounds the normalized product by \(C_{a,\varepsilon}e^{2\varepsilon N}\). For (8), choose a fixed closed interval \(I\subset(\max(\pi\beta,\pi/4),\pi/2)\). Every source propagation from the terminal point to \(r\leq\beta N\) crosses all of \(I\). By (6), choose the same \(L\) sufficiently large that each full block inside \(I\) has norm at most \(e^{-\gamma_0 L}\), with \(\gamma_0>0\). There are \(N|I|/(\pi L)+O(1)\) such blocks. Make the ordinary-block \(\varepsilon\) smaller than, for example, \(\gamma_0|I|/(8\pi)\). The negative block budget therefore remains a fixed negative multiple of \(N\). Near the only singular coefficient endpoint, direct use of (1) gives a universal constant \(C\) with \[ \|T_N(r)\|\leq C\frac{N^2}{(r+1)^2}, \quad0\leq u_r\leq a<\pi/8. \tag{10} \] For the second coefficient use \(|1-QZ^2|/|1-QZ|\leq C\), \(|1+QZ|\leq2\), and \(|1-Z|\geq4(r+1)/N\). The first coefficient has the same bound because \(|H+H^{-1}|\leq2\). Thus all steps with \(r+1\leq aN/\pi\) cost at most \(\exp\{O(Na\log(1/a))+O(\log N)\}\), by the elementary factorial bound. This tends to rate zero as \(a\downarrow0\). It does not grow like \(N^{O(N)}\). Finally the scalar envelope product is bounded by the exact right-endpoint Riemann sum \[ \sum_{j=r}^{M-1}\log\rho_0((j+1)\pi/N) \leq N E(\pi r/N). \tag{11} \] Together with the source bound (2), these estimates prove (7). For (8), first fix the strictly contracting interval and its budget, then make \(a\log(1/a)\) small enough, and finally make \(\varepsilon\) small enough. The loss from (10) and all ordinary blocks is then strictly smaller than that budget. This proves (8) uniformly in every indicated physical color and index. The proof supplies exponential-rate bounds. It does not assert a polynomial prefactor uniform through every spectral collision. ## 4. Strict circle and original-source core gaps Interchange the two original finite sums as in the mixed source theorem. In the complete Newton basis \(B_r(w)=\prod_{a<r}(c_a-w-w^{-1})\), the exact mixed low-core coefficient has magnitude \[ |b_{h,r}|=\frac{s_{2r}}{s_r^6}|V_{h,r}|. \tag{12} \] All marked phases remain in the equality defining that coefficient; (12) is used only for its upper bound. The uniform factorial and Newton-factor estimates in [the coherent complete-base theorem](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) therefore imply, for every fixed \(R>1\), \[ \limsup_N\frac1N\log \max_{0\leq h\leq M}\|c_{N,h}\|_R\leq j(\log R). \tag{13} \] For every fixed \(0<\delta<1/2\), there is \(\varepsilon_R(\delta)>0\) such that \[ \boxed{\quad\limsup_N\frac1N\log \max_{\delta N\leq h\leq M}\|c_{N,h}\|_R \leq j(\log R)-\varepsilon_R(\delta).\quad} \tag{14} \] To prove strictness, let \(u_*\in(\pi/4,\pi/2)\) be the unique maximum of the complete profile \(J_R\). Choose \(u_*/\pi<\beta<1/2\). For \(r\leq\beta N\), use (8). For \(r>\beta N\), use (7): that interval lies strictly above the complete maximum, so its continuous profile \(J_R+E=J_R\) has a fixed gap below \(j\). Both assertions are uniform around the entire \(|w|=R\) circle; the already proved arc inequality bounds each Newton factor by its negative-axis value up to a constant. The finite \(r\) sum costs only a factor \(N\). There is also a direct ORIGINAL-source consequence. For each fixed odd \(s\geq3\), choose its complete geometric radius \(R_s=\exp[2\operatorname{arsinh}(\tan(\pi/s))]\). If every color deficit is \(0\leq h_i\leq M\) and at least one has \(h_i\geq\delta N\), then \[ \boxed{\quad\limsup_N\frac1N\log \left|\Phi_2\left(\prod_{i=1}^s c_{N,h_i}\right)\right| \leq \frac{V_s}{2\pi}-\varepsilon_{R_s}(\delta). \quad} \tag{15} \] Indeed the exact full-Hermite source residue has the circle bound \[ |\Phi_2(F)|\leq \frac{N^2(R+R^{-1})}{(1-R^{-N})^2}R^{-N} \max_{|w|=R}|F(w+w^{-1})|. \] Apply (13)--(14) to its factors, and use \(s j(\log R_s)-\log R_s=V_s/(2\pi)\). This step retains the actual derivative source and every finite winding. It does not replace it by a semisimple trace. The global alias terms \(RP_{N,h_i}\) are not covered by (13)--(15). In the small cusp corridor they have the separate [proved source gap](actual_pretzel_mixed_alias_source_gap.md) for odd \(s\geq5\). At macroscopic deficits, their old \(56^{h_i}\) bound may be too large. No claim about the full colored cube or fixed long fillings is made without resolving those terms.

title: Independent audit of the corrected literal pretzel cap order
text: # Independent audit of the corrected literal pretzel cap order 29 October 2026. The physical box order is left to right, while the turned operators compose right to left. The corrected port theorem uses the latter traversal and satisfies EVERY original bottom and top cap. This audit checks the full physical tensor identity with arbitrary NONCOMMUTING degree-preserving boxes, so commutativity of Casimir polynomials cannot conceal an ordering error. ## 1. What the actual cups and caps force Use original box b input (a_b,b_b) and output (c_b,d_b), with physical boxes labeled left to right. The actual source pairs bottom: b_b with a_(b+1), outer a_1 with b_s; top: d_b with c_(b+1), outer c_1 with d_s. The marked outer row is unrestricted before the full contraction. Integer-degree conservation forces its total degree d only after all boxes and ordinary turns are assembled. It is kept literally in the finite checks below. For a physical box parameter t_b and t'_b=U_b t_b, the corrected unturned meridians are bottom (h(t'_b),h(t_b)^(-1)), top (g(t'_b)^(-1),g(t_b)). Consequently both inner caps, and the two outer caps at closure, require EXACTLY t_b=t'_(b+1), equivalently t_(b-1)=U_b t_b. (1) This is the propagation order s,s-1,...,1. The previous forward assignment t_(b+1)=U_b t_b does NOT satisfy the physical caps in general; the fact that product U_b=1 would close that unrelated cycle does not repair its individual cap failures. ## 2. An exact index identity detects the operator order For the actual unscaled turn write (Rot B)_((u,b);(v,e))=x^(u-e)B_((d-u,v);(b,d-e)). In the product Rot(B_1)...Rot(B_s), input to factor i is output from factor i+1. Write its intermediate indices (u_i,b_i), cyclically. The corresponding physical input/output of B_i are (a_i,b_i^phys)=(b_i,d-b_(i+1)), (c_i,d_i^phys)=(d-u_i,u_(i+1)). (2) These are precisely the two original cap matchings above. The pivot on the second traced head is g_b=x^(2b-d); thus (1/N)Tr[(I tensor g)Rot(B_1)...Rot(B_s)] has the original turn factor (1/N)x^[(s-1)d+2a_1-sum a_i-sum c_i]. This is the direct cup/cap/marked factor, with no extra average or component sign. The identity holds for ANY physical integer-degree preserving boxes, even when their turns do not commute. In particular one cannot freely reverse the factors by an unmentioned Casimir specialization. Each factor still acts rightmost first, proving (1). ## 3. Reverse traversal does not reverse geometric orientation For the complete geometric anchor label its cyclic traversal by i=1,...,s corresponding to physical b=s,s-1,...,1. Then z_(i+1)=U_b z_i and the geometric face labels must follow THIS same traversal. This is not a permutation of physical source boxes. There is also an explicit oriented-diagram check: the planar half turn (X,Y,Z)->(-X,-Y,Z) sends b to s+1-b and its port labels to a_b -> d_(s+1-b), b_b -> c_(s+1-b), c_b -> b_(s+1-b), d_b -> a_(s+1-b). It exchanges the two displayed cap matchings and their corresponding outer arcs. Its ambient determinant is +1 and its planar determinant is +1. It preserves the over/under coordinate Z, hence each oriented crossing sign. It is a rigid rotation, not complex conjugation or a mirror. The actual turn also obeys Rot^2 B=B with all its x factors; this can be checked directly in the displayed index formula. Thus no curl or quantum half-twist change is introduced. Transport each oriented crossing disk AND its oriented auxiliary circle in this rotation. The primitive meridian and disk longitude are carried together, with their intersection number and zero self-linking preserved. The actual retained R^(-1) remains R^(-1). The geometric generators are relabeled by the reverse physical traversal; their developed maps and their positive regulator are not conjugated. This geometric relabeling does not replace the original marked row by another local source. The finite tensor checks leave that row in its ORIGINAL slot. ## 4. An explicit holomorphic isometry fixes the orientation qualification The geometric reverse traversal can also be checked directly in the complete developing coordinates, without inferring it from a diagram. Use the port theorem's rho,alpha and indexed vertices. The Mobius map F(zeta)=rho^2/zeta is HOLomorphic and hence an orientation-preserving H3 isometry. It sends Z_i -> Z_(-i), U_i^+ -> U_(-i-1)^-, U_i^- -> U_(-i-1)^+. Thus it reverses the cyclic traversal while exchanging top and bottom, as required by the literal cap map above. Directly on the complete source generators it has F g_i F^(-1)=h_(1-i)^(-1), F h_i F^(-1)=g_(1-i)^(-1), F P_i F^(-1)=P_(-i)^(-1), F C_i F^(-1)=C_(-i)^(-1). (3) The first two follow from the displayed g,h matrices and z_i z_(1-i)=r^2/rho^2. The third uses P_i=g_i g_(i+1)^(-1) and h_i g_i=A. For the fourth use C_i=I-(P_i+I)/(1+Y), P_i^(-1)+I=-(P_i+I), and (P_i+I)^2=0. The same indexed matrices generate the geometric holonomy group, so (3) proves that F normalizes it. It is therefore the actual orientation-preserving hyperbolic isometry implementing this relabeling, not a complex conjugate of the geometric representation. There is an IMPORTANT marking qualification: the two peripheral generators are jointly inverted, (mu_i,lambda_i)-> (mu_(-i)^(-1),lambda_(-i)^(-1)). Their intersection number and positive cusp ratio are unchanged. In particular this preserves the positive diagonal mu_+ marking up to JOINT orientation reversal; it does not change mu_+ to mu_-=mu_+-lambda. The filled slope mu+p lambda changes only its overall orientation. In the quantum packet this is exactly the Weyl pair m_i<->-m_i, whose two contributions were retained and proved equal. There is no hidden framing shear or volume-orientation reversal. Accordingly the corrected [global port/anchor theorem](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md) has no remaining cap-order or orientation objection from this audit. Its full face-isometry calculation is still the source of the actual geometric anchor; cyclic closure alone would not establish it. [Fresh audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_literal_cap_order.py) checks literal generic noncommuting physical tensors, the original full marked row and pivot, distinguishes the reversed matrix product, checks every inverse-pair cap with nonconstant U_b, and checks the rigid half-turn port/crossing convention. It also checks the full holomorphic generator/peripheral identities (3) at complete widths through s=25. ## 5. Completion audit of the stated sharp-upper assembly The final [long-pretzel sharp upper theorem](actual_long_pretzel_sharp_volume_upper_bound.md) passes this independent assembly audit after the corrected cap order and the explicit holomorphic marking qualification above: - Its whole-source limit is the original marked Kraw, not a selected color term. The actual reduced Kashaev normalization has the same modulus; the optional one-cut modified factor is applied only once. - Every stationary local matrix is glued by the actual physical caps in (1). The nearby commuting peripherals are regular semisimple, so the scalar filled-slope eigenvalues really give +/-I matrices and a representation of the FILLED group in PSL2. - The preferred SL sign lambda=-L_H^(-1), its centered character, the actual filling quadratic and the source factor 2pi are retained. The paired regulator therefore has the same absolute constant as the complete positive geometric anchor. - The old ideal boundary is first compared with an axis cusp using the explicit O(Y^(-2)) homotopy. Only then are compatible old/new finite solid-torus vertices placed on that axis. Thus the filled representation regulator has no lost boundary constant. - The representation-volume estimate uses only the descended PSL2 action. No faithfulness or unproved SL2 descent is required. The theorem's stated scope is essential and correct: fixed odd s>=25, independently sufficiently large FIXED signed slopes, and a HYPERBOLIC filled complement. Equality with its hyperbolic volume is not claimed. This audit does not turn that broad-class upper bound into a theorem for every hyperbolic knot or a proof of the full volume conjecture.

title: Local charge selection for independently long pretzel fillings
text: # Local charge selection for independently long pretzel fillings 29 October 2026. This proves a uniform analytic property of the ACTUAL mixed-source action, not a choice of a new quantum invariant. For independently large positive or negative filling integers, the nonzero charges of smallest absolute value have strictly largest real critical action throughout a fixed local charge corridor. Their local coefficients do not cancel under the exact Weyl symmetry. Global color and Fourier-tail estimates remain separate inputs to a theorem about the whole filled knot. ## 1. The source action and its Fourier transform Fix odd s>=5. Use the independently proved analytic action Phi(chi) in [the mixed-source theorem](actual_pretzel_mixed_cusp_period_survival.md) and its [exact analytic source packet](actual_pretzel_exact_analytic_color_packet.md). Write F0=V_s/(2pi), u_s=atan(sec(pi/s)), tau=(1+exp(2iu_s))/2. Both Re tau and Im tau are strictly positive. The exact source's selected action is holomorphic, even separately in each chi_i, and Phi(chi)=F0+(i tau/pi) sum_i chi_i^2+O(||chi||^4). (1) All roots and action constants continue from the original complete source. In particular F0 is not a freely chosen normalization. There is a unique holomorphic chi(z) near zero satisfying partial_(chi_i) Phi(chi(z))+2i z_i=0. Indeed the derivative in chi at zero is (2i tau/pi)I. Define Psi(z)=Phi(chi(z))+2i sum_i chi_i(z)z_i. (2) This is the local action of the actual color Fourier transform: chi_i=pi h_i/N and exp(2pi i h_i z_i) contributes 2i chi_i z_i to the exponent divided by N. Existence of (2) alone is not the asymptotic evaluation of that finite transform; its contour/error estimates must use the exact analytic packet, not a pointwise O(1/N) error on the color grid. Uniqueness and the separate evenness of Phi give separate evenness of Psi. Differentiation of (2) gives Psi_(z_i)=2i chi_i, hence Psi(z)=F0-(i pi/tau) sum_i z_i^2+O(||z||^4). (3) Put b=pi Im(tau)/|tau|^2>0. For real z this has real quadratic term -b sum_i z_i^2. In a sufficiently small complex polydisk, Psi has a convergent series in z_1^2,...,z_s^2. ## 2. Remove the apparent singularity at infinite slope For fixed nonzero integers p_i and charges m_i, the actual centered filling kernel with P_i=-p_i has local phase T_m(z)=Psi(z)-2pi i sum_i (p_i z_i^2+m_i z_i). (4) The half twist is already included in Phi; it is not removed here. Set epsilon_i=1/p_i and t_i=m_i/p_i. The critical equation is z_i=-t_i/2+epsilon_i Psi_(z_i)(z)/(4pi i). (5) At epsilon=0 its derivative in z is I. Consequently one fixed polydisk in (t,epsilon) has a unique holomorphic solution z(t,epsilon), with z(t,0)=-t/2. The epsilons can vary independently and can have either sign. No comparability of the filling lengths is required. Completing the square in (4) gives T_m(z(t,epsilon)) =(pi i/2) sum_i t_i^2/epsilon_i+B(t,epsilon), B(t,epsilon)=Psi(z(t,epsilon)) +(i/(8pi)) sum_i epsilon_i Psi_(z_i)(z(t,epsilon))^2. (6) The last expression is holomorphic even when any epsilon_i=0. For real t,epsilon the first term in (6) is purely imaginary. Thus Re B is exactly the real critical action whenever p_i are real and nonzero. The apparent large charge-dependent phase is not discarded; it is explicitly isolated from its real growth. Equation (5), the symmetry of Psi and uniqueness show that B is separately even in the t_i. Thus B(t,epsilon)=Bhat(t_1^2,...,t_s^2,epsilon) for a holomorphic Bhat near zero. Equations (3),(6) imply partial_(xi_i) Re Bhat(0,0)=-b/4, xi_i=t_i^2. (7) Continuity now gives fixed positive t0,epsilon0 such that on the REAL box 0<=xi_i<=t0^2, |epsilon_i|<=epsilon0, partial_(xi_i) Re Bhat(xi,epsilon)<=-b/8. (8) This is a uniform derivative estimate, not a comparison only along the diagonal t_1=...=t_s. ## 3. Every nonminimal local charge has a strict action gap Take independent integers |p_i|>=1/epsilon0, enlarged if necessary so that 1/|p_i|<t0. Let all m_i be NONZERO integers with |m_i/p_i|<=t0. Choose any signs sigma_i in {+1,-1}. Integrate (8), one squared coordinate at a time, from xi_i=1/p_i^2 to xi_i=m_i^2/p_i^2. Equation (6) gives Re T_m(z_m) <= Re T_sigma(z_sigma) -(b/8) sum_i (m_i^2-1)/p_i^2. (9) The rightmost term is strictly negative unless every |m_i|=1. For each fixed tuple of slopes this is a positive exponential gap in N, even when some slopes are much larger than others.
