Every choice of signs sigma has exactly the same complex critical value, since (4) is preserved by the simultaneous transformations (m_i,z_i)->(-m_i,-z_i), separately in each coordinate. The quadratic approximation also has a useful exact-in-p form. Solving (5) for the quadratic part of Psi and using analytic perturbation gives, uniformly in the same parameter polydisk, z_i=-m_i tau/(1+2p_i tau)+O(|epsilon_i| ||t||^3), T_m(z_m)=F0+i pi sum_i m_i^2 tau/(1+2p_i tau) +O(||t||^4). (10) Here constants may depend on s and the chosen fixed polydisk. There is no singular denominator for the permitted real slopes: Im tau>0. Consequently Re T_m(z_m)=F0-pi Im(tau) sum_i m_i^2/|1+2p_i tau|^2+O(||t||^4). (11) The exact inequality (9), rather than the truncated expansion (11), is what proves charge ordering for arbitrarily unequal slopes. Equation (11) has the expected negative quadratic volume correction; it does not identify the full action with the filled geometric volume. ## 4. Nonzero local amplitude and the exact sign pairing The exact combined filling formula retains the amplitude product_i m_i sinh(2pi i z_i) and the finite parity character product_i (-1)^(m_i(N-1)); see [the original filling kernel](actual_coherent_filling_gaussian_chirp.md) and the subsequent source-inclusive Fourier calculation. The local Fourier-source amplitude is holomorphic and nonzero near zero whenever its analytic stationary evaluation has been established. Write Psi_(z_i)=z_i Q_i(z_1^2,...,z_s^2) with Q_i analytic. Equation (5) becomes z_i=-t_i/[2(1-epsilon_i Q_i(z)/(4pi i))]. (12) Shrink the polydisk so the denominator is nonzero and |z_i|<1/4. For t_i!=0, z_i is nonzero; therefore sinh(2pi i z_i) is nonzero. The Hessian in (4) is also nondegenerate: multiplication of its i-th row by epsilon_i makes it tend uniformly to -4pi i I. Its real part on real tangent vectors is the negative definite real part of Psi'' near zero. The translated real local contour thus has a nonzero Gaussian coefficient with its branch fixed by that contour. Under m_i->-m_i and z_i->-z_i, both m_i and its sinh factor change sign. Their product, the parity character, the source amplitude and the local integral are unchanged. This is also an exact change of variables in the finite-interval charge integral when the retained source is separately even. Hence the 2^s minimal signed charges ADD; they cannot cancel solely because of their signs or level parity. This does not remove any other charge by assumption. ## 5. Scope of the result The proof establishes local charge dominance for the actual action and a nonzero paired local coefficient. To turn it into an asymptotic for the original filled scalar one must still bound the complementary color regions and Fourier regions, retain every endpoint current, and compare the action with the correctly marked filled geometry. Those requirements cannot be replaced by (11) or by formal stationary equations. The exact source packet and exact filling kernel supply the inputs for those additional estimates.

title: The actual mixed source action is the marked geometric regulator
text: # The actual mixed source action is the marked geometric regulator 29 October 2026. This gives the regulator comparison needed AFTER an actual representation/port lift has been established. It retains the ordinary-circle spin, both preferred peripheral flags, and the exact filling charge. The comparison is by an elementary differential identity and the already calibrated complete geometric anchor, rather than by matching cusp Hessians or naming a source action a volume. ## 1. Inputs and the specific branch under comparison Fix an odd s>=5 and the selected analytic mixed-source branch near complete auxiliary colors. The source construction supplies the holomorphic function Phi_s and its NONZERO amplitude. Put z_i=Log H_i, ell_i=Log L_(H_i), G(z)=2pi i Phi_s(z/(2i))+C_real, partial_(z_i)G=ell_i, G(0) has imaginary part V_s. Here C_real is the recorded real Cartan/quarter-turn phase constant. For example the original exp(-is pi(N-1)/4) leading character contributes s pi^2/2. Such constants are kept in a complex-period equality and do not change its regulator norm. The following geometric inputs concern the SAME selected branch, as established in [the literal global-port and geometric-anchor theorem](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md): 1. The literal mixed Hurwitz/quarter-turn port and global source equations lift it to representations rho_z of the ACTUAL augmented link group, with main meridian fixed complete. The [source-selected local lift](actual_pretzel_mixed_regular_character_lift.md) supplies its explicit auxiliary C and disk product P; a mere trace equation would not replace global port gluing. 2. At z=0 that representation is the positively oriented geometric one of the original half-twisted augmented diagram. The explicit white-face/port anchor and the absolute auxiliary translations C=W(1+ic), P=2icW, rather than just a cusp derivative, fix this comparison. The local lift records those matrices in section6; the complete geometric volume is V_s. The statements below use these proved inputs explicitly. Neither global port gluing nor the absolute anchor is replaced by formal saddle equations or by a coincident peripheral trace alone. The [literal mixed longitude certificate](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md) now fixes the actual preferred eigenvalues on the positive meridian flag: M_i=H_i^(-1/2), lambda_i=-L_(H_i)^(-1). The minus comes from g_j=(-1)^(j-1)K_j and the literal typed loop [2,1,1,2]. Its disk word has zero self-writhe. There is no additional lambda->M^k lambda framing change hidden in these coordinates. ## 2. Retain the spin before taking a regulator norm Continue logarithms from completeness as u_i=Log M_i=-z_i/2, v_i=Log lambda_i=pi i-ell_i, Gbar=G-pi i sum_i z_i. Then EXACTLY \[ d\overline G=2\sum_i v_i\,du_i. \tag{1} \] Thus the preferred connection is the same one derived directly from the actual mixed universal crossings. The spin is a specified physical character, not an identically one change of the source. Its marked norm is \[ \boxed{D_{\rm src}(z) =\operatorname{Im}\overline G -2\sum_i\operatorname{Re}u_i\operatorname{Im}v_i =\operatorname{Im}G -\sum_i\operatorname{Re}z_i\operatorname{Im}\ell_i.} \tag{2} \] Indeed Im(Gbar)=ImG-pi sum Re z_i, while 2 Reu_i Imv_i=-pi Re z_i+Re z_i Im ell_i. The central terms cancel IN THIS PAIRED EXPRESSION. They were not removed from the separate action or kernel. The squared geometric peripheral logarithms retain their corresponding 2pi i deck shift. Writing z_i=x_i+i y_i and ell_i=a_i+i b_i, direct differentiation gives \[ dD_{\rm src}=\sum_i(a_i\,dy_i-x_i\,db_i) =2\sum_i(\operatorname{Re}v_i\,d\operatorname{Im}u_i -\operatorname{Re}u_i\,d\operatorname{Im}v_i). \tag{3} \] This is the actual half-meridian-step factor two. It is not inferred from a classical polynomial normalization. ## 3. The geometric regulator has the SAME derivative and absolute anchor For the actual representation rho_z, define beta(rho_z) by a FIXED finite oriented fundamental triangulation/idealized relative chain of the augmented-link complement. Decorate each lifted cusp with its specified peripheral eigenflag and develop its tetrahedra using the ACTUAL matrices of the port theorem. Internal faces cancel and the orientation and peripheral marking are those of that same diagram. This is the topological fundamental-chain construction in [the actual fundamental-cycle theorem](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md), not its additional identification of a unipotent five-dilogarithm COEFFICIENT with the shadow chain. That coefficient identity uses unipotence and is NOT being extended to semisimple auxiliary meridians. Use the audited coisotropic boundary pairing of [the Bloch boundary calculation](bloch_lift_and_boundary_torsor.md), section2, on this developed chain. For several boundary tori the same calculation is their direct sum: peripheral rows on distinct tori have zero intersection pairing, and the meridian/longitude rows on each torus have the same pairing -2. The resulting identity uses the group/eigenflag gluing equations, not parabolicity of those peripheral matrices. In the full squared peripheral coordinates it is delta beta=-(1/2)sum m_i wedge l_i. Equivalently, delta beta=-2 sum_i M_i wedge lambda_i. Here m_i=M_i^2 and l_i=lambda_i^2; using unsquared coordinates without their factor two would be incorrect. The main-component contribution is constant because its meridian is fixed at one. Work first where the developed shapes are regular. A sufficiently small neighborhood of the explicitly identified complete anchor has such a fixed finite chain; any normalized degenerate summands and their regulator limits are handled by the already proved five-point chain invariance and continuity. No equality with the transformed source dilogarithm list is assumed in this definition of beta. For a shape t, the elementary Bloch--Wigner differential is dD(t)=log|t| dArg(1-t)-log|1-t| dArg(t). Applying it to the displayed boundary identity gives dD(beta)=2 sum_i[Re v_i dIm u_i-Re u_i dIm v_i], which is exactly (3). This is the same calculation as [the actual preferred action/regulator identity](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md), sections5--6, and [its complex peripheral continuation](complex_peripheral_action_and_conversion_bound.md), section1. Those proofs use local logarithmic identities and face cancellation, so no assumption of equal component meridians enters. At the complete anchor, D(beta(rho_0))=V_s=ImG(0) and all Re z_i are zero. Consequently the two functions with equal differential have the SAME absolute constant on this connected regular branch: \[ \boxed{D_{\rm src}(z)=D(\beta(\rho_z)).} \tag{4} \] Use a simply connected sufficiently small marked parameter neighborhood. The explicit auxiliary C has a regular noncentral parabolic limit, so a diagonalizing-frame singularity at completeness does not invalidate this comparison. The identity extends through that removable limit. It does not splice distinct character components at a coincident peripheral point or reset logarithms independently. This proof needs neither an assumed equality of unmarked primitives nor a new theorem imported from the literature. Actual port gluing, preferred peripheral coordinates, and the COMPLETE geometric anchor are the explicit inputs that prevent an arbitrary additive volume. ## 4. The actual chirp's stationary action is precisely this regulator For independently signed nonzero fixed fillings and integer charges m_i, the original full-normal centered Gaussian kernel supplies the holomorphic action W(z)=G(z)+sum_i (z_i-2pi i m_i)^2/(4p_i), z_i+2p_i ell_i=2pi i m_i at stationarity. (5) All real Cartan constants and the retained normal amplitude can be kept beside this leading action. At a stationary point the second term in W is sum p_i ell_i^2. The real part of the stationary equation is Re z_i=-2p_i Re ell_i, so \[ \boxed{\operatorname{Im}W(z_*) =\operatorname{Im}G(z_*) +2\sum_i p_i\operatorname{Re}\ell_i \operatorname{Im}\ell_i =D_{\rm src}(z_*)=D(\beta(\rho_{z_*})).} \tag{6} \] In particular there is no unestimated complex endpoint correction left at the filling saddle. It is canceled by the ACTUAL filling quadratic, not deleted by replacing a boundary holonomy with a unit value. The same conclusion matches the source Fourier action used in the proved whole-source asymptotic. If zeta denotes its frequency variable, ell_i=-2pi i zeta_i, z_i=2i chi_i, A=Phi_s(chi)+2i sum chi_i zeta_i -2pi i sum(p_i zeta_i^2+m_i zeta_i). At its critical point direct substitution gives 2pi i A=G+sum p_i ell_i^2 up to the already recorded REAL Cartan constants. Therefore 2pi Re A=Im W=D(beta(rho_(z_*))). (7) This checks the source normalization rather than identifying exponents only up to an unknown scalar or a factor of two. ## 5. The actual filled slope and the remaining geometric distinction The preferred-spin relation gives M_i lambda_i^(p_i)=(-1)^(p_i+m_i). At the selected long-filling point these peripheral matrices are regular semisimple, not nontrivial unipotents with an accidentally unit eigenvalue. Indeed the local all-unit charge saddle has every color coordinate nonzero; the separately even analytic source has nonzero linear longitude derivative there. Both coordinates remain in a small neighborhood of zero, so their distinct reciprocal eigenvalues cannot acquire a nonzero full period. The explicit C and P commute and use the specified COMMON eigenflag. Thus their matrix product C_i P_i^(p_i) is the displayed scalar +/-I. Hence the PSL2 representation kills the primitive disk-framed slope mu_i+p_i lambda_i and extends over the corresponding filled manifold. The central sign is not assumed to be +I in a preassigned SL2 lift. The representation-volume straightening and smearing proofs use only the actual PSL2 isometric action, so they apply to this descended representation directly. The original retained negative half twist belongs to the base meridian; it was not replaced by a p_i+1 slope. In the geometric cusp anchor that base meridian is the primitive positive diagonal, not just its length. Here is a compatible FINITE-chain proof of invariance under the filling. It is not enough to put only the new vertices at one ideal flag while leaving unrelated old boundary data unchanged. At a filled cusp the peripheral image is cyclic and preserves a target geodesic axis. First replace the OLD augmented ideal-cusp development by the axis-valued cusp map of [the general-peripheral volume proof](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md), sections1--2. Its explicit face-compatible conical comparison (4a) and homotopy have boundary volume O(Y^(-2)) in (4b). Hence this replacement preserves the absolutely normalized AUGMENTED regulator as the cutoff Y tends to infinity; it is not an assumed zero-volume homotopy on an arbitrary old boundary. Fix a finite cusp cutoff and a common finite triangulation on its boundary. The OLD boundary map is now on the preserved axis. Because the filling slope is killed, its equivariant vertex assignment factors through the solid torus group Z. Extend the SAME boundary assignment to the new solid-torus vertices equivariantly on that axis. Axis contractibility provides the face-compatible extension, and every new straight tetrahedron is collinear and has zero volume. Thus the finite compact CORE PLUS FILLING chain computes the filled representation volume with no new contribution. The unfilled main cusp retains its original parabolic end convention. Taking Y to infinity, the controlled old-cusp comparison proves that the value in (6) is the regulator of the EXTENDED filled representation, with the same orientation, primitive marking, and absolute constant. It follows, using the independently proved representation-volume bound, that the selected source exponent is at most the filled manifold's hyperbolic volume whenever that manifold is hyperbolic. To replace this upper bound by EQUALITY one must additionally prove that this extended representation is its positive geometric Dehn-filling representation. A correctly glued positive near-complete geometric deformation with primitive 2pi filling supplies that fact; it is not inferred merely from (4) or a cusp Hessian. The present note does not substitute for that geometric extension proof. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.py) includes exact symbolic checks of (2),(6), alongside the original mixed-R/pivot/framing certificate. The representation lift and absolute anchor are separately checked geometric inputs, not consequences of those elementary scalar checks.

title: A uniform original-source alias gap near complete pretzel colors
text: # A uniform original-source alias gap near complete pretzel colors 29 October 2026. For every fixed odd number of boxes \(s\geq5\), the high-band terms in the exact cusp-color split are exponentially smaller than the complete augmented geometric period on a sufficiently small, fixed cusp-color corridor. This is a bound on the ORIGINAL source, including all Casimir normal coefficients. The complete-color circle estimate is used coherently before passing to its Hermite norm. The assertion is an error bound relative to the **complete-color** geometric rate. To obtain a mixed-color asymptotic one must still prove the selected core asymptotic, with a comparable rate, throughout that corridor. No fixed-filling volume theorem follows here. For \(s=3\) the proof below has zero limiting margin; a separate cancellation is needed. Use \(d=N-1\), \(q=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q=q^2\), \(x=q^d=-q^{-1}\), and \(M=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\). All boxes, turns and the source \(\Phi _2\) are exactly those in [the original complete-base polynomial theorem](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md). The exact two-band split is \[ z_{N,r}=c_{N,r}+R P_{N,r},\qquad 0\leq r\leq M, \qquad \|RP_{N,r}\|_{\mathrm H}\leq56^r\quad(r>0), \tag{1} \] where \(r=N-j\) is the actual auxiliary-color deficit and the remainder is zero for \(r=0\). The faithful norm and all source normalizations are retained from [the two-band theorem](actual_pretzel_cusp_color_two_band_bound.md). ## 1. A bounded dual Casimir on a coherent circle Let \(\mathscr R\) be the literal quarter-turn, and define \(\mathcal D=\mathscr R\circ(\Omega\cdot)\circ\mathscr R^{-1}\) on the physical pair commutant. In the physical continuant basis, \[ \boxed{\quad \mathcal D f_v=c_v f_v+b_v f_{v-1},\qquad c_v=q^{2v+1}+q^{-2v-1},\quad b_v=Q^v+Q^{-v}-2.\quad} \tag{2} \] Here \(b_0=0\). This operator preserves polynomial degree, including in the full degree-\(d\) algebra, so it preserves the low core. For completeness, (2) follows from an actual Hopf Ward identity. For a pair intertwiner \(B\), write \(\beta_v=B_{d,v;d,v}\). The original coproduct of \(F\) gives \[ B_{d-1,v+1;d,v}= x^{-1}Q^d\frac{1-Q^{v+1}}{1-Q^d} (\beta_{v+1}-\beta_v). \tag{3} \] The last row of the physical \(\Omega\) block of total degree \(d+v\) has off-diagonal \(Q^{-1}(1-Q)(1-Q^{-v-1})\) and diagonal \(2q^{-1}+(q-q^{-1})Q^{-v-1}\). Inserting (3) gives \[ (\Omega B)_{d,v;d,v} =c_v\beta_v+ q^{-1}(1-Q^{v+1})(1-Q^{-v-1})\beta_{v+1}. \] The first row of the rotated box is \(x^{v-d}\beta_v\); its adjacent phase converts the second coefficient to \(b_{v+1}\). The cyclic first row of the middle Casimir block proves (2) for the entire commutant, not just its semisimple quotient. In the symmetric Laurent variable \(z=w+w^{-1}\), (2) is the explicit rational difference operator \[ (\mathcal D F)(w)=a(w)F(Qw)+a(w^{-1})F(Q^{-1}w)+c(w)F(w), \tag{4} \] \[ a(w)=\frac{(qw-1)^3}{q(w^2-1)(qw+1)},\qquad a(w^{-1})=\frac{(w-q)^3}{q(w+q)(w^2-1)},\qquad c(w)=\frac{8qw}{(w+q)(qw+1)}. \] Here \(F(w)\) means \(f(w+w^{-1})\). This formula is exact at the specified root and retains every normal coefficient. Its apparent poles are removable on symmetric Laurent polynomials. An all-degree algebra check of (4) is short. Put \(P_r(w)=(qw;Q)_r(q/w;Q)_r\). The two shifted product ratios give \[ \mathcal D P_r=c_rP_r- \frac{(Q^r-1)^4}{qQ^r}P_{r-1}. \tag{5} \] Expand the physical continuant by its finite identity \[ f_v=x^v\sum_{r=0}^v \frac{(Q^{-v};Q)_rQ^r}{F_r^3}P_r. \] The ratios of adjacent coefficients are \((1-Q^{r-v})Q/(1-Q^{r+1})^3\) and \(x^{-1}(1-Q^{r-v})/(1-Q^{-v})\). Substitution in (5) proves (2) coefficient by coefficient. All denominators \(F_r\) here have \(r<N\); no root-zero division or omitted self-pair is used. For every fixed radius \(\varrho>1\), let \(\|f\|_{\varrho}=\max_{|w|=\varrho}|f(w+w^{-1})|\). Since \(|Q|=1\), the shifts preserve that circle, and (4) gives \[ \boxed{\quad \|\mathcal D f\|_{\varrho} \leq K_{\varrho}\|f\|_{\varrho},\qquad K_{\varrho}=2+\frac{16\varrho}{(\varrho-1)^2}.\quad} \tag{6} \] Indeed each shifted coefficient is at most \((\varrho+1)^2/(\varrho-1)^2\), and the central one at most \(8\varrho/(\varrho-1)^2\). The constant is independent of \(N\), polynomial degree and color deficit. ## 2. All low cores are generated from the complete core Let \(\mathsf T_r(z)=2\cos(r\arccos(z/2))\), including \(\mathsf T_0=2\). The elementary sine addition identity, reduced modulo the FULL \(\mathcal P_N=\mathsf T_N+2\), gives \[ L_{N-r}=(-1)^N L_r+ \frac{(-1)^r}{2}\mathsf T_r(\Omega)L_N. \tag{7} \] Multiply by the literal half twist \(R^{-1}\), then rotate. For \(1\leq r\leq M\), the rotated \(R^{-1}L_r\) has only the high continuant band \(v\geq N-r>M\); this is the same finite Gaussian support computation used in the two-band theorem. The second term of (7) has degree at most \(M\) after rotation, by (2). Consequently the low-degree projection is exactly \[ \boxed{\quad c_{N,r}=\frac{(-1)^r}{2} \mathsf T_r(\mathcal D)z_N.\quad} \tag{8} \] The Chebyshev recurrence and (6) imply, also for \(r=0\), \[ \|c_{N,r}\|_{\varrho} \leq (K_{\varrho}+1)^r\|z_N\|_{\varrho}. \tag{9} \] This keeps the coherent complete-base polynomial. Bounding its continuant summands separately is unnecessary. The interval \([-2,2]\) lies inside the ellipse \(w+w^{-1}\), \(|w|=\varrho\). By the maximum principle and the ordinary degree-\(M\) Markov inequality, applied to a real part after a unit phase rotation at each derivative evaluation, \[ \|c_{N,r}\|_{\mathrm H} \leq(1+M^2/N^2)\|c_{N,r}\|_{\varrho} \leq\frac54(K_{\varrho}+1)^r\|z_N\|_{\varrho}. \tag{10} \] Thus the passage to the faithful normal-source norm costs only a constant. It does not drop the source derivative. ## 3. A strict source alias gap for every odd \(s\geq5\) The proved coherent-circle theorem in [the complete-base asymptotic](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) gives, for each fixed \(\eta>0\), \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N \log\|z_N\|_{e^\eta}\leq j(\eta),\qquad j(0)=\frac{v_8}{\pi},\qquad j'(\eta)=\frac1\pi\arctan\sinh(\eta/2). \tag{11} \] In particular \(j(\eta)-j(0)=O(\eta^2)\). Uniformly over every integer color choice \(0\leq r_i\leq\delta N\), a source term with a nonempty alias set \(S\), \(|S|=m\), has upper rate \[ \frac1N\log\left|\Phi_2\left( \prod_{i\in S}RP_{N,r_i} \prod_{i\notin S}c_{N,r_i}\right)\right| \leq (s-m)j(\eta) +\delta\big[(s-m)\log(K_{e^\eta}+1)+m\log56\big]+o(1). \tag{12} \] The \(o(1)\) is uniform in these colors. This is (1), (10), submultiplicativity of the faithful norm, and the exact estimate \(|\Phi_2(f)|\leq3N^3\|f\|_{\mathrm H}\). The finite sum of at most \(2^s-1\) such terms has the same upper rate. All original circle, half-twist and source phases remain in the exact terms being bounded. Let \[ A_s=\frac{V_s}{2\pi} =\frac{4s}{\pi} \left[\Lambda\left(\frac\pi4+\frac\pi{2s}\right) +\Lambda\left(\frac\pi4-\frac\pi{2s}\right)\right]. \] The complete-base theorem proves the original source has rate \(A_s\). Its margin over the worst alias envelope at \(\delta=0\) is \[ g_s=A_s-(s-1)j(0)>0\qquad(s\geq5). \tag{13} \] Here is an elementary uniform proof. With \(A(\alpha)=\Lambda(\pi/4+\alpha/2)+ \Lambda(\pi/4-\alpha/2)\), \(A(0)=G\) (Catalan's constant), \(A'(0)=0\), and \(A''(\alpha)=-1/(2\cos\alpha)\). Hence \[ g_s\geq\frac{4G}{\pi}- \frac{\pi}{s\cos(\pi/s)}>0 \qquad(s\geq5). \] Indeed the second summand is less than 1 for \(s\geq5\), while \(4G/\pi>1\), for example from \(G>1-1/9\). Fix \(\eta>0\) with \((s-1)(j(\eta)-j(0))<g_s/4\), and then fix \(\delta>0\) so that \(s\delta[\log(K_{e^\eta}+1)+\log56]<g_s/4\), and also \(\delta<1/4\). Equations (12)--(13) prove the genuine uniform original-source bound \[ \boxed{\quad \left|\Phi_2\left(\prod_i z_{N,r_i} -\prod_i c_{N,r_i}\right)\right| \leq \exp\{N(A_s-g_s/2+o(1))\}, \quad 0\leq r_i\leq\delta N, \quad s\geq5\text{ odd}.\quad} \tag{14} \] One may choose \(\eta\) of order \(\sqrt\delta\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\); (12) then loses \(O_s(\delta\log(1/\delta))\) above \((s-1)j(0)\). This optimization is not needed for the fixed-corridor theorem. The proof does not estimate the low-core **selected period** from below, does not supply a gap for all colors outside the corridor, and does not sum the filling kernels. Those are separate questions. ## 4. The other color-cube corners are also controlled For an actual small ordinary color \(1\leq j\leq M\), the same finite Gaussian support computation gives a pure high band. Exact sine-factorial complementation gives the particularly simple identity \[ \boxed{\qquad z_{N,N-j}=(-1)^N R P_{N,j},\qquad \|z_{N,N-j}\|_{\mathrm H}\leq56^j.\qquad} \tag{15} \] For example \(j=1\) is exactly the original crossing \(R\). To see that the uniform constant does not acquire an extra \(N^{O(j)}\) factor, the apparent upper-band ratio is \[ \frac{s_{N-j+t-1}}{s_{2t-1}s_{N-j-t}} =\frac{s_{j+t-1}}{s_{2t-1}s_{j-t}},\qquad1\leq t\leq j. \] It is the SAME short Gaussian ratio as in the \(56^j\) proof. All large factorial indices are complemented before estimating. Consequently let every actual color \(j_i\) lie either in the low corner \(1\leq j_i\leq\delta N\) or the complete corner \(N-\delta N\leq j_i\leq N\). If at least one color is in the low corner, expand only the complete-corner colors by (1). Every resulting term has at least one short crossing sector. The proof of (14) therefore gives uniformly \[ \left|\Phi_2\left(\prod_i z_{N,N-j_i}\right)\right| \leq\exp\{N(A_s-g_s/2+o(1))\},\qquad s\geq5\text{ odd}. \tag{16} \] Thus all the OTHER binary corners of the original color cube have a rigorous gap. This does not cover its intermediate-color slabs. ## 5. The three-box endpoint is genuinely source-sensitive For \(s=3\), \(A_3=2j(0)\), so (13) has zero margin. The full source \(\Phi_2(Rz_N^2)\) is a useful diagnostic: its nodal maximum has rate approaching \(2j(0)\), but direct evaluation of the complete derivative-plus-value source at levels \(N=16,32,64,128\) gives respectively \[ N^{-1}\log|\Phi_2(Rz_N^2)|= 1.2930259621,\ 1.2612009276,\ 1.2297272136,\ 1.2060473620. \] These finite values suggest an additional source cancellation. They neither prove its rate nor justify a uniform mixed-color gap. The accompanying audit retains the exact crossing derivative in this diagnostic and replays the high-level value at doubled precision. ## 6. The global intermediate-color test remains a diagnostic [The separate exact-source diagnostic](../experiments/diagnose_actual_pretzel_global_colored_source.py) evaluates all equal-color and all single-changed-color periods at \(N=24,48,72\), \(s=3,5\), using the literal all-color two-band coefficients and the complete derivative-plus-value functional. It also checks 544 sorted mixed-color samples at \(N=48\), and replays the selected source values at doubled precision. The sampled maximum is complete color; the largest noncomplete sampled tuples are \((0,0,4)\) and \((0,0,0,0,4)\) in color deficits. This supplies no uniform asymptotic upper bound for intermediate colors or for the unsampled mixed-color cube. In particular it is not an input to (14) or (16).

title: Survival of the full original mixed-color pretzel period near completeness
text: # Survival of the full original mixed-color pretzel period near completeness 29 October 2026. Proof assembly independently reviewed for source reconstruction, marked normalizations, analytic interpolation and contour estimates. The discrete summation proof below uses the exact finite cotangent contour, retaining every endpoint current. For every fixed odd s>=5, a fixed open cusp-color corridor has a nonzero selected asymptotic for the FULL original mixed-color augmented source. The upper color band, lower inner indices, finite-grid residuals and original Hermite marked functional are all estimated. This is a mixed-source theorem; the subsequent coherent filling sum is not replaced by one of its terms. ## 1. Statement and unchanged source Let z_(N,h)=rotation(R^(-1)L_(N-h)) be the full physical polynomial from the two-band source theorem, and put A_(s,N)(h_1,...,h_s)=Phi_2(product_i z_(N,h_i)). All auxiliary colors are actual integers j_i=N-h_i. For each fixed odd s>=5 there is delta_s>0 such that, uniformly for 0<=h_i<=delta_s N and chi_i=pi h_i/N, A_(s,N)(h)=N^(3/2) exp(-i s pi(N-1)/4) A_s(chi) exp[N Phi_s(chi)](1+O(1/N)). (1) The functions Phi_s and A_s below are holomorphic on a fixed complex neighborhood of chi=0, even separately in each chi_i, and A_s has no zeros there. At the complete point, Phi_s(0)=V_s/(2pi), A_s(0)=C_s, with the SAME V_s,C_s as the complete augmented-period theorem. Evenness of the amplitude follows from the full low-core coefficients; its definition by analytic continuation is fixed at the complete point. The full physical polynomial contains a non-even alias band, but that band is exponentially smaller in this corridor. In particular (1) is actual uniform noncancellation on an OPEN macroscopic corridor h_i<=delta_s N, not only fixed normal jets or h_i=o(N). The choice s>=5 is used for the independently quantified alias gap; no assertion for s=3 is inferred from that estimate. ## 2. The analytic high-index phase is attached to the finite source Use the notation S(tau,chi), C(tau,chi) of the [mixed inner source theorem](actual_pretzel_mixed_inner_source_wkb.md), and define the analytic sine primitive J_sin(tau)=integral_0^tau Log(2sin(pi t))dt. On a fixed high-index neighborhood tau>1/4 and small complex chi put B(tau,chi)=S(tau,chi)-S(tau,0) +2J_sin(tau)-J_sin(tau-chi/pi)-J_sin(tau+chi/pi), D(tau,chi)=[C(tau,chi)/C(tau,0)] sin(pi tau)/sqrt(sin(pi tau-chi)sin(pi tau+chi)). (2) All roots and logarithms continue from their positive real complete values. These functions are even in chi, B(tau,0)=0, D(tau,0)=1, and D is nonzero after shrinking the neighborhood. These expressions follow from the actual coefficient, not a new semiclassical normalization. Indeed q^(h^2)D_(h,r)/D_(0,r) =G_N(r)^2/[G_N(r-h)G_N(r+h)], where G_N is the positive sine-factorial completion. Its bulk asymptotic has exponential part 2J_sin(tau)-J_sin(tau-chi/pi) -J_sin(tau+chi/pi) and prefactor sin(pi tau)/sqrt(sin(pi tau-chi)sin(pi tau+chi)). Multiplying by the SELECTED inner U_(h,r), including its exponentially accurate analytic interpolant, gives (2). For w=-exp(eta), define the analytic phase Psi(u,eta,chi)=(-Lambda(2u)+6Lambda(u))/pi +(1/(2pi))integral_0^(2u)Log(2cosh eta+2cos v)dv +B(u/pi,chi). (3) The analytic continuation of Lambda on this regular u-neighborhood is fixed by its real values. At chi=0 this is the already calibrated complete Newton phase. For real eta near eta_s=2asinh(tan(pi/s)), its complete critical index is u_0(eta)=atan(cosh(eta/2)), Psi_uu(u_0,eta,0)<0. The holomorphic implicit-function theorem therefore specifies a unique critical u_*(eta,chi) near u_0, and j(eta,chi)=Psi(u_*(eta,chi),eta,chi). (4) The local amplitude is explicitly a(eta,chi)=1/(4sqrt(pi)) [sqrt(sin(2u_*))/sin(u_*)^(5/2)] exp(iu_*/2) D(u_*/pi,chi)/sqrt(-Psi_uu(u_*,eta,chi)). (5) All factors are nonzero near completeness. At chi=0 this reduces to exp(iu_0/2)/[2((T+2)(T+6))^(1/4)], T=2cosh eta. ## 3. Discrete analytic Laplace lemma, including its actual error barrier Here is the precise local summation argument used in (4),(5). Choose a fixed real index window [a,b] about u_0, strictly within (pi/4,pi/2). Choose its physical endpoints on the grid pi r/N; their O(1/N) motion does not change any of the fixed gaps below. The source theorem supplies an analytic interpolation of its inner packet on a FIXED complex window, with relative grid residual O(exp(-cN)), uniform in small complex chi. Retain that residual. The original Newton factor has an analytic interpolation there too. With alpha_+=(N+1)/2-iN eta/(2pi), alpha_-=(N+1)/2+iN eta/(2pi), take Bhat_N(r,eta)=q^(-r^2) Fhat_N(alpha_++r-1)Fhat_N(alpha_-+r-1) /[Fhat_N(alpha_+-1)Fhat_N(alpha_--1)]. (6) At every integer r this is EXACTLY product_(k<r) (2cos((2k+1)pi/N)+2cosh eta). All four factorial arguments remain in regular compact substrips. Their marked bulk expansions give the integral term in (3), with leading prefactor ONE: the half-step in alpha_± cancels the two endpoint square-root factors. This continues uniformly to complex u=pi r/N and eta in fixed smaller neighborhoods; no extrapolation from real integer values is used. The remaining original factorial factors use the same Fhat/G_N completion. Thus the interpolated high-window summand is holomorphic and equals its explicit nonzero amplitude times exp(N Psi), with a uniform analytic relative O(1/N) error. On the physical grid it agrees with the original summand up to the RETAINED exponentially small inner residual. Use the following EXACT finite cotangent formula, which avoids any conditional sum of Poisson endpoint terms. For the integers k<=r<=l in this window, place its vertical sides at the HALF-grid points a_N=(k-1/2)pi/N and b_N=(l+1/2)pi/N. Let f_N(u) denote the analytic interpolated r-summand, with all the prefactors just specified, and let Gamma be the positively oriented rectangle with these vertical sides and fixed imaginary heights +/-d. Then sum_(r=k)^l f_N(pi r/N) =N/(2pi i) integral_Gamma f_N(u)cot(Nu)du. (3a) This is the interpolated-grid sum; its retained difference from the ORIGINAL source grid is bounded separately below. The residue of cot(Nu) at each enclosed physical point is 1/N, so (3a) has no endpoint half weights or new lattice multiplicity. Choose d>0 inside the fixed holomorphic tube. The complete real phase has a fixed gap at both window endpoints. By continuity, the full vertical sides stay below Re j by a fixed amount, uniformly after making d and then the eta,chi neighborhoods sufficiently small. On those sides cot(N(a_N+it))=-i tanh(Nt), and similarly at b_N, so its modulus is at most one. Their ENTIRE integrals are therefore poly(N)exp[N(Re j-gamma)] for some gamma>0. They are retained currents, not terms assigned value zero. On the upper and lower horizontal sides, respectively, cot(Nu)=-i+O(exp(-2Nd)), cot(Nu)=+i+O(exp(-2Nd)). At the complete real parameters, holomorphic Taylor expansion gives sup Re Psi(x+/-id)<=j_0+C d^2 for real x in the window: its first normal derivative is imaginary there. The eta and chi perturbations change this bound and Re j continuously by O(|eta-eta_s|+|chi|^2). Choose d first with C d^2<d/4, and then the fixed parameter neighborhood with this perturbation less than d/4. The horizontal cotangent remainders consequently have a uniform fixed exponential gap. This bounds ALL nonzero Fourier modes together, without an unsupported absolute summation of individual 1/m endpoint terms. Shrink that neighborhood also so that |Im u_*|<d/2 and Re u_* stays a fixed positive distance from both vertical sides. With the counterclockwise orientation, the two constant cotangent parts give N/(2pi) times the sum of the lower and upper left-to-right ordinary integrals. Deform EACH ordinary integral inside the analytic rectangle to the horizontal segment through u_*(eta,chi). The connecting vertical segments at a_N,b_N have the already proved endpoint gap. Away from a small central neighborhood, the shifted segment has the same strict gap by the complete profile and small parameter continuity. In the center, Re Psi<=Re j-c_1|u-u_*|^2. Thus both ordinary integrals give the SAME saddle integral, with total coefficient N/pi. Uniform analytic Gaussian expansion gives exactly (5), with relative O(1/N). No unknown original-cycle intersection number is assigned. The total grid-residual contribution is at most poly(N)exp[N(j_0+C|eta-eta_s|+C|chi|^2-c)], by the source theorem, where j_0 is the complete action at eta_s. Choose the fixed eta neighborhood and chi disk so small that this remains exponentially below Re j. This is WHY relative O(1/N) accuracy on the real grid alone would not suffice, and why the exponential interpolation is used here. ## 4. The lower indices and the rest of the circle are genuinely smaller The full physical real-color bound in the mixed source theorem gives |q^(h^2)A_(h,r)/D_(0,r)| <=poly(N)exp[N(E(pi r/N)+C chi^2)], (7) including r<h. The complete-circle proof showed that the positive Newton envelope J_R(u)+E(u) has a unique maximum at u_0>pi/4, with a strict gap on u<=pi/4 and on every complement of a fixed neighborhood of u_0. Its angular envelope also has a strict gap away from the negative axis. Both gaps persist for fixed sufficiently small REAL chi by (7) and continuity. The high-index WKB provides the same bound on the remaining compact index intervals. Consequently the box's original low core satisfies, uniformly on a fixed complex neighborhood of the negative point of the circle, for the physical REAL chi on its specified integer-color grid, c_(N,h)(-exp eta-exp(-eta)) =exp(-i pi(N-1)/4)a(eta,chi) exp[Nj(eta,chi)](1+O(1/N)), (8) up to an exponentially smaller retained remainder. On the original circle outside that neighborhood, the entire low core has a fixed exponential gap relative to the complete maximum, persisting for small chi. These assertions use the actual real-grid lower packets; no off-grid extension of the region r<h is needed. The leading functions a,j are holomorphic in chi; this statement does not identify an unexamined off-grid continuation of those lower physical packets with that holomorphic leading expression. In (8) eta varies in a fixed complex neighborhood, while chi is a PHYSICAL REAL color pi h/N. The leading functions and high-index interpolants are holomorphic in chi; no analytic continuation of the full low-index physical packet is asserted here. ## 5. The original marked period, followed by the alias estimate For the product of low cores the exact marked residue is (-1)^(N-1) N^2/(2pi i) integral_(|w|=R_s) product_i c_(N,h_i)(w+w^(-1)) w^N(1-w^(-2))/(1+w^N)^2 dw. (9) Let eta_*(chi) be the unique nearby solution sum_i partial_eta j(eta_*,chi_i)=1. It exists since the complete derivative of the left side is s cos(pi/s)/(2pi)>0. Define Phi_s(chi)=sum_i j(eta_*,chi_i)-eta_*, A_s(chi)=2sinh(eta_*) product_i a(eta_*,chi_i) /sqrt(2pi sum_i partial_eta^2 j(eta_*,chi_i)). (10) The branch of the square root is fixed at the complete real point. The same finite complex-contour argument as in section3, now in eta=log(-w), moves the central arc to eta_*. No pole of (9) is crossed: Re eta remains strictly positive. The global circle gaps in section4 control its complement. The real Gaussian integral along the local vertical direction gives (1) for the low-core product, with the ORIGINAL sign and N^(3/2) normalization exactly as in the complete-period proof. Finally the [uniform original alias source gap](actual_pretzel_mixed_alias_source_gap.md) proves for odd s>=5, and a sufficiently small fixed corridor, |Phi_2(product_i z_(N,h_i)-product_i c_(N,h_i))| <=poly(N)exp[N(Phi_s(0)-gamma_s)], gamma_s>0. (11) Shrink delta_s until Re Phi_s(chi)>Phi_s(0)-gamma_s/2. Then (11) is exponentially smaller than the just computed nonzero core period. This proves (1) for the FULL original source, keeping every normal derivative and every nonempty alias subset. ## 6. Quantitative curvature and what filling still requires The leading action is even in each chi_i. Its quadratic term can be calculated directly from the actual mixed recurrence, without assuming a topological longitude convention. Normalize by D_(0,r), put u=pi r/N, Y=exp(2iu), c=cot(u)^2, and write its classical backward eigenvalues as Y^(-1)v. Then v^2-[(c-1)cos(chi)^2-2i sqrt(c)sin(chi)^2]v-c=0. The selected high-index root is v=-1 at chi=0. Differentiation in chi^2 gives delta Log(Y^(-1)v)=Y chi^2+O(chi^4). The actual endpoint factor has zero leading action. Therefore j(eta,chi)=j(eta,0) -(1+Y_*(eta))chi^2/(2pi i)+O(chi^4). Envelope differentiation at the outer critical point gives Phi_s(chi)=V_s/(2pi) -(1+Y_s)/(2pi i) sum_i chi_i^2+O(||chi||^4), Y_s=exp(2iu_s), u_s=atan(sec(pi/s)). (12) In particular on the real physical corridor, Re Phi_s(chi)=V_s/(2pi) -sin(2u_s)/(2pi) sum_i chi_i^2+O(||chi||^4). (13) This proves strict quadratic decay away from complete color within that corridor, as well as a nonzero analytic leading amplitude. The next operation is still the ENTIRE original filling-color sum. Its exact Weyl fold and normal-weighted Gaussian kernel must be combined with (1), and intermediate colors outside this corridor must be bounded. No independent full-twist factor may be discarded. The identification of the filled critical action with the marked geometric volume must also respect the actual meridian/longitude orientation. A complete augmented-source or mixed-cusp theorem is not a fixed filled-knot volume theorem.

title: Mixed cusp-color inner packets: exact source and uniform holomorphic WKB
text: # Mixed cusp-color inner packets: exact source and uniform holomorphic WKB 29 October 2026. The low core of the ACTUAL rotated circle of color j=N-h has a second-order selected recurrence at every integer h. Near the complete color it admits a source-fixed, nonzero analytic amplitude on any fixed high-index interval r/N>1/4. A literal zero in the endpoint recurrence also provides a uniformly holomorphic ratio interpolant which is EXACT at the physical r-grid. Optimal analytic Euler--Maclaurin gives an exponentially accurate action interpolant, with its residual source explicitly retained. This is a theorem about the low core. The original upper band R P is the separate, nonzero term in [the exact two-band theorem](actual_pretzel_cusp_color_two_band_bound.md). It is not discarded or incorporated into the following amplitude. No mixed-color period, fixed filling, or knot-volume theorem follows without the remaining outer-source comparison. ## 1. Literal finite packets and their fixed factorial continuation Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, M=floor(d/2), F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a|, and the original continuants f_v. For an INTEGER 0<=h<=M the low core is exactly c_(N,h)=kappa^(-1)sum_(v=h)^M a_(h,v)f_v, a_(h,v)=N^2 s_(2v)/[s_v^2 s_(v-h)s_(v+h)]. Its marked phase is not optional: a_(h,v)x^v=N^2 q^(h^2) F_(2v)/[F_v^2F_(v-h)F_(v+h)]. Interchanging the actual two finite sums therefore gives kappa c_(N,h)(z)/N^2 =q^(h^2)sum_(r=0)^M (-1)^r Q^(r(r+1)/2)P_r(z) A_(h,r)/F_r^3, A_(h,r)=sum_(v=max(h,r))^M Q^(-vr)F_(2v)/[F_vF_(v-h)F_(v+h)F_(v-r)]. (1) All original normalizations remain. For r>=h define D_(h,r)=Q^(-r^2)F_(2r)/[F_rF_(r-h)F_(r+h)], U_(h,r)=A_(h,r)/D_(h,r). On a high interval r/N>=tau_0>1/4 and |chi| small, put h=N chi/pi. The source's complex continuation means replacing ONLY F_(v-h),F_(v+h) in (1), with v=r,...,M, by the canonical Fhat_N(v-h),Fhat_N(v+h) of [the exact original factorial interpolation](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md). All these arguments stay in regular compact factorial substrips. The same replacement defines D_(h,r). This is holomorphic in complex chi on a fixed disk and agrees with every physical integer h there. No assertion about the off-grid continuation of the omitted low indices r<h is needed for this high-index theorem. ## 2. Exact finite transformation and the all-index Ward equation For r>=h, n=M-r, the exact normalized finite sum is U_(h,r)=sum_(k=0)^n (qQ^r;Q)_k(-qQ^r;Q)_k(-Q^(r+1);Q)_k Q^(-rk) /[F_k(Q^(r+1-h);Q)_k(Q^(r+1+h);Q)_k]. (2) It is balanced because the product of its two lower parameters is independent of h. The OWN finite transformation (3) in [the coherent inner proof](actual_pretzel_coherent_inner_gauss_elimination.md) applies exactly, with no absent amplitude. For example at odd N, choosing its lower parameters in the safe order gives U_(h,r)=(qQ^h;Q)_n/(Q^(r+1+h);Q)_n *sum_(j=0)^n (Q^(2r+1);Q^2)_j(-Q^(-h);Q)_j Q^j /[(Q^(2r+2-2h);Q^2)_jF_j]. (3) For physical integers r>=h all magnitudes on the second line are positive after its exact term phase (i q^h)^j is removed. The monotonicity used at h=0 is NOT asserted when h is macroscopic. There is a stronger exact source equation. Write H=Q^h and T_h=H+H^(-1). For EVERY physical 0<=h<=M and 0<=r<=M, QY^2(1-Q^2Y)A_(h,r+2) +Y(T_h Q^3Y^2+Q+1)A_(h,r+1) -Q(QY+1)(QY^2-1)A_(h,r)=0, Y=Q^r, (4) A_(h,M)=D_(h,M), A_(h,M+1)=0. The equation includes r<h. For its direct proof use the summand in (1), z=Q^v and the rational certificate g_h(z)=(1-z/H)(1-Hz)(1-z/Y)/z^2. The v-step ratio is Y^(-1)(1-Qz^2)(1+Qz)/[(1-Qz/H)(1-QHz)(1-Qz/Y)]. Consequently the telescoping difference is (1/(YQ^2)-1)z^(-2) +(1/(YQ)+H+H^(-1)+1/Y)z^(-1) -1/(YQ)-1-(H+H^(-1))/Y. The lower endpoint vanishes at z=H or z=Y, according to whether the actual sum starts at h or r. Its upper endpoint has F_(2M+2)=0. The r-step ratio is z^(-1)-Y^(-1), so the first two moments yield (4). On the high interval r>|Re h| the SAME proof holds for the specified complex-h factorial completion: the lower endpoint is z=Y and all shifted-factorial identities are exact. Thus this is the continuation of the original finite source, not a selected formal solution of an annihilator. Normalize (4) by its actual D_(h,r). With den_r=(1-QY/H)(1-QYH), one obtains exactly U_r=p_N U_(r+1)+q_N U_(r+2), p_N=-Q^(-2)Y^(-1)(T_hQ^3Y^2+Q+1)/den_r, q_N=-Q^(-4)Y^(-2)(1-Q^2Y)(1-Q^3Y^2)(1+Q^2Y) /(den_r den_(r+1)). (5) Here den_(r+1)=(1-Q^2Y/H)(1-Q^2YH). At r=M-1, q_N=0 at BOTH parities, independently of H. Thus the selected source is U_M=1 and U_(M-1)=p_N(M-1); no value of D_(h,M+1) is divided out. The recurrence is used where its displayed denominators are nonzero; this holds uniformly in the small complex cusp corridor below. At extreme colors outside that corridor one uses the uncanceled exact equation (4), rather than evaluating a spurious 0/0 at r=M. ## 3. A uniform dominant channel, with its endpoint included Fix tau_0>1/4, tau_0<1/2. Put epsilon=1/N, tau=r/N, Y=exp(2pi i tau), H=exp(2i chi), and Q=exp(2pi i epsilon). Regard the rational coefficients (5) as analytic functions p(tau,chi,epsilon),q(tau,chi,epsilon). Let p_0,q_0 denote their values at epsilon=0. Explicitly, p_0=-Y^(-1)(2cos(2chi)Y^2+2) /[(1-Y/H)(1-YH)], q_0=-Y^(-2)(1-Y^2)^2/[(1-Y/H)^2(1-YH)^2]. The roots of mu^2-p_0 mu-q_0=0 at chi=0 are mu_1=-Y^(-1), mu_2=Y^(-1)cot(pi tau)^2. On every compact real interval I contained in (1/4,3/4), there is a fixed complex neighborhood and a fixed chi disk on which the continuation mu=mu_1 is analytic, nonzero, and satisfies |mu_2/mu|<=kappa<1, Re mu>=m>0. (6) These hypotheses are CHECKABLE from the displayed rational quadratic: at chi=0 the ratio is cot(pi tau)^2<1 and Re(-Y^-1)>0; compactness and sufficiently small complex neighborhoods preserve both strict inequalities. All coefficient denominators stay nonzero. No eigenvalue selection from unknown period data occurs. In particular tau=1/2 is INCLUDED: mu(1/2,chi)=1, q_0 has a double zero there, and the epsilon derivative q_1 also vanishes there. The eigenvalue and source frame do not become singular at the physical terminal point. ## 4. A holomorphic ratio interpolant which matches the source exactly Choose sigma>0 small enough that [tau_0-sigma,1-tau_0+4sigma] lies strictly inside (1/4,3/4), and shrink its complex tube and the chi disk until (6) holds. Let L_N=ceil((1/2-tau_0+2sigma)N), F_tau(z)=p(tau,chi,epsilon)+q(tau,chi,epsilon)/z. For tau in a fixed complex neighborhood of [tau_0,1/2], define v_N(tau)=F_tau o F_(tau+epsilon) o ... o F_(tau+(L_N-1)epsilon) (mu(tau+L_N epsilon)). (7) Every iterate is within C epsilon of its corresponding nonzero mu. Indeed F_tau(mu(tau+epsilon))-mu(tau)=O(epsilon), while its z derivative has modulus at most kappa+O(epsilon)<kappa'<1 on those disks. A sufficiently large C gives an invariant disk at each backwards step. This proves that (7) is uniformly holomorphic, nonzero and bounded, with a uniform bounded inverse. At EVERY physical tau=r/N with tau_0N<=r<M, the continued fraction reaches r=M-1. There q_N=0 EXACTLY, so it forgets its entire remaining analytic tail and takes the value p_N(M-1). Hence v_N(r/N)=U_r/U_(r+1) EXACTLY, (8) and every physical high-index U_r is nonzero. This works also for complex chi in the fixed disk because the wall zero is independent of H. There is no assertion that v_N(M/N) equals a nonexistent physical ratio U_M/U_(M+1); the source product stops at M-1. Moreover the Riccati defect of (7) is O((kappa')^L_N): adding one future step changes its terminal value by O(epsilon), which is contracted by the preceding L_N steps. Thus the chosen terminal function cannot hide a macroscopic source change. ## 5. The selected action and a nonzero joint amplitude All derivatives in the following formula are derivatives of the EXPLICIT rational functions (5). Let p_1=partial_epsilon p|_0, q_1=partial_epsilon q|_0, nu=[p_1+q_1/mu-q_0(partial_tau mu)/mu^2] /[1+q_0/mu^2]. The denominator equals 1-mu_2/mu and is bounded away from zero. The analytic trial ratio mu+epsilon nu has Riccati residual O(epsilon^2), obtained by Taylor expansion at tau+epsilon. Applying the same strict contraction as in section4 gives uniformly on a fixed complex neighborhood v_N=mu+epsilon nu+O(epsilon^2). (9) The principal log is well defined by Re v_N>0. Define S(tau,chi)=integral_tau^(1/2) Log mu(s,chi) ds, C(tau,chi)=sqrt(mu(tau,chi)) *exp[integral_tau^(1/2)nu(s,chi)/mu(s,chi)ds]. (10) The square root is its branch equal to one at tau=1/2. Both are holomorphic on fixed neighborhoods, and C has a uniform nonzero lower bound on compact subsets. The physical selected packet is U_(h,r)=C(r/N,chi)exp[N S(r/N,chi)](1+O(1/N)), (11) uniformly in physical r/N>=tau_0 and complex chi in a fixed small disk. The proof is to sum Log v_N, use (9) and one-step Euler--Maclaurin. Since Log mu(1/2,chi)=0, replacing the true endpoint M/N by 1/2 introduces O(1/N), at BOTH parities. There is no extra unknown endpoint matching constant. In particular U_M=1 is its original source normalization, not an imposed WKB scale. At chi=0, the formulas calibrate against the independent finite transformation: S(tau,0)=i pi(1/2-tau)^2, C(tau,0)=sqrt(sin(pi tau)) *exp[-3pi i(1/2-tau)/2]. (12) This calibration also follows directly without that transformation: substitution in the rational derivatives gives nu/mu=-(pi/2)cot(pi tau)-(5pi i/2), and Log mu=i pi-2pi i tau. Integrating these two expressions in (10) proves (12), with its constant fixed by C(1/2,0)=1. Thus the joint amplitude is an analytic nonzero deformation of the already proved complete-color amplitude. This is not a formal normal-jet assertion: it is uniform for h up to delta N with a fixed sufficiently small delta, and for the displayed complex factorial completion. ## 6. Exponentially accurate analytic action, with residual source kept This strengthening matters before taking an oscillatory outer sum. An O(1/N) error on individual real-grid terms alone cannot justify a complex saddle at a fixed nonzero chi. The functions f_N=Log v_N are uniformly bounded and holomorphic on a FIXED larger complex neighborhood of [tau_0,1/2]. On an inner neighborhood there are constants B,a>0, independent of N, such that |f_N^(k)|<=B k! a^(-k). Put b_N=M/N and, for K_N=floor(pi a N/4), define the analytic Euler--Maclaurin expression E_N(tau)=N integral_tau^b_N f_N(s)ds +(f_N(tau)-f_N(b_N))/2 +sum_(k=1)^K_N B_(2k)/(2k)! N^(1-2k) [f_N^(2k-1)(b_N)-f_N^(2k-1)(tau)]. (13) The Bernoulli polynomial remainder is bounded by C N (K_N/(pi a N))^(2K_N), after shrinking a if necessary. This follows from |B_(2k)(x)|<=4(2k)!/(2pi)^(2k) and the displayed Cauchy derivative bound. Hence, for some c>0, U_(h,r)=exp[E_N(r/N)](1+R_(N,r)), |R_(N,r)|<=C exp(-cN), (14) uniformly on the physical high grid and the complex chi disk. There is NO approximation of source values prior to this bound: the product of the exact grid ratios (8) is precisely U_r. Its endpoint product is empty and equals one at r=M. The interpolant E_N is holomorphic in complex tau,chi. Equations (9) and (13) also give, uniformly on an inner complex neighborhood, exp(E_N(tau))=C(tau,chi)exp[N S(tau,chi)](1+O(1/N)). (15) Indeed the higher Bernoulli terms in (13) sum to O(1/N), and f_N=Log mu+N^(-1)nu/mu+O(N^-2) there. The grid residual R is retained explicitly; it is not relabeled a homogeneous solution or zero current. One may use exp(E_N) in an outer analytic estimate ONLY after bounding that residual in the whole original sum. For example on a fixed negative-w neighborhood and |chi| small, its total high-packet contribution is at most poly(N)exp{N[j_0+C|chi|^2-c]}, (16) where j_0 is the complete-color real action envelope on that neighborhood. This follows by the original factorial estimates, the even analytic perturbation S(tau,chi)-S(tau,0)=O(chi^2), and (14); no unrestricted exterior operator norm is inserted. For a fixed small enough chi disk the error barrier survives any O(|chi|^2) action perturbation, in particular a smaller O(|chi|^4) loss from a nearby complex index saddle. This supplies the quantitative source input for a finite-Poisson or cotangent contour argument in the outer r variable. Its endpoint currents, the lower r packets, and the R P upper color band still require their own estimates. No such current is erased by (14). ## 7. A full real-color upper envelope retains the lower indices For physical integer h define V_(h,r)=q^(h^2)A_(h,r)/D_(0,r). Its normalized recurrence has EXACTLY the complete-color q_N and in the shifted variable Z=Q^(r+1) its other coefficient changes by p_(h,N)-p_(0,N)=-Z(T_h-2)/(1-Z)^2. (17) For 0<=r<=tau_0N, the old full branch envelope rho=max(1,cot(pi(r+1)/N)^2) gives |p_h-p_0|/rho<=C|chi|^2, uniformly even at r=0. The globally conditioned frame of [the all-index source bound](actual_pretzel_all_index_backward_envelope.md) therefore changes its one-step bound only by the factor 1+C|chi|^2. The selected high-index anchor (11), together with s_r^2/(s_(r-h)s_(r+h))<=1 for real physical h<=r<=M, is at most exp(CN chi^2) times a fixed polynomial. Iteration proves |V_(h,r)|<=poly(N)exp{N[E(pi r/N)+C chi^2]}, E(u)=(2/pi)integral_u^(pi/4)log cot v dv for u<pi/4, E(u)=0 for u>=pi/4. (18) The exact mixed Ward (4) proves this also for r<h; its lower telescoping endpoint is then v=h. Thus no low-index terms have been omitted. At a fixed complete-color outer radius the strict old lower-index profile gap persists for sufficiently small |chi|. This is a controlled continuity estimate, not a claim that the second recurrence branch disappears. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_mixed_inner_source_wkb.py) checks the original finite mixed coefficients, balanced transform, all-r Ward and normalized endpoint wall at both parities; verifies the holomorphic source ratios and the calibrated selected amplitudes. Fresh replay: PASS 17 complete finite-field families N=2,...,18, with EVERY admissible integer color and inner index, the original low-core marked phases and odd mixed finite transformation; four independent canonical complex-Fhat source cases; and six full selected analytic-WKB families at N=32,33,64,65,128,129. The last families include complex chi and compare the literal finite source, its exact continued-fraction ratios and its normalized nonzero amplitude. The exponential Euler--Maclaurin barrier is proved analytically above; finite tests are supplementary, not an inference of that barrier. ## 8. The actual analytic Newton factor has prefactor one Let w=-exp eta, initially eta>0 real, and set alpha_+=(N+1)/2-iN eta/(2pi), alpha_-=(N+1)/2+iN eta/(2pi). Then Q^(alpha_+)=qw and Q^(alpha_-)=q/w EXACTLY, with the negative-argument logarithmic marks retained. Define Bhat_N(r,eta)=q^(-r^2) Fhat(alpha_++r-1)Fhat(alpha_-+r-1) /[Fhat(alpha_+-1)Fhat(alpha_--1)]. (19) At physical integer r it is EXACTLY the original Newton product product_(a<r)(c_a+2cosh eta). The claim below holds uniformly on fixed complex neighborhoods with tau=r/N in a compact subinterval of (0,1/2), eta near a fixed positive real value, and all four scaled factorial arguments in compact subsets of 0<Re a<1: Bhat_N(N tau,eta) =exp{N/(2pi) integral_0^(2pi tau) Log(2cosh eta+2cos v)dv} *[1+O(1/N)]. (20) There is no missing periodic multiplier or square-root factor. Here is the branch calculation. Put a_+=1/2-i eta/(2pi), a_-=1/2+i eta/(2pi), and f(a)=[Li2(1)-Li2(exp(2pi i a))]/(2pi i). The canonical factorial expansion on its marked strip gives Fhat_N(Na-1/2)=sqrt(iN) exp[Nf(a)] [1+O(1/N)]. Indeed the displacement contributes -f'(a)/2, where f'(a)=Log(1-exp(2pi i a)); it cancels the variable part of the factorial square-root prefactor. The remaining sqrt(iN) has the same fixed mark exp(i pi/4)sqrt N at all four arguments, so it cancels between numerator and denominator. In particular one must NOT reset Log[i(1-X)] to an unrelated principal logarithm. The exponent of (19) divided by N is f(a_++tau)+f(a_-+tau)-f(a_+)-f(a_-)-i pi tau^2. Its tau derivative is Log(1+exp(eta)Y)+Log(1+exp(-eta)Y)-2pi i tau =Log(2cosh eta+2cos(2pi tau)). At real 0<tau<1/2 the two arguments on the left have positive imaginary parts, their arguments sum to 2pi tau, and the argument on the right is positive. Thus the integer logarithmic ambiguity is ZERO. Holomorphic continuation gives the same identity on the specified complex neighborhood. Both primitives vanish at tau=0, which proves (20) with its constant. This is sufficient for a fixed high-index Poisson window whose upper cutoff is STRICTLY below 1/2. It is not a uniform bulk asymptotic through tau=1/2: there an upper scaled factorial reaches the edge of its strip, and using a reset dilogarithm could lose a second-shift current. Physical indices beyond such a fixed cutoff must first be bounded by their strict profile gap, or their upper continuation treated separately. Formula (20) makes no such endpoint current vanish. The updated audit includes four marked Newton-factor cases: exact integer-r identities at N=8,9 and complex-r,complex-eta bulk asymptotics at N=12,24, computed independently with the canonical finite Barnes product. Fresh full replay passes these together with the finite mixed-source and selected-WKB families listed above.

title: The selected mixed pretzel packet has an explicit regular character lift
text: # The selected mixed pretzel packet has an explicit regular character lift 29 October 2026. This identifies the regular algebraic branch selected by the ORIGINAL mixed inner source with an explicit auxiliary meridian. It does not identify a representation by matching cusp Hessians. The source Riccati ratio fixes the internal critical root, the literal factorial ratios fix its two remaining conjugate variables, and a two-by-two matrix calculation realizes the resulting disk-product character. The literal quarter-turn port identification and global concatenation are supplied separately; neither a trace equation alone nor this local calculation is being substituted for that gluing proof. ## 1. Recover the internal critical point from the selected finite source Use the exact original mixed sums, normalizations, and source endpoint in [the mixed inner theorem](actual_pretzel_mixed_inner_source_wkb.md): A_(h,r)=sum_(v=r)^M Q^(-vr) F_(2v)/ [F_v F_(v-h) F_(v+h) F_(v-r)], D_(h,r)=Q^(-r^2) F_(2r)/[F_r F_(r-h) F_(r+h)], U_(h,r)=A_(h,r)/D_(h,r). Here r is in its fixed high window, h is in the small cusp corridor, H=Q^h, Y=Q^r, and the prescribed factorial completion is used for complex h. In particular no arbitrary solution of the Ward equation is chosen. The exact source has U_M=1 and its last backward coefficient vanishes. Its proved selected ratio tends to the simple dominant root mu of mu^2-p mu-q=0, den=(1-Y/H)(1-YH), p=-Y^(-1)[(H+H^(-1))Y^2+2]/den, q=-Y^(-2)(1-Y^2)^2/den^2. (1) The adjacent D ratio has the limit d(Y,H)=Y^(-2)(1-Y^2)(1+Y)/den. There is also a literal, exact moment identity. The ratio of the v-th summand of A_(h,r+1) to that of A_(h,r) is Q^(-v)-Q^(-r). The v=r endpoint on the second sum is zero, so this holds after summing, with no missing boundary term. Consequently the effective internal root selected by that source is X^(-1)=Y^(-1)+d(Y,H)/mu, X=Y mu/[mu+Yd(Y,H)]. (2) Substitution of (2) in (1), followed by clearing its regular denominators, gives precisely (Y+T+1)X^2-(TY+2)X+Y-1=0, T=H+H^(-1). (3) This equivalence is algebraic on the stated regular chart. At H=1 the SOURCE-selected root mu=-Y^(-1) gives X=(Y-1)/(Y+3), rather than the other normalized channel. Thus (2) also fixes the branch on a small complex neighborhood by holomorphic continuation. All denominator exclusions in (1)--(3) are retained. ## 2. Literal phase and its conjugate coordinates The complete phase S_0 is the finite-factorial phase in [the independent symbol audit](actual_pretzel_geometric_symbol_audit.md). The exact mixed summand changes it by S=S_0-2Li2(X)+Li2(X/H)+Li2(XH)+(Log H)^2/2. (4) The last term is the ORIGINAL q^(h^2) factor, not an adjustable flattening. The original common kappa and all quarter-turn phases remain as in the source theorem. Differentiating the actual product-log chart gives exp(S_x)=(1+X)^2(X-1)/[(X-Y)(1-X/H)(1-HX)], exp(S_y)=(1-Y/X)(1-wY)(1-Y/w)/(1-Y)^3, U=exp(S_t)=(wY-1)/(w-Y), L=exp(S_LogH)=(H-X)/(1-HX), (5) where x=Log X,y=Log Y,t=Log w. Equation exp(S_x)=1 is exactly (3). The second equation exp(S_y)=1 is (1-Y/X)[1-(w+w^(-1))Y+Y^2]=(1-Y)^3. (6) On the regular branch the same integer inner mark as in the complete source is retained by continuation. Equations (5)--(6) do not erase that mark. They identify the exponentiated critical coordinates; the marked primitive remains the one fixed by the finite source. The displayed L is also fixed directly by the exact physical h-shift: the original q^(h^2), F_(v-h), F_(v+h) factors have limiting ratio H(1-X/H)/(1-HX)=L. Thus no undetermined square root of an auxiliary longitude is inserted. The auxiliary physical meridian is M=H^(-1/2), with branch M=1 at h=0. A positive physical-color/meridian shift reverses the h-shift. Its preferred longitude marking also retains the original ordinary-circle pivot sign. The [typed longitude certificate](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md) proves that the preferred M-eigenflag longitude is precisely -L^(-1). ## 3. The dual Casimir is an actual four-punctured trace The literal quarter-turn dual-Casimir operator in [the original alias theorem](actual_pretzel_mixed_alias_source_gap.md) has principal symbol D(w,U)=((w-1)/(w+1))^2(U+U^(-1))+8w/(w+1)^2. (7) This symbol has an explicit trace realization. Put t=(w-1)/(w+1), P_0=diag(w,w^(-1)), and define mu_1=[[2w/(w+1),1],[-t^2,2/(w+1)]], mu_2=P_0 mu_1^(-1), mu_3=[[2/(w+1),wU],[-t^2/(wU),2w/(w+1)]], mu_4=(mu_3 mu_2 mu_1)^(-1). (8) Each matrix has determinant one and trace two. Their ordered product is I, and direct multiplication gives Tr(mu_2 mu_1)=w+w^(-1), Tr(mu_3 mu_2)=D(w,U). For w not in {0,1,-1} and U!=0 this tuple is irreducible: the first pair alone has distinct fixed flags. This is an explicit character lift, rather than an inference from the dimension of a trace variety. Substituting (5) and using (3),(6) gives the exact identity D(w,U)=-(L+L^(-1)). (9) For a reproducible rational verification, solve (3) as Y=[1+2X-(T+1)X^2]/[1-TX+X^2], then solve (6) for w+w^(-1); substitute these in (7). No equation at a collision divisor is canceled and then reintroduced as a regular solution. At completeness D=-2 although L=1; the central minus sign in (9) must therefore be retained. ## 4. A framed auxiliary meridian, including its parabolic limit Let P be the actual unrotated disk-product matrix, with determinant one and trace D in (9). Define beta=-(H-X)(1-HX)/[sqrt(H)(H+1)(1-X^2)], C=beta(P-YI). (10) All square roots are the branch through H=1. Equations (3),(9) imply det C=1, Tr C=sqrt(H)+1/sqrt(H), [C,P]=0. (11) More precisely, on the P-eigenflag with eigenvalue lambda=-L^(-1), C has eigenvalue M=H^(-1/2); on the reciprocal flag it has M^(-1). These assertions follow by the scalar identities beta(lambda-Y)=H^(-1/2), beta(lambda^(-1)-Y)=H^(1/2). The formula has a removable complete-color degeneration. At H=1, equation (3) on the selected branch gives Y=(1+3X)/(1-X), so C=I-(P+I)/(1+Y), Tr P=-2. (12) For noncentral P this is a NONCENTRAL trace-two unipotent. Thus the auxiliary meridian does not collapse to I merely because its eigenvalue becomes one. Formula (10) is finite in a bounded port frame at this limit, although a frame diagonalizing P becomes singular there. Here is a direct tangle test. For actual meridians a,b,C, put P=ba. The positive Hurwitz convention is (a,b)->(a^(-1)ba,a). The literal auxiliary threading word [2,1,1,2] sends the auxiliary meridian to P^(-1)CP. Closing that physical auxiliary component is therefore EXACTLY [C,P]=1; under this condition the main outputs are (C^(-1)aC,C^(-1)bC). Following it by the retained negative half twist gives r=C^(-1)bC, s=C^(-1)bab^(-1)C. (13) For generic H!=1 diagonalize P as diag(lambda,lambda^(-1)), with lambda=-L^(-1), and set t_lambda=(lambda-1)/(lambda+1). One may take a=[[2lambda/(lambda+1),1], [-t_lambda^2,2/(lambda+1)]], b=P a^(-1), C=diag(M,M^(-1)). Then (13) gives Tr(r^(-1)a)=2-t_lambda^2 [2+lambda H+lambda^(-1)H^(-1)]. (14) Substitution of L=(H-X)/(1-HX) and the two actual stationary equations (3),(6) makes (14) exactly w+w^(-1). Thus the selected factorial branch satisfies the mixed threaded-half-twist character relation, with the original auxiliary meridian and a specified flag. The regular formula (10), not this singular diagonal frame, is used at H=1. ## 5. Scope of the local certificate This proves a source-selected regular local character lift and an explicit auxiliary-meridian matrix. The additional literal quarter-turn ordering, conjugating frames, and global source/cap equations are proved in [the global port theorem](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md). The [preferred-longitude certificate](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md) retains its sign and framing. The [marked action comparison](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) then identifies the source action with the regulator of the extended filled representation. These separately proved steps are not inferred from matching a cusp Hessian. They give a representation-volume upper bound; identifying the deformed representation as the filled geometric holonomy is an additional requirement for equality. In particular the global propagation is RIGHT TO LEFT in the original left-to-right box label b. If its rotated input is t_b and output t'_b=U_b t_b, the actual original bottom ports are (h(t'_b),h(t_b)^(-1)) and top ports are (g(t'_b)^(-1),g(t_b)). Both original neighboring caps therefore impose t_b=t'_(b+1); the outer turns impose t_s=t'_1. The condition product U_b=1 closes this propagation in the order s,...,1. One must not replace these literal relations by a forward box-label traversal. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_mixed_regular_character_lift.py) checks the cleared rational identities, full two-by-two character and threading formulas, complete parabolic limit, and the exact finite source moment on both level parities. Finite computations supplement the algebraic proof above. ## 6. Absolute complete crossing-circle holonomies match the geometric cusp The [literal port and geometric-anchor proof](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md) identifies the main meridians with the white-face holonomies of the explicit four-antiprism construction. Here is an absolute matrix check for the AUXILIARY generators; it is stronger than comparing cusp Hessians or only a ratio of translations. Set alpha=pi/s, c=cos(alpha), t=csc(alpha), rho^2=sec(alpha)+tan(alpha), R=rho^4, w=-R, U=exp(2i alpha), z_i=t rho^(-1) exp((2i+1)i alpha), and use the actual raw port matrices g(z)=[[-2w/(w+1),z],[-t^2/z,-2/(w+1)]]. Their fixed flags are z/t. The unrotated disk product is P_i=g(z_i)g(Uz_i)^(-1), with trace -2 and fixed flag Z_(i+1)=rho U^(i+1). Direct multiplication gives (P_i)_21=t^2(1-t)(1-U^(-1))/z_i. Rotate the boundary coordinate by zeta'=U^(-i-1)zeta and then use m_i(zeta)=1/(zeta'-rho). The new lower-left entry before this last Mobius map is c'=U^(i+1)(P_i)_21=2i rho(1-t). For any trace-minus-two matrix fixing rho, write P=-I+N. The kernel of N is (rho,1), so N=c'[[rho,-rho^2],[1,-rho]]. Conjugating by the matrix [[0,1],[1,-rho]] of m_i gives m_i P_i m_i^(-1)=-I+[[0,c'],[0,0]]. Consequently its PROJECTIVE translation is -c'. Since rho^2(t-1)=ct and the actual cusp rectangle has width W=1/(rho sin(alpha))=t/rho, this translation is exactly -c'=2ic W. (15) The source-selected complete Y equals exp(2i atan(sec(alpha))), hence 1+Y=2ic/(1+ic). Using (12), the same coordinate m_i sends the actual auxiliary meridian to the translation -c'/(1+Y)=(1+ic)W. (16) Equations (15)--(16) are precisely the primitive disk longitude and the POSITIVE diagonal half-twist meridian in [the face-labeled cusp calculation](actual_augmented_pretzel_crossing_circle_cusp.md). Thus the complete auxiliary matrices, not just their flags or their first deformation derivative, match those of the actual half-twisted augmented geometry. The central minus sign of the SL2 disk product is retained throughout. Together with the independently checked white and shaded face pairings in the port proof, this anchors the actual complete representation, not merely its numerical volume. Reversing the cyclic TRAVERSAL label to respect that operator order does not change the oriented complete geometry. There is an explicit holomorphic Mobius isometry F(zeta)=rho^2/zeta. It sends Z_k -> Z_(-k), U_k^+ -> U_(-k-1)^-, U_k^- -> U_(-k-1)^+, Q_k -> Q_(-k-1), T_k^+ <-> T_(-k)^-, W_+ <-> W_-. Under the literal cross-copy shaded gluing, applying F to both sides gives the SAME gluing at index -k read in its inverse direction: the original U_(k-1)^+ -> U_k^- becomes U_(-k)^- -> U_(-k-1)^+, and the other outer vertex behaves likewise. Thus the reverse traversal is matched by an orientation-preserving isometry, not by an assumed mirror identification. The original boxes and their source labels are not permuted in the quantum formula.

title: Literal port gluing and the complete geometric holonomy anchor
text:
# Literal port gluing and the complete geometric holonomy anchor 29 October 2026. The selected regular mixed source has an explicit matrix lift to the ORIGINAL augmented pretzel diagram. Its common \(w\) and outer equation \(\prod_iU_i=1\) glue the actual ports. At completeness, every white AND shaded face map agrees with the explicit four-antiprism geometry. Thus its base representation is the oriented geometric holonomy, not merely a character with the same cusp Hessian or a representation with similar trace equations. This note uses the actual stationary identities in [the local mixed-character lift](actual_pretzel_mixed_regular_character_lift.md). It does not infer a source cycle or a quantum asymptotic from those identities; those were proved separately from the finite source. The lift below is a DIRECT algebraic construction: its group relations, framed peripheral eigenvalues and cap equalities are verified explicitly. It does not require a further assertion identifying the canonical state graph of an arbitrary scalar operator \(F(\Omega)\) from its unwrapped eigenphase. In particular a state-versus-observable Hurwitz convention is not silently used to choose between \(U\) and \(U^{-1}\). ## 1. A common two-head frame and the literal turned ports Let \(w
e0,\pm1\), set \(k=(w-1)^2/(w+1)^2\), and for \(z
e0\) put \[ g(z)= egin{pmatrix} -2w/(w+1)&z\-k/z&-2/(w+1) \end{pmatrix},\qquad h(z)=g(-wz),\qquad A=\operatorname{diag}(w,w^{-1}). 	ag{1} \] They have determinant one and trace \(-2\), and \(h(z)g(z)=A\). Neither meridian is central on this chart. The fixed flag of \(g(z)\) is \(z/r\), where \(r=(w-1)/(w+1)\); the fixed flag of \(h(z)\) is \(-wz/r\). For a rotated box with character \(U
e0\), take incoming pair \((g(z),h(z))\) and outgoing pair \((g(Uz),h(Uz))\). The original turn index map is \[ (\mathscr R B)_{(u,b);(v,e)} =x^{u-e}B_{(d-u,v);(b,d-e)}. \] The actual cup/cap identifies the bent meridian with its inverse. Choose based paths along these turn arcs. Therefore the original UNROTATED box has incoming and outgoing ordered meridians \[ (a,b)=(h(Uz),h(z)^{-1}),\qquad (r_{\mathrm{out}},s_{\mathrm{out}})=(g(Uz)^{-1},g(z)). 	ag{2} \] Their common product is the actual crossing-disk product \[ P=ba=h(z)^{-1}h(Uz)=g(z)g(Uz)^{-1} =s_{\mathrm{out}}r_{\mathrm{out}}. 	ag{3} \] This is the literal turn convention, rather than a free choice of independent strand gauges. At the quantum level the same turns and their scalars are those of the exact rotated source. Their normalization does not alter the group inverse relation. ## 2. The auxiliary circle is an explicit regular centralizer On the local regular stationary branch write \[ U= rac{wY-1}{w-Y},\qquad L= rac{H-X}{1-HX},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}P=-L-L^{-1}. \] The stationary \(X\) equation also gives the exact identity \[  rac{1+YL}{1+Y/L}= rac{L^2}{H}. 	ag{4} \] These are the rational equations certified from the actual finite factorial phase, with its selected branch, in the linked local theorem. Put \[ \Delta=(1+YL)(1+Y/L)=1-Y\operatorname{Tr}P+Y^2, \] \[ J= rac{I-YP}{\sqrt\Delta},\qquad C= rac{YI-P}{\sqrt\Delta}. 	ag{5} \] The square root is its analytic branch tending to \(1+Y\) at \(H=1,L=1\). It is nonzero near the complete branch. Both matrices have determinant one, commute with \(P\), and \(JC=-P\). On the \(P\)-eigenflag with eigenvalue \(\lambda=-L^{-1}\), equation (4) gives \[ C	ext{ eigenvalue }M=H^{-1/2}, 	ag{6} \] on the branch tending to \(+1\). The reciprocal flag has eigenvalue \(M^{-1}\). Thus this is the actual auxiliary meridian together with the preferred disk-longitude eigenvalue \(-L^{-1}\); its SL spin character is kept. title: A direct positive ideal triangulation and the full source angle critical point
text: # A direct positive ideal triangulation and the full source angle critical point 29 October 2026. The ACTUAL half-twisted augmented pretzel polyhedra admit a positive geometric ideal triangulation with compatible face pairings. The proof below checks every homogeneous face map; no general Epstein--Penner existence theorem is used. This removes an optional dependency from the Casson--Rivin presentation. The already proved finite-center/equivariant-map geometric completion does not need it. ## 1. An explicit homogeneous section of every original ideal cell Use alpha=pi/s, rho^2=sec(alpha)+tan(alpha), and the actual P_s vertices Z_i=rho exp(2ii alpha), U_i^+=rho^-1 exp((2i+1)i alpha), U_i^-=rho^3 exp((2i+1)i alpha). The face cycles and their literal half-twist pairings are those of [the geometric cellulation](actual_augmented_pretzel_geometric_volume.md) and [the complete port anchor](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md). Put O=(0,rho) in upper half-space. The rotation R(z)=exp(2i alpha)z and the holomorphic half-turn F_i(z)=rho^2 exp(4ii alpha)/z (1) are genuine global P_s isometries: substitution permutes its vertices, and hence its convex hull. In particular F_i: (Z_i,U_(i-1)^+,U_i^+) ->(Z_i,U_i^-,U_(i-1)^-). (2) The finite dihedral group generated by R and F_0 fixes O. Conversely a point fixed by the rotation lies on the vertical axis, and F_0 fixes only height rho on that axis. Averaging any finite interior point in the future hyperboloid over this finite group and normalizing stays inside every strict supporting halfspace. The average is O. Thus O is STRICTLY interior to P_s, not merely a guessed symmetry center. In the Lorentz model use the ideal light lift l(z)=(|z|^2+1,2Re z,2Im z,|z|^2-1), V(z)=rho l(z)/(|z|^2+rho^2). (3) Then -<O,V(z)>=1, using the unit hyperboloid representative of O. All lifted ideal vertices of this cell lie in the SAME affine three-plane A_O={v:-<O,v>=1}, which does not contain the origin. Since F_i fixes O, its Lorentz action carries V(z) EXACTLY to V(F_i z), without an additional scalar on the light ray. ## 2. Every actual face map preserves these lifts Let r_+ be the reflection in the white W_+ plane. Develop the second cell as r_+ P_s and give it center r_+ O and light lifts r_+ V(z). These satisfy its analogous affine normalization. For a white face Q or W_-, the literal transition from the second cell to the first is r_face r_+. Applied to its face vertices it gives (r_face r_+) r_+ V(z)=r_face V(z)=V(z), (4) because a Lorentz plane reflection fixes the ENTIRE plane, including the normalized light vectors, not only their projective endpoints. For W_+ the transition is identity and r_+ itself fixes those vectors. Thus every white face preserves the homogeneous lifts exactly. For shaded faces, the complete port proof gives actual orientation- preserving transitions gamma_i^+ and gamma_i^- with the ordered maps gamma_i^+ r_+ : (Z_i,U_i^-,U_(i-1)^-) ->(Z_i,U_(i-1)^+,U_i^+), gamma_i^- r_+ : (Z_i,U_(i-1)^+,U_i^+) ->(Z_i,U_i^-,U_(i-1)^-). (5) They agree on those three ideal points with the GLOBAL isometry F_i in(1). This statement checks all three vertices, not only a fixed flag. The maps gamma_i^plusminus r_+ reverse ambient orientation, whereas F_i preserves it. Consequently their precise difference is reflection in the source triangle plane: composing with that plane reflection makes an orientation-preserving Mobius map fixing three distinct points, which is identity. Such a plane reflection fixes each V(z) exactly. It follows that on the actual face vertices gamma_i^plusminus r_+ V(z)=F_i V(z)=V(target z). (6) Equation(6) is the needed scalar-normalization check. It does NOT assert that gamma_i maps the second CELL CENTER to the first center. Only its homogeneous face section is required, and that has now been proved. The literal reverse-cap traversal is the same holomorphic F_0 combined with an index reversal; it preserves(3) and is not a mirror gluing. Thus the two cells, every face pairing and all their translates have Gamma-equivariant ideal lifts with affine face maps. The complete face-pairing identities make this assignment consistent. This proof uses the actual retained half twists; it does not replace the source by its untwisted partner. ## 3. A finite compatible subdivision, proved directly Here is the elementary affine subdivision argument for these cells. For a three-dimensional convex cell with v vertices, vertex heights modulo affine functions have dimension v-4. For a paired n-gonal face, requiring the two height restrictions to differ by an affine function imposes at most n-3 linear conditions. Under such a condition the two lower-face subdivisions match, since adding an affine function does not change a regular subdivision. For a finite paired affine cellulation, the total remaining dimension is at least sum_cells(v-4)-sum_facepairs(n-3) =(1/2)sum_cells(f-4). (7) Use twice the edge count for the sum of face side counts and v-e+f=2 for each convex three-cell. Every cell has f>=4, and equality means a tetrahedron. If some cell is not tetrahedral, (7) is positive. Choose a nonzero compatible class of heights and take its lower convex subdivision. At least one cell refines nontrivially; all new cells are three-dimensional, use only old vertices and have matched affine faces. Every original vertex is extreme in projection, so the lower subdivision does not discard an original boundary vertex. Repeat. This terminates: assign each resulting three-cell one affine- independent quadruple of its original vertices. Two cells with disjoint interiors cannot contain the same nondegenerate tetrahedron. Within each original cell only finitely many quadruples exist, while every nontrivial refinement increases the cell count. If a non-tetrahedral cell remained, (7) would permit another refinement, contradicting this finite bound. Thus a finite compatible tetrahedral subdivision results. Apply this argument in the affine planes from(3)--(6). Four affine- independent light vectors in A_O are LINEARLY independent because A_O does not contain zero.
