Hence their ideal hyperbolic tetrahedron is nonflat. Convex subdivision gives its positive orientation. The result is a finite POSITIVE GEOMETRIC IDEAL triangulation of the actual complete augmented manifold. No literature triangulation existence theorem is needed for this class. At the selected sufficiently long filling, move its ideal vertex orbits by the actual bounded framed representation and its marked peripheral flags. Every one of the finitely many shapes stays in the upper half-plane by continuity. Contractible edge transitions are identity, so positive edge angle sums remain exactly2pi. This gives a positive source angle point on the ACTUAL ideal triangulation. ## 4. The full edge/peripheral tangent space, not just the source-family tangent For t tetrahedra and h cusp tori let E be the edge-Hamiltonian space in the 2t-dimensional real shape symplectic space. Its rank is t-h. The rank statement can be checked directly: an edge-row relation has equal sums on opposite edge pairs in every abstract tetrahedron. Its six local coefficients therefore have the form lambda_ij=a_i+a_j. The formula a_i=(lambda_ij+lambda_ik-lambda_jk)/2 shows that a_i agrees across matched faces. Connected ideal vertex links propagate it to one constant per cusp. Conversely every cusp constant gives a relation. The ideal Euler count gives t global edges, so precisely h independent relations leave rank t-h. The edge rows are isotropic: the local skew corner counts cancel across paired faces. The peripheral rows belong to E^perp; the same local normal-curve count pairs a primitive meridian and longitude by -2, with different cusp tori pairing zero. Thus their 2h rows span the ENTIRE symplectic quotient E^perp/E. This is the actual marked incidence calculation underlying the [boundary pairing proof](bloch_lift_and_boundary_torsor.md), not a claim that stationarity on a small source family exhausts the angle tangent. Use centered projective logs U_i,V_i, so the reduced form is Omega_red=-(1/2)sum_i dU_i wedge dV_i. (8) At any positive full complex gluing solution, its real shape-log vector lies in E^perp. EVERY affine angle tangent satisfying the edge equations lies there too. The sine rule for a positive tetrahedron gives dVol(delta theta)=Omega(Re shape,delta theta) =(1/2)sum_i[Re V_i delta Im U_i -Re U_i delta Im V_i]. (9) Consequently an incomplete gluing point is critical on its FULL fixed- peripheral-ANGLE slice, even though it need not maximize the larger unfilled cusp angle domain. No nonlinear gluing condition is imposed on the tangent delta theta in(9). For the actual filled source, Re(U_i+p_iV_i)=0. On the larger affine slice fixing only Im(U_i+p_iV_i)=the actual primitive2pi angle, its contribution in(9) is (1/2)Re V_i delta Im(U_i+p_iV_i)=0. Every unfilled main cusp has U_i=V_i=0, so it contributes zero as well. Thus the source is stationary on the FULL filled-slope angle slice, not merely on its selected critical representation curve. ## 5. Concavity, boundary maxima and the actual hyperbolic value For angles alpha,beta,gamma>0 with sum pi, the negative Hessian of Lambda(alpha)+Lambda(beta)+Lambda(gamma) in (alpha,gamma) is [[cot alpha+cot beta,cot beta], [cot beta,cot gamma+cot beta]]. Its determinant is1 and its first diagonal entry is sin(gamma)/(sin(alpha)sin(beta))>0. It is strictly positive definite. Thus total ideal volume is strictly concave on every affine positive angle slice. At the positive source point its full constrained derivative vanishes by(9). Every straight segment from it to a different point in the closed angle polytope stays positive before its final endpoint; its volume is strictly decreasing after its initial zero derivative. Continuity at zero/pi angles then makes EVERY different boundary value strictly smaller as well. The source point is the unique GLOBAL maximum. The value is the marked source regulator because the shapes develop the same actual representation and oriented fundamental class. The [primitive-angle proof](actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.md) and [general geometric completion](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md) identify it with the complete filled metric and its hyperbolic volume. The complete augmented maximum V_s and the finite filled maximum V_src(p) are different: each uses its OWN affine peripheral constraints. This proves the optional Casson--Rivin certificate for the current explicit augmented family, with all existence/rank premises checked. For an arbitrary base, the general geometric completion remains valid without an ideal triangulation. A universal Casson--Rivin presentation still needs a verified positive ideal angle chart; it does not follow from an arbitrary original source critical point or a matching action alone. [The focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_positive_ideal_angle_certificate.py) passes 90-digit NUMERICAL checks of all labeled homogeneous white/shaded vertex maps for six widths, including even widths and the literal half twists. It compares FULL Lorentz/Hermitian light matrices in the normalization(3), not projective point images alone. It also checks the analytical identity F_i(O)=O to that precision. The exactness assertions are supplied by(1)--(6), not by finite-precision arithmetic. The finite compatible-subdivision, rank and strict-concavity arguments above are analytical and do not rest on these samples.

title: The proposed pretzel radial homotopy has no strict boundary-action gap
text: # The proposed pretzel radial homotopy has no strict boundary-action gap **Subsequent resolution for this source.** The obstruction proved below remains valid, but the [full coherent period theorem](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) now combines the equal-height contributions by an exact finite inner transformation and controls all remaining indices with both recurrence branches. It proves complete-base survival without the false strict boundary gap. The unfilled augmented link, not a fixed knot filling, is the scope of that result. 29 October 2026. For the EXACT phase of the double sum in [the complete original pretzel polynomial](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md), the original-radius diagonal boundary attains the SAME action as the candidate shifted interior saddle, for EVERY fixed real w<-1. Consequently no uniform strict boundary gap holds on the proposed closed homotopy rho_X in [rho_*,0]. This does not refute a deformation which coherently fills or combines that endpoint current. It identifies the endpoint contribution such a deformation must retain. ## 1. Phase, branches, and the candidate saddle Write w=-W, W>1, X=exp(rho+i theta), Y=exp(i phi), with 0<phi<theta<pi and rho<=0. Use the principal dilogarithm, taking the boundary value of Li2(Y/X) from Im(Y/X)<0. Thus its continuation to theta=phi at rho<0 is its LOWER-side value on (1,infinity). The phase is S=-6Li2(1)-Li2(X^2)+4Li2(X)+Li2(1/X)-Li2(Y/X) +Li2(w)+Li2(1/w)-Li2(wY)-Li2(Y/w)+3Li2(Y). Put F=Im S. The lower-side convention is essential at the diagonal; resetting its logarithm changes F by a radial mark. Set A=W+W^(-1) and phi_*=2 arctan(sqrt(A+2)/2), Y_*=exp(i phi_*), X_*=(Y_*-1)/(Y_*+3), rho_*=log|X_*|, theta_*=arg X_*. Then rho_*<0 and 0<phi_*<theta_*<pi. These are the specified exponentiated stationary equations. On this chart D_X S=0 and D_Y S=2pi i at the point. The retained mark -2pi i Log Y makes the latter an actual zero derivative; because |Y|=1 this mark is real on the angular triangle and does not change F or the result below. ## 2. An exact identity equates the diagonal and interior actions For ANY 0<phi<pi, set Y=exp(i phi), X(Y)=(Y-1)/(Y+3), and define G(X;Y)=-Li2(X^2)+4Li2(X)+Li2(1/X)-Li2(Y/X). The following equality is exact: Im G(X(Y);Y)=3 Cl2(phi)-Cl2(2phi)=Im G(Y;Y). (1) Here Cl2(a)=Im Li2(exp(i a)); it uses the same continuous principal boundary values, not a changed dilogarithm sheet. Proof. X(Y) is in the upper unit disk. Indeed Im X=4sin(phi)/|Y+3|^2 and |X|^2=(2-2cos(phi))/(10+6cos(phi))<1. Moreover 1-Y/X=(1+Y)^2/(1-Y) has argument (pi+phi)/2, so Y/X lies in the lower half-plane and arg X>phi. All the displayed logarithms therefore vary continuously. Direct differentiation gives D_X G=2Log(1-X^2)-4Log(1-X) +Log(1-1/X)-Log(1-Y/X). Its exponential is one at X=X(Y). Its limit as phi decreases to zero is zero, fixing the integer logarithmic ambiguity, hence D_X G=0 on the entire interval. Thus d_phi Im G(X(Y);Y)=log|1-Y/X| =2log|1+Y|-log|1-Y|. The same derivative is obtained from 3Cl2(phi)-Cl2(2phi), since d_a Cl2(a)=-log|1-exp(i a)|. Both sides of (1) tend to zero as phi increases to pi. This proves (1), including its constant. The other terms of S depend only on Y,w, so (1) proves F(rho_*,theta_*,phi_*;w)=F(0,phi_*,phi_*;w). (2) In particular the diagonal boundary of the ORIGINAL radius is not strictly below the candidate interior action. ## 3. It is precisely the maximum on that boundary edge On rho=0, theta=phi, inversion of the two w-dependent dilogarithms gives the explicit real function B_W(phi)=6Cl2(phi)-Cl2(2phi) -2Im Li2(-exp(i phi)/W)+phi log W. (3) There is no omitted imaginary constant: Li2(-W),Li2(-1/W) are real, and Log(-wY)=log W+i phi in the inversion formula. With t=tan(phi/2)>0, differentiation and elementary sine algebra give B_W'(phi)=log([(A+2)+(A-2)t^2]/(4t^4)). (4) The numerator minus 4t^4 equals -(1+t^2)(4t^2-A-2). Hence B_W has a UNIQUE maximum, at t^2=(A+2)/4, which is exactly phi_*. Combining (2)--(4), max_(0<=phi<=pi) F(0,phi,phi;w)=F_* . (5) Equations (2) and (5) disprove the requested strict uniform boundary gap for every w<-1. They do not assert that another boundary edge or an intermediate radius exceeds F_*, nor that a fixed strictly shifted triangle lacks its own boundary gap. No such extra statement is needed. For reference, the opposite far corner has the exact lower-side value F(rho,pi,pi;w)=pi(log W-rho). It rises under the radial shift and therefore also cannot be dismissed by an unmarked endpoint rule. ## 4. The equal-action boundary is present in the original finite source The exact double summand in formula (11a) of the original polynomial is, with F_j=(Q;Q)_j, A_(v,r)=F_(2v)/F_v^4 * (Q^(-v);Q)_r Q^r/F_r^3 *(qw;Q)_r(q/w;Q)_r, 0<=r<=v<=M=floor((N-1)/2). At the DIAGONAL physical endpoint r=v it is exactly A_(v,v)=(-1)^v Q^(-v(v-1)/2) *F_(2v)(qw;Q)_v(q/w;Q)_v/F_v^6. (6) Every factor in (6) is nonzero for w<-1 and 0<=v<=M. In particular this is not an outside-support zero of (Q^(-v);Q)_r: that zero first occurs at r=v+1. The outer polynomial/source factors N^2/kappa remain as in the original formula. No nonzero coefficient for the ENTIRE period is inferred by taking a single endpoint term. An exact factorial completion also makes the retained endpoint plain. Put h=2pi i/N, delta=v-r, alpha_+=d/2+Log(W)/h and alpha_-=d/2-Log(W)/h. With the exact Fhat_N of [the original factorial interpolation](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md), the following meromorphic function takes the literal values A_(v,r): Ahat(v,r)=exp(pi i r+h[-vr+r(r+1)/2]) *Fhat(2v)/[Fhat(v)^3 Fhat(v-r)Fhat(r)^3] *Fhat(alpha_++r)/Fhat(alpha_+) *Fhat(alpha_-+r)/Fhat(alpha_-). (7) Both alpha choices satisfy Q^(alpha_++1)=qw and Q^(alpha_-+1)=q/w. Their sum uses the actual negative-w logarithmic marks; the product has no unspecified periodic factor. Formula (7) follows from the exact factorial shift and (Q^(-v);Q)_r=(-1)^r Q^(-vr+r(r-1)/2) F_v/F_(v-r) at the physical integers. The physical change (v,r)->(delta,r) is unimodular, so its local lattice residues have no new Jacobian. This constructs the SAME finite residue functional in the new coordinates; it is not a pointwise identity between two products of cotangents or permission to omit their chart-change currents. Near delta=0 and a compact tangential neighborhood of the equal-action point, Fhat(delta) is holomorphic, nonzero and Fhat(0)=1; all other scaled factorial arguments lie in regular compact substrips. Thus the cot pole at delta=0 has its ORIGINAL NONZERO residue (6). Conversely 1/Fhat(delta) has simple zeros at delta=-1,-2,...,-m for any fixed small normal collar m<N, canceling those newly enclosed cot poles provided the remaining factors stay regular. This permits the familiar zero-side local filling; it does not delete delta=0 or supply a strict action gap there. Finite-height connecting contours and all their currents must be retained exactly as in the proved simple seam filling. An exact residue cycle is the sum of small product circles about (delta,r) in Z_>=0^2 with delta+r<=M, with density Ahat times the two unit-residue cotangent factors. It is the original finite sum. Moving it to the shifted saddle requires an actual relative-cycle operation through this equal-action endpoint packet. Its coefficient, possible coherent cancellation, and any resulting uniform asymptotic remain unproved by radial concavity alone. The subsequent [coherent finite inner elimination](actual_pretzel_coherent_inner_gauss_elimination.md) does handle this packet without postulating that radial homotopy: an exact balanced finite transformation keeps the half shift and proves its nonzero amplitude in the geometric range. The [whole circle/period assembly](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) uses that coherent sum and an all-index two-branch upper envelope, rather than the false strict boundary-gap premise disproved here. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_radial_boundary_gap.py) supplements the proof with high-precision branch/derivative equalities and literal finite-factorial diagonal identities. It is not used to infer an asymptotic or a selected thimble coefficient.

title: The actual pretzel winding period and its explicit positive saddle family
text: # The actual pretzel winding period and its explicit positive saddle family **Subsequent global proof.** The [coherent circle and period theorem](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) now proves survival for this complete augmented source, with explicit nonzero leading constant and original normalization. The local symbol calculations below alone do not imply that result; its additional finite transformation, global recurrence bound and Gaussian estimates are supplied in the linked proof. 29 October 2026. The complete augmented odd-pretzel source has an exact one-variable residue with finitely many integer windings. Its literal factorial coefficients give a positive-shape stationary family for every fixed odd number of boxes. The action and the full Hessian can be computed explicitly. This identifies candidate exponential rates of the ORIGINAL period; it does not prove that its selected cycle has a nonzero coefficient at those saddles or that every other contribution is smaller. In particular a proposed strict radial-homotopy boundary gap is false: an original diagonal face has the same action height. That face must be combined with the interior contribution using the exact source, not discarded as exponentially small. ## 1. Exact winding, including its normal multiplicity Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, kappa=q^(d^2/2), and M=floor(d/2). The [literal complete base polynomial](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md) is denoted z_N(z). It is the actual quarter-turn of R^(-1)L_N, with degree at most M and every scalar retained. For s odd boxes the unchanged raw marked source is A_(N,s)=Phi_2(z_N^s), Phi_2(F)=(-1)^d N^2 [z^d](F mod P_N), P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2. The [full commutant and marked-trace proof](actual_pair_casimir_commutant_and_rotated_trace.md) establishes this on all physical channels, not a semisimple projection. Any existing external framing/peripheral line still multiplies A_(N,s). Polynomial division or residues at infinity give EXACTLY Phi_2(F)=(-1)^d N^2/(2*pi*i) integral F(z)/P_N(z) dz, (1) around every finite node. Put z=w+w^(-1). On |w|=R>1 this is a positively oriented ellipse enclosing those nodes, and P_N(w+w^-1)=(1+w^N)^2/w^N. Consequently A_(N,s)=(-1)^d N^2/(2*pi*i) integral_(|w|=R) z_N(w+w^-1)^s w^N(1-w^-2)/(1+w^N)^2 dw. (2) The full squared denominator is compulsory. Expanding it on |w|>1 gives the finite coefficient identity A_(N,s)=(-1)^d N^2 sum_(m>=1) (-1)^(m-1)m ([w^(mN-1)]-[w^(mN+1)]) z_N(w+w^-1)^s. (3) Only m<=floor((sM+1)/N) can occur. At fixed odd s these are eventually m=1,...,(s-1)/2. The coefficient m is the retained confluent/normal source. There is no authorization to keep only m=1 before estimating the others. The existing complete-base audit checks (3) against literal original sources at all tested even and odd levels. An immediate exact upper bound is |A_(N,s)| <= N^2 (R+R^-1)/(1-R^-N)^2 * R^-N *max_(|w|=R)|z_N(w+w^-1)|^s. (4) The [coherent capacity diagnostic](actual_pretzel_coherent_radial_capacity_diagnostic.md) tests (4) with the actual polynomial and all normal channels. A sampled circle maximum is not a certified analytic upper bound. ## 2. The phase comes from the literal finite coefficient Write F_a=(Q;Q)_a. The complete-base theorem gives kappa*z_N(w+w^-1)/N^2 =sum_(v=0)^M sum_(r=0)^v F_(2v)/F_v^4 * (Q^-v;Q)_r(qw;Q)_r(q/w;Q)_r Q^r/F_r^3. (5) The positive continuant coefficient used to prove this simplifies to b_v=N^2 |F_(2v)|/|F_v|^4. Indeed the original cosine product is (Q^(v+1);Q)_(d-2v)=F_(d-v)/F_v=N/|F_v|^2. The fixed phase in the continuant then gives b_v x^v=N^2F_(2v)/F_v^4. This removes no phase from the finite sum (5). Set X=exp(2*pi*i*v/N), Y=exp(2*pi*i*r/N). On a regular compact subdomain the leading phase of a summand in (5), derived by integrating its exact factorial/Pochhammer logarithms, is S(X,Y;w)=-6Li_2(1)-Li_2(X^2)+4Li_2(X)+Li_2(1/X) -Li_2(Y/X)+Li_2(w)+Li_2(1/w) -Li_2(wY)-Li_2(Y/w)+3Li_2(Y). (6) The exponent convention is exp[N*S/(2*pi*i)]. At the points below use principal dilogarithms continued on their indicated upper/lower sides. The overall kappa^-1 contributes a real leading action constant pi^2, and thus does not change the volume rate. Endpoint-uniform expansions and contour selection do not follow from the interior phase calculation. Its exponentiated logarithmic derivatives are exp(S_logX)=(1+X)^2/[(X-1)(X-Y)], exp(S_logY)=(1-Y/X)(1-wY)(1-Y/w)/(1-Y)^3, exp(S_logw)=(wY-1)/(w-Y). (7) These also follow directly from the exact consecutive-term ratios in (5). They are algebraic equations for the stationary support, with the logarithmic marks still to be specified. ## 3. All box counts have an explicit positive-shape stationary branch For one winding m with 0<m<s/2 put alpha=pi*m/s, eta=2 asinh(tan alpha), beta=atan(sec alpha), w_*=-exp(eta), Y_*=exp(2i beta), X_*=(Y_*-1)/(Y_*+3)=i sec(alpha)/(2-i sec(alpha)). (8) Then |Y_*|=1, |X_*|<1 and 0<arg Y_*<arg X_*<pi. Eliminating X from the first two equations in (7) gives Y=(3X+1)/(1-X), w+w^-1=6-16Y/(1+Y)^2. (9) With U=exp(2*pi*i*m/s), the third equation gives Y=(Uw+1)/(w+U). Substitution factors exactly as (w-1)^2[(U+1)^2w^2-2(U^2-6U+1)w+(U+1)^2]=0. The positive branch (8) is the root outside the unit circle and obeys w+w^-1=2-16U/(1+U)^2=2-4 sec^2(alpha). (10) The factor w=1 is not silently identified with this branch. There is an essential inner mark: on the specified dilogarithm sheets, S_logX=0, S_logY=2*pi*i, S_logw=2i alpha. (11) Thus the genuinely stationary marked phase for the s separate factors of z_N^s is W_m=sum_(i=1)^s [S(X_i,Y_i;w)-2*pi*i Log Y_i] -2*pi*i*m Log w. (12) Equation exp(S_logY)=1 does not justify omitting that mark. At (8) it changes only the real part of the action, since |Y_*|=1. ## 4. Exact action and nondegeneracy Let Lambda(theta)=-integral_0^theta log|2sin t|dt. The action on (8) is Im W_m=8s [Lambda(pi/4+alpha/2)+Lambda(pi/4-alpha/2)]. (13) One direct proof uses the stationary equations with their marks. For the action per box, differentiation in alpha gives dV/dalpha=-2log|w_*|=-4asinh(tan alpha). Elementary differentiation of the right side of (13), divided by s, gives the same derivative. Both sides tend to zero as alpha tends to pi/2; on the phase side this follows from dilogarithm inversion and (pi-2alpha)log|w_*|->0. This fixes the additive regulator constant. In particular s=3,m=1 gives 4v_8, where v_8=8Lambda(pi/4). Among this specified positive branch family the action strictly decreases with m, so m=1 has the largest action. This is not a classification of every complex or endpoint contribution of the original cycle. The Hessian is nondegenerate, without an assumed Gaussian coefficient. In logarithmic coordinates (X,Y,w), let H_3 be the Hessian of S and H_2 its X,Y block. On the stationary loci, det H_3=-Y(Y-1)(Y+3)^2(w^2-6w+1) /[4(w-Y)(Y+1)^2(Yw-1)], det H_2=-Y^2(Y+3)^2(w-1)^2 /[(w-Y)(Y+1)^3(Yw-1)]. (14) All factors are nonzero at (8). The effective outer Schur entry is i cos(alpha). For the full 2s+1 variables of (12), block elimination therefore gives det Hess W_m=s (det H_2)^(s-1) det H_3 !=0. (15) These are local phase statements. A nondegenerate stationary point with nonzero local factorial amplitude is not yet a nonzero coefficient in the selected original global period. ## 5. The equal-height original face is a genuine remaining obstruction The proposed shift of log|X| from zero to log|X_*| cannot be justified by a strict boundary gap. For every upper unit Y and X=(Y-1)/(Y+3), the X-dependent part of (6) has exactly the SAME imaginary part as at X=Y. The original diagonal edge X=Y has its unique maximum at Y_*. Hence it reaches the height of the shifted interior stationary point for every w_*<-1. The [independent exact boundary calculation](actual_pretzel_radial_boundary_gap.md) proves this identity with its branch marks. The actual r=v summand in (5) is nonzero, and its endpoint residue survives the exact factorial interpolation. It cannot be dismissed as an exterior zero or an exponentially smaller boundary prism. The next analytic requirement is to combine that diagonal-face period and the interior contribution coherently, or eliminate the redundant inner sum by an exact transformation. Until this is done, (13)--(15) and numerical agreement with (4) do not prove augmented-base survival, and still less the volume limit after fixed long fillings. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_pretzel_winding_phase_and_geometric_saddles.py) checks the algebraic elimination, all logarithmic marks, Hessian factors, and the action formula. Exact finite winding/source checks remain in the linked complete-base audit. No selected-cycle claim is inferred.

title: The actual primitive gauge has a Gaussian resonant endpoint
text: # The actual primitive gauge has a Gaussian resonant endpoint 27 October 2026. The canonical finite Hilbert-90 gauge from the original source has an exactly computable resonant endpoint. Its polynomial Ward identity contains two retained highest-degree terms. The endpoint is a quadratic Gauss period, of size N^(-1/2), despite the gauge's exponential operator norm on the flat relative module. This settles the endpoint of THIS specified source gauge. It does not evaluate the knot-dependent endpoint sum or identify the marked geometric A-period. In particular it supplies no additional knot-volume conjecture proof. ## 1. Canonical polynomial and exact unreduced Ward equation Use Q=exp(2pi*i/N), N>=2, F_r=(Q;Q)_r, and v_N(z)=sum_(r=0)^(N-1) (-1)^r Q^(r(r-1)/2)z^r/F_r. Let g_N(z)=sum_(r=0)^(N-1)c_r z^r be the CANONICAL degree-<N representative of v_N(z)v_N(Qz) modulo z^N. It is the actual primitive source gauge in [the Fourier transport theorem](actual_source_fourier_twisted_traces.md), whose regular-disk action was proved in [the gauge-action note](actual_hilbert90_gauge_dilogarithm_action.md). As an ordinary polynomial, before setting z^N=0, it obeys (1-z)(1-Qz)g_N(Qz)-g_N(z) =-(2/N)z^N+c_(N-1)z^(N+1). (1) To prove this, first keep the full ordinary product w_N(z)=v_N(z)v_N(Qz), including its degrees N,...,2N-2. The exact Euler Ward equation is (1-z)v_N(Qz)=v_N(z)-z^N/N. Multiplying its versions at z and Qz gives (1-z)(1-Qz)w_N(Qz)-w_N(z) =-z^N[v_N(z)+v_N(Qz)]/N+z^(2N)/N^2. (2) Hence the coefficient of z^N is -2/N, and coefficients below N vanish. Removing the high tail of w_N does not alter that z^N coefficient: its own degree-N contribution to the left side is (Q^N-1)[z^N]w_N=0. The left side for g_N has degree at most N+1; its top coefficient is Q^N c_(N-1)=c_(N-1). This proves (1). Equivalently it gives the exact coefficient relation c_(N-2)=(1+Q)c_(N-1)-2Q/N. Setting the polynomial argument z=1 in (1) now yields g_N(1)=2/N-c_(N-1). (3) Both source terms in (1) are required. If (1) were replaced by its homogeneous identity in z^N=0 before evaluation, the selected endpoint would be changed. ## 2. The retained coefficient is an exact Gauss period The root factorial identity F_(N-1)=N gives, coefficient by coefficient, [z^(N-1-r)]v_N(z)=Q^(r+1)F_r/N, 0<=r<N. For example this follows from F_(N-1-r)=N(-1)^r Q^(r(r+1)/2)/F_r. Substituting it into the convolution for c_(N-1) cancels every factorial and gives c_(N-1)=(1/N)sum_(r=0)^(N-1) (-1)^r Q^(r(r-1)/2). (4) Thus (3)-(4) are an exact algebraic period evaluation of the canonical endpoint at every level, including composite N. They are not an identification of the nilpotent algebra with scalar points. The representative and the degree-N source were fixed before evaluation. ## 3. Direct Gaussian asymptotic, with the finite boundary retained Put T_N=sum_(r=0)^(N-1)(-1)^r Q^(r(r-1)/2), omega_N=exp[-pi*i*(N+1)/4-pi*i/(4N)]. Then T_N=sqrt(N) omega_N+O(1), (5) c_(N-1)=omega_N/sqrt(N)+O(1/N), g_N(1)=-omega_N/sqrt(N)+O(1/N). (6) Here is a proof of (5) without importing an incomplete-Gauss-sum estimate. On integer r the summand equals exp(2pi*i*f(r)), where f(x)=[x^2-(N+1)x]/(2N). Periodize exp(2pi*i*f(x)) times the indicator of [-1/2,N-1/2]. This is a piecewise smooth periodic function, and zero is away from its discontinuities. Its symmetrically summed Fourier series therefore gives the finite Poisson identity T_N=sum_(m in Z)^sym I_m, I_m=integral_(-1/2)^(N-1/2) exp(2pi*i*(f(x)-m*x)) dx. (7) For N>=4, f' lies in [-3/4,1/2]. For every nonzero m, integration by parts expresses I_m as [exp(2pi*i*(f(x)-m*x))/(2pi*i*(f'(x)-m))]_a^b +(1/(2pi*i)) integral_a^b f''(x) exp(2pi*i*(f(x)-m*x))/(f'(x)-m)^2 dx, with a=-1/2, b=N-1/2. The second term is O(m^-2), uniformly in N: f''=1/N, the interval has length N, and |f'(x)-m|>=|m|/4. The boundary terms also have an absolutely summable PAIRED bound. Both endpoints have exp(-2pi*i*m*x)=(-1)^m, and 1/(t-m)+1/(t+m)=2t/(t^2-m^2)=O(m^-2) uniformly for -3/4<=t<=1/2. Hence the sum of all m!=0 terms in (7) is O(1). No separate divergent boundary sums have been discarded. For m=0, complete the square around a_0=(N+1)/2. This gives I_0=exp[-pi*i*(N+1)^2/(4N)] sqrt(N) *integral_(-(N+2)/(2sqrt(N)))^((N-2)/(2sqrt(N))) exp(pi*i*y^2) dy. The complete Fresnel integral is exp(pi*i/4). It follows by Gaussian regularization, and its two tails are O(1/R) by one integration by parts beyond |y|=R. The displayed endpoints have size comparable to sqrt(N), so replacing them by infinity changes I_0 by O(1). Its complete value is sqrt(N) omega_N. Together with the nonzero Fourier modes this proves (5). The finitely many smaller levels do not affect the asymptotic. Equations (3)-(4) finish (6). In particular the exact resonant source gauge satisfies |g_N(1)|=N^(-1/2)[1+O(N^(-1/2))], log|g_N(1)|=-(1/2)log N+O(N^(-1/2)), (1/N)log|g_N(1)| -> 0. (8) It is nonzero for all sufficiently large N. No all-level nonvanishing claim beyond this is needed for (8). ## 4. Consequence for the actual source comparison The operator gauge has a positive exponential norm on a regular flat-metric chart, as already proved, while its canonical resonant endpoint (8) has no positive exponential rate. Neither its operator size nor a regular-chart dilogarithm value determines this selected endpoint. The high coefficient in (1) becomes the leading term of the endpoint; the source carry must be retained. This endpoint is not the original figure-eight invariant. Already at N=2, g_2(1)=1 whereas the original source identity for 4_1 gives Kashaev_2(4_1)=1+4=5. The whole-source proof for that knot uses a separate positive product sum, not this universal gauge. No equality with that invariant or a general knot period is introduced here. Thus this is a usable fully evaluated local source period, but it does not close the selected geometric-period or volume-norm gate for a general actual word. It specifies what has to be composed with that word and its other source sectors before any volume conclusion can follow. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_primitive_gauge_endpoint.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_primitive_gauge_endpoint_results.json) check the canonical polynomial coefficients, the FULL unreduced Ward equation and Gauss-period identity exactly at finite-field roots. High-precision samples separately diagnose (5)-(8); the uniform proof above establishes their asymptotic scope.

title: Original output Fourier projection removes the colliding negative-transfer poles
text: # Original output Fourier projection removes the colliding negative-transfer poles 28 October 2026. Keeping the ORIGINAL finite physical output projection resolves the simultaneous endpoint collisions left by the scalar simple-seam calculation. There is an exact matrix-valued total-transfer interpolant. At EVERY newly crossed negative integer its projected operator has a zero, including when its unprojected scalar coefficient has a pole. Consequently the complete cotangent density is holomorphic across the whole negative normal collar. Its operator norm and contour mass cost are exp(o(N)) on any collar of width N^alpha, alpha<1, uniformly in ALL physical input basis states. This is an actual full-source normal-boundary operation, not a favorable scalar interpolation with its output tails deleted. The Fourier/sinc factors are retained explicitly. It neither discards the original k=0 residue nor bounds an unrestricted bulk exterior by hyperbolic volume. ## 1. Literal physical Fourier projection and the interpolated crossing Use the original balanced complete heads, N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2pi*i/N), x=-exp(-pi*i/N), with orthonormal basis |j>,0<=j<=d. In L^2 of the unit circle use normalized measure dtheta/(2pi) and the specified logarithmic lift 0<=theta<=2pi. The orthogonal projection of exp(i nu theta) to the physical Fourier band is the ENTIRE vector v_N(nu)=sum_(j=0)^d s_j(nu)|j>, s_j(nu)=(exp(2pi*i*nu)-1)/(2pi*i*(nu-j)), (1) with its removable value one at nu=j. Thus v_N(j)=|j> inside the physical band, and v_N(j)=0 at every other integer. At an invalid integer its vector zero is at least simple. Orthogonality proves ||v_N(nu)||<=||exp(i nu theta)||_L2 <=exp(2pi |Im nu|). (2) No N-dependent conditioning or a nonpositive pivotal metric is used. Let the scalar r_N(a,b;z), 0<=a,b<=d, be the EXACT factorial interpolation of the ORIGINAL positive crossing: r_N(a,b;z)=kappa x^(-a-b+z)Q^(b(a-z)) *Fhat(b+z)F_a/[Fhat(z)F_b Fhat(a-z)]. (3) The normalizers, Gaussian, Cartan and completed factorial are those of [the total-transfer theorem](actual_total_transfer_endpoint_packets.md). Define the operator-valued continuation by its actual input columns, Rhat_N(z)|a,b>=r_N(a,b;z) v_N(b+z) tensor v_N(a-z). (4) This is precisely the contraction of the two original output Fourier projections with the scalar monomials of the physical crossing kernel. It is not an arbitrary change of its output source. At an integer 0<=k<=d it equals the ORIGINAL kth transfer slice: valid outputs give their literal basis vectors and forbidden transfers have their exact factorial zeros. The opposite crossing uses its actual conjugate mirror. Therefore the half-integer closed cotangent rectangle gives an OPERATOR identity before applying any knot closure, R_plus=integral_Gamma pi cot(pi z) Rhat_N(z) dz/(2pi*i), (5) where Gamma encloses precisely 0,...,d. The full original kappa is in (3); all physical head projections and any external pivotal, framing, peripheral or marked source are unchanged. Fubini on finite contours applies (5) simultaneously to every crossing of a fixed signed word. ## 2. Exact cancellation at a simultaneous negative endpoint collision Fix z=-s, with 1<=s<N. In this normal range Fhat has a simple pole at each negative integer, and a simple zero at N,...,2N-2. These orders follow directly from its convergent Gamma product or its shift continuation. Put I_1=1 if b<s, otherwise 0, I_2=1 if a+s>=N, otherwise 0. The scalar coefficient (3) has local order ord_(z=-s) r_N = 1-I_1-I_2. (6) The first invalid output is b-s<0, and the second is a+s>d. Formula (1) supplies a simple vector zero at EACH invalid output. Thus the complete column in (4) has order at least (1-I_1-I_2)+I_1+I_2=1. (7) In particular the double collision I_1=I_2=1 is not discarded: its scalar pole is canceled by TWO actual physical projection zeros, leaving another zero. This is exactly the source factor lost if one studies the scalar factorial coefficient alone. All scalar singularities in this collar lie at these integers. Consequently Rhat is holomorphic on the negative collar and vanishes at all its integers. Its complete density pi cot(pi z)Rhat_N(z) is holomorphic there too. No derivative residue or logarithmic source term has been omitted; the ENTIRE sinc vectors in (1) are retained before taking the removable limits. ## 3. Uniform polynomial base bound at every physical input endpoint Fix T>0 and let 0<=Re nu<=1, |Im nu|<=T. Uniformly in 0<=n<=d, |Fhat(n+nu)/F_n|<=C_T N^(C_T), |F_n/Fhat(n-nu)|<=C_T N^(C_T), |1/Fhat(nu)|<=C_T N. (8) Here is a direct estimate, including the input endpoints. On the fixed nu rectangle, its defining product gives Fhat(nu) bounded by C_T N^(-Re nu), and its reciprocal by C_T N^(Re nu). For the first ratio use the exact product Fhat(n+nu)/F_n=Fhat(nu) product_(j=1)^n (1-Q^(j+nu))/(1-Q^j). Each ratio is at most 1+C_T/min(j,N-j); the sum of their logarithms is O_T(log N). For the second ratio when n>=1, start at Fhat(1-nu) and use factors j=2,...,n. Its ratios are bounded by 1+C_T/min(j-1,N-j), and |F_1/Fhat(1-nu)| is polynomially bounded. For n=0 use 1/Fhat(-nu)=(1-Q^(1-nu))/Fhat(1-nu), which is regular and satisfies the same bound. Thus (8) does not hide a large F_n or its inverse at the physical endpoints. Since the Cartan multiplier in (3) is bounded on this fixed-height rectangle at physical a,b, (8) gives |r_N(a,b;nu)|<=C_T N^(C_T), uniformly for ALL a,b. Together with (2), this is the required bounded normal base for the actual projected operator. ## 4. A subexponential-cost compensated collar for the entire word The same exact ratio used for the sourced Ward equation gives r_N(z+1)/r_N(z) =c(1-Q^(b+z+1))(1-Q^(a-z))/(1-Q^(z+1)), c=xQ^(-b). (9) Take the rectangle -s-1/2<=Re z<=-1/2, |Im z|<=T, with s<N/2. On either half-integer vertical side or either nonzero-height horizontal side, write z=nu-M, 0<=Re nu<=1. Inverting (9) M times costs at most (C_T N^2)^M: each denominator 1-Q^(integer+nu) has magnitude at least c_T/N there, while the numerator is bounded. The distance from an integer is bounded below by min(1/2,T). The base estimate (8) and (2) therefore give on this ENTIRE boundary ||pi cot(pi z)Rhat_N(z)|| <=N^(C_T)(C_T N^2)^(s+1). (10) The matrix operator norm costs only another factor N from its N^2 input columns. The cotangent is bounded on these edges. Its apparent interior poles have already been removed in Section 2. The maximum principle applied to every scalar matrix coefficient <u,Rhat v>, or to this holomorphic complete density, extends (10) through the interior with the same bound. The added contour has length O_T(s+1). Moving the original left edge from -1/2 to -s-1/2 and retaining BOTH finite-height connecting pieces changes (5) by zero: all enclosed new poles are removable. Thus this is an exact source-preserving collar move with quantitative operator cost exp[O_T((s+1)log N)]. (11) For s<=N^alpha with any fixed alpha<1 this is exp(o(N)). The number of crossings and physical heads of a fixed diagram does not grow with N, so finitely many such original operator collar operations have the same subexponential additional cost. Every original cup, cap, pivot, phase and external line remains as prescribed. For an artificial positive split k=R the adjacent contours have opposite interface currents; moving them together retains the same integer residues with opposite signs. Equations (5)--(11) address the ACTUAL outer normal source as well, including the simultaneous collisions which a scalar split had left uncontrolled. ## 5. Scope of the advance This removes an artificial negative-transfer exit of normal width N^alpha at the full finite physical source, with explicit tame cost. The original integer residues 0,...,d remain enclosed. In particular it does not contradict the full-rate low Markov packet: no original residue has been declared zero or individually lower-rate. The physical input labels in (4) are the ORIGINAL finite basis labels. The bound is uniform over all of them, so it is an operator/source statement rather than a selected fixed-clock phase claim. If those input indices are themselves replaced by independent complex contour variables, one must retain the corresponding input projections and their joint sources; (7) is not an assertion for an arbitrary scalar continuation with those physical projections removed. Nothing here assigns a sharp geometric bound to an unrestricted bulk exterior, a real radial cutoff face, or a transfer collar of macroscopic width whose cost in (11) is no longer subexponential. It does not identify every stationary branch of a split sinc density with a knot representation: the entire physical projection must stay. The theorem is a quantitative full-source normal-boundary filling, not the global sublevel transport or volume conjecture. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_projected_transfer_cot_completion.py): original physical integer transfer slices, all simultaneous negative endpoint pole cancellations, fixed-height projected density limits, and finite-source tests including both physical input endpoints. The literal positive test includes the original common Cartan factor kappa=q^((N-1)^2/2), with its inverse in the negative crossing. An independent proof review verified the pole-order count, uniform endpoint base bounds, half-integer denominator estimates and operator maximum principle; the corrected full-scalar audit replay passed. The same audit now checks the [upper extension](actual_projected_transfer_upper_collar.md), its exact N-shift and fractional base identity, all physical upper collision orders and the two-sided expanded cotangent residue sum.

title: Both outer transfer collars admit a controlled original-source filling
text: # Both outer transfer collars admit a controlled original-source filling 28 October 2026. This completes the upper-end counterpart of the [all-input projected lower-collar theorem](actual_projected_transfer_cot_completion.md). The original positive and negative physical crossings admit exact cotangent contours with BOTH ends extended by N^alpha, alpha<1. Every new integer pole is removable, uniformly over all physical input states. The added contour pieces have exp(o(N)) operator cost. This is a local operator identity which may be inserted in any fixed original signed word with its closure unchanged. It does not estimate the unrestricted bulk factors or identify a geometric saddle of the full Fourier-projected density. ## 1. Retain the same original projected interpolation Use d=N-1, Q=exp(2pi*i/N), x=-exp(-pi*i/N), and the full original Cartan scalar kappa. With the exact completed factorial Fhat, set r(a,b;z)=kappa x^(-a-b+z)Q^(b(a-z)) Fhat(b+z)F_a/[Fhat(z)F_b Fhat(a-z)], Rhat(z)|a,b>=r(a,b;z) v_N(b+z) tensor v_N(a-z), v_N(nu)=sum_(j=0)^d [(exp(2pi*i*nu)-1)/(2pi*i*(nu-j))]|j>. (1) The removable component at nu=j is one. The vector is the actual orthogonal Fourier projection onto the original physical head; it vanishes at every integer outside 0,...,d and obeys ||v_N(nu)||<=exp(2pi|Im nu|). (2) No physical head is replaced by a different representation or metric. At integer k in 0,...,d, Rhat(k) is the original kth transfer slice. The lower-collar proof establishes its zero at every negative integer -s with 1<=s<N, including scalar poles canceled by invalid-output projection zeros. ## 2. Exact N-shift and the upper base strip Iterating the original first-shift equation gives an additional exact identity of the SAME meromorphic factorial, Fhat(z+N)=(1-exp(2pi*i*z)) Fhat(z). (3) Indeed product_(r=1)^N(1-Q^(z+r))=1-exp(2pi*i*z). This retains the full central factor; it is not replaced by its value at a root. Put z=d+w. Applying (3) to the three affected factorials gives the identity Fhat(b+d+w)F_a/[Fhat(d+w)F_b Fhat(a-d-w)] =[Fhat(b-1+w)/F_b] [F_a/Fhat(a+1-w)] [1-exp(-2pi*i*w)]/Fhat(w-1). (4) The shared factors 1-exp(2pi*i*w) in numerator and denominator have been canceled as meromorphic functions, not evaluated separately at an integer. The remaining central factor in (4) is still explicit. Fix T>0. On the fixed fractional strip 0<=Re w<=1, |Im w|<=T, away from integers by a fixed positive distance, each expression on the right of (4) has modulus bounded by a fixed power of N, uniformly over every a,b in 0,...,d. Only such fractional points are needed on the half-integer vertical and fixed-height horizontal edges below. Here is the endpoint-uniform bound in detail. Set nu=1-w. The basic fixed-argument Gamma product gives polynomial upper and inverse bounds for Fhat(w), Fhat(nu) and Fhat(1-nu). For b>=1, Fhat(b-nu)/F_b =[Fhat(1-nu)/F_1] product_(j=2)^b (1-Q^(j-nu))/(1-Q^j). Every quotient is at most 1+C_T/min(j,N-j), so the product is polynomial by the harmonic sum. For b=0 use Fhat(-nu)=Fhat(1-nu)/(1-Q^(1-nu)); the single denominator is at least c_T/N on the stated fractional edges. Likewise F_a/Fhat(a+nu) =Fhat(nu)^(-1) product_(j=1)^a (1-Q^j)/(1-Q^(j+nu)). For j<=N-2 each quotient is at most 1+C_T/min(j,N-j-1). If j=N-1 occurs, treat it separately: its denominator is at least c_T/N away from the excluded integer w=0, and its numerator is bounded. This adds only a polynomial factor. Finally 1/Fhat(w-1)=(1-Q^w)/Fhat(w) is polynomially bounded, as is 1-exp(-2pi*i*w) at fixed height. These statements prove the uniform polynomial base bound for (4) without hiding a large complete factorial or its inverse. The original Cartan in (1) has bounded modulus at this fixed height, since a,b are physical integers and its prescribed logarithms have bounded imaginary coefficients. ## 3. All newly crossed upper integer poles are removable Take k=N,...,2N-2. The factorial orders, directly from (3) and its nonzero original strip, are: ord Fhat(k)=1, ord Fhat(b+k)=1+1_(b+k>=2N), ord [1/Fhat(a-k)]=1+1_(k-a>=N+1). Thus the scalar r(a,b;z) at z=k has order 1+1_(b+k>=2N)+1_(k-a>=N+1)>=1. (5) Both outputs b+k and a-k are outside the physical band. The two vectors in (1) therefore each supply one further zero. In particular Rhat has a zero of order at least three at every such k, and its complete cotangent density is holomorphic there. Even the scalar coefficient already has a zero on this upper collar; the full physical projection remains part of the operator identity. The only factorial singularities in the collar are at these integer points. There is no unrecorded noninteger pole. Formula (5) includes the physical input endpoints and all their simultaneous collisions. ## 4. Uniform collar estimate and the two-sided contour identity The exact step recurrence is r(z+1)/r(z) =xQ^(-b)(1-Q^(b+z+1))(1-Q^(a-z))/(1-Q^(z+1)). (6) On a half-integer vertical edge or a fixed nonzero-height horizontal edge, each forward step costs at most C_T N: its single denominator is bounded below by c_T/N, and the two numerators are bounded. Starting with the base strip (4), for 1<=s<N/2 this proves ||pi cot(pi z)Rhat(z)|| <=N^(C_T)(C_T N)^(s+1) (7) on the boundary of d+1/2<=Re z<=d+s+1/2, |Im z|<=T. The finite number N^2 of input columns adds only a factor N to the operator bound. Equations (2) and (5), followed by the matrix maximum principle, extend (7) throughout the filled upper collar. The original contour encloses exactly the physical transfers 0,...,d. Extend its left edge to -s-1/2 and its right edge to d+s+1/2, retaining both finite-height connecting pieces. The added integers are -s,...,-1 and N,...,N+s-1. The lower theorem and (5) show that every new pole of the complete density is removable. Consequently, as an ORIGINAL physical operator, R_plus=integral_(extended rectangle) pi cot(pi z)Rhat(z) dz/(2pi*i). (8) Each added collar has length O_T(s+1), and both have the conservative uniform operator cost exp[O_T((s+1)log N)]. (9) For s<=N^alpha, alpha<1, this is exp(o(N)). The negative crossing uses its exact antiunitary mirror Rhat_minus(z)=Flip conjugate(Rhat_plus(conjugate z)) Flip, with the conjugate full Cartan scalar. Its residue identity and both collar bounds follow with the same orientations at the integer residues. Finitely many such identities can be composed inside any fixed signed braid word before its original marked closure is taken. The scale is compatible with the earlier regular descent window. In the normalized transfer variable z/N, a width s=N^(1-epsilon) is a collar of width N^(-epsilon). The regular-region flow cost is exp(O(N^(B epsilon) log^2 N)), while (9) costs exp(O(N^(1-epsilon) log N)). Both are subexponential whenever 0<epsilon<1/B. Thus these two local quantitative estimates do not require incompatible cutoff scales. Compatibility of scales alone does not identify the off-grid Fourier-projected density with the previous scalar phase or estimate its projection-angle currents. The cost in (9) concerns the added operator contours, not the norm of an arbitrary exterior contraction. The original residues 0,...,d, the whole sinc/Fourier source and every framing/pivotal/peripheral line remain. A claimed full-volume bound must still estimate the remaining bulk current with this source retained. An independent proof review verified the exact N-shift normalization in (4), all upper divisor orders in (5), the uniform all-input fractional base bound and the forward-recurrence cost. The expanded [projected audit](../experiments/audit_actual_projected_transfer_cot_completion.py) passed for EVERY physical input a,b at N=2,...,8. It checks the exact N-shift and fractional identity (4) off the integer lattice, the full upper matrix zero orders at N through N+min(3,N-2), and both-collar cotangent residue sums against the ORIGINAL positive and negative E/Cartan crossing matrices. The positive kappa=q^((N-1)^2/2) and its negative inverse are included explicitly. These tests supplement the uniform proof and do not change its full physical-source scope or establish a sharp whole-knot volume estimate.

title: The projected transfer word, its degree repair, and its remaining source seams
text: # The projected transfer word, its degree repair, and its remaining source seams 28 October 2026. The two projected outer-collar theorems are genuine original-operator contour identities. They can be inserted simultaneously in a fixed signed word. A contractive degree average makes the entire off-grid word preserve the original integer degree, without changing its integral or its collar estimates. This does not yet reduce the sharp bound to the known regular critical regulator theorem. The retained physical interpolation still has Fourier interval currents and fails the other crossing Ward equations pointwise. This is a limitation of THIS phase representation, not an impossibility of tame linear projections onto the intertwiner space. ## 1. Exact full word and a cost-free degree average Use Rhat_sigma(z) of [the lower](actual_projected_transfer_cot_completion.md) and [upper](actual_projected_transfer_upper_collar.md) collar theorems. It acts on the ORIGINAL orthonormal two-head space H_N tensor H_N. Every physical input index remains an integer in 0,...,d, d=N-1. The full original Cartan factor kappa is included. Write D|a,b>=(a+b)|a,b> and E_D(A)=sum_T P_T A P_T =integral_0^(2pi) exp(itD) A exp(-itD) dt/(2pi), B_sigma(z)=E_D(Rhat_sigma(z)). (1) This is a completely positive contraction in operator norm and a contraction in Hilbert--Schmidt norm. It is a fixed linear map of the matrix entries, so holomorphy, removable zeros, and the collar bounds survive unchanged. The integer transfer slices are also graded, hence E_D fixes EACH original integer slice in this case. Consequently, for any of the enlarged finite-height rectangles Gamma_i, R_sigma=integral_(Gamma_i) pi cot(pi z) B_sigma(z) dz/(2pi i). For a fixed braid word the SAME original scalar is exactly K_N=chi_(beta,N) integral_(product Gamma_i) Phi_N(B_m(z_m)...B_1(z_1)) product_i [pi cot(pi z_i) dz_i/(2pi i)]. (2) Here B_i is embedded on its actual neighboring heads, all spectators are identities, and Phi_N is the original marked pivotal closure or cup/cap functional. All integrals are compact and all head spaces finite, so their ordered composition and Fubini in (2) are exact. The product is now degree preserving POINTWISE in every transfer z_i. The original marked cap may therefore be restricted to its forced degree-d fiber after the ordinary caps, exactly as for the original whole word. This removes a real potential source error; the degree leak of the unsymmetrized interpolant is not unavoidable. For any fixed number of factors the added individual collars have exp(o(N)) operator cost, uniformly over their physical inputs. This is not an estimate on an unrestricted exterior word, which may itself have an exponential norm or scalar period. ## 2. What the repaired physical kernel actually is Put s_c(nu)=[exp(2pi i nu)-1]/[2pi i(nu-c)], sinc(pi w)=sin(pi w)/(pi w). The removable values are retained. If T=a+b, the positive kernel (1) is B_+(z)|a,b>=r(a,b;z) sum_(c=max(0,T-d))^(min(d,T)) sinc^2(pi(b+z-c)) |c,T-c>. (3) Indeed s_(T-c)(a-z)=exp(-2pi iz)s_c(b+z), and the two phase factors cancel in their product, leaving the ENTIRE square in (3). For complex z it is not the modulus square. For real z its coefficients are nonnegative before multiplying by the original scalar r. The exact Fourier representation is sinc^2(pi w)=integral_(-1)^1 (1-|t|) exp(2pi iwt)dt. (4) Thus (2) retains physical interval data even after repairing degree. Splitting (4) into its two analytic intervals leaves endpoints t=+/-1 and a common interface t=0. The weight vanishes at the outer endpoints only to first order; its derivative has a jump at zero. These are not automatically exponentially negligible. Integrating explicitly gives sinc^2(pi w)=[2-exp(2pi iw)-exp(-2pi iw)]/(4pi^2 w^2), (5) with the complete removable value at w=0. Splitting the numerator without its joint cancellation would introduce a false double pole. At an INTERIOR stationary point of (4) the missing output relation b+z=c is restored. At an interval endpoint or interface it is not an available stationarity equation. Such a restricted critical scheme must not simply be substituted into the previously proved FULL original critical ideal. The existing uniform vector bound exp(2pi|Im nu|) is tame at the FIXED transfer height of the collar theorems. At a macroscopic complex transfer z=N zeta, however, (5) can itself have exponent 2pi N|Im zeta|. This is a leading source phase, not a half-density which may be discarded. For example for w=N xi with Im xi>0 and xi bounded away from zero, sinc^2(pi N xi) =-exp(-2pi iNxi)/(4pi^2N^2xi^2)(1+o(1)). (6) The analogous opposite exponential occurs when Im xi<0. These are the original Fourier endpoint sectors. They may subsequently cancel in the complete source, but the outer-collar estimate does not prove that cancellation or identify their coupled stationary support. ### A quantitative whole-word bound for the COMPLETE projection There is a stronger estimate than bounding the individual sinc entries. It controls the complete interval/interface aggregate, with no N-dependent conditioning. Embed the original finite head space isometrically in L^2([0,2pi],dtheta/(2pi)). If S is the head swap and D_r(z) is diagonal on the ORIGINAL finite input basis with entries r(a,b;z), then literally Rhat_+(z)=P_N^(tensor 2) M_z S D_r(z), (M_z f)(theta1,theta2) =exp(iz(theta1-theta2)) f(theta1,theta2). (6a) The output coefficients of (6a) are exactly the two sinc vectors, so no boundary source has been changed. Multiplication has norm exp(2pi|Im z|), the swap is isometric and P_N is orthogonal. Thus ||B_+(z)||op <= ||Rhat_+(z)||op <=exp(2pi|Im z|) max_(a,b physical)|r(a,b;z)|. (6b) The same holds for the literal negative antiunitary mirror. In particular REAL-transfer projection is contractive: it adds NO N factor and no exponential rate to the scalar diagonal coefficient envelope. This is not an estimate on a new norm or a changed source. There is also an exact sharp absolute-column version. For nu=u+iv, sum_(c in Z) |sinc^2(pi(nu-c))| =sinh(2pi|v|)/(2pi|v|), (6c) with value 1 at v=0. Indeed the original Fourier coefficients satisfy |s_c(nu)|^2=exp(-2pi v)|sinc^2(pi(nu-c))|. Plancherel for exp(i nu theta) gives sum |s_c|^2=(1-exp(-4pi v))/(4pi v), which proves (6c). Restricting to the finite allowed c in (3) only decreases the sum. Thus (3)'s physical output column has l1 norm at most |r| times the right side of (6c). At real transfer the weights form a subprobability distribution. For any original b-head one-cut source, or fixed-width marked plat, its actual functional norm is polynomial in N at complete color. Tensoring the local operators with spectators changes none of (6b). Consequently the COMPLETE interval sources in any fixed word satisfy the genuine bound |Phi_N(B_m(z_m)...B_1(z_1))| <=poly_beta(N) exp(2pi sum_i |Im z_i|) product_i max_(a,b)|r_sigma_i(a,b;z_i)|. (6d) Every original cup/cap normalization and the explicit external chi in (2) is retained. This is a quantitative full-source statement, not a claim that separately cut Fourier sectors obey the same bound. On fixed-height cotangent contours, the projection cost in (6d) is O_T(1)^m. Their lengths, cotangent bounds and fixed word length add only polynomial factors. Thus the endpoint/interface aggregate does not create a new exponential envelope ON THOSE CONTOURS. Conversely the macroscopic complex cost in (6b) cannot be replaced by a uniform polynomial for this same scalar interpolation. If z=N zeta, Im zeta!=0, and Re(b+z) lies in the physical output band, choose an allowed c with |b+Re z-c|<=1. Formula (3) then has an individual output coefficient of size |r(a,b;z)| exp(2pi N|Im zeta|)/poly(N), (6e) provided its total-degree block contains that c. For example a+b=d contains every physical c. The denominator in (5) is O(N^2), while its numerator has the stated exponential size. Hence the rate 2pi|Im zeta| is sharp already for the retained physical kernel. This does not prove it survives the exterior knot pairing; it proves that such a cancellation must be retained in a sharp complex-contour argument rather than absorbed into a polynomial projection norm. ## 3. An exact remaining E-coproduct defect Use the original complete scaled currents Ecal|a>=(Q^-a-1)|a-1>, K|a>=x Q^-a|a>, E=Ecal tensor K + I tensor Ecal, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=-q^-1. The original complete R commutes with E. Its repaired interpolation B_+(z) does not. An exact entry at z=1/2 is <0,0|[E,B_+(1/2)]|1,0> =(Q^-1-1) r(0,0;1/2) (4/pi^2) (1-Q+q^-1). (7) To check it, the two degree-one output weights in (3) are both 4/pi^2, while r(1,0;z)/r(0,0;z) =x^-1 (1-Q)/(1-Q^(1-z)). At z=1/2 this gives (7) directly. It is nonzero at EVERY N>=2: r(0,0;1/2)=kappa x^(1/2)/Fhat(-1/2) is nonzero, and 1-Q+q^-1=0 would imply q^3=q+1. The latter is impossible since |q+1|>=sqrt(2)>1. Therefore degree repair alone does not turn the pointwise five-function density into the complete crossing Ward solution. This defect is visible to an ORIGINAL source. At N=2 use precisely the balanced cup and FULL marked row p_(a,b)=2 x^(a-1) delta_(a+b,1), m_(a,b)=x^b/4, x=i. A direct four-state calculation gives m [E,B_+(1/2)] p =(-16-52i)/(9pi^2 Fhat(-1/2)) != 0. (8) All original kappa and x phases are included in this formula. A marked-fiber replacement must not be applied AFTER the degree-lowering insertion E; (8) uses the full marked row. In contrast, the complete cotangent integral of this commutator is [E,R]=0. Its compensating source currents are therefore essential to any argument based on pointwise Ward equations. This is not a new nonzero knot invariant with an arbitrarily inserted coupon; it tests the proposed density identity before the exact integral is assembled. ## 4. Tame projections exist; they do not supply a free phase theorem No impossibility of a further tame algebraic repair follows from (7). For example the Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal projection onto the common E,F,K intertwiner space always exists, has HS norm one, and has operator-to-operator norm at most N on a two-head space of dimension N^2. It preserves the complete R integral and every added zero. It need not preserve the separate original transfer residues. More importantly E,F,K intertwiners need not implement the specified braid crossing: they also include other functions of the two-head Casimir. Their phases and canonical relations have to be derived afresh. The same warning applies to the full Hurwitz intertwiner line. If the complete physical algebra makes that solution space span{R}, its HS projection is exactly P_R(A)=<R,A>_HS R / ||R||_HS^2. (9) It is still tame as a linear operator. At an integer transfer k the scalar coefficient is lambda_k=||R_k||_HS^2/||R||_HS^2, sum_k lambda_k=1, because the original transfer slices have disjoint matrix-entry supports. But the entire known exponential crossing matrix R is now a CONSTANT factor in the density P_R(Rhat(z))=lambda_N(z)R. The original word asymptotic is not obtained by analyzing the harmless scalar lambda alone. Such a projection changes the phase representation and packages its difficulty into the retained R factor; it does not contradict (7) or provide the requested sharp geometric bound. ## 5. Critical-path conclusion The theorem removes both artificial OUTER transfer collars, with the physical projections and source retained. Formula (2) is an exact full-word representation, and (1) repairs its pointwise degree at no norm cost. This is substantive source control. What is not yet proved is a bulk-only estimate with exponential rate at most the knot volume. The regular critical-regulator theorem applies to the genuine full crossing/gluing equations. To use it here one must either control the complete Fourier interval currents in (4)--(6), show their coupled stationary support belongs to that actual saturated graph, or give a different phase-preserving source transport. Keeping the finite physical head sums avoids these new complex-head seams, but then the remaining positive matrix bound still loses the global outer phase and is not sharp by knot volume. These alternatives are not supplied by the two local collar estimates alone. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_projected_transfer_word_source.py): exact degree-averaged columns and contraction, original R and E Ward, the all-level entry (7), the full original source (8), the retained triangle Fourier identity, and the exact full-intertwiner projection weights. No sharp bound for a knot family is inferred.

title: Exact auxiliary colors of the pure Conway leaf
text: # Exact auxiliary colors of the pure Conway leaf 29 October 2026. The literal turned crossing circle has an exact positive core and a disjoint, signed alias at every ordinary auxiliary color. Every alias coefficient is at most N/2 in absolute value, uniformly in the color and at both parities. The complete-circle core also simplifies to one positive factorial ratio. These are identities in the FULL pair Casimir algebra, so they retain its projective normal directions. The leaf here is `h_j=Rturn(L_j)`, the one used in the [positive complete-circle Conway grammar](actual_positive_complete_circle_conway_trees.md). It has no extra half-twist. The older belt leaf `Rturn(R^-1 L_j)` has a different alias and is not covered by this bound. This local theorem alone does not prove a global mixed-color gap or a long-filling theorem. ## 1. Literal source and notation Set \[ q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad D=N-1,\quad M=\lfloor D/2\rfloor, \quad \theta=\pi/N,\quad s_r=\prod_{u=1}^r2\sin(u\theta),\quad s_0=1. \] Write \(\mathsf T_n(z)=2T_n(z/2)\), so \(\mathsf T_0=2,\mathsf T_1=z\), and put \[ H_N=\mathbb C[z]/(\mathsf T_N(z)+2),\qquad c_k=q^{2k+1}+q^{-2k-1},\qquad B_r(z)=\prod_{k=0}^{r-1}(c_k-z),\qquad \widehat B_r=B_r/s_r^2. \tag{1} \] The [original crossing-circle calculation](actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md) gives, for the actual auxiliary module of dimension j and its original pivot, with no extra factor 1/j, \[ L_j=(-1)^{j-1}U_{j-1}(z/2),\quad 1\le j\le N, \qquad h_j=R_{\rm turn}L_j. \tag{2} \] The [actual turn and marked closure](actual_positive_newton_multiplication.md) satisfy \[ R_{\rm turn}\widehat B_r=\widehat B_{D-r},\qquad \phi(\widehat B_i\widehat B_j)=\delta_{i+j,D},\qquad \phi(L_Nf)=N\sum_{k=0}^{D}f(c_k). \tag{3} \] The sum counts each of the N listed roots, including repetitions. These equations hold in the repeated-root algebra (1), not just its quotient consisting of values at the distinct nodes. In particular the \(\widehat B_v\) coefficient of \(R_{\rm turn}f\) is \(\phi(f\widehat B_v)\). ## 2. A generic Chebyshev--Newton identity With q initially generic and \({a\brack b}_q\) the symmetric quantum binomial, one has the polynomial identity \[ U_{j-1}(z/2)=\sum_{r=0}^{j-1}(-1)^r {j+r\brack 2r+1}_q B_r(z). \tag{4} \] Here is a direct derivation. For a formal variable t, successive division of \(1-zt+t^2=(1-c_rt+t^2)+t(c_r-z)\) gives \[ \frac1{1-zt+t^2} =\sum_{r\ge0}\frac{(-t)^rB_r(z)} {\prod_{i=0}^{r}(1-c_it+t^2)}. \tag{5} \] The remainder after r stages is divisible by \(t^{r+1}\), which justifies the formal identity. The denominator in its rth term is \[ \prod_{a=0}^{2r+1}(1-q^{-(2r+1)+2a}t). \] Its reciprocal has coefficient of \(t^n\) equal to \(q^{-(2r+1)n}{n+2r+1\brack 2r+1}_{q^2}\), where the binomial on the right is the ordinary Gaussian one. This formula follows by induction on the number of factors using the finite geometric series and the Gaussian Pascal recurrence. Converting to the symmetric binomial cancels the displayed q power. Taking \(n=j-r-1\) proves (4), since the left side of (5) generates the Chebyshev polynomials. For \(1\le j\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), all factorial arguments in (4) are less than N. Specialization therefore gives, without any zero-over-zero division, \[ \boxed{\quad h_j= \sum_{r=0}^{j-1}(-1)^{j-1+r}b_{j,r}\widehat B_{D-r},\qquad b_{j,r}=\frac{s_r^2s_{j+r}}{s_{2r+1}s_{j-r-1}}>0.\quad} \tag{6} \] This is an equality of full polynomials of degree below N after the actual turn, so it includes every repeated-node derivative. For larger j one must retain the Laurent-polynomial binomial in (4), rather than substitute a factorial quotient containing zeros. The next identity avoids all such zero quotients. ## 3. Positive core plus the actual low-color alias For \(0\le h\le M\), define \(L_0=h_0=0\). Then exactly \[ \boxed{\quad h_{N-h}=\sum_{v=h}^{M}A_{N,v}(h)\widehat B_v+(-1)^Nh_h, \qquad A_{N,v}(h)=\frac{N^2s_{2v}} {s_v^2s_{v-h}s_{v+h}}>0.\quad} \tag{7} \] The first sum is the core. If h>0, (6) puts the entire alias in indices \(v\ge N-h\); these are disjoint from the core indices \(h\le v\le M\). At h=0 the alias is zero. In particular the complete-circle coefficients are simply \[ h_N=\sum_{v=0}^{M}a_{N,v}\widehat B_v,\qquad a_{N,v}=\frac{N^2s_{2v}}{s_v^4}. \tag{8} \] To prove (7), first use the elementary Chebyshev identity \[ U_{N-h-1}=\tfrac12(\mathsf T_hU_{N-1} -\mathsf T_NU_{h-1}). \] It follows either by multiplying sines and cosines at \(z=2\cos t\), then extending as a polynomial identity, or directly from the Chebyshev recurrence. In the full algebra (1) it becomes \[ L_{N-h}=(-1)^h\frac{\mathsf T_h}{2}L_N+(-1)^NL_h. \tag{9} \] No passage to root values was made in (9). To compute the turn of its first term, it is now legitimate to use the special trace identity (3). Its coefficient at v is \[ (-1)^hN\sum_{k=0}^{D}\cos(h(2k+1)\theta) \widehat B_v(c_k). \tag{10} \] For v>M, \(B_v\) vanishes at all the nodes c_k, so (10) is zero. For v<=M, a finite Laurent expansion gives \[ B_v(w+w^{-1})= \sum_{u=-v}^{v}(-1)^u \frac{[2v]_q!}{[v+u]_q![v-u]_q!}\,w^u. \tag{11} \] For example this follows from \[ B_v(w+w^{-1}) =q^{-v^2}(qw;q^2)_v(q/w;q^2)_v =(-1)^vw^{-v}(q^{1-2v}w;q^2)_{2v}, \] and the finite binomial expansion; its q powers cancel on conversion to symmetric binomials. Evaluating at \(w=q^{2k+1}\), the Fourier average in (10) selects u=+h and u=-h. There are no other Fourier aliases because \(v+h\le2M<N\). The two equal terms cancel the factor 1/2 in the cosine; at h=0 there is just its constant term. This is exactly (7). Moreover the core is pointwise dominated by the complete core: \[ 0<A_{N,v}(h)\le a_{N,v}\quad(0\le h\le v\le M). \tag{12} \] Indeed the ratio \(a_{N,v}/A_{N,v}(h)\) is \(s_{v-h}s_{v+h}/s_v^2\). Its successive ratio as h increases is \[ \frac{\sin((v+h)\theta)}{\sin((v-h+1)\theta)}\ge1, \] since the two arguments sum to \((2v+1)\theta\le\pi\). For h>0 this is strict except at the odd-level endpoint \(v=(N-1)/2\), where equality holds for every allowed h. ## 4. An exact uniform N/2 bound for every alias coefficient For all N>=2, \(1\le j\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), and \(0\le r<j\), \[ \boxed{\qquad 0<b_{j,r}\le N/2,\qquad \sum_{r=0}^{j-1}b_{j,r}\le jN/2\le N^2/4.\qquad} \tag{13} \] The stronger final N^2/4 follows from j<=N/2. The proof uses the actual sine product, not its limiting action. Rewrite (6) as \[ b_{j,r}=\frac{s_r^2}{s_{2r+1}} \prod_{u=-r}^{r}2\sin((j+u)\theta). \tag{14} \] For fixed r this positive product, regarded as a function of real j on \(r<j<N-r\), is symmetric about N/2 and log concave: each summand \(\log\sin((j+u)\theta)\) has strictly negative second derivative. Hence its maximum occurs at j=N/2. The value of (14) there is \[ B_r=2\, \frac{\prod_{u=1}^{r}2\sin(2u\theta)} {\prod_{u=0}^{r}2\sin((2u+1)\theta)}. \tag{15} \] Here one cancels \((2\sin u\theta)(2\cos u\theta) =2\sin2u\theta\). The ratio \[ \frac{B_{r+1}}{B_r} =\frac{\sin((2r+2)\theta)}{\sin((2r+3)\theta)} \] is <=1 and then >=1, with at most one change: the comparison changes at \((4r+5)\theta=\pi\). Thus the maximum over \(0\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor-1\) occurs at an endpoint. At r=0 it is \(\csc\theta\). If N=2m, the other endpoint is \(B_{m-1}=m\), because the even sine product in (15) is m and the odd product is 2. These product evaluations follow directly by factoring \(t^m-1\) and \(t^m+1\) at t=1. If N=2m+1, reflection \(\sin(k\theta)=\sin((N-k)\theta)\) cancels the even factors against the odd factors other than the first, and gives \(B_{m-1}=\csc\theta\). Finally \(\sin(\pi/N)\ge2/N\), proving (13). Consequently the alias in (7) has a uniform polynomial coefficient norm, even when its physical color h grows proportionally to N. This is not a positive-source assertion: its coefficients genuinely alternate. For odd N and h=1 the alias is \(-\widehat B_D\). For even N>=4 and h=2, it has coefficient \(-c_0\) at \(\widehat B_D\). These signs cannot be dropped in the original mixed-color source. ## 5. Its real action and a marked local complex interpolation Let \(J(x)=\int_0^x\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt\). Uniformly at all integer arguments between 0 and N-1, the elementary endpoint-aware sum estimate is \(\log s_r=NJ(r/N)+O(\log N)\). For a direct proof, subtract \(\log t+\log(1-t)\) from the integrand. The remainder extends smoothly to [0,1] and has an O(1) Riemann-sum error. The two subtracted logarithms give ordinary factorial ratios, whose sum-minus-integral errors are O(log N) uniformly, including r=0 and r=N-1. Writing \(x=v/N\) and \(\chi=h/N\), (7) therefore has rate \[ \log A_{N,v}(h)=Ng_\chi(x)+O(\log N),\qquad g_\chi(x)=J(2x)-2J(x)-J(x-\chi)-J(x+\chi), \tag{16} \] uniformly over \(0\le h\le v\le M\). On the interior \(0<\chi<x<1/2\), \[ \partial_\chi g_\chi(x) =\log\frac{\sin\pi(x-\chi)}{\sin\pi(x+\chi)}<0, \qquad \left.\partial_\chi^2g_\chi(x)\right|_{\chi=0} =-2\pi\cot(\pi x)<0. \tag{17} \] The loss is uniform on compact interior sets with chi bounded away from zero. At x=1/2 the continuum loss vanishes, consistently with the exact odd-level endpoint equality in (12); an arbitrary global color gap cannot be inferred without controlling endpoint sources. There is also a fixed, even, holomorphic continuation of this actual core coefficient, without assigning a formal Newton index the role of a peripheral holonomy. Let G_N be the sine-factorial interpolation proved in [the exact interpolation note](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md), with \(G_N(r)=s_r\), and define \[ \mathcal A_N(x,\chi)= \frac{N^2G_N(2Nx)}{G_N(Nx)^2G_N(N(x-\chi))G_N(N(x+\chi))}. \tag{18} \] It is holomorphic and nonzero wherever the four scaled arguments lie in the interpolation's strip, and it agrees EXACTLY with (7) at its lattice arguments. On any fixed compact complex corridor where 2x, x, x-chi and x+chi have real parts strictly between 0 and 1, the proved uniform factorial expansion gives \[ \mathcal A_N(x,\chi) =N^{1/2}\, \frac{\sqrt{\sin(2\pi x)}} {2^{3/2}\sin(\pi x) \sqrt{\sin\pi(x-\chi)\sin\pi(x+\chi)}} e^{Ng_\chi(x)}(1+O(N^{-1})). \tag{19} \] All logarithms and square roots are continued from the positive real corridor. The error and every fixed derivative are uniform on a smaller corridor. Thus the local coefficient is an even analytic function of the ACTUAL auxiliary-color deficit chi, with the exact finite values and their marks fixed. This does not assert that the whole finite source already has a single analytic saddle packet: its original support, alias pieces, boundary contributions and contour still require their separate estimates. ## 6. Consequence for arbitrary fixed Conway circuits, and scope There is a useful intrinsic description of the alias subspace: \[ \mathfrak n_N=\operatorname{span}\{\widehat B_v: v\ge\lceil N/2\rceil\} =\operatorname{Nil}(H_N),\qquad \mathfrak n_N^2=0. \tag{20} \] Indeed \(B_{\lceil N/2\rceil}\) contains every distinct factor of \(\mathsf T_N+2\) once, including its simple factor at odd N. The subspace on the left is therefore the kernel of evaluation at all distinct nodes. Every remaining root has multiplicity two, so this is precisely the square-zero nilradical. Equivalently the exact Newton multiplication vanishes when its two input indices sum to at least N. Formula (6) is triangular with nonzero last coefficient \(b_{j,j-1}=s_{j-1}^2\), so \[ h_1,\ldots,h_{\lfloor N/2\rfloor} \quad\hbox{are a basis of }\mathfrak n_N. \tag{21} \] Thus the signed alias is exactly part of the source's radical data. In a product of any number of mixed pure leaves, terms with two aliases vanish identically. In particular each robust three-leaf seed contains at most one alias term in its exact expansion. The actual turn reverses the Newton indices and does NOT preserve this nilradical; it cannot be quotiented out of a Conway circuit. Each ordinary circle color in an arbitrary fixed robust Conway expression can now be replaced exactly by (6) or (7), followed by the existing full Newton multiplication and actual coordinate reversal for every turn. This gives a finite, source-preserving signed circuit with polynomial alias leaf coefficients and positive core coefficients bounded by the corresponding complete ones. All original colors, marked cuts, pivots and normal directions are retained. It is an exact deformation through ordinary AUXILIARY COLORS; it is not yet a deformation in a separately identified geometric meridian or longitude. Polynomial leaf aliases can acquire exponential growth when multiplied by other circuit factors. Consequently (13) alone is not a proof of an exponentially negligible whole alias sector. That global source comparison, the complex whole-source saddle, and the geometric peripheral interpretation are the additional steps needed before invoking a long-filling transfer theorem. Audit: [generic polynomial identities, all root coefficients and literal physical turns](../experiments/audit_actual_pure_conway_auxiliary_color_leaf.py). The principal-root inequalities are proved above; finite-field calculations are used only to verify exact identities. Independent internal analytical review by the coherent-current agent checked the generic generating-series identity, full-algebra Chebyshev split, finite Fourier coefficients, exact N/2 bound, marked complex prefactor and nilradical basis. A fresh replay passed 36 generic identities, 2,079 full root polynomials, 54 actual turns, 14 literal mixed crossing loops, 143,450 alias inequalities and 146,299 core-domination inequalities. The root agent also completed an independent analytical review of the local proof.

title: Finite local curvature of the original boundary models
status: Finite local curvature through both folds
text: # Finite local curvature of the original boundary models 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. The actual 220/222 determinants and the actual 202 positive polynomial have logarithmic curvature bounded above and below by constant multiples of N, uniformly through the fold. The other retained factors have nonlinear derivatives of size O(s+1), where s is the channel deficit. These are finite local source statements. No graph-rank, stationary-point, Gaussian reduction or original-period assertion is made. ## 1. Actual clocks and the finite core factors Put N>=3, d=N-1, theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), Q=q^2. Keep an ACTUAL integer channel a with a0 N<=a<=floor(d/2), a0>0, m=d-a, s=d-2a. All estimates are for sufficiently large N, including either maximal folded parity. Coefficients below range in fixed positive compact sets. Use the exact physical half-index clocks U=q^-1 X, V=q^-1 Y, QUV=XY. (1) The half-index is not dropped, and a is not replaced by a limiting continuous color. The actual source determinant is H_a^1(U,V)=V^a K_a det[I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+], K_a=[2a choose a]_Q. (2) The a-by-a Hermitian positive matrices H_-,H_+ have diagonal d_n=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], 0<=n<a, and upper adjacent entries h_n^+/-=sqrt(b_n)[sin(n theta)+/-i cos(n theta)], b_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)], 1<=n<a. We take H_+ to have the plus upper entry and H_- the minus entry, as in the [source determinant](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md). These are the original finite coefficients, including the fold endpoint. For negative raw clocks X,Y set alpha=-X/2>0, beta=-1/(2Y)>0, M=I+alpha H_-+beta H_+. The finite nonlinear core factors of the six models are: * 220: det(I+alpha H_-), depending on the first raw log clock; * 022: det(I+beta H_-), after the literal reversed reciprocity, depending on the second raw log clock with opposite sign; * 222: det M, retaining BOTH actual finite clocks; * 202: P_a(w)=sum_(k=0)^a beta_(a,k)^2 w^k, w=QUV=XY>0, beta_(a,k)=S_a/(S_k S_(a-k)), S_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(r theta); * 200 and 002: no order-N nonlinear core is extracted here. Every source scalar, affine phase, monomial and large-partner product remains in the finite models of the [correlated-band theorem](actual_correlated_boundary_band_ratio.md). The word "core" separates a derivative calculation, not a change to the source. Positivity below refers to real LOGARITHMIC RADII. A change of normalized magnetic head nu changes its clock by exp(2pi i nu), so pullback to those heads retains the factors 2pi i and the literal incidence signs. No positivity in real magnetic-angle directions is asserted. ## 2. An exact noncommutative determinant Hessian Write Xmat=alpha H_-, Ymat=beta H_+, and A=M^-1/2 Xmat M^-1/2, B=M^-1/2 Ymat M^-1/2. For real u,v let D differentiate alpha->alpha exp(tu), beta->beta exp(tv). The finite matrix differentiation identity gives D^2 log det M =Tr[u^2 A+v^2 B-(uA+vB)^2] =u^2 Tr(Xmat M^-2)+v^2 Tr(Ymat M^-2) +(u-v)^2 Tr(AB). (3) Indeed A+B=I-M^-1. Substitute this in Tr(A-A^2) and Tr(B-B^2) and use cyclicity of trace. No commutativity of H_- and H_+ is assumed. Each term on the last line is nonnegative: for example Tr(AB)=Tr(A^1/2 B A^1/2)>=0. Since A,B are positive and A+B<I, the first line also gives D^2 log det M<=a(u^2+v^2). (4) For actual raw log-clock directions (u,v), equation (1) instead changes alpha by exp(tu) and beta by exp(-tv). Thus the last square in (3) is (u+v)^2, while the first two squares are unchanged. This sign is part of the original second-clock normalization. The one-variable beta=0 specialization of (3) is (alpha partial_alpha)^2 log det(I+alpha H_-) =Tr[alpha H_-(I+alpha H_-)^-2]. (5) ## 3. A finite bulk argument gives the lower bound through the fold The actual Cholesky pivots are p_(n-1)=sin(n theta)/[cos(n theta)sin((2n-1)theta)], 1<=n<=a. Consequently, for h_n the upper entry of either H matrix, z*Hz=sum_(n=1)^(a-1) p_(n-1) |z_(n-1)+(h_n/p_(n-1))z_n|^2 +p_(a-1)|z_(a-1)|^2. (6) This is the original square decomposition; it follows by multiplying its factors and the displayed finite trigonometric pivot identity. Only ACTUAL rows appear. No virtual endpoint or singular extension beyond the maximal folded matrix is used. Select every other adjacent square whose two indices lie in a fixed bulk interval, for example a0 N/4<=n<=a0 N/2. Their supports are disjoint, and their number is at least cN. The pivots, h_n, row norms and reciprocal row norms are bounded on this interval independently of N and a. If w_j are the normalized column vectors of those squares, they are orthonormal, and (6) gives Xmat>=c P, P=sum_j w_j w_j*, rank P>=cN. (7) On the support of each w_j all entries of M are uniformly bounded, since it is wholly inside that same bulk interval. Thus <w_j,Mw_j><=C. For the spectral probability measure of M at w_j, convexity of lambda->lambda^-2 gives <w_j,M^-2 w_j>>=<w_j,Mw_j>^-2>=C^-2. Taking the trace of (7) against the positive M^-2 proves Tr(Xmat M^-2)>=cN. (8) Apply the same argument separately to the squares of H_+ to prove Tr(Ymat M^-2)>=cN. Their selected projections need not coincide. The uniform lower and upper compact bounds on alpha,beta are used here. Together with (3),(4), this proves cN(u^2+v^2)<=D^2 log det M<=CN(u^2+v^2). (9) The same proof with beta=0 and (5) proves cN<=log-radius curvature of the 220 core<=CN. Exact reciprocity gives the 022 statement with its recorded inverse clock. These estimates require a/N bounded below, but no upper gap from the fold. Large final entries do not affect the selected bounded bulk squares or their expectations. ## 4. Exact 202 curvature is a uniformly nondegenerate variance For positive w define the probability weights pi_k=beta_(a,k)^2 w^k/P_a(w), 0<=k<=a. Direct differentiation, with all finite coefficients retained, gives (w partial_w)^2 log P_a(w)=Var_pi(k). (10) Here is a uniform two-sided estimate without differentiating a limiting Laplace formula. The EXACT consecutive weight ratio is R(k)=w[sin((a-k)theta)/sin((k+1)theta)]^2. Extend its logarithm to real 0<=x<=a-1. It satisfies (log R)'(x) =-2theta sin((a+1)theta) /[sin((a-x)theta)sin((x+1)theta)]. (11) Since a0 N<=a<=floor(d/2), this is at most -c/N throughout its interval. For w in a fixed positive compact the crossing of R through one is a distance cN from both ends: for x<=cN the numerator sine is bounded below while the denominator is at most Cc, and the reverse holds for x>=a-cN.
