Choose c small using the two bounds on w. Thus any modal integer k_* lies in [cN,a-cN]. On a fixed smaller bulk neighborhood of k_*, (11) has absolute value at most C/N. The adjacent modal logarithmic ratios are consequently O(1/N). Multiplying the exact ratios away from k_* now yields, for every k, weight(k)/weight(k_*)<=C exp[-c(k-k_*)^2/N]. (12) The bulk upper bound on the ratio drops also gives a fixed positive lower bound for that ratio whenever |k-k_*|<=2sqrt(N), for large N. It follows by summing (12) and those central terms that c sqrt(N) weight(k_*)<=P_a(w)<=C sqrt(N) weight(k_*). The upper Gaussian bound gives E[(k-k_*)^2]<=CN, hence Var(k)<=CN. Each of the two integer shells k_*-2sqrt(N)<=k<=k_*-sqrt(N) and k_*+sqrt(N)<=k<=k_*+2sqrt(N) has probability at least c>0. For independent samples K,K', the identity Var(K)=E[(K-K')^2]/2 therefore gives Var(K)>=cN. This proves cN<=(w partial_w)^2 log P_a(w)<=CN. (13) In the actual two raw log-clock directions this is the quadratic form Var(k)(u+v)^2, because w=QUV=XY EXACTLY. The affine phase (-1)^a Q^[a(a-1)/2] contributes no curvature. ## 5. Fixed holomorphic logarithmic derivatives are O(N) The preceding finite bounds have uniform complex neighborhoods. For a positive reference M and complex z_1,z_2 near zero, M(z)=I+exp(z_1)Xmat+exp(z_2)Ymat. Conjugating its increment by M^-1/2 gives (exp(z_1)-1)A+(exp(z_2)-1)B, whose norm is less than one half on a fixed polydisc, because A,B are positive with A+B<I. The matrix logarithm series is therefore convergent and |Log(det M(z)/det M)|<=C a. Cauchy's formula on a smaller fixed polydisc proves that every fixed positive-order logarithmic derivative is O(N), including mixed derivatives and both maximal-fold parities. The same proof covers 220 by setting Ymat=0. The normalization of the logarithm is relative to its positive reference determinant; no absolute O(N) bound on unrelated scalar logs is needed. For 202 the proved original negative-root theorem factors P_a(w)=C_a product_j(w+rho_j), rho_j>0. For w in a positive compact and small complex z, every factor w exp(z)+rho_j stays a fixed relative distance from zero. Its marked logarithmic ratio is O(1) uniformly in rho_j; summing over a factors and using Cauchy gives the same O(N) bound for every fixed positive-order derivative. In particular, changing the logarithmic base clocks by O(N^-1) changes each core Hessian by O(1), by the third-derivative bound and integration along that short path. This controls the ACTUAL finite-r clock correction to the real signed limiting clocks. It does not discard the order-one transport term in the determinant or its source phase. ## 6. The retained noncore factors have O(s+1) nonlinear cost Use the EXACT finite models from the correlated-band theorem on its fixed complex clock polydisc. Let z_1,z_2 denote logarithmic clock variations; marked heads are pulled back by their actual affine lifts. All statements below concern fixed derivatives of total order at least two. A function linear in these logarithms has zero such derivatives, even when its value or first derivative is large. The root cup identity is exactly p_(d-s)(x)=F_s exp(pi i x) q^[(s-1)x] /product_(j=1)^s(1-Q^(x+j)). (14) Its character is retained. At finite auxiliary clocks every denominator is uniformly separated from zero, so each logarithmic derivative of order at least two costs O(s). At an escaping clock of size N^2 or N^-2, first factor its full linear monomial if necessary; the remaining derivatives cost O(s/N^2). Physical cups have s=0 and are EXACT linear characters, as are their inverse caps. Literal dual reversals and their Chevalley scalar are affine substitutions with their recorded signs. For 202/222 the retained partner product P_s(T)=product_(r=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^r) has fixed logarithmic derivatives O(s): its positive total neighborhood is separated from the forced arc. For 220/022 its total has size N^2 or N^-2; after retaining the exact leading linear monomial its nonlinear derivatives cost O(s/N^2). These statements hold uniformly in a sufficiently small near-fold neighborhood s<=eta N, including both folded parities. The 200 model retains (-1)^m Q^{m(m+1)/2}(UV)^m product_(r<m)(1-Q^r/U) times its zero-free Bessel factor. The monomial has zero nonlinear derivatives. The product contributes O(m/N^2)=O(N^-1), and the Bessel logarithm contributes O(1) on its fixed zero-free complex compact. For 002, extract the exact constant product of -Q^r from product_(r<m)(V-Q^r); its remaining product has the same O(N^-1) cost, and its Bessel factor has O(1) cost. No Bessel factor or phase is discarded. The 022 reciprocity prefactor is also exactly linear in the logarithmic heads. All other original white monomials, half-twist channel weights, fixed root gamma/h0 factors and physical pivotal characters are affine in the varying logarithmic heads, or independent of them. Their actual values and first derivatives remain part of the source; this theorem does not assert that they satisfy a stationary equation. An exposed coherent binomial row, including its actual first-head normalization, is not one of these local tensor factors. Its separate nonlinear action and curvature are not removed by this decomposition. Consequently, for one actual local boundary model, its logarithm decomposes locally as an AFFINE retained source term, the applicable core from section 1, and a remainder whose every fixed nonlinear logarithmic derivative is O(s+1). For any fixed collection of these local factors with the literal bounded affine head substitutions, the correction is O(S+1), S=sum deficits. This is just a derivative bound on a finite product; it asserts no rank of that affine substitution. Finally the actual root numerator/model ratio has a holomorphic O(N^-1) remainder on this same fixed normalized-head neighborhood. The logarithm and all its fixed derivatives are O(N^-1) on a smaller polydisc. Thus it adds only that error to the local curvature estimates. Generic quantum normals are a separate calculation and are not obtained by differentiating this ROOT identity. These facts identify the finite local sources of order-N curvature and bound their retained corrections. They do not prove a transverse rank, stationarity of the complete geometric sample for the actual labels, a nonzero Gaussian coefficient, or an original relative-cycle pairing. Focused audit: [finite source curvature and corrections](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_boundary_model_curvature_results.json). An exact noncommuting matrix identity, two finite trigonometric identities and two original half-index identities check the algebraic interfaces. The audit reconstructs 888 original Cholesky rows and checks 63 finite matrix Hessians, 153 bulk Jensen vectors and 126 complex preconditioned neighborhoods through both folded parities. It checks 80 original positive weight families, 3580 exact sine ratios, 32 separated shell masses and 16 phase-normalized polynomial derivatives. At 85 digits it also compares 30 derivatives of the ORIGINAL finite H sum and 30 derivatives of its literal leading-V coefficient with the determinant derivatives, with maximum error below 1.4e-84. Finally it checks 72 determinant logarithmic derivatives, 144 nonlinear corrections from all six models and 72 interior/escaping cup corrections. Sample lower bounds and rates are diagnostics; the uniform assertions are proved above. Independent full analytical source/geometry review: PASS. The reviewer checked the noncommutative Hessian and inverse second-clock sign, actual Cholesky squares and Jensen lower bound at both folds, exact variance ratios and two-shell normalization, uniform complex logarithmic derivative neighborhoods, and every retained cup, forced-product and Bessel correction. The O(S+1) statement is explicitly about nonlinear derivatives; source values and first derivatives remain. No rank or stationary-point assertion is included in this review. Independent primary full analytical review and fresh redirected audit: PASS. The primary reader checked the finite Hessian identity, original bulk-square/Jensen argument, 202 variance proof, uniform complex derivative bounds and retained O(s+1) corrections. The fresh replay reproduced the reported matrix, weight, correction and original-H/leading-coefficient derivative checks, including both folded parities. This validates the finite local theorem only; the rank and stationarity questions remain separate.

title: Actual complementary heads and the outgoing large-clock packet
status: Exact generic complemented heads and the outgoing boundary determinant
text: # Actual complementary heads and the outgoing large-clock packet 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. Two exact source identities extend the proved boundary packets. Generic Chevalley complementation transports the retained 0F1 normals to the small second-clock regime. A separate positive-matrix comparison controls the outgoing large-second-clock numerator at the root, through the fold. The original scalar factors and large partner remain explicit. This does not yet assemble every cup factor or select a global period. ## 1. An exact generic reciprocity, before any root collision Let H=H_m^B(U,V) be the actual generic white polynomial, and put A0=Q^d=(BQ)^(-1), d=N-1 fixed. Then H(A0/V,A0/U)=A0^m(UV)^(-m)H(U,V). (1) Here U=Q^x,V=Q^y use their marked logarithms, and the complementary heads are EXACTLY d-y,d-x. In particular d does not move with the quantum period, and (1) may be genuinely differentiated. There is a direct independent-variable proof from the actual [white Ward equations](actual_augmented_plat_framing_density_source_ward.md). Set Htilde=(UV/A0)^m H(A0/V,A0/U). It is polynomial of degree at most m in each variable. Substituting X=A0/V,Y=A0/U shows that the E equation for H becomes the F equation for Htilde, and the F equation becomes its E equation, with the original coefficients. For example multiply the E equation at X,Y by UV/A0^2; it reads U(1-V)H(QX,Y)+(1-U)H(X,QY)=(Q^m-UV)H(X,Y), which is precisely the transformed F equation. These two equations determine the polynomial up to one scalar. To see this without a finite-grid continuation assumption, expand in the Newton basis P_b(U)=product_(r<b)(U-Q^r). After removing the first b basis terms, evaluate the F equation at U=Q^b. The coefficient h_b(V) must satisfy Q^b(1-V)h_b(V/Q)=(1-VQ^(b-m))h_b(V). Among polynomials of degree at most m its solutions are exactly the multiples of V^b P_(m-b)(V), as follows by coefficient comparison, starting at its lowest power. Induction gives the actual Newton basis used in the source. The E equation then fixes its adjacent coefficients by the original generic ratio. This is a rational-function proof for generic Q,B; specialization follows after clearing denominators. Finally H(0,0)=(-1)^m Q^[m(m-1)/2]. The coefficient of U^mV^m in Htilde is A0^(-m)H(0,0)=(-B)^m Q^[m(m+1)/2], exactly the top coefficient of H. This proves (1) with scalar ONE, and in particular retains the actual Chevalley normalization. ## 2. The genuine small-second-clock packet Suppose at the root U_N is in a fixed compact subset of C*, V_N=N^(-2)v_N with v_N in such a compact, and the fixed marked heads have size O(N log N). Retain t=N^2 epsilon and all moving quantities from the [generic resonant hard-edge theorem](actual_q_hahn_generic_resonant_hard_edge.md). The transformed clocks U'=A0/V,V'=A0/U satisfy its hypotheses. At t=0 define kappa'_N=A0(0)/v_N, V'_N=A0(0)/U_N, K'_N=sin^2(pi m/N)(V'_N-1)/(pi^2 kappa'_N V'_N). Equation (1) transports the exact normalization as well: Z_low(t)=c_m(t)A0(t)^m product_(r<m)(1-Q(t)^r V(t)/A0(t)) =(-1)^m Q(t)^[m(m-1)/2] product_(r<m)(1-B(t)Q(t)^(r+1)V(t)). (2) Thus, uniformly on each fixed |t|<=rho<pi, H_m^B(U,V)/Z_low(t) =0F1(;1-t/(pi i);-K'_N)+O((1+log N)/N). (3) All fixed scaled genuine quantum jets have the same convergence. The transformed heads d-y,d-x are fixed as epsilon varies; neither the A0 derivative nor the marked character is suppressed. Equation (2) notably cancels the B powers in c_m A0^m exactly. The estimate remains absolute across zeros of the limiting function. ## 3. A uniform comparison of the two actual positive matrices At the ROOT let a<=floor((N-1)/2), theta=pi/N, and use the actual Hermitian matrices H_+,H_- from the [full physical determinant theorem](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md). Their diagonal is d_n=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], and their adjacent upper entries are sqrt(B_n)[sin(n theta)+/-i cos(n theta)], B_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. They satisfy, uniformly in N,a including the maximal folded a, H_+ <= 2H_-+8I, H_- <= 2H_++8I. (4) Here the inequalities are Hermitian quadratic-form inequalities. The proof retains their exact endpoint coefficients. Both matrices have the same Cholesky pivots as the positive D matrix, namely p_(n-1)=sin(n theta)/[cos(n theta)sin((2n-1)theta)]. Write their quadratic forms as sums of squared adjacent Cholesky terms and the final positive pivot. Flipping an offdiagonal phase changes its term by 2i sqrt(B_n)cos(n theta)/p_(n-1) times the next coordinate. The inequality |x+y|^2<=2|x|^2+2|y|^2 gives an additional diagonal cost 8 B_n cos^2(n theta)/p_(n-1) =4sin(2n theta)/sin((2n+1)theta)<=8. Indeed sin(2n theta)=2cos(theta)sin((2n+1)theta) -sin((2n+2)theta), and the last sine is nonnegative for every actual offdiagonal n<=a-1. This proves the first inequality in (4), and complex conjugation proves the second. No lower eigenvalue estimate or inverse channel norm is introduced. ## 4. The actual root numerator when the second clock is large Put K_a=[2a choose a]_Q. The exact source determinant, with its retained scalar, gives H_a^1(U,V)/V^a =K_a det[I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+]. (5) For example derive this from R_a(z;-cos gamma) =det[zI-(e^(i gamma)H_-+e^(-i gamma)H_+)/2], with z=q^t/U, e^(i gamma)=q q^t and (q^t)^2=UV, before canceling the displayed powers. This proves (5) as a polynomial identity and does not make a square-root choice in its final formula. Let qU range in a fixed compact subset of Re z<0, and let V=N^2 kappa_N with kappa_N in a fixed compact subset of C*. Set M0=I-(qU/2)H_-. Then H_a^1(U,V)=V^a K_a det(M0)[1+O(N^-1)]. (6) This is a UNIFORM RELATIVE estimate, including folded a. To prove it put D0=I+(eta/2)H_-, where -Re(qU)>=eta>0. The conjugated M0 has inverse norm at most one, while (4) bounds D0^(-1/2)H_+D0^(-1/2) uniformly. Thus the relative perturbation from the last term in (5) has norm O(N^-2). Expanding Log det costs at most a O(N^-2)=O(N^-1). This also proves nonvanishing and a marked relative logarithm on the stated domain. At qU negative real, det M0 is strictly positive. K_a and V^a retain their original phases. For the actual LARGE root channel m=d-a, the exact root partner identity supplies H_m^1(U,V)=H_a^1(U,V) product_(r=a)^(m-1)(UV-Q^r). Consequently its corresponding packet is H_m^1(U,V)=V^m U^(m-a) K_a det(M0)[1+O(N^-1)]. (7) The added product differs from (UV)^(m-a) by 1+O(N^-1). This is explicitly a ROOT identity: it is not differentiated as a generic large/small collision. Generic normals in this second large-clock regime remain separate from (6),(7). ## 5. The genuine paired 200/220 circle There is an exact geometric use of the negative ray in (6). Take the root theorem's 200 box with B=-J, J=[[1,1],[0,1]], and write A=[[a,-(a+1)^2/4],[4,-2-a]], P=BA, C=I+b(P+I), Aout=C^-1 A C, Q1=e[[1,z],[0,1]], W=A^-1Q1, e=+/-1. Direct multiplication, with the ACTUAL inverse collar transport, gives W_21=-4e, (Aout W)_21=16e b^2, U_geom,out=-W_21/(Aout W)_21=1/(4b^2). (8) Here C names the auxiliary collar, so its inverse gives the displayed transport. Conventions naming the transport itself C write C A C^-1 instead. The lower-left entry and ratio in (8) are unchanged under b->-b, so this squared-ray certificate is identical in those two notations; it does not change any primitive peripheral mark. The [marked complete rectangle collar](actual_matching_edge_geometric_target_polynomial.md) has b=-i/(2c), c>0, including its retained half-twist convention. Thus U_geom,out=-c^2. The physical half-index argument is U=q^-1 U_geom,out up to the retained finite-r correction, so qU approaches precisely this negative ray. Formula (7) therefore gives the nonzero outgoing 220 numerator paired with the incoming 200 Bessel packet. No independent phase of U has been chosen. The actual white monomial, F_m denominator, categorical dual, channel cup, physical caps and exterior source scalar still have to be retained when assembling the full box. Their exact lifts and logarithmic-escape estimates remain available; they are not set equal to one by (8). Other prefix patterns, original boundary currents and the global relative-cycle coefficient are not resolved by this local paired-numerator statement. Focused audit: [original generic reciprocity and complementary packets](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge_results.json). It checks 126 original generic reciprocity four-jets, retaining 504 coefficients; three exact paired-circle matrix identities; 17 folded positive-matrix comparisons and 173 pivot evaluations; 21 small and 21 large original-source determinant identities; and eight each of root220 relative-rate, generic002 packet and genuine002 first/second normal diagnostics. These finite checks supplement the proofs and do not prove their uniform asymptotic estimates. Independent analytical reviews checked the generic Ward uniqueness and scalar, marked complement normalization, both uniform Hermitian comparisons through the fold, actual root determinant and forced partner factors, and the squared geometric collar ratio. A separate fresh redirected audit replay passed every stated check at 95 digits. The review covers the exact reciprocity, genuine002 normals and root220 numerator packet; it does not supply generic220 normals, a completed boundary-circle packet or a global period coefficient.

title: The actual q-Hahn numerator at a deficient integer degree
status: Forced support zeros and selected fixed-degree packet
text: # The actual q-Hahn numerator at a deficient integer degree 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. Fix an actual integer degree t below the small channel a. The original generic numerator has an exact forced factor, which persists BEFORE root specialization. Its residual root polynomial is a positive-spectrum real Jacobi determinant. This gives a nonzero relative root amplitude at complex magnetic coordinates away from its explicit cuts, and polynomial cost for genuine q derivatives of this ORIGINAL numerator. The degree t stays an integer. A joint complex-degree estimate and the full exceptional operator's generic boundary factors are not asserted. Nor does a nonzero off-grid local packet change the fact that every original physical entry in the forbidden degree slice, including its q normals, is zero. ## 1. The forced factor is an identity of the original generic source Use the exact generic source and recurrence of [the small-channel normal theorem](actual_q_hahn_small_channel_generic_normals.md). Thus N>=3, d=N-1, q varies near q0=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, B=Q^-N, and H_a^B is the ORIGINAL finite Newton numerator. Its monic reverse polynomial is R_a(q;t,z)=z^a S_a^B(q^t/z,Q^t)/(Q^(ta) K_a), S_a^B(U,T)=U^a H_a^B(U,T/U), K_a=(B^2 Q^(a+1);Q)_a/(BQ;Q)_a. (1) Throughout 0<=t<a<=floor(d/2). All coefficients and K_a are holomorphic root units where required; in particular K_a(q0)!=0. At U=Q^r, 0<=r<=t, every kth summand of H_a^B contains product_(j<k)(U-Q^j) *product_(j<a-k)(Q^t/U-Q^j). Either k>r or a-k>t-r, so it vanishes. This is true at GENERIC q, with all the original B factors retained. Consequently F_t(q,z)=product_(r=0)^t(z-q^(t-2r)) divides R_a(q;t,z). (2) The nodes are distinct near q0. At a=t+1 monicity gives R_(t+1)=F_t exactly. Write the genuine generic recurrence as R_(n+1)=(z+alpha_n(q;t))R_n+beta_n(q;t)R_(n-1). When a>=t+2, its next step, together with (2), forces beta_(t+1)(q;t)=0 IDENTICALLY. (3) Indeed a nonzero scalar times the lower-degree monic R_t cannot be divisible by F_t. It follows that the quotient V_m(q;t,z)=R_(t+1+m)(q;t,z)/F_t(q,z) has its own exact tail recurrence V_0=1, V_1=z+alpha_(t+1), V_(m+1)=(z+alpha_(t+1+m))V_m +beta_(t+1+m)V_(m-1). (4) When a=t+1 the quotient is simply V_0=1, and no recurrence at a larger degree is needed. No q derivative couples a nonempty tail back across the vanished bridge (3). This differs from differentiating a factorization that holds only at a root of unity. ## 2. Exact root locations in the deficient chart Put theta=pi/N and c=-cos((t+1)theta)<0. The root recurrence is alpha_n=c/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], beta_n=B_n[cos^2(n theta)-c^2], B_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. (5) For n>=t+2, n<a, beta_n<0. Hence V_(a-t-1) is the characteristic polynomial of a real symmetric Jacobi matrix: its diagonal entries are -alpha_n for n=t+1,...,a-1, and its adjacent entries are sqrt(-beta_n), n=t+2,...,a-1. Its roots are in fact POSITIVE, not merely real. The exact root recurrence has R_a(z;-c)=(-1)^a R_a(-z;c). Set t_hi=N-t-2, -cos((t_hi+1)theta)=-c. Then t_hi>=d-a lies in the original complete-column chamber. Its proved root factorization has forced LEFT unit-arc roots and a negative-real residual. Reflection z->-z gives precisely the forced roots in (2) and positive-real roots for V. Their simplicity also follows from the irreducible real Jacobi matrix in (4). Thus every zero of the ACTUAL root polynomial R_a is on {q^(t-2r):0<=r<=t} union (0,infinity). (6) Choose compact real parameter ranges 0<sigma_0<=sigma=t/N<=sigma_1<1/2, sigma+eta<=alpha=a/N<=1/2, eta>0. (7) Take the common slit domain Omega=C\([0,infinity) union {exp(i phi):|phi|<=pi sigma_1}). (8) It is connected and simply connected: in the logarithm plane with 0<Arg z<2pi the removed unit arc is two finite vertical slits attached to the two edges of the strip. In particular negative real z belongs to Omega. The root polynomial is nowhere zero there, uniformly for the levels and parameters in (7). ## 3. The actual selected leading phase and relative amplitude Fix z0=-1. There are functions S_(sigma,alpha),A_(sigma,alpha), holomorphic in z on Omega, with S(z0)=0,A(z0)=1 and A nowhere zero, such that on each fixed compact in Omega R_a(q0;t,z)/R_a(q0;t,z0) =A_(sigma,alpha)(z) exp[N S_(sigma,alpha)(z)] *(1+O(N^-1)). (9) The error and all its fixed z derivatives are uniform. The ACTUAL ratios sigma=t/N and alpha=a/N are used. No uniform continuation in complex sigma is claimed. Here is a proof and a normalization that determines the functions. From (6), logarithmic derivatives of N^-1 Log[R_a(z)/R_a(-1)] are uniformly bounded on compact subsets of Omega; the logarithm is zero at -1. Its higher derivatives have the same local bounds. For z=-r<0 use the exact reflection R_a(q0;t,-r)=(-1)^a R_a(q0;t_hi,r), t_hi=N-t-2. (10) The right side is the already proved ACTUAL high-degree packet. Consequently every normal-family limit agrees there with S_(sigma,alpha)(-r) =Phi_alpha(1-sigma,v_r)-Phi_alpha(1-sigma,v_1) -pi i(v_r-v_1), v_r=(1-sigma)/2+i log(r)/(2pi), v_1=(1-sigma)/2. (11) The identity theorem fixes its continuation uniquely on Omega. The finite offset -2 in (10) is retained for the absolute anchor; only its limit is used in (11). Sequential compactness gives the claimed uniform leading convergence over (7), even when the actual parameters approach their limits slower than 1/N. For an explicit transport proof of the relative error, put D=z partial_z, kappa=2pi i, U=exp(pi i sigma)/z, T=exp(2pi i sigma), J=exp(2pi i alpha). The SAME root finite polynomial satisfies exactly (QU-1)(U-T) R(z/Q)+(QT-U)(1-U) R(Qz) +[2U+2QTU-(1+Q)U^2-T(Q^-a+Q^(a+1))]R(z)=0. (12) This is the original generic Casimir identity for S, with the monic reverse substitution (1); it is valid at these deficient degrees too. Write A0=(U-1)(U-T), C0=2U(1+T-U)-T(J+J^-1), H(p,z)=A0(exp(kappa p)+exp(-kappa p))+C0. For p=D S the selected characteristic is H(p,z)=0. Its derivative H_p is nonzero on Omega. Indeed C0^2-4A0^2=-16 T^2 sin^2(pi alpha) W/z^2, W=1-2cos(pi sigma)z+cos^2(pi alpha)z^2. (13) When sigma<alpha<=1/2, all finite roots of W are positive real: for alpha<1/2 its quadratic has positive sum and product and cos^2(pi sigma)>cos^2(pi alpha); at alpha=1/2 it is linear with positive root. Also A0 vanishes only at the excluded unit-arc endpoints. This proves uniform simplicity on the stated compacts. The first coefficient of (12), after its exact shifts are expanded, is H1=kappa[U(U-T)exp(-kappa p) +T(1-U)exp(kappa p)+2TU-U^2-TJ], rho=-(H1+(D p)H_(p,p)/2)/H_p. (14) Define A by D Log A=rho and A(-1)=1. Simplicity and the larger- compact Cauchy bounds first give D(N^-1 Log R)-p=O(N^-1). Cauchy gives that bound for its fixed derivatives too. Substituting a second time into (12) then gives D(N^-1 Log R)=p+rho/N+O(N^-2). Integrate along compact paths from -1. The exact normalized ratio at the starting point is one, proving (9) and its error. This is an actual finite-shift bootstrap, not a formal transport ansatz. The coefficients are smooth in the real parameters (7), by the simple characteristic and the actual anchor (11). The absolute anchor in (9) is explicitly known from (10) and the original ordinary normalization: R_a(q0;t,-1)=(-1)^a b_a^-1 product_(r=0)^(a-1)2sin[pi(t_hi-r)/N] *q0^[-d t_hi/2-(a^2-da)/2] *fhat_a(t_hi,t_hi/2), b_a=s_(2a)/s_a^2. (15) The fhat on the last line is the proved nonzero ordinary packet evaluated at its ACTUAL high total t_hi=N-t-2, including a half-integer magnetic center when necessary. Thus (9) has no unfixed multiplicative phase or scale. One may apply that packet and the elementary sine-product estimate directly to (15). ## 4. Polynomial cost of genuine generic-q numerator derivatives Let z=q^(t-2u), with the complex physical coordinate u held fixed while q=q0 exp(epsilon) varies. Require a FIXED logarithmic lift: the root z lies in a fixed compact of Omega and |u|<=C N. For example, take u=(t-Log(z)/(pi i/N))/2 with the marked branch of Log on Omega. The fixed integer t and a obey (7). Then for each fixed m |partial_epsilon^m R_a(q;t,q^(t-2u))|_(epsilon=0) <=C_m N^(10m) |R_a(q0;t,q0^(t-2u))|. (16) Here the polynomial is the ORIGINAL generic R from (1), with B=Q^-N. It is not obtained by differentiating the root recurrence (5) while discarding B. A root value z alone does not fix this jet: replacing u by u+N L preserves z(q0) but changes its q derivative by -2N L z. The bounded marked lift is therefore necessary. To prove (16), first split off the genuine factor (2). On a small generic disk its explicit logarithmic derivative is O(N^2), since all root distances from the compact to the unit arc are bounded below. For the residual determinant (4), freeze each upper entry at its positive root value sqrt(-beta_n(q0)); put the generic lower entry equal to -beta_n(q)/sqrt(-beta_n(q0)). Its diagonal is z(q)+alpha_n(q). The determinant is precisely the actual V. At the root this matrix is the alternating-sign unitary conjugate of zI minus the positive-spectrum real Jacobi matrix in section 2: the frozen positive offdiagonals differ from its negatives by that diagonal sign gauge. Its inverse is bounded by the inverse distance of the compact from [0,infinity). Moreover, for n>=t+2, cos^2((t+1)theta)-cos^2(n theta) =sin((n+t+1)theta)sin((n-t-1)theta)>=c/N, uniformly on (7). Since B_n>=1/4, every frozen upper entry has size at least c N^-1/2. The original generic recurrence estimates give alpha_n'=O(N^5), beta_n'=O(N^7), uniformly for all required n<=a. Thus the perturbed determinant matrix differs from its root matrix by at most C N^(15/2)|epsilon| in operator norm. On |epsilon|<=c N^-10 its determinant ratio is bounded uniformly above and below: apply det(I+M0^-1(M-M0)) with dimension at most N. The forced product has the same property there. Cauchy's formula proves (16). The same argument bounds the exact scalar K_a and monomial factors in (1), whose relative logarithmic derivatives are polynomial. Therefore (16) also controls the ORIGINAL unnormalized Newton numerator at these complex magnetic arguments. It does not divide by D_a(Q^t), which vanishes here. ## 5. The local kernel application and the remaining period problem The [entire exceptional source](actual_matching_edge_entire_operator_kernel.md) uses two copies of these root R polynomials at the SAME deficient integer degree. If both determinant arguments lie in fixed compacts of Omega, (9),(15) give their actual nonzero root packet, with the residual sine product and original normalization retained. This includes large genuinely nonreal determinant arguments; the forbidden physical nodes on the unit arc remain outside Omega. This is the chart supplied by the [actual global real-deficient frame](actual_augmented_plat_real_deficient_frame.md). For each level choose t_N near N/6 and set d_N=tan(pi t_N/N) in that construction. Its two failed factors then have the EXACT real normalized degree t_N/N, with the determinant arguments in the upper and lower half-planes. Fixing one sufficiently large geometric X and an interior midpoint keeps these arguments in fixed compact subsets of Omega as N grows. The marked magnetic lifts stay bounded after division by N. In the folded limit alpha->1/2, the original magnetic momentum associated to this numerator is Y=-exp(-2pi i D S). Its selected branch is Y(z)=(z-i sqrt(1-2cos(pi sigma)z))^2 /[1-2cos(pi sigma)z+z^2], (17) where the square root is positive at z<0 and continued through the respective half-plane. To check the sign, (10) sends z=-r to high z=r>0, whose proved selected characteristic has the PLUS square root. Replacing r by -z gives exactly (17). Characteristic simplicity continues it uniquely. This is the actual geometric branch established in the frame theorem, with its output disk normalization retained. It does not identify a contributing global period or the absolute action with the link volume. Equation (16) controls the actual generic q-Hahn NUMERATORS. A full generic exceptional-kernel continuation still has its original boundary factors; it is not proved merely by replacing q in the root entire formula. Nor is this a joint complex-degree theorem. Finally, each real integer forbidden separation h>a gives an IDENTICALLY ZERO original physical operator slice, including every generic-q normal. Deforming only its magnetic finite sums cannot turn that zero slice into a nonzero original period. A local geometric contribution in such a representation must cancel or fail selection there. Actual transport of the degree period, or another source-preserving grouping, remains necessary for a global nonzero contribution. No general long-twist volume theorem is inferred from this local chart result. Focused audit: [original generic factorization, actual finite shifts and selected complex packets](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_deficient_degree_packet.py). Primary-agent and independent full analytical reviews: PASS. The readers checked the generic support factor and persistent zero bridge, residual sign gauge and positive spectrum, root-location normal family, actual finite-shift bootstrap, high-total anchor with both offsets, bounded marked lifts and the genuine numerator perturbation estimates. The actual geometric branch and the identically zero physical slice remain distinct in these reviews. Fresh independent focused replay: PASS. It reproduced 672 forced-node four-jet checks, 182 generic zero bridges, 560 tail factorizations and 560 original numerator comparisons, followed by 280 exact finite shifts. Twelve positive residual matrices, 24 selected relative amplitudes and 72 genuine numerator checks also passed at 150 digits. The maximum N-scaled relative error was below 1.326; the independent literal generic-source relative error was below 1.1e-136. Numerical rate tests check normalization; the uniform estimates are proved above.

title: Exact coefficient duality for the original complete-channel polynomial
text: # Exact coefficient duality for the original complete-channel polynomial 30 October 2026. The positive coefficients of the actual magnetic polynomial are log-concave. Consequently a positive-radius evaluation recovers each coefficient within a factor at most j+1. The selected ordinary source action then gives a uniform coefficient rate, with an explicit optimal radius, throughout the interior coefficient-slope domain. This theorem keeps the source's physical total and integer channel. It neither deletes the Fourier phases when coefficients are sewn nor proves cancellation control for the original graph contraction. ## 1. The original polynomial and its positive coefficients Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, and retain the ACTUAL complete range 0<=j<=floor(d/2), d-j<=t<=d. The proved magnetic factorization is fhat(u)=q^(du) Q^(-ju) G_t(Q^u), G_t(q^t z)=c_t P_(N,t,j)(z), c_t=q^[j(t+j-d)]/(Q;Q)_j, P(z)=B_h(z) A_n(z)=sum_(k=0)^j p_k z^k, h=d-t, n=t+j-d, h+n=j. (1) Here B_h has the positive coefficients beta(h,k)=s_h/(s_k s_(h-k)), where s_r=product_(a=1)^r 2sin(pi a/N). The actual residual A_n has positive leading coefficient and n negative real roots. These are properties of the original coproduct polynomial, proved in [the magnetic corridor theorem](actual_q_hahn_magnetic_complex_corridor.md), not a replacement of its values by an interpolating polynomial. In particular p_k>0 for every 0<=k<=j. The source condition t+j>=d is essential here. Although its ordinary analytic continuation has a larger domain, positivity of this factorization is not asserted for arbitrary nonphysical t or for limiting tau+xi<1. ## 2. Log-concavity and an exact polynomial-loss duality The coefficient sequence p_0,...,p_j is log-concave: p_k^2>=p_(k-1)p_(k+1), 1<=k<j. (2) An elementary proof is enough. The consecutive ratio of B_h is beta(h,k)/beta(h,k-1) =sin((h-k+1)pi/N)/sin(k pi/N). Its decrease follows by cross multiplication: the difference of the two adjacent numerators is sin(pi/N)sin((h+1)pi/N)>0. The h=0 sequence consists of one coefficient and is included. Now let a_k be any nonnegative log-concave sequence with interval support, extended by zero elsewhere. Multiplication of its polynomial by z+rho, rho>0, gives b_k=rho a_k+a_(k-1), and b_k^2-b_(k-1)b_(k+1) =rho^2(a_k^2-a_(k-1)a_(k+1)) +rho(a_k a_(k-1)-a_(k-2)a_(k+1)) +(a_(k-1)^2-a_(k-2)a_k)>=0. (3) The middle term is nonnegative by the decreasing consecutive ratios; zero endpoints cause no problem. Factoring A_n into its positive linear factors and iterating (3) proves (2). For EVERY k=0,...,j the exact finite statement is p_k <= inf_(w>0) P(w) w^(-k) <= (j+1)p_k. (4) The first inequality holds because p_k w^k is one positive summand. For an interior k choose p_(k-1)/p_k <= w <= p_k/p_(k+1). This interval is nonempty by (2). At such a tilt, the kth term is a mode of the entire sequence p_l w^l, again by decreasing ratios. Its sum is at most j+1 times that term, proving the upper inequality. For k=0 and k=j, take w to zero and infinity respectively; the infimum equals the endpoint coefficient. For j=0 all statements are identities. Thus (4) is a two-sided estimate for actual coefficients, with no unknown exponentially small cancellation or probability prefactor. It is not an asymptotic Gaussian coefficient formula. ## 3. The correct radial free energy and its explicit derivative Set tau=t/N, xi=j/N and w=exp(y), y real. Because the polynomial coordinate in (1) is z=Q^u/q^t, the corresponding magnetic variable is nu=u/N=tau/2-i y/(2pi). (5) The reciprocal determinant coordinate is 1/w, not w. Taking absolute values in the EXACT source normalization (1) gives log P(exp y)=log s_j-(d-2j)y/2+log|fhat(N nu)|. (6) Use the actual selected action Phi_xi from [the full physical packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md). For complete physical indices with tau in a fixed compact subinterval of (1/2,1), xi bounded away from zero, and y in a fixed finite interval, N^(-1)log P(exp y)=F(tau,xi;y)+O(log N/N), F=J(xi)-(1/2-xi)y +Re Phi_xi(tau,tau/2-i y/(2pi)). (7) The scaled parameters in (7) are their ACTUAL values at level N. The possible complete boundary displacement tau+xi=1-1/N is retained; its limiting parameters satisfy tau+xi>=1. The packet and the factorial estimate are uniform for these indices. The derivative in y of the error in (7) is O(1/N) on smaller compact intervals. The log s_j term is independent of y and has not been dropped. There is an explicit derivative requiring no new saddle selection. Put c=-cos(pi tau)>0, C=cos(pi xi), s=sin(pi xi)>0, B=w^2+2cw+C^2. On (5) the selected multiplier is Y=exp(Phi_nu)=(s+i sqrt(B))^2/(1+2cw+w^2), Arg Y=2 arctan(sqrt(B)/s) in (0,pi). (8) It has modulus one, and the square root is positive real. This is the already calibrated ordinary branch on this central vertical line. Differentiating (7), with its MINUS sign in (5), yields F_y=xi-1/2+pi^(-1) arctan(sqrt(B)/s), F_yy=s w(w+c)/[pi sqrt(B)(1+2cw+w^2)]>0. (9) As y tends to minus or plus infinity, F_y tends respectively to 0 and xi, including the folded endpoint C=0. Every interior slope 0<lambda<xi therefore has a unique finite optimal tilt. It is explicitly a=pi(1/2-xi+lambda), w_*=sqrt(c^2-C^2+s^2 tan(a)^2)-c>0, y_*=log w_*. (10) The quantity s tan(a) is strictly greater than C for lambda>0, which proves positivity of this root. Formula (10) also gives uniform finite tilt bounds on compact interior slope families. Equivalently, the selected magnetic momentum at that coefficient is Y_*=exp[2pi i(lambda+1/2-xi)], Log Y_*=2pi i(lambda+1/2-xi) in i(0,pi). (10a) Thus the Fourier index prescribes the FULL local phase on this selected radial saddle, not only the modulus of a multiplier. Its radial boundary variable is the positive root (10), equivalently w_*^2+2cw_*+C^2=s^2 tan^2(pi(1/2-xi+lambda)). Actual network orientation and incidence are still needed to combine these local characters into global equations. ## 4. Uniform actual coefficient rates Take any compact family of limiting complete parameters with 1/2<tau<1, 0<xi<=1/2 and tau+xi>=1. Keep the coefficient slope lambda strictly inside (0,xi), uniformly on that family. For all legal integer sequences N,t,j,k approaching this family, use the actual scaled values tau_N=t/N, xi_N=j/N, lambda_N=k/N. Define L(tau,xi,lambda) =F(tau,xi;y_*)-lambda y_*, (11) where (10) fixes the unique positive tilt. Then log p_k=N L(tau_N,xi_N,lambda_N)+O(log N), (12) uniformly over that family and both level parities. The value in (11) is also the infimum over all real y of F-lambda y. Its slope derivatives obey L_lambda=-y_*, L_(lambda lambda)=-1/F_yy(y_*)<0. (13) For completeness, no unbounded minimizer is hidden in (12). The finite function F_N(y)=N^(-1)log P(exp y) is convex, and its derivative is the tilted mean of k/N. Choose fixed endpoints y_-<y_+ beyond the compact set of optimal tilts (10). By (9) there is a uniform strict gap between F_y(y_-) and the target slopes, and between those slopes and F_y(y_+). The derivative convergence in (7) puts every finite minimizer of F_N-lambda_N y in [y_-,y_+] for large N. The uniform value estimate (7), followed by (4), proves (12). Boundary slopes k/N approaching zero or xi, unbounded tilts, and physical degree endpoints tau=1/2 or tau=1 are outside this uniform statement. Their exact finite inequality (4) remains valid; a rate or relative amplitude at those boundaries needs its own estimates. No relative coefficient amplitude is claimed even in the interior. ## 5. What this supplies for a sewn source Each original coefficient has now an actual positive radial variational description, retaining its normalizer and its Fourier index. This permits the index k to remain a shared variable in an exact affine wire/cycle compiler. If a positive comparison partition is assembled from these coefficients, their actions must first be summed on that shared incidence set before taking any maximum. The original magnetic source is reconstructed with its displayed Fourier factors and scalar c_t. A positive coefficient theorem does not erase those phases, identify a graph contraction with the product of coefficient envelopes, or prove a nonzero geometric overlap. Those are separate requirements for the full volume conjecture. Focused audit: [original positive coefficients and radial duality](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_fourier_coefficient_variational.py). Three formal identities check the log-concavity step, curvature and inverse tilt. At 90 digits, 794 actual positive polynomials satisfy 3,938 log-concavity and tilted-mode checks; nine literal off-lattice source values check the radial sign and normalization. Eighteen interior coefficient sequences check the stated rate and tilt gradient. The uniform theorem is proved above, not inferred from those sequences. Independent analytical reviews: PASS. The root reader and an independent reader checked the original polynomial support and scalar, log-concavity including endpoints, modal infimum inequality, corrected radial sign, selected characteristic and strict curvature, explicit tilt, and the uniform trapping of finite minimizers. A fresh independent audit replay passed all three formal identities, 794 polynomials, 3,938 mode checks, nine original radial source values, and eighteen coefficient-rate checks. The reviews retain discrete channels, interior slopes and the distinction between positive coefficients and a coherently sewn graph source.

title: The actual ordinary packet on the full strict physical tube
status: Selected full physical complex amplitude; finite correction
text: # The actual ordinary packet on the full strict physical tube 30 October 2026. A second exact Hermitian realization of the original q-Hahn determinant puts its zeros in a sharp angular cone. It extends the ordinary joint action and nonzero relative amplitude from the central wedge to the FULL strict physical tube. Both magnetic coordinates vary complexly; the channel remains an actual integer. The finite source has a small upper-boundary correction, which is necessary: an explicit one-channel counterexample is given below. Every fixed compact in the full physical tube is covered for all sufficiently large N. No contributing global cycle or coherent whole-source estimate is asserted. ## 1. Exact source and a second determinant Put theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), Q=q^2, d=N-1 and 1<=j<=floor(d/2). Write t=N tau, u=N nu, xi=j/N, z=exp[pi i(tau-2nu)], gamma=pi(tau+1/N). The ORIGINAL joint source is exactly fhat_j(u,t-u)=x^u q^(jt) [2j choose j]_Q R_j(z;-cos gamma)/Delta_j(Q^t), x=q^d, Delta_j(T)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)(T-Q^r). (1) All powers and scalar factors are those of [the original joint amplitude theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md). Let b_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. The exact monic recurrence is R_0=1, R_1=z+c/cos(theta), R_(n+1)=[z+c/(cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta))]R_n +b_n[cos^2(n theta)-c^2]R_(n-1). (2) Define j-by-j real matrices A and K, indexed by 0,...,j-1: A_(n,n)=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], A_(n-1,n)=A_(n,n-1)=sqrt(b_n)sin(n theta), K_(n-1,n)=sqrt(b_n)cos(n theta), K_(n,n-1)=-sqrt(b_n)cos(n theta), K_(n,n)=0. Then the SAME polynomial has the second exact determinant R_j(z;-cos gamma)=det[zI-cos(gamma)A-sin(gamma)K]. (3) Indeed the upper and lower adjacent entries of J_gamma=cos(gamma)A+sin(gamma)K are sqrt(b_n)sin(n theta+gamma) and sqrt(b_n)sin(n theta-gamma). Their product is b_n[cos^2(gamma)-cos^2(n theta)], so the continuant of zI-J_gamma is exactly (2). The two Hermitian matrices H_+=A+iK, H_-=A-iK (4) are POSITIVE DEFINITE. Their adjacent entries have modulus sqrt(b_n) and their diagonal equals that of the proved positive matrix D in [the first determinant theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.md). A diagonal unitary phase gauge makes each of these tridiagonal offdiagonals positive real. Thus each H_+ and H_- is unitarily equivalent to D, including the maximal channel. Consequently J_gamma=(e^(i gamma)H_-+e^(-i gamma)H_+)/2. (5) This is a source-exact matrix identity, not an asymptotic model. ## 2. A sharp finite angular exclusion, and its necessary correction For any eigenvector v of J_gamma with norm one, its eigenvalue is zeta=(h_-/2)e^(i gamma)+(h_+/2)e^(-i gamma), h_-=v*H_-v>0, h_+=v*H_+v>0. (6) If pi/2<Re gamma<3pi/2, these two rays bound a left angular cone. Put a_gamma=min(Re gamma,2pi-Re gamma). Every nonzero eigenvalue satisfies |Arg zeta|>=a_gamma; the inequality is strict when the two boundary rays are distinct. When Re gamma=pi all eigenvalues are strictly negative real. Positive coefficients in (6) also exclude a zero eigenvalue in this range. Define the full physical tube P={ (tau,nu) in C^2: 1/2<Re tau<1, 0<Re nu<Re tau }, and its finite-level subdomain P_N={ (tau,nu) in P: Re tau<1-1/(2N) }. (7) For a physical point the principal argument of z in (1) is exactly pi(Re tau-2Re nu), with absolute value <pi Re tau. On P_N, a_gamma>pi Re tau. Therefore (3) is nonzero there. The factors Delta_j(Q^t) are also nonzero: their zeros require tau=r/N modulo an integer, 0<=r<j<N/2. All remaining factors in (1) are nonzero. Thus the ORIGINAL finite source is holomorphic and nowhere zero on P_N. The case j=0 is its explicit nonzero exponential. The correction in (7) cannot simply be deleted for every finite N. Already j=1 has its zero at z_N=cos[pi(tau+1/N)]/cos(pi/N). Take tau_N=1-1/(4N)+i and delta=3pi/(4N). Then z_N=[-cos(delta)cosh(pi)+i sin(delta)sinh(pi)]/cos(pi/N), Arg z_N=pi-arctan[tan(delta)tanh(pi)] <pi Re tau_N. (8) For the strict inequality, set a=pi/(4N): tan(a)/tan(3a)<1/3<tanh(pi), valid for N>=3. Define nu_N=[tau_N-Log(z_N)/(pi i)]/2 with the principal logarithm. It satisfies 0<Re nu_N<Re tau_N, but (1) vanishes. The denominator is nonzero. This is an exact finite-source counterexample on P. These points approach the boundary of P as N grows and therefore do not obstruct the fixed-compact theorem below. ## 3. Uniform inverse and logarithmic bounds on full physical compacts Fix a compact K0 contained in P. For all large N, K0 lies in P_N and gamma has real part between pi/2 and pi. Put M=zI-(e^(i gamma)H_-+e^(-i gamma)H_+)/2. The three coefficients z, -e^(i gamma), -e^(-i gamma) lie in one open half-plane through zero. To see this, write a=Re gamma and psi=Arg z. The latter satisfies |psi|<a. The other two arguments are pi-a and -(pi-a). Their angular span together with psi is strictly less than pi. On a fixed physical compact the span stays uniformly below pi, because Re nu and Re(tau-nu) are bounded below and Re tau stays away from 1/2 and 1. Their moduli also have positive lower and finite upper bounds on K0. Rotate the half-plane by a phase beta. Locally, and uniformly on a finite cover of K0, this gives Re(e^(-i beta)M)>=delta I+eta_- H_-+eta_+ H_+, delta,eta_-,eta_+>=c_(K0)>0. (9) Hence ||M^(-1)||<=C_(K0). Conjugating M by H_+^(-1/2), or by H_-^(-1/2), also gives |tr(M^(-1)H_+)|+|tr(M^(-1)H_-)|<=C_(K0)j. Since partial_z M=I and partial_gamma M=-(i/2)e^(i gamma)H_-+(i/2)e^(-i gamma)H_+, both logarithmic derivatives of R_j with respect to z and gamma are O_(K0)(j). No lower eigenvalue bound for D, H_+ or H_- is used. The result is uniform through the folded channel. The scalar factors in (1) have the same explicit O(N) logarithmic derivative bounds as before. Thus the first derivatives of N^(-1)Log fhat_j are uniformly bounded on full physical compacts. Choose its scalar holomorphic logarithm on the convex P_N by continuation from its already fixed central value. The exact real center phase remains Im Log fhat_j(t/2,t/2)=pi[d(t-j)+j^2]/(2N). (10) The principal matrix logarithm of the old central realization is not being asserted outside its domain. A central anchor bounds the continued normalized scalar logarithm, and Cauchy estimates give all its fixed derivatives on smaller physical compacts. The normal-family argument now extends the ACTUAL selected leading action throughout P. Any subsequential limit agrees on the central open subset with the already proved Phi_xi, and hence everywhere by the holomorphic identity theorem. This gives local uniform convergence with all derivatives, uniformly for xi=j/N in compact real subintervals of (0,1/2], always using its actual value. ## 4. The characteristic is simple on the entire tube Set gamma0=pi tau, s=sin(pi xi), C=cos(pi xi), and W=1-2cos(gamma0)z+C^2 z^2, V=1-2cos(gamma0)z+z^2. (11) Both are nonzero on P. This has a two-dimensional positive-cone proof which includes C=0. Let u=(1,0)^T, v=(s,C)^T and B_gamma0=e^(i gamma0)u u*+e^(-i gamma0)v v*. Its trace is 2cos(gamma0), its determinant is C^2, and det(I-z B_gamma0)=W. Every nonzero eigenvalue is a NONNEGATIVE combination of the same two left-cone rays, with at least one positive coefficient. It therefore lies in the closed cone |Arg lambda|>=pi Re tau. Reciprocation preserves that cone, so its reciprocal cannot be the physical z, whose argument has smaller absolute value. This proves the assertion for W. Taking s=0,C=1 proves it for V. The full source characteristic from the exact Casimir shift is H=A(Y+Y^(-1))+D-(J+J^(-1))=0, A=(U-T)(1-U)/T, D=2U(1+T-U)/T, U=e^(2pi i nu), T=e^(2pi i tau), J=e^(2pi i xi). Here A!=0 on P, and xi is bounded away from zero. Its two solutions are Y_+=(s z+i sqrt(W))^2/V, Y_-=(s z-i sqrt(W))^2/V. (12) The square root is the holomorphic continuation from the selected central branch on the simply connected P. It is NOT necessarily the pointwise principal square root outside the central wedge. The numerators in (12) are nonzero because W+s^2 z^2=V. The two roots are distinct because s,z,W,V are nonzero. Thus H_a!=0 for a=Log Y on the selected sheet throughout P, including xi=1/2. The second source characteristic remains simple in Phi_tau: its derivative is (1-T)exp(Phi_tau), which is nonzero. The leading action in section 3 already supplies this actual holomorphic logarithm, rather than selecting a new solution of that equation. ## 5. The actual nonzero amplitude, with its original normalization The two finite source shifts (11),(12) of [the original joint amplitude proof](actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md) are rational identities for the SAME finite function (1). They therefore hold on the enlarged domain. The proof's two derivative bootstraps now apply on full physical compacts: the preceding section supplies uniform characteristic simplicity, and section 3 supplies uniform Cauchy bounds on slightly larger compacts. Explicitly let G_N=N^(-1)Log fhat, a=Phi_nu and b=Phi_tau. The exact Casimir shift first gives partial_nu G_N-a=O(N^(-1)); Cauchy's formula gives the same bound for its derivatives. A second substitution gives partial_nu G_N=a+N^(-1)r+O(N^(-2)). The exact coproduct shift then gives, by the same two substitutions, partial_tau G_N=b+N^(-1)s1+O(N^(-2)). (13) Here r and s1 are EXACTLY the coefficients (16),(17) in that proof, with its original integer offsets and actual xi=j/N. Their formulas are holomorphic on P by the simplicity just proved. The errors and their fixed derivatives are uniform on smaller compacts. The one-form s1 d tau+r d nu is closed: equate the mixed derivatives of the actual G_N in (13), use Cauchy bounds on the remainders, and pass to admissible xi sequences. The coefficient functions depend locally analytically on xi by the simple characteristic and their already normalized central values. Thus closedness holds at every real xi in the stated interval, including its folded end. On the simply connected P this form defines a nonzero holomorphic B_xi, normalized by the ALREADY PROVED central real-lattice amplitude. Integrating (13) from a nearby genuine central sample along compact paths gives fhat_j(Nnu,N(tau-nu)) =N^(-1/2) B_(xi_N)(tau,nu) exp[N Phi_(xi_N)(tau,nu)](1+O(N^(-1))) (14) on every compact subset of P. Fixed derivatives of the relative error have the same bound on smaller compacts. At the initial sample Log fhat-N Phi+(1/2)log N-Log B is O(N^(-1)), and its gradient has that same bound by (13). Thus no additive phase, sample character, or normalization constant is introduced during continuation. In the original overlap B is the exact coefficient Acal(w_*)exp[pi i(alpha(w_*)-nu)] from the central proof. Both level parities, arbitrary fixed complex magnetic displacements, and the discrete folded limit are included. ## 6. The generic-normal bounds use the same enlarged corridor The proved small-channel generic-normal and near-fold paired-normal bounds also extend to any fixed compact K0 in P. There is one necessary change in their matrix perturbation argument. Use M in (9) as the root tridiagonal realization. For each adjacent pair, freeze whichever of its two root entries has larger modulus, and set the opposite generic entry so their product is -beta_n(q) in the ORIGINAL generic recurrence. One must not always freeze the upper entry: sin(gamma+n theta) can vanish at an integer degree. The chosen entry is uniformly bounded below because sqrt(b_n)>=1/2 and |sin(gamma+n theta)|^2+|sin(gamma-n theta)|^2 =2|sin gamma|^2 cos^2(n theta) +2|cos gamma|^2 sin^2(n theta). On fixed physical compacts, for all large N, both |sin gamma| and |cos gamma| are bounded below. Therefore the larger adjacent entry has a positive uniform lower bound. The diagonal is unchanged. The old generic coefficient bounds give ||M(q)-M(q0)||=O(N^7|epsilon|), and (9) supplies the bounded root inverse. All scalar factors and their derivatives retain their former estimates. It follows that the original small-channel N^8 fixed-jet bound holds on K0. Its last inverse cofactor still equals R_(j-1)/R_j, so the EXACT large-channel recurrence and scalar argument of [the near-fold theorem](actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md) give the same paired bound |w_(j,l)/C_j|<=C_(K0)N^8(C_(K0)N^16)^(l-j) (15) when l-j<=eta_(K0)N. Thus its subexponential consequence for (l-j)log N=o(N) holds on the full strict physical tube's fixed compacts as well. The fixed positive scaled-channel limitation and the distinction between an upper bound and an amplitude remain unchanged. ## 7. Scope The ordinary local packet now covers the full strict physical domain, and its selected sheet is continued from the original central source. Membership in that physical domain, matching the geometric sheet, choosing a contributing original cycle, and controlling the coherent contraction remain separate global tasks. The finite boundary example (8) explains why the theorem is stated on fixed compacts for sufficiently large N rather than by deleting the exact finite correction everywhere. Focused audit: [cone, literal source and full physical amplitudes](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet_results.json). The three formal cone identities and 242 exact actual-source determinants passed. Six explicit finite-boundary counterexamples were checked. Eight original generic adapters passed, including four cases with a genuinely vanishing upper root entry. At 180 digits, 16 independent terminating-source comparisons and 16 amplitude calibrations strictly OUTSIDE the central wedge passed; 16 actual subprincipal gradient corrections also passed. The largest N-scaled relative amplitude error was 1.184 and the largest N-squared gradient remainder was 16.406. These are normalization regressions; the cone and two-shift argument give the uniform result. An independent full analytical review checked the same-polynomial Hermitian realization, the finite cutoff and explicit boundary counterexample, rotated coercivity and logarithmic estimates, the continued scalar logarithm, the rank-one PSD discriminant proof, and both amplitude bootstraps with their original central normalization. It also checked the larger-offdiagonal generic lift and the unchanged near-fold scope. The review preserves the fixed-compact, discrete-channel statement and does not infer a global contributing cycle or coherent source estimate. A second independent full analytical review and fresh focused replay also passed. It checked the finite angular cutoff and counterexample, all rotated inverse and weighted trace bounds, the marked scalar-log continuation, W and V including the rank-one endpoint, both actual amplitude bootstraps, and the larger-entry generic adapter. Its replay reproduced all formal, exact, and 180-digit counts above. A further analytical reader independently checked the same source and domain interfaces without duplicating that replay. The reviews retain the finite-boundary caveat and all stated global limitations.

title: The actual generic white numerator at the resonant hard edge
status: Genuine quantum normals through the boundary hypergeometric parameter
text: # The actual generic white numerator at the resonant hard edge 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed source theorem. A genuine quantum deformation of the original white numerator has a uniform boundary packet. Its root limit is a Bessel function, while its retained quantum normals differentiate the ORDER parameter of a confluent hypergeometric function. The exact large monomial normalization stays in the answer. No zero of the limiting function, cup divisor, or global selected cycle is removed. ## 1. The original generic polynomial and its exact reindexing Use the ACTUAL polynomial H_m^B(U,V) in the [generic white-source theorem](actual_generic_boundary_gauge_and_source.md), not a small root-colliding replacement for the large white channel. Write Q=q^2, B=Q^(-N), and H_m^B(U,V)=sum_(k=0)^m c_k V^k product_(r<k)(U-Q^r) product_(r<m-k)(V-Q^r), c_k=(-1)^k B^k Q^[k(k+1)/2] [m choose k]_Q (BQ^(m-k+1);Q)_k/(BQ;Q)_k. (1) In particular c_m=(-B)^m Q^[m(m+1)/2], EXACTLY. Divide by the actual k=m term Z_m=c_m(UV)^m product_(r=0)^(m-1)(1-Q^r/U). (2) Setting k=m-l gives the identity H_m^B/Z_m=sum_(l=0)^m T_l, T_0=1, T_l=(-1)^l B^(-l)Q^[-ml+l(l-1)/2] [m choose l]_Q (BQ^(m-l+1);Q)_l/(BQ;Q)_l (UV)^(-l) product_(r<l)(V-Q^r) /product_(r=m-l)^(m-1)(1-Q^r/U). (3) This is a termwise identity of the original generic source. The additional Pochhammer ratio in (3) is essential: replacing it by another Gaussian binomial before differentiating would erase the normal proved below. To verify the ratio directly, cancel (BQ^(l+1);Q)_(m-l)=(BQ;Q)_m/(BQ;Q)_l in c_(m-l)/c_m. ## 2. A joint boundary packet with the actual moving parameter Fix delta>0, and suppose m=m_N is an integer with delta<=mu_N=m/N<=1-delta. At the original root q0=exp(pi i/N), choose marked, possibly complex head lifts x_N,y_N such that U_N(0)=q0^(2x_N)=N^2 kappa_N, V_N(0)=q0^(2y_N)=V_N^0, |x_N|+|y_N|<=C N(1+log N). (4) The kappa_N and V_N^0 range over fixed compact subsets of C minus zero. Their logarithms are the specified head marks, not reset principal values. Set epsilon=t/N^2, q_N(t)=exp(pi i/N+t/N^2), Q_N=q_N^2, B_N=Q_N^(-N), U_N(t)=exp[2x_N Log q_N(t)], V_N(t)=exp[2y_N Log q_N(t)]. (5) All integers N,m and all marked head lifts stay fixed under this quantum deformation. Define K_N=sin^2(pi mu_N)(V_N^0-1)/(pi^2 kappa_N V_N^0), b(t)=1-t/(pi i), F(t;K)=sum_(l>=0) (-K)^l/[l! (b(t))_l]. (6) The last line DEFINES the function customarily written 0F1(;b(t);-K); no hypergeometric transformation is imported. On any fixed |t|<=rho<pi, the actual normalized source satisfies H_m^(B_N(t))(U_N(t),V_N(t))/Z_m(t) =F(t;K_N)+O((1+log N)/N), (7) uniformly in all the displayed compact parameters. At t=0 this is sum (-K_N)^l/(l!)^2=J_0(2sqrt(K_N)), interpreted by its entire series so that no square-root choice is necessary. The root specialization is the same actual boundary model as in [the resonant root hard-edge theorem](actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.md). The result is holomorphic in t on a larger disk of the same type. Consequently, for every fixed j and a smaller disk, N^(-2j) partial_epsilon^j[H_m^B(U,V)/Z_m]|_0 =partial_t^j F(t;K_N)|_0+O((1+log N)/N). (8) These are GENUINE generic-q normals of the specified source at fixed marked heads. They are not derivatives of its root Bessel formula. Across zeros of F the estimates are absolute in the normalization (2). Relative estimates require a compact avoiding the relevant zeros. For example, with H_l=sum_(r=1)^l 1/r and H_l^(2)=sum_(r=1)^l 1/r^2, the first two retained limits are partial_t F(0;K)=(pi i)^(-1) sum_(l>=0) (-K)^l H_l/(l!)^2, partial_t^2 F(0;K)=(pi i)^(-2) sum_(l>=0) (-K)^l[H_l^2+H_l^(2)]/(l!)^2. (8a) They follow by differentiating the actual denominator in (6), and are generally nonzero even though the root Bessel formula alone has no moving-q parameter. ## 3. Proof: fixed terms, uniform domination and the error For each fixed l and r, the actual small denominator factors are 1-Q_N^r=(-2pi i/N)r(1+O(N^-1)), 1-B_N Q_N^r=(-2pi i/N)[r-t/(pi i)](1+O(N^-1)). (9) The second line follows from B_N Q_N^r=exp[(2pi i r-2t)/N+2rt/N^2]. This fixes the sign of b(t). The first limiting singular parameter is t=pi i, corresponding to the nearby moving period N-1. Our disks stay strictly away from it. The two numerator products in (3) each tend to (1-exp(2pi i mu_N))^l. Combining their phase with (-1)^l Q_N^(-ml) and the two factors (-2pi i/N)^l gives (-N^2 sin^2(pi mu_N)/pi^2)^l. Moreover U_N(t)/U_N(0) and V_N(t)/V_N(0) are 1+O((1+log N)/N), and the last denominator product in (3) tends to one. Thus the lth term tends to (-K_N)^l/[l!(1-t/(pi i))_l], (10) with the ACTUAL generic denominator rather than a squared factorial. Here is a uniform summable bound, including large l. On a slightly larger fixed t disk with radius less than pi, for all 1<=r<=m, |1-Q_N^r|>=c_delta r/N, |1-B_N Q_N^r|>=c_(delta,rho) r/N. (11) For r bounded, (9) and |r-t/(pi i)|>=r(1-rho/pi) prove the second estimate. For larger r it follows from the root sine bound and its O(N^-1) perturbation; dividing at a sufficiently large fixed r makes this comparison uniform. All numerator factors are bounded by a constant. The powers of B,Q in (3) have bounded modulus (or may be absorbed in C^l). Since |U_N(t)|>=c N^2 and |V_N(t)|>=c, the two binomial-type factors and (UV)^(-l) cancel their N^(2l) costs. Finally product_(r=m-l)^(m-1)|1-Q_N^r/U_N(t)|^(-1)<=exp(C/N). It follows that |T_l|<=C^l/(l!)^2, uniformly for 0<=l<=m. The limiting terms satisfy the same type of bound. This proves normal-family convergence by the actual finite series, not by matching a formal solution of a differential equation. The error in (7) can also be quantified directly. For l<=cN, with c chosen below delta/2, compare each product in (3) with (10). The numerator phases and the two denominator products have relative logarithmic error O(l^2/N), and the retained moving heads add O(l(1+log N)/N). Apply |exp(w)-1|<=|w|exp(|w|), and absorb exp(C l^2/N)<=exp(C' l) into the preceding factorial majorant. Summing gives O((1+log N)/N). This comparison is made factorwise for product_(r<l)(V-Q^r), without dividing by V_N^0-1; it is therefore uniform when K_N=0 as well. A telescoping product difference gives the same bound there. For l>cN both factorial tails are smaller than every inverse power of N. This proves (7), uniformly on the larger t disk. Cauchy's formula then proves (8) and all fixed t derivatives of the error. ## 4. The exact normalization is not a harmless constant Equation (2) is kept at the moving parameter. In particular it contains U_N(t)^m even though U_N(t)/U_N(0) tends to one. For standard fixed marks Log U_N(0)=2log N+Log kappa_N, U_N(t)^m/U_N(0)^m =exp[mu_N t Log U_N(0)/(pi i)] =N^[2mu_N t/(pi i)] exp[mu_N t Log kappa_N/(pi i)]. (12) Other retained head carries give their actual additional factors; they are not removed from (2). The exact top coefficient contributes c_m(t)/c_m(0)=exp[t(-2Nm+m(m+1))/N^2]. (13) The remaining product in (2) is nonzero on the stated disks. Its logarithmic t derivatives are uniformly bounded with the same marked heads. Equations (12),(13), V_N(t)^m and that product give the original unnormalized jets by ordinary Leibniz. In particular they are not obtained by simply differentiating J_0 at fixed K. On any compact where F(0;K_N) stays away from zero, (7),(8) give a nonzero local root packet and relative fixed-normal bounds. If the limiting Bessel factor vanishes, the normalized series and its true parameter derivatives are still covered, but no nonzero leading amplitude is asserted. The theorem concerns the actual white numerator; all scalar, cup and marked contraction factors must still be restored before discussing an operator or its original finite period. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_generic_resonant_hard_edge.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_generic_resonant_hard_edge_results.json) check 20 symbolic reindexed coefficients, 54 nonroot and 54 root original-H four-jet identities with 432 coefficients, 48 complex scaled-parameter packets, 24 genuine scaled first/second normals, 12 independent terminating source values, six retained top-term normalizations and both harmonic normal formulas. Finite convergence errors are recorded as diagnostics, separately from the uniform proof. Independent parent, geometry and source analytical reviews passed the exact generic ratio, denominator sign, uniform finite-series bound, absolute error at V=1, fixed-head Cauchy normals and retained top-term phases. The parent also freshly replayed the full audit and reproduced every count. The result is restricted to the specified white numerator and its normalization, with limiting zeros retained; it is not a full-operator or selected-period theorem.

title: The physical selected Fourier action has a global Legendre chart
text: # The physical selected Fourier action has a global Legendre chart 30 October 2026. The local action change of [holomorphic Legendre transport](actual_q_hahn_holomorphic_fourier_legendre_transport.md) is globally one-to-one on the full physical tube. This removes a possible multiple-chart ambiguity for the selected classical action. It does not provide analytic continuation of individual finite Fourier coefficients. ## 1. Statement Fix 0<xi<=1/2 and the original marked selected action Phi_xi. Retain all the source constants and logarithmic characters in the local theorem. Write P={1/2<Re tau<1, 0<Re nu<Re tau}, y=2pi i(nu-tau/2), F=J(xi)+(xi-1/2)y+Phi_xi(tau,nu) -i pi(tau-xi+xi^2)/2, lambda=F_y=xi-1/2+Phi_nu/(2pi i). (1) Let O be the image of P in (tau,y). Then (tau,y) -> (tau,lambda) (2) is a biholomorphism from O onto its open image D_xi. In particular the selected Legendre action F-lambda y is a SINGLE holomorphic function on D_xi, with its original additive phase fixed by (1). The image D_xi is not asserted convex, a product, or the whole complex coefficient plane. ## 2. A source-selected square root is injective on each physical fiber Fix tau. Put a=pi Re tau in (pi/2,pi), w=exp(y), c=-cos(pi tau), C=cos(pi xi), s=sin(pi xi), B(w)=w^2+2cw+C^2, V(w)=w^2+2cw+1. The physical w-domain is exactly the sector S_tau={w!=0: |Arg w|<a}. (3) The marked y-strip has imaginary width 2a<2pi, so exp maps that strip bijectively onto (3). The full physical packet proves B and V nonzero there. Therefore both roots alpha,beta of B belong to the complementary closed cone K_tau={0} union {w!=0: |Arg(-w)|<=pi-a}. This cone is convex: its angle is 2(pi-a)<pi. The whole segment [alpha,beta] consequently misses S_tau. This conclusion also covers xi=1/2, when one root is zero. For distinct roots, the function r(w)=(w-alpha) sqrt((w-beta)/(w-alpha)) (4) is holomorphic on C minus [alpha,beta], using the principal square root in the displayed ratio. Indeed that ratio is a nonpositive real number precisely on the removed segment. It satisfies r(w)^2=B(w), r(w)=w+c+O(1/w) at infinity. (5) The reflection R(w)=alpha+beta-w=-2c-w preserves the slit domain and B. Thus r(R(w))/r(w) is a constant sign on its connected domain. The asymptotic condition (5) fixes that sign to be minus: r(-2c-w)=-r(w). (6) If r(w_1)=r(w_2), the equation B(w_1)=B(w_2) gives either w_1=w_2 or w_2=-2c-w_1. The second alternative, by (6), would force r(w_1)=0, impossible off the slit. Hence r is injective on the slit complement, and in particular on S_tau. If alpha=beta, the normalized root is simply r(w)=w+c and the same conclusion is immediate. The root in (4) is the ACTUAL selected source root. For real tau and positive w it is the positive square root used to calibrate the source. For any compact path in the allowed tau strip, a sufficiently large positive w makes B(w)/w^2 uniformly close to one. Its continuation remains the root with (5), so the same calibration holds at the end of the path. Equality then extends through the connected physical w-sector. No pointwise principal square root of B is substituted for this continued root. ## 3. The selected momentum and action are globally single-chart The actual selected source multiplier is Y=exp(Phi_nu)=(s+i r)^2/V=(s+i r)/(s-i r). (7) The last equality uses V=s^2+B. Its two factors do not vanish on the physical domain because V is nonzero. Since s>0, the last expression is an injective Möbius function of r. Equations (6),(7) prove that Y is injective on each physical w-sector. If two marked lambda values in (1) agree, their exponentials Y agree. They therefore have the same w, and the marked strip then gives the same y. The map (2) is thus globally injective. Its Jacobian F_yy is everywhere nonzero by the local theorem. The holomorphic inverse theorem supplies local holomorphic inverses; injectivity makes them agree on overlaps. This proves the stated biholomorphism onto D_xi and the single-valued Legendre action. This is a global coordinate result for the ALREADY selected ordinary action. It does not choose a different source sheet, complexify the actual integer channel, or turn the coefficient label into an available complex finite-source variable. The real integer coefficient rate, exceptional block, partner normals and global period questions keep the scopes of their separate theorems. Focused audit: [reflection and momentum injectivity identities](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_global_fourier_legendre_chart.py). Primary-agent full analytical review: PASS. The reader checked the complementary convex cone, normalized slit root, reflection sign, injective root and Möbius momentum, source calibration along complex tau paths, marked exponential strip and global inverse onto its image. Independent full analytical review and fresh focused audit: PASS. A second reader checked the same proof, including repeated roots and xi=1/2, and reproduced the three exact algebraic identities. Both reviews retain the open-image scope and infer no finite complex-index coefficient theorem or contributing global source cycle.

title: The selected Fourier action has a nonsingular holomorphic Legendre chart
text: # The selected Fourier action has a nonsingular holomorphic Legendre chart 30 October 2026. The actual selected ordinary q-Hahn action admits a local holomorphic Legendre change at EVERY point of the full strict physical tube. Restoring the exact coefficient phase recovers the original magnetic coordinate and action. This is a theorem about the selected classical action. It does not continue a finite coefficient index away from its integer lattice or prove a source integration-cycle statement. ## 1. The actual source fixes the additive phase Fix a real channel parameter 0<xi<=1/2. Use the selected holomorphic action Phi_xi(tau,nu) of the [full physical packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md), on P={1/2<Re tau<1, 0<Re nu<Re tau}. The actual finite channel remains an integer j, with j/N tending to xi. No complex finite-channel interpretation is made here. Put y=2pi i(nu-tau/2), w=exp(y), C=cos(pi xi), s=sin(pi xi), c=-cos(pi tau). The image O of P in (tau,y) coordinates is convex. On a real radial slice, tau and y are real, and the source polynomial P_(t,j)(w) is positive when its actual complete support t+j>=d is imposed. The finite source identity, including its scalar, is fhat_j(N nu)=q^[(d-2j)N nu] c_(t,j) P_(t,j)(exp y), c_(t,j)=q^[j(t+j-d)]/(Q;Q)_j, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1. (1) Use the original product logarithm (Q;Q)_j=(-i)^j q^[j(j+1)/2] s_j, s_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N). At nu=t/(2N)-iy/(2pi), with real y, the exact argument supplied by the prefactors of (1) is pi[d(t-j)+j^2]/(2N), (2) independent of y. This is a marked product logarithm, not a principal argument chosen anew after reducing (2) modulo 2pi. Dividing its logarithm by N yields the absolute phase C_0(tau,xi)=i pi(tau-xi+xi^2)/2. (3) Consequently define on O F_xi(tau,y)=J(xi)+(xi-1/2)y +Phi_xi(tau,tau/2-iy/(2pi))-C_0(tau,xi). (4) On the real complete radial slice this is precisely the REAL positive-polynomial action in the [coefficient variational theorem](actual_q_hahn_fourier_coefficient_variational.md). The constant and linear terms in (4) are fixed by (1), not by an arbitrary integration constant. Formula (4) also defines its holomorphic continuation in tau and y. Throughout this note xi is a fixed real parameter. ## 2. The Legendre derivative has no critical point on O Write B=w^2+2cw+C^2, V=w^2+2cw+1. The selected square root of B is continued from its positive value on the real radial slice. The full packet proves B and V nonzero: they are w^2 times its two nonzero characteristic factors. Since O is convex, the selected square root is globally defined there. The selected source multiplier has the exact expression Y=exp(Phi_nu)=(s+i sqrt(B))^2/V. (5) This retains the continued root. It does not assert that sqrt(B) is pointwise principal outside the real slice. Differentiating (4),(5) on that slice and continuing the identity gives F_y=xi-1/2+Phi_nu/(2pi i), F_yy=s w(w+c)/(pi sqrt(B) V). (6) The only possible new zero in the second line is w+c=0. It is AUTOMATICALLY excluded by the strict physical domain. Indeed put T=exp(2pi i tau), U=exp(2pi i nu). Then w+c=0 is equivalent to U=(1+T)/2. The principal argument of T is theta=2pi(Re tau-1), strictly between -pi and 0. The argument of the positive sum 1+T lies strictly between theta and 0, for every |T|>0. But an allowed physical U has its argument lift in (0,2pi Re tau); its principal argument is either in (0,pi] or in (-pi,theta). It cannot equal that of (1+T)/2. Because s>0, w!=0, B!=0 and V!=0, equation (6) proves F_yy never vanishes on O. (7) This includes the endpoint xi=1/2. The real radial curvature is positive, but the proof of (7) uses the full complex physical domain, not positivity of a complex Hessian. ## 3. Local action transport with its exact phase Let lambda=F_y. By (7), (tau,y)->(tau,lambda) is locally biholomorphic at EVERY point of O. In each such chart define L_xi(tau,lambda)=F_xi(tau,y)-lambda y. (8) These are local Legendre charts on the marked action graph. No global injectivity of the projection to (tau,lambda) is asserted. They satisfy L_lambda=-y, L_lambdalambda=-1/F_yy, lambda=xi-1/2+Phi_nu/(2pi i), L_tau=Phi_tau+pi i(lambda-xi). (9) On real complete radial parameters and 0<lambda<xi, this L is the actual coefficient rate already proved. At other complex lambda it is an analytic ACTION chart, not yet an asymptotic formula for individual finite Fourier coefficients. For an arbitrary physical nu in the same local chart, consider H(tau,nu;lambda)=L_xi(tau,lambda) +2pi i(lambda+1/2-xi)(nu-tau/2). (10) Stationarity in lambda gives y=2pi i(nu-tau/2). (11) Substitution of (4),(8) then yields the exact critical-value identity H_crit=J(xi)+Phi_xi(tau,nu)-C_0(tau,xi). (12) The original prefactor contributes -J(xi)+C_0(tau,xi), by (1), and therefore restores precisely Phi. In particular no discarded quadratic phase has to be guessed from a Hessian or a volume value. Differentiation of (12) also preserves the original magnetic momentum and the tau momentum; the latter includes the explicit shift in (9). ## 4. Actual affine cycle coordinates and retained characters At a vertex of the exact shared-cycle compiler, let u_v=epsilon_v x_c+B_v, b_v=max(0,T_i-d), t_i=min(T_i,2d-T_i), delta_v=(B_v-b_v)/N-t_i/(2N), X_c=x_c/N. The normalized magnetic coordinate is nu_v=epsilon_v X_c+(B_v-b_v)/N. The exact finite coefficient phase contains the linear term 2pi i(lambda_v+1/2-xi_i)(delta_v+epsilon_v X_c), up to the explicitly retained finite d/N correction. Thus its classical lambda equation is (11), with y_v=2pi i(delta_v+epsilon_v X_c). It recovers the ORIGINAL coordinate nu_v, with either actual degree adapter and the original white-map reversal. It does not force the new y_v to be real. This is the precise action-level distinction from the [all-radial obstruction](actual_positive_fourier_radial_geometric_obstruction.md). For a closed physical cycle, the exact coefficient constraint is sum_v epsilon_v(lambda_v+1/2-xi_i) +(1/2)sum_b epsilon_b =n_c+(b_c+E_c/2)/N. (13) The original marked charge b_c, finite pivotal shift E_c/2 and the integer Fourier winding n_c remain specified. In a leading stationary action the multiplier includes the term -2pi i n_c X_c. It must remain in a critical-value calculation. Likewise a factor (-1)^a has its original product logarithm; replacing it by another logarithm differing by 2pi i a is invisible on integer colors but changes a continued action character. The local identity (12) does not authorize either omission. ## 5. The remaining quantum statement is separate This theorem gives an everywhere nonsingular LOCAL selected-action change for ordinary physical factors. It explains how restoring the exact phase permits nonradial magnetic critical coordinates; it does not construct their finite coefficient asymptotics, select a contributing global period, bound a complementary contraction, or prove that complex critical contributions survive. Completed partner normals and the exceptional four-port block retain their previous scope. In particular, the finite positive coefficient theorem still concerns actual integer indices and real complete parameters with interior slopes. Holomorphic action transport alone cannot replace the missing analytic statement about those coefficients or the full source cycle. Focused audit: [source prefactor and Legendre derivative identities](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_holomorphic_fourier_legendre_transport.py). Primary-agent full analytical review: PASS. The reader recomputed the finite product phase and absolute constant, both derivative shifts, critical-value restoration, exclusion of the caustic on the full tube, and exact winding and finite charge terms. Both actual degree adapters and the white-map reversal retain their original scope. Independent full analytical review and fresh audit: PASS. A second reader checked the same source-normalized action identities and the continued square-root convention, and reproduced the five exact audit identities. Neither review infers complex finite coefficient indices, global injectivity from the local argument, or a contributing source cycle.

title: An exact accretive determinant for the joint magnetic source
text: # An exact accretive determinant for the joint magnetic source 30 October 2026. The finite rational continuation specified in [the magnetic corridor note](actual_q_hahn_magnetic_complex_corridor.md), section 6, has an exact tridiagonal determinant. Its Hermitian part is positive on a joint complex domain in the pair degree and the magnetic coordinate.
