This proves joint zero exclusion and uniform logarithmic derivative bounds for the ORIGINAL finite source, including both parities, composite levels and the folded channel endpoint. The domain is a central wedge; it is smaller than the fixed-real-degree strip. No global source cycle, magnetic stationary point, or volume limit is selected by this theorem. ## 1. The exact finite source, including its scalar Put d=N-1, theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), Q=q^2, x=q^d and 0<=j<=floor(d/2). Gaussian binomials below have base Q. The source is fhat_j(u,v)=x^u H_j(U,V)/D_j(UV), U=Q^u, V=Q^v, T=UV=Q^t, t=u+v, D_j(T)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)(T-Q^r), H_j(U,V)=sum_(a=0)^j [j choose a]_Q^2 q^[a(a-d)] V^a product_(r=0)^(a-1)(U-Q^r) product_(r=0)^(j-a-1)(V-Q^r). (1) All exponential powers use these displayed logarithms. At physical integer u,v this is the original normalized complete-circle column; (1) also specifies its continuation, without interpolating samples. Set S_j(U,T)=U^j H_j(U,T/U). Since q^[a(a-d)]=(-1)^a Q^[a(a+1)/2], this is the polynomial S_j(U,T)=sum_(a=0)^j (-1)^a Q^[a(a+1)/2] [j choose a]_Q^2 T^a product_(r=0)^(a-1)(U-Q^r) product_(r=0)^(j-a-1)(T-UQ^r). (2) It has degree at most j separately in U and T. Two exact evaluations are S_j(U,0)=(-1)^j Q^[j(j-1)/2] U^j, S_j(0,T)=T^j [2j choose j]_Q. (3) For the second, the finite coefficient identity sum_a Q^(a^2)[j choose a]_Q^2=[2j choose j]_Q follows by comparing z^j in product_(r=0)^(2j-1)(1+Q^r z), split into its two j-factor blocks. All scalar factors in (3) are nonzero: 2j<N. ## 2. A joint Casimir identity, proved before continuation The exact polynomial identity is -Q^(-j)(U-T)(1-QU) S_j(QU,T) -Q^j(U-QT)(1-U) S_j(U/Q,T) +[2(1+QT)U-(1+Q)U^2 -T(Q^(j+1)+Q^(-j))] S_j(U,T)=0. (4) Here is a finite proof which does not extend an integer-t recurrence without justification. For the j+1 original complete slices T=Q^(d-j),...,Q^d, the exact physical Casimir equation gives (4). The entire-U equation on each slice is already proved in section 4 of the magnetic corridor note: its leading U^(j+2) coefficient cancels, and its U=0 value and all original t+1 column nodes make the remaining polynomial of degree at most j+1 vanish. This includes t=d-j=j when N is odd and the channel is maximal. The left side of (4) has degree at most j+1 in T. At T=0, substitute the first identity in (3); the remaining factor is -U(1-QU)-U(1-U)+2U-(1+Q)U^2=0. The j+1 distinct nonzero complete slices and T=0 are j+2 distinct zeros, so (4) holds identically in T and U. This argument proves the complex-degree source identity at every admissible N directly. The focused audit also verifies (4) coefficientwise at formal Q for j=2 through 6; the proof does not depend on those checks. Write c=-cos((t+1)theta), P_j(z;c)=S_j(q^t z,Q^t)/[Q^(jt) [2j choose j]_Q]. (5) The constant coefficient is 1. Substitution into (4), followed by coefficient comparison, gives, with p_(j,-1)=0 and p_(j,0)=1, sin(k theta) sin((2j+1-k)theta) p_(j,k) =2c sin^2((j+1-k)theta) p_(j,k-1) +sin((j+2-k)theta) sin((j+1-k)theta) p_(j,k-2). (6) All denominators for 1<=k<=j are positive. Thus this identity determines P_j for every complex t, not only for physical slices. Define the monic reverse polynomial R_j(z;c)=z^j P_j(1/z;c). Equation (1) is exactly fhat_j(u,t-u)=x^u q^(jt) [2j choose j]_Q R_j(q^t/U;c)/D_j(Q^t). (7) In particular no root-dependent normalization is discarded. ## 3. The ordinary three-term recurrence For 1<=n<floor(d/2), put B_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. (8) The recurrence is R_0=1, R_1=z+c/cos(theta), R_(n+1)=[z+c/(cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta))]R_n +B_n[cos^2(n theta)-c^2]R_(n-1). (9) We prove that no lower-degree terms are hidden in (9). Set [r]=sin(r theta)/sin(theta) and D_q z^r=[r]z^(r-1). Equation (6) is equivalent to L_c R_n=[n][n+1]R_n, L_c=D_q ((z^2+2cz+1)D_q). (10) Indeed L_c z^r=[r][r+1]z^r+2c[r]^2z^(r-1)+[r][r-1]z^(r-2). The eigenvalues for n=0,...,J, J=floor(d/2), are distinct: their successive differences are [2n]>0. Define finite moments mu_0=1, mu_(-1)=0, and [r+1]mu_r+2c[r]mu_(r-1)+[r-1]mu_(r-2)=0 (1<=r<=2J-1). (11) No denominator vanishes, since 2J<N. On available degrees let <z^m,z^n>=mu_(m+n). The difference <z^m,L_c z^n>-<L_c z^m,z^n> is [n-m] times the left side of (11) at r=m+n, by the elementary sine addition identities. Thus the R_n are pairwise orthogonal whenever the requisite total degree is at most 2J-1. Inductively assume the lower norms are nonzero for generic c. In the expansion of zR_n-R_(n+1), pairing with R_k, k<=n-2, kills every coefficient below R_(n-1), since multiplication by z is symmetric. The two remaining coefficients are read from the top powers. Equation (6) gives p_(n,1)=c tan(n theta)/sin(theta), p_(n,2)=[2c sin^2((n-1)theta)p_(n,1) +sin(n theta)sin((n-1)theta)] /[sin(2theta)sin((2n-1)theta)], (12) where p_(1,2)=0. Subtracting these coefficients at n and n+1 gives exactly (9). The norm identity is <R_n,R_n>=-B_n[cos^2(n theta)-c^2]<R_(n-1),R_(n-1)>. It proves the generic nonvanishing needed for the next induction step, starting at norm 1; hence there is no assumption of positivity of this auxiliary moment functional. Polynomial continuation in c then gives (9) for every c. Only moments through 2J-1 are used, including for the maximal channel. The moment functional is a proof device, not a new quantum inner product. ## 4. A positive definite real part For a chosen size j, define real j-by-j matrices D and K, with indices 0,...,j-1. Their diagonal and adjacent entries are D_(n,n)=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], D_(n-1,n)=D_(n,n-1)=sqrt(B_n), K_(n-1,n)=sqrt(B_n)cos(n theta), K_(n,n-1)=-sqrt(B_n)cos(n theta), K_(n,n)=0. (13) All other entries are zero. Thus D is symmetric and K is skew-symmetric. The tridiagonal determinant recurrence and (9) give R_j(z;c)=det(zI+cD+K). (14) Every leading principal minor of D is explicitly det D_m=2^m product_(r=1)^m sin(r theta) /product_(r=m+1)^(2m) sin(r theta)>0, 1<=m<=j. (15) To see the formula without solving a separate determinant problem, compare the leading c^m coefficient of R_m(0;c)=p_(m,m)(c) in (14). Iteration of the highest-c terms of (6) gives precisely (15). All factors are positive because 2m<N. Sylvester's criterion gives D positive definite, including when j=floor(d/2). If Re c>0, the Hermitian part of cD+K is (Re c)D>0. For any eigenvector, its eigenvalue therefore has positive real part. The zeros of R_j all lie strictly in Re z<0; reversal gives the same statement for P_j. No real-rootedness assertion is needed or made for noninteger t. For positive real c the coefficients in (6) are positive, so R_j(1;c)>0. More generally A=zI+cD+K is invertible whenever Re z>=0 and Re c>0. In the open product of right half-planes its logarithmic derivatives satisfy |partial_z log det A|<=j/Re z, |partial_c log det A|<=j/Re c. (16) The first follows from Re A>=(Re z)I and the inverse operator norm. For the second conjugate by D^(-1/2): D^(-1/2) A D^(-1/2) =zD^(-1)+cI+D^(-1/2)KD^(-1/2). Its Hermitian part is at least (Re c)I, and its inverse has trace partial_c log det A. Thus (16) uses no uniform lower eigenvalue bound for D, which could degenerate as the channel approaches 1/2. ## 5. An N-independent joint central wedge Use scaled variables tau=t/N and upsilon=u/N, retaining j as its actual integer channel. Consider the convex domain W={ (tau,upsilon) in C^2: 1/2<Re tau<1, |2Re upsilon-Re tau|<1/2 }. (17) For every admissible N and j, c=-cos(pi(tau+1/N)), z=exp(pi i(tau-2upsilon)). (18) The first has positive real part on (17): for N>=2 its cosine argument has real part strictly between pi/2 and 3pi/2. The second has positive real part by the second inequality. Also D_j(Q^t) has no zero on W. Such a zero would require tau=r/N plus an integer, with 0<=r<=j-1<N/2, contrary to 1/2<Re tau<1. Consequently the exact original finite function (7) is holomorphic and nowhere zero throughout W, simultaneously in tau and upsilon. The zero channel j=0 is the explicit nonzero exponential and needs no matrix. On every compact subset of W the quantities Re c, Re z and the separation from the denominator zeros have positive lower bounds uniformly for sufficiently large N. Equations (7), (16), and the product formula for D_j show that both first logarithmic derivatives of N^(-1)log fhat are uniformly bounded. Higher derivatives on smaller compacts follow from Cauchy's formula. Since W is convex, a logarithm is fixed by one marked base value, and normalized logarithmic ratios are locally bounded uniformly in N and j. There is a convenient exact phase normalization at a REAL center upsilon=tau/2 with 1/2<tau<1, even when t=N tau is noninteger. Here c>0 and R_j(1;c)>0. Writing each D_j factor as 2i q^(t+r)sin((t-r)theta), and using [2j choose j]_Q=q^(j^2) times a positive sine-binomial, gives Arg fhat_j(t/2,t/2)=pi[d(t-j)+j^2]/(2N). (19) This is a specified continuous argument, rather than its value modulo 2pi. Thus the joint continuation carries the same marked center phase as the original real-degree corridor. ## 6. What this removes, and what it leaves The pair degree is now genuinely complex in an exact source-defined zero-free domain. Neither integer sampling nor a formal WKB solution is used to declare that continuation. The logarithmic estimates are uniform at the folded endpoint and can support a subsequent normal family or finite-shift argument for a joint selected action. The present theorem does not assert a joint amplitude asymptotic, a globally admissible frame for an arbitrary plat, or intersection of its original cycle with the geometric critical point. In particular W is a central wedge, not the whole fixed-t magnetic strip, and simultaneous membership of all source coupons in W is an additional global question. These distinctions remain even though (14) is an exact algebraic identity. Audit: [exact joint determinant and source checks](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.py). Independent analytical review: a second reader checked the exact finite source normalization, Gaussian Vandermonde scalar, complete-slice and T=0 continuation argument, finite-moment proof with its endpoint degree bounds, three-term and determinant signs, positive principal minors, both accretive resolvent estimates, the joint domain and its poles, and the exact noninteger center phase. The proof passed. The review retains the distinction between this local joint theorem and a global source frame, asymptotic amplitude, or selected cycle. The independent fresh audit replay also passed: five formal-Q source identities, 400 coefficient recurrences, 968 determinant values, 121 principal-minor formulas, 80 nonphysical source values, nine complex pair-degree/magnetic comparisons, and three noninteger center-phase checks. A further independent analytical reader and the root reader checked the full proof and reported no defect. The exact finite theorem and its stated global limitations are unchanged.

title: The actual joint magnetic and pair-degree amplitude
text: # The actual joint magnetic and pair-degree amplitude Subsequent full-domain result: the [full strict physical packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) extends the actual ordinary amplitude and the stated small/near-fold complex bounds to fixed physical compacts, with the necessary finite-level boundary correction. The [selected-factor corollary](actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md) then selects every ordinary factor outside one prescribed matching-edge block. Global contraction and period estimates remain open. The argument below keeps its original domain and proof scope. 30 October 2026. This note continues the ORIGINAL terminating q-Hahn kernel jointly in the pair degree t and the magnetic coordinate u. The channel j remains an integer. The exact accretive determinant, the canonical center phase and two original finite-shift equations give an actual nonzero amplitude, not only a formal stationary ansatz. The domain is a central complex wedge. It is independent of N on compact subsets and includes the folded limit j/N=1/2. This is not yet a contributing-cycle or whole-source theorem for an arbitrary plat. ## 1. The source and the domain Put h=1/N, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, and x=q^d=-q^(-1). Let 1<=j<=floor(d/2), xi=j/N. The literal terminating sine-product continuation is the function fhat_j(u,v) in section 6 of [the magnetic corridor](actual_q_hahn_magnetic_complex_corridor.md). Its Gaussian-binomial coefficients, denominator and exponential prefactor are unchanged. Set t=N tau, u=N nu, v=t-u, U=exp(2pi i nu), T=exp(2pi i tau), z=exp[pi i(tau-2nu)], c_h=-cos[pi(tau+h)]. (1) Use the convex, simply connected tube D={ (tau,nu) in C^2 : 1/2<Re tau<1, |2Re nu-Re tau|<1/2 }. (2) It lies inside 0<Re nu<Re tau. On each compact subset of D, for all sufficiently large N, Re c_h>0 and Re z>0. All factors T-Q^r, 0<=r<j, are nonzero there. The channel ratio xi lies in a fixed compact subinterval of (0,1/2], with its actual value j/N used in every coefficient function below. The [exact determinant theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.md) supplies the monic polynomial R_j(z;c_h)=det(z I+c_h D_j+K_j), D_j real symmetric positive definite, K_j real skew-symmetric. (3) The letter D_j in (3) denotes the matrix, not the product denominator in the rational H_j formula. In this note write that product as Delta_j(T)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)(T-Q^r). The exact scalar normalization is fhat_j(u,t-u) =x^u q^(jt) [2j choose j]_Q R_j(z;c_h)/Delta_j(T). (4) It follows by taking the U^0 coefficient of U^j H_j(U,T/U): the finite Gaussian Vandermonde identity gives T^j[2j choose j]_Q. This identity follows by taking the middle coefficient in the product of two finite Gaussian binomial products; it has no division by [N]. Here 2j<N, so its scalar is nonzero. ## 2. A canonical joint logarithm, including its finite phase Let beta(2j,j) be the positive sine binomial. Factoring each sine in Delta_j makes (4) equivalent to fhat_j(Nnu,N(tau-nu)) =beta(2j,j) exp{pi i[d nu+(j^2-dj)/(2N)]} R_j(z;c_h)/product_(r=0)^(j-1) 2sin[pi(tau-r/N)]. (5) Every sine has positive real part on D. The matrix in (3) has positive Hermitian part when Re z,Re c_h>0, so its principal matrix logarithm exists. Define Log R_j by the trace of that matrix logarithm. This is holomorphic on the product of the two right half-planes and is real on z,c_h>0. With the positive real logarithm of beta(2j,j), equation (5) therefore specifies a holomorphic Log fhat on each fixed compact portion of D for all large N. These specifications agree on overlaps; no interpolation or sampling character is introduced. For REAL tau with 1/2<tau<1, at the noninteger center u=t/2, R_j(1;c_h) and all the sine factors are positive. The prescribed phase is exactly Im Log fhat_j(t/2,t/2) =pi[d(t-j)+j^2]/(2N). (6) In particular (6) holds between adjacent integer degrees. It fixes the possible pair-degree sampling alias as well as the magnetic one. For A=zI+cD_j+K_j, accretivity gives |partial_z Log det A|<=j/Re z, |partial_c Log det A|<=j/Re c. (7) For the second estimate conjugate by D_j^(-1/2): the resulting matrix has Hermitian part at least (Re c)I, and its c derivative is I. No lower bound for the smallest eigenvalue of D_j is needed. Consequently the estimates remain uniform at the folded limit. The explicit prefactors in (5) and (7) give locally uniform bounds for all first derivatives of G_N(tau,nu)=N^(-1)Log fhat_j(Nnu,N(tau-nu)). (8) A real complete-chamber lattice anchor bounds G_N itself. Cauchy estimates then bound every fixed holomorphic derivative on smaller compact subsets. ## 3. The actual selected joint leading action For real tau,nu with tau+xi>=1 and 0<nu<tau, the preceding real amplitude theorem has the phase Phi_xi(tau,nu)=psi_(tau,xi,nu)(w_*)+pi i nu(1-xi), w_*=exp[pi i(tau+xi-1)]. (9) Its magnetic continuation is already proved at integer t. The canonical logarithm there agrees with (5): at nu=tau/2 their prescribed phases are (6), and continuation in nu fixes the rest. The bounds in section 2 give a normal family jointly in tau and nu. For any real complete-chamber tau, choose nearby actual integer degrees t_N with |t_N/N-tau|<=1/N. The derivative bound changes G_N by O(1/N) between those degrees. On each such slice the existing magnetic theorem identifies the limit (9), with the canonical logarithm just checked. Thus every subsequential joint limit agrees with (9) on a real open set, and hence throughout the connected tube D by the holomorphic identity theorem. This proves for the WHOLE sequence, locally uniformly with all fixed derivatives, G_N(tau,nu)-Phi_(xi_N)(tau,nu) ->0, xi_N=j/N. (10) Here Phi is the resulting holomorphic continuation on D. The same subsequence argument gives uniformity for compact real channel-ratio families, including xi=1/2. The elementary characteristic equations below also make its local analytic dependence on xi explicit. There is no finite continuation of the discrete index j in this assertion. ## 4. Two source-exact finite shifts The determinant note proves the entire Casimir identity for complex T by polynomial degree: its cleared residual has T-degree at most j+1, vanishes on the j+1 complete physical slices and also at T=0. Thus the fixed-t Casimir equation is valid for the ACTUAL joint kernel. With f=fhat_j(Nnu,N(tau-nu)), it is A_+ f(tau,nu+h)+A_- f(tau,nu-h)+(D_h-C_h)f=0, (11) A_+=(U-T)(1-QU)/T, A_-=(U-QT)(1-U)/(QT), D_h=(U/T)[2(q^(-1)+qT)-(q+q^(-1))U], C_h=q J+q^(-1)J^(-1), J=exp(2pi i xi). The original normalized coproduct gives a SECOND exact identity: (1-QT)f(tau+h,nu) =x(1-U)f(tau,nu-h)+(U-QT)f(tau,nu). (12) One direct finite proof of (12) uses the Newton summands of H_j. Each summand separately satisfies (1-Q^(-j)UV)H(U,V) =(1-U)H(U/Q,V)+U(1-V)H(U,V/Q). Replace V by QV and use Delta_j(QT)/Delta_j(T)=(1-QT)/(1-Q^(1-j)T), together with the exact x^u factor. This proves (12) for the original sum. The Newton identity alone does not determine the Gaussian-squared coefficients; it is used together with (11), not as a characterization. Put a=Phi_nu, b=Phi_tau, and A=(U-T)(1-U)/T, D=2U(1+T-U)/T, H(tau,nu,a)=A(e^a+e^(-a))+D-(J+J^(-1)). (13) Passing to the limit in the ACTUAL shifted ratios gives H(tau,nu,a)=0, (1-T)e^b=(U-1)e^(-a)+U-T. (14) The first equation is simple throughout D. Indeed its discriminant, apart from nonzero factors, vanishes only if cos^2(pi xi) z^2+2c_0 z+1=0, c_0=-cos(pi tau). For Re z>0 this would require c_0=-(cos^2(pi xi)z+1/z)/2, whose real part is negative, contrary to Re c_0>0. The same argument includes xi=1/2. Also A!=0 and J!=1 on the stated domain. Hence H_a!=0. The second equation is simple in b, since (1-T)e^b!=0. The prescribed real-chamber values and these simple equations also give local analytic dependence on xi, including through xi=1/2. This concerns the coefficient functions of the asymptotic, not an interpolation of the finite discrete channel. ## 5. Two actual derivative bootstraps and a closed amplitude form Let a_N=partial_nu G_N and b_N=partial_tau G_N. The joint Cauchy bounds and exact finite shifts imply f(tau,nu+/-h)/f=exp(+/-a_N)[1+(h/2)partial_nu a_N+O(h^2)], f(tau+h,nu)/f=exp(b_N)[1+(h/2)partial_tau b_N+O(h^2)]. (15) All errors here and below are uniform on compact subsets, with actual xi_N used. Define A_1^+=-2pi i U(U-T)/T, A_1^-=-2pi i U(1-U)/T, D_1=2pi i U(T-1)/T, C_1=pi i(J-J^(-1)), H_1=A_1^+e^a+A_1^-e^(-a)+D_1-C_1. Equation (11), simplicity and (10) first imply a_N-a=O(h). Cauchy's estimate gives the same derivative bound. Substitution a second time then proves a_N=a+h r+O(h^2), r=-[H_1+(Phi_(nu,nu)/2)H_(a,a)]/H_a. (16) Use this in (12). Its simplicity and the already bounded derivatives first give b_N-b=O(h), and the second substitution gives b_N=b+h s+O(h^2), (17) s={ (1-U)e^(-a)[pi i+r-Phi_(nu,nu)/2] +2pi i T(e^b-1) -(1-T)e^b Phi_(tau,tau)/2 }/[(1-T)e^b]. No logarithmic alias is introduced when solving these equations: a_N and b_N already converge to the prescribed derivatives in (10). The holomorphic one-form omega=s d tau+r d nu (18) is closed. To see this directly, use the equality of the mixed derivatives of the ACTUAL G_N in (16)--(17), and Cauchy bounds for the O(h^2) remainders. It gives partial_tau r-partial_nu s=O(h). Take sequences of admissible xi_N tending to any fixed xi; the coefficient functions are continuous, so that difference is exactly zero. This proves closedness without assuming a formal transport solution equals the finite source. On the simply connected tube D there is therefore a nonzero holomorphic B_xi with d Log B_xi=omega. Fix its constant by the known real physical amplitude at a strict real complete-chamber point, for example tau=1-xi/2, nu=tau/2. Nearby actual lattice samples supply the same normalization to relative error O(h). Integrate (16)--(17) from such a sample along compact paths in D. The gradient of Log f-N Phi+(1/2)log N-Log B is O(h), and its initial value is O(h), choosing the logarithm of its near-one ratio at that sample. Thus the ACTUAL original kernel satisfies fhat_j(Nnu,N(tau-nu)) =N^(-1/2) B_(xi_N)(tau,nu) exp[N Phi_(xi_N)(tau,nu)](1+O(N^(-1))). (19) The relative error has the same bound under each fixed derivative on smaller compact subsets. This proves the joint complex amplitude, including arbitrary O(1/N) noninteger shifts of t, fixed complex scaled displacements, both level parities and composite levels. Near the original physical real chamber, comparison with the prior amplitude theorem identifies the coefficient with B_xi(tau,nu)=Acal_(tau,xi,nu)(w_*) exp[pi i(alpha_(tau,xi,nu)(w_*)-nu)]. (20) Both integer offsets are retained. Formula (18) continues (20) wherever a particular internal-saddle coordinate ceases to be a convenient chart. It does not redefine the finite kernel. ## 6. What this removes from the general problem Pair degree and magnetic coordinate may now vary together in a uniform complex central domain. A finite product of these ordinary column factors, composed with the actual affine wire maps of a fixed plat, has the corresponding joint estimate on any compact common preimage of D. The number of factors is fixed with the diagram, so the relative errors still multiply to 1+O(1/N). This statement does not itself place the geometric critical point in that domain, match its sheet to the selected one, choose a contributing physical cycle, or estimate a coherent sum over wires and channels. It also does not continue the discrete channel j or bound new generic-q normal currents. Those remain explicit tasks in the general original-source volume conjecture. ## 7. An explicit algebraic test for the selected local sheet The preceding continuation has a useful exact branch description. Put s=sin(pi xi), C=cos(pi xi), c_0=-cos(pi tau), W=1+2c_0 z+C^2 z^2, V=1+2c_0 z+z^2. (21) Both W/z and V/z have positive real part when Re c_0,Re z>0. Their arguments and the argument of z lie in (-pi/2,pi/2), so W and V avoid the nonpositive real axis. In particular the PRINCIPAL square root sqrt(W) is holomorphic and has positive real part. The actual selected magnetic multiplier is Y=exp(Phi_nu)=(s z+i sqrt(W))^2/V. (22) To prove this, substitute U=exp(pi i tau)/z into (13). It gives Y+Y^(-1)=2-4W/V. The two solutions are (s z+/-i sqrt(W))^2/V. Their numerators are nonzero, since a zero would force V=0; the two solutions are distinct. At a real center c_0>0,z=1, the actual canonical derivative has imaginary part strictly between 0 and pi, fixing the plus sign. Holomorphic continuation on D then proves (22) everywhere. This also includes the folded endpoint C=0. Suppose a candidate marked geometric multiplier Y_geo satisfies the same characteristic equation at a point of D. Then r_geo=[V Y_geo-s^2 z^2+W]/(2i s z), r_geo^2=W. (23) Consequently it belongs to the source-selected local sheet if and only if Re r_geo>0. This is a strict algebraic inequality after the already selected peripheral square roots in z,c_0 are retained. It is a checkable additional condition on a geometric candidate, not a proof that every coupon of a general plat satisfies it in one common frame. The contributing-cycle problem remains separate. Audit: [the original joint source, both shifts and amplitudes](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.py). The primary reader's fresh run and an independent fresh replay passed. The finite comparisons test the normalization and correction formulas; sections 2--5 supply the uniform analytical proof. Independent source-transport review: full analytical read PASS. The reviewer checked the exact scalar and principal matrix-logarithm normalization, noninteger center phase, joint normal-family selection, both original finite shifts, discriminant exclusion throughout the central wedge, both subleading gradient corrections, closed amplitude form, and the normalized lattice anchor including +(1/2)log N. The review retains the integer-channel hypothesis and does not infer a contributing global cycle or a bound on an assembled coherent sum. Fresh independent 160-digit audit replay also PASS: 476 exact off-lattice coproduct identities, 32 independent terminating-source/ determinant comparisons, 32 joint amplitude calibrations and eight actual folded-channel gradient corrections. The maximum scaled relative error was 0.476 and the maximum N-squared gradient remainder was 0.407; these finite checks confirm the conventions, while the written argument supplies the uniform theorem. Independent analytical review: a second reader checked the exact source-to-sine normalization and canonical matrix logarithm, joint normal-family selection using nearby physical degrees and the marked center phase, simplicity on the full central tube including xi=1/2, and both source-exact finite shifts. The two subprincipal corrections were independently expanded with their signs and integer offsets. The review also checked Cauchy control of their remainders, closedness from the actual mixed derivatives, and normalization at moving lattice samples before integration. The proof passed. This review does not supply a common physical frame, selected whole-source cycle, or continuation of the discrete channel. The explicit selected-sheet formula in section 7 received a separate independent analytical review. Its characteristic equation and recovered square root were checked by two formal polynomial identities, and four complex saddle comparisons distinguished the selected and opposite signs. Those additional focused checks passed; no global sheet or cycle assertion was added.

title: A joint complex packet in the deficient geometric chamber
