text: # A joint complex packet in the deficient geometric chamber 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. The actual monic q-Hahn numerator has an N-independent joint complex-degree and magnetic corridor around the real deficient frame. Both its selected root amplitude and its genuine generic-q numerator derivatives are controlled there. The proof uses the original finite determinant, an explicitly bounded low block, and a positive tail matrix. This does not continue the full exceptional operator's generic boundary factors or select a nonzero global period. The original forbidden integer-degree slices remain identically zero. ## 1. The finite determinant and the joint domain Fix 0<sigma_*<kappa<alpha_0<1/2. Put theta=pi/N, a/N=alpha in [alpha_0,1/2], with the actual integer channel 0<=a<=floor((N-1)/2). The degree t=N sigma may be complex. Use the ORIGINAL root monic numerator R_a(z;c) from the joint source theorem, with c=-cos(pi(sigma+1/N)), C=-c, d_n=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], b_n=sin(n theta)/[cos(n theta) sqrt(sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta))]. (1) Its exact recurrence is R_0=1, R_1=z-C d_0, R_(n+1)=(z-C d_n)R_n -b_n^2[C^2-cos^2(n theta)]R_(n-1). (2) No physical integer-degree assumption is used in (2): it is the already proved polynomial identity for the literal finite Newton numerator, for every complex degree. For each fixed sufficiently small angle vartheta>0 there are epsilon>0 and R>1, independent of N and a, such that R_a has no zeros on the PRODUCT domain |sigma-sigma_*|<epsilon, Omega_R={z: |z|>R, vartheta<Arg z<2pi-vartheta}. (3) Here Arg is the logarithm cut on the positive real axis. Both epsilon and R may depend on vartheta; R can be chosen O(1/sin vartheta), while epsilon can be chosen proportional to vartheta. All statements below concern sufficiently large N and fixed compact subsets of (3), uniformly in the allowed discrete channels. ## 2. A positive tail plus a bounded error Choose m=floor(kappa N), so 0<m<a for large N. In the determinant matrix with characteristic polynomial (2), take indices 0,...,m-1 as a low block. Its diagonal entries are C d_n; take its upper entries to be 1 and its lower entries to be b_n^2(C^2-cos^2(n theta)). These entries and their C derivatives are uniformly bounded. Indeed n/N<=kappa+o(1)<1/2, and b_n cos^2(n theta) =sin(2n theta)/[2 sqrt(sin((2n-1)theta) sin((2n+1)theta))]<=1. (4) The last inequality holds throughout the used range, for N>=5: sin(2n theta)>=sin(2theta), and sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta) =sin^2(2n theta)-sin^2(theta). Thus the low block J_L has operator norm at most a constant L, independent of N. On the tail m,...,a-1 choose the analytic square root sqrt(C^2-cos^2(n theta)) positive at C=cos(pi sigma_*), and take the symmetric adjacent entry b_n times this square root. All these branches exist on a fixed C disk: kappa>sigma_* separates every radicand uniformly from zero. Let D_T be the principal tail submatrix of the positive matrix whose diagonal is d_n and whose adjacent entries are b_n. Its positivity is already proved by the exact principal minors in the joint source determinant theorem. The tail matrix is EXACTLY J_T(C)=C D_T+E_T(C), (E_T)_(n-1,n)=(E_T)_(n,n-1) =-b_n cos^2(n theta) /[C+sqrt(C^2-cos^2(n theta))], (5) with zero diagonal. Formula (4) and the strict cutoff show ||E_T(C)||+||partial_C E_T(C)||<=E_0. (6) The same conclusion for every fixed C derivative follows on a slightly smaller disk. No lower eigenvalue bound for D_T, and no uniform bound on its largest eigenvalue, is required. Keep the interface upper entry equal to 1 and the lower entry gamma_m=b_m^2(C^2-cos^2(m theta)), which is uniformly bounded. The resulting tridiagonal determinant is exactly R_a by (2). This bounded nonsymmetric low block avoids choosing square roots at the moving integer-degree zero of a recurrence coefficient. If C stays in a sufficiently small disk about cos(pi sigma_*), and z is in (3), then dist(z,C[0,infinity))>=c |z| sin(vartheta). (7) The inverse of zI-C D_T therefore has norm at most the reciprocal of the right side. Choosing R sufficiently large, (6) gives the same bound, up to a factor two, for (zI-J_T)^-1. The low inverse has norm at most (|z|-L)^-1. Its Schur complement changes the tail by the rank-one matrix gamma_m [(zI-J_L)^-1]_(m-1,m-1) e_0 e_0^T. (8) Its norm is O(1/|z|). A second Neumann estimate proves that the FULL determinant is nonzero and that its displayed tridiagonal matrix M has ||M^-1||<=C_vartheta/|z|. (9) This proves (3) using the actual finite determinant, including both parities and the folded endpoint. ## 3. Joint logarithmic bounds and the source-selected amplitude Fix a negative reference z_*=-R_* with R_*>R. The product domain (3) is simply connected. Define the logarithm of R_a(z)/R_a(z_*) to be zero at z_*, for every sigma. Then |partial_z Log R_a|+|partial_sigma Log R_a|<=C_K N (10) on each fixed compact K, with analogous normalized higher derivative bounds on smaller compacts. For completeness the large D_T causes no loss in (10). The Schur tail is S=zI-C D_T-E_T-gamma e_0e_0^T, with gamma the bounded expression in (8), and C S^-1 D_T=z S^-1-I-S^-1 E_T -gamma S^-1 e_0e_0^T. (11) Thus its trace against a C derivative is O(N) by (6),(9). The low-block derivative is bounded; gamma and its derivatives are bounded by the low resolvent formula. This proves (10). There are functions S_(sigma,alpha)(z), A_(sigma,alpha)(z), holomorphic jointly in sigma and z on (3), with S(z_*)=0, A(z_*)=1 and A nowhere zero, such that R_a(z;c)/R_a(z_*;c) =A_(sigma,alpha)(z) exp[N S_(sigma,alpha)(z)] (1+O(N^-1)). (12) The error and its fixed derivatives are uniform on compacts. The phase and amplitude depend smoothly on the real channel parameter alpha, which always remains the ACTUAL a/N. The anchor is selected by an exact source identity, not by a choice of an algebraic root. For every complex sigma put t_hi=N(1-sigma)-2, u_hi=t_hi/2+iN log(R_*)/(2pi), beta_a=s_(2a)/s_a^2. The reflection R_a(z;-c)=(-1)^a R_a(-z;c) and the original ordinary normalization give exactly R_a(-R_*;c)=(-1)^a beta_a^-1 product_(r=0)^(a-1)2sin(pi(t_hi-r)/N) *q^[-(N-1)u_hi-(a^2-(N-1)a)/2] *fhat_a(t_hi,u_hi). (13) This is in the already proved JOINT high-degree physical packet: Re(t_hi/N)>1/2, its real magnetic coordinate is centered, and the complete-channel margins follow from alpha_0>sigma_*. Its two wire coordinates remain strictly inside their domains for a small fixed complex sigma disk. The offset -2, the actual half-integer center when present, and every phase in (13) remain literal. All sine factors have a fixed distance from their zeros. Consequently (13) supplies a nonzero relative absolute anchor, jointly in sigma, by that ordinary packet and an elementary finite-product Euler--Maclaurin estimate. It also does so on an open interval of negative z around z_*. The bounds (10) give a normal family for the normalized logarithms. Every limit agrees on that negative interval with the anchor's source-selected leading phase. The identity theorem fixes it on Omega_R, for each complex sigma; compactness makes convergence uniform jointly in sigma and the real parameter alpha. There is no interpolation from integer degree samples in this argument. Here are explicit transport equations proving the relative error. Put D=z partial_z, kappa_q=2pi i, U=exp(pi i sigma)/z, T=exp(2pi i sigma), J=exp(2pi i alpha). The original finite numerator satisfies the exact root equation (QU-1)(U-T)R(z/Q)+(QT-U)(1-U)R(Qz) +[2U+2QTU-(1+Q)U^2-T(Q^-a+Q^(a+1))]R(z)=0. (14) Set A0=(U-1)(U-T), C0=2U(1+T-U)-T(J+J^-1) and H(p,z)=A0(e^(kappa_q p)+e^(-kappa_q p))+C0. The selected p=D S satisfies H=0. Its discriminant is C0^2-4A0^2=-16T^2 sin^2(pi alpha) W/z^2, W=1-2cos(pi sigma)z+cos^2(pi alpha)z^2. (15) All roots of W remain in the excluded small positive sector. Indeed write C_s=cos(pi sigma), b=cos(pi alpha), and use the analytic sqrt(C_s^2-b^2) positive at the real center. The roots are 1/(C_s+sqrt(C_s^2-b^2)) and (C_s+sqrt(C_s^2-b^2))/b^2, with the second omitted at b=0. The gap alpha_0>sigma_* gives uniform branches and a uniform argument bound, even as b tends to zero. Shrink epsilon if necessary. Also A0 has zeros only near the unit circle, outside Omega_R. Hence H_p is nonzero throughout the domain. The exact first transport term is H1=kappa_q[U(U-T)e^(-kappa_q p) +T(1-U)e^(kappa_q p)+2TU-U^2-TJ], rho=-(H1+(D p)H_(p,p)/2)/H_p. (16) Larger-compact Cauchy bounds, the exact shifts in (14), and the proved actual leading convergence first give p_N-p=O(N^-1), where p_N=D(N^-1 Log R_a). A second substitution then gives p_N=p+rho/N+O(N^-2), uniformly jointly in sigma and z. Define D Log A=rho and A(z_*)=1 and integrate along compact paths from z_*. This proves (12), including fixed derivatives. It is the actual finite-shift bootstrap, not a formal WKB choice. ## 4. Genuine generic-q numerator normals Now use the original generic recurrence with B=Q^-N, not the root-only recurrence (2). Hold t=N sigma and a fixed while q=q0 exp(epsilon_q) varies. A marked magnetic lift u is also held fixed, with |u|<=C N and z(q)=q^(t-2u). Assume its root parameters lie in a compact subset of (3). Then |partial_(epsilon_q)^r R_a(q;t,z(q))|_0 <=C_r N^(10r) |R_a(q0;t,z(q0))|. (17) The same estimate applies to the original unnormalized Newton numerator after retaining its exact K_a and monomial factors. The bounded marked lift is necessary: u->u+NL leaves the root coordinate unchanged but changes its genuine q derivatives. To prove (17), first conjugate the root matrix above by the diagonal unitary with entries (-1)^n, so its offdiagonal signs are positive in the following convention. Its inverse bound (9) is unchanged. In the low block and at the interface freeze the upper entries at 1. In the tail freeze each upper entry at its ROOT complex value b_n sqrt(C^2-cos^2(n theta)); it is bounded away from zero. Set every generic lower entry to minus the actual generic recurrence coefficient beta_n divided by that frozen upper entry. The diagonals use the actual generic alpha_n. This determinant is exactly the original generic R_a. The previously proved generic recurrence estimates, with t/N in a fixed complex compact, give |alpha_n'|<=C N^5 and |beta_n'|<=C N^7 on the required small generic disk. The same bounds follow directly by differentiating their finite rational formulas: the only small denominators are the original spectral gaps, while q^t and its marked derivatives have bounded scaled parameters. Thus the matrix changes by at most C N^7 |epsilon_q|; z(q) changes by O(N|epsilon_q|). By (9), on |epsilon_q|<=c N^-10 the determinant ratio and its inverse are bounded, since its dimension is at most N. Cauchy's formula gives (17). The original K_a and monomials are controlled on this same disk by their finite root-unit products. No derivative of a root-only reflection is used. ## 5. The actual geometric chart and the remaining period The real-deficient-frame theorem has sigma_*=1/6. Its two determinant arguments have |z| asymptotic to a positive constant times X^2 and imaginary parts of opposite sign, each comparable to X, with X arbitrarily large. Keep the midpoint in a compact subinterval of its allowed range. Choose vartheta proportional to 1/X and then X sufficiently large. The proof above needs only R=O(1/sin vartheta)=O(X), so BOTH actual arguments lie strictly in (3). A small fixed complex neighborhood of this chosen geometric frame, or a fixed compact family around it, is therefore covered. One fixed vartheta does not cover the entire unbounded X-family, whose arguments approach the cut. The negative-real anchor in (13) is exactly the reflected source branch calibrated in that framing theorem. At the folded limit its magnetic characteristic is Y=(z-i sqrt(1-2cos(pi/6)z))^2 /[1-2cos(pi/6)z+z^2], (18) with the square root continued from positive values at negative z through the upper or lower half-plane respectively. The two values agree with the actual input/output geometric momenta, including the output's C^-1 disk shift. This comparison uses the proved anchor and corridor, not arbitrary root selection. The entire completed root kernel is a residual sine product times two such R polynomials. In this deficient corridor the residual sine arguments, after removing their recorded integer sign, lie in a strict zero-free strip because alpha>Re sigma by a fixed margin. Thus its exact product and (12),(13) give a nonzero joint ROOT packet, including complex degree, in a neighborhood of the actual geometric frame. At a maximal folded channel the residual product remains empty or one factor as specified by the exact source, so both level parities are kept. The normal estimate (17) is for the ORIGINAL q-Hahn numerators. The full exceptional generic operator still has its unspecialized boundary factors and requires its own lift; it cannot be obtained by varying q in the canceled root kernel. In particular, an actual large-partner column cannot be replaced by the small-channel numerator in (17) solely because their root values coincide; their genuine generic derivatives are different. Most importantly, the complete fixed forbidden integer-separation physical slice is identically zero. Its magnetic deformation alone must retain that zero. Joint degree analysis now has a local analytic input, but no degree contour, nonzero global coefficient, complementary source gap, or general volume equality has been proved here. Focused audit: [original joint numerator, tail determinant and selected amplitude](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_joint_deficient_degree_packet.py). It checks 248 independent-degree original four-jet identities, 124 exact finite-shift equations, 72 determinant and Schur identities, 24 positive tail matrices and 586 endpoint coefficient bounds. At 120 digits, 12 literal reflected high anchors, 24 joint complex amplitudes and 72 genuine numerator checks pass. The finite matrix and asymptotic samples remain diagnostics; the uniform estimates are proved above. Primary-agent full analytical review: PASS. The reader checked the exact determinant, bounded tail correction through the folded endpoint, Schur inverse and logarithmic trace bounds, joint reflected anchor with its -2 offset, both finite-shift orders, genuine small numerator normal disk and the finite-X geometric coverage. The full generic operator and selected degree period remain open. Independent geometric and analytical review: PASS. A second reader checked the positive-tail argument, joint high anchor, marked geometric upper/lower branches and finite-X neighborhood, including the residual sine strip. The small/large generic partner distinction and the exact zero-slice limitation are retained. Independent source and analytic review with fresh audit replay: PASS. A third reader checked the original recurrence and both finite-shift orders, the exact joint reflected anchor, the determinant perturbation with bounded marked lifts, and all source-normalization limitations. Its redirected replay reproduced all 248/124 exact source/shift checks, 72 determinant/Schur checks, 24 positive tails, 586 coefficient checks, 12 literal anchors, 24 amplitudes and 72 genuine numerator checks.

title: The actual magnetic polynomial and its complex corridor
status: Complex magnetic corridor; fixed degree and channel
text: # The actual magnetic polynomial and its complex corridor Subsequent joint extension: the [accretive determinant](actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.md) and [joint amplitude theorem](actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md) now allow pair degree and magnetic coordinate to vary together on a central complex domain. The channel remains discrete. The theorem below keeps its larger fixed-degree magnetic strip; its original review scope records the state before that subsequent extension. 30 October 2026. This note concerns the original complete-circle column, at fixed integer pair degree t and channel j. Its finite continuation in the magnetic coordinate u is specified by its terminating factorial sum, not chosen from an interpolation class. An exact coproduct recurrence places every zero outside the physical magnetic strip. The original Casimir difference equation then upgrades the real magnetic amplitude theorem to a complex corridor in u/N. The continuation keeps t and j REAL and discrete. It is not a joint continuation in all magnetic/channel variables of an assembled plat. In particular it does not choose the global source integration cycle. ## 1. A literal finite continuation, with all prefactors Write d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, and assume the actual complete-circle inequalities d-j<=t<=d, 0<=j<=floor(d/2). For a nonnegative integer a define the entire function beta(z,a)=product_(r=0)^(a-1) 2sin(pi(z-r)/N) / s_a, s_a=product_(r=1)^a 2sin(pi r/N). The ORIGINAL continuation is the finite sum fhat_(N,t,j)(u)=exp(pi i u) q^[-(j+1)u] sum_(a=0)^j q^[(t+j-d)a] beta(j,a) beta(u,a) beta(t-u,j-a)/beta(t,j). (1) All exponential powers in (1) use their displayed logarithms. At an integer 0<=u<=t, a term outside the original support vanishes because one of its numerator sine factors is zero. Thus (1) is EXACTLY the physical Casimir column, including its original scalar and phase. Off that lattice those terms are retained; no fictitious support truncation is made. Put U=Q^u and T=Q^t. There is a polynomial G_t of degree at most j with fhat_(N,t,j)(u)=x^u U^(-j) G_t(U), G_t(1)=1. (2) An explicit polynomial, with m=j-a and w=q^(t+j-d), is G_t(U)=i^(-j)s_j/beta(t,j) sum_(a=0)^j w^a q^[-mt-(a(a-1)+m(m-1))/2] product_(r=0)^(a-1)(U-Q^r) product_(r=0)^(m-1)(T-UQ^r) / (s_a^2 s_m^2). (3) Indeed each first product in the sine expression contributes i^(-a)q^[-au-a(a-1)/2], and the second contributes i^(-m)q^[-mt-mu-m(m-1)/2]. Their common u factor is q^(-ju). This proves (2)--(3), including the degree, rather than inferring an interpolation from its values. ## 2. The original coproduct proves the root factorization Keep N and j fixed and let t range from d-j to d. The actual divided coproduct F, normalized by the first component, gives G_(t+1)(U)=[Q^j(1-U)G_t(U/Q) +(U-Q^(t+1))G_t(U)]/(1-Q^(t+1)). (4) To check its normalization directly, the unnormalized component at degree t+1 is (1-Q^u) f_t(u-1)+q^(-d+2u)(1-Q^(t+1-u))f_t(u). Its u=0 value is x^(-1)(1-Q^(t+1)). Dividing by this value and using (2) gives (4). The term of degree j+1 cancels, so its right side is again a polynomial of degree at most j. Equality on the t+2 original physical nodes proves the polynomial identity as well. At t=d-j the actual highest vector gives the exact base G_(d-j)(U)=(UQ;Q)_j/(Q;Q)_j. (5) For example its u-th component is (-1)^u q^[-(2j+1)u](Q^(u+1);Q)_j/(Q;Q)_j, directly from the original highest-vector equation. There are d-j+1>=j+1 physical nodes, so this determines the degree-j polynomial in (5). Set h=d-t and n=j-h=t+j-d. Define B_h(z)=product_(r=0)^(h-1)(1+q^(h-1-2r)z). Its coefficients are the positive sine binomials beta(h,a). Equations (4)--(5) prove the factorization G_t(q^t z)=c_t B_h(z) A_n(z), c_t=q^(jn)/(Q;Q)_j, A_0=1. (6) Here A_n is a real polynomial of degree n with positive coefficients and n simple negative roots. The following direct argument proves these assertions at every step, not merely at sampled levels. When h decreases to h-1, n increases to n+1. The residual update is A_(n+1)(z)=-Im[q^(-j-h)(1+q^h z)^2 A_n(qz)]/sin(h pi/N), (7) where (7) is stated for REAL z. Its holomorphic polynomial meaning is the corresponding coefficientwise difference of conjugate polynomials. Explicitly, if A_n=sum a_k z^k, then a'_k=[sin((j+h-k)theta)a_k +2sin((j-k+1)theta)a_(k-1) +sin((n-k+2)theta)a_(k-2)]/sin(h theta), theta=pi/N, a_k=0 outside 0<=k<=n. (8) All coefficients of degrees 0 through n+1 are positive. The putative degree n+2 coefficient is zero, since j=h+n. The scalar in (6) changes by c_(t+1)=q^j c_t. To obtain (7), use B_h(q^(-1)z)=(1+q^(-h)z)B_(h-1)(z), B_h(qz)=(1+q^h z)B_(h-1)(z) in (4); its residual numerator is q^(2j)(1+q^(-h)z)^2 A_n(q^(-1)z) -q^(-2h)(1+q^h z)^2 A_n(qz). Now suppose A_n(z) has roots -rho_k, rho_k>0. At z=-r, r>0, the continuous argument of the quantity inside Im in (7) is -(j+h)theta+2Arg(1-q^h r)+sum_k Arg(rho_k-qr). It strictly decreases from -(j+h)theta, which lies in (-pi,0), to -(n+2)pi as r tends to infinity. The limiting endpoint is not reached at finite r. Each factor stays nonzero and each individual argument strictly decreases. Therefore exactly n+1 multiples of pi are crossed, with nonzero derivative. Equation (7) has n+1 distinct negative roots. Since its degree is at most n+1, these are all its roots and the degree is exactly n+1. This starts from A_0=1 and proves (6). **Exact zero theorem.** G_t has its h forced zeros U=Q^(t+1),...,Q^d, and its n residual zeros lie on U=-q^t rho with rho>0. The residual zeros are simple; a residual zero can coincide with a forced zero, which causes no problem below. In the scaled magnetic variable upsilon=u/N, the latter zeros have Re upsilon=(1+t/N)/2 modulo 1. Every zero therefore lies OUTSIDE S_tau={upsilon in C: 0<Re upsilon<tau}, tau=t/N. (9) The exact finite function (1) is nonzero on this entire strip, at both parities and composite levels. This conclusion is special to the original physical Fourier argument w=q^(t+j-d); it is not an assertion of joint zero-freeness in independent w and upsilon. ## 3. The canonical magnetic logarithm and its selected limit Let (tau,xi)=(t/N,j/N) remain in a compact strict real parameter set with 0<xi<tau<1, xi<=1/2, tau+xi>=1 in the limiting complete chamber. The actual integer parameters may have tau+xi=1-1/N; all constructions use those actual parameters and are uniform for this O(1/N) boundary displacement. Consider compact subsets inside S_tau, uniformly away from both vertical boundaries. Factorization (6) gives locally uniform bounds for N^(-1)Log[fhat(N upsilon)/fhat(N upsilon_0)] (10) and all its fixed derivatives. Here upsilon_0 is near tau/2 and the logarithm is continued in the simply connected strip. For each root, the logarithmic derivative is 2pi i U/(U-zeta). The possible root locations in section 2 are uniformly separated from the image of the chosen compact set; radial roots are compactified by their radius in [0,infinity]. Integrating along compact paths bounds each root's logarithmic ratio uniformly. There are j<=N/2 roots, and the explicit exponential in (2) supplies only a bounded normalized term. The phase at the noninteger center is fixed exactly, not guessed: B_h(1)A_n(1)>0 in (6), and hence a specified argument is Arg fhat(t/2)=pi[d(t-j)+j^2]/(2N). (11) This uses (Q;Q)_j=(-i)^j q^[j(j+1)/2]s_j with its original product phase. The leading imaginary action at the center is therefore pi(tau-xi+xi^2)/2. A nearest integer to t/2, together with the bounded logarithmic derivative in (10), supplies its real leading value from the actual real-magnetic theorem. Write the previously selected physical action, for REAL upsilon, as Phi_(tau,xi)(upsilon)=psi_(tau,xi,upsilon)(w_star) +pi i upsilon(1-xi), w_star=exp[pi i(tau+xi-1)]. (12) At the center its internal saddle is alpha=xi/2+i eta. The paired J terms make Ecal(alpha) real, so Im Phi(tau/2) is exactly pi(tau-xi+xi^2)/2, agreeing with (11) to leading order. The same pairing gives Ecal'' real negative and A(alpha)B(alpha)>0. Therefore the continued Acal amplitude is positive real there. The remaining order-one phase exp[pi i(alpha-tau/2)] is -pi(tau-xi)/2, exactly the difference between (11) and N Im Phi. This checks both the additive logarithmic mark and its finite phase. The actual real-magnetic amplitude theorem supplies its values on all physical samples. Normal-family limits of (10) must have the same real part there. More precisely, adjacent physical sample ratios and bounded second derivatives give exp(g'(upsilon))=exp(Phi'(upsilon)) on the real interval. Thus g'-Phi' is a constant 2pi i integer. This sampling alias must be removed; dense samples alone do not remove it. At the center, positivity of all coefficients of B_h A_n gives 0<=Im[N^(-1)partial_upsilon Log fhat(N upsilon)]<=pi in the limit, with real part zero. The selected derivative in (12) lies STRICTLY between 0 and pi on that imaginary axis. Indeed the internal saddle there is alpha=xi/2+i eta, eta>=0. Its exact phase equation is 4Arg sin(pi(xi/2+i eta)) +2Arg sin(pi((tau-xi)/2+i eta))=pi(tau+xi-1). Consequently Phi'(tau/2)=pi i(1-xi) +2i Arg sin(pi((tau-xi)/2+i eta)) has imaginary part in [pi(1-xi),pi tau], a compact subinterval of (0,pi). The integer alias is zero. Equation (11) fixes the remaining additive constant. Compactness and the identity theorem now prove convergence of the WHOLE actual sequence, including derivatives: N^(-1)Log fhat(N upsilon) -> Phi_(tau,xi)(upsilon). (13) The right side is the holomorphic continuation selected by the actual polynomial. The same subsequence argument gives uniformity for compact real parameter families. It does not interpolate t or j. ## 4. The exact magnetic difference equation and its simple branch Let f(upsilon)=fhat(N upsilon), h_N=1/N, U=exp(2pi i upsilon), T=exp(2pi i tau), and Jc=exp(2pi i xi). The original symmetric physical Casimir gives the exact finite difference equation A_+(upsilon,h_N) f(upsilon+h_N) +A_-(upsilon,h_N) f(upsilon-h_N) +(D_(h_N)(upsilon)-c_(h_N))f(upsilon)=0, (14) where q=exp(pi i h_N), Q=q^2 and A_+=(U-T)(1-QU)/T, A_-=(U-QT)(1-U)/(QT), D_h=(U/T)[2(q^(-1)+qT)-(q+q^(-1))U], c_h=q Jc+q^(-1)Jc^(-1). It is an identity for the entire continuation (1). One direct check uses (2): after removing its exponential, the residual is a polynomial in U of degree at most j+1, since its top degree j+2 cancels. Its constant coefficient is zero. It also vanishes at the t+1 original physical nodes U=1,Q,...,Q^t, by the actual Casimir eigenvector equation, including both boundary rows. Since t>=j, these zeros plus U=0 force the polynomial to vanish identically. No generic contiguous identity or missing endpoint equation is presumed. Put A=(U-T)(1-U)/T, D=2U(1+T-U)/T, H(upsilon,a)=A(e^a+e^(-a))+D-(Jc+Jc^(-1)). (15) The branch selected in (13) satisfies H(upsilon,Phi')=0. It is simple throughout the strip in the limiting complete chamber. Its characteristic discriminant is exactly (Jc+Jc^(-1)-2) [Jc+Jc^(-1)+2-4U(1+T-U)/T]. (16) The second factor's zeros, after U=exp(pi i tau)X, obey X^2-2cos(pi tau)X+cos^2(pi xi)=0. Because tau>=1-xi and xi<=1/2, its finite nonzero roots are negative real. They lie on the same excluded magnetic line as the residual roots in section 2. A zero root at xi=1/2 is not a finite U. Also A has no zero inside S_tau and Jc!=1. Hence H_a!=0 there. On compact subsets it remains bounded away from zero, also for the actual O(1/N) displacement below tau+xi=1. ## 5. Actual complex amplitude from the magnetic finite shifts This section proves a fixed complex corridor theorem around any compact real magnetic interval inside (0,tau). The preceding root and discriminant estimates also permit compact paths farther inside the strip, with the continued functions specified in sections 3--4. Write G_N=N^(-1)Log f and a_N=G_N'. The exact zero theorem and (13) give bounded holomorphic derivatives and a_N->Phi' on larger compact sets. Taylor expansion of the ACTUAL shifted ratios in (14) yields f(upsilon+/-h_N)/f(upsilon) =exp(+/-a_N)[1+(h_N/2)a_N'+O(h_N^2)]. (17) Expand the displayed finite coefficients as A_+=A+h_N A_1^++O(h_N^2), A_-=A+h_N A_1^-+O(h_N^2), and similarly for D and c. Explicitly, A_1^+=-2pi i U(U-T)/T, A_1^-=-2pi i U(1-U)/T, D_1=2pi i U(T-1)/T, c_1=pi i(Jc-Jc^(-1)), H_1(upsilon,a)=A_1^+e^a+A_1^-e^(-a)+D_1-c_1. Equations (14) and (17) imply 0=H(upsilon,a_N) +h_N[H_1(upsilon,a_N)+(a_N'/2)H_aa(upsilon,a_N)] +O(h_N^2). Uniform simplicity first gives a_N-Phi'=O(h_N). Cauchy's estimate on a larger compact set improves its derivative to the same order. Substitution a second time proves the ACTUAL correction a_N=Phi'+h_N b+O(h_N^2), b=-[H_1(upsilon,Phi')+(Phi''/2)H_aa(upsilon,Phi')] /H_a(upsilon,Phi'). (18) Let Btilde solve the scalar holomorphic equation Btilde'/Btilde=b, with its nonzero value at the real center fixed by the previous [actual amplitude theorem](actual_q_hahn_uniform_complex_amplitude.md). Then Btilde is holomorphic and never zero on the corridor. The center may be noninteger: use the nearest physical sample to fix the constant to relative error O(1/N), since both Btilde and the previous explicit amplitude are smooth and nonzero there. Integrating (18) from that physical sample proves fhat_(N,t,j)(N upsilon) =N^(-1/2) Btilde_(tau,xi)(upsilon) exp[N Phi_(tau,xi)(upsilon)](1+O(N^(-1))). (19) The error is uniform on the complex corridor, with each fixed derivative on smaller compact subsets. Thus the transport solution in (18) is justified by the original polynomial and a known actual constant; it is not a formal ansatz substituted for it. The amplitude in (19) is the continuation of the earlier explicit one: Btilde_(tau,xi)(upsilon) =Acal_(tau,xi,upsilon)(w_star) exp[pi i(alpha_(tau,xi,upsilon)(w_star)-upsilon)]. (20) To see this without assuming an unproved transport identity, compare (19) with the previous actual theorem at physical real samples. Taking sequences of parameters and samples tending to any strict real point proves equality of the two nonzero amplitudes there. Their holomorphic continuations are therefore identical. The local coefficient functions are analytic across tau+xi=1, so the identity also covers the actual O(1/N) boundary displacement. This analytic identity between coefficient functions is NOT a claimed finite interpolation of t or j. The phases and the order-one factor in (20) retain both original integer offsets. No root-normal derivative has been taken. The theorem supplies an actual complex magnetic packet at fixed real t,j; global magnetic/channel summation, complex pair-degree or channel continuation, and the original global cycle remain separate. ## 6. A canonical joint rational continuation, without a joint estimate There is also a source-defined joint continuation in u and v=t-u. Set U=Q^u, V=Q^v and retain the phase x^u=exp(pi i d u/N). For fixed N and j define the finite polynomial H_j(U,V)=sum_(a=0)^j [j choose a]_Q^2 q^[a(a-d)] V^a product_(r=0)^(a-1)(U-Q^r) product_(r=0)^(j-a-1)(V-Q^r), D_j(T)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)(T-Q^r). (21) The original terminating formula, extended with its own finite sine products, is exactly fhat_j(u,v)=x^u H_j(U,V)/D_j(UV). (22) The denominator and the marked exponential are retained. This is a specified finite rational function, not a choice of factorial interpolation. In (21) the binomial is the GAUSSIAN binomial. If one uses the positive sine binomial instead, the same coefficient is beta(j,a)^2 q^[a(2j-a-d)] V^a. (23) Indeed [j choose a]_Q=q^[a(j-a)] beta(j,a). Confusing these two binomials changes the original phase, already at j=2. For a direct derivation, substitute the two finite sine products used in (3), and use beta(t,j)=i^(-j)q^[-jt-j(j-1)/2] D_j(Q^t)/s_j. Removing this denominator leaves the phase q^[a t+a(j-a)] before the original w^a is included. Since w=q^(t+j-d), and Q^(at)U^(-a)=V^a, the remaining phase is exactly q^[a(2j-a-d)]. This proves (22). Restricting UV=T to an actual integer degree recovers G_t(U)=U^j H_j(U,T/U)/D_j(T). (24) No joint zero-location theorem for H_j(U,V), or joint complex asymptotic in pair degree and magnetic coordinate, is asserted here. The preceding strip theorem uses the essential restriction that UV=Q^t with t real and integer. Formula (22) specifies a possible next object without supplying the missing estimates for it. Audit: [exact magnetic polynomial and complex corridor](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_magnetic_complex_corridor.py). Independent analytical review: a second reader checked the literal terminating continuation, coproduct normalization and negative-root factorization, the strip zero exclusion, canonical center phase and sampling-alias removal, the endpoint-inclusive Casimir equation and its discriminant, and the actual finite-shift amplitude bootstrap. The real-center normalization and both original integer offsets were independently recalculated. The joint rational appendix, including the Gaussian-versus-sine binomial phase, also passed. The primary reader's fresh audit replay was retained rather than duplicated. The theorem still fixes real discrete pair degree and channel; it supplies neither a joint complex estimate nor a selected whole-source cycle. Root review: full analytical read and fresh audit PASS. The review checked the original terminating function, exact coproduct normalization, residual root induction, canonical center phase, removal of the sampling alias, Casimir polynomial identity, simple branch and two-order derivative bootstrap. The replay included 186 independent joint sine-product checks and 32 complex magnetic amplitude regressions. The joint rational formula is exact; joint complex asymptotics and the global source remain open.

title: The actual paired normal on a fixed complex corridor near the fold
status: Complex paired-normal bound; shrinking channel window
text: # The actual paired normal on a fixed complex corridor near the fold Subsequent full-domain result: the [full strict physical packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) extends the actual ordinary amplitude and the stated small/near-fold complex bounds to fixed physical compacts, with the necessary finite-level boundary correction. The [selected-factor corollary](actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md) then selects every ordinary factor outside one prescribed matching-edge block. Global contraction and period estimates remain open. The argument below keeps its original domain and proof scope. 30 October 2026. The original paired normal admits a polynomial bound on every fixed compact magnetic corridor when the two channel indices remain a bounded number of steps apart. More generally it has only subexponential relative cost when their separation s satisfies s log N=o(N). The magnetic corridor is genuinely complex and has width independent of N. This follows from the original generic source, not from interpolation of its physical-grid values. The channel window in this statement shrinks in scaled coordinates. It does not give subexponential cost at a fixed nonzero scaled channel displacement, a relative normal amplitude, or a whole-source estimate. ## 1. Statement and exact source Let q0=exp(pi i/N), d=N-1, and let 0<=j<l, j+l=d, s=l-j. For q=q0 exp(epsilon) put Q=q^2, B=Q^(-N), x=q^d and t=N tau, u=N nu, U=Q^u, T=Q^t, sigma=q^t, D_m(T)=product_(r=0)^(m-1)(T-Q^r). Use the literal generic finite source from [the small-channel generic theorem](actual_q_hahn_small_channel_generic_normals.md) and [the collision theorem](actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.md): C_m(q;t,u)=x^u H_m^B(U,T/U)/D_m(T), H_m^B(U,V)=sum_(a=0)^m (-1)^a B^a Q^[a(a+1)/2] [m choose a]_Q (BQ^(m-a+1);Q)_a/(BQ;Q)_a V^a product_(r<a)(U-Q^r) product_(r<m-a)(V-Q^r). (1) All powers use log q=pi i/N+epsilon. In particular this is the original generic highest-weight-d deformation, not the root-only squared-binomial formula. Its paired normal is w_(j,l)(t,u)=[D C_j(q0;t,u)-D C_l(q0;t,u)] /[-2N Delta_j], Delta_j=q0^(2j+1)-q0^(-2j-1), D=q d/dq. (2) Let K be a compact subset of the joint central wedge W={ (tau,nu): 1/2<Re tau<1, |2Re nu-Re tau|<1/2 }. There exist eta_K,c_K,C_K>0 such that, for all sufficiently large N and all 1<=s<=eta_K N of the required parity, |w_(j,l)(N tau,N nu)/C_j(q0;N tau,N nu)| <= C_K N^8 (C_K N^16)^s, (tau,nu) in K. (3) Every function in this quotient is holomorphic on a neighborhood of K, and C_j(q0) is nonzero there. No omitted tail is used in (3). Consequently, for bounded s the cost is polynomial in N. Uniformly over any windows 1<=s<=h_N with h_N log N=o(N), |w_(j,l)| <= exp(o(N)) |C_j(q0)| (4) on the SAME fixed complex compact K. This includes windows of size O(N^a) for every fixed a<1, in particular square-root windows. ## 2. The generic recurrence is valid beyond the small channel Keep B temporarily independent of Q. Put A=B^(-1) and K_m=(B^2 Q^(m+1);Q)_m/(BQ;Q)_m, S_m(U,T)=U^m H_m^B(U,T/U), R_m(z)=z^m S_m(sigma/z,sigma^2)/(sigma^(2m) K_m). These are monic polynomials for generic parameters. Their exact source normalization is C_m=x^u q^(mt) K_m R_m(sigma/U)/D_m(T). (5) Write Lambda_n=AQ^(-n)+BQ^(n+1), b_n=[(1+A)+Q sigma^2(1+B) -Q^(-n)(Q sigma^2+A)-Q^n(BQ sigma^2+1)]/sigma, d_n=Q^(1-n)+Q^n-1-Q, u_0=0, u_n=b_n/(Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-1)), v_0=v_1=0, v_n=(b_(n-1)u_n+d_n)/(Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-2)), n>=2, alpha_n=u_(n+1)-u_n, beta_n=v_(n+1)-v_n-alpha_n u_n, n>=1. Then, as RATIONAL identities in generic B,Q,sigma, R_0=1, R_1=z+alpha_0, R_(n+1)=(z+alpha_n)R_n+beta_n R_(n-1). (6) The small-channel note proves these formulas by its original Casimir identity and finite moment argument. Their use at a large channel requires an additional justification. Fix n and clear the denominators in (6). The residual is a finite Laurent polynomial in B,Q,sigma,z, independent of the source size N. For every N>=2n+3 the proved small-channel result makes it vanish at B=Q^(-N), identically in generic Q,sigma,z. Writing the residual as sum_a B^a p_a(Q,sigma,z), choose N larger than all its finite Q-exponent widths. The supports of Q^(-Na)p_a are then disjoint. Therefore every p_a is zero. This proves (6) formally for every n. The scalar identity for K_m already has the independent finite Vandermonde proof and no small-channel restriction. Thus (5),(6) describe the actual large generic source wherever their generic factors are defined. At the actual root some monic R_m have poles because K_m vanishes. We do not assume these monic polynomials are holomorphic there. ## 3. A small generic circle controls every intervening row Let a_K=inf_K(Re tau-1/2)>0. Choose 0<eta_K<min(1/4,a_K). Then l/N<1/2+eta_K/2 and every extra source divisor T=Q_0^r, j<=r<l, remains uniformly separated from K. The same holds for the factors already present in D_j. All elementary exponentials q^n, B and sigma, and their inverses, are uniformly bounded for |epsilon|<=c N^(-3), n<=N, (tau,nu) in K. Use the circle |epsilon|=rho_N=c_K N^(-8), (7) with c_K chosen from the small-channel theorem, decreasing it if needed. That theorem supplies a tridiagonal matrix M_j(epsilon) with det M_j=R_j(z), z=sigma/U. At zero it is the original accretive matrix zI+cD+K_skew, c=-cos((t+1)pi/N), and its change in operator norm is O(N^7 |epsilon|). Consequently, throughout the disk enclosed by (7), ||M_j^(-1)||<=C_K, |C_j(q)/C_j(q0)|<=C_K, |R_(j-1)(z)/R_j(z)|<=C_K. (8) The last identity follows from the last diagonal entry of M_j^(-1): the cofactor is its leading (j-1)-row determinant, exactly R_(j-1). Thus the initial two values for propagating (6) are controlled. For every n<=l, the only spectral denominators in (6) are Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-1) =(1-Q)A Q^(-n)(1-B^2 Q^(2n)), Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-2) =(1-Q^2)A Q^(-n)(1-B^2 Q^(2n-1)). (9) At the root a vanishing last factor in (9) occurs only at 2n=N or 2n-1=N, respectively. All other last factors have modulus at least c/N, and both first factors have modulus at least c/N. These nonresonant differences therefore stay at least c/N^2 on the circle (7). At a resonant n the last factor is exactly 1-Q^(-N)=1-exp(-2N epsilon), whose modulus is at least c N rho_N on that circle. Multiplication by the first factor gives a lower bound c rho_N. Hence EVERY required denominator on (7) obeys |Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-r)|>=c_K rho_N, r=1,2, (10) with r=2 used only for n>=2. This explicitly retains the folded resonance rather than pretending its root denominator is a unit. The numerators b_n,d_n are O_K(1). The definitions in section 2 and (10) give, on the circle, |u_n|+|alpha_n|<=C_K rho_N^(-1), |v_n|+|beta_n|<=C_K rho_N^(-2). Propagating the two-component recurrence (6) exactly s times, from R_(j-1),R_j to R_l, now gives |R_l(z)/R_j(z)|<=(C_K N^16)^s. (11) No positivity, missing-current cancellation, or interpolation of physical samples enters this estimate. ## 4. The scalar ratio and holomorphy of the FULL source The scalars in (5) cannot be discarded. Their exact cancellation is K_l/K_j= product_(r=2j+1)^(2l)(1-B^2 Q^r) /[product_(r=j+1)^l(1-B^2 Q^r) product_(r=j+1)^l(1-BQ^r)]. (12) There are 2s numerator and 2s denominator factors. The denominator indices lie uniformly near N/2 under s<=eta_K N, so all those denominators are bounded below on (7). The numerator factors are uniformly bounded above. One numerator factor vanishes at the center of the circle; it is retained in (12). Thus |K_l/K_j|<=C_K^s, |D_j(T)/D_l(T)|<=C_K^s, |q^((l-j)t)|<=C_K^s. (13) Equations (5),(8),(11),(13) prove on the circle |C_l(q;t,u)/C_j(q0;t,u)| <=C_K(C_K N^16)^s. (14) We apply Cauchy's formula to C_l, NOT to its singular monic factor. The original finite expression (1) proves C_l is holomorphic throughout the enclosed disk: its factors (Q;Q)_a and (BQ;Q)_a have indices a<=l<N and are units at q0; their possible zeros stay outside this polynomially small disk. Its factors D_l(T) are uniformly nonzero by the separation at the beginning of section 3. The finite numerator is entire in the displayed exponentials. Thus every apparent monic pole inside (7) is already canceled in the original source, before Cauchy's estimate is used. Consequently (14), and the small-channel bound for C_j, imply |D C_l(q0)/C_j(q0)|<=C_K N^8(C_K N^16)^s, |D C_j(q0)/C_j(q0)|<=C_K N^8. (15) Finally |Delta_j|=2sin(pi s/N) and 2N |Delta_j|=4N sin(pi s/N)>=8s>=8 in this near-fold range. Dividing the two ACTUAL generic derivatives in (15) by the original gap in (2) proves (3). ## 5. What the estimate supplies The full paired normal, including its large-channel tail, is holomorphic and has at most subexponential relative cost on a fixed complex magnetic corridor for s log N=o(N). This can accompany the proved ordinary-column complex action in a shrinking channel window at the complete endpoint. It is an upper bound: no nonzero normal amplitude or leading coefficient is asserted. For s proportional to N the bound (3) is too large to identify an exponential rate. In particular it does not control a fixed nonzero scaled channel shift that might arise at a filling saddle. The extra-pole obstruction outside the near-fold corridor remains valid. Neither physical-grid interpolation nor an assertion that the generic monic determinant is regular has been used to avoid it. Focused audit: [full generic large source and resonant circle](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound_results.json). Exact dual arithmetic passed 208 all-degree source recurrences, 582 original large-channel generic value-and-normal comparisons, and 110 scalar-ratio identities. At 220 digits, 120 literal nonphysical large-source circle comparisons, 5,080 spectral-gap checks, 30 original-versus-transverse paired normals, and 120 retained scalar identities passed. The maximum source comparison error was below 1.1e-206. Both bounded and square-root-sized channel separations occur in these checks. The uniform conclusion is the proved circle estimate, not an inference from the samples. An independent analytical review checked the all-degree rational recurrence, every intervening folded denominator, the inverse cofactor starting ratio, the exact K_l/K_j cancellation, and the holomorphy of the original C_l before applying Cauchy's formula. It also checked the actual gap and the s log N=o(N) scope. No fixed positive scaled-channel displacement or amplitude theorem is included in that review. A second independent full analytical review and fresh audit replay also passed. It checked the formal recurrence lift, the resonant circle lower bounds, the retained scalar cancellation, and the holomorphy of the full large-channel source despite its singular monic factors. Its replay reproduced all exact and 220-digit counts above. The conclusion remains a relative upper bound in the stated shrinking channel window on a fixed magnetic corridor.

title: The actual finite-clock boundary determinant through the fold
status: Positive finite-clock boundary determinant and retained trace transport
text: # The actual finite-clock boundary determinant through the fold 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. The original 222 boundary has two finite negative raw clocks, by the literal [right-angled prefix sign theorem](actual_right_angled_resonant_prefix_signs.md). At the ROOT this puts its actual white numerator in a positive definite determinant, including the maximal folded channel. This note proves a uniform relative perturbation formula which retains the order-one transport term, and an explicit leading logarithmic rate through the fold. The proof uses the finite determinant, matrix traces and elementary sums, not a saddle selection assumption. These are numerator results. Scalar phases, partner products and all source normalization remain explicit. No genuine generic quantum derivative, full source cycle, or volume equality follows. ## 1. The literal source and its negative raw clocks Put N>=2, d=N-1, theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), Q=q^2 and 0<=a<=floor(d/2). Let H_a^1(U,V) be the root white polynomial in the [resonant boundary theorem](actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.md). Its exact determinant, proved in the [complementary boundary theorem](actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge.md), is H_a^1(U,V)=V^a K_a det[I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+], K_a=[2a choose a]_Q. (1) The empty determinant for a=0 is one. The Hermitian positive definite matrices H_-,H_+ have common diagonal d_n=1/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], 0<=n<a, and upper adjacent entries sqrt(B_n)[sin(n theta) -/+ i cos(n theta)], 1<=n<a, B_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. (2) Their positivity follows from the original exact Cholesky pivots; it holds at both level parities and through the folded endpoint. Use the ACTUAL half-index arguments U=q^-1 X, V=q^-1 Y, X<0, Y<0, alpha=-X/2>0, beta=-1/(2Y)>0. Then the matrix in (1) is EXACTLY M=I+alpha H_-+beta H_+ > I. (3) In particular its determinant is positive, while V^a and K_a retain their original phases. This statement concerns the raw clocks X,Y, not an independently rotated pair of physical heads. The original 222 geometry supplies precisely these limiting signs. The exact finite-r arguments differ from their limits, and are handled next; they are not silently set equal to their limits. ## 2. Uniform relative transport, with its first correction retained Change the coefficients in (3) to alpha(1+e_-), beta(1+e_+), allowing complex e_-,e_+. Set eta=|e_-|+|e_+|<1 and E=M^(-1/2)[alpha e_- H_-+beta e_+ H_+]M^(-1/2). Both alpha M^(-1/2)H_- M^(-1/2) and beta M^(-1/2)H_+ M^(-1/2) are positive semidefinite, and their sum is I-M^-1<I. Hence ||E||<=eta, with no dependence on N,a, or a small eigenvalue of an individual H matrix. The marked logarithm, zero when e_-=e_+=0, therefore satisfies Log(det(M+Delta M)/det M)=tr E+R, |R|<=a eta^2/[2(1-eta)], |Log(det(M+Delta M)/det M)|<=-a log(1-eta). (4) Indeed expand tr Log(I+E) in its absolutely convergent matrix power series, use |tr E^j|<=a eta^j, and sum the terms j>=2. This also proves nonvanishing and specifies the relative branch. If X is changed to X(1+u) and Y to Y(1+v), the exact choices are e_-=u, e_+=(1+v)^(-1)-1. (5) Thus O(N^-1) relative clock corrections give det(M+Delta M)/det M=exp(tr E)[1+O(N^-1)]. (6) The trace need not tend to zero: it is an order-one source transport term and must stay. Corrections O(log N/N) have at most O(log N) logarithmic cost, with a nonzero relative factor. The estimates are uniform through the fold. The factors V^a, K_a and all other source factors remain outside this comparison and are kept EXACTLY. These are clock perturbations at one root, not the moving-Q or moving-B generic quantum derivatives. ## 3. The determinant's leading rate Suppose a/N tends to xi in [0,1/2] and alpha,beta tend to positive limits. The convergence below is uniform when alpha,beta stay in compact subsets of the positive reals. For 0<=t<1/2 write c(t)=cos(pi t), D(t)=1+(alpha+beta)/c(t)^2, b(t)^2=[(alpha+beta)^2-4alpha beta c(t)^2]/[4c(t)^4], lambda_+(t)=[D(t) +sqrt(1+[2(alpha+beta)+4alpha beta]/c(t)^2)]/2. The square root here is positive real. Then (1/N)log det M -> I(xi;alpha,beta), I(xi;alpha,beta)=integral_0^xi log lambda_+(t) dt. (7) The endpoint xi=1/2 is included. The improper integral converges because log lambda_+(t)=O(1+|log(1/2-t)|). An a=0 subsequence has empty determinant and rate zero. Here is a proof from the actual finite matrices. The diagonal of M is 1+(alpha+beta)d_n; the squared modulus of its upper entry is B_n[(alpha+beta)^2 sin^2(n theta) +(alpha-beta)^2 cos^2(n theta)]. (8) Away from t=1/2 these converge to D(t), b(t)^2. On each fixed closed interval below 1/2, entries are uniformly bounded. The few initial n, for which the B_n continuum approximation is not uniform, do not affect the Riemann limit: after removing an arbitrarily short initial interval convergence is uniform, while all the removed entries have a common bound. Their contribution to each fixed matrix trace moment is bounded by that interval's length times a constant depending only on the moment. For a fixed integer j, expand tr M^j into closed nearest-neighbor walks of length j. Away from the two ends, each walk sees entries whose variation over j indices tends uniformly to zero. The constant-coefficient walk sum is the zeroth Fourier coefficient of [D(t)+2b(t)cos(phi)]^j; complex offdiagonal phases cancel because a closed walk traverses each edge equally in both directions. Endpoint walks contribute O(j/N) to the normalized trace. Consequently, for every polynomial P and xi<1/2, (1/N)tr P(M) -> integral_0^xi (1/(2pi)) integral_0^(2pi) P(D+2b cos phi) dphi dt. (9) All eigenvalues of M lie in [1,C_xi] by (3) and the bounded row sums. The limiting symbol lies in the same type of interval: D-2b>=1. Approximate log on this interval by truncating log z=log R-sum_(j>=1)(1-z/R)^j/j, R>C_xi. The tail converges uniformly geometrically since z>=1. Its trace error divided by N is bounded by (a/N) times the uniform error. Thus (9) holds for log as well. Finally D+2b cos phi=lambda_+ |1+(b/lambda_+)exp(i phi)|^2, where b/lambda_+<1. Expanding the scalar logarithm in powers of exp(i phi) shows that its second factor has mean logarithm zero. This proves (7) below the fold, without invoking a limiting matrix theorem. To include the fold, cut off the last h<=delta N+O(1) indices. Write M in these two principal blocks. Its Schur complement S on the last block satisfies I<=S<=M_tail: the lower bound follows by minimizing the quadratic form of M>=I over the first block. The upper bound is the explicit positive Schur subtraction. Hence 0<=log det M-log det M_bulk <=log det M_tail<=sum_tail log[1+(alpha+beta)d_n]. (10) The last inequality follows, for example, from its Cholesky pivots being no larger than its diagonal entries. With j_n=N-2n-2>=1 at every allowed diagonal entry, d_n<=C N^2/j_n^2. The j_n have step two. Integral comparison for the sum of log j therefore bounds (10) by C h[1+log(N/max(1,h))]+O(log N). After division by N this tends to zero as delta tends to zero. The same integrable bound handles the tail of (7). This proves the endpoint, including every sequence of actual folded colors. For varying positive parameters, (4) bounds the normalized logarithmic change by C(|Delta log alpha|+|Delta log beta|), uniformly in the channel and N on positive compact sets. Thus the fixed-parameter argument extends uniformly to compactly varying alpha,beta; the integral in (7) has the same continuity by its integrable fold bound. ## 4. The original scalar and large partner Let Lambda(x)=-integral_0^x log|2sin v| dv. The exact magnitude of K_a is s_(2a)/s_a^2, where s_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N). Elementary Riemann sums, splitting off the integrable endpoint logarithms, give (1/N)log|H_a^1(q^-1X,q^-1Y)| -> xi log|Y|+[2Lambda(pi xi)-Lambda(2pi xi)]/pi +I(xi;alpha,beta). (11) Equation (1), not just (11), retains its complex scalar phase. For the actual large channel m=d-a, keep the exact root identity H_m^1(U,V)=H_a^1(U,V) product_(r=a)^(m-1)(UV-Q^r). (12) For xi bounded away from zero and XY in a positive compact, the product in (12) is uniformly away from its factors' zeros. Its additional logarithmic rate is integral_xi^(1-xi) log|XY-exp(2pi i t)| dt. (13) The finite q^-2 in UV=Q^-1 XY and the exact endpoints stay in (12). At small colors, or under complex perturbations near any forced divisor, use that exact product, not a claimed uniform relative replacement of it. No derivative of (12) is used to assert a generic quantum normal. This is a boundary extension of the earlier strict physical-tube theorem: the canonical raw negative clocks have limiting real total degree one, which lies on that tube's boundary. Unlike the whole rational column, the numerator determinant has no omitted Delta_a(UV) denominator. This note estimates the numerator only. The action in (7) has the ORIGINAL selected normalization. To check this directly, rotate both raw clocks to X_delta=e^(-i delta)X and Y_delta=e^(-i delta)Y, with fixed small delta>0. Their actual heads lie in the earlier strict physical tube for all sufficiently large N. The two determinant coefficients become alpha e^(-i delta) and beta e^(i delta), so (4) bounds the difference of their normalized marked logarithms from the negative-clock value by C delta, uniformly in N and through the fold. The strict-tube theorem gives the original selected action at each fixed delta. Taking N to infinity and then delta to zero identifies its boundary value with (7). The branch is transported by (4) from the positive determinant; at X=Y=-1 this is the old real center, where the determinant is positive, so the two branches agree there. Continuation through the connected negative-clock quadrant retains that equality. The exact factors V^a and K_a are still those of (1). No unrelated solution of the characteristic equation or new additive constant is being selected by the trace-walk calculation. This comparison uses the strict-tube theorem for xi>0. At xi=0, the present small-a/N trace bounds and scalar sums give rate zero; the selected boundary value there follows by continuity, without invoking the earlier fixed-positive-color packet at zero color. It supplies one piece of the original boundary source, not its global cycle coefficient or the full complementary-color gap. Focused audit: [original numerator and determinant checks](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_negative_clock_boundary.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_negative_clock_boundary_results.json). At 90-digit precision it compares 48 literal source numerators, 30 independent dense determinants and 48 large-partner identities. It checks 36 retained trace corrections against the proved remainder bound, six independent dense trace calculations and 42 positive Schur-tail inequalities. The 36 leading-rate diagnostics supplement the written proof; they are not its justification. Independent validation: a full analytical reader checked the original source identity, retained phases, uniform trace correction, trace-walk limit, folded Schur tail and large-partner scope, then freshly replayed the focused audit with all counts reproduced. A second reader separately checked the entire leading-rate and folded-endpoint argument, including the nonuniform initial rows and compact parameter dependence. Both reviews passed. These conclusions concern the root numerator only; no generic quantum-normal or global-period conclusion is inferred. The selected-action boundary comparison was additionally checked by the second reader, with the actual half-index offsets and positive-center branch retained; targeted review PASS.

title: Negative roots of the actual complete-channel source polynomial
text: # Negative roots of the actual complete-channel source polynomial 30 October 2026. The finite polynomial inside EVERY physical complete-channel q-Hahn column has only negative nonzero roots. They are simple; its sole possible zero at the origin is the forced support power. This is an all-level theorem for the ACTUAL finite coefficients, not an inference from the stationary quadratic or a sampled real-root plot. In particular the physical Fourier evaluation of that polynomial never vanishes. The proof uses an exact two-binomial recurrence and an elementary sine coefficient multiplier. An independent sine-operator peeling proof of the two-binomial step is retained in section5. ## 1. The exact source polynomial and its support Put N>=2, d=N-1, theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), and s_r=product_(k=1)^r 2sin(k theta), s_0=1, beta(n,a)=s_n/[s_a s_(n-a)] for 0<=a<=n, beta(n,a)=0 outside that integer range. For physical 0<=t<=d, 0<=u<=t and 0<=j<=t set v=t-u and P_(t,j,u)(z)=sum_a E_a z^a, E_a=beta(j,a) beta(u,a) beta(v,j-a)/beta(t,j). (1) Its nonzero support is exactly a0=max(0,j-v), a1=min(j,u), n=a1-a0. (2) All coefficients in this interval are strictly positive. The actual [complete augmented-plat compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md) uses the further restrictions j<=floor(d/2), t+j>=d and the exact physical evaluation f_u(c_j)=(-1)^u q^[-(j+1)u] P_(t,j,u)(q^delta), delta=t+j-d>=0. (3) Equation (1) is precisely that finite compiler coefficient, with no q-factorial normalizer omitted. The theorem holds even without those further complete-image restrictions: P(z)=C z^a0 product_(h=1)^n(z+rho_h), C>0, rho_h>0, and all rho_h distinct. (4) If n=0 this is a positive monomial, with no nonzero roots to list. ## 2. A two-binomial polynomial has simple negative nonzero roots For u,v>=0 with t=u+v<N define Q_j^(u,v)(z)=sum_a beta(u,a) beta(v,j-a) z^a, 0<=j<=t. (5) The symmetric quantum-binomial product is the finite identity B_k(w)=sum_a beta(k,a)w^a =product_(r=0)^(k-1)(1+q^(k-1-2r)w). (6) For an elementary proof, use B_k(w)=(1+q^(k-1)w)B_(k-1)(q^-1 w). The two coefficient terms combine to beta(k,a) by the sine addition identity; B_0=1 starts the induction. No root-location assertion for B_k is made: its roots usually lie on a unit-circle arc. Let F(w,z)=B_u(zw)B_v(w)=sum_j Q_j(z)w^j. Its q-shifts obey (1+q^-u zw)(1+q^-v w)F(qw,z) =(1+q^u zw)(1+q^v w)F(q^-1 w,z). Comparing the coefficient of w^j and dividing by 2i gives the EXACT three-term recurrence sin(j theta) Q_j =[z sin((u-j+1)theta)+sin((v-j+1)theta)] Q_(j-1) +z sin((t-j+2)theta) Q_(j-2), (7) with Q_0=1 and Q_1=[sin(u theta)z+sin(v theta)]/sin theta. First suppose j<=min(u,v). For 2<=j<=min(u,v), every sine coefficient shown in (7) is strictly positive, since t<N. At any negative zero r of Q_(j-1), the sign of Q_j(r) is opposite to that of Q_(j-2)(r). Starting with Q_0,Q_1, a direct induction therefore gives j SIMPLE negative roots of Q_j strictly interlacing those of Q_(j-1). For completeness, adjacent roots of Q_(j-1) give j-2 alternating sign intervals; its rightmost root has Q_j<0 while Q_j(0)>0; and its leftmost root has sign opposite to the sign of Q_j at negative infinity. These provide all j roots. The leading and constant coefficients are positive by (5). All other j are reduced to this case by the following EXACT identities: Q_j^(u,t-u)(z)/beta(t,j) =Q_u^(j,t-j)(z)/beta(t,u), (8) Q_j^(u,v)(z)=z^u Q_(t-j)^(u,v)(1/z), (9) Q_j^(u,v)(z)=z^j Q_j^(v,u)(1/z). (10) Identity (8) follows coefficientwise by canceling six sine factorials; (9),(10) follow from beta(k,a)=beta(k,k-a). Their Laurent expressions are exactly polynomials because the same forced support zeros are present on both sides. Choose the smallest of j,t-j,u,v. If it is j, use (7). If it is t-j, use (9). If it is u, use (8). If it is v, use (10) and then (8). The new degree parameter is at most both new group sizes, so the previous Sturm induction applies. Reversal replaces each nonzero negative root by its reciprocal and multiplication by a positive constant or a forced power of z does not change its sign or simplicity. Thus (5) has exactly its forced zero of order a0, followed by n simple negative roots, for EVERY 0<=j<=t<N. ## 3. The sine multiplier preserves negative roots Let D=z d/dz and define the REAL coefficient operator S_r=sin[theta(D+r)], S_r A(z)=[e^(ir theta)A(e^(i theta)z) -e^(-ir theta)A(e^(-i theta)z)]/(2i). (11) Suppose A has degree n and only negative roots, with positive leading coefficient, and 0<r, r+n<N. Then S_r A has n SIMPLE negative roots. Here is a direct proof. Write A(z)=C product(z+rho_h), rho_h>0. For x>0 follow the continuous argument arg[e^(ir theta)A(-e^(i theta)x)]. Each factor rho_h-x e^(i theta) has strictly decreasing argument, with derivative -rho_h sin(theta)/|rho_h-x e^(i theta)|^2. The total argument decreases from r theta to (r+n)theta-n pi. It crosses exactly 0,-pi,...,-(n-1)pi, once each. Those crossings are exactly the n negative roots of (11); the factors being measured never vanish on x>0. Its leading and constant coefficients are positive. Repeated roots of the input do not spoil the strict argument monotonicity. A forced power z^a is retained: S_r[z^a A]=z^a S_(r+a)A. Thus the same assertion applies if 0<r+a and r+a+n<N. The elementary root reflection s_a s_(d-a)=N gives beta(j,a)=s_j/N product_(r=1)^(d-j) 2sin[(a+r)theta], 0<=a<=j. (12) Consequently multiplication of the a-th coefficient by beta(j,a), on a polynomial of degree at most j, is the exact operator M_j=(s_j/N) 2^(d-j) product_(r=1)^(d-j) S_r. (13) Every factor in (13) satisfies r+degree<=d<N. On a polynomial with its forced zero at the origin the shifted inequality in section3 is the same one. It therefore preserves that zero and all remaining negative roots. Applying M_j to Q_j and dividing by the positive beta(t,j) gives precisely (1). Equations (5)--(13) prove (4). The empty product j=d causes no exception: then j=t=d and n=0. ## 4. The actual Fourier value and its logarithmic branch In the complete-image chamber, 0<=delta<=j<=floor(d/2). Thus q^delta has argument between 0 and pi/2, strictly below pi/2 at finite N. It lies away from every zero in (4), so the ACTUAL canonical column (3) is nonzero, including all magnetic endpoints. More generally P(z)/P(1) has a canonical holomorphic logarithm on C minus the nonpositive real axis, fixed to be zero at z=1. Its exact factorization is Log[P(z)/P(1)]=a0 Log z +sum_h Log[(z+rho_h)/(1+rho_h)]. (14) For real |phi|<pi this also gives the elementary bound cos(phi/2)^n <= |P(e^(i phi))|/P(1) <= 1. (15) This follows from |e^(i phi)+rho|^2=(1+rho)^2-4rho sin^2(phi/2). The loss in (15) can be exponential in N. It is not a subexponential whole-source bound, a Gaussian amplitude estimate, or a proof of noncancellation after summing different physical magnetic variables. The zero-free logarithm is the rigorous input for a separate local complex asymptotic argument. ## 5. Independent sine-operator peeling proof of section2 There is a second own proof that does not use the recurrence or the intersection duality. Begin with the finite Laurent polynomial A_initial(z)=z^j B_v(1/z)=z^(j-v) B_v(z). Apply the coefficient multiplier beta(u,a). By (12) with j replaced by u, it is proportional to product_(r=1)^(d-u) S_r. The same product is zero on every unwanted Laurent power: for a<0 the factor r=-a occurs, and for a>u the factor r=N-a occurs. This uses v<=d-u and j<=u+v<=d. On the wanted powers it equals beta(u,a) exactly, so its output is the polynomial (5). The factors commute. If j>u, apply first r=N-j,...,d-u in increasing order. The identity S_(N-k) B_k=sin(k theta) B_(k-1) removes each forced high power, with the fixed prefactor z^(j-v) accounted for in the shift. If j<v, next apply r=v-j,...,1 in decreasing order. The identity S_0 B_k=sin(k theta) z B_(k-1) removes each forced negative Laurent power. All extracted constants are positive. The remaining polynomial is a positive multiple of z^a0 B_n(z), with a0,n as in (2). The unused factors have r from max(0,v-j)+1 to d-max(u,j). After extracting z^a0 their parameters are s=r+a0. They satisfy 0<s and s+n<N, and their number is n+(d-t) >= n. (16) Use at least n of these factors to strip B_n. More generally, S_s[B_k(z) A(z)]=B_(k-1)(z) T_(s,k)A(z), T_(s,k)A=Im{e^(is theta)(1+q^k z)A(qz)} (17) for real z; equivalently take the two conjugate polynomial terms as in (11). If A has m negative roots, positive leading coefficient, and k+m=n, the argument at z=-x decreases strictly from s theta to (s+k+m)theta-(m+1)pi. Here 0<k<N and 0<s+n<N. It therefore crosses exactly m+1 multiples of pi, giving T_(s,k)A exactly m+1 SIMPLE negative roots and positive leading/constant coefficients. Starting with A=1, each step reduces k by one and increases m by one. After n steps no B factor remains and all roots are negative. The remaining d-t ordinary S_s factors preserve them by section3. This independently proves the complete support and root assertion for Q. It also explains why a reciprocal sine factorial by itself need not be a multiplier: the proof uses the whole paired coefficient structure. Audit: [exact recurrence, dualities, finite source coefficients and root counts](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.py). Independent geometric/algebraic review: full analytical read and fresh audit PASS. The reviewer checked the recurrence/Sturm reduction and factorial dualities, the sine-multiplier normalization, and separately every shifted high/negative-power removal and unused-operator count in the independent peeling proof. The replay passed 76 generic recurrences, 6,800 finite recurrences, 8,720 dualities and peelings, and 867 original Casimir entries. title: The actual partner normal is transverse to a generic collision
text: # The actual partner normal is transverse to a generic collision Subsequent complex estimate: the [near-fold theorem](actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md) controls the full paired normal on a fixed complex compact when (l-j) log N=o(N). It is a relative upper bound in a shrinking scaled channel window; fixed nonzero scaled shifts and a leading normal amplitude remain open. The theorem below retains its original scope. 30 October 2026. The large partner in the original mixed-circle column can be compared with the small column BEFORE specializing q. Their equality holds on a generic spectral-collision hypersurface. This gives an exact transverse derivative formula for the original first normal, and an explicit finite tail. The tail has genuine additional poles; there is no individual-normal holomorphic theorem on the entire joint central wedge. No polynomial relative bound for that normal on a smaller corridor is proved here. Nor does a pole of an individual continued column imply a pole of the full physical coupon after all measures and terms are combined. ## 1. The original generic column in a symmetric finite form Use Q=zeta^2, d=N-1, B=Q^(-N), x=zeta^d, U=Q^u, T=Q^t and X=U^(-1). Write (a;Q)_k=product_(r=0)^(k-1)(1-a Q^r). The actual generic Clebsch column from [the mixed compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md), section 2, has the finite expression C_m=x^u F_m, F_m(Q,B;X,T)=sum_(k=0)^m (Q^(-m);Q)_k (B^2 Q^(m+1);Q)_k (X;Q)_k Q^k /[(BQ;Q)_k (T^(-1);Q)_k (Q;Q)_k]. (1) In (1), B is temporarily an independent variable. Its specialization B=Q^(-N) is the ORIGINAL generic source; B is not a replacement quantization. All displayed denominator factors are units near a primitive N-th root with B=1, except the indicated T divisors. For clarity, the finite transformation in (1) has a direct proof. The original bivariate numerator is H_m^B(U,V)=sum_(a=0)^m (-1)^a B^a Q^[a(a+1)/2] [m choose a]_Q (BQ^(m-a+1);Q)_a/(BQ;Q)_a V^a product_(r<a)(U-Q^r) product_(r<m-a)(V-Q^r), F_m=H_m^B(U,T/U)/product_(r<m)(T-Q^r). (2) The normalized generic Casimir operator, after removing x^u, has eigenvalues Lambda_m=B^(-1)Q^(-m)+B Q^(m+1). On the Newton basis P_k(X)=(X;Q)_k its action is triangular: L P_k=Lambda_k P_k+eta_k P_(k-1), eta_k=(B^(-1)-Q^k)(1-Q^(k-1)/T)(1-Q^(-k)). (3) One can check the lower term without a summation transformation. At X=1,Q^(-1),...,Q^(2-k), the shifted polynomial vanishes, so the lower term is divisible by P_(k-1). At X=Q^(1-k), only the X/Q shift remains; its coefficient is (B^(-1)-Q^k)(1-Q^(k-1)/T), and P_k(X/Q)/P_(k-1)(X)=1-Q^(-k). The leading coefficient gives Lambda_k. Consequently the coefficients of a degree-m eigenfunction normalized to F_m(1)=1 satisfy a_(k+1)/a_k=Q(1-Q^(k-m))(1-B^2 Q^(m+k+1)) /[(1-BQ^(k+1))(1-Q^k/T)(1-Q^(k+1))]. (4) For generic parameters these eigenvalues are distinct. The degree-m normalized eigenfunction is unique, and (4), with a_0=1, gives (1). Rational continuation then proves the identity wherever defined. There is no small-channel restriction hidden in this argument. To justify the generic operator identity for a fixed arbitrary m, first take every integer source size N>=2m+1. The original generic Clebsch calculation and its sufficiently many complete physical t slices give the identity at B=Q^(-N), after clearing denominators. The cleared residual is a FIXED finite Laurent polynomial in B,Q,U,T. Write it as sum B^a p_a(Q,U,T). For N larger than its finite Q-exponent widths, the supports of Q^(-Na)p_a are disjoint. Its vanishing at all such N forces every p_a=0. Thus (3) and the actual numerator identity are formal in B,Q, and apply equally to a large m<N. The physical slice count at one fixed N is not being applied to a large partner. ## 2. The collision identity is generic Fix 0<=j<l and j+l=N-1. The eigenvalue difference factors as Lambda_l-Lambda_j =B^(-1)Q^(-l)(1-Q^(l-j))(1-B^2 Q^N). (5) On the generic hypersurface B^2 Q^N=1, the two numerator parameters of (1) for m=j are the two numerator parameters for m=l in the opposite order. In the large series the second parameter is Q^(-j), so its terms k>j vanish. Therefore, IDENTICALLY in X,T, F_l=F_j on B^2 Q^N=1. (6) Work locally near the actual primitive root Q_0, B=1, with the denominators in (1) inverted. The collision is smooth there because its B derivative is nonzero. Equation (6) gives a regular rational function R_(j,l) such that F_l-F_j=(1-B^2 Q^N) R_(j,l). (7) At even N another algebraic component of the collision can meet denominator divisors. This does not affect the stated local germ: every factor 1-BQ^r, 1<=r<N, is a unit at Q_0,B=1. The assertion does not cancel a denominator identically zero on an irrelevant component. At the actual root, (6) also proves the useful bivariate factorization H_l^1(U,V)=H_j^1(U,V) product_(r=j)^(l-1)(UV-Q_0^r). (8) This is an identity of the continued source numerator, not just an equality on the physical integer magnetic grid. ## 3. The actual generic-q normal becomes a transverse B derivative Return to B=Q^(-N), q=exp(pi i/N), Q_0=q^2, x=q^(N-1), and put Delta=q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1), D=zeta d/dzeta. The actual tensor Casimir eigenvalue is lambda_m(zeta)=zeta^(2N-2m-1)+zeta^(-2N+2m+1), D(lambda_j-lambda_l)(q)=-2N Delta. The root-only expression q^(2m+1)+q^(-2m-1) has the same value but would give the WRONG derivative sign. The actual mixed compiler uses w_j=[D C_j(q)-D C_l(q)]/[-2N Delta]. (9) Along this ACTUAL generic family, D(1-B^2 Q^N)=2N at the root. Since F_l-F_j vanishes identically in X,T on the collision, the derivatives of x^u, X=zeta^(-2u), and T=zeta^(2t) do not contribute to the derivative of the difference. Equations (7),(9) give exactly w_j=x^u R_(j,l)(Q_0,1;X,T)/Delta =x^u [B partial_B(F_j-F_l)]_(Q_0,1)/(2 Delta). (10) The partial derivative in the second line holds Q,X,T fixed. This is an exact consequence of generic collision divisibility. It is NOT differentiation of the root-only identity F_l=F_j. In particular the large partner's generic normal has not been dropped. ## 4. The explicit surviving derivative tail All expressions in this section are at Q=Q_0. Put a=Q^(-j), b=Q^(-l), c_k=(a;Q)_k(b;Q)_k(X;Q)_k Q^k /[(Q;Q)_k^2(T^(-1);Q)_k], L_k(y)=-sum_(r=0)^(k-1) y Q^r/(1-y Q^r). For k<=j, every factor in L_k(a),L_k(b) is a unit. Differentiating (1) in B and subtracting cancels the common denominator derivative. For k>j the single vanishing numerator factor has derivative [y partial_y(y;Q)_k]_(y=Q^(-j)) =-(a;Q)_j(Q;Q)_(k-j-1). Thus the ORIGINAL normal is w_j=x^u/Delta * { sum_(k=0)^j c_k [L_k(b)-L_k(a)] +(a;Q)_j sum_(k=j+1)^l (b;Q)_k(Q;Q)_(k-j-1)(X;Q)_k Q^k /[(Q;Q)_k^2(T^(-1);Q)_k] }. (11) The second line is a nonempty tail whenever j<l. Bounded harmonic coefficients in the first line do not bound this coherent sum relative to F_j; nor do they remove the tail. Equation (11) records all of it with the original normalizer. ## 5. Genuine extra poles obstruct a whole-wedge normal theorem As a polynomial in X, w_j/x^u has EXACT degree l. Only the k=l tail term contributes its highest coefficient, which is (-1)^l Q^[l(l+1)/2] (Q^(-l);Q)_l(Q^(-j);Q)_j(Q;Q)_(l-j-1) /[Delta (Q;Q)_l^2(T^(-1);Q)_l]. (12) Its numerator is nonzero: all nonzero factorial indices are less than N, and 2j+1<N gives Delta!=0. Therefore each divisor T=Q^r, j<=r<l, (13) is a genuine SIMPLE pole of the normalized normal for generic X. The highest-coefficient residue is nonzero and cannot be canceled by lower powers of X. Its residue polynomial has degree l, so it does not vanish on an open set of magnetic coordinates. The ordinary small column F_j has no pole at any of (13). Its denominator only uses r<j. If N/2<r<l, the scaled pair degree tau=r/N lies strictly inside the joint central wedge. An open set of its central magnetic coordinates avoids the finitely many roots of the residue polynomial. Thus the actual terminating continuation of this INDIVIDUAL first normal cannot be holomorphic on that whole wedge, let alone admit a uniform relative polynomial estimate there. These additional divisors lie below the physical high-partner range t>=l. On a fixed compact tau>1/2 they disappear when j/N is sufficiently close to 1/2. Consequently (13) does not disprove a smaller corridor near the folded endpoint. It also does not prove such a corridor estimate: the tail in (11) still requires control. Finally, (13) is not a theorem about poles of the entire mixed coupon. The original inverse measure and the other terms may cancel individual-column poles. Nor does it exclude a separately specified whole-source continuation. It rules out silently extending the ordinary-column joint theorem to this canonical generic normal. Audit: [generic collision, original normal and pole certificates](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.py). Independent analytical review and fresh audit: PASS. A second reader rederived the Newton-basis coefficient ratio, checked the fixed-degree Laurent-support extension, actual eigenvalue-gap sign, transverse factor, core and tail signs, and the noncanceling highest-coefficient poles. The fresh audit passed 4,123 original generic-q normal comparisons, 445 nonphysical tail checks and 614 nonzero extra-pole residues, as well as the generic transformations and noncyclotomic collisions. No smaller-corridor estimate or full-coupon pole is inferred. Primary-agent independent analytical review and fresh replay: PASS. It checked the actual-source ratio recurrence and all-degree extension, the tensor-eigenvalue gap convention, transverse derivative and tail factor two, and the nonzero leading pole residues. The same focused audit counts passed; the stated scope is unchanged.

title: Every fixed generic jet of an actual physical q-Hahn column
status: All physical generic column and divided-pair jets
text: # Every fixed generic jet of an actual physical q-Hahn column 30 October 2026. This note extends the physical prefix estimate to the original generic deformation. Every fixed generic-q derivative of every admissible physical column has polynomial cost relative to its nonzero root value, including large channels. The actual divided pair also has polynomial fixed generic jets. The upper half of the column is treated by its backward generic recurrence, not by differentiating a root-only reflection identity. The statement is on integer physical degrees and magnetic indices. It supplies no fixed complex magnetic neighborhood, no nonzero confluent amplitude, and no completed four-port or network norm. ## 1. The actual generic column and its endpoints Fix N>=3, d=N-1, q0=exp(pi i/N), and integers 0<=m<=t<=d, 0<=u<=t. Write q=q0 exp(epsilon), Q=q^2, x=q^d, v=t-u, and F_r=(Q;Q)_r. The original finite source is C_m(q;t,u)=sum_(a=max(0,m-v))^(min(m,u)) (-1)^a x^(u-2a) Q^[av+a(a-1)/2] F_(N-m+a-1)F_(N-a-1)/(F_(N-m-1)F_(N-1)) [u choose a]_Q [v choose m-a]_Q/[t choose m]_Q. (1) These are precisely the genuine generic highest-vector ratios of the [mixed compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md), not the squared-binomial formula obtained after root specialization. All factorial indices in (1) are below N. The function is regular near q0. Its endpoints are exact monomials: C_m(q;t,0)=1, C_m(q;t,t)=(-1)^m q^[dt-2Nm+m^2+m]. (2) For the second equality only a=m survives; the original ratio of F-factorials is then one. These formulas hold before differentiating. There are universal c,C>0 such that, simultaneously for all the integer indices above, C_m(q0;t,u)!=0, |C_m(q0 exp(epsilon);t,u)/C_m(q0;t,u)|<=C for |epsilon|<=cN^(-8). (3) The functions in (3) are holomorphic on that disk. In particular, for every fixed r>=0, |D^r C_m(q0;t,u)|<=C_r N^(8r)|C_m(q0;t,u)|, D=q d/dq. (4) There is no small-channel restriction on m in (3),(4). ## 2. The original generic physical Casimir block The degree-t balanced tensor basis has entries indexed by u=0,...,t. Let J_t(q) have diagonal D_u, upper entries A_u^+ and lower entries A_u^- (the superscripts refer to the matrix positions). A direct application of the original generic coproduct gives D_u=q^-1 Q^(u-t)(1-Q^(N-u))(1-Q^u) +q^(-2d-1)Q^u(1-Q^(N-t+u))(1-Q^(t-u)) +q^(2d+1)Q^-t+q^(-2d-1)Q^t, (J_t)_(u,u+1)=A_u^+ =q^-N Q^(2u+1-t)(1-Q^(N-u-1))(1-Q^(t-u)), (J_t)_(u+1,u)=A_u^- =q^-N(1-Q^(N-t+u))(1-Q^(u+1)), 0<=u<t. (5) For example the lower offdiagonal is the contribution of F on the first head after E on the second; the upper offdiagonal retains both Cartan factors of the opposite path. Their generic values differ. Replacing them by their equal root values before differentiating would change the source. The vector (1) satisfies J_t(q) C_m(q;t,.)=lambda_m(q) C_m(q;t,.), lambda_m=q^(2N-2m-1)+q^(-2N+2m+1). (6) This follows from its highest degree m, highest weight 2d-2m, and the original coproduct Casimir. Alternatively, substitution of the finite highest-vector and its divided descendants yields (5),(6) entry by entry. Thus the normalization C_m(0)=1 in the magnetic index fixes the SAME source vector, not an auxiliary eigenvector. At q0 the two offdiagonals in (5) coincide, and (5) simplifies to D_u=U/T [2(q0^-1+q0 T)-(q0+q0^-1)U], A_u=(U-T)(1-Q0 U)/T, U=Q0^u, T=Q0^t, Q0=q0^2. (7) For the reversal matrix P_t, (7) also gives P_t J_t(q0) P_t=conjugate(J_t(q0)). (8) Only this ROOT identity is needed below. No generic version of (8), or a flat high-degree adapter, is assumed. ## 3. A polynomial generic neighborhood from prefix coercivity The [physical prefix theorem](actual_q_hahn_physical_partner_normal_bound.md) proves, for every 1<=h<=floor(t/2), Im J_[h](q0) >= 4 sin^3(pi/N)/h^2 * I. (9) Although that note applies the estimate to complete double channels, its weighted-row identity and positive Dirichlet proof use only 1<=t<=d and h<=floor(t/2). In this entire range the weights 1/sin((t-r)pi/N) are positive, its row residual is 4 sin(r pi/N) sin^2(pi/N) sin(t pi/N) /sin((t-r-1)pi/N)>=0, and every retained conductance is at least 4sin(pi/N).
