The same Poincare step therefore proves (9) for all t used here. It requires no sign assumption on -cos((t+1)pi/N) and no channel condition t>=l. The bound is independent of the real spectral parameter. Since lambda_m(q0) is real, it implies ||(lambda_m(q0)I-J_[h](q0))^-1||<=C N^5. (10) The reversed prefix has the conjugate root matrix by (8), hence has the same inverse bound. This holds for every m<=t, not merely for the two members of a double node. Every elementary exponent in (5),(6) is O(N). On a fixed disk |epsilon|<=c/N the entries and eigenvalues are O(1) and their epsilon derivatives are O(N), uniformly over all indices. The bandwidth is fixed. For either the forward or reversed prefix, ||M(epsilon)-M(0)||<=C N|epsilon|, M(epsilon)=lambda_m(q)I-J_prefix(q). (11) Combining (10),(11), on rho_N=cN^(-8) the relative perturbation has norm at most Cc/N^2. Decrease c so that it is below 1/2. For prefix size h<=N, |det M(epsilon)/det M(0)| <=(1+Cc/N^2)^h<=C, (12) and the determinant is nonzero throughout the disk. The offdiagonal products introduce only polynomial local costs. At the root |A_u^+|=|A_u^-| =4 sin((t-u)pi/N) sin((u+1)pi/N) >=4 sin^2(pi/N)>=16/N^2. (13) Equation (5) gives derivative O(N), so these entries remain nonzero on the same disk. Their relative logarithmic changes are bounded by C N^3|epsilon|. A product of at most N such entries therefore has a uniformly bounded ratio to its root value, and so does its inverse. In fact its logarithmic change is O(N^4|epsilon|). For u<=floor(t/2), the exact forward recurrence gives C_m(q;t,u)=det(lambda_m(q)I-J_[u](q)) / product_(r=0)^(u-1) A_r^+(q). (14) The empty determinant and product at u=0 are one. Equations (10)--(14) prove root nonvanishing and (3) on this half. For u>=ceil(t/2), put h=t-u and reverse the ACTUAL generic recurrence. Normalize its endpoint by the exact nonzero C_m(q;t,t) in (2). The normalized reversed column has initial entry one and is again a leading-prefix determinant divided by its own upper offdiagonal product. Its prefix has size h<=floor(t/2). Equations (8)--(13) apply to this reversed generic matrix because its ROOT is conjugate to the forward one and its generic entries satisfy the SAME bounds. The endpoint exponent in (2) is O(N^2), so its ratio on the small disk is also uniformly bounded. This proves (3) on the upper half, including t=0,1 by the endpoint formulas alone. Cauchy's formula now gives (4) for the genuine generic source. The derivative holds N,t,u fixed, as the original compiler does. ## 4. The completed divided pair also has fixed generic jets Suppose j<l, j+l=d and l<=t. Put s=l-j and define the ORIGINAL generic divided pair W_(j,l)(q;t,u)= (C_j(q;t,u)-C_l(q;t,u))/(lambda_j(q)-lambda_l(q)). (15) The [exact collision identity](actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.md) gives C_j(q0;t,u)=C_l(q0;t,u), and its actual gap is lambda_j-lambda_l=(q^s-q^-s)(q^N-q^-N). (16) The second factor has a simple zero at q0; the first does not. Thus (15) has a removable singularity, with root value exactly the retained physical paired normal W_(j,l)(q0;t,u) =[D C_j-D C_l]/[-2N Delta_j], Delta_j=q0^(2j+1)-q0^(-2j-1)=q0^s-q0^-s. (17) On |epsilon|=rho_N, the first factor in (16) has modulus at least c/N and the second at least cN rho_N. There are no other zeros inside this disk. The two bounds (3), using their equal root values, therefore give |W_(j,l)(q;t,u)|<=C rho_N^-1 |C_j(q0;t,u)| on |epsilon|=rho_N. Cauchy's formula applied AFTER the removable singularity is filled proves, for every fixed r>=0, |D^r W_(j,l)(q0;t,u)| <=C_r N^[8(r+1)] |C_j(q0;t,u)|. (18) For r=0 the earlier N^6 physical paired-normal estimate is sharper. The additional content here is the higher genuine generic-q jets, including the variation of the matrix, both original columns, and the gap. Equation (18) is not obtained by treating a q derivative as a spectral derivative. For example D W at the root contains second q derivatives of the original columns, as it must. ## 5. Interface and limits The [matching-edge rewrite](actual_matching_edge_marked_four_port_block.md) needs Taylor order two after clearing its simple poles. Equations (4),(18) remove a possible physical-column obstruction to controlling such jets. To apply them to a completed target pair one must STILL prove its exact expression in these normalized columns, their divided pair, and its actual scalar measures. The native boundary cost of that four-port tensor has not been replaced by a polynomial in this note. Nor is a surrounding contraction estimated here. The estimates concern integer t,u. They do not prove a fixed complex magnetic corridor or control the extra poles of the large partner's unrestricted continuation. The separate shrinking-channel complex theorem and the present physical generic theorem address different domains. No lower bound for W or a nonzero selected global contribution follows from either upper estimate. Audit: [original generic physical matrix and retained divided-pair jets](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_physical_generic_jet_bound.py). The focused exact audit passed 1,204 original physical column four-jets, 1,204 generic eigenvector equations, 2,408 forward/backward comparisons, 432 generic endpoint jets, and 378 divided-pair jets through order two. It retains 4,816 column and 1,134 pair coefficients; 323 tested second pair jets are nonzero. Those checks verify source and normal conventions, while the prefix perturbation proof supplies the uniform bounds. Two independent analytical reviews passed the genuine generic matrix, the all-t prefix coercivity, exact backward endpoint normalization, polynomial disk and offdiagonal estimates, and the original removable gap with its retained generic derivatives. One reviewer independently replayed the focused audit and reproduced all reported counts. The reviews preserve the integer physical domain and do not infer a completed four-port norm or a fixed complex magnetic neighborhood.

title: A polynomial bound for the actual partner normal on the physical grid
status: All physical paired first normals; complex corridor open
text: # A polynomial bound for the actual partner normal on the physical grid Subsequent complex estimate: the [near-fold theorem](actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md) controls the full paired normal on a fixed complex compact when (l-j) log N=o(N). It is a relative upper bound in a shrinking scaled channel window; fixed nonzero scaled shifts and a leading normal amplitude remain open. The theorem below retains its original scope. 30 October 2026. Every original physical magnetic entry of a complete double Casimir channel has a polynomially bounded confluent normal relative to its nonzero ordinary value. This includes both halves of every physical degree block, both parities, and every complete double channel. The estimate is for the ACTUAL generic divided difference. It is not an estimate obtained by differentiating a root-only formula. The argument is a positive-imaginary-part estimate for a half-prefix of the original complex symmetric Casimir matrix, followed by its exact reflection symmetry through first order at a double spectral node. No complex magnetic continuation, global magnetic contour, or whole marked-source estimate follows from this physical-grid statement. ## 1. The source and the quantitative statement Put theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), Q=q^2, d=N-1, x=q^d. Let 0<=j<l, j+l=d, l<=t<=d, 0<=u<=t, c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1), Delta_j=q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1). All these indices are integers. Let C_(j,u) be the original root column normalized by C_(j,0)=1. Let w_(j,u) be its actual confluent normal as specified by [the mixed compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md): w_(j,u)=[D C_(j,u)-D C_(l,u)]/[-2N Delta_j], D=zeta d/dzeta, evaluated at zeta=q. (1) Both generic columns in (1) use the original highest weight d and its full factorial ratio. Then EVERY C_(j,u) is nonzero and |w_(j,u)/C_(j,u)|<=N^6/256+N^2/8. (2) If t/N stays in a fixed compact subset of (0,1), the right side can be replaced by C_K N^4. In the present complete range t>=l this only requires a fixed upper separation from t/N=1. No separation from the folded channel is required. ## 2. The actual prefix has positive imaginary part The original degree-t Casimir block J_t is complex symmetric tridiagonal, as proved directly from the balanced tensor operators in [the complete Hermite packet](actual_complete_casimir_hermite_packet.md). For r=0,...,t put U_r=Q^r, T=Q^t. Its entries simplify exactly to D_r=U_r/T [2(q^(-1)+qT)-(q+q^(-1))U_r], A_r=(U_r-T)(1-QU_r)/T, 0<=r<t. (3) Every A_r is nonzero. For 1<=m<=floor(t/2), let J_[m] be its leading m-by-m principal submatrix. Because the matrix is symmetric, its Hermitian imaginary part is the entrywise imaginary-part matrix. Set h_r=(t-2r)theta and c=-cos((t+1)theta). Its diagonal and upper offdiagonal imaginary parts, including the next boundary coefficient, are d_r=4 sin(h_r)[c+cos(theta)cos(h_r)], o_r=4 sin(h_r-theta)sin((t-r)theta)sin((r+1)theta). (4) For 0<=r<m these o_r are positive. Introduce positive weights a_r=1/sin((t-r)theta), 0<=r<=m. A direct sine expansion gives the EXACT weighted row identity d_r-o_(r-1)a_(r-1)/a_r-o_r a_(r+1)/a_r =4 sin(r theta)sin^2(theta)sin(t theta) /sin((t-r-1)theta) >=0, (5) where the r=0 term involving o_(-1) is absent. The right side is zero at r=0. All denominators in (5) are positive in the stated range. One elementary verification expands sin(b-a) and cos(a+b+theta), with a=r theta and b=(t-r)theta. After multiplying by sin(b-theta)/4, the residual is precisely sin(a)sin^2(theta)sin(a+b). Conjugate Im J_[m] by diag(1,-1,1,...), so its offdiagonals are -o_r. For a vector v write v_r=a_r y_r, and set y_m=0. Equation (5) expresses its quadratic form as sum_(r=0)^(m-1) k_r |y_r-y_(r+1)|^2 +sum_(r=0)^(m-1) V_r a_r^2 |y_r|^2, k_r=o_r a_r a_(r+1) =4 sin((t-2r-1)theta)sin((r+1)theta) /sin((t-r-1)theta), V_r=the nonnegative right side of (5). (6) There is a genuine Dirichlet term at the right endpoint; it is not discarded when the prefix is taken. The conductances obey k_r>=4 sin(theta). (7) Indeed the two numerator sine arguments alpha,beta are at least theta, with alpha+beta=(t-r)theta<pi. On the interval theta<=alpha<=alpha+beta-theta, their product is minimized at an endpoint, so sin(alpha)sin(beta)>=sin(theta) sin(alpha+beta-theta), which is (7). Since a_r<=1/sin(theta) and sum|y_r|^2<=m^2 sum|y_r-y_(r+1)|^2, equations (6),(7) prove Im J_[m] >= [4 sin^3(theta)/m^2] I. (8) The sign-conjugation is unitary and does not change this lower bound. For t/N in a fixed compact inside (0,1), all a_r in this half-prefix are uniformly bounded; the stronger lower bound is c_K/N^3. ## 3. Lower-half spectral derivatives Let f_r(z) be the original normalized forward column, f_0=1, f_r(z)=det(zI-J_[r])/(A_0 ... A_(r-1)). (9) The real point c_j is a double eigenvalue of J_t. The actual source and normal are exactly C_(j,r)=f_r(c_j), w_(j,r)=f_r'(c_j). (10) This is the generic-confluence identity in the complete Hermite packet and the mixed compiler: differentiating the two normalized generic columns cancels the common q derivative and retains the original eigenvalue-gap derivative -2N Delta_j. For ANY real z, (8) gives ||(zI-J_[m])^(-1)||<=m^2/[4 sin^3(theta)]. In particular the determinant in (9) is nonzero there. Taking its logarithmic derivative gives |f_m'(z)/f_m(z)| =|tr((zI-J_[m])^(-1))| <=m^3/[4 sin^3(theta)]. (11) Since m<=N/2 and sin(theta)>=2/N, (11) is at most N^6/256. The compact-degree improvement of (8) gives C_K N^4 instead. For m=0 the normal is zero and the value is 1. ## 4. Reflection extends the bound through the full physical block Let P reverse the indices 0,...,t. Formula (3) gives exactly P J_t P=conjugate(J_t). (12) The characteristic polynomial is p_(t+1)(z)=product_(m=0)^t(z-c_m), and the forward column satisfies (J_t-zI)f(z)=-p_(t+1)(z)e_t/(A_0 ... A_(t-1)). (13) At a double node c_j, both the residual and its first derivative vanish. Reflecting and conjugating (13), and using uniqueness of the forward recurrence with its first component fixed, therefore gives, at that node, f_(t-r)=f_t conjugate(f_r), f'_(t-r)=f'_t conjugate(f_r)+f_t conjugate(f'_r). (14) This is a first-order identity at a DOUBLE node. It is not inferred by differentiating a value identity known only at isolated points. One may justify (14) as an identity modulo (z-c_j)^2: the reflected column has first entry conjugate(f_t(conjugate z)); its first-row error is a multiple of p_(t+1)(z), so its forward recurrence agrees to this order. Setting r=t in the value identity gives |f_t|=1. The endpoint normal has a particularly simple ORIGINAL generic calculation. At u=t only a=m survives in the generic Clebsch sum, and its highest-vector ratio R_(m,m) is identically 1. Thus C_(m,t)(zeta)=(-1)^m zeta^[d(t-2m)+m(m-1)]. (15) The two exponents for j,l differ by N(l-j). Combining (15) with the actual gap in (1) gives f'_t(c_j)/f_t(c_j)=-(l-j)/(2 Delta_j), |f'_t/f_t|<N/[4 sin(theta)]<=N^2/8. (16) For r>t/2 apply (14) with t-r in the lower half. Its value is nonzero and f'_r/f_r=f'_t/f_t+conjugate(f'_(t-r)/f_(t-r)). (17) Equations (11),(16),(17) prove (2) for every physical entry. ## 5. Scope of the estimate The paired normal, including its formerly hidden large-channel contribution, is controlled on the entire physical grid. Its exponential rate there cannot exceed that of its ordinary column by more than O(log N)/N. This is a relative entrywise statement; it does not control cancellations after a whole graph is sewn. The high-total-degree blocks are transported by the constant Chevalley-plus-flip adapter in the complete Hermite packet. Thus the same root spectral-column estimate applies after the stated physical index translation. It is the root confluent column being transported here, not a new generic-q adapter assumed to be flat. The estimate does NOT extend by continuity to a fixed complex magnetic neighborhood. The canonical large-partner continuation has the additional degree poles proved in [the generic collision note](actual_q_hahn_partner_normal_collision.md), and its finite tail requires a separate complex estimate. A bound on integer magnetic samples, even at all levels, supplies no such analytic continuation theorem. Focused audit: [original normal, positive prefix and reflection](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_physical_partner_normal_bound.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_physical_partner_normal_bound_results.json). The symbolic weighted-row identity passed. Exact arithmetic checked 131 original Casimir blocks, 726 weighted-row identities, 8,578 actual generic paired normals and their first-order reflections, and 571 original endpoint normals. At 90 digits, 10,164 actual relative-normal bounds passed; the audit also checked 288 positive prefix matrices and 2,384 conductance inequalities. These finite checks supplement the uniform proof above. An independent analytical review checked the original source conventions, weighted Dirichlet identity, conductance minimum, Poincare bound and N^6 constant, the reflected recurrence modulo the double characteristic zero, and the generic endpoint exponent difference N(l-j). It also checked that the high-degree adapter transports the actual root spectral column without assuming flatness of an individual generic derivative. Its verdict covers the stated physical-grid theorem only. A second independent analytical review and fresh replay passed. That reader verified the weighted row identity independently as a formal Laurent identity, the alternating conjugation and boundary Dirichlet term, the conductance and resolvent constants, and the first-order reflection with the actual generic endpoint sign. The fresh audit passed all reported exact and high-precision checks, including 8,578 original generic paired normals and 571 endpoints. No complex magnetic continuation or whole-source bound is inferred.

title: Genuine numerator normals at positive-total framing boundaries
status: Actual positive-total boundary determinants and generic normals
text: # Genuine numerator normals at positive-total framing boundaries 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. A uniform spectral gap for the SUM of the two original positive matrices controls the actual generic numerator in both the202 and222 boundary regimes. The actual total square root and every logarithmic head lift remain in the source normalization. Near the fold, all fixed genuine quantum derivatives have subexponential relative cost when the partner separation satisfies s log N=o(N). This is a numerator theorem. It does not assign a generic amplitude to a root collision or prove a global source period. The separate root222 determinant action and the root202 coefficient packet retain their own normalizations and hypotheses. ## 1. An exact uniform gap, including the folded endpoint Let theta=pi/N, N>=3, and 1<=a<=floor((N-1)/2). Use the actual Hermitian H_-,H_+ from the [source determinant](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md), with diagonal d_r=1/[cos(r theta)cos((r+1)theta)] and upper entries sqrt(B_n)[sin(n theta) +/- i cos(n theta)], B_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. Then EXACTLY H_-+H_+ >= cos(theta) I >= I/2. (1) Here is a direct weighted-path proof. Put J=(H_-+H_+)/2 and w_r=sqrt(sin((2r+1)theta)), 0<=r<a. Alternating-sign conjugation turns its real offdiagonal e_n=sqrt(B_n)sin(n theta) negative. For an interior row r, subtracting its two weighted neighbors from the diagonal gives d_r-e_r w_(r-1)/w_r-e_(r+1)w_(r+1)/w_r = [sin(r theta)cos(r theta)/(1+sin(r theta)) +sin((r+1)theta)cos((r+1)theta) /(1+sin((r+1)theta))] /sin((2r+1)theta) >= cos(theta)/2. (2) For the equality, use sin((2r+1)theta)=sin(r theta)cos((r+1)theta) +sin((r+1)theta)cos(r theta). For the inequality, bound both denominators 1+sin by 2 and use sin(r theta)cos(r theta)+sin((r+1)theta)cos((r+1)theta) =sin((2r+1)theta)cos(theta). The r=0 formula has its left term zero. At the final row r=a-1, subtracting the finite positive quantity sin^2(a theta)/[cos(a theta)sin((2a-1)theta)] from the ACTUAL one-neighbor residual gives exactly the expression in (2). Thus that actual residual is larger. This last comparison does not introduce a virtual B_a or w_a: at the maximal odd fold those separate quantities would be singular or zero. All weights and coefficients actually used in the matrix are positive. For a=1 the same finite comparison applies with no actual neighbor. Finally, for x_r=w_r y_r the quadratic form is the sum of e_n w_(n-1)w_n |y_n-y_(n-1)|^2 and the weighted residual diagonal terms. Thus (2) proves J>=cos(theta)I/2 and hence (1). No limiting matrix or unproved eigenvalue asymptotic is used. ## 2. The actual total phase and the two boundary domains Fix the actual logarithmic heads sigma,u and put, GENERICALLY, q=q0 exp(epsilon), Q=q^2, B=Q^-N, U=q^(2u), V=q^(2(sigma-u)), b=q^sigma, X=qU, Y=qV, T=XY=q^2UV, w=qb=q^(sigma+1), z=b/U. In particular T=w^2 and z/w=1/X exactly. The square root w is the original exponential, not a freely chosen branch. At the root, the exact normalized source is H_n^1(U,V)=(qUV)^n K_n det M_n, M_n=X^-1 I-H_-/2-H_+/(2T), (3) where K_n=[2n choose n]_Q for the small channel n and the matrices are its n-row truncations. Indeed the original monic determinant is R_n(z)=det[zI-(wH_-+w^-1H_+)/2]; divide its matrix by w and use H_n=b^n K_n R_n. Thus the factor w^n, including its sign and every integer logarithmic character, is retained in (qUV)^n. For physical half-index heads write X=exp(2pi i x), Y=exp(2pi i y), sigma=N(x+y)-1. Then w=exp(pi i(x+y)) exactly. On the canonical physical logarithms, when T is positive and both arguments lie strictly between 0 and 2pi, their sum is 2pi and w is the NEGATIVE square root of T. The same sign persists in that marked neighborhood. If another actual integral lift changes this sign, (3) retains the change; none of the estimates below replaces it by the canonical sign. Let T at epsilon=0 range in a sufficiently small fixed complex neighborhood of a compact subset of (0,infinity). Two domains are allowed: * 202: X/N^2 belongs to a fixed compact subset of C*. * 222: X belongs to a fixed compact neighborhood of a negative real compact subset of C*. Require the marked heads to satisfy |sigma|+|u|<=C N(1+log N). These are conditions on the actual arguments, not on an arbitrarily reset logarithm. In202, Y=T/X is small; in222 both raw finite clocks are near negative reals. The [actual prefix-sign theorem](actual_right_angled_resonant_prefix_signs.md) supplies precisely these limiting signs where its dictionary applies. For all sufficiently large N, on both domains the matrix in (3) satisfies Re(-M_n)>=cI, ||M_n^-1||<=C, (4) uniformly for all small n through the fold. Indeed Re(1/T)>=eta>0, and (1) bounds H_-+eta H_+ below by a fixed positive multiple of I. For202 the term 1/X is O(N^-2), so it cannot close that gap. For222, Re(1/X)<0 adds a positive diagonal term. Thus the root numerator is nonzero. This proof retains the additive identity term and does not infer an inverse bound from positivity alone. ## 3. A genuine generic disk and its cofactor The all-degree ORIGINAL generic recurrence, with B=Q^-N retained, is R_(n+1)=(z+alpha_n)R_n+beta_n R_(n-1). Its coefficients and rational all-degree proof are in the [actual paired-normal theorem](actual_q_hahn_near_fold_complex_partner_bound.md). Here the generic scalar is K_n(q)=(B^2Q^(n+1);Q)_n/(BQ;Q)_n, whose root value is the Gaussian binomial in (3). Its generic derivatives are not those of that root simplification. Set G_n=R_n/w^n. As exact generic identities, G_(n+1)=(X^-1+alpha_n/w)G_n+(beta_n/w^2)G_(n-1), H_n^B(U,V)=(qUV)^n K_n G_n. (5) For n<=a the nonzero original spectral differences are bounded below by cN^-2 on a small polynomial disk. Here b and w are bounded above and away from zero; their derivatives have size O(N log N). The quotient formulas for alpha_n,beta_n therefore give (alpha_n/w)'=O(N^5(1+log N)), (beta_n/w^2)'=O(N^7(1+log N)). (6) The original b_n,d_n in those formulas are O(1), with derivatives O(N(1+log N)); the preceding u_n and v_n have sizes O(N^2),O(N^4). This gives (6) directly, with no generic specialization of a root reflection. The derivative of X^-1 is no larger than O(N log N) in either domain and is smaller in202. For each edge of the actual root matrix M_a, freeze whichever of its upper and lower entries has larger absolute value. Their SUM is -sqrt(B_n)sin(n theta)(1+T^-1). Since sqrt(B_n)>=1/2 and |1+T^-1| is bounded below, the frozen entry has absolute value at least c/N for every n=1,...,a-1. The first bound follows directly from sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)<=sin^2(2n theta) and the displayed formula for B_n. Keep it in its ORIGINAL orientation and put the other generic entry equal to -beta_n/(w^2 frozen_entry). The diagonal is X^-1+alpha_n/w. At the root this is exactly M_a, with all edge phases intact. At generic q its determinant and every leading principal minor are exactly the recurrence in (5), since each adjacent product is the original one. No constant choice of upper versus lower is required, and no parameter-dependent similarity is silently dropped. By (6) this generic matrix differs from its root by O(N^8(1+log N)|epsilon|) in operator norm. Choose |epsilon|<=rho_N=cN^-10. (7) Equations (4),(6) give uniformly bounded inverse and two-sided determinant ratio. Indeed the logarithm of the determinant ratio costs at most O(N^9(1+log N)rho_N), which is bounded and tends to zero. The last diagonal inverse entry is the actual cofactor, so |G_(a-1)/G_a|<=C. (8) The exact source scalar K_a has logarithmic derivative O(N^3), and (qUV)^a has logarithmic derivative O(N^2(1+log N)). Their two-sided ratios are bounded on (7). Thus the small H_a itself has bounded two-sided relative variation on this disk. ## 4. The actual large partner and every fixed normal Let m=d-a, s=m-a, with 0<=s<=eta N and eta sufficiently small. The literal root identity is H_m^1=P_s(UV)H_a^1, where P_s(UV)=product_(r=a)^(m-1)(UV-Q^r). Since UV=q0^-2T is near a positive real compact and these r lie near N/2, every added factor is bounded above and away from zero. In particular H_m^1 is nonzero. On the boundary of (7), the original folded spectral differences are at least c rho_N; all others are at least cN^-2. The ORIGINAL generic recurrence coefficients alpha_n/w and beta_n/w^2 are therefore at most C rho_N^-1 and C rho_N^-2. Starting from (8), propagating the s rows costs at most (CN^20)^s. The exact generic K_m/K_a ratio has 2s numerator factors and 2s denominator factors. Those denominator indices stay near N/2, so the ratio costs only C^s. The factor (qUV)^s also costs C^s relative to the retained root P_s(UV). Thus on the circle, and then throughout its disk, |H_m^B(U(q),V(q))/H_m^1(U(q0),V(q0))| <=C(CN^20)^s. (9) The passage inside uses the ORIGINAL finite H_m sum: all its generic factorial denominators have indices below N and are units on this disk. Singular monic R_m factors were never assigned a holomorphic root value. Cauchy's formula now gives, for each fixed k, |partial_epsilon^k H_m^B|_0 <=C_k N^(10k)(CN^20)^s |H_m^1(U(q0),V(q0))|. (10) For s=0 this follows directly from the small determinant argument. For bounded s the cost is polynomial, covering both maximal folded parities. For s log N=o(N) it is subexponential. This does not cover a fixed nonzero scaled partner separation and does not give a nonzero leading normal amplitude. The source factor (qUV)^n, the integer characters and every marked head are retained before taking the derivative. The result applies to the individual actual202/222 numerator factors. Any surrounding white monomials, cups, pivots, marks and finite support cycles must still use their literal source identities and their own estimates. Neither the positive gap nor finite-jet control selects the original global relative period. Focused audit: [positive-total source and retained-normal checks](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_positive_total_boundary_normals.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_positive_total_boundary_normals_results.json). The 120-digit run checks both exact trigonometric identities, 389 actual weighted rows including 24 finite last-row comparisons, 24 folded matrix gaps, 12 original root phase/determinant identities, 48 original generic determinants and 48 cofactors, 48 actual large-partner generic-circle values and 24 first/second normals. Four cases have one root edge EXACTLY zero and retain the opposite edge. Twelve tests keep identical root clocks but change sigma to sigma+N; their genuine first normals differ, verifying why marked lifts cannot be reset. Maximum source error was below 3.3e-119. These finite checks supplement the proof; they do not establish its uniform estimates by numerical sampling. Independent full analytical reviews checked the finite endpoint gap, actual marked source normalization, both coercive boundary domains, oriented larger-edge construction through an exactly zero opposite edge, generic determinant and cofactor perturbation, folded spectral denominators, retained K_m/P_s scalar factors, and holomorphy of the original finite sum before Cauchy's estimate. Fresh redirected audit replays passed all stated checks at 120 digits. The primary reader's separate full proof review and fresh replay also passed, including the marked-lift normal differences. The result remains the stated individual-numerator, shrinking-channel normal bound; no leading normal amplitude, whole-network contraction estimate or global relative-cycle coefficient is inferred.

title: The original q-Hahn source at a resonant framing boundary
status: Original resonant boundary packets and retained source zeros
text: # The original q-Hahn source at a resonant framing boundary 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. The actual prefix words give an explicit degeneration of the original white arguments when the residual framing parameter tends to infinity. One of its large-clock regimes has a uniform, source-normalized Bessel limit. The numerator is the actual LARGE generic-channel numerator specialized at the root; neither a scalar symbol nor an off-lattice channel is substituted. This is a local root-value boundary model. Genuine quantum normals are separate. It neither puts every box in this regime nor computes the coefficient of the geometric component in the original global period. ## 1. Actual prefix words determine the escaping heads Normalize the reference positive meridian to J=[[1,1],[0,1]], and keep the original common framing F(r,s)=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], with s nonzero. For every actual based prefix Q=[[a,b],[c,d]] put L_Q(r)=Tr(Q F E11 F^-1) =-c r^2/s+(a-d+c/s)r+d+b s. (1) These are the actual prefix diagonals. On a fixed horizontal cut the physical clock of its i-th wire is X_i=-L_(Q_(i-1))/L_(Q_i). No independent local frame is chosen. For the complete discrete faithful holonomy, each prefix is either genuinely quadratic in (1), or constant. Indeed c=0 implies a=d=+/-1. To see this directly, conjugating J by Q supplies translations a^(2n). If |a^2| differs from one these accumulate at the identity. If |a^2|=1, the discrete additive group generated by these translations has rank at most two; rotations preserving it form a finite group. Thus a^2 is a root of unity. If a^2 is not one, the upper triangular Q has finite projective order, contrary to the free deck action. Consequently Q=+/-[[1,b0],[0,1]], whose L_Q is constant. This argument uses actual holonomy words, not arbitrary matrices assigned to ports. Fix s so all the finitely many constant L_Q are nonzero. Let e(Q)=0 in this constant case and e(Q)=1 in the quadratic case. At r=N rho, with rho in a fixed compact subset of C*, X_i=C_i(s) r^k_i (1+O(1/r)), k_i=2(e(Q_(i-1))-e(Q_i)) in {-2,0,2}. (2) For two quadratic prefixes the limiting ratio is the ratio of their lower-left entries, with the displayed minus sign. These are actual geometric limiting data. They are not independently optimized. The k_i obey the homogeneous original cup/cap/coupon incidence equations, since the exact products of the corresponding clocks do. Thus the logarithmic escape is one coupled integral flow. On a cut, each run of quadratic prefixes has paired -2/+2 boundary transitions. The exact finite affine offsets have a uniform convenient realization. If X_i=exp(2pi i x_i) with the recorded logarithmic lift, set i_i=N x_i-1/2, Q_N^(i_i)=q_N^-1 X_i. (3) This prescription applies to the PHYSICAL V_d heads. It gives every physical cup/cap i_1+i_2=N-1 and q_N^(d-2i_i)=-1/X_i. At a white vertex define the channel row by its ORIGINAL equation r0=i_1+i_2-(d-a), with the actual discrete a retained. An auxiliary V_(2a) head is not assigned the same universal -1/2 offset. Its finite color is equivalently (a+1/2)/N. Thus degree constraints remain exact, but this is not evaluation of every finite channel at the complete parabolic stationary point. It samples the principal geometric germ without asserting finite-N stationary equations. For k_i!=0, the imaginary index has size N log N. For X_i=1+zeta/r+O(r^-2), instead, i_i=zeta/(2pi i rho)-1/2+O(N^-1), (4) up to its retained integer logarithmic lift. The -1/2 is essential. A point near a negative half-integer is not an original integer support zero. An O(1/N) perturbation of a clock near one must not be discarded. The same caution applies to characters: exp(2pi i i_i)=-X_i^N. (5) Its magnitude need not be one, and can be N^(2N) in (2). ## 2. The literal white, dual and exceptional arguments At a circle write a0=L_W, a1=L_(AW), a1'=L_(Aout W), a2=L_(PW), where P=BA=Bout Aout and W is its original prefix. Its incoming geometric clocks are U=-a0/a1, V=-a1/a2, T=UV=a0/a2, (6) and the output replaces a1 by a1'. By the actual generic white formula, the numerator is H_m^B(q_N^-1 U,q_N^-1 V), with m=d-a, B=Q^-N. The channel a remains the actual discrete integer. For prefix degrees (deg a0,deg a1,deg a2), the root arguments have the following orders; the factors q_N^-1 in (3) remain in each entry. | Degrees | U | V | T | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 000 | finite | finite | finite | | 002 | finite | r^-2 | r^-2 | | 020 | r^-2 | r^2 | finite | | 022 | r^-2 | finite | r^-2 | | 200 | r^2 | finite | r^2 | | 202 | r^2 | r^-2 | finite | | 220 | finite | r^2 | r^2 | | 222 | finite | finite | finite | Here "finite" means a nonzero limit, which can still meet a further chart divisor, including one. For the original complete-circle boxes, 000 and 020 are impossible: a0 and a2 constant would make P preserve the reference main cusp, although P is a nontrivial longitude of a different, auxiliary cusp. Distinct cusp lifts have disjoint small horoballs and cannot have the same center. For routed crossing bands one must retain all eight rows unless that extra hypothesis is proved. There is no implicit Hermitian adjoint. The literal pi dual uses the reversed complementary indices (d-j,d-i). The exact Chevalley identity W_a(d-j,d-i;2a-r0) =zeta^[(d-2a)(a-r0)] W_a(i,j;r0) (7) reduces it to the incoming white with its actual scalar retained. Alternatively its two raw H arguments are the reversed reciprocals Q^d/Q^j,Q^d/Q^i. All routing spectra and their paired partners remain. For the exceptional inverse turn retain its actual coordinates h=v-u, ell=t-v, sigma=d-h, r0=a-h. Its two numerator pairs are exactly (Q^(sigma-u),Q^u), (Q^ell,Q^(sigma-ell)). (8) With physical half-index sampling these are the original outgoing and incoming pairs in (6), respectively. The moving factorial arguments are r0,2a-r0 in the channel cup and v,d-v,ell,d-ell in the inverse physical cups; ordinary pi has the analogous original complemented indices. This specifies their whole marked logarithmic lifts. The specified generic exceptional lift has root character exp(-2pi i v). Restoring the original physical turn contributes the inverse exp(2pi i v), exactly as in the [source lift](actual_matching_edge_generic_deficient_operator_lift.md), equation (13). They cancel BEFORE an estimate. Bounding them separately at (2) could introduce artificial N log N growth. None of this proves uniform asymptotics for the listed moving factorials or numerators. ## 3. A uniform original-root packet when the first clock is large Put Q=exp(2pi i/N), and keep an actual integer m with delta <= mu=m/N <= 1-delta, delta>0. At the root the exact polynomial is H_m^1(U,V)=sum_(k=0)^m c_k V^k product_(j<k)(U-Q^j) product_(j<m-k)(V-Q^j), c_k=(-1)^k Q^[k(k+1)/2] [m choose k]_Q^2. (9) This includes the actual large m=d-a. Suppose U=N^2 kappa_N, V=V_N, where kappa_N and V_N range in fixed compact subsets of C*. Keep the EXACT last Newton term E_N=c_m (UV)^m product_(j<m)(1-Q^j/U), c_m=(-1)^m Q^[m(m+1)/2]. (10) It is nonzero for large N. Define the entire function Bessel(K)=sum_(l>=0) (-K)^l/(l!)^2 =J_0(2sqrt(K)), K_N=sin^2(pi mu)(V_N-1)/(pi^2 kappa_N V_N). (11) The series, not a square-root branch, defines the notation. Uniformly on those compacts, H_m^1(U,V)/E_N=Bessel(K_N)+O(N^-1). (12) In particular U=N^2 kappa(1+O(N^-1)), V=V0+O(N^-1) gives the same formula with K=sin^2(pi mu)(V0-1)/(pi^2 kappa V0). The finite m/N, the phase c_m, and the product in (10) have not been discarded. Equation (12) is an absolute normalized estimate. A relative packet is asserted only on a compact set where Bessel(K) is nonzero. Here is a proof retaining the WHOLE finite polynomial. Set k=m-l. The exact ratio of that summand to (10) is (-1)^l Q^[-ml+l(l-1)/2] [m choose l]_Q^2 * (UV)^(-l) product_(j<l)(V-Q^j) /product_(j=m-l)^(m-1)(1-Q^j/U). (13) For j<=m<=(1-delta)N, |1-Q^j|>=c_delta j/N. Consequently |[m choose l]_Q|<=(C_delta N)^l/l! for EVERY l<=m. The denominator in (13) has inverse bounded independently of N,l, since |U|>=cN^2. Thus every term is bounded by C^l/(l!)^2. This proves uniform summable tail domination, not just convergence of the fixed-l terms. For fixed l, expand the exact Gaussian products. The identity exp(-2pi i mu)(1-exp(2pi i mu))^2/(-2pi i)^2 =sin^2(pi mu)/pi^2 gives precisely (-K_N)^l/(l!)^2. Uniformly for l<=N^(1/4), the product expansion has absolute error at most C^l(1+l)^C/[N(l!)^2]. This follows by expanding each of the l numerator and denominator factors; their relative errors are O(l/N), while product_(j<l)(V-Q^j) is compared in absolute value if V=1. The factorial bound makes the remaining tail smaller than every power of N. Summing proves (12). ## 4. A geometric transition with an explicit nonzero model Consider a 200 box whose second raw puncture is the reference B=-J. Then Q1=AW=epsilon[[1,b],[0,1]], Q2=BQ1, epsilon=+/-1. Write A21=c_A. The actual complete disk relation Tr(BA)=-2 and Tr A=-2 give c_A=4. Since W=A^-1Q1, its lower-left entry is -epsilon c_A. Substituting (1),(6), at r=N rho gives kappa=Q0_21 rho^2/[s L_Q1], V0=-L_Q1/L_Q2, K=sin^2(pi mu) s^2/(4pi^2 rho^2). (14) The q_N^-1 argument corrections are included in the O(N^-1) allowed in (12). They were not dropped in (4), where their size is decisive. The inverse orientation B=-J^-1 gives the same squared expression. In the actual first-slot Fourier convention eta_j=Q^j and p=eta_j^-1, the resonant scale for each fixed nonzero integer j is r=1/(1-exp(-2pi i j/N))-beta s, rho -> 1/(2pi i j). Hence this local boundary factor tends Bessel(-j^2 s^2 sin^2(pi mu)) =I_0(2j s sin(pi mu)). (15) For Re s!=0 it is nonzero. An elementary proof avoids a zero theorem: if I_0(z)=0, f(t)=I_0(zt) obeys (t f')'=z^2 t f, f(0)=1, f'(0)=0,f(1)=0. Integration against conjugate f gives z^2 integral_0^1 t|f|^2=-integral_0^1 t|f'|^2<0. Thus z is purely imaginary. The ordinary regular framing exclusions remove finitely many s values; Re s!=0 can also be imposed wherever that first-cut frame is legitimately varied. In particular on the legitimate real interior first-cut slice A_cut=exp(2pi i alpha), 0<alpha<1, one has s=exp(-2pi i alpha)-1 and Re s=cos(2pi alpha)-1<0. The local nonvanishing condition is therefore automatic on that slice, after its other regular exclusions. This is not a proof that an arbitrary selected global frame path reaches every required box in the 200 regime. The j=0 node is the exact resonance r=infinity, not an additional finite rho value. No uniform result in growing j or across all eight regimes is claimed. In particular 202 leaves a nontrivial whole boundary polynomial in T; it does not reduce to the last term in (10). ## 5. The paired small-second-clock endpoint The 002 regime has an equally direct original-source proof; it does not use an unrecorded interchange of the two physical legs. Let V=kappa_N/N^2, U=U_N, E_N^0=product_(j<m)(V-Q^j), K_N^0=kappa_N sin^2(pi mu)(1-U_N)/pi^2, (16) where kappa_N,U_N lie in fixed compact subsets of C*. Then H_m^1(U,V)/E_N^0=Bessel(K_N^0)+O(N^-1). (17) The EXACT ratio of its kth Newton term to E_N^0 is c_k V^k product_(j<k)(U-Q^j) /product_(j=m-k)^(m-1)(V-Q^j). (18) The denominator product differs from (-1)^k Q^[mk-k(k+1)/2] by a relative O(k/N^2), uniformly for k<=m. Together with the same Gaussian bound as before, this gives C^k/(k!)^2 domination for EVERY k. Its fixed-k limit is [kappa_N sin^2(pi mu)(U_N-1)/pi^2]^k/(k!)^2. The product-error argument in section 3, including absolute comparison when U_N=1, proves the uniform O(N^-1) remainder. Both the exact phase and the full endpoint product are retained in (16),(18). For a genuine 002 disk with first puncture A=-J write Q0=epsilon[[1,b],[0,1]], Q1=AQ0 and Q2=BQ1. The complete trace relation gives B21=4. Substitution into (1),(6) now gives U0=(1+b s)/(1+(b+1)s), kappa=s(1+(b+1)s)/(4rho^2), K^0=sin^2(pi mu)s^2/(4pi^2rho^2). (19) Thus the same fixed-Fourier I0 factor and its legitimate real first-cut nonvanishing apply. The exact physical argument shifts q_N^-1 change U0,kappa by the permitted O(N^-1); the actual endpoint product is still kept. This proves paired 200/002 models, not the unproved reduction of 022/220 or 202 to either one. ## 6. The mixed 202 boundary retains a whole positive polynomial Put V=T/U and define the exact boundary polynomial A_b(T)=(-1)^b Q^[b(b-1)/2] P_b(QT), P_b(w)=sum_(k=0)^b beta(b,k)^2 w^k, beta(b,k)=s_b/[s_k s_(b-k)]. (20) Termwise in (9), A_b is the limit as U tends to infinity with T fixed. For the actual small channel a<=floor((N-1)/2), P_a is precisely the two-binomial polynomial Q_a^(a,a) in the [proved negative-root theorem](actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.md). Its roots are negative real and simple. Retain this whole polynomial; it is not a replacement by its largest coefficient. If U=N^2 kappa with kappa in a fixed compact subset of C*, and T in a fixed compact subset of C minus (-infinity,0], then H_a^1(U,T/U)=A_a(T)(1+O(N^-1)), (21) uniformly in the actual discrete a. There is no lower bound on the distance of a/N from zero needed for this statement. For the ACTUAL large channel m=d-a, the exact root partner identity gives H_m^1(U,T/U)=A_a(T) product_(r=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^r)(1+O(N^-1)). (22) The forced unit-arc factors in (22) are displayed, including their zeros. At such a zero both sides are zero exactly. No generic normal is inferred by differentiating this root collision identity. Here is a uniform relative proof, including complex cancellation. After taking out its exact phase, H_a is sum_(k=0)^a beta(a,k)^2(QT)^k product_(r<k)(1-Q^r/U) product_(r<a-k)(1-(T/U)Q^-r). (23) Expand BOTH correction products by the finite quantum binomial identity, proved by multiplying their linear factors. The term of degree i in the first is a polynomial in Q^k proportional to U^-i product_(r<i)(1-Q^(k-r))/(Q;Q)_i; the degree-j term in the second is proportional to (T/U)^j product_(r<j)(1-Q^(-a+k+r)) /(Q^-1;Q^-1)_j. (24) The omitted factors in (24) have modulus one. These identities hold also when i>k or j>a-k: the corresponding numerator contains zero. Therefore expanding (24) gives an EXACT finite linear combination of A_a(Q^hT), with 0<=h<=i+j. Since i,j<=a<N/2, the sum of absolute coefficients of this combination is at most (C/N)^(i+j)/(i!j!). (25) Indeed |(Q;Q)_i|>=(c/N)^i i!, and each numerator polynomial in Q^k has coefficient sum at most 2^i; the second factor is identical. The i=j=0 term is exactly A_a(T). Write P_a(w)=C_a product_l(w+rho_l), rho_l>0. On the indicated compact T domain, w=QT remains a fixed distance in angle from the negative ray for large N. For 0<=h<=cN, choose c small enough so the rotation from QT to Q^(h+1)T remains in this domain. The bound |w P_a'(w)/P_a(w)|<=C a then gives |A_a(Q^hT)/A_a(T)|<=exp(C h). For EVERY other h one still has the crude bound exp(CN), by applying (|w|+rho)/|w+rho|<=C to each root. Sum (25) first over 1<=i+j<=cN; the exp(C h) factor leaves O(N^-1). For i+j>cN, the factorial tail in (25), even multiplied by exp(CN), is smaller than every inverse power of N. This proves (21) without replacing a complex sum by its positive envelope. The original root identity H_m=H_a product_(r=a)^(m-1)(T-Q^r) proves (22). For the ACTUAL right-angled matching-polyhedron source, the 202 condition gives a useful geometric certificate: T_infinity is POSITIVE. Use precisely the literal white-reflection prefixes proved in [the original cut dictionary](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md), section 3: Q_i=r_(F_i)r_(F_ref). The exterior first-slot reference white face F_ref contains the fixed point p of the original marked main meridian. The 202 middle prefix is upper triangular and fixes p. Thus r_(F_1)r_(F_ref)(p)=p and r_(F_ref)(p)=p force r_(F_1)(p)=p. In other words p lies on the MIDDLE white circle. This is a consequence of the actual common prefix, not a new local framing choice. In the recorded disk coordinate eta that circle has diameter [0,1]. Its puncture lifts and product are A=-[[1,0],[2,1]], B=-[[3,-2],[2,-1]], P=BA=-[[1,2],[0,1]]. (26) Writing eta0 for p and conjugating by [[0,-1],[1,-eta0]] sends p to infinity. Direct multiplication gives A21=-2 eta0^2 and B21=-2(eta0-1)^2. Since Q1 is upper triangular, Q0=A^-1 Q1 and Q2=B Q1 have leading lower-left ratio T_infinity=-A21/B21=-eta0^2/(eta0-1)^2>0. (27) Indeed eta0/(eta0-1) is purely imaginary on that circle. The two outer prefixes are genuinely quadratic, so eta0 is neither 0 nor 1; the positive value is finite and nonzero. Therefore the actual T=T_infinity+O(1/N) at r=N rho lies in a fixed compact subset of the domain of (21). This applies with every retained half twist, since the proved outside white-reflection prefixes are unchanged. The certificate requires this actual right-angled cut and its marked first-slot reference. It is not asserted for arbitrary routed 202 crossings lacking that dictionary. No basing or reference meridian is changed. The 022/220 boundary polynomials still require their separate source treatment, and no global contributing cycle follows from (27). The full matched source still needs its original boundary current, remaining factors, normal extraction and selected relative cycle. The local nonzero Bessel factor proves none of their noncancellation. Focused audit: [original coefficients, marked prefix signs and boundary packets](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge_results.json). It checks 9 exact geometric identities, all 8 incidence patterns, 72 literal-source comparisons, 72 endpoint packets, 24 mixed-boundary identities and 24 complex relative 202 packets. These are focused checks of the proof, not a global-period experiment. Primary-agent full analytical review and fresh audit: PASS. The reviewer checked the exact endpoints, complete coefficient normalization and tail bounds, physical/channel offset distinction, both Bessel models, and the relative 202 shift expansion with forced partner roots retained. Independent full analytical review and fresh redirected audit: PASS. The reviewer rederived the original large-H coefficient phases, both endpoint models, all-l domination, the two finite correction expansions, and the actual geometric 200/002 calibrations. A further targeted review and independent symbolic check passed the literal first-slot RA202 positive-ray certificate. No generic-normal or global-cycle claim was inferred from these root-value results.

title: The actual q-Hahn column selects a complex leading action
text: # The actual q-Hahn column selects a complex leading action 30 October 2026. The negative-root theorem gives an asymptotic for the ACTUAL local Fourier sum, including its cancellation. The normalized logarithm converges on the entire slit plane to the analytic continuation of its positive real variational action. In the right half-plane this selects a nondegenerate internal saddle with its original logarithms. This is a local leading-order theorem at both level parities. It does not give a complete amplitude expansion, a uniform generic-q normal, or a noncancellation theorem for the assembled plat source. ## 1. The exact finite polynomial and its logarithm Use the ORIGINAL coefficients of the [phase compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md): P_N(w)=sum_a E(t_N,j_N,u_N,a) w^a, E(t,j,u,a)=beta(j,a) beta(u,a) beta(t-u,j-a)/beta(t,j), a0_N=max(0,u_N-t_N+j_N), a1_N=min(j_N,u_N). Here 0<=j_N<=t_N<N and 0<=u_N<=t_N. Every beta is the positive sine binomial at theta=pi/N. No fitted scalar or knot value enters this definition. The [negative-root theorem](actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.md) proves the exact factorization P_N(w)/P_N(1)=w^a0_N product_(r=1)^(a1_N-a0_N) (w+rho_(N,r))/(1+rho_(N,r)), rho_(N,r)>0. (1) Consequently on Omega=C minus (-infinity,0] the actual polynomial has a unique holomorphic logarithm that is real at w=1. Define L_N(w)=Log(P_N(w))/N. (2) This is a specified logarithm, not the principal argument of a possibly many-times-wound numerical value. Its real part is always log|P_N(w)|/N, independent of that qualification. ## 2. The real variational problem is strict Suppose (t_N,j_N,u_N)/N -> (tau,xi,upsilon), 0<xi<tau<1, 0<upsilon<tau. (3) Set a0=max(0,upsilon-tau+xi), a1=min(xi,upsilon), and use J(s)=integral_0^s log(2 sin(pi y))dy, B(v,a)=J(v)-J(a)-J(v-a), Ecal(alpha)=B(xi,alpha)+B(upsilon,alpha) +B(tau-upsilon,xi-alpha)-B(tau,xi). The interval (a0,a1) is nonempty. For every real w>0 the function Ecal(alpha)+alpha log w has a unique interior maximum, denoted alpha(w), and write its value as psi(w). Its derivative is Ecal'(alpha)=log[sin^2(pi(xi-alpha)) sin(pi(upsilon-alpha)) / (sin^2(pi alpha) sin(pi(tau-upsilon-xi+alpha)))]. The derivative tends to +infinity at a0 and -infinity at a1. Its second derivative is strictly negative: Ecal''=-pi{2[cot(pi(xi-alpha))+cot(pi alpha)] +cot(pi(upsilon-alpha)) +cot(pi(tau-upsilon-xi+alpha))}<0. (4) For the sign, the first paired arguments sum to pi xi in (0,pi); the second pair sums to pi(tau-xi) in (0,pi). Apply cot A+cot B=sin(A+B)/(sin A sin B). All displayed individual arguments lie in (0,pi) on the support interior. Uniform sine-factorial estimates give log E(t_N,j_N,u_N,a)=N Ecal_N(a/N)+O(log N), over the ENTIRE finite support; Ecal_N uses the actual scaled parameters. The support is an interval of the full integer lattice. An upper bound by its largest term and a lower bound by a nearest lattice point to the unique maximizer therefore prove L_N(w) -> psi(w), w>0. (5) The argument is uniform when (3) ranges over a compact subset of its strict domain and w ranges over a compact positive interval. Factorial endpoints are included in the upper bound; none is silently removed before taking the maximum. ## 3. Negative roots prove the complex limit For each compact K in Omega, sup_(w in K,rho>=0) |Log((w+rho)/(1+rho))| < infinity. (6) Indeed (w+rho)/(1+rho) is on the segment between w and 1. Its modulus stays bounded above and away from zero uniformly on K, and its argument stays on the single branch between Arg w and zero. Equivalently compactify rho by rho/(1+rho) in [0,1]. The same bound applies to Log w. Since a1_N<N, (1) implies that L_N(w)-L_N(1) is locally uniformly bounded on Omega. Equation (5) bounds L_N(1). Cauchy estimates and subsequence compactness now give holomorphic subsequential limits, uniformly on compact subsets. All such limits agree on the positive real axis by (5); the identity theorem makes them identical on the connected slit plane. Thus the WHOLE sequence converges: L_N(w) -> psi_hol(w), locally uniformly on Omega. (7) All complex derivatives converge locally uniformly as well. This proves existence and uniqueness of the analytic continuation in (7), instead of assuming that an arbitrary algebraic saddle has that role. The same subsequence argument proves uniformity for compact strict parameter families in (3): any proposed failure has a convergent parameter subsequence, to which the preceding proof applies. Continuity of psi_hol in those parameters follows by the same compactness and positive-axis uniqueness argument. Only elementary compactness for holomorphic functions is used here: Cauchy estimates give equicontinuity on a compact exhaustion; successive subsequences converge there, and the real-axis values determine their unique holomorphic limit. No contour replacement of the finite source or unproved saddle coefficient is inserted. ## 4. A positive root measure fixes the branch Put alpha_hol(w)=w psi_hol'(w). Differentiating (1) yields w L_N'(w)=a0_N/N+(1/N)sum_r w/(w+rho_(N,r)). (8) The measures (1/N)sum_r delta_rho have total mass tending to a1-a0. Compactify their domain by adjoining zero and infinity. Any weak limit mu obeys alpha_hol(w)=a0+integral w/(w+rho) dmu(rho). (9) For real w, the envelope derivative of the strict maximum gives alpha_hol(w)=alpha(w). The barrier equation shows alpha(w)->a0 as w decreases to zero and alpha(w)->a1 as w increases to infinity. Thus mu has no mass at zero or infinity and has total mass a1-a0 on (0,infinity). Formula (9), rather than a chosen ordering of quadratic roots, specifies the actual selected branch. For Im w>0 its imaginary part is strictly positive. If additionally Re w>=0 and w!=0, then a0<Re alpha_hol(w)<a1. (10) For (10), each integrand w/(w+rho) has real part strictly between zero and one. At positive real w, alpha_hol is the original real interior maximum. Along the physical first-quadrant arc all four sine arguments in (4) stay nonzero: their imaginary parts are nonzero away from the positive real axis, and their real-axis initial values lie in the support interior. More explicitly, (10) keeps each argument in the vertical strip 0<Re s<1. There Re(sin(pi s))>0, so its logarithm has one analytic branch agreeing with the positive real logarithm. The saddle equation therefore continues there without an arbitrary logarithm reset: Ecal'(alpha_hol(w))+Log w=0. (11) It is nondegenerate throughout that quadrant. In fact alpha_hol'(w)=integral rho/(w+rho)^2 dmu(rho) never vanishes there. For 0<=Arg w<pi/2 the integrands lie in an open angular sector of width less than pi; at Arg w=pi/2 each has strictly negative imaginary part. Their positive integral is nonzero. Differentiating (11) gives Ecal''(alpha_hol(w))=-1/[w alpha_hol'(w)] !=0. (12) Thus on the physical arc psi_hol is exactly the continued critical value Ecal(alpha_hol)+alpha_hol Log w, with its positive-axis normalization. This conclusion concerns the leading logarithm. It does not by itself compute a Gaussian prefactor or an error O(1/N). ## 5. Consequence for every actual complete-circle column On a complete-circle channel, the exact column is f_(u_N)(c_(j_N))=(-1)^u_N q^[-(j_N+1)u_N] P_N(q^delta_N), delta_N=t_N+j_N-(N-1). If (3) holds and xi<=1/2, tau+xi>=1, then q^delta_N -> w_star=exp[pi i(tau+xi-1)], 0<=Arg w_star<=pi/2. Equation (7) supplies the actual, cancellation-sensitive limit lim_N (1/N)log|f_(u_N)(c_(j_N))| =Re psi_hol(w_star). (13) Both level parities and all composite levels are included. The explicit unit prefactor gives the unwrapped leading complex phase psi_hol(w_star)+pi i(upsilon-xi upsilon) in the compiler's convention. At the folded endpoint xi=1/2 this selects the actual local branch of its previously derived quadratic. The high physical degree block uses its already proved exact index translation, so (13) applies there in those translated variables too. For comparison, negative roots give the finite bound cos(phi/2)^(a1_N-a0_N) P_N(1) <= |P_N(exp(i phi))| <= P_N(1), |phi|<pi. (14) The lower factor can be EXPONENTIAL in N. It is not a polynomial normalization loss. Formula (13) determines that cancellation rate through the selected analytic action instead of dropping it. This does not yet control cancellations among different magnetic or channel states in a whole plat, the mixed-color aliases, the original generic first normals, or the selected global geometric period. Those remain necessary for the general long-filling volume equality. Audit: [actual Fourier columns and selected complex action](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_selected_complex_action.py). The analytic proof above is uniform; finite numerical checks only verify the formula conventions and the selected continuation. Independent source-transport review: full analytical read and fresh 100-digit audit PASS for twelve actual finite polynomials, including the folded endpoint and both level parities. The reviewer separately checked the uniform real Laplace step, slit-plane normal-family argument, compact parameter continuity, removal of endpoint mass in the positive root measure, and the nonvanishing saddle derivative on the physical quadrant. The actual logarithmic sheets and remaining global/amplitude limitations were retained in the review. Independent geometric review: full analytical read and fresh 100-digit replay PASS as well, including the root-measure endpoint masses, strict support strip and nonzero derivative in the physical quadrant. The review does not extend the real magnetic parameter theorem to an unproved complex global source packet.

title: Polynomial cost of the actual small-channel generic normals
status: Polynomial fixed generic derivatives; small channels
text: # Polynomial cost of the actual small-channel generic normals 30 October 2026. This note concerns the ORIGINAL generic highest-weight N-1 columns, including the factors that simplify only at the root of unity. On compact subsets of the joint central wedge, every fixed generic-q derivative of a small-channel column has at most polynomial cost relative to that column's root value. The estimate includes the folded small channel and both parities. It does not bound the paired large-channel derivative, the confluent spectral normal formed from both channels, or the whole marked source. ## 1. The exact generic deformation Fix N>=3, d=N-1 and q0=exp(pi i/N). Let q vary near q0; put Q=q^2, B=Q^(-N), A=B^(-1), x=q^d, t=u+v, U=Q^u, V=Q^v, T=UV, s=q^t, D_j(T)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)(T-Q^r). All complex powers use log(q)=pi i/N+epsilon. Gaussian binomials and Pochhammer products below have base Q. Define H_j^B(U,V)=sum_(a=0)^j (-1)^a B^a Q^[a(a+1)/2] [j choose a]_Q (B Q^(j-a+1);Q)_a/(BQ;Q)_a V^a product_(r<a)(U-Q^r) product_(r<j-a)(V-Q^r), C_j(q;t,u)=x^u H_j^B(U,V)/D_j(T), S_j^B(U,T)=U^j H_j^B(U,T/U). (1) This is the actual generic column in [the mixed compiler](actual_mixed_augmented_plat_compiler.md), section 2, at physical t,u. It also specifies a finite rational continuation for complex t,u. To check the source before differentiating, its highest-vector ratio is exactly R_(j,a)=(Q^(N-j);Q)_a/(Q^(N-a);Q)_a =Q^[a(a-j)] (B Q^(j-a+1);Q)_a/(BQ;Q)_a. (2) Converting the three Gaussian binomials in that compiler into finite Newton products gives (1). In particular the additional factor is B^a times the displayed Pochhammer ratio. Merely inserting a power of -q^(-N) into the root-only squared-binomial formula would give the wrong generic source and the wrong first derivative. The exact leading scalar is S_j^B(0,T)=T^j K_j, K_j=(B^2 Q^(j+1);Q)_j/(BQ;Q)_j. (3) Here is an elementary proof of the finite identity used in (3). For generic a,c,Q and integer n>=0, sum_(k=0)^n (Q^(-n);Q)_k (a;Q)_k / [(Q;Q)_k(c;Q)_k] (c Q^n/a)^k =(c/a;Q)_n/(c;Q)_n. (4) Multiply both sides by a^n(c;Q)_n. Each side is a polynomial of degree at most n in a. At a=c Q^m, 0<=m<n, the quotient (a;Q)_k/(c;Q)_k=(c Q^k;Q)_m/(c;Q)_m is a polynomial in Q^k of degree m. For each of its powers Q^(rk), r<=m, the finite binomial sum on the left is (Q^(r-m);Q)_n=0. Thus the left polynomial has all the n roots of product_(r<n)(a-cQ^r). Its constant term, from k=n alone, is (-1)^n c^n Q^[n(n-1)/2], fixing the multiplier to 1. This proves (4) as a rational identity. Taking n=j, a=B^(-1)Q^(-j), c=BQ gives (3), after converting (Q^(-j);Q)_a to the Gaussian binomial. No asymptotic identity is used here. ## 2. The generic Casimir polynomial and its three-term recurrence The exact equation for S=S_j^B is Q^(-j)(QU-A)(U-T) S(QU,T) +Q^j(BQT-U)(1-U) S(U/Q,T) +[(1+A)U+QT(1+B)U-(1+Q)U^2 -T(AQ^(-j)+BQ^(j+1))]S(U,T)=0. (5) It follows from the actual generic coproduct Casimir, whose column eigenvalue is q^(2N-1-2j)+q^(-2N+1+2j). Alternatively, one can verify its extension from physical columns by exactly the finite degree argument used for the root equation in [the joint determinant note](actual_q_hahn_joint_accretive_determinant.md). The residual has degree at most j+1 in U: the top degree cancels; its constant coefficient also vanishes. At each original complete slice t=d-j,...,d, its original t+1 column values and U=0 force the whole U polynomial to vanish. The residual has degree at most j+1 in T. These j+1 slices, together with T=0, force its vanishing identically. At T=0 use S(U,0)=(-1)^j Q^[j(j-1)/2]U^j; the residual cancels directly. This proves (5) in a neighborhood of the actual root, where all these finite source columns and distinct slice values are defined. Let R_n(z) be the monic reverse polynomial obtained from (1): R_n(z)=z^n S_n^B(s/z,s^2)/(s^(2n)K_n). Equation (5) says L R_n=Lambda_n R_n for the triangular operator L z^n=Lambda_n z^n+b_n z^(n-1)+d_n z^(n-2), Lambda_n=AQ^(-n)+BQ^(n+1), b_n=[(1+A)+Qs^2(1+B)-Q^(-n)(Qs^2+A) -Q^n(BQs^2+1)]/s, d_n=Q^(1-n)+Q^n-1-Q. (6) Terms with negative powers are absent, since b_0=d_0=d_1=0. Write the two coefficients below the leading one as u_n,v_n. Their exact expressions are u_0=0, u_n=b_n/(Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-1)), n>=1, v_0=v_1=0, v_n=(b_(n-1)u_n+d_n)/(Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-2)), n>=2. For 0<=n<j, put alpha_n=u_(n+1)-u_n, beta_n=v_(n+1)-v_n-alpha_n u_n (n>=1). Then exactly R_0=1, R_1=z+alpha_0, R_(n+1)=(z+alpha_n)R_n+beta_n R_(n-1). (7) For completeness, a finite moment argument rules out extra lower terms in (7). Set mu_0=1, mu_(-1)=0 and impose (BQ^(r+1)-A)mu_r +[(Qs^2+A)-(BQs^2+1)Q^r]mu_(r-1)/s +(Q^r-Q)mu_(r-2)=0, 1<=r<=2j-1. (8) The difference of the two monomial pairings for L factors as (Q^n-Q^m)Q^(-n-m) times (8) at r=m+n. Thus L is symmetric for this finite moment functional. Its eigenvalues of degrees 0,...,j are distinct near the root. The usual finite orthogonality argument now kills the terms below R_(n-1) in zR_n-R_(n+1); the top two coefficients give (7). This argument can first be made at generic s, where the preceding norms do not vanish: the norm recursion is h_n=-beta_n h_(n-1). At B=1 the beta_n are the nonzero polynomials in c displayed below, so generic nonvanishing follows inductively. Rational continuation then proves (7) also when a particular beta_n vanishes. No positive generic moment functional is assumed. Combining (1),(3) gives the exact normalized source C_j=x^u q^(jt) K_j R_j(q^t/U)/D_j(Q^t). (9) All the generic coefficients in this section retain B=Q^(-N). Equation (7) is not a deformation chosen after specialization. ## 3. A uniformly controlled generic neighborhood Let W be the joint wedge 1/2<Re(t/N)<1, |2Re(u/N)-Re(t/N)|<1/2. For every compact K contained in W there are constants c_K,C_K>0, independent of N and 0<=j<=floor((N-1)/2), such that |C_j(q0 exp(epsilon);t,u)/C_j(q0;t,u)|<=C_K whenever |epsilon|<=c_K N^(-8), (t/N,u/N) in K. (10) In particular the denominator on the left is nonzero. The power 8 is a convenient conservative bound; no optimal power is claimed. Here are explicit estimates proving the assertion. At epsilon=0, put theta=pi/N, c=-cos((t+1)theta), z=q0^(t-2u). On a fixed K, Re c and Re z have positive lower bounds for all sufficiently large N. The root recurrence (7) is alpha_n=c/[cos(n theta)cos((n+1)theta)], beta_n=Bcal_n[cos^2(n theta)-c^2], Bcal_n=sin^2(n theta)/[cos^2(n theta) sin((2n-1)theta)sin((2n+1)theta)]. Thus its determinant is M_0=zI+cD+Kskew, with the actual positive D and real skew matrix Kskew in the joint determinant note. Accretivity gives ||M_0^(-1)||<=1/Re z, uniformly in the channel, including the fold. Construct the generic tridiagonal matrix M_epsilon with diagonal z(q)+alpha_n(q). Freeze its upper entries to their ROOT values r_n=sqrt(Bcal_n)[c+cos(n theta)], 1<=n<j, and use lower entries -beta_n(q)/r_n. Its determinant is R_j by (7), and at epsilon=0 it is exactly M_0. There is no square-root choice for the generic beta_n. Since sqrt(Bcal_n)>=1/2 and Re c is uniformly positive, |r_n| is bounded below independently of N. The only spectral differences in (6),(7) factor as Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-1) =(1-Q)A Q^(-n)(1-B^2 Q^(2n)), Lambda_n-Lambda_(n-2) =(1-Q^2)A Q^(-n)(1-B^2 Q^(2n-1)). (11) At the root their nonzero factors give lower bounds c/N^2 for all required n<=j. All elementary exponents have size O(N), so these bounds persist in a disk |epsilon|<=c N^(-3). On a smaller such disk, direct differentiation of (6),(7) gives uniformly |u_n|=O(N^2), |u_n'|=O(N^5), |v_n|=O(N^4), |v_n'|=O(N^7), |alpha_n'|=O(N^5), |beta_n'|=O(N^7). (12) Here primes mean d/d epsilon. The coefficients b_n,d_n,Lambda_n are O(1), with derivatives O(N); (12) follows by the quotient rule and (11). Consequently the tridiagonal operator norm satisfies ||M_epsilon-M_0||<=C_K N^7 |epsilon|. On the disk in (10), ||M_0^(-1)(M_epsilon-M_0)||<=C_K c_K/N. Choose c_K small. The determinant ratio is bounded by (1+C_K c_K/N)^j, and hence uniformly bounded; it is also nonzero. The remaining scalar factors in (9) have controlled ratios on the same disk. The exponents of x^u q^(jt) have size O(N^2). Each root factor of K_j has size at least c/N, its derivative is O(N), and there are O(N) factors; thus |(log K_j)'|=O(N^3). The factors of D_j(Q^t) are separated uniformly from zero on K, so its logarithmic derivative is O(N^2). Integration over the N^(-8) disk bounds all these scalar ratios. This proves (10). Finitely many remaining N can be absorbed by changing constants; j=0 follows immediately from C_0=x^u. ## 4. Consequence for actual generic derivatives, and its limit Cauchy's estimate applied to the exact source in (10) gives, for every fixed integer m>=0, |(q d/dq)^m C_j(q0;t,u)| <=C_(K,m) N^(8m) |C_j(q0;t,u)|. (13) The derivative holds t,u,N fixed, exactly as the original generic compiler does. At physical integer t,u it is its actual generic normal; at complex t,u it is the derivative of the finite source continuation (1). Combining (13) with the proved joint root-value amplitude preserves its leading exponential action, as an upper bound, for these fixed-order small-channel derivatives. The mixed compiler's confluent column is proportional to D C_j-D C_(N-1-j). Except at the simple folded endpoint, its second term is a LARGE channel. In that channel K_l vanishes at the root and the monic recurrence crosses resonant eigenvalue differences. The argument above does not apply. In particular (13) is not a bound for that difference, its spectral derivative, a complete mixed kernel, or a generic normal of the whole pointed invariant. Focused audit: [actual generic values and normals](../experiments/audit_actual_q_hahn_small_channel_generic_normals.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_q_hahn_small_channel_generic_normals_results.json). It passed 1,304 original generic value-and-derivative comparisons, 216 generic determinant identities, 216 generic Casimir identities, 216 Vandermonde value-and-derivative identities, and 1,041 original root-normal comparisons in exact finite-field dual arithmetic. At 100 digits, 48 nonphysical generic comparisons and 24 original root-normal comparisons passed; 96 points on the stated polynomial disk were also sampled. The disk samples are regressions, not the proof of uniform control. An independent analytical review checked the original B deformation, the finite Vandermonde interpolation proof, the generic Casimir complete-slice argument, the moment proof and its endpoints, and the N^5/N^7 quotient estimates giving the N^(-8) matrix neighborhood. It also checked the retained scalar ratios and the fixed-t,u Cauchy derivative convention. This review covers the stated small-channel theorem only. A second independent full analytical review and fresh focused replay also passed. It checked the generic source factors before specialization, the finite interpolation and moment arguments, both spectral-gap factorizations, the frozen-upper-entry determinant, and every scalar normalization used in the Cauchy bound. Its replay reproduced all exact and 100-digit counts above. The paired large channel remains excluded.

title: A uniform nonzero complex amplitude for the actual q-Hahn column
text: # A uniform nonzero complex amplitude for the actual q-Hahn column Subsequent extension: [joint pair-degree and magnetic amplitudes](actual_q_hahn_joint_complex_amplitude.md) are now proved on a central complex domain, using the original finite kernel and an exact accretive determinant. The present theorem and its proof retain the real-parameter hypothesis stated below. 30 October 2026. The original finite q-Hahn polynomial has a full leading asymptotic, with a specified nonzero amplitude and relative error O(1/N), uniformly on compact subsets of the right half-plane. Its magnetic parameters are the ACTUAL scaled integers, varying in a compact strict REAL parameter set. No rate of convergence of those parameters is assumed. The proof starts with the previously proved actual logarithmic limit, then uses the exact finite difference equation to improve its error. A positive real Gaussian sum fixes the actual multiplicative constant. Thus the transport equation below describes the original polynomial, not merely a formal solution with an unspecified connection coefficient. This theorem does not interpolate the discrete magnetic parameters holomorphically, take a generic-q first normal, or control the assembled global magnetic/channel sum. ## 1. Original finite source and theorem Let 0<=j<=t<N, 0<=u<=t, v=t-u, theta=pi/N, and s_n=product_(r=1)^n 2 sin(r theta), beta(n,a)=s_n/(s_a s_(n-a)), E_a=beta(j,a) beta(u,a) beta(v,j-a)/beta(t,j), P_N(w)=sum_(a=a0)^a1 E_a w^a, a0=max(0,j-v), a1=min(j,u). (1) These are exactly the coefficients of the [original complete-circle phase compiler](actual_augmented_plat_phase_compiler.md). Put lambda_N=(tau,xi,upsilon)=(t/N,j/N,u/N), D={0<xi<tau<1, 0<upsilon<tau}. All uniform statements below take lambda_N in a fixed compact subset K of D. In particular all saddles at w=1 stay a uniform distance from the factorial boundaries, even when the two descriptions of a support endpoint exchange at upsilon=xi or upsilon+xi=tau. Use the original energy J(s)=integral_0^s log(2 sin(pi y))dy, Bcal(b,a)=J(b)-J(a)-J(b-a), Ecal_lambda(alpha)=Bcal(xi,alpha)+Bcal(upsilon,alpha) +Bcal(tau-upsilon,xi-alpha)-Bcal(tau,xi). For positive real w, let alpha_lambda(w) be the unique interior maximum of Ecal_lambda(alpha)+alpha log w. The [selected complex action theorem](actual_q_hahn_selected_complex_action.md) continues both alpha and its critical value psi_lambda holomorphically to Re w>0, with psi_lambda(w)=Ecal_lambda(alpha_lambda(w)) +alpha_lambda(w) Log w, w psi_lambda'(w)=alpha_lambda(w). (2) All logarithms continue from their real values at w=1. Define, with derivatives in the variable s, A_lambda(s)=sin^2(pi s) sin(pi(tau-upsilon-xi+s)), B_lambda(s)=sin^2(pi(xi-s)) sin(pi(upsilon-s)), F_lambda(s,w)=A_lambda(s)-w B_lambda(s), C_lambda=(sin(pi xi)/2) sqrt[sin(pi upsilon) sin(pi(tau-upsilon)) sin(pi(tau-xi))/sin(pi tau)]. The root selected in (2) satisfies F_lambda(alpha,w)=0. Define Acal_lambda(w)=sqrt(2 pi) C_lambda /sqrt[B_lambda(alpha_lambda(w)) F_(lambda,s)(alpha_lambda(w),w)]. (3) The square root is the holomorphic continuation of its positive real value at w=1. It is well-defined and never zero on Re w>0. **Theorem.** Uniformly for lambda_N in K and w in any compact subset of Re w>0, P_N(w)=N^(-1/2) Acal_(lambda_N)(w) exp[N psi_(lambda_N)(w)] (1+O(N^(-1))). (4) The relative error is holomorphic in w. On smaller compact subsets each fixed number of its w derivatives is O(N^(-1)) as well. Formula (4) uses the actual lambda_N, not an arbitrarily chosen limiting triple. Replacing lambda_N by its limit without controlling the displacement would in general change the leading exponential and the amplitude. ## 2. Exact finite difference equation, including endpoints Let D_w=w d/dw and h=1/N. The coefficient ratio in (1) gives the exact identity sin^2(pi h D_w) sin(pi h(D_w+v-j)) P_N(w) =w sin^2(pi h(j-D_w)) sin(pi h(u-D_w)) P_N(w). (5) For every supported a, its coefficient equation is sin^2(a theta) sin((v-j+a)theta) E_a =sin^2((j-a+1)theta) sin((u-a+1)theta) E_(a-1). At the lower endpoint either a=0 or v-j+a=0. At the first integer above the upper endpoint either j-a+1=0 or u-a+1=0. Thus the zero coefficients outside the support satisfy the SAME equation; there is no endpoint source term in (5). In functional calculus notation, [A_lambda(h D_w)-w B_lambda(h D_w)]P_N=0. (6) Every sine product in (6) is a finite linear combination of the four shifts w -> exp(i pi k h)w, k=-3,-1,1,3. In particular (6) is an exact finite-shift identity, not an infinite differential expansion. ## 3. Uniform simplicity and the actual derivative bootstrap The [negative-root theorem](actual_q_hahn_negative_root_source_polynomial.md) gives positive rho_r and P_N(w)/P_N(1)=w^a0 product_r (w+rho_r)/(1+rho_r). It fixes a holomorphic Log P_N real at w=1. Put G_N(w)=Log P_N(w)/N, a_N(w)=D_w G_N(w). The actual leading-limit theorem proves a_N-alpha_(lambda_N) -> 0 (7) uniformly on larger compact subsets of the right half-plane, also when the real parameters vary in K. Fixed w derivatives converge there too. Alternatively the explicit expression a_N=a0/N+(1/N)sum_r w/(w+rho_r) directly bounds every fixed derivative on those compact subsets. These bounds are independent of the positions of the negative roots. For completeness, the selected branch is uniformly simple here. Its positive limiting root measure gives alpha_lambda'(w)=integral rho/(w+rho)^2 dmu_lambda(rho). For Re w>0 the integrands lie in an angular sector of width less than pi, so their positive integral cannot vanish. Its measure has positive mass strictly between zero and infinity. The support-strip property of alpha makes A and B nonzero. Differentiating its saddle equation gives F_s(alpha,w) D_w alpha=w B(alpha)=A(alpha), Ecal''(alpha)=-F_s(alpha,w)/A(alpha). (8) Consequently F_s is nonzero. Continuity in the real parameters and compactness make its modulus bounded away from zero on each of the sets used below. Complex conjugation supplies the same statement in the lower right quadrant. Fix nested compact neighborhoods within Re w>0. For each fixed c=i pi k, k in {-3,-1,1,3}, all small shifts stay in the larger one. Taylor's theorem along the short logarithmic segment, using the uniform derivative bounds, yields P_N(exp(c h)w)/P_N(w) =exp(c a_N(w)) [1+(h c^2/2)D_w a_N(w)+O(h^2)]. (9) Indeed the exponent before exponentiating is N[G_N(exp(c h)w)-G_N(w)] =c a_N+(h c^2/2)D_w a_N+O(h^2). This is an estimate for the actual polynomial ratios. Inserting all four shifts into (6), with their exact sine coefficients, proves 0=F(a_N,w)+(h/2)(D_w a_N) F_ss(a_N,w)+O(h^2). (10) Equation (7) and the uniformly simple zero first imply a_N-alpha=O(h). To justify this improvement, use the uniform expansion F(a_N,w)=F_s(alpha,w)(a_N-alpha)+O(|a_N-alpha|^2), absorb the quadratic term using (7), and use boundedness of D_w a_N in (10). Cauchy's estimate on a slightly larger compact set then gives D_w a_N-D_w alpha=O(h) and the analogous estimate for every fixed further derivative. Substitution back into (10) now proves the sharper actual estimate a_N=alpha-(h/2)(D_w alpha)F_ss(alpha,w)/F_s(alpha,w) +O(h^2). (11) The order h^2 remainder is justified by the first improvement and Cauchy, not assumed as a WKB ansatz. Differentiating (3) and using (8) gives the exact transport identity D_w log Acal_lambda =-(1/2)(D_w alpha)F_ss(alpha,w)/F_s(alpha,w). (12) For example, differentiate log(B(alpha)F_s(alpha,w)). Its two extra terms cancel: (B'/B)D_w alpha+w F_sw/F_s =(B'/B)(wB/F_s)-wB'/F_s=0. Thus (11) identifies the logarithmic derivative of the ACTUAL source with the explicit amplitude to error O(h^2). ## 4. The real sum fixes the constant, with arbitrary lattice offset On a compact interior subinterval the sine-factorial estimate is s_n=sqrt[2N sin(pi n/N)] exp[N J(n/N)](1+O(N^(-1))). One elementary derivation subtracts log x from log(2 sin pi x), applies the trapezoidal estimate to the resulting smooth function, and applies the usual integral remainder estimate for log(n!). The errors and their required finite derivatives are uniform away from 0 and 1. Applied to every factor of (1), this gives E_a=N^(-1) C_lambda /sqrt[A_lambda(a/N)B_lambda(a/N)] exp[N Ecal_lambda(a/N)](1+O(N^(-1))). (13) The positive real saddle alpha=alpha_lambda(1) stays uniformly inside the support. Strict concavity and the global factorial O(log N) bound give an exponential loss outside a fixed saddle neighborhood. Inside that neighborhood put z=(a-N alpha)/sqrt N. Taylor expansion of the phase and the smooth prefactor in (13) gives a Gaussian times H(alpha)+N^(-1/2)[H'(alpha)z +H(alpha)Ecal'''(alpha)z^3/6] +O(N^(-1)(1+|z|^8)), with a uniformly integrable Gaussian majorant; one may first restrict |z|<=N^(1/20), whose complementary tails are exponentially small. Here H=C_lambda/sqrt(AB). The term of order N^(-1/2) is ODD. No arithmetic assumption about N alpha is needed.
