If one of the adjacent transfers is zero, this deduction is unavailable and that joint corner is deliberately retained. ## 3. The exact whole source and its normal cotangent contour Use the [cardinal completion](actual_scalar_cardinal_source_completion.md) of the COMPLETE original averaged marked source, before splitting any head bands. For a one-component diagram its coordinates are exactly u=(t,k_1,...,k_m), and every arc h=t+sum_j epsilon_j k_j has epsilon_j in {0,+1,-1}. Hence (t,k) -> (h,k), determinant 1, (6) is an INTEGRAL bijection. All original valid states have 0<=h,k_j<=d. Choose a fixed O(N) complex box in these coordinates, and sufficient fixed cardinal powers at each original factorial occurrence. The completed scalar is holomorphic throughout the box, equals the original scalar on valid integer states, and vanishes at invalid integer states, including simultaneous scalar poles. Consequently the ORIGINAL scalar is exactly chi_N/N times the product cotangent residue integral of that completed scalar in (h,k). Every pi*cot(pi*h) and pi*cot(pi*k_j) factor is retained. This assertion follows by the finite residue sum, not by dropping a transformed source factor: a pointwise pullback of the old cotangent in t would instead be pi*cot(pi*(h-sum epsilon_j k_j)). Taking the k residues first gives integer k and its exact periodic equality with pi*cot(pi*h). Thus the new source representation and the old one have the SAME complete integer residues, with no Jacobian, grid factor, or omitted side current. For a regular lower head face the original left normal edge Re h=-1/2 can now move to Re h=-M-1/2. All negative integer cotangent poles have zero residue because the completed scalar vanishes there. The two finite-height horizontal connecting pieces are retained in this closed rectangle identity. At an upper face move the right edge from Re h=d+1/2 to Re h=d+M+1/2, retaining the same connecting pieces and all cotangent factors. No physical integer state is crossed or deleted. The tangent variables are fixed, not replaced by independent off-grid outputs. Their actual unwrapped arc forms shift with h according to (6). The bounds below hold uniformly while every other head and every transfer stays in its stated bulk chamber. ## 4. Uniform normal estimate, including all original phases Fix an imaginary-height bound T and a compact marked BULK chamber for the remaining factorial arguments. For a literal fixed-height source contour one may require their scaled real parts in [eta,1-eta], with bounded scaled imaginary parts and consistent factorial branches. Let B_N be the unwindowed original scalar at the endpoint h=0 or d, with that head factorial replaced by its actual finite value. All other factorials, pivots and kappa remain in B_N; the same original external chi_N/N multiplies both sides of every estimate. There are constants C,B,delta>0 depending only on the diagram and this chamber such that, for 1<=M<=delta*N, the WHOLE windowed scalar on the outward normal edge satisfies |Atilde_N| <= N^B exp(C(M+1)) [C(M+1)/N]^(2M) |B_N|. (7) The same estimate with the appropriate integer floor of the normal distance holds on the horizontal connecting pieces. The powers of N absorb the finite number of fixed cardinal windows and the bounded normal factorial base. On a macroscopic nonreal tangent chamber one may expand the BULK windows by their exact finite-mode packet and apply (7) to each specified bulk mode with its original integer-marked N-order phase retained: its right-hand B_N is then the MODE-WEIGHTED bulk amplitude, including that exponential, rather than the literal unwindowed B_N used on the fixed-height contour. The HEAD windows stay whole: their separated modes have poles at outside-band integers and their matched currents are essential to the same contour identity. No wrong-side bulk-window exponential or normal cancellation current is erased. Here is a direct uniform proof. At a lower face write h=nu-M with nu in the fixed strip -1<=Re nu<=0, |Im nu|<=T. The exact factorial step gives 1/Fhat_+(h)=product_(r=0)^(M-1)(1-Q^(nu-r)) / Fhat_+(nu). (8) The reciprocal base on that compact strip is O_T(N^C): shift once to 0<=Re(nu+1)<=1, where the bounded-order Gamma expansion gives the usual polynomial base, and retain 1-Q^(nu+1). Moreover |1-Q^(nu-r)| <= C_T(r+1)/N for M<=delta*N. The gathered head factor is its SQUARE by (5). At the upper face write h=d+nu+M with 0<=Re nu<=1. Exactly, Fhat_+(h)=Fhat_+(d+nu) product_(r=1)^M(1-Q^(nu+r-1)), Fhat_+(d+nu)=N exp[i*pi*nu*(nu+d)/N]/Fhat_+(-nu). (9) The second identity is the actual factorial reflection, including its chirp. It proves a polynomial upper base through both endpoints; the first proves the same small-factor product as (8). For every OTHER bulk factorial, a normal displacement of size M+1 has relative modulus at most exp(C(M+1)). This follows either from the uniform complex factorial symbol with bounded logarithmic derivative on the marked compact chamber, or by the exact unit step followed by the bounded fractional Gamma base. The logarithmic derivative of E_N in (4) is O_word(1) on the fixed O(N) box, so ALL Cartan, conversion, pivot and Gaussian phases cost exp(C(M+1)) too. Finally the exact cardinal bound is sqrt(N)*exp(2pi*|Im ell|). On a fixed-height joint contour every Im ell is bounded by a diagram constant, independent of N and M. This proves (7), also at coincident negative integer poles, since all completed factors are holomorphic. For M=N^alpha, 0<alpha<1, the entire collar has exp(o(N)) cost, and its far edge relative to B_N is at most exp[-2(1-alpha)N^alpha log N+O(N^alpha+log N)]. (10) One may also take M=floor(delta*N) with a sufficiently small fixed delta. Then its far edge has a strict exponential drop exp[-c*delta*N*log(1/delta)] relative to the endpoint bulk amplitude. The whole intervening collar has only polynomial normal overhead: choose delta so C+2log(C*delta)<0 in (7), and treat bounded M with the polynomial base. This is a NORMAL estimate; it does not bound the unrestricted tangent exterior amplitude B_N by volume. ## 5. What has and has not been removed The zero-side direction comes from composing the two original neighboring scalar factors FIRST. It is absent from an isolated low-head kernel K_R, whose Hardy residues cancel at its apparent matching pole. No such pole residue was asserted here. The whole head bands remain together in the original finite source, and the outer cotangent edge is filled with its exact scalar continuation. This removes a regular head endpoint as a compulsory scalar POLE exit. It supplies a quantitative outward contour with the original normalization and unwrapped routing. It does not prove that the remaining whole cycle reaches the geometric thimble, or that every simultaneous endpoint cluster has this direction. In particular a head endpoint next to a zero transfer, a repeated head face, and escaping tangent bulk coordinates require their own compensated whole-source treatment. The full global growth estimate remains open. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_regular_head_face_cot_filling.py): literal signed head incidence, original statewise composition, exact negative-root conversion and both normal small-factor identities.

title: Actual quantum-A energy propagation with regulator weights
text: # Actual quantum-A energy propagation with regulator weights 28 October 2026. A geometric regulator weight cancels the diagonal growth of a smooth spectral branch, but does not by itself control the actual source or channel mixing at each time step. This can be checked EXPLICITLY for the actual affine figure-eight operator, on a regular arc with distinct eigenvalues and no turning-point or resonance issue. The calculation identifies a concrete missing estimate in the proposed rigid-dynamics argument. It does not rule out a better exact Green representation: the [pointed Newton--Green theorem](pointed_newton_green_barrier.md) already provides one for this prototype. Nor does it replace the whole source by a largest-eigenvalue prescription. ## 1. Keep the actual affine operator and source Use C F_N=D(3-U-U^-1), U=Y^N, with the exact coefficients and normalizations of the pointed Green note. On a regular part of the root orbit U=1, its forward inhomogeneous recurrence is w_(j+1)=T_Q(Y_j) w_j+f_Q(Y_j), w_j=(F_N(Y_j),F_N(Q^-1Y_j))^t, T_Q=[-c0/c+, -c-/c+; 1,0], f_Q=(D/c+,0)^t, Y_(j+1)=Q Y_j. (1) This is the ORIGINAL affine source, not an arbitrary homogeneous initial vector. The equation is used away from zeros of c+ only. Its global root singularities and complete-point normal pointing remain exactly those in the actual operator/source theorem. Put Q=exp(h), h=2pi i/N. The limiting homogeneous transfer is T0(Y)=[P(Y),-1;1,0], P(Y)=Y^2+Y^-2-Y-Y^-1-2. (2) Its roots satisfy lambda+lambda^-1=P. On a regular spectral chart with lambda!=+/-1 choose V(Y)=[lambda,lambda^-1;1,1], a(Y)=Y/(Y^2-1), dot P=Y dP/dY. Differentiating the ACTUAL quantum coefficients, not just the classical symbol, gives T_Q=T0+h T1+O(h^2), T1=[-aP,2a;0,0]. (3) The source tends to f0=((Y+1)^2/Y,0)^t. (4) All these expansions are uniform on compact regular arcs. The roots and V can be continued there with their original marks. ## 2. The exact first-order channel connection is nonzero Write Lambda=diag(lambda,lambda^-1). Since dot lambda=dot P lambda^2/(lambda^2-1), the transfer between successive CLASSICAL eigenframes is V(QY)^-1 T_Q(Y) V(Y)=Lambda+h B(Y)+O(h^2), B=V^-1 T1 V-V^-1 dot V Lambda. (5) Direct rational multiplication gives B12=a/lambda+dot P/(lambda^2-1)^2, B21=a lambda+dot P lambda^4/(lambda^2-1)^2. (6) These include BOTH the subprincipal quantum coefficient and the moving-frame derivative. Ignoring the latter is not a time-step energy calculation. At the regular point Y=i, P=-4, lambda=-2-sqrt(3), one obtains EXACTLY B12=i(sqrt(3)-1)/6, B21=-i(sqrt(3)+1)/6. (7) Both are nonzero. The same point is an actual root-orbit sample for every N divisible by four. This mixing is therefore actual quantum transport, not a synthetic matrix counterexample. ## 3. What happens to the proposed step energy Suppose a genuinely identified peripheral branch has its ABSOLUTELY marked regulator R_i(theta), Y=exp(i theta). The [general peripheral bound](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md) and the actual boundary differential give |R_i|<=Vol(X), dR_i/dtheta=log|lambda_i|. (8) This identity uses the squared meridian Y and the actual longitude eigenvalue. It is not asserted for an unidentified factor of an arbitrary annihilator. Let G_N(theta)=diag(exp[-N R_i(theta)/(2pi)]), u_j=G_N(theta_j) V(Y_j)^-1 w_j. Then the EXACT step and source are u_(j+1)=A_(N,j) u_j+g_(N,j), A_(N,j)=G_N(theta_(j+1)) V(Y_(j+1))^-1 T_Q(Y_j)V(Y_j) G_N(theta_j)^-1, g_(N,j)=G_N(theta_(j+1)) V(Y_(j+1))^-1 f_Q(Y_j). (9) The ordinary energy identity is therefore ||u_(j+1)||^2=||A_(N,j)u_j||^2 +2 Re <A_(N,j)u_j,g_(N,j)>+||g_(N,j)||^2. (10) The source and its cross term have NOT been dropped. Equation (8) makes the diagonal factors of A have modulus 1+O(1/N). But for i!=k, (5) gives (A_(N,j))_(ik) =[h B_ik+O(h^2)] exp{N[R_k(theta_j)-R_i(theta_(j+1))]/(2pi)}. (11) A nonzero O(1/N) connection can thus have EXPONENTIALLY large weighted norm when the branch regulators differ. It is not absorbed by |R_i|<=Vol or by a polynomial number of time steps. For the actual geometric/conjugate figure-eight branches the complete regulator limits are +Vol and -Vol. They remain separated on a small regular punctured arc near completeness. The coefficients (6) are analytic on its connected hyperbolic spectral interval and are not identically zero by (7); their isolated zeros cannot fill that arc. Thus there are regular points with a fixed regulator gap and a nonzero dangerous entry in (11). The natural instantaneous weighted transfer is not uniformly contractive even in this solved prototype. The source is also genuinely present in both channels. At Y=i, f0=(2,0)^t, and V^-1 f0 is a nonzero multiple of (1,-1)^t. Its weighted norm cannot be declared polynomial solely because the UNWEIGHTED affine source is bounded. A common constant shift of all R_i changes source weights and the final evaluation together; it does not remove the relative exponential factors in (11). ## 4. What a successful dynamical estimate must add Equations (9)--(11) are a source-exact time-step formulation. To get a sharp cumulative upper bound from regulator weights one still needs an actual estimate on mixing and source response, for example an exact triangular source flag or an exponentially accurate branch connection with its Stokes and boundary matrices controlled. A fixed finite-order adiabatic diagonalization only replaces 1/N in (11) by a power of 1/N; that still does not beat a fixed regulator gap. Using the exact fundamental solution as the weight would trivially remove the dynamics, but would already encode the unproved Green response. It is not an independently derived estimate. Conversely, this calculation is not a lower bound for the complete invariant: the actual selected solution can and does exhibit cancellations between the terms in (10). Eigenvalue collisions require block transport rather than (5), and the complete root resonance needs its original source/normal Schur data. Neither issue explains away (11), which occurs on an entirely regular arc. The known figure-eight pointed Newton factorization supplies extra exact source structure and its endpoint evaluation metric; the actual five-crossing recurrence already needs a different two-channel treatment. No broad knot class has yet been shown to have the additional structure needed for a sharp regulator bound. The subsequent [pointed metric theorem](actual_pointed_metric_transport_and_crossing_obstruction.md) adds a quantitative limitation: even after retaining the actual input and output costs, a well-conditioned full-space positive metric may be forced to pay the larger spectral envelope. Its exact analytic example requires exponential metric conditioning to recover the true coherent rate. This is a general cocycle obstruction, not a further claim about the actual figure-eight operator above. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_regulator_weighted_a_transfer.py): the actual quantum coefficient expansion, both exact connection entries, the nonzero radical values, the original affine source, and finite root-orbit convergence of the mixing formula.

title: A single resolved head defect is forced to match; multiple defects retain charge
text: # A single resolved head defect is forced to match; multiple defects retain charge 28 October 2026. For a FULL finite canonical trace configuration of the original braid source, one isolated noncentral head-endpoint mismatch cannot survive: preservation of the actual lower (or upper) Borel moment forces its missing normal match. This gives a regulator bound for that specified class of restricted critical configurations. It is not an exact deletion of the quantum endpoint current or a bound on its entire period. For several mismatches the same calculation gives an exact weighted linear conservation law. There are genuine cycle charges. An explicit closed defective Hurwitz configuration shows that independent flag-stabilizer rescalings cannot in general be replaced by common crossing frames. That example has action zero and is not an excess-volume counterexample. ## 1. The original matrices and the endpoint relation Use the classical limits of the ORIGINAL physical matrices in [bounded quantum meridian transport](actual_bounded_quantum_meridian_transport.md): L_-(K,f)=[[1,0],[-K f,K]], L_+(K,e)=[[K,e],[0,1]], G=L_-^(-1)L_+=[[K,e],[fK,fe+K^(-1)]]. (1) The parabolic leaf is fe+K+K^(-1)=-2, so G has determinant one and trace -2. At a resolved lower endpoint write B=1-s and K=-B^(-1), f=tau, e=s^2/[B tau]. (2) Then s=0, tau!=0 gives G(tau)=[[-1,0],[-tau,-1]]. (3) The two sides of the physical head source may have tau_L!=tau_R. This is an actual source possibility, not merely a bad coordinate: the [resolved head calculation](actual_resolved_head_face_geometry.md) and the [endpoint factorial chart](actual_endpoint_head_factorial_chart.md) retain its finite window K_R(tau_L/tau_R), which is not supported only at ratio one. The normal clock is the same on both sides; the missing normal derivative is the logarithmic tau ratio. The actual crossing canonical graph preserves BOTH Borel products. For b heads put M_-=L_(-,b)...L_(-,1) =[[1,0],[-K_total F_total,K_total]], F_total=sum_j (K_1...K_(j-1))^(-1) f_j. (4) This is the leading canonical consequence of the literal original Hopf intertwining, with no scalar or framing normalization changed. The upper product similarly retains E_total and K_total. Both signs of a genuine crossing preserve these moment matrices. ## 2. Precise one-defect theorem, including the original source premise Consider an ORIGINAL one-component closed braid, with its justified whole-word averaged trace source chi_N/N Tr[(I tensor g tensor ... tensor g)W_N]. (5) Suppose a FULL restricted critical configuration has all the following properties: 1. It lifts to a finite canonical composition of the genuine resolved local crossing graphs, in their actual order and with their actual tags. There is no other transfer face or auxiliary relation replacing a genuine local graph. A tangential critical point in an arbitrary cleared chart is not being assumed to have this property. 2. Every ordinary wire matches its full phase point. There is exactly ONE nonmatching wire, with the lower endpoint relation (2)--(3): K_L=K_R=-1, e_L=e_R=0, f_L=tau_L and f_R=tau_R, both finite and nonzero. The upper version is obtained by exchanging e and f. 3. The trace is taken at a regular cut away from that defect. Its full leading canonical closing is the identity. All original pivotal and marked factors remain. Any original source face that replaces this identity by a different relation must instead be counted as another defect; it is not silently ignored. Then tau_L=tau_R. (6) ### Proof At a head j the difference of its two lower factors is Delta L_(-,j)=-K_j(tau_R-tau_L) E_21. Every genuine crossing preserves M_-. Every other wire matches. The regular trace fixed-point condition identifies the initial and final physical phase points, so their M_- matrices are equal. Therefore 0=M_-,final-M_-,initial =L_(-,b)...L_(-,j+1) Delta L_(-,j) L_(-,j-1)...L_(-,1). (7) All left and right factors are invertible. Thus Delta L_(-,j)=0 and (6) follows. This argument uses a complete canonical fixed point, not a separate Ward equation for an arbitrarily restricted operator. Here is why (5) provides the stated regular closing. In the original physical index basis it is a diagonal trace pairing, hence identifies the two clock variables and their exponentiated conjugate positions at a full regular stationary point. The actual pivot is g_a=x^(1-N)Q^(-a): its logarithm is order one in a/N, not order N. It and the factor 1/N are retained amplitudes and introduce no new leading canonical graph at a finite regular cut. The external chi_N and the common Cartan lines do not alter that closing. The cardinal source's exact integer modes shift logarithmic positions by integer turns and leave these multiplicative matching relations unchanged. Matched factorial frame changes cancel across the trace; replacing only one side would not be the original source. Consequently (7)'s top/bottom equality is supplied by the FULL original stationary trace closing under property 3. It has NOT been inferred from the operator equation [F_total,W_N]=0 after inserting a projector. Indeed [F_total,P_R] is generally nonzero. This theorem does not set that finite quantum rank-one current to zero. ## 3. Regulator consequence and its limits After (6), every wire and crossing is on the genuine graph, so the configuration is an honest parabolic knot representation. Apply the representation-independent marked fundamental-cycle calibration in [the actual regulator theorem, Section 5](actual_wall_critical_regulator.md#5-the-marked-fundamental-cycle-comparison-extends-beyond-faithfulness). It uses generic auxiliary flags and sends forced repeated developed vertices to zero in the normalized alternating complex. Finite shape limits at 0,1,infinity contribute zero by continuity of D; one does not have to deform an abelian knot representation through irreducible representations to use this chain identity. The omitted normal is the physical Log B=0 normal. Its contraction with the real logarithmic coordinates in the phase-defect identity is zero. After the restored match, all original integer logarithmic marks are retained exactly as in the full critical calibration. The actual representation-volume bound consequently gives |Im W_critical| <= Vol(S^3 minus K). (8) On a joint regular framed critical closure this also follows directly from [the saturated compactification](saturated_critical_regulator_compactification.md). No assertion that an arbitrary endpoint tuple lies in that closure is used as a substitute for the restored physical matching above. This conclusion concerns the one-defect configurations with the three explicit properties above. The assertion that an arbitrary restricted source face lifts to that finite composition remains a separate check. In particular no escaping conjugating frame, uncontrolled Bruhat denominator, second source defect or non-genuine transfer relation is covered by the word "finite." Nor does (8) bound the whole endpoint period, its transport mass or its normal neighborhood. The exact beta normal-jet calculation shows why evaluating a collision fiber is not enough for such a claim. ## 4. The exact multiple-defect boundary-to-interior charge equation For several lower-branch head jumps the argument is still exact, but its conclusion is a conservation law. Across a defect on head j, lower triangular multiplication gives Delta M_- = -(K_j...K_b) Delta tau_j E_21, Delta F_total=omega_j Delta tau_j, omega_j=(K_1...K_(j-1))^(-1). (9) The weights are evaluated at the actual time slice of that defect. They depend only on the physical clocks, not on the tau jumps. Crossings preserve F_total between defects; the defects do not change K_total. For a closed canonical trace the exact necessary equation is sum_defects omega_j Delta tau_j=0. (10) With prescribed boundary moment difference b, the right side becomes b. All weights are nonzero and rational in the actual finite clocks. If r such jumps are treated as independent boundary data, this map has an (r-1)-dimensional complex kernel when r>=2. The upper moment does not eliminate these f-branch charges: e=0 on both sides, so its jump is zero. Upper-branch defects have the analogous upper equation. Thus (10) is a genuine exact forced Borel transport equation, but it has retained homogeneous charges. It is not a coercive inverse for all jumps. The rest of the nonlinear closed Hurwitz equations can impose additional conditions; they must be proved, not replaced by uniqueness of a proposed geometric solution. ### A stable forced transport with its kernel retained Although (10) cannot remove the homogeneous charge, its forced part does have a controlled inverse. Write A=(omega_1,...,omega_r). In the Euclidean norm on these actual scalar tau-jump coordinates, Delta tau=A^* b/||A||_2^2 + h, A h=0, ||A^+||=1/||A||_2, ||I-A^+A||=1. (10a) If every physical clock in the relevant slices lies in N^(-epsilon)<=|K_h|<=N^epsilon, then ||A^+|| <= N^((b_heads-1)epsilon)/sqrt(r). (10b) Here b_heads is the braid width, distinguished from the boundary datum b. This is polynomial in N for a fixed word and fixed epsilon. It does not normalize the unknown knot period or suppose h is small. There is also a fully rational, holomorphic version, useful for the frame torsor. Choose one defect p; its weight is always a unit. Keep the other r-1 charges rho_j unchanged and set Delta tau_j=rho_j (j!=p), Delta tau_p=omega_p^(-1) [b-sum_(j!=p)omega_j rho_j]. (10c) All coefficients are rational in the actual finite clocks. Their norms on that window are at most C_word N^(2(b_heads-1)epsilon). Thus boundary data propagate stably AFTER the homogeneous charges are supplied. This is a quantitative forced Borel flow, rather than an inference that rigidity kills its kernel. The metric is explicitly the scalar charge metric; no bound in an unmatched quantum fusion frame is being asserted. The weights here are the PRESCRIBED ACTUAL clock trajectory. Solving (10c) does not assert that arbitrary rho_j leave later clocks unchanged under the nonlinear R maps, or solve all of their fixed-point equations. That feedback must remain in any use as an interior construction. ## 5. A closed free-charge example and a common-frame obstruction There is an explicit family where these charges are real geometric data of the defective canonical composition. Set on every head K_j=-1, e_j=0, f_j!=0, z_j=(-1)^(j-1) f_j. All based meridians are then H_j=-I-z_j E_21. (11) Direct substitution in the ORIGINAL based Hurwitz law shows that BOTH crossing signs simply SWAP adjacent z_i,z_(i+1). Equivalently their unbased f map is (f_i,f_(i+1))->(-f_(i+1),-f_i). This preserves the lower Borel product exactly, as it must. For any one-component braid the underlying permutation is a single cycle. Choose two distinct nonzero numbers a,b and let the initial z tuple equal b except at one position, where it is a. Its final tuple differs at precisely two positions. Closing the other heads honestly and allowing two endpoint jumps closes the entire finite defective configuration. Their z charges are +(a-b) and -(a-b), so (10) holds. Both jumps may be nonzero, while every crossing remains on the genuine resolved graph. The window K_R evaluated at a/b or b/a is not identically zero; for a/b=2 both are nonzero at every finite R. This does not assert a nonzero integrated knot contribution. These jumps cannot always be absorbed by common crossing frames. For example use the actual one-component word (1,-2,1,-2) and the initial tuple (a,b,b), a!=b, a,b!=0. At its first crossing the two noncentral commuting nilpotents have the relation (H_2+I)=(b/a)(H_1+I). (12) The ratio b/a is invariant under ANY COMMON SL2 conjugation of this crossing. Commutation is likewise invariant. If all crossings of an honest one-component Wirtinger representation have commuting incident meridians, the under meridian is unchanged at every crossing; following the knot makes every meridian the SAME matrix. Its crossing ratios must therefore all be one. Equation (12) cannot become that honest configuration by common crossing frames and matching wire frames. Independent head rescalings would change (12), but those are precisely the unproved extra covariance; they are not gauge equivalence of the original local crossing configuration. There is also a simple peripheral restriction. A diagonal stabilizer conjugates U(tau)=I+tau E_21 by tau->d^(-2)tau. An actual peripheral holonomy must centralize its noncentral meridian, forcing d^2=1. Thus an arbitrary residual diagonal scale cannot be dismissed as allowed longitude holonomy. This free-charge example lies on the ALL-clock/all-transfer endpoint stratum; its regulator is zero and that full endpoint packet already has a subexponential operator bound. It is not a counterexample to the volume upper bound. It does show that Borel conservation and common-frame freedom alone do not remove multiple defect charges. ## 6. What is now proved One finite, isolated head defect is restored at a genuine full trace critical point, with the original source premise made explicit. Its critical regulator is bounded by the knot volume. Several defects satisfy the exact rational charge equation (10); there is no automatic coercivity or common-frame removal. A general boundary estimate still needs the complete multi-defect source or an additional controlled transport of its homogeneous charges. No quantum endpoint current, unknown knot period, or exponential normal contribution is divided out. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_resolved_head_defect_moment_gluing.py): original signed quantum Borel intertwining, exact triangular jump weights, original trace-pivot scale and the closed free-charge example.

title: Resolved physical head faces: the original crossing and the missing wire equation
text: # Resolved physical head faces: the original crossing and the missing wire equation 28 October 2026. A physical clock B tending to one need not make its meridian central. The resolved chart f=(1-B)p finite contains a genuine noncentral unipotent. The restricted positive crossing at input b=0, including bulk transfer, is exactly the projection of the ORIGINAL Hurwitz graph in this chart. Its action can have nonzero regulator. This local resolution does not identify arbitrary restricted-face critical points of the full word with knot representations. At a shared head the two resolved parameters still have to agree. Fixing the head face omits precisely that equation, and the complete sublinear head packet has a generically nonzero off-diagonal reproducing kernel. The packet and every normal coefficient must remain in the source. ## 1. Restricted stationary values, with the singular normal removed correctly Write the actual marked phase in clock logarithms Z as W=sum_j epsilon_j Li2(A_j)+Z^t C Z/2+i kappa^t Z+c, A_j=exp(v_j.Z+i phi_j), C real symmetric, Im c=0. On a physical face a set of integral real forms obeys a_f.Z=2pi i n_f, n_f integer. (1) All its active shape-one terms have finite REAL Li2(1) values, with their recorded flattenings. Restrict those terms to their constants before differentiating. Call the resulting regular extension W_reg; the original normal derivatives of W itself may be logarithmically infinite. If the restricted phase is stationary in ALL complex tangent directions, elementary linear algebra gives partial W_reg=sum_f lambda_f a_f. (2) The active normals annihilate rho=Re Z. The same exact phase-defect calculation as for the full action therefore gives Im W_face=sum_(j inactive) epsilon_j D(A_j). (3) Indeed the defect is rho.Im(partial W_reg), which vanishes by (1)--(2). The omitted D(1) terms are zero. Integer mode marks from the cardinal windows are retained; they only add integer multiples of the face forms or of the other clock logarithms. They do not alter this proof. Equation (3) is a regulator CALIBRATION, not a bound by knot volume. Exponentiating (2) gives defect characters exp(lambda_f) in the regular- part equations. It does not impose the missing full normal equations or membership in the saturated original critical graph. In particular one must not evaluate the original unsaturated rational equations at their 0/0 shape-one factors. ## 2. A finite noncentral head chart For one actual head use the physical Gauss coordinates K=-1/B, e=(B^-1-1)/p, f=(1-B)p. Put s=1-B and tau=s p. Then K=-1/(1-s), e=s^2/[(1-s)tau], f=tau. (4) At s=0, tau!=0 this is a finite NONCENTRAL lower unipotent meridian. It was absent from the finite-p centrality argument. The complementary chart retains e finite and f tending to zero. The two branches obey the exact physical equation e f=(1-B)^2/B. (5) Consequently two finite nonzero e- and f-parameters cannot describe the same limiting head at B=1. Any change of chart or source adapter must preserve (5); its small action alone does not justify deleting it. The change is symplectic on the regular overlap. For the Liouville form, Log B dLog p - Log B dLog tau =d Li2(1-B). (6) This generating function tends to zero at B=1. Its normal derivative is still needed when matching adjacent charts. ## 3. The actual b=0 crossing is locally the resolved Hurwitz graph Use input clocks A,B, input positions p,r, and transfer U. The positive physical outputs have clocks C=BU and E=A/U. The actual input fields are e1=(1-A)/(A p), f1=(1-A)p, e2=(1-B)/(B r), f2=(1-B)r. The original Hurwitz graph has d=1-e1 f2, U=1/d. Let B tend to one in the chart (4), keeping A,p,tau regular and e1!=0. For any regular bulk U one can choose tau=(1-U^-1)/e1. (7) The limit is the ORIGINAL crossing graph, not a replacement map. Its output clocks and positions are C=U, E=A/U, p_out1=p/(1-A), p_out2=(A-U)p/[U(1-A)]. (8) Substitution in all six original Gauss formulas proves these identities. For example the output fields are e_out1=-A e1^2 tau, f_out1=-U tau/A, e_out2=-U e1, f_out2=-(1-A)p/U+tau(A/U-1/A). They equal the physical fields of (8). The chart is regular for A,U,A/U away from 0 and 1 and p,tau nonzero. There is an independent generating-function check using the literal physical coefficient, rather than assuming that a face belongs to the graph. At b=0 the EXACT coefficient is r(a,0,k)=kappa x^(-a+k) F_a/F_(a-k). (9) Let u=Log A, v=Log U, x tending to -1 on its retained lift. Its leading action, up to a real constant, is W_face=-Li2(A)+Li2(A/U)-i pi(u-v). (10) The original output/input position terms are v Log p_out1+(u-v)Log p_out2-u Log p. Stationarity in u and v gives EXACTLY (8). The omitted incoming second position is replaced by (7), finite in tau and divergent in r=tau/s. Thus every regular point of this restricted local canonical relation lifts to the resolved ORIGINAL local graph. This is a useful positive local theorem. It includes bulk k; such a face must not be declared central merely because B=1. The direct five-symbol regulator on this face is R_face=D(A/U)-D(A). (11) It need not vanish. At a simultaneous opposite head degeneration A=B=1, with e1 and f2 finite and e1 f2=1-U^-1, it becomes D(1/U). These are limits of the genuine local crossing regulator. Their nonzero values do not contradict the finite-p central theorem, whose physical-position hypothesis has failed. ## 4. An exact mixed factorial gauge and its scope Let D_j=F_j on the original head basis. Apply basis factor D^-1 to input 1 and output 2, and D to input 2 and output 1. With c=b+k, e=a-k, the transformed physical coefficient is exactly (F_e F_b)/(F_c F_a) r(a,b,k) =kappa x^(-a-b+k) Q^(b(a-k))/F_k. (12) All physical supports remain. This displays explicitly how the e- and f-type endpoint charts remove the local head-factorial singularities. The clock phases are still present. The actual current differs from the corresponding unweighted shift by its retained diagonal Q phase; no cyclic wrap is identified with the nilpotent shift. For a low packet 0<=j<=R=o(N), elementary sine bounds give |F_j| >=(4/N)^j j!, ||D|| ||D^-1|| <=exp[O(R log(eN/R))]. (13) For large N every root factor in that packet has modulus below one, so the smallest product is F_R and the displayed estimate follows from R!>=(R/e)^R. Reflection gives the same type of bound at the high packet, with its explicit N and unit phases. Thus the basis change and its inverse cost exp(o(N)); it is legitimate source transport on the WHOLE retained packet. Its adjoining wire/source factors remain. The stronger uniform two-band statement, its globally invertible truncated gauge, its band-interface arrows and mandatory cyclic correction are proved in [the endpoint head chart](actual_endpoint_head_factorial_chart.md). ## 5. What still has to be matched across a resolved head On a shared head the original identity gluing has the same B on the two sides and p_left=p_right. Equation (4) then implies tau_left=tau_right. (14) This condition is not restored merely by fixing s=0. For example the wire generating term on the regular overlap is Log B [Log tau_left-Log tau_right]. At B=1 its VALUE is zero and all tangent derivatives in the tau's are zero. Its omitted normal derivative is exactly the logarithm of the ratio in (14). This gives an explicit explanation of why the face-value identity (3) does not supply global representation gluing. Retaining all coefficients in a low packet preserves the exact source, but also retains its off-diagonal current. In the corresponding monomial head frames the identity wire is the reproducing kernel K_R(xi/eta)=sum_(j=0)^R (xi/eta)^j, (15) in coefficient/constant-term normalization. The unitary finite Fourier matrix kernel is K_R/N, as in the endpoint head chart; that polynomial normalization does not change the exponential conclusion below. Here xi,eta are the two resolved head coordinates. The adjacent factorial gauges cancel; a known pivot only changes its specified ratio. The kernel is polynomial and generically nonzero when xi!=eta. Its apparent Hardy matching pole is removable because both terms in K_R(q)=[1-q^(R+1)]/[1-q] have equal opposite residues at q=1. For example K_R(2)=2^(R+1)-1, so even a fixed off-diagonal separation is not suppressed at rate exp(-cN) when R=o(N). This is a statement about the actual retained source packet, not an arbitrary inserted coupon. It does not prove that the mismatch survives the exterior knot pairing. Normal stationarity before restricting the face WOULD impose (14). But a proof at exponential scale cannot infer that stationarity merely from the source being exactly preserved or from the gauge norm being subexponential. Endpoint and interface currents of the shrinking normal packet must either be estimated coherently or included in an actual resolved gluing theorem. Likewise an e/f wire must retain (5), not replace its small generating action by a unit. ## 6. Consequence for the desired face bound Local blowup resolves an important apparent obstruction: bulk transfer at a physical head endpoint can lie on the genuine crossing graph with finite noncentral meridians. The regulator and the tangent phase agree there exactly. If ALL resolved wires also satisfy their original matching equations and the full marked closure, these local graphs assemble to an original boundary-parabolic knot representation and the already proved representation-volume bound applies. Arbitrary restricted-face stationarity supplies neither (14) nor its e/f counterpart. Thus no blanket |R_face|<=Vol(K) theorem for every cardinal-window physical-face critical point is proved by the local resolution or tame basis change alone. The precise missing source estimate is for the complete off-diagonal normal-packet currents, with the original exterior phase retained. This is stronger and more specific than the old finite-position centrality statement. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_resolved_head_face_geometry.py): all six rational Gauss output identities, the two tangent generating equations, exact mixed gauge factors, endpoint packet norms, the noncentral resolved input and the retained off-diagonal wire source.

title: The actual resonant framed moment point is smooth over the quantum parameter
text: # The actual resonant framed moment point is smooth over the quantum parameter Research proof, 27 October 2026. The framed multiplicative moment scheme is smooth at the actual primitive-root head, including its quantum normal direction. Its cyclic-vector quotient has relative dimension 2N over Q. The ACTUAL ordered source section is a transverse cut by 2N equations, not an extra singularity of this ambient scheme. The proof gives an explicit Jacobian inverse and a literal quotient chart; no general quiver-variety smoothness theorem is used. This is a finite-head geometric theorem. It does not determine the scalar of an actual closed word, compare that word to a geometric regulator, or identify the distinct divisor 1-lambda^N of the geometric Fourier-framing pole. ## 1. Scheme and the actual resonant point Fix N at least two over C. Let X,Y be invertible N by N matrices, v a column, w a row and Q an invertible scalar. Set \[ G=Q^{-1}XYX^{-1}Y^{-1}-I-vw. \] Let M_N be the finite-type scheme cut out by ALL N squared entries of G. At a primitive Q_N put \[ X=B=\operatorname{diag}(1,Q_N,\ldots,Q_N^{N-1}),\quad Y=P,\quad v=e_0,\quad w=0, \] where P e_j=e_(j+1 modulo N). This is exactly the actual resonant head and its scaled moment covector in [the actual rank-one moment/source construction](actual_rank_one_multiplicative_moment_and_orbit_source.md). In particular BP=Q_N PB, so G=0. The root rank drop of vw is part of the specified point, not removed by inverting its normal. Taking determinants gives the automatic scheme-theoretic equation \[ 1+wv=Q^{-N}. \tag{1} \] Indeed det(I+vw)=1+wv, and det(Q inverse XYX inverse Y inverse) is Q inverse N. Their difference belongs to the ideal of the matrix entries of G. Equation (1) is not an additional independent moment equation, including on nonreduced bases. ## 2. Exact Jacobian and a right inverse at the actual point Use left tangent coordinates delta X=aB, delta Y=bP and epsilon=delta Q/Q_N. At the indicated point, direct differentiation of the four factors gives \[ dG=(I-\operatorname{Ad}P)a+(\operatorname{Ad}B-I)b -e_0\,\delta w-\epsilon I. \tag{2} \] There is no delta v term because w=0. The factor Q has been retained; replacing the commutator by an unscaled one would change the last term and the equation. The two adjoint actions commute at the root because BP differs from PB by the scalar Q_N. Here is an explicit relative right inverse, with epsilon fixed to zero. For any target H in Mat_N, put \[ t=\operatorname{Tr}H,\quad T=H-tE_{00},\quad \delta w=-t e_0^t,\quad \delta v=0, \] \[ a=\operatorname{diag}(a_0,\ldots,a_{N-1}),\quad a_0=0, \quad a_i=\sum_{k=1}^i T_{kk}\ (i>0), \] \[ b_{ij}=\frac{T_{ij}}{Q_N^{i-j}-1}\ (i\ne j),\qquad b_{ii}=0. \tag{3} \] All denominators are nonzero. The diagonal identity a_i-a_(i-1 modulo N)=T_ii follows because Tr T=0. Hence (I-Ad P)a equals diag T, while (Ad B-I)b is its off-diagonal part. Adding -e_0 delta w yields H, proving surjectivity of the relative Jacobian onto ALL Mat_N, not only sl_N. There is also a literal unit minor. Choose the tangent directions delta w_0, a_i for i=1,...,N-1, and b_ij for i not j. Their diagonal block has determinant -1; their off-diagonal block has determinant product_(i not j)(Q_N^(i-j)-1). Thus an N squared Jacobian minor is a unit. These left tangent coordinates differ from ordinary matrix-entry coordinates by invertible linear changes, so this is also a unit minor in an ordinary local chart. Consequently M_N is smooth over the Q-line at this point, of relative dimension N squared plus 2N. For completeness, this conclusion can be obtained directly without a smoothness import: on the open set where that minor is a unit, every square-zero error in G is removed uniquely in the chosen N squared coordinate directions by its inverse Jacobian. The other coordinates and Q are free. Repeating this for successive nilpotent ideals gives the formal local lifting property; the displayed polynomial/ Laurent finite presentation and unit minor give its usual smooth algebraic chart. No inversion of 1-Q^N occurs. In the flat positive root matrix norm, this particular right inverse can be bounded by 2 N^(3/2). Indeed the off-diagonal inverse gap is at most N/4, the trace row has norm sqrt N, and the diagonal prefix sum has norm at most N. The diagonal trace correction has norm sqrt N: its output is (-sum_(i>0)H_ii,H_11,...,H_(N-1,N-1)). Combining these estimates in the orthogonal product norm gives the displayed bound. This is only a bound on the explicit local Jacobian inverse, not a global neighborhood, word norm or selected-period estimate. ## 3. The Q-normal direction and the root determinant law The actual whole curve gives an explicit tangent lift of epsilon=1: \[ a=J_{head}=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,\ldots,N-1),\quad b=0,\quad \delta v=0,\quad \delta w=-N e_0^t. \tag{4} \] In fact (I-Ad P)J_head=I-NE_00, and substituting (4) into (2) gives zero. This is the derivative of the exact whole family X=diag(Q^j),Y=P,v=e_0,w=(Q inverse N minus one)e_0^t. Its divided defect, endpoint walls and actual co-source orbit are the ones already retained in the boundary theorem. Tracing (2) on a tangent vector to M_N gives delta w v=-N epsilon. This agrees exactly with differentiating (1). The zero root covector does not obstruct lifting the quantum normal. Locally delta=1-Q^N is another base coordinate because its derivative is -N Q_N inverse times delta Q. Thus the same smoothness gives actual local flatness over that normal parameter. It does not identify it with another geometrical pole normal. ## 4. A literal cyclic-vector quotient, with the correct dimensions On the open set where \[ H_v=[v,Yv,\ldots,Y^{N-1}v] \] is invertible, use it as the basis. In that basis v=e_0 and Y is the companion matrix with first N-1 columns e_1,...,e_(N-1) and last column tau=(tau_0,...,tau_(N-1)), with tau_0 invertible. The remaining coordinates are the N squared entries of X, N companion coefficients and N entries of w, besides Q, subject to the N squared moment equations. This is an explicit quotient, not a GIT assumption: every cyclic point is uniquely a pair of its matrix H_v and these companion- slice data. The cyclic chart is therefore GL_N times the slice, and simultaneous conjugation is left multiplication on the GL_N factor. Its stabilizer is trivial over all commutative base rings: an automorphism fixing Y and v fixes the entire cyclic basis. At the root the orbit matrix H_v is I. Any tangent right inverse from (3) can be put into the slice by the infinitesimal gauge minus delta H_v, without changing dG. Explicitly the j-th column of delta H_v is \[ P^j\delta v+\sum_{k=0}^{j-1}P^k(\delta Y)P^{j-1-k}v. \] Thus the sliced relative Jacobian is also surjective. The quotient is smooth over Q, of RELATIVE dimension 2N. Each fixed-Q fiber has dimension 2N; including the Q direction gives total dimension 2N+1. Vector pointing removes the scalar stabilizer as well. No source covector of the actual Whittaker type is presumed on every ambient point merely from this construction. ## 5. The actual ordered source section is a transverse cut Inside the companion slice impose the additional ACTUAL equations \[ Xv=v,\qquad Y^N=I. \tag{5} \] Since v is cyclic, the second equation is equivalent exactly to the N equations tau=e_0: applying it to v fixes the last companion column, and conversely that column makes Y=P. The first supplies the N equations X e_0=e_0. The constrained scheme is exactly the actual source section over the Q-base. Indeed with Y=P, the moment equation says that the image of XP-QPX lies in the zeroth line. The lower-row recurrence and the fixed first column force X=diag(Q^j), as in [the aligned cyclic-frame proof](flat_cyclic_source_frame_and_scalar_period.md), without division by delta. The remaining first row then gives w=(Q inverse N minus one)e_0^t. This argument works over arbitrary commutative bases and therefore rules out hidden nilpotent thickening. These 2N constraints are transverse at the actual root. To see this directly, a fixed-Q tangent in their common kernel has delta Y=0 and delta X e_0=0. The lower rows of the linearized moment relation give the same cyclic recurrence for delta X; its first column is zero, so every entry is zero. The top row forces delta w=0. The ambient sliced tangent has dimension 2N by Section 4. Hence the differentials of these 2N constraint functions form an isomorphism onto C^(2N). They are relative local coordinates. The actual Whittaker co-source is now canonical ell=ones transpose. It has ell v=1 and ell Y=ell, and its required orbit and both endpoint deletions are still retained; smoothness does not set their derivatives to zero. In particular this source section is not all of the smooth ambient 2N-dimensional moment fiber. There is a natural intermediate sourced locus. Adjoin a row ell with ell v=1, ell Y=ell, and impose Xv=v, but do NOT impose Y^N=I. In the cyclic companion frame the row is forced to be ones and the remaining equation is sum_i tau_i=1. These N+1 conditions are independent combinations of the transverse coordinates above, so this locus is smooth of relative dimension N-1 near the root. Imposing the remaining N-1 companion conditions gives the actual ordered section. This is a local assertion here; its explicit global recurrence classification can be proved separately. The subsequent [pointed companion theorem](pointed_companion_source_and_polynomial_hilbert90.md) now proves precisely that GLOBAL classification: the sourced cyclic chart is a principal open affine (N-1)-space over Q, with polynomial matrices, a canonical clock gauge and an explicit residual-polynomial co-source. Its proof needs no root-gap division and works over arbitrary commutative coefficient rings. ## 6. What this softens, and what it does not fix The resonant rank drop at the ACTUAL point is not a singularity of the source-vector-framed moment scheme. There is a smooth whole Q-normal deformation space, an explicit free quotient chart and a transverse actual source section. This supplies a precise algebraic setting in which comparisons can be made BEFORE quantum jets. The actual meridian parameter M and its kappa and norm factors can be retained as additional base coordinates and endpoint data. The argument does not identify them with the Q-normal or erase their source ratios. Likewise it does not identify delta with the independent intrinsic pole norm 1-lambda^N. Identifying these finite frames or their smooth moment spaces does not compare the selected scalar evaluations of a full actual crossing word. A closed scalar cI remains a separate word section. No regulator action, selected endpoint pairing or volume growth has been deduced from smoothness or from this finite quotient alone. ## 7. Reproducible exact audit [The independent script](../experiments/audit_actual_resonant_moment_smoothness.py) and [its output](../experiments/actual_resonant_moment_smoothness_results.json) check (2)-(4), an explicit Jacobian right inverse on every matrix unit, the actual Q-normal tangent, the companion-slice ranks and both sourced transversality dimensions over primitive-root fields. These are exact linearization tests supporting the direct proof, not an imported generic-parameter moduli theorem.

title: Actual prefix signs at the right-angled framing boundary
status: Original white-face lifts fix every finite boundary clock sign
text: # Actual prefix signs at the right-angled framing boundary 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. For the original right-angled matching-polyhedron cut, the limiting clock signs are determined by the OUTWARD face normals with their actual source lifts. In particular every 222 pair has two negative limiting clocks, every 022/220 finite clock is negative, and every 202 total is positive. There is no independent choice of signs or local framing. The input is the labeled geometric certificate and the actual white-reflection prefix dictionary. The statement is not asserted for an arbitrary routed crossing that lacks that dictionary. It does not compute the coefficient of a global selected period. ## 1. Keep the actual reflection lifts Fix the original exposed first physical head, with positive marked meridian J=[[1,1],[0,1]]. Its ideal fixed point p is infinity. The exterior reference white face F_ref contains p. Indeed the first head is the product of the two adjacent white reflections, and p is their common ideal vertex. The exterior spine is the recorded one in [the actual cut proof](actual_right_angled_selected_framing_obstruction.md), section 3, not a newly chosen basing path. For an outward UNIT spacelike face normal n write M(n)=[[n0+n3,n1-i n2],[n1+i n2,n0-n3]], H_f=adj M(n_f)=[[a_f,b_f],[bar b_f,d_f]], J_f=[[0,-1],[1,0]] bar H_f =[[-b_f,-d_f],[a_f,bar b_f]]. (1) The anti-linear map J_f followed by conjugation is its plane reflection. The ACTUAL trace-minus-two prefix lift is Q_f=J_f bar J_ref. (2) Consecutive products telescope with these signs; this is precisely the lift fixed by the original source dictionary. Multiplying individual Q_f by arbitrary minus signs would change the clock signs below and is not allowed. The marked ideal vertex lies in the inward halfspace of every face. For its null lift p=(1/2,0,0,1/2), this inequality is <n_f,p>=-(n0-n3)/2=-a_f/2<=0. Consequently a_f>=0; a_f=0 iff p is on F_f, a_f>0 for every nonincident white face. (3) Strictness is exactly the nonincident supporting inequality in the positive labeled certificate. Since a_ref=0 and det H_ref=-1, |b_ref|=1. Multiplying the recorded matrices now gives (Q_f)21=-a_f bar b_ref. (4) Thus all NONZERO lower-left prefix entries have the SAME phase and a strictly positive real coefficient. This is an equality of the actual SL2 lifts, not a projective sign convention inferred after computing a ratio. ## 2. The boundary table with its real signs In the common frame F(r,s)=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], let L_f=Tr(Q_f Pi), Pi=F E11 F^-1. For a nonincident face the leading term is L_f=(a_f bar b_ref/s)r^2(1+O(1/r)). (5) For incident faces it is constant, by the actual cusp-stabilizer calculation in the [source boundary theorem](actual_q_hahn_resonant_hard_edge.md). Fix s away from these finitely many constant-prefix zeros. At an original circle, label the consecutive incoming white faces F_0,F_1,F_2 as in that source theorem; the output has its own middle face and the SAME outer faces. Put X=-L_0/L_1, Y=-L_1/L_2, T=XY=L_0/L_2. (6) With 0 denoting an incident/constant face and 2 a nonincident/ quadratic face, (4)--(6) prove the following limits: | Pattern | Forced finite boundary data | | --- | --- | | 222 | X_infinity=-a_0/a_1<0, Y_infinity=-a_1/a_2<0 | | 022 | Y_infinity=-a_1/a_2<0 | | 220 | X_infinity=-a_0/a_1<0 | | 202 | T_infinity=a_0/a_2>0 | The a_i in this table are the positive coefficients in H_f, NOT the complex prefix diagonals L_i. In 002 and 200 the finite ratios of constant prefixes retain their actual dependence on s; the paired Bessel packets already keep that dependence. The two outer faces cannot both contain this marked MAIN cusp: their common ideal vertex is the distinct auxiliary cusp of the disk. Thus 000/020 do not occur in these original complete-circle boxes. The same proof holds with every retained half twist. Its shaded pairings and primitive auxiliary marking change, but the exact outside white-reflection prefix loops (2) do not. It also proves the signs for every original white interval and cup/cap adjacency to which the same dictionary applies. It does not authorize an arbitrary routed band to be assigned these original face labels. ### One main component gives every 200/002 Bessel calibration Suppose the fixed retained-half-twist diagram has ONE main component; the auxiliary crossing circles are still present. This is the relevant connectivity hypothesis when subsequent independent full twists produce a knot. Full twists do not change that connectivity. Every original based physical puncture is then a conjugate of the marked primitive main meridian or its inverse. In the recorded trace-minus-two lift it has the form -g J^epsilon g^-1, epsilon=+1 or -1, with g an ACTUAL element of the complete holonomy group. In a 200 box both Q_1 and Q_2 fix infinity, so the actual second puncture B=Q_2 Q_1^-1 does also. Its unique parabolic fixed point implies g(infinity)=infinity. The complete torus-cusp stabilizer acts by translations on its horospheres; hence g commutes with J. One can also see the absence of another multiplier directly: a dilation would make conjugates of J accumulate at the identity, while a nontrivial unit-modulus rotation would give a fixed axis in hyperbolic space. Discreteness and the free complete deck action exclude both. Therefore B=-J^epsilon in every original 200 box. Likewise Q_0,Q_1 fix infinity in a 002 box, so its actual first puncture is A=-J^epsilon. This is primitive meridian conjugacy, with no added longitude, cusp translation or independent local basing. It can fail when there is more than one main component. The orientation does not change the Bessel parameter. For 200 write Q_1=e[[1,z0],[0,1]], e=+1 or -1. Since Tr A=Tr B=Tr(BA)=-2, B=-J^epsilon forces A_21=4epsilon. At r=N rho the actual raw clocks give U_raw/N^2 -> -4epsilon rho^2/[s(1+z0 s)], V_raw -> (1+z0 s)/(1+(z0+epsilon)s). Their actual white arguments remain q^-1 times these clocks. Substituting these limits in the proved 200 Bessel parameter cancels epsilon and gives K=s^2 sin^2(pi mu)/(4pi^2 rho^2), mu=m/N. For 002 write Q_0=e[[1,z0],[0,1]]. Now A=-J^epsilon forces B_21=4epsilon, and U_raw -> (1+z0 s)/(1+(z0+epsilon)s), N^2 V_raw -> s(1+(z0+epsilon)s)/(4epsilon rho^2). The proved 002 parameter gives the SAME K. All constant-prefix zeros remain excluded as above. Thus the original 200/002 Bessel theorems cover every such original box in this one-main-component class, including either orientation and every fixed retained-half-twist pattern. At the literal Fourier scaling rho=1/(2pi i j), fixed j!=0, the limit is I_0(2j s sin(pi mu)); it is nonzero when Re s!=0. This is a local root-numerator conclusion, with exact normalizations retained in the source theorem. It does not add a generic normal or a global period claim. There is also a nonzero local choice compatible with the actual [off-node source family](actual_braided_residual_framing_current.md), section 5. Take rho in a positive real compact and s=exp(-2pi i alpha)-1 with alpha in a compact subset of (0,1/2), still avoiding the finitely many excluded constant-prefix zeros. The packet is J_0(s sin(pi mu)/(pi rho)), with a nonreal argument, and is therefore nonzero. For completeness, if J_0(z)=0, its radial equation (t f')'=-z^2 t f for f(t)=J_0(zt), integrated against bar f, gives z^2 integral_0^1 t|f|^2=integral_0^1 t|f'|^2>0; hence z is real. On the same positive-rho compact the exact source family's limiting factor rho(1-exp(-1/rho))exp(t_coh/rho) is nonzero as well. This is compatibility of local parameter choices: the coherent variable t_coh is not identified with alpha, and the unknown whole-source coefficient or a selected cycle is not determined. ## 3. Actual half-index and factorial consequences Retain physical head i=N x-1/2, with X=exp(2pi i x), exactly as in the source boundary theorem. The actual white argument is q^-1 X, not X. A negative finite limiting clock has a logarithmic lift with Re x=1/2; a pair of them has canonical total Re(x+y)=1. This is a boundary of the earlier strict physical packet, not a point claimed to lie in one of its fixed compact subsets. In particular the 222 finite head clocks stay away from X=0,1 and infinity. The finite clocks of 022/220 do also. The remaining head in 022/220 has imaginary part of order N log N; its actual factorial normals have the separately proved [logarithmic-escape control](actual_moving_period_factorial_logarithmic_escape.md) when their stated argument hypotheses hold. Auxiliary rows still come from i+j=(d-a)+r0 with the ACTUAL discrete a. They are not assigned the universal physical-head -1/2 offset. For 202 the total is on a positive compact ray for a fixed diagram and boundary chart, so the whole-polynomial relative packet in the source boundary theorem applies without changing the reference cusp. For 220 the actual qU approaches a strictly negative ray, exactly the domain of the complementary determinant packet; 022 is transported by the ACTUAL generic reciprocity with its scalar and marks retained. There is also a useful exact finite matrix consequence for the 222 LIMITING clocks, separate from an asymptotic statement. The original small-channel determinant identity in the [complementary source theorem](actual_q_hahn_complementary_hard_edge.md) is H_a^1(U,V)/V^a=[2a choose a]_Q det[I-(qU/2)H_--(q^-1/(2V))H_+]. (7) The Hermitian matrices H_-,H_+ are positive definite for every actual a<=floor((N-1)/2), including the fold. At the physical half-index arguments U=q^-1 X_infinity, V=q^-1 Y_infinity, (7) contains I+|X_infinity|H_-/2+H_+/(2|Y_infinity|)>=I. (8) Thus this exact limiting-argument determinant is strictly positive. For the large m=d-a the original forced partner product remains. No generic derivative is obtained by differentiating that root collision identity. Nor does (8) by itself replace the actual r=N rho arguments by their limits: their O(1/N) perturbation can change a determinant of size O(N) by an order-one factor. The boundary dictionary supplies honest geometric domains for the actual numerators and factors. It does not prove a full 222 packet, erase finite offsets or characters, or supply the original relative framing-cycle coefficient. Focused audit: [actual signed cuboctahedral prefixes](../experiments/audit_actual_right_angled_resonant_prefix_signs.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_right_angled_resonant_prefix_signs_results.json). The labeled ideal right-angled cuboctahedron, cube matching in one coordinate and marked main edge in another supply all six permissible patterns. The audit retains the actual SL2 lifts and their trace-minus-two heads; it checks 168 support inequalities, 24 right angles, six prefix matrices, 16 ordered disk triples and two half-index identities. Eight additional exact symbolic cases retain both primitive orientations, both prefix lifts and both 200/002 endpoint formulas. Primary-agent independent normal-lift calculation: PASS. The common phase, strict inward-halfspace signs and recorded source lifts were checked directly. Independent full analytical review and fresh redirected audit: PASS. That reader additionally checked the pattern consequences, actual half-index cancellation and the limited SPD conclusion. No generic partner differentiation, boundary asymptotic or global period is inferred. The one-main-component corollary received independent primary and coherent-source proof reviews: PASS. Both primitive orientations, the actual cusp-conjugacy argument, the two Bessel parameter reductions and the nonreal-argument J_0 criterion were checked. The coherent-source reader freshly replayed the expanded audit, including all eight signed cases. The local nonzero packets and the separate off-node source factor are not identified with a whole-source or relative-cycle coefficient.

title: The right-angled cut obstructs an all-central selected frame
status: No all-central selected frame; exactly two physical failures
text: # The right-angled cut obstructs an all-central selected frame Subsequent full-domain result: the [full strict physical packet](actual_q_hahn_full_physical_complex_packet.md) extends the actual ordinary amplitude and the stated small/near-fold complex bounds to fixed physical compacts, with the necessary finite-level boundary correction. The [selected-factor corollary](actual_augmented_plat_selected_factor_localization.md) then selects every ordinary factor outside one prescribed matching-edge block. Global contraction and period estimates remain open. The argument below keeps its original domain and proof scope. 30 October 2026. The shaded-face circle packing does give common exteriors. It does not supply a frame in which every original ordinary column is both in the proved central domain and on its selected endpoint sheet. For the literal projection Morse prefixes of a positively certified right-angled augmented plat, the following argument instead gives an obstruction to that simultaneous choice. The unfolded geometric critical germ, the actual quantum source, and the volume conjecture are not contradicted. The obstruction concerns this particular all-column physical-support/selected-sheet route. The decisive dictionary is section 3. It retains the actual projection basepaths and the positive normalizations of the reflection lifts; an abstract circle packing without this dictionary would not prove the statement. ## 1. Geometric input and statement Let Q be the labeled convex ideal right-angled polyhedron supplied by [the actual matching-graph certificate](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md). Its shaded faces are triangles; its white faces are the actual projection regions. Every edge separates the two colors, and every vertex has four alternating incident faces. The shaded triangles are paired by the actual crossing disks. Half twists retain the face quotient and primitive marks recorded in that construction. At the horizontal cuts outside the crossing boxes use the original ordered Morse meridians H_1,...,H_m and prefixes Q_i=H_i...H_1. The exterior projection region is F_0. The two conditions in question are: * Every input and output triple has canonical wire logarithms in the CENTRAL domain of the framing criterion and the joint kernel theorem. * Every input and output lies on the source-selected endpoint sheet in the selected-local certificate, with the positive geometric orientation. Subject to the literal prefix identification proved in section 3, NO common rank-one frame has both properties. The argument uses the weaker necessary strict-support test, not a failure peculiar to the central wedge boundary. ## 2. Disks of nonadjacent facets and the white-normal polyhedron Use Lorentz signature (-,+,+,+). Choose an interior point of Q as the Klein origin, and write every outward unit facet normal as n=(n_0,n_vec). Then n_0>0. Adjacent normals have Lorentz product zero. Distinct facets which do not share an edge have disjoint supporting planes in hyperbolic space. Here is a direct proof for this ideal right-angled setting. If two such facets share an ideal vertex, their planes are the opposite vertical planes of its rectangular horosphere link, hence are parallel. Otherwise their closed ideal boundaries are disjoint. A bounded- distance minimizing sequence between the two facets cannot escape: two bounded-distance sequences escaping to infinity have the same ideal limit, which would be a common ideal boundary point. Thus the distance is achieved at finite points. A minimizing point in a facet interior has a perpendicular joining geodesic. If it is on an edge, the neighboring facet plane is orthogonal. The tangential direction toward the other closest point lies in the outward normal cone of that edge, by minimality; but its scalar product with the same edge normal is nonpositive because the other point belongs to Q. Orthogonality makes these two statements force the tangential component to vanish. There are no finite vertices. The minimizing segment is therefore perpendicular to both supporting planes. Intersecting planes have no positive-length common perpendicular. The planes are disjoint. The orientations face the common interior of Q, so their outward halfspaces are disjoint. Indeed, for disjoint planes the alternative orientations would put one plane strictly in the outward halfspace of the other, making its supporting inequality redundant or removing that facet of Q. Their unit normals consequently have product at most -1. In particular same-colored outward ideal disks have disjoint interiors, with tangencies only at shared ideal vertices. A finite set of these disks has a nonempty open common exterior: take a point on one boundary away from all finitely many tangencies and then move a little to its exterior. For each WHITE face f put v_f=n_f,vec/n_f,0, C=conv{v_f}. (1) For each SHADED face b with outward normal m_b, exactly its three neighboring white normals satisfy m_b,vec . v_f=m_b,0. (2) Every other white normal satisfies the strict inequality < in (2), by the preceding disjoint-plane argument. Those three v_f are not collinear: their three unit normals have Gram matrix with diagonal 1 and off-diagonal -1, of determinant -4. They are linearly independent, and their positive affine normalizations are therefore not collinear. Thus they give an exposed triangular facet of C. These triangles have exactly the dual incidence of the original checkerboard sphere: two white vertices are joined at each ideal vertex of Q, and the two shaded triangles there are its two incident facets. The cyclic links at a white vertex are the original white-face boundary cycles. Consequently the known triangles form an embedded closed connected two-manifold in the boundary of the three-dimensional convex hull C. Along every known edge both convex-hull sides are already present; at every vertex the known cyclic link is the whole link. There is no room for an extra facet. Equivalently this closed triangulated sphere is both open and closed in the boundary of C. Hence C={ y in R^3 : m_b,vec . y <= m_b,0 for EVERY shaded b }. (3) This is an equality of finite Euclidean convex polyhedra. It is stronger than merely saying that C meets the unit ball. It identifies C with the intersection of the shaded inward halfspaces, extended in Klein coordinates. Its vertices are generally outside the unit ball and its edges are tangent to that ball. Let K be the open common exterior of all shaded ideal disks. A flag in K, viewed as a unit vector on the Klein sphere, is a STRICT interior point of C. The distinction matters: an arbitrary hyperbolic geodesic need not meet C. Only the selected flags will supply its required endpoints in C. ## 3. The literal white-reflection prefixes Let r_f be reflection in the white face plane f. At a horizontal Morse cut outside all crossing boxes, label the white intervals encountered from the exterior left spine by F_0,F_1,...,F_m. The original prefix loop surrounding the first i punctures is the two-white-face bigon: it crosses the projection cut in F_0 and F_i, with its upper and lower paths lying in the two opened projection balls. The horizontal cut misses every crossing-disk half sheet; the exterior spine misses them as well. Thus these paths need no unrecorded shaded-face deck transformation. Reversing the literal cut identifies its projective holonomy as Q_i=r_(F_i) r_(F_0), H_i=r_(F_i) r_(F_(i-1)). (4) The order is the original convention Q_i=H_i...H_1, not its inverse. It can be checked in the canonical incoming disk coordinate eta, in which its punctures are 0 and 1 and its auxiliary flag is infinity. The consecutive white reflections are r_0(eta)=-conjugate(eta), r_mid(eta)=conjugate(eta)/(2conjugate(eta)-1), r_1(eta)=2-conjugate(eta). They give A=r_mid r_0, B=r_1 r_mid and P=r_1 r_0, exactly the original canonical puncture pair after eta=1/(2s+1). A cup or cap has equal first and last white regions, so (4) gives the required inverse pair. A retained half twist changes the shaded pairing and the auxiliary primitive meridian; it does not change these outside two-white-face loops. The input and output before/after a box have the same two outer white faces. Both are adjacent to BOTH shaded faces meeting at that box's auxiliary ideal vertex. The lift signs are also fixed. In the Hermitian Lorentz model use M(n)=[[n_0+n_3,n_1-i n_2],[n_1+i n_2,n_0-n_3]], H(n)=adj M(n), E=[[0,-1],[1,0]], J(n)=E conjugate(H(n)). For an outward UNIT spacelike normal, J(n) conjugate(J(n))=I, and J(n) followed by conjugation is its plane reflection. Direct multiplication gives tr[J(n_g) conjugate(J(n_f))]=2<n_g,n_f>. (5) The consecutive white planes at a main segment are tangent and face the common interior, so their product is the required trace -2 lift. The actual negative-parabolic heads therefore telescope without independent signs: Q_i=J(n_(F_i)) conjugate(J(n_(F_0))). (6) Changing from a unit normal to the normalized vertex (1,v_f) rescales by n_f,0>0. Thus the linear coefficients used below have only POSITIVE relative normal factors. Arbitrary sign choices for reflections would lose this fact. ## 4. Selected sheets put both global flags in K Write the common projector as Pi=v ell, ell(v)=1, and let w=ker ell. Put w_0=r_(F_0)(v). For a coupon whose left prefix interval is F, equation (4) gives W_prefix v=r_F(w_0). (7) Its two shaded disk circles bound the region Omega of the selected-local certificate. This is precisely the common exterior of those two outward shaded disks: at their common auxiliary vertex they become the parallel sides of the original cusp rectangle. The primitive orientation gives the positive strip between them, not either exterior complementary half-plane. Both planes are orthogonal to the adjacent white plane F. Thus r_F preserves EACH shaded halfspace and preserves Omega. On the CENTRAL domain the proved selected input/output tests require w and W_prefix v in Omega. By (7) this is equivalent to w,w_0 in Omega. Every shaded face occurs in exactly one original disk pair, so all the tests together imply w in K, w_0 in K. (8) This proves the separated strip intersections are nonempty in this geometry; it does NOT yet give the coupled physical-support inequalities. The latter are what fail below. ## 5. Polarization forces a failed strict-support triangle For every original prefix, its diagonal is a_f=ell[ J(n_f) conjugate(J(n_(F_0))) v ] =ell[ J(n_f) conjugate(w_0) ]. Since ell has kernel w, all a_f are one common nonzero scalar times the polarized circle forms L_n(w,w_0)=det(w,J(n)conjugate(w_0)). (9) These are real-linear in the Lorentz normal n. Up to complex conjugation, (9) is the Hermitian polarization w^* H(n) w_0. For a null normal with M(n)=y y^*, direct factorization gives w^* H(n) w_0=conjugate(det(y,w)) det(y,w_0). (10) If w!=w_0, the simultaneous real and imaginary kernel of (9) is therefore the Lorentz two-plane spanned by the two null lifts of w and w_0. To verify that it has exactly dimension two, send these two distinct flags to the coordinate axes: the condition is the vanishing of one off-diagonal Hermitian entry. If w=w_0, the kernel is a real hyperplane containing its null lift; the following argument still applies. By (8) and (3), those null lifts, normalized to time coordinate 1, give points of the STRICT interior of C. Thus the affine kernel of (9) meets int C. A real line in that kernel, through such a point, meets the boundary of the bounded polyhedron C. Let a boundary point lie in a shaded facet with neighboring white vertices v_0,v_1,v_2. It has barycentric coordinates lambda_i>=0, sum lambda_i=1. Linearity gives sum_i lambda_i L_((1,v_i))(w,w_0)=0. (11) The unit normal n_i is n_i,0(1,v_i), with n_i,0>0. By (9), equation (11) is a nontrivial NONNEGATIVE relation among that facet's three actual prefix diagonals a_i, after dividing each weight by n_i,0 and renormalizing their sum. Therefore 0 in conv_R{a_0,a_1,a_2}. (12) But this shaded facet is one original input or output factor. Its strict physical-support criterion requires exactly the opposite of (12). If the boundary point lies on an edge or vertex, zero weights are allowed in (11), and the same contradiction follows. A vanishing diagonal would additionally violate the regular chart rather than evade the argument. Thus the geometric oriented-strip conditions and simultaneous strict physical support cannot both hold for this literal right-angled factorization. In particular the proved CENTRAL-domain source-sheet certificate has no common frame here. ## 6. A generic pair has exactly two failed physical triples The obstruction has bounded combinatorial size. For a generic pair of DISTINCT flags w,w_0 in K, its affine polarization kernel is a line through int C which meets the boundary in the interiors of exactly TWO facets. A facet's diagonal triangle contains zero if and only if this line meets that facet: both directions follow from (9), the positive normal scalings, and barycentric coordinates. Therefore exactly two original input/output triples fail the convex-hull test, independently of the number of bridges, boxes, or white faces. Such generic pairs exist, and one may also avoid every total-degree seam and regular-chart divisor. Indeed distinct endpoint pairs in the open set K times K parameterize an open set of hyperbolic geodesics, equivalently Klein affine lines meeting the open ball with these endpoints. Meeting any one fixed edge line of C imposes a nonzero real algebraic coplanarity condition on this four-real-dimensional line space. It cannot contain an open subset. Avoiding the finitely many such conditions makes the two boundary intersections interior to facets. A bounded convex polyhedron and an interior-crossing line have exactly two boundary points. For a disk, put its two outer white circles at Re eta=0 and Re eta=1. If eta(w)=a+ib and eta(w_0)=c+id, its actual right flag has coordinate -c+id under the left white reflection. Up to a common scalar the two outer prefix coefficients are a_0=-(a+c)+i(d-b), a_2=(a+c-2)-i(d-b). Thus Im(a_0 conjugate(a_2))=-2(d-b). The seam condition is exactly Im eta(w_0)=Im eta(w), a proper real analytic condition on ANY open subset of K times K. The strip coordinate is finite there and its imaginary part is nonconstant. A finite union of these seam loci also has empty interior. At cups and caps the two outer faces coincide, but one may additionally avoid a real ratio for the two DISTINCT adjacent white coefficients. This too is a proper algebraic condition: for any two distinct white normals, real dependence of their complex polarizations means that the kernel Lorentz plane meets their real span. In the affine chart it is the coplanarity condition for the kernel line and the line through those two white vertices, including parallel intersection at infinity. A fixed such condition has empty interior in the open space of secants. Avoiding it is stronger than, and implies, the required cup/cap canonical-log test. Finally (w,w_0) maps to the common frame by v=r_(F_0)(w_0), ell(v)=1, ker ell=w. Away from v=w this is a real analytic diffeomorphism onto an open part of the frame quotient. The finitely many proper algebraic regular-chart divisors cannot contain that open part. All the exclusions can be made simultaneously. At every remaining facet the framing criterion therefore gives STRICT PHYSICAL support, with its canonical low or high adapter. Exactly two facets still fail that criterion. The next corollary shows that their identities can in fact be prescribed. This is a geometric localization statement. It does not show that the other factors lie in the smaller central domain, extend the proved source-sheet equivalence to the whole physical strip, or estimate the two exceptional factors. Those distinctions prevent this corollary from being mistaken for a global amplitude theorem. ### The two exceptional facets can be prescribed Choose ANY two distinct shaded facets b_1,b_2 of C. Each supporting hyperbolic plane lies in the inward halfspace of every other shaded plane. Its whole unit-sphere circle therefore belongs to its C facet; away from the finitely many tangency points it lies in that facet's relative interior. Equivalently, the triangular facet circumscribes this circle and its edges touch at the original ideal vertices. Choose distinct non-tangency points r_i on the two circles. Their open chord is in int C, since its endpoints are relative-interior points of different facets, and it lies in the open unit ball. Perturb each r_i a little within its own facet, away from the circle's center, to a point p_i OUTSIDE the closed unit ball and still in the relative facet interior. A fixed midpoint of the chord remains in the open ball by continuity. Thus the line through p_1,p_2 has two distinct sphere intersections, both strictly between the p_i and hence in int C. These sphere flags w,w_0 belong to K. The full intersection of their line with C is precisely [p_1,p_2], so its two failed facets are exactly b_1,b_2. All these properties persist on an open set of endpoint pairs. The finite edge, seam, cup/cap, projector and regular-chart exclusions from the preceding argument can therefore be imposed as well. For an algebraic positive certificate the flags may also be chosen algebraic: the strict feasible set is open in a rational chart of the sphere-pair space, and algebraic points are dense there. In particular take the two shaded triangles incident to the ORIGINAL marked physical main edge of the matching graph. They are distinct and meet at that edge's ideal vertex in Q. The two exceptional ordinary column factors can be localized at those two vertices, without moving the mark or changing the source.
