Thus the z-dependent expression in (8) is bounded above by its n-dependent constant minus (1/2)|log(z/2)|. Evaluation at z=2 and the following limits show that its maximizers stay in one fixed compact subset of (0,infinity). On that compact, continuity and homogeneity give uniformly F(2,B_n,2)=(1/2)log B_n+o(1), F(2,B_(n-1),B_n)=(1/2)log B_n+F(0,1,1)+o(1), 2F(2,B_(n-1),z)=log B_(n-1)+o(1). The limiting z-dependent function is -2F(2,z,0)+(1/2)log z. Its derivative vanishes only when the angle at z is pi/2, namely at z=2; strict log-radius convexity makes this its unique maximum. Substituting in (8) proves sup_(z>0) G_n(z)=-log n+K+o(1), K=F(2,1,2)+2F(2,1,0)-(3/2)log2. (9) In particular the best fixed-old-radius test is NEGATIVE for every sufficiently large n. Full radius readjustment is essential here. This does not say that the fully optimized smoothed capacity exceeds the original capacity: the former is an infimum over ALL remaining radii, whereas (8) varies only the merged radius. ## 4. Remaining general comparison Literal smoothing identifies opposite middle faces. It is not ordinary deletion of the shared white edge01, and a generic graph-minor volume inequality is not automatically its capacity inequality. Section3 also rules out promoting the one-variable test to a theorem forced by every positive labeled certificate. The general connected untwisted smoothing gap and its near-complete small-color corridor are now [proved separately](actual_smoothed_block_representation_volume.md) in the original fixed flat-plat scope. That theorem does not provide the missing presentation adapter for the family in section3. The present note retains its exact sufficient source bound in section1 and its independent matched-graph functional limitation. Signed varied ports and far-color source bounds remain separate. Focused audit: [original source and labeled certificate checks](../experiments/audit_actual_smoothing_fixed_radius_gap.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_smoothing_fixed_radius_gap_results.json). At 80 digits it checks ten literal original marked L_1 contractions against the shorter face-coefficient source, retaining every remaining half twist and the original cups, mark, and measure. These original matrix fixtures test section1; they are NOT the Apollonian graphs of section3 and do not establish the missing adapter. The audit also checks two symbolic tangency identities; nine perfect matchings, three-connected graphs, and connected literal smoothings; 2,340 white and 3,816 shaded support values; and 432 original right-angle incidences. Seven finite optimized one-variable profiles and one positive-marked regularization check diagnose the exact normalization. The analytic argument, not those finite profiles, proves the all-n limitation in (9). Primary full analytical proof and audit-code review: PASS. Independent targeted geometric review: PASS, including the literal embedded matched graph, perfect matching, interstice insertion, convex supporting-halfspace induction, and the actual opposite-face smoothing. These reviews do not infer a full optimized smoothing gap or an L_h alias bound. Independent full analytical proof/code review and fresh redirected 80-digit replay: PASS. Every reported source, certificate, and profile count was reproduced. The review retains the sufficient nature of (3), the exact charge/alias qualifications after (5), and the fixed-old-face scope of the counterfamily. ### Source-coverage correction, 30 October 2026 The earlier wording called the section3 family an original source counterexample to the fixed-radius strategy. The verified statement is the narrower geometric matched-graph CAPACITY obstruction (9). The frozen exact face identity proves a fixed flat-plat formula, not the general Morse formula that the earlier inference would need. An arbitrary link-to-plat isotopy does not verify preservation of the designated complete-circle tensors, their original mark or the face coefficient normalization. All displayed geometry, functional formulas and asymptotics remain unchanged. The audit code and saved results are unchanged; no rerun or new original-source comparison is claimed by this correction. title: Adversarial audit of the source-volume Casson--Rivin argument
text: # Adversarial audit of the source-volume Casson--Rivin argument 29 October 2026. Independent analytical review. The claimed filled-volume identification is not circular on the proved source family, but it uses several substantial inputs BEFORE strict concavity. This note separates them and distinguishes the two volumes in the user's question. ## 1. The two volumes must remain distinct The notation \(V_s\) is the volume of the COMPLETE AUGMENTED base, with its crossing-circle cusps UNFILLED. The source limit for the actual filled link is \[ V_{\rm src,s}(\boldsymbol p)=2\pi\operatorname{Re}\mathcal A_s(\boldsymbol p). \] The whole-source theorem establishes this number as the original quantum limit before asserting geometric equality. It is not set equal to \(V_s\). Indeed [local charge selection](actual_pretzel_long_filling_charge_selection.md), sections 2--3, gives a strict source action drop for every sufficiently long finite tuple: \[ V_{\rm src,s}(\boldsymbol p)<V_s,\qquad V_{\rm src,s}(\boldsymbol p)\longrightarrow V_s \quad\text{as }\max_i|p_i|^{-1}\longrightarrow0 . \tag{1} \] The derivative estimate there, equation (8), proves the strict inequality; it is stronger than an expansion with an unquantified remainder. For orientation, its quadratic formula (11) reads \[ V_{\rm src,s}(\boldsymbol p)=V_s- 2\pi^2\operatorname{Im}\tau_s \sum_i|1+2p_i\tau_s|^{-2} +O_s(\|\boldsymbol p^{-1}\|^4). \tag{2} \] This is only a local expansion. Equality with the ACTUAL filled hyperbolic volume requires the further geometric argument below. ## 2. What proves the source has a positive interior angle point The dependencies in [the Casson--Rivin note](actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) are: 1. **Original source selection, not formal gluing.** Its section 1 invokes [whole-source survival](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md), sections 1--2. This establishes the exact original invariant's nonzero full-sequence asymptotic and hence its rate \(V_{\rm src}\). The color complement, all aliases, original normal terms, endpoint currents and noncancellation are analytic premises. Concavity does not prove them. 2. **An actual marked representation near a known geometric point.** [The literal port theorem](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md), sections 1--6, supplies the source-selected \(\rho_z\), its cap order, preferred peripheral words, and the COMPLETE geometric anchor \(\rho_0\). This uses the explicit augmented geometry. It does not assume that a filled \(\rho_{\boldsymbol p}\) is geometric. 3. **A positive chart at the COMPLETE base.** Casson--Rivin section 2 chooses a fixed positive geometric ideal triangulation of that complete manifold. The CURRENT class-specific input is [the direct positive ideal-angle certificate](actual_pretzel_positive_ideal_angle_certificate.md), sections 1--3: exact homogeneous lifts of the actual polyhedra, all original white/shaded half-twist face maps, and finite compatible affine subdivision give this triangulation directly. Its section 4 also checks the full edge/peripheral tangent rank. The former [Ge audit](ge_geometric_triangulation_audit.md), sections 1--3, conditional on Epstein--Penner, remains an alternative route; it is no longer a dependency for this actual class. The direct proof asserts no universal all-ideal existence theorem for an arbitrary augmented base, and is not itself a quantum source-selection theorem. 4. **Continuity, not an assumed maximizer.** Equivariantly move those finitely many ideal vertices using the selected peripheral flags. They vary continuously from the complete noncentral parabolic flags. Cross-ratios stay in the upper half-plane in one fixed neighborhood. Exact representation relations give the complex edge equations; their angular lifts remain \(2\pi\). The source's inverse-slope implicit-function argument puts every sufficiently long independently signed tuple in that neighborhood. It follows that the actual source point is in the RELATIVE INTERIOR of the prescribed affine angle slice. Thus the interior critical point is not obtained from the statement “a concave functional has a maximum.” It is supplied by an actual source-selected representation which is a small deformation of an independently identified positive complete geometry. None of these steps assumes the desired filled-volume equality. The alternative [finite-center core construction](actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md), sections 2--5, and the [general equivariant averaging construction](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md), sections 2--5, prove the geometric completion without requiring the all-ideal triangulation input. They are sufficient for final equality even when one does not use the Casson--Rivin angle presentation. ## 3. The constrained functional is concave and uses FILLED slopes The actual domain in Casson--Rivin section 3 is the positive angle polytope with tetrahedral sums \(\pi\), edge sums \(2\pi\), and \[ \operatorname{Im}(U_i+p_iV_i)=-2\pi,\qquad U_i=-z_i,\quad V_i=-2\ell_i , \tag{3} \] on each filled auxiliary cusp. The logarithms are the SMALL centered PROJECTIVE logs. An old SL longitude sign is not added as a further geometric rotation. A remaining main cusp has its chosen meridian angle zero; the source representation in fact has both its peripheral logs zero. With two main components, the corresponding conditions are imposed on BOTH unfilled cusps. Equation (3) is the all-positive unit charge convention. The other minimal charge signs use their corresponding eigenflag marks. The existence/noncancellation of the selected contribution was already proved in the quantum source theorem. For tetrahedral angles \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma=\pi\), let \[ \mathcal V(\theta)=\sum_t [\Lambda(\alpha_t)+\Lambda(\beta_t)+\Lambda(\gamma_t)]. \] In the two free angles its negative Hessian is \[ \begin{pmatrix} \cot\alpha+\cot\beta&\cot\beta\\ \cot\beta&\cot\gamma+\cot\beta \end{pmatrix}. \tag{4} \] Its determinant is \(1\), and its first diagonal entry is \(\sin\gamma/(\sin\alpha\sin\beta)>0\). Therefore the functional is STRICTLY CONCAVE, not convex, on every affine positive-angle slice. Maximizing on the old UNFILLED completeness slice would concern \(V_s\) and would not prove the filled claim. The large signed integers \(p_i\) belong in the actual affine constraints (3). ## 4. Why stationarity holds for all angle tangents Casson--Rivin section 4 correctly uses the coisotropic edge reduction, not a derivative only along the much smaller representation variety. For \(x=\Log z,\ y=\Log z''\), direct sine-rule differentiation gives \[ d\mathcal V(\delta\theta) =\sum_t(\operatorname{Re}x_t\,\delta\gamma_t -\operatorname{Re}y_t\,\delta\alpha_t). \] The REAL log vector of a complex gluing solution and EVERY tangent obeying the homogeneous edge-angle constraints lie in the edge coisotropic space. The audited boundary pairing, independently on each boundary torus, consequently gives \[ d\mathcal V(\delta\theta)=\frac12\sum_i [\operatorname{Re}V_i\,\delta\operatorname{Im}U_i -\operatorname{Re}U_i\,\delta\operatorname{Im}V_i]. \tag{5} \] There are no cross-torus intersection terms. At the source point the REAL part of its actual filling equation is \(\operatorname{Re}U_i+p_i\operatorname{Re}V_i=0\). Each term of (5) is therefore \[ \tfrac12\operatorname{Re}V_i\, \delta\operatorname{Im}(U_i+p_iV_i)=0 . \] Unfilled cusp terms vanish because both actual logs are zero. This proves the full KKT criticality on the affine slice, including variations not arising from nearby complete gluing solutions. Strict concavity then makes the source point the unique global maximizer, including comparison with the boundary by continuity. ## 5. Absolute calibration, boundary correction, and smooth completion The source-to-volume equality is not fixed by a cusp Hessian alone. [The marked regulator proof](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md), sections 1--4, uses the SAME group representation, eigenflags, preferred longitude and COMPLETE anchor to prove \[ D_{\rm src} =\operatorname{Im}G-\sum_i\operatorname{Re}z_i \operatorname{Im}\ell_i =D(\beta(\rho_z)). \tag{6} \] Its section 3 defines \(\beta\) by an actual decorated fundamental chain, not an unproved extension of a unipotent coefficient identity. The literal spin \(\lambda=-L_H^{-1}\) is retained before the paired norm. Its exact filling term is \[ W=G+\sum_i(z_i-2\pi i m_i)^2/(4p_i). \] At stationarity \(\operatorname{Re}z_i=-2p_i\operatorname{Re}\ell_i\), so \(\operatorname{Im}W=D_{\rm src}\). Thus no unestimated complex endpoint term is suppressed when passing from the source action to the volume functional. Finally Casson--Rivin section 6 invokes independently proved smooth completion. The [primitive log theorem](actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.md), sections 2--5, identifies the actual log-link periods BEFORE multiplying by a large slope. The selected slope period is exactly \(2\pi\) in absolute angular value, not merely scalar PSL holonomy and not a \(4\pi\) branched fill. The [compact log-link and tube proof](long_pretzel_equality_critical_audit.md), sections 2--5, gives the full tube and degree-one complete filling; the unfilled cusp or cusps remain complete. Therefore the regulator value is the volume of a genuine positive complete hyperbolic metric on the ACTUAL filled topology. Comparing it to a specified hyperbolic metric via the independently proved representation-volume inequality in both directions identifies their volumes without assuming a separate equality-rigidity theorem. The dependency chain is \[ \text{whole source rate}\ \longrightarrow\ \text{actual marked }\rho_{\boldsymbol p}\ \longrightarrow\ \text{positive interior angle point and filled-slope KKT} \ \longrightarrow\ \max\mathcal V=V_{\rm src} \ \longrightarrow\ \text{smooth complete filled volume}. \tag{7} \] No arrow is justified solely by the previous maximum's numerical value. In particular neither a KKT equation without the positive chart/primitive logs nor strict concavity without a verified source point proves the assertion. ## 6. Current exact quantum scope The old Casson--Rivin and survival bodies state odd \(s\geq25\). The subsequent [width extension](actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.md), sections 5--6, supplies the missing whole-color gap for every fixed odd \(s\geq9\). Section 8 of that note separately verifies the parity-independent source and normalization and gives the ORIGINAL single-cut reduced two-component link theorem at every fixed even \(s\geq10\). For even width both unfilled main cusps remain parabolic and complete; the boundary-pairing and completion arguments are their direct sum. The even-link statement is not obtained by calling a link a knot or modifying each component separately. In both cases all \(|p_i|\) are independently sufficiently large FIXED integers. Their signs and ratios are unrestricted. The common threshold may depend on the fixed width, and can be enlarged once to enter the fixed positive geometric neighborhood. Neither width nor slopes grow with the quantum level \(N\); both level parities and composite levels remain included. Widths \(3,5,7\) and even \(4,6,8\) are not supplied by this current global source estimate. The general geometric certificate applies far beyond pretzels, but the actual quantum source survival is not thereby established for arbitrary graphs or all hyperbolic knots. **Verdict:** the proved-family equality is noncircular with these dependencies. Casson--Rivin is a valid concave variational characterization of the already source-selected point; it is not a substitute for the source-selection and geometric-existence inputs. No new computation was used in this audit.

title: A source-fixed quantitative norm for the actual divided fusion current
text: # A source-fixed quantitative norm for the actual divided fusion current 29 October 2026. The TWO-PHYSICAL-HEAD factorial-fusion defect has a polylogarithmic norm and inverse norm in a specified source-fixing factorial metric. This controls the complete unipotent current, not just its homogeneous bulk, and is an operator estimate before any exterior is paired or phases discarded. The metric is the physical gauge L^(1/2), distinct from the LENGTH frame L^(1/4) in the normalized binary blocks. Merging larger physical blocks is a separate issue: its degree-N current has a genuine positive angle norm. No polynomial bound for arbitrary block fusion or a sharp whole-knot energy estimate is inferred. ## 1. The unchanged original current and factorial identity Use N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1 and the ORIGINAL complete balanced head. Put Ecal|a>=(Q^-a-1)|a-1>, K|a>=x Q^-a|a>, x=-q^-1, F_a=(Q;Q)_a, s_a=|F_a|, p_N(X)=sum_(a=0)^d X^a/F_a. Let A=Ecal_1 K_2, B=Ecal_2 and C=A+B. The genuine generic Weyl lift, divided BEFORE root specialization, gives the actual operator J=[C^N/(1-Q^N)]_root =sum_(a=1)^d N B^(N-a) A^a/[F_a F_(N-a)]. (1) This is the already proved [divided-Ward fusion](divided_ward_factorial_fusion.md), including its normal direction and even-level signs. One has J^2=0 and [J,C]=0. Its full finite factorial identity is EXACTLY p_N(-tB)p_N(-tA)=Theta(t) p_N(-tC), Theta(t)=I+(-t)^N J/N, Theta(t)^-1=I-(-t)^N J/N. (2) The sign (-t)^N, all degrees of the finite product, and its actual inhomogeneous/normal current are retained. No equality of the bare homogeneous factors without Theta is asserted. ## 2. An explicit source-fixed physical metric Let L_a=s_a^2/N, G_a=L_a^(1/2)=s_a/sqrt(N), G=diag(G_a). Exact root complementation gives G_a G_(d-a)=1. Thus G on both legs fixes every ORIGINAL cup and ordinary cap, and the full marked co-source after its permitted whole-network degree restriction, as in [the weighted physical Fourier theorem](actual_weighted_fourier_plat_energy.md). The original pivots commute with G. No exponential condition number is charged at that paired source, although G itself is exponentially conditioned in the flat physical basis. The marked-row assertion is used on the fully assembled original degree-preserving operator, or with its actually transported row. It is not a replacement of the unrestricted marked row after splitting off a degree-changing current sector. Directly, G Ecal G^-1 |a> =(Q^-a-1)/|1-Q^a| |a-1>, 1<=a<N. (3) It is a unit-phase unilateral lowering shift, of operator norm1; K remains unitary. Hence every power of the transformed A or B is a contraction. Write ||T||_G=||G^(tensor2) T G^(-tensor2)||. The precise two-head estimate is ||J/N||_G <= R_N, R_N=sum_(a=1)^d 1/[s_a s_(N-a)] =(1/N)sum_(a=1)^d 1/|1-Q^a| <=(1/2)H_(floor(N/2)), (4) where H_r=sum_(j=1)^r1/j. Indeed (1),(3) give the first inequality. Reflection yields s_a s_(N-a)=N|1-Q^a|, and |1-Q^a|>=4 min(a,N-a)/N proves the last bound. In particular ||Theta(t)||_G, ||Theta(t)^-1||_G <=1+|t|^N R_N. (5) For fixed-log tags |t|<=exp(c/N), both norms are O_c(log N). They are polynomial for the more general condition |t|^N<=N^c. There is no such claim for fixed |t|>1. This is a concrete positive Hermitian metric and an explicit bound, not a Gram chosen from an unknown terminal knot operator. In ordinary unitary Fourier coordinates its matrix is H_F=F (L tensor L) F^*, (6) with F the two-head unitary Fourier transform. It is generally non-diagonal. Equivalently conjugate the current by (F_1 G) tensor (F_1 G) and use the flat norm, where F_1 is one-head Fourier. The same source and dual factors must be transported. ## 3. All-exterior scope and coherent packet metrics Identity(2) is an identity of the original finite matrices, so it can be inserted into ANY specified original polynomial exterior, including its actual caps and cut. For a boundary column v, and for a whole boundary matrix V in the corresponding Hilbert--Schmidt norm, (5) gives both comparisons (1+|t|^N R_N)^-1 ||p_N(-tC)V||_G <=||p_N(-tB)p_N(-tA)V||_G <=(1+|t|^N R_N)||p_N(-tC)V||_G. (7) All currents are still present in the exact operator. Tensoring spectators does not change this norm. A FIXED number of such two-physical-head adapters costs at most a fixed power of log N, if their tags obey the stated fixed-log bound and their physical metric interfaces are matched. This is before dephasing; phases in (1) have not been estimated separately at the selected scalar. An arbitrary left exterior X does not turn (7) into a relative comparison of |source(X p_N(B)p_N(A)V)| and |source(X p_N(C)V)|. A scalar may cancel or vanish. Moving an adapter across X requires its actual intertwining relation, or the transported boundary Gram X^*H X. The bounded local adapter does not establish either automatically. There is a useful exact compatibility test for a new packet Gram. If P is ANY invertible function of this SAME total current C, then P commutes with J and Theta. In the pulled-back Gram H_P=P^* (G^2 tensor G^2) P the norm of Theta is therefore exactly its norm in G. Consequently (5)--(7) remain valid. This is a genuine way to include the retained current in a non-diagonal coherent packet metric. The actual q-Pascal matrix is a nilpotent Euler function of a physical current, up to recorded chirps, but identifying its relative register with this two-head C requires the typed module map; it is not inferred from equal dimensions. An arbitrary P need not fix the original source: its vector, co-vector and Riesz norm must be transported through that map. ### Overlapping physical pairs really do have a common tame metric On any fixed b-head space use the SAME global gauge G^(tensor b). Every two-head E-coproduct adapter on adjacent heads, tensored with the spectator identity, has the bound(5) in this metric. The pairs may overlap. No commutation between different adapters is required. Consequently, for a fixed finite word U of these adapters or their inverses, ||U||_G, ||U^-1||_G <=product_j (1+|t_j|^N R_N). (7a) Fixed-log tags give a fixed power of log N. The same physical gauge fixes the original paired endpoints as stated above. This is a valid quantitative overlap lemma, not an estimate only for disjoint two-head blocks. There is an exact limitation on what that word can implement. For b=3, N>=3, take a_i>0 with a_1+a_2+a_3=N. On the input |a_1,a_2,a_3>, every single two-head J leaves a third positive head unchanged. Every product of two or more J's lowers total degree by at least2N and therefore annihilates that input. Hence EVERY word of bare pair adapters and inverses has <0,0,0|U|a_1,a_2,a_3>=0. (7b) By contrast, the full three-head current in(8) has the NONZERO coefficient of modulus1/(s_(a_1)s_(a_2)s_(a_3)) there. Thus bare overlapping tame pair adapters cannot generate that full block correction. A further typed packet conjugation or other operator is necessary. Conjugating by a function of the SAME current is covered above; an overlapping packet for a DIFFERENT current need not commute and is not covered. Opposite raising/lowering orientations also require their actual mirror and metric adapters; (7a) asserts the common E-coproduct orientation just specified. ### A neighboring packet Gram carries an explicit angle weight There is also a quantitative test of the remaining interface. On three actual heads put C_23=Ecal_2 K_3+Ecal_3 and P_23=p_N(C_23). In the coherent packet Gram H_23=P_23^* G_global^2 P_23, G_global=G tensor G tensor G, the neighboring J_12 is measured by its conjugate P_23 J_12 P_23^-1 in the base G metric. On head3=0 the actual packet restricts EXACTLY to p_N(x B), B=Ecal_2: Ecal_3 kills that subspace and K_3=x there. J_12 preserves it as well. For A=Ecal_1 K_2 one has BA=Q^-1 AB. The finite Euler shift equation, with the nilpotent argument Z=xB, gives exactly p_N(Z) A^a p_N(Z)^-1 =A^a product_(j=1)^a(1-Q^-j Z)^-1. (7c) All inverses are finite polynomials because Z^N=0. The coefficient of Z^h in the last product is Q^-h [a+h-1 choose h]_(Q^-1), by the finite coefficient form of the elementary q-binomial generating identity. For 0<=h<a<N and a+h-1<N this coefficient uses only nonzero factorials. In the matrix entry from |a,N-a+h,0> to |0,0,0>, the term a of J_12 is the UNIQUE term lowering head1 to zero, and the displayed h is the unique extra lowering on head2. The conjugated G Ecal G^-1 shifts and K factors have unit modulus. Thus the entry of P_23 (J_12/N) P_23^-1 in the base G frame has modulus |[a+h-1 choose h]_Q|/[s_a s_(N-a)]. (7d) This is a full operator entry, including the retained current and the inverse packet, not one term selected before their cancellation. For N=4k, a=2k,h=k, formula(7d) is exactly |[3k-1 choose k]_Q|/(2N) =(1/2)w_N(k,2k-1,k), (7e) where the three nonnegative indices sum to d. It is an explicit positive affine-angle ENERGY weight. Its logarithmic rate is Lambda(pi/4)*2/pi=Catalan/pi, by the uniform factorial estimate. It must receive geometric accounting rather than being declared polynomial. The same entry of the conjugated Theta_12 is multiplied by |t|^N; its identity term is zero on these distinct input/output states. If |t|^N and its reciprocal are polynomially bounded, this entry has the same exponential rate. An upper bound on |t| alone would not justify that lower-rate assertion. Consequently the nice two-head adapter bound does not automatically persist in a neighboring total-current packet Gram. This does not exclude a global coherent Gram, a source-restricted estimate, or an angle-energy comparison that RETAINS(7e). It pinpoints the additional typed recoupling which the global estimate must handle. ## 4. Why arbitrary-width block fusion is not automatically tame For b actual physical heads let C_b be the total Ecal and J_b=[C_b^N/(1-Q^N)]_root. The exact q-multinomial expansion is J_b/N=sum_(a_1+...+a_b=N,0<=a_i<N) phase(a) product_i Ecal_i^(a_i) K_dressings /product_i F_(a_i). (8) Here every phase and K dressing has modulus one after the complete source-fixed gauge G^(tensor b). Thus ||J_b/N||_G <= sum_(a_1+...+a_b=N,0<=a_i<N) product_i s_(a_i)^-1. (9) For any tuple in (8), its matrix coefficient from |a_1,...,a_b> to |0,...,0> is supplied by that UNIQUE term. Its modulus in the G frame is exactly product_i s_(a_i)^-1. No cancellation in the operator sum can remove this lower bound. The uniform root-factorial estimate and the positive simplex maximum proved in [the clock-source note](actual_length_gauge_clock_source.md) therefore yield, for each fixed b>=2, lim_(N->infinity) (1/N)log||J_b/N||_G =b Lambda(pi/b)/pi. (10) For b=2 this is zero, in agreement with the sharper bound(4). For b=3 it is v_3/pi, with a_i/N near1/3. This is a real positive angle weight in the ACTUAL divided operator, not a hypothetical scalar exterior or a numerical bad state. Likewise the mixed adapter merging blocks X,Y contains the tuples straddling both blocks. When their total has at least three physical heads, the uniform tuple still straddles them. On total input degree N its exponential has only its first degree-N term; higher normal powers cannot cancel that matrix coefficient. Thus the two-head bound cannot be silently iterated into a polynomial bound for arbitrary block fusion. The positive angle cost has to be retained and controlled by the global geometric incidence. This does not obstruct a sharp geometric energy theorem. It identifies a tame local current adapter and the explicit angle energy that appears at the first genuinely larger fusion. Global source gluing and geometric edge support remain to be proved. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_source_fixed_divided_fusion_norm.py): literal actual matrices, complete factorial/Theta identities, source-fixed metric, norm/inverse bounds, and the unique multihead coefficient with all Frobenius phases retained.

title: The original source has an exact Fourier resolution into twisted traces
text: # The original source has an exact Fourier resolution into twisted traces 27 October 2026. The all-strand endpoint source admits a resolution into UNIT-density Frobenius traces on one common matrix algebra of actual word coefficients. Their source-conjugation transport satisfies an explicit nonabelian norm equation. Primitive Fourier sectors have finite cyclic transport (as do gcd-two sectors); the remaining transport is unipotent, with index EXACTLY gcd(k,N). The zero sector has index EXACTLY N when N>2. Thus nilpotence exists but is not uniformly bounded in level. Individual sectors are not knot invariants: an actual braid-conjugacy test changes their values while preserving their marked Fourier sum. No sector is identified here with a geometric A-period, nor is its coefficient bounded subexponentially. This note does not replace the already proved symmetric trace on the full E,F,K centralizer in [the integral cut theorem](integral_projective_cut_duality.md). ## 1. The actual endpoint is a Nakayama-relative line Use the actual root algebra and cap of [the Euler/Cauchy theorem](actual_euler_cap_cauchy_boundary.md): A_0=<H,f | H^N=1, Hf=Q^-1 fH, f^N=0>, e_j=(1/N)sum_k Q^(jk)H^k, tau(f^a e_j)=delta_(a,N-1), nu(H)=QH, nu(f)=f, tau(ab)=tau(b nu(a)). Set z=xf, J=1/[(1-z)(1-Qz)] and E=e_(N-1)J, nu(E)=e_0 J, s=f^(N-1)e_0. The rational expression J is an actual finite polynomial because z is nilpotent. Its degree-(N-1) coefficient is zero at Q^N=1. Also e_(N-1)J e_(N-1)=e_(N-1). Consequently E^2=E, tau(E)=0, tau(s)=1, E a nu(E)=rho_0(Ja) s for EVERY a in A_0, (1) rho_0=[f^(N-1)e_0]. For (1), the two endpoint idempotents in e_(N-1)Ja e_0 select exactly its f^(N-1)e_0 coefficient. Right multiplication by J does nothing to s since s f=0. Thus the actual source is a specified rank-one linear compression between DIFFERENT projectives. Ordinary compression E a E would erase it: E is a primitive idempotent lifting e_(N-1), so E A_0 E=C E, and tau vanishes on that entire corner. More explicitly put n=e_(N-1)(J-1). Then n^2=0, n e_(N-1)=0, and E=(1-n)e_(N-1)(1+n). The corner claim follows from e_(N-1)A_0 e_(N-1)=C e_(N-1). In contrast (1) is nonzero at a=s. This linear compression is not a word quotient. Already at N=2, the actual positive crossing coefficient is a_R=eta I+(eta^-1/2)s, eta=exp(pi*i/4). Here J=1. The map P(a)=E a nu(E) has P(e_0)=0 but P(a_R e_0)=(eta^-1/2)s!=0. Transport on the selected scalar line alone would lose real word data. One must retain the projective memory E A_0, or another independently proved source complex. Nor is the single cap a twisted trace for some automorphism merely because tau is. If tau(Eab)=tau(Eb theta(a)) for every a,b, Frobenius nondegeneracy implies nu(E)nu(a)=theta(a)nu(E). Thus nu(E)A_0=A_0 nu(E). A normal idempotent is central: both off- diagonal corners vanish. But the center of A_0 is C and E is a proper primitive idempotent. This rules out that shortcut. The Fourier resolution below instead uses invertible densities. ## 2. Align all tail heads on ONE actual coefficient algebra The [all-strand source theorem](all_strand_euler_cauchy_cap.md) decomposes the closed tail into r=N^(b-2) normalized Borel heads. For b>=3 label them lambda=(t,j), with y_lambda=YQ^-j; for b=2 use one head and j=0. Let C_lambda be its actual two-leg fusion. The physical GLOBAL H=K_total/(xY) acts in that local regular frame as Q^-j times left multiplication by H. Replace that local frame by Psi_lambda=C_lambda composed with nu^-j. (2) Indeed nu^-j(Ha)=Q^-j H nu^-j(a), so (2) intertwines the same global H and f on every copy. Consequently the full actual braid, INCLUDING all off-diagonal tail transitions, acts on row vectors by right multiplication by a matrix A in B=Mat_r(A_0). Transposing the usual array of block right coefficients gives this row-vector convention. Operator composition is right action in its original order; no diagonal blocks are extracted during multiplication. The physical Euler-dressed coefficient matrix is b=U^-1 A U, U=diag(u(z)), u(z)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1) z^a/(Q;Q)_a. The matrix Frobenius functional and Nakayama map are T(b)=sum_lambda tau(b_(lambda,lambda)), nu acts entrywise, T(ab)=T(b nu(a)). Changing from the local head to (2) sends its word coefficient to nu^j of the local coefficient. Therefore the ORIGINAL source from the all-strand theorem becomes EXACTLY P_W=chi_W gamma_0 T(D b), gamma_0=N x^(b(1-N))Q, D=diag_lambda[Q^-j e_(j-1)J]. (3) All original framing and full peripheral factors remain in chi_W. This is valid for varying actual meridian x=-M/q at the fixed root on its original source lattice. It does not equate central-F and moving-q normals. Formula (3) follows either from the literal pivotal trace or from rho_j(Jb)=tau(e_(j-1)Jb); no invariant is divided out to choose the frame. ## 3. Fourier resolution into genuine unit-density traces The idempotent Fourier formula gives D=(1/N)sum_(k=0)^(N-1) C_k, C_k=diag_lambda[Q^(-j+(j-1)k)] H^k J. (4) Every C_k is a UNIT of B. Define Phi_k(a)=T(C_k a), theta_k=Ad_(C_k) composed with nu. Then Phi_k is a nondegenerate Frobenius functional and Phi_k(ab)=Phi_k(b theta_k(a)), P_W=(chi_W gamma_0/N)sum_k Phi_k(b). (5) For the twisted trace identity, T(C_k ab)=T(b nu(C_k)nu(a)). Since nu(C_k)=Q^k C_k, its scalar multiplier cancels in inner conjugation, giving theta_k as stated. These are actual whole-word source sectors, not characters assigned to semisimple root points. Their Fourier SUM recovers the original nonunit source density D. If desired the space of all invertible Frobenius densities is a torsor under the noncommutative unit group B^times. It is not yet the G_m/norm-one torus of a simple quantum A-eigenline. Passing to that latter object requires its own central spectral compatibility. ## 4. Exact finite-order and unipotent source transport Put g=gcd(k,N), d=N/g, taking g=N,d=1 when k=0. The scalar- diagonal phases in C_k have Nth power one. Using HfH^-1=Q^-1 f, the product formula for its Nth power is C_k^N=G_k(z) I_r, G_k(z)=[(1-z^d)(1-Q^d z^d)]^-g. (6) Indeed multiplication visits every dth-root orbit of z exactly g times. The two factors in J give the two products displayed in (6). All are units on the actual nilpotent source. Also nu(C_k)=Q^k C_k and nu^N=Id. Hence theta_k^N=Ad_(G_k(z) I_r). (7) In particular primitive k has g=1, z^N=0, so G_k=1 and theta_k^N=Id. This conclusion is valid at every composite N too. The same holds for g=2: Q^d=-1 and the two denominator factors multiply to 1-z^N=1. For g>2 the bound (8) is sharp. For the remaining k, G_k=1+O(z^d). On the basis f^a H^j, Ad_(G_k)(f^a H^j) =f^a [G_k(z)/G_k(Q^-j z)] H^j. The factor in brackets minus one belongs to (z^d), and Ad_(G_k) fixes all functions of z. Iterating a difference therefore gains one further factor z^d on each iteration, proving the sharper bound (theta_k^N-Id)^g=0. (8) To see sharpness, the leading term for g>2 is G_k(z)=1+g(1+Q^d)z^d+O(z^(2d)). The ratio at j=1 has nonzero leading coefficient g(1+Q^d)(1-Q^-d)z^d. Its (g-1)st power survives because d(g-1)<N. Thus the index is exactly g. In particular there is no uniform level-independent bound. For k=0 and N>2, G_0(z)=J(z)^N=1+N(1+Q)z+O(z^2). Its ratio at j=1 has nonzero linear coefficient N(1+Q)(1-Q^-1). Thus (Ad_(G_0)-Id)^(N-1)(H)!=0, while its Nth power is zero: the index in (8) is EXACTLY N. The exception N=2 has J=1, so its cyclic transport is already finite order. The growing index and the unestimated word coefficients prevent using nilpotence alone as a subexponential norm estimate. There is an explicit Hilbert-90 gauge in every g<=2 sector. Put C_k^0=diag_lambda[Q^(-j+(j-1)k)]H^k and mu_k=Ad_(C_k^0) composed with nu. It sends z to Q^-k z. Choose the finite nilpotent exponential g_k(z)=exp sum_(a=1)^(N-1) (1+Q^a)z^a/[a(Q^(ka)-1)]. (8a) At g=1 every displayed denominator is a unit. At g=2 the sole resonant degree a=d has numerator zero too; choose that coefficient to be zero rather than interpret a zero-over-zero expression. Coefficient comparison in the finite logarithm proves g_k(Q^k z)/g_k(z)=J(z), theta_k=Ad_(g_k) composed with mu_k composed with Ad_(g_k^-1). (8b) For k=1 this gauge is especially concrete: g_1(z)=v(z)v(Qz)=[u(z)u(Qz)]^-1 =(1-z)^-1 u(z)^-2. (8c) Thus the finite cyclic transport is explicitly solved, but its comparison gauge contains TWO quantum Euler factors. It is not a polynomial-norm estimate and must retain those factors in a regulator comparison. For g>2 the nonzero resonant term at degree d prevents solving the same scalar-polynomial gauge equation: its numerator 1+Q^d is nonzero while Q^(kd)-1=0. This is precisely the remaining unipotent defect rather than an omitted normalization choice. The subsequent [uniform actual-gauge action proof](actual_hilbert90_gauge_dilogarithm_action.md) now makes this metric issue quantitative. For the CANONICAL finite polynomial g_1, uniformly on |z|<=1/4, g_1(z)=exp[(2/h)Li_2(z)+O(1/N)], h=2pi*i/N. Its flat right-regular operator and inverse have positive exponential norm rates, so its condition number grows exponentially. This is the specified actual source gauge, not an arbitrary rescaling. In contrast, [its Euler meridian half-step](actual_euler_meridian_half_step.md) has a polynomial condition bound and a nonzero exact sourced endpoint. Both results retain their degree-N carries and stated metrics. ## 5. The source-conjugation torsor has a concrete norm equation For any actual invertible word coefficient c, or any unit of B, put h_k(c)=c theta_k(c)^-1. Twisted cyclicity gives the exact PERIOD equation Phi_k(c^-1 b c)=Phi_k(b h_k(c)). (9) This states precisely how the sector co-source must be transported under conjugation. Its ordered cyclic norm telescopes: product_(r=0)^(N-1) theta_k^r(h_k(c)) =c theta_k^N(c)^-1 =c G_k c^-1 G_k^-1. (10) Sectors with gcd(k,N)<=2 therefore have a genuine nonabelian norm-one source equation; the other sectors retain an explicit unipotent commutator defect. On an independently identified commutative simple eigenline this would become an ordinary Hilbert-90-type comparison. Neither that eigenline nor its geometric support is assumed here. The nonprimitive defect and the marked Fourier sum cannot simply be deleted. The individual values Phi_k(b) are not knot invariants. There is an exact actual-matrix witness with the SAME braid index and writhe: at N=3 over F_1009, the figure-eight word beta=(1,-2,1,-2) has sector values [224,545,410], average 393, whereas sigma_1 beta sigma_1^-1=(1,1,-2,1,-2,-1) has [619,845,724], average 393. All external normalization factors are identical in this comparison. Thus an adapter depending only on level, color, braid index and writhe cannot turn these fixed sectors into ordinary-color knot evaluations. Equation (9), with its actual transported co-source, is required. The sum in (5) does give the original invariant. There is also a local E-commutation obstruction: at N=2, J=1 and theta_k sends the nonconstant part f e_0 of the actual crossing to Q^-k f e_1. After undoing the Euler/fusion frame its right operator no longer commutes with the actual total E. The audit checks a nonzero literal commutator. Consequently theta_k is an automorphism of the full Borel-relative algebra, not generally of the smaller actual E,F,K centralizer. Its sectors must not be identified with that centralizer's existing symmetric cut trace. ## 6. What this advances and what remains This gives an explicit source-preserving Fourier family with a fully solved finite-level cyclic transport equation, including its nonabelian norm defect. It also identifies the exact linear source line and shows why ordinary corner compression erases it. These are algebraic statements about the actual selected source and the completed original word at arbitrary braid index. They do not supply a nonzero selected geometric A-sector, a bound for the sector sum, or a sharp volume norm. In particular finite cyclic transport, even in primitive sectors, does not bound the value of a word; the norm-one condition alone permits large comparison matrices. The zero sector's nilpotence index grows with N and its contribution has not been proved negligible. The source family is therefore an exact input for the required singular/nonlocal geometric comparison, not that comparison itself. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_source_fourier_twisted_traces.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_source_fourier_twisted_traces_results.json) check seven levels N=2,...,8, all basis relative-line compressions, twisted cyclicity, sector inverses, exact norm equations, the sharp zero-sector nilpotence index, and the common-frame ORIGINAL source on six signed words of braid indices two, three and four. The noninvariance and E-commutation witnesses use literal original crossing matrices and pivots, not replacement traces.

title: A source-preserving odd framing period

text: # A source-preserving odd framing period 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. A specified difference of the two nearest physical bands, with its exact quantum coefficient, has the SAME normalized value as the original complete invariant. Its normalization is nonzero at every level and costs only O(N) on an interior real coherent cut. In the actual routed physical chart the underlying odd form has an explicit nonzero logarithmic residue; the actual coherent base weight remains part of the source. This closes the old distinction between the unchanged scalar and an inserted odd observable. It does not determine the original relative cycle's winding, justify a quantum boundary-scale limit from separate local packets, or supply the missing mixed-color global estimate. ## 1. The literal source and its normalization Fix N>=2, d=N-1, q0=exp(pi i/N). Use the original regular generic channel, with epsilon the genuine quantum parameter, C_e(X)=P_V[A U^-1(X tensor I)U B], C_e(I)=z(e)I. (1) Here A:W->V and B:V->W may have different actual Morse widths, U is the recorded braid carrying the chosen W head to FIRST position, and P_V closes the other physical heads with g_e=(-1)^d K_e. All original cups, caps, complete-circle scalars and peripheral lines are retained. These are exactly the hypotheses of the [braided source theorem](actual_braided_two_cut_source_adapter.md). The statement applies at arbitrary fixed width and to the specified regular complete-source sector sum. It does not make a bare root mark a generic intertwiner. Let T_n=sum_(r-s=n)E_rs be the UNWRAPPED physical band, and set beta_a(t)=binom(d,a)t^a(1-t)^(d-a), e_t=beta(t)1^T, O_N=T_1-q0 T_-1, kappa_N(t)=1-q0-t^d+q0(1-t)^d. (2) The [actual divided-descendant theorem](actual_explicit_root_channel_normal_adapter.md) proves C_0(T_n)=z_0 T_n, including both n=+1 and n=-1. Moreover Tr(e_t T_1)=1-beta_d and Tr(e_t T_-1)=1-beta_0. Consequently the exact original scalar is Tr[e_t C_0(O_N)]/kappa_N(t)=z_0, (3) wherever kappa_N!=0. No second pivotal closure or new state is inserted in (3). The numerator is the original coherent FIRST-cut row applied to two actual neighboring bands of (1). For real 0<=t<=1 it is nonzero at EVERY N. Indeed put A0=1-t^d, B0=1-(1-t)^d and theta=pi/N. Then A0,B0>=0, A0+B0>=1, and exactly |kappa_N|^2=(A0-B0)^2 cos^2(theta/2) +(A0+B0)^2 sin^2(theta/2) >=sin^2(theta/2)>=N^-2. (4) There is no odd/even exception. On any fixed t in [delta,1-delta], kappa_N=(1-q0)[1+O_delta(N(1-delta)^(N-1))], kappa_N=-pi i/N+O_delta(N^-2). (5) Thus its inverse has size O(N), without an exponential cost. For complex coherent t, keep the explicit kappa_N and its actual zeros; (4) is not a claim on arbitrary complex t. The exact finite period in (3) is kappa_N^-1 [sum_(0<=a,l<d) beta_a C_0(E_(l+1,l))_(a+1,a) -q0 sum_(1<=a,l<=d) beta_a C_0(E_(l-1,l))_(a-1,a)]. (6) These are TWO different physical support sets, with the original internal head sums and their own finite endpoint rows. Neither is wrapped cyclically or identified with the other's support cycle. Their common primitive charged chart and meromorphic local currents are supplied by the [common-band theorem](actual_matching_graph_common_band_ward_current.md). If the cut is already the first physical slot, U=I is permitted. For a different selected edge, its actual U and U^-1 remain in (6). ## 2. Genuine quantum normals and the indispensable q coefficient The ordinary closed source is F_e=D_N(e)z(e), with D_N=(-1)^d[N]_(q0 exp(epsilon)), D_N(0)=0 and D_N'(0)=nu_N. For example retain the literal regular lift O_e=T_1-q0 exp(epsilon)T_-1 and kappa_e=Tr(e_t O_e). Equation (3) implies exactly Z_e=Tr[e_t C_e(O_e)]/kappa_e, D_N(e)[Z_e-z(e)]=O(epsilon^2), [epsilon]D_N Z_e/nu_N=z_0. (7) Every original exterior scalar is the same on both sides. This is a whole-source FIRST-trace-normal identity. It does not assert Z_e=z(e), equality of higher quantum normals, or permission to differentiate (3) as a generic identity. The audit retains nonzero individual normal defects of that false replacement. There is also a specified eigenkernel lift. With h_s(q) the ACTUAL normalized generic descendants in the adapter theorem, put O_e^h=(T_1-q T_-1)diag(h_s(q)), q=q0 exp(epsilon). Both its bands lie in the same generic descendant family, so C_e(O_e^h)=lambda(e)O_e^h exactly and lambda(0)=z_0. Using its own actual coherent normalization in (7) therefore gives the same first trace normal. This option changes the generic boundary germ; no ordinary coupon or bare mark is silently substituted. The finite q0 in (2) is essential, not a disposable phase. Exactly O_N=(1+q0)/2 (T_1-T_-1) +(1-q0)/2 (T_1+T_-1). (8) Without it, the coherent normalization would be (1-t)^d-t^d, which is exponentially small in the interior and zero at t=1/2. The actual O(1/N) normalization comes from the retained quantum coefficient. Endpoint terms in (2) also remain exact. ## 3. The actual routed momentum and its logarithmic form This section concerns the proved regular geometric chart of the certified complete source. Its local nonzero amplitude and framing form are those of the [source Ward density theorem](actual_augmented_plat_framing_density_source_ward.md). No geometric assertion for an arbitrary algebraic channel is inferred. Write A'=A U^-1 and B'=U B. The inserted head is literally the FIRST physical slot at this new level, so its lower-prefix adapter is the identity. Its meridian is the ACTUAL Hurwitz-transformed meridian, not the old unbraided selected-wire matrix. Inserting E_(l+1,l) changes the first exposed output by +1 and the A'-side input by +1. The original boundary generating form gives +Log p_cut-Log p_e. The coherent row used here has p_cut=1. Thus the two actual local principal ratios are T_1 : p_e^-1, T_-1 : p_e. (9) This is the same bounded-band source calculation as [the physical port theorem, Section 6](actual_two_cut_framing_port_reconstruction.md), now with the route and its physical prefix explicitly fixed. For completeness a suitable noncommuting first-slot route exists in the certified complete-circle source. Choose a slice entering an actual circle box. Its two main meridians A,B have Tr A=Tr B=Tr BA=-2. They cannot both fix reference infinity: two upper triangular trace-minus-two parabolics have product trace +2. The positive route R_1...R_j makes its new first meridian V_j^-1 mu_j V_j, V_j=mu_(j-1)...mu_1, by the actual Hurwitz rule. If every routed candidate fixed infinity, induction would make every original mu_j upper triangular, a contradiction. Thus some recorded route has nonzero lower-left entry. This uses the original reference, main component and complete-circle geometry, not a free reframing. In the same trace-two parabolic normalization as the port theorem, write that routed meridian and the cut frame as mu_e=I+c[[b,-b^2],[1,-b]], c!=0, F(r,s)=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], s!=0, R=r-sb, A_cut=(1+s)^-1. Directly conjugating by F gives p_e=(R-1)/R, k-1=(c/s)R(1-R). (10) On its regular chart R!=0,1 and k-1!=0, the underlying ORIGINAL marked scalar density is Omega_src=(c_D/s) dr wedge dLog A_cut, c_D!=0. (11) The factor c_D is independent of the framing point; the ORIGINAL marked source and transverse Gaussian normalization is in it. The full channel Gaussian, when included under its proved hypotheses, changes it by its retained nonzero factor, not an assigned unit. That original marked row has entries 1/N, whereas (6) uses beta_a(t). Thus the literal new source retains the base weight B_(N,t)(a)=N beta_a(t)/kappa_N(t). (11a) It multiplies the corresponding two band densities. It is not globally absorbed into the framing-constant c_D: beta_a has its own coherent action as the first cut varies. At a legitimate first-cut localization one instead retains its ACTUAL nonzero local Gaussian factor. The following rational-form calculations concern (11) times the odd symbol; the full coherent source additionally keeps (11a), or that localized factor, and its original first-cut cycle. The q-retained combination of the two classical ratios is exactly p_e^-1-q0 p_e=(1-q0)+1/(R-1)+q0/R. (12) At fixed s its product with the residual one-form c_D dr/s has primitive (c_D/s)[(1-q0)r+Log(R-1)+q0 Log R]. (13) Its residues at R=1, R=0 and r=infinity are respectively c_D/s, q0 c_D/s and -(1+q0)c_D/s. On a FIXED first-cut fiber the coherent base weight is independent of r, so it multiplies all three residues unchanged; after a proved first-cut Gaussian the retained factor does the same. These are local meromorphic-form residues. They do not assert that the original period surrounds any of those divisors with a nonzero relative coefficient. There is an exact noncancellation check for a SPECIFIED sample of this underlying residue. Use the canonical half-index clocks A_a=q0 Q0^a, s_a=A_a^-1-1, Q0=q0^2, 0<=a<=d, G_N(t)=sum_a beta_a(t)/s_a. (13a) None of the s_a is zero. Since |A_a|=1 and A_a!=1, Re[A_a/(1-A_a)]=-1/2. Thus for every real 0<=t<=1, Re G_N(t)=-1/2, |G_N(t)|>=1/2. At t=1/2 the exact pairing a with d-a has A_(d-a)=A_a^-1 and equal beta weights, so G_N(1/2)=-1/2 exactly at both parities. Retaining the base co-source and its original 1/N averaging explicitly, the sampled fiber residue is (1/N)sum_a [N beta_a(t)/kappa_N(t)] *[-(1+q0)c_D/s_a] =-(1+q0)c_D G_N(t)/kappa_N(t)!=0. (13b) This is a finite algebraic sample of the UNDERLYING meromorphic form. It is not an identification with the actual quantum period's residue, its first-cut pushforward, or a uniform packet outside a fixed chart. At fixed framing point q0 tends to one. Put s2=k-1. Equations (10)--(11) give the leading odd form exactly as (p_e^-1-p_e)Omega_src =c_D ds wedge ds2/[(1+s)s s2]. (14) The UNDERLYING form (14) has double logarithmic residue c_D!=0 at s=s2=0, in the displayed order. This is not automatically the full coherent-weighted residue there: (11a) varies with the base clock, and an interior coherent localization is a different operation. Equivalently the physical two-position deck exchanges p_e and p_e^-1; its odd density times this odd observable is the nonzero deck-EVEN form (14). This is a statement about the specified leading form. A formal two-sheet trace cancels an odd-density part only when the actual two-sheet pushforward with its orientations is being taken; it is not automatically the original global cycle. ## 4. What this replacement does and does not settle Equation (3) closes the source-preservation gap left in Section 7 of the older port theorem: the q-weighted odd observable is now an EXACT normalized source for the unchanged scalar. It does not replace the relative cycle by a field trace or determine its winding. The original two support cycles, their marked orientations and every endpoint term in (6) are still required in that comparison. There is a separate uniformity issue at the resonant boundary. For r=N rho, with rho bounded away from zero and s,b bounded, the RATIONAL expression (12) has p_e^-1-q0 p_e=(2/rho-pi i)/N+O(N^-2), (p_e^-1-q0 p_e)/kappa_N -> 1+2i/(pi rho) (15) for an interior real coherent t. Here both parts of (8) have the SAME order. Separate O(1/N) errors in the two actual quantum band packets can alter the normalized limit (15). Consequently (15) is classical-symbol data, not a proved uniform quantum boundary-period kernel. A source-level joint expansion with sufficient cancellation control remains necessary there. Finally this complete-source identity supplies neither a nonzero mixed-color packet nor a global contributing-cycle theorem for long fillings. Its exact finite algebra is uniform in fixed width; its geometric residue has the stated certified complete-source scope. ## Validation The [focused original-source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_source_preserving_odd_framing_period.py) and its [results](../experiments/actual_source_preserving_odd_framing_period_results.json) check 22 actual original/routed sources, including rectangular cuts: 200 root odd entries, 188 literal band terms, 22 whole first normals and 400 generic eigenkernel jet entries. Independent symbolic calculations check all four physical Gauss entries, the q decomposition and primitive, three one-form residues, the oriented doublelog form and residue, and the two CLASSICAL boundary limits. At 80 digits, 315 all-level/both-parity normalization checks reproduce (4), with maximum identity error 2.11e-81. The expanded audit also checks the exact inverse-clock residue identity, 315 specified coherent residue samples and 63 symmetric t=1/2 samples; the largest real-part error is 2.02e-77. These samples retain the stated underlying-form scope. Independent full analytical review and fresh original-source replay: PASS.
