title: The actual source cannot descend by a raw finite critical-algebra quotient
text: # The actual source cannot descend by a raw finite critical-algebra quotient 28 October 2026. There is a precise algebraic obstruction to using the new exact sewing as an exact multiplicative quotient onto a fixed geometric critical algebra while retaining every coupon. The original cut pairing is faithful. Moreover an insertion which vanishes on the geometric critical scheme can still have the FULL volume exponent in an actual hyperbolic-knot period. The latter is proved below for the original figure-eight source: its geometric polynomial p(Z)=Z^2-Z+1 has N * mu_N(p(Z)p(Z^-1))/K_N -> 2pi sqrt(3). (1) Thus the critical relation costs a power of N, not a smaller exponential action. This changes the needed construction: a geometric critical algebra must arise through a specified formal or derived reduction with Gaussian counterterms and source degree, rather than by an exact raw source-preserving algebra quotient or by discarding all insertions of smaller exponential order. ## 1. A perfect cut excludes every proper exact algebra quotient Let C be a finite algebra over a field and let tau:C->k have nondegenerate pairing (x,y)->tau(xy). If an algebra quotient pi:C->A carries the same co-source, tau=lambda pi, then pi is injective. Indeed for x in ker pi and every y in C, tau(xy)=lambda(pi(x)pi(y))=0, and nondegeneracy gives x=0. The same proof works over a ring when the displayed pairing is perfect. The [actual projective cut theorem](integral_projective_cut_duality.md) applies this hypothesis to C_(b,R)=End_(E,F,K)(V_M^(tensor b)), R=k[[M-1]], tau=d_N(M) times the ORIGINAL pivotal first cut. Its pairing is perfect over R and on the complete fibre, with rank N^(2b-3) for b>=2. Thus there is no proper exact quotient of this full coupon algebra through which that whole source factors. Exact sewing and basis changes do not alter the conclusion, since they retain the original cut. The statement also survives the normal direction. Modulo u^(J+1), u=M-1, the R-linear trace pairing remains perfect. Even the scalar top-normal co-source lambda_J(c)=[u^J]tau(c) has nondegenerate k-pairing lambda_J(cd): choose the lowest nonzero u coefficient of c, pair it nontrivially by tau's special-fibre perfect form, and multiply the other input by the complementary power of u. Hence an exact algebra quotient preserving this co-source and all normal coupon products is again injective. Retaining divided sources does not justify semisimplifying their algebra. This excludes a SPECIFIC strong construction. It does not exclude a derived pushforward, a source-compatible corner or restricted insertion algebra, or an action-normalized associated graded. Such constructions must state which operations and currents they retain. Boundary Ward homotopies need not be algebra quotients. ## 2. An actual complete-colour nilpotent source survives There is a small exact model inside the original crossing. At N=2 take q=i, Q=-1, x=i in the original balanced frame: K=diag(i,-i), F=[[0,0],[2,0]], E=[[0,1/2],[0,0]]. Use the original coproduct and normalized Casimir Omega. On two heads it is exactly Omega=[[0,0,0,0], [0,4i,-4,0], [0,-4,-4i,0], [0,0,0,0]], Omega^2=0, Omega!=0. The full two-head centralizer is k[Omega], of dimension two. With the ORIGINAL averaged first-cut Phi and closed pivot (-i,i), direct contraction gives Phi(1)=0, Phi(Omega)=-4, Gram_(1,Omega)(Phi(xy))=[[0,-4],[-4,0]]. (2) Multiplying by the original modified dimension d_2(1)=i/2 retains perfection and makes the offdiagonal entries -2i. The reduced classical Casimir point Omega=0 forgets exactly the nonzero source in (2). For the normalized actual crossing R_0=1+(i/4)Omega one has Phi(R_0)=-i. Its nilpotent term is essential, even though all characters of k[Omega] send it to zero. This persists in a full original hyperbolic-knot check. On three heads form the original figure-eight word W=R_(1)^+ R_(2)^- R_(1)^+ R_(2)^- in its operator-action order. Its writhe is zero, so the crossings' common Cartan factors cancel. With both ORIGINAL closed pivots and the ORIGINAL first-cut average, exactly Phi_3(W)=5, Phi_3(1)=0. (3) Replacing each local crossing by its value at Omega_i=0 would give zero instead of five. This replacement is not a proved algebra map of the global word; (3) shows precisely why that local-character substitution cannot represent the original source. No arbitrary source or renormalized model was introduced. There is a second exact local-to-global warning. At every N, Tr(g)=0 for the complete-colour pivot. Therefore, for an actual local coupon X, Phi_(b+1)(X tensor I)=Phi_b(X) Tr(g)=0. (4) A nonzero local sourced class can be killed by the original global pivotal closure. Nonzero local sine jumps, nonzero Fourier coefficients or nonzero local radial symbols do not by themselves imply a nonzero global geometric image. ## 3. The exact original figure-eight insertion algebra has rank N Use its proved [whole-source identity](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md): K_N=sum_(n=0)^(N-1)w_(N,n), w_(N,n)=|(Q_N;Q_N)_n|^2>0. On this EXACT reduced whole-source expression retain the literal insertion Z=Q_N^n. Define mu_N(f)=sum_n w_(N,n) f(Q_N^n), A_N=C[Z,Z^-1]/(Z^N-1). (5) No change of the unweighted period is made: mu_N(1)=K_N. Every weight in (5) is nonzero. Root evaluation identifies A_N with C^N and its pairing mu_N(fg) with a diagonal pairing whose entries are those weights. It is nondegenerate. Consequently Section 1 applies: no proper multiplicative quotient of A_N retains all these literal inserted moments. In particular no quotient of uniformly bounded rank can do so. This remains true if the proposed relation has N-dependent coefficients. If mu_N(p q)=0 for every Laurent polynomial q, then p(Q_N^n)=0 for every n. Its representative in A_N is zero, or equivalently p is divisible by Z^N-1. For degrees less than N a nonzero relation is impossible. This is an exact whole hyperbolic-knot source calculation, stronger than checking an unrelated identity insertion or changing a normalized source functional. It does not assert that (5) is already the geometric critical observable of a different polarization. ## 4. The geometric relation retains the full exponent Let p(Z)=Z^2-Z+1. Its two roots are the complete regular ideal shapes. The actual positive source has its unique bulk maximum at x_*=5/6, Z_*=exp(5pi*i/3), also a root of p. Nevertheless mu_N(p(Z)p(Z^-1))>0 (6) at every N, and its exponential rate is the SAME as K_N. Since p has real coefficients and |Z|=1, the insertion in (6) is |p(Z)|^2=(2cos(2pi*n/N)-1)^2. Here is a quantitative proof. Put Phi(x)=integral_0^x Log(4sin^2(pi*t))dt, lambda=-Phi''(5/6)=2pi sqrt(3). The endpoint-aware factorial estimate gives the uniform central expansion w_(N,n)=2N sin(pi*x) exp(N Phi(x))(1+O(1/N)), x=n/N, on every compact subinterval of (0,1). Away from x_* the already proved strict maximum gives an exponential gap. Under xi=sqrt(N)(x-x_*), the normalized sums therefore converge, including their second moments, to the real Gaussian of variance 1/lambda. This follows directly by Taylor expansion, a Gaussian bound on a fixed central neighborhood, and the outside exponential estimate. For g(x)=|p(exp(2pi*i*x))|^2, g(x_*)=g'(x_*)=0, g''(x_*)/2=12pi^2. Thus discrete Laplace evaluation gives the exact limit N mu_N(g)/K_N ->12pi^2/lambda=2pi sqrt(3). (7) In particular lim N^-1 Log mu_N(g)=Vol(4_1)/(2pi), although g belongs to the ideal of the geometric critical polynomial. A vanishing of finite order at the saddle loses only powers of N. The same argument gives the full exponent for every fixed nonzero polynomial insertion |f(Z)|^2, even when it vanishes at Z_*. Therefore an associated graded which discards ONLY smaller exponential rates cannot impose p(Z)=0 while retaining this source. The ordinary semiclassical H-adic leading symbol does impose that relation, but its next Gaussian contractions and normal/divided co-source remain necessary: (7) records one of the terms it would otherwise erase. Here H=Log Q is the quantum semiclassical direction; it is not the distinct meridian normal U-1. A source comparison must retain both rather than identify their filtrations. ## 5. A constructive exact current module in the SAME original source The correct relation can be exhibited without guessing a critical quotient or dividing by the unknown scalar. Put A(Z)=2-Z-Z^-1=(1-Z)(1-Z^-1), S_Q f(Z)=f(QZ), B_Q=A(QZ) S_Q. The actual weights in (5) satisfy w_(n+1)=A(Q^(n+1))w_n, w_0=1, w_N=0. Consequently telescoping the ORIGINAL finite sum gives, for every Laurent polynomial insertion f, EXACTLY mu_N((I-B_Q)f)=f(1). (8) The endpoint value on the right is compulsory. For example the left side for f=1 is one, rather than zero. This is an affine q-difference/Green identity with the original endpoint source, not an ideal relation for the multiplication algebra. There is also a unique completely algebraic realization. On the finite clock A_N one has S_Q^N=I and B_Q^N=product_(l=1)^N A(Q^l Z) =(1-Z^N)(1-Z^-N)=0. It follows that mu_N=ev_(Z=1)(I-B_Q)^-1 =ev_(Z=1)sum_(k=0)^(N-1)B_Q^k. (9) Evaluation of the k-th term is exactly w_k f(Q^k), proving that (9) uses the original period, not an adapter normalized by K_N. Equation (8) uniquely determines this functional. At the classical limit Q=1 its operator has multiplication symbol 1-A(Z)=Z+Z^-1-1=p(Z)/Z. (10) Thus the finite geometric algebra really does appear, but as the principal symbol of a sourced DIFFERENCE OPERATOR. Away from the root set Q=exp(H). Its next formal term contains the Euler derivative, so integration by parts produces higher Gaussian contractions. It is precisely those terms that make (7) compatible with the classical critical relation (10). Equations (8)--(10) supply an actual nonzero affine source object with fixed operator data and exact endpoint pointing. They do not prove a general geometric trace descent. They show concretely which category permits the desired reduction: relative twisted difference/de Rham cohomology, with its boundary current, rather than the raw multiplicative algebra. ## 6. The resulting next construction target The irreducible trace nonvanishing theorem requires an ACTUAL descended critical algebra and source. The exact sewing and its regularized periods do not yield it by taking a raw multiplicative quotient: Sections 1--3 forbid that operation on the full faithful source objects. Taking the final matrix Ward cohomology first instead leaves only its scalar pointed line, rather than a new nontrivial geometric field action. The appropriate test is therefore on the partly integrated weighted/current module, BEFORE final scalar Ward closure: construct its action-normalized formal or derived critical observable, with the required Gaussian counterterms, and map the original relative sewing and meridian-normal co-source through that reduction. A literal flow observable need not satisfy its critical polynomial there; (7) shows the required counterterms are already visible at order 1/N. The existing [formal insertion construction](actual_pointed_commutant_and_critical_observable.md) provides such a renormalized critical observable on the transverse FORMAL block. The still-missing step is its source-compatible whole/derived realization from the exact sewn period. This is a sharper requirement than finding another local nonzero unit. The lemma and original-source calculations above do not prove that realization, but rule out two tempting constructions and specify which source information it must retain. [Exact source and scaling audit](../experiments/audit_actual_source_quotient_critical_relation.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_source_quotient_critical_relation_results.json).

title: The actual multi-leg source has no nonzero two-sided null ideal
text: # The actual multi-leg source has no nonzero two-sided null ideal Research proof, 27 October 2026. For three or more strands, the original pivotal highest-input source on the FULL Borel-relative word algebra does not factor through any proper algebra quotient. Every path coefficient can be detected after actual relative matrix coupons. For two strands its maximal null ideal is instead explicit, and the minimal algebra quotient is the triangular path algebra of a line. This is a boundary on algebraic reductions of the entire relative algebra, not an obstruction to a linear relative-period transform, a current-complex quotient, a singular geometric comparison, or a quotient of a smaller actual-word/observable algebra. In particular it does not disprove the volume conjecture. It specifies what a source-preserving attempt to discard the nilpotent shell would need to avoid. ## 1. The actual algebra and the relevant notion of source quotient Fix an original root Q of order N>=2. Let A_0=<H,f | H^N=1, Hf=Q^-1 fH, f^N=0>, z_(a,j)=f^a e_j, 0<=a,j<N. The exact multiplication is the one in [the actual Borel fusion theorem](actual_borel_regular_fusion_and_divided_cap_period.md). Think of z_(a,j) as an oriented path of length a starting at j and ending at j+a modulo N. A product whose total length is at least N is zero. On b strands that theorem identifies the actual tensor module with a free LEFT A_0 module of rank r=N^(b-2). Consequently the full Borel-relative endomorphism algebra is B_b=Mat_r(A_0^op). The original source is the actual pivotal partial trace on all but the first strand, followed by first input e_0 and output ell=ones^t. In coefficient form write Psi(T)=sum_(t,s) Lambda_(t,s)(a_(t,s)). (1) Here T_(t,s)=R_(a_(t,s)) acts by right multiplication in the regular algebra. All original external factors may be included or retained externally. At a regular complete fiber they are nonzero, so they do not change any null ideal below. Define the maximal two-sided source-null ideal by I_Psi={T : Psi(U T V)=0 for every U,V in B_b}. (2) It is the largest two-sided ideal contained in ker(Psi). If an algebra homomorphism pi:B_b->C preserves the source, meaning Psi=lambda composed with pi, then ker(pi) is contained in (2). This formulation does not assume that an arbitrary geometric relative-period map is an algebra homomorphism. ## 2. Literal physical top rows detect all residue classes Use the ORIGINAL full fusion basis, not the later tail-head decomposition. Its tail labels are s=(s_3,...,s_b), 0<=s_i<N. The seed associated with f^a e_k in copy s is f_total^a(e_0 tensor e_(k-sum(s) mod N) tensor e_s). Let X=product_i x_i be the product of the actual highest K roots. The source of the diagonal relative top path is exactly Lambda_(s,s)(f^(N-1)e_k) =gamma_s delta_(k,sum(s) mod N), gamma_s=N X^(1-N) Q^(1-sum(s)), gamma_s!=0. (3) This is a direct physical cap calculation. Returning every tail output to its input s forces zero lowering steps on those legs. For the remaining N-1 steps to return the second output to the required pivotal index, all of them must go to the second leg, whose initial index must be zero. Thus k=sum(s) modulo N; any other k would require N first-leg lowering steps, impossible in total degree N-1. The coefficient of the second-leg steps is F_(N-1)=N, and their K_1 inverses supply x_1^(1-N). The second pivotal entry contributes x_2^(1-N)Q, while the tail pivots contribute product_(i>=3) x_i^(1-N)Q^-sum(s). This is (3). The all-ones first output row remains the actual one; only its zero-index entry occurs in this particular top-row calculation. No normalized trace or geometric co-source is substituted. ## 3. For b>=3, no relative algebra ideal can be discarded **Theorem.** For b>=3, I_Psi=0. Take a nonzero element T of a two-sided ideal I in B_b. Some coefficient a_(t,s) has a nonzero coefficient c of f^a e_j. Relative matrix units first move that entry to any chosen diagonal copy; left/right coefficient idempotents isolate it, because e_(j+a) a_(t,s) e_j=c f^a e_j. (4) Only one degree between zero and N-1 has that start and endpoint. Multiplication by f^(N-1-a) then gives f^(N-1-a) [c f^a e_j]=c f^(N-1)e_j. (5) All these operations are allowed relative matrix coupons, so the result stays in I. For b>=3 choose a diagonal tail copy u with sum(u)=j modulo N, for instance u_3=j and all later u_i=0. Equation (3) evaluates the resulting element to c gamma_u!=0. Thus no nonzero ideal is contained in ker(Psi), proving the theorem. The coefficient algebra is opposite to physical operator composition; this only exchanges which of the two matrix-coupon sides realizes the left or right coefficient factor in (4)-(5). Both sides are available in (2), so no commutativity assumption enters the proof. In particular ANY source-preserving algebra quotient of B_b is injective. This includes nilpotent ideals: the entire radical cannot be removed, nor can a nonzero subideal of it. The result is stronger than an example of one nonzero radical contribution. It does not say Psi(UT) alone is a nondegenerate bilinear pairing; the proof uses both coupon sides. Nor does it say that every relative coupon is an actual braid word or commutes with the full quantum-group E action. The algebra in the theorem is the full actual Borel commutant furnished by fusion. A reduction on a strictly smaller operator algebra needs its own analysis. ## 4. The two-leg contrast: the exact quotient is triangular For b=2, the actual cap is Lambda(f^a e_k)=x_2^(1-N) x_1^-a Q^-(k+a) F_(k+a)/F_k, if k+a<N, 0, if k+a>=N. (6) Define the wrapped-path span I_cut=span{f^a e_k : k+a>=N}. (7) It is a two-sided ideal: further path concatenation cannot undo crossing the cut from N-1 to zero, and paths of total length at least N vanish. The source (6) kills it. Conversely every nonwrapped path has a nonzero source value, and the two endpoint idempotents isolate its coefficient as in (4). Thus no larger two-sided ideal lies in the source kernel, so I_Lambda=I_cut, dim I_cut=N(N-1)/2. (8) The quotient is the lower triangular N-by-N matrix algebra under f^a e_k -> E_(k+a,k) if k+a<N, and zero otherwise. This respects the path multiplication and gives all triangular matrix units. Its dimension is N(N+1)/2. In these coordinates the ORIGINAL cap is the matrix coefficient Lambda(T)=x_2^(1-N) r^t T c, r_i=x_1^-i Q^-i F_i, c_k=x_1^k/F_k. (9) Every r_i and c_k is nonzero. The effective triangular nilpotence length still grows with N. Its existence does not provide a bounded-rank critical algebra or a subexponential coefficient bound. The b>=3 theorem explains why one cannot apply this two-leg quotient independently to intermediate diagonal blocks of a multi-strand word. Off-diagonal tail transitions expose all cyclic residue classes before the final selected contraction. Only the completed word may be passed to the diagonal-source formula of [the all-strand Euler/Cauchy theorem](all_strand_euler_cauchy_cap.md). ## 5. Consequence for the geometric comparison The exact endpoint functional is a tractable finite linear source, but its full algebra source does not descend to a smaller algebra by deleting a null ideal once b>=3. A fixed geometric critical algebra cannot be obtained as such a quotient of B_b while retaining all sourced relative matrix coupons. Morita equivalence may remove the matrix factor, but A_0 still has N simple modules and Loewy length N, so it is not Morita equivalent to one fixed finite etale critical algebra as N grows. This specifies the kind of comparison still available: a linear relative-period or current-complex map, a separately constructed singular/nonlocal transform, or a restriction to an actual smaller meridian/word algebra with a proved invariant source quotient. Zero-source linear current spaces need not be ideals, so they are not excluded by the theorem. The result does not establish a nonzero selected geometric class or a volume norm. ## 6. Exact checks [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_source_two_sided_quotient.py) and its [saved results](../experiments/actual_source_two_sided_quotient_results.json) check (3) against the literal original physical source after the actual coproduct fusion for braid indices three and four. They also check all relative matrix-basis coefficient recovery certificates in (4)-(5), and the two-leg wrapped ideal at levels two through eight. The proof above is all-level and does not depend on a finite rank fit or on an assertion about untested knots. The saved run reports PASS on seven physical-source cases, 125 literal top rows, 3067 relative matrix-basis recovery certificates, and seven two-leg levels. A separate agent independently inspected the all-level source calculation, path isolation and quotient argument, finding no issue. The distinction between the full Borel commutant and the smaller actual full-quantum-group word algebra is essential to the conclusion's scope.

title: A positive supported Racah factorial, its metric and retained partner current
text: # A positive supported Racah factorial, its metric and retained partner current 29 October 2026. This is an independent finite FACTORIAL theorem. It does not assume that a proposed four-port source coefficient is a Racah sum. On the full folded supported chamber it proves a common phase, a positive root normalization, a uniform positive Laplace principle, and polynomial relative bounds for every fixed generic-q normal jet. Complementary high partners have the same positive value core but an additional explicitly retained normal current. Connecting these formulas to the actual source requires its separate typed coefficient identity. A positive root value is not by itself a bound on a complete Hermite recoupling operator. ## 1. Seven factorials, with a root unit at every denominator Fix N>=3, D=N-1, M=floor(D/2), q=exp(pi i/N), and six INTEGER folded spins 0<=a,b,c,d,e,f<=M. Define four faces and three quads F=(a+b+e, c+d+e, a+d+f, b+c+f), Q=(a+b+c+d, a+c+e+f, b+d+e+f). (1) Assume every F_i>=D. Every face is an ordinary triangle: its two smaller entries sum to at least D minus its largest, which is at least its largest because D>=2M. Moreover EVERY face deficit F_i-2ell lies in [0,D]. Every difference Q_k-F_i is one such deficit of a complementary face. Therefore z_-=max F_i <= z_+=min Q_k, D<=z_-<=z_+<=4M<=2D, 0<=z-F_i<=D, 0<=Q_k-z<=D. (2) Use the GENUINE generic symmetric factorial [n]!_zeta, with [u]_zeta=(zeta^u-zeta^-u)/(zeta-zeta^-1). Set S(zeta)=sum_(z=z_-)^(z_+) (-1)^z [z+1]! /[product_i [z-F_i]! product_k[Q_k-z]!]. (3) No negative factorial is assigned a value: the displayed interval is the true finite range. By (2), every denominator is a unit at q. The numerator contains EXACTLY ONE factor [N]. Factoring it BEFORE specialization defines the analytic function G(zeta)=(-1)^D S(zeta)/[N]_zeta. (4) Let s_r=product_(u=1)^r 2sin(pi u/N), s_0=1. The exact positive root value is R_N:=G(q)=N sum_z s_(z-D) /[product_i s_(z-F_i) product_k s_(Q_k-z)]>0. (5) Indeed the signs of [N+1],...,[z+1] multiply to (-1)^(z+1-N). Together with (-1)^(D+z) this is +1. Also s_D=N. The powers of 2sin(pi/N) cancel, since sum_i(z-F_i)+sum_k(Q_k-z)=z, sum_i F_i=sum_k Q_k=2(a+b+c+d+e+f). Thus (5) is a finite exact identity, including boundary faces F_i=D, collapsed z intervals, both level parities and composite levels. ## 2. The exact positive face metric For a face (x,y,z) of sum F, define the generic squared triangle factor and its regular normalization by Delta_F^2=[F-2x]![F-2y]![F-2z]!/[F+1]!, D_F(zeta)=(-1)^(F-D)[N]_zeta Delta_F^2. It is analytic and nonzero at q, with positive root value d_F=D_F(q) =s_(F-2x)s_(F-2y)s_(F-2z)/(N s_(F-D))>0. (6) The natural positive normalized scalar is W_N=R_N sqrt(product_faces d_F). (7) This metric is not optional in a geometric interpretation. The branch-independent generic squared identity is EXACTLY [N]^2 S(zeta)^2 product_faces Delta_F^2 =G(zeta)^2 product_faces D_F(zeta). (8) The root of its right side is W_N^2>0. There is no residual sign, because sum_faces(F-D)=2(a+b+c+d+e+f)-4D is even. Equation(8) defines a finite factorial normalization; it is not a claim that an as-yet-unproved physical recoupling matrix is unitary in this metric. The ordered physical Clebsch norms, source gamma factors and any intermediate quantum dimensions must still be matched by an actual coefficient theorem. A quantum dimension can vanish at the odd simple endpoint. It is not canceled by evaluating (7) alone; its generic source limit must be retained before interpreting this as a physical Gram. ## 3. A uniform positive action on the ENTIRE folded chamber Put L(t)=integral_0^t log(2sin(pi u))du on [0,1], continuously at both endpoints. Write x=(a,b,c,d,e,f)/N, D_N=D/N, and use the same linear forms F_i(x),Q_k(x). On I_N=[max_i F_i(x),min_k Q_k(x)] define A_N(x,Z)=L(Z-D_N)-sum_i L(Z-F_i(x)) -sum_k L(Q_k(x)-Z), V_N(x,Z)=A_N(x,Z) +(1/2)sum_faces[sum_(ell in face)L(F(x)-2x_ell) -L(F(x)-D_N)]. (9) Uniformly over ALL allowed integral labels, log R_N=N max_(Z in I_N) A_N(x,Z)+O(log N), log W_N=N max_(Z in I_N) V_N(x,Z)+O(log N). (10) Proof. Every factorial index is in [0,D], so the uniform elementary sine-factorial estimate log s_r=N L(r/N)+O(log N) applies to every term, including endpoints. There are at most 2N positive terms. Their maximum gives the upper bound and one term gives the lower. The modulus of continuity of L is O(epsilon log(1/epsilon)); rounding Z to a feasible integral index changes N times the action by at most O(log N). All constants are independent of the labels. The same estimate applied to the four explicit factors (6) proves the second line. Thus no cancellation or selected complex saddle is required. For any convergent scaled-label sequence, (10) yields the corresponding max-action limit, with D_N replaced by 1. This is an action theorem; identification with an actual geometric tetrahedron is a separate task. Two calibrations expose the metric's role. At all six scaled labels 1/3, the bare action maximum is 3v3/pi, whereas the face metric adds -2v3/pi and the normalized maximum is v3/pi. At all six labels 1/2, the metric action is zero and the normalized maximum is v8/pi. Here v3=3Lambda(pi/3), v8=8Lambda(pi/4). The maxima occur respectively at Z=7/6 and Z=7/4, by direct differentiation of (9). The independently proved [local hyperideal geometry theorem](actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume.md) now identifies this normalized maximum with actual truncated-tetrahedron volume. Its exact Casimir angle coordinates are a_ell=(ell+1/2)/N. Using Z=(z+7/4)/N shifts the numerator factorial argument by 3/(4N), each denominator argument by 1/(4N), and every face-metric argument by 1/(2N). The same uniform endpoint modulus gives the SHARP scalar bound log W_N=(N/pi)Vol_ext(T(a_ell))+O(log N) (10a) on the entire supported chamber, with a universal error constant. Vol_ext denotes the continuous boundary-volume extension when an odd simple channel has zero dihedral angle. This is a local scalar energy calibration, not a proof that a source graph supplies the corresponding cell gluing or a completed Hermite metric. ## 4. Polynomial relative generic normal jets, not just root values Take zeta=q exp(t), with ALL integer labels fixed, and cancel the single displayed [N] in each term of (3). This is the actual generic factorial germ, not a formal root recurrence continued off the root. There is a universal c>0 such that on |t|<=r_N=c/[N^2(1+log N)] (11) the functions G and each D_F are holomorphic and nonzero, and their ratios to their positive root values differ from one by less than 1/4. The canonical analytic square roots of D_F, positive at t=0, therefore define H(t)=G(t) product_F sqrt(D_F(t)), with H(0)=W_N. Shrinking the SAME universal c if necessary gives |H/H(0)-1|<1/4. Here is a uniform proof. After cancellation, all factors zeta-zeta^-1 cancel too, by the factorial degree equality used in section1. Every remaining factor is zeta^u-zeta^-u, 1<=u<2N, u!=N. At t=0 its absolute value is at least 4 dist(u,N Z)/N. For |t|<=N^-2, its derivative has absolute value at most 30N. Thus each unit factor's logarithmic change is bounded by 15N^2|t|/dist(u,N Z) when that relative change is small. Across a summand there are at most eighteen copies of the harmonic sum sum_(k=1)^N 1/k; the four face factors have the same fixed bound. Consequently each product ratio has logarithmic change at most C N^2(1+log N)|t|, with universal C. Choosing, for example, a sufficiently small c<=10^-6 makes every summand stay in a small common sector around its POSITIVE value in (5). A positive weighted sum stays in that sector as well. This proves (11), including the nonzero lower bound and analytic square roots. Cauchy's inequality now gives, for every fixed k>=0 and F=G or H, |F^(k)(0)|/k! <=2 r_N^-k F(0), |(1/F)^(k)(0)|/k! <=2 r_N^-k/F(0). (12) Thus finite normal jets and inverse scalar jets have polynomial relative cost UNIFORMLY throughout this folded supported chamber. This scalar assertion does not estimate a change of physical frame. Together with (10a), it bounds squared fixed normal jets by a polynomial times exp[(2N/pi)Vol_ext(T(a_ell))], with all joint labels still shared. ## 5. Complementary partners: positive value core and a real missing current Now replace ANY subset of the six folded labels ell by D-ell. At each face, its new deficits are old deficits, their complements D-old_deficit, the old excess F-D, or its complement D-(F-D). They all lie in [0,D]. Its new sum lies in [D,2D]. Therefore (2)'s denominator-unit assertion survives at EVERY one of the up to 64 partner assignments, and the new z range is nonempty with z_-<=2D. Also the sum of its six labels is at most 4D, because every new face has sum at most 2D. Hence z_+<=8D/3<3N-1. The generic sum still contains [N] in every term, but some terms now contain [2N] too. The EXACT decomposition is (-1)^D S(zeta)/[N]_zeta=C(zeta)+[2N]_zeta T(zeta), (13) where C sums the TRUE terms z<=2D after deleting the numerator [N], and T sums the terms z>=2N-1 after deleting BOTH [N] and [2N]. All their denominators are units. At q the nonempty core is exactly the positive expression (5), with z truncated at 2D. The positive metric (6) and squared identity (8) apply at every partner value too. The core C has the same polynomial scalar-jet bound as section4. The term [2N]T is NOT zero as a generic normal. In particular ((-1)^D S/[N])'(0)=C'(0)+(4N/(q-q^-1))T(0). (14) Writing z=2N-1+k, its retained root value is explicitly T(0)=-2sin(pi/N)N^2 sum_k (-1)^k s_k /[product_i s_(2N-1+k-F_i) product_j s_(Q_j-2N+1-k)]. (15) Every index in (15) is physical. The alternating sum must remain coherent. Its absolute-value envelope is not a substitute for it. For example N=4, partner labels (2,2,2,2,2,1) arise by five flips from the supported folded labels (1,1,1,1,1,1). Their faces are (6,6,5,5), quads (8,7,7). Core z=6 gives C(0)=sqrt(2), while the single tail term z=7 gives T(0)=-1. The EXTRA first normal in (14) is exactly 8sqrt(2)i. Deleting the tail loses actual data. Accordingly (12) is a theorem for the complete LOW-fold scalar germ and for partner value cores. It is NOT asserted for the full partner germ without a further coherent estimate for T. Nor are the partner columns deleted from a physical Hermite cluster. This is the remaining normal interface for using the positive factorial in a full recoupling energy argument. A research lead, originally unproved, is preserved by the [64-partner value diagnostic](../experiments/diagnose_supported_racah_partner_value_reflection.py) and its [recorded root images](../experiments/supported_racah_partner_value_reflection_diagnostic_results.json). For three specified folded tuples per level when distinct, every one of the 64 complement bit patterns was checked at N=3,...,10: 1408 comparisons showed no failure of W_squared invariance. These are exact finite cyclotomic-root images, not a uniform complex identity proof. No symmetry of generic germs, bound on the [2N] current, completed physical Gram or volume theorem is inferred from that observation. The subsequent [actual partner-reflection theorem](actual_racah_partner_reflection_identity.md) now proves the root-value symmetry uniformly from the actual reciprocal source and analytic projector residues. Its exact first-normal counterexample shows why this does not establish generic-jet symmetry. ## 6. An exact valuation interface to the separately proved physical kernel The preceding factorial theorem has not used a source identity. One can now APPLY the independently proved [actual inverse four-port theorem](actual_general_four_port_single_racah_kernel.md), equations (23),(24). Put its external highest weights (A,B,C,D_ext)=(2a,2b,2c,2d), E=2e and G=2f. It states L_(G,E)=chi_E X_E/(b_G J_n S0 V_n) *S, p=min(a+d,b+c), q=max(a+d,b+c), s=p+q, n=p-f, t0=q-p, V_n=zeta^n (Q^(-p-f-1);Q)_n /[F_n(Q^(t0+1);Q)_n(Q^(-s-1);Q)_n]. (16) Throughout the fully supported folded chamber, chi_E X_E, b_G and J_n are root units, while S0 has exactly one [N] zero. This follows directly from the source product formulas: all their physical factorial indices are <=D, whereas the numerator of S0 is [s+1]! with D<=s<=2D. For X_E at its endpoint, its numerator index is <=A when that endpoint is H, and <=B when it is A. Hence no endpoint root zero has been hidden in that assertion. Both f faces imply p+f>=D and q+f>=D. The sole possible numerator zero of V_n is at index k=p+f-D. It is INSIDE 0,...,n-1 exactly when 2f<D. Its denominator has no root zero: t0+n=q-f<=D, and the first potential zero in (Q^(-s-1);Q)_n has index s-D>=n. Consequently the actual inverse coefficient has exact order ord_q L_(G,E)=-1 if 2f<D, ord_q L_(G,E)= 0 if 2f=D. (17) Its leading coefficient is nonzero by the positive finite sum (5). Thus a positive root factorial does NOT turn the uncompleted physical coefficient matrix into a finite positive operator: paired output channels have genuine simple poles and must be combined with their partners in a regular Hermite frame. The same bookkeeping in the actual ordered invariant norm N_E=n_(ab)^e n_(cd)^e [2e+1] gives order two for paired e and order one for odd simple e. These are source-frame orders, not optional quantum-dimension factors. Equations (16),(17) supply an explicit local interface for matching the positive metric (6) to a completed physical recoupling energy; they do not complete that matching or bound the partner current (15). Audit: [true root factorials, partner ranges and retained Taylor coefficients](../experiments/audit_actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.py). The common phase, metric, uniform action and jet arguments above are independent of the proposed actual four-port source identity. Independent internal review: the global audit agent completed a full analytical read of sections1–6 and a fresh primary replay. The harmonic unit-factor estimate and inverse jets, exact high-partner current, N=4 nonzero normal, source pole orders and norm orders all passed. The replay checked eight exhaustive folded levels, 1202 supported tuples, 686 partner metrics, the retained-current fixture and six metric-action calibrations. That verdict does not include a full partner-jet bound or a positive completed physical recoupling Gram.

title: A tame Hermite frame for the original source channel
text: # A tame Hermite frame for the original source channel 29 October 2026. The colliding c_0 Casimir channel containing the ORIGINAL cup has an explicit generalized vector with harmonic-sum coefficients. Its source-adapted Hermite frame has UNIFORMLY bounded physical condition number after a common N^(3/2) scale. In that frame the original marked and ordinary caps are exactly the two coordinate rows, and the full crossing is a unit scalar times a Jordan matrix with uniformly bounded off-diagonal coefficient. This proves an actual source-controlled Hermite Gram for the selected T=N-1 channel, including its derivative direction. It does not estimate recoupling from this channel into all other channels on overlapping pairs. No full-channel q-Racah norm or sharp knot bound follows yet. ## 1. The original physical source and Casimir Fix `q=exp(pi*i/N)`, `Q=q^2`, `d=N-1`, `rho=q-q^(-1)`, `x=q^d=-q^(-1)`, `N>=2`. On balanced heads use exactly mathsfF|a>=(1-Q^(a+1))|a+1>, Ecal|a>=(Q^(-a)-1)|a-1>, K|a>=xQ^(-a)|a>, F_tot=mathsfF_1+K_1^(-1)mathsfF_2, E_tot=Ecal_1 K_2+Ecal_2, Omega=F_tot E_tot+qK_tot+q^(-1)K_tot^(-1). Missing endpoint arrows are zero. Work on the physical integer-degree d subspace with basis `|u,d-u>`, `0<=u<=d`. Let `c_*=q+q^(-1)`. The ORIGINAL cup, ordinary pivotal cap and marked row restrict here to p_u=N x^(u-d), ell_u=x^(-u)Q^(-u)/N, m_u=x^(d-u)/N^2. (1) The unrestricted marked row is not replaced by this restricted row on other degrees; every vector constructed below has degree d. These are the fixed actual turns, with no invented scalar frame. Define finite harmonic sums H_0=0, H_u=sum_(j=1)^u 1/(1-Q^j), g_u=x^(u-d)=p_u/N, v_u=-g_u H_u/rho. (2) Then the exact Jordan equations are (Omega-c_*)g=0, (Omega-c_*)v=g. (3) In particular g,v are independent, and their span is the actual size-two c_* block inside integer degree d. This block, rather than the entire 2N-dimensional c_* generalized eigenspace across degrees, is the source channel treated in this note. ## 2. Derivation from generic q with actual cup duality retained Use a variable z near q and the ordinary highest-weight representation of highest weight d=N-1. Put `Q_z=z^2`, `x(z)=z^d`, `F_a(z)=product_(j=1)^a(1-z^(2j))`. Keep the standard highest-weight endpoint, including `mathsfF|d>=0`. All factorials with `a<N` are nonzero near q. The top-channel descendant and spin-zero invariant cup may be normalized as g_u(z)=x(z)^(u-d), h_u(z)=g_u(z) R_u(z), R_u(z)=(-1)^u z^[-u(u+1)] F_u(z)F_(d-u)(z)/F_d(z). (4) Indeed `g(z)=F_tot(z)^d|0,0>/F_d(z)`. The finite coproduct binomial proves its displayed components. The E equation for an invariant degree-d vector gives the successive ratio h_(u+1)/h_u=-z^[d-2u-2] (1-z^(2u+2))/(1-z^(2d-2u)), which is (4); direct F and K equations give `F_tot h=0`, `K_tot h=h`. Thus h is the ACTUAL self-duality cup up to the stated analytic unit normalization. Its paired evaluation is transported reciprocally. One does not extend the root-only expression `K^(1-N)` as a generic-q pivot or assume a root cyclic endpoint away from q. The exact Casimir eigenvalues are Omega(z)g(z)=c_top(z)g(z), Omega(z)h(z)=c_triv(z)h(z), c_top(z)=z^(2N-1)+z^(-2N+1), c_triv(z)=z+z^(-1). (5) These follow from the defining coproduct: the top highest vector has K-root `z^(2d)`, while h is invariant. They can also be checked directly from the entries above. Root complementation gives `R_u(q)=1`, so `h(q)=g(q)`. Meanwhile D_logz(c_triv-c_top)|q=2N rho, D_logz R_u|q=-2N H_u. (6) For the second equation, differentiate (4) and pair its last u factorial terms with indices `N-j`. Their sum reduces to `-2N sum_(j<=u)(1-Q^j)^(-1)`; the quadratic integer terms cancel. All derivatives are at fixed N and the actual root, at either parity. Consequently lim_(z->q) [h(z)-g(z)]/[c_triv(z)-c_top(z)]=v. (7) Applying (5) before the limit proves (3). This is a normalized divided difference of actual Clebsch channels, with the original cup kept. It does not use the fixed-q common-meridian splitting at a dual cap; that cap's exact dual-color product keeps its Casimir nodes collided. An analytic rescaling of h or g, equal to one at q, can add a multiple of g to v. The source-adapted vector in Section3 removes precisely that ambiguity. Thus the final Hermite frame does not depend on the unphysical first derivative of an eigenvector normalization. ## 3. Exact original co-sources and the canonical Hermite lift The finite sums in (1)--(2) give ell g=0, m g=1/N, gamma_N:=ell v=q x^(-d)/(N rho^2) =(-1)^N/(N rho^2), mu_N:=m v=-(sum_(u=0)^d H_u)/(N^2 rho). (8) In particular gamma_N is NONZERO at every level. To check its value, interchange the two finite sums: sum_(u=0)^d Q^(-u)H_u =sum_(j=1)^d [sum_(u=j)^d Q^(-u)]/(1-Q^j) =-1/(1-Q^(-1)). Also `q x^(-d)=(-1)^N`, by `x=q^d` and the actual half-period q. This accounts for the full parity sign. Define the SOURCE-ADAPTED generalized vector t_N=(v-mu_N p)/gamma_N. (9) Then all original source pairings are exactly m p=1, m t_N=0, ell p=0, ell t_N=1, (Omega-c_*)t_N=theta_N p, theta_N=1/(N gamma_N)=(-1)^N rho^2. (10) Thus the two original co-sources, not newly chosen dual rows, are the inverse frame on this actual Jordan channel. In particular `(Omega-c_*)|span(p,t_N)=theta_N p ell`, agreeing with the retained rank-one nilpotent source. No ordinary quantum dimension is divided out. The generalized direction and the marked co-source remain. The replacement `v->v+lambda g` changes `mu_N` by `lambda/N`, so the numerator in (9) is unchanged. This proves the normalization independence asserted after (7). ## 4. Fourier--Plancherel gives uniform physical conditioning For `1<=j<N`, |1-Q^j|>=4min(j,N-j)/N, |rho|>=4/N. Hence, with `Harm_N=1+log N`, max_u |H_u| <=(N/2)Harm_N, ||v||_2 <=(N^(5/2)/8)Harm_N, |mu_N| <=(N/8)Harm_N, |gamma_N|^(-1)=N|rho|^2<=4N. These estimates already give polynomial frame bounds without a spectral projector. A stronger exact Fourier calculation removes their condition growth. On degree d the original marked row is `m=p^*/N^3`, so (10) gives `p^*t_N=0`. If `Hbar=(1/N)sum_u H_u`, (9) becomes (t_N)_u=(-1)^(N+1)N rho g_u(H_u-Hbar). (11) Use the unnormalized cyclic Fourier transform `Hhat_k=sum_(u=0)^d H_u Q^(-ku)`. Pairing j with N-j gives `H_d=d/2`. The cyclic difference of H therefore has value `-d/2` at zero and `(1-Q^u)^(-1)` at `u=1,...,d`. Its Fourier transform is EXACTLY `-k`, for `1<=k<=d`: successive transforms differ by `sum_(j=1)^d Q^(-kj)=-1`, starting at zero for k=0. Consequently Hhat_k=-k/(1-Q^(-k)), 1<=k<=d, ||t_N||_2^2=N|rho|^2 sum_(k=1)^d k^2/|1-Q^k|^2. (12) This is ordinary finite Plancherel on the FULL physical N-window; no Fourier channel is omitted or independently dephased. The elementary root identity is sum_(k=1)^d |1-Q^k|^(-2)=(N^2-1)/12. For a direct proof differentiate `P(z)=(z^N-1)/(z-1)` twice at one. The first reciprocal sum is d/2 and the sum of squared reciprocals is `d(5-N)/12`; their difference is the displayed absolute sum. Pairing k and N-k then gives N^2(N^2-1)/48 <=sum_(k=1)^d k^2/|1-Q^k|^2 <=N^2(N^2-1)/24. Since `4/N<=|rho|<=2pi/N`, it follows that N^3/4<=||t_N||_2^2<=pi^2 N^3/6, p^*t_N=0, ||p||_2^2=N^3. (13) For the two physical columns `V=[p,t_N]` this proves sigma_min(V)>=N^(3/2)/2, sigma_max(V)<=pi N^(3/2)/sqrt(6), kappa(V)<=2, uniformly EVERY N>=2. (14) For the last bound use the known first column norm N^(3/2), not just the two extreme singular-value bounds: the other column's relative norm lies in `[1/2,pi/sqrt(6)]`, and `pi/sqrt(6)<2`. The condition number is therefore at most two; N=2 attains two. The exact inverse on its range is still the two ORIGINAL rows m,ell by (10). The ordinary row on the full physical degree-d space has a larger norm because it also sees other channel directions; its restriction here is precisely the coordinate dual of t_N. No inverse of a possibly ill-conditioned whole Casimir projector was used. ## 5. An actual positive Hermite Gram and crossing bound On `S_N=span(p,t_N)` define the positive inner product ||w||_(Herm)^2=|m w|^2+|ell w|^2. (15) It makes p,t_N orthonormal. It has rank two on S_N, not rank one, and retains BOTH the value and derivative channels. Both original co-sources have dual norm one. Equation (14) compares this Gram uniformly with N^(-3) times the physical metric. This is an explicit source-controlled Hermite Gram, not a metric defined from an unknown knot scalar or terminal word. Keep the original crossing's common Cartan scalar kappa. The independently derived Casimir polynomial has r(c_*)=1, r'(c_*)=-d/(2rho). Therefore in the p,t_N frame the EXACT original signed crossing is R_+=kappa [[1,tau_N],[0,1]], R_-=kappa^(-1) [[1,-tau_N],[0,1]], tau_N=(-1)^(N+1)d rho/2, |tau_N|<=pi. (16) Thus, for every signed integer l, ||R_+^l||_(Herm)<=1+pi|l| (17) at the original complete root, since `|kappa|=1`. The original full Cartan, pivot, framing and modified-dimension line have not been renormalized; (16) is a basis expression for that same operator. The PHYSICAL operator norm on this SAME invariant source channel is consequently at most `2(1+pi|l|)`, uniformly in N. The Gram (15) is asserted on the SELECTED TWO-DIMENSIONAL invariant channel only. Adjacent crossings may take it into other intermediate Casimir channels. Extending it through the full q-Racah transform, with the source, is the remaining problem. Declaring the rest of the physical tensor space orthogonal would not control that leakage, and no such full-channel estimate is claimed here. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_tame_c0_hermite_source_frame.py): literal original E/F Casimir and signed R, all original source rows, generic-q cup/descendant divided difference, parity and frame singular values at both odd and even levels.

status: Explicit rational source gauge and commuting finite-jet connection
text: # A flat finite-jet connection for the actual tensor source 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. The specified generic white tensors, cups and categorical duals have exact moving-period head transport. After imposing their ORIGINAL integral affine head constraints, this gives explicit commuting differential/rational operators on every finite order of genuine quantum jets. The root parity character is retained. Divisors, the finite support and the original exposed-head trace normalization are retained as well. This is a statement about the actual continued tensor summand. It does not identify its finite sum with a periodic sum, move its residue cycle across a divisor, or prove that a geometric saddle contributes. ## 1. The local source factors and their exact shifts Fix N>=3, d=N-1, zeta=exp(pi i/N+epsilon), P=pi i/Log zeta, Q=zeta^2, eta=exp(2pi i P), Delta=N-P. (1) All highest weights and finite polynomial degrees remain FIXED integers as epsilon varies. Use the actual large-channel white continuation from the [generic source theorem](actual_generic_boundary_gauge_and_source.md): W_a(i,j;r)=(-1)^m zeta^[-dr+di-m(m-1)] H_m^(Q^(-N))(Q^i,Q^j)/F_m, m=d-a, i+j=m+r, F_m=(Q;Q)_m. (2) It is the original generic W_a:V_(2a)->V_d tensor V_d, including both physical degree halves. The channel is m=d-a, not its root-colliding small partner a. For ANY integers p,q, (2) gives W_a(i+Pp,j+Pq;r+P(p+q))=(-1)^(d q) W_a(i,j;r). (3) Indeed Q^P=1 leaves the finite polynomial arguments unchanged, and the remaining exponent is -dPq. In particular shifting i by P at fixed i+j multiplies W by (-1)^d. The two physical legs are ordered; the asymmetric form of (3) is intentional. Use the specific moving-period factorial of the [factorial theorem](actual_moving_period_factorial_normals.md), with Fhat_P(z+P)=[1-exp(2pi i z)]Fhat_P(z). For an actual fixed highest weight L<N, its continued ordered cup is p_L(x,L-x)=exp(pi i x) zeta^[x(L-x-1)] Fhat_P(x)Fhat_P(L-x)/F_L. (4) The physical cup has the additional, head-independent factor N zeta^(-d^2). Put Y=exp(2pi i x). Direct substitution, retaining both the quadratic monomial and exp(pi i x), gives p_L(x+nP,L-x-nP)=mu_(L,n)(P,x) p_L(x,L-x), mu_(L,n)=(-1)^(Ln) (1-Y)/(eta^(-n)-Y), n in Z. (5) For n=1 the two factorials contribute (1-Y)/(1-eta^(-1)/Y); the monomials contribute (-1)^(L-1)/Y. This is (5). Repetition telescopes, and reversing the shift proves the formula for negative n. These are meromorphic identities, also where a displayed ratio must be cleared first. The cap is the ACTUAL matrix inverse, so ell_L(x,L-x)=1/p_L(L-x,x). (6) Its multiplier is 1/mu_(L,-n)(P,L-x), not the inverse of mu_(L,n)(P,x). This distinction keeps the cyclic and pivotal normalizations. Physical cup and cap scalars remain in the tensor. The generic Chevalley monomial zeta^[-(L+1)x] has multiplier (-1)^((L+1)n), and the original pivotal clock (-1)^L zeta^(L-2x) has multiplier one. Integer affine characters exp[2pi i ell(heads)] have multiplier eta^(ell(n)). Categorical white duals are expanded in their original ordered W, cup, cap and reversal factors. Thus (3)--(6) apply to their actual finite source, without replacing a dual by an adjoint or dividing by its root norm. Scalar channel weights, fixed generic normalizers and the original half-twist eigenvalues do not depend on magnetic heads and are unchanged by these shifts. ## 2. The actual affine head lattice Take a fixed typed tensor network built from these factors, its original physical turns, and recorded integer affine characters. Fix an admissible assignment of the finite channel labels. Impose every literal head equation, including i+j=m+r at a white vertex, x+y=L at a cup or cap, and equality of each pair of contracted indices. Write the resulting integer affine system as B h=b. Choose one integer solution h0 and a Z-basis A of ker_Z B, and set h=h0+A x, x in C^k. (7) This is a primitive free lattice parametrization. Indeed ker_Z B is saturated: Z^n/ker_Z B is isomorphic to the free subgroup im_Z B of Z^rows. The chosen basis also spans the complex kernel. An inconsistent channel assignment has no original summands and is discarded. The original finite admissibility inequalities are kept separately; (7) does not remove or wrap them. Let S(epsilon,x) be the MEROMORPHIC summand obtained from the specified continuations (2),(4),(6), retaining all scalars, ordering and characters. It agrees with the actual generic summand at every admissible integer head assignment. Any exposed boundary heads are held fixed, or their explicitly chosen factors and their constraints are included in (7); an arbitrary boundary environment is not silently assigned a continuation. Use an admissible generic stratum of these head equations. A factor whose head argument is constant on this chart is left as its original constant source factor. In particular an admissible physical integer cup is evaluated by its finite factorials. A forbidden constant polar stratum is not made into a source by substituting into a 0/0 ratio: keep its originally zero summand as zero, or use a separately proved generic cancellation. No transport is asserted for an undefined constant polar interpolation. For b in Z^k, every local head changes by an integer multiple of P under x->x+Pb. Multiplying the LITERAL local identities gives S(epsilon,x+Pb)=C_b(P,x) S(epsilon,x). (8) The multiplier C_b is explicit: multiply the signs (3), the cup factors (5), the inverse factors at the reversed cap arguments (6), and the stated clock/character factors. In particular it belongs to the rational field generated by eta and Y_l=exp(2pi i z_l(x)), where each z_l is the corresponding integer affine head argument. There are no omitted Fourier or peripheral characters. Since N is an integer, each multiplier is N-periodic in every free coordinate. Its root value, on a chart avoiding Y_l=1, is the explicit sign C_b(N,x)=chi(b) in {1,-1}. (9) The sign is a lattice character. It includes the white-leg signs and the parity of each actual highest weight; it is not reset to one when N changes parity. Any additional boundary character must be explicitly transported before extending this source class. The construction also works termwise for the finite channel sum. For the usual matching source the homogeneous head system is the same for all channel assignments, each channel weight 2a is even, and h0 is integral. Require also that the integer LINEAR coefficients of every separately recorded head character be unchanged across the assignments. Thus, whenever a common primitive basis is used and this character-coefficient condition holds, the same C_b applies to that sum: exp(2pi i h0)=1 and the local parities are unchanged. This concerns only the chosen algebraic extensions of the summands on their admissible strata. Their support-dependent cycles remain separate; it does not create a single unconstrained periodic sum. If a different source has label-dependent parity, character coefficients or different homogeneous constraints, retain the corresponding finite vector of summands and its diagonal transport instead of asserting a common multiplier. There is an explicit rational trivialization, obtained from the actual cup rather than an existence theorem. Put g(z)=exp(2pi i z)/[1-exp(2pi i z)]. Then g(z+nP)/g(z)=(1-Y)/(eta^(-n)-Y), so p_L/g has the constant P-shift character (-1)^(Ln). For each factor of the network put one g at the cup's first argument, and an inverse g at the literal cup argument used by an inverse cap. Multiply these factors and all separately retained exp(2pi i ell(heads)) characters: G(x)=product_cup_factors g(z_l(x))^(e_l) *exp[2pi i ell(h0+A x)], e_l=+1 or -1. (9a) The product in (9a) includes ONLY cup/cap arguments which are NONCONSTANT on the chosen free chart. A constant argument has shift number zero and multiplier identically one, so requires no g factor; in particular we never insert the undefined g of a fixed integer. Simplify mu_(L,0)=1 before evaluating any such constant argument. The cap argument in (9a) is L-x when its first matrix index is x. White, Chevalley and clock factors require no additional rational gauge. Thus G is a SPECIFIED rational function of the marked head exponentials, independent of P, and C_b(P,x)=chi(b) G(x+Pb)/G(x). (9b) Equivalently S/G is P-quasiperiodic with exactly chi. This is an algebraic identity on the meromorphic source; the zeros and poles of G are part of the identity. In particular G can be singular on the original physical lattice. It is not an allowable reason to delete a factor from a period integral. Nor is this rational gauge automatically subexponential on scaled complex charts. For z=N(x+iy) with fixed y>0, |g(z)|=exp(-2pi N y)(1+o(1)). Thus G can contribute to the leading action as well as to divisor residues. Conjugating the transport does not normalize away that contribution or the volume; any asymptotic source calculation must retain it. ## 3. A genuine commuting finite-jet representation Take Taylor jets of the actual source after its proved generic cancellations, on a head chart where it is regular in epsilon. If an intermediate decomposition has a known scalar pole of order M, first multiply it by epsilon^M; recovering its original Laurent coefficients then requires the corresponding higher Taylor order. No principal part is discarded by the transport construction. Let D_b be the constant directional derivative in direction b and M_f denote multiplication by f. Since x+Nb=(x+Delta b)+Pb, (8) gives the exact local identity S(epsilon,x+Nb)=T_b S(epsilon,x), T_b=exp(Delta D_b) M_(C_b). (10) In this formula the derivative acts on BOTH C_b and S. Modulo epsilon^(J+1) it is the explicit finite differential operator T_b^(J)=sum_(r=0)^J Delta^r D_b^r M_(C_b)/r! mod epsilon^(J+1). (11) Only the order-J Taylor coefficients of the rational multiplier are needed. Its coefficients are rational in the marked Y_l and retain their divisors; no infinite Taylor series is required for a finite quantum jet. These operators commute and represent the free head lattice, not merely when applied to the particular source. The rational gauge makes the statement especially explicit. Since G(x+Nb)=G(x), (9b),(10) give the exact operator identity T_b=chi(b) M_G exp(Delta D_b) M_(G^(-1)). (11a) Thus all the operators are simultaneous conjugates of ordinary translations. This proves their group law directly. Equivalently, the local multipliers obey the exact P-shift cocycle C_(b+c)(P,x)=C_b(P,x+Pc) C_c(P,x). (12) This follows either directly from (3),(5), or by composing the literal meromorphic identities. Their N-periodicity gives C_b(x-Delta c)=C_b(x+Pc). Hence, as operators on local meromorphic functions, T_b T_c =exp[Delta D_(b+c)] M_(C_b(x-Delta c)C_c(x)) =T_(b+c)=T_c T_b. (13) The same holds after finite-jet truncation. Normalize by the retained root character, U_b=chi(b)^(-1)T_b^(J). Since Delta is in (epsilon) and C_b/chi(b)=1 mod epsilon, (U_b-I) raises the epsilon filtration, product_(r=1)^(J+1)(U_(b_r)-I)=0. (14) Thus the normalized transport is a commuting unipotent representation on finite jets of the ACTUAL tensor summand. Its inverses are finite geometric series, or simply U_(-b). The number of vertices need not be small; J is the chosen finite derivative order. This is a local statement in the meromorphic coefficient field, not a bound near its poles or a nilpotence theorem for global source periods. Its logarithmic connection is explicit as well: U_b=exp[Delta nabla_b] mod epsilon^(J+1), nabla_b=D_b-D_b Log G=M_G D_b M_(G^(-1)). (14a) These commuting derivatives have the recorded simple logarithmic poles along the integral-head divisors of (9a). No unspecified gauge or discarded boundary character enters their construction. For clarity, write S=S0+epsilon S1+O(epsilon^2), and C_b=chi(b)[1+epsilon c_b1+O(epsilon^2)]. Since P'(0)=iN^2/pi, (10) is S0(x+Nb)=chi(b) S0(x), S1(x+Nb)=chi(b)[S1-P'(0)D_b S0+c_b1 S0]. (15) For a cup factor with argument z_l and shift number n_l, its contribution to c_b1 is 2pi i P'(0) n_l/[1-exp(2pi i z_l)]. (16) For an inverse cup use its literal argument and the negative of this contribution. An eta^k character contributes 2pi i P'(0)k. White and clock signs have zero derivative. Thus (15) is explicit even before a particular network is chosen. The simple poles in (16) are essential genuine normal terms. ## 4. A concrete exceptional-operator connection The [literal generic exceptional lift](actual_matching_edge_generic_deficient_operator_lift.md) is an example with three free coordinates (t,u,v). Put r=a-v+u, ell=t-v, Y_r=exp(2pi i r), Y_v=exp(2pi i v), Y_ell=exp(2pi i ell), s=d-2a, A(Y)=(1-Y)/(eta^(-1)-Y), B(Y)=(1-Y)/(eta-Y). Applying the two actual large whites, the Chevalley scalar and the three ordered cups of that lift gives C_u=(-1)^s A(Y_r), C_v=(-1)^s B(Y_r)/[A(Y_v)B(Y_ell)], C_t=1/A(Y_ell). (17) These are identities for the full generic polynomial kernel and for its completed version: the moving face scalar is independent of t,u,v. They preserve the retained exp(-2pi i v) root character; that character is one under an integer N-shift but not under a moving P-shift. It must not be erased before forming (17). Equation (17), including its cocycles, is a short source-specific certificate for the abstract-looking operators (10). Its poles include the actual channel-row divisors of the continued kernel. The formulas do not replace that kernel by its phase-canceled root value before differentiation. Here the rational gauge (9a) is particularly short: G_K=g(r)/[g(v)g(ell)] =exp[2pi i(u-v-t)] (1-Y_v)(1-Y_ell)/(1-Y_r). (17a) Substitution in (9b) reproduces all three multipliers (17), with chi_u=chi_v=(-1)^s and chi_t=1. Formula (17a) includes its integer exponential and its actual channel-row pole. ## 5. Ordinary closure, the exposed mark, and remaining scope For the original marked invariant use the SAME exposed physical head and its actual generic ordinary pivotal closure. If F(epsilon) is that finite closed source, its normalization is D_N(epsilon)=(-1)^d[N]_(q0 exp(epsilon)), nu_N=D_N'(0)=2N(-1)^N/(q0-q0^(-1)), Z=F'(0)/nu_N. (18) The transport above applies to its actual continued ordinary summand and its retained first jet before carrying out this normalization. It does not create a generic continuation of the bare dense root mark. If an off-root marked row is specified, it must be transported covariantly with its original cup; otherwise the ordinary closure and (18) are the available source theorem. Likewise a regular Hopf lift of a complete-circle coupon and the literal moving-q exceptional polynomial are distinct generic germs. Use whichever has actually been specified; (10) never identifies them merely because their root values agree. At the original lattice, Y_l=1. The normalized rational operators can therefore have poles even where the complete source has a removable cancellation. Equalities (8),(10) hold meromorphically, and may be cleared of denominators before specialization. They are not permission to discard a residue or apply an individual singular factor to a root value without its full generic germ. Finally, a shift of the summand does not preserve its finite admissibility polytope. A residue-cycle representation also has its own cotangent factors and boundary. To pass from (10) to a global period identity one must carry that original cycle, its crossed divisors and all affine mark/peripheral characters. No such cycle deformation or nonzero selected contribution is proved here. ## 6. Focused source checks The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_tensor_source_finite_jet_connection.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_tensor_source_finite_jet_connection_results.json) verify the rational trivialization and all three literal exceptional kernel multipliers, their cocycles and first-normal connections, and a shared integral head chart. Independent evaluations of the original large white polynomial, moving-factorial cups and the full generic completed kernel check 24, 6 and 6 moving-period shifts respectively. Three genuine fixed-N transports include first and second normals. The largest relative identity error at 85 digits was below 1.2e-82. These checks do not replace the arbitrary-network multiplication and operator proofs, and make no assertion about a transported period. Independent full analytical reviews by the primary and cluster-source agents passed the literal source shifts, cap ordering, primitive head chart, rational gauge, operator group law and finite-jet conclusion. The reviews retain the constant-head omission, common-character condition for color sums, possible exponential action of G, and ordinary-closure/bare-mark distinction. The cluster-source agent also checked the root-regular or cleared-Laurent jet scope and freshly replayed the entire focused audit with the reported counts and error. No global cycle or volume-equality conclusion is included in this review.

title: The adjoint finite-jet connection on the original source cycle
status: Adjoint connection on the original cotangent period
text: # The adjoint finite-jet connection on the original source cycle 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed and frozen. The exact tensor-source transport has a corresponding identity for the ORIGINAL cotangent period. Its adjoint acts on the cotangent density as well as on the explicit source gauge. The resulting double-pole and finite-part terms are retained. This does not make the finite head sum periodic or move its cycle to the geometric critical point. ## 1. The actual period and the specified source connection Use the [actual tensor-source connection](actual_tensor_source_finite_jet_connection.md). After the original integral affine head equations, write the primitive free lattice as h=h0+A x, x in C^k. Constant head factors remain their original source constants. Fix the finite channel labels, or retain the finite vector of label sectors when their characters differ. Every outside tensor, turn and peripheral character is part of the specified meromorphic source S(epsilon,x). At the original marked arc use its ordinary generic pivotal closure and subsequent exposed-trace normal, or an explicitly chosen covariant generic marked row. No generic continuation of the bare root mark is supplied by this theorem. Initially assume S is root-regular in epsilon on a common neighborhood of the cycle, after retaining its actual meromorphic cancellations. If a chosen representation has a finite Laurent pole of order M, apply the statements to epsilon^M S through order J+M to recover the original Laurent jet through order J. One must not use only J translation terms before multiplying a source with such a pole. Put P=pi i/Log(q0 exp(epsilon)), Delta=N-P, and P'=iN^2/pi. For b in Z^k, let D_b=sum b_j partial_(x_j). The source theorem proves S(epsilon,x+Nb)=chi(b) G(x) exp(Delta D_b)[G(x)^-1 S], (1) where chi(b) is the actual parity character and G is the explicit P-independent rational cup/character gauge. Its construction omits constant head factors; in particular it never inserts g(integer) for an identically constant cup argument. Formula (1) is meromorphic and its exponential is a FINITE differential operator modulo any fixed epsilon^(J+1). The original lattice density and normalized period are W(x)=product_(j=1)^k pi cot(pi x_j), I_Gamma[S]=(2pi i)^(-k) integral_Gamma W(x) S(x) dx, (2) with dx=dx1 wedge ... wedge dxk. Gamma is the original sum of compact local tori, or a specified closed cycle on the same source chart. It avoids the divisors of S, W, G and G^-1 on its surface on a common epsilon germ, or the genuinely canceled meromorphic integrands are used throughout. Its interior may contain the original cotangent and source poles. The [source-null extension theorem](actual_matching_edge_degree_cycle_boundary.md) allows its explicitly proved zero ordered tori to be included as well. Other polar strata are not implicitly added or removed. ## 2. Exact adjoint transport of every finite quantum jet For every fixed J, on the original CLOSED cycle one has I_Gamma[S(epsilon,x+Nb)] =chi(b)(2pi i)^(-k) integral_Gamma G^-1 exp(-Delta D_b)(W G) S dx mod epsilon^(J+1). (3) All derivatives in (3) act on the actual top-form density W G. This is not a replacement of the original period by a period of S/G. The final meromorphic integrand is used with every cancellation and divisor retained, rather than evaluated factor by factor at G=0 or G=infinity. Proof: for meromorphic f,g with no pole on the cycle, integral_Gamma f D_b g dx=-integral_Gamma (D_b f) g dx. Indeed D_b(fg) dx=d(fg contraction_b(dx)), whose integral on a closed cycle is zero. This argument needs no pole-free interior. Apply it r times to the r-th term of (1), with f=W G and g=G^-1 S. Since Delta is independent of x and belongs to (epsilon), only r<=J occurs for the root-regular source specified in section 1. For a Laurent source use the cleared source and the enlarged order stated there. This proves (3) without an infinite differential expansion or an analytic translation of Gamma by the small complex number Delta. For the literal translated cycle Gamma+Nb, a change of variables also gives I_(Gamma+Nb)[S]=I_Gamma[S(epsilon,x+Nb)], (4) because the ORIGINAL W is N-periodic. This is an identity of the specified continued source at that translated cycle. It does not say the shifted head values are admissible original states or vanish outside the physical basis. In particular the meromorphic continuation need not vanish at out-of-basis shifted indices. If a geometric deformation from one cycle to the other crosses source divisors, their tubes and residues remain in that deformation. Equations (3),(4) compute the translated period; they do not identify the two cycles in the complement of those divisors. ## 3. The first normal and the original exposed trace normalization Write S=S0+epsilon S1+O(epsilon^2). Formula (3) yields I_(Gamma+Nb)[S0]=chi(b) I_Gamma[S0], I_(Gamma+Nb)[S1]-chi(b) I_Gamma[S1] =chi(b) P' (2pi i)^(-k) integral_Gamma G^-1 D_b(W G) S0 dx. (5) The sign is positive: Delta'=-P' and the adjoint exponential is exp(-Delta D_b). The correction includes derivatives of BOTH W and G. Writing it as W D_b Log(WG) is permissible only as a meromorphic identity; the un-divided density in (5) specifies its actual periods. For the original ordinary exposed-head closure, retain nu_N=2N(-1)^N/(q0-q0^-1), P'/nu_N=(-1)^(N+1) N sin(pi/N)/pi. (6) When the original root closure I_Gamma[S0] is zero, its translated root closure is also zero by (5), so division of the first-normal identity by nu_N gives the exact corresponding marked-period difference. Its correction density has the nonzero order-one scalar in (6), rather than an arbitrarily assigned boundary coefficient. It is not yet a nonzero global geometric contribution. For a primitive direction with several nonzero b_j, D_b differentiates the corresponding ORIGINAL cotangent factors. A chosen degree h need not be a primitive free variable. For h=A0 x_j+B0 at fixed other coordinates, the weight is (pi/A0)cot(pi(h-B0)/A0) dh. The finite-part rules of the boundary theorem apply with that weight. Neither (3) nor (5) replaces it by pi cot(pi h) dh. ## 4. A literal cup exhibits a nonzero double-pole correction For one varying cup argument, its source gauge is g(x)=Y/(1-Y), Y=exp(2pi i x), pi cot(pi x)=-pi i(1+2g(x)). Let w=pi cot(pi x). The correction density in (5) is g^-1 (w g)'=w'+w * 2pi i/(1-Y). (7) At an integer n, with y=x-n, this equals -2/y^2+pi i/y+O(1). Consequently its residue against a root source regular there is pi i S0(n)-2 S0'(n). (8) Both copies of the derivative matter: one comes from the original cotangent and one from the actual cup gauge. For the ordered fixed-L cup with L=d=N-1, the exact fixed-root reflection gives p_d(0,x)=exp(pi i d x/N). On a physical n in [0,d], the difference of its translated and parity-weighted original first-normal cotangent periods is therefore exactly (-1)^d N(N-2) exp(pi i d n/N). (9) This is the ordered channel-cup normalization of the source theorem. For the physical cup, multiply by its original root scalar N q0^(-d^2); its generic scalar derivative cancels from the difference because the corresponding root difference is zero. The translated cup can have a generic pole at n+N. Its cotangent period is the actual Laurent finite part, not its value at that pole. Thus (9) is a concrete counterexample to silently declaring these continued periods periodic. ## 5. Scope of the cycle identity The source connection, the original primitive lattice and the original weight together determine every finite-order correction in (3). The isolated wall residues and source-null ordered periods are already given by the boundary theorem. Their combination supplies exact finite-head transport with its boundary terms retained. What remains separate is a deformation of the FULL original period through all its source divisors to a contributing geometric cycle, including its noncompact ends and the coherent outside contraction. No equality of the positive envelope with volume, no periodic extension of the physical basis, and no nonzero saddle coefficient follows from this adjoint identity. Focused verification: [adjoint and original cup audit](../experiments/audit_actual_tensor_source_translated_cycle_normals.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_tensor_source_translated_cycle_normals_results.json). The audit checks 60 exact meromorphic adjoint residues through derivative order three, the actual cotangent double-pole coefficient, and 12 genuine translated first-normal cup finite parts obtained independently from the original moving-Gamma Laurent coefficients. The latter agree with (9) to relative error below 5.3e-38 at 100 digits. These are checks of the retained local periods, not evidence for a global saddle coefficient. Primary-agent full analytical review: PASS. The reader checked the closed-cycle exact-differential argument, finite Taylor/Laurent order, the adjoint sign, original mark and trace normalization, and the actual cup double-pole and translated finite-part calculation. The result retains all source and gauge divisors and makes no contributing-cycle assertion. Independent current-agent full analytical review and fresh redirected audit: PASS. The reader checked the primitive top-form normalization, Stokes argument and adjoint sign, the actual cotangent measure and dependent-degree Jacobian, root-regular or cleared-Laurent jet orders, and the original exposed-trace normalization. The literal moving-Gamma cup Laurent coefficients and reversed-cup turn were independently rederived before replaying all 60 exact adjoint residues and 12 actual translated first-normal finite parts. No wrapped physical state or geometric contribution was inferred.

title: An open six-head bridge reduces exactly to a typed current and angle packet
text: # An open six-head bridge reduces exactly to a typed current and angle packet 29 October 2026. The first bridge crossing that couples the two ordinary cap pairs of a six-head source can be eliminated as an EXACT map between complete multiplicity modules. The cap forces one physical transfer. All spectator inputs and operator coefficients remain open. The resulting six-head terminal packet is the four-head packet composed with the map below, not a scalar knot-by-knot replacement. The through-head feedback factors into a contractive strict shift and a unitary clock in a source-fixing factorial metric. Its remaining angle coefficient is explicit. It has EXTRA factorial powers, so this does not yet prove the requested reduction to one half-density angle cell or a sharp arbitrary-prefix energy estimate. The actual remaining charge and operator, rather than an unspecified boundary current, are identified in (9)--(12). ## 1. Complete source modules and the physical terminal Use the original principal root N>=2,d=N-1,q=exp(pi*i/N),Q=q^2, x=q^d=-q^-1,F_a=(Q;Q)_a,s_a=|F_a|,kappa=q^(d^2/2). All crossings and turns are literal original physical ones from [the complete source module](actual_complete_source_multiplicity_module.md). In particular ell|a,b>=x^(-a)Q^(-a)/N delta_(a+b,d), p_(a,b)=N x^(-b)delta_(a+b,d). Let W_2=(V^tensor4)_(degree2d), W_1=(V^tensor2)_(degree d), L_0=ell_12 tensor I_34:W_2->W_1. Let I_w:V->V^tensor5 be the COMPLETE intertwiner of w in W_2, and D_2 w=I_w|d>. Define the six-head-source terminal rows by T_n^(6)=(ell_12 ell_34 tensor <d|_5) (I_123 tensor R_45^2) Pi_(4,n) D_2. The last marked cap has already been justified through the whole invariant-tensor source; it is not individually replaced by ell. Let T_n^(4) be the corresponding original three-physical-head terminal on W_1 from [the positive terminal packet](actual_terminal_packet_positive_gram.md). Since the cap ell_12 is a Hopf map, deleting it commutes with every prefix coproduct in the highest/lowest intertwiner. In particular (ell_12 tensor I_345)I_w=I_(L_0 w). It also commutes with the specific terminal R_45^2 and Pi_(4,n). Consequently, for EVERY input column and every adjoining exterior, T_n^(6)=T_n^(4)L_0. (1) Now place ONE actual adjacent signed bridge crossing R_23^epsilon immediately before that terminal. It acts on the middle two physical heads of W_2, so define L_epsilon=L_0 R_23^epsilon:W_2->W_1. The complete source identity becomes T_n^(6) R_23^epsilon=T_n^(4)L_epsilon. (2) This keeps the crossing that couples the eliminated cap to the remaining port. It is not commuted past the cap as an unknown scalar. ## 2. Every entry of the positive open bridge, with the original phases Take an input |a,b,c,e> of integer degree2d. For epsilon=+1 the cap forces the actual transfer and surviving output to be k=d-a-c, u=b-k, output |u,e>, u+e=d, 0<=k<=min(b,d-c). (3) There is exactly ONE original positive crossing coefficient, so (L_+)_(u;(a,b,c,e)) =kappa/N x^(-a-b-c+k)Q^(-a+cu) F_(d-a)F_b/(F_k F_c F_u), (4) with zero outside (3). This follows directly by multiplying the cap with the literal R coefficient. In particular the original common Cartan kappa and cap1/N have not been discarded. The true nonnegative angle charges are a+c+k=d. (5) The through-head relation b=u+k is a SECOND actual constraint; the spectator is e=d-u. Thus the external through degree has not been frozen independently of the angle charge k. Root reflection F_aF_(d-a)=N(-1)^aQ^[a(a+1)/2] rewrites (4) as a phase times F_b/(F_a F_c F_k F_u). This is a closed finite kernel, not a sum of absolute paths. Tensoring an arbitrary spectator space leaves (2)--(5) unchanged. If the input entries are matrices on that space, they multiply this kernel in their original order. No commutation of spectator operators is used. ## 3. The negative bridge and its retained complement charges For epsilon=-1 the literal negative crossing instead forces k=a+c-d, u=b+k, output |u,e>, u+e=d, 0<=k<=min(c,d-b). Its exact full coefficient is (L_-)_(u;(a,b,c,e)) =kappa^(-1)/N (-1)^k x^(b+c-k-a) Q^[-bc-ck+k(k-1)/2-a] F_u F_c/(F_k F_b F_(d-a)). (6) If A=d-a and C=d-c, its nonnegative charges are A+C+k=d, b=u-k. (7) Equations (6)--(7), including their phase, are the actual negative source kernel. They are not obtained by deleting an end channel or assuming a scalar beta identity for noncommuting ports. ## 4. The full feedback is a contractive physical current in a typed metric Use the PHYSICAL diagonal coordinate gauge G_a=s_a/sqrt(N)=L_a^(1/2), tau_a=F_a/s_a. It fixes every original paired cup and ordinary cap because G_aG_(d-a)=1. The full marked source is transported literally; on the assembled invariant source its complementary-degree restriction is the one already proved in the complete module. This is not the different quarter physical gauge or length gauge. For the POSITIVE bridge conjugate input and output heads by G. On the total-degree slices the output pair is complementary, so its product gauge is one. Equation (4) factors EXACTLY as Lhat_+ entry=gamma_(a,c,k) U_(c,k)[u,b], gamma_(a,c,k) =kappa N (-1)^a x^(-d+k) Q^[a(a-1)/2] /(s_a s_c F_a F_c F_k), U_(c,k)|b>=1_(b>=k) x^(-u)Q^(cu) tau_b/tau_u |u>, u=b-k. (8) Every nonzero coefficient of U is a UNIT PHASE and different inputs have different outputs. Hence ||U_(c,k)||_op=1 for k<N. More intrinsically it is the literal strict lowering current G(F^T)^kG^-1, followed by the unitary clock x^(-J)Q^(cJ). The condition u+e=d is a final orthogonal degree projector on the retained head and its untouched spectator; its norm is1. For the NEGATIVE bridge use the dual source-fixing gauge G^-1. With A,C as in (7), its exact factorization is Lhat_- entry=gamma^-_(A,C,k) U^-_(c,k)[u,b], gamma^-_(A,C,k)=kappa^(-1)N(-1)^(k+C)x^(A-C-2k) Q^[C(C+1)/2+k(k-1)/2-a] /(s_A s_C F_A F_C F_k), U^-_(c,k)|b>=1_(b+k<N) x^u Q^(-cu) tau_u/tau_b |u>, u=b+k. (9) This is a unitary clock times the contractive strict raising G^-1 F^k G. No cyclic wrap or transfer alias is added. These typed gauges both fix the original paired turns, but they are different: changing between them across a later overlap retains the actual G^2 interface. It is not declared polynomial. ## 5. What remains after one exact bridge elimination Both scalar factors have the same known magnitude on their actual angle triple, denoted (A,C,k) in the signed typed coordinates: |gamma|=N/(s_A^2 s_C^2 s_k). (10) Thus feedback has been isolated as a contractive operator rather than estimated by an arbitrary exterior norm. But the scalar energy is NOT the single half-density-cell weight w_d(A,C,k): |gamma|^2=N^2/(s_A^4 s_C^4 s_k^2). The extra factorial powers are genuine in the exact kernel. They must be grouped coherently with the subsequent T packet or another physical boundary contraction. Deleting them would change (4),(6). This identifies the specific missing angle-energy comparison; it does not rule out such a further coherent contraction. For completeness the entire open bridge has an exact row Gram in these typed source metrics. Rows have disjoint spectator color e. Therefore Lhat_+ Lhat_+^*=diag(E_+(u)), E_+(u)=N^2 sum_(k=0)^(d-u) s_k^(-2) sum_(A+C=d-k) s_A^(-4)s_C^(-4), E_-(u)=E_+(d-u). (11) Equation (11) retains the actual restriction k<=d-u, or k<=u in the negative orientation. It is not replaced by independent unconstrained tetrahedra or by an ideal-edge angle equation. Most importantly (2) remains the COHERENT composition, so its pointed doubled energy for any vector- or operator-valued input is sum_n ||T_n^(4)L_epsilon w||^2. (12) No diagonal sum of |gamma|^2 paths has been inserted into (12). The [closed all-input terminal kernel](actual_terminal_packet_closed_kernel.md) now makes this remaining operator explicit: each six-head entry is T_(n,u) times (4) or (6), with u=b-k or b+k and u=d-e.
