General physical columns and endpoint phases Put d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d=-q^-1, F_r=(Q;Q)_r and s_r=|F_r|. For 0<=j<=floor(d/2), let h=d-j and H^(j)_a=q^(a^2)[h choose a]_Q at |a,h-a>, W^(j)_r=F_pair^r H^(j)/F_r, 0<=r<=2j. (1) These are the original balanced physical pair and its original ordered coproduct. The highest equation follows directly from H_(a+1)/H_a=-x^-1 Q^a(1-Q^(h-a))/(1-Q^(a+1)). For a+b=h+r, their finite binomial expansion is W_r(a,b)=F_a F_b F_h *sum_s q^(s^2)x^(-r+a-s)Q^[s(r-a+s)] /[F_s^2 F_(h-s)^2 F_(a-s) F_(r-a+s)], (2) where max(0,a-r)<=s<=min(h,a). All denominators have index<N. This follows by expanding F_pair=A+B with AB=Q^-1 BA, just as in the [central proof](actual_trivalent_steinberg_central_anchor.md). The exact endpoints at EVERY retained j are W_(2j)(j+t,d-t)=ell_j H_t, 0<=t<=h, ell_j=q^[j(d-2j)], W_j(0,d)=q^(-j^2). (3) For the first, its lowest-vector recurrence fixes the successive ratios; the first coefficient in (2) is q^(-j^2) sum_s Q^(s^2)[h choose s]_Q[j choose s]_Q =q^(-j^2) F_d/(F_h F_j)=q^[j(d-2j)]. The equality in the middle is finite Vandermonde, proved by coefficient extraction in the finite binomial product. Root reflection gives F_h F_j=N(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)] and F_d=N. The last expression in (3) comes from the sole s=0 term of (2). The displayed lowest column also has zero next F arrow by its literal ratio; no generic semisimple decomposition is assumed. ## 2. The corner of the actual black tensor Choose j_1=a, j_2=b, j_3=c with the triangle inequalities and let r=b+c-a. The magnetic indices (2a,r,0) have physical pair degrees (d+a, d-a+c, d-c), whose sum is exactly 3d. Apply the three rows W^dagger P to the original nested cup source p_16 p_23 p_45. Its corner is N^3 A_N, where the exact original-source kernel gives A_N=conjugate(ell_a) sum_(k=0)^min(d-a,d-c) x^(k+a+c-2d) conjugate[H^(a)_k H^(c)_k W^(b)_r(c+k,d-a-k)]. (4) Indeed set the first physical cup color to d-k in the literal [black vertex kernel](actual_trivalent_complete_circle_vertex_kernel.md). Its other two colors are a+k and c+k. Formula (3) then gives (4), including the conjugate lowest-column scalar. The positive evaluation below is proved by the separate finite transformations linked above. ## 3. Precisely normalized positive evaluation Set J=a+b+c and delta=J-d. For delta>=0 define R_N=N sum_(max(a,b,c)<=t<=min(a+b,a+c,b+c)) s_t/[s_(t-a)s_(t-b)s_(t-c)s_(d+t-J) s_(a+b-t)s_(a+c-t)s_(b+c-t)], C_N=s_a s_b s_c/(N s_delta), e=2a^2-ab-ac+bc-J-3. (5) The proved original-source identity is A_N=(-1)^(N+J) q^e C_N R_N, J>=d; A_N=0, J<d. (6) The zero branch is now proved independently by the [root-Fourier coefficient theorem](actual_trivalent_root_fourier_source_certificate.md): the actual scalar is a specified coefficient of degree d in a polynomial of degree J. That proof keeps the complete Fourier mode and its exact low-mode cancellation. The two finite transformations linked above prove the positive branch, its exact phase, and every root denominator. The asymmetry of e belongs to the specified ordered corner (2a,r,0). The positive modulus C_N R_N is symmetric. Neither C_N nor the support cutoff may be suppressed. For example the unnormalized candidate has R_N(0,0,0)=1 whereas the original source is zero, and at even N=4, a=b=c=1 one has R_N=2sqrt(2), C_N=1/sqrt(2), |A_N|=2. At odd N=2m+1, (a,b,c)=(m,j,m), C_N=1 and (6) reduces to the [proved one-channel formula](actual_trivalent_one_channel_source_packet.md). At the even nearest center a=b=c=N/2-1, C_N=cos(pi/N), consistent with the separately proved [weighted quartic and retained normal](actual_trivalent_even_central_normal_packet.md). The [joint scalar saddle theorem](actual_trivalent_candidate_racah_partition_geometry.md) proves a unique joint saddle, a strict global color gap, and a complex packet for the positive expression in (5). Through the proved (6), these are now original-source SCALAR estimates. The complete CD normalization, the magnetic tensor, ordinary/marked white rows and their ordered sewing are additional data. ## 4. Exact checks and their logical limit The [independent finite-source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_trivalent_general_scalar_candidate.py) builds W from the ORIGINAL coproduct, instead of (2) or (5), and evaluates the literal source corner. It checks every retained triangle triple at N=2,...,16: 539 supported triples and 1,212 vanishing triples, including all root phases and both parities. It also checks (3) at every retained j in those levels. A separate high-precision calculation checked the full complex phase and modulus on all 636 triangle triples at N=2,...,13; an additional 305 supported triples at N=11,13,17 were used to determine and check the candidate phase modulo N. These computations supply reproducible counterexample searches and normalization evidence. They do not by themselves prove the positive branch of (6) for arbitrary N. That proof is the finite algebra linked above, with an independent derivation and internal analytical reviews; it is not an assumed literature identity.

title: Every original crossing has a two-Newton, one-Rogers source layer
text: # Every original crossing has a two-Newton, one-Rogers source layer 28 October 2026. The nine original scalar atoms admit a complete partition into three disjoint trivalent sinks. Two sinks are the PROVED Newton/Barnes template; the third is its actual all-U Rogers polynomial. A positive Gaussian must first be combined with its adjacent reciprocal factorial. A negative Gaussian stays ONCE and is shared by its indicated Newton and Rogers variables. This yields an exact one-internal-variable crossing kernel WITH its original final nonnegative Hardy barrier, then a simultaneous layer on any signed word and any bridge count. Each Newton kernel can be replaced by its explicit two-full-Psi source plus its retained central current. No positive-factorial edge, Gaussian or original cap is used twice. The resulting current branches are not classified as geometric degeneracies. ## 1. Fixed kernels and original normalization Put Q=exp(2pi*i/N), d=N-1, F_a=(Q;Q)_a and p_a=(-1)^a Q^(a(a-1)/2)/F_a, U(t)=sum_(a=0)^d t^a/F_a, V(t)=sum_(a=0)^d p_a t^a, F(t)=sum_(a=0)^d F_a t^a. These finite expressions are used to prove the source identity. Their original full-Psi coefficient/relative-cycle realizations may be reinserted exactly; they are not replaced by a new positive invariant. Keep the original color x, not only its complete value. Define B_N(u,v)=sum_(i+j<N) F_(i+j)/F_i *p_j u^i v^j, R_N(u,v)=sum_(i+j<N) F_(i+j)/(F_iF_j) u^i v^j. (1) B_N is the proved Newton polynomial. R_N is the actual truncated Rogers--Szego generating kernel; it is not assumed to satisfy the same beta theorem. All factorial normalization is already contained in the coefficients in (1). No residual N^3 is to be inserted after the three original factorials have been contracted this way. Let the two input variables of one crossing be z_0,z_1 and its outputs z_6,z_7. The four original internal head vertices after Hardy-forest contraction are z_2,z_3,z_4,z_5. Write t=z_4. The original external Cartan scalar kappa remains external. Write Pi_+^(6) for the original nonnegative Hardy projection on the first OUTPUT variable z_6. It is independent of N. This barrier is retained in the physical crossing and in every separated branch below. ## 2. Literal nine-atom table, including the Gaussian placement The original atom slots, in traversal order, are as follows. The table displays the finite coefficient kernels; every F carries its actual factorial support. | Slot | Positive crossing | Negative crossing | | --- | --- | --- | | 0 | U(z_2/z_1) | same | | 1 | V(x^(-1)z_2/z_0) | same | | 2 | U(z_3/z_0) | same | | 3 | F(t/z_2) | same | | 4 | U(x^(-1)z_3/t) | V(g_- x^(-1)z_3/t) | | 5 | U(g_+ z_5/t) | U(g_- z_5/t) | | 6 | F(z_6/z_3) | same | | 7 | U(x^(-1)z_5/z_6) | same | | 8 | F(z_7/z_5) | same | Here a Gaussian is still represented by its ORIGINAL moment g_s=-x^(-2s)exp(-s h/2)exp(sqrt(pi)(1+i s)xi), sqrt(N/(2pi))exp(-Nxi^2/2)d xi, h=2pi*i/N, s=+1 or -1. (2) The original diagonal entries are d_a=(-1)^a x^(-2a)Q^(a(a-1)/2). For R_+ the active Gaussian index is the slot-5 reciprocal index h_5, hence its full exponent is g_+^(h_5). For R_- the Gaussian precedes the central transfer; the index is h_5+h_4, hence the two displayed g_- factors are the SAME Gaussian variable. This is a literal gate-order calculation, not two independently integrated Gaussians. The four internal affine vertex equations are h_0+h_1+h_3=d, h_2+h_4+h_6=d, h_3+h_4+h_5=d, h_5+h_7+h_8=d. (3) The first, second and fourth are sinks. Their atomic stars {0,1,3}, {2,4,6}, {5,7,8} are PAIRWISE DISJOINT and partition ALL nine atoms. The third equation is at the remaining source vertex t; its integration is retained. The table follows either by coefficient conservation in the strict original word or by weighted Hardy-forest residues. At the Gaussian edge z_out=z_in/g_s, logarithmic residue measure has no extra g_s Jacobian. This gives precisely the two placements in the table. Its original caps are unchanged. ## 3. Positive crossing: absorb one COMPLETE Gaussian cell In the positive word C D U_+ C^(-1), the Gaussian D is adjacent to the reciprocal second-head factorial in C. Their exact combined diagonal coefficient is d_a/F_a=p_a x^(-2a). (4) Thus the COMPLETE Gaussian-plus-slot-5 cell is exactly V(x^(-2)z_5/t). It has no remaining Gaussian variable or extra scalar. One first contracts that whole Gaussian cell, then uses the Newton identity. It is not a pointwise deletion of g_+ in an arbitrarily separated full-Psi sector. Contract the three disjoint sinks in (3). The guaranteed first star {0,1,3} gives B_N(t/z_1,x^(-1)t/z_0). The last star {5,7,8}, after (4), gives B_N(x^(-1)z_7/z_6,x^(-2)z_7/t). The middle star is R_N(z_6/z_0,x^(-1)z_6/t). Consequently the ENTIRE raw positive crossing kernel is Ktilde_+=kappa CT_t [ B_N(t/z_1,x^(-1)t/z_0) R_N(z_6/z_0,x^(-1)z_6/t) B_N(x^(-1)z_7/z_6,x^(-2)z_7/t)]. (5) On the ORIGINAL finite input heads, the PHYSICAL finite-head crossing is K_+=Pi_+^(6) Ktilde_+. All upper support and second-output lower support are already enforced by the three factors; only negative first-output tails remain in the raw expression. In particular the all-U middle star was not renamed Newton. The original Gaussian is accounted for by the exact identity (4), including its color x^(-2a) and linear root phase. ## 4. Negative crossing: one shared Gaussian, not two For the negative crossing, stars {0,1,3} and {2,4,6} have the original U,V,F types and give Newton kernels directly. The last star is all-U and gives the Rogers polynomial. The exact raw negative kernel is Ktilde_-=kappa^(-1)sqrt(N/(2pi))integral_R exp(-Nxi^2/2) CT_t [ B_N(t/z_1,x^(-1)t/z_0) B_N(z_6/z_0,g_-x^(-1)z_6/t) R_N(g_-z_7/t,x^(-1)z_7/z_6)] dxi. (6) On those same finite input heads, K_-=Pi_+^(6) Ktilde_-. For example the raw kernels, on input (0,0), have a nonzero output (-1,1) from h_7=1, with coefficient kappa^(+/-1)x^(-1). The final original Hardy barrier removes it. Thus (5)--(6) are not asserted entrywise finite-head operators without that barrier. The two appearances of g_- are linked by the SINGLE Gaussian measure (2). Keeping only one or integrating each independently changes the original phase. No remaining Rogers sink is declared a Newton move without a further proved transformation. One finite coefficient proof checks (5)--(6) directly. On an input (a,b), put h_1=j, h_2=a-j, h_5=b+j-h_4 and output (c,e)=(h_2+h_4-h_7,h_5+h_7). The first Newton coefficient is F_(b+j)/F_b *p_j x^(-j). The second chosen Newton and the Rogers factor supply exactly the remaining original F and reciprocal F coefficients. Their Gaussian powers are h_5 for the positive crossing before (4), and h_5+h_4 for the negative crossing. Illegal original indices have zero coefficient. This proves the entire matrix equality, not merely a scalar cap evaluation. ## 5. Simultaneous exact layer on an arbitrary original word For m signed crossings, select the TWO Newton stars specified in (5) or (6) at each crossing. They are disjoint inside each crossing and occur at distinct internal sink vertices in the original ordered word. Spectator/Hardy contractions cannot merge one of these sinks with a later crossing: it has only its three atomic incidences and its affine charge -d. Thus there are exactly 2m independent Newton contractions, one remaining Rogers polynomial and one remaining internal t variable per crossing. Every F edge is used exactly once. Perform the positive Gaussian contraction (4) before expanding any new beta sectors. Retain one Gaussian per negative crossing. Glue the output and input head variables with the SAME original Hardy/source identifications and pair with the SAME original cups, ordinary caps, full marked cap, and external peripheral/framing line. Equations (5)--(6) then give the original whole period. This is valid for any bridge count and the whole original nonzero color x family at the fixed physical root. At each chosen Newton sink use its exact original-source identity B_N(u,v)=S_N(u,v)+D_N(u,v)I_N(u,v), D_N=1-u^N+v^N, S_N=(N/phi_N)u^N Psi_+(h-Logu)Psi_+(Log(v/u)) exp[-Log(v/u)Logu/h]. (7) This is the [proved beta source](actual_trivalent_quantum_beta_source.md) with the [exact Fermat normalizer](exact_balanced_source_normalizer_fermat.md), not bare replacement of a factorial coefficient by its symbol. Multilinearity gives at most 2^(2m)=4^m source branches, with all Rogers kernels, remaining Gaussians and original caps retained. Expanding each D into its three monomials would give at most 4^(2m) terms; keeping it grouped is preferable. The number depends on the word, not N. The branches live on specified logarithmic/relative source charts. They need not be separately single-valued scalar periods or independently absolutely integrable on an uncontinued original torus. Start on a common regular marked chart, use (7), and continue with its exact beta currents. Equivalently use common finite Gaussian cutoffs and matched pole indentations BEFORE summing the branches. Their sum is the original finite polynomial integrand, so its limiting period is fixed by the original absolute convergence theorem. No independent finite part is chosen for one branch alone. The joint deck/source gluing is part of the retained source extension; deleting current sectors would destroy it. Thus this is an exact finite-branch whole-source NORMAL FORM. It is not a proof of termwise global growth estimates or of dominance of the all-S branch. There is an optional whole-source reduction of the last Hardy barrier, but it has a different scope. The COMPLETE raw B/R kernel has only nonnegative incoming index demands, so it annihilates any negative input head. Its only unphysical output is a negative first head. The next crossing touching that head annihilates it; if no crossing touches it again, the original finite final source annihilates it. Therefore the raw complete crossings give the same whole-word source after summing their complete finite kernels. This no-healing argument must NOT be applied separately to the meromorphic S/I branches. The displayed branch normal form retains Pi_+^(6), unless that full-word source reduction has first been performed before splitting. ## 6. What the actual central monomials do For the guaranteed first star the literal central function is A=u^N-v^N=t^N[z_1^(-N)-x^(-N)z_0^(-N)]. (8) It is a free scalar boundary function, not identically zero or one. At the other positive star it is A_F=x^(-N)z_7^N/z_6^N-x^(-2N)z_7^N/t^N, and at the negative central star it is A_C=z_6^N/z_0^N-g_-^N x^(-N)z_6^N/t^N. (9) The original peripheral x^N and the Gaussian norm g_-^N remain. They cannot be evaluated at an ideal point before normal source operations. A separately chosen cyclic boundary-character extension with z_1^N=x^N z_0^N would make (8) zero, but that is not a specialization theorem for the original finite-head scalar source. There IS an exact finite-input support statement. The original inverse fusion kernel after the first contraction is U(z_3/z_0)B_N(t/z_1,x^(-1)t/z_0). (10) Its monomial indexed by i,j,r has incoming exponents (r+j,i) and outgoing (r,i+j), with i+j<N. Multiplication by u^N demands incoming second index i+N; multiplication by v^N demands incoming first index r+j+N. Both are outside the original head. Therefore each inserted WHOLE-kernel tail in (10) is zero on every original finite-head input. This holds before closing a knot, for every original color. It is a degree-tail annihilation, not a scalar value A=0 assigned inside (7). The separated full-Psi and Barnes kernels are not finite nonnegative head polynomials. They do not inherit this support assertion termwise. The exact constraint after splitting is instead the equal-sum statement exterior[A S_N]+exterior[A D_N I_N]=0, (11) whenever the indicated original finite-head exterior is used. It is invalid to set A=0 in a generic inverse norm or to conclude from (11) that each current vanishes. Inputs outside the original head already detect the nonzero degree shifts. Likewise the current monomials do not force a degenerate Hurwitz representation. On any regular logarithmic current branch they add to its action respectively 0, 2pi*i(Logt-Logz_1), 2pi*i(Logt-Logz_0-Logx). (12) Their logarithmic momenta change by integer 2pi*i shifts, while their EXPONENTIATED canonical relation is unchanged. Thus they are lifted charge/degree corrections to whatever regular current graph is present, not automatic identity or rank-deficient classical maps. The known full-Psi deck mixing can put the same growing S class into I, so a current-only quotient cannot be imposed without transporting this source extension. ## 7. Audit and remaining obligation Run python3 experiments/audit_actual_trivalent_layer_crossing_source.py The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_trivalent_layer_crossing_source.py) checks the exact inverse-fusion kernel, both original signed/color crossings, two arbitrary Gaussian dilation values before moment contraction, the positive complete-cell identity, whole original pivotal word sources, the disjoint graph partition and the full-B degree-tail assertion. All original normalization factors are read from the independent original crossing evaluator. To reach a global volume theorem one still needs to control the remaining Rogers fibers and the combined marked source branches, and show a nonzero geometric exterior coefficient or a suitable global norm gap. Positivity of a single local bipyramid does not give that gap, as the explicit original-source nongrowth chamber already demonstrates. The normal form above states exactly the actual network and currents to which such a proof must apply.

title: Whole-label asymptotic of the original signed marked theta source
text: # Whole-label asymptotic of the original signed marked theta source 29 October 2026. The exact coherent magnetic contraction in the [all-channel marked theorem](actual_trivalent_all_channel_marked_contraction.md) gives a sharp positive partition before any estimate. This note proves its entire-label gap and the nonzero Gaussian asymptotic after ANY fixed signed twists on its three original pair edges. Both parities, the odd simple endpoint weight, paired-circle first normals and the sole physical marked normal are retained. No complement geometry or arbitrary graph sewing theorem is inferred. ## 1. Actual raw source and the theorem Set N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, kappa=q^(d^2/2), m=d/2, M=floor(m), and s_u=product_(r=1)^u 2sin(pi r/N). For physical folded labels 0<=j_i<=M put J=sum j_i, delta=J-d, and r_i=J-2j_i. Let k_j=2 except at the odd simple node j=m, where k_j=1. The EXACT marked raw channel contribution is Z_N(j)=N^2 product_i k_(j_i) *[product_i s_(r_i)/s_delta] R_N(j)^2, J>=d, Z_N(j)=0, J<d. (1) Here R_N is the proved finite factorial partition. Formula (1) has already summed EVERY magnetic index with the genuine ordinary white dual and original unrestricted physical marked row. It is not the black tensor's Euclidean norm. There is no outside component normalization in this raw source. Insert the original R^(e_i)L_N on edge i, for arbitrary FIXED signed integers e_1,e_2,e_3. The raw whole source is exactly Theta_N(e)=sum_j Z_N(j) product_i omega_(j_i)^(e_i), omega_j=kappa(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)]. (2) This includes the full original Cartan scalar. A separately recorded external line factor chi_N remains outside Theta_N. Put j0=v8/pi=8 Lambda(pi/4)/pi and define the literal unit phase Omega_N=kappa exp(i pi d/2) q^[m(m+1)] (-1)^d, q^r means exp(i pi r/N), including fractional r. Then Theta_N(e)=N^(3/2) exp(2N j0) Omega_N^(e_1+e_2+e_3) /[16 product_i sqrt(2-i e_i)] *[1+O_e(1/N)]. (3) EACH square root has positive real part. Equivalently choose the determinant square root by continuation from e=0. The principal square root of the product can have the WRONG SIGN for large same-sign twists, for example e=(5,7,9). The leading constant in (3) is nonzero. Thus for both parities and composite levels lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|Theta_N(e)|=4v8. (4) This is an actual source limit. It is not a claim that its complement has volume 4v8 absent a separate literal topological certificate. ## 2. A whole-label strictly concave action Let L(x)=integral_0^x log(2sin pi u)du and set sigma_i=(m-j_i)/N, x_i=1/4+sigma_i-(sum sigma)/2, i=1,2,3, x_4=1/4+(sum sigma)/2. The physical supported set has sigma_i>=0, sum sigma_i<=m/N; all four x_i lie in (0,1/2) and sum x_i=1. On the compact limiting support the endpoints are included by continuity. The established scalar partition has rate Phi=-(2)sum_(i=1)^4 L(x_i). Its extra weight in (1) has rate sum_(i<=3)L(2x_i)-L(1-2x_4)=sum_(i<=4)L(2x_i). Consequently the complete channel contribution has action E(sigma)=sum_(i=1)^4[L(2x_i)-4L(x_i)] =sum_(i=1)^4 h(x_i), h(x)=-2[L(x)+L(1/2-x)]. (5) The last equality follows from the elementary duplication and reflection identities for L. DIRECTLY h(1/2-x)=h(x), h''(x)=-4pi/sin(2pi x)<0, 0<x<1/2. (6) Hence h is strictly concave, with unique maximum at x=1/4. Equation (5) has its UNIQUE maximum at sigma=0, with E(0)=2j0, Hess_sigma E(0)=-4pi I_3. (7) The four tetrahedral sign rows mapping sigma/2 to x-1/4 have orthonormal columns. Flipping ANY one sigma_i takes that row set to the negatives of a permutation of itself. Together with (6) this proves E is SEPARATELY EVEN in every sigma_i, not merely stationary at zero. In particular E(sigma)=2j0-2pi sum sigma_i^2+O(||sigma||^4). (8) The uniform all-index O(log N) sine-factorial estimate, including zero indices, and the at-most-N inner R sum give log[Z_N(j)/product_i k_(j_i)]=N E(sigma)+O(log N) (9) uniformly on the ENTIRE supported physical set. The actual half-step in m only changes this global estimate by O(log N). All forbidden labels contribute zero exactly. By compactness and strictness of (7), for every fixed rho>0 there is gamma_rho>0 such that sum_(max sigma_i>=rho) Z_N(j) <=poly(N)exp[N(2j0-gamma_rho)]. (10) Thus a complete physical-label complement is exponentially small. Since every physical twist in (2) has modulus one, the SAME bound controls the signed source complement before any cancellation. ## 3. Uniform local prefactor, including the three half-steps The exact complex scalar partition theorem gives, uniformly on a fixed small sigma polydisk, Rwin_N=N^(-3/2)exp(NPhi) /[4sqrt(product_i cos(pi sigma_i))]*(1+O(1/N)). Its actual physical omitted terms have a strict gap. The remaining sine factors in (1) have indices r_i=2N x_i-1/2, delta=N(1-2x_4)-1/2. The canonical half-shifted factorial formula S_hat_N(Na-1/2)=sqrt(N)exp[NL(a)](1+O(1/N)) therefore gives product_i s_(r_i)/s_delta =N exp{N sum_(i=1)^4 L(2x_i)}*(1+O(1/N)). The N^2 in (1), this N, and Rwin_N^2's N^-3 cancel EXACTLY. Thus locally on the physical lattice Z_N(j)=product_i k_(j_i) *exp[N E(sigma)]/[16 product_i cos(pi sigma_i)] *(1+O(1/N)). (11) The error is uniform on a fixed corridor. On a smaller corridor, real coercivity E<=2j0-c||sigma||^2 holds. The known exact complex factorial window also gives bounded fixed derivatives, but no off-grid identification with auxiliary meridians is needed here. ## 4. Exact signed twist chirp and parity unfolding At EVERY physical folded label, omega_j=Omega_N exp(i pi N sigma^2). (12) Indeed j=m-Nsigma and 2m+1=N. Writing (-1)^j=exp(pi i j), the q exponent difference between the two sides of (12) is -2N(d-j), an integer multiple of 2N. This proves (12) with its literal fractional root, not an arbitrary choice of sqrt(kappa). If N is odd, Nsigma is an integer >=0 and the zero point has weight one while every positive point has weight two. If N is even, Nsigma lies in Z+1/2, is positive, and every point has weight two. Thus the k_j weights unfold any EVEN leading integrand EXACTLY to the full integer respectively half-integer lattice. Their product unfolds all three directions. The supported simplex boundary is a fixed distance from zero, so extending the local Gaussian lattice to infinity has an exponential error. Insert (8),(11),(12) into (2). Quartic action errors contribute relative O(1/N) after absolute Gaussian integration, because N||sigma||^4 has Gaussian mean O(1/N). The even amplitude's error is O(||sigma||^2), with the same O(1/N) expectation. Uniform factorial errors in (11) are O(1/N) already. The fixed signed chirp has modulus one on the real grid, so these absolute error estimates remain valid. Equation (10) controls the rest of the original sum. For A_i=2-i e_i, Re A_i=2. The one-dimensional exact Gaussian Poisson identity gives, with epsilon=0 or 1/2, sum_(h in Z+epsilon) exp[-pi A_i h^2/N] =sqrt(N)/sqrt(A_i) *sum_(ell in Z)exp[-pi N ell^2/A_i]exp(2pi i ell epsilon). Its nonzero Fourier modes are exponentially small because Re(1/A_i)=2/(4+e_i^2)>0. Multiply the three identities and the factor 1/16 from (11). This proves (3), including its nonzero phase, N^(3/2), both parity cosets and every fixed signed triple. No uniform assertion for twists growing with N is made. ## 5. Source and geometry scope The magnetic growth of an individual black vertex has been contracted COHERENTLY with the actual white/marked source before (1). This positive partition is specific to that two-vertex wiring. Formula (3) does not make arbitrary white vertices adjoints, does not bound an arbitrary branched graph in a tensor-product norm, and does not identify a spectral channel parameter with a peripheral color. Any hyperbolic-volume conclusion still needs the complement's separate literal geometric certificate and original external line. That separate certificate is now given in [the actual theta-link and angle geometry](actual_marked_theta_link_and_angle_geometry.md): the literal source is the three-box augmented pretzel matching, its complete complement has four regular ideal octahedra for every fixed signed e, and the original reduced one-cut external line has modulus one. Together with (3), it identifies (4) with the ACTUAL complement volume for that complete link family. It does not prove a filled-knot statement or general open-graph source factorization. Audit: [exact phases/folding and all-parity whole-label sums](../experiments/audit_actual_trivalent_marked_theta_label_asymptotic.py). Root's independent analytical review passed the whole-label action, strict gap, actual half-step prefactor, separate evenness, both parity folds, literal Omega_N and each Gaussian square-root branch, including the relative O_e(1/N) error. A fresh primary audit passed 4,159 exact rational root-phase checks, 127 exact parity-fold families, symbolic action identities and six complete-label families with 24 coherent signed profiles. The separately proved full-normal marked source identity is the input; numerical profiles supplement this proof.

title: An actual noncentral trivalent source packet with two Steinberg legs
text: # An actual noncentral trivalent source packet with two Steinberg legs 29 October 2026. The odd central quartic transform extends to EVERY retained node on one leg of the ORIGINAL black trivalent source, with the other two legs central. It gives an exact common-phase positive factorial sum, a fixed complex color packet, and a strict physical complement gap. This is one actual magnetic coefficient, not a replacement for the full three-channel vertex or its white/marked rows. Set N=2m+1>=3, d=2m, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, F_a=(Q;Q)_a and s_a=|F_a|. All indices are unwrapped. Original normalizations are those of the [full vertex kernel](actual_trivalent_complete_circle_vertex_kernel.md). ## 1. Actual source coefficient and exact positive evaluation For 0<=j<=m put t=d-j. In the ORIGINAL physical pair define h^(j)_a=q^(a^2)[t choose a]_Q at |a,t-a>, W^(j)_r=F_pair^r h^(j)/F_r, 0<=r<=2j. (1) The highest equation follows from the ratio -x^-1 Q^a(1-Q^(t-a))/(1-Q^(a+1)). Its Casimir is c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1). At physical degree d, W^(j)_j(a,d-a)=q^(-j^2) f_a(c_j). (2) Indeed both sides solve the same actual tridiagonal eigenvector recurrence, and the first entry of the coproduct binomial is N x^-j/(F_t F_j)=q^(-j^2). No inverse frame is used. Extract the black source rows (W^(m)_d,W^(j)_j,W^(m)_0), after the literal port exchanges of the full kernel. Their pair degrees are (3m,2m,m), summing to 3d. The actual coefficient is N^3 B_(N,j), where B_(N,j)=sum_(k=0)^m x^(k-d) conjugate[(h^(m)_k)^2 W^(j)_j(m+k,m-k)]. (3) Here the exact lowest-column identity W^(m)_d(m+k,d-k)=h^(m)_k was proved with all phases in the [central anchor](actual_trivalent_steinberg_central_anchor.md#2-exact-source-normalizations-including-both-ends). Thus (3) is an original source coefficient, not a chosen abstract 6j. Define z_j(k)=s_(j+k)/[s_(j-k)s_k^2], 0<=k<=j, z_m(k)=beta(m,k)^2=N/[s_k^2 s_(m-k)^2]. The exact all-node formula is B_(N,j)=q^[m(2-3m+2j)] P_(N,j), P_(N,j)=sum_(k=0)^j z_j(k)z_m(k)>0. (4) It includes j=0,m, every odd composite N, and recovers the central quartic at j=m. In the specified CD basis sqrt(N)W on the two central legs and sqrt(2N)f(c_j) on the middle leg, j<m, the coefficient is sqrt(2)N^(9/2)q^(-j^2)B_(N,j). At j=m it is N^(9/2)B_(N,m). The sqrt(2) is the actual double-node FIRST-normal multiplicity; one must not continue it through the odd simple node. ## 2. Own finite proof at every node Let J_0 denote the actual complete anti-Pascal recoupling, not the six-head cup. The [central proof](actual_trivalent_steinberg_central_anchor.md#4-a-finite-coherent-quartic-transform) established by finite binomial inversion (J_0)_(a,b)=x D_aD_b[a+b choose a]_(Q^-1), D_a=(-q^-1)^a, a+b<=d; zero otherwise, conjugate(J_0) P J_0=P. (5) The actual other Casimir is lower bidiagonal, with diagonal c_a and lower entry Q^a+Q^-a-2. Hence y_j=J_0 f(c_j) is REAL, supported at d-j,...,d, with (y_j)_(d-j+k) =s_(d-j)s_j/[s_(d-2j+k)s_k s_(j-k)^2]. (6) Its last entry is (J_0)_(d,0)=1. Solve the first-order recurrence backwards from there using (c_a-c_j)/[-(Q^a+Q^-a-2)] =-q^-1(1-Q^(a-j))(1-Q^(a+j+1))/(1-Q^a)^2. The second occurrence of c_j forces all earlier entries to zero. Root reflection F_aF_(d-a)=N(-1)^a Q^[a(a+1)/2] cancels every phase in (6). Reversal P y_j is exactly the vector z_j above. At this root z_j(i)=(-q)^i(Q^-j;Q)_i(Q^(j+1);Q)_i/F_i^2. For k<=j form C_(j,k)=sum_(i=k)^j z_j(i)D_i[i choose k]_(Q^-1). With n=j-k, its k-th term times the remaining series is (Q^-j;Q)_k(Q^(j+1);Q)_k/F_k^2 *sum_(r=0)^n (Q^-n;Q)_r(Q^(j+k+1);Q)_r Q^(-kr) /[F_r(Q^(k+1);Q)_r]. The SECOND finite q-Chu applies: b=Q^(j+k+1), c=Q^(k+1), and cQ^n/b=Q^-k. It is the own finite identity obtained from the first q-Chu at base Q^-1 by inverting parameters, as in the central proof. All denominator indices are <=j<N. Its product side simplifies to C_(j,k)=(-1)^j q^[k^2-j(j+1)]z_j(k). (7) Vandermonde in (5) now gives, for ANY j,l<=m, z_j^T J_0 z_l=x(-1)^(j+l)q^[-j(j+1)-l(l+1)] *sum_(k=0)^min(j,l)z_j(k)z_l(k). (8) To recover the actual source, (2),(3) and the phases of h^(m) give B_(N,j)=q^[j^2-4m^2] f(c_j)^dagger J_0 f(c_m). Since y_j,y_m are real, (5) rewrites this matrix element as z_j^T J_0 z_m. Equation (8) and q^N=-1 give precisely (4). This evaluates the coherent source BEFORE any absolute values. ## 3. Entire physical color bound and strict complement gap For k<=j<m, z_(j+1)(k)/z_j(k) =sin[pi(j+k+1)/N]/sin[pi(j-k+1)/N]>=1. (9) For k>0 the difference of these sines is 2cos[pi(j+1)/N]sin(pi k/N)>0. Therefore 1=P_(N,0)<=P_(N,j)<=P_(N,m), log P_(N,j)<=N j0+O(log N), j0=v8/pi. (10) For EVERY fixed delta>0 there is gamma_delta>0 such that max_(m-j>=delta N) P_(N,j) <=poly(N)exp[N(j0-gamma_delta)]. (11) Outside a fixed neighborhood of k/N=1/4 the central quartic terms already have a strict gap. Inside it, sum log(9) over a fixed subinterval between j/N and 1/2. Its continuous positive integral is uniformly bounded below when (m-j)/N>=delta. The uniform O(log N) sine-factorial estimate covers endpoints. This proves (11), with an empty physical range simply ignored. ## 4. Exact complex-color factorial packet Let S_hat_N be the [canonical sine factorial](exact_factorial_interpolation_and_complex_contours.md), with S_hat_N(a)=s_a and S_hat_N(z)S_hat_N(d-z)=N EXACTLY. Fix a small epsilon>0, I_N={k:|k/N-1/4|<=epsilon}, and set Pwin_N(sigma)=N sum_(k in I_N) S_hat_N(m-Nsigma+k) /[S_hat_N(m-Nsigma-k)s_k^4s_(m-k)^2]. (12) This is an EXACT holomorphic function on a fixed small complex sigma disk, with all scaled factorial arguments in a compact bulk strip. It is EXACTLY EVEN by reflection. At physical sigma=(m-j)/N it is exactly the retained terms of (4). Their omitted positive terms have a uniform exponential gap, also relative to the retained packet after shrinking the disk. The original source completion is q^[m(2-m)-2mN sigma]Pwin_N(sigma); at integral deficit s its extra character is (-1)^s q^s, which has NOT been deleted. Put J(t)=integral_0^t Log(2sin pi a)da on the marked bulk strip and F(t,sigma)=J(1/2-sigma+t)-J(1/2-sigma-t) -4J(t)-2J(1/2-t). (13) The canonical complex factorial expansion, including the actual half-step m/N=1/2-1/(2N), gives the summand in (12) as exp[NF(t,sigma)]/[4N^2 sin^2(pi t)] *[1+O(1/N)], (14) uniformly on a slightly larger complex t,sigma tube. The square root of the numerator/denominator sine ratio cancels the phase shift exp[-(G(1/2-sigma+t)-G(1/2-sigma-t))/2], G=J'. The remaining exp[G(1/2-t)]=2cos(pi t) cancels its denominator. Thus (14) has neither an unknown periodic multiplier nor a missing half-step constant. The unique real saddle continues holomorphically as t_*(sigma)=atan(cos pi sigma)/pi, A(sigma)=-F_tt(t_*,sigma) =2pi[1+cos^2(pi sigma)]^2/cos^3(pi sigma). For real small sigma, strict concavity follows directly from the cotangent derivatives in (13). Let Phi(sigma)=F(t_*,sigma). Then Phi(0)=j0, Phi'(sigma)=-2 artanh(sin pi sigma), Phi''(sigma)=-2pi/cos pi sigma, Phi(sigma)=j0-pi sigma^2+O(sigma^4). (15) The EXACT packet has the uniform COMPLEX asymptotic Pwin_N(sigma)=N^(-3/2) exp[NPhi(sigma)] /[4sqrt(cos pi sigma)] *[1+O(1/N)]. (16) Here sqrt is +1 at zero. For completeness, enclose I_N by half-grid vertical sides and horizontal sides of fixed small height b, using the exact kernel pi N cot(pi N t). The vertical sides have |cot|<=1 and retain the source endpoint currents; their phase has a strict window boundary gap. On horizontal sides the cotangent error is O(exp(-2pi N b)), whereas phase growth is <=Cb^2+C|sigma|^2b. Choose b first with Cb^2<pi b and then shrink the complex sigma disk. All these errors and the endpoint connectors are exponentially gapped. The main contours deform through t_* within the same zero-free factorial strip. Analytic Gaussian integration of (14) gives (16), since sqrt(2pi/A)/(4sin^2(pi t_*))=1/[4sqrt(cos pi sigma)]. This proves uniformity for the exact packet, not just its real-grid leading terms. Cauchy estimates keep every FIXED color derivative. In particular on smaller real/imaginary corridors, |Pwin_N(x+iy)|<=poly(N)exp[N(j0-cx^2+Cy^2)], c>0. (17) ## 5. Remaining branching interfaces The theorem concerns a genuine original black coefficient with two central legs. The double-node CD factor above has retained the first normal of the complete circle BEFORE its fixed-root image is taken. Equation (12) continues color in this coefficient; it does NOT take derivatives of a moving-q physical source germ. Here sigma is an INTERNAL pair-Casimir channel deficit. It has not been identified with an auxiliary meridian or an ordinary-circle color parameter; such an identification needs its own actual source and peripheral transport certificate. For three independently noncentral legs the actual kernel still has three distinct highest/descendant polynomials. The reduction to (8) used the two central legs essentially. One magnetic coefficient also does not bound all other T_i, or identify the distinct U,V,V_m. Paired socle columns have W^dagger P W=0, whereas the central column has W^dagger P W=I; its retraction cannot simply be continued. Those remain explicit interfaces before an arbitrary noncrossing triple-partition graph can be estimated by this positive packet. Audit: [literal source and all-node finite transform](../experiments/audit_actual_trivalent_one_channel_source_packet.py). Tests supplement the finite proof and contour estimate; no sewn-graph survival or new hyperbolic-volume claim is inferred from them. Independent internal analytical review passed the all-node finite transform, actual source phase, entire-color gap, half-step amplitude and exact complex-window contour argument. A fresh primary replay passed ten original all-node families N=3,...,21, three whole-color Laplace profiles and two canonical complex factorial windows.

title: An exact original trivalent beta cycle and its norm remainder
text: # An exact original trivalent beta cycle and its norm remainder 28 October 2026. The original balanced head equation at a trivalent vertex now has a specified one-dimensional relative source. Its finite convolution is an explicit Newton polynomial. A norm-corrected Barnes contour splits this polynomial into a NONZERO balanced residue block and an explicitly retained normalization term. The Barnes factor of that latter term is uniformly bounded on compact positive boundary families. No unknown knot coefficient or replaced invariant occurs. This is a local source theorem. The norm factor can have exponential size; the rate of the nonzero residue block and its comparison with that normalization term are separate. Nonvanishing of this block does not yet prove the global knot period selects it after all other boundary integrations. ## 1. The source and its exact finite polynomial Use the ORIGINAL full functions Psi_+, Psi_- from [the circle-and-boundary source theorem](actual_modular_dilog_circle_and_boundary_source.md). Put N>=2, d=N-1, h=2*pi*i/N and Q=exp h. Their coefficients through degree d are p_a=(-1)^a Q^(a(a-1)/2)/(Q;Q)_a, m_a=Q^a/(Q;Q)_a. After the exact reflection of the positive factorial order, the trivalent fiber field is precisely F_N(L;U,V)=r^d Psi_-(Log U-L) Psi_+(Log V-L)Psi_+(-L), r=exp L. (1) The graph incidence argument in [the bipyramid source note](positive_bipyramid_source_transport.md#4-the-original-source-law-checked-on-the-actual-reduced-graph) shows that its constant Laurent coefficient is the original complete source convolution, with all original boundary tags retained. The finite q-binomial calculation gives [r^0] F_N=(Q^(-d)/N) B_N(Q^2 U,Q V), B_N(u,v)=sum_(a=0)^d product_(j=0)^(a-1)(u-Q^j v). (2) The empty product is one. Thus u=Q^2 U, v=Q V and N Q^d are exact tags and normalization, not only their classical limits. The basic original-source recurrences are B_N(u,v)=(u-v)B_N(u,Qv)+D_N(u,v), v B_N(Qu,Qv)=(u-1)B_N(u,v)+D_N(u,v), D_N(u,v)=1-u^N+v^N. (3) The second follows by summing Q^a p_a=(u p_a-p_(a+1))/v for the Newton products p_a. Both endpoint terms are part of the source. ## 2. A single exact outer-Hankel current At large r, each full Psi in (1) has its first N ordinary coefficients plus O_N((1+|Log r|)|r|^(-N)). Therefore F_N is its ordinary Laurent polynomial down through the constant term plus O_N(log|r|/|r|), uniformly over a bounded logarithmic turn. Its generalized constant coefficient is consequently an actual limit of full lifted circles. Write M_N(r)=(r^N-V^N)(r^N-1)/[r^N(r^N-U^N)], C_N(R)=(1/(2*pi*i)) integral_(log R-i*pi)^(log R+i*pi) F_N(L)dL. For R initially larger than max(1,|U|,|V|), with the fixed logarithmic marks in (1), the EXACT source identity is [r^0]F_N=C_N(R)+(1/(2*pi*i)) integral_R^infinity [M_N(-s)-1]F_N(log s-i*pi) ds/s. (4) Indeed F_N(L+2*pi*i)=M_N(exp L)F_N(L). Apply Cauchy's theorem to the logarithmic rectangle log R<=Re L<=log S and let S increase to infinity. The circle's positive Laurent powers integrate to zero, and its remainder tends to zero. The outer integral converges because M_N(-s)-1=O_N(s^(-N)) and d=N-1. This identity is the simultaneous pushforward of the coefficient source. It carries all mixed original radial pieces; it is not a replacement by three bare circles. Subsequent contour continuation retains the poles and end faces it crosses. No unproved positive separating contour is assigned to (4). ## 3. A convergent Barnes contour with a variable central norm Consider the positive boundary chamber Im u<0, Im(v/u)>0. (5) Fix Log u with -pi<Arg u<0 and c=Log(v/u) with 0<Im c<pi. Their sum is the continuous logarithm of v, whose imaginary part lies strictly between -pi and pi. Choose 0<epsilon<1 with 2*pi*epsilon/N<Im c. Define g(a)=exp(a Log u) Psi_+(c)/Psi_+(c+h a), t=exp(2*pi*i*a), lambda(t)=u^N-v^N t, I_N(u,v)=integral_(-epsilon-i*infinity)^(-epsilon+i*infinity) g(a)/(exp(-2*pi*i*a)-1) da. (6) The line is oriented UPWARD. The exact full-Psi steps give g(n)=product_(j<n)(u-Q^j v), g(a+N)=[u^N-v^N exp(2*pi*i*a)]g(a). (7) The variable exponential in (7) is essential. A constant Floquet multiplier is true at integer samples only, and cannot be used in a complex contour argument. On the entire strip -epsilon<=Re a<=N-epsilon, the denominator Psi_+(c+h a) has no zeros: its argument has positive imaginary part, whereas the zeros of Psi_+ occur at nonpositive imaginary integer combinations of h and 2*pi*i. Thus g is holomorphic there. ## 4. Exact norm-pole residue transport Assume temporarily u^N!=1 and D_N!=0, and choose alpha with exp(2*pi*i*alpha)=(u^N-1)/v^N, -epsilon<Re alpha<1-epsilon, v_*=v exp(h alpha), so u^N-v_*^N=1. (8) Avoid parameters with a pole on the two chosen vertical sides; the result extends by continuation. Use the ORIGINAL sample-preserving norm-corrected differential omega=2*pi*i D_N t g(a) da/[(t-1)(1-lambda(t))]. (9) Its residues are g(n) at n=0,...,N-1 and -g(alpha+k) at alpha+k, k=0,...,N-1. At the latter points g(alpha+k)=g(alpha) product_(j<k)(u-Q^j v_*). The factor t in (9) is important BOTH for these residues and for the ends. For Im a tending to positive infinity it supplies the decay exp(-2*pi Im a). For Im a tending to negative infinity, the two denominator factors and this numerator leave the decay exp(-2*pi |Im a|), overcoming the full right-edge growth of g. The full-Phi horizontal asymptotics prove that the horizontal sides of the width-N rectangle tend to zero, uniformly in its real coordinate. On its two vertical sides, (7) gives omega(a+N)-omega(a) =2*pi*i D_N g(a)/(exp(-2*pi*i*a)-1) da. The residue theorem therefore proves the exact source-cycle identity B_N(u,v)=S_N(u,v)+D_N(u,v) I_N(u,v), S_N(u,v)=g(alpha) B_N(u,v_*). (10) All central norm factors are retained. The extra norm poles are not discarded: their complete balanced Fourier block is the first term. Changing alpha by an integer does not change S_N, by the balanced version of (3). Thus (10) is independent of the root/deck choice. The balanced block B_N(u,v_*) is nonzero if uv_*!=0. One elementary proof takes the discrete Fourier transform of the cyclic sequence p_k=product_(j<k)(u-Q^jv_*), for which p_N=p_0=1. Its Fourier components obey a first-order cyclic recurrence with all coefficients nonzero. No component, including their zero-frequency sum B_N, can vanish. This is a finite source statement, not an asymptotic argument. The other factors in S_N are nonzero in the stated chamber. At D_N=0, equation (10) extends directly and S_N=B_N is nonzero. At u^N=1 the norm pole escapes and must be checked separately. If u_0=Q^(-j) with its lower principal argument, the first nonzero coefficient of B_N(u_0,w) is b_j w^j, b_j!=0. This follows from (u_0 Q^k-1)b_k=Q^(k-1)b_(k-1) and its nonzero top coefficient. As u tends to u_0, v_*^j contributes [(u^N-1)/v^N]^(j/N), exactly cancelling the opposite power in exp(alpha Log u). Since Psi_+(c+h alpha) tends to one, the finite limit is Psi_+(c)b_j v^j!=0. This is a fixed-N collision calculation; no uniform collision asymptotic is assumed. Consequently S_N is nonzero throughout (5), after these specified removable continuations. ## 5. The Barnes normalization term is uniformly tame For every compact K inside (5), there are C_K and N_K such that |I_N(u,v)|<=C_K, (u,v) in K, N>=N_K. (11) This bound includes the norm collisions just described. To prove it, write a=-epsilon+i N y and x=v/u. The uniform actual full-Psi symbol on the entire selected strip gives the leading real exponent R_N(y)=-y Arg u+ Im[Li_2(x)-Li_2(x exp(-2*pi*i*epsilon/N-2*pi*y))]/(2*pi). Here N R_N(0)=O_K(1). Its EXACT leading derivative is R_N'(y)=-Arg u- Arg(1-x exp(-2*pi*i*epsilon/N-2*pi*y)). (12) It lies between -Arg u>0 and pi-Arg v+O_K(1/N)<2*pi. Thus R_N(y)<=O_K(1/N)+eta y for y<=0, while R_N(y)-2*pi*y<=O_K(1/N)-eta y for y>=0, with a fixed eta>0. The denominator in (6) supplies precisely exp(-2*pi*N*y) on the positive half-line and is bounded on the negative half-line. The full-Psi amplitude ratio is bounded uniformly for all real y, because its selected argument stays a fixed distance from the positive real ray. Its relative error is O_K(1/N). The resulting integrand is bounded by C_K exp(-eta |Im a|). This proves (11); the apparent N in da=N i dy cancels its decay scale N^(-1). A fixed finite set of smaller N is treated by the original horizontal full-Phi bounds. The leading normalization symbol can also be determined rather than left unspecified. Uniformly on the same compact families, I_N=1/(1-u+v)-h*v*(u-v)/(1-u+v)^3+O_K(h^2). (11a) For a on the fixed vertical line with |Im a|<=C log N, the actual full-Psi symbol and its holomorphic derivative bound give g(a)=(u-v)^a [1-h*a*(a-1)*(v/u)/(2*(1-v/u)) +O_K(h^2*(1+|a|^6))]. Here Log(u-v)=Log u+Log(1-v/u) has imaginary part in (-2*pi,0). The exponentially decaying tails proved above permit a cutoff C log N with error smaller than any fixed inverse power, while the displayed error integrates to O(h^2). The elementary convergent Barnes identity integral_(Re a=-epsilon,up) w^a/(exp(-2*pi*i*a)-1) da =1/(1-w) holds on that cut plane, first by closing to the right for |w|<1 and then by analytic continuation. Applying w^2*d_w^2 proves (11a). The same coefficient also follows from the exact current recurrence I_N(u,v)=(u-v)I_N(u,Qv)+1 on their common logarithmic chamber. Thus the retained term is three explicit norm phases 1,u^N,v^N times an analytic normalization symbol. This asymptotic description does not discard possible subdominant exponentially small pieces. The normalization group's rate therefore obeys limsup (1/N) log |D_N I_N| <=max(0,log|u|,log|v|), (13) uniformly on compact families. It is NOT always exponentially small. For instance it can have the original boundary norm rate. Any proof of a geometric lower bound must compare S_N with this retained term and with the subsequent exterior source; it cannot discard (13). ## 6. The actual homogeneous source line, with its normalizer explicit The zero-charge part now really is an explicit torsor section. Put c_*=c+h alpha, so exp(N c_*)=1-u^(-N). Equation (10) becomes S_N(u,v)=A_N(u) exp[-c Log u/h] Psi_+(c), A_N(u)=exp[c_* Log u/h] B_N(u,u exp c_*)/Psi_+(c_*). (14) Changing c_* by h leaves A_N unchanged by (3) and the full-Psi shift. Thus A_N depends only on u and is NONZERO; there is no unidentified knot scalar in this local source formula. On a common lower logarithmic chamber (and subsequently by the specified analytic continuation), the exact source equations imply A_N(Qu)=(1-u^(-1))A_N(u). (15) The selected function Psi_+(h-Log u) has the same step. Their quotient is h-periodic in Log u. This observation alone does NOT make that quotient constant or tame. The subsequent [exact normalizer proof](actual_trivalent_beta_normalizer.md) uses the actual source's divisor and both end bounds to determine it: A_N(u)=(N/phi_N) u^N Psi_+(h-Log u). (15a) The central u^N is compulsory and may have an exponential rate. Periodicity by itself would not have justified its omission. The classical growing saddle of the original fiber is r=V/(1+V-U), and its signed positive bipyramid has V/r and 1/r upper and U/r lower. The exact nonzero section (14) is the candidate that can carry this growing block. Its comparison with the full geometric normal contour and the bound (13) remains the next step. The earlier charged REAL kernel with negative volume rate is not used as a substitute for this original source. ## 7. Positive geometry alone does not dominate this local source There is a useful exact obstruction to dropping the norm-gap or the exterior boundary functional. Whenever |u|+|v|<=c<1, |B_N(u,v)|<=1/(1-c), B_N(u,v) -> 1/(1-u+v) as N -> infinity. (16) Every Newton product is bounded by c^a. For each fixed a it tends to (u-v)^a as Q tends to one, so dominated convergence proves both claims. This is an open chamber of the ORIGINAL polynomial source. It contains genuine strictly positive signed bipyramids. For example take u=-4*i/5 and v=1/100. The three-side shapes and two outputs are p=1+v-u=101/100+4*i/5, q=p/v=101+80*i, H=u*q=64-404*i/5, p/H=v/u=i/80, q/H=1/u=5*i/4. Both p,q are upper, H is lower, and both outputs are upper; their oriented volume D(p)+D(q)-D(H)=D(i/80)+D(5*i/4) is strictly positive. Nevertheless the actual local source (16) has rate ZERO. The exact original tags in (2) converge to these same shapes, so this is not a replacement by a different quantum atom. Thus a positive classical bipyramid cannot by itself force the scalar trivalent source to grow at its volume. Its boundary Legendre terms, branch marks and the complete exterior pairing matter. In a family where the explicit residue rate DOES strictly exceed max(0,log|u|,log|v|), (10)--(13) instead give B_N=S_N(1+o(1)) with an exponentially small relative remainder, once the residue's uniform logarithmic error is controlled. The present note proves the exact source decomposition and remainder bound; it does not assume that inequality for every positive bipyramid or every knot network.

title: An independent root-Fourier certificate for the trivalent black scalar
text: # An independent root-Fourier certificate for the trivalent black scalar 29 October 2026. This derives an EXACT Euler-polynomial coefficient formula from the actual highest/descendant source. It proves its integer saturation support J>=d by cancellation of a complete Fourier mode. The positive C R identity is not assumed in this derivation; its remaining finite transformation is now separately [proved](finite_trivalent_euler_racah_transform.md). This coefficient certificate retains all original phases and root endpoint currents. Let N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, F_a=(Q;Q)_a. Assume integer 0<=j_i<=floor(d/2) satisfying the triangle inequalities, and put r=j_2+j_3-j_1 and J=j_1+j_2+j_3. Thus 0<=r<=2min(j_2,j_3). Use the original balanced coproduct and highest vectors h^(j)_k=q^(k^2)[d-j choose k]_Q. The selected actual black coefficient is N^3 A, with A=q^[-j_1(d-2j_1)] sum_k x^[k+j_1+j_3-2d] conjugate[h^(j_1)_k h^(j_3)_k W^(j_2)_r(j_3+k,d-j_1-k)]. (1) Here k=0,...,min(d-j_1,d-j_3), W^(j)_r=F_pair^r h^(j)/F_r. This is the literal endpoint extraction of the all-port vertex, including its lowest-column phase; no generic 6j formula is used. ## 1. Exact coefficient theorem Define the unnormalized Jackson difference D_Q g(T)=[g(T)-g(QT)]/T, D_Q T^h=(1-Q^h)T^(h-1), f(T)=(TQ^(1-j_3);Q)_(j_3), g(T)=(TQ;Q)_(j_2). The source-exact identity is A= N q^E/[F_(j_1)F_(j_2)F_(j_3)F_r] *[T^d] g(T)^2 D_Q^r f(T)^2, E=3j_1^2+j_2^2+j_3^2-2j_1j_2-2j_1j_3 +2j_2j_3-2j_3-2. (2) Every polynomial and denominator is finite; all denominator indices are below N. In particular deg(g^2 D_Q^r f^2)=J, so J<d implies A=0 EXACTLY. (3) This is an original-source cancellation before taking absolute values, not an admissibility rule imposed on a guessed 6j symbol. ## 2. Own finite Fourier proof The original coproduct binomial gives, with b=d-j_1-k, W^(j_2)_r(j_3+k,b)=F_(j_3+k)F_bF_(d-j_2) *sum_z q^(z^2)x^[-r+j_3+k-z] Q^[z(r-j_3-k+z)] /[F_z^2 F_(d-j_2-z)^2 F_(j_3+k-z) F_(j_2-j_1-k+z)]. The range is exactly where every displayed denominator index is nonnegative and <N. Substitute this and the two highest vectors in (1). Use only conjugate(F_a)=(-1)^a Q^[-a(a+1)/2]F_a, F_(d-a)=N(-1)^a Q^[a(a+1)/2]/F_a, q^N=-1. After the factors N cancel, the result is A=(-1)^(j_3)q^B/[F_(j_1)F_(j_2)F_(j_3)] *sum_(k,z) (-1)^(k+z) q^[(k-z)^2+(1+2j_1-2j_2)k+(1-2j_3)z] [(Q^(k+1);Q)_(j_3)(Q^(z+1);Q)_(j_2)]^2 /[F_(j_3+k-z)F_(j_2-j_1-k+z)], B=3j_1^2-2j_1j_2+j_2^2-j_3-2. (4) Equation (4) displays all phase bookkeeping; no root sign is left in an unspecified scalar. Put l=k-z and p=j_3+l. The two last factorials force p=0,...,r. For fixed p the z-dependent factor is Q^[(1-r)z] (Q^(z+p-j_3+1);Q)_(j_3)^2(Q^(z+1);Q)_(j_2)^2. Its sum extends EXACTLY to z=0,...,N-1. For z>d-j_2 the second Euler factor contains 1-Q^N. If k=z+p-j_3<0 then k>=-j_3 and the first factor contains 1-Q^0; if k>d-j_3 it contains 1-Q^N. There is no k>=N wrap because z<=d-j_2 and p-j_3<=j_2-j_1 imply k<=d-j_1. Thus all added states are killed by their literal factorial zeros. For a polynomial P(T) of degree <=2(j_2+j_3)<2N, complete root Fourier summation consequently selects precisely sum_(z=0)^(N-1) Q^[(1-r)z]P(Q^z) =N([T^(r-1)]P+[T^(N+r-1)]P). (5) Absent or negative coefficient indices mean zero. The p sum in (4) is, after its explicit constant phase is extracted, H(T)=sum_(p=0)^r (-1)^p Q^[p(p-1)/2+(1-r)p] [r choose p]_Q f(Q^pT)^2. If f(T)^2=sum_h c_h T^h, the finite binomial theorem gives H(T)=sum_h c_h T^h(Q^(1-r+h);Q)_r =T^r D_Q^r f(T)^2. (6) In fact for h<r the product contains 1-Q^0, while for h>=r it equals F_h/F_(h-r). Therefore the LOW Fourier coefficient r-1 in (5) vanishes EXACTLY. The surviving high coefficient is [T^(N+r-1)]g^2H=[T^d]g^2D_Q^r f^2. The p-independent phase in (4) is q^E, with E as in (2), and its factorial denominator is F_r. This proves (2) and (3), including r=0 and all level parities. ## 3. A finite low-degree version at saturation depth delta For delta=J-d>=0, put c_e=[U^e](U;Q)_(j_3)^2. Reversal of the two finite Euler products in (2) gives [T^d]g^2D_Q^r f^2 =Q^[j_2(j_2+1)-j_3(j_3-1)] [U^delta] (UQ^(-j_2);Q)_(j_2)^2 *sum_(e=0)^(2j_3-r) c_e F_(2j_3-e)/F_(2j_3-e-r) U^e. (7) Thus only coefficients <=delta need be computed. All denominator indices in (7) are physical: delta<=j_i and delta<=2j_3-r follow from the bounds on the other two j's. For any fixed saturation depth this is a fixed-length source formula, with no unspecified boundary data or q-normal derivative. It is not claimed that its summands have a common phase. ## 4. Two entire saturation layers are manifestly nonzero Let Lead=Q^[j_2(j_2+1)-j_3(j_3-1)] F_(2j_3)/F_(2j_3-r). This is the NONZERO leading coefficient of g^2D_Q^r f^2. Therefore on the entire layer delta=0, equation (2) gives A=Nq^E Lead/[F_(j_1)F_(j_2)F_(j_3)F_r]!=0. (8) For delta=1, so J=N, the next-to-leading coefficient divided by Lead is -2/(1-Q) [Q^(-j_2)(1-Q^(j_2)) +(1-Q^(j_3))(1-Q^(2j_3-r))/(1-Q^(2j_3))] =2Q^(-2j_2)(1-Q^(j_2))(1-Q^(j_2+j_3)) /[(1-Q)(1+Q^(j_3))]. (9) The first equality follows by taking the next coefficient in the two Euler squares before the Jackson derivative: their ratios are -2sum_(a=1)^(j_2)Q^-a and -2sum_(a=0)^(j_3-1)Q^a; the derivative multiplies the latter ratio by (1-Q^(2j_3-r))/(1-Q^(2j_3)). For the second equality use 2j_3-r=J-2j_2=N-2j_2 and cancel the factor 1-Q^(j_3) in 1-Q^(2j_3). Every factor on the last line of (9) is nonzero. Indeed J=N and 2j_i<=d force j_i>=1; also j_2+j_3=N-j_1 lies strictly between 0 and N, and j_3<N/2 excludes 1+Q^(j_3)=0. Multiplying (9) by the nonzero prefactor in (2) proves A!=0 on the ENTIRE delta=1 layer, at both level parities. Empty small-N layers are simply absent. These are genuine all-triple source nonvanishing statements, not deductions from a presumed positive formula. ## 5. The subsequent exact transformation The complete positive formula from this independent route equates the finite coefficient in (2) or (7), including its displayed phase, to (-1)^(N+J)q^[2j_1^2-j_1j_2-j_1j_3+j_2j_3-J-3] *[prod_i s_(j_i)/(N s_delta)] R_N(j). Equation (3) already proves its saturation-zero branch. The [one-central-channel result](actual_trivalent_one_channel_source_packet.md) supplies a proved nonzero boundary line. The finite coefficient-to- short-series and Sears bridge is now proved in the linked finite Euler-to-Racah transform, with an independent square-linearization derivation. Finite experiments alone do not prove it. No sewn-graph energy, magnetic norm or hyperbolic-volume claim is made from this coefficient formula. Audit: [literal source, Fourier selection and coefficient theorem](../experiments/audit_actual_trivalent_root_fourier_source_certificate.py).

title: A short finite square-linearization proof of the positive source scalar
text: # A short finite square-linearization proof of the positive source scalar 29 October 2026. This proves the remaining source-coefficient-to-short-series identity by finite product linearization and root cancellation. It is independent of the Jackson-Leibniz/Newton derivation. The input is the already proved original-source coefficient theorem, not a proposed 6j formula. All root denominators and zero coefficients are retained. Put N>=2, d=N-1, Q^N=1 with Q primitive, F_k=(Q;Q)_k. Take retained triangle labels a,b,c<=floor(d/2), let J=a+b+c, delta=J-d>=0, r=b+c-a, and H=2c-r=a+c-b=d-2b+delta. In particular 0<=delta<=min(a,b,c,H), 0<=r<=2min(b,c), 2b,2c<N. The reversed coefficient in the [actual root-Fourier theorem](actual_trivalent_root_fourier_source_certificate.md) is C_delta=[U^delta](UQ^-b;Q)_b^2 *sum_(e=0)^H [V^e](V;Q)_c^2 F_(2c-e)/F_(H-e) U^e. (1) The first three sections prove exactly C_delta=T_0 H_c, T_0=Q^[delta(delta-1-2b)] F_b^2 F_(2c) /[F_H F_delta F_(b-delta)^2], H_c=sum_(k=0)^delta (Q^-delta,Q^-c,Q^-c,Q^-H;Q)_k Q^k /(Q,Q^-2c,Q^(b-delta+1),Q^(b-delta+1);Q)_k. (2) Every denominator here is nonzero. No ordering such as a=max(a,b,c) is required. Section 4 completes the finite Sears transformation and explicit phase conversion to the positive factorial partition. ## 1. An elementary finite product linearization For generic v and nonnegative m,n, (U;v)_m(U;v)_n =sum_(k=0)^min(m,n) A_(m,n,k) U^k(U;v)_(m+n-k), A_(m,n,k)=(-1)^k v^[k(k-1)/2] (v;v)_m(v;v)_n /[(v;v)_k(v;v)_(m-k)(v;v)_(n-k)]. (3) Here is a finite induction. The m=0 case is immediate. With S=m+n, (1-v^m U)U^k(U;v)_(S-k) =U^k(U;v)_(S+1-k) +(v^(S-k)-v^m)U^(k+1)(U;v)_(S-k). Consequently the next coefficient is A_(m,n,k)+(v^(m+n-k+1)-v^m)A_(m,n,k-1) =A_(m+1,n,k). Substitution of the displayed factorials proves this equality; the interior ratio is (1-v^(m+1))/(1-v^(m+1-k)). Endpoints follow by clearing denominators and setting out-of-range coefficients to zero. Thus (3) is a polynomial identity, and specializes at Q with m=n=c because c<N. The largest product length 2c is also below N here. Apply the coefficient multiplier V^e -> F_(2c-e)U^e/F_(H-e), 0<=e<=H, to (3) with m=n=c, discarding coefficients above H. In its k-th term the finite binomial coefficient [2c-k choose e-k]_Q cancels the factor F_(2c-e). The remaining finite binomial theorem gives sum_(e=0)^H [V^e](V;Q)_c^2 F_(2c-e)U^e/F_(H-e) =sum_(k=0)^min(c,H) (-1)^k Q^[k(k-1)/2] F_c^2 F_(2c-k) /[F_k F_(c-k)^2 F_(H-k)] U^k(U;Q)_(H-k). (4) No coefficient beyond the genuine derivative range H is introduced. ## 2. The exact root coefficient cancellation For 0<=n<=b put I_n=[U^n](UQ^-b;Q)_b^2(U;Q)_(d-2b+n). Since (U;Q)_N=1-U^N and n<N, coefficient extraction gives exactly I_n=[U^n] (UQ^-b;Q)_b /(UQ^(n-1-2b);Q)_(b+1-n). (5) Indeed the missing factor in the length-N product runs from exponent n-1-2b through -1. Its last b factors cancel one of the two numerator products. Formal division is valid because every Euler factor has constant coefficient one. The discarded numerator term U^N cannot affect the coefficient n. Set h=b+1-n>=1 and z=Q^(n-1-2b). The reciprocal finite-product coefficient is z^l(Q^h;Q)_l/F_l: it follows either by multiplying the factors, or from the recurrence obtained by shifting U to QU. Expanding the numerator in (5), and dividing by its v=0 term, gives I_n=z^n (Q^h;Q)_n/F_n *sum_(v=0)^n (Q^-n;Q)_v Q^[(b+1)v]/F_v. The factors (Q^-b;Q)_v cancel in numerator and denominator; they are nonzero since v<=n<=b<N. The finite binomial theorem evaluates the sum as (Q^(b+1-n);Q)_n=(Q^h;Q)_n. Therefore I_n=Q^[n(n-1-2b)] F_b^2/[F_n F_(b-n)^2]. (6) This proof includes n=0 and uses no analytic limit or infinite series. ## 3. Consecutive terms give the exact short series Insert (4) into (1). Only k<=delta contributes, and put n=delta-k. Since H-k=d-2b+n, equation (6) applies term by term. The result is C_delta=sum_(k=0)^delta T_k, T_k=(-1)^k Q^[k(k-1)/2+(delta-k)(delta-k-1-2b)] *F_b^2 F_c^2 F_(2c-k) /[F_k F_(c-k)^2 F_(H-k) F_(delta-k) F_(b-delta+k)^2]. (7) Every factor is a physical factorial with index in 0,...,d. The initial term is precisely T_0 in (2). Its consecutive ratio is T_(k+1)/T_k =Q * (1-Q^(k-delta))(1-Q^(k-c))^2(1-Q^(k-H)) /[(1-Q^(k+1))(1-Q^(k-2c)) (1-Q^(b-delta+k+1))^2]. (8) The apparent extra power in this ratio is Q^(H-delta+2b+2)=Q^(N+1)=Q. This is exactly the root relation that is needed, rather than a generic-q continuation of the root source. Equations (7),(8) prove (2). All denominator ranges are safe: k+1<=delta<=c,b; 2c-k is positive and below N for every ratio used; b-delta+k+1<=b<N. Empty sums and delta=0 give the same formula without a ratio. This closes the finite source coefficient bridge. Its remaining finite normalizations are evaluated next. Physical CD and magnetic tensor normalizations remain distinct from this scalar calculation. ## 4. The symmetric positive scalar, with its full original phase Put r_1=a+b-c, r_2=H=a+c-b. In (2), use the root equality Q^(b-delta+1)=Q^(-a-c), and apply the [own finite Sears identity](finite_balanced_sears_operator_proof.md) with length delta, retained parameter Q^-c, and both selected denominators Q^(-a-c). It gives H_c=K_1 H_sym, K_1=(Q^-a,Q^(-a-b);Q)_delta /(Q^(-a-c),Q^-r_1;Q)_delta, H_sym=4phi3(Q^-delta,Q^-a,Q^-b,Q^-c; Q^(-a-b),Q^(-a-c),Q^(-b-c);Q,Q). (9) Every descending denominator index is at least delta, and every upper factorial index is below N. Thus this is a direct finite specialization. No division by H_sym is used. Its kth term is strictly positive at the principal root: the sine factors are positive, and their residual phase is q^[k(J-delta+1)]=q^(Nk)=(-1)^k, cancelling the denominator's remaining (-1)^k. The k=0 term is one. Here is a short explicit normalization of the ACTUAL source. Let E_F=3a^2+b^2+c^2-2ab-2ac+2bc-2c-2, E_src=2a^2-ab-ac+bc-J-3, tau_u=(-1)^u q^[u(u+1)], F_u F_(d-u)=N tau_u. The original Fourier theorem says A=N q^[E_F+2b(b+1)-2c(c-1)] C_delta/(F_a F_b F_c F_r). (10) Converting K_1 to factorials introduces NO phase: the sums of its two numerator and denominator descending parameters agree. Explicitly K_1=F_a F_(a+b) F_(d-b) F_(d-2c) /[F_(a-delta) F_(d-c) F_(a+c) F_(r_1)]. Insert T_0 from (2) into (10) and reflect complements. Its remaining factorial prefactor is exactly N^2 tau_b tau_(2c) tau_(a+b)/(tau_c tau_(a+c)) /[F_r F_(r_1) F_(r_2) F_delta F_(a-delta) F_(b-delta) F_(c-delta)]. (11) The tau signs multiply to (-1)^(2b)=1. The seven denominator indices sum to 2d, so F_u=(-i)^u q^[u(u+1)/2]s_u contributes the net sign (-1)^d. If E_total is the remaining q exponent, direct expansion gives E_total-E_src+N(J+1)=2N(2b+1). Thus the exact phase of (11), including (10), is (-1)^(N+J)q^E_src. Its positive modulus proves A=(-1)^(N+J)q^E_src D_sym H_sym, D_sym=N^2/[s_r s_(r_1)s_(r_2)s_delta s_(a-delta)s_(b-delta)s_(c-delta)]>0. (12) This proves nonvanishing on EVERY supported triangle, at both parities. For completeness the same symmetric series is the positive R_N. Choose a maximal label a for this SYMMETRIC positive object. Its first term and the first finite Sears prefactor are R_0=s_a s_(b+c)/[s_(a-b)s_(a-c)s_b s_c s_r], K_0=(Q^(a+1),Q^-2b;Q)_r /(Q^(a-b+1),Q^-b;Q)_r. The long series is obtained by the consecutive ratio of the seven sine-factorial summand. The proved Sears identity changes it to H_b, and the same identity changes H_b to K_2 H_sym, where K_2=(Q^-c,Q^(-a-c);Q)_delta /(Q^(-b-c),Q^-r_2;Q)_delta. The finite denominator ranges are safe since r<=b,c and delta<=r_2. The phases in K_0 and K_2 cancel internally, so both are positive. Their sine-factorial products and reflection s_u s_(d-u)=N give R_0 K_0 K_2 =N^3/[s_a s_b s_c s_r s_(r_1)s_(r_2) s_(a-delta)s_(b-delta)s_(c-delta)]. (13) Both sides are symmetric; the choice of a maximal chart places no restriction on the source ordering. Combining (12),(13) proves the original all-channel identity A=(-1)^(N+J)q^E_src [s_a s_b s_c/(N s_delta)]R_N. The source is zero for J<d by the independent Fourier degree theorem. This entire finite proof concerns the actual black scalar. It does not bound its magnetic tensor or replace the marked white co-source. Audit: [finite product, weighted coefficient and root bridge](../experiments/audit_actual_trivalent_square_linearization_bridge.py). The separate [full-source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_trivalent_general_scalar_candidate.py) compares the final phase and normalization with original coproduct columns. Two independent analytical reviews checked Sections 1--3; the independent longer Fourier/Newton route checks the full symmetric source identity. A further independent analytical review of Section 4 rederived its seven-factorial prefactor, phase congruence and positive R_0 K_0 K_2 normalization without invoking a maximal-order source symmetry. Finite checks supplement these all-parameter proofs.

title: An exact odd central Clebsch anchor for the trivalent source
text: # An exact odd central Clebsch anchor for the trivalent source 29 October 2026. At the odd-level simple Steinberg channel, the actual trivalent black source has one genuine three-channel invariant tensor and one explicit finite scalar. Its highest and lowest Clebsch columns, middle column, normalization and positive complete-circle factor are computed below. Its coherent scalar is then evaluated by OWN finite binomial identities as a positive fourth-power sine-binomial sum, with a nonzero all-odd asymptotic. This supplies a central anchor for the new [ordered branching packet](actual_trivalent_complete_circle_vertex_kernel.md). No even-level confluence estimate, uniform complex packet, global source survival or geometric maximum is claimed. ## 1. The actual simple channel and its full Clebsch columns Let N=2m+1>=3, d=2m, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d=-q^(-1), F_r=(Q;Q)_r. Use the ORIGINAL balanced Ecal,F,K and their ordered coproducts. Define a physical pair vector of degree m by h=sum_(a=0)^m h_a |a,m-a>, h_a=q^(a^2) [m choose a]_Q =q^(ma) beta(m,a), beta(m,a)=|[m choose a]_Q|. (1) The last equality uses the principal root: the Gaussian binomial has phase q^[a(m-a)], and all its sine factors have positive sign. Its highest-vector equation follows from the literal ratio h_(a+1)/h_a =-x^(-1) Q^a (1-Q^(m-a))/(1-Q^(a+1)). (2) Indeed Ecal_pair h=0 and its highest K is x, so its Casimir is -2. Put W_r=F_pair^r h/F_r, 0<=r<=d, W|r>=W_r. (3) The same original commutator used for a physical highest-weight-N module gives F_pair W_r=(1-Q^(r+1)) W_(r+1), Ecal_pair W_r=(Q^(-r)-1) W_(r-1), K_pair W_r=x Q^(-r) W_r. (4) Endpoints are zero. All interior coefficients in (4) are nonzero, so W is an actual injective Hopf intertwiner V_N -> V_N tensor V_N. There is no generic semisimple replacement of the root module here. Every entry has the explicit finite Clebsch form. If b=m+r-a and 0<=a,b<=d, then W_r(a,b)=F_a F_b F_m *sum_s q^(s^2) x^[-r+a-s] Q^[s(r-a+s)] /[F_s^2 F_(m-s)^2 F_(a-s) F_(r-a+s)], (5) where max(0,a-r)<=s<=min(m,a). If a or b is outside the physical basis, the entry is zero. All denominator indices in this finite range are less than N. To prove (5), write F_pair=A+B with A=F_1, B=K_1^(-1)F_2, so AB=Q^(-1)BA. Expand (A+B)^r=sum_k [r choose k]_Q A^k B^(r-k), and apply its k=a-s term to the s-th summand of (1). Dividing by F_r leaves precisely the six displayed factorials. Thus (5) is an own finite binomial calculation, with its full root phases. ## 2. Exact source normalizations, including both ends Two useful cancellations are W_d(m+t,d-t)=h_t, 0<=t<=m, W_m(0,d)=q^(-m^2). (6) For the first, the lowest-vector equation in (4) shows that its successive ratio is the ratio in (1); only its first scalar needs checking. Substitute r=d,a=m in (5), then use F_t F_(d-t)=N(-1)^t Q^[t(t+1)/2]. (7) Its first scalar becomes (-1)^m q^[-m(3m+1)] sum_(s=0)^m Q^(s^2) [m choose s]_Q^2. Finite q-Vandermonde makes the sum [2m choose m]_Q=N/F_m^2. For completeness, extract the coefficient of z^m in (z;Q)_m(zQ^m;Q)_m=(z;Q)_(2m) using the finite binomial expansion, then set a=m-k in its convolution. Its residual exponent is a^2, which proves exactly this finite Vandermonde identity. Since F_m^2=N(-1)^m q^[m(m+1)], the total scalar is q^(-2mN)=1. This proves the first equation(6). In the second equation, only s=0 survives in (5); the value is x^(-m)N/F_m^2=q^(-m^2). Let f_a(z) be the ORIGINAL middle-degree Casimir continuants normalized by f_0=1. The node -2 is SIMPLE at odd N. Consequently W_m(a,d-a)=q^(-m^2) f_a(-2). (8) No derivative node is treated as a second simple value. The simple node is being used only at the odd central anchor. The exact positive/reflection normalization is W^dagger P W=I_N, (L_N P)_Steinberg=N W W^dagger. (9) Here the subscript selects the actual -2 simple block on the full physical pair, in every degree m,...,3m. To check the first column of (9), use (1), conjugate the Gaussian phase, and apply terminating q-Chu with parameters(Q^(-m),Q^(-m);Q), argument Q. It gives h^dagger P h =q^(m^2) sum_a Q^[a(a+1)] [m choose a]_Q^2 =q^(m^2)(-1)^m Q^[-m^2-m(m+1)/2]=1. (10) The last exponent uses q^N=-1. The elementary finite q-Chu proof is given in [the source quadratic transform](actual_half_color_quadratic_source_transform.md#2-elementary-finite-q-chu-and-durfee-identities); it is a polynomial binomial expansion, not an imported summation theorem. Adjoint covariance Ecal_pair^dagger P=-P F_pair now gives the norm of each descendant: its ratio is |1-Q^(r+1)|^2 before division by F_(r+1)/F_r. Thus every W_r has P-norm one, and different r have disjoint physical degrees. The actual simple spectral projector is W W^dagger P, proving the second part of (9). Equivalently sqrt(N) W is a valid full-degree CD factor for this channel; replacing first-entry normalization by it is a KNOWN unit phase change within each magnetic row, not an arbitrary frame removal. ## 3. The entire central black vertex is one genuine 3j tensor Use the actual nested six-head J=p_16 p_23 p_45 and define the unscaled Hopf row pi=W^dagger P. Its central black packet is U^0=(pi tensor pi tensor pi) J. (11) The row pi is a Hopf map by (4),(9) and the original adjoint covariance. Hence (11) is a genuine invariant of V_N tensor V_N tensor V_N. This invariant space is ONE dimensional. Bending its third leg by the original duality identifies it with Hom(V_N,V_N tensor V_N). Every such map has image in the -2 Casimir kernel. That actual simple kernel is exactly the single W(V_N) above, with dimension N; Schur's elementary E/F/K argument therefore gives dimension one. Define its canonical nonzero tensor Theta=(W tensor I) p, Theta_(a,b,c)=N x^(-c) W_(d-c)(a,b). (12) In particular Theta_(d,m,0)=N q^(m^2), by (6). Therefore the WHOLE central black vertex is U^0=N^2 q^(-m^2) A_N Theta, A_N=sum_(k=0)^m x^(k-d) conjugate(h_k^2 W_m(m+k,m-k)). (13) To obtain its scalar, evaluate (11) at the magnetic indices(d,m,0). The only remaining physical colors are the N-term source contraction of the branching kernel, with h_(m-t) from the lowest and highest columns. Reindex k=m-t and use (6). It gives U^0_(d,m,0)=N^3 A_N, which with (12) proves (13). In the positive CD factor sqrt(N) W, the vertex is N^(3/2) times U^0, including the original N^3 of J. Formula(5) makes A_N a fully explicit terminating factorial sum. The next section proves its positive collapse, retaining all phases; that positivity is not a premise of the source reduction above. The ordinary and marked white packets remain the distinct actual kernels of the branching theorem, with each f_alpha replaced by the specified sqrt(N) W_r. In particular the marked vertex is NOT declared to be a zero-current 3j covector: its last arc has the exact P-removal and whole-source degree qualification already proved there. Equation(13) concerns the invariant BLACK vertex only. Thus this central reduction preserves the source distinction that prevented the false trivalent norm-square replacement. ## 4. A finite coherent quartic transform The scalar of the ACTUAL vertex has the exact evaluation A_N=q^[m(2-m)] sum_(k=0)^m beta(m,k)^4. (14) In particular it is nonzero at EVERY odd N, including composite levels. Here is a finite proof, rather than an absolute-value bound. Let f=(f_a(-2))_(a=0)^d and use the actual symmetric anti-Pascal recoupling J on the complete N-channel source module. Root factorial reflection(7) rewrites its entries as J_(i,j)=x D_i D_j [i+j choose i]_(Q^(-1)), D_i=(-q^(-1))^i, i+j<=d; zero otherwise. (15) It is important that this is the full invertible recoupling, not just the simple node. It obeys conjugate(J) P J=P. (16) This follows by finite q-binomial inversion. More explicitly, the (i,j) entry of the left side has a=j,...,d-i. If i+j>d it is zero. If n=d-i-j=0 its sole term is the squared modulus of an antidiagonal entry, hence one. If n>0, put a=j+t and use(7) on its factorials. After factoring the nonzero t-independent terms, the sum is sum_(t=0)^n (-1)^t Q^[t(t-1)/2+(1-n)t] [n choose t]_Q =(Q^(1-n);Q)_n=0. This proves(16) with the actual phase, without assuming a positive or unitary ordinary pivotal trace. The other actual pair Casimir is the real upper bidiagonal matrix B with diagonal c_i=q^(2i+1)+q^(-2i-1) and upper entry b_i=Q^i+Q^(-i)-2. The established source relation J A J^(-1)=B^T gives y=J f explicitly: y_i=0, i<m; y_(m+k)=beta(m,k)^2, 0<=k<=m. (17) For clarity, this needs only its first-order eigenvector recurrence. Before i=m the diagonal c_i+2 is nonzero. After i=m, -b_i/(c_i+2)=sin^2(pi(m+1-k)/N)/sin^2(pi k/N), i=m+k. The final entry is y_d=f_0=1. This proves(17), including its absolute normalization, directly from the two actual Casimir matrices. By(1),(8),(13), A_N=q^(-3m^2) f^dagger J f. Since y is REAL, (16) gives conjugate(f)=P J P y. Put z=P y. It has support0,...,m and z_i=beta(m,i)^2. Therefore f^dagger J f=z^T J z. (18) All entries i,j<=m in this quadratic form have i+j<=d, so the zero-truncation in(15) no longer intervenes. Finite Vandermonde, by the same product-coefficient proof as in Section2, gives [i+j choose i]_t =sum_(k=0)^min(i,j) t^(k^2)[i choose k]_t[j choose k]_t. Consequently (15),(18) become z^T J z=x sum_(k=0)^m Q^(-k^2) C_k^2, C_k=sum_(i=k)^m beta(m,i)^2 D_i [i choose k]_(Q^(-1)). (19) The SINGLE remaining transform is exactly evaluable: C_k=(-1)^m q^[k^2-m(m+1)] beta(m,k)^2. (20) To prove it, put n=m-k and convert every Gaussian factor in(19) to base Q. Factoring its k-th term gives C_k=(-1)^k q^(-k) Q^[k^2-mk] [m choose k]_Q^2 *sum_(r=0)^n (Q^(-n);Q)_r^2 Q^(-kr) /[F_r(Q^(k+1);Q)_r]. (21) Here Q^(m+1)=-q is precisely the half-root relation that cancels the otherwise alternating summation argument. Apply the SECOND terminating q-Chu identity with b=Q^(-n), c=Q^(k+1): sum_(r=0)^n (Q^(-n);Q)_r(b;Q)_r (c Q^n/b)^r/[F_r(c;Q)_r] =(c/b;Q)_n/(c;Q)_n. (22) Its argument is cQ^(2n)=Q^(-k), exactly as in(21). This is another own finite identity: take the already proved q-Chu of Section2 at base Q^(-1), parameters b^(-1),c^(-1), and use (a;Q^(-1))_r=(-a)^r Q^[-r(r-1)/2](a^(-1);Q)_r. That substitution gives(22) term by term and on its right side. All its denominators here have indices<=m<N. At the root its right side is (Q^(m+1);Q)_n/(Q^(k+1);Q)_n =(-1)^n Q^[-mn+n(n-1)/2]. Substituting this into(21) and using [m choose k]_Q^2=Q^[k(m-k)] beta(m,k)^2 gives(20). Now EVERY k-dependent phase cancels in(19): f^dagger J f=x q^[-2m(m+1)] sum_k beta(m,k)^4 =q^(-2m^2) sum_k beta(m,k)^4. Multiplying by q^(-3m^2) gives q^(-5m^2) times that positive sum. Finally q^(-5m^2)=q^[m(2-m)], since their exponent difference is -2mN. This proves(14) with the actual root lift and full source. ## 5. Nonzero local scalar asymptotic, with its exact normalization Let G(t)=log(2sin(pi t)), J(t)=integral_0^t G(u)du and j0=-8J(1/4)=v8/pi. Here v8=4 times Catalan's integral is only a named numerical constant; no link-volume identification is assumed. Then the finite positive scalar in(14) obeys sum_k beta(m,k)^4 =(1/4) N^(-3/2) exp(N j0)(1+O(N^(-1))), A_N=(q^[m(2-m)]/4) N^(-3/2) exp(N j0)(1+O(N^(-1))). (23) An elementary sine-factorial Laplace proof keeps the affine shift m=(N-1)/2. On compact0<t<1, Euler summation after separating the logarithmic endpoint gives s_a=sqrt(2N sin(pi a/N)) exp[N J(a/N)](1+O(N^(-1))). The same endpoint separation gives the uniform logarithmic error O(log N) for all0<=a<N, sufficient for a global large-deviation gap. Since s_m^2=N EXACTLY, beta(m,k)^4=N^2/(s_k^4 s_(m-k)^4). Its limiting exponent -4J(t)-4J(1/2-t) has a UNIQUE maximum at1/4: its derivative is4log cot(pi t), positive before1/4 and negative afterward, and its second derivative there is -8pi. Write k=m/2+sqrt(N)u, retaining its actual integer or half-integer coset. The compact factorial formula gives the symmetric local density beta(m,k)^4 =(1/2)N^(-2) exp[N j0-4pi u^2] *[1+O((1+u^4)/N)] (24) on a growing Gaussian window; outside a smaller fixed macroscopic window there is the strict exponent gap just proved. The odd terms cancel because k and m-k occur symmetrically. The shifted Gaussian Riemann sum has mesh N^(-1/2), integral1/2 and relative errorO(1/N), by the integrable second-derivative trapezoidal estimate. Multiplying the factor1/2 in(24) by this integral gives exactly1/4 in(23). This proves both the all-odd nonvanishing and its scalar rate. The corresponding highest black-source coefficient in the CD frame sqrt(N)W is N^(9/2)A_N, hence has leading magnitude (N^3/4) exp(Nj0). The ENTIRE black tensor still includes Theta in(13). No claim about its full positive norm, the marked white tensor, even confluent channels or a sewn graph's maximum follows by maximizing this one coefficient. Those are the next genuine branching estimates. Audit: [actual generators, every finite Clebsch entry, source endpoint and central invariant tensor](../experiments/audit_actual_trivalent_steinberg_central_anchor.py). The review independently rederived the second q-Chu phases, the finite full-J inversion, and the affine-shift factor 1/4 in(23). title: A genuine circle turn changes positive face reflection to full Krein inertia
