text: # A genuine circle turn changes positive face reflection to full Krein inertia 29 October 2026. The positive original complete-circle face form does NOT remain positive through the genuine cup/cap quarter-turn used in the actual four-rung contraction. This is an all-level finite theorem, including the complete Hermite normals. Its obstruction is already present on the ORIGINAL cup and its canonical normal direction, not only on an arbitrary ambient input. An explicit full-rank positive metric repairs Cauchy at polynomial ordinary source cost; controlling its energy through overlapping recouplings is a separate problem. ## 1. Exact original operators and the full turned circle Set N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^d, and s_r=product_(k=1)^r 2sin(pi k/N), s_0=1, c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1), P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2, Bhat_v(z)=product_(k=0)^(v-1)(c_k-z)/s_v^2. Let Omega be the ORIGINAL physical pair Casimir, P the literal physical swap, and L_N=(-1)^d U_d(Omega/2). The full operator identities already proved are Omega^*P=P Omega, P_N(Omega)=0, P L_N>=0, (turn A)_((a,b);(c,e))=x^(a-e)A_((d-a,c);(b,d-e)). (1) The turn in (1) is the original unscaled cup/cap turn. It is not a crossing or a relabeling. It is precisely the physical turn used in the [actual rung/cycle reduction](actual_cube_four_rung_positive_source.md), and its Newton reversal holds with repeated roots and all normals in [the full turn theorem](actual_newton_turn_positive_gram.md). Write M=floor(d/2), k_j=2 for 2j<d and k_j=1 for 2j=d. Let E_j be the FULL Hermite cluster projector and L_j=L_N E_j. For v<=j put z_j(v)=s_(j+v)/(s_(j-v)s_v^2), h_j=sum_(v=0)^j z_j(v)Bhat_v. The exact all-normal identity is turn L_j=N k_j h_j, f_N:=turn L_N=N sum_(j=0)^M k_j h_j. (2) Here is a parity-independent proof, rather than extrapolation of the odd rung theorem. The original Frobenius functional satisfies phi(L_j a)=N Tr(E_j m_a)=N k_j a(c_j). Its multiplication trace has algebraic multiplicity two on a paired node and one on the odd simple node; the nilpotent trace is zero only AFTER the full operator identity is used. Newton duality and genuine turn reversal therefore give the v-th coefficient of turn L_j as phi(L_j Bhat_v)=N k_j Bhat_v(c_j). Direct paired-sine factorization gives Bhat_v(c_j)=z_j(v) for v<=j and zero otherwise. This proves (2) in the complete N-dimensional algebra, not merely at its nodes. Consequently, at EVERY distinct Casimir node c_k, f_N(c_k)=N sum_j k_j sum_(v<=min(j,k))z_j(v)z_k(v) >=N sum_j k_j=N^2, f_N(c_0)=N^2. (3) All summands are positive real, and z_j(0)=1. The same formula covers the high partner since c_(d-k)=c_k. In particular f_N is invertible in the full Hermite algebra, despite the radical of L_N. ## 2. Exact full physical inertia after the actual turn There is a unique real Hermite polynomial g_N of degree<N whose positive nodal square roots and paired normal values are g_N(c)=sqrt(f_N(c)), g_N'(c)=f_N'(c)/(2sqrt(f_N(c))) at a double node. (4) Every nodal value in (4) is nonzero by (3), so g_N(Omega) is invertible and g_N(Omega)^2=f_N(Omega). Since the coefficients of g_N are real, (1) gives the exact congruence P f_N(Omega)=g_N(Omega)^* P g_N(Omega). (5) It follows, without an eigenvector conditioning estimate, that the reflected TURNED circle has inertia positive: N(N+1)/2, negative: N(N-1)/2, zero:0. (6) These are the inertia dimensions of the literal swap. Thus no invertible change of full physical basis, including one mixing all Hermite channels, can make this turned reflected form positive. For an explicit negative vector, choose any antisymmetric physical v and put u=g_N(Omega)^(-1)v; its value in (5) is -||v||^2. The conclusion concerns the specified physical reflection P. It does not rule out a different positive metric or a source-dependent coherent regrouping of a whole graph. In particular it does not contradict positivity of the actual full cube scalar. ## 3. The obstruction survives on the completed ORIGINAL source packet Use exactly the original degree-d cup p, ordinary cap ell, marked row m and canonical Hermite direction t from the [source frame theorem](actual_tame_c0_hermite_source_frame.md): p_u=N x^(u-d), ell_u=x^u/N, m_u=x^(d-u)/N^2, ell=p^*P/N^2, ell p=0, ell t=1, mp=1, mt=0, (Omega-c_0)p=0, (Omega-c_0)t=theta_N p. These imply p^*Pp=0 and p^*Pt=N^2. Functional calculus retaining the actual first normal gives [p,t]^* P f_N(Omega)[p,t] =[[0,N^4],[N^4,beta_N]], beta_N=t^*P f_N(Omega)t real, determinant=-N^8<0. (7) The derivative term f_N'(c_0)theta_N p is present; its contribution to the upper row is zero because p^*Pp=0. Thus (7) does not omit a normal. It proves that the complete original two-dimensional source packet already has one positive and one negative direction after the turn. One cannot repair this by dropping the cup (which is null) or by replacing t with a value-only channel. ## 4. A concrete positive Cauchy repair, with exactly polynomial boundaries The SAME g_N gives a different, positive, full-rank metric G_N=g_N(Omega)^*g_N(Omega). (8) This retains every physical degree and Hermite normal. Its definition uses the actual turned circle, not an unknown knot invariant. Since g_N(c_0)=N, and ell Omega=c_0 ell, the literal source costs are ||p||_(G_N)^2=N^5, ||ell||_(G_N^-1)^2=1/N^3. (9) Indeed ||p||_2^2=N^3, ||ell||_2^2=1/N, g_N(Omega)p=Np, and ell g_N(Omega)^(-1)=ell/N. For every physical input psi and arbitrary tensor spectators, |ell psi|^2 <= N^-3 ||g_N(Omega)psi||_2^2. (10) This is an ORDINARY-cap inequality with the actual cup and cap. It is not a local replacement of the original unrestricted marked row. Applying it to a marked link first requires its already typed whole-source conversion, with all original peripheral factors kept. Equations (5),(8) separate the exact issue at a geometric turn: the original physical reflection supplies g^*P g, while positive Cauchy uses g^*g. The latter is a genuine available metric, but its transport through an overlapping source recoupling is not controlled by (9). Polynomial correlated cell cost and a positive closed Racah scalar do not identify these two sewing operations. Audit: [literal turn, source packet and Hermite square-root checks](../experiments/audit_actual_turned_circle_reflection_inertia.py). The all-N proof is (2)--(7); complex inertia tests supplement it. No general graph growth or volume theorem is asserted here. Independent internal review: the crossing/source agent completed a full analytical read and fresh replay of eleven exact physical turn/source cases and six complex full-Hermite families. The review checked the source-plane determinant, ordinary source costs, inertia and retained derivative directions without identifying the constructed positive repair with a physical mirror.

title: A factorial-frame bound for complete original twist blocks
text: # A factorial-frame bound for complete original twist blocks 28 October 2026. An explicit normalized **physical** Borel fusion and its exact inverse improve the uniform twist-block estimate. For absolute constants C,A, every N>=2 and every integer ell satisfy ||B_N^ell||_op <= C N^A(1+|ell|) exp(12 gamma_* N), gamma_*=-integral_0^(1/6)log(2sin(pi t))dt. (1) The same holds for HS norm with one additional factor N. Here B_N is either actual complete crossing with its original Cartan/root framing line; those complete scalar factors have modulus one. No arbitrary condition number is removed. Every fusion metric cost is bounded in the original balanced flat norm, and the common Cartan is kept on the meridian continuation used in the proof. In volume units 24pi gamma_*=12v_3, where v_3 is the regular ideal tetrahedron volume. The preceding independently checked bound 2pi log(7+5sqrt(2)) in [the convex block note](actual_convex_gauge_block_energy.md) remains valid; (1) is a sharper result, with a separate explicit-frame audit. Neither bound is the sharp knot-volume theorem. The later [joint projector-profile theorem](actual_twist_block_projector_barrier.md) improves 12v_3 further to 4v_3+2v_8 by maximizing the coupled projector interval profile. It uses the exact physical frames and source continuation established here; the coarser proof below is unchanged. The subsequent [joint projector estimate](actual_twist_block_projector_barrier.md) sharpens the volume constant further to 4v_3+2v_8. It uses the SAME physical frames, source and meridian-circle argument below, but maximizes the complete projector factorial profile together. The independent bound (1) and its proof remain valid. ## 1. The actual normalized fusion and inverse Fix q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, d=N-1, F_a=(Q;Q)_a. Continue the original meridian M near one and set x=-M/q, Y=M^2. On each balanced physical head use the literal matrices K|a>=x Q^(-a)|a>, F|a>=(1-Q^(a+1))|a+1>, Ecal|a>=(M Q^(-a)-M^(-1))|a-1>, Ecal=rho^2 E. Missing endpoint arrows are zero. This is the original nilpotent N-color meridian family; it is not a generic cyclic representation. The total lowering operator is f=F_1+K_1^(-1)F_2, f^N=0. For total integer degree T, set I_T=[max(0,T-d),min(T,d)]. The actual free Borel fusion columns are f^a|0,T-a>. Normalize each by its nonzero physical factorial F_a. In the basis |u,T-u> this gives C_T(u,a)=x^(u-a) F_(T-u)/[F_(a-u)F_(T-a)], u<=a, C_T(u,a)=0 otherwise. (2) These are triangular matrices with diagonal one. Expanding f^a by the finite Q-binomial theorem proves (2) directly. Their exact inverses are C_T^(-1)(u,a)=(-1)^(a-u)Q^((a-u)(a-u-1)/2) C_T(u,a). (3) Indeed (2) factors as diag_u(x^u F_(T-u)) times the upper Euler-Toeplitz matrix (1/F_(a-u)) times its inverse diagonal. The inverse Euler coefficients are (-1)^h Q^(h(h-1)/2)/F_h. This proves (3) for arbitrary nonzero M, not only at the complete root. In particular both matrices have the SAME entrywise moduli. All normalized factorials and powers of M in these physical frames are retained. ## 2. The sharp elementary factorial cost of this frame Write J(s)=integral_0^s log(2sin(pi t))dt. The already proved endpoint-uniform factorial estimate gives log|F_a|=N J(a/N)+O(log N) uniformly in 0<=a<N. On the triangle u,v>=0, u+v<=1, max [J(u+v)-J(u)-J(v)]=2gamma_*. (4) To check (4), fix s=u+v. The expression is strictly concave in u: its second derivative is -pi sin(pi s)/[sin(pi u)sin(pi(s-u))]<0. The maximum has u=v=s/2. Its derivative in s is log(2cos(pi s/2)), so s=2/3 is the unique maximum. Its value is -3J(1/3)=-2J(1/6)=2gamma_*; the last identity follows by integrating the sine doubling formula and using J(1-s)=-J(s). Every entry of (2) is a Q-binomial coefficient times x^(u-a). Equations (2)--(4) therefore prove, uniformly on |M-1|<=1/(8N^3), ||C_T||, ||C_T^(-1)|| <= C_0 N^A0 exp(2gamma_*N). (5) The factor |x|^(u-a) is uniformly bounded there, and converting max entry to norm costs at most N. The bound is uniform in the integer degree T. Thus the full physical fusion condition number costs exp(4gamma_*N+O(log N)). It has not been declared subexponential. ## 3. A literal bidiagonal Casimir in this normalized frame Use the actual normalized tensor Casimir Omega=F_tot Ecal_tot+qK_tot+q^(-1)K_tot^(-1), Ecal_tot=Ecal_1K_2+Ecal_2, K_tot=K_1K_2. It commutes with f. Direct application to the seed vector gives Omega|0,j>=c_j(Y)|0,j> +(M Q^(-j)-M^(-1)) f|0,j-1>, c_j(Y)=q^(-1)Y Q^(-j)+qY^(-1)Q^j. (6) For example the first physical offdiagonal term before rewriting is (M Q^(-j)-M^(-1))(1-Q)|1,j-1>. Subtracting that same multiple of f|0,j-1> leaves the Cartan diagonal c_j(Y); this verifies (6) without inverting an endpoint coefficient. Commuting Omega through f^a and retaining the normalizer F_a gives C_T^(-1) Omega C_T |a,j> =c_j(Y)|a,j>+b_j(M)|a+1,j-1>, j=T-a, b_j(M)=(M Q^(-j)-M^(-1))(1-Q^(T-j+1)). (7) Targets outside the physical basis are omitted. In particular when j=0 the formal coefficient M-M^(-1) need not vanish away from completeness; |a+1,-1> is absent by the original endpoint convention. At a=d the displayed factor 1-Q^N genuinely vanishes. Thus (7) is an actual finite bidiagonal matrix, denoted H_T(M), valid also at the complete collisions. It uses no cyclic head completion. The actual generic-meridian crossing polynomial, derived from its finite highest-weight matrix in [the meridian Casimir note](meridian_casimir_source.md#1-the-fixed-operator-and-its-generic-meridian-spectrum), has eigenvalue lambda_j(Y)=nu_j Y^(-j), nu_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j+1)), |nu_j|=1. (8) This is the original crossing with the explicit common Cartan scalar recorded separately. Equations (2),(7),(8) identify its complete degree block by similarity, rather than merely comparing its spectrum. The finite-matrix verification of (8) is short. At total degree j write a highest vector h_j=sum_(a=0)^j beta_a |a,j-a>, beta_0=1. Its actual Ecal equation gives beta_(a+1)/beta_a =-e_(j-a)/[e_(a+1)xQ^(-(j-a-1))], e_a=M Q^(-a)-M^(-1). For generic M these denominators are nonzero. Multiplying cancels the e factors and gives beta_j=(-1)^j x^(-j)Q^(j(j-1)/2). The coefficient of |0,j> in the checked R h_j comes only from the zero-transfer term on |j,0>, so its eigenvalue is beta_j x^(-j), which is exactly (8). The N descendants of each h_j are nonzero generically by the elementary E F^r recurrence; f^N=0. Distinct c_j(Y) make these N summands independent and their dimensions total N^2. The defining finite R commutes with the actual total generators, so this computes the whole generic crossing, not just selected entries. ## 4. Explicit interval projectors with only one possible collision Fix nonnegative physical degrees r<=s from the j-interval of H_T. For generic M its c_j(Y) are distinct. The j-to-k bidiagonal spectral projector E_k has entry, from column s to row r, (E_k)_(r,s)= product_(l=r+1)^s b_l(M) /product_(l=r,l!=k)^s [c_k(Y)-c_l(Y)] if r<=k<=s, (E_k)_(r,s)=0 otherwise. (9) One proof expands the triangular resolvent: [(z-H_T)^(-1)]_(r,s)=product b_l/product_(l=r)^s(z-c_l), then takes the residue at c_k. This proves the full matrix formula, including intervals touching a physical endpoint. The exact factorization of each difference is c_k(Y)-c_l(Y) =qY^(-1)(Q^k-Q^l)[1-Y^2 Q^(-(k+l+1))]. (10) The first product of differences in (10), for l in [r,s], l!=k, has absolute value exactly |F_(k-r)F_(s-k)|. Its reciprocal is at most exp(2gamma_*N+O(log N)). The additional common factor |qY^(-1)|^(s-r) is not exactly one on the later meridian circle, but its logarithm is O(N delta) there and it is uniformly bounded above and below. For the second product the integers k+l+1 form an interval of length at most N, inside [1,2N-1], with the entry l=k omitted. There is at most ONE zero at M=1: k+l+1=N. If this is the omitted entry, there is no zero. This explicitly includes the simple self-paired node when N is odd and the near-endpoint nodes when N is even. After removing this possible zero and the omitted entry, the root product is a circular interval product of 1-Q^m. It is a ratio of factorials, or two such ratios when the interval crosses N. Its leading logarithm is the difference of two endpoint values of J; J(1)=0 accounts for the crossing. Hence that product AND its reciprocal are at most exp(2gamma_*N+O(log N)). Omitting one additional nonzero factor changes the bound only by O(log N), since 4/N <= |1-Q^m| <=2, 1<=m<N. This is a whole-product estimate; multiplying N separate polynomial bounds is not used. ## 5. The shrinking meridian circle retains all normalizers For any integer ell choose delta=1/[8N^3(1+|ell|)], M=1+delta exp(i theta). (11) All c_j(Y) are distinct on this circle: the other solutions of M^4=Q^m are a distance of order 1/N from one, while delta is smaller. For a nonzero root factor the relative change in its logarithm is O(delta/|1-Q^m|). Summing around a full interval costs at most O(delta N(1+log N))=O(1), because |1-Q^m|>=4min(m,N-m)/N. Thus the noncolliding product bound in Section 4 remains uniform on (11); there is no N^O(N) loss. The possible zero factor has magnitude |1-M^4| >=3delta, since |M^3+M^2+M+1|>=3 on this small circle. Its reciprocal costs at most C N^3(1+|ell|). The numerator of (9) has two interval products. At M=1 their moduli are |F_s/F_r|, |F_(T-r)/F_(T-s)|, where all indices lie in [0,d]. Each has leading exponent at most 2gamma_*N. Neither numerator interval contains a root-zero factor. The same harmonic-sum comparison preserves those bounds on (11). The factors M^(-1) in the first numerator product and qY^(-1) in each denominator difference contribute only exp(O(N delta)) over the complete intervals; they are retained on both sides. Combining them with BOTH denominator products proves, for all entries and degrees, |(E_k)_(r,s)| <= C_1 N^A1(1+|ell|) exp(8gamma_*N). (12) The eigenvalue powers in (8) are uniformly bounded on (11): |M^(-2j ell)| <= exp(4N|ell|delta) <2. Summing the at most N projectors and converting max entry to operator norm costs only a further polynomial. Combining with (5) gives ||B_N(M)^ell|| <= C_2 N^A2(1+|ell|) exp(12gamma_*N) (13) on the entire circle, in the ORIGINAL physical metric. The full original common Cartan has not disappeared. On the retained branch alpha=d+Log M/Log q it is kappa(M)=q^(alpha^2/2), kappa(M)/kappa(1) =M^d exp[(Log M)^2/(2Log q)]. (14) Its ell-th power has modulus bounded by exp(2N|ell|delta+C N|ell|delta^2), uniformly less than a fixed constant. Thus (13) holds for the unstripped crossing too, with its SAME original Cartan. The original framing scalars at M=1 have modulus one. There is no color-dependent factor chosen from a knot period here. Finally every actual signed crossing power is holomorphic near M=1: the finite defining R and its inverse have only the constant nonzero factorials F_a and powers of nonzero M as denominators. The apparent spectral poles in (9) cancel in the full matrix. Cauchy's formula at the center of (11), with the full matrix and Cartan retained, bounds its norm by the maximum norm on that circle. This proves (1). The circle integral introduces no extra delta^(-1) factor, since dM and the Cauchy denominator have the same radius. ## 6. Source-preserving whole-word consequence and scope The bound concerns a coherently contracted actual twist block before any absolute values. It can replace that block inside any original braid or plat, of arbitrary width, without changing a cap, pivot, modified-dimension factor, marked source or framing line. Therefore the preceding block-energy argument, on consecutive repeated-generator blocks of the specified original braid word, improves to limsup_N (2pi/N)log|P_N| <=sum_twist blocks min(|ell|v_8,12v_3). (15) The original reduced Kashaev scalar has the same bound. Blocks and width are fixed while N tends to infinity. The estimate is uniform in ell as stated in (1), but the whole-word asymptotic uses a fixed braid word. The strict comparison 12v_3<4v_8 makes every consecutive repeated-generator block of length at least four improve its separate-crossing bound. No tangle conversion of an arbitrary unoriented diagram twist region is asserted. This is still a coarse repeated-generator-block upper bound, not an estimate by Vol(S^3-K), a nonzero selected geometric coefficient or the volume conjecture. The strict constant comparison needs no numerical volume premise. For G=sum_(n>=0)(-1)^n/(2n+1)^2, G>8/9. The elementary Fourier series of the sine integral gives v_3=(3sqrt(3)/4)sum_(k>=0) [(3k+1)^(-2)-(3k+2)^(-2)]. The decreasing positive summand bounds its tail from k=1 by its first value plus its integral, so that sum is at most 3/4+9/400+1/60. Together with sqrt(3)<7/4 this gives v_3<10/9. Since v_8=4G>32/9, one obtains 3v_3<10/3<32/9<v_8, which proves 12v_3<4v_8 rigorously. Explicitly, this whole-source bound also holds at ODD braid width. For the original b-strand complete cut, retain the unitary pivot g and the original unit zero-framing correction in W. The exact cut identity is C=Tr_env[W(I tensor g^(tensor(b-1)))]=K_N I. Therefore |K_N| <= N^(b-1)||W||_op <= N^(b-1) product_t min(||B_sign(t)||_op^|ell_t|, C N^A(1+|ell_t|)exp(12gamma_*N)). (16) The first inequality follows directly by summing the N^(b-1) environment diagonal matrix elements and applying the operator norm. No positivity premise for the pivotal trace is required. The full ADO state differs at completeness by its retained root phase/N. Thus (16) includes all original source factors in modulus and gives (15) for either parity of braid width, without relying only on the even-plat notation of the gauge construction. ## 7. Independent actual-matrix audit python3 experiments/audit_actual_twist_block_factorial_frame.py The audit evaluates the generic-meridian R directly from the finite E^h tensor F^h sum, independently of the spectral reconstruction. It checks the normalized physical fusion, its explicit Euler inverse, the bidiagonal Casimir intertwining, every interval-projector entry, the difference factorization and the one-collision count, all physical degree endpoints, signed powers and the full Cartan continuation. Fresh result: **PASS**, 240 signed meridian/degree families through N=9, including both level parities. [Saved results](../experiments/actual_twist_block_factorial_frame_results.json). The new bound's exponential constants come from the uniform analytic product proof, not extrapolation of those finite tests. The previous Hermite norm theorem is left intact as an independent coarser bound.

title: A sharp projector barrier for the original repeated-crossing blocks
text: # A sharp projector barrier for the original repeated-crossing blocks 28 October 2026. The actual physical factorial frame gives a sharper uniform bound when its spectral-projector interval products are estimated together. Write v_3 for the regular ideal tetrahedron volume and v_8 for the regular ideal octahedron volume. There are absolute constants C,A such that, for every N>=2 and every integer ell, ||B_N^ell||_op <= C N^A(1+|ell|) exp[N(2v_3+v_8)/pi]. (1) B_N is the ORIGINAL complete crossing in the balanced physical metric, with its original unit Cartan and framing factors. The HS estimate costs one further factor N. No spectrum-only or semisimplicity assumption is used. The proof retains the actual nilpotent blocks by the meridian Cauchy argument in [the factorial-frame theorem](actual_twist_block_factorial_frame_bound.md). This improves that theorem's volume constant 12v_3 to 4v_3+2v_8. It is a coarse bound for the whole original knot source at arbitrary braid width, not the desired sharp hyperbolic-volume estimate. ## 1. The entire projector product, with its physical domain Keep the actual degree-T bidiagonal Casimir and interval-projector formula from Sections 3--5 of the factorial-frame theorem. Let integer indices 0<=r<=k<=s<N obey 0<=T-s<=T-r<N. Its projector entry is (E_k)_(r,s)=product_(l=r+1)^s b_l(M) /product_(l=r,l!=k)^s(c_k(M^2)-c_l(M^2)). Put J(u)=integral_0^u log(2sin(pi t))dt on [0,1], and extend J periodically. This is consistent because J(1)=0. In the following formula T,r,s,k denote the integer indices DIVIDED by N. The exact root-factorial identities give the leading projector exponent p(T,r,s,k)=J(s)-J(r)+J(T-r)-J(T-s) -J(k-r)-J(s-k)-J(k+s)+J(k+r). (2) The last two terms use the periodic extension. The physical domain is 0<=r<=k<=s<=1, 0<=T-s<=T-r<=1. (3) The numerator consists of two ordinary interval products. The first denominator is |F_(k-r)F_(s-k)|. The second is a circular root interval, with one factor omitted and at most one complete-meridian zero. Thus the endpoint-uniform factorial estimate gives (2) with error O(log N) after removing that possible zero. The +1 in k+l+1 shifts endpoints by 1/N; the logarithmic modulus of continuity of J bounds its effect by O(log N), uniformly even at the endpoints. This does not assume uniform separation from a root. On the specified circle |M-1|=delta=1/[8N^3(1+|ell|)], all noncolliding products change by a uniformly bounded factor, using the harmonic sum of their relative changes. The one possible zero costs at most C delta^(-1). The prefactors which are not exactly unit off the complete fiber have modulus exp(O(N delta)). Consequently |(E_k)_(r,s)| <=C_0 N^A0(1+|ell|) exp[N p(T/N,r/N,s/N,k/N)]. (4) Here the notation on the right restores integer indices. The constants are independent of the degree block and of the chosen spectral node. ## 2. Exact maximization of the projector exponent Let G(u)=log|2sin(pi u)|, periodically extended. For 0<=l<=1, every interval of length l has its G-integral between B(l)=2J(l/2), A(l)=J((1+l)/2)-J((1-l)/2)=-2J((1-l)/2). (5) Indeed G is symmetric and increases strictly with distance from its integer zero until that distance reaches 1/2. The minimum interval is centered at an integer and the maximum at a half-integer. Alternatively, differentiate J(t+l)-J(t): its regular stationary intervals have exactly these two centers. Moving through a singular endpoint gives the same ordering by continuity and monotonicity. The cases l=0,1 follow by limits. Set l=s-r. Both numerator differences in (2) are integrals over an interval of length l, so each is at most A(l). The last difference, J(k+s)-J(k+r), is at least B(l). The remaining split denominator obeys J(k-r)+J(s-k)>=2J(l/2). (6) For 0<l<1 this follows directly from strict convexity: d^2/dx^2 [J(x)+J(l-x)] =pi sin(pi l)/[sin(pi x)sin(pi(l-x))]>0. Symmetry places the minimum at x=l/2; the endpoints follow by continuity. Combining (5)--(6) gives p<=2A(l)-4J(l/2) =-4[J((1-l)/2)+J(l/2)] <=-8J(1/4)=v_8/pi. (7) For the last inequality the two arguments have sum 1/2, and the same convexity calculation places their minimum at 1/4 each. Equality in ALL these inequalities holds at T=1, r=1/4, s=3/4, k=1/2. These values satisfy (3). Thus v_8/pi is the exact maximum of the specified projector profile, not an estimate obtained by separately maximizing its factorials. The identity -8J(1/4)=v_8/pi uses v_8=8 Lambda(pi/4) and J(u)=-Lambda(pi u)/pi. ## 3. Restore both physical frames, eigenvalues and the complete source The explicit physical fusion and its inverse each have norm exp[2 gamma_* N+O(log N)], where gamma_*=v_3/(2pi). Both are necessary. The spectral eigenvalue powers are bounded on the delta circle; the full original Cartan obeys kappa(M)/kappa(1) =M^(N-1) exp[(Log M)^2/(2Log q)], whose ell-th power is bounded there too. Summing projectors costs only a polynomial. Equations (4)--(7) therefore bound the full matrix power on the circle by C N^A(1+|ell|) exp[N(4gamma_*+v_8/pi)]. The original matrix power is holomorphic across M=1 for either sign of ell. Cauchy's formula transfers this estimate to its center without another inverse delta. Since 4gamma_*+v_8/pi=(2v_3+v_8)/pi, this proves (1), including the complete nilpotent normal contribution. For a fixed b-strand braid closing to a knot, the original reduced cut is K_N I=theta_N^(-w) Tr_env[W_N(I tensor g_N^(tensor(b-1)))], where the retained complete pivot g_N is unitary and |theta_N|=1. Expanding that partial trace in an orthonormal environmental basis gives |K_N|<=N^(b-1)||W_N||_op. (8) This is a norm bound for the actual complex pivotal trace, not a claim that it is positive. Partition the specified word into consecutive repeated-generator blocks with nonzero exponents ell_t. The matrices are coherently multiplied inside each block BEFORE estimating. From (1), (8), and the independently proved one-crossing exponent, limsup_N (2pi/N)log|K_N| <=sum_t min(|ell_t|v_8, 4v_3+2v_8). (9) This applies to odd or even braid width and either sign of each block. It implies the corresponding full Fourier-energy upper bound by the audited polynomial ordinary-color remainder. The complete full-state modified-dimension factor is a specified root phase divided by N, so its exponential rate obeys the same estimate. None of those factors has been reset at an intermediate meridian. Every block of at least four crossings improves its separate-crossing bound, since 4v_3+2v_8<4v_8. The block must be a repeated generator of the specified braid; arbitrary diagram twist regions would require a proved tangle conversion. Formula (9) has not been shown to be bounded by Vol(S^3 minus K). It proves neither the sharp upper bound nor geometric survival. ## 4. Verification The root agent independently checked the actual factorial-frame proof and replayed its 240 generic-meridian signed-degree comparisons. Two other agents independently verified (2)--(7), including the circular interval and endpoint shifts. The supplementary audit `experiments/audit_actual_twist_block_projector_barrier.py` checks the profile inequalities, exact factorial products after zero removal, physical endpoint domains and convergence at the maximizing profile. These checks supplement the uniform proof above.

title: A polynomial-cost Fourier kernel for every original twist block
text: # A polynomial-cost Fourier kernel for every original twist block 29 October 2026. Every signed power of the original equal-color crossing has an explicit Chebyshev expansion whose coefficient mass is O(N(1+|ell|)). It retains the full Casimir Hermite jets, including the odd simple node. For a full twist ell=2p this supplies the coefficient kernel for the entire ordinary circle-color packet, rather than an inversion of a single complete-color circle. The [literal mixed-color circle calculation](actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md) identifies the displayed operators with the original pivotal encircling sources. This is therefore an exact quantitative source transformation at arbitrary width, with the marked cut unchanged. Polynomial coefficient mass does not prevent cancellation in the resulting filling sum, and does not prove geometric survival. ## 1. The complete local spectral data Use N>=2, d=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, kappa=q^(d^2/2). The original pair Casimir Omega has polynomial P_N(z)=2T_N(z/2)+2, c_k=w_k+w_k^(-1), w_k=q^(2k+1), 0<=k<N. Its distinct nodes have multiplicity two, except c=-2 when N is odd. The original full checked crossing is R=kappa r_N(Omega), with the original, already derived values and jets nu_k=r_N(c_k)=(-1)^k q^[k(k+1)], r_N'(c_k)/nu_k=-(d-2k)/[2(w_k-w_k^(-1))] (1) at double nodes. The possible simple node has only the value condition. These are the complete physical spectral data; there is no semisimple projection. For a negative power use the actual inverse crossing, not its adjoint. For any integer ell let f_(N,ell) be the unique polynomial of degree less than N representing r_N^ell modulo P_N. Negative powers exist because every nu_k is nonzero. Define finite data h_k=nu_k^ell, d_k=-(ell/2)(d-2k) h_k. (2) At double nodes, d_k=(w_k-w_k^(-1))f'(c_k). At the odd simple node d-2k=0 and w_k-w_k^(-1)=0, so d_k=0 without prescribing an additional derivative. All |h_k|=1 and |d_k|<=|ell|N/2. ## 2. Exact Fourier-Hermite interpolation Take the marked finite Fourier transforms H_n=(1/N)sum_k h_k w_k^(-n), D_n=(1/N)sum_k d_k w_k^(-n), 0<=n<N. (3) Then the COMPLETE polynomial is f_(N,ell)(z)=a_0+sum_(n=1)^d a_n 2T_n(z/2), a_0=H_0, a_n=[D_n+(N-n)H_n]/N, 1<=n<N. (4) Here is a direct proof, avoiding a conditioned confluent Vandermonde inverse. Set g(w)=f(w+w^(-1)). Its Laurent coefficients are a_0 and the symmetric pair a_n at exponents n and -n. Since w_k^N=-1, the node values and logarithmic derivatives have Fourier aliases H_n=a_n-a_(N-n), D_n=n a_n+(N-n)a_(N-n), 1<=n<N, H_0=a_0, D_0=0. (5) Solving the two equations gives (4). The paired nodes k,d-k have the same h and opposite d, so the compatibility conditions for (5) are automatic. At n=N/2, when present, H_n=0 and the second equation still gives the correct coefficient. At the odd simple node the logarithmic derivative of every such g is zero. Thus (4) imposes exactly the N original Hermite conditions, with no extra endpoint constraint, at every even and composite level too. Equation (4) immediately gives the uniform coefficient bounds |a_0|<=1, |a_n|<=1+|ell|/2. (6) No separation bound for nearby Casimir nodes is needed. ## 3. Full circle-color coefficients and their norm Let U_j denote the second-kind Chebyshev polynomial, U_0=1, U_1=z when its argument is z/2. Put a_N=a_(N+1)=0 and define beta_j=(-1)^j(a_j-a_(j+2)), 0<=j<N. (7) The identities 2T_n=U_n-U_(n-2), n>=2, and 2T_1=U_1 give f_(N,ell)(Omega) =sum_(j=0)^d beta_j (-1)^j U_j(Omega/2), R^ell=kappa^ell sum_(j=0)^d beta_j L_(j+1), L_(j+1)=(-1)^j U_j(Omega/2). (8) All phases, including kappa^ell, are retained. Summing (6) gives sum_(j=0)^d |beta_j| <= 2N(1+|ell|/2). (9) For ell=2p, (8) is an exact full-twist filling kernel of mass at most 2N(1+|p|). The separate [physical circle proof](actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md) realizes L_j as the actual ordinary pivotal j-color encircling operator, including its original framing and trace. A single L_N is not inverted or declared sufficient; the whole degree-<N basis occurs in (8). This bound holds uniformly in N and p, including negative twists and all gcd/parity cases. There is no division by p or by a Gauss sum. For ell=0 the expansion reduces exactly to L_1=I. For full twists the data in (3) are particularly explicit: h_k=Q^[p k(k+1)], d_k=-p(d-2k)h_k, H_n=(1/N)sum_k Q^[p k(k+1)]q^[-n(2k+1)]. (10) The corresponding D_n is the SAME finite quadratic sum with its retained linear normal weight -p(d-2k). Dropping this weight would erase the derivative data of the original crossing and generally change the invariant. Formula (10) specifies the filling phases before any large-N or long-filling analysis. ## 4. Simultaneous filling and the actual remaining theorem Replace a fixed collection of disjoint twist blocks R^(2p_i) by (8) BEFORE any exterior contraction. Distributivity gives the exact sum of the same original tensor diagram with circle operators L_(j_i) in those slots. All spectator tensors, the original marked cut and peripheral/framing line retain their order and values. The total coefficient mass is at most product_i [2N(1+|p_i|)]. (11) For a fixed number of blocks this is polynomial when the p_i are fixed; more generally its logarithm is o(N) whenever sum_i log(1+|p_i|)=o(N). Thus no exponential coefficient cost is introduced by retaining the complete circle-color data. Together with the physical circle identification, this supplies an original-source input for simultaneous crossing-circle fillings. It does not identify a fixed complete-color augmented-link scalar with this packet, nor replace its trace by a different invariant. The next geometric survival question is substantive: obtain a nonzero selected geometric period for that actual MIXED-COLOR augmented source and control the coherent filling sum (10). Taking absolute values in (11) gives only a maximum over the base packet; it does not automatically yield the smaller filled-manifold volume. No broad original-knot volume theorem is claimed by this expansion. The [complete Fourier--Hermite Gram](actual_filling_fourier_hermite_gram.md) turns these coefficients into an explicit positive Cauchy metric. Its exact dual cost is 1+ell^2(N^2-1)/(12N^2), uniformly bounded in N for a fixed twist. A literal original normalization insertion also proves that this metric's energy can be excessive even when the final knot is hyperbolic. A sharp geometric energy estimate requires more than the controlled filling-source norm. [Audit](../experiments/audit_actual_twist_circle_fourier_kernel.py): PASS 81 signed full-physical crossing-power comparisons at N=2,...,10 and 64 complex full-Hermite/coefficient-mass cases through N=48. Independent proof review checked both Fourier aliases, the even middle index, the odd simple node, and the circle-basis conversion.

title: A finite Gaussian certificate for original signed-twist source endpoints
text: # A finite Gaussian certificate for original signed-twist source endpoints 29 October 2026. Every FIXED signed crossing power has an explicit original-source endpoint asymptotic. Its leading coefficient is a finite algebraic function of N modulo8k. Nonvanishing can therefore be checked by finite exact arithmetic rather than assumed from a spectral curve. Powers3,4,5 all pass uniformly in N. Power4 supplies the next source endpoint after the [two-twist interaction](actual_newton_two_twist_interaction_packet.md). This is an endpoint theorem, not a new whole-knot asymptotic or a claim that arbitrary recurrences have no channel conversion. ## 1. The FULL original source, including its repeated nodes and signs Let N>=2,d=N-1,q=exp(pi i/N),Q=q^2,kappa=q^(d^2/2), and r=R/kappa. Use the actual fixed-root g-pivotal one-cut functional phi and put c_j=q^(2j+1)+q^(-2j-1), A_j=q^(2j+1)-q^(-2j-1), nu_j=(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)], j=0,...,d. For EVERY integer k the exact full-normal source is phi(r^k)=(-1)^(d+1)/2 sum_(j=0)^d nu_j^k [c_j-(k/2)(d-2j)A_j]. (1) This is derived from the actual spectral-JET functional, not an eigenvalue-only trace. At each double node, phi(f)=(-1)^d sum_double[(4-c^2)f'(c)-cf(c)] +odd_simple f(-2), r'(c_j)/r(c_j)=-(d-2j)/(2A_j). Since 4-c_j^2=-A_j^2, inserting f=r^k gives (1). Indices j,d-j give equal contributions; the odd simple node has c=-2,A=0 and is counted correctly by the half-sum. In particular the factor(-1)^d from the ORIGINAL pivot is retained. For the full crossing multiply (1) and all asymptotics below by kappa^k. The small powers are explicit exceptions to a nonzero N^(3/2) leading term: phi(1)=0, phi(r)=(-q)^d, and phi(r^2)=N(-q)^d. They are retained exact source identities, not discarded endpoints. ## 2. A finite, residue-class leading coefficient Fix k>0, put epsilon=k mod2, and for integers m define s_m=(2m-epsilon)/(2k), a(s)=(1-2s)sin(2pi s), b(s)=cos(2pi s), G_k(N)=sum_(0<s_m<1) (-1)^m a(s_m) exp[-i pi N(m-epsilon/2)^2/k]. (2) Then the all-level original source satisfies phi(r^k)=C_(N,k) N^(3/2)G_k(N)+O_k(N), C_(N,k)=(-1)^(d+1) exp[-i pi epsilon/2-i pi k/(4N)] (-i sqrt(k)/2)e^(i pi/4). (3) When k is odd the error improves to O_k(sqrt N). Negative powers are exactly complex conjugates of positive powers because r^sharp=r^(-1), the Newton basis and phi being real. To prove (3), use the half-grid s_j=(j+1/2)/N. EXACTLY on that grid, nu_j^k=exp[-i pi epsilon/2-i pi k/(4N)] exp[i pi N(ks_j^2+epsilon s_j)]. It is important to use epsilon, not k, in the linear term: replacing one by the other off the lattice changes its retained integer mark. Equation (1) is therefore the stated scalar prefactor times sum_j [b(s_j)-(ikN/2)a(s_j)] exp[i pi N(ks_j^2+epsilon s_j)]. The periodized amplitude is continuous at0 and1 because k+epsilon is even and a,b have matching endpoint values. Twice integrating its Fourier coefficients proves absolute convergence, so exact half-grid Fourier selection gives sum_j A(s_j)e^[i pi N(ks_j^2+epsilon s_j)] =N sum_(m in Z)(-1)^m integral_0^1 A(s)e^[i pi N(ks^2+(epsilon-2m)s)] ds. (4) For the finitely many interior stationary points complete the square. The compact-cutoff Gaussian integral is e^(i pi/4) A(s_m) e^[-i pi N(m-epsilon/2)^2/k]/sqrt(kN) +O_k(N^(-3/2)). An elementary justification is Fourier inversion of the smooth cutoff amplitude, the damped Gaussian integral, and |exp(it)-1|<=|t| against its integrable second Fourier moment. Away from those cutoffs two integrations by parts give summable O_k(N^(-2)(1+|m|)^(-2)) when A=a. For A=b the first boundary terms have matching endpoint phases and their difference is O_k(N^(-1)(1+|m|)^(-2)); hence their total is still summable. For odd k there is no endpoint resonance: the a sum in(4) equals its displayed stationary contribution plus O(N^(-1/2)). The b sum itself is O(sqrt N), with nonstationary remainder O(1). For even k the two possible resonant endpoints have a=0. Write a(s)=s a_0(s) near0 and similarly near1; one integration using the derivative of exp(i pi Nk s^2) bounds each endpoint integral by O_k(1/N). Their contribution to(4) is O_k(1). The b sum is O_k(sqrt N). Multiplying the a sum by N proves the error in(3). All endpoint and half-grid currents have thus been included. ## 3. A finite NONVANISHING test, and three explicit uniform cases Every coefficient in (2) is algebraic, and G_k(N) is periodic in N modulo8k. Consequently, if its finitely many residue-class values are all nonzero, their minimum modulus is positive and (3) proves c_k N^(3/2)<=|phi(R^k)|<=C_k N^(3/2) (5) at every sufficiently large level, with no parity or coprimality restriction. Failure of this leading test does not prove a zero endpoint: lower-order terms may survive. For example k=1,2 have G_k=0 and require their exact lower-order identities. Here are own exact nonvanishing checks: G_3(N)=-(2sqrt3/3)exp(-i pi N/12), G_4(N)=-exp(-i pi N/4). For k=5 put a_1=(4/5)sin(pi/5), a_2=(2/5)sin(3pi/5). Pairing m with k+1-m gives G_5(N)=2exp(-i pi N/20)[-a_1+a_2exp(-2pi i N/5)], |G_5(N)|>=2(a_1-a_2) =(8/5)sin(pi/5)[1-cos(pi/5)]>0. (6) These are uniform exact phase calculations, not fits at sampled levels. ## 4. A genuinely new endpoint for the next reduced turn word Let the original finite Green coefficients be P_i=F_i^2 sum_(v=0)^i Q^v/F_v^2, P_0=1, P_i=(1-Q^i)^2P_(i-1)+Q^i. The exact Newton source column obeys (r^3 1)_i=(-q)^i P_i, phi(r^4)=(-q)^d sum_(i=0)^d P_i. (7) For a finite proof of the first equality, multiply the known r and r^2 source kernels. The remaining convolution is F_i sum_j nu_j/F_(i-j); its generating series satisfies the displayed first-order P recurrence, with P_0=1. The second equality uses nu_j[d choose j]_Q=1 in the literal last-row multiplication by r. Combining k=4 in(3),(6) with(7) gives the explicit all-parity endpoint sum_(i=0)^d P_i =N^(3/2)exp[i pi(3-N)/4]+O(N). (8) Thus the next repeated-two-twist source has a known nonzero polynomial endpoint, rather than an unknown boundary value. Its interior is a new higher-order Ward problem; (8) does not by itself prove the necessary dominant projection or a coherent long-word estimate. This is the reusable analytic input a purely algebraic A-curve test would miss. A marked recurrence and its spectral cover must be supplemented by the ACTUAL source endpoint and any reciprocal inhomogeneous current. The finite certificate(2)--(5) supplies such endpoints for a family of original twist powers. It is a root-value source theorem; no q-normal derivative of a different generic source germ is substituted. ## 5. The next actual reduced word has an explicit rank-three current The previous endpoint is not merely a free parameter. Put C=T_1P_rev and consider its actual source vector C T_(-3)1. Its coefficients are (C T_(-3)1)_i=kappa^(-2)(-q)^(i-d)K_i, K_i=sum_(j=0)^i nu_j [i choose j]_Q conjugate(P_(d-j)). (9) The modular reduction identifies this with the fourth repeated two-crossing/turn run, up to its already recorded unit scalar. Thus it is a genuine next-depth original word, not an arbitrary clock coupon. Its two scalar endpoints are known: K_0=conjugate(P_d), K_d=sum_j conjugate(P_j). (10) They have the nonzero polynomial asymptotics of powers3 and4 above. There is also an EXACT whole-index Ward equation, including its current. Write G_i=K_i/F_i, G_i=0 for i<0, and Y=Q^i. Then for1<=i<=d, (1-Y)^3 G_i+B_iG_(i-1)+C_iG_(i-2)+D_iG_(i-3) =Q^2 delta_(i,1), B_i=-(1+Q+Q^2)+(4+3Q)Y-3Y^2, C_i=Q+Q^2+Q^3-(1+4Q)Y, D_i=Q^3(Q^(i-2)-1). (11) In particular D_2=0 is a second exact source reset. To verify (11), put B_j=conjugate(P_(d-j)); its original backward Green relation is (1-Q^j)^2B_j=B_(j-1)-Q^j. The coefficient a_j=nu_j B_j/F_j therefore satisfies (1-Q^j)^3a_j=-Q^j a_(j-1)-nu_j Q^j/F_(j-1). Convolve with E(z)=sum z^k/F_k and use sum nu_j z^j/F_j=(Qz;Q)_infinity, as a formal identity below degreeN. The generating equation is (z;Q)_3G(z)+(Qz-3)(1-Qz)(1-Q^2z)G(Qz) +3(1-Q^2z)G(Q^2z)-G(Q^3z)=Q^2z, whose coefficients are exactly (11). All finite denominators are units. For the monic variable M_i=F_i^3G_i=F_i^2K_i the classical spectral polynomial is lambda^3+(-3+7Y-3Y^2)lambda^2 +(3-5Y)(1-Y)^3lambda-(1-Y)^7. (12) At Y=1 this is lambda^2(lambda+1). The initial data obey M_0=conjugate(P_d), M_1=(1-3Q+Q^2)conjugate(P_d)+Q^2; the actual current is visible. Equation (12) is a concrete new vector-recurrence test for any proposed general spectral criterion. The known scalar endpoints (10) do NOT by themselves determine its dominant projection across the cubic cover. That requires a full vector boundary/current certificate; no single-branch survival or sharp next-depth rate is asserted here. Audit: [full original signed matrices, finite coefficients and Gaussian endpoints](../experiments/audit_actual_twist_endpoint_gaussian_certificate.py). Independent proof review and primary replay passed, including the fixed-root pivot sign, all original positive/negative matrices, half-grid marks, endpoint resonances and explicit k4/k5 nonvanishing. The k=0,1,2 exceptions and possible vanishing of a scalar leading coefficient remain explicit. The [endpoint-vector companion](actual_newton_run_endpoint_vectors.md) resolves all Gaussian boundary modes even when that scalar cancels.

title: Whole Fourier polarization of the actual second cut
text: # Whole Fourier polarization of the actual second cut Research theorem, 27 October 2026. The second identity wire admits an exact change of polarization over its WHOLE actual coefficient ring. It preserves the original source, every peripheral factor, both endpoint defects and normal derivatives. Its Fourier variable is independent of the old physical edge position. A bounded-band Gaussian statement gives a character incidence, rather than an identification of these two bases. ## 1. The actual tensor and its unchanged source Use the literal two-cut tensor of [the port reconstruction](actual_two_cut_framing_port_reconstruction.md), T_(c,d;a,b), 0<=a,b,c,d<N. The original pivots, caps, crossing scalars, preferred peripheral lifts and zero-framing line are already in T. Opening an internal identity edge supplies no new pivot. Its original source is Phi(T)=(1/N) sum_(a,c,b) T_(c,b;a,b). (1.1) Thus the first cut retains its actual rank-one row, including all first output bands. The second cut is an identity closure. For charge-zero uninserted/scalar-Green tensors c+d=a+b; (1.1) then also equals the double-diagonal sum/N. Current tensors require (1.1), not that restricted formula. Let R be the actual ring localized at the differences Q^i-Q^j, i!=j, for 0<=i,j<N. Every such difference is a unit at a primitive Q_N. Retain all other actual parameters, including q with q^2=Q, M, Q^N, M^N and the original peripheral rational maps/lattices. Put y_j=Q^j, V_(j,b)=y_j^b. The determinant is the usual product of y_j-y_i. Elementary polynomial interpolation gives the exact inverse (V^-1)_(b,j)=[X^b] L_j(X), L_j(X)=product_(m!=j) (X-y_m)/(y_j-y_m). (1.2) This is an isomorphism of finite free R-modules before taking jets. Define T^V=(I tensor V) T (I tensor V^-1). Partial trace on the second wire proves EXACTLY sum_j T^V_(c,j;a,j)=sum_b T_(c,b;a,b), Phi(T^V)=Phi(T). (1.3) All actual matrix products, inserted Green observables and Hopf rows are transported by this same conjugation. For example the actual two-port coproduct is (I tensor V) Delta(h) (I tensor V^-1), with the original ordering and prefixes. It is not replaced by a scalar left/right action on a reshaped diagonal array. An internal wire requires V and V^-1 on its two sides, so arbitrary word composition, cups/caps and all existing closure factors are preserved. For original source maps psi and phi on that wire, a general boundary source is transported as V psi and phi V^-1. Here the identity closure is invariant, which explains (1.3). This is a basis change of the actual state and source, not the definition of a replacement state. At the primitive root, character orthogonality gives (V^-1)_(b,j)=Q_N^(-bj)/N. (1.4) The RAW new two-variable array retaining the first source is Jtilde_(a,j)=sum_c T^V_(c,j;a,j), Phi(T)=(1/N)sum_(a,j) Jtilde_(a,j). (1.5) For charge-zero T this becomes the exact full-band formula Jtilde_(a,j)=(1/N) sum_(b,q) Q_N^(jq) T_(a-q,b+q;a,b). (1.6) Only physically supported terms occur, with zero extension otherwise. The 1/N in (1.6) is the Fourier inverse; it does NOT replace the original 1/N in (1.5). The entire finite band range is transformed before any Gaussian expansion. At Q_N, if one instead fixes c=a in T^V, charge conservation forces d=b in the old tensor. Consequently T^V_(a,j;a,j)=(1/N)sum_b T_(a,b;a,b), independent of j. The new momentum coordinate survives because the first source is retained, rather than replaced by a diagonal trace. ## 2. Exact whole clock and shift operators, including endpoints On the old head let B=diag(Q^b), J=diag(b), and U=sum_(b<N-1) E_(b+1,b), Uflat=sum_(b>0) E_(b-1,b). These are truncated shifts; U^-1 is not notation for Uflat. Put C=V B V^-1, Y=diag(y_j), u_j=y_j^N, v^t=e_(N-1)^t V^-1, uminus_j=y_j^-1, w^t=e_0^t V^-1. Direct evaluation of a polynomial at the N nodes proves C_(i,j)=delta_(j,i+1) if i<N-1, C_(N-1,j)=L_j(Q^N), V U V^-1=Y-u v^t, V Uflat V^-1=Y^-1-uminus w^t. (2.1) For example (V U)_(j,b)=y_j^(b+1), except for its missing last column. Subtracting that column gives the rank-one correction. The backward identity removes the missing first column. At Q_N, C is the cyclic backward shift, u is the all-ones column, v_j=y_j/N, and w_j=1/N. The WHOLE last row in (2.1) must be retained before normal differentiation. For 1<=m<N the complete higher forward carry is V U^m V^-1=Y^m -sum_(b=N-m)^(N-1) (y_j^(b+m))_j e_b^t V^-1. (2.2) In particular the transform does not cyclically identify the original finite head or its Green tails. The finite relative head/tail module is carried along by the same isomorphism. Unwrapped tails are not discarded or aliased by using (1.4); their exact independent-power Fourier cap is recorded in [the finite Fourier theorem](finite_band_fourier_cap_and_independent_clock.md). The actual balanced finite matrices, as literal compressed matrices for whole Q,M, are F=U(I-QB), Ecal=Uflat(M B^-1-M^-1 I), K=x B^-1, x=-M/q. Their exact transforms are F^V=Y(I-QC)-(1-Q^N)u v^t, Ecal^V=Y^-1(M C^-1-M^-1 I) -(M-M^-1)uminus w^t, K^V=x C^-1. (2.3) Indeed v^t C=Q^(N-1)v^t and w^t C^-1=w^t. These identities prove (2.3), including its signs. Thus the two actual endpoint defects delta=1-Q^N and kappa=M-M^-1 remain distinct. At the complete root both vanish, but D_Q[-delta u v^t]_(Q_N)=N u v^t, D_M[-kappa uminus w^t]_(M=1)=-2 uminus w^t. (2.4) Here D_Q=Q partial_Q and D_M=M partial_M with the other parameter fixed. The simultaneous integral-color path must subsequently be pulled back with its actual q/M relation. These normal terms cannot be removed by specializing (2.3) prematurely. Likewise C^N=V diag(Q^(Nb)) V^-1, C^N|_(Q_N)=I, D_Q(C^N)|_(Q_N)=N V J V^-1. (2.5) The cyclic root value does not identify its whole normal clock. ## 3. The normal connection of this actual basis change For fixed N, the matrix A_Q=(D_Q V)V^-1=J_eval (V J V^-1), J_eval=diag(j), (3.1) is regular at the primitive root. Differentiating an arbitrary whole transported matrix gives D_Q T^V=(I tensor V)(D_Q T)(I tensor V^-1) +[I tensor A_Q,T^V]. (3.2) Every normal jet follows by the product rule; the connection term is forced. Partial trace of its commutator is zero entrywise on the first wire, so it preserves the full original source also at first normal order. Invariant functions or extra source-dependent coupons must themselves be transported, rather than commuted past V without their endpoint terms. In the usual complex root metric V/sqrt(N) is unitary. Hence ||A_Q||_op <= (N-1)^2. (3.3) This is a polynomial bound for the forced FIRST normal basis term, not a bound for the actual entire knot state. Regularity holds in a root-dependent neighborhood for each N. It does not produce a single meromorphic family at the accumulation point Log Q=0. The same statements hold with the original full ADO peripheral line d_N(M)=epsilon_N (M-M^-1)/(M^N-M^-N) retained as its actual rational map/source lattice. Nothing here replaces it by its complete value epsilon_N/N before derivatives. ## 4. Independent band and position variables before polarization Write J^(p,q)_(a,b)=T_(a+p,b+q;a,b) and F(x,y;xi,eta)=sum J^(p,q)_(a,b) x^a y^b xi^p eta^q. The coupling variables x,y generate position weights. The physical input clock at the second cut is B=Q^b, while eta generates the OUTPUT OFFSET q. Direct index identities give B_input: y -> Qy, B_output: (y,eta) -> (Qy,Qeta), q moment: E_eta=eta partial_eta, Phi(T)=(1/N) CT_eta F(1,1;1,eta). (4.1) These are different commuting coordinates before a polarization. The last cap closes the band and leaves the physical b sum intact. The finite root average and unwrapped alias corrections are exact in [the independent-clock cap theorem](finite_band_fourier_cap_and_independent_clock.md). Equations (1.2)--(1.6) instead change the actual wire basis: the old physical b is summed internally, and j becomes an external spectral coordinate. This is a source-preserving change of polarization, rather than the substitution B=eta. For a finite Laurent test h(eta)=sum h_n eta^n, its literal cap coupon is X_h=sum_(n>=0) h_n U^n +sum_(n<0) h_n Uflat^(-n), with unsupported shifts zero. Indeed CT selects q=-n, and (X_h)_(b,b+q)=h_(-q). Thus CT h F is the original source with X_h inserted on the identity wire. The Toeplitz coupon map is not multiplicative at finite endpoints. Its original Ward row must be retained. The actual negative-band moment calculation in [the boundary-current note](actual_negative_band_boundary_moment_and_ward_atom.md) gives explicit signed-crossing examples where this insertion is nonzero although the uninserted source is zero. ## 5. Principal incidence and the first bounded-test correction This section is a LOCAL formal Gaussian theorem with bounded band tests. It is separate from the exact whole finite transform above. Keep the old physical exterior positions (A,B) fixed. Use the actual integral tree extension of the port-offset lattice in [the port theorem](actual_two_cut_framing_port_reconstruction.md). For charge-zero offsets (p,q)=(-q,q), let nu=Hq be the small continuous boundary displacement. The resulting enlarged actual phase and amplitude are S(u,nu), a_0(u,nu), with u transverse. They come from those original coefficient atoms, including Cartan, pivot and half-step terms. Work at a regular critical point with S_u=0, invertible S_uu, and nonzero a_0. Let u(nu) be its formal critical continuation and put W(nu)=S(u(nu),nu), A_0(nu)=a_0(u(nu),nu)/sqrt(det(-S_uu(u(nu),nu))), p_e=exp(W'(0)), alpha=(partial_nu log A_0)(0), beta=W''(0)/2. (5.1) The square-root line is the original fixed Gaussian line; its constant choice cancels in the ratio. If a varying lattice measure is needed, it is included in a_0. The chosen affine integral tree coordinates have fixed measure. Formal stationary phase gives, for EACH fixed q, Z_q/Z_0=p_e^q[1+H(q alpha+q^2 beta)+O(H^2)]. (5.2) Proof: write the actual formal block as exp(W(nu)/H) A_0(nu)[1+H z_1(nu)+O(H^2)] and substitute nu=Hq. Taylor expansion gives (5.2). The first Gaussian correction z_1 cancels from this normalized ratio at order H; its difference z_1(Hq)-z_1(0) first contributes at order H^2. All constant base lines cancel too. This proof neither estimates a saddle remainder nor sums q growing with N. For an explicit contraction form let G=S_uu^-1, g=d_u log a_0, ell=S_nu, and b^i=-G^(ij)g_j+(1/2)G^(il) S_(ljk)G^(jk). Implicit differentiation and the determinant rule give exactly alpha=partial_nu log a_0+b^i ell_i -(1/2)G^(ij)ell_(ij), beta=(S_(nu nu)-ell_i G^(ij)ell_j)/2, (5.3) all evaluated at nu=0,u(0). This also derives (5.2) directly with covariance -HG. Actual bounded changes of the chosen tree particular solution translate u and give the same block ratios. Flattening/period marks are held fixed; an N-dependent log-deck move is not such a bounded translation. Now interpret Delta(t)=sum_(q in Z)t^q as a FORMAL Laurent distribution, paired only with finite Laurent tests. It is not an ordinary function to evaluate at t=1. Equations (5.2) yield Zhat(eta)=Z_0{Delta(eta p_e) +H(alpha E_eta+beta E_eta^2)Delta(eta p_e)+O(H^2)}. For every fixed Laurent polynomial h, finite coefficient extraction therefore gives the rigorous bounded-test identity CT_eta h(eta) Zhat(eta) =Z_0{h(p_e^-1) +H{-alpha E_eta h+beta E_eta^2 h}_(eta=p_e^-1) +O(H^2)}. (5.4) Each test uses only finitely many fixed bands, so the port theorem and Gaussian contraction suffice. The principal Fourier incidence is eta p_e=1. It does not eliminate the physical B coordinate. For the ACTUAL identity cap h=1, the right side is Z_0 exactly, including all corrections: only q=0 is extracted. The remaining physical position sum and its original support/tails persist. If beta!=0, (5.4) has a second derivative on test functions; an ordinary coordinate substitution plus a scalar unit has only a first derivative at this order and cannot reproduce this map. The principal geometric chart eta_geo=p_e^-1 and its rational boundary residues can still be studied. They are NOT images of the original finite cap eta=0 merely by (5.2) or (5.4). In particular [the exact first Gaussian calculation](figure_eight_first_loop_cap_residue.md) is a calculation on that candidate geometric incidence boundary, not a proof of the cap-cycle pushforward. A whole open-phase Fourier stationary construction must use (1.2)--(1.6), its full support and source before any local reduction. ## 6. Audit and scope [The exact operator/source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_two_cut_fourier_polarization.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_two_cut_fourier_polarization_results.json) check generic/root Vandermonde inverse and carries, the forced normal connection, both actual boundary terms, full source and actual signed-braid tensors. The bounded-test formulas are independently checked on quadratic non-diagonal Gaussian models. This theorem supplies a genuine whole change of polarization of the actual pointed finite state. It proves no global geometric cycle comparison, no nonzero selected geometric block, and no hyperbolic-volume limit. Those require transporting the actual source through the remaining geometric/cyclotomic construction.

title: Two physical cuts reconstruct both framing positions and their port currents
text: # Two physical cuts reconstruct both framing positions and their port currents Research construction, 27 October 2026. Two actual edge positions can be used as integral framing coordinates. Opening those two physical edges gives a literal four-port tensor whose double diagonal is the partially summed two-position array. The original source is its sum divided by N, with no second pivot inserted. The full port bands retain the actual Hopf currents and their cut co-sources. For bounded port shifts, proper coefficient ratios and the same transverse Gaussian give a canonical nonzero LOCAL band-kernel map. It is linear on the interior current identities; the exact finite endpoint rows remain separate relative data. It is not a product-preserving finite-matrix map, nor a selection of the global framing cycle or its orientation. ## 1. An etale pair of physical edge positions exists integrally Use the original actual coefficient model, its full marked peripheral factors, and the regular geometric critical chart of [the partial support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md). At fixed meridian its critical framing torsor has dimension two. The original cut position a_0 has nonzero differential there. Every transfer is an integer difference of physical edge positions, in the actual oriented boundary convention. Here differentials on the critical chart mean the continuous logarithmic physical clocks u_e=H a_e; the integer labels specify their lattice and are not independent continuous functions there. If every edge differential were a multiple of da_0 on this two-dimensional tangent space, all transfer differentials would be multiples of da_0. All independent flow differentials would then have rank at most one, a contradiction. Thus some other physical edge e has da_0 wedge da_e != 0 (1.1) on a dense open subchart. This selects a FIXED edge of the diagram, not a level-dependent change of state. Shrink to its regular etale chart and put a=a_0, b=a_e. There is no hidden lattice index. Let G be the connected closed four-valent diagram graph, with the actual oriented integer flow lattice L=ker(incidence). Bivalent bends/cups/caps may be collapsed after transporting their dual basis labels; their actual frame matrices and scalar coefficients remain in the tensor network. The affine relabeling a->N-1-a in a self-dual chart, if used, is recorded rather than discarded. It does not change L or its index. For any set S of removed edges, incidence ranks give rank(ev_S:L->Z^S)=|S|+1-c(G\S). (1.2) Indeed rank L=E-V+1, and its kernel under evaluation on S is the cycle lattice of G\S, of rank E-|S|-V+c(G\S). For S={e_0,e}, (1.1) forces rank two, hence G\S is connected. Choose a spanning tree disjoint from both edges. Fundamental cycles of the complementary chords form an integral basis of L, and their evaluations on these two edges are the two coordinate vectors, up to the fixed orientation signs. Thus (a,b,j_1,...,j_(m-1)) (1.3) are unimodular actual flow coordinates. No finite cover or congruence class is introduced. The actual finite support and all zero-extension boundary inequalities are transported by this integer change of variables. The physical clocks are A=Q^a and B=Q^b. Actual q^a,q^b and the original half-Cartan root marks are retained in the coefficient field, as in the partial support theorem. The unimodular argument introduces no NEW lattice cover and does not erase those existing lift characters. ## 2. A literal cut tensor, rather than an invented second state In a braid circuit write the word as A B at a level containing the selected edge e, on tensor slot t. Let E_bd^(t) be the literal matrix unit inserted into that wire. Keep the original closure caps, pivots and framing/peripheral lines in the SAME places. Let P denote their contraction, leaving the original cut open. Define the four-port tensor by T_(a,b)^(c,d)=[P(A E_bd^(t) B)]_(c,a). (2.1) This is an explicit reconstruction using N^2 insertions in the ORIGINAL network. The inserted matrix unit replaces the identity on that one edge; no extra color, trace, state, cap or pivot has been introduced. The same definition works in any cup/cap/plat diagram: replace that literal wire identity by E_bd and contract all other original tensors. It is independent of how the finite contraction is parenthesized. Since sum_b E_bb=I, re-closing just this identity edge gives C_(c,a)=sum_b T_(a,b)^(c,b). (2.2) If the original diagram happens to put a diagonal transport on this edge, it is retained on its ORIGINAL side in (2.1), or its known entries are included in T. An independently added g_b would change (2.2). In particular cutting an ordinary internal identity edge does NOT authorize a second pivotal trace. Set J_(a,b)=T_(a,b)^(a,b). (2.3) Actual total-index conservation makes the reclosed C diagonal termwise for the original kernel and all scalar Green moments. The original cut coupon has diagonal entries 1/N, hence original reduced period=(1/N)sum_(a,b) J_(a,b). (2.4) This is 1/N, not 1/N^2. Every original pivot, zero-framing line, meridian lift character, base compact factor and external d_N(M) remains where it was in (2.1); multiplying (2.4) by the retained external line gives the original full state. Equivalently the exact weighted family is F(x,y)=(1/N)Tr_cut[ x^J P(A y^(J_t) B)]. (2.5) Its coefficient of x^a y^b is J_(a,b)/N. Thus the two-position array is realized by two physical wire couplings before any formal completion. It is not only an arbitrary array relabeled as a matrix. ## 3. Actual Hopf transport through the cut coupon In a genuine integral q-family use the ordinary cap P_o. At the original root use the original pivotal cap with its retained scalar adapter. For any actual h, pivotal Hopf naturality gives the exact insertion identity D_h P_o(A X B)=P_o[A D_h,tot(X) B], (3.1) where X is ANY inserted operator at the chosen intermediate level, and D_h=ad_h-epsilon(h). The words A,B intertwine the respective actual coproduct representations; their boundary object orders are not silently identified. For a plat, the same proof uses its actual intertwiners and duality maps before and after the chosen wire. Thus (3.1) is valid with all actual cups/caps present. For X=E_bd^(t), (3.1) is a specified current map from the physical second cut to the original cut. It contains the TRUE total adjoint, including its mixed terms; the local coupon is not presumed to be a tensor-product submodule. For example, in a parallel ordered tensor object E_tot=sum_i E_i K_(i+1)...K_l, F_tot=sum_i K_1^(-1)...K_(i-1)^(-1) F_i. For a local coupon X in slot t, put k_X X=K_t X K_t^(-1) when X is a weight matrix unit. Then D_E,tot(X)=[E_tot,X] K_tot^(-1), D_F,tot(X)=F_tot X-k_X^(-1) X F_tot. (3.2) The E commutator has its local term [E_t,X]K_(t+1)...K_l and, for EVERY i<t, the term E_i K_(i+1)...K_(t-1) [K_t,X] K_(t+1)...K_l. The F expression has its local term K_1^(-1)...K_(t-1)^(-1)(F_tX-k_X^(-1)XF_t), and the prefix terms (1-k_X^(-1))X K_1^(-1)...K_(i-1)^(-1)F_i for i<t. Terms i>t cancel exactly. These are the actual induced off-diagonal/prefix rows; omitting them amounts to replacing the true coproduct by a different one. In a dual tensor slot use its actual contragredient matrices, with the same ordered formula. If the weighted word or scalar Green insertions occur, (3.1) has the explicit additional local crossing/weight currents from [the whole Ward construction](actual_divided_ward_closure_and_green_caps.md). For the frozen off-root ADO cap add its recorded defect R_h=chi^(-1)ptr_K[M_(Z^J),ad_h]. (3.3) Thus this construction does not assume auxiliary truncated generic-q/M matrices are genuine Hopf intertwiners. It applies directly on the original root family or on the genuine integral q-family, and keeps the actual defect rows on another lift. ## 4. The off-diagonal port bands and the ORIGINAL source Retain the complete bands J^(p,q)_(a,b)=T_(a,b)^(a+p,b+q), (4.1) zero outside all four actual port ranges. This is a lossless finite encoding of T. In a parallel oriented charge convention the original scalar tensor has p+q=0. A contragredient cut uses its recorded sign or index reversal, not a new conservation law. The source on these bands is essential. With the original cut row e_0, (2.2) gives on EVERY current tensor Phi^(2)(T)=sum_(a,b,p) (e_0)_(a,a+p) J^(p,0)_(a,b). (4.2) In the original balanced source e_0 has every entry 1/N. Thus a homogeneous current of cut degree d uses its p=d band with the same factor 1/N. Only a charge-zero scalar kernel reduces to (2.4). Applying the J^(0,0) source to all Hopf currents would delete precisely the original off-diagonal cut co-sources. For illustration the first output/input port actions are exactly (L_A T)^(p,q)_(a,b) =sum_r A_(a+p,a+r) J^(r,q)_(a,b), (R_B T)^(p,q)_(a,b) =sum_s B_(a+s,a) J^(p-s,q)_(a+s,b). (4.3) The second-port formulas interchange a,p with b,q. Substituting the actual E,F,K, antipodes or dual matrices gives every shifted band and its endpoint coefficient. The [independent band-current audit](two_cut_port_band_current_audit.md) records these rows explicitly. All divided rows are obtained with the full actual coproduct, not by raising a projected scalar row. The grouped array matrix has ROW=a and COLUMN=b. It is not the ordinary matrix of a one-cut tangle. Even the actual two-cut unknot has T_(a,b)^(c,d)=delta_(c,b)delta_(d,a), so J=I. Then the double diagonal of (E tensor I)T is zero, whereas EJ=E is nonzero. Thus a single physical Hopf port action does NOT descend to ordinary left multiplication on J. Actual boundary reordering may also require braidings or dualities. Those matrices, and their transported coproduct order, must be kept rather than assigning the grouped T a naive Delta action. There is nevertheless an explicit scalar-coordinate lift. For matrix units define the balanced port channel L_ij(T)=(E_ij tensor I)T(E_ji tensor I). Its double diagonal is E_ij J. On the second port the channel (I tensor E_ji)T(I tensor E_ij) has double diagonal J E_ij. These formulas produce exact row and column position shifts and clocks. Their matrix-algebra unit on the full tensor space is a diagonal projection, not its identity. A physical crossing can leave that projection and return through an exchange band, so these channels are NOT a product-preserving replacement of the whole R network. The [two-coordinate Green/coherent construction](two_cut_matrix_green_and_coherent_source.md) supplies the full left/right Toeplitz shifts with both row/column tails and their corner. Apply its relative endpoint construction bandwise to the actual allowed windows in (4.1). No tail created by a Green translation is folded back into a physical port. ## 5. A canonical nonzero local Gaussian map for bounded bands This physical opening supplies more than scalar coordinate names. Remove both cut edges. The remaining internal graph is connected. Prescribing port shifts p,q with the balanced total charge gives an integer boundary-divergence vector of total zero. The incidence matrix of the chosen spanning tree solves it integrally: the flow on an oriented tree edge is the signed sum of divergences in its child subtree. All internal chord flows remain free. Consequently each fixed band has actual coefficients I^(p,q)(a,b,j), j in Z^(m-1), on an affine integral flow coset, with the same free chords as I^(0,0). Relative to the latter parametrization, every local edge position and crossing transfer changes by an integer constant, bounded in terms of the diagram and |p|+|q|. Actual proper factorial/Cartan ratios therefore give, on the strict interior, I^(p,q)=R_(p,q)(q,M,clocks) I^(0,0). (5.1) This is an identity derived from the ORIGINAL coefficients. R_(p,q) is a finite product of the recorded rational shift ratios and meridian/lift monomials. Every common base-only Cartan, compact-factor and peripheral line remains common; it is not reset to a numerical ideal value. On the regular geometric chart, the variable shape arguments avoid 0 and 1, so for FIXED bounded port shifts its leading coefficient is a unit. The strict-support cone remains nonempty for all large N after such a fixed shift. Equation (5.1) is an INTERIOR identity; its finite zero-extension endpoint rows remain their separate relative data. Because (a,b) is etale on the critical torsor, the remaining m-1 Hessian is nondegenerate. Let G_(a,b) be the original transverse Gaussian and define Z^(p,q)=G_(a,b)[R_(p,q) I^(0,0)]. (5.2) This has the same marked action/base line as Z^(0,0), and its leading amplitude is R_(p,q)|_crit times the nonzero amplitude of Z^(0,0). In particular it is nonzero on the stated chart. The construction is independent of the integral particular-flow choice. Two choices differ by a cycle supported entirely in the internal graph, hence by an integer translation of the transverse chords. The exact formal Gaussian translation identity, with its correspondingly shifted insertion and critical point, identifies the two formulas when these choices are fixed independently of N (or differ by uniformly bounded shifts). Adding an N-dependent full cycle is a finite logarithmic-deck move and also requires transport of its separate flattening/period mark. A different fixed unimodular chord basis changes only the actual recorded orientation/half-density frame. This is a canonical LOCAL band-kernel after those original marks are fixed. Every bounded ordinary port Ward row in Sections 3--4 is a finite linear combination of shifts and insertions in these same actual affine arrays. Formula (5.2), with the exact opposite shift on its insertion, is consequently a linear COCHAIN pushforward of their INTERIOR current identities. The exact finite support and framing endpoints stay in the explicitly recorded relative summand; this assertion does not evaluate their geometric images. This is the translation-covariant Wick formula of [the residual-current theorem](residual_gaussian_ward_currents.md), now with BOTH external coordinates represented by physical cuts. The principal B1 fields project independently to (a,b) by (1.1). Their scalar position directions therefore have the left/right array realization above; their complete Hopf rows retain the off-diagonal and prefix data of (3.2)--(4.3). This is not an identification of a finite fixed-N matrix algebra with a scalar function algebra. It is a linear map on an actual local coefficient/current completion. It also makes no claim for port shifts growing like N, for summing all such bands, or for the behavior at the two external finite-window boundaries. ## 6. The nearest actual bands measure the physical wave momentum Their principal ratio can be computed without guessing an extra source. Use the ACTUAL balanced/factorial boundary frame. The crossing generating functions satisfy dS_vertex=sum_out Log(p_new) du -sum_in Log(p_new) du. (6.1) This follows from the exact generating relations already derived from the actual crossing ratios in [the marked holonomy calculation](marked_braid_holonomy.md), with the canonical boundary form in [the determinant-line proof](quantum_source_bridge_extension.md). The actual diagonal factorial frame change adds its output-minus- input boundary primitive; accordingly its momentum is p_new=(1-A)p_old. Using p_old in (6.1) while keeping the new constant source would change the band marks. Sum (6.1) over the open network at its original geometric critical point. All internal edge terms cancel by momentum continuity. The only boundary terms are Log p_(0,out) du_(0,out)+Log p_(e,out) du_(e,out) -Log p_(0,in) du_(0,in)-Log p_(e,in) du_(e,in). (6.2) The original cut has p_(0,in)=p_(0,out)=1. At the second identity edge p_(e,in)=p_(e,out)=p_e. The original closed pivotal phases can add 2pi i integer multiples to the logarithmic momenta. Their exponentiated multipliers are one; their finite coefficients and flattening/period marks remain retained in the exact ratios. In the band J^(p,q), the inputs a,b are held fixed and the outputs are a+p,b+q. Hence the first action change is (S_(p,q)-S_0)/H=p Log p_(0,out)+q Log p_(e,out)+O(H). The integral tree particular flow makes no additional term: its internal contributions cancel in (6.2). The shifted regular amplitude tends to the original amplitude. Thus the ratio in (5.1) has the EXACT marked principal symbol R_(p,q),0=p_cut^p p_e^q. For the nearest charge-zero exchange bands this gives R_(+1,-1),0=p_e^(-1), R_(-1,+1),0=p_e. (6.3) These are the ACTUAL local edge wave momenta in the physical Gauss matrix. If a developed Wirtinger meridian is written in a common global frame, its prefix conjugation must be retained: that matrix is not silently identified with the local Gauss matrix solely because both are meridians. There is a useful precise parity consequence on a physical two-parabolic chart. Suppose the matrices in the same ACTUAL physical cut frame are as follows, with Tr(g_cut g_e) a FIXED representation invariant on that framing chart: g_cut=[[1+s,-s],[s,1-s]], g_e=[[k,(1-k)p_e],[(k-1)/p_e,2-k]]. Put z=s(k-1), c=Tr(g_cut g_e)-2 and c=z(2-p_e-p_e^(-1)), D=-z(p_e-p_e^(-1)). The two branches at fixed position clocks exchange p_e and its inverse. On the regular chart z!=0,p_e!=0, (6.3) therefore proves R_(+1,-1),0-R_(-1,+1),0=D/z. (6.4) The principal ODD orientation section is realized by two actual nearby port bands. It was not imposed by a field trace or by a postulated Weyl action. If the two-position density is Omega_cut=dlog A wedge dlog B/(B D), its product with this actual odd-band symbol is the nonzero DECK-EVEN density dlog A wedge dlog B/(B z). (6.5) Equations (6.4)--(6.5) require the displayed physical Gauss chart (including any prefix adapter); they are not a replacement of that dictionary for an arbitrary pair of developed word matrices. ## 7. The remaining orientation and global-source datum An etale two-position chart need not have degree one. On a two-sheeted framing chart its leading density can be odd under the deck involution. The local choice of geometric critical point and marked square-root/orientation in (5.2) then selects a local sheet; ordinary field trace of that odd density would be zero. The literal source (4.2) and full relative finite-window tails do not authorize replacing a selected cycle by that field trace. Section 6 now computes an actual local odd-band observable that distinguishes those sheets, when the physical chart is fixed. However the original second-edge closing operation is the q=0 identity-cap source (4.2). It has not been proved that its global relative current/cycle selects the odd combination in (6.4). Substituting that inserted observable for the uninserted scalar state would be a different problem. The construction supplies a specified physical current/source problem, a nonzero local band map and two independent position directions. It does not yet determine the global marked cycle or prove that its geometric coefficient survives the final contraction. Exact actual tensor audits: [script](../experiments/audit_actual_two_cut_ports.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_two_cut_ports_results.json).

title: Polynomial-cost inversion of the actual two-head Ward current
text: # Polynomial-cost inversion of the actual two-head Ward current 28 October 2026. The actual two-head lowering current admits a uniformly polynomial inverse on the orthogonal complement of its exact kernel, at EVERY total integer degree. This is a statement in the original Euclidean head metric, uniformly on compact meridian annuli. It does not use the potentially exponentially conditioned fusion matrix to estimate an inverse. In particular, a local current equation cannot introduce an extra exponential loss merely through its inversion. Kernel and cokernel charges remain explicit. Neither this fact nor nilpotence of the current proves that the whole knot's selected geometric contribution is nonzero. ## 1. The actual current and the bound Fix N>=2, Q=exp(2pi i/N), d=N-1, and x!=0. In the balanced physical basis the current is F |a,b> = (1-Q^(a+1)) |a+1,b> + x^-1 Q^a (1-Q^(b+1)) |a,b+1>, (1) where arrows outside 0,...,d vanish. This is the actual coproduct current F_1+K_1^-1 F_2 in the fusion conventions of [the original kernel](fusion_canonical_chart_and_retained_source_wall.md). Let H_s be the span of a+b=s, and F_s:H_s -> H_(s+1). For every nonzero F_s, all its nonzero singular values obey sigma >= min(1,|x|^-1) 2 sin(pi/N)/N. (2) Consequently its Moore--Penrose inverse satisfies ||F_s^+|| <= max(1,|x|) N/[2 sin(pi/N)] <= max(1,|x|) N^2/4. (3) Here the last inequality is sin(pi/N)>=2/N. F_(2d)=0 has zero pseudoinverse; its kernel is retained, not inverted. In particular this is uniform on every fixed compact meridian annulus. ## 2. Unitary reduction to a weighted path The only nonzero entries of F_s are on two adjacent diagonals. Their bipartite support graph is a path. Independent unitary phases on its row and column vertices therefore make all entries real, with opposite signs on the two diagonals: choose one vertex phase and propagate along the path. There is no loop consistency condition, and these changes of frame have norm and inverse norm exactly one. For 0<=s<=N-2, F_s^* is unitarily equivalent to A_L with L=s+1. For N-1<=s<=2N-3, F_s is unitarily equivalent to A_L with L=2N-2-s. In both cases 1<=L<=N-1, and (A_L f)_i = a_i f_i-b_i f_(i+1), 0<=i<L, a_i=2sin(pi(L-i)/N), b_i=2sin(pi(i+1)/N) (4) when |x|=1. For general x, multiply a_i by |x|^-1 in the lower-degree case, and b_i by |x|^-1 in the upper-degree case.
