At |x|=1, for the lower degrees the coefficient on row a=i is |1-Q^(s-i+1)|=a_i, and on row a=i+1 it is b_i. For the upper degrees put a=s-d+i. The output degree starts at a=s-d+1, so each row has the two coefficients |1-Q^(s-d+i+1)|=2sin(pi(L-i)/N), |1-Q^(d-i)|=2sin(pi(i+1)/N), as claimed. In particular every coefficient in (4) is at least a_min=min(1,|x|^-1) 2sin(pi/N). (5) The adjoint reduction in the lower degrees preserves nonzero singular values; it is not a replacement of the original current by another quantum operator. ## 3. A unimodal exact kernel supplies a spectral estimate The row rank of A_L is L, and its kernel is spanned by the positive vector eta defined by eta_0=1 and eta_(i+1)/eta_i=a_i/b_i. Equivalently, eta_i= r^i |(Q;Q)_L/[(Q;Q)_i (Q;Q)_(L-i)]|, (6) where r=|x|^-1 for the lower-degree case and r=|x| for the upper-degree case. The ratios are nonincreasing in i. One direct verification extends the ratio to real i and differentiates its logarithm: d/di log[sin(pi(L-i)/N)/sin(pi(i+1)/N)] = -(pi/N) sin(pi(L+1)/N) /[sin(pi(L-i)/N)sin(pi(i+1)/N)] <= 0. (7) Thus eta, and hence the probability weights p_i=eta_i^2 / sum_j eta_j^2, are unimodal. They may have very different magnitudes; no lower bound on every p_i is assumed. The constant ratio factor r does not change (7). When L=N-1 the ratios are constant; the kernel is uniform when |x|=1. Set w_i=a_i^2 p_i=b_i^2 p_(i+1), P_i=sum_(j<=i) p_j. Unimodality gives min(P_i,1-P_i) <= (L+1) max(p_i,p_(i+1)). (8) Indeed before a mode the prefix is at most (i+1)p_i; at or after a mode the suffix is at most (L-i)p_(i+1). Together with (5), this implies w_i >= [a_min^2/(L+1)] min(P_i,1-P_i). (9) For a complex-valued function g on the path, the exact variance identity and Cauchy--Schwarz along each interval give Var_p(g)=sum_(i<j) p_i p_j |g_i-g_j|^2 <= L sum_(r=0)^(L-1) P_r(1-P_r)|g_(r+1)-g_r|^2 <= [L(L+1)/a_min^2] sum_r w_r |g_(r+1)-g_r|^2. (10) For f_i=sqrt(p_i)g_i, orthogonality to ker A_L is exactly sum_i p_i g_i=0, while ||f||^2=Var_p(g), ||A_L f||^2=sum_r w_r |g_(r+1)-g_r|^2. Equation (10) proves the stronger estimate sigma_min(A_L)>=a_min/sqrt(L(L+1))>=a_min/N. (11) This proves (2)--(3) in every degree without an asymptotic limit. ## 4. The exact retained charges and use in transport Let h_s=F_s^+. Orthogonal projections P_s onto ker F_s and Q_(s+1) onto ker F_s^* satisfy the exact equations h_s F_s=I-P_s, F_s h_s=I-Q_(s+1). (12) All projectors are explicit: pull the normalized rank-one vector (6) through the unitary path gauges. For s<N-1 the kernel of F_s is zero and its cokernel has rank one. For N-1<=s<2d the kernel has rank one and its cokernel is zero. At s=2d the whole one-dimensional source is kernel. At the invariant dual-pair degree s=d, L=d and eta_i=|x|^i. Putting back the actual phases gives the normalized invariant cup with coefficients proportional to x^a. Thus the original cup charge survives this contraction exactly; it is not a zero-current term to be removed. The full K=1 constraint singles out this degree's charge as in [the original Ward corner reduction](actual_rogers_bridge_transport.md). For a compatible physical equation F_s v=j, (12) produces the unique minimum-norm solution v=h_s j, with ||v|| <= max(1,|x|)(N^2/4)||j||. (13) For an incompatible j the exact retained obstruction is Q_(s+1)j. Similarly a row annihilating ker F_s factors through F_s with a coefficient row of norm at most max(1,|x|)(N^2/4) times its own norm. Thus, for a fixed finite sequence of such compatible local solves, the inversion cost alone is polynomial in N. The currents or retained charges themselves can still be exponentially large. This is complementary to the cyclic-character contraction used for the sewn wall currents. Here the metric and operator are those of the literal nilpotent physical heads, not a cyclic replacement. It gives a genuine local flow estimate for the proposed torsor transport. It does not assert that arbitrary interbridge kernels obey each separate pair's Ward equation, nor that a simultaneous many-head reduction has the same estimate. Those compatibilities must be established before iterating (13) across a knot diagram. ## 5. A holomorphic contraction on the actual scaled meridian tube The Moore--Penrose inverse used in (12) depends on a Hermitian metric. Pointwise bounds on a fixed annulus do not by themselves give a holomorphic torsor map there. On the meridian scale used by the quantum jets, however, an algebraic contraction has the same polynomial cost. Fix |x_0|=1, write x=z x_0, and on H_s put D_s(z)|a,s-a>=z^a |a,s-a>. The literal coefficients in (1) give F_s(z x_0)=z^-1 D_(s+1)(z) F_s(x_0) D_s(z)^-1. (14) Define the holomorphic matrix and projections h_s^hol(z)=z D_s(z) h_s(x_0) D_(s+1)(z)^-1, P_s^hol(z)=D_s(z) P_s(x_0) D_s(z)^-1, Q_(s+1)^hol(z)=D_(s+1)(z) Q_(s+1)(x_0) D_(s+1)(z)^-1. Equations (12) hold EXACTLY with these matrices and F_s(z x_0). All entries are Laurent polynomials in z with fixed coefficients. When x_0 is algebraic, the coefficients are algebraic: the appropriate full-rank Gram inverse computes h_s(x_0) over the field generated by Q,x_0 and their complex conjugates. For z=exp(u/N) and |Re u|<=C, every diagonal D and its inverse has norm at most exp(C). Consequently ||h_s^hol(exp(u/N))|| <= exp(2C+C/N) N^2/4, (15) ||P_s^hol||, ||Q_(s+1)^hol|| <= exp(2C). Every fixed-order u derivative has the same polynomial bound with an additional constant depending only on its order and C. To see this directly, differentiation acts on h by a scalar 1/N and left/right multiplication by diag(a/N), of norms at most one. The rth derivative therefore costs at most (2+1/N)^r. This is a genuine holomorphic, source-compatible local contraction on the entire marked quantum meridian tube. It avoids inferring analytic transport from a nonholomorphic inverse. On a fixed-width annulus, (14) can instead have exponentially large diagonal norms; no bound like (15) for that particular holomorphic contraction is asserted there. Likewise a many-head compatibility problem cannot be solved by applying (14) to pairs whose separate Ward equations are not satisfied. ## 6. Verification [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_two_head_ward_contraction.py) compares the singular spectra of the literal complex current and the weighted-path reduction, checks the bound on every degree at small levels, and tests the kernel, projector and compatible-solve identities. Larger levels test the balanced and unbalanced path regimes. These are diagnostics of the formulas; (4)--(11) are the uniform proof.

title: The selected endpoint source is a marked two-pole cycle
text: # The selected endpoint source is a marked two-pole cycle 27 October 2026. The exact all-strand coefficient source has an ordinary one-variable contour representative, with two nearby marked pole cycles. Neither pole is an invariant by itself: a characteristic-zero actual figure-eight braid calculation changes BOTH endpoint values under braid conjugacy while leaving their difference unchanged. The coalescing-root limit also has a precise cyclotomic boundary layer. Replacing it by one ordinary double-pole contour loses even the constant source. This gives a concrete contour input for gate C. It does not prove a nonzero geometric thimble intersection. The final section records the derived source-symbol test that a whole geometric comparison would need. ## 1. Exact contour of the original all-strand source Use the canonical degree-<N endpoint polynomials from [the original all-strand theorem](all_strand_euler_cauchy_cap.md), and combine all tail heads BEFORE attempting a source limit: T_N(Z)=sum_lambda Q^-j B_lambda(Z), S_N=T_N(1)-T_N(Q^-1), Q=exp(2pi*i/N). No unknown invariant is divided out in forming T_N. Its coefficients are determined by the actual complete word, its actual fusion/Euler frames and every off-diagonal tail transition. The original full peripheral and framing line is retained in that theorem; in modulus the reduced original invariant satisfies |Kashaev_N(K)|=N|S_N|/|1-Q|. (1) Define the source differential omega_N(T)=T(z) dz/[z^N(1-z)(1-Qz)]. (2) Its residue at zero is the original rational-kernel coefficient functional. Since degree T<N, its order at infinity is at most -3, so there is no residue at infinity. Its two other residues are Res_(z=1) omega_N=-T(1)/(1-Q), Res_(z=Q^-1) omega_N=T(Q^-1)/(1-Q). (3) Here both centers have z^N=1. Thus the global residue theorem gives the EXACT all-level source identity Res_(z=0) omega_N =[z^(N-1)] T(z)/[(1-z)(1-Qz)] =[T(1)-T(Q^-1)]/(1-Q). (4) Equivalently the small positive circle around zero can be deformed to the negative sum of the two pole circles. The opposite signs in their scalar periods come from the residues, not a choice to discard one contour. Formula (4) is a representation of the existing finite source, not the definition of a replacement state. ## 2. An actual braid conjugacy changes both endpoint values At N=2 use q=i, Q=-1, x=i and eta=exp(pi*i/4). The original balanced positive crossing, with its actual common Cartan line, is R_+=[[eta,0,0,0], [0,0,eta^-1,0], [0,eta^-1,2i eta^-1,0], [0,0,0,eta]]. Use its literal inverse, K=diag(i,-i), F_(1,0)=2 and the original pivot K^-1. Form the original three-strand word, tail-head fusion and right Euler conjugation from the all-strand theorem. Exact matrix multiplication over Q(i,sqrt(2)) gives beta=(1,-2,1,-2), T_beta(Z)=-1+(5/2)Z, beta'=(1,1,-2,1,-2,-1)=sigma_1 beta sigma_1^-1, T_beta'(Z)=2+(5/2)Z. (5) Both words have the same braid index and writhe, so all external source, peripheral and framing factors agree. Their endpoint pairs are beta: (T(1),T(-1))=(3/2,-7/2), beta': (T(1),T(-1))=(9/2,-1/2). (6) Both endpoints change by three, while both differences are exactly five, the same original reduced cut value. The change is a constant polynomial, which the source (4) annihilates. Thus neither individual endpoint can be identified with an intrinsic marked knot period using only a scalar adapter depending on N, color, braid index and writhe. The transported co-source or the complete two-endpoint difference is required. This is an exact actual-word countertest, not an arbitrary polynomial chosen to mimic a knot. ## 3. The pole collision has a cyclotomic boundary layer There is a simple all-level warning against merging the two poles before retaining the normal clock. For the constant polynomial one, [z^(N-1)]1/[(1-z)(1-Qz)]=0 at every original root, since this coefficient is (1-Q^N)/(1-Q). If one sets Q=1 in that rational kernel first, the same coefficient instead becomes [z^(N-1)](1-z)^-2=N. (7) This is a failure of the premature specialization, not a failure of the exact residue formula. The original source is normalized on the cyclotomic relation Q^N=1 and must retain it through the pole collision. To see the correct normal geometry, put H=2pi*i/N and z=exp(H xi). The two source poles are xi=0 and xi=-1 on their local logarithmic lifts. The pullback of (2) is EXACTLY H T_N(exp(H xi)) exp(H xi) exp(-2pi*i xi) /[(1-exp(H xi))(1-exp(H(xi+1)))] dxi. (8) On compact xi charts away from 0,-1 this has the kernel form H^-1 exp(-2pi*i xi) T_N(exp(H xi)) /[xi(xi+1)] * (1+O(H)) dxi. (9) The poles stay one unit apart, and the cyclotomic exponential survives. A fixed-z double-pole model that omits these data is not the source normal limit. In particular an ordinary residue of the principal geometric framing density alone cannot decide the selected endpoint class. ## 4. What a whole geometric source calculation would have to show There is a precise local source-symbol criterion once a uniform WHOLE asymptotic near the two endpoints has been proved. Let D=z partial_z and suppose on a fixed complex neighborhood of one T_N(z)=H^alpha exp(S(z)/H) [a_0(z)+H a_1(z)+O(H^2)], (10) with holomorphic S,a_0,a_1, uniform errors (including the required derivatives), and a_0(1)!=0. This hypothesis concerns the complete selected tail sum T_N, not one unsummed local geometric block. Set mu=exp(-D S(1)). Direct Taylor expansion at z=exp(-H) gives S_N=H^alpha exp(S(1)/H) {(1-mu)a_0(1) +H[(1-mu)a_1(1)+mu D a_0(1) -(mu/2)D^2 S(1)a_0(1)] +O(H^2)}. (11) If mu!=1, the first coefficient is nonzero. If mu=1, the principal coefficient cancels and the next source coefficient is D a_0(1)-(1/2)D^2 S(1)a_0(1). (12) The uniform Taylor expansion proves these formulas: write S(exp(-H))=S(1)-H D S(1)+(H^2/2)D^2 S(1)+O(H^3) and do the same for the amplitude. No contour or thimble selection is assumed during that algebraic expansion. If the first nonzero coefficient of the resulting derived source series occurs at some fixed finite order, and (10) holds to that order with controlled error, the original invariant has the same exponential rate Im S(1)/(2pi). In particular a calibrated action with Im S(1)=Vol(X) would imply the required volume rate. This is a sufficient conditional source criterion, not a proof that (10) holds for the knot state or that its derived coefficient is nonzero. The source variable here is the right-Euler coefficient variable. Its identification with a geometric framing or peripheral clock is still required. Only AFTER such a marking could a classical closure relation be used to assert mu=1. The actual source-wall and fusion-orientation audit in [the canonical-chart theorem](fusion_canonical_chart_and_retained_source_wall.md) prevents making that substitution by inspection. Thus the cycle problem is not settled by Rivin uniqueness: it must transport the marked TWO-pole functional and establish its first nonzero derived coefficient on the actual selected geometric image. Exact finite source jets or the unsourced nonzero Gaussian alone do not establish these hypotheses. No broad knot class is proved here. ## 5. Exact checks [The actual-source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_two_pole_source_contour.py) and [saved results](../experiments/actual_two_pole_source_contour_results.json) pass 15 literal signed-word cases, levels N=2,...,6, and three same-index/same-writhe figure-eight braid conjugacies. The N=2 pair (5)-(6) is additionally checked by exact characteristic-zero matrix multiplication. All original word, pivot, fusion and Euler factors are used. Finite-field tests verify conventions; the residue and boundary-layer proofs above are all-level.

title: Exact cotangent source atlases and their universal-transport limitation
text: # Exact cotangent source atlases and their universal-transport limitation 28 October 2026. The TU pulling atlas of the ORIGINAL physical source has a finite compatible residue implementation, with explicit fixed integer coefficients and no exponentially conditioned chart adapter. Elementary cotangent changes retain calculable side currents. Artificial chart divisors cancel in their complete aggregate. There is an essential limit: these are UNIVERSAL identities on every holomorphic test function. Such identities cannot move the whole source to a cycle on which the completed original state is smaller than its largest physical lattice value. This follows from a direct holomorphic hull argument below, and does not require an unproved knot example. Thus the atlas solves an algebraic source-coordinate problem, not the state-specific cancellation needed for the sharp volume bound. ## 1. The exact original source functional Fix a nonempty one-component signed braid with m crossings, put r=m+1 and d=N-1, and keep its actual integral coordinates u=(t,k_1,...,k_m). Let Lambda_N=dP intersect Z^r, T_N(f)=sum_(n in Lambda_N) f(n). (1) Here P is the physical polytope in [the physical-face proof](actual_physical_face_outward_action.md). The cardinal-completed original scalar F_N is holomorphic on the specified O(N) complex box D, equals the EXACT original state at each valid n, and vanishes at every invalid integer state in the box. The complete original invariant is chi_N/N times T_N(F_N), with kappa, pivots, half-Cartan and every conversion phase inside F_N. No scalar line is altered below. Let kappa_0(s)=1/(1-exp(2*pi*i*s)); this symbol denotes a cotangent kernel, NOT the original crossing scalar kappa. At an integer n its residue is -1/(2*pi*i). Thus, on a sufficiently small product torus Gamma_n around n, integral_(Gamma_n) f(u) product_i[-2*pi*i*kappa_0(u_i) du_i] /(2*pi*i)^r=f(n). (2) The same is true with product_i pi*cot(pi*u_i) du_i. Exactly, pi*cot(pi*s)=-2*pi*i*kappa_0(s)+pi*i. (3) Every term in the difference of these PRODUCT kernels lacks at least one coordinate pole and integrates to zero on the FULL small torus. These terms are not zero on arbitrary partial chart chains. If (3) is used on a partial domain, its explicit 2^r-1 lower-pole terms are retained as source currents. The original finite source is therefore the coherent middle-dimensional cycle sum Gamma_Lambda=sum_n Gamma_n with either COMPLETE kernel. It has at most N^r local components. No norm estimate on F_N is used. ## 2. Finite compatible affine-unimodular charts The proved pulling triangulation gives finitely many cells u=d v_j+B_j y, y in d*Delta, B_j in GL_r(Z), (4) with their number and matrices depending only on the fixed diagram. Assign shared lattice faces once using a fixed half-open convention. Let Lambda_j be the resulting disjoint partition of Lambda_N. This is a partition of the ORIGINAL finite states, not a new source. Put A_j=B_j^(-1). Since d v_j is integer and A_j is unimodular, the joint poles of the new chart kernel are the SAME integer lattice. For each n in Lambda_j take Gamma_(j,n)=n+A_j^(-1) T_epsilon, omega_j=(-2*pi*i)^r det(A_j) product_i kappa_0((A_j u)_i) du_1...du_r. (5) The affine translation in (4) is harmless by INTEGER periodicity; no exponential monomial multiplier has been canceled. The induced orientation in (5) retains its determinant +/-1. The ordinary multivariate Cauchy residue calculation gives exactly integral_(Gamma_(j,n)) f omega_j/(2*pi*i)^r=f(n). Consequently T_N(f)=sum_j integral_(sum_(n in Lambda_j) Gamma_(j,n)) f omega_j/(2*pi*i)^r. (6) This identity is valid for EVERY f holomorphic near these cycles and their enclosed local polydiscs. All coefficients are one, all counting Jacobians are one, and it is the exact original functional (1). There is a simultaneous quantitative initial-cycle construction. Collect the finite integer row forms appearing in all chart matrices and in the elementary side currents of Section 3. Choose small radii epsilon_1 >> epsilon_2 >> ... >> epsilon_r with ratios less than 1/(4rC), where C bounds their integer coefficients in any chosen chart. Choose epsilon_1 so every linear form has modulus below 1/4. Its FIRST nonzero term then dominates the remaining terms, so every such form has modulus at least a fixed positive multiple of epsilon_r on the corresponding hierarchical torus. It cannot hit an integer. These radii depend on the diagram, not on N or n. All source kernels and chart Jacobians on this initial atlas are bounded by diagram constants. Its total logarithmic/Euclidean mass is O_word(N^r). This is a polynomial INITIAL mass bound, not a bound for an unconstructed global steepest-descent deformation. The union may still pass near individual large state values. ## 3. Explicit elementary side-current algebra Write x,y for two affine integer row forms. Their integer constants do not affect the periodic kernels. The exact identities are kappa_0(x)kappa_0(y) =kappa_0(x+y)kappa_0(y) -kappa_0(x+y)kappa_0(-x), kappa_0(x)kappa_0(y) =kappa_0(x-y)kappa_0(y) +kappa_0(x)kappa_0(y-x), kappa_0(-x)=1-kappa_0(x). (7) For example they follow immediately, with all terms retained, from kappa_0(x)kappa_0(y) =kappa_0(x+y)[kappa_0(x)+kappa_0(y)-1]. The first line changes the first row from x to x+y and leaves y; the second changes it from x to x-y. The extra product is an EXPLICIT side-current kernel in another unimodular basis. A sign change has the displayed lower-pole current. A row swap only changes the recorded coordinate orientation. Multiplying by all spectator kernels gives the r-dimensional identities without hidden factors. Factor each fixed GL_r(Z) chart matrix into unit row shears, row swaps and sign changes. This is constructive integer elimination. Follow just the intended main basis through this fixed sequence; at each step retain its one extra kernel from (7). Telescoping gives K_reference=c_main K_chart+sum_n c_n K_side,n, (8) where every c is +1 or -1, and every side kernel is specified by that step. The number of terms is at most the number of steps plus one. It is independent of N. The ordinary powers of 2*pi*i and all determinants in converting (8) to normalized forms are fixed diagram constants. Products of lower-pole terms from (3) are also explicit and finite. None is silently declared source-null on a partial cycle. The side currents can carry the ENTIRE selected residue. Already in two local variables, the leading Cauchy identity is 1/(xy)=1/[(x+y)y]+1/[x(x+y)]. (9) On |x|<<|y|, the first right-hand term has integral zero, the second integral one, while the left integral is one. Thus retaining only the main new chart fails even for f=1. This is not an exponentially large adapter; it is a compulsory unit source current. ## 4. Aggregate cancellation and its exact chain qualification Equations (7)--(8) are pointwise meromorphic identities. In any common compact domain remove the SAME small tubes about the union of all appearing chart divisors. Apply Stokes on the remaining chains, retaining every tube boundary and every partial-chart side prism. Sum the kernels BEFORE taking the tube limit. At a divisor artificial to the reference kernel, every principal part cancels exactly in that aggregate. The same is true at dependent intersections: on each common regulator boundary the sum IS the reference meromorphic form, so it is not necessary to pretend that the individual singular currents have independent limits. Original coordinate divisors remain genuine source divisors and retain their original residues. No physical point is deleted by (8). This proves tame gluing on any PROVIDED compatible common chain homotopy. If neighboring chart homotopies have the same embedded interface with opposite induced orientations and the same regulator, their full side-current sums agree with the reference form and cancel. No exponential chart-change coefficient is introduced. On regions whose distances to all appearing integer hyperplanes are at least N^(-A), every kernel is bounded by N^C: globally |kappa_0(z)|<=C[1+dist(z,Z)^(-1)]. (10) In a fixed O(N) real box there are O_word(N) parallel translates per row form, hence polynomially many arrangement cells in fixed dimension. Piecewise-linear common chains with polynomial complexity therefore have polynomial source-kernel overhead. What is NOT proved is that separately chosen descending chart cycles have compatible interfaces or that their remaining side currents have small phase. The local identity does not construct that homotopy. Replacing each chart by an independently convenient contour and then omitting the difference currents is invalid. In fact there is a general obstruction to closing that gap by UNIVERSAL cot algebra alone. ## 5. Universal source rewrites cannot lower the state maximum Let D be a complex domain, Lambda a finite nonempty set in D, and w_p nonzero fixed complex weights. Suppose a compact union C of contours and finite complex source measure mu satisfy sum_(p in Lambda) w_p f(p)=integral_C f dmu (11) for EVERY holomorphic f on D. Each p belongs to the O(D)-holomorphic hull of C. Here is a direct proof, independent of any source model. If p is outside that hull, choose a holomorphic g with |g(p)|>sup_C|g|. Choose an ordinary polynomial L_p equal to one at p and zero at every other point of Lambda; for instance interpolate a generic linear coordinate separating the finite set. Apply (11) to f=L_p g^k. The result is |w_p| |g(p)|^k <=||mu|| sup_C|L_p| (sup_C|g|)^k, which is impossible as k tends to infinity. Therefore, for EVERY holomorphic F on D, max_(p in Lambda)|F(p)|<=sup_C|F|. (12) The conclusion holds for any finite number of chart cycles and kernels: combine their measures on their union. It still holds if the cycle was chosen after inspecting F, provided the resulting source identity remains valid for all holomorphic test functions. No polynomial-versus-exponential estimate is needed for this obstruction; finite total variation is enough. All constructions in Sections 1--4 are universal in this sense. Thus they cannot, by themselves, produce a low-|F_N| source cycle below a larger original lattice summand. An ordinary homotopy in the complement of every genuine integer source divisor is an even more restrictive instance: it separately preserves each Cauchy evaluation. Rewriting the cotangent form does not defeat that issue while its full test-function functional is preserved. The issue occurs in the actual model: the independently derived [signed Markov source family](actual_cotangent_homology_and_global_gluing_criterion.md) keeps the SAME hyperbolic knot and normalized period while each additional alternating-sign stabilization adds v_8/(2pi) to one valid original state's exponential rate. Its complete original pivotal traces are checked directly. Exact normalization pruning evades this family by composing the ACTUAL source cell first; it is not an identity on arbitrary multipliers of each intermediate state. This does NOT forbid a sharp upper bound for the original scalar. That bound concerns cancellations among the values of the PARTICULAR original F_N. Exact q-binomial fusion, Hopf-Ward equations and matched normalization cells can relate those values in ways invalid for an arbitrary holomorphic multiplier. Such an operation can change the individual-evaluation source homology while preserving its actual scalar. Pure coordinate changes and the universal algebra (7) do not. ## 6. Result and the precise outstanding step The original finite residue functional has a finite affine-unimodular atlas, polynomial initial mass, explicit fixed-coefficient side currents, and exact aggregate cancellation of ARTIFICIAL cotangent divisors. These statements include its complete original source. A global phase-small cycle does not follow. Beyond choosing compatible interfaces, one must use an ORIGINAL-STATE-specific Ward/fusion identity to recombine genuine evaluation residues. The transport must then control the resulting full currents. A construction that stays universal on all holomorphic test functions cannot accomplish that step, by (12). This is a mathematical limitation of that proposed route, not a claim that the volume conjecture is false. [Supplementary audit](../experiments/audit_actual_unimodular_cot_source_atlas.py) checks the exact shear algebra, compulsory unit side current and whole original source reindexing in fixed affine-unimodular charts.

# An actual unprojectivized Frobenius source is a marked Borel torsor Research proof and independent audit, 27 October 2026. The actual high-color coherent source, its scale character, and one first descendant recover the complete framing two-form explicitly. The scale must be retained before normalizing the projector. A marked Kummer cover is necessary: the actual Sym^N data know the N-th power of that scale, not its unmarked root. This is a source/framing moment map. It does not yet intertwine the full network Gaussian coefficients or prove the selected volume norm. ## 1. Original divided matrices give the whole coherent source Use the actual high integral color with r=N and the root Frobenius matrices e,f,h: \[ ev_k=(N-k+1)v_{k-1},\quad fv_k=(k+1)v_{k+1},\quad hv_k=(N-2k)v_k . \] The pure-power source is \[ \psi(a,b)=\sum_{k=0}^Na^{N-k}b^kv_k . \] Its exact root differential laws are \[ e\psi=b\partial_a\psi,\quad f\psi=a\partial_b\psi,\quad h\psi=(a\partial_a-b\partial_b)\psi . 	ag{1} \] Thus this is the actual Sym^N source cone, not an auxiliary representation. It also has a specified ORIGINAL whole q-germ on every residue string s: \[ \psi_s(q;a,b)= \sum_{k=0}^N rac{a^{N-k}b^k}{k!} (F^{(N)}(q))^kw_{0,s}. \] The divided matrices have regular integral Gaussian entries, so this is polynomial in a,b and regular in q, including a=0. The corresponding whole duals use the actual \(\exp(u	au E^{(N)}(q))\), with their actual pairing units retained. The linear SL2 formulas (1) are root formulas; their full normal deformations are the actual bounded-PBW operators already proved. The distinguished fixed root co-source is \(\lambda_+(v_k)=2^{-N} inom Nk\). Its scale pairing is \[ \lambda_+\psi(a,b)=((a+b)/2)^N. 	ag{2} \] Normalizing by this quantity is legitimate only off its source wall and must not erase the character or its quantum derivatives. ## 2. Retain the scale AND the contragredient dual flag For the actual cut-Borel generators \[ M_1=h+2f,\qquad M_2=e+f , \] the standard ket \(w_+=(1,1)^t\) is an eigenvector of BOTH. Its vector cone alone has a one-dimensional orbit at that anchor. The correct paired source retains its contragredient dual flag. Write the standard ket and dual as \[ w=\alpha(1,1)^t,\qquad \ell= rac{(1,u)}{\alpha(1+u)},\qquad \ell w=1 , \quad \alpha
e0,\quad u
e-1 . \] Their ACTUAL Sym^N source and normalized co-source are \[ \psi_\alpha=\alpha^N\sum_kv_k,\qquad \lambda_{\alpha,u}(v_k)=  rac{ inom Nk u^k}{\alpha^N(1+u)^N}. 	ag{3} \] They pair to one. These are the source vector and co-source separately, not only their scale-invariant rank-one projector. Let g preserve the projective ket line \(w_+\), act on w by g, and on the dual by \(\ell g^{-1}\). Direct differentiation gives \[ Y_1=\alpha\partial_\alpha+2u(1+u)\partial_u,\qquad Y_2=\alpha\partial_\alpha+(u^2-1)\partial_u . 	ag{4} \] These have rank two at \((\alpha,u)=(1,1)\). The normalized projector alone would forget alpha and lose that direction. Here u is an affine flag chart. Include u=infinity as well: in the global affine coordinate m=(1-u)/(1+u), write \[ \ell= rac{(1+m,1-m)}{2\alpha},\qquad \lambda_{\alpha,m}(v_k)=\alpha^{-N} inom Nk \left( rac{1+m}{2}ight)^{N-k} \left( rac{1-m}{2}ight)^k . \] These formulas are regular for every m in A^1, including m=-1 (the chart point u=infinity). The FULL marked paired space is G_m times A^1; the displayed finite-u chart alone is not preserved by every Borel element. This full space is genuinely a Borel torsor on the STANDARD marked cover. A group element fixing w and its normalized dual fixes the complementary dual kernel as well; determinant one then forces identity. The Borel has the same dimension as this open paired source space and acts transitively: scale w, then use its unipotent subgroup to move the dual with its fixed nonzero pairing. Equivalently use \(m=(1-u)/(1+u)\); (4) become \[ Y_1=\alpha\partial_\alpha+(2m-2)\partial_m,\qquad Y_2=\alpha\partial_\alpha+2m\partial_m , \] the ordinary free affine Borel action on \(\mathbb G_m	imes\mathbb A^1\). More explicitly, in the standard basis \(w_+=(1,1),w_-=(1,-1)\), the unique group element from the reference \((\alpha,m)=(1,0)\) is \[ g(\alpha,m)=  egin{pmatrix}\alpha&-m/\alpha\0&\alpha^{-1}\end{pmatrix}. \] It sends the ket to the stated ket and the reference dual contragrediently to the stated dual. ## 3. The exact equivariant internal-frame map For constants \(C
e0,D\), put \[ s=C\alpha^2,\qquad r= rac1{1+u}+D\alpha^2,\qquad A= rac1{1+s}. 	ag{5} \] The regular A/Omega_cut chart additionally requires 1+C alpha^2!=0. The framing map and invariant Haar form have their stated rational meanings on the larger open alpha!=0, u!=-1; the cut-density pole is retained at the omitted divisor. The letter r here is the framing coordinate; the color highest weight was fixed to N. Calculation in (4) gives \[ Y_1(r)=2(r-1),\quad Y_2(r)=2r-1,\quad Y_1(s)=Y_2(s)=2s . \] Thus the actual paired-source Borel fields map EXACTLY to \[ \xi_1=2(r-1)\partial_r+2s\partial_s,\qquad \xi_2=(2r-1)\partial_r+2s\partial_s, 	ag{6} \] the original compensated cut-framing fields. The map has nonzero local Jacobian on this open set. It is a marked sign cover of the PGL2 framing torsor, not an identification of every Fr generator with an old head current. Choose \(C=-2,D=0\). The actual source anchor \((\alpha,u)=(1,1)\) maps to \[ (r,s)=(1/2,-2),\qquad A=-1. \] It is a regular frame with nonzero Borel fields. This repairs the vanishing-vector obstruction of the normalized compact Fr projector at its anchor. The original complete meridian signs, full peripheral dimension line, and half-form marks remain separate. Formula (5) does not equate the OLD physical clock with the new diagonal Q^R clock; the controlled Fourier polarization dictionary is still required. ## 4. A scale character and ONE actual descendant give the full two-form The Berry form of (3) is \[ \lambda_{\alpha,u}d\psi_\alpha=N\,d\log\alpha . \] Its curvature is zero on this Borel. It must NOT be called the framing area form. The missing covector comes from an actual first descendant: \[ U=\lambda_+\psi_\alpha=\alpha^N,\qquad m= rac1N\lambda_{\alpha,u}h\psi_\alpha = rac{1-u}{1+u}. 	ag{7} \] Both are literal source/co-source pairings of original divided matrices. Define \[ \omega_H= rac1N d\log U=d\log\alpha,\qquad \omega_U=- rac{dm}{2\alpha^2} = rac{du}{\alpha^2(1+u)^2}. \] They satisfy \(d\omega_H=0\), \(d\omega_U=-2\omega_H\wedge\omega_U\), the explicit Borel Maurer differential law. The invariant Haar form and the actual compensated framing form are respectively \[ \widehat\Omega=- rac{dr\wedge ds}{s^2},\qquad \Omega_{m cut}=- rac{dr\wedge ds}{s(1+s)} . \] Substitution of (5) gives the exact source identities \[ \widehat\Omega=- rac2C\,\omega_H\wedge\omega_U, \qquad  oxed{\ \Omega_{m cut}= rac A N\,d\log U\wedge dm\ }. 	ag{8} \] The constant D drops out. Hence the rank-two co-source form is recovered from SCALE plus DESCENDANT, not from Berry curvature. Its covariance under (6) is exactly \(\operatorname{div}_{\Omega_{m cut}}\xi_i=2A\). The Haar form instead is invariant. This retains the source-density correction needed by the actual geometric Ward currents. For C=-2, the exact power character is \[ U^2=\left( rac{A-1}{2A}ight)^N. 	ag{9} \] In particular \(Y_iU=NU\). The factor \(2^N\), the power N, and its marked root cannot be replaced by their value at one point. Equation (9) is a SOURCE/frame character. It is not, without the missing network map, the knot meridian's ADO modified-dimension character. ## 5. The old cut-clock normal really detects this scale The specified actual whole divided-source construction has a concrete old-clock normal pairing, derived in [the controlled Fourier/current dictionary](controlled_fourier_current_and_conormal_dictionary.md). Let \(U_s(q;a,b)\) be its actual fixed-cut pairing and use the root-one ratios \(U_0/U_s\) on the head strings. The resulting UNNORMALIZED whole source satisfies \[ \Phi_Q(I)=U_0(q;a,b),\qquad \left[ rac{\Phi_Q(Q^SZ^R)}{1-Q^N}ight]_{Q_N} = rac{((a+b)/2)^N}{N(1-Q_N)},\quad Z=Q^N. 	ag{10} \] With a=b=alpha its numerator is exactly U of (7). The scalar multiplier is nonzero, has modulus between \(1/(2\pi)\) and \(1/4\), and tends to \(-1/(2\pi i)\). For completeness, put \(\delta=1-Q^N\). The per-string ratio \(U_s(q;a,bZ)/U_s(q;a,b)\) has first coefficient \(-N b/(a+b)\), independent of s at the root. The sums \(\sum_sQ_N^s=0\) kill that contribution and all overall source-unit derivatives. The remaining exact identity \(\sum_s sQ_N^s=-N/(1-Q_N)\) proves (10). The reduced head clock gives the same SELECTED scalar after these cancellations, although its operator Ward commutators differ. Thus (10) detects the scale line; it is not by itself a new independent Fr scalar-current theorem. Dividing the whole functional by U_0 returns the normalized original same-high-color scalar. Retaining U_0 separately keeps the actual source line and all its derivatives. This compares the high color with itself; its off-root jets are not equated with the low N-color jets. ## 6. The Kummer marking and remaining global comparison The ACTUAL pure-power source is unchanged under \((a,b)\mapsto(\zeta a,\zeta b)\), \(\zeta^N=1\). Likewise the paired Sym^N data (3) know alpha^N, not alpha. To use the standard Borel torsor and (5), retain the marked Kummer cover \(\alpha^N=U\), anchored by alpha=1. The unmarked actual Sym^N orbit is a homogeneous quotient by this finite isotropy, which need not be normal in the Borel. For N>2 it inherits neither a Borel quotient group nor a free SL2 Borel torsor action; the central-sign N=2 exception is below. The common marked SL2-Borel cover, rather than that quotient, carries the free source action and the frame sign-cover map. One cannot silently descend (5) to the unmarked Sym^N cone: alpha^2 generally changes under a mu_N root when N>2. Its frame sign cover only removes mu_2. At N=2 this subgroup is central: the quotient does inherit the PGL2 Borel group and its free torsor action, although the SL2 Borel action has kernel mu_2. For N>2 the finite isotropy is not normal in the Borel, so no quotient group structure is silently imposed. The unframed geometric character is gauge-invariant, but the relative endpoints, log sheets and period characters still require their own descent. This is precisely why the root mark belongs to the source torsor. At \(U=0\), or at the missing dual flag \(u=-1\), source vectors and inverse duals cannot be specialized separately. The actual paired fractional lattice or normal source complex must remain. On a physical cut loop the scale may approach this boundary, so no growing-neighborhood norm or cycle comparison follows from the regular local torsor. Equations (4), (6), (8), and (10) are concrete actual source/framing data. The remaining theorem is specific: map the whole network's ordinary/divided Ward currents and their charged normal neighbors to these source forms, preserving the final co-source and relative endpoints. The geometric Gaussian coefficients and global selected contribution have not been identified by an abstract Borel isomorphism. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_actual_frobenius_borel_torsor.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_frobenius_borel_torsor_results.json) check the ACTUAL divided-source and dual matrix fields, scale/descendant pairings, frame pushforward, area form, and co-source covariance in 63 symbolic checks at N=2 through 9.

title: Every regular full wall critical action has the actual representation regulator
text: # Every regular full wall critical action has the actual representation regulator 28 October 2026. The nine-atom full-Psi scalar crossing has the SAME Bloch--Wigner regulator as the original five-dilogarithm ADO crossing, for both signs, on its entire regular rational graph. This is proved without inferring a regulator from holonomy alone: their Bloch wedges are identical, the parameter chart is connected, and a real chart fixes the regulator constant. Integer norm/carry marks add 2*pi*i times logarithms to the action. At every regular FULL interior critical point these terms cancel from the imaginary critical value by an exact real-quadratic identity. Consequently the critical value is the regulator of the actual boundary-parabolic knot representation, after the existing marked fundamental-cycle comparison. This controls critical VALUES, not the original cycle's selected coefficient or its singular/escaping contributions. The [audit](../experiments/audit_actual_wall_critical_regulator.py) and [results](../experiments/actual_wall_critical_regulator_results.json) verify both rational crossing maps in all six Gauss coordinates, factor the Bloch wedges identically over Q(A,B,z,w), check the real normalization and complex regulators, and verify the off-critical integer-mark identity. No literature proof is used in these calculations. ## 1. The actual nine atom graphs Use physical clocks A,B and head coordinates z,w at complete color x=-1. At a current pair (a,b,p,r), the elementary principal maps are: | Gate | Bloch contribution | Position/clock update | | --- | --- | --- | | U diagonal on i | -[1-B_i] | z_i -> z_i(1-B_i) | | F diagonal on i | +[1-B_i] | z_i -> z_i/(1-B_i) | | U_- | -[t], t=-r/p | a -> a/(1-t), b -> b(1-t) | | V_- | +[t], t=-r/p | a -> a(1-t), b -> b/(1-t) | | U_+ | -[t], t=-p/r | a -> a(1-t), b -> b/(1-t) | | V_+ | +[t], t=-p/r | a -> a/(1-t), b -> b(1-t) | | D_+ | 0 | r -> -r/b | | D_- | 0 | r -> -br | Read the ORIGINAL strict factorization in traversal order: C^(-1): U_2, V_-, U_1, F_2; positive center: U_+, D_+; negative center: D_-, V_+; C: U_2, F_1, U_-, F_2. (1) The nine nonzero Bloch entries define beta_9^+ or beta_9^-. All are explicit rational functions of A,B,z,w. This is the [actual scalar full-Psi action](actual_full_psi_scalar_flow_cycle.md), with its reflected monomials and Gaussian retained. The physical generators are K=-1/a, e=(a^(-1)-1)/p, f=(1-a)p. (2) Direct rational substitution in (1) gives EXACTLY the independently proved actual crossing maps (4.6)--(4.7) of [the marked braid calculation](marked_braid_holonomy.md). This is checked algebraically for every one of the six output Gauss coordinates; equality of maps is not inferred from equality of finite root-level matrices or from a presumed saddle selection. ## 2. Regulator equality with the original coefficient symbol Let C_+=(1-e_1 f_2)^(-1), and C_-=1-(B/A)e_2 f_1. The original coefficient Bloch symbols are beta_5^+=[B]+[C_+]+[1/A]-[BC_+]-[C_+/A], beta_5^-=[A]+[C_-]+[1/B]-[AC_-]-[C_-/B]. (3) On the common regular rational crossing graph, delta(beta_9^sign-beta_5^sign)=0 in Lambda^2(Q(A,B,z,w)^* tensor Q). (4) There are two independent ways to check (4). For a signed dilog generating expression, its wedge is its incoming symplectic boundary minus the outgoing boundary; the internal monomial coordinates cancel, and symmetric real quadratic/Gaussian terms contribute zero. Both graph maps in Section 1 are the same actual map. In the physical position convention the common boundary is z wedge A+w wedge B-z_out wedge A_out-w_out wedge B_out. In the original coefficient convention it is A wedge p_in,1 plus B wedge p_in,2 minus the two outgoing terms, with p=z^(-1), so these are identical. The complete color -1 is torsion and disappears rationally. Alternatively factor every rational shape and its complement into irreducibles; the audit verifies the full antisymmetric coefficient matrix of (4) is identically zero for BOTH signs. Rational constant factors are retained in this check, not silently discarded. The differential of the Bloch--Wigner regulator D is a homomorphism of the multiplicative wedge: for one shape its differential is log|a| dArg(1-a)-log|1-a| dArg a. Thus (4) gives d D(beta_9^sign-beta_5^sign)=0. (5) The regular parameter space is a nonempty complex Zariski-open subset of (C^*)^4, obtained by removing finitely many rational zeros, poles and shapes equal to 1. It is connected: connect generic points by complex affine lines avoiding the finitely many excluded points on each line. Hence (5) is a single real constant on this space. Every rational argument in (1)--(3) has REAL coefficients. A generic real input avoids the finite excluded algebraic sets. Every shape is then real, so EVERY D value is zero. Therefore that constant is zero: D(beta_9^+)=D(beta_5^+), D(beta_9^-)=D(beta_5^-). (6) This fixes exactly the regulator information needed here. No claim is made that wedge equality alone identifies an integral Bloch class, an integral flattening, or a complex period torsor. ## 3. Exact cancellation of integer wall marks at full critical points Use logarithmic coordinates Z=rho+i theta. Consider W(Z)=sum_j epsilon_j Li_2(A_j(Z)) +1/2 Z^t C Z+i kappa^t Z+c, A_j(Z)=exp(a_j^t Z+i*pi*nu_j), (7) where a_j,nu_j,C,kappa are real, C is symmetric, and Im c=0. Branches of Li_2 and Log(1-A_j) are matched; D remains its single-valued Bloch--Wigner value on the recorded local sheet. On its ordinary unflattened local branch the exact identity is Im W-sum_j epsilon_j D(A_j) =rho^t Im(gradient W). (8) Indeed Im Li_2(A)=D(A)-log|A| Arg(1-A), and log|A_j|=a_j^t rho. Also Im(1/2 Z^t C Z)=rho^t C theta, while Im(i kappa^t Z)=kappa^t rho. The right side of (8) is precisely this difference. Consistent alternative dilog branches carry their explicit integer logarithmic marks into kappa and the real constant; one must not change the Li_2 sheet without its mark. A simple atomic negative-ray source has its retained factor A_j^N. In exp(W/h), h=2*pi*i/N, it adds 2*pi*i Log A_j. Transverse iterated wall charges add integer sums of such logarithms. They only change kappa by real integer multiples of 2*pi*a_j and add a REAL constant from i*pi*nu_j. Equation (8) remains true. At a FULL critical point, gradient W=0 ==> Im W=sum_j epsilon_j D(A_j). (9) The integer norm charges therefore do not create an additional critical exponential rate log|A_j| after the critical equations are imposed. Dropping full stationarity would make this conclusion false: the residual term on the right side of (8) is then present. The actual scalar action is of the form (7). Put eta_s=sqrt(2*pi*i*s)xi_s at each Gaussian. Its original Gaussian term -pi*i*xi_s^2 becomes -s*eta_s^2/2, a REAL quadratic. The actual atomic arguments are signed monomials in the head positions and exp(eta_s). For each coupled cap put p=2*pi*i*s_cap; its interval term is p Log r, a REAL bilinear form in logarithmic coordinates. Original reflected monomials and complete-color signs give the i*kappa terms. Thus Gaussian and cap variables must be retained in the FULL stationarity condition of (9). ## 4. What regular wall stationary points represent An integer logarithmic wall mark shifts derivatives by multiples of 2*pi*i but leaves the EXPONENTIATED canonical equations unchanged. At a finite regular full interior critical point these are the same actual rational crossing/Hurwitz maps as in Section 1 and the same inverse-meridian cap equations proved in [the coupled-cap note](actual_coupled_caps_interval_source.md). They define a representation of the original oriented knot group, with the original marked source and preferred peripheral convention. For a noncentral complete meridian the peripheral longitude commutes with a nontrivial unipotent matrix, whose centralizer in PSL(2,C) is the unipotent one-parameter group. Thus this is a genuinely boundary-parabolic representation. A cut wall is not generally a physical clock B=1: its DILOG argument A_j is negative real, and an auxiliary flat atom can occur over a noncentral representation. The restriction "full" includes regular wall chains whose remaining real tangent directions span the full complex cotangent space. Their interior complex stationary equation is gradient W=0. It excludes endpoint extrema, rank-deficient/nontransverse corner strata, escaping flags, and singular sources where a constrained stationary equation does not imply the full equation. ## 5. The marked fundamental-cycle comparison extends beyond faithfulness The proof in [the crossing fundamental-cycle note](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) uses unipotence, the actual Hurwitz words, oriented crossing balls, face cancellation and a degree-one peripheral reconstruction. None of its determinant/five-term certificates requires the DEVELOPING representation rho to be faithful. The group used in its relative configuration complex is the original hyperbolic knot group Gamma; its peripheral malnormality concerns Gamma, independently of rho. For any boundary-parabolic rho with noncentral meridians, choose its fixed peripheral flags and generic auxiliary flags. Forced repeated DEVELOPED vertices map to zero in the normalized alternating configuration complex. This is a chain map: repeated-vertex face terms cancel in pairs. The same explicit three five-term boundaries therefore give the rho-developed relative fundamental cycle. Unipotent cancellation uses a nonzero translation because the meridians are noncentral; central representations are handled separately and have trivial PSL image in the one-component case. Consequently, summing (6) over the actual word and keeping the original turn orientations gives sum_crossings D(beta_9)=Vol(rho). (10) Caps contribute their original pairing/marking, not an additional independently assigned tetrahedral regulator. The preferred-longitude correction is the same determinant-one writhe shear as in the fundamental-cycle proof. When a finite developed shape approaches 0,1 or infinity, D extends continuously by zero, so normalized degenerate tetrahedra do not add an unknown constant. This continuity does not justify a quantum source limit at a singular chart. Combining (9)--(10), EVERY regular FULL interior wall critical action in the recorded actual source has its actual representation regulator. The separately proved [sharp representation-volume bound](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md) therefore gives |Im W_critical|<=Vol(M) for all these regular full critical values. This statement alone gives neither a global contour bound nor a selected geometric lower bound. Normalization ray cells can have the full geometric rate, as the retained source calculations already show; they must be grouped exactly rather than called negligible.

title: Source-preserving weighted Fourier energy for the original plat
text: # Source-preserving weighted Fourier energy for the original plat 28 October 2026. There is an exact positive factorial gauge which fixes every original plat turn. It gives a concrete family of weighted Fourier norms and a finite convex upper-bound problem for the **original** scalar. Its gauges can be exponentially conditioned; no such condition number is paid at the paired source. Whole inverse crossing pairs can be contracted before taking positive norms. This does not give the sharp hyperbolic-volume estimate. In particular, same-frame diagonal scaling cannot reduce the local crossing's flat Hilbert--Schmidt norm. A short exact doubled-source calculation below identifies the coherent sewing probability which still needs an estimate. ## 1. The physical factorial gauge fixes the original paired source Put Q=exp(2 pi i/N), d=N-1, x=-exp(-pi i/N), F_a=(Q;Q)_a. The exact root reflection identity is F_a F_(d-a)=N (-1)^a Q^(a(a+1)/2). (1) Consequently the actual middle-certificate frame and its positive part, Gamma_a=(-1)^a Q^(-a(a-1)/2) F_a^2 =Q^a |F_a|^2, L_a=|F_a|^2/N, obey at EVERY index Gamma_a Gamma_(d-a)=N^2 Q^(-1), L_a L_(d-a)=1. (2) The second relation is an exact equality of positive real numbers. It is not an asymptotic bound near a selected cap index. Use the original physical cup, ordinary cap, and full marked row: p_(a,b)=N x^(-b) delta_(a+b,d), ell_(a,b)=x^b g_a/N delta_(a+b,d), m_(a,b)=x^b/N^2, g_a=x^(1-N)Q^(-a). For EVERY real t, positive powers defined by their real logarithm give (L^t tensor L^t)p=p, ell(L^(-t) tensor L^(-t))=ell. (3) The marked row has the same identity on pair degree d. It is not an identity of the unrestricted row m. In an assembled original k-cup plat the exact integer-degree argument forces the final marked pair to have degree d after the ordinary caps are taken. Diagonal gauges preserve that argument. Thus (3) holds for the full marked source in its legitimate whole-network scope. More generally, choose arbitrary positive numbers A_(r,a) on the odd head of pair r and set the even-head entries to A_(r,d-b)^(-1). The product gauge G fixes p^(tensor k) and its original ordinary/marked co-source exactly. L^t on both heads is the special case (2). These are physical-head transformations; they do not identify a fusion-relative index with a physical one. For clarity, retain the proved original whole-source normalization from [the actual plat Gram theorem](actual_plat_cup_cap_gram_support.md): P_N=chi_N N^(k-1) <phi,W uhat>, uhat=p^(tensor k)/||p^(tensor k)||, phi=G_top^dagger uhat, ||phi||=||uhat||=1. (4) Here G_top is the original unitary product of ordinary pivots; the marked pair has none. The external chi_N, framing and peripheral line are exactly those in that theorem. The gauge G just defined commutes with G_top and fixes uhat and phi. Therefore, for ANY two such endpoint gauges G_in,G_out, <phi,G_out W G_in^(-1) uhat>=<phi,W uhat>. (5) This provides a genuine source-preserving positive gauge freedom. It does not declare one isolated Gamma in a local five-point word removable; such a local replacement still needs its typed interfaces. ## 2. Exact weighted Plancherel and the dual metric Let F be the normalized unitary finite Fourier matrix, F_(r,a)=Q^(ra)/sqrt(N). For a physical head vector v put vhat_t=F L^t v, H_t=F L^(-2t) F^dagger. Then exactly, for arbitrary v,w, <v,w>=<vhat_t,H_t what_t>, (H_t)_(r,s)=N^(-1)sum_a Q^((r-s)a)(N/|F_a|^2)^(2t). (6) H_t is positive definite. These are the compulsory dual norm weights of this factorial Fourier transformation. Flat Fourier energy of L^t v is a different norm from that of v. Equation (2) pairs the weights reciprocally on the original cap charge, explaining the source cancellation in (3); it does not make H_t the identity. The usual unitary Fourier changes can now be made at every physical wire, with all turns transported. In the G=L^t frame their original turn arrays are unchanged before the unitary Fourier transform. All interior inverse frames cancel literally. Thus this weighted duality extends to any signed original word and its doubled norm, including the marked pair, with no exponential source renormalization. The size of the weights remains explicit. Uniformly in a, log L_a=2N J(a/N)+O(log N), J(s)=integral_0^s log(2 sin(pi u))du. (7) Hence (6) carries the full factorial dilogarithm action. It cannot be replaced by a flat positive trace merely because its source normalization is exact. ## 3. A computable positive energy upper-bound hierarchy Partition a fixed original word into consecutive actual blocks W=B_l ... B_1. Choose arbitrary positive diagonal tensor gauges G_j on all live physical heads between blocks; only the endpoint gauges are required to satisfy the paired-source condition of Section 1. Define C_j=G_j B_j G_(j-1)^(-1). All factors, pivots, and sources in (4) remain original. From (5), ordinary Cauchy--Schwarz and submultiplicativity give the finite-N bound |P_N| <= |chi_N|N^(k-1) product_j ||C_j||_op <= |chi_N|N^(k-1) product_j ||C_j||_HS. (8) This is not a largest-root or a favorable-source prescription. The right side is an explicit optimization problem in known original block matrices. At the finest partition the blocks are literal crossings, whose entries are given by the finite factorial formula. There is no unknown knot scalar in that objective. Write a diagonal gauge entry as exp(s_j(I)), where s_j(I) is the sum of its head log entries. Each summand in its logarithmic HS objective is (1/2)log sum_(I,J) |(B_j)_(I,J)|^2 exp(2s_j(I)-2s_(j-1)(J)). (9) It is convex in every gauge logarithm: the Hessian of log-sum-exp is the positive covariance matrix of its exponent vectors. The paired endpoint conditions are linear equations in these same logarithms. No minimum-attainment hypothesis is needed to take the infimum in (8). The factorial choices in Section 1 are legitimate points of this feasible set, even when they depend exponentially on N. Merging neighboring blocks never worsens the best HS bound, since ||AB||_HS <= ||A||_HS ||B||_HS with the intervening gauge cancelled. In particular an actual neighboring R R^(-1) block is exactly the identity, of polynomial HS norm N^k. Its exponential cost is zero. Thus one can perform exact signed-pair and other verified word reductions before taking norms, rather than charging their separate positive crossing energies. This is a constructive renormalization of those pairs with the original source retained. The same block principle applies to a local contraction containing an actual turn. In particular the defining complete ADO Markov calculation gives, for either sign with its own original zero-framing correction, Tr_2[Rhat_+ (I tensor g)]=I, Tr_2[Rhat_- (I tensor g)]=I. (9a) For arbitrary one-head exterior matrices A,B it follows that Tr_2[(A tensor I) Rhat_sigma (B tensor I) (I tensor g)]=AB, sigma=+,-. (9b) No division by AB or by a knot period occurs. Thus a genuine curl subnetwork, including its original cap, can be replaced by the identity **before** forming its doubled positive block energy. Its doubled map is then the identity trace-preserving channel and has zero exponential cost. This works inside any larger knot word. It does not replace an unclosed crossing by a trace-preserving channel. More generally any verified exact local tensor contraction can be used as a block, with its original boundary source retained, before applying (8). The finest flat bound already proves an unconditional whole-period estimate. For a word of m crossings, the independently proved [actual crossing norm theorem](weighted_crossing_source_gap.md) gives log||R_+||_HS=log||R_-||_HS =N v_8/(2pi)+O(log N). Tensoring with a fixed number of spectator identities adds only O(log N). All complete external lines in chi_N have polynomial magnitude. Therefore limsup_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|P_N| <= m v_8. (10) The same holds for the original reduced Kashaev scalar, since its complete modified-dimension factor is a known root phase divided by N. This is a crossing bound, not the desired sharp Vol(S^3-K) bound. The convex bound (8)--(9), including exact block reductions, is an operative way to improve it; no assertion is made that it has already reached the hyperbolic volume for a broad knot class. ## 4. The remaining positive coherent sewing probability The precise cost of closure can be stated before any scalar-cut reduction. Let W act on one open head tensor an environment of dimension D=N^(b-1), and keep the original unitary environment pivot g. Group vec(W) by its open input/output pair and environment pair. Put h_g=vec(g^dagger)/sqrt(D), P_g=I_(open pair) tensor |h_g><h_g|, C=Tr_env[W(I tensor g)]. P_g is an orthogonal positive projector. Direct expansion of the matrix indices proves ||C||_HS^2=D <vec(W),P_g vec(W)>. (11) This identity holds for nonscalar C. Under any unitary Fourier transform of the half-edge indices, BOTH vec(W) and h_g transform, and the right side is unchanged. It is not the same as replacing the projector by an identity or dephasing its channels. If the original cut is C=K_N I, the normalized projection probability on the free vectorized word is p_g=N|K_N|^2/(D||W||_HS^2), 0<=p_g<=1. (12) The positive source opening Pi=N g_1 E_d(Z_1Z_2)E_0(X) in [the exact cap Fourier theorem](actual_middle_wall_fourier_packet.md#5-the-original-affine-cap-is-a-charged-fourier-mode) satisfies ||(C tensor I)Pi||_HS^2=N||C||_HS^2 for arbitrary C. Thus it supplies a normalized local positive realization of (11), but leaves its exterior coherent projection in place. For a normalized single positive crossing (the unknot curl), C=I exactly. With b=2, (12) becomes the all-N identity p_curl=||R_+||_HS^(-2), log p_curl= -N v_8/pi+O(log N). (13) This uses the original residual twist and pivotal cap; they have not been reset. It explains why local positive energies can have a larger rate than the closed period. The block renormalization in Section 3 is one exact way of contracting such source effects before bounding; it is not permission to discard the coherent probability for a general knot word. There is also a sharp restriction on improving a local block by a same-frame positive diagonal gauge. The actual balanced crossing is symmetric, R^t=R. For ANY positive diagonal D, ||D R D^(-1)||_HS^2 =sum_(i,j)|R_(i,j)|^2 D_i^2/D_j^2 >=sum_(i,j)|R_(i,j)|^2=||R||_HS^2, (14) by pairing i,j and j,i and using r+r^(-1)>=2. Fourier changes do not alter this norm. Thus isolated same-frame factorial scaling cannot remove the regular octahedral rate; an improvement must use actual coupled block contraction or a controlled whole-source estimate. ## 5. Audit and current scope [The audit](../experiments/audit_actual_weighted_fourier_plat_energy.py) passes N=2,...,12. It checks exact factorial reflection, preservation of the original cup/cap and the correctly restricted marker for positive and negative real gauge powers, the non-flat dual Fourier metric, the nonscalar source projector identity, unitary transport of its coherent source, actual crossing symmetry, the local norm minimum, and the normalized unknot-curl probability. Eight complete original four-head plats additionally test the literal ordinary plus full marked source, its whole-degree reduction, unequal paired endpoint gauges, arbitrary internal gauges and the positive block energy bound. The extra external Cartan/framing lines are common unit phases on both sides of those source comparisons. [Saved results](../experiments/actual_weighted_fourier_plat_energy_results.json). The new constructive point is the original-source-preserving paired factorial gauge and its explicit positive convex energy hierarchy. The sharp geometric estimate for that hierarchy, or a direct bound on its remaining coherent sewing probability, has not been proved. No global geometric coefficient or hyperbolic-volume lower bound is inferred here.

title: Weyl symmetry of the actual state and automatic operator reciprocity
text: # Weyl symmetry of the actual state and automatic operator reciprocity Research note, 26 October 2026. This removes the extra quantum-reciprocity hypothesis from the preceding normal-period formulation when the operator is the primitive minimal operator of the actual normalized ADO family. The state symmetry, its peripheral factors, and the monomial reciprocity are proved directly. They hold for every knot at every level, with the usual finite exceptional set for a chosen operator's specialization. They do not prove injectivity of its relevant root-fiber sector, identify its classical geometric factors, or establish the regulator norm. The state is the literature one fixed in [the ADO audit](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). Its all-level annihilator is nonzero by [the finite-state proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md). No new ordering of a classical polynomial or replacement state is chosen here. ## 1. The actual reduced and full periods have reflected meridians Use q=exp(pi*i/N), x=q^alpha, M=-qx and Y=M^2. On the actual N-dimensional color the matrices and coproduct are H v_a=(alpha-2a)v_a, K v_a=x q^(-2a)v_a, E v_a=[a][alpha-a+1]v_(a-1), F v_a=v_(a+1), Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E, Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F. Let a= N-1 and alpha'=2a-alpha. Then x'=q^(-2)x^(-1), M'=M^(-1), theta_(alpha')=theta_alpha, theta_alpha=q^((alpha^2+2(1-N)alpha)/2). (1.1) The conclusion is the exact state identity F_N(M)=F_N(M^(-1)), N_N(M)=N_N(M^(-1)). (1.2) Here N_N is the full modified-trace period. The evenness already proved in [the meridian descent](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) therefore also gives F_N(Y)=F_N(Y^(-1)). The shift in x in (1.1) is essential; unshifted inversion of x is not the statement. ### A generator proof of the turnover Define the Chevalley algebra involution chi(E)=F, chi(F)=E, chi(K)=K^(-1), chi(H)=-H. The displayed coproduct and antipodes S(E)=-E K^(-1), S(F)=-K F give directly, on every generator, Delta chi=(chi tensor chi)Delta^op, chi S=S^(-1)chi, chi(K^(1-N))=K^(N-1). (1.3) For the actual finite universal R, termwise substitution gives (chi tensor chi)(R)=R_21. (1.4) Indeed its Cartan q^(H tensor H/2) is unchanged, and each E^k tensor F^k becomes F^k tensor E^k, with the same coefficient. This also checks inverse crossings. Pullback by chi reverses tensor order; with the ordinary flip as tensor-order map, (1.4) is precisely the positive-crossing identity for turning the diagram through pi about its vertical axis. For clarity, this turnover includes the cups and caps. Right duals use the action through S. Equation chi S=S^(-1)chi identifies the pulled-back right dual with the left dual of the pulled-back module. The evaluation f(v) and coevaluation sum_i v_i tensor v_i^* then become the left evaluation and coevaluation after reversing tensor order. In the common right-dual presentation, the left closing maps are evaluation with the pivot and coevaluation with its inverse. The last identity in (1.3) therefore sends the closing matrix g to g^(-1), exactly as the spatial turnover does. The zigzag contractions remain identity maps. Equation (1.1) checks the twist on the color; the balancing identity extends that check to its tensor products. Consequently the turnover identity holds for each crossing, inverse crossing, cup, cap and twist, and hence for their compositions. This is a generator proof for the actual ribbon-tangle evaluation. A rotation of the marked framed knot is an ambient isotopy. If the boundary ribbon frame is moved by the rotation, it conjugates the cut endomorphism by the same endpoint map on both sides; that has no effect on its scalar. No knot-invertibility assumption is involved. Thus the reduced knot scalar is unchanged by replacing its color by its Chevalley pullback. Here is the explicit identification of that color, including all normalizations. In the Chevalley pullback of V_alpha set w_b=d_b v_(N-1-b), d_0=1, d_b=product_(s=1)^b [s][alpha'-s+1]. (1.5) For generic alpha these are a basis. The root identities [N-s]=[s] and [z-N]=-[z] give [b][alpha'-b+1]=[N-b][alpha-(N-b)+1]. Substitution now proves E_chi w_b=[b][alpha'-b+1]w_(b-1), F_chi w_b=w_(b+1), K_chi w_b=q^(alpha'-2b)w_b, H_chi w_b=(alpha'-2b)w_b. So this color is exactly V_(alpha'). Combined with the turnover identities, it proves the first part of (1.2) at generic colors. The cut scalar is Laurent polynomial in x at zero framing, so the identity extends through all exceptional colors as a whole germ. One can also keep the stripped Cartan scalar throughout the calculation. If R_0,theta_0 denote the normalized crossing and residual twist used in the finite cut formulas, their reflected comparison has the same explicit multiplier h_N(x)=q^(-2)x^(2N-2), C R_(0,alpha') C^(-1)=h_N P R_(0,alpha) P, theta_(0,alpha')=h_N theta_(0,alpha). (1.6) Here C is the tensor square of the basis map in (1.5), and P flips the two factors; use h_N^(-1) for the inverse crossing. The product h_N^w is cancelled by the exact zero-framing correction h_N^(-w). Thus there is no unrecorded scalar or branch factor in (1.2). This cancellation is before any ideal-color specialization. Finally the full factor is d_N(M)=eta_N*(M-M^(-1))/(M^N-M^(-N)), eta_N=i^(N+3). It is exactly invariant under M inversion. Hence the full equality in (1.2) also holds as a meromorphic whole-germ identity, including its poles, residues and the cancelled value d_N(1)=eta_N/N. ## 2. The actual normal-state ideal is reflected Put f=Y-1 and v_N(Y)=f F_N(Y). On rational meridian functions use R h(Y)=h(Y^(-1)), J=-Y R. Equation (1.2) gives, for the actual state at every level, J v_N=v_N. (2.1) On the formal quantum torus T Y=q^2Y T, write Q=q^2. Direct composition gives J^2=1 and the algebra involution jmath(B)=J B J, jmath(Y)=Y^(-1), jmath(T)=Q T^(-1). (2.2) Let I_v be the actual all-level annihilator ideal of v_N. It is nonzero and satisfies jmath(I_v)=I_v: apply J to its exact root equations and use (2.1). There is no assumed AJ theorem in this argument. This is the existing full ADO operator ideal in recorded conventions. Indeed, with U=Y^N at a root, u_N=F_N/S_N=f F_N/(U-1), N_N(M)=eta_N M^(N-1)u_N(Y). The shift fixes U and has the character q^(N-1)=-q^(-1) on M^(N-1). Thus I_v=I_u, and it is obtained from the full literature ideal by that explicit character twist. It also equals the fixed rational gauge f I_F f^(-1). These statements retain all actual period factors; they do not algebraize v_N as a function of q. ## 3. Primitive minimality forces unitary monomial reciprocity Over C(q,Y)[T^(+/-1)] choose the actual least-order operator B, with support 0,...,d. Clear its rational denominators and remove the common coefficient content, recording those operations. Then B=sum_(j=0)^d b_j(q,Y)T^j, b_j in A=C[q^(+/-1),Y^(+/-1)], gcd_A(b_0,...,b_d)=1, b_0*b_d!=0. (3.1) This primitive representative is unique up to C^* q^r Y^s. The state lattice remains the actual one from v_N and the full formula in Section 2, rather than a newly chosen companion lattice. Since the ideal is reflected, T^d jmath(B) is another actual order-d operator. Minimality gives B=h(q,Y)T^d jmath(B). (3.2) Its coefficient list is Q^j b_j(q,Q^(-d)Y^(-1)), in reversed order. It is primitive because this substitution is an automorphism of the Laurent UFD and each Q^j is a unit. Comparing the valuations at every irreducible of A in the two primitive lists forces h to be a unit: h=c_0 q^a Y^b, c_0 in C^*. The reflection is involutive, but the degree-restoring map S_d(B)=T^d jmath(B) satisfies S_d^2(B)=Q^d B. Applying it twice to (3.2) gives h(q,Y)h(q,Q^(-d)Y^(-1))*Q^d=1. Hence c_0=epsilon in {1,-1} and a=d(b-1). Multiplying (3.2) by J on the right therefore yields the exact intertwiner B J=J' B, J'=c(q,Y)T^d R, c(q,Y)=sigma*q^(dm)*Y^m, sigma in {1,-1}, m in Z. (3.3) Here m=b+1 and sigma=-epsilon. In particular c(q,Y)c(q,Q^(-d)Y^(-1))=1, |c(q,Y)|=1 when |q|=|Y|=1. (3.4) Thus the two root-fiber reflections are unitary involutions. The primitive minimal operator of the actual normal state automatically has exactly the reciprocity required by the preceding period note. This is uniform for every knot. It does not require primeness, alternatingness, a prescribed coefficient ordering, or a conjectured classical symbol. The original half-root q is retained: q^(dm) must not be replaced by a guessed integer power of Q. Primitivity also makes its q=1 symbol B_cl nonzero: otherwise every coefficient would have the common factor q-1. Specializing (3.3) gives the balanced polynomial identity B_cl(Y,L)=-sigma*Y^(m-1)*L^d*B_cl(Y^(-1),L^(-1)). This is a proved symmetry of the actual classical symbol. Its geometric A-component still needs a separate survival theorem. ## 4. The Weyl sector of the normal source is now automatic For this B, choose the actual F-annihilator P=B*f. It is an operator identity, with right factor f retained. This construction does not assert that every primitive reduced-state annihilator has that factor; the necessary positive-growth test in [the normal-period note](peripheral_normal_period.md) still concerns each such annihilator separately. On the central fiber U=1 write B_N(t)=B_0+t B_1+..., t=U-1, using the fixed roots Y_r(t)=Q_N^r(1+t)^(1/N). The actual vector v_N(t) has (v_0)_r=(Q_N^r-1)C_r(q_N), (v_0)_0=0, B_0 v_1=-B_1 v_0, K_N=N*(v_1)_0. (4.1) The state symmetry proves J v_0=v_0 at every level, including any level with K_N=0 and without a rank-one assumption. Inversion sends t to -t+O(t^2), while the derivative of J(t) is J/N. Differentiating (3.3) and applying it to v_0 gives exactly J' B_1 v_0=-B_1 v_0. (4.2) The complete evaluation vector e_0 has J-parity -1. Thus both the source and the desired functional live in the -1 sectors. The unwanted symmetry sector has zero overlap in this pairing. Let B_- be B_0 restricted from the -1 domain to the -1 range. It suffices that B_- be injective; surjectivity onto the entire range sector is unnecessary. The actual derivative guarantees that the source is in its image. Then its left inverse, or its Moore--Penrose inverse, gives K_N=-N e_0^* B_-^+ B_1 v_0. (4.3) Extra +1 kernel vectors do not change the complete value. More generally the value is unique whenever e_0 annihilates the kernel of B_-, even if that restriction is not injective. Those root-fiber conditions remain to prove for a broad class of actual operators. The bounded source estimates from the preceding note apply: ||B_1||=O(1/N), ||v_0||=O(sqrt(N)D_N). Consequently the exponential part must come from the specified inverse pairing, with its actual source overlap. Reciprocity alone supplies neither its inverse norm nor a nonzero geometric contribution. ## 5. The metric period is independent of primitive generator units Another primitive minimal generator is B'=u B with u=c_0 q^a Y^b. At the root, let D_u be its diagonal multiplication matrix on the orbit. It is |c_0| times a unitary matrix. Differentiation gives B_0'=D_u B_0, B_1'v_0=D_u B_1v_0, because the extra derivative of u multiplies B_0 v_0=0. Thus the normal equation and its complete period are unchanged. The range reflection is conjugated by D_u, so its Weyl-sector norm is changed only by the fixed scalar |c_0|. The positive exponential rate and the exact pairing (4.3) are therefore well defined for the primitive minimal operator, with the marked actual lattice. This does not license dropping a nonunit meridian factor. Such a factor is outside the remaining generator ambiguity and its zeros, poles, state gauge and normal jets must be kept as before. The ambient relation J T J=Q T^(-1) also gives, with the exact ADO character kappa=-q^(-1), J(kappa*T)J=(kappa*T)^(-1), (kappa*T)^N=(-1)^(N-1). (5.1) The even-level sign is part of the descended data. This concerns the ambient orbit module, not an assertion that the scalar solution line is invariant under T. ## 6. The bounded polar source is a finite sine transform The actual symmetry also proves the ordinary-color identity C_(N-j)(q_N)=C_j(q_N), 1<=j<N. (6.1) In the notation of [the regular-period note](regularized_kashaev_period.md), write a_r=[Y^r]p_N for the Taylor coefficients of its proper polar function at zero. Pair j with N-j in its already proved formula. With theta_j=pi*j/N this gives exactly a_r=-(2/N)sum_(j=1)^(N-1) C_j(q_N) sin((2r-1)theta_j)sin(theta_j). Define the usual real sine matrix S_(a,j)=sqrt(2/N)sin(pi*a*j/N). For 1<=a,j<N, its rows are orthonormal: expand the sine products as differences of cosines and sum the two finite geometric series. Integer row labels outside that interval are zero or signed copies of these rows. Thus a_r=-sum_j S_(2r-1,j)S_(1,j)C_j(q_N), |a_r|<=D_N, r>=0. (6.2) The bound follows either from the operator norm of S diag(C_j)S^t, or by Cauchy--Schwarz. In particular a_0=sum_j S_(1,j)^2 C_j(q_N), sum_j S_(1,j)^2=1. Therefore the fixed Laurent-window source of the regular period is a finite linear combination of these explicit sine moments, with coefficients from the chosen fixed operator. No surgery or TQFT comparison theorem is being assumed for this description. It improves the earlier 2D_N bound and specifies its exact Weyl structure. It does not give a lower bound on the source's projection to a geometric singular vector or algebraize these moments in q. ## 7. Coverage, verification, and the remaining norm problem This symmetry has existing coverage: the abstract of [Martel--Willetts, 2112.15204](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.15204) advertises the inherited ADO symmetry and orientation independence. Quantum-torus Weyl reciprocity is also covered in [Le's lectures, Section 5.9](https://letu.math.gatech.edu/Papers/Lectures_Luminy_2014_new.pdf). No unified-invariant, homological, AJ or asymptotic proof from those sources is a premise here. The proofs above use the actual finite R, the pivotal pairings, primitive minimality and Laurent arithmetic. No novelty claim is made for Weyl symmetry or balanced operators. [The independent audit](../experiments/audit_actual_weyl_descent.py) checks 27 local Chevalley comparisons through level 15, including the ideal color; 63 actual cut turnovers at generic meridians; 25 complete Laurent-state reflections, with their ordinary-color and sine-source identities; 60 monomial-reciprocity cases; and sine orthogonality at nine even/composite/odd levels. These exact finite-field checks validate the uniform formulas, rather than proving their scope by enumeration. Results are in [the output](../experiments/actual_weyl_descent_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_actual_weyl_descent.py The [triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md) already fixes the marked geometric Bloch action and its volume norm on the actual classical critical branch. This note now makes the quantum Weyl descent uniform for the actual knot state and its primitive minimal normal operator. What remains is the root-fiber solvability and inverse-pairing norm in (4.3), together with survival of the geometric factor in the actual operator. No equality D_N=A_K or volume conjecture is inferred. The subsequent [peripheral-fusion proof](actual_peripheral_fusion.md) also derives these boundary conventions directly from adjacent-color fusion and heterogeneous crossings. In the odd normal state w_N=(M-M^(-1))F_N, the fundamental parallel acts as -(T+T^(-1)); in v_N=M*w_N it acts as kappa*T+kappa^(-1)T^(-1), with the same kappa=-q^(-1). At M=1 the fusion has an explicitly retained square-zero Casimir residue with normalized pivotal trace. This provides exact quantum boundary data, while the geometric source and norm comparison above remain unproved. The subsequent [ramified Weyl-fibre proof](ramified_weyl_fibre.md) extends the quadratic descent to the actual branch-point lattice. Explicit units U^(1/(2N)) and U^(m/(2N)) linearize both involutions; the invariant lattice over s=((U-1)/(U+1))^2 retains the first negative coefficient as a special-fibre coordinate. The full ADO period is (eta_N/2)e_0^*b_0 there. The half-root in (3.3) also determines the exact sector dimensions, exposing signatures for which the optional injectivity condition cannot hold. This algebraic evaluation supplies no additional volume-growth theorem.

title: The original complete core has a finite coupled face-coefficient system
status: Exact polynomial system and fold selection; regular-chart momenta
text: # The original complete core has a finite coupled face-coefficient system 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. The original four-component circle system admits a polynomial source gauge that preserves its first component. Tensoring it on the actual shared face variables gives an exact whole-source system coupling only finitely shifted face coefficients. The original finite support and a source-selected fold adapter determine its polynomial solution. Its reduced characteristic is identified algebraically with the existing ORDERED local character transport. This is a system for the complete-image external-color core. It does not erase its ordinary small-color subsets, eliminate the coefficient family to a scalar A-polynomial, or establish a complex asymptotic of its period. ## 1. A polynomial four-component source gauge Use N>=3, d=N-1, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2 and the actual polynomial Z_j(x,b,y), 0<=j<=d, of the [fixed-fold source theorem](actual_positive_face_fixed_fold_packet.md), equation(10). Write Z_-1=0 and Delta_j=(x-Q^j y)(x-Q^(-j)y), Pcal_j=P_d(x,y)/product_(r=1)^j Delta_r, P_d(x,y)=product_(r=1)^d(x-Q^r y). The rational presentation of Pcal_j is used only to define the following source; its canceled polynomial expressions are proved below. Retain omega_j=q^(d^2/2)(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)], U_j=omega_j^epsilon Pcal_j (Z_j^b Z_j^c, Z_j^b Z_(j-1)^c, Z_(j-1)^b Z_j^c, Delta_j Z_(j-1)^b Z_(j-1)^c)^T. (1) Here the superscript b or c indicates the middle face, not a power. The first component is precisely the original reflected complete-circle polynomial omega_j^epsilon B_ext,j. In the notation of the fixed-fold note, U_j=G_j V_j with G_j=diag(1,1,1,Delta_j). ALL FOUR components of (1) are polynomials in x,b,c,y. Below the fold, Pcal_j is the ordinary forced polynomial, so the claim is immediate. Above the fold put r=d-j and s=d-2r. The actual large-H reflection gives Z_j=P_s Z_r, Pcal_j=P_s^-1. For s>=2, Z_(j-1)=P_(s-2) Z_(r+1), so the second and third components reduce respectively to P_(s-2) Z_r^b Z_(r+1)^c and P_(s-2) Z_(r+1)^b Z_r^c. At the even first bridge s=1, they instead reduce to Z_M^b Z_M^c, where M=floor(d/2). Finally (U_j)_4=omega_j^epsilon B_ext,(j-1), j>=1, because Delta_j Pcal_j=Pcal_(j-1). It is zero at j=0.
