This proves polynomiality, including zero-face evaluations, without choosing a Laurent expansion at a pole. The component degrees are d,d-1,d-1,d. The gauge G is not invertible on Delta_j=0; no such divisor is discarded. Put theta=pi/N and retain the actual finite coefficients u_j=cos((j-1)theta)sin(j theta), v_j^b=sin((2j-1)theta)[x+y+2b cos(j theta)cos((j-1)theta)], barw_j=sin((j-1)theta)cos(j theta), w_j=barw_j Delta_(j-1), L_j=u_j^2 Delta_j, r_j=(-Q^j)^epsilon. The exact polynomial-gauge recurrence is L_j U_j=r_j N_j U_(j-1), (2) N_j= [v_j^b v_j^c, -v_j^b w_j, -w_j v_j^c, barw_j^2 Delta_(j-1)] [u_j v_j^b, 0, -u_j w_j, 0] [u_j v_j^c, -u_j w_j, 0, 0] [Delta_j u_j^2,0, 0, 0]. Indeed N_j=G_j M_j G_(j-1)^-1 on the localized field. Its only apparent denominator is w_j^2/Delta_(j-1), and it cancels exactly as displayed. Thus (2) is polynomial and extends across that divisor. The ORIGINAL finite sequence is zero outside 0,...,d. The equations at j=0 and j=N remain true: the first uses u_0=0 and U_-1=0; the last uses the two actual terminal scalar relations and u_N=0. There is no periodic closing arrow or omitted endpoint current. Every coefficient of (2) is Laurent in Q^j. Its face degree is at most three. If mathcal U(z)=sum_(j=0)^d U_j z^j and Theta f(z)=f(Qz), then exactly [L(Theta)-z(-Q Theta)^epsilon N(Q Theta)]mathcal U(z)=0. (3) The Laurent Theta powers lie between -5 and5; the z-degree is at most1. These bounds are independent of N. The first component is unchanged from the original finite core. For its full Fourier gauge S(chi)=exp(pi i d chi)mathcal U(exp(-2pi i chi)), retain exactly exp(pi i d chi)Theta mathcal U=q^d S(chi-1/N). (4) ## 2. The original source selects the fold crossing This section concerns the finite source, not a choice of formal WKB solution. Work over the face coefficient field localized at the Delta_j that occur, and put M=floor(d/2), s0=d-2M and h=M+s0+1=d-M+1. The known initial vector is U_0=omega_0^epsilon P_d(x,y)(1,0,0,0)^T. Let R4 reverse the four components. The ACTUAL source has the exact polynomial fold adapter U_h=q^((s0+1)epsilon) R4 U_M. (5) A direct proof uses h=d-(M-1) and h-1=d-M in the large-H reflection. The first and fourth components exchange because B_ext,(d-j)=B_ext,j; the two cross products exchange with their forced factors. Finally Delta_h=Delta_M and omega_h/omega_M=q^(s0+1). These give every component of (5), including the even bridge s0=1. No new square root is required. The adapter is a unit phase times a permutation. Near the actual fold Delta_M=(x+y)^2-4xy sin^2((s0+1)pi/(2N)) is uniformly positive on the stated positive radius compact. The adapter advances one step at odd levels and TWO at even levels. To see why this matters, write N=2H, M=H-1. At j=H the leading coefficient is nonzero and the transfer has rank one: U_H=(1,A^-1,A^-1,1)^T (U_(H-1))_1, A=x+y. (6) At j=H+1 its leading coefficient is zero, while N_(H+1) has just one nonzero row, sin^2(theta)(A^2,-A^3,-A^3,A^2). It annihilates (6), so this row places no condition on U_(H+1). An invertible analytic gauge cannot change this rank loss. For generic face data and every even N>=4, the finite system (2), with zero support outside 0,...,d and prescribed U_0, therefore has a THREE-dimensional affine freedom whenever it has a solution. States through U_H are determined. The new U_(H+1) is an arbitrary four-vector; all later transfers through d are invertible. The terminal row at N imposes one nonzero condition. The determinant of N_j is [Delta_j/Delta_(j-1)](u_j w_j)^4, so these assertions retain the relevant factors. At odd N, u_j never vanishes inside 1,...,d, and the prescribed U_0 already determines every state. The source adapter (5) fixes the even free vector and restores uniqueness. Its compatibility with the terminal equation is provided by the literal Newton source and its reflection. This is not a claim of three different original sources: the unsupplemented operator has extra solutions, while its specified source data fixes one. ## 3. Exact whole-source coefficient equations Use the actual labeled planar source graph. Each circle i has its literal four incident faces (x_i,b_i,c_i,y_i), with all repeated or shared face names identified. Tensor the local polynomial vectors: W(z_1,...,z_R;L)=tensor_(i=1)^R mathcal U_i(z_i;L). It has 4^R components and is polynomial in EVERY face variable. For any nonnegative exponent vector n, define the finite coefficient family C_n(z)=[product_f L_f^(n_f)] W(z;L), (7) and set it to zero if some n_f<0. The component indexed by alpha has face degree dR-m(alpha), where m counts its local second/third indices. Thus the entire family is finite. It is not a choice of rational-series expansion or a coefficient integral through newly introduced divisors. Let S_i be the operator (3) acting on tensor factor i. Expand its actual face-polynomial coefficients as S_i=sum_nu L^nu S_(i,nu)(z_i,Theta_i). All nu are nonnegative and |nu|<=3. Exact coefficient extraction gives sum_nu S_(i,nu)(z_i,Theta_i) C_(n-nu)(z)=0, i=1,...,R, for every n. (8) These are the sought finite FACE SHIFTS. No scalar equation for only one selected coefficient is inferred. The operators commute before extraction: they act on separate external registers and separate tensor factors, while their shared face multiplications commute. The coupled coefficient equations inherit this compatibility. The local initial vectors and adapters (5) tensor to give the actual finite solution. Over the localized face field, uniqueness follows by advancing each register through its regular rows and its specified fold jump; the constructions in different registers commute. Polynomiality then follows from (1), not from an assertion about arbitrary operator solutions. The adapters can equally be recorded coefficientwise in (7). Let u,v be the two ORIGINAL marked faces and define n* by n*_u=n*_v=0, n*_f=d for every other face f. For the all-first tensor component, the exact original entire complete core is F_N(h)=chi_(D,N) N^R exp[pi i d sum_i h_i/N] (C_(n*))(exp(-2pi i h_1/N),...,exp(-2pi i h_R/N))_(1,...,1). (9) This follows from the source-exact reflected Fourier pairing and the original marked face-coefficient theorem. It retains the common twist phase, N^R measure, original mark and finite parity. The two marked faces are set to zero only AFTER polynomial extraction. Equation (9) is the empty subset in the external reflection formula; ordinary-color subsets are not represented by deleting them from this statement. ## 4. The principal characteristic is the actual ordered character map There is an exact algebraic identification with [the original local critical-character map](actual_augmented_plat_local_critical_character_map.md). Use its variables T,U,V,J and internal roots Z,W. On a regular chart, P(X,Y)=T(J-Y)^2(X-Y)+(Y-1)^2(TY-XJ)=0. (10) The source convention has b incoming and c outgoing. Thus the OLD ordered map has T=x/y, U=-x/c at the output and V=-x/b at the input. Put r=(J+1)^2/(4J), A=x+y, and D=A^2-4xy r, B_b=A+2br, B_c=A+2cr, e_out(Z)=-y Z(J-1)^2(TZ-UJ)/[J U(J-Z)^2], e_in(W)=-y W(J-1)^2(TW-VJ)/[J V(J-W)^2]. (11) Then (10) implies exactly e_out^2-2B_c e_out+D=0, e_in^2-2B_b e_in+D=0. (12) Here is a finite polynomial certificate. By homogeneity set y=1, x=T. For one generic triangle with middle face z=-T/X, write e=-Z(J-1)^2(TZ-XJ)/[J X(J-Z)^2] and B_z=T+1+2zr. Then e^2-2B_z e+D=-P(X,Z) K(X,Z)/[J X^2(J-Z)^4], K=J^3 X(J-T) +[JT(1-J^2)+2J^2X(T-1)]Z +[X(1-JT)+2T(J-1)]Z^2. Conversely the resultant of P(X,Z) and J X(J-Z)^2 e+Z(J-1)^2(TZ-XJ) is J^4 X^2(J-1)^4(T-X)^2 (e^2-2B_z e+D). Thus, away from the displayed degeneracies and the quadratic discriminant, the two local roots correspond to the two continuant roots. This is an elimination of the ACTUAL critical equation. The same character map's ordered centralizer eigenratio is R0=ZW(J-1)^4(TZ-UJ)(TW-VJ) /[JUV(J-Z)^2(J-W)^2(T-J)(TJ-1)]. Since D=y^2(T-J)(T-J^-1), its exact factorization is R0=e_out e_in/D. (13) It is therefore the lambda in the reduced continuant quartic D(lambda^4+1)-4B_bB_c(lambda^3+lambda) +(4B_b^2+4B_c^2-2D)lambda^2=0. (14) The polynomial gauge changes no full principal determinant: with u=(1/2)sin(2pi mu), J=exp(2pi i mu), the retained determinant is u^8 D^3 Pquartic(z(-J)^epsilon), (15) where Pquartic is the left side of (14). This polynomial identity follows by similarity where D!=0 and hence extends as a polynomial; it does not license canceling u or D on their zero strata. The finite Fourier equation has the stationary relation z(-J)^epsilon lambda=1. With z=exp(-2pi i chi), equations(13)--(15) give precisely R0(-J)^epsilon=exp(2pi i chi)=M_aux^-2. (16) This is the marked meridian relation of the original threading word, including its half-twist shear and inverse eigenratio, rather than a new normalization of the trace curve. The magnetic and total momenta agree as well. For one original H Newton summand, let its two raw heads be X,Y with XY=T and internal root Z. Differentiating the two literal Newton products, at their stationary root, gives the exponentiated logarithmic forces p1=Z(X-1)/(X-Z), p2=JZ(Y-1)/(YZ-J). For example the first product contributes integral_0^kappa Log(X-exp(2pi i t))dt; exponentiating 2pi i times its logarithmic X derivative gives p1. The second product and its literal Y^k factor give p2. The retained white monomial q^(d i) contributes the additional minus sign in the fixed-total first-head momentum. Thus -p1/p2=(1-X)(TZ-XJ)/[J(X-Z)(T-X)], (16a) which is exactly the old magnetic Y(X,Z), with no Hermitian reversal. For the full circle, the original residual sine product contributes -(T-J)/(TJ-1) to the total-degree force; the monomial q^[d(R+S-sigma)] T^-a contributes -J^-1. Consequently e^(Theta_tau)=J^-1 (T-J)/(TJ-1) p2(U,Z)p2(V,W) =JZW(T-J)(T-U)(T-V)/[(TJ-1)(TZ-UJ)(TW-VJ)]. (16b) Here each p2 uses its own second head T/U or T/V. These are the literal normalization factors from the source circle formula, not functions adjusted to fit the character equation. Equations(13), (16a),(16b) recover all three derivatives used by the original ordered-character theorem. Its typed incoming/output construction therefore preserves the entire ordered product P=BA and transports the two punctures by the same centralizer. The integer logarithmic marks are still required before turning these exponential equations into additive stationary equations. ## 5. Branch calibration and what has not been eliminated For positive regular face radii and mu=1/2-delta with small delta>0, the actual positive continuants select e_out=E_c(delta), e_in=E_b(delta), as in the fixed-real fold theorem. Equation(13) then selects the positive product branch. Put C=pi[sqrt(bA+xy)+sqrt(cA+xy)]/A. At delta=0, R0=1, J=-1, and (1/2) dR0/dJ=C/(2pi i). The derivative follows from dJ/ddelta=2pi i and d Log R0/ddelta=2C. In the original ordered map this is exactly the additive parabolic conjugator coefficient: the matrix transport is `I+[C/(2pi i)](P+I)`, not the identity merely because R0=1. With the retained half twist, its primitive cusp ratio is tau=1/[C/(2pi i)-epsilon/2]=2pi i/(C-pi i epsilon), agreeing with the independently marked rectangle calculation. Equations(10)--(16) hold first on the stated regular character chart. Their cleared polynomial relations have zero-face limits, but taking such limits can lose flag or branch information. The original source and the large-H adapters, rather than an arbitrary quartic root, specify those limits. In particular no new geometric branch is inferred merely from the quartic at u=0. In a prospective coefficient saddle, a face shift n->n-nu has multiplier L^nu, with L_f=exp(-partial_(n_f/N) action). The actual shared-face incidence in (8) is therefore retained. The Cauchy stationary equations for the original coefficient use its literal target n*, not independent triangle radii. Under the primitive face/head change of variables they are the original magnetic conservation/gluing equations wherever the full local character chart is regular. This last comparison is a stationary-equation identification, not a theorem that a solution is selected by the finite period. At the two marked zero faces one must retain the actual boundary limit and co-source. The equations do not eliminate the neighboring coefficient indices, prove a scalar A-polynomial for an arbitrary network, or identify every component of their characteristic variety with a geometric component. Nor do they prove a fixed complex external-color packet, its nonzero saddle coefficient, or the needed bounds for the nonempty small-color subsets. Their exact finite source solution, primitive normalization and local ordered-character interface are what is established here. Focused [exact source audit](../experiments/audit_actual_whole_source_coupled_face_difference_system.py), with [saved results](../experiments/actual_whole_source_coupled_face_difference_system_results.json): PASS. It constructs 50 literal homogenized Newton polynomials and checks 300 canceled source components, 360 polynomial recurrence rows, 15 exact core Fourier pairings, 192 coupled rows with 27,254 shared-face coefficient equalities, and 12 marked tetrahedral-graph coefficient extractions. Seven symbolic certificates check the polynomial gauge and original ordered magnetic/total/channel character maps. The independently developed fold block uses 336 original Newton values, 48 source jumps, 2,208 system rows and 48 full finite-system rank checks through N=18 and both parities. The rank counts concern the explicitly localized operator field; finite fixtures do not assert a geometric certificate or an asymptotic theorem. Independent root review of the full proof and audit source: PASS. Its fresh redirected replay reproduced all recorded symbolic, polynomial, shared-face coefficient and fold-selection checks. The review includes the original incoming-b/output-c convention and the full magnetic, total and channel character identities; it does not extend those regular-chart identities to a reconstructed marked zero-face representation. Independent source/transport review: PASS for the polynomial gauge, exact whole-source coefficient system, source-selected fold jump, and final ordered magnetic/total momentum comparison. The three-dimensional even operator freedom and its elimination by the literal source adapter were also checked independently. The original finite system, source polynomial and audit are frozen; the geometric boundary and period qualifications in section 5 remain part of the result.

title: Polynomial actual boundary Gram costs on the entire supported color domain
text: # Polynomial actual boundary Gram costs on the entire supported color domain 29 October 2026. The correlated six-head marked boundary Gram has POLYNOMIAL source cost on EVERY supported folded color cell, at both level parities. No fixed central corridor is required. The second-root- zero Racah terms do not need a uniform strict exponential gap: a global elementary sine-product inequality bounds every such term by the same action as a positive main term. All low/high partner branches, the original marked normal and every lower moment are retained. This controls the pointed algebraic Gram from the [actual six-pants boundary](actual_six_pants_boundary_torsor_and_sewing.md). It does not identify its constructed reflection with a physical mirror, bound the physical change of frame or general recouplings, or prove a graph's sharp geometric energy/noncancellation. ## 1. The whole-support theorem Let N>=2, d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), q=exp(pi i/N), and take ANY 0<=l_1,l_2,l_3<=M, l_1+l_2+l_3>=d. (1) There is one paired axis for each 2l_i<d; let their number be r<=3. The actual regular source cell, complete-circle coordinates eta_i, original marked co-source lambda and nested-cup vector v_l are those of the proved boundary theorem. In particular m_I=lambda(eta_I v_l), tau_l=m_all=Z_N(l)/N^(3-r)>0, q_l(eta)=sum_I (m_(I^c)/tau_l)eta_I, q_l(0)=1, K_l=sum_I |coeff_I(q_l^(1/2))|^2. (2) There are absolute constants C,C0, independent of N and of ALL labels satisfying (1), such that max_I |m_I/tau_l|<=C0 N^C, 1<=K_l<=C0 N^C. (3) The exponent may be increased between the two estimates. Thus the actual source and dual costs of this prescribed Gram are exactly K_l and tau_l^2 K_l, with log K_l=O(log N)=o(N) uniformly on the whole support. The estimates include saturation faces, edges, corners, nearest paired neighbors and odd simple axes. Unsupported open source cells are not deleted. They lack the positive top moment in (2), so (3) is asserted precisely on (1). The theorem does not assert a polynomial norm for the embedding of this finite coordinate cell into the physical tensor product. ## 2. The original generic trace and all its normal factors The [proved generic source identity](actual_generic_trivalent_racah_source_identity.md) and the genuine ordered physical trace give, for each unfolded ordinary triangle j=(a,b,c), the EXACT rational function T_j=(-1)^d product_i[2j_i+1] *[r_1]![r_2]![r_3]!/[J+1]! *product_i([j_i]!^2[d-j_i]!/[N+j_i]!) S_j^2, J=a+b+c, r_i=J-2j_i, S_j=sum_t (-1)^(d+t)[N+t]! /{[d+t-J]! product_i[t-j_i]![J-j_i-t]!}, max(j_i,J-d)<=t<=J-max(j_i). (4) Here [n] and [n]! are symmetric quantum integers and factorials at zeta=q(1-Z)^(1/(2N)), with the branch through q. These are the actual source functions, not a separately normalized 6j model. The unfolded choices are j_i=l_i or d-l_i on a paired axis, and the single l_i on a simple axis. With the original paired-circle unit ell_j(Z)=L_N(c_j(zeta))/Z, the physical moment formula is m_I=(-1)^d(q-q^(-1)) [Z^(r+1-|I|)] sum_unfolded Z^r T_j product_(i in I)ell_(j_i)(Z). (5) There are at most eight summands and the coefficient order is <=4. The original marked physical trace is exactly the one in (5). No ordinary quantum dimension is specialized to zero before this coefficient is extracted. Two elementary integer facts now hold on the ENTIRE supported domain. For every unfolded branch, d<=J<=2d, 0<=r_i<=d. (6) To verify them, increase a coordinate from l_i to d-l_i. The maximum J is 3d-sum l_i<=2d and the minimum is sum l_i>=d. For r_i, its maximum over the flips is 2d-sum l_i<=d and its minimum is sum l_i-2l_i>=d-2l_i>=0. In particular every unfolded branch is an ordinary triangle. Moreover EVERY one of the seven denominator factorial indices in S_j is less than N, for every true term. Indeed 0<=d+t-J<=d-max j_i<=d, 0<=t-j_i<=some other label<=d, 0<=J-j_i-t<=some other label<=d. (7) For example t<=j_i+j_k bounds t-j_i, and t>=j_k bounds J-j_i-t. No root denominator appears in any Racah summand. Its numerator contains [N] once for t<N and both [N],[2N] for t>=N; t<=2d<2N excludes a third zero. This is the only termwise change at the second band. ## 3. A uniform global profile, including the second-zero band Let L(t)=integral_0^t log|2sin(pi u)|du, extended periodically to R. Its period is 1 and L(-t)=-L(t). Define the EXACT half-step scaled colors a_i=(j_i+1/2)/N, S=sum a_i, x_i=S/2-a_i (i=1,2,3), x_4=1-S/2. Equations (6) imply 0<x_i<1/2 for all four i, sum_i x_i=1. (8) The half-step is useful: a high-partner replacement j_i->d-j_i is exactly a_i->1-a_i. It permutes the four x coordinates while replacing each by its complement 1/2-x. There is no O(1/N) error in this assertion. For instance flipping the first color sends (x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4) ->(1/2-x_4,1/2-x_3,1/2-x_2,1/2-x_1). (9) For a summand put s=(t+3/4)/N and v=s-S/2=(t-J/2)/N. Its three child pairs obey x_i+v=(t-j_i+1/4)/N>0, x_i-v=(J-j_i-t+1/4)/N>0, i<=3. (10) Also x_4+v=1-(J-t+3/4)/N is in (0,1). The fourth minus argument is x_4-v=1-s=(N-t-3/4)/N: it is positive for t<N and negative for t>=N, precisely the second-zero band. After removing its one or two root zeros, the absolute factorial summand has, up to polynomial factors, the profile H_x(v)=-sum_(i=1)^4 [L(x_i+v)+L(x_i-v)]. (11) For t<N the numerator is s_t; for t>=N it is s_(t-N), apart from the complete root-orbit polynomial factors. Both have rate N L(s) up to O(log N), because L has period 1. The denominator d+t-J has rate L(1+s-S)=-L(S-s). Substitution of (10) then gives (11). This same argument covers endpoints: changing an argument by O(1/N) changes N L by O(log N), uniformly even at a zero of sine. One may prove this modulus of continuity by integrating |log u| over an interval of length O(1/N) near the nearest integer. The decisive inequality is H_x(v)<=H_x(0)=Phi(x):=-2sum_i L(x_i) (12) for EVERY actual term, including the second-zero band. Here is a direct elementary proof. The function is even in v, and (10) gives |v|<min(x_1,x_2,x_3). For v>0 away from its logarithmic corner, put alpha_i=pi x_i and theta=pi v. Then H_x'(v)=log |P_minus/P_plus|, P_plus=product_i sin(alpha_i+theta)>0, P_minus=product_i sin(alpha_i-theta). (13) If theta<alpha_4, every factor is positive and sin(alpha_i+theta)-sin(alpha_i-theta) =2cos(alpha_i)sin(theta)>0. Thus |P_minus|<P_plus. If theta>alpha_4, exactly the fourth minus factor is negative. Expand the sum of the two products: P_plus+P_minus =2 sum_(A subset {1,2,3,4}, |A| even) cos(theta)^(4-|A|)sin(theta)^|A| product_(i in A)cos(alpha_i) product_(i notin A)sin(alpha_i)>0. (14) Every factor is nonnegative, and an interior term is strictly positive by (8). Since P_minus<0, (14) again says |P_minus|<P_plus. Continuity across theta=alpha_4, where (13) tends to minus infinity, proves (12). Evenness treats negative v. No local concavity or uniform strict exponential tail gap was used. The integer nearest t=J/2 is a true term of the FIRST band: (6) gives max(j_i,J-d)<=floor(J/2) and ceil(J/2)<=min(J-max j_i,d). At that term |v|<=1/(2N), so the same uniform modulus of continuity gives H_x(v)=Phi(x)+O(log N/N). ## 4. Positive main value and polynomial normal envelopes For t<N, the exact root identity is ([N+t]!/[N])|_q=(-1)^t[d]![t]!. All denominators in (4) are positive symmetric factorials at q. Thus S_main/[N] has ONE common phase (-1)^d. Its positive absolute sum is Rcore_N(j)=N sum_(true t<N) s_t/{s_(d+t-J) product_i s_(t-j_i)s_(J-j_i-t)}. It has at most N terms and contains the midpoint term identified above. The uniform two-sided sine-factorial estimate and (12) therefore give, throughout the whole support and every branch, N^(-C)e^(N Phi(x))<=Rcore_N(j) <=N^C e^(N Phi(x)). (15) The estimate uses only ONE midpoint summand for its lower bound; no bulk Hessian, saddle width or distance from a saturation face is assumed. Second-band terms, after removing [N][2N], obey the same upper bound by (12). They may approach the leading action at boundary scales, which is why a uniform strict gap is unnecessary. Use the common disk |Z|<=c/N^2. A quantum-factorial ratio with a fixed number of factors and indices <=3N has, after explicitly removing its zeros, a polynomial envelope relative to its nonzero root product on this disk. This follows either from the proved [bounded normal factorial estimate](bounded_normal_quantum_factorial_envelope.md) or directly: a nonzero 1-q^(2k) has magnitude >=c0/N; its change is O(|Z|), and O(N) such factors accumulate only bounded relative growth here. Removed [N] and [2N] factors and the symmetric-int normalization cost fixed powers of N. Their count is uniformly bounded. Equations (7),(12),(15) hence bound the ENTIRE holomorphic S_j/Z by poly(N)e^(N Phi(x)). Cauchy estimates for four fixed normal orders add only another fixed power of N. No alternating-sum cancellation is needed for the second-zero terms. To include the complete prefactor of (4), note first that ([N] [j]!^2[d-j]!/[N+j]!)|_q=(-1)^j. (16) Its zero-removed envelope is polynomial, with no factorial action. All three r_i are <N, while N<=J+1<2N. The zero-removed triangle factor therefore has rate P(x)=sum_(i=1)^3 L(2x_i)-L(S-1), up to O(log N). Each simple axis contributes one dimension zero [2j+1]=[N]; the other dimensions and all ell_j in (5) have polynomial fixed jets, uniformly to the nearest paired neighbor. If s0=3-r is the number of simple axes, the prefactor without S^2 has zero order s0-4. Multiplication by Z^r and S^2, whose order is at least two, leaves order at least ONE. Consequently Z^r T_j product ell is holomorphic on the common disk; it is never estimated as a bare singular expression. The preceding bounds give for its fixed jets |[Z^k]{Z^r T_j product ell}|<=N^C exp(N E(x)), k<=4, E(x)=P(x)+2Phi(x) =sum_(i=1)^4[L(2x_i)-4L(x_i)] =-2sum_(i=1)^4[L(x_i)+L(1/2-x_i)]. (17) The second equality uses L(S-1)=-L(2x_4), and the third is the elementary duplication identity for L. This expression is unchanged by every permutation or individual complement x_i->1/2-x_i. Equation (9) therefore makes E EXACTLY the same function for all unfolded branches of a fixed folded triple, with these half-step coordinates. Finally the PROVED actual positive top moment has the exact weight Z_N(l)=N^2 product_i k_(l_i) s_(J_l-2l_1)s_(J_l-2l_2)s_(J_l-2l_3) /s_(J_l-d) *R_N(l)^2. The same midpoint argument (15), uniform factorial bounds and its positive prefactor give N^(-C)exp(N E_fold)<=tau_l<=N^C exp(N E_fold) (18) on the ENTIRE supported domain. Endpoint factors s_0=1 cause no problem, and replacing their scaled arguments by the half-step ones changes logarithms by only O(log N). Combine (5),(17),(18), sum at most eight branches, and absorb the polynomial |q-q^-1|: this proves the first estimate in (3). The finite square root of q_l=1+n_l is sum_(k=0)^r binom(1/2,k)n_l^k, with n_l^(r+1)=0. It is a polynomial of degree <=3 in at most seven normalized moments. Thus the first estimate implies the second, with constants independent of the labels and N. Its constant coefficient is one, so K_l>=1. This completes the whole-support actual Gram theorem. ## 5. Scope and verification The new ingredient beyond the central-corridor bound is the global sine-product inequality (12)--(14), together with the half-step folding coordinates. A second-zero action gap may vanish at boundary scales; uniform positive factorial comparison replaces it. The result controls the correlated marked Gram on its actual regular source cells. It supplies neither a physical mirror interpretation of that Gram nor a bound for genuine transitions between different pair decompositions. Those remain separate global source/geometry tasks; polynomial K alone has no hidden cuboctahedral volume term. The [multiprecision source diagnostic](../experiments/diagnose_actual_whole_support_boundary_conditioning.py) uses the proved generic trace (4), every partner and the original physical circle normal. It compares two precisions and two normal steps on saturation faces/corners and interior examples. These are diagnostics; the uniform theorem follows from the finite generic source identity, (12), common-disk factorial envelopes and the positive midpoint bound, not sampling. The [focused audit](../experiments/audit_actual_whole_support_boundary_gram_envelope.py) and [recorded results](../experiments/actual_whole_support_boundary_gram_envelope_results.json) verify the universal even-product polynomial with an identically zero cleared numerator; 46,495 unfolded integer branches and 257,107 true Racah terms at N=2,...,32; 215 independent generic physical-double-sum versus Racah traces; and five all-moment original marked crosschecks. Floating-point action comparisons in that audit are labeled diagnostics; the proof of (12) is the exact sign argument (13),(14). The separate [paired-precision data](../experiments/actual_whole_support_boundary_conditioning_diagnostic_results.json) include ten boundary/interior cases through N=256, both parities, simple axes and saturation corners. The largest displayed K is below 2.78; this finite observation is not used to choose the polynomial exponent or prove its uniformity. Independent internal analytical review: the Euler-atom agent re-derived the entire support/half-step/range argument, both bands of (12), first- band midpoint, common-disk fixed jets, full prefactor zero count and the actual positive tau lower bound, and reported PASS. This is an internal proof check, not external peer review or a global source volume theorem. The primary agent independently checked the half-step domains, exact partner transformation, midpoint admissibility, both signs of the global sine-product inequality, root-zero accounting and the uniform fixed-jet argument, then freshly replayed the focused audit: PASS.

title: The original whole word as a marked cyclic-dilogarithm resolvent period
text: # The original whole word as a marked cyclic-dilogarithm resolvent period 28 October 2026. Every actual signed braid word admits an exact period on a product of the literature cyclic-dilogarithm curves. The marked cycle and its full original cap are specified, and the finite-head walls are retained inside rational resolvents. There is no restriction on a geometric atom argument, or asymptotic replacement of a finite polynomial by a chosen phase. The cyclic dilogarithm and its nilpotent anchoring were already proved in [the unfolded Ward calculation](unfolded_ward_factorial_and_regulator.md) and [the Rees crossing calculation](rees_whole_crossing_source_factorization.md). The [full-atom note](full_euler_atom_dilog_and_endpoint_regions.md) also gives their exact scalar Taylor Cauchy formula. The new content here is their contraction into the ORIGINAL strict signed word with the specified source and an explicit product cycle. This constructs a global algebraic period representation; it does not prove a geometric intersection number or a volume estimate. ## 1. The marked curve realizes the literal nilpotent operators Put `Q=exp(2pi*i/N)` and let C_N be the normalization of y^N=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^j t)^j. (1) At t=0 choose the sheet y=1. On its disk `|t|<1` this specifies the analytic function D_N(t)=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^j t)^(j/N). All powers have their common constant-one mark, rather than independent roots chosen after specialization. Weighted root summation gives for `1<=a<N` [t^a]log D_N=1/[a(1-Q^a)]. (2) Consequently the first N Taylor coefficients of D_N and its inverse are precisely those of the literal u_N and v_N. For ANY actual nilpotent matrix T with `T^N=0`, and any `0<r<1`, u_N(T)= (1/(2pi*i)) integral_(gamma_0) y(t)(tI-T)^-1 dt, v_N(T)= (1/(2pi*i)) integral_(gamma_0) y(t)^-1(tI-T)^-1 dt. (3) Here gamma_0 is the positively oriented circle `|t|=r` lifted to that sheet of C_N. It is closed. Expand the exact resolvent (tI-T)^-1=sum_(a=0)^(N-1)T^a t^(-a-1). (4) Termwise Cauchy evaluation and (2) prove (3). Thus this is exact holomorphic functional calculus on the actual finite head. It does not claim that the scalar evaluations u_N(z) and D_N(z) agree away from a nilpotent argument. ## 2. The full original rational source kernel Use the strict factorization in [the original Euler/Gaussian network](actual_euler_gaussian_cauchy_network.md): C=F_2 U_- F_1 F_2^-1, C^-1=F_2 F_1^-1 V_- F_2^-1, R_+=kappa C D U_+ C^-1, R_-=kappa^-1 C V_+ D^-1 C^-1, where `U_±=u_N(T_±)`, `V_±=v_N(T_±)`, `T_-=x^-1 S_1^-S_2^+`, `T_+=x^-1 S_1^+S_2^-`. Every T has Nth power zero. Spectator heads are extended by identity. Every crossing has exactly three such Euler atoms; its factorial and Gaussian factors remain the specified matrices. Let beta have b heads and m signed crossings, and let `A_L ... A_1`, `L=10m`, be its literal stripped matrix word in the correct order. Mark its `r=3m` Euler slots by `j=1,...,r`. At slot j set `sigma_j=+1` for u and `-1` for v and replace its factor by the rational matrix mathscr R_j(t_j)=(t_j I-T_j)^-1. (5) All other factors retain their actual values. Write B_l for the resulting factors. Let the ORIGINAL averaged first-cut functional be Phi_(b,N)(W)=(1/N) sum_(a,c,k_2,...,k_b) (product_(i=2)^b g_(k_i)) W_((c,k_2,...,k_b),(a,k_2,...,k_b)), g_k=(xQ^-k)^(1-N). (6) One may instead keep the original fixed-first-input-zero source by fixing a=0 and removing 1/N. The equality of their original uninserted knot closures is the prior scalar-closure theorem; no equality for arbitrary inserted resolvents is assumed here. Choose one of these original sources and keep it throughout. Define the rational scalar R_(beta,N)(t_1,...,t_r)=Phi_(b,N)(B_L ... B_1). (7) This is an entirely explicit rational function with poles only at the coordinate loci `t_j=0`; its Laurent powers in each variable run from -1 through -N. It retains every finite-head projector because each T_j is the literal truncated transfer. It also retains all pivotal closures and the first-cut coupon. There is no quotient that kills the degree-zero wall terms. If chi is the ORIGINAL external dimension, framing and common Cartan factor, included exactly once, then the original scalar is P_(beta,N)(M)=chi_(beta,N)(M)/(2pi*i)^r integral_(gamma_0^r) R_(beta,N)(t) product_(j=1)^r y_j^(sigma_j) dt_j. (8) The proof applies (3) to each slot, in its original order, and then the finite linear functional (6). No Fubini convergence issue arises on the compact small circles: the matrices have finite dimension and the curves are regular there. Equation (8) holds for the full root meridian family, with the same external factors as the actual invariant. It is not an assertion about generic-q normal derivatives. Thus the desired first step of the torsor route is concrete: the algebraic curve, the meromorphic differential, and the original marked cycle are all supplied. The number r of curve factors depends on the braid word, not on N. The curve and source rational function themselves do depend on N. There is also a FULL version with no factorial constants hidden in the rational source. The exact reflection identity is F_a=N Q^(-a-1) [t^(N-1-a)]D_N(t)^-1. Consequently replace each factorial diagonal on its head by F^-1=(1/(2pi*i)) integral_(gamma_0) y diag_(a)(t^(-a-1)) dt, F=(1/(2pi*i)) integral_(gamma_0) y^-1 diag_(a)(N Q^(-a-1)t^(a-N)) dt. (9) Every crossing has six such factorial diagonals and three transfer Euler atoms. Apply (9) to all six. Formula (8) now holds on `C_N^(9m)` with a new rational source formed by the same ordered matrix contraction; its only remaining local constants are the specified Gaussian diagonals and explicit powers of N,Q,x. Their marked Gaussian phase and all external Cartan, dimension and framing factors are retained. All actual factorial growth is inside the cyclic-dilogarithm differential. Both the minimal `3m` and full `9m` representations are exact. ## 3. An all-inverse realization with no growing infinity factors An exact change of auxiliary completion makes the cut-cycle problem simpler. Write `v_(Q^-1)` for the SAME finite factorial formula with Q replaced by its inverse. Directly, (Q^-1;Q^-1)_a=(-1)^a Q^(-a(a+1)/2)F_a, [t^a]v_(Q^-1)(t)=Q^a/F_a, u_Q(T)=v_(Q^-1)(Q^-1 T). (10) These are identities of the actual finite polynomials and operators, not conjugations of the physical invariant. Define C_(N,epsilon) by (1) with `Q^j` replaced by `Q^(epsilon*j)`; its y=1 sheet at zero is the corresponding cyclic dilogarithm. Equation (10) replaces each u resolvent in (8) EXACTLY by (1/(2pi*i)) integral_(gamma_0 on C_(N,-1)) y^-1(tI-Q^-1 T)^-1 dt. (11) For the full factorial version replace F^-1 by (1/(2pi*i)) integral_(gamma_0 on C_(N,-1)) y^-1 diag_(a)(Q^-a t^(-a-1)) dt, (12) while F still uses the inverse-y formula in (9) on C_(N,+1). The v transfers likewise keep their original inverse-y curve. Thus the full original word is an exact period on a product of `9m` oriented curves C_(N,epsilon), with EVERY algebraic factor equal to y^-1. All physical Gaussian, pivotal, Cartan, framing and dimension factors are unchanged. The rational source is formed by the same original ordered contraction. This auxiliary completion changes the analytic function beyond its first N Taylor coefficients. It does not discard the infinity contribution of the old positive-y representation; it supplies a different exact period for the same finite operator. No generic-q continuation follows from it. For every variable in this all-inverse realization, the rational matrix kernel is `O(t^-1)` at infinity. Also |y^-1|=O(|t|^(-(N-1)/2)). (13) Every outer cut arc therefore has integral tending to zero in absolute value, for every fixed N>=2. At a root `t=Q^(-epsilon*j)` the exponent of y^-1 is `-j/N>-1`, so each cut endpoint is integrable. Consequently all variables admit convergent radial cut deformations without an infinity regularization. The banks and monodromy of these cuts must be kept on the chosen sheet. For even N a large base circle need not close on a single sheet; (13) applies to its cut arcs, not to an unmarked closed lift asserted without proof. On the normalization the finite branch endpoints do not in fact produce poles of the differential. If `g=gcd(N,j)`, a uniformizer has `t-alpha=s^(N/g)` and `y=unit*s^(j/g)`. Hence `y^-1 dt` has nonnegative order `(N-j)/g-1`. The rational matrix kernel is regular at alpha. The cut deformation is genuine sheet and homology transport, not a sum of residues at those branch points. The [explicit Hankel cycle theorem](actual_cyclic_dilog_hankel_cycle.md) computes these banks and their exact nonzero sine weights, and carries them through the entire original ordered source. ## 4. The full original source is polynomially bounded on these cuts At `|M|=1` one has `|x|=1`. Equip the actual head basis with its ordinary Euclidean norm. Each truncated transfer and its Q^-1 multiple have operator norm at most one. Therefore on the ENTIRE exterior `|t|>=1`, including its endpoint circle, ||(tI-T)^-1|| <= sum_(a=0)^(N-1)|t|^(-a-1) <= N/|t|. (14) The full all-inverse factorial kernels obey ||diag_(a)(Q^-a t^(-a-1))||<=1/|t|, ||diag_(a)(NQ^(-a-1)t^(a-N))||<=N/|t|. (15) Every Gaussian diagonal is unitary here. The averaged original cut in (6) is `Tr[(E tensor G^(tensor(b-1)))W]`, where `E=J/N` is the rank-one orthogonal projection onto the constant head vector and G is the unitary pivotal diagonal. Its trace norm is exactly `N^(b-1)`. Thus `|Phi(W)|<=N^(b-1)||W||`. Each crossing contains three transfer resolvents, three direct factorial kernels and three inverse-factorial kernels. Taking the norm of their ORIGINAL ordered product proves the uniform bound for the full all-inverse rational source |R_(beta,N)(t)| <= N^(b-1+6m) product_(j=1)^(9m)|t_j|^-1, whenever all |t_j|>=1 and |M|=1. (16) For the retained fixed-first-input-zero source, its first coupon has trace norm sqrt(N); the right side acquires only that additional factor. No actual source is replaced to obtain a bound. A fixed total number k of logarithmic t-derivatives costs at most a constant depending on k,m times an additional factor `N^k`, by differentiating the finite resolvents and diagonal monomials. Thus the whole rational source has no hidden exponential growth on the canonical exterior cut chain. This global upper-amplitude control is unconditional for the specified root source. It supplies neither a lower bound nor a nonzero geometric coefficient. A complex rational source bounded by a polynomial may still carry rapidly varying phase or vanish on the relevant critical image. Those remain part of the cycle-selection and lower-bound question. ## 5. What a global cut deformation must retain Unlike the finite scalar Euler polynomials, the y factors in (8) have genuine branch divisors at `t=Q^-j`. This puts a possible cut deformation on an actual marked algebraic cover. The resolvent expression avoids replacing a finite projector by a spurious reproducing pole. Any subsequent deformation must still be an equality of marked cycles on this cover, with its infinity and branch-boundary terms retained. For example the leading magnitude of `y` at infinity is `|t|^((N-1)/2)`; its inverse decays by that order. Formula (4) therefore gives automatically decaying infinity behavior for each v-variable coefficient. For a positive-y u-variable coefficient of T^a, the absolute-decay argument applies when `a>(N-1)/2`; it gives no automatic vanishing below that threshold. Lower powers may need a boundary or Taylor regularization. Whether the original source cancels their coefficients is an explicit question about (7), not a freedom to discard them. Nonzero examples occur in the actual figure-eight word in the audit. The all-inverse realization above avoids that particular regularization problem by an exact change of auxiliary curve. The marked small circle in (8) is now a definite cycle whose branch-cut or relative-chain image can be computed. It has not been proved to project with degree one to a positive Rivin angle domain, nor to have nonzero geometric thimble coefficient. Equation (8) avoids assuming that coefficient; it is a suitable starting point for proving or disproving the needed cycle map. The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_whole_word_cyclic_dilog_resolvent.py) checks the Taylor identification from the fractional product, each original signed crossing, whole signed words with their original cap, and the retained low-power u-source terms.

title: Independent proof of additive full-cyclotomic descent
text: # Independent proof of additive full-cyclotomic descent Research audit and proof, 27 October 2026. The additive analogue of the full rank-one theorem is valid with the weighted exponential--Puiseux uniqueness lemma. The pole-order induction needs the whole orbit function, not just its highest principal coefficient. The proof below makes that cancellation explicit. This concerns additive comparison torsors with trivial homogeneous action. It does not by itself solve a residual twisted by a nontrivial geometric companion matrix, or construct the selected knot comparison. The volume conjecture remains unproved. ## 1. Statement and full-root propagation Let c(Q,Y) belong to ℚ(Q,Y), sigma(Y)=QY. Suppose that for every sufficiently large N, sum_(j=0)^(N-1)c(zeta_N,zeta_N^jY)=0 (1.1) as a rational identity in Y. Then there is b in ℚ(Q,Y) such that c(Q,Y)=b(Q,QY)-b(Q,Y). (1.2) For coefficients in a field K contained in C the same conclusion over K(Q,Y) holds if the hypothesis is supplied at every primitive root for the fixed coefficient embedding. The rational coefficient case obtains these conjugate identities by Galois action. An appropriate sufficient condition over a number field is the full coefficient-conjugate marking of the multiplicative theorem. For fixed k, xi_N=exp(2pi*i*k/N) has order m=N/gcd(k,N). Its true m-step sum is zero for all sufficiently large N; the N-step sum repeats it gcd(k,N) times. Thus these scaled roots are available without a coprimality restriction on k,N. ## 2. Exact pole-cluster cancellation Over a finite algebraic splitting field write the unique partial fraction expansion c(Q,Y)=sum_l c_l(Q)Y^l +sum_(mu,r) a_(mu,r)(Q)/(1-mu(Q)Y)^r, (2.1) with finitely many Laurent monomials, distinct nonzero algebraic mu, and positive pole orders r. The Laurent coefficients belong to the original rational field. Choose the common algebraic coefficient field large enough for all partial fractions. At a primitive m-th root, the universal orbit function is Psi_(m,r)(u)=sum_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-zeta_m^j z)^(-r), u=z^m, Psi_(m,r)(u)=m sum_(l>=0) binom(ml+r-1,r-1)u^l. (2.2) This follows from expansion at z=0 and root orthogonality. The binomial is a polynomial in l of degree r-1. Hence Psi is rational and has an order-r pole at u=1 with highest coefficient Psi_(m,r)(u)=m^r/(1-u)^r +lower pole orders. (2.3) For example this coefficient follows inductively from Psi_(m,r+1)=Psi_(m,r)+(m*u/r) partial_u Psi_(m,r). Equivalently use the leading coefficient m^(r-1)/(r-1)! of the binomial polynomial in (2.2) and the order-r pole of sum l^(r-1)u^l. Fix a root specialization outside the finite bad set and a cluster of poles for which mu(Q)^m has the same value lambda. Let R be the largest pole order still present. At U=Y^m=1/lambda, the order-R coefficient of the averaged rational function is m^R sum_(mu^m=lambda) a_(mu,R)(Q). It must vanish. Crucially, the entire contribution of that order is the same universal function Psi_(m,R)(lambda U) multiplied by this sum. It therefore vanishes identically, including all its lower pole orders. One may now descend to R-1. Induction proves sum_(mu^m=lambda) a_(mu,r)(Q)=0 for every r,lambda. (2.4) This avoids mixing an order-R lower principal part with a genuine order-(R-1) coefficient. Moving poles and their partial-fraction weights are algebraic, so accidental collisions or poles of the weights exclude only finitely many sufficiently near Q=1 roots, unless the algebraic branches are identical and were already combined. For large m all nonconstant Laurent monomials average to zero. The pole terms tend to zero at infinity. Comparing the remaining constant there gives m c_0(Q)=0. Infinitely many root values therefore give c_0(Q)=0 identically. ## 3. Weighted scaled moments detect the generic Q-orbits At xi_N, use (2.4) at its true order m, then raise mu^m to the gcd(k,N)-th power. For every fixed r this gives sum_mu a_(mu,r)(xi_N) mu(xi_N)^N=0. (3.1) Choose the common ramification and Puiseux forms of [the full multiplicative proof](full_rank_one_cyclotomic_descent.md): mu(exp(2pi*i*t))=a t^nu exp(lambda_mu(t^(1/e))), A_mu(t)=exp(lambda_mu(t^(1/e))/t). The algebraic weights a_(mu,r)(exp(2pi*i*t)) are meromorphic in t^(1/e). They are precisely allowed by the weighted uniqueness lemma. At each fixed scaled root k that lemma separates the groups (nu,a), giving, after rescaling the argument, sum_(mu in (nu,a)) a_(mu,r)(Q(t)) A_mu(t)^k=0. (3.2) The weights are not raised to the k-th power. Within one group, partition the mu by identical functions A_mu. Let the distinct nonzero functions be A_1,...,A_h and let W_l(t) be the sum of their weights. For k=1,...,h, equation (3.2) is sum_l W_l(t) A_l(t)^k=0. This matrix is a Vandermonde matrix times a diagonal matrix of the nonzero A_l, and is invertible over the common function field on the ramified punctured disk. Hence every W_l=0 identically. For branches with the same (nu,a), equality A_mu=A_eta is equivalent to mu(Q)/eta(Q)=Q^j for an integer j. (3.3) One direction is immediate. For the other, their logarithmic difference divided by t has exponential one and therefore is a constant 2pi*i j, exactly as in the multiplicative proof. Thus the identical-A classes are the generic Q-shift orbits of the pole parameters. We have proved zero total weight in each such orbit, separately for every pole order r. ## 4. A finite additive flow constructs the rational primitive On an orbit mu=Q^u eta write the order-r weights as a_u(Q). Their total is zero. Define the finite cumulative flow e_u=-sum_(v<=u) a_v, b_(eta,r)=sum_u e_u/(1-Q^u eta Y)^r. (4.1) Then sigma b_(eta,r)-b_(eta,r) is the required pole contribution, because the coefficient at index u is e_(u-1)-e_u=a_u. For a nonzero Laurent exponent l, use the primitive c_l(Q)Y^l/(Q^l-1). (4.2) The constant Laurent coefficient has already been shown to vanish. The sum of (4.1)--(4.2) solves (1.2) over the splitting field. The pole flow is the unique finite-support flow on its infinite Q-orbit. Since c is rational over ℚ(Q), Galois permutations preserve the resulting whole pole part. The Laurent part is already rational. Choosing the free constant in that Laurent part to be zero therefore gives b in ℚ(Q,Y). The same descent works over K(Q). Any two rational solutions differ by a rational sigma-invariant, hence by a function of Q alone. This is generic rational descent. Pole divisors of b at the ideal meridian remain part of its lattice. A source-compatible marked cut or normal residue cannot be inferred from (1.2) alone. ## 5. The finite nilpotent extension consequence Combining the full multiplicative and additive results gives a direct finite induction for upper-triangular comparison transport. Suppose an upper-triangular rational matrix B(Q,Y) has identity cyclic monodromy at every sufficiently large primitive root. Its diagonal coefficients have norm one, so the multiplicative theorem trivializes them by rational diagonal gauges. The matrix is now unipotent and its root monodromy remains identity. The first superdiagonal of its monodromy is the cyclic sum of that superdiagonal of B. The additive theorem removes it by a rational unipotent gauge. After this removal the second superdiagonal has the same property; continue by distance above the diagonal. Only finitely many steps occur, at most the nilpotence class. This proves rational triviality for the stated upper-triangular comparison object. It does not assert nilpotence of the original braid image, nor triangularity or identity curvature for the unknown actual/geometric comparison. Those inputs must be established. A twisted source residual (sigma-C)b=Delta is not automatically the untwisted problem (1.2). [Exact independent audit](../experiments/audit_additive_cyclotomic_descent.py). [Results](../experiments/additive_cyclotomic_descent_results.json).

title: Cyclotomic descent for rational sources and unipotent torsors
text: # Cyclotomic descent for rational sources and unipotent torsors Research proof, 27 October 2026. This addresses the source extension, rather than only its multiplicative norm line. The proof uses the weighted sequence-uniqueness lemma proved in [full rank-one descent](full_rank_one_cyclotomic_descent.md), and finite flows on rational partial-fraction orbits. No published q-curvature theorem is used as a premise. The result is uniform in the number of source coordinates. It applies to a specified rational unipotent comparison with whole cyclotomic transport identities. Constructing that comparison for the actual knot period, and verifying its source and peripheral lattice, remain necessary. The volume conjecture is not proved by this conditional descent theorem. ## 1. An additive descent theorem Let k be the rational number field, let sigma(Y)=QY on k(Q,Y), and take c in k(Q,Y). Suppose that for every sufficiently large integer N, sum_(j=0)^(N-1) c(zeta_N,zeta_N^j Y)=0, zeta_N=exp(2pi*i/N), (1) as an identity of whole rational functions of Y. Then c(Q,Y)=b(Q,QY)-b(Q,Y) (2) for some b in k(Q,Y). Conversely (2) implies (1) at every level where its rational specializations are defined. There are no hypotheses on the ramification or limiting values of the moving poles at Q=1. The ambiguity in b is precisely k(Q). The theorem does not assert regularity of b at the ideal meridian. The same proof works over a subfield k of C if (1) is given at every primitive root for the chosen coefficient embedding. For rational coefficients this follows from Galois conjugation. For a number field, knowing the chosen principal root alone is not silently treated as knowing all its coefficient conjugates. ## 2. Partial fractions and the charges seen by a root fiber Over a finite algebraic splitting field of k(Q), write uniquely c(Q,Y)=sum_m c_m(Q)Y^m +sum_(mu,r>=1) a_(mu,r)(Q)/(1-mu(Q)Y)^r. (3) The first sum is a finite Laurent polynomial; all mu are nonzero algebraic functions, and the second sum is finite. The partial fraction part is proper at infinity and has no pole at zero. All identities below omit the finitely many root levels at which a coefficient specialization fails or two distinct pole functions coincide. A nonzero algebraic function has only finitely many such specialization zeros on its finite algebraic cover. At a primitive N-th root set U=Y^N and D_U=U partial_U. For r>=1, sum_j (1-mu zeta_N^j Y)^(-r) =N/(r-1)! product_(ell=1)^(r-1)(N D_U+ell) (1-mu^N U)^(-1). (4) For r=1 this is the elementary geometric-series identity, first as a power series and then as a rational identity. Applying the operators (D_Y+ell) proves the general formula. Its pole at U=mu^(-N) has exact order r with nonzero highest coefficient. Terms with the same mu^N in (4) give exactly the same rational function. Compare the highest remaining pole order in (1), then descend in r. At every cluster C of equal values mu(zeta_N)^N, sum_(mu in C) a_(mu,r)(zeta_N)=0 (5) for each r. Laurent polynomials have no finite nonzero poles and do not affect this comparison. In particular, for each r, sum_mu a_(mu,r)(zeta_N) mu(zeta_N)^N=0. (6) For xi_N=exp(2pi*i*k/N), with fixed positive integer k, its actual order is m=N/gcd(k,N). Apply (5) at order m and raise the common m-th powers to the gcd(k,N)-th power. This proves sum_mu a_(mu,r)(xi_N) mu(xi_N)^N=0 (7) for every sufficiently large N. It does not use a primitive N-step formula at a nonprimitive scaled root. ## 3. Generic orbit charges from the weighted rigidity lemma Choose the common convergent Puiseux forms near Q=1 provided by the elementary finite-cover argument in the rank-one note. Put t=Log Q/(2pi*i), and write mu(exp(2pi*i*t))=a_mu t^(nu_mu) exp(lambda_mu(t^(1/e))), A_mu(t)=exp(lambda_mu(t^(1/e))/t), (8) where a_mu!=0, nu_mu is rational, and lambda_mu(0)=0. The coefficients a_(mu,r)(exp(2pi*i*t)) are meromorphic Puiseux germs after the same further finite ramification. At xi_N, (7) becomes a sum of terms N^(-nu_mu N)(a_mu k^(nu_mu))^N a_(mu,r)(exp(2pi*i*k/N)) A_mu(k/N)^k. (9) The weighted exponential--Puiseux uniqueness lemma separates every pair (nu_mu,a_mu). It applies to the partial-fraction weights as well as to the exponentials; those weights need not be units. For each such pair, and every positive integer k, it gives the identity of punctured analytic germs sum_(mu in pair) a_(mu,r)(exp(2pi*i*t)) A_mu(t)^k=0. (10) Here the argument was rescaled from kt to t after applying the lemma. These are identities of functions, not only formal jets. Group equal functions A_mu. If A_1,...,A_h are the distinct nonzero functions in one pair and w_i is the sum of its weights, then (10) for k=1,...,h has coefficient matrix (A_i^k). Its determinant is a nonzero product of the A_i and their pairwise differences in the field of meromorphic functions on the ramified punctured disk. Hence w_i=0 for every i. Within a fixed (nu,a), equality A_mu=A_eta is equivalent to mu(Q)/eta(Q)=Q^v for an integer v. (11) Indeed exp((lambda_mu-lambda_eta)/t)=1 forces the exponent to be a constant in 2pi*i Z on the connected punctured cover. Conversely (11) has this property. Thus the generic additive orbit charges vanish: sum_(mu in each Q-shift orbit) a_(mu,r)(Q)=0 (12) for every pole order r. The rational-function identities follow from the analytic germ identities because these coefficients are algebraic functions of Q. ## 4. A finite flow solves the transport equation On one infinite orbit write mu_v=Q^v mu_0, and set a_v equal to the coefficient in (3), or zero if that pole is absent. The a_v have finite support and sum zero. Define e_v=-sum_(u<=v) a_u. Then e_v has finite support, and b_orbit=sum_v e_v/(1-Q^v mu_0 Y)^r satisfies sigma(b_orbit)-b_orbit=sum_v a_v/(1-Q^v mu_0 Y)^r. The equality follows coefficientwise from e_(v-1)-e_v=a_v. This flow is unique among finite-support flows on that orbit. The total proper partial-fraction solution b_pole descends to k(Q,Y). One way to see this is to apply any splitting-field automorphism tau. The difference tau(b_pole)-b_pole is invariant under Y->QY. A rational invariant has no finite nonzero poles, since their Q-orbits would be infinite; its remaining Laurent polynomial is therefore constant in Y. Both proper parts vanish at infinity, so that constant is zero. Thus b_pole is Galois invariant. Subtract its coboundary from c. The remaining Laurent polynomial still has zero cyclic sum at all sufficiently large roots. Its nonzero powers sum to zero once N exceeds the largest absolute value of their nonzero exponents, so its constant coefficient obeys N c_0(zeta_N)=0 at infinitely many Q-values. Consequently c_0=0. Finally b_Laurent=sum_(m!=0) c_m(Q)Y^m/(Q^m-1) solves the Laurent part. This proves (2), its field of definition, and the stated constant ambiguity. The construction does not throw away the factors Q^m-1 or any Y-meridian factor in b. ## 5. Unipotent and Heisenberg descent Let C(Q,Y) be a d-by-d upper unitriangular rational matrix. Use the column transport equation sigma(v)=C v, C_[N]=sigma^(N-1)(C)...sigma(C) C. (13) If C_[N] specializes to I at Q=zeta_N for every sufficiently large N, then there is a rational upper unitriangular G such that C=sigma(G) G^(-1). (14) To prove this, filter strictly upper triangular matrices by their distance above the diagonal. In the first surviving diagonal of C-I, multiplication adds the entries, so (13) says exactly that their cyclic sums vanish. Solve each by the additive theorem and gauge by a unitriangular matrix carrying those solutions. This kills that diagonal. The cyclic curvature remains identity, because it transforms by conjugation with the specialized G. Repeat through the finite d-1 diagonals. The process terminates and gives (14). Only finitely many bad root levels are introduced by each fixed rational gauge. For the Heisenberg matrix C=[1 u w; 0 1 v; 0 0 1], G=[1 p r; 0 1 q; 0 0 1], the equations are explicitly sigma(p)-p=u, sigma(q)-q=v, sigma(r)-r=w+u q. (15) The first two are additive. With these solved, set G0=[1 p 0;0 1 q;0 0 1]. Then sigma(G0)^(-1) C G0 has only central entry w+u q. Its cyclic curvature is identity, so the additive theorem solves the last equation. This retains the central cross term; solving only the two abelian equations would miss the regulator coordinate. Two solutions of (14) differ on the right by a constant upper unitriangular matrix over k(Q). A regular specified anchor can fix that ambiguity. A generic gauge alone need not preserve the integral cut lattice or the complete meridian specialization. The combination with multiplicative descent also proves the same existence assertion for every invertible upper triangular rational C, with G upper triangular. Each diagonal entry has cyclic norm one, so the rank-one theorem supplies its rational diagonal gauge. Apply that diagonal gauge first; the remaining matrix is upper unitriangular and the finite induction above applies. This covers a rationally split full flag without assuming unipotence in advance. In particular an affine source over such a flagged homogeneous module is handled by the augmented triangular matrix C_aff=[C c; 0 1]. If its full cyclic curvature is identity, the theorem solves its source together with the homogeneous transport. A rational gauge can be chosen with bottom row (0,...,0,1), so its top-right column is precisely an affine particular solution. This is stronger than solving the homogeneous norm while leaving the source arbitrary. ## 6. What this supplies to the proposed A-torsor argument This gives the requested group-theoretic termination in a precise setting: finite unipotence makes all transport equations solvable after their whole cyclotomic curvature has vanished. It includes the Heisenberg group underlying the marked regulator torsor, and is independent of crossing number, bridge number, or knot family. It does not infer that a general quantum A-module is unipotent. If the relevant comparison is a rank-one homogeneous line with a source, first trivialize the line by the full multiplicative theorem, then apply the additive theorem to its transformed source. More generally the triangular result handles every rationally split full flag and its affine source. A flag appearing only on a formal normal completion has not thereby supplied that rational flag. Rivin's positive maximizer supplies a marked algebraic geometric branch. The theorem here would descend an already constructed rational quantum/geometric comparison from its full cyclotomic transport identities, without choosing unrelated levelwise gauges. The actual comparison, its whole transport identities, its source and cut anchor, and the selected regulator norm still have to be proved. Algebraicity of the critical shape does not supply those identities by itself. The [regulator applicability audit](regulator_curvature_obstruction.md) makes the word comparison essential. A regular rational family with identity absolute curvature has a rationally trivial differential limit, even if its initial rational gauge is singular at Q=1. The marked regulator's logarithmic residues exclude such absolute triviality. Nor does equality of two noncentral matrix curvatures make their whole Hom curvature identity. The relative comparison object and its specified flat subobject must be constructed first. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_additive_unipotent_cyclotomic_descent.py). [Audit results](../experiments/additive_unipotent_cyclotomic_descent_results.json). [Independent proof audit](additive_cyclotomic_descent_independent_audit.md).

title: Adequacy excludes a fixed algebraic meridian period
text: # Adequacy excludes a fixed algebraic meridian period Research note, 26 October 2026. There is a uniform consequence of alternatingness relevant to the torsor problem: the actual color periods cannot be the traces of a fixed algebraic function of q and M. This does not exclude an algebraic period torsor with transcendental horizontal sections, or level-dependent algebraic root sections. It excludes a proposed finite algebraic section before one attempts to identify its norm with volume. The C_j(q) and meridian convention M=-q^j are those independently fixed in [the ADO pointing note](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). No Jones asymptotic is used. The result concerns exact degree spans. ## 1. An elementary bound for any fixed algebraic trace Suppose, for all sufficiently large positive integers j, C_j(q) satisfies a fixed nonzero relation F(q,-q^j,C_j(q))=0, F(q,M,Y)=sum_i f_i(q,M)Y^i, f_i in C[q^(+/-1),M^(+/-1)]. (1.1) Collect coefficients first and discard zero f_i. For large j every remaining f_i(q,-q^j) is nonzero: a collision of its q-exponents a+bj requires j=(a'-a)/(b-b'), leaving only finitely many exceptional positive j. All its q-exponents have absolute value at most A+Bj, for fixed A,B depending only on F. Let d_j be the largest q-exponent of the nonzero Laurent polynomial C_j. In (1.1), the largest exponent among deg_q f_i(q,-q^j)+i*d_j must occur at least twice. Otherwise its nonzero leading coefficient cannot cancel. Thus for two distinct indices i,k, d_j=(deg_q f_k(q,-q^j)-deg_q f_i(q,-q^j))/(i-k). It follows that |d_j|<=2(A+Bj). Applying the same argument to the least exponents bounds the smallest exponent as well. Hence span_q C_j=O(j). (1.2) This applies even if a different algebraic branch is selected for each j: the fixed polynomial relation is all that was used. A single overall framing monomial, even one with exponent quadratic in j, does not change the span and cannot evade the conclusion. The rational-function case is simpler. If C_j=p(q,-q^j)/r(q,-q^j) is Laurent polynomial, span(C_j)=span(p_j)-span(r_j)<=span(p_j)=O(j). Finite algebraic covers require the valuation argument above. ## 2. Exact extreme degrees for an adequate diagram We give the diagram proof rather than importing a degree theorem. Use the Kauffman bracket with empty value one, loop value delta=-A^2-A^(-2), and crossing expansion A times its A-smoothing plus A^(-1) times its B-smoothing. Let D be a connected knot diagram with c crossings. Let v_A,v_B be the circle counts in its all-A and all-B states. D is A-adequate if changing one crossing of the all-A state merges two distinct state circles; define B-adequacy analogously. For an A-adequate diagram, the all-A summand has top degree c+2v_A, with coefficient (-1)^v_A. Every other state has degree at least four lower: if k>=1 crossings are changed, the first change loses one circle and each later change adds at most one. Its circle count is at most v_A+k-2, so its top degree is at most c-2k+2(v_A+k-2)=c+2v_A-4. Thus the top coefficient cannot cancel. The all-B argument similarly gives bottom degree -c-2v_B. Let D^(n) be the n-parallel blackboard cable. Its crossing count is c*n^2, and its all-A and all-B circle counts are n*v_A,n*v_B. To see this directly, follow the arcs through the n by n crossing tile after uniform smoothing: it becomes n parallel copies of the original smoothing and creates no internal circle. A single changed cable crossing joins parallel copies belonging to distinct original state circles. Thus cabling preserves each adequacy condition. Consequently maxdeg_A <D^(n)>=c*n^2+2n*v_A, mindeg_A <D^(n)>=-c*n^2-2n*v_B. (2.1) ## 3. Passing from parallel strands to the actual color The j-dimensional color, n=j-1, is the Chebyshev threading S_0(X)=1, S_1(X)=X, S_(n+1)(X)=X*S_n(X)-S_(n-1)(X). (3.1) Thus S_n(D)=D^(n) plus a linear combination of cables D^(n-2r), r>=1. Both extreme degrees in (2.1) strictly move outward with n. The lower cables cannot cancel either extreme of the leading cable. For completeness, the color convention in (3.1) agrees, up to an overall color sign and framing monomial, with the fixed highest-weight periods. At generic q and n>=1 the tensor product of the fundamental module V_1 with V_n decomposes as V_1 tensor V_n = V_(n+1) direct-sum V_(n-1). With Delta(E)=E tensor K+1 tensor E, highest vectors are v_+ tensor w_0 and [n]_q*v_- tensor w_0-q^n*v_+ tensor w_1. Successive F-actions give dimensions n+2 and n; the usual E F^r highest-vector formula shows that these submodules are disjoint and exhaust the tensor product. Naturality of the finite R-matrix and additivity of the pivotal trace then give (3.1). This is the representation-ring calculation behind threading, not an additional asymptotic comparison theorem. The fundamental checked R-matrix has eigenvalues q^(1/2) and -q^(-3/2). Writing it as A*I+A^(-1)*e with A=q^(1/2) gives e^2=(-A^2-A^(-2))*e. This is the local bracket relation. An overall mirror convention changes exponent signs, and the zero-framing correction is a monomial; neither changes the span. The unreduced colored bracket therefore has A-span 2c*n^2+2n*(v_A+v_B). The unknot color S_n(delta) has A-span 4n. Dividing by this quantum dimension gives the reduced period C_j. Spans add under products of nonzero Laurent polynomials. Since q=A^2, we obtain span_q C_j=c*(j-1)^2+(v_A+v_B-2)*(j-1). (3.2) In particular every nontrivial adequate diagram gives genuinely quadratic growth, independently of its framing. For a connected reduced alternating diagram, its two state graphs are the checkerboard plane graph and its dual. A loop in either would be a nugatory crossing, so both adequacy conditions hold. Euler's formula gives v_A+v_B=c+2. Hence span_q C_j=c*j*(j-1). (3.3) Here c is the crossing count of that diagram; no crossing-minimality theorem is required for the argument. ## 4. Consequence for the period torsor Equations (1.2) and (3.2) contradict each other for every nontrivial adequate knot. Therefore there is no fixed finite algebraic meridian section whose traces at M=-q^j equal all the actual C_j(q), even allowing arbitrary algebraic branches in those specializations. This applies in particular to the entire class of hyperbolic alternating knots considered by the user. A large degree span supplies no lower bound at a particular root of unity; it does not exclude cancellation in the volume evaluation. This conclusion is compatible with a period of an algebraic connection or difference module. The underlying equations or torsor can be algebraic while its selected horizontal section is transcendental. It is also compatible with rational sections at each individual root level: their degrees or algebraic complexity can grow with that level. It is the fixed finite algebraic presentation in (1.1) that fails. The [affine extension construction](affine_quantum_a_period.md) uses this to rule out a split source extension whenever its geometric block has either stated nonresonance property. It does not yet identify that nonsplit class with the Bloch regulator or establish its archimedean norm growth. ## 5. The perturbative coefficients are polynomial in the color A second elementary fact is useful for the extension test. For every knot, with q=exp(h), C_j(exp(h))=sum_(k>=0) p_k(j)h^k, p_k in C[j]. (5.1) Only polynomiality is asserted; no diagonal summation, Alexander identity, convergence uniform in j, or large-color limit is used. Here is a direct proof from the cut braid. Write each checked crossing as its permutation times R or R^(-1). At each fixed h-order the unpermuted factors have finite expansions in tensor products of words in E,F,H: the r-th nilpotent R-term has factor (q-q^(-1))^r/[r]_q! of order h^r, the Cartan factor is exp(h H tensor H/2), and the pivotal factors are exp(h H). Negative crossings are formal inverses with the same finiteness property. Move the permutations to one end. Each coefficient is then a finite sum of a single permutation times such tensor words. The braid closure has one component, so that permutation is a single cycle. Its cut partial trace is the ordered product of the tensor words around this cycle; it creates no separate trace loop or color-dependent dimension factor. This identity follows by identifying the intermediate matrix indices along the cycle. At fixed h-order, reorder each product into PBW form F^a H^b E^c. The relation [E,F]=(exp(hH)-exp(-hH))/(exp(h)-exp(-h)) has polynomial coefficients in H at each h-order, so the reordering is finite. On the highest vector of color j, E kills it and F lowers its weight. Its highest component consequently evaluates the a=c=0 terms at H=j-1. It is polynomial in j. The zero-framing correction is the exponential of h times a polynomial in j and preserves this property. This proves (5.1) for the actual reduced cut period. This is the elementary polynomiality part of existing perturbative color theory; see the scope of [Rozansky, q-alg/9604005](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9604005). The stronger Melvin--Morton assertions are not premises here. ## 6. Coverage and independent checks Adequate colored-degree growth is existing coverage, including [Le, math/0407521](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0407521) and [Kalfagianni, 1601.03307](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.03307). Their stated scope is used for comparison; the extreme-state, cabling, threading, and valuation arguments above supply the proof here. No AJ or slope-conjecture theorem is imported. The [exact diagnostic script](../experiments/audit_adequacy_algebraic_periods.py) computes brackets by Temperley--Lieb multiplication and closure, forms the Chebyshev combination, divides by the actual unknot color, and checks the spans. It separately checks the circle counts and single-crossing adequacy of the cables. Examples are diagnostics of the uniform proof, not the scope of its statement. The [results](../experiments/adequacy_algebraic_periods_results.json) also check the fundamental local braid/bracket identity.

title: The actual Mellin period is transcendental for every nontrivial adequate knot
text: # The actual Mellin period is transcendental for every nontrivial adequate knot Research theorem, 27 October 2026. The actual Fourier--Mellin section has a bounded rational source and a specified formal source lattice. For every nontrivial adequate knot that selected section is transcendental over C(Q,X). This follows from the already proved quadratic color-degree span and an elementary valuation bound for algebraic power series, proved below without an Eisenstein theorem. This is a theorem about the actual pointed period for a wide knot class, including hyperbolic alternating knots. It does not identify its geometric A-component or prove its root-value volume growth. ## 1. Algebraic power series have linearly bounded coefficient valuations Let K be a characteristic-zero discretely valued field, with valuation v, valuation ring R and uniformizer pi. Completeness is unnecessary. Let f(X)=sum_(n>=0)c_n X^n in K[[X]] be algebraic over K(X). Then there are constants A,B>=0 such that v(c_n)>=-A-Bn for all nonzero coefficients. (1.1) Here and below zero coefficients satisfy the bound by v(0)=infinity. **Proof.** Choose a polynomial P(X,Z) in K[X,Z] for which P(X,f)=0 and P_Z(X,f)!=0. Such a choice exists because the minimal polynomial is separable in characteristic zero. Put m=ord_X P_Z(X,f), choose k>m, p(X)=sum_(n=0)^(k-1)c_n X^n, f=p+X^k w. Since p-f has order at least k>m, ord_X P_Z(X,p)=m. Taylor expansion gives a polynomial F(X,W)=X^(-m-k) P(X,p+X^k W) in K[X,W]. (1.2) Indeed the linear term is divisible by X^(m+k). The terms of degree j>=2 in W have exponent at least kj, and kj-(m+k)=k(j-1)-m>0. The constant term P(X,p) is divisible by X^(m+k) because substituting w makes the entire Taylor sum zero. At X=0, therefore, F(0,W)=aW+b, a=[X^m]P_Z(X,p)!=0. Let w_0=-b/a, which is the constant coefficient of w. Set W=w_0+V and divide by a. The resulting polynomial has the exact form V+X H(X,V)=0, H in K[X,V]. (1.3) This is the useful normalization: all other monomials have positive X order. Write H=sum h_(i,j) X^i V^j. Choose an integer B>=0 with v(h_(i,j))+B(i+1)>=0 for every nonzero h_(i,j). (1.4) There are finitely many coefficients, so such a B exists. Under X=pi^B x the selected series z(x)=V(pi^B x) satisfies z+x H_B(x,z)=0, H_B(x,z)=pi^B H(pi^B x,z) in R[x,z]. (1.5) Its constant term is zero. In the coefficient recursion, the coefficient of x^n on the right depends only on earlier coefficients of z because of the outer factor x. Induction shows z belongs to xR[[x]]. Thus, writing V=sum_(r>=1)v_r X^r, v(v_r)>=-Br. For n>=k+1 one has c_n=v_(n-k), and hence v(c_n)>=-B(n-k)>=-Bn. The finitely many coefficients through c_k are covered by increasing A. This proves (1.1). No analytic convergence and no a priori integrality of the original coefficients is used. The truncation removes the possible singular derivative, normalization gives one unit linear coefficient, and a single rescaling of X makes the finite recursion integral. ## 2. Consequence for rational-function coefficients in Q Apply the theorem to K=C(Q), first with the valuation at Q=0 and then with the valuation at Q=infinity. For a Laurent polynomial c_n(Q), these valuations are respectively v_0(c_n)=mindeg_Q c_n, v_infinity(c_n)=-maxdeg_Q c_n. Consequently an algebraic f(X) with Laurent-polynomial coefficients must satisfy mindeg_Q c_n>=-A_0-B_0n, maxdeg_Q c_n<= A_infinity+B_infinity n, span_Q c_n=O(n). (2.1) The algebraic relation may have arbitrary complex coefficients; their Q-valuations are zero. Thus this conclusion applies to algebraicity over C(Q,X), not only over the rational number field. It also covers any finite algebraic cover supplying a scalar branch in the selected integer-power series lattice. ## 3. The actual adequate color coefficients violate this bound The actual fixed-color functions C_n(Q) are Laurent polynomials, and the [adequacy proof](adequacy_and_algebraic_periods.md) establishes their extreme degrees directly from adequate states, cabling and threading. For an adequate diagram with c>0 crossings and state-circle counts v_A,v_B it gives, in the q parameter, span_q C_n=c(n-1)^2+(v_A+v_B-2)(n-1). The [actual Q-polarization](fourier_mellin_actual_source.md) has Q=q^2 and C_n even in q, so span_Q C_n=(1/2)c(n-1)^2 +(1/2)(v_A+v_B-2)(n-1). (3.1) In particular it has a strictly positive quadratic coefficient. For a reduced connected alternating diagram this simplifies to span_Q C_n=c n(n-1)/2. The zero-framing monomial does not change the span. Choose the fixed n_0 of the actual Fourier--Mellin construction and retain its exact selected section Z(Q,X)=sum_(n>=n_0) C_n(Q) X^n. (3.2) If Z were algebraic over C(Q,X), equation (2.1) would bound its coefficient spans linearly. This contradicts (3.1) for every nontrivial adequate knot. We have therefore proved Z(Q,X) is transcendental over C(Q,X). (3.3) Subtracting or adding any fixed initial-color polynomial preserves algebraicity. Thus the conclusion holds for every fixed starting color, including the start-one generating period. ## 4. The precise source/lattice conclusion The actual bounded-source identity is P^M Z=B, Z in X^(n_0) C(Q)[[X]], (4.1) where B is the fixed nonzero Laurent source from finitely many small colors. The source-lattice condition makes this solution unique, by the leading-coefficient argument of the Fourier--Mellin construction. Hence no scalar section on a finite algebraic cover, satisfying this actual source and this formal lattice, can replace Z. The selected whole period is necessarily transcendental. There is a useful operator consequence. Every nonzero actual Q-operator of a nontrivial adequate knot has positive generic Y-exponent span. Otherwise all its Y exponents would be a single m, and its Fourier image would have the form A(Q,X)S^m with A!=0. Equation (4.1) would make S^m Z=B/A rational, and hence Z rational, contradicting (3.3). Thus the actual Mellin source object has positive difference order for this whole knot class; no artificial factor is needed to create that order. This is not a claim about the operator's specialized symbol at Q=1. This does not contradict algebraicity of the underlying equations, gluing place, comparison torsor or connection. Their marked periods can be transcendental. Nor does it contradict rationality of the root fibers: the original [cyclotomic residue construction](cyclotomic_mellin_residue.md) gives a rational function at each Q_N whose degree grows with N. The assertion is not generic affine nonsplitting without the lattice. A rational or algebraic particular solution outside X^(n_0)[[X]] could coexist with the selected transcendental solution, differing by a homogeneous solution. We have not excluded that possibility. The theorem excludes a pointed algebraic splitting compatible with the actual source lattice and coefficient cut. Finally, quadratic degree span gives no lower bound for a specified root value. Cancellation can still occur at Q_N. The exact identity <K>_N=[X^N]Z(Q_N,X), or its infinity-residue version, remains the original volume target. No exponential regulator estimate is inferred from transcendence alone. [Exact valuation-normalization audit](../experiments/audit_adequate_mellin_transcendence.py). [Results](../experiments/adequate_mellin_transcendence_results.json).

title: Entire adjacent source projectors and their lattice groupoid
text: # Entire adjacent source projectors and their lattice groupoid Research note, 26 October 2026. On three strands, the two adjacent actual meridian projectors have a joint two-channel polar form. Its overlap is an explicit original pivotal cut moment. The remaining projector terms are regular at completeness. This determines their full local meridian germs, beyond the residue. There is also a uniform obstruction: these two projectors cannot both preserve one finite meridian lattice. A comparison must retain their changes of lattice. This concerns the original ADO source operators, not a replacement quantum invariant. The selected geometric period and volume conjecture remain unproved. ## 1. Adjacent cups and caps give opposite source matrix units Keep N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), and x=-M/q, u=Log M, R=C[[u]], delta=rho(M^2-M^(-2)), nu=(-1)^N rho^2. At M=1 use the actual cup C=vec(D^(-t)) and cap L=vec(gD)^t, where D_(N-1-a,a)=q^(a^2) and g=K^(1-N). Their two snakes are identities and LC=0. This follows directly by multiplying the two antidiagonal matrices: gD D^(-t)=I and D^(-t)gD=I. The remaining scalar uses x(1)^(1-N)q^((N-1)^2)=1. On W_0=V^(tensor 3) put i_1=C tensor I, i_2=I tensor C, c_1=L tensor I, c_2=I tensor L. The snakes and zero loop give c_1 i_2=c_2 i_1=I, c_1 i_1=c_2 i_2=0. (1.1) Consequently (i_1,i_2) and (c_2,c_1)^t split two copies of V, and the two nilpotents Pi_i=i_i c_i are opposite matrix units. In particular Pi_i^2=0, Pi_1 Pi_2 Pi_1=Pi_1, Pi_2 Pi_1 Pi_2=Pi_2, Tr(Pi_1 Pi_2)=N. (1.2) Tensoring the other strands gives the same identities and trace N^(b-2). This is the loop-zero Temperley--Lieb relation derived from the actual cups and caps. ## 2.
