Integral numerators and the charged simple block Let E_1,E_2 be the actual last Casimir projectors on positions 12 and 23 at generic M, and set T_i=delta E_i. They are rational matrices regular at M=1. To see this without evaluating a projector there, let Omega_i be the pair Casimir and let P_i be the integral projector onto the colliding c_0,c_last cluster. That unordered cluster is separated from the other roots at M=1; polynomial Bezout interpolation therefore gives regular P_i. Then T_i=(Omega_i-c_0)P_i, T_i^2=delta T_i, T_i(1)=nu Pi_i. (2.1) All these identities use the exact branch difference delta, not just its linear coefficient 4rho*u. Use the charged color P=V_z, z=-M^3/q, required by [the meridian charge calculation](sewn_source_and_meridian_charge.md). Let S be the total-Casimir projector of W=V_x^(tensor 3) onto its z block. Its complete Casimir is -2 and its derivative in the central polynomial is (-1)^(N+1)N^2. Thus S is integral. This block is P with multiplicity N. Each E_i S has rank one on that multiplicity space: the pair image V_(M^2) tensored with V_x contains P once in the explicit highest-vector fusion. The remaining operators F_i=E_i(1-S) (2.2) are integral idempotents. Indeed T_i(1)(1-S(1))=0 since Pi_i factors through the complete color V with Casimir -2. Their integral numerators T_i(1-S) are therefore divisible by delta in R. Their ordinary rank is N(N-1). This already isolates all poles in the charged block, uniformly in N. ## 3. The exact overlap is an actual cut moment Normalize the highest vector of the last two-color branch by h=sum_(a=0)^(N-1) h_a v_a tensor v_(N-1-a), h_0=1, h_(a+1)/h_a=-e_(N-1-a)(x)Q^(N-a-2)/[e_(a+1)(x)x]. Its coefficients are units near the complete color where needed. The covector vanishing on the F-descendants of all other branches has unnormalized coefficients lambda_a=(-1)^a x^(-a)Q^(a(a-1)/2). This follows from lambda_(a+1)+x^(-1)Q^a lambda_a=0, the two entries of the actual total F at degree N-2. Its normalization is Z=sum_a lambda_a h_a. On the total highest vectors h tensor v_0 and v_0 tensor h, the cross-projection coefficients of E_1 and E_2 are both lambda_(N-1)/Z. Only the component of pair degree N-1 can contribute; the others have zero last-branch projection. Thus the equality of these two coefficients is exact. The finite calculation in the appendix gives, with r=x^(-2), Z=(1+r^N)(1-rQ^(-1))/(1-r^2 Q^(-3)). Using r=Q/M^2 and lambda_(N-1)=(-1)^N q M^(1-N) yields delta*lambda_(N-1)/Z=A_N(M), A_N=(-1)^N rho (M+M^(-1)) *(qM^2-q^(-1)M^(-2))/(M^N+M^(-N)). (3.1) The complete value is A_N(1)=nu. In particular A_N is a unit of R. Its full M^N+M^(-N)=M^(-N)(1+U) factor is retained. Comparison with the independently proved original pair moment in Section 7 of [the cut-density note](geometric_rigidity_and_cyclic_source.md) shows A_N(M)=Phi_pair(T_1), A_N/delta=Phi_pair(E_last). (3.2) where Phi_pair is the original scalar pivotal partial trace, before multiplication by the full modified dimension. Hence the overlap is fixed by the actual cut, with its phase and peripheral function, rather than selected by a model normalization. ## 4. A joint regular frame for the full polar source Let theta=x(1)^(1-N). Define two P inclusions by highest vectors theta*h tensor v_0 and theta*v_0 tensor h and then the original total F descendants. Call them U_0,U_1. They are regular rational intertwiners and at completeness become i_1,i_2. The common theta is necessary to keep the original complete cup frame. On their images, (3.1) gives the integral matrices t_1=[delta A_N;0 0], t_2=[0 0;A_N delta]. (4.1) Here and below scalar matrices act on the two-copy multiplicity factor, with identity on P. There are regular rational rows r_1,r_2 with T_1 S=U_0 r_1 and T_2 S=U_1 r_2. For example, extract them with any coordinate left inverse of the primitive U_i; the factorization makes them H-linear. Their values on U=(U_0,U_1) form C=[delta A_N;A_N delta]. Its determinant delta^2-A_N^2 has value -nu^2 at M=1, hence is a unit. Set R=C^(-1)(r_1,r_2)^t. Then RU=I, T_i S=U t_i R, R(1)=(c_2,c_1)^t. (4.2) This proves an exact joint normal form, retaining every meridian coefficient of the actual projectors: E_1=U [1 A_N/delta;0 0]R+F_1, E_2=U [0 0;A_N/delta 1]R+F_2. (4.3) The regular F_i annihilate S and the common source corner e=UR. Both E_i vanish on the remaining N-2 multiplicity directions of S. Thus no additional polar channel has been discarded. Tensoring the construction with the remaining colors proves it for b>=3, with P replaced by the charged P_b of the preceding note. There is an intrinsic version of the source corner. On S put G=A_N^2-delta^2, e=[T_1T_2+T_2T_1-delta(T_1+T_2)]/G. (4.4) This is the same regular projector onto two copies of P. Its matrix units follow from (t_1t_2-delta t_1)/G=E_11, (t_2t_1-delta t_2)/G=E_22, (t_1-delta E_11)/A_N=E_12, (t_2-delta E_22)/A_N=E_21. (4.5) Thus the integral numerators generate Mat_2(R) on the source multiplicity space. Their joint comparison torsor, with the charged P fixed, is R^times: End_H(P)=R and a simultaneous intertwiner of the full matrix algebra is scalar. This specifies the local torsor and its trace calibration on three strands. After tensoring, the unrestricted comparison group is instead End_H(P_b)^times unless the spectator action is also fixed. Identifying such a torsor with a triangulation realization still requires its actual source operators and overlap to be matched. The [subsequent spectral-source calculation](actual_braid_group_and_spectral_source.md#6-a-cover-can-split-the-spectral-algebra-instead-of-killing-it) places these formulas in a universal rank-four algebra. For two numerators with t_i^2=delta t_i, the expression z=t_1t_2+t_2t_1-delta(t_1+t_2) is central. On the cover A^2=z+delta^2, with A,z units, (4.5) are its explicit matrix units. The actual root is exactly (3.1). This is a spectral splitting and scalar-torsor reduction, not nilpotence of the full source group. Genuine pure braid powers have a connected SL_2 quotient; their invariant plane is not generally this particular two-cup corner. ## 5. Whole sewn cuts now have an exact source decomposition For any integral whole knot operator B(M), let B_ij=R_i B U_j. The original calibrated rectangular trace identity gives mathfrak_t_W(B E_1) =mathfrak_t_P(B_00)+(A_N/delta)mathfrak_t_P(B_10) +mathfrak_t_W(B F_1), mathfrak_t_W(B E_2) =mathfrak_t_P(B_11)+(A_N/delta)mathfrak_t_P(B_01) +mathfrak_t_W(B F_2). (5.1) These are identities of full meridian germs, not only residues. The P trace uses the original d_N(M^3), including the exact dimension ratio already recorded in the charged-source note. The full affine source coefficient 1+U^(-1) multiplies these entire identities and is retained before specialization. The regular terms can cancel the source diagonal term. For example, on three strands the full cut of E_i itself is zero, while mathfrak_t_P(I)=d_N(M^3). Consequently mathfrak_t_W(F_i)=-d_N(M^3). (5.2) No positivity or noncancellation assertion follows from the nonzero source corner or its perfect bilinear trace. There is a useful exact simplification only after retaining the whole affine coefficient. For c=1+U^(-1), equation (3.1) gives c A_N/delta =(-1)^N M^(1-N)(qM^2-q^(-1)M^(-2))/(M^2-1). (5.3) Indeed c/(M^N+M^(-N))=M^(-N). Thus the 1+U factor cancels in the full off-diagonal source, with its phase and monomial left explicit. Its pole is precisely Y-1, the meridian divisor in [the actual normal-period construction](peripheral_normal_period.md). This is a rational identity before specialization, not a reset of a numerical factor at M=1. It does not identify the full global normal module or its selected knot period. ## 6. No one finite lattice can regularize adjacent projectors From (4.3), on the source corner Tr(E_1E_2)=N A_N^2/delta^2. The remaining trace is regular, since it comes from F_1F_2. As delta=4rho*u+O(u^2) and A_N(1)=(-1)^N rho^2, Tr_(W_b)(E_1E_2) =N^(b-2)rho^2/(16u^2)+O(u^(-1)). (6.1) The leading coefficient is nonzero in characteristic zero. If a full finite R-lattice were stable under both projectors, their product would be an integral endomorphism and its ordinary trace would belong to R. Equation (6.1), invariant under every meromorphic change of basis, contradicts this. This proof does not require H-linearity of the hypothetical lattice. In fact the traces of (E_1E_2)^m have pole order 2m, so the algebra of both unscaled projectors is not contained in a finite integral endomorphism order. Multiplying either projector by a meridian unit, including a peripheral factor with nonzero complete value, does not remove this obstruction. Each projector separately has an elementary stable lattice. For the source pair, replacing P direct_sum P by delta^(-1)P direct_sum P gives the matrices E_1 -> [1 A_N;0 0], E_2 -> [0 0;A_N/delta^2 1]. (6.2) Thus one elementary change shifts the pole into the adjacent operator with order two. The appropriate retained data form a groupoid of lattices and their source maps. The integral numerators T_i and their polar quotients must stay distinguished. This does not disprove a relative triangulation comparison with different lattices on its charts. It rules out a common finite regularization of these actual source arrows. ## 7. What remains and exact verification The entire local adjacent polar source is now explicit, with its charged object, overlap, trace, regular terms and lattice obstruction. This removes the restriction of the earlier sewn calculation to a residue. Its common comparison group is scalar only after the ordered integral numerators have been matched. These R-unit inversions are fixed-level meridian statements. The value A_N(1)=(-1)^N rho^2 tends to zero as N grows, so they are not automatically unit inversions in the joint quantum--meridian completion S=C[[u,h]] used for the point-source model. A comparison of those two realizations must retain this additional lattice information. No cross-level norm bound is inferred from the frame. The subsequent [uniform Frobenius source base](uniform_frobenius_source_base.md) now resolves this coefficient degeneration on a specified meridian chart. It retains w=M^N and the root phases, records the exceptional rho line, and extends the normalized two-channel algebra. Its marked Frobenius period also evaluates the full original cap normalization. This concerns the coefficient algebra; the full color object and selected knot period have not thereby been extended across levels. The full meridian atlas still contains its specified transitions, and their whole-germ cancellation must be compared with the relative triangulation source. The actual selected section has not been identified with the marked geometric period. Neither the formal normal-block comparison nor (5.1) proves the regulator norm across levels. The volume conjecture remains unproved. The finite sum in the appendix has existing coverage as the [first q-Chu--Vandermonde identity, DLMF 17.6.2](https://dlmf.nist.gov/17.6.E2). The formula and scope were checked after deriving our independent certificate. No published proof technique is imported. The cup/cap relations and matrix-algebra facts are existing elementary theory; no novelty is claimed for them. The calculation here fixes the actual overlap, charge and pole data in the original conventions. [The audit](../experiments/audit_adjacent_polar_source.py) checks the generic telescoping certificate and the universal two-by-two relations symbolically. Six complete original tensor cases verify the opposite cup/cap units and vanishing of the regular-remainder numerators. Twelve generic pairs of actual full projectors verify the charged inclusions, retractions, overlap, regular idempotents and their ranks and full modified cuts. Forty-eight full tensor-cut decompositions for the identity and figure-eight words check (5.1), with original framing and normalization. Even and odd composite levels are included. [Results](../experiments/adjacent_polar_source_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_adjacent_polar_source.py ## Appendix. An independent finite-sum certificate From the actual highest-vector recurrence, at the primitive root Q, Z=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) [(r^(-1)Q^2;Q)_k/(r;Q)_k] *(r^2 Q^(-3))^k. For a generic base Q define f_(n,k)={n choose k}_Q (a;Q)_k(c Q^k;Q)_(n-k) *(-c/a)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2). Let t=Q^n, z=Q^k. The ratio f_(n+1,k+1)/f_(n+1,k) is R(z)=-(c/a)(z-Q t)(1-a z)/[(1-Qz)(1-cz)]. Set H(z)=-Q t(1-z)(1-cz/Q)/[z(1-Q t)(1-c t)]. Direct rational simplification gives R(z)H(Qz)-H(z) =1-(1-(c/a)t)(1-Q t/z)/[(1-Q t)(1-c t)]. Multiplication by f_(n+1,k), followed by summation, telescopes; the two boundary terms vanish. Hence F_n=sum_k f_(n,k) satisfies F_(n+1)=(1-cQ^n/a)F_n and F_0=1. This proves sum_(k=0)^n [(Q^(-n);Q)_k(a;Q)_k/ ((Q;Q)_k(c;Q)_k)](cQ^n/a)^k =(c/a;Q)_n/(c;Q)_n. Specialize n=N-1, a=r^(-1)Q^2, c=r after proving this rational identity. The factors (Q;Q)_k are nonzero for k<N, and Q^(-n)=Q cancels the matching numerator and denominator. Thus Z=(r^2 Q^(-2);Q)_(N-1)/(r;Q)_(N-1) =(1+r^N)(1-rQ^(-1))/(1-r^2 Q^(-3)). All cancellations are whole rational identities. At the complete color the displayed final denominator is nonzero and Z has its required simple zero. No infinite product or root asymptotic is used.

title: The actual ADO threaded character and a separating source projector
text: # The actual ADO threaded character and a separating source projector Research note, 26 October 2026. This proves an exact, uniform formula for Chebyshev-threaded interior loops in the specified ADO evaluation. It retains the odd-thread signs and framing phases and then isolates a parity-independent even character. A null-homologous loop separates this character from the complete hyperbolic character for every hyperbolic knot. Thus identifying fixed central eigenlines is the wrong proposed comparison in that setting. A source extension can still encode the period as a distinguished splitting; a precise projector lemma states what an actual construction would have to provide. The proof uses the fixed unrolled matrices and elementary exact sequences, not a published Chebyshev--Frobenius or quantum-trace theorem. No quantum invariant or state is replaced. The volume conjecture and the construction of the required geometric source extension remain unproved. ## 1. Fixed evaluation and actual annular threading Let K be an oriented zero-framed knot, q=exp(pi*i/N), N>=2. Use the literature color V_alpha and parameters x=q^alpha, M=-qx, Y=M^2, U=Y^N=M^(2N). The pivot is K^(1-N). The core cut evaluation is the one already fixed in [the ADO note](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). Write F_N^L(M) for its reduced scalar with an additional framed fundamental-color link L in the complement; N_N^L=d_N F_N^L is the full period. The fundamental color W and its exact framed skein relation are those of [the peripheral-fusion calculation](actual_peripheral_fusion.md). For a further framed oriented loop gamma disjoint from L and K, let C_n(gamma) be its annular Chebyshev threading, with C_0(X)=2, C_1(X)=X, C_(n+1)(X)=X C_n(X)-C_(n-1)(X). Products mean framed parallels, and the definition is linear on the resulting link combinations. It has integer coefficients and uses no singular Jones--Wenzl projector. Choose the Seifert zero framing in S^3 as reference, and write f for gamma's framing, ell=lk(gamma,K), b=lk(gamma,L), the sum over the components of L. ## 2. Integral Weyl modules without divided-factorial denominators For m>=0 define D_m on u_0,...,u_m by H u_j=(m-2j)u_j, K u_j=q^(m-2j)u_j, E u_j=[m-j+1]u_(j-1), F u_j=[j+1]u_(j+1). These formulas have no factorial denominators. The identity [j+1][m-j]-[j][m-j+1]=[m-2j] checks the commutator, and the H and K relations follow directly from the weights. At the specified root E^N=F^N=0: every product of N consecutive quantum integers contains a multiple of N. They are therefore actual weight modules for the same restricted unrolled quantum group, even when m>=N. Only the auxiliary loop's color is changed here; the core color and its reduced or full normalization stay fixed. For every m>=1 there is the exact sequence 0 -> D_(m+1) -> W tensor D_m -> D_(m-1) -> 0. (2.1) Here are explicit maps, valid before and after root specialization: i(v_j)=q^(-j)w_0 tensor u_j+w_1 tensor u_(j-1), pi(w_0 tensor u_j)=t_(j-1), pi(w_1 tensor u_j)=-q^(-j-1)t_j, where missing endpoint vectors are zero. They preserve H and K. Substitution in Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E and Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F verifies E and F using [j+1]=q[j]+q^(-j) and q[j+1]-[j]=q^(j+1). The map i is injective, pi is surjective, and pi*i=0. Their dimensions give exactness. All these assertions use unit matrix entries and do not divide by [N]. Also W tensor D_0=D_1. Consequently in the Grothendieck group of these actual modules, [D_m]=U_m([W]/2), C_n([W])=[D_n]-[D_(n-2)], n>=2. (2.2) This follows recursively from (2.1); it is not a generic-q semisimplicity argument specialized through a pole. ## 3. Root subquotients, including their pivots and twists At m=N there is the additional exact sequence 0 -> D_(N-2) -> D_N -> C_(+N) direct-sum C_(-N) ->0, (3.1) where C_h is the one-dimensional module with H=h, K=q^h, E=F=0. The submodule map is u_a -> [a+1]v_(a+1), 0<=a<N-1. These coefficients are nonzero. The quotient consists of the two endpoint weights +N and -N. The endpoint transitions to the quotient vanish because [N]=0. This checks every generator and proves (3.1). Combining (2.2) and (3.1), C_N([W])=[C_(+N)]+[C_(-N)]. (3.2) For delta_N=(-1)^(N-1), both one-dimensional colors have dim_q(C_(+/-N))=delta_N, theta(C_(+/-N))=delta_N*i^N. (3.3) Indeed their pivot is q^((1-N)h), their crossing is q^(h^2/2), and closing that crossing gives the twist q^(h^2/2+(1-N)h). These are exactly (3.3) at h=+/-N. No framing phase is omitted. The polynomial identity C_(2N)(X)=C_N(X)^2-2 and tensoring one-dimensional colors then give C_(2N)([W])=[C_(+2N)]+[C_(-2N)]. (3.4) These latter colors have pivot one, twist one, and trivial double braiding with W. Their double braiding with V_alpha is the scalar x^(+/-2N)=M^(+/-2N). This is the even character used below. It does not silently replace the odd-thread data (3.3). ## 4. Why these Grothendieck identities compute the actual knot period The closed auxiliary-component evaluation is additive in a short exact sequence of colors. A direct proof uses a braid with the core cut and a basis adapted to the auxiliary submodule. The finite R, its inverse and the pivot preserve the filtration on each colored strand, with the strand positions exchanged at a crossing. A state can move only down the filtration along the underlying auxiliary component. Closing its trace forces it to return to its initial filtration piece; therefore every contributing state stays in one graded piece around that entire component. Summing those pieces gives exactly the two subquotient-colored evaluations. Separate closed components are treated independently. This is filtered linear algebra on the literal cut contraction, not an assumption about additivity of a modified trace on the core. Naturality of R and the tensor-product crossing identities proved in the peripheral note identify tensor colors with framed parallels. Thus (3.2)--(3.4) apply to the stated annular threadings for arbitrary gamma, including knotted gamma and diagrams with auxiliary self-crossings. For C_h, h=+/-N, the ratio between the two possible crossings with a core strand is the scalar monodromy q^(hH)=x^(+/-N). With a W strand it is -1. Unlinking the auxiliary component by crossing changes therefore records only its linking numbers. Its remaining one-dimensional knot evaluation is its pivotal dimension times its framing twist. This last statement can also be checked directly: on a one-component braid with B strands and writhe w, the zero-framing value is g^(B-w)=g, since g=+/-1 and B-w is odd. Its self-crossing scalar cancels against the twist. We obtain the exact whole-germ formulas F_N^(L union C_N(gamma)) =delta_N*(delta_N*i^N)^f*(-1)^b *(x^(N ell)+x^(-N ell))*F_N^L, F_N^(L union C_(2N)(gamma)) =(U^ell+U^(-ell))*F_N^L. (4.1) In the first line x^N=delta_N*M^N, so its multiplier can also be written delta_N^(ell+1)*(delta_N*i^N)^f*(-1)^b times M^(N ell)+M^(-N ell). In the second line every auxiliary framing and W-linking phase cancels exactly. The same equations hold for the full period N_N^L, retaining the entire modified dimension. For the boundary meridian ell=1 and f=b=0, the first equation is C_N(M+M^(-1))=M^N+M^(-N). For the preferred parallel ell=0, it is 2delta_N, agreeing with the full ADO character T^N=(-1)^(N-1). These provide independent checks of both signs. No universal Chebyshev homomorphism at degree 2N, or an unproved identification of its source skein parameter, is asserted. Equation (4.1) is the specific evaluation identity proved here, including the actual fourth-root phases at degree N. ## 5. The marked ramified fibre has the trivial even character The even eigenvalues in (4.1) are the squared-trace coordinates of the abelian character with meridian rho_U^ab(mu)=diag(U^(1/2),U^(-1/2)): (tr rho_U^ab(gamma))^2-2=U^ell+U^(-ell). (5.1) The square-root sign is irrelevant to this coordinate. At U=1 the value is two for every gamma. This includes the whole marked fibre of [ramified Weyl descent](ramified_weyl_fibre.md): in its coordinate z=(U-1)/(U+1), U^ell+U^(-ell) is even with constant term two. It multiplies both a_0 and b_0 by two. No extra odd coefficient changes the complete normal functional. In particular a null-homologous gamma has ell=0, and its even threading acts by exactly two on the entire meromorphic family, not just at the complete point. This also survives the canonical polar subtraction and its affine source equation: each part is multiplied by the same constant two. This does not require K_N to be nonzero. The ordinary anchor (a_0)_1/(Q-1)=1 makes the actual marked fibre nonzero at every level. Nor does (5.1) contradict a hyperbolic semiclassical critical point: the threading degree 2N grows with the level. Fixed small observables and fixed root-central characters are different data. ## 6. A null-homologous geometric separator for every hyperbolic knot Let rho_hyp be the complete holonomy. Two conjugates of a cusp meridian have distinct fixed points: otherwise the meridian conjugates, which generate the knot group, would all preserve one point, contradicting the non-elementary complete holonomy. After conjugation and harmless SL_2 signs, write them as p=[1 1;0 1], q=[1 0;s 1], s!=0. A direct multiplication gives tr[p^a,q]=2+a^2*s^2, (tr[p^a,q])^2-4=a^2*s^2*(a^2*s^2+4). (6.1) The choices a=1 and a=2 cannot both make the second expression zero when s!=0. Thus one of the two commutator words gamma has lk(gamma,K)=0, g_gamma(rho_hyp):=(tr rho_hyp(gamma))^2-2 !=2. (6.2) Represent the word by an embedded loop and choose its framing. The even threading formula is independent of that framing. The squared trace is independent of the lift to SL_2. The witness is uniform; no alternatingness or knot table is used. The positive ideal triangulation represents this same complete holonomy, so g_gamma-2 is a unit in its local geometric character ring. This is a precise interior-character distinction not detected by the common parabolic peripheral values alone. ## 7. What a fixed-central-character comparison can and cannot identify Suppose a proposed geometric root realization identifies the even threaded observable C_(2N)(gamma) with the scalar g_gamma(rho)=(tr rho(gamma))^2-2. This is explicit comparison data; no published quantum-trace Frobenius theorem is being assumed to establish it here. At the hyperbolic point, (6.2) and the actual evaluation (5.1) give distinct eigenvalues. Any intertwiner preserving this observable between the actual evaluation fibre and that fixed geometric central-character fibre must be zero: its matrix Phi satisfies (g_gamma(rho_hyp)-2)*Phi=0. The same holds locally because the difference is a unit. A scalar Hilbert-90 frame change or finite faithfully flat cover cannot change these scalar eigenvalues. In particular a direct equality of these two *fixed central eigenlines* cannot be the missing state comparison. This is not an obstruction to a source extension, a comparison only after the correct relative pushforward, or a varying-centre realization with a hyperbolic semiclassical saddle. Such a second realization need not have the fixed hyperbolic root character. It also does not show that the entire cyclic module of an actual operator lacks geometric factors: its selected evaluation is a particular quotient, and the distinction matters. ## 8. A separating observable can select the source period exactly There is a useful positive consequence for the extension approach. Over a difference field (F,sigma), take a specified source system sigma(w)=A_aug*w, A_aug=[ C b;0 1 ]. Suppose it carries an actual difference endomorphism X_gamma=[ G d_gamma;0 2 ], sigma(X_gamma)*A_aug=A_aug*X_gamma, (8.1) and 2I-G is invertible. Its unique eigenvector of eigenvalue two whose source coordinate is one is w=(v,1), v=(2I-G)^(-1)*d_gamma. (8.2) This vector is automatically horizontal. Applying sigma to its eigenvalue equation and using (8.1) shows that both sigma(w) and A_aug*w are eigenvectors of sigma(X_gamma) with eigenvalue two and last coordinate one. Invertibility gives uniqueness, hence sigma(w)=A_aug*w. This proves the source equation, without a monodromy computation or a root-rank hypothesis. Equivalently the eigenline projector is P_2=[0 (2I-G)^(-1)d_gamma;0 1], P_2^2=P_2. It preserves the difference structure by (8.1). If G=g_gamma I is a fixed geometric central character, the separator (6.2) makes the inverse a regular scalar near the complete point. Its denominator supplies no growing-level volume exponent. Any such exponent must remain in the actual source coefficient d_gamma and its selected period pairing. The even threading theorem supplies the eigenvalue two for the actual null-homologous observable. The geometric triangulation supplies a classical separator with g_gamma!=2. What is still missing is construction of an actual relative gluing/source system with the endomorphism (8.1), its off-diagonal coefficient, and the marked normal functional. Neither block can be chosen to force the desired value. The lemma is a criterion for that construction, not a proof that it has already been achieved. Specializing a generic nonsplit source extension to a split root-level extension causes no contradiction: its distinguished splitting (8.2) can still carry large periods. Splitting and the norm of the specified splitting are separate statements. If a specified generic source class is nonsplit, a separating endomorphism of the form (8.1) cannot exist over that generic difference field: (8.2) would split it. It cannot arise after a finite sigma-stable algebraic cover either, by the normalized-trace descent proved in [the affine note](affine_quantum_a_period.md). The actual threaded observables have degree 2N and depend on the level. Their root-level existence supplies no such fixed generic endomorphism. This retains the distinction between an algebraic evaluation at each level and a fixed-degree presentation across all levels. ## 9. Literature coverage and what has not been imported The common skein/gluing framework is already covered by [Garoufalidis--Yu, A quantum trace map for 3-manifolds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12424) and [Panitch--Park, 3d Quantum Trace Map](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12850). The later [Chen--Kricker, On 3d Quantum Trace Maps](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13268) advertises partial comparison of these constructions. Their abstracts and the scope of the quantum-gluing definition were consulted for coverage. No global trace-map, equivalence, Frobenius-compatibility, or knot-state-comparison proof from these works is a premise here. In particular no phase identification between their quantum parameters and the actual ADO parameters is inferred by citation. Chebyshev threading and root-of-unity representation theory have existing coverage; no novelty is claimed for that framework or for the elementary spectral projector. The results here are the independent, normalization-matched evaluation identities, the uniform geometric separator, and the resulting precise source comparison criterion for this fixed knot period. ## 10. Independent diagnostics [The audit](../experiments/audit_ado_threaded_shadow.py) constructs the actual modules and R matrices. It checks 52 integral Weyl sequences and 11 root subquotient sequences through level 18. At levels 2,3,4,5 it checks 192 heterogeneous R-trace cases, including positive/negative linking, an extra fundamental strand, both threading degrees, and all three framing signs. Sixteen actual knotted auxiliary traces test the closed-component additivity through nontrivial positive and negative knot braids. The commutator witness and the separating source projector are also checked symbolically. The [results](../experiments/ado_threaded_shadow_results.json) support the uniform algebraic proofs and establish no volume asymptotic.

title: Affine flag frames and transport of the selected vacuum
text: # Affine flag frames and transport of the selected vacuum Research note, 25 October 2026. This gives full-matrix covariance under affine changes of a flag frame. It also identifies a limitation of the unit pointing in the preceding recoupling note: an intertwiner at fixed central character generally transports that unit to a nonconstant vector. The resulting period transport must be retained in the proposed torsor. These are uniform algebraic statements, with no knot examples as inputs. Throughout, n is odd, omega is a primitive n-th root, and all displayed endpoint roots, affine differences and central characters are nonzero. Work on their common splitting cover. Permutations are literal ones. ## 1. An explicit Hilbert-90 transport, including its scalar Fix a central character g=(lambda,mu). Two endpoint pointings have b^n-lambda*a^n=mu=b'^n-lambda*a'^n. Use the two modules on K[x]/(x^n-lambda), with common multiplication X and with Y=(b-aX)sigma^(-1), Y'=(b'-a'X)sigma^(-1). Set r(x)=(b'-a'x)/(b-ax). Every denominator and numerator is invertible since its cyclic norm is mu. Their ratio has norm one. Choose alpha^n=lambda and specify h_0=1, h_j=product_(k=1)^j r(omega^k alpha), 1<=j<n. Norm one gives h_n=h_0, including the last step at x=alpha. Let H(X) be the unique polynomial of degree less than n with H(omega^j alpha)=h_j. It can be written explicitly using the spectral idempotents e_j(X)=(1/n) sum_(k=0)^(n-1) [X/(omega^j alpha)]^k, H(X)=sum_j h_j e_j(X). (1.1) All h_j are units, so H is invertible. The recurrence proves H X=X H, H Y=Y' H, H(alpha)=1. (1.2) These statements prove existence, not just an appeal to Hilbert 90. They also prove uniqueness: an intertwiner commutes with X and is a polynomial in it; its cyclic recurrence fixes it up to scalar, and the last normalization fixes that scalar. In particular, for three pointings at the same central character and the same marked root alpha, H_(2,1) H_(1,0)=H_(2,0) (1.3) exactly. This follows either from the product formula or from (1.2). Changing the marked root to omega alpha replaces H by H/h_1. Thus this normalization is a section on a marked spectral cover, not an invariant scalar after forgetting that cover. Its determinant is exactly product h_j. There is an elementary test for the selected vector. If H*1 is a scalar multiple of 1, then H itself is scalar because powers of X applied to 1 span the module. Equation (1.2) then implies a=a', b=b'. Therefore distinct endpoint pointings at a fixed central character are not identified by an intertwiner taking unit to unit. This does not obstruct an intrinsic period construction: it specifies the vector that construction must transport. ## 2. Ordered flags, additive transports and triangle modules In an affine chart, let p_i be distinct points and choose roots A_i^n=p_i. Assign the oriented edge i<j the affine central character g_ij=(1,p_i-p_j), with endpoints A_j -> A_i. These compose: g_ij*g_jk=g_ik. The construction in `pointed_period_descent.md`, Section 1, gives the pointed factorization C_ijk: E_ik tensor V_ijk -> E_ij tensor E_jk, (2.1) where the relative triangle module has central character and endpoints lambda_ijk=(p_i-p_k)/(p_j-p_k), mu_ijk=-(p_i-p_j)/(p_j-p_k), incoming=A_j/A_k, outgoing=A_i/A_k. (2.2) Its normalized Steinberg parameter is t_ijk=p_j(p_i-p_k)/[p_i(p_j-p_k)]. This explains precisely which auxiliary affine-origin data occur in the earlier Steinberg normalization. The unscaled central character in (2.2) is translation invariant; the normalized pointing is not. The explicit Racah closure of the preceding note extends to these matched endpoint modules. The ordered relative operators (2.2) in that note did not use X_i^n+Y_i^n=1. On four flags the right relative pair V_013,V_123 has matching endpoints A_1/A_3. Its total and relative pointed modules are V_023 and V_012, respectively. Thus the same general-endpoint factorization gives R_0123: V_023 tensor V_012 -> V_013 tensor V_123. (2.3) All central powers follow from the affine product law. The four ordered operator identities and the unit ideal certificates prove (2.3) as the actual Racah map, with scalar one. No new choice of quantum function or unaudited matrix identity is used. ## 3. Full affine covariance, including the triangle matrices Translate all p_i by B and choose compatible new roots A_i'^n=p_i+B. The edge central characters g_ij stay fixed. Since their lambda is one, mark alpha=1 on every edge and use (1.1) to define T_ij: E_ij -> E_ij'. These intertwiners compose exactly for successive endpoint choices. There is a unique triangle map S_ijk satisfying (T_ij tensor T_jk) C_ijk =C_ijk' (T_ik tensor S_ijk). (3.1) Here existence is substantive: conjugate the left side by C_ijk' and remove T_ik on the total factor. The result commutes with the total full matrix algebra. Its commutant is precisely identity tensor End(V_ijk). Consequently it has the form identity tensor S_ijk. The relative-operator identities also show that S_ijk intertwines the two unscaled triangle algebras (2.2). Everything is invertible, which proves uniqueness and invertibility of S_ijk. This is a finite, explicit construction of the full triangle matrix; it is stronger than covariance of its determinant. Naturality of the two three-edge evaluation maps now gives the exact tetrahedral identity R_0123' (S_023 tensor S_012) =(S_013 tensor S_123) R_0123. (3.2) To check its scalar, insert (3.1) in the two tree evaluations, use the pointed Racah identity, and cancel their common invertible evaluation and T_03. Thus the identity is literal, with all scalar factors intact. Equations (1.3) and (3.1) prove the exact composition law for the S maps. A common scaling p_i -> u^n p_i, A_i -> u A_i identifies X with X and Y with uY on each edge. The relative operators D=X_1+Y_1/Y_2 and -C=-(Y_1/Y_2)X_2, the endpoint ratios (2.2), and the C and R matrices are unchanged. The edge transport ratios in (1.1) are also unchanged by a common scaling. Together with translations this proves full covariance for the affine group, on the compatible endpoint-root cover. The proof applies at every odd n, including composite n. For a finite exterior contraction, use the dual S map on the oppositely oriented copy of each shared triangle. Interior maps cancel. The only surviving maps act on boundary tensors and on the chosen period vectors. No convergence or angle assumption is needed. This is a relative statement about finite tensors with the specified duality pairings, not yet about arbitrary literature integration cycles. ## 4. The vector and normalization lines do not disappear For B nonzero, the incoming triangle endpoints in (2.2) change: equality of their n-th powers would imply (p_j+B)/(p_k+B)=p_j/p_k, B(p_k-p_j)=0, contrary to distinct flags. The intertwiner S_ijk therefore cannot map the old unit line to the new unit line, by the test in Section 1. The transported vector is S_ijk*1 and must be retained. Thus the unit vacua coherent under recoupling in a fixed frame are not already a frame-independent selected period. An argument using only scalar commutants or determinant roots would miss this matrix-valued change. Normalization remains equally explicit. Taking determinants in (3.1) gives (det S_ijk)^n =[(det T_ij det T_jk)/(det T_ik)]^n *det C_ijk/det C_ijk'. (4.1) The previously proved general-endpoint determinant yields, for translations, det C_ijk/det C_ijk' =(A_k^n/A_k'^n)^(n(n-1)/2). (4.2) Both are identities of generic units. Determinant-normalized frames require the corresponding roots and their phases. The unnormalized construction (3.1) already chooses an exact scalar; one must not replace (4.1) by an unspecified equality after taking absolute values or by specializing a peripheral parameter first. The endpoint and spectral covers, the full triangle transport and its selected vector, and the determinant line are therefore different parts of the proposed period object. The finite Heisenberg cover alone records only part of it. ## 5. Literature comparison and the remaining projective problem This is a direct reconstruction within the existing cyclic Weyl/Borel recoupling definition, not a claim of a new quantum dilogarithm. Baseilhac--Benedetti's [matrix-dilogarithm construction](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306283), Sections 3 and 5 and Appendix 8, is a closer existing framework than the surface theory alone. Their [analytic families](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.4261), Introduction and Section 4, already organize rational quantum-hyperbolic state sums over covers of augmented character varieties. Neither global theorem is assumed in the proofs above. The explicit pointed transports here record what would need to match in a comparison with a chosen published state. The subsequent `projective_frame_period_torsor.md` handles all projective frames by compatible triangle Weyl rescalings and determinant rigidity on a root cover anchored at the identity. The actual selected literature period and its cycle still need to be identified under this local descent. The regulator comparison across levels remains a further theorem. In particular, finite central characters and semiclassical shape coordinates must be matched before using the rational Faddeev formula for growth. Those last steps are not supplied by the frame theorem or by Hilbert 90. The later [source-flag proof](source_flag_transport.md) writes this origin dependence intrinsically by adding a marked point s in P^1. Changing s gives the same normalized Hilbert-90 map in the shared face frames. Using the actual reverse edge caps fixes its face scalar and proves dual and cyclic naturality at every level for finite sources. Its first normal coefficient is a concrete affine translation of normal lifts; the selected cut row moves inversely. The global meridian/source and regulator identification remain open.

title: The inhomogeneous quantum-A period is an affine difference torsor
text: # The inhomogeneous quantum-A period is an affine difference torsor Research note, 26 October 2026. A homogeneous norm line alone does not record how a knot period is sourced. A literature-defined inhomogeneous A-equation gives a more structured object: an affine extension of its geometric difference module by a trivial line. Its class survives finite algebraic covers unless it was already split. At a root, a finite cyclic resolvent reconstructs its period. These statements do not prove that every knot has the required inhomogeneous factor or identify its extension class with the classical regulator. Inhomogeneous noncommutative A-polynomials are existing definitions; see Section 1.5, equation (2), of [Garoufalidis--Sun, 0802.4074v2](https://arxiv.org/html/0802.4074v2#S1.SS5). No creative-telescoping proof or knot operator from that paper is being assumed. The homogeneous operator and actual state remain those of [the all-level formulation](all_level_a_period.md). No minimal-order claim is made for a pair extracted from a given homogeneous operator. Its source is fixed by the actual finite color pointing, rather than selected to change the period. ## 1. The affine extension class Over F=C(q,M), sigma(M)=qM, take a specified pair A y=b, A=sum_(i=0)^d a_i(q,M)T^i, b in F, T y=sigma(y), a_0*a_d!=0. (1.1) Its column companion equation is sigma(v)=C v+c, c=e_d*b/a_d, sigma((v,1)^t)=U*(v,1)^t, U=[C c; 0 1]. (1.2) C here is the forward solution companion (superdiagonal one and last row -a_i/a_d). This is the transpose-dual convention to the cyclic-module matrix used in the intrinsic norm-torsor note. Translation v -> v+t changes the source by c -> c+sigma(t)-C t. Thus the source defines the additive class [c] in F^d/(sigma-C)F^d. (1.3) It is zero exactly when (1.2) has a rational particular solution. The inhomogeneous solution set, when nonempty, is an affine torsor under the vector space of homogeneous solutions. This linear and affine structure is proved by subtraction of equations, not by a nonlinear test on scalar sections. More precisely, (1.3) measures a horizontal point of a trivial affine bundle with semilinear transport. The underlying affine space has ordinary F-points; nonsplitting concerns the horizontal equation. This qualification is essential when comparing the difference extension to the ordinary algebraic norm torsor at a fixed root. The class is intrinsic under changes v -> Gv+t with G invertible: the augmented matrices change by the usual difference gauge U -> G_aug(qM) U G_aug(M)^(-1). One must transport the period functional and its actual meridian lattice along with that gauge. ## 2. Finite algebraic covers do not kill a nonzero affine class Let L/F be finite in characteristic zero, with sigma extending to an automorphism of L. If t in L^d solves sigma(t)-C t=c, then t_0=Tr_(L/F)(t)/[L:F] belongs to F^d and solves the same equation. Indeed trace is semilinearly natural, Tr(sigma(t))=sigma(Tr(t)), and C,c are over F. Consequently pullback on the classes (1.3) is injective. This is the relevant finite-cover descent statement. It differs from multiplicative Hilbert 90 on a fixed finite cyclic extension. A nonsplit generic source cannot be made into a rational particular solution merely by replacing F with a finite sigma-stable algebraic cover. The qualification sigma-stable is necessary. The subsequent [common period-space note, Section 6](common_frobenius_regulator_period_space.md#6-rational-frobenius-base-change-preserves-source-classes) proves an additional injectivity statement for the rational Frobenius enlargement. If sigma(w)=-w, extraction of the Laurent w^0 coefficient commutes with sigma-C and retracts the enlarged source quotient onto the original one. Thus a nonsplit source defined over F remains nonsplit over F(w), also after finite stable algebraic covers. This does not concern unrestricted formal or analytic period extensions. Its Section 7 also bounds the presentation degrees needed by exact separate root splittings. ### Formal splitting is a different operation Put q=exp(h), delta=M*d/dM, and assume C,c are formal meromorphic in h with coefficients in C(M), with C regular in h. If det(I-C_0)!=0 in C(M), the source has a unique formal particular solution in C(M)((h)). At order h^k, its coefficient is determined by (I-C_0)v_k=c_k-sum_(ell>=1) [(delta^ell/ell!)-C_ell]v_(k-ell). (2.1) Only previously computed coefficients occur on the right. The sum is finite at each order, starting at the lowest h-order of c. This proves the assertion by recursion. In scalar companion form, the condition is A_0(M,1)!=0 generically; it does not require nonvanishing at a special boundary point. Thus an extension can be generically nonsplit, remain nonsplit on every finite stable algebraic cover, and nevertheless split after formal completion. That completion is not a finite cover. Its formal splitting is not automatically an actual selected period or a convergent section. For the nonsplit example in Section 6, its coefficients begin v_0=1/(1-M), v_1=-M/(1-M)^3, v_2=M*(1+4M+M^2)/(2*(1-M)^5). They have boundary poles at M=1, while the exact root period there is the regular finite expression (6.3). Evaluating the coefficients separately at that point would lose the period. This locates the algebraization and boundary comparison that remains after formal branch lifting; it does not identify it with the Bloch regulator. ## 3. Exact affine descent at a root of unity Now let q have order n, E=C(M), K=C(u), u=M^n. Put C_j=C(q^j M), c_j=c(q^j M), and form the forward monodromy H=C_(n-1)...C_0, s=sum_(j=0)^(n-1) C_(n-1)...C_(j+1)c_j. Empty matrix products are identity. The augmented monodromy is U_(n-1)...U_0=[H s; 0 1]. (3.1) A rational solution necessarily obeys (I-H)v=s. (3.2) Conversely consistency of this ordinary E-linear equation suffices. Define the affine semilinear map Phi(v)=sigma^(-1)(C v+c). Its n-th iterate is H v+s. On the nonempty affine solution space W of (3.2), Phi^n is identity and Phi preserves W. For any v_0 in W the affine average v=(1/n)sum_(j=0)^(n-1) Phi^j(v_0) (3.3) is fixed by Phi and hence solves (1.2). Affine averaging is valid because its coefficients sum to one. This is an explicit additive cyclic descent argument for any level, including even and composite. In the nonresonant case det(I-H)!=0, there is a unique rational particular solution and no average is needed: v_N=(I-H)^(-1)s. (3.4) Each component is a Cramer quotient. Apparent zeros of its denominator must be canceled in the whole meridian germ. The solution transfer monodromy H is the transpose of the corresponding cyclic-module monodromy, so this uses the same central spectrum as the norm-torsor formulation, with the source retained. If (3.2) is inconsistent there is no rational period. If it is consistent and resonant, (3.3) supplies one; the others form an affine torsor under the homogeneous rational solutions. One must keep their actual lattice and pointing. There is no conflict between a nonsplit generic extension and rational splittings at individual roots. Specialization changes the order of sigma and its constant field. The finite inverses (3.4) can exist at every level without forming a fixed algebraic section in (q,M); the adequacy theorem excludes just such a section for the actual traces. This is information forgotten by performing Hilbert 90 separately at unrelated levels. The subsequent [actual threaded-character calculation](ado_threaded_shadow.md) gives another exact selection criterion. A null-homologous 2N-threaded loop acts on the actual period and its polar subtraction by two. If an actual extension carries a compatible observable X=[G d_gamma;0 2] with 2-G invertible, its unique source-one eigenvector is ((2-G)^(-1)d_gamma,1); commutation with difference transport makes this vector horizontal. A complete hyperbolic commutator supplies a classical scalar gap g_gamma!=2. The actual relative extension, observable and off-diagonal coefficient are still unconstructed. For a nonsplit generic source no such fixed generic separating endomorphism can exist, since it would split the class; level-dependent degree-2N observables are different data. ## 4. A simple algebraic criterion for nonresonance There is no need to compute a growing monodromy determinant when the operator has a unique extremal coefficient. Suppose, as Laurent functions of M, exactly one a_i has the strictly smallest order at M=0. The same criterion works with the strictly largest degree at infinity. Generic uniqueness persists at q_N for all but finitely many levels. For a nonzero rational homogeneous solution y with order k at zero, each sigma^i(y) has the same order k. The terms a_i sigma^i(y) would have a unique least order and could not sum to zero. Thus there is no rational homogeneous solution at these levels. This implies det(I-H)!=0. Here is a direct descent justification: if ker(I-H) were nonzero, the homogeneous semilinear Phi above has Phi^n=1 on that kernel. For nonzero w in it, some average sum_j Phi^j(fw) with f in E is nonzero. Otherwise the distinct field automorphisms sigma^(-j), applied to all f, would satisfy a nontrivial E-linear relation. Their independence follows by taking a relation with fewest terms and subtracting its value at af from one coefficient times its value at f. A choice of a distinguishing two automorphisms shortens the relation, a contradiction. The nonzero average would give a homogeneous rational companion solution, contradicting the valuation argument. This criterion is uniform in n and concerns the actual quantum coefficients. A classical extremal pattern alone does not prove it: coefficients vanishing at q=1 can change the M-extremum at every nonzero quantum parameter. ## 5. Returning to the actual all-level period Suppose a specified actual all-level reduced annihilator factors as P=(T-sigma(b)/b)A, b!=0, (5.1) and its generic color traces satisfy A C=b. More generally, after such a factorization, A C_j/b(q,-q^j) is independent of j. Its value kappa(q) is computed from finitely many fixed colors. If kappa!=0, replace b by the exact source kappa(q)b; the first factor is unchanged. No root-dependent source normalization is chosen. At a root, (5.1) implies A F_N=c_N(u)b, c_N in C(u). (5.2) Choose a fixed integer color J where b and the coefficients are regular and b(q,-q^J) is not identically zero; a sufficiently large fixed J avoids the finitely many exceptional trace identities. For all large N, the quotient-color identity and A C=b give c_N(1)=1. Its germ is regular there, since b is nonzero at that reference color and A F_N is regular there. If the geometric block A is nonresonant, (3.4) is the unique inhomogeneous root solution h_N. Equation (5.2) gives F_N=c_N(u)h_N, <K>_N=[h_N(M)]_(M=1). (5.3) The reference pointing has fixed the central unit exactly on this fiber. Its unit property also proves that h_N has a regular whole germ there. Formula (3.4), or its Cramer quotients, is therefore an exact source-normalized A-period formula. A rational homogeneous left factor and the nonresonance criterion are extra properties to prove for the chosen literature operator, not new definitions of a favorable quantization. The full ADO factor remains eta_N*(M-M^-1)*M^N/(u-1), with its residue and first jet as in [the meridian note](bounded_meridian_jets.md#5-the-full-ado-normalization-keeps-its-residue-and-first-jet). It is not erased from (5.3) or replaced by its numerical value before the whole-germ comparison. ## 6. Adequacy forces this extension to be nonsplit Under the actual-source hypotheses of Section 5, suppose A is nonresonant at infinitely many levels (the extremal criterion is a sufficient condition). If [c]=0 generically, a fixed rational particular solution h(q,M) exists. At every nonresonant level uniqueness gives h_N=h(q_N,M), so for every sufficiently large fixed j, C_j(q_N)=h(q_N,-q_N^j) at infinitely many distinct q_N. Polynomial rigidity makes the identity hold rationally in q. But for any nontrivial adequate knot the [degree-span theorem](adequacy_and_algebraic_periods.md) excludes even a fixed algebraic meridian trace, and in particular a rational one. Therefore [c]!=0. (6.1) By Section 2 it remains nonzero under every finite sigma-stable algebraic cover. This supplies a broad knot-class constraint on the extension, including all the hyperbolic alternating knots in the user's proposed class, whenever the explicit source and nonresonance properties have been established. It is not a proof that all those knot operators possess those properties. ### A formal test that does not require cyclotomic nonresonance There is a second, often simpler route to (6.1). Put q=exp(h), M=-exp(Xh), with X an independent color variable, and expand the trace operator over C(X)((h)): a_i(exp(h),-exp(Xh))=h^nu*(alpha_i(X)+O(h)), (6.2) where nu is the least h-order among the coefficients; some alpha_i may be zero. Let R be their maximum degree at X=infinity. If the sum of their degree-R leading coefficients is nonzero, the leading trace operator A_*=sum_i alpha_i(X)T^i, T r(X)=r(X+1), has no nonzero rational solution. Indeed, for r(X)=a X^k(1+O(1/X)), the coefficient of X^(R+k) in A_*r is a times that nonzero sum. Suppose a rational splitting g(q,M) of the source exists. Its trace expansion is in C(X)((h)); the lower h-order is finite, and all its coefficients are rational in X. Subtract it from the actual color period's formal expansion. By the independently proved [color polynomiality](adequacy_and_algebraic_periods.md#5-the-perturbative-coefficients-are-polynomial-in-the-color), this difference is also in C(X)((h)) and is annihilated by A. Its first nonzero h-coefficient would be a nonzero rational solution of A_*, a contradiction. Thus the difference is zero formally. For every sufficiently large fixed integer j the two trace functions are rational in q; all their Laurent coefficients at q=1 agree, so they agree identically. This contradicts the adequacy degree span. Therefore (6.1) follows from this formal test without any hypothesis on root-level kernel dimensions. Only finitely many fixed j must be excluded when expanding a rational trace: the first nonzero denominator coefficient is a fixed nonzero polynomial in X, and subsequent coefficients only introduce powers of it. If the coefficients are regular at (q,M)=(1,-1) and A_0(-1,1)!=0, the test reduces to that one nonvanishing value. When they share an apparent peripheral zero, (6.2) keeps the actual leading polynomial in X instead of substituting into a zero-over-zero expression. ### Nonsplitting is not itself a positive volume theorem The equation sigma(y)-M*y=1 is a simple nonsplit generic example. A rational particular solution cannot have a pole in C^*: a finite q-orbit chain of poles would leave an unmatched endpoint. It must therefore be Laurent polynomial. Its order at zero must be nonnegative, whereas comparing degrees at infinity forces its degree to be at most -1, a contradiction. The argument uses generic q, so its nonzero powers have infinite orbits. At a root of even order n its exact particular solution is y_n(M)=[sum_(r=0)^(n-1) q^(-r(r+1)/2) M^r] /(1+M^n). (6.3) The cyclic norm of M is -M^n and (6.3) follows directly from (3.4), or by translating the finite sum. At M=1 the denominator is exactly two, and |y_n(1)|<=n/2. Thus this nonsplit source has no positive exponential growth. It is not a knot model. It demonstrates why the regulator identification, rather than nonsplitting alone, is the missing norm theorem. ## 7. Why the classical A-equation alone cannot select volume The source class is essential. Given any ordered operator A with nonzero b=A(1), form P=(T-sigma(b)/b)A. The coherent period y=1 solves A y=b and P y=0 at every level. Its affine extension is split, with the constant companion vector as a splitting. If the classical b is nonzero, the classical symbol of P is (L-1)A_0(M,L). Thus one may use the geometric factor of a hyperbolic knot in A_0 and still obtain a split model with zero exponential growth. This is not the knot's literature quantization or state. It shows why the source extension, actual quantum operator, and finite pointing cannot be inferred solely from the classical A-polynomial. There is a corresponding classical warning about matrix norms. For the figure-eight geometric curve L^2-t(M)L+1=0, t(M)=M^4-M^2-2-M^-2+M^-4, the log spectral radius on M=exp(i theta), 0<=theta<=pi, is positive on two reflected intervals (0,pi/3) and (2pi/3,pi). It has equal integrals on them. Hence choosing the largest modulus at each point counts two equal contributions, whereas a relative period from a zero-volume real place to one complete place uses one contribution. Numerical integration gives the full integral 2.0298832128193, twice the required action Vol/2 in the recorded square-holonomy convention. The diagnostics label this a numerical classical check; it is not a quantum volume proof. The normalized curve matters for the zero-volume reference. Under the conjugation/Weyl involution (M,L)->(1/conj(M),1/conj(L)), a conjugation-odd volume primitive vanishes at a fixed normalized place. A smooth torus point fixed in these coordinates has one place and therefore value zero. At a node, the two normalized places can be exchanged, as at the complete figure-eight point; its coordinate values on the torus do not force volume zero. This is an intrinsic algebraic way to locate a possible classical reference, subject to the actual marked regulator's conjugation compatibility. It does not yet transport the quantum source to it. ## 8. Status and checks The affine class (1.3), finite-cover trace descent, cyclic averaging, resolvent, extremal-coefficient criterion, and formal nonsplitting test are proved above. The standard inhomogeneous-operator coverage was checked to avoid presenting a new definition. The independent [diagnostics](../experiments/audit_affine_quantum_a_period.py) check nonresonant and resonant affine descent, an inconsistent source, the scalar source factorization, a whole-germ rank drop, the formal trace criterion, and the nonsplit Gaussian-source example. [Results](../experiments/affine_quantum_a_period_results.json) are supplementary exact checks, not proofs of a broad knot operator class. The necessary next comparison is between the actual nonsplit source class and the marked regulator extension, with their peripheral pointing and norms. It is not supplied by Hilbert 90 at one level, by nonzero extension alone, or by maximizing classical eigenvalues. The volume conjecture remains unproved. The subsequent [regular-period theorem](regularized_kashaev_period.md) supplies a canonical rootwise affine source for any specified actual all-level operator, without Section 5's rational left-factor hypothesis. Its construction subtracts the full state's proper polar function, fixed by every ordinary-color value. Positive trace bounds make all those data polynomial in N. After a fixed gauge and denominator clearing, the source lies in a fixed Laurent space with polynomially bounded coefficients. The selected complete regular value is exactly a weighted cyclic field trace. Under a separate rational rank-one hypothesis, regularity at the nonzero pole anchor and at completeness fixes this affine value uniquely. A single generic rational source, its nonsplit class, geometric coupling, and the regulator norm do not follow from this rootwise construction.

title: Fixed algebraic central factors cannot change the volume rate
text: # Fixed algebraic central factors cannot change the volume rate Research note, 25 October 2026. This is a normalization theorem for the A-module torsor program. It retains the central variable before root specialization and evaluates whole period germs. It does not assume that an unknown comparison of the Kashaev and geometric periods is algebraic, and does not prove the volume conjecture. ## 1. The specialization theorem Fix nonzero c in C and an integer k>=1. At level N put t_N=1/N, q_N=exp(c/N), z=M^(kN). Let R be an algebraic function over the fixed field C(q,t,M,z), on any fixed finite algebraic cover. For each sufficiently large N, choose a branch after the displayed substitutions. Assume its whole germ at M=1 has a finite nonzero value r_N. A finite ramified germ is allowed, provided its value at M=1 is defined. **Theorem.** There are constants B,C>0, independent of N and of the chosen branches, such that C^(-1)N^(-B) <= |r_N| <= C N^B. (1.1) Consequently log|r_N|=O(log N), so multiplying an already specified period by r_N does not change its exponential volume rate. The assumption is a fixed finite algebraic presentation of the factor across levels. Being algebraic separately at every N is insufficient. The theorem also allows rational dependence on N itself, since N=1/t. ## 2. Proof by bounded central jets Choose an algebraic relation, clear denominators, and write P(q,t,M,z,Y)=sum_(i=0)^d G_i(q,t,M,z)Y^i=0, where each G_i has finite Laurent support in M,z and rational coefficients in q,t. Introduce M=exp(y). After q=exp(ct), z=exp(ky/t), each coefficient is a finite exponential sum G_i(t,y)=sum_(a,b) g_(i,a,b)(t) exp((a+kb/t)y). (2.1) The g coefficients are meromorphic germs at t=0. Its y-jets are J_(i,j)(t)=sum_(a,b) g_(i,a,b)(t)(a+kb/t)^j, (2.2) also meromorphic germs. The exponent functions a+kb/t are distinct for all sufficiently small nonzero t after identical pairs are combined. A Vandermonde matrix shows that a nonzero coefficient with S monomials has some nonzero jet of order less than S. There is no hidden identically zero relation caused by q=exp(ct): a nonzero rational function in q,t cannot vanish identically on that germ. After clearing denominators such a relation would be a polynomial exponential sum sum_j p_j(t)exp(jct)=0. On a ray with ct real and tending to positive infinity, the highest exponential dominates all lower ones, contradicting a nonzero polynomial p_j. Let m be the smallest jet index for which some J_(i,m) is a nonzero meromorphic germ. All lower jets vanish identically. For sufficiently small nonzero t the order m is stable, because a nonzero meromorphic germ has no zeros accumulating at zero. Divide all coefficients in the relation by y^m and evaluate the whole branch at y=0. It follows that every r_N is a nonzero root of the same meromorphic polynomial Q(t_N,Y)=sum_i J_(i,m)(t_N)Y^i. (2.3) The common factorial m! is irrelevant. The polynomial Q is nonzero. Remove its power of Y so that its constant and leading coefficients are nonzero meromorphic germs. Ratios of its coefficients have at most a fixed power pole at t=0. The elementary root bound for a monic polynomial gives |r_N|<=C N^B. Apply the same bound to its reciprocal polynomial to obtain the lower bound. This proves (1.1) uniformly for every nonzero branch value. This proof never evaluates separate vanishing numerator and denominator factors. The bounded jet m performs their common algebraic cancellation before specialization. ## 3. The actual ADO normalization is an example For the literature meridian family, write f=M-M^(-1), k=2 and q_N=exp(pi*i/N). The reduced/full factor is d_N(M)=eta_N f(M) M^N/(M^(2N)-1), |eta_N|=1. After retaining z=M^(2N), its quotient by eta_N is the fixed algebraic function R(M,z)=f(M)*sqrt(z)/(z-1), (3.1) with the root sqrt(z)=M^N specified. Its polynomial relation is Y^2(z-1)^2-f(M)^2 z=0. After substitution, the lowest common y-jet is of order two and gives 4N^2 Y^2-4=0. Thus Y=+/-1/N. The specified root germ selects +1/N and hence d_N(1)=eta_N/N, exactly as independently proved from the state definition. This is a fixed algebraic central factor despite its level-dependent powers in M. Likewise 1+M^N=1+sqrt(z) evaluates to 2 on the specified root. It remains part of an exact comparison. The theorem says that such a factor has no exponential effect after its whole nonzero germ has been correctly specified; it does not authorize omitting it from a move identity. ## 4. How this fits the two torsors The finite cyclic norm-torsor comparison permits central scalar factors. The formal A-curve connection retains the action and meromorphic connection coefficients, but actual difference periods can contain functions of the invariant z=exp(2pi*i*Log M/h). At h=pi*i/N this is M^(2N). The exact ADO factor illustrates this missing difference-constant datum; see [the formal period construction](formal_a_curve_period_torsor.md). If a genuine comparison between two selected quantum-period realizations has a factor from a fixed finite algebraic central cover, (1.1) controls that normalization uniformly. This strengthens the earlier bound for a fixed meromorphic germ in q alone. The qualification matters. The levelwise unit (z/2)^N evaluates to 2^(-N) at z=1. It has no fixed finite algebraic presentation of the kind in the theorem; its exponential behavior is exactly excluded by that hypothesis. Hilbert 90 at separate levels does not exclude it. No fixed algebraic comparison between the actual Kashaev period and a geometric quantum-period realization has been constructed here. In particular the theorem is not applied to an assumed algebraic ratio between the Kashaev invariant and the bare classical exponential of volume. The full period comparison and its geometric norm are still the outstanding theorem in [the primary formulation](a_polynomial_torsor_status.md). `experiments/audit_algebraic_central_normalization.py` checks bounded central jets, canceled rational germs, the actual algebraic ADO factor, and its root selection. The growth bound itself is the proof above.

title: Exact binomial conversion with algebraic clock coefficients
text: # Exact binomial conversion with algebraic clock coefficients 28 October 2026. This supplements the [analytic conversion counterexample](analytic_two_channel_conversion_counterexample.md). The failure of a bound by the maximum complete marked-branch action already occurs with polynomial coefficients over Q(i), on a compact interval with no zero or coincident eigenvalues. This is a recurrence example, NOT a knot operator; the clock x below is not the meridian M. Fix delta=1/16. Take integers H=16r, n=H-2r=14r, and x_j=(r+j)/H, j=0,...,n-1, T_j=[ x_j 1/n; 0 i(1-x_j) ], P_n=T_(n-1)...T_0. The source is e_2 and the observable is e_1*. Thus the selected scalar is (P_n)_12. The eigenvalues x and i(1-x) are nonzero and distinct on [delta,1-delta], with gap |x-i(1-x)|>=1/sqrt(2). Eigenframes and their derivatives are uniformly bounded. The principal family is diagonal; the exact family differs from it only by the entry 1/n. ## 1. Exact finite identity Expanding according to the unique off-diagonal step gives (P_n)_12=(1/n) C_(H,r) i^(-r) sum_(m=r)^(H-r-1) binom(H,m)i^m, C_(H,r)=H^(-(n-1))(H-r-1)!(H-r)!/H! . (1) Indeed the term with conversion at step k has, apart from (1/n)i^k, the positive weight H^(-(n-1)) (H-r-1)!(H-r)! / ((r+k)!(H-r-k)!). (2) This proves (1) without an asymptotic argument. The same scalar is the solution of the exact second-order recurrence u_(j+2)=[x_(j+1)+i(1-x_j)]u_(j+1) -i x_j(1-x_j)u_j, u_0=0, u_1=1/n. (3) Its coefficients are polynomial in x_j and 1/H over Q(i), and its leading shift coefficient is one. The principal characteristic roots are again x and i(1-x). Thus this is also a scalar companion example. ## 2. Growth follows from the binomial theorem and elementary tails Write h(delta)=-delta log(delta)-(1-delta)log(1-delta). The full sum is (1+i)^H, with modulus exp[H log(2)/2]. The omitted tails satisfy |omitted tails|<=(2r+1)exp[H h(delta)]. (4) For completeness, binom(H,m)<=exp[H h(m/H)] follows because the m-th term of the binomial probability sum with p=m/H is at most one. Entropy increases on [0,1/2] and is symmetric, giving (4) for both tails, including the single endpoint m=H-r. Since Delta=log(2)/2-h(1/16)>0, the middle sum equals (1+i)^H times 1+O(H exp(-H Delta)). There is no unresolved oscillatory cancellation in this conclusion. Applying the elementary factorial asymptotic log(m!)=m log(m)-m+O(log(m)) to (1) gives lim_(r->infinity) (1/n)log|(P_n)_12|=Gamma, Gamma=-1+[2(1-delta)log(1-delta)+log(2)/2]/(1-2delta). (5) Each continuously marked eigenvalue has the SAME complete action I=(1/(1-2delta)) integral_delta^(1-delta) log(x) dx =-1+[(1-delta)log(1-delta)-delta log(delta)]/(1-2delta). (6) Their discrepancy is strictly positive: Gamma-I=[log(2)/2-h(delta)]/(1-2delta)>0. (7) The diagonal entries of P_n have rate I, so its full norm also has rate Gamma. Both numbers happen to be negative with this normalization; multiplying every matrix by the fixed rational scalar 4 makes both positive and preserves the discrepancy. No positivity of the rate is needed to refute the proposed upper bound. The diagonal principal product has rate I. Thus the polynomial 1/n perturbation changes the leading exponential rate, despite the uniformly separated spectrum. Algebraicity in a clock variable alone does not remove this phenomenon. The additional structure of an actual quantum knot operator, its meridian dependence, and its selected source remain separate, essential questions. [Audit](../experiments/audit_algebraic_clock_conversion.py): exact Gaussian-integer triangular products, identity (1), the independently iterated scalar companion, and asymptotic tail/rate checks. An independent agent checked the full proof and freshly reran the audit: PASS. Its review retained the distinction between an algebraic clock example and an actual quantum-meridian operator.

title: What a finite algebraic source criterion can certify
text: # What a finite algebraic source criterion can certify 29 October 2026. This audits the proposed A-polynomial/gluing-ideal route. It separates a finite certificate for the ACTUAL hyperbolic value from the remaining estimate on the original quantum period. It supplies a specific obstruction using the actual source's value/normal pair, not a claim that knot A-polynomials never contain enough information. ## 1. A finite classical certificate is available For a specified actual decorated triangulation/port diagram, the useful algebraic object is its FULL marked gluing ideal on the regular locus, saturated by every inverted shape/frame denominator. A peripheral elimination polynomial alone is weaker. The following are checkable finite data: * The actual oriented ideal manifold triangulation: face identifications, circular edge links and the intended torus vertex links, with its degree-one marked identification with the original exterior. Retain actual integer gluing/peripheral incidence and all multiplicities. * An algebraic complete solution with every positively ordered shape in the upper half-plane. Its sign inequalities can be certified by real-algebraic isolating intervals, rather than by a fitted shape. Require true complex edge products1, unit unwrapped edge winding, and both marked peripheral linear products1. Unit winding itself is a finite sign test: along ordered edge factors w_j with Im w_j>0, put p_0=1,p_j=product_(k<=j)w_k. Count indices for which Im p_(j-1)<0 and Im p_j>=0; the count must be1. Each factor turns through strictly less than pi, so this counts exactly the positive real-ray crossings, including a landing on that ray. Positive cusp link triangles and unit edge winding give a nonsingular similarity torus; peripheral linear products1 make it a complete flat torus. * Full edge rank and the marked peripheral symplectic pairing. The [explicit ideal certificate](actual_pretzel_positive_ideal_angle_certificate.md) proves these for the actual current cellulation; the general [stationarity audit](source_angle_stationarity_critical_audit.md) makes the required rank conditions explicit. * The marked gluing Jacobian is then nonzero, rather than an extra assumed analytic input. Positive polarization proves it after choosing independent edge and marked peripheral constraints: if (A B) has full row rank n and its n-dimensional row space is real Lagrangian in R^(2n), and tau_j=1/(z_j-1), then Im tau_j<0 and (A+B diag tau)v=0 would put (v,diag(tau)v) in its complexified Lagrangian kernel, contradicting sum Im(tau_j)|v_j|^2<0 unless v=0. * An actual localized inverse between the selected source critical scheme and this decorated group/gluing scheme, retaining the original meridian, preferred longitude, flags and central signs. These certify an etale geometric germ and identify the selected regular critical representation there. They are stronger than finding the same peripheral polynomial or matching a cusp derivative. At a positive full gluing solution, the coisotropic identity gives the volume derivative for EVERY affine angle tangent: dV=(1/2)sum_i(Re V_i dIm U_i-Re U_i dIm V_i). At a complete point this vanishes on the whole edge-angle domain. At a filled point, Re(a_i U_i+b_i V_i)=0 makes it vanish on the FULL fixed-slope-angle domain. Strict concavity makes that positive point the unique global maximum, including against boundary points. Thus these data identify V_source with hyperbolic volume once the marked source action is calibrated on the same branch. The exponentiated filling equation is not enough: the actual primitive period must be +/-2pi i, not zero or a higher multiple. The [general geometric completion](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md) proves the needed degree-one statement from the bounded near-complete framed representation and these small log periods. Its equivariant construction avoids a universal ideal-triangulation existence premise. When an angle presentation is used, its positive chart must be supplied separately; a topological triangulation alone is not that certificate. ## 2. Why A or a localized quantum module does not specify the actual source There is an exact example INSIDE the existing original-source theory. Let F_N(Y) be the actual reduced meridian period and put f_N(Y)=(1-Y)F_N(Y). This is the normalized actual function used in [the whole Newton source transform](newton_actual_source_canonical_transform.md). Both are meromorphic sections of gauge-equivalent q-difference modules over the localized meridian field. If P=sum a_k(q,Y)T^k annihilates F, Tg(Y)=g(QY), then P_f=(1-Y)P(1-Y)^(-1) has coefficients a_k(q,Y)(1-Y)/(1-Q^kY) and annihilates f. Away from Y=1 its classical symbol is EXACTLY the same as P's. Clearing and saturating apparent meridian factors does not restore the source row. Nevertheless at the complete physical point f_N(1)=0, -partial_Y f_N(1)=F_N(1)=K_N. (1) For the actual figure-eight, the already proved exact K_N=sum_r|F_r|^2 is positive at every level. Thus the full nonzero geometric growth is in the NORMAL coefficient in(1), while the value is identically zero. This is not two different knot invariants with the same A-polynomial. It proves the narrower necessary statement: the same localized peripheral curve/module does not tell one which actual value or normal functional computes the original invariant. A criterion must therefore retain the integral pointed lattice and its specified normal co-source, not just a meromorphic gauge class or a saturated classical ideal. Regular-singular language on a punctured meridian disk does not by itself restore this lost lattice datum. The bounded-normal-factorial theorem gives estimates for prescribed jets of explicit kernels; it does not choose which jet the source uses. There is a second independent loss. The peripheral differential fixes an action only up to a meridian-independent constant. Bloch lifts of the same boundary wedge can differ by a closed Bloch class with nonzero regulator. The [Bloch-period audit](bloch_lift_and_boundary_torsor.md), sections3--4, shows precisely why the actual fundamental-class lift and complete volume anchor must accompany the A-curve. They are not recovered from the peripheral equation's Jacobian or degree. ## 3. Exact algebraic support does not yet give the whole quantum estimate The [actual coefficient normal-period theorem](actual_geometric_normal_period.md) proves a nonzero local formal geometric normal block and a formally unit gauge to the calibrated geometric line. It explicitly leaves the two framing modes and their original relative pushforward unevaluated. The algebraic local ring and nonsingular Hessian are therefore real progress, but they do not prove that the original whole period retains that block. This is visible in an exact endpoint calculation, rather than a generic appeal to Stokes phenomena. The [sourced telescoping audit](sourced_telescoping_geometric_support_criterion.md), section5, has for the actual relative interval J_v(S_eta f)=exp(-v)J_v(f) +exp(-v)[integral_1^(1+eta)-integral_0^eta] exp(vt/eta)f(t)dt. Already f=1 excludes the naive homogeneous shift-covariant replacement. The endpoint source must be transported or canceled exactly. A proof of interior ideal equality cannot delete this term by saturation. Similarly, the [saturated critical compactification](saturated_critical_regulator_compactification.md) bounds all TRUE full critical limits, but explicitly does not put every endpoint of the original relative cycle into that closure. Its exact Pachner counterexample shows cleared equations can create false boundary volume; full saturation removes that false component, not an arbitrary physical boundary current. The [algebraic-clock conversion example](algebraic_clock_conversion_counterexample.md) also warns against replacing whole transport by selected principal root actions: a polynomial offdiagonal perturbation changes the leading exponential rate despite nonzero distinct roots and bounded eigenframes. It is not a knot operator or a counterexample to a knot-specific theorem. It rules out deriving the needed propagation solely from that generic algebraic/spectral regularity. Thus a DECORATED POINTED quantum module could in principle supply the missing source theorem, but it must supply more than its regular local ring: actual normal evaluation, relative boundary/shift covariance, and a quantitative nonzero geometric pushforward. No impossibility theorem for such a source-specific algebraic construction is asserted. The [general original-source filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) provides one concrete successful bridge from base data: an exact even complex color packet, global complementary source gap, marked actual representation and calibrated action imply full nonzero long-filling asymptotics. Those analytic base estimates have been proved for the current explicit source class, not for every ideal satisfying the classical tests in section1. This distinction keeps the active broader equality objective from being replaced by a principal-curve criterion.

title: The actual period from an all-level A-operator and finite pointing
text: # The actual period from an all-level A-operator and finite pointing Research note, 25 October 2026. Starting from any specified nonzero all-level annihilator of the actual reduced ADO state, the Kashaev value is recovered from that operator and finitely many fixed small colors, without a rank-one or regular-orbit assumption. Singular steps require a uniformly bounded quantum-parameter jet. Those initial jets are bounded because the colors are fixed. This gives an exact operator period; its volume growth remains unproved. The definitions and independently checked normalization are those of [the ADO note](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). In particular F_N(-q_N^j)=C_j(q_N), 1<=j<=N, F_N(1)=<K>_N, q_N=exp(pi*i/N), (0.1) where C_j(q) is the fixed finite-dimensional reduced period, with unknot normalization one. It is Laurent polynomial in the recorded quantum parameter, analytic at q=1, and C_j(1)=1. Only finitely many fixed colors will be input. No large-color Jones estimate or unverified holonomicity theorem is used. ## 1. Cross-level rigidity gives the generic trace recurrence Fix a specified nonzero all-level reduced ADO annihilator P=sum_(i=0)^d a_i(q,M)T^i, TM=qMT, d>=1, (1.1) with rational coefficients, annihilating F_N for all but finitely many N. Clear denominators once so that a_i are Laurent polynomials. This changes no state or peripheral normalization. A possible order-zero annihilator of this nonzero state is necessarily zero. For any fixed positive integer j form the Laurent polynomial H_j(q)=sum_(i=0)^d a_i(q,-q^j) C_(j+i)(q). (1.2) At every sufficiently large N with N>=j+d, (0.1) and the actual ADO equation give H_j(q_N)=0. Infinitely many distinct q_N occur.
