The continuous coefficient-independent support theorem in [the flow-cycle proof](actual_full_psi_scalar_flow_cycle.md) states that EVERY feasible whole-source atomic order satisfies 0<=h_j<=d=N-1. (1) Let L_N denote the COMPLETE original head/source pairing, at fixed moment variables t and Gaussian tuple xi. Evaluate the exact finite cup/cap polynomials first; the full marked row is restricted by total degree as previously proved. No Ward identity is reapplied per sector. For any subset S of atoms, K(s)=1/(1-s)=K_N(s)+s^N K(s), K_N(s)=sum_(h=0)^(N-1)s^h. (2) Expand (2) in the original common chamber |s_j|<1. Every term with a nonempty tail subset has at least one order h_j>=N and therefore NO feasible whole-source route by (1). Its L_N pairing is zero, pointwise in all t and xi and independently of the coefficients at the other atoms. Consequently L_N[ product_j K(s_j) ] =L_N[ product_j K_N(s_j) ]. (3) One may replace any selected subset instead of all atoms. In the common chamber the right side is a finite Laurent polynomial in the moment variables. Equation (3) identifies the complete head pushforward with that polynomial; it is stronger than equality after a special full-Psi or Gaussian integration. The statement does NOT remove arbitrary head-reset tails or Laurent coupons. A microfactor that heals an out-of-range index can invalidate (1). No such new operator or arbitrary head-angle cutoff is inserted here. The proof applies to the original strict whole word and its authorized original source. ## 2. Pole clusters disappear in a genuine holomorphic representative Each K_N is a polynomial. At s=1, K_N(1)=N, so the numerator 1-s^N cancels the Cauchy denominator exactly. Replacing the participating atoms of ANY compact cluster by (3) makes the entire source holomorphic across that cluster. Multiplying these polynomials does not require independent characters: coincident poles, undirected circuits and all higher intersections are covered at once. Other true singularities of the full functions or coordinate boundary are a separate issue. This gives a precise regrouping of the TOTAL source represented by P_bare+W_cut in [the exact pushforward](actual_full_psi_cut_wall_pushforward.md). The regrouping is performed by the algebraic tail annihilator (1), not by defining W_cut to be a difference. Separate cluster cutoffs can destroy the Fourier support argument and create side prisms; their individual period values are not asserted to cancel. The whole current has the explicit pole-free representative (3). After the valid head-Hardy forest contraction, the head kernel is a finite Laurent polynomial. Its complete head Cauchy integral is independent of ALL finite nonzero head radii. The head radii can be chosen fixed, independently of t, and there are no atomic-pole residues when changing them. Positive factorial monomials, Gaussian coefficients and all original cap factors remain explicit. ## 3. Keep full Psi and resolve the window by one interval On the principal logarithmic chart put B(s)=Log s/(s-1), B(1)=1, K_N(s)=N B(s) integral_0^1 exp(Nu Log s)du. (4) The right side is exactly (s^N-1)/(s-1). Near ANY compact cluster s_j=1, choose Log_j 1=0 for each atom. Then every B(s_j) is holomorphic and nonzero. All dependent-cluster source densities are regular. The interval endpoints, original factors N and every logarithmic mark are retained. At other logarithmic sheets of s=1, do not separate a compensating pole and zero; use the polynomial or its selected local chart instead. Thus (3)--(4) give a full-Psi/continuous-Gaussian period with a fixed interval per atom and the original fixed cap intervals if desired. It has no atomic Cauchy poles and no finite matrix source. Its number of integration variables depends on the word, not on N. For absolute convergence use the principal-log estimate already proved for cap intervals: |B(s)|<=C(1+|log|s||)exp(-max(0,log|s|)). On any fixed compact u-path in 0<=Re u<=1, this bounds the interval density in (4) by C N(1+|log|s||)exp(d max(0,log|s|)+C_path N). (5) Choose arbitrary fixed head radii. The explicit Gaussian coefficients of A_j have logarithmic moduli at most C(1+sum|xi|). On a radial moment piece t_j=-r_j, (5) is therefore bounded by a polynomial in 1+sum|xi|+sum|log r_j| times N^B exp(CN(1+sum|xi|)) product_radial r_j^(-d). The exact full-Psi ray measure has modulus sqrt(1+r_j)r_j^(N-1)dr_j/(2*pi). Its power cancels r_j^(-d) because d=N-1. The remaining logarithms are integrable at zero; the continuous Gaussian dominates exp(CN sum|xi|). Fixed outer circles are compact. This proves joint absolute convergence of the new interval source directly, with fixed head radii. No divergent high-tail integral is evaluated in this new chamber: tail cancellation was proved first in the original common chamber. The source logarithm seams are explicit relative interval derivatives. For L->L+2*pi*i the difference of the two densities N L e^(NuL)/(e^L-1) is d_u{[e^(Nu(L+2*pi*i))-e^(NuL)]/(e^L-1)}. Its primitive vanishes at u=0 and u=1. Thus angular seams do not create an omitted source period. Full-Psi moment-circle endpoints and their paired radial ends still match by the original full-function monodromy. All these matches can also be checked by integrating the interval first, which recovers the single-valued polynomial K_N. ## 4. The joint interior critical scheme is the actual geometric scheme Write T_j=Log t_j and U_j=2*pi*i*u_j. On a chosen local sheet the window logarithm is L_j=Log A_j-T_j-2*pi*i*n_j, n_j in Z. On a recorded full-Psi leading-phase cell, including its exact integer monodromy expansion, the extended phase contains W_ext=sum_j [epsilon_j Li_2(e^T_j)+U_j L_j +2*pi*i*m_j T_j] +original Gaussian, reflected and cap phase. (6) Each m_j is its retained integer ray/monodromy mark. The full-function symbol is applied only where its stated uniform phase is valid; dilogarithmic divisors such as t=1 require separate treatment. At an interior joint critical point, T_j=Log A_j-2*pi*i*n_j, U_j=2*pi*i*m_j-epsilon_j Log(1-A_j). (7) The normal Hessian in (T_j,U_j) is [ epsilon_j A_j/(1-A_j) -1 ] [ -1 0 ], with determinant -1. It is independent of ALL incidence ranks and circuits. The normal blocks are independent over the external head, Gaussian and cap variables. Thus every regular compact Cauchy cluster is resolved by nondegenerate normal pairs, not an unresolved meromorphic intersection. Eliminating (T,U) in (6) yields exactly the actual nine-atom action with its original integer logarithmic marks. The extra constants from n_j are real phase constants. Its full critical equations are the original Hurwitz/cap representation equations, and its critical regulator satisfies [the proved sharp representation-volume bound](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md). The factor B(1)=1 and determinant -1 give a nonzero LOCAL normal density. They do not determine the original global normal/thimble cycle coefficient. For a positive oriented shape epsilon_j Im A_j>0 on its ordinary half-plane branch, with m_j=0, (7) gives 0<Re u_j<1/2. Thus its normal interval point lies strictly inside the actual allowed vertical strip; an endpoint-fixed compact complex interval path can pass through it while preserving (5). This is an allowed source-path statement, not a noncancellation proof. The product source cycle is maximal totally real on a regular phase chart: order its coordinates (T,Gaussian,U,cap,head Z), and the real parameters by their moment/Gaussian/interval paths and head angles. The complex Jacobian is block triangular with nonzero path derivatives and iI on the head angles. Thus interior stationarity of the complex phase is full holomorphic stationarity here. This is not merely a stationary real-part envelope. ## 5. Atomic interval endpoints cannot be finite regular stationary points At u_j=e in {0,1}, the derivative in U_j is omitted, but T_j is still a free regular moment coordinate. Stationarity in all the remaining complex directions forces -epsilon_j Log(1-e^T_j)-2*pi*i*e+2*pi*i*m_j=0. Exponentiating gives 1-e^T_j=1, so t_j=0. There is NO finite nonzero regular endpoint stationary point. The same applies to simultaneous atomic endpoints. A constrained boundary maximum without the other stationarity equations is not covered. The original CAP interval endpoints are different: they give central physical meridians and value zero under the separately proved regular endpoint theorem. Moment outer endpoints are matched parts of one full-Psi relative cycle, not independent new boundaries. Log seams are matched by the relative derivative above. True zero ends, phase singularities and escape in later contour deformations still need their recorded estimates or further source analysis. ## 6. The actual interval variables have a radial Legendre/flow interpretation The new variables also make the proposed flow/Rivin structure explicit on a stated positive chamber. Use the unshifted marks m_j=0 and set T_j=sigma_j+i*vartheta_j, U_j=2*pi*i*u_j, V=rho+i*theta, Log A_j=a_j.V+i*pi*nu_j. V contains the head and the transformed Gaussian logarithms. The original cap variables are likewise purely imaginary multiples of their real interval parameters in this calculation. All remaining quadratic coefficients are real. Consequently the WHOLE imaginary action has the form Im W_ext=sum_j [epsilon_j Im Li_2(exp T_j) -2*pi*u_j*sigma_j] +rho dot F(theta,u,cap), (8) where F is the original affine head/Gaussian flow expression. More explicitly its atomic part is 2*pi*sum_j a_j u_j; the original real quadratic, reflected, sign and cap terms supply the remaining affine terms. Thus minimizing over the unrestricted rho gives a finite value exactly when F=0. These are linear equations, not additional guessed geometric constraints. Equivalently they follow by differentiating the imaginary action in the head/Gaussian radial variables. This is an identity for the LEADING phase W_ext. Exact q half-steps and d=N-1 rather than N remain in the recorded finite-N amplitude; it is not an equality for the full finite-N logarithm of the density. The unrestricted radial minimization is in the complexified coordinate space. The original real Gaussian path has eta_s=sqrt(pi)(1+i*s)xi_s, so its real and imaginary parts are linked; it does not already supply that independent radial polarization. For one atom assume epsilon*vartheta in (0,pi). Put alpha=epsilon*vartheta, beta=2*pi*u, gamma=pi-alpha-beta. If alpha,beta,gamma are all positive, the radial expression f(sigma)=epsilon Im Li_2(exp(sigma+i*vartheta))-beta*sigma has derivative -epsilon Arg(1-t)-beta and strictly positive second derivative epsilon Im(t)/|1-t|^2. Its derivative tends to -beta at minus infinity and gamma at plus infinity. There is a unique global minimum, at exp(sigma)=sin(beta)/sin(gamma). At this minimum -epsilon Arg(1-t)=beta, so EXACTLY min_sigma f=epsilon D(t) =Lambda(alpha)+Lambda(beta)+Lambda(gamma). (9) Combining (8)--(9) on F=0 gives the sum of the positive tetrahedral volumes, OFF criticality in the remaining angular variables. The actual interval coordinate u is therefore beta/(2*pi). The imaginary parts of the other normal equations impose the affine angle matching vartheta_j=a_j.theta+pi*nu_j-2*pi*n_j. On any fixed marked chamber, these and F=0 are the actual linear angle/flow constraints; positivity cuts out a convex domain. The usual strict tetrahedral concavity holds on the quotient by directions leaving every angle unchanged. This is an identity for the newly constructed ORIGINAL source, not a newly defined positive model. Its scope is essential: the original signed nine-atom atlas is not known to place its geometric point in one simultaneous positive chamber, and such a choice cannot be assumed from geometricity alone. The previously found indefinite actual-phase Hessian precludes repairing that issue by arbitrary real Gaussian changes. Transport to a positive chart and control of the ORIGINAL interval cycle still require proof. Equations (8)--(9) explain which flow and volume optimization that transport must carry; they do not supply its missing geometric coefficient. ## 7. What has and has not been canceled The compact artificial Cauchy-pole clusters of the total source are removable, including arbitrary dependent circuits. The local L1-pole growth countermodel cannot be applied to the regrouped holomorphic kernel as though its uncanceled denominator were still present. This does not prove that every localized compact nonstationary piece has a sharp exponential bound: artificial cutoffs have side currents, and the new fixed-interval phase has its genuine critical/endpoint geometry. It supplies that geometry explicitly. In particular the normal interval period at fixed A is EXACTLY the original finite v_(epsilon,N)(A); its global normal-cycle coefficient cannot be read off from the local Hessian. The known coefficient-one atom region in [the full Euler-region theorem](full_euler_atom_dilog_and_endpoint_regions.md) is an anchor, not an assertion about every positive shape. What remains includes source-compatible analysis of the zero ends and dilogarithmic degenerations, and a nonzero selected geometric lower bound. The exact pole-free representative and normal resolution remove a specific obstruction to those steps; they do not constitute the broad volume conjecture by themselves.

title: The Fourier rank conditions follow from knot-exterior homology
text: # The Fourier rank conditions follow from knot-exterior homology Research note, 25 October 2026. This supplies a uniform independent proof of the two rank conditions in `singular_faces_and_six_two.md`. It applies to every globally branched oriented ideal triangulation of a knot exterior in S^3. No geometricity, quantum-invariant existence theorem, or finite census assertion is used. ## 1. Statement Let X be the ideal compactification of an oriented one-cusped manifold M, with its single ideal vertex. Assume H^1(X;R)=0. For ordered face pairings put D=X_0-X_1+X_2, R=X_2-X_3, E=diag(epsilon). **Theorem.** Rank D=N. For any basis F of ker D, set T=E R F, U=X_0 F, K=basis of ker T, P=basis of im T, C=K^T U^T P. Then rank C=dim ker T. Thus the Fourier reduction of the existing charged tensor always has a well-defined convergent residual integral. The full stacked face matrix [D;R] can still be singular. For knot exteriors in S^3 the cohomology assumption is automatic, as proved in Section 4. The theorem is also valid whenever the stated ideal-compactification cohomology vanishes. ## 2. A local relation is exactly an ideal edge cocycle Introduce three numbers (a,b,c) in an ordered tetrahedron of sign epsilon. Define four local momentum coefficients and four position coefficients p=(b,b+c,c,c), q=(a,-a,a+epsilon*b,-epsilon*b). (2.1) Suppose across every glued face pair i,j they satisfy p_(t,i)=p_(u,j), q_(t,i)+q_(u,j)=0. (2.2) The vector space of such relations is naturally isomorphic to the space of cellular real 1-cocycles on the ideal triangulation X. **Proof.** In one tetrahedron give its vertices potentials n_0=0, n_1=c, n_2=b+c, n_3=b+c+epsilon*a. For the face opposite i, list its three vertices as u<v<w and let omega_i=epsilon*(-1)^i. Direct substitution gives p_i=n_v-n_u, q_i=omega_i*(n_w-n_v). (2.3) The same face has opposite omega on its two occurrences. Because face gluings preserve the three-vertex order, (2.2) is exactly equality of the two independent vertex differences on that face. Consequently all local differences lambda_ij=n_j-n_i descend to a single number on each global oriented edge. They sum to zero around every triangular face, so define a cellular edge cocycle. Conversely, a global edge cocycle is locally a gradient on each tetrahedron: set n_0=0 and n_i=lambda_0i. The triangular cocycle relations give every other edge difference. Then recover c=n_1-n_0, b=n_2-n_1, a=epsilon*(n_3-n_2). Equations (2.3) prove the face matching conditions. The constructions are inverse. This proves the claimed isomorphism, including injectivity. There is only one ideal vertex, so the cellular coboundary map from 0-cochains to 1-cochains is zero. Hence H^1(X;R)=0 says that the cocycle space itself is zero. All relations (2.1)--(2.2) must therefore vanish. ## 3. Applying the local lemma to the matrices First, if D^T a=0, use (2.1) with b=c=0 in every tetrahedron. Its position coefficients match because their paired sums are exactly D^T a; the momentum coefficients are zero. The lemma forces a=0. Thus D has full row rank N. Next suppose C has a nonzero left-null vector z. The corresponding global face assignment k=F K z obeys Dk=0, Rk=0. Let b=X_0 k. Since P spans E R(ker D), the condition z^T C=0 is b^T E R F=0. Therefore R^T E b annihilates ker D and is in im D^T. Choose a with D^T a+R^T E b=0. (3.1) Set c=X_2 k. The equations Dk=Rk=0 say that the four occurrences of k in a tetrahedron are (b,b+c,c,c), exactly the momentum coefficients in (2.1). They match on paired faces since k is a global face assignment. The local position coefficients in (2.1) sum over faces to the left side of (3.1). Thus they match as well. The lemma forces a=b=c=0, hence k=0. Since F K has independent columns, z=0, a contradiction. C has full row rank as asserted. This argument uses only real finite-dimensional linear algebra and the explicit cocycle lemma. In particular it does not infer convergence from a general TQFT theorem with an unaudited analytic proof. ## 4. Why the cohomology vanishes for knot exteriors Let M be the compact exterior of a knot in S^3. Its ideal compactification is M with its connected boundary torus collapsed to one point. Thus H^1(X;R)=H^1(M,boundary M;R). In the cohomology exact sequence of this pair, H^0(M)->H^0(boundary M) is an isomorphism. Hence H^1(M,boundary M) injects into H^1(M), with image the kernel of restriction to H^1(boundary M). Mayer--Vietoris for S^3=M union a solid torus gives H_1(M;Z)=Z and shows that the boundary meridian maps to its generator. For example H_1(boundary M)->H_1(M) direct-sum H_1(solid torus) is an isomorphism; the meridian is zero in the solid torus, and the other boundary generator generates its H_1. The meridian therefore generates H_1(M). Restriction H^1(M)->H^1(boundary M) is injective, so its kernel and H^1(M,boundary M) vanish. This proves the required hypothesis. ## 5. Consequence and the remaining distinction The full-tensor volume theorem in `singular_faces_and_six_two.md` now applies to **every globally branched complete positive geometric ideal triangulation of a knot exterior in S^3**. Its Fourier rank assumptions have a uniform topological proof, rather than being additional census conditions. The independent geometry-to-saddle and analytic proofs remain necessary and are supplied in that note. This is still a statement about the full charged tensor at complete angles. A knot quantum A-state additionally needs its specified boundary fiber, phase, normalization, and peripheral identification. The general preferred-longitude/fiber construction and equivalence of arbitrary realizations are not consequences of the rank theorem alone. For 6_2 these are supplied by the separate finite certificates. The subsequent `preferred_longitude_cochains.md` supplies the uniform preferred-longitude relation. The ordinary-fiber construction and then `fourier_boundary_state.md` supply the normalized meridian state for both possible boundary ranks, preserving the complete geometric volume limit. Geometric realization and global triangulation identification are still separate obligations. The subsequent `preferred_longitude_cochains.md` now gives the uniform preferred-longitude relation. `general_boundary_state_and_framing.md` constructs the meridian state whenever the longitude increases the B rank, with an exact correction for any rational longitude shear. The other boundary-rank case remains separate. There is also no assertion here that every ideal triangulation admits a global branching or that every hyperbolic alternating knot has the required positive geometric realization of the chosen combinatorics. Those are separate uniform construction questions. The script `reduce_singular_faces.py` checks (2.3) symbolically and recomputes the ideal edge-cocycle matrix in each finite example. As a useful boundary check, the two-component word RLRLRL has a nonzero cocycle and local-relation space; the one-vertex hypothesis should not be dropped without a replacement argument.

title: Exact deck characters of the original four-function crossing
text: # Exact deck characters of the original four-function crossing 28 October 2026. The exact balanced Fourier crossing has a specified continuation away from its sampling grids. Its four full-turn characters are explicit rational functions of the central coordinates. They compute the logarithmic seams in a contour deformation of the original period. A function that is periodic at the original grid need not remain periodic between the grid points. This calculation uses the full function, its Gaussian and every affine logarithmic mark. It does not infer a geometric cycle from a rational character or identify the central variety below with the knot A-curve. ## 1. The fixed continuation and its four characters Use the EXACT kernel (14) of [the balanced crossing theorem](actual_balanced_fourier_crossing_kernel.md). Put h=2*pi*i/N, t=2*pi*i, X=pi*i-h/2, x=exp(X), s=x^N, and retain the port logarithms a,b,c,d. In particular s=(-1)^(N+1). Let A=exp(Na), B=exp(Nb), C=exp(Nc), D=exp(Nd), beta=b-a-X, f=d-c-X, rho=c-a, lambda=d-b+t, G=d-a-X, H=b-c+X, E=N f+(N+1)lambda/2+(G H+lambda^2/2)/h. The full continuation is M=constant * (C/A)(1-C/A)^2 exp(E) *Psi(beta)Psi(h-f)Psi(lambda+t+h)/Psi(rho). (1) The constant includes the original kappa*zeta_0^2/N. The old central parameters are used as the values of these exponentials, rather than replacing exp(Nrho) by a new independent constant off the grid. For a full positive turn of the indicated port, the exact ratios are M(a+t,b,c,d)/M = mu_a = s C(A-sB)/[B(A-C)], M(a,b+t,c,d)/M = mu_b = s(D-B)/(A-sB), M(a,b,c+t,d)/M = mu_c = s(A-C)/(D-sC), M(a,b,c,d+t)/M = mu_d = s B(D-sC)/[C(D-B)]. (2) These are meromorphic identities on the retained logarithmic cover; the displayed quotients are first interpreted where all factors are regular. No imaginary part is reset to a principal argument. Proof: the full function obeys Psi(z+t)/Psi(z)=1/(1-exp(Nz)), Psi(z-t)/Psi(z)=1-exp(Nz). The four exponential arguments in (1) have central values U=sB/A, V=sC/D, W=D/B, R=C/A. The Gaussian factors exp(Delta E), for turns in a,b,c,d respectively, are sC/B, -U, sA/D, -sD/C. (3) For example a turn in b has Delta E=-(N+1)t/2+N G-N lambda+Nt/2 =-t/2+N(beta-t), so its factor is -U, including the half-turn sign. Combining (3) with the four full-function multipliers gives (2). Thus neither a Gaussian phase nor a complete-color sign was dropped. ## 2. Balanced grids and their off-grid seams On the local sampling multisection C=sB, D=sA all four characters equal one. More precisely, mu_a-1 = A(sC-B)/[B(A-C)], mu_b-1 = (sD-A)/(A-sB), mu_c-1 = (sA-D)/(D-sC), mu_d-1 = D(sB-C)/[C(D-B)]. (4) Hence, on this regular chart, the simultaneous unit-character locus is EXACTLY C=sB, D=sA. The converse follows from the first two numerators, since A,B are nonzero. The other two equations are redundant. Also mu_a mu_b mu_c mu_d=1. (5) This is the common-scale symmetry, not four independent gluing equations. All four shifts commute because the characters depend only on A,B,C,D, which are invariant under full logarithmic turns. For example, start with a balanced grid (A0,B,C,D), C=sB and D=sA0, and vary only its a-port away from A=A0. Then mu_a=1 still, but mu_b-1=(A0-A)/(A-sB), mu_c-1=s(A-A0)/(D-sC). The other ports acquire seams. Periodicity in the moved port alone therefore does not justify a simultaneous closed-torus deformation. These formulas locate the exact central differences that recur in the [wire-current calculation](whole_fermat_toric_residue_and_wire_source.md). ## 3. Sewn characters and the limitation of grid periodicity For an internal variable shared by two original crossing ports, the full-turn ratio of the product is the product of its two characters from (2), with the orientations and negative-crossing conjugate transport retained. The rational boundary co-source is single-valued in that variable; it adds no logarithmic multiplier. Thus the sewn scalar form has a directly computable rational deck character nu_e. On the propagated balanced central multisection, nu_e=1 because each incident local character is one. Off that multisection, imposing nu_e=1 is a NONTRIVIAL equation, not a consequence of the Fourier frame change. A logarithmic branch lip contributes a multiple of (nu_e-1) times the complete kernel. Such a lip cannot be omitted on the grounds that its value at the root grid is zero. In particular, zeros on the grid may cancel the grid denominator and leave a regular but nonzero relative source term. The exact Newton/Rogers examples in the linked wire note exhibit that mechanism. The open-braid frame theorem now removes all interior frame adapters, but it does not remove the logarithmic seams of this off-grid full continuation. The characters (2) specify those seams without an unspecified torsor multiplier. Geometric selection still requires an actual relative-period transformation, with these terms retained. ## 4. Verification [The independent finite-product audit](../experiments/audit_balanced_crossing_deck_characters.py) computes Psi from its rational product and dilogarithm definition, then checks every full-turn ratio at both parities, without applying the shift law in the evaluator. Symbolic checks verify (4), (5), and the unit-character locus. These checks supplement the uniform calculation (2)--(3); they are not a knot volume test.

title: The balanced Verma crossing is a coherent-source exponential
text: # The balanced Verma crossing is a coherent-source exponential Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual balanced factorial lattice has a completed highest-weight model whose block shift and divided F-power are a literal Weyl pair. This note evaluates the universal crossing on that model. Its root resonance is an exact exponential; on coherent kernels it gives finite E-semicyclic crossings with changing source parameters. Their selected one-cut operator is exactly the original one, including its full meridian normalization. The Burau transport and the Verma/Alexander root period were already proved in [the earlier Verma note](frobenius_verma_period.md), and an F-semicyclic crossing in [the carry-braiding note](semicyclic_carry_braiding.md). Those are not new conclusions here. The new comparison is the balanced normal-source/Fock kernel, its evaluated cyclotomic pole, and its relation to those existing objects. This source base remains triangular/reducible. It is not the geometric A-curve or a volume proof. [Independent proof audit](balanced_verma_coherent_braiding_independent_audit.md). ## 1. The actual balanced infinite lattice Initially q,M are generic, Q=q^2, x=-M/q and rho=q-q^(-1). On a free basis w_a, a>=0, put K w_a=x Q^(-a) w_a, Ecal w_a=(M Q^(-a)-M^(-1)) w_(a-1), a>=1, Ecal w_0=0, F w_a=(1-Q^(a+1)) w_(a+1), Ecal=rho^2 E. The adjacent-entry subtraction gives [Ecal,F]=rho(K-K^(-1)); the two weight equations are immediate. Thus this is a genuine generic quantum-group module. Its root head 0<=a<N is exactly the original balanced finite color. The [common-Verma source note](common_verma_two_wall_source.md) gives its two boundary walls and normal extension; the construction below can also be checked directly from the displayed matrices. Remove only the common Cartan scalar q^(H_1 H_2/2) at w_00, retaining it as the same marked external line as in the original crossing. The remaining Cartan diagonal on a pair of colors is D w_(a,b)=x_2^(-a)x_1^(-b)Q^(ab) w_(a,b). The uncheck universal crossing is D R_0, with R_0=sum_(k>=0) (-1)^k q^(k^2) Ecal_1^k tensor F_2^k/(Q;Q)_k =P_Q(q Ecal_1 F_2). (1) The sum terminates on every fixed input. It is regular at every prescribed q_N=exp(pi*i/N), including on tail blocks. Indeed its entry from (a,b) to (a-k,b+k), 0<=k<=a, is exactly (-1)^k q^(k^2) {b+k choose k}_Q product_(j=a-k+1)^a (M_1 Q^(-j)-M_1^(-1)). (2) The Gaussian coefficient is a polynomial. This cancellation is essential before root specialization. In particular the terms k>=N do not in general vanish in the infinite root module. ## 2. Root blocks, the Weyl pair, and the two integral lattices Fix q=q_N, write gamma=(-1)^(N+1), kappa_i=M_i-M_i^(-1), and kappa_(i,N)=M_i^N-M_i^(-N). Split a=rN+a_bar, 0<=a_bar<N. On the product completion over the block index, let B be the backward block shift. Periodicity of the literal coefficients gives Ecal=Ecal_head tensor I+kappa W tensor B, F=F_head tensor I, K=K_head tensor I, W=E_(N-1,0), Ecal^N=gamma kappa_N B. (3) The divided operator, formed before specializing, is T=[F^N/(Q;Q)_N]_root. Its action from block r to block r+1 is r+1, because {(r+1)N+a_bar choose N}_Q tends to r+1. Thus [B,T]=I. In the Fock realization h_a tensor t^r/r!, B=partial_t and T=t. The coherent kernel is theta_s(h_a)=h_a exp(s t), B theta_s=s theta_s, T theta_s=partial_s theta_s, pi_0 theta_s=I. (4) It embeds the finite source module with Ecal_s=Ecal_head+kappa s W, F_s=F_head, K_s=K_head. Formula (4) is a kernel identity: replacing B,T by s,partial_s as an algebra homomorphism would reverse their commutator. The earlier unbalanced Verma lattice has Fv_a=v_(a+1). Generically w_a=v_a/(Q;Q)_a is a diagonal change of basis; on blocks a>=N it has root poles. The two root modules therefore have different central powers and cannot be identified by a regular root-fiber basis change. On each fixed total-position sector the generic matrices are conjugate, and their diagonal traces coincide as regular whole functions. This preserves the earlier graded Verma/Alexander period while retaining the singular factorial lattice, rather than identifying its two special fibers. ## 3. The whole crossing's resonant exponential Use log P_Q(Z)=-sum_(m>=1)Z^m/[m(1-Q^m)], with Z=q Ecal_1 F_2. On each total-position sector all sums terminate. Since F^N=(1-Q^N)N T+O((1-Q^N)^2), terms m>=N not divisible by N vanish at the root. For m=jN, j>=2, the numerator has j vanishing factors and the denominator only one; these vanish as well. The sole additional logarithm term is m=N: -q_N^N Ecal_1^N tensor [F_2^N/(1-Q^N)]_root/N =Ecal_1^N tensor T_2. The remaining m<N terms are the logarithm of the finite nilpotent part, since F_head^N=0. Consequently R_0,root=exp(gamma kappa_(1,N) B_1 T_2) R_0,<N. (5) The two factors commute: B_1 commutes with Ecal_1, and T_2 commutes with F_2, as follows also from their generic definitions. On every fixed total-position sector the exponential terminates. On the product completion its entries are defined sectorwise. This is an exact operator evaluation of the whole quantum factorial's cyclotomic resonance, not an asymptotic truncation. ## 4. Finite coherent crossings and their changing parameters Before applying D, the exponential in (5) sends the kernel pair (s_1,s_2) to (s_1,s_2+gamma kappa_(1,N)s_1). The finite part depends on s_1 but not s_2, so this translation introduces no derivatives of its coefficients. The Cartan block ratio is D_(rN+a,sN+b)/D_(a,b)=x_2^(-Nr)x_1^(-Ns). It therefore rescales the two coherent parameters. The complete uncheck parameter map is (s_1,s_2) -> (x_2^(-N)s_1, x_1^(-N)(s_2+gamma kappa_(1,N)s_1)). (6) The finite matrix from the source to this target is exactly R_s=D_head sum_(k=0)^(N-1) (-1)^k q_N^(k^2) Ecal_(1,s_1)^k F_(2,head)^k/(Q;Q)_k. (7) Equations (5)--(6) prove that (7) is the restriction of the regular infinite crossing to its coherent kernels. It intertwines the genuine root quantum-group actions in those changing fibers. The marked common Cartan scalar remains the original one. For equal knot colors put chi=x^N=gamma M^N and t=M^(-2N)=chi^(-2). After the checked flip the source map is L_+(chi)=[[1-chi^(-2),chi^(-1)],[chi^(-1),0]]. (8) Its inverse is L_-=[[0,chi],[chi,1-chi^2]]. These are exactly the earlier Frobenius Verma block matrices. Positive and negative coherent finite crossings are literal inverses with the intermediate parameters updated. The positive finite matrix is flip times (7). For the inverse, first flip and apply D_head^(-1), then use the finite inverse series sum_(k<N)q_N^k Ecal_(1,s_1)^k F_2^k/(Q;Q)_k, where s_1 is the recovered original source parameter. The infinite crossing satisfies the braid equation on finite total-position sectors as a generic polynomial identity. Its regular root specialization does also. Restricting to the coherent kernels proves the finite changing-source braid equation with scalar one. No unrelated normalization root is chosen in this argument. This agrees with, rather than enlarges without proof, the semicyclic coherence already established in the older F chart. ## 5. The exact original selected cut, including a boundary blowup Every L_+ and L_- fixes the line s_j=chi^(1-j)s. On this line the coherent crossings are endomorphisms of one ordered tensor module. Their finite coefficients are polynomial in the source parameters. An Ecal wrap raises integer residue position by N-1 instead of lowering it by one; a term containing r wraps therefore raises total position by rN relative to the ordinary crossing. F_head has no wrap. The same statement holds for the inverse finite series and every braid word, with the parameters transported. In the original pivotal partial trace over b-1 strands, closed indices equal their input indices. A positive-degree source term would then raise the remaining cut index by at least N, impossible in a space with indices 0,...,N-1. Hence the entire one-cut matrix is source independent: C_beta(M;s_1,...,s_b)=C_beta(M;0,...,0). (9) In particular it has exactly the original reduced ADO value and Kashaev specialization. This is an equality of cut operators; the prescribed pivot, zero-framing scalar and whole external d_N(M) line are retained. No extra cyclic invariant is substituted. There is a useful regular boundary chart. Write mu_j=kappa s_j, and use Ecal_mu=Ecal_head+mu W in (7). The source map (8) is linear in mu as well, and all its matrix entries are regular in M. Thus (9) extends to M=1 with mu fixed, even though s=mu/kappa is singular there. The central power is Ecal_mu^N=gamma u_N(M)mu, u_N=kappa_N/kappa, u_N(1)=N. (10) This distinguishes the regular mu chart from setting kappa=0 while keeping s finite, which would erase the cyclic source. Equality of the selected cut continues through this boundary because it is a polynomial whole identity, not because a singular coherent kernel was evaluated independently. ## 6. What this does and does not add to the A-torsor route The actual factorial lattice, divided normal power, coherent source, and semicyclic crossing now belong to one explicitly compared object. The source-period exponential in (5) is fixed by the whole function; its group action has the Weyl/regular-centralizer realization proved in the common-Verma note. The source independence (9) and exact normal factor (10) retain the original selected knot value. The earlier unbalanced Verma trace still supplies the full factor Delta_K(M^(2N)); its cancellation at completeness is a whole-germ statement, not permission to drop the Alexander divisor. This note does not replace the already proved graded trace identity. The base transport (8) is triangular/reducible holonomy. Even on the nonzero exceptional mu chart, F^N=0 and all root-center meridians stay in the same Borel. This does not identify the source base with the irreducible geometric A-curve. Nor does an exact coherent kernel prove which geometric stationary period survives the original contraction or give its archimedean norm. The global geometric source and regulator comparison remains open. For literature coverage only, [Baseilhac, 1101.3440](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.3440) explicitly treats root quantum-group representations through quantum coadjoint action and Heisenberg doubles, with odd-order roots in its stated scope. [Negron, 2311.13797](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.13797) states a quantum-Frobenius tensor-category framework at roots of arbitrary order. These prevent a novelty claim for the broad representation-theoretic framework. No theorem from either paper is a proof premise of the finite matrix and kernel identities here. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_balanced_verma_coherent_braiding.py) and [results](../experiments/balanced_verma_coherent_braiding_results.json) compare the polynomial Gaussian crossing with (5), coherent kernels, changing-source inverses, and braid equations at even and composite levels. They support the uniform proofs above, not a volume claim.

title: Independent audit of balanced Verma coherent braiding
text: # Independent audit of balanced Verma coherent braiding Audit, 27 October 2026. I checked [the balanced Verma proof](balanced_verma_coherent_braiding.md) against the displayed actual coefficients, the earlier [Verma period](frobenius_verma_period.md), and the [F-semicyclic chart](semicyclic_carry_braiding.md). The proof is sound as stated. No additional matrix test was needed, and no geometric-source or volume conclusion is inferred. ## 1. The lattice, divided shift, and exact resonance Substituting \(\mathcal E=\rho^2E\) into the original Euler coefficient gives \[ q^{k(k-1)/2}\frac{\rho^k}{[k]_q!}\rho^{-2k} =\frac{(-1)^kq^{k^2}}{(Q;Q)_k}, \] because \((1-Q)/\rho=-q\). The displayed balanced crossing entry follows by multiplying the \(E\)-arrows and canceling the \(F\)-product against \((Q;Q)_k\). Its Gaussian coefficient is polynomial, so the root specialization is regular on each finite total-position sector, including transfers \(k\ge N\). On root blocks, the literal \(E\)-wrap is \(\kappa B\), while the \(F\)-edge at every block boundary is zero. The full \(E\)-cycle is \[ \mathcal E^N=(-1)^{N+1}\kappa_N B. \] The canceled coefficient of \(F^N/(Q;Q)_N\) is \(\binom{(r+1)N+\bar a}{N}_Q=r+1\). Thus \(B=\partial_t,\ T=t\) on \(t^r/r!\), with \([B,T]=1\). The coherent kernel has the stated \(B\)-eigenvalue and \(T\)-derivative identities. Those are kernel identities, not a commutator-preserving substitution \(B\mapsto s,T\mapsto\partial_s\). For the logarithm of \(P_Q(q\mathcal E_1F_2)\), the only extra surviving term is the resonance \(m=N\): \[ -\frac{q_N^N}{N}\mathcal E_1^N \otimes\left[\frac{F_2^N}{1-Q^N}\right]_{\rm root} =\mathcal E_1^N\otimes T_2. \] Here \(q_N^N=-1\) at every level. For \(m=jN\), \(j\ge2\), the numerator has \(j\) vanishing factors and the denominator one; nonresonant \(m>N\) has a vanishing numerator and a unit denominator. The low-degree part is the logarithm of the nilpotent finite factorial. Since \(T_2\) commutes with \(F_2\), it commutes with the resonance. Exponentiating therefore proves the exact factorization, with its sign. All operations are finite on each total-position sector; the stated product completion is defined sectorwise. ## 2. Changing centers and the inverse The resonance translates \[ (s_1,s_2)\mapsto (s_1,s_2+(-1)^{N+1}\kappa_{1,N}s_1). \] Its finite head coefficient depends on \(s_1\), not \(s_2\), so no derivative of that coefficient is lost. The Cartan block ratio is exactly \(x_2^{-Nr}x_1^{-Ns}\); its \(Q\)-powers are full \(N\)-cycles. It rescales the coherent parameters exactly as in the note. For equal colors, with \(\chi=x^N=(-1)^{N+1}M^N\), \[ (-1)^{N+1}\kappa_N=\chi-\chi^{-1}. \] After the checked flip this gives \[ L_+= \begin{pmatrix}1-\chi^{-2}&\chi^{-1}\\ \chi^{-1}&0\end{pmatrix}, \quad L_-= \begin{pmatrix}0&\chi\\ \chi&1-\chi^2\end{pmatrix}. \] They are literal inverses and fix the stated ordered line. The inverse finite Euler coefficient is \(q_N^k/(Q;Q)_k\); it has no additional \((-1)^k\). The recovered original source parameter must be used after the flip and inverse Cartan, as the proof does. The regular infinite braid identity restricts through injective coherent kernels, whose head projection is the identity. This proves scalar-one changing-source coherence. It does not identify the new E-semicyclic chart with the older F-semicyclic chart; their positive center transports are oppositely oriented, consistently with their formulas. ## 3. Source independence of the whole original cut In every finite positive crossing, an \(E\)-wrap raises integer residue position by \(N-1\) in place of a lowering by one. Its net change from the ordinary crossing is therefore \(+N\). The \(F\)-factor has no wrap. The negative inverse uses the same \(E\)- and head-\(F\) arrows, so it has the same nonnegative wrap-degree rule. Flips and Cartan/pivotal factors do not change this degree. After tracing \(b-1\) strands, a term with \(r\) wraps would have cut change \(rN\). The open index range is \(0,\ldots,N-1\), forcing \(r=0\) and equal cut endpoints. Thus the entire cut matrix, not only a trace, agrees with the original nilpotent one. The argument keeps the full pivot, zero-framing scalar and external \(d_N(M)\) line. On the fixed source line this is a genuine endomorphism evaluation. Before source closure, the same degree argument remains a coordinate-matrix contraction; it does not define a new topological invariant. ## 4. The boundary extension and earlier Verma period Replacing \(\kappa s\) by the independent \(\mu\) makes every finite crossing coefficient polynomial in \(\mu\). The center transport remains regular and linear for equal colors. The selected-cut identity holds for \(\kappa\ne0\), hence extends as a whole polynomial identity to \(M=1\), with \(\mu\) fixed. The cycle product is exactly \[ \mathcal E_\mu^N =(-1)^{N+1}u_N(M)\mu, \quad u_N(1)=N. \] No singular coherent kernel with \(s=\mu/\kappa\) is evaluated separately at the boundary. Finally, the generic factorial basis change has poles on the tail root blocks. It cannot identify the two root infinite modules. It does preserve diagonal entries on every finite total-position sector as generic whole identities, which continue to the root. This is compatible with the earlier graded Verma trace and its full Alexander divisor. The finite coherent cut is a different selected contraction, and the proof does not delete that divisor or replace the earlier period formula. The resulting source centers remain triangular/reducible. The proof therefore supplies an exact coherent source realization of the actual cut, with the regular boundary chart, but no irreducible geometric A-component or selected volume asymptotic.

title: Coverage check for the belt-stack filling route
text: # Coverage check for the belt-stack filling route 29 October 2026. This is a check of stated scope in primary sources, not an audit or use of their proofs. No novelty claim follows from this limited search. * Roland van der Veen, [Proof of the volume conjecture for Whitehead chains](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0611181v2), states a volume-conjecture result for an infinite link family containing the Whitehead link and Borromean rings. The complete belt stacks may be covered by this family. An exact tangle/peripheral dictionary remains necessary before claiming either inclusion or a new topological class. * Dionne Ibarra, Emma N. McQuire and Jessica S. Purcell, [Augmented links, shadow links, and the TV volume conjecture: a geometric perspective](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09296v1), describe an isometry between octahedral fully augmented link exteriors and fundamental shadow-link exteriors. Their abstract states a Turaev--Viro volume result for the case without half-twists. An isometry of exteriors does not itself identify our marked original quantum source, its root convention or its filling kernel. * Ce Shen, [The Chen--Yang volume conjecture for long integral fillings of fundamental shadow links](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11839v3), states a theorem for sufficiently long integral fillings of any fixed marked fundamental shadow-link exterior, allowing mixed signs and unrelated magnitudes. Its stated invariant is SO(3) Turaev--Viro on odd levels, with a further signed WRT expansion. This directly overlaps the geometric long-filling theme; it does not, by its statement alone, establish our original marked Kashaev source on the full sequence of levels. The present source calculation independently retains the actual ordinary auxiliary-color operators, the full Hermite normal trace, and the original marked closure. Its squared Fourier kernel and global physical-color estimate are proved in [the outer-color theorem](actual_outer_color_squared_kernel.md). That theorem does not claim the deformed source/regulator comparison from a literature theorem, a shared cusp shape or matching volumes. The actual marked comparison is proved separately in the [typed global lift](actual_belt_stack_typed_character_composition.md), and is included in the [full equality assembly](actual_long_filled_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md).

title: The boundary algebra needs its Bloch-period lift
text: # The boundary algebra needs its Bloch-period lift Research note, 25 October 2026. This identifies a structural datum not retained by the boundary algebra alone. The construction is classical; the point here is to state exactly what the proposed quantum period must lift. No identification with algebraic K_3 is used as a proof premise. ## 1. The five-term relation is an algebraic identity Let P(F) be the rational vector space generated by [x], x in F minus {0,1}, with the five-term relations [x]+[y]-[xy] -[x(1-y)/(1-xy)]-[y(1-x)/(1-xy)]=0 (1.1) whenever all terms are defined. Work in F^* tensor Q and set delta[x]=x wedge (1-x). Use the usual oriented-shape identifications [1/x]=-[x] and [1/(1-x)]=[x] as well. Delta respects them rationally by expansion; the discarded signs are torsion. They record vertex reversal and cyclic choice of an opposite edge pair. The map respects (1.1). This can be proved without any dilogarithm: write the formal multiplicative coordinates as additive symbols X=log x,Y=log y,A=log(1-x),B=log(1-y),C=log(1-xy). The five terms of delta are X wedge A+Y wedge B-(X+Y) wedge C -(X+B-C) wedge (A-C)-(Y+A-C) wedge (B-C)=0. (1.2) Expansion proves the equality. The rational Bloch group needed here is B(F)=ker delta. These definitions discard torsion, so they do not silently settle the separate integral or flattening questions. ## 2. A uniform boundary formula Let z_j be the nondegenerate literature shape coordinates of a one-cusped gluing chart, and z_j''=1-z_j^(-1). Use the independently audited edge and marked peripheral matrices. In multiplicative coordinates tensor Q, the edge equations are homogeneous because their fixed signs disappear. The peripheral rows have pairing -2. Then the tetrahedral symbol beta=sum_j[z_j] satisfies delta beta=-(1/2) m wedge l, (2.1) where m,l are the full peripheral monomials in those same conventions. If using independently oriented shape coordinates, insert their orientation signs consistently in both the symplectic form and beta. Here is the linear-algebra proof, avoiding individual triangulations. On the formal shape space use Omega=sum_j du_j wedge dv_j, with u_j=z_j, v_j=z_j'' in the additive notation of F^* tensor Q. The edge Hamiltonian vectors form an isotropic space E of dimension r-1. The homogeneous edge solution space is E^perp; its symplectic quotient is two-dimensional. The Hamiltonian vectors for m,l have pairing -2. On this quotient, Omega_red=-(1/2) dm wedge dl. For example its value on the m and l Hamiltonian vectors is -2, whereas (dm wedge dl) on them is 4. This determines the form; its pullback proves the same identity on E^perp. Alternating bilinearity therefore gives sum_j u_j wedge v_j=-(1/2)m wedge l for coordinates in any Q-vector space, including F^* tensor Q. Finally z wedge z''=z wedge(1-z) in this rational group: the missing sign -1 is torsion and z wedge z^(-1)=0. This proves (2.1). No angle limit or inverse face matrix appears. At completeness m=l=1, so beta lies in B(F). ## 3. Volume is already a regulator evaluation For a complex embedding define D(z)=Im Li_2(z)+log|z| Arg(1-z), with its single-valued continuation. Its differential is dD(z)=log|z| dArg(1-z)-log|1-z| dArg z. (3.1) The bilinear map f wedge g -> log|f| dArg g-log|g| dArg f sends (1.2) to the differential of the corresponding five-term sum of D values. That differential is zero. The nondegenerate complex parameter domain is the complement of finitely many algebraic divisors in C^2, hence connected. On 0<x,y<1 the sum is zero. Thus D obeys (1.1) everywhere by this constant-function argument. Consequently D(beta) is independent of five-term re-presentations. For a complete positive geometric triangulation the oriented ideal tetrahedron volume is D(z_j), so Vol(M)=D(beta). (3.2) This is an exact period evaluation, not a definition via a quantum asymptotic. The logarithmic/Heisenberg refinement also records the complex period and its branch constants. Those constants must remain when comparing exact complex quantum states. For a finite idealized fundamental chain, changing its presentation by the boundary of five decorated vertices produces precisely a five-term relation. The symbol map is therefore the natural way to pass from tetrahedral coordinates to the fundamental-class period. For an explicit check, normalize those vertices to infinity,0,1,a,b and use cross-ratio r(infinity,0,1,z)=z. Their alternating boundary is [a]-[b]+[b/a]-[(1-b)/(1-a)] +[a(1-b)/(b(1-a))]. Putting a=x,b=xy and applying the two oriented-shape identifications turns this into (1.1). Thus this chain relation is coordinate-independent and needs no knot example. We do not infer a global quantum-state identity merely from this classical chain relation. ## 4. Why the unpointed boundary module is too small Equation (2.1) specifies the boundary symbol. Its Steinberg realization splits the corresponding cyclic boundary algebra on the gluing field. The finite edge reduction constructs that splitting module directly. This is the boundary layer of the theory. The choice beta is a *lift* of that boundary symbol. Two lifts with the same boundary can differ by an element of B(F), and their regulator values need not agree. In particular the boundary m=l=1 does not force the volume to vanish. An unpointed splitting of the boundary algebra has forgotten the datum that can carry this period. The candidate intrinsic object must therefore retain (marked boundary Heisenberg algebra, its pointed splitting module, a Bloch/Heisenberg period lift beta). The phrase K_2 versus K_3 describes this degree distinction: the Steinberg symbols belong to the boundary-symbol problem, whereas the Bloch/regulator lift carries the next period datum. No theorem identifying a specific integral Bloch group with K_3 is required for the elementary argument above. ## 5. The quantum comparison target The pointed Steinberg module has an exact algebraic factorization; its multiplicity spaces have a basis-free categorical pentagon. The Heisenberg cover fixes their finite normalization data, and the rational Faddeev identity supplies the continuous dilogarithm period. The missing theorem is a compatible global regulator construction taking the idealized fundamental class to this *pointed period* object, with the literature integration cycle and normalization. It must identify the quantum five-term coherence with the classical period lift, and compare its normalized size across finite levels with (3.2). This is one uniform target. More boundary-matrix examples cannot replace it, and an appeal to Hilbert 90 for the unpointed module alone does not establish it. The subsequent `boundary_regulator_period.md` now supplies the classical parallel boundary section and its invariant norm explicitly: log||P||=2D(beta)/pi. The affine reference term in its primitive is retained. `equivariant_roots_and_phase_descent.md` supplies coherent peripheral root lines and a finite scalar descent theorem, with a relative fundamental-class phase left for calibration. The selected literature period/cycle and its norm comparison across quantum levels remain outstanding.

title: The boundary period line has an exact volume norm
text: # The boundary period line has an exact volume norm Research note, 25 October 2026. This constructs the continuous boundary period and its norm directly from the audited symplectic boundary formula. It is the classical Chern--Simons/regulator framework, not a new quantum definition. No global theorem identifying a published quantum state is assumed. The last section states the exact remaining quantum comparison. Use a nondegenerate one-cusped gluing chart, full peripheral rows with pairing -2, and the oriented tetrahedral Bloch lift beta. Flat real shapes other than 0 and 1 are allowed. All logarithms below live on their matched continuation cover; constants from their branches remain. ## 1. The peripheral line and its invariant norm On the logarithmic cover of (C^*)^2 use U=Log m, V=Log l. Define a line by the deck action (U,V,p) -> (U+2pi i a,V+2pi i b,exp(bU-aV)p), a,b in Z. (1.1) This is an actual action: composing two multipliers introduces only exp(2pi i(bc-ad))=1. The form A=-(U dV-V dU)/(2pi i) (1.2) transforms to A+d(bU-aV), so d-A defines a connection on the line. Its curvature form dA is -dU wedge dV/(pi i). On a peripheral Lagrangian curve, in particular a smooth geometric A-polynomial branch, its pullback is flat. Set B(U,V)=Re U Im V-Re V Im U. The norm log||p||=log|p|-B(U,V)/(2pi) (1.3) is invariant under (1.1): B changes by 2pi(b Re U-a Re V), precisely the change of log|p| times 2pi. No choice of a logarithm branch is being hidden in this norm. ## 2. A branch-compatible tetrahedron primitive For a tetrahedron choose u=Log z and v=Log z'', where z''=1-z^(-1). Write w=Log(1-z)=u+v+pi i k with a fixed odd integer k on the chosen logarithmic sheet. Continue Li_2 so that dLi_2(z)=-w du. Put T(z)=Li_2(z)+(1/2)u w+(pi i k/2)u. (2.1) Direct differentiation gives dT=(1/2)(u dv-v du). (2.2) The compatible branch of the Bloch--Wigner identity gives exactly Im T=D(z)-(1/2)(Re u Im v-Re v Im u). (2.3) Indeed D=Im Li_2+Re u Im w; substitute w=u+v+pi i k in (2.1). The k terms cancel in (2.3). The branch identity for D continues because its derivative is single valued and its continuation constants are real: a loop about zero changes u by 2pi i and leaves Li_2 fixed; a loop about one changes w by 2pi i and Li_2 by -2pi i u. Their commutators add multiples of (2pi i)^2. Thus (2.3) does not discard flattening terms by taking an unmatched principal branch. ## 3. Centering the affine gluing equations Collect x=(u_j,v_j), with the orientation signs in Omega(x,y)=sum_j epsilon_j(u_j y_vj-v_j y_uj). The logarithmic edge equations are affine with purely imaginary constants. Choose a purely imaginary vector x_0=i a_0 satisfying those equations and the chosen complete peripheral logarithms. It need not be a shape point. Such a vector is obtained by taking the imaginary part of a complete logarithmic shape point; equivalently one can use the rational angle reference already constructed in the state notes. This existence is asserted for a chart with that complete point. Subtract its peripheral values in defining U,V, so U=V=0 at the chosen complete lift. Then xi=x-x_0 satisfies the homogeneous edge equations, xi in E^perp. The audited coisotropic boundary identity is Omega(xi,eta)=-(1/2)(U(xi)V(eta)-V(xi)U(eta)), xi,eta in E^perp. (3.1) This is the same pairing calculation that gives delta beta=-(1/2)m wedge l. Define R_X=sum_j epsilon_j T(z_j)-(1/2)Omega(x_0,x)+C, C real. (3.2) Equations (2.2) and (3.1) prove dR_X=-(1/4)(U dV-V dU). (3.3) The centering term in (3.2) is necessary because the edge equations are affine. Applying a homogeneous symplectic formula without it would lose a branch-dependent linear term. There is also an exact norm identity. Since Re x is in E^perp, and Im x-a_0 is in E^perp, (2.3) and (3.1) give Im R_X=D(beta)-(1/2)Omega(Re x,Im x-a_0) =D(beta)+(1/4)B(U,V). (3.4) No angle positivity, saddle estimate or limit is used here. Changing the purely imaginary reference within the same affine edge and complete peripheral constraints changes x_0 by an element of E. Its pairing with x-x_0 vanishes. The change in R_X is consequently a real constant, since both references are purely imaginary. Thus this reference choice affects only the unitary phase of P_X below. ## 4. The regulator is a norm of a parallel period Define on the logarithmic continuation cover P_X=exp(2R_X/(pi i)). (4.1) Equations (3.3)--(3.4) say exactly d log P_X=A, log||P_X||=2D(beta)/pi. (4.2) At the geometric complete point the last value is 2Vol(W)/pi. Thus volume is already the norm of a continuous period section. This identity is uniform on the stated nondegenerate gluing charts. Two compatible chart presentations of the same marked Bloch lift have the same boundary connection and norm. Their parallel sections therefore differ by a constant of absolute value one on a connected overlap. Under a logarithmic deck change the comparison with the multiplier in (1.1) can likewise retain a constant unitary character. This records a flat phase twist of the pullback line. The calculation does not silently trivialize it or identify it with a particular published Chern--Simons phase. That identification requires the global lift and phase calibration, alongside the finite scalar data of `equivariant_roots_and_phase_descent.md`. The exact five-term invariance of D(beta) already proved in the Bloch note makes the norm in (4.2) independent of its tetrahedral presentation. Its complex phase contains the additional period datum. The boundary symbol alone does not fix the value of that section. The action (1.1) and connection (1.2) have the same ordered-coordinate form as the classical line described in Baseilhac--Benedetti, [Analytic families of quantum hyperbolic invariants](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.4261v3), Section 4.4, equations (56)--(57). Their ordered coordinates are (lambda,mu)=(longitude,meridian), whereas ours were (m,l). Exchanging the ordered coordinates dualizes this line. A literal comparison must therefore retain the peripheral orientation/inversion convention as well as the phase calibration. The connection and volume norm above were derived from the local primitive and coisotropic reduction, without assuming that source's global identification theorem or a same-order identification of its marked line with ours. ## 5. The remaining quantum comparison is now a precise norm statement Let J_n be the prescribed, fully normalized literature meridian state at b^2=1/n, evaluated at the complete peripheral point. The conventions in the state notes give h_n=n/(n+1)^2, not 1/n. The requested volume law -2pi h_n log|J_n| -> Vol(W) is exactly equivalent to 4h_n log|J_n|+log||P_hyp|| -> 0. (5.1) The equality log||P_hyp||=2Vol(W)/pi proves this equivalence with all constants fixed. Establishing (5.1) is still a quantum theorem. It requires identifying the selected global period/cycle and controlling its comparison across levels; no finite-level phase normalization proves it. In the actual Faddeev chart the finite central character is t_n=exp((n+1)y), as independently derived in the rational bridge. The map of parameters must therefore remain part of this comparison. The work here supplies the exact classical target and its norm. It does not replace the all-alternating goal by a theorem about the existence of that target, or assert an unproved quantum comparison. The subsequent `rational_period_pushforward.md` constructs an exact folded period for the specified source realization and identifies its local gluing/regulator summands with all measures retained. It also shows why boundary specialization can preserve a residue even when the open special gluing fiber has lost its point. Transport and localization of that cycle, followed by (5.1), remain necessary.

title: Bounded meridian jets for a fixed quantum A-operator
text: # Bounded meridian jets for a fixed quantum A-operator Research note, 25 October 2026. A fixed recurrence needs only a bounded amount of meridian jet data to cross all singularities on a root orbit. The bound depends on the operator, not the level. There is no rank-one or regular-orbit hypothesis. The subsequent [all-level period theorem](all_level_a_period.md) uses coherence across levels to replace these potentially unknown meridian jets by controlled jets of finitely many fixed small colors in the quantum parameter. The state and conventions are those of [the ADO pointing calculation](kashaev_ado_pointing.md): q_N=exp(pi*i/N), M_j=-q_N^j, F_N(M_j)=C_j(q_N), 1<=j<=N, F_N(1)=<K>_N, F_N(-q_N)=1. (0.1) The C_j are the actual reduced fixed-color periods, not new initial conditions chosen to obtain a desired asymptotic. Their identity in (0.1) was independently proved by the filtered quotient-color argument in [the root-orbit note](root_orbit_pointing.md). ## 1. A uniform bound on singularities Take a specified nonzero reduced-state operator P=sum_(i=0)^d a_i(q,M)T^i, T h(M)=h(qM), d>=1. (1.1) Clear its rational denominators once, retaining the fixed operator and the state normalization, so all a_i are Laurent polynomials. Let D be the M-exponent span of a_d. For all sufficiently large N, a_d(q_N,M) is a nonzero Laurent polynomial and its exponent span is at most D. The excluded levels are finite: any one nonzero q-coefficient of a_d has only finitely many nonzero roots. Use the same local coordinate at each orbit point: M=M_j(1+z), M_j=-q_N^j. (1.2) The points M_j, 1<=j<=2N, are distinct. The sum of the multiplicities of all nonzero roots of a_d(q_N,M) is at most D. In particular, S_N=sum_(j=1)^(N-d) ord_(M=M_j) a_d(q_N,M) <= D. (1.3) This is a count with multiplicity. It does not require a torsion-point classification, primeness of N, or estimates on nearly vanishing factors. ## 2. Exact recovery from finitely many initial jets Write the forward companion equation on column states as V_j(z)=(F_N(M_j(1+z)),...,F_N(M_(j+d-1)(1+z)))^t, V_(j+1)(z)=B_j(z)V_j(z). The superdiagonal of B_j is one; its last row is (-a_0/a_d,...,-a_(d-1)/a_d), evaluated at (q_N,M_j(1+z)). Each B_j has pole order at most the j-th summand in (1.3). Thus r_N(z)=e_d^t B_(N-d)(z)...B_1(z) =sum_(k=-S_N)^infinity r_(N,k) z^k. (2.1) Let J_k=([z^k]F_N(M_1(1+z)),..., [z^k]F_N(M_d(1+z)))^t. All these are ordinary meridian germs of the actual Laurent polynomial state. The scalar r_N(z)V_1(z) is regular and equals F_N(1+z). Hence <K>_N=sum_(k=0)^S_N r_(N,-k) J_k. (2.2) More generally the output jet of order h needs initial jets only through S_N+h, and therefore through D+h. All negative coefficients of r_N V_1 vanish by the equation and regularity of the actual state; they are compatibility equations, not an excuse to evaluate an undefined quotient. This gives at most d(D+1) scalar initial data for the value, independent of N. When the orbit is regular, S_N=0 and (2.2) is the ordinary initial value formula. No claim that its higher meridian jets are small is made. For computation one can avoid multiplying Laurent matrices. Put C_j=a_d(q_N,M_j(1+z)) B_j and multiply the polynomial matrices C_j, together with the complete scalar denominator product. If its order at z=0 is S_N, retain the numerator through order S_N+h and divide by the denominator's unit part. This computes the same whole germ. For fixed d,D,h this requires O(N) field operations up to a constant depending on the fixed truncation and matrix sizes. ## 3. An intrinsic bound on the integral kernel defect The same statement applies to the actual integral solution lattice, not just a selected scalar period. Put n=2N, u=M^n, O=C[u]_(u-1), and represent P on E=C(M) over C(u), as in [the cofactor construction](root_orbit_pointing.md#4-the-root-period-can-be-read-from-the-quantum-a-operator). Let Lambda=ker_(C(u)) P intersection O^n. This is a saturated free O-module. Complete and use u=(1+z)^n, R=C[[z]]. Evaluation at the n root germs M_j(1+z) is an invertible Vandermonde change of basis over R. It identifies Lambda_R with a saturated submodule of R^n. Choose an integral basis, with matrix G(z) of size n by r, and let A(z) be its first d rows. Generic recurrence propagation shows r<=d and A has column rank r over C((z)). Its Smith exponents obey 0<=b_1<=...<=b_r<=D. (3.1) Here is a proof of the bound. Propagation through the whole orbit uses each point at most once; the total pole budget is still at most D. Therefore G=L A for a meromorphic n by d matrix L with z^D L integral. Since G is saturated, it has an integral left inverse Q. Consequently (Q z^D L) A=z^D I_r. Smith normal form implies every z^b_i divides z^D, proving (3.1). In particular if two integral solutions have the same initial meridian jets through D, their difference vanishes on the entire central fiber. The order-h version follows by the same calculation. This is the precise bounded extension data in the kernel lattice. It is a genuine linear solution module. No module structure is being inferred from a nonlinear condition on proposed scalar sections. The bound can be sharp: for f=(M+q)^D and P=f(M)T-f(qM), the solution lattice has rank one, but its first evaluation has order D. Its first nonzero initial jet is the D-th. This example has zero reference value; it does not contradict the earlier rank-one theorem with a nonzero anchor. ## 4. Ordinary initial values can miss a jet Consider the fixed second-order operator P=(M+q)T^2-[(q^2+1)M+q(q+1)]T+q^2(M+1). (4.1) It annihilates both 1 and f=(M+q)(M+q^2). At a root of order 2N, N>=3, all rational solutions are C(u)-linear combinations of these two functions. Indeed, putting g=sigma(f)-f, its equation is g*sigma(Delta h)-sigma(g)*Delta h=0. Thus Delta h=c(u)Delta f and h=b(u)+c(u)f. The basis (1,f) is integral and saturated: at the first and third orbit points its evaluation minor is a unit. At the first two points the minor has order one, since [z] (f(-q^2(1+z))-f(-q(1+z)))=q^2(q^2-1). The Smith exponents are (0,1). Every h_N=1+c_N f has both ordinary initial values equal to one, yet h_N(1)=1+c_N(1+q_N)(1+q_N^2). The exact missing datum is h_N(1)=1+[(1+q)(1+q^2)/(q^2(q^2-1))] *([z]h_N(-q^2(1+z))-[z]h_N(-q(1+z))). (4.2) Taking c_N=a^N, a>1, gives logarithmic rate log(a), with the same fixed operator and the same two ordinary initial values. These are manufactured states, not knot invariants. The example explains why an independent bound on meridian jets cannot be silently assumed. The all-level theorem below uses additional coherence actually available for the knot state. ## 5. The full ADO normalization keeps its residue and first jet Keep the exact factor N_N=d_N F_N, d_N=eta_N*(M-M^-1)*M^N/(M^(2N)-1), eta_N=i^(N+3). The regular numerator is R_N=(u-1)N_N=eta_N*(M-M^-1)*M^N F_N. Its reference residue and target jet are R_N(-q)=eta_N*(-1)^N*(q-q^-1), [z]R_N(1+z)=2 eta_N <K>_N. (5.1) These follow by direct substitution; the second retains the zero of M-M^-1 until differentiation. The factor M^N has shift character -1, and the exact generic full/reduced gauge is d_N(qM)/d_N(M)=-(qM-q^-1 M^-1)/(M-M^-1). On the initial d colors, N>d, the diagonal multiplication by eta_N*(M-M^-1)*M^N is a meridian unit. At the target it has one zero. Thus the full target transfer row acquires a factor z and the required output first jet compensates for that zero: transport under this actual gauge needs no additional initial jet beyond the reduced bound D. Using a general full-state operator directly also gives the weaker bound D_full+1 by Section 2. A central unit equal to one at u=1 cannot change (2.2) or (5.1): the whole output is regular, and its value, or first coefficient after the target zero, only sees that unit's constant term. This is distinct from erasing a generic peripheral factor. ## 6. Coverage, checks, and the remaining comparison Desingularization of q-difference equations and systems is existing coverage: [Koutschan--Zhang, 1801.04160](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04160) and [Barkatou--Jaroschek, 1802.01150](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.01150). Only their stated scope was consulted here. No algorithm or proof from them is a premise; the degree, propagation, and Smith arguments above are complete. No novelty claim is made. The [exact diagnostics](../experiments/audit_bounded_meridian_jets.py) check 30 second-order examples, including higher contact orders and the full-state gauge, and 28 examples attaining the first-order bound. Even and composite levels are included. The [results](../experiments/bounded_meridian_jets_results.json) are diagnostics of these uniform proofs, not a knot-class or volume test. For a specified actual annihilator, the finite-jet bound is now unconditional in its root-level rank. The subsequent [finite cut-state proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md) now constructs a nonzero actual all-level annihilator for every knot in principle. Its geometric symbol still requires independent identification. The [next theorem](all_level_a_period.md) removes the unknown meridian jets from the exact period formula using cross-level polynomial coherence. It does not establish the geometric regulator norm.

title: The actual complete period is a bounded-source first-normal response
text: # The actual complete period is a bounded-source first-normal response Research proof and independent source test, 27 October 2026. The ordinary-color bound and the normal boundary factor give an exact first-normal descriptor system for every knot. On a regular companion chart this becomes a fixed-rank affine transfer, with the same characteristic curve as the actual normal operator. The forcing is polynomially bounded; the complete value is its specified normal cut. This goes beyond regarding the complete value as an unspecified large entry of a Gram inverse. It does not prove that the response excites the geometric branch. Section 3 constructs a coherent source-wall change which preserves any prescribed finite prefix of actual colors, Weyl symmetry and the ordinary-color bounds, but kills complete growth and moves the original contribution to arbitrarily high normal order. ## 1. A universal bounded-source normal equation Use \(q_N=e^{\pi i/N}\), \(Q_N=q_N^2\), the actual reduced root state \(F_N(Y)\), and the actual generic colors \(C_j(q)\), with \[ F_N(Q_N^j)=C_j(q_N)\ (1\le j<N),\qquad C_N(q_N)=F_N(1)=K_N. \] The independently proved [positive trace bound](regularized_kashaev_period.md) gives \[ |C_j(q_N)|\le D_N=O(N^{b-1}),\qquad 1\le j<N. \tag{1} \] Fix a polynomial presentation of an actual normal operator \[ B=\sum_{i=0}^{d}b_i(q,Y)T^i,\qquad TY=q^2YT,\quad d\ge1, \qquad B[(Y-1)F_N]=0. \tag{2} \] Such an operator exists by applying the actual finite-state theorem to the weighted state; the primitive minimal presentation is available in [actual Weyl descent](actual_weyl_descent.md). Equivalently \(B(Y-1)\) is an actual polynomial annihilator of \(F_N\). The right factor is retained, rather than inverted at the cut. Define the generic weighted colors \[ d_j(q)=(q^{2j}-1)C_j(q),\qquad X_j(q)=(d_j(q),\ldots,d_{j+d-1}(q))^t . \tag{3} \] Cross-level polynomial rigidity gives the exact generic recurrence \[ \sum_i b_i(q,q^{2j})d_{j+i}(q)=0. \tag{4} \] For fixed \(j\), evaluate (2) at all sufficiently large roots with \(j+d<N\); this gives infinitely many zeros of the fixed Laurent polynomial on the left of (4), proving (4). Put \(p_j(q)=b_d(q,q^{2j})\), and let \(\mathcal N_j(q)\) have \(p_j\) on the superdiagonal and last row \(-b_0(q,q^{2j}),\ldots,-b_{d-1}(q,q^{2j})\). Then, before any specialization, \[ p_j X_{j+1}=\mathcal N_jX_j. \tag{5} \] Choose a fixed sufficiently large initial color \(j_0\) as in [the all-level theorem](all_level_a_period.md), so none of the generic \(p_j\), \(j\ge j_0\), is identically zero. At level \(N\), use the scaled color-normal parameter \[ q=q_N(1+s/N),\quad x_j=X_j(q_N),\quad y_j=[\partial_sX_j(q_N(1+s/N))]_{s=0}. \tag{6} \] All dots below denote this derivative, including the moving argument \(Y=q^{2j}\). Exact differentiation of (5) gives \[ p_jx_{j+1}=\mathcal N_jx_j,\qquad p_jy_{j+1}-\mathcal N_jy_j =g_j:=\dot{\mathcal N}_jx_j-\dot p_jx_{j+1}, \tag{7} \] where the undotted coefficients in (7) are evaluated at \(q_N\). No division by \(p_j(q_N)\) has occurred. Thus (7) remains valid at every singular step. The complete cut is exactly \[ K_N=\frac12 e_d^t y_{N-d+1}. \tag{8} \] Indeed \(d_N(q_N)=0\), while \[ \partial_s[(q_N(1+s/N))^{2N}-1]_{s=0}=2. \] The derivative of \(C_N\) is multiplied by the vanishing factor. Only its value \(K_N\) remains. The source in (7) is polynomially bounded uniformly in all steps. Every component of \(x_j\), \(j_0\le j\le N-d+1\), is either an ordinary weighted color, bounded by \(2D_N\), or the final zero \(d_N(q_N)\). Also \[ \dot b_i(q,q^{2j}) =\frac1N(q\partial_q+2jY\partial_Y)b_i(q,Y) \big|_{q_N,Q_N^j}=O_B(1). \tag{9} \] This follows monomial by monomial: \(q^aY^c\) contributes the bounded factor \((a+2jc)/N\). Hence \[ \|x_j\|=O_B(D_N)\quad(j_0\le j\le N-d+1),\qquad \|g_j\|=O_B(D_N)\quad(j_0\le j\le N-d). \tag{10} \] It also lies in exactly one fixed coordinate: \[ g_j=e_d\gamma_j,\qquad \gamma_j=-\sum_{i=0}^d \dot b_i(q_N,Q_N^j)d_{j+i}(q_N). \tag{10a} \] For each of the first \(d-1\) rows, \(\dot{\mathcal N}_jx_j=\dot p_j(x_j)_{r+1}\) and \(\dot p_jx_{j+1}=\dot p_j(x_j)_{r+1}\), so the two terms cancel. This proves (10a) even when \(p_j=0\). In scalar form the normal response is simply \[ \sum_{i=0}^d b_i(q_N,Q_N^j)y_{j+i} =-\sum_{i=0}^d\dot b_i(q_N,Q_N^j)d_{j+i}(q_N), \qquad y_N=2K_N, \tag{10b} \] where \(y_r=\partial_sd_r(q_N(1+s/N))|_{s=0}\). The forcing is therefore a bounded single-channel source, not an arbitrary vector in the companion space. The initial \(x_{j_0},y_{j_0}\) are bounded because they use finitely many fixed Laurent-polynomial colors. Equations (7)--(10) prove an actual, universal bounded-source first-normal response theorem. The normal is along the honest integral-color family, with its moving meridian. No off-root horizontal ADO section is assumed. ## 2. Fixed-rank transfer and its precise singular-step qualification Where \(p_j(q_N)\ne0\), put \[ A_j=\mathcal N_j/p_j. \] Then (7) becomes the exact rank-\(d\) affine equation \[ x_{j+1}=A_jx_j,\qquad y_{j+1}=A_jy_j+\dot A_jx_j. \tag{11} \] Here \(\dot A_jx_j=e_d\gamma_j/p_j\); the divided normal source retains the same single channel. Equivalently the doubled column has rank-\(2d\) transport \[ \binom{x_{j+1}}{y_{j+1}} =\begin{pmatrix}A_j&0\\ \dot A_j&A_j\end{pmatrix} \binom{x_j}{y_j}. \tag{12} \] All its input is fixed small-color pointing. For \(J=N-d+1\), define \(\Phi(k,j)=A_{k-1}\cdots A_j\). The exact selected response is \[ 2K_N=e_d^t\left[ \Phi(J,j_0)y_{j_0} +\sum_{j=j_0}^{J-1}\Phi(J,j+1)\dot A_jx_j \right]. \tag{13} \] This is an explicit source coupling, rather than a choice of a largest characteristic root. An adjoint row \(\lambda_j=\lambda_{j+1}A_j,\ \lambda_J=e_d^t\) gives the equivalent formula \[ 2K_N=\lambda_{j_0}y_{j_0} +\sum_j\lambda_{j+1}\dot A_jx_j. \tag{14} \] If the nonzero \(p_j(q_N)\) have a uniform polynomial lower bound, then the divided coefficients and the forcing in (11) have polynomial bounds too. A simple sufficient condition is that \(b_d(1,Y)\) have no zeros on the unit circle. In that case they are uniformly bounded apart from the already bounded \(x_j\). This is a checkable operator condition, not asserted for every primitive normal operator. The transfer has no new classical characteristic actions: \[ \det\!\left(LI- \begin{pmatrix}A_j&0\\\dot A_j&A_j\end{pmatrix}\right) =\det(LI-A_j)^2. \tag{15} \] On a regular limiting chart \(j/N\to u,\ Y=e^{2\pi iu}\), the off-diagonal block tends to \(2uY\partial_YA_{\rm cl}(Y)\). Thus the first-normal extension doubles the characteristic of the actual operator; it does not introduce a new regulator action. Identification of a geometric factor and excitation of its marked branch are further assertions. At a zero of \(p_j(q_N)\), (13) is understood only through its whole meromorphic germ and cancellation. The descriptor equation (7) stays valid, but its first-normal solutions need not have a unique cut. Higher lifts can select \(y_j\). The existing bounded jet budget, applied to \(B\), supplies a uniform finite procedure: to recover this first derivative, retain the total pole budget plus one input jet. It does not justify deleting singular steps or replacing their actual lattices by (11) at a zero. Consequently the unconditional theorem is (7)--(10). A regular fixed-rank affine transfer is its stated chartwise strengthening. Bounded forcing alone gives no exponential lower bound for (13); the source-weighted Green response is the quantity to estimate. ## 3. A coherent source-wall change can hide growth to any normal order Here is an exact obstruction to deducing the selected growth from ordinary-color bounds, a geometric localized factor and a finite prefix of color pointing. It is not a new knot invariant. Start with the actual family of any knot. Fix positive integers \(J,m\), and put \[ X=Y+Y^{-1},\quad a_r(q)=q^{2r}+q^{-2r},\quad t_J(q,X)=\prod_{r=1}^J(X-a_r(q)), \] \[ R_J(q,Y)=\frac{t_J(q,X)}{t_J(q,2)},\qquad h_{J,m}(q,Y)=(1-R_J(q,Y))^m . \tag{16} \] For \(N>J\), define the whole root function and generic colors by \[ \widetilde F_N(Y) =1+h_{J,m}(q_N,Y)(F_N(Y)-1), \] \[ \widetilde C_j(q) =1+h_{J,m}(q,q^{2j})(C_j(q)-1). \tag{17} \] The denominator in (16) is nonzero at every such \(q_N\). These families have the following exact properties. 1. Their first \(J\) generic colors are literally unchanged, since \(R_J(q,q^{2j})=0\) for \(1\le j\le J\). 2. Every \(\widetilde C_j(q)\) is Laurent polynomial and \(\widetilde C_j(1)=1\). 3. They satisfy all ordinary-color identities and also complete integral-color compatibility: \[ \widetilde F_N(Q_N^j)=\widetilde C_j(q_N),\qquad \widetilde C_N(q_N)=\widetilde F_N(1)=1. \] 4. Reciprocity is preserved. All ordinary values remain polynomially bounded uniformly in \(j<N\). 5. At each level, \(\widetilde F_N(Y)-1\) vanishes to order at least \(2m\) at \(Y=1\), regardless of how large \(F_N(1)\) is. For the only nonobvious algebraic claim in item 2, write \(Q=q^2\). For \(j>J\), direct factorization gives \[ R_J(q,q^{2j}) =(-1)^JQ^{-jJ+J(J+1)/2} {j-1\brack J}_Q\,{j+J\brack J}_Q. \tag{18} \] Both Gaussian coefficients are polynomials. Formula (18) follows from \[ a_j-a_r=Q^{-j}(1-Q^{j-r})(1-Q^{j+r}),\quad 2-a_r=-Q^{-r}(1-Q^r)^2 . \] For \(j\le J\) the numerator is zero. The apparent pole at \(q=1\) therefore cancels in every fixed color, proving item 2. For item 4, the numerator of \(R_J(q_N,Y)\) is bounded by \(4^J\) on the unit circle, whereas its denominator has modulus \(\prod_{r=1}^J4\sin^2(\pi r/N)\gg_JN^{-2J}\). Thus \[ |\widetilde C_j(q_N)| =O_{J,m}(N^{b-1+2Jm}). \] In fact the same reasoning bounds the multiplier by a fixed power of the quantum dimension \([j]_{q_N}\): use \(\sin^2(\pi j/N)/\sin^2(\pi r/N)=[j]^2/[r]^2\). Thus it is not merely a loss of all semisimple-type polynomial control. For item 5, \(1-R_J(q,Y)\) vanishes at \(X=2\), and \[ X-2=(Y-1)^2/Y. \] The original complete growth has therefore been moved beyond any prescribed finite number of normal jets, while the new complete period is identically one. Choosing the actual figure-eight family, whose positive exponential growth was proved separately, makes this a concrete growth-changing example. More precisely, set \[ c_{N,J}=\sum_{r=1}^J\frac1{2-a_r(q_N)} \asymp_J N^2 . \] All summands are positive at these roots.
