(3.4) Consequently kernels, cokernels and all derived two-term source classes of the actual head operator are preserved. In a presentation over a commutative coefficient ring, det K_con=(-1)^rank(T_time)det E when square. Over an Ore ring the stronger unimodular presentation equivalence is available directly, with no determinant convention. The number of extra multiplier/constraint pairs is only (m-1)[binomial(bN,b)-N^b]. (3.5) Thus the presentation has size linear in word length, despite the potentially exponentially many excursion patterns. It does not assert a rank bound independent of N. ## 4. The selected cut and the actual normal source survive exactly For the open source let f=(psi,0,...,0), with the original head source at time zero. Applying the original final cut to h_m gives the actual word evaluation. Extend any such cut by P_0 in (3.4). Then the extension (3.2) preserves it identically, including all scalar factors and the physical meridian derivative. An arbitrary pivotal matrix trace can equivalently be treated as its literal linear functional on the resulting head transfer matrix; no new rank-one normalization is needed. The preservation is stronger than point evaluation. Suppose a regular whole Q-family has E(Q)h(Q)=epsilon f_1+O(epsilon^2), Q=zeta(1+epsilon), and h_0 is in ker E_0. Write coefficient subscripts 0,1. Differentiating (3.2) and taking cokernels gives [K_(con,1) I_(0,0)h_0] =I_(1,0)[E_1 h_0] in coker K_(con,0). (4.1) The terms K_(con,0)I_(0,1)h_0 and I_(1,1)E_0h_0 disappear in this quotient. The same exact chain map preserves every higher normal jet, since (3.2) is a whole identity, and preserves the marked co-source through (3.4). If a specified scalar quantum-A/source complex has already been mapped to an actual head presentation by maps J,R satisfying E J=R P, the new whole sourced-module map is explicitly K_con(I_0 J)=(I_1 R)P. (4.2) In the cited companion-monodromy construction the target is E=M=T^N-I, with J and R=S_N r as proved there. It is not automatically the word-time head operator E of Section 2. Applying the abstract constrained-extension theorem with E=M gives an extension of that known source complex; identifying it with the specific Verma word presentation would require a supplied chain map between those presentations. Equation (4.2) does not construct that missing map. Wherever the supplied map exists, its factors N and its physical derivation D_phys=Y partial_Y+N U partial_U are unchanged. The normal X=2 cut remains a co-source on its thickened lattice; it is not replaced by an ordinary reduced-fiber evaluation. Formula (4.2) requires the supplied head presentation; it does not manufacture an all-level bounded-order scalar equation from a fixed-N matrix calculation. More generally, established elimination relations on the original pointed head network survive the contractible extension (3.3) exactly. It keeps the actual period and its established source relations without removing a lattice factor. It does not prove an equivalence with an unspecified scalar quantum-A presentation. The ambient Verma presentation of this same pointed network now has all its constraint currents visible. ## 5. Exact behavior under the actual irregular Rees transformation There is an intrinsic form of (3.1). Let i_T,p_T be the internal tail inclusion and projection. Then K_con=[[L,i_T],[p_T,0]]. (5.1) This formulation transports under any actual ambient gauge C_V, including the ramified irregular Rees gauge, by L'=C_V L C_V^(-1), i_T'=C_V i_T, p_T'=p_T C_V^(-1), K_con'=diag(C_V,I)K_con diag(C_V^(-1),I). (5.2) The source maps and cut are conjugated by the same matrices. The multiplier is an abstract copy of the discarded-state source module; no regular geometric identification of that copy is assumed. On the image of the original finite total-index module this is a finite-rank identity. Its Rees image is spanned by explicit irregular vectors and need not be a regular finite-rank submodule of the full cyclic root chart. Each finite u-jet has the known pole bounds, while the whole source retains its exponential and head flags. In particular i_T'p_T'=C_V(1-P)C_V^(-1). Its complementary head projector is the actual transformed projector, containing the factor exp[-sum p_i u_i/d]. Dropping that factor from the constraint changes (5.1) and destroys the source equivalence. The whole crossing factorization gives a regular cyclic matrix and a resonant base period, but these source constraints remain alongside both. ## 6. The remaining comparison is now a finite memory/source residual Removing the constraints gives L and the exact Schur operator S=E-tK. Keeping them gives K_con and exactly E. The mismatch is the explicitly computed operator S-E=-delta w B F^(-1)C. (6.1) Equation (2.9) is its first mixed-normal contribution to the actual word. Its Rees conjugate must be evaluated with the constraints and source poles retained; its apparent two-wall vanishing does not authorize discarding it before contraction. At a head characteristic point one cannot generally identify E with S by a regular source-preserving gauge. Already in rank one, E=x, B=C=F=1 gives S=x-delta w. Their characteristic loci differ. The augmented operator K_con is still unimodularly equivalent to diag(x,J), including at x=0. Thus the constrained extension works where an E^(-1)-based correction would have removed the actual characteristic point from the comparison. This gives a concrete next target rather than a proposed phase: transport the actual constraint/source complex (5.1) to the chosen geometric framing module, or prove that its memory and co-source residuals have the required marked transgression there. Smoothness of the geometric algebraic place alone does not make (6.1) zero. The exact source extension is uniform in braid word and works before quantum jets. It does not make the intermediate excursion-counting family topological, prove a new geometric source identification, or infer a selected exponential from its whole equality. The normal d at fixed N and the physical large-level parameter remain distinct. The [universal algebra audit](../experiments/audit_constrained_verma_word_source_extension.py) checks the finite excursion sums, two-wall coefficients, constrained source maps and stable equivalence, including noncommutative entries. The [independent proof audit](constrained_verma_word_independent_audit.md) also checks the finite-word rank, ordered Feshbach maps, constrained source equivalence and normal-jet formulas, with the distinct word-time/companion-presentation qualification in Section 4 retained.

title: Controlled cyclic completion of the actual Euler source
text: # Controlled cyclic completion of the actual Euler source Research note, 26 October 2026. The nilpotent Euler polynomial in the actual R-matrix has a canonical completion by the existing cyclic dilogarithm. We compute its entire coefficient normalization, derive its boundary pentagon through the mixed central jet, and prove polynomial bounds for its coefficient change on marked compact central charts, uniformly in N. This treats a genuine N-dependent algebraic normalization, not a fixed-degree substitute. This is local source transport. It does not identify the global meridian source extension, select a geometric period of a knot, or prove the volume conjecture. ## 1. The Euler polynomial is an actual quantum-group atom Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2 and rho=q-q^(-1). Define c_j=(-1)^j Q^(j(j-1)/2)/(Q;Q)_j, P_N(X)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1)c_j X^j. (1.1) Every denominator is nonzero. In the normalized actual uncheck crossing of [the semicyclic construction](semicyclic_carry_braiding.md), the Euler part is precisely Theta=P_N(q rho^2 E_1 F_2). (1.2) Indeed [j]_q!=q^(-j(j-1)/2)(Q;Q)_j/(1-Q)^j and rho(1-Q)=-q rho^2. Substituting into its original coefficient q^(j(j-1)/2)rho^j/[j]_q! gives (1.2). The original Cartan factor, flip and full source wrap are retained. For the uncheck holonomy map the second F wrap is phi_2/K_1^N, exactly as in that note; for the checked map its input F wrap is phi_2. No new invariant or replacement crossing is defined. An exact polynomial recurrence already displays the boundary: (1-X)P_N(QX)=P_N(X)-X^N/N. (1.3) The coefficients below X^N cancel by their defining recurrence. The top one is -Q^(N-1)c_(N-1)=-1/N, since (Q;Q)_(N-1)=N, c_(N-1)=Q/N. Thus the familiar 1/N source is forced by the actual Euler atom. When X^N=0, (1.3) is its ordinary nilpotent shift identity. ## 2. The uncompleted pentagon has noncentral boundary terms Let XY=QYX, U=X^N, V=Y^N. Normal order means X before Y. For the unmodified truncated pentagon put D=P_N(X)P_N(-YX)P_N(Y)-P_N(Y)P_N(X). The coefficient of X^p Y^s on the first product is exactly sum_k c_(p-k)c_(s-k)Q^(-k)/(Q;Q)_k, (2.1) where 0<=k,p-k,s-k<N. This follows by reordering (-YX)^k=(-1)^k Q^(-k(k+1)/2)X^kY^k. For p,s<N it equals c_p c_s Q^(-ps): the generic pointed compact pentagon's coefficient uses only indices below N and can therefore be specialized without a vanishing denominator. Consequently D lies in the central ideal (U,V), with the exact three-block decomposition D=U B_X+V B_Y+UV B_XY, deg_X,deg_Y B_*<N. (2.2) The coefficients are (2.1) with the indicated wrapped exponents. Two useful nonzero coefficients are [X^N Y]D=1/[N(1-Q)], [X^(2N-2)Y^(2N-2)]D=Q^3/N^3. (2.3) For N=2 this is exactly D=U Y/4+V X/4-UV/8. A central scalar cannot repair this specific unmodified operator identity. Its U constant coefficient would have to vanish, while the nonzero UY coefficient in (2.3) would remain. This comparison retains arbitrary central scalar functions, not only their values at a complete point. It does not refute a differently normalized or source-completed move, or a particular contracted scalar identity. ## 3. Use the literature cyclic completion, with its marked root The alternate cyclic dilogarithm already defined in [the four-atom note](four_cyclic_atoms.md) is d_N(X)=(1-X^N)^((N-1)/(2N)) product_(r=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^rX)^(-r/N). (3.1) It is normalized by d_N(0)=1, with its roots continued from that point. Write nu=(1-U)^(1/N), nu(0)=1. Direct expansion gives log d_N(X)=-sum_(k>=1,N does not divide k) X^k/[k(1-Q^k)]. (3.2) The terms with k divisible by N cancel between the factors of (3.1). In particular d_N(X)=P_N(X) when X^N=0. Finite product cancellation, or (3.2), gives (1-X)d_N(QX)=nu d_N(X), product_(a=0)^(N-1)d_N(Q^a X)=1. (3.3) This is the existing cyclic function, including its determinant normalization. It supplies a completion of the actual atom (1.2). It is not a claim that each separate compact Verma factor can be evaluated at a root without the whole compression used there. ## 4. An explicit norm-torsor formula for every coefficient Reduce d_N(X) in the free algebra with X^N=U: d_N(X)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1)a_j(U)X^j. The coefficient equations of (3.3) give a_j=a_0 product_(r=1)^j Q^(r-1)/(Q^r-nu). Equivalently, with the c_j of (1.1), a_j/c_j=a_0 product_(r=1)^j (Q^r-1)/(Q^r-nu). (4.1) The entire scalar is fixed by the following product, with a_0(0)=1: a_0(U)^N=nu^(-N(N-1)/2) product_(r=1)^(N-1) [(nu-Q^r)/(1-Q^r)]^(N-r). (4.2) Here is an independent determinant proof. Put T_nu(X)=sum_j t_j X^j, t_j=product_(r=1)^j Q^(r-1)/(Q^r-nu), t_0=1, X e_j=e_(j+1), X e_(N-1)=U e_0, S e_j=Q^j e_j. The relation is (1-X)S T_nu=nu T_nu S. The cyclic bidiagonal matrix (1-X)S has characteristic polynomial lambda^N-nu^N, by its diagonal and full cyclic determinant terms. An eigenvector of eigenvalue lambda normalized to have zeroth coordinate one has v_j(lambda)=Q^(j(j-1)/2)/product_(r=1)^j(Q^r-lambda). To compute the determinant of these columns at lambda=nu Q^a, multiply each column by product_(r=1)^(N-1)(Q^r-lambda). The resulting row polynomials have degrees N-1-j. Their determinant is a fixed nonzero Q constant times the ordinary Vandermonde. The original denominator product is U^(N-1), and the zeroth coordinates of T_nu's columns have product U^(N-1)product_j t_j. Those factors cancel. Scaling the Vandermonde by nu then proves det T_nu=nu^(N(N-1)/2) product_(r=1)^(N-1) [(1-Q^r)/(nu-Q^r)]^(N-r). (4.3) The remaining Q constant is fixed by nu=1,U=0: T_nu is then P_N of a nilpotent matrix and has determinant one. Equations (3.3) and det(a_0 T_nu)=1 give (4.2). This also proves uniqueness in the marked formal neighborhood. Two unit solutions of (3.3) differ by a central function f(U). Their norms imply f(U)^N=1; f(0)=1 forces f=1 in characteristic zero. The root is not independently reset at each occurrence. ## 5. The first central jet is explicit and nonscalar Write a_j(U)=c_j+U r_j+O(U^2), and R_N(X)=sum_j r_j X^j. Differentiating (4.1)--(4.2) gives r_0=(1/N^2)sum_(k=1)^(N-1) k/(1-Q^k), r_j/c_j=r_0+(1/N)sum_(k=1)^j 1/(1-Q^k). (5.1) For the first formula use sum_k(1-Q^k)^(-1)=(N-1)/2, obtained by pairing k with N-k, including its even-level middle term. The increments in the second formula are nonzero. Thus R_N is not a scalar multiple of P_N; changing only a scalar source line cannot replace this operator jet. For the actual complex roots, (5.1) also proves directly max_j |r_j/c_j|=O(1+log N). (5.2) Indeed |1-Q^k|>=4 min(k,N-k)/N, and the resulting harmonic sum is O(log N). This is a coefficient estimate in the specified Euler frame, not a condition-number estimate for every tensor operator or a lower bound for a contracted knot period. ## 6. The pentagon extends through the nilpotent central order Let R=K[[U,V]], with the roots of 1-U,1-V,1-U+UV marked by their value one. The algebra A_R=R<X,Y>/(XY-QYX,X^N-U,Y^N-V) is free over R with basis X^iY^j, 0<=i,j<N. Formula (3.1) defines units there: its reduction is P_N of a nilpotent element. The strict cyclic pentagon proved in [the root pentagon note](cyclic_tetrahedron_pentagon.md) is d_N(Y)d_N(bX) =d_N(X)d_N(-YX/a)d_N(Y/h), (6.1) a^N=1-U, b^N=1-V, h^N=1-U+UV. Its anchored branches are regular in this order. Localizing the free order to its generic central field gives the proved identity; torsion freeness therefore extends it to A_R itself. This includes its nilpotent source, rather than replacing the source by a generic unpointed splitting module. Here is its complete first mixed jet, modulo (U^2,V^2), which retains UV. Put T=-YX, P_Z=P_N(Z), R_Z=R_N(Z), and partial f(Z)=Z f'(Z). The three transported factors are B_X=P_X+U R_X-(V/N)partial P_X -UV(R_X+partial R_X/N), B_T=P_T+(U/N)partial P_T-UV R_T, B_Y=P_Y+(U/N)partial P_Y+V R_Y +UV(-partial P_Y/N+R_Y+partial R_Y/N). Then exactly in this quotient, (P_Y+V R_Y)B_X=(P_X+U R_X)B_T B_Y. (6.2) These formulas follow by expanding the actual transported norm roots and arguments in (6.1). In particular (bX)^N=U-UV, (-YX/a)^N=-UV, and (Y/h)^N=V+UV in this quotient. Thus the corner term -UV R_T is derived, not a freely chosen correction. Omitting it gives a nonzero operator at every level: R_N is nonzero by (5.1), the powers T^j are independent in the nilpotent PBW basis, and the remaining P_X,P_Y factors are units. Any specified external vectors and covectors inherit (6.2), with their full source and co-source transported. A nonzero omitted corner is detectable by some exterior functional: coefficient extraction in the PBW basis is perfect, and pairing with the complementary monomial detects a chosen coefficient. This does not prove that a particular knot's selected cut has nonzero geometric coupling. The central variables here are primitive quantum-plane centers. They are not the earlier meridian wall coordinate or the point source of the scalarized A-curve. Nor is this free primitive order a common stable lattice for the unscaled adjacent meridian projectors; their double-pole obstruction remains unchanged. ## 7. Uniform polynomial bounds beyond fixed algebraic degree Let D be a simply connected domain containing 0 but not 1, and let L(U)=Log(1-U) on D with L(0)=0. Take nu_N(U)=exp(L(U)/N), Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N). For every compact K in D there are constants B,C, independent of N>=2 and 0<=j<N, such that C^(-1)N^(-B)<=|a_j(U)/c_j|<=C N^B, U in K. (7.1) Proof. L is bounded on K, so |nu_N-1|<=C_K/N. For roots with min(r,N-r) larger than a fixed constant, the ratios (nu_N-Q_N^r)/(1-Q_N^r) are 1+O_K(1/min(r,N-r)). Their logarithmic moduli have the same bound, whose sum is O_K(log N). There are only finitely many remaining endpoint indices. Their ratios converge uniformly on K to (L(U)-2pi*i*r)/(-2pi*i*r), or its negative-index version. These limits never vanish: L(U)=2pi*i*r, r!=0, would imply U=0, where the chosen L is zero. Hence their moduli and inverse moduli are bounded. Finitely many small N satisfy the same bound by compactness and the identical nonvanishing argument. Finally log|nu_N|=Re L/N. In (4.2), all product weights (N-r)/N are bounded by one. Thus |log|a_0||=O_K(1+log N); (4.1) gives the same bound for every coefficient ratio. This proves (7.1). Both ratios and their inverses are holomorphic on D with the marked roots. Cauchy estimates on a fixed small circle about zero therefore bound every fixed central Taylor jet by a power of N. The sharper first-jet estimate is (5.2). The bounded logarithm lift is essential. Arbitrary cut indices growing with N can make nu stay away from one and are not covered by this proof. The theorem also does not compare sums of complex terms from different source channels: polynomial entrywise factors alone do not exclude global cancellation. ## 8. An exact comparison with the original factorial source and cut This completion also identifies a specified source vector, not only an operator normalization. Put p_a(nu)=(Q nu;Q)_a, S_N(nu)=p_(N-1)(nu), J_(j,a)=Q^(-j) delta_(a,N-1-j), gamma_N(U)=a_0(U)/S_N(nu). Complementing the finite product gives exactly t_j(nu)=Q^(-j)p_(N-1-j)(nu)/S_N(nu), vector(a_j)=gamma_N J vector(p_a). (8.1) For the product identity, the omitted factors are product_(k=1)^j(1-Q^(-k)nu); dividing their reciprocals by Q^j gives the factors Q^(k-1)/(Q^k-nu) of t_j. No endpoint factor is deleted. At U=0, nu=1 and gamma_N=1/N, so this is the literal reflection identity c_j=Q^(-j)(Q;Q)_(N-1-j)/N. The full affine source equation is transported too. Let (L_p v)_a=v_(a+1)-(1-Q^(a+1)nu)v_a, (L_a v)_j=(Q^j-nu)v_j-Q^(j-1)v_(j-1), with cyclic indices, and let R_0 be the reversal without its Q^(-j) phase. Direct substitution proves the matrix identity L_a (gamma_N J)=-gamma_N R_0 L_p. (8.2) The actual factorial source is L_p p=(1-U)e_(N-1). Its image is therefore L_a a=-gamma_N(1-U)e_0. Thus (8.1) identifies these pointed finite cyclic source presentations with their entire boundary coefficient. It does not merely compare their kernels. The auxiliary argument shift delta(nu)=Qnu is transported as well. On an overlap of its specified lifted charts it gives delta(a_j)=[delta(gamma_N)/gamma_N] [(1-Q^(-j)nu)/(1-Qnu)] a_j. (8.2a) This follows from the actual factorial identity p_a(Qnu)/p_a(nu)=(1-Q^(a+1)nu)/(1-Qnu). The ratio of gamma_N is fixed by (4.2) and the retained endpoint, with its root continued on the lifted cover. A cut change can leave the principal source chart and meet its polar lattice; (8.2a) does not assert regularity of each separate ratio there. For the physical argument nu=M^2, this is the squared-meridian shift. The full local two-direction source transport is thus obtained by conjugation, while its lattice arrows are retained. For any specified co-source lambda_p, set lambda_a=lambda_p J^(-1)/gamma_N. Then lambda_a vector(a)=lambda_p vector(p) exactly. Over C, J is unitary; the full source change is a scalar times a unitary matrix, with no hidden matrix condition number. On the compact marked charts of Section 7, C^(-1)N<=|S_N(nu_N(U))|<=C N. (8.3) Indeed S_N(nu)=U/(1-nu), with its whole value N at U=0; S_N/N converges uniformly to -U/L(U), whose value at zero is one and which is nonzero on the chart. This and Section 7 give polynomial upper and lower bounds for gamma_N and its inverse. Thus the actual vector and co-source transport has uniform normalization control, despite its growing algebraic degree. This is stronger than an entrywise estimate alone. For the physical meridian argument nu=M^2 at a root, the exact parameter relation is U=1-M^(2N). With the original phase eta_N=i^(N+3), the full ADO dimension remains d_N(M)=eta_N M^(N-1)/S_N(M^2), gamma_N/d_N=a_0/(eta_N M^(N-1)). (8.4) The coherent source branch M=(1-U)^(1/(2N)) makes the second factor polynomially bounded as well. At completeness gamma_N=1/N while d_N(1)=eta_N/N; the phase has not been identified with one. The U here is the primitive center complementary to the meridian center, not the variable called U=M^(2N) in several earlier notes. Equations (8.1)--(8.4) give a local, source-compatible comparison between actual factorial data and the coefficients of the existing cyclic dilogarithm. They apply at each fixed root and on its marked central chart. They do not identify the knot's global meridian difference extension or its selected geometric period. Passing to spectral values of X at U=0 would still collapse these coefficient directions; the coefficient lattice and co-source are retained. The subsequent [Rivin flow and paired-source calculation](rivin_flow_and_quantum_source.md#6-a-paired-source-identity-needed-by-a-quantum-flow-lift) also computes the exact involutive norm of this comparison: gamma_N(M)gamma_N(M^(-1))=d_N(M)/(N eta_N). The marked roots at M=1 fix its phase. Transforming both actual dual source frames therefore gives the full Gaussian cap scalar N eta_N/(Q d_N), with its reflected operator retained. This calibrates opposite source orientations and supplies a local norm-one edge variable for a proposed global flow lift. It does not identify that lift or the selected knot period. The [subsequent source-connection calculation](cyclic_source_connection_and_resonant_flags.md) expresses gamma_N itself as a cyclic dilogarithm times the exact monomial and S_N factors, with a fixed phase. Its rational connection gives transport beyond the compact central chart. At the other norm-root lifts z=Q^r of U=0, its regularized value is a specified phase times (Q;Q)_r/N. The corresponding primitive operator has image X^r V and rank N-r. The opposite source weights and actual caps are regularized together on their common cover. This retains the kernel that an invertible-frame assumption would miss, without inferring the knot's geometric coupling from it. ## 9. Existing coverage, checks and the remaining global theorem Definition (3.1) is the alternate cyclic dilogarithm recorded by [Ip--Yamazaki, 1412.5777](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.5777), not a new quantum definition. Cyclic Fourier analysis and coefficient-mutation coverage also occur in [Ishibashi, 2501.02316](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.02316). Its [16 October correction, 2610.23572](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23572) explicitly adds lifting data on a mu_N-cover and an extra phase in general pentagons. Only the stated coverage was consulted; none of those papers' pentagon, Fourier or strict-lift proofs is used. Our strict identity is restricted to the already proved compatible anchored cover. Unrelated root choices are not equated. No novelty is claimed for cyclic completion, cyclic Fourier normalization or the compact pentagon. The contribution needed here is their explicit actual-R source calibration, mixed central boundary terms and uniform coefficient control in that frame. The determinant, jet and bound proofs above are direct. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_controlled_cyclic_euler_source.py) checks the full noncommutative defect, mixed-source pentagon, cyclic normalization determinant, literal finite-product jet, and agreement with the actual crossing at both colors and wraps. Complex-number bound samples are labeled diagnostics; the uniform bound is proved in Section 7. [Results](../experiments/controlled_cyclic_euler_source_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_controlled_cyclic_euler_source.py This removes a local ambiguity in transporting the actual Euler source. A full colored geometric triangulation, its meridian extension class, actual selected cut and regulator norm comparison are still required. The coefficient bound is not promoted to a lower bound for the original Kashaev value.

title: The controlled Fourier gauge sends the geometric cut clock to a conormal shift
text: # The controlled Fourier gauge sends the geometric cut clock to a conormal shift Research proof, 27 October 2026. The controlled source gauge has an explicit quadratic kernel. It gives exact transformed head Ward operators, hence an actual crossing/current Hamiltonian dictionary. It also distinguishes two clocks which have identical-looking coherent coordinate descriptions but are different actual insertions. The difference survives the normalized source pairing. The relevant first-normal coupling is computed from the whole clock, not inferred from its reduced root representative. The result does not yet send both actual framing-current equations to the full sourced geometric period. It identifies the required polarization/normal adapter and rules out a source-preserving identification which simply equates the coupled position clock with the old geometric cut clock. ## 1. Exact finite kernel and observables Use the actual high-color basis and source of [the cyclotomic wall construction](cyclotomic_diagonal_wall_current_source.md), with r=N. Write R=0,...,N for the Frobenius block index, S=0,...,N-1 for the head index, A=Q_N^S and B=Q_N^R. Let V increase S modulo N. Take the explicitly normalized Fourier matrix \[ {\cal F}_{S',S}=N^{-1}Q_N^{S'S},\quad {\cal F}^{-1}_{S,S'}=Q_N^{-SS'},\quad H_0=G(I\otimes{\cal F}),\quad G=\sum_R P_R\otimes V^R. \] The actual matrix kernel is exactly \[ (H_0)_{R,S';R,S}=N^{-1}Q_N^{S(S'-R)}. \tag{1} \] The reduction of S'-R modulo N changes no power of Q_N. Finite geometric-series multiplication gives \[ \begin{split} H_0 A H_0^{-1}&=V^{-1},& H_0 V H_0^{-1}&=B^{-1}A,\\ H_0 B H_0^{-1}&=B,& H_0e_{\rm Fr}H_0^{-1}&=e_{\rm Fr}V^{-1},& H_0f_{\rm Fr}H_0^{-1}&=f_{\rm Fr}V. \end{split} \tag{2} \] The Fr matrices in (2) are the actual divided matrices with their root sign normalization, not an independent classical copy. Their last two conjugates are exactly the endpoint-completed generators constructed from divided powers and actual normal wrap entries. In particular the OLD head clock is the NEW head shift. The new position clock restricted to the correlated source satisfies A|P=B|P, but this inserted A is not H_0 A_old H_0^(-1). Conjugating an entire word transforms its old observables as well as its sources; it does not replace this distinction by a choice of terminology. ## 2. Actual transformed Ward operators, including the endpoints First keep the ORIGINAL INTEGRAL head frame of the wall source. Let M^2=1 and x=-M/q_N. The sign M is the retained meridian lift; in the high r=N color it is (-1)^N before its specified one-dimensional lift adapter. The genuine Hopf scaling is Ecal=rho^2 E. With C_q=diag(q_N^S), the actual root matrices are \[ K=xA^{-1},\quad {\cal E}=M\rho V^{-1}(C_q-C_q^{-1}),\quad F=V(q_NC_q-q_N^{-1}C_q^{-1})/\rho. \tag{3} \] These are Ecal=M rho^2 E_St and F=F_St. Their E edge at S=0 and F edge at S=N-1 vanish exactly, since [0]=[N]=0. Define the whole finite polynomial matrix \[ \Psi_w(V)=\frac1N\sum_{\ell=0}^{N-1} \sum_{s=0}^{N-1}(wQ_N^\ell)^sV^\ell, \qquad\Psi_\pm=\Psi_{q_N^{\pm1}}. \tag{3a} \] It is exactly Fourier w^S Fourier^(-1). The controlled shift commutes with this circulant matrix, so H_0 C_q^(+/-1)H_0^(-1) =Psi_(+/-). Hence the exact transformed actual current operators, in the SAME wall source frame, are \[ \begin{split} K^{H_0}&=xV,\\ {\cal E}^{H_0}&=M\rho BA^{-1}(\Psi_+-\Psi_-),\\ F^{H_0}&=B^{-1}A(q_N\Psi_+-q_N^{-1}\Psi_-)/\rho. \end{split} \tag{4} \] These are original head Ward currents for the ACTUAL conjugated crossing: conjugate the input/output coproducts with the same endpoint H_0's. The original exact R intertwining equation then gives its exact transformed equation, with no omitted Cartan, twist, cap, source or internal projector. Thus (4) is a concrete crossing/current identity, not only an identification of orbit dimensions or groups. It has a useful negative consequence. The transformed Fr generators in (2) commute with all three transformed head operators (4), because the two original factors commute. They are distinct commuting actions at the root. Calling the Fr generators the old geometric head currents without a normal comparison would contradict this exact operator fact. For comparison there is a simpler BALANCED-frame formula, but its frame adapter must not be erased. The explicit integral-to-balanced diagonal matrix is \[ D_s=(1-Q_N)^s q_N^{s(s-1)/2}. \] Direct adjacent entries give D F_St D^(-1)=V(1-Q_NA) and D(M rho^2 E_St)D^(-1)=V^(-1)(MA^(-1)-M^(-1)). If one defines a FRESH unit shift and unit Fourier gauge H_B in those balanced coordinates, its formulas are \[ {\cal E}^{H_B}=BA^{-1}(MV-M^{-1}),\quad F^{H_B}=B^{-1}A(1-Q_NV^{-1}),\quad K^{H_B}=xV. \tag{4a} \] The transported original integral shift is instead D V D^(-1), which is weighted. Thus H_B is not obtained by silently retaining the same unit V while calling it the transported wall H_0. To compare the two actual words one must include D (and its actual whole q-germ when normal jets are compared), with both sources, duals and every internal projector. The logarithm of this diagonal can contribute to the phase. No Gaussian/large-level phase estimate is inferred merely from its invertibility at fixed N. The actual whole source gauge H(q)=K_src(q)H_0 of the wall note has K_src(q_N)=I and retains its compression unit. Equation (4) is its root dictionary. If K_src=I+delta K_src,1+O(delta^2), every first-normal transformed operator has the additional term [K_src,1,O^(H_0)]. That known source-germ term must be included rather than treating constant H_0 as the entire whole source comparison. ## 3. The exact quadratic generating family and its conormal Put H_N=2pi i/N and mark logarithmic positions \[ Q_R=H_NR,\quad q=H_NS,\quad q'=H_NS'. \] The kernel (1) is N^(-1) exp(W/H_N), with the exact quadratic generating function \[ W=q(q'-Q_R). \tag{5} \] Use dW=p'_h dq'+(p'_R-p_R)dQ_R-p_h dq. The canonical transformation is therefore \[ Q'_R=Q_R,\quad q'=Q_R-p_h,\quad p'_h=q,\quad p'_R=p_R-q. \tag{6} \] It preserves dQ_R wedge dp_R+dq wedge dp_h. Logarithmic marks are required: a cyclic index wrap adds its specified integral 2pi i period to the quadratic generator. It is not discarded while composing marked phases. The root Frobenius parity remains its separately recorded character. The Fr index R is UNWRAPPED: R=0 and R=N are distinct endpoint states even though B has the same eigenvalue there. No cyclic Fr wrap is added to its nilpotent divided matrices. Formula (6) is the local marked canonical map of the exact quadratic kernel; the finite endpoint constraints and the Fr O(N) source clutch remain in the finite operator problem. No analytic stationary-phase comparison or global flat Weyl quantization of that source line has been assumed. For a normally ordered original head observable h(A,V), (2) is an exact finite difference Egorov formula. Its leading Hamiltonian is the old Hamiltonian under \[ q=p'_h,\qquad p_h=Q_R-q'. \tag{7} \] For example IN THE BALANCED FRAME the principal Hamiltonians are e^p(M e^(-q)-M^(-1)) and e^(-p)(1-e^q). Under (7) they give precisely the principal symbols of (4a). In the original integral frame the functions Psi_+/- in (4) are retained instead; converting their marked phase requires the displayed diagonal adapter. The quadratic Hamiltonian dictionary itself follows directly from the actual finite Fourier kernel, without importing a general semiclassical Egorov theorem or suppressing this basis change. The original uniform head source has p_h=0. Its image is the actual constraint q'=Q_R, exactly P from the wall construction. The Fr source psi(t)=sum_R t^Rv_R has p_R=Log t, so its correlated image has the conormal relation \[ p'_R+p'_h=\operatorname{Log}t. \tag{8} \] Thus the actual OLD cut position A_old=e^q is e^(p'_h), or t/e^(p'_R), on this marked conormal. It is not e^(Q_R). Equation (8) is a concrete relative-Fr-momentum adapter, including the source parameter. It is a relation on a source conormal, not a replacement of two independent momentum operators by ordinary functions before contraction. ## 4. The normalized source detects the clock distinction For every pair of Fr source flags, e_D is supported on the selected states z_j of the wall theorem. A head shift changes S while fixing R. Hence \[ PV^{-1}P=0,\qquad \operatorname{Tr}(e_DV^{-1})=0. \tag{9} \] On the same source the other insertion has the exact, nonconstant character \[ \operatorname{Tr}(e_D A) =\left(\frac{1+Q_Ntu}{1+tu}\right)^N,\qquad T=\frac{tu}{1+tu}. \tag{10} \] Equations (9)--(10) are actual finite matrix pairings. Thus there cannot be a source-preserving whole-observable comparison which identifies these two clocks. The polynomial Fr-clock normal graph in the parent's finite-clock construction is an actual INSERTED clock image and a useful source cycle; it is not yet the image of the old cut observable under (1). An additional polarization and current comparison is necessary. The same distinction appears in the original geometric directions. In the old complete critical frame, both cut-Borel generators obey \[ \delta p_h=0,\qquad \delta q=-2(1-A_{\rm old}). \tag{11} \] Here delta p_h=0 is exactly ker(ell), the fixed inverse-cut-flag condition, rather than a new gauge assumption. Lift these old geometric directions without changing the ancillary Fr variables. Equation (6) carries their CUT components to \[ \delta q'=\delta Q_R=0,\quad \delta p'_h=-2(1-A_{\rm old}),\quad \delta p'_R=2(1-A_{\rm old}). \tag{12} \] They lie in the relative conormal direction (8). Their independence as the two full geometric framing fields is carried by the other actual flow coordinates; it is invisible in these identical cut components. One source clock or one cut current does not determine that independent internal coordinate. ## 5. The whole clock has an exact first-normal Fr coupling The normal coupling does exist, but it uses more data than a root clock value. Before specializing let Q=q^2, Z=Q^N, delta=1-Z, and retain the actual unwrapped color clock \[ C_Q=Q^{J_{\rm un}}=Q^S Z^R. \tag{13} \] Let e(q)=tau E^(N)(q) and f(q)=F^(N)(q) be the actual generic integral divided matrices; the sign tau is constant on the marked root. They lower and raise R by one, respectively, while preserving S. Thus matrix grading alone proves the exact whole identities \[ [e(q),C_Q]=(Z-1)C_Qe(q),\qquad [f(q),C_Q]=(Z^{-1}-1)C_Qf(q). \tag{14} \] Regular division and the root evaluation give the actual normal cut-current insertions \[ [\,[e,C_Q]/\delta\,]_0=-A e_0,\qquad [\,[f,C_Q]/\delta\,]_0=A f_0. \tag{15} \] The same identities hold for the true tensor divided coproduct and the TOTAL clock: every mixed coproduct term lowers or raises the unwrapped total index by N. Hence (14)--(15) retain those mixed terms, rather than replacing a divided Hopf action by a primitive single-factor commutator. Actual R intertwining and total-index conservation transport this normal identity through every crossing; closing strands still requires its actual pivotal and relative co-source rows. ### The full head resolvent in the correct polarization The whole transformed clock can itself be written explicitly. Write zeta=Q_N while Q remains the variable in the ORIGINAL q-family, and keep H_0 fixed at zeta. Equation (3a) gives \[ C_Q^{H_0}=Z^R\Psi_Q(V),\qquad \Psi_Q(V)=\sum_{\ell=0}^{N-1} \frac{1-Q^N}{N(1-Q\zeta^\ell)}V^\ell. \tag{15a} \] Every quotient in (15a) is the polynomial N^(-1) sum_(s=0)^(N-1)(Q zeta^ell)^s. In particular its resonant 0/0 at ell=N-1 is not separately evaluated or removed. This identity follows from the exact finite Fourier sum; it retains the entire whole function before restricting its normal jets. Its first normal is \[ \begin{split} C_Q^{H_0}=V^{-1}+\delta\bigg[ -RV^{-1}-\frac{N-1}{2N}V^{-1} +\sum_{\ell\ne N-1}\frac{V^\ell}{N(1-\zeta^{\ell+1})} \bigg]+O(\delta^2). \end{split} \tag{15b} \] Thus the needed head pseudoinverse coefficients arise from the actual Fourier-clock operator; they are not guessed to make two classical vector fields agree. Equivalently the head part is -V^(-1) Shat/N, where Shat=Fourier S Fourier^(-1). Its operator norm is (N-1)/N in the root unit metric, since Fourier has condition number one. The individual nonresonant coefficients and their resonant diagonal term must be kept together. Let e_t(q)=H_0 e(q)H_0^(-1), f_t(q)=H_0 f(q)H_0^(-1). Their root values are the compensated generators e_Fr V^(-1) and f_Fr V. They commute with the reduced whole head function Psi_Q(V) for ALL q, because e(q),f(q) preserve S. Consequently the head terms in their differentiated commutator cancel exactly. The extra R term of (15b) alone supplies the remaining normal interaction: \[ [e_t(0),-RV^{-1}]=-e_{\rm Fr}V^{-2},\qquad [f_t(0),-RV^{-1}]=f_{\rm Fr}. \tag{15c} \] These are precisely -C_0 e_t(0) and C_0 f_t(0) from (15), with C_0=V^(-1). This is an explicit actual normal crossing/current Hamiltonian identity in the CORRECT shift polarization. It shows where the head resolvents cancel and where the surviving Fr normal current originates, rather than identifying it from orbit names. The whole source gauge does not invalidate the calculation. If K_src=I+delta K_1+..., it adds [K_1,C_0] and [K_1,e_t(0)] to the two first coefficients. Their extra commutator contributions sum to [K_1,[e_t(0),C_0]]=0 by Jacobi; similarly for f. Thus the normal coupling is preserved with the actual compression unit and source germ retained. Nothing here removes the finite endpoint or relative normal co-source when the word is closed. ### A nonzero actual old-clock normal map to the unprojectivized source line Keeping the source line, rather than only its normalized projector, provides a concrete additional comparison. Let r=N. On each actual residue string use the homogeneous divided source \[ \psi_s(q;a,b)=a^N\exp((b/a)F^{(N)}(q))w_{0,s},\quad U_s(q;a,b)=\Lambda_s(q)\psi_s(q;a,b), \tag{15d} \] where Lambda_s is the original actual divided co-source. The first formula extends polynomially at a=0, since the terminating degree-R term is a^(N-R)b^R(F^(N))^R/R!. At the root \[ U_s(q_N;a,b)=((a+b)/2)^N=:U_*. \] On a+b!=0 the U_s are units as whole q-germs. Keep the exact root-one ratios and define the actual source/co-source \[ \psi=\sum_s\psi_s,\qquad \Lambda=\frac1N\sum_s\frac{U_0}{U_s}\Lambda_s, \qquad\Lambda\psi=U_0. \tag{15e} \] This is the whole retraction with a COMMON UNNORMALIZED source line. Normalizing by U_0 returns the original scalar high-color period; retaining it records the actual weight-N scale character. The ratios U_0/U_s, with all their normal derivatives, have not been set equal to their root value one. For the actual old whole clock (13), finite matrix multiplication gives the exact whole formula \[ \Lambda C_Q\psi =\frac{U_0(q;a,b)}N\sum_{s=0}^{N-1}Q^s \frac{U_s(q;a,bZ)}{U_s(q;a,b)}. \tag{15f} \] Its root value is zero, but its regular normal quotient is \[ \boxed{\left[\frac{\Lambda C_Q\psi}{1-Q^N}\right]_{q_N} =\frac{((a+b)/2)^N}{N(1-Q_N)}.} \tag{15g} \] Here is a proof retaining the source derivatives. Put D_Q=Q d/dQ. The derivative of the ratio in (15f) is, at the root, N mu with mu=b partial_b log U_*=Nb/(a+b), independent of s. The explicit q-derivatives of the two U_s cancel in the ratio; they were not assumed zero. This Fr mean term and the derivative of U_0 multiply sum_s Q_N^s=0. The remaining head term is \[ \left.D_Q(\Lambda C_Q\psi)\right|_0 =\frac{U_*}N\sum_s sQ_N^s=\frac{U_*}{Q_N-1}, \qquad D_Q(1-Q^N)|_0=-N, \] which proves (15g) by regular division at the simple normal zero. The entire expression (15f), not independent Taylor choices at each string, specifies the lift being divided. Thus the known head unit N(1-Q_N) extracts the actual source character U_* from a literal OLD-cut-clock normal co-source. Its inverse has uniformly bounded modulus: 1/(2pi)<=|1/[N(1-Q_N)]|<=1/4. No exponential adapter is hidden in this factor. For an actual scalar long-knot matrix the same calculation gives U_* K_N/[N(1-Q_N)] at the root, with the original external peripheral line separately retained. There is an exact root Borel-character statement as well. The actual divided source is the degree-N coherent vector of (a,b), and its fixed root row is the N-th symmetric power of (1,1)/2. If (1,1)g=chi(g)(1,1), then U_*(g(a,b))=chi(g)^N U_*(a,b). Equation (15g) is a nonzero equivariant map to this weight-N source line. At the equal-flag anchor the generator e+f, which fixes the normalized projector, acts on the unnormalized source with weight N. That previously invisible scale has therefore been retained by an ACTUAL clock-normal map, rather than inserted after identifying two abstract Borel groups. This is a map of the cut/normal source CHARACTER. It does not equate the old clock value with a function of a+b, identify its two full internal framing currents, or prove a geometric summand survives the original finite cut. Dividing by U_0 at the outset would discard exactly the scale which (15g) detects. At this SELECTED SCALAR order the reduced clock Q^S gives the same answer: its omitted Fr-mean term already vanishes in the root head sum. Thus (15g) alone does not distinguish the whole and reduced normal actions. Their distinction is the operator/current identity (14)--(15), not an inferred independent scalar Fr current. By contrast e(q) and f(q) commute with the reduced clock Q^S for ALL q. Consequently (15) depends on the chosen whole lift (13). Two observables with the same numerical root value give different normal currents. This is exactly the whole-variable datum needed before quantum jets are restricted. There is also a precise limitation. The operation delta^(-1)ad(e) is not a regular derivation of the entire Fr source algebra: [e_0,f_0]=h_0 is generally nonzero. On delta times a lifted matrix g its root value is [e_0,g_0], not zero. It therefore does not descend to the root quotient independently of the lift. Equations (14)--(15) define a normal/source-complex insertion with a specified whole clock, not an ordinary classical vector field on every root observable. The normal connection, source unit, and endpoints are essential to extending it. ## 6. What the current dictionary now requires The actual old head Hamiltonians and fields are explicitly given by (4), (7), and (12), while (14)--(15) are an actual Fr-normal coupling with every tensor mixed term retained. These are the two concrete inputs to the missing framing-current comparison. Simply mapping the Fr coherent quadric to the physical meridian graph does not intertwine them, as (9)--(10) proves at the selected source. In particular the bare Fr commutator fields cannot be substituted for the two cut-Borel fields while preserving a clock A=e^(cT). In x=Log v,T coordinates their actual coherent values are \[ X_e=v\partial_x+v(1-T)\partial_T,\quad X_f=-v^{-1}\partial_x-Tv^{-1}\partial_T,\quad X_h=2\partial_x. \] A fixed linear combination has T velocity alpha v(1-T)-beta T/v. This can be a function of T alone only if alpha=beta=0, whereas (11) requires a nonzero such function. Head/source-dependent coefficients and the normal lift are therefore necessary. Their existence as rational or logarithmic functions is not itself the missing network-current identity. No claim is made that this dictionary already kills the two full Green boundaries or produces a nonzero full geometric period. It specifies which physical observable, normal insertion and relative conormal class the required map must preserve. [Exact finite and symbolic audit](../experiments/audit_controlled_fourier_current_dictionary.py). The tests concern the actual matrix/current identities and the quadratic canonical map, not global cycle selection or asymptotics. The [saved results](../experiments/controlled_fourier_current_dictionary_results.json) pass seven full finite gauges N=2,...,8, both marked complete meridian lifts, three Fr flag pairs, five actual normal families N=2,...,6, and 323 nonzero mixed divided-coproduct entries. Twenty actual divided-source cone checks include both polynomial endpoints a=0 or b=0. Thirty nonconstant head-dependent source normal units are retained in those tests; they have not been replaced by constant binomial coefficients before checking (15g).

title: Critical-path audit of the original volume-conjecture goal
text: # Critical-path audit of the original volume-conjecture goal **Source-to-volume variational step audited, 29 October.** The [general certificate](source_volume_casson_rivin_certificate.md) and [full-tangent audit](source_angle_stationarity_critical_audit.md) prove why the selected source point maximizes the CORRECT filled-slope angle functional. This requires full complex edge gluing and real peripheral slope equations, not just a restricted source saddle. The [direct positive ideal chart](actual_pretzel_positive_ideal_angle_certificate.md) supplies the actual family's ideal triangulation and quotient rank without a general existence theorem. Primitive end completion gives V_src,s(p)=Vol(actual filled complement). The geometric step is closed for the current source theorem; broader original-source asymptotics remain the general goal's unresolved part. **Broader equality goal active, 29 October.** The [current frontier](general_equality_frontier.md) records the new concrete quantum scope s>=9 and the general geometric completion theorem for arbitrary cusped hyperbolic bases. The latter settles which hyperbolic volume is involved whenever the actual selected representation and primitive periods are supplied. The remaining broad task is an original whole-source geometric packet and global gap beyond the pretzel graph. A conditional propagation theorem is not a proof of those hypotheses and is not completion of this broader goal. **Full equality established, 29 October.** The original goal is equality, not the intermediate upper bound. The [geometric completion theorem](actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md) now proves the source-selected representation is the holonomy of a complete positively oriented hyperbolic metric on the actual filled knot. The [Casson--Rivin proof](actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) puts the source point at the unique maximum on its filled-slope angle slice. Together with the entire-source nonzero asymptotic this yields the original Kashaev volume equality for every fixed odd s>=25 and independently sufficiently long fixed signed p_i. See the [requirement-by-requirement equality audit](long_pretzel_volume_equality_completion_audit.md). The general conjecture beyond this class remains outside the theorem. All earlier checkpoints below are historical. **Upper-bound milestone completed, 29 October.** The [assembled full-source theorem](actual_long_pretzel_sharp_volume_upper_bound.md) proves an existing limit bounded above by the ACTUAL filled hyperbolic volume for every fixed odd width s>=25 and all independently sufficiently large fixed signed twists, assuming the knot is hyperbolic. Its selected rate is exactly the volume of an explicitly constructed representation of the filled knot group. The [completion audit](long_pretzel_upper_bound_completion_audit.md) records the analytic and geometric dependencies. This meets the stated sharp-upper-bound alternative. Full volume-conjecture equality still requires proving that the selected representation has the geometric volume; no such equality is claimed. The checkpoints below are historical. **Whole filled-source survival, 29 October.** The [full original long-pretzel source theorem](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md) now proves a nonzero asymptotic for every fixed odd s>=25 and all independently sufficiently large fixed signed p_i. This is the whole color sum for R^(-(2p_i+1)), not just an augmented link or a cusp subsum. The [global alias/core estimates](actual_pretzel_global_alias_and_colored_source_gap.md) control every complementary color, including the even middle color. The [corridor theorem](actual_pretzel_cusp_corridor_filling_survival.md) retains every Fourier endpoint current and proves exact addition of the minimal signed charges. Its rate is 2pi Re A_s(p), and its original leading coefficient is nonzero at all sufficiently large N. The remaining critical assertion is equality of that selected source rate with the correctly marked filled hyperbolic volume, or a sharp geometric upper bound for it. A regular lift of this selected critical point to the actual knot representation and its calibrated regulator would supply the relevant comparison. The matching cusp Hessian is evidence of a coordinate convention, not proof of that lift. Do not mark the original goal complete before this step is established. The status paragraphs below predate the whole filled-source theorem. **Complete augmented-base gate closed, 29 October.** The [full coherent period theorem](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) now proves a nonzero original leading coefficient at EVERY fixed odd pretzel width s>=3, both N parities, with all Casimir normals and finite winding weights retained. It combines exact inner elimination, a uniform two-branch Ward estimate, a sharp global circle bound and two real Gaussian calculations. The equal-height boundary obstruction is resolved for this source by the finite transformation; it is not assumed away. The explicit positive Fourier energy also has the sharp rate, so this milestone goes beyond another source identity or a formal saddle. The independently constructed geometric right side is the [actual complete augmented link volume](actual_augmented_pretzel_geometric_volume.md). The [complete-point normalization audit](actual_complete_augmented_source_normalization.md) also proves exact equality of absolute values with the original reduced Kashaev link invariant; the full one-cut modified convention contributes the retained factor i^(N+3)/N. No exponential external factor is left unexamined at this complete point. The remaining original-knot critical path is now the coherent filling problem: control the full mixed-color source and its actual filling sum, with the filled volume rather than the larger unfilled volume. The complete base is a link with s+1 components. Its theorem does not settle the fixed pretzel knots, general alternating knots, or arbitrary augmented diagrams. The quantitative 56^r cusp remainder estimate remains available, but survival of ONE complete-color term cannot be substituted for survival of that entire filling sum. Earlier status paragraphs below predate this complete-base theorem. **Current critical gate, 29 October.** A [positive reflected-circle metric](actual_complete_circle_reflection_positive.md) now has EXACT polynomial boundary costs on the original physical source, including the [marked all-width closure](actual_reflection_marked_boundary_metric.md). Thus the requested special-inner-product Cauchy inequality is proved. Its energy has not been bounded by the geometric angle partition. For arbitrary odd numbers of augmented pretzel boxes, the complete original source reduces to one [explicit half-degree Casimir polynomial](actual_pretzel_complete_base_casimir_polynomial.md), with all root values, normal derivatives and finite winding weights. The [marked stationary phase calculation](actual_pretzel_winding_phase_and_geometric_saddles.md) and its [independent audit](actual_pretzel_geometric_symbol_audit.md) prove the nondegenerate regular geometric branch and its antiprism Lobachevsky action, including a strict gap to the other regular mixed branches on the specified chart. These do NOT prove that the original period has that leading term. Its actual diagonal endpoint has [exactly the same exponential height](actual_pretzel_radial_boundary_gap.md); a strict endpoint-gap shortcut is false. The remaining analytic task is coherent control of that endpoint with the interior contribution, and a global sharp circle bound or nonzero selected-cycle coefficient. The [defect theorem](charged_star_triangle_defect_jets.md) extends this to sum L_i=2d-e, each pair sum>=d. The exact contracted polynomial is a specified triangle product times a degree-e polynomial R_e, whose marked coefficient c_e is explicit and nonzero. The uniform norm estimate has logarithm O(e log(1+N/e)+log(e+1)) after division by |c_e|. Thus EVERY sublinear e=o(N), including a growing Gaussian window, costs exp(o(N)). Its rate is explicitly calibrated: the scalar gives TWO limiting ideal-tetrahedron volumes under 2pi/N normalization. No factor of two or residual source polynomial is lost. On the unit anchor torus, the incidence defect S_a-2d is exactly twice the angular source-phase frequency, away from factor zeros. The [global cut-jet theorem](charged_source_cut_jets.md) uses e_I=d|I|-m_I, where m_I counts factors wholly in the anchor set I. Negative e_I annihilates the selected coefficient; e_I=0 factors it with its exact outside endpoint monomials. General e_I retains its precise boundary-choice jet. Joint flags and weighted rays cover coordinate corners with no omitted normal source. Sublinear boundary deficits have exp(o(N)) boundary-choice norm. Feasible endpoint assignments canonically factor into strongly connected residual cores; feasibility itself does NOT prevent phase cancellation. The [feedback theorem](actual_clock_feedback_normal_form.md) separately performs every bridge charge sum with all Fourier fugacities retained. The whole original source includes the explicit operation R^nu Y^h -> Q^(nu^T T h)R^nu Y^h, for its actual integer underhistory matrix T. It does not descend to evaluation Y=1. Suppressing it changes original invariant values even in the figure-eight example. Its unit coefficient norm is not a noncancellation theorem for the final source. All of these are exact or quantitatively controlled reductions of the ORIGINAL state, applicable beyond any fixed knot list. They do not show that its surviving cores have sublinear defects, nor that its geometric contribution is nonzero after the remaining clock sum and source pairing. Macroscopic defects and phase cancellation remain the central global difficulty. Gates C, D and the sharp scalar part of E remain open; the active volume-conjecture goal is not complete. ## 26. Forced critical flow and a required macroscopic source sector 28 October 2026. The previous continuation proved exact fusion and sublinear-jet norm estimates. This turn tests whether that regime contains the actual leading state, rather than assuming that it does. For the actual unit-factor polynomial and charges q_i, put delta_i=S_i-2q_i, where S_i counts incident factors. At every regular anchor critical point the [new flow theorem](charged_critical_flow_and_chambers.md) gives EXACTLY sum_(f joining i,j) (|X_i|^2-|X_j|^2)/|alpha_f X_i-beta_f X_j|^2=-delta_i. All conductances are positive. For a high-radius cut I with gap g, C_I crossing factors and source deficit e_I, this implies C_I tanh(g/2)<=2e_I-C_I, g<=log(e_I/(C_I-e_I)). The exact residual-core factorization already proved gives strict integer Hall margins 1<=e_I<=C_I-1. Consequently every regular critical point of a k-anchor, M-factor core satisfies max_i |X_i| / min_i |X_i| <= (M-1)^(k-1). For a fixed diagram M=O(N), so this is uniform polynomial radial properness, without assuming small defects. A fixed fractional cut margin improves it to a bound independent of N. This concerns regular anchor criticals at actual integer clocks; complex clock continuation and noncoordinate collisions are separate problems. If all defects vanish, the maximum principle forces all radii equal. On the original unit torus, log modulus is strictly concave on each angular chamber and phase is constant there. There is one nondegenerate critical point per chamber. If opposite-sign chambers have a strict exponential height gap, a direct Fourier derivative bound gives a nonzero selected coefficient with the maximal rate. This supplies an actual source-accessibility mechanism in its stated class, not an assumed unknown geometric intersection number. The [all-level alternating-source theorem](actual_alternating_balanced_source.md) then checks applicability. After exact closure contraction, each alternating-knot anchor has delta_(i->j)=h_i-h_j along the cyclic physical overencounter order. Balance therefore forces all clocks equal. For the ORIGINAL figure-eight word the valid whole trace source and its pointwise cyclic support imply h_0=0, h_1+h_3>=N-1 in every nonzero fixed-clock coefficient. Its defects are exactly (-h_3,h_1,h_2-h_1,h_3-h_2). Hence max_i |delta_i| >= (N-1)/2. Every balanced sector, and every sequence with all defects o(N), vanishes in this representation. These are exact original-source support statements, independently proved and audited, not numerical claims about saddle dominance. They do NOT rule out later full-block contractions or cluster fusions that combine opposite defects. They do rule out using the current sublinear pointwise jet regime as the whole invariant before such a proved reduction. The [critical-selection audit](charged_torus_critical_selection.md) also proves that properness, source flatness and a unique largest critical value do not by themselves force a contribution. Its explicit unit-cyclotomic coefficient example has uniform strict Hall margins, yet an exact Cauchy-circle bound excludes its highest critical value. It is not a knot counterexample; it identifies the extra source selection content needed in a valid theorem. Two proposed shortcuts have exact source checks: the [feedback Gaussian](actual_feedback_geometric_selection_obstruction.md) is a decoupled normalized unit and leaves the original critical germ unchanged; an [ordinary common Möbius action](actual_nilpotent_mobius_source_and_ward_obstruction.md) does not intertwine the original crossing or supply its framing co-source. These operations cannot supply a missing geometric coefficient simply from their algebraic existence. The constructive next target is the macroscopic forced core, with its original clock feedback and selected source, or an exact global fusion which absorbs those defects before applying tame-jet estimates. The general regulator/period selection and sharp scalar estimate remain open. No new broad knot class is asserted to satisfy the original volume conjecture; the active goal remains incomplete.

title: The actual crossing sum and the complete Bloch fundamental class
text: # The actual crossing sum and the complete Bloch fundamental class Research note, 26 October 2026. This closes a classical comparison left open in [the marked braid note](marked_braid_holonomy.md). The setting is an oriented hyperbolic knot complement, its complete geometric representation, and the actual reduced ADO crossing conventions already fixed. At the complete color the crossing Bloch sum is the oriented idealized fundamental class. In particular its Bloch--Wigner regulator is the hyperbolic volume. The comparison is in the rational oriented pre-Bloch group. It does not identify an integral flattening, a full complex quantum period, or the component selected by the actual finite contraction. The original volume conjecture remains unproved. ## 1. Statement and conventions Use the balanced factorial basis of the preceding note. For q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^alpha and M=-qx, its positive crossing has input A=Q^a,B=Q^b, shift C=Q^k, and symbol beta_+=[B]+[C]+[x^2/A]-[BC]-[x^2C/A]. (1.1) The inverse crossing has the independently checked symbol beta_-=[A]+[C]+[x^2/B]-[AC]-[x^2C/B]. (1.2) At the classical complete color M=1, x=-1. The actual critical correspondence supplies meridians mu_j=-H_j of trace 2, and their Hurwitz crossing relation. Fix the geometric representation with the orientation of the knot exterior. Let beta_D be the sum of (1.1)--(1.2) over the diagram at this critical representation, with its regular frame. Then beta_D=beta_[M,partial M] in P(C) tensor Q, D(beta_D)=Vol(M). (1.3) Here the right side is the marked idealized fundamental class, not an unspecified lift of the peripheral wedge. If T is the positive complete triangulation supplied by the audited existence theorem, the same statement is beta_D=sum_(Delta in T)[z_Delta]. (1.4) It is useful to separate this from the remaining quantum claim: (1.3) identifies the classical Bloch period attached to the actual coefficients. It does not prove the growth rate of their sum. We use normalized oriented configurations: a tuple with repeated developed points is zero, and reversing a tetrahedron reverses its symbol rationally. Cross-ratios are r(v0,v1,v2,v3) =det(v3,v1)det(v2,v0)/(det(v3,v0)det(v2,v1)), r(infinity,0,1,z)=z. (1.5) The boundary of five points is the five-term relation. If some points coincide, its remaining alternating terms cancel in pairs. Thus normalized degenerate configurations cause no additional Bloch generator. This matters for diagrams with redundant arcs. ## 2. Region vectors come directly from the actual holonomy chart Consider a positive crossing. Write a for the over-meridian, b for the incoming under-meridian, and c=a^(-1)ba for the outgoing under-meridian. The same letters in a tetrahedron denote their unique fixed flags. Choose unipotent SL(2) lifts. Choose a generic region vector s and an auxiliary vector p. Put s_0=s, s_M=a s, s_P=c s, s_R=b a s=a c s, p_1=a p, w_i=det(p,s_i). (2.1) Region vectors propagate across an oriented arc by its meridian or inverse. The equality ba=ac is exactly the consistency condition at a crossing. Hence the data propagate over the projection sphere; all dual-face relations are these crossing relations. The initial region vector is arbitrary. These are the same region words obtained by multiplying the actual Hurwitz meridians, not an additional representation. To verify the coordinates, let P_j=mu_j...mu_1 in a braid slice, and set w_j=(P_j)_11 in the frame p=(0,1),s=(1,0). The previous Gauss reconstruction gives K_j=-(w_j/w_(j-1)), A_j=x/K_j. The minus sign is from H_j=-mu_j. At x=-1, near one crossing, A=w_0/w_M, B=w_M/w_R, C=w_0 w_R/(w_M w_P). (2.2) The last relation follows equally from C=K_2/K'_1. Therefore the actual expression (1.1) becomes [w_M/w_R]+[w_0w_R/(w_Mw_P)]+[w_M/w_0] -[w_0/w_P]-[w_R/w_P]. (2.3) The nondegenerate Gauss chart constructed in the preceding note keeps these five arguments away from 0 and 1. The auxiliary vectors can additionally avoid the finitely many coincidences used in the calculations below. ## 3. An explicit three-five-term certificate Write T(v0,v1,v2,v3) for the oriented tetrahedron symbol in (1.5). The fixed flag of a is also denoted a, and similarly for b,c. Unipotence and determinant preservation give T(a,p,s_0,s_M)=[w_M/w_0], T(b,p,s_M,s_R)=[w_R/w_M], T(a,p,s_P,s_R)=[w_R/w_P], T(c,p,s_0,s_P)=[w_P/w_0], T(s_M,s_R,p_1,p)=[w_0w_R/(w_Mw_P)]. (3.1) For the middle identity, use det(p_1,s_M)=det(p,s_0) and det(p_1,s_R)=det(p,s_P). For the other four, the relevant unipotent meridian fixes its cusp vector with eigenvalue one. These are determinant identities, including their signs. The five-term sum (2.3) consequently equals T(a,p,s_0,s_M)-T(b,p,s_M,s_R) -T(a,p,s_P,s_R)+T(c,p,s_0,s_P) +T(s_M,s_R,p_1,p). (3.2) It equals the four-tetrahedron shadow expression Gamma=-T(p,a,c,s_0)+T(p,a,c,s_P) +T(p,a,b,s_M)-T(p,a,b,s_R). (3.3) Here is a finite certificate, rather than an appeal to a shadow-volume theorem. Apply a to the whole tetrahedra containing c,s_0,s_P; this replaces them by b,s_M,s_R and changes their auxiliary p to p_1. Cross-ratios are invariant. After those replacements, the difference of (3.2) and (3.3) is J=T(a,p,s_0,s_M)+T(a,p,p_1,s_M) -T(a,p,s_P,s_R)-T(a,p,p_1,s_R), (3.4) modulo the following explicit five-vertex boundaries: -partial(b,p,p_1,s_M,s_R) +partial(a,b,p,p_1,s_M) -partial(a,b,p,p_1,s_R). (3.5) Expansion of the alternating boundaries verifies (3.5) as a formal oriented-chain identity. Finally J=0. To see this, send a to infinity. Its meridian acts as z->z+t, t!=0. For z=r(a,p,s,a s), one has r(a,p,a p,a s)=z/(z-1). The two symbols cancel by [z/(z-1)]=-[z]. Apply this to s=s_0 and s=s_P in (3.4). This proves (3.3) in the rational pre-Bloch group, without a regulator limit. For a negative crossing, use the same block read backwards with reversed orientation. The actual inverse formula agrees: substituting (A,B,C)->(B/C,AC,1/C) in beta_+ gives -beta_-. Thus the certificate applies to both actual crossings. ## 4. The four tetrahedra form the diagram crossing block The local vertex order is (p,over,under,region), with four tetrahedra and coefficients | Tetrahedron | Developed vertices | Orientation | | --- | --- | --- | | 0 | (p,a,c,s_0) | -1 | | 1 | (p,a,c,s_P) | +1 | | 2 | (p,a,b,s_M) | +1 | | 3 | (p,a,b,s_R) | -1 | Faces are numbered by the omitted local vertex. The internal face pairings are (0,0)<->(2,0), (1,0)<->(3,0), (0,3)<->(1,3), (2,3)<->(3,3), (4.1) with identity vertex maps on their faces. The first two have developing transport a, because (a,c,s_0)->(a,b,s_M) and (a,c,s_P)->(a,b,s_R). The other two have transport one. The underlying block is a ball. Its tetrahedra attach in the order 0,1,2,3 along 0,1,1,2 previous faces; the last two faces are adjacent. Its six vertices are over, under, P_01, P_23, S_02, S_13. There are eight exterior triangles and twelve exterior edges, the octahedral graph. Its sole internal edge joins over to under and has valence four. To see the developed octahedron, transport tetrahedra 2,3 by a^(-1). Its vertices are then a,c,p,a^(-1)p,s_0,s_P. (4.2) Thus the occurrence of different b/c and region flags is ordinary face transport in this same crossing ball. For an explicit orientation check, use over=(0,0,1), under=(0,0,-1), P_01=(1,0,0), P_23=(-1,0,0), S_02=(0,1,0), S_13=(0,-1,0). The determinants in the four displayed vertex orders are -2,2,2,-2. These are exactly the signs in the table. The over-strand runs north to south and the under-strand west to east, giving a positive crossing in the oriented projection chart. Reverse the block for a negative crossing. Its four strand-end slots consist of two triangles each: | Positive-crossing end | Left region face | Right region face | | --- | --- | --- | | over input | (0,2) | (2,2) | | over output | (1,2) | (3,2) | | under input b | (2,1) | (3,1) | | under output c | (0,1) | (1,1) | Join each output to the next input along the diagram strand, preserving p, the arc vertex, the region vertex, and left/right side. For a negative crossing interchange the inputs and outputs and reverse all four orientations. This specifies every face pairing, including braid closure, without a knot-by-knot choice. ### Why this is the complement, with degree one Here is the cellular reconstruction. Cut the projection sphere into crossing disks and the intervening arc/region strips. Use one pole in each of the two complementary projection balls. The dual decomposition relative to the over- and underpass bands has one crossing ball with an over-to-under diagonal and four alternating pole/region corners. Subdivide it about that diagonal: its four pieces and their internal faces are exactly (4.1). At an arc strip the two exposed triangles on each side are identified to those on the next crossing, preserving the three vertex types. These are exactly the slots in the table. The remaining pieces are the two pole stars and the regular neighborhood of the knot. Consequently truncating the knot vertex gives the exterior; the two pole stars are balls. Taking the barycentric subdivision before this dual subdivision gives a common subdivision with the original projection-ball decomposition. Thus these identifications do not attach an additional handle or a covering of a crossing neighborhood. There is also a direct peripheral degree check. Truncate the over and under vertices of the four oriented tetrahedra. With outward boundary orientation their link triangles are over: - (p,c,s_0)+(p,c,s_P) +(p,b,s_M)-(p,b,s_R), under: (p,a,s_0)-(p,a,s_P) -(p,a,s_M)+(p,a,s_R). (4.3) At the over vertex, transport the first two triangles by a. The two copies of p differ by p->a p, a *single* meridian translation. At an underpass the chart changes by a^(-1), the actual Wirtinger transport c=a^(-1)ba. Along each oriented strand the left and right region edges in (4.3) join to the next end in the slot table. Following all ends around a knot therefore gives one meridional circle times one traversal of the knot. Its longitudinal transition is the blackboard longitude. Replacing that by the preferred longitude subtracts the writhe times the meridian, a determinant-one shear of the peripheral basis. Hence the cusp cycle has degree one, not an unspecified multiple of the peripheral torus. For a hyperbolic knot exterior H_3(M)=H_2(M)=0, so the boundary map H_3(M,partial M)->H_2(partial M) is an isomorphism. The degree-one check, with the orientation already fixed, identifies this chain with [M,partial M]. ## 5. Face cancellation also checks the flat bundle and marking The boundary of (3.3), after the a-transport on the faces without p, is B(s_0,c)-B(s_M,b)-B(s_0,a)+B(s_P,a), B(s,g)=(p,g,s)-(p,g,g s). (5.1) The face calculation uses no volume formula. Each B is the two region-side faces at one strand end. The slot table makes them cancel with the neighboring end, so the global cycle is closed in the ideal configuration complex. Local monodromy about the over-arc is a, and underpass transport is c=a^(-1)ba; thus the developed flat bundle is the specified representation rho. The two extra vertex orbits are free vertices, while the knot vertex has the peripheral stabilizer. One can formalize the comparison in the augmented configuration complex on Gamma/P disjoint-union Gamma.p disjoint-union Gamma.s. It is acyclic by coning a finite cycle from a fresh vertex. In positive chain degrees its Gamma-action is free, using peripheral malnormality. Its degree-three coinvariant homology therefore realizes the relative group homology of (Gamma,P); the two extra trivial stabilizers add no H_2 term. The cusp link in (4.3) is exactly its connecting map to H_2(P). This also explains why the extra projection poles do not change the relative fundamental class. Map a developed tetrahedron to its cross-ratio symbol. The five-point boundary is the five-term relation, so the map depends only on this relative fundamental class. Two developed presentations of that same class have equal rational pre-Bloch images. Apply it to the diagram cycle and to the positive geometric triangulation T. Equations (3.2)--(3.5) then prove (1.3)--(1.4). Signed or degenerate tetrahedra in the diagram cause no problem; T supplies the positive representative. ## 6. The generic peripheral correction is retained The cancellation of J in (3.4) used unipotence. Its generic form is explicit, so this argument does not erase meridian information before the complete specialization. Keep M generic. In the actual Gauss chart the region expression for beta_+ is [M w_M/w_R]+[w_0w_R/(w_Mw_P)]+[M w_M/w_0] -[M w_0/w_P]-[M w_R/w_P]. (6.1) For its four outer tetrahedra choose the M-eigenflag of the over-meridian and the M^(-1)-eigenflags of the under-meridians. The two eigenflag choices are intentionally distinguished. Determinant preservation gives exactly the factors in (6.1). The same three five-term boundaries leave J=F_(M^2)(z_0)-F_(M^2)(z_P), F_kappa(z)=[z]+[z/(z-kappa)], z_0=M w_M/w_0, z_P=M w_R/w_P. (6.2) To verify it, put the over-eigenflag at infinity. Its projective action is z->kappa*z+t, kappa=M^2. If z=r(a,p,s,a s), direct subtraction gives r(a,p,a p,a s)=z/(z-kappa). For kappa=1 the two oriented symbols cancel. Away from it they give an explicit correction to the class, and the two eigenflags need not agree on neighboring strand roles. The cut's selected flag in the previous note was the M^(-1)-flag; that distinction must be transported in a family-level comparison. Equation (1.3) is a complete-color statement, not a generic-meridian identity obtained by silently identifying the two flags. The quantum factor d_N(M), its wall/central-defect ratio, and all meridian germs remain exactly as in the preceding notes. Vanishing of the classical correction at M=1 is not permission to discard its meridian jets or a quantum specialization factor. ## 7. Scope, coverage, and checks The classical shadow-volume construction has existing coverage in [Inoue--Kabaya](https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.2923), and diagrammatic potential/volume comparisons in [Cho](https://doi.org/10.1017/S144678871600001X). These were checked for coverage after deriving the certificate and face table. Their proofs are not premises here. The contribution to this project is an explicit comparison in the actual ADO source and meridian conventions, not a novelty claim for shadow volumes. The [audit](../experiments/audit_crossing_fundamental_cycle.py) and [results](../experiments/crossing_fundamental_cycle_results.json) check the three five-term boundaries as a formal chain identity, the five determinant identities and parabolic cancellation, the generic affine correction, the octahedral shelling and orientation, and the global face pairing. With --regina it checks eleven diagrams, including both stabilizations, a cancelling pair, multiple components, and mixed signs. Every constructed triangulation is exactly isomorphic to the independently constructed, *unsimplified* Regina link complement. This is stronger validation than a match of homology or volume; the general identification is the cellular argument above. A complex calibration compares both local crossing orientations and the global two-tetrahedron regulator in three frames. The complete classical Bloch--Wigner comparison is now supplied. Integral flattenings, the full complex period, source-preserving quantum transport, survival of the geometric branch after elimination, and its contribution to the actual selected quantum period remain separate. In particular, (1.3) does not imply (2pi/N)log|<K>_N| -> Vol(M). That original conjecture remains the active target.

title: Full crossing spectra distinguish the two actual normal paths
text: # Full crossing spectra distinguish the two actual normal paths Independent proof and audit, 27 October 2026. The whole Gamma comparison transports actual scalar source factors. It cannot be extended to a scalar-adjusted similarity of the two checked crossing matrices on the same finite tensor fiber. This failure holds for every level, including arbitrary nondiagonal gauges. It does not exclude transport of the base, a relative kernel, or an enlarged normal module. The local coefficient comparison is [the actual crossing calculation](actual_crossing_q_normal_meridian_ratio.md). The compatible constructive statement is the [whole bulk response](quantum_normal_crossing_bulk_response.md). ## 1. Exact spectra and the general obstruction Write \(n=N-1\). On the highest-weight basis use \[ K u_i=q^{\alpha-2i}u_i,\qquad Fu_i=u_{i+1},\qquad Eu_i=[i]_q[\alpha-i+1]_q u_{i-1}. \] The actual full positive checked crossing, including its common Cartan factor, has the following generic eigenvalues: \[ r_j(q,\alpha)=(-1)^j q^{\alpha^2/2-j(2\alpha-j+1)},\qquad 0\le j<N. \tag{1} \] Here generic means away from the explicitly finite eigenvalue collision and highest-weight degeneracy loci. There are two different multiplicity formulas: * For the ordinary integral \(N\)-color, \(\alpha=n\) and generic moving \(q\), the multiplicity of \(r_j\) is \(2(n-j)+1\). * At \(q_0=e^{\pi i/N}\), for a generic typical \(N\)-color with \(\alpha=n+b\), the multiplicity of every \(r_j\) is \(N\). These multiplicity lists are different for every \(N\ge2\). Therefore the moving-\(q\) integral crossing and the fixed-root typical crossing are not similar, even after either is multiplied by any nonzero scalar function. The conclusion survives meromorphic or ramified changes of matrix basis: an equality of such matrices would imply equality over their common generic fraction field, where the eigenvalue multiplicities disagree. Retaining an additional common Cartan, zero-framing, or peripheral scalar cannot change this argument. Here is a direct proof of both formulas. At total index \(j<N\) the vector \[ v_j=\sum_{a=0}^j c_a u_a\otimes u_{j-a},\qquad c_0=1, \] in the kernel of \(\Delta E=E\otimes K+1\otimes E\) is unique for generic parameters. Successive coefficient cancellation gives \[ c_j=(-1)^j q^{-j(\alpha-j+1)}. \tag{2} \] The checked crossing preserves this highest vector line. To compute its eigenvalue, inspect the coefficient of \(u_0\otimes u_j\). In the actual \(Pq^{H\otimes H/2}\sum_k(\cdots)E^k\otimes F^k\), only the input \(u_j\otimes u_0\) with \(k=0\) can contribute. Its coefficient is \(c_jq^{\alpha^2/2-\alpha j}\), which is (1). For generic moving \(q\) and integral \(\alpha=n\), the string generated from \(v_j\) by \(\Delta F\) has highest weight \(2n-2j\) and length \(2(n-j)+1\). Indeed \[ E F^r v_j=[r]_q[2n-2j-r+1]_qF^{r-1}v_j \] proves nonvanishing through its stated length. A further nonzero vector would be a highest vector of negative integral weight; its successive \(F\)-vectors would never terminate by the same identity, contradicting finite dimension. The distinct generic Casimir eigenvalues separate these strings. Their dimensions sum to \(N^2\). At \(q_0\) and generic \(\alpha=n+b\), each string instead has exactly length \(N\). The displayed \(EF^r\) factors are nonzero for \(1\le r<N\), whereas \((\Delta F)^N=0\): the root quantum-binomial formula leaves only the two \(N\)-th powers, both zero on the actual head. Its generic Casimir eigenvalues are proportional to \(q_0^{2\alpha-2j+1}+q_0^{-2\alpha+2j-1}\); as functions of the generic meridian they are distinct for \(0\le j<N\). Thus these \(N\) independent strings exhaust the \(N^2\)-dimensional tensor product. Since the checked crossing commutes with the coproduct, its eigenvalue (1) has multiplicity \(N\). ## 2. Literal first-normal diagnostics Set \(c=2\pi i\), \(H_0=c/N\). The matched first-normal parameters may be written \[ q=q_0(1+\epsilon/N),\quad M_{\rm col}=-q^N=1+\epsilon, \qquad q=q_0,\quad M_{\rm root}=1+\epsilon,\quad \epsilon^2=0 . \] These are the tangents of \(H=H_0/(1-b/N)\), \(M_{\rm col}=e^{Hb/2}\) and \(M_{\rm root}=e^{H_0b/2}\), with \(\epsilon=cb/(2N)\). To make the normalization explicit, let \(R_0\) have the common Cartan \(q^{\alpha^2/2}\) removed, put \(x=q^\alpha=-M/q\), and use \[ \mathcal R=x^nR_0 . \] This is exactly the same-auxiliary zero-framing crossing \(R/\theta_{\rm aux}\), since \(\theta_{\rm aux}=q^{\alpha^2/2-n\alpha}\). At \(N=2\), \[ \operatorname{Tr}\mathcal R_{\rm col}=3q-q^{-1} =4q_0+\epsilon q_0, \] \[ \operatorname{Tr}\mathcal R_{\rm root} =2q_0(M+M^{-1})=4q_0+O(\epsilon^2). \tag{3} \] Thus even the first-normal traces differ in this specified normalization. An arbitrary first-normal scalar could change this one trace; the generic multiplicity theorem does not have that normalization dependence. There is also an independent module invariant. With \(\gamma=(-1)^{N-1}\), the actual \(K^N\) matrices are \[ K_{\rm col}^N =\gamma\,\operatorname{diag} (1+\epsilon(n-2j))_{j=0}^{N-1},\qquad K_{\rm root}^N=\gamma(1+N\epsilon)I . \] Their trace derivatives are \(0\) and \(\gamma N^2\). The moving-\(q\) first normal has a nonzero traceless component; the fixed-root one is scalar. Thus a strict module intertwiner retaining \(K\) already fails before forming a whole word.
