At \(b=-1\), the endpoint alias in [the coefficient audit](actual_crossing_q_normal_meridian_ratio.md) gives an additional elementary failure of sparse diagonal transport: the root coefficient with input \(i=N-1,j=0,k=1\) contains \(1-e^{-c}=0\), whereas the color coefficient contains \(1-e^{-cN/(N+1)}\ne0\). The root and color endpoint zero divisors are different. This is compatible with the folded, two-chart scalar source-factor comparison, which is not a crossing intertwiner. ## 3. Exact verification and the constructive scope [The independent script](../experiments/audit_crossing_normal_spectra.py) assembles the literal balanced checked crossing in its conserved total-index blocks. It computes all power traces and recovers the characteristic polynomial by Newton identities over finite fields and their dual numbers. It compares generic integral, generic root-meridian, integral first-normal, and root first-normal matrices at \(N=2,\ldots,8\): 840 exact characteristic coefficients pass. It also checks (3) and the two \(K^N\) trace derivatives. The full output is [the saved exact audit](../experiments/crossing_normal_spectra_results.json). The positive result that remains available is the full-source bulk insertion theorem. Its exact source factor is \[ W_{\rm aux}=\frac1N x^{n\kappa} Q^{n\sum_{\rm closed}i}\prod_t r_{0,t}, \qquad \kappa=\operatorname{writhe}-b_{\rm strands}+1 . \] The ordinary/auxiliary adapter \(q^{Nn\kappa}(Q^N)^{\sum i}\) removes the pivot-dependent linear response. Hence the remaining insertion is \((\mathcal E-1)\mathcal A\), including the constant \(c\kappa/2\) of the marked whole action. On a flattened critical block it is \(-S_{\rm geo}/c\). These source and constant signs agree directly with the literal adapter. This proves a local formal block response; it supplies neither a same-fiber crossing similarity nor a selected global period.

title: Which custom definitions can agree with the literature construction?
text: # Which custom definitions can agree with the literature construction? Research note, 25 October 2026. The earlier custom candidates are preserved in `quantum_a_volume.md`. They have different answers to the equivalence question. The exact comparison below keeps q and the peripheral variable Q generic. **Subsequent target clarification.** Kashaev's original invariant is the target; the AK/Faddeev constructions discussed below are comparison objects. The [crossing proof](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md) and [ADO pointing proof](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) now fix the original enhanced state and its meridian normalization independently of published comparison proofs. The exact triangular Kashaev crossing has, with k=a-c and d=b+k, |A_(c,d;a,b)|=s_N(a)s_N(b+k) /(s_N(a-k)s_N(b)s_N(k)). Thus the positive sine factorials occur in the actual literature kernel. Its phase, pairing, and modified-dimension lattice are also specified in those notes. This is a direct local connection with the earlier positive candidate. Equality of the full positive sum and the complex Kashaev period has not been established. ## 0. Current comparison after reviewing the notes The custom constructions are not a single definition. Their status is: | Construction | Comparison with the specified literature object | Useful result | | --- | --- | --- | | Compact local product Psi_q | Exactly the numerator factor of Faddeev Phi; its modular-dual completion is exactly Phi | A local definition that can be retained with its full completion | | Positive sine-factorial sum | No exact generic-boundary state equivalence established | An independently proved volume rate and a positive comparison action | | Naive figure-eight cone-transfer recurrence | No rational two-component gauge, even after a finite power cover of the peripheral coordinate | A classical-action/volume model with a different quantum deformation | | Minimal annihilator of the fixed Faddeev state | Uses the literature annihilator convention; existence is proved independently in the b-shift algebra | A way to formulate the volume law for the same state and operator | | Inverse Fourier transform of the normalized charged tensor | Exactly recovers the preceding meridian state in ordinary charts and extends it to a moving longitude plane | A tensor-derived state and volume theorem for every globally branched complete positive geometric chart | For the last row, `general_annihilator_and_volume.md` supplies the existence and geometric-component arguments. The uniform twist geometry and the subsequent `twist_topology_and_peripherals.md` now supply the explicit twist-knot realizations and preferred peripheral certificates. The subsequent phase and tetrahedral-symmetry audits prove selected-state equivalence along certified proper positive paths, including the actual three-to-two-tetrahedron figure-eight move. A general connecting-path theorem remains an obligation. The further `six_three_and_two_bridge_audit.md` gives a complete independent geometric and peripheral certificate for the specified 6_3 literature state. The subsequent `singular_faces_and_six_two.md` evaluates singular face contractions of the original charged operators, rather than changing the tetrahedral function. It recovers an exact boundary fiber for 6_2 and proves its volume law and minimal-annihilator existence. Thus a direct reduction of the literature tensor is useful beyond the earlier invertible-face formulation. It does not establish equivalence of the positive factorial sum. The further boundary-state note proves the exact Gaussian change between a rationally sheared peripheral coordinate and the true meridian. This is an explicit equivalence for the stated tensor-derived states. It does not identify the earlier naive cone-transfer state or the positive factorial state with them. An operator by itself does not select the solution or its exponential normalization. The structural continuation in `pointed_steinberg_recoupling.md` now gives an algebraic role for finite q-factorial ratios: they are the kernel of a pointed cyclic-module factorization, with its generic normalization unit determined. The cyclic dilogarithm frames live on the explicit Heisenberg torsor of `heisenberg_period_torsor.md`. This supplies a uniform comparison target for the positive factorial candidate, retaining its phases. Equality of its full contracted period with that target remains unproved. The further `fourier_boundary_state.md` now removes the ordinary-fiber rank restriction. Its definition uses the existing charged tensor and real level, followed by a completely normalized inverse Fourier transform. The quadratic level term makes its coordinate the actual meridian. It agrees exactly with the preceding fiber/Gaussian state wherever that state is defined. Rational geometry and matrix certificates for a six-tetrahedron 5_2 realization verify the additional moving-plane case. This is a useful reformulation of the literature tensor; it is not an identification of either earlier positive state with it. Independence of arbitrary triangulations and equality with a canonical intrinsic knot state remain obligations. ## 1. The compact quantum product has an exact literature completion Our local function was Psi_q(x)=(x;q)_infinity=product_(k>=0)(1-q^k x), |q|<1. It satisfies Psi_q(qx)=Psi_q(x)/(1-x), and the formal pentagon in the earlier note. This function is directly related to the Faddeev function used in the literature state; it is one of its two compact product factors. More precisely, take Re b>0 and Im(b^2)>0, and put q=exp(2 pi i b^2), q_tilde=exp(-2 pi i b^(-2)), X=exp(2 pi b Z), X_tilde=exp(2 pi Z/b). Then both |q| and |q_tilde| are less than one, and the exact identity is Phi_b(Z) = Psi_q(-q^(1/2) X)/Psi_q_tilde(-q_tilde^(1/2) X_tilde). (1.1) This is equation (44) of Andersen–Kashaev, [arXiv:1109.6295v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6295v2), with its compact product notation expanded and the square roots fixed by the displayed exponentials. The following argument checks the identity instead of assuming the source's proof. **Independent verification.** Let P_b(Z) be the product quotient on the right. The elementary shift equation for Psi gives P_b(Z-i b/2)=(1+exp(2 pi b Z)) P_b(Z+i b/2), P_b(Z-i/(2b))=(1+exp(2 pi Z/b)) P_b(Z+i/(2b)). The factors in the other product cancel in each equation. The same two equations were derived directly for Phi from its integral in Section 2.2 of `literature_state_volume.md`. Their continuation to the present complex-b domain follows by holomorphic dependence on b from a common initial strip. The quotient R(Z)=Phi_b(Z)/P_b(Z) is therefore meromorphic and has periods i b and i/b. They are linearly independent over the reals in the stated complex-b domain. Both Phi_b and P_b tend to 1 as Re Z tends to minus infinity on a fixed horizontal line in their initial strip. For Phi this follows by moving the defining w-contour a small positive distance; for P it follows from the absolutely convergent products. A meromorphic function with two independent periods and this left-end limit must be identically 1. To see this explicitly, the real translation flow on the compact period torus is recurrent. There are R_k tending to plus infinity whose classes tend to zero. At a regular point Z_0 of the initial strip, R(Z_0)=lim_k R(Z_0-R_k)=1. The meromorphic identity theorem extends the result to the plane. This fixes the normalization as well as the functional equations and proves (1.1). For real b>0, neither compact infinite product is defined by an absolutely convergent |q|<1 product. Their *completed quotient*, continued as the Faddeev integral, has a well-defined value. Dropping the dual factor at this boundary is not justified by (1.1). In particular, the compact pentagon by itself does not establish the required global unit-circle state-integral identities. **Usefulness.** The compact product was a useful local definition. Its precise connection to a standard literature building block is now explicit. To obtain the literature knot state one still needs its dual factor, Gaussian, measure, boundary variables, and integration cycle. Equation (1.1) does not identify our entire custom knot model with the standard one. ### 1.1 Exact local operator agreement does not determine the completion Write the numerator in (1.1) as N_b(Z) and the denominator as D_b(Z). The modular-dual variable is unchanged by Z->Z-i b, since exp(2pi(Z-i b)/b)=exp(2pi Z/b). Hence D_b(Z-i b)=D_b(Z), N_b(Z-i b)=(1+q^(-1/2)exp(2pi b Z))N_b(Z). The completed Phi_b=N_b/D_b satisfies exactly the same latter equation. Thus the custom compact factor and the literature tetrahedron function already agree at the level of this local quantum difference operator. This is an exact partial equivalence, stronger than a shared classical action. Their quotient is an i b-periodic function, generally nonrational in the peripheral exponential. The second, dual shift equation and the left-end normalization fix the completion in Section 1. The first operator alone does not. The period factor can depend on b and can affect a semiclassical limit on a prescribed ray. This is a concrete reason that a volume conjecture must specify the state and normalization together with its quantum A-operator. The formulas here initially hold in the convergent complex-b product domain of (1.1); the real-b state uses the completed continuation, not a bare divergent product on the unit circle. ## 2. The positive angle-factorial model retains magnitudes of q-factorials At q=exp(2 pi i/N), and 0<=k<N, the exact identity is (q;q)_k =(-i)^k exp(pi i k(k+1)/(2N)) s_N(k), s_N(k)=product_(j=1)^k 2 sin(pi j/N). (2.1) It follows term by term from 1-exp(2 pi i j/N)=-2 i exp(pi i j/N) sin(pi j/N). Consequently 1/s_N(k)=(-i)^k exp(pi i k(k+1)/(2N))/(q;q)_k. (2.2) The custom positive state can therefore be written with compact q-factorial weights and an explicit compensating quadratic phase. This gives a concrete starting point for a comparison with cyclic or root-of-unity quantum dilogarithms. It does not say that discarding or compensating those phases commutes with summation, elimination, or Pachner moves. Its proven Laplace volume limit remains useful. It supplies a positive comparison action whose maximum is the complete geometric volume. It does not yet control the interference and contour of the literature state. The specialized local ratio 8 is still only a comparison of bare amplitudes. Products of peripheral units can specialize to 8. To decide the correct move law one must lift the boundary variables, specify how they enter the state, compute the exact multiplier, and check compositions of moves. No particular generic multiplier is identified by the single numerical test. In particular the test proves neither equivalence nor an obstruction modulo permitted boundary factors. ### 2.1 The factor-eight test has a measure-scale asymptotic There is more information available without inventing a peripheral extension. For the same symmetric bipyramid, on the lattice progression 6|N, write L_N=s_N(N/3)^(-6), R_N=s_N(2N/3)^(-3) sum_(p=1)^(N/3-1) [s_N(p)s_N(N/3-p)]^(-3). Then L_N/R_N ~ N. (2.3) Thus the discrepancy has a natural scale associated with the extra summation variable. An explicit measure factor N would remove this leading discrepancy; it would not establish the exact finite-N identity, since L_6/R_6=8. Here is the calculation. Uniformly for x in compact subsets of (0,1) with Nx integral, Stirling and Euler–Maclaurin applied after extracting the factor 2 pi j/N at the origin give s_N(Nx)=sqrt(2N sin(pi x)) exp(-N Lambda(pi x)/pi)(1+O(1/N)). The two-tetrahedron expression therefore has leading form L_N ~ 3^(-3/2) N^(-3) exp(N V/pi), V=6 Lambda(pi/3). For the three-tetrahedron sum let x=p/N. Its classical volume is v(x)=3[Lambda(2pi/3)+Lambda(pi x)+Lambda(pi(1/3-x))]. Its unique maximum is at x=1/6, where v=V and v''=-6 sqrt(3) pi^2. At this point the product of the three tetrahedral prefactors is 3^(-3/4)N^(-9/2). Summing the Gaussian with spacing 1/N supplies 3^(-3/4)sqrt(N). The uniform logarithmic factorial bound in the earlier note controls the endpoints, which have a strict volume gap. Consequently R_N ~ 3^(-3/2) N^(-4) exp(N V/pi), proving (2.3). This identifies a missing leading measure scale, not a full boundary multiplier or a proof of equivalence. More generally a nonzero rational boundary factor regular near (q,M)=(1,1) has zero contribution to a semiclassical limit h log|Z|. A finite-order zero or pole also contributes zero when approached along a nonzero algebraic path, since h log h tends to zero. The exact specialized state can still be zero or undefined if the factors are canceled in the wrong order. Factors accumulated in a number growing like 1/h can change the exponential rate. Exact move invariance and invariance of the volume rate are separate statements. ### 2.2 How a generic boundary multiplier changes the operator Let A=sum_j a_j(q,Q)E^j annihilate Z and let Z'=U(q,Q)Z, where U is a nonzero rational peripheral factor and E Q=q Q E. Before any specialization, A'=U A U^(-1) =sum_j a_j(q,Q) U(q,Q)/U(q,q^j Q) E^j (2.4) annihilates Z'. Clearing denominators must be recorded, since it introduces explicit peripheral factors. This is the precise scalar gauge law; replacing U by its value at Q=1 before shifting would give the wrong equation. For example, for U=1+Q^n the coefficient multiplier is (1+Q^n)/(1+q^(jn)Q^n). Although U(q,1)=2, its generic shift ratios carry nonconstant information. A product of three such factors can specialize to 8. This illustrates the user's normalization point without claiming that these particular factors are the missing multiplier in the bare bipyramid calculation. For a fixed number of moves, a nonzero multiplier meromorphic of finite order in a semiclassical parameter h has h log|U|->0 along any path on which its leading nonzero term is c h^k. It preserves the volume rate on that path. This statement requires the nonzero leading term: an identically vanishing specialization cannot be assigned a logarithmic rate by it. Nor does it apply to an exponential normalization exp(C/h). Generic normalization, exact quantum equivalence and volume-rate equivalence therefore remain distinct questions. ## 3. The naive cone-transfer equation is a different rational q-system For the figure-eight knot put F(Q)=Q^4-Q^3-2Q^2-Q+1, t(Q)=F(Q)/Q^2, A_custom=E^2-t(Q)E+1, E Q=q Q E. This is the earlier left-ordered cone-transfer equation, expressed in Q=m^2 so that its commutation parameter agrees with the literature one. For the literature operator audited in Section 4 of `literature_state_volume.md`, divide by its leading coefficient and write A_lit=E^2-T(Q)E+d(Q), T(Q)=(q^2 Q^2-1) R(Q)/(q^2 Q^2(q Q^2-1)), R(Q)=q^4 Q^4-q^3 Q^3-q(q^2+1)Q^2-qQ+1, d(Q)=(q^3 Q^2-1)/(q Q^2-1). The earlier scalar-gauge invariant already distinguishes these operators. The following stronger statement also rules out a rational change of the two-component solution basis, in these fixed peripheral coordinates. **Proposition 3.1.** For generic q, the companion systems C_custom(Q)=[[t(Q),-1],[1,0]], C_lit(Q)=[[T(Q),-d(Q)],[1,0]] admit no invertible rational matrix D(Q) satisfying C_lit(Q) D(Q)=D(qQ) C_custom(Q). (3.1) This excludes equivalence over C(q,Q), including overall rational equation multipliers and rational scalar gauges. It does not address a change of polarization or a gauge with essential singularities. **Proof.** It suffices to work at a generic positive real q!=1: a matrix rational in q,Q could be specialized there, away from its finitely many bad parameters. The q-orbits of nonzero finite points are then infinite. First D has no finite nonzero poles. C_custom and its inverse are regular there. C_lit has poles only at alpha_+=q^(-1/2) and alpha_-=-q^(-1/2), and zeros of its determinant only at q^(-1)alpha_+ and q^(-1)alpha_-. Consider a q-orbit containing a pole of D. If beta is its lowest-index pole, evaluate (3.1) at beta/q. Its right side has a pole and D on its left side is regular. Hence C_lit must have a pole there: beta=q alpha_+ or beta=q alpha_-. Every pole of D on that orbit therefore has index at least 1 relative to alpha. At its highest-index pole C_lit is regular and invertible, so (3.1) forces another pole of D one step farther along the orbit, a contradiction. Orbits containing no alpha give an immediate contradiction at their lowest-index pole. Thus every entry of D is Laurent polynomial in Q. Taking determinants in (3.1), and using that a rational q-periodic function is constant, yields det D(Q)=c(q)(q Q^2-1), c(q)!=0. (3.2) Write the lower row of D as (a(Q),b(Q)). If v=(f(qQ),f(Q))^T is a custom solution vector, its image is (h(qQ),h(Q))^T with h(Q)=a(Q) f(qQ)+b(Q) f(Q). The upper row is forced by the second row of (3.1) to be (a(qQ)t(Q)+b(qQ), -a(qQ)). (3.3) It remains to bound the Laurent degrees of a,b. This can be done entirely formally at zero and infinity. For a scalar equation E^2 f-U(Q)E f+v(Q) f=0, the formal quotient r(Q)=f(qQ)/f(Q) obeys r(qQ)r(Q)-U(Q)r(Q)+v(Q)=0. Its two distinct slopes give the following unique formal branches. The leading constants follow by balancing this displayed equation; their formal series are obtained recursively because the slopes are distinct: | Location | Custom large branch | Literature large branch | Custom small branch | Literature small branch | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Q=infinity | q^(-2)Q^2 | q Q^2 | Q^(-2) | q^(-1)Q^(-2) | | Q=0 | q^2 Q^(-2) | Q^(-2) | Q^2 | q^2 Q^2 | For each branch set H_branch=a r_branch+b=h/f. It is nonzero: otherwise the invertible D would kill the corresponding entire solution vector via (3.3). Its leading integral Laurent power is fixed by r_lit/r_custom = H_branch(qQ)/H_branch(Q). At infinity the powers of H_large and H_small must therefore be 3 and -1; at zero their orders must be -2 and 2. Subtracting the two branch identities gives a=(H_large-H_small)/(r_large-r_small). Thus a has highest degree 1 at infinity and lowest order 0 at zero. From b=H_small-a r_small one gets highest degree at most -1 at infinity and lowest order at least 2 at zero. Since a,b are Laurent polynomials, a=A+BQ, b=0. Equations (3.2)–(3.3) now demand (A+BqQ)(A+BQ)=c(q)(qQ^2-1). The coefficient of Q is AB(1+q), so AB=0. But the right side has both a nonzero constant and a nonzero quadratic coefficient. This is impossible. QED. This result does not follow just from a different determinant: d(Q) is itself a q-coboundary. The pole argument and both endpoint degree constraints are needed. **Corollary 3.2 (finite power covers do not remove the obstruction).** The same non-equivalence holds over rational functions of q^(1/D) and Q^(1/D) for every fixed positive integer D. In particular it covers rational factors in the meridian eigenvalue m when Q=m^2, including (1+m^n). **Proof.** Write Q=M^D and let E act by M->q^(1/D)M. Specialize to a generic positive q!=1 and take its positive D-th root. The finite-pole propagation argument in Proposition 3.1 works separately on every lifted orbit, so a,b are Laurent polynomials in M. The formal endpoint constraints become degree_infinity a=D, order_zero a=0, degree_infinity b<=-D, order_zero b>=2D. Thus b=0 and a is a polynomial of degree D with nonzero constant term. The determinant identity becomes a(q^(1/D)M) a(M)=c(q)(q M^(2D)-1). (3.4) All roots on the right have modulus q^(-1/(2D)). If rho is a root of a, then rho and q^(-1/D)rho must both be roots on the right. They have different moduli, and rho cannot be zero. This is impossible. A rational gauge over the stated function field would specialize to a gauge at some such generic positive q, so none exists. QED. The exclusion is still for fixed peripheral coordinates (and their finite power covers). It does not exclude Fourier-type changes of polarization, nonrational gauges, or a different corrected quantization of the custom classical action. ### 3.1 What survives of the custom volume theorem Both systems have the same geometric classical characteristic equation after removing the explicitly recorded limiting prefactor. Their difference at generic q is a quantum correction. The positive transfer and dominant-root estimates in the earlier note remain valid for their specified states and may also apply to bounded perturbations of a literature transfer system when the contour selects its dominant solution. They do not, by themselves, identify that selected solution or its absolute exponential normalization. There is also an opposite exponential convention to track: the custom norm grows like exp(+V/h), while the literature Faddeev state here decays like exp(-V/(2 pi b^2)). This can be compatible with a change of semiclassical ray or polarization, but it is not an exact equality of states on the rays already specified. A transform proving such a relation would have to be written down with its measure and integration cycle. ## 4. Relation to the manuscript and next mathematical obligations The manuscript's Schläfli identity and Euclidean endpoint explain the custom cone-transfer normalization. Its warnings about measures, Jacobians and pole accumulation also explain why equality of a classical action is too weak to identify quantum states. The independent literature-state proof in `literature_state_volume.md` avoids the compact-fold limit by staying at a nondegenerate positive ideal saddle. It gives a useful broad analytic criterion using the same polyhedral volume functional. The original proof obligations now have the following status: 1. Uniform positive geometric and preferred peripheral certificates are supplied for both twist families in the two twist notes. Their extension to broader alternating families remains open. 2. A general annihilator-existence theorem for the same rescaled literature integrals is proved in `general_annihilator_and_volume.md`. Explicit useful minimal operators beyond 4_1, and stronger full-symbol equalities, remain separate algebraic work. 3. Global move identities with generic boundary factors, exact normalization and integration cycles remain to be audited before identifying arbitrary realizations as one knot state. `faddeev_pentagon_audit.md` now supplies the positive Faddeev charged pentagon, its exact phase, and its insertion into proper absolutely convergent full face contractions. It also gives the explicit constant equivalence J_coarea=J_printed/p_1^2 for the fiber-measure convention. The remaining work includes the precise meridian polarization and continuation between other move patterns. `peripheral_phase_and_state.md` subsequently reconstructs the exact charged-tensor phase and identifies the fiber integral with a specified published AK level. Its transform is injective, and move covariance reduces to an affine phase and possible meridian translation. This is an explicit equivalence for the fixed realizations; the coefficients and contours for general connecting sequences still require checks. `tetrahedral_symmetry_and_figure_eight.md` supplies one actual zero-slope certificate: the two published figure-eight realizations differ only by their explicit phase, and their selected minimal operators agree. This does not identify the different naive custom cone-transfer operator. The geometric-endpoint moment argument in the peripheral-phase note now forces zero slope along any certified proper positive path. It gives state equivalence up to the retained scalar within that component, rather than assuming arbitrary triangulations lie in one component. For 4_1, the state asymptotic and explicit minimal annihilator are treated in the companion note. For the certified geometric state-integral class, the analytic volume theorem and general annihilator-existence proof are now available. The two twist families also have uniform geometric and preferred peripheral certificates. Exact global move equivalence and the extension to all alternating knots remain unfinished; neither follows from the shared classical action of the custom and literature constructions.

title: The actual meridian cut and the geometric cyclic point source
text: # The actual meridian cut and the geometric cyclic point source Research note, 26 October 2026. The original two-factor pivotal cut has two normalized branch weights that are consecutive meridian translates. Their ideal, their normalization defect, and the cokernel of the regularized cut recover the same length-one point module as the geometric cyclic lattice. A specified formal gauge places the geometric branch collision on exactly these actual cut walls. This proves a local comparison of the source and cut presentations as modules over the quantum--meridian base, with their residues and full normalization line recorded. It does not identify the actual global affine difference extension, its selected knot section, or its regulator norm across levels. ## 1. Two consecutive shift factors come from the actual cut Keep the original conventions q=q_N=exp(pi*i/N), x=-M/q, Y=M^2, U=M^(2N), sigma(M)=qM, rho=q-q^(-1), c=q+q^(-1). Use the branch-marked comparison of the actual Casimir pair with the geometric node in Section 7 of [the geometric rigidity note](geometric_rigidity_and_cyclic_source.md). Write d=L_+-L_-, d(u)=kappa*u+O(u^2), u=Log M, kappa!=0, and B=R[xi]/(xi(xi-d)), R=C[[u]]. The branch xi=d is marked + and xi=0 is marked -. If f belongs to B, denote its branch values by f_+,f_-. Set p=q^(-1)M^2-qM^(-2), r=qM^2-q^(-1)M^(-2). There is an exact meridian identity, before any specialization: r=sigma(p). (1.1) Let Phi_N be the actual scalar pivotal cut on this pair, including the full ADO modified dimension. The earlier exact cut formulas give the branch expression Phi_N(f)=Gamma_N [r f_+ + p f_-]/d, (1.2) where the complete common frame is Gamma_N=(-1)^N d_N(M) d/ [(M-M^(-1))(M^N+M^(-N))] =-zeta_N U d/[(U-1)(U+1)], zeta_N=q^(N(1-N)/2). (1.3) This retains both peripheral factors and the original phase. It is an identity of whole meridian germs; its zeros and poles are not separately evaluated. At completeness it has value Gamma_N(1)=-zeta_N*kappa/(4N). (1.4) For example, to derive (1.2) directly, let gamma_N=(-1)^N d/ [(M-M^(-1))(M^N+M^(-N))]. The density coefficients from that note obey theta_-=theta_0=-gamma_N*p, theta_+=theta_0+theta_1*d=gamma_N*r. The residue functional on B is (f_+-f_-)/d. Substituting these two density values and multiplying by the actual d_N proves (1.2). This is a consequence of the actual projector cuts, not a chosen geometric trace. ## 2. The common algebraic cut germ has a point defect For the local two-parameter comparison put S=C[[u,h]], q=exp(h), M=exp(u), sigma(u)=u+h, sigma(h)=h. Keep Gamma_N as the full normalization line in (1.3). After factoring this recorded line, the cut coefficients have a common algebraic germ independent of N. This does not assert an off-root deformation of the entire N-dimensional root representation. The two wall equations have expansions p=4u-2h+O((u,h)^2), r=4u+2h+O((u,h)^2). Consequently (p,r)=(u,h)=:m, det partial(p,r)/partial(u,h)|_0=16. (2.1) This equality follows from the invertible linear coefficient matrix and formal inversion. Their walls are exactly the balanced half-step meridian walls on the chosen local cover: p=0 <=> M^2=q, r=0 <=> M^2=q^(-1). (2.2) For example p=q^(-1)M^(-2)(M^2-q)(M^2+q); the other factor is a unit near q=M=1. The first wall equation pulls back to the second under sigma. Their product is the exact expression pr=(M^2-M^(-2))^2-(q-q^(-1))^2. (2.3) Thus their intersection is a reduced point, with ordered residue Res_0 du dh/[p sigma(p)]=1/16. (2.4) At a fixed actual root q_N!=1, this is not a second source at M=1: p(1)=-rho and r(1)=rho are both nonzero. The point in (2.1) records their joint quantum--meridian degeneration. ## 3. The cut pairing and its regularized dual retain this point Extend the geometric node to S and retain d=d(u). The normalized density element is theta_hat=-p+b xi, b=(p+r)/d=c(M^2-M^(-2))/d. (3.1) Its branch values are -p and r. Since d=kappa*u+O(u^2), b is a unit and b(0,0)=8/kappa. The full density is Gamma_N theta_hat; factoring its line has not changed the period. For the residue functional Res_B(a+b_1 xi)=b_1, the normalized trace-pairing matrix in the basis 1,xi is H_cut=[ b r ], [ r d r ]. It has determinant pr. Elementary simultaneous row and column operations with the unit b reduce it to diag(b,pr/b). Therefore the pairing's cokernel is the nodal divisor module coker H_cut = S/(p r). (3.2) Its normalization has the exact sequence 0 -> S/(pr) -> S/(p) direct_sum S/(r) -> S/(p,r) -> 0, (3.3) where the last map is the difference of the two reductions at their intersection. Injectivity uses (p) intersect (r)=(pr), since p,r are regular local coordinates. Its cokernel is exactly the length-one point module S/m. Thus normalization of the cut degeneracy divisor loses a specified point datum. There is also a direct presentation from the cut itself. On the normalization V=S^2, multiplying (1.2) by d gives the regular row ell_hat:V -> S, (f_+,f_-) -> r f_+ + p f_-. Its image is m and its single primitive relation is (p,-r). Hence 0 -> S --(p,-r)--> S^2 --(r,p)--> S -> S/m -> 0. (3.4) For exactness, if r a+p b=0, coprimality gives a=p t and b=-r t. This is the complete proof of the relation. The full regularized cut is Gamma_N ell_hat, with Gamma_N still recorded. The factor d used for regularization has a simple meridian zero; replacing it by another such factor requires keeping their unit ratio. This does not evaluate the original cut by substitution. ## 4. Calibrating the geometric cyclic generator to the actual wall Let a,b_geo be any two geometric formal shift ratios in S^times, with common complete value L_c and classical difference a(0,u)-b_geo(0,u)=kappa*u+O(u^2), kappa!=0. Here a and b_geo are the two ratios of [the nonzero geometric normal blocks](actual_geometric_normal_period.md), with their existing leading marked actions. We now give an exact formal unit gauge whose branch collision is the actual wall p=0. On the specified square-root meridian cover define R_0(h)=[b_geo/a]_(M=q^(1/2)), A(h)=(R_0(h)-1)/(q^3-q), g(M,h)=1+(M^2-q)A(h). (4.1) R_0(0)=1, and q^3-q has a simple h zero, so A belongs to C[[h]] and g is a unit with g(0,0)=1. The formula uses division by a known first-order zero with divisible numerator, not a punctured formal germ. In particular g|_(M=q^(1/2))=1, sigma(g)|_(M=q^(1/2))=R_0. Change the first branch ratio by the exact unit gauge a_star=a sigma(g)/g, b_star=b_geo. (4.2) It follows identically that a_star-b_star vanishes on p=0. Its classical specialization remains a(0,u)-b_geo(0,u), because sigma is identity at h=0. Therefore Delta_star=a_star-b_star=v p, v in S^times, v(0,0)=kappa/4. (4.3) This proves the factorization: the vanishing gives divisibility by the smooth local equation p, and the derivative ratio gives the displayed nonzero unit. No higher recursion is needed. The construction is the unique affine function of M^2 with the two prescribed values in (4.1). It preserves the leading marked regulator action. It chooses a model geometric cyclic generator; it does not identify the original selected knot generator. For the split module with ratios a_star,b_star, keep e=(1,1) and f=(1,0). The complete all-shifts cyclic lattice is exactly Lambda_star=sum_(j in Z) S T^j e =S e direct_sum (p,r)S f. (4.4) Indeed Te and T^2e generate component differences Delta_star and a_star sigma(Delta_star)+Delta_star sigma(b_star). Their ideal is (p,r)=m. Every positive or negative shifted difference vanishes at (0,0); invertibility of both ratios covers negative shifts. This proves both inclusions in (4.4). ## 5. A local source and cut presentation now agree Equation (4.4) has generators e,p f,r f and one relation r(p f)-p(r f)=0. Dualizing this presentation gives Ext^1_S(Lambda_star,S)=S/(p,r)=S/m. (5.1) Explicitly the dual relation is the row (0,r,-p); its cokernel is S/(p,r). After reversing the sign of its last generator and discarding the zero first column, it is the regularized actual cut row (r,p) in (3.4). This is an explicit comparison of the two source presentations, not only an equality of their lengths. The normalization quotient in (3.3) gives the same point module. The calibrated geometric ordered residue also has the required value: Res_0 du dh/[Delta_star sigma(Delta_star)] =(4/kappa)^2/16=1/kappa^2. (5.2) The two density branch values have an opposite ordered sign, since they are -p,r; their normalized ordered residue is -1/16. This sign is retained under comparison rather than absorbed into the phase zeta_N or a longitude sign. The full physical frame Gamma_N has the exact complete value (1.4) and remains separate. Thus the actual two-factor cut has now specified the same local point ideal, presentation, and calibrated residue as a geometric cyclic model whose collision has been placed on its meridian wall. This strengthens a fixed-N nodal-order isomorphism. It identifies how a source appears when q and M degenerate together and why an ordinary normalization or ordinary dual alone can forget it. The following assertions have not been established by this local comparison: * The actual global meridian source has this difference-module presentation, including its induced transport on the source. * The actual selected knot section is the calibrated model generator. * Sewing the other crossings preserves this class and pairs it nontrivially with the geometric block. * The resulting selected root period has the regulator norm across levels. In particular (5.1) does not imply vanishing of the global affine extension obstruction in Section 8 of the normal-period note. That requires an intertwining map with the actual source arrows, not just the presentation over S. The positive triangulation supplies the geometric ratios needed in Section 4; the actual projector cuts supply the walls in Sections 1--3. ## 6. Coverage and independent exact checks Modified traces have existing coverage in [Beliakova--Blanchet--Gainutdinov, 1801.00321](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.00321). The literature quantum-A definition remains the recurrence definition covered by [Garoufalidis--Sun, 0802.4074](https://arxiv.org/abs/0802.4074). Only their abstracts were consulted for scope in this step; no proof or recurrence coefficient from either is used. No novelty claim is made for modified-dimension numerators, normal crossings, cyclic-vector changes, or the elementary presentation duality. [The audit](../experiments/audit_cut_wall_source.py) verifies the universal shift identity, all wall factorizations, the two-coordinate Jacobian, the complete trace-pairing reduction, and the primitive cut relation with exact rational functions. Four rational formal ratio pairs check (4.1)--(4.3), including nonzero subprincipal terms and both complete longitude signs. Twelve generic root cases at N=2,3,4,5,6,9 construct the original tensor E,F,K and actual highest-vector projectors, then contract them with the original pivotal matrix. Their two projector cuts agree with (1.2), including the complete common peripheral frame. Six complete cases independently contract the confluent Casimir projector and nilpotent. The level checks include both parities and even and odd composite levels. They validate the exact coefficient derivation, not the global selected-period assertions. [Results](../experiments/cut_wall_source_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_cut_wall_source.py The subsequent [equivariant transport calculation](equivariant_cut_source_transport.md) now supplies the meridian matrices for the normalized presentations above. It identifies the cut complex with an explicit quotient of the geometric dual cyclic presentation, tensored with the dual geometric period line. The point source therefore keeps its inverse complete longitude character. The root matrices verify the cut-weight shift, while the physical difference-constant normalizer and its poles remain retained. The actual global source, selected section and central lattice at U=1 still need comparison.

title: The prefix-adapted framing density has an exact cyclotomic source factor
text: # The prefix-adapted framing density has an exact cyclotomic source factor Research calculation, 27 October 2026. This computes an actual finite root-filter functional on the rational density supplied by the [prefix-adapted framing chart](prefix_adapted_two_position_framing_cover.md). The result keeps an explicit power character and its cyclic norm. It is not a proof that this root filter is the original source after geometric Gaussian pushforward. That interchange remains unproved. ## 1. The density, with the physical prefix retained Fix the complete parabolic meridian mark. Use signed developed prefix products U,V from the actual braid-to-Gauss dictionary; the physical inverse position is k=ell_U/ell_V. On the framing torsor write P = [[r, r(1-r)/s], [s,1-r]], ell_W = Tr(W P), A=1/(1+s), B=1/k. For a matrix W write c_W=W_21 and h_W=W_11-W_22. The equation ell_(U-kV)=0 is quadratic in r. In the regular quadratic field put D = partial_(r/s) ell_(U-kV). The actual framing two-form is Omega = ell_V/(B D) dlog A wedge dlog B. (1.1) Its field trace over the two-position base is Tr Omega = T(B) dlog A wedge dlog B, T(B) = W B/(c_U B-c_V)^2, W = c_V h_U-h_V c_U. (1.2) In particular it need not be zero. The earlier special case V=I had W=0 and an odd unweighted density; that case cannot be used for an arbitrary physical edge. The chart note proves (1.1)--(1.2) from the actual prefix dictionary. For completeness the elementary trace calculation is short. Put tau=r/s, C=U-kV, and write ell_C = -s c_C tau^2+(c_C+s h_C)tau+d_C+s b_C. At its two simple roots the values of D are opposite. Reducing the quadratic ell_V modulo ell_C, or subtracting its two root values, gives Tr(ell_V/D) = (c_V h_C-h_V c_C)/c_C^2 = W/(c_U-k c_V)^2. Multiplication by 1/B gives (1.2). Notice that the trace coefficient has no remaining s dependence. The coefficients in (1.2) are intrinsic marked character functions. With the reference cut meridian J=[[1,1],[0,1]], direct multiplication gives c_W = Tr(J W)-Tr(W), W = Tr(J(VU-UV)). (1.3) Thus c_U,c_V,W, and their ratios below are rational trace-word functions of the marked representation. Conjugating while retaining J does not change them. Equivalently its residual unipotent centralizer fixes c_W and changes h_W by a common multiple of c_W, which cancels from W. They live on the marked character cover, not in the free framing-coordinate field. On a geometric component generically finite over the peripheral curve, they are algebraic over its A-curve field. The identities here concern the complete parabolic slice; no independent full holonomy deformation is imposed. ## 2. Exact root averaging is a derivative of a cyclic norm Suppose c_U!=0, W!=0, and set lambda=c_V/c_U, gamma=W/c_U^2, T(B)=gamma B/(B-lambda)^2. (2.1) Let Q be a primitive N-th root and assume lambda^N!=1. Define the finite algebraic functional A_N(T) = (1/N) sum_(b=0)^(N-1) T(Q^b). Then, EXACTLY, A_N(T) = gamma N lambda^(N-1)/(1-lambda^N)^2. (2.2) No limiting operation or quantum expansion is involved in (2.2). To prove it, first use the literal cyclic norm product_(b=0)^(N-1)(1-lambda Q^(-b)) = 1-lambda^N. (2.3) With theta=lambda partial_lambda, direct differentiation gives T(B)=-(gamma/lambda) theta^2 log(1-lambda/B). Applying theta twice to log (2.3) proves (2.2). Logarithms are only notation for logarithmic derivatives of rational functions here; no branch of a logarithm is needed. Equivalently the ordinary partial-fraction identity for B^N-1 proves the same formula. The case lambda=0 is taken directly: T(B)=gamma/B and A_N(T)=0 for N>1. Formula (2.2) is then interpreted by its polynomial limit. The displayed rate assertions below assume lambda!=0. This also has a WHOLE off-root representative. Before setting Q^N=1 retain P_N(Q,lambda)=product_(b=0)^(N-1)(1-lambda Q^(-b)). For arbitrary nonzero Q, away from the specified poles, (1/N)sum_b T(Q^b) = -gamma/(N lambda) theta^2 log P_N. (2.4) Only after taking the actual whole derivatives may P_N specialize to (2.3). Its Q derivative is Q partial_Q log P_N = sum_b b lambda Q^(-b)/(1-lambda Q^(-b)). (2.5) Specializing (2.3) first and differentiating it would incorrectly erase this current. The exact finite product retains the quantum normal, its moments, and its source factors. ## 3. A nonzero rational density can acquire an exponential source weight At any fixed complex lambda with 0<|lambda|!=1 and gamma!=0, (2.2) implies lim_(N->infinity) (1/N)log|A_N(T)| = -|log|lambda||. (3.1) For |lambda|<1 the denominator tends to one, and the numerator has rate log|lambda|. For |lambda|>1 factor lambda^(2N) out of the denominator; the resulting rate is -log|lambda|. There is no contradiction with the polynomial bounds for a fixed algebraic coefficient on one controlled arc. A_N has a growing cyclic norm and power character; it is not evaluation of one fixed algebraic function of Q near one. Nor does (3.1) prove that the actual geometric coefficient is exponentially small. The source pairing has not been shown to commute with this field trace and principal-density sampling. It does show that such an interchange cannot be declared harmless merely because T is rational and pointwise nonzero. Ordinary B residues do not replace this functional either. The one-form T(B)dlog B=gamma dB/(B-lambda)^2 is exact and has zero ordinary residues. Its finite cyclic average (2.2) is nevertheless nonzero. The marked source and its cyclic norm supply information which absolute de Rham exactness would lose. ## 4. A calibration on the actual figure-eight representation chart The prefix chart note constructs a fixed triple for the actual mixed braid (1,-2,1,-2), over u^2+u+1=0. For its third physical strand the signed developed prefix products reduce to V = [[1,1],[-u,1-u]], U = [[u+1,2u+1],[1-u,3-u]]. These are determinant-one matrices. The chart computation gives W=2u+1, lambda=1/(u+2), gamma=-lambda. Consequently (2.2) becomes A_N(T)=-N lambda^N/(1-lambda^N)^2, (4.1) |lambda|=1/sqrt(3). At either marked geometric embedding its rate is therefore -log(3)/2. This is a calibration of the exact density functional, not a recomputation of Kashaev's figure-eight invariant. In particular it must not be inserted as a new prefactor in that invariant. A source-preserving comparison must instead explain how this character and its dual/source normalization are transported. The example tests a general prefix formula; the conjecture target remains unrestricted hyperbolic knots. The [symbolic audit](../experiments/audit_cyclic_framing_density_source.py) checks the cyclic norm, an independent companion-matrix trace, the whole off-root current, and the exact figure-eight field values.

title: The actual cyclic sewing has a canonical regularized cut cycle
text: # The actual cyclic sewing has a canonical regularized cut cycle 28 October 2026. The exact two-head cyclic sewing comparison introduces additional poles which do survive the ORIGINAL source. This note carries those terms to the original cyclic-dilogarithm cuts without dropping them. At a ramified endpoint only two Taylor subtraction terms are needed; equivalently, at most two ordinary derivatives make its radial integral absolutely convergent. Unramified cyclic poles contribute their specified residues. The prescription applies entry by entry and through the whole original ordered word. This is an exact comparison of selected periods, including their boundary terms. It is not a positivity theorem or a geometric lower bound. In particular the positive radial symbol of the unsplit resolvent does not automatically apply separately to these differentiated sewing terms. ## 1. The actual additional divisor On a total-index residue fibre, the actual two-head transfer is a cyclic shift with one or two edges removed. Write its cyclic completion as `A=a S`, where `S^N=I` and `a=x^-1`, or `a=Q^-1 x^-1` for the opposite-root realization of an original u factor. Its cyclic resolvent is R_A(t)=(tI-A)^-1. The exact two-cut Woodbury comparison has a sewing matrix C_h(t)=[[1,-(a/t)^(N-h)],[-(a/t)^h,1]], 1<=h<=N. The `h=N` case uses the same cut column twice and reduces to the one-cut identity. The pure cyclic and the two diagonal sewing terms are analytic at zero and have zero original small-circle functional-calculus period. The remaining two cross terms contain two copies of `R_A` and negative powers of t. Thus their only new nonzero finite poles lie at t^N=a^N, (1) with order at most two in each integration variable. They decay at infinity. The original nilpotent resolvent has no such poles: their cancellation belongs to the complete sewing identity. At completeness `x=-q^-1`, so both realizations retain EXACTLY a^N=(-1)^(N+1). (2) For odd N, (1) meets every finite dilogarithm branch point, with the additional unramified point t=1. For even N its points are interlaced with the Nth roots. Away from completeness the full factor `a^N=(-1)^(N+1) M^-N` is retained. No replacement by a numerical scalar before taking the source is justified. The theorem below uses the unit circle case, in particular the complete point; small-circle sewing itself is an identity in the full meridian parameter. ## 2. One-variable regularized Hankel theorem Fix `Q=exp(2 pi i/N)`, epsilon in {1,-1}, and the original marked branch A_epsilon(t)=product_(k=1)^(N-1) (1-Q^(epsilon k)t)^(-k/N), A_epsilon(0)=1. Let B(t) be a scalar or matrix rational function with poles only at zero and finitely many points of the unit circle, each nonzero pole of order at most two, and with B(t)=O(t^-1) at infinity. Let Gamma_0 be a sufficiently small positive circle, lifted to the marked sheet. Put alpha_j=Q^(-epsilon j), u_j=j/N, g_j(r)=product_(k!=j,1<=k<N) (1-r Q^[epsilon(k-j)])^(-k/N). Every logarithm has the radial continuation already specified for the original cut. Let Z be the unramified poles of B, excluding zero. Then (1/(2 pi i)) integral_(Gamma_0) A_epsilon(t) B(t) dt =sum_(j=1)^(N-1) sin(pi u_j)/pi FP integral_1^infinity alpha_j (r-1)^(-u_j) g_j(r) B(alpha_j r) dr -sum_(beta in Z) Res_(t=beta) A_epsilon(t) B(t) dt. (3) If B is regular at a branch endpoint, FP is the ordinary convergent integral. At a pole alpha_j, write x=r-1 and the Laurent germ f_j(x)=alpha_j g_j(1+x) B(alpha_j(1+x)) =b_(-2)x^-2+b_(-1)x^-1+O(1), (4) with a missing coefficient set to zero. Its finite part means EXACTLY integral_0^1 x^-u [f_j(x)-b_(-2)x^-2-b_(-1)x^-1] dx +integral_1^infinity x^-u f_j(x) dx -b_(-2)/(u+1)-b_(-1)/u. (5) Both integrals in (5) converge absolutely. This formula fixes the subtraction convention; there is no adjustable finite constant. The numbers 1/u and 1/(u+1) are retained. In particular the former can grow with N at small cut labels. ### Proof and signs Deform the original small circle within the marked cut plane. The outer arcs tend to zero because `A_epsilon=O(|t|^(-(N-1)/2))` and B=O(t^-1). As in the original Hankel proof, this is a sectorwise deformation and does not assume that the entire outer circle has a closed lift at even N. The two radial banks have difference 2i sin(pi u_j) (r-1)^(-u_j) g_j(r). The factor dt contributes alpha_j dr, giving the first term in (3). Ordinary positively oriented circles about additional unramified poles are moved to the other side of the contour identity, giving the MINUS sign in its residue term. Near a ramified endpoint, integrate each term `b_n x^(n-u)` of (4) on the two banks and the joining small arc before sending its radius to zero. The arc cancels exactly the divergent powers from n=-2,-1. There is no constant logarithmic term because u is strictly between zero and one. The remaining finite part is (5). Equivalently, on the normalization put `t-alpha=s^(N/d)`, `d=gcd(N,j)`. A possible local residue would require `(n+1)N=j` for an integer n, which cannot hold for 1<=j<N. These endpoint poles are of second kind; they do not supply an independently choosable residue cycle. This proves (3) entry by entry, with the same marked endpoint continuation as the original small circle. ## 3. At most two derivatives give a convergent flow integral Let p in {0,1,2} be the pole order in (4), and put H_j(x)=x^p f_j(x). This is analytic at zero. Integration by parts with the endpoint finite parts retained gives, for p>=1, FP integral_0^infinity x^(-u-p) H_j(x) dx =1/[u(u+1)...(u+p-1)] integral_0^infinity x^-u H_j^(p)(x) dx. (6) For p=0 use the original integral. Each derivative in the integration by parts removes one negative integer power. Its factor is positive `1/(u+p-1)` at the first step and so on. The possible finite boundary term at zero is absent because all the exponents are nonintegral; the divergent terms are exactly those subtracted in (5). At infinity, `g_j(1+x)=O(x^(-(N-1)/2+u))`, so `H_j=O(x^(p-1-(N-1)/2+u))`. Every intermediate boundary term tends to zero. The final integrand in (6) is integrable both at zero and infinity. Rationality and the finite product expression also give these derivative estimates directly. Equation (6) is particularly convenient for computing the marked period without subtracting two numerically divergent endpoint quantities. These derivatives act on the COMPLETE H_j, including the cyclic resolvents, power characters and source entries. Applying them only to the dilogarithm factor would change the original period. Neither H_j^(p) nor the subtraction terms need be positive. ## 4. The extra terms survive an original crossing cap The actual two-head calculation at N=2, M=1, Q=-1, x=i uses the opposite-root u transfer with a=i, the original fusion C, D=I and the original averaged cap with pivots (-i,i). After those contractions the unsplit transfer and the sum of its two cyclic cross terms are respectively B_nil(t)=2i/t^2, B_cross(t)=-2i(t^2-1)/[t^2(t^2+1)^2]. (7) Here `A_epsilon(t)=(1+t)^(-1/2)` for either orientation. Their original small-circle periods are both -i. However B_cross has unramified double poles at beta=+i,-i, off the negative real dilogarithm cut. Its coefficients there are at +i: b_(-2)=i, b_(-1)=-2, at -i: b_(-2)=i, b_(-1)= 2. Consequently the residue sum which MUST be subtracted in (3) is i A_epsilon'(+i)-2 A_epsilon(+i) +i A_epsilon'(-i)+2 A_epsilon(-i), (8) and is nonzero. Thus even a whole original cap does not delete the new cyclic-pole correction. The original crossing's external common Cartan line multiplies both representations equally and is unchanged. ## 5. Tensoring the prescription preserves the entire source Apply (3) to each Euler variable of the exact cyclic sewing network, and use the ordinary original Hankel rule on its factorial variables. Each variable has at most two cyclic-resolvent factors, irrespective of level or braid length. The subtraction order is therefore at most two PER EULER VARIABLE. The number of variables and of cross-sewing types depends on the fixed word; the number of root-labelled cuts and unramified cyclic poles still grows with N. All pole loci in a variable depend only on its own coordinate and the retained meridian, not on the other integration variables. The ordered matrix contraction is finite. Its products of endpoint Laurent expansions have independent variables; taking their finite constant parts and ordinary residues commutes. Equivalently apply the proved one-variable identity repeatedly to the original compact product circles, where every integral is initially convergent. This defines a tensor prescription even when an unregularized multiple radial integral would fail to be absolutely convergent. The outcome is an exact selected cyclic period with explicit endpoint jets and pole residues, not a bare cyclic state. It retains the full original boundary source and every peripheral factor. The required future geometric comparison must carry this specified relative cycle. The finite subtraction order makes that target more concrete, but does not identify its leading hyperbolic component or prove that it survives the final sum. [Independent numerical contour diagnostics](../experiments/audit_cyclic_sewing_regularized_cut_cycle.py).

title: The cyclic source connection and its resonant flags
text: # The cyclic source connection and its resonant flags Research note, 26 October 2026. The source comparison in [the Euler calculation](controlled_cyclic_euler_source.md) has an exact logarithmic connection. Its scalar is another cyclic dilogarithm, with a specified phase. This gives both its classical generating action and a regularization at every nontrivial root of unity. The regularized primitive operator has a computable kernel. Its source frames still glue by the original actual cap. These are local identities for the existing cyclic dilogarithm and actual factorial source. They do not identify the selected Kashaev period with a geometric cycle. Cyclic Fourier transforms are already part of the literature coverage recorded in the Euler note; no novelty is claimed for the underlying cyclic function. The proofs and the source and cap normalizations here are direct. ## 1. The scalar comparison is an explicit algebraic period Put q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, and use a primitive generator X with X^N=U, z^N=1-U, z=M^2. The symbol z in this note is the norm root, not an eigenvalue of X. The branch near U=0 is initially z=1 and M=1. Let S_N(z)=1+z+...+z^(N-1), Dcal_N(z)=product_(k=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^k z)^(k/N), kappa_N=sqrt(N) exp[pi*i*(N-1)*(N-2)/(12N)]. Define the logarithms in Dcal inside |z|<1 and continue them together. At z=1 these factors are nonzero, and Dcal_N(1)=kappa_N. (1.1) Indeed Arg(1-Q^k)=pi*k/N-pi/2. Pairing k with N-k gives the modulus sqrt(N), and summing these weighted arguments gives the displayed phase. This phase is retained at even and composite levels as well. For the scalar gamma_N=a_0/S_N of the Euler source comparison, its exact formula is gamma_N(z)=M^(-(N-1)) Dcal_N(z) /[kappa_N S_N(z)]. (1.2) Here M is the retained square-root meridian mark. To prove (1.2), start with the previously proved determinant formula a_0^N=z^(-N(N-1)/2) product_(r=1)^(N-1)[(z-Q^r)/(1-Q^r)]^(N-r). Replace r by N-k in each numerator and denominator. The factors -Q^r cancel, leaving Dcal_N(z)^N/kappa_N^N. Both sides of the resulting root identity are one at z=1. Continuation from that mark proves (1.2), including its phase. Thus no unknown scalar is needed for this local comparison. On its cover it is an evaluation of the specified finite algebraic product. Its exact connection is d log gamma_N=-(N-1)dM/M-d log S_N(z) -(1/N)sum_(k=1)^(N-1) k Q^k dz/(1-Q^k z). (1.3) This is a rational connection on the marked base. Transport along a path is the ratio of the explicit products (1.2), with their branches transported. A loop around z=Q^(-k) has residue k/N-1 for gamma_N. Resetting an N-th root after the loop would change that transport. ## 2. The parameter trajectories must be specified There are three distinct uses of these formulas. * At fixed primitive center U on a compact marked chart away from U=1, z=exp(Log(1-U)/N) approaches one. The earlier polynomial coefficient bounds apply. * At a fixed small primitive coordinate X=x with |x|<1, U=x^N approaches zero and z approaches one. This also lies in a compact central chart. Bounding coefficients in that chart does not by itself bound a contracted complex sum. * At a fixed norm-root coordinate z with |z|<1, U=1-z^N approaches one, and the coherent logarithm is N Log z. The compact-chart bound does not apply. Formula (1.2) has an exponential, explicitly computable size here. For |x|>1 the fixed-primitive-coordinate trajectory also escapes every bounded central chart. A geometric construction must specify which local polarization and trajectory it uses; the same letter for two classical-looking shapes cannot do so. ## 3. The generating action with a uniform error bound For fixed z away from zero and the unit circle set G(z)=-log|z|/2-Im Li_2(z)/(2pi), |z|<1, G(z)=-log|z|+Im Li_2(1/z)/(2pi), |z|>1. Only dilogarithms inside the unit disk occur in these formulas. Put w=z in the first case and w=1/z in the second. Then log|gamma_N(z)| =N G(z)-log N/2+log|z|/2+log|1-z|/2 -log|1-w^N|+R_N(z), (3.1) where, with delta=abs(|z|-1), |R_N(z)| <= [4pi^2 |z|/delta^2+4pi/delta]/(12N). (3.2) In particular this holds uniformly on compact subsets of either indicated domain. Here is an elementary proof. Taking moduli in the determinant formula gives exactly log|gamma_N|=-(N-1)log|z|/2-log N/2 +sum_(r=1)^(N-1)(1-r/N)log|z-Q^r| -log|S_N(z)|. (3.3) The denominator product used here has logarithm log N/2 by pairing r with N-r. For f(t)=(1-t)log|z-exp(2pi*i*t)|, the composite trapezoid estimate gives sum_(r=1)^(N-1) f(r/N) =N integral_0^1 f(t)dt-log|1-z|/2+R_N. Its second derivative is bounded by the numerator of (3.2). Expanding the convergent logarithmic series in the disk gives integral f=-Im Li_2(z)/(2pi), |z|<1, integral f=log|z|/2+Im Li_2(1/z)/(2pi), |z|>1. Substitute S_N=(1-z^N)/(1-z) to obtain (3.1). On the inside chart the real part of the holomorphic generating action is G, with Ghol(z)=-Log z/2-Li_2(z)/(2pi*i), dGhol=[-1/2+Log(1-z)/(2pi*i)] dz/z. (3.4) This identifies the limiting local connection, rather than assuming that a root-central normalization has zero rate. The source-free frame is still an exact expression: C_N(z)=M^(N-1) S_N(z) gamma_N(z) =Dcal_N(z)/kappa_N. (3.5) Retaining these source factors, the induced regulator norm on the inverse frame obeys, uniformly on compact punctured subdisks, (2pi/N)[-log|C_N(z)| +N log|z| Arg(1-z)/(2pi)] =D_Bloch(z)+O(log N/N). (3.6) This follows directly from the already proved [cyclotomic logarithmic-series estimate](cyclotomic_normalization_tower.md#4-the-local-norm-from-an-exact-logarithmic-series). The logarithmic correction is part of the regulator metric. Equation (3.6) is not an equality with the absolute value of the full knot contraction. The paired exact identity remains gamma_N(M)gamma_N(M^(-1)) =Gamma_N=M^(N-1)/[N S_N(M^2)] =d_N(M)/(N eta_N), eta_N=i^(N+3). (3.7) Consequently G(z)+G(1/z)=-abs(log|z|)/2, exactly the rate of this specified modified-dimension factor. The local large factors cancel or persist according to the actual cap and source; they cannot be omitted before contraction. ## 4. A regularized evaluation at every nontrivial N-th root Let 1<=r<N, zeta=Q^r, and choose M_zeta=exp(pi*i*r/N). Continue M from one counterclockwise to this mark. Approach z=t*zeta with 0<t<1 and set u=1-z^N=1-t^N>0. Define gamma_tilde_(N,r)=u^(r/N) gamma_N. (4.1) On the N-th-root cover this has a finite nonzero value at z=zeta, with its radial root marked as positive. Exactly, gamma_tilde_(N,r)(zeta) =M_zeta^(-(N-1)) (Q;Q)_r/N. (4.2) For a proof, isolate k_0=N-r in Dcal_N(z). This factor is (1-Q^(k_0)z)^(1-r/N), while S_N has a simple zero. Moreover (1-Q^(k_0)z)/(1-z^N) -> 1/N. Reindexing all remaining logarithms gives, with no unspecified phase on the radial branch, product_(k!=k_0)(1-Q^k zeta)^(k/N) =kappa_N N^(-r/N)(Q;Q)_(r-1). Insert these equations in (1.2); the last factor 1-zeta completes (Q;Q)_r. This proves (4.2). Thus the singular scalar is replaced by an explicit algebraic evaluation. There is more information than its norm. Write the actual Euler coefficients as c_0=1, c_s=product_(j=1)^s Q^(j-1)/(Q^j-1). Use the full factorial/source reflection a_j(z)=gamma_N(z) Q^(-j)(Qz;Q)_(N-1-j). At the same regularized fiber it gives a_tilde_j=0, j<r, a_tilde_(r+s)=M_zeta^(-(N+1)) c_s, 0<=s<N-r. (4.3) Indeed the factorial vanishes precisely in the first case. At j=r, multiplying (Q;Q)_r by the complementary factorial gives N, and Q^(-r)=M_zeta^(-2). The subsequent coefficient recurrence is the original Euler recurrence with index s. In the primitive regular module, X^N=u and its special fiber has X^N=0. The whole regularized operator is therefore u^(r/N) d_N(X)|_(z=zeta) =M_zeta^(-(N+1)) X^r sum_(s=0)^(N-1-r)c_s X^s. (4.4) Its image is X^r V, its kernel has dimension r, and its rank is N-r. These images form the standard nested source flag. In particular this operation is not an invertible change of primitive operators. Their determinant is u^r before taking the special fiber. A proposed flow lift must retain this flag or the corresponding relative lattice, rather than evaluating an unregularized inverse at the divisor. There is an exact discrete transport underlying all these fibers. Keep X and u=1-z^N fixed, and shift z->Qz, M->qM. On the common marked cover, with epsilon=q^(-(N+1)), d_N(X;Qz)=epsilon u^(-1/N) X d_N(X;z). (4.6) For a direct proof, the cyclic-product recurrence gives gamma_N(Qz)/gamma_N(z) =q^(-(N-1)) u^(-1/N)(1-Qz). Insert it into the exact reflected-factorial coefficients and use their Euler recurrence. The coefficient of X^0 wraps by X^N=u and satisfies the same identity. Equivalently, if T_z denotes the coefficient polynomial with constant term one, (1-z) T_(Qz)(X)=Q^(-1) X T_z(X). Iterating (4.6) from the principal lift z_0=(1-u)^(1/N) gives u^(r/N) d_N(X;Q^r z_0) =epsilon^r X^r d_N(X;z_0). (4.7) The last factor is an integral unit near u=0. This constructs the complete local lattice transport, not merely its limiting rank. After N steps its multiplier is epsilon^N=(-1)^(N-1), consistent with M->-M on the marked double cover. Dropping that mark would erase a phase at even levels. The shift here holds the primitive X fixed; an actual global meridian shift also changes crossing matrices and Cartan data. This local equation alone is not the knot's quantum A-polynomial. The complete integral statement is just as simple. Take R=C[[u]] and its spectral order S=R[X]/(X^N-u)=C[[X]]. The regularized coefficient a_tilde_j is divisible by u when j<r, and a_tilde_r is a unit. Consequently its multiplier is f_reg=X^r h, h in S^*, image(f_reg)=X^r S, coker(f_reg)=S/(X^r). (4.8) Indeed replace each lower term u b_j X^j by X^(N+j)b_j before dividing by X^r. Every resulting exponent is positive, except the unit constant a_tilde_r. Hence h is a unit. As an R-module, the cokernel is C^r and is killed by u. The Smith factors are exactly N-r units and r copies of u; there are no higher powers. The source comparison is an isomorphism onto the spectral line lattice X^r S, although its map into the original R-lattice loses rank. This is an explicit integral replacement for an invertible-matrix claim. For a product of m such blocks and integral invertible adapters, its inverse has poles of order at most m: each block inverse has at most one pole. Tensoring adds the same orders. This bound is independent of N for a fixed finite network. Applying it to a proposed geometric presentation requires checking that its adapters and scalar source lines are precisely the regular ones specified here. For a fixed root zeta=exp(2pi*i*theta), 0<theta<1 rational, take levels with N theta integral. Equation (4.2) gives (2pi/N)log|gamma_tilde_(N,Ntheta)(zeta)| ->-D_Bloch(zeta). (4.9) This follows by an integrable logarithmic Riemann sum for log|(Q;Q)_(Ntheta)|; subtract log N exactly as in (4.2). For zeta=exp(pi*i/3) it includes all levels divisible by six. It supplies the local resonant regulator rate, not a knot volume theorem or a restriction of that conjecture to these levels. ## 5. The regularized source frames glue by the actual cap Use the actual dual colors, J^2=Q I, and B=gamma_N J. Let u=1-z^N be the common local parameter at z=zeta. The opposite source has residue -(N-r)/N after pullback under M->M^(-1). On the common cover take B_tilde=u^(r/N) B, Bdual_tilde=u^((N-r)/N) Bdual. Both comparison matrices are finite and invertible there. The second root is transported on the common cover, rather than independently reset along an inverse radial path. Their scalar product is, exactly, gamma_tilde gamma_dual_tilde =u Gamma_N=M^(N-1)(1-z)/N. (5.1) For the actual cap C_x^t, x=-M/q, the already audited dual-frame calculation therefore gives Bdual_tilde^(-t) C_x^t B_tilde^(-1) =N C_x/[Q M^(N-1)(1-z)] (5.2) at the resonant fiber. This is finite and invertible because zeta!=1. Cups and pivots transform by the same bases. Thus this local regularization preserves actual duality, including the Gaussian and modified-dimension factors. It does not turn the ordinary trace into the modified trace. The flag pairing also shows why normal data are needed. The actual C_x is anti-diagonal with nonzero entries. Hence (X^r V)^perp=X^(N-r) V (5.3) in the indicated bases. Pairing both leading source vectors therefore gives zero, even though the cap is invertible and both vectors are nonzero. This is a local statement about these factorial source vectors, not about the knot period. Their full pairing, including its normal factor, is explicit. Write p_a(z)=(Qz;Q)_a and x=-M/q. Since C_x e_a=M^a q^(a^2) e_(N-1-a), direct multiplication gives p(z^(-1))^t C_x^t p(z)=S_N(z) G_N(M), G_N(M)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1)(-1)^a M^(-a)q^(2a^2+a). (5.4) To prove it, use the exact complement identity p_a(z^(-1)) p_(N-1-a)(z) =S_N(z)(-1)^a z^(-a)Q^(a(a+1)/2). The zero of S_N at zeta is simple, and its first normal coefficient is governed by this finite Gaussian sum. For example, if N is odd and r is even, M=q^r makes it the ordinary quadratic sum with b=(N+1-r)/2, and |G_N|^2=N. Indeed expand its norm, set the index difference to k and sum Q^(2ka): only k=0 survives. If N is even and r=3 mod 4, the terms with indices a and a+N/2 cancel, so G_N(q^r)=0. This follows because their ratio is (-1)^(N/2+(N+1-r)/2)=-1. Thus even the first normal term requires its actual phase. These uniform identities locate the issue in a computable source pairing; they neither show nor imply vanishing of the full Kashaev invariant. ## 6. What this supplies for the Rivin flow The [angle flow](rivin_flow_and_quantum_source.md) supplies a geometric path and its marked A-curve potential. Equations (1.2)--(1.3) now supply exact local transport for the scalar source line; (3.1) gives its action along specified trajectories; (4.3)--(4.4) give its degeneration and source flag; (4.6)--(4.8) construct its discrete transport on the spectral line lattice; and (5.2) gives compatible actual gluing through a resonance. This removes a local scalar and lattice ambiguity. It still does not assign every geometric shape to the actual network's norm-root coordinate or transport its selected cut cycle. In particular a covector can annihilate X^r V. The flag makes that coupling question explicit, without proving it is nonzero for the actual knot. Convexity of the classical volume cannot by itself remove this remaining selected-period question. [The audit](../experiments/audit_cyclic_source_resonances.py) checks the new frame identity against independent matrix determinants, its connection against determinant derivatives, every resonant source flag and its first-order Smith factors at the tested levels, the actual regularized caps and their normal Gaussian moments, the marked complex phase and the proved error bound. [Results](../experiments/cyclic_source_resonance_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_cyclic_source_resonances.py

title: Cyclic modules, the Kashaev color, and a recoupling lattice at degeneration
text: # Cyclic modules, the Kashaev color, and a recoupling lattice at degeneration Research note, 25 October 2026. This supplies an integral extension of the local algebra used in the torsor construction. The results are uniform in every level N>=2. They are explicit representation and lattice calculations, not an appeal to a theorem about quantum knot invariants. No novelty is claimed for cyclic quantum-group representations. The distinguished Kashaev state remains the one fixed in [kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md) and [kashaev_ado_pointing.md](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). ## 1. A regular quantum-group family through the nilpotent fiber Put q=exp(pi*i/N), omega=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), and R=C[t,t^(-1)], E_t=R[x]/(x^N-t), X f(x)=x f(x), sigma f(x)=f(omega*x). The following endomorphisms are regular over R, including t=1: F=(1-X)sigma^(-1), E=(1-omega*X)/(omega*X*rho^2) sigma, K=-q^(-1)X^(-1). (1.1) All inverses in (1.1) exist over R. Direct multiplication gives K E=q^2 E K, K F=q^(-2)F K, E F-F E=(K-K^(-1))/rho. (1.2) For a short verification let f(X)=(X+X^(-1)-2)/rho^2. Then FE=f(X), EF=f(omega*X), and f(omega*X)-f(X)=(q X-q^(-1)X^(-1))/rho. The last numerator equals K-K^(-1). The normalized Casimir is rho^2 FE+qK+q^(-1)K^(-1)=-2. (1.3) The central powers follow by multiplying around the cyclic orbit: F^N=1-t, E^N=(-1)^(N-1)(1-t)/(t*rho^(2N)), K^N=(-1)^(N-1)/t. (1.4) Thus the inverses of F used in the generic quantum-torus chart are unnecessary in this quantum-group lattice. At t=1 both E and F are nilpotent, while the module stays simple. To see the fiber explicitly, evaluate functions at omega^j, and write e_j for the corresponding delta vectors. Put p_j=product_(a=1)^j(1-omega^a), v_j=p_j e_j. Then F v_j=v_(j+1), E v_j=[j]_q^2 v_(j-1), K v_j=q^(N-1-2j)v_j, (1.5) with the endpoint vectors zero. These are exactly the Kashaev color matrices in the crossing proof. The K eigenvalues are distinct and all adjacent E,F coefficients are nonzero. Matrix units are obtained from the K spectral projectors and these adjacent maps. For t!=1, X,F already generate the full matrix algebra because 1-X is invertible. Hence the image of this family in End_R(E_t) is the full matrix bundle: fiberwise surjectivity implies surjectivity over R by Nakayama. This concerns the image of the given family, not an assertion that every central quotient of the unrestricted quantum group is Azumaya. ## 2. The pointing also extends The cyclic vacuum equation is (X+F-1)v=0. Its kernel over R is R*1. Away from t=1 this follows from (X+F-1)=(1-X)(sigma^(-1)-1). At t=1 its rows in the evaluation basis are the N-1 independent differences v_(j-1)-v_j. Thus its rank remains N-1 and its kernel line remains primitive. In the basis (1.5), its specialized vector is v_vac=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) p_j^(-1) v_j. (2.1) It is a quantum Whittaker vector rather than the highest-weight vector. The functional eps(f)=Tr_(E_t/R)(f)/N is regular and eps(1)=1. On a knot's cut operator, which is scalar at t=1, pairing with this vector and functional gives the same Kashaev period as pairing with the highest-weight vector. No possibly large change-of-basis norm is discarded; scalarity cancels that change exactly. ### A tensor convention that must be retained The algebra extension above is not by itself a Hopf-algebra comparison. The Borel coproduct used in the pointed recoupling notes is Delta_B X=X tensor X, Delta_B F=F tensor 1+X tensor F. For the standard quantum-group coproduct and X=-q^(-1)K^(-1), Delta_q X=-q X tensor X, Delta_q F=F tensor 1-q X tensor F. (2.2) These formulas give the exact scalar mark that any tensor comparison must carry. It has the following explicit endpoint transport; an algebra isomorphism alone would not provide it. ### A matched endpoint chain for the actual coproduct Write kappa=-q. In an ordered tensor product of b factors, put U_j=K_j^(-1)=kappa*X_j, c_j=kappa^(1-j), F_j^new=c_j*F_j, E_j^new=c_j^(-1)*E_j. These are still the regular quantum-group representations (1.1), with a constant scaling automorphism of E,F. Their Borel coordinates are now U_j,F_j^new, with the actual coproduct Delta U=U tensor U, Delta F=F tensor 1+U tensor F. The unit vector of factor j solves (F_j^new+a_j U_j-b_j)1=0, a_j=kappa^(-j), b_j=kappa^(1-j), a_j=b_(j+1). (2.3) Thus these are exactly matched endpoint modules in the [endpoint formulation](pointed_period_descent.md), at all levels. The iterated coproduct acts on the unit tensor by the telescoping sum F_tot 1=sum_(j=1)^b kappa^(j-1)*c_j*x_1...x_(j-1)*(1-x_j) =1-x_1...x_b, U_tot=kappa^b*x_1...x_b. (2.4) Consequently its pointing is (F_tot+kappa^(-b)U_tot-1)1=0. More generally the substitution m:E_(t_1...t_b) -> E_(t_1) tensor ... tensor E_(t_b), f(x) -> f(x_1...x_b), (2.5) intertwines F with F_tot, and multiplication by kappa^b*x with U_tot. Each summand shifts the product coordinate by omega^(-1), so the same telescoping calculation proves (2.5) on every f, not just on the vacuum. The central marks are retained: U_j^N=kappa^N*t_j, (F_j^new)^N=c_j^N*(1-t_j), U_tot^N=kappa^(bN)*product t_j, F_tot^N=1-product t_j. (2.6) At the nilpotent fiber, the individual automorphism is the explicit basis conjugation v_h -> c_j^h v_h. It is a unit at every level, even when kappa^N=-1. Moreover c_j=(-q)^(1-j) is one fixed monomial in the generic quantum parameter; it is not an unrelated scalar chosen separately at each level. At the specified complex roots its basis-conjugation entries all have absolute value one. Thus the scalar in (2.2) is accounted for at the Borel pointing and tensor-embedding level without changing the nilpotent color. At this stage (2.5) has only been checked on the Borel action. The subsequent [Casimir comparison](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md) proves its full E-action, identifies both actual crossings on the transported recoupling lattice, and derives the pivotal closing trace. The selected global geometric period and its norm remain additional comparison requirements. ## 3. Pointed Borel factorization at all levels For nondegenerate s,t, the existing relative operators are Z=Y_1 Y_2^(-1), D=X_1+Z, C=ZX_2, X_tot=X_1X_2, Y_tot=X_1Y_2+Y_1, tau=(1-st)/(1-t). The generic commutation and vacuum-ideal certificates in the preceding notes do not use parity. For the central powers one must retain (ZX_2)^N=(-1)^(N-1) Z^N X_2^N. Consequently X_tot^N=st, Y_tot^N=1-st, D^N=tau, (-C)^N=1-tau (3.1) for every N>=2. The quantum-binomial argument requires primitivity, not primality or oddness. Simplicity and the common vacuum then give the pointed factorization at every level, with the same kernel C_(s,t)(u^a v^b) =w^a product_(j=1)^b(1-omega^j w)/(1-omega^j z), w=x_1x_2, z=x_2. (3.2) In the monomial bases used in the earlier note, its determinant is det C_(s,t)=sigma_N f(s,t)^(N(N-1)/2), f(s,t)=t(1-st)/(1-t)^2, sigma_N=(-1)^(N(N-1)^2/2). (3.3) The earlier formula without sigma_N applies to odd N. For completeness, the change from x_1^a x_2^b to w^a z^b contributes sigma_N*t^(N(N-1)/2): translation of the z exponent by a has sign (-1)^(a(N-1)). The numerator-column norms contribute (1-st)^(N(N-1)/2). The remaining z-column determinant has sign (-1)^(N-1), phase omega^(N(N^2-1)/3), and denominator (1-t)^(N-1). Its N-th power has no sign or phase. Multiplying these factors proves (3.3), including the even-level sign. ## 4. Blow up the simultaneous nilpotent point Use the discrete valuation ring A=C(a,b)[[eps]], with a,b,a+b nonzero, and substitute s=1-eps*a, t=1-eps*b. This records a direction above (s,t)=(1,1). Its relative parameter is tau=(a+b)/b-eps*a, f(s,t)=eps^(-1) (a+b)/b^2 * (1+O(eps)). (4.1) In particular the exceptional relative parameter remains nondegenerate. The direction unit (a+b)/b^2 is part of the normalization torsor. **Integral recoupling theorem.** The invariant factors of C_(s,t) over A are eps^(-1), multiplicity N(N-1)/2, 1, multiplicity N(N+1)/2. (4.2) Thus C^(-1) is regular. The image lattice C A^(N^2) contains the basic target lattice A^(N^2), and their quotient is killed by eps and has dimension N(N-1)/2 over the residue field. This is the precise lattice change across the pole, with the vacuum retained. ### Uniform proof Pass to the w,z evaluation bases with w_i=omega^i (st)^(1/N), z_j=omega^j t^(1/N), using formal roots with constant term one. Their Vandermonde changes are units in A, so invariant factors are unchanged. Formula (3.2) becomes N blocks, whose entries are B_i(j,d)=product_(k=1)^d(1-omega^k w_i) /(1-omega^k z_j), 0<=d<N. (4.3) Define r_i=[-i]_N if i!=0, and r_0=N. The numerator has one simple zero exactly when d>=r_i; the denominator has one exactly when d>=r_j. Therefore every entry has pole order at most one. The residue eps*B_i has nonzero columns only for 1<=d<r_i, and rows r_j<=d. The square submatrix r_j,d in {1,...,r_i-1} is triangular with nonzero diagonal. Its rank is r_i-1. The denominator-column matrix, before multiplying by the numerator factors, has determinant valuation -(N-1): multiply its columns d=1,...,N-1 by eps and evaluate at eps=0. The row j=0 is supported only on column zero; the other rows are the same nonzero triangular residue matrix. Numerator factors add valuation N-r_i. Hence val(det B_i)=1-r_i. Since all poles are simple and the residue has rank r_i-1, exactly r_i-1 invariant factors have valuation -1. The remaining valuations are nonnegative, and their sum is zero, so all are zero. Summing over r_i=1,...,N proves (4.2). There is also an explicit integral frame for each block: multiply its source columns d=1,...,r_i-1 by eps. The resulting matrix has a unit determinant. This gives the lattice modification without a numerical limit or an unspecified regularization. ## 5. The determinant root retains the exceptional unit For odd N, h=(N-1)/2 and the preceding normalized frame can use gamma^N=f^(-h). For even N an explicit determinant-one cover is gamma^(2N)=-f^(-(N-1)). (5.1) Indeed sigma_N=(-1)^(N/2) in this case, so raising (5.1) to N/2 cancels the sign in (3.3). This is a genuine even-level phase. On the ramified cover eps=delta^(2N), gamma has valuation N-1. Its remaining unit retains (a+b)/b^2 through the displayed root equations. The determinant-normalized C still needs the source and target lattices of (4.2); determinant one alone does not make its entries regular in the original lattices. Generic pointed recouplings obey the categorical pentagon at all levels. Extension of their specified scalar normalizations through a whole degeneration requires compatible transported lattices and the phases above.
