Consequently a nonzero inclusion or quotient between scalar root long-knot operators forces equality of their scalars. No division by a zero quantum dimension is involved. For n=kN+r, 0<r<N, the quotient of D_(n-1) on its first r vectors has E coefficient (-1)^k[r-j], unchanged F coefficient [j+1], and shifted H,K. This is exactly D_(r-1) tensor C_(kN) with the stated coproduct. The killed tail is a submodule because its boundary E coefficient is [kN]=0. For n=kN, the first N vectors form a submodule because its outgoing F coefficient is [N]=0. Its E coefficient is (-1)^(k-1)[N-j], so it is D_(N-1) tensor C_((k-1)N). The rescaling by [j]!, j<N, identifies D_(N-1) with the actual Kashaev color by unit entries. Together with (1.2) this proves the all-color periodicity claimed in the construction, including multiples of N. ## 3. The residue for an arbitrary fixed tail The periodic root series is [sum_(r=1)^(N-1)C_r X^r+K_N X^N]/(1-X^N). Its constant term at infinity is -K_N. Removing the initial colors up to any fixed n_0-1 subtracts a polynomial with no constant term; it does not change the residue against dX/X at infinity. Thus the infinity residue is K_N for every such tail. The finite residue at gamma^N=1 is -P_N(gamma)/N, since gamma times the derivative of 1-X^N there is -N. Root orthogonality makes their sum -K_N. There is no additional pole at X=0 because the selected tail starts in positive degree. For n_0>1 the rational function can acquire a higher-order pole at infinity from that subtracted polynomial. The statement about simple cyclotomic poles concerns its finite poles. This causes no change to the residue identity. These arguments establish the stated periodic rational root fiber and the exact original Kashaev residue. They do not establish its geometric support or exponential regulator norm. [Exact statewise phase audit](../experiments/audit_cyclotomic_shift_framing.py). [Results](../experiments/cyclotomic_shift_framing_results.json).

title: A local cyclotomic normalization tower and its regulator norm
text: # A local cyclotomic normalization tower and its regulator norm Research note, 25 October 2026. The normalization in the [Heisenberg torsor](heisenberg_period_torsor.md) is a finite-product object. Its compatibility between levels can be proved without a Habiro-ring or algebraic K-theory theorem. This note supplies those identities for every level, including even and composite levels, and derives its local archimedean norm directly. This is a local result, not the identification of a contracted knot invariant with a product of tetrahedron norms. The cyclic dilogarithm and its recurrence are existing definitions (Faddeev--Kashaev, [hep-th/9310070](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9310070)). No novelty is claimed for the finite products or their distribution. The larger rings and K3-indexed modules introduced in [Garoufalidis--Scholze--Wheeler--Zagier](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04241v2) concern Frobenius-modified arithmetic gluing of formal series. None of their theorem claims or proofs is used below. The local identities here do not construct those modules or identify their elements with Kashaev's actual values. ## 1. One pointed root at every level For N>=1 let zeta_N=exp(2pi*i/N) and set D_N(x)=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-zeta_N^j*x)^j, Q_N(x)=D_N(x)^2/(1-x^N)^(N-1), s_N(x)^(2N)=Q_N(x), s_N(0)=1. (1.1) The last equation defines a unique formal power series in Q(zeta_N)[[x]]: raising a series with constant term one to the power 2N is a bijection in characteristic zero. It also defines its analytic branch on |x|<1. Outside that disk one retains the root torsor and a specified continuation, rather than suppressing its phase. For odd N, (1.1) reduces to the earlier normalization: s_N(x)^N=product_(j=0)^(N-1) (1-zeta_N^j*x)^(j-(N-1)/2). (1.2) This follows by squaring (1.2) and using its constant term. For even N the half-integral centering is represented by the 2N-th root in (1.1); no oddness assumption is inserted into a formula with halves. Index translation in the finite product gives exactly D_N(zeta_N*x)/D_N(x)=(1-x)^N/(1-x^N), s_N(zeta_N*x)/s_N(x)=(1-x)/(1-x^N)^(1/N). (1.3) All roots in (1.3) have constant term one. These are the cyclic intertwiner recurrence and its determinant normalization, with a pointing that fixes the local scalar. ## 2. Exact compatibility between arbitrary levels Let N=m*n and choose zeta_m=zeta_N^n, zeta_n=zeta_N^m. Then D_(mn)(x)=D_m(x^n) product_(b=0)^(m-1) D_n(zeta_(mn)^b*x)^m, Q_(mn)(x)=Q_m(x^n) product_(b=0)^(m-1) Q_n(zeta_(mn)^b*x)^m, s_(mn)(x)=s_m(x^n)^(1/n) product_(b=0)^(m-1) s_n(zeta_(mn)^b*x). (2.1) These are equalities of the pointed formal series, hence of their matched continuations. There is no restriction that m,n be coprime or avoid a set of bad primes. This statement concerns characteristic-zero finite-product identities; it does not assert integral or p-adic gluing at those primes. For the first equality write each index as j=a*m+b. The exponent a*m yields the D_n factors, while the exponent b yields product_(a=0)^(n-1)(1-zeta_n^a*zeta_(mn)^b*x)^b =(1-zeta_m^b*x^n)^b. The denominators in Q multiply correctly because (m-1)+m(n-1)=mn-1. Raise the last equality of (2.1) to the power 2mn and use the pointed root to prove it without a scalar ambiguity. For three levels, every regrouping has the same power and constant term; equivalently, one groups the index by three digits. This proves associative distribution with its phases fixed locally. The maps here include x -> x^n and deck rotations of x. Consequently this identity is not an equality of independently chosen values at one fixed central character for every level. ## 3. A direct Galois/Kummer certificate Let K=Q(zeta_N), let a be prime to N, 1<=a<N, and let sigma_a send zeta_N to zeta_N^a while fixing x. With [k]_N the residue in {0,...,N-1}, put B_(N,a)(x)=product_(k=1)^(N-1) (1-zeta_N^k*x)^((a*[a^(-1)*k]_N-k)/N). Its exponents are integers. Reindexing the product proves sigma_a(D_N)^a/D_N = B_(N,a)^N. (3.1) Thus the class of D_N in K(x)^*/K(x)^(N*) has the inverse cyclotomic Galois character, since a*sigma_a[D_N]=[D_N]. In terms of Q_N, sigma_a(Q_N)^a/Q_N =B_(N,a)^(2N)*(1-x^N)^(-(a-1)(N-1)). (3.2) This is an explicit local Kummer certificate. It does not show that these classes satisfy the global Bloch five-term relation with the required period normalization, nor identify a global Chern class. ## 4. The local norm from an exact logarithmic series On |x|<1, expand the logarithms in (1.1). The finite sums are sum_(j=1)^(N-1) j*zeta_N^(j*k) =-N/(1-zeta_N^k) if N does not divide k, =N(N-1)/2 if N divides k. The divisible terms cancel the denominator of Q_N exactly. Therefore log s_N(x)=sum_(k>=1, N does not divide k) x^k/[k*(1-zeta_N^k)]. (4.1) There is no asymptotic assumption in (4.1). For any r<1 it implies, uniformly on |x|<=r, log s_N(x)=-N Li_2(x)/(2pi*i) -(1/2)log(1-x)+E_N(x), |E_N(x)| <= pi*r/[4N(1-r)] +2*r^(floor(N/2)+1)/(1-r). (4.2) Here N>=2. One elementary proof splits the sum at k=N/2. For the first part use 1/(1-exp(2pi*i*k/N))=1/2+(i/2)cot(pi*k/N), 0 <= 1/u-cot(u) <= u/2, 0<u<=pi/2. The last inequality follows from sin(u)-u*cos(u)=integral_0^u v*sin(v)dv and sin(v)<=sin(u). This bounds each error coefficient by pi*k/(4N). In the tail, for a nondivisible k, |1-zeta_N^k|^(-1)<=N/4. Bound the difference coefficient by N and use 1/k<2/N. The same bound includes the omitted divisible terms of the two comparison series. Geometric summation proves (4.2). In particular E_N=O_r(1/N). Define the metric on the inverse of this specified local frame by log ||s_N(x)^(-1)||_reg =-log|s_N(x)|+N log|x| Arg(1-x)/(2pi). (4.3) The expression extends at x=0. On this disk the branch of Arg is the one from log(1-x). With the Bloch--Wigner function D(x)=Im Li_2(x)+log|x| Arg(1-x), equation (4.2) gives the quantified comparison (2pi/N)log ||s_N(x)^(-1)||_reg =D(x)+(pi/N)log|1-x|-(2pi/N)Re E_N(x). (4.4) It is valid at all levels. This establishes the local regulator rate of the existing normalization frame on compact subdisks. The norm is specified in (4.3); it is not a new definition of the knot invariant and is not yet its absolute-value norm. ## 5. What happens outside this chart and at resonance The restriction in (4.2) matters. Cyclic factors have zeros on the unit circle, and an independent evaluation of one frame can be undefined even when the whole period has a regular germ. For example x=exp(pi*i/3) has x^N=1 at multiples of six. A whole period identity and its lattice must be specialized before its individual factors. The [recoupling lattice](cyclic_steinberg_lattice.md) gives one explicit instance of such a regular integral replacement. An exact identity also detects the chart correction. With S=N(N-1)/2 and T=sum_(j=1)^(N-1)j^2, direct inversion gives D_N(x)D_N(1/x) =(-1)^S*zeta_N^T*x^(-S) [(1-x^N)/(1-x)]^N, Q_N(x)Q_N(1/x) =(-1)^(N-1)*zeta_N^(2T) (1-x^N)^2/(1-x)^(2N). (5.1) For any matched root choices away from the divisors, it follows that log|s_N(x)|+log|s_N(1/x)| =log|1-x^N|/N-log|1-x|. (5.2) One must transport the regulator metric as well as this algebraic frame. In particular, using the unchanged formula (4.3) on both sides of inversion would introduce the quadratic logarithmic term log|x| Arg(-x); it would not give D(x)+D(1/x)=0. The logarithmic connection and its frame transport supply additional data. ## 6. The remaining knot theorem This gives an exact local system across all levels and proves its local regulator estimate. The [regular cyclic/Steinberg family](cyclic_steinberg_lattice.md) also places the vacuum in the actual Kashaev color. Neither result says that contracting the knot tensor is a product of these scalar norms. Contraction includes phases and cancellation, and its distinguished global pairing still has to be compared with the geometric period. The required global assertion remains (2pi/N)log|<K>_N| -> Vol(S^3 minus K). No Hilbert-90 calculation or rigidity of a finite-level unpointed intertwiner fixes that pairing by itself. A proof must identify its integral pointing, its global normalization, and its archimedean norm. The identities above do not establish that assertion for a knot class. `experiments/audit_cyclotomic_normalization.py` checks distribution, Galois certificates, inversion, and the series and norm estimates. They are diagnostics for the uniform proofs, not replacements for them.

title: What fixed algebraic rigidity can force for the actual selected period
text: # What fixed algebraic rigidity can force for the actual selected period 28 October 2026. Exact cyclotomic pointing already determines the actual quantum period. It does not automatically make its geometric coefficient nonzero. Two precise facts sharpen the torsor target: 1. The SAME original figure-eight family has exponential growth on its complete meridian arc and bounded values on every fixed-color meridian arc approaching the same complete classical point. A uniform dominant geometric comparison regular on the raw central fibre is therefore impossible. The divided normal source is essential, rather than an optional choice of coordinates. 2. The explicit whole-word Kummer period has a fixed number of variables, but growing cover genus and growing character homology. It has not yet supplied the fixed finite-rank algebraic object required by the existing whole-comparison rigidity theorem. These are proofs about the original anchored state and its actual cover. No rescaled invariant or adjustable levelwise source is used. ## 1. The source is already fixed; uniqueness is not the missing datum Use the actual family and conventions of [the all-level operator theorem](all_level_a_period.md) and [the normal-period theorem](peripheral_normal_period.md): q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q_N=q_N^2, Y=M^2, F_N(1)=K_N, F_N(Q_N^j)=C_j(q_N), 1<=j<N. For each FIXED j, C_j(q) is the specified Laurent-polynomial ordinary-color period, C_j(1)=1. The exact all-level recurrence, its actual finite initial window and its bounded quantum jets determine K_N uniquely. The [Mellin theorem](mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness.md) strengthens this to the entire rational root section with its pole lattice. There is consequently no freedom to alter the knot period while keeping those exact data. The unresolved assertion is that this unique anchored object has the required selected regulator character. Uniqueness cannot be converted into existence of a regulator comparison without producing a candidate satisfying the original source, lattice and quantum-normal equations. ## 2. Fixed algebraic coefficients have polynomial size on a fixed-color arc Put t=1/N and retain the root source coordinates (t,Q,Y) on the central slice U=Y^N=1. Let E be a fixed finite FIELD extension of k(t,Q,Y), k a fixed embedded characteristic-zero field. A specified finite residue-field mark and an etale selected place can be retained. Let a be a nonzero element of E, regular on the marked chart where the arc is tested. For all sufficiently large FIXED positive integers j, every specialized conjugate of a on gamma_j(t)=(t,exp(2pi*i*t),exp(2pi*i*j*t)) (1) has upper and lower polynomial bounds at t=1/N, for all large N. The required lower bound on j depends on the fixed presentation of a, not on N. In particular it cannot be exponentially small or zero at infinitely many large levels. Here is a direct proof, including the possible vanishing issue. Choose a polynomial relation for a with nonzero constant and leading coefficients, clear all denominators, and consider each nonzero coefficient P(t,Q,Y). Write P=sum_(r,s) p_(r,s)(t) Q^r Y^s. Let A be the span of its Q exponents. For j>A the integers r+js belonging to different collected pairs (r,s) are distinct. Thus P(gamma_j(t))=sum_(r,s) p_(r,s)(t) exp(2pi*i*(r+js)t) is not identically zero. Independence follows by successively applying the constant-coefficient operators partial_t-2pi*i*(r+js), with powers exceeding the polynomial degrees, to isolate one exponential. A nonzero resulting analytic germ has finite vanishing order at t=0. Apply this to the finitely many relation coefficients. Cauchy's root bound and the same bound for the reciprocal polynomial give c N^(-B)<=|a_(i,N)|<=C N^B. (2) The proof is uniform over all roots of the selected relation. It does not assume bounded absolute cyclotomic degree or heights. In particular, the complete figure-eight scalar itself cannot be a fixed algebraic function of (t,Q) on a finite cover: (2) would give zero exponential rate, contradicting (3) below. This does not exclude a fixed algebraic connection or torsor with a transcendental marked horizontal period. Its irregular regulator character must be retained before applying algebraic coefficient rigidity. For algebraic sections on a finite integral shape cover, apply the argument to a fixed nonzero norm or a polynomial relation on the selected irreducible component. Clearing actual poles must precede specialization. A statement about a fixed algebraic section is much stronger than algebraicity at each separate N. ## 3. An original-source obstruction to a regular central-fibre comparison Take the ORIGINAL figure-eight knot. The independently proved [whole-source identity](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md) gives lim_(N->infinity) N^-1 Log|F_N(1)| =Vol(4_1)/(2pi)>0. (3) For every fixed j>=1, the SAME family and SAME original cap give F_N(Q_N^j)=C_j(q_N)->1. (4) No normalization, operator or source was changed between (3) and (4). Both arcs approach (Q,Y,U)=(1,1,1), and U=1 on both. More literally, the actual pivot has g_k(M)=M^(1-N)g_k(1). On these unit-meridian arcs its change is a specified common unit for every closed head. Moving that unchanged factor into its retained external line leaves the same numerical cut functional. Thus this growth contrast does not hide an independently chosen co-source. Suppose a proposed whole geometric comparison on the raw central fibre had the form F_N(Y)=a_N(Y) G_N(Y)+R_N(Y), (5) where a is a nonzero section of the fixed algebraic type in Section 2. Suppose on every fixed-color arc (1) its geometric period and remainder satisfied, for a common V>0, N^-1 Log|G_N(Q_N^j)|->V, |R_N(Q_N^j)|<=exp(N(V-delta_j)), delta_j>0. (6) Then (5) is impossible. Choose a fixed j larger than the presentation bound of Section 2. Its a_N(Q_N^j) is nonzero and polynomially bounded above and below. Equations (5)--(6), by the reverse triangle inequality, give positive exponential growth on that arc, contradicting (4). Equivalently, if bounded ordinary-color values force the coefficient to vanish on EVERY fixed-color arc, the exponential separation proof in Section 2 forces its algebraic restriction to the raw central fibre to vanish identically. It cannot then give the nonzero complete value by ordinary regular evaluation. This excludes a tempting shortcut: a uniform dominant geometric block with a regular algebraic scalar coefficient on that fibre. It does NOT exclude a source-preserving normal extension, a nonregular meridian lattice, or cancellation between blocks with the same exponential size. The latter possibilities are precisely data which raw algebraic point rigidity does not fix. ### The original divided source explains the necessary distinction The exact actual source is already known to use the normal extension. With U=Y^N and t_mu=U-1, set Y_r(t_mu)=Q_N^r(1+t_mu)^(1/N), v_N(t_mu)_r=(Y_r(t_mu)-1)F_N(Y_r(t_mu)). Then the unconditional original state identity is K_N=N e_0^*[t_mu^1]v_N, whereas the central state v_N(0) contains only the polynomially bounded ordinary-color row. The source has degree minus one; it is not ordinary evaluation of the lowest state degree. See [the source-adapted filtration](source_adapted_leading_filtration_and_actual_scale_test.md). The elementary expression (U-1)/(Y-1), U=Y^N, likewise vanishes at every proper root-orbit point and has complete whole-germ value N. It is not a regular function on the raw two-variable fibre U=1 at Y=1. This illustrates the required divided lattice; it does not define a replacement invariant or prove its regulator coefficient is nonzero. Thus the actual source-anchored example supports the user's normal-torsor viewpoint, while ruling out its regular scalar version on the unextended central fibre. ## 4. The explicit Kummer period has growing ambient rank For an odd prime p the actual one-variable cyclic cover is C_p: y^p=product_(j=1)^(p-1)(1-Q_p^j t)^j. It is connected. Its p-1 finite branch points have ramification index p, since each j is coprime to p. Infinity is unramified: the polynomial degree p(p-1)/2 is divisible by p. Counting the Euler characteristic of the punctured p-sheeted cover and filling its ramified points gives 2-2g=p*2-(p-1)*(p-1), g=(p-1)(p-3)/2. (7) The growth persists in the particular nontrivial deck character used by y^-1 dt. Remove the finite branch points from the base sphere. It retracts to a graph with one vertex and p-2 loops. In any nontrivial deck-character component the covering graph chain groups have dimensions 1 and p-2, and its boundary map has rank one: a branch generator acts by a nontrivial p-th root. Hence that character's H_1 has dimension p-3. Filling the ramification points changes only the trivial character, because each such point is deck-fixed. Therefore dim H_1(C_p)_chi=p-3 (8) for every nontrivial character chi, including the selected one. The small-circle source has an additional important feature. Removing the p preimages of t=0 adds one boundary-circle dimension to each nontrivial character. The original selected circle projects into that canonical one-dimensional boundary subspace. Thus growing ambient rank DOES NOT rule out a smaller selected period object. It does show that fixed variable count alone has not constructed such an object uniformly in p. In particular the compact C_p cannot all be the smooth proper fibres of one fixed finite-type algebraic curve family on finitely many strata: their genus is unbounded. A fixed selected torsor must be a genuinely constructed reduction or comparison, not an automatic consequence of the displayed Kummer equations. ## 5. What a successful rigidity certificate would now have to contain The existing [whole-comparison rigidity theorem](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) can promote bounded algebraic quantum-jet identities to an exact whole comparison. The existing [critical-source theorem](irreducible_critical_source_and_whole_norm.md) can then force every geometric coefficient nonzero from an irreducible descended critical line and a nonzero exact source moment, or from a faithful trace realization. Fixed algebraic coefficients automatically have polynomial norms on the root arc. Those theorems would remove a separately assumed nonzero geometric weight. Their inputs are substantive and finite: * a fixed algebraic comparison space or an explicitly bounded selected quotient of the actual Kummer/quantum object; * the source-normal pairing, its meridian pole lattice and its quantum-normal connection retained by that comparison; * an actual descended critical line/observable with its exact source moments, rather than only a classical shape field; * control of the TOTAL compact remainder after that projection. The first three have not been supplied for the selected knot period. The new exact cut construction supplies the original cycle, and its infinity bound removes a real global escape obstacle. It does not make their fixed algebraic reduction or critical source moment automatic. Equations (3)--(4) show why that reduction must retain the divided source before passing to a central or associated-graded fibre.

title: Degenerate alias faces: a general bound and two exact obstructions
text: # Degenerate alias faces: a general bound and two exact obstructions Research note, 28 October 2026. This note concerns the remaining **classical wrong-edge faces** of `general_legendre_rivin_contour.md`. It proves a uniform bound for a combinatorially specified class of triangulations. Two tempting routes to an unconditional bound fail on actual positive knot triangulations: repairing only the flat tetrahedra, and giving the complete edge multipliers an automatic favorable sign. Neither counterexample disproves volume domination. Neither the bound nor the counterexamples identify an original quantum wall with a classical face. That source comparison remains necessary. The reproducible exact/Arb audit is `experiments/audit_degenerate_alias_faces.py`, with fixture `experiments/degenerate_alias_face_fixture.json` and results `experiments/degenerate_alias_face_results.json`. ## 1. A uniform star bound for all wrong-edge faces Let an ideal triangulation of a one-cusped knot exterior have (t) tetrahedra and (t) global edges. Let (E) be its nonnegative edge-angle incidence matrix. Its three columns per tetrahedron count the two opposite local edges, so every column sums to two. Consider a weak nonnegative alias angle locus \[ \alpha_{ja}\geq0,\qquad \sum_{a=0}^2\alpha_{ja}=\pi, \qquad E\alpha=2\pi k,\qquad k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^t. \tag{1} \] Summing all edge equations gives \(\sum_e k_e=t\). Consequently, if the edge winding differs from the original vector \(\mathbf1\), at least one edge has (k_e=0). All angle summands incident to that edge are then zero. Every tetrahedron meeting it has at least one zero angle, and its continuous volume \[ V_j=\Lambda(\alpha_{j0})+\Lambda(\alpha_{j1}) +\Lambda(\alpha_{j2}) \] is zero: \(\Lambda(0)=0\) and \(\Lambda(\pi-a)=-\Lambda(a)\). Write (s_e) for the number of **distinct tetrahedra** incident to edge (e), and (v_3) for the volume of the regular ideal tetrahedron. Since every other tetrahedron has volume at most (v_3), \[ \boxed{\quad V(\alpha)\leq(t-s_e)v_3 \quad\text{whenever }k_e=0.\quad} \tag{2} \] In particular, put \(s_{\min}=\min_e s_e\). If a positive complete triangulation satisfies \[ \boxed{\quad\operatorname{Vol}(M)>(t-s_{\min})v_3,\quad} \tag{3} \] **every wrong-edge weak nonnegative alias locus has a common strict volume gap** \[ \operatorname{Vol}(M)-V(\alpha) \geq\operatorname{Vol}(M)-(t-s_{\min})v_3>0. \tag{4} \] This is a bound on the whole cell, including all its corners, with no stationarity or repair assumption. For several zero edges, replace (s_e) by the size of the union of their tetrahedron stars. Linear constraint propagation can force still more tetrahedra to be flat. The bound applies to an actual face integral once that integral has the specified phase, a uniform subexponential density bound, and a chain of subexponential mass. It then gives the corresponding exponential loss. These quantum hypotheses are not inferred from the angle equations. Condition (3) is a useful sufficient criterion, not an assertion about all geometric triangulations. It becomes weak for triangulations with many thin tetrahedra. ## 2. Flat-only repair can fail on an actual positive triangulation A proposed universal argument was: retain every positive tetrahedron, change only flat tetrahedra, and restore the original edge winding. Such a repair would preserve or increase volume. The following exact example shows that the repair need not exist. Use the six-tetrahedron standard (7_4) triangulation with undecorated isomorphism signature `gLvQQbefdfefmexnaxk`. Its explicit face gluings and edge matrix are saved in the fixture. Index tetrahedra and edges from zero and write a tetrahedron's angles in units of \(\pi\) as \((a_j,b_j,c_j)\). The edge matrix, displayed in three-column blocks, is \[ E=\begin{pmatrix} 100&110&110&000&001&000\\ 011&011&000&001&010&001\\ 001&100&010&010&100&100\\ 010&000&001&100&010&000\\ 100&001&001&110&000&011\\ 000&000&100&001&101&110 \end{pmatrix}. \tag{5} \] Here `110` denotes the row block \((1,1,0)\). The audit reconstructs this matrix from the individual face permutations; it does not trust a transcribed gluing matrix. Consider the rational alias point \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} j&a_j&b_j&c_j\\\hline 0&3/10&0&7/10\\ 1&1/30&19/30&1/3\\ 2&1/3&2/3&0\\ 3&0&1&0\\ 4&29/30&0&1/30\\ 5&19/30&1/30&1/3 \end{array} \tag{6} \] Direct multiplication gives \[ E\alpha=2(1,1,2,0,1,1)^T. \tag{7} \] Exactly tetrahedra (0,2,3,4) are flat; tetrahedra (1,5) are strictly positive. Every ORIGINAL angle structure, satisfying the local sums one and \(E\alpha=2\mathbf1\), obeys the identity \[ 3(a_1+a_5)+b_1+2b_5-3 =c_0+b_3+2c_3+b_4\ \geq0. \tag{8} \] This is an elementary linear combination of the original tetrahedron and edge equations. At (6), its left side is \(-3/10\). Hence **no modification of just tetrahedra (0,2,3,4) can restore the original edge equations while retaining tetrahedra (1,5)**. For a second exact verification, let (A=(L;E)), where (L) records local sums. Let (F\) be the twelve columns belonging to the four flat tetrahedra and (P\) the other six columns. If (q\) denotes (6), a repair would require \[ A_F x=(\mathbf1,2\mathbf1)^T-A_Pq_P=:b_F, \qquad x\geq0. \] The rational vector \[ y=(0,-1,2/3,2/3,2/3,-1; -1/3,1,-1/3,-1,1/3,-1/3)^T \] satisfies \[ A_F^Ty=(0,0,2/3;\ 0,0,0;\ 0,2/3,4/3;\ 0,2/3,0)^T \geq0, \qquad y^Tb_F=-1/5. \tag{9} \] Thus nonexistence is certified by rational arithmetic, with no numerical optimization used in the proof. ### This is genuinely positive complete geometric input The shape certificate uses the upper-half-plane root (a) of \[ a^3+2a-1=0, \qquad a\approx-0.2266988257582+1.4677115087102i. \] The six positively oriented shapes are \[ \left(\frac{1+a-a^2}{2},\ a,\ \frac{1+a}{2},\ 2+a+a^2,\ 3+a+a^2,\ a\right). \tag{10} \] The audit verifies, by exact polynomial reduction, every edge product and both peripheral products. Arb root isolation proves positivity and the marked logarithmic equations: edge angles (2\pi\), peripheral angles zero. These give the complete cusp and complete metric. The Bloch--Wigner sum is rigorously enclosed by \[ 5.13794120187341776984134833947484503 <\operatorname{Vol}(7_4)<5.13794120187341776984134833947484504. \] The face permutations have one ideal vertex and torus vertex link. An optional independent Regina/SnapPy comparison verifies validity, orientability, and the stated knot label and isomorphism signature. The star sizes of (5) are \((4,5,6,4,5,4)\). Therefore (2), unlike the failed repair, bounds **all** weak wrong-edge loci for this triangulation: \[ V_{\mathrm{wrong\ edge}}\leq2v_3 =2.02988321281930725004240510854904057\ldots <\operatorname{Vol}(7_4). \tag{11} \] Thus (6) is an obstruction to a proposed proof mechanism, not a counterexample to volume domination. ## 3. Complete edge multipliers need not have the favorable sign Concavity at the complete geometric point gives the valid inequality \[ V(\alpha)\leq V_g+2\pi\sum_e\mu_e(k_e-1), \tag{12} \] where \(-\log(2\sin\alpha_{ja,g})\) is expressed as a tetrahedron multiplier plus the incident edge multipliers. Decoration changes do not change the pairing with feasible defects. However, its sign is not automatically nonpositive. Use the independently audited three-tetrahedron (5_2) chart. Its complete triples are \[ (A,B,C),(A,B,C),(B,C,A),\qquad (A,B,C)=(\pi-3\theta,2\theta,\theta),\quad 0<\theta<\pi/3. \] Set \[ b=-\log(2\sin2\theta),\qquad c=-\log(2\sin\theta). \] Stationarity gives \(-\log(2\sin A)=(2b+c)/3\). For the exact edge matrix \[ E=\begin{pmatrix} 200&011&110\\ 010&110&101\\ 012&101&011 \end{pmatrix}, \] one can take the edge multipliers \[ \mu=((b-c)/3,\ b-c,\ 0), \tag{13} \] up to their common additive ambiguity. The alias assignment \[ (0,0,1),(1,0,0),(0,0,1) \] has winding (k=(0,1,2)). Consequently, \[ \boxed{\quad \sum_e\mu_e(k_e-1) =\frac{c-b}{3} =\frac{\log(2\cos\theta)}{3}>0.\quad} \tag{14} \] All its tetrahedra are flat. Their actual volume is zero; (12) simply has the wrong sign to prove the desired bound. The positive defect is rigorously enclosed near (0.14059978716148\). ## 4. What the compact Legendre contour does and does not supply here For the original marked potential, clamped radial minimization on the whole angle cube gives the compact positive contour and its unique geometric maximum. An alias changes that potential by \[ W_m(x)=W(x)+2\pi i\,m^Tx, \qquad \operatorname{Im}W_m =\operatorname{Im}W+2\pi m^T\rho. \] The same convex/concave construction can be applied to (W_m), but it then minimizes a different function and has a different angle cell. The original upper bound cannot be transferred by dropping the linear term. Formula (14) demonstrates concretely why comparison at the fixed geometric radius need not have the desired sign. Clipping makes the contour compact; it does not, by itself, compare distinct winding cells. The surviving general routes are therefore substantive: control the actual wall charges by source/Ward cancellation, prove a stronger topological volume comparison, or use a verifiable gap such as (3). The present note proves the third route when its stated criterion holds and rules out two universal shortcuts to the second.

title: The elevated wall source is not supplied by the finite divided-Ward orbit
text: # The elevated wall source is not supplied by the finite divided-Ward orbit Research proof and two exact tests, 27 October 2026. The binomial wall co-source has a literal realization on the degree-N symmetric power of the already proved divided-source standard module. That realization does not automatically carry the true divided Hopf coproduct. A finite-head weight bound rules out a full SL2-equivariant embedding at fixed bridge number and large N. The most immediate q-binomial elevation also fails a bounded diagonal comparison. These are precise restrictions on proposed constructions, not a claim that a linear relative B1 current map is impossible. An explicit weighted stabilization shows why its second transfer coordinate needs an actual network map in addition to a cut orbit. The later [actual high-color construction](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md) evades the fixed-head dimension restriction explicitly. Integral color N(N+1) carries the required Sym^N divided multiplicity, its coherent row is exactly B_N, and its root knot scalar equals K_N with all braiding/peripheral signs retained. Its normal block arrows are actual regularized entries of E,F. This is a source enlargement, not a contradiction to the fixed-head nilpotence bound. Its full divided coproduct/current map and the geometric source projection remain separate requirements. ## 1. The actual wall row and its literal tensor-source realization The [cut-current theorem](actual_gauss_wall_cut_current_complex.md) gives B_N(J)=[1/(N2^N)]sum_(j=0)^N binom(N,j)J_j. (1) J here has the matrix normalization of equation (14a) in the cut-current note. Original raw Green arrays use N B_N instead; that coefficient is retained. Use the actual two-dimensional divided-source subspace L=span(Ubar,W), Ubar=(sum E_(j,j+1))/(N-1), W=E_(N-1,0), Phi(Ubar)=Phi(W)=1/N. On L the explicitly proved normalized divided Hopf adjoints are the standard SL2 matrices e,f,h. Let M_j be the sum of the distinct tensors with j copies of W and N-j copies of Ubar. Then the literal coupon row ell=((N/2)Phi)^(tensor N) satisfies `ell(M_j)=binom(N,j)/2^N`. Hence B_N(J)=(1/N)ell(sum_j J_j M_j). (2) This is an exact source pairing. The primitive tensor SL2 action induced from L makes their span Sym^N L, with a highest string of length N+1. That primitive action is not automatically the true global divided Hopf adjoint on the tensor-source network. Its coproduct contains the mixed ordinary divided powers already computed in the actual fusion theorem. Equation (2) does not discard those terms, nor prove a monoidal Ward intertwiner. ## 2. A fixed-head equivariance obstruction On H=V_N^(tensor b) retain the ordinary integer position grading. For a matrix unit indexed by an output tuple r and input tuple s, its matrix weight is `sum r_i-sum s_i`, in -b(N-1)<=weight<=b(N-1). The true E Hopf adjoint decreases this weight by one. Therefore its degree-N divided-normal operator J_E decreases it by N; normal division changes the coefficient, not the support degree. It follows exactly that (J_E)^(2b)=0 on End(H). (3) On Sym^N L, by contrast, `e^(2b)` is nonzero when N>=2b. Consequently there is no nonzero full-SL2-equivariant map of Sym^N L into this finite-head adjoint space intertwining its e with the actual normalized J_E when N>=2b. Indeed such a map is injective: the standard highest-weight polynomial module Sym^N L is irreducible in characteristic zero, as is seen by raising a nonzero highest weight term and then applying the lowering operator. Equation (3) contradicts injectivity. The same argument applies to a proposed nonzero full-SL2 intertwiner into any subquotient with this same weight bound. It does not rule out a non-equivariant linear current map, a Borel-only quotient, an enlarged normal/tail complex, or a source involving a number of additional factors growing with N. It identifies the additional sector a full equivariant construction would have to supply. ## 3. The first divided q-binomial row has a different whole-head lattice At Q=Q_N, all middle coefficients of `{N choose j}_Q` vanish. Their exact first divided-normal values are d_(N,j)=[{N choose j}_Q/(1-Q^N)]_(Q=Q_N) =N/[(Q_N;Q_N)_j(Q_N;Q_N)_(N-j)] =(-1)^(j-1)Q_N^[-j(j-1)/2]/(1-Q_N^j), 0<j<N. (4) The proof cancels the single numerator factor 1-Q^N before specialization and then pairs the complementary root factors. In particular `|d_(N,j)|=1/[2sin(pi j/N)]`. If the degree-zero endpoint coefficients 1 and the degree-one middle coefficients (4) are put in the same trial source row, the result is `(1,d_1,...,d_(N-1),1)`. This statement specifies the trial Rees identification: it does not identify its two normal degrees by an unproved map. A diagonal adapter to the ordinary row `(binom(N,0),...,binom(N,N))` has endpoint entry one and middle entries `binom(N,j)/d_(N,j)`. Its condition number in every common diagonal metric is at least 2^(N+1)/(N+1), N even, sqrt(3)2^N/(N+1), N odd>=3. (5) Choose a central coefficient, which is at least 2^N/(N+1), and use `2sin(pi j/N)>=sqrt(3)` (equal to 2 at even N). The endpoint-to-center ratio proves (5). Overall row normalization does not remove this condition number. Thus the most immediate q-binomial/Frobenius elevation is not the bounded full-head Gamma unit already proved at source degree N-1. A higher normal extension or a different linear current map might still repair it. Simply replacing classical binomial weights by the first divided q-binomial weights would change the actual co-source. ## 4. An actual weighted stabilization does not give a second cut Weyl identity There is a small universal test using the literal crossing, rather than an arbitrary array. Set N=2, q=i, Q=-1, M=1, x=i. Take a positive Markov stabilization, whose new crossing transfer is k, and attach a weight w^k. Its full root framing and pivot normalization has kappa_D=0. The two cut diagonal entries, computed directly from the actual finite coefficients, are C_0(w)=1, C_1(w)=2w-1. (6) For the second entry the routes are `(i,j,k)=(1,0,1)` and `(1,1,0)`, with their complete normalized weights 2w and -1. The zeroth entry has the single route `(0,0,0)` with weight 1. Thus the original normalized cut gives exactly w; at w=1 this is the correct identity tangle after the twist correction. For a preceding scalar knot cut F I, this local operation gives F times (6). Therefore the transfer distribution after the normalized cut is `(0,F)`. Its unnormalized transfer sum is F. Encoding that sum by a two-dimensional auxiliary diagonal source means the matrix diag(0,2F). The two hemisphere co-sources of that transfer source are then lambda_2^+=F/4, lambda_2^-=3F/4. (7) They are not the two equal cut values F/2. This is an exact universal local stabilization test, not a knot-by-knot argument. It shows that applying a second auxiliary Bernstein reflection to a transfer index is not already the actual cut Weyl identity. The original unweighted invariant remains unchanged. This does not rule out an adapted second framing coordinate on a hyperbolic geometric chart: the new stabilization transfer need not be etale on that critical framing torsor. It proves that such an identification must use its actual network and current equations; it cannot follow from the one-cut source orbit or its two Weyl charts alone. The concrete next map must therefore transport the degree-N wall row (1), the two actual cut endpoints, and the second network framing current together, possibly in a normal/tail extension. The finite cut-current chain map is already explicit. No selected geometric cycle, global microstalk or volume limit is asserted here. Verification is recorded in [audit_degree_elevated_wall_source.py](../experiments/audit_degree_elevated_wall_source.py) and its [results](../experiments/degree_elevated_wall_source_results.json). The coupon and stabilization tests are exact rational-complex matrix calculations. The divided q-row formula and conditioning bound are checked at 80-digit precision for N=2 through 32; their general proof is the finite product cancellation (4). No kernel of the full knot network or selected volume limit is inferred from these tests.

title: Degree elevation preserves the cut and transports the actual head Borel complex
text: # Degree elevation preserves the cut and transports the actual head Borel complex Research proof, 27 October 2026. The uniform co-source obtained by integrating the paired Fr dual has N+1 states, whereas the original head has N. A cyclic identification duplicates its endpoint and does not preserve the head row. The explicit matrix degree elevation below corrects this on ALL head matrices. Together with retained whole arrow gauges it gives an actual cut-Ward cochain map, including the original co-source homotopy. It is not a multiplicative R-network map or a proof of Gaussian/source descent. The earlier [degree-elevated wall note](degree_elevated_wall_source_and_divided_ward.md) constructed the binomial wall row and its fixed-head equivariance obstructions. It did not construct the full matrix degree elevation, its uniform-cut identity, or the actual head-current map proved here. ## 1. Full matrix elevation, with both endpoint entries Put n=N-1. In the actual Fr symbol convention sigma_r(C)=ell_r(u) C psi_r(t)/(1+tu)^r, where psi_r(t)_j=t^j and ell_r(u)_i=binom(r,i)u^i, define \[ (\mathcal E_NC)_{ij} =\frac{N-i}{N}C_{ij}+\frac{i}{N}C_{i-1,j-1}, \qquad 0\le i,j\le N. \tag{1} \] Every out-of-range old entry is zero. Both terms are required. Binomial cancellation gives the exact polynomial identity \[ \ell_N(u)(\mathcal E_NC)\psi_N(t) =(1+tu)\ell_n(u)C\psi_n(t), \qquad\sigma_N(\mathcal E_NC)=\sigma_n(C). \tag{2} \] The map is injective because the symbol numerator determines every matrix entry. It is unital and preserves BOTH actual uniform rows: \[ \frac{\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal E_NC)}{N+1} =\frac{\operatorname{Tr}C}{N},\qquad \frac{\sum_{ij}(\mathcal E_NC)_{ij}}{N+1} =\frac{\sum_{ij}C_{ij}}N. \tag{3} \] Indeed each old entry C_ij occurs with total coefficient ((N-i)+(i+1))/N=(N+1)/N, and the same holds for diagonal entries. The second identity is the original average rank-one coupon, not only the ordinary trace. For a diagonal C the elevated entries are \[ \widetilde C_R=\frac{N-R}{N}C_R+\frac RN C_{R-1}, \quad\widetilde C_0=C_0,\quad\widetilde C_N=C_{N-1}. \tag{4} \] Thus the actual paired-Fr interval, whose integrated dual is uniform 1/(N+1), gives the original head average exactly after (4). By contrast the uncorrected cyclic P_diag insertion repeats C_0 at R=N; it gives weights 2/(N+1),1/(N+1),...,1/(N+1). For C_R=Q_N^R its value is 1/(N+1), while the old head average is zero. Formula (4) is the required endpoint correction, not an identification of these different rows. The binomial wall B_N remains its separate co-source with its original factor 1/N. ## 2. Exact classical and whole Cartan covariance The actual divided Fr matrices on degree r satisfy e psi=(rt-t^2 partial_t)psi, f psi=partial_t psi and h psi=(r-2t partial_t)psi, with their corresponding dual formulas. The normalized commutator fields are independent of r. Applying them to (2) proves \[ \mathcal E_N([x_n,C])=[x_N,\mathcal E_NC], \qquad x=e,f,h. \tag{5} \] This is also checked directly from (1); it is not an assumed published quantization result. Since both terms of (1) have the same i-j, for EVERY nonzero whole parameter Q, \[ \mathcal E_N(\operatorname{Ad}_{Q^{-J_n}}C) =\operatorname{Ad}_{Q^{-J_N}}\mathcal E_NC. \tag{6} \] The image therefore is a global P1 operator/co-source submodule under the ordinary divided Fr f and whole Cartan dilation. Its two extreme entries (0,N),(N,0) are identically zero. It is not the entire End(Sym^N); in particular an arbitrary degree-N wall current need not belong to it. ## 3. Actual whole head arrows give a strict cut-current map In a specified original head basis let K_j=xQ^(-j), F_(j+1,j)=f_j(q), 0<=j<N-1, with all f_j actual nonzero arrow units near q_N. This includes the original balanced f_j=1-Q^(j+1) and the integral f_j=[j+1]_q, with their actual source adapters carried. Define the WHOLE diagonal gauge \[ D_0=1,\qquad D_{j+1}/D_j=(j+1)/f_j(q). \] Then DFD^(-1)=f_n, the classical degree-n lowering matrix, and DKD^(-1)=K. Every q-factorial, source and dual in this gauge is retained; invertibility at fixed N is not an asymptotic norm bound. Put T_0(C)=E_N(DCD^(-1)). Equations (5)--(6) give the LITERAL whole matrix cochain identities \[ T_0((\operatorname{Ad}_K-I)C) =(\operatorname{Ad}_{Q^{-J_N}}-I)T_0(C),\qquad T_0([F,C])=[f_N,T_0(C)]. \tag{7} \] Thus the actual two-row cut-Ward complex maps isomorphically onto its image subcomplex by T_0 in degree zero and the displayed two row maps in degree one. This is an explicit current map, not a declaration that two Borel groups are abstractly isomorphic. The actual Hopf F row is transported too, with its explicit ordered K-row correction retained: \[ \operatorname{ad}_F(C)=[F,C]+K^{-1}[K,C]F, \quad [K,C]=((\operatorname{Ad}_K-I)C)K. \tag{8} \] Use this invertible row operation before (7). Its product term is sent by the LINEAR map T_0 with its full order; T_0 is not applied to its factors separately. The target may use the ACTUAL whole divided Fr lowering matrix on any fixed residue string s. If its arrow is beta_(R,s)(q), set B_(0,s)=1 and B_(R+1,s)/B_(R,s)=beta_(R,s)/(R+1). These are regular actual units with root one, and F^(N)|_s=B_s f_N B_s^(-1). Consequently \[ T_s=\operatorname{Ad}_{B_s}T_0 \tag{9} \] has the same strict properties with actual F^(N)|_s in place of f_N. B_s commutes with the whole memory Cartan Q^(-R). This Cartan is the specified Fr memory observable; it is not silently relabeled as the original high-color quantum K, whose root action is on the head factor. The actual opposite divided generator and mixed tensor coproduct still require their specified normal rows. ## 4. Original cut co-source and its exact transported homotopy Conjugations preserve trace, so (3) gives tau_Fr T_s=tau_head. Before D,B are inserted, (3) also preserves the original average coupon on ALL matrices. After those gauges the actual source and dual are transported; a binomial or uniform row cannot simply be substituted for the conjugated row. There is nevertheless an explicit comparison of the original head average Phi_h and the uniform Fr interval row Phi_Fr on the image. Let B_h be the actual head matrix [K,B_h]=e_h-I/N. In the target let K_Fr=Q^(-J_N) and put \[ (B_{\rm Fr})_{ij}=\frac1{(N+1)(Q^{-i}-Q^{-j})} \quad(i\ne j,\ \{i,j\}\ne\{0,N\}), \] with the diagonal and the two extreme corners zero. Every displayed denominator is a unit near Q_N. The omitted corners of T_s(C) are IDENTICALLY zero, so the actual trace homotopies give \[ \Phi_h(C)-\Phi_{\rm Fr}(T_sC) =-\operatorname{Tr}(B_h[K,C]) +\operatorname{Tr}(B_{\rm Fr}[K_{\rm Fr},T_sC]). \tag{10} \] The last commutator equals T_s((Ad_K-I)C) K_Fr. Thus (10) is an explicit cochain homotopy on the actual cut-Ward complex. It holds with the whole D and B_s units present, not only at their numerical root values. On actual diagonal Green arrays these conjugations do nothing and (3)--(4) preserve the original cut exactly. On Ward-closed cut matrices the homotopy is zero as well. The raw Green 1/N normalization remains the one in the original certificate. The excluded extreme target corners and the complementary operator subspace cannot be discarded if an arbitrary Fr-valued wall or normal current leaves the image. This is where an additional endpoint/mixed-normal source may still occur. ## 5. Scope of this actual map The source and coefficient complex at the FINAL finite cut is now explicitly related to global Fr P1 operators, the integrated uniform Fr co-source, and the actual head Hopf rows. It does not turn T_s into an algebra homomorphism: already N=2, E_2(P_0)=diag(1,1/2,0), so E_2(P_0)^2!=E_2(P_0). Products, R crossings and mixed coproducts must therefore be transported as whole ordered operators, not factor by factor. Nor has an internal remaining flow index been identified with this open cut matrix index. The geometric Gaussian/source comparison must still map its two retained currents and normal endpoint classes to the explicit finite complex. The result here is a genuine cut cochain map and co-source homotopy, not a selected geometric period or volume limit. [Exact matrix and coherent-symbol audit](../experiments/audit_degree_elevation_actual_head_ward.py). The [results](../experiments/degree_elevation_actual_head_ward_results.json) pass fourteen actual generic-q/root cases N=2,...,8 and 406 full matrix units. They check the complete symbols and both uniform rows, whole arrow gauges, the actual Fr divided string, Hopf row correction and co-source homotopy. These are actual finite cut identities, not a Gaussian or selected-cycle test.

title: The degree-elevation complement is one marked quantum-normal wall line
text: # The degree-elevation complement is one marked quantum-normal wall line Research theorem and actual crossing/source calculation, 27 October 2026. The complement omitted by actual cut degree elevation has dimension 2N+1, but its whole memory-Borel complex contracts to ONE two-term wall complex. The contraction retains the two extreme corners and uses no division by the wall parameter. Its root norm is O(N) in the natural unitary spin metric. The source on that wall is essential. The original coherent cut assigns it 2^(-N); the uniform interval assigns 1/(N+1). Their exponential ratio cannot be discarded as a Ward homotopy. An explicit charged component of the FIRST ACTUAL universal R normal hits the wall generator in an ordered current calculation. No full-network cancellation or selected geometric contribution is inferred from these local statements. ## 1. The actual missing subspace and its global boundary polynomial Use [actual matrix degree elevation](degree_elevation_actual_head_ward_map.md) \(\mathcal E_N:\operatorname{End}\operatorname{Sym}^{N-1} \to\operatorname{End}\operatorname{Sym}^{N}\). It is injective, unital, cut-preserving and equivariant for the ACTUAL divided classical commutators. Write \[ \mathcal I_N=\operatorname{im}\mathcal E_N,\qquad \operatorname{End}\operatorname{Sym}^{N} =\mathcal I_N\oplus\mathcal W_N. \] The summands have adjoint spins 0,...,N-1 and N respectively; \(\dim\mathcal W_N=2N+1\). A concrete quotient map is \[ \operatorname{ob}_N(C)(u) =u^N\ell_N(u)C\psi_N(-1/u) =\sum_{i,j}(-1)^j{N\choose i}C_{ij}u^{N+i-j}. \tag{1.1} \] Its kernel is exactly I_N: the symbol numerator is divisible by 1+ut precisely when its restriction t=-1/u vanishes. The degree bound then leaves a numerator of bidegree at most N-1, giving the unique old matrix. Its image is every polynomial of degree at most 2N. Thus W_N is the GLOBAL H0(O(2N)) boundary module, rather than an arbitrary missing collection of matrix entries. Its two endpoint corners are e^N=N!E_(0,N) and f^N=N!E_(N,0). For complete direct verification, (1.1) takes ad e,ad f,ad h to partial_u, 2Nu-u^2 partial_u, 2N-2u partial_u, and takes Ad(Q^(-J)) to g(u)->Q^N g(u/Q). The [independent incidence/source calculation](degree_elevation_wall_residual_and_source_moments.md) records this quotient and its one-sided clock residuals. One may project onto W_N algebraically without choosing a split matrix basis: the adjoint Casimir \(\mathcal C=(\operatorname{ad}h)^2/2+ \operatorname{ad}e\operatorname{ad}f+ \operatorname{ad}f\operatorname{ad}e\) has eigenvalues 2l(l+1). Its polynomial projector onto eigenvalue 2N(N+1) is \(\prod_{l=0}^{N-1}(\mathcal C-2l(l+1))/ [2N(N+1)-2l(l+1)]\). All denominators are nonzero constants. ## 2. The exact whole Borel complex Let R be the actual coefficient field completed in delta=1-Q^N, retaining Q=Q_N(1-delta)^(1/N). Work first in the untwisted target frame, with memory K=Q^(-J), rho=Ad K and F=ad f. The ACTUAL whole arrow gauge B_s(q) sends f to the original F^(N)|_s and commutes with memory K. Conjugating the complex below by B_s carries all its units and source marks. The memory K is not the old physical high-color head clock. On any invariant spin module define \[ \begin{split} d_0C&=((\rho-I)C,FC),\\ d_1(X,Y)&=(\rho-Q^{-1})Y-Q^{-1}FX. \tag{2.1} \end{split} \] The identity rho F=Q^(-1)F rho proves d_1d_0=0 exactly over R. No root specialization has occurred. For spin l choose a basis v_0,...,v_L, L=2l, satisfying Fv_j=v_(j+1) and rho v_j=Q^(l-j)v_j. Each j<L gives a separate three-term fork \[ R\ \xrightarrow{a\mapsto(A_ja,a)}\ R^2 \xrightarrow{(x,y)\mapsto Q^{-1}(-x+A_jy)}\ R, \quad A_j=Q^{l-j}-1. \tag{2.2} \] It contracts using h_1(x,y)=y and h_2(z)=(-Qz,0), whether or not A_j vanishes at the root. The only remaining terms are \[ [R\xrightarrow{Q^{-l}-1}R]_{0,1},\qquad [R\xrightarrow{Q^l-Q^{-1}}R]_{1,2}. \tag{2.3} \] This is a literal direct decomposition, not a numerical rank argument. In particular it keeps both possible resonance lines. For W_N take l=N and normalize the chain by \[ v_j=\frac{(-1)^N}{(2N)!}(\operatorname{ad}f)^j e^N, \quad v_{2N}=f^N. \tag{2.4} \] The last equality follows by expanding the commutator: only its middle term survives, giving ad(f)^(2N)e^N=(-1)^N(2N)!f^N. The second arrow in (2.3) is a unit since its root is 1-Q_N^(-1). The entire complement therefore contracts to \[ \boxed{\ [R f^N\xrightarrow{,Q^{-N}-1,}R f^N]_{0,1}\ }, \qquad Q^{-N}-1=\frac\delta{1-\delta}. \tag{2.5} \] The coefficient has a SIMPLE zero, with derivative one. At the root H0 and H1 are each the one-dimensional marked wall line, and H2=0. Over the whole formal DVR, H0=0 and H1=R/(delta). Its root kernel and its first-normal Bockstein must therefore be retained together; no free whole horizontal source line is being asserted. ## 3. Explicit projection and contraction retaining every unit For x=sum x_jv_j, y=sum y_jv_j and z=sum z_jv_j, projection to (2.5) is pi_0(C)=C_(2N) and pi_1(x,y)=x_(2N); inclusion uses v_(2N) in degree zero and (v_(2N),0) in degree one. Put \[ \begin{split} h_1(x,y)&=\sum_{j=0}^{2N-1}y_{j+1}v_j,\\ h_2(z)&=\left(-Q\sum_{j=1}^{2N}z_jv_{j-1},\ (Q^N-Q^{-1})^{-1}z_0v_0\right). \tag{3.1} \end{split} \] Direct substitution gives h_1d_0=I-iota_0pi_0, d_0h_1+h_2d_1=I-iota_1pi_1, and d_1h_2=I. Only Q^N-Q^(-1), a unit, is inverted. The wall delta is never inverted. Conjugating all maps by the ACTUAL B_s(q) gives the same contraction on the actual whole target complement Ad(B_s)W_N. The original source/co-source must be conjugated or evaluated with those same B_s units; root B_s=I does not erase their derivatives. In the unitary Fr metric ||v_k||^2=binom(N,k), e and f are adjoints. The highest-spin Hilbert--Schmidt module has an orthonormal chain with F-arrow coefficients sqrt((j+1)(2N-j)). Its anchored F inverse has norm 1/sqrt(2N). Using those coefficients in (3.1), its fork inverses have that same bound; the remaining unit inverse has root norm 1/[2 sin(pi/N)]. The orthogonal W_N projector has norm one. Hence the root complement contraction has norm O(N), explicitly at most max(1/sqrt(2N),1/[2 sin(pi/N)]). This is a bound on the COMPLEX contraction, not on every source functional or on a uniform off-root neighborhood. ## 4. The actual global co-source on the extra module Under (1.1), the basis (2.4) is \(\operatorname{ob}_N(v_j)=N!u^j/(2N-j)!\). Thus any ACTUAL cut functional Phi restricts to the global dual Čech class \[ c_\Phi(u)=\sum_{j=0}^{2N} \frac{(2N-j)!}{N!}\Phi(v_j)u^{-j-1} \quad\text{in }H^1(O(-2N-2)). \tag{4.1} \] Its residue pairing with ob_N(C) equals Phi(C) on W_N, by the [explicit two-chart source pairing](global_frobenius_cech_source_and_endpoints.md). The two corner components occupy different north/south Laurent modes. Neither is a zero Čech class merely because it was absent from the degree-elevation image. For the normalized wall generator w=f^N/N!=E_(N,0), ||w||_HS=1, the ACTUAL paired coherent source gives \[ \Phi_m(w)=\left(\frac{1-m}{2}\right)^N, \qquad \Phi_+(w)=2^{-N}\quad(m=0). \tag{4.2} \] The uniform interval row gives instead \[ \Phi_{\rm uni}(w)=\frac1{N+1}. \tag{4.3} \] The ratio is 2^N/(N+1), GENUINELY exponential. For the unnormalized divided generator f^N the two values are N!/2^N and N!/(N+1). Their actual normalization has not been hidden by declaring its matrix unit to be the source value one. The coupled original source makes the head endpoint explicit: \(\Phi_{e_D}(w\otimes H_{\rm head})=2^{-N}(H_{\rm head})_{00}\). The Fr endpoints 0 and N are the SAME cyclic head endpoint. The uniform interval row is not that original coherent coupon. Since w is root Ward-closed, no root co-source homotopy on the full target can equate (4.2) and (4.3). There is still an exact relative-endpoint interpretation: Phi_m(w)dm/2=-d[((1-m)/2)^(N+1)/(N+1)]. Its interval integral from -1 to +1 is 1/(N+1), while its endpoint-coherent value at m=0 is 2^(-N). Exactness of a primitive does not eliminate its marked endpoint jump. The global class (4.1), actual normal units, and relative endpoint density remain together. The OTHER omitted corner w_high=E_(0,N) has response Phi_m(w_high)=((1+m)/2)^N. It is carried by the contracted forks, not a second H0 wall: Fw_high!=0. Its interval primitive is ((1+m)/2)^(N+1)/(N+1), with a nonzero POSITIVE-endpoint jump. Thus the two corners have different cochain roles even though their uniform integrals and their coherent values at m=0 agree. Contracting the highest corner requires its recorded Ward/source homotopy, rather than deleting its relative endpoint pairing. ## 5. An unavoidable charged FIRST ACTUAL R normal sees the wall In the constant actual integral frame, put I_1=R_0^(-1)R_1. For r=N its first resonant transfer, including every head entry, is exactly \[ (I_1)_{(-1,+1)}=N e\otimes f \otimes I_{\rm heads}. \tag{5.1} \] This is the original universal R tail, not an appended operator: the first-normal coefficient is kappa_N E^(N) tensor F^(N), kappa_N=N(-1)^(N-1), and E^(N)=(-1)^(N-1)e. All nonresonant normal terms change at most ONE Fr block, while Cartan terms change neither. Thus no other first-normal term can cancel the charged component (-1,+1) of (5.1). The actual whole diagonal arrow gauges B_s(q) add first-normal gauge terms of ZERO Fr block charge. They therefore cannot erase this charged channel; their units remain in all other rows. Let n=N-1 and choose actual old-head matrix coupons P_0=E_(0,0) and C_low=E_(n,0). Put X=E_N(P_0), Y=E_N(C_low). Their entries are \[ X=\operatorname{diag}(1,1/N,0,\ldots),\qquad Y=N^{-1}E_{N-1,0}+E_{N,1}. \] Here fY=Yf=w. Consequently the charged (-1,+N) component of the ACTUAL adjoint normal current is \[ \Pi_{(-1,+N)}[I_1,X\otimes Y] =N[e,X]\otimes w\otimes I_{\rm heads}. \tag{5.2} \] Its first factor is \([e,X]=-(N-1)E_{0,1}-(N-1)E_{1,2}/N\), an elevated old head current. The second factor is precisely the wall generator, not an element of I_N. At a generic root the first factor is a memory-Cartan Ward term, since its charge has unit Q_N-1. Thus (5.2) is a concrete LOCAL Ward/carry source with a wall-valued coefficient; it is not a closed scalar knot invariant by itself. Its two legitimate paired values are different: \[ (\Phi_{\rm uni}\otimes\Phi_{\rm uni})(5.2) =-\frac{N-1}{N+1},\qquad (\Phi_+\otimes\Phi_+)(5.2) =-\frac{N(N-1)}{2^{2N-1}}. \tag{5.3} \] Both are nonzero. The relative co-source can therefore detect this actual omitted-corner channel; it cannot be dropped as a zero Čech boundary or replaced by its uniform value. Under the controlled coupled-source gauge G, the e and f factors also acquire their literal head shifts V^(-1) and V. The source coupon must be conjugated WITH the operator. Leaving a head shift behind while changing the source would give a different pairing, potentially zero. No such change is made in (5.3). For the relative interaction-commutator used here, I(0)=I and its root commutator is zero. Thus its first coefficient depends only on (5.2), even when the input coupons and paired source have their actual whole lifts. This does NOT remove the separate lift terms in the whole Euler/current formula (8d) of the [endpoint-completed clock theorem](endpoint_completed_normal_clock_euler_current.md). That formula still uses the prescribed H_1 and its charged head neighbors. No general current descent follows by replacing it with this one isolated interaction channel. ## 6. Low raw PBW order versus ordered products and clock gauges A PBW operator of degree d<N has normalized coherent numerator divisible by (1+ut)^(N-d), so ob_N vanishes. In particular raw interaction coefficients of order j lie in the elevation image on every Fr leg whenever N>2j, by the actual all-normal bound. The first possible order for a raw PBW complement is ceil(N/2). This is an exclusion bound; attainment by a particular actual crossing or closed word is a separate assertion. This does NOT say multiplication by such a coefficient preserves the image: (5.2) is already a first-normal counterexample on elevated input coupons. Nor does it apply to a controlled source gauge containing genuine whole clock dilations. Their one-sided symbols can have nonzero ob_N even at root order. Their actions must be kept as whole functions with their source characters. The [Clebsch strictification](clebsch_memory_dilation_and_actual_r_excursions.md) keeps its complementary memory sector for precisely this reason; neither that construction nor (2.5) declares the full actual R network image-invariant. Every actual offimage current must be projected by (1.1) and then checked in the explicit complex (2.1). A CLOSED residual reduces to its ONE wall component; its value there uses the ORIGINAL source row, not automatically (4.3). The global geometric Ward/current map, its charged head neighbors and the selected regulator norm remain to be proved. This result replaces an arbitrary 2N+1-dimensional missing source by an exact single marked Bockstein wall line and exhibits an actual R channel which makes its source normalization unavoidable. [Exact actual-matrix/complex audit](../experiments/audit_degree_elevation_complement_wall.py). [Results](../experiments/degree_elevation_complement_wall_results.json). [Independent quotient/source audit](degree_elevation_wall_residual_and_source_moments.md).

title: The exact degree-elevation residual and its selected endpoint source
text: # The exact degree-elevation residual and its selected endpoint source Independent proof and source audit, 27 October 2026. Degree elevation maps the original head cut-Ward complex into the Fr source and preserves its original cut. Its missing operator channel has an explicit incidence polynomial. After the two Borel rows are contracted, one resonant endpoint remains, and its ACTUAL selected co-source differs exponentially from the uniform interval row. One-sided clock moments also have an explicit auxiliary correction. These formulas identify concrete data to compute in the relative orbit co-source test. They do not construct the internal geometric Gaussian map or a selected-volume estimate. ## 1. An explicit polynomial detects exactly the missing channel Use the actual divided Fr basis v_i of Sym^N and put \[ b_D(u,t)=\ell_N(u)D\psi_N(t),\qquad \mathfrak o_N(D)(u)=u^N b_D(u,-1/u) =\sum_{i,j=0}^N(-1)^j\binom NiD_{ij}u^{N+i-j}. \tag{1} \] This is a polynomial of degree at most 2N. The [degree-elevation map](degree_elevation_actual_head_ward_map.md) satisfies \[ \ker\mathfrak o_N=\mathcal E_N\operatorname{End}(\mathrm{Sym}^{N-1}). \tag{2} \] Indeed the symbol numerator of E_N(C) is (1+tu)b_C. Conversely, vanishing in (1) says that the polynomial b_D is divisible by the irreducible polynomial 1+tu. The quotient has degree at most N-1 in each variable, hence is the unique symbol numerator of an old head matrix. Formula (2) is an EXACT image criterion, stronger than vanishing of the two extreme corners alone. Every degree 0,...,2N occurs from a matrix unit, so (1) is surjective. It realizes the full highest-spin quotient directly: \[ \begin{split} \mathfrak o_N([e,D])&=\partial_u\mathfrak o_N(D),\\ \mathfrak o_N([f,D])&=(2Nu-u^2\partial_u)\mathfrak o_N(D),\\ \mathfrak o_N([h,D])&=(2N-2u\partial_u)\mathfrak o_N(D),\\ \mathfrak o_N(\operatorname{Ad}_{Q^{-J}}D) &=Q^N\mathfrak o_N(D)(u/Q). \tag{3} \end{split} \] For example the commutator f acts on the normalized symbol by (-partial_t-u^2 partial_u); it differentiates 1+tu by -u(1+tu). Restriction to t=-1/u gives exactly the second line of (3). The other formulas follow the same way or by matrix units. For the ORIGINAL whole divided string gauge B_s of the head-Ward map, use instead \[ \mathfrak o_{N,s}(D)=\mathfrak o_N(B_s^{-1}DB_s). \tag{4} \] All B_s units and their normal derivatives remain present. A Fr Green/current matrix can use the old head co-source homotopy precisely when this polynomial vanishes, or after its nonzero remainder has been accounted for separately. ## 2. Independent contraction of the quotient current complex In the quotient write weight m=-N,...,N, let B=ad_f raise weight, and let A=Ad_K-I, K=Q^-J. The actual two-row complex is \[ d_0=(A,B),\qquad d_1(X,Y)=(\operatorname{Ad}_K-Q^{-1})Y-Q^{-1}BX. \tag{5} \] It is a complex because Ad_K B=Q^-1 B Ad_K. Put a_m=Q^-m-1 and Bv_m=b_m v_(m+1). Every b_m for m<N is a nonzero integer in characteristic zero, hence a unit. For each m<N the three-term summand is \[ R\xrightarrow{(a_m,b_m)}R^2 \xrightarrow{(-Q^{-1}b_m,Q^{-1}a_m)}R, \] which contracts using b_m. This works even when a_m=0, so the other root resonances at m=0 or -N leave no hidden classes. The remaining bottom degree-one arrow has coefficient Q^N-Q^-1, a unit near a primitive N-th root for N>=2, and contracts as well. What remains is EXACTLY \[ R\xrightarrow{Q^{-N}-1}R \quad\text{in degrees zero and one}. \tag{6} \] The top generator may be taken to be f^N=N!E_(N,0). With Z=Q^N and delta=1-Z, its differential is Q^-N-1=delta/Z. Thus the first-normal Bockstein has coefficient PLUS ONE in the delta convention, or -N in the Log Q normal. There is no degree-two quotient homology. This is the quotient theorem for the specified Fr MEMORY Cartan. It does not identify it with the original high-color quantum K. For the old physical clock C_Q=Q^S Z^R, the same endpoint changes Fr block R by N, so its conjugation character is Z^N instead. Those whole normal characters must not be interchanged because their root numerical values happen to coincide. There is an equally explicit root-cycle classification. A matrix commuting with the regular nilpotent f is a polynomial in f. Cartan closure at Q_N removes every power f^j except j=0,N. Thus every scalar-coefficient root cycle is \[ D=aI+cE_{N,0},\qquad c=D_{N,0}. \tag{6a} \] The old degree-elevation image contributes only the scalar part. With head coefficients the same statement holds entrywise; the actual selected head co-source must then be applied as well. The full quotient construction is recorded in [the complement Bockstein wall](degree_elevation_complement_bockstein_wall.md). The unit-fork calculation above is an independent proof audit. ## 3. The original selected endpoint co-source is not the uniform row The uniform rank-one Fr cut and the selected coherent Fr cut give \[ \Phi_{\rm uni}(E_{N,0})=\frac1{N+1},\qquad \Phi_+(E_{N,0})=2^{-N},\qquad \Phi_{\rm uni}(f^N)=\frac{N!}{N+1}. \tag{7} \] These are literal matrix pairings in the actual divided basis. Under B_s the frozen uniform row acquires the retained whole factor B_(N,s)/B_(0,s); transporting the row itself compensates it exactly. The root factor is one, but its normal coefficients cannot be erased. E_(N,0) is Ward-closed at the root: it commutes with f, and its K conjugation character is Q^-N=1. Therefore the difference of the two co-sources in (7) is NOT Ward-exact on the full Fr target. Their ratio 2^N/(N+1) cannot be inferred to be a harmless algebraic normalization. The head-map homotopy applies on the image (2), where both extreme corners vanish; it does not extend to this additional endpoint class without its retained source. An exact source gauge can still compare the two descriptions by conjugating ALL currents and the endpoint generator too. It does not justify freezing that generator while replacing its co-source. In the coordinates (6a), the two root periods are respectively a+c/(N+1) and a+2^-N c. This source character is visible as a whole function, not just as a list of matrix values. For the actual paired Borel coupon e_(alpha,m)=psi_alpha lambda_m, \[ \mathfrak o_N(e_{\alpha,m})(u) =\left[(1+u)\frac{(1+m)u-(1-m)}2\right]^N, \qquad\Phi_m(E_{N,0})=((1-m)/2)^N. \tag{8} \] The normalized scale alpha cancels; its UNNORMALIZED power line alpha^N must still be retained in the original source object. At the selected m=0 the first polynomial is 2^-N(u^2-1)^N. The actual interval average over m=-1,...,1 instead integrates the second character to 1/(N+1). This explains both agreement on closed scalar cuts and disagreement on the new endpoint. The whole retained-weight interval comparison in [the global Cech source](global_frobenius_cech_source_and_endpoints.md) keeps its density; it does not assert that these two endpoint co-sources are equal or Ward-homotopic on the entire target. There is a head-matrix version for the actual coupled coupon e_D. Write s(i)=i for i<N and s(N)=0. Its Fr blocks are \[ (e_D)_{ij}=2^{-N}\binom Nj E_{s(i),s(j)}. \] Consequently \[ \mathfrak o_N(e_D)(u)=2^{-N}u^N a(u)b(u)^t, \tag{9} \] where a_0=1+u^N, b_0=1+(-1)^N u^-N, and for 1<=S<N, a_S=binom(N,S)u^S, b_S=(-1)^S binom(N,S)u^-S. This expression is a polynomial despite its factored Laurent notation. Its bottom and top coefficients are respectively (-1)^N2^-N E_00 and 2^-N E_00. In particular the ACTUAL selected functional satisfies \[ \Phi_{e_D}(E_{N,0}\otimes H) =2^{-N}H_{00}. \tag{10} \] The surviving source cannot be replaced by the uniform interval row merely because both return the same closed knot scalar. ## 4. Exact one-sided clock and Green moment corrections Split E=E_0+E_1 using its two terms, so (E_1C)_ij=(i/N)C_(i-1,j-1). For every retained scalar function g on the indicated finite spectra, \[ \begin{split} E(g(J_{\rm head})C) &=g(J_N)E_0(C)+g(J_N-1)E_1(C),\\ E(Cg(J_{\rm head})) &=E_0(C)g(J_N)+E_1(C)g(J_N-1). \tag{11} \end{split} \] The functions at the extra argument -1 may be chosen arbitrarily where their multiplier is zero; they must be regular wherever that multiplier is nonzero. These identities follow directly from the row and column indices. In particular \[ E(w^J C)=w^{J_N}\{E(C)+(w^{-1}-1)E_1(C)\}, \tag{12} \] and the polynomial moment correction is exactly the backward difference [p(J_N-1)-p(J_N)]E_1(C). Ad-clock covariance is strict because the same auxiliary offset cancels between row and column. One-sided Green moments do not have that cancellation. For normalized degree-h moments the backward difference contains the explicit powers N^-s, s=1,...,h; they are retained before any period/character estimate. ## 5. Whole word strictification retains a genuine auxiliary source There is a direct positive strictification of (11). On Sym^(N-1) tensor C^2 define \[ \begin{split} i_+v_k&=v_k\otimes u_0+v_{k-1}\otimes u_1,\\ p_+(v_k\otimes u_0)&=(N-k)v_k/N,\\ p_+(v_k\otimes u_1)&=(k+1)v_{k+1}/N. \end{split} \] Then p_+i_+=I and E(C)=p_+(C tensor I)i_+. The complementary projector is I-i_+p_+; it is the Sym^(N-2) channel. EXACTLY, \[ E(CD)-E(C)E(D) =p_+(C\otimes I)(I-i_+p_+)(D\otimes I)i_+. \tag{13} \] Thus the full auxiliary operator algebra is multiplicative and preserves an ordered actual word, while a product of upper compressions omits the displayed lower-channel excursions. The original head number is J_total minus the auxiliary bit; its two blocks have total degrees J_N and J_(N-2)+1. This is the operator explanation of (11)--(12). An exact source-preserving FINAL CUT choice even has both external ends in the upper channel. Set \[ \Psi=i_+\mathbf1_{N+1}=\mathbf1_N\otimes(u_0+u_1), \qquad\Lambda=\frac{\mathbf1_{N+1}^t}{N+1}p_+. \] Its auxiliary dual is correlated with the head: \[ \Lambda(v_k\otimes u_0)=\frac{N-k}{N(N+1)},\qquad \Lambda(v_k\otimes u_1)=\frac{k+1}{N(N+1)}. \] It pairs with Psi to one, annihilates the lower channel, and gives Lambda(C tensor I)Psi=sum(C_ij)/N for EVERY head C. The same holds for a full ordered word with all internal excursions kept. A product auxiliary dual is a different source. Closed/pivotal strands require their actual transported caps and pivot operators; the unweighted final-cut identity does not substitute for those. This is an auxiliary matrix-word extension of the old head R, not an equality with the existing actual high-integral-color R. ## 6. The precise remaining relative source calculation For the norm-orbit test Lambda_rel omega, the new head map removes the cut K/F rows on its image by its actual co-source homotopy. An arbitrary Fr-valued current first has the explicit remainder (1)/(4). The quotient contraction (6) reduces its cohomological source obstruction to the one resonant endpoint; its selected weight is (7)--(10), NOT automatically the uniform row. This does not prove that the two INTERNAL framing Green currents land in that head image, or that their remaining relative endpoint and logarithmic carry classes cancel. A map of those actual currents must retain (11), all lower excursions in (13), the physical versus memory-clock distinction, charged normal head neighbors, the original chirp and full peripheral line. The explicit residual polynomials and endpoint coefficient are now finite tests for that map, rather than a general group-theoretic identification or an assumed scalar normalization. [Exact residual/source audit](../experiments/audit_degree_elevation_wall_residual.py).

title: The divided adjoint pairs nontrivially with the actual missing edge
text: # The divided adjoint pairs nontrivially with the actual missing edge Research proof, 27 October 2026. The genuine complete integral Weyl color gives a divided Hopf-adjoint operator on its matrix space. Applied to the literal missing cyclic edge, it has an exact nonzero pairing with the prescribed marked cut. This yields a cohomologous divided-normal realization of the original knot cut functional. It does not prove survival of the geometric Gaussian period. ## 1. The two normal directions are distinct Keep `Q=q^2`, `x=-M/q`. In the balanced basis the generic truncated raising entries are Ecal_(a-1,a)=M Q^(-a)-M^(-1), 1<=a<N. The absent cyclic entry is the specified coefficient w(q,M)=M Q^(-N)-M^(-1), W=E_(N-1,0). It vanishes identically on the genuine integral Weyl color `M=-q^N`. At the fixed root `Q^N=1` it becomes `w=kappa=M-M^(-1)`. These two restrictions are different normal directions. If `delta=1-Q^N`, their exact relation is w=kappa+M delta/(1-delta). At the complete intersection `M=1,delta=0`, one has `dw=d kappa+d delta`; the Weyl curve is `w=0`, not `kappa=0`. No tensor divided power below is identified with the generic-M cyclic-edge normal by replacing one parameter with the other. ## 2. The actual divided Hopf adjoint Take the genuine Weyl family `V(q)=D_(N-1)(q)` on `M=-q^N`, as in [the factorial fusion proof](divided_ward_factorial_fusion.md). For a matrix `T` its actual generic Hopf adjoint is A(T)=ad_Ecal(T)=[Ecal,T]K^(-1). Write `A=X+Y`, with X(T)=Ecal T K^(-1), Y(T)=-T Ecal K^(-1). Then `XY=Q YX` and `X^N=Y^N=0` for every generic `q`. Hence the same q-binomial cancellation as for the tensor divided power defines a regular actual operator on the root matrix space: J_ad=[A^N/(1-Q^N)]_(q=q_N) =sum_(j=1)^(N-1) c_j Y^(N-j)X^j, c_j=N/[(Q;Q)_j(Q;Q)_(N-j)]. (1) This is the divided **Hopf** adjoint. It need not equal ordinary commutation by the divided power on `V`; that latter power is zero on the individual color. Formula (1) retains the mixed antipode terms acting through `V tensor V*`. ## 3. Exact action on the missing edge At the actual root set epsilon_a=Q^(-a)-1, P_a=product_(s=1)^a epsilon_s, P_(N-1)=(-1)^(N-1)N, K^N=(-1)^(N-1)I. Let `l=N-j`. The `j`-th term of (1) applied to `W=E_(N-1,0)` is supported only at matrix entry `(l-1,l)`. Its coefficient is c_j (-1)^l Q^(-l(l-1)/2-jl) P_(N-1) epsilon_l K^(-N). Using c_j=c_l=(-1)^(l-1)Q^(-l(l-1)/2)/(1-Q^l), epsilon_l=(1-Q^l)Q^(-l), and `Q^N=1`, every coefficient simplifies to `-N`. Therefore J_ad(W)=-N sum_(l=1)^(N-1) E_(l-1,l). (2) This holds for every `N>=2`, with the original balanced root basis. For the literal marked source and co-source, e_(a,b)=1/N, Phi(T)=Tr(eT)=Tr(g D T), equation (2) gives the exact nonzero pairing Phi(J_ad(W))=-(N-1). (3) The normalized ordinary trace of (2) is zero. Thus the marked normal pairing is visible before the ordinary scalar Ward quotient. Its degrees are explicit: `W` raises matrix index by `N-1`, `J_ad` lowers it by `N`, and the marked cut supplies the remaining one-step pairing. This is a mixed divided-normal/missing-edge cochain calculation, not a nonzero closed geometric class. ## 4. An actual cohomologous divided-normal cut Define the literal all-matrices row Phi_div(T)=-Phi(J_ad(T W))/(N-1). (4) Equation (3) says `Phi_div(I)=1`. Let `delta_W(T)=([K,T],[F,T])` and let `h_W` be the explicit actual Ward contraction in [the finite Ward note](actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction.md), so h_W delta_W=I-i p, p(T)=Tr(T)/N, i(c)=c I. Since `(Phi_div-Phi)i=0`, one obtains the exact cochain homotopy on **all** matrices, Phi_div-Phi=(Phi_div-Phi)h_W delta_W. (5) In particular every actual closed cut tangle is Ward closed, hence equals `F_N(1) I`. Equations (4)--(5) give Phi_div(C_K)=Phi(C_K)=F_N(1)=Kashaev_N(K). (6) Thus (4) is an explicit divided-normal source realization of the original invariant, with its source and normalization fixed. It is not a new invariant or a redefinition of its numerical values. The full ADO value retains the entire external marked line; at completion it multiplies (6) by `i^(N+3)/N`. That scalar is not absorbed into (4). ## 5. Pivotal partial trace commutes with the genuine divided adjoint For the genuine generic integral colors use the generic pivotal partial trace ptr_K(T)=Tr_closed[(I tensor K_closed)T]. The generic Hopf adjoint and this trace commute on every matrix. This follows from the ordinary antipode cancellation; equivalently the generic pivotal cap is a Hopf map. Apply the generic identity to the `N`-th adjoint power and divide both sides by `1-Q^N`. The divided operators are regular by the q-binomial argument on the corresponding tensor-and-dual colors. Specialization gives ptr_K J_ad,total=J_ad,cut ptr_K. (7) At the root, the actual pivot satisfies `g_closed=K_closed^(1-N)=chi_closed^(-1)K_closed`, where the entire scalar `chi_closed=K_closed^N` is retained. Thus (7) holds also for the original actual pivotal partial trace `ptr_g`. The order of the marked edge matters. For an arbitrary full tensor matrix `T`, the cut edge lifts as `W_cut tensor I_closed`, so the exact all-matrices identity is Phi_div(ptr_g T) =-Phi(ptr_g[J_ad,total(T(W_cut tensor I))])/(N-1). (8) Here `ptr_g(T(W_cut tensor I))=(ptr_g T)W_cut` was used. There is no license to replace the argument of `J_ad,total` by `T` and move the edge unchanged outside it. The mixed Hopf-adjoint terms are essential. Equations (7)--(8) transport the new source through the actual contraction while keeping its insertion order. ## 6. What this proves about cohomology and HPL The action `J_ad` lowers matrix weight by `N`, so its square is zero on `End(V_N)`. It annihilates `I` and has zero normalized ordinary trace on every matrix. It consequently induces a chain map on the split image Ward complex: set J_ad^1(delta_W T)=delta_W(J_ad T). This is well defined because the kernel of `delta_W` is `k I` and `J_ad(I)=0`. Its action on scalar Ward cohomology is zero. Likewise the marked row `Phi J_ad` is Ward exact, by composing the old cut homotopy with this chain map. This is consistent with the nonzero cochain pairing (3): the missing edge is not Ward closed. The normalized row (4), in contrast, has the same **nonzero** cohomology class as the original cut, by (5). It is now represented using a genuine divided adjoint and the literal missing edge. This gives concrete source data for a future source-preserving Gaussian chain comparison. It does not construct that comparison or show which geometric formal class has nonzero image. Nilpotence of an inserted operator and exact scalar Ward normalization alone do not supply the missing HPL map or an asymptotic volume theorem. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_divided_ward_factorial_fusion.py) and [results](../experiments/divided_ward_factorial_fusion_results.json) check (2)--(5) on every matrix unit at seven levels and verify the all-matrices pivotal and ordered-insertion identities (7)--(8).

title: A divided-normal source orbit and the canonical framing form
