text: # A divided-normal source orbit and the canonical framing form Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual divided Hopf adjoints contain a two-dimensional standard SL2 module. Its cut Borel orbit is an explicit sign cover of the classical framing torsor, with the correct canonical two-form and leading co-source covariance. The same normal matrices admit a concrete clock/shift realization and a regular diagonal comparison with the actual cyclic source. These are algebraic source, group, and density maps. They do not identify this source orbit with the two internal critical framing coordinates of the knot network. The exact loss of information after a normalized cut is computed below, rather than suppressed. The later [unprojectivized high-color source theorem](actual_unprojectivized_frobenius_borel_torsor.md) realizes a marked Borel torsor using ACTUAL Sym^N divided source vectors and their contragredient co-source. Retaining scale U and one actual descendant m gives Omega_cut=(A/N)dlog U wedge dm; an actual old-clock normal row detects that scale. This retains the prequantum character erased by a normalized projector. It does not infer the full network-current comparison from the standard group/density formulas already proved here. ## 1. The actual standard module and its cut covector At complete color fix N>=2, Q=q_N^2, and the original balanced space V_N. Let W=E_(N-1,0), U=sum_(j=0)^(N-2) E_(j,j+1), Ubar=U/(N-1). The [complete divided-Ward theorem](complete_color_divided_ward_and_fusion.md) proves for the true divided Hopf adjoints J_E,J_F that J_E(W)=-N U, J_E(U)=0, J_F(U)=N W, J_F(W)=0. Consequently on L=span(Ubar,W), the operators e_sl=-J_E/[N(N-1)], f_sl=(N-1)J_F/N, h_sl=[e_sl,f_sl] are exactly the standard two-dimensional SL2 Lie matrices in the ordered basis (Ubar,W). This action exponentiates algebraically on L. It is an action on the **linear source space**: the divided Hopf coproduct has mixed terms, so no action by automorphisms of the full matrix multiplication algebra is inferred. For the actual cut Phi(C)=Tr(e C), e_ij=1/N, one has Phi(Ubar)=Phi(W)=1/N. Thus the restricted cut covector is phi=(1,1)/N. Let G_phi be the SL2 Borel preserving its projective line. For v=a Ubar+b W, z=a+b!=0, there is a unique g in G_phi with gW=v. In these source coordinates it is g_v=[[a+1/z,a],[b-1/z,b]], det(g_v)=1, phi g_v=z phi. (1) This proves directly that the open source orbit z!=0 is a genuine G_phi torsor with anchor W, not merely a dimension count. ## 2. An equivariant sign cover of the geometric B1 framing torsor Let j(g)=z(g)g^(-T), where phi g=z(g)phi. It has row sums one and determinant z(g)^2. Since z is a character, j is a group homomorphism. Its kernel is {I,-I}; it is the usual sign cover of the row-stochastic PGL2 cut Borel, with the sign retained. Take F_0=[[0,1],[1,-1]] and define F(v)=F_0 j(g_v)^(-1) =[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], r=a/z, s=z^(-2). (2) Every regular framing matrix of this form has two lifts, related by v->-v. Source left translation g_0 sends F(v) -> F(v) j(g_0)^(-1). Thus (2) has exactly the established right-frame action convention; replacing j(g)^(-1) by j(g) would reverse it. Pull back the canonical complete framing two-form and cut coordinate: Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)], A_cut=1/(1+s). On the open set 1+z^2!=0 their exact source expressions are Omega_src=2 da wedge db/(1+z^2), A_src=z^2/(1+z^2). (3) Indeed dr wedge ds=-2 z^(-4) da wedge db, and s(1+s)=(1+z^2)z^(-4). No determinant or sign is omitted. For the two geometric cut stabilizers xi_1=h+2f, xi_2=e+f, the corresponding source matrices are -xi_i^T. Their vector fields are X_1=(-a-2b)partial_a+b partial_b, X_2=-b partial_a-a partial_b. Both satisfy X_i(z)=-z and div_(Omega_src) X_i=2 A_src. (4) Their images under (2) are exactly the two compensated geometric fields in [the residual Ward proof](residual_gaussian_ward_currents.md). Equation (4) is the same leading covariance as the actual cut co-source b_i/H=-2 A_cut. This is an explicit source-level density comparison with its fixed group convention. The divided action on L and the ordinary finite Ward action on the network are distinct actions. Equation (4) does not by itself intertwine them or identify their internal source coordinates. ## 3. The relative centralizer coordinate and its transgression The geometric additive centralizer coordinate is tau=r/s=a z. The source vector field V=z^(-1)(partial_a-partial_b) has V(tau)=1 and V(A_src)=0. Direct contraction gives iota_V Omega_src=dlog A_src, Omega_src=dtau wedge dlog A_src. (5) Therefore the marked interval tau=0,...,1 transgresses the source form to exactly the canonical logarithmic cut form. Translating both endpoints by a regular function tau_0(A_src) changes neither this two-form nor that relative class. Poles of such a section require their marked boundary lattice; (5) does not delete them. This gives a concrete classical source orbit for the same relative framing complex. To make it the **network's** source comparison, the actual boundary currents must still be sent to its endpoint and logarithmic-carry co-sources. The [full-certificate calculation](full_certificate_framing_boundary.md) states those unresolved currents explicitly. ## 4. The orbit matrix is an actual cyclic quantum-torus generator Put c=a/(N-1). In the original finite matrix algebra, v=c U+b W, K v=Q v K, v^N=b c^(N-1) I. (6) The last identity follows by following one complete cyclic string. For a b!=0, v and the clock K give the split cyclic torus, not only an abstract two-dimensional representation. There is an explicit regular diagonal comparison with the actual E-cyclic source from [the coherent crossing proof](balanced_verma_coherent_braiding.md). At M=1 write epsilon_j=Q^(-j)-1, P_j=product_(l=1)^j epsilon_l, P_0=1. Every P_j, j<N, is nonzero and P_(N-1)=(-1)^(N-1)N. Set mu=b c^(N-1)/P_(N-1), D_jj=P_j/c^j. Then D commutes with K and direct arrow comparison gives D(Ecal_head+mu W)D^(-1)=v. (7) The transformed F is fixed by the original Casimir: Ftilde=(-2-qK-q^(-1)K^(-1))v^(-1), Ftilde^N=0. (8) Thus the orbit has a rational matrix gauge into a genuine actual source family. This does not assert that its G_phi action preserves matrix multiplication or the knot's entire intertwiner network. The source coordinate A_src in (3) is still a parameter function; it has not been identified with the physical clock x/K by (6). ## 5. The original cut has an exact marked cyclic anchor For z!=0 define the normalized matrix coupon e_v=(N/z) v e. It has rank one, trace one and e_v^2=e_v, since e v e=(z/N)e. Its entries are explicit: (e_v)_ij=r/(N-1), i<N-1, (e_v)_(N-1,j)=1-r, r=a/z. (9) The **whole coupon**, not only its diagonal restriction, loses the scale z. Its row Phi_v(C)=Tr(e_v C) is cohomologous to the original normalized cut on the actual split Ward complex, by (Phi_v-Phi)h delta=Phi_v-Phi. On closed scalar cut operators it therefore returns exactly the original invariant. At r_*=(N-1)/N, equation (9) is literally e_v=e on all matrices. Retaining the shift and its eigenvalue mark fixes the scale as well: the actual point v_*=(N-1)Ubar+W=U+W=S, S^N=I, S e=e, e=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1)S^j (10) is the original cyclic shift and selected eigenprojector. It has a_*=N-1,b_*=1,z_*=N. Its image in (2)--(3) is the exact source orbit section r_*=1-1/N, s_*=1/N^2, A_*=N^2/(N^2+1), tau_*=N(N-1). (11) The companion gauge (7) has c=1 and mu=1/[(-1)^(N-1)N] there. Thus the original cut has an intrinsic cyclic-source anchor; it is not fixed by normalized coupon data alone. Equation (11) approaches a framing boundary as N grows. It is a section of the constructed source orbit, not yet a proof that the network's geometric period is evaluated at that same section. There is a second exact restriction. For any diagonal cut array, Phi_v(C)=r sum_(j<N-1)C_jj/(N-1)+(1-r)C_(N-1,N-1). (12) Every actual uninserted one-cut array is diagonal before its final internal sums. Hence (12) probes only one strand-index weight; the two orbit parameters do not themselves create two internal flow coordinates. The divided-adjoint cut is likewise precisely the endpoint functional on these arrays, as proved in the full-certificate note. A pre-collapse source-current map remains necessary. ## 6. The logarithmic normal comparison has a separate scale The [strict Fock-to-normal comparison](fock_cyclic_normal_mellin_map.md) retains resonant U^k sectors and the relative endpoint U, on the marked logarithmic torsor. The bare geometric pullback here is u=Log U=N Log A_src, Omega_cut=(1/N)dtau_geo wedge du. It does not identify the Fock coherent parameter with tau_geo. At the physical H_N=2pi*i/N, a putative canonical phase tau_geo Log A/H_N is tau_geo u/(2pi*i), whereas the exact source kernel is exp(s_Fock u). Matching them would rescale the endpoint and change U to U^(1/(2pi*i)); that adapter has not been established. title: Independent audit of the divided-source framing orbit
text: # Independent audit of the divided-source framing orbit Audit, 27 October 2026, of [the explicit framing-orbit note](divided_source_framing_orbit.md). The group/sign-cover, density, cyclic-source gauge and marked-anchor claims are correct in their stated domains. None identifies this orbit with the internal framing of the knot network. The actual divided Ward block is standard SL2 in the ordered basis Ubar,W: the rescalings give eW=Ubar, fUbar=W, and both opposite actions zero. The cut covector is (1,1)/N. For z=a+b!=0, g_v=[a+1/z a;b-1/z b] has determinant one, carries W to v, and multiplies that covector by z. These equations determine its first column uniquely, proving free transitivity rather than only matching dimensions. The contragredient is essential. Since (1,1)g=z(1,1), the matrix j(g)=z g^(-T) has row sums one. It is a homomorphism with kernel {+I,-I}. Conversely a row-stochastic invertible matrix has two preimages after choosing the square root of its determinant. Thus this is exactly the retained SL2 sign cover. The inverse right-frame action gives F_0 j(g_v)^(-1)=[a/z b/z;z^(-2) -z^(-2)]. The opposite choice F_0j(g_v) would not have the asserted action convention. With r=a/z and s=z^(-2), direct differentiation gives -dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)]=2 da wedge db/(1+z^2). The source matrices -xi_i^T give the two vector fields in the note. Their ordinary coordinate divergence is zero, while X_i(z)=-z, so their divergence in this density is 2z^2/(1+z^2)=2A_src. This matches the actual leading co-source sign. Also tau=a z and V=z^(-1)(partial_a-partial_b) obey Vtau=1, VA_src=0, and contraction with the density gives dlog A_src. The stated relative transgression is therefore exact. For the matrix comparison, D_j=P_j/c^j sends each upper edge epsilon_(j+1) to c. Its wrap sends mu to mu P_(N-1)/c^(N-1)=b. Hence D E_mu D^(-1)=v. The clock commutes with D, so the original Casimir identity fixes Ftilde in the stated order (-2-qK-q^(-1)K^(-1))v^(-1). Its N-th power is zero because it is conjugate to the actual truncated F. This gauge requires a,b!=0, as explicitly stated; the whole source orbit only requires z!=0 and is larger than that companion chart. The normalized coupon is literally e_v=(N/z)v e, whose first N-1 rows are r/(N-1) and last row is 1-r. Thus its entire response on arbitrary matrices depends only on r. For the split Ward contraction h delta=I-i p, p=Tr/N, the difference between its row and the original row vanishes on I. Therefore (Phi_v-Phi)h delta=Phi_v-Phi; the stated cochain homotopy is valid. This proves neither equality on arbitrary matrix insertions nor an internal two-coordinate source map. At r=(N-1)/N one has v=(z/N)S, S=U+W. The exact permutation identities are S^N=I, Se=e and e=(1/N)sum_j S^j. The first condition on v alone permits z/N in mu_N. Its marked eigenvalue one on e forces z/N=1. Thus the extra clock/eigenvalue mark really restores z=N; normalized coupon data alone cannot do so. Substitution gives precisely r=1-1/N, s=1/N^2, A=N^2/(N^2+1), tau=N(N-1), and mu=1/[(-1)^(N-1)N]. Independent exact checks verified the sign-cover matrix, form and vertical current symbolically, and S^N, Se and the full projector identity at eleven integer levels N=2,...,12. The proof arguments above establish the general statements. title: Independent proof audit of the divided Ward / marked-edge bridge
text: # Independent proof audit of the divided Ward / marked-edge bridge Audit, 27 October 2026. I checked the current proofs in [the marked divided-adjoint note](divided_adjoint_marked_edge_pairing.md), [factorial fusion](divided_ward_factorial_fusion.md), [the general complete-color construction](complete_color_divided_ward_and_fusion.md), and section 5.1 of [the unfolded Ward theorem](unfolded_ward_factorial_and_regulator.md). No defect was found in the stated operator, source, pivot, or moving-representation identities. This is a proof audit; I did not rerun the authors' matrix checks. ## 1. The divided adjoint and its exact marked pairing For \(\mathcal E=\rho^2E\), the genuine generic Hopf adjoint is \[ A(T)=[\mathcal E,T]K^{-1}=X(T)+Y(T),\qquad X=L_{\mathcal E}R_{K^{-1}},\quad Y=-R_{\mathcal E K^{-1}}. \] The relation \(K\mathcal E=Q\mathcal E K\) gives \(XY=QYX\). On the individual integral Weyl color, \(X^N=Y^N=0\) identically before specialization. The mixed \(Q\)-binomial coefficients have the single canceled factor \(1-Q^N\), giving the stated regular divided Hopf adjoint. Ordinary commutation by a one-factor divided matrix would lose these mixed terms. For \(W=E_{N-1,0}\), the term \(Y^lX^j\), \(j+l=N\), has only the entry \((l-1,l)\). Its phase is \[ (-1)^lQ^{-l(l-1)/2-jl} P_{N-1}\epsilon_lK^{-N}. \] Using \[ c_l=\frac{(-1)^{l-1}Q^{-l(l-1)/2}}{1-Q^l},\quad \epsilon_l=(1-Q^l)Q^{-l},\quad P_{N-1}K^{-N}=N, \] the sign is \(-1\) and the exponent is \(-lN\). Thus every superedge coefficient is exactly \(-N\), including even and composite \(N\): \[ J_{\rm ad}(W)=-N\sum_{l=1}^{N-1}E_{l-1,l}. \] For the literal marked row \(\Phi(T)=\operatorname{Tr}(eT)\), \(e_{ab}=1/N\), this gives \(\Phi(J_{\rm ad}W)=-(N-1)\). Consequently \[ \Phi_{\rm div}(T)=-\frac{\Phi(J_{\rm ad}(TW))}{N-1} \] has \(\Phi_{\rm div}(I)=1\). Its equality with the original row on scalar cut operators is exact. The all-matrices homotopy \[ \Phi_{\rm div}-\Phi =(\Phi_{\rm div}-\Phi)h_W\delta_W \] follows directly from \(h_W\delta_W=I-ip\) and the fact that the row difference kills \(I\). It neither assumes nor supplies a geometric representative for that scalar cohomology class. ## 2. Partial trace: the generic pivot and the insertion order For the genuine generic integral color, the compatible pivot is \(K\). The all-matrices pivotal partial trace intertwines the Hopf adjoint. This can be checked on generators: the closed \(E\)-terms cancel because \(K^{-1}K=I\), and the closed \(F\)-terms cancel by the same cyclic trace identity. Thus it intertwines every power, and hence the quotient by \(1-Q^N\) before specialization. The total tensor-and-dual divided adjoint is regular: its multinomial expansion has individual nilpotent powers and the same canceled root factors. Therefore the divided partial-trace identity specializes legitimately. Only after this specialization does one use \[ g=K^{1-N}=(K^N)^{-1}K \] with \(K^N\) scalar. This proves the identity for the actual root pivot \(g\). It does not replace the generic \(g\)-pivot by \(K\) while taking a derivative. The nonconstant derivative of \(K^{-N}\) is correctly retained in the separate normal adapter calculation. For an arbitrary full matrix \(T\), \[ \operatorname{ptr}_g(T(W\otimes I)) =(\operatorname{ptr}_gT)W. \] Combining this with divided-adjoint naturality gives exactly the stated ordered formula for \(\Phi_{\rm div}\operatorname{ptr}_g\). It does not give a formula with the edge moved outside \(J_{\rm ad,total}\). The note retains the correct order. ## 3. Fusion and the even-level character The generic ordered factorial product equals the finite quantum exponential of the total raising matrix. At degree \(kN+s\), cancellation gives \[ \left[ \frac{(Q;Q)_{kN+s}}{(1-Q^N)^k} \right]_{\rm root} =N^k k!(Q;Q)_s. \] Thus the full root defect is \(\exp((-t)^NJ_b/N)\), not merely its first term. All powers terminate by total-position degree. The inherited block term is \(J_X\otimes\chi_Y\), where \[ \chi_Y=K_Y^N=(-1)^{(N-1)\operatorname{length}(Y)}. \] Expanding the two sides of the additive three-block identity cancels every inherited \(J\) term. Within each side the remaining operators commute because the inner mixed term commutes with its block's total raising operator and \(K\). Exponentiation therefore proves the displayed twisted associativity. The factor \(\chi\) is essential at even \(N\); the signs in the notes are correct. The extension to both divided \(E\) and \(F\) directions is explicitly not asserted unipotent. The invariant two-dimensional block with opposite nilpotents generates an \(\mathrm{SL}_2\) action, consistently with that qualification. ## 4. The moving representation retains exactly one resonant log term In the integral lift, \(C(Q)\) is nilpotent generically and \[ C(Q)^N=(1-Q^N)J_b(Q) \] with \(J_b(Q)\) regular. Thus evaluating the unfolded logarithm at \(-tC(Q)\) is a finite rational matrix calculation. For \(m\ge N\) not divisible by \(N\), its denominator \(1-Q^m\) is a unit at the root, while \(C(Q)^m\) has at least one \(1-Q^N\) factor. For \(m=kN\), \(k\ge2\), its numerator has \(k\) such factors and its denominator only one. These terms vanish at the root. The only extra surviving logarithm term is \[ \frac{(-t)^N J_b}{N}. \] Since \(J_b\) commutes with the root total raising operator, exponentiation gives the exact finite ghost times the literal nilpotent factorial. Higher ghost powers arise from this exponential, even though higher dilogarithm powers vanish before exponentiation. With \(Q=Q_Ne^h\), \(C(Q)^N=-NhJ_b+O(h^2)\). Substitution into the coefficientwise pole \(-\operatorname{Li}_2((-tC(Q))^N)/(N^2h)\) gives the same surviving term, with its sign. Setting \(C^N=0\) first would incorrectly discard it. ## 5. The two normals and the remaining global issue The absent generic edge \[ w(Q,M)=MQ^{-N}-M^{-1} \] vanishes on the integral Weyl curve \(M=-q^N\), but restricts to \(\kappa\) on the root wall. The exact auxiliary defect \[ [\mathcal E,F]-\rho(K-K^{-1}) =-(1-Q^N)w(Q,M)E_{N-1,N-1} \] is correct by direct adjacent-entry subtraction. The routewise pivot/twist adapter is likewise the product of the \(b-1\) closed factors \(K^{-N}\) and the writhe correction. Its root value is one by knot parity; its derivative retains the closed-position moment. The notes distinguish these normals. The marked divided row is a concrete new realization of the original cut class and is transported through exact finite partial trace. It does not yet map the partial geometric Gaussian block into that class. Ordinary full closure still kills an uncompensated positive divided ghost by position degree, and the nonzero marked-edge tests are cochain tests. No passage to a selected global geometric coefficient follows from these identities alone; the notes' scope statements correctly preserve that distinction.

title: The divided Ward power is an exact unipotent factorial fusion defect
text: # The divided Ward power is an exact unipotent factorial fusion defect Research proof, 27 October 2026. Work in the genuine generic quantum group Weyl color `D_(N-1)(q)`, whose complete root specialization is the original Kashaev color. A mixed first-normal divided power on two factors is nonzero although the individual divided powers vanish. It is exactly the multiplicativity defect of the literal finite Ward factorial. The defects have a coherent associative fusion law, with the even-level Frobenius signs retained. These are operator and normal-source statements. They do not prove that the ghost survives the selected scalar knot contraction. ## 1. The integral Weyl lift and its divided power Put `Q=q^2`, `rho=q-q^(-1)`. On `D_(N-1)(q)` use F v_a=v_(a+1), E v_a=[a]_q [N-a]_q v_(a-1), K v_a=q^(N-1-2a) v_a, 0<=a<N, with endpoint vectors zero. These are genuine finite quantum-group matrices for generic `q`. In the meridian convention `x=-M/q`, their color is `x=q^(N-1)`, hence `M=-q^N`. At `q_N=exp(pi*i/N)` this is the complete color `M=1`, including even and composite `N`. Use `Ecal=rho^2 E`; its coproduct is Delta Ecal=Ecal tensor K+1 tensor Ecal. In the balanced basis `w_a=v_a/(Q;Q)_a`, the raising coefficient is Ecal w_a=(q^(-N)-q^(N-2a))w_(a-1). At the root this becomes `(Q^(-a)-1)w_(a-1)`, the actual complete matrix. These basis changes are units at the root for `a<N`. On two factors put A=Ecal tensor K, B=1 tensor Ecal, C=A+B. They satisfy `AB=Q BA`, and `A^N=B^N=0` for every generic `q`. The normal-ordered q-binomial expansion is C^N=sum_(j=1)^(N-1) {N choose j}_Q B^(N-j) A^j. Every coefficient has a simple factor `1-Q^N`; its quotient is regular at every primitive `N`-th root. Thus the literal first-normal operator J=[C^N/(1-Q^N)]_(q=q_N) is well defined and equals J=sum_(j=1)^(N-1) N B^(N-j) A^j/[(Q;Q)_j (Q;Q)_(N-j)]. (1) Here `(Q;Q)_(N-1)=N`. This is the scaled divided quantum-group power, not an arbitrary operator added to the root color. It records the specified generic integral lift. Its individual one-factor counterpart is zero because `Ecal^N=0` identically there. One has `[J,C]=0`, and `J^2=0`: both follow from the generic identity, or from total-index lowering by `N` in a two-factor space whose maximum total index is `2N-2`. Every generic braid intertwines `C`, so division by the scalar and specialization show that it also intertwines `J`. ## 2. A uniform explicit nonzero entry The vector `w_(N-1) tensor w_1` has only one surviving term in (1), namely `j=N-1`. Its coefficient is `1/(1-Q)`. At the root, Ecal^(N-1)w_(N-1)=(-1)^(N-1)N w_0, Ecal w_1=(1-Q)Q^(-1)w_0, K^(N-1)w_1=q_N^((N-1)(N-3))w_1. The phase therefore simplifies, using `q_N^N=-1`, to J(w_(N-1) tensor w_1)=-N q_N w_0 tensor w_0. (2) This proves nonvanishing at every `N>=2` with the original balanced root normalization. No odd-level restriction is used. ## 3. Exact factorial fusion, including all degrees Define the positive-argument finite factorial p_N(X)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) X^j/(Q;Q)_j. At generic `q`, q-binomial expansion gives the finite identity p_N(B)p_N(A)=sum_(n=0)^(2N-2) C^n/(Q;Q)_n. (3) Indeed the coefficient of `B^i A^j` on both sides is `1/[(Q;Q)_i(Q;Q)_j]`; terms with either index at least `N` vanish. For `n=N+s`, cancel `1-Q^N` in (3) before taking the root. Since [(Q;Q)_(N+s)/(1-Q^N)]_root=N (Q;Q)_s, the resulting summand is `J C^s/[N(Q;Q)_s]`. Terms with `s>=N-1` vanish by total degree. Therefore the exact root identity is p_N(B)p_N(A)=(I+J/N)p_N(C). (4) The literal Ward polynomial has argument `-t Ecal`, not positive `Ecal`. Thus its corresponding form is p_N(-tB)p_N(-tA) =(I+(-t)^N J/N)p_N(-tC). (5) The sign `(-t)^N` must not be suppressed. The first missing degree is `N`, but (4)--(5) identify the **entire** finite product defect. Since `J^2=0`, its logarithm is exactly `(-t)^N J/N`. This is also the resonant logarithm of the unfolded factorial. The degree-`N` term of `log p_infinity(X)=sum_m X^m/[m(1-Q^m)]` is `X^N/[N(1-Q^N)]`. Along the specified tensor lift its regular value is `J/N`. The normal extension, rather than the bare root identity `C^N=0`, retains this term. ## 4. Coherent fusion on arbitrary ordered blocks For an ordered block `X` of Steinberg factors let `C_X` be its total `Ecal`, `K_X` its total `K`, and J_X=[C_X^N/(1-Q^N)]_root, chi_X=K_X^N=(-1)^((N-1) length(X)) I. Regularity of `J_X` follows from the ordered q-multinomial expansion: all nonzero exponent tuples have entries below `N`, while the numerator has the factor `1-Q^N`. The operator lowers total degree by `N`, and satisfies `[J_X,C_X]=[J_X,K_X]=0` at the root. For any `k,s` with `0<=s<N`, direct factor grouping gives [(Q;Q)_(kN+s)/(1-Q^N)^k]_root =N^k k! (Q;Q)_s. Consequently the root of the generic finite quantum exponential is E_X(t)=exp[(-t)^N J_X/N] p_N(-t C_X). (6) The exponential is finite: its `k`-th term lowers total degree by `kN`, so it terminates before `k=length(X)`. Formula (6) is also the ordered product of the individual factorials, with each individual raising generator dressed by all later `K` factors. For two consecutive blocks define the mixed divided power j_(X,Y)=J_(X tensor Y)-J_X tensor chi_Y-1 tensor J_Y. The coproduct q-binomial expansion gives explicitly j_(X,Y)=sum_(a=1)^(N-1) N (1 tensor C_Y)^(N-a)(C_X tensor K_Y)^a /[(Q;Q)_a(Q;Q)_(N-a)]. (7) The inherited terms `J_X tensor chi_Y` and `1 tensor J_Y` commute with both arguments in (7). Canceling them in the generic q-exponential product proves the block fusion identity p_N(-t(1 tensor C_Y)) p_N(-t(C_X tensor K_Y)) =Theta_(X,Y)(t) p_N(-t C_(X tensor Y)), Theta_(X,Y)(t)=exp[(-t)^N j_(X,Y)/N]. (8) These transitions are unipotent. In a block of length `b`, all their nonconstant terms lower total degree by at least `N`; the ideal of such endomorphisms has `b`-th power zero. This nilpotence bound is independent of the level `N`. ### Associativity, with the Frobenius character retained For three consecutive blocks, direct cancellation of the inherited `J_X,J_Y,J_Z` terms gives the exact additive identity j_(X,Y) tensor chi_Z+j_(X tensor Y,Z) =1 tensor j_(Y,Z)+j_(X,Y tensor Z). (9) Within the left pair the two operators commute: `j_(X,Y)` commutes with `C_(X tensor Y)` and `K_(X tensor Y)`, and the next mixed operator is a polynomial in that block's total raising operator and the last block's raising operator. The corresponding right pair commutes for the same reason. Exponentiating (9) therefore gives [Theta_(X,Y) embedded with degree-N factor chi_Z] Theta_(X tensor Y,Z) =Theta_(Y,Z) Theta_(X,Y tensor Z). (10) This is the coherent twisted fusion-cocycle identity. At odd `N` the displayed character is one; at even `N` it can invert the embedded unipotent transition. It is part of the tensor convention. Repeated application proves independence of parenthesization. Thus the actual divided-power normal extension has literal coherent unipotent fusion transitions on this ordered tensor category. No braided source torsor, chosen cohomology class, or selected-period survival is inferred solely from the associative identity. This nilpotence statement concerns the positive raising-factorial transitions. Adjoining lowering divided powers is a different operation and need not preserve a nilpotent group. ## 5. The Hopf-adjoint and cohomological qualifications The new normal generator avoids the finite-order-flow obstruction: it is not the logarithm of the finite-order `ad_K`. It acts nontrivially on tensor and dual multiplicity data even though its one-color action vanishes. Its first-normal coproduct is not primitive; the mixed term (7) is indispensable. A factorwise primitive flow with zero action on each individual color would miss the entire operator (2). For matrix Ward complexes one must use its **divided Hopf adjoint**, not just the ordinary commutator with `J_X`. The coproduct has the inherited `J` terms and the mixed lower-power terms in (7). The antipode is the regular specialization of the generic antipode; in this normalization it gives `S(J)=-J K^(-N)`. Hence on an endomorphism `T` its action has the form ad_J(T)=J T K^(-N)-T J K^(-N) +sum_(a=1)^(N-1) c_a Ecal^a T S(Ecal^(N-a)K^a), c_a=N/[(Q;Q)_a(Q;Q)_(N-a)]. (11) The mixed terms need not vanish on arbitrary matrices, even when `J` vanishes on the underlying single-color module. Commutation of `J` with a braid alone does not replace this all-matrices action. A compatible pivotal trace can be obtained from the genuine generic Hopf trace before dividing and specializing, retaining the actual root pivotal and peripheral scalar adapters. The separate original marked defect is still not an ordinary intertwining coupon. Moreover the mixed insertion is negligible under the ordinary full cut trace for a grading reason. Any braid operator has total-degree zero, while `J_X` lowers total degree by `N`. Closing all but one color forces the remaining color to lower by `N`, impossible in the range `0,...,N-1`. Thus the ordinary cut operator with this insertion is zero. A nonzero relative class would have to retain compensating wrap and marked-cut currents before taking this quotient. Their existence and nonzero pairing have not been proved by (4) or (10). Finally, nilpotence by itself does not identify a class in the geometric Gaussian pushforward. It makes a specified perturbation finite only after that perturbation is an actual filtered chain map on a common source complex. The map, differential, endpoint/carry terms, and the nonzero leading scalar projection are still required. The exact fusion cocycle supplies new coherent normal-source data; it does not by itself supply these HPL hypotheses or a selected volume asymptotic. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_divided_ward_factorial_fusion.py) and [results](../experiments/divided_ward_factorial_fusion_results.json) compare (1) with an independent generic-q normal derivative, check the full signed factorial identities, and verify triple fusion associativity with both Frobenius characters.

# Independent audit: doubled Rivin phases and critical source traces 27 October 2026. The current proofs in [the doubled-phase optimizer](doubled_phase_rivin_optimizer.md) and [the irreducible critical-source theorem](irreducible_critical_source_and_whole_norm.md) pass independently, with the corrected requirement that a density on a reducible etale algebra be a unit on every selected component. ## 1. The phase map and the optimizer The fixed-meridian shape Jacobian is invertible by the stated positive Lagrangian pairing. Its peripheral slopes satisfy \(	au_-=\overline{	au_+}\), \(\operatorname{Im}	au_+>0\). Thus the doubled logarithmic phase Jacobian \[  egin{pmatrix}1&-1\	au_+&-	au_-\end{pmatrix} \] has nonzero determinant \(	au_+-	au_-\). The selected normalized shape germ is genuinely etale over the two phase ratios. The conclusion is local at the chosen place and is not an assertion about the raw singular plane A-polynomial fiber. On unit phases, the conjugation involution and local uniqueness force \(w= ar z\). Positivity persists. Stationarity on the affine fixed-two-phase angle slice supplies the real edge equations; the imaginary edge equations were already imposed. Strict concavity then makes this point the unique global maximizer of that entire affine angle fiber and its closure. This does not assert such a positive optimizer at arbitrary remote phase values. Writing \(u=x+ia,v=y+ib\), the derivative is \(d\Phi=x\,db-y\,da\). Solving the phase Jacobian gives \[ \operatorname{Hess}\Phi = rac1{\operatorname{Im}	au_+}  egin{pmatrix}|	au_+|^2&-\operatorname{Re}	au_+\ -\operatorname{Re}	au_+&1\end{pmatrix}. \] It is positive definite with determinant one. The stated complex algebraic formula is exactly the same calculation before the real restriction. The rational cotangent formulas also prove the claimed algebraicity of the constrained covariance. Neither covariance is thereby the actual quantum Gaussian density. The centered complete meridian and longitude signs are explicitly retained as external characters. They must accompany any later SL2 or quantum comparison. The added global real corollary also passes. Within ONE fixed affine edge-angle and logarithmic marking, equal unwrapped boundary phases place two positive edge solutions in the same strictly concave affine fiber. They coincide; the sine rule then identifies their shapes. The phase map is a local diffeomorphism at every positive point, so this global injection is a diffeomorphism onto its open image, of absolute degree one. Fixed edge winding numbers and unwrapped phases are essential. This proves neither image convexity or surjectivity nor any degree statement for the periodic phase torus or quantum cycle. ## 2. The marked regulator primitive and the H5 connection Direct differentiation yields \[ d\left[ rac{R_--R_+}{i} + rac{\widetilde u v-u\widetilde v}{4i}ight] = rac{(u+\widetilde u)d(v-\widetilde v) -(v+\widetilde v)d(u-\widetilde u)}{4i}. \] Thus the bilinear correction and all signs are correct. Conjugate fundamental-class marks and zero centered logs at completeness give \(\Phi=-2\operatorname{Vol}\) without fitting an additional integration constant. For the displayed five-dimensional Heisenberg matrix, the central entry of \(\Pi^{-1}d\Pi\) is \[ dZ-A_{\log}\,dQ_{\log}+B_{\log}\,dP_{\log}, \] which vanishes exactly by the primitive equation. Its curvature reduces to \(2(du\wedge dv-d\widetilde u\wedge d\widetilde v)=0\). Every product of three connection matrices is zero, so marked transport is exactly identity plus the single and double ordered integrals. The central initial value \(-8i\operatorname{Vol}\) is essential; setting the four logarithms initially to zero does not determine it. This is a whole algebraic flat period connection, with generally transcendental horizontal matrix. Exponentiating its additive center is an analytic period evaluation, not an algebraic character of the additive group. ## 3. Irreducible trace descent and finite moments The trace pairing proof is exact: its Gram matrix is \(V^tV\) for the Vandermonde embedding matrix. Hence the density \(a=\eta(\psi)\) is uniquely reconstructed from the stated \(d\) moments by \(G^{-1}m\). In a rank-one line over a FIELD, nonzero source and nonzero co-source imply \(a
e0\). Every embedding coefficient is then \(\sigma_i(a)
e0\). The normalization \(\lambda(\psi)=1\) is a convenient sufficient certificate, not a necessary one. For higher-rank lines the normalization still certifies \(a
e0\), but mere individual nonvanishing does not, as stated. For a reducible etale algebra a faithful normalized matrix trace sees every primitive idempotent with weight rank/dimension. The density multiplying that faithful trace must be a UNIT on every selected etale component. Mere nonzero density is insufficient: \((1,0)\) in \(F	imes F\) would kill the second component. The current note now includes this correction. Neither critical-field irreducibility nor normalized trace descent has been proved for an actual global geometric quotient of the quantum state. The explicit component, splitting-field and already-closed-scalar qualifications are necessary. ## 4. The whole arc and height estimates Distinct exponentials with polynomial coefficients are linearly independent: the stated differential operators isolate one exponential with an invertible operator on its polynomial factor. Their order-\(m\) constant-coefficient equation bounds the zero order at the origin by \(m-1\). Hence every fixed nonzero rational coefficient on the physical source slice has finite vanishing order. Applied to a polynomial relation with nonzero constant and leading terms, Cauchy bounds and their reciprocals give polynomial upper and lower bounds for ALL specialized conjugates. This argument does not need bounded absolute cyclotomic degree. The degree-independent naive-height inequality \((1+H)^{-1}\le|\alpha|\le1+H\) is correct after removing zero constant powers and reversing the polynomial for the lower bound. The bounded-Weil-height counterexample is also correct: the displayed monic polynomial is Eisenstein at two, and all roots of modulus at least one lie in the disk centered at \(2^N\) with radius two. The fixed-point map there is a strict contraction for every \(N\ge2\), so only its one real root lies outside the unit disk. Its Weil height stays bounded while its chosen archimedean value grows exponentially. The resulting finite-sum rate theorem correctly requires a strict TOTAL dominance gap or a smaller-rate bound on any total remainder. Rivin concavity alone supplies neither global period descent nor that gap over all complex sectors. These are substantive sufficient theorems for a proposed whole source comparison. They do not prove its existence or the selected volume limit. ## 5. Precise scope of the optimizer algebraicity The current proofs already establish the claimed classical algebraicity under their stated positive gluing/rank inputs: [geometric rigidity](geometric_rigidity_and_cyclic_source.md) Section1, [doubled phase optimization](doubled_phase_rivin_optimizer.md) Sections3--5, and [whole comparison rigidity](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) Section1. No algebraicity correction is needed in those statements. It is not a new conclusion obtained from quantum jets. Here is an independent short proof. Let F be the peripheral coefficient field and K=F(z_1,...,z_t) the selected shape field. Differentiate the normalized polynomial gluing equations over F. The invertible shape Jacobian gives J(dz_j)=0, hence every dz_j=0 in Omega_(K/F). If K/F had positive transcendence degree, choose a transcendence basis and its coordinate derivations. In characteristic zero each extends uniquely over the remaining finite separable field extension, producing a nonzero derivation of K. But all dz_j=0 makes every such derivation zero, a contradiction. Thus K/F is finite algebraic. The complete normalized isolated point has F=Q with its recorded algebraic lift characters, and therefore has algebraic shape coordinates. For the ordinary one-cusped geometric branch the correct field is the function field of its marked peripheral CURVE, Frac(Q[M^+/-1,L^+/-1]/(A_geo)), after choosing the component and normalized place. M and L are dependent. The result is already finite algebraic over the meridian field Q(M) locally. It is not a claim that arbitrary independent complex M,L give a geometric shape solution, or that all shape coordinates are integral over the unlocalized full polynomial ring Q[M,L]. At the complete parabolic lift, M=+1 or -1 and the selected longitude character is retained. This gives algebraic numbers for the UNFRAMED ideal shapes. The raw actual braid critical scheme still has its two framing directions: its other shape/ position coordinates become algebraic numbers only after those framing marks are fixed algebraically as well. Fixing a meridian alone does not isolate that entire framed critical scheme. Strict concavity identifies the unique positive real stationary point on the stated affine angle fiber. Complex transversality and polynomial gluing, rather than uniqueness alone, supply the algebraicity. With two independent boundary PHASES the doubled curve is the appropriate algebraic cover; those phase variables are not two independent full peripheral holonomies. Algebraic shapes do not imply algebraic logarithms or regulator values. The regulator is a transcendental FUNCTION/period of its algebraic connection; this wording makes no theorem that the particular hyperbolic-volume NUMBER is transcendental. For definition/coverage only, see [Zagier, The Dilogarithm Function, Sections I.3--4](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/zagier/files/doi/10.1007/978-3-540-30308-4_1/fulltext.pdf). No proof from that source is imported here. The actual selected wall coefficient2^-N supplies a concrete reminder that even nonzero algebraic source values can have exponential size: all weight-N characters must be retained before applying a bounded whole-algebraic coefficient argument. ## 6. The whole selected-line polar criterion The [whole selected-line theorem](whole_selected_line_polar_character.md) also passes independently. On the EXACT marked ray s_N=kappa N^(-1/e), kappa^e=pi i, a meromorphic rank-one connection integrates to C s^rho exp(B(s)+H(s)), with finite B=sum b_r s^-r and convergent H holomorphic. Its normalized log modulus is exactly the displayed finite sum of distinct powers N^(r/e-1), plus O(logN/N). The r=e contribution is 2Im(b_e); terms r>e can contribute zero only when each real coefficient vanishes on that ray. A fixed meromorphic frame changes dlog only by a logarithmic pole and preserves B. The logarithmic quotient by exp(S_geo/h) gives the stated volume rate and O(logN/N) error. This is a genuinely useful sufficient GLOBAL target, not an assumption that a local Gaussian block is the actual selected invariant. For a perturbed physical ray the polar primitive must first be pulled back to that exact ray; imaginary leading high poles can otherwise produce real lower terms. The theorem uses the exact ray and does not make that mistake. The accumulating zeros of a sum of two different exponential characters correctly obstruct a single meromorphic selected line. The amplified whole-unit example has primitive -2i pi^2/h and normalized rate -4pi^2 as printed. Existence of the ACTUAL selected line, its original co-source and its marked leading regulator character is still the new theorem to prove.

title: The Rivin optimizer is a whole algebraic function of the boundary phases
text: # The Rivin optimizer is a whole algebraic function of the boundary phases Research proof, 27 October 2026. The positive geometric edge curve and its conjugate place have an étale two-parameter **phase-ratio map**. Its inverse is the unique constrained Rivin optimizer. Consequently the optimizer shapes, peripheral norms, constrained Hessian and all higher derivatives of the boundary potential are algebraic functions of two independent multiplicative boundary phases. The potential itself is a marked logarithmic regulator period, with an explicit primitive. This strengthens the earlier algebraicity over an already selected meridian: it constructs the algebraic inverse of the real boundary phase optimization. It is a classical whole-function statement, not a quantum-source selection or volume-conjecture theorem. ## 1. Assumptions and the retained marks Let T be a one-cusped ideal triangulation with t tetrahedra and a specified positive complete geometric shape point z^0, meaning Im z_j^0>0. Use the open algebraic shape space with `z_j(1-z_j)!=0` and the monomial edge/peripheral equations over Q, including their original sign characters. No branching of all tetrahedra at once is required for this local calculation. We use the independently established marked gluing linear data: * t-1 independent real integral edge rows span an isotropic space E; * its symplectic reduction E^perp/E is the marked peripheral plane; * a primitive meridian row adjoined to the edges has rank t and is isotropic; * the peripheral convention is `Omega_red=-(1/2)du wedge dv`. These are the explicit rank and marking inputs, not consequences of concavity alone. They are proved for the actual knot gluing complex in the preceding integral peripheral notes. The proof below also works for any triangulation supplied with this data. Let the original SL2 eigenvalues be calM,calL, with complete characters calM_c,calL_c in {+1,-1}. Keep those characters on their prescribed finite cover and set the centered logs u=2Log(calM/calM_c), v=2Log(calL/calL_c), m=exp(u), ell=exp(v). (1) Thus u=v=0 at the complete place. Their signs are external marked characters, not reset by squaring or centering. They must be reinserted when an SL2 A-polynomial or a quantum peripheral operator is used. ## 2. The constrained variational equation fixes moduli only after phases For each tetrahedron take compatible logs x_j=Log z_j, y_j=Log z_j'', z_j''=1-z_j^(-1), alpha_j=Im x_j, gamma_j=Im y_j, beta_j=pi-alpha_j-gamma_j. All three angles are positive. The angle domain has the usual linear tetrahedral and edge equations. Its volume is V(theta)=sum_j[Lambda(alpha_j)+Lambda(beta_j)+Lambda(gamma_j)], Lambda'(theta)=-Log(2sin theta). On each tetrahedral angle simplex the negative Hessian in alpha,gamma is [[cot alpha+cot beta,cot beta], [cot beta,cot gamma+cot beta]]. (2) Its determinant is one and its first diagonal entry is `sin gamma/(sin alpha sin beta)>0`. Hence V is strictly concave on every affine angle slice. Write Omega=sum_j dx_j wedge dy_j. The sine rule gives exactly dV(delta theta)=Omega(Re(x,y),delta theta). (3) For example Re x=Log(sin beta/sin gamma) and Re y=Log(sin alpha/sin beta), which verifies (3) by direct differentiation. Edge-angle tangents form E^perp. Fix the TWO real peripheral angles a=Im u, b=Im v. Their common tangent space is E, since their two rows give a basis of E^perp/E. Therefore an interior stationary point on this affine fixed-(a,b) slice satisfies Re(x,y) in E^perp. (4) Equation (4) is exactly the missing real part of the edge gluing equations. Their imaginary parts were imposed by the angle equations. Thus the stationary point solves full complex edge gluing. Its real peripheral logs are outputs of the optimization, not separately fixed constraints. This distinction is essential. Fixing arbitrary independent complex values m and ell overdetermines the one-dimensional geometric edge curve. Conversely imposing nonlinear full holonomy constraints in angle variables is not an affine constraint to which strict concavity can simply be applied. The correct independent real optimization parameters are a,b; the multiplicative algebraic parameters constructed below are their squared phases. Any positive stationary point is the unique global maximizer on that affine slice, and on its closure. For any other point the segment from the positive stationary point is interior until its possible final endpoint. Its second derivative is strictly negative by (2) and its initial derivative is zero, so its volume is strictly smaller, including by continuity at a degenerate final endpoint. ## 3. Positive gluing gives the required complex transversality Here is the short rank calculation, recorded to make all algebraic inverses explicit. At a positive shape dy_j/dx_j=tau_j=1/(z_j-1), Im tau_j<0. Let (A B) be the rank-t isotropic matrix of edges and the marked meridian. The fixed-meridian logarithmic shape Jacobian is J=A+B diag(tau_j). (5) If Ja=0, the shape tangent `(a,diag(tau)a)` lies in the complexification of a real Lagrangian. Its symplectic pairing with its conjugate is zero. But directly (i/2)Omega((a,tau a),conjugate(a,tau a)) =sum_j Im tau_j |a_j|^2<0 unless a=0. Hence det J!=0. The edge curve is smooth at the positive point and is étale over the complex meridian m. The conjugate place has the conjugate invertible Jacobian. Write its peripheral slopes as tau_+=dv/du, tau_-=d(v_tilde)/d(u_tilde). They are algebraic rational functions on the corresponding shape curve: solve (5) for a unit meridian variation and apply the longitude row. On the positive real pair tau_-=bar(tau_+), and the reduced symplectic identity gives Im tau_+=-2sum_j Im tau_j |dx_j/du|^2>0. (6) Thus the two peripheral slopes are distinct. This is the transversality which strict concavity by itself would not supply. ## 4. The doubled normalized curve is étale over the phase torus Let X_+ be the chosen normalized positive edge-curve place and X_- its conjugate place. Work on their product, retaining the shape cover if the peripheral curve alone forgets shapes. Define P_mu=m_+/m_-, P_lambda=ell_+/ell_-, A=m_+m_-, B=ell_+ell_-. (7) The map to the two-dimensional phase torus is algebraic over Q. Its logarithmic Jacobian in the local coordinates u,u_tilde is [[1,-1],[tau_+,-tau_-]], determinant=tau_+-tau_-. (8) It is invertible at the chosen complete pair by (6). Equivalently one may use both sets of edge equations and the two ratio equations (7); their full shape Jacobian is the product of the two fixed-meridian Jacobians and (8), up to explicit nonzero monomial coordinate factors. It follows that the selected doubled shape germ is étale over `(P_mu,P_lambda)=(1,1)`. Its shapes, norms A,B and slopes are algebraic over Q(P_mu,P_lambda). A component defined only after a number-field extension causes no loss of algebraicity over Q: the entire defining gluing/ratio system is over Q, and its selected unramified component is generically finite over the phase torus. For completeness, the algebraicity does not follow merely from a unique real optimum. For the full polynomial system at fixed phase values, invertibility of its Jacobian makes every shape differential over the phase coefficient field zero. A finitely generated characteristic-zero field of positive transcendence degree has nonzero differentials (choose a transcendence basis). Thus the selected shape field extension is algebraic and finite. This is a local étale statement with a selected place. It does not assert that all branches form a finite étale cover over a Zariski neighborhood of (1,1). Other places can ramify above the same base value. The selected completed local factor, after its finite residue-field mark, is the power-series ring in the two phase parameters and is finite étale over the completed base. Every specified nilpotent phase lift has a unique shape lift at that mark. Globally the same function field is finite over the phase field, but branch and deleted divisors must be retained in any continuation. ## 5. The algebraic inverse is the entire positive optimizer on its phase fiber For real phases near the complete point take P_mu=exp(2ia), P_lambda=exp(2ib), Log P_mu=2ia, Log P_lambda=2ib. (9) The product-curve real involution `(z,w)->(bar w,bar z)` covers `(P_mu,P_lambda)->(1/bar P_mu,1/bar P_lambda)`. It fixes the chosen conjugate pair. Uniqueness of the local inverse in (8) therefore forces w=bar z on the real phase torus. Positivity of z persists in a sufficiently small neighborhood. These shapes satisfy the full edge gluing and the fixed boundary phases, so Section 2 makes their angles the unique GLOBAL volume maximizer of that whole positive affine angle fiber. Thus the constrained optimum is not merely obtained by a flow limit: its shapes are the values of the selected whole algebraic inverse (7). The angles themselves are logarithmic phases of these shapes and need not be algebraic numbers or functions. There is also a global real statement on the fixed affine angle/log-marking. Take all positive solutions of the full edge equations in that marked angle domain. Each is stationary on its fixed-(a,b) fiber by (3)--(4). Strict concavity therefore makes the map to the UNWRAPPED angle pair (a,b) injective. Equations (5)--(8) make it a local real diffeomorphism at every such point. Consequently it is a diffeomorphism onto its open image, with one classical sheet there (absolute degree one). The image is not asserted to be all feasible phase pairs or convex. Different log-lift fibers can have the same periodic (P_mu,P_lambda), so this global assertion is not made over the unmarked phase torus. It does not assign a degree to the quantum compact source cycle or its critical projection. The complex peripheral values are recovered algebraically on this cover. They lie on the marked A-curve, rather than being two independent full holonomy parameters. Complete m=ell=1, or the original calM_c,calL_c=+1 or -1, gives the recorded algebraic complete shape field. ## 6. The multiplicative Legendre graph and its full Hessian are algebraic Let V_boundary(a,b) be this maximal volume and put Phi(a,b)=-2 V_boundary(a,b). The reduced form and (3) give dV_boundary=(1/2)(Re v da-Re u db), u=Phi_b+ia, v=-Phi_a+ib. (10) On the doubled real slice the norm coordinates in (7) therefore satisfy the whole multiplicative identities exp(2Phi_b)=A, exp(-2Phi_a)=B. (11) A and B are algebraic functions of P_mu,P_lambda. Hence the exponentiated Legendre graph is algebraic over the phase torus, while its first derivatives are marked logarithms of algebraic functions. There is an explicit algebraic Hessian. Write Delta=tau_+-tau_-. Then Hess_(a,b) Phi =(2i/Delta)[[tau_+tau_-,-(tau_++tau_-)/2], [-(tau_++tau_-)/2,1]], det Hess Phi=1. (12) On the real slice, tau_+=p+iq with q>0, this is (1/q)[[p^2+q^2,-p],[-p,1]], which is positive definite. Formula (12) follows by solving `dLog P_mu=du-du_tilde` and `dLog P_lambda=tau_+du-tau_-du_tilde`, then applying (10). Its determinant is one directly, without a period estimate. All derivatives of Phi of order at least two are algebraic on this cover: the phase derivatives are the algebraic vector fields `2iP_mu partial_(P_mu)` and `2iP_lambda partial_(P_lambda)`, extended uniquely to the finite characteristic-zero function field. The same statement holds for the full constrained angle fluctuation matrix. For example cot(alpha_j)=i(z_j+w_j)/(z_j-w_j), and similarly for the other two shape orders. Thus (2), its restriction to any fixed rational basis of the affine constraint kernel, its inverse covariance and its determinant are rational functions of the doubled shapes. Their determinants are units on the positive chart. Its positive real Gaussian square root is therefore an algebraic marked half-density on a finite cover. This variational Hessian is not thereby the actual quantum state's separately normalized Gaussian amplitude. ## 7. The potential is an explicit marked regulator period On the doubled logarithmic cover retain u,v,u_tilde,v_tilde and the sums and differences Log A=u+u_tilde, Log B=v+v_tilde, Log P_mu=u-u_tilde, Log P_lambda=v-v_tilde. Equation (10) becomes the exact closed logarithmic one-form dPhi=[Log A dLog P_lambda-Log B dLog P_mu]/(4i). (13) Its derivative is `[du wedge dv-du_tilde wedge dv_tilde]/(2i)=0`, since each pair is pulled back from a curve. All differentiated log coordinates are algebraic logarithmic differentials on the whole doubled-phase cover. Let R_+,R_- be the existing marked Heisenberg regulator periods on the two shape factors, with dR_+=-(u dv-v du)/4, dR_-=-(u_tilde dv_tilde-v_tilde du_tilde)/4. An exact primitive is Phi=(R_--R_+)/i +(u_tilde v-u v_tilde)/(4i)+C. (14) Differentiate (14): its cross term is the differential of the displayed bilinear expression, and the remaining terms give exactly (13). The bilinear term cannot be omitted away from completeness. The constant is fixed by the original fundamental-class marks, not fitted to a desired volume. With conjugate marks at the complete place, `R_-=bar R_+`, centered logs are zero, and the already proved Bloch fundamental-class evaluation is `Im R_+=Vol`. Both (14) and the definition of Phi then give `Phi=-2Vol`, so C=0 with these marks. Other sign/log sheets carry their recorded period characters and the corresponding constant; they are not identified with this sheet. Thus the optimizer is a whole algebraic shape/norm function, and its volume potential is a whole logarithmic regulator period on that cover. Its algebraic Hessian and every fixed jet are evaluations of these functions. The statement does not require treating a formal Taylor expansion as the primary object. ## 8. A fixed two-step unipotent connection carries the whole potential The logarithmic primitive has a fixed algebraic period object before any quantum jet or level is chosen. Write A_log=Log A, B_log=Log B, P_log=Log P_mu, Q_log=Log P_lambda, Z=4i Phi. Form the five-dimensional Heisenberg period matrix Pi=[[1,A_log,-B_log,Z], [0,1,0,Q_log], [0,0,1,P_log], [0,0,0,1]]. Its equation is exactly Pi^(-1)dPi=Omega, Omega=[[0,dlog A,-dlog B,0], [0,0,0,dlog P_lambda], [0,0,0,dlog P_mu], [0,0,0,0]]. (14a) The top-right entry vanishes precisely by (13). Every nonzero entry of Omega is an algebraic logarithmic differential on the fixed doubled curve. Its only possible curvature entry is dlog A wedge dlog P_lambda-dlog B wedge dlog P_mu =2(du wedge dv-du_tilde wedge dv_tilde)=0. Thus (14a) is a flat algebraic connection on that whole cover. The group law has a four-dimensional additive quotient and a one-dimensional center; commutators are central and third nested commutators vanish. In the displayed representation every product of three connection matrices is already zero. Along a marked path, transport is therefore EXACTLY the sum of the identity, single integrals of Omega, and double ordered integrals of Omega. No asymptotic expansion or infinite transport iteration is needed. The marked value of Z at the complete point is -8i Vol, by (14). It is the central fundamental-class period; zero initial logarithms alone would leave this central constant free. The connection is algebraic, while its horizontal period matrix generally is not. In particular exponentiating the central period is a specified analytic period evaluation, not an algebraic character from the additive center to the multiplicative group. This realizes the proposed whole geometric torsor explicitly. It does not make an arbitrary quantum A-module unipotent or construct the selected quantum-source map into this torsor. ## 9. Direct A-polynomial formulation and the essential normalization Let calA(m,ell) be a polynomial equation for the marked squared peripheral curve. If the chosen A-polynomial uses SL2 variables, retain the finite sign cover (1) instead. Equation (10) implies calA(exp(Phi_b+ia),exp(-Phi_a+ib))=0, calA(exp(Phi_b-ia),exp(-Phi_a-ib))=0. (15) On the whole algebraic phase cover, a necessary elimination presentation is calA(m,ell)=0, calA(m/P_mu,ell/P_lambda)=0, A=m^2/P_mu, B=ell^2/P_lambda. (16) The selected normalized places are essential. At P_mu=P_lambda=1 the raw first two equations in (16) coincide and contain the entire diagonal peripheral curve. They are not an étale zero-dimensional fiber by themselves. The opposite geometric and conjugate places on the normalization are distinct even where their plane images collide. Their product has the nonzero determinant (8). If needed, retain the finite shape cover of that normalization as well. Thus an A-polynomial formulation can encode the optimizer without a knot-by-knot calculation, but it must keep the chosen normalized A-place/torsor and its fundamental period. An unmarked plane equation and positivity at one point do not discard the diagonal or other peripheral components. ## 10. Coverage and the quantum boundary Classical angle-volume optimization and volume potentials on peripheral curves are established subjects. The coverage already recorded in the repo includes Rivin and [Futer--Gueritaud](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.0440), and the coverage-only search includes Guilloux--Marche, [Volume function and Mahler measure of exact polynomials](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01395), and Johansson--Samuelsson Kalm, [arxiv:1412.1585](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.1585). No proof from those papers is used here. The refinement proved in this note is the explicit phase-doubled algebraic inverse, its normalization requirements, and the marked primitive (14). No new Ronkin, Harnack or dimer identification is asserted. The theorem assumes a positive geometric ideal triangulation and the stated integral gluing/peripheral rank data. It does not infer right-angled geometric Menasco cells from alternatingness. Those combinatorial diagrams need their own geometric hypotheses. The classical proof makes no knot-family restriction once its explicit geometric input is supplied. The whole quantum A-state and its selected cycle are additional objects. The doubled-phase cover may supply a fixed algebraic coefficient space for a proposed comparison, but it does not construct that comparison, prove a bounded quantum comparison space, or establish a nonzero selected geometric contribution. Its regulator period is not made algebraic by algebraicity of the optimizer. No volume conjecture follows without that remaining source/period theorem. ## 11. Focused exact audit [audit_doubled_phase_rivin_optimizer.py](../experiments/audit_doubled_phase_rivin_optimizer.py) and its [results](../experiments/doubled_phase_rivin_optimizer_results.json) verify the phase Jacobian, algebraic Hessian and determinant one, the real positive Hessian, rational tetrahedral covariance, the marked regulator primitive and its closedness, and the exact H5 Maurer--Cartan matrix. All triple connection-matrix products vanish, and its sole curvature coefficient is exactly the stated difference of the two curve symplectic forms. An exact algebraic node chart also checks the whole phase inverse, norm-gradient/Hessian identities and the unnormalized A-equation's diagonal fiber. It is a convention stress test, not an additional knot case or a replacement for the general proof. The independent [doubled-phase and source audit](doubled_phase_and_critical_source_independent_audit.md) checks the real branch, global fixed-affine-fiber maximizer, unwrapped positive projection, sign characters, period constants, normalization requirements and the H5 transport. All focused symbolic checks passed. No quantum normal-family or selected source conclusion is inferred from them.

title: An exact dual clock lift to the centralizer normal co-source
text:
# An exact dual clock lift to the centralizer normal co-source Research theorem, 27 October 2026. Every actual finite cut clock has an explicit polynomial centralizer-normal co-source, valid on ALL matrices. On the physical scaled clock this polynomial converges locally uniformly to a whole exponential, with uniform factorial coefficient bounds. Its derivatives transport every bounded normalized cut-position moment exactly. The lift is contravariant: it represents a trace FUNCTIONAL. It is not a multiplicative symbol map, a crossing intertwiner, or an internal Gaussian source comparison. ## 1. The dual Toeplitz map of the actual compact source Put \(n=N-1\). In the source coordinates \(T=va\), the actual coherent matrix symbol is \[ f_C(v,T)=\sum_{i,j=0}^n C_{ij} inom nj v^{i-j}T^j(1-T)^{n-j}. \] Let \(\omega_I=-\Omega_0/(2\pi i)\), whose marked compact period is one. Angular integration and the beta integral give, for every polynomial \(P\), \[ \int_\Gamma P(-T)f_C\,\omega_I = rac1N\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal T_N(P)C), 	ag{1} \] where the diagonal Toeplitz row is \[ [\mathcal T_N(b^h)]_j =(-1)^h rac{(j+1)^{\overline h}} {(N+1)^{\overline h}}, \qquad h\ge0,\quad 0\le j<N. 	ag{2} \] A bar denotes the rising factorial. Formula (2) holds at ALL polynomial degrees, not only below \(N\). On polynomials of degree at most \(n\), \(\mathcal T_N\) is an isomorphism onto the diagonal matrices: its h-th basis column is a polynomial in j of degree h with nonzero leading coefficient, evaluated at the N distinct integer points. This is different from the covariant symbol quantization \(b^h\mapsto(-1)^h(J)_h/(n)_h\). The all-matrix pairing here is the normalized ORDINARY TRACE. On the actual position-conserving weighted-word and Green cut arrays it agrees with the original average cut because those arrays are diagonal. It is not the original average functional \(\Phi(C)=N^{-1}\sum_{i,j}C_{ij}\) on arbitrary off-diagonal Ward matrices. Any such Hopf-current comparison must retain and transport that original coupon separately. The trace extension is stated explicitly rather than identified with all possible actual co-sources. ## 2. Exact inversion for the WHOLE clock For any complex \(w\), define the polynomial of degree at most n \[ P_{N,w}^{\vee}(b)=\sum_{h=0}^n a_{N,h}(w)b^h, \] \[ a_{N,h}(w)=  rac{(N+1)^{\overline h}}{h!} \sum_{r=h}^n(-1)^r inom rh(w-1)^r . 	ag{3} \] Then exactly \[ \mathcal T_N(P_{N,w}^{\vee})=w^J , \qquad Je_j=je_j. 	ag{4} \] Thus for EVERY matrix C, \[  rac1N\operatorname{Tr}(w^JC) =\int_\Gamma P_{N,w}^{\vee}(-T)f_C\,\omega_I . 	ag{5} \] Here is a direct proof. The polynomial identity \[ (j)_r=\sum_{h=0}^r(-1)^{r-h} inom rh  rac{r!}{h!}(j+1)^{\overline h} 	ag{6} \] follows, for example, by comparing coefficients in \((1+\delta)^j\): sum the right side over r with weight \(\delta^r/r!\), use \(\sum_{r\ge h}(-1)^{r-h} inom rh\delta^r =\delta^h/(1+\delta)^{h+1}\), and then the rising-binomial series. Now expand \(w^j\) in the Newton basis \[ w^j=\sum_{r=0}^n rac{(j)_r}{r!}(w-1)^r \quad(0\le j\le n). \] Insert (6), collect h, and apply (2). This is precisely (3)--(4). Useful exact endpoint formulas are \[ P_{N,w}^{\vee}(0)=\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}(1-w)^r,\qquad P_{N,w}^{\vee}(-1)=w^N-(w-1)^N. 	ag{7} \] These are not the actual clock eigenvalues at j=0,n. Confusing dual polynomial evaluation with a matrix endpoint would lose finite endpoint corrections. ## 3. Scaled clocks, moments, and uniform whole limits Put \(w=e^{z/N}\). On every compact complex z-set, \(|w-1|\le C/N\). For all sufficiently large N, \[ |a_{N,h}(e^{z/N})| \le  rac{(N+1)^{\overline h}}{h!}  rac{|w-1|^h}{(1-|w-1|)^{h+1}} \le C_1\, rac{C_2^h}{h!}, \qquad 0\le h<N. 	ag{8} \] Indeed \((N+1)^{\overline h}\le(2N)^h\) for h<N, while \((1-C/N)^{-h-1}\) is bounded uniformly in that range. For each fixed h, the leading r=h term in (3) gives \[ a_{N,h}(e^{z/N})\longrightarrow(-z)^h/h!. \] The factorial majorant proves the WHOLE locally uniform limit \[ P_{N,e^{z/N}}^{\vee}(b)\longrightarrow e^{-zb} \quad\hbox{on }\mathbb C_z	imes\mathbb C_b. 	ag{9} \] This also proves convergence of every fixed derivative by Cauchy's formula. No WKB asymptotic interpretation of these derivatives is used. Differentiation of (4) gives the exact normalized moment identities \[ \mathcal T_N\!\left(\partial_z^r P_{N,e^{z/N}}^\veeight) =(J/N)^r e^{zJ/N}. 	ag{10} \] At z=0 these give every fixed normalized polynomial cut-position moment. Unnormalized moments \(J^r\) retain the explicit factor \(N^r\). Formula (10) is a whole clock-coupling identity, valid before any internal flow sum. The bounded moment has a stronger finite normal-order statement. Put \[ G_{N,r}(b)=\left.\partial_z^r P_{N,e^{z/N}}^\vee(b)ight|_{z=0}. \] It has degree at most \(\min(r,n)\). In particular for every fixed r and all \(N>r\), its normal pole in (13) has order at most r+1, INDEPENDENT of N. An exact closed formula is \[ [b^h]G_{N,r}=  rac{(N+1)^{\overline h}}{N^r h!} \sum_{s=h}^{\min(r,n)} S(r,s)(-1)^s inom sh s!, \qquad 0\le h\le\min(r,n), 	ag{10a} \] where \(S(r,s)\) are Stirling numbers of the second kind. This follows by differentiating \((e^{z/N}-1)^s\) at zero, whose r-th derivative is \(s!S(r,s)/N^r\). For r at most n the leading coefficient is \((-1)^r(N+1)^{\overline r}/N^r\), while each lower coefficient is \(O_r(N^{h-r})\). Hence \[ G_{N,r}(b)=(-b)^r+O_r(1/N) \] on every fixed compact b-set. Arbitrary bounded-degree normalized Green cut-position polynomials follow by linearity. Their actual source-normal pole depth is therefore bounded even though the WHOLE clock uses degree \(N-1\). Beta reflection gives \[ \mathcal T_N(P(-1-b))_j=\mathcal T_N(P)_{n-j}. \] Injectivity on degree at most n therefore proves \[ P_{N,w}^\vee(-1-b)=w^nP_{N,w^{-1}}^\vee(b). 	ag{11} \] The centered polynomial \[ \widehat P_N(z,b)=e^{-nz/(2N)}P_{N,e^{z/N}}^\vee(b) \] reflects z to -z and tends to \(e^{-z(b+1/2)}\). For the identity matrix, (5) is EXACTLY the retained source character \[ \int_\Gamma\widehat P_N(z,-T)\omega_I = rac1N\operatorname{Tr}e^{z(J-n/2)/N} = rac{\sinh(z/2)}{N\sinh(z/(2N))}. 	ag{12} \] Thus this lift reproduces the same whole source norm/peripheral factor as the scaled-meridian and Gamma-source calculations. ## 4. Normal residue and global affine clutch Use the normal centralizer coordinate \(b=-a/\eta\) and \[ 
u_{m cut}=- rac{d\eta}{\eta}\wedge  rac{\Omega_0}{1-\eta v}. \] For every h, expansion of the geometric denominator gives \[ \operatorname{Res}_{E}(b^h
u_{m cut}) =-(-T)^h\Omega_0 . \] Linearity, (3), and (5) yield the exact source pairing \[  rac1N\operatorname{Tr}(w^JC) = rac1{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma \operatorname{Res}_{E} \left(P_{N,w}^\vee(b)f_C
u_{m cut}ight). 	ag{13} \] This is a SOURCE-KERNEL lift; it is not asserted to be the internal Gaussian image of that kernel. The north and south torsor coordinates obey \[ b_S=b_N+ rac1{v\eta},\qquad b_S-1-b_N= rac{1-\eta v}{v\eta}. \] Use \(P(b_N)\) north and \(P(b_S-1)\) south. Their difference is divisible by the Gauss-wall factor. After multiplication by \(
u_{m cut}\) the Gauss-wall pole cancels, leaving only \(\eta^{-r}d\eta\wedge\Omega_0\) with \(r\ge2\). Each has an explicit normal primitive and zero E-residue. Thus (13) retains a compatible affine Cech moment marking. Bare \(P(b_S)\) would have the wrong residue polynomial. At finite N the normal pole degree can reach N, since \(\deg P^\vee=N-1\) and \(
u_{m cut}\) already has a simple normal pole. It must not be replaced by a bounded normal jet. After taking the explicit residue formula, (8)--(9) do allow locally uniform convergence of the whole residue to its exponential source form. No algebraicity of that limiting horizontal exponential is claimed. ## 5. Exact finite cut-current endpoints For an arbitrary zero-extended finite current \(J_j\), set \(\lambda_{N,w}^{m head}(J)=N^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}w^jJ_j\). For \(w
e0\), direct summation by parts gives \[ \lambda_{N,w}^{m head}((S-1)J) =(w^{-1}-1)\lambda_{N,w}^{m head}(J) + rac{w^{N-1}J_N-w^{-1}J_0}{N}. 	ag{14} \] Including both actual tails gives the full finite row \(N^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}w^jJ_j\), for which the endpoint terms telescope and the factor is exactly \(w^{-1}-1\). Its z-derivatives retain every normalized position-moment endpoint. The original raw Green arrays already contain \(1/N\). Equations (5), (13), and (14) use matrix-normalized arrays; \(I_{m mat}=NI_{m raw}\), \(J_{m mat}=NJ_{m raw}\). Equivalently use N times these rows on raw arrays. No factor N is absorbed into an endpoint. ## 6. Whole word composition is exact; Gaussian naturality is additional An actual transfer clock can be split into literal input/output position clocks. For the recorded checked R conventions, \[ R_+:(i,j)\mapsto(j+k,i-k),\qquad R_-:(i,j)\mapsto(j-k,i+k), \] so \[ w^kR_+=(I\otimes w^{-J})R_+(w^J\otimes I),\qquad w^kR_-=(I\otimes w^J)R_-(w^{-J}\otimes I). 	ag{15} \] These are exact coefficient identities with the same Cartan and pivot lines. Products and tensor products use the actual operator composition, or equivalently the exact finite coherent STAR product. Thus all weighted words and their coupling derivatives retain their source meaning. Pointwise multiplication is not that star product. Already at N=2 the actual inverse clocks obey \(\operatorname{Tr}(w^Jw^{-J})/2=1\), whereas \[ \int_0^1[1+(w-1)T][1+(w^{-1}-1)T]\,dT =1+ rac{w+w^{-1}-2}{6}. \] At the actual root clock w=-1 this is 1/3, not one. The DUAL pairing (5) gives one exactly. Moving a dual clock through an actual crossing therefore requires the transpose of its finite star action. A scalar polynomial in b represents diagonal co-sources only; after an off-diagonal crossing one generally needs the full angular/coherent dual source as well. The normal residue is not a multiplicative operator-algebra map. Consequently this theorem supplies the actual whole CUT clock and all its normalized moments, including tails and affine clutch. The independent second framing coordinate still needs its network map. Nor is the source-dependent transverse Gaussian pushforward proved natural for this contravariant star action. These are the specific remaining couplings, rather than a defect in the finite clock formula. ## 7. Why the raw framing moments are not the finite critical field For the actual scalar closed cut \(C=F_NI\), the polynomial normal-centralizer moments from (1) normalize to \[ \mu(b^h)=(-1)^h/(h+1). \] Their Hankel matrices are signed Hilbert matrices, positive definite at EVERY size: \(\mu(p\overline p)=\int_0^1|p(-T)|^2dT>0\) for nonzero p. Hence no nonzero polynomial ideal is annihilated. This raw framing co-source cannot factor through a fixed finite algebra in b, even for the actual figure-eight. This does not contradict a finite algebra of ISOLATED TRANSVERSE geometric critical points. The framing variable is meant to be integrated first, or retained in a relative/twisted complex. It does rule out defining that critical observable as the raw Toeplitz image of b: \(\mathcal T_N\) is not multiplicative. A finite list of moments reconstructs a density only AFTER its critical polynomial relation has actually been supplied. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_dual_clock_normal_cut_source.py) and [results](../experiments/dual_clock_normal_cut_source_results.json): 337 symbolic clock, normalized-moment, reflection, endpoint and finite-current identities pass at N=2 through 11.

title: An endpoint-completed whole Jackson current from actual divided matrices
text: # An endpoint-completed whole Jackson current from actual divided matrices Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual high-color divided raising/lowering currents, with two literal anchored primitives, recover the WHOLE Jackson differential on the physical unwrapped clock. Its root value is the clock Euler derivative. The missing bottom state is repaired explicitly, so the identity holds on every state, not only in a bulk chart. A rational function and its shift are retained before matrix evaluation. This is an actual current/source map on the commutative physical character subalgebra. The exact off-diagonal correction below shows why it is not yet a map of all head Hopf currents or a full geometric Gaussian/source comparison. ## 1. Whole actual matrices and regular anchored inverses Use the original high integral color with r=N from [the actual source theorem](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md). In its fixed sign frame write w_(R,S), 0<=R<=N, 0<=S<N, and set \[ Z=Q^N,\quad\delta=1-Z,\quad J=NR+S,\quad C_Q=Q^J=Q^S Z^R. \] Keep the ORIGINAL generic integral divided matrices \[ e(q)=\tau E^{(N)}(q),\qquad f(q)=F^{(N)}(q),\quad \tau=(-1)^{N^2-1}. \] They preserve S and change R by -1 and +1. Their nonzero arrow coefficients alpha_(R,S)(q), R>=1, and beta_(R,S)(q), R<N, are regular units near the marked root: their root values are N-R+1 and R+1. Define actual inverse arrows \[ e^\dagger w_{R,S}=\alpha_{R+1,S}^{-1}w_{R+1,S}\ (R<N), \quad e^\dagger w_{N,S}=0, \] \[ f^\dagger w_{R,S}=\beta_{R-1,S}^{-1}w_{R-1,S}\ (R>0), \quad f^\dagger w_{0,S}=0. \] These are whole rational matrix germs of the actual divided coefficients, not inverses of nilpotent matrices. With P_0,P_N the two block endpoint projectors, they satisfy EXACTLY \[ e^\dagger e=I-P_0,\quad ee^\dagger=I-P_N,\qquad f^\dagger f=I-P_N,\quad ff^\dagger=I-P_0. \tag{1} \] Their root operator norms are at most one in the fixed unit basis. No uniform estimate on a growing q-neighborhood is assumed. In the actual positive Fr metric ||v_R||^2=binom(N,R), the sharper bound is ||e^dagger||=||f^dagger||=1/sqrt(N); the two endpoint projectors still have norm one. This follows from the normalized inverse arrow 1/sqrt((R+1)(N-R)). ## 2. The whole Jackson identity, with its shifted argument Let g(Q,t) be a retained Laurent polynomial, or a rational function whose denominators at BOTH C_Q and ZC_Q are invertible in the chosen whole matrix chart. Q remains fixed when its t argument is shifted. Define the actual current \[ \mathcal J_Z(g)=\frac{-e^\dagger[e,g(Q,ZC_Q)] +P_0f^\dagger[f,g(Q,C_Q)]}{1-Z}. \tag{2} \] Then, as an exact whole rational matrix identity, \[ \boxed{\ \mathcal J_Z(g) =\frac{g(Q,C_Q)-g(Q,ZC_Q)}{1-Z}.\ } \tag{3} \] Proof. The actual block grading gives eC_Q=ZC_Qe and fC_Q=Z^(-1)C_Qf. The inverse arrows have the opposite degrees. Keeping operator order and the SHIFTED argument in (2) therefore gives \[ e^\dagger[e,g(ZC_Q)] =[g(ZC_Q)-g(C_Q)](I-P_0), \] \[ f^\dagger[f,g(C_Q)] =[g(C_Q)-g(ZC_Q)](I-P_N). \] Since P_0P_N=0, their combination is the full difference, with no missing endpoint. This proves (3). In particular replacing g(ZC_Q) by g(C_Q) in the first commutator would give a different operator and would not prove this identity. The right side has a regular value at Z=1 whenever the stated function chart is regular. For every integer k, \[ \mathcal J_Z(t^k)=\frac{1-Z^k}{1-Z}C_Q^k, \] and it obeys the exact twisted product rule \[ \mathcal J_Z(gh)=\mathcal J_Z(g)h(C_Q) +g(ZC_Q)\mathcal J_Z(h). \tag{4} \] Thus the construction is a whole function calculus before its normal jets are taken. An explicit q-dependent coefficient is carried unchanged in the difference; its separate q-derivative is not silently included in a clock derivative. At the root A=Q_N^S, (3) gives \[ \mathcal E(g):=[\mathcal J_Z(g)]_0 =A\partial_A g(Q_N,A)\,I_{\rm Fr}. \tag{5} \] The shifted argument in (2) has the same leading divided commutator as its unshifted value, so equivalently E(g)=[-e^dagger[e,g(C_Q)]/delta+P_0 f^dagger[f,g(C_Q)]/delta]_0. For every remaining head matrix entry the output of (5) is the literal multiplication by the indicated head character. ## 3. The normal jet and the literal finite cut The derivative in (5) is not a derivation of the reduced finite clock algebra k[A^+/-1]/(A^N-1): it sends A^N-1 to N. The whole normal datum is essential. More precisely, for frozen coefficients k containing Q_N, the actual map g(t)->g(C_Q) modulo delta^2 has kernel \[ (t^N-1)^2. \tag{6} \] Indeed root vanishing implies g=(t^N-1)h. On w_(R,S), C_Q^N-1=-J delta+O(delta^2). Vanishing at first normal order then implies J h(Q_N^S)=0 for every R. For each S at least one of J=NR+S is nonzero, so h vanishes at all N roots. This proves (6), and the converse follows by squaring the simple normal zero. Thus (5) is the actual clock conormal-jet derivative \[ k[t^{+/-1}]/(t^N-1)^2\longrightarrow k[A^{+/-1}]/(A^N-1),\quad g\mapsto Ag'(A). \] It is a derivation relative to the root evaluation, not a discarded normal direction on the fixed fiber. Write uniquely g=g_0+(t^N-1)g_1 modulo its square, with both g_i of degree<N. For the ORIGINAL averaged cut phi_N, the exact source row is \[ \phi_N(\mathcal E(g))=N\phi_N(g_1). \tag{7} \] The canonical polynomial g_0 contributes no constant coefficient after Ag_0'. The factor N in (7) is explicit. An unnormalized Fr source line multiplies both sides by its retained pairing unit; normalizing it does not change the head factor. Apply this linear map coefficientwise to the sourced relative interval complex R(E) of [the literal framing transgression](relative_framing_source_transgression.md). It commutes strictly with the interval differential, its two endpoint rows and its polynomial contraction. Thus (2)--(7) give an ACTUAL Fr-current realization of the clock-normal piece of that relative cut map, with the original averaged co-source. They do not assign an independent transfer coordinate to the cut. In particular both geometric compensated fields obey xi_i(A)=-2A(1-A). Hence the actual current -2(1-A) E has precisely their common clock component on every retained character g. The difference of the two geometric fields, which moves the other framing coordinate, is not determined by this common component. ## 4. The two primitives have a global P1 realization On the actual Fr source identify v_j with binom(N,j) z^j in H^0(P1,O(N)). Then e=partial_z, and the root inverse e^dagger is exactly the anchored integral integral_0^z, with its degree-(N+1) tail projected away. This gives (1) with the constant and top coefficient projectors. The opposite f^dagger is the corresponding south-chart primitive. These operators also have explicit global differential lifts. Writing D=z partial_z, take q_N(D) with q_N(j)=1/[(j+1)(N-j)] for j<N and q_N(N)=0. Then e^dagger=F q_N(D), f^dagger=E q_N(N-D) on H^0. Their differential order generally grows with N; it is NOT the bounded PBW normal-depth filtration of a crossing. Their identities on the full Cech resolution hold up the explicit contraction homotopy constructed in [the global source/co-source complex](global_frobenius_cech_source_and_endpoints.md). The induced H^0 identities (1)--(3) are literal finite matrices. Dual Serre residue carries the same endpoint projectors, rather than deleting the two anchored boundary terms. All q-dependent arrow inverses and source units in (2) are retained coefficientwise in this lift. This does not make the chosen cut pseudoinverses into Hopf intertwiners on arbitrary tensor products. For example a trivial classical tensor summand is annihilated by both e and f; no repair using their currents alone can produce the identity on that summand. A whole-word map must transport the actual cut projector and mixed coproduct, not blindly tensor (2). ## 5.
