Exact off-diagonal correction Let H(q) be a retained head-matrix insertion, and keep its order to the RIGHT of the clock function. The same current formula with g(ZC_Q)H and g(C_Q)H has the exact result \[ \mathcal J_Z(gH) =\frac{g(C_Q)-g(ZC_Q)}{1-Z}\,H +\frac{-g(C_Q)e^\dagger[e,H] +g(ZC_Q)P_0f^\dagger[f,H]}{1-Z}. \tag{8} \] This follows by the ordered product commutator, using e^dagger g(ZC_Q)=g(C_Q)e^dagger and f^dagger g(C_Q)=g(ZC_Q)f^dagger. If H is an actual head operator whose root commutes with the Fr e,f, the remainder is regular, but it generally does not vanish. If H contains noncommuting Fr insertions, regularity itself requires its additional normal source correction. Thus (3) does not supply the TRUE head Hopf currents merely by relabeling a scalar derivative. Their missing terms are the two explicit inserted moments in (8). The old physical clock and its whole Fourier-resolvent lift are those in [the controlled current dictionary](controlled_fourier_current_and_conormal_dictionary.md), not the distinct new position clock on the diagonal source. Conjugating (2) and every inverse/projector by the whole source gauge preserves the identity exactly, including that dictionary. ### The constant-head correction is an explicit inner connection For a head matrix H kept CONSTANT in q and R, the root remainder in (8) has a closed form. Define \[ \ell_0=0,\qquad \ell_S=-\frac12\sum_{k=1}^{S} \frac{q_N^k+q_N^{-k}}{q_N^k-q_N^{-k}},\quad L_h=\operatorname{diag}(\ell_S),\quad\Sigma=2P_0-I. \] Then the actual divided-arrow matrices give \[ \mathcal E(H)=[\Sigma\otimes L_h,H]. \tag{8a} \] To prove this, write alpha_(R,S)=a_R+delta a_(1,R,S)+... and beta_(R,S)=b_R+delta b_(1,R,S)+..., with a_R=N-R+1,b_R=R+1. Exact commutation of E^(N) with the ordinary E, and F^(N) with ordinary F, along adjacent nonzero head arrows gives BOTH recurrences \[ \frac{a_{1,R,S}}{a_R}-\frac{a_{1,R,0}}{a_R}=\ell_S, \qquad \frac{b_{1,R,S}}{b_R}-\frac{b_{1,R,0}}{b_R}=\ell_S. \tag{8b} \] For example the adjacent F ratio has normal increment -1/2 (q^S+q^(-S))/(q^S-q^(-S)); differentiating the actual q-integer gives it directly. The E ratio gives the same increment. On R>=1, -e^dagger[e,H]/delta therefore gives -[L_h,H]; the literal R=0 repair contributes +[L_h,H]. All R-only constants commute with H. This proves (8a), without setting any individual arrow derivative to zero. Pairing k and N-k in the sum proves ell_(N-1)=0. Its root size is O(N log N), and no head endpoint coefficient has been inverted at a zero. For the actual normalized paired Fr source, the selected coefficient is c_N(m)=<Sigma>=2((1+m)/2)^N-1. Thus the original cut evaluates this correction to c_N(m) Phi_h([L_h,H]). It is an EXPLICIT original head Ward boundary. Let K=xA^(-1) and let B_cut be the actual matrix of the Ward contraction, [K,B_cut]=e_h-I/N. Since [K,L_h]=0, \[ \Phi_h([L_h,H])=-\operatorname{Tr}([B_{\rm cut},L_h][K,H]). \tag{8c} \] This follows by applying the original cut homotopy and Jacobi; the ordinary head trace of a commutator is zero. Hence this coefficient part vanishes IDENTICALLY on the actual diagonal Green arrays and on Ward-closed head partial traces. The endpoint-dependent polynomial c_N(m), including its values -1 and +1 at m=-1,+1, remains in the cochain homotopy. The unnormalized scale line multiplies this identity by its retained pairing rather than being canceled by hand. Actual q-dependent insertions have an additional specified lift term. If H=H_0+delta H_1+... with H_0 a constant-head matrix, then \[ \mathcal E(H)=[\Sigma L_h,H_0] -e_0^\dagger[e_0,H_1]+P_0f_0^\dagger[f_0,H_1]. \tag{8d} \] This includes the true block-wrap and mixed Hopf-normal coefficients. They cannot be removed using only (8c). If the fully closed actual matrix and its first normal are scalar, every term in (8d) vanishes; an unsummed current or a Fr-valued moment need not have that property. ## 6. A finite spectrum does not determine the whole Jackson current Fix a head eigenvalue c=Q^S and write C_s=c Z^R on its N+1 block states. Retain the actual polynomial FUNCTION \[ p_N(t)=\prod_{R=0}^{N}(t-cZ^R). \] Although p_N(C_s)=0 identically, its shifted value is \[ p_N(ZC_s)=c^{N+1}Z^{N(N+1)/2} \prod_{k=1}^{N+1}(Z^k-1)\,P_N, \tag{9} \] where P_N is the TOP STATE PROJECTOR, distinct from the polynomial p_N. All lower shifted points remain in the finite spectrum, but the top point cZ^(N+1) does not. Therefore \[ \mathcal J_Z(p_N) =-\frac{c^{N+1}Z^{N(N+1)/2}\prod_{k=1}^{N+1}(Z^k-1)}{1-Z}P_N =(-1)^N c^{N+1}(N+1)!\delta^N P_N+O(\delta^{N+1}). \tag{10} \] Consequently the WHOLE current depends on the retained function and its shifted observable, not only on the single finite matrix g(C_s). It is invisible through every normal order B<N in this example. The degree of p_N is N+1 and grows with N, so this does not contradict a bounded-presentation cyclotomic rigidity theorem. It gives a concrete actual-source reason to retain functions before their finite evaluations and jets. ## 7. The marked Green logarithm has a carry pole, not the regular Euler value The character theorem must not silently replace the marked logarithmic torsor. Put h=Log Q near h_N=2pi i/N and retain \[ \operatorname{Log}C_Q=hJ,\qquad \operatorname{Log}Z=Nh\quad\hbox{near }2\pi i. \] This is not the branch of Log Z near zero. A retained polynomial moment P(J)=P(Log C_Q/Log Q) shifts to P(J+N). The SAME actual whole current therefore gives the exact identity \[ \mathcal J_Z(P(J))=\frac{P(J)-P(J+N)}{\delta}. \tag{11} \] For a coefficient function F, retain F(Q,ZC_Q,J+N) as well as P(J+N). In particular a Cartan chirp q^(J^2) has root shift factor (-1)^N; freezing that coefficient while shifting P would change the actual carry. More generally let T carry every retained coefficient and the marked index simultaneously. Then the pole residue is exactly \[ \operatorname{Res}_{\delta=0}\mathcal J_Z =(I-T_0). \tag{12} \] On a coefficient fixed by this transport, T_0=e^(N partial_J), and (T_0-I)^(h+1)=0 on moments of degree<=h. On the normalized index J/N it is translation by one. With a nontrivial coefficient transport the associated grade retains that transport minus I; polynomial degree alone does not make it nilpotent. Equation (11) is the actual divided-current realization of the bounded Green carry in [the whole carry source](green_moment_carry_filtration.md). The pole is absent for the single-valued regular characters in Section 2, and present for these marked moments. Subtracting it without its relative endpoint/period class would remove the very moment repair used in the full scalar certificate. No such subtraction or global cancellation is inferred here. [Exact actual-matrix and whole-function audit](../experiments/audit_endpoint_completed_normal_clock_euler.py). The [results](../experiments/endpoint_completed_normal_clock_euler_results.json) pass five actual generic-q families, seven actual root-normal families, 1498 off-diagonal head matrix-unit connection identities, 40 actual marked-clock/carry matrix identities (including a Cartan chirp), six whole finite-spectrum polynomial defects, and 42 symbolic bounded-moment carry checks. The [independent whole-function audit](whole_clock_function_algebra_and_endpoint_extension.md) also checks the endpoint product and distinguishes this retained function algebra from a fixed finite matrix quotient. The theorem supplies a clock/source-current component and the correction (8); it does not prove full sourced geometric support or a selected-volume limit.

title: Meridian transport on the cut source and its geometric dual
text: # Meridian transport on the cut source and its geometric dual Research note, 26 October 2026. The comparison in [the cut-wall note](cut_wall_and_cyclic_source.md) matched source presentations over S=C[[u,h]]. Here their normalized presentations are compared with meridian transport included. The geometric source has the inverse marked longitude character, which is retained explicitly. The result concerns the actual local cut coefficients and a calibrated formal geometric cyclic model. It does not identify the full knot's affine source, selected section, or volume norm. ## 1. The full actual cut has a difference-constant normalization line Keep q=q_N=exp(pi*i/N), x=-M/q, Y=M^2, U=M^(2N), and sigma(M)=qM. Define p=q^(-1)M^2-qM^(-2), r=sigma(p), c_2=q^2+q^(-2). The actual two-factor modified cut in the previous note is Phi_N(f)=C_N(U)[r f_+ + p f_-], C_N(U)=-zeta_N U/[(U-1)(U+1)], zeta_N=q^(N(1-N)/2). (1.1) Thus C_N=Gamma_N/d in that note. It is not Gamma_N that is meridian-constant: the geometric gap d is not constant. At an actual root sigma(U)=U, so sigma(C_N)=C_N exactly. The physical normalization is a marked meromorphic constant line, including its central lattice and both poles. It is not declared a unit at U=1 or absorbed into a coefficientwise formal unit. All statements below about regular S-presentations concern the normalized coefficients, with this line kept separately. The elementary exact identity sigma^2(p)=c_2 sigma(p)-p (1.2) follows by expanding its two monomials. It provides a fixed transport matrix for the cut coefficients: J=[ c_2 1 ], w=(r,p), [ -1 0 ] sigma(w)=w J, det J=1. (1.3) These identities are rational in q,M; they require no formal approximation. At roots they describe the actual weights before any node specialization. ## 2. The wall presentation is meridian-equivariant Work now over S with q=exp(h), M=exp(u), sigma(u)=u+h. Give S^2 the semilinear operator T=J sigma and S the operator sigma. The exact sequence of underlying S-modules is 0 -> S --j--> S^2 --ell--> S -> S/m -> 0, j=(p,-r)^t, ell=(r,p), m=(p,r)=(u,h). (2.1) Every arrow intertwines its stated meridian transport. Indeed J sigma(j)=j, ell J=sigma(ell). (2.2) The first identity uses (1.2); the second is (1.3). Consequently the normalized point source in (2.1) has character 1. This is a specified semilinear presentation, not just an isomorphism of point modules. Tensoring its cut with the recorded C_N line preserves equivariance on its original root meridian chart. Its polar specialization remains a whole-germ operation. The ordered scalar source residue stays fixed under the base meridian change: Res du dh/[p sigma(p)] =Res du dh/[sigma(p) sigma^2(p)]=1/16. (2.3) One direct verification is that the transformation of the two equations in (1.2) has determinant one. Equivalently their two Jacobian determinants at u=h=0 both equal 16. Also sigma(du wedge dh)=du wedge dh. These are statements about the base residue; a tensor period line has its own character. ## 3. The geometric cyclic free presentation has an exact shift matrix Let a,b be the calibrated geometric ratios from the preceding note, so a-b=v p, v in S^times, a(0,0)=b(0,0)=L_c, v(0,0)=kappa/4. Keep the actual SL2 longitude sign L_c; it is not set to one. On the normalized split module V=S^2 use T=diag(a,b)sigma, e=(1,1), f=(1,0), and Lambda=S e direct_sum m S f. Its generators e,pf,rf give the free presentation 0 -> F_1 --R--> F_0 --E--> Lambda -> 0, R=(0,r,-p)^t, E=[ 1 p r ], [ 1 0 0 ] with the following semilinear transports: T_(F_1)=a sigma, T_(F_0)=B sigma, B=[ b 0 0 ], [ v 0 -a ], [ 0 a a c_2]. (3.1) These are automorphisms: det B=b a^2 is a unit. Direct multiplication proves both compatibility identities E B=diag(a,b) sigma(E), B sigma(R)=a R. (3.2) The first uses a=b+vp, and the second uses (1.2). Thus the single relation is itself a meridian line, with ratio a. This records information that an S-module presentation alone omitted. ## 4. Dualizing gives exactly the cut complex with a period-line twist For a semilinear free module T=C sigma, its S-dual transport is C^(-t) sigma. This follows directly from (T phi)(z)=sigma(phi(T^(-1)z)). The dual of (3.1) is therefore the two-term presentation [F_0^vee --R^t--> P_a^vee], where P_a denotes the line with ratio a. Its degree-one cohomology is Ext^1_S(Lambda,S). The explicit dual matrix is B^(-t)=[ 1/b -c_2 v/(ab) v/(ab) ], [ 0 c_2/a -1/a ], [ 0 1/a 0 ]. (4.1) Its first coordinate line is stable, has ratio b^(-1), and maps to zero under R^t. It is exactly P_b^vee: as a functional on V it kills f and sends e to one. Hence this zero column may be quotiented out as a difference submodule, not just deleted from an underlying linear presentation. Define the constant quotient map Q=[ 0 1 0 ], [ 0 0 -1 ]. Then the full matrix identities are Q B^(-t)=a^(-1)J Q, R^t=(r,p)Q. (4.2) They prove an isomorphism of quotient difference complexes: [F_0^vee -> P_a^vee]/P_b^vee[0] = P_a^vee tensor [S^2_(J sigma) --(r,p)--> S_sigma]. (4.3) Thus the normalized actual cut presentation is precisely the universal factor of the geometric dual cyclic presentation; the dual geometric period line is the remaining factor. All arrows and meridian matrices are specified by (4.2). Taking degree-one cohomology gives the equivariant comparison Ext^1_S(Lambda,S)=P_a^vee tensor S/m, T on the point = L_c^(-1). (4.4) The scalar base residue remains (2.3). Multiplication by the two units v,sigma(v) changes it to 1/kappa^2 in the calibrated geometric equations. The opposite sign from the two ordered density values -p,r remains the sign already recorded in the cut-wall note. Neither that sign nor L_c^(-1) is absorbed into zeta_N. This closes the local equivariance calculation for the normalized cut and the calibrated geometric cyclic model. ## 5. The original root matrices check this transport The calculation has a direct check on the original root model. For V_x tensor V_x its generic highest roots are z_j=x^2 Q^(-j), Q=q^2, 0<=j<N. The actual full projector cuts, proved from the pivotal matrices, are d_(z_j). Substitution of the original modified dimension gives d_(z_j)=C_N(U) p_j, p_j=q^(-2j-1)M^2-q^(2j+1)M^(-2), sigma(p_j)=p_(j-1 mod N). (5.1) Here p_0=p and p_(N-1)=r. The actual highest-vector meridian matrix G=H(qM)P H(M)^(-1) intertwines total E,F,K and gives the full affine crossing identity with source (1+U^(-1))E_(N-1). Its label cycle induces exactly (5.1). Thus (1.3) describes the cut weights under this original meridian comparison, not only a chosen model shift on functions. There is a useful specialization qualification. For N>2 the free wall matrix has J^N=I, since its distinct eigenvalues are q^2,q^(-2). At N=2 they coincide; J^2 is not identity. The actual cut then has r=-p and its image is nevertheless N-periodic. Its extra kernel must be retained. The formal free presentation near q=1 is not thereby a free periodic root module at every distant root. No new topological invariant is inferred. ## 6. The universal part of every tensor cut uses two Fourier moments The existing intrinsic cut formula also identifies its universal coefficient part for arbitrary strand count b>=2. At generic color the final highest roots are z_j=x^b Q^(-j), and an actual intertwiner has multiplicity-block traces A_j. Put C_b=-zeta_N/[x^(bN)-x^(-bN)], J_+(A)=sum_j Q^(-j)Tr A_j, J_-(A)=sum_j Q^j Tr A_j. The full original cut is exactly mathfrak_t_W(A)=C_b[q x^b J_+(A) -q^(-1)x^(-b)J_-(A)]. (6.1) This follows by substituting the modified-dimension numerator in the already proved full trace formula. It reduces the cut coefficients to at most two Fourier moments. It does not reduce the N-dimensional trace quotient or the knot's quantum-A module to dimension two. The block traces still depend on the entire braid and its centralizer transitions. There is also an exact parity statement. Since sigma(x)=qx and q^N=-1, sigma(C_b)=(-1)^b C_b. Every fixed-label weight d_(z_j), as a rational function of M, therefore satisfies [T^2-(-1)^b(q^b+q^(-b))T+1] d_(z_j)=0. (6.2) For even b the common frame is meridian-constant; for odd b its sign line remains. For even b the actual fusion labels also permute under the known meridian atlas. No generic EFK-module comparison for odd b is being asserted by (6.2). Individual Fourier moments can be polar in a singular fusion frame, so (6.1) must still be specialized as a whole. ## 7. Scope, coverage and checks This supplies an exact semilinear local source presentation and its comparison to the geometric dual cyclic model, with the marked period character and the actual normalization line kept. The earlier all-orders normal-block comparison can transport P_a to the dual of the corresponding actual formal normal line. It does not identify that line with the selected finite sum. The actual global source arrows, knot section, and central lattice at U=1 still have to be transported through sewing. The pole in C_N is genuine difference-constant period data; its cancellation cannot be inferred from a regular S-unit gauge. Nonzero pairing of the selected source with the geometric block, and its regulator norm across levels, remain unproved. In particular this note does not establish the global affine comparison equation for c_K,c_T. Modified-trace and formal difference-equation coverage is the existing coverage recorded in the preceding notes. No novelty claim is made for free resolutions, semilinear duality, or cyclic presentations. All displayed intertwiners and coefficient identities are proved by the direct calculations above. [The audit](../experiments/audit_equivariant_cut_source.py) checks the universal wall transport, relation transport, full free cyclic matrix, dual, stable branch line, quotient chain map and residue. Twelve generic original root cases at N=2,3,4,5,6,9 construct the actual E,F,K, original crossings and meridian matrices. All 116 projector cuts at both colors agree with (5.1); the full affine crossing identity and retained normalizer are checked. The N=2 extra kernel is recorded, not treated as periodicity of its free presentation. Four exact symbolic width checks retain the parity in (6.2). [Results](../experiments/equivariant_cut_source_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_equivariant_cut_source.py The subsequent [sewn-source theorem](sewn_source_and_meridian_charge.md) now transports the actual residue through arbitrary full knot operators and gives a regular rational lift of its projective corner. It also forces a further marking: one surviving meridian must carry charge three. Its step and full dimension factor are retained. The inverse complete longitude character above cannot distinguish that odd charge from charge one. The entire source and its selected geometric period still need comparison.

title: Equivariant peripheral roots and the remaining scalar period
text: # Equivariant peripheral roots and the remaining scalar period Research note, 25 October 2026. The local projective-frame theorem does not by itself choose compatible deck roots around a knot. This note supplies that compatibility and a scalar descent argument. Its inputs are the directly proved cyclic recoupling and frame identities; no global quantum-hyperbolic invariance theorem is assumed. Let W be a compact core of a one-cusped hyperbolic knot complement in S^3, Gamma=pi_1(W), and P=pi_1(partial W). The same proofs apply to more cusps with one copy of the peripheral data for each cusp. Let n be odd. Retain the ordered ideal vertices and all peripheral markings. Work on the nondegenerate decorated-representation locus described below. The conclusions concern finite-level algebraic tensors and their scalar phases. Identification of the selected literature period and its integration cycle, as well as its compatibility across levels, remains outstanding. ## 1. Root lines on Gamma/P are determined at the peripheral stabilizer First an elementary groupoid lemma. Let a group Gamma act transitively on V=Gamma/P. A Gamma-equivariant complex line over V is determined, up to equivariant isomorphism, by its one-dimensional P-representation chi on the fiber at v_0=P. The reconstruction is the associated line Gamma times_P C_chi -> Gamma/P. This can be checked by sending [g,z] to g.z in the fiber at gv_0; the relation [gp,z]=[g,chi(p)z] makes the map well defined and invertible. An equivariant n-th root line, with an identification of its n-th tensor power with this line, therefore amounts to a character delta:P->C^* such that delta^n=chi. Its isomorphism classes form a torsor for Hom(P,mu_n). For P=Z^2 with its marked meridian mu and longitude lambda, write M=chi(mu), L=chi(lambda). Every pair of roots m^n=M, l^n=L gives delta(mu^a lambda^b)=m^a l^b, and conversely. Thus the root-line cover has degree n^2 and deck group mu_n times mu_n. No semisimplicity of the full peripheral representation is needed: only its invariant line. At a complete unipotent or signed-unipotent character the same statement holds. The signs and the n^2 root choices are retained. These are isomorphism classes of roots of the decorating line. They do not classify the complete quantum period, its normalization phase, or its continuous dilogarithm factor. ## 2. An explicit multiplicative root of the projective denominator Choose an SL(2,C) lift rho of the decorated projective representation and a peripheral fixed point p_0. Put p_v=rho(r_v)p_0, where r_v in Gamma is a representative with r_v v_0=v and r_(v_0)=1. In an affine chart write d(g,p)=c_g p+d_g, rho(g)(p,1)=d(g,p)(rho(g)p,1). Choose a chart avoiding zero and infinity on the points in use. For a fixed representation the orbit is countable, so a complex frame can avoid the entire orbit. For algebraic families every finite diagram uses its own common nondegenerate Zariski open chart. We do not assume one finite open chart avoids every possible group-word denominator. The matrix multiplication identity gives exactly d(gh,p)=d(g,rho(h)p)d(h,p). (2.1) The peripheral character is chi(h)=d(h,p_0), h in P. Choose delta as in Section 1, and choose a_v with a_v^n=d(r_v,p_0), a_(v_0)=1. For g in Gamma define h(g,v)=r_(gv)^(-1)g r_v in P and set D(g,v)=a_(gv) delta(h(g,v))/a_v. (2.2) Substitution into (2.1) proves D(g,v)^n=d(g,p_v), D(g_1g_2,v)=D(g_1,g_2v)D(g_2,v). (2.3) For the second identity use h(g_1g_2,v)=h(g_1,g_2v)h(g_2,v). The intermediate a values cancel. This constructs the root cocycle; independently taking roots of the denominators would not prove the second equation. Changing a_v by zeta_v in mu_n changes D by the coboundary zeta_(gv)/zeta_v. Changing coset representatives gives an isomorphic root line. Conversely any such multiplicative D restricts to delta at v_0, so Section 1 proves that these are all root-line choices modulo object gauges. Internal root choices are frames, while the two peripheral characters remain actual data. For a finite diagram, every r_v is a fixed group word. Its matrix entries and d(r_v,p_0) are algebraic functions of the decorated representation; only finitely many n-th roots occur. Thus (2.2) is algebraic on its nondegenerate root chart. The construction on all configurations uses compatible charts; this statement does not assert that the entire quantum period lives on a degree-n^2 cover. An SL(2) lift exists for the knot group under discussion. The obstruction is the central two-cocycle obtained from arbitrary lifts of the projective matrices. Since W is aspherical, its class is in H^2(W;mu_2)=0: knot-exterior homology is H_1=Z, H_2=0, so the universal coefficient calculation gives zero. Trivializing that cocycle constructs a lift. Its two choices differ by a sign character of Gamma. For odd n, changing rho(g) by epsilon(g) and D(g,v) by the same epsilon(g) preserves (2.3). Ratios D(g,v_j)/D(g,v_i) are unchanged, so the triangle Weyl rescalings do not acquire an unrecorded sign from this lift choice. If peripheral coordinates are squared eigenvalues, their root cover is equivalent after choosing the lift: if u^n=chi^2, set delta=u^((n+1)/2)/chi. Then delta^n=chi and delta^2=u. The inverse is u=delta^2. This records the unhalved versus eigenvalue convention without dropping a sign. ## 3. The triangle transports can be made strictly equivariant The ideal vertices of the universal cover are Gamma/P. Assume the decorating map has infinite image; this holds on the non-elementary locus containing the geometric representation. Use configurations with distinct developing points. For each ordered triangle f=(i,j,k), lambda_f=(p_i-p_k)/(p_j-p_k). Equations (2.3) give compatible Weyl rescalings kappa(g,f)=D(g,j)/D(g,i), nu(g,f)=D(g,k)/D(g,i). Choose endpoint roots A_v^n=p_v. Choose a marked spectral root alpha on one representative of each triangle orbit, and propagate it by alpha_(gf)=kappa(g,f)alpha_f. The action on ordered triangles is free. Indeed P is malnormal in the hyperbolic knot group: a nontrivial element in two distinct conjugate maximal peripheral subgroups would be a parabolic fixing two distinct cusp points in the faithful geometric action, which is impossible. Thus an element fixing two distinct ideal vertices is the identity. In particular the propagation is well defined. It uses this property of the underlying knot group, not faithfulness of the variable rho. The explicit H K construction in `projective_frame_period_torsor.md` now yields unnormalized maps S(g,f) with the strict law S(g_1g_2,f)=S(g_1,g_2f)S(g_2,f). (3.1) Their determinant roots can also be chosen multiplicatively. For each free triangle orbit choose f_0, write f=r_f f_0 uniquely, and choose b_f^n=det(S(r_f,f_0))^(-1), with b_(f_0)=1. Set rho(g,f)=b_(gf)/b_f, S_hat(g,f)=rho(g,f)S(g,f). Then det S_hat=1 and (3.1) still holds exactly. Different b choices are scalar frame gauges. This removes a possible triangle-level composition anomaly constructively. It does not yet make arbitrary independent tetrahedron normalizations equivariant. ## 4. The remaining tetrahedral phase is an explicit cocycle Choose shared face roots xi and the signed Racah matrices R_hat as in the projective-frame note. They have determinant (-1)^((n-1)/2) and satisfy the ordered pentagon. For t=(0,1,2,3), define Delta(g,t) by R_hat(gt)(S_hat(g,023) tensor S_hat(g,012)) =Delta(g,t)(S_hat(g,013) tensor S_hat(g,123))R_hat(t). The previously proved ordered operator comparison and Schur argument prove that this scalar exists and is nonzero. Determinants give Delta(g,t) in A=mu_(n^2). (4.1) Here A is cyclic of order n^2; it is different from the peripheral deck group mu_n times mu_n. There is no reduction of A to mu_n being assumed in this note. Strict composition of S_hat gives Delta(gh,t)=Delta(g,ht)Delta(h,t). (4.2) Apply the ordered pentagon before and after g and cancel the common invertible S maps. Its scalar part gives product_(i=0)^4 Delta(g,t_without_i)^((-1)^i)=1. (4.3) Literal tensor permutations cause no extra scalar in this calculation; they occur on both sides of the same pentagon. Thus Delta is simultaneously a group one-cocycle and a configuration three-cocycle. ## 5. Why relative degree four is the relevant obstruction Let C_k be the free abelian group on ordered (k+1)-tuples of ideal vertices whose developing points are distinct, with alternating face boundary. Its augmented complex is exact. For any finite cycle choose one vertex whose developing point avoids its finitely many points; prepending it gives a cone, and boundary(cone)+cone(boundary)=identity. Infinite image of the decoration supplies that vertex. For k>=1 the Gamma action on C_k is free by malnormality. Also C_0=Z[Gamma/P]. With I=ker(C_0->Z), the complex ... -> C_3 -> C_2 -> C_1 -> I -> 0 is therefore a free Gamma-resolution. Its invariant cochains in degrees k>=2 compute H^k(Gamma,P;A). One can see the degree shift directly: Ext^(k-1)_Gamma(I,A) is computed at C_k; applying Hom and Ext to 0->I->Z[Gamma/P]->Z->0 gives the relative cohomology exact sequence, using the induced-module identification with P-cohomology. Both W and its boundary torus are aspherical with these fundamental groups. Their cellular resolutions identify this relative cohomology with H^k(W,partial W;A). In particular H^4(Gamma,P;A)=0, H^3(Gamma,P;A)=A. (5.1) The first equation follows from the dimension-three relative cellular complex. The second evaluates a cocycle on the oriented relative fundamental class. It also follows without a field assumption from H_3(W,partial W;Z)=Z and H_2(W,partial W;Z)=Z, both free. Thus the statement holds for composite n as well. ## 6. Scalar descent theorem and its residual period torsor Equations (4.1)--(4.3), freeness on tetrahedra, and (5.1) imply that the R_hat matrices admit A-valued corrections making both equivariance and the ordered pentagon exact. Here is a proof that retains the phase. Choose t_0 in each free tetrahedron orbit and put kappa(g t_0)=Delta(g,t_0)^(-1). By (4.2), replacing R_hat(t) by kappa(t)R_hat(t) makes the tensors equivariant. Its pentagon discrepancy is the four-cochain Omega=delta kappa. Equation (4.3) implies that Omega is Gamma-invariant, and delta Omega=1. The vanishing H^4 in (5.1) gives an invariant three-cochain b with delta b=Omega^(-1). Hence R_tilde(t)=kappa(t)b(t)R_hat(t) (6.1) is equivariant and satisfies the pentagon exactly. Its determinant is unchanged because the correction lies in mu_(n^2). Two such corrections differ by an invariant three-cocycle. Modulo shared-face scalar gauges, their choices form a torsor for H^3(Gamma,P;mu_(n^2))=mu_(n^2). (6.2) This residual value is measured on [W,partial W]. Choosing it is a global period normalization. Hilbert 90 for a field does not remove it. All phase corrections have absolute value one at each level; the generic nonconstant units removed in obtaining R_hat and S_hat remain recorded in their normalization lines. This proof is local in the algebraic parameter space. On a common irreducible root chart every phase in A is locally constant, so the cochain corrections may be chosen constant on that chart. Every finite recoupling diagram uses finitely many roots and such equations. We do not infer a finite degree for the full global period cover from the degree-n^2 peripheral root-line calculation. ## 7. What this closes, and the remaining comparison ### 7.1 The same descent retains arbitrary generic scalar units The scalar descent argument itself works for any abelian coefficient group B with trivial Gamma action. The free relative homology gives H^4(Gamma,P;B)=0 and H^3(Gamma,P;B)=B. Thus if the unnormalized intertwiners and Racah maps have scalar discrepancy in F^*, where F is their common algebraic function field, the same argument corrects equivariance and pentagon while retaining a residual F^* period torsor. Here Gamma acts on the configuration labels; the parameter field is fixed. This is not a theorem for an unspecified semilinear field action. The hypotheses hold for the unnormalized H K transports and raw pointed Racah maps above: their cocycle and pentagon are exact, and the ordered operator comparison makes the discrepancy scalar. Determinant normalization reduces this particular discrepancy to the finite phase subgroup considered in Sections 4--6. Before that normalization all generic units remain functions, including any peripheral factors. The function-field argument supplies rational sections generically, not a license to specialize a pole. This explains the proper treatment of a numerical move multiplier. Its value at a complete point does not identify its generic cochain, its residual period class, or the normalization selected by the literature state. A factor such as 1+M^n must remain in that generic comparison. No identification of the earlier positive factorial model with these operator tensors follows from the scalar theorem. An arbitrary F^* correction can change norms across levels; its exact period class must be fixed before claiming a volume law. ### 7.2 Scope The result supplies coherent global deck-root multipliers, strict triangle transports, and a scalar descent theorem for the local cyclic recoupling system. It isolates the remaining finite scalar normalization as a relative fundamental-class period. Tensor contraction with specified duality pairings is consequently equivariant, and ordered nondegenerate 2--3 recouplings have a common normalization. These assertions are uniform in the hyperbolic knot group and in every odd level. This is not yet a construction of the prescribed intrinsic knot state. The selected vectors, duality and vertex-order conventions, the global literature period/cycle, and the comparison between finite and continuous dilogarithm periods still have to be matched. A proof of connectedness for arbitrary admissible realizations is not supplied by the scalar cohomology calculation. The volume comparison across levels remains necessary and cannot be replaced by the finite phase normalization. The degree-n^2 peripheral cover and global character-cover framework are already present in Baseilhac--Benedetti, [Analytic families of quantum hyperbolic invariants](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.4261v3), Theorem 1.1 and Section 4. The purpose here is the direct root induction and relative scalar-obstruction proof within the specified local system, without assuming that paper's global invariance or asymptotic arguments.

title: Euler-factor source families and the literal crossing argument
text: # Euler-factor source families and the literal crossing argument 27 October 2026. Multiplying the actual primitive gauge period by one Euler factor gives an exactly solvable inverse-factor family. At the resonant shifts a=Q^r it transfers the selected local period from the Gaussian point 2 to the boundary point 0. This is a real source effect of an N-dependent unit, rather than an inference from its classical symbol. A further forward Euler factor has a nonreal formal critical pair; its selected asymptotic is not proved here. The Euler polynomial is literally the one in the original R-matrix. Its ARGUMENT must also be retained: the physical R atom and the right source variable are different operators. We prove this distinction, and give the exact literal signed crossing coefficients in the actual two-leg Borel fusion. No family below is substituted for the original knot invariant. ## 1. The actual atom and its right-source argument are distinct Fix q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^-1, N>=2. Write F_k=(Q;Q)_k, u_N(z)=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) z^k/F_k, v_N(z)=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) (-1)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2)z^k/F_k. In the normalized actual unchecked crossing the nilpotent factor is Theta=v_N(X), X=q rho^2 E_1 F_2, Theta^-1=u_N(X). (1) This follows coefficient by coefficient from the original coefficient q^(k(k-1)/2)rho^k/[k]_q!, since [k]_q!=q^(-k(k-1)/2)F_k/(1-Q)^k, rho(1-Q)=-q rho^2. It agrees with [the existing actual-atom proof](controlled_cyclic_euler_source.md). Every Cartan, flip, framing and peripheral line remains its original factor. Formula (1) does not replace that whole crossing by one scalar Euler function. The [actual source gauge](actual_source_fourier_twisted_traces.md) instead uses z=xf in the RIGHT coefficient algebra of Borel fusion. On the physical two-leg regular module its right operator has rank N(N-1). At the complete color, both E_1 and F_2 have rank N-1, so the physical X in (1) has rank (N-1)^2. Hence these two nilpotent operators cannot be similar for any N>=2. Their Euler units minus identity have the same respective ranks, because their linear coefficients are units and the remaining factor is invertible. Thus u_N(a z) below is an explicit actual-source COUPON using the same Euler polynomial as the literal inverse R atom. It cannot be called a complete crossing insertion by equating its argument with X. A whole crossing comparison has to carry its actual fusion, weight-diagonal factor and finite-path support as well. ## 2. Exact signed crossing coefficients in the actual Borel fusion In the actual two-leg fusion C, with z_(a,k)=f^a e_k, remove only the recorded common Cartan scalar kappa from the positive crossing. Its unique RIGHT coefficient is exactly a_+=sum_(a,k>=0,a+k<N) (-1)^k x^(-a-2k) Q^(k(k-1)/2) f^a e_k/F_a. (2) The inverse crossing, with scalar kappa^-1 recorded, has coefficient a_-=sum_(a,k>=0,a+k<N) (-1)^k x^(a+2k) Q^(-k(k-1)/2-ka) f^a e_k/F_a. (3) Here x is the actual same-color highest K eigenvalue and M=-qx; the formulas hold at fixed root for generic M and at completeness. They are not obtained by a numerical fit at M=1. For a direct proof of (2), the actual positive crossing sends e_0 tensor e_j to x^-j e_j tensor e_0. The fusion kernel is C_(u,v;a,k)=x^(u-a) F_a F_v/[F_(a-u)F_k], 0<=u<=a, v=k+a-u<N. It preserves the unwrapped total degree a+k=u+v. Fixing that degree j, solve its triangular system for the right coefficient. The finite Euler inverse convolution gives F_a [f^a e_k]a_+=(-1)^k x^(-a-2k)Q^(k(k-1)/2), a+k=j<N, and there are no coefficients with a+k>=N. This proves (2). The nonwrapped paths form a triangular subalgebra. Its diagonal weights are d_k=(-1)^k x^-2k Q^(k(k-1)/2); inversion of its Euler factor gives (3). It also follows by direct multiplication of (2) and (3) in the full actual coefficient algebra. The completed expression u_N(x^-1 f) D(H), D e_k=d_k e_k, has the same coefficients as (2) on nonwrapped paths. Its wrapped terms require their own source comparison; they may not be erased from a general inserted word simply because one two-leg cap kills them. At M=1 its Euler argument is x^-1 f=x^-2 z=Q z. (4) Thus the actual crossing's right Euler profile is related to the resonant a=Q case below, rather than an unmarked replacement of its argument by z. The diagonal D and the source-supported finite path information remain essential for the whole crossing. ## 3. The full inverse-factor family has a retained norm source Let g_N(z)=v_N(z)v_N(Qz) modulo z^N, w^-_(N,a)(z)=g_N(z)u_N(a z) modulo z^N, J^-_N(a)=[z^(N-1)]w^-_(N,a)(z). (5) All use their canonical degree-<N representatives. The exact parameter polynomial is J^-_N(a)=(1/N)sum_(k=0)^(N-1) product_(r=0)^(k-1)(a-Q^r). (6) To prove (6), the finite q-binomial coefficient identity gives [z^k]v_N(z)u_N(a z) =a^k(a^-1;Q)_k/F_k =product_(r=0)^(k-1)(a-Q^r)/F_k. It is polynomial at a=0 as well. The reflected coefficient of v_N(Qz) at degree N-1-k is F_k/N. Convolution cancels the remaining factorial and yields (6). Writing P_k(a)=product_(r=0)^(k-1)(a-Q^r), the identity P_k(Qa)=Q^k(a-Q^-1)P_(k-1)(a) and P_(k+1)(a)=(a-Q^k)P_k(a) yield the exact parameter transport J^-_N(Qa)=(Qa-1)(a-1)J^-_N(a) +(Qa/N)(2-a^N). (7) The complete norm P_N(a)=a^N-1 enters its derivation. The source 2-a^N cannot be replaced by its value at a marked point before transporting the parameter. The entire canonical wave in (5), before setting z^N=0, obeys (1-z)(1-Qz)w^-_(N,a)(Qz)-(1-a z)w^-_(N,a)(z) =[(a^N-2)/N]z^N+J^-_N(a)z^(N+1). (8) All lower coefficients follow from nilpotent Euler cancellation. For the degree-N coefficient, use the ordinary polynomial identities u_N(aQz)=(1-a z)u_N(a z)+a^N z^N/N and the full gauge Ward equation. Their source gives (a^N-2)/N. Truncating a product's degree-N tail does not change that coefficient because Q^N-1=0. The degree-N+1 coefficient is the displayed top period. This proves (8) without treating evaluation as a nilpotent character. For moments j_m=[z^(N-1)]z^m w^-_(N,a), (8) implies exactly j_(m+2)=(1+Q-aQ^(m+2))j_(m+1) +(Q^(m+2)-Q)j_m, j_0=J^-_N(a), j_1=(1+Q-aQ)J^-_N(a)+Q(a^N-2)/N. (9) The generic cleared classical source support is z(z+a-2)=0. That polynomial alone does not select its branch. ## 4. A proved source branch transfer at resonant inverse atoms For fixed r>=0 and N>r, take a=Q^r. Exact Euler transport gives w^-_(N,Q^r)(z)=v_N(Qz)(z;Q)_r modulo z^N. (10) For a fixed polynomial P, the BASE period on v_N(Qz) is L_N(P)=[z^(N-1)]P(z)v_N(Qz) =(1/N)sum_m [z^m]P(z) F_m, (11) once N exceeds its degree. Since F_0=1 and F_m=O_m(N^-m) for every fixed m>=1, (10)-(11) prove J^-_N(Q^r)=N^-1[1+O_r(N^-1)], [z^(N-1)]P(z)w^-_(N,Q^r)(z)/J^-_N(Q^r) -> P(0), (12) with error O_(P,r)(1/N). Its original period is nonzero for all sufficiently large N and has zero exponential rate. In particular J^-_N(1)=1/N, J^-_N(Q)=Q/N (13) exactly. Before adding this inverse factor, the gauge period is c_N~omega_N/sqrt(N), and its fixed polynomial observables select 2. After the factor the Gaussian leading component disappears and the evaluated boundary source selects 0. The actual finite period has not vanished; its leading source class has changed. At a=1 this can also be seen from the minimal Ward equation: w^-=v_N(Qz), so (1-Qz)w^-(Qz)-w^-(z)=-z^N/N. Its classical source support is only z=0. The extra root z=1 of the generic cleared polynomial z(z+a-2) at a=1 comes from an unremoved factor 1-z. It cannot be used as a selected critical point. Source saturation is necessary at the resonant atom, even though the multiplying Euler polynomial is a unit in the nilpotent algebra. Thus fixed-degree source selection cannot simply be extended to all Euler units. This is an exact family of source probes built from the actual atom polynomial. It is not a statement that a literal complete R crossing, including D(H), always destroys a Gaussian branch. ## 5. Adding a forward factor gives a different critical problem For completeness define the other actual-polynomial source probe w^+_(N,a)=g_N(z)v_N(a z) modulo z^N, J^+_N(a)=[z^(N-1)]w^+_(N,a), b^+_N(a)=[z^(N-2)]w^+_(N,a). Its full unreduced Ward equation is (1-z)(1-Qz)(1-a z)w^+_(N,a)(Qz)-w^+_(N,a)(z) =-[(2+a^N)/N]z^N +[(1+a+aQ^-1)J^+_N(a)-aQ^-1 b^+_N(a)]z^(N+1) -aJ^+_N(a)z^(N+2). (14) The degree-N source follows by multiplying the exact Euler and gauge Ward equations; it retains 2+a^N. The remaining two coefficients are read from the cubic factor and the top two canonical coefficients. This is an exact recursion/source statement, not an assertion about which critical class survives. At a=1 its classical equation is (1-z)^3=1. Besides the boundary root zero it has the two nonreal points z_+=3/2+i sqrt(3)/2, z_-=conjugate(z_+). On the marked upper branch, the coefficient action S_+(z)=3Li_2(z)-2pi*i Log z is stationary at z_+, since Log(1-z_+)=-2pi*i/3. Its imaginary part is exactly Im S_+(z_+)=3D(z_+)=2D(exp(pi*i/3)). (15) For example the cross-ratio triangle has angles pi/6,pi/6, 2pi/3, so D(z_+)=2Lambda(pi/6)-Lambda(pi/3)=2Lambda(pi/3). The elementary duplication identity gives (15). This is the same positive regulator number calibrated for the original figure-eight source in [its independent Bloch calculation](figure_eight_bloch_specialization.md). No selected asymptotic for J^+_N(1) is proved here. Numerical rate samples are saved as diagnostics only. Neither a nonreal formal critical point nor the equality of the regulator number in (15) identifies this universal source probe with a knot invariant or supplies its nonzero thimble coefficient. ## 6. Verification and critical-path consequence The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_euler_atom_source_family.py) and [saved results](../experiments/euler_atom_source_family_results.json) pass 23 levels, 115 parameter cases, both unreduced Ward families, the exact parameter transport and resonant fixed-observable selection formulas. Twelve literal crossing tests at complete and generic meridians verify (1)-(3) directly from the original color matrices and actual fusion. The rank mismatch of the two atom arguments is checked at every complete test. The inverse-family result gives a real source-branch transfer and identifies the exact resonant saturation that any full-word theorem must handle. The signed crossing formulas specify what is additionally needed to pass from the Euler function family to a literal crossing. Nothing here replaces the original state by a positive model, asserts new move invariance, or proves the general volume conjecture.

title: Squared-meridian descent and the signed cyclic norm
text: # Squared-meridian descent and the signed cyclic norm Research note, 26 October 2026. The actual reduced knot period is even in its meridian eigenvalue M. Its specified quantum operator therefore descends to Y=M^2. At q=exp(pi*i/N), the cyclic extension then has degree N, matching the parameter Q=q^2 in the actual factorials. The full ADO period retains a sign line at even levels. These exact statements do not identify a root central curve with the geometric A-curve or establish the selected volume limit. The input is the actual state and exact insertion proved in [the longitude/action note](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md). The general norm theorem remains [the intrinsic construction](intrinsic_quantum_a_norm_torsor.md). ## 1. The exact insertion uses the squared meridian For a b-strand knot braid of writhe w put kappa_D=w-b+1; it is even. Let q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, Y=M^2=Qx^2. At a crossing with input indices a,b and shift k set A=Q^a, B=Q^b, C=Q^k. The exact insertion is L_D(q,Y;s)=q^(-kappa_D) product_positive (1-YC/A)/(BC(1-Y/A)) product_negative A(1-YC/B)/(1-Y/B). (1.1) Indeed x^(-w)=product_crossings x^(-sign). Each factor cancels x against tau_sign^(-1) in the longitude note. Its integer-position coboundary already fixes the q-phase; no square root is being chosen. The finite identities are therefore F_N(q^j M)=sum_s W_N(M;s) product_(r=0)^(j-1)L_D(q,Q^rY;s). (1.2) At special meridians this means the whole cancelled inserted weight. ## 2. Each closed state has cyclic norm one Here A^N=B^N=C^N=1. The elementary identity product_(r=0)^(N-1)(1-Q^r z)=1-z^N proves, as rational identities, product_r (1-Q^rYC/A)/(BC(1-Q^rY/A))=1, product_r A(1-Q^rYC/B)/(1-Q^rY/B)=1. The remaining framing norm is q^(-N*kappa_D)=(-1)^kappa_D=1. Thus Norm_(Y->QY,N)(L_D)=1. (2.1) Take j=N in (1.2). Since q^N=-1, this gives F_N(-M)=F_N(M). (2.2) This applies to every knot and every N>=2, with no positivity, alternatingness, primality, or parity restriction. At Y^N=1 cancel the rational norm first; do not evaluate two vanishing products. A direct proof also works for the auxiliary finite closed lift. The finite formulas show that a closed state's total x-power is E=(N-1)kappa_D +sum_positive(-a-b-k)+sum_negative(a+b-k). All other x-dependence is through Qx^2. Modulo two, either crossing's contribution is c-a, where c is its first output index. The integer position coboundary proves sum_crossings(c-a)=0. Hence E is even. After x=-q^(-1)M the lift uses only Q,Y. This last assertion about a finite lift does not imply q-sign stability of the all-level minimal operator on the specified sequence of roots. ### A nonzero actual annihilator can nevertheless be chosen over Q=q^2 The auxiliary finite lift is enough for an existence statement which does not assert that minimal-operator symmetry. There is a nonzero specified all-level operator P_K(Q,Y,T) in ℚ(Q,Y)[T;sigma], sigma(Y)=QY, (2.3) annihilating the original reduced F_N at Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N), outside a finite set of coefficient poles. No full-state sign or modified-dimension factor is removed by this assertion. Here is the construction. The finite closed lift has a sum of individual closed-state weights. Rewrite its crossings by the exact Q-Pochhammer formulas in the relative octahedral note. All entries apart from a monomial in x are rational functions of Q and Qx^2=Y. The monomial's total exponent is E above. Its parity proof is statewise and holds for generic q: kappa_D is even and sum(c-a)=0 on the entire integral closed-flow lattice. Thus E/2 is integral on that lattice. In an integral lattice basis, x^E=(Y/Q)^(E/2) has integral exponents; the remaining Q exponents are integer-valued quadratic forms. We obtain an actual finite lift G_N(Q,Y) in ℚ(Q)[Y^(+/-1)] with proper Q-Pochhammer factors, the same integer support and the same boundary faces. Its value at Q_N is exactly F_N(Y). Apply the already proved filtered shift-span and finite-moment argument in [the finite-sum proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md), now with base Q, meridian Y, shift Y->QY and central variable Z=Q^N. Its alignment condition holds with Pochhammer step one. It gives a nonzero operator A(Y,Z,T) over ℚ(Q). Strip its largest common central factor (Z-1)^h before specialization. For each fixed N, Q^N-1 is a nonzero rational function of generic Q, so this stripping preserves the exact off-root identity for G_N. At Q=Q_N all factorial lengths are less than N and are regular. Setting Z=1 therefore gives the nonzero operator (2.3). This argument constructs an actual annihilator over the smaller parameter field. It does not prove that the annihilator ideal defined only on the selected half-roots is invariant under q->-q, nor that its old minimal generator descends. One can instead work with the specified operator (2.3), or with the minimal generator in the nonzero ideal over C(Q,Y). All finite lifts have rational coefficients in Q. Their root identities therefore have the expected Galois conjugates at the other primitive Q-roots. This supplies the correct parameter setting for a cyclotomic-curvature comparison. It does not show identity of the entire cyclic transport, existence of its geometric comparison line, or the selected regulator norm. ## 3. The actual minimal meridian operator descends Let I be the actual all-level annihilator ideal in R_M=C(q,M)[T;sigma], sigma(M)=qM. It is nonzero by [the finite cut-state proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md). The involution iota(M)=-M, iota(q)=q, iota(T)=T commutes with sigma. Equation (2.2) implies iota(I)=I: evaluate any actual annihilating equation at -M. Coefficient specializations are understood after clearing denominators, as in that all-level definition. Every coefficient decomposes uniquely as a_0(q,Y)+M*a_1(q,Y). Thus P=P_0+M P_1 in I implies P_0=(P+iota(P))/2 and M P_1=(P-iota(P))/2 are in I, and so is P_1. The descended ideal in R_Y=C(q,Y)[T;sigma], sigma(Y)=q^2Y is consequently nonzero. If P is the unique monic least-order operator in I, P-iota(P) has smaller order and is zero. Its coefficients lie in C(q,Y); minimal order is unchanged by the descent. The full state also gives an iota-stable ideal: its parity scalar (-1)^(N-1) is nonzero and cancels in the same argument at every level. Its shift gauge is rational in q,Y. No descent in q is inferred. Classically, twisting an SL(2) knot representation by the sign character of its abelianization sends M to -M and fixes the preferred longitude. The full lifted peripheral locus descends to (Y,L). Individual irreducible lift components may be exchanged by this twist; their separate evenness is not assumed. ## 4. The natural root norm torsor has degree N At a level where its leading/trailing coefficients and companion specialization are defined and nonzero, specialize the descended specified module at q_N. On C(Y) write T=B(Y)sigma, sigma(Y)=Q_NY. Its order is N, and H_N=B(Y)B(Q_NY)...B(Q_N^(N-1)Y), D_N(U,W)=det(W-H_N), U=Y^N=M^(2N). (4.1) Translation conjugates H_N by B, so D_N belongs to C(U)[W]. On a simple spectral component with function field k, set S=k[Y]/(Y^N-U). The eigenline has rank one over this cyclic etale algebra. In a frame T e=a e and Norm_(S/k)(a)=W. Thus the norm torsor has dimension N-1. The intrinsic Hilbert-90 comparison and cyclic stable lattice apply with this N, retaining apparent poles and the pointing. The reduced rational period in Y forces a W=1 sector. This identifies neither that sector nor D_N with the geometric classical A-curve. Matching the order of the factorial parameter does not identify the fixed-center and fixed-semiclassical-shape trajectories. ## 5. The full ADO period retains the even-level sign The independently fixed full normalization is d_N(M)=eta_N M^(N-1)/S_N(Y), S_N(Y)=1+Y+...+Y^(N-1), eta_N=i^(N+3). Consequently d_N(-M)=delta_N d_N(M), delta_N=(-1)^(N-1). Its rational shift gauge factors as g(q,Y)=-q^(-1)(QY-1)/(Y-1) =kappa(q)*sigma(f)/f, kappa(q)=-q^(-1), f=Y-1. (5.1) At the actual root kappa=q^(N-1), and exactly Norm_N(g)=kappa^N=delta_N. (5.2) The full state has W=delta_N: W=-1 at even N and W=1 at odd N. After the explicit constant-character twist kappa, the remaining Hilbert-90 comparison is the rational frame f. The entire scalar is d_N(M)=eta_N M^(N-1)(1-Y)/(1-U). (5.3) Retain its central factor and germ at U=Y=1; d_N(1)=eta_N/N. At even N the full period is a section of this parity line over the quadratic M-cover, rather than a rational function of Y. For rank d, the scalar twist gives, up to companion-frame gauge, H_N^full=delta_N H_N^reduced, D_N^full(U,W)=delta_N^d D_N^reduced(U,W/delta_N). (5.4) These are signed root norm identities, not classical A-polynomial identities. They retain the factors lost by an unmarked comparison of norm-one sectors. ## 6. The former 2N norm is the square of this one Extend the same module to C(M), with sigma(M)=q_NM. Its coefficients still depend only on Y and sigma^N(Y)=Y. Therefore H_(2N)=H_N^2, D_(2N)(U,V)=(-1)^d Res_W(D_N(U,W),W^2-V). (6.1) Over a splitting field the latter is the elementary identity product_i(V-lambda_i^2)=(-1)^d product_i(lambda_i^2-V), so it holds also with repeated eigenvalues. The former 2N-description retains V=W^2; the N-description retains the sign W=delta_N. No sign has been removed by a numerical evaluation at M=1. ## 7. The regulator conversion agrees with the actual half-step Put H=Log Q=2pi*i/N, u=Log M. The action in the longitude note obeys dS_Q=2 Log(L) du, equivalently dS_Q=Log(L) dLog(Y). The full geometric peripheral rows are m=Y,l=L^2, whose exponent determinant in (Y,L) is two. Hence the marked regulator is R=S_Q-(1/2)Log(Y)Log(L)=S_Q-u Log(L). (7.1) This is the action already calibrated by Im S_Q=Vol at completeness. In the original M-shift parameter h=Log q=H/2, the action is S_q=S_Q/2 and the peripheral exponent determinant is four. Both give the same exponential and invariant regulator norm. This resolves a parameter and parity conversion, not selection or cancellation in the finite period. The subsequent [integral half-longitude theorem](integral_half_longitude.md) now realizes this conversion directly in the saturated edge lattice: the preferred longitude has a unique integral half-class and pairs by -1 with the actual marked meridian. Its Weyl lift satisfies TY=QYT at every level. The square of that lift retains an explicit edge character, and at even N its central sign cannot be changed by replacing T with -T. This supplies the marked boundary algebra; the actual central lift and selected source still require matching. ## 8. Verification [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_even_meridian_descent.py) compares 40 dense cut matrices at generic auxiliary parameters and actual roots. It checks local longitude norms and the full sign at ten levels including even and composite ones, and symbolically verifies the spectral square identity in ranks one through three. All checks passed; the proofs above are uniform. Results are in [the audit output](../experiments/even_meridian_descent_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_even_meridian_descent.py

title: The balanced source normalizer is fixed by its compact Fermat divisor
text: # The balanced source normalizer is fixed by its compact Fermat divisor 28 October 2026. The explicit balanced finite source fixes the entire central periodic factor in the trivalent quantum-beta section. For the actual root and the original full-function marks one has EXACTLY A_N(u)=(N/phi_N) u^N Psi_+(h-Log u), h=2pi*i/N, phi_N=sqrt(N)exp{i*pi[1/4-(N+N^(-1))/12]}. (1) The factor u^N is indispensable. This is an identity of the actual local source, not a choice of normalization or a comparison after dividing by an unknown knot invariant. The proof uses a compact algebraic curve and its divisor; no asserted published Fourier or cyclic-dilogarithm evaluation is a premise. ## 1. The exact statement on a balanced source Let Q=exp h and u^N-w^N=1. The actual polynomial is B_N(u,w)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1) product_(j<a)(u-Q^j w). Its [positive Fourier norm](actual_sink_source_convolution.md#2-balanced-nonvanishing-and-its-exact-positive-norm-ratio) proves B_N!=0 whenever w!=0, including u=0. Take z=Log u and c=Log(w/u), with compatible marked continuations. The identity equivalent to (1) is B_N(u,w)=(N/phi_N)u^N Psi_+(h-z)Psi_+(c) exp(-cz/h). (2) The left side is the ORIGINAL finite polynomial. All full-Psi marks and the scalar on the right are the ones already fixed by its defining integral and original coefficient moments. Initially take real u>1 and real positive w=(u^N-1)^(1/N). Set t=u^(-1), s=w/u, so s^N+t^N=1 with 0<s,t<1. Let D_N(y)=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^j y)^(j/N) with every factor anchored at y=0. The independently proved rational full-function identity reads Psi_+(L)=exp[i Li_2(exp(NL))/(2pi*N)] (1-exp(NL))^(1+iL/(2pi))/D_N(exp L). (3) Use Psi_+(h-z)=Psi_+(-z)/(1-t). Euler's ordinary dilogarithm identity for s^N+t^N=1 then cancels ALL logarithmic cross terms in the proposed right side of (2). It becomes B_cand=K_N s^N/[(1-t)D_N(s)D_N(t)], K_N=(N/phi_N)exp[i*pi/(12N)]. (4) For example the dilogarithm sum is pi^2/6+N^2cz; the two binomial powers in (3) and exp(-cz/h) cancel that cz term exactly. No transcendental central factor is left in the Nth power of (4): B_cand^N=K_N^N s^(N^2)/[(1-t)^N product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^j s)^j product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^j t)^j]. (5) Thus (5) is a rational function on the compact Fermat curve. ## 2. The divisor of the ACTUAL finite polynomial Use the smooth projective curve C_N: s^N+t^N=1. It is connected: its affine polynomial is Eisenstein over C[t] at t-1. In these coordinates the actual finite function is B_N=sum_(a=0)^(N-1)t^(-a)(s;Q)_a. (6) Its only possible zeros or poles are at s=0, t=0 or infinity. Away from those loci u,w are finite nonzero, and the exact Fourier recurrence proves B_N!=0. At infinity u=0 and w^N=-1; the same recurrence still has every coefficient nonzero, so B_N is finite and nonzero there as well. At s=0,t=Q^j, one has u=Q^(-j), w=0. The order of B_N is exactly j, for j=0,...,N-1. To prove this, write B_N(u,w)=sum_k b_k(u)w^k. Its finite source recurrence gives (uQ^k-1)b_k=Q^(k-1)b_(k-1), 1<=k<N. At u=Q^(-j), the coefficients before k=j vanish; the top coefficient is nonzero, so b_j!=0 by backward recurrence. For j=0 the constant is N. Along the Fermat curve the perturbation of u has order N in w, which does not change this first nonzero order j<N. At t=0,s=Q^(-k), the order is a POLE of order k, k=0,...,N-1. Indeed s-Q^(-k) has order N in t. In (6), terms a>k therefore have order at least N-a>0, while among a<=k the unique highest pole is a=k with nonzero coefficient. For k=0, B_N tends to one. These calculations also cover every composite and even level. The divisor of B_N^N is consequently: zero order Nj at s=0,t=Q^j, pole order Nk at t=0,s=Q^(-k), with no other zeros or poles. Orders zero mean ordinary nonzero values, not deleted points. ## 3. The candidate has the same divisor, including infinity Read the orders directly from (5). At s=0,t=Q^j, j!=0, t-Q^j has order N in s. The only vanishing t-factor is j'=N-j, with exponent N-j. The numerator has order N^2. The net zero order is N^2-N(N-j)=Nj. At j=0 the factor (1-t)^N instead has order N^2, cancelling the numerator. At t=0,s=Q^(-k), k!=0, the only vanishing s-factor is j'=k, with order Nk; it gives the required pole. At k=0 no such factor occurs. At infinity both s,t have simple poles. The numerator has degree N^2 and the denominator has degree N+2 sum_(j=1)^(N-1)j=N^2, with nonzero leading coefficients. Thus (5) has neither a zero nor a pole there. Therefore B_N^N/B_cand^N is a rational function on the compact connected C_N with no zero or pole. It is constant. Its constant and its Nth root are fixed by a marked source value, not a free scalar. Take t->0,s->1 on the initial positive branch. Equation (6) gives B_N->1. Also c=(1/N)Log(1-u^(-N))=-u^(-N)/N+O(u^(-2N)), Psi_+'(0)=-Psi_+(h)=-phi_N. The latter follows directly from Psi_+(c+h)=Psi_+(c)/(1-exp c) and its nonzero marked value. Thus the right side of (2) tends to one as well. The constant in the Nth powers is one; their continuous Nth-root ratio is one on this marked branch. Analytic continuation proves (2), and hence (1). Every deck factor is consistent. Increasing c by h changes w to Qw and multiplies BOTH sides of (2) by 1/(u-w), by the balanced finite source equation and the full-Psi shift. Increasing c or z by 2pi*i has its complete central multiplier canceled by exp(-cz/h). Thus the asserted continuation keeps the original source rather than selecting an independent norm-one trivialization. ## 4. The actual trivalent source now has no unknown periodic factor For the original chamber Im u<0, Im(v/u)>0, put c=Log(v/u). The [exact beta source](actual_trivalent_quantum_beta_source.md) is therefore explicitly B_N(u,v)=S_N(u,v)+(1-u^N+v^N)I_N(u,v), S_N=(N/phi_N)u^N Psi_+(h-Log u)Psi_+(c) exp(-c Log u/h). (7) There is an exact version in the ORIGINAL reflected field variables. Write z=Log U, c_0=Log(V/U), and retain the actual tags u=Q^2U,v=QV with Log u=z+2h and c=c_0-h. The backward full-Psi shift gives the balanced part of its constant coefficient as C_N^(bal)(U,V)=Q^(2-d)/phi_N *U^(N+1)(U-Q^(-1))(U-Q^(-1)V)/V^2 *Psi_+(-z)Psi_+(c_0)exp(-c_0 z/h), d=N-1. (7a) Its remaining ORIGINAL current is exactly C_N^(current)=Q^(-d)/N*(1-U^N+V^N)I_N(Q^2U,QV). (7b) Indeed Psi_+(-z-h)=(1-Q^(-1)/U)Psi_+(-z) and Psi_+(c_0-h)=(1-Q^(-1)V/U)Psi_+(c_0); expanding the Gaussian accounts for Q^2 U^3/V^2. Thus the full physical right shapes are literally 1/U and V/U. The boundary polynomial, central U^N, Gaussian and Q^(2-d) remain. The bare fiber has the expected nonzero N^(-1/2) factor phi_N^(-1). These equations are at the original physical root; no off-root replacement of Q^N or of its derivatives is being asserted. Here I_N is its specified upward Barnes contour and is uniformly O(1) on compact positive boundary families. Equation (7) retains the original current; it does not assert that it is negligible for every positive bipyramid. The full-Psi strip estimate now gives the residue rate on the ENTIRE chamber, including |u|=1 and geometric clock rotations. Uniformly on compact subsets, log|S_N|=N Lambda(u,v)+O(log N), Lambda=[ImLi_2(v/u)-ImLi_2(u) +(pi-Arg(v/u))log|u|-Arg(u)log|v|]/(2pi). (8) Both full-function arguments in (7) stay in regular angular strips. The central source u^N in (7) supplies log|u| to the rate; omitting it changes (8). There is no Diophantine small-factor estimate hidden at |u|=1. In fact the ENTIRE leading block is explicit. The exact shift Psi_+(h-Log u)=Psi_+(-Log u)/(1-u^(-1)) and the uniform full-function symbol give S_N=(N/phi_N) (1-v/u)^(1/2)/(1-u^(-1))^(1/2) exp{[Li_2(v/u)+Li_2(1/u)-Log(v/u)Log u +2pi*i Log u]/h} *[1+O(1/N)]. (8a) All square roots and dilogarithms inherit their original upper-strip marks. The factor N/phi_N retains its exact phase and has modulus sqrt(N). Both shapes v/u and 1/u are upper. The half-density in (8a) is consequently nonzero and bounded above and below, after dividing by sqrt(N), on every compact positive boundary family. The affine 2pi*i Log u term is the retained central source, not an arbitrarily added choice of classical action. Consequently every compact family with Lambda>max(0,log|u|,log|v|) by a fixed positive margin has ORIGINAL local source B_N=S_N(1+O(N^C exp(-eta N))). This extends the local [positive-norm growth theorem](actual_sink_source_convolution.md) beyond its elementary |u|<1 product estimate. The exact actual Q shifts u=Q^2U,v=QV and its NQ^d normalization are carried by that theorem unchanged. Thus in the gap chamber the actual local source has exactly the growing two-face block (8a), with relative error O(1/N)+O(N^C exp(-eta N)). This supplies its nonzero leading coefficient rather than postulating the survival of a saddle. This is an exact local torsor/source normalization followed by a local noncancellation theorem. A broad knot proof still requires a simultaneous positive-chart and exterior-cycle comparison putting the actual relevant fibers in this gap chamber, or retaining their other currents by another method. The companion audit checks the full-Psi normalizer against the ACTUAL balanced finite source at both |u|<1 and |u|>1. The divisor argument, not finite numerical agreement, proves the all-level identity above.

title: Audit of the exact quantum clock shear and its actual root source
text: # Audit of the exact quantum clock shear and its actual root source Independent proof audit, 27 October 2026. The finite diagonal operator below exactly quantizes the smooth symmetric-frame sphere shear. At the marked root it is the entire previously proved balanced-to-symmetric coordinate change. Its off-root quantum-factorial residual and first normal jets remain essential. Use [the actual global q-difference source](integral_color_global_q_difference_source.md) and [the factorial-frame theorem](quantum_factorial_frames_and_cyclotomic_source.md). No geometric R-intertwiner or global selected-volume claim is inferred. ## 1. Exact finite star automorphism Let n=N-1, J x^j=jx^j, and put q=exp(s/(2N)), m=q^N, M=-m, U_j=q^[Nj-j(j+1)/2], U_0=1. (1) The coherent-symbol map sigma is injective: after multiplying by its incidence denominator, distinct matrix units have distinct monomials v^i z^j. Its exact star product is sigma(A)*sigma(B)=sigma(AB). Thus sigma(A) -> sigma(U A U^(-1)) (2) is a global automorphism of that finite star algebra for every N. For imaginary s it is unitary in the Euclidean metric and in the diagonal coherent metric. It preserves the exact normalized trace. Let a_hat=J_-/n, b_hat=J_+/n and T_hat=J/n, where J_-x^j=jx^(j-1), J_+x^j=(n-j)x^(j+1). The adjacent ratio is U_j/U_(j-1)=m q^(-j). Hence the two transformed entries are j m^(-1)q^j/n and (n-j)m q^(-j-1)/n. Exact binomial summation gives sigma(U a_hat U^(-1)) =m^(-1)q a[1+(q-1)T]^(n-1), sigma(U b_hat U^(-1)) =m q^(-1)b[1+(q^(-1)-1)T]^(n-1), sigma(U T_hat U^(-1))=T, (3) with a=z/(1+vz), b=v/(1+vz), T=vz/(1+vz). Their uniform fixed-derivative limits are a/r,r b,T, where r=exp[s(1-T)/2]. In the affine source coordinates (v,a) this is exactly Psi_s(v,a)=(rv,a/r). The elementary uniform logarithm estimate used for the global generator symbols proves the O(1/N) error. For imaginary s the map sends the same real compact sphere to itself, with its orientation and clock preserved. The quantum clock assertion is exact, not just principal: U commutes with J, q^J, Q^J, K, every polynomial index moment, and every diagonal endpoint projector. In particular both literal wall probes E_00,E_nn survive unchanged. The rank-one cut coupon is not fixed; it is conjugated by (2). ## 2. The whole actual frame comparison and the original source The actual regular basis-vector frame is h_j=D_j w_j, D_j=(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)/2]/{n choose j}_q. Its coordinate change is D^(-1). Direct multiplication gives D_j U_j=M^j/{n choose j}_q, D^(-1)=U V, V_j={n choose j}_q/M^j. (4) At q=q_N, M=1 and {N-1 choose j}_(q_N)=1. Consequently U_(q_N)=D_(q_N)^(-1) (5) exactly for every parity and every entry. Thus (2) at that root is the literal actual balanced-to-symmetric frame conjugation, with all tensor crossing operators transported by the same U. This is stronger than a principal-symbol comparison, but is a change of actual source frame rather than a geometric holonomy intertwiner. The balanced source transforms exactly as psi_h=U ones, phi_h=ones^t U^(-1)/N, Gamma_h=U Gamma U^(-1). (6) The cup and its dual basis are transported inversely. Both actual diagonal pivots commute with U, and their original twists and normalization lines are retained. Thus the whole root pointed network is the original one in the symmetric frame. Off the root, the full coordinate change is U V and cannot be replaced by U if the target is that specified symmetric frame. The top value is also exact: U_n=q^[N(N-1)/2], U_n(q_N)=i^(N-1)=i^(N+3)=epsilon_N. (7) The exponent N(N-1)/2 is an integer, so no hidden square-root choice occurs in (7). This is the original phase already present in the quantum-factorial frame, identified as one extreme source weight. It does not determine the full modified-dimension line or authorize deleting any other scalar factor of the network. ## 3. Its residual has nonzero root-normal jets Although V_j(q_N)=1, its first q-logarithmic derivative is [q partial_q Log V_j]_(q_N) =-Nj+iN sum_(r=1)^j cot(pi*r/N). (8) For a proof, write the q-binomial as product_(r=1)^j [N-r]_q/[r]_q. The logarithmic derivative of [k]_q is k coth(k Logq)-coth(Logq). At Logq=pi*i/N, coth((N-r)Logq)=-coth(r Logq), so each binomial factor contributes -N coth(r Logq)=iN cot(pi*r/N). The M^j denominator contributes -Nj, proving (8). These jets need not be small as N grows. For example V_n=M^(-n), so its derivative is exactly -Nn even though its root value is one. Thus U is the complete root frame, not a replacement for the whole off-root source comparison or its normal connection. The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_exact_clock_shear_star_automorphism.py) checks the symbols, star multiplication/source covariance, full clock and endpoint projectors, actual root frame and phase, and the residual derivatives.

title: An exact factorial interpolation for the original selected contours
text: # An exact factorial interpolation for the original selected contours 28 October 2026. The original finite quantum factorials admit an explicit holomorphic interpolation with a uniform complex dilogarithm expansion. This permits a contour representation of the ACTUAL finite state sum without replacing a finite Euler polynomial by its wrong exterior branch. The lattice values, reflection phase and original support cycle are all retained. A contour carrying a nonzero geometric saddle is still required; the interpolation does not select that saddle by itself. This is within the existing Barnes/double-sine analytic-difference framework, not a novelty claim for a special function. For coverage see [Ruijsenaars, On Barnes' Multiple Zeta and Gamma Functions](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/2100) and [Narukawa, multiple sine functions and elliptic gamma functions](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306164). Only coverage is used from those papers. The product, normalization, functional identities and asymptotic comparison needed here are proved below directly. They concern the ORIGINAL root factorial, not a newly normalized knot state. ## 1. A convergent whole function with the exact lattice values Fix an integer N>=2, Q=exp(2 pi i/N). On the strip -1<Re z<N define G_N(z)=(2 pi/N)^z Gamma(z+1) * product_(k>=1) Gamma(Nk+z+1)/[Gamma(Nk-z)(Nk)^(2z+1)]. (1) All positive-base powers use the real logarithm. Each Gamma argument has positive real part in this strip. On every compact z set the logarithm of the kth factor is O_(N,K)(k^-2): in the Gamma-ratio expansion the 1/k term cancels. More explicitly, its leading term is -z(z+1)(2z+1)/(6N^2 k^2). The product and its logarithmic derivatives therefore converge locally uniformly. It is holomorphic and nonzero on the strip and G_N(0)=1. Gamma's functional equation gives on overlapping strips G_N(z+1)/G_N(z) =(2 pi/N)(z+1) product_(k>=1)[1-(z+1)^2/(N^2 k^2)] =2 sin(pi(z+1)/N). (2) The last equality is the ordinary convergent sine product. This also gives the meromorphic continuation of (1). Define the marked factorial Fhat_N(z)=exp[i pi z(z+1)/(2N)-i pi z/2] G_N(z). (3) Then EXACTLY Fhat_N(z+1)=[1-Q^(z+1)] Fhat_N(z), Fhat_N(0)=1, Fhat_N(n)=(Q;Q)_n, 0<=n<N, (4) where Q^z always means exp(2 pi i z/N). In particular the interpolation is attached to the original finite state before any asymptotic choice. For any marked alpha and nonnegative integer n where the ratio is regular, (4) also gives Fhat_N(alpha+n)/Fhat_N(alpha)=(Q^(alpha+1);Q)_n. (5) Thus color-shifted factorials have the same exact interpolation. Their whole meridian marks and original prefactors remain part of the state. This is a fixed-root identity, not a moving-q normal-jet theorem. ## 2. Reflection is exact, with no undetermined periodic factor The whole sine product satisfies G_N(z)G_N(N-1-z)=N. (6) Here is a proof that fixes a possible periodic ambiguity. Differentiate the logarithm of the left side using (1), initially on the stated strip. Writing psi for the logarithmic derivative of Gamma, the partial sum through k=K telescopes to psi(NK+z+1)-psi(N(K+1)-z). It tends to zero locally uniformly as K tends to infinity. Hence the left side is constant. At z=0 its value is the literal product product_(j=1)^(N-1)2sin(pi j/N)=N, obtained by evaluating the derivative of t^N-1 at t=1. This proves (6). The corresponding marked identity is Fhat_N(z)Fhat_N(N-1-z) =N exp[i pi z(z-N+1)/N]. (7) The phase in (7) cannot be discarded in a complex contour deformation. ## 3. A finite Barnes-G formula for independent computation Let B denote the Barnes G function with B(1)=1 and B(w+1)=Gamma(w)B(w), normalized by its convergent Weierstrass product. The infinite product (1) equals the finite expression G_N(z)=(2 pi/N)^z Gamma(z+1) * product_(r=0)^(N-1) B(1+(r-z)/N)/B(1+(r+z+1)/N). (8) For completeness its scalar is fixed, not inferred from a recurrence. Apply Gamma multiplication to each factor of (1), and put a_r=(r+z+1)/N, b_r=(r-z)/N. The product through k=K becomes the right side of (8) times H_K=Gamma(K+1)^(-(2z+1)) product_r B(K+1+a_r)/B(K+1+b_r). One has H_K(0)=1 by telescoping in r. Direct differentiation of the defining Weierstrass product gives d/dw log B(1+w)=w psi(1+w)-w-1/2+(1/2)log(2 pi). The ordinary uniform digamma expansion on a positive large argument therefore gives partial_z log H_K=O_Kcompact(1/K), since sum_r(a_r+b_r)=N. Integrating from zero to z proves H_K->1. This establishes (8) with scalar one; it does not require a quoted multiple-Gamma normalization theorem. ## 4. Uniform complex asymptotics, including the first correction Let K be any compact subset of 0<Re x<1. Define the analytic primitive J(x)=integral_0^x Log(2sin(pi t)) dt, continued from 0<x<1, with its integrable logarithmic endpoint at zero. The sine has positive real part on this strip, so its indicated logarithm is single-valued there. Uniformly on K, log G_N(Nx) =N J(x)+(1/2)Log(2N sin(pi x)) +pi cot(pi x)/(12N)+O_K(N^-3). (9) The logarithm and square-root marks are the ones positive on the real interval. Every fixed derivative also satisfies the corresponding uniform remainder bound on a smaller compact set. ### Direct proof with a summable remainder Use the elementary Gamma Stirling expansion through 1/(12w), with remainder O(|w|^-3) in a closed right-half-plane sector. That remainder bound follows, for example, by integrating the bounded periodic fourth Bernoulli polynomial in the Euler summation remainder; its integral is bounded by a constant times integral_0^infinity|w+t|^-4 dt. For x in K all arguments Nx and N(k+x),N(k-x) remain in such a sector, uniformly in k. The kth logarithmic factor in (1) becomes N phi_k(x)+(1/2)Log(1-x^2/k^2) +(1/(12N))[1/(k+x)-1/(k-x)] +O_K(N^-3 k^-3), where phi_k(x)=(k+x)Log(1+x/k)-(k-x)Log(1-x/k)-2x. The remainders are summable. Since phi_k(0)=0 and phi_k'(x)=Log(1-x^2/k^2), the sine product sums the leading terms to J(x) after including the Gamma(Nx+1) factor. It likewise sums the half-logarithms to (1/2)Log(2N sin(pi x)). Finally 1/x+sum_(k>=1)[1/(k+x)-1/(k-x)]=pi cot(pi x) gives the displayed 1/N term. This proves (9) with the stated uniform remainder. Cauchy's formula proves the derivative assertion. Equivalently, writing X=exp(2 pi i x) on the same logarithmic strip, Fhat_N(Nx)=sqrt(iN(1-X)) *exp{N[Li_2(1)-Li_2(X)]/(2 pi i) +pi cot(pi x)/(12N)+O_K(N^-3)}. (10) The square root means sqrt(2N sin(pi x))exp(i pi x/2), not an independent principal-root reset. The equality of the leading primitives follows by differentiating and fixing the value at x=0. No continuation through an unrecorded dilogarithm cut occurs in 0<Re x<1, since X avoids the real interval [1,infinity). Unlike a pointwise assertion about a finite Euler polynomial, (10) holds on full complex compact subsets of this strip. In particular it remains useful when a geometric coefficient saddle has a nonzero imaginary index coordinate. ## 5. The original finite sum has a marked residue cycle Take the ACTUAL finite coefficient sum for a fixed braid, after its integral closure equations have been solved as in the existing normal-period calculation. Its dimension d depends on the word, not on N. Write its allowed lattice support as S_N. All factorial arguments at an allowed point are integers between zero and N-1; retain every Gaussian, pivot, cap, framing and peripheral factor. Replace each factorial in that same summand by Fhat_N of its original affine index form, using (5) for a marked color shift. Call this meromorphic interpolated summand I_N(z). It agrees with the literal original coefficient at every allowed integer point. Choose small positively oriented product circles about the points of S_N, with no other integer poles or interpolation poles inside, and let Gamma_N be their oriented sum. Then exactly sum_(k in S_N) I_N(k) =(1/(2 pi i)^d) integral_(Gamma_N) I_N(z) product_(j=1)^d [pi cot(pi z_j) dz_j]. (11) Each cotangent has residue one. Equation (11) is therefore a direct multivariable residue identity, with the original finite support encoded in its specified cycle. It does not replace that cycle by a preferred infinite contour or omit a finite-head wall. At completeness, on any complex tube where every scaled factorial argument has real part strictly between zero and one, the interpolated summand has no factorial zero or pole. Formula (10) gives its actual complex phase and a uniform nonzero leading amplitude there. The cotangent pole lattice and the support boundary still have to pass through any proposed deformation of Gamma_N. Neither a nonzero interpolant nor a unique critical point establishes its intersection coefficient with the original cycle. This makes a possible route to the main theorem more concrete: a source-preserving deformation of (11) to a positive geometric chain could use a uniform complex expansion of the SAME lattice summand. The whole contour and boundary estimate, including noncancellation, remain necessary. In particular no 5_2 or broad knot volume theorem is asserted by this interpolation result. [Exact functional-equation and complex-asymptotic diagnostics](../experiments/audit_exact_factorial_interpolation.py).

title: Exact quad transport retains a finite cross-wall sewing source
text: # Exact quad transport retains a finite cross-wall sewing source 28 October 2026. There is an exact finite Fourier/chirp transform of a pointed cyclic source into its positive quad rotation. Its coefficient is nonzero and polynomially bounded on fixed-log root trajectories. This alone is not the required global bridge: that source parameter is a source-flag cross-ratio, and the ORIGINAL crossing has nilpotent finite-head walls. Those walls admit a useful global reduction. Each actual two-head Euler resolvent is a cyclic resolvent plus four explicit sewing terms. On the original small circle only TWO cross-wall terms contribute. Thus a word with m crossings has an exact cyclic comparison with at most `2^(3m)` sewing sectors, retaining the original caps and peripheral factors. The source-free cyclic bulk has zero original period. This is a theorem about the actual source, not a geometric nonvanishing assertion. ## 1. Exact sewing for the literal two-head transfer Let S be the cyclic unit raising shift on the actual head `e_0,...,e_(N-1)`, and let `J_+,J_-` be its truncated raising and lowering shifts. Fix a nonzero marked scalar a. The actual positive transfer and its cyclic completion are T=a J_+ tensor J_-, A=a S tensor S^-1. (1) They preserve the total index modulo N. In its residue-k fiber use `b_n=e_n tensor e_((k-n) mod N)`, `0<=n<N`, and put `h=k+1`. Then A is a times the cyclic raising shift in n. The actual T deletes the outgoing edges at n=N-1 and n=k; if k=N-1 those edges coincide. Its two path lengths are h and N-h, with the zero-length second path omitted at h=N.
