Quadratic q-monomials change by linear functions of (N,k), hence by Laurent monomials of degree O(R) in z,t; x-shifts of x^L contribute the same kind of monomial. Powers q^O(R^2), and the shifted scalar factors, are scalars in Q(q). Without boundaries this proves the O(R^(s+2)) estimate immediately. Ignoring the zero extension at a boundary would be incorrect. ### Boundary stratification and its codimension Choose C so |ell_nu(0,beta)-ell_nu(0,0)|<=C R for all shifts in (3.1). Partition the integer pairs (N,k) by declaring each support form either greater than C R, less than -C R, or equal to one particular integer in [-C R,C R]. A stratum with a form less than -C R contributes zero to every shifted term. On any remaining stratum the supported shifts are a fixed subset: large forms remain positive, while near-boundary forms have fixed integer values. An empty subset contributes zero. Otherwise choose beta_0 from that subset. All q-factorial ratios between it and another supported shift have nonnegative endpoint indices. Their intervening factorial factors have strictly positive indices. A common denominator can therefore be chosen nonzero on the stratum. The x-dependent factors are nonzero for generic x. Thus the interior estimate still applies there. Suppose the fixed near-boundary forms have rank r as affine constraints on (N,k). Their consistent integer labels have only O(R^r) possibilities: choose r independent forms, after which all dependent labels are determined. There are finitely many choices of forms and large/small patterns. On each such stratum, the multiplicative variables z,t satisfy r independent binomial constraints z^b product_i t_i^a_i=q^d. (3.2) The Laurent monomials of degree O(R) in x,z,t modulo these constraints span a space of dimension O(R^(s+2-r)). To see this integrally, use Smith normal form of the fixed constraint lattice. The r constrained exponents can be reduced modulo fixed integers; the other s+2-r exponents range through O(R) integers. This also keeps the finitely many components if the lattice is not saturated. The varying right sides q^d are coefficient-field scalars. Restrict the family (3.1) to all these strata. A function is determined by its restrictions, and multiplication by the nonzero reference summand or common denominator does not increase dimension. Consequently its dimension is at most sum_(r=0)^(s+1) O(R^r)*O(R^(s+2-r)) =O(R^(s+2)). (3.3) This proves the global bound. It also treats small N, intersecting boundary faces, and redundant support inequalities. In particular it does not assume that the index polytope is a box. The same estimate holds for a finite sum on the same lattice by applying it to the direct sum of their spaces. One can retain separate term components in the elimination below, so cancellation between terms is not an assumption. ## 4. Elimination without internal multiplication variables The PBW monomials of the operators in (3.1) are linearly independent in the formal Ore algebra. There are (R+1)^(s+3) of them. For large R this exceeds the bound (3.3). Finite linear algebra yields a nonzero formal operator P(x,z,T,S_1,...,S_s) I=0 (4.1) with coefficients in Q(q), and no multiplication t_i in P. Identity (4.1) is global on the zero-extended integer array, not merely an equality of ratios at interior indices. The construction is effective in principle. List the boundary strata, clear the proper denominators, reduce their monomials by the binomial constraints, and solve the resulting finite linear system over Q(q). No efficiency or minimal-order claim is made. ## 5. Finite moments repair vanishing under summation For each N introduce independent formal units w_i and the finite Laurent polynomial F_N(q,x,w)=sum_(k in Z^s) w^k I_N(q,x;k). Since the support is finite, translation of the sum is exact: sum_k w^k S_i I(k)=w_i^(-1) F_N(q,x,w). Thus (4.1) becomes P(x,q^N,T,w_1^(-1),...,w_s^(-1)) F_N(q,x,w)=0. (5.1) Expand the nonzero polynomial P in its commuting internal shifts around S_i=1: P=sum_alpha A_alpha(x,z,T)(S-1)^alpha. Choose a nonzero A_alpha at least total degree h. Set w_i=exp(v_i) in (5.1). Its coefficient of v^alpha at that least degree is (-1)^h A_alpha(x,q^N,T) F_N(q,x,1)=0. (5.2) Every term in which a positive-degree moment of F_N occurs has a lower-degree coefficient of P, and therefore vanishes. Hence A_alpha is a genuine nonzero meridian operator for the summed state, even if P(x,z,T,1,...,1)=0. This is a formal finite-moment argument, with no convergence, contour shift, or boundary omission. ## 6. Specializing q^N=-1 without losing the operator Apply (5.2) to the actual off-root lift L_N. Clear denominators and write its nonzero operator as A(x,z,T)=(z+1)^h A_0(x,z,T), where at least one coefficient of A_0 has nonzero value at z=-1. The factor is central. For every fixed positive N, q^N+1 is a nonzero rational function of generic q, so the identity for L_N also implies A_0(x,q^N,T)L_N(q,x)=0 before specialization. At q=q_N the lift is regular, as proved in Section 1. Therefore P_K(q,x,T)=A_0(x,-1,T), P_K(q_N,x,T)F_N(x)=0 (6.1) for all but finitely many N. The excluded levels are poles of the fixed rational q-coefficients. P_K is nonzero by construction. This cancels a common operator factor before specialization of an auxiliary lift. It changes neither the state nor any peripheral factor in a state comparison. In particular the actual full ADO factor d_N is still the whole rational germ of the pointing note. At the trivial quotient color the actual reduced state has value one. Thus an order-zero multiplication operator cannot annihilate it at all large levels. After removing a common shift, (6.1) has positive order and nonzero leading and trailing coefficients in Q(q,x). Its existence proves that the actual localized all-level annihilator ideal is nonzero for every knot. The exact change x=-q^(-1)M and the fixed full/reduced shift gauge transport this operator to the meridian M and to the full literature ADO normalization. In the localized skew polynomial ring over Q(q,M), left Euclidean division gives the unique monic element of least order in the actual nonzero ideal. This is the literature minimal-operator convention; the construction above need not compute that minimal element efficiently. ## 7. What this settles and what the triangulation must still supply The [all-level exact period theorem](all_level_a_period.md) can now be applied to a nonzero actual annihilator for every knot, with its finite fixed-color pointing and bounded q-jets. Existence of such an operator is no longer an unaudited premise in that application. No proof of an equality with a Jones recursion ideal is needed for this implication. This proof does not show that the minimal operator has the geometric A-component in its classical symbol, that it has a rational inhomogeneous source factor, or that its period has the geometric regulator norm. A positive ideal triangulation supplies the geometric Bloch class and gluing branch. The exact comparison between its quantum gluing period and the actual cut-state module remains necessary, as detailed in [the triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md). The subsequent [relative octahedral presentation](relative_octahedral_period.md) now rewrites these very cut-state coefficients into five tetrahedral atoms, proves their local ideal-octahedron geometry, and derives the finite factorial's source and exact cyclic boundary transition. This gives explicit local input for the remaining comparison; it does not identify this eliminated meridian operator's global geometric block or its selected regulator period. The [diagnostics](../experiments/audit_finite_sum_annihilator.py) check the generic off-root crossing lift and its inverse against the actual root matrices, explicit global boundary certificates, and the finite-moment and central-specialization repairs. Their [results](../experiments/finite_sum_annihilator_results.json) are checks of these ingredients, not a volume theorem or an efficient all-knot computation of minimal operators.

title: The finite trivalent Euler coefficient to short balanced series
text: # The finite trivalent Euler coefficient to short balanced series 29 October 2026. This completes the missing finite coefficient identity from the independent [root-Fourier source proof](actual_trivalent_root_fourier_source_certificate.md). The proof uses only the coproduct Euler coefficient, finite Newton interpolation, finite Vandermonde, and the [own finite Sears lemma](finite_balanced_sears_operator_proof.md). It does not import a 6j evaluation. Set N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2pi i/N), F_k=(Q;Q)_k. Let a,b,c be nonnegative integers <=floor(d/2), satisfying the triangle inequalities, and put r=b+c-a, delta=a+b+c-d>=0, r_1=a+b-c, r_2=a+c-b. Thus delta<=min(a,b,c,r,r_1,r_2). Every finite factorial used below has a physical index in 0,...,d. Write D_Q h(T)=[h(T)-h(QT)]/T and P=[T^d](TQ;Q)_b^2 D_Q^r (TQ^(1-c);Q)_c^2, C_delta=Q^[-b(b+1)+c(c-1)] P. (1) The EXACT identity needed by the actual source normalization is C_delta=Q^[b(a+c-b)+c(2c+1)] *F_(2b)/F_(a+b-c)*F_a^2/[F_delta F_(a-delta)^2] *4phi3(Q^-delta,Q^-r,Q^-b,Q^-b; Q^(-b-c),Q^(-b-c),Q^(-2b);Q,Q). (2) The series terminates at min(delta,r). All denominator Pochhammers are nonzero up to that length. No generic-q normal limit is taken. ## 1. Jackson Leibniz and a finite moment identity The finite Leibniz formula follows by induction from D_Q(uv)=(D_Qu)v+u(QT)D_Qv. Apply it to f(T)^2, f=(TQ^(1-c);Q)_c: D_Q^r f^2=(-Q^(1-c))^r F_c^2 *sum_s [r choose s]_Q Q^[s(s-1)/2+(r-s)(r-s-1)/2] (TQ^(1-c+r);Q)_(c-s) (TQ^(1-c+r-s);Q)_(c-r+s) /[F_(c-s)F_(c-r+s)]. (3) Only max(0,r-c)<=s<=min(r,c) occurs. When multiplied by (TQ)_b^2, the Euler product in a term of (3) is EXACTLY (TQ;Q)_b (TQ^(b-a+1);Q)_a (TQ^(b-a-s+1);Q)_c. (4) To verify (4), compare exponent intervals using their endpoints; the two sides have the same multiplicity at every integer exponent. This argument works for EVERY triangle (a,b,c), not only a maximal first label. Reversing degree J=a+b+c to degree delta in (4) gives the three factors A(U)=(UQ^-b;Q)_b(UQ^-b;Q)_a, (UQ^(s-r);Q)_c. The signs cancel since r+J=2(b+c). The full phase in this reversal is P=Q^Z0 F_c^2F_r [U^delta]A(U) *sum_s w_s (UQ^(s-r);Q)_c, w_s=Q^[s^2-s(r+c)]/[F_sF_(r-s)F_(c-s)F_(c-r+s)], Z0=r(1-c)+r(r-1)/2+b(b+1)/2+ab-a(a-1)/2 +c(b-a)+c(c+1)/2. (5) The crucial moment is computed explicitly. The finite Newton identity x^ell=sum_(k=0)^ell (Q^-ell;Q)_k Q^k(x;Q)_k/F_k (6) follows by induction using x(x;Q)_k=Q^-k[(x;Q)_k-(x;Q)_(k+1)]. Put x=Q^(s-c), multiply by Q^(c ell), and sum against w_s. The factor (Q^(s-c);Q)_k cancels F_(c-s), leaving Vandermonde of lengths c-k and c. The exact result is sum_s w_s (Q^(s-c);Q)_k =(-1)^k Q^[-ck+k(k-1)/2-(c-k)r] F_(2c-k)/[F_rF_(2c-k-r)F_(c-k)F_c]. (7) This is an own finite Vandermonde calculation: after cancellation, its summand exponent is (c-k-s)(r-s), up to the displayed constant, and the product-coefficient identity gives [2c-k choose r]_Q. Out-of-range terms are zero. In the use below k<=delta<=2c-r, so every displayed denominator is regular. Expand (UQ^(s-r);Q)_c by the finite binomial theorem, insert (6), and put ell=k+v. The remaining v sum is another FINITE Euler product. Equations (6),(7) give sum_s w_s (UQ^(s-r);Q)_c =Q^(-cr) sum_k (-1)^k Q^[k(k-1)/2]U^k *F_(2c-k)(UQ^(c-r);Q)_(c-k) /[F_rF_(2c-k-r)F_kF_(c-k)^2]. (8) All sums here are finite, so their interchange has no convergence hypothesis. In (5), the last Euler factor in (8) joins the length-a factor contiguously, because c-r=a-b. ## 2. The root coefficient collapse Let L=delta-k, so 0<=L<=b. The only remaining coefficient after (8) is [U^L](UQ^-b;Q)_b(UQ^-b;Q)_(d+L-b) =Q^[L(L-1-2b)] F_b^2/[F_LF_(b-L)^2]. (9) Here is a finite proof. Put M=d+L-b. The finite binomial expansion of the left side, extracting its zeroth summand, is (-Q^-b)^L Q^[L(L-1)/2][M choose L]_Q *2phi1(Q^-L,Q^-b;Q^(M-L+1);Q,Q^(b+1)). At this ROOT, Q^(M-L+1)=Q^(N-b)=Q^-b. The equal numerator and denominator cancel, with no zero reached because L<=b<N. The remaining finite binomial sum is (Q^(b+1-L);Q)_L. Converting its two factors to F gives exactly (9). This is the source-specific root collapse; no continuous-color replacement is used. Combining (5),(8),(9), and writing Z=Z0-cr+delta(delta-1-2b)-b(b+1)+c(c-1), one obtains C_delta=Q^Z F_b^2 F_(2c) /[F_(r_2)F_delta F_(b-delta)^2] *H_c, H_c=4phi3(Q^-delta,Q^-r_2,Q^-c,Q^-c; Q^(-a-c),Q^(-a-c),Q^(-2c);Q,Q). (10) For example the raw kth term before normalization is (-1)^k Q^[k(k-1)/2+(delta-k)(delta-k-1-2b)] F_(2c-k) /[F_(2c-k-r)F_kF_(c-k)^2F_(delta-k)F_(b-delta+k)^2]. Its successive ratio gives (10); the residual argument is Q because 2+2b+2c-r-delta=N+1. This makes the root mark explicit. ## 3. Two proved Sears transformations meet at one symmetric series Use the own finite Sears identity, with length delta, on H_c. Keep Q^-c and choose d=e=Q^(-a-c). It gives H_c=K_1 H_sym, K_1=(Q^-a,Q^(-a-b);Q)_delta /(Q^(-a-c),Q^-r_1;Q)_delta, H_sym=4phi3(Q^-delta,Q^-a,Q^-b,Q^-c; Q^(-a-b),Q^(-a-c),Q^(-b-c);Q,Q). The root equalities Q^(a+1-delta)=Q^(-b-c) etc fix all three denominators. Applying the SAME finite Sears lemma to the H_b on the right side of (2) gives H_b=K_2 H_sym, K_2=(Q^-c,Q^(-a-c);Q)_delta /(Q^(-b-c),Q^-r_2;Q)_delta. (11) Every factorial index is physical, since delta<=a,b,c,r_i. Thus neither transformation crosses a root pole. No division by H_sym is needed; the comparison is between their explicit prefactors. For clarity the complete phase cancellation is recorded. Let tau_u=(-1)^u Q^[u(u+1)/2], so F_uF_(d-u)=N tau_u. Converting (11) to factorials and reflecting complements gives [F_b^2F_(2c)/(F_(r_2)F_delta F_(b-delta)^2)](K_1/K_2) /[F_(2b)F_a^2/(F_(r_1)F_delta F_(a-delta)^2)] =tau_b^2 tau_(2c) tau_(a+b) tau_(b+c) /(tau_(2b)tau_c tau_a tau_(a+c)^2) =Q^K, K=-a^2+ab-2ac-a+bc+b+c^2. The residual sign is (-1)^[2(b-a)]=1. Finally direct expansion gives Z+K-[b(a+c-b)+c(2c+1)] =-(a-b+c+delta)(a+b+c-delta+1) =-N(-N+2a+2c+1). Its Q power is ONE. Substituting into (10),(11) proves EXACTLY (2) for every admissible supported triangle at both parities. ## 4. Fully symmetric, manifestly positive root form The same calculation also removes every ordering qualification. No step in (3)--(11) assumed a maximal first label. With the original source phase E_src=2a^2-ab-ac+bc-J-3, the actual scalar has the FULLY symmetric positive form A_source=(-1)^(N+J)q^E_src D_sym H_sym, D_sym=N^2/[s_r s_(r_1)s_(r_2)s_delta s_(a-delta)s_(b-delta)s_(c-delta)]. (12) Here q=exp(pi i/N), s_u=|F_u|. Every H_sym summand is POSITIVE: in (Q^-u;Q)_k each factor is i q^(-u+l) times its positive sine. The full term phase is q^[k(J-delta+1)]=q^(Nk)=(-1)^k, which cancels the denominator phase (-1)^k. All descending sine indices are nonnegative up to the true termination min(delta,a,b,c). The zeroth term is one. Thus (12) proves nonvanishing for EVERY supported triangle, at both parities and composite levels. For an explicit check of the absolute normalization, insert K_2 from (11) and the source prefactor Nq^[E+2b(b+1)-2c(c-1)]/(F_aF_bF_cF_r), with E from the Fourier theorem, into (2). Reflect complementary factorials. Their modulus is exactly D_sym. Their F-power difference is 1-N, and the remaining q exponent, after (-i)^(1-N) is included, differs from N(N+J)+E_src by 2N(-N+b+c+1). Hence the full phase is precisely the one in (12), not merely an unspecified unit. The positive candidate factorial sum, calculated in a chart with a maximal label and then transformed by the same finite Sears lemma, has R_N=N^3 H_sym/[s_a s_b s_c s_r s_(r_1)s_(r_2) s_(a-delta)s_(b-delta)s_(c-delta)]. (13) The long/short calculation and phase equivalence are recorded with their explicit initial term in the [finite candidate transform port](actual_trivalent_general_finite_transform_port.md#1-exact-long-and-short-series-for-the-candidate-factorial-object). For a direct normalization check, in its maximal-a chart the initial term is N s_a/[s_(a-b)s_(a-c)s_(a-delta)s_b s_c s_r]. Its first Sears factor has modulus s_(b+c)s_(2b)s_(a-b)s_(a-c)/[s_a s_(r_1)s_b s_c]; the phases of its two ascending and two descending Pochhammers cancel exactly, so this factor is POSITIVE. The second factor K_2 in (11) is also positive: all four negative-parameter Pochhammer phases cancel. Its modulus is s_c s_(a+c)s_(d-a)s_(d-2b) /[s_(c-delta)s_(d-b)s_(b+c)s_(r_2)]. Multiply these three displayed factors and use sine reflection; the result is exactly the positive prefactor in (13). Both sides of (13) are manifestly symmetric, so a maximal chart can be chosen for ANY label order. Combining (12),(13) proves A_source=(-1)^(N+J)q^E_src [s_as_bs_c/(N s_delta)]R_N for every supported triangle. The lower-saturation branch is zero by the independent complete-clock cancellation. ## 5. Original-source conclusion and its separate sewing scope Together with the root-Fourier coefficient theorem and the explicitly normalized candidate long-to-short series calculation, (2) proves the positive trivalent scalar identity, rather than checking it at finitely many levels. The scalar is zero for J<d; for J>=d it is the specified unit phase times C_N R_N, hence NONZERO. This scalar conclusion does not estimate the whole magnetic tensor: its descendant coefficients can carry additional exponential factorials. Ordinary white and marked white source contractions, full Hermite normals and ordered graph sewing still retain their actual independent data. In particular the scalar action maximum must not be relabelled as an already proved full vertex norm bound. Audit: [all finite coefficient stages and source phases](../experiments/audit_finite_trivalent_euler_racah_transform.py). Root and independent internal proof reviews passed the complete finite bridge, both Sears prefactors, all root denominator ranges, the original source phase, positive symmetric series and every-label extension. A fresh exact replay passed fifteen full supported root families through N=16 at every intermediate finite stage, with a symbolic check of the remaining phase multiple. The root's independent [square-linearization proof](actual_trivalent_square_linearization_bridge.md) reaches the same H_c without the Jackson-Leibniz/Newton route. Tests are supplementary; the finite proofs establish the identity.

title: The first quantum-normal connection of an actual root module
text: # The first quantum-normal connection of an actual root module Research construction, 27 October 2026. This gives a canonical algebraic object from the first quantum-normal germ of a specified difference module. It needs no global differential equation in the quantum parameter and no off-root horizontal extension of the actual ADO state. It retains a source and cut, and distinguishes a genuine connection from the nonsemisimple kernel-to-cokernel case. This is attached to the specified actual operator, with its pointing. It is not an identification of its classical geometric component or of its selected norm with the Bloch regulator. The volume conjecture remains unproved. ## 1. Root monodromy and its first normal differential Fix N>=2 and a primitive N-th root zeta. Put Q=zeta(1+epsilon), E=C(Y), U=Y^N, sigma_Q f(Y)=f(QY), D=Y partial_Y. Let T(Q)=B(Q,Y)sigma_Q be a specified rank-d difference module, regular and invertible as a matrix germ over E[[epsilon]]. Write H(Q,Y)=B(Q,Y)B(Q,QY)...B(Q,Q^(N-1)Y), T(Q)^N=H(Q,Y)sigma_Q^N, H=H_0+epsilon H_1+O(epsilon^2). Because Q^N=(1+epsilon)^N, sigma_Q^N=I+N epsilon D+O(epsilon^2). Thus L(Q)=T(Q)^N-I has the exact first expansion L=L_0+epsilon L_1+O(epsilon^2), L_0=H_0-I, L_1=H_1+N H_0 D. (1.1) The H_1 term differentiates every occurrence of Q in the product, including its shifted arguments. Omitting those moving-argument derivatives would give a different object. Set K=ker L_0, C=coker L_0 and let pi:E^d->C. Both are E-vector spaces. There is a natural linear map iota:K->C given by inclusion followed by quotient. Define D_N:K -> C, D_N(x)=pi(L_1 x)/N^2. (1.2) For f in E it satisfies the Leibniz rule D_N(fx)=f D_N(x)+(D f/N)iota(x). (1.3) Indeed pi H_0=pi and H_0 x=x on K. In particular for f in C(U), D f/N=U partial_U f. This is an algebraic differential operator between K and C with the specified symbol iota; it is not always an endomorphism of one line. ## 2. Exact cyclic descent The root operator T_0=B(zeta,Y)sigma_zeta commutes with H_0, so it preserves K and induces an operator on C. Its N-th power is H_0, which acts as identity on both spaces. They therefore have cyclic semilinear descent to C(U). One direct spanning formula makes the descent explicit. For a vector x in either space put Av(x)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1)T_0^j x. Then x=sum_(r=0)^(N-1) Y^r Av(Y^(-r)x/N). (2.1) This follows from the finite Fourier sum (1/N)sum_r zeta^(-jr)=delta_(j,0). Thus invariants span over E. Their independence over the invariant field C(U) follows by taking a shortest E-linear relation, normalizing one coefficient to one, and subtracting its T_0 translate: all coefficients must be invariant. The operator (1.2) respects this descent. The exact identity [T(Q),L(Q)]=0 gives at first order T_0 L_1+T_1 L_0=L_0 T_1+L_1 T_0. On K, after projection to C, the terms with L_0 vanish. Hence D_N T_0=T_0 D_N. It follows that (1.2) induces D_N:K^(T_0) -> C^(T_0) with symbol U partial_U times the descended iota. This explains the normalization N^2. Dividing L_1 only by N would leave N times the natural logarithmic derivation on the central coordinate U. If eigenvalue one of H_0 is semisimple, then E^d=ker(H_0-I) direct-sum im(H_0-I), and iota is an isomorphism. Its inverse identifies (1.2) with a genuine logarithmic connection on the descended invariant bundle. In particular a simple eigenvalue one gives an algebraic line with connection over C(U). If there is a Jordan block of size greater than one at eigenvalue one, iota need not be invertible. One must retain the full K->C operator. For a rank-two Jordan block it can have zero symbol but a nonzero order-zero part. Replacing it by an inverse matrix or a line connection in that case would lose first-normal information. This construction is initially over the rational function fields C(Y) and C(U). At a special central fiber, such as U=1, the rank of H_0-I can jump. Its fiber kernel and cokernel must not be identified automatically with those generic spaces. Evaluating the selected period there requires the original saturated lattice and its source/co-source jets, or the full first-order complex of Section 4. No complete-fiber regularity is assumed here. ## 3. Gauge invariance, including quantum-normal gauges Let v=G(Q,Y)w, with G=G_0+epsilon G_1+... regular and invertible. Then B'=G^(-1) B sigma_Q(G), H'=G^(-1) H sigma_Q^N(G). Since sigma_Q^N(G)=G_0+epsilon(G_1+N D G_0)+..., H'_0=G_0^(-1)H_0G_0, H'_1=G_0^(-1)H_1G_0 +G_0^(-1)H_0(G_1+N D G_0) -G_0^(-1)G_1G_0^(-1)H_0G_0. (3.1) Equivalently, as first-order differential operators, G_0 L'_1-L_1 G_0=L_0 G_1-G_1 L'_0. (3.2) The right side vanishes between K' and C. Thus G_0 identifies the two kernel-to-cokernel operators canonically. A pure quantum- normal gauge G_0=I changes H_1 by a commutator with H_0, invisible between K and C. A Y-dependent G_0 requires the N D G_0 term in (3.1); it cannot be omitted. This is gauge invariance of a fixed difference module and its first quantum-normal germ. Different left multiples of an annihilator can add extraneous modules. No invariance under such additions is claimed without their source and cut comparison. ## 4. The exact source and co-source normal equations Suppose a supplied section has expansion v=v_0+epsilon v_1+... and L(Q)v(Q)=epsilon s+O(epsilon^2). Then v_0 in K, L_0 v_1+L_1 v_0=s, D_N(v_0)=pi(s)/N^2. (4.1) Changing v_1 by h changes s by L_0h and leaves pi(s) unchanged. Under the gauge of Section 3, s'=G_0^(-1)s. Thus the normal source class is intrinsic to the specified first-order section problem. The full first-order source problem is the two-term block operator [ L_0 0 ] [v_0] = [0], [ L_1 L_0 ] [v_1] [s]. (4.2) Keeping only the map K->C forgets the lift ambiguity and can lose a normal cut functional. For a supplied scalar cut p(Q)=ell(Q)v(Q)+k(Q), its first coefficient is p_1=ell_0 v_1+ell_1 v_0+k_1. (4.3) The transformed data are v'_0=G_0^(-1)v_0, v'_1=G_0^(-1)v_1-G_0^(-1)G_1G_0^(-1)v_0, ell'_0=ell_0G_0, ell'_1=ell_1G_0+ell_0G_1, and (4.3) is unchanged. This retains the normal co-source; an unpointed connection alone would not recover it. The full ADO normalization remains the original marked dimension line d_N(M), including its sign and canceled meridian germ. A chosen quantum-normal derivative of that line requires its whole lifted phase and cap data. The construction here does not replace it by its numerical complete value or infer that derivative from the root value alone. ## 5. A first-normal source from the original finite lift There is actual input for (4.1) that does not assume the ADO state is horizontal off its root. Retain the auxiliary finite lift G_N(Q,Y) and the pre-specialization annihilator from the [Q-only finite-sum construction](even_meridian_norm_descent.md): Acal(Q,Z,Y,S)G_N(Q,Y)=0 at Z=Q^N, P(Q,Y,S)=Acal(Q,1,Y,S)=sum_(j=0)^d a_j S^j. Choose the coherent Laurent Ore presentation before specializing, including any fixed shifts needed for nonzero a_0,a_d. It can be Laurent in S before specialization. At a regular root, G_N is a whole Q-germ and its value is F_N(Y). Since Q^N=1+N epsilon+..., P G_N=-N epsilon (partial_Z Acal)(zeta,1,Y,S_zeta)F_N+O(epsilon^2). (5.1) The moving shifts have already been retained in Acal; their extra derivatives multiply Q^N-1 and contribute only at second order to this difference. Define h_1 to be the displayed first coefficient. Let A(Q,Y) be the solution companion matrix of P, so that for v=(G_N,S G_N,...,S^(d-1)G_N)^t, sigma_Q v=A v+e_d(P G_N/a_d). Take T=A^(-1)sigma_Q, in the convention of Section 1. Then (T-I)v=epsilon r_1+O(epsilon^2), r_1=A(zeta,Y)^(-1)e_d h_1/a_d(zeta,Y). (5.2) The exact factorization T^N-I=(I+T+...+T^(N-1))(T-I) yields s=sum_(j=0)^(N-1)T_0^j r_1. (5.3) Its cokernel class is T_0-invariant, since T_0s-s=(H_0-I)r_1. Thus the actual first-normal source descends to C(U), with normalization pi(s)/N^2. Equations (5.1)--(5.3) construct a source from the central derivative of the specified finite-sum annihilator. They do not make the actual root state horizontal for the normal connection. Vanishing of this source class is a condition to prove, not a consequence of rootwise T_0-invariance. Its comparison with a geometric regulator source is still required. The later [source-corrected construction](source_corrected_quantum_normal_connection.md) uses this very same preoperator to make the right-hand side a linear source rule R_N(v), rather than a fixed source value. Its corrected operator D_N-R_N annihilates every compatible root section. If the selected section has nonzero symbol iota(v), this removes all nonconstant central multipliers c(U) while retaining their actual source derivatives. The unsourced D_N still need not annihilate the section. The nonzero-symbol condition and the supplied whole lifting rule are essential. ## 6. A finite-factorial check which distinguishes those statements Take the local factorial G_N(Q,Y)=(Y;Q)_N. It has the exact central equation Acal=S-(1-ZY)/(1-Y), Z=Q^N. At Z=1, P=S-I, so T=sigma_Q, H_0=1, H_1=0. The descended normal connection is U partial_U. The root section is F_N=1-U. It is T_0-invariant, but it is not horizontal for this connection. The actual source calculation gives h_1=-N Y(1-U)/(1-Y), s=-N(1-U)sum_j zeta^jY/(1-zeta^jY) =-N^2 U. Consequently D_N(1-U)=-U=pi(s)/N^2, exactly as (4.1) requires. This is an explicit source identity from the same finite-factorial atoms used in the actual knot state. It is not a claim that the whole knot period is the product of these local sections. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_first_quantum_normal_connection.py). [Results](../experiments/first_quantum_normal_connection_results.json).

title: A finite whole-source proof of the five-crossing cyclotomic transform
text: # A finite whole-source proof of the five-crossing cyclotomic transform 28 October 2026. The candidate in Section 6 of [the actual five-crossing source](five_two_whole_source_reduction.md) is an exact identity for EVERY primitive Nth root Q, N>=2, and arbitrary nonzero Y. No Jones identity, ordinary-color interpolation, or published Bailey proof is used. Write q=Q in the proof, `d=N-1`, `F_a=(q;q)_a`, and H_n(x)=sum_(j=0)^n {n choose j}_q x^j, T_n(Y)=product_(r=1)^n(Y+Y^-1-q^r-q^-r). Then the ORIGINAL reduced whole source satisfies F_N(Y)=sum_(n=0)^d C_n(q)T_n(Y), C_n(q)=(-1)^n q^(-n(n+3)/2)H_n(q^(-n-1)). (1) Every original turn, cap, Cartan and framing factor is already contained in the starting triple source below. No factor is changed in proving (1). The original full ADO modified-dimension germ, if attached, multiplies both sides unchanged. The proof supplies three reusable finite identities: a terminating three-factor q-Chu transform, a generic Newton connection, and a root Rogers-polynomial convolution with an arbitrary extra variable. ## 1. Elementary finite identities For k<N and arbitrary a,b, sum_(ell=0)^k (q^-k;q)_ell(a;q)_ell(b;q)_ell q^ell/F_ell =sum_(r=0)^k {k choose r}_q a^(k-r)b^r(a;q)_r. (2) Expand `(b;q)_ell`, set ell=r+s, and use sum_(s=0)^n(q^-n;q)_s(c;q)_s q^s/F_s=c^n. (3) For completeness, expand `(c;q)_s` in (3). For each expansion index r the remaining sum is `(q^(1-(n-r));q)_(n-r)` by the finite q-binomial theorem. It vanishes unless r=n; that last coefficient is c^n. Substituting (3) into the expansion of (2), together with `(q^-k)_r/F_r=(-1)^r q^(-kr+r(r-1)/2){k choose r}`, cancels every extra sign and power. This proves (2). It is symmetric in a,b, so either factor may be expanded. We also need the finite q-Vandermonde consequence sum_(u=0)^a sum_(j=0)^b {a choose u}_q {b choose j}_q q^(ju)=H_(a+b)(1). (4) To prove (4), compare coefficients in the finite q-binomial expansion of a product of lengths a and b. It gives `{a+b choose l}=sum_(u+v=l){a choose u}{b choose v} q^((b-v)u)`. Replace v by b-j and sum over l. All denominators used in this application have indices at most d; no root-zero factorial is divided out. ## 2. Reduce the ACTUAL triple to a symmetric polynomial basis The previously proved original source is F_N(Y)=sum_(m+ell<=d)sum_(j=0)^m Y^(2(d-m))q^(j(m+1)+m+ell+2) {m+ell choose ell}_q {m choose j}_q (q/Y;q)_(m+ell)(q^(j+1)/Y;q)_ell. (5) Replace j by m-j and put k=d-m. The ell sum becomes the left side of (2) with `a=q^-k/Y`, `b=q^(-k-j)/Y`, because `q^(m+1)=q^-k`. Use the SYMMETRIC form of its right side. After the exact prefactor cancellation `q^(m(m+2)+2)=q^(k^2+1)`, equation (5) is q sum_(k=0)^d Y^k(q/Y;q)_(d-k) *sum_(r=0)^k {k choose r}_q sum_(j=0)^(d-k){d-k choose j}_q q^(jr)(q^(-k-j)/Y;q)_r. (6) Expand the last Pochhammer with index s. Use `{k choose r}{r choose s}={k choose s}{k-s choose r-s}`. The remaining sums over r-s and j are exactly (4), with lengths k-s and d-k. Thus F_N(Y)=q sum_(k=0)^d Y^k(q/Y;q)_(d-k) *sum_(s=0)^k {k choose s}_q(-1/Y)^s q^(-ks+s(s-1)/2)H_(d-s)(1). (7) Interchange k,s, set `n=d-s`, `k=s+r`, and reflect the root Gaussian by {d-n+r choose r}_q =(-1)^r q^(-nr+r(r-1)/2){n choose r}_q. (8) All powers simplify to F_N(Y)=q sum_(n=0)^d (-1)^n q^(-n(n+1)/2) H_n(1) P_n(Y), (9) P_n(Y)=sum_(r=0)^n {n choose r}_q(-Y)^r q^(r(r+1)/2)(q/Y;q)_(n-r). For the sign at either parity, the root calculation used here is `(-1)^(d-n)q^(-(d-n)(d-n+1)/2) =(-1)^n q^(-n(n+1)/2)`. It follows from the full identity `(-1)^d q^(d(d+1)/2)=1`; no even-level sign is discarded. ## 3. Generic Newton connection For generic q, and hence at the present root whenever n<N, P_n(Y)=(-1)^n q^(n(n+1)/2) sum_(k=0)^n q^(n-k){n choose k}_q T_k(Y). (10) Here is a direct verification independent of (5). The defining finite convolution for P_n gives P_0=1, P_1=1-qX, P_n=(1-q^n X)P_(n-1)+q^n(1-q^(n-1))P_(n-2), X=Y+Y^-1. (11) One way to verify (11) purely formally is to set `A(z)=sum_n P_n z^n/F_n`. Its defining convolution gives `A(qz)/A(z)=(1-z)/[(1-qYz)(1-qz/Y)]`; the two first-order series equations follow immediately by comparing successive coefficients in the finite q-binomial series. Comparing coefficients in this displayed equation gives (11). This is an identity of formal rational coefficients, not a rootwise infinite-product evaluation. Set `R_n=(-1)^n q^(-n(n+1)/2)P_n`. Then (11) becomes R_n=(X-q^-n)R_(n-1)+(q^(1-n)-1)R_(n-2). (12) The sum on the right of (10), after removing its prefactor, satisfies the same recurrence and initial values. To check a T_k coefficient, use `X T_k=T_(k+1)+(q^(k+1)+q^(-k-1))T_k` and `{n choose k}={n-1 choose k-1}+q^k{n-1 choose k}`. The only remaining ratio is `{n-2 choose k}/{n-1 choose k} =(1-q^(n-1-k))/(1-q^(n-1))`, which makes the two residual terms `q^-n-q^(-k-1)` cancel. This proves (10). Substitution of (10) into (9) cancels BOTH quadratic phases and signs. Consequently the actual Newton coefficient is C_k(q)=q sum_(n=k)^d q^(n-k){n choose k}_q H_n(1). (13) ## 4. A reusable ROOT convolution evaluates every coefficient In fact for arbitrary x, as a polynomial identity in x, q sum_(n=k)^d q^(n-k){n choose k}_q H_n(x) =(-1)^k q^(-k(k+3)/2) x^d H_k(q^(-k-1)/x). (14) The right side is interpreted after multiplying by x^d, so is polynomial also at x=0. Thus every x-Euler moment can be differentiated in (14), with its source character `x^(N-1)` retained. Here is a finite coefficient proof. Put `h_x(z)=sum_(n=0)^d H_n(x)z^n`. Gaussian generating functions and the exact root product `prod_(r=0)^d(1-q^r z)=1-z^N` give h_x(z)=sum_(j=0)^d (xz)^j(q^(j+1)z;q)_(d-j). (15) Indeed both sides have degree at most d, and their first N coefficients agree by `sum_(n>=j){n choose j}z^n=z^j/(z;q)_(j+1)`. This last generating identity follows directly from q-Pascal; it is used only through degree d where all factorials are units. Set `a=q^(-k-1)=q^(d-k)`. The convolution sum_(r=0)^(d-k) a^r {r+k choose k}_q H_(d-r)(x) is the coefficient of z^d in `h_x(z)/(az;q)_(k+1)`. In (15), every term with `j<=d-k-1` cancels the whole denominator, leaving a polynomial of degree d-k-1 and hence ZERO z^d coefficient. Write the remaining j as d-k+s, `0<=s<=k`. Its quotient is x^(d-k+s)z^(d-k+s)/(az;q)_(s+1). Its z^d coefficient is `x^(d-k+s)a^(k-s){k choose s}`. Summing over s gives x^d H_k(a/x). (16) Finally use the exact root reflection `{d-r choose k}=(-1)^k q^(-rk-k(k+1)/2){r+k choose k}` in the left side of (14), setting n=d-r. Its prefactor is `(-1)^k q^(-k(k+3)/2)` and the remaining sum is (16). This proves (14) at every parity and composite level. ## 5. The candidate is proved as a WHOLE meridian identity Take x=1 in (14) and substitute into (13). This gives exactly (1), proving the candidate (6.1) of the source note. At Y=1, `T_n(1)=(-1)^n q^(-n(n+1)/2)F_n^2`, so in the ORIGINAL Q orientation the exact reduced state is <5_2>_N=sum_(0<=j<=n<N) Q^[-n(n+2)-j(n+1)](Q;Q)_n^3 /[(Q;Q)_j(Q;Q)_(n-j)]. (17a) This is the source-preserving double sum used by the inner quadrature theorem; its endpoints are not changed. Equivalently, with t=Q^-1, F_N(Y)=sum_(n=0)^(N-1) t^n(tY;t)_n(t/Y;t)_n sum_(j=0)^n t^(j(j+1)){n choose j}_t. (17) All steps were identities of Laurent polynomials in Y. Therefore every fixed-root meridian derivative, including the normal complete-color source, is retained. No conclusion about generic-q derivatives of the actual whole crossing is obtained by differentiating the root identity in Q. This proves a finite source transform; it does not establish the saddle selection or the exponential volume lower bound. Those analyses may now use (17) as an identity of the ORIGINAL state, with its original normalization. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_five_two_finite_chu_bridge.py) checks the reusable generic identities, every intermediate root transform, the x-polynomial convolution, and whole-Y Laurent coefficients at small levels. The uniform proof is the finite calculation above, not interpolation of test colors.

title: An unconditional finite q-Chu reduction of the actual five-crossing source
text: # An unconditional finite q-Chu reduction of the actual five-crossing source 28 October 2026. The actual three-index period in [the whole-source calculation](five_two_whole_source_reduction.md) has a two-index whole-meridian reduction by elementary finite q-binomial identities. This reduction does not assume the candidate Newton coefficients in its Section 6. The further transform is now proved in [the full cyclotomic proof](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md); this note records the independent double-sum route. Write q=Q here (the Gaussian base, not the half-root), `d=N-1`, `F_a=(q;q)_a`, and `H_a(z)=sum_j {a choose j}_q z^j`. Every denominator below has index less than N. ## 1. A reusable terminating three-factor transform For k with `F_1,...,F_k` nonzero, and arbitrary a,b, exactly sum_(ell=0)^k (q^-k; q)_ell (a;q)_ell (b;q)_ell q^ell/F_ell =sum_(r=0)^k {k choose r}_q a^(k-r)b^r(a;q)_r. (1) This is a polynomial identity in a,b, without a genericity condition on their Pochhammer factors. First prove the finite q-Chu identity sum_(s=0)^n (q^-n;q)_s(a;q)_s q^s/F_s=a^n. (2) Expand `(a;q)_s` by the finite q-binomial theorem and interchange the finite sums. For its coefficient with index r the remaining sum is sum_(t=0)^(n-r)(q^(-(n-r));q)_t q^t/F_t =(q^(1-(n-r));q)_(n-r). The last equality is the same finite q-binomial theorem. It is zero unless r=n, because otherwise one factor is `1-q^0`. The r=n term simplifies to a^n, proving (2). To prove (1), expand `(b;q)_ell`, put ell=r+s, and use (2) with length k-r and parameter a q^r. The inner sum is `(a q^r)^(k-r)`. Substitute (q^-k;q)_r/F_r=(-1)^r q^(-kr+r(r-1)/2){k choose r}_q. All signs and q powers cancel, leaving exactly (1). ## 2. Applying it to the ORIGINAL triple source Start with the proved actual source formula F_N(Y)=sum_(m+ell<=d)sum_(j=0)^m Y^(2(d-m))q^(j(m+1)+m+ell+2) {m+ell choose ell}_q {m choose j}_q (q/Y;q)_(m+ell)(q^(j+1)/Y;q)_ell. (3) Replace j by m-j and put k=d-m. At a primitive Nth root, `q^(m+1)=q^-k` and `q^(m(m+2)+2)=q^(k^2+1)`. The ell sum is the left side of (1) with a=q^-k/Y, b=q^(-k-j)/Y. Its r-th term is `Y^-k q^(-k^2-jr){k choose r}(q^-k/Y;q)_r`. The prefactor in (3) consequently simplifies to q Y^k. Set n=k-r and use the exact contiguous product (q/Y;q)_(d-k)(q^-k/Y;q)_(k-n) =(q/Y;q)_(d-n), which follows from q^N=1 before any Y evaluation. One obtains F_N(Y)=q sum_(0<=n<=k<=d) Y^k {k choose n}_q (q/Y;q)_(d-n) H_(d-k)(q^n). (4) This is already an exact simpler finite source transform. It preserves arbitrary Y and all of its meridian derivatives. ## 3. One more finite q-binomial sum gives a DOUBLE sum Expand H in (4). Put k=n+r and `d-k=j+s`, so `n+r+j+s=d`. The root reflection identity gives F_(n+r) F_(j+s) =N(-1)^(j+s)q^((j+s)(j+s+1)/2). (5) Fix n,j and set `L=d-n-j=r+s`. The remaining r,s sum is sum_(s=0)^L (-1)^s q^(s(s+1)/2+js)Y^-s /(F_s F_(L-s)) =(q^(j+1)/Y;q)_L/F_L. (6) Equation (6) is the ordinary finite q-binomial theorem. Thus the whole actual reduced scalar has the unconditional formula F_N(Y)=Nq sum_(n,j>=0,n+j<=d) (-1)^j q^(j(j+1)/2+nj) Y^(d-j) (q/Y;q)_(d-n)(q^(j+1)/Y;q)_(d-n-j) /[F_n F_j F_(d-n-j)]. (7) The factor N in (5)-(7) is the exact full root factorial, not a normalization chosen after evaluating Y. The original Cartan, turning, cut and framing factors are already included in (3), so remain included in (7). The separate full ADO modified-dimension factor multiplies both unchanged. Equivalently, with k=d-n, (7) is Nq Y^d sum_(k=0)^d (q/Y;q)_k^2/[F_(d-k)F_k] * sum_(j=0)^k (q^-k;q)_j Y^-j /[F_j(q/Y;q)_j]. (8) Formula (8) is initially read after cancelling Pochhammer denominators termwise back to (7); no division at a Y source zero is implied. ## 4. Relation to the proved cyclotomic formula Putting t=q^-1, the proved cyclotomic form in the original note is F_N(Y) =sum_(n=0)^d t^n(tY;t)_n(t/Y;t)_n sum_(j=0)^n t^(j(j+1)){n choose j}_t. (9) The inner normalized coefficient is the elementary Bailey convolution `sum_j t^(j^2+j)/[F_j(t)F_(n-j)(t)]`. Equations (1)-(8) give an independent double-sum expression. The [full proof](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md) instead uses the symmetric three-factor expansion, a generic Newton connection, and an exact root Rogers-polynomial convolution to prove (9). Repeated ordinary-color nodes are not used as an interpolation proof. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_five_two_finite_chu_bridge.py) checks (1) at generic finite parameters and compares (3), (4), (7), and the original literal source at primitive roots with unrestricted whole-meridian evaluations. The displayed finite identities, not the samples, establish their scope.

title: A proved outer maximum for the cubic reduced phase
text: # A proved outer maximum for the cubic reduced phase 28 October 2026. For the exact double-sum phase supplied by the [finite transform](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md), the selected inner critical branch has a rigorously concave reduced outer action on a full horizontal band. The explicit bent contour through its cubic stationary point also has a unique global maximum there. The sloped part is controlled analytically, without a mesh-based positivity assumption. This is a theorem about the explicit reduced phase and its contour. The original outer sum still has to be carried to that contour, including its aliases and the inner endpoint pieces. Equality of the cubic critical value with the marked hyperbolic regulator is also separate: numerical agreement or equality of trace fields does not prove that action identity. ## 1. The phase and a specified inner critical branch Use the branch J'(z)=Log(2sin(pi z)) continued from 0<z<1, and set S(x,y)=3J(x)-J(y)-J(x-y) +i*pi*(3x+2y-x^2-xy-y^2). (1) Its added lattice characters are retained in this definition. Let 1/2<Re x<1, 0<=Im x<=Log(2)/(2pi), X=exp(2pi*i*x), T=1/X-1. The number T lies in the upper half-plane and 1<=|T+1|<=2. The quadratic v-1/v=T (2) has exactly one root in the first quadrant. Indeed its two roots have product -1 and share the sign of their imaginary parts. A root could be purely imaginary only if T belonged to i[2,infinity). The present circles, centered at -1 with radii at most 2, meet the imaginary axis below sqrt(3), so they avoid that ray. The chosen root is analytic here. Put Y=-v, y_s(x)=1+Log(Y)/(2pi*i) =1/2+Log(v)/(2pi*i), (3) where 0<Arg v<pi/2 and -pi<Arg Y<-pi/2. Then 1/2<Re y_s<Re x<1 and 0<Re(x-y_s)<1/2. For the latter inequality, (T+1)v=v^2+v-1 has positive imaginary part, so Arg(T+1)+Arg v lies strictly between zero and pi. All three J arguments in (1) therefore stay on their stated strips. The quadratic equation gives S_y(x,y_s)=0. Exponentiating that derivative gives 1-X/Y=X(1-Y). The logarithmic derivative itself is zero, rather than an unretained multiple of 2pi*i: it is constant modulo that multiple on this connected branch and tends to zero at x->1 from the real interval. Define W(x)=S(x,y_s(x)). (4) ## 2. Exact reduced Hessian Differentiating (1)--(3), or taking its Schur complement, gives exactly W''(x)=2pi*i R(v), R(v)=(v^2+v+4)(v^2+v-1)/(1-v^4). (5) Equivalently, with s=v+1/v=sqrt(T^2+4) on its marked branch, R=(T+1)/(2T)*[(3T-2)/s-5]. (6) These formulas are independent of an added constant logarithmic flattening. Such a flattening still matters for W and W'. ## 3. Horizontal strict concavity on the whole band Write v=a+ib, a,b>0, r=a^2+b^2, and d=|T+1|^2. The present band has 1<=d<=4. Equation (2) gives the exact constraint r^2+(3-d)r+1+2a(r-1)-4a^2=0. (7) Direct multiplication gives Im R=b P_0/|1-v^4|^2. Reducing its real polynomial numerator by (7) gives P=a[2r^2+(6d+4)r-8] +2r^3+2r^2+(13-5d)r+8. (8) This numerator is STRICTLY positive on the stated domain. Here is an elementary certificate. Its constant part is at least C(r)=2r^3+2r^2-7r+8>0. For 0<=r<=1 this is at least 8-7r>=1. For r>=1 it is increasing and C(1)=5. If the coefficient of a in (8) is nonnegative, this proves the claim. Otherwise r<1. Since a<=sqrt(r), replacing a by w=sqrt(r) gives a lower bound. The result is affine in d, with coefficient w^2(6w-5). For w<=5/6 its minimum over 1<=d<=4 occurs at d=4: L_4=2w^6+2w^5+2w^4+7w^2(4w-1)+8(1-w)>0. For w>=1/4 every displayed term is nonnegative. For w<1/4, the last two terms alone exceed 6-7/16>0. For w>=5/6 the minimum occurs at d=1: L_1=2w^6+2w^5+2w^4+10w^3+8(w^2-w+1)>0. Thus Im R>0. Consequently partial_u^2 Re W(u+i eta)<0 (9) for EVERY horizontal line in the band. This proves global horizontal concavity directly from the explicit phase, rather than assuming that a different positive triangulation controls these original reduced coordinates. ## 4. The cubic stationary point and its exact flattening Let rho be the unique real root of rho^3+rho^2-1=0. Elementary evaluation gives 3/4<rho<4/5. Let v_g be the upper-half-plane root of v^3-v^2+1=0, Re v_g=(1+rho)/2, |v_g|^2=1/rho. Define X_g=1/(1+v_g^2), x_g=1+Log(X_g)/(2pi*i)=u_g+i eta_g, y_g=1/2+Log(v_g)/(2pi*i). The critical identities v_g^2(1-v_g)=1 and v_g^5=-(1+v_g) give T_g=v_g^2. On the branch of Section 1, W'(x)=3Log T-Log v-Log(1+v)-i*pi. At the cubic point this is 5Log v_g-Log(1+v_g)-i*pi=0. The sign of pi is fixed: the argument difference lies between -pi/2 and 5pi/2 and is an odd multiple of pi, hence equals pi. Thus (x_g,y_g) is a genuine stationary point of (1) in its stated flattening, not merely a solution of exponentiated equations. Useful exact values are |T_g|=1/rho<4/3, Re(1/T_g)=(1-rho)/2>1/10, D:=|1+T_g|^2=3+rho-rho^2<13/4<4. It follows that eta_g=Log(D)/(4pi)<Log(2)/(2pi). Numerically x_g=.869193400032383...+.092187637885157...i, y_g=.612022435578528...-.022377151124418...i, Re W(x_g)=.450109610025218.... The last decimal is an evaluation of (1). It is not used as a proof of regulator calibration or source intersection. ## 5. Analytic dominance on the sloped outer segment Set theta_g=2pi(1-u_g)=Arg(1+T_g), c=eta_g/(1-u_g)=Log|1+T_g|/theta_g. Then 0<c<1. For completeness theta_g>pi/4: writing 1+T_g=A+iB gives A=(3-rho^2)/2, B^2-A^2=(-2+rho+3rho^2)/2>0. Also Log|1+T_g|<(1/2)Log(13/4)<pi/4. On the sloped segment x=u+i c(1-u), u_g<=u<1, write theta=2pi(1-u), T=exp[(c+i)theta]-1. The function |T| increases with theta on [0,theta_g], so |T|<=4/3. A further useful lower bound is Re(1/T)>=(1-rho)/2>1/10. (10) To prove it, let h(theta)=sinh(c theta) -(2-rho)[cosh(c theta)-cos theta]. It vanishes at both endpoints, by the exact geometric value of Re(1/T_g). Its second derivative is strictly negative: 2-rho>1 and 0<=theta<=theta_g<pi/2. Thus h>=0, which is (10) after using the elementary real coth formula. Equation (6) also gives an absolutely convergent expansion R=-3/T-9/4+E(T), E=(3/4)T+(T+1)(3T-2)/(4T) *[(1+T^2/4)^(-1/2)-1]. For r_T=|T|<2 the binomial derivative bound yields |E|<=3r_T/4+(1+r_T)(2+3r_T)r_T /[32(1-r_T^2/4)^(3/2)]. At r_T<=4/3 the right side is at most 1+63/(20sqrt(5)). Combining with (10), Re R<=(63/sqrt(5)-31)/20<0. (11) The horizontal-band theorem already gives Im R>0 here. Therefore the ENTIRE sloped reduced action satisfies d^2/du^2 Re W(u+i c(1-u)) =2pi[2c Re R-(1-c^2)Im R]<0. (12) Its first derivative vanishes at u_g, so it strictly decreases to the right. This proves the sloped dominance analytically. ## 6. An explicit sufficient outer saddle contour Fix any alpha in (1/2,u_g). The piecewise contour x(u)=u+i min(eta_g,c(1-u)), alpha<=u<=1 (13) has a UNIQUE global maximum of Re W at x_g. The left piece is covered by (9), the right piece by (12), and W'(x_g)=0. There is a strict action gap away from every neighborhood of x_g. The finite endpoint value at u=1 is submaximal by strict decrease, without requiring a separate numerical bound. For an analytic nonzero amplitude with a controlled uniform asymptotic expansion on this contour, ordinary one-variable saddle evaluation therefore has a nonzero Gaussian leading coefficient at x_g. The kink at x_g is harmless: its two tangent directions, 1 and 1-i c, lie in the same negative Gaussian cone. In fact W''(x_g) has negative real AND negative imaginary parts, and c<1, so rotating between those directions keeps the quadratic real part strictly negative. The two local half-rays give the full marked Gaussian, rather than an undetermined zero intersection factor ON THIS specified path. This is not a proof that the original outer residue cycle equals (13). That step must control the actual outer aliases and the inner connector/end-point integrals along the deformation. For example, a constant-height translation of the WHOLE triangle would retain an inner endpoint with action larger than the cubic value; reduced saddle concavity alone would miss it. The exact [inner quadrature theorem](source_preserving_inner_quadrature.md) is an input for that separate source-preserving comparison, not permission to discard its remaining complex endpoint pieces. [Algebra and contour audit](../experiments/audit_five_two_reduced_outer_concavity.py) and [saved diagnostics](../experiments/five_two_reduced_outer_concavity_results.json).

title: Exact Bloch and hyperbolic calibration of the selected five-crossing phase
text: # Exact Bloch and hyperbolic calibration of the selected five-crossing phase 28 October 2026. This identifies the critical value of the EXACT original two-index source in [the finite transform](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md). It does not infer a volume limit from the existence of that critical point. Selection of the finite contour is separate. ## 1. The algebraic point and its logarithmic marks Let rho be the positive real root of rho^3+rho^2-1=0, and put v=(1+rho)/2+i sqrt(1/rho-(1+rho)^2/4). Then v is the upper nonreal root of v^3-v^2+1=0. In particular 1-v=v^(-2), v^3=v^2-1, v^5=-(1+v). X=1/(1+v^2), Y=-v, Z=X/Y, x=1+Log(X)/(2pi i), y=1+Log(Y)/(2pi i). (1) The logarithms on the right are principal; X,Y lie in the lower half-plane. Thus 1/2<Re y<Re x<1. Use the marked primitive J(z)=integral_0^z Log(2sin(pi t))dt, S(x,y)=3J(x)-J(y)-J(x-y) +i pi(3x+2y-x^2-xy-y^2). (2) All three arguments have real part strictly between zero and one. The stationary equations, with the actual marks, are 3Log(1-X)-Log(1-Z)-2(2pi i x)-(2pi i y)+4pi i=0, -Log(1-Y)+Log(1-Z)-(2pi i x)+2pi i=0. (3) Their exponentials are verified by reducing in Q[v]/(v^3-v^2+1): (1-X)^3=X^2 Y(1-Z), 1-Z=X(1-Y). (4) There is no unnoticed integer in (3). For example rho is between 7548/10000 and 7549/10000 by direct polynomial signs and strict monotonicity. Formula (1) then isolates v in the first quadrant near .87744+.74486i, X near .38150-.41040i, and Z near -.02193+.48634i. Principal arguments give Arg(1-X) in (.57,.61), Arg(1-Z) in (-.50,-.40), Im(2pi i x) in (5.44,5.50), Im(2pi i y) in (3.82,3.86). The imaginary part of the first expression in (3) is therefore between -.19 and .20; its real part is zero by (4), so the integer multiple of 2pi i is zero. The second expression is handled by 1-Z=X(1-Y): both Log(1-Z)-Log(1-Y) and principal Log X have arguments in (-pi,0). This proves the marked stationary equations exactly. ## 2. The critical action is its Bloch regulator Write D for the Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm, D(z)=Im Li_2(z)+log|z| Arg(1-z). With l_X=2pi i x and l_Y=2pi i y, direct differentiation and evaluation at zero give 2pi i S=Li_2(1)-3Li_2(X)+Li_2(Y)+Li_2(Z) -l_X^2-l_X l_Y+2pi i(2l_X+l_Y). (5) All dilogarithms have the branches inherited from 0<Re z<1; their arguments avoid [1,infinity). Set a=Re l_X, b=Re l_Y, A=Im l_X, B=Im l_Y. The imaginary part of the polynomial term in (5) is a(4pi-2A-B)+b(2pi-A). Taking imaginary parts of (3) shows that this equals -3log|X| Arg(1-X)+log|Y| Arg(1-Y) +log|Z| Arg(1-Z). Consequently, with no unrecorded additive constant, 2pi Re S(x,y)=-3D(X)+D(Y)+D(Z). (6) ## 3. An explicit finite Bloch identity The right side of (6) is exactly 3D(v). Here is a short proof using only the six cross-ratio symmetries, duplication, and one five-term relation. First 1-v=v^-2 gives D(v^2)=D(v). Duplication D(z^2)=2D(z)+2D(-z) gives D(-v)=-D(v)/2. D(-v^2)=D(X), since X=1/(1+v^2). D(v^4)=2D(v)+2D(X). (7) The same cubic equation gives the literal field identities -v^4=(-v-1)/(-v), A_0=v(1+v)/(1+v^2)=v^8/(v^8-1). (8) Hence D(-v^4)=D(-v), D(A_0)=-D(v^8), and duplication once more gives D(v^8)=2D(v^4)+2D(-v^4)=3D(v)+4D(X). (9) The five-term identity in multiplicative form at (v,-v) is D(v)+D(-v) =D(-v^2)+D(v(1+v)/(1+v^2)) +D(-v(1-v)/(1+v^2)) =D(X)-D(v^8)+D(Z), (10) because 1-v=v^-2. Substitution of (7)-(9) into (10) yields -3D(X)+D(-v)+D(Z)=3D(v). (11) The regulator identities used here can be checked directly: their exterior derivatives vanish using dD=log|z| dArg(1-z)-log|1-z| dArg z, and their real degenerate values fix the constants. Thus (11) is not a numerical rational relation or a conclusion from the degree of the trace field. ## 4. Why 3D(v) is the hyperbolic volume of the marked complement Use the explicitly paired three-tetrahedron p=0 odd family in [the face and angle audit](twist_family_audit.md) and its [independent topological and peripheral audit](twist_topology_and_peripherals.md). That marked family is the 7/3 five-crossing knot complement. Its positive symmetric angle coordinates are U=(A,B,C), V=(A,B,C), W=(B,C,A), A+3C=pi, A+B+C=pi. (12) The face audit proves that averaging into this symmetric locus preserves all edge equations and does not decrease total volume. The full volume is strictly concave. Thus an interior stationary point of the one-dimensional symmetric volume is its full maximum. Put theta=Arg v. From 1-v=v^-2 and the stated branch one has C=theta, B=2theta, A=pi-3theta, all positive. These are the three angles of the ideal shape v, up to cyclic order. The Euclidean sine rule gives |v|=sin B/sin A, |1-v|=sin C/sin A. The modulus relation |v|^2|1-v|=1 therefore says exactly sin^3 A=sin^2 B sin C. (13) Equation (13) is the derivative-zero equation for 3[Lambda(pi-3theta)+Lambda(2theta)+Lambda(theta)]. It is the interior maximum by strict concavity. The explicit multiplier construction in Section 3.5 of the face audit glues the cusp triangles isometrically, gives trivial edge dilation and complete torus cusps, and hence supplies a complete hyperbolic metric. Its three tetrahedra each have volume D(v). The topological marking fixes the complement, and the positive orientation fixes its volume sign. Therefore Vol(S^3 minus 5_2)=3D(v), Re S(x,y)=Vol(S^3 minus 5_2)/(2pi). (14) This step uses the already audited classical face geometry; it assumes no quantum state identity for that triangulation. ## 5. Scope The selected algebraic point has the exact marked volume action. This resolves the calibration of that point. The actual finite source contour and the exclusion of all competing source pieces still have to be established before (14) implies an asymptotic statement for the original invariant. [Exact field identities and marked-regulator diagnostic](../experiments/audit_five_two_selected_bloch_calibration.py).

title: A selected-contour proof for the original five-crossing prototype
text: # A selected-contour proof for the original five-crossing prototype 28 October 2026. This assembles an independent, computer-assisted proof of the volume asymptotic for the ORIGINAL normalized Kashaev invariant of the marked 7/3 five-crossing knot 5_2. It uses exact finite source transforms, explicit contours, and outward-rounded interval bounds. No Jones asymptotic or published quantum-state asymptotic theorem is an input. This is a prototype for the broader goal, not a proof for a broad class of hyperbolic knots. Coverage only: this knot's asymptotic is already the subject of [Ohtsuki, Quantum Topology 7 (2016), 669-735](https://ems.press/journals/qt/articles/14527). Only the publisher's bibliographic record and abstract were consulted for that coverage check. No novelty claim is made for the knot case, and that paper's proof is not an input to the argument below. ## 1. Statement and normalization Let K_N denote the original reduced Kashaev invariant with the cut, Cartan, cups/caps and zero framing specified in [the literal four-plat source](five_two_whole_source_reduction.md). Thus K_2=-7 in this handedness. Let v be the upper nonreal root of v^3-v^2+1=0, X=1/(1+v^2), Y=-v, x_g=1+Log(X)/(2pi i), y_g=1+Log(Y)/(2pi i). Write J'(z)=Log(2sin(pi z)) on 0<Re z<1 with J(0)=0, and S(x,y)=3J(x)-J(y)-J(x-y) +pi i(3x+2y-x^2-xy-y^2), S_g=S(x_g,y_g). Then K_N=C N^(3/2) exp(N S_g) [1+O(1/N)], (1) C != 0, Re S_g=Vol(S^3 minus 5_2)/(2pi). (2) The O constant is for this fixed knot and normalization. In particular lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|K_N| =Vol(S^3 minus 5_2). (3) The phase S_g has its stated logarithmic mark, not a value chosen modulo a constant after taking absolute values. The constant in (1) is C=2pi a(x_g,y_g)/ [sqrt(-S_yy(x_g,y_g)) sqrt(-W''(x_g))], a(x,y)=sqrt(2) exp{[3Log sin(pi x)-Log sin(pi y)-Log sin(pi(x-y))]/2 -pi i(3x+2y)}, (4) W(x)=S(x,y_s(x)). The root y_s and both Gaussian square roots are fixed below by the actual oriented contours. In particular the principal square roots of -S_yy and -W'' at the selected point have positive real parts. Every factor of (4) is nonzero. ## 2. Exact original finite source and controlled real collars The [finite whole-meridian transform](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md) proves, before taking any asymptotic, that K_N=sum_(0<=j<=n<N) Q^[-n(n+2)-j(n+1)] F_n^3/[F_j F_(n-j)], Q=exp(2pi i/N), F_n=(Q;Q)_n. (5) This identity retains the original normalization and all fixed-root meridian derivatives. It is a finite q-binomial proof, not root-color interpolation. The uniform real factorial estimate, including both endpoint rows, gives for each summand in (5) log|summand|=N A(n/N,j/N)+O(log N), A(x,y)=3J(x)-J(y)-J(x-y). (6) Let c_*=max_[0,1]J=J(5/6), so 2c_*=Vol(4_1)/(2pi)<.324. For x<=.51, J(x)<=.01 log 2, and J(y),J(x-y)>=-c_*. Thus A<.345 throughout that low-index region. For x>.5 the REAL angular Hessian of A is strictly negative: if a=cot(pi x), b=cot(pi y), c=cot(pi(x-y)), then b+c>0, a=(bc-1)/(b+c)<0 and det Hess A/pi^2=3-2bc>1. Its inner maximum is therefore at y=x/2. For x>=.99, A(x,y)<=3J(x)-2J(x/2) <=3*.01[1-log(.04)]+.01 log 2 <.134. (7) Here 2sin(pi t)>=4t for 0<=t<=1/2 bounds J(x), and J(x/2)>=-.005 log 2 bounds the other term. Enlarging these strict bounds slightly handles a change of at most 1/N in either cutoff. Take a_N=ceil(.51N+1/2), b_N=floor(.99N-1/2). The omitted terms of (5) have total size O(N^B exp(.345N)) for some fixed B. There are only O(N^2) terms, already included in this polynomial. ## 3. Inner quadrature with the original endpoint source For n in this window, use the ENTIRE interpolation f_(N,n)(w)=Q^[-n(n+2)-w(n+1)] F_n^3/[Fhat_N(w)Fhat_N(n-w)] exp(2pi i w). It agrees with the original summand at every allowed integer w. Exact factorial reflection turns it into a Gaussian times the finite product (Q^(w+1);Q)_(N-1-n). The [inner quadrature theorem](source_preserving_inner_quadrature.md) proves |sum_(j=0)^n f_(N,n)(j)-integral_0^n f_(N,n)(w)dw| <=C log(N+1)|F_n|^2. (8) Summing (8) costs at most C log(N+1) K_(4_1),N, whose proved exponent is 2c_*<.324. All inner discrete corrections are therefore below the selected rate; no Fourier mode is assumed. Define the holomorphic outer function using the SAME interpolation: g_N(z)=exp(4pi i z) integral_0^z Q^[-z(z+2)-w(z+1)] Fhat_N(z)^3/[Fhat_N(w)Fhat_N(z-w)] exp(2pi i w)dw. (9) At integer z=n its value is exactly the integral in (8). Thus the original invariant equals sum_(n=a_N)^(b_N)g_N(n), up to the explicitly bounded collar and inner-quadrature errors. ## 4. Exact outer quadrature, with all four source edges Set L=a_N-1/2, R=b_N+1/2, ell=L/N, r=R/N. Define u_g=Re x_g, h_g=Im x_g, c=h_g/(1-u_g), h(u)=min(h_g,c(1-u)), x_+(u)=u+i h(u), x_-(u)=u-.1i, ell<=u<=r. (10) The [finite-height outer residue formula](source_preserving_outer_finite_height_quadrature.md) expresses the original integer sum EXACTLY as the unweighted integral over z=N x_+(u), plus: * the upper contour with kernel 1/(exp(-2pi i z)-1); * the lower contour with kernel 1/(exp(2pi i z)-1); * the two upper vertical source edges with weights 1/(1+exp(-2pi t)); * the two lower vertical source edges with weights 1/(1+exp(2pi t)). The half-integer edges enclose precisely the original integers. The formula retains the off-lattice exp(4pi i z) character, rather than silently replacing the selected Poisson source. For each complex x on these paths the actual inner contour can be changed, by holomorphy, to 0 -> i lambda(x) -> Re x+i lambda(x) -> x, T=exp(-2pi i x)-1, v(x)=[T+sqrt(T^2+4)]/2, y_s(x)=1/2+Log(v(x))/(2pi i), lambda(x)=Im y_s(x). (11) The square-root branch puts v in quadrant I. All factorial arguments y,x-y have nonnegative real part, at most .99, and stay in a bounded imaginary range. The endpoint-uniform Gamma-product bound in the outer note proves |g_N(Nx)|<=C N^(3/2) exp[N G(x)], G(x)=max_(inner polygon) Re S(x,y). (12) Thus an endpoint singularity contributes at most a polynomial factor; the interior asymptotic is not being applied at zero. ## 5. The rigorous whole-contour bounds There are two independent types of evidence here. The [analytic outer concavity proof](five_two_reduced_outer_contour_concavity.md) shows that W(x)=S(x,y_s(x)) has its unique global maximum of real part on x_+ at x_g. It proves both the constant-height and sloped segments, using their explicit algebraic Hessian. The [analytic inner maximum reduction](selected_inner_angular_contour.md) shows that the full horizontal inner segment has its maximum at the selected saddle or the RIGHT endpoint. Both vertical connectors reduce to their endpoints and at most one explicit stationary point. It proves these assertions for the whole complex strip used in (10)-(11), not merely on sampled points. The resulting one-variable tests have the following certified outward-rounded Arb bounds: | Actual contour piece | Certified phase upper bound | |---|---:| | Upper inner left connector | .200 | | Upper inner right connector, including its interior maximum | .445 | | Entire lower inner polygon, after the outer kernel weight | .400 | | All four outer vertical source edges, with their prescribed weights | .440 | | Selected critical value | .45010 < Re S_g < .45012 | The executable proof is [certify_selected_inner_contours.py](../experiments/certify_selected_inner_contours.py), with [the interval certificate](../experiments/selected_inner_contour_certificate.json). It uses 192-bit acb/arb arithmetic and covers its closed parameter intervals by 1,832 verified dyadic cells. Floating-point displays are not used in a passing comparison. Boundary values use the one-sided J mark, including Re J(i tau)=-pi|tau|/2. The vertical source boxes include u in [.5099,.5101] and [.9899,.9901], so contain the rounded half-grid endpoints for all sufficiently large N. The top and bottom curve bounds hold throughout [.51,.99]. On the upper curve h>=.007, so its weighted phase is at most .45012-2pi*.007<.407, using the analytic outer maximum and the certified inner connectors. Equation (12) and the EXACT outer formula consequently give sum_(n=a_N)^(b_N) g_N(n) =integral_(N x_+) g_N(z)dz +O(N^(5/2) exp(.440N)). (13) The still retained inner connectors of the MAIN upper integral have total size O(N^B exp(.445N)). This is below Re S_g. No cancellation assumption is used to discard any of these pieces. ## 6. The surviving local Gaussian is nonzero On the upper horizontal inner segment, the selected saddle is a strict nondegenerate maximum; the analytic proof gives S_yy=-2pi i(v^2+1)/[v(v+1)], Re S_yy<0. W''=2pi i (v^2+v+4)(v^2+v-1)/(1-v^4). On a fixed complex neighborhood of x_g all connector gaps persist uniformly. The actual interpolation has its nonzero analytic interior amplitude exp(4pi i Nx)K_N(Nx,Ny) =sqrt(N) a(x,y) exp[N S(x,y)] (1+O(1/N)), (14) with a as in (4). Ordinary one-variable Gaussian integration on the specified inner segment gives g_N(Nx)=N a(x,y_s(x)) sqrt(2pi/[-S_yy(x,y_s(x))]) exp[N W(x)](1+O(1/N)). (15) Equation (15) holds uniformly on that fixed complex neighborhood; away from it only the absolute phase estimates are used. This Gaussian has coefficient one: the integral was deformed from its actual finite interval to this single horizontal maximum, with its connectors separately bounded. The analytic outer proof gives Re W''(x_g)<0 and Im W''(x_g)<0, and 0<c<1. Therefore both tangent directions 1 and 1-i c of the bent upper curve belong to the same negative Gaussian cone. The two oriented half-rays combine to the full Gaussian; there is no undetermined intersection coefficient at the kink. A local contour deformation within that cone also gives the usual integer-power expansion. Outside any fixed neighborhood of x_g the strict analytic outer maximum and the certified inner endpoint bounds give an exponential gap. Integrating (15), including dz=N dx, therefore gives (1) with precisely (4). Its power N^(3/2) is N^2 from the two integration measures, sqrt(N) from the factorial amplitude, and N^-1 from two nondegenerate Gaussian variables. Every omitted contribution in Sections 2-5 has a strictly smaller exponential rate. ## 7. Exact marked volume calibration and scope [The explicit Bloch calibration](five_two_selected_bloch_calibration.md) proves, at this same marked critical point, 2pi Re S_g=-3D(X)+D(Y)+D(X/Y)=3D(v) =Vol(S^3 minus 5_2). (16) The first equality uses the marked stationary equations, so all logarithmic modulus terms are accounted for. The second uses one explicit five-term relation and three duplications. The last uses the independently audited three-tetrahedron positive angle maximum and the actual knot marking. Neither numerical agreement nor equality of trace fields is the calibration argument. Equations (1) and (16) prove (3). The broad hyperbolic-knot goal remains open. The reusable part is concrete: an exact finite bridge transform; quadrature whose errors retain and bound the original endpoints; and a certified contour with one nonzero geometric Gaussian. Extending these properties to a sufficiently broad class is required before claiming a general torsor or A-polynomial volume theorem. [Finite-level normalization diagnostics](../experiments/audit_five_two_selected_volume.py) check the displayed nonzero prefactor and marked action against the exact original double sum through N=192. They support the normalization audit; the proof of the limit is the argument and interval certificate above, not extrapolation of those values. Assembly audit, 28 October: two independent agent reviews checked the whole proof, including the finite source identity, both quadratures, the analytic maximum reductions and outward-rounded certificate, the fixed-neighborhood Gaussian expansion, its prefactor and contour orientation, and the exact Bloch/three-tetrahedron calibration. Both reported no remaining conditional source or cycle identification for this prototype. The root review independently checked the source transform, quadrature signs and endpoint estimates, reran the rigorous certificate, and verified the marked finite-level normalization.

title: The actual whole source for the 7/3 five-crossing plat
text: # The actual whole source for the 7/3 five-crossing plat Research note, 27 October 2026. This derives an exact finite source formula for 5_2 from the same oriented mixed-color four-plat method used for 4_1. All turns, the cut coupon, full Cartan scalar and zero-framing correction are retained. Both the three-index Gaussian/Pochhammer formula and its cyclotomic coefficient transform are proved for the whole meridian family. At completeness the transform gives an explicit two-index formula for the original state. This is a diagnostic for arbitrary-bridge source transport, not a restriction of the main volume target to the twist family. No broad selected-period or hyperbolic-volume theorem is asserted here. ## 1. The marked plat and exact framing Set q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=-M/q, Y=M^2=Qx^2, d=N-1 and xvee=x^(-1)Q^(-1). Use beta=sigma_2^2 sigma_1^(-2) sigma_2. (1.1) Its action order is sigma_2, sigma_1^(-1), sigma_1^(-1), sigma_2, sigma_2. With the same rational-tangle marking as in the [figure-eight proof](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md), T=[1 1;0 1], U=[1 0;1 1], T^2 U^2 T (0,1)^t=(7,3)^t. (1.2) This is the two-bridge 7/3 plat, with continued fraction [2,2,1] or [2,3], giving the five-crossing twist-knot diagram 5_2 in the handedness fixed by (1.1). The actual three-braid word used in the earlier prototype is retained as an independent finite evaluation check in the audit; no Jones formula is used. The top colors are [V(x),V(xvee),V(xvee),V(x)] and their orientations are [+, -, -, +]. Every crossing has positive oriented writhe, so the framing correction is the inverse fifth power of the actual color twist. Put A=alpha, B=2d-alpha, so q^A=x, q^B=xvee. The full mixed Cartan contribution is q^((3B^2-2AB)/2). Including the twist q^(-(5/2)(A^2-2dA)) gives exactly q^(3dB)=xvee^(3d). (1.3) Formula (1.3) is included in the contraction. Omitting either its Cartan or framing part would change the whole meridian identity. ## 2. The same literal source has different bottom cap types Use the exact balanced mixed R coefficients and turns from the figure-eight proof. Cut the fourth top leg at index zero. Because this cut is a left pivotal trace, its coupon is D_0=g E_00, and Tr(g^(-1)D_0 C)=C_00. Thus it is the original reduced scalar cut. The top source indices are (a,d-a,d,0), 0<=a<N, and their coefficient, including the two cups and the coupon, is N^2 x^(a-2d). The final colors are now [V(x),V(xvee),V(xvee),V(x)]. Thus the first bottom cap is ev_R(x), while the second is ev_L(x). This differs from the figure-eight contraction and is essential. If the surviving first output index is b and its dual partner is d-b, then the two cap coefficients are x^(d-b)g_b/N=x^(-b)Q^(-b)/N, x^d/N, g_b=x^(-d)Q^(-b). (2.1) All cap and cup factors are literal finite matrices. No ordinary quantum dimension is divided out, and no separate modified trace is assigned to each bridge. ## 3. Forced transfer elimination Write the five transfers in action order as k_1,...,k_5. The first positive crossing has second input index d, so k_1=0. After the next two negative crossings write their transfers as k and ell. The successive states are (a,d,d-a,0), (d-k,a+k,d-a,0), (a+k-ell,d-k+ell,d-a,0), with a+k<N, 0<=ell<=k. (3.1) The fourth positive crossing has transfer j<=a. The last bottom cap forces the fifth transfer to be j-a, hence k_4=a, k_5=0. (3.2) The final state is (a+k-ell,d-a-k+ell,d,0). The first cap relation follows automatically. Thus the exact surviving routes are (0,k,ell,a,0), with support (3.1). This elimination uses only the actual unwrapped finite support. Set j=k-ell, n=a+k and m=a+j=n-ell. The whole boundary factor from the cups, cap types in (2.1), and the coupon is x^(-d-j) Q^(-a-j). Multiplying by the five mixed crossing entries and (1.3), then reflecting the two terminal Gaussian binomials, gives W_(a,k,ell)=(-1)^ell Y^(2d-2n+ell) Q^(a(k+1)+k^2+2k+2-ell*j-ell(ell+1)/2) {n choose k}_Q {k choose ell}_Q (Q/Y;Q)_k (YQ^(-n);Q)_ell (Q^(j+1)/Y;Q)_a. (3.3) The reflection identities used here are {d choose a}_Q=(-1)^a Q^(-a(a+1)/2), {d-j choose ell}_Q =(-1)^ell Q^(-ell*j-ell(ell+1)/2) {j+ell choose ell}_Q. They hold because Q has primitive order N and all upper indices involved are less than N. ## 4. An exact whole-source Gaussian formula Invert the ell factors of (YQ^(-n);Q)_ell in (3.3): (YQ^(-n);Q)_ell =(-Y)^ell Q^(-n*ell+ell(ell-1)/2) (Q^(m+1)/Y;Q)_ell. The signs cancel. The remaining products and binomials simplify by {n choose k}_Q {k choose ell}_Q ={m+ell choose ell}_Q {m choose j}_Q, (Q/Y;Q)_k (Q^(j+1)/Y;Q)_a (Q^(m+1)/Y;Q)_ell =(Q/Y;Q)_(m+ell)(Q^(j+1)/Y;Q)_ell. Their monomial exponent becomes j(m+1)+m+ell+2. We obtain the following proved identity for the actual reduced whole period: F_(5_2),N(Y) =sum_(m,ell>=0,m+ell<N) sum_(j=0)^m Y^(2(N-1-m)) Q^(j(m+1)+m+ell+2) {m+ell choose ell}_Q {m choose j}_Q (Q/Y;Q)_(m+ell)(Q^(j+1)/Y;Q)_ell. (4.1) Every factor is finite. This is a Laurent-polynomial identity before setting Y=1 or Y^N=1. In particular the displayed Y^(2(N-1-m)) is retained, including all of its meridian jets. The exact original full ADO factor d_N(M), if desired, multiplies both sides as its unchanged whole germ. At N=2 the formula gives, exactly, F_(5_2),2(Y)=-2Y-3-2/Y, <5_2>_2=-7. The sign is fixed by the above framing and source, rather than chosen from the knot determinant. ## 5. Reciprocal Newton space and two proved boundary rows Formula (4.1) has minimum Y exponent at least -d, term by term: the minimum in a term is 2d-3m-2ell, and m+ell<=d. The already proved actual Weyl symmetry F(Y)=F(Y^(-1)) therefore bounds the maximum exponent by d as well. Consequently there are unique coefficients C_n^(N), 0<=n<=d, in F_N(Y)=sum_(n=0)^d C_n^(N) T_n(Y), T_n(Y)=product_(r=1)^n(Y+Y^(-1)-Q^r-Q^(-r)). (5.1) This is a statement about whole reciprocal Laurent polynomials, not interpolation of a few root values. The T_n are monic Newton polynomials of degree n in Y+Y^(-1), including at a root Q. The actual anchor at Y=Q gives C_0^(N)=1. The coefficient of Y^(-d) in (4.1) comes only from m=d,ell=0. Since (-1)^d Q^(d(d+1)/2)=1, the top row is exactly C_d^(N)=Q sum_(j=0)^d {d choose j}_Q. (5.2) There is a useful source-basis simplification valid at every n: (1-Y)T_n(Y)=-Y^(n+1)(Q^(-n)/Y;Q)_(2n+1). (5.3) Thus the normal source has one contiguous Pochhammer rather than two separated products. Equation (5.3) follows by inverting (Y;Q)_(n+1) in (1-Y)T_n and joining its factors with (Q/Y;Q)_n. It may be useful when transporting sources through arbitrary bridge convolutions. It does not itself prove the remaining coefficient transform. ## 6. The proved whole-source cyclotomic transform For every primitive Nth root Q, every N>=2, and arbitrary nonzero Y, the exact simplification is C_n(Q)=(-1)^n Q^(-n(n+3)/2) sum_(j=0)^n Q^(-j(n+1)){n choose j}_Q, F_N(Y) =sum_(n=0)^(N-1) C_n(Q) T_n(Y). (6.1) Equivalently its inner summand is Q^(-j(j+1)){n choose j}_(Q^(-1)). The [direct finite proof](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md) starts from (4.1), applies an elementary terminating three-factor q-Chu transform and q-Vandermonde, and then uses a generic Newton connection and a finite root Rogers-polynomial convolution. Every parity sign and source factor is retained. The proof is a Laurent-polynomial identity in Y; repeated ordinary-color nodes are not used as interpolation data. Thus it includes all fixed-root meridian jets and the normal complete-color source. At Y=1, use T_n(1)=(-1)^n Q^(-n(n+1)/2)(Q;Q)_n^2. Writing F_n=(Q;Q)_n, the ORIGINAL reduced Kashaev state is therefore <5_2>_N=sum_(0<=j<=n<N) Q^[-n(n+2)-j(n+1)] F_n^3/[F_j F_(n-j)]. (6.2) This is the exact double sum used by the [source-preserving inner quadrature](source_preserving_inner_quadrature.md). Neither (6.1) nor (6.2) asserts saddle selection, a noncancellation estimate, or a volume limit. The full modified-dimension function remains its original separate factor when the full ADO period is used. ## 7. Independent checks The [literal-path audit](../experiments/audit_five_two_whole_source.py) starts with the original E/Cartan mixed crossing entries, the two exact cups, the fourth-leg coupon, and the differently oriented bottom caps. It sums all paths and checks the forced route pattern and each surviving weight in (4.1). Twenty-seven whole contractions at levels 2 through 10 and three meridians per level pass; eighteen are also compared with the original six-crossing three-braid cut. The audit checks (1.2)--(1.3), the normal-basis product identity, the top Newton row, the proved cyclotomic values and (6.2). The uniform proof of (4.1) is the source and transfer calculation in Sections 1--4. The proof of (6.1) is the separate [finite transform](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md), whose [audit](../experiments/audit_five_two_finite_chu_bridge.py) also compares whole-Y Laurent coefficients and checks the reusable generic and root convolution identities. The finite checks validate the formulas; they do not establish their all-level scope. [Results](../experiments/five_two_whole_source_results.json).

title: Fixed-root Ward data do not admit a literal scalar formalization
text: # Fixed-root Ward data do not admit a literal scalar formalization Research note, 27 October 2026. This isolates an obstruction to one proposed shortcut from the exact all-matrices Hopf-Ward diagram to the geometric Gaussian period. It also specifies what a homological perturbation argument would have to supply. The obstruction applies to a fixed-root, composition-preserving formalization. It does not rule out a linear source-compatible comparison in a larger all-level category, and does not invalidate the partially summed support theorem. ## 1. The fixed-N action cannot become a nontrivial near-identity flow Fix `N>=2`, a characteristic-zero cyclotomic coefficient field, and the actual matrices. Since K^N=x^N I, their conjugation action satisfies (ad_K)^N=I. (1.1) The same relation holds on every tensor Hopf-adjoint matrix space. **Finite-order lemma.** Let `E` be a separated, complete, H-torsion-free module in characteristic zero, with `N` invertible. If a continuous endomorphism `U` satisfies U=I+O(H), U^N=I, then `U=I`. Proof: if `U=I+H^s D mod H^(s+1)`, expansion of the fixed finite power gives `U^N=I+N H^s D mod H^(s+1)`, hence `D=0`. Induction and separatedness give the result. Equivalently the H-adic logarithm exists and `N log U=0`. Consequently a comparison preserving (1.1) cannot send the actual fixed-N adjoint action to a regular operator with principal form U=I+H A(h_sl/2)+O(H^2) and a nonzero conjugation field on a framing coefficient algebra. The same applies to the two cut-stabilizer fields obtained from actual Hopf-adjoint combinations in [the finite Ward calculation](actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction.md). If an equivariant linear map has only an invariant image, this conclusion applies only on that image: `U` acts as identity there. An invariant rank-one scalar quotient is therefore **not** excluded. The obstruction concerns simultaneously retaining the full fixed-N action and realizing its nontrivial classical framing transport on that image. ## 2. All matrices cannot map multiplicatively into scalar symbols Let `A_H` be an H-adically separated, H-torsion-free complete algebra whose special fibre is an integral domain. Then `A_H` is a domain. Indeed two nonzero elements have finite H-valuations, and the product of their first nonzero symbols cannot vanish. The same is true after inverting `H`. There is no unital algebra map End(k^N) -> A_H[1/H], N>1. (2.1) The matrix algebra is simple, so a unital map is injective, whereas its nontrivial orthogonal idempotents cannot inject into a domain. Thus the exact all-matrices finite diagram cannot be mapped multiplicatively to a scalar deformation quantization with a reduced integral geometric special fibre. Even on a smaller subalgebra, the literal nilpotent relation gives a concrete symbol obstruction. The actual raising matrix obeys `Ecal^N=0`. Any composition-preserving scalar principal-symbol map therefore sends it to `e` with `e^N=0`, so `e=0` on the reduced geometric chart. This is incompatible with the nonzero interior moment-map symbol used for the geometric conjugation fields. Matrix-valued formal targets evade the domain statement: they can retain matrix idempotents and nilpotents.
