They do not thereby evade the finite-order lemma if the adjoint action is required to become near identity on the image. Linear maps of current complexes need not preserve products and are not ruled out by (2.1). ## 3. Why this is a fixed-root obstruction, not a contradiction to bulk support For fixed `N`, there is no scalar base change sending the primitive root `Q_N` to `exp(H)` in a characteristic-zero formal field while retaining its defining equation: it would require exp(NH)=1, which is false as a formal power series for nonzero fixed `N`. Equivalently the formal neighbourhood of `Q=1` in `Q^N=1` is the single reduced point `H=0`. The geometric scaling instead has `N` growing and positions of order `1/H`, with `A=Q^a` and `Q^N=1` retained through an independent Frobenius parameter before specialization. It is an all-level unfolding, not the formal completion of one finite matrix algebra. This is exactly why the proper-ratio construction in [the partial support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md) is legitimate: it first proves a rational contiguity identity in independent variables and only then specializes its central parameter. It does not map every fixed-N matrix and every finite relation into the scalar formal coefficient algebra. The source itself makes the distinction visible. In the finite color algebra `C_N=k[A^+/-1]/(A^N-1)`, canonical representatives obey A f_tilde-(Af)_tilde=f_(N-1)(A^N-1). The cut of `(Af)_tilde` contains `f_(N-1)`, even though ordinary multiplication by `A` followed by the zero residue does not. This degree-near-N carry is part of the exact source. A bounded-degree scalar formal coefficient expansion cannot silently replace it. The [relative source construction](relative_framing_source_transgression.md) retains it explicitly and is linear rather than multiplicative. ## 4. What homological perturbation would prove, if its hypotheses were supplied Here is a precise sufficient formal statement. Work in a common H-complete **source-unfolded** category, with all endpoint and carry components included. Suppose a complex `(C,d0)` has a contraction onto a one-degree geometric line `G`, with maps `p,i,k` satisfying p i=I, d0 k+k d0=I-i p, k^2=k i=p k=0. The line may carry its retained exponential regulator factor; scalar coefficients and formal units are taken after that factor is fixed. Suppose `d=d0+Delta` is a differential, and `k Delta` and `Delta k` raise the H filtration by at least one. Define i_D=(I+k Delta)^(-1)i, p_D=p(I+Delta k)^(-1), k_D=k(I+Delta k)^(-1), d_G=p Delta(I+k Delta)^(-1)i. All inverse operators here are the convergent geometric series in the stipulated filtration, and `p_D=p+O(H)`. These signs use `d0 k+k d0=I-i p`. The identities follow by substituting `i_D=i-k Delta i_D` and `d0 Delta+Delta d0+Delta^2=0`; for example they give `d i_D=i_D d_G`. The corresponding identities for `p_D,k_D` follow by the same multiplication, yielding the perturbed contraction. Since `G` is concentrated in one degree, `d_G=0`. If the original marked closed source `c` is a d-cocycle and p(c mod H)!=0, then `p_D c` is nonzero: its first coefficient is the displayed nonzero projection. A compatible diagram of actual partial traces and Ward complexes would carry this class to a scalar Ward line. If its leading scalar map is nonzero, the perturbed scalar map is a unit and the class survives. The exact finite cut homotopy `Phi-p=b delta` would then identify its prescribed cut with that scalar projection. This would be a formal source-survival theorem; it would still assert no convergence or selected rootwise asymptotic. The compatibility requirement is substantial. Given chain maps in a diagram, perturbation transports them to `p_D' f i_D`, but their nonzero leading action must be checked. Chain-map identities and normalization of a different class do not force it. ## 5. Which hypotheses are already available The current notes supply the following separate exact inputs: * A nonzero transverse geometric Gaussian contraction with two actual framing coordinates left external, including exact contiguity. * A literal finite relative source complex and the original `psi,phi,e,D`, with all canonical carries retained. * An exact finite Hopf-adjoint partial-trace chain map for every matrix, and a finite cut Ward contraction onto `k I`. * The uniform nonzero classical normal density in the marked cut determinant line. They do not yet supply a common source-unfolded complex `C`, its unperturbed source-compatible contraction, the perturbation `Delta` realizing the actual Ward currents after transverse elimination, or the nonzero leading scalar map on the **geometric** class. In particular the auxiliary relative coordinate of the finite source has not been identified with the internal Gaussian framing mode. The finite Ward homotopy cannot merely be inserted into the formal geometric series and declared small. Its coefficients contain 1/(k_a-k_b)=1/[x(exp(-Ha)-exp(-Hb))] =1/[x H(b-a)]+O(1) for fixed `a!=b`, and the cumulative F inverse likewise contains `1/(1-exp(H(r+1)))`. Thus an `O(H)` correction need not make `k Delta` topologically nilpotent. A suitable rescaled classical complex may repair this, but its source and endpoint compatibility must be constructed. Polynomial bounds in `N` do not establish the required H-adic smallness. There is therefore no justified HPL shortcut from the current separate inputs to scalar source survival. A literal multiplicative fixed-root-to-scalar formalization is impossible by Sections 1--2. A linear all-level comparison, retaining the Frobenius and source normal directions and explicitly transporting the currents, remains possible and is the appropriate next algebraic object. The finite all-matrices chain map alone does not construct it.

title: The flat cyclic source frame is rigid; its scalar period is separate
text: # The flat cyclic source frame is rigid; its scalar period is separate Independent algebraic theorem, 27 October 2026. The actual highest-input clock, cyclic repair and paired source have a whole matrix-algebra description BEFORE quantum jets. On the source-cyclic chart their scheme-theoretic classification is elementary. A rank-one defect must be aligned with the actual source line; rank one alone does not imply this. The rigid frame does not fix the scalar of a closed transport. ## 1. The actual source frame and its coefficient ring Fix N>=2, Q a unit, and invert only 1-Q^k for 1<=k<N. Write delta=1-Q^N, B_0=diag(1,Q,...,Q^(N-1)), P_0 e_j=e_(j+1 mod N), E_0=E_00, A_0=e_0 1^t. Here 1^t is the ORIGINAL all-ones output row. These are the literal highest-input data of [the actual two-wall boundary](actual_highest_whittaker_boundary_and_moving_walls.md), not an additional state. Direct entries give B_0 P_0-Q P_0 B_0=delta E_(0,N-1), B_0 P_0 B_0^-1 P_0^-1 =Q[I+(Q^-N-1)E_0], B_0 A_0=A_0, A_0 P_0=A_0, A_0^2=A_0, P_0^N=I, E_0 A_0=A_0, A_0 E_0=E_0. (1.1) The last two identities express equality of the two IMAGE lines. They do not identify the source row with the defect row: E_0 is e_0 e_0^t, whereas A_0 is e_0 1^t. That distinction is retained. The normalization A_0^2=A_0 is the specified primitive pair 1^t e_0=1. Any original external d_N(M) line remains attached as that exact separate source factor; it is not divided away at one of its zeros/poles to obtain this primitive matrix statement. Without the specified normalization, BA=A and AP=A allow every scalar multiple a A_0, so even the source scale would be free. Work with rank-N vector bundles over this coefficient ring or any specified COMMUTATIVE base algebra. Source and defect projectors have locally free image of rank one. No delta inverse is adjoined. ## 2. An explicit classification on the cyclic source chart Let E have rank N, let P be invertible with P^N=I, and let A be an idempotent rank-one source. Put L=im A. Suppose BA=A, AP=A, im(BP-QPB) contained in L, (2.1) and suppose the source orbit map Theta: direct_sum_(j=0)^(N-1) L -> E, Theta(l_0,...,l_(N-1))=sum_j P^j l_j (2.2) is an isomorphism. Then in this CANONICAL line-valued frame P=P_0 tensor I_L, B=B_0 tensor I_L, A=A_0 tensor I_L. (2.3) Proof. AP^j=A makes A act by summing the N input copies into the zeroth copy. P cycles them. BA=A makes the first column of B equal to (I_L,0,...,0)^t. Every entry of B in this frame is an endomorphism of L, hence a scalar over the base. Since the image in (2.1) lies in the zeroth copy, the other rows give B_(i,j+1 mod N)=Q B_(i-1,j), 1<=i<N. (2.4) For i>=j this recurrence and the first column yield B_(i,j)=Q^j delta_(i,j). For i<j they yield B_(i,j)=Q^i B_(0,j-i). The wrap case j=N-1 in (2.4) has left side zero, forcing every B_(0,k)=0 for 1<=k<N. This proves (2.3). In particular B is automatically invertible. No wall cancellation, eigenvalue argument or flatness theorem was needed for this proof. This is a classification over arbitrary base algebras on the specified open chart, including algebras with nilpotents. Its groupoid is the groupoid of line bundles L, by E=L^direct_sum N. If E is required to be globally free, retain the corresponding trivialization condition on that direct sum. Over a local base L is free. Choosing a source vector v trivializing L, with Av=v, makes Theta a canonical ordinary basis and removes all its automorphisms. Without that vector marking the remaining automorphisms are precisely multiplication by a central unit on L. The cyclic hypothesis is automatic near the actual root source. Indeed at a primitive Q_N the actual multiplicative relation reduces to BP=Q_N PB. If Bv=v, the N vectors P^jv have distinct eigenvalues Q_N^j. They are nonzero and independent over every residue field. Rank N makes them a basis. In a local deformation of that root point their determinant stays a unit, proving (2.2). This does not assert cyclicity on unrelated global components. ## 3. The multiplicative defect and its explicit flat saturation Suppose also that R is a rank-one idempotent with AR=R, RA=A, BPB^-1P^-1=Q[I+(Q^-N-1)R]. (3.1) The image of its commutator lies in im R=L, so Section 2 applies. In its canonical frame R=e_0 rho with rho_0=1. Equations (1.1) and (3.1) reduce EXACTLY to delta (R-E_0)=0, delta rho_j=0, 1<=j<N. (3.2) If the base is flat over the normal parameter, or more generally delta is a nonzero divisor on it, (3.2) forces R=E_0. This is the actual normalized defect, recovered before taking jets. The unsaturated presentation has the explicit coordinate algebra R_base[rho_1,...,rho_(N-1)]/(delta rho_j). (3.3) When delta is a nonzero divisor on R_base, this presentation is not flat at the wall. Its delta-saturation kills the rho_j and is just R_base. If the supplied base already has delta-torsion, saturation also removes that base torsion. At delta=0 alone the multiplicative relation cannot see these projector-row parameters. A rank-N module can be locally free over this nonflat comparison base; that is not a substitute for flatness/saturation of the base over the normal parameter. If the module itself is flat over that normal base, the nonzero-divisor hypothesis above applies. If R is marked to be the actual E_0, these excess parameters never arise. ## 4. The whole endpoint-corrected algebra is a matrix algebra Set chi(X)=product_(j=0)^(N-1)(X-Q^j), D=R[X]/chi(X), e_j(X)=product_(k!=j)(X-Q^k)/(Q^j-Q^k). The node differences are units in the stated head localization. Evaluation at them identifies D with R^N: the e_j are orthogonal idempotents summing to one. The polynomial map tau(X)=Q^-1[X-delta e_0(X)] (4.1) cycles these evaluations, so it is an algebra automorphism with tau^N=I and tau(e_j)=e_(j+1 mod N). Form the explicit algebra with basis f P^a, f in D, 0<=a<N, and multiplication (f P^a)(g P^b)=f tau^a(g)P^(a+b mod N). (4.2) Associativity follows from tau being an automorphism. Define E_(i,j)=e_i P^(i-j mod N). These satisfy E_(i,j)E_(k,l)=delta_(j,k)E_(i,l), sum_i E_(i,i)=I. They form a basis: fixing i,a recovers e_iP^a uniquely. Therefore (4.2) is EXACTLY Mat_N(R), with no rank comparison or unverified quiver theorem as a premise. The original source is recovered by A_0=e_0 sum_(j=0)^(N-1)P^j, Tr(A_0)=1. (4.3) Thus the original paired-source matrix can be recovered from the flat normalized defect and cyclic transport; the defect and source rows remain different. Every coefficient, root norm and endpoint term is retained in (4.1), rather than imposing an impossible whole BP=QPB with P^N=I. This adds the explicit finite ALIGNED SOURCE classification and whole matrix-algebra presentation to the boundary note. It does not duplicate or contradict [the whole clock function theorem](whole_clock_function_algebra_and_endpoint_extension.md). That theorem concerns the UNCORRECTED infinite-order shift on a coalescing clock and requires its endpoint tower. Here the nodes Q^j are distinct at each fixed primitive root, and (4.1) changes the last shift by its actual finite endpoint defect. A fixed-N head localization is not a common neighborhood of Log Q=0 as N grows. This finite algebra does not discard whole functions, unwrapped Green tails or their separate source extension. ## 5. Rank one without source alignment is insufficient There are flat rational families through the actual N=2 root which satisfy every OTHER condition but are not the canonical clock. Put near Q=-1 delta=1-Q^2, h=Q-Q^-1, t=delta/(1-delta^2), x=delta^2/(1-delta^2), P=[[0,1],[1,0]], A=[[1,1],[0,0]], B=[[1,t h],[0,Q+x h]], R=[[1+x,-t],[t,-x]]. (5.1) All entries are rational and regular there; B is invertible. Since t^2=x(1+x), direct multiplication proves R^2=R, Tr R=1, rank R=1, BA=A, AP=A, P^2=I, BPB^-1P^-1=Q[I+(Q^-2-1)R]. (5.2) At Q=-1 these are EXACTLY B_0,P_0,A_0,E_0. Nevertheless the second eigenvalue Q+xh of B is generically different from Q, so no conjugation can identify it with B_0. The rank-N module and every displayed rational family are flat. What fails is AR=R, namely alignment of the moving defect with the actual source line. Even correct classical source/defect markings and flatness of the objects do not impose that whole relation. Taking delta replaced by delta^k in x,t makes the tilt invisible to an arbitrarily long fixed jet, without changing this conclusion. The ACTUAL fixed E_00 defect is aligned and is covered by the positive theorem, not by this counterexample. ## 6. The scalar closed period is not fixed by this frame Over any base the commutant of the matrix units in Section 4 consists of scalars: commuting with E_ii makes a matrix diagonal, and commuting with E_ij makes all its diagonal entries equal. Consequently a closed frame-intertwiner is C=c I, Tr(A_0 C)=c, (6.1) with c an ARBITRARY scalar (a unit if C is invertible). Adjoining c, or an invertible c, gives a flat finite-type extension with the exact same frame, defect and normalized source. Source-frame classification alone imposes no equation on that period. It also does not supply a regulator action or fix a leading norm. This is a statement about insufficient structural conditions, not permission to change the original actual knot state. Once the complete actual crossing word and every scalar/cap/peripheral normalization are supplied, that word fixes c. A comparison of the FULL word evaluations through the canonical source frame preserves it automatically. Merely identifying their clock/source matrix algebras does not compare their selected word sections. There is no contradiction with strict vector-pointed rigidity. An intertwiner C preserving a specified nonzero v must satisfy cv=v and hence c=1. A generic actual knot period C=cI is NOT such a source-vector-preserving automorphism; it preserves the coupon A by conjugation while its cut pairing is c. Demanding strict preservation at that final step would assume the desired normalization and exclude the actual nontrivial period. Here the actual scalar-knot example is on its original ROOT fiber with generic M. Its whole auxiliary q-normal lift need not be scalar, as the explicit unknot in [the one-index source audit](actual_one_index_fourier_source_and_ward_reduction.md) shows. No extension of root scalarity is used in this argument. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_flat_cyclic_source_frame.py) and [saved results](../experiments/flat_cyclic_source_frame_results.json) check the universal recurrence equations, all matrix units/source moments, arbitrary conjugate frames, wall parameters and the explicit nonaligned rational family. No geometric selected-cycle or hyperbolic-volume theorem follows from this finite-frame result. The [independent proof audit](mobius_and_flat_source_frame_independent_audit.md) checks the commutative-base classification, corrected crossed product, saturation scope and nonaligned counterexample. It also distinguishes the actual root scalar closure from its auxiliary whole q-normal lift.

title: A flat pointed torsor lifts; an etale classical optimizer need not
text:
# A flat pointed torsor lifts; an etale classical optimizer need not Independent proof and audit, 27 October 2026. This adds a constructive comparison formula and a flatness criterion to [whole cyclotomic reconstruction](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md). It also gives rational quantum objects for which a unique reduced classical pointed comparison fails to lift. Thus it distinguishes an actual sufficient theorem from an implication that classical Rivin rigidity alone does not supply. The fixed-meridian Rees Poisson map and its new whole Heisenberg primitive are checked in Section 5. Section 6 gives a concrete actual crossing obstruction to a naive positive weighted-norm proof. None of the statements below asserts the selected volume asymptotic. ## 1. A flat marked comparison has exactly one lift Let \(R=k[[\epsilon]]\), with \(k\) of characteristic zero. Suppose a whole, bounded algebraic comparison problem has been specified, including its sources, cuts and lattice. Complete its comparison algebra at a chosen classical point and call the resulting \(R\)-algebra \(B\). Assume \[ B/\epsilon B=k,\qquad  igcap_{n\geq 0}\epsilon^nB=0, \qquad \epsilon	ext{ is a nonzero divisor on }B. 	ag{1} \] Then \(R\longrightarrow B\) is an isomorphism. In particular the marked comparison exists uniquely to every formal quantum order. Here is a direct proof. Given \(b\in B\), choose its residue \(c_0\in k\) and write \(b=c_0+\epsilon b_1\). Repeat this for \(b_1\), obtaining \[ b-\sum_{j<n}c_j\epsilon^j\in\epsilon^nB. \] The element \(f=\sum c_j\epsilon^j\in R\) therefore maps to \(b\), by separatedness. Thus \(R	o B\) is surjective. A nonzero element of its kernel would be \(\epsilon^m\) times a unit, contradicting the last condition of (1) and \(B/\epsilon B
e0\). This proves the assertion. Over this DVR, the last condition is exactly \(R\)-flatness. A finite separable marked classical residue field is handled after its specified unramified base extension. With a finite algebraic presentation, this is a statement about its selected algebraic formal germ; it does not assert that an arbitrary formal period is algebraic. The same result retains several normal directions. Let \(R\) be any complete Noetherian local ring, with maximal ideal \(\mathfrak m\) and residue field \(k\). If \(B\) is separated for \(\mathfrak mB\), is \(R\)-flat, and \(B/\mathfrak mB=k\) through the specified residue map, then \(B=R\). Choose generators of \(\mathfrak m\) and repeat the residue argument by total degree; completeness of \(R\) and separatedness of \(B\) give \(B=R/I\), \(I\subseteq\mathfrak m\). Flatness, applied to \(0	o I	o R\) and tensoring with \(B\), forces \(I/I^2=0\). Since \(I\) is finitely generated and \(I=I^2\subseteq\mathfrak mI\), Nakayama gives \(I=0\). Thus quantum and meridian normals can be retained together. There is a useful converse formulation. The first two conditions already imply \(B=R/I\). If comparisons exist modulo \(\epsilon^n\) for every \(n\), the maps \(R/I	o R/\epsilon^n\) give \(I\subseteq(\epsilon^n)\) for all \(n\); hence \(I=0\). No additional choice of compatible lifts is needed once the pointed comparison is unique. Comparisons at several different cyclotomic levels become such a test only after a fixed whole presentation and the reconstruction hypotheses have been supplied. This is a genuine existence theorem for a flat whole pointed comparison. Flatness of the two objects separately is a different condition. ## 2. Cyclic pointing constructs the only possible comparison Here the comparison need not be guessed. Let \(A\) be a coefficient algebra with an automorphism \(\sigma\). Let \(V_i=A^r\) carry the semilinear transport \(T_i(v)=A_i\sigma(v)\), source \(s_i\), and cut \(\ell_i\), for \(i=1,2\). Form the cyclic matrices \[ V_i^{m cyc}=[s_i,T_i s_i,\ldots,T_i^{r-1}s_i]. \] Assume their determinants are units on the marked lattice chart. Define \[ C=V_2^{m cyc}(V_1^{m cyc})^{-1},\qquad a_i=(V_i^{m cyc})^{-1}T_i^r s_i,\qquad m_i=\ell_i V_i^{m cyc}. 	ag{2} \] Then \(C\) and its inverse are regular on that chart, and \[ CT_1=T_2C,\quad Cs_1=s_2,\quad\ell_2C=\ell_1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a_1=a_2,\quad m_1=m_2. 	ag{3} \] Moreover \(C\) is the only pointed transport comparison. Indeed every such comparison must send each \(T_1^j s_1\) to \(T_2^j s_2\), which forces (2). Its transport residual vanishes on the first \(r-1\) cyclic vectors. On the last vector it vanishes exactly when their last cyclic relations \(a_i\) agree. Equivalently, \[ A_i\sigma(V_i^{m cyc})=V_i^{m cyc}\operatorname{Comp}(a_i); \] substituting (2) proves the transport identity. The cut identity is exactly equality of the two rows \(m_i\). Consequently, near a regular cyclic classical comparison, its whole comparison algebra is \[ B=R/I,\qquad I=(	ext{entries of }a_1-a_2,\ m_1-m_2), 	ag{4} \] with additional supplied connection residuals included if required. This makes the flatness defect an explicit finite obstruction ideal. Classical agreement says only \(I\subseteq(\epsilon)\); flatness says \(I=0\). If the objects and these finitely many iterates have a fixed bounded algebraic presentation, the [cyclotomic jet theorem](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) tests the residuals in (3), after denominators and algebraic norms are handled in the stated lattice. Thus a regular cyclic source gives a canonical comparison and a finite exact certificate. There is no unknown unbounded family of levelwise gauges in this construction. The hypotheses are substantive: the rank must be fixed for a uniform test, both cyclic determinants must be units, and the whole transports and pointings must already exist. Generic cyclicity away from a source boundary does not imply these unit conditions. The full finite \(N\)-dimensional module and a rank-one local geometric block are also not interchangeable objects. For compatible differential period connections, horizontality can follow from this uniqueness. If the connections commute with transport, and the two source connection laws agree under \(C\), then \(E=
abla_2C-C
abla_1\) commutes with transport and kills the source. It kills every cyclic vector, so \(E=0\). For the mixed quantum and meridian law, the extra meridian intertwining in [the whole comparison theorem, Section 5](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) is required. This argument does not construct either connection. ## 3. Two explicit failures of classical-to-quantum lifting ### Flat objects with a nonflat pointed comparison Take rank-one free \(R\)-modules, with transports \(T_1=1\) and \(T_2=1+\epsilon\), and sources \(s_1=s_2=1\). Both objects are flat. A source-preserving comparison is forced to be \(C=1\), so its remaining equation is \(\epsilon=0\). Its comparison algebra is \(R/(\epsilon)\). There is one reduced classical pointed comparison and no quantum lift. The same example works for meridian-difference transports \(T_1=\sigma\), \(T_2=(1+\epsilon)\sigma\) over \(k(Y)[[\epsilon]]\), with \(\sigma(Y)=e^\epsilon Y\). It has the same classical graph \(L=1\), etale over \(Y\). Thus etaleness of that graph and flatness of the objects do not imply flatness of their pointed comparison. ### Even the unpointed algebraic gauge can fail Put \(Q=e^\epsilon\), \(\sigma(Y)=QY\), and compare the rank-one transport multipliers \[ a_1(Q,Y)=1,\qquad a_2(Q,Y)=1+ rac{Q-1}{Y}. 	ag{5} \] They are rational whole functions, regular formally at \(Q=1\), with the same classical etale graph \(L=1\). An algebraic formal unit solving the gauge equation \(\sigma g=a_2g\), with leading term \(g_0\), would satisfy \[ Y\partial_Yg_0=g_0/Y,\qquad d\log g_0=dY/Y^2. 	ag{6} \] This is impossible on every finite algebraic cover. A logarithmic derivative of an algebraic meromorphic function has only simple poles. At a place \(Y=t^e\), the right side of (6) has pole order \(e+1>1\). The analytic solution \(g_0=\exp(-1/Y)\) demonstrates precisely the excluded irregularity. Multiplying both multipliers by any common nonzero rational \(a_0(Y)\) gives the same failure over the graph \(L=a_0(Y)\). The issue is therefore not the particular constant classical graph. At first quantum order, the difference of subprincipal transport defines the necessary logarithmic connection (6); classical etaleness does not trivialize that connection. The full cyclic norm detects the failure exactly: \[ \prod_{j=0}^{N-1}a_2(Q_N,Q_N^jY) =1-\left(- rac{Q_N-1}{Y}ight)^N
e1. 	ag{7} \] For fixed \(Y
e0\), its difference from one is smaller than every power of \(1/N\). Thus even this rational transport produces a curvature error invisible to its asymptotic \(1/N\) expansion. It is visible to the *exact* whole cyclotomic test. In the opposite direction, the independently proved [full rank-one descent theorem](full_rank_one_cyclotomic_descent.md) does give a positive result: a comparison multiplier in \(\mathbb Q(Q,Y)^*\), with exact whole norm one at every sufficiently large root, has one rational gauge. Other coefficient fields require the whole-root marking in that theorem. Its source anchor fixes the residual scalar, provided the gauge and inverse are regular on the prescribed source lattice. Equations (5)--(7) explain why the whole norm hypothesis cannot be replaced by a classical optimizer or an all-orders asymptotic norm identity. ## 4. The actual Rees source has a concrete regular-lifting obstruction The [actual Rees construction](irregular_rees_full_cyclic_module.md) has block clock \(D_Zf(u)=f(Zu)\), \(Z=Q^N\), and \[ G^{-1}D_ZG=e^{u/N}D_Z,\qquad G=e^{u/[N(Z-1)]}. 	ag{8} \] The original vacuum is fixed by \(D_Z\). There is no regular clock intertwiner sending this vacuum to a nonzero regular limiting vector. For such an intertwiner \(C\), applying (8) to the vacuum and reducing at \(Z=1\) would give \[ (e^{u/N}-1)\,C_0(1)=0 \quad	ext{in }k[[u]], \] so \(C_0(1)=0\). Allowing mixing among head clocks does not help: the equations become \((Q_N^j e^{u/N}-1)f_j(u)=0\), and each factor is a nonzero divisor. The exact irregular gauge instead sends the source to \(e^{-u/[N(Z-1)]}\), as retained in that note. This is not a claim that two identical whole-center families are inequivalent: their normal central characters differ, and the source gauge is explicitly irregular. It is a concrete warning that a regular generator-module limit and matching closed-point data do not produce a regular pointed lift through the source boundary. The newly regular Rees module has not silently made the comparison algebra flat. ## 5. Independent check of the Rees Poisson and period formulas The new Sections 6--7 of [the Rees module note](irregular_rees_full_cyclic_module.md) are sound. With \(d=N(Q^N-1)\), \[ (Q^{N^2}-1)/d\longrightarrow1,\qquad (Q^{-N^2}-1)/d\longrightarrow-1. \] They give \(\{k,e\}=ke,\ \{k,f\}=-kf\); the actual universal Casimir gives \(\{e,f\}=k^{-1}-k\). For \(\{p,u\}=1\), \[ U=e^{up},\quad k=\gamma M^N/U,\quad e=p\gamma(M^N/U-M^{-N}),\quad f=(1-U)/p \] has exactly these brackets, and \[ du\wedge dp=d\log U\wedge d\log p =-d\log k\wedge d\log e. \] At \(M=1\), \(v=1/p,w=e/\gamma\) gives \(\Omega=dw\wedge dv/(1+wv)\), with the stated regular E-wrap limit \(w/N\). The fixed-root normal \(d\) remains distinct from the physical \(2\pi i/N\). The new [whole Gauss period transgression](rees_gauss_period_transgression.md) also checks. For \(B=M^N,t=U/B^2\), its four period coordinates satisfy the flat algebraic connection \[ d\mu=dB/B,\quad d\xi=dt/t,\quad d\ell=-dt/(1-t),\quad dH=\xi\,d\ell. \] This is a fixed Heisenberg times additive-logarithm torsor, before level restriction. With \(x=\xi+2\mu\), \[ W=H+2\mu\ell-x^2/2,\qquad 	heta_{m Gauss}-	heta_{m source} =dW+(x-2\ell)d\mu . \] Both the sign and the peripheral correction follow by direct differentiation. The resolved \(M=1\) primitives have exterior derivative \(dw\wedge dv/(1+wv)\); their difference is the derivative of the stated regular \(W-\operatorname{Li}_2(1)\). This is an actual local period connection, not merely matching symplectic dimensions. Its existence does not by itself prove a flat pointed comparison with the irregular selected source. ## 6. Scalarity does not make a positive weighted norm sharp There is an actual crossing example, requiring no speculative analytic sector. Close one leg of a positive checked crossing at complete color \(M=1\). This is the framed unknot kink. Write \[ Q=e^{2\pi i/N},\quad q=e^{\pi i/N},\quad x=-q^{-1}, \qquad P_a(Q)=(Q;Q)_a. \] At fixed cut index \(a\), closure forces the crossing index \(k=a-b\), \(0\le b\le a\). Substituting the actual balanced crossing and pivot gives the diagonal cut terms \[ x^{1-N}\, Q^{b^2} rac{P_a(Q)^2}{P_b(Q)^2P_{a-b}(Q)}. 	ag{9} \] For clarity, the unsubstituted crossing coefficient is \[ (-1)^kq^{k^2} \left[\prod_{j=b+1}^{a}(Q^{-j}-1)ight] {a rack k}_Q\, x^{-a-b}Q^{ab}\, (xQ^{-b})^{1-N}; \] elementary cancellation gives (9), including its phase. The exact finite identity \[ \sum_{b=0}^{a} Q^{b^2} rac{P_a(Q)^2}{P_b(Q)^2P_{a-b}(Q)}=1 	ag{10} \] can be proved without importing a knot formula. Partitions with largest part at most \(a\) have generating function \(1/P_a\). Separate them by their Durfee square of size \(b\). Its weight is \(Q^{b^2}\); the part below it has generating function \(1/P_b\), and the rectangle to its right has generating polynomial \({a rack b}_Q=P_a/(P_bP_{a-b})\). This proves (10) as a formal rational identity, hence at every root with \(a<N\). The exact kink scalar is \(x^{1-N}\), of modulus one. Nevertheless, if \(4\mid N\), \(a=N/2,b=N/4\), the modulus of this one closed term is \[  rac{P(N/2)^2}{P(N/4)^3},\qquad P(m)=\prod_{r=1}^{m}2\sin(\pi r/N). \] The integrable logarithmic Riemann sum gives \[ \lim_{4\mid N	o\infty} rac1N\log|	ext{term}| = rac{3\,G}{2\pi}>0, 	ag{11} \] where \(G=\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2\). Indeed \(\int_0^{1/2}\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt=0\) and \(\int_0^{1/4}\log(2\sin\pi t)\,dt=-G/(2\pi)\). Every internal diagonal basis weight cancels around this closed term; a normalized cut basis vector and its dual cancel their external weight too. Thus any bound obtained by replacing all entries by absolute values, including products of induced coordinate weighted norms, is at least this exponentially large term. It cannot be sharp for the unit scalar (10). This does not rule out a specially chosen wavepacket or a phase-sensitive propagation theorem. For this kink, the cut \(a=0\) is already cancellation-free. It does show why scalarity alone and strict concavity of a classical shape functional do not supply the required sharp positive norm for an arbitrary normalized source. A useful coherent-state argument must prove its phase-sensitive propagation and stability through the actual crossings and caps, rather than infer them from the algebraic optimizer. ## 7. The concrete whole-torsor task There is now a precise positive route: construct the two whole pointed objects, prove regular cyclicity on their marked lattices, and evaluate the finite residuals (3). A flat comparison algebra, or sufficiently deep exact cyclotomic tests in the fixed presentation, then gives the unique comparison; a compatible marked connection gives horizontality. Rivin rigidity supplies the unique algebraic geometric place. The new Rees--Gauss identity supplies a fixed algebraic period connection on actual source coordinates. Neither presently implies the comparison-flatness or removes the irregular projectors. Those are explicit equations and source conditions to prove. Even after that algebraic comparison, the physical large-level norm requires a calibrated nonzero selected contribution and its growth estimate.

title: A strict Fock-to-cyclic-normal Mellin map and its logarithmic obstruction
text: # A strict Fock-to-cyclic-normal Mellin map and its logarithmic obstruction Research construction, 27 October 2026. This gives an explicit linear comparison from the actual completed Fock source to the whole cyclic normal source, including its Weyl operators, cut, pivot adapter and relative endpoint carry. The target must retain a marked logarithmic torsor. A global algebraic comparison with the same nonzero vacuum and normal derivative is impossible on every finite cover. The comparison below is between specified source/normal complexes. It is not an algebra map of fixed-N matrix algebras and does not identify their full quantum-group actions. It also does not fix the physical 2pi*i adapter required for a geometric Fourier integral. ## 1. The two actual source modules and the explicit map Fix a primitive N-th root Q in characteristic zero. In [the common-Verma source](common_verma_two_wall_source.md), write the completed Fock module as Fhat=H[[t]], h_j t^r/r!=v_(rN+j), B=partial_t, T=t, [B,T]=I, 0<=j<N. Here H is the original balanced finite head, with source psi=1 and co-source phi=(1/N)sum_j. Its block vacuum projection is pi_0. Retain the whole cyclic normal algebra and physical derivative: Chat=k[[U-1]][A]/(A^N-U), D_phys=A partial_A+N U partial_U, nabla=D_phys/N. Mark alpha(U)^N=U, alpha(1)=1. Put u=Log U, u(1)=0, and epsilon_j=(1/N)sum_(l=0)^(N-1)Q^(-jl)(A/alpha)^l. These are mutually orthogonal idempotents summing to one. They evaluate to delta_(j,a) on A=alpha Q^a, and nabla epsilon_j=0. The literal topological linear isomorphism is M(v_(rN+j))=epsilon_j u^r/r!. (1.1) It is invertible because the epsilon_j form a basis over k[[U-1]] and u is a formal parameter with first coefficient U-1. Directly, M B=nabla M, M T=(Log U)M, M theta_s(h_j)=epsilon_j U^s. (1.2) Thus all integer resonant sectors U^k are present as the images of coherent kernels theta_k. They are functions of the whole normal U, rather than being set to one before transport. This is an exact normal polarization comparison. It does not say that the actual clock q-normal, block-number operator T B, and nabla are the same operator. In particular M(T B)=u nabla M; other current directions must be transported with their own marked operator adapters, not inferred from (1.2). ## 2. The original cut and its normal pivot line are preserved Let tau=Tr_(Chat/k[[U-1]])/N. The canonical A-power basis gives tau(f)=f_0(U), and tau(epsilon_j)=1/N. Hence [tau M(f)]_(U=1)=phi pi_0(f), M(psi)=1, tau nabla=U partial_U tau. (2.1) There are two different source projectors. The coefficientwise extension e_H tensor I is carried to f |->tau(f)1, retaining every normal coefficient. The actual finite-rank ambient coupon Gamma=i e_H pi_0 is instead carried to f |-> [tau(f)]_(U=1) 1. They agree on the vacuum but not on its first normal. In particular the first projector commutes with nabla, whereas [nabla,Gamma_U]f=-[tau(nabla f)]_(U=1)1. (2.2) This is the additional finite normal cut row. It cannot be discarded by identifying the whole-normal and finite-vacuum projectors. These are strict linear cut comparisons, without identifying matrix composition with scalar coefficient multiplication. The root pivot also has two distinct whole-normal lifts. With K_U=xA^(-1), define g_red=x^(1-N)A^(-1), g_lit=K_U^(1-N)=U g_red, D_red=g_red^(-1)e, D_lit=U^(-1)D_red. (2.3) The reduced representative agrees with the original pivot on U=1. Only g_lit is its literal clock power off that fiber. In the horizontal epsilon frame the exact adapters are g_red=alpha^(-1) M g_H M^(-1), D_red=alpha M D_H M^(-1), g_lit=alpha^(N-1) M g_H M^(-1), D_lit=alpha^(1-N) M D_H M^(-1). (2.4) Thus their physical normal derivatives differ: D_phys(g_red)=-g_red, D_phys(D_red)=D_red, D_phys(g_lit)=(N-1)g_lit, D_phys(D_lit)=-(N-1)D_lit. Both products are exactly e and horizontal. The adapter U and its first derivative remain part of a comparison of the two lifts; the common root value does not identify their normal phases. The full external d_N(M) line is unchanged and remains distinct from this internal U normal. The underlying full quantum modules are not identified: for example the uncorrected cyclic operator (1-A)S^(-1) has N-th power 1-U, whereas the root balanced head F has N-th power zero. The map (1.1) does not suppress that endpoint source or claim to intertwine these two different F actions. ## 3. An explicit relative source-chain map with endpoint U Use an independent source-centralizer coordinate sigma with marked endpoints zero and one. Keep it distinct from any physical geometric framing parameter. On Fhat-valued series define the twisted relative complex P=H[sigma][[t]], R_T^1=P, R_T^2=P direct_sum Fhat direct_sum Fhat, delta_T h=((partial_sigma-T)h,h(0),h(1)). Every t coefficient in P is polynomial in sigma; endpoint evaluation and antiderivation are therefore defined coefficientwise. The t-adic completion permits exp(sigma T) while retaining those endpoint maps. Conjugation by exp(sigma T), with exp(T) at the second endpoint, identifies this complex with the ordinary relative source complex. Its transgression is L_T(a,b_0,b_1) =integral_0^1 exp(-sigma T)a(sigma)dsigma -exp(-T)b_1+b_0. (3.1) The inclusion is f |->(exp(sigma T)f,0,0). Both identities L_T delta_T=0 and L_T i_T=I follow by differentiating exp(-sigma T)h(sigma). They hold before applying any cut. Applying M coefficientwise gives a strict isomorphism to the whole-normal complex delta_U h=((partial_sigma-Log U)h,h(0),h(1)), L_U(a,b_0,b_1) =integral_0^1 U^(-sigma)a(sigma)dsigma -U^(-1)b_1+b_0. (3.2) The coherent inclusion becomes f |->(U^sigma f,0,0). The endpoint carry is literally U. It has not disappeared through specialization of A^N=1. The whole averaged co-source and its residue realization from (2.1) commute with this chain map. The original finite cut is obtained after evaluation U=1; its normal derivative requires the extra row (2.2), rather than a horizontal vacuum assumption. There is also an exact compatible normal connection on the entire relative complex. On degree one it is B-sigma. On degree two it is (B-sigma,B,B-1). These commute with delta_T because [B-sigma,partial_sigma-T]=0. Under M they are (nabla-sigma) and (nabla-sigma,nabla,nabla-1), respectively. Transgression carries them to B and nabla. Using bare B without the sigma term would give curvature -I and would be incorrect. This is an explicit Heisenberg normal/source complex, not a conditional lifting argument. ## 4. The logarithmic torsor is necessary, not a finite-cover choice The completed map (1.1) has a global version only after adjoining the marked logarithmic torsor of U. On any simply connected marked sheet, nabla(Log U)=1 and all formulas above are actual functions. Changing the logarithm shifts its additive torsor coordinate. There is a sharp obstruction to replacing it by algebraic functions. Suppose a linear comparison into the algebraic whole-normal field, or any finite algebraic cover, intertwines B with nabla and carries some vacuum h to a nonzero horizontal value c. Since B(Th)=h, its image f would satisfy U partial_U f=c. After applying a constant component functional if necessary, c is a nonzero constant. Thus df=c dU/U. At a zero or pole of U on the normalized compact curve, its right side has nonzero residue. An exact differential of an algebraic function has zero residues. Finite covers multiply that residue by a positive ramification index and cannot remove it. This contradiction proves that no such nonzero vacuum/cut-preserving algebraic linear map exists. The obstruction already appears on the first excited Fock vector; it is not an asymptotic or high-jet problem. It also does not contradict (1.1): Log U is a valid formal function at U=1. The required common object is a marked logarithmic differential torsor, rather than only a finite algebraic source cover. It can be presented as the algebraic bundle with coordinate t and connection dt=dU/U; the obstruction is to an algebraic horizontal section, not to the existence of that bundle. ## 5. Relation to the actual two-dimensional divided-adjoint orbit The explicit divided-adjoint source orbit and its marked geometric framing chart are proved in [the framing-orbit note](divided_source_framing_orbit.md). With its coordinates v=a Ubar+bW, z=a+b, the map is r=a/z, s_geo=z^(-2), A_cut=z^2/(1+z^2), tau_geo=r/s_geo=a z, Omega_cut=d tau_geo wedge dlog A_cut. (5.1) This establishes an explicit bare group/form comparison. It does not identify the source-relative sigma in Section 3 with tau_geo at the physical quantum scale. If u=Log U=N Log A_cut, then Omega_cut=(1/N)d tau_geo wedge du. At H_N=2pi*i/N, a geometric Fourier phase tau_geo Log A_cut/H_N is tau_geo u/(2pi*i). Matching it with the source kernel exp(s_Fock u) would therefore require s_Fock=tau_geo/(2pi*i), changing the unit source endpoint U to U^(1/(2pi*i)). A marked residue/phase adapter is required before claiming such a physical polarization identity. There is also a direct source-collapse limitation. On a diagonal cut matrix C the normalized raw orbit insertion is Phi(Cv)/Phi(v) =(a/z)/(N-1) sum_(j<N-1) C_jj+(b/z)C_(N-1,N-1). It depends only on a/z. Thus the two orbit parameters do not by themselves become two independently measured internal framing coordinates of the scalar partial knot state. The whole-normal and relative current data above are necessary to retain the additional direction before collapse. ## 6. What is new here and what remains The earlier first-quantum-normal and source/monodromy notes give the actual module/cokernel connection, its source, and the normal lattice cut. The relative-framing note realizes the finite boundary cut as a residue complex. They do not contain the explicit Fock Mellin map (1.1), its endpoint-U relative chain map (3.2), or the global algebraic obstruction in Section 4. Those maps now compare the actual Fock and whole-normal boundary objects directly, retaining both the reduced pivot lift and literal clock-power lift with their exact U adapter, the distinct finite- vacuum cut row, and every endpoint factor. They do not prove that a computed geometric Gaussian class has the original selected image under this map. Its extension through the actual source boundary, the physical 2pi*i adapter and global period coefficient remain separate requirements. No regulator volume identity is inferred. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_fock_cyclic_normal_mellin_map.py). [Results](../experiments/fock_cyclic_normal_mellin_map_results.json). [Independent Mellin and Green audit](fock_mellin_and_green_independent_audit.md).

title: Independent audit of the normal Mellin and full Green maps
text:
# Independent audit of the normal Mellin and full Green maps Audit, 27 October 2026. The normal Mellin map and relative connection are sound. The revised Mellin section 2 and residual normal-current section 6 explicitly retain both pivot lifts and both projector extensions, with their correct normal rows. There is no outstanding correction. The full discrete Green/current calculation is sound and does not assert cancellation of the remaining geometric boundary terms. No test reruns were needed. ## 1. The strict normal Mellin map For \(A^N=U\), \[ D_{m phys}=A\partial_A+NU\partial_U \] preserves the relation, and \(
abla=D_{m phys}/N\) has \(
abla\Log U=1\). With the marked \(\alpha^N=U\), the elements \(A/\alpha\), hence every \(\epsilon_j\), are horizontal. The map \[ v_{rN+j}\longmapsto\epsilon_j(\Log U)^r/r! \] is therefore a topological linear isomorphism carrying \(B\) to \(
abla\), \(T\) to multiplication by \(\Log U\), and the coherent kernel to \(\epsilon_jU^s\). The averaged trace and its \(U=1\) value give precisely the stated original vacuum cut. There is a useful projector distinction. The coefficientwise extension \(e_H\otimes I\) maps to \(f\mapsto	au(f)1\). The finite-rank ambient coupon \(i e_H\pi_0\) instead maps to \(f\mapsto[	au(f)]_{U=1}1\). Both recover the same head cut; their whole-normal extensions are different. The revised finite-vacuum row is exactly \[ [
abla,\Gamma_U]f=-[	au(
abla f)]_{U=1}1: \] the derivative of the constant output of \(\Gamma_U\) is zero, while \(\Gamma_U
abla\) is its displayed evaluated trace row. The coefficientwise projector commutes with \(
abla\). For \(\partial_\sigma-T\), the compatible normal direction is \(B-\sigma\): \[ [B-\sigma,\partial_\sigma-T]=0. \] The two scalar commutators cancel with opposite signs. Endpoint evaluation gives the degree-two corrections \((B-\sigma,B,B-1)\), and direct differentiation of \(e^{-\sigma T}h\) proves the transgression formulas. Under Mellin transport the endpoint is exactly \(U\); no specialization to one occurs before this identity. The algebraic primitive obstruction is also valid. A vacuum-preserving intertwiner on an algebraic finite cover would give \(df=c\,dU/U\), \(c
e0\). On the compact normalized curve the right side has nonzero residues at zeros/poles of \(U\), whereas an exact algebraic differential has zero residues. Ramification multiplies rather than kills the residue. The formal logarithmic torsor avoids, rather than contradicts, this global algebraic obstruction. ## 2. Two whole-normal lifts of the finite pivot The displayed formulas in [the Mellin note](fock_cyclic_normal_mellin_map.md) are correct for the **root-reduced lift** \[ g_{m red}=x^{1-N}A^{-1},\quad D_{m red}=g_{m red}^{-1}e. \] They have adapters \(\alpha^{-1}\) and \(\alpha\), and physical derivatives \(-g_{m red}\) and \(+D_{m red}\), respectively. The revised note separately retains the literal power of \(K_U=xA^{-1}\): \[ g_{m lit}=K_U^{1-N} =x^{1-N}A^{N-1}=U g_{m red}. \] Its matching defect is \(D_{m lit}=U^{-1}D_{m red}\). The adapters are then \(\alpha^{N-1}\) and \(\alpha^{1-N}\), and \[ D_{m phys}(g_{m lit})=(N-1)g_{m lit},\qquad D_{m phys}(D_{m lit})=(1-N)D_{m lit}. \] Both choices give \(gD=e\) and the same finite source at \(U=1\), but their individual normal jets differ. The revised proof now states this \(U^{\pm1}\) adapter explicitly. Residual normal-current section 6 is consistent with these formulas. The divided Frobenius shift is \(-D_{m phys}\), the averaged trace satisfies \(	au D_{m phys}=NU\partial_U	au\), and its paired matrix row has the same covariance for either lift. Its coefficientwise extension is explicitly separated from \(\Gamma_U\), so the latter's extra finite-vacuum normal derivative has not been dropped. The physical \(2\pi i\) caveat is correct: \(	au_{m geo}\Log A/H_N=	au_{m geo}\Log U/(2\pi i)\). The bare kernel \(U^{s_{m Fock}}\) therefore needs \(s_{m Fock}=	au_{m geo}/(2\pi i)\); its unit endpoint cannot silently be identified with the geometric unit meridian interval. ## 3. The universal Green formula and its signs For \(D_i=S_i-1\), the exact product rule is \[ pD_if=D_i[(S_i^{-1}p)f]+(S_i^{-1}p-p)f. \] Iterating it in the stated word order gives the displayed current formula. For \(p_\alpha=\prod_i inom{k_i}{\alpha_i}\), backward differences of total degree \(>|\alpha|\) vanish; at degree \(|\alpha|\), only \( eta=\alpha\) survives, with value \((-1)^{|\alpha|}\). Using \(PI=0\) moves the divergence sum to the other side, producing exactly the negative sign in the definition of \(J_i\). These are identities on entire zero-extended arrays. The polynomial moment does not lose a support boundary, and all currents remain finite. External Ore operators commute with the index polynomials and internal shifts. ## 4. Transverse pushforward and the unresolved relative boundary The formal current identity follows from the already established interior identity by the same algebraic product rule, with \(k_i=u_i/H\). No separate density argument for polynomial logarithms is needed. The transverse Gaussian translation identity kills the transverse differences even with their insertions; external coordinate/base shifts commute with the recentered Wick construction. Exactly the two stated framing differences remain. For a translated chain, \(\int_\Gamma(F_H^*J-J)=\int_{F_H\Gamma-\Gamma}J\); the Cartan homotopy therefore has the stated boundary sign. Its logarithmic loop changes the index lift by \(2\pi i/H_N=N\), preserving the polynomial-current jump. The complete residual Ward ideal does not set these relative endpoints or carries to zero. Finally, on the actual diagonal one-cut array, \(CW=C_{N-1,N-1}W\). Thus the ordered divided row is exactly that endpoint value, as claimed. This does not create an additional independent framing index. The Green note correctly presents a full scalar certificate with a two-current geometric defect, not a full geometric annihilation or survival theorem.

title: Formal quantum-A periods on the classical curve
text: # Formal quantum-A periods on the classical curve Research note, 25 October 2026. This pursues the norm-torsor and A-curve direction specified in the user's pasted attachment. It constructs the formal branch and its period connection directly from a specified quantum A-operator. It does not assume equality of a root-of-unity central curve D_n with the classical A-curve. The actual Kashaev-period identification and volume conjecture remain unproved. Formal solutions of q-difference equations are existing theory; see the stated coverage of Garoufalidis--Geronimo, [math/0405331](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0405331). No proof or analytic asymptotic theorem from that source is used below. The calculations here are coefficient lifting, formal connections, and algebraic local models. No novelty is claimed for formal difference-equation methods. ## 1. A branch lifts by an explicit noncommutative Hensel recursion Normalize the specified operator at q=1 so that its first nonzero h-coefficient has order zero, and write q=exp(h), delta=x*d/dx, sigma_h=exp(h*delta), Ahat=sum_(j=0)^d p_j(h,x)T^j, T f=sigma_h(f)T, p_j(h,x) in C(x)[[h]], P(x,L)=sum_j p_j(0,x)L^j. Suppose C is a normalized component of P=0 with function field k, x nonconstant and L nonzero, on which P_L is nonzero generically. In particular the selected component has multiplicity one. Extend delta to k by delta(L)=-x P_x/P_L. **Formal factor theorem.** There is a unique a(h)=L+h a_1+h^2 a_2+... in k[[h]]^* such that T-a is a right factor of Ahat. All a_j are algebraic functions on C, computed recursively from the operator. For a proof, the right remainder is R(a)=sum_j p_j(h,x)*product_(s=0)^(j-1) sigma_h^s(a). (1.1) Its constant coefficient is P(x,L)=0. Once a_1,...,a_(n-1) are known, its coefficient at h^n is P_L(x,L)*a_n + known_n. Every shift of h^n a_n agrees with h^n a_n modulo h^(n+1), which proves the displayed coefficient. Set a_n=-known_n/P_L. Formal right division by the monic T-a then gives Ahat=Qhat*(T-a). (1.2) This is an intrinsic branch of the given operator, rather than a new quantization selected for its growth. A noncharacteristic left multiple Bhat*Ahat has the same lifted branch: its symbol factor B_0(x,L) is a unit in k, so uniqueness in (1.1) applies again. A change of cyclic generator by a finite operator C(T) gives, on this branch, multiplication by the scalar obtained by the same remainder formula (1.1), with C in place of Ahat. When C_0(x,L) is nonzero this is a unit of k[[h]]. Thus the gauge law below also handles noncharacteristic changes of cyclic generator. The hypothesis that P contains the geometric classical A-component still has to be justified for the actual knot operator. This theorem does not prove an AJ statement. ## 2. The resulting period connection and its gauge law Choose a local logarithm v=Log L and put u=Log x. The Bernoulli operator defines an exact formal differential Theta_A(h)= [h*delta/(exp(h*delta)-1)] Log a(h) *du =v du+h theta_1+h^2 theta_2+... . (2.1) The quotient means its power series 1-h*delta/2+h^2*delta^2/12-... . The coefficients theta_j for j>=1 are meromorphic algebraic differentials on C. Indeed Log(a/L) has coefficients in k, and delta(Log L)=delta(L)/L belongs to k. Locally a formal solution of sigma_h(psi)=a psi is a horizontal period frame for d log psi=Theta_A(h)/h. (2.2) To verify (2.2), apply exp(h*delta)-1 to log psi. Its formal inverse on derivatives is exactly the Bernoulli series in (2.1). Local primitives supply such frames; their integration constants are additional period data. For a frame change psi -> g psi, g in k[[h]]^*, the ratio changes by a -> a*sigma_h(g)/g. Formula (2.1) gives exactly Theta_A -> Theta_A+h*d log g. (2.3) Thus (2.2) is a well-defined formal line with connection and a torsor of horizontal period frames. Changing the cyclic frame changes its presentation by the usual connection gauge; it does not alter its leading period differential. This also gives a precise formal comparison criterion. For two such ratios a,b with the same leading L, write (Theta_a-Theta_b)/h=omega_0+h omega_1+... . They are equivalent by a unit g in k[[h]]^* exactly when omega_0=d log g_0 for some g_0 in k^*, omega_j=d g_j for some g_j in k, j>=1. (2.4) One direction is (2.3). For the converse take g=g_0 exp(sum_(j>=1)h^j g_j). The comparison is unique up to delta-constant units C[[h]]^*. Equation (2.4) displays the period obstructions explicitly; finite-level Hilbert 90 does not make them vanish automatically for the infinite-order formal shift. ## 3. The first correction retains the operator's ordering Let P_1(x,L)=sum_j [h]p_j(h,x)L^j. Expanding (1.1) gives a_1=-[P_1+(L*delta L/2)P_LL]/P_L, theta_1=[-P_1/(L P_L) -(delta L/2)(P_LL/P_L+1/L)]du. (3.1) Equivalently, putting P_sub=P_1-(x L/2)P_xL, theta_1=-(1/2)d log(L P_L)-P_sub/(L P_L)*du. (3.2) The partial derivatives in P_sub refer to the displayed left-ordered symbol. Formula (3.2) follows by differentiating P_L along C. In the special case P_sub=0, this correction is the square-root line (L P_L)^(-1/2). In general the extra differential is retained. No preferred ordering or vanishing subprincipal term is assumed. ### The actual peripheral normalization includes a difference constant The reduced and modified-trace literature periods satisfy N_N(M)=d_N(M)F_N(M), with f(M)=M-M^(-1), d_N(M)=eta_N f(M)/(M^N-M^(-N)), d_N(qM)/d_N(M)=-f(qM)/f(M), q=exp(pi*i/N). For consistent logarithms let chi=Log(-1). The formal branch ratios therefore give the exact connection-presentation change Theta_modified=Theta_reduced+chi*dlog M+h*dlog f. (3.3) The sign character and the meridian divisor are separate data. In particular the leading classical shift variable changes sign. There is further period data not recovered from this shift ratio. Write u=Log M, h=pi*i/N, and w=exp(2pi*i*u/h)=M^(2N). Then exactly d_N(M)=eta_N f(M) exp(pi*i*u/h)/(w-1). (3.4) The exponential changes sign under u->u+h, while w is invariant. Thus 1/(w-1) is a genuine difference constant. It is outside the coefficientwise meromorphic formal class used in Section 2 and is not removed by that section's Bernoulli inversion. Its pole cancels the zero of f in the whole germ and gives d_N(1)=eta_N/N. This identifies a specific piece of the actual period pointing that a formal branch alone would forget. The [central normalization lemma](algebraic_central_normalization.md) controls factors from a fixed finite algebraic central presentation; it does not supply an unknown global period comparison. The subsequent [regular-period theorem](regularized_kashaev_period.md) also shows why a plain uniform branch amplitude for the reduced state would lose essential data at completeness. Exactly F_N=S_N R_N+P_N, where P_N interpolates the ordinary root colors and S_N vanishes at all those orbit points but has value N at Y=1. All ordinary values are polynomially bounded. In particular F_N(q_N)=1 excludes a uniform nonzero geometric WKB amplitude for F_N across M=1,q_N if its complete value has positive exponential growth. The regular period R_N removes this polar/zero structure with the full original gauge retained; its affine source has bounded Laurent support and polynomially bounded coefficients. A norm theorem for R_N is still needed to identify the actual period with the formal geometric branch. ## 4. The leading period is the regulator action, with conversion explicit First center at the marked point: use u=Log(x/x_c), v=Log(L/L_c), and replace the uncentered S by S-(Log L_c)*u. The extracted solution character exp((Log L_c)*u/h) remains explicit; it is not discarded. Now let S denote this centered leading primitive, dS=v du. Suppose the centered geometric peripheral functions used by the regulator obey m/m_c=(x/x_c)^a (L/L_c)^b, l/l_c=(x/x_c)^c (L/L_c)^d, Delta=a*d-b*c !=0. Then U=a u+b v and V=c u+d v. Direct differentiation gives dR=-Delta*(u dv-v du)/4, R=(Delta/2)S-(Delta/4)u v+constant. (4.1) This identifies the leading *differential* of the formal quantum-A period with the central coordinate of the regulator Heisenberg torsor in [the focused formulation](a_polynomial_torsor_status.md). For example, if the geometric holonomies are m=x^2,l=L^2, then Delta=4. At the centered complete point u=v=0, (4.1) gives Im S=(1/2)Vol + Im(constant). (4.2) For the ADO root parameter h=pi*i/N, a period exp(S/h) has (2pi/N)log|exp(S/h)|=2 Im S. Thus these square-holonomy conventions give the required volume coefficient when the marked additive constant agrees. The subsequent [actual longitude/action calculation](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md) now proves this peripheral conversion for the actual classical critical correspondence. Its compatible discrete-character lift also fixes Im S=Vol/2 in this q-parameter, without an undetermined imaginary constant. This does not prove that the geometric component survives in the selected sum's minimal operator or its quantum period. Equivalently the [squared-meridian descent](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) uses Y=M^2, step H=Log(q^2)=2h, and S_Q=2S. In (Y,L) the full peripheral exponent determinant is two, and R=S_Q-(Log Y)(Log L)/2. Both conversions give the same marked connection and norm. For other conventions Delta, the constant character, and the root parameter must all be retained. Merely writing the same letters for operator variables and full geometric holonomies would lose a factor. ## 5. Formal lattices at a simple collision The subsequent [geometric rigidity calculation](geometric_rigidity_and_cyclic_source.md) constructs regular formal ratios on the two normalized geometric gluing germs, with distinct slopes at the complete peripheral point. An exact scalarization model then has a classical meridian factor despite having no common local quantum coefficient divisor. Its all-shifts cyclic lattice retains a length-one source at (u,h)=(0,0). This gives an additional reason to keep integral factors and the cyclic generator when comparing the normalized curve with an actual operator. It does not remove the hypotheses on a given operator below. The function-field construction does not by itself allow evaluation where P_L=0. Here is an explicit extension at two common local types. Let t be a uniformizer on the normalization, with x(0),L(0) nonzero, and assume the operator coefficients are regular there. Suppose ord_t(P_L)=1, delta=b(t)t^(-mu)*d/dt, b(0)!=0, mu in {0,1}, L=L_0+O(t). Mu=0 covers an unramified branch through an ordinary double point; mu=1 covers a simple ramification of the x-projection. Then ord_t(a_n) >=-[(mu+2)n-1], n>=1. (5.1) For a proof, delta increases pole order by at most mu+1. In the known h^n remainder, a term with two positive-order a-coefficients has pole order at most (mu+2)n-2. A term with one positive-order coefficient must also contain a derivative or another h-coefficient; the same bound follows. For derivatives of L alone, delta^r L has pole order at most r(mu+1)-1, which also gives this bound. Division by P_L adds at most one. This proves (5.1) by induction. Set w=mu+2 and use the formal weighted chart h=t^w epsilon. Then a=L_0+t*A(t,epsilon), A in C[[t,epsilon]], h*delta=b(t)[t^2 epsilon*d/dt -w*t*epsilon^2*d/depsilon]. (5.2) The second expression acts at fixed h and preserves the power-series ring. Its exponential is a formal automorphism. Since a has nonzero constant term, the rank-one difference module and its lattice extend on this chart. This is an algebraic formal replacement of the poles, not an instruction to evaluate a divergent coefficient at t=0. The chart (5.2) alone does not cover the complete evaluation at fixed nonzero h. It resolves the joint formal degeneration. The other chart must retain the colliding branches, as the next construction shows. ## 6. A rank-two algebraic connection at an ordinary double point Assume the classical symbol has an ordinary double point p=(x_0,L_0), with x_0 L_0 !=0, satisfying P=P_x=P_L=0, P_LL!=0, P_xL^2-P_xx P_LL !=0. (6.1) Use h=tau^2 and x=x_0+tau*s. Extract the constant shift character L_0 from the solution, so T acts on the remaining factor as L_0 exp[tau*(x_0+tau*s)*d/ds]. Taylor expansion of the given operator has zero terms of orders tau^0 and tau^1. Dividing by tau^2 gives a formal differential operator whose leading term is L_node=A_2*d_s^2+B_1*s*d_s+C_2*s^2+D_0, A_2=x_0^2 L_0^2 P_LL(p)/2, B_1=x_0 L_0 P_xL(p), C_2=P_xx(p)/2, D_0=P_1(p). (6.2) All derivatives in this formula are evaluated at p. To check it, expand the coefficients at x_0+tau*s and each j-th shift to order two. The identities P_x=P_L=0 remove the linear terms, and sum_j j^2 p_j L_0^j=L_0^2 P_LL+L_0 P_L gives the second derivative. The mixed coefficient is x_0 L_0 P_xL*s*d_s. This proves (6.2) with the left ordering and quantum first coefficient unchanged. The complete formal operator, normalized by A_2, has the unique factorization L(tau)=U(tau)*[d_s^2+b(s,tau)d_s+c(s,tau)], U(0)=1, b,c in C[s][[tau]], (6.3) where U is a unit in the tau-adic completed differential-operator ring. For the proof, at order tau^n divide the known residual differential operator on the right by the monic leading operator of order two. Its quotient specifies [tau^n]U and its remainder, of order less than two, specifies the tau^n coefficient of b*d_s+c. Ordinary Ore division proves existence and uniqueness recursively. Each step uses polynomial coefficients and a constant nonzero leading coefficient. Thus this branch pair has a free rank-two formal connection lattice, regular at s=0. Other classical roots are excluded by the completion around L_0. The construction is unchanged up to isomorphism by a noncharacteristic left multiple of the original operator. The two slopes alpha of the classical node obey P_LL alpha^2+2P_xL alpha+P_xx=0. The leading quadratic exponent of the corresponding formal periods is alpha*s^2/(2x_0 L_0), exactly the rescaling of the leading action in Section 4. Two period constants are still required at the regular point s=0. The operator does not select their values or the actual knot's combination of branches. ## 7. What this proves toward the requested comparison For any specified operator with the geometric component in its classical symbol, its simple generic branch now has a canonical formal ratio, a gauge-covariant period connection, and the same leading regulator differential after the peripheral conversion. The local construction also retains a colliding pair in a regular rank-two lattice at an ordinary double point. This does not prove that every relevant knot operator has that symbol, that its complete point has only an ordinary double collision, or that the actual selected ADO period realizes the formal geometric branch with the marked normalization. A formal solution does not establish convergence or its root-of-unity evaluation. Multiplication by exp(c/h) already shows why the action constant matters for volume. The next comparison must identify the actual all-level pointed period, with its peripheral lattice, in this A-curve period torsor. The classical regulator fixes what its normalization must be; the present algebra does not prove the identification. The full norm statement in the focused formulation remains unproved. The subsequent [actual normal-period proof](actual_geometric_normal_period.md) constructs a nonzero formal normal block directly from the actual crossing coefficients. Positive gluing rigidity identifies its Hessian radical with the two framing directions, and the quotient of its algebraic Gaussian amplitude with the geometric one gives an all-orders formal gauge. This is additional local coefficient information; it does not prove that the selected sum's minimal operator contains that block or that its actual source and cut select it. Sections 7--8 of that note state the exact role of the ideal triangulation theorem and the remaining source-gauge equation. `experiments/audit_formal_a_curve_torsor.py` checks the noncommutative lifting, first correction, exact gauge law, collision pole bounds, and rank-two local reduction against independent exact factorizations and shift actions. These are diagnostics for the uniform proofs here.

title: Four literature cyclic-dilogarithm atoms for the actual crossing
text: # Four literature cyclic-dilogarithm atoms for the actual crossing Research note, 26 October 2026. This gives an exact root-level factorization of the genuine semicyclic holonomy crossing into four literature cyclic quantum dilogarithms. Each atom transports its center; their determinant normalizations and external root factor are explicit. An anchored scalar-rigidity argument fixes the remaining phase. The factorization holds at every N, including even and composite levels. The object being factorized is the actual crossing already identified in [the semicyclic braid proof](semicyclic_carry_braiding.md). Its nilpotent boundary, cut period, pivot, twist and full ADO normalization are retained. This does not assign all colored face/turn data to an arbitrary positive geometric triangulation or prove its selected norm. ## 1. The literature atom, including its determinant Fix q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2 and N>=2. On a split quantum torus let a primitive monomial m have m^N=w. Choose roots mu^N=w, nu^N=1-w, mu nu !=0. For its eigenvalues mu Q^j define the pointed cyclic function f_0=1, f_j=nu^j/(mu;Q)_j, 0<=j<N. (1.1) Its cyclic recurrence is f_(j+1)/f_j=nu/(1-mu Q^j). The last step is the identity (mu;Q)_N=1-mu^N=nu^N. Spectral idempotents define the matrix C=f(m) without choosing an analytic infinite product. If m acts on an N^2-dimensional two-pair torus, each eigenvalue occurs N times. Put F=product_(j=0)^(N-1) f_j, gamma^N=F^(-1), gamma=1 at mu=0, D_atom=gamma C. (1.2) Then det C=F^N and det D_atom=1. For a general number of spectator pairs the same normalization works by multiplicity. This is exactly the standard alternate cyclic-dilogarithm definition mathfrak_d_N(z;Q)=(1-z^N)^((N-1)/(2N)) product_(ell=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^ell z)^(-ell/N). (1.3) Indeed, writing D_N(z)=product_(ell=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^ell z)^(ell/N), finite cancellation gives F=nu^(-N(N-1)/2) D_N(mu)^N, gamma=nu^((N-1)/2)/D_N(mu), gamma f_j=mathfrak_d_N(mu Q^j;Q). (1.4) Compatible roots are part of the formulas. Include the square roots required by half powers when N is even; no inverse of two modulo N is used. Definition (1.3) is the literature cyclic dilogarithm, not the full ADO dimension d_N(M), which remains a different function. ## 2. An atom is an intertwiner between changing centers Suppose m A=Q^k A m, k integral. Formal compact conjugation has the rational expression r_m(A)=A product_(ell=0)^(k-1)(1-Q^ell m)^(-1), k>0, r_m(A)=A product_(ell=k)^(-1)(1-Q^ell m), k<0. (2.1) The value at k=0 is A. These are finite expressions; after inverting 1-w every factor is invertible at the root. The Nth central power changes by (1-w)^(-k). In the splitting frame take A'=nu^(-k) A. The recurrence (1.1) gives exactly r_m(A) C=C A', r_m(A) D_atom=D_atom A'. (2.2) This proves the atom comparison directly, including composite levels. In particular the atom is not evaluated repeatedly in one frozen central representation. ## 3. The four monomials and the two independent norm factors Use two uniform clock/shift pairs S_i e_a=s_i Q^a e_a, Z_i e_a=z_i e_(a+1), S_i Z_i=Q Z_i S_i. Start with s_1=s_2=1, source roots z_1,z_2 nonzero, and put x=q^alpha, k=x^N, a=z_2/z_1, r=a^N=phi_2/phi_1. The quantum-group embedding is the previously proved one F_i=Z_i, K_i=x S_i^(-1), rho^2 E_i=qx Z_i^(-1)(1-S_i^(-1)) (1-Q^(-1)x^(-2)S_i), rho=q-q^(-1). Thus E_i^N=0 initially and phi_i=z_i^N. The compact four-factor identity of [the Verma proof](verma_tetrahedral_transport.md) has the ordered monomials m_1=-Qx A S_1^(-1), m_2=x^(-1)A, m_3=Qx A, m_4=-x^(-1)A S_1, A=Z_1^(-1)Z_2. (3.1) Their coefficients, order and q phase are retained. Define Delta_1=1+kr, Delta_2=1-r/[k(1+kr)], nu_1^N=Delta_1, nu_2^N=Delta_2, nu_3=nu_1^(-1), nu_4=nu_2^(-1). (3.2) Assume these factors are nonzero. They are full functions, not constants selected after peripheral evaluation. The root Cartan map first changes z_1,z_2 to z_1/x,z_2/x, leaving s_1=s_2=1. Its matrix is C_cartan e_(i,j)=Q^(ij)e_(i,j). (3.3) For each subsequent atom m=c A S_1^b, the commutation integers with (S_1,S_2,Z_1,Z_2) are (1,-1,b,0). By (2.2) its target roots are (s_1,s_2,z_1,z_2) -> (s_1/nu,s_2 nu,z_1/nu^b,z_2). (3.4) Evaluate m_i in the frame reached before that atom. Compatible spectral roots and norm factors are | Atom | Spectral root mu_i | nu_i^N | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | q x a | Delta_1 | | 2 | a/(x nu_1) | Delta_2 | | 3 | Q x a/nu_1 | Delta_1^(-1) | | 4 | q a/(x nu_1 nu_2) | Delta_2^(-1) | The negative monomial signs are accounted for by q^N=-1 and (A S_1^b)^N=(-1)^(b(N-1)) A^N S_1^(bN). Multiplication verifies mu_i^N+nu_i^N=1 in every row, at every parity. For completeness the successive clock-center product factors are Delta_1, Delta_2, Delta_1^(-1), Delta_2^(-1). They restore both clock roots exactly with the compatible choices in (3.2). The final shift roots are z'_1=z_1 nu_1 nu_2/x, z'_2=z_2/x. (3.5) Their powers are precisely the genuine holonomy targets: phi'_1=phi_1/k+(1-k^(-2))phi_2, phi'_2=phi_2/k. Here Delta_1 Delta_2=1+kr-r/k. This is a direct center calculation for the complete four-factor word. ## 4. The exact normalized crossing formula Let D_i be (1.2)--(1.3) for atom i in its transported frame. Let B_src and B_tar be the changes from the standard F-circle bases to the uniform clock/shift bases: B_src e_(i,j)=z_1^i z_2^j e_(i,j), B_tar e_(i,j)=(z'_1)^i(z'_2)^j e_(i,j). These are the actual monomial frame changes: v_a=z_i^a e_a has F v_a=v_(a+1), with wrap phi_i. On the root cover anchored by nu_1=nu_2=gamma_i=1 at a=0, the uncheck crossing is exactly R^0=(nu_1 nu_2)^(-(N-1)/2) B_src^(-1) C_cartan D_1 D_2 D_3 D_4 B_tar. (4.1) Products have their displayed order and changing-frame meaning. The inverse gives the negative crossing, with its centers and all roots transported as in the genuine braid theorem. Here is a proof of the scalar, rather than an unspecified projective factorization. Conjugating the generic compact four-factor identity gives a rational quantum-torus identity. The proof in the linked Verma note is a formal algebra identity before root specialization. Its rational conjugations have finite expressions (2.1), so clearing the indicated denominators specializes that identity at every root. Equations (2.2)--(3.5) then show that the right side of (4.1) and the genuine semicyclic R^0 intertwine the same full matrix algebra with the same central data and Casimirs. They differ by a scalar lambda on the generic regular chart. Each D_i has determinant one on the N^2-dimensional pair. The exact remaining determinants are det C_cartan=Q^((N(N-1)/2)^2), det B_tar/det B_src=(nu_1 nu_2/x^2)^(N^2(N-1)/2), det R^0=x^(-N^2(N-1))Q^((N(N-1)/2)^2). The external factor in (4.1) cancels the entire extra determinant. Thus lambda^(N^2)=1. (4.2) This does not by itself discard lambda. Use the formal source anchor a=0: the matrices m_i/mu_i extend there, f_j=1, D_i=identity, and all specified norm roots equal one. The zeroth coordinate of the right side applied to v_00 has a regular value one. This coordinate does not involve an inverse singular frame entry, since (B_src)_00=(B_tar)_00=1. The genuine crossing fixes v_00. Therefore lambda has value one at this formal anchor. A root-of-unity-valued algebraic function is constant on the irreducible anchored component, so lambda=1. This proves (4.1) with its phase fixed. Other lifted components retain their phases; the theorem does not identify independent choices of normalization roots. ## 5. The raw scalar is explicit and must be retained If raw pointed C_i rather than the literature D_i are used, write R_raw=B_src^(-1)C_cartan C_1 C_2 C_3 C_4 B_tar. Then R_raw=lambda_raw R^0, with lambda_raw^(N^2) =(nu_1 nu_2)^(N^2(N-1)/2) product_i F_i^N. (5.1) The complete formula and branch on the anchored cover are equivalently fixed by (4.1) and gamma_i^N=F_i^(-1). Thus determinants control a real normalization line, with its root phase selected by the actual pointing. They are not permission to throw away an arbitrary scalar period. The external root in (4.1) also remains necessary even though the four atom norm factors multiply to one. At fixed nonzero Delta_1,Delta_2 its log-modulus is -(N-1)/(2N) log|Delta_1 Delta_2|. This is bounded across N under that fixed-central specialization. No bound for an unrecorded moving-center specialization or the entire selected knot period is inferred. ## 6. Peripheral functions that become numerical multipliers For a positive checked crossing on the common fixed line of the genuine braid theorem, its uncheck source pair is swapped. Hence its ratio r is k. Write U=k^2=M^(2N), retaining the actual sign k=(-1)^(N-1)M^N. Equations (3.2) give Delta_1=1+U, Delta_2=U/(1+U), Delta_3=1/(1+U), Delta_4=(1+U)/U. (6.1) At M=1 these specialize to 2,1/2,1/2,2. They must be transported as the functions in (6.1), including their compatible roots and the external product whose Nth power is U. This is a concrete occurrence of the peripheral factors the user asked us to retain. It does not by itself repair the earlier positive scalar model's failed move. The scalar, Cartan frame and source normalization of the actual crossing are now accounted for before any such evaluation. Taking absolute values of individual atom entries would still change the quantum contraction. There is also an exact framing norm check on this fixed line. Let beta_ext=(nu_1 nu_2)^(-(N-1)/2) be the external factor in (4.1), and theta_0=x^(1-N) the actual residual twist. Since (nu_1 nu_2)^N=U=x^(2N), (beta_ext/theta_0)^(2N)=1. (6.2) Their moduli therefore cancel exactly in a zero-framed braid evaluation. The remaining phase is part of the specified root cover and pointing; it is not discarded. This checks the normalization of the tetrahedral presentation against the actual framing, rather than adding a free global multiplier. ## 7. Boundary specialization and scope of the comparison After recombination the operator (4.1) is exactly the polynomial semicyclic crossing. Its nilpotent boundary phi_1=phi_2=0 therefore has the original regular value, even though individual atom expressions or uniform frames can be singular. Use the complete identity or its transported lattice for that specialization. The common carry theorem and its bounded normal jets describe the integral recoupling source; the cut operator remains F_N(M)I and the full ADO factor is unchanged. We have consequently identified actual finite root crossings, their genuine braid maps and selected source with explicit literature cyclic tetrahedron atoms, including scalar roots and an external frame. This is a local operator factorization that can be substituted into any already specified finite braid contraction, transporting every paired and boundary leg. It does not prove that arbitrary face turns or all colored Pachner presentations of a positive geometric knot triangulation carry that same relative source and evaluation. The external semicyclic character is still reducible, and fixed root centers still differ from fixed semiclassical shape coordinates. The geometric A-operator/source identification and the selected Bloch-regulator norm across levels remain unproved. There is a concrete check on the distinction just made. At the complete point on the fixed semicyclic center line, (6.1) gives the four central shapes (-1, 1/2, 1/2, -1). Their Bloch--Wigner regulators are all zero because they are real. Thus that fixed-center Bloch sum is not the nonzero hyperbolic fundamental-class regulator. This does not compute the selected quantum period's growth; it shows why a local factorization and matching central equations alone cannot replace the remaining source/cycle and parameter comparison. The subsequent [root tetrahedral pentagon](cyclic_tetrahedron_pentagon.md) now supplies a strict local three-to-two identity for these same finite atoms on a compatible anchored cover. It includes the monomial shears, their changing splitting frames, and all norm and determinant roots. Thus specified exterior contractions can transport this local move exactly. It does not supply the entire geometric tensor presentation. Ordinary five-term transport preserves the zero regulator of the fixed central cycle just computed, so the geometric comparison must still retain the relative source and its selected realization. ## 8. Definitions, coverage and exact diagnostics Formula (1.3) is the alternate cyclic-dilogarithm definition displayed with Definition 3.3 in [Ip--Yamazaki, 1412.5777](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.5777). Only its definition is used; (1.1)--(1.4) prove the needed functional and determinant identities directly. The abstract of [McPhail-Snyder--Reshetikhin, 2509.02354v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02354v2) already covers a four-dilogarithm holonomy factorization. No novelty or independent global invariant is claimed. No published factorization or coherence proof is a premise above. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_four_cyclic_atoms.py) constructs all transported clock/shift modules, cyclic spectral matrices, and central roots over finite fields. It checks 18 crossings at generic and Kashaev colors for N=2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,12. All 72 atom intertwiners satisfy their four generator equations. It independently compares the complete raw product with the actual semicyclic crossing, records its nonzero scalar, and verifies the exact determinant identity (5.1). It checks both restored clock roots and the full final F central powers. Normalization phases in (4.1) are fixed by the uniform anchored argument, rather than unrelated numerical choices of roots. All checks passed. Results: [four_cyclic_atoms_results.json](../experiments/four_cyclic_atoms_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_four_cyclic_atoms.py

title: Recovering the meridian state when the shape plane moves
text: # Recovering the meridian state when the shape plane moves Research note, 25 October 2026. This extends `general_boundary_state_and_framing.md` to the other possible boundary rank. We retain the original charged Andersen--Kashaev tensor and its existing level convention, rather than replacing its tetrahedral function.
