The new construction is inverse Fourier transformation of a specifically leveled tensor. For ordinary fibers it is exactly the state already constructed, including its Gaussian normalization. Definitions used: Andersen--Kashaev, [arXiv:1109.6295v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6295v2), equations (4) and (18), and the Fourier/Gaussian framework of Andersen--Kashaev, [arXiv:1409.1208v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.1208v1), Section 6. All Fourier identities, phases, and analytic arguments needed below are reconstructed here or in the preceding notes. We do not assume an analytic theorem from either source. ## 1. The two ranks and a rational angle path Let a globally branched ideal triangulation of a knot exterior in S^3 have a complete positive geometric structure. Use the independently proved Fourier reduction and cochain identity: W=im S=im B^T, dim W=d=N-2k, G=-2Q+P_+, H=-G/2, L={(t,s):t in W, s-Gt in W^perp}=ker(A|-B). Here the full A,B use N-1 independent edge rows and the unhalved preferred-longitude row. The oriented meridian and longitude have intersection 1, so A_m B_l^T-B_m A_l^T=-2. Rank B_ed is either d-1 or d. The preceding ordinary-fiber theorem treats d-1. We call d the moving-plane case, without assuming that this is the same as any degeneration of the hyperbolic structure. Choose a rational strict reference angle structure theta0, in units of pi, with lifted angular meridian and longitude both zero. Existence follows by rational density around the complete geometric angles. Below physical angles are in radians. Write a for the first shape angle and b'' for the angle of the literature double-prime shape: d0=pi*1-a0, W0=b0''-G d0. The angular gluing equations are A_r a+B_r b''=nu_r. Their homogeneous edge block has rank N-1. Adding both peripheral rows has rank N+1: edge rows are symplectically orthogonal to both peripheral rows, while their mutual pairing is -2. Therefore a rational angle variation (a1,b1'') exists with A_ed a1+B_ed b1''=0, A_m a1+B_m b1''=0, A_l a1+B_l b1''=1. (1.1) Put d1=-a1, W1=b1''-G d1 and theta(lambda)=theta0+lambda*theta1. For real lambda in a neighborhood of zero all physical angles remain strictly positive, mu=0 and the angular longitude equals lambda. The coefficients of theta1 are rational; lambda is measured in radians. If rank B_ed=d-1, then d1 is in W, as proved in the ordinary-fiber note. If rank B_ed=d, then d1 is outside W. Indeed otherwise the projected edge identity gives B_ed W1=0, and B_l is in the row space of B_ed. The longitude variation would then also be zero, contrary to (1.1). Thus S_ext=[S,-d1] has rank d+1 (1.2) in the moving-plane case. ## 2. The exact level and inverse Fourier definition Let T_b(lambda) denote the phase-free reduced integral with all Jacobians, in the common-Phi convention: T_b(lambda)=c_X*(2pi sqrt(h))^(-d) integral_R^d exp[(i y^T H y+(W0+lambda W1)^T y)/(2pi h)] product_j Phi_b(y_j/(2pi sqrt(h))) dz, y=i(d0+lambda d1)+S z, h=b^2/(1+b^2)^2. For real small lambda the exact charged-kernel calculation gives Z_AK(theta(lambda);b) =exp(pi i N/12+i K0(theta(lambda))/h) T_b(lambda), with the explicit K0 of the preceding boundary-state note. Define A_ref(lambda)=lambda W1.d0+(lambda^2/2)W1.d1, K(theta(lambda))=K0(theta(lambda))+A_ref(lambda)/(2pi), L_b(lambda)=exp[-i A_ref(lambda)/(2pi h)] T_b(lambda). (2.1) Consequently L_b is exactly exp(-pi i N/12) times the existing AK leveled tensor at level ell=-4K/pi. No scalar has been suppressed. For real lambda this is an allowed real b-independent level. Complex lambda below means analytic continuation of this precise normalization from its real interval. Define the meridian state by Fourier inversion: J_b(h,x)=1/(8pi^2 h) integral_R L_b(i tau) exp[-i tau x/(4pi h)] d tau. (2.2) The factor 1/(8pi^2 h) follows from the Fourier frequency tau/(4pi h). It is essential for comparison of states, although its logarithm contributes no volume rate. In the moving-plane case this is an ordinary absolutely convergent integral. Substituting (2.1), set y=i d0+S z-tau d1 and I0_b(y)=exp[(i y^T H y+W0^T y)/(2pi h)] product_j Phi_b(y_j/(2pi sqrt(h))). Then the exact formula is J_b(h,x)=c_X/(8pi^2 h)*(2pi sqrt(h))^(-d) integral_R^(d+1) I0_b(y) exp{[i tau W1^T S z-i tau^2 W1.d1/2-i tau x/2]/(2pi h)} dz d tau. (2.3) Every extra quadratic coefficient is real. For real z,tau,x its extra exponential has modulus one. On the horizontal plane Im y=d0, Re(i y^T H y+W0^T y)=b0'' . Re y. Strict angles give 0<b0''_j<d0_j<pi. The exact Phi tails therefore bound the modulus by C exp(-c sum_j |Re y_j|), for fixed b; derivatives only add polynomial factors. By (1.2) this is an exponential bound in |z|+|tau|. It proves absolute convergence, Schwartz regularity, and holomorphy of (2.2) on a small horizontal x strip. The same estimates on smaller real-lambda intervals give analytic continuation of (2.1) to a vertical lambda strip. Explicitly, for lambda=s+i tau, Im y=d0+s d1. The real terms from i tau W1.y and -i A_ref cancel. The remaining modulus is exactly the charged product for theta(s), and hence decreases exponentially in |z|+|tau|, uniformly on smaller s intervals. Fourier inversion, followed by a contour shift within that strip, proves exactly L_b(lambda)=integral_R J_b(h,x) exp(lambda x/(4pi h)) dx. (2.4) Equivalently, this recovers the state from the normalized tensor. Uniqueness is ordinary Fourier uniqueness. No imaginary-charge value is postulated independently of its analytic continuation. This also gives the local factorization for general angles, including nonzero angular meridian mu. Let theta be near theta0, with angular longitude lambda, and set d_bar=d0+lambda d1, W_bar=W0+lambda W1, Delta W=W_theta-W_bar, K(theta)=K0(theta)+[A_ref(lambda)+Delta W.d_bar]/(2pi). (2.5) The fixed-longitude relation gives d_theta-d_bar in W and Delta W in W^perp. Contour translation through the convex positive angle segment changes T_b by precisely exp[i Delta W.d_bar/(2pi h)]. Thus Z_AK(theta;b)=exp(pi i N/12+i K(theta)/h) integral_(R+i mu) J_b(h,x) exp(lambda*x/(4pi h)) dx. (2.6) Locally the small mu contour lies in the holomorphic x strip above; its translation changes no integral. Formula (2.5) is an explicit real angle polynomial, and ell=-4K/pi is its existing AK level. This supplies the general peripheral factorization near completeness, rather than only the zero-meridian slice used to define the Fourier transform. Continuation beyond these strips needs its own contour control; no global continuation through singularities is asserted. The factor two can also be checked directly for a variation at fixed longitude: its symplectic pairing with theta1 gives Delta W.d1-W1.(d_theta-d_bar)=-mu/2. The corresponding real tau term in the shifted z contour is -tau*mu/2; the x contour Im x=mu supplies +tau*mu/2. They cancel exactly. The audit verifies this identity on the entire balanced angle space, with both peripheral variations free, before any specialization. ## 3. Agreement with the ordinary-fiber construction Suppose rank B_ed=d-1 and retain p,beta from the preceding note. Write d1=S eta1. The zero-meridian condition gives S^T W1=p/2, p^T eta1=-beta, W1.d1=-beta/2. In (2.3) change z to z+tau eta1. The extra classical phase becomes i tau(p^T z-x)/2-i beta tau^2/4. If beta is nonzero, its Fresnel integral gives precisely J_b(h,x)=1/(2pi sqrt(h)*sqrt(2i beta)) integral exp[i(x-x')^2/(8pi beta h)] J_old(h,x') dx'. The square root is the branch recorded in the ordinary-fiber note. If beta=0, Fourier inversion gives delta(p^T z-x), recovering its positive coarea fiber exactly. These operations may be justified by a Gaussian cutoff and Schwartz Fourier inversion; no absolute Fubini assertion is made for (2.3) in this noninjective case. Also (2.1) reduces exactly to K=K_old-beta*lambda^2/(8pi). Thus the inverse Fourier definition agrees with the previously normalized meridian state in every ordinary-fiber chart. It is an extension of the same construction, including its finite-b phase. ## 4. Independence of the auxiliary angle path For vectors (a,c), where c denotes the double-prime angle, use the symplectic form Omega((a,c),(a',c'))=a.c'-c.a'. The kernel of the edge, meridian and longitude rows is the symplectic dual of the edge-row space. It is isotropic with every solution of the homogeneous edge equations. This follows directly by dimensions and the peripheral pairing -2; it is not an additional NZ theorem. Consequently, if delta d,delta W are angle variations with zero meridian and longitude, then delta d in W, delta W in W^perp, delta W.d1=W1.delta d. (4.1) Change theta1 by such a variation, keeping theta0 fixed. Contour translation in W changes T_b(lambda) by exactly exp{i[lambda delta W.d0+lambda^2 delta W.d1]/(2pi h)}. The change in A_ref is the same polynomial, by (4.1) and delta W.delta d=0. Hence L_b and J_b are unchanged, not merely equal in modulus. The argument first holds for small real lambda where both paths have positive angles and then continues analytically. Changing the reference theta0 to another strict rational reference with mu=lambda=0 gives only J_new=exp[i (W_new-W0).d0/(2pi h)] J_old. (4.2) This is the previously recorded central phase. It is retained in the level and leaves the boundary annihilator unchanged. ## 5. Exact classical equations and the extra saddle direction The moving-plane action in (2.3) is F_ext(z,tau;x)=F0(y)+i tau W1^T S z -i tau^2 W1.d1/2-i tau x/2, F0(y)=i y^T H y+W0^T y-i sum_j Li_2(-exp y_j), y=i d0+r, r=S z-tau d1. Use the lifted shape deviations u=Log z_shape-i a0=-r, v=Log z_shape''-i b0'', D=v-G r. Differentiation gives grad_z F_ext=i S^T(D+tau W1). At a z-critical point rho=D+tau W1 is in W^perp. From (1.1) and the projected cochain identities one obtains, with full lifted holonomies H_r=A_r u+B_r v, H_ed=0, H_l=-tau. (5.1) For the remaining derivative, partial_tau F_ext =-i(b1'' . u-a1 . v)-i x/2. The angle variation (a1,b1'') differs from (B_m^T,-A_m^T)/2 by a symplectic dual edge vector, because its longitude is one and its meridian is zero. Thus on H_ed=0, b1'' . u-a1 . v=-H_m/2, partial_tau F_ext=i(H_m-x)/2. (5.2) All reference constants cancel in these formulas; the holonomies are differences from their specified reference lifts. Hence the full saddle equations are the edge equations with H_m=x, and the boundary phase derivative is i H_l/2. The variable x really is the meridian coordinate, without a zero-shear assumption. At the complete shapes H_m=H_l=0. They lie in the lambda=0 plane y=i d0+W by the preferred-longitude relation. Equations (5.1)--(5.2) put their saddle at tau=0, including the new transverse direction. Its phase value is the old F0 value, whose real part is -Vol(M). ## 6. Contour deformation and the volume theorem Write d_geo-d0=S eta for the difference to the actual complete geometric angles. Move the z contour through z+i s eta, 0<=s<=1, keeping tau real. These are the convex strict angle structures with zero meridian and longitude, so (4.1) applies at each s. There is a potentially dangerous new linear tau term. It cancels exactly: if delta W=W_s-W0 and delta d=S s eta, the real linear change from F0 is tau*delta W.d1, while the cross term in (2.3) contributes -tau*W1.delta d. Equation (4.1) makes their sum zero. The modulus on every intermediate plane is therefore the charged product for its positive angles. Its exponential tails are uniform on the compact angle segment. The Phi poles stay outside 0<Im y_j<pi, and Cauchy side faces vanish. This justifies the contour deformation for the complete d+1 dimensional integral. On the geometric horizontal plane its real Hessian is -S_ext^T diag[Im(e^y/(1+e^y))] S_ext. All diagonal entries are positive and S_ext has full column rank. Thus this Hessian is negative definite. The added real quadratic chirp affects only the imaginary part. The geometric critical point is the unique maximum on this plane and has a nonzero complex Gaussian coefficient. The previously proved uniform Phi remainder and global linear tail estimates now give the ordinary multivariate complex saddle asymptotic, in dimension d+1. The prefactor in (2.3) is h^(-d/2-1), and the saddle factor is h^((d+1)/2). The resulting polynomial scale is h^(-1/2), agreeing with the ordinary-fiber normalization. In particular the state is nonzero for all sufficiently small h and lim_(h->0+) -2pi h log|J_b(h,0)|=Vol(M). (6.1) Together with the ordinary-fiber theorem this proves (6.1) for every globally branched complete positive geometric knot triangulation, with its specified normalized tensor-derived meridian state. The extra boundary-rank and zero-shear hypotheses have been removed. ## 7. Quantum operator and the limits of the result Every Phi argument and Gaussian coefficient in (2.3) is rational, apart from the recorded pi offsets and powers of h. The independent finite-product, dimension-count and moment argument of `general_annihilator_and_volume.md` therefore applies to this state. It gives a nonzero annihilator and its primitive minimal generator in the existing Andersen--Malusa b-shift algebra, after the stated finite coefficient cover and descent. No Jones-polynomial input is used, and no preservation of minimal degree under a fractional Gaussian conjugation is assumed. In its conventions Q=exp(-2pi b t), E f(t)=f(t-i b), t=x/(2pi sqrt(h)), EQ=qQE, q=exp(2pi i b^2). Equations (5.1)--(5.2) give the classical branch Q=exp(-H_m), E=exp(H_l/2). The previously proved uniform saddle substitution makes its geometric peripheral factor divide the classical symbol of the minimal annihilator. All generic peripheral coefficients must still be retained. Equality to the entire A-polynomial, equality to a Jones AJ operator, and an explicit coefficient list do not follow from existence alone. This is a theorem for the specified realizations. It does not construct complete positive triangulations for all alternating knots, treat flat tetrahedra, prove arbitrary global state identifications, or establish an H-triangulation limit. Those remain parts of the original objective. It also does not identify the positive factorial sum with this complex state. The exact matrix, polynomial, branch and Fourier-normalization checks are in `experiments/audit_fourier_boundary.py`. They include a six-tetrahedron 5_2 chart with rank B_ed=rank B=4, so that its longitude really moves the shape plane. Its topology calibration uses three explicitly recorded 2--3 moves; the local quantum move identity is not inferred from this combinatorial calibration. ## 8. A certified moving-plane example The fixture has ideal triangulation signature gLLPQcdefeffikdqhtk. Its stacked face kernel has dimension k=1, its reduced dimension is d=4, both B ranks are 4, c_X=1, and S_ext has rank 5. The rational zero-meridian longitude variation can be chosen with d1=(1/2,0,0,0,0,0). Thus this is an actual instance of (2.3), not just an abstract symplectic matrix example. In its native positive convention the six shapes are a, a, (a+2)/a^2, a-1, a^2/((a-1)(a+2)), -(a+1)^2/a, a^3+3a^2+2a+1=0. Rouche's inequality on the rational disc centered at (-337641021+562279512i)/10^9, of radius 10^(-8), has remainder-to-linear ratio less than 0.044. Rational images and argument intervals put every physical angle above 0.14 radians. All native edge and peripheral products reduce exactly modulo this cubic; the argument intervals fix the six edge branches at 2pi and both peripheral branches at zero. The script separately verifies the literature shape equations after the recorded vertex reorderings, without guessing a global conjugation. Regina verifies each of the three legal 2--3 moves from the already audited three-tetrahedron twist chart. Its initial combinatorial isomorphism maps the independently marked twist meridian to minus the source meridian, with zero longitude shear and zero additive angle correction. The final preferred longitude also has a separate integral dual-boundary certificate. These are topology and marking checks; a complex quantum-state identity along this particular sequence is not asserted without its level and move-phase audit. The resulting hyperbolic volume is 2.82812208833078316276... . The 70-digit numerical diagnostic of the full five-direction saddle is recorded separately from the rational geometry and matrix certificates. ## 9. A uniform boundary phase, independent of the angle path For every balanced angle structure in the local factorization domain, let d=pi*1-a, W=b''-Gd, with fixed zero-peripheral reference d0,W0. If r is the number of tetrahedra, set L_tet(theta)=-pi*r/24+sum_j epsilon_j(c_j-b_j)/12, where b_j denotes the middle physical angle. Then exactly K(theta)=L_tet(theta) +[d0.W-W0.d-d0.W0]/(4pi)-lambda*mu/(8pi). (9.1) The first two terms are affine in the angles; the only quadratic peripheral term is universal. The auxiliary path theta1 has disappeared. For the proof, the charged phase and W=2Qd-C reduce to K0=L_tet-d.W/(4pi). Write d=d0+lambda*d1+delta d, W=W0+lambda*W1+delta W. At fixed longitude, delta d lies in the allowed shape subspace, delta W annihilates it, and the peripheral pairing gives delta W.delta d=0, delta W.d1-W1.delta d=-mu/2. Expansion of (2.5) cancels lambda^2. Its remaining quadratic term is lambda*(delta W.d1-W1.delta d)/(4pi), giving (9.1). This is the boundary Heisenberg term hidden in the separate chart normalizations. It connects the continuous level with the structural period line of `heisenberg_period_torsor.md`. The identity retains the full angle polynomials before any peripheral specialization.

title: An actual bounded source in the Fourier--Mellin polarization
text: # An actual bounded source in the Fourier--Mellin polarization Research construction, 27 October 2026. A fixed rational inhomogeneous source need not be assumed as a special factorization of the original meridian operator. It can be constructed in the Fourier--Mellin polarization directly from any actual all-level operator and finitely many fixed colors. The original Kashaev invariant is retained as an exact coefficient period. It is not replaced by point evaluation or by a new state. This gives an actual sourced quantum-A object for arbitrary knots. Its classical geometric support and selected regulator norm still require proof; the volume conjecture is not proved here. ## 1. Actual input and the Q convention Choose the nonzero rational operator supplied by the [Q-only construction](even_meridian_norm_descent.md), clear its coefficient denominators, and remove a common shift: P=sum_(j=0)^d a_j(Q,Y) T^j, a_j=sum_m a_(j,m)(Q) Y^m, TY=QYT, a_0 a_d!=0. (1.1) Here d>=1, the m support is finite, and the coefficients belong to the rational function field ℚ(Q). The associated fixed-color periods are C_n(Q), normalized by C_n(1)=1. They are the actual finite reduced periods of the existing color-pointing theorem. The exact identities are F_N(Y=Q_N^n)=C_n(Q_N), 1<=n<=N, C_N(Q_N)=F_N(1)=<K>_N, Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N). (1.2) There is no large-color asymptotic premise in (1.2). For completeness these fixed-color functions descend to Q=q^2 as well. On the ordinary n-dimensional color x=q^(n-1), use the same stripped crossing coefficients, ordinary pivot K and residual twist x. The total x-power on a closed state is E_ord=b-1-w+sum_positive(-a-c)+sum_negative(a+c) =-kappa_D+2sum_negative a-2sum_positive c, because sum(c-a)=0. It is even for a knot. All remaining factors are expressed in Q and x^2. At x=q^(n-1) this is a rational function of Q. The known Laurent regularity and normalization of C_n are those of the original finite color construction, not an additional asymptotic or Jones-identification assumption. Applying the actual root equation to (1.2), then using infinitely many distinct Q_N for every fixed n, gives the generic recurrence sum_(j=0)^d a_j(Q,Q^n) C_(n+j)(Q)=0, n>=1. (1.3) This is the same elementary cross-level rigidity used in the [all-level period theorem](all_level_a_period.md). ## 2. Choose a nonsingular fixed starting color Let A be the Q-exponent span in the collected Laurent support of a_d(Q,Y). For every integer r>A, the substitution a_d(Q,Q^r) is nonzero. Indeed distinct monomials Q^u Y^v become Q^(u+rv), and a collision with v!=v' would imply r<=|u-u'|<=A. Equal-v terms were already collected. Choose the fixed integer n_0>=d+A+1. (2.1) Then a_d(Q,Q^(n_0-d))!=0, and also a_d(Q,Q^(r-d))!=0 for every r>=n_0. Every C_n is nonzero since C_n(1)=1. These facts will give both a nonzero source and unique formal propagation in the chosen source lattice. ## 3. The exact Fourier--Mellin operator and its boundary source Form the actual formal generating period Z(Q,X)=sum_(n>=n_0) C_n(Q) X^n in X^(n_0) ℚ(Q)[[X]]. (3.1) Let S act by S f(X)=f(QX), so SX=QXS. The quantum-torus Fourier map is the exact algebra map Y |-> S, T |-> X^(-1). It respects TY=QYT because X^(-1)S=QSX^(-1). In the recorded left-coefficient ordering its image is P^M=sum_(j,m) a_(j,m)(Q) Q^(-mj) X^(-j) S^m. (3.2) Negative m are allowed; they are invertible shifts. A fixed left power of S makes the displayed operator have nonnegative order, transporting its source by the same power, if that convention is desired. No factor of the source is discarded by doing so. Multiplying (1.3) by X^n and summing n>=n_0 gives P^M Z=B(Q,X), (3.3) where the source is the explicit fixed Laurent polynomial B=sum_(j,m) a_(j,m)(Q) Q^(-mj) X^(-j) sum_(r=n_0)^(n_0+j-1) C_r(Q) Q^(mr) X^r. (3.4) The empty sum for j=0 is zero. The identity follows termwise from sum_(n>=n_0) Q^(mn) C_(n+j) X^n =Q^(-mj) X^(-j) [Z(Q,Q^m X) -sum_(r=n_0)^(n_0+j-1) C_r(Q) Q^(mr) X^r]. Every coefficient of every X power involves only finitely many terms; convergence is not assumed. The source uses exactly the d fixed colors C_(n_0),...,C_(n_0+d-1). Its X powers lie between n_0-d and n_0-1. Its lowest coefficient is [X^(n_0-d)]B=C_(n_0)(Q) a_d(Q,Q^(n_0-d))!=0. (3.5) Thus it is a genuine nonzero bounded source, not a possibly vanishing right-hand side inferred from formal elimination. ## 4. The pointing and the original period are retained Equation (3.3), together with the lattice condition Z in X^(n_0)[[X]], specifies Z uniquely. A nonzero homogeneous difference W in this lattice, of lowest power r>=n_0, would contribute at power r-d only through j=d. Its coefficient would be a_d(Q,Q^(r-d)) [X^r]W, which is nonzero by (2.1), a contradiction. Thus the source and specified lattice retain the actual finite-color pointing. For every N>=n_0 the original invariant is exactly <K>_N=[ [X^N]Z(Q,X) ]_(Q=Q_N) =Res_(X=0) Z(Q_N,X) X^(-N-1)dX. (4.1) The first expression means whole-germ specialization of the coefficient C_N(Q). Even if coefficients of a recurrence or a companion solution have poles at Q_N, C_N itself is the original regular Laurent period. No division by such a pole precedes its cancellation. The residue notation means coefficient extraction; it does not assert an analytically convergent contour realization. The full ADO period is still d_N(M)F_N(M), with its marked pole, residue, first jet and sign retained in the original meridian realization. This change of polarization constructs the same reduced Kashaev scalar in (4.1); it does not silently evaluate or remove d_N. A comparison of full-state realizations must transport that specified normalization line as well. ## 5. Classical support and the affine extension At Q=1 the symbol of (3.2) is exactly P_cl(S,X^(-1)). (5.1) Thus the classical Fourier transformation exchanges the meridian coordinate and the inverse longitude coordinate in the specified ordering. If a geometric factor occurs in the original actual symbol, its transformed geometric factor occurs here. No such factor is inferred merely from the transform. The marked regulator action is compatible with this polarization. Let y=Log Y, lambda=Log(L/L_c) and use H=Log Q, centering the longitude logarithm at the chosen complete lift L_c. Use the corresponding centered WKB action dW=lambda dy. The original constant character L_c is retained separately, rather than dropped from the period. In centered coordinates x=Log(X/X_c)=-lambda, X_c=L_c^(-1), with new momentum y. Hence W^M=W-y lambda, dW^M=y dx. (5.2) Its symmetric regulator coordinate is unchanged: R=W-(1/2)y lambda =W^M-(1/2)x y. (5.3) Indeed dR=(lambda dy-y d lambda)/2, exactly the marked regulator differential after Y=m and L^2=l are substituted. At the chosen complete lift y=0 the Legendre correction vanishes, including a retained longitude sign. Thus the previously calibrated complete imaginary action is preserved. This checks the classical marked action, not a normalization or asymptotic theorem for the quantum coefficient period (4.1). Grouping the m powers of S and using its usual companion realization turns (3.3), when its S-order is positive, into an affine difference extension with rational coefficients and the explicit source (3.4). One can homogenize it by the exact source annihilator (S-B(Q,QX)/B(Q,X)) P^M Z=0. (5.4) The source quotient and the chosen formal lattice must remain marked; (5.4) is not permission to replace the original object by an arbitrary homogeneous solution. If the transformed order is zero, (3.3) is instead its rational algebraic source equation; no artificial order is inserted to manufacture a geometric block. This removes the need to assume a special inhomogeneous right factor in order to obtain some canonical generic sourced polarization of the actual A-period. It does not prove that this extension is generically nonsplit, identify its geometric source class, or bound the selected coefficient norm in (4.1). ## 6. The precise comparison residual For two supplied affine systems sigma v_i=C_i v_i+c_i, a proposed map v_act=P v_geo+b is horizontal precisely when sigma(P) C_geo=C_act P, (sigma-C_act)b=c_act-sigma(P)c_geo. (6.1) Thus after a homogeneous comparison P, the remaining obstruction is the explicit class [c_act-sigma(P)c_geo] in F^d/(sigma-C_act)F^d. (6.2) An affine cut ell_i v_i+k_i is preserved additionally when ell_act P=ell_geo, k_act+ell_act b=k_geo. (6.3) The second equation retains the dual affine constant. Generic matrix invertibility does not by itself transport the boundary lattice. The new construction supplies the actual side of (6.1)--(6.3) in this polarization. It does not supply the geometric side or assert that their class (6.2) vanishes. Multiplicative rank-one curvature descent alone does not solve this additive source problem. The [actual Mellin normal-source theorem](actual_mellin_normal_source_rigidity.md) now uses this very source quotient to exhibit a dual cocycle with value one on the selected section. Its normal symbol is therefore nonzero for every knot, without a semisimplicity assumption. Whole first-normal compatibility removes central scalar freedom on that selected line. The [cyclotomic jet theorem](mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness.md) additionally fixes arbitrary root sections in the exact pole lattice using a bounded number of source-compatible quantum levels. Neither theorem constructs the geometric side of (6.1)--(6.3) or estimates the selected residue's norm. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_fourier_mellin_actual_source.py). [Results](../experiments/fourier_mellin_actual_source_results.json).

title: Independent audit of the Fourier partial geometric-support theorem
text:
# Independent audit of the Fourier partial geometric-support theorem 27 October 2026. Proof pass of Section 7 of [the partial-support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md), with the source category and normalization checked against [the whole wire polarization](actual_two_cut_fourier_polarization_and_cap.md) and [the actual Fourier normal block](actual_fourier_polarized_geometric_normal_block.md). The new result is an operator for an actual all-level ROOT partial family, with a nonzero formal geometric line. It is not an operator identity for the whole generic-q Vandermonde germ or a theorem about the final selected geometric coefficient. ## 1. The actual raw source retains both factors of 1/N The literal partial trace on the second wire is invariant under I tensor V, retaining the first original rank-one row. Thus \[ \widetilde F_N(a,j)=\sum_c T^V_{c,j;a,j} = rac1N\sum_{b,
u,u}Q_N^{j
u}W_N(a,b,
u,u), \qquad F_N= rac1N\sum_{a,j}\widetilde F_N(a,j). \] The inner 1/N is the Fourier inverse and the outer 1/N is the original first-cut source. Charge conservation changes the first output to a-nu, but does not impose nu=0 before transforming. Summing j afterward kills exactly the nonzero offsets in their actual range |nu| less than N. The four original head bounds and original pivots stay in W_N; no new second pivot occurs. Restricting c=a early would make the transformed diagonal independent of j and would destroy this construction. The generic-q Vandermonde inverse is the Lagrange coefficient matrix, not Q^(-bj)/N. The proper lift used in the certificate is the latter monomial kernel. They agree at every original root for every M, which is sufficient for its all-level ROOT meridian identity. Their q-normal derivatives generally differ. The theorem states this distinction rather than suppressing the actual connection or carries. ## 2. The nonzero certificate survives its new dimensions and boundaries Opening the two physical cuts adds one independent integer boundary offset on the integral tree flow chart. After polarization the internal labels are b,nu,u, of dimension r_F=m+1; a and j remain external. All positions, transfers and factorial lengths are fixed integral affine forms in these variables and N. The additional factor q^(2j nu) has a rational proper ratio under every internal shift. Its external multiplication character is q^j; the possible q square roots and existing signs remain on their stated covers. The Section 2 count therefore has r_F+4 multiplication variables, including x,z=q^N,q^a,q^j. Its image space is O(R^(r_F+4)), while the independent Ore monomials including the meridian and r_F internal shifts number (R+1)^(r_F+5). The boundary count also extends: if near-boundary linear forms have rank c on N,a,j,b,nu,u, their labels have O(R^c) possibilities and their c binomial reductions remove the same c multiplication degrees. No external label is silently treated as fixed during that count. A strict cone exists by taking the old transfer variables small and positive and the cut positions away from both endpoints. The tree particular open flow changes all these finitely many affine forms by fixed multiples of nu; a sufficiently smaller two-sided nu interval preserves strict inequalities. The Fourier index j has its own independent interior interval. Thus the open identity extends to the independent character field by the same cone-density proof; it is not an identity known only at one discrete frame. The factor 1/N is a common line fixed by all relevant shifts and does not affect the dimension count. Strip the largest common z+1 factor from the WHOLE finite-array certificate before evaluating z=-1. Finite original head factorial denominators remain regular at q_N. Least-degree expansion in the internal shifts around one then produces a nonzero meridian operator after exact finite moment extraction. Every actual zero-extension stratum is included. There is no multiplication by an independently supplied geometric factor. ## 3. The formal geometric block is supplied by the actual open phase The entire open coefficient, with its original finite factorial arguments, gives S_open, not just a list of fixed-band ratios. The new Fourier monomial gives the exact additional phase vt. Fixing the old first physical position leaves one old framing radical xi in the (b,u) variables. The old Hessian has precisely that radical. The mixed derivative c satisfies c dot xi=d log p_e(xi). This is nonzero on the new regular polarization chart. Hence \[ H_{new}= egin{pmatrix}H_0&c\c^t&\gamma\end{pmatrix} \] has zero kernel: pairing its first equation with xi kills the last coordinate, then the remaining vector is a multiple of xi, and the last equation kills that multiple. This argument is valid even at an old two-position projection caustic. It assumes the original regular coefficient-shape chart, as stated. The birational (A,p_e) assertion at a complete discrete-faithful point also passes. An upper triangular word in the discrete torsion free projective group has equal diagonal entries: contracting or recurrent conjugates of the cut parabolic otherwise contradict discreteness, and a nontrivial finite diagonal ratio gives torsion. If p_e were independent of the remaining frame coordinate, the prefix Mobius formula would force U-V=b E_12 and both U,V upper triangular. Their equal-diagonal property would then make the second position independent too, contradicting the chosen pair. The displayed rational inverse consequently defines a nonempty birational chart. This is not a global compactification assertion. At the selected incidence v=-Log p_e, the new critical point has t=0 and value S_geo. The Fourier character is one there, the original leading amplitude is a unit, and the new Hessian is invertible. There is therefore a nonzero formal Gaussian block with the original regulator action. The normalized Fourier pair has (1/N)H_N^(-2)=1/(2 pi i H_N). Its ordered cross-pair phase is explicitly fixed; it does not hide a variable source factor. This argument permits macroscopic nu as an actual proper-array coordinate before contraction. It does NOT sum a fixed-offset asymptotic formula over offsets growing with N. ## 4. Why the SAME operator acquires the geometric factor The auxiliary coefficient realization has the exact proper ratios used by the finite certificate. Translating every nondegenerate internal formal integration coordinate gives the exact exponential weight character. Applying the SAME least-moment extraction to that identity therefore makes the finite-array operator annihilate the nonzero formal block. No unsummed framing radical or omitted Green endpoint is used in this step: both framing coordinates are external in the Fourier partial family. For a fixed external cut position and Fourier character, its critical value remains S_geo throughout the meridian deformation germ. The geometric point stays at t=0 and the other critical equations hold; the derivative at fixed external labels is the preferred longitude derivative. Thus its first meridian shift ratio is L_geo. Strip the operator's common scalar q-1 valuation. Its first nonzero classical symbol vanishes on L_geo for independent external framing characters, so the marked irreducible A_geo divides it over their transcendental coefficient field. Formal Ore right division gives the stated line quotient as well. Positive shift order follows from the nonzero block; an order-zero nonzero multiplier cannot annihilate it. The geometric factor is consequently forced by a nonzero operator constructed from the actual finite family, rather than appended to an unrelated annihilator. The proof does not identify the minimal full scalar operator, and the factor may be lost in the final source-paired sum over a,j. The complete peripheral line is still transported by its ordered Ore gauge. ## 5. Independent check of the whole wire map and bounded-test formula The Lagrange inverse, both truncated-shift carries and the actual Ecal,F,K transforms in the whole polarization note pass algebraically. In particular their endpoint terms have coefficients 1-Q^N and M-M inverse separately. The derivative connection A_Q=(D_Q V)V inverse=J_eval(V J V inverse) has the displayed order; the resulting commutator drops out only after the actual partial trace. Its root norm bound (N-1)^2 follows from V/sqrt(N) unitary. For the independent bounded-band theorem, implicit differentiation gives u prime=-S_uu inverse S_u nu. Differentiating the determinant of the Hessian gives exactly the stated alpha, and differentiating the critical action gives beta=(S_nu nu-ell_i G^ij ell_j)/2. The first Gaussian correction cancels in Z_q/Z_0 at order H. Formal constant-term integration by parts then produces -alpha E_eta h+beta E_eta squared h with the printed signs. These finite tests keep physical B and Fourier eta independent. They are consistent with, but are not used as a substitute for, the macroscopic open-phase proof in Sections 2--4 above.

title: Independent audit: actual Fourier currents can lose geometric support
text: # Independent audit: actual Fourier currents can lose geometric support Proof audit, 27 October 2026, of [the actual Fourier cancellation theorem](actual_fourier_source_cancellation.md). The actual current/source equations, cyclic contraction and nonzero geometric formal block pass with the qualifications below. This does not refute the volume conjecture or show that the original uninserted knot period loses its geometric contribution. ## 1. The current and whole source are literal actual operations For the original four-port tensor and B=diag(Q^b) on its second wire, W(T)=((I tensor B)T(I tensor B^-1)-T)/(Q-1) has coefficient [q]_Q T on output offset q=d-b. For every integer q, [q]_Q=(Q^q-1)/(Q-1) is a Laurent polynomial. Thus this is an actual finite port current with unchanged support and source tensors. It is not an assumed total Hopf action on a diagonal reshaping. The identity-wire closure sets d=b, where the multiplier is exactly zero. Therefore ptr_second W(T)=0 entrywise as a WHOLE rational finite-matrix identity, including all its specified normal derivatives. All original first-port bands, pivots, scalar phases and d_N(M) factors remain. No root scalarity, source invariance on charged matrices or positivity hypothesis is needed for this cancellation. At the primitive root the raw Fourier kernel is Q_N^(jq)/N, so its effect is exactly (J_(j+1)-J_j)/(Q_N-1), with cyclic j. There is no further original-cut 1/N after fixing the first input. The printed centered prefix inverse satisfies Dh=hD=I-P, and its nonconstant Fourier eigenvalues are (Q_N-1)/(Q_N^k-1), all of modulus at most one. The distance identity follows from orthogonal projection onto the constant line. These statements concern the declared finite root source complex, not a bound for the full word or its normal germs. Off root the actual whole Vandermonde inverse has its last-row carry. Its transformed current is not the uncorrected cyclic difference. The note explicitly uses the whole partial-trace identity for normal sources, which is the correct scope. ## 2. The formal shift uses the specified proper root lift The geometric construction uses the ORIGINAL open coefficient model and its specified proper lift Q^(jq)/N. Multiplication by [q]_Q is consequently exactly the external shift difference Z_W(v,H)=(Z(v+H,H)-Z(v,H))/(exp(H)-1). This is a coefficient identity before Gaussian contraction. Formal contraction at the shifted critical point commutes with that base shift, by the same translated-critical-point argument used for the partial certificate theorem. It is stronger than summing bounded q asymptotics; every original finite-band term is retained first. This identity is NOT asserted for the actual whole Vandermonde inverse away from the root. Those two partial families agree on the original roots but have different normal source germs. The note preserves this distinction. Likewise the local critical branch need not be periodic under v->v+2pi*i even though the original finite root family is cyclic. Its global continuation/ selected source is precisely the issue being tested. The critical action is frame-independent: on the open Fourier critical family t=0, so the envelope derivative with respect to v is t=0. The added vt term also vanishes there. Thus no derivative of a moving leading phase has been omitted. With all common base/peripheral lines retained, Z=C exp(S_geo/H)(A_0(v)+H A_1(v)+...), the shift yields Z_W=C exp(S_geo/H)(partial_v A_0+O(H)). The common line C can retain M-dependent peripheral data; the v derivative does not replace or reset it. ## 3. Why the leading derivative is genuinely nonzero The uniform actual principal-density theorem gives, on its marked half-density cover, Omega_beta^2=-(T_beta/2) Omega_cut^2. Here T_beta is independent of the representation's simultaneous framing conjugation. This follows directly from its determinant definition, not an imported torsion theorem. If S is the derivative of simultaneous conjugation and G its adjoint action on sl_2, the complex maps transform as A'=S A G^-1, D'=S D S^-1, M'=G M S^-1. Use V_c'=S V_c and W'=S W G^-1 in its determinant ratio. The same det(S) occurs in numerator and denominator, while det(G)=1; they cancel. The last equality follows, for example, because conjugation on all 2x2 matrices has determinant one and fixes the scalar line, hence also has determinant one on sl_2. The square-root ratio is a nonzero function whose square is frame-independent. In characteristic zero its framing derivatives are therefore zero. The fixed ordered phase/sign remains in its marked line and cannot become an arbitrary v-dependent factor. At completeness and fixed good A, s=A^-1-1 is fixed and Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)] =-(partial_v r/s) dlog A wedge dv. The Fourier Gaussian normalization supplies the actual Jacobian to the same exterior coordinate volume. Consequently A_0(v)=c(M,A) partial_v r, with c nonzero and independent of v, up to the recorded fixed Fourier phase. On the proved complete birational (A,p_e) chart, r is a nonconstant rational function of eta=exp(v)=p_e^-1. If partial_v A_0 vanished, then eta partial_eta r would be a constant d. The rational derivative dr has zero residue at eta=0, whereas d deta/eta has residue d. Thus d=0 and r is constant, a contradiction. This proves nonzero leading current amplitude on a dense regular open; its marked meridian germ remains nonzero. The nonzero statement is at a GOOD first-position phase. The highest-input a=0 specialization has the exact one-sided support, but no nonzero geometric block is thereby proved at its A=1 boundary. These are two properties of the same actual family at different first-input phases. They must not be presented as a simultaneous one-sided highest-boundary counterexample. The weaker, needed obstruction already follows: a genuine zero-source actual family has nonzero regular geometric partial support. ## 4. A clean certificate proof avoids a unit-amplitude shortcut The current multiplier is (exp(t)-1)/(exp(H)-1) in the enlarged open phase. It vanishes at t=0 and carries H^-1. Thus the original unit-principal-amplitude premise cannot simply be invoked for its UNCONTRACTED current integrand. The exact shift constructs the formal contraction, including those finite negative powers, and the preceding proof makes its final leading coefficient nonzero. There is a simple independent way to obtain its certified meridian operator. Let D(eta) be an already constructed nonzero operator annihilating the proper partial family J(eta) and its formal block. The coefficient substitution eta->Q eta commutes with the meridian Ore step, so D(Q eta) annihilates J(Q eta) and its corresponding shifted block. A nonzero common LEFT multiple L of these two operators annihilates their difference divided by Q-1, and hence both the actual root current family and the SAME formal current. Such a multiple needs only finite coefficient linear algebra. If the two orders are r,s, seek X of order at most s and Y of order at most r with X D=Y D_shift. There are r+s+2 unknown coefficients and at most r+s+1 equations over the coefficient field. A nonzero solution gives a nonzero common multiple, since the Ore polynomial ring over a field is a domain: leading coefficients multiply with an automorphism and cannot vanish. Clear denominators in this exact combination before root/source specialization, using the existing finite-array specialization guard. Its nonzero formal current has the same leading action and a nonzero coefficient on a dense open, so the original classical symbol argument forces the same geometric A-factor. No independent A-polynomial is inserted into an annihilator. The final actual scalar current is nonetheless identically zero, and its scalar annihilator is the unit operator. This establishes the claimed loss of partial support in the source pushforward. The exact audit script [checks the coefficient/source complex](../experiments/audit_zero_source_fourier_current.py) and its whole two-color carry guard. The analytic growth, selected cycle and uninserted knot period are not determined by this example.

title: The Frobenius clock needs a logarithmic internal-centralizer adapter
text: # The Frobenius clock needs a logarithmic internal-centralizer adapter Independent current-map theorem and audit, 27 October 2026. The actual Frobenius source gives the correct finite cut clock and a regular finite approximation to the old physical Springer graph. It does not identify the internal centralizer coordinate by an algebraic symplectic map. That coordinate necessarily contains a logarithm of the source angular flag. The same source Cartan current has two distinct geometric interpretations, which must not be conflated. There is also an exact metric qualification for the controlled head-shift gauge: its standard-coordinate unitarity does not give a polynomial bound in the compact coherent metric. ## 1. The actual finite clock graph and its marked flux Use the r=N actual Frobenius source of [the two-clock theorem](high_color_two_clock_normal_source.md), with \(v=t\), \(a=u/(1+tu)\), \(T=va\), and \(\Omega=dv\wedge da=-dT\wedge d\log v\). The covariant symbol of the actual operator \(Q_N^{-R}\) is exactly \[ F_N(T)=[1+\alpha_NT]^N,\qquad \alpha_N=Q_N^{-1}-1,\quad Q_N=e^{c/N},\ c=2\pi i. \] On the cyclotomic diagonal source, \(Q_N^S=Q_N^R\) as OPERATORS, so this is the single symbol of the inverse head clock. It does not license pointwise products or inversion of symbols. Put \[ \eta_N=\frac{1-F_N(va)}v,\qquad A_N=F_N^{-1}. \] The division by v is polynomially removable at zero. On the opposite chart \(V=1/v,T'=1-T\), \[ F_N(1-T')=[1+(Q_N-1)T']^N,\qquad \eta'_N=-v^2\eta_N=\frac{F_N(1-T')-1}{V}. \] Thus both pole clutches are retained by an actual algebraic finite-clock graph. Uniformly on compact complex source sets, it converges with fixed derivatives to \((1-e^{-cva})/v\), the earlier physical graph. This convergence identifies geometric coordinate functions. Section 6 distinguishes the NEW diagonal position clock from the OLD physical clock after the actual Fourier/shear source gauge; they must not be identified merely from the diagonal constraint. For N>=3 and \(0\le T\le1\), \[ \cos^N(\pi/N)\le|F_N(T)|\le1 . \] The graph avoids the Gauss wall. In particular its lower bound is at least 1/8 for every N>=3. Level two is excluded: its chord passes through zero. Let \(\Xi=d\log F\wedge d\log v\) on the resolved target. Its exact pullback is \[ \Xi_N=-\frac{N\alpha_N}{1+\alpha_NT}\Omega . \] The marked chord logarithm satisfies \(\Log(Q_N^{-1})=-c/N\). Hence \[ \int_{\Gamma_N}\Xi =cN\Log(Q_N^{-1})=-c^2=4\pi^2 . \tag{1} \] This is the same integer wall flux as the old physical cycle. The explicit continuation is \[ \widetilde T_N(T)=-\frac N c\Log(1+\alpha_NT). \] It has \(\widetilde T_N(0)=0\), \(\widetilde T_N(1)=1\) on that marked sheet. The finite graph is the physical graph evaluated at \((v,\widetilde a_N=\widetilde T_N/v)\). Its derivative is the nonzero unit \[ \widetilde T_N'=-\frac{N\alpha_N}{c(1+\alpha_NT)} =1+O(1/N) \] near the real compact cycle. Moreover \[ \Phi_N^*\Omega-\Omega =d[(T-\widetilde T_N)d\log v]. \tag{2} \] The primitive extends at both pole fibers: its coefficient vanishes at T=0 and T=1. Thus (2) is a genuine source-form homotopy near the compact cycle, not a dropped endpoint. For a nonconstant word kernel its pullback must also transport that kernel; multiplying the old kernel by the area multiplier alone is not the same operation. ## 2. An algebraic map to the original two-frame torsor is impossible The ORIGINAL internal two-frame form is \[ \Omega_{\rm cut}=d\tau\wedge d\log A,\qquad A=(1+s)^{-1},\quad\tau=r/s . \] Fix \(A=A_N(T)\) as above, or the physical limit \(A=e^{cT}\). Suppose a nonzero form comparison with the compact source is required, with multiplier depending only on T: \[ d\tau\wedge d\log A=\kappa(T)\Omega,\qquad\kappa\ne0 . \] Writing \(d\log A=g(T)dT\), with \(g\ne0\), forces \[ \partial_v\tau=\frac{\kappa(T)}{g(T)v}. \tag{3} \] Thus \(\tau=(\kappa/g)\Log v+\tau_0(T)\) locally. No single-valued rational or finite-algebraic tau can satisfy (3). Fix generic T and pass to a place above v=0 on a finite algebraic cover. The differential of a meromorphic function has zero residue; the pullback of a nonzero multiple of \(dv/v\) has nonzero residue, multiplied by the ramification index. This proves the obstruction. On the MARKED LOG cover, one may instead take \[ \tau=\Log v/c . \] Then the exact finite graph gives \[ d\tau\wedge d\log A_N=\widetilde T_N'\Omega . \] At the physical limit the multiplier is one. The deck transformation \(\Log v\mapsto\Log v+c\) gives \(\tau\mapsto\tau+1\): it is precisely a relative centralizer endpoint, not an algebraic finite-cover identification. Changing tau by a function of A does not change this two-form; its poles and branch endpoints remain part of the source. This identifies the additional torsor needed for the current map: a logarithmic centralizer with its marked translation and pole clutches, rather than a single-valued coordinate on a split B1 chart. ## 3. The actual Cartan current has two different geometric images The actual Frobenius Cartan commutator current is \[ X_h=2v\partial_v-2a\partial_a =2\partial_{\log v}\ \text{at fixed T}. \] Its Hamiltonian is \(H=1-2T\), with \(\iota_{X_h}\Omega=-dH=2dT\). Under the logarithmic centralizer map of Section 2, \[ X_h\longmapsto(2/c)\partial_\tau . \] This is a concrete vertical-current match on the marked cover. By contrast, under the old PHYSICAL SPRINGER map \(v=1/p\), \(T=\Log A/c\), the SAME current changes the COMMON DIAGONAL MOMENTUM p and leaves A fixed. That old map forgets the original internal centralizer coordinate r. It is therefore not the above identification of the vertical two-frame current. Restoring momentum and retaining the centralizer as a separate logarithmic coordinate is essential. There is an exact finite quantum distinction as well: \[ \sigma(\Log Q_N^{-R})=-cT,\qquad \Log\sigma(Q_N^{-R})=-c\widetilde T_N . \] Their equality holds only at leading N-order. Passing from the linear actual Cartan moment to a logarithm of the clock symbol requires the corresponding star/current correction, not ordinary pointwise functional calculus. Equations (1)--(3) do not erase it. ## 4. The root gauge cost depends on the metric The controlled source gauge \(G=\sum_RP_R\otimes V^R\) is a unitary permutation in its constant coordinate basis. This correctly gives the root same-color source comparison and does not change any exact period when all operators, sources, duals and projectors are transported. In the compact head's binomial coherent metric the conclusion is different. Put \(n=N-1\) and use \(g_s=1/\binom ns\); the dual binomial convention gives the same condition-number conclusion. For any diagonal metric on the Frobenius factor, its weight cancels because G fixes R. Choose a central head s and a block R sending it to head zero. Then \[ \|G\|\ge\sqrt{\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}} . \] The inverse has the same lower bound, by reversing that cycle. Consequently \[ \operatorname{cond}_{\rm coherent}(G) \ge\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor} \ge\frac{2^n}{n+1}. \tag{4} \] Thus its standard-metric polynomial cost cannot be imported into a coherent-metric leading-norm estimate. This does NOT affect exact gauge invariance or the exact root equality with K_N. A whole normalized source unit and near-identity matrix germ are likewise sufficient for exact same-color identities, but do not give a uniform estimate on a growing normal neighborhood. Any leading geometric norm argument must retain its actual metric/source adapter. The current-map problem has therefore acquired explicit logarithmic, star, and metric data; none is supplied by an abstract identification of the two SL2 actions. ## 5. The selected diagonal coupon nevertheless has a tame coherent norm There is a stronger positive statement for the ACTUAL selected line. It does not require bounding G on the whole module. Use the root TENSOR coherent metric \[ g_{R,S}=\frac{\binom NR}{\binom{N-1}S}. \] The Frobenius numerator is fixed by the actual divided action: \(F^\dagger=E\) implies \((R+1)g_{R+1}=(N-R)g_R\), hence \(g_R=\binom NR\). The head denominator is the existing compact kernel metric. This is not the binomial metric of one ordinary color of dimension \(N(N+1)\). On the selected vectors \(z_k=w_{k,k}\), \(0\le k<N\), and \(z_N=w_{N,0}\), the actual source and co-source are \[ \psi_D=\sum_{k=0}^Nz_k,\qquad \lambda_D(z_k)=2^{-N}\binom Nk . \] Their pairing is one. Directly, \[ \|\psi_D\|^2 =\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\frac{\binom Nk}{\binom{N-1}k}+1 =N\sum_{j=1}^N\frac1j+1, \] \[ \|\lambda_D\|^2 =4^{-N} \left[\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \binom Nk\binom{N-1}k+1\right] =\frac{\binom{2N-1}{N-1}+1}{4^N}. \tag{5} \] The second equality is Vandermonde. Since \(\binom{2N}{N}/4^N\le1/\sqrt{N+1}\), proved by comparing successive ratios, and the harmonic sum is at most \(1+\log N\), the selected rank-one coupon satisfies \[ \|e_D\|=\|\psi_D\|\,\|\lambda_D\| =O(N^{1/4}\sqrt{1+\log N}). \tag{6} \] The same bound holds for its trace-functional norm. The source orientation is important. Under the Frobenius BINOMIAL COORDINATE change \(D_{\rm Fr}=\operatorname{diag}\binom Nk\), source coefficients become \(\binom Nk\), dual coefficients become \(2^{-N}\), and the Frobenius metric becomes \(1/\binom Nk\). These transform together and reproduce exactly (5); mixing the old source with the new metric would give a false exponential factor. Thus the controlled shear is exponentially conditioned on the full product space, while its selected coupled coupon is polynomially bounded in that SAME coherent metric. This is a useful period-line bound, stronger than a standard coordinate-norm observation. It still does not control the whole crossing norm, a growing normal neighborhood, a big-color coherent metric, or the selected coefficient after the unknown Gaussian/source comparison. The tame bound (6) is for the SELECTED anchor, not uniformly for its entire coherent orbit in this ambient product metric. Indeed put \(t=u=x\), \(0<x<1\). Then \[ \psi_D(x)=\sum_kx^kz_k,\qquad \lambda_D(x)(z_k)=\binom Nk \frac{x^k}{(1+x^2)^N}. \] Its source norm is at least one. On \(k\le N/2\), the dual norm numerator satisfies \[ \sum_k\binom Nk\binom{N-1}k x^{2k}+x^{2N} \ge\frac12\sum_{k\le N/2}\binom Nk^2x^{2k} \ge\frac{(1+x)^{2N}}{8(N+1)}. \] For the last step, pairing k with N-k shows that the lower half of \(\sum_k\binom Nkx^k\) is at least half its total; then apply Cauchy--Schwarz to that half. Consequently \[ \|e_D(x,x)\| \ge\frac1{\sqrt{8(N+1)}} \left(\frac{1+x}{1+x^2}\right)^N . \] At the actual real coherent point \(x=1/2\) the ratio is 6/5. Thus the whole real orbit can have an exponential ambient condition number despite the tame selected anchor. The intrinsic Fr coherent metric transported by G would instead make this orbit orthogonal; its comparison with the ambient product metric is precisely the large adapter that cannot be discarded. ## 6. The actual polarization changes the physical clock Let \(A_{\rm old}=Q^S\) be the original head clock and V the unit cyclic head shift. The actual source gauge is \(H_0=G(I\otimes\mathcal F)\), with \(\mathcal F_{s,t}=Q^{st}/N\). Direct finite Fourier calculation gives \[ H_0A_{\rm old}H_0^{-1}=V^{-1},\qquad H_0V_{\rm old}H_0^{-1}=Q^{-R}Q^S. \tag{7} \] Thus the OLD physical clock is a NEW SHIFT. The new constraint \(Q^S=Q^R\) concerns the new POSITION coordinate. The finite clock graph in Section 1 is an actual new-position source graph, but (7) prevents identifying it with the old cut observable without its polarization/source adapter. This has an exact all-level source test. The diagonal projector P selects \(z_j=(j,j)\) and \(z_N=(N,0)\). Since V changes S while fixing R, \[ PV^{-1}P=0. \] Hence every Frobenius coherent source supported on P has zero expectation of the transformed OLD clock V^{-1}. Its expectation of the NEW diagonal clock \(Q^R=Q^S|_P\) is instead the nonconstant binomial function of T. These actual moments are different at root order, even though the unweighted closed knot matrix is scalar. The root generating kernel is \(N^{-1}Q^{s_{\rm old}(s_{\rm new}-R)}\). On marked logarithmic coordinates its canonical phase is \[ W=q_{\rm old}(q_{\rm new}-q_R). \] With the usual stationary transform convention, \[ p'_{\rm head}=q_{\rm old},\quad p_{\rm old}=q_R-q_{\rm new},\quad p'_R=p_R-q_{\rm old}. \tag{8} \] For the source \(\psi(t)\), the coupled conormal relation is \(p'_R+p'_{\rm head}=\Log t\). This is a Fourier/Legendre polarization change, not the equality of the two position clocks. Its whole q-germ is still the supplied finite matrix gauge; a root generating phase alone does not specify all its q-jets. There is a useful exact NEUTRAL CURRENT formed from the charged physical clock. In the new factor coordinates, \[ \widetilde E=(e_{\rm Fr}\otimes I)V^{-1},\qquad \widetilde F=(f_{\rm Fr}\otimes I)V . \] These are precisely the actual endpoint-completed ladders built from divided powers and the first-normal wrap arrows. They commute with P and have the nonzero Fr coherent Hamiltonians. Bare \(V^{-1}\) does not preserve P; dressing it by the divided generator compensates its charge. Thus the old clock can enter the coupled current complex as a charged correspondence whose neutral dressed version is observable. This is an actual finite-source identity, not yet the full geometric current map. The whole lift of the original position clock matters too. For \(C_Q=Q^SZ^R=Q^J\), \[ [e(q),C_Q]/\delta\longrightarrow-A_{\rm head}e_0,\qquad [f(q),C_Q]/\delta\longrightarrow A_{\rm head}f_0 . \] In contrast the reduced head clock \(Q^S\) commutes with these divided operators for every q. The scaled commutator is therefore a statement about the specified NORMAL LIFT, not its root value. It is not a regular derivation on the whole Fr algebra: \([e,f]\) already has nonzero root value. All source, charged neighbor, and endpoint components must remain in that comparison. The subsequent [unprojectivized actual source theorem](actual_unprojectivized_frobenius_borel_torsor.md) retains the missing scale rather than forcing a constant-generator identification through the normalized quadric. On its marked paired source cover, two actual Borel fields map to the internal framing fields, and the actual scale U plus one descendant m give Omega_cut=(A/N)dlog U wedge dm. The old-clock normal pairing above detects U. This repairs that source/framing moment problem; it does not turn the two root clock observables into the same operator or construct the remaining whole network/Gaussian current map. ## 7. The selected coupled source is orthogonal in a hybrid metric The metric in Section 5 is the tensor product of TWO classical coherent metrics. There is another useful, explicit metric on the same actual source: keep the Fr coherent metric and the original flat head metric, \[ g_{R,S}=\binom NR . \tag{9} \] This is a different norm statement; it does not alter any of the conditioning results in the earlier metric. At the marked root, G sends (R,S) to (R,S+R mod N). It preserves (9) exactly. The actual Fourier matrix F_(S,T)=Q_N^(ST)/N has F^*F=I/N, so H_0=G(I tensor F) is a scalar N^(-1/2) times a unitary map in (9). Its condition number is ONE. Conjugation by H_0 is isometric on both the operator and Hilbert--Schmidt norms. These statements concern the ORIGINAL finite Fourier adapter, including its 1/N; it has not been replaced by a different source. The original source coupon e_+ tensor e_h is an orthogonal rank-one projector in this metric. Its transported coupled coupon is likewise orthogonal. Explicitly, with s(R)=R mod N, \[ \psi_D=\sum_{R=0}^N v_R\otimes e_{s(R)},\qquad \lambda_D(v_R\otimes e_S)=2^{-N}\binom NR\delta_{S,s(R)}. \] Thus \[ \|\psi_D\|^2=2^N,\qquad \|\lambda_D\|_*^2=2^{-N},\qquad\|e_D\|=1. \tag{10} \] In particular |Phi_D(T)|<=||T|| for every actual inserted matrix in this specified metric. This does not estimate the norm of the full crossing word or its geometric block. The head factorial gauge in degree elevation is not automatically isometric in (9). No bound on its full whole-q source transport is inferred. The highest-spin Fr projection is orthogonal for the induced Hilbert--Schmidt norm. Consequently it remains a contraction after conjugation by H_0. On b fixed strands, a projected inserted matrix has source pairing bounded by its Hilbert--Schmidt norm, hence by the square root of the ambient dimension times its operator norm. This costs a power of N, while the operator's own size remains to be proved. It is a selected-source estimate at the root, not a uniform estimate on the full Borel orbit or a moving-q neighborhood. ## 8. A normalized highest-spin clock residue and the source character There is a direct normalization check for the boundary polynomial in [the highest-spin quotient](degree_elevation_complement_bockstein_wall.md). On the Fr leg put \[ B_0=\operatorname{diag}_{R=0}^N((-1)^R\binom NR),\qquad U_z=\operatorname{diag}(z^R). \] B_0 is the weight-zero vector in the highest adjoint spin N: the adjoint Casimir has eigenvalue 2N(N+1). Its squared Hilbert--Schmidt norm is binom(2N,N). Since U_z has weight zero, its entire highest-spin component is EXACTLY \[ P_{W_N}(U_z)=\frac{(1-z)^N}{\binom{2N}N}B_0. \tag{11} \] The unnormalized obstruction polynomial is (1-z)^N u^N. Formula (11) retains the conversion to the actual coherent operator norm. For |z|=1 it gives \[ \|P_{W_N}(U_z)\|_{HS} =\frac{|1-z|^N}{\sqrt{\binom{2N}N}} \le\sqrt{2N+1}. \tag{12} \] The last bound follows from binom(2N,N)>=4^N/(2N+1). An unnormalized factor 2^N in the obstruction polynomial is therefore not by itself an exponential operator-norm obstruction. The SOURCE comparison on the surviving endpoint is different. For the normalized endpoint W=f^N/N!=E_(N,0), \[ \Phi_{\rm Fr,uniform}(W)=\frac1{N+1},\qquad \lambda_+ W\psi_+=2^{-N},\qquad \Phi_D(W\otimes H)=2^{-N}H_{00}. \tag{13} \] In the actual paired Borel family the last coefficient is ((1-m)/2)^N H_00. Its integral over dm/2 from -1 to 1 is H_00/(N+1), whereas its selected value at m=0 is 2^(-N)H_00. The exact ratio 2^N/(N+1) must remain in a source comparison. At the root W is closed for the MEMORY Cartan/F complex, so these two rows cannot differ by a Ward coboundary on the full target. The previously proved head-cut homotopy applies on the degree-elevation IMAGE; it does not justify replacing this extra endpoint row. The actual physical clock still has the distinct polarization dictionary in Section 6. Indeed even in (9) the uniform Fr coupon has squared norm \[ \|\psi_+\lambda_{\rm uniform}\|^2 =\frac{2^N}{(N+1)^2}\sum_{R=0}^N\binom NR^{-1} \ge\frac{2^{N+1}}{(N+1)^2}. \tag{14} \] This does not prevent cancellations in its interval period. It prevents treating its replacement of the selected coherent row as a tame source gauge without the full character/period calculation. The tame Fourier/controlled change (9)--(10) and the distinct interval-source character (13)--(14) are separate exact statements. [The exact matrix and source audit](../experiments/audit_highest_spin_cutoff_and_hybrid_metric.py) checks the coherent highest-spin normalization, actual coupled source/Fourier metric, endpoint character and the PBW pole cutoff.

title: The untruncated Verma period and its exact Alexander factor
text: # The untruncated Verma period and its exact Alexander factor Research note, 26 October 2026. This constructs a single graded Verma cut series and proves its exact rational specialization at every root q_N=exp(pi*i/N), including even and composite levels. Its root period is the actual reduced ADO state divided by the full Alexander factor Delta_K(M^(2N)). This root normalization already occurs in Willetts; Section 9 records the statement coverage. The proof here is an independent crossing, filtration and polynomial-trace calculation. It does not assume a completion theorem or identify the generic graded series with a completed literature invariant. The root state has exactly the original all-level quantum A-ideal and the original Kashaev specialization. The construction also turns the [reducible period anchors](closed_braid_period_line.md) into explicit polar data. It does not yet identify this period with the marked Bloch regulator or prove the volume conjecture. ## 1. A graded cut series with no root-dependent truncation Put Q=q^2 and x=q^alpha. On the infinite highest-weight Verma basis v_a, a>=0, use K v_a=xQ^(-a)v_a, E v_a=[a]_q[alpha-a+1]_q v_(a-1), F v_a=v_(a+1). For a fixed input vector the universal crossing sum is finite. After removing its common Cartan factor, cancel the divided-factorial denominators before specializing. In terms of the polynomial Gaussian coefficient {a choose n}_Q the positive checked entry is R^+_(b+n,a-n; a,b) =x^(-a-b+n)Q^((a-n)b){a choose n}_Q (x^(-2)Q^(a-n);Q)_n, 0<=n<=a. (1.1) The negative checked entry is R^-_(b-n,a+n; a,b) =x^(a+b-n)Q^(-ab){b choose n}_Q (x^2 Q^(1-b);Q)_n, 0<=n<=b. (1.2) To derive (1.1), write the product of the n E coefficients as [a]_q!/[a-n]_q! times the color product, use {a choose n}_q=q^(-n(a-n)){a choose n}_Q, and combine the Cartan exponent. For (1.2) apply the inverse Cartan first and reverse the color-product factors; the signs and quadratic powers cancel. Thus every displayed coefficient is Laurent polynomial in q,x. There is no [N]_q denominator left to interpret. At generic q these are the mutually inverse checked Verma crossings. Their identities follow from the formal R coefficient recurrence already derived in the [local braiding note](regular_holonomy_braiding.md). Each homogeneous total-index sector is finite, and its entries are Laurent polynomials. Those identities therefore specialize at roots by polynomial identity. Terms with n>=N are included; they need not vanish after the cancellation in (1.1)--(1.2). Let beta be a b-strand braid of writhe w whose closure is K, and put c=b-1-w. Let B_beta be the product of these checked crossings and inverses. Define the auxiliary graded series V_beta(q,x;tau)=x^c sum_(a_2,...,a_b>=0) tau^(a_2+...+a_b)Q^(-a_2-...-a_b) <0,a_2,...,a_b|B_beta|0,a_2,...,a_b>. (1.3) The factor x^c combines the ordinary pivot K on the closed strands and the residual twist x. Every coefficient of tau is a finite sum: crossings preserve total index, so all intermediate indices are bounded by that coefficient's total degree. Consequently (1.3) is defined in Z[q^(+/-1),x^(+/-1)][[tau]]. This assertion does not require convergence or a value at tau=1 for generic q. The graded auxiliary series is not asserted to be a knot invariant. ## 2. Exact Frobenius block decomposition Now q=q_N, Q of order N, and k=x^N. Write a=NA+r, b=NB+s, n=NC+t, 0<=r,s,t<N. The root Gaussian identity is {NA+r choose NC+t}_Q={A choose C}{r choose t}_Q. (2.1) For an elementary proof, expand product_(j=0)^(a-1)(1+Q^j z) by Gaussian coefficients and factor each full N-cycle as 1-(-z)^N. Comparing coefficients proves (2.1), with the cycle signs canceled by the Gaussian prefactor. No primality assumption on N enters. Also (hQ^j;Q)_(NC+t)=(1-h^N)^C(hQ^j;Q)_t. (2.2) Substitution in (1.1) gives its residue entry at (r,s,t) times {A choose C}k^(-A-B+C)(1-k^(-2))^C. (2.3) Substitution in (1.2) gives its residue entry times {B choose C}k^(A+B-C)(1-k^2)^C. (2.4) The positive output block indices are (B+C,A-C), apart from a possible carry when s+t>=N. The negative ones are (B-C,A+C), apart from a carry when r+t>=N. A carry lowers the sum of the residue indices by exactly N. Nonzero entries have t<=r in the positive case and t<=s in the negative case. Thus neither sign can increase total residue degree. Identify the block indices (A_1,...,A_b) with monomials in Z_1,...,Z_b. The carry-free block actions (2.3)--(2.4) are the symmetric-power actions of the mutually inverse matrices L_+(k)=[[1-k^(-2),k^(-1)],[k^(-1),0]], L_-(k)=[[0,k],[k,1-k^2]]. (2.5) On the associated graded for total residue degree, the entire Verma crossing therefore factors as actual finite checked R_N^sign tensor Sym L_sign(k). (2.6) The finite residue part is exactly the actual truncated ADO crossing: a carry is precisely the term removed by its nilpotent F endpoint. This proves the comparison rather than replacing the finite R by an unverified cyclic one. Every closed diagonal term in (1.3) returns to its initial residue degree. Since all carries strictly lower that degree, none can occur on a contributing path. Hence (2.6) computes the full graded cut trace exactly, not only its leading term. ## 3. Polynomial blocks give a rational period Let L_beta(k) be the product of (2.5) embedded in b dimensions, in the same operator order as B_beta. Delete its first row and column and call the resulting matrix A_beta(k). Define D_beta(k;z)=det(I-z A_beta(k)). The first block index is cut at zero. Projecting the first output block to zero amounts to setting Z_1=0. The remaining polynomial trace is therefore the trace on Sym of A_beta, and sum_(d>=0) z^d Tr(Sym^d A_beta)=1/D_beta(k;z). (3.1) For a proof, verify the identity on diagonal matrices by multiplying geometric series. For each coefficient both sides are polynomials in the matrix entries; diagonalizable matrices are Zariski dense. The coefficient identities follow for all matrices, including nondiagonalizable ones. The identities have integer coefficients, so they also support the exact finite-field diagnostics. Let P_(N,beta)(x;tau) be the finite residue cut polynomial: sum over 0<=r_2,...,r_b<N with the same factors x^c Q^(-sum r_i) and tau^(sum r_i) as in (1.3). Combining (2.6) and (3.1) proves V_beta(q_N,x;tau) =P_(N,beta)(x;tau)/D_beta(x^N;tau^N). (3.2) This is an identity of formal tau series and hence an explicit rational continuation in tau. The denominator, including its polar divisor, is retained. Equation (3.2) also specifies its actual relative algebraic equation D_beta V_beta=P_(N,beta). Its shift/grade variable is internal; this is not yet the desired affine meridian q-difference source equation. ## 4. The entire normalized denominator is Alexander The classical matrices (2.5) have a common right and left fixed vector v(k)=(1,k^(-1),...,k^(1-b))^t. Conjugating by diag(1,k,...,k^(b-1)) gives the usual Hurwitz/Fox blocks [[1-k^(-2),k^(-2)],[1,0]] and their inverses. The deleted minor of I-L_beta thus presents the ordinary Alexander module, by the infinite-cyclic-cover argument in the [closed-braid note](closed_braid_period_line.md). It is an Alexander polynomial up to a Laurent unit. The exact unit is fixed here. Put D_beta(k)=D_beta(k;1). Then Delta_K(k^2)=k^(-c)D_beta(k), c=b-1-w. (4.1) Here Delta_K is the symmetric normalization with Delta_K(1)=1. The following direct checks fix all units in (4.1). First, c is even for a knot. The sign change k->-k conjugates every block by diag(1,-1,1,...), so k^(-c)D_beta is Laurent in k^2. At k=1 the matrix L_beta is the one-cycle strand permutation; its deleted I-L cofactor is one. At k=-1 it is diagonally conjugate to the same permutation, with the same cofactor. For reciprocity introduce the upper triangular matrix H(k) with diagonal one and H_ij=(1-k^2)k^(i-j) for i<j. Multiplication of a single 2-by-2 block proves L_i(k^(-1))^t H(k)L_i(k)=H(k). It follows for every word. Over C(k), I-L_beta has rank b-1, because its deleted cofactor is nonzero at k=1. Thus its adjugate is D_beta(k)v(k)v(k)^t. Use H(k)v(k)=k^(-2(b-1))v(k^(-1)), v(k^(-1))^t H(k)=v(k)^t, det L_beta=(-1)^w k^(-2w). The adjugate of I-L_beta^(-1), together with knot parity w=b-1 modulo two, gives D_beta(k^(-1))=k^(-2c)D_beta(k). Consequently the right side of (4.1) is reciprocal and takes value one at k=1. These properties uniquely fix the usual symmetric Alexander normalization. The same formula can be checked under braid moves without losing units. Conjugation preserves D_beta, since the common left/right vector v is fixed. A last-strand positive stabilization preserves D_beta; a negative one multiplies it by k^2, by a last-coordinate Schur complement. The corresponding c changes by zero and two. Thus (4.1) is unchanged in both cases. ## 5. Exact comparison with the prescribed ADO state At the root the ordinary pivot K and the actual ADO pivot satisfy g_ADO=K^(1-N)=k^(-1)K. The residual actual twist is x^(1-N)=x/k. For b strands and writhe w these give exactly P_(N,beta)(x;1)=k^c F_N(M), M=-q_N x. (5.1) Combining (3.2), (4.1) and (5.1) proves the root-period identity V_beta(q_N,x;1)=F_N(M)/Delta_K(M^(2N)). (5.2) The evaluation at tau=1 means the rational continuation (3.2). It is defined over C(x); particular Alexander roots may be poles. This is a direct all-knot, all-level comparison. The exponent c, the sign of q_N^N and the full function Delta_K are accounted for. At M=1, k=(-1)^(N-1), c is even, and Delta_K(1)=1. Therefore V_beta(q_N,q_N^(N-1);1)=F_N(1)=<K>_N (5.3) as a regular whole germ, including even levels. No asymptotic normalization is involved. Although the graded series (1.3) is diagram dependent, its rational root specialization (5.2) is a knot invariant with the prescribed meridian and framing. For the full ADO normalization multiply both sides by the entire known function d_N(M)=i^(N+3)M^(N-1)/(1+M^2+...+M^(2N-2)). The factor Delta_K(M^(2N)) does not replace this function. Both divisors and their whole specializations are retained. ## 6. The same actual quantum A-ideal and pointed fiber Let sigma(M)=q_N M. Since U=M^(2N) is fixed by sigma, Delta_K(U) is a central scalar for the root meridian difference action. Multiplication by this nonzero rational function therefore gives, for every specified meridian operator P, P F_N=0 iff P(F_N/Delta_K(U))=0. (6.1) Thus the two root families have exactly the same all-level annihilator ideal as defined for the actual ADO state. The assertion holds in the reduced normalization and, with d_N retained, in the full one. It does not assert equality with a colored-Jones recursion ideal or a classical A-curve. There is also exact compatibility with the marked ramified fiber. Reciprocity makes Delta_K(U) even in z=(U-1)/(U+1), and its constant term is one. Hence 1/Delta_K(U)=1+O(z^2). Multiplying by it leaves both coordinates (a_0,b_0) of the [ramified Weyl fiber](ramified_weyl_fibre.md) unchanged. In particular it preserves the normal Kashaev functional, not merely an unpointed root solution line. Away from U=1 its entire factor still matters. This supplies an explicit untruncated root-period realization of the same quantum-A problem. The existence of the formal series (1.3) and its root rational continuation does not yet identify a generic completion, a geometric classical factor of the minimal operator, or the regulator norm. ## 7. The reducible anchor is actual polar data On a local meridian cover choose U=M^(2N) near an Alexander root alpha and a branch M(U) through M_*. Equation (5.2) is an exact meromorphic period identity. If alpha is a simple root, Res_(U=alpha) V_beta dU =F_N(M_*)/Delta_K'(alpha). (7.1) The [upper triangular comparison](closed_braid_period_line.md) independently computes F_N(M_*) as the selected cut period of the exact nonabelian reducible family. Thus (7.1) matches that period with a specified residue of the untruncated trace. For a multiple root the same whole ratio gives all principal-part coefficients from the corresponding meridian jets. If the numerator vanishes the pole order can decrease; no nonvanishing claim is assumed. The Alexander divisor is therefore not only a classical necessary attachment locus: it is the actual pole divisor of this global root trace, with selected polar data fixed by the ADO state. An occurrence can cancel when the numerator vanishes. This construction retains such cancellations and does not evaluate the numerator and denominator separately at the divisor. ## 8. What this adds to the triangulation comparison The local relative factorial source and the classical Alexander deformation matrix now have a common global trace interpretation. Untruncated Verma crossings give the explicit period (1.3); the Frobenius polynomial blocks produce its full Alexander denominator, and (5.2) identifies its selected root value with the prescribed quantum-A period. This supplies actual global period data rather than choosing a scalar on a torsor to impose the desired answer. The remaining geometric theorem must transport this selected relative period to the ideal-triangulation gluing realization, including its poles, source and boundary pointing, and establish its marked Bloch-regulator norm. The geometric fundamental class and its classical action are already identified in the linked [triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md). Neither the algebraic polynomial trace (3.1) nor cancellation of the Alexander factor at U=1 controls that quantum norm. The target remains (4/N)log|F_N(1)| -> log||P_hyp||=2Vol(M)/pi. No such estimate, noncancellation theorem or selected-period identification with the Bloch regulator is proved here. The subsequent [pointed tetrahedral transport](verma_tetrahedral_transport.md) does establish a local part of the transport: exact four-factor Verma crossings, a scalar-one formal tetrahedral pentagon, and preservation of the rational root period under finite formal operator rewrites with the same external pointing. Complete compression to the original lattice is performed before root specialization. Individual compact products can be singular; their norm characters and poles remain in the relative data. Application to an arbitrary positive geometric triangulation and the regulator norm are additional work. ## 9. Coverage and independent verification [Willetts, 2003.09854v2, Introduction Result 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2003.09854v2) already states a completed invariant with root evaluation ADO divided by Delta_K(A^(2r)). That is the prior coverage of the normalization in (5.2). Its completion, comparison and recursion proofs are not premises here. We prove the root trace formula by the displayed Gaussian cancellation, residue filtration, symmetric-power trace and explicitly normalized Fox cofactor. Equality of the generic graded auxiliary series with Willetts's completed element is not claimed. The literature ADO definition remains the fixed state. [The audit](../experiments/audit_frobenius_verma_period.py) compares the full untruncated coefficients with the block factorization, tests both signs and full homogeneous-sector inverse matrices, and checks the finite crossing against the actual ADO matrices. Independent symbolic checks verify the Fox minor, duality, reciprocity, conjugation and stabilization units. Full graded Verma traces are computed by unbounded-index sparse propagation to a stated degree and compared with the rational formula using independently constructed finite ADO matrices. Polar samples are retained. See [the results](../experiments/frobenius_verma_period_results.json). These checks support the uniform proof and establish no volume asymptotic.
