The supplied complete point theta_* belongs to P. Let F(rho,theta)=Im W(rho+i theta). Directly from (1), F(rho,theta)=sum_j Im Li_2(exp(rho_j+i theta_j)) -rho^t beta(theta). (3) In particular F is separable in its radial variables, even though the affine angle constraints couple its angle variables. ## 2. A unique radial minimum constructs the contour globally For every theta in P, partial_(rho_j)F=-Arg(1-exp(rho_j+i theta_j))-beta_j, partial_(rho_j)^2 F =Im[z_j/(1-z_j)]>0. (4) As rho_j tends to -infinity the first derivative tends to -beta_j<0; at +infinity it tends to gamma_j>0. Hence F has a UNIQUE global radial minimum, with the explicit solution rho_L,j(theta)=log[sin beta_j(theta)/sin gamma_j(theta)], x_L(theta)=rho_L(theta)+i theta. (5) The equality follows from the ordinary sine rule: its positive shape has argument theta and Arg(1-z)=-beta. Existence and uniqueness also follow from (4), without assuming an optimizer or a contour intersection. On every compact angle subpolytope the radial objective is uniformly coercive. On this graph the OFF-CRITICAL identity is exactly F(rho_L(theta),theta) =sum_j [Im Li_2(z_j)-rho_L,j beta_j] =sum_j D(z_j) =V(theta). (6) Here D is Bloch--Wigner and V is the ordinary sum of ideal tetrahedron volumes. Thus the original discrepancy between off-critical dilogarithm action and volume disappears on this specified nonlinear contour. This is stronger than comparing only their critical values. Rivin strict concavity makes theta_* the unique global maximum of (6). Its value is the marked hyperbolic volume. The volume extends continuously to the compact closure of P, and every other point of that closure has strictly smaller volume. In particular its boundary has a strict uniform volume gap. The noncompact radial behavior of (5) at some faces is recorded; it has not been declared harmless for an arbitrary quantum amplitude. ## 3. The contour is an algebraic phase graph on a finite cover Set p_j=exp(2i theta_j), q_j=exp(2i gamma_j). Then (5) gives the WHOLE rational identity z_j=(1-p_j q_j)/(1-q_j), q_j=exp(2i kappa_j) product_k p_k^(-C_jk). (7) On the positive real phase locus, z_j/conjugate(z_j)=p_j, z_j''/conjugate(z_j'')=q_j, z_j''=1-1/z_j. Since C is rational, one fixed finite cover of the phase torus makes all the monomials in (7) ordinary Laurent monomials. For the actual integral logarithmic gluing marks kappa/pi is also rational, so its constants are roots of unity. The contour is therefore the positive real locus of a rational algebraic graph on that marked finite cover. It is not primarily a collection of asymptotic jets. Formula (7) retains the sign and winding marks through kappa and C. The graph also glues explicitly across the POSITIVE quad atlas. The cyclic rotation x'=y, y'=-x-y+i pi permutes the angles and acts on their squared phases by the monomial map p'=q, q'=(pq)^(-1). Substituting these into (7) gives z'=(1-p'q')/(1-q') =q(1-p)/(1-pq)=1-1/z. Thus these reference contours are the same positive angle-to-shape construction in different quad coordinates, not unrelated local saddles. This is a classical algebraic atlas identity; the corresponding EXACT finite quantum quad/source transformation is not inferred from it. ## 4. A positive Hessian structure controls its Jacobian and all Schur reductions Let H=W_xx and write H=K+iD, D=diag_j Im[z_j/(1-z_j)]>0, K=I-C+diag_j Re[z_j/(1-z_j)]=K^t. (8) This holds throughout the positive product of half-planes, not just on the contour or at its maximum. The real Hessian of F in radial/angle coordinates is Hess F=[[D,K],[K,-D]]. (9) Differentiating its radial minimum gives R:=d rho_L/d theta=-D^(-1)K, Hess V=-G, G=D+K D^(-1)K>0. (10) These formulas prove strict concavity directly in the selected angle coordinates. The complex contour Jacobian is J_L=R+iI=-D^(-1)conjugate(H), H J_L=-G. (11) It is invertible EVERYWHERE on P. Indeed H has positive imaginary part, so Hu=0 would imply u^*D u=0. Thus the contour is a totally real immersion with no vanishing holomorphic volume Jacobian. Its determinant and Gaussian half-density have continuous nonzero marks on the convex P. There is no local Maslov obstruction or a zero Jacobian to be overcome by a limit. This structure survives arbitrary successive Gaussian eliminations. If a complex symmetric matrix H has Im H>0, partition it as [[E,F],[F^t,G_0]]. The principal block E is invertible and its Schur complement S=G_0-F^t E^(-1)F obeys Im S>0. (12) For a vector v put w=(-E^(-1)Fv,v). Then v^*S v=w^*H w, whose imaginary part is w^*(Im H)w>0. This proves (12) without a diagonalization or a scalar-root argument. It is the all-rank version of the positive-half-plane phenomenon checked explicitly in the five-crossing reduction. Real full-rank linear restrictions also preserve the condition, since Im(L^t H L)=L^t(Im H)L>0. Conversely a same-dimensional REAL symplectic Gaussian change cannot repair an indefinite imaginary Hessian. If H'=(E+F H)(A+B H)^(-1) is its usual fractional action, the symplectic identities give Im H'=(A+B H)^(-*) (Im H)(A+B H)^(-1). Hermitian inertia is unchanged. This distinguishes a positive chart construction from an unproved Gaussian repair of the original indefinite flow chart. Controlled elimination or a nonlinear Euler/quad transform requires its own source map. ## 5. An exact radial homotopy with automatically lower boundary prisms Put rho_*=Re x_* at the complete point. Let Q be ANY compact convex angle polytope contained in P with theta_* in its interior. Compare the two ACTUAL chains Gamma_0(theta)=rho_*+i theta, Gamma_1(theta)=rho_L(theta)+i theta, theta in Q, Gamma_s(theta)=[(1-s)rho_*+s rho_L(theta)]+i theta. (13) The fixed-radii theorem makes F(rho_*,theta) strictly concave with its unique maximum V_* at theta_*. The Legendre chain has the same property by (6). Convexity in rho gives the WHOLE homotopy inequality F(Gamma_s(theta)) <=(1-s)F(rho_*,theta)+sV(theta)<=V_*. (14) Equality is possible only at theta_*. On the ENTIRE boundary prism [0,1] times boundary(Q), compactness yields F<=V_*-delta_Q, delta_Q>0. (15) Thus this contour deformation comes with a proof of its boundary gap; a boundary estimate is not appended as an unverified condition. Its whole image is compact for fixed Q, and stays in the original positive holomorphic chamber. For any holomorphic top form omega_N on that image, Stokes gives the EXACT period difference as the oriented boundary-prism period. In particular if its actual uniform finite-level form is omega_N=N^mu exp[NW/(2pi i)] (a_0(x)+O(1/N)) dx_1...dx_t, with its original base line retained, then (15) proves that the two selected periods differ by O(N^B exp[N(V_*-delta_Q)/(2pi)]). No coefficient is set to one by normalization. If a_0(x_*) is a unit, each chain has one selected oriented saddle (multiplicity one), with its nonzero ORIGINAL density, contour Jacobian and Gaussian determinant retained. The numerical coefficient is their specified product, not the number one. Nonvanishing follows directly from the unique maximum, (11), and the negative real Gaussian Hessian; its power is N^(mu-t/2). It is not an assumption that an unspecified thimble intersects a quantum source. The statement is for these explicit chains and their retained prism. Applying it to an original knot state requires an exact source-preserving positive-chart realization of that state. It does not assert that realization merely from classical gluing or from a nonzero local normal density. ## 6. Every nonzero integer alias has an explicit radial escape direction For an integer vector m, the logarithmic alias is W_m(x)=W(x)+2pi i m^t x, F_m=F+2pi m^t rho. For theta in P, (4) has the global range -beta_j<partial_(rho_j)F<gamma_j, beta_j,gamma_j in (0,pi). Consequently, whenever m_j!=0, sign(m_j) partial_(rho_j)F_m >=2pi|m_j|-pi>=pi|m_j|. (16) There is NO critical point of any nonzero alias anywhere in this marked positive chamber. Moreover the explicit flow rho_j(s)=rho_j(0)-s sign(m_j), m_j!=0, rho_j(s)=rho_j(0), m_j=0 obeys the uniform whole-function inequality dF_m/ds<=-pi ||m||_1. (17) For example start at constant rho_*. After a fixed displacement S>2||rho_*||_infinity one has F_m(S,theta)<=V_* -pi(S-2||rho_*||_infinity)||m||_1. (18) Thus all translated alias BULK chains have explicit exponential loss, uniformly even in the infinitely many alias labels. Only finitely many translation directions are used, but no claim that finitely many Stokes branches exhaust the problem is made. The decay in ||m|| controls the remaining labels. The exact radial homotopy also retains its boundary face periods. Unlike (15), those alias prisms need NOT automatically be below V_*: their initial phases include 2pi m^t rho_*. They cannot be erased because their interiors have no critical point. This construction therefore reduces positive-chamber alias competition to explicit face sources; it does not prove those face sources vanish or have smaller rate in every knot. The original finite-mode or finite-height quadrature remains the way to carry those sources into a genuine comparison. ### Topology separates positive peripheral aliases from degenerate edge walls For the actual one-cusped triangulation there is a further uniform restriction. It has t edges and t tetrahedra: compactifying its torus cusp to the ideal vertex gives Euler characteristic one, so 1-#edges+2t-t=1. Choose the rows as t-1 ACTUAL independent edge rows followed by the marked meridian, as in the supplied gluing input. An integer alias changes the imaginary equations to A theta+B gamma=Im c+2pi Bm. Undoing the fixed quad rotations, its edge totals are therefore 2pi(1+k_e), with integer k_e on those t-1 rows. For strictly positive tetrahedra every edge total is positive, so k_e>=0. But the sum over ALL edge angles is exactly 2pi t, and hence the omitted edge has total 2pi(1-sum k_e). Its positivity forces sum k_e<=0. Consequently EVERY k_e is zero. Thus any strictly positive alias cell has its ORIGINAL edge angle equations. If m!=0, invertibility of B makes its remaining meridian-angle shift a nonzero integer multiple of 2pi. Such cells are distinct fixed-meridian-angle slices of the SAME full Rivin angle polytope. Their closures omit the unique complete maximizer. Strict concavity and compactness therefore bound their volume maxima strictly below V_*. Only finitely many integer meridian windings are feasible because that angle polytope is compact, so the gap is uniform over all feasible nonzero POSITIVE peripheral aliases. This statement is not extended to all weak nonnegative alias loci. A nonzero edge alias can survive only on a degenerate wall, with at least one edge angle zero. Since all local angles are nonnegative there, every tetrahedron incident to that edge has a zero angle and zero volume. The remaining face source is lower dimensional, but its TOTAL period or volume is not bounded by the preceding argument. Its original quantum source terms must still be retained. In particular a bound for the positive interior modes does not prove a bound for every degenerate wall. The proposed universal extension to all weak wrong-edge loci is now **FALSE**, as proved by the [certified positive-geometric counterexample](positive_geometric_alias_volume_counterexample.md). Six legal positive 2-to-3 moves on the same 5_2 knot give a nine-tetrahedron positive complete triangulation. A rational weak alias angle assignment has volume 3.76403683049..., exceeding the complete hyperbolic volume 2.82812208833.... Its complete marked meridian angle is exactly zero, and its full marked defect is Bm for an explicitly retained integer m, with det B=-2. Thus this is not an artifact of dropping the peripheral equation or enlarging the integer alias lattice. Here the strictly positive wrong-edge locus is EMPTY. The weak locus is not the topological closure of a nonempty positive cell, so the preceding positive-peripheral-alias theorem is unchanged. No coefficient of the oversized weak locus in the original quantum source has been computed. The counterexample therefore refutes universal FACE VOLUME domination; it does not assert an oversized original quantum period. Source exclusion or exact Ward/sewing cancellation remains necessary wherever such a weak locus is encountered. Compact radial clipping alone does not give the false comparison between different integer-shifted potentials. An independent useful sufficient bound remains: if s_min is the minimum number of DISTINCT tetrahedra incident to an edge, every wrong-edge weak locus has volume at most (t-s_min)v_3. The [star-bound note](degenerate_alias_faces_and_repair_obstructions.md) proves this and supplies exact counterexamples to universal flat-only repair and to an automatic favorable sign of complete edge multipliers. ## 7. Tests against the actual source and the critical-path consequence The [original figure-eight counterchart](positive_quad_chart_and_actual_torus_signature.md) has an indefinite angular Hessian on a valid transverse slice. It does not satisfy (8). Choosing new radii in that original chart cannot make this theorem apply. A source-preserving change to the positive quad chart is still necessary. The [selected five-crossing proof](five_two_selected_volume_proof.md) also needed a bent outer source and bounded lower/vertical pieces. That source theorem is not a consequence of (16). It verified exactly the face and kernel terms that a critical-point-only argument would miss. The new general advance is the explicit algebraic Legendre chain (5)--(7), its nonvanishing Jacobian and Schur-closed positive Hessian, and the radial homotopy (13)--(15) with a proved boundary gap. The target contour on every supplied positive triangulation is no longer guessed. What remains for a broad original-knot theorem is its exact quantum source transport, with the alias face periods in Section 6 retained. No broad volume conjecture is claimed proved by this lemma. There is a simple exact check on the word "automatic" in the boundary claim. In the scalar positive potential C=0, kappa=2pi/3, the angle interval is 0<theta<pi/3, gamma=2pi/3, beta=pi/3-theta. Its positive critical point is theta_*=pi/6, rho_*=-log(3)/2 and V_*=2v_3/3. But at the arbitrary initial radius rho_0=0, the angle endpoint theta=pi/3 has F(0,pi/3)=Im Li_2(exp(pi i/3))=v_3>V_*. The equalities follow from the ordinary Lobachevsky duplication identity. Thus radial boundary prisms from an arbitrary starting source radius need not be lower, even though the whole positive volume problem is strictly concave. This is a test of the analytic positive Lagrangian data, not a claim that this one-tetrahedron data is an actual knot triangulation or a substituted quantum invariant. It proves why (13) specifies rho_* and why the missing original-source transport cannot be supplied by concavity alone. The underlying angle-volume and Legendre viewpoints have the coverage already recorded in [the Rivin/flow note](rivin_flow_and_quantum_source.md). No novelty is claimed for Legendre duality or for the positive symplectic Hessian. The explicit whole off-critical chain, its boundary-prism inequality, algebraic phase graph and alias escape are proved here from the displayed formulas, without adopting a published quantum-cycle comparison. [All-rank identity and scope audit](../experiments/audit_general_legendre_rivin_contour.py) and [saved results](../experiments/general_legendre_rivin_contour_results.json).

title: Long filling across a finite-order zero of the original source amplitude
text: # Long filling across a finite-order zero of the original source amplitude 30 October 2026. The general original-source filling theorem does not need its leading analytic amplitude to be a unit at the complete point. A NONZERO amplitude germ is sufficient away from its pulled-back analytic zero set. That exceptional set occupies density zero among large signed integer slope boxes. Suitable rational rays avoid it eventually; a coordinate monomial times a unit avoids it at EVERY independently sufficiently long slope tuple. This removes one source hypothesis. It does not construct the required whole-source gap or complex packet for an arbitrary plat, and it does not prove that an unknown original source has a nonzero amplitude germ. The source, its full normal terms and all peripheral factors remain the ones in the [general transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md). ## 1. The precise weaker packet hypothesis Fix a diagram and a chosen nonempty set of b filled circle ports. Keep the exact all-input full-twist identity, known nonzero outer factor chi_N, entire physical color-complement gap, and exponentially accurate finite corridor interpolation of the general transfer theorem. The finite packet C_N is holomorphic and even separately in all b coordinates on the SAME fixed complex neighborhood required there. Replace only its relative unit-amplitude assumption by C_N(x)=N^mu exp[N phi(x)] [a(x)+r_N(x)], sup |r_N| <= C/N, (1) uniformly holomorphically on that neighborhood. Here a is a nonzero holomorphic GERM, allowed to satisfy a(0)=0; phi is separately even, phi(0)=F0 real, phi''(0)=2pi i diag(tau_1,...,tau_b), Im tau_i>0. (2) The explicit original unit phase eta_N stays outside C_N, as before. An absolute holomorphic remainder in (1) is essential. A pointwise estimate on physical colors, or an estimate obtained by division by an amplitude that vanishes, does not supply this hypothesis. Separate evenness of a follows even if not assumed: the holomorphic functions N^(-mu) exp[-N phi] C_N are separately even and converge uniformly to a. The same is then true of r_N. Their fixed derivatives are uniformly bounded on smaller domains by Cauchy's formula. The upper Gaussian corridor estimate uses boundedness of a+r_N, not a lower bound for a, so it remains valid. If some auxiliary cusps are UNFILLED, first set their color variables to zero in the actual packet and action. The amplitude required here is the resulting restricted germ a_I(x_I)=a(x_I,0). A nonzero full germ need not have a nonzero restriction: a(x_1,x_2)=x_2^2 vanishes identically when only port 1 is filled. Such a restriction needs its own first nonzero asymptotic coefficient; it is not covered by (1). ## 2. The actual filling map and its source divisor Put epsilon_i=1/p_i for the fixed nonzero integer slopes. The minimal charge source saddle xi(epsilon) solves phi_i(xi)+pi i epsilon_i(xi_i-1)=0, 1<=i<=b. (3) The analytic implicit-function theorem gives a unique small solution, xi(0)=0, and DIRECT differentiation gives D xi(0)=diag(1/(2 tau_1),...,1/(2 tau_b)). (4) In particular xi is a local biholomorphism. The factor 2 in (4) comes from the original full-twist convention and must be retained. There is a stronger coordinatewise statement. Separate evenness writes phi_i(x)=x_i psi_i(x), where psi_i is analytic and psi_i(0)=2pi i tau_i. Equation (3) becomes xi_i=epsilon_i u_i(epsilon), u_i(epsilon)=pi i/[psi_i(xi(epsilon))+pi i epsilon_i], u_i(0)=1/(2 tau_i). (5) Every u_i is a unit on a sufficiently small common polydisk. Thus xi_i is nonzero whenever epsilon_i is nonzero, independently of the relative sizes and signs of the other coordinates. Define the pulled-back source germ f(epsilon)=a(xi(epsilon)), Z={epsilon: f(epsilon)=0}. (6) It is nonzero because xi is locally invertible. Therefore Z is a proper complex analytic zero set, with its multiplicities supplied by f. Multiplying a by a nowhere-zero analytic change of source trivialization leaves Z unchanged. This is the source divisor used here; it is not inferred from the classical A-polynomial. The map (3) involves the marked analytic action and logarithmic coordinates. Even if the exponentiated shape branch is algebraic, Z is NOT asserted to be Zariski closed in epsilon or in the slopes. ## 3. Full-source transfer off the divisor For every independently sufficiently long fixed signed tuple p with f(1/p)!=0, the full original invariant has the SAME action and N-power as the general transfer: K_N(p)=chi_N eta_N kappa^(-sum p_i) N^mu D(p) exp[N S_p] [1+O_p(N^-1)], (7) where S_p=phi(xi)+(pi i/2) sum_i (xi_i-1)^2/p_i. (8) The coefficient D(p) is nonzero. Its source-amplitude factor is exactly a(xi); no value a(0) is inserted in its place. Here is the required modification of the proof, rather than an application of a theorem whose unit hypothesis has failed. Use the same local Fourier critical map xi_F(z), action Psi(z), and determinant branches as in the general transfer. Analytic finite-window stationary phase applied to (1) gives the ABSOLUTE expansion F_N(z)=N^(mu+b/2) exp[N Psi(z)] [B(z)+O(N^-1)], B(z)=(2pi)^(b/2) a(xi_F(z)) / sqrt(det[-phi''(xi_F(z))]). (9) Both the remainder and its fixed derivatives are uniform on a smaller fixed complex neighborhood. The proof expands the bounded analytic amplitude a+r_N on the translated Gaussian contour, so it never divides by a or B. Thus (9) is valid also on their zero sets. Every global-color, finite-color-endpoint, noncentral Fourier and large-charge estimate in the transfer uses an UPPER bound for C_N and its controlled derivatives. Those estimates are unchanged by (1). The strict ordering of nonminimal charges depends on phi, not on a lower amplitude bound. For fixed p their exponential losses dominate all the bounded amplitude factors. At the second saddle use (9) in its absolute form. Put z_i*=(xi_i-1)/(2p_i), T_1(z)=Psi(z)-2pi i sum_i(p_i z_i^2+z_i). Then T_1(z*)=S_p and the leading coefficient is D(p)=Gamma(p) a(xi), Gamma(p)=2^b (2pi)^b product_i sinh(2pi i z_i*) / [sqrt(det[-phi''(xi)]) sqrt(det[-T_1''(z*)])]. (10) The determinants are nonzero on the chosen translated contours. Equation (5) and smallness imply z_i* is nonzero for each finite p_i; also |z_i*|<1/4, so its sinh factor is nonzero. Hence Gamma(p)!=0. At fixed p with a(xi)!=0, division by this now NONZERO leading coefficient turns the absolute O_p(N^-1) into the relative error in (7). Its constant may increase as p approaches Z. The 2^b minimal signed-charge sectors still ADD. Under a sign change of one charge, its saddle coordinate changes sign; the exact packet and its leading amplitude are separately even. The charge times sinh factor, determinant branch and exact parity character have the same transformation as in the original proof. This argument uses the exact source symmetry, not positivity of a. Consequently lim_N (2pi/N) log|K_N(p)|=2pi Re S_p. (11) If the SAME source branch has the actual marked representation, primitive peripheral equations and complete regulator anchor required by the general geometric completion theorem, the right side is the actual filled hyperbolic volume. Nothing in this amplitude extension supplies those independent certificates. Points in Z are excluded from this particular leading-coefficient argument. They are NOT counterexamples to a volume limit: a later Gaussian or source coefficient may give the same exponential rate. The diagram and slopes remain fixed BEFORE N tends to infinity; no joint large-N/large-slope uniformity is asserted. ## 4. Coordinate zeros permit every independently long slope Suppose on the chosen filled-coordinate chart a(x)=product_i x_i^(2 nu_i) v(x), nu_i>=0, v(0)!=0. (12) The even powers are consistent with the actual separate evenness. Combining (5) and (12) gives the exact germ factorization f(epsilon)=product_i epsilon_i^(2 nu_i) V(epsilon), V(0)!=0. (13) Thus EVERY independently sufficiently large signed nonzero tuple p avoids Z, and uniformly over those tuples, c product_i |p_i|^(-2 nu_i) <= |a(xi(1/p))| <= C product_i |p_i|^(-2 nu_i). (14) No slope-comparability condition enters. The conclusion is therefore as strong in its slope quantifier as the old unit-amplitude transfer. For ONE filled cusp every nonzero separately-even analytic germ automatically has the form (12), so the complete-point unit assumption can always be dropped in that one-variable case. For completeness the known filling prefactor also has a uniform magnitude comparison. Here z_i*=(-epsilon_i/2)(1+O(||epsilon||)) and diag(epsilon_i) T_1''(z*)=-4pi i I+O(||epsilon||). The other Hessian remains bounded and invertible. Formula (10) gives |Gamma(p)| comparable to product_i |p_i|^(-3/2), on each signed orthant, and hence on their finite union. Under (12), |D(p)| is comparable to product_i |p_i|^(-2 nu_i-3/2). This is a statement about the slope-dependent leading coefficient, not a uniform error estimate when slopes grow with quantum level N. ## 5. Rational-ray survival for a general nonzero amplitude Let d be the vanishing order of f at zero, including d=0 for a unit, and let P_d be its first nonzero homogeneous Taylor polynomial. For fixed nonzero signed integers q_1,...,q_b with P_d(1/q_1,...,1/q_b)!=0, (15) the ray p_i=n q_i satisfies f(1/(nq))=n^(-d)[P_d(1/q)+O_q(n^-1)]. (16) Every sufficiently large n therefore avoids Z, with magnitude comparable to n^(-d). Applying (7) separately at each fixed ray point gives its full quantum volume limit whenever the geometric certificates hold. The ray parameter n is not the quantum level N. There is such a rational ray in EVERY prescribed sign orthant. Indeed multiply P_d(1/q) by product_i q_i^d. The result is a nonzero polynomial in the q_i. A nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on the entire product of infinite one-sided integer sets: fix all but one variable, use the finite root count, and induct on the number of variables. This proves existence without assuming rational or algebraic coefficients for P_d. Condition (15) is sufficient, not necessary. A ray on which P_d vanishes may have a nonzero higher-order coefficient in f. ## 6. Density one in every large signed integer box Fix signs sigma_i. Among tuples p_i=sigma_i n_i, T<=n_i<=2T, n_i integers, the number lying in Z is o(T^b) as the integer scale T tends to infinity. Thus the proportion for which (7) applies tends to one. This does not assert that ALL tuples avoid Z or that its exact integer points lie in a fixed algebraic hypersurface. Here is an elementary counting proof. Put t_i=n_i/T in [1,2]. Uniform analytic Taylor remainder estimates on this compact set give T^d f(sigma_1/(Tt_1),...,sigma_b/(Tt_b)) =P_d(sigma_1/t_1,...,sigma_b/t_b)+O(T^-1). Therefore a bad tuple satisfies |Q(t)|<=C/T, where the NONZERO polynomial Q(t)=product_i t_i^d P_d(sigma_1/t_1,...,sigma_b/t_b) has no negative powers. Choose a nonzero real polynomial R from the real or imaginary part of Q. On [1,3]^b its first derivatives are bounded. To each bad grid point t attach the disjoint half-open cube product_i[t_i,t_i+1/T). Every point of that cube then satisfies |R|<=C'/T, with one fixed constant C'. Hence #bad/T^b <= volume{x in [1,3]^b: |R(x)|<=C'/T}. (17) A nonzero real polynomial has zero set of Lebesgue measure zero. For a direct proof, write it as a polynomial in its last variable. Except on the common zero set of its coefficients, contained in the zero set of one nonzero lower-dimensional coefficient, every fiber has finitely many roots. Induction and Fubini prove the claim. The sublevel sets on the right of (17) decrease to that zero set, so continuity of finite measure makes their volumes tend to zero. This proves the stated density without a quantitative sublevel or Diophantine theorem. The unit case d=0 is immediate as well. ## 7. Finite level classes and exact scope The argument also covers finitely many level classes, for example even and odd N, with the SAME phi and separate uniform expansions (1) having nonzero germs a_r. All original class-dependent unit phases are retained. Use the finite union of their divisors. Outside it each class has (7), possibly with its own nonzero coefficient; the exponential limit (11) holds along the full sequence. The union still has density zero in each signed slope box. A rational ray avoiding the product of the finitely many first nonzero Taylor polynomials avoids every divisor eventually. If each amplitude is a coordinate monomial times a unit, every independently long tuple works at all the level classes. For partial fillings these nonzero-germ checks must again be made AFTER restricting the unfilled variables. The advance is removal of the complete-point UNIT requirement, including arithmetic survival of many long fillings. A proven nonzero finite-order marked source amplitude can now be used even when its complete value vanishes. The exact mixed source, its global gap, its uniform complex packet and its actual geometric marking remain necessary. No arbitrary-plat equality, whole knot A-polynomial identification, or nonzero-source theorem is inferred from this lemma. Audit: [implicit saddle, coordinate zeros and integer-slope examples](../experiments/audit_general_long_filling_source_divisor.py). The density-one statement is proved by the analytic rescaling and measure argument above, not by the finite counts in that audit. Independent internal analytical review: the primary agent and a second reader checked the factor-two implicit saddle, absolute two-stage stationary expansion, unchanged full-source error budget, minimal charge addition, coordinate divisor, rational rays, density-one mesh argument and the partial-filling restriction. Both fresh audit replays passed. The source and geometric hypotheses remain conditional as stated; these reviews do not establish them for arbitrary plats.

title: Long filling with the actual finite-level critical action
text: # Long filling with the actual finite-level critical action 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed and frozen. The complete core theorem retains a holomorphic action S_N in its exponential. Its convergence to S does not justify replacing exp(N S_N) by exp(N S). The long-filling argument can retain S_N throughout. This removes that compatibility issue without assuming a new asymptotic expansion of S_N. The full mixed-source gap remains a separate hypothesis. ## 1. Precise hypotheses and conclusion Retain the original full-twist identity, endpoint and normal currents, and normalization chi_N of the [general filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md). Fix the diagram and its b filled ports. Suppose there are nonzero scalars c_N with (1/N) log|c_N| -> F0, and exact finite holomorphic packets C_N, separately even, on the SAME fixed complex color neighborhood used in that theorem. Assume C_N(x)=c_N exp[N phi_N(x)] [a_N(x)+r_N(x)], (1) phi_N(0)=0, phi_N -> phi holomorphically, sup|r_N|=O(1/N). Here phi_N and a_N are separately even and holomorphic. On a slightly smaller fixed neighborhood assume |a_N| is bounded above and below by positive constants, uniformly in N. Uniform bounds on still smaller domains give bounds on their fixed derivatives by Cauchy's formula. Assume phi''(0)=2pi i diag(tau_1,...,tau_b), Im tau_i>0. (2) The full physical-color complement and the error between the original mixed source and its retained unit phase times C_N obey the same exponential gap as in the original transfer, now measured relative to |c_N|. A gap measured relative to exp(N F0) also suffices after reducing its positive exponent, because log|c_N|=N F0+o(N). Then there is a diagram-dependent threshold T such that every FIXED signed integer tuple p with all |p_i|>T has K_N(p)=chi_N eta_N kappa^(-sum p_i) c_N D_N(p) exp[N S_(p,N)] [1+O_p(1/N)], (3) where the actual finite-level critical point xi_N is the small solution of partial_i phi_N(xi_N)+pi i (xi_N,i-1)/p_i=0, S_(p,N)=phi_N(xi_N)+(pi i/2)sum_i(xi_N,i-1)^2/p_i. (4) For each such fixed p, |D_N(p)| is bounded above and bounded away from zero for all large N. No convergence of a_N or of D_N is required. The actions S_(p,N) converge to S_p defined by (4) with phi in place of phi_N. Consequently lim_N (2pi/N) log|K_N(p)|=2pi(F0+Re S_p). (5) The normalization chi_N is the original known nonzero factor with log|chi_N|=o(N), and eta_N and the displayed kappa factors are the retained unit phases. No unknown value of the filled invariant is used to choose a normalization. The diagram and p are fixed before N tends to infinity, and neither equal signs nor comparable slopes are required. All source scalars use the same convention as the original transfer: any common recorded exterior framing unit occurs once, either in c_N or in the displayed outer factors, as in that source's exact identity. ## 2. Uniform local estimates Holomorphic convergence on a fixed neighborhood implies uniform convergence of all fixed derivatives on a smaller one. Separate evenness makes every phi_N Hessian at zero diagonal. By (2), its negative real quadratic part on real color directions is uniformly positive for all large N. Taylor's formula therefore gives the same Gaussian corridor upper bound as in the original transfer, with constants independent of N: |C_N(x+i y)| <= C |c_N| exp[N(-a0 |x|^2+B0 |y|^2)]. (6) The holomorphic implicit-function construction is uniform as well. Define the actual finite-level Fourier critical map and action by grad phi_N(xi_F,N(z))+2pi i z=0, Psi_N(z)=phi_N(xi_F,N(z))+2pi i xi_F,N(z).z. They exist on one fixed polydisc and converge with fixed derivatives to their limiting counterparts. Psi_N is separately even, Psi_N(0)=0, and its quadratic coefficients converge to -i pi/tau_i. Use the EXACT finite packet C_N in the finite color sum. The contour argument in the original transfer uses its holomorphy, (6), and the fixed-width complement gap; these estimates are uniform here. Applying stationary phase directly to (1), including its holomorphic absolute remainder, gives F_N(z)=c_N N^(b/2) exp[N Psi_N(z)] [B_N(z)+O(1/N)], B_N(z)=(2pi)^(b/2) a_N(xi_F,N(z)) /sqrt(det[-phi_N''(xi_F,N(z))]). (7) All errors and fixed derivatives are uniform on a smaller fixed domain. The Gaussian square root is fixed by the translated original contour. Neither the grid error nor exp[N(phi_N-phi)] is Fourier transformed as an independent approximation. The action phi_N remains in (7). ## 3. Charges, noncancellation and the leading coefficient For each nonzero charge vector m put T_(m,N)(z)=Psi_N(z)-2pi i sum_i(p_i z_i^2+m_i z_i). The proof excluding zero charges is an exact identity of the original normal-current kernel and any even packet; it is unchanged. The finite color endpoints and large-charge tails use (6) and its fixed derivatives, so their exponential estimates are uniform in N too. When estimating one charge coordinate, spectator chirps stay on their original real grids or real contours, as in the original transfer. Thus there is no cost growing exponentially with another fixed slope. For the remaining local charges set e_i=1/p_i and t_i=m_i/p_i. Solve uniformly in N z_i=-t_i/2+e_i partial_i Psi_N(z)/(4pi i). Separate evenness and completing the square give T_(m,N)(z_(m,N))=(pi i/2)sum_i t_i^2/e_i +Bhat_N(t^2,e). At the limit (t,e)=(0,0), partial_(t_i^2) Re Bhat = -pi Im(tau_i)/(4|tau_i|^2)<0. Uniform derivative convergence preserves a fixed negative upper bound on one common neighborhood for every sufficiently large N. Integrating in the squared real t coordinates therefore gives the same strict action ordering between |m_i|=1 and every other local charge. All finite nonlocal charges and endpoint connectors obey the same uniform estimates as the original transfer. Shrink the inverse-slope polydisc once so the minimal-charge action is closer to zero than the global source gaps. At the minimal charge, xi_N and the second saddle are related exactly by z_(N,i)*=(xi_N,i-1)/(2p_i). The exponent is exactly S_(p,N) in (4), not its limiting value. Uniform implicit convergence gives xi_N -> xi and S_(p,N) -> S_p. Write partial_i phi_N(x)=x_i g_(i,N)(x). The stationarity equation gives xi_N,i=e_i pi i/[g_(i,N)(xi_N)+pi i e_i]. The denominators are uniformly nonzero near zero. Hence for fixed nonzero e_i all xi_N,i are nonzero; moreover |xi_N,i|<1/2 after shrinking the common polydisc. In particular z_(N,i)* is nonzero and small. The two Gaussian integrations give the precise coefficient D_N(p)=2^b (2pi)^b a_N(xi_N) product_i sinh(2pi i z_(N,i)*) /[sqrt(det[-phi_N''(xi_N)]) sqrt(det[-T_(1,N)''(z_N*)])]. (8) Both determinants stay nonzero, with the branches of the original translated contours. For each fixed p the sinh factors have nonzero limits, and a_N is uniformly bounded away from zero. Formula (8) is therefore bounded above and away from zero. The 2^b minimal signed charges have identical action and coefficient: evenness applies at each N, while m_i sinh(2pi i z_i) and the actual parity character are unchanged by simultaneous sign reversal. They add exactly as before. This proves (3). Taking logarithms of absolute values divided by N proves (5). ## 4. Application to the established complete core For the [actual core packet](actual_complete_core_complex_packet.md), set c_N=F_N(0), phi_N(chi)=S_N(chi)-S_N(0), a_N(chi)=sqrt(det K_N(0)/det K_N(chi)). These satisfy (1)--(2) on a fixed smaller neighborhood. In fact the separate channel reflection makes S_N and det K_N separately even: flipping chi_i flips the corresponding critical delta_i, and conjugates the Hessian by that coordinate reflection. Its determinant is unchanged. The square root is the branch equal to one at zero. Thus a_N converges to a nonzero unit and its bounds required above hold. The complete-source theorem gives log|c_N|/N -> Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). The packet cusp parameter in (2) is pi i/(C_i-pi i epsilon_i), half the primitive geometric cusp parameter; the original filling kernel already retains that convention. The [actual marked regulator](actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.md) identifies F0+phi with the geometric action, with its recorded boundary correction and primitive peripheral logs. Under the STILL REQUIRED whole mixed-source complement and corridor-error gaps, the general geometric filling completion therefore identifies (5) with the actual filled hyperbolic volume for every independently long fixed signed p. This note closes the finite-action compatibility issue only. It neither proves those mixed-source gaps nor extends the complete-core theorem to filled knots by itself. No additional finite Taylor expansion of S_N, nor an exchange of a level limit with the filling transform, is used. Independent analytical review checked the exact saddle conversion, both Gaussian powers and the coefficient (8), uniform complex and charge estimates, finite-level evenness, noncancellation, and the actual core normalization and cusp factor. No new finite computation is claimed: this is a uniform extension of the stated conditional transfer proof, not a numerical test of its missing source hypotheses.

title: Positive marked gluing is unramified at every cusp simultaneously
text: # Positive marked gluing is unramified at every cusp simultaneously 30 October 2026. For an actual positive complete ideal triangulation with c torus cusps, the marked decorated geometric germ is smooth of dimension c. The small meridian similarity logarithms U_1,...,U_c are local coordinates. More generally one may prescribe the logarithm of ANY one nonzero primitive peripheral path on each cusp. In particular the mixed coordinates consisting of main meridians and auxiliary longitudes are unramified for an arbitrary marked augmented plat. This is the multi-cusp geometric statement needed by a future comparison with the full Casimir plat critical scheme. Its proof extends the repo's own edge-lattice and polarized-Jacobian arguments; no external rigidity proof is used. It supplies geometric rigidity, not that source comparison. ## 1. Hypotheses and provenance Supply an actual marked positive complete ideal gluing certificate in the sense of [the general certificate theorem](general_marked_positive_gluing_certificate.md). There are t positively oriented ideal tetrahedra, all faces are paired, there are no finite vertices, and the c ideal vertex links are tori. The quotient is the specified oriented manifold Y, with its actual primitive peripheral paths. For an augmented plat those paths include the original crossing-disk meridians and zero-self-linking longitudes, with every retained half twist fixed in the topology. Such a certificate is already constructed from each positive labeled right-angled polyhedron certificate in [the general matching-graph geometry](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md). The present theorem does NOT prove existence of a positive certificate for every abstract matching graph or every hyperbolic augmented diagram. Hyperbolicity alone should not be silently substituted for this input. The ingredients previously proved in the repo are: * The signed edge rows are isotropic and have rank E-V over Q: [pointed tetrahedron gluing](pointed_tetrahedron_gluing.md), sections 3--4. Its face-cancellation and vertex-sum proofs already cover arbitrary closed orientable vertex links, not just knots. * The normal-curve intersection formula is a sum of local cusp-triangle identities: [integral half-longitude](integral_half_longitude.md), section 2. That proof is componentwise. Its later KNOT-specific divisibility assertion is unnecessary here and is not used. * Positivity gives transversality to a full real isotropic system by polarization: [geometric rigidity](geometric_rigidity_and_cyclic_source.md), section 1. Its statement there was written for one cusp. The missing assembly is the all-cusp rank argument, the exact mixed peripheral coordinate statement, and the corresponding decorated representation germ with its Artin-ring marking retained. Those are proved below. No H2(Y)=0 shortcut is used. ## 2. The all-cusp marked Jacobian is invertible Use quad coordinates u_j=Log z_j, v_j=Log z'_j=-Log(1-z_j), z'_j=1/(1-z_j), t_j=dv_j/du_j=z_j/(1-z_j). These are the first two ordered quad parameters in this proof. Since Im z_j>0, Im t_j=Im z_j/|1-z_j|^2>0. (1) This convention differs from using Log z'' as the second coordinate; that convention has negative imaginary derivative and proves the same transversality. One must transform the equation rows with the quad order. Let Omega be the direct sum of the standard alternating forms on the (u_j,v_j) planes. Write E for the real span of the edge equation rows. The torus-link Euler count gives E_global=t. The vertex-sum dependence proof then gives dim E=t-c, Omega(E,E)=0. (2) For completeness, a dependence among the edge rows requires the three opposite-pair sums in every tetrahedron to be equal. Over R this is exactly an assignment lambda_ab=s_a+s_b to its six edges. Three edge values on a face determine its three s-values uniquely, so the s-values descend to the c ideal vertices. The assignment from vertex values to edge values is injective because the three zero sums on a triangle force all its vertex values to vanish. Thus there are precisely c edge-row dependences. Isotropy is the cancellation of the four signed face forms under the actual orientation-reversing pairings. A normal peripheral path gives a row in E^perp, well defined modulo E. For two paths the pairing of these rows is, up to the fixed quad/cusp orientation sign, TWICE their oriented intersection number. The local normal-flow proof applies separately to every cusp, and paths on different cusps have zero intersection. Therefore the 2c rows of primitive peripheral bases are independent in E^perp/E. Its dimension is exactly 2c by (2), so they form a real basis of that quotient. Only this nondegeneracy is needed below; all actual holonomy signs are retained in the marked path equations themselves. Choose one nonzero primitive path gamma_i on each cusp. Its class is nonzero in that cusp's two-dimensional summand, and different chosen classes pair to zero. Thus E together with these c rows has rank t and is isotropic. Choose t-c independent edge equations and append the c actual gamma equations. Their real coefficient matrix is (A B), with rank(A B)=t, A B^t=B A^t. (3) The logarithmic shape Jacobian is J=A+B diag(t_j). (4) It is invertible. If Jx=0 then w=(x,diag(t_j)x) lies in the complexified kernel of (A B). The kernel of a full-rank isotropic t-row system is itself real Lagrangian, so Omega(w,conjugate(w))=0. But directly (i/2) Omega(w,conjugate(w)) =sum_j Im(t_j)|x_j|^2, which is strictly positive for x!=0 by (1). Hence x=0. All edge equations are affine logarithmic equations on this chart. Their dependent rows have compatible constants because the complete point satisfies them. Solving the selected t-c rows therefore solves all edge equations near that point. The holomorphic implicit-function theorem applied to (4) proves that the edge-gluing germ is smooth of dimension c and that the c prescribed peripheral logarithms are local coordinates. Exponentiating changes the Jacobian only by nonzero monomial factors. Thus the same algebraic germ is etale over its marked peripheral multipliers. ## 3. This is the actual decorated representation germ, also infinitesimally The geometric object includes a common fixed flag for each peripheral group. Keep its eigenvalue/similarity character, not merely the trace of an unmarked peripheral matrix. Normalize an ordered triple of developed ideal vertices. At the complete positive point all required tetrahedral vertex differences and face-triple determinants are nonzero. They remain units in a sufficiently small local chart and over every local Artin algebra with this residue point. Starting with shape coordinates, develop the first ordered tetrahedron. Across each face, its ordered triple determines a UNIQUE projective transformation and hence the next tetrahedron. Around a global edge the resulting transformation fixes its two distinct ideal endpoints. Its similarity multiplier is the actual edge shape product. The edge equation sets that multiplier to one, so this transformation is projectively the identity. The face generators and these edge relations are the actual dual two-skeleton presentation of the ideal triangulation. They therefore construct a representation of pi1(Y). Each developed cusp vertex is fixed by its actual peripheral subgroup, and its marked similarities have precisely the path monomials used in section 2. Conversely, a nearby representation with those peripheral flags develops every ideal vertex equivariantly from its cusp flag. Cross-ratios of the four vertices give the shape coordinates. The face transformations coincide on three distinct flags, and the edge products telescope to one. Normalizing the same ordered triple makes these constructions inverse. Every step uses rational expressions with UNIT denominators. The two constructions therefore remain inverse over local Artin algebras, not only on complex points. This identifies the positive gluing germ with the actual decorated representation germ modulo simultaneous PGL2 conjugation. A specified SL2 lift and its central signs are retained on their local sign cover; they are not reset by the projective construction. There is an important infinitesimal distinction. For a fixed unipotent matrix M=[[1,1],[0,1]], a projectively invariant flag (1,e), with e^2=0, can move: M(1,e)=(1+e)(1,e) modulo e^2. Its eigenvalue changes. Thus an UNSPECIFIED invariant flag is not the same Artin datum as an eigenflag with exact eigenvalue one. If the eigenvalue is prescribed to be one, the first coordinate forces e=0. More generally a noncentral parabolic matrix with a unit off-diagonal entry has a rank-one nilpotent part, and its kernel is its unique free eigenline with the exact repeated eigenvalue. The log equations in section 2 retain this character and remove that ambiguity when the corresponding log is fixed. It follows in particular that the marked decorated geometric germ has no nonzero infinitesimal deformation at fixed values of ALL the chosen peripheral coordinates. This is a statement about this actual germ; it does not identify a different source gradient scheme with it. ## 4. The marked cusp derivative is exactly diagonal Now choose the actual meridians as the c coordinate paths, and denote their small PROJECTIVE similarity logs by U_i. Let V_i be the small log of the actual preferred longitude similarity. Send the selected peripheral flag to infinity using a bounded holomorphic frame. Write mu_i(z)=exp(U_i)z+m_i(U), lambda_i(z)=exp(V_i)z+l_i(U). At completeness m_i(0),l_i(0) are the two actual primitive translations; m_i(0)!=0 and tau_i=l_i(0)/m_i(0), Im tau_i>0 (5) for the positive oriented basis. Peripheral commutativity gives EXACTLY (exp(U_i)-1) l_i(U)=(exp(V_i)-1) m_i(U). (6) Since m_i remains a unit, U_i=0 implies V_i=0 on the centered log branch. Consequently V_i is analytically divisible by U_i. Differentiating (6) at completeness yields dV_i=tau_i dU_i, partial V_i/partial U_j=delta_ij tau_i. (7) This proves the zero cross-cusp first derivatives without an assumed potential, symmetry of a Hessian, or a source convention. It also proves that fixing a main meridian multiplier to one keeps that entire main peripheral group parabolic nearby, with its longitude multiplier one. The translation pair remains real-linearly independent near the complete point, so these main cusp ends remain complete. The logs here are PROJECTIVE similarity logs. Chosen SL2 eigenvalue logs are U_i/2,V_i/2 with their original central signs retained. Their ratio in (7) is still tau_i; no factor of two is introduced by changing both. ## 5. Relative rigidity for arbitrary marked augmented links Partition the cusps into s main cusps and r auxiliary crossing circles, with c=s+r. Impose the exact main conditions U_main=0. The resulting decorated geometric germ is smooth of dimension r, with U_aux as coordinates. Equation (6) gives V_main=0 identically. Equation (7), or directly the choice gamma=mu on main cusps and gamma=lambda on auxiliary cusps in section 2, shows that V_aux is ALSO a local coordinate system. Thus the mixed marked projection (U_main,V_aux) is unramified at the complete point. In particular the germ with all these values fixed has no nonzero infinitesimal deformation modulo simultaneous conjugation. This is the precise geometric rigidity needed for channels recording selected auxiliary longitude eigenvalues. Every retained half-twist partner is treated with its own ACTUAL triangulated topology and primitive collar paths. The theorem does not replace a half twist by a fractional integral change of peripheral basis on the old link. When a right-angled matching-graph certificate is used, its explicit primitive cusp translations provide the tau_i in (5), with their separately calibrated source signs. No framing is deduced from a source Hessian. For the full Casimir plat phase, a further theorem must identify its linearized or Artin-ring critical equations with this decorated germ, including incidence multipliers, scale quotients and the actual marked cap. The local character map and this geometric rigidity are inputs to that theorem. They do not yet prove its magnetic Hessian radical or a nonzero original-source amplitude. Physical-cycle selection and global coherent estimates remain separate even after such an identification. Audit: [actual three-cusp marked gluing](../experiments/audit_general_marked_multicusp_gluing_rigidity.py), [results](../experiments/general_marked_multicusp_gluing_rigidity_results.json). It constructs cusp normal curves on an actual doubled-octahedron quotient, checks edge rank 5 and marked rank 8 for all eight meridian/longitude choices, and computes the exact diagonal peripheral derivative. The test curves are explicitly chosen primitive bases of that fixture; they are not substituted for the original crossing-disk marking of another link. Independent character/current review: full analytical read and fresh audit PASS. The reviewer checked edge-row dependencies, the componentwise peripheral pairing basis, positive polarized Jacobian, actual developing/ cross-ratio inverse over Artin rings, exact eigenflags, and all eight mixed marked Jacobians in the three-cusp fixture. No source critical-scheme comparison or automatic positive-triangulation existence was inferred. Root review: full analytical read and fresh audit PASS. The review checked the torus Euler count, vertex-sum rank argument, quad-coordinate sign, real-Lagrangian transversality, decorated-representation Artin inverse, exact-eigenvalue distinction and commuting-similarity cusp derivative. The stated positive marked geometric certificate remains a hypothesis.

title: A general marked positive gluing certificate, without a convex polyhedron
text: # A general marked positive gluing certificate, without a convex polyhedron 30 October 2026. A finite positive ideal gluing certificate is enough for the geometric anchor in the general augmented-plat program. No convex right-angled polyhedron, checkerboard decomposition, Conway expression, or bridge-width restriction is needed. There is also a useful simplification: for an actual ideal triangulation with torus links, positivity and the MULTIPLICATIVE edge equations already force unit edge winding. One need not impose an additional logarithmic angle equation at every edge. This is a direct sufficient certificate theorem. It does not establish that every augmented diagram has such a solution, or select the original quantum source's geometric period. The existing general source-regulator completion theorem requires still less geometric structure: an actual complete marked hyperbolic base and a nearby framed representation. The certificate below supplies that base and its absolute volume by finite algebraic data. ## 1. Exact hypotheses and the marked topological certificate Let Y be the interior of a compact oriented three-manifold with nonempty torus boundary. In the intended application Y is the ACTUAL augmented plat exterior, with its given crossing disks, main components, half twists and primitive peripheral paths. Supply a finite oriented ideal triangulation T with all of the following: * Every tetrahedron face is paired. There are no finite vertices, unpaired boundary faces, material boundary faces or extra cone points. * Away from the deleted ideal vertices, the face quotient is a three-manifold; every ideal vertex link is a compact torus. The orientation is coherent across the face pairings. * The quotient has a specified orientation-preserving homeomorphism to Y, taking its labeled ideal ends and peripheral paths to the ACTUAL marked ones. A triangulation of an unrelated link, the same number of cusps, or the same numerical volume does not supply this datum. This topology condition is finite and reviewable: for example a common subdivision with the literal disk/projection cut and its labeled boundary maps gives a simplicial certificate. It is separate from solving shape equations. One can instead begin with a triangulation constructed directly on the specified exterior. Give each oriented tetrahedron t a shape z_t with Im(z_t)>0, and set z'_t=1/(1-z_t), z''_t=1-1/z_t. (1) The tetrahedral ordering assigns these parameters to its three opposite edge pairs. Use precisely those orderings in every equation. Require product_(tetrahedral edge incidences at e) w_(t,e)=1 (2) for every global edge e, where w is its assigned z,z',or z''. Incidences are counted with multiplicity, including identified edges of one tetrahedron. These are full complex equalities, not modulus equations. Finally require completeness of every cusp. One explicit algebraic version is that the complex linear similarity multipliers of both recorded primitive peripheral paths are one: a_mu=1, a_lambda=1. (3) They are computed from the actual face-path words in the corner triangles, with their literal signs. They are rational monomials in the tetrahedral shapes in a fixed convention. They are PROJECTIVE similarity multipliers; SL eigenvalues require their selected square roots and central signs. An equivalent finite horosphere certificate is given in section 4. THEOREM. These data construct a positively oriented complete finite- volume hyperbolic metric on the actual Y, with Vol(Y)=sum_t D(z_t)>0. (4) Here D is the Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm, once for each oriented fundamental tetrahedron. There is no unrecorded factor two. The geometric holonomy, its peripheral paths and its fundamental-class regulator are those of the given marked topology. ## 2. Why multiplicative edge equations force winding one Write n for the number of tetrahedra, e for the number of global edges, and h for the number of ideal vertices. There are 2n paired faces. End-compactify Y by coning each boundary torus to its deleted ideal vertex. Since chi(Y_compact)=0 and each torus has Euler characteristic zero, the end compactification has Euler characteristic h. The tetrahedral cell count gives h-e+2n-n=h, hence e=n. (5) For completeness, chi(Y_compact)=0 follows by doubling the oriented compact three-manifold: its double has Euler characteristic zero by pairing complementary cells, and the gluing boundary has Euler characteristic zero. Alternatively count the triangulated cusp links: there are 4n link triangles, 6n link edges, and 2e link vertices, with multiplicity at the two ends of every global edge. Their total Euler characteristic is 2e-2n=0. The actual manifold/link hypothesis excludes an edge reversal that would invalidate this count. All three parameters in (1) have positive imaginary part. Their arguments lie in (0,pi), and zz'z''=-1 gives Arg z+Arg z'+Arg z''=pi. (6) Indeed the sum lies strictly between zero and 3pi and is pi modulo 2pi. Thus the sum of all six dihedral angles of one ideal tetrahedron is 2pi. At an edge e, equation (2) implies that its positive total angle is 2pi m_e for a positive integer m_e. Summing over ALL edges, sum_e m_e=n=e. (7) Every summand is at least one and there are e summands. Consequently m_e=1 for EVERY edge. This is the promised unit-winding proof; it uses positivity and torus links globally, not an arbitrarily chosen branch of Log(2). The same edge product also removes longitudinal translation. To see both parts directly, develop the edge to the vertical line from 0 to infinity. Consecutive incident faces determine rays in its transverse complex plane. The next tetrahedral sector changes their ratio by its assigned w. Multiplying all sectors gives exactly (2). The modulus records translation along the edge and the argument records rotation. Thus translation is zero, while (7) says the sectors fill one full turn. The local edge development is an ordinary ball neighborhood, not a branched 4pi-or-higher neighborhood with the same PSL word. Ideal faces are all isometric triangles, so their specified vertex maps glue by actual isometries. Face interiors, tetrahedron interiors and the just-checked finite edge neighborhoods therefore carry a nonsingular oriented hyperbolic metric. ## 3. Complete cusps from the actual similarity links A horospherical corner of an ideal tetrahedron is an oriented Euclidean triangle, defined up to positive scale. The face maps glue these as oriented Euclidean SIMILARITIES on the compact topological cusp torus. Section 2 makes every link vertex nonsingular: its incident angles sum to 2pi and its transverse edge holonomy is identity. The similarity structure consequently has a well-defined linear holonomy character of the torus group. By (3) this character is trivial on its actual two generators and hence on the whole group. Choose one corner's scale and transport it along link paths. The scale returns to itself around every loop, so the corner triangles acquire compatible Euclidean metrics. The compact link is a nonsingular flat Euclidean torus, and is complete. Its lifted local development covers the whole Euclidean plane: lift finite line segments using completeness, and use that the plane is simply connected. Its deck group is therefore a discrete rank-two translation lattice. In particular the two primitive paths have nonzero, real-linearly independent translation periods; these are a CONSEQUENCE, not an extra numerical assumption hiding in (3). Realize these compatible corner scales by actual horospheres in each tetrahedron. A uniform shrink makes all the chosen corner neighborhoods disjoint. Their face maps agree on the horospheres, and each assembled end has the standard metric dt^2+exp(-2t) ds_link^2. There are finitely many tetrahedra, so the part left after truncating these ends is compact. The metric on all of Y is complete and has finite volume. Its universal developing cover is H3, by the same complete-local-isometry segment-lifting argument. Thus its actual holonomy is discrete and faithful. Summing the oriented volumes of its disjoint tetrahedral interiors proves (4). ## 4. A finite real-algebraic test and a local decoration alternative Write z_t=x_t+i y_t. Positivity is y_t>0. Equations (1)--(3), after clearing only their specified nonzero denominators, are real polynomial equalities and equalities in finitely many variables. Every denominator in (1) is nonzero automatically by y_t>0. Literal peripheral paths must still be evaluated in the same marked convention. If an exact algebraic point is supplied, isolating intervals distinguish its real embedding and certify all strict inequalities. A numerical residual alone is not an exact solution certificate. One may replace (3) by finite COMPATIBLE HOROSPHERE data. Give each corner triangle a positive scale and require equality of the corner segment lengths under every paired face. These equations are algebraic: canonical squared side lengths are rational expressions in x_t,y_t; positive scale squares remove square roots. All transitions are then Euclidean isometries. The resulting nonsingular compact torus is flat and complete as above. Its orientation-preserving deck isometries must be translations, since a nontrivial rotation of the Euclidean plane has a fixed point and cannot act as a deck transformation. Hence its full complex linear holonomy is one, recovering (3). This decoration version is sometimes easier to audit than long peripheral monomials. It does NOT remove the primitive paths: those remain needed to identify a filling slope and source peripheral logs. A strictly positive angle assignment alone is weaker than this certificate. It controls angle sums, but does not supply the complex edge modulus equations or complete cusp scales. Conversely an arbitrary nondegenerate complex solution with negatively oriented tetrahedra cannot be used in (7): its winding terms need not be positive. Such data need a different nonsingular developing-map certificate. ## 5. Absolute regulator and the source comparison that remains The actual tetrahedral quotient is an oriented degree-one fundamental chain. Its developed ideal shapes therefore give beta_T=sum_t [z_t], D(beta_T)=Vol(Y). (8) This is the absolute geometric anchor. If all shapes lie in a common number field, (8) is its actual marked algebraic Bloch chain; the complete peripheral boundary vanishes after tensoring with Q, by the finite fundamental-chain boundary calculation already proved in the repo. No assertion about integral flattenings or an identification of different fields is needed for the real regulator identity (8). For a nearby actual framed representation, develop the SAME marked ideal vertices using its peripheral fixed flags and take cross-ratios. Positivity and nondegeneracy persist in a small neighborhood. This constructs shapes from an existing representation; it does not assume existence of a representation for arbitrary specified peripheral values. The marked peripheral and regulator calculations of [the general source-regulator theorem](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md) then apply on that connected branch. In particular a proposed source action G must still satisfy dG=(1/2) sum_s V_s dU_s, Im G(0)=sum_t D(z_t), (9) with the ACTUAL primitive projective logs. Then Im G-(1/2)sum_s Re U_s Im V_s equals the actual representation volume. At nearby unit-charge primitive filling points the existing general completion theorem identifies this with the filled hyperbolic volume. Neither solving (2) nor knowing (8) proves (9) for the original quantum source. Whole-color control, normal sectors, selected cycles, nonzero amplitudes and the source's branch selection remain additional tasks. ## 6. The exact variational criterion, in both directions Let A_T be the angle polytope of this ACTUAL triangulation. Its variables are three opposite-pair angles per tetrahedron, each nonnegative; their tetrahedral sums are pi and their global edge sums are 2pi. Write A_T^+ for its strictly positive part and define V(theta)=sum_t [Lambda(alpha_t)+Lambda(beta_t)+Lambda(gamma_t)], Lambda(a)=-integral_0^a log(2 sin s) ds. (10) The following equivalent criteria give the same complete metric: * There is a positive complete gluing certificate of section 1. * V has a critical point in A_T^+. * The maximum of V on the closed angle polytope is attained in A_T^+. When these hold, the critical point is UNIQUE, including as a maximizer of the closed polytope, and its value is the actual Vol(Y). This is the needed general Casson--Rivin optimization statement. Here is a direct proof of both directions and the normalization; no geometric existence theorem is being inserted into the implication. ### The elementary horocycle and length identity For one positive ideal tetrahedron, choose an arbitrary horosphere at each of its four corners. At corner a, its Euclidean triangle has angles theta_ab, theta_ac, theta_ad. The sine law gives one positive number C_a such that its side in the ideal face abc has length s_(a;bc)=C_a sin(theta_ad). In an ideal triangle, the signed truncated length of its edge ab is ell_ab=-log[s_(a;bc) s_(b;ac)]. To check the constant directly, send that triangle to (infinity,0,1). The corner segment at infinity on height H has length 1/H; the segment at zero on a horocycle of Euclidean diameter d has length d. Their edge distance is log(H/d), proving the formula. Overlapping horospheres give its signed version, with the same identity. Put S=sin(alpha)sin(beta)sin(gamma) and u_a=-log C_a-(1/2)log S. The two opposite angle pairs other than theta_ab occur in the product of the two corner segments. Consequently ell_ab=log sin(theta_ab)+u_a+u_b. (11) Conversely ANY four real values u_a are realized by positive corner horospheres: take C_a=exp(-u_a)/sqrt(S). On tetrahedral angle variations, the sum of the three angles at every corner is fixed. Equation (11) and opposite-pair equality therefore give the differential identity dV_t=-(1/2) sum_(six tetrahedral edges ab) ell_ab dtheta_ab. (12) Indeed the four u terms cancel by the corner angle sums, and each opposite pair supplies -log sin(alpha) d alpha; the missing log 2 also cancels because d alpha+d beta+d gamma=0. This derives the ideal Schlaefli formula used here directly from (10) and actual horocycle lengths. ### Complete gluing implies a critical point and the unique maximum At the complete metric choose the compatible cusp horospheres of section 3. Each global edge e has ONE truncated length ell_e in all incident tetrahedra. Summing (12) gives dV=-(1/2) sum_e ell_e d(total angle at e)=0 (13) on the tangent space of A_T. Thus the geometric point is critical. The Hessian of V_t on gamma=pi-alpha-beta is negative definite. The negative Hessian matrix is [[cot alpha+cot gamma, cot gamma], [cot gamma, cot beta+cot gamma]]. Its first diagonal entry is sin(beta)/(sin(alpha)sin(gamma))>0, and its determinant is 1, by the cotangent addition identity when alpha+beta+gamma=pi. Hence V is strictly concave on the product of positive tetrahedral angle simplices and on A_T^+. It extends continuously to the compact closed angle polytope. Along a segment from its critical positive point to ANY other closed point, all intermediate points are positive, the initial derivative is zero, and the second derivative is strictly negative. The volume strictly decreases, so the endpoint also has smaller value. This proves the unique global maximum assertion, including boundary points. ### A positive critical point reconstructs complete gluing Conversely let theta in A_T^+ be critical. Since its constraints are linear, elementary row-space/kernel duality supplies real multipliers lambda_t for the tetrahedral sums and eta_e for the global edge sums: -log(2 sin alpha_t)=lambda_t+eta_e+eta_f, (14) where e,f are the two opposite edge incidences carrying alpha_t. The same formula holds for beta and gamma, with multiplicity if e=f. Constraint dependencies do not affect this statement. Construct the positive ideal tetrahedron with these angles, for example z_t=[sin(beta_t)/sin(gamma_t)] exp(i alpha_t). Put L_e=-2 eta_e. Equation (14) gives L_e+L_f-2log sin(alpha_t)=2lambda_t+2log 2, the SAME value for all three opposite pairs in t. Therefore there exist four real numbers u_a, one per tetrahedral corner, such that L_(ab)=log sin(theta_ab)+u_a+u_b (15) for all six incidences. Here is the entire linear algebra: set b_ab=L_(ab)-log sin(theta_ab). The three opposite-pair sums of b are equal, which is precisely the two compatibility conditions for the six equations b_ab=u_a+u_b. They have a unique solution, starting with u_a=(b_ab+b_ac-b_bc)/2 and then u_b=b_ab-u_a, etc. By (11), choose the actual tetrahedral corner horospheres realizing these u_a. Thus EVERY incident tetrahedron now has the same prescribed truncated length L_e on a global edge. The three side lengths of an ideal face determine its three corner horocycle sizes uniquely: if s_a s_b=exp(-L_ab), then log s_a=(-L_ab-L_ac+L_bc)/2. Consequently all face pairings match all corner horospheres. Around each global edge these maps preserve the two endpoint horospheres, so its dilation is zero. Its total angle is 2pi by the angle-polytope constraint, so its full edge holonomy is identity and the local development is nonsingular. The compatible corner decorations give complete flat cusp tori by section 4. Thus these shapes satisfy the edge and complete peripheral equations and construct the actual complete geometric metric. This proves the converse. In particular, a nonempty strict angle polytope alone is NOT the criterion. Its volume maximum must lie in the strict interior. The proof above explains exactly what that interior optimum supplies. ## 7. A purely algebraic certificate for that strict optimum The variational criterion has a finite real-algebraic form with no logarithms. For each opposite angle pair take a unit phase w_(t,a) in the upper half-plane. Require |w_(t,a)|^2=1, Im w_(t,a)>0, product_(three pairs in t) w_(t,a)=-1, product_(incidences at global edge e) w_(t,a)=1. (16) The tetrahedral argument is pi by the same range check as (6), and the global arguments are exactly 2pi by (5)--(7). Thus these are an actual strict angle structure, with no missing angle winding. Add positive real variables A_t and B_e and require, at every opposite pair whose global edges are e,f, 2 Im(w_(t,a)) A_t B_e B_f=1. (17) Taking real logarithms gives precisely (14), with lambda_t=log A_t and eta_e=log B_e. Therefore (16)--(17) imply a positive critical point, hence actual complete geometry and the unique volume maximum. Conversely every such complete positive geometric point supplies these multipliers by the preceding proof. Equations (16)--(17) and strict positivity are finite polynomial conditions in real and imaginary parts. Repeated edge incidences retain the corresponding factor B_e^2. This is a simple algebraic sufficient criterion on ANY actual marked ideal triangulation, without first finding a convex Q_Delta. It is not a purely combinatorial classification: proving nonemptiness of this strict semialgebraic system for a chosen broad diagram class is still an existence problem. Its distinguished strict point is an honest geometric optimum, rather than an arbitrary branch of the exponentiated equations. Failure for one supplied triangulation is not a proof that Y is nonhyperbolic; a different marked triangulation may admit the certificate. The unique positive optimum also has ALGEBRAIC phases and shapes. Normalize its angles by pi. The closed angle polytope is rational, and its atoms are the rational coordinate angle triples, with weight one. The already proved [rational angle-optimizer theorem](positive_source_algebraic_volume_period.md) therefore applies directly. More explicitly, choose a rational tangent basis, exponentiate stationarity after clearing its denominators, and use the strictly negative Hessian to obtain an invertible complex Jacobian at the selected phase point. Differentiating those polynomial equations forces its coordinates to have zero transcendence degree over the coefficient number field. Formula z=exp(i alpha) sin(beta)/sin(gamma) then gives algebraic positive shapes. This proves algebraicity of the marked optimum; it does not make its dilogarithm value algebraic or identify any cyclotomic quantum source with that period. There is also a precise DECORATION TORSOR in this certificate. With the strict phases fixed, all positive multiplier solutions (A_t,B_e) correspond exactly to compatible choices of cusp horospheres. Indeed the reconstruction above converts each solution to corner horospheres; between two solutions their corner scale ratios agree across every paired face, and hence are constant on each actual cusp. If changing the horosphere at cusp v changes its corner term u by s_v, then L_e changes by s_v+s_w at an edge with endpoints v,w. Put t_v=exp(s_v/2). The exact action is A_t -> A_t product_(four corners v of t) t_v, B_e -> B_e/(t_v t_w), t_v>0. (18) It preserves (17) because the two opposite edges together use all four corners. The preceding horosphere comparison proves transitivity. It is free: a fixed B would give s_v+s_w=0 on every edge; the three edge equations of any tetrahedral face force each of its corner values to be zero, even when some global cusp labels coincide. Thus the positive solution fiber is a torsor for one positive scale per cusp. This is the actual geometric cusp-decoration gauge, NOT the still-unidentified quantum-period selection torsor. No assertion that the same monomial action is free over C is made; its sign kernels and square-root choices would have to be retained there. ## 8. The weakest useful general class and what was removed There are three different levels of geometric input: 1. An actual complete finite-volume marked hyperbolic base Y is enough for the already proved general geometric completion/regulator implication. It needs no ideal triangulation at all. 2. An actual marked positive complete gluing certificate as above gives that base and its regulator by finite explicit equations, uniformly for arbitrary plat width and arbitrary triangulation incidence. 3. A convex positive right-angled Q_Delta certificate gives such a triangulation by the coning construction in [the matching-graph theorem](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md). Thus (2) is a broader usable certificate than requiring (3). We do not claim a new existence theorem for positive ideal triangulations of all hyperbolic manifolds, nor a combinatorial characterization of all graphs admitting Q_Delta. Neither is needed for the implication proved here. For the general long-twist target, one can retain its existing hypothesis that the ACTUAL augmented exterior is hyperbolic, and use ANY independently certified geometric base instead of first reconstructing a right-angled convex polyhedron. A common marked positive triangulation is a convenient way to compare a source Bloch chain with its actual fundamental class. The broad quantum theorem remains about the original augmented source on this geometric base; the certificate has not replaced that source by a state sum defined from T. ## 9. Coverage and independent exact checks For coverage, the antecedent is explicit in [Futer--Gueritaud, *From angled triangulations to hyperbolic structures*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.0440): its abstract states the Casson--Rivin theorem that a critical point of the angle-structure volume functional gives a complete hyperbolic structure. No novelty of that theorem is claimed. Sections 2--7 above give the direct proof and exact marked-certificate form used here; they do not import an existence theorem for arbitrary augmented plats. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_general_marked_positive_gluing_certificate.py) constructs an eight-tetrahedron face quotient from two regular ideal octahedra with the original two bowtie pairings. It checks orientation of every face map, three torus vertex links, all eight complex edge products, and angle sum exactly 2pi at every edge. Ninety-six paired corner-segment checks give compatible horospheres. The same exact data satisfy the critical-point multiplier equations independently; the restricted Hessian determinant and four-corner compatibility identity are checked symbolically. These test the stated geometric and variational certificate, not a quantum source selection theorem. [Recorded results](../experiments/general_marked_positive_gluing_certificate_results.json). Primary-agent and separate independent analytical reviews: PASS, with fresh replays of the exact audit. Both reviews checked E=T and unit edge winding, complete torus links, actual primitive topology, the signed horocycle length constant, both directions of the variational criterion, dependent constraints and repeated edge incidences, the strict boundary maximum, the algebraic phase/multiplier certificate, and the precise positive cusp-decoration torsor. The Bloch boundary claim is explicitly rational. These reviews certify the stated geometric implication; they do not assert positive-certificate existence for every diagram or select its quantum period.

title: The full original augmented-plat source on its matching graph
text: # The full original augmented-plat source on its matching graph 30 October 2026. EVERY fixed original augmented plat has an exact state sum on the SAME marked cubic graph Delta as its geometric projection/disk cut. The nonmatching edges carry the physical V_N; a matching edge carries an ordinary Q_j=V_(2j), summed over ALL folded labels. Every term is the original first normal of its genuine generic pivotal closure. The statement holds at both parities and composite levels, with the actual paired nilpotent circle sectors retained. This is a full complete-circle source identity, not merely a selected central sector. It supplies the source-compatible graph to be resummed. It proves no positivity, dominant branch, mixed auxiliary-color packet, or volume asymptotic. ## 1. The actual complete-circle factorization Fix an original 2k-plat with r crossing boxes, all outside wires and cups/caps recorded, signed retained exponents epsilon_i, and ONE exposed original marked physical arc. Put d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, s_u=product_(v=1)^u 2sin(pi v/N), s_0=1. The all-input complete circle is the sum of its full folded sectors. The proved physical factorization in [the original all-channel source](actual_trivalent_all_channel_marked_contraction.md) is L_N=sum_(j=0)^M L_j, R^epsilon L_j=omega_j^epsilon h0_j W_j pi_j, pi_j=G_j^-1 W_j^dagger P, G_(j,a)=s_(2j)/(s_a s_(2j-a)), h0_j=k_j N s_(2j)/s_j^2, k_j=2 if 2j<d, k_j=1 if 2j=d, omega_j=q^(d^2/2) (-1)^j q^[j(j+1)]. (1) Here W_j:Q_j->V_N tensor V_N is the actual first-entry-one Clebsch map, and P is the original two-head reversal. Crucially, pi_j W_j=0 on a paired node, pi_j W_j=I on the odd simple node 2j=d. (2) Thus W_j pi_j is not generally a projector. Formula (1) includes the circle's original first-normal coefficient before introducing Q_j; no semisimple root quotient is made. All input physical degrees are included in (1). ## 2. Split the actual graph, preserving its typed vertices For a fixed label vector j=(j_1,...,j_r), split each coupon as W_j pi_j.
