Its intermediate edge Q_j is exactly the crossing-disk edge d_i in Delta. The remaining legs follow the actual outside main intervals and carry V_N. The vertex cyclic orders are the disk-side sectors of [the matching-graph construction](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md). Consequently the state graph has matching edges D: Q_(j_i), nonmatching edges: V_N, vertices: the actual ordered W_(j_i) or pi_(j_i). (3) Every vertex has two physical legs and one matching-channel leg. This requires no bipartite coloring, no Fisher structure, and no ordering of all black vertices below all white ones. Cups/caps and actual head reversals are retained at every bend. One does not replace a cyclic turn by an unclocked index permutation. Let Z_Delta(j) denote the contraction in (3) with the ORIGINAL exposed physical mark, after removing only the displayed scalar factors in (1). Multilinearity of the actual ordered coupon word gives A_(D,N)=sum_(j in {0,...,M}^r) product_i[h0_(j_i) omega_(j_i)^epsilon_i] Z_Delta(j). (4) This is the raw source before its independently recorded exterior framing line. Physical coupons in overlapping strand positions have not been commuted. Only the independent finite color sums distribute over their original order. ## 3. An explicit regular generic lift at EVERY folded label Keep N and the root constants h0_j,omega_j fixed. Let zeta=q exp(t) and use the generic balanced highest-weight-d object V_d(zeta), with Q=zeta^2 and F_u=(Q;Q)_u. Its actual physical cup is pV_(a,d-a)=N zeta^(-d^2) (-1)^a zeta^[a(d-a-1)] F_a F_(d-a)/F_d, ellV=pV^-1. (5) On Q_j choose the ordinary highest-weight-2j cup pQ_j with first coefficient one, given by the same formula with d replaced by 2j and the initial scale omitted. All its factorial indices are <N. The regular W_j(t) has highest degree l=d-j and coefficients h_u(t)=(-1)^u zeta^(-du) Q^[u(l-1)-u(u-1)/2] (Q^(j+1);Q)_u F_(d-u)/F_d, W_(j,a)(t)=F_pair(t)^a h(t)/F_a, 0<=a<=2j. (6) All denominator indices in (5),(6) are below N. The original highest recurrence and divided coproduct prove its generic Hopf covariance, including its last endpoint; this is the already checked finite construction in the cited all-channel note. Put gamma_j=q^(2-j^2)/N^2, a FIXED nonzero root constant, and define pi_j(t)=gamma_j^-1 D_t(W_j(t)), D_t(W_j)=pQ_j(t)^T W_j(t)^T [ellV(t)^T tensor ellV(t)^T] P. (7) At t=0 this is exactly pi_j of (1). Equation (7) retains the ordinary cup normalization, both physical inverse cups, reversed tensor order and gamma_j. It divides by NO vanishing paired norm pi_j W_j. Thus W_j(t)pi_j(t) is a regular generic Hopf coupon whose root is the actual normalized circle sector, at both parities. This is a chosen lift of a fixed-root map. It is not asserted to be the original circle's entire moving-q germ, nor a new off-root link invariant. That distinction causes no ambiguity in the marked root scalar below. ## 4. Every marked sector is ONE retained trace normal Let F_Delta(j;t) be the ordinary closed original diagram obtained by using the regular W_j(t)pi_j(t) coupons, the original outside cups/caps, and an ordinary cap also at the chosen marked arc. Splitting its coupons gives exactly the typed generic network (3), with (5)--(7). Leave that exposed physical arc open. Generic Hopf covariance makes the resulting endomorphism of V_d a scalar z_Delta(j;t) I: generic K has distinct weights and every interior F arrow is nonzero, so its commutant is scalar. All entries are regular, so z_Delta is holomorphic. The literal physical closure therefore gives F_Delta(j;t)=D_N(t) z_Delta(j;t), D_N(t)=(-1)^d [N]_(q exp(t)), D_N(0)=0, nu_N=D_N'(0)=2N(-1)^N/(q-q^-1) !=0. (8) The original unrestricted root marked row has m pV(0)=1. After the other actual caps act, the remaining column is z_Delta(j;0)pV(0), so that mark extracts precisely z_Delta(j;0). Hence Z_Delta(j)=F_Delta'(j;0)/nu_N. (9) Only the physical trace factor is divided out. The mark is not put on a channel Q_j, whose dimension or norm could vanish, and no bare mark is moved through an enclosing cap. The exposed one-head cut is part of the specified original diagram. If another regular generic Hopf lift has the same root coupons, it has the same root open endomorphism and marked scalar. Its ordinary closure differs by D_N(t) times a holomorphic scalar vanishing at zero, so its normalized first derivative is the same. This proves the required lift independence without identifying moving-q germs. Combining (4),(9) gives the full source theorem: A_(D,N)=(1/nu_N) sum_(j in {0,...,M}^r) product_i[h0_(j_i) omega_(j_i)^epsilon_i] F_Delta'(j;0). (10) Equivalently the first derivative is taken after summing the regular finite physical networks. For fixed N the sum is finite. Its regular physical presentation needs only first jets; a singular recoupling frame may require higher Laurent coefficients before its pole cancellations recover this same first normal. ## 5. The special odd endpoint and the exact geometric target For N=2m+1 and all j_i=m, Q_j=V_N, h0_m=N and pi_m W_m=I. Then all edges of Delta carry the same ordinary object, and (10)'s central contribution is N^r omega_m^(sum epsilon_i) F_Delta'(m,...,m;0)/nu_N. This recovers the earlier endpoint interface, without extending its projector argument to even levels. Equation (10) includes the paired sectors at every parity instead of discarding them. If Delta has the actual positive right-angled ideal polyhedron Q_Delta, its shaded triangles are the source vertices in (3), and its ideal vertices are the source edges. The literal quotient gives the actual complete augmented volume 2Vol(Q_Delta). Coning Q_Delta and using the identical subdivisions in its second copy gives a marked positive ideal triangulation T. Its GLOBAL angle polytope is sum_(three opposite pairs in t) alpha_(t,a)=pi, sum_(all tetrahedral incidences at global e) alpha_(t,e)=2pi, alpha>=0. (11) All incidence coefficients come from the actual complete face-pairing words, including the shaded half twists. The [proved positive gluing theorem](general_marked_positive_gluing_certificate.md) gives its unique positive maximum and absolute value max_(11) sum_t V_ideal(alpha_t)=2Vol(Q_Delta). (12) A separately certified marked positive triangulation may replace Q_Delta. Thus (10) and (11) are now on the same actual topology. An exact coherent resummation must STILL show how its state variables map to these edge incidences and how its retained source action equals the single constrained functional (12). Ordinary spin triangle inequalities or independently maximized vertex factorials do not supply (11). The original phase obstruction excludes independent magnetic-leg positive gauges; it does not exclude a coherent positive resummation. The NC class is recovered when Delta is the Fisher expansion of its source graph Gamma. Its facial triangle contractions give the known local coefficients and the Gamma-network first normal. The odd cube's clocked rung resummation gives a positive global Newton period and its shared core action. Those are actual special reductions of (10), not a proof that every Delta has the same positive form. ## 6. What this settles and what remains Equation (10) is a full-source matching-graph state sum for every fixed plat width. It retains all internal folded labels, both level parities, all paired nilpotent circles, actual cup/dual constants and one original mark. No vanishing root norm is inverted. The external line is not renormalized using a hoped-for answer. It permits zero sectors and zero whole source values. It does not prove endpoint dominance or even complete-color nonvanishing. It is not yet the mixed auxiliary-circle-color packet required for long fillings. Those fillings still require the whole-color gap, selected geometric cycle, actual peripheral branch and unit logarithmic charge. A formal first-normal formula alone provides none of those estimates. ## 7. Coverage only and exact verification [Van der Veen, arXiv:0805.0094v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0805.0094), Definitions 1--2 and Theorem 2, starts with a specified KTG-move sequence and gives a sufficient augmentation multiplicity. Its stated formula holds at ODD N and is zero at EVEN N, with an explicitly so(3) conclusion. Its singly augmented outside is built from regular ideal octahedra. That is not an all-level theorem for every single- circle matching graph or for all independently long fillings. Only its definitions and theorem statements are used here for coverage. [Ibarra--McQuire--Purcell](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09296) addresses OCTAHEDRAL fully augmented links, states its TV result without half twists, and sets Dehn fillings aside. The invariant and root differ from the original marked source here. [Belletti](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.01904) states a Yokota upper-bound conjecture, results for a specified large family and TV consequences. Neither supplies the original coherent first-normal estimate for arbitrary Delta. No proof technique from those papers is used here. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.py) checks eight original plats at N=2,...,6 and widths k=2,3,4. It checks 204 fixed-label generic trace normals and five EXHAUSTIVE color sums, using independently constructed original Casimir/circle/R matrices. It explicitly verifies the paired zero pi_j W_j, the complete circle sum, actual signed twists, and the unrestricted marked contraction. The outside-interval compiler also checks every oriented matching-graph face. The regular generic jets retain (5)--(7) before specialization. [Recorded results](../experiments/general_matching_graph_full_normal_source_results.json). These are exact source-identity checks, not finite-level evidence for an unproved nonvanishing or asymptotic claim. The four-box width-two fixture has positions (1,0,2,1), zero based. Its two middle circles surround complementary pairs in a transverse four-punctured sphere and cobound the unpunctured annulus between those pairs. They are parallel augmentations, so this fixture is NOT an essential hyperbolic skeleton. The source also explains its even zeros: on the regular four-head invariant space the two complementary pair Casimirs agree, by the actual generic cup duality. Their circle product is therefore L_N^2, which is zero at even levels. The retained disjoint half twists commute with this product. These exact zeros are not being presented as hyperbolic counterexamples. The audit tests the finite source identity even on such degenerate diagrams. Independent source-transport and character/current reviews: both full analytical reads and fresh audit replays PASS. They checked the regular all-label lifts, actual cup constants and gamma, exposed physical mark, trace-normal sign, lift independence and the full finite summation. The even-zero fixture was checked as the stated parallel-circle obstruction. Neither review infers nonvanishing, a selected geometric branch or a general asymptotic from (10).

title: Long fillings of a general original quantum source
text: # Long fillings of a general original quantum source 29 October 2026. The Fourier filling mechanism is independent of the pretzel graph. This theorem isolates its actual analytic inputs and proves that they propagate to every independently sufficiently long fixed signed integral filling. The new general geometric theorem then identifies the resulting rate with the actual filled hyperbolic volume. This is a CONDITIONAL quantum transfer theorem. It does not assert its source hypotheses for every diagram, or count them as proved merely because the diagram has a positive geometric triangulation. Establishing them for broader original sources is part of the active goal. ## 1. Exact source and hypotheses Fix a diagram with b specified crossing-circle ports on original complete target strands. Retain its entire marked closure, all Cartan factors, and its literature normalization. Let A_N(h_1,...,h_b) be its ORIGINAL mixed-circle scalar, with auxiliary colors j_i=N-h_i. The [all-input circle basis](actual_crossing_circle_source_and_filling.md) gives the exact finite identity K_N(p)=chi_N kappa^(-2 sum p_i) sum_(j_1,...,j_b=1)^N product_i beta_(j_i-1)^(-p_i) A_N(N-j_1,...,N-j_b). (1) This substitutes each actual full twist R^(-2p_i), leaving the base coupons and retained half twists in A_N. The beta coefficients retain all confluent Casimir jets. Multilinearity of the original diagram proves(1), even if adjacent physical operators do not commute. The independent color-register functionals commute; no physical operator is moved through another. Keep chi_N explicitly and require its known normalization to be nonzero with log|chi_N|=o(N). Here A_N is defined before precisely that recorded outer factor; chi_N is not included a second time in the mixed scalar. It is not chosen using the value of the completed unknown invariant. Assume the following for this fixed source. **Global source gap.** There is a fixed sufficiently small delta>0, H=floor(delta N), a real F0 and gamma>0 such that max_(some h_i>H) |A_N(h)| <= poly(N) exp[N(F0-gamma)] (2) over the ENTIRE physical color cube 0<=h_i<=N-1. The estimate includes ordinary colors, every alias and every marked normal term. **Exact analytic corridor packet.** There is a finite holomorphic packet C_N(x), even in each coordinate, on a fixed complex neighborhood of the box |Re x_i|<=2delta, |Im x_i|<=sigma0, with |A_N(h)-eta_N C_N(h/N)| <=poly(N) exp[N(F0-gamma)] (3) for 0<=h_i<=H. Here eta_N is an explicit retained unit phase. On that fixed complex neighborhood, C_N(x)=N^mu a(x) exp[N phi(x)](1+O(N^-1)), (4) uniformly, where a and phi are holomorphic and separately even, a(0)!=0, phi(0)=F0, and phi''(0)=2pi i diag(tau_1,...,tau_b), Im tau_i>0. (5) A known imaginary constant in phi(0) may instead be retained explicitly as exp[iN Im phi(0)] in eta_N. This only separates its specified unit phase; it does not change the original state or an unknown growth rate. The uniform complex statement is essential. A pointwise approximation on the physical grid is not enough for the Fourier contour estimates. One may shrink delta, with the global gap(2) required for the chosen corridor. By(4)--(5), after shrinking the neighborhood, |C_N(x+iy)|<=poly(N) exp[N(F0-a0||x||^2+B0||y||^2)] (6) with a0>0. All constants may depend on the fixed diagram, not on N. These assumptions concern a specified original source and specified interpolation, not a choice of solution of its recurrence. ## 2. The source action and theorem Define the local analytic Fourier transform by grad phi(xi(z))+2pi i z=0, Psi(z)=phi(xi(z))+2pi i xi(z) dot z, B(z)=(2pi)^(b/2) a(xi(z))/sqrt(det[-phi''(xi(z))]). The implicit-function theorem applies by(5). The Gaussian square root is the one from the translated original real contour. Both Psi and B are separately even; B(0)!=0 and Psi(z)=F0-i pi sum_i z_i^2/tau_i+O(||z||^4). (7) For integer nonzero charges m_i put T_m(z)=Psi(z)-2pi i sum_i(p_i z_i^2+m_i z_i). For all independently sufficiently large fixed signed p_i, let z_* be the unique nearby critical point of T_1. Then K_N(p)=chi_N eta_N kappa^(-sum p_i) N^mu D(p) exp[N T_1(z_*)](1+O_p(N^-1)), (8) where D(p)=2^b (2pi)^(b/2) B(z_*) product_i sinh(2pi i z_*,i) /sqrt(det[-T_1''(z_*)]) is NONZERO. Consequently lim_N (2pi/N)log|K_N(p)|=2pi Re T_1(z_*). (9) The slopes and diagram are fixed before N tends to infinity. There is no slope-comparability, same-sign, prime-level or parity restriction. The constants and threshold are source dependent. ## 3. Exact filling, including every endpoint and normal term The full Hermite coefficients obey sum_j |beta_j^(-p)|<=2N(1+|p|). Thus(2)--(3) cost only polynomial multiples of exp[N(F0-gamma)] in the WHOLE finite sum(1). No non-even alias is folded into C_N. For its exact even corridor define F_N(z)=sum_(|h_i|<=H) C_N(h/N) exp(2pi i h dot z). The [full-normal Fourier identity](actual_filling_source_fourier_endpoint_gap.md), sections4--5, is valid for ANY even packet. In each color its sampled kernel is the derivative of exp(-2pi i p N z^2) sinh(2pi i z) F_N(z). Its values vanish at z=+/-1/2 and its derivatives match at the two endpoints. Therefore the exact charge representation retains only m!=0. The complete b-port expression has integrand exp[-2pi i N sum_i(p_i z_i^2+m_i z_i)] product_i[m_i sinh(2pi i z_i)] F_N(z), with the unchanged parity phases and kappa factors. Its infinite charge series converges with the paired endpoint currents retained. This identity uses both original normal contributions; a value-only Fourier kernel would not give the same zero-charge cancellation. Hypothesis(6) is precisely the source-specific input of the exact cotangent-contour Fourier estimate. Its proof applies coordinatewise to C_N: noncentral frequencies, finite color endpoints and fixed mixed derivatives all have an exponential source gap. The paired high-charge current has a double zero at the endpoint. Its weighted bound is a constant times poly(N,p) m/(m-|p|)^3 exp[N(F0-g)], for m>2|p|+2delta+2, and is summable. The imaginary contour width is fixed by the SOURCE, not divided by the largest slope. In several coordinates use the exact telescoping difference of the full color functionals and their finite-charge restrictions, as in equation(14a) of that note. All spectator chirps stay on their REAL finite grids or finite real integrals while one tail is removed. Thus these bounds do not incur exp(N|p_j|) costs from another port. This is why independently unequal slopes are permitted. ## 4. The central packet and all nonminimal charges The central Fourier calculation in section6 of the same note uses only(4)--(6), analytic implicit stationarity and a real Gaussian. It gives, uniformly on a fixed small complex z-neighborhood, F_N(z)=N^(mu+b/2) B(z) exp[N Psi(z)](1+O(N^-1)). (10) No separate pointwise error is transformed as if it had an exponential Fourier gap; the exact finite analytic C_N is used throughout. The [local charge proof](actual_pretzel_long_filling_charge_selection.md) also depends only on the stated analytic structure. Here is its extension when the diagonal cusp parameters tau_i are different. Put epsilon_i=1/p_i,t_i=m_i/p_i. The saddle equations become z_i=-t_i/2+epsilon_i Psi_i(z)/(4pi i). They have a unique holomorphic solution in one fixed polydisk of (t,epsilon), with z_i=-t_i/2 at epsilon=0. Completing the square isolates a purely imaginary term on real t,epsilon: T_m(z_m)=(pi i/2)sum_i t_i^2/epsilon_i+Bhat(t^2,epsilon). The remainder is analytic and even in every t_i. If b_i=pi Im(tau_i)/|tau_i|^2>0, then partial_(t_i^2) Re Bhat(0,0)=-b_i/4. Shrink one fixed polydisk so each derivative is <=-b_i/8. Integrating these inequalities along the squared coordinates gives Re T_m(z_m)<=Re T_1(z_*) -sum_i (b_i/8)(m_i^2-1)/p_i^2. (11) Thus only |m_i|=1 can be leading among local nonzero charges. Every component z_i is nonzero for m_i!=0: separate evenness writes Psi_i=z_i Q_i(z_1^2,...,z_b^2), and the saddle equation solves z_i=-t_i/[2(1-epsilon_i Q_i/(4pi i))]. The sinh factors in(8) therefore do not vanish. The real part of the translated-contour Hessian remains strictly negative, so its Gaussian determinant is nonzero for signed as well as positive slopes. The finite nonlocal charges are treated by the same source estimate: outside |z_i|<=t0/4 the real source has a fixed Fourier gap; inside, |m_i+2p_i z_i|>=|p_i|t0/2 for a charge with |m_i/p_i|>=t0. A fixed imaginary shift in that coordinate decreases its filling phase, including the endpoint connectors. The gap is independent of the largest other slope. Local connector bounds use |Im z_i|<=C|p_i|^-1 |m_i/p_i|, which follows from the same separately even factorization. These are the arguments of sections4--5 of the [corridor proof](actual_pretzel_cusp_corridor_filling_survival.md); they do not use a common value of tau_i or a cyclic diagram. The 2^b minimal signed charges have identical complex action. Under (m_i,z_i)->(-m_i,-z_i), m_i sinh(2pi i z_i) is unchanged; the exact parity characters are unchanged as well. They ADD. Gaussian integration of(10) supplies N^(-b/2), giving(8). Finally Re T_1(z_*) tends uniformly to F0 as max_i|1/p_i| tends to zero, so the threshold can absorb the fixed global/error gaps(2)--(3). This proves the full-source, not only corridor, theorem. ## 5. When the rate is the ACTUAL hyperbolic volume Add the following independent geometric certificates for the SAME source. The base diagram is a fixed complete finite-volume cusped hyperbolic manifold Y. The analytic critical packet has an actual bounded framed representation family rho_x near the oriented complete holonomy, with the remaining components parabolic. Its original peripheral marking and absolute source action satisfy G=2pi i phi(x)+recorded real constant, z_i=2pi i x_i, ell_i=partial_(z_i)G=phi_i(x), U_i=-z_i, V_i=-2ell_i, with the literal spin kept when converting to these centered projective logs. Require the actual regulator comparison and the absolute anchor ImG(0)=Vol(Y), rather than merely a matching Hessian. The Fourier and filling stationarity equations then give EXACTLY ell_i=-2pi i z_*,i, U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i, 2pi Re T_1(z_*)=Vol(rho_p). The [general geometric completion theorem](general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.md) applies to this actual nearby framed representation. It gives a complete smooth hyperbolic metric on the correctly marked filled topology and hence lim_N (2pi/N)log|K_N(p)|=Vol(Y(p)). (12) That theorem handles arbitrary bases and primitive slopes. The quantum transfer proved HERE concerns the integral full-twist kernel(1); arbitrary rational quantum surgery kernels would need their own exact source and endpoint proof. No rational-filling quantum statement is silently added by the more general geometric theorem. ## 6. Current proved applications and active generalization task The established long-pretzel family supplies every hypothesis by explicit source and port proofs. The improved width estimate is being audited separately. For a general augmented diagram, identity(1) is already available, but the complete complex packet(3)--(5), its global gap(2), and its actual marked representation anchor must still be established. The theorem propagates those base certificates to all long fillings; it does not manufacture them from the A-polynomial or geometry alone. The active goal of the most general original-invariant equality remains open beyond the source classes where those hypotheses are proved. The [signed octahedral belt-stack assembly](actual_long_filled_octahedral_belt_stack_volume.md) now supplies all these hypotheses for another class, at every fixed nonempty stack width and fixed outer crossing power. Its literal inner color continuation, squared outer Fourier kernel, global source gaps, typed peripheral lift and complete face anchor give full equality for independently long signed integral fillings of ANY subset of auxiliary circles. Unfilled colors remain at h=0; they are not assigned p=0. This application does not turn the present conditional theorem into an unconditional statement for arbitrary graph sources. ## 7. Independent proof audit An independent read checked the exact N powers, the Cartan kernel factor, the all-unit parity cancellation, and the unequal-cusp charge estimate. It also checked the coordinate conversion dG=ell dz=(1/2)VdU and 2pi i T=G+sum p_i ell_i^2 up to its recorded REAL constant. The general theorem retains its base-source hypotheses; the audit does not establish them for a new diagram. The improved pretzel source proof currently verifies them for fixed odd s>=9. The [robust Conway filling theorem](actual_conway_long_filling_source_limit.md) now supplies every quantum hypothesis and the [actual marked peripheral branch](actual_conway_marked_peripheral_deformation.md) for all retained cylindrical robust factors. Arbitrary finite branching and turns are allowed; any subset of auxiliary circles may be filled along independently sufficiently long fixed signed integral slopes. Its complete mixed-color gap and uniform complex packet are proved separately. These pure full-twist fillings remain links with at least 2S+1 main components for S seeds, so this application is not a new knot-family claim. The [signed Conway extension](actual_odd_conway_long_filling_volume.md) now supplies the same hypotheses for arbitrary fixed pure or signed odd-half-twist patterns on C(FG), with both children robust. Its exact complex packet retains eta_N and every integer offset, its supporting-plane estimate controls every alias and physical color, and its actual odd-link primitive meridians realize the selected action shear. Constructive parity assignments give knots after filling all auxiliary circles. The minimal C(A) and arbitrary short fillings are not included in this signed mixed-color application.

title: The representation-volume bound with general peripheral holonomy
text: # The representation-volume bound with general peripheral holonomy 28 October 2026. The independently proved smearing argument for [boundary-parabolic representations](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md) also bounds representations whose peripheral images preserve a geodesic axis. Its proof needs integrable pullback volume and integrable finite- radius face errors, rather than a globally bounded derivative of the developing map. Axis-valued cusp maps supply exactly those properties. Consequently the marked regulator of EVERY actual SL2(C) representation of a finite-volume hyperbolic knot group has absolute value at most the manifold volume. This includes unit meridian and nonunit longitude. It supplies a geometric bound for a genuine peripheral-curve primitive; it does not identify a quantum-A component with that curve, or estimate the actual sourced quantum Green function. ## 1. Peripheral classification and an equivariant cusp development Let X=Gamma\H3 be an oriented complete finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold and rho:Gamma->SL2(C), followed by its PSL2 action. Each peripheral image consists of commuting matrices. If one has distinct eigenvalues, both common eigenlines are preserved by every commuting matrix, so the image preserves their joining geodesic axis. Otherwise the image is central or has a nontrivial unipotent, whose commuting matrices preserve its unique eigenline and act parabolically there. Thus each cusp is either of axis type or of the boundary-parabolic type already treated. Central images may be treated as axis type with zero translation. No discreteness or irreducibility is required. For an axis-type cusp use domain coordinates (w,y), with w in C, y>Y and peripheral translations w->w+lambda. Choose an oriented target axis gamma(t), parametrized by hyperbolic distance. Its peripheral action is rho(gamma_0) gamma(t)=gamma(t+chi(lambda_gamma0)), where chi is the real translation character. The rotations about the same axis act trivially ON the axis. Extend chi from the lattice to a real-linear function of w and set f(w,y)=gamma(chi(w)+log y). (1) This is exactly peripheral-equivariant. It is smooth on finite cusp truncations and its image has dimension at most one. Hence f^*(vol_H3)=0 on the ENTIRE axis cusp. (2) It need not be globally Lipschitz: its horizontal derivative in the hyperbolic domain metric can grow like y. Equation (2), not a false global Lipschitz assertion, is what is used below. On parabolic cusps retain the old affine conical map, which has a uniform hyperbolic derivative bound and integrable pullback volume. Extend over the compact truncated core equivariantly by geodesic interpolation on a finite triangulation and a collar. Contractibility of the target gives the extension. The resulting f is locally Lipschitz, has a finite derivative bound on every fixed metric neighborhood of the truncated core, and has absolutely integrable pullback volume on X. Define Vol(rho)=integral_X f^*(vol_H3). (3) ## 2. Choice independence and the actual regulator normalization Two axis-cusp maps for the same noncentral peripheral image can be joined by an equivariant axis-valued homotopy. Its boundary-torus homotopy has zero 3-volume because it lies in that axis. Reversing the chosen axis endpoint is also such a homotopy. For a central peripheral image the maps may be independent of w; a homotopy then has zero horizontal derivatives and again zero boundary 3-volume. Parabolic-cusp choices have the vanishing boundary estimate already proved in the linked note. Stokes on a truncated core therefore proves that (3) is independent of these choices. Map (1) tends to a peripheral fixed ideal endpoint as y tends to infinity. Truncate an ideal fundamental chain and compare its developed straightening with f by the same face-compatible geodesic homotopy on the compact pieces. Internal faces cancel. The comparison with the IDEAL straightening is not generally axis-valued on a cusp: the other developed vertices need not lie on that axis. Its boundary term instead vanishes by the following explicit estimate. Put the selected fixed endpoint at infinity and the preserved axis at horizontal coordinate zero. An ideal straightening can be parametrized conically near that vertex, along the vertical geodesic rays to infinity. On a finite triangulation of a fundamental cusp cross-section its map has form f_cone(w,y)=(a(w),y b(w)), b(w)>0. (4a) Here a,b and their piecewise first derivatives are bounded on the fundamental cross-section, and b is bounded below there. Extend these functions using peripheral equivariance. If that peripheral acts by (z,y)->(l_gamma z,|l_gamma|y), their transformation rules are a(w+lambda)=l_gamma a(w), b(w+lambda)=|l_gamma|b(w). The conical parametrization is chosen on the common cusp cross-section and its faces before extending over the finite tetrahedral interiors; thus adjacent straight faces use the same tail parametrization. It is an allowed proper straightening of the same developed ideal chain. For a tetrahedron with vertex infinity, its faces incident to that vertex are vertical, and its deep tail is foliated by these vertical rays; this gives the claimed conical choice after subdivision. Join the axis map to (4a) by the EXPLICIT equivariant homotopy H_t(w,y)=(t a(w), y exp((1-t)chi(w)+t Log b(w))). On a fundamental cross-section the horizontal coordinates and their w,t derivatives are O(1), while its height is comparable to y and its height derivatives are O(y). The hyperbolic volume form is height^-3 dx_1 wedge dx_2 wedge dheight. Hence integral_(cusp torus at y times [0,1]) |H^*vol| <=C/y^2 ->0. (4b) This estimate is independent of any assertion of global Lipschitzness or a zero comparison volume. On parabolic cusp tails use the old vanishing horospherical estimate. Thus, with the SAME marked fundamental-cycle convention, Vol(rho)=sum_Delta oriented Vol(straight_rho Delta) =sum_Delta D(z_Delta). (4) Auxiliary ideal flags and degenerate tetrahedra are handled by the finite-chain approximation used in the linked proof. This identifies the absolute regulator normalization; it is not an arbitrarily shifted primitive of a peripheral differential. ## 3. Finite-radius smearing without a global Lipschitz bound Use the finite regular tetrahedron T_R and symmetric Lorentz straightening/homotopy of the linked smearing proof. For each fixed R its diameter is finite. That proof compares the developed straight tetrahedron with integral_(g T_R) f^*vol by a sum of FOUR oriented face-prism errors b_rho(g,face). Their integrability is the only new issue. On an axis cusp, if a domain face lies entirely in one lifted cusp horoball, both f on that face and the straight interpolation of its three vertex images lie on the SAME target axis. The complete face-prism homotopy is axis-valued, so b_rho(g,face)=0 there. (5) A cusp horoball is convex. For fixed R, every remaining domain face which encounters an axis cusp and is not contained in it has its frame basepoint in a FIXED metric neighborhood of the truncated core. That neighborhood is compact modulo Gamma. On it f has some finite Lipschitz bound L_R, so the finite-radius face-prism estimate of the old proof bounds b there. On parabolic cusps the old global cusp bound applies. Hence every fixed-R face error is absolutely integrable on Gamma\Isom+(H3). No bound uniform in R is asserted or needed. For EACH fixed R the four ordered regular faces are congruent by orientation-preserving isometries. Right Haar invariance makes their integrated error values identical; their alternating sum is exactly zero. Fubini for f^*vol is justified by its absolute integrability. With frame-fiber Haar mass normalized to one, this gives Vol(T_R) Vol(rho) =integral_(Gamma\G) Vol(straight f(g T_R)) dg. (6) Every target straight tetrahedron has absolute volume at most v3, by the independently proved ideal-tetrahedron bound. The Haar mass of the frame quotient is Vol(X). Therefore |Vol(rho)|<=v3 Vol(X)/Vol(T_R). Let R tend to infinity, so Vol(T_R) tends to v3. This proves |Vol(rho)|<=Vol(X). (7) There is no interchange of an unbounded family of face errors in this last step: their cancellation was exact separately at every finite R. Any joint projective shape limit of actual representation families has the same bound, because each D extends continuously through 0,1,infinity. ## 4. Consequence and limitation for the actual A-curve route On a genuinely identified peripheral representation curve, retain the actual eigenvalues M and ell and the marked Bloch chain. Its already proved boundary identity is delta beta=-2 M wedge ell. The Bloch--Wigner differential gives, along |M|=1, dR=2 log|ell| dArg M =log|ell| dArg Y, Y=M^2. (8) Thus R is an ABSOLUTELY normalized primitive of the logarithmic longitude modulus on a specified representation branch, and (7) bounds it by the knot volume, including along nonunit-longitude arcs. For two points on that same branch, |integral log|ell| dArg Y|<=2Vol(X). (9) If the initial marked regulator is independently known to be zero, the bound relative to it improves to Vol(X). A unitary meridian alone does not make that initial regulator zero; the complete hyperbolic representation is an immediate example. This does NOT bound the integral of the pointwise largest root of an arbitrary quantum-A symbol: that prescription may switch branches and forgets their regulator constants. Nor does it identify the classical symbol of an arbitrary all-level annihilator with a genuine peripheral curve. The existing actual-state reciprocity theorem expressly makes no such identification. Finally a quantum Green response requires its original affine/normal source, finite-jet resonance and boundary matching determinant. Bound (7) is a proved geometric input to that problem, not a substitute for the missing sourced transfer estimate.

title: Strict representation-volume loss from an actual kernel
status: Strict volume and regular smoothing theorem
text: # Strict representation-volume loss from an actual kernel 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. This proves a geometric implication once the source capacity has been identified with the indicated representation volume. It does not identify smoothed blocks with JSJ pieces or supply that representation by itself. ## 1. Statement and the exact radial construction Let X=Gamma\H^3 be oriented, complete and finite-volume. Let rho:Gamma->SL2(C), followed by its action on H^3. Its peripheral matrix images commute. In this note ker(rho) means the kernel of that PSL2 action, so a central sign is retained as acting trivially. Use the equivariant map f already constructed in the [general-peripheral volume proof](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md): on each sufficiently deep axis cusp it is exactly f(w,y)=gamma(chi(w)+log y), and on a parabolic cusp, after target normalization, it is f(w,y)=(A w,y). Here chi is real-linear, A is real-linear, and neither is assumed injective. Central peripheral images are included in the axis case chi=0. The parabolic affine height constant could be retained and does not affect the arguments. Extend f smoothly on the compact core. The conclusion is: Vol(rho)=Vol(X) => ker(rho) is trivial. (1) Orientation reversal gives the same statement for absolute equality. Together with the non-strict bound derived below from the same maps, a nontrivial kernel therefore gives |Vol(rho)|<Vol(X). For a REAL parameter s>2 put Z_s=integral_H3 exp(-s d(x,y))dy, nu_x^s=Z_s^-1 integral_H3 exp(-s d(x,y)) mu_(f(y))dy, where mu_z is the probability visual measure at z on the target ideal sphere. Z_s is independent of x. These are rho-equivariant probability measures. They have no atoms: each visual measure has none and Tonelli applies. Their Busemann potentials are finite, strictly convex, and proper, so their barycenters F_s(x) exist uniquely. Properness follows directly from nonatomicity: choose uniformly small spherical caps of mass<1/4, and compare Busemann growth along rays outside such a cap. Strict convexity follows because the support is not contained in the two endpoints of one geodesic. Thus F_s is rho-equivariant. Write v_xi=grad B_xi at F_s(x), eta_y=grad_x d(x,y), and use the joint probability measure in the definition of nu_x^s. Set H=E[v v^T], B=I-H, A=E[v eta^T]. The hyperbolic Busemann identity Hess B_xi=I-v_xi v_xi^T and differentiation of the barycenter equation give EXACTLY B DF_s=s A. (2) Radial symmetry on the DOMAIN gives E[eta eta^T]=I/3, regardless of f. Hence matrix Cauchy--Schwarz gives AA^T<=H/3 and |Jac F_s| <= s^3/(3sqrt3) sqrt(det H)/det(I-H) <= (s/2)^3. (3) The last scalar inequality holds for nonnegative eigenvalues lambda_1+lambda_2+lambda_3=1. Its maximum is attained only when all lambdas=1/3. To check this without an external rigidity theorem, differentiate log[det(I-H)/sqrt(det H)] under that constraint. An interior critical point has at most two distinct eigenvalues; on (t,t,1-2t) the ratio is 2(1-t)^2/sqrt(1-2t), minimized uniquely at t=1/3. The boundary liminf is at least2, larger than 8/(3sqrt3); other boundary approaches have infinite ratio. For s in (2,3], the first two x-derivatives of nu_x^s have uniformly bounded total variation. Indeed derivatives of exp(-s d) cost bounded powers of s and at second order at most coth d. The radial integral of its 1/d singularity is finite. More explicitly, Z_s=8pi/[s(s^2-4)], E_radial[coth d]=s/2, so the second-derivative norm is at most 3s^2/2. This also justifies differentiating the radial integral and gives the local C^2 estimates used below whenever B is uniformly positive. No global Lipschitz bound for F_s is asserted. ## 2. Cusp control, retaining the potentially large axial shift Fix s>2 throughout this section; its constants need not be uniform as s decreases to2. Let x=(w,y) lie in a chosen deep lifted cusp horoball H={y>Y}. Its kernel mass outside H is bounded by zeta(y)<=C_s y^(-(s-2)). (4) This follows because the distance from x to the complement is log(y/Y), while the radial tail is bounded by C_s exp[-(s-2)log(y/Y)]. First physical-w derivatives of the entire kernel have total variation at most s/y, since the physical vector partial_w has hyperbolic norm1/y. ### Axis cusp with nonzero chi Conditioning the kernel on H gives a rotationally symmetric mixture of visual measures whose centers lie on the SAME target axis. At a target point with distance rho from the axis, every rotationally symmetric probability measure has outward radial Busemann derivative at least tanh(rho/2). This can be checked one azimuthal circle at a time: its averaged potential is log[(cosh rho+sqrt(cosh^2 rho-b^2 sinh^2 rho))/2], 0<=b<=1, whose radial derivative is minimized at b=1 and equals tanh(rho/2). The outside mass contributes a gradient of norm at most zeta. The barycenter equation therefore implies dist(F_s(w,y),axis)<=C_s zeta(y). (5) This conclusion does NOT require control of its axial displacement. Here is the needed axial estimate. Scale domain coordinates by w'=w+y u, y'=y v. The conditional axis-center coordinate is chi(w)+log y + y chi(u)+log v, and its density in (u,v) is proportional to exp[-s d((0,1),(u,v))] du dv/v^3, v>Y/y. (6) The distribution of the center coordinate divided by y converges to that of chi(u). Its latter density is continuous, symmetric and strictly positive near zero. These facts follow by integrating the positive density in (6); tails are integrable because s>2. For clarity, the visual average of the Busemann potential on an axis at distance t from its visual center is h(t)=t coth t-1, h'(t)=coth t-t csch^2 t, h''(t)=2 csch^2 t(t coth t-1)>0. (7) Its derivative tends to the sign function. Thus the axial force of the conditioned measure, evaluated at chi(w)+log y+y a, converges to the strictly increasing median-force function of chi(u), uniformly on a small fixed a-interval. Equation (5) and the full barycenter equation imply that its axial force at the actual F_s is O(zeta). Explicitly, compare at the nearest axis point by radial parallel transport: the Busemann gradient has derivative norm at most1, and the normalized axial unit vectors differ by O(rho). Thus (5) changes that force component by only O(zeta). Consequently the actual axial coordinate lies in that central interval for all sufficiently large y. There is a quantitative lower bound which is stronger than a formal perturbation claim. Restrict v to [1,2], the coordinate of u orthogonal to chi to a fixed compact interval, and chi(u) to the interval of width2/y placing the axis center within distance1 of the actual axial coordinate. On this compact part of (6) the density is bounded below. It therefore has mass at least c_s/y. By (5), every such visual center is within target distance2 of F_s. Its visual measure has density bounded below by a fixed positive multiple of mu_(F_s). Since the visual average of Hess Busemann at its own basepoint is (2/3)I, B(F_s(w,y)) >= (c_s/y) I. (8) This bound survives arbitrary coupling of axial and transverse derivatives: it is a lower bound on the WHOLE Hessian, not just one diagonal entry. Combining (8), (2), and the raw physical-w kernel derivative bound gives ||partial_(w_j) F_s|| <= C_s. (9) One can also recover an axial displacement O(zeta y) relative to the conditioned axial barycenter from (7), but it need not tend to zero and is not used in (8)--(9). In particular this argument does not compare an O(zeta) perturbation to an O(1/y) gap as if it were small. In Fermi coordinates (rho,theta,t) about the target axis the invariant primitive of hyperbolic volume is beta_ax=(1/2)sinh^2 rho dtheta wedge dt, ||beta_ax||=(1/2)tanh rho. (10) It is invariant under every axial translation and rotation, and is smooth across the axis. Equations(5),(9) imply integral_(fundamental cusp torus at y)|F_s^*beta_ax| <=C_s zeta(y)->0. (11) ### Central axis and parabolic cusps When chi=0, after translating the target by log y, the conditioned measure converges in total variation to the mixture of visual measures at gamma(log v) with the full density(6). It has full support and a strictly positive barycenter Hessian. The outside mass tends to zero, so barycenters and Hessians converge in this normalization. Therefore the physical-w derivatives are O_s(1/y). The flux(11) again vanishes. For a parabolic cusp the same scaling changes f(w+y u,y v) to (A u,v) after the target translation by A w and dilation by y. The conditioned measure converges in total variation to the fixed full-support mixture at (A u,v). Its barycenter is at a fixed positive height and its Hessian is positive. The outside mass is o(1), so the full barycenter stays near it in scaled coordinates. In particular ||partial_(w_j)F_s||=O_s(1/y). The invariant primitive beta_par=-(1/2)height^-2 dx_1 wedge dx_2, ||beta_par||=1/2 then gives a cusp-torus flux O_s(y^-2). This includes rank-deficient A. The continuity used in these two normalized cases is elementary: the fixed nonatomic limit assigns mass less than1/8 to all sufficiently small spherical caps. Total-variation convergence makes their masses less than1/4 uniformly. The Busemann potentials are then uniformly proper by the same ray estimate as in section1, confining their barycenters to a compact set. On that set the potentials and their fixed derivatives converge; strict convexity gives the asserted barycenter and Hessian convergence. ### Identification of the integral The absolute Jacobian bound(3) makes F_s^*vol integrable. Compare it to the original cusp-adapted f on a truncated core using an equivariant homotopy. On each cusp the target volume form has the invariant primitive just displayed. The boundary homotopy integral is exactly the difference of the two primitive fluxes; paired fundamental sides cancel by invariance. Both fluxes tend to zero by (11) and its parabolic version, and by the explicit original f. Stokes therefore proves, separately for EACH fixed s>2, integral_X F_s^*vol = Vol(rho). (12) No limit in s was exchanged with a cusp estimate. Combining(3) and(12) gives directly, for every s>2, |Vol(rho)| <= (s/2)^3 Vol(X). Letting s decrease to2 proves the non-strict bound used here. Thus this note does not depend on the old smearing proof of that inequality; the linked peripheral note supplies the canonical regulator-volume normalization and the original cusp-adapted map. ## 3. Equality forces an isometric limit and excludes a kernel Assume Vol(rho)=Vol(X)>0 and take s_j decreasing to2. Equations(3),(12) give the nonnegative deficit integral_X [(s_j/2)^3-Jac F_(s_j)] =[(s_j/2)^3-1]Vol(X) ->0. (13) On any fixed compact ball there are points x_j tending along a subsequence to x_0 with Jac F_(s_j)(x_j)->1. The strict maximum in (3) forces H(x_j)->I/3. Moreover AA^T<=H/3 and (2) imply that all singular values of DF_(s_j)(x_j) tend to1; their product has positive sign. This uses no assumed convergence of rho or of the map values. Postcompose each map by a target isometry sending F_(s_j)(x_j) to one fixed point. Call the maps G_j. A kernel element of rho still acts trivially on EVERY G_j, even though these normalizing isometries can diverge. We only need this kernel-invariance, not convergence of the conjugated representations. There is one fixed source radius on which the G_j have uniform C^2 bounds. Indeed whenever B>=kappa I, equation(2) bounds DF by C/kappa; differentiating H bounds its derivative by C(1+||DF||). Starting at H near I/3, a fixed-radius bootstrap preserves B>=kappa. The uniform first and second measure-derivative bounds after(3), together with bounded target Busemann derivatives, then bound second derivatives of G_j. Arzela compactness gives a C^1 limit on that ball. On the ball the deficit tends to zero in L1 by(13), while C^1 compactness makes the Jacobians converge uniformly. The limiting Jacobian is1 everywhere. The strict matrix inequality in(3) now forces its derivative to be an orientation-preserving isometry at every point. Thus the limit is a local hyperbolic isometry. This convergence propagates across any fixed finite chain of overlapping source balls. At a point in the known overlap, uniform Jacobian convergence again forces H_j->I/3, so the same bootstrap opens the next ball with the same radius and bounded target values. Finite covers of paths, then a diagonal exhaustion, give a global local-isometry limit G_infinity:H^3->H^3. Equivalently, its initially fixed local isometry extends uniquely along paths; H^3 is simply connected and complete, so it is a global isometry. If gamma is in ker(rho), then G_j(gamma x)=G_j(x) exactly. Choose a compact path from x to gamma x and pass to this same limit. The global isometry would satisfy G_infinity(gamma x)=G_infinity(x), forcing gamma=1. This proves(1). Reducible escape cannot evade the argument: target normalization was explicit and kernel-invariance survives it. Negative maximal volume is handled by a fixed target orientation reversal before the construction. ## 4. The actual regular-smoothing corollary Suppose a nonempty set of untwisted crossing-circle components of the original connected certified augmented exterior X is deleted by the literal identity smoothing, and the resulting connected diagram has its OWN positive labeled right-angled certificate. Retain every remaining half twist and the original peripheral labels. Let Y be that actual complete smoothed exterior. Its core source capacity is Vol(Y)/(2pi), by the independently proved face-coefficient and coning normalization. No abstract existence theorem supplies this certificate. For example, when the entire literal smoothed white cellulation is one simple triangulated sphere with at least four vertices, the [capacity-block construction](actual_smoothed_source_capacity_blocks.md), section4, supplies exactly this labeled certificate by its proved Hall, disk-development, and supporting-halfspace argument. The topological operation is meridional Dehn filling of precisely the deleted crossing-circle components: their original crossing disks fix the slope, and the untwisted physical strands keep their original pairing. Compose the induced quotient pi_1(X)->pi_1(Y) with the actual complete holonomy of Y. This representation rho has nontrivial kernel: each deleted meridian was an essential nontrivial parabolic in the original certified complete exterior, and becomes trivial after filling. Its absolute representation volume is EXACTLY Vol(Y), with the same orientation. To check the normalization, first replace the axis cusp map gamma(chi(w)+log y) on each filled cusp by gamma(chi(w)), using an axis-valued homotopy and a collar. Its boundary homotopy has zero 3-volume, so the representation volume is unchanged. Unlike the old log y map, the new map extends continuously over the filled solid torus by its longitude core map. The extension has rank at most one and contributes zero volume. It does not require that the image core curve be embedded or even nontrivial. A filled core image may instead be parabolic. Because the killed meridian is in its kernel, its real-linear translation map A has rank at most one. Replace the cusp map (A w,y) by (A w,1). The vertical homotopy lies in the vertical plane over that one translation line, so its rank is at most two and its 3-volume is zero. The new map extends over the filled solid torus by the rank-one longitude map along that horocycle. A central image is included by taking A=0. Thus the same zero-volume filling-cap argument covers every possible commuting peripheral image of the actual quotient. On the remaining cusps keep the actual complete parabolic markings and their conical maps. The extended map from the filled topological exterior to Y induces the identity on its fundamental group and agrees with the actual peripheral homotopy classes. Since the universal cover of Y is contractible, it is properly homotopic to the actual identification with Y, using the conical maps on the remaining ends. It therefore has degree one. Integration of the target volume form, or Stokes on truncated cores followed by the already proved vanishing horospherical boundary terms, gives Vol(rho)=Vol(Y). Applying(1) and the bound just proved now yields the STRICT comparison Phi_sm=Vol(Y)/(2pi)<Vol(X)/(2pi)=Phi_old. (14) This needs neither a balanced split nor the original packing variables to remain fixed. At the attained smoothed packing the gap is positive. Replacing its marked zero variables by sufficiently small fixed positive ones preserves a strict gap, with their target exponents still zero. For a single port, the [actual polynomial small-circle insertion](actual_small_circle_polynomial_face_insertion.md) therefore gives the corresponding full-source small-h upper gap with cost C^(h-1). For a connected untwisted subset covered by the [simultaneous polynomial correspondence](actual_simultaneous_small_circle_face_correspondence.md), the cost is product C_i^(h_i-1), including protected outgoing faces and dependency cycles. These are applications of that exact source theorem; disconnected smoothings and signed small ports remain outside this corollary. ## 5. Scope still needed for degenerate smoothing To apply this geometric strictness result to the actual smoothed capacity one must construct a representation of the ORIGINAL complete source group whose volume is the sum of the proved capacity blocks, and show that the actual essential deleted crossing meridian lies in its kernel. For a connected certified hyperbolic smoothed exterior this is the literal filling quotient and its marked volume normalization. For a degenerate block decomposition it still requires the actual gluing/peripheral argument. No quantum source product or unproved JSJ identification is substituted here. ## 6. Literature coverage and validation Maximal representation-volume rigidity is established territory. The abstract of [Francaviglia, *Hyperbolic volume of representations of fundamental groups of cusped 3-manifolds*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0305275) states a stronger discrete-and-faithful conclusion at maximal volume. That reference is coverage and attribution only. The construction, matrix bound, cusp-flux control, and kernel-exclusion argument above are supplied here rather than importing that theorem's proof. No novelty claim is made for natural-map volume rigidity. Primary full analytical review: PASS, including the nonperturbative axial quantile estimate, whole-Hessian lower bound, fixed-s cusp-volume identification, matrix maximum, and propagation of the normalized local isometry limit, together with the actual filling-cap normalization in section4. Independent full analytical review: PASS. The reviewer checked the same map and cusp arguments, the kernel-preserving target normalization, and both the axial and rank-one parabolic filling-cap cases. The regular smoothing source corollary retains its exact certificate, marking, and untwisted polynomial-insertion hypotheses. Neither a degenerate block sum representation nor a signed-small-port quantum bound is inferred. No finite numerical test is used as a substitute for these analytic arguments.

title: A uniform representation-volume gap for fixed peripheral words
text: # A uniform representation-volume gap for fixed peripheral words 30 October 2026. This extends the supplied [natural-map proof](general_representation_volume_kernel_strictness.md) to a varying sequence of representations. No quantum source estimate follows from this geometric statement alone. Let X=Gamma\H^3 be the fixed oriented finite-volume complete hyperbolic exterior, with its fixed marked complete PSL2 holonomy iota. For each n let rho_n:Gamma->SL2(C), followed by its PSL2 action, and let Vol(rho_n) have the same canonical peripheral-regulator normalization as in that note. Then Vol(rho_n) -> Vol(X) implies, after passing to a subsequence and conjugating by orientation-preserving target isometries g_n, that g_n rho_n(gamma) g_n^-1 -> iota(gamma) (1) for every fixed gamma in Gamma, with one common conjugation and the actual marking. A fixed final conjugation is absorbed into g_n. For absolute volumes tending to Vol(X), pass to a constant-sign subsequence; the limit is either iota or its orientation-reversed conjugate. ## Proof with nonuniform cusp data Choose any s_n>2 tending to2. For rho_n choose its own cusp-adapted map f_n and its natural map F_n=F_(s_n,f_n). The cusp estimates are used separately at the fixed pair (s_n,rho_n), and prove exactly integral_X Jac F_n = Vol(rho_n). No uniform cusp constants, uniform cusp truncation, or exchange of a cusp limit with n is needed. The radial construction, however, gives uniform INTERIOR estimates independent of f_n: |Jac F_n| <= (s_n/2)^3, AA^T <= H/3, (I-H) DF_n=s_n A, ||D_x nu_n||_TV <= s_n, ||D_x^2 nu_n||_TV <= 3s_n^2/2. The latter bounds differentiate only the domain radial kernel. Therefore integral_X [(s_n/2)^3-Jac F_n] ->0. (2) This is a nonnegative deficit. On any fixed compact lifted ball it tends to zero in L1 as well: the projection has bounded finite multiplicity on that ball. Choose points with Jacobians tending to1. The strict matrix inequality forces H->I/3 and all singular values of DF_n to1 there. Normalize their target images by orientation-preserving isometries g_n. The same fixed-radius Hessian bootstrap as in the frozen note now gives uniform C2 bounds near those points: positivity of I-H controls DF_n; its first variation is bounded by C(1+||DF_n||), and the uniform second measure derivative controls D2F_n. A C1 subsequential limit has Jacobian1 everywhere by (2). The strict matrix inequality forces its derivative to be an orientation-preserving isometry. This convergence propagates along finite chains of overlapping fixed-radius balls; target values in the new ball stay bounded by the known overlap and derivative bound. A diagonal exhaustion gives G_n=g_n F_n -> G_infinity locally in C1 on H^3, where G_infinity is a global orientation-preserving hyperbolic isometry. This construction does not assume compactness or irreducibility of the representations and does not claim that the normalizing g_n are bounded. It remains to use the equivariance, rather than only kernel invariance. Set rho'_n=g_n rho_n g_n^-1. For every fixed gamma and x, rho'_n(gamma) G_n(x)=G_n(gamma x). (3) Choose four fixed source points whose G_infinity-images are noncoplanar. Both sets of points in (3) converge. The isometries rho'_n(gamma) are precompact: their values at one fixed target point are bounded, because that point is o(1) from G_n(x), and the stabilizer of a point is compact. Every limiting isometry sends the four G_infinity(x)-points to their G_infinity(gamma x)-images. These determine an isometry uniquely, so rho'_n(gamma) -> G_infinity iota(gamma) G_infinity^-1. Absorb G_infinity^-1 in the common g_n. This proves (1) simultaneously for every fixed gamma; it also suffices to check a finite generating set. The SL2 central signs need not stabilize, and are immaterial for trace squared. No assertion about their lift is made. ## Uniform peripheral gap in the marked finite-dimensional problem Fix finitely many actual peripheral words m_1,...,m_b and delta>0. Suppose each iota(m_i) is parabolic or central, so tr^2 iota(m_i)=4. Then there is g=g(X,{m_i},delta)>0 such that EVERY actual SL2 representation satisfying max_i |tr^2 rho(m_i)-4| >= delta has |Vol(rho)| <= Vol(X)-g. (4) Otherwise a sequence violating every positive gap would have absolute volumes tending to Vol(X). Apply the proved compactness statement, passing to a constant-sign subsequence. Trace squared is continuous and conjugacy-invariant; its value at every selected word would tend to4 in either orientation, contradicting the fixed delta. This proof supplies a positive gap, not an effective numerical value. For a physical peripheral eigenvalue m=e^(pi i chi) with real chi, |tr^2 rho(m_i)-4|=4 sin^2(pi chi). Thus a selected real color parameter a fixed distance from the integer aliases meets (4), IF it is the eigenvalue of an actual representation whose volume controls the relevant source period. The latter implication is NOT proved here: it requires the source action, its cycle, its upper bound, and cancellation of all ordinary complementary terms to be established separately. This statement is not a bound on F_N or L_h. The fixed finite set is essential. One cannot take a supremum over ALL peripheral words whose exponents are allowed to grow with n: powers of a near-parabolic element may have trace far from ±2. The actual finite set of marked crossing-circle meridians is within the theorem's scope. ## Validation and scope Root full analytical review: PASS. The review checked the uniform interior measure estimates despite varying cusp maps, the fixed-pair volume identity, normalized isometry propagation, the use of exact equivariance to recover the marked character, and the finite-fixed-word quantifier. No numerical test substitutes for this analytic argument. The source action/period upper bound and the complementary-color cancellation remain separate requirements. Independent full analytical review: PASS. The reviewer checked the fixed-pair cusp normalization versus representation-independent interior estimates, the propagated isometric limit, convergence of the conjugated isometries from four noncoplanar points, and the fixed finite peripheral quantifier. The absolute-volume orientation alternative and the source limitations remain explicit. The theorem is frozen after these reviews.

title: Volume equality for the original signed augmented source
text: # Volume equality for the original signed augmented source 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. This note proves a uniform relative folded-channel estimate from the ORIGINAL finite continuants, then sums the actual half-twist phases. It concerns a fixed connected certified right-angled augmented diagram, at arbitrary fixed bridge width, through both parities and all sufficiently large levels. The external crossing-circle colors needed for long fillings are not the internal channels estimated here. ## 1. Exact source and statement Use the labeled geometric certificate and original marked normalization of the [untwisted theorem](general_untwisted_augmented_source_volume.md). Let R be the number of crossing circles, d=N-1, M=floor(d/2), and s0=d-2M in {0,1}. Retain any fixed vector of actual half twists epsilon_i in {0,1,-1}, and the separately specified exterior framing unit chi_(D,N). Write Y_D^epsilon for the certified complete augmented exterior with those recorded face pairings. Its volume is 2Vol(Q_D), unchanged by the half-twist pairings. The [exact marked coefficient identity](actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.md) is A_(D,N)^epsilon = chi_(D,N) N^R sum_(0<=a_i<=M) product_i[k_ai omega_ai^epsilon_i] F_N(a), F_N(a)=product_i beta_ai^2 * C_(N,a), (1) where C_(N,a) is the specified nonnegative face coefficient of product_i[D_ai,in D_ai,out P_(d-2ai)]. The two marked faces are set to zero; all the other face variables are shared. Here beta_a=S_(2a)/S_a^2, S_j=product_(r=1)^j 2sin(pi r/N), omega_a=q^(d^2/2)(-1)^a q^[a(a+1)], q=exp(pi i/N), k_a=1 if 2a=d, and k_a=2 otherwise. No trace normal is missing from (1): the original complete-circle coefficient is already included in these factors. This is the root complete source identity, not a differentiation of an off-grid root formula or a statement about individual generic-q normals. Let l_N be the unique positive critical radius of the all-maximal coefficient, with one finite face radius fixed by homogeneity. The [global coefficient theorem](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md) gives l_N -> l^geom. For circle i, let (x_i,b_i,c_i,y_i) be its actual four face radii at l_N, including the prescribed zeros, and put A_i=x_i+y_i, C_i(l_N)=pi[ sqrt(b_i A_i+x_i y_i) +sqrt(c_i A_i+x_i y_i)]/A_i, Z_i,N=C_i(l_N)-pi i epsilon_i. (2) The actual zero patterns have A_i>0 and C_i>0. All their positive coordinates stay in compact sets, so Re Z_i,N has a uniform positive lower bound. Each square root of Z_i,N below has positive real part. We prove the stronger asymptotic A_(D,N)^epsilon =chi_(D,N) N^R F_N(M,...,M) product_i omega_M^epsilon_i *(pi N)^(R/2) product_i Z_i,N^(-1/2) *[1+o(1)]. (3) In particular the original signed source is nonzero for all sufficiently large N, and lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N) log|A_(D,N)^epsilon| =2Vol(Q_D)=Vol(Y_D^epsilon). (4) All quantifiers hold for each fixed connected diagram with its actual nondegenerate labeled certificate; the diagram does not grow with N. Neither one main component nor a restricted graph grammar is required. The statement includes signed complete augmented link exteriors, including those whose main strands form one component, that satisfy the certificate. It does not assert the volume limit after independently long Dehn fillings of the crossing circles. ## 2. An endpoint-safe recurrence for the normalized determinant For one actual triangle write D_a(x,b,y)=det[bI+(x/2)H_-+(y/2)H_+], Z_a^b=beta_a D_a(x,b,y), e_a=Z_a^b/Z_(a-1)^b, A=x+y>0, theta=pi/N. The original tridiagonal entries and sine products give EXACTLY e_1=A+2b cos(theta), e_a=(1+tau_a)[A+2b cos(a theta)cos((a-1)theta)] -tau_a[A^2-4xy cos^2((a-1)theta)]/e_(a-1), tau_a=tan((a-1)theta)/tan(a theta), 2<=a<=M. (5) For clarity, beta_a/beta_(a-1) equals sin((2a-1)theta)sin(2a theta)/sin^2(a theta). Multiplying the literal continuant recurrence by this ratio gives (5); its off-diagonal product becomes tau_a times the displayed quadratic. No matrix of virtual size beyond M is used. Since 0<=tau_a<1 and 0<=4xy<=A^2, induction in (5) proves A<=e_a<=2A+4b. (6) If T_b=sqrt(bA+xy)=0, necessarily b=0 and xy=0, and e_a=A identically. This single-variable case is retained separately. In every other fixed zero pattern T_b/A is bounded above and below by positive constants on the positive radius compact. Set k=N/2-a, so k_min=N/2-M=(s0+1)/2, and set E_k=e_a/A, lambda_b=2pi T_b/A, E_k^*=exp(lambda_b k/N). Then (5) becomes, with tau=tan(k theta)/tan((k+1)theta), E_k=(1+tau)[1+(2b/A)sin(k theta)sin((k+1)theta)] -tau[1-(4xy/A^2)sin^2((k+1)theta)]/E_(k+1). (7) Choose a sufficiently small fixed delta0>0. Substituting E^* in (7), its residual R_k satisfies uniformly for k_min<=k<=2delta0 N |R_k|<=C[k/N^2+k^3/N^3]. (8) Here is the cancellation behind this estimate. Uniform Taylor expansion gives tau=k/(k+1)+O(k/N^2). The two terms linear in k/N cancel. The quadratic k^2/N^2 terms cancel because lambda_b^2=4pi^2(b/A+xy/A^2). The finite k+1 offset leaves an O(k/N^2) term, which must not be dropped; the remaining Taylor terms are O(k^3/N^3). Taylor remainders are uniform when k theta is in the stated small compact interval, including k=1/2 and k=1. This approximate solution selects the actual positive solution without an asymptotic boundary condition. Start at k0 in [2delta0 N-2,2delta0 N] on the actual integer or half-integer lattice. By (6) both E_k0 and E_k0^* are bounded. Subtracting (7) for the two sequences gives an error recurrence with nonnegative multiplier K_k=tau[1-(4xy/A^2)sin^2((k+1)theta)] /(E_(k+1)E_(k+1)^*) <=tau exp[-lambda_b(k+1)/N]. The exact telescope of the tau factors therefore bounds propagation from j to k by P_kj<=C(k/j) exp[-c(j^2-k^2)/N]. (9) For k<=delta0 N the starting error is exponentially small, because the recurrence was started at twice this cutoff. Summing (8) with (9) gives |E_k-E_k^*|<=C[N^-1+k^2/N^2]+Ce^(-cN), |log(e_a/A)-lambda_b k/N| <=C[N^-1+k^2/N^2]+Ce^(-cN). (10) Indeed the residual sum is at most Ck sum_(j>=k) exp[-c(j^2-k^2)/N](N^-2+j^2/N^3). For k<=sqrt(N), comparison with Gaussian integrals bounds it by Ck/N^(3/2)<=C/N. For k>=sqrt(N), write j=k+l and use j^2-k^2>=2kl to obtain C[N^-1+k^2/N^2]. This proves (10) at both physical fold endpoints. The exact constant case T_b=0 satisfies it with zero error. ## 3. The original circle has a relative folded packet For t=M-a>=0, the t removed pivots have k=k_min,...,k_min+t-1, hence sum k=t(t+s0)/2. Summing (10), Z_(M-t)^b/Z_M^b =A^(-t) exp[-pi T_b t(t+s0)/(AN)] *exp[O(t/N+t^3/N^2)]. (11) The original forced product changes by the EXACT paired factors P_(s0+2t)(x,y)/P_s0(x,y) =product_(k=k_min)^(k_min+t-1) [A^2-4xy sin^2(k theta)] =A^(2t) exp[O(t^3/N^2)]. (12) Combining the two triangles, the powers of A cancel. With B_(N,a)=beta_a^2 D_a(x,b,y)D_a(x,c,y)P_(d-2a)(x,y), log[B_(N,M-t)/B_(N,M)] =-C(x,b,c,y)t(t+s0)/N+O(t/N+t^3/N^2), C=pi(T_b+T_c)/A>0. (13) This is uniform on the stated radius compacts for 0<=t<=delta0 N. For any fixed 0<delta<1/6, it is a relative 1+o(1) packet uniformly for t<=N^(1/2+delta). Choosing delta0 smaller if necessary also gives B_(N,M-t)/B_(N,M)<=C0 exp[-c0 t^2/N] (0<=t<=delta0 N). (14) The O(t/N) term in (13) is absorbed by a constant plus a small multiple of t^2/N; the cubic term is absorbed by choosing delta0. No limiting-rate error has been used as a relative estimate. We also need finite radius derivatives, but not derivatives of the sharp error (10). For any actual principal matrix M_j at real positive radii, a fixed sufficiently small complex logarithmic radius change gives M_j(z)=M_j(0)^(1/2)(I+E)M_j(0)^(1/2), ||E||<1/4 uniformly j,N. This follows from its sum of positive semidefinite radius summands; zero faces stay zero. If v=M_j(0)^(-1/2)e_last, the ratio of the last inverse entries is v^*(I+E)^(-1)v/(v^*v)=1+O(||E||), uniformly even when M_j is ill-conditioned. Its reciprocal is the ratio of the original Schur pivots. Thus the marked logarithm of each pivot ratio is uniformly bounded on this polydisc. Cauchy estimates give all fixed logarithmic radius derivatives O(1). The paired factors in (12) have the same property near the fold. Consequently partial_z^j log[B_(N,M-t)/B_(N,M)]=O_j(t), j>=1, (15) uniformly there. This is a finite matrix estimate, including the single-variable and both maximal-fold cases. ## 4. Transfer from shared-radius values to actual coefficients Use the fixed n=R-1 log-radius gauge of the coefficient theorem. Put f_t(z)=log[product_i B_(N,M-ti)(l^geom exp z)]-d sum_f log l_f; the beta factors are constant in z. Let z_t be its unique positive critical radius, and z_0 that of the all-maximal vector. For max t_i<=N^(1/2+delta), the global coefficient theorem supplies both critical points in the same fixed neighborhood, with Hessians between cN and CN, fixed higher derivatives O(N), and its relative O(N^-1) coefficient formula uniformly. Its hypotheses hold since sum s_i=o(N). Write A_t=sum_i t_i(t_i+s0)/N, eta_t=C sum_i(t_i/N+t_i^3/N^2). Equation (13), uniformly on a real neighborhood, says f_t(z)-f_0(z) =-sum_i C_i(z)t_i(t_i+s0)/N+error, |error|<=eta_t. (16) The C_i have bounded first derivatives. Comparing the minimum of f_t with its value at z_0 and using the strong convexity of f_0 gives |z_t-z_0|<=C[A_t/N+sqrt(eta_t/N)], f_t(z_t)-f_0(z_0) =-sum_i C_i(z_0)t_i(t_i+s0)/N +O(eta_t+A_t^2/N). (17) For example, the lower comparison is obtained by completing the square in cN|z-z_0|^2-C A_t|z-z_0|-eta_t, while the upper comparison uses z=z_0. This argument does not differentiate the remainder in (16). By (15) and the O(N) third derivatives of f_0, the Hessians at their respective minima differ by O(sum_i t_i)+O(N|z_t-z_0|). Their determinant ratio therefore tends to1 uniformly in this window. For delta<1/6, eta_t=o(1), A_t^2/N=o(1), and the displacement in (17) is o(1). Restoring the uniform relative coefficient formulas yields the actual finite-source sector ratio F_N(M-t_1,...,M-t_R)/F_N(M,...,M) =exp[-sum_i C_i(l_N)t_i(t_i+s0)/N] *[1+o(1)] (18) uniformly on the whole stated window. All beta/CD normalization, the two physical fold offsets and the shared radius constraints have been retained. There is no continuous-color interpolation assumption. ## 5. The full signed channel sum, including its tails The original finite half-twist has the exact ratio omega_(M-t)/omega_M=exp[pi i t(t+s0)/N]. (19) Its (-1)^a factor cancels the apparent nearest-node alternation; it cannot be discarded before expanding the quadratic exponent. Multiply (18) by (19) and retain k_a from (1). If N is odd, k_M=1 and all other k_a=2, giving the full integer Gaussian. If N is even all k_a=2 and t(t+1)=(t+1/2)^2-1/4, giving the full half-integer Gaussian. In either case, uniformly for Z in compact subsets of Re Z>0, sum_(t>=0) k_(M-t) exp[-Z t(t+s0)/N] =sqrt(pi N)/sqrt(Z) *[1+o(1)], (20) where the notation on the left extends the corresponding multiplicity pattern to the infinite Gaussian lattice. This follows directly by the real Riemann sum for exp(-Zx^2), with Gaussian tail domination; the integral is sqrt(pi)/sqrt(Z) by analytic continuation from Z>0. The even factor exp(Z/4N) tends to1. Truncation at the window of (18) has exponentially small Gaussian tails. The uniform o(1) in (18) causes o(N^(R/2)) absolute error in the normalized signed sum, since its absolute Gaussian majorant has that order. The product of the nonzero integrals in (20) has order N^(R/2) with a fixed positive lower bound on its modulus after normalization. This proves a nonzero signed leading coefficient on the window. It remains to justify deleting every other original channel. Evaluate each positive coefficient at the SAME all-maximal critical radius l_N. The central coefficient formula gives, with n=R-1, F_N(M-t)/F_N(M) <=C N^(n/2) product_i[B_(N,M-ti)(l_N)/B_(N,M)(l_N)]. (21) When all t_i<=delta0 N but some t_i>N^(1/2+delta), (14) makes the right side at most a polynomial times exp(-cN^(2delta)). The polynomial number of labels and their bounded k factors are harmless. The proof of (14) started at 2delta0 N, so no unresolved initial continuant error remains at this mesoscopic cutoff. If some t_i>delta0 N, the [uniform all-channel common-radius theorem](actual_positive_face_channel_rate.md) gives a strict macroscopic rate gap, uniformly at l_N -> l^geom. All other circle rates are bounded above by their fold values. Dividing by the central coefficient, whose rate is the same fold value, leaves exp(-cN+o(N)); again the number of labels is polynomial. All phases have modulus1. Thus neither tail affects the window's leading coefficient. Equations (18)--(21) establish (3). Finally the [absolute source coning anchor](actual_original_boundary_stationary_character.md) and the central coefficient theorem give N^-1 log F_N(M,...,M) -> Vol(Y_D^epsilon)/(2pi). Every additional factor in (3) is polynomial or a unit, and its displayed Gaussian product is nonzero. This proves (4). ## 6. Scope and verification This closes cancellation of the retained half-twist phases for the ORIGINAL complete augmented source under the stated general geometric certificate. It uses the exact marked compact-torus coefficient, not an assumed geometric intersection number or an independently normalized local thimble. The distinct external-color packet and its aliases needed to pass to independently long filled knots remain unproved by this theorem. No whole-source generic-q normal or growing-diagram uniformity is claimed. Focused audit: [original signed finite sources and folded factors](../experiments/audit_general_signed_augmented_source_volume.py), with [saved results](../experiments/general_signed_augmented_source_volume_results.json). At 90 digits it checks 1260 original normalized pivots, 280 direct original determinants, 180 exact single-summand pivots, 756 forced pairs and 756 circle ratios, 108 literal half-twist ratios and their fold multiplicities, and 476 complex-radius pivot comparisons. Ten whole original W/pi source sums at bridge widths two and three are compared with the independently summed face coefficients, retaining all phases, physical cups and the original marked cap. These finite source fixtures are normalization tests, not geometric certificates; their possible zeros do not assert a failure of the theorem's nondegenerate certificate hypothesis. Forty all-channel tetrahedral signed sums and 168 local folded packets are asymptotic diagnostics. The uniform estimates and noncancellation are proved above. Two independent full analytical reviews: PASS. The readers checked the literal source normalization and common half-twist phase, endpoint-safe continuant, uniform residual and contraction, shared-radius minimum and Hessian comparison, both exact channel lattices, signed Gaussian and both tail ranges. Independent full audit-code read and fresh redirected 90-digit replay: PASS, reproducing every recorded count and maximum exact relative error below 1.2e-89. The conclusion is the stated complete signed augmented-link equality; external filling colors remain separate.

title: A general source-regulator equality theorem and its exact quantum scope
text: # A general source-regulator equality theorem and its exact quantum scope 29 October 2026. The geometric equality step extends to EVERY oriented complete finite-volume cusped hyperbolic three-manifold. No pretzel, alternating, bridge-width, polyhedral, or positive ideal-triangulation hypothesis is required. The proof below constructs the nearby local geometry explicitly by equivariant averages, rather than assuming a general deformation or Dehn filling theorem. This does NOT extend the proved original-source asymptotic to every knot. Section8 identifies the additional quantum hypotheses, their proved pretzel instance, and the currently missing broader source estimates. Neither a formal saddle nor a correct cusp Hessian supplies those inputs. ## 1. General geometric completion theorem Let M be an oriented complete finite-volume hyperbolic three-manifold with h torus cusps and geometric holonomy rho0. Fix primitive oriented bases (mu_i,lambda_i) of its actual peripheral groups. On each torus fix the complete Euclidean cusp coordinate, so its two holonomies are translations by a real-linearly independent pair of complex numbers. There is a neighborhood U of the complete FRAMED representation with the following property. A point of U consists of an actual representation rho: pi1(M) -> PSL(2,C) and, for each cusp, a common peripheral fixed flag close to its complete flag. Use a frame depending continuously on that flag to send it to infinity. The peripheral transformations are then complex similarities. Let U_i,V_i be the uniquely small logarithms of the complex similarity multipliers of mu_i,lambda_i, continued from zero at completeness. Select any subset F of cusps to fill. Suppose: 1. Every unfilled peripheral group is parabolic, so BOTH similarity multipliers are one. It remains nontrivial near rho0. 2. For each i in F, choose an arbitrary primitive integer pair (a_i,b_i) and a sign epsilon_i in {+1,-1}, and impose the ACTUAL log equation a_i U_i+b_i V_i=2pi i epsilon_i. (1) Then rho descends to the Dehn filling of M along the actual slopes sigma_i=a_i mu_i+b_i lambda_i. The descended representation is the holonomy of a positively oriented COMPLETE finite-volume hyperbolic metric on that filled topology. In particular it is discrete and faithful there. Any number of cusps may remain, including zero. The neighborhood U is fixed before the slopes: the conclusion applies to every slope tuple and framed representation satisfying these conditions inside U. It does NOT assert existence of such a representation for all slopes. Existence is supplied by the actual source branch in the proved application, and must be supplied in another application. For nearby representations, (1) itself forces the relevant slopes to be long. The proof is independent of a graph presentation and of any geometric triangulation existence theorem. Sections2--5 establish it directly. ## 2. A nearby equivariant developing map on every compact core Identify the universal cover of the complete M with H3, and write Gamma for pi1(M), acting by rho0. Choose a compact cusp-truncated core and a slightly larger compact collar. Cover that compact set by finitely many open balls which lift injectively to H3, and choose a smooth partition of unity subordinate to them. Write eta_(j,gamma) for the lifts using one chosen lift of the j-th ball. Thus sum_(j,gamma) eta_(j,gamma)(x)=1, eta_(j,gamma)(rho0(delta)x)=eta_(j,delta^-1 gamma)(x). The sum is locally finite. On a fixed compact fundamental part only finitely many gamma occur. No freeness of the deformed action is assumed. Use the future unit hyperboloid in Minkowski space for H3. Form Y_rho(x)=sum_(j,gamma) eta_(j,gamma)(x) rho(gamma) rho0(gamma)^-1 x, E_rho(x)=Y_rho(x)/sqrt(-<Y_rho(x),Y_rho(x)>). (2) Every summand is future timelike unit. A convex combination with nonnegative weights summing to one is future timelike, so normalization is defined. The Lorentz action of PSL(2,C) makes (2) unambiguous without choosing SL signs. Reindexing gamma gives exactly E_rho(rho0(delta)x)=rho(delta)E_rho(x). (3) At rho=rho0 every summand in (2) equals x, so E_rho0(x)=x.
