On the compact fundamental part, only finitely many matrices and derivatives of fixed smooth weights occur. Consequently E_rho tends to the identity in C1 as rho tends to rho0. For rho in one sufficiently small neighborhood, it is an orientation-preserving local diffeomorphism. Equivariance then gives this property over the whole lifted compact core and collar. This is the needed compact-core deformation proof. It uses neither an unproved compatible geodesic mesh nor a subdivision that could invert thin tetrahedra. It also does not assume local character-variety rigidity. ## 3. An explicit positive similarity link and an entire cusp tail In one complete cusp write its cover as (w,t) in C x [t0,infinity), (w,t) -> (w+lambda,t), lambda in Lambda, dev0(w,t)=(w,exp(t)), where Lambda is the complete translation lattice. In the moving selected flag frame, denote the deformed affine action by A_rho(lambda)(z)=a_lambda z+b_lambda. It is a homomorphism from Lambda to Aff(C), tends to the original translation action, and all a_lambda are nonzero. Choose a smooth compactly supported nonnegative function eta on C with sum_(lambda in Lambda) eta(w-lambda)=1. Such eta is obtained from any bump whose translates cover a fundamental parallelogram by dividing by its positive periodic translate sum. Define d_rho(w)=sum_lambda eta(w-lambda) A_rho(lambda)(w-lambda). (4) Affine maps commute with convex combinations of total weight one, so d_rho(w+nu)=A_rho(nu)d_rho(w). (5) At completeness every term is w. On a fixed compact fundamental domain, d_rho is C1-close to w; its real Jacobian is therefore positive and nonzero. Equivariance propagates this local-diffeomorphism property everywhere. Thus (4) gives a genuine nonsingular similarity structure on the COMPACT cusp torus, not just a formal list of peripheral matrices. The developed images and Euclidean lengths of fixed generator paths are uniformly bounded near completeness. Let chi_rho:C->R be the real-linear extension of the character lambda -> log|a_lambda|. The map F_rho(w,t)=(d_rho(w),exp(t+chi_rho(w))) (6) is exactly rho-equivariant in upper half-space: its horizontal and vertical coordinates transform by a_lambda z+b_lambda and |a_lambda|y. Its differential is triangular with positive determinant exp(t+chi_rho(w)) det_R Dd_rho(w). Hence it is an orientation-preserving local diffeomorphism for EVERY t>=t0. At completeness it is dev0. Restore the continuously varying flag frame when viewing (6) in the global target H3. Define it on one chosen lift of each disjoint cusp neighborhood and propagate by rho-equivariance to the other lifts. The exact peripheral equivariance makes the coset representative irrelevant, so this gives a well-defined map on the entire lifted end. On a fixed compact cusp collar it is C1-close to the original developing map. Interpolate E_rho and F_rho by the unique hyperbolic geodesic between their values, with a smooth Gamma-invariant cutoff in t. The interpolation is rho-equivariant and is C1-close to the identity on that compact collar. Thus it too is a positive local diffeomorphism after one further uniform shrink of U. Set it equal to E_rho on the compact part and F_rho on each deep tail. We have now constructed a global rho-equivariant developing LOCAL DIFFEOMORPHISM on the ideal-end-deleted original manifold. Pulling back the H3 metric yields an actual oriented curvature-minus-one metric. There are no polyhedral edge or vertex singularities to check: the map is a smooth local diffeomorphism everywhere at finite points. The construction is simultaneous at all finitely many cusps. It works on a single neighborhood of the complete framed representation, with no comparison between different deformation sizes or slopes. ## 4. The small multiplier logs are the actual log-link periods At a filled cusp (1) ensures at least one multiplier is nontrivial. Commutativity of affine peripheral maps implies that they have a common finite fixed point q in addition to infinity. For a generator with a!=1, this is q=b/(1-a). The two original generator translations are nonzero. As the representation approaches completeness, at least one such formula therefore gives |q|->infinity, uniformly over the small framed neighborhood with its parabolic locus removed. The image of an ENTIRE closed fundamental parallelogram under d_rho is uniformly bounded by the compact C1 estimate in section3. Fixed generator paths also have uniformly bounded developed images and Euclidean lengths. For U sufficiently small the whole parallelogram image misses q, including its interior, not only its boundary paths. Equivariance and the fact that every peripheral map fixes q then show that the ENTIRE development misses q. On the simply connected link cover choose f=Log(d_rho-q). The differential df is invariant under deck transformations and is invertible as a REAL two-dimensional differential: d_rho is a positive local diffeomorphism and the logarithm has nonzero complex derivative. Thus |df|^2 descends to a nonsingular Euclidean metric on the compact link torus. It is complete. Its lifted local isometry f is globally one-to-one onto C: lift every Euclidean line segment by completeness to get a covering of C, which is simply connected. Its periods therefore form an injective rank-two translation lattice. For each fixed generator path of length at most L and image in |d|<=R, |Delta f|<=L/(|q|-R) ->0. (7) The endpoint affine action gives exp(Delta_mu f)=exp(U) and similarly for V. Their differences are integer multiples of 2pi i. Both the actual increments in (7) and the prescribed small multiplier logs tend to zero, so these integers are EXACTLY zero in U: Delta_mu f=U, Delta_lambda f=V. (8) The neighborhood needed for (8) is independent of the slopes, because one first proves (8) for the FIXED basis before multiplying by a_i,b_i. No diagonalizing-frame singularity or hidden large winding is allowed. SL eigenvalue signs must first be centered to these projective geometric logs; an old longitude spin is not an extra geometric rotation. For completeness, q need not be bounded by the inverse of one chosen coordinate if that coordinate vanishes. Choose either generator with nonunit multiplier. Each numerator stays bounded away from zero, and max(|a_mu-1|,|a_lambda-1|) tends uniformly to zero. This proves the uniform |q|->infinity statement even when one generator is parabolic. ## 5. Primitive filling gives a complete smooth hyperbolic manifold Translate q to zero. Then d_rho=e^f. On the compact link quotient the positive function exp(t0+chi_rho(w))/|d_rho(w)-q| is bounded above: numerator and denominator transform by the same |a_lambda|. Thus the explicit end (6) contains the ENTIRE equivariant epigraph y>A|d-q| for some finite A. There is no unproved assumption that an abstract cusp link is realized by an actual full geometric end. About the axis 0--infinity put r=y/|d-q| and use R=asinh(1/r), theta=Im f, X=Re f+(1/2)log(1+r^2). Direct substitution into the upper-half-space metric gives ds^2=dR^2+cosh(R)^2 dX^2+sinh(R)^2 dtheta^2. (9) The epigraph contains the whole punctured tube 0<R<R0. A log period L acts by (X,theta)->(X+Re L,theta+Im L). By (1),(8), the actual primitive slope has period 2pi i epsilon. Choose integers c,d with ad-bc=1. Its complementary primitive period cU+dV has nonzero real part, since the log-link period lattice has real rank two. Adding R=0 in (9) is therefore an ordinary smooth hyperbolic solid torus, with meridian EXACTLY a mu+b lambda. The angular period is 2pi, not a multiple or a merely exponentiated relation. The affine holonomy of that meridian is the identity, since it has multiplier one and fixes both q and infinity. Thus rho descends to the actual filled fundamental group. Either epsilon sign changes the orientation of the meridian parameter, not the positive orientation of the metric. At an unfilled cusp all a_lambda=1. Formula (4) is an ordinary translation-equivariant local diffeomorphism. Its compact Euclidean link is complete, so its lifted development is the Euclidean plane. Here chi=0 and (6) contains a full horoball quotient: the cusp is complete and has finite volume. The remaining middle region is compact. The finitely many attached bounded-radius solid tori and the ordinary unfilled cusps prove that the whole filled metric is complete and finite-volume. Its complete universal developing cover is H3: lift geodesic segments under its complete local isometry to obtain a covering of simply connected H3. Consequently the descended holonomy is discrete and faithful. This proves the theorem in section1 without importing a deformation, Dehn filling, discrete-faithfulness, or character-uniqueness theorem. ## 6. Absolute regulator calibration for any such source branch Let rho_z now be an actual connected marked representation family near rho0, and use the small squared peripheral logs U_i,V_i above. The elementary marked Bloch boundary/fundamental-chain calculation used in [the general peripheral volume proof](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md) and [the source regulator proof](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) is independent of the diagram and number of cusps. In these coordinates it says d Vol(rho_z)=(1/2)sum_i [Re V_i dIm U_i -Re U_i dIm V_i]. (10) Here Vol(rho) is the absolute representation volume of the SAME oriented fundamental class and cusp eigenflags. One way to check the factor is to use eigenlogs u=U/2,v=V/2 (with their fixed central signs): the boundary is -2 sum M_i wedge lambda_i, so the Bloch--Wigner differential is 2 sum(Re v dIm u-Re u dIm v), exactly (10). Distinct boundary tori have zero mutual intersection pairing. No equal-color assumption enters. Suppose a holomorphic source potential F on this marked branch has dF=(1/2)sum_i V_i dU_i, Im F(0)=Vol(M). (11) These are hypotheses about the actual peripheral connection and its absolute COMPLETE anchor, not just about its Hessian. Define D_F=Im F-(1/2)sum_i Re U_i Im V_i. (12) Direct differentiation of (11) gives the right side of (10). Both functions equal Vol(M) at the complete point. Therefore throughout the connected marked branch D_F=Vol(rho_z). (13) This is an absolute identity. It does not reset logarithms on loops, splice different character lifts at a projected node, or infer a constant from a matching stationary polynomial. Nonzero spin terms must be retained when converting the literal source to the centered form (11); they cancel only in the paired expression (12). At an actual filled point from section1, the representation volume in (13) is the volume of its constructed complete geometric metric. If comparing with any other complete hyperbolic metric on the same marked oriented filled topology, apply the independently proved representation-volume inequality in BOTH directions. Their volumes are equal. No unproved equality case or imported rigidity theorem is needed to identify (13) with its usual hyperbolic volume. The finite filling-chain normalization is also diagram-independent: replace the old cusp map by its axis-valued comparison, whose shared conical boundary homotopy has volume O(Y^-2); then extend the SAME finite boundary triangulation through the solid torus with every vertex on that axis. All added tetrahedra have zero volume. This is the compatible construction in the cited peripheral/source proofs; putting only unrelated new vertices on the axis would not suffice. ## 7. Arbitrary primitive filling action, with the exact boundary term When a source branch has local U coordinates and (11), a primitive slope a_i mu_i+b_i lambda_i with b_i!=0 has filling potential F_sigma(U)=F(U)+sum_(i in F) [a_i U_i^2/(4b_i)-pi i epsilon_i U_i/b_i]. (14) Its U_i derivative is (a_i U_i+b_i V_i-2pi i epsilon_i)/(2b_i). At its stationary filling point and with unfilled cusps complete, Im F_sigma =Im F-(1/2)sum_(i in F) Re U_i Im V_i =Vol(rho)=Vol(M(sigma)). (15) Indeed Im V_i=(2pi epsilon_i-a_i Im U_i)/b_i, which proves (15) without deleting a complex endpoint term. Constants already known to be real do not affect (15), but remain in any exact period formula. If b=0, primitivity forces |a|=1 and (1) cannot occur with small U; there is therefore no omitted near-complete filling in this chart. Equivalently one may change the primitive basis and its potential. For the existing convention U=-z,V=-2ell,a=1,b=p, epsilon=-m, (14) is G(z)+(z-2pi i m)^2/(4p) up to a REAL constant. This recovers the exact chirp/source formula, including its factor two and its retained longitude spin. ## 8. The conditional QUANTUM bridge, and what is actually proved The geometric theorem is unconditional for every actual framed representation satisfying section1. To prove the volume conjecture for a new original knot/source family one must additionally prove: * An exact original-source construction or selected-cycle argument supplies the ACTUAL near-complete representation of the base group, with the literal caps, all port equations, chosen eigenflags and true primitive preferred peripheral markings. * The selected parameter point exists in the fixed neighborhood, with all unfilled cusps complete and the actual small log equations (1) with unit charges. An exponentiated equation alone is insufficient. * The source action has the calibrated derivative and complete constant (11), and its filling kernel has the boundary correction (14) in the same convention. * The COMPLETE original finite source has a nonzero asymptotic contribution with exponential action F_sigma/(2pi i), with all other terms controlled. In particular its scalar has the form K_N=exp[N F_sigma/(2pi i)] A_N, (1/N)log|A_N| ->0, (16) after the recorded original framing/normalization factors. This must be established from the source, not assumed from a formal saddle. It includes overflow and alias bands, all colors, normal derivative channels, boundary currents, Stokes accessibility and noncancellation, at the desired full sequence of levels. Then (15),(16) prove lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|K_N|=Vol(M(sigma)). (17) This bridge is transparent about which work remains quantum. It does not assert that a positive norm, formal gluing solution, local normal block or representation-volume upper bound implies (16). Nor does it assume every augmented diagram has a known positive original-source base period. Those conclusions need independent proofs. The [existing full original-source pretzel theorem](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md), its [literal global lift](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md), and its [marked regulator certificate](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) do supply all four inputs for fixed odd s>=25 and independently sufficiently long fixed signed slopes, subject to the unchanged quantifiers of those source theorems. The subsequently independently audited [varying-radius alias extension](actual_pretzel_all_width_extension.md) lowers that actual quantum width threshold to every fixed odd s>=9: its entire-color bound is B_*<.81, whereas the exact width-nine source margin is greater than .812633708. All other local analytic and geometric ingredients were already valid there. The remaining widths3,5,7 are not proved by this envelope. The [specific positive-core proof](actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md) was already sufficient for that class. The present result removes ALL graph/polyhedron/width restrictions from the GEOMETRIC implication, but does not claim a new unproved original-invariant family. For other fully augmented bases, crossing-circle source/filling identities are exact, but a whole-source open-corridor survival estimate and complete global color/alias gap have not been proved just by those identities. For arbitrary knots, a classical A-curve or the general representation-volume inequality still does not provide the missing selected-source asymptotic. These are specific unproved quantum inputs, not residual uncertainty about which hyperbolic volume (15) denotes. There is now a stronger, independently checked way to supply the last quantum bullet for integral crossing-circle fillings: the [general original-source long-filling transfer](general_original_source_long_filling_transfer.md) proves the filled nonzero asymptotic from an EXACT even holomorphic BASE color packet, its uniform complex Gaussian expansion, and a strict gap over the entire complementary physical color cube. Its exact multilinear filling identity retains every confluent normal coefficient, and its Fourier proof keeps the endpoint currents and all charges. Thus one need not assume the desired filled asymptotic in each new application. What remains to prove for another augmented base is that specified original packet and global gap, together with its actual bounded geometric lift and calibration. The theorem does not infer those base certificates from the underlying hyperbolic geometry. ## 9. Adversarial scope audit of the current equality claim The existing long-pretzel equality proof passes the following geometric checks: its actual base holonomy is complete and positively oriented; its local port construction is a genuine representation, not trace data alone; its bounded cusp frames persist; the unfilled main cusp is genuinely parabolic; its geometric multiplier logs are centered before forming the slope; and the surviving source charges give primitive 2pi, rather than an accidentally killed PSL word. These are precisely the hypotheses used here. The following stronger statements are NOT justified by that proof: * Equality for every knot, every augmented diagram, short fillings, growing width, or slopes growing with N. * Inferring hyperbolicity from killing a slope without the local geometry and actual winding. A 4pi cone completion has the same killed PSL meridian and is excluded only by the unit period. * Replacing framed representation convergence by convergence of a few traces or cusp ratios. The finite C1 construction needs the actual finite generator matrices and selected flags in a bounded frame near the complete holonomy. A singular diagonalizing frame is not that input; the literal bounded port lift supplies it in the established application. * Calling the complete augmented volume Vol(M) the volume of a nontrivial finite filling. The latter is (15), evaluated at its actual selected parameter point. * Obtaining existence of a nearby representation for arbitrary long slopes from the conditional wording of section1. A source analytic family or an independently proved deformation theorem must supply that existence. * Treating Casson--Rivin strict concavity on the OLD complete-cusp angle slice as the filled equality proof. Its constraints differ. The direct construction above does not need an all-ideal angle chart or a universal positive triangulation existence claim. Thus the genuine extension here is a universal geometric completion and absolute calibration theorem for any ACTUAL selected near-complete source branch. It leaves the full-source estimates exactly where they belong, and does not replace the active broader equality goal by a generic conditional assertion. ## 10. Focused construction checks [The new focused audit](../experiments/audit_general_source_regulator_hyperbolic_equality.py) passes exact arbitrary-slope action algebra, eight Lorentz normalization/reindexing-equivariance families, and sixteen explicit affine-cusp/primitive-slope families with both winding signs. Its compactly supported cubic partition checks the positive real link Jacobian, exact affine and height equivariance, small log increments, and nonzero complementary core period. This tests the NEW construction, not only its inherited tube-coordinate formula. The universal argument is the analytical C1-continuity/compactness proof above; these finite checks make no additional knot-source or general existence claim. Two independent analytical readers checked the equivariant geometric construction; the second also checked the arbitrary-slope action and spin conversion through section7. Both reported PASS. The review clarified that the ENTIRE fundamental parallelogram image must avoid q before equivariance is used; this follows from section3's compact C1 estimate and is now explicit in section4. The concrete width-nine source extension and the general long-filling transfer have separately passed independent proof reads and fresh focused audit replays.

title: Coverage of the untwisted augmented-source volume theorem
status: Primary theorem statements and exact parity compatibility
text: # Coverage of the untwisted augmented-source volume theorem Checked 30 October 2026 against the primary versions linked below. This compares definitions and theorem statements with [the untwisted source theorem](general_untwisted_augmented_source_volume.md). It imports no external proof or proof technique and makes no priority claim. The present statement fixes one connected augmented plat, its actual labeled convex ideal right-angled cut polyhedron, and its complete link exterior. It concerns the original single-mark root invariant, no retained half twists, and the full integer sequence of levels. It does not concern arbitrary filled knots, all retained half-twist sums, or an invariant chosen only after fixing a geometric triangulation. ## 1. The invariant name is not a distinction Murakami--Murakami, *The colored Jones polynomials and the simplicial volume of a knot*, arXiv:math/9905075v2, 10 June 1999, Theorem 4.9, identifies their Kashaev invariant with the normalized colored Jones evaluation for every link and every integer N>=2. The introduction specifies N-dimensional colors, a primitive N-th Jones root, and unknot value one. Thus an overlapping colored-Jones theorem cannot be excluded merely by calling our source "original Kashaev." [Primary version, pp.1 and15](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9905075v2). Our parameter dictionary is q=exp(pi i/N), Jones t=q^2, and skein A=exp(pi i/(2N)). The [literal source identity, section4](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md) divides exactly one ordinary physical trace factor D_N=(-1)^(N-1)[N] before root specialization, equivalently retains its specified first normal. It is not division by one quantum dimension for every component. Mark, framing and dual-order phases must still be matched in any concrete comparison; they cannot convert an exact zero into a nonzero value when they are units. ## 2. Direct overlapping link results and the parity test Van der Veen, *Proof of the volume conjecture for Whitehead chains*, arXiv:math/0611181v2, 30 July 2007, Main Theorem, covers W_(a,b,c,d). Its b=1 conclusion runs over all N; this includes the named Whitehead-link and Borromean-ring examples. For b>=2 the statement is odd-only and the even evaluations vanish. Definition1 makes b the number of Belt tangles. The generic normalization on printed p.4 is sum_n [2n+1]/[N] times the composed tangle eigenvalues, so the even zeros are not explained by a different number of component reductions. The text also records a Seifert piece when b>=2. [Primary version, pp.2--4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0611181v2). This possible contradiction was checked against the actual diagram, not dismissed by terminology. In Figure1 a Belt is one circle around two straight strands. The stated commuting composition permits two Belt copies to be adjacent. Their circles cobound an annulus disjoint from those strands; the literal cut graph has two parallel MAIN edges with an intervening white bigon. A nondegenerate face of the required convex ideal polyhedron cannot be that bigon. Independently, our exact face polynomial reproduces the even zero: the intervening middle-face degree is at most a_1+a_2<=N-2, whereas the marked coefficient requires N-1. This is a finite source compatibility check, not an asymptotic argument. The complete labeled geometric certificate is essential; connectedness or the word "augmented" alone is insufficient. Van der Veen, *The volume conjecture for augmented knotted trivalent graphs*, Algebraic & Geometric Topology9 (2009), 691--722, Definition2 and Theorem2, uses a KTG move sequence and a sequence-dependent minimum number of augmentation rings at every unzip. It states an odd-N SO(3) volume law and zero even-N evaluations. The singly augmented outside consists of regular ideal octahedra; additional rings introduce the stated Seifert pieces. The normalization divides by an unlink according to SPLIT components, not by every link component. This is substantial prior augmented-family coverage, but the theorem's multiplicity and parity hypotheses must be retained. [Published primary paper, pp.692,695--696](https://msp.org/agt/2009/9-2/agt-v9-n2-p02-s.pdf); [arXiv:0805.0094v2, 5 February 2009](https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.0094v2). ## 3. Octahedral results and nearby quantum regimes Ibarra--McQuire--Purcell, *Augmented links, shadow links, and the TV volume conjecture: A geometric perspective*, New York J. Math.32 (2026), 1--34, Definition2.8, restricts "octahedral" to the indicated regular-ideal-octahedron decomposition. Theorem2.12 identifies these complements with fundamental shadow-link complements. Theorem4.15 gives the untwisted Turaev--Viro volume limit at exp(2pi i/r), odd r. Theorem4.16 also gives a colored-Jones limit for equal colors m at t=exp(4pi i/(2m+1)), with m even; Remark4.17 presents the extension to all m as an expectation. This is not the ordinary N-dimensional/Jones-root exp(2pi i/N) specialization merely by renaming m. The introduction explicitly attributes earlier Kashaev coverage of octahedral augmented examples to van der Veen. [Published primary version, pp.4,8,30--31](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2026/32-1p.pdf). The earlier arXiv:2506.09296v1 has different theorem numbering; the numbers here are those of the journal version. Wong--Yang, *Relative Reshetikhin--Turaev invariants, hyperbolic cone metrics and discrete Fourier transforms I*, arXiv:2008.05045v4, 11 December 2022, Theorem6.3, states generalized colored-Jones asymptotics for twisted octahedral fully augmented links at exp(4pi i/r), odd r, with colors giving sufficiently small cone angles. Theorem6.1 includes the corresponding odd-r Turaev--Viro statement, including twists. These are important overlapping geometric families and quantum conclusions, not a theorem restricted to the untwisted case. Their root/color and relative-RT conventions still need to be retained when comparing the exact invariant above. [Primary version, sections1.1 and6](https://arxiv.org/html/2008.05045v4). ## 4. General polyhedra and triangulations are separate coverage Belletti, *An upper bound conjecture for the Yokota invariant*, arXiv:2002.01904v2, 20 June 2024; published AGT25 (2025), 645--675, Theorem4.9, proves its upper-bound conjecture for graphs obtained from the tetrahedron by the two specified vertex/face moves. The trivalent Yokota invariant is a unitary bracket absolute square, with odd root order and its own admissible colors. The right-angled rectification and TV consequences are relevant prior coverage, but do not identify the original single-mark all-level link source. [Primary version, Definition2.7 and Theorem4.9](https://arxiv.org/html/2002.01904v2). Ge's *Geometric ideal triangulations of hyperbolic 3-manifolds*, arXiv:2609.27635v1, submitted 23 September 2026, is an existing primary preprint. Theorem1.1 states geometric ideal triangulation existence for every complete finite-volume cusped hyperbolic 3-manifold. This is a geometric statement, not a Kashaev/colored-Jones asymptotic, an invariant-normalization identity, or a theorem selecting an original quantum period. No inference about the correctness of its proof is made in this coverage check. [Primary statement](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.27635v1). Jun Murakami's 13 October 2026 IPAM talk abstract explicitly describes fully augmented right-angled polyhedra and their complexified filling deformations. This is a closely related existing program, but that abstract does not state the present full-level untwisted theorem. [Primary event abstract](https://mathinstitutes.org/videos/25102). The search also found Casandra Monroe's 2018 Princeton senior thesis, *Knot Too Big: The Volume Conjecture for Augmented Links*. Its repository abstract concerns fully augmented links. The repository's PDF endpoint required authentication during this check, so its theorem statements were NOT verified; its title alone supports neither inclusion nor exclusion. [Primary repository record](https://theses-dissertations.princeton.edu/items/c0cd5846-e602-42cc-b935-b9e36c73fb7e). ## 5. Publication wording supported by this check The result should acknowledge existing Whitehead-chain, augmented-KTG and octahedral-link volume results. Its precise statement concerns the recorded original source for any fixed untwisted augmented plat with the specified complete labeled right-angled certificate, without assuming a regular octahedral decomposition. The consulted primary statements do not by themselves establish inclusion of that entire class with that exact all-level normalization. This bounded check is not an exhaustive novelty conclusion. For any claimed overlapping diagram, first match the literal topology, augmentation multiplicities, quantum root and color dimension, one-cut normalization, framing, and level subsequence. Existing covered cases remain covered; a different presentation is not a new case. Conversely, a TV or generalized-Jones theorem cannot silently be substituted for the ordinary root specialization. The known parallel-belt even-zero family shows why these checks are mathematical requirements rather than bibliographical qualifications. No external proof techniques were used. The theorem's own proof remains the exact source/coefficient identity, its global coefficient asymptotic, the uniform channel upper rate, and its absolute geometric normalization. Independent targeted review: `conway_reduced_geometry` checked the literal parallel-Belt annulus/bigon and the even-level middle-face degree obstruction in section2: PASS. This review does not audit the external volume proofs or the other bibliographical comparisons.

title: Volume equality for the original untwisted augmented source
text: # Volume equality for the original untwisted augmented source 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed. This theorem concerns the original complete-circle source of every fixed connected augmented plat carrying the stated labeled right-angled geometric certificate, with NO retained half twists. Its bridge width and matching graph are arbitrary. Both quantum parities and composite levels occur. The source is exactly the original marked root invariant with its recorded normalization; its value is not chosen using the geometric answer. This is a theorem about complete augmented LINK exteriors. It does not assert the volume conjecture for general long-filled k-bridge knots. In a standard adjacent-cap2k-plat the zero-half-twist skeleton has k main components. A full twist cannot change that component count. Thus the untwisted result must not be advertised as that knot theorem. ## 1. Precise statement Fix the literal connected2k-plat box diagram D, k>=2, with R designated crossing circles and its original physical mark. Require a labeled convex ideal right-angled polyhedron Q_D whose face identifications are the actual projection/crossing-disk cut of this diagram. The actual quotient is its complete hyperbolic augmented exterior Y_D and Vol(Y_D)=2Vol(Q_D). This is the [marked geometric certificate](general_augmented_plat_matching_geometry.md), not merely the existence of an unlabeled polyhedron or a positive triangulation of unspecified topology. There is no restriction on R, bridge width, a Conway grammar, or an octahedral decomposition. Let A_(D,N) be the ORIGINAL marked complete-circle root source of [the full matching-graph identity](general_matching_graph_full_normal_source.md), with epsilon_i=0 at every box. Write chi_(D,N) for its separately specified exterior framing factor (one when absent); it has modulus1 in the recorded normalization and is retained below. Then lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N) log|A_(D,N)| =Vol(Y_D). (1) In particular A_(D,N) is nonzero for all sufficiently large N. The limit runs over all positive integer levels, including even and composite levels. It is not an iterated limit in which the diagram grows with N. ## 2. The exact positive finite source Set d=N-1 and M=floor(d/2). The [marked face-coefficient theorem](actual_original_marked_face_coefficient.md) gives EXACTLY A_(D,N)=chi_(D,N) N^R sum_(a in {0,...,M}^R) product_i[k_ai beta_ai^2] C_(N,a), (2) C_(N,a)=[product_(f!=u,v)L_f^d] product_i[D_ai,in D_ai,out P_si] at L_u=L_v=0. All C_(N,a) are nonnegative, so positivity concerns the scalar after the displayed common unit phase is removed. The original mark removes exactly the two face exponents u,v, and total polynomial degree dR excludes every additional Fourier alias. The primitive face grid supplies precisely N^R after its original single1/N marked factor. The complete-circle normal is already in k_ai beta_ai^2. No root-only replacement for an uncomputed generic normal is made here. The finite identity also holds for several main components. It requires connected projection and the literal single marked cap. It does not replace that mark by independent reduced normalizations on each link component. ## 3. Lower bound from an actual positive coefficient Choose the single original label vector a_i=M at every circle. The [global coefficient saddle theorem](actual_positive_face_coefficient_saddle.md) applies through both folds. It proves a positive coefficient with an exact compact-torus integral, a unique positive critical radius near the actual circle packing, and a nonzero relative Gaussian asymptotic. Its absolute action is computed from the source determinant and the actual facet coning: lim (1/N)log C_(N,(M,...,M))=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). (3) At the fold beta_M has zero normalized logarithmic rate, k_M is1 or2, and the factor N^R is polynomial. After removing the same unit phase, every other term of (2) is nonnegative. Keeping this ONE actual term therefore proves the required lower bound. No local-contour contribution or cancellation coefficient is left to assume in this step. ## 4. Upper bound for the whole original sum Evaluate all face polynomials at the SAME finite positive circle-packing radii l_f, with L_u=L_v=0. Positivity gives for each exact coefficient C_(N,a)<= product_i[D_ai,in(l)D_ai,out(l)P_si(l)] /product_f l_f^d. (4) The [uniform channel-rate theorem](actual_positive_face_channel_rate.md) keeps the original beta factors and proves a uniform logarithmic rate for every integer a_i, including0 and both folds. At these shared radii the local circle rate is strictly increasing in mu_i=a_i/N up to1/2. Its derivative is the explicit positive quantity log[E_b(mu_i)E_c(mu_i)/D_xy(mu_i)]. Thus (4), WITH the beta factors in (2), has normalized rate at most the all-fold value plus o(1), uniformly over all label vectors. The actual coning identity fixes that value absolutely as Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). There are only (M+1)^R channel vectors, the multiplicities are at most 2^R, and the outside N^R is polynomial. Summing the upper bounds does not change their exponential rate. This proves the matching upper bound and hence (1). The same argument gives a strict macroscopic channel gap: for each fixed eta>0, terms having some a_i/N<=1/2-eta have a smaller common-radius upper rate by a positive diagram-dependent amount. It does not by itself give a relative asymptotic in the sqrt(N) folded window. ## 5. What remains for the requested knot theorem Retained half twists preserve the exact positive coefficients but attach the original phases product_i omega_ai^epsilon_i to different channels. The upper bound above survives. Positivity no longer supplies the lower bound for that signed sum. A uniform relative folded-window estimate and a nonzero signed Gaussian coefficient are still required generally. Long fillings require a further source theorem in the EXTERNAL crossing-circle colors. These are different from the internal a_i in (2). The existing exact long-filling transform and marked geometric filling threshold do not supply that mixed-color packet or its alias gap. The target remains: every fixed essential hyperbolic2k-plat skeleton, with independently sufficiently long FIXED signed full twists, has the original knot volume limit. This note establishes the complete untwisted augmented-source theorem and a general signed-source upper bound; it does not mark that larger target as solved. ## 6. Dependencies and verification scope The proof combines exact source normalization/support/measure, a global positive coefficient saddle, a uniform all-channel upper rate, and an absolute geometric coning identity. Each dependency has a separate written proof and focused original-source audit. No finite set of knot examples, estimated limiting graph values, or unverified literature proof replaces any of these steps. No novelty or literature-coverage claim is made by this note. Independent source and geometry reviews of the complete theorem and its dependency chain: PASS. The primary reader checked every dependency and freshly replayed its focused audit. The reviewers confirmed the N^R measure, retained common exterior phase, all-label upper bound, positive central-sector lower bound, both folded parities and absolute 2Vol(Q) normalization. This is the stated complete untwisted augmented-link theorem; the general signed long-filled knot conjecture remains open. The [primary-statement coverage comparison](general_untwisted_augmented_source_literature_coverage.md) records prior overlapping families and root conventions. In particular, the parallel-belt examples with even-level zeros fail the required nondegenerate cut certificate; the exact coefficient formula reproduces their zeros. No external proof or priority claim is used.

title: Whole original mixed-source volume in the untwisted corridor
text: # Whole original mixed-source volume in the untwisted corridor 30 October 2026. Independently reviewed and frozen. The whole original mixed source has the actual geometric volume limit throughout a fixed near-complete corridor at its untwisted external circle ports. This follows from the frozen source gap, complex core and marked geometric assembly; no additional numerical theorem is needed. Fix a certified connected augmented flat plat D and a set E of its UNTWISTED external circle ports. The other ports stay at external color N and may keep their original signed half twists. Use the original cups, ordinary caps, unrestricted mark and scalar normalization throughout. Write A_N(N-h_E,N_else) for this actual mixed source and F_N^E(h) for its exact empty-subset cosine core, with deficits zero off E. The [block-representation/corridor theorem](actual_smoothed_block_representation_volume.md), section5, supplies delta0,gamma>0 and K such that, for all large N of either parity and every integer 0<=h_i<=delta0*N, |A_N(N-h_E,N_else)-F_N^E(h)| <=N^K exp[N(Phi_D-gamma)], Phi_D=Vol(Y_D)/(2pi). The [global complex-core theorem](actual_complete_core_complex_packet.md), sections1 and6, supplies a zero-free relative unit asymptotic on one fixed complex neighborhood of completeness, with exact finite-N phase S_N tending uniformly to the selected S. In particular uniformly on a smaller real neighborhood, (1/N)log|F_N^E(N chi)|=Re S(chi)+o(1), S(0)=Phi_D. Choose 0<delta<=delta0 so the real cube [0,delta]^E lies in that neighborhood and Re S(chi)>=Phi_D-gamma/2 there. Its uniform lower bound gives, after decreasing a constant c>0 and increasing N0, A_N(N-h_E,N_else)/F_N^E(h)=1+O(exp(-cN)) (1) uniformly on the entire PHYSICAL integer corridor 0<=h_i<=delta*N. Polynomial factors and the uniform o(N) in the core lower bound are absorbed by, for example, any c<gamma/4 after increasing N0. No equality of off-grid continuations or of genuine-q normal families is used. The ratio is legitimate because the actual core is zero-free there for all sufficiently large N, of both parities. By the [marked geometric assembly](actual_complete_core_geometric_deformation.md), sections2--4, the selected representation rho_chi has main meridians complete and crossing-circle logs U_i=-2pi*i*chi_i. For real chi, Re U_i=0, so its regulator boundary correction vanishes. Thus for ANY integer sequence h_N with 0<=h_N<=delta*N and h_N/N tending to chi, lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|A_N(N-h_(N,E),N_else)| =Vol(rho_chi). (2) This is the WHOLE original mixed source, not merely its cosine core. The class and fixed width are arbitrary within the actual labeled certificate, and constants may depend on D. The representation is the actual near-complete marked geometric family; no cone-manifold completion, distant-color estimate, signed varied-port corridor, filled-knot invariant equality or uniformity over growing diagrams is asserted. Equations (1)--(2) use only already frozen uniform theorems and need no new numerical audit. Root full analytical review of the corollary and its quantifiers: PASS. The finite-N phase remains in the relative core asymptotic; only its uniform limiting action is used for the exponential comparison and the volume limit. No off-grid or genuine-q identity is inferred. Independent coherent full analytical review: PASS, including uniform core nonvanishing, both level parities, physical integer deficits, untwisted varied ports and the complete signed complement.

title: A generic bilinear Euler reduction toward the actual Racah source sum
text: # A generic bilinear Euler reduction toward the actual Racah source sum 29 October 2026. This records two OWN finite identities: a bilinear Euler linearization and a generic Euler-moment formula for the actual source B_abc. They hold before root specialization and include high fold partners. The final source-to-single-Racah identity targeted in section4 is now proved independently by the [actual source-column/Jacobi argument](actual_generic_trivalent_racah_source_identity.md). The finite comparisons in this note remain supporting checks, not the proof of that identity. Use the notation and ACTUAL source normalization of [the generic six-head theorem](actual_generic_six_head_tetrahedral_source.md): N=d+1, Q=zeta^2, F_n=(Q;Q)_n, and ordinary triangles a,b,c in 0,...,d. Put r=b+c-a, r1=a+b-c, r2=a+c-b. All formulas in this note are generic rational identities. Only the source formula already proved there, not a named quantum 6j evaluation, is a premise. ## 1. Own bilinear finite Euler linearization For nonnegative m,n and a generic parameter V, (U;Q)_m(UV;Q)_n =sum_(k=0)^n C_(n,k) U^k(U;Q)_(m+n-k), C_(n,k)=Q^[k(k-1)/2] [n choose k]_Q product_(s=0)^(k-1)(Q^(m-s)-V). (1) Proof by induction on n. For the old basis vector with L=m+n, U^k(U)_(L-k)(1-UVQ^n) =U^k(U)_(L+1-k) +Q^n(Q^(m-k)-V)U^(k+1)(U)_(L-k). Thus C_(n+1,k)=C_(n,k)+Q^n(Q^(m-k+1)-V)C_(n,k-1). The displayed formula satisfies this by the elementary Gaussian Pascal identity. At n=0 the assertion is exactly (U)_m. No infinite product or summation formula is needed. The relevant specialization is m=n=b,V=Q^N: (U)_b(UQ^N)_b =sum_(k=0)^b Q^(bk)[b choose k]_Q (Q^(N-b);Q)_k U^k(U)_(2b-k). (2) At a root Q^N=1, (2) reduces to the previously proved finite square linearization. GENERICALLY its factor (Q^(N-b);Q)_k must remain; it cannot be replaced by its root value before taking a normal. ## 2. A source-exact generic Euler-moment formula Write c_e=[U^e](U;Q)_b(UQ^N;Q)_b, M_(a,n)=sum_(k=0)^(d-a) Q^[(a+1+n)k] F_(d-k)F_(a+k)/(F_(d-a-k)F_k), P=2a^2-b^2+3c^2-2ac+2bc -d(a+b+2c+1)+b+c. Then the ACTUAL analytic source sum from the generic six-head note is B_abc=(-1)^(d+b-c) zeta^P/(F_a F_b F_c F_r1) *sum_(e=0)^r c_e Q^(-ce) F_(2b-e)/F_(r-e) M_(a,r-e). (3) There is a second elementary expression for its moments: M_(a,n)=F_a^2 [z^(d-a)] (zQ^(a+1);Q)_n/(z;Q)_(2a+2+n). (4) Proof of (4). Divide the summand by F_a^2 and use the two Gaussian coefficients [a+k choose a]_Q[d-k choose a]_Q. Their convolution is the coefficient of z^(d-a) in 1/[(z;Q)_(a+1)(zQ^(a+1+n);Q)_(a+1)] =(zQ^(a+1);Q)_n/(z;Q)_(2a+2+n). The reciprocal finite-product coefficient formula is proved by induction on its length, so this is a finite generating-function calculation. Here are the source steps giving (3), including its phase. The generic cup/highest-vector ratio simplifies exactly to h_j(u)/P_d(u)=Q^(-ju)[j+u choose j]_Q. Expand the middle W entry in the actual B using its physical coproduct formula. With k,z its two summation variables, the result is B=zeta^C/(F_a F_b F_c) sum_(k,z) (-1)^(k+z) zeta^[(k+z)^2 +(2a+2c-2d+1)k+(2a-2d-1)z] *F_(d-k)F_(a+k)F_(b+z)F_(d-z) /[F_(d-a-k)F_k F_z F_(d-b-z) F_(a+b-d+k+z)F_(d-c-k-z)], C=2a^2+2c^2-d(3a+b+2c)+d^2. (5) All ranges here are the true physical ranges: every factorial index is nonnegative. Put k+z=d-a-b+p. The last two factorials become F_p F_(r1-p), so 0<=p<=r1. The two ratios involving z are (Q^(d-a-b+p-k+1);Q)_b (Q^(a+k-p+1);Q)_b. The k range extends to 0,...,d-a: each added nonphysical state is killed by a factor 1-Q^0 in one of these two finite products, before any root specialization. Reverse the second product. Up to the displayed overall phase it gives f_k(T)=(TQ^(d-a-b-k+1);Q)_b(TQ^(-a-b-k);Q)_b, sum_(p=0)^r1 (-1)^p Q^[p(p-1)/2-2bp] [r1 choose p]_Q f_k(Q^p). On its monomial T^e this operator multiplies by (Q^(e-2b);Q)_r1. It is EXACTLY zero for r<e<=2b; for e<=r it is (-1)^r1 Q^[(e-2b)r1+r1(r1-1)/2] F_(2b-e)/F_(r-e). Since f_k(T)=f_0(TQ^-k) and the two starts of f_0 differ by Q^N, its coefficient is Q^[-(a+b)e]c_e. Its combination with Q^(er1) is Q^(-ce). The remaining k sum is M_(a,r-e). The outside signs and zeta powers simplify to those in (3). This proves (3) by finite Gaussian algebra, at both parities and including all high partners. ## 3. The finite gap in this reduction, now closed by the source recurrence Equations (2)--(4) retain the GENERIC normal, unlike the old root Fourier/square reduction. But their remaining Euler coefficient and finite quantum-Hahn moment are not collapsed directly in this note. The separate generic source-column proof now establishes the desired single-sum identity, preserving precisely these normal terms. The root identity Q^N=1 turns the two Euler products into a square; doing that first loses the normal of their relative shift. For example, the proposed single-sum representation in the next section has, when a=max(a,b,c) and b+c<=d, the balanced series 4phi3(Q^-r,Q^(N+a+1),Q^-b,Q^-c; Q^(N-b-c),Q^(a-b+1),Q^(a-c+1);Q,Q). The independently proved finite Sears identity transforms it to a series with numerator parameters Q^-r, Q^-b, Q^(-J-1), Q^(N-b), and denominators Q^(N-b-c),Q^(-b-c),Q^(-2b). At the root the apparent extra termination length is delta=J-d. GENERICALLY its length is r, and terms k>delta carry a root zero whose derivative need not vanish. They cannot be removed by differentiating the root-short formula. This is a precise remaining normal-source issue, not evidence that the desired transform fails. ### 3a. Exact normalization to a reciprocal polynomial of bounded color degree This subsection is a further PROVED reduction of the generic source. Assume a=max(a,b,c), put X=Q^N and A=Q^(a+1), and define H_n(X)=sum_(t=0)^n [n choose t]_Q (A;Q)_t(A;Q)_(n-t) X^t, P_a(X)=(XQ^-a;Q)_(2a+1). The moment from (4) factors as M_(a,n)=F_a^2 P_a(X)/F_(2a+n+1) *H_n(X). (5a) For a finite proof, expand the numerator in (4). Its t-th term has the factor (XQ^(-a-t);Q)_(2a+n+1), whose common subproduct is P_a(X). The remaining two tails give sum_(t=0)^n [n choose t]_Q X^t(A/X;Q)_t(AX;Q)_(n-t)=H_n(X). Here is an own formal-coefficient verification of the last identity, without infinite-product evaluation. The series with coefficients (B;Q)_k/F_k is the unique initial-value-one formal series G_B(z) with G_B(Qz)=(1-z)G_B(z)/(1-Bz), as checked coefficient by coefficient. Both products G_(A/X)(Xz)G_(AX)(z) and G_A(z)G_A(Xz) have the SAME functional equation and initial value, so their finite degree-n coefficients agree. Only coefficients through n are used. Define the explicit SOURCE polynomial R_SRC(X)=sum_(e=0)^r c_e(X) Q^(-ce) F_(2b-e) H_(r-e)(X) /[F_(r-e)F_(J+1-e)], c_e(X)=[U^e](U;Q)_b(UX;Q)_b. (5b) Equations (3),(5a) give the precise actual normalization B_abc=(-1)^(d+b-c) zeta^P F_a/(F_b F_c F_r1) *P_a(X) R_SRC(X). (5c) Every c_e is reciprocal of degree at most e in the sense X^e c_e(1/X)=c_e(X). The same assertion holds for H_n of degree n. Consequently deg R_SRC<=r, X^r R_SRC(1/X)=R_SRC(X). (5d) All dependence on the physical d in the residual polynomial has disappeared: it enters only through X and the known outside factor. This is not a polynomial fit to physical data. The exact TARGET polynomial corresponding to the proposed Racah sum in (6) is R_TGT(X)=Q^(br) F_b^2 F_c^2 F_r1/F_(J+1) *sum_(k=0)^r (-1)^k Q^[3k(k-1)/2+(a-2b-2c+1)k] (XQ^(-a-r+k);Q)_(r-k)(XQ^(a+1);Q)_k /[F_k F_(a-b+k)F_(a-c+k)F_(b-k)F_(c-k)F_(r-k)]. (5e) To derive the conversion, first take d>=b+c and write z=d+a+k in the proposed sum. Replacing each symmetric factorial by zeta^(-n(n-1)/2)F_n/(1-Q)^n cancels every 1-Q factor. The ratio F_(N+a+k)/F_(d-b-c+k) is (XQ^(-b-c+k);Q)_(J+1). Its common factor P_a leaves exactly the two tails displayed in (5e). The remaining zeta exponent, relative to P in (5c), is 2br+3k(k-1)+2(a-2b-2c+1)k. The signs agree. The needed finite polynomial identity is R_SRC(X)=R_TGT(X) (5f) and is now established by the separate source recurrence, own finite Sears transformation and infinite-d polynomial argument. It covers d<b+c and high partners: in the fixed k range, a formally negative bottom index d-b-c+k is represented by the product (XQ^(-b-c+k);Q)_(J+1), which then contains the LITERAL factor 1-Q^0 and vanishes. For every physical d>=a, P_a(Q^N) is a generic unit. Thus precisely the inadmissible extra k terms vanish, restoring the correct lower limit z>=J without assigning a nonzero factorial to a negative index. Neither matching degrees nor exact finite-field tests alone prove (5f). There is at least one exact triangular interpolation value. Substituting (2) in the coefficient form of (5b) gives R_SRC(X)=sum_(k=0)^r C_k F_(2b-k)/F_(J+1-k) Q^(-ck) *[U^(r-k)] (UQ^-c;Q)_c(UQ^(a+1);Q)_(b-k) /(UX;Q)_(a+1), C_k=Q^(bk)[b choose k]_Q(XQ^-b;Q)_k. (5g) All manipulations here need only coefficients through r; the weighted Euler linearization agrees through that order even when its formal tail extends farther. At X=Q^b only k=0 survives. Canceling the common positive Euler interval and taking the coefficient gives R_SRC(Q^b)=F_(2b)/F_(J+1) *Q^(br)[c choose r]_Q(Q^(-b-c);Q)_r. (5h) Explicitly the remaining coefficient is [U^r](UQ^-c)_c divided by (UQ^b)_(c-r+1). Expanding its numerator, the two Gaussian factors combine to [c choose r][r choose p]; the finite binomial theorem then gives (5h). At X=Q^(b-s), 0<=s<=r, the k sum in (5g) truncates at k=s. The exact higher interpolation values, or an equivalent direct coefficient certificate for (5f), are not evaluated here. The complete identity is supplied by the independently proved actual channel recurrence, rather than these interpolation values. ## 4. The normalized single-Racah identity, proved by the source recurrence For symmetric quantum factorials [n]!_zeta=zeta^[-n(n-1)/2]F_n/(1-Q)^n, define the finite sum S_R=sum_z (-1)^z [z+1]! /([z-J]! product_j[z-d-j]! [d+a+b-z]![d+a+c-z]![d+b+c-z]!), max(J,d+a,d+b,d+c)<=z <=min(d+a+b,d+a+c,d+b+c). The precisely normalized identity, now proved in the linked generic source-column theorem, is B_abc = (-1)^J zeta^[a^2-b^2+c^2-ab-ac+bc-cd] *[a]![b]![c]!/[J+1]! *S_R. (6) The phase and factors agree with exact generic physical calculations, including high partner channels. Those comparisons are NOT the proof of (6): the linked proof uses the actual source coefficient COLUMN, uniform Fricke/boundary certificates and our own finite AW/Sears calculation. Formula (3) remains an independent Euler source reduction. The low-fold source zero and the one [N] factor in (6) can be compared term by term with the existing positive root Racah partition. High-partner ranges that cross N still require their actual zero orders and coherent cancellations. Neither a general boundary-conditioning theorem nor arbitrary-graph growth is asserted here. Audit: [generic Euler identities and separately labeled target tests](../experiments/audit_generic_trivalent_bilinear_racah_port.py). The audit verifies (1), (3), (4), and compares (6) independently; its historical result schema distinguishes the separate target tests from the Euler identities proved by that audit. The completed generic identity has its own uniform symbolic certificate and source audit.

title: Geometric local rigidity and the source lost by scalarizing quantum A
text: # Geometric local rigidity and the source lost by scalarizing quantum A Research note, 26 October 2026. This supplies a local geometric period for the proposed comparison and identifies a precise two-parameter source defect when its two geometric branches are scalarized. The uniform arguments are elementary polarized linear algebra, formal Gaussian contraction of the existing tetrahedron module, and exact Ore identities. The local formal period is not identified with the selected finite ADO evaluation. No quantum volume limit is proved. ## 1. Positive shapes make marked gluing unramified Take a positive complete geometric ideal triangulation with t tetrahedra, as supplied by [the audited geometric input](ge_geometric_triangulation_audit.md). Choose positive local orders and compatible logarithms u_j=Log z_j, v_j=Log z_j'', z_j''=1-z_j^(-1), tau_j=dv_j/du_j=1/(z_j-1), Im tau_j<0. (1.1) No compatible global branching is required for this calculation. The already proved integral edge/peripheral identities give t-1 independent real edge rows, together with the marked meridian row. Write their full-rank matrix as (A B). Its rows are isotropic: A B^T=B A^T. (1.2) The logarithmic gluing Jacobian at fixed meridian is J=A+B diag(tau_j). (1.3) It is invertible. Indeed ker(A B) is a real Lagrangian subspace. If J a=0, the shape tangent w=(a,diag(tau)a) belongs to its complexification, so Omega(w,bar w)=0. On the other hand (i/2)Omega(w,bar w)=sum_j Im(tau_j)|a_j|^2<0 for every nonzero a. Thus a=0. This proves nonsingularity uniformly, without a census or an imported rigidity proof. The exponentiated gluing equations are algebraic on the open set z_j(1-z_j)!=0. Multiplying (1.3) by their nonzero monomial derivatives changes its determinant only by units. Hence the marked-meridian projection of the geometric gluing germ is etale. After passing to its residue field, its completed local ring is K[[U]], U=Log m. Its successive shape coefficients are uniquely recovered by the invertible Jacobian recursion. The complete shapes are algebraic: at m=1 they are an isolated point of equations over Q. This is a local algebraic rigidity statement for this gluing branch, not a quantum-state selection theorem. ## 2. The two geometric peripheral slopes are distinct Keep the full marked boundary convention already derived in [the regulator note](boundary_regulator_period.md): Omega_red=-(1/2)dU wedge dV, U=Log m, V=Log l, m=M^2, l=L_intr^2. Along the geometric branch normalize dU=1 and write a_j=du_j/dU. The same polarized identity, now on the edge coisotropic space, gives Im(dV/dU)=-2 sum_j Im(tau_j)|a_j|^2>0. (2.1) The vector a cannot vanish since dU=1. Thus the marked cusp derivative tau_cusp=dV/dU is nonreal and nonzero. Complex conjugation supplies a second nondegenerate gluing germ with derivative bar(tau_cusp). Both map to (m,l)=(1,1). Use the actual meridian coordinate u=Log M=U/2 and a specified longitude lift L_c=+1 or -1. Its sign is retained. The two longitude branches L_+,L_- satisfy L_+(0)=L_-(0)=L_c, L_+'(0)=L_c tau_cusp, L_-'(0)=L_c bar(tau_cusp). (2.2) Their difference has a simple zero. These two local images form a transverse two-branch subgerm of the peripheral curve. There may be other components; no assertion of their absence or of global irreducibility is made. ## 3. A nonzero formal period from the existing tetrahedron module Let Q=exp(epsilon). Use the compact tetrahedron solution already appearing in [the pointed gluing construction](pointed_tetrahedron_gluing.md): psi_Q(Qz)=(1-z)psi_Q(z), psi_Q=P_Q^(-1). Here multiplication by z and forward Q-shift have quantum-torus parameter R=Q^(-1). Keeping this inversion is essential. Its formal logarithm on a compatible dilogarithm sheet is Log psi_Q(z)=-Li_2(z)/epsilon-(1/2)Log(1-z) -sum_(g>=1) B_(2g) epsilon^(2g-1) Li_(2-2g)(z)/(2g)!. (3.1) It follows either by expanding the defining product formally or by substitution in the displayed difference equation. Its leading amplitude (1-z)^(-1/2) is nonzero on the nondegenerate shape cover. Higher coefficients are rational functions of z after adjoining the recorded square-root frame. Write w=Log(1-z)=u+v+pi*i*k with k odd. The exact Gaussian shear exp(-u^2/(2epsilon)-pi*i*k*u/epsilon) changes its leading action to F_j(u)=-Li_2(e^u)-u^2/2-pi*i*k*u, F_j'=v, F_j''=tau_j. Its full shifted equation includes the half-step character phi(u+epsilon)=exp(-epsilon/2)(1-exp(-u))phi(u). (3.2) This factor is retained, rather than set to one. Finite-root Weyl characters and SL2 lifts still have to be matched in the actual state comparison; a formal square-root convention alone does not identify those finite-level data. For completeness, a nondegenerate formal Gaussian presentation can always be obtained. Since det(A-iB)!=0 by Section 1, its multilinear column expansion has a nonzero term choosing one column from each A_j,B_j pair. Swap (u_j,v_j)->(v_j,-u_j) for the corresponding subset. The new B is invertible. These partial formal Fourier transforms keep Im tau_j<0, because tau_j becomes -1/tau_j, and keep the local amplitude a unit. They act on the existing quantum torus; they are not a claimed global tetrahedral face-tensor comparison. Complete the real gluing rows to a symplectic matrix (A B;C D), using the marked half-longitude lift so that the last momentum is p_U=-V/2. All affine reference characters are retained as in the regulator centering calculation. For invertible B, the full generating action in constraint values q is W(u;q)=sum_j F_j(u_j)+(1/2)u^T B^(-1)A u -u^T B^(-1)q+(1/2)q^T D B^(-1)q. (3.3) Both quadratic matrices are symmetric. The last term is necessary for the marked momentum: at a critical point, partial_q W=-B^(-T)u+D B^(-1)q=p. The internal Hessian is H=diag(tau_j)+B^(-1)A, Im H<0. (3.4) It is invertible. In particular there is a nonzero local formal period, with a Gaussian leading coefficient equal to the product of the local units times det(-H)^(-1/2), and the specified Fourier, measure and character factors. The half-density cover retains all these roots; their absolute scalar is not equated to the ADO cut. Here the formal Gaussian is well-defined for an elementary reason. Subtract W_* and the full quadratic t^T Ht/2, leaving terms of degree at least three. Wick contraction has covariance -epsilon H^(-1). At each epsilon order only finitely many cubic and higher vertices can contribute. Its leading coefficient is the nonzero amplitude at t=0. No leftover quadratic divided by epsilon is admitted. Formal integration by parts follows directly from the same Wick rule, so this is the local formal gluing period of the supplied tetrahedron and edge equations. All coefficients are regular at the complete point: the shape denominators and Hessian determinant there are units. This does not show that a finite root-level projected vector is nonzero, or that the formal series converges on the desired sequence. ## 4. The dual line has the actual marked regulator action Distinguish the gluing vector from its period functional. At fixed edge values (3.3) gives dW_*=-V dU/2. Thus its scalar state has inverse-longitude leading shift in the actual M convention. The dual formal line has action -W_*. The exact Bloch identity used in [the actual action proof](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md) applied to (3.3) gives, at the complete point, Im W_*=-D(beta_T)=-Vol(M). (4.1) Indeed the quadratic coefficients are real, the complete constraint values and reference linear coefficients are purely imaginary, the internal derivatives vanish, and the boundary quadratic term at those values is real. Its imaginary part is therefore precisely the negative tetrahedral Bloch sum. No imaginary integration constant is selected to force this value. Put h=Log q, epsilon=Log Q=2h and S_geo=-W_*/2, R_geo=-W_*-UV/4. (4.2) Then the dual line exp(S_geo/h) satisfies dS_geo=(V/2)d(U/2), dR_geo=-(U dV-V dU)/4, Im S_geo|_complete=Vol(M)/2. (4.3) The retained SL2 longitude sign is its explicit solution character. Its meridian ratio has leading value L_intr, rather than its inverse. Consequently this dual formal line has the already marked regulator connection and complete regulator norm. This identifies which formal line is the candidate for the actual classical action; it does not identify a finite state with the dual of another state. On either geometric embedding, its normalized ratio has the form a(h,u)=L_intr(u)+h a_1(u)+h^2 a_2(u)+..., with every coefficient regular at u=0. The exact action differential, algebraic unit leading amplitude and rational Gaussian vertices show that these coefficients are algebraic on the normalized gluing germ. Thus the two embeddings supply two regular formal ratios with the distinct slopes (2.2). If an operator of this dual gluing module annihilates the local section, its first nonzero classical symbol vanishes on this geometric longitude branch: substitute the ratio and take the constant formal coefficient. This gives the geometric factor for that gluing object. It does not identify the annihilator ideal of the selected ADO sum with the dual gluing ideal. ## 5. A scalar quantum-A equation must retain the collision data Let sigma(u)=u+h, S=C[[u,h]], and a,b in S^times be any two such regular ratios, with a(0,0)=b(0,0)=L_c and kappa=partial_u(a-b)(0,0)!=0. For a scalar operator P=sum p_j(h,u)T^j, put P_0(u,L)=sum p_j(0,u)L^j and P_1=sum [h]p_j L^j. The first-order right-remainder calculation gives on a branch (P_0)_L a_1+P_1+(L L'/2)(P_0)_(LL)=0. (5.1) If P annihilates both regular formal lines, evaluate at the collision. Subtract their two conditions to obtain (L_c/2)(L_+'-L_-')(P_0)_(LL)(0,L_c)=0. (5.2) Thus P_0 cannot be just the reduced two-branch equation times a factor nonzero there: that would have (P_0)_(LL)!=0. It must retain additional vanishing data, such as a meridian factor or an additional characteristic multiplicity. This is a necessary condition on a proposed comparison operator. It does not assert that the unknown actual minimal knot operator already acts on both formal geometric lines. There is an exact model with no extra characteristic branch. Write Delta=a-b. The primitive regular second-order operator P=ab sigma(Delta)-(a sigma(a)-b sigma(b))T+Delta T^2 (5.3) annihilates both lines. Substitution gives zero on each without division. Its classical symbol is P_0=(L_+-L_-)(L-L_+)(L-L_-). (5.4) The additional factor L_+-L_- is u times a unit. Nevertheless the quantum coefficients have no common local divisor. Indeed Delta and sigma(Delta) have independent linear parts: Delta=kappa*u+beta*h+O((u,h)^2), sigma(Delta)=kappa*u+(kappa+beta)h+O((u,h)^2). Their Jacobian determinant is kappa^2, so they generate (u,h). The constant and leading coefficients in (5.3) are units times sigma(Delta) and Delta. The coefficient ideal is exactly (u,h), which has no common nonunit divisor. Cancelling the meridian factor after h=0 therefore changes the integral quantum data. ## 6. The complete cyclic source is a length-one point defect On the split semilinear module V=S e_a direct_sum S e_b let T e_a=a e_a, T e_b=b e_b and choose e=e_a+e_b. The two-vector cyclic frame (e,Te) has determinant b-a and cokernel S/(Delta). It is not in general T-stable. Keep every shift and define Lambda=sum_(j in Z) S T^j e subset V. Use f=(1,0), e=(1,1), so V=S e direct_sum S f. The differences of the two components of Te and T^2e are Delta, a sigma(a)-b sigma(b) =a sigma(Delta)+Delta sigma(b). They generate (Delta,sigma(Delta))=(u,h). Every shifted component difference vanishes at (0,0), including negative shifts since a,b are units. Hence exactly Lambda=S e direct_sum (u,h)S f, V/Lambda=S/(u,h), T acts on this quotient by L_c. (6.1) This is a length-one source supported at the simultaneous quantum and meridian point. Lambda has rank two but three generators in its complete fiber. A free presentation has generators e,u f,h f and the single relation h(u f)-u(h f)=0. Its ordinary dual loses that point quotient: Lambda^vee=V^vee, Lambda^(vee vee)=V. (6.2) For a direct proof, a functional on the ideal (u,h) sends u,h to A,B with hA=uB. Coprimality forces A=u c,B=h c, so it extends uniquely to S. This proves (6.2) without a duality theorem. The normalization or generic period line alone has therefore forgotten a specified source even though all its dual vectors lift. The same free presentation also computes the part retained by duality with its relation included: Ext^1_S(Lambda,S)=S/(u,h). (6.3) Indeed applying Hom(-,S) to S -> S^3 -> Lambda gives the row (0,h,-u), whose image is (u,h). Thus keeping that single relation retains the source that the ordinary dual loses. The ordered two-variable residue of this source has nonzero value Res_0 du dh/(Delta sigma(Delta))=1/kappa^2. (6.4) This follows directly from their invertible Jacobian. It is a local algebraic source residue, not the hyperbolic volume or the value of the selected knot invariant. ## 7. Relation to the actual source and what remains ### A fixed-level nodal order and its cut can be compared explicitly Fix N first and retain the two geometric branches marked in (2.2). Write d(u)=L_+(u)-L_-(u), so d'(0)=kappa. Their spectral order is A_geo=R[xi]/(xi(xi-d)), R=C[[u]], xi=L-L_-. The actual two-color Casimir pair c_0,c_last has local order A_src=R[t]/(t(t-delta_s)), delta_s=c_last-c_0=rho(M^2-M^(-2)), t=z-c_0. The unit alpha=delta_s/d has alpha(0)=4rho/kappa. Choosing c_last -> L_+ and c_0 -> L_- fixes the explicit isomorphism psi:A_src -> A_geo, psi(t)=alpha xi. (7.1) It transports the partial normalization and conductor (u,t) to their geometric counterparts. On the fraction fields it also sends the actual source projector E_last=t/delta_s to the geometric branch projector xi/d. Their polar residues therefore agree under the same map. This is a marked local-order comparison; choosing these branch marks is not a proof of the global quantum period comparison. Let Phi_src be the actual scalar pivotal cut on the local pair. Put C=M+M^(-1), D_N=M^N+M^(-N), c=q+q^(-1). The already proved two-color projector weights give the exact whole-germ formulas A(u)=Phi_src(1)=(-1)^N c C/D_N, B(u)=Phi_src(t)=(-1)^N rho C(qM^2-q^(-1)M^(-2))/D_N. (7.2) For example the two projector numerators add to (q+q^(-1))(M^2-M^(-2)); their common denominator is M^(2N)-M^(-2N). Dividing by the original color dimension ratio cancels M^N-M^(-N) and leaves precisely D_N. This derives (7.2), including its full 1+U factor: D_N=M^(-N)(1+U), U=M^(2N). No specialization of that peripheral factor was made in deriving the comparison. Use the geometric algebraic residue Phi_geo(a+b xi)=b. It is perfect, but its value on 1 is zero. A scalar rescaling cannot generally match (7.2). The unique matching unit density is theta=theta_0+theta_1 xi, theta_1=A, theta_0=B/alpha-A d =(-1)^(N+1) [d/(M-M^(-1))] (q^(-1)M^2-qM^(-2))/D_N, Phi_src(a)=Phi_geo(theta psi(a)). (7.3) This equality is checked on 1,t and therefore holds identically. At completeness it reads theta_0(0)=(-1)^N kappa*rho/4, theta_1(0)=(-1)^N(q+q^(-1)). (7.4) The first coefficient is nonzero, so theta is a unit. For N>2 the second is nonzero as well. It is fixed by the actual pivotal cut and must be retained. Equivalently the complete actual Casimir projector and its nilpotent satisfy Phi_src(e_0)=(-1)^N(q+q^(-1)), Phi_src(J_N)=(-1)^N rho^2. These are precisely (7.4) under t -> (4rho/kappa)xi. The full ADO cut multiplies theta by the original d_N(M), keeping eta_N. In fact that full density has a fixed rational central presentation. Put Y=M^2, U=M^(2N) and zeta_N=q^(N(1-N)/2)=i^(1-N). Then Theta=d_N(M)theta =zeta_N U/((U-1)(U+1)) [d(u)(q^(-1)Y-qY^(-1)) -(q+q^(-1))(Y-Y^(-1))xi]. (7.5) This follows by writing d_N(M)=eta_N(M-M^(-1))M^N/(U-1) and D_N=M^(-N)(1+U) in (7.3). Its only N dependence is the specified root data and evaluation U=Y^N. Both peripheral factors and the full phase remain. At M=1 the numerator and U-1 must be combined on that actual root curve before evaluation. The expression is not a replacement of the root constraint by an independent geometric central character. Every fixed meridian jet of (7.1), (7.3), and their inverses is polynomially bounded in N in these marked bases. Indeed kappa and the geometric Taylor coefficients are fixed, rho has size comparable to 1/N, and D_N=2cosh(Nu) has fixed-order Taylor coefficients polynomial in N and constant term two. The other vanishing ratios have nonzero normalized constant terms; their inverse coefficients follow by finite recursive division. At the complete fiber the full density's coefficients have sizes O(N^(-2)), O(N^(-1)), and its inverse has coefficients O(N^2), O(N^3), respectively. These bounds keep all phases. This controls a local, non-scalar source/cut normalization. It does not identify the difference transport or chosen global section, control jets whose order grows with N, or exclude cancellation in the final scalar contraction. ### The fixed-level wall and the two-parameter point remain distinct At each fixed N the actual [meridian source order](intrinsic_cut_and_meridian_atlas.md) has an elementary partial normalization, quotient C[[u]]/(u), and a conductor dual. The formal geometric scalarization here has the different two-parameter defect S/(u,h). Both are explicit data erased by generic line comparison. They must not be identified merely because each has length one. The relation q_N^N=-1 in the actual root family is additional data beyond the formal completion at h=0. The local comparison must retain the actual root germ and pointing as well. The [full integral cut theorem](integral_projective_cut_duality.md) provides the actual self-dual centralizer and its unit-group torsor. Section 6 explains why order or dual-lattice comparison alone can still miss the cyclic source pointing. A full comparison must carry that source as well as its operator, selected section and cut functional. The positive triangulation now supplies an unramified marked gluing germ, a nonzero local formal period, the required dual regulator action, and a concrete scalarization constraint at the peripheral collision. The actual finite ADO source has not been transported to that formal geometric line. Nor has its coefficient or possible cancellation in the selected period been established. No asymptotic specialization of the formal series is assumed. The original target remains (4/N)log|F_N(1)|-log||P_hyp|| ->0. ## 8. Coverage and exact diagnostics Geometric deformation and peripheral-potential theory are existing subjects of [Neumann--Zagier, Volumes of hyperbolic three-manifolds](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/zagier/files/doi/10.1016/0040-9383%2885%2990004-7/fulltext.pdf). Its introduction and scope were consulted for coverage, not its proof techniques. No novelty claim is made for polarized transversality, formal stationary phase or cyclic-vector methods. The arguments above reconstruct the exact statements needed for the current marked ADO comparison. The old analytic AK volume calculation remains a separate state-comparison problem. [The audit](../experiments/audit_geometric_rigidity.py) checks 25 exact rational-complex symplectic gluing charts with one to five tetrahedra, including singular B blocks requiring partial Fourier changes. It checks invertibility, the marked cusp energy identity, all Hessian/Jacobian coordinate factors and the full boundary Gaussian derivative. The local tetrahedron difference equation is checked through epsilon^5, retaining its half-step character. Six exact Ore examples test both remainders, the classical meridian factor, the absence of a common local quantum divisor and the nonzero point-defect residue. These are abstract uniform diagnostics, not six claimed knot operators. Eight additional cases at N=2,3,4,5,6,9,12,15 check the actual nodal cut formulas and the matching unit density, both at the complete fiber and at a generic color. The geometric slope in these finite-field diagnostics is an arbitrary nonzero parameter; the cusp nonvanishing itself is proved in Section 2. [Results](../experiments/geometric_rigidity_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_geometric_rigidity.py The subsequent [cut-wall source theorem](cut_wall_and_cyclic_source.md) now relates the two-parameter cyclic point module above to the actual cut. Its normalized branch density values are -p,sigma(p), where p=q^(-1)M^2-qM^(-2). The resulting point ideal, regularized cut presentation and calibrated residue agree with the geometric cyclic model after an explicit regular formal unit gauge. The physical ADO common frame remains fixed. This identifies a local source presentation, while the global difference action and selected quantum period still have to be compared.

title: The ordinary one-cut section is not generically zero on the figure-eight geometric root component
text: # The ordinary one-cut section is not generically zero on the figure-eight geometric root component Independent audit, 27 October 2026. The ordinary quantum dimension of an individual cyclic color is zero, but this does **not** force the pivotal one-cut functional of the closed-braid Hom line to vanish. For the figure-eight root-holonomy component, generic nonvanishing holds at **every** level \(N\ge2\). There are also literal full-quantum nonzero tests at complete irreducible points, for \(N=2,3,4\), in both Riley embeddings. This concerns the full root-center object [constructed here](closed_braid_period_line.md), not an identification of its root-central geometric point with the semiclassical geometric block of the original nilpotent state. It gives no volume estimate and no general-knot nonvanishing theorem. ## 1. Zero quantum dimension does not decide the one-cut section In a regular color \(K_{aa}=xQ^{-a}\), and \[ \operatorname{Tr}(g)= x^{1-N}\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}Q^{a(N-1)}=0, \qquad g=K^{1-N}. \] For a knot Hom-line frame \(J\), the partial pivotal trace is \(\operatorname{ptr}(J)=cI\). The full trace equation only says \(\operatorname{Tr}(g)c=0\), which is \(0=0\). It cannot imply \(c=0\). The identity tensor, whose partial trace does vanish, is not a model for every braid Hom-line frame. Vanishing is independent of a nonzero scalar rescaling of \(J\). It is also independent of a change of splitting-module bases: conjugate every local module and pivot, conjugate \(J\) by the tensor basis change, and the cut conjugates by the first basis change. Thus zero/nonzero evaluation is an intrinsic question on the admissible splitting cover, not a determinant-root normalization. ## 2. A direct algebraic Riley component, including the attachment Use the classical action word \((\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^2\). Put \[ A=\begin{pmatrix}z&1\\0&z^{-1}\end{pmatrix}, \quad B=\begin{pmatrix}z&0\\u&z^{-1}\end{pmatrix}, \quad C=A^{-1}BAB^{-1}A. \] The first fixed-braid equation is built into this expression for \(C\). The second is \(CA=BC\); preservation of the ordered product then gives the third. Direct multiplication yields \[ CA-BC= \begin{pmatrix}0&P/z\\-uzP&-uP\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \boxed{P=u^2+(z^2+z^{-2}-3)(u-1).} \tag{2.1} \] At \(z=1\), the equation is \(u^2-u+1=0\), giving the two complete irreducible figure-eight Riley representations. For the root center, retain the selected actual Casimir branch by putting \[ z=M^N,\qquad \Omega=-M-M^{-1}. \] This is compatible with the central Chebyshev relation and \(\Omega(1)=-2\). It is not an assumption equating a root center with a principal symbol. The curve \(P(u,M^N)=0\) is irreducible over \(\mathbb C(M)\) for every \(N\). Its discriminant is \[ \frac{(M^{4N}-3M^{2N}+1)(M^{4N}+M^{2N}+1)}{M^{4N}}. \] Each numerator factor has only simple nonzero roots: write \(y=M^{2N}\), and its two roots are distinct and nonzero. The two factors have no common root, since their difference is \(4M^{2N}\). The discriminant therefore has \(8N\) simple zeros and is not a square in \(\mathbb C(M)\). This proves irreducibility of the quadratic in \(u\). Let \(\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2>1\). At \(u=0,z=\varphi\), \(z^2+z^{-2}=3\), so (2.1) holds. The representation is upper triangular and nonabelian: \(B\) is diagonal but does not commute with the nonzero upper entry of \(A\), since \(\varphi\ne\varphi^{-1}\). It is an actual nonabelian reducible Alexander attachment point on the same irreducible Riley curve as the complete geometric points. The upper-triangular chart has central \(F_i^N=0\), all central crossing divisors equal to one, and a common \(K\)-root \(x=q_N^{N-1}M_*\), where \[ M_*=\varphi^{1/N}>1. \] The semicyclic and balanced coherent crossing constructions give invertible frames there, regular through their zero section. Thus the Hom line and its evaluation are defined at this attachment point. ## 3. A uniform positive anchor proves generic nonvanishing The exact whole-cut source-independence theorem, proved by the nonnegative wrap-degree argument in [balanced coherent braiding](balanced_verma_coherent_braiding.md), identifies the selected cut on this \(F^N=0\) family with the actual reduced figure-eight value \(F_N(M_*)\), up to the nonzero chosen Hom-frame unit. A wrap contributes \(+N\) to residue degree; the one-cut range cannot absorb it, so this is an equality of whole cut matrices. The independently proved [whole figure-eight identity](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md) is \[ F_N(Y)= \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} \prod_{r=1}^n\bigl(Y+Y^{-1}-Q_N^r-Q_N^{-r}\bigr), \qquad Y=M^2. \] At \(Y=M_*^2>1\), every factor is \[ Y+Y^{-1}-2\cos(2\pi r/N) \ge Y+Y^{-1}-2>0. \] Hence \[ \boxed{F_N(M_*)>0\qquad\text{for every }N\ge2.} \tag{3.1} \] A section of the dual of an invertible line on an irreducible component cannot be identically zero if it is nonzero at one regular point of that component. Trivialize the line near that point: the section is an ordinary function with a nonzero value, and thus a nonzero rational function. Applying this to (3.1) gives: **All-level conclusion.** On the framed Riley component containing the complete geometric representations, with the selected Casimir branch and its admissible source cover, \(\operatorname{ev}_{\beta,N}\) is not identically zero for any \(N\ge2\). It is nonzero on a dense open set. The statement is intrinsic under splitting-basis changes. The root-cover phases change a chosen frame by a unit; they do not turn a nonzero section into the zero section. At charts where one chain presentation degenerates, an isomorphic splitting chart is required, rather than interpreting its singular basis as a vanishing period. This does not prove that the section is nonzero at every complete point, or exclude a zero divisor elsewhere. ## 4. Exact full-quantum tests at complete irreducible points The script [audit_geometric_root_holonomy_cut.py](../experiments/audit_geometric_root_holonomy_cut.py) constructs the literal global quantum automorphism at the complete Riley tuple.
