At the m=1 germ q=1+x, the exact formal identity (q^5)^(5^(-a))=(q^(5^(-a)))^5 makes the quotient in equation (21) equal one. Every other local component is one, and the order is preserved under fifth powers. Hence all u^(a) are admitted invertible sections, with linear coefficient 5^(-a) at m=1. Let M be their full module as defined, i.e. the H-span of every admitted invertible section. Every element of M has integral constant coefficient at m=1: all defining sections do, and finite H-linear combinations preserve it. If g_1,...,g_r generated M, write g_(i,1)=A_i+B_i x+O(x^2), A_i in Z_5, B_i in Q_5. Choose B>=0 so that every B_i lies in 5^(-B)Z_5. For h_i in H, the coefficient of x in sum h_i g_i is a sum of terms C_i B_i+D_i A_i, with C_i,D_i in Z_5. It therefore remains in 5^(-B)Z_5. It cannot produce 5^(-a) when a>B. This contradiction proves that M is not finitely generated, and in particular not free of rank one as asserted in Theorem 1, p. 9. No analytic radius condition is imposed by the printed definition. Requiring later continuation or integral slopes would be an added hypothesis, not a property established by the defining test. Lemma 3.4, equation (184), p. 39, separately requires the linear coefficient to be integral. Corollary 3.5 retains that requirement, and Lemma 3.6 equation (195), p. 41, explicitly includes it. The counterexamples exploit exactly this missing condition in (20). Adding it excludes these fractional-power examples, but a complete repair still requires checking all subsequent uses. It does not remove the constant-sign obstruction in Section 2. ## 4. The printed Gaussian normalization leaves a forbidden term Equation (110), p. 28, defines formal Gaussian contraction on R[[w,w^3/h,h]]. Equation (114), p. 29, gives the purported normalized input. Already m=1,k=0 disproves that normalization. From the defining Pochhammer product, independently, log(q*z*exp(w);q)_infty =-sum_(n>=1) z^n exp(nw)q^n/[n(1-q^n)], q=exp(h) =Li_2(z exp(w))/h+(1/2)Li_1(z exp(w))+O(h). The quadratic term in the polar Taylor expansion is Li_0(z)w^2/(2h). The printed exponential subtracts Li_0(z)w^2/h, leaving -Li_0(z)w^2/(2h). This monomial is outside the stated domain: nonnegative powers of w,w^3/h,h cannot have exponents (2,-1). At w=0 its regular logarithm is -log(1-z), so the printed psi has value (1-z)^(-1)+O(h), rather than 1+O(h). This is not merely a choice of a scalar Gaussian phase. The n-th power of the unwanted quadratic term has w^(2n)h^(-n); Gaussian contraction contributes h^n, so infinitely many nonzero terms enter the coefficient of h^0. In the formally allowed A=0 case of the t-deformed construction, equation (119) gives Lambda=-Li_0(z). The extra exponential then cancels the Gaussian kernel exactly. This example concerns the formal construction before t=1; the degenerate z=0 specialization for A=0 is not being offered as admissible data for the arithmetic Theorem 5. For general m the necessary polar subtractions are Li_2(z^m)/(m^2 h), Li_1(z^m)w/(m h), Li_0(z^m)w^2/(2h). The regular constant logarithm of the product must also be subtracted, where (114) adds it. These corrections follow by splitting the Pochhammer product into its m residue classes and expanding each factor. They identify the intended local normalization; they do not verify the repaired global identification theorem. ## 5. Equation (165) has the stated sign error Definition (32), p. 12, gives in rank one A=1,m=2,k=0 H(t)=1+q^3 t^2/[(1-q)(1-q^2)]+O(t^4). For sigma H(t)=H(qt), the coefficient of t^2 in (1-sigma)(1-q^(-1)sigma)H is q^3. The printed right side of equation (165), p. 35, gives -q^3. Thus the recurrence fails as printed independently of the Gaussian issue. For the general rank-one congruence series, let n=k+mj. Its coefficients have successive ratio c_n/c_(n-m)=(-1)^(A*m) q^(A*m*n-A*m*(m-1)/2)/(q^(n-m+1);q)_m. It follows that the corrected operator recurrence is product_(r=0)^(m-1)(1-q^(-r)sigma)H(t) =(-1)^(A*m) q^(A*m*(m+1)/2) t^m sigma^(A*m)H(t). The q-exponent in the operator prefactor is unchanged; the sign is (-1)^(A*m). The coefficient of sigma^(A*m) on the previous term is q^(A*m*(k+m(j-1))); extracting coefficients must retain that factor. The finite q-binomial expansion gives the product on the left. ## 6. Scope and implications for this project Theorem 5 explicitly restricts to root orders prime to Delta. The global collection in Section 2 becomes identically one there because its exceptional order 2 disappears. It therefore does not disprove Theorem 5's restricted arithmetic membership assertion. The local error still occurs at the good prime 5 and order 1, but it is not itself a counterexample to membership of the particular series constructed in Theorem 5. That restricted statement needs a separate audit with corrected definitions and formulas; it has not been verified or disproved here. The distinctions are: | Printed claim | Independent finding | | --- | --- | | Definition 1.3 / Theorem 1 | The admitted span need not be finitely generated. | | Definition 1.4 / Theorem 2 | The all-order zero-class set is not additive and differs from H_R. | | Equation (114) | Wrong polar subtraction and constant normalization; input leaves the stated Gaussian domain. | | Equation (165) | Wrong sign, with a direct coefficient correction. | | Restricted Theorem 5 | Not directly refuted by these examples; not independently verified here. | No result from this paper has been used as a premise of the project's A-curve torsor proofs. In particular these findings do not by themselves affect the independently derived finite cyclic norm equation or its Hilbert-90 comparison. They do rule out importing the printed unrestricted module theorems without repair. The exact diagnostics in `experiments/audit_gswz_printed_definitions.py` check the constant tests, fractional-power Frobenius identity, Gaussian expansion, and recurrence coefficients. The all-order arguments and the non-finite-generation proof are those above, not extrapolations from finite computations.

title: A Heisenberg torsor and a uniform finite period
text: # A Heisenberg torsor and a uniform finite period Research note, 25 October 2026. The purpose is structural: replace matrix-chart restrictions and individual knot calculations by an intrinsic algebraic object. Definitions of the local cyclic quantum dilogarithm already exist. The results below reconstruct its normalization as a Heisenberg torsor, give an exact finite face reduction, and identify the boundary module that any global construction must preserve. This is not a proof of the full volume conjecture. The missing assertion is identified in Section 7. In particular a splitting module, a selected period vector, and a numerical growth law are different data. The comparison with existing literature is in `structural_literature_delta.md`. No novelty is claimed for Hilbert 90, finite Heisenberg representations, cyclic dilogarithms, or Heisenberg covers of Fermat curves. ## 1. The norm equation identifies the first cover Fix an odd integer n>=3, a field k of characteristic zero containing a primitive n-th root omega, and t on U=P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}. Let x^n=t. The elementary identity Norm_(k(x)/k(t))(1-x)=product_j(1-omega^j x)=1-t (1.1) is the Steinberg norm relation. It gives a direct splitting of the cyclic algebra A_t=k(t)<X,Y>/(X^n=t, Y^n=1-t, XY=omega YX). Indeed on E=k(t)[x]/(x^n-t), let X be multiplication by x and let Y f(x)=(1-x)f(omega^(-1)x). These operators satisfy all three relations. After adjoining x they are a diagonal operator with distinct eigenvalues and a cyclic shift with nonzero coefficients, and generate the full matrix algebra. Consequently A_t is already End_(k(t))(E). This proves the splitting; it does not assume a norm-residue or Brauer-group theorem. Now choose c^n=1-t. The ratio r(x)=(1-x)/c has cyclic norm one. The equation d(omega x)=r(x)d(x) (1.2) is exactly a Hilbert 90 equation over k(t,c). Its explicit solution on the cyclic spectrum, with its initial value left free, is w_0=1, w_j=c^(-j) product_(a=0)^(j-1)(1-omega^a x), d_j=s w_j, 0<=j<n. Equation (1.1) closes the recurrence at j=n. Conversely the recurrence determines all d_j from s. Thus the solution set is a G_m-torsor before normalization. This is an elementary proof of the Hilbert 90 instance needed here, rather than an invocation without a specified cocycle. One can also solve it in the cyclic function field itself. Write sigma(x)=omega*x, sigma(c)=c, and for a in k(t,c)(x) set H(a)=sum_(j=0)^(n-1) w_j^(-1) sigma^j(a). The recurrence and w_n=1 give sigma H(a)=r H(a). At least one H(x^k), 0<=k<n, is nonzero: after division by x^k these expressions are the finite Fourier transform of the nonzero vector (w_j^(-1)). The Fourier matrix is invertible. This proves the required field descent constructively as well. Determinant normalization still requires its separately recorded n-th root. For the user's generic peripheral factor, put t=-M^n. Since n is odd, product_j(1+omega^j M)=1+M^n. (1.3) The factor is a cyclic norm, not a disposable numerical multiplier. An unnormalized recurrence changes its n-step central character by this factor. At M=1 it equals 2. This identifies an exact mechanism for such factors; it does not identify the multiplier of the earlier positive factorial model from its one factor-eight test. ## 2. Determinant normalization gives a Heisenberg cover Set Delta=product_(j=0)^(n-1) w_j. The determinant-one normalization of the diagonal intertwiner D=diag(d_0,...,d_(n-1)) is s^n=Delta^(-1). Because n is odd, the expression simplifies to s^n=product_(a=0)^(n-1) (1-omega^a x)^(a-(n-1)/2). (2.1) Thus all coefficients live on the finite etale cover of U T_n: x^n=t, c^n=1-t, s^n=Delta^(-1). (2.2) Its degree is n^3 as a finite locally free cover. Every factor is a unit over U, so these are actual torsors there, rather than equations silently evaluated at a branch point. There are three deck transformations, written as maps of points: A:(x,c,s) -> (omega x,c,s(1-x)/c), B:(x,c,s) -> (x,omega c,s), C:(x,c,s) -> (x,c,omega s). The norm identity and the determinant product show that they preserve (2.2). Direct substitution proves A^n=B^n=C^n=1, C central, AB=C^(-1)BA. (2.3) They give a free transitive action on every geometric fibre: A and B choose the first two roots, and C chooses the last. Therefore T_n is a torsor for the finite Heisenberg group H_n, not just an unspecified scalar normalization line. The extra central root records the failure of the first two root changes to commute on the normalized intertwiner. For comparison with the standard cyclic dilogarithm convention, let q=omega^((n+1)/2), so q^2=omega and q^n=1, and set p^-=1/c, p^+=-x/(q c). Then (p^-)^n+(p^+)^n=1 and p^-+q^(2j+1)p^+=(1-omega^j x)/c. Thus d_j is exactly the spectral cyclic-dilogarithm definition, with its determinant root retained. This is a reparameterization, not a new local quantum function. The normalization cover, viewed over t, has the explicit Heisenberg structure (2.3). If U0 e_j=omega^j e_j and P0 e_j=e_(j+1), then D U0 D^(-1)=U0, D P0 D^(-1)=P0(1-x U0)/c. (2.4) The commutant of U0,P0 consists of scalars: commuting with U0 forces a matrix to be diagonal, and commuting with P0 makes its diagonal constant. Consequently this intertwiner is unique up to scalar. Determinant one reduces the ambiguity to mu_n. A mu_n-valued algebraic function on an irreducible parameter component is constant, since its n-th power is one. This is the precise rigidity statement available for comparing two intertwiners of the same automorphism. It does not prove that two arbitrary products implement that same automorphism, nor that every projective scalar cocycle is trivial. Those are separate coherence statements. ## 3. The face contraction is an exact finite Fourier evaluation Let X be the ideal compactification of a globally branched knot exterior. Its single ideal vertex and H_1(X;Z)=0 are the topological inputs. Let r be the number of tetrahedra, and use the existing face selectors D_f=X_0-X_1+X_2, R_f=X_2-X_3, Epsilon=diag(epsilon). Work over R=Z/nZ. The following argument also works for even n; oddness is needed for the Weyl normalization in Section 5. Define the finite groups and maps V=ker D_f, T(v)=Epsilon R_f v, U(v)=X_0 v, K=ker(T:V->R^r), H=T(V), W={w in H : (U k).w=0 in R for every k in K}. (3.1) For w in W choose any v with Tv=w and put q_W(w)=-(Uv).w in R. (3.2) This is independent of the lift: changing v by k changes it by -(Uk).w, which vanishes by definition. Its polarization is bilinear, so q_W is a quadratic function on the finite abelian group W. Use self-dual Haar measure n^(-1/2) times counting measure on R. Its delta function at zero has value sqrt(n). For an arbitrary function F:R^r->C define the charged-kernel-style contraction Z_n(F)=n^(-r/2) sum_(v in V) omega^(-(Uv).Tv) F(Tv). (3.3) All signs and local spectral factors can be included in F. This is the full face measure and all r independent delta factors, not a bare unnormalized sum. **Theorem.** For every such knot triangulation, including singular face matrices and every composite n, |V|=n^r, |W|=n^r/|K|^2, Z_n(F)=|W|^(-1/2) sum_(w in W) omega^(q_W(w))F(w). (3.4) There is no limiting operation or choice of inverse face matrix. **Proof of the topological input over R.** The local cocycle lemma of `automatic_face_regularity.md` uses only addition and sign changes, so it holds over R. The universal coefficient theorem gives H^1(X;R)=Hom(H_1(X;Z),R)=0; with one ideal vertex its edge cocycles themselves vanish. Thus D_f^T has trivial kernel over R. Perfect finite character duality implies D_f is surjective, and |V|=n^r. For k in K, define a character of V/K by kappa(k)([v])=omega^(-(Uk).Tv). This is well-defined. If it is trivial, R_f^T Epsilon Uk annihilates ker D_f and hence belongs to im D_f^T. Choose a with D_f^T a+R_f^T Epsilon Uk=0. Locally write b=X_0k,c=X_2k. The equations D_fk=R_fk=0 give face values (b,b+c,c,c), and the last equation gives the paired position values (a,-a,a+epsilon*b,-epsilon*b). They are exactly the same local ideal edge cocycle. It vanishes, so k=0. Therefore kappa is injective. Dualizing this injection gives a surjection V/K -> K^vee. Its kernel is identified by T with W. Hence |W|=|V|/|K|^2. Finally sum (3.3) over each coset v+K. Its coefficient is omega^(-(Uv).Tv) sum_(k in K) omega^(-(Uk).Tv). Character orthogonality makes this zero outside W and |K| times the displayed phase on W. Since n^(-r/2)|K|=|W|^(-1/2), (3.4) follows, including its exact measure. QED. This formulation survives primes dividing the integer face torsion. W need not be a free R-module; its cardinality and quadratic function are the invariant data. A rational nullspace dimension cannot replace these data at such a prime. ## 4. The period is algebraic, with its normalization specified When F is a product of local cyclic-dilogarithm entries, its coefficients are algebraic functions on products of the torsors T_n. Formula (3.4) is then a finite algebraic matrix coefficient on that parameter space. Specializing an algebraic decorated holonomy gives an algebraic number, with every determinant root and Fourier factor retained. This is an exact finite period in the representation-theoretic sense. It does not yet identify it with the continuous Faddeev state. The local bridge and the additional dilogarithm period are given in `rational_quantum_dilogarithm_torsor.md`. ## 5. Edge reduction gives one irreducible boundary module Here is the invariant version of the face/edge linear algebra. Let Lambda=R^(2r) with its standard alternating form. The r-1 independent edge rows span a primitive isotropic submodule E_ed. Their primitivity for odd n has a uniform proof. A dependence among all r edge rows says that in each tetrahedron the three opposite-pair sums of edge values are equal. Since 2 is invertible, such values are uniquely lambda_ij=a_i+a_j. A face's three edge values recover its three a_i, so the a_i agree across glued faces. There is one ideal vertex; the dependence is therefore the constant edge assignment. Deleting one row removes it. The same argument modulo every prime divisor of n gives a unit minor locally, hence a split injection over R. Isotropy is the local cusp-intersection cancellation already proved in `preferred_longitude_cochains.md`. The full meridian/longitude pairing is -2, a unit in R. Therefore E_ed^perp/E_ed is a free symplectic R-module of rank two, (5.1) with its generators supplied by the marked peripheral curves. It does not depend on the projection rank of a face matrix. In the r-fold clock/shift module of dimension n^r use Weyl operators W(a,b)=omega^(-a.b/2) X^a Y^b, W(v)W(w)=omega^(Omega(v,w)/2)W(v+w). For an edge character chi define the exact projector Pi_chi=|E_ed|^(-1) sum_(e in E_ed) chi(e)^(-1)W(e). All nonidentity Weyl monomials have trace zero, so rank Pi_chi=n^r/|E_ed|=n. (5.2) The boundary Weyl operators act on H_chi=im Pi_chi. For a class v in E_ed^perp/E_ed, their trace on H_chi is zero unless v=0. Their n^2 matrices are therefore trace-orthogonal and span End(H_chi). This proves irreducibility and scalar commutant directly. More generally, start with the split local cyclic algebras A_(t_j) from Section 1 over the gluing function field. The classical gluing equations make the commuting edge operators have n-th powers one. Their projector gives the same rank-n boundary module, now with the actual peripheral central characters. After a central-root extension the trace argument above applies, and descends the dimension and irreducibility assertions. Thus the interior gives a splitting of the boundary cyclic algebra on its gluing field. This is a uniform quantum Hamiltonian reduction. Singular face projections are alternate presentations of the same reduction, rather than additional species of quantum states. ### 5.1 Reduction of the torsor itself On a nondegenerate gluing chart pull back one T_n for each classical tetrahedral coordinate t_j. Push out their r central mu_n groups by multiplication, with the recorded orientation convention. The product cover becomes a torsor P for the Heisenberg extension of Lambda. In Weyl coordinates this group has law (v,z)(w,z')=(v+w,zz'*omega^(Omega(v,w)/2)). Choosing the inverse central generator matches (2.3); orthogonals and the reduction are unchanged. All fixed signs in edge central characters are incorporated before the next step. For an edge monomial product_j t_j^a_j(1-t_j)^b_j=1, its root eta=product_j x_j^a_j c_j^b_j is mu_n-valued. These roots give a moment map P -> E_ed^vee. In root coordinates the edge vector is e=(b,-a); under a deck vector v, eta_e(p.v)=eta_e(p)*omega^(Omega(e,v)). For a prescribed character chi its fibre P_chi is a torsor for the preimage H(E_ed^perp). The Weyl lift of E_ed is central in that subgroup by isotropy. Its quotient is a torsor for H(E_ed^perp)/E_ed = H(E_ed^perp/E_ed). (5.3) This is the Heisenberg group of one boundary pair. Indeed on each geometric fibre, primitivity makes Lambda -> E_ed^vee surjective with kernel E_ed^perp. Each moment fibre is nonempty and transitive with that stabilizer; quotienting its free E_ed action proves (5.3). These finite etale constructions descend. Thus a boundary H_n-torsor is constructed on every gluing chart, without a proper-face hypothesis or an angle limit. Identifying its period section on the intrinsic decorated character space remains the global task; a quotient group alone does not identify the section. The later [pointed tetrahedron gluing theorem](pointed_tetrahedron_gluing.md) extends the edge-lattice step to all levels for S^3 link exteriors. Its integral argument includes the missing prime 2 and proves primitivity without a global branching. With the full Weyl phases retained, the saturated boundary reduction has dimension N^c at every N for c cusps. The marked unhalved peripheral rows are a separate issue: their pairing -2 can give an index-two lattice, whose algebra has two sectors at even levels. The earlier odd-n identification with the full marked boundary algebra is therefore not extended by silently inverting 2. The subsequent [integral half-longitude proof](integral_half_longitude.md) now identifies the saturation for a knot as the marked meridian and half of its preferred longitude. A mod-two dual-face cocycle and nullhomology of the longitude give this integral result before N is chosen. The Weyl lift then has TY=q^2 YT; its square retains the full edge character. Matching the actual central longitude, source and selected period still requires comparison. ## 6. The torsor that still has to be globalized For two presentations over an identified decorated-character function field, with matched peripheral lifts, let H_X,H_Y be these irreducible boundary modules. Their module-intertwiner space I_XY=Hom_(A_boundary)(H_X,H_Y) is one-dimensional. Its invertible part is a G_m-torsor; a specified identification of determinant lines reduces it to a mu_n-torsor. Hilbert 90 handles descent of a specified multiplicative cocycle at the function-field level. It neither chooses a canonical section nor trivializes an arbitrary mu_n or degree-two obstruction. The local module has a canonical vacuum, the unit killed by X+Y-1, as proved in `pointed_steinberg_recoupling.md`. Tensoring these units and applying the edge projector gives an algebraic candidate J_X=Pi_chi(1 tensor ... tensor 1) in H_X. It can vanish on a locus; irreducibility of its ambient module has not removed that possibility. A face contraction such as (3.4) is a scalar period. Matching its boundary cut and frames to this projected vector is an additional comparison, not an already proved consequence of the scalar formula. The relevant object is therefore the pointed splitting module (H_X,[J_X]), together with its normalization line. An unpointed intertwiner exists uniformly; proving that it takes [J_X] to [J_Y] is the actual state-invariance assertion. Calling the unpointed intertwiner line a torsor does not discharge that assertion. The intended intrinsic object is the pointed boundary splitting module with the reduced Heisenberg/dilogarithm period torsor. Its global definition must identify the gluing charts of decorated flat local systems and verify one universal quantum five-term coherence. A list of individually certified knot triangulations cannot substitute for that statement. ## 7. What rigidity can prove, and the remaining volume assertion Once two normalized constructions are sections of the same pointed intertwiner line and implement the same quantum automorphism, their ratio is mu_n-valued and constant on each irreducible lifted parameter component. One normalization fixes their exact equality there; descent must still respect the deck transformations (2.3). This is the useful algebraic rigidity mechanism. The classical dilogarithm regulator is a value of the corresponding period torsor, rather than an asymptotic definition of hyperbolic volume. The requested conjecture still needs a uniform comparison of the normalized quantum period with that classical regulator. Fixed-level Zariski rigidity alone supplies no comparison between different n: the covers T_n and their period vectors vary with n. The theory should replace repeated saddle computations by this single compatibility theorem; at present that theorem has not been proved. The next proof obligations are consequently structural: 1. Construct the pointed period object on the intrinsic decorated character space and prove its universal five-term descent. 2. Match its normalization and cycle with the existing Faddeev state, using the exact local rational-parameter bridge. 3. Prove compatibility of its normalized size with the dilogarithm regulator on the complete geometric class, uniformly in the class of knots requested by the user. These preserve the full objective. The finite reductions and torsor identification above are tools toward it, not a redefinition of success. The subsequent pointed recoupling, period-descent and frame-transport notes now prove local selected-vector coherence and full projective matrix covariance on the stated root covers. In particular `projective_frame_period_torsor.md` supplies the operator comparison, determinant normalization and identity anchor needed to apply the rigidity mechanism of this section. Actual vector transport is essential: the unit in an endpoint frame is generally not taken to the new unit. The intrinsic equivariant knot period, its literature cycle and the regulator comparison across levels are still outstanding.

title: All finite quantum-normal orders have bounded Frobenius degree
text: # All finite quantum-normal orders have bounded Frobenius degree Research theorem and independent exact audit, 27 October 2026. For the ACTUAL integral high-color R-matrices, the coefficient of delta^j, after factoring the root signed block permutation, has Frobenius PBW degree at most 2j. The bound is uniform in the level, color multiplicity, number of crossings, and number of braid strands. The canonical actual divided sources obey the same relative bound after their root unipotent rotations. Orders two and three are sharp. This extends the [first-normal theorem](high_color_first_normal_r_and_frobenius_degree.md) using the original finite integral matrices, not an assumed formal quantum group lift. It does not identify the two geometric framing currents, bound the numerical coefficient sizes, or prove a regulator norm of the selected period. ## 1. Actual family, frame and filtration Fix N>=2 and r>=0. Use D_m(q), m=N(r+1)-1, in the constant sign frame \(w_{a,s}=(-1)^{Na(a-1)/2+as}u_{aN+s}\) of [the high-color source proof](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md). Put q_N=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2 and delta=1-Q^N. All quantum derivatives below use the actual local branch \[ q=q_N(1-\delta)^{1/(2N)}. \tag{1.1} \] Retain its marked half-Cartan root. The root multiplicity generators are e,f,h of Sym^r, with \(ew_a=(r-a+1)w_{a-1}\), \(fw_a=(a+1)w_{a+1}\), \(hw_a=(r-2a)w_a\). Write A=(r-h)/2 for the block number. Give e,f,h degree one and arbitrary head matrices degree zero. On b strands use total degree in U(sl2^b). The root crossing is its original head matrix times the block flip and parity \(\varepsilon^{A_1+A_2}\), \(\varepsilon=(-1)^m\). This whole signed permutation is retained separately, not replaced by a bounded-degree polynomial in A_1,A_2. Root conjugation by it preserves the filtration: permutations exchange Lie factors, parity changes the signs of e,f and fixes h, and heads only conjugate the head matrix coefficients. **All-order crossing theorem.** For \(R(\delta)=\sum_{j\ge0}\delta^jR_j\), either crossing sign satisfies \[ R_0^{-1}R_j\ \in\ U_{\le2j}(\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2) \otimes\operatorname{End}(\text{heads}). \tag{1.2} \] Coefficients may depend on N,r and the marked root. There is no uniform archimedean bound on their sizes in (1.2). ## 2. Quantum-integer jets have controlled polynomial block degree Write an integer argument as l=AN+s, 0<=s<N. With z=Log(q/q_N), \[ [AN+s]_q=(-1)^A \frac{q_N^s e^{(AN+s)z}-q_N^{-s}e^{-(AN+s)z}}{q-q^{-1}}. \tag{2.1} \] The coefficient of z^j after the sign is a polynomial in A of degree at most j. If s!=0, the constant coefficient is nonzero and independent of A. If s=0, division by delta gives \[ \frac{[AN]_q}{\delta}=(-1)^{A+1}\frac{A}{\rho_N} \left(1+\sum_{j\ge1}\delta^jP_j(A)\right), \qquad \deg P_j\le j,\quad \rho_N=q_N-q_N^{-1}. \tag{2.2} \] To prove (2.2), factor A z from the numerator sinh(ANz), and factor z from delta=1-exp(2Nz). The other factors are formal units. The remaining coefficient of z^j has A-degree at most j. Substitution \(z=\operatorname{Log}(1-\delta)/(2N)\) preserves this bound. This proves both statements without any unramified-root or nonresonance hypothesis on an algebraic shape. For a product of any number of such factors, its extra normal order j has extra block-polynomial degree at most j: the orders chosen from its factors sum to j. Denominator units depending on k,N,r but not the input block do not change this conclusion. ## 3. Every transfer has an exact valuation and divided factor Write its transfer k=aN+b, 0<=b<N. For input heads s,t, put \[ c_E=a+\mathbf1_{s<b},\qquad c_F=a+\mathbf1_{t+b\ge N}. \tag{3.1} \] These are its actual E and F block changes. The E numerator of E^(k)=E^k/[k]_q! crosses c_E multiples of N, while its denominator crosses a. The corresponding F counts are c_F and a. Hence \[ \begin{split} E^{(k)}_{s',s} &=\delta^{c_E-a}e^{c_E} \sum_{j\ge0}\delta^jP_{j,s}(A),\\ F^{(k)}_{t',t} &=\delta^{c_F-a}f^{c_F} \sum_{j\ge0}\delta^jQ_{j,t}(A),\\ \deg P_{j,s},\deg Q_{j,t}&\le j, \quad s'=s-b\pmod N,\quad t'=t+b\pmod N. \tag{3.2} \end{split} \] Constants depending on the recorded heads and parameters are included in the polynomials. Their order is literal: the polynomial is evaluated on the INPUT block before e^c or f^c acts. Both exponents c_E-a,c_F-a are zero or one. Here are the sign and boundary details. The zero numerator factors in E supply \(\prod_{h=0}^{c_E-1}(r-A+1+h)\), precisely the coefficient of e^(c_E). Those in F supply \(\prod_{h=1}^{c_F}(A+h)\), precisely f^(c_F). Every higher jet remains divisible by these products by (2.2). Thus the expression vanishes at the actual finite boundaries; it is not an interpolation outside the color. The constant beta gauge also cancels ALL input-block signs, for arbitrary k. For E, the sum of the integer parts in its k numerator arguments is -kA plus an A-independent integer. Its beta quotient has exponent \[ kA-Nc_E(c_E+1)/2+c_Es'. \tag{3.3} \] For F the numerator sign has exponent +kA plus a constant, and its beta quotient has exponent \[ -kA-Nc_F(c_F-1)/2-c_Ft'. \tag{3.4} \] The block signs cancel in each case. All remaining signs are head and transfer constants. Formula (2.1) shows the SAME sign accompanies every jet, so no hidden parity character occurs in (3.2). The actual nilpotent R term is \[ q^{k(k-1)/2}\rho^k[k]_q! E^{(k)}\otimes F^{(k)}. \tag{3.5} \] Since [k]_q! has delta-order a, this term's exact possible starting order is \[ \nu=c_E+c_F-a =a+\mathbf1_{s<b}+\mathbf1_{t+b\ge N}. \tag{3.6} \] At total nilpotent order j>=nu, its PBW degree is at most \[ c_E+c_F+(j-\nu)=j+a\le2j. \tag{3.7} \] In particular only k<(j+1)N can contribute to order j, however large the actual color is. This includes all resonant tails and all head boundary carries, not only the first one. ## 4. Cartan, inverses and arbitrary words The output unrolled weights are affine in the two input blocks. The varying part of the Cartan is \(\exp(zH_1H_2/2)\). Its delta^j coefficient is a polynomial of block degree at most 2j. Its ROOT value is the head Cartan times the original parity \(\varepsilon^{A_{1,out}+A_{2,out}}\). Relative to input parity this adds only \(\varepsilon^{c_F-c_E}\), a head/transfer sign. Combining the Cartan order j-l with (3.7) at nilpotent order l gives \[ 2(j-l)+(l+a)\le2j. \] This proves (1.2) for positive crossings. Multiplication by the inverse root head matrix changes only head coefficients. For the other sign, write R=R_0(I+sum_(j>=1)delta^j A_j). The inverse interaction coefficients obey \(B_j=-A_j-\sum_{l=1}^{j-1}A_lB_{j-l}\). Induction gives degree at most 2j. The necessary root conjugations and checked flips preserve the filtration by Section 1. Thus BOTH signs satisfy the same theorem. For every braid word W, product differentiation at any finite order is a sum of products of root-conjugated local interactions. Their normal orders add to j and their PBW degrees add to at most 2j. Hence, on arbitrarily many strands, \[ W_0^{-1}W_j\in U_{\le2j}(\mathfrak{sl}_2^b) \otimes\operatorname{End}(\text{heads}).\tag{4.1} \] No growing word length changes the degree bound, although it changes its coefficients and number of terms. ## 5. Pivots, full scalar factors and knot closure A whole pivot factor K(q)^c=q^(cH) has normal order-j coefficient of block degree at most j, for any specified integer c, including c=1-N. Thus ordinary and frozen ADO pivotal families and their EXACT normal adapter K^(-N) satisfy the filtration. The matching integral twist is a scalar and does not raise the degree. A regular marked external scalar line, including the canceled complete germ of d_N(M), likewise changes no Fr degree. If a retained scalar has a genuine pole of normal order p, its Laurent coefficient at order j instead uses the reduced bound 2(j+p); its valuation must not be erased before applying the bound. For a one-knot closure, the root Frobenius permutation has one cycle. Its ordered partial trace multiplies all inserted Fr words along that component. Their total degree stays at most 2j. Moving them through the retained parity factors only changes signs; the total uninserted parity on the knot is even. Thus the full order-j long matrix is in End(head) tensor U_(<=2j)(sl2). There is a corresponding exact hierarchy of Ward identities for the ACTUAL ORDINARY integral ribbon family, with pivot K(q) and matching twist: its generic long matrix is C_(N(r+1))(Q) times identity, so every nonscalar Fr coefficient vanishes at every normal order. For r>=2j the image of U_(<=2j)(sl2) has adjoint spins 0,1,...,2j, of dimensions 1,3,...,4j+1. Highest vectors e^l and their successive commutators with f exhibit these summands; their dimensions add to (2j+1)^2. Hence precisely \[ (2j+1)^2-1=4j(j+1) \tag{5.1} \] nonscalar head coefficient identities follow. For r<2j replace 2j by r in this count. Casimir powers only change the scalar part. Frozen ADO auxiliary closures still satisfy the DEGREE bound, but need not be generically scalar. Their scalar Ward hierarchy requires the full pivotal/source adapter, not root pivot equality alone. This is a finite exact hierarchy for every prescribed normal depth. It is not the claim that the divided Hopf action on arbitrary tensor products is primitive, or that its selected geometric image is nonzero. ## 6. The actual whole divided sources have the same relative bound Set \(F_N(\delta)=F^{(N)}(q)\) and \(E_N(\delta)=\tau E^{(N)}(q)\), where tau=(-1)^(Nr-1). The case k=N of (3.2) has NO head carry and gives \[ F_N=f+\sum_{j\ge1}\delta^j F_j,\qquad E_N=e+\sum_{j\ge1}\delta^j E_j,\qquad F_j,E_j\in U_{\le j+1}(\mathfrak{sl}_2) \otimes\operatorname{End}(\text{heads}). \tag{6.1} \] The heads here are diagonal residue strings. Their exact source operators are finite exponentials, as in the actual high-color note. For a fixed source parameter t define \[ A(\delta,t)=e^{-tf}\exp(tF_N(\delta)). \] It satisfies A(0,t)=I and the exact interaction ODE \[ \partial_t A=e^{-t\operatorname{ad}f}(F_N-f)A. \tag{6.2} \] Root adjoint unipotent conjugation preserves every PBW degree. Its series is finite on each filtered piece, since ad f is nilpotent there. At normal order l>=1 the coefficient on the right of (6.2) has degree at most l+1<=2l. Solving its coefficient recursion by integration and products therefore gives \[ [\delta^j]A(\delta,t)\in U_{\le2j}. \tag{6.3} \] The same proof applies to exp(-ue)exp(uE_N), and to the right interaction exp(uE_N)exp(-ue). Consequently the ORIGINAL source and co-source jets, after their recorded root unipotent rotations, are obtained by degree-at-most-2j operators on their fixed rank-one source and dual. This is an operator result, not a criterion which assumes such jets exist. There is a still more concrete finite source bound. Formula (3.2) for k=N says F_j=f P_j(A) and E_j=e Q_j(A), with polynomial degree at most j. The F interaction stays in the Borel algebra generated by f,A, and the E interaction in that generated by e,A. On the highest source v_0, A v_0=0. After the root unipotent rotation the order-j source vector therefore lies in \[ \operatorname{span}\{v_0,fv_0,\ldots,f^{2j}v_0\}. \tag{6.4} \] The rotated dual is supported on the corresponding first 2j+1 dual descendants. To see it, order the Borel monomials with A against the highest source or dual; the degree bound limits the remaining raising or lowering power to 2j. Thus fixed quantum depth B needs at most 2B+1 Fr source descendants, independently of N and r, while the full root coherent/prequantum source is retained by its exact unipotent frame. The actual normalization units U_s(q;t,u) of the two-flag source are still retained. Their inverses are head-diagonal scalar formal series on 1+tu!=0, so they do not increase Fr degree. This does not bound their coefficient norms or permit evaluating them at the source wall 1+tu=0. The rank-one root coupon itself is NOT asserted to lie in PBW degree zero. The precise coupon statement is a sum of left-degree-2a and right-degree-2b operators around that fixed coupon, with a+b<=j. Conflating this relative bound with a small-degree polynomial formula for the rank-one projector would be false when r is large. ## 7. Clock gauges and the exact coherent source realization The [actual coherent dictionary](high_color_two_clock_normal_source.md) turns (1.2) and (6.3), at any fixed depth B, into differential operators of order at most 2B. Its one-sided connection terms and all finite polynomial endpoints remain exact. A controlled gauge G=V^A, with V the cyclic HEAD shift, is not a plain polynomial Fr operator. In a head Fourier basis it is a finite sum of head projectors times clocks Q_N^(cA). Enlarge the filtration by giving those clocks degree zero. Their conjugation rescales e,f and fixes h, so this crossed-product filtration is multiplicative and Ad G preserves it. The coherent source realizes these clocks as the exact finite dilations and source characters of the two-clock note, not as differential operators of falsely bounded order. Thus after this controlled clock gauge the PBW part still has degree at most 2j, but genuine whole dilation factors must be retained. Arbitrary quantum-normal gauges or source-wall divisions have NOT been declared filtration-preserving. No assertion here bounds the number of dilation factors, gives a fixed finite-type whole comparison, identifies the internal framing-current image, or derives the volume limit from local jets. The result supplies actual bounded-normal-order operators and source jets for those further exact comparisons. ## 8. Independent exact checks [The audit](../experiments/audit_high_color_all_normal_filtration.py) uses polynomial Gaussian recursion and genuine truncated series through delta^3, including the full half-Cartan phase. At N=2,3,4 and r=8 it checks 83,000 actual coefficient jets and 1,584 shiftwise PBW-polynomial membership conditions. The r=8 spaces make the bounds at orders two and three nonvacuous. The k=0 Cartan component fails degree 2j-1 at both orders: 2j is sharp. It also checks 48 actual source OPERATOR jets after root unipotent rotation, rather than only their value on one vector, and verifies the full actual positive/negative R inverse through order three on a separate small high color. No division by a vanishing factorial is used in the test: Gaussian entries are multiplied by [k]! before specializing. [Results](../experiments/high_color_all_normal_filtration_results.json).

title: The actual first normal high-color crossing has Frobenius degree at most two
text: # The actual first normal high-color crossing has Frobenius degree at most two Research proof and exact audit, 27 October 2026. The first \(\delta=1-Q^N\) coefficient of the actual integral high-color crossing is a quadratic operator on the classical Frobenius multiplicity variables, with arbitrary finite head coefficients. The first resonant tail has a universal exact factorization. Both statements retain the full Cartan and mixed block signs. This is an actual first-normal crossing theorem. It does not identify whole low/high color jets or construct the full two-current Gaussian source map. The normal variable differentiates the original generic integral matrix family with its ordinary pivotal data. A frozen root ADO pivot is a different off-root source and requires its explicit route adapter; no scalarity of that frozen family is assumed. ## 1. Actual matrices and the filtration being used Use [the high integral color](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md), with dimension \(N(r+1)\), \(m=N(r+1)-1\), and the constant sign basis \(w_{a,s}\), \(0\le a\le r\), \(0\le s<N\). At the root the ordinary head matrices are independent of a. The divided matrices are \[ \mathsf E=[E^N/[N]_q!]_{q_N}=\tau e_{\rm cl},\qquad \mathsf F=[F^N/[N]_q!]_{q_N}=f_{\rm cl}, \qquad \tau=(-1)^{Nr-1}. \] The root block number is \(a=(r-h_{\rm cl})/2\), so multiplication by a is a degree-one classical enveloping operator. Give \(e_{\rm cl},f_{\rm cl},h_{\rm cl}\) PBW degree one. On two strands use total degree for \(U(\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2)\). Head matrix coefficients have degree zero. The full root crossing also has its literal block flip and parity \(\varepsilon^{a+b}\), \(\varepsilon=(-1)^m\); these are retained separately, not asserted to be bounded-degree polynomials in a,b. Write \(R(\delta)=R_0+\delta R_1+O(\delta^2)\). Then \[ R_0^{-1}R_1\in U_{\le2}(\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2) \otimes\operatorname{End}(\text{heads}). \tag{1} \] This assertion is uniform in N and r. Its scalar coefficients may depend on N,r and the marked root. It is not a uniform numerical norm bound on those coefficients. ## 2. Transfer orders and the universal resonant factor The full positive un-checked R is \[ q^{H\otimes H/2} \sum_{k\ge0}q^{k(k-1)/2}\rho^k[k]_q!\, E^{(k)}\otimes F^{(k)}, \qquad E^{(k)}=E^k/[k]_q!,\quad \rho=q-q^{-1}. \tag{2} \] Each divided matrix has regular integral Gaussian entries. The factor \([k]_q!\) has \(\delta\)-order \(\lfloor k/N\rfloor\), since every positive multiple of N contributes one simple zero. Hence all \(k\ge2N\) transfers vanish modulo \(\delta^2\). For \(k=N+b\), \(0\le b<N\), divided-power multiplication gives \[ D_{N+b}= \frac{q^{N(N-1)/2+Nb}\rho^N[N]_q!} {{N+b\brack b}_q}\, D_b\,(E^{(N)}\otimes F^{(N)}), \tag{3} \] where \(D_k\) denotes the k-th term of the nilpotent sum in (2). This is an exact generic identity before taking a normal coefficient. At the root, \[ {N+b\brack b}_{q_N}=(-1)^b,\qquad q_N^{Nb}=(-1)^b, \] so these factors cancel. Also \[ \left[ q^{N(N-1)/2}\rho^N[N]_q!/\delta \right]_{q_N} =N(-1)^{N-1}=:\kappa_N . \tag{4} \] Indeed \(\rho^N[N]_q!= (-1)^Nq^{-N(N+1)/2}(Q;Q)_N\), and \((Q;Q)_{N-1}=N\). Therefore the entire first resonant tail is \[ [R_{\ge N}/\delta]_{q_N} =\kappa_N R_0(\mathsf E\otimes\mathsf F). \tag{5} \] Equation (5) includes checked crossings as written: the divided operator is on the INPUT, to the right. The same full root R, including the mixed parity and original common half-Cartan line, must be used. Moving an isolated factor through it without its sign would change this statement. The Frobenius degree of (5) is two. ## 3. Nonresonant head terms have degree at most one Fix \(k<N\). In \(E^k\) or \(F^k\) at most one head boundary can be crossed. If neither side crosses, every factor is \([AN+s]_q\), \(s\not\equiv0\bmod N\). With \(\delta=1-q^{2N}\), its first derivative at the root is, apart from the root sign \((-1)^A\), affine in A: \[ \left.\partial_\delta[AN+s]_q\right|_0 =-\frac{(-1)^A}{2N} \left[ \frac{(AN+s)(q_N^s+q_N^{-s})}{\rho_N} -[s]_{q_N}\frac{q_N+q_N^{-1}}{\rho_N} \right]. \tag{6} \] The constant beta gauge cancels every block-dependent root sign in the ordinary head coefficient. Differentiating a product once therefore gives a degree-one polynomial in the two block numbers. If E crosses one boundary, its one vanishing integer has first normal value proportional to \(r-a+1\). The other head factors are nonzero. In the beta gauge its remaining sign is independent of a: for input head s<k the total sign is \((-1)^{kr+1+s}\). Thus this contribution is an actual \(e_{\rm cl}\) factor with a head coefficient. The F boundary likewise gives \(b+1\), hence \(f_{\rm cl}\), with no remaining block-dependent sign. If both sides cross, their two zeros give order \(\delta^2\), so nothing survives in the first normal. The remaining factors \(\rho^k\), \(q^{k(k-1)/2}\), and \([k]_q!^{-1}\) are regular head-dependent scalars for \(k<N\). They do not raise the Frobenius degree. Hence the entire nonresonant nilpotent first-normal coefficient has degree at most one after the retained root parity is factored. ## 4. The Cartan part raises the bound to two The unrolled weight is \(H_{a,s}=m-2s-2Na\). Since \(q=q_N(1-\delta)^{1/(2N)}\), \[ \left.\partial_\delta q^{H_1H_2/2}\right|_0 =-\frac{H_1H_2}{4N} q_N^{H_1H_2/2}. \tag{7} \] The multiplier is quadratic in a,b. Its product with a first-normal boundary or resonant term is second order and does not enter R_1. Equations (5)--(7) prove that, after factoring the root signed block swap, every head matrix coefficient of R_1 has total Frobenius degree at most two. The root crossing is a signed block flip tensored with the original head crossing. Conjugation by it preserves the PBW degree: the flip permutes the two Lie algebras, parity changes the signs of e,f and leaves h fixed, and the head factor only changes head coefficients. This proves the interaction form (1). For a negative crossing, differentiation of the exact inverse gives \[ (R^{-1})_1=-R_0^{-1}R_1R_0^{-1}. \] The same root conjugation argument proves the identical degree bound. The root half-Cartan and zero-framing factors are never replaced by their ideal numerical values. A coherent realization of the classical multiplicity variables turns (1) into a differential operator of order at most two, with its one-sided source/dual connection terms retained. It does not make the entire divided Hopf action primitive or remove its mixed coproduct terms. ## 5. The same bound holds for every braid word and its knot closure This local filtration is stable under arbitrary word composition. Let W(delta) be any fixed braid word on b high-colored strands. The derivative of a product, written in its interaction frame, is a sum of conjugates of the local interactions R_0^(-1)R_1. Every root factor is its head crossing times a signed permutation of the Frobenius factors. These permutations exchange generators and their parity factors change only the signs of e,f. Therefore W_0^(-1)W_1 lies in U_(<=2)(sl2^b) tensor End(all heads). (8) There is no crossing-count or bridge-count restriction on (8). Its coefficients and number of terms may depend on the word; the enveloping DEGREE stays at most two. A root pivot has no block dependence, and its first normal coefficient is affine in the unrolled weight, hence of degree at most one. The original zero-framing twist is a scalar on each generic integral color and introduces no extra Frobenius degree. Now close all but one strand of a braid whose closure is one knot. For the scalar Ward corollary below, use the ACTUAL generic ordinary integral ribbon family, with pivot K(q) and its matching zero-framing twist. Its reduced scalar is C_n(q). The root comparison with the ADO pivot was proved with its explicit signs; it is not an equality of those pivotal families off the root. The root Frobenius permutation has one cycle. In its partial trace, the Frobenius factors of any inserted monomial are multiplied in their order along that component. Degrees add to at most two. Transporting them past parity operators changes only their recorded signs. The total parity around the uninserted component is even, as in the high-color closure proof. Consequently the first normal long-knot matrix has C_1 in End(head) tensor U_(<=2)(sl2), (9) with the actual pivots, twist and ordered insertions retained. This is a statement about the full matrix before choosing a new source or identifying an internal geometric frame. There are exact resulting Ward identities. The generic actual integral-color long-knot operator is C_n(q) times identity, so its first normal coefficient (9) is also scalar. For r>=2 the image of U_(<=2)(sl2) under the adjoint classical action is the sum of spins zero, one and two, of dimensions 1,3,5. This follows directly by the highest vectors 1,e,e^2 and repeated commutation with f; their distinct h-weights and the nonzero raising strings make the three summands independent. The quadratic Casimir only changes the scalar summand in the given representation. Thus all eight nonscalar spin-one and spin-two coefficients of (9) vanish as head matrices. Its scalar head coefficient is the actual derivative of C_n(q) times the head identity. These are finite exact source identities for an arbitrary knot, and their coherent differential realization is given by the [actual two-flag Ward dictionary](high_color_two_clock_normal_source.md). They do not by themselves identify the relevant geometric current or prove that a selected geometric period survives. If one instead freezes the auxiliary ADO pivot to K(q)^(1-N) off the root, the matrix-degree bound (9) still holds: its normal pivot contribution is still degree one. Its generic long matrix need not be scalar, however. The eight vanishing coefficients then require the exact pivotal/normal source adapter and do not follow from root-only pivotal equality. This qualification is essential to the final Ward corollary, not to (1), (5), or (8). ## 6. Independent exact tests [The audit](../experiments/audit_high_color_first_normal_r_degree.py) assembles the ACTUAL integral R entries over a finite field and its dual numbers, using polynomial Gaussian recursion before specialization. A primitive fourth-level root retains the full half-Cartan phase. Its dual parameter is exactly \(q=q_N(1-\delta/(2N))\). At \((N,r)=(2,3),(3,3),(4,4),(5,3)\), it checks: * all transfers \(k\ge2N\) vanish to first order; * 3112 resonant coefficient identities (5), including boundaries; * all 174 nonzero head blocks of the parity-stripped first normal lie in the exact PBW-degree-two span; * some blocks do not lie in degree one, so the quadratic bound is genuinely needed in these examples. The PBW span is computed independently from the classical e,f,h matrices, with modular pivot rows and exact reconstruction; no proposed coefficient decomposition is supplied to the test. [Results](../experiments/high_color_first_normal_r_degree_results.json) record the ranks and level data. These checks support the uniform proof; they are not a selected-period or global-current theorem. The [actual-source audit](high_color_wall_source_independent_audit.md) checks the high integral matrix, divided source and Ward dictionary used here. The [memory-clock proof](actual_memory_clock_and_normal_transfer.md) then applies this crossing bound with its exact first-normal carry factors and independently checked inverse crossing.

title: Two actual clocks and the compact Frobenius source orbit
text: # Two actual clocks and the compact Frobenius source orbit Research construction, 27 October 2026. The high integral color has an exact whole source with a head clock and a Frobenius block clock. The latter is invisible at the root but survives in its first quantum normal. The divided-source orbit is the same twisted cotangent surface as the compact coherent source, with its actual weight-N prequantum clutch. These identities use original integral matrices, not an abstract extra SL2 representation. No identification of both internal geometric framing currents is made. In particular, a Frobenius block index is not a crossing transfer, and equality of low/high root periods does not equate their whole quantum-normal lifts. ## 1. The canonical actual two-flag source retraction Use [the high integral color](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md), with dimension N(r+1), basis w_(k,s), 0<=k<=r, 0<=s<N, q_N=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2 and Z=Q^N. The actual whole divided matrices give on each s-string \[ \Psi_s(q)=\exp(F^{(N)}(q))w_{0,s},\qquad \Lambda_s(q)=2^{-r}w_{0,s}^*\exp(\tau E^{(N)}(q)). \] Let Rw_(k,s)=k w_(k,s). Introduce independent source/dual coordinates t,u and retain their normalization as an ACTUAL whole germ: \[ \begin{split} U_s(q;t,u)&=\Lambda_s(q)(tu)^R\Psi_s(q),\\ I_{t,u}(q)e_s&=t^R\Psi_s(q),\\ P_{t,u}(q)|_{s\text{-string}} &=U_s(q;t,u)^{-1}\Lambda_s(q)u^R. \end{split} \tag{1.1} \] Here P returns the scalar coefficient in the s-th head basis vector. At the root \[ U_s(q_N;t,u)=2^{-r}(1+tu)^r. \tag{1.2} \] Thus on 1+tu!=0, these are regular whole source/co-source germs, and P I=I_N exactly. All derivatives of U_s are retained. Their normalized weights need not be binomial away from the root. A chosen normalized head source and co-source may be attached to this retraction. For example a head coherent parameter h gives diagonal weights \[ H_s(h)={N-1\choose s}\frac{h^s}{(1+h)^{N-1}}. \tag{1.3} \] This is an explicit ordinary polynomial coherent cut in the specified head frame; transport the source and its dual together if a different actual head basis is used. Their diagonal weights (1.3) are unchanged by that diagonal frame transport. No claim that its ordinary SL2 action is the quantum braid action is required. The resulting normalized functional on the actual high color is \(\Phi_{h;t,u}(C)=\lambda_hP_{t,u}CI_{t,u}\psi_h\). For the actual scalar high-color long-knot matrix it gives the SAME whole ordinary color period C_(N(r+1))(Q), since lambda_h psi_h=1 and PI=I. At q_N this is K_N. The original external ADO modified dimension line remains the one in the high-color source note. ## 2. The two-clock character is an exact whole rational expression Let Jw_(k,s)=(kN+s)w_(k,s), and Sw_(k,s)=s w_(k,s). The fixed integer floor is retained, and \[ J=S+NR,\qquad Q^J=Q^S Z^R. \tag{2.1} \] Define A=Q^S and B=Z^R as actual diagonal operators. At the root B=I, while A is the original nontrivial head clock. For all integer a,b the source character is exactly \[ \Phi_{h;t,u}(A^aB^b) =\sum_{s=0}^{N-1}H_s(h)Q^{as} \frac{U_s(q;tZ^b,u)}{U_s(q;t,u)}. \tag{2.2} \] Equation (2.2) is an identity of whole q-germs, including their actual divided-factorial coefficients and normalization units. It is not obtained by extending root binomial weights arbitrarily. At q_N, (2.2) is independent of t,u and equals \([(1+hQ_N^a)/(1+h)]^{N-1}\). Consequently a root observable depending only on Q^J loses the independent Frobenius source coordinate. ## 3. Its first quantum normal recovers the block moment exactly Write D_Q for Q partial_Q along the actual q-family, so D_Q is one half of q partial_q. Put x=tu and \[ \mu=r x/(1+x). \] For a diagonal insertion f(A,B) independent of q except through these clocks, the exact first-normal identity is \[ \left.D_Q\Phi_{h;t,u}(f(A,B))\right|_{q_N} =\sum_sH_s(h) [sA\partial_A+N\mu B\partial_B] f(A,B)|_{A=Q_N^s,B=1}. \tag{3.1} \] Any explicit coefficient derivative of f must be added if present. To prove (3.1), write the normalized s-string weights as w_(k,s)(q). Their sum is exactly one, hence their derivatives sum to zero. At the root f(A,1) is independent of k, so every derivative of the WHOLE source/co-source weights cancels. The remaining clock derivative is \(sA\partial_A+NkB\partial_B\). The root weights are \({r\choose k}x^k/(1+x)^r\), whose mean is mu. This cancellation does not set the individual source derivatives to zero; many are nonzero in the exact audit. In particular, for r>0, \[ \Phi(A)|_{q_N}=\left(\frac{1+hQ_N}{1+h}\right)^{N-1}, \qquad \frac1{Nr}\left.D_Q\Phi(B)\right|_{q_N} =\frac{tu}{1+tu}. \tag{3.2} \] The first depends nontrivially on h, and the second nontrivially on x=tu. Their Jacobian in h,x is nonzero away from the explicit denominators and the zero of 1+hQ_N. Thus root plus first-normal data give TWO independent source coordinates, even though all zeroth-order block-clock values are one. For the required r=N, the normalization in the second expression is N^2 exactly. The block number is intrinsic to the actual root divided action: \(R=(r-[e_{\rm cl},f_{\rm cl}])/2\). Its clock satisfies \(Bf_{\rm cl}B^{-1}=Zf_{\rm cl}\) and \(Be_{\rm cl}B^{-1}=Z^{-1}e_{\rm cl}\). These are literal finite matrix identities for the graded source, not an assumed scalar holonomy character. ## 4. The actual divided-source orbit is the compact source surface For r>=1, on the root multiplicity factor the source and dual are \[ \psi(t)=\sum_{k=0}^rt^kv_k,\qquad \lambda(t,u)(v_k)={r\choose k}\frac{u^k}{(1+tu)^r}. \] The actual divided generators in the high-color proof give exact normalized moments \[ E=\lambda e_{\rm cl}\psi/r=\frac{t}{1+tu},\quad F=\lambda f_{\rm cl}\psi/r=\frac{u}{1+tu},\quad H=\lambda h_{\rm cl}\psi/r=\frac{1-tu}{1+tu}. \tag{4.1} \] They satisfy H^2+4EF=1. These are single-insertion matrix moments, not an assertion that products of expectations equal expectations of products. The corresponding coadjoint projector convention is \[ \mathcal J(t,u)= 2\frac{(1,t)^t(1,u)}{1+tu}-I =\begin{pmatrix}H&2F\\2E&-H\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \mathcal J^2=I. \tag{4.2} \] Its marked eigenflags are (1,t) for +1 and (u,-1) for -1. For a chosen meridian eigenvalue M the explicit matrix \((M+M^{-1})I/2+(M-M^{-1})\mathcal J/2\) has determinant one, trace M+M^(-1), and those marked eigenflags. This is a source moment map to the meridian conjugacy class; it has not been identified with the internal critical holonomy of the knot word. Now set \[ v=t,\qquad a=u/(1+tu),\qquad T=va. \tag{4.3} \] Then F=a, E=v(1-va), H=1-2va. The root source connection is obtained directly by differentiating the actual source vector: \[ \lambda\,d\psi=\frac{r u\,dt}{1+tu}=r a\,dv, d(\lambda d\psi)=-r\,dv\wedge da. \tag{4.4} \] On the reciprocal chart t'=1/t,u'=1/u one has \[ v'=1/v,\qquad a'=v-v^2a. \tag{4.5} \] Thus the two source connection forms differ by r dlog v. The source vectors themselves have clutch psi_n=v^r psi_s after basis reversal. The coherent SOURCE VECTOR spans the tautological O(-r) line; its dual co-source/polynomial line is O(r). The latter is the positive prequantum line, with connection -lambda dpsi. Keeping both signs explicit, this is the SAME affine cotangent torsor Conn(O(1)) as the original compact source, with exact two-form dv wedge da and its nontrivial affine clutch (4.5). For r=N the dual prequantum weight is N, obtained from the actual divided source; the original head half-form/degree-(N-1) line remains separate. This goes beyond an abstract identification of two SL2 actions: the variables, connection, clock generator T=R/r in its source expectation, density chart, and transition are all explicit actual matrix formulas. Its marked inverse/positive flags and dual/source polarization have not been swapped silently. ### Actual divided commutators give exact compact-source currents There is an exact current dictionary before any head partial trace. Use the unnormalized dual row ell(u)_k=binom(r,k)u^k and put sigma_r(C)=ell C psi/(1+tu)^r. Directly from the actual divided matrix entries, \[ \begin{array}{lll} f_{\rm cl}\psi=\partial_t\psi,& e_{\rm cl}\psi=(rt-t^2\partial_t)\psi,& h_{\rm cl}\psi=(r-2t\partial_t)\psi,\\ \ell e_{\rm cl}=\partial_u\ell,& \ell f_{\rm cl}=(ru-u^2\partial_u)\ell,& \ell h_{\rm cl}=(r-2u\partial_u)\ell. \end{array} \tag{4.6} \] The degree-r endpoints are exact: the top term is killed by rt-t^2 partial_t, and the bottom by partial_t. Consequently \[ \begin{split} \sigma_r([e_{\rm cl},C]) &=(\partial_u+t^2\partial_t)\sigma_r(C),\\ \sigma_r([f_{\rm cl},C]) &=-(\partial_t+u^2\partial_u)\sigma_r(C),\\ \sigma_r([h_{\rm cl},C]) &=2(t\partial_t-u\partial_u)\sigma_r(C). \tag{4.7} \end{split} \] These vector fields preserve the exact compact two-form dt wedge du/(1+tu)^2. The formulas extend entrywise when C has actual head-matrix coefficients, so no scalar symbol or head partial trace is assumed before deriving the currents. One must retain the normalized source terms for one-sided actions. For example \[ \begin{split} \sigma_r(e_{\rm cl}C)&=(\partial_u+rt/(1+tu))\sigma_r(C),\\ \sigma_r(Ce_{\rm cl})&=(-t^2\partial_t+rt/(1+tu))\sigma_r(C),\\ \sigma_r(f_{\rm cl}C)&=(-u^2\partial_u+ru/(1+tu))\sigma_r(C),\\ \sigma_r(Cf_{\rm cl})&=(\partial_t+ru/(1+tu))\sigma_r(C). \end{split} \tag{4.8} \] Thus sigma is NOT being used as a multiplicative map to ordinary functions. Its exact left/right differential actions or corresponding star product transport matrix products. An actual Frobenius enveloping-degree-d operator has by (4.6)--(4.8) a differential realization of order at most d, with polynomial r-degree at most d. This is the explicit source adapter available for a bounded-degree normal crossing/current calculation. A proof that the actual mixed normal crossing operators produce the TWO required geometric framing currents is still needed. Whole block clocks also have an exact source action. For B_xi=xi^R and a matrix C independent of t,u, \[ \begin{split} \sigma_r(CB_\xi)(t,u) &=\left(\frac{1+\xi tu}{1+tu}\right)^r \sigma_r(C)(\xi t,u),\\ \sigma_r(B_\xi C)(t,u) &=\left(\frac{1+\xi tu}{1+tu}\right)^r \sigma_r(C)(t,\xi u),\\ \sigma_r(B_\xi C B_\xi^{-1})(t,u) &=\sigma_r(C)(\xi^{-1}t,\xi u). \tag{4.9} \end{split} \] Thus a head/block clock gauge can be transported as exact finite dilations, retaining its source character, rather than expanded as a polynomial Fr operator of falsely bounded degree. Its first normal generator is the Cartan moment already proved in (3.1). ## 5. The remaining source and holonomy comparisons The off-root color still follows M_high=-q^(N(r+1)), Y_high=Z^(r+1), whereas the original N-color path follows Y_low=Z. All powers q^N and M^N, including the high-color lift sign, remain in the original whole source and external peripheral line. Formula (3.1) does not equate these paths. Nor is R a literal crossing transfer. A total position is s+Nk; a crossing transfer is a difference of such total positions. The transparent root multiplicity braid merely permutes its block labels, so its block-transfer difference is zero at zeroth order. The mixed normal crossing/coproduct and the two-current coupling are needed to relate the new source variables to the TWO internal geometric framing flows. The explicit first-normal block arrows in the high-color proof are part of that map, not its conclusion. At 1+tu=0, the coherent normalization vanishes. The actual units U_s in (1.1) must be retained before taking any simultaneous normal or meridian limit. The compact source identification above does not permit evaluating a separately canceled root expression at that source wall or infer a regular geometric period there. [Exact two-clock/source audit](../experiments/audit_high_color_two_clock_source.py). [Results](../experiments/high_color_two_clock_source_results.json).

title: Independent audit of the actual high-color wall source
text: # Independent audit of the actual high-color wall source 27 October 2026. The current [high integral-color construction](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md) passes independently, including its generic source germ and signed crossing/closure comparison. No additional test rerun was needed. The constant beta gauge gives precisely \(E=(-1)^rE_{\rm St}\), \(F=F_{\rm St}\), \(K=(-1)^rK_{\rm St}\) on every block, while retaining the block-dependent unrolled H. The root Gaussian evaluation yields \[ \mathsf Fw_{k,s}=(k+1)w_{k+1,s},\qquad \mathsf Ew_{k,s}=(-1)^{Nr-1}(r-k+1)w_{k-1,s}. \] Thus the stated normalization gives the ordinary irreducible \(\operatorname{Sym}^r\) action. The root and generic block decompositions must remain distinct. The two regularized between-block edges are also correct: F gives \(\rho^{-1}f_{\rm cl}\otimes E_{0,N-1}\), and E gives \((-1)^{r+1}\rho^{-1}e_{\rm cl}\otimes E_{N-1,0}\). The first \(h=\log(q/q_N)\) factors follow from \(1-Q^N=-2Nh+O(h^2)\); the N is essential. The exponential source has all coordinates one, while its dual coordinates are \(2^{-r}\binom rk\). Their pairing and coupon trace are one. With a rank-one head projector, the normalized high trace multiplied by \(r+1\) gives exactly \(1/(N2^r)\sum_k\binom rkJ_k\). For r=N this is the wall row, including its final k=N entry. Replacing the marked head projector by identity changes this normalization by N. The new generic source germ is valid. Both integral divided matrices are regular Gaussian-polynomial matrices and preserve the residue classes modulo N for generic q as well. Their exponentials terminate on each finite string. Since the source pairing is one at the root, its denominator is a genuine unit germ; its normalized coupon is regular, idempotent, and has trace one. The string coupons are disjoint, so their sum has trace N. The exact scalar high-color identity then proves (4.4), with its actual source derivatives retained. This does not identify those derivatives with the lower color. For the signed crossing proof, the full Cartan ratio is \[ q_N^{-N[aH_W(j)+bH_W(i)]+2N^2ab} =(-1)^{m(a+b)} . \] The factor is independent of head positions but cannot be discarded on an inserted block-changing network. Both crossing signs have this same ratio. The pivot block factor is one, and the twist change is an integer multiple of \(2N^2\), giving root phase one. On an uninserted one-knot closure the block index is constant, so the mixed sign becomes its square. The remaining one-dimensional shift constants cancel against the retained pivot/twist by knot parity. Thus the original reduced Kashaev scalar is retained exactly. Finally, \(M_{\rm high}=(-1)^r\) at the root, and the full modified-dimension adapter is \((-1)^{r(N-1)}\), indeed one for r=N. The old external ADO line remains the appropriate one. There is no new dimension-\(N(r+1)\) modified trace inferred. This proves an actual high-color realization of the wall co-source and its original quantum-normal arrows. It supplies neither the entire two-current network map nor equality of low/high whole quantum jets. A vector multiplicity action also does not by itself identify the full divided Hopf adjoint on matrix observables. Those limitations are correctly explicit in the construction. The subsequent [actual two-clock source](high_color_two_clock_normal_source.md) also passes independently. Its whole retraction is regular on \(1+tu\ne0\). Per-string normalization is what cancels all source-weight derivatives in the first clock derivative; setting those derivatives individually to zero would be wrong. The remaining block mean gives \(Nr\,tu/(1+tu)\), with the required \(N^2\) for r=N. The exact source/dual divided-action formulas give the stated one-sided normalized terms \(rt/(1+tu)\), \(ru/(1+tu)\). Subtracting left and right actions gives the compact divergence-free vector fields. The formulas hold entrywise with head-matrix coefficients and retain the matrix/star product, including the reversed composition order for right actions. Their Berry curvature is \(-r\Omega\); the dual positive prequantum connection has curvature \(+r\Omega\). The coherent-vector \(O(-r)\) and dual \(O(r)\) clutch signs are correct. Combined with [the actual first-normal R theorem](high_color_first_normal_r_and_frobenius_degree.md), this supplies a differential realization of that crossing correction of order at most two on the Frobenius source. It still does not identify the independent transfer flow with the geometric centralizer current. The [all-order Frobenius filtration](high_color_all_normal_frobenius_filtration.md) also passes independently. The quantum-integer coefficient at extra normal order j has block-polynomial degree at most j after its root sign and any forced linear zero are removed. For arbitrary transfer \(k=aN+b\), the exact numerator/denominator zero count is \(c_E+c_F-a\). The printed beta exponents cancel all input-block parity signs. Factoring the forced e- and f-strings then gives nilpotent degree \(j+a\le2j\); Cartan adds at most twice its normal order. Inverses, root-conjugated products and ordinary one-knot closure preserve the bound. The source interaction ODE is exact. Root unipotent adjoint conjugation is locally nilpotent on every PBW piece, so Duhamel products have degree at most twice their summed normal orders. Since the raw source jets remain in the respective Borel, their rotated order-j vectors use only the first \(2j+1\) source descendants, with the analogous dual statement. The head-diagonal normalization units remain present. The controlled-shift gauge preserves this filtration only in the explicit enlarged algebra retaining its degree-zero finite dilation factors. Their number and analytic norms have not been bounded by this PBW theorem. The scalar Ward hierarchy uses the ordinary generic integral ribbon family; a frozen root pivot does not acquire generic scalarity from this argument. The revised [controlled Fourier/current dictionary](controlled_fourier_current_and_conormal_dictionary.md) also passes. Its original INTEGRAL head currents use the exact finite circulant \(\Psi_w=\mathcal Fw^S\mathcal F^{-1}\); its simpler balanced-head formulas require the separately retained diagonal adapter. The full head-clock normal resolvent has the correct resonant coefficient \(-(N-1)/(2N)\) and all nonresonant coefficients \(1/[N(1-\zeta^{\ell+1})]\). The actual tensor divided-power commutator with the total unwrapped clock follows from its exact degree N, so no mixed coproduct term is omitted. The old-clock scalar normal pairing with the unprojectivized source also checks: source-unit and Fr-mean derivatives die under the finite root sum, leaving the nonzero scale character divided by \(N(1-\zeta)\). Its coefficient is uniformly bounded and nonzero. This is a scale-line detection statement, not an independent scalar Fr Ward theorem, and does not identify the new position clock with the old physical shift. The later [marked unprojectivized source torsor](actual_unprojectivized_frobenius_borel_torsor.md) also passes the independent source/form calculation: the actual paired ket/dual Borel vector fields, equivariant map to r,s, scale and first-descendant moments, and Omega_cut=(A/N)dlog U wedge dm are exact. Its Berry curvature is correctly kept separate. The regular A/Omega_cut chart omits 1+C alpha^2=0. Its standard marked cover is the torsor; the unmarked Sym^N orbit has nonnormal mu_N isotropy for N>2, with the central-sign PGL2 exception at N=2 retained explicitly. The [global Frobenius polynomial/Cech source](global_frobenius_cech_source_and_endpoints.md) passes in its revised form. Both explicit contractions, the residue Stokes sign, and the additional source-homotopy term are correct. The matrix-unit coefficients act in the ACTUAL divided basis; their global differential lifts are compared only up the stated homotopies. The dual operators retain the canonical-bundle +2 and the two distinct north/south endpoint cochains. Clock actions on a source and its adjoint row satisfy residue ADJOINTNESS; simultaneous pairing-preserving transport uses the inverse dual clock, as now explicitly stated. Its whole retained-weight interval proof is exact: the actual pairing U cancels before integration, the elementary beta integral gives c_k/[(N+1)binom(N,k)], and both subsequent normalization units have root one. Delta annihilates the actual source, so K=I+psi Delta has inverse I-psi Delta, fixes that source and has the claimed co-source orientation. The base-shift and connection transport must include sigma(K) and dK respectively. No uniform metric, PBW degree or geometric-current conclusion is silently imported into this rational source gauge. The [endpoint-completed whole Jackson current](endpoint_completed_normal_clock_euler_current.md) also passes independently. Its actual inverse arrows are regular germs, its shifted argument and endpoint projector orders are essential, and its finite normal kernel and averaged factor N are correct. The off-diagonal remainder retains the ordered matrix currents, so the assertion remains a character-subalgebra map. The [whole function/endpoint extension proof](whole_clock_function_algebra_and_endpoint_extension.md) adds the infinite-order functional-quotient obstruction, an exact flat confluent tower and its Newton lattice, and root inverse norm N^(-1/2). The actual top spectral-polynomial defect begins at normal order N; it cannot be discarded at the whole-function level merely because any fixed smaller jet misses it. The [actual relative endpoint period](actual_frobenius_relative_endpoint_period.md) keeps the marked moving endpoints and original normalization units through all normal orders. Its explicit first-normal counterexample shows that the naive original divided-Borel generator does not automatically equal that source connection. The retained-weight uniform interval is rational; the unweighted normalized interval is a different relative period. Their exact distinction and the source-current correction remain necessary for a future network/Gaussian comparison. The [full matrix degree-elevation/current map](degree_elevation_actual_head_ward_map.md) passes independently: its two row-index terms give exact symbol, normalized trace and original average-cut preservation; the whole head D and actual divided-string B_s gauges have the correct orientations. The Hopf F-to-commutator row operation retains its ordered K-row product. Its B_Fr homotopy is regular because the two omitted target corners vanish IDENTICALLY on its image. This image condition cannot be extended to arbitrary Fr currents. The [complement Bockstein wall](degree_elevation_complement_bockstein_wall.md) also passes: every interior fork contracts by a unit f-arrow, even at intermediate resonant weights. The bottom remaining arrow is a root unit and the top one is delta/(1-delta). Its co-source must remain the ACTUAL one: selected coherent weight2^-N and uniform interval weight1/(N+1) differ on a genuine root Ward cycle. They cannot be equated by a fixed-current co-source homotopy. The literal charged first-normal R current, its wall coefficient and both displayed source pairings check. The [explicit incidence/source audit](degree_elevation_wall_residual_and_source_moments.md) gives the exact quotient polynomial, whole selected source character and one-sided Green moment correction. In particular Ad-clock covariance does not remove the auxiliary bit from one-sided clock coupons. Finally, the [Clebsch matrix-memory strictification](clebsch_memory_dilation_and_actual_r_excursions.md) passes with its full lower channel, whole gauge/source/cap transport and auxiliary trace1/2. The per-strand minimality and metric factors are correct. Its actual R leakage and inverse-pair defect are nonzero uniformly in N, so upper-only words cannot replace the strictified word. This is an exact extension of the old head R representation; matching it to the actual high-color R or internal Gaussian currents remains a separate theorem. The revised hybrid-metric conclusions in [the clock/current source audit](frobenius_clock_and_internal_centralizer_map.md) Sections 7--8 also pass independently. Keeping the Fr binomial metric and OLD flat head metric makes G unitary and the original Fourier/N scalar-unitary, so their conjugation is exactly isometric. The selected coupled e_D is then an orthogonal rank-one projector. The highest-spin Hilbert--Schmidt projection remains contractive; converting HS to operator bounds costs only sqrt(ambient dimension). For the phase clock its normalized highest-spin coefficient is (1-z)^N/binom(2N,N), with the stated polynomial HS bound. This does not alter the selected2^-N versus uniform1/(N+1) wall source or bound the actual R word, normal neighborhood or head D gauge. The earlier exponential G bound used a DIFFERENT head coherent metric and remains valid there. The whole divided-Ward/pivotal closure identities and their actual Cartan wall inverse pass the independent proof audit recorded in [the global Green tail/current note](global_green_cut_tails_and_wall_transport_residual.md). It verifies the divided coproduct/adjoint q-powers, frozen cap clock and first-normal signs, the ordered N-term cap cancellation, the literal diagonal Cartan-unit inverse, and the nonzero sourced R return at first order delta^N. The full selected source and mixed coproducts remain present. This is an actual cut-current construction; its partial-Gaussian/internal-framing map remains the separate stated task. The [whole Fermat-trace source](whole_frobenius_source_fermat_trace.md) passes independently at every residue and parity. Its constant-frame ket retains beta divided by the ACTUAL Gaussian coefficient; that coefficient has root(-1)^(ks), leaving the stated triangular phase in the divided-kN expansion. The dual sign cancels the symmetric Gaussian root phase and gives binom(N,k). Each full deck block is exactly1+t, and the leftover degree<N is killed by the filter. The norm sign theta_s and all Z powers check as well; its fractional head norm/trace factors multiply to the original source character. For the first normal, zero-factor ratios have zero first relative log derivative. Grouping nonzero residues gives kN times the partial cotangent sum, with complementary partial sums equal; q partial_q=-2N partial_delta gives the printed ell_s sign. The flag derivative, whole cap-clock ratio and root-identity pair gauge are exact. This compares whole coupons only when all inserted operators and source connections are conjugated too; it does not equate their untransported quantum jets or bound their growing-N period norm. The [whole actual Ward-grid contraction](whole_high_color_ward_grid_contraction.md) passes independently with no correction. K separates head residues, the actual diagonal divided Cartan separates Fr blocks, and the selected ordinary/divided F edge entries read diagonal differences without ANY off-diagonal contamination. The comb subtree signs, trace-centered primitive and complete rational source row check. Its target is correctly im(delta), an explicit direct summand; the unrestricted four-row cokernel is not declared zero. In the stated hybrid root metric the inverse K and H gaps have the printed bounds. The normalized actual F edge has size at least one, the divided edge at least sqrt(r), and the path integration matrix has squared Frobenius norm D(r+N-1)/2. Orthogonal output pieces therefore give exactly the stated maximum norm bound. The selected e_D source has Hilbert--Schmidt norm one, so its homotopy cost is polynomial. Actual whole source units, grading, peripheral lines and all gauge adapters remain present. The two-word variant also checks: H+K/2 has simple full-grid root spectrum by the triangle inequality, and F+Fdiv has distinct one-step/N-step edge positions. Subtracting its action on the already recovered off-diagonal matrix is essential and is included. This is an actual finite-cut contraction, with its true mixed Hopf and pivotal current endpoints supplied by the cap theorem. It is not yet a nonzero map from the internal geometric period complex.

title: An actual high integral color carries the degree-N Frobenius wall row
text: # An actual high integral color carries the degree-N Frobenius wall row Research construction, 27 October 2026. The actual integral color of dimension N(r+1), specialized at the level-N root, has a classical Sym^r multiplicity space. Its generators are literal divided powers of the original quantum matrices, not an auxiliary classical source. For r=N a marked coherent co-source gives exactly the binomial wall row with N+1 entries. The original reduced knot scalar is retained by exact all-color periodicity. This constructs the wall functional as an actual color insertion. It does not yet intertwine both framing-current complexes, identify whole quantum jets of different colors, or prove selected geometric source survival or a volume norm. ## 1.
