The original integral matrix family Let N>=2, r>=0, m=N(r+1)-1, and let D_m(q) have its integral Weyl basis u_j, 0<=j<=m: \[ \begin{split} H u_j&=(m-2j)u_j,\quad K=q^H,\\ E u_j&=[m-j+1]_q u_{j-1},\qquad F u_j=[j+1]_q u_{j+1},\\ [a]_q&=(q^a-q^{-a})/(q-q^{-1}). \end{split} \tag{1.1} \] Out-of-range vectors are zero. These are the ACTUAL integral color matrices used in [all-color periodicity](cyclotomic_mellin_residue.md), not the generic-M typical module. Put q_N=exp(pi i/N), Q_N=q_N^2, and write j=kN+s with 0<=k<=r and 0<=s<N. Make the unit sign change \[ w_{k,s}=\beta_{k,s}u_{kN+s},\qquad \beta_{k,s}=(-1)^{Nk(k-1)/2+ks}. \tag{1.2} \] At the root, both ordinary block edges vanish: F at s=N-1 has coefficient [(k+1)N]=0, and E at s=0 has coefficient [(r+1-k)N]=0. With D_(N-1) denoting the Steinberg head, direct adjacent entries give \[ \begin{split} E&=I_{r+1}\otimes(-1)^rE_{\rm St},\qquad F=I_{r+1}\otimes F_{\rm St},\\ K&=I_{r+1}\otimes(-1)^rK_{\rm St},\\ H&=I_{r+1}\otimes H_{\rm St} +N\operatorname{diag}(r-2k)\otimes I_N. \end{split} \tag{1.3} \] For example the F coefficient before gauging is (-1)^k[s+1], and the consecutive beta ratio is (-1)^k. The E coefficient is (-1)^(r-k)[N-s], whose beta ratio gives (-1)^r[N-s]. The K and H identities follow from m-2j=N-1-2s+N(r-2k). Thus the ordinary small quantum action has r+1 invariant Steinberg blocks. The unrolled H is NOT constant on this multiplicity space. A map mixing k is not automatically an unrolled intertwiner. ## 2. Divided powers have a nonzero classical block action Keep the original generic matrices before specializing and define \[ \mathsf E=\left[E(q)^N/[N]_q!\right]_{q=q_N},\qquad \mathsf F=\left[F(q)^N/[N]_q!\right]_{q=q_N}. \tag{2.1} \] These ratios are regular matrix Laurent polynomials. On u_j their coefficients are the symmetric Gaussian polynomials \[ \mathsf F:u_j\longmapsto {j+N\brack N}_{q_N}u_{j+N},\qquad \mathsf E:u_j\longmapsto {m-j+N\brack N}_{q_N}u_{j-N}. \tag{2.2} \] Here boundary maps are zero. This is a regular integral division before specialization, not division of the zero root matrices. The needed Gaussian evaluation has an elementary proof. The identity \[ \prod_{j=0}^{a-1}(1+Q^jz) =\sum_h Q^{h(h-1)/2}{a\brack h}_Q z^h \] follows by coefficient induction. For a=AN+s, 0<=s<N, at Q_N the product is (1-(-z)^N)^A times a product of degree s. Its z^N coefficient, divided by Q_N^(N(N-1)/2)=(-1)^(N-1), gives \({AN+s\brack N}_{Q_N}=A\). The symmetric Gaussian convention is \({a\brack N}_q=q^{-N(a-N)}{a\brack N}_{q^2}\). Therefore before the beta gauge the signs and coefficients are exactly \[ \begin{split} \mathsf F u_{kN+s}&=(-1)^{kN+s}(k+1)u_{(k+1)N+s},\\ \mathsf E u_{kN+s}&=(-1)^{N(r+1-k)-1-s} (r+1-k)u_{(k-1)N+s}. \end{split} \tag{2.3} \] The beta ratios then give \[ \mathsf F w_{k,s}=(k+1)w_{k+1,s},\qquad \mathsf E w_{k,s}=\tau(r-k+1)w_{k-1,s},\quad \tau=(-1)^{Nr-1}. \tag{2.4} \] Consequently \[ e_{\rm cl}=\tau\mathsf E,\quad f_{\rm cl}=\mathsf F, \quad h_{\rm cl}w_{k,s}=(r-2k)w_{k,s} \tag{2.5} \] satisfy [e_cl,f_cl]=h_cl, [h_cl,e_cl]=2e_cl and [h_cl,f_cl]=-2f_cl. They are the ordinary irreducible Sym^r action on k and commute with the root E,F,K head action in (1.3). Their nilpotence order is r+1, so r=N has the degree-N string unavailable in a fixed number of original small-head factors. This is a SINGLE-COLOR divided action. Divided powers on tensor products have mixed coproduct terms. Its classical multiplicity action must not silently be substituted for that entire tensor action or for a Hopf action on all matrix observables. ## 3. The actual first-normal block edges recover the same generators Extend the sign frame (1.2) constantly in q, put Z=Q^N=q^(2N), delta=1-Z, and retain the actual generic matrices. Let F_cross and E_cross be just their between-block entries. They are divisible by delta. With rho=q_N-q_N^(-1), the exact regularized root values are \[ \begin{split} [F_{\rm cross}/\delta]_{q_N} &=\rho^{-1} f_{\rm cl}\otimes E_{0,N-1},\\ [E_{\rm cross}/\delta]_{q_N} &=(-1)^{r+1}\rho^{-1}e_{\rm cl}\otimes E_{N-1,0}. \end{split} \tag{3.1} \] To check every sign, the F edge has coefficient (-1)^k[(k+1)N]_q and the E edge has coefficient (-1)^(k-1)[(r+1-k)N]_q. For every positive integer a, \[ \left[\frac{[aN]_q}{1-Q^N}\right]_{q_N} =\frac{(-1)^{a+1}a}{\rho}. \tag{3.2} \] This follows by factoring Q^(aN)-1 by Q^N-1 before evaluating; no derivative of a singular quotient is inferred from root values. Equations (3.1) follow immediately. In the normal variable h=Log(q/q_N), delta=-2Nh+O(h^2), so the same entries are respectively -2N f_cl/rho and 2(-1)^r N e_cl/rho at first h-order. Thus the classical source is encoded canonically in the actual quantum-normal block edges. The root decomposition is not a product decomposition of the generic high-color module. ## 4. A coherent divided source gives exactly the binomial wall row On the multiplicity space write v_k for its basis. The actual divided operators in (2.5) construct the finite source and co-source \[ \psi_+=\exp(f_{\rm cl})v_0=\sum_{k=0}^rv_k,\qquad \lambda_+=2^{-r}v_0^*\exp(e_{\rm cl}), \quad \lambda_+(v_k)=2^{-r}{r\choose k}. \tag{4.1} \] Both exponentials terminate. Direct multiplication gives lambda_+(psi_+)=1. The rank-one coupon e_+=psi_+lambda_+ is idempotent and has trace one. These are Frobenius/divided coherent operators on the ACTUAL high integral color, not an ordinary Sym^r action postulated on the old fixed-N head. Let J=(J_0,...,J_r) be any array over a characteristic-zero commutative coefficient algebra, and insert its literal diagonal block operator diag(J_k) tensor I_N. Let P_s be any rank-one head coordinate projector and tau_high=Tr/[N(r+1)]. Then \[ (r+1)\tau_{\rm high} [(e_+\otimes P_s)(\operatorname{diag}J\otimes I_N)] =\frac1{N2^r}\sum_{k=0}^r{r\choose k}J_k. \tag{4.2} \] For r=N this is EXACTLY the actual wall row B_N(J), including its 1/N and the k=N endpoint. The coupling to the original Green array is explicit: the multiplicity block k takes the original entry J_k, equivalently the Kronecker coupling delta_(k,j). Formula (4.2) is valid pointwise for all remaining flow variables and hence after their finite sums. It applies to polynomial or retained logarithmic moment coefficients as a linear functional; no multiplication or Toeplitz-symbol identification is used. If P_s is replaced by I_N, the coherent functional has value one on the identity and the right side is N times (4.2). The marked rank-one head accounts for the wall normalization; it must not be dropped while claiming equality of source rows. This realizes B_N as a marked co-source on an actual larger color. It does not prove that the delta_(k,j) coupling intertwines the second framing current or its entire divided Hopf coproduct. Those equations must still be checked, with their endpoint carries. ### The coherent source has a canonical actual whole quantum germ There is no need to extend the root binomial row arbitrarily. The generic integral divided matrices E_N(q)=E(q)^N/[N]_q! and F_N(q)=F(q)^N/[N]_q! are regular, and preserve every residue s while moving the block index k. On the fixed s-string define \[ \begin{split} \Psi_s(q)&=\exp(F_N(q))w_{0,s},\\ \Lambda_s(q)&=2^{-r}w_{0,s}^*\exp(\tau E_N(q)),\\ u_s(q)&=\Lambda_s(q)\Psi_s(q),\qquad e_s(q)=\Psi_s(q)\Lambda_s(q)/u_s(q). \end{split} \tag{4.3} \] The finite exponentials terminate. At q_N, u_s=1 by (4.1), so its whole germ is a unit, with no root pole canceled by hand. Equation (4.3) is a regular idempotent of trace one. Different s-strings are disjoint, hence E_coh(q)=sum_s e_s(q) is an idempotent of trace N. For the ACTUAL generic high-color scalar long-knot operator, \[ \frac1N\operatorname{Tr}[E_{\rm coh}(q)C_{\rm high}(q)] =C_{N(r+1)}(Q) \tag{4.4} \] identically as a whole germ. The marked string e_s(q) gives the exact whole wall weights \(N^{-1}\Lambda_s\operatorname{diag}(J_k)\Psi_s/u_s\). At the root these reduce to (4.2). Their quantum derivatives are determined by the ORIGINAL divided matrices and the retained unit u_s, rather than inferred from the numerical binomial row. Equation (4.4) compares this color with itself. It is not an off-root equality with C_N(Q), and does not make e_s(q) an unrolled intertwiner or prove a current-complex map. ## 5. The reduced scalar is the original one; whole Q-jets are different The actual zero-framed long-knot operator on D_m(q) is C_(m+1)(Q) times identity, by the original integral color construction. Its regular root specialization is still scalar. The independently proved all-color identity gives \[ C_{N(r+1)}(Q_N)=C_N(Q_N)=K_N. \tag{5.1} \] Thus the normalized coherent functional with unmarked head identity returns K_N. Its marked wall version returns K_N/N, as expected from B_N(1)=1/N. The full original ADO normalization is still the old marked line eta_N K_N/N, with its peripheral meridian germ; one does NOT replace it by an imagined eta_(N(r+1))/[N(r+1)] line. The high-color meridian path before specializing is \[ M_{\rm high}=-q^{N(r+1)},\quad Y_{\rm high}=M_{\rm high}^2=Z^{r+1},\qquad M_{\rm low}=-q^N,\quad Y_{\rm low}=Z. \tag{5.2} \] At the root M_high=(-1)^r. In particular r=N uses the other lift at odd N. The one-dimensional shift and its zero-framing phase must be retained in comparing it with the original ideal lift. For the external modified-dimension line the exact sign-chart law is \(d_N(\sigma e^u)=\sigma^{1-N}d_N(e^u)\), with sigma=(-1)^r. Its retained adapter sigma^(N-1)=(-1)^(r(N-1)) is identically one when r=N. This does not install a new modified trace on the large ordinary Weyl module: the original external d_N line is retained. The fixed-color whole functions C_(N(r+1))(Q) and C_N(Q) have not been identified away from Q_N. Their normal meridian slopes already differ in (5.2), and (3.1) is the actual block-extension normal data. For a nontrivial adequate knot their different quadratic degree spans prove that the two whole Laurent polynomials are unequal. Consequently this source elevation is an exact ROOT and first-normal MODULE construction, not yet a source-preserving equality of the whole Q-jets needed by Mellin reconstruction. It supplies the missing degree-N wall representation while retaining the precise additional normal comparison which remains to be established. ## 6. Verification and remaining network map The following audit checks (1.3), every divided coefficient including both boundaries, the full classical commutators, coherent source and co-source normalization, the literal wall row, and both normal block edges at even, odd and composite levels. The actual high-color braiding/closure proof and its independent audit are recorded below. The remaining network question is whether the explicit block/Green coupling in (4.2), together with (3.1), transports the FULL actual two-current relative source complex. No cancellation of the second framing current or nonzero final geometric projection follows from the existence of the coherent wall row alone. [Divided-source audit](../experiments/audit_high_integral_color_frobenius_source.py). [Results](../experiments/high_integral_color_frobenius_source_results.json). ## 7. The actual braiding retains a definite mixed half-Cartan sign Here is an independent direct crossing and closure proof, with no tensor-product theorem used as a premise. Put n=N(r+1), m=n-1, and let W be the N-dimensional root color W=D_(N-1) tensor C_(Nr), H_W(i)=m-2i, 0<=i<N. In the gauged basis of Section 1 the high color has the same ordinary E,F,K as W on every block, while H_high(w_(a,i))=H_W(i)-2Na. The generic universal R specializes integrally: on integral Weyl vectors its kth factorial coefficient is a product of two Gaussian polynomials and [k]_q!. Thus every k>=N term vanishes at q_N; there is no division by [N] at the root. For k<N its nilpotent part preserves the two block indices and is exactly that of W. The remaining Cartan ratio is q_N^(-N[a H_W(j)+b H_W(i)]+2N^2ab) =epsilon^(a+b), epsilon=(-1)^m. (7.1) All head weights have parity m, so this sign is independent of i,j and the transfer. The same calculation applies whether the Cartan is evaluated before or after the nilpotent term, since the head weights change by even integers. Inversion retains the same sign. Consequently, for BOTH checked crossing signs, Rcheck_high^(+/-)(w_(a,i) tensor w_(b,j)) =epsilon^(a+b) sum_(k,l)(Rcheck_W^(+/-))_(ij)^(kl) w_(b,k) tensor w_(a,l). (7.2) The common highest-weight half-Cartan scalar is the original one on the marked exponential sheet. It is the same for high and W in (7.2); it is not set to one. The sign in (7.1) is genuinely nontrivial for some even/odd levels and block pairs. Thus the factorization is not an unmarked flip on arbitrary inserted arrays. Mixed source or current coupons must carry this sign. The original root pivot has no additional block factor: q_N^((1-N)(H_W(i)-2Na))=q_N^((1-N)H_W(i)). (7.3) The twist is also the same on every block. Shifting a highest weight m by -2Na changes the ordinary twist exponent h(h+2)/2 by -2Na(m+1)+2N^2a^2, whose q_N-power is one. For a CLOSED BRAID whose closure is one knot, the multiplicity index is transported by the permutation without changing along the component. Closure therefore makes it a single value a. Every mixed crossing sign in (7.2) is then epsilon^(2a)=1. Equations (7.3) and the twist calculation show that its reduced zero-framed head scalar is precisely the scalar of W. To compare W with the original Steinberg color, retain the one-dimensional shift h=Nr. With b braid strands and writhe w, the actual crossing constant is s_0=q_N^(h^2/2)(-1)^(r(N-1)), g_h=q_N^((1-N)h)=(-1)^(r(1-N)). The crossing index coboundaries telescope around the knot. Crossings contribute s_0^w, closed pivots g_h^(b-1), and the specified zero-framing twist contributes (s_0 g_h)^(-w). Their product is g_h^(b-1-w)=1, since the parity of a one-cycle braid permutation gives b-1-w even. This is the same direct phase calculation used in the [all-color periodicity proof](cyclotomic_mellin_residue.md). It proves for the ACTUAL high-color long-knot operator C_high(q_N)=K_N I_(N(r+1)). (7.4) In particular a normalized Frobenius source/co-source and the original head cut retain K_N exactly. The full ordinary normalized trace corresponds instead to the normalized trace on the multiplicity factor; both evaluate (7.4) to K_N. The wall coupon with a rank-one head projector has normalization 1/N, precisely as in (4.2), rather than normalization one. The old external modified-dimension line and its sign law remain those of Section 5. This proof compares actual ROOT periods. Whole generic colors and their quantum-normal slopes are different as (5.2) records. Nor does (7.4) identify inserted Green networks: their block-changing normal arrows and mixed signs require their literal couplings. [Independent signed-crossing and original-period audit](../experiments/audit_frobenius_high_color_braiding.py). [Results](../experiments/frobenius_high_color_braiding_results.json). ## 8. Coverage Divided-power quantum groups and Steinberg/Frobenius tensor structures are established representation-theoretic constructions. For coverage, [Sutton--Tubbenhauer--Wedrich--Zhu, 2105.07724](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.07724) studies SL2 tilting modules, quantum-number root conventions and integral divided-power models, including the complex root-of-unity case. No tensor-product, trace, or braiding proof from that paper is a premise here. The calculations above prove the explicit all-parity module signs, actual first-normal edge, coherent wall coupon, its whole high-color source germ, and the original marked scalar adapter in the conventions used by the actual knot state.

title: Coverage audit for the hyperbolic-knot target
text: # Coverage audit for the hyperbolic-knot target **29 October: fixed long fillings.** A further primary-source coverage check distinguished our fixed-twist, N-to-infinity statement from [Lee, 2307.09903](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.09903): its abstract first passes to a skein/categorical limit as twist counts tend to infinity and then relates the limiting evaluation to octahedral volumes. The abstract of [Galakhov et al.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physletb.2015.02.029) concerns a conjectured explicit formula for colored polynomials of arbitrary pretzels. [1101.2844](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.2844) concerns noncommutative A-polynomial computations for the restricted (-2,3,n) family and numerical volume-conjecture work. These scope checks supply no proof premise to the present full-source estimates or marked representation-volume comparison. They also do not justify a claim of novelty or an exhaustive absence of overlapping results. **29 October: augmented-base coverage check.** The new [complete augmented pretzel period proof](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md) is an independent original-source calculation, not a novelty claim. The abstract of van der Veen's [augmented knotted trivalent graph paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.0094) states volume-conjecture coverage for augmented KTGs and an arithmetic containing-link corollary. The abstract and introductory scope of [Ibarra--McQuire--Purcell](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09296) concern OCTAHEDRAL fully augmented links and a Turaev--Viro result without half twists; the published introduction also records earlier Kashaev coverage for octahedral fully augmented links. These are coverage statements, not proof inputs to the new finite-source, recurrence or Gaussian arguments. They do not by themselves classify the exact overlap with every non-octahedral s-antiprism base here. No claim that this base family was previously uncovered is made. Its complete augmented links must also be distinguished from the fixed-slope filled knots, which the new base theorem does not settle. Research record, 25 October 2026. Hyperbolicity is a standing assumption. The user permits an unbounded, sufficiently broad knot class, and requests literature checks for coverage rather than proof techniques. Accordingly, the external statements below are not hypotheses accepted on the authority of their proofs. No proof section of these papers is needed for this audit. ## 1. Keep the quantum object fixed The target is Kashaev's original invariant and volume conjecture, approached through a literature-defined quantum A-module and its distinguished period. The later Andersen--Kashaev meridian state and Andersen--Malusa b-shift annihilator are comparison objects. An annihilating equation alone does not select a solution or its normalization. An AK volume theorem does not settle the original conjecture without the corresponding comparison. The independent local and analytic arguments in the existing notes may duplicate stated literature coverage. That is independent verification, not evidence of a new theorem about previously uncovered knots. ## 2. Checked coverage statements | Source and statement checked | Stated scope | Consequence for this project | | --- | --- | --- | | Ben Aribi--Wong, [2410.10776v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10776v2), abstract and introductory theorems | Jones-function existence for FAMED one-cusped hyperbolic manifolds with H2=0; geometricity adds the AK volume asymptotic. The paper includes all hyperbolic twist knots. | Our twist-family theorem and positive FAMED saddle theorem overlap this coverage. They remain useful as independently audited arguments. | | Ben Aribi--Guilloux--Wong, [2512.17437v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17437v1), abstract | FAMED geometric realizations for more than 42,000 knot complements, including the stated crossing and tetrahedron census ranges. | Additional isolated small-knot certificates do not establish an unbounded new class. The census claim is not a uniform membership theorem. | | Wong, [2512.23198v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23198v1), Definitions 1.1 and 1.5, Theorems 1.11 and 1.14, Corollary 1.16 | A full-tensor theorem for generalized FAMED semi-geometric triangulations; the Jones-function theorem imposes additional longitude/meridian conditions. Definition 1.5(2) excludes a longitude-dependent affine shape plane. Definition 1.5(3) prescribes a meridian without a longitude shear. | The generalized singular reduction already has substantial stated overlap. Our moving-plane Fourier construction removes a condition appearing in this particular statement, but this alone is not new knot-family coverage. | | Wong, [2609.33922v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.33922v2#S1.SS2), Theorems 1.1 and 1.4, Remark 1.2 | A KLV volume/torsion theorem for geometric triangulations; an RT-type function for angle-supporting triangulations with a suitable quad type; a weighted squared-norm factorization. Agreement of the RT-type function with the AK Jones function is asserted on FAMED data. The remark defines an AK analogue more generally. | This is close to our Fourier constructions. Its stated general KLV theorem does not by itself identify the original AK meridian state or its quantum A-operator. The introduction also explicitly leaves full invariance unresolved. | | Liu--Ming--Sun--Wu--Yang, [2608.16560v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16560), abstract | Cusped modular-double Turaev--Viro-type invariants with an exponential volume law. | A broad volume theorem for this literature object is already claimed. Equivalence with our selected AK state would still require a precise map and normalization. | | Ge, [2609.27635v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27635v1), Theorem 1.1 and Sections 2--4 | Every finite-volume cusped hyperbolic 3-manifold admits a finite geometric ideal triangulation realizing completeness. | At the user's subsequent request, the affine-subdivision argument was independently audited, with exact stress tests. See the separate audit. A global branching and the quantum cycle comparison are additional requirements. | The last three entries are recent coverage changes. They must be retained when assessing the scope of any proposed theorem here. The user separately authorized a proof audit of Ge's geometric result; that authorization does not extend to importing the quantum papers' proof techniques. For the principal algebraic direction, Guilloux--Marche, [1804.01395](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01395), already studies exact polynomials, a class containing knot A-polynomials, and their volume functions. Its definitions and stated coverage identify classical regulator exactness as existing theory. A quantum theorem still has to identify the distinguished period and its normalization. The [intrinsic norm-torsor note](intrinsic_quantum_a_norm_torsor.md) reconstructs the required elementary descent arguments independently. ### All-level state and torsor coverage The following are definitions and stated scope, not imported proofs: * Murakami--Murakami, [math/9905075](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9905075), states the Kashaev/colored-Jones comparison for all levels. Our crossing note reconstructs the needed matrix and period identities directly. This is independent verification of known coverage. * Baseilhac--Benedetti, [1101.1851](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.1851), states an odd-level quantum-hyperbolic/Kashaev comparison. Its link specialization uses the trivial ambient character. It must not be silently replaced by a fixed hyperbolic character of the complement. * Willetts, [2003.09854](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.09854), states an all-knot completion unifying ADO and colored Jones, with the Alexander factor retained. That unification and its recursion-ideal theorem have not been adopted here. Our modified-dimension gauge is proved from the defining finite matrices instead. The later [Frobenius Verma calculation](frobenius_verma_period.md) independently proves the stated root normalization ADO/Delta by untruncated crossing coefficients and the polynomial-block trace. It also proves equality of the actual root annihilator ideals under this central factor. It does not identify the generic completion or adopt a colored-Jones recursion comparison. * Garoufalidis--Scholze--Wheeler--Zagier, [2412.04241v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04241v2), introduces proposed K3-graded Habiro modules. The user subsequently requested a separate [independent audit](gswz_printed_definition_audit.md). It confirms counterexamples to the printed unrestricted Theorems 1 and 2: the local span need not be finitely generated, and the global set need not be additive. It also verifies formula errors in (114) and (165). Theorem 5 restricts to specified good root orders; the supplied examples do not directly refute its restricted membership conclusion, which remains independently unverified here. No theorem from this paper is a premise of the A-curve torsor construction or its requested volume comparison. The direct [ADO pointing proof](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) also identifies a structural limitation of a fixed-level approach: rational root states have a central shift sector v=1. Retaining the original quantum family and its pointing is necessary before comparing with the geometric classical A-curve. A finite splitting torsor alone is insufficient. The subsequent [finite cut-state proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md) now independently establishes a nonzero actual all-level meridian annihilator for every knot. It does not adopt the literature holonomicity or recursion-ideal comparison theorems. The [triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md) specifies the remaining geometric-symbol, relative-source, and regulator-norm comparison. These existence results do not establish the volume conjecture for a broad knot class. ## 3. What alternatingness supplies and what it does not Menasco's diagrammatic checkerboard decomposition is useful combinatorial data. It must not be identified automatically with a decomposition into right-angled cells in the complete hyperbolic metric. Gan, [2005.07904v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.07904), classifies alternating links with both checkerboard surfaces totally geodesic as three links, with octahedral, cuboctahedral and icosidodecahedral projection graphs, and characterizes them as right-angled completely realisable. Thus the strong geometric interpretation is highly restrictive. This coverage statement does not invalidate the combinatorial Menasco decomposition. An augmented link and a knot obtained by filling its crossing circles are also different manifolds. A right-angled augmented-link realization, or a TV volume theorem for it, cannot be transferred to the filled knot without a separate quantum filling argument. ## 4. What would count as closing a broad class here The present independent theorem covers every globally branched complete strictly positive geometric knot triangulation, for its specifically normalized tensor-derived meridian state. The remaining requirements are not additional finite rank scans: 1. Uniform membership of a stated unbounded knot class in the hypotheses, established independently if a literature existence proof is not used. 2. Identification of the selected literature state across the required realizations, with its peripheral functions, phase and cycle retained. 3. Application of the independently proved volume and annihilator results to this same state. Hyperbolic two-bridge knots beyond twist knots and suitable highly twisted alternating families are possible class targets. The sources checked here do not state an unconditional all-two-bridge or all-alternating AK theorem. This search result is not a claim that no such theorem exists elsewhere. Selecting a new matrix condition on knots already in a stated census does not satisfy the uniform-class requirement. ## 5. Subsequent steering The user explicitly rejected further reduction of the main objective to FAMED or other chart-by-chart AK hypotheses. The principal direction is the intrinsic period torsor and general algebraic properties of the A-polynomial. The geometric existence input is audited separately in [ge_geometric_triangulation_audit.md](ge_geometric_triangulation_audit.md).

title: The identity cut has an exact orientation-cover source
text:
# The identity cut has an exact orientation-cover source 27 October 2026. This is a finite whole-source identity for the actual four-port tensor. It replaces neither the state nor its selected cap. It introduces an orientation factor together with its compensating measure, keeps the cap's marked sheet, and retains every finite band. The comparison with the geometric momentum below is a principal local comparison; a whole Gaussian/source comparison is not inferred. ## 1. Retain the original cap and every port band Use the literal tensor and port order of [the physical two-cut construction](actual_two_cut_framing_port_reconstruction.md). With zero extension outside all four physical ranges, put \[ \mathcal F_T(x,y;\xi,\eta) =\sum_{a,b,\mu,
u}T_{a+\mu,b+
u;a,b} x^a y^b\xi^\mu\eta^
u. \] The first original balanced cut has matrix coefficients 1/N; the second cut closes by its original identity, without a new pivotal weight. Thus, with all original pivots and external scalar lines already inside T, \[ F(\eta)=\mathcal F_T(1,1;1,\eta),\qquad \Phi_{m id}(T)= rac1N[\eta^0]F =\mathop{m Res}_{\eta=0}F(\eta) rac{d\eta}{N\eta}. 	ag{1} \] The sums over the first output and input remain in F. This is not the normalized trace of a reshaped two-position matrix. In particular, charged current tensors use all their first-port bands as in (1). The same formula works coefficientwise for every whole crossing or source coupling; no specialization of those coefficients is required. ## 2. An exact orientation factor with the compensating measure Introduce the quadratic cover \[ u=\eta+\eta^{-1},\qquad v=\eta-\eta^{-1},\qquad v^2=u^2-4. \] Its involution is eta to eta inverse, fixing u and changing v to -v. On this cover the following is a literal equality of rational forms: \[  oxed{\quad F(\eta) rac{d\eta}{N\eta} =[vF(\eta)] rac{du}{N(u^2-4)}.\quad} 	ag{2} \] Indeed du=v d eta/eta. Consequently the original source equals the marked residue of the orientation-twisted section G=vF against the new measure. The multiplication by v is the nearest-band difference on the full kernel. Its compensating measure is essential. There is a precise parity qualification. G is odd if F is even under eta inversion. For arbitrary actual T the correct law is instead \[ G\circ\iota=-v(F\circ\iota). 	ag{3} \] Thus (2) is an orientation twist without an assumed involution symmetry of the whole braid word. It does not declare the scalar function G odd when the actual tensor does not have that symmetry. Multiplication M_v identifies the full Laurent kernel space with its submodule v times that space. On this image every actual linear current A transports as M_v A M_v inverse, and its co-source transports by (2). The inverse is used only on that image. This is a strict source-preserving change of presentation, not division by a possibly vanishing selected period. All endpoint/corner summands are part of the same full kernel. ## 3. The original cap marks the sheet at infinity The point eta=0 determines a particular preimage of u=infinity: \[ v/u\longrightarrow-1,\qquad \eta=(u+v)/2,\qquad t=1/u= rac{\eta}{1+\eta^2}=\eta+O(\eta^3). 	ag{4} \] The last equality gives an actual local uniformizer of order one. Residues in eta and t therefore agree, including their signs. On this sheet v is asymptotic to -u. For a constant F, the right side of (2) is asymptotic to -F du/(Nu), whose standard residue at u=infinity is +F/N. The other preimage, eta=infinity and v/u tending to +1, has residue -F/N. Taking an unmarked sum of the two sheet residues would cancel this constant cap. The original tensor fixes the first sheet in (4); there is no additional choice of an odd cycle. The apparent poles of du/(u^2-4) at u=2,-2 introduce no new poles in the TOTAL form: at eta=1,-1 the factor G=vF cancels them. This uses the actual finite Laurent nature of F. The measure may not be evaluated independently and then assigned its own endpoint terms. ## 4. A finite tail formula, not just the nearest coefficient Write F=sum F_j eta^j and G=sum G_j eta^j. Near the marked eta=0, \[  rac{du}{Nv^2}= rac{d\eta}{N(\eta^2-1)} =- rac1N\sum_{k\geq0}\eta^{2k}d\eta. \] Consequently the exact new source is \[ \Psi(G)=- rac1N\sum_{k\geq0}G_{-2k-1}. 	ag{5} \] Only finitely many coefficients contribute for any actual tensor. Since G_j=F_(j-1)-F_(j+1), the partial sum through k=K is \[ - rac1N\sum_{k=0}^K G_{-2k-1} = rac{F_0-F_{-2K-2}}N. 	ag{6} \] The final coefficient outside the full support vanishes, proving Psi(vF)=F_0/N exactly. Formula (6) is the retained finite endpoint term. Dropping it early, using only -G_-1/N, or replacing (5) by the constant coefficient of vF changes the source. For the literal two-cut unknot tensor, which is the flip tensor, \[ F_{m unknot}(\eta) =\sum_{j=-(N-1)}^{N-1}(N-|j|)\eta^j. 	ag{7} \] The original cap and (5) both give one. The constant coefficient of vF is zero. Keeping only -G_-1/N gives 2/N for N at least two; the remaining finite tail contributes (N-2)/N. This actual tensor already detects the distinction between an odd insertion at the old source and the source-preserving orientation change (2). ## 5. Whole clocks and their connection term Let r be an invertible whole clock parameter. The change eta to r eta acts on the cover by \[  egin{split} u_r&=	frac12(r+r^{-1})u+	frac12(r-r^{-1})v,\ v_r&=	frac12(r-r^{-1})u+	frac12(r+r^{-1})v. \end{split} 	ag{8} \] It preserves u squared minus v squared and the marked eta=0 point. It also preserves the original logarithmic measure exactly: \[  rac{du_r}{v_r}= rac{du}{v},\qquad \iota\,	au_r\,\iota=	au_{r^{-1}}, 	ag{8a} \] where tau_r is eta to r eta and iota is eta to eta inverse. For the actual whole Q dilation set r=Q in (8). These transports form the multiplicative torus with its inversion involution; the resulting group is dihedral in this precise sense, not automatically nilpotent. At a primitive finite root the dilation itself has finite order. None of these identities drops its whole normal dependence before specialization. For G=vF the actual transformed section representing F(r eta) is \[ \widetilde S_rG= rac{v}{v_r}G(u_r,v_r). 	ag{9} \] In particular a clock does not act by an unaccompanied u substitution. Writing D=eta partial_eta=v partial_u+u partial_v, differentiation of (9) gives the exact connection \[ \widetilde D=D-u/v,\qquad M_v D=\widetilde D M_v, \qquad (\widetilde DG) rac{du}{Nv^2}= rac1N d(G/v). 	ag{10} \] Its marked residue is zero. All finite clock derivatives follow before taking any quantum normal or large-N limit. Although (9)-(10) have denominators, the corresponding sections lie in the transported image and the total original form is retained. Physical port clocks have mixed kernel actions. In the full kernel, input clocks Q^a,Q^b act by x to Qx,y to Qy; output clocks Q^(a+mu), Q^(b+nu) act by (x,xi) to (Qx,Qxi) and (y,eta) to (Qy,Qeta). Thus (8)-(10) transport precisely the eta component while keeping the simultaneous y rescaling for an output clock. General boundary braiding/prefix adapters still act in their original order. Independent whole crossing couplings commute with M_v, and differentiating them preserves (2), (5) and every finite endpoint in (6). ## 6. Compatibility with the actual prefix framing cover The independent proof of [the actual prefix chart](prefix_adapted_two_position_framing_cover.md) retains U=mu_j...mu_1, V=mu_(j-1)...mu_1, k=ell_U/ell_V and \[ z=s(k-1),\qquad D=(-1)^jz(p-p^{-1}),\qquad \Omega_{cut}= rac{\ell_V}{BD}d\log A\wedge d\log B. 	ag{11} \] Here p is the actual balanced local wave momentum and B=1/k at completeness. The two nearest actual output exchange bands have principal ratios p inverse and p, respectively. Distinguish the finite Fourier-band variable eta_F in Sections 1--5 from the geometric parameter eta_geo=p inverse. The boundary action gives the principal Fourier incidence eta_F p=1. This is not a coordinate isomorphism of the original source spaces or a map of their cycles. On this incidence the geometric orientation factor is \[ v_{geo}=p^{-1}-p,\qquad D=(-1)^{j+1}zv_{geo}. 	ag{12} \] The orientation factor of the exact cap cover consequently has the correct geometric sign line. Retaining the actual inverse-prefix clock, whose whole expression is (q/M)^(j-1) product_(i<j) Q^(J_i), gives the principal equality \[ \ell_V^{-1}(R_{(+1,-1),0}-R_{(-1,+1),0})\Omega_{cut} = rac{(-1)^{j+1}}{Bz}d\log A\wedge d\log B. 	ag{13} \] The density alone is not generally odd: ell_V can differ on the two sheets. Formula (13) includes precisely the prefix factor that would be lost by substituting a developed meridian for the physical one. Equations (2) and (13) are compatible orientation formulas on that incidence; they are not an equality of their whole selected period complexes. In particular eta_F and the physical position B are independent before that correspondence. Closing the second port by the eta_F constant term does not sum its input position b or identify that sum with a physical B cycle. The marked residue in (4)-(6) involves all finite bands and their endpoint, whereas the existing transverse Gaussian theorem handles fixed bounded port offsets on a regular interior chart. Transporting that full residue/endpoint through the Gaussian comparison remains necessary. In particular (13) alone is not permission to insert a new odd observable into the original knot period. There is also a direct comparison with the UNINSERTED principal cap measure, including its rational base Jacobian. Write sigma=(-1)^j, t_W=Tr W and \[ A_0=c_U+s t_U,\qquad A_1=c_V+s t_V. \] In the reference frame Tr(JC)=c_C+t_C. In the moving cut frame it is s(beta-gamma)+(1-s)t_C. Using (4.1) of the prefix note gives \[ u_{geo}=p+p^{-1}= rac{\sigma(A_0-kA_1)}{s(k-1)},\qquad \left. rac{\partial u}{\partial k}ight|_s = rac{\sigma(A_1-A_0)}{s(k-1)^2}. 	ag{14} \] The extra s derivative vanishes after wedging with d log A. Together with D=-sigma s(k-1)v and the density in (11), this proves \[  oxed{\quad  rac{\Omega_{cut}}{\ell_V} = rac{k-1}{A_1-A_0}\,d\log A\wedge rac{du_{geo}}{v_{geo}} = rac{k-1}{A_1-A_0}\,d\log A\wedge rac{d\eta_{geo}}{\eta_{geo}}. \quad} 	ag{15} \] This equality is on the further regular chart A_1-A_0 nonzero and k not one. It includes the actual inverse-prefix clock ell_V inverse and an explicit rational Jacobian on the two-position base. Applying (2) to the final one-form in (15) gives the same orientation-twisted section and compensating measure as an algebraic formula. To use it for the period still requires an actual transform of the source and its physical input-position sum. No such transform follows from (15). For a genuine quadratic prefix this Jacobian chart is generically nonempty; a linear prefix or exceptional first-position fiber requires another coordinate rather than division by its vanishing Jacobian. Formula (15) identifies the geometric density's algebraic one-form shape with the logarithmic measure appearing in the finite cap. It does not identify their source functionals, transport the marked eta_F=0 cap, sum the independent physical input-position b, or carry the finite tail (6) through the transverse Gaussian. Those remain the precise global comparison data. ### 6.1. The geometric compactification has a zero-residue boundary There is an exact algebraic boundary test on the geometric incidence cover, not an image of the original marked finite cap or its cycle. In this subsection eta means eta_geo and u,v are its cover coordinates. Solving (14) for k gives \[ k= rac{su+\sigma A_0}{su+\sigma A_1},\qquad k-1= rac{\sigma(A_0-A_1)}{su+\sigma A_1}. 	ag{16} \] At the geometric eta_geo=0 boundary, u is asymptotic to eta inverse and v to minus eta inverse. Consequently \[ k-1= rac{\sigma(A_0-A_1)}s\eta+O(\eta^2),\qquad D\longrightarrow A_0-A_1. 	ag{17} \] At the other preimage eta=infinity the limit is D=A_1-A_0. The two points of this GEOMETRIC compactification reach k=1, or physical B=1, on two algebraic sheets. This does not say that the original eta_F cap maps to either point. At k=1 one has det(U-V)=0, so the exact discriminant is (A_0-A_1)^2. If c_U-c_V is nonzero, the root formula r=(c_C+s h_C-D)/(2c_C) shows that r, and hence ell_V, is finite at (17). On this regular boundary chart, \[  rac{\ell_V(k-1)}{A_1-A_0} =- rac{\sigma\ell_V(0)}s\eta+O(\eta^2). 	ag{18} \] Thus the full leading framing density Omega_cut itself is regular at that geometric boundary and has ZERO eta_geo logarithmic residue. The apparent eta logarithm in (15) is canceled by its rational Jacobian. A nonzero cap source cannot be obtained by discarding that Jacobian and declaring a regular constant amplitude there, even if a proposed source map assigned the cap to that boundary. This is a property of the principal prefix chart, not an assertion that such a source map exists or that the selected quantum period vanishes. For example the genuine figure-eight prefix in Section 6 of the prefix note, at s=1 and u_shape squared plus u_shape plus one equal to zero, has \[ c_U-c_V=1,\quad A_0-A_1=3+u_{shape},\quad r\longrightarrow-2,\quad \ell_V\longrightarrow2+3u_{shape}. \] All displayed regularity conditions hold there. For a scalar meromorphic amplitude a(eta), the exact residual to compute is \[ [\eta^0]\left(a(\eta)  rac{\ell_V(k-1)}{A_1-A_0}ight)d\log A. 	ag{19} \] A holomorphic amplitude gives zero. If its only negative term is a_-1/eta, the result is -sigma ell_V(0) a_-1/s times d log A; larger poles require the corresponding full finite coefficient sum in (19). The actual finite kernel has negative Fourier-band powers whose order grows with N. They cannot be substituted into a(eta_geo) without the actual source transform. That transform must retain the original source, norm, physical input-position sum, endpoints and any escaping/polar block contribution. The bounded interior Gaussian theorem does not evaluate (19) as the original cap. [The actual boundary-moment and Ward-atom calculation](actual_negative_band_boundary_moment_and_ward_atom.md) makes this distinction testable. The finite weighted negative-band functional is exactly an original source paired with a K-Ward current and does not equal the identity source on actual signed tensors. An original negative factorial circuit does supply an explicit inverse-norm pole, but its presence in the selected full geometric source is a separate transport question. ## 7. Reproducible actual tensor checks [The independent audit script](../experiments/audit_identity_cut_orientation_cover.py) uses literal signed braid tensors with their original pivotal, half-Cartan, framing and peripheral scalar lines. It checks (1), (5)-(6), the unknot formula, whole input/output clock rescalings and the connection (10). It also tests the same finite source formula on every port matrix unit with endpoint indices included. The results are recorded in [the audit output](../experiments/identity_cut_orientation_cover_results.json). These checks validate the finite source change; they are not a global geometric period or volume asymptotic calculation.

title: Actual integral-color coherent symbols, uniformly including the poles
text: # Actual integral-color coherent symbols, uniformly including the poles Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual integral N-color family admits a globally regular polynomial source frame. Its generator symbols have exact finite formulas and uniform expansions on the entire real compact source, including both poles. Moving q and the integral color together gives the expected exponential clock. An explicit flag shear compares its principal moment matrix with the varying-meridian Grothendieck chart. Every change of frame below is an exact diagonal quantum-factorial change of the actual representation and source. Its large size cannot be discarded when comparing selected periods. Uniform asymptotics of the individual generators do not prove uniform asymptotics of the full R word. The exact symmetric whole-q-difference model is developed in [the global integral-color source note](integral_color_global_q_difference_source.md). The quantitative frame norm, its dilogarithmic generating function, and the root flag-current bookkeeping are given in [the quantum-factorial source comparison](quantum_factorial_frames_and_cyclotomic_source.md). ## 1. The actual integral family and its polynomial frame Fix N>=2, put n=N-1, and use c=2pi*i, s=c lambda, 0<=lambda<=1, q=exp(s/(2N)), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), M=-q^N, m=q^N=exp(s/2). Write `[j]_q=(q^j-q^(-j))/rho`, with its Laurent-polynomial continuation when rho=0. In the ordinary-falling polynomial frame the actual integral module has F e_j=(n-j)e_(j+1), E e_j=[j]_q[N-j]_q/(N-j)e_(j-1), K e_j=q^(n-2j)e_j. (1) The absent boundary edges are zero. Put Ecal=rho E and Fcal=rho F. These are the operators compared below. They satisfy exactly K Ecal K^(-1)=Q Ecal, K Fcal K^(-1)=Q^(-1) Fcal, Fcal Ecal+qK+q^(-1)K^(-1)=(q^N+q^(-N))I. (2) For example the diagonal entry of Fcal Ecal is `rho^2[j]_q[N-j]_q`; expanding the two q-numbers proves (2). Use the same actual compact coherent kernel as before: sigma_C(v,z)=sum_(i,j=0)^n v^i C_ij binom(n,j)z^j /(1+vz)^n. Its globally regular source coordinates are T=vz/(1+vz), a=z/(1+vz), b=v/(1+vz), ab=T(1-T), a=T/v, b=v(1-T), Omega_0=dv wedge da. On the compact real source `z=bar(v)`, both |a| and |b| are at most one half, and 0<=T<=1. The pole-chart change is `V=1/v, a'=v-v^2a`. ## 2. Exact finite-N symbols have no polar singularities Let R_x(T)=1+(x-1)T, W_N(T)=q^N+q^(-N)-q^(-N)R_Q(T)^N -q^N R_(Q^-1)(T)^N. Then the exact actual symbols are sigma_K=q^n R_(Q^-1)(T)^n, sigma_(K^-1)=q^(-n)R_Q(T)^n, sigma_A=R_Q(T)^n, A e_j=Q^j e_j, sigma_Fcal=n rho b, sigma_Ecal=a H_N(T), H_N(T)=W_N(T)/[N rho T(1-T)]. (3) The apparent divisions in the last formula are removable. Indeed W_N is a polynomial which vanishes exactly at T=0 and T=1, so it is divisible by T(1-T). It is also divisible by rho^2 as a Laurent polynomial in q, making rho=0 removable. Its two endpoint values agree: H_N(0)=H_N(1)=q^n-q^(-n). (4) Thus (3) is a globally regular source function, including its two pole fibers, not just a formula on the open torus. Here is the short coefficient proof. In the Ecal kernel use binom(n,j)/(N-j)=binom(N,j)/N, rho^2[j]_q[N-j]_q =q^N+q^(-N)-q^(2j-N)-q^(N-2j). Extend the sum to j=0,N, where its summand is zero. The binomial theorem gives W_N divided by `N rho v(1-T)`; since `T/v=a`, this is exactly (3). The Fcal formula follows from `sum_j(n-j)binom(n,j)x^j=n(1+x)^(n-1)`. ## 3. Uniform asymptotics hold on the entire compact source Define the whole principal functions A_inf=exp(sT), k=m exp(-sT), f=s b, W(T)=m+m^(-1)-k-k^(-1) =4sinh(sT/2)sinh(s(1-T)/2), H(T)=W(T)/[sT(1-T)], e=a H(T). (5) Every apparent division in (5) is removable, including s=0. For each fixed nonnegative integer l there is a finite constant C_l, independent of N and lambda in [0,1], such that in smooth coordinate norms on the whole real compact source ||sigma_A-A_inf||_(C^l) +||sigma_K-k||_(C^l) +||sigma_(K^-1)-k^(-1)||_(C^l) +||sigma_Ecal-e||_(C^l) +||sigma_Fcal-f||_(C^l) <= C_l/N. (6) The following proof includes the endpoint estimates. For fixed S and l, the binomial exponent has the elementary bound ||R_(exp(s/N))(T)^N-exp(sT)||_(C^l[0,1]) <=C_(S,l)|s|^2/N (7) for |s|<=S. For large N expand the logarithm of `1+(exp(s/N)-1)T`; its difference from sT/N and its fixed T derivatives are uniformly bounded. Alternatively differentiate the binomial power explicitly. The two first s coefficients are identical, giving the |s|^2 factor. The finitely many smaller N have the same bound by compactness after dividing out s^2. Apply (7) to W_N-W with two extra T derivatives. This difference vanishes at both endpoints. For any such function g, g(T)/[T(1-T)] =-T integral_0^1 y g''(Ty)dy -(1-T)integral_0^1 y g''(1-(1-T)y)dy. (8) Differentiation of (8) bounds its C^l norm by a fixed multiple of the C^(l+2) norm of g, with no endpoint loss. Moreover `N rho/s=sin(pi lambda/N)/(pi lambda/N)` is bounded below by 2/pi on this family. Equations (7)--(8) therefore give ||H_N-H||_(C^l[0,1])<=C_l |s|/N. The corresponding Fcal bound follows from `n rho=s+O(|s|/N)`. The K and clock estimates use (7) and the one missing power n=N-1. Multiplication by the globally smooth functions a,b proves (6) in both compact pole charts. This also proves uniformity at lambda=0; it does not divide a nonzero estimate by a vanishing rho without its |s| factor. The exact star product is still required for finite matrices. Ordinary products of symbols equal the classical products only in this controlled principal limit. In particular (2) gives the principal Casimir identity `ef+k+k^(-1)=m+m^(-1)`. ## 4. The moving-q clock and the actual principal moment matrix The actual simultaneous path has `M=-q^N=-m`, so the principal Gauss parameter is x=-M=m. Its clock is precisely A_inf=exp(sT), k=x/A_inf. (9) Thus moving q really changes its frequency from c to c lambda. Changing only M at fixed q_N would not do that. Where its factors are nonzero, the old balanced momentum is p_bal=(1-A_inf)/f =(1-exp(sT))/[s v(1-T)]. (10) The full moment matrix is globally regular even where this particular momentum chart fails: mu=[k,e;k f,m+m^(-1)-k], det mu=1. (11) Its eigenvalues are m and m^(-1). The actual knot-meridian sign in the old convention is `-mu`, since M=-m. At lambda=1 its projective sign gives the complete physical meridian. All M and SL2 sign markings are retained; choosing one of the two eigenflags is additional augmented data. For the m-eigenflag use the slope v_geo in `[1:v_geo]`. Directly, v_geo=(m-k)/e=k f/(k-m^(-1)) =r_s(T)v, r_s(T)=s(1-T)/(1-exp[-s(1-T)]). (12) Consequently (11) is exactly the whole Grothendieck matrix from [the exponential detour](compact_exponential_cech_current_detour.md) evaluated at `(T,v_geo)`. The source shear (v,a)->(r_s(T)v,a/r_s(T)) preserves T and Omega_0 exactly, because `Omega_0=-dT wedge dlog v`. For lambda<1 it is regular on the whole real compact sphere. In this ordinary-falling frame it becomes singular at lambda=1,T=0. This particular singularity is frame dependent, as the next section proves. The other eigenflag, corresponding to the original inverse-cut marking `M^(-1)=-m^(-1)` on `-mu`, has slope v_inv=s v(1-T)/(1-exp(sT)). (13) Equations (12)--(13) must not be silently interchanged. ## 5. An exact quantum-factorial change removes the first flag artifact The symmetric q-falling frame has E_q e_j=[j]_q e_(j-1), F_q e_j=[n-j]_q e_(j+1). Its change from (1) is diagonal. If `e'_j=g_j e_j`, then g_0=1, g_(j+1)/g_j=(n-j)/[n-j]_q. All these factors are nonzero on 0<=lambda<=1. The exact finite symbols in this frame are sigma_(rho E_q)=[R_q(T)^n-R_(q^-1)(T)^n]/v, sigma_(rho F_q)=v[q^nR_(q^-1)(T)^n-q^(-n)R_q(T)^n]. (14) Their endpoint divisions are removable, and the same elementary binomial argument proves uniform C^l convergence on the entire compact sphere to e_sym=2sinh(sT/2)/v, f_sym=2v sinh(s(1-T)/2), k=m exp(-sT). (15) The m-eigenflag now has the regular slope v_+=exp(s(1-T)/2)v, (16) through lambda=1, including both poles. The inverse eigenflag is v_-=-exp(-sT/2) sinh(s(1-T)/2)/sinh(sT/2) v. (17) For lambda<1 it reverses the two pole flags, whereas at lambda=1 the ratio of the two sines is one and (17) equals (16). The two corner limits `(lambda,T)=(1,0),(1,1)` therefore retain the inverse-flag collision/bubble data. Regularity of (16) does not justify deleting that augmentation information. The exact principal comparison is b_s(T)=2sinh(s(1-T)/2)/[s(1-T)], e=b_s e_sym, f=f_sym/b_s. (18) Equivalently use the symplectic source shear `v_sym=v/b_s(T), a_sym=b_s(T)a`. At lambda=1,T=0, b_s vanishes; the ordinary-frame pole in (12) is thus a basis artifact. These are exact matrix and principal-coordinate comparisons, not a boundedness assertion about the changing frame. ## 6. The original balanced word and pointed source are retained exactly There is also an explicit exact adapter to the existing balanced integral module. In that frame F_bal v_j=(1-Q^(j+1))v_(j+1), Ecal_bal v_j=(M Q^(-j)-M^(-1))v_(j-1). At M=-q^N define d_j=(Q;Q)_j/[rho^j(n)_j] =(-1)^j q^(j(j+1)/2)[j]_q!/(n)_j, D=diag(d_j), d_0=1. (19) Here `(n)_j=n(n-1)...(n-j+1)`. The second expression makes lambda=0 removable, with value `(-1)^j j!/(n)_j`. Every d_j is nonzero on the full real path, including lambda=1. Directly, D^(-1)F_bal D=rho F, D^(-1)Ecal_bal D=rho E, D^(-1)K D=K. (20) For the second identity use `M Q^(-j)-M^(-1)=-rho q^(-j)[N-j]_q`. Thus (20) is an exact quantum-factorial frame of the actual integral representation, not a newly ordered classical polynomial. Conjugating every strand by D conjugates every actual factorial R matrix by `D tensor D`. The Cartan factor, pivot, transfer weights and head projectors are kept; the diagonal factors commute with the latter three. Internal D factors telescope through an arbitrary word. Its cut matrix transforms as C_poly=D^(-1)C_bal D. The literal rank-one source transforms at the same time: psi_poly=D^(-1)psi_bal, phi_poly=phi_bal D. (21) All pointed pairings are therefore exactly unchanged. For every weighted knot word the cut matrix is diagonal by integer-weight conservation, so its actual normalized source is also its same normalized trace before and after (20). The weighted Green current identities are preserved coefficientwise. The genuine integral Hopf pivot K and the original auxiliary root-compatible pivot `K^(1-N)` must still be distinguished. Their exact closed-strand adapter is `K^(-N)`. It commutes with every displayed diagonal change of frame and remains an actual position-dependent insertion off the root: K^(-N)e_j=q^(-Nn)q^(2Nj)e_j. At q_N it becomes the retained scalar `(-1)^n`; along the moving-q path it cannot be replaced by that value. The external modified-dimension and framing factors likewise stay their original ones. The basis identity does not equate two generic quantum invariants whose pivots or external source factors were chosen differently. Equation (20) does not license replacing (21) by an unrelated vacuum or discarding the size of D in asymptotics. Likewise the symmetric q-falling adapter and its source must be retained. Their quantum-factorial norms can carry exponential size. The individual uniform generator bounds (6) and (15) prove neither a uniform full-word star expansion nor the selected geometric period. They give the exact source frames and global classical moment maps to which such a theorem would have to apply. ## 7. Exact audit and endpoint checks [audit_integral_color_coherent_symbols.py](../experiments/audit_integral_color_coherent_symbols.py) and its [results](../experiments/integral_color_coherent_symbols_results.json) verify all finite symbols, removed endpoint values, Casimir normalization, and both diagonal frame adapters at levels 2 through 6 over the rational function field in q. They also check the two principal augmented flags and ordinary/symmetric shear identities. A separate 70-digit grid check uses N=8,16,32,64,128, includes lambda=0,1, both exact T endpoints, nearby T=10^(-8), and the color-scale endpoint positions T=1/N,1-1/N. It agrees with the proved uniform rate. These numerical checks audit conventions and cancellation; the uniform whole-sphere assertion is the argument (7)--(8), not an extrapolation from that grid.

title: The actual integral-color path has a global polynomial q-difference model
text: # The actual integral-color path has a global polynomial q-difference model Research proof, 27 October 2026. Along the simultaneous path q_lambda=exp(pi*i lambda/N), M=-q_lambda^N, the finite head is a genuine integral-color quotient for every parameter. Its standard q-polynomial operators patch on O(N-1), with removable q=1 values. There is also an explicit regular frame for the original balanced source and all its crossing matrices along the entire closed path. The source, cup, cap and pivot changes are recorded. The standard ordinary closure gives the existing reduced color C_N(q); the literal auxiliary pivot gives the earlier auxiliary word with its known off-root route adapter. They agree at both endpoints but are not silently identified in the interior. Use [the common-Verma quotient](common_verma_two_wall_source.md) and [the divided-color/pivot calculation](complete_color_divided_ward_and_fusion.md). The independent [ordinary-frame symbol audit](integral_color_coherent_symbols_and_uniform_poles.md) and [factorial-frame analysis](quantum_factorial_frames_and_cyclotomic_source.md) give complementary uniform symbol and frame estimates. ## 1. The simultaneous path stays on the genuine quotient wall Put n=N-1, Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), and q_lambda=exp(pi*i lambda/N), M_lambda=-q_lambda^N, 0<=lambda<=1. Then w=M Q^(-N)-M^(-1)=0, delta=1-Q^N=1-exp(2pi*i lambda). (1.1) The tail of the genuine balanced infinite module is invariant on this wall. Its finite head is therefore a quotient for the whole path. The truncated Hopf defect -delta*w*E_(n,n) vanishes identically; there is no generic-M finite Hopf premise. The endpoints are (q,M)=(1,-1) and (q_N,1). Both also have delta=0. The two wall parameters have not been identified: this path lies in w=0 and meets the root wall at its endpoints. Its logarithmic derivative is the integral-color direction dLog M=N dLog q, not the fixed-meridian q-normal derivative. ## 2. The integral color and the two polynomial frames In the ordinary F-shift basis v_j, 0<=j<=n, the genuine color is K v_j=q^(n-2j)v_j, F v_j=v_(j+1), E v_j=[j]_q[N-j]_q v_(j-1), (2.1) with both boundary arrows zero and [r]_q=(q^r-q^(-r))/rho. Its matrices are Laurent regular at q=1 with [r]_1=r. The user's ordinary-falling polynomial basis is e_j=v_j/(n)_j, (n)_j=n!/(n-j)!. It gives exactly F e_j=(n-j)e_(j+1), E e_j=[j]_q[N-j]_q/(N-j)e_(j-1). (2.2) On the polynomial space H_N=H^0(P1,O(n)), e_j=x^j, this is F=x(n-J), E=x^(-1)[J]_q[N-J]_q/(N-J), K=q^(n-2J), J=x partial_x. (2.3) The inverse N-J is legitimate on this space: its eigenvalues are 1,...,N. Equivalently it is the finite polynomial operation integral_0^1 t^(N-1)f(x/t)dt. Thus (2.3) is an exact operator on H_N, including q=1. It is not claimed to be a scalar first-order q-difference expression on unrestricted functions. For a simpler q-difference realization, use symmetric q-falling factorials [n]_q^(fall,j)=product_(r=0)^(j-1)[n-r]_q, f_j=v_j/[n]_q^(fall,j). Then E f_j=[j]_q f_(j-1), F f_j=[n-j]_q f_(j+1). (2.4) With the marked shift T_q f(x)=f(qx), these have the exact forms E_q=(T_q-T_(q^-1))/(rho x), F_q=x(q^n T_(q^-1)-q^(-n)T_q)/rho, K_q=q^n T_(q^-2). (2.5) The apparent x pole cancels on polynomials; the highest coefficient of F_q is zero, so all three preserve degree <=n. Their q=1 values are partial_x, x(n-J), I, respectively. Along the entire path, for 1<=r<N, [r]_(q_lambda)=sin(pi lambda r/N)/sin(pi lambda/N)>0, with value r at lambda=0. None of the q-falling frame factors vanishes or has a pole. The ordinary-falling frame differs by e_j=R_j f_j, R_j=[n]_q^(fall,j)/(n)_j. (2.6) These are units on the fixed-N path. This is not a uniform-in-N norm assertion; the factorial-frame note records its possible exponential conditioning. ## 3. The q-difference operators patch globally on O(n) The south section of a north polynomial is (J_n f)(y)=y^n f(1/y). Direct substitution into (2.5) gives J_n E_q J_n^(-1)= y(q^n T_(q^-1)-q^(-n)T_q)/rho, J_n F_q J_n^(-1)=(T_q-T_(q^-1))/(rho y), J_n K_q J_n^(-1)=q^(-n)T_(q^2). (3.1) Thus E and F interchange and K inverts, in the same line-bundle transition that defines O(n). The q=1 limits give its usual global sl2 vector-field action. This is an exact globally patched q-difference realization, not a substitution into a local symbol. The frame R in (2.6) also patches by J_n R J_n^(-1); it need not have a scalar first-order difference expression. For q!=1 on the given path, spectral interpolation in T_q expresses it and its inverse as finite q-difference matrices. Coefficients of that interpolation can have removable q=1 singularities even though the operators themselves are regular. The reciprocal polynomial chart J_n is not automatically the previously fixed balanced physical Weyl/source matrix. Transporting a specified such matrix C into the h frame below gives D^(-1)CD, with all its original phases and source factors. The chart identities (3.1) do not authorize replacing that transported matrix by J_n. ## 4. A regular frame keeps the actual balanced pointing Let w_j be the original balanced common-Verma basis. Its exact relation to (2.1) is v_j=(Q;Q)_j w_j, (Q;Q)_j=product_(r=1)^j(1-Q^r). (4.1) For example along M=-q^N the balanced Ecal arrow is -q^(-j)rho[N-j]_q, and multiplication by 1-Q^j=-q^j rho[j]_q proves (2.1), with E=Ecal/rho^2. The factors in (4.1) have zeros at q=1. Treating (4.1) as an invertible integral frame there would lose source information. The correct regular balanced-to-polynomial frame is instead h_j=D_j w_j, D_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j+1)/2)/{n choose j}_q =(Q;Q)_j/[rho^j [n]_q^(fall,j)], (4.2) where the binomial is the symmetric q-binomial. Its ratio is D_j/D_(j-1)=-q^j [j]_q/[N-j]_q. Here D changes basis vectors, so its inverse conjugates old coordinate matrices. The coordinate gauge in the [independent source-detour audit](integral_color_source_detour_audit.md) is exactly D^(-1), expressed using the ordinary Q-binomial. All factors in (4.2) are nonzero analytic functions on the closed path. Their endpoint values are D_j(0)=(-1)^j/binom(n,j), D_j(1)=(-1)^j q_N^(j(j+1)/2). (4.3) For the second equation use [N-r]_(q_N)=[r]_(q_N), so {N-1 choose j}_(q_N)=1. In particular the root frame is a unitary diagonal phase in the original Euclidean basis. In this regular frame the actual Gauss matrices are precisely Ecal= rho E_q, F= rho F_q, K=K_q. (4.4) Both first operators are regular and vanish at q=1. The original ordinary Uq generators are E=rho^(-1)E_q,F=rho F_q on this frame; their individual lattice need not be regular at q=1. The ordinary integral Uq lattice of (2.4) is regular there. These two lattice statements must remain distinct. Their braiding matrices agree nonetheless for q!=1: the common Hopf rescaling of E and F cancels in every E^k tensor F^k term of the actual universal finite-color crossing, and K and the Cartan weights stay unchanged. Equivalently, the change from f_j to h_j divides by rho^j on every leg, which commutes with each crossing by exact total-index conservation. The finite crossing and its inverse therefore extend regularly to the usual flip at q=1 in this model. No divergent ordinary generator is inserted into a limit without this cancellation. ### 4.1 Source, dual source, cup and cap The prescribed balanced cut has psi_j=1 and phi_j=1/N. In the regular frame (4.2) it is exactly psi_h,j=D_j^(-1), phi_h,j=D_j/N, Gamma_h,ij=D_j/(N D_i), phi_h psi_h=1. (4.5) These are regular at both endpoints. They are not silently replaced by a constant vector and average covector. Their norms need not be bounded uniformly in N; already D_j(0) contains ordinary binomial factors. The dual basis is transformed inversely. Consequently the exact cup sum_j w_j tensor w_j^* equals sum_j h_j tensor h_j^*. For either diagonal pivot g, the right cap has entries ev_g(h_j tensor h_k^*)=delta_(jk) g_j, so the basis change preserves the cup/cap pair without a missing determinant or endpoint multiplier. All source and co-source normal derivatives follow by differentiating (4.2)--(4.5). For an actual one-cut closed braid array, total integer index conservation makes its remaining cut matrix diagonal, even before using a Hopf or Schur argument. Therefore its exact scalar cut is phi_h C psi_h=(1/N)Tr C. (4.6) This is why the same actual scalar is represented by the fixed compact coherent trace period in the h frame. Equality (4.6) does not identify all offdiagonal source operators or erase their derivatives before the closed network has been formed. ## 5. The ordinary and literal auxiliary closures stay distinguished The genuine ordinary pivotal closure uses K. With its original ordinary zero-framing twist and finite-color normalization, (2.5) gives exactly the existing reduced color C_N(q). For generic q the one-cut ordinary operator is scalar by actual Hopf naturality and irreducibility; the resulting Laurent period extends to the whole path, including both endpoints. Its values are C_N(1)=1, C_N(q_N)=Kashaev_N. (5.1) The root auxiliary construction uses K^(1-N). Away from q_N it differs from the ordinary cap by the diagonal K^(-N), with entry q^[-Nn+2Nj]. Its associated twist also differs. The exact zero-framed b-strand route adapter is the previously proved factor q^[Nn(ell-b+1)+2N sum_(closed legs)j_a], (5.2) where ell is writhe. It equals one at both q=1 and q=q_N because ell=b-1 modulo two for a knot. Its interior values and derivatives are generally state-dependent and are retained. Thus (4.2) is a genuine unit frame for the same balanced auxiliary pointing along the path. Identifying its literal-pivot scalar with C_N(q) in the interior requires (5.2), not a basis argument. For either specified closure, the new model preserves the entire word and original scalar. Neither the full root modified-dimension line nor an ordinary quantum dimension is declared an off-root extension of the other by this construction. ## 6. Exact finite coherent symbols and uniform endpoint behavior Use the fixed compact coherent kernel of dimension N, variables v,z, and T=vz/(1+vz). Put B_+=1+(q-1)T, B_-=1+(q^(-1)-1)T. Binomial summation of the actual matrices (4.4) gives exactly sigma_(Ecal)=[B_+^n-B_-^n]/v, sigma_F=v[q^n B_-^n-q^(-n)B_+^n], sigma_K=q^n[1+(q^(-2)-1)T]^n. (6.1) The first numerator vanishes at T=0 and the bracket in the second vanishes at T=1. Thus these are smooth entire-sphere symbols in the actual coherent charts, including both poles. For s=2pi*i lambda, q=exp(s/(2N)), their limits are e_s=2sinh(sT/2)/v, f_s=2v sinh(s(1-T)/2), k_s=exp[s(1/2-T)]. (6.2) Convergence is O(1/N) in every fixed smooth derivative norm on the real sphere, uniformly for lambda in [0,1]. To prove it, expand n Log[1+(exp(epsilon*s/(2N))-1)T], epsilon=+1 or -1. Its difference from epsilon*sT/2 and every fixed derivative is O(1/N), uniformly on the compact (lambda,T) rectangle. The endpoint zero factors may be divided using the exact integral identities g(T)/T=integral_0^1 g'(uT)du and g(T)/(1-T)=-integral_0^1 g'(1-u(1-T))du. These remove the apparent v or south-chart pole with the same derivative bound. The kernel charts then give the stated whole- sphere estimate. No such estimate is asserted for an arbitrary growing full braid matrix. These principal functions satisfy identically e_s f_s+k_s+k_s^(-1)=2cosh(s/2). (6.3) They describe the same meridian conjugacy class as the simultaneous path. At lambda=0 their multiplicative Gauss matrix is I. Its first lambda derivative retains the nonzero ordinary sl2 moment map; no dimension-N integral representation has disappeared. At lambda=1 the trace is -2, with the marked central sign of the original complete source. The plus eigenflag has the particularly simple exact principal form h_+(v,T)=exp[s(1-T)/2]v. (6.4) It is a clock-preserving canonical shear. For imaginary s and the real compact sphere its multiplier has modulus one, so the shear sends the very same sphere to itself. The root factorial-frame note records its quadratic generator, the inverse eigenflag and the two negative inverse-flag bubbles. This smoother plus flag does not permit replacing the actual inverse-flag source or its endpoint current by a different marking. The uniform estimates above concern the generator symbols only. The actual selected period has the exact nearby-root ladder C_N(q_(N+k))=C_k(q_(N+k)); in particular it equals one at lambda=N/(N+1). The independent source-detour audit proves its dense ordinary-color bounds and the resulting necessary endpoint nonuniformity. Those statements coexist with the fixed-N analytic source and uniform generator limits; no uniform full-word saddle amplitude is being inferred. ## 7. Exact gain and remaining scope The actual integral-color family now has a whole fixed-space q-difference realization with explicit global clutch. The balanced pointing, cup and both cap choices can be transported through a unit frame on the closed simultaneous path. The only singular factorial change is displayed in (4.1), and its regular network cancellation is proved rather than assumed. The scalar compact trace remains the actual one for every specified closure. This does not remove the off-root pivot adapter, compare the full root-normal source with a fixed-meridian q-jet, or bound the unknown full-word norm in (6.1). Nor does it construct a global geometric A-branch through the whole path or identify its selected regulator phase. It supplies an actual globally patched family on which those further comparisons can be posed with all source factors visible. The [exact audit](../experiments/audit_integral_color_global_q_difference_source.py) checks the bases, matrices, global patch, true source/cup, actual crossing cancellation, both walls, and endpoint symbols. The [independent proof audit](integral_color_source_detour_audit.md) also verifies the integral quotient, source frames, pivotal distinction and exact resonance sampling constraints.

title: The integral-color path: actual sources, pivots and dense resonances
text: # The integral-color path: actual sources, pivots and dense resonances Independent proof audit, 27 October 2026. The path \(q_\lambda=e^{\pi i\lambda/N}\), \(M=-q_\lambda^N\) does give an honest \(N\)-dimensional integral-color quotient and its actual crossings. It is not automatically the same off-root source as the auxiliary finite ADO lift with its root pivot frozen. This distinction is explicit below. The ordinary-color bounds impose a second exact constraint: the actual color path has polynomial values on a sampling grid of spacing \(O(1/N)\), and its nearest higher-root value is literally one. A uniform positive dominant WKB solution on the real interval cannot describe this selected function. ## 1. Exact quotient and basis comparisons On the common balanced Verma module, \[ \delta=1-Q^N,\qquad w=M Q^{-N}-M^{-1},\qquad Q=q^2. \] The choice \(M=-q^N\) has \(w=0\). The tail is invariant and the finite head is the genuine integral quotient, with \[ K e_j=q^{N-1-2j}e_j,\quad \mathcal E e_j=q^{-N}(1-Q^{N-j})e_{j-1},\quad F e_j=(1-Q^{j+1})e_{j+1}. \tag{1} \] The original finite crossing is its literal quotient crossing. The word excursion adapter is proportional to \(\delta w\), so it vanishes on this whole path, not merely at its root endpoint. Let \(u_j\) be the ordinary highest-weight basis with \(Fu_j=u_{j+1}\), \(Eu_j=[j]_q[N-j]_q u_{j-1}\), and \(\mathcal E=\rho^2E\). Then \[ e_j=u_j/(Q;Q)_j \tag{2} \] gives exactly (1). For every fixed \(N\), this gauge is invertible on \(0<\lambda\le1\), including at \(q_N\); all factors have index \(j<N\). It is singular at \(q=1\). The balanced coupon \(e_{ij}=1/N\) becomes \[ e^{\rm ordinary}_{ij} =\frac{(Q;Q)_j}{N(Q;Q)_i}. \tag{3} \] Its normalization remains one, but its separate source and co-source flags need not have a regular \(q=1\) limit. There is a second useful exact gauge, regular also at \(q=1\). In the polynomial basis it gives \[ \mathcal E_{\rm sym}=v^{-1}(T_q-T_q^{-1}),\qquad F_{\rm sym}=v(q^nT_q^{-1}-q^{-n}T_q),\quad n=N-1. \] The diagonal conjugation from (1) is \[ D_j=(-1)^j q^{j(j+1)/2-Nj}{N-1\brack j}_{Q}. \tag{4} \] Its adjacent ratio is the old \(\mathcal E\) coefficient divided by \(q^j-q^{-j}\), which proves both generator comparisons. At \(q=1\), \(D_j=(-1)^j\binom nj\); at the actual root, \[ D_j=q_N^{-Nj-j(j+1)/2}, \] of modulus one. Thus (4) is invertible along the closed path for fixed \(N\), but its condition number can be exponential in \(N\) in the interior or at the classical endpoint. Exact finite equivalence does not imply equality of naive principal symbols in these different frames. The normalized trace is basis invariant. On every one-cut diagonal array, including the scalar index-weighted arrays, the original balanced coupon equals this trace. This avoids the coordinate singularity of (3) for those evaluations. For off-diagonal Ward insertions the coupon must still be transported; normalized trace is not a replacement on all matrices. ## 2. The pivotal adapter is essential off the root The generic integral-color quantum invariant uses the ordinary pivot \(g_{\rm int}=K\). The root ADO pivot is \(g_{\rm root}=K^{1-N}\). Away from \(Q^N=1\), \[ S^2=\operatorname{Ad}K\ne\operatorname{Ad}K^{1-N}. \] For example their conjugations of \(\mathcal E\) differ by \(Q^{-N}\). Hence a frozen ADO right cap is not a generic Hopf pivotal cap, even though the quotient module and its crossings are genuine. For a \(b\)-strand knot braid of writhe \(\mathfrak w\), the ordinary integral twist and frozen ADO twist at \(\alpha=n\) are \[ \theta_{\rm int}=q^{n(n+2)/2},\qquad \theta_{\rm root}=q^{-n^2/2}. \] Their ratio is \(q^{-Nn}\). The exact difference of the two zero-framed state arrays is therefore the weight \[ q^{Nn(\mathfrak w-b+1)} (Q^N)^{\sum_{\text{closed strands}}j_a}. \tag{5} \] It retains an actual number-operator clock, not just a scalar. At \(q_N\) its clock is one and its scalar is \((-1)^{n(\mathfrak w-b+1)}=1\) by knot parity. Thus the ordinary reduced endpoint is the original \(K_N\). At \(q=1\), the ordinary reduced period is also one. Neither endpoint equality removes the nonconstant adapter in between or its quantum-normal derivatives. There is an explicit small example. For \(N=2\), use the stabilized unknot, the two-strand braid \(\sigma_1\). Its ordinary reduced value is one. With the frozen pivot \(K^{-1}\) and frozen twist \(q^{-1/2}\), its normalized one-cut value instead is \[ 1+\frac{q^2-q^{-2}}2 =1+i\sin(\pi\lambda). \tag{6} \] To check this, use the actual fundamental checked crossing \(q^{1/2}I-q^{-1/2}U\), with \(U|_{01,10}=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}q&-1\\-1&q^{-1}\end{smallmatrix}\right]\). Closing the second leg with \(K^{-1}\), then applying the frozen twist correction, gives diagonal entries \(1\) and \(1-q^{-2}+q^2\); their average is (6). It agrees at both endpoints but is not the integral-color invariant inside the interval. This is a comparison of two explicit interpolations, not a claim that a generic ADO invariant was defined incorrectly. The valid actual interpolation is \(C_N(q)\) with its ordinary caps and twist. At the root its reduced one-cut evaluation is regular even though its ordinary quantum dimension \([N]_{q_N}\) vanishes. One must not evaluate an unreduced closure divided by \([N]\) as two separately vanishing quantities. ## 3. Exact sampling and the necessary nonuniformity Set \[ A_N(\lambda)=C_N(e^{\pi i\lambda/N}). \] For every integer \(r>N\), the value at \(\lambda=N/r\) is an ordinary color at the principal root \(q_r\). The actual unitary trace bound gives \[ |A_N(N/r)|\le [N]_{q_r}^{b-1}\le (r/2)^{b-1}. \tag{7} \] On any fixed closed interval \(J\subset(0,1)\), these sampling points have mesh \(O_J(1/N)\) and their bound is \(O_J(N^{b-1})\). Consequently a positive dominant WKB expansion with a uniformly nonvanishing subexponential amplitude cannot hold on any open real interval below one. Choose a point of positive continuous rate and a small compact interval on which it stays positive. A sampling point in that interval contradicts (7). More generally, if \[ u_N(\lambda)=N^{-1}\log^+|A_N(\lambda)| \] are equicontinuous on such a compact interval, then \(\sup_Ju_N\to0\): compare every point with its neighboring sampling point. Thus a positive exponential spike requires loss of that equicontinuity. There is an exact stronger endpoint ladder. At level \(r=N+k\), ordinary-color Weyl symmetry gives \[ C_N(q_{N+k})=C_k(q_{N+k}),\qquad 1\le k<N. \tag{8} \] For each fixed \(k\), the right side tends to one and is bounded. In particular \[ A_N\!\left(\frac{N}{N+1}\right)=1 \tag{9} \] for every knot. Its distance from the target is \(1/(N+1)\). If \(|K_N|\) has positive exponential rate, a nonzero smooth dominant WKB amplitude cannot remain uniform even across this endpoint window. An unconditional quantitative form is \[ \sup_{\lambda\in[N/(N+1),1]}|A_N'(\lambda)| \ge (N+1)(|K_N|-1), \] and hence \[ \sup_{\lambda\in[N/(N+1),1]} |q\partial_q C_N(q)| \ge \frac{N(N+1)}\pi(|K_N|-1). \tag{10} \] This follows by integrating the derivative along the interval, so it does not assume a real-valued period or a mean-value point for a complex function. The already proved figure-eight asymptotic makes (9)--(10) an actual exponential endpoint example. Ordinary-color unitarity controls values, not the normal derivatives needed here. Pointwise asymptotics at an individual nonsampled irrational parameter are not excluded. Nor do these bounds exclude a geometric branch with a resonance-dependent source coefficient. They do exclude treating that coefficient as uniformly nonzero and smooth merely because the classical optimizer is. ### A whole scaled boundary profile cannot be algebraic The same exact ladder constrains the functions-before-jets program. Use \(c=2\pi i\), \(H=\log Q\), and the scaled normal \[ z=N^2(H-c/N),\qquad \mathfrak f_N(z)= C_N\!\left(\exp\!\left[\frac{c}{2N} +\frac{z}{2N^2}\right]\right). \] The nearby principal level \(N+k\) is exactly \[ z_{N,k}=-\frac{ckN}{N+k}\longrightarrow-ck,\qquad \mathfrak f_N(z_{N,k})=C_k(q_{N+k})\longrightarrow1. \tag{11} \] Also \(\mathfrak f_N(0)=K_N\). Here is the precise conditional conclusion. Choose a subsequence with \(|K_N|\to\infty\), for example one having a positive exponential rate, and suppose \(\mathfrak f_N/K_N\) converges locally uniformly to a holomorphic function \(g\) on a connected domain containing zero and every point \(-ck\), \(k\ge1\). Then \[ g(0)=1,\qquad g(-ck)=0\quad(k\ge1). \tag{12} \] Local uniform convergence permits the moving evaluations (11), so this needs no unproved interchange of pointwise limits. Such a nonzero whole profile is not algebraic over \(\mathbb C(z)\). Indeed, for an irreducible polynomial relation \(P(z,g)=0\), the infinitely many zeros in (12) force \(P(z,0)\) to vanish identically. Thus \(w\) divides \(P(z,w)\), forcing \(g=0\), contrary to \(g(0)=1\). Neither the required growth nor this normal-family convergence is asserted for a general knot. A germ on a small neighborhood of zero alone is not excluded, and the conclusion does not prohibit algebraic coefficients for an individual local geometric WKB branch. It says that, if a normalized whole selected boundary profile exists through all nearby resonances, an algebraic critical coefficient cannot be that entire profile. A genuinely nonalgebraic period function is required; its resonance zeros and one normalization do not determine it uniquely. ## 4. Principal flags depend on the valid source frame The symmetric frame in (4) has principal functions \[ e=\frac{2\sinh(sT/2)}v,\quad f=2v\sinh(s(1-T)/2),\quad k=e^{s/2-sT},\qquad s=2\pi i\lambda. \] Its two eigenflags are \[ v_+=e^{s(1-T)/2}v,\qquad v_-=-e^{-sT/2} \frac{\sinh(s(1-T)/2)}{\sinh(sT/2)}v. \] The plus flag has degree \(+1\) and exactly the original Fubini--Study current on the real sphere at every level parameter. For \(0<\lambda<1\), the inverse flag has degree \(-1\), whereas at \(\lambda=1\) its interior limit equals the plus flag and has degree \(+1\). Writing \(\varepsilon=1-\lambda\), the two inverse-flag bubbles are \[ v=\varepsilon y:\quad v_-\to-1/\bar y,\qquad V=1/v=\varepsilon y:\quad v_-\to\bar y . \] Each has degree \(-1\).
