(1.2) For example (1.2) on u^r/r! has the required coefficient 1-Z^(r+1) into the next block. The apparent inverse L+1 is just division by the nonzero integer r+1 on that basis. ## 2. The exact irregular transformation and head gauge Put epsilon=Z-1, d=N epsilon, and choose the marked local ramification eta^N=d. Define G=exp(u/d), D_head h_j=eta^j h_j, C=D_head G^(-1). The exponential belongs to the u-adic completion with Laurent eta coefficients. Each u coefficient has a finite pole; there is no claim of a single uniform pole bound for the whole function. Conjugate first by G^(-1)(-)G, then by D_head(-)D_head^(-1), and apply the genuine Hopf scaling Ecal->eta Ecal,F->eta^(-1)F: Ehat=eta C Ecal C^(-1), Fhat=eta^(-1) C F C^(-1), Khat=C K C^(-1). (2.1) The direction of the head conjugation is essential. It cancels eta on every nonwrap E entry and contributes d on its wrap; it cancels eta^(-1) on every nonwrap F entry and contributes d^(-1) on its wrap. There is no unresolved irregular expansion in the transformed operators. Since G^(-1)D_ZG=exp(u/N)D_Z, G^(-1)D_(Z^-1)G=exp(-u/(NZ))D_(Z^-1), G^(-1)B G=B+1/d, the exact entries become Ehat_j=M Q^(-j)exp(-u/(NZ))D_(Z^-1)-M^(-1), j>0, Ehat_0=(1+d partial_u) [M exp(-u/(NZ))D_(Z^-1)-M^(-1)], Fhat_j=1-Q^(j+1)exp(u/N)D_Z, j<N-1, Fhat_(N-1) f =-(u/N) integral_0^1 exp(tu/N)f((1+epsilon t)u)dt, Khat_j=-(M/q)Q^(-j)exp(-u/(NZ))D_(Z^-1). (2.2) The F wrap formula follows by x=1+epsilon t in (1.2), retaining the reversed integration endpoints. Each coefficient of (2.2) is a regular formal series in epsilon,u. Integration is polynomial antiderivation coefficientwise, not a convergence assumption. The generic quantum-group relations hold because (2.1) is conjugation and Hopf scaling of a genuine module. Their regular specializations are therefore exact root identities. ## 3. The full cyclic root module and its central chart Fix q=q_N, Q=Q_N and put y=exp(u/N), U=y^N=exp(u), gamma=(-1)^(N+1). Taking the regular value of (2.2) gives K_j=-(M/q_N)y^(-1)Q_N^(-j), Ecal_j=M y^(-1)Q_N^(-j)-M^(-1), F_j=1-y Q_N^(j+1), (3.1) with j read modulo N, including both wraps. All entries act by multiplication. For F the wrap limit is -(u/N)integral_0^1 exp(tu/N)dt=1-y, including its regular u=0 value. The resulting entries are Laurent algebraic functions of M,y. Thus the module formulas extend from the marked formal y=1 neighborhood to y in G_m. This extends the module chart, not a selected irregular source or its global continuation data. Direct multiplication, or specialization of the regular relations, gives [Ecal,F]=rho_N(K-K^(-1)), F Ecal+q_N K+q_N^(-1)K^(-1)=-M-M^(-1). The exact central powers are k=K^N=gamma M^N/U, e=Ecal^N=gamma(M^N/U-M^(-N)), f=F^N=1-U. (3.2) Consequently e f=k+k^(-1)-gamma(M^N+M^(-N)). (3.3) For U!=1 the F arrows are all units. Clock projectors followed by their cyclic F arrows give every matrix unit, so this is a genuine split regular root color, rather than a Borel-only model. Apply the additional genuine root Hopf scaling Ecal->lambda Ecal,F->lambda^(-1)F. Given an admissible central triple (k_t,e_t,f_t) satisfying (3.3), with all entries nonzero, choose U=gamma M^N/k_t, lambda^N=e_t/[gamma(M^N/U-M^(-N))]. (3.4) The denominator is nonzero because its product with 1-U is e_t f_t. On the indicated N-th-root cover, (3.4) realizes e_t, and (3.3) forces the realized f to be f_t. Thus the family covers a dense full fixed-Casimir central chart. It is not restricted to the triangular source locus F^N=0. It does not itself prove that an actual knot's selected source reaches a chosen point of that chart. ## 4. The selected source is irregular and its lattice flags remain Let the original finite head source be i psi, with psi_j=1, and its co-source phi pi_0, phi_j=1/N. Its finite-rank coupon is Gamma=i e pi_0. Under the actual transformation C the exact source and co-source are psi_new=D_head exp(-u/d)psi, phi_new=phi D_head^(-1)pi_0, phi_new psi_new=1. (4.1) Here pi_0G=pi_0, but G does not preserve the source vacuum. In particular G^(-1)Gamma G=exp(-u/d)Gamma, not Gamma. The full transformed coupon has entry (Gamma_new)_(i,j) =eta^(i-j)exp(-u/d)/N times evaluation at u=0. (4.2) It is exactly idempotent by (4.1). On u jets of order at most h, its eta pole order is bounded by Nh+N-1, equivalently its d pole order by h+(N-1)/N. The head lattice has the explicit flags eta^j h_j, with the opposite dual flags eta^(-j)h_j^*. The normalized pairing does not make those flags or the essential source exp(-u/d) disappear. The coefficientwise head projector e tensor I is different: G commutes with it and only the ramified D_head changes it. It cannot be substituted for the original finite Gamma. The same issue occurs at every internal finite-head compression, not just at the final cut. For the whole-head projector P=i pi_0 (identity on H), one has exactly C P C^(-1)=exp(-u/d)P. (4.3) On b legs the scalar is exp(-(u_1+...+u_b)/d). The actual off-root finite word is the product with its intermediate head projectors retained. Each becomes this irregular source under the transformation. In particular the pre-gauge two-wall word correction delta*w*H_beta from the common-Verma note cannot be discarded after taking module Rees symbols: those source poles and normal co-sources can compensate its vanishing factors. Thus the module has a regular full-cyclic limit while the source is an explicitly recorded irregular section. Equality of finite pairings before degeneration does not provide a regular limiting selected period or a Stokes coefficient. ## 5. The literal pivot lift is selected, with its U adapter Conjugation preserves the identity g=K^(1-N). Since Khat has a regular root value, its literal power has that same regular limit: g_lit=K_U^(1-N)=U g_red, g_red=x^(1-N)A^(-1), A=yQ_N^j, x=-M/q_N. Therefore this construction selects the literal whole-clock lift, not the reduced root representative. Their paired defects satisfy D_lit=U^(-1)D_red and both products give the same cut projector; their separate normal derivatives differ. The exact distinction is retained in [the Mellin comparison](fock_cyclic_normal_mellin_map.md), Section 2. The whole external modified-dimension line d_N(M), Cartan half-character, and zero-framing phases remain marked. ## 6. The actual cyclotomic-normal Poisson form There is a fixed-N normal Planck parameter already present in this construction: d=N(Q^N-1). The generic weight relations give [K^N,Ecal^N]=(Q^(N^2)-1)Ecal^N K^N, [K^N,F^N]=(Q^(-N^2)-1)F^N K^N. The two scalar ratios after division by d have root values +1 and -1. Thus the actual divided-commutator Poisson bracket on the root center satisfies {k,e}=ke, {k,f}=-kf. (6.1) It is independent of the choice of lifts: changing a lift by d times an operator adds a commutator with a central root element. The quantum Casimir is central before specialization. Its root Chebyshev relation (3.3), on a fixed-M leaf, consequently forces {e,f}=k^(-1)-k. (6.2) This follows first where e!=0 by bracketing (3.3) with e, then extends as the polynomial bracket identity. The Casimir relation is not being declared central merely because it vanishes in one representation; it is the specialization of the actual universal central Casimir. Vary the actual irregular phase to G_p=exp(pu/d), with p!=0. The Rees momentum is Pi=d partial_u, so [Pi,u]=d and G_p^(-1)Pi G_p=Pi+p. This fixes {p,u}=1. In (2.2) replace u/N in the exponent by pu/N and (1+d partial_u) on the E wrap by (p+d partial_u). The F wrap limit is (1-y)/p, y=exp(pu/N). Other entries remain the corresponding nonwrap entries. Hence its central functions are exactly U=exp(up), k=gamma M^N/U, e=p gamma(M^N/U-M^(-N)), f=(1-U)/p. (6.3) Direct differentiation with {p,u}=1 gives (6.1)--(6.2). The exact source symplectic form is Omega=du wedge dp=dlog U wedge dlog p =-dlog k wedge dlog e, (6.4) holding M fixed. The last equality follows from e=p(k-gamma M^(-N)). This is precisely the fixed-meridian Gauss leaf form used in the actual holonomy/moment-map proof, not just an unrelated symplectic parameterization. To match its usual balanced center coordinates set e_G=e/rho_N^N, f_G=-rho_N^N f. Then G=[k e_G;k f_G k^(-1)+e_G f_G] has trace gamma(M^N+M^(-N)); the physical gamma*G has trace M^N+M^(-N). Constant root scalings do not change (6.4). Varying M requires its peripheral boundary terms and is not part of this fixed-leaf identity. ## 7. A regular chart at the parabolic source boundary At M=1 set v=1/p and w=e/gamma. The same central chart is U=(1+wv)^(-1), k=gamma(1+wv), e=gamma w, f=w v^2/(1+wv), Omega=dw wedge dv/(1+wv). (7.1) These are algebraic identities. The form is regular and nonzero at v=0, including w=0. The locus w=0 maps to the identity central point; its v coordinate retains the exceptional direction. Thus (7.1) is a regular resolving chart at that collapsed point, not a claim of a complete global resolution without its other chart. The module entries also extend across v=0 on the marked y cover. Here y=(1+wv)^(-1/N), and its E wrap is [(1+wv)^(1/N)-1]/v -> w/N, while its F wrap is v[1-(1+wv)^(-1/N)] ->0. The nonwrap entries tend to the actual head values. Consequently the v=0 module is exactly the previously constructed E-semicyclic source with mu=w/N, and w=0 is the actual complete head. This is a concrete source boundary of the full conjugacy-class chart. It does not prove that the selected knot period reaches a chosen geometric point in that chart. ## 8. What has and has not been bridged The full cyclic module is obtained from the genuine actual Verma module by an explicit irregular Rees transformation. This supplies a module-level route from the original head lattice to dense root color charts with both central powers nonzero. Its construction does not assume that a generic typical finite head extends to a Lusztig module, nor identify the two regular wall normals. At U=1 its generic-M value is the E-semicyclic s=1 fiber, with wrap coefficient kappa=M-M^(-1), rather than the nilpotent s=0 head. They coincide at M=1. The previously proved whole E-semicyclic cut independence is relevant, but is a separate word/source comparison and is not a consequence of this module specialization. No regular limit of the transformed source has been asserted. The generator module limit alone also does not prove that a whole conjugated R network has a regular scalar limit with this selected source. The remaining tasks include its ramified flags, irregular source class, physical phase adapters, and actual geometric/cut comparison. No global regulator period or volume limit follows from the central-chart coverage alone. The parameter d is a local root normal for fixed N, not the physical large-N parameter H_N=2pi*i/N. If H=Log Q on the marked root sheet, then d=N^2(H-H_N)+higher order. The actual finite auxiliary state is regular at that fixed root. A nonzero polar geometric phase exp(S/d) is therefore not automatically its selected phase: polar pieces in a full source-preserving contraction must be accounted for or canceled. The root regular part can still have N-dependent growth. The exact module and Poisson maps above do not settle that separate norm problem. The uncompressed universal Verma braid has its own already proved root Alexander-normalized period in [the earlier Verma note](frobenius_verma_period.md). It is not identified with the compressed selected period by dropping the projectors (4.3); their full normal adapter remains necessary. [Exact module and source audit](../experiments/audit_irregular_rees_full_cyclic_module.py). [Results](../experiments/irregular_rees_full_cyclic_module_results.json).

title: A literature quantum A-family with the Kashaev evaluation fixed
text: # A literature quantum A-family with the Kashaev evaluation fixed Research note, 25 October 2026. The preceding [crossing calculation](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md) independently identifies the normalized enhanced Kashaev period with the reduced highest-weight quantum-group period. Here we give its meridian family, its exact normalization lattice, and its implications for the norm torsor. Definitions are the unrolled quantum-group R, pivotal and modified-dimension formulas in Brown--Dimofte--Garoufalidis--Geer, [2005.08176](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08176), Section 2. Their holonomicity and recursion-ideal comparison theorems are not assumed. The calculations below use the displayed definitions directly. ## 1. The zero-framed reduced family is rational in its color Fix r>=2, q=exp(pi*i/r), and x=q^alpha. On V_alpha use H v_j=(alpha-2j)v_j, K v_j=x q^(-2j)v_j, E v_j=[j]_q[alpha-j+1]_q v_(j-1), F v_j=v_(j+1), 0<=j<r. Use the finite universal R from the preceding note with k<r, pivotal matrix K^(1-r), and twist theta_alpha=q^((alpha^2+2(1-r)alpha)/2). Let F_r(alpha) be the reduced (1,1)-tangle scalar for a zero-framed knot, with unknot value one. It is the usual modified-trace ADO invariant divided by the modified dimension, not a new local weight. **Rationality lemma.** F_r(alpha) is a Laurent polynomial in x with complex coefficients at fixed q. Proof: remove the common factor q^(alpha^2/2) from each positive R and its inverse from each negative R. The remaining entries are Laurent polynomials in x, since q^((alpha-2c)(alpha-2d)/2) =q^(alpha^2/2) x^(-c-d) q^(2cd), [alpha-j+1]_q =(x q^(-j+1)-x^(-1)q^(j-1))/(q-q^(-1)). All denominators [k]_q!, k<r, are nonzero constants. For a braid word of writhe w, the total removed factor is q^(w alpha^2/2). It cancels with theta_alpha^(-w); the remainder is x^(-w(1-r)). The pivotal entries are also Laurent monomials in x. Finite products, sums and partial traces prove the assertion. Scalarity on generic typical colors and the resulting identity extend through the finite exceptional set. In particular F_r(alpha+2r)=F_r(alpha). This has a direct algebraic proof from the defining matrices; it is not a consequence imported from a holonomicity theorem. ## 2. Exact specialization to the original Kashaev period At alpha=r-1 the matrices are the r-dimensional highest-weight matrices of the crossing note. The two pivotal conventions differ by K^(1-r)=(-1)^(r-1) K. The corresponding twists differ by the same sign. For a b-strand braid closing to a knot, w has parity b-1. Hence the resulting factor (-1)^((r-1)(b-1-w)) is one. The dual convention in the crossing note is equivalent to the original highest-weight color: an explicit intertwiner with its dual is B v_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j-r)) v_(r-1-j). For example, with Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E and Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F, the antipodes are S(E)=-E K^(-1) and S(F)=-K F. Direct substitution verifies B on E,F,K. The same substitution in the finite R gives R^T=(B tensor B)R(B^(-1) tensor B^(-1)). Consequently the already specified enhanced period satisfies F_r(r-1)=<K>_r. (2.1) This is a uniform matrix and pairing comparison for knots, with the zero framing and unknot normalization fixed. The subsequent [root-orbit pointing proof](root_orbit_pointing.md) extends this calculation to every integer color 1<=j<=r: F_r(M=-q^j)=C_j(q), where C_j is the reduced j-dimensional period. Its proof uses the invariant quotient of the color and a filtered cut-trace argument for a one-component braid closure. In particular F_r(-q)=1 supplies a nonzero reference anchor on the same central fiber as M=1. For the full state this is a residue anchor, as the modified dimension has a pole at M=-q. The [all-level period theorem](all_level_a_period.md) now uses these identities and polynomial rigidity to recover the exact Kashaev value from any specified actual all-level annihilator and finitely many fixed small colors. Whole q-germs handle singular steps with a uniform jet bound. Root-level rank one is not required. ## 3. The generic peripheral factor is an actual cyclic lattice gauge Write N_r(alpha)=d_r(alpha)F_r(alpha) for the modified-trace ADO invariant. Its defining modified dimension is d_r(alpha)=-q^(r(1-r)/2) (q^(alpha+1)-q^(-alpha-1))/(q^(r alpha)-q^(-r alpha)). Introduce the marked meridian coordinate M=-q x, so that M=1 at alpha=r-1. Then, exactly, d_r(M)=eta_r (M-M^(-1))/(M^r-M^(-r)) =eta_r M^(r-1)/P_r(M^2), eta_r=(-1)^(r+1)q^(r(1-r)/2)=i^(r+3), P_r(t)=1+t+...+t^(r-1). (3.1) Thus the modified-dimension factor is the cyclic stable-lattice generator 1/P_r(t) from Section 3.1 of the intrinsic norm-torsor note, with t=M^2, together with its explicit monomial and phase. This is an instance in the literature state itself, not just a model. At M=1 the whole rational germ is regular and evaluates to d_r(1)=eta_r/r, <K>_r=r eta_r^(-1) N_r(r-1). (3.2) Setting numerator and denominator separately to zero would discard this value. The exact comparison keeps the peripheral polynomial P_r and its specialization P_r(1)=r. No topological or norm conclusion uses a bare numerical multiplier in its place. There is also a level-independent difference equation. Since the color shift sends M to q M and q^r=-1, d_r(qM)/d_r(M)=g(q,M), g(q,M)=-q^(-1)(q^2 M^2-1)/(M^2-1). (3.3) If f(M)=M-M^(-1), then g=-f(qM)/f(M). Thus this normalization line is a fixed rational gauge tensored with the sign character of the shift. Its root-level realization is the explicit peripheral divisor in (3.1). It is not a collection of arbitrary independent finite-level scalars. The subsequent [relative octahedral calculation](relative_octahedral_period.md) also derives 1/P_r(M^2) as the missing cyclic transition of the finite factorial actually appearing in these R entries. Its polynomial recurrence retains the source M^(2r)e_partial, and its cyclic system is nonsingular even on the completion's polar divisor. Thus this normalization has an explicit local relative origin as well as the meridian gauge calculation above. The global source/regulator comparison is not inferred from it. ## 4. The literature annihilator ideal and the pointed conjecture The all-level ADO annihilator ideal is defined in the literature by I_ADO={P(q,x,T): P(q_r,x,T)N_r(x)=0 for all but finitely many r}, T x=q x T, q_r=exp(pi*i/r). See equation (1.5) of the cited definition source. Under x=-q^(-1)M, the exact change from N_r to F_r induces the automorphism of the localized Ore algebra C(q,M)[T^(+/-1);sigma] M -> M, T -> g(q,M) T. (4.1) Indeed d_r^(-1) T d_r=g T. Therefore existence of a nonzero all-level annihilator is equivalent in the two normalizations, and their localized ideals correspond by (4.1). No unverified equality with the colored-Jones recursion ideal or AJ specialization is needed for this statement. The subsequent [finite cut-state proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md) now supplies a nonzero actual all-level meridian annihilator for every knot. The cited paper's holonomicity theorem remains outside the proof premises; the stronger multicomponent dimension statement is not needed for this conclusion. At M=1 the comparison uses the lattices and regular whole period germs in (3.1)--(3.2), since the localized coefficient g is meromorphic there. Localization alone does not specify this specialization. The subsequent [actual peripheral-fusion proof](actual_peripheral_fusion.md) derives this gauge from the pivotal partial traces of the two adjacent-color projectors, without a modified-trace comparison theorem. The full state has elementary boundary actions M+M^(-1) and T+T^(-1). The fusion wall at M=1 has a nonzero square-zero Casimir residue with exactly normalized partial trace; its actual knot coefficient and the normal Kashaev functional are retained as distinct meridian derivatives. Peripheral skein relations thus yield actual annihilators, without identifying the entire ideals or their geometric components. For this literature family with its prescribed pointing, the desired quantum-A volume statement is lim_(r->infinity) (2*pi/r) log|F_r(M=1)|=Vol(S^3 minus K). (4.2) Equations (2.1) and (3.2) identify (4.2) with Kashaev's original conjecture. The same rate for N_r at the regular germ M=1 is equivalent, since log r/r tends to zero and |eta_r|=1. This is a precise formulation with a fixed literature state, not an arbitrary solution of an operator. Equation (4.2) is not proved here. ## 5. What a root-of-unity central torsor does and does not select There is a useful general constraint. Let a nonzero rational function h(x) solve a specialized finite-order q-difference equation with q a primitive n-th root. Let H=T^n be its companion monodromy as in the intrinsic norm-torsor note. Then det(I-H)=0. (5.1) Proof: evaluation at h is a nonzero module map from the cyclic operator module to (C(x),sigma). On the target sigma^n=1. Hence the map kills H-I, so H-I cannot be invertible. This proof uses the solution pairing, not an identification of column vectors with solutions. Both F_r and N_r are rational in x at zero framing. Thus any specified all-level operator annihilating them has a central v=1 sector at its regular root levels n=2r. This finite-level sector must not be identified automatically with the geometric component of the classical q->1 A-curve. The quantum family and its distinguished pointing remain essential. No assertion is made that the literal classical A-curve is the central spectral curve of each root-level state. The required torsor comparison is therefore a comparison of the all-level pointed period with the marked geometric regulator, retaining the normalization lattice. The cyclic norm torsor alone does not select the volume-dominant geometric sector.

title: The specified Kashaev crossing and its period pairing
text: # The specified Kashaev crossing and its period pairing Research note, 25 October 2026. This uses Kashaev's crossing weights, [q-alg/9504020](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9504020), equations (2.7)--(2.12), and the enhanced braid definition recorded in Murakami--Murakami, [math/9905075](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9905075), Sections 1 and 4. Their comparison proofs are not premises. We derive the Fourier identity and normalization comparison below directly from finite products. This is an independent verification of a known comparison, not a new volume theorem. It fixes the literature state to which a quantum A-module argument must apply. All integers N>=2, including even and composite levels, are allowed. The subsequent [Casimir/lattice comparison](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md) expresses this same crossing and its inverse by confluent Casimir polynomials, retaining the double-point derivatives and exact writhe phase. It also derives the actual pivotal closing trace on that spectral algebra and identifies the operators through the singular cyclic recoupling lattice. ## 1. The Fourier transform is triangular Put omega=exp(2*pi*i/N), p_j=product_(h=1)^j(1-omega^h), p_0=1, and bar_p_j=product_(h=1)^j(1-omega^(-h)). Let R^o be exactly the unbraided matrix in Kashaev's equation (2.12). Use F_ij=omega^(ij)/sqrt(N), A=(F^(-1) tensor F^(-1)) R^o(F tensor F). **Fourier identity.** With indices in {0,...,N-1}, the only nonzero entries are A_(a-k,b+k ; a,b) =omega^(1+(a-k)(b+1)) p_a p_(b+k)/(p_(a-k) p_b p_k), 0<=k<=min(a,N-1-b). (1.1) In particular, conservation here is equality of ordinary integer sums, not just equality modulo N. ### Direct proof For a nonzero original entry introduce residues u=[j-i-1], v=[i-l], t=[l-k], h=[k-j]. The two theta factors say u+t<N and v+h<N. Their total is congruent to -1 modulo N, so u+v+t+h=N-1. Conversely every such composition and one free j specify exactly one original entry. In these coordinates, i=j-1-u, k=j+h, l=j+h+t (mod N), R^o_(i,j ; k,l)=N omega^(1-(t+h)(u+h)) /(p_u bar_p_v p_t bar_p_h). (1.2) The free j-sum in the Fourier transform gives the conservation delta. Put z=t+h. The remaining sum factors into A_(c,d ; a,b)=delta_(a+b=c+d mod N) sum_(z=0)^(N-1) omega^(1+c-z^2+z(a+b)) S_(N-1-z)(omega^(c-z)) S_z(omega^(z-a)), (1.3) where the elementary finite binomial identity is S_m(X)=sum_(j=0)^m X^j/(p_j bar_p_(m-j)) =product_(j=1)^m(X-omega^j)/p_m. (1.4) For a direct induction, use bar_p_m=(-1)^m omega^(-m(m+1)/2)p_m and compare coefficients in (1-omega^m)S_m(X)=(X-omega^m)S_(m-1)(X). The first factor in (1.3) vanishes unless c<=z; the second vanishes unless z<=a. Using p_(N-1)=N and the same formula for bar_p_j, the surviving sum, with m=a-c, is omega^(1+c(b+1)) (p_a/p_c) sum_(j=0)^m (-1)^j omega^(j(j-1)/2) omega^((b+1)j)/(p_j p_(m-j)) =omega^(1+c(b+1)) (p_a/p_c) (omega^(b+1);omega)_m/p_m. (1.5) The last equality follows from the same finite binomial identity. If b+m>=N, this Pochhammer symbol contains 1-omega^N and vanishes. Otherwise d=b+m as an ordinary integer and the symbol is p_(b+m)/p_b. This proves (1.1), with no primality assumption. ## 2. A literal comparison with the root-of-unity quantum-group matrix Let s=exp(pi*i/N), H_j=N-1-2j, and use the N-dimensional highest-weight module with H v_j=H_j v_j, K v_j=s^(H_j)v_j, E v_j=[j]_s^2 v_(j-1), F_low v_j=v_(j+1). At the endpoints the missing vectors are zero. These are the specialized usual matrices E v_j=[j]_s[N-j]_s v_(j-1), since [N-j]_s=[j]_s. Let R^q=s^(H tensor H/2) sum_(k=0)^(N-1) s^(k(k-1)/2)(s-s^(-1))^k/[k]_s! E^k tensor F_low^k. (2.1) Every denominator in (2.1) is nonzero. Put G_j=p_j/(1-omega)^j=s^(j(j-1)/2)[j]_s!, D_j=(-s)^j, gamma=omega*s^(-(N-1)^2/2). Then (1.1) gives exactly A=gamma (D G tensor G) R^q (G^(-1) tensor G^(-1)D^(-1)). (2.2) Here G,D are diagonal. To verify (2.2), substitute the matrix elements of E^k and F_low^k in (2.1), replace each [j]_s! by s^(-j(j-1)/2)p_j/(1-omega)^j, and cancel. The remaining exponent and factorials are precisely those in (1.1). Thus exponentially large factorials in G have not been declared harmless; their positions in the exact conjugations remain specified. ## 3. The published enhancement and every braid word Let P swap tensor factors, and let S v_j=v_(j+1 mod N). In the enhanced Kashaev convention used here, B_K=P(R^o)^T, mu_K=-s S, alpha_K=-s, beta_K=1. (3.1) The transpose/order in (3.1) matters. Substituting (2.8) of Kashaev in P(R^o)^T gives exactly the four-index enhanced crossing definition. For the quantum-group dual convention put B_q=P(R^q)^T, mu_q=K^(-1), alpha_q=s^((N^2-1)/2), beta_q=1. (3.2) Equation (2.2), transposed and with the tensor factors exchanged, gives a similarity of B_K with gamma*B_q. For a braid on b strands, define U_b=F^(-tensor b) tensor_(j=1)^b (G^(-1)D^(j-1)). The meaning is the product of F^(-tensor b) with the displayed diagonal tensor product. Since B_q conserves the integer weight sum, it commutes with D tensor D. Thus the same U_b works simultaneously for every adjacent generator and its inverse: rho_K(word)=gamma^(w(word)) U_b rho_q(word) U_b^(-1). (3.3) The enhancement also matches exactly: U_b mu_q^(tensor b) U_b^(-1)=mu_K^(tensor b), gamma*alpha_q=-s=alpha_K. (3.4) For the first identity, diagonal G,D commute with mu_q and F^(-1)diag(omega^j)F=S; also s^(-(N-1))=-s. The quantum-group partial traces have values alpha_q and alpha_q^(-1). One way to verify the scalars is to use the coproduct intertwining equations for (2.1) and trace cyclicity: the weighted partial traces commute with the dual module's generators. These act irreducibly because their adjacent coefficients are nonzero and the K eigenvalues are distinct. The traces are therefore scalar. The positive trace at v_(N-1) and negative trace at v_0 each have a single contributing term, giving s^((N^2-1)/2) and its inverse. The coproduct equations themselves reduce to the coefficient recurrence c_(k+1)/c_k=s^k(s-s^(-1))/[k+1]_s of the finite sum (2.1). These checks are elementary algebra and do not invoke a global state-integral theorem. For a braid closure with one component, cut the first strand and take the weighted partial trace over the others. The unnormalized operator is scalar: it is a quantum-group endomorphism of the simple color. Conjugations on the traced factors cancel by cyclicity; conjugation on the open factor cancels because this operator is scalar. Finally the factors gamma^(w) cancel against alpha_K^(-w) by (3.4). **Consequence.** The normalized enhanced Kashaev period in (3.1) equals the reduced N-colored quantum-group period at s=exp(pi*i/N), with unknot value one. This holds for every braid presentation of a knot and every N>=2. It is a direct independent verification of the standard enhanced-state comparison, not an appeal to its published proof. The usual quantum-group parameter for the colored Jones polynomial is omega=s^2; the chosen dual and tensor-order convention is retained. ## 4. A printed phase needs attention The literal candidate inverse printed in Kashaev's (2.15), combined with the normalization (2.12), fails the identity (2.16) already at N=2: the product is -I. This is checked in characteristic zero with rational entries. The exact cyclotomic diagnostics at further levels give omega*I. We use the actual matrix inverse in (3.3), determined by (2.2), rather than silently deleting this phase. This observation concerns a printed normalization identity, not a counterexample to the knot volume conjecture. The enhanced definition (3.1) specifies its own actual inverse and scalar normalization. ## 5. Reproducible algebraic checks and scope `experiments/audit_kashaev_crossing.py` evaluates the original four-index weight independently of (1.1), checks its complete Fourier transform, the quantum-group matrix comparison, and the enhanced partial traces. It includes even and composite levels. Prime-field diagnostics are supplementary to the characteristic-zero identities proved above. The coefficient and enhancement identities fix a literature state uniformly, with no FAMED hypothesis or knot census. They do not prove the AJ conjecture or the Kashaev volume conjecture. In particular, they do not make the AK/Faddeev contour state equal to this finite period. That is a different comparison. A standard noncommutative A-polynomial can now be discussed together with this distinguished reduced quantum-group period, rather than an arbitrary solution of its recurrence. Root-of-unity periodicity and the geometric q->1 branch must still be distinguished in its period-torsor comparison.

title: An independent audit of the Li–Wang regulator line
text: # An independent audit of the Li–Wang regulator line Research audit, 26 October 2026. The source is Weiping Li and Qingxue Wang, [On the Generalized Volume Conjecture and Regulator, arXiv:math/0610745v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0610745v1), the nine-page 2006 version. Its [version-specific HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0610745v1) was checked against the PDF. The earlier math/0604057 is not needed here. This is a correctness and terminology audit, not a claim about novelty or a proof of colored-Jones asymptotics. The core flat regulator line is valid with logarithms continued along paths. The paper does not construct our root-of-unity quantum norm torsor. There are two distinct branch qualifications: a literal use of the printed discontinuous logarithm fails, while an endpoint-only scalar reading of its later special Chern–Simons integral requires additional trivialization data. Neither qualification disproves the continued-log regulator. ## 1. What the source actually supplies The terminology is a flat line bundle: Introduction, p. 1; §3.2, equation (3.6), pp. 4–5; and Remark 2(iii), p. 7. The universal Heisenberg bundle's explicit construction is referred to Bloch and Ramakrishnan, rather than written out. The inspected text contains neither “torsor” nor “principal.” Proposition 3.2, p. 5, supplies a K2-torsion assertion; Theorem 3.3, p. 6, deduces exactness and rational periods. Equation (3.9), p. 7, remains a conjecture. [Primary text, §§3.2–3.3](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0610745v1#S3.SS2). Removing the zero section of a complex line gives an analytic principal C* bundle. Calling that associated object a torsor is mathematically legitimate. It is a translation of the line-bundle construction, not a separate scalar norm equation or an identification with a quantum object. The calculations below independently check the relevant construction. ## 2. Rebuild the logarithmic quotient and its connection Set t=2πi. On the logarithmic cover of (C*)² write f=exp(F), g=exp(G). The following deck transformations define an analytic line: D_(a,b)(F,G,z)=(F+t a,G+t b,exp(aG) z), a,b in Z. (2.1) Indeed, applying D_(a,b) and then D_(c,d) gives the product multiplier exp((a+c)G+t cb)=exp((a+c)G). Thus the action is an actual action. Local branches F_j=F_i+t a_ij, G_j=G_i+t b_ij give local fiber-coordinate transitions z_j=exp(a_ij G_i)z_i; the same calculation checks their cocycle. Declare A=F dG/t, nabla=d-A. (2.2) Then A changes by a dG, the logarithmic differential of exp(aG). Consequently (2.2) descends. In this declared convention its curvature is F_nabla=-dA=-dF wedge dG/t. (2.3) On a smooth complex curve with f,g invertible, dF and dG are locally holomorphic multiples of the same local parameter differential. Their wedge is zero. The pullback connection is therefore flat. No K2 torsion is needed for this flatness. Lift a based loop γ starting with logarithms F0,G0. Write its endpoint as (F0+t a,G0+t b). Parallel transport in (2.2) multiplies z by exp(∫γ F dG/t). Comparing the endpoint fiber to the initial fiber requires exp(−aG0), by (2.1). The holonomy is exactly r(f,g)(γ)=exp((∫γ F dG−G0 ∫γ dF)/t). (2.4) This reproduces the source's (3.6), with continued logarithms. Shifting F by t r and G0 by t s changes the numerator by t²(rb−sa), so the exponential is branch independent. Concatenation adds an extra t²ab' to the numerator, also invisible after exponentiation. Flatness proves homotopy invariance; rank-one holonomy also gives the usual base-point independence under transport. There is a normalization issue in the printed curvature statements, Proposition 3.1(1), p. 4, and Remark 2(iii), p. 7. With (2.4) fixed as holonomy, the actual connection curvature in convention (2.2) is (2.3), not the unnormalized dF wedge dG. The discrepancy is invisible after restriction to a curve, where both vanish. A nonzero universal curvature or Chern class must retain the connection convention and its factors of 2πi. We do not use the source's unnormalized formula as such a universal Chern–Weil identity. ## 3. Verify that the holonomy descends through the K2 relations Bilinearity follows directly from (2.4). For antisymmetry, the sum of the two numerators is ∫γ d(FG)−G0 ∫γ dF−F0 ∫γ dG=t²ab, whose exponential after division by t is one. The local tame-symbol calculation can also be done without a cited proof. At a puncture with parameter w, let f=w^a u(w), g=w^b v(w), u(0)v(0)!=0. On a small positive circle, continuous logarithms give the limiting numerator/t as bF0−aG0+tab/2. Its exponential is (−1)^(ab) u(0)^b/v(0)^a. (3.1) The radius-dependent powers cancel. Flatness on the punctured disc identifies this limit with the actual small-loop holonomy. For the Steinberg relation, first use f=w,g=1−w on P1 minus {0,1,infinity}. The small-loop values at both 0 and 1 are one by (3.1). These loops generate its fundamental group, so the character is trivial. Pulling back along f proves r(f,1−f)=1 on its domain. Thus the homomorphism out of the symbol presentation of K2 is verified here, including its tame signs. One need not assume a published dilogarithm argument for these particular checks. ## 4. Exactly what torsion gives Suppose q{l,m}=0 in the function-field K2. Then (2.4) has q-th power one. If the relation is initially realized after deleting extra points, the inclusion of that smaller punctured curve surjects on the fundamental group of the larger one; the already-defined character therefore has q-th power one on the source's Y_h as well. Its image has order **dividing** q. Equality with the K2 order is not required and is not implied by applying a homomorphism. The transfer arithmetic in Proposition 3.2 is correct: if restriction to a degree-n field extension kills 2{l,m}, then transfer back gives 2n{l,m}=0. This audit has not independently rederived, from a knot presentation, the existence of that finite extension or the cited order-two statement in it. Those are the geometric K2 inputs to the paper's knot-wide application. They are explicitly kept separate from the directly verified regulator construction and its conditional consequences. For those consequences write F=log l=x+iu and G=log m=y+iv, continuing u,v on the path. Integration by parts on a closed loop gives Im(∫ F dG−G0 ∫ dF)=∫(x dv−y du), Re(∫ F dG−G0 ∫ dF)=−∫(y dx+u dv)+v0∫du. (4.1) The boundary contribution in the first identity cancels the real part of G0 ∫dF. At the paper's complete base point m0=1, choose G0=0. Finite-order holonomy then gives ∫γ (x dv−y du)=0, (q/(4π²))∫γ(y dx+u dv) is an integer. (4.2) The first integrand is a globally defined closed real form; all its periods vanish, so it is exact. The second is a continued-branch integral. Changing the initial branch u by 2πk changes its normalized value by an integer multiple of q. This verifies the substantive quantization deduction under the K2-torsion hypothesis. It gives finite monodromy and a trivial q-th tensor power of the flat line, not a pointing of the original line and not a quantum asymptotic estimate. ## 5. A literal fixed-cut reading fails; the continued-log reading survives Immediately after (3.6), p. 4, the source fixes 0≤arg z<2π and describes the discontinuity on the positive real axis. A literal pointwise insertion of this discontinuous log into the integral cannot define the asserted regulator. Continuous path logs, or equivalent transition contributions at cuts, are necessary. An exact diagnostic uses the algebraic curve l=−z, m=z, z in C*, base point z=1. (5.1) Its symbol {−z,z} is zero: the Steinberg relation applied to z and z^(-1) gives {z,z}={z,−1}, hence {z,−z}=2{z,−1}=0. Thus its K2 order is q=1. On z=exp(iθ), 0≤θ≤2π, continuous logarithms give arg l=π+θ and log m0=0. Therefore ∫ log l dlog m=−∫_0^(2π)(π+θ)dθ=−4π², r(l,m)=1. (5.2) With pointwise 0≤arg l<2π, arg l instead jumps at θ=π. The same integral becomes −∫_0^π(π+θ)dθ−∫_π^(2π)(θ−π)dθ=−2π², literal_fixed_cut_r(l,m)=−1. (5.3) The corresponding normalized real period is 1/2 rather than an integer. This is a counterexample to the **literal fixed-cut reading** of the general construction and quantization inference. It is not a knot A-curve counterexample and does not contradict (2.4) or (4.2). Interpreting (3.6) using continued logs repairs this issue. ## 6. The later special invariant needs its path or endpoint frame After Remark 2(iii), p. 7, the paper defines, for a path c from the complete base point to (l,m), the quantity U_c=−q∫c(y dx+u dv). (6.1) Remark 3, on the same page, describes U/(2π)² as well-defined in R/Z. The path is indeed present in the preceding definition. On that marked path domain (6.1) is a meaningful quantity. The assertion cannot be inferred as a single-valued function of an **unmarked endpoint** from the closed-loop statement (4.2) alone. To see the obstruction, insert a based loop γ before c and let a=wind_γ(l). The l logarithm on the following copy of c has changed by 2πia. Consequently U_(γ*c)−U_c=U_γ−2πq a∫c darg m, (U_(γ*c)−U_c)/(4π²) =−q a Δ_c arg(m)/(2π) mod Z. (6.2) The right side is generally not integral. For (5.1), let c_θ run from angle 0 to θ with continuous arguments. Direct integration gives U_(c_θ)=−πθ−θ²/2, U_(c_(θ+2π))−U_(c_θ)=−4π²−2πθ. (6.3) At θ=π/2 the difference divided by 4π² is −5/4. Thus even the valid continued-log interpretation does not make this integral a function of the unmarked endpoint on a general torsion-symbol curve. The same obstruction (6.2) applies on any curve possessing the stated winding loop and a path with the indicated nonintegral endpoint phase; we do not assert a specific knot example from (5.1). There is a precise section interpretation. Put rho=−y dx−u dv+i(x dv−y du) =F dG−d(yF). (6.4) Then d rho=dF wedge dG. Under u→u+2πa it changes by −2πa dv. Thus rho is a local connection potential, not a single global scalar form. The smooth gauge z_tilde=exp(−yF/t)z changes (2.2) to rho/t and has deck multiplier exp(i a v). Its q-th tensor power retains exp(iq a v), exactly the endpoint phase missing from an endpoint-only reading of (6.1). A path-cover value or a local coordinate of a bundle section is consistent. A chosen global endpoint frame, or explicit cut corrections, is additional data. The vanishing of the exterior derivative in Remark 2(iii) does not itself supply it. ## 7. Keep the categories and our normalization separate The universal object in (2.1) is analytic. Its nonzero vectors form an analytic principal C* bundle. Its restriction to a curve with (2.2) is a flat bundle; the sheaf of horizontal vectors is a rank-one local system. H1 with **constant** C* coefficients classifies these flat objects, rather than just their underlying holomorphic lines. The universal analytic bundle is not an algebraic G_m torsor on (G_m)². Integrating (2.3)/(2πi) on the real two-torus gives −1 in our declared convention, so the underlying topological line is nontrivial. In contrast C[f^(±1),g^(±1)] is a factorial regular ring, and its algebraic Picard group is zero. The universal line therefore cannot be the analytification of an algebraic line on that torus. This obstruction concerns the universal torus bundle, not every restriction of it. In particular a finite-monodromy restriction can be studied with a finite-cover algebraic model, but that is further category/comparison information, not the displayed analytic quotient. The associated Heisenberg group can be written (F,G,H)*(F',G',H') =(F+F',G+G',H+H'+F G'). (7.1) Its center is additive and the quotient is the additive (F,G) plane. Left multiplication by (ta,tb,t²c) sends H to H+taG+t²c. Exponentiating H/t gives precisely (2.1); dH−F dG is invariant. The noncommutative central extension, its integral lattice quotient, and the resulting analytic C* bundle are related constructions, not interchangeable names for one algebraic G_m torsor over the A-curve. There is also a factor of two in a direct comparison with [our boundary line](boundary_regulator_period.md). On a **common** torus with U=log m,V=log l, the regulator potential is V dU/t. The gauge z_sym=exp(−UV/(2t))z changes it to A_sym=(V dU−U dV)/(2t), z_sym'=(−1)^(ab)exp((bU−aV)/2)z_sym. (7.2) Squaring removes the sign and gives exactly our deck multiplier exp(bU−aV) and potential (V dU−U dV)/t. Thus, on the same torus and with these conventions, our boundary line is the **square** of the symmetrized r(l,m) line. Matching the actual papers additionally requires transporting squared eigenvalues and complete-point shifts; the literal variable names are not that transport. Reversing (l,m) dualizes the regulator. These constants should not be hidden inside a generic statement that the two lines are the same. [Our common period space](common_frobenius_regulator_period_space.md) has an explicit algebraic unipotent connection and further exponential periods. Nothing here identifies their selected periods with the knot state. [Our quantum norm construction](intrinsic_quantum_a_norm_torsor.md) instead begins with a specialized q-difference module, a finite etale cyclic algebra S/k, and N_(S/k)(a)=v. That solution variety is a torsor under the norm-one torus, while its scalar intertwiners form a separate G_m torsor. Neither follows from (2.4) or from calling a line's nonzero vectors a torsor. ## 8. Reproducible scope [The exact audit script](../experiments/audit_li_wang_heisenberg.py) checks the deck cocycle, connection transformation, curvature constant, antisymmetry, branch shifts, Heisenberg horizontal form, local secondary-potential transformation, factor-of-two comparison, and both explicit branch diagnostics. [Recorded results](../experiments/li_wang_heisenberg_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_li_wang_heisenberg.py The verified result is the analytic regulator line, its continued-log holonomy, and the quantization deduction conditional on K2 torsion. The knot K2 input has not been independently reproved here. The endpoint-only reading of the later special invariant needs correction or additional marking. No quantum norm-torsor comparison or volume conjecture is proved by this audit.

title: The literal FIRST five-point operator word and its original full source
text: # The literal FIRST five-point operator word and its original full source 28 October 2026. This realizes the FIRST classical certificate -partial(b,p,p_1,s_M,s_R) of [the crossing fundamental cycle](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md), with its actual flag order. It uses the original two physical heads, one compulsory second-head strict cut, the original factorial frame, and its marked full-Psi function. No auxiliary head or unrelated quantum-torus coordinates are introduced. The resulting two-to-three operator identity is embedded in the ENTIRE original crossing. Every finite projector, marked scalar, Cartan factor and original cup/cap remains. This closes this literal local certificate; it does not by itself supply a positive geometric face atlas or a global selected-cycle degree. ## 1. The actual FIRST five flags, in the same bounded frame Keep the complete original conventions Q=exp(2pi*i/N), d=N-1, x=-q^(-1), lambda=x^(-1)=Qx, S_1^N=mu, S_2^N=x^N mu, Z=Z_1, T=Z_2, X=x S_2 S_1^(-1). Thus XZ=QZX and XT=Q^(-1)TX. Use the actual balanced Gauss generators e_j,f_j,K_j of the [shared quantum meridians](actual_shared_quantum_flags_and_charged_exchange.md). In the bounded homogeneous frame Y=-ZS_1, L=[[Y,0],[-S_1,1]], the FIRST flags have the following canonical columns and retained right tags. This is the SAME frame as in [the literal middle configuration](actual_middle_five_point_wall_factorization.md). | Flag | Canonical column | Right tag in L flag = column times tag | | --- | --- | --- | | b | (1,1-X)^t | Y | | p | (0,1)^t | 1 | | p_1 | (1-Z,1)^t | lambda | | s_M | (1,1)^t | YK_1 | | s_R | (1,R)^t | YK_2K_1 | Here R=1-(1-T)X. (1) For the last row, the exact coproduct/Gauss first column is s_R=(K_2K_1,F_tot K_2K_1)^t, F_tot=f_1+K_1^(-1)f_2. Since f_1-S_1=Y and K_1^(-1)f_2Y^(-1)=-(1-T)X, one has F_tot-S_1=RY, proving the row without dividing by any nilpotent flag determinant. Every right tag is retained. At unit wrap marks these tags are unitary, as is the previous bounded-frame convention up to its fixed two-by-two condition. Classically the ordered tuple is therefore (b,p,p_1,s_M,s_R) =(1-X,infinity,1/(1-Z),1,1-(1-T)X). (2) The reciprocal in (2) is only a commutative chart notation; the actual finite flag is the homogeneous column in the table. ## 2. Its five literal cross-ratios Put n_cl=-X(1-Z)/Z, G=1-n_cl+n_cl T. Using exactly the determinant convention r(v0,v1,v2,v3) =det(v3,v1)det(v2,v0)/(det(v3,v0)det(v2,v1)), the FIRST face table is | Omitted flag | Cross-ratio r_j | Sign in -partial | | --- | --- | --- | | b | G | - | | p | G/T | + | | p_1 | 1/T | - | | s_M | (1-1/n_cl)/T | + | | s_R | 1-1/n_cl | - | These are direct determinants of the five columns in (2), not an arbitrary renamed five-term pattern. The independent symbolic audit checks all five rational identities. Define the convenient quad coordinates a_cl=n_cl(1-T), y_cl=-n_cl T/(1-n_cl), J_cl=T/G. The rational oriented pre-Bloch rules [1-z]=-[z], [1/z]=-[z], [1-1/z]=[z], and [z/(z-1)]=-[z] convert that literal table to -partial=[a_cl]-[J_cl]+[T]-[y_cl]-[n_cl]. (3) In particular (3) compares the two signed lists left: [n_cl]-[T], right: -[y_cl]-[J_cl]+[a_cl]. (4) The signed right list minus the left list is the specified FIRST negative boundary. These signs and quads are fixed below by the actual finite operators. ## 3. The genuine finite cut and the ORIGINAL crossing atom Let E_d(T) be the original second-head index-d projector and put n=e_1 S_2=(Q-Z^(-1))X, c=n(1-E_d(T)), a=e_1 f_2. (5) The classical n is exactly n_cl from Section 2. Its second-head cut is indispensable. It gives, at the actual finite level, cT=Q^(-1)Tc, c^N=0, a=c(1-QT). (6) Indeed c=e_1 tensor J_(+,2) uses the literal strict second-head raise. Acting on input index j, its multiplication by 1-QT supplies 1-Q^(j+1), exactly the coefficient of f_2. The possible wrap of n is killed by that same original zero. Use the original finite Euler function P_Q(A)=sum_(h=0)^d p_h A^h, p_h=(-1)^h Q^(h(h-1)/2)/(Q;Q)_h. Let F_j=(Q;Q)_j and retain the marked scalar phi_N=sqrt(N) exp{i*pi[1/4-(N+N^(-1))/12]}. The original marked full-Psi root clock is mathcal F_T=marked Psi(QT)=phi_N diag_j(1/F_j). The logarithmic lift at index j is 2pi*i*(j+1)/N. In particular the index-d value uses the regular TOP lift, not the bottom zero. Set F=mathcal F_T^(-1)=phi_N^(-1)diag_j(F_j). (7) Consecutive factorial ratios, including the strict top edge, prove F c F^(-1)=c(1-QT)=a. (8) Thus the ENTIRE original uncheck crossing is R_0=D P_Q(a)=D F P_Q(c) F^(-1). (9) D is its original Cartan diagonal. Its nonzero common Cartan scalar kappa, flip, writhe correction and peripheral normalization remain the original external lines. Equation (9) is a matrix identity, not a change of invariant or a replacement of the original source. ## 4. Exact two-to-three sequence and all developed arguments Abbreviate P=P_Q(c) and define the transported marked clock H=P^(-1)TP, F_H=P^(-1)FP, y=-Q cH, Y=P_Q(y). (10) All displayed inverses exist. In particular H^N=1 and y^N=c^N=0. The relation cH=Q^(-1)Hc follows by conjugating (6). Conjugating (8) gives F_H c F_H^(-1)=c(1-QH)=c+y. (11) Moreover yc=Qcy. The ordered finite binomial theorem therefore gives P_Q(c+y)=P_Q(y)P_Q(c). Every term of degree >=N vanishes because it contains that degree of c. Thus (11) yields the exact FIRST operator sequence F_H P=Y P F_H, P F_H=Y^(-1)F_H P. (12) This is a two-to-three identity at every level, including even and composite N. Its one marked full-Psi factor is the SAME transported F_H on both sides; its scalar phi_N^(-1) has not been reset. The left word P F_H develops to c and the negative clock T, since PHP^(-1)=T. The right word develops to y with negative orientation, the negative marked clock J=Y^(-1)HY=H(1+cH)^(-1), (13) and the final positive argument Y^(-1)F_H c F_H^(-1)Y=a. (14) Here (13)--(14) are exact ordered identities, not only symbols. For a proof, the finite Euler recurrences give (1-c)H=T, Y^(-1)cY=c(1-y), Y^(-1)HY=H(1-Q^(-1)y)^(-1). Since (1-y)H=H(1-Q^(-1)y), substitution in (11) gives Y^(-1)c(1-QH)Y =c(1-y)-QcH =c-Qc(1-c)H=c(1-QT)=a. The denominator 1+cH in (13) is a unit because cH is nilpotent; there is no inverse of a singular clock determinant. J is a conjugate of H, so J^N=1 with its integer clock mark transported by the same Y, not chosen afresh. Classically H=T/(1-n_cl), and (10), (13), (14) give precisely y_cl,J_cl,a_cl of Section 2. Thus the five developed signed arguments of (12) are the literal FIRST table (3)--(4). There is also a useful fixed-degree ordered Ptolemy form, involving the ORIGINAL unsplit atom a rather than a guessed scalar quotient: G_first=1-a=1-c+Tc, J=G_first^(-1)T, r=Jc=-y(1-y)^(-1), 1-r=G_first^(-1)(1-c). (14a) For (14a), invert (13): J^(-1)=H^(-1)+c=T^(-1)(1-c)+c =T^(-1)(1-c+Tc)=T^(-1)(1-a). Also Jc=QcH(1+QcH)^(-1), which is the displayed quad of y. All inverses in (14a) are units because a,c,y are nilpotent. The first literal face complements G_first and 1-c, the clock J, and the fourth-face quad r therefore satisfy exact ordered equations on the original physical heads, with the strict c-wall retained. They are not products of separately compressed coordinate ports. Combining (9)--(12) embeds the identity in the ORIGINAL crossing: R_0=D P F_H F^(-1) =D Y^(-1)F_H P F^(-1). (15) The terminal F^(-1) is a compulsory interface. Deleting it changes the operator and original period. The inverse checked crossing is the inverse of (15), with the SAME original scalars; the exact audit compares it independently with the original negative formula. The operator proof (5)--(15) actually extends over the whole original color parameters at this fixed physical q root: use the original e_1(x_1), the same strict J_(+,2), and the original mixed Cartan D(x_1,x_2). Equations (6), (8), and the finite binomial proof are unchanged. Thus it also preserves the whole meridian color germ and its normal derivatives. The literal five-flag table of Sections 1--2 and the explicit source evaluations below are stated at completeness. No off-root Hopf or generic-q invariant is being asserted. ## 5. The complete strict wall and its current Every power of the cut is explicit: c^h=n^h(1-sum_(j=N-h)^(N-1)E_j(T)), 0<=h<N. (16) For h=0 the sum is empty. The forbidden second-head wrap inputs are exactly those j with j+h>=N. The first-head nilpotence is retained independently. Thus (16) supplies the whole finite source wall, not merely its principal approximation. Write mu_2=S_2^N=x^N mu and W=nE_d(T)=mu_2 e_1 tensor |0><d|, F_tot=f_1 tensor I+K_1^(-1) tensor f_2. Its actual total-current commutator is [F_tot,W]=mu_2( [f_1,e_1] tensor |0><d| +(1-Q)K_1^(-1)e_1 tensor |1><d| -(1-Q^(-1))e_1K_1^(-1) tensor |0><d-1|). (17) This follows by applying f_2 before or after the missing wrap. It is retained in (5), (16), and all conjugated interfaces. No separate wall or radial summand is asserted Ward-invariant. Applying the ordinary typed commutator product rule to the exact operator equality (15) transports every other original current as well. At an interior position of a word the full W remains; one does not replace it by a scalar source value. ## 6. Original cup, marker, and uncanceled marked scalar Keep the ORIGINAL balanced cup and full marker p=N sum_(j=0)^d x^(j-d)|j,d-j>, m|a,b>=x^b/N^2, mp=1. (18) On this whole degree-d cup, any forbidden second-head input in (16) has first index <h and is already killed by e_1^h. Thus c^h p=n^h p, m c^h p=1, 0<=h<N. (19) For the moment in (19), summing the explicit complete e_1 coefficients reduces it to (1/N)sum_(j=h)^d (Q^(-j);Q)_h=1. Extend the sum to all j modulo N: its omitted terms are zero, its constant coefficient contributes N, and all positive powers Q^(-ell j), 0<ell<=h<N, sum to zero. This proves (19) directly from the original source. The finite hockey-stick contraction already used for the original middle factor now gives Pp=N|d,0>, Hp=p, F_Hp=phi_N^(-1)p. (20) The transported T-index here is zero, hence the nonzero marked Psi argument is Q with its recorded index-one logarithmic lift. Consequently the two words of (12) have the exact source value mP F_Hp=mY^(-1)F_H Pp=1/(N phi_N). (21) Its modulus is N^(-3/2), with no adjustable normalization. Equation (21) evaluates the unadorned local word on the literal cup. In the full original embedding (15), its actual incoming source is F^(-1)p and its actual outgoing row retains flip D. Those interfaces are kept as operators. The full marked original one-crossing source therefore remains exactly its old value: m flip D [P F_H] F^(-1)p =m flip D [Y^(-1)F_H P] F^(-1)p=1, (22) before the unchanged common scalar kappa. This is also checked against the original E/Cartan coefficient evaluator. No unknown knot period enters the source or any adapter. ## 7. Full-Psi coefficient cycles and scope Every factor of (15) has the same exact full-Psi coefficient realization as in [the full-function source theorem](actual_modular_dilog_circle_and_boundary_source.md). For an explicit contractive core let J_(minus,1) and J_(+,2) be the original strict shifts and use the previously proved factorial/Gaussian frame H_e|j>=lambda^j(-1)^jQ^(j(j-1)/2)|j>/F_j. Then c=(H_e tensor I)(J_(minus,1) tensor J_(+,2)) (H_e^(-1) tensor I). The core has norm <=1. Also y=P^(-1)(-QcT)P, so its Euler factor and inverse reduce, through the explicitly retained P interfaces, to the same kind of strict shift times a unit clock. F and F^(-1) are the marked second-head factorial diagonals with the phases (7); their moment realizations retain the original reflected factorial factors N and phi_N. Every coefficient moment is kept as its FULL circle-minus-ray source, or its equivalent exact atomic-window resolution. The inverse Euler factor Y^(-1) uses the original inverse polynomial on its nilpotent argument, not an unmarked inverse of a scalar full-Psi function. All root marks, finite cuts and radial terms remain in their actual operator order. The common Cartan/writhe/ peripheral lines in (15) are unchanged. This proves the FIRST literal finite five-point operator identity and its full original source, uniformly for the crossing. It does not prove that every displayed framed face is already in a common positive geometric polarization, that separated radial pieces have a gap, or that the global geometric cycle is selected. Run python3 experiments/audit_literal_first_full_phi_certificate.py The audit verifies the five literal rational faces, 27 exact complete/wrap families through N=10, all strict-cut powers and current (17), the developed arguments, both original crossing signs, and the complete cup/marked source including (21)--(22). Eighteen additional mixed-color operator checks verify the whole-color extension, without applying the complete source formulas away from their stated color.

title: A literal middle five-point operator identity with its complete finite source
text: # A literal middle five-point operator identity with its complete finite source 28 October 2026. This realizes the middle classical certificate +partial(a,b,p,p_1,s_M) from [the crossing fundamental cycle](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) as an exact finite relative operator identity inside the original crossing factorization. Its developed arguments are the five cross-ratios of that **specific** configuration, with the required quad/orientation changes. The X face is a strict cut of a cyclic unit; its full projector correction is explicit. The original cup selects a nonzero top marked full-Phi value. This is an identity with marked full-Phi and nilpotent Euler operators, including their factorial face frames and circle/radial sources. It does not assert that each factor separately is an already assigned positive charged tetrahedron in a regular geometric face frame. That further face/Fourier assignment, the other two certificates, and the global selected cycle remain separate work. ## 1. Fixed actual coordinates and the original crossing factor Use complete original heads with Q=exp(2pi*i/N), d=N-1, x=-q^(-1), lambda=x^(-1)=Qx, S_1^N=mu, S_2^N=x^N mu, Z=Z_1, X=x S_2S_1^(-1), XZ=QZX, X^N=Z^N=1. The literal five flags were calculated in [the middle-configuration note](actual_middle_five_point_wall_factorization.md). With every right flag tag retained, an explicit bounded homogeneous frame sends them to (a,b,p,p_1,s_M)=(0,1-X,infinity,(1-Z,1)^t,1). (1) The fourth entry is a homogeneous column; no inverse of 1-Z is taken. Put P(A)=sum_(h=0)^d (-1)^hQ^(h(h-1)/2)A^h/F_h, F_h=(Q;Q)_h, n=e_1S_2=(Q-Z^(-1))X, P=P(n), n_-= -e_1Z_2S_2. The exact original uncheck crossing is R_0=D P(n_-)P. (2) D is the original Cartan diagonal. Its common scalar line kappa, framing and peripheral factors remain external and identical throughout. The checked crossing is flip R_0 with that same line; none of these factors is reset. ## 2. The fifth clock is an actual quantum cross-ratio Define H=P^(-1)ZP=Z(1-n)=Z+(1-QZ)X. (3) The finite Euler recurrence proves the middle equality. Thus H is invertible, H^N=1 and nH=QHn, without taking any singular reciprocal of 1-Z. Its commutative symbol is H_cl=X+Z-XZ, the H appearing in the five cross-ratios of (1). Let Psi be the full literature function with the exact normalization in [the modular moment theorem](actual_modular_dilog_circle_and_boundary_source.md). Retain phi_N=sqrt(N) exp{i pi[1/4-(N+N^(-1))/12]}. The elementary marked root evaluation, independently proved in [the marked-flag note](actual_marked_full_phi_flag_pentagon.md), gives F_Z=marked Psi(QZ) =phi_N diag_j[1/F_j], 0<=j<N. (4) The argument at clock index j is on logarithmic lift 2pi*i*(j+1)/N. Thus j=d uses the regular TOP value, not the zero on the bottom lift. The finite missing arrow of n lies at input j=0. The exact conjugation is F_Z n F_Z^(-1)=n(1-Z). (5) Transport the **entire** clock mark, rather than choosing a new one, by F_H=P^(-1)F_ZP. (6) It is the marked full-Phi function of QH in this transported integer frame. Equations (3), (5), and commutation of P with n give F_H n F_H^(-1)=n(1-H). (7) All matrices in (3)--(7) are invertible where claimed at the physical root. The inverse of 1-H is not used. ## 3. The exact two-to-three word and the original R Since n and -nH Q-commute and share nilpotent degree, the finite ordered binomial theorem proves F_H P=P P(-nH)F_H. Equivalently the literal two-to-three sequence is P(n)F_H^(-1)=F_H^(-1)P(n)P(-nH). (8) Multiplying by the displayed interface F_H gives an exact refactorization of the original crossing, including every exterior operator: R_0=D P(n_-) F_H^(-1)P(n)P(-nH)F_H. (9) The final F_H is a retained face/source adapter; deleting it would change the original period. In a network one can use (8) on that specified subword or (9) as a full crossing replacement with its adapter. These are not definitions of a new invariant. ## 4. All five developed arguments and the exact X-wall Use the actual preceding factors to transport each argument to the common input frame. The two arguments on the left of (8) are n and the negative clock Z, since PHP^(-1)=Z. The three on the right are the negative clock H and u=F_H^(-1)nF_H, w=-F_H^(-1)P nH P^(-1)F_H =-F_H^(-1)nZF_H. (10) These are explicit finite matrices, and they simplify to K=X(1-E_0(Z)), u_Z=-Z^(-1)K, u=P^(-1)u_ZP, w=QK=QX(1-E_0(Z)). (11) Here E_0 is the original first-clock zero-index projector. It is the required finite source wall, not an omitted exceptional case. For a proof, F_Z^(-1)nF_Z=u_Z follows from consecutive factorial ratios. Also n=u_Z+QK, u_Z(QK)=Q(QK)u_Z, P(n)=P(u_Z)P(QK). (12) Every term of degree >=N vanishes because K is a strict cut shift. Conjugation by P(u_Z) sends QK to QK(1-u_Z)^(-1). Substitution of (6) into w in (10) then gives w=P^(-1)[-u_Z Z(1-u_Z)^(-1)]P =P^(-1)[QK(1-u_Z)^(-1)]P=QK, proving the last identity of (11) at all levels. The corresponding exact ordered quad relation is r=wH^(-1)=-u(1-Q^(-1)u)^(-1), r^N=0. (13) The inverses in (12)--(13) exist because u is nilpotent. They are not inverses of a clock determinant with a nontrivial kernel. Classically, away from the boundary divisors, (10)--(13) become u_cl=n_cl/(1-H_cl)=-X/[Z(1-X)], w_cl=X, r_cl=X/H_cl, u_cl=r_cl/(r_cl-1). Thus u is the negative-quad coordinate of the tetrahedron with cross-ratio X/H, while w is the precisely cut X tetrahedron. The developed signed list of (8) is therefore left: [n_cl]-[Z], right: -[H_cl]-[X/H_cl]+[X]. (14) This is exactly the middle certificate of (1), since n_cl=-X(1-Z)/Z is the positive-quad coordinate of its omitted-a tetrahedron. It is not a five-point relation for freely chosen unrelated flags. Statement (14) identifies the rational geometric arguments and their quantum cuts. It does not discard the nonlinear factorial frames in assigning a positive tetrahedral kernel or its complete phase. Those frames remain in (4), (6), and the period construction below. ## 5. The complete original source is nonzero and polynomial Keep the actual cup and full marker p=N sum_(a=0)^d x^(a-d)|a,d-a>, m|a,b>=x^b/N^2, mp=1. Then exactly P(n)p=N|d,0>, Hp=Q^(-1)p, F_Hp=(phi_N/N)p. (15) To prove the first identity, the coefficient of |u,d-u> is N x^(u-d) times sum_(h=0)^(d-u) Q^(-h(u+1)) {u+h choose h}_Q ={N choose u+1}_(Q^(-1)). The equality is the finite Gaussian hockey-stick identity. At the primitive root it is zero for u<d and one for u=d. The remaining identities in (15) follow from (3), (4), and (6). In particular the actual cup selects the TOP marked QH argument, with value phi_N/N. Consequently both sides of (8) have the exact source value mP(n)F_H^(-1)p=phi_N^(-1). (16) This is nonzero and has modulus N^(-1/2). In (9) the retained final adapter has factor phi_N/N on the cup. The full checked original crossing therefore has exactly its old source value, including kappa and all original framing/peripheral lines. The scalar has not been reset to one in (8). The complete cut correction is known at every order, not just to first order: w^a=Q^a X^a(1-sum_(j=0)^(a-1)E_j(Z)), mw^ap=1-a/N, 0<=a<N. (17) These formulas follow from the strict shift and the original uniform marked clock distribution. Thus the projector correction can be of order one at bulk a; it is not legitimate to remove it because an individual endpoint weight is 1/N. At an interior position of a longer word one must keep F_H as an operator and every projector of (17). The scalar simplification (15) applies to this actual input cup. The earlier counterexamples to untransported interior cut relocation are unaffected. ## 6. Full-Phi/Fourier frames and all radial components Every operator in (8)--(9) has an explicit fixed-complexity full-Phi/Gaussian relative-period realization. Let T=J_(minus,1) tensor S_2, D_n|j>=lambda^j(-1)^jQ^(j(j-1)/2)|j>, H_n|j>=D_n(j)|j>/F_j. Then the exact frames are n=H_n T H_n^(-1), u_Z=D_n T D_n^(-1), w=lambda T, H_n=phi_N^(-1)D_nF_Z. (18) D_n is a unitary linear/quadratic Gaussian at unit marks. T is the literal strict compression of a unit shift; its missing Fourier/Hardy endpoint is exactly the projector in (11), not a new boundary convention. For unit S_2 all these cores have norm at most one. Their inverses as Euler operators use the opposite root/orientation, retaining its phase. For each Euler polynomial in a contractive core use the exact circle-minus-radial operator P_epsilon(T)=B_epsilon(T)-E_epsilon(T) of the modular-circle theorem. For diagonal frames use (F_Z)_j=phi_N(-1)^jQ^(-j(j-1)/2) [B_+(j)-E_+(j)], (F_Z^(-1))_j=(N/phi_N)Q^(-j-1) [B_+(d-j)-E_+(d-j)]. (19) All phases and the factors phi_N,N are retained. For example P(-nH)=P^(-1)P(-nZ)P, and -nZ=H_n(-TZ)H_n^(-1), another contractive core. Equations (6), (18), and (19) therefore expand the full word (9) into finitely many explicit Phi/Gaussian integrals and their original coefficient cycles. Every bracket in (19), and every transfer bracket, is kept as B-E in its original order. Expanding their product includes ALL circle/radial components with their signs; no individual component is identified with the whole original scalar. The radial kernel alone has the proven harmonic or diagonal polynomial bound, while other full-Phi factors can still give an exponential period. No global domination estimate is inferred from those local bounds. The exact operator identity also transports every actual Ward current: apply the ordinary typed product rule to (8) or (9). In particular, the X-wall is QXE_0=QE_dX, whose original current is explicitly [F_tot,E_dX]=(Q^(-1)-1)mu^(-1) |d><0| tensor S_2^2. It remains in (11), (17), and (19). The other current terms are finite commutators of the displayed P, F_Z and their inverses; differentiating the exact operator word gives their equal full sum. This is not a claim of sectorwise Ward vanishing. ## 7. Scope and exact audit This provides the literal middle five-point relative operator sequence, its original R embedding, its marked full-Phi clocks, every strict projector moment, and the nonzero original cup coefficient. It is an actual finite identity at every N, including even N, with no hypothetical source replacement. To obtain a complete positive geometric tensor presentation one must still assign these framed operators to the proper oriented geometric face kernels and transport the actual relative cycle. The other two classical certificates are not declared proved by (8). A local operator equality does not give a global geometric intersection degree. Run python3 experiments/audit_literal_middle_full_phi_certificate.py The exact prime-field audit checks 27 complete/wrap families through N=10: (8), the entire original R word (9), the cut identities and every moment (17), and the original source (15)--(16). The common phi_N power is retained symbolically in those homogeneous tests; its phase and modulus were independently checked in the marked-full-Phi audit.

title: The physical THIRD five-point word with its original source
text: # The physical THIRD five-point word with its original source 28 October 2026. The THIRD certificate -partial(a,b,p,p_1,s_R) has a physical two-head realization. The construction uses the inverse of the actual shared-flag braid transport, followed by the already proved FIRST identity at the opposite root. Finite factorial reflection embeds its inverse word in the ENTIRE original crossing. All clock marks, strict cuts, scalar lines and original endpoint sources remain. This replaces the proposed use of the auxiliary vacuum pentagon for this face table. That auxiliary formula remains an exact original-R port, but its contracted source has a forced degenerate clock face. The physical construction below does not use those compressed ports. This closes the literal local operator/source certificate at the same level as FIRST and MIDDLE. It does not identify its framed factors with a positive charged geometric state or transport the original global cycle to the positive reference cycle. ## 1. The actual third flags and their useful order Keep the complete conventions of the [shared actual flags](actual_shared_quantum_flags_and_charged_exchange.md): Q=exp(2pi*i/N), x=-q^(-1), lambda=x^(-1)=Qx, S_1^N=mu, S_2^N=x^N mu, Z=Z_1, T=Z_2, X=x S_2S_1^(-1), a_u=TX, n_+=e_1S_2, n_-=-e_1Z_2S_2, P_+=P_Q(n_+), M=P_Q(n_-), A=M P_+=P_Q(e_1f_2), R_0=D A, B=flip D A. The unchanged common scalar kappa is external to B and R_0; all original framing and peripheral factors are retained there. Define H=P_+^(-1)ZP_+=Z(1-n_+), R=1-(1-T)X, X_R=a_u R^(-1), Z_R=1-R(1-Z). (1) Here H is a root clock. R is a unit since ((1-T)X)^N=0. Neither is an inverse of a missing-arrow projector. In the SAME bounded homogeneous frame used by FIRST and MIDDLE, the actual THIRD tuple has columns and original right tags | Flag | Column | Right tag | | --- | --- | --- | | a | (1,0)^t | -ZS_1 | | b | (1,1-X)^t | -ZS_1 | | p | (0,1)^t | 1 | | p_1 | (1-Z,1)^t | lambda | | s_R | (1,R)^t | (-ZS_1)K_2K_1 | The fifth row is the actual total-lowering first column, as proved in [FIRST](literal_first_full_phi_certificate.md). No flag determinant has been inverted to obtain this table. At the commutative regular chart, rescaling s_R to one gives (a,b,p,p_1,s_R)=(0,1-X_R,infinity,1/(1-Z_R),1), H=X_R+Z_R-X_R Z_R. (2) The original homogeneous columns, rather than the displayed scalar reciprocals, remain the finite definitions. ## 2. Inverse actual flag transport gives the missing polarization Put a_eff=Q a_u Z^(-1), C=A^(-1)a_eff A. (3) The following are exact physical matrix identities: Z_R=A^(-1)ZA, C=H^(-1)X_R, CZ_R=QZ_R C, C^N=Z_R^N=1. (4) Thus X_R and Z_R are not renamed as a quantum torus. The actual coupled torus is C,Z_R, and its required polarization is X_R=HC, with the displayed order. There is no auxiliary compression. Here is an all-level proof of the nontrivial middle identity in (4). Use t_2,Delta,v,t_3,H_1,H_2 from the shared-flag note. Its independently proved forward relations are BS_1B^(-1)=t_2, B t_2 B^(-1)=t_3, BG_1B^(-1)=H_2, t_2=F_tot+xK_tot^(-1)S_2, t_3=t_2-QDelta v^(-1). Direct multiplication of those original Gauss matrices gives H_2(1,S_1)^t=(1,t_3)^t x v. (5) For clarity, its upper-right entry is beta=e_2K_1, its lower-right entry is lambda+t_2 beta, and its upper row on (1,S_1) is x v. The second component is consequently t_2 x v-lambda Delta, which is the second component in (5). The rank-one expression for G_1-lambda and G_1^(-1) gives G_1^(-1)(1,t_2)^t=(1,t_0)^t lambda^(-1)QH, t_0=S_1+Q^(-1)Delta H^(-1)=xS_2H^(-1). (6) The first tag in (6) follows by expanding 1-lambda^(-1)e_1Delta=QH. Its last equality follows from S_1H+Q^(-1)Delta=xS_2; S_2 commutes with H. Conjugating the ENTIRE column (6) by B and using (5) proves B^(-1)S_1B=xS_2H^(-1). (7) Both first tags are units. No uniqueness of a nilpotent eigenline is presumed. Because B preserves the original F_tot and K_tot, the formula for t_2 also gives B^(-1)S_2B=x^(-1)K_tot(S_1-F_tot). (8) Cartan and flip conjugation give, with x^2=Q^(-1), flip D a_eff D^(-1) flip=X^(-1). Hence C=B^(-1)X^(-1)B. Substitute (7)--(8), together with S_1-F_tot=RZS_1, K_tot=x^2 Z^(-1)T^(-1), [K_tot,R]=0. In order, this gives C=H^(-1)X Z^(-1)R^(-1)K_tot^(-1) =H^(-1)TXR^(-1)=H^(-1)X_R, proving the missing polarization identity without a finite-level guess. For the first identity in (4), A=P_Q(e_1f_2) and the Euler recurrence give A^(-1)ZA=Z(1-e_1f_2). The actual relation Z e_1f_2=-(1-T)X(1-Z) identifies this with (1). Finally a_eff Z=QZ a_eff and a_eff^N=1 give the last two identities in (4). Define the actual nilpotent nu=C(1-Z_R)=A^(-1)n_-A=P_+^(-1)n_-P_+. The original Euler recurrence then proves the ordered relation H=Z_R(1-nu)^(-1), X_R=HC, H=Z_R(1-C+CZ_R)^(-1). (9) All inverses in (9) exist since nu^N=0. In particular these are full coupled physical operators, not products of distinct typed ports. ## 3. All five actual face arguments The permutation (a,b,p,p_1,s_R) -> (a,s_R,b,p_1,p) is even. Computing determinants of the columns in Section 1 gives the following table, with c_cl=C and t_cl=Z_R at the classical symbol: | Omitted position in (a,s_R,b,p_1,p) | Cross-ratio | Sign in -partial | | --- | --- | --- | | a | g=1-C+CZ_R=Z_R/H | - | | s_R | g/Z_R=1/H | + | | b | 1/Z_R | - | | p_1 | (1-1/C)/Z_R | + | | p | 1-1/C | - | These are EXACTLY the FIRST table with parameters C,Z_R, on this evenly reordered ACTUAL third configuration. The calculation uses the specified five flags, not equality of two arbitrary zero Bloch sums. Put at this classical chart nu=C(1-Z_R), y=-CZ_R/(1-C). The table's signed sum is -partial_THIRD=[nu]-[H]+[Z_R]-[y]-[C]. (10) Its explicit remaining quad relations are y/(y-1)=X_R, nu/(nu-1)=1-H/Z_R. Thus (10) is also -[1-H/Z_R]-[H]+[Z_R]+[X_R]-[C]. (11) For comparison, the original THIRD order has cross-ratios (1/nu, 1/(1-Z_R), C, X_R, H). Expansion of its negative alternating boundary gives exactly (11). The cross-ratios and both quads are checked independently by symbolic determinants in the accompanying audit. ## 4. Opposite-root FIRST on the physical transported clock Set r=Q^(-1). Its original finite Euler function is P_r; this is not a replacement invariant. It is an explicit auxiliary factor inside the following identity for the ORIGINAL P_Q crossing. Let E_Q(Z_R) denote the actual spectral projector at Z_R=Q, transported by the SAME A in (4). Put c_3=C(1-E_Q(Z_R)), a_3=c_3(1-rZ_R)=C(1-rZ_R)=C^(-1)nu C. (12) Then c_3Z_R=r^(-1)Z_Rc_3 and c_3^N=a_3^N=0. The missing arrow is at Z_R=Q, not Z_R=1. The inverse-root clock index is j_new=-j modulo N, so that this is precisely its top index d. Keep the actual negative-orientation full function and scalar phi_-=conjugate(phi_+), phi_+=sqrt(N)exp{i*pi[1/4-(N+N^(-1))/12]}, F_3=[marked Psi_-(r Z_R)]^(-1). In the transported clock frame its value at old index j is F_3(j)=phi_-^(-1)(r;r)_((-j) mod N). (13) The logarithmic lift is -2pi*i*(j_new+1)/N. In particular the cut index j_new=d uses the regular negative TOP value -2pi*i, not the bottom zero. Consecutive factorial ratios prove F_3 c_3 F_3^(-1)=a_3. All these factors can be constructed without knowing A: use the explicit rational formulas (1), (4) for C,Z_R and the root-clock projectors E_(Q^j)(Z_R)=N^(-1)sum_k Q^(-jk)Z_R^k. Equations (3)--(4) prove which ORIGINAL transported clock mark those explicit factors carry; they do not define a new factor by an unknown conjugated crossing. Define P_3=P_r(c_3), H_3=P_3^(-1)Z_RP_3, F_H3=P_3^(-1)F_3P_3, y_3=-r c_3H_3, Y_3=P_r(y_3). The independently proved FIRST identity now applies on these physical heads. In inverse-word form it is F_H3^(-1)P_3^(-1) =P_3^(-1)F_H3^(-1)Y_3. (14) The exact developed FIRST arguments before word inversion are c_3, Z_R, y_3, J_3, a_3, with J_3=Y_3^(-1)H_3Y_3=(1-a_3)^(-1)Z_R. Their classical values are precisely C,Z_R,y,H,nu of (10). At finite N one keeps J_3, a_3, their marks and their displayed q-shifts; one does not replace them by H and nu as exact matrices. Here is the exact common-port convention, including a common-output realization if preferred. For a product acting right to left, develop an argument at the right/input port by conjugating it by the inverse of all factors to its right. The left word of (14) then develops H_3 to P_3H_3P_3^(-1)=Z_R and leaves c_3 unchanged. The right word develops its three arguments to Y_3^(-1)F_H3 c_3 F_H3^(-1)Y_3=a_3, Y_3^(-1)H_3Y_3=J_3, y_3. Thus this is the forward FIRST common-left/output table read in reverse at the inverse word's right/input port. It is not the unconjugated output table of the raw inverse word. To realize the SAME table in a common-left/output frame, put W_3=P_3F_H3=F_3P_3, hat(O)=W_3 O W_3^(-1). Conjugate EACH individual factor and its current in (14) by W_3. Its total product remains exactly the original inverse word, because W_3 commutes with W_3^(-1). The framed equality is hat(F_H3^(-1)) hat(P_3^(-1)) =hat(P_3^(-1)) hat(F_H3^(-1)) hat(Y_3). (14a) The developed arguments at its common-left/output port are (Z_R,c_3) on the left and (a_3,J_3,y_3) on the right, exactly. For example hat(H_3)=Z_R, hat(c_3)=a_3, and developing the second left argument gives c_3. All W_3/W_3^(-1) face frames in (14a) are retained; no claim of a tame size or trivial action is made. There are two orientation changes in (14): the Euler/full-Psi root is r=Q^(-1), and the FIRST word is inverted and read with its original input/output face types reversed. Relative to the original h=2pi*i/N these changes cancel. Its signed face boundary is therefore the specified negative THIRD boundary (10), with the above even flag order. All inverse-word interface marks are transported from (13), not reselected independently. ## 5. Exact reflection embeds the entire word in the ORIGINAL R Set B_3=P_r(a_3). Nilpotent factorial reflection gives exactly P_r(t)=P_Q(Qt)^(-1)=(1-t)P_Q(t)^(-1) for every t^N=0. Indeed (r;r)_h=(-1)^h Q^(-h(h+1)/2)(Q;Q)_h, so the P_r coefficient is Q^h/(Q;Q)_h, the inverse Euler coefficient of Qt. Apply this to (12): B_3=C^(-1)(1-nu)P_Q(nu)^(-1)C, A=P_+ C B_3^(-1) C^(-1)(1-nu). (15) Here P_Q(nu)=P_+^(-1)MP_+, proving the second equality. The factor 1-nu is a compulsory original source adapter; it is not set to one. Also B_3=F_3P_3F_3^(-1)=P_3F_H3F_3^(-1). Substitution of (14) into (15) gives the COMPLETE physical THIRD refactorization R_0=D P_+ C F_3 [F_H3^(-1)P_3^(-1)] C^(-1)(1-nu) =D P_+ C F_3 [P_3^(-1)F_H3^(-1)Y_3] C^(-1)(1-nu). (16) Either bracket in (16) may equivalently be written with its fully framed factors from (14a); its product is identical. That is the common-output face version whose literal determinants were used above. There is no unstated conjugation of a single face alone. All factors are explicit original physical matrices or their specified finite Euler/full-Psi frames. The inverse actual checked crossing is obtained by inverting the ENTIRE displayed word, with the same external scalar and closing conventions. There is no auxiliary index left to suppress. ## 6. The complete source and every cut remain Keep the original p=N sum_j x^(j-d)|j,d-j> and full marker m|a,b>=x^b/N^2. In the local identity (14), its literal input and output from (16) are psi_3=C^(-1)(1-nu)p, ell_3=m flip D P_+ C F_3. (17) The ENTIRE input adapter has the useful exact cancellation C^(-1)(1-nu)=R (TX)^(-1) Z_R. (17a) Indeed C^(-1)=X_R^(-1)H=R(TX)^(-1)H and H(1-nu)=Z_R. Thus the original incoming source requires no inverse of H or R. On unit wrap marks, X,T,Z are unitary, so ||R||<=3 and ||Z_R||<=1+||R||||1-Z||<=7.
