Consequently the adapter in (17a) has operator norm at most 21, uniformly in N. In the original Euclidean head metric this gives ||psi_3||<=21 N^(3/2). This is a bound on the actual input adapter, not on its inverse, the outgoing factorial frame, or the entire geometric cycle comparison. Thus both sides have exactly the original normalized one-crossing source value 1. With the unstripped original crossing that value has the same original kappa line. In a longer tangle, replace p and m by its actual exteriors in (17); equality holds before any contraction. The scalar phi_- in F_3 and F_H3 is retained and cancels in the full word because those precise interfaces have opposite powers. No selected scalar is divided out. The full transported strict cut is c_3^h=C^h[1-sum_(j=1)^h E_(Q^j)(Z_R)], 0<=h<N. (18) This follows by following C's decreasing old clock indices: its deleted input is j=1, and the forbidden inputs for h arrows are exactly j=1,...,h. It includes the wrapped index-zero path and every parity. Neither the sum nor the individual projectors is deleted on source grounds. Every actual Ward current is transported by applying its ordinary typed commutator product rule to the full equality (16). Each nilpotent Euler factor in (16) has the exact original full-Psi circle-minus-radial moment realization, using the appropriate root orientation. The new clock frame is explicitly (13) transported by A and P_3. Thus all corresponding radial relative-source terms and factorial frame factors stay in the identity. This statement uses the finite matrix theorem and the already proved moment theorem; it does not replace a generalized coefficient functional by bare evaluation of Psi. The theorem is at the physical complete root for all N and all typed wrap marks mu. An off-root Hopf identity or a complete meridian-normal version of the flag table is not asserted here. ## 7. Why the earlier auxiliary port did not supply this table In [the auxiliary construction](third_region_quantum_face_extension.md), C_0=C_B|0> and rho=<0|P_0 satisfy exactly (B_aux-1)C_0=0, rho(H_0-1)=0, <0|W=<0|. Consequently its auxiliary pentagon has a face forced to one on every regular fully contracted stationary configuration. Simultaneous controlled or Gaussian similarities only transport these eigenconstraints. They do not give the generic regular THIRD configuration by multiplying its differently typed ports. That construction remains a valid exact R formula. Equations (4), (12)--(17) instead realize THIRD on the physical coupled flags and keep its true polarization and full source. ## 8. Audit and remaining geometric obligation Run python3 experiments/audit_literal_third_full_phi_certificate.py The [audit](../experiments/audit_literal_third_full_phi_certificate.py) checks all five symbolic actual face determinants, 27 level/wrap families through N=10, both inverse actual flag transports, the coupled physical coordinates, opposite-root marking, all powers of the strict cut, the inverse-word common-port developments and all individual W_3 frames, exact reflection, the full original positive and negative crossing, and the original one-crossing source. The all-level proofs above do not depend on that finite coverage. This does not make the full operator word a product of already positive charged tetrahedral kernels. Its factorial and source adapters have to be transported through the appropriate full-Phi Fourier/quad maps with their relative cycles. The three literal certificates fix the actual face/source algebra to which those maps must apply. They do not prove that the original global cycle selects the geometric reference class or its volume rate.

title: Literature definition, independent audit, and equivalence question
text: # Literature definition, independent audit, and equivalence question Current scope, 25 October 2026: The target is Kashaev's original invariant. The AK definitions audited below are comparison objects. The subsequent [direct crossing audit](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md) and [ADO pointing calculation](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) now specify the original enhanced state and its literature all-level annihilator ideal, with independent matrix, pairing and normalization proofs. No AJ or all-level holonomicity theorem is assumed merely from accepting that ideal's definition. * Use a quantum object defined in the existing literature, with its prescribed state, operator conventions, normalization and parameter regime. * Do not assume the correctness of the published proofs. Reconstruct and check the identities and analytic arguments actually needed. * Preserve the earlier custom constructions as comparison candidates. They become results about the chosen literature object only after an equivalence has been established; a common classical A-curve or volume rate is insufficient. * Retain peripheral variables and allowed boundary factors before specializing to the complete ideal point. A numerical multiplier in a specialized 2–3 comparison is not by itself an obstruction to the appropriately normalized move identity. ## 1. An existing definition to audit Andersen–Malusa, *A Geometric Quantisation view on the AJ-conjecture for the Teichmueller TQFT*, arXiv:1711.11522v3 (30 April 2024), Section 5, Definition 5, printed page 21: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.11522v3 The object is the specified Andersen–Kashaev state J^(b,N)_(M,K), and its annihilating left ideal in the q-difference algebra. The paper singles out a primitive operator of minimal shift degree when the relevant ideal is nonzero. The state and its quantum operators are described in Sections 2.1–2.3 and 5. This is not an instruction to choose a convenient solution of a naively ordered classical A-polynomial. For general knots the same source treats existence/nontriviality and the classical-symbol identification as conjectural. Those are proof obligations here, not consequences of accepting the definition. The purported statements for 4_1 and 5_2 likewise remain to be independently checked. The source and original PDF for the underlying construction are Andersen–Kashaev, *A TQFT from quantum Teichmueller theory*: https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.6295 . Fix a source version before transferring formulas. ## 2. Necessary checks 1. Write the exact published state integral, quantum dilogarithm, Gaussian, Haar/spectral measure, contour and peripheral multiplication/shift operators. 2. Verify the local functional equations and quantum commutators directly. 3. Verify noncommutative elimination using explicit certificates. 4. Check the passage from integrand equations to state equations: contour changes, residues, endpoint terms and parameter domains must be accounted for. 5. Establish nonzero state, minimality and the classical limit with all removable or nonremovable factors recorded. 6. For volume, establish the appropriate asymptotic for that exact normalized state. Existing claims about contour deformation, saddle selection and uniform error estimates are not assumed. The earlier computations in `quantum_a_volume.md` do not discharge these checks for the literature state. ## 3. How to test equivalence with the custom candidate Match variables first: in the classical symbol the literature Q corresponds to m^2, so its q-commutation parameter must be compared with the square of the parameter for a shift acting on m itself. Include orientations, Fourier or Gaussian conjugations and peripheral/framing changes explicitly. Then compare operators at generic q and generic peripheral variables, allowing the units or boundary factors permitted in the stated construction. For a second-order equation with coefficients a_0(X),a_1(X),a_2(X), EX=qXE, I(X)=a_0(qX)a_2(X)/(a_1(qX)a_1(X)) is invariant under multiplying the equation by a scalar function and under a scalar gauge f(X)=g(X)u(X). It is consequently a useful test for the simplest possible equivalence, including right multiplication by scalar units. It does not test equivalence by a general matrix gauge or change of polarization. Finally relate the states themselves. An operator equivalence alone does not identify a selected integration cycle, a particular solution, or an exponentially significant normalization. ## 4. Peripheral factors and the factor-eight observation The local angle-factorial test evaluated two specialized amplitudes, 1/27 and 1/216 at N=6. Its ratio 8 establishes only failure of strict equality of those bare amplitudes. A factor such as (1+M^a) is a unit near M=1 and specializes to 2. Products of such factors can produce 8. This illustrates why the numerical observation cannot decide the correct move law; it does not identify its missing factor. For each move, the calculation should retain its boundary variables and determine whether the multiplier is an allowed unit, a change of boundary trivialization, a projective scalar, a quantum-dilogarithmic factor, or a genuine anomaly. Its behavior under composition of moves must then be checked. Factors vanishing at the ideal point require separate limit analysis. Generic localization permits division by them, while the analytic germ at M=1 may not. That distinction is already visible in right factors involving Q-1 in the literature operator comparison. ## 5. Current proof status The literature definitions are starting data. No equivalence between the custom cone-normalized states and the literature state is established. No failure of topological invariance modulo allowed boundary factors has been proved by the factor-eight test. Neither publication nor matching numerical volume asymptotics is being used as a substitute for an audited proof. An initial exact algebraic check is reproducible with `python3 experiments/compare_literature_quantum_a.py`. It compares the custom figure-eight operator with the explicit candidate q P'_q obtained from equation (13) of arXiv v3. Their scalar-gauge invariants differ for generic q, although their classical invariants agree. Thus a mere scalar normalization in the same peripheral coordinates cannot identify these two operators. This does not exclude a more general intertwiner or change of polarization, and it does not assume that the candidate is the minimal annihilator of the literature state. The same calculation finds a discrepancy among the formulas **as printed in arXiv v3**: right-multiplying q P'_q by Q-1 agrees with equation (5) in the constant and quadratic shift coefficients, but its linear shift coefficient has an additional factor qQ-1. Inserting that factor into the printed equation (5) makes the asserted right-factor identity exact. This was checked against the original v3 TeX source, not inferred from PDF text extraction. The classical prefactor stated in Theorem 17 also needs reconciliation with the explicit specialization in the proof of Theorem 19. These may be typographical errors; they do not by themselves disprove the underlying construction. The journal version and any corrections must be checked before attributing the discrepancies to the final published article. ## 6. Subsequent independent proofs and exact comparisons The full derivations are in `literature_state_volume.md` and `custom_literature_equivalence.md`. 1. The Faddeev defining integral gives a uniform *complex* O(b^2) logarithmic remainder on every smaller strip |Im z|<=pi-delta, for all Re z. The proof explicitly handles the upper indentation and normalization constant. 2. On a contour through the regular ideal saddle, the exact literature figure-eight state satisfies J_b(0)=3^(-1/4) exp(-Vol(4_1)/(2 pi b^2))(1+o(1)). The contour has a fixed strip gap; the manuscript's compact-fold pole accumulation is not being passed through. 3. The v3 Ore certificate for equation (13) is exactly correct. It was expanded in the noncommutative four-generator algebra, separately from the printed equation (5) discrepancy above. The integrand equations were recovered from the defining integral, and the finite contour shifts justified near the semiclassical parameter. A local uniform saddle expansion and the nonsquare classical discriminant rule out a rational first-order annihilator. Thus the explicit second-order operator is minimal for this level-one state on its specified analytic branch. No general-level-N theorem is inferred. 4. The same remainder estimate and a negative definite real Hessian prove a volume law for the published FAMED state integral (4.5), given positive complete shapes and the finite face, edge and peripheral matrix certificates. This does not prove a quantum annihilator exists for every member of that class, nor verify blanket knot-family or census membership claims. 5. Our compact Psi_q is an exact factor of Phi_b after its second, dual compact product is included. Functional equations and the left-end normalization independently prove this equality in the convergent complex-b regime. 6. The two figure-eight companion systems are inequivalent even under rational two-by-two gauges in the same peripheral coordinates. The proof uses finite pole propagation and formal degrees at zero and infinity; a scalar invariant alone would not suffice. Changes of polarization and nonrational transforms remain separate questions. The exact generic-q factors are retained throughout. In particular the minimal operator's classical specialization contains (Q^2-1) times the geometric quadratic; those factors cannot be canceled at Q=1 without a limit analysis. The bare factor-eight observation about the different positive factorial model continues to have only the limited interpretation in Section 4 above. There is a further scalar-normalization discrepancy to reconcile in the displayed change of variables preceding equation (4.5) of the FAMED preprint: the stated Jacobian is p_1 but the displayed fiber prefactor is p_1 rather than 1/p_1. The broad volume proof explicitly fixes the printed integral; the difference is a recorded nonzero constant, not an assumed exact equality of differently normalized states. This discrepancy was also checked in the original v2 TeX source, lines 3277–3292. The N=1 dilogarithm convention was separately checked from the finite-product definition (122) of Andersen–Kashaev, arXiv:1409.1208. ## 7. General existence and the explicit twist families `general_annihilator_and_volume.md` now proves a nonzero annihilator exists for the rescaled geometric FAMED integrals in the Andersen–Malusà b-shift algebra. Exact finite products give a common denominator with linear degree growth. A dimension count eliminates the internal multiplication variables. If the resulting operator vanishes when the internal shifts are set to 1, exponential moments extract its first nonzero Taylor coefficient. A finite restriction-of-scalars argument returns to the prescribed peripheral field. The operator of least degree then exists by skew-polynomial division. The same exact state has a locally uniform, nonzero geometric saddle asymptotic. Consequently the classical symbol contains the geometric peripheral component with explicitly recorded PSL/SL lift, inverse and factor-of-two conventions. No claim that all other classical components have been removed is made. There are two finite-b conventions that must not be identified: the natural Andersen–Malusà algebra uses q_b=exp(2pi i b^2) and a spectral shift -i b; FAMED Section 4.4 uses q_F=exp(4pi i hbar) and scaled shift +4pi i hbar. The existence theorem here is for the former action on the rescaled published integral. It does not establish the latter's conditional AJ hypothesis. Moreover the source's displayed WKB substitution for its positive shift gives exp(-H_l) from its stated potential derivative, so its inverse-longitude convention requires reconciliation before use. For 4_1 the exact conversion of the two literature state normalizations is J_F(hbar,2pi sqrt(hbar)t) = zeta_b/(2pi sqrt(hbar)) exp(pi(b+b^(-1))t) J_AM,b(t). This boundary factor changes the classical longitude root's sign. It is retained at generic peripheral value, and only then evaluated at t=0. The factor is exponentially significant at a fixed scaled boundary value. `twist_family_audit.md` reconstructs the two explicit infinite face families, their face Gaussian, the edge/face matrix identity, and positive complete geometric angle maxima by formulas valid for every fixed twist parameter. It includes a multiplier/horosphere proof that an interior angle maximum produces a complete metric. The exact finite checks rebuild edge incidences and the matrices from the face pairings for p=0,...,8 in both parities. They support the all-p formulas; they are not used as a substitute for them. A further generic-boundary discrepancy was found in arXiv:1903.09480v5: the even-family theorem prints x(x-y_U-y_W), while the derivation at TeX lines 8791–8802 gives x(y_U-y_W-x). The direct face-matrix substitution agrees with the latter. Both expressions agree at x=0. The exact state fixed for this audit is the later FAMED integral, and the final journal version of the older twist paper has not been checked for the discrepancy. The subsequent `twist_topology_and_peripherals.md` reconstructs the knot-diagram identification and independently identifies the peripheral curves by constant-size normal-curve certificates. Its meridian separates the marked-edge germs before drilling; its primitive longitude is an integral boundary in the complement, and its angular branch correction is zero. Exact diagnostics and optional Regina recognition check eighteen examples against those uniform formulas. Global exact state transformations and the extension to every alternating knot remain unfinished. The active goal is not marked complete on the basis of the state-integral criterion or the twist-family theorem for specified literature realizations. ## 8. Independent positive local move and a fiber-normalization equivalence `faddeev_pentagon_audit.md` derives the Faddeev Fourier formula from both shift equations, fixes its constant using Fourier inversion and a Fresnel asymptotic, and obtains the generic scalar Ramanujan integral from two shift identities and its residue at zero. Pole cancellation in the contour shifts is explicit. These give the bounded operator pentagon by an integrable spectral regularization. For the charged operators defined in AK (18), the resulting exact identity is T_12(a_4,c_4)T_13(a_2,c_2)T_23(a_0,c_0) =exp(pi i c_b^2 P/3)T_23(a_1,c_1)T_12(a_3,c_3), P=2(c_0+a_2+c_4)-1/2, under the full positive charge relations recorded in that note. It holds with all face boundary variables unspecialized. The charged proof is a contour translation of the scalar uncharged kernel identity; it does not treat the separately unbounded exponential charge factors as bounded. The phase and all boundary-linear terms are also checked symbolically. The same note identifies the exact factor J_coarea=J_printed/p_1^2 for the FAMED fiber Jacobian convention. It is a nonzero constant normalization, so these two states have the same annihilator and volume rate. This does not silently replace the printed state: its factor is recorded throughout. The local identity can be contracted with a convergent exterior kernel or Schwartz boundary states. An explicit invertible face matrix also makes the full positive tensor contraction absolutely convergent; this supplies the gluing justification for embedded replacements of the audited operator pentagon pattern when both full face matrices are invertible. General gluing, movement outside the positive chamber, the level/framing convention, and the exact polarized fiber-state covariance still need their own checks. No generic multiplier for the different positive factorial comparison model is inferred from it. ## 9. Exact peripheral phase and state recovery `peripheral_phase_and_state.md` upgrades the magnitude relationship to the complex identity Z_AK(X,alpha)=sigma_X exp(pi i N/12+i K_X(alpha)/hbar) integral_(R+i mu) (J_printed(hbar,x)/p_1^2) exp(lambda x/(4pi hbar)) dx, sigma_X=sign(det(script-A)p_1). It derives K_X from the charged kernel and defining inversion identity, including the imaginary lift in the boundary coordinate. Choosing the published AK level ell=-4K_X/pi removes exactly that angle phase. The fiber state is then uniquely recovered by analytic continuation and Fourier–Laplace injectivity with the proved exponential tail bounds. On balanced angles K_X is affine apart from the universal term -lambda mu/(8pi). Compatible positive moves cancel this quadratic term; the remaining scalar transform law is eta exp(i(d_0+d_1 lambda)/hbar). A zero-slope certificate identifies the same state up to its recorded scalar. A nonzero slope requires an explicit meridian translation and its contour check. The slope is not silently set to zero. The generic mixed-sign phase identity is symbolic. Eighteen twist angle spaces were checked in their entirety, and pointwise quantum checks using the independently derived real-b remainder agree within 9e-15. The raw phase varies even at fixed peripheral angles in all eighteen examples. Actual move sequences, other vertex-order patterns, and the all-alternating geometric extension remain unfinished. ## 10. A calibrated connecting move for the figure-eight state `tetrahedral_symmetry_and_figure_eight.md` derives all three adjacent vertex transposition identities from the audited Fourier formula. The published Gaussian triangle kernels supply an exact S_3 action: their cyclic product has cube scalar exp(3pi i/12-pi i/4)=1. Gaussian regularization justifies their cancellation in the proper contractions used here. The note reconstructs the actual 3–2 bipyramid in the p=0 even twist triangulation. Its canonical signs are all negative, so the adjoint pentagon is required. It transports the full positive angle space and the preferred peripheral rows, which reverse both meridian and longitude. The affine phase certificate has slope zero and constant 11pi/12. An explicit orientation-preserving automorphism of the resulting two-tetrahedron triangulation also reverses both peripheral curves and has zero phase difference. Transform uniqueness proves its selected state is even. Thus, for the stated face orders and printed normalizations, J_3(hbar,x)=-exp[-pi i/12+11pi i/(12hbar)]J_2(hbar,x). The corresponding minimal order-two operator is exactly the same; its reflection multiplier is only -q^(-6)Q^(-6), and no nonmonomial peripheral factor has been removed. The exact face, angle, phase, automorphism and operator checks are reproducible. Independent two-dimensional versus one-dimensional integration agrees within 1.2e-12 in four checked cases. General connecting sequences and the all-alternating extension remain open. The further argument in Section 6.1 of `peripheral_phase_and_state.md` removes the affine phase slope for any certified positive path with compatible complete geometric endpoints. At lambda=0 the full saddle has x(y*)=0, so hbar times the logarithmic longitude derivative of its normalized transform tends to zero. Comparing the exact affine transform laws forces d_1=0. Consequently selected-state annihilator ideals and volume limits are invariant along these certified proper positive paths; no meridian translation is discarded by convention. Path existence beyond the audited components and the all-alternating geometric certificates are still required. ## 11. An independent edge theorem and a certified non-twist example `face_edge_stokes_identity.md` proves the edge rows A_ed=B_ed G for any globally branched oriented face pairing with invertible script-A. The proof constructs a face assignment from arbitrary edge values and cancels an oriented face sum. It also proves rank B_ed=N-1 for one-cusped triangulations. This sharpens the earlier finite-certificate treatment; it neither assumes nor proves that the preferred-longitude row follows automatically. The folded-layer construction in the appendix of Guéritaud--Futer, [arXiv:math/0406242](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0406242), gives explicit face permutations from an R/L word. Its combinatorics have been reconstructed in `experiments/layered_two_bridge.py`. The general geometricity proof in that paper has not been adopted as an unaudited hypothesis. For the particular word RLRL, `six_three_and_two_bridge_audit.md` supplies an independent rational Rouché certificate, polynomial gluing identities, rational logarithmic-argument bounds, and a preferred-longitude cellular boundary certificate. These prove positive complete geometric and peripheral data for the specified 6_3 state and put it under our analytic volume and annihilator theorems. Optional combinatorial isomorphism checks calibrate the standard knot marking; they are kept separate from the exact geometric and preferred-longitude calculations. No claim that all canonical two-bridge triangulations are proper is used: exhaustive branching searches find singular face matrices for every compatible ordering of several such triangulations, beginning with 6_2. ## 12. Evaluating singular face contractions before extracting the state `singular_faces_and_six_two.md` evaluates the same charged kernels using independent Fourier integration. It assumes rank D=N and a surjective kernel-to-frequency matrix C; neither assumption is replaced by a presumed TQFT existence theorem. The resulting normalization is a product of three explicit Jacobians, and the residual integral is absolutely convergent. The Stokes identity extends to its allowed shape subspace. Complete horosphere decorations then identify the geometric critical point and give a volume theorem for the full reduced tensor under the displayed hypotheses. For 6_2 a separate exact certificate produces a three-variable selected meridian fiber, the complete positive algebraic shapes and logarithmic branches, the preferred-longitude cellular relation, and its entire angle-dependent tensor-to-fiber phase. Its existence and volume law follow without inverting the singular face matrix. The boundary factorization is the type used in AK v2 Conjecture 1(1); it is not the undefined specialization of the proper FAMED formula. Minimal annihilator existence uses the same Andersen--Malusà convention as before. The full intrinsic AK conjecture, including arbitrary triangulation identifications and H-triangulation limits, has not been proved by this calculation. ## 13. The Fourier rank conditions are automatic for branched knot exteriors `automatic_face_regularity.md` identifies the exact local linear obstruction with a cellular ideal edge cocycle. It then proves that the obstruction vanishes from H^1(M,boundary M)=0 for a knot exterior, using the cohomology sequence and the boundary meridian generator. This proves rank D=N and surjectivity of C uniformly, independently of the convergence assertion in AK's Theorem 7. The completed independent full-tensor volume theorem now applies to every globally branched complete positive geometric ideal triangulation of a knot exterior in S^3. The general selected boundary state and triangulation identifications remain separate obligations. ## 14. Preferred-longitude cochains and the meridian shear Two further primary sources were located and read in this continuation: * Kambampati, [arXiv:2610.04103v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04103v1), submitted 2 October 2026, supplies a cochain construction for the preferred longitude, including singular face matrices. * Wong, [arXiv:2512.23198v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23198v1), submitted 29 December 2025, defines generalized FAMED and additional longitude--meridian conditions. Its analytic theorems are not premises of the new positive-geometry argument. `preferred_longitude_cochains.md` reconstructs the first source's local face potentials, derives its auxiliary potentials from endpoint sums, and proves closure and peripheral period matching on the dual spine. The independent local audit checks 60 potential/arc identities. A separate integer endpoint formula, checked in all 1152 ordered arc-pair cases, proves the peripheral symplectic normalization with the full factor two. The resulting rank and preferred-longitude relations are proved using these cancellations and knot-exterior cohomology, rather than adopted from the source's theorem. `general_boundary_state_and_framing.md` then proves the selected-state volume law whenever the longitude increases the B rank. It permits a rational meridian shear, records its exact Gaussian correction and all scalar phases, and proves volume preservation by a positive-Phi saddle argument. Its exact operator action is Q -> q^beta Q E^(2beta), E -> E, with no specialization. The additional zero-shear expectation in Wong's Definition 1.5 is not used. The other affine-plane case, flat tetrahedra, arbitrary triangulation identifications and H-triangulation limits remain outside that theorem. ## 15. Inverse Fourier recovery when longitude moves the shape plane `fourier_boundary_state.md` now treats that other boundary rank, using the same charged tensor and the same AK level definition. Its Fourier and Gaussian operators are those in the A=R specialization of Section 6 of Andersen--Kashaev, [arXiv:1409.1208v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.1208v1). The particular inverse transform, measure and angle-dependent quadratic level are specified and independently derived. No new tetrahedral function or unselected recurrence solution is substituted. The inverse Fourier integral is absolutely convergent when the longitude moves the shape plane. Its extra critical equation is the meridian equation; its real Hessian is negative definite at the complete geometric point. The full small-peripheral factorization includes an explicit real level polynomial. In the ordinary-fiber case it recovers the preceding fiber/Gaussian state exactly. Thus the combined volume theorem and the independent annihilator argument apply to every globally branched complete positive geometric ideal knot triangulation. Neither extra condition (2) nor the zero-shear expectation in Wong's Definition 1.5 is needed for this tensor-derived realization. Literal equality to a different printed complex-state formula still requires matching its specified normalization. An exact six-tetrahedron 5_2 certificate realizes the additional rank case. Its algebraic shapes, logarithmic branches, preferred-longitude cellular relation and Fourier constants are independent checks. Optional Regina calibration verifies the three legal combinatorial 2--3 moves and the initial marked meridian; this does not assume a quantum state identity along them. General global triangulation identification, flat tetrahedra, all-alternating geometric realizations and H-triangulation limits remain open. This does not claim the full intrinsic AK conjecture. ## 16. Structural period torsors instead of additional knot cases The current comparison is `structural_literature_delta.md`. It explicitly marks standard local definitions, independent reconstructions and the missing global assertion. In particular the cyclic dilogarithm and its 6j interpretation are existing constructions; renaming them is not a new proof of the conjecture. `heisenberg_period_torsor.md` derives the cyclic norm equation and its determinant root as a finite Heisenberg torsor. It evaluates every finite face contraction by character orthogonality, including composite levels at which the support is not a free module. Its coisotropic quotient constructs a boundary torsor on each nondegenerate gluing chart. `pointed_steinberg_recoupling.md` identifies the local Faddeev difference module with the pointed Steinberg vacuum at rational b^2. It derives two generic quantum left-ideal identities, an explicit q-factorial kernel and its determinant unit, and proves the basis-free pentagon by coassociativity. No local integral identity is needed for that algebraic coherence theorem. Published matrix conventions and their global periods still have to be matched. `rational_quantum_dilogarithm_torsor.md` independently reconstructs the existing exact local rational-parameter formula, retaining its Heisenberg period and branches. Finally `bloch_lift_and_boundary_torsor.md` proves the rational boundary wedge identity and records the Bloch period whose regulator is the volume exactly. The target is a global pointed period carrying that lift and its regulator comparison. Neither Hilbert 90 for an unpointed module nor fixed-level rigidity alone supplies the remaining comparison across quantum levels. The later `pointed_period_descent.md` proves the explicit Racah closure and its signed shared-face normalization. `affine_frame_period_transport.md` and `projective_frame_period_torsor.md` give full projective-frame covariance of those local tensors on a compatible root cover, using explicit norm-one intertwiners and a determinant rigidity argument anchored at the identity frame. Their exact audits retain the scalar before normalization; the inversion diagnostic gives 1084/925. The unit vacuum is generally transported to a nonconstant vector, so local pointed recoupling does not by itself select the global literature period. The comparison also now includes Baseilhac--Benedetti's existing [matrix dilogarithms](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306283) and [analytic character-cover families](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.4261v3), Theorem 1.1 and Section 4.4. The latter already describes the classical period as a parallel Chern--Simons section. Their global theorems have not been adopted as premises; their published normalizations, weights and selected periods must be compared explicitly to ours. `equivariant_roots_and_phase_descent.md` now constructs the root multipliers around the knot from the peripheral root characters, normalizes triangle transports multiplicatively and treats the remaining scalar pentagon/equivariance discrepancy in relative group cohomology. The residual phase is evaluated on the relative fundamental class; it is not removed by field Hilbert 90. `boundary_regulator_period.md` independently derives the classical boundary connection and invariant norm, including the centering term for affine logarithmic edge constraints. It has the ordered-coordinate form of Baseilhac--Benedetti Section 4.4, equations (56)--(57), while recording that their longitude/meridian order is reversed from ours; exchanging that order dualizes the line. It also retains a possible flat unitary phase twist. Its exact regulator norm does not prove the remaining quantum comparison for the selected literature state. ## 17. The rational state as an exact relative period `rational_period_pushforward.md` gives the exact change of variables from the prescribed rational Gaussian--Faddeev class, with the source contour, Jacobian, quantum half phases and Q^n factors retained. It proves multidimensional cubical folding and a unimodular Koszul reduction, and derives the local gluing residue and its Hessian. Garoufalidis--Kashaev [1411.6062](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.6062), Section 2.1, is the one-dimensional methodological comparison; its global theorem is not used in higher dimensions. The source-pole criterion requires positive factors and polar coorientation; independent argument regulators can be used only with the corresponding holomorphic period germ. The Faddeev-pair diagnostic has H=-1 and a nonzero period, so open gluing solutions alone need not retain the selected period at a special parameter. Its generic moving gluing residue has a regular value at the removed polar divisor, verified independently using the defining Phi integrals. The cycle and that specialization data remain part of the comparison object.

title: Coverage check: normalized Racah factorials and hyperideal volume
text: # Coverage check: normalized Racah factorials and hyperideal volume 29 October 2026. Coverage only: primary-source definitions and theorem statements were checked. Their proofs are not inputs to our independent [factorial/normal theorem](actual_supported_racah_common_phase_and_normal_metric.md) or [local geometry theorem](actual_four_port_hyperideal_angle_volume.md). The local 6j–hyperideal-volume relationship is established literature; no novelty is claimed for recovering it here. Our convention is zeta=exp(pi i/N), [u]=(zeta^u-zeta^-u)/(zeta-zeta^-1), integer graph spins j<=floor((N-1)/2), and four face sums>=N-1. W_N is the positive magnitude of the regularized face-normalized scalar, with [N] removed before evaluation. Its exact Casimir angles are pi-(2j+1)pi/N. The uniform result includes closed-chamber sequences and O(log N) error for log W_N; its fixed normal jets are derivatives in zeta=q exp(t), not merely coefficients in a large-N expansion. ## Closest prior statements **Costantino (2007).** Definition3.2 gives the strict hyperbolic-type conditions 1<face sum<2 and triangle deficits between0 and1. Theorem3.9 gives a simple pole and the volume growth of the regularized [n]6j coefficient. His [u] uses q^(u/2), so q_paper=zeta^2 makes the quantum integers IDENTICAL to ours. The D-block volume is twice the tetrahedron volume, matching our pi/N normalization. This already covers the interior leading rate, without an odd-level restriction; parity/composite levels alone are not a new distinction. [Definitions3.1–3.2 and Theorem3.9](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0611399v4), [published article](https://doi.org/10.2140/gt.2007.11.1831). **Chen–Murakami (2023; preprint2017).** Theorems1–2 give the volume limit when a tetrahedron has an ideal or ultra-ideal vertex and a refined Gram-determinant prefactor for specified rational-angle sequences. They take odd r, xi_r=exp(2pi i/r), q=xi_r^2 and [u]=(q^(u/2)-q^(-u/2))/(q^(1/2)-q^(-1/2)). Their scaling is spin/r=(pi-angle)/(4pi). Substituting r=2N would match our quantum integer but violates their odd-r hypothesis. Their explicit halfshift is also prior art. [Theorems1–2 and definition in§2](https://arxiv.org/html/1706.04887v3), [journal DOI](https://doi.org/10.4310/JDG/1679503803). **Belletti–Detcherry–Kalfagianni–Yang.** Theorem1.2 gives the sharp, tuple-uniform v8+O(log r/r) upper capacity for r-admissible6j symbols; AppendixTheoremA.1 states the ideal/hyperideal volume limit under explicit face/deficit conditions. Their root is exp(2pi i/r), r odd, with doubled integer colors. This is substantial overlapping coverage, but a universal v8 bound is not the same statement as our label-dependent two-sided closed-chamber volume estimate. Setting r=2N introduces the [N] poles that their odd-root evaluation avoids. [Theorem1.2,§2 and AppendixA](https://arxiv.org/html/1807.03327v2). **Belletti–Yang (2025).** Theorem1.4 covers generalized hyperbolic volume growth under a negative diagonal-cofactor hypothesis. Theorem1.5 states a refined asymptotic along sequences with fixed sides of the color wall and a limiting tetrahedron without ideal vertices. The root remains exp(2pi i/r), r odd. Their§2 records the earlier ideal/hyperideal cases as well. These results preclude presenting the local volume mechanism as new. [Theorems1.4–1.5 and§2.2](https://londmathsoc.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1112/topo.70033), [arXiv version](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.13864). **Costantino–Murakami (2013).** Their graph face model and6j symbols use non-integral quantum-group representations and relate them to truncated-tetrahedron volume. This is relevant background, not an identified equality with our ordinary highest-weight Hermite source. [Publisher abstract and primary paper](https://ems.press/journals/qt/articles/4181). ## What this bounded check establishes The verified interior local volume claim is covered, most directly by Costantino after the explicit root substitution. Our exact all-chamber O(log N) estimate, scalar generic-normal/inverse-jet bounds and retained [2N] partner current have more specific technical statements; this bounded statement check neither proves they are absent elsewhere nor supports a novelty claim. A refined large-level asymptotic is not automatically a theorem about fixed-root generic-q jets, and a lowest-nonzero Laurent coefficient is not an arbitrary prescribed source normal. None of these local statements supplies our literal marked-source normalization, a positive completed recoupling Gram, or general graph sewing/peripheral constraints. Turaev–Viro conclusions are not silently substituted for original Kashaev invariants. The full-source problem remains separate.

title: Primary-source coverage of the root-normal planar-network period
text:
# Primary-source coverage of the root-normal planar-network period 29 October 2026. This is a definitions and theorem-scope comparison only. It neither imports nor endorses the papers' proofs. No identification of our period with a named invariant is asserted from terminology or matching growth. The source object being compared is the exact period in [the original NC Morse-graph reduction](actual_nc_morse_graph_first_normal_source_reduction.md): \[ q_*=e^{\pi i/N},\quad \zeta(t)=q_*e^t,\qquad Z_\Gamma={C_\Gamma\over
u_N} \left.(S_\Gamma\Xi_\Gamma)'ight|_{t=0}. \] Here \(\Xi_\Gamma\) uses the specified ordinary canonical ordered 3j tensors; \(S_\Gamma\) is the explicit product of source coefficients. The labels satisfy \(0\le j_e\le(N-1)/2\). When every vertex is supported, \(\sum_{e
i v}j_e\ge N-1\), the source factors are nonzero at the root and \(\Xi_\Gamma(0)=0\). Thus this case retains a **fixed first normal**, even when that normal itself vanishes. The distinct marked-white boundary case is retained in the cited source theorem. ## Closest root-normal definition **Costantino–Guéritaud–van der Veen, _On the volume conjecture for polyhedra_, arXiv:1403.2347, §1.2.2 (Evaluation), Conjecture 1.3 and Theorem 1.4.** Their \(\operatorname{ev}_N(f)\) extracts the first **nonzero** Laurent coefficient about \(A_*=e^{\pi i/(2N)}\); for their unitary spin network, whose square is meromorphic, they extend this by a square root, up to sign. The polyhedral volume statement uses \((\pi/N)\log|\operatorname{ev}_N \langle\Gamma,c_Nangle^U|\). Theorem 1.4 establishes the stated limit for the tetrahedron-derived local-move family shown there. The paper explicitly notes that this family excludes the cube; its general-graph statement remains a conjecture, with an additional conditional result. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1403.2347). This is the closest prescription found, but it does not fix the order to one. For a regular scalar \(f\) with a simple zero, our coordinate convention gives \(\partial_t f=(A_*/2)\operatorname{ev}_N(f)\), since \(\zeta=A^2\). At a higher-order zero our first normal is zero and their extracted coefficient is not. The canonical/unitary vertex factors, their root orders, and \(C_\Gamma S_\Gamma/
u_N\) have not been equated. The earlier **Costantino, _6j-symbols, hyperbolic structures and the Volume Conjecture_**, Geometry & Topology 11 (2007), 1831–1854, likewise explicitly studies the lowest Laurent term of quantum 6j-symbols, and gives results for fundamental shadow links in connected sums of \(S^2	imes S^1\). This is additional coverage of the leading-term prescription, not an identification of every fixed-first-normal planar network. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0611399). ## Named neighboring invariants | Primary definition | Exact relevant domain and comparison | |---|---| | **Yokota invariant**, in Belletti, _An upper bound conjecture for the Yokota invariant_, Definitions 2.2, 2.5, 2.7; Theorem 4.9 | Odd \(r\), \(q=e^{2\pi i/r}\), even integer colors at most \(r-2\), with triangle sum at most \(2r-4\). For a trivalent graph, \(Y_r=|\langle\Gamma,\mathrm{col}angle^U|^2\), with unitary theta evaluation 1; higher valence uses a weighted desingularization sum. No fixed root derivative occurs in this definition. Its upper-bound theorem covers graphs generated from the tetrahedron by the two specified vertex/face moves; the geometric supremum is the volume of the right-angled rectification. Under the naive identification \(r=N\), integer colors \(2j_e\) in our supported sector have sum at least \(2N-2\), outside that admissibility cutoff. Root, color and normalization changes therefore require an explicit comparison. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.01904). | | **Renormalized Reshetikhin–Turaev invariant**, Geer–Patureau-Mirand–Turaev, _Modified quantum dimensions and re-normalized link invariants_, §3, Theorem 3 | For closed colored ribbon graphs admitting an allowed simple cut color \(V\), the definition is \(F'(L)=d_J(V)\langle T_Vangle\), where \(d_J(V)=d_0S'(V,J)/S'(J,V)\) and \(d_0
e0\) is a chosen scale. This is a cut/modified-dimension prescription, including root-of-unity examples. The theorem is not a definition by a fixed first derivative of an arbitrary ordinary integral spin network. Equality would need the cut category, vertex lifts and scale matched. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0711.4229). | | **Logarithmic knot invariant**, Jun Murakami, _From colored Jones invariants to logarithmic invariants_, introductory Theorem 1 | At \(\xi=e^{\pi i/N}\), the named invariant obeys \(\gamma_s^{(N)}= rac{\xi}{2N}\partial_q[(q-q^{-1})(V_s+V_{2N-s})]_{q=\xi}\), \(1\le s\le N\). The paper identifies \(\gamma_N^{(N)}\) with its Kashaev normalization. This is a genuine root-derivative formula, but for knots and this prescribed combination of colored Jones polynomials, rather than our arbitrary canonical 3j network with its source factors. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1287). | | **Colored-Alexander/SL(2,C) graph invariant**, Costantino–Murakami, _On SL(2,C) quantum 6j-symbols and their relation to hyperbolic volume_ | The graph invariant uses nonintegral quantum-group representations and extends a colored Alexander invariant. Its tetrahedral volume results do not, by definition alone, cover the ordinary integral-label first-normal network above. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.4277). | The word “renormalized” is also used for a separate operation in Costantino, _Integrality of Kauffman brackets of trivalent graphs_: multiplying the generic bracket by explicit quantum-factorial factors to obtain an integral Laurent polynomial. That is not itself a root-normal prescription. [Primary journal definition](https://doi.org/10.4171/QT/49). ## Augmented graphs and right-angled link complements **Van der Veen, _The volume conjecture for augmented knotted trivalent graphs_, Definition 2, Definition 7 and Theorem 2.** For a fixed KTG move sequence \(\mathcal S\), the theorem supplies a threshold \(n(\mathcal S)\): each unzip must receive at least that many augmentation rings. At \(A=e^{\pi i/(2N)}\), the normalized invariant is \(\phi_N^{	heta}N^r\mathrm{sixj}_N^{t+1}\) for odd \(N\), and zero for even \(N\), where \(t\) counts triangle moves, \(r\) rings, and \(\mathrm{sixj}_N=\sum_{k=0}^{(N-1)/2}[{(N-1)/2\atop k}]^4\). Its outside has volume \((2t+2)v_8\). Normalization divides by the bracket of the \(s\)-fold unlink for **split components**, not all link components. Thus this is substantial augmented-graph/odd-\(N\) coverage, with an exact central quartic factor. It does not state coverage of every singly augmented NC Morse graph at both parities. A literal graph mapping and the prescribed normalization are still needed. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0805.0094). **Ibarra–McQuire–Purcell, _Augmented links, shadow links, and the TV volume conjecture: a geometric perspective_**, Theorems 2.12 and 4.15. The paper identifies octahedral fully augmented link complements with fundamental shadow-link complements, and states the Turaev–Viro volume limit for octahedral fully augmented links with no half-twists, at \(q=e^{2\pi i/r}\), odd \(r\). For \(c\) crossing circles the volume is \(2(c-1)v_8\). This covers a related geometric class and a different quantum invariant; it does not define our derivative period. [Primary journal paper](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2026/32-1p.pdf). ## Coverage conclusion Among the checked definitions, **leading Laurent evaluation**, **renormalized RT**, **logarithmic knot invariant**, and **Yokota invariant** are different prescriptions. None of the checked statements directly names or covers the entire weighted fixed-first-normal period above for every original NC Morse graph. This is not a claim that no such identification exists elsewhere. Any claimed coverage must specify the variable and normal coordinate, root order, canonical versus unitary vertex factors, color lattice, original single marked cut and framing factors, graph construction, and parity. No proof technique from these sources is used in this comparison.

title: An independent audit of literature state integrals and their volume limits
text: # An independent audit of literature state integrals and their volume limits Research note, 25 October 2026. No novelty claim is made. The definitions below come from the cited literature. The estimates, contour arguments and algebraic checks needed here are supplied separately; a published theorem is not being used as its own proof. There are three different conclusions: * For the figure-eight knot, the specified Andersen–Kashaev state has the volume limit, and the explicit second-order literature operator is its minimal annihilator over the rational q-difference field, with the qualifications about analytic continuation below. * A multivariate argument proves the volume limit for the explicit literature integral (4.5) of Ben Aribi–Wong whenever the stated finite matrix and positive geometric certificates are supplied. This includes the certified geometric FAMED class. The subsequent `general_annihilator_and_volume.md` proves existence of a minimal operator for these rescaled integrals in the Andersen–Malusà b-shift algebra, without an efficient coefficient formula. * Neither argument proves a theorem for every alternating knot, nor establishes all the global topological identities of Teichmüller TQFT. ## 1. Fixed sources and conventions 1. Andersen–Kashaev, *A TQFT from quantum Teichmüller theory*, [arXiv:1109.6295v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6295v2), Definition 15, equation (38), and Appendix A, equations (42)–(48). 2. Andersen–Malusà, *A Geometric Quantisation view on the AJ-conjecture for the Teichmüller TQFT*, [arXiv:1711.11522v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.11522v3), Definition 5 and Section 5.1. The algebraic certificate was checked against this version's TeX source. Corrections to other printed formulas in that version are discussed in `literature_definition_audit.md`. 3. Ben Aribi–Wong, *The Andersen–Kashaev volume conjecture for FAMED geometric triangulations*, [arXiv:2410.10776v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.10776v2), Definitions 1.1 and 2.7–2.10 and equation (4.5). Their asymptotic theorem is not assumed below. 4. Andersen–Kashaev, *Complex Quantum Chern–Simons*, [arXiv:1409.1208](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1409.1208), equation (122), fixes the finite-product convention for the level-N dilogarithm. Take b>0, q=exp(2 pi i b^2), and hbar = (b+b^(-1))^(-2) = b^2/(1+b^2)^2. The level-one boundary operators are Q f(x)=exp(-2 pi b x) f(x), E f(x)=f(x-i b), E Q=q Q E. Thus classical Q is m^2. All factors in Q are retained until after taking operator identities. The complete point is Q=1 in this convention; it is not an ideal point of the algebraic curve at infinity in the Culler–Shalen sense. ## 2. Quantum dilogarithm from its defining integral Start with the literature definition log Phi_b(Z) = integral_(R+i0) exp(-2 i Z w)/(4 sinh(b w) sinh(w/b) w) dw. (2.1) The contour passes above zero. It can equally be taken on a sufficiently small positive horizontal line. The exponential of this integral is holomorphic and nonzero in |Im Z|<(b+b^(-1))/2. This assertion follows from locally uniform convergence on a displaced contour, not from an asserted zero/pole formula. ### 2.1 A uniform complex remainder on an entire horizontal strip For every delta>0 there is C_delta such that, for 0<b<=1 and |Im z|<=pi-delta, log Phi_b(z/(2 pi b)) = Li_2(-exp z)/(2 pi i b^2) + R_b(z), sup_z |R_b(z)| <= C_delta b^2. (2.2) The logarithm is the one prescribed by (2.1), and the dilogarithm branch is analytic on |Im z|<pi and tends to zero as Re z tends to minus infinity. The supremum includes every real part of z. **Proof.** Substitute w=b t into (2.1). Subtract the leading kernel to obtain I(z)=1/4 integral_(R+i0) exp(-i z t/pi)/(t^2 sinh t) dt, K_b(t)=1/(4 t sinh t) [1/sinh(b^2 t)-1/(b^2 t)]. First evaluate I without assuming a quantum-dilogarithm asymptotic. Put J(z)=integral_(R+i0) exp(-i z t/pi)/sinh t dt. A rectangle translated upward by i pi gives (1+exp z) J(z)=-2 pi i exp z. Indeed the integrand changes by -exp z on translation, and the enclosed pole at i pi has residue -exp z. The vertical edges tend to zero for |Im z|<pi. Consequently I''(z)=-J(z)/(4 pi^2) = i exp z/(2 pi(1+exp z)). This is the second derivative of Li_2(-exp z)/(2 pi i). Both I and I' tend to zero as Re z tends to minus infinity: move the t contour to Im t=a, 0<a<pi, and use its exponentially decaying kernel. This fixes both integration constants. The finite-part integrals at zero are thereby fixed by the upper contour, rather than by an unspecified regularization. On the positive real axis K_b is real, and its odd continuation has residue c_b^rem=-b^2/24 at zero. Write c=c_b^rem in the following formulas; this is not the usual quantum-dilogarithm constant i(b+b^(-1))/2. Taylor expansion, uniformly for 0<b<=1, gives K_b(t)=c/t+O(b^2 t) (0<t<=1). For t>=1 use |1/sinh v-1/v|<=C v for v>0, obtaining |K_b(t)|<=C b^2 exp(-t). Define H_b(t)=K_b(t)-c exp(-t)/t. Then integral_0^infinity |H_b(t)| exp((1-delta/pi)t) dt <= C_delta b^2. The clockwise upper indentation at zero contributes -i pi c. Pairing the positive and negative halves of the real contour therefore yields the exact, ordinary convergent formula R_b(z)=-2 i [ integral_0^infinity H_b(t) sin(z t/pi) dt + c arctan(z/pi)] - i pi c. (2.3) Here integral exp(-t) sin(z t/pi)/t dt=arctan(z/pi), with the branch analytic on |Im z|<pi. This arctangent is bounded on each smaller closed strip, including as Re z tends to either infinity. The preceding weighted L1 bound controls the remaining integral uniformly on that strip. This proves (2.2). QED. Two normalization checks follow directly: R_b(0)=i pi b^2/24, R_b(z)+R_b(-z)=i pi b^2/12. (2.4) Together with Li_2(-e^z)+Li_2(-e^(-z))=-pi^2/6-z^2/2, they give the exact inversion identity, initially on the common strip, Phi_b(Z) Phi_b(-Z) = exp(i pi Z^2+i pi(b^2+b^(-2))/12). (2.5) The scalar in (2.5) has modulus one for b>0. It has not been silently discarded in an operator or state comparison. ### 2.2 Functional equation independently recovered Subtract the logarithms (2.1) at Z-i b/2 and Z+i b/2. The factor sinh(bw) cancels, leaving -1/2 integral_(R+i0) exp(-2 i b Z t)/(t sinh t) dt. Its derivative in Z is 2 pi b exp(2 pi b Z)/(1+exp(2 pi b Z)), by the same rectangle evaluation of J. Both it and log(1+exp(2 pi b Z)) vanish at the left end of the strip. Hence Phi_b(Z-i b/2) =(1+exp(2 pi b Z)) Phi_b(Z+i b/2). (2.6) The second functional equation follows by b<->b^(-1) in (2.1). Thus neither the functional equation nor the normalization in (2.2) is imported from an unchecked asymptotic theorem. ## 3. The exact literature figure-eight state Equation (38) of Andersen–Kashaev defines chi_b(x)=integral_(R-i0) Phi_b(x-y)/Phi_b(y) exp(2 pi i x(2y-x)) dy. (3.1) In the level-one convention used for the Andersen–Malusà boundary operators, J_b(x)=exp(4 pi i c_b x) chi_b(x), c_b=i(b+b^(-1))/2. (3.2) At x=0 the two states agree. Our volume theorem refers to this specified state, rather than an arbitrarily chosen solution of a difference equation. The level identification can be checked directly from the definition, not just its functional equations: the finite product (122) in *Complex Quantum Chern–Simons* has j=0,...,N-1 and argument x/sqrt(N)+(1-1/N)c_b-i b^(-1)j/N-i b{(j+n)/N}. At N=1 and n=0 it is the single factor Phi_b(x). The change n->-n in Andersen–Malusà is trivial at N=1, the Haar measure becomes ordinary Lebesgue measure, and the Gaussian is exp(pi i y^2). Their Gaussian ratio equals exp(2 pi i x(2y-x)). The algebra below also derives the operator directly from (3.1)–(3.2), so it does not need an assumed general-N identification or a general-N proof. **Theorem 3.1.** As b tends to zero through positive real values, J_b(0)=chi_b(0) = 3^(-1/4) exp(-Vol(S^3\4_1)/(2 pi b^2)) (1+o(1)). (3.3) In particular lim -2 pi b^2 log|J_b(0)| = lim -2 pi hbar log|J_b(0)| = Vol(S^3\4_1)=2 D(exp(i pi/3)). (3.4) Here D is the Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm. The geometric identification is the two-regular-ideal-tetrahedron decomposition of the complete figure-eight complement; its six tetrahedral edge angles around each edge sum to 2 pi. **Proof.** Set u=2 pi b y and eta=2 pi/3. Move the contour to u=t-i eta, -infinity<t<infinity. Both u and -u remain in the fixed strip |Im u|<pi, where the defining logarithms are holomorphic and nonzero. Equation (2.2) gives chi_b(0)=1/(2 pi b) integral_R exp(F(t)/(2 pi b^2)) exp(R_b(-u)-R_b(u)) dt, F(t)=[Li_2(-exp(-u))-Li_2(-exp u)]/i. (3.5) The last exponential is 1+O(b^2), uniformly for all t. The classical action S(u)=i F(t) satisfies S'(u)=log(1+exp(-u))+log(1+exp u), S'(-i eta)=0, S''(-i eta)=-i sqrt(3). On the stated line, the sum of logarithms is the continuous logarithm of 2+2 cosh(t-i eta). For t>0 that number has negative imaginary part, since its imaginary part is -sqrt(3) sinh t. For t<0 its imaginary part is positive. It follows that Re F has its unique global maximum at t=0, with F(0)=-2 D(exp(i pi/3))=-V, F''(0)=-sqrt(3). The real derivative tends to -eta at the positive end and +eta at the negative end. Thus Re F(t)<=-V-c|t| outside a compact interval. This gives absolute convergence and uniform control of the noncompact tails. For completeness, (R-i0) in (3.1) can first be any small negative horizontal displacement. Between two strictly negative scaled heights in (-pi,0), the same tail computation is uniform; the vertical ends of the deformation vanish. This proves contour independence and then its prescribed lower boundary value. No poles are crossed in moving to the chosen line. On a small interval around zero, expand the holomorphic F to second order. Its quadratic term is real and negative. Outside that interval the strict maximum and linear tails give an exponentially smaller contribution. Scaling t=b v and dominated convergence gives integral exp(F(t)/(2 pi b^2)) dt = exp(-V/(2 pi b^2)) (2 pi b)/3^(1/4) (1+o(1)). The uniform O(b^2) quantum amplitude cannot change or cancel this nonzero leading Gaussian term. Multiplying by 1/(2 pi b) proves (3.3). QED. This is a fixed ideal geometric saddle, separated from the quantum poles by a fixed gap in scaled coordinates. It is not the shrinking compact tetrahedron fold in Section 11 of the user's manuscript. No uniform passage through that fold has been used. ## 4. Exact quantum A-operator and minimality for the figure-eight state Let I(x,y) be the integrand of (3.1), without the outside factor in (3.2). Put Q_1=exp(-2 pi b x), Q_2=exp(-2 pi b y), and let E_1,E_2 shift x,y downward by i b. From (2.6) and the elementary Gaussian shift, E_1 I=q Q_1^2 Q_2^(-2)(1+q^(-1/2)Q_1^(-1)Q_2) I, E_2 I=Q_1^(-2)(1+q^(1/2)Q_1^(-1)Q_2)^(-1) (1+q^(-1/2)Q_2^(-1))^(-1) I. (4.1) This independently verifies the local input to the literature elimination. Clearing denominators in the proper order gives exactly g_1,g_2 in the v3 source. The explicit certificate q^(9/2) Q_1^2 P=q a_1 g_1-a_2 g_2 was independently expanded in the four-generator Ore algebra. The executable certificate, including every coefficient, is `experiments/audit_ore_certificate.py`; its residual is identically zero. This check alone does not justify integrating shifts. To do that, first take b sufficiently small, x in a small neighborhood of zero in the scaled variable X=2 pi b x, and the contour used in Section 3. All the finitely many shifts in P lie in a fixed smaller holomorphic strip. The action at X=0 has strictly decaying linear tails, and these tails persist uniformly for small complex X and small contour translations. Therefore vertical boundary terms vanish. Integrating E_2^j I gives the same integral as I; E_1 can be brought outside the integral. This proves P_q(E,Q,1) chi_b=0. The shift of the outside factor in (3.2) is q times that factor. Consequently the polynomial q P_q(q^(-1)E,Q,1) annihilates J_b. In normal order it is Ahat_q=a_2(Q) E^2+a_1(Q) E+a_0(Q), a_2=q^2 Q^2(q Q^2-1), a_1=-(q^2 Q^2-1) [q^4 Q^4-q^3 Q^3-q(q^2+1)Q^2-q Q+1], a_0=q^2 Q^2(q^3 Q^2-1). (4.2) The identity holds on the just-proved nonempty parameter domain. It extends by analytic continuation wherever the same literature state and operators are continued. This last wording is deliberate: a newly chosen contour after crossing poles is not automatically the same continued state. ### 4.1 Minimality is a separate argument We now prove that the state cannot have a rational first-order annihilator. This avoids inferring minimality from the elimination output. In scaled variables X=2 pi b x, u=2 pi b y the classical exponent numerator for chi_b is S(X,u)=Li_2(-exp(X-u))-Li_2(-exp u)-X(2u-X). (4.3) The saddle at (X,u)=(0,-2 pi i/3) is nondegenerate. The implicit function theorem gives a holomorphic saddle u(X) for small complex X. The gap at the maximum, the linear tails, and the fixed strip gap in Section 3 persist in a small complex neighborhood of X=0. Deform the contour a small amount to pass through u(X). The same Gaussian argument, uniformly on compact subsets of this neighborhood, proves a nonzero leading asymptotic and therefore J_b(x-i b)/J_b(x) -> ell(Q), Q=exp(-X), (4.4) ell=exp(-partial_X S(X,u(X))). The prefactor exp(4 pi i c_b x) in (3.2) contributes q to this ratio and hence does not change (4.4). The derivative of the saddle itself does not enter, because partial_u S=0. Put Y=exp(-u(X)). Exponentiating the critical equation and evaluating the derivative in (4.4) gives Q Y^2+(Q^2+Q-1)Y+Q^2=0, ell=(Q^2+QY)/Y^2. Eliminating Y, for Q^2!=1 and then by analytic continuation, gives Q^2 ell^2-F(Q) ell+Q^2=0, F(Q)=Q^4-Q^3-2Q^2-Q+1. (4.5) Its discriminant is F(Q)^2-4Q^4 =(Q-1)^2(Q+1)^2(Q^2-3Q+1)(Q^2+Q+1), (4.6) which is not a square in C(Q). The branch ell(Q) cannot be a rational function, even though it is holomorphic locally at the complete point. Suppose (r_1(Q,q)E+r_0(Q,q))J_b=0 with rational coefficients. Clear denominators and remove their common vanishing power at q^(1/2)=1 (or q=1 when coefficients are rational in q). At least one specialized coefficient at q=1 is nonzero. Taking (4.4) would give r_1(Q,1) ell(Q)+r_0(Q,1)=0, contradicting (4.6). A nonzero order-zero annihilator is excluded by (3.3). The coefficients in (4.2) have no common nonunit factor at generic q. Thus (4.2), up to the declared Laurent units and a choice of sign, is the primitive minimal-degree operator of Definition 5 for this state. This argument is over the rational q-difference coefficient field; it does not assert new Hilbert-space domain or all-level-N results. ### 4.2 The full classical peripheral factor The exact specialization of (4.2) is Ahat_1=(Q^2-1)[Q^2 E^2-F(Q)E+Q^2]. (4.7) The primitive generic-q coefficients acquire a common factor only in the classical limit. Dividing by Q^2-1 and then setting Q=1 is not the same operation as specializing the full operator at Q=1. In particular this is a concrete example of why the user's warning about peripheral factors matters. The independently established volume statement is (3.4) for the state of this minimal operator, with its normalization fixed by (3.1)–(3.2). It does not assign a volume rate to every solution of (4.2). ## 5. A broad state-integral theorem, with explicit certificates We now use the *existing* integral (4.5) of Ben Aribi–Wong, rather than choosing a new positive integrand. The theorem below provides sufficient data that can be checked without accepting their asymptotic proof. Let X be an ordered ideal triangulation with N tetrahedra. To avoid confusing the two pairs of matrices, write script-A, script-B for face matrices and A,B for the N-by-N Neumann–Zagier matrices. Supply the following certificates: 1. script-A is invertible and the face construction gives a real symmetric Gaussian matrix Q_f. Let H=Q_f-diag((epsilon_j+1)/4), G=-2H. 2. B is invertible and the finite identity G=B^(-1)A holds. This is the matrix identity in the literature FAMED definition. 3. Positive complete shapes z_j in the upper half plane, with compatible logarithms, satisfy A Log z+B Log z''=i nu, nu in pi Z^N, and the remaining edge and meridian completeness equations. The tetrahedra are the actual geometric triangulation, so sum D(z_j)=Vol(M). 4. For the boundary coordinate of the literature integral, set p=2 B^(-1)e_N. Supply a rational constant gamma for which p^T(-Log z+i pi 1)=i pi gamma. (5.1) It can be checked directly at the geometric solution, or obtained from the symplectic peripheral certificate described below. Choose p_1!=0 by relabeling. In this notation the literature integral at its complete boundary value is J_X(hbar,0)=C_X (2 pi sqrt(hbar))^(-N) integral exp((i y^T H y+c^T y)/(2 pi hbar)) product_j Phi_b(y_j/(2 pi sqrt(hbar))) dy_2 ... dy_N, c=B^(-1)nu-G pi 1, y_1=(i pi gamma-sum_(j>=2) p_j y_j)/p_1. (5.2) Use the exact nonzero constant C_X of the chosen literature convention and the horizontal contour through y*=-Log z+i pi 1. Its imaginary coordinates all lie in (0,pi). Thus the source's angle structure can be chosen to be the actual complete geometric angle structure. **Normalization detail.** Equation (4.5) as printed has C_X=p_1/det(script-A). The displayed preceding change of variables x=p^T y-i pi gamma has Jacobian p_1, so directly disintegrating the full Lebesgue measure instead gives 1/(p_1 det(script-A)), with signs depending on orientation conventions. This constant discrepancy needs reconciliation in an exact state comparison. The subsequent `faddeev_pentagon_audit.md`, Section 7.1, makes the conversion explicit: J_coarea=J_printed/p_1^2, with orientations fixed consistently. This is also independent of which coordinate is eliminated when the coarea fiber form is used. For the complex identity with positive Lebesgue disintegration, the orientation sign is sign(det(script-A)p_1). The full tensor phase and its exact state-recovery formula are derived in `peripheral_phase_and_state.md`. It is present also in the v2 TeX source, lines 3277–3292; it is not a PDF extraction artifact. The theorem uses the printed integral as its fixed definition; either explicit nonzero constant has the same volume limit. No boundary-dependent or exponentially significant factor is hidden in that observation. **Theorem 5.1.** For the exact integral (5.2), with these certificates, lim_(b->0+) -2 pi hbar log|J_X(hbar,0)|=Vol(M). (5.3) The integral is nonzero for sufficiently small b. The conclusion is not conditioned on a presumed asymptotic formula or absence of cancellations. ### 5.1 Finite identities and geometric saddle The kinematical reduction requires no stationary phase: integrating delta(script-A f+script-B t) in the face variables f gives K_X(t)=|det(script-A)|^(-1) exp(2 pi i t^T Q_f t). The determinant follows from an ordinary invertible linear change of variables. Formula (2.5) converts negative and positive tetrahedral factors to the common product of Phi_b used in (5.2), with the explicit unit-modulus constants retained when reconstructing the whole partition function. The face identity G=B^(-1)A is a supplied finite matrix identity, not a consequence of calling a triangulation geometric. The subsequent `face_edge_stokes_identity.md` proves its edge rows for every globally branched triangulation with an invertible face matrix; the specified peripheral row and its completion remain separate requirements. The subsequent peripheral-phase note explicitly reconstructs those constants and the complete angle-dependent phase, rather than using the magnitude formula as a state identity. Condition (5.1) can be certified using rational matrices C,D with A D^T-B C^T=Id, B^(-1)A symmetric, 2 e_N^T(C Log z+D Log z'')=H_m+i pi nu_m. Indeed B^(-T)=D G-C, so at the complete gluing solution p^T y*=H_m+i pi nu_m -2 i e_N^T D B^(-1)nu +2 i pi e_N^T B^(-T)1. Here H_m=0 by completeness and the other coefficients give gamma explicitly. This reconstructs the step needed from the symplectic peripheral data. The existence of particular C,D can be checked as part of the certificate; their geometric interpretation is not inferred merely from invertibility of B. The classical phase of (5.2) is F_0(y)=i y^T H y+c^T y-i sum_j Li_2(-exp y_j). Its gradient is grad F_0=-i G y+c+i Log(1+exp y). At y*=-Log z+i pi 1, Log(1+exp y*)=Log z''. Hence grad F_0(y*)=i B^(-1)(A Log z+B Log z'')+B^(-1)nu=0. (5.4) This is a full critical point before restricting to the boundary fiber. For y=h+i d, direct use of the definition of the Bloch–Wigner function gives Re F_0(y)=h dot Re(grad F_0(y))+sum_j D(-exp y_j). At y*, -exp y_j*=1/z_j, and D(1/z)=-D(z). Therefore Re F_0(y*)=-sum_j D(z_j)=-Vol(M). (5.5) Only elementary identities of the dilogarithm and the checked gluing equations enter this critical-value calculation. ### 5.2 A uniform bound, the hbar/b^2 distinction, and no cancellation It would be incorrect to replace sqrt(hbar) by b inside Phi_b without accounting for the error. Put s=b^2 and define the exact classical part F_s(y)=i y^T H y+c^T y -i/(1+s)^2 sum_j Li_2(-exp((1+s)y_j)). (5.6) Since hbar/b^2=(1+s)^(-2), (2.2) gives the exact integrand representation exp(F_s(y)/(2 pi hbar)) a_b(y), a_b(y)=exp(sum_j R_b((1+s)y_j)). (5.7) On any horizontal fiber with all (1+s)Im y_j in a fixed compact subset of (0,pi), a_b=1+O(s) uniformly over all its real directions. Parametrize the boundary fiber by y=y*+T u, u in C^(N-1), where T is the real, full-column-rank matrix implementing (5.2). On a horizontal contour its real Hessian is Hess_u Re F_s = -T^T diag( Im[exp((1+s)y_j)/(1+exp((1+s)y_j))] ) T. (5.8) Every diagonal entry inside the bracket is strictly positive, because 0<(1+s)Im y_j<pi. Hence (5.8) is negative definite at every finite real point. At s=0, the complex Hessian restricted to the fiber is invertible: its Hermitian real part is negative definite. The holomorphic implicit function theorem therefore gives a critical point u_s=O(s) of the restricted F_s. The contour can be translated a small complex amount to u_s+R^(N-1); all imaginary coordinates keep a fixed strip gap. Here are the global bounds needed for this translation and for Gaussian asymptotics. On the translated contour, Re F_s has zero gradient at its critical point and is strictly concave everywhere. On the unit ball its negative Hessian has a uniform positive lower bound for sufficiently small s. Along any outward ray concavity makes the radial derivative nonincreasing. Consequently there is c>0, independent of small s, such that Re F_s(y_s+T v) <= Re F_s(y_s)-c min(|v|^2,|v|), v in R^(N-1). (5.9) The same linear tail bound, with adjusted constants, holds during the small contour translation. The quantum amplitude is uniformly bounded by (5.7). Thus all boundary faces at infinity vanish in the contour deformation, and the noncompact tails are uniformly negligible in stationary phase. The Gaussian matrix has negative definite real part. Its Gaussian integral is nonzero, with the square root of its determinant fixed by continuation from real negative definite matrices. Equations (5.7)–(5.9) therefore give J_X(hbar,0) = C_X/(2 pi sqrt(hbar)) exp(F_s(y_s)/(2 pi hbar)) /sqrt(det(-Hess_u F_s(y_s))) (1+o(1)). (5.10) In particular a cancellation between unrelated saddles has not been assumed away: the contour has a unique strict maximum, its local Gaussian is nonzero, and the rest is exponentially smaller. Since F_s(y_s)->F_0(y*) and hbar tends to zero, (5.5) and (5.10) prove (5.3). QED. The N=1 case, if applicable, is a zero-dimensional fiber and follows directly from (5.7); the determinant and Gaussian integration are then omitted. ### 5.3 What this proves about a broad knot class For every knot exterior with a supplied positive geometric FAMED triangulation and compatible peripheral certificates, the published integral (4.5) has the volume law (5.3), by the above argument. The theorem does not depend on a claimed census computation or a claimed proof that a family has these certificates. Such membership claims need their own verification. The subsequent twist-family note supplies uniform face, angle and geometric certificates for the explicit literature families. Its [topological companion](twist_topology_and_peripherals.md) reconstructs the diagrammatic identification with the named twist knots and independently identifies the meridian and preferred longitude, including their branches. General two-bridge and alternating families are not yet covered by those formulas. Menasco's checkerboard polyhedra provide combinatorics; their existence alone does not supply the positive shape solution and matrix identity in items 1–4. A claim that they are actual all-right-angled cells of the complete metric requires additional hypotheses. Theorem 5.1 is a theorem about the specified literature *state integral*. The subsequent note `general_annihilator_and_volume.md` supplies a finite dimension-count and exponential-moment proof of annihilator existence in the Andersen–Malusà b-shift algebra for these rescaled integrals, as well as their classical geometric component. The canonical knot-state identification and the different finite-b operators of the FAMED paper remain separate questions. `twist_family_audit.md` supplies uniform geometric and matrix formulas for the two explicit twist face families; the topological companion identifies those families and their peripheral rows. Invariance of the whole state under all triangulation changes, including the correct boundary factors, also requires its own exact identities. ## 6. Reproducible diagnostics Run python3 experiments/audit_ore_certificate.py python3 experiments/check_literature_state_volume.py The first is an exact polynomial computation. The second evaluates the convergent remainder (2.3), checks (2.6) at several points, and evaluates the full quantum integrand on the contour in (3.5). For b=0.5,0.35,0.25,0.18,0.12, the scaled state exp(V/(2 pi b^2)) J_b(0) is approximately 0.6786085741, 0.7155266487, 0.7356954991, 0.7468279065, 0.7539044805, approaching 3^(-1/4)=0.7598356857. Changing Gaussian quadrature order from 128 to 256 changes the reported answers by at most 2e-11. These diagnostics support the calculations; the bounds and proofs above carry the conclusions.

title: Literal crossing-transfer Ward currents and their partial pushforward
text: # Literal crossing-transfer Ward currents and their partial pushforward Research construction, 27 October 2026. This writes the actual R intertwining identities coefficient by coefficient in the unwrapped transfer index. They give exact divergence currents and an explicit rank-one cyclic-edge source. The current identities compose under the actual tensor contractions and have a linear formal Gaussian pushforward with all inserted moments retained. No map from the scalar partially summed Gaussian block to the full matrix Ward complex is assumed here. A nonzero local cyclic-edge source is not asserted to be a nonzero selected framing cohomology class or global geometric contribution. ## 1. Actual coefficients and conventions Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2. Allow two colors x_1,x_2, with M_i=-q x_i. In the balanced basis the generator entries are K_i(n)=x_i Q^(-n), f(n)=1-Q^(n+1), 0<=n<N-1, e_i(n)=M_i Q^(-n)-M_i^(-1), 1<=n<N. Outside the displayed ranges f and e_i denote zero actual matrix edges. In particular e_i(0)=0. The last absent cyclic raising edge would instead have coefficient kappa_i=M_i-M_i^(-1). Let s=+1 or -1 and let r_s(a,b,k) be the actual checked crossing coefficient from inputs (a,b) to outputs (c,d)=(b+s k,a-s k), (1.1) with the output colors x_2,x_1. Extend it by zero unless a,b are in 0,...,N-1 and s=+1: 0<=k<=min(a,N-1-b), s=-1: 0<=k<=min(b,N-1-a). The explicit balanced formulas are those proved from the literal R matrices in [the actual four-plat calculation](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md), Section 2. Their common full Cartan line is retained. Every Ward identity here is homogeneous in that line: removing it only while checking an equality does not change or reset its prescribed phase. Let E_a,E_b shift the indicated input index by one, and let (S h)(a,b,k)=h(a,b,k+1). These are ordinary translations of unwrapped integer indices; k is never reduced modulo N. ## 2. The four literal F and E crossing currents The actual coproducts are Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F, Delta Ecal=Ecal tensor K+1 tensor Ecal. Checked R intertwines the input coproduct with the same coproduct in the switched color order. Taking one matrix entry gives f(a) r_s(a+1,b,k) +K_1(a)^(-1)f(b) r_s(a,b+1,k-s) =f(b+s k-1) r_s(a,b,k-s) +K_2(b+s k)^(-1)f(a-s k) r_s(a,b,k), (2.1) and K_2(b)e_1(a) r_s(a-1,b,k) +e_2(b) r_s(a,b-1,k+s) =K_1(a-s k-1)e_2(b+s k+1)r_s(a,b,k+s) +e_1(a-s k)r_s(a,b,k). (2.2) These are exact zero-extended array identities with the actual truncated edge functions. They include every corner and endpoint. For example, (2.1) has target (b+s k,a-s k+1): raising the first input gives its first term, raising the second input changes the required transfer to k-s, and the two output insertions give its right side. The same check with target (b+s k,a-s k-1) proves (2.2). This derives the formulas directly from actual matrices, not from a guessed q-hypergeometric summation identity. They may also be checked on the strict interior as rational identities of Q,x_1,x_2,Q^a,Q^b,Q^k, using the displayed proper crossing ratios. At endpoints the truncated edges, rather than unrestricted rational interpolation, specify the actual source. For an explicit independent-variable verification put A=Q^a, B=Q^b,C=Q^k. The three ratios r(a+1,b,k)/r, r(a,b+1,k)/r, r(a,b,k+1)/r are, for s=+1, BC/x_2 * (1-x_1^2/A)/(1-x_1^2 C/A), A/(x_1 C) * (1-QBC)/(1-QB), -x_2 A/(Q x_1^2 BC) * (1-QBC)(1-Qx_1^2 C/A)/(1-QC), and for s=-1, x_2/B * (1-QAC)/(1-QA), x_1/A * (1-x_2^2/B)/(1-x_2^2 C/B), (1-QAC)(1-Qx_2^2 C/B)/(x_2(1-QC)). They follow by canceling adjacent Gaussian and Pochhammer factors. Use inverse ratios at the shifted arguments for negative shifts. Dividing (2.1)--(2.2) by r then gives zero rational functions after substitution of these ratios. In (2.2) the common q^(-1) from e_i=q^(-1)(x_i^(-1)-Qx_i/Q^n) cancels. This establishes the interior identity before any root or fixed-N evaluation. ## 3. Explicit transfer divergences Define the following literal currents, including their coefficients: J_F,s=[K_1(a)^(-1)f(b)E_b-f(b+s k)] r_s, D_F,s=f(a)E_a+K_1(a)^(-1)f(b)E_b -K_2(b+s k)^(-1)f(a-s k)-f(b+s k). Then (2.1) is exactly D_F,s r_s+(S^(-s)-1)J_F,s=0. (3.1) For the raising current define J_E,s=[e_2(b)E_b^(-1) -K_1(a-s k)e_2(b+s k)] r_s, D_E,s=K_2(b)e_1(a)E_a^(-1)+e_2(b)E_b^(-1) -K_1(a-s k)e_2(b+s k)-e_1(a-s k). Then (2.2) is exactly D_E,s r_s+(S^s-1)J_E,s=0. (3.2) For instance S^s applied to the second term of J_E replaces its coefficient by K_1(a-s k-1)e_2(b+s k+1), explaining both shifted coefficients in (2.2). Operator order is as displayed. The D operators still contain internal multiplication characters. Thus summing these identities does not give a closed scalar Ward operator on the uninserted partial sum alone. The natural exact target includes the corresponding inserted moments. ## 4. The missing cyclic edge is an explicit wall source Let W=E_(N-1,0) and put Ecyc_i=Ecal_i+kappa_i W.
