Define the input and output two-leg cyclic coproduct matrices by the same displayed coproduct expression in their respective color orders. The actual checked matrix R_s obeys the exact equality R_s Delta_in(Ecyc)-Delta_out(Ecyc)R_s =R_s(kappa_1 W tensor K_2+kappa_2 I tensor W) -(kappa_2 W tensor K_1+kappa_1 I tensor W)R_s. (4.1) It follows by subtracting the actual Ecal intertwining equation. This is a retained boundary source, not an assertion that the original R is an intertwiner for the completed colors. If R(a,b;c,d) denotes its ordinary four-index entry, the right side is precisely kappa_1 1_(a=0) K_2(b) R(N-1,b;c,d) +kappa_2 1_(b=0) R(a,N-1;c,d) -kappa_2 1_(c=N-1) K_1(d) R(a,b;0,d) -kappa_1 1_(d=N-1) R(a,b;c,0). (4.2) Thus the wrap is a change in the actual integer conservation sector by N, with four fully specified endpoint currents. It is not a periodic reinterpretation of the transfer bounds. For equal colors this is kappa times [R_s,W tensor K+I tensor W]. At M=1 the actual and cyclic raising matrices agree, but dividing this source by the meridian gap retains a generally nonzero matrix. For the positive crossing and N>=3 one explicit entry is from input (0,N-1) to output (N-1,N-1). After factoring only the recorded common Cartan unit, its divided source is x^(-(N-1)) [x^(2-N)Q^2-1]. (4.3) At the prescribed complete x=q^(N-1), the expression in brackets is Q-1 for odd N and -Q-1 for even N. It is nonzero for N>=3. This proves a local first-normal source survives the missing-edge division. It does not prove its class is nonzero after the global framing Ward quotient or the actual cut. ## 5. Composition and the linear partial-current pushforward For equal-color b-strand braids the iterated missing-edge operator is W_tot=sum_i I^(tensor(i-1)) tensor W_i tensor K_(i+1)...K_b. For a word R_beta=R_m...R_1 the source composes by the exact rule [R_beta,W_tot] =sum_t R_m...R_(t+1)[R_t,W_tot]R_(t-1)...R_1. (5.1) Spectator terms in W_tot commute through a local crossing because it preserves the product K_iK_(i+1); the remaining terms are exactly the local currents above. Mixed colors use (4.1) with the color list switched after every crossing. Actual cups, caps and pivots contract these matrix currents with their original Hopf-adjoint rules from [the exact Ward/cut construction](actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction.md). There is an explicit linear current pushforward which is available before any open-matrix-index identification. For a finite zero- extended transverse array, or for its nondegenerate formal Gaussian realization G, translation covariance gives G[(S^v-1)J]=0, G[h(S^v-1)J]=G[(S^(-v)h-h)J]. (5.2) The first identity is finite reindexing, respectively formal Gaussian integration by parts; the second follows by translating the entire product hJ. It is valid with all rational insertions h regular on the chosen formal chart. Therefore (3.1)--(3.2) give exact Ward identities in the partially contracted inserted-moment module, with separate finite and formal realizations. For the formal one, first take the independent-variable interior identity just proved. Endpoint indicators are not assigned an unjustified formal meaning; they remain the explicit finite boundary sources to be compared. For more than one internal coordinate use the displayed vector translation v and sum the currents. The global integral flow elimination has determinant +/-1; edge current translations are consequently integral translations of the remaining independent flow coordinates, with explicit affine offsets obtained by the same closure solver. Keeping the two framing coordinates external leaves their current operators present. The Gaussian contraction kills only transverse divergences. It does not integrate either framing direction or replace the retained moment module by an unproved scalar Ward character. This is a linear map of current identities. It is not a unital map of finite matrix algebras into a scalar quantization. In particular the fixed-N matrix relation (Ad_K)^N=I must not be silently replaced by a nontrivial formal near-identity scalar action. The interior all-level proper-ratio formalization unfolds those fixed-N relations before taking H=Log Q as a formal parameter. ## 6. The exact remaining source-survival question The local Ward currents, their cyclic endpoint source, composition, and transverse linear pushforward are now specified. The full finite operator-valued Hopf-adjoint diagram also exists. What is not yet constructed is the comparison from this partially contracted inserted-current module, with its remaining external currents, to the cut Ward complex and its normal co-source. There is an exact cancellation which makes this distinction necessary. The proof that pivotal partial trace intertwines Hopf adjoints also applies to Ecyc: it has the same K-weight, and gK^(-1)=K^(-N) is central. Write C_beta=ptr(R_beta) for the actual fully closed (1,1)-tangle matrix, with its fixed scalar zero-framing line retained. It is scalar by the actual K,F Ward contraction. Hence ptr([Ecyc_tot,R_beta] K_tot^(-1)) =[Ecyc,C_beta] K^(-1)=0. Using the actual Ecal intertwining identity and (5.1), this gives the whole meridian identity ptr([W_tot,R_beta] K_tot^(-1))=0. (6.1) It first follows away from kappa=0 by canceling that nonzero scalar, then extends to M=1 through the regular whole matrix germ. Thus the ordinary full contraction of the divided cyclic-wall source is zero even when individual local matrices in (4.3) are nonzero. A surviving source class must be relative to the marked defect and its endpoints before this ordinary contraction; it cannot be inferred from local nonzero matrix entries. That map must carry the boundary source (4.2), canonical carry and the actual normal cut row. Nondegeneracy of the transverse Hessian alone does not supply it: the D operators in Section 3 visibly retain inserted internal moments. A nonzero matrix such as (4.3) can become exact or cancel after further contraction. Neither its nonzero local coefficient nor Schur normalization proves a nonzero selected global Bockstein class or a volume limit. [Exact local-current audit](../experiments/audit_local_r_ward_transfer_currents.py). [Results](../experiments/local_r_ward_transfer_currents_results.json).

title: Equality audit: positive geometric core and primitive tube completion
text: # Equality audit: positive geometric core and primitive tube completion 29 October 2026. The whole-source theorem already fixes a nonzero limit equal to the regulator of an explicit filled representation. A sharp representation-volume bound does NOT make that representation geometric. This note isolates and proves the remaining local END-completion lemma. It uses a positive geometric deformation of the compact core, not an unfilled Casson--Rivin maximum and not convergence of volumes alone. ## 1. Exact inputs needed from the original source For each fixed odd s>=25 the [whole original source theorem](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md) provides a nonzero asymptotic at every independently sufficiently long fixed signed tuple p. Its constants may depend on s and that fixed tuple; there is no assertion uniform in slopes growing with N. All auxiliary colors, both root parities, the middle color, every normal jet, and the original single marked source are retained there. The [literal port theorem](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md) constructs rho_z of the ACTUAL augmented-link group. It includes the right-to-left cap order, rather than a permutation of arbitrary pretzel boxes. At z=0 its complete main and auxiliary generators are the oriented four-antiprism geometric holonomy. The [preferred-peripheral certificate](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md) fixes M_i=H_i^(-1/2), lambda_i=-L_i^(-1), including the ordinary-circle spin. The [regulator comparison](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) then gives, at a selected filling point, source rate = Vol(rho_p). For equality with the manifold volume one needs more than the facts that rho_p kills the slope and Vol(rho_p) tends to the augmented volume. The two additional geometric inputs used below are precise: * A FIXED finite partially ideal geometric triangulation of the complete augmented manifold, every tetrahedron strictly positive. Finite face and cell centers are allowed. An arbitrary ideal topological triangulation is insufficient. * Transporting its vertex orbits by rho_z and the selected cusp flags gives a nearby positive developing triangulation with local degree one at its finite faces, edges and vertices. Equivariance and the local degree statement concern the SAME original marked manifold. The finite-center construction of this input is proved in [the geometric-core and filling theorem](actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md), sections2--4. It has been independently read in full: matched face-center fans and finite cell centers give24s positive tetrahedra, exact contractible edge transitions remove both screw and cone defects, and the finite spherical links have degree one. The result below is independent of whether an all-ideal positive subdivision is available. ## 2. A compact affine link becomes an honest translation torus Consider one ideal end of such a positive developing triangulation. Its oriented link is a compact torus T. Sending the selected peripheral fixed flag to infinity identifies the link triangles with Euclidean triangles and their transitions with orientation-preserving complex similarities. Its developing map d: universal_cover(T) -> C is a local homeomorphism, including at the link vertices. Local degree one and the positive Euclidean angle sums are essential here. Suppose the peripheral affine holonomies have a common finite fixed point q. Assume d avoids q. On the simply connected cover choose f=Log(d-q). The differential df is invariant under the deck group, because an affine holonomy has d-q -> a_gamma(d-q). It is everywhere nonsingular. Thus |df|^2 (1) is a nonsingular Euclidean metric on the COMPACT torus T. It is complete. The lifted f is a local isometry from its complete simply connected Euclidean cover to C; it is a global isometry. To see this directly, lift every straight segment starting at f(x). The corresponding unit speed geodesic exists for the whole segment by completeness. This proves surjectivity and path lifting; since C is simply connected, the local isometry is a one-sheeted covering. Consequently f gives a global coordinate on the link cover. Its deck translations form a rank-two lattice Lambda={L_gamma : f(gamma x)=f(x)+L_gamma}. (2) The map pi_1(T)->Lambda is injective. Rank one or a nonzero deck element with zero period would contradict the compact flat-torus quotient. This argument controls the DEGREE of the logarithmic development, not just its local derivative. ### Why q is avoided in the selected near-complete family Choose the peripheral flag normalization continuously from the complete geometric cusp. A fixed fundamental union of link triangles has bounded developed image, uniformly near completeness. A meridian has affine form d -> a d+b, a ->1, b -> b_0!=0. When a!=1 its common finite fixed point is q=b/(1-a), so q goes to infinity. For sufficiently small deformation it misses that entire finite fundamental image. Every other developed triangle is its affine translate; the holonomy fixes q, so none of those triangles meets q either. This proves the hypothesis globally on the link cover. The selected source family approaches the base uniformly as max_i |p_i|^(-1) goes to zero. Therefore one small geometric neighborhood works for independently unequal signed sufficiently long slopes. No comparison between the different |p_i| is required. There is no genericity exception a_i=1 at a selected finite filling. Exact separate evenness gives V_i=tau_i(z)U_i holomorphically, with tau_i near its nonreal complete cusp value. If U_i=0 then V_i=0, contradicting U_i+p_iV_i=+/-2pi i. The selected logs are small, so exp(U_i)=1 also forces U_i=0. Thus every selected auxiliary meridian has a_i!=1 and the stated finite second fixed point exists. ## 3. The actual end contains a full punctured tube Translate q to zero in upper half-space coordinates (z,y), y>0. The link development now has z=exp(f). Every incident geometric tetrahedron has its chosen ideal vertex at infinity. Its faces through infinity are vertical planes. Above a bounded lower height its part over its Euclidean link triangle is therefore a vertical product. The opposite face cannot be vertical: otherwise all four vertices would lie in one hyperbolic plane and the tetrahedron would have zero volume. This works with finite as well as ideal remaining vertices. There are finitely many such pieces in a fundamental link domain and that domain avoids zero. It follows that for some finite A>0 the end contains the full equivariant epigraph y>A|z|. (3) Indeed bound every lower cutoff y_0(z)/|z| on those finitely many compact pieces; affine deck similarities multiply numerator and denominator by the same positive number. Since f is globally one-to-one onto C, the different pieces meet coherently across their side faces and do not introduce an uncounted logarithmic covering. Put r=y/|z|. Cylindrical coordinates about the vertical 0--infinity axis are R=asinh(1/r), theta=Im f, X=Re f+(1/2)log(1+r^2). The hyperbolic metric is exactly dR^2+cosh(R)^2 dX^2+sinh(R)^2 dtheta^2. (4) A link deck translation f->f+L_gamma acts by (X,theta)->(X+Re L_gamma,theta+Im L_gamma). Equation (3) says that the end contains the WHOLE region 0<R<R_0 of this tube, not merely a narrow subset tending toward its axis. ## 4. Primitive logarithmic angle is the decisive completion condition Let alpha be a primitive filled slope and choose beta so (alpha,beta) is a basis of pi_1(T)=Z^2. Suppose its ACTUAL log-link period is L_alpha=+2pi i or -2pi i. (5) Because Lambda has real rank two, Re L_beta!=0. The quotient of (4) for 0<R<R_0 therefore has one angular period exactly 2pi and one loxodromic screw generator. Adding R=0 is the ordinary smooth hyperbolic solid torus, with core length |Re L_beta|. Its meridian is exactly alpha. Either sign in (5) gives a smooth tube; it chooses the orientation of its meridian parameter, not a mirror of the positive compact core. This proves smooth filling and discreteness directly from the local metric. Killing alpha in PSL2 alone would NOT suffice. If instead L_alpha=2pi i m with |m|>1, the same construction has cone angle 2pi|m| at its core. All punctured local geometry and the killed PSL slope could still hold, but the completion would be branched rather than smooth. If L_alpha=0, injectivity of the logarithmic period map would already contradict a nonsingular compact link torus. The [primitive-angle proof](actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.md) identifies the actual periods with the source logarithms, including their integer windings. In the source conventions, U_i=Log(M_i^2)=-z_i, V_i=Log(lambda_i^2) centered at completeness=-2ell_i, U_i+p_i V_i=-2pi i m_i. The surviving charges satisfy |m_i|=1, precisely (5). The complete SL2 longitude sign is NOT used as an uncentered 2pi i contribution to V_i. The proof of the period identification must remain separate from merely checking exp(U_i+p_i V_i)=1. At the unfilled main cusp all affine multipliers are one. Its positive compact link is an ordinary complete Euclidean torus by the same flat-metric argument, and its end contains a full horoball quotient. Thus the completed filled metric has finite volume and exactly the required complete main cusp. ## 5. What follows, without assuming a character-variety uniqueness theorem Combining the positive-core input with sections2--4 yields a complete oriented hyperbolic metric on the ACTUAL filled knot complement. Its holonomy is rho_p. The developing map on its complete universal cover is a local isometry to H3. Lifting geodesic segments exactly as above makes it a covering of H3; since H3 is simply connected it is a global isometry. Hence rho_p is discrete and faithful. One can compare its volume to any specified complete hyperbolic metric on the same oriented manifold without importing an additional volume- rigidity assertion. Apply the proved sharp representation-volume inequality once with each complete structure as domain and the other structure's holonomy as target. The finite fundamental chain has the same oriented degree one in both cases. The two inequalities give Vol(rho_p)=Vol(the filled hyperbolic manifold). (6) Together with the already proved whole-source asymptotic and marked regulator comparison, this is the required equality. The proof is conditional ONLY on the explicit positive-core input and the actual primitive-period certificate, both stated above; convergence of Vol(rho_p) to the augmented volume is not used as an equality argument. ## 6. Casson--Rivin and Gromov: the exact scope of the extremal argument Strict concavity of the ideal-tetrahedron volume on an affine POSITIVE angle slice gives at most one interior critical point and makes that point its global maximum. It does not by itself prove: * that a supplied topological ideal triangulation has a positive geometric realization; * that the SOURCE point lies in that same angle slice; * that the correct filling slope and its integer log angle are used; * that a locally geometric but incomplete end completes without a branching multiplicity. In particular, the UNFILLED complete-cusp angle constraints have a different maximum from a finite Dehn filling. For actual peripheral logarithms u,v the regulator variation is dV=2 sum(Re v dIm u-Re u dIm v). On a slice fixing only the rotational filling condition Im(u+p v)=constant, this becomes dV=-2 sum(Re u+p Re v)dIm v. The real filling condition Re(u+p v)=0 is therefore the relevant stationarity condition. Replacing this modified slice by the original complete-cusp slice would be incorrect. A positive all-ideal triangulation and the full-rank marked gluing rows can make this a strict-concavity proof of uniqueness; the finite-center completion above does not need that additional representation. Likewise the Gromov/representation-volume norm inequality proves only |Vol(rho)|<=Vol(M). Equality needs an actual equality certificate. Here that certificate is the complete local isometry constructed from the positive core and the primitive tube, rather than proximity of two volumes or a formal maximum principle. ## 7. A precise local-uniqueness lemma when positive ideal rows are supplied There is also a short independent local-rigidity statement. Suppose an ACTUAL positive all-ideal triangulation has t tetrahedra and c cusps, and its t-c independent edge equations together with the c specified meridian equations form a full-rank real isotropic row matrix (A B). Thus its row space is Lagrangian, not just an arbitrary selection of cleared polynomial equations. Write shape logs x_j=Log z_j and y_j=Log(1-z_j^(-1)). At the positive complete point, dy_j=tau_j dx_j, tau_j=1/(z_j-1), Im tau_j<0. The fixed-meridian gluing Jacobian A+B diag(tau_j) is invertible. If a vector a were in its kernel, (a,diag(tau)a) would lie in the complex Lagrangian kernel of (A B). Its symplectic pairing with its conjugate would be zero; multiplied by i/2 that pairing is sum_j Im(tau_j)|a_j|^2, which is strictly negative unless a=0. The holomorphic implicit-function theorem therefore gives a UNIQUE local positive shape solution for each set of small marked meridian logs. Any sufficiently close framed representation whose equivariant ideal vertices give that same positive triangulation satisfies those gluing equations and is this shape germ, up to its already specified framing. Thus no additional near-complete branch can be substituted while keeping the SAME marked geometric gluing data. This lemma neither asserts full rank for unverified rows nor obtains the source's geometric realization from an arbitrary topological triangulation. Even with this local uniqueness, the primitive-angle and end-completion arguments in sections2--4 remain necessary to identify a smooth filled manifold rather than a branched completion. ## 8. Final independent audit verdict The primitive-angle proof and the positive-core construction have now both passed independent analytical reads, and two independent readers checked sections2--5 of this note. Thus the stated geometric inputs are supplied, rather than left as formal hypotheses. The completed metric and its degree-one fundamental chain identify the source regulator with the actual hyperbolic volume for the precise long-pretzel class. The separate [Casson--Rivin presentation](actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) also checks: its coisotropic first-variation formula applies to every tangent of the marked ANGLE slice, because both the actual real log vector and an arbitrary edge-angle tangent lie in E^perp. It does not assume that every such tangent solves nonlinear gluing. The factor1/2 for squared peripheral coordinates is correct, and the source's real filling equations kill the boundary derivative on the filled rotational slice. Strict concavity then gives a unique maximum. The geometric completion remains in that proof's dependency chain; the maximum alone does not identify a smooth filled end. The conclusion remains restricted to every fixed odd s>=25 and all independently sufficiently long fixed signed p_i, with the ORIGINAL source and normalization. It is not a conclusion for all hyperbolic knots, short fillings, or slopes growing with the quantum level.

title: Completion audit of the original-source upper-bound milestone
text: # Completion audit of the original-source upper-bound milestone **Historical intermediate audit.** The user correctly clarified that the objective is full hyperbolic-volume equality. That equality is now proved for the same class by the subsequent geometric completion and recorded in the [full equality audit](long_pretzel_volume_equality_completion_audit.md). The upper-bound audit below is retained as a proof dependency, not as a substitute for the equality objective. 29 October 2026. The milestone was to prove geometric survival OR a sharp hyperbolic-volume bound for the full original source across a broad class. The [assembled theorem](actual_long_pretzel_sharp_volume_upper_bound.md) meets the upper-bound alternative. Full volume-conjecture equality is not part of this completion claim. For every fixed odd s>=25 there exists p_s such that, for independently chosen fixed signed integers |p_i|>=p_s, the original pretzel diagram with boxes R^(-(2p_i+1)) satisfies, if its knot complement is hyperbolic, lim_N (2pi/N)log|<K>_N|=Vol(rho_p)<=Vol(S^3 minus K). The limit uses the original normalized Kashaev invariant. Both level parities and composite levels are included. The width is unbounded over the class but fixed before N tends to infinity. The slopes are also fixed before that limit; their signs and relative magnitudes are independent. There is no claim of a uniform simultaneous width/level limit, of short-slope coverage, or of all-knot coverage. ## Proof dependencies | Required step | Certificate and scope | | --- | --- | | Full original finite source and normalization | [Whole-source theorem](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md), with all colors, Cartan factors, half weights and marked derivatives. The reduced invariant has the raw source's absolute value; the optional full modified convention keeps its factor i^(N+3)/N. | | Global control away from the cusp corridor | [Global alias and color gap](actual_pretzel_global_alias_and_colored_source_gap.md), including ordinary colors, the even middle color and every normal term. The explicit strict width inequality holds for all odd s>=25. | | Exact complex packet and coherent Fourier filling | [Analytic color packet](actual_pretzel_exact_analytic_color_packet.md), [endpoint and charge estimates](actual_filling_source_fourier_endpoint_gap.md), and [corridor survival](actual_pretzel_cusp_corridor_filling_survival.md). These retain paired endpoint currents, the exact zero-charge cancellation and summable high-charge tails. | | Nonzero leading term for the entire source | [Full-source assembly](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md): the minimal signed charges add, all other terms have a strict gap for each fixed allowed slope tuple, and D_s(p) is nonzero. | | Representation of the actual diagram | [Local lift](actual_pretzel_mixed_regular_character_lift.md) and [global port theorem](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md) verify explicit matrices, group relations and every cap in the actual right-to-left composition order. | | Preferred peripheral coordinates and filled slope | [Mixed longitude certificate](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md): M=H^(-1/2), lambda=-L^(-1), with no unrecorded meridian shear. Commuting regular semisimple matrices satisfy C P^p=+/-I, so the actual primitive slope is killed in PSL2. | | Absolute orientation and regulator constant | The port theorem matches every white and shaded face at the complete anchor. The [cap-order audit](actual_pretzel_literal_cap_order_audit.md) verifies the holomorphic reversal F(zeta)=rho^2/zeta, including its joint peripheral inversion. The [marked regulator proof](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) has the same differential and absolute anchor as the developed fundamental chain. | | Augmented-to-filled representation volume | The marked regulator proof uses the controlled axis-cusp homotopy of the [general peripheral volume proof](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md), then one compatible finite core-plus-solid-torus chain. Both old boundary vertices and new filling vertices use the same invariant axis. | | Upper bound by the actual filled volume | The [independent representation-volume argument](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md) proves |Vol(rho)|<=Vol(K) by averaging finite regular tetrahedra. It assumes hyperbolicity of K, not faithfulness of rho or a quantum conjecture. | ## Final calibration issues and their resolution The literal cap traversal is right to left. Generic noncommuting physical boxes were checked to prevent commutativity of the special Casimir source from hiding a reversed order. The complete holomorphic reversal is orientation preserving; it jointly inverts the auxiliary meridian and longitude. The corresponding filling slope is inverted as a whole, consistently with the retained pair of signed source charges. The representation lift is constructive. It verifies the actual unrotated threaded half-twist group word, the selected peripheral eigenflag and the caps. It does not infer a canonical state graph from nodal R eigenphases or use the trace identity symmetric under U inversion to choose an orientation. No additional unproved U/Ward calibration enters the theorem. The regulator chain is the developed fundamental triangulation of the actual link complement. Its boundary pairing works for the selected semisimple auxiliary meridians. The separate unipotent five-dilogarithm coefficient identity is not being extended without proof. The spin terms cancel only in the full paired regulator, and the complete anchor fixes the absolute additive constant. ## Verification The source and geometric arguments received independent analytical reviews. Fresh primary-agent runs of the four analytic supporting audits passed; their exact scope is recorded in section4 of the whole-source theorem. Controlled analytic Gaussian packets in those scripts calibrate signs and densities; they are not substituted for proofs of the actual-source uniform estimates. Fresh final primary-agent replays also passed: - `audit_actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.py`: exact port matrices, six reverse-cap families, seven complete white and both shaded face families, and twelve signed filling-spin/Hurwitz cases. - `audit_actual_pretzel_literal_cap_order.py`: seven original marked noncommuting tensor families, six full-cap families and six complete holomorphic generator/peripheral families. Independent final reviewers checked the preferred-longitude and local character-lift audits as well as the signed unequal-slope quantifiers, the PSL descent, absolute regulator and finite filling-chain argument. Finite experiments verify identities and conventions; the linked analytic arguments supply the asymptotic theorem. ## What remains beyond this milestone The upper inequality does not prove Vol(rho_p)=Vol(K). A positive geometric filling/completion argument, or another equality proof, is still needed for the full volume conjecture for this class. General hyperbolic or alternating knots remain outside the stated theorem. The user's Cauchy observation is exact: |bv|^2<=(bG^(-1)b^*)(v^*Gv). For the complete augmented base, [the explicit weighted Fourier metric](actual_pretzel_coherent_circle_and_period_asymptotic.md#8-the-requested-special-inner-product-is-an-explicit-fourier-norm) has polynomial dual cost, a separately proved sharp geometric energy and polynomially small normalized overlap. The filled-knot theorem above instead uses the whole-source asymptotic and its representation regulator. It does not assert a sharp metric-energy theorem for arbitrary source words.

title: Completion audit: full hyperbolic-volume equality for the original source
text: # Completion audit: full hyperbolic-volume equality for the original source 29 October 2026. The objective is EQUALITY with the actual hyperbolic volume. An upper bound alone does not satisfy it. The earlier upper-bound checkpoint is an intermediate result; this audit concerns the complete equality on the same broad class. ## 1. Statement and unchanged quantifiers For each fixed odd integer s>=25 there is P_s such that, for every independently chosen FIXED signed tuple |p_i|>=P_s, the original pretzel knot with boxes R^(-(2p_i+1)) has lim_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|<K>_N|=Vol(S^3 minus K). The invariant and its cut normalization are the original reduced Kashaev invariant. Both parities and all composite quantum levels are included. The slopes may have different signs and arbitrarily different sizes. The width is unbounded across the class, but both it and the slopes are fixed before N tends to infinity. The threshold may depend on the fixed width. No statement for arbitrary knots, short slopes, or widths/slopes growing with N is included. The standing hyperbolicity assumption can be retained. In fact the constructed smooth complete metric proves hyperbolicity in this sufficiently long range. This strengthening is not needed to reduce or change the original equality target. ## 2. Requirements and authoritative evidence | Requirement | Evidence and conclusion | | --- | --- | | Briefly audit the essential previous ingredients | Section1 of the [Casson--Rivin equality note](actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) isolates the unchanged finite source, coherent inner elimination, global color gap, exact complex packet, full endpoint/charge analysis and marked representation regulator. | | Entire original invariant, rather than a selected formal block | The [whole-source theorem](actual_long_pretzel_full_source_survival.md) proves the full asymptotic with D_s(p)!=0. Its global estimate includes every auxiliary color and normal derivative; original framing factors have the verified modulus. | | Actual source-selected representation and absolute regulator | The [port theorem](actual_pretzel_port_lift_and_geometric_anchor.md), [preferred longitude](actual_mixed_crossing_circle_preferred_longitude.md) and [marked regulator comparison](actual_pretzel_marked_regulator_and_filling_action.md) give Vsrc=Vol(rho_p) on the original filled topology, with its exact peripheral sign and complete oriented anchor. | | Positive geometric realization of that representation | Sections2--4 of the [geometric completion proof](actual_long_pretzel_geometric_filling_completion.md) construct24s positive partially ideal tetrahedra from the original two polyhedra. Their equivariant deformation verifies all shared faces, exact edge return, angle winding one, spherical finite-vertex links and nonsingular compact similarity cusp links. | | Smooth primitive filling, not merely scalar slope holonomy | The [primitive-angle proof](actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.md) identifies the actual geometric log periods U=-z, V=-2ell and U+pV=-2pi i m, |m|=1. Bounded finite generator paths and the escaping second fixed point exclude hidden integer log windings before multiplication by p. | | Complete degree-one geometry with no branched or covered end | Sections2--5 of the [tube proof](long_pretzel_equality_critical_audit.md) use the compact flat log-link to obtain its entire plane development and injective period lattice. The actual epigraph is a full tube; primitive angle2pi completes smoothly. The main cusp remains a full horoball quotient. | | Casson--Rivin extremal identification | Sections2--5 of the [variational proof](actual_long_pretzel_casson_rivin_equality.md) put the source point inside the actual filled-slope positive angle slice. The coisotropic first variation holds for ALL angle tangents and vanishes by the source equations. Strict concavity makes this the unique global maximum, including over the boundary. | | Gromov-norm comparison reaches equality | The completed metric is on the actual oriented filled manifold. Applying the independently proved [representation-volume inequality](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md) in both directions between it and the specified hyperbolic metric forces equal volumes. This does not assume that an almost-maximal volume is already maximal. | | Preserve independently signed long slopes and all levels | The source critical point is holomorphic in all inverse slopes near zero. One fixed geometric neighborhood therefore works whenever max_i|1/p_i| is sufficiently small. No ratio between slopes is bounded. The original all-level asymptotic remains unchanged. | ## 3. The actual equality chain The completed and variational proofs give lim_N (2pi/N)log|<K>_N| =Vsrc_s(p) =D(beta(rho_p)) =max_(theta in A_p) V_T(theta) =Vol(S^3 minus K). Here A_p uses the filled rotational constraints Im(U_i+p_iV_i)=-2pi, not the complete UNFILLED cusp constraints. At the source point ReU_i+p_iReV_i=0, so for every tangent of A_p, dV_T=(1/2)sum_i ReV_i d(ImU_i+p_iImV_i)=0. The main cusp term is zero because its peripheral image is parabolic. The negative tetrahedral Hessian is positive definite with determinant1. Thus the source is the unique constrained maximizer. The separate primitive tube proof ensures that this maximum is realized on the actual smoothly filled knot, rather than on a branched local structure. For the customary all-ideal angle presentation, the prior audited positive ideal-subdivision input is used. The independent finite-center metric completion proves the final geometric equality without relying on that optional all-ideal presentation. These dependencies are not conflated. ## 4. Verification and limits of the checks The primary agent read the new positive-core, primitive-period and compact-log/tube proofs against the existing source, port and regulator statements. Independent reviewers checked the primitive spin and angle, the complete tube and its degree, the positive-core construction, and the Casson--Rivin first variation on arbitrary angle tangents. The source and geometric thresholds were checked for signed unequal slopes. A fresh primary-agent run of `experiments/audit_actual_long_pretzel_primitive_filling_angle.py` passed its exact spin/angle algebra,120 signed core families,32 small-log calibrations and5 Fermi metric checks. These checks calibrate formulas; the uniform proof of smooth completion is in the notes, not inferred from those finite examples. The previous full-source audits and their precise analytical scope are recorded in the whole-source theorem and the earlier upper-bound completion audit. In particular, the new proof does not rely on any of the following insufficient substitutes: a scalar killed peripheral word; convergence of filled volumes to V_s; a positive quantum norm without survival; an arbitrary topological triangulation; or strict concavity without a verified source point in the correct constrained angle domain. The evidence establishes full equality for the class in section1. The general volume conjecture for arbitrary hyperbolic knots remains outside this theorem, rather than being declared complete by this audit.

title: The actual cut period, its flag torsor, and its classical holonomy
text: # The actual cut period, its flag torsor, and its classical holonomy Research note, 26 October 2026. This continues the [relative octahedral calculation](relative_octahedral_period.md). It identifies the global *classical critical correspondence* of the actual cut state with a framed knot representation variety, retaining the boundary vector that gives the original invariant. It also identifies a split Borel framing torsor and proves a boundary-wedge/complete-regulator rigidity statement for the crossing Bloch sum. No assertion about which critical component contributes to the finite period is made. The holonomy braid map and existence of representation-associated diagrammatic critical points have existing coverage. Section 9 records it. The proofs here are direct calculations from our fixed actual R coefficients, not imports of those papers' proofs. ## 1. An exact change of boundary vector, at every level and color Put q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), x=q^alpha, M=-qx as in [the ADO note](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). Let F_a=(Q;Q)_a, 0<=a<N, psi_a=1/F_a, phi_a=F_a/N. (1.1) These coefficients are units, F_(N-1)=N, and sum_a phi_a psi_a=1. Let C_N(x) be the actual zero-framed cut operator of a knot. The previously proved intertwining and irreducibility calculation gives C_N(x)=F_N(M) I at generic color; Laurent continuation extends the matrix identity to exceptional colors. Therefore phi^t C_N(x) psi=F_N(M) (1.2) for every color, including the Kashaev color M=1. This is a bilinear algebraic pairing, with no complex conjugation. Now use the basis w_a=v_a/F_a. A matrix transforms by D^(-1)CD, where D=diag(1/F_a). In this basis psi is the constant vector 1 and phi is the normalized averaging functional (1/N)sum_a. Equation (1.2) becomes F_N(M)=(1/N) sum_(a,b) (C_N^new(x))_(a,b). (1.3) This is an exact presentation of the existing invariant. It is useful because its boundary vector has a simple geometric flag, without fixing a state coordinate to its endpoint a=0. ## 2. The actual relative meridian module in that basis Let A be multiplication by Q^a on functions of a modulo N, and let sigma f(A)=f(QA). Let e_partial be the idempotent supported at a=N-1. The actual conjugated quantum-group matrices are K=x A^(-1), F=(1-A)sigma^(-1), rho^2 E=q^(-1)(x^(-1)-x A^(-1))sigma -c(x)e_partial sigma, c(x)=q^(-1)(x^(-1)-Qx) =q^(-1)x^(-1)(1-M^2). (2.1) For F the coefficient at a=0 vanishes, so the cyclic formula already has the actual nilpotent endpoint. For E, cancellation of the adjacent factorials gives rho^2 E_(a,a+1)=q^(-1)(x^(-1)-xQ^(-a)), a<N-1. The cyclic formula would add the entry from 0 to N-1 with coefficient c(x). Subtracting it gives precisely the actual truncated E. This proves (2.1), including its exceptional row. Write E_cyc for the operator in (2.1) before subtracting this rank-one term. Multiplication around its orbit gives (rho^2 E_cyc)^N=(x^N-x^(-N))I, (rho^2 E)^N=0. (2.2) Indeed the product for the first operator is q^(-N)x^(-N)(1-x^(2N))=x^N-x^(-N). At M=1 the wall coefficient c and the central defect both vanish, and the cyclic and actual E operators agree. Away from that point E_cyc is a comparison module; replacing E by E_cyc in the knot contraction has not been justified and is not done here. The full modified dimension now has another exact interpretation: d_N(M)=q^(N(1-N)/2) c(x)/(x^N-x^(-N)) =i^(N+3) M^(N-1)/(1+M^2+...+M^(2N-2)). (2.3) To prove it, use qx-(qx)^(-1)=-c(x) in the defining modified-dimension formula. Thus the full meridian factor is a specified phase times the ratio of a local boundary defect to the cyclic central defect. At M=1 evaluate their whole ratio, giving d_N(1)=i^(N+3)/N. The two zeros must not be evaluated separately. This agrees with the missing-transition calculation in the preceding note; it retains its full peripheral function. This is the local color representation, with its internal state-index wall. Turning that wall into a specified global inhomogeneous meridian A-equation requires elimination with the source retained. That identification is not assumed here. ## 3. Crossing Bloch sums change by a boundary coboundary For a crossing with input indices a,b and output indices c,d, the basis change gives exactly r_new=F_c F_d r_old/(F_a F_b). (3.1) For the positive crossing c=b+k,d=a-k, put A=Q^a, B=Q^b,C=Q^k,X=x^2. Its non-Gaussian finite product is now F_(b+k)/(F_b F_k) * (QX/A;Q)_k. Its five-dilogarithm symbol is beta_+=[B]+[C]+[X/A]-[BC]-[XC/A]. (3.2) The Gaussian and sign in the preceding note are unchanged. For the inverse crossing c=b-k,d=a+k the product and symbol are F_(a+k)/(F_a F_k) * (QX/B;Q)_k, beta_-=[A]+[C]+[X/B]-[AC]-[XC/B]. (3.3) The difference between either new symbol and the old one is [A]+[B]-[U]-[V], U=Q^c,V=Q^d. (3.4) It cancels on each shared strand of a finite contraction. The cut vector and covector transform at the remaining endpoints as in Section 1. Thus this basis change does not lose a global period or insert an unspecified normalization. Both (3.2) and (3.3) have the form [u]+[v]+[w]-[uv]-[vw]. (3.5) They have the five ordered tetrahedron shapes v, u, 1/(uv), w, 1/(vw), with ideal vertices infinity,0,1,v,uv, v(1-w)/(1-vw), by the previous cross-ratio proof. The positive case uses (u,v,w)=(B,C,X/A); the negative uses (A,C,X/B). The inverse orientation is consistent: substituting (A,B,C)->(B/C,AC,1/C) in beta_+ gives -beta_- by [1/C]=-[C]. No additional negative sign is inserted in the negative coefficient's already computed symbol. ## 4. Deriving the rational crossing map from the actual symbols For clarity, derive it first in the old basis. Its physical coordinates do not change with (3.1). Let p,r denote the classical eigenvalues of the input Q-shifts and put P(A)=(1-A)(1-x^2/A)/x, K_1=x/A, e_1=P(A)p, f_1=p^(-1), K_2=x/B, e_2=P(B)r, f_2=r^(-1). (4.1) These are the commuting symbols of K,rho^2 E,F. They obey K_i+K_i^(-1)+e_i f_i=x+x^(-1). (4.2) In the new basis, the same coordinates are K=x/A, e=(1-x^2/A)p_new/x, f=(1-A)/p_new, p_new=(1-A)p. (4.3) Let S be the positive generating expression G_++Phi already derived from the actual R coefficient. Its output coordinates are U=BC,V=A/C. The canonical relation on the constraint UV=AB is exp(S_a)=p_out,2/p, exp(S_b)=p_out,1/r, exp(S_c)=p_out,1/p_out,2. (4.4) Here derivatives are in log A,log B,log C. Substitution of the exact contiguity symbols gives p_out,1=Ar/(Cx), p_out,2=(BC/x)*(1-A)(1-x^2/A) /((1-A/C)(1-x^2C/A))*p, C=1/(1-e_1 f_2). (4.5) The last equality follows on cancelling the common factors in the third equation of (4.4); equivalently r(C-1)=C P(A)p. It is not a guessed holonomy map. Write d=1-e_1 f_2. In physical coordinates the resulting map R is K'_1=K_2 d, K'_2=K_1/d, f'_1=K_1 f_2/d, e'_2=e_1/(K_2 d), e'_1=(d e_2+e_1(dK_2-K_2^(-1)))/K_1, f'_2=K_2(d f_1+f_2(d/K_1-K_1)). (4.6) The inverse is also derived from the negative crossing symbol. Writing c=1-(K_1/K_2)e_2 f_1, it is K'_1=K_2 c, K'_2=K_1/c, e'_1=K_1 e_2, f'_2=f_1/K_2, f'_1=f_1+f_2/K_1-f_1/(K_2^2 c), e'_2=K_2 e_1+e_2-K_1^2 e_2/c. (4.7) All equations are rational identities on their specified open charts. The symbolic audit derives both (4.6) and (4.7) from their respective generating relations and checks that they compose to the identity. ## 5. A matrix proof that this is meridian holonomy Define two triangular matrices and a determinant-one matrix by b_+(K,e)=[ K e ], b_-(K,f)=[ 1 0 ], [ 0 1 ] [-Kf K ] G=b_-^(-1)b_+=[ K e ]. [ Kf K^(-1)+ef ] The crossing map satisfies three exact factorizations: b'_(+,2)b'_(+,1)=b_(+,2)b_(+,1), b'_(-,2)b'_(-,1)=b_(-,2)b_(-,1), b'_(+,2)b'_(-,1)=b_(-,2)b_(+,1). (5.1) The last follows immediately from the four simple entries of (4.6); the other two are the preserved coproducts. Direct substitution proves all three. The map also swaps the two Casimirs K+K^(-1)+ef. For two strands define H_1=G_1, H_2=b_(-,1)^(-1)G_2 b_(-,1). Equations (5.1) imply H'_2=H_1, H'_1=H_1^(-1)H_2 H_1. (5.2) For example H'_2=(b'_(-,2)b'_(-,1))^(-1)b'_(+,2)b'_(-,1) =b_(-,1)^(-1)b_(+,1)=H_1. The total product H_2H_1 is preserved, which gives the other equality. This proves the Hurwitz/Wirtinger conjugation rule by matrix multiplication. For b strands, set B_(-,j)=b_(-,j)...b_(-,1) and H_j=B_(-,j-1)^(-1)G_j B_(-,j-1). (5.3) The same calculation applies to adjacent strands; later prefix products do not change because their two factors have the same product in (5.1). Hence (5.3) intertwines every mixed braid word with the ordinary conjugation action on meridians. Composition uses the order in which the actual operator acts: rightmost factor first when a braid is written as a matrix product. The conjugation action uses that same convention. This map is birational, with an explicit inverse. Given H_j, let P_j=H_j...H_1. When its upper-left entries are nonzero put B_-(P)=[ 1 0 ], B_+(P)=[ P_11 P_12 ], [-P_21 P_11] [ 0 1 ] so P=B_-(P)^(-1)B_+(P). Recover b_(+,j)=B_+(P_j)B_+(P_(j-1))^(-1), and the analogous b_(-,j). In particular K_j=(P_j)_11/(P_(j-1))_11. This proves the inverse, rather than only counting dimensions. The braid relations now follow from (5.2). On any common regular chart these are identities of schemes, including Artin test rings; the rational identities clear to polynomial identities with unit denominators. No reducedness or isolated-critical-point assertion is needed. The actual meridians in this convention are mu_j=-H_j. Their traces are M+M^(-1), since x=-M at the classical symbol. The central minus sign preserves (5.2). The cut's unit vector p_new=1 gives f=1-A,e=(1-x^2/A)/x, and directly G (1,1)^t=x^(-1)(1,1)^t. (5.4) Thus it selects the peripheral eigenflag 1, with meridian eigenvalue M^(-1). The inverse is explicit; this flag must not be silently called the M-eigenflag when marking holonomies. ## 6. The actual cut's critical locus and a nonempty geometric chart Close strands 2,...,b by the actual pivotal trace and use the constant vector and normalized average on the first strand. For internal variables the exponentiated stationary equations are precisely equality of the closed position and momentum coordinates. At the two cut endpoints the constant boundary vectors give p_new,in=p_new,out=1. The pivotal factor on a closed strand is x^(1-N)Q^(a(N-1)). With h=Log Q, N=2pi*i/h, its leading logarithmic expression is 2pi*i(log A-log x). Its internal momentum multiplier is one. The residual writhe factor x^(w(N-1)) depends only on x. Thus these factors do not change the exponentiated internal stationary equations. Their logarithmic branches and peripheral derivatives remain part of the period. Preservation of the product of K's forces the two cut positions to agree once all the other strands have closed. Equation (4.3) then makes their physical e,f agree as well. Consequently the critical equations are exactly R_beta(z)=z, with the first meridian eigenflag equal to 1. (6.1) Conversely every point of this open fixed locus satisfies the critical equations and the cut boundary conditions. Under (5.3), (6.1) is the familiar presentation <mu_1,...,mu_b | beta(mu_j)=mu_j> of the braid-closure knot group, with the fixed eigenflag. This presentation follows by applying van Kampen to the braid strands and identifying their endpoints: at each crossing (5.2) is exactly the understrand meridian relation. Thus we have an identification of open critical schemes with framed, augmented representation schemes. This is not yet a claim about the classical symbol of a minimal *summed* meridian operator. There is a useful uniform nonemptiness result. Fix any such representation whose meridians are noncentral, and its selected meridian eigenvector w. This includes the complete hyperbolic representation. Choose a covector alpha with alpha(w)=1, then a vector v with alpha(v)=1. In the basis (v,w-v), the chosen flag is 1. For every partial product P in every stage of the finite braid word, its upper-left entry is alpha(Pv). For one strand in such a stage, e_j=0 exactly when alpha is a left eigenline of H_j. Avoid these finitely many covector lines. Also f_j=0 exactly when v is an eigenline of P_(j-1)^(-1)P_j. These matrices are conjugate to a noncentral meridian, so again there are only finitely many forbidden lines. The conditions alpha(Pv)=0 and v=w exclude finitely many additional points of the affine line alpha(v)=1. None of alpha(Pv)=0 vanishes identically there: P is invertible. One can therefore avoid all of them simultaneously. This proves that all K_j,e_j,f_j can be made nonzero at every stage, in a frame respecting the actual cut flag. The positive and negative crossing denominators then remain nonzero. Moreover all five shapes in (3.5) avoid 0 and 1: the input conditions exclude A,B in {1,x^2}, the output conditions exclude the corresponding U,V, and e_1 f_2!=0 (respectively e_2 f_1!=0) excludes C=1. This asserts nondegenerate tetrahedron shapes; it does not assert positivity or distinctness of every pair of nonadjacent developed octahedron vertices. Thus every hyperbolic knot's complete representation lies in the actual cut state's complex, exponentiated critical locus on a chart with nondegenerate tetrahedra. A chosen such frame works on a Zariski open neighborhood of the point in the augmented representation scheme. No alternatingness is needed. ## 7. The framing torsor is explicitly split Over the irreducible augmented character locus, fixing the selected flag to 1 leaves the group B_1=Stab_(PGL_2)(1), a two-dimensional split Borel group. It acts freely on framed representations because their projective centralizer is trivial. Its orbits are precisely the framed realizations of one augmented character. The full framed locus is a B_1 torsor; the regular critical chart is an open subset of that torsor. The open chart is not asserted to be preserved by every B_1 element. It can be split algebraically. For a non-elementary representation choose fixed group words g,h such that p, rho(g)p, rho(h)p are distinct. Send this ordered triple to (1,0,infinity). The unique fractional transformation is rational in its three points and gives a section on their nondegenerate locus. If necessary choose the two words so this frame is also regular in Section 6: the infinite projective orbit is Zariski dense in P^1, its square is dense in the space of pairs, and the good frames form a nonempty open subset. The words can then be held fixed near the complete character. Equivalently, over the augmented function field H^1(k,B_1)=0. After sending the flag to infinity, B_1 is G_a semidirect G_m. For a Galois cocycle, Hilbert 90 kills its multiplicative part. Its remaining additive cocycle b_gamma is killed by averaging: a=(1/|G|)sum_gamma b_gamma satisfies b_gamma=a-gamma(a). This is a proof of the splitting, not an assumed rigidity claim for the quantum period. It removes an ordinary framing torsor; it does not kill a horizontal difference-extension class or the central Bloch regulator. ## 8. A global boundary wedge and complete-frame regulator rigidity Let beta_beta be the sum of (3.2)--(3.3) over the braid, with their actual input/output variables. Work rationally in F^* tensor Q and use delta[z]=z wedge (1-z). Let S be the total classical generating expression, including the retained Gaussian factors. Write x for the common meridian coordinate, and put L_intr=exp((1/2)[partial_(Log x) S]_critical). (8.1) This is the intrinsic conjugate coordinate from the actual meridian q-shift: h=Log Q is twice its step. Initially this is on the logarithmic/root cover specified by the coefficients. The derivative in (8.1) holds internal coordinates fixed before restricting to the exponentiated critical equations; a global flattening for a critical primitive is not being assumed. No topological longitude identification is built into its name. The subsequent [exact longitude proof](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md) now supplies that identification. Its finite meridian insertion fixes the square-root sign by an integer-position coboundary. The knot's eigenvector transport then proves that (M,L_intr), with M=-x classically, is the preferred peripheral pair on the M-eigenflag. The actual cut uses the opposite M^(-1)-flag, whose longitude eigenvalue is L_intr^(-1). There is an exact rational wedge identity on the critical locus: delta beta_beta=-2 x wedge L_intr. (8.2) Here is the proof. For one crossing, write its five shapes as monomials z_j in A,B,C,x with signs eps_j. If X_i denotes one of these four multiplicative generators, then delta beta=-sum_i X_i wedge exp(partial_i Phi). The Gaussian G has symmetric quadratic coefficient matrix in their logarithms, so sum_i X_i wedge exp(partial_i G)=0. Its constant signs are torsion and disappear rationally. Hence Phi may be replaced by S=G+Phi in this identity. The generating relations (4.4) then give exactly delta beta=A wedge p_in,1+B wedge p_in,2 -U wedge p_out,1-V wedge p_out,2 -x wedge exp(partial_(Log x) S). For the inverse crossing use U=B/C,V=AC and S_c=Log p_out,2-Log p_out,1; the same formula results. Internal leg terms cancel. Closed legs have equal positions and momenta, and the two cut momenta are 1. The last term is -2x wedge L_intr by (8.1). This proves (8.2). It is the previous boundary coefficient -1/2 in m=x^2,l=L_intr^2. The wedge alone does not fix the marked longitude. The subsequent vector-transport proof linked above fixes its flag, sign and framing. At the complete color x=-1, (8.2) is zero in the rational wedge. Thus beta_beta is a Bloch class on this critical component. Applying the directly proved Bloch--Wigner differential shows d D(beta_beta)=0 along its framing torsor. The good complex frame locus is a nonempty Zariski open subset of the connected rational group B_1, hence connected. Its regulator value is independent of the regular frame. This is an explicit classical rigidity argument for the *actual crossing* sum. The [crossing fundamental-cycle proof](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) now identifies this complete rational Bloch class with the marked idealized fundamental class, and hence the constant with Vol(M). It gives a three-five-term certificate, a four-tetrahedron diagram face table, and the degree-one peripheral check. This supplies the classical datum that the wedge alone did not fix. The quantum source and selected period must additionally be transported, and its exponential norm established. Existence of the critical component does not show that its period coefficient is nonzero or that other components do not cancel it. ## 9. Coverage, verification, and the remaining target Coverage checked after deriving these formulas: * [Kashaev--Reshetikhin, braiding for quantum gl_2](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0410182) covers holonomy braiding at roots of unity. We reconstruct the rational map from the actual crossing symbols and prove its conjugation rule by (5.1). * [McPhail-Snyder--Reshetikhin, cyclic modules and flat connections](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02354) states a four-holonomy-dilogarithm factorization. It is coverage of a comparison framework, not a theorem identifying its geometric-character invariant with the original cut period. * [Cho, existence of an optimistic-limit solution](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.0525) covers critical equations associated with representations. The existence statement here therefore carries no novelty claim. Its boundary and meridian conventions are instead derived from (1.1)--(2.3) of the actual literature state. The [audit](../experiments/audit_marked_braid_holonomy.py) and [results](../experiments/marked_braid_holonomy_results.json) check both symbolic generating maps, their inverse, all three matrix factorizations, the exact Hurwitz rule, and the cut flag. They check 300 mixed braid words, each of length twelve, in three finite fields, together with braid relations and Gauss reconstruction. At ten levels, including even and composite ones, they check the boundary vectors, rank-one E correction, cyclic defect and nilpotency, and dimension ratio. Thirty actual cut contractions at levels 2 through 6 give the same period under the boundary/basis change. A three-field algebraic figure-eight calibration checks a nondegenerate geometric critical chart. A high-precision complex calibration checks the regulator's sign and frame independence against its two-regular- tetrahedron value in three frames. These are validations, not the general mechanism. The original volume conjecture remains the target. This note supplies an actual-state geometric critical locus, its framing torsor, and a global rational Bloch boundary formula; the next note identifies its complete fundamental-class lift. A global quantum source comparison, the minimal meridian operator's geometric classical factor, and the selected volume limit remain unproved. The subsequent [regular holonomy-braiding note](regular_holonomy_braiding.md) derives a quantum counterpart of this classical transport. It gives rational generator formulas, the full unrestricted root-center map, and a regular module/intertwiner line through the actual color. Their checked center map is the inverse map (4.7), as required by pullback. Its pointed determinant normalization preserves the original zero-framed knot period after the explicit twist compensation. A global relative gluing source and its selected regulator period remain unproved.

title: Cyclotomic Mellin functions are fixed by bounded quantum jets
text: # Cyclotomic Mellin functions are fixed by bounded quantum jets Research proof, 27 October 2026. In the actual Fourier--Mellin polarization, a bounded number of quantum jet levels fixes the whole rational root function, not only a selected scalar multiple of it. The normal-order bound is independent of N. The source, formal starting lattice and cyclotomic pole lattice are all necessary inputs. This extends the existing [bounded-jet operator-period reconstruction](all_level_a_period.md) from one coefficient to the whole rational Mellin fiber. The sparse valuation and recurrence arguments are the same ones; no novelty is claimed for them. The new scope is arbitrary competing root sections, without a rank, semisimplicity, scalar-ratio or minimality hypothesis. The result is uniqueness, not a construction of a regulator section satisfying those exact data or an estimate of its residue. In particular it does not prove the volume conjecture. ## 1. The actual operator, source and pole lattice Use the specified actual Q-only color recurrence P=sum_(j=0)^d a_j(Q,Y)T^j, TY=QYT, sum_j a_j(Q,Q^r) C_(r+j)(Q)=0, r>=1, with d>=1, a_0 a_d!=0, and Laurent-polynomial coefficients after one fixed denominator clearing. Retain the actual colors, source and conventions of [the Fourier--Mellin construction](fourier_mellin_actual_source.md). Let A be the Q-exponent span, D the Y-exponent span, and s the number of collected monomials of a_d. Choose a fixed n_0>=d+A+1, B=D(s-1), k=B+1. The actual formal series and its exact source are Z(Q,X)=sum_(r>=n_0) C_r(Q) X^r, P^M Z=mathcalB(Q,X), P^M=sum_(j,ell) a_(j,ell)(Q) Q^(-ell*j) X^(-j) S^ell, S f(X)=f(QX). The Laurent polynomial mathcalB is fixed by the d actual colors C_(n_0),...,C_(n_0+d-1). Its full quantum jets are retained, rather than just its value at one root. At Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N), the actual root section Z_N is rational. Let p_<(N,X)=sum_(r=1)^(n_0-1) C_r(Q_N) X^r. The exact color periodicity proved in [the cyclotomic residue theorem](cyclotomic_mellin_residue.md) gives the pole lattice (1-X^N)[Z_N(X)+p_<(N,X)] in X C[X], of degree at most N. (1) It also gives Z_N in X^(n_0)C[[X]] and K_N=Res_infinity Z_N(X)dX/X. Condition (1) is more than having simple finite cyclotomic poles: it fixes the allowed polynomial part at infinity as well. ## 2. Finite reconstruction theorem For all sufficiently large N, let W_N be a rational function with W_N in X^(n_0)C[[X]], (1-X^N)[W_N+p_<] in X C[X], degree<=N. (2) Put Q=Q_N(1+epsilon), R_k=C[epsilon]/(epsilon^k). Suppose there is a polynomial truncation Wtilde_N=sum_(r=n_0)^N w_r(epsilon)X^r, w_r in R_k, w_r(0)=[X^r]W_N, whose source equation has the correct coefficients in the finite window [X^m](P^M Wtilde_N-mathcalB)=0 in R_k, n_0-d<=m<=N-d. (3) Then exactly W_N=Z_N. In particular its residue is the original Kashaev value K_N. There are k=B+1 quantum levels in (3): orders zero through B. The number of X coefficients grows with N, but the required quantum normal order does not. No bounded X-degree is assumed for higher actual quantum jets; only the indicated finite window is used. Truncating the actual formal Z at X^N supplies one such lift, since omitted higher coefficients cannot enter that window. ### Proof Subtract that actual truncation and write its coefficients as e_r(epsilon), with e_r=0 for r<n_0. Coefficient comparison in the exact Fourier ordering gives sum_(j=0)^d a_j(Q,Q^m)e_(m+j)=0 in R_k. (4) Indeed the factor Q^(-ell*j) in the Fourier transform cancels the j-part of the shift on the exponent m+j, leaving Q^(ell*m). No square-root or index offset is suppressed here. For r>=n_0 set h_(r-d)(Q)=a_d(Q,Q^(r-d)), mu_(r-d)=ord_(Q=Q_N) h_(r-d), M_r=sum_(t=n_0)^r mu_(t-d). All h_(r-d) are nonzero Laurent polynomials: r-d>A prevents collisions of distinct Q^uY^v monomials after Y=Q^(r-d). Each has at most s monomials, hence its nonzero-root vanishing order is at most s-1 by the logarithmic-derivative Vandermonde argument already proved in the operator-period note. The points Q_N^(r-d), n_0<=r<=N, are distinct. For all large N the Laurent polynomial a_d(Q_N,Y) is not identically zero; it has at most D nonzero roots. Thus M_N<=D(s-1)=B. (5) These statements exclude only finitely many levels of the fixed coefficient field. They do not assume regular propagation at every color. Induct in (4), with m=r-d. All earlier error coefficients are divisible by epsilon^(k-M_(r-1)). The other operator coefficients are regular in epsilon. Since h_(r-d) is a unit times epsilon^mu_(r-d), it follows that e_r in epsilon^(k-M_r) R_k. (6) This remains valid in the truncated ring: the annihilator of epsilon^mu consists of epsilon^(k-mu) multiples, with at least the divisibility claimed in (6). By (5), k-M_r>=1 through r=N. Hence every root coefficient through X^N agrees. Subtract the two pole conditions (1)--(2). The polynomial (1-X^N)(W_N-Z_N) has degree<=N, and all its coefficients through that degree are zero by (6) and the common starting lattice. It vanishes identically. This proves the theorem. ## 3. A literal unknot example shows why root data are insufficient The actual unknot has C_r(Q)=1. The following nonminimal operator is nonetheless an actual all-level annihilator: P=(T-Q)[(1-QY)T-(1-Y)] =(1-Q^2Y)T^2+(1+Q)(QY-1)T+Q(1-Y). (7) The inner bracket applied to 1 is (1-Q)Y; the outer T-Q kills it. Here D=1, s=2, so B=1 and k=2. Its exact Fourier operator and source, for any fixed admissible n_0, are P^M=X^(-2)(1-X)(1-QX)(1-S), Z(Q,X)=X^(n_0)/(1-X), mathcalB=X^(n_0-2)[1-Q^(n_0)+(Q^(n_0)-Q)X]. (8) At the root, for every constant lambda, W_N=Z_N+lambda X^N/(1-X^N) (9) has the same affine source, starting lattice, prescribed prefix and cyclotomic pole lattice. It has residue 1+lambda instead of 1. This is an alternative root section of an ACTUAL unknot operator, not a different knot invariant. No nonzero lambda in (9) has the first normal lift (3). One way to see this is (4) at m=N-2: its earlier errors are zero, and h_(N-2)=1-Q^N has a simple zero, so the first normal equation forces e_N(0)=0. There is also a whole-function obstruction, not just the coefficient argument. Write U=X^N, f(U)=lambda U/(1-U). After canceling the nonzero rational prefactor in (8), a first-order homogeneous lift would require (1-S_0)g_1=N U f'(U), S_0 g(X)=g(Q_N X). The cyclic average of its left side is zero, whereas that of its right side is N^2 U f'(U), nonzero if lambda!=0. This argument is valid in C((X)) as well as in C(X). Thus the required two jet levels are genuinely necessary in this actual example. Root operator, affine source and pole lattice by themselves do not determine the residue. ## 4. Relation to the selected-line and regulator questions [The selected Mellin-line theorem](actual_mellin_normal_source_rigidity.md) uses the observable source quotient to remove central scalar multipliers at first normal order, without semisimplicity. The present result also handles additions in the homogeneous source-kernel, as illustrated by (9); it uses the larger fixed jet budget and the exact cyclotomic pole lattice. The theorem gives a finite exact target for a proposed whole comparison. Such a candidate still must supply (2)--(3), with the actual source and coefficients through the stated orders. An algebraic classical optimizer or a local geometric Gaussian does not yet supply that lift or its global pole behavior. No hyperbolic-volume growth follows from uniqueness alone. Verification: [script](../experiments/audit_mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness.py) and [results](../experiments/mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness_results.json). The [independent proof audit](mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness_independent_audit.md) checks the finite Fourier window, truncated-ring valuation induction, pole numerator reconstruction and sharp actual unknot obstruction.

title: Independent audit of bounded-jet cyclotomic Mellin uniqueness
text:
# Independent audit of bounded-jet cyclotomic Mellin uniqueness 27 October 2026. The proof of [the whole-function uniqueness theorem](mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness.md) passes independently. Its finite X-window, uniform quantum-jet budget, and cyclotomic numerator condition are sufficient as written. No semisimplicity, minimal operator, or scalar-ratio hypothesis is needed. ## 1. The finite window really is closed In the exact Fourier ordering, a monomial \(X^{-j}S^\ell\) takes the coefficient \(w_{m+j}\) to power \(X^m\), with factor \(Q^{\ell m}\) after the retained \(Q^{-\ell j}\). Since \(0\le j\le d\) and \(m\le N-d\), only coefficients through \(w_N\) enter. Hence a truncation at \(X^N\) is enough for the entire indicated window. Negative S-powers cause no change to this statement: they rescale the same X exponent. Subtracting the actual truncation therefore gives precisely \[ \sum_{j=0}^d a_j(Q,Q^m)e_{m+j}=0 \quad mod\epsilon^{B+1}. \] The starting lattice sets every \(e_r\) below \(n_0\) to zero. There is no unmentioned assumption on the X-degree of higher quantum-normal coefficients. ## 2. The singular-step budget and truncated valuation argument After one fixed coherent denominator clearing, \(a_d\) is Laurent polynomial in \(Q,Y\). Its Q-span \(A\) implies \(a_d(Q,Q^m)
e0\) for \(m>A\): equality of two collected exponents \(u+mv\) with different \(v\)'s would force \(m\le A\). Its at most \(s\) remaining monomials have nonzero-root multiplicity at most \(s-1\), by the logarithmic-derivative Vandermonde determinant. For all sufficiently large levels, \(a_d(Q_N,Y)
e0\) as a Laurent polynomial in \(Y\). The visited Y-values are distinct; there are at most \(D\) roots on them. Thus the sum of all leading vanishing orders through coefficient \(N\) is at most \(B=D(s-1)\). The excluded levels include any zeros or poles of fixed Q-scalar clearing factors and any specialization where all Y-coefficients of \(a_d\) vanish. There are only finitely many such root values. No uniform lower bound on their nonzero numerical magnitudes is needed. The truncated-ring step is valid despite zero divisors. If \(k=B+1\), \(h=\epsilon^\mu u\) with \(u\) a unit, and \(he\in\epsilon^tR_k\), \(t\le k\), then \[ e\in\epsilon^{t-\mu}R_k\qquad(t\ge\mu). \] The additional annihilator \(\epsilon^{k-\mu}R_k\) is already contained in that asserted ideal. Applying this at each step gives \(e_r\in\epsilon^{k-M_r}R_k\), so every root coefficient through \(X^N\) agrees. In particular no singular step was divided at its root value. For the finitely many fixed initial colors the leading trajectory polynomials are units at all sufficiently large roots, as suggested in the outline. The written proof is stronger: the total budget would handle their vanishing as well, whenever its other hypotheses hold. ## 3. The whole pole lattice is the necessary last step Subtracting the two cyclotomic conditions gives \[ H(X)=(1-X^N)(W_N-Z_N)\in\mathbb C[X],\qquad \deg H\le N . \] Both expansions have the same starting lattice and agree through power \(N\). Thus every coefficient of \(H\) through its maximal degree vanishes, proving \(W_N=Z_N\). Simple cyclotomic poles alone would not suffice: an arbitrary polynomial part of higher degree could remain invisible to the finite window. The stated degree bound and prescribed low prefix are therefore substantive source-lattice data. The residue at infinity is then fixed, including the case that the actual Kashaev value vanishes. ## 4. The exact actual-unknot sharpness example checks Direct Ore multiplication gives the displayed actual operator \[ (T-Q)[(1-QY)T-(1-Y)]. \] The inner bracket applied to the actual color \(1\) is \((1-Q)Y\), which the outer factor kills. Its exact Fourier transform is \(X^{-2}(1-X)(1-QX)(1-S)\). Applying this to \(X^{n_0}/(1-X)\) gives exactly the stated finite source. The leading trajectory is \(1-Q^r\); only \(r=N\) vanishes in the reconstruction range, and it has multiplicity one. The alternative root section \(\lambda X^N/(1-X^N)\) is shift-invariant and preserves the affine root source and all the stated root pole/prefix data. Its residue contribution is \(+\lambda\). Its first normal would require \[ (1-S_0)g_1=NUf'(U),\qquad f(U)=\lambda U/(1-U). \] The cyclic average kills the left side and gives \(N^2Uf'(U)
e0\) on the right for \(\lambda
e0\). This works in the formal Laurent field as well as the rational field. The two required jet levels in this actual example are therefore sharp. The proof and the saved exact diagnostics support the stated uniqueness theorem. They do not construct a regulator candidate in the same pole and source lattice, establish its bounded quantum lift, or estimate the selected residue. Those remain the geometric comparison and volume questions.

title: An actual meridian source on the tensor Casimir cover
text: # An actual meridian source on the tensor Casimir cover Research note, 26 October 2026. This derives an inhomogeneous meridian equation from the literature ADO crossing itself. Its source is a specified spectral projector, with the full factor 1+M^(-2N). The coincident spectral directions at completeness are the actual meridian confluence, not a separately chosen infinitesimal model. Their source residue is a fixed rank-one cup/cap operator. The result is local to two tensor factors. It is not an identification of the full knot quantum-A operator with its geometric A-polynomial, nor a proof of the selected regulator norm. The connection constructed below still has to be assembled through the whole colored network. ## 1. The fixed operator and its generic meridian spectrum Use q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), N>=2, and the actual ADO color x=-M/q. Put Y=M^2, U=Y^N=M^(2N). On V(x), the matrices E,F,K and checked crossing B_N(M) are exactly those in [the semicyclic source proof](semicyclic_carry_braiding.md), restricted here to F^N=0. In particular K v_a=xQ^(-a)v_a, F v_a=v_(a+1), F v_(N-1)=0, and E v_a=e_a(x)v_(a-1). Let Omega be the actual tensor Casimir, E_tot=E tensor K+1 tensor E, F_tot=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F, Omega=rho^2 F_tot E_tot+q K_tot+q^(-1)K_tot^(-1). For generic M its N distinct Casimir nodes and crossing values are c_j(Y)=q^(-2j-1)Y+q^(2j+1)Y^(-1), lambda_j(Y)=nu_j Y^(-j), nu_j=(-1)^j q^(j(j+1)), 0<=j<N. (1.1) Each component has dimension N. Here is an elementary verification. At total degree j write the highest vector as h_j=sum_(a=0)^j b_a v_a tensor v_(j-a), b_0=1. Its E-equation is b_(a+1)/b_a=-e_(j-a)(x)/ (e_(a+1)(x) x Q^(-(j-a-1))). For generic x the denominators are nonzero. Multiplication gives b_j=(-1)^j x^(-j)Q^(j(j-1)/2). The defining finite R is triangular, so the coefficient of v_0 tensor v_j in B h_j comes only from its zero-th term on v_j tensor v_0. Thus lambda_j=(-1)^j x^(-2j)Q^(j(j-1)/2)=nu_jY^(-j). The N descendants F_tot^r h_j are nonzero generically: the E F^r recurrence has no zero coefficient for 0<r<N. F_tot^N=0 by the root q-binomial identity. Their different Casimir nodes imply a direct sum, and the dimensions total N^2. This proves the spectrum and complete decomposition without importing a tensor-decomposition theorem. Define T_0(z)=2,T_1(z)=z,T_(n+1)=zT_n-T_(n-1). Since T_n(a+a^(-1))=a^n+a^(-n), (1.1) proves product_j(z-c_j(Y))=P_(N,U)(z), P_(N,U)(z)=T_N(z)+U+U^(-1). (1.2) Thus the actual local spectral algebra is A_(N,U)=C(U)[z]/P_(N,U)(z). It splits after the specified root cover Y^N=U. The polynomial r(Y,z) of degree less than N with r(Y,c_j)=lambda_j satisfies B_N(M)=r(Y,Omega). (1.3) The scalar conventions are explicit. At M=1 the usual highest-weight quantum-group R in the earlier crossing calculation has checked matrix lambda_0 B_N(1), with lambda_0=q^((N-1)^2/2). The ADO crossing used here is already B_N(1); its original pivot, zero-framing twist and full modified dimension are not changed. ## 2. The affine meridian equation and its full peripheral source Let sigma(Y)=QY and sigma(z)=z on the split spectral algebra. The nodes obey c_j(QY)=c_(j-1)(Y), with indices modulo N. For the values in (1.1), lambda_(j+1)(QY)=-Y^(-1)lambda_j(Y), j<N-1, lambda_0(QY)=1, -Y^(-1)lambda_(N-1)(Y)=-U^(-1). Let E_(N-1)(Y,z) be the spectral idempotent with value one at c_(N-1) and zero at the other nodes. Interpolation therefore proves the exact equation sigma(r)=-Y^(-1)r+(1+U^(-1)) E_(N-1). (2.1) This source has not been chosen to obtain a desired period: the exceptional last component is forced by the actual highest-weight eigenvalues. The generic idempotent is E_(N-1)=product_(j=0)^(N-2) (z-c_j(Y))/(c_(N-1)(Y)-c_j(Y)). (2.2) The homogeneous cyclic norm is exactly Norm_sigma(-Y^(-1))=-U^(-1), (2.3) because Q^(N(N-1)/2)=(-1)^(N-1), at both parities. Thus 1+U^(-1) is precisely 1 minus that norm. It becomes two at completeness, but it must first be retained as a whole function multiplying (2.2). There are two different norms here. The Casimir-algebra norm of r is Norm_spec(r)=(product_j nu_j)Y^(-N(N-1)/2), det B_N=Norm_spec(r)^N. (2.4) The root phase product_j nu_j is retained. Equation (2.3) instead concerns the cyclic meridian transport. Iterating (2.1) gives an affine monodromy with homogeneous block -U^(-1) and source s=(1+U^(-1))r. Away from U=-1 the cyclic resolvent reconstructs the unique solution r. These are identities before any polar specialization. At a resonance or a node collision a displayed zero times a projector pole cannot be evaluated separately. ## 3. A genuine matrix meridian comparison, including parity There is an explicit operator realization of sigma in (2.1). Let H(M) have columns F_tot^r h_j(M), ordered by j and then r. Let P send label j to j+1 modulo N, keeping r fixed. Put G(M)=H(qM) P H(M)^(-1). (3.1) The highest K-root of component j at M is x^2 Q^(-j). It equals that of component j+1 at qM. The descendants use the same fixed F normalization. Consequently G intertwines all three actual total E,F,K operators. In particular it keeps the Casimir observable z fixed. Equations (1.1) and (3.1) give the actual matrix identity G(M)^(-1) B_N(qM) G(M) =-Y^(-1)B_N(M) +(1+U^(-1)) E_(N-1)(Y,Omega). (3.2) This is not merely equality of spectra. H and G are specified rational matrices on the generic color chart; no unrelated normalization is chosen at each shift. The meridian cover also keeps its sign. After N shifts, M becomes -M. If S_2 is the sign matrix (-1)^a on the second factor, the highest-vector recurrence gives H(-M)=S_2 H(M) diag_(j,r)((-1)^j). (3.3) Thus the N-step matrix transport is H(-M)H(M)^(-1), with both its color parity and spectral-sign unit retained. The 2N-step transport is identity. On the abstract Casimir algebra (2.1) already uses Y, whose shift has order N; forgetting the parity on the actual tensor module would require the explicit identification (3.3). The subsequent [intrinsic cut and meridian atlas](intrinsic_cut_and_meridian_atlas.md) assembles these maps on a generic even-strand braid using explicit centralizer transitions and preserves the full selected cut. It does not construct the integral geometric triangulation comparison. ## 4. Its complete spectral jet is the actual meridian confluence Write u=Log M near M=1. Pair j with l=N-1-j, and put h=2j+1<N. Then nu_l=nu_j and exactly c_j-c_l=-(q^h-q^(-h))(Y-Y^(-1)), lambda_j=nu_j M^(-2j), lambda_l=nu_j M^(-2l). The confluent divided difference is therefore [(lambda_j-lambda_l)/(c_j-c_l)]_(M=1) =-nu_j(N-1-2j)/(2(q^h-q^(-h))). (4.1) The double point is an honest finite flat meridian algebra. In the pair factor, eta=z-c_j(M) satisfies eta(eta+c_j-c_l)=0. (4.2) At completeness it becomes eta^2=0. The unit r specializes to nu_j plus the coefficient (4.1) times eta. Replacing its value-and-divided-difference interpolation rows by the confluent rows gives an invertible Hermite Vandermonde. Thus the coefficients of r are regular at M=1. Equation (1.3) specializes to the earlier crossing polynomial, including its nilpotent part. For odd N the node with 2j+1=N is simple and has only its value condition. No inverse of two modulo an even N is used. This supplies a meridian derivation of the same jet that the earlier proof obtained by varying q. In particular it identifies a specific actual spectral jet with the meridian collision; the internal carry parameter epsilon and the auxiliary source coordinate remain different data. ## 5. The polar source residue is the actual cup/cap Let c_0=q+q^(-1), and let e_0 be the idempotent of the double c_0 factor of P_(N,1). On the actual nilpotent tensor module write J_N=(Omega-c_0)e_0, J_N^2=0. (5.1) Let J_x be the actual self-duality matrix at the Kashaev color, (J_x)_(N-1-a,a)=q^(a^2), and g=K^(1-N). Use the existing cup and right cap to form cup=vec(J_x^(-t)), cap=vec(g J_x)^t, Pi_N=cup*cap. (5.2) Then exactly Pi_N^2=0, rank Pi_N=1, ptr_g(Pi_N)=I, J_N=(-1)^N rho^2 Pi_N. (5.3) Here is a proof of the last identity. At generic q the total degree-d Casimir characteristic polynomial has labels 0 through min(d,2N-2-d), by the highest-vector decomposition already proved in the preceding Casimir note. At this root, the node c_0 occurs with multiplicity two only at degree N-1, and with multiplicity one in every other degree. Hence J_N has rank at most one and is zero off degree N-1. Commutation with E_tot,F_tot then makes its image invariant. The invariant vector and covector spaces are one-dimensional, by simplicity and the actual self-duality of V_N. Thus J_N is a scalar multiple of the cup/cap in (5.2). The independently proved closing functional in [the Casimir trace calculation](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md#8-the-actual-closing-trace-is-a-spectral-jet-functional) gives ptr_K(J_N)=-rho^2 I.
