Thus W introduces only the old Vandermonde head units and a meridian monomial, not a new peripheral norm denominator. Its whole inverse is D_2 V inverse. The identity W(qM)D_rho=W(M), rho=q^(-ell), proves the revised whole matrix meridian equation with its original L insertion. Consequently arbitrary ordered operators and source/current maps transport by this basis change before any jets. The separate pure L path identity concerns the stated actual word and its covariantly transported insertion complex; it is not permission to hold an arbitrary M-dependent inserted coupon fixed under a meridian step. ## 3. Whole matrix connection and packet connection are different objects Direct differentiation gives \[ \Gamma_M=(D_MW)W^{-1}=\ell VJ_{head}V^{-1},\qquad \Gamma_Q=(D_QV)V^{-1}\quad(M\text{ fixed}), \] \[ D_M T^W=W(D_MT)W^{-1}+[\Gamma_M,T^W]. \] Thus the covariant derivative has sign D_M minus ad Gamma_M. The commutator's partial trace is zero ENTRYWISE on the first wire. Every mixed/normal derivative of the exact source identity is preserved by the product rule, including the actual M(q) chain rule. At the root V divided by sqrt N is unitary, so the full matrix connection has norm ell(N-1). This is a source frame estimate, not a bound on the actual crossing word. For a charge-zero fixed-input a the scalar packet instead has unwrapped representatives nu=a-c, c=0,...,N-1. Its matrix is \[ H_a=F_a\operatorname{diag}(M^{\ell\nu})F_a^{-1},\quad (F_a)_{j,c}=Q_N^{j(a-c)}. \] The nu=0 column is the all-ones vector. It follows exactly that H_a times ones is ones and Sigma H_a=Sigma. Cyclic shifts, normalized differences and their centered primitive are diagonal in that same root Fourier basis, so H_a commutes with them. For absolute M one the map is unitary; the distance to the zero-source cyclic current space is therefore unchanged AT THE SAME M. This does not compare the norms of different meridian states or turn the L insertion into a scalar longitude. The packet connection is A_a=ell F_a diag(a-c)F_a inverse, with zero source and constant mode and norm at most ell(N-1). It is not the full Gamma_M above. More explicitly, on the common Fourier-label space, for a<N-1, \[ A_{a+1}-A_a=\ell N\Pi_{a+1},\qquad H_{a+1}H_a^{-1}=I+(M^{\ell N}-1)\Pi_{a+1}, \tag{1} \] where Pi_(a+1) is the Fourier-mode projector with residue a+1. Only one unwrapped representative has changed by N. This proves why packets for different a cannot be silently identified through their residues. Charged/unwrapped tail modules retain their own independent alias powers and the full tensor map, as the note states. ## 4. Peripheral and alias powers remain whole The complete ratio is exactly \[ \frac{d_N(qM)}{d_N(M)} =q^{N-1}\frac{q^2M^2-1}{M^2-1} \frac{M^{2N}-1}{q^{2N}M^{2N}-1}. \] The formula follows from the original finite S_N ratio, with the same phase on the two sides. It is a canceled whole meromorphic germ; norm-zero numerator and denominator are not evaluated separately. At a root its generic-M reduction agrees with the known -q inverse peripheral gauge, but that reduction does not give its whole q-normal adapter. The independent alias V_eta=eta^N transforms by V_eta to (q^N)^(-ell)V_eta. At the actual root this is the sign (-1)^ell. A head window has only its zero multiple of N, so its constant coefficient is unchanged even on the antiperiodic grid. Unwrapped current tails can have other multiples, whose retained characters and normal derivatives cannot be omitted. The optional first-wire source formula also passes. Its coefficient M^(ell(a-c))-1 is precisely the quotient by the genuine head Cartan gap Q^(a-c)-1 times the actual D_K entry. The packet derivative signs, wrap M^(ell N), and polynomial source-row bounds are correct. They are an alternative source homotopy, not a substitute for the exact all-tensor invariance of the main second leg. ## 5. The geometric filter formulas have their exact conditional scope For p_hor=alpha p, alpha=M^ell, the coordinate density transforms as \[ G\frac p{(p-\lambda)^2}d\log p =\alpha G\frac{p_{hor}}{(p_{hor}-\alpha\lambda)^2} d\log p_{hor}. \] This extra factor alpha is necessary. It makes the finite-filter ratio alpha^N times [(1-lambda^N)/(1-alpha^N lambda^N)] squared, with the printed M derivative at one. The finite sampling identity on p^N=S has numerator N S lambda^(N-1); antiperiodic S=-1 therefore retains its minus sign. All these formulas pass. The proven Möbius/single-pole framing theorem is complete-M only. The horizontal gauge alone does not extend that theorem to general M. The current note correctly makes a marked lambda(M) branch conditional and does not identify its rational filter with the actual quantum source. Its singularities must be accounted for by the actual whole word/source correction, not hidden by this gauge. ## 6. The remaining Green residual is typed and nonzero in general With sigma_M I_h=L I_h and R_i=S_i I_h/I_h, one obtains sigma_M R_i/R_i=S_i L/L. Therefore \[ L\,d_{\sigma R,i}(f)=d_{R,i}(Lf) \] with exactly the displayed order. This is a genuine semilinear connection on the proper-array insertion/current complex. Full zero extension retains its boundary strata. After source pairing, multiplying an ordinary difference by L leaves the finite residual sum_s [L(s-e_i)-L(s)]H(s). It is not generally zero and does not become zero by substituting the critical longitude into the sum. Thus the theorem removes a real endpoint half-character and supplies a tame actual source transport. It does not prove a nonzero selected geometric quotient, kill actual zero-source currents in that quotient, or bound the selected regulator norm. Those are correctly stated as remaining source/word comparisons rather than normalization choices.

title: A macroscopic polynomial quantum-normal window for every fixed plat
text: # A macroscopic polynomial quantum-normal window for every fixed plat 28 October 2026. For an original knot presented as a fixed 2k-plat, ordinary-color quantum-normal jets are polynomially bounded throughout k(j-1)+1<=N. (1) The endpoint is INCLUDED. This follows from a one-sided angular positive-path interval and elementary polynomial differentiation; no derivative of a singular root path basis is taken. Thus the conclusion controls a macroscopic part of the actual pointed quantum-A source, not only finitely many small colors. It does not bound the remaining high-color packet or independent meridian derivatives of the root ADO state. ## 1. Exact original family and statement Let C_j(q) denote the ORIGINAL reduced, zero-framed ordinary integral color-j knot scalar. The ordinary pivot is K(q), with its matching ribbon twist. At q_N=exp(pi*i/N), j<N, its equality with the original reduced root state is the independently proved quotient/cabling comparison, with the actual half-Cartan and parity adapters retained. Off the root this note uses that ORDINARY integral family. It does not differentiate a frozen ADO pivot as though it were the same family. Fix the plat word and k. Its actual Laurent degree in the marked variable z=q^(1/2) obeys deg_Laurent C_j <=D_j<=C_word (j+1)^2. (2) For every fixed r>=1 there is a constant C_(word,r) such that, for all N and j>=1 satisfying (1), |partial_s^r C_j(q_N(1+s/N)) at s=0| <=C_(word,r) j^(k-1)(D_j+1)^(2r+1). (3) For r=0 the sharper bound is |C_j(q_N)|<=j^(k-1). In particular the right side of (3) is polynomial in N, for example C_(word,r) N^(k+4r+1). There is no level-parity or primality restriction. The same polynomial conclusion holds for the root normal coordinate Delta=1-q^(2N), q=q_N(1-Delta)^(1/(2N)), (4) and for the actual weighted colors d_j(q)=(q^(2j)-1)C_j(q), including their fixed-order jets. The constants can change with r and the word, but not N or j in this window. For k>=2, the endpoint of (1) is below N, so these are ordinary colors. The k=1 knot is the unknot, whose reduced scalar is one; its possible j=N endpoint is harmless and can instead be handled separately. ## 2. Positivity on the full one-sided angular interval Put m=j-1 and n=2km. The fundamental cable of this colored plat has n endpoints. Work in its VACUUM path space: nonnegative paths a_0=a_n=0, |a_(i+1)-a_i|=1. Every such path has maximum height at most n/2=km. This is the important improvement over the full trace path space, whose paths need not end at zero. On pi/(2N)<=theta<pi/N, q=exp(i theta), (5) condition (1) implies that all required weights mu_a=[a+1]_q=sin((a+1)theta)/sin theta, 0<=a<=km, are strictly positive. At the upper endpoint, mu_(km) is allowed to become zero if km+1=N. Positivity is only asserted strictly BELOW that endpoint. For completeness the elementary TL generator on this orthonormal path basis has, when a_(i-1)=a_(i+1)=a, the two-state matrix e_i[b,c]=sqrt(mu_b mu_c)/mu_a, b,c in {a-1,a+1}. The omitted height -1 has weight zero. Its nonzero eigenvalue is (mu_(a-1)+mu_(a+1))/mu_a=2cos theta. The same elementary adjacent calculation gives e_i e_(i+1)e_i=e_i; disjoint generators commute. The maximum-height states introduce no missing term: a neighbor of an editable middle height is at most km-1, so its two weights are within the stated finite vacuum range. Thus every elementary fundamental crossing B_i=q^(1/2)I-q^(-1/2)e_i (6) is unitary: its eigenvalues are q^(1/2) and -q^(-3/2). Negative crossings are its adjoints. These are the actual ordinary full-Cartan normalizations, not a changed braid operator. Jones--Wenzl recursion on each m-strand color block has positive denominators [1],...,[m], is selfadjoint, and gives an orthogonal projection onto the original color-j cable subspace. Its quantum trace is EXACTLY [m+1]=[j]. One direct induction uses f_m=f_(m-1)-([m-1]/[m])f_(m-1)e_(m-1)f_(m-1) and the ordinary partial trace, giving [2][m]-[m-1]=[m+1]. The actual generic cabling comparison follows from the explicit highest-weight embedding and the original R coproduct. Its proof in [the ordinary-color audit](actual_ordinary_color_comparison_audit.md) is algebraic BEFORE root specialization, so it applies throughout (5), where none of those denominators vanish. No root-only quotient has been analytically differentiated. ## 3. The original plat normalization and the improved bound A single actual colored cup has squared positive norm [j]: closing it against its adjoint evaluates precisely the quantum trace of its Jones--Wenzl projector. The k disjoint ordinary colored cups therefore have squared norm [j]^k. The actual output caps have the same norm. The required self-dual orientation and ribbon identifications retain their original signs and q monomials; on (5) these are unitary factors, not additional positive dimension factors. They stay in C_j(q), and their degree is included in (2). One can see the cup normalization directly in the orthonormal vacuum path model: one colored cup is sqrt([j]) times the unique length-2m mountain path. The k-cup source is [j]^(k/2) times the concatenation of those mountains. Every internal color projector fixes this source. The cabled braid is unitary and maps the prescribed color subspace to its actual corresponding output subspace. Consequently the raw ordinary colored plat scalar has absolute value at most [j]^k. The reduced KNOT scalar is the raw scalar divided by ONE [j]. This is its original cut/trace identity, not one division per cup or per strand. Hence throughout the CONTINUOUS interval (5), |C_j(exp(i theta))|<=[j]^(k-1)<=j^(k-1). (7) The last inequality follows from [j]=sum_(a=0)^(j-1)q^(j-1-2a) and positivity. The full zero-framing line has modulus one on this interval. Neither it nor any original pivotal factor is reset. At theta=pi/N, use continuity of the actual Laurent polynomial C_j. This includes equality in (1) even though the top path weight becomes zero. It is invalid to differentiate that singular path basis; the next step differentiates only a bounded POLYNOMIAL on the closed one-sided interval. This is why the endpoint is genuinely included. ## 4. An elementary quadratic Laurent-degree bound For clarity, (2) does not rely on a colored-Jones degree theorem. In an integral highest-weight color-j basis, the original universal R nilpotent coefficient is a Gaussian polynomial times a product of at most j-1 quantum integers and a power of q-q^(-1). Its divided-power denominator cancels in the Gaussian coefficient. The latter's Laurent degree is O(j^2), as follows by its finite Pascal recurrence. The Cartan exponent is a product of two weights of size at most j-1, and hence also has degree O(j^2). Both signs have the same degree bound. A fixed word adds only a fixed number of such degrees. The actual pivotal powers contribute O_word(j), and the matching ribbon framing contributes O_word(j^2). Use the reduced cut scalar, rather than introduce a division by [j]: it is a finite sum of these integral entries and pivots. Thus its Laurent support is contained in [-C_word(j+1)^2,C_word(j+1)^2] in z=q^(1/2). Summing paths cannot increase that support. This proves (2) with a fixed coarse word constant while retaining the half-root. ## 5. Endpoint differentiation without a cited Markov inequality Let z_N=q_N^(1/2) be its original marked branch. Put a=tan(pi/(8N)), t=a(x-1)/2, -1<=x<=1, z=z_N(1+i t)/(1-i t). The q-angle now runs exactly from pi/(2N) to pi/N. Define P(x)=(1+t^2)^D C_j(z^2), D=D_j. (8) It is a polynomial of degree at most 2D: multiplication clears every Laurent monomial's denominators. Since D a^2=O_word(1), (7) gives sup_[-1,1]|P|<=exp(D a^2)j^(k-1)<=C_word j^(k-1). (9) For any complex polynomial P of degree n, expand it as sum_(l=0)^n c_l T_l(x). The cosine integral for its Chebyshev coefficients gives |c_0|<=M and |c_l|<=2M, M=sup|P|. The elementary differential equation (1-x^2)T_l''-x T_l'+l^2 T_l=0 implies, at x=1, T_l^(r+1)(1)=(l^2-r^2)T_l^r(1)/(2r+1). Thus, for each FIXED r, |T_l^r(1)|<=C_r(l+1)^(2r), and |P^r(1)|<=C_r M(n+1)^(2r+1). (10) The derivatives of (1+t^2)^(-D) at x=1 have bounded fixed-order norms because D a^2=O_word(1). The angular chain rule costs at most C_r N^r. Applying (9)--(10) to (8) therefore proves |partial_theta^r C_j(exp(i theta)) at theta=pi/N| <=C_(word,r)N^r j^(k-1)(D_j+1)^(2r+1). (11) This is an endpoint estimate, so a two-sided positive arc is not needed. Finally q partial_q=(1/i)partial_theta on that angular curve. For q=q_N(1+s/N), the order-r operator is N^(-r) product_(l=0)^(r-1)(q partial_q-l). Its expansion uses only angular derivatives through r, and (11) gives (3). For (4) it is instead the fixed polynomial (-1)^r product_(l=0)^(r-1)((q partial_q)/(2N)-l), which has the same bound. Derivatives of q^(2j)-1 on either scale are bounded at fixed order since j<=N. This proves the weighted color statement too. ## 6. The entire low-color packet is bounded on a complex normal disk There is a useful strengthening of the fixed-jet assertion. Fix ANY A>4. Uniformly for every color satisfying (1), the ACTUAL entire ordinary family obeys |C_j(q_N exp(s/N))|<=C_(word,A)(D_j+1)j^(k-1) <=C_(word,A)N^(k+1), |s|<=2N^(-A). (12) No eigenframe, recurrence denominator, truncated Taylor polynomial or root color quotient is used on this disk. To prove (12), keep the same polynomial P in (8). The half-root ratio is now exp(s/(2N)), so its exact rational coordinate is t=-i tanh(s/(4N)), x=1+2t/a. Consequently |x-1|<=C|s|. For |x-1|<=d<1/4 the elementary formula T_l(x)=[(x+sqrt(x^2-1))^l +(x-sqrt(x^2-1))^l]/2 gives |T_l(x)|<=exp(C l sqrt(d)): the two reciprocal factors have moduli at most 1+C sqrt(d). The finite Chebyshev expansion and |c_l|<=2M from (9) yield |P(x)|<=C(D_j+1)j^(k-1) exp(C D_j sqrt(|s|)). Since D_j=O_word(N^2) and A>4, this exponential is bounded by a word constant on the whole displayed disk. The denominator in (8) is nonzero there and its inverse has modulus at most exp(C D_j |t|^2), also bounded. This proves (12), including the one-sided-positivity endpoint: only the original real-arc bound was used in its polynomial continuation. The weighted d_j(q)=(q^(2j)-1)C_j(q) has the same bound, since |q^(2j)|<=exp(4N^(-A)) on this disk. The linear normal q=q_N(1+s/N) and the normal (4) map smaller disks of comparable radius into this exponential disk by their exact logarithms. Cauchy's formula on a slightly smaller circle gives simultaneous polynomial bounds for ANY fixed jet depth of this ENTIRE packet. This stronger result is important at singular recurrence steps: one can transport the honest holomorphic low-color germs around nearby coefficient zeros, rather than infer that a finite Taylor truncation selected the correct meromorphic continuation. No recurrence denominator has been declared absent from that circle; the actual scalar colors themselves are holomorphic and bounded. ## 7. What this supplies for the original pointed source For fixed k, the interval reaches j<=1+floor((N-1)/k). At every singular recurrence step whose entire retained bounded jet packet lies within this color interval, its ACTUAL quantum-normal data are polynomially bounded without inverting that singular step. In particular a 2-bridge presentation controls the ordinary-color quantum jets through the midpoint, including the valid endpoint. The original complete/root source and all remaining high-color normal packets stay in the subsequent boundary transport. This does NOT assert a meridian-derivative bound for F_N(Y) at fixed q_N. Along C_j(q), q and Y=q^(2j) move together. Nor does pointwise unitarity at q_N extend the result beyond (1): there the continuous vacuum path space encounters nonsemisimple wall channels. Those channels and their original source must be retained. No bound for the complete K_N or the full high-color response is inferred. [Audit](../experiments/audit_ordinary_color_macroscopic_normal_jet_window.py): continuous untruncated vacuum path unitarity, colored cup/JW normalization, endpoint-inclusive angular bounds and exact Chebyshev endpoint derivative estimates.

title: Auditing the ordinary-color remainder in the original Fourier energy
text: # Auditing the ordinary-color remainder in the original Fourier energy 28 October 2026. The question is the precise inequality used when replacing the original complete-color value by a positive Fourier norm. The proof below uses the actual finite crossing matrices and a reconstructed positive path trace. No published asymptotic, unitarity, ADO/Jones comparison, or volume-conjecture theorem is a premise. The root convention is essential. Set q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, [j]=sin(pi j/N)/sin(pi/N). Let a fixed braid on b strands close to a ONE-component zero-framed knot, and let C_j(q) denote its original reduced ordinary j-color, with unknot value one. Then, for every 1<=j<N, |C_j(q)| <= [j]^(b-1) <= sin(pi/N)^(1-b). (1) There is no corresponding assertion at j=N. The statement is also not asserted at arbitrary Galois-conjugate roots. The immediate consequence needed in the Fourier argument is the all-level, all-ordinary-color estimate 0 <= E_N-|K_N|^2 <= (N-1)(N/2)^(2b-2). (1a) Here the braid presentation, and therefore b, is fixed as N varies. Neither hyperbolicity nor alternatingness is needed for this bound. The positive-energy identity is exact; only the replacement of its ordinary-color remainder by a polynomial uses the estimate. ## 1. The positive algebra and its trace can be checked directly Put delta=q+q^(-1)=2cos(pi/N), and mu_a=sin((a+1)pi/N)/sin(pi/N), 0<=a<=N-2. These numbers are positive; with zero boundary values they satisfy mu_(a-1)+mu_(a+1)=delta mu_a. On walks of length m in the chain 0,...,N-2 starting at zero, let U_i change only the middle height of a return (c,a,c), with coefficient sqrt(mu_a mu_a')/mu_c. Direct local multiplication gives U_i*=U_i, U_i^2=delta U_i, U_i U_(i+1) U_i=U_i, U_i U_j=U_j U_i for |i-j|>1. Consequently B_i=q^(1/2)I-q^(-1/2)U_i is unitary: its eigenvalues are q^(1/2) and -q^(-3/2). The same displayed relations prove the braid relation. Inverse crossings are the actual inverses. The weighted trace tau_m(A)=sum_walks mu_(last height) A_(walk,walk) is positive. Its weight is central in the path algebra because every generator preserves the last height, so it is tracial too. Directly, tau_(m+1)(A tensor I)=delta tau_m(A), tau_(m+1)((A tensor I)U_m)=tau_m(A). (2) In the first identity sum over the last step using the mu recurrence. In the second identity only the unchanged middle height contributes to the diagonal: mu_c from the last vertex cancels the denominator mu_c of U_m, leaving exactly the weight mu_a on the length-m walk. These recursions identify the trace with the ORIGINAL fundamental quantum trace. Indeed the latter has K=diag(q,q^(-1)) and U block [[q,-1],[-1,q^(-1)]] on (01,10), zero on (00,11); its partial K-trace is I and Tr K=delta. Both traces therefore satisfy (2), with value one on the empty diagram. Uniqueness does not require semisimplicity: the Temperley--Lieb relations inductively span the next algebra by the included algebra and elements A U_m B, and traciality plus (2) determine both types. The spanning claim follows by reducing each U_m A U_m with the preceding spanning statement and the two local quadratic/adjacent relations. ## 2. Ordinary colors are positive projections in this trace Write n=j-1. The recursively defined color projector is p_0=p_1=I, p_(m+1)=p_m tensor I -[m]/[m+1] (p_m tensor I)U_m(p_m tensor I). For n<=N-2 every denominator used is nonzero and every coefficient is real. The local algebra proves idempotence and annihilation by U_1,...,U_(n-1); hence its path realization is an orthogonal projector. The trace recursion gives tau_n(p_n)=[n+1]=[j]. This is the actual highest-weight color, not a color assigned to an unrelated positive model. In the ordinary fundamental tensor space, the common kernel of the U_i has one vector at each tensor weight: the local 01/10 relation fixes their coefficient ratio and adjacent exchanges connect all words of that weight. The vectors obtained by successive coproduct F-actions on the highest tensor span those lines. Their coefficients involve only nonzero [r]!, r<=n. Thus they give the original j-dimensional highest-weight module. The projector acts as identity on this common kernel and has image in it. Restricting the cabled finite universal R to these images gives the original j-color R, by its coproduct identities. A direct coefficient proof of both identities, including the Cartan factors, is given in the [independent color audit](actual_ordinary_color_comparison_audit.md#4-the-fundamental-cable-is-the-literal-colored-r). The retained highest-vector Cartan scalar is q^(n^2/2); the ordinary framing twist is q^(n(n+2)/2). Both have modulus one. For b colored strands let P be the tensor product of these projectors. The trace of a disjoint colored closure, or (2) successively, gives tau(P)=[j]^b. The cabled braid is unitary in the path representation and preserves P. It also preserves each last-height block. In an orthonormal basis of Im P within each such block, its diagonal entries have modulus at most one and every trace weight is positive. Therefore |tau(P B P)| <= tau(P)=[j]^b. Dividing by the NONZERO original ordinary quantum dimension [j], and retaining the unit-modulus zero-framing factor, proves (1). At j=N the relevant quantum dimension is [N]=0. In the positive path trace the corresponding negligible projector has zero image. The division just used is unavailable. This is precisely why this proof places no polynomial bound on K_N. ## 3. The ADO orbit really has these ordinary-color values At the orbit color x=q^(j-1), the original N-dimensional module has the invariant subspace U=span(v_j,...,v_(N-1)); its quotient is the ordinary j-dimensional module. Every tensor factor of the finite R, its inverse, and the pivot preserves U. In a basis adapted to U, each matrix path along an underlying strand can enter U but cannot leave it. A one-component braid closure passes through the open cut. For its quotient block that cut starts and ends outside U, forcing every contributing path around the component to stay in the quotient. Thus the induced cut is exactly the all-j-colored cut, even though the other braid strands were traced first. No assertion of this form is made for a separate closed link component. The conventions agree after the explicit signs are kept: K^(1-N)=epsilon_j K, theta_ADO=epsilon_j theta_ordinary, epsilon_j=(-1)^(j-1). The braid permutation is a b-cycle, so its writhe w satisfies w=b-1 modulo 2. The resulting sign is epsilon_j^(b-1-w)=1. Consequently the ORIGINAL even meridian family satisfies F_N(Q^j)=C_j(q), with F_N(1)=K_N. This is the filtered matrix argument of `root_orbit_pointing.md`, with the precise one-component and framing hypotheses exposed. To distinguish the two coordinates used in the older notes, write this as F_N^M(-q^j)=F_N^Y(Q^j)=C_j(q), Y=M^2. The functions in this identity are REDUCED periods. The full ADO state also carries its original modified-dimension factor, which can have a pole at an ordinary orbit point. Neither its value nor a transverse derivative is bounded by (1). No such value or derivative is used in the Fourier remainder below. ## 4. An explicit positive Fourier remainder Set c_0=K_N and c_j=C_j(q) for 1<=j<N, and use the unitary transform chat_k=N^(-1/2) sum_(j=0)^(N-1) Q^(-kj)c_j. Finite character orthogonality proves exactly E_N:=sum_k |chat_k|^2 =|K_N|^2+R_N, 0<=R_N=sum_(j=1)^(N-1)|C_j(q)|^2 <=sum_(j=1)^(N-1)[j]^(2b-2). (3) In particular this remainder is polynomial uniformly over the entire ordinary-color range, including j=N-1, rather than just at fixed j. There is an explicit sharper constant. Put r=b-1>=1 and assume N>r. The Fourier expansion of sin^(2r)(pi j/N) has frequencies -r,...,r. Only its constant coefficient survives summation over all N roots; that coefficient is binom(2r,r)/4^r. The j=0 summand is zero. Hence 0<=R_N <= N binom(2r,r)/(4^r sin^(2r)(pi/N)) <= binom(2r,r) N^(2r+1)/16^r. (4) For b=1 the closure is the unknot and R_N=N-1 instead. For small N<=r the sum bound (3) remains valid without the simplified formula. Equivalently chat=K_N u+e, where u is the constant unit vector, e is orthogonal to u, and ||e||^2=R_N. This orthogonality is exact; there is no discarded cross term. There is also an unconditional logarithmic statement, which is safer than writing an equality of unsmoothed logarithms before a positive rate has been established. The trivial ordinary color satisfies C_1=1, so R_N>=1 for every N>=2. Set P_(N,b)=(N-1)(N/2)^(2b-2)>=1. Then the exact energy identity and (1a) give 1+|K_N|^2 <= E_N <= P_(N,b)(1+|K_N|^2), (4a) 0 <= log E_N-log(1+|K_N|^2) <= log P_(N,b). In particular, uniformly without any nonvanishing assumption, (pi/N)log E_N =(pi/N)log(1+|K_N|^2)+O_b(log N/N). (4b) With log 0=-infinity this is equivalently 0 <= (pi/N)log E_N-max(0,(2pi/N)log|K_N|) <= (pi/N)log(2P_(N,b)). (4c) For any fixed V>0, (4a)--(4c) prove (2pi/N)log|K_N| -> V if and only if (pi/N)log E_N -> V. (5) The implication from positive energy to the original invariant uses the fact that a polynomial remainder is smaller than any sequence with strictly positive exponential rate. It does not assume eventual nonvanishing of K_N; that nonvanishing follows from the positive energy rate and (3). An unrestricted equality of log E_N and 2 log|K_N| at exponential scale does NOT follow merely from the polynomial remainder: zeros or exponentially small values would invalidate that inference. ## 5. What is verified, and what remains The existing audit `experiments/audit_regularized_kashaev_period.py` was independently rerun during this check: all 30 positive-path versus original-cut comparisons, 62 ordinary-color inequalities, and ten exact finite-field polar/orbit calculations passed. Those finite checks supplement the uniform proofs above; they do not prove a volume limit. Two fresh independent audits also passed and were read and rerun by the root agent: * [Positive path algebra](ordinary_color_positive_trace_independent_audit.md): both Markov identities on noncommuting words, the full projection induction including the first zero-dimension projection, and 42 signed colored closures including j=N-1. * [Original color identification](actual_ordinary_color_comparison_audit.md): the uniform one-component filtered trace proof and direct R coproduct calculation, supplemented by 228 exact whole-knot cut comparisons and 22 signed-cable families, with the original Cartan and twist phases. The explicit sine-energy identity in (4) was independently checked in 225 pairs (N,r), with 80-digit arithmetic; its proof is the finite character calculation above. No defect was found in either uniform proof. These checks establish the remainder estimate's stated scope, not the geometric size of the remaining Fourier energy. The polynomial remainder in (3) has an independent algebraic proof. The positive energy E_N still requires its geometric exponential estimate. In particular, the canonical cleared operator B(Y-1) becomes Bhat(S-I) in the dual cyclic coordinate and kills the constant mode u exactly. Retaining the original normal/pointed source is therefore essential when estimating that energy. Plancherel validates the positive target; it does not by itself supply its size.

title: Independent algebra audit of the ordinary-color positive trace bound
text: # Independent algebra audit of the ordinary-color positive trace bound 28 October 2026. This independently checks the positive path algebra used in Section 2 of `regularized_kashaev_period.md`. No published volume, Jones asymptotic, positivity theorem or recoupling identity is a premise. The local path matrices, trace, projections, cabling and framing estimate are proved below. The separate identification with the ORIGINAL reduced ordinary-color cut is being audited in `actual_ordinary_color_comparison_audit.md`. Verdict: the path-algebra proof is correct. The estimates include every color j<N, in particular j=N-1. The explicit arguments below fill in the two compressed steps: the Jones--Wenzl square relation and multiplicative trace of disjoint color projections. ## 1. Local matrices, without an imported positive trace For N>=3 set theta=pi/N, q=exp(i theta), delta=q+q^(-1), and mu_a=sin((a+1)theta)/sin(theta), 0<=a<=N-2. These weights are strictly positive. With mu_(-1)=mu_(N-1)=0 they obey mu_(a-1)+mu_(a+1)=delta mu_a, including the two endpoints. The Hilbert space H_m has its orthonormal basis the length-m walks (a_0,...,a_m) in {0,...,N-2}, a_0=0, |a_i-a_(i-1)|=1. The operator U_i is zero unless a_(i-1)=a_(i+1)=c. It then replaces a_i by a neighbor a_i' of c with coefficient sqrt(mu_(a_i')mu_(a_i))/mu_c. (1) It is real symmetric. On a fixed pair of equal outer neighbors its nonzero block is vv^t/mu_c, with v_a=sqrt(mu_a). The neighbor identity implies U_i^2=delta U_i. Here is the complete adjacent-product calculation. In U_i U_(i+1) U_i, suppose the original outer heights for the first U_i are c,c and a_(i+2)=d. The middle operator forces the first replacement a_i'=d; the final U_i forces the middle replacement a_(i+1)'=c. The three coefficients multiply to sqrt(mu_(a_i)mu_d)/mu_c * mu_c/mu_d * sqrt(mu_d mu_(a_i''))/mu_c =sqrt(mu_(a_i)mu_(a_i''))/mu_c. This is precisely U_i. All forced heights are allowed neighbors, so no nonexistent boundary height or zero weight is divided by. The opposite adjacent relation is identical. Distant U's commute since they change distinct middle heights and share only fixed endpoints. Consequently B_i=q^(1/2)I-q^(-1/2)U_i is unitary: the coefficient of U_i in B_i B_i^* is delta-q-q^(-1)=0. Expanding its braid relation reduces its difference to a multiple of q-(q+q^(-1))+q^(-1)=0. This proves unitarity and braiding directly at the chosen principal root. ## 2. The weighted trace and both Markov identities Define tau_m(A)=sum_paths mu_(a_m) A_(a,a). Every U_i and B_i preserves a_m. Hence the positive diagonal matrix of endpoint weights commutes with their algebra, and tau is a positive tracial functional. For the included operator A on H_(m+1), summing over the last neighbor b of a_m gives tau_(m+1)(A tensor I)=delta tau_m(A). (2) For the second identity, a diagonal contribution to (A tensor I)U_m requires that the U_m replacement leave a_m unchanged, since A preserves its m-th endpoint. U_m also forces a_(m+1)=a_(m-1). Its diagonal entry is mu_(a_m)/mu_(a_(m-1)); multiplication by the trace weight cancels the denominator. Every length-m prefix has exactly this allowed final neighbor. Thus tau_(m+1)((A tensor I)U_m)=tau_m(A). (3) These arguments apply to arbitrary elements of the generated algebra, not only its diagonal or commuting words. The same identities determine the planar closure trace algebraically. Indeed the elementary TL relations inductively imply TL_(m+1)=TL_m + TL_m U_m TL_m. To reduce a word containing two U_m's, decompose its intervening TL_m word into TL_(m-1) plus TL_(m-1)U_(m-1)TL_(m-1); commute the former past U_m, then use U_m^2=delta U_m or U_m U_(m-1) U_m=U_m. Traciality, (2) and (3) therefore recursively fix the trace on every word, starting with tau_0(1)=1. Closing a planar pairing diagram and assigning delta to each resulting circle obeys the same relations and recursions: the square relation creates one circle, the adjacent relation none. Hence it is that same trace. In particular horizontal juxtaposition of two diagrams multiplies their traces, since their closed circle sets are disjoint. By linearity, tau_(r+s)(A tensor B)=tau_r(A)tau_s(B). (4) This proves the product-color trace used below rather than assuming it. ## 3. Color projections through the last permitted color Write [r]=sin(r theta)/sin(theta). Starting with p_0=p_1=I, set p_(m+1)=p_m-([m]/[m+1])p_m U_m p_m. (5) The first term is included on m+1 strands. Every denominator is positive for m+1<=N-1. For m=1 the required square relation is simply U_1^2=delta U_1, so no generator U_0 is needed. For m>=2 let g=p_(m-1), c=[m-1]/[m], and f=p_m=g-cgU_(m-1)g. Then fg=gf=f, and g commutes with U_m. Therefore x=fU_m f satisfies x^2=(delta-c)x=([m+1]/[m])x. (6) The first equality follows by inserting f=g-cgU_(m-1)g between the two U_m's and using the square/adjacent TL relations. More explicitly, commuting g past U_m and using fg=f gives fU_m fU_m=delta fU_m-c fU_m U_(m-1)U_m g=(delta-c)fU_m. Multiplication on the right by f gives (6). It follows that (5) is a selfadjoint idempotent and annihilates U_m on both sides. Earlier U_i are already annihilated by f. Conversely any vector killed by all internal U_i is fixed by p_(m+1), since p_(m+1)-I lies in their generated ideal. This verifies the intended common-kernel projection, with no generic semisimplicity assumption. Use positivity, (2)--(3), idempotence and traciality to compute tau_(m+1)(p_(m+1)) =delta tau_m(p_m)-([m]/[m+1])tau_m(p_m) =delta[m+1]-[m]=[m+2]. (7) In the middle line tau_(m+1)(p_m U_m p_m)=tau_m(p_m). The base values tau_0(p_0)=[1] and tau_1(p_1)=[2] start the induction. Thus the j-color projection is p_(j-1), with trace [j]>0 for ALL j<N. As a useful endpoint check, p_(N-1) is still definable (its last denominator is [N-1]>0), but its positive trace is [N]=0. It is therefore the ZERO operator in this path representation. There is no nonzero positive projection which may be divided by [N]; the proof explicitly stops before the Kashaev color. ## 4. Cabling, the retained trace, and framing For b strands of common ordinary color j let ell=j-1 and put P=p_ell tensor ... tensor p_ell on b ell fundamental strands. Its factors commute and are orthogonal projections, so P is one too. Equation (4) proves exactly tau(P)=[j]^b. (8) A positive crossing of two ell-strand blocks is the usual ell^2 fundamental braid word. The Yang--Baxter relation slides every internal block generator through it, moving the first block's generator to the second and vice versa. Applying the polynomial recursion (5) proves that this block crossing interchanges the two p_ell factors and hence commutes with their product. Its inverse does too. Thus every cabled colored braid is unitary and preserves P, directly in the positive path representation. No assertion that the original tensor metric itself is positive is used. Let U denote this unitary cabled word. Since the endpoint weight D is positive and commutes with both U and P, Schatten Cauchy--Schwarz gives |tau(PU)|=|Tr(D^(1/2)P U P D^(1/2))| <=Tr(DP)=[j]^b. (9) Equivalently restrict to the image of P and sum unitary diagonal entries with their positive weights. The reduced closure divides by the retained [j]>0, yielding |C_j(q_N)|<=[j]^(b-1), 1<=j<N. (10) Here identifying that reduced closure with the original cut is the separate actual-color comparison, not an extra positivity premise. The actual zero-framing factor is a power of q^((j^2-1)/2), and all retained fundamental/color Cartan phases likewise have modulus one. They do not change (9)--(10). Their exact values are retained in the comparison audit. At N=2 the only ordinary color is j=1 and C_1=1. Finally sin(pi/N)>=2/N implies [j]<=sin(pi/N)^(-1)<=(N/2), so for a fixed b-strand presentation the whole ordinary-color vector has polynomial size. This conclusion concerns the specific principal root and the ordinary range; it makes no estimate for j=N. ## 5. Independent checks [The new audit](../experiments/audit_positive_ordinary_color_path_trace.py) constructs the path matrices without importing any Jones/trace library. It checks adjacent relations, noncommuting Markov words, every permitted projection including j=N-1, the vanishing next projection, disjoint color traces, cabled-braid preservation and both crossing signs. Whole colored closures include their zero-framing unit phases. These finite checks supplement the uniform proofs above and are not a premise for (10). An additional independent proof reread checked the trace recursion without semisimplicity, the expanded square calculation in (6), preservation of the two color projections under block braiding, the j=N-1 endpoint and the empty-cable N=2 case. It found no substantive gap in this path-algebra argument. A fresh run of the audit passed; those computations remain supplementary to the all-level proof, and do not replace the separate comparison with the original ordinary-color cut.

title: Shared source caps, triangle orderings and the remaining tetrahedral defect
text: # Shared source caps, triangle orderings and the remaining tetrahedral defect Research note, 26 October 2026. This gives exact shared-edge cap transport, tetrahedron reversal and coherent cyclic face orderings for the existing pointed recoupling tensors. It also gives an explicit counterexample to extending those results to all vertex orderings of the bare tetrahedron tensor. Thus the ideal-triangulation comparison still requires a source-compatible tensor symmetrization. The actual endpoint caps and their finite-factorial normalization are those proved in [relative pivotal duality](relative_pivotal_duality.md). No different knot invariant or regulator realization is defined here. The volume conjecture remains unproved. ## 1. One marked cap on each edge Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2. On a nondegenerate flag chart choose distinct p_i=A_i^N, with A_i nonzero. Give an oriented edge the existing affine character and endpoint module g_ij=(1,p_i-p_j), E_ij=E_(g_ij;A_j,A_i). Thus g_ij g_jk=g_ik. Choose a marked K-root x_ij with x_ij^N=1 and put x_ji=Q^(-1)x_ij^(-1). (1.1) Let J_ij be the actual source-normalized endpoint cap from the preceding note. It pairs E_ij with E_ji. In particular J_ij^(-t)J_ji=X_ij^(N-1). (1.2) The cap on the total edge ik is its already assigned J_ik. It is not chosen independently each time that edge occurs in a triangle. For example the dual of a product mark x is Q^(-1)x^(-1), whereas the product of two dual marks is Q^(-2)x^(-1). These are different marked cyclic cuts. For general multiplicative central X-characters, define omega_ijk=x_ij x_jk/x_ik, omega_ijk^N=1. Direct cancellation gives omega_ijk omega_ikl=omega_ijl omega_jkl, omega_kji=Q^(-1)omega_ijk^(-1). (1.3) Thus the root discrepancy is coherent triangle data, with a specified reversal law. It is not set to one independently on each face. No division by two or three modulo N is used. ## 2. Root changes are explicit norm-one transports with a source wall Write the finite cap scalar of the preceding note as c(x;a,b)=-1/(N xQ) product_(s=1)^(N-2)(b-a x^(-1)Q^s). At fixed endpoints and central character, c(Qx;a,b)/c(x;a,b) =Q^(-1)(b-a/x)/(b-aQ^(-2)/x). (2.1) This follows by canceling the two finite products. The product of (2.1) over the full N-orbit is one. The cap scalar itself is an explicit Hilbert-90 primitive for this transport. These ratios are functions; for N>=3 they are not generally phases or constants. All zero and pole factors remain. At the actual source choose a=x_0, b near 1 and let the mark be Q^j x_0. In the normal coordinate b-1, ord c(Q^j x_0;x_0,b) =0 for j=0,N-1, and 1 for 1<=j<=N-2. (2.2) Indeed the single vanishing factor occurs exactly at s=j in the product, and its first coefficient is nonzero. At N=2 both charts have order zero. Thus moving the cut can require a first normal coefficient even though its generic cyclic norm is one. Its finite cyclic lattice and the dual linking pairing retain that coefficient. A value at b=1 without its source lattice does not specify this transport. There is an exact cancellation law for the face metrics. If a change of marks rescales edge caps by J'_ij=u_ij J_ij, then the induced face pairing obeys M'_ijk=(u_ij u_jk/u_ik)M_ijk. (2.3) This follows immediately from the factorization defining M. The two products of these face factors around a tetrahedron are equal by cancellation. Consistent shared edge choices therefore retain their full factors without an independent tetrahedron normalization. The actual selected boundary vectors and covectors must be transported as well. ## 3. Exact tetrahedron reversal Use the pointed factorization C_ijk:E_ik tensor V_ijk -> E_ij tensor E_jk, and the triangle metrics defined by C_ijk^t(J_ij tensor J_jk)P C_kji =J_ik tensor M_ijk. (3.1) Here P is the literal flip. The total cap in (3.1) is the shared edge cap. For four flags let R_0123:V_023 tensor V_012 -> V_013 tensor V_123 be the existing pointed Racah map. Then exactly (M_023 tensor M_012)R_3210 =R_0123^t(M_013 tensor M_123). (3.2) For a proof let I_L,I_R be the two three-edge fusion tree evaluations, with I_L=I_R(I tensor R_0123). Reverse their leaf order and use the inverse affine characters. Applying (3.1) twice factors the paired leaf contraction as J_03 tensor M_023 tensor M_012 for one tree and J_03 tensor M_013 tensor M_123 for the other. Substitution of the tree relation and cancellation of J_03 gives (3.2). This fixes the whole scalar, without determinant rigidity. Equation (1.2) and the group-like pivot also give M_kji=M_ijk^t. (3.3) Indeed the double-dual operator on the two leaves is their tensor pivot, which is the pivot of the total edge. Removing that same total cap leaves the identity on the relative factor. Thus face reversal is paired exactly. Choosing a local product mark for a total cap changes (3.2). If r_ijk=c(x_ij x_jk;A_k,A_i)/c(x_ik;A_k,A_i), its defect is r_023 r_012/(r_013 r_123). (3.4) The audit finds nontrivial examples at every tested N>=3. These factors are retained as their full functions; (3.4) is not a new permitted normalization of the knot period. ## 4. The cyclic face map from the actual invariant tensor The relative triangle has operators D=X_1+Y_1Y_2^(-1), Z=-Y_1Y_2^(-1)X_2, DZ=QZD, D^N=lambda, Z^N=mu, lambda+mu=1. Its endpoint parameters are u=A_j/A_k, v=A_i/A_k. Turn the total leg of C_ijk using its assigned cap: T_ijk=(C_ijk tensor I)coev_ik. Here the relative factor is retained as the argument; in indices T_(abc,l)=sum_s C_(ab,sl)(J_ik^(-1))_(cs). It identifies V_ijk with the invariant subspace of E_ij tensor E_jk tensor E_ki. This space has dimension N: rigid duality identifies it with the N-dimensional fusion multiplicity space, and C_ijk is the explicit isomorphism. On invariants cyclic rotation is rot=P_231(g_ij^(-1) tensor I tensor I), g_ij=X_ij^(N-1). The antipode and pivot identities make this an invariant tensor again. Three rotations give the inverse total pivot, which acts as the identity on invariants. Thus there is a unique invertible matrix L_f for f=(i,j,k), r f=(j,k,i), such that T_(r f)L_f=rot T_f, L_(r^2 f)L_(r f)L_f=I. (4.1) This is a finite construction with the scalar fixed by the displayed actual tensors. It does not reset a unit. The corresponding relative algebra map is h(D)=-D^(-1)Z, h(Z)=Q D^(-1), h^3=1, D_(r f)L_f=L_f h(D_f), Z_(r f)L_f=L_f h(Z_f). (4.2) One can derive (4.2) directly on invariants. The total Y equation gives Y_2Y_3^(-1)=-D^(-1)X_1X_2 there, while D X_2=X_1X_2-Z. These give the first formula. The total X equation and the Q commutation give the second formula. Both phases in (4.2) are consequently determined. ## 5. The raw cyclic map has a matrix-valued pairing defect Let bar f=(k,j,i), and f'=(i,k,j), so r f'=bar f and bar(r f)=f'. The exact defect of the raw map is L_f^t M_(r f)L_(f')^(-1) =M_f G_(bar f), G_(bar f)=D_(bar f)^(1-N) =lambda_(bar f)^(-1)D_(bar f). (5.1) This is not a scalar for N>=2. The source cap alone does not make the raw invariant rotation a face pairing symmetry. Here is a uniform calibration of (5.1). The reversal anti-map on the relative algebra is a(D)=-Z^(-1)D, a(Z)=QZ^(-1). Substitution of a and h shows that the defect G commutes with D_(bar f) and Q-commutes with Z_(bar f). Since this pair generates the full matrix algebra, G=c D_(bar f). To determine c, edge-cap scalar gauges may be removed by (2.3); they cancel from G. Use the raw endpoint trace caps. Put alpha_f=A_k^(N-1)/(p_j-p_k). Their relative unit functional is (M_f e_0)(F)=alpha_f tau_D[D F/(v-uD)], (5.2) where tau_D is normalized multiplication trace in k[D]/(D^N-lambda). Its defining shift recurrence follows from a(Z)+u_(bar f)a(D)-v_(bar f), and its scalar follows by pairing the two endpoint units in (3.1). Finite trace cancellation gives (M_f)_(0,1)=alpha_f u^(N-2)lambda/mu, (M_f)_(N-1,0)=alpha_f lambda v^(N-1)/mu, (M_f)_(N-1,N-1)=0. (5.3) For example tau[D/(v-uD)]=u^(N-1)lambda/mu; the adjacent shifted denominator gives the first identity. The last identity reduces to tau[D^(N-1)]=0. The pointed factorial formula for C gives L_f e_0=ell_f e_(N-1), ell_f=lambda/mu, L_f^(-1)e_0=(v e_(N-1)-u lambda e_0)/(ell_f mu). (5.4) For the scalar in (5.4), with raw caps the invariant unit tensor is (A_k-A_i X_3)sum_(s=0)^(N-1)(X_1X_2X_3)^s. Apply the pointed finite-product formula to the rotated relative monomial of degree N-1. The identity product_(s=1)^(N-1)(b-aQ^s t)=(b^N-a^N)/(b-at) at t^N=1 gives ell_f=lambda/mu. The inverse in (5.4) then follows by (4.2) and Z^N=mu. Now evaluate the (0,0) entry of (5.1), use (5.3)--(5.4) on f,r f,f', and divide by (M_f)_(0,1). It gives c=(alpha_(r f)/alpha_f) mu/v^(N-1) =mu(p_j-p_k)/(p_k-p_i) =-mu/lambda=lambda_(bar f)^(-1). This proves (5.1) with its full scalar at every N. The audit checks the intermediate trace and unit formulas, as well as the complete matrix identity. ## 6. Corrected face orderings preserve the actual pairing Choose once a phase tau_N with tau_N^3=Q. This is an ordinary algebraic phase choice, including when 3 divides N; no inverse of three modulo N is required. Define U_f=tau_N lambda_f L_f D_f^(-1) =tau_N L_f D_f^(N-1). (6.1) Thus the correction is exactly the relative face pivot, with its recorded cubic phase. The second expression is polynomial; invertibility at a degenerate central point still requires the retained lattice and source. These maps have exact cyclic and dual-pairing coherence: U_(r^2 f)U_(r f)U_f=I, U_f^t M_(r f)U_(f')^(-1)=M_f. (6.2) For the cyclic identity, pulling the inverse D factors through (4.2) gives (L D^(-1))_(r^2 f)(L D^(-1))_(r f)(L D^(-1))_f =h^2(D)^(-1)h(D)^(-1)D^(-1) =-Q^(-1)I. The three central lambda values are lambda,-mu/lambda,1/mu; their product is -1. Combining this with tau_N^3=Q proves the first equation of (6.2). For the second, move D factors through the reversal pairing using a. Equation (5.1) then gives the scalar mu/lambda for L D^(-1). The lambda factors in (6.1) cancel it because lambda_(f')=mu_f. The common phase cancels as well. The lifted quantum cyclic algebra map is now h_correct(D)=-Q D^(-1)Z, h_correct(Z)=Q D^(-1). (6.3) It has order three and obeys the strict dihedral relation with the reversal anti-map a. Equations (3.3) and (6.2) therefore give coherent oriented triangular order changes with the actual dual pairing. The selected vectors and covectors are transported by these full matrices. Interior adapters cancel in a specified finite contraction. The inverse D and lambda in (6.1) are operator and central data, not discarded numerical multipliers. At a wall, whole transport is interpreted on its actual lattice and dual source, as in the preceding note. This face result does not assert all tetrahedron vertex symmetries. ## 7. The bare tetrahedron still fails the full vertex-order test This is a separate, explicitly failed proposed bridge. Use the raw R above as the positive tetrahedron map. Regard its source duals as reversed face modules using M^(-1), and place its four tensor legs in boundary-face order (123),(320),(013),(210). For a negative tetrahedron use R^(-1) with the opposite face orientations. For another ordered vertex list identify its oriented faces by the corrected U maps in (6.1) and permute its four legs back to the same boundary-face order. This completely specifies the tensor comparison being tested. It is false that the resulting tensors are always scalar multiples. An even permutation already gives a counterexample: N=2, A=(2,3,4,5), vertex order (1,2,0,3). There is a short exact reduction certificate. Work modulo 241 with primitive generator 7, q=177, Q=-1 and tau_N=16. Then q^2=-1 and tau_N^3=-1. With the face tensor flattened in the displayed boundary order, its first two coefficients and those of the reordered tensor are original: (83,239), reordered: (141,0). Their proportionality minor is 0*83-239*141=41 mod 241, which is nonzero. All denominators and required matrix minors in the construction are nonzero at this point. This is also a characteristic-zero obstruction to the proposed rational identity: 241 splits the cyclotomic coefficient field, and a zero rational identity could not have this nonzero good reduction. At the odd level N=3 the same even permutation has a regular certificate modulo 397: the two coefficient pairs are (344,139) and (10,262), with minor 207. Thus the ordering issue also occurs on the odd-level recoupling system covered by the matrix-dilogarithm framework. Consistent edge-cap scalar gauges cannot remove this counterexample. By (2.3) they rescale each face pairing, and the T-based cyclic maps rescale by the ratio of their total-edge cap scalars. Thus each compared four-tensor is only rescaled. Nonproportionality is unchanged. A scalar tetrahedron factor cannot fix it either. This refutes this bare-tensor prescription with these face adapters. It does not refute a literature charged matrix dilogarithm, a different specified tetrahedral decoration, or the actual knot invariant. The audit finds only the identity and full reversal scalar equivalent among the 24 orders in its N=2,3,4 configurations. A source-compatible tensor symmetrization or a comparison retaining additional operator trace data is still required before global gluing to an arbitrarily ordered positive ideal triangulation. The later [root-charge diagnostic](braided_source_groupoid.md#1-fixed-face-adapters-are-not-repaired-just-by-root-charges) checks a stronger repair proposal: keep these face adapters and vary both literal standard-kernel root charges. At a regular N=3 point all 81 reference/reordered charge pairs still have nonzero proportionality minors. Thus that repair does not supply the missing tetrahedron assignment. This is not a test of a different published adapter prescription. The actual source braiding and its retained spectral jets are constructed separately in the braided source groupoid. ## 8. Coverage, verification and the remaining volume comparison The abstract of [Baseilhac--Benedetti, math/0306283](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306283) already distinguishes a basic ordered matrix dilogarithm from its decorated symmetrization. It supplies coverage of this problem, not a proof premise or an identification with the actual source used here. No novelty is claimed for charged tetrahedral symmetry or cyclic 6j-symbols. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_oriented_tetrahedron_source.py) checks N=2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,12. Shared-cap reversal, the raw nonscalar cyclic defect, its uniform trace calibration, the corrected cyclic and metric identities, all 24 face cap gauge and tetrahedral charge identities, and the root mark norm/source formulas pass. The separate full vertex test fails with the explicit certificate above, as recorded in [the results](../experiments/oriented_tetrahedron_source_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_oriented_tetrahedron_source.py The positive triangulation theorem supplies a geometric marked Bloch representative. The constructions here provide further actual source and orientation data for a comparison, and the failed test identifies an additional operator-level requirement. They do not identify the global selected period, its geometric A-component, or its regulator norm across levels. The subsequent [standard matrix comparison](standard_matrix_dilog_source_comparison.md) now makes the candidate charged replacement concrete: the actual pointed fusion map is written in the literature odd-level basic kernel with four face gauges, its input permutation and selected unit scalar. Root-charge changes become explicit Weyl leg operators and their Heisenberg phase, while the integer-charge prefactor remains a full function. The normal source chart has a regular standard kernel and the same integer carry poles. This identifies the local tensor and its actual source; it does not by itself prove that the globally prescribed charged face pairings are the induced ones, or repair the failed uncolored vertex-order prescription. The subsequent [shared face proof](shared_standard_face_gluing.md) now gives one frame per ordered triangle on the common flag chart. In it these actual pairings and corrected cyclic maps are explicit Gaussian matrices times their retained source-normalized scalars. Every ordered tetrahedron has a standard-kernel formula with an explicit clock/shift insertion. This is a compatible local frame description; it does not assert proportionality of the different uncolored vertex-order tensors or identify the global selected geometric period.

title: The original state has charged simplex amplitudes and a retained quadratic phase
text: # The original state has charged simplex amplitudes and a retained quadratic phase 28 October 2026. This is a statement about the ORIGINAL enhanced Kashaev state, before a Fourier or Fermat change of basis. Each nonzero crossing entry has four nonnegative factorial indices adding to N-1. Its absolute action is concave on that charged simplex, strictly concave on each face with at least three positive coordinates. The exact phases are quadratic and remain indispensable: reversing a crossing leaves its entire support and every absolute weight unchanged. The original cut forces the state onto proper faces. In particular, one must not assume an interior optimizer of the four-angle action is accessible to the original source. The [first-strand support reduction](original_source_cyclic_variation_peeling.md) proves that the first head stays zero and gives the corresponding exact q-Pascal boundary operator, including the two unit-modulus end crossings. No broad volume-conjecture estimate follows from concavity alone. ## 1. Both actual crossings have the same charged support Use Q=exp(2 pi i/N), s=exp(pi i/N), F_j=product_(r=1)^j(1-Q^r), and the literature normalization proved in [the crossing audit](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md). Write B_+=P(R^o)^t and B_-=B_+^{-1}. For an entry with input (a,b) and output (c,d), put u=[b-a-1], v=[a-c], t=[c-d], h=[d-b], (1) where brackets take values 0,...,N-1. Then exactly B_+[(c,d),(a,b)] =N Q^[1-(t+h)(u+h)]/(F_u conjugate(F_v) F_t conjugate(F_h)) (2) when u+v+t+h=N-1, and it is zero otherwise. This follows by substituting (i,j,k,l)=(a,b,d,c) into the original unbraided formula. The two printed theta inequalities are equivalent to this sum condition: the sum is congruent to -1 modulo N, and those inequalities bound it strictly below 2N. For the ACTUAL inverse, including the Q^{-1} correction to the printed inverse, its factorial indices are (h,u,v,t). Its numerator is N Q^[(u+v)(v+t)-1]. In particular the support is identical. Using the sum in (1) gives the stronger entrywise identity B_-[(c,d),(a,b)] =Q^(c+d-a-b) conjugate(B_+[(c,d),(a,b)]). (3) Indeed the exponent left after division by conjugate(B_+) is (u+v)(v+t)-(t+h)(u+h), congruent to h-v modulo N, and h-v is congruent to c+d-a-b. Thus if Z e_j=Q^j e_j, B_-=(Z tensor Z) conjugate(B_+) (Z tensor Z)^{-1}. (4) Conjugation in (3)-(4) is entrywise complex conjugation, not adjoint. It does not make the original braid transfer positive or unitary. The exact charged absolute weight is therefore, for either sign, |B_+[(c,d),(a,b)]|=|B_-[(c,d),(a,b)]| =N/|F_u F_v F_t F_h|. (5) ## 2. The uniform real action and its convex geometry Let Lambda(0)=0 and Lambda'(theta)=-log(2 sin theta) on (0,pi). The elementary uniform root-factorial estimate, including the two endpoints, is log|F_j|=-(N/pi)Lambda(pi j/N)+O(log(N+1)), 0<=j<N. (6) For clarity its uniformity does not require staying in the bulk. Split log(2 sin pi x) into log x+log(1-x) plus a smooth function on [0,1]. Stirling bounds for the two resulting factorial products and a bounded Riemann-sum error for the smooth part prove (6), uniformly in j. With alpha=(u,v,t,h)/N, (5)-(6) give (1/N)log|B_+|=H(alpha)+O(log(N+1)/N), H(alpha)=(1/pi)sum_(r=1)^4 Lambda(pi alpha_r), sum alpha_r=1-1/N. (7) For a fixed whole word, the error remains O_word(log N), and its number of state variables is fixed. Thus the absolute action of an actual state is the sum of these local H, with the original support and cut constraints. No scalar replacement state is needed to define this action. Here is the strict-concavity statement, including the obtuse case. For k>=3, theta_r>0 and sum theta_r=pi, the quadratic form sum_r cot(theta_r) w_r^2, sum_r w_r=0, (8) is positive definite. If every angle is at most pi/2, this is immediate; at most one coefficient can be zero in this open simplex. Otherwise exactly one angle, say theta_1, exceeds pi/2. Put s_0=sum_(r>1)theta_r=pi-theta_1<pi/2. Cauchy--Schwarz gives sum_(r>1)cot(theta_r) w_r^2 >= (sum_(r>1)w_r)^2 / sum_(r>1)tan(theta_r). The addition formula for tan gives sum_(r>1)tan(theta_r)<tan(s_0), since there are at least two positive summands and their sum is below pi/2. This strictly dominates the negative term -cot(s_0) w_1^2 whenever w_1 is nonzero. If w_1=0, the remaining positive diagonal form is positive on every nonzero vector. This proves (8). The same proof works when the angle sum is strictly below pi: then cot(sum_(r>1)theta_r)>cot(pi-theta_1), strengthening the inequality. Since the Hessian of sum Lambda is minus this cotangent form, H is strictly concave on the open charged simplex. It extends continuously as a concave function to its closure. On a face at limiting charge sum alpha=1, the same assertion holds for its k>=3 active coordinates. A two-coordinate face instead has zero action, because Lambda(theta)+Lambda(pi-theta)=0. One-coordinate faces also have zero action. Thus strictness on a forced source face must be checked, not inferred from strictness in the unattained open four-coordinate simplex. The value at the balanced point is 2 pi H(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4)=8 Lambda(pi/4), the regular ideal octahedron volume. This calibrates the local absolute envelope. It is not a claim that its sum over a diagram equals the knot-complement volume. ## 3. Whole-word winding regions and their source faces Fix the original arc colors divided by N and choose integer lifts of the brackets in (1). The crossing indices are then affine functions of these colors; their sum is exactly 1-1/N. Nonnegativity defines a convex polytope for each choice of lifts. There are finitely many choices for a fixed word, independently of N. The pivotal closures must be imposed with their ORIGINAL shifts, not as unshifted equality of colors. On a region with all four coordinates positive at every crossing, the Hessian of the whole absolute action has kernel exactly the variations which leave every crossing index fixed. At a crossing, this requires all four incident arc variations to be equal. On a connected projection these equalities propagate to a common translation of all arc colors. Fixing the original cut color removes that translation. Therefore the whole action is strictly concave on any such nonempty region. It has at most one interior critical point; if one exists, it is the unique maximum on that region's closure. This assertion is deliberately not an existence claim. For the original one-cut source, some four-coordinate interiors are inaccessible. On a forced face, discard the zero-action one- and two-coordinate crossing faces. The exact strictness criterion is injectivity, on the remaining tangent space, of the combined corner maps at crossings with at least three active coordinates. This is a finite linear-algebra calculation. When it fails there are real flat directions, which need elimination before applying an ordinary nondegenerate Laplace argument. This gives a finite, source-dependent concavity problem. It does not put a nonzero quantum coefficient on its maximizer, or equate an absolute-state maximum with the geometric regulator. ## 4. The quadratic phase is part of the same original state The exact factorial phase is F_j=|F_j| exp[pi i j(j+1)/(2N)-pi i j/2]. (9) Write alpha_u,...,alpha_h for (1)/N, and define D(alpha)=alpha_u^2+alpha_t^2-alpha_v^2-alpha_h^2, L(alpha)=alpha_u+alpha_t-alpha_v-alpha_h, B(alpha)=-2pi(alpha_t+alpha_h)(alpha_u+alpha_h) -(pi/2)D(alpha)+(pi/2)L(alpha). Equations (2) and (9), without an asymptotic approximation, give B_+=|B_+| exp[i N B(alpha)-i(pi/2)L(alpha)+2pi i/N]. (10) The negative crossing uses the complex conjugate of (10), multiplied by the exact phase Q^(c+d-a-b) from (3). Thus on every fixed winding region the leading phase of the WHOLE original state is a real quadratic function of its arc colors, with crossing signs retained. The remaining linear phases, pivotal scalars, and writhe factor remain explicit. One may consequently define a phase homotopy by multiplying every chosen exact phase angle of the whole summand by tau in [0,1]. At tau=0 this is the absolute sum of that original presentation; at tau=1 it is the original invariant. Intermediate values are not claimed to be knot invariants. Concavity supplies a possible initial real maximum on each accessible face, but does not prove continuation of its integration cycle or nonvanishing at tau=1. There is a sharp reason that phase cannot be ignored. For a fixed braid POSITION word, (3) implies that changing any crossing signs changes neither its supported state set nor any absolute-state summand. The enhancement mu=-s S is a unit-modulus cyclic shift, and the writhe normalization also has modulus one, so the statement holds through the ORIGINAL full closure. Yet crossing changes can change the knot or unknot it. For example the position word (1,2,1,2) has the trefoil closure with all signs positive and the figure-eight closure with alternating signs. Their actual values differ, while their entire absolute-state sum is identical. This is an exact finite-state obstruction, not just a comparison of formal critical potentials. The new concavity therefore cannot by itself settle source selection. A reduced-alternating argument might additionally use its specified phase and projection, but those are additional information. The desired global theorem must carry (10) and the forced source faces all the way to the geometric contour. ## 5. Independent finite checks [The audit](../experiments/audit_original_crossing_winding_convexity.py) checks (1)-(5) against the independently implemented original crossing and its true inverse over finite fields, including even and composite levels. Complex checks verify (9)-(10), the full original pivotal contraction, the figure-eight normalization, and the equal absolute sums of the two signed words above. The cotangent tests supplement, and do not replace, the proof (8).

title: The original source has no automatic positive reflection form
text: # The original source has no automatic positive reflection form 27 October 2026. A universal reflection/Gram argument for the ORIGINAL Kashaev source fails at every level: its identity value is zero while an actual normalized unknot word has nonzero value. A two-channel reflection square has source -2. The standard alternating three-strand weaving transfer also cannot be made a positive Hermitian operator, at any level N>=3, by a positive metric or a scalar phase. These are obstructions to AUTOMATIC positivity of the original word source or transfer. They do not rule out a separately proved positive formula for a particular knot family, a word-dependent source elimination, an explicitly projected positive channel, or the existing positive squared norm of the original invariant. They do not disprove the volume conjecture. ## 1. The original source is not a positive functional Fix q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, N>=2, complete color x=-q^-1=q^(N-1), and retain the original pivot K e_a=x Q^-a e_a, g=K^(1-N). For b>=2 the original reduced one-cut source on actual braid intertwiners is t_b(A)=Tr[(P_0 tensor g^(tensor(b-1)))A]. (1) The all-ones first output row gives the same value on these integer-weight-preserving words. The full source is its original nonzero dimension factor d_N(1)=i^(N+3)/N, with the original zero-framing line. No ordinary quantum dimension is divided out. Since Q has exact order N, Tr(g)=x^(1-N)sum_(a=0)^(N-1)Q^-a=0, t_b(I)=0. (2) Let B_i be the original checked crossing with its own common Cartan factor recorded, and theta its original twist factor. Use the actual zero-framing normalized generator Bhat_i=theta^-1 B_i. The ordinary positive Markov chain W_b=Bhat_(b-1)...Bhat_1 closes to the unknot and has t_b(W_b)=t_b(W_b^-1)=1. (3) This can be checked directly without a knot-polynomial formula. At each last-strand pivotal closure the actual positive crossing has partial trace theta I; its inverse has theta^-1 I. For the positive crossing evaluate on the first highest vector: the closure forces both local indices zero, leaving g_0. For the inverse evaluate on the first lowest vector: only its zero transfer survives, leaving theta^-1. The root scalar-closure identity makes those the whole partial traces. Repeating the closures proves (3), with every original factor retained. **No-go theorem.** There is no involution dagger on a unital complex algebra containing these actual words, and no nonzero scalar multiple of t_b, which makes it a positive linear functional on all A^dagger A. Indeed a positive functional obeys Cauchy--Schwarz. Its value on the identity is zero by (2), so its value on every element would be zero. Equation (3) contradicts this. Equivalently, if the reflection Gram matrix on the channels I,W_b were Hermitian, its upper-left entry would be zero and its off-diagonal entry nonzero. Its determinant is negative. For the usual anti-linear inverse-word reflection, W_b^dagger =W_b^-1. The explicit formal braid combination A=I-W_b gives A^dagger A=2I-W_b-W_b^-1, t_b(A^dagger A)=-2. (4) This is an actual source evaluation of a linear combination of original braid words. It is not an invented negative test functional. The full dimension/phase line multiplies both positive and negative directions by the same fixed nonzero scalar; no phase can turn their indefinite Gram form positive. ## 2. The original cups and caps have the same obstruction The actual nonzero cup and cap obey cap cup=Tr(g)=0. They therefore cannot be Hermitian adjoints in a positive-definite reflection structure: that identity would be the squared norm of the nonzero cup. This is the actual isotropic cup/cap channel already exhibited in [the sewn-source construction](sewn_source_and_meridian_charge.md). One marked cap changes its specified channel and gives the normalized unknot value, but it does not convert ALL ordinary cup/cap pairings in a multi-bridge plat into positive adjoint pairings. Thus drawing a braid or plat as two reflected halves is not by itself a proof that its original scalar is a sum of absolute squares. A valid restricted formula must prove how its actual co-source becomes the required adjoint on the particular image subspace, with the marked cap and all other turns retained. ## 3. Even the basic alternating weaving transfer is not positive Let T_N=B_12 B_23^-1 on three original same-color strands. Its two crossing scalars and zero-framing factors cancel, since the word has writhe zero. It is the block repeated in the alternating weaving words (sigma_1 sigma_2^-1)^m. Consider its invariant physical total-index-one subspace with basis |100>,|010>,|001>. Literal crossing coefficients give T_N|_1=[[1-Q,0,1], [-q,0,0], [0,-q^-1,1-Q^-1]]. (5) For example the local index-one crossing block is [[1-Q,-q],[-q,0]] in the ordered pair |10>,|01>. The two coefficients are rho/x=1-Q and x^-1=-q at x=-q^-1. Multiplying the two adjacent blocks gives (5). This is a computation in the original head, without a proposed positive replacement crossing. Its exact characteristic polynomial is (lambda-1) [lambda^2-(1-Q-Q^-1)lambda+1]. (6) At N=3 it is (lambda-1)^3 but the matrix in (5) is not identity. Thus it is nontrivially unipotent and cannot be self-adjoint in any positive-definite Hermitian metric. At every N>=4 the two other roots are exp(+/-i theta_N), where cos(theta_N)=[1-2cos(2pi/N)]/2, pi/3<=theta_N<2pi/3. They are nonreal. Every positive-metric self-adjoint operator has real spectrum. Consequently T_N cannot be a positive Gram operator C^dagger C after any similarity. Multiplying it by a scalar phase cannot help: its eigenvalue 1 forces that phase to be positive real, leaving the nonreal pair unchanged. Nor does a fixed power remove the obstruction. For any fixed m>=1, the positive eigenvalue condition for T_N^m would require m theta_N to be an integer multiple of 2pi. The angle theta_N is strictly increasing to 2pi/3, so this cannot hold for all sufficiently large N. Indeed each admissible multiple can occur at most once. A fixed alternating weave block therefore cannot be converted into a positive transfer at all levels by taking a fixed number of repetitions. This statement concerns the transfer as an operator. A positive scalar identity for a particular closure could still result from source cancellation and a nontrivial finite-sum identity, as the [actual figure-eight proof](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md) demonstrates. Operator positivity is stronger than that scalar conclusion. ## 4. What remains possible for a positive high-weight channel The unit-circle eigenpair in (6) does not exclude a separately constructed positive spectral channel elsewhere in the tensor module. Such a route would require at least: 1. An explicit source-compatible projection or relative source reduction on the actual word, rather than deleting the nonpositive channels from the invariant by definition. 2. A proved positive representation of the retained scalar with its original marked cap, phases and peripheral line. 3. A bound showing that omitted channels cannot cancel the desired leading contribution, plus a nonzero coupling to the calibrated geometric critical class. The existing positive trace for ordinary colors does not automatically give these facts on the Kashaev projective color. Its quantum dimension is precisely zero, while the modified source detects its nonsemisimple data. Nor does Rivin uniqueness establish positivity of this quantum source. No new positive high-weight channel satisfying these conditions has been constructed here. There IS already a valid positive formulation for all knots: the [original cyclic norm](regularized_kashaev_period.md#6-a-positive-trace-norm-gives-another-exact-formulation) satisfies H_N=|K_N|^2/N+O(poly(N)), and the [pointed A-Gram theorem](pointed_a_gram_period.md) expresses its equivalent pointed norm by positive polynomial coefficients. Those constructions retain the actual source and target. They are not an ordinary reflection-positive word trace, and their geometric exponential estimate and source overlap remain open. The present obstruction does not invalidate them. ## 5. Exact checks and scope [The audit](../experiments/audit_original_reflection_gram_obstruction.py) and [saved results](../experiments/original_reflection_gram_obstruction_results.json) check 17 literal original-source cases, braid indices two through four, including the normalized positive unknot chain, its actual inverse and (4). Seven exact root tests check the literal invariant block (5). Its characteristic polynomial is also checked symbolically. The complex positivity conclusion comes from the all-level proof, not from an inference about finite-field signs. This rules out the automatic Gram/reflection route and its basic alternating-transfer version. It neither rules out a separately proved positive family nor supplies a hyperbolic volume lower bound. A genuine selected geometric-cycle or source-compatible positive-channel theorem is still needed.

title: Exact cyclic variation and peeling the original Kashaev cut
text: # Exact cyclic variation and peeling the original Kashaev cut Research note, 28 October 2026. This is an exact support theorem for the original enhanced crossing in [the independently derived crossing convention](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md). It uses neither a Fourier gauge nor an asymptotic estimate. It applies to every braid position word and every assignment of crossing signs. ## 1. The local cyclic interval Write Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), q=exp(pi*i/N), and [x] for the representative in {0,...,N-1}. For a checked crossing with input (a,b) and output (c,d), put u=[b-a-1], v=[a-c], t=[c-d], h=[d-b]. For either crossing sign the support condition is exactly u+v+t+h=N-1, [a-b]=v+t+h. (1) Thus, after lifting b to an integer, the output is in the cyclic interval b <= d_lift <= c_lift <= a_lift=b+[a-b]. (2) This follows directly from the original four-index weight and the actual inverse, including its Q^(-1) normalization. Negative crossings permute the four factorial indices, so they have the same support. Given colors x=(x_1,...,x_b) and fixed sentinels L,R, define the integer cyclic variation V_(L,R)(x)=[L-x_1]+sum_(i=1)^(b-1)[x_i-x_(i+1)] +[x_b-R]. (3) Every supported adjacent crossing makes V nonincreasing. Indeed, with neighboring colors p,s, its three affected summands satisfy [p-c] <= [p-a]+v, [d-s] <= h+[b-s], [c-d]=t, v+t+h=[a-b]. (4) The inequalities are the elementary triangle inequality for nonnegative cyclic distance. Their defects are nonnegative multiples of N. ## 2. The actual source forces a face at every cut crossing The original enhancement is mu=-q S, where S e_j=e_(j+1 mod N). Fix the first cut color to zero. Each summation path in the actual weighted partial trace runs from x_in =(0,[A_2+1],...,[A_b+1]) x_out=(0,A_2,...,A_b). (5) This is a statement about an individual nonzero path, before summing coefficients. Choose L=0 and R=[A_b+1]. The interior tail distances in (3) agree at the two endpoints. Direct subtraction gives V(x_in)-V(x_out) = 0 if A_2=0, -N otherwise. (6) Monotonicity therefore forces A_2=0, and V must be constant throughout the path. Both inequalities in (4) are consequently equalities at every crossing. At any crossing in position 1, its left neighbor is the sentinel 0, so [0-c]=[0-a]+v. (7) Only these crossings change x_1. Telescoping (7) from x_1=0 back to x_1=0 shows that the sum of their nonnegative v's is zero. Therefore x_1=0 at EVERY stage; every position-1 crossing has v=0. (8) In particular, no original source path can lie in a chamber with all four crossing angles positive at every vertex. Formal strict concavity on such a chamber is not an assertion that the original source occupies that chamber. Before the first position-1 crossing, only position-2 crossings can change x_2. Their left equality in (4) makes [0-x_2] nondecreasing. It starts at N-1, because A_2=0. Hence x_2 stays 1 until the first position-1 crossing. After the last position-1 crossing the same quantity ends at zero, so x_2 is already zero and remains zero. Consequently: first position-1 crossing: u=v=0; last position-1 crossing: v=t=0. (9) If there is only one such crossing, both statements hold. If there are none, the original source has no supported paths. These statements remain valid for links; no scalar-endomorphism assertion is required. The original absolute crossing weight is N/|F_u F_v F_t F_h|, with F_j=product_(r=1)^j(1-Q^r). The reflection |F_j F_(N-1-j)|=N shows that BOTH end crossings in (9) have absolute weight exactly one. Every other cut crossing is on the tetrahedral three-corner face v=0. This is an actual source-support reduction. ## 3. Exact q-Pascal boundary operators Set T^sigma_(k,j)=(B_sigma)_(0,k ; 0,j). All indices below lie in {0,...,N-1}. Directly from the original crossing formula, T+_(0,j)=Q^(1-j), T+_(k,0)=0 for k>0, T+_(k,j)=(-1)^(j-1) Q^[k+(j-1)(j-2)/2] {k-1 choose j-1}_Q, 1<=j<=k<=N-1, (10) and all remaining entries vanish. The actual inverse crossing gives T-_(k,j)=Q^(k-j) conjugate(T+_(k,j)). (11) Thus T-_(0,j)=Q^(-1), and, for 1<=j<=k<=N-1, T-_(k,j)=(-1)^(j-1) Q^[-j-(j-1)(j-2)/2] {k-1 choose j-1}_(Q^-1). (12) For example, (10) follows by replacing N/F_(N-k) with bar_F_(k-1) and bar_F_r with (-1)^r Q^[-r(r+1)/2]F_r. The wrap row k=0 is kept; it is not an optional endpoint correction. In fact T-=(T+)^(-1). To prove this without compressing an inverse by fiat, let P be the positive-index block of T+, indexed r,i=0,...,N-2: P_(r,i)=Q^(r+1)(-1)^i Q^[i(i-1)/2]{r choose i}_Q. The finite q-binomial theorem gives the inverse q-Pascal matrix ({r choose i}_Q)^(-1) =(-1)^(r-i)Q^[(r-i)(r-i-1)/2]{r choose i}_Q. The resulting inverse of P is exactly (12). For the wrap row, the finite q-hockey-stick identity and the root specialization imply sum_(r=i)^(N-2) P_(r,i)=-Q^(-i). This gives the constant wrap row Q^(-1) in the inverse of T+. The formula is valid at every N>=2, without a prime-level assumption. ## 4. The full original scalar after peeling Let W be the braid word in its actual operator order, let w be its writhe, and let alpha=-q. Construct a word W_peel on b-1 heads by replacing every position-1 crossing by T+ or T-, and every crossing in position i>=2 by the same original B+ or B- in position i-1. No sign, ordering, Cartan scalar, or framing factor changes. For b>=2 the exact fixed-cut scalar is K_N(W)=(-q) alpha^(-w) [ Tr_(heads 3,...,b) ( W_peel (I tensor mu^(tensor(b-2))) ) ]_(0,1). (13) The trace in (13) is over the remaining heads except its first one. For b=2 this is just (-q)alpha^(-w)(W_peel)_(0,1). The outside factor -q is the retained pivotal coefficient on the removed ordinary trace of original head 2. The original writhe w is unchanged, including crossings replaced by T.
