Proof: expand the original weighted partial trace into paths. Section 2 forces every first-head label to zero and A_2=0. Restrict each crossing coefficient accordingly and perform the remaining sums. This gives (13) term by term, before using cancellation. It is stronger than a formal compression identity for arbitrary sources. The first-strand shell is therefore removed uniformly for every original braid. This differs from [the classical arbitrary-bridge deformation reduction](arbitrary_bridge_source_reduction.md): (13) is an identity of the actual finite quantum scalar. Iterating it without preserving the new T boundary operators is not justified. The remaining T/B word is complex, and this theorem supplies no geometric saddle coefficient or volume lower bound. ## 5. Reproducible checks `experiments/audit_original_source_cyclic_variation_peeling.py` checks the original matrices and their actual inverses over cyclotomic prime fields, both q-Pascal formulas and their product, every supported local cyclic-variation inequality at small levels, full original signed-word scalars against (13), and the forced faces path by path. The same-position trefoil and figure-eight words have identical support and absolute local weights, while their actual selected scalars differ. The source reduction therefore does not remove the need to control the original phases.

title: The oversized weak alias fails at the last Pachner norm wall
text: # The oversized weak alias fails at the last Pachner norm wall 28 October 2026. This traces the certified oversized weak alias of [the nine-tetrahedron counterexample](positive_geometric_alias_volume_counterexample.md) backward through its actual last $2\to3$ move. The first inverse step already has no boundary-preserving nonnegative angular preimage. The exact five-term map locates the norm divisor and its direction data. This does not prove that the original quantum source assigns zero to the wall. The exact audit is [audit_oversized_alias_last_pachner_wall.py](../experiments/audit_oversized_alias_last_pachner_wall.py), with [results](../experiments/oversized_alias_last_pachner_wall_results.json). It derives the local vertex labels from the actual saved face permutations, verifies the shape map in the certified cubic field, and checks the angle and norm identities symbolically. ## 1. A universal angular preimage criterion Label a triangular bipyramid by equatorial vertices $A,B,C$ and apices $D,E$. The actual old tetrahedron orderings in this example are $$ (D,A,B,C),\qquad (B,E,C,A). $$ Its new orderings are $$ (E,D,C,B),\qquad(E,D,B,A),\qquad(E,D,A,C). \tag{1} $$ Write each new angle triple as $(\alpha_j,\beta_j,\gamma_j)$, $j=0,1,2$. The new internal edge $DE$ and its opposite equatorial edge both carry $\alpha_j$. Each triple sums to $\pi$. Boundary angle preservation uniquely forces the old triples to be $$ \begin{split} X={}&(\beta_1+\gamma_2,\ \beta_0+\gamma_1,\ \gamma_0+\beta_2),\\ Y={}&(\gamma_0+\beta_1,\ \gamma_1+\beta_2,\ \beta_0+\gamma_2). \tag{2} \end{split} $$ For example, old edge $DA$ is split between the new $\beta_1$ and $\gamma_2$ corners; the other entries follow in the same way from the actual vertex labels. Both forced old sums are $$ \sum X=\sum Y=\sum_j(\beta_j+\gamma_j) =3\pi-\sum_j\alpha_j. \tag{3} $$ Consequently: **A boundary-preserving replacement by two nonnegative angle tetrahedra exists if and only if the new internal angle is exactly $2\pi$.** When this holds, (2) supplies the replacement and every old triple sums to $\pi$. If the new non-internal angles are positive, both old triples are positive. The three equatorial angle equations are then also preserved; for instance $$ X_0+Y_1=\alpha_0,\quad X_2+Y_2=\alpha_1,\quad X_1+Y_0=\alpha_2. \tag{4} $$ This is an angular boundary statement, not an assertion that arbitrary off-critical shape moduli or quantum integration cycles are transported by this linear map. In particular the angular image of an ordinary positive Pachner chart, and its continuous closure with its angle marks retained, has internal winding **one**. Exponentiating the edge equation and then admitting every weak nonnegative winding locus forgets this local support condition. ## 2. The certified face fails at the first reverse step The last forward move in the six-move sequence is $(1,0)$: old tetrahedron 1, face opposite its vertex 0, is adjacent to old tetrahedron 0. The actual face maps identify the new tetrahedra as final tetrahedra $0,1,2$ with orderings (1). Their new edge is final global edge 7, locally $01$ in every new tetrahedron. Its three opposite equatorial edges are final global edges $8,6,3$, respectively. At the oversized rational point the three new triples are $$ (0,1/20,19/20),\quad (0,2/5,3/5),\quad (0,1/10,9/10), \tag{5} $$ in units of $\pi$. Their new edge winding is zero. Formula (2) would force the old triples $$ X=(13/10,13/20,21/20),\qquad Y=(27/20,7/10,19/20), \tag{6} $$ each summing to $3$, rather than $1$. Equivalently, preserving the three equatorial angles would require their sum to be zero, whereas the sum of those six old angles is necessarily $2\pi$. Thus the face cannot be pulled back even one step through the previous nonnegative angular contour with its boundary marks fixed. No earlier part of the six-move chain is needed to find the obstruction. Each forced old local sum has an extra $2\pi$; removing it requires a non-positive angle or a change of branch/boundary charge. ## 3. The exact actual five-term map Use the cross-ratio convention $$ [p,q;r,s]=\frac{(p-r)(q-s)}{(p-s)(q-r)}. $$ Normalize $D=\infty,A=0,B=1,C=x$. If $y$ is the old native shape of $(B,E,C,A)$, then $$ E=\frac{xy}{x+y-1}. $$ For the new native shapes $u,v,w$ of (1), direct substitution gives $$ \boxed{\quad u=\frac{x}{1-y},\qquad v=\frac{(1-x)(1-y)}{xy},\qquad w=\frac{y}{1-x},\qquad uvw=1. \quad} \tag{7} $$ The audit verifies these identities for the actual old and new geometric shapes in the field $a^3-2a^2+3a-1=0$. The inverse is $$ \boxed{\quad x=\frac{u(1-w)}{1-uw},\qquad y=\frac{w(1-u)}{1-uw}. \quad} \tag{8} $$ In the positive geometric branch the new edge has the marked relation $$ \operatorname{Log}u+\operatorname{Log}v+ \operatorname{Log}w=2\pi i. \tag{9} $$ For a positive tetrahedron with angles $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$, the native shape is $$ z=e^{i\alpha}\frac{\sin\beta}{\sin\gamma}. $$ At (5), $\alpha=0$ and $\beta+\gamma=\pi$, so all three radial minimum shapes are exactly $$ u=v=w=1. $$ Their marked log sum is zero, not $2\pi i$. The inverse (8) is simultaneously $0/0$, on the norm divisor $1-uw=0$. The weak point is not a limit of the positive geometric branch: near three positive real unit shapes their principal arguments are all small positive numbers and cannot sum to $2\pi$. Away from the simultaneous corner, the inverse logarithmic connection forms have genuine divisor residues $$ \operatorname{Res}_{1-uw=0}d\log x =\operatorname{Res}_{1-uw=0}d\log y=-1. \tag{10} $$ At the simultaneous corner the numerator zeros matter. Blow up by $$ u=1+\varepsilon A,\qquad w=1+\varepsilon B, \quad AB(A+B)\ne0. $$ Then $$ x\longrightarrow\frac{B}{A+B},\qquad y\longrightarrow\frac{A}{A+B},\qquad x+y\longrightarrow1. \tag{11} $$ Thus the exceptional divisor retains the direction $A:B$. Its finite old shapes cannot both lie in the upper half-plane, since their sum is real. Formula (10) is a generic divisor residue; it must not be copied unchanged to the simultaneous corner where the numerator and denominator valuations cancel. ## 4. Exact comparison with the retained cyclic pentagon norms Use the primitive pentagon of [cyclic_tetrahedron_pentagon.md](cyclic_tetrahedron_pentagon.md), with its actual centers and roots: $$ a_N^N=1-U,\qquad b_N^N=1-V,\qquad h_N^N=H=1-U+UV. $$ The exact substitution for (7) is $$ U=w,\qquad V=x,\qquad H=1-y. \tag{12} $$ Its left centers $(V,(1-V)U)$ are precisely $(x,y)$. Its right centers are $$ \left(U,\frac{-UV}{1-U},\frac{V}{H}\right) =\left(w,\frac1{1-v},u\right). \tag{13} $$ The middle new shape has undergone the indicated quad rotation; its center cannot be frozen at $v$. Under (11), the three right norm-root powers behave as $$ \begin{split} a_N^N&=1-w\sim-\varepsilon B,\\ (h_N/a_N)^N&=\frac{1-y}{1-w} \sim-\frac1{\varepsilon(A+B)},\\ (a_Nb_N/h_N)^N&=\frac{(1-w)(1-x)}{1-y} \sim-\varepsilon A. \tag{14} \end{split} $$ Their valuations are therefore $(1/N,-1/N,1/N)$ on a compatible root cover. The middle center in (13) goes to infinity. The anchored cyclic pentagon theorem is localized away from these norm divisors and does not itself supply this simultaneous boundary extension or its source/co-source residues. Equivalently, a small loop of $\varepsilon$ around zero, at fixed generic direction $A:B$, changes the three compatible root frames by $(Q,Q^{-1},Q)$, where $Q=e^{2\pi i/N}$. The two old norm roots $b_N,h_N$ have no local winding at a generic finite direction. This is a concrete root-torsor monodromy charge. It cannot be removed by choosing the three right roots independently. Norm-root zeros cannot justify deleting the wall. For example, in the normalized finite atom of that note put $t=1-\text{center}$ and choose the spectral root $\mu=(1-t)^{1/N}$. Its eigenvalues obey $$ f_0=1,\qquad f_j=\frac{t^{j/N}}{(\mu;Q)_j}, \qquad D_j=\gamma f_j,\qquad \gamma^N=\left(\prod_jf_j\right)^{-1}. $$ For $1\le j<N$, exactly one denominator factor vanishes: $1-\mu\sim t/N$. All other factors are nonzero at a primitive $N$th root, including composite $N$. Hence $$ \operatorname{ord}_tD_0=\frac{N-1}{2N},\qquad \operatorname{ord}_tD_j=\frac{2j-N-1}{2N}\quad(1\le j<N). \tag{15} $$ There are both zeros and poles for every $N\ge2$, while their sum is zero. A vanishing norm root does not give a vanishing operator or source. This is consistent with the original [cap-wall residue theorem](cap_wall_fermat_quad_residue_transport.md): at its actual Fermat cusp a raw source has a compulsory simple pole with nonzero cap residue. The relevant boundary extension must retain those residues, the dual shift, and the central Jacobian, rather than assign zero from the norm alone. ### A removable singularity for the full normalized local product There is nevertheless a precise local extension, with a narrower claim than separate atom or source extension. Fix a generic holomorphic blow-up curve with $x(0)=x_0\notin\{0,1\}$ and $y(0)=1-x_0$ as in (11). Choose regular initial cyclic clock/shift frames and the compatible root component of the strict primitive pentagon. Then its **full normalized right three-atom product**, expressed between the common initial and final frames, extends holomorphically and invertibly across the ramified corner. Indeed the left centers are $x$ and $y$, whose limiting values are neither zero nor one. Their norm roots $b_N,h_N$ are therefore locally nonzero holomorphic functions; their normalization determinants are nonzero as well. The two left matrices are holomorphic and invertible. The common final splitting roots are $b_N$ times the initial first root and the initial second root divided by $h_N$; they remain regular and nonzero. On the punctured compatible root cover the exact pentagon identifies the right product with this left product. The equality supplies its removable extension. This conclusion retains all determinant roots and common-frame identifications. A raw product must retain its raw scalar from the pentagon theorem. No claim is made that its unnormalized individual factors have removable singularities. The argument gives no estimate uniform in $N$, no right to drop intermediate residues, and no comparison with an original knot source unless the required exterior source/co-source maps have also been transported. ## 5. The precise constructive target The local classical support test is now explicit: **an inverse positive angular Pachner replacement must retain new-edge winding one, not merely the exponentiated equation $uvw=1$.** For the certified excessive face, the failing move, its marked integer defect, the norm divisors, and the direction $A:B$ are known. The remaining quantum task is a matched source/carry extension of this last move across (14), proving how its marked $2\pi$ charge is represented and paired. Original integer degree conservation can retain information lost modulo $N$, but no identification of that integer carry with this geometric edge winding has been proved here. The existing Ward augmentation shows that some wall charge survives; it does not allow all walls to be discarded. In particular we have not proved a zero quantum coefficient for (5), nor inferred an oversized original period. What is available for a general proof is a universal local angular admissibility criterion and an exact divisor calculation on which the required quantum source theorem can be tested.

title: Independent audit of the partial geometric-support construction
text: # Independent audit of the partial geometric-support construction Audit, 27 October 2026, of [the partial geometric-support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md). The new partial-sum argument is valid given the repository's actual critical-chart/Hessian theorem and the global zero-extended finite-array dimension lemma. In particular its transverse moment argument avoids assuming the missing covariance of a full framing-period functional. This audit does not assert the selected global period is nonzero on the geometric branch. ## 1. Why a pair of actual external coordinates suffices Let V be the tangent space of actual independent flow coordinates, with symmetric Hessian B and two-dimensional radical R. A coordinate projection p:V->k^2 whose restriction to R is invertible exists by selecting a nonzero two-by-two minor of a basis of R. Put K=ker p. Then V=R direct_sum K and B restricted to K is nondegenerate: any vector orthogonal to K is also orthogonal to R, and hence to V; if it belongs to K it is zero. Fixing those two original coordinates therefore gives precisely a nondegenerate transverse stationary problem. Its internal critical equations have a unique local solution over the external coordinates and meridian. The full two-dimensional framed critical germ maps etale to those same external coordinates, so its internal solution is that unique solution. Thus the full critical gradient vanishes on the partially contracted branch, including its external components. The critical action consequently has zero frame derivatives and retains the marked unframed meridian/longitude derivative. This is stronger than choosing an arbitrary framing section after performing the finite sum: the external labels remain genuine independent variables in both the certificate and the formal block. ## 2. Exact contiguity survives the specialization used here The global certificate annihilates the entire zero-extended array, including the finite boundary. Dividing by a nonzero common central power of z+1 is valid for every fixed generic integer N, since q^N+1 is a nonzero rational function of q. The full-array identity therefore specializes regularly at z=-1, q=q_N, after fixed scalar denominators are cleared. A nonzero fixed rational operator can have only finitely many exceptional q_N levels. Separately, the interior cone-density argument makes the divided certificate a rational contiguity identity in independent variables q,x,z,Ahat,Bhat,t. That identity can also be specialized at z=-1. This separate independent-variable identity is essential: a relation only on a finite frame grid at one root would not suffice for the formal Gaussian block. The compact-product formal solution has exactly the same interior shift ratios, since its Bernoulli series obeys the functional equation P_Q(Qz)=P_Q(z)/(1-z) coefficientwise. Fixed singular arguments such as P_Q(Q) occur only in the retained common base line; all variables on the chosen regular geometric chart avoid the polar divisors. Thus the formal identity uses rational factor cancellation, never evaluation of an individual infinite compact product at a root. ## 3. The finite and formal moment repairs agree exactly The physical logarithmic internal coordinate is u_i=Hj_i, H=Log Q. Hence exp(v dot j) is implemented in the formal period by the phase S+v dot u, divided by H. Its critical point deforms uniquely because the transverse Hessian is invertible. The weighted formal period belongs to the original WKB line times k((H))[[v]]; its negative H orders may grow with the v degree. No uniform lower H bound over all v degrees is required. Formal Gaussian contraction satisfies integration by parts. For the quadratic kernel exp(x^t B x/(2H)), Wick covariance is -H B^(-1); contraction of a derivative of a monomial cancels the contraction of (Bx)_i/H times that monomial. Expanding cubic and higher vertices gives the same identity coefficientwise, with finitely many contractions in each allowed order. Thus a formal total derivative has zero contraction. Translate one internal coordinate by H. The weighted integrand then changes by exp(-v_i) after the corresponding formal change of coordinate. Equivalently the infinitesimal translation equation is G_v(H partial_i f)=-v_i G_v(f); integrating the translation parameter gives G_v(S_i f)=exp(-v_i)G_v(f). The H-dependent shift is a valid formal translation around the unique critical germ. The determinant half-line is continued with that same germ, rather than rechoosing its square root after shifting. External multiplication and the meridian step commute with this contraction. The latter shifts log M by H/2, while Ahat,Bhat are held fixed, and carries the critical point to its unique nearby one. It leaves H and the retained common base line fixed. There are no internal multiplication variables in the certificate's operator coefficients. Therefore its expansion in (S-1) has exactly the same least nonzero multi-degree after either finite weighted summation or formal transverse contraction. At that degree every positive moment is multiplied by a lower, identically zero operator coefficient. The same nonzero D_alpha annihilates the actual partial finite family and its nonzero transverse formal block. This would not justify an unproved integration functional in either of the two remaining framing directions. They remain external. ## 4. The leading-symbol conclusion and its scope After dividing the common scalar q-1 valuation, the operator has a nonzero leading classical symbol. The transverse formal block has unit leading amplitude and the actual marked longitude as its leading meridian ratio. Its annihilation therefore forces that symbol to vanish on the marked geometric longitude branch. The external coordinates range over a dense open frame chart by the etaleness in Section 1. They are algebraically independent over the geometric branch field; a purely transcendental extension does not split its irreducible rational defining polynomial. Thus the stated A_geo factor divisibility over Q(Ahat,Bhat) is valid. The conclusion concerns the specifically constructed partial-state annihilator. It neither identifies its minimal operator nor says that the full finite scalar contraction retains that component. In particular a nonzero local formal transverse block is not yet a nonzero selected global geometric contribution. No global cycle, Stokes, cancellation, or volume conclusion has been added here.

title: A geometric A-factor for an actual partially summed quantum state
text: # A geometric A-factor for an actual partially summed quantum state Research note, 27 October 2026. This proves a bulk geometric-support theorem for the original finite coefficient model. Leave two actual integer flow coordinates unsummed, and eliminate all remaining flow coordinates. The resulting finite family has a specifically constructed nonzero all-level meridian annihilator whose first nonzero classical symbol contains the marked geometric A-factor. The construction does not append a known classical factor. This partial family retains its two framing indices. Pairing them with the selected full finite source is a further operation. The theorem does not assert survival under that operation, a statement about the minimal scalar annihilator, or a volume limit. ## 1. The actual partial family Use a knot braid with `b` strands and `m` crossings, the balanced factorial boundary frame, and the original normalized cut average. Set q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=-M/q, Y=M^2. All crossings, the original pivot, the full zero-framing correction, the cut factor `1/N`, lift characters and base-only compact factors are retained. If the full ADO state is wanted, its complete original marked factor `d_N(M)` remains an external line; it is not absorbed into a formal unit or replaced by its value at completeness. Closing strands `1,...,b-1` gives a cofactor of the knot permutation matrix minus identity, with determinant `+1` or `-1`. Solve these closures integrally. The independent actual flow coordinates are k=(a_0,k_1,...,k_m), d=m+1. The remaining closure follows from total-index conservation. The summand is the actual product of the finite crossing and boundary coefficients, zero outside its finite integral support. On the regular geometric critical chart the Hessian has a two-dimensional radical equal to the tangent space of the framing torsor. This is the Morse--Bott statement for the **actual** coefficient phase proved in [the normal-period note](actual_geometric_normal_period.md). Select two members `chi_1,chi_2` of the displayed actual coordinate list whose differentials are independent on this radical. Such a pair exists because the radical is a two-dimensional subspace of the coordinate tangent space. No integral change of variables is made. Keep `chi=(a,b)` external and sum only over the remaining `r=d-2=m-1` coordinates `j`. The actual partial array is F_N^chi(M;a,b)=sum_(j in Z^r) I_N(q_N,-M/q_N;a,b,j). The sum is finite and includes its exact boundary. Its final contraction over the two external indices is the original reduced scalar state. The auxiliary off-root lift uses the same normalized cut trace and the same partial array, with generic `q`; topological invariance of that off-root lift is not a premise. For coefficient bookkeeping put z=q^N, Ahat=q^a, Bhat=q^b, t_i=q^(j_i). The physical phase coordinates are `A=Ahat^2=Q^a` and `B=Bhat^2=Q^b`. Keeping `Ahat,Bhat` avoids suppressing the genuine square-root characters in a meridian half-step. Alternatively one may work on their stated finite etale cover. Let `T` send `M` to `qM` (equivalently `x` to `qx`) while holding `q,Ahat,Bhat` fixed. ## 2. A global partial-array certificate The proof in [the finite-array annihilator note](finite_sum_annihilator.md) extends with the two external multiplication variables. Its summand ratios are proper and aligned rational functions in q,x,z,Ahat,Bhat,t_1,...,t_r. For `0<=e_x,e_z,e_A,e_B,e_T,beta_i<=R`, consider x^e_x z^e_z Ahat^e_A Bhat^e_B T^e_T S^beta I, where `S_i` shifts `j_i` by one and never shifts `a,b`. These are `(R+1)^(r+5)` independent formal Ore monomials. Their image span has dimension `O(R^(r+4))` over `Q(q)`. In the interior, clear the rational shift ratios by one common denominator whose Laurent degrees are `O(R)` in the `r+4` multiplication variables `x,z,Ahat,Bhat,t`. For the boundary proof, stratify every support inequality according to whether it is far inside, far outside, or has one specified integer value in an interval of length `O(R)`. If the near-boundary forms have rank `c` on `(N,a,b,j)`, there are `O(R^c)` consistent sets of their labels. On each resulting stratum, the associated `c` binomial relations leave `O(R^(r+4-c))` Laurent monomials after the fixed Smith reductions. The total contribution is again `O(R^(r+4))`. Supported shifts have nonzero common denominators on the stratum, exactly as in the original proof. Empty and lower-dimensional supports are included. Finite linear algebra therefore constructs a nonzero certificate P(x,z,Ahat,Bhat,T,S) I=0 (2.1) on the whole zero-extended array, with no multiplication by any internal `t_i`. Separate summand components, if present, can be retained in a direct sum, giving a common certificate. The full flow support has a nonempty open cone of strict inequalities: take all transfers small and positive compared with `N` and the free cut position near `N/2`. Every position is then `N/2+O(epsilon*N)`. This is unchanged by choosing a subset of the coordinates as external. Consequently (2.1), divided by a nonzero interior reference term, is a rational identity in all independent multiplication variables. The precise lattice-cone density proof is in [the sourced-telescoping audit](sourced_telescoping_geometric_support_criterion.md), Section 2. This step is needed: a relation only on isolated discrete frame values would not suffice for the formal geometric argument. ## 3. Root specialization and transverse moment repair Clear fixed coefficient denominators and divide the largest common central power `(z+1)^s` from the **whole** certificate, obtaining `P0`. For each fixed generic `N`, `q^N+1` is a nonzero rational function of `q`, so the global array identity survives this division. The finite summands are regular at `q_N`; their crossing factorial denominators have indices below `N`. Thus P1(x,Ahat,Bhat,T,S)=P0(x,-1,Ahat,Bhat,T,S) (3.1) is nonzero and annihilates the actual root partial arrays for all but finitely many levels. The same specialization is valid for the independent-variable interior contiguity identity. Expand in the commuting transverse shifts only: P1=sum_alpha D_alpha(x,Ahat,Bhat,T)(S-1)^alpha. Let `h0` be the least total degree with a nonzero coefficient, and choose any nonzero `D_alpha` of that degree. Give the finite internal sum independent weights `exp(v dot j)`. Exact translation of the whole finite zero-extended sum sends `S_i` to `exp(-v_i)`. At degree `v^alpha`, every positive moment multiplies a coefficient of degree below `h0`, and hence is zero. Therefore D_alpha(q_N,-M/q_N,q_N^a,q_N^b,T) F_N^chi(M;a,b)=0. (3.2) This is a genuine nonzero all-level operator for the actual partial family. All external labels and all finite boundary strata are kept. ## 4. The same certificate acts on the exact formal transverse period Write `H=Log Q=2 Log q`. In logarithmic physical flow coordinates, the actual interior coefficient has a formal realization I_form=C_beta(H) exp(S/H) a(u,H), with the original characters, `a(u,H)=a_0(u)(1+O(H))`, and `a_0` a unit on the chosen geometric chart. The retained base line `C_beta(H)` includes the cut average and the fixed compact factors. It is not evaluated at an individual root. This formal realization has the **exact** rational contiguity ratios, not merely their leading symbols. One construction uses the original monomials and the compact-product series, for variable arguments different from `0,1`, log P_Q(z)=Li_2(z)/H +(1/2)log(1-z) +sum_(n>=1) B_(2n) H^(2n-1)/(2n)! Li_(2-2n)(z). Its formal functional equation is `P_Q(Qz)=P_Q(z)/(1-z)`. This follows either coefficientwise from the Bernoulli generating function or by expanding the defining geometric-series logarithm. Thus its ratios agree to all orders with cancellation of the original finite factors. Signs and logarithm sheets are the ones fixed by the actual critical-correspondence calculation. The fixed singular argument `P_Q(Q)` stays in the base-only line. Pivotal monomials and the framing correction have their literal exact shift ratios as well. Now fix the two external coordinates `chi`. The remaining coordinate space complements the radical of the symmetric Hessian. The restricted `r` by `r` Hessian is therefore nondegenerate. The critical point of `S` in the remaining variables is unique in the chosen formal germ. The full geometric critical surface is etale over `chi`, so its unique point at each nearby external `chi` supplies a solution of these transverse equations. By uniqueness this is the same partial critical germ, and all of the full critical equations hold there. Its unweighted Gaussian contraction is nonzero, with leading amplitude a_0/sqrt(det(-H_perp)). (4.1) Introduce independent weights by replacing the phase with S_v(u)=S(u)+sum_(i=1)^r v_i u_i. The formal implicit-function theorem gives a unique critical point `u(v)` with `u(0)=u_*`, because `H_perp` is invertible. Formal stationary contraction there defines `Z_chi(v)`. It is a formal power series in `v` whose coefficients lie in the original WKB line times Laurent series in `H`. Its value at zero is nonzero. The action difference divided by `H` can produce increasingly negative finite `H` orders as the `v` degree grows; this is allowed. Formal stationary contraction is invariant under a translation of an internal integration coordinate. Explicitly, for the unit shift `u_i -> u_i+H`, substituting `y_i=u_i+H` in the formal Gaussian gives G_v(S_i f)=exp(-v_i) G_v(f). (4.2) This is an identity of formal stationary expansions at their corresponding critical points, with an elementary termwise proof. For one shifted coordinate its weighted phase is S(u+H e_i)+v dot u = S_v(u+H e_i)-H v_i. Its critical point is `u(v)-H e_i`. Centering at that point gives exactly the same Hessian, higher vertices, amplitude Taylor series and coordinate volume as centering `S_v` at `u(v)`. Only the constant phase changes, by `-H v_i`. Thus every Wick coefficient is multiplied by `exp(-v_i)`. No integration-by-parts theorem is a premise of this argument. No finite-array endpoint or framing endpoint is being discarded here: this is a formal contraction of precisely the `r` nondegenerate transverse variables. Both framing coordinates remain external throughout. The same formal contraction commutes with the meridian step `T`. The shifted critical point is the unique nearby one with the same external `Ahat,Bhat`; the formal construction and its retained half-density are natural under that base shift. Multiplication by external rational coefficients commutes as well. Apply this contraction to the exact interior identity (3.1). By (4.2), P1(x,Ahat,Bhat,T,exp(-v)) Z_chi(v)=0. The same least-degree moment coefficient used for the **finite** partial sum therefore gives D_alpha Z_chi(0)=0. (4.3) Unlike full framed integration, this implication has no missing relative-source covariance assumption. Nondegeneracy of the transverse block and leaving both framing coordinates external provide it directly. The subsequent [full Green-certificate calculation](full_certificate_framing_boundary.md) also transports the actual fully summed scalar operator to this transverse block. Its image includes two explicitly computed framing boundary currents. Their final endpoint and logarithmic-carry functional is retained; neither the formal residual Ward ideal nor the source torsor identities currently prove its cancellation. Thus the distinction between the present partial theorem and the full scalar claim is now an explicit source defect, not an omitted ordinary Gaussian variable. ## 5. The classical symbol has the geometric factor Divide `D_alpha` by its common scalar `(q-1)` valuation and clear remaining rational denominators. Call the resulting nonzero operator `Dhat`. Scalar division is valid both in the actual root identities (for all large `N`) and in the formal WKB line. Let d_cl(M,Ahat,Bhat,L) be its first nonzero classical symbol in the stated meridian and lift gauge. The exact preferred-longitude calculation for the actual phase gives leading [T Z_chi(0)/Z_chi(0)]=L_geom(M). Indeed the full critical gradient vanishes on the framing torsor, so the critical action has zero derivative in both frame directions. Its meridian derivative at fixed `chi` is therefore the same marked longitude derivative as on the unframed geometric branch. The transverse amplitude is a unit and does not alter this leading ratio. Equation (4.3) now gives d_cl(M,Ahat,Bhat,L_geom(M))=0. (5.1) The two selected flow coordinates are etale coordinates on the framing torsor. Consequently their values range over a dense open part of a two-dimensional frame space over the geometric branch. Equation (5.1) is therefore a relation over the purely transcendental frame coefficient field, not only at one frame. Let `A_geo(M,L)` denote the irreducible rational polynomial defining the Zariski closure of the marked geometric longitude branch, in the same sign, inverse and preferred-longitude convention. Its irreducibility is preserved by the independent transcendental frame variables. Clearing peripheral denominators in (5.1) proves A_geo(M,L) divides d_cl(M,Ahat,Bhat,L) over `Q(Ahat,Bhat)`, up to the recorded monomial and lift gauges. This is the claimed geometric-support theorem. In particular the constructed operator has positive meridian-shift order; a nonzero order-zero rational multiplier cannot annihilate this nonzero formal period on a dense open chart. The whole construction of `Dhat` uses actual finite coefficients, global boundary linear algebra, central specialization, and transverse moment extraction. It never multiplies an operator by an independently supplied `A_geo`. ### The actual certified module has a formal geometric line quotient There is a corresponding precise formal torsor statement. Let `K_geo` be the algebraic function field of the marked geometric gluing branch and its two retained framing coordinates, with the recorded half-density and sign covers. Put `h=Log q`, and let `Z_geo^chi` be the nonzero transverse block just constructed. On this field the shift is the formal automorphism `sigma=exp(h delta)`, where `delta=M partial_M` fixes both framing coordinates and extends uniquely to the algebraic and half-density covers in characteristic zero. Its shift ratio b_geo=T(Z_geo^chi)/Z_geo^chi in K_geo[[h]]^*, b_geo|_(h=0)=L_geom has algebraic coefficients. The meridian-independent base-only line cancels in this ratio. The exponent difference has leading `Log L`, and its higher derivatives are algebraic after exponentiating that leading logarithm; the transverse amplitudes and all their meridian derivatives are algebraic as proved in the normal-period calculation. Right division in the meridian Ore ring over `K_geo((h))` gives Dhat=Q_geo (T-b_geo)+r_geo. Applying this to `Z_geo^chi` gives `r_geo Z_geo^chi=0`. This period is nonzero in its formal exponential line, so `r_geo=0`. Thus `T-b_geo` is a right factor of an operator constructed from actual partial arrays. Equivalently its cyclic module has a formal rank-one quotient on the marked geometric branch. It is not asserted to be a rational generic factor or a quotient of the minimal full scalar operator. The action of this line is the marked actual crossing regulator action: in the `h` convention its complete imaginary value is `Vol/2`, with the original peripheral and base-only lines retained. The existing formal Gaussian comparison transports it to the positive triangulation's marked regulator line by an algebraic formal unit. No convergence, rootwise value of that formal unit, or nonzero coefficient in the selected scalar period follows from this factor. In fact every nonzero moment operator obtained from a whole partial-array certificate by this procedure annihilates the same formal block. Their generated left ideal in the localized meridian Ore ring over `Q(q,M,Ahat,Bhat)` is nonzero. Every element annihilates both the actual partial arrays and the formal block. Its unique monic least-order generator consequently also has a geometric classical factor after taking its first nonzero `(q-1)` symbol. This defines a minimal **certified partial** operator; it is not asserted to equal the minimal annihilator of one selected scalar solution. Clear its coefficient denominators in a polynomial Ore combination before evaluating discrete frame labels; this retains identities also at labels where the localized formula itself has a pole. The full literature normalization is transported exactly, if desired. For the full partial array `N_N^chi=d_N(M)F_N^chi`, retain d_N(M)=i^(N+3)M^(N-1)/(1+M^2+...+M^(2N-2)), g_N(q,M)=d_N(qM)/d_N(M) =q^(N-1)(q^2 M^2-1)/(M^2-1) * (M^(2N)-1)/(q^(2N)M^(2N)-1). At the ACTUAL root q^N=-1 its meromorphic meridian-germ restriction is g_bar(q,M)=-q^(-1)(q^2 M^2-1)/(M^2-1). The constructed full ROOT operator is the Ore gauge Dhat_full=Dhat|_(T -> g_bar^(-1) T). This notation means ordered Ore substitution, not commutative substitution of powers. Its all-level identity is a meromorphic whole MERIDIAN-germ identity ON THE ROOT FIBERS, with the complete displayed `d_N` retained. For a whole quantum-normal source use g_N, or its actual independent powers z=q^N,w=M^(2N), before specializing. The expression g_bar is only its root restriction; their q-normal derivatives are not identified. Equivalently, g_N=q^(-1)z (q^2 M^2-1)/(M^2-1) * (w-1)/(z^2 w-1). Here the actual meridian step sends w to z^2 w. It is not a constant dual-nome coordinate off the root. Also g_N has limit +1 at q=1 with N FIXED, whereas the root-character-specialized g_bar below has limit -1. These are different classical regimes; the root-symbol statement is not a claim that their fixed-N whole quantum-normal symbols agree. The [independent peripheral-shift audit](full_peripheral_shift_root_and_normal_audit.md) checks this full ratio, the ordered gauge direction and its retained-character normal discrepancy explicitly. At generic classical `M`, `g_bar->-1`, so its geometric factor is `A_geo(M,-L_full)` in the full shift convention. The regular completion at `M=1` uses the original source lattice and complete normalization germ; the separate pole of the localized `g_bar` is not evaluated there. ## 6. Scope of the result The proof applies to every knot for which the audited regular geometric critical chart and Hessian-radical statement hold. In particular its braid complexity is unrestricted: it is not confined to two-bridge, twist, alternating, or a fixed bridge number. The geometric input and the retained SL2 sign cover are exactly those of the actual normal-period theorem; no literature asymptotic or creative-telescoping theorem is a premise. The finite partial state and its operator depend on the braid and the selected two flow coordinates. They have been constructed from the original coefficient model; no topological invariance of this two-index extension is asserted. Summing its remaining two indices with the original selected source requires further elimination. The geometric factor can be lost in that pushforward. The theorem does not identify the full scalar minimal quantum-A operator, the selected global geometric cycle, Kashaev's volume growth, or the value of any individually normalized compact product at a root. ## 7. A source-preserving Fourier partial family has the same geometric factor There is now a second actual partial family with a different and useful framing polarization. It requires the FULL four-port tensor, not only its double diagonal. Use the original first-cut rank-one source and Fourier-transform the second identity wire as in [the whole polarization construction](actual_two_cut_fourier_polarization_and_cap.md). At a primitive root put V_jb=Q^(jb), with V^(-1)_bj=Q^(-bj)/N, and T^V=(I tensor V)T(I tensor V^(-1)). Define the RAW partial family by Ftilde_N(M;a,j)=sum_c (T^V)_(c,j;a,j) =(1/N)sum_(b,nu,u) Q^(j nu) W_N(M;a,b,nu,u). (7.1) Here W_N is the ORIGINAL raw open coefficient on its integral flow coset, T_(a-nu,b+nu;a,b)=sum_u W_N, and u has m-1 internal chord coordinates. All four actual port bounds and every original phase/pivot/peripheral line remain in W_N. The Fourier factor 1/N in (7.1) is not the first-cut source normalization. The original selected scalar is exactly F_N(M)=(1/N)sum_(a,j) Ftilde_N(M;a,j). (7.2) Indeed the sum over j kills every nonzero offset nu in its actual range |nu|<N and restores the identity second closure. It does not replace the physical b sum by evaluation of a momentum function. Equivalently, partial trace on that wire is invariant under the whole invertible basis change. If its first cut were also made diagonal BEFORE this operation, charge conservation would force nu=0, and the resulting array would be independent of j. The sum over c in (7.1) is essential. The following assertions hold under the regular geometric input of this note. **Fourier partial support theorem.** There is a nonzero all-level meridian operator constructed from (7.1) by finite coefficient linear algebra and moment repair, whose first nonzero classical symbol contains the same marked geometric A-factor. On a dense geometric framing chart its nonzero normal block is parametrized by the original cut position and the second physical wave momentum. At the discrete-faithful complete point these are birational framing coordinates; no new quadratic framing cover is required. This does not assert a geometric factor after the final selected sum (7.2). Here is the certificate and specialization proof, including the distinction between root data and the whole q-normal source. First keep a,j external and b,nu,u internal. Their number is r_F=m+1. Removing both physical cuts leaves the same connected graph, so the integral tree particular flow makes W_N proper with linear finite support, exactly as in the two-cut proof. The added monomial Q^(j nu) is also proper: shifting nu multiplies it by the external character Q^j, and shifting any remaining flow has its stated rational coefficient. There is a nonempty strict cone: take all original transfers small and positive, the original positions near N/2, and the open offset nu in a sufficiently small two-sided interval about zero. The Fourier index j may independently range through a strict subinterval of its original head. The formula on the right of (7.1), with the same monomial Fourier kernel at generic q, is a convenient AUXILIARY whole coefficient lift. At every root it is the literal actual family. Its common factor 1/N can be kept as a source line or removed from a homogeneous coefficient certificate, since internal and meridian shifts fix it. The finite support-stratum count of Section 2 applies with r replaced by r_F and the second external character replaced by q^j, retaining its square-root mark when required. Thus a nonzero whole certificate with no internal multiplication characters exists. Strip its largest common q^N+1 power from the ENTIRE certificate before root evaluation. The least internal-shift moment then gives a nonzero meridian operator annihilating the actual root arrays (7.1), by the exact same zero-extended summation identity as Sections 2--3. This auxiliary lift is not identified with the actual generic-q inverse Fourier matrix. The source-preserving whole basis change uses the Vandermonde V(Q) and its Lagrange inverse, with their explicit connection and endpoint carries. Its inverse equals Q^(-bj)/N at the root but generally has different normal jets. Thus the argument proves an operator identity for the literal ALL-LEVEL ROOT partial family; it does not discard the source normal terms in the whole polarization theorem. All M-dependent identities at a fixed root still agree, since the two Fourier bases are independent of M. The geometric normal block comes from the macroscopic open coefficient phase, rather than extrapolating a bounded-band Taylor formula to offsets of order N. Put t=H nu, v=Hj. Its phase is Phi=S_open(a,b,t,u)+v t. (7.3) On the original geometric critical manifold t=0, the old internal equations hold and partial_t S_open=Log p_e, in the actual balanced boundary frame. Therefore (7.3) is stationary precisely on the selected geometric germ with v=-Log p_e, eta=exp(v)=p_e^(-1). The original cut position together with p_e is etale on a nonempty geometric open chart. The bordered-Hessian proof in [the Fourier normal-block theorem](actual_fourier_polarized_geometric_normal_block.md) then gives a nondegenerate (m+1)-dimensional internal Hessian. Its mixed entry along the old fixed-cut framing tangent is the nonzero derivative of Log p_e. The added Fourier pair has its literal factor 1/N and supplies no new exponential action. The geometric critical value is still S_geo, since t=0. The auxiliary coefficient realization has the same exact proper ratios and full marked formal phase (7.3). It consequently has a nonzero formal Gaussian block. Translate its internal variables in the whole certificate and extract the least weighted moment as in Section 4. The operator obtained from the finite root arrays annihilates that SAME normal block. Section 5 now applies: its first nonzero classical symbol vanishes at the marked geometric longitude and has the geometric A-factor. The formal Ore right-factor statement follows by the same division argument. The original peripheral dimension line is transported using the ordered Ore gauge already displayed above. Its separate whole normal adapter is not replaced by a root norm in this proof. Nor is the sum over j interpreted as the old cap point eta=0: the correct new source is the finite j sum in (7.2), with every tail/carry retained on inserted currents. Survival and the volume norm after that last sourced pushforward remain unproved. ## 8. The original root period has a one-exterior-index Fourier presentation One of the two exterior sums can be removed EXACTLY, without replacing the first-cut source by a double diagonal. The [fixed-column/Ward theorem](actual_one_index_fourier_source_and_ward_reduction.md) proves that the fully reclosed one-cut word C_N(M) is scalar on the actual root family. This follows directly from its true K,F intertwining: K has distinct eigenvalues and F connects all successive head basis vectors with nonzero coefficients. Hence every first column sum is the same selected scalar. In the RAW Fourier presentation above, sum_j Ftilde_N(M;a,j)=sum_c(C_N(M))_(c,a)=F_N(M) for EVERY a in [0,N-1]. (8.1) The full peripheral factor, if present, multiplies both sides as its original line. Equation (8.1) keeps the sum over c in (7.1). Replacing it by c=a before Fourier polarization would destroy the momentum coordinate and is a different operation. This statement also has a controlled WHOLE source defect. The whole actual balanced K,F Ward contraction gives h delta C=C-I Tr(C)/N, delta C=((Ad K-I)C, F C-K^(-1)C K F). If lambda_a(C)=sum_c C_(c,a) and Phi is the original rank-one average, then (lambda_a-Phi)(I)=0 and therefore lambda_a-Phi=(lambda_a-Phi) h delta. (8.2) Its primitive and the original source adapters are explicit in the fixed-column theorem. Thus (8.1) is not extended to an arbitrary off-root lift by setting its Ward defects to zero. The actual whole normal derivatives act on every term of (8.2). There is a uniform way to fix a good interior sequence of first input indices while retaining the geometric normal block. The bad first-position fibers of its nonempty algebraic open chart form a FINITE set: after writing its finitely many shape/Jacobian units as rational functions of the first position and momentum, an entire fiber can fail only at a common zero of their nonzero coefficient functions. Also exclude the finitely many first half-phases where the already constructed operator's nonzero leading symbol becomes identically zero in M, the second exterior character and L. Clearing the specified denominators first makes this an ordinary polynomial coefficient test. Choose a rational theta=k/d in (0,1) such that A_*=exp(2pi*i*k/d), alpha_*=exp(pi*i*k/d), avoid these finite bad sets, including A=1. Such a choice exists because these algebraic phases are infinite. Put a_N=floor(kN/d), r_N=kN modulo d. At the original root its physical and half clocks are EXACTLY A_N=A_* q_N^(-2r_N/d), Ahat_N=alpha_* q_N^(-r_N/d). (8.3) These indices are in the strict interior for all sufficiently large N. For each fixed residue class r_N=r the right side is one fixed algebraic q germ on a marked d-th-root cover, and it tends to the chosen good geometric framing phase. The same nondegenerate normal block therefore persists there, with its original geometric action. Substitute Ahat=alpha_* q^(-r/d) in the operator of Section 7, after its stated coefficient localization. This is an Ore homomorphism because the meridian shift fixes q and both exterior frame characters. By the choice of alpha_* its first nonzero classical symbol stays nonzero and still has the SAME geometric A-factor. On N residue class r the specialized operator annihilates the actual one-index partial family G_(N,r)(M;j)=Ftilde_N(M;a_N,j), F_N(M)=sum_j G_(N,r)(M;j). (8.4) Its formal geometric line is now over the marked geometric representation field and ONE momentum coordinate. No restriction to a knot family or bridge number has been introduced. The values G_(N,r) still contain the original bulk finite contractions; this is one exterior source index, not an asserted closed single-product formula for the knot invariant. For a WHOLE quantum-normal source calculation, (8.3) must not freeze the underlying power coordinates. Before root restriction, the actual fixed-N clocks are A_N=(Q^N)^(k/d) Q^(-r/d), Ahat_N=(q^N)^(k/d) q^(-r/d), (8.5) with the logarithmic/finite-cover marks Log(Q^N)=N Log Q and Log(q^N)=N Log q. Their root values give (8.3), but their normal derivatives retain the N terms. The operators in (8.4) are certified ALL-LEVEL ROOT operators, as in Section 7; no whole q-normal identification is inferred from (8.3). If one wants a single operator across these finitely many residue classes, take a common LEFT multiple of their nonzero specialized operators in the localized meridian Ore ring and then clear the original denominators. A naive ordered product is not justified. The per-residue statement (8.4) already suffices for the present source reduction. It still does not prove that the final one-index sum retains its geometric block with the regulator norm. That is the remaining selected-period theorem. The [actual Fourier current theorem](actual_fourier_source_cancellation.md) now provides a rigorous scope test for this last step. The literal second-port Cartan current has zero whole second partial trace, yet on the good-A chart its formal geometric block is a nonzero derivative of the block above with the SAME action. Its own partial certificate still has a geometric classical factor, while its selected scalar is identically zero. Thus a geometric partial factor is not a certificate of survival under the last source. The final theorem must control the actual class in the cyclic source/current quotient, including the polar and normal data.

title: The peripheral delta module and the normal derivative of the knot period
text: # The peripheral delta module and the normal derivative of the knot period Research note, 26 October 2026. This identifies a boundary component which any positive-volume proof must retain. The ordinary principal-root colors force polynomial growth if a polynomial annihilator acts nontrivially on the complete-color delta vector. When that boundary component is retained, a simple rank condition expresses the actual complete period as the first normal derivative of a homogeneous kernel line. The derivative has a polynomially bounded source. Its size is therefore an inverse-operator and source-coupling problem, in the natural cyclic trace metric. These are necessary-condition and conditional period theorems, with uniform proofs below. The rank condition and the boundary-factor condition are not asserted for every hyperbolic knot operator. The regulator norm and original volume conjecture remain unproved. The subsequent [actual Weyl-descent proof](actual_weyl_descent.md) constructs P=B*(Y-1) from the primitive minimal normal operator for every knot and proves its unitary reciprocity. Thus those symmetry data in Section 6 are available for the canonical actual operator. The special-fiber injectivity and norm estimates remain additional; Section 2's necessity test still concerns every polynomial annihilator. The subsequent [peripheral-fusion proof](actual_peripheral_fusion.md) derives the regular normal boundary lattice from the actual fundamental parallel, retaining its pole before changing lattice. Its odd normal state w_N=(M-M^(-1))F_N has K_N=(1/2)partial_(Log M)w_N at M=1. The adjacent-color splitting there has a nonzero square-zero Casimir residue whose pivotal partial trace is identity. These exact quantum extension data do not establish the root-fiber rank or the regulator norm. The subsequent [ramified Weyl-fibre theorem](ramified_weyl_fibre.md) retains this derivative as an ordinary coordinate of a descended algebraic fibre over s=((U-1)/(U+1))^2. Its - sector generator is z e_- rather than a vector discarded by setting z=0 first. The source equation and complete functional then hold in that fibre, with their original rank qualifications. An explicit dimension formula gives signatures for which negative-sector injectivity cannot hold; saturated kernels and further lifting data remain available. No regulator norm is inferred from this descent. ## 1. Fixed state, ring, and principal-root bound Use the actual literature state in [the ADO audit](kashaev_ado_pointing.md), with q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q_N=q_N^2, Y=M^2, F_N(Y) Laurent polynomial, K_N=F_N(1)=<K>_N, F_N(Q_N^r)=C_r(q_N), 1<=r<N. The [regular-period theorem](regularized_kashaev_period.md) reconstructs the positive path trace directly from the actual fundamental crossing. For any fixed b-strand knot braid it proves |C_r(q_N)|<=D_N=sin(pi/N)^(1-b)<= (N/2)^(b-1). (1.1) Take a specified actual annihilator with denominators cleared and recorded, in the polynomial quantum torus R=C(q)[Y^(+/-1),T^(+/-1); T Y=q^2Y T], P=sum_(j=0)^d a_j(q,Y)T^j, a_j in C[q^(+/-1),Y^(+/-1)]. (1.2) An initial power of T permits the nonnegative shift convention. The [existence](finite_sum_annihilator.md) and [squared-meridian descent](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) theorems supply such an actual operator, but do not yet identify its classical geometric factors. ## 2. A nonzero complete column forces polynomial growth For 0<=i<=d put r_i(q)=a_i(q,q^(-2i)). (2.1) If r_i is not identically zero, it has finite vanishing order nu_i at q=1. For all large N, |r_i(q_N)|>=c_i N^(-nu_i). Evaluate the actual equation at Y=Q_N^(-i). Its i-th term is r_i(q_N)K_N. If N>d, every other term uses a noncomplete orbit color, and hence has modulus at most C_P D_N by (1.1). The fixed Laurent coefficients are bounded on the unit torus. Consequently |K_N|<=C N^(b-1+nu_i). (2.2) Thus a positive exponential volume rate requires a_i(q,q^(-2i))=0 for every i. (2.3) Equivalently every coefficient is divisible in the Laurent ring by q^(2i)Y-1. Polynomial division at its nonzero root proves this equivalence. Hence the required factorization is exactly P=B*(Y-1), B in R with Laurent coefficients. (2.4) This is right multiplication: its i-th coefficient is b_i(q,Y)*(q^(2i)Y-1). A monic operator over C(q,Y) can have poles on those divisors; an ordinary evaluation of that localized operator cannot replace the cleared equation used above. The result is a dichotomy, not a proof that all hyperbolic operators already satisfy (2.3). If an actual hyperbolic-knot annihilator violated it, (2.2) would contradict its positive-volume conjecture. Conversely (2.3) alone supplies no exponential lower bound. ## 3. The missing component is a fixed boundary module At generic q define Delta=R/R*(Y-1), delta=class of 1. It has C(q)-basis T^j delta, j in Z, and Y T^j delta=q^(-2j)T^j delta. Therefore P delta=0 is exactly (2.3). The module is simple at indeterminate q: polynomial interpolation in Y isolates one term of any nonzero finite combination of these distinct eigenvectors, and powers of T then generate all of them. Every vector is killed by a nonzero polynomial in Y. Localizing the meridian to C(q,Y) therefore kills Delta completely. For a polynomial annihilator ideal I, positive exponential growth would imply I is contained in R*(Y-1). Its cyclic module would have Delta as a quotient. For one specified P satisfying (2.4), this quotient already follows without a volume assumption. The generic norm torsor over C(q,Y) needs a meridian lattice to retain this boundary datum. At the actual root, impose T^N=1 as well. The resulting Delta_N is the N-dimensional clock-and-shift module with Y^N=T^N=1, at every parity and composite level. It is irreducible because the N distinct Y-eigenvalues and their cyclic shift generate all matrix units. On functions of the root orbit the complete delta vector is e_0=(1,0,...,0), e_0(Y)=S_N(Y)/N modulo Y^N-1. Thus P annihilates this vector on the central fiber when (2.4) holds. If c_N=(0,C_1,...,C_(N-1)), the actual state there is F_bar_N=c_N+K_N e_0. (3.1) Every vector in this affine line satisfies the same special operator equation and has the same ordinary-color pointing. The complete coefficient is fixed by extension away from the central fiber. This affine ambiguity is not permission to change the actual state. At q=1, (2.4) also gives the vertical factor Y-1 in the classical polynomial symbol. Removing vertical factors to state an A-curve equation discards this specific boundary-module datum. The marked integral/meridian extension must therefore accompany that curve. ## 4. The actual full period is a normal derivative Assume (2.4) for the specified operator. Work near U=Y^N=1, with t=U-1 and the fixed root germs Y_r(t)=Q_N^r*(1+t)^(1/N), 0<=r<N. Represent B by the cyclic matrix B_N(t): its row r, column r+j modulo N receives b_j(q_N,Y_r(t)). Write B_N(t)=B_0+t B_1+O(t^2), (B_1)_(r,r+j)=(1/N)(Y*d/dY)b_j(q_N,Q_N^r). (4.1) Retain the full vector of the actual state and put v_N(t)_r=(Y_r(t)-1)F_N(Y_r(t)), v_N(t)=v_0+t v_1+O(t^2). Since P F_N=0, B_N(t)v_N(t)=0. At the special fiber, (v_0)_0=0, (v_0)_r=(Q_N^r-1)C_r(q_N), 1<=r<N, B_0 v_0=0, B_0 v_1=-B_1 v_0, (v_1)_0=K_N/N. (4.2) The last identity keeps the zero of Y-1 until differentiation: Y_0'(0)=1/N. In particular the complete full ADO value is exactly N_N(1)=eta_N (v_1)_0, eta_N=i^(N+3). (4.3) Indeed the full state, before specialization, is N_N(M)=eta_N M^(N-1)*(Y-1)F_N(Y)/(U-1). Its poles, its sign character, and its phase have all been retained. The normal derivative realizes their cancelled whole germ. Suppose now that rank B_0=N-1. (4.4) The known nonzero vector v_0 spans its kernel; the reference component is Q_N-1 because C_1=1. The solutions of the inhomogeneous normal equation in (4.2) form a genuine affine torsor under C*v_0. Since (v_0)_0=0, its complete-coordinate functional is constant. Thus (4.2) determines K_N exactly, without choosing the derivative of a central normalization unit. More explicitly replacing v_N(t) by c(1+t)v_N(t), c(1)=1, adds c'(1)v_0 to v_1. The complete value in (4.3) does not change. This is the anchored normal-period comparison, with its specified root germs. The rank condition is additional to the existence of the actual operator; it is not assumed for every knot. The regular complete scalar of the preceding note is R_N(1)=(v_1)_0-p_N(1), |p_N(1)|<=D_N. (4.5) So the normal derivative and that regularized field-trace period give the same positive-volume target. ## 5. The first obstruction selects a point of the delta torsor Let D(t)=diag(Y_r(t)-1), so P_N(t)=B_N(t)D(t). At zero, Im D(0) is the hyperplane of vectors with zero complete coordinate. Its kernel is C*e_0. Since ker B_0=C*v_0 is inside this hyperplane, rank P_0=N-2, ker P_0=span(e_0,c_N). (5.1) The first lifting obstruction is the linear map kappa:ker P_0 -> coker P_0, x -> [P_1 x]. (5.2) This is the usual first Bockstein: a lift x+t x_1 solves the equation through first order exactly when P_0 x_1+P_1 x=0. In particular P_1 e_0=(1/N)B_0 e_0. This is not in Im P_0. Otherwise e_0 would differ from a vector in Im D(0) by a member of ker B_0, also in Im D(0), a contradiction. The actual vector c_N+K_N e_0 lifts. Hence kappa has rank one on the two-dimensional kernel, and its kernel selects that exact line. Choose any left null vector ell of P_0 with ell P_1 e_0 nonzero. The period is the exact ratio K_N=-ell P_1 c_N/(ell P_1 e_0). (5.3) Changing ell subject to this condition gives the same answer, because the actual lift exists. This derivative pairing records the boundary extension that the ordinary special kernel omits. Under (4.4) the rank loss in P is exactly one simple Smith factor; no unverified higher-order lift is being used. More singular cases need the higher jets retained in the [bounded-jet construction](bounded_meridian_jets.md). ## 6. A bounded source and the exact inverse-matrix period Use the Hermitian norm on the orbit coming from the cyclic trace; the unnormalized Euclidean version differs only by the common factor N^(1/2). The fixed Laurent coefficients give ||B_1||<=C_B/N, ||v_0||<=2D_N*sqrt(N). (6.1) For the first inequality write B_1 as a finite sum of diagonal coefficient matrices times unitary cyclic shifts, and bound each Y-derivative on the unit torus. Thus the normal equation has a polynomially bounded, explicitly specified source. Let B_0^+ be the Moore--Penrose inverse. Since e_0 is perpendicular to ker B_0, every solution of (4.2) has the same complete coordinate, and exactly K_N=-N*e_0^* B_0^+ B_1 v_0. (6.2) If s_N is the smallest nonzero singular value of B_0, then |K_N|<=2 C_B D_N sqrt(N)/s_N. (6.3) Consequently positive volume growth would force an exponentially large inverse norm in this specified boundary problem. The source itself cannot supply that positive exponent. Small singular values alone are insufficient: (6.2) also retains the source and the complete-coordinate pairing. In a singular-vector decomposition it is the sum of their two overlaps divided by the corresponding singular values. No largest-eigenvalue prescription is being used. The geometric action already has imaginary value Vol at completeness, by the [actual action proof](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md). What remains is to prove that (6.2), with these exact overlaps, has that regulator norm. Neither (6.3) nor the existence of a geometric critical point proves that estimate. Extra left operator factors can also create small singular values with zero relevant overlap. ### A Weyl symmetry isolates the relevant inverse There is a stronger reduction when the *actual operator* has a checked reciprocity. Write R h(Y)=h(Y^(-1)), Q=q^2, and suppose J=-Y R, J'=c(q,Y)T^d R, B J=J' B, c(q,Y)c(q,Q^(-d)Y^(-1))=1, |c(q,Y)|=1 on the unit torus. (6.4) Both give unitary involutions on the root orbit; B_0 intertwines them. Their -1 eigenspaces are orthogonal to the +1 eigenspaces, and e_0 has J-eigenvalue -1. The factor Y-1 is the squared-meridian form of the Weyl denominator, up to the retained monomial M. If J v_0=v_0, differentiating the operator identity at U=1 proves J' B_1 v_0=-B_1 v_0. Explicitly inversion sends t to -t+O(t^2), and the domain involution has derivative J/N. Applying the differentiated identity to v_0 kills the terms containing B_0 v_0 and leaves exactly this source parity. Thus only the -1 symmetry sector enters the complete normal period. Under (4.4) this source parity is automatic whenever K_N is nonzero. Indeed the one-dimensional kernel makes J v_0=epsilon*v_0. If epsilon=-1, the same differentiation gives source parity +1. The -1 part of v_1 would then be a multiple of v_0 and have zero complete coordinate, forcing K_N=0. More generally (4.4) can be weakened in this symmetry setting: it suffices that J v_0=v_0 and B_0 is injective on the -1 domain. The actual derivative places the source in its image. Extra +1 kernel vectors do not affect the value. Writing the restricted Moore--Penrose inverse as B_-^+, the exact period is K_N=-N e_0^* B_-^+ B_1 v_0. (6.5) It is this inverse and its specified source that need a regulator norm theorem. Small singular values in the other symmetry sector make no contribution. Reciprocity is additional quantum data; it is not assumed merely from the classical A-curve's inversion symmetry. The subsequent [actual-state proof](actual_weyl_descent.md) now derives this reciprocity for the primitive minimal normal operator of every knot, and also proves J v_0=v_0 directly. An arbitrary nonprimitive or left-multiplied operator still needs its own checked intertwiner and lattice. There is an explicit Hilbert-90 descent of the reflected kernel frame. If its generic rational kernel is a C(U)-line, reciprocity gives J v=gamma(U)v, gamma(U)gamma(U^(-1))=1. When J v_0=v_0, gamma is a unit at U=1 with gamma(1)=1. Set g(U)=(1+gamma(U))/2. Direct division gives g(U)/g(U^(-1))=gamma(U). Thus g*v is J-invariant and g(1)=1. This is an explicit frame change of the same pointed line, not a replacement knot state. Its derivative adds g'(1)v_0 and leaves the complete normal period unchanged. Zeros or poles of this frame elsewhere remain part of the lattice data. This is quadratic Hilbert 90 on the central involution, after the normal pointing has already fixed the value at the branch point. The ambient cyclic orbit also retains a precise signed dihedral relation. Direct multiplication gives J T J=Q*T^(-1). With the actual ADO character kappa=-q^(-1), put T_tilde=kappa*T. Then J T_tilde J=T_tilde^(-1), T_tilde^N=kappa^N=(-1)^(N-1). (6.6) Thus the uniform half-root lambda=-q, lambda^2=Q, is compatible with the Weyl action and with the full even-level sign. This is an action on the ambient orbit module. It does not assert that the scalar operator's rational solution line is stable under T; only its checked reflection intertwiner and central frame descent are used. Neither Hilbert-90 descent nor this finite symmetry supplies the missing regulator norm. ## 7. A fixed initial form bounds the rational root period rank There is a simple separate certificate for generic rational rank. For any Laurent polynomial operator L, let r be the least Y-exponent in its coefficients and define I_0(q,z)=sum_j [Y^r]a_j(q,Y)*z^j. (7.1) At q_N, suppose this initial form is nonzero. On E=C(Y) over C(U), U=Y^N, represent Y^(-r)L in the monomial basis 1,Y,...,Y^(N-1). Its matrix is integral over C[U]. Modulo U it is lower triangular: positive powers of Y either increase the basis exponent or wrap with a positive power of U. Its diagonal entries are I_0(q_N,Q_N^k). The principal submatrix on their nonzero indices has nonzero determinant. Therefore dim_(C(U)) ker L <=#{0<=k<N : I_0(q_N,Q_N^k)=0}. (7.2) This counts distinct lattice roots, not their multiplicities. If I_0=g(q)*z^a*(z-q^(2s))^m, with g(q_N) nonzero and m>=1, the bound is one at every such level. Any known nonzero rational period then proves generic rank one. The same applies at infinity. This is a condition on the actual quantum initial form, not on the commutative A-polynomial alone. Terms vanishing at q=1 can change the extremal Y-coefficient. The bound certifies the generic line used in Hilbert 90. It does not replace (4.4), which concerns its special fiber and the normal derivative. A rational kernel line may acquire extra special solutions; that possibility is exactly what the lattice retains. The subsequent [torsion initial-rank theorem](torsion_initial_rank.md) extends the pure-binomial test: rational-coefficient initial forms have only finitely many isolated torsion-grid exceptions outside their contained binomial torsion curves. Their eventual root count is given by finite periodic congruences. A single occupied curve therefore gives generic rank one even in the presence of non-toric initial factors. The proof keeps the q half-root and provides an explicit exceptional-level bound. It does not establish the special negative-sector injectivity or regulator norm. ## 8. The rank hypothesis cannot be suppressed For a manufactured root family let F_N(Y)=1+a_N S_N(Y), B=(T-1)(T-Q), P=B*(Y-1). Then P F_N=0 because (Y-1)F_N=Y-1+a_N(U-1), and B kills 1,Y. All ordinary orbit values are one, while K_N=1+N*a_N is arbitrary. Here B_0 has a two-dimensional kernel. Its complete-coordinate functional does not vanish on that kernel, so the first normal equation leaves this freedom. The quantum initial form also has two distinct lattice roots, consistent with (7.2). These are not knot states. In particular choosing a_N to change the complete value violates the coherent all-level color data, whose recovery is proved in [the all-level theorem](all_level_a_period.md). The example only explains the rank requirement for the simpler normal equation (6.2), not a new ambiguity in the actual invariant. ## 9. Independent operator and actual-state calibration The audit derives a telescoping operator for the finite block H_N(Y)=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) t_k(Y), t_k=product_(r=1)^k(Y+Y^(-1)-Q^r-Q^(-r)). The subsequent [whole-source four-plat proof](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md) identifies H_N with the actual figure-eight ADO state at every level, with all peripheral factors retained. The derivation here does not take that equality as a premise. Put Z=Q^k and C(Y,Z)=(Y-1)^2 Z/((Y-Z)(1-YZ)), D(Y)=Y(Y+1)(Q-Y^2)(QY^2-1), g=Q^2Y^2-QY^4+QY^3+QY-Q+Y^2, c_-=Y^2(Q-Y)(QY^2-1), c_0=-(Y-1)^2(Y+1)g, c_+=Y^2(QY-1)(Q-Y^2). The finite products give the two Y-shift ratios and the k-ratio directly. Substitution proves the exact rational certificate sum_(j=-1)^1 c_j(Y)*t_k(Q^jY)/t_k(Y) =D(Y)*(C(Y,QZ)*t_(k+1)/t_k-C(Y,Z)). (9.1) At a root Q^N=1, C(Y,1)=-1 and t_N=Y^N+Y^(-N)-2. Telescoping therefore gives (c_-T^(-1)+c_0+c_+T)H_N =D(Y)*(3-U-U^(-1)). (9.2) The central factor is retained. Applying D(Y)T-D(QY) kills the source. Left multiplication by T removes the negative shift. The common coefficient factor removed in the audit is exactly Q^3Y(Q^3Y^2-1)^2, recorded before any specialization. The resulting polynomial P has every boundary column factor, initial form z(Q-z), and classical symbol (Y-1)^2(Y+1)^2*(z-1)*Y^2*A_geo(Y,z), A_geo=z^2-(Y^2-Y-2-Y^(-1)+Y^(-2))*z+1. (9.3) This checks the familiar geometric peripheral polynomial and the additional boundary factors in fixed conventions. It does not prove an AJ theorem for arbitrary knot operators or identify root central curves with A_geo. For this calibrated operator the exact reciprocity in (6.4) is c(Q,Y)=-Q^12 Y^8 and d=3. Substituting its coefficients verifies -Q^j Y b_j(Y)=c(Q,Y)b_(3-j)(Q^(-3)/Y). The two involution and unit-norm identities follow by multiplication. The -1 domain has dimension ceil(N/2), including every parity. The audit verifies the source parity and recovers the same period using only that folded inverse. This removes an irrelevant symmetry sector before any asymptotic estimate; it is not such an estimate. [The audit](../experiments/audit_peripheral_normal_period.py) verifies the certificate symbolically. At levels 2,3,4,5,6,7,8,10 it proves coefficientwise equality of H_N with independently computed actual figure-eight cut Laurent polynomials over the stated finite fields, and verifies their annihilation. At eleven levels through 18 it checks both matrix ranks, the derivative product rule, and exact recovery of the complete block period by (4.2), (5.2), and the Weyl-folded inverse (6.5). It also checks 50 initial-root dimension examples and six explicit rank- ambiguity examples. All checks passed. The larger block tests do not extend the actual-state comparison beyond its stated levels. That all-level comparison is now supplied by the independent four-plat proof, which also proves the selected volume limit and leading coefficient for the actual figure-eight invariant. Results are in [the output](../experiments/peripheral_normal_period_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_peripheral_normal_period.py The boundary delta module, first lifting obstruction, Moore--Penrose inverse and initial-form argument use standard module and linear algebra. Their proofs above specify their role in the actual marked period; no novelty claim or imported analytic theorem is made. The quantum-torus Weyl involution already has explicit coverage in [Le's lectures, Section 5.9](https://letu.math.gatech.edu/Papers/Lectures_Luminy_2014_new.pdf). Only its scope is used for coverage; no AJ, state-comparison or analytic conclusion from that source is a premise. The weighted involutions and source parity above were obtained by direct operator identities, with all monomial phases retained. The [geometric triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md) supplies the marked Bloch action for the comparison with this normal period. Its norm, the actual geometric factor's survival, and the original volume conjecture remain open in this project.

title: Exact peripheral phase, state recovery, and move covariance
text: # Exact peripheral phase, state recovery, and move covariance Research note, 25 October 2026. Definitions are the charged operators in Andersen–Kashaev [arXiv:1109.6295v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6295v2), equation (18), its real level in equation (4), and the state integral (4.5) of Ben Aribi–Wong [arXiv:2410.10776v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.10776v2). This note reconstructs the *complex* identities, including the phases that their magnitude formulas do not specify. It does not infer a state equality from equality of absolute values. The positive local kernel and its proper contractions are independently proved in `faddeev_pentagon_audit.md`. The complete geometric saddle and annihilator statements remain those of the previous notes. The new results here are an exact tensor-to-fiber formula, uniqueness of the fiber state from that normalized tensor function, and an affine phase criterion for transporting it under the audited positive moves. ## 1. Data and conventions Write b>0 for the quantum parameter, Q=b+b^(-1), h=Q^(-2), c_b=iQ/2. The letter Q here is not the peripheral multiplication operator; that operator will be denoted mathsf-Q in Section 6. For tetrahedron j let its physical angles a_j,b_j,c_j be in radians and sum to pi. Its sign is epsilon_j. Put d=pi 1-a, C=diag(epsilon)c, delta_j=(epsilon_j+1)/2, N_+=sum_j delta_j, H=Q_f-diag(delta)/2, G=-2H. The face matrix script-A is invertible and gives the kinematical Gaussian Q_f. For the chosen longitude use the certified matrices A,B with B^(-1)A=G, p=2B^(-1)e_N, c_0=B^(-1)nu-G pi 1. On the balanced angle space its exact linear identity is W:=2Q_f d-C=c_0+(lambda/2)p, (1.1) where lambda is the angular holonomy of the chosen longitude. This follows from the actual edge/longitude angle equations, with their branch constants. It is also checked on the entire affine angle spaces in the accompanying script, rather than only at one complete structure. Fix the rational lift gamma in x=p^T y-i pi gamma, mu=p^T d-pi gamma. (1.2) The fiber contour then has Im x=mu. When mu is called a meridian holonomy, the corresponding normal-curve/peripheral certificate is required. For the twist families it is supplied by `twist_topology_and_peripherals.md`; gamma=0, mu=a_U-a_V, reversing the source's meridian orientation in the even case. For other data (1.2) alone defines a spectral coordinate, not a topological identification of a meridian. Choose p_1!=0 by relabeling. Let J_print be the literal printed integral, including its factor p_1/det(script-A), and put J_or=J_print/p_1^2, sigma_X=sign(det(script-A) p_1). (1.3) Thus J_or uses the oriented coarea fiber form. The sign sigma_X converts it to the positive Lebesgue disintegration of the full integral. It cannot be inferred from a formula for its modulus. ## 2. Charged kernel versus the phase-free dynamical convention For a positive tetrahedron, set its AK charges to a/(2pi),c/(2pi). The Fourier identity proved in the pentagon note gives its charged kernel as the phase-free dynamical factor times u(a,c;b)=exp[-pi i/12+i k(a,c)/h], k(a,c)=a c/(4pi)+(a-c)/12-pi/24. (2.1) Indeed its Fourier factor is exp(-pi i/12)psi_(c/(2pi),b_angle/(2pi)). Insert the defining psi and use a+b_angle+c=pi. The remaining x-dependent factor is exactly exp(Q c s)/Phi_b(s-iQ(pi-a)/(2pi)). For a negative tetrahedron take the adjoint and change spectral variable t=epsilon s. Its phase is u^(-1), and its remaining dynamical factor is exactly the negative factor in the FAMED definition. No sign Jacobian appears for Lebesgue integration on the real line. Let Z_AK be the contraction of the specified charged kernels and Z_D the FAMED convention with its phase-free dynamical factors. Then exactly Z_AK=U_X Z_D, U_X=exp[-pi i sum(epsilon)/12 +i sum_j epsilon_j k(a_j,c_j)/h]. (2.2) This uses the existing charged-operator definition. In the original v2 Theorem 4, formula (5) contains an alpha_3 even though the immediately following indexing only defines alpha_0,alpha_1,alpha_2. We avoid resolving that printed indexing by guesswork: equation (18) and its Fourier kernel fix (2.1) unambiguously. Its scalar agrees algebraically with the displayed varphi_T when alpha_0=a/pi, alpha_2=c/pi. No claim about the final journal version is made from this version-specific observation. ## 3. The exact tensor-to-fiber identity The phase-free contraction has the absolutely convergent spectral form Z_D=1/|det(script-A)| integral_R^N exp(2pi i t^T Q_f t) product_j exp(Q epsilon_j c_j t_j) Phi_b(epsilon_j(t_j-iQd_j/(2pi)))^(-epsilon_j) dt. Set u=-t+iQd/(2pi), y=2pi u/Q, with left-to-right Lebesgue contour orientations. The inversion identity Phi(z)Phi(-z)=zeta exp(pi i z^2), where zeta=exp[pi i(Q^2-2)/12], gives Z_D=zeta^(-N_+) exp[i Theta_X/(2pi h)] (Q/(2pi))^N/|det(script-A)| integral_(Y_alpha) exp[(i y^T H y+W^T y)/(2pi h)] product_j Phi_b(Q y_j/(2pi)) dy, Theta_X=C^T d-d^T Q_f d. (3.1) This is an affine substitution, not a deformation across a pole. In particular the constant terms have h, not sqrt(h), in their denominator. It follows by expanding 2pi i(-u+iQd/(2pi))^T Q_f(-u+iQd/(2pi)) and Q C^T(-u+iQd/(2pi)). The mixed-sign generic expansion is checked symbolically in the script. Disintegrate y into x and its fiber, using (1.1)–(1.3). The imaginary lift in (1.2) contributes exp(i gamma lambda/(4h)). Combining (2.2), (3.1), and the coarea Jacobian gives the exact result Z_AK(X,alpha;b) =sigma_X exp[pi i N/12+i K_X(alpha)/h] integral_(R+i mu) J_or(h,x) exp(lambda x/(4pi h)) dx, (3.2) where K_X(alpha)=sum_j epsilon_j k(a_j,c_j)-pi N_+/12 +Theta_X/(2pi)+gamma lambda/4. (3.3) The b-independent constant pi N/12 results from combining the inversion constant and the charged normalization; it is not an unspecified projective scalar. All entries of K_X are explicit real angle polynomials. For real angles,b, the multiplier in (3.2) has modulus one, but it matters in state recovery and quantum-operator comparison. The level in the *existing* AK definition acts by F_b(X,ell)=exp(pi i ell/(4h))Z_AK(X). Consequently the explicit b-independent allowed choice ell=-4K_X(alpha)/pi gives sigma_X exp(-pi i N/12)F_b(X,-4K_X(alpha)/pi) =integral J_or(h,x)exp(lambda x/(4pi h))dx. (3.4) This identifies the fixed fiber integral with a particular realization of the published leveled tensor state. It is a choice of level, not yet a claim that this level choice is preserved by every triangulation change. ## 4. Existence, contour independence, and uniqueness of the fiber state These points can be proved directly for positive proper FAMED data. The dynamical factors in Section 3 decrease exponentially at both real ends. Thus the original spectral integrand is bounded in modulus by C exp(-c sum_j |t_j|), with c>0. On compact subsets of the positive angle space the bound is uniform. Under the substitution in Section 3 this is a corresponding bound for the weighted full y integrand. Its Phi poles have imaginary coordinate at least pi in the y variable: the first pole is 2pi c_b/Q=i pi. Hence the product numerator is holomorphic throughout the box 0<Im y_j<pi. On a fiber the extra longitude factor is constant in the internal variables. The preceding exponential bound therefore proves absolute convergence of J_or and local holomorphy in x.
