The real map (y_1,...,y_N)->(x,y_2,...,y_N) is invertible, so the same bound also gives exponential decrease of J_or(x)exp(lambda x/(4pi h)) on the horizontal x contour. Positive angle structures form a convex open subset of an affine space. Two choices with the same mu can be joined inside it. Their fiber contours have the same x and remain in the pole-free box. Along a compact part of this segment the tail estimate stays uniform, including when lambda varies: its factor is constant along each fiber. Cauchy's theorem with vanishing side faces therefore identifies the fiber integrals. The image of the positive angle space in (mu,lambda) has an open interior. One way to certify this is to parameterize its affine equations by a and lambda: B invertible determines the z'' angles uniquely from A a+B angle(z'')=nu+lambda e_N, and the other angles follow by their tetrahedron sums. All remaining edge equations must be included or their redundancy certified. With p!=0, mu=p^T(pi 1-a)-pi gamma and lambda have independent differentials. The twist script checks rank two directly. Thus J_or is holomorphic on the horizontal band of meridian values supplied by positive angles. For fixed mu and an interval I of compatible longitude values, its transform L_X(lambda)=integral_(R+i mu) J_or(h,x) exp(lambda x/(4pi h))dx is holomorphic on the vertical strip Re lambda in I. Uniform exponential bounds on smaller strips justify differentiation. Varying the horizontal contour inside the compatible positive chamber does not change L_X. **Uniqueness.** Values of L_X on any real open subinterval of I determine J_or on its band. For two proposed states with the stated weighted decay, the identity theorem first gives equality on the vertical strip. On lambda=lambda_0+i tau the transform, after the explicit constant from Im x=mu is removed, is the ordinary Fourier transform of J_or(s+i mu)exp(lambda_0 s/(4pi h)). This is in L1. Fourier injectivity gives equality on that horizontal line, then holomorphy gives equality on the common band. In contrast, equality of the magnitudes of L_X supplies none of this uniqueness. ## 5. The balanced phase is affine up to one universal term Eliminating C from (3.3) by (1.1), and using a_j+b_j+c_j=pi, gives K_X(alpha)=L_X^angle(alpha)-lambda mu/(8pi) +gamma lambda/8, L_X^angle(alpha)=-pi N/24 +sum_j epsilon_j(c_j-b_j)/12-c_0^T(pi 1-a)/(4pi). (5.1) The superscript distinguishes the affine angle expression from the Fourier–Laplace transform L_X above. Equation (5.1) is an exact identity on the balanced angle space. Its only quadratic dependence is the universal meridian–longitude term. It is especially useful when comparing moves that preserve the same peripheral coordinates. For both twist families the script verifies (1.1) and (5.1) on their entire affine angle spaces for p=0,...,8. It checks the tangent Hessian, gradient and constant, so agreement at a single special angle is not the evidence. The proof of (5.1) is the displayed elimination for arbitrary N. The raw phase K_X varies even at fixed mu,lambda in every tested twist example; discarding it on account of its unit modulus would lose actual information. ## 6. Exact covariance under a certified positive move Suppose X,Y are proper positive FAMED realizations related by the audited operator-pentagon pattern or its adjoint, with compatible peripheral curves, coordinates and overlapping positive contour chambers. Write its tensor law as Z_AK(X,alpha)=exp(i rho(alpha)/h)Z_AK(Y,alpha'), where rho=-pi P/12 for the original pentagon and +pi P/12 for its adjoint. The map of angles is affine. The two scalar transforms obey exactly L_X(lambda)=eta exp(i D(alpha)/h)L_Y(lambda), eta=(sigma_Y/sigma_X)exp[pi i(N_Y-N_X)/12], D=K_Y(alpha')-K_X(alpha)+rho(alpha). (6.1) Because mu and lambda agree, the quadratic terms in (5.1) cancel. D is affine in the remaining angle variables. The transforms depend only on lambda. Where they are nonzero, varying angles at fixed lambda in (6.1) forces the continuous real function D to be constant on each such fiber. Hence, on the connected positive move chamber, D=d_0+d_1 lambda. (6.2) This is an affine linear-algebra statement, not an assumption that a quantum normalization vanishes. Nonzero transforms are guaranteed near the semiclassical regime when the previous positive geometric state theorem applies: the state is nonzero, so its transform cannot be identically zero by Section 4. Holomorphic continuation removes isolated transform zeros. For rational face/peripheral data, d_0 is in pi Q and d_1 is rational. Two generic angle evaluations, or coefficient comparison, determine them. If d_1=0, uniqueness immediately gives the exact state identity J_or,X(h,x)=eta exp(i d_0/h)J_or,Y(h,x). (6.3) Thus this finite phase certificate proves equality of the annihilator and of the volume rate for the *same selected state*, with every scalar retained. For the printed normalizations one must also multiply by p_(1,X)^2/p_(1,Y)^2. If d_1 is nonzero, (6.1) remains the exact transform relation; it must not be replaced by (6.3). Put a=4pi i d_1. When the relevant fiber band contains the required contour translation, inverse transformation gives J_or,X(h,x)=eta exp(i d_0/h)J_or,Y(h,x-a). (6.4) Without that strip/continuation check, (6.4) is not asserted. If it holds, an annihilator in the natural b-shift algebra transports by a coefficient substitution. Since mathsf-Q=exp[-(1+b^2)x], A_X(mathsf-Q,E)=A_Y(exp[(1+b^2)a]mathsf-Q,E), exp[(1+b^2)a]=exp(4pi i d_1)q^(2d_1), q=exp(2pi i b^2). The formula is in the finite root extension when required; descent to the prescribed coefficient field uses restriction of scalars as in the earlier annihilator note, and need not preserve the minimal order over that field. This retains the finite power of q and the root of unity in the meridian lift. The complete value cannot be substituted before this comparison. ### 6.1 Geometric endpoints force the affine slope to vanish There is a stronger conclusion when both endpoints have the positive complete geometric certificates of the volume theorem, with the boundary origins fixed by p^T y*=i pi gamma. Under the hypotheses of Section 6, d_1=0. (6.5) Here is a proof that does not assume state invariance. The normalized transform L_X is the full N-variable integral from (3.1), with its angle phase removed. At lambda=0 its leading potential is F_0, whose *full* gradient vanishes at the positive complete y*. This follows directly from the certified edge/longitude matrix identity and the complete logarithmic equations, just as in the earlier fiber saddle calculation. The same exact quantum remainder applies. With s=b^2, its b-dependent potential at a nearby longitude parameter is F_s(y,lambda)=i y^T H y+c_0^T y +(lambda/2)(p^T y-i pi gamma) -i/(1+s)^2 sum_j Li_2(-exp((1+s)y_j)). On the full real horizontal plane the real Hessian is -diag(Im sigmoid((1+s)y_j)), strictly negative for the positive strip. The full Hessian is invertible, so its critical point y_s tends to y*. Concavity gives the same quadratic-near/linear-far coercivity bound as in the fiber proof, now in N real directions. The exact remainder is uniformly bounded and tends to zero on a smaller strip. The nonzero Gaussian and the strict tail gap therefore prove L_X(h,0)!=0 for all sufficiently small b. Insert the linear moment x(y)=p^T y-i pi gamma. The same saddle argument applies: the additional polynomial factor is integrable against the coercive tails, and the ratio of the two Gaussian expansions tends to x(y*)=0. Differentiation under the convergent integral consequently gives lim_(b->0+) h L_X'(0)/L_X(0) =lim (1/(4pi)) integral x(y)I_b(y)dy / integral I_b(y)dy =0. (6.6) All constant measure factors cancel in this ratio. The same result holds for Y. Differentiate the exact relation (6.1)–(6.2): h [L_X'(0)/L_X(0)-L_Y'(0)/L_Y(0)]=i d_1. Taking the limit proves (6.5), since d_1 is independent of b. This proves that the translation alternative in (6.4) cannot occur for these compatible geometric endpoints with their complete origins fixed. It was necessary to retain that alternative before this argument, rather than cancel it at the ideal point by convention. The argument also applies to a finite certified path of proper positive moves. Compose its exact tensor laws first. The endpoint K polynomials cancel their common quadratic peripheral term, while the sum of local pentagon phases is affine in the path's angle variables. The transform uniqueness argument again gives d_0+d_1 lambda. Its identity, initially on the path's nonempty open longitude interval, extends analytically to zero: the intersection of the endpoint admissible longitude projections is an interval containing zero and that initial interval. The contour-independent local transform charts of Section 4 patch along this interval. Apply (6.6) only at the endpoints. Intermediate triangulations need their proper positive kernel contractions and the specified move/peripheral certificates; they need not have complete geometric saddle certificates for this step. **Consequence.** Within every such certified positive-path component of geometric endpoint realizations, the selected coarea states differ only by the recorded boundary-independent scalar eta exp(i d_0/h). Their annihilator ideals, primitive minimal operators and volume limits agree after the fixed peripheral coordinates are identified. The printed states also retain their explicit p_1^2 ratio. This is a statement for certified paths, not an assertion that an arbitrary topological Pachner path stays positive or proper. ## 7. Scope and reproducible checks Equations (3.2)–(3.4) supply the exact relationship between the specified literature fiber integral and its leveled charged tensor realization. Section 4 proves state recovery, and Section 6 reduces covariance for the audited moves to an explicit affine phase and, if needed, a contour shift. These improve the previous magnitude-only relationship. Section 6.1 rules out the nonzero slope for compatible positive complete geometric endpoints by a full-integral saddle moment. Thus only the scalar phase remains for any connecting path satisfying the stated certificates. The subsequent `tetrahedral_symmetry_and_figure_eight.md` applies this criterion to the actual figure-eight 3–2 move. It audits the ordering kernels, proves d_1=0 and d_0=11pi/12 on the entire angle space, and records the simultaneous meridian/longitude reversal. A verified automorphism then makes the two-tetrahedron state even, giving an exact scalar equivalence at the same boundary value and the same minimal operator. **Corollary for the volume theorem.** Under the positive complete geometric and finite matrix certificates in `literature_state_volume.md`, the selected inverse-transform state of the leveled tensor realization (3.4) is exactly J_print/p_1^2. Its primitive minimal annihilator exists in the prescribed Andersen–Malusà b-shift algebra, its classical symbol contains the certified geometric peripheral component, and lim_(b->0+) -2pi h log|J_or(h,0)|=Vol(M). This follows from the exact state identity here, the annihilator proof in `general_annihilator_and_volume.md`, and the independently proved saddle theorem. The nonzero constant p_1^2 contributes zero to the limit. Thus the state in that theorem is an exact specified leveled AK realization, not a solution selected only for its convenient asymptotic. The uniform twist certificates give this corollary for every fixed parameter in the two stated twist families and their recorded mirror convention. What is still needed for a single intrinsic knot state across arbitrary realizations is a certified connecting sequence, its compatible peripheral lifts, the constants for the exactly normalized framed state, and any continuation outside the positive chamber. The slope is already zero for the certified geometric endpoints of Section 6.1. A path through the required geometric triangulations is not supplied just by the existence of a topological Pachner sequence. The all-alternating extension also still needs its geometric and finite matrix certificates. None of these remaining claims is inferred from the affine form (6.2). Run `python3 experiments/audit_peripheral_phase.py`. It checks the generic mixed-sign Gaussian identity, eighteen complete affine twist angle spaces, their peripheral rank, and four pointwise quantum identities using the independently derived real-b defining-integral remainder. The maximum pointwise relative error was below 9e-15. The symbolic identities and contour bounds above, rather than those finite samples, carry the proofs.

title: Exact Bell weights and a source-balanced positive Gram
text: # Exact Bell weights and a source-balanced positive Gram 29 October 2026. The phase-ratio coefficient of the ORIGINAL conjugate source has one positive angle-energy profile, rather than its square. Its radius factors and normalization are explicit. A second result constructs a canonical positive Gram for the ACTUAL right/left Fermat frames: both source costs reduce to a rational chord sum, polynomial away from the normalized central divisor. With the original cap normalizers retained, the cost is O(1+|epsilon|logN) uniformly at every cap index. This supplies a quantitative special-inner-product input, not a bound on the interior original word. ## 1. Exact magnitude on the Fermat fiber Use sigma=-1 and the actual normalized P,L and Bell basis of [the source-exact reflection theorem](phase_ratio_double_and_fermat_source.md). Let u^N+v^N=1 and assume the factors below are nonzero. Define t=v/barv, a=baru/u, A_j=|1-t Q^(-j)|, B_j=|1-a Q^j|, C_j=|1-at Q^j|. The two original source equations give BOTH recurrences |c_(s,r+1)|/|c_(s,r)|=A_r/(|u| C_(s-r)), |c_(s,r)|/|c_(s-1,r)|=|v| C_(s-r)/B_s. (1) For n in Z define Cprod(0)=1 and Cprod(n)/Cprod(n-1)=C_n, using reciprocal products for n<0. Put f_(s,r)=|u|^(-r)|v|^s [product_(j=0)^(r-1) A_j] Cprod(s-r) /[product_(j=1)^s B_j], 0<=s,r<N. (2) Empty products equal one. Starting at (0,0), (1) proves |c_(s,r)|=kappa_N f_(s,r), kappa_N=||P||_2^2/[sum_(s,r) f_(s,r)^2]^(1/2). (3) This determines the normalization by a specified positive finite sum, with no unknown knot period. Indeed the Bell transform is unitary and its input is P tensor barP, so sum|c|^2=||P||^4. The all-nonzero theorem on the open positive-central fiber justifies normalizing at (0,0). Other nonsingular root marks have the same formula with their actual chord factors, not principal arguments silently substituted. On the PRINCIPAL positive-central component, kappa_N=c_(0,0)>0 also fixes the scalar phase. The defining sum for c_(0,0) is real by pairing a with -a. It never vanishes on this connected component by (1), and as U=u^N tends to zero in the upper half-plane the principal roots give P_a->1 and c_(0,0)->sqrtN. Hence its sign is positive everywhere there. A different root mark must keep its own phase; this argument does not silently identify those marks. If the actual column is Gamma P, multiply c and kappa_N by |Gamma|^2. No Gamma, inverse-frame normalization or cap residue factor has been removed. The radii |u|,|v| in (2) may depend arbitrarily on N. Formula (3) remains exact and does not declare kappa_N or those radius factors subexponential. ## 2. Three shifted positive factorials, and both chambers For a Frobenius center U=u^N in the upper half-plane, take the principal marked roots and write alpha=Arg(U)/pi, beta=-Arg(1-U)/pi, gamma=alpha+beta, 0<alpha,beta,gamma<1. Define the positive shifted factorial T_N(L;delta)=product_(j=1)^L 2sin[pi(j+delta)/N], -1<delta<0, 0<=L<=N. Every displayed sine is positive. Set A_full=|1-t^N|, C_full=|1-(at)^N|. Reflection of the numerator arcs in (2) gives the exact formulas r>s: |c_(s,r)|=kappa_N A_full |u|^(-r)|v|^s /[T_N(N-r;-beta) T_N(s;-alpha) T_N(r-s;gamma-1)], (4) r<=s: |c_(s,r)|=kappa_N A_full C_full |u|^(-r)|v|^s /[T_N(N-r;-beta) T_N(s;-alpha) T_N(N-s+r;gamma-1)]. (5) Proof. A_j=2sin[pi(j+beta)/N], B_j=2sin[pi(j-alpha)/N]. For r>s the reciprocal negative-index Cprod gives the factors 2sin[pi(j+gamma-1)/N], j=1,...,r-s. Replace the A numerator by its complete product divided by the remaining arc, and reflect that arc. This proves (4). For r<=s also complement the positive C numerator by its complete product; the same reflection proves (5). The three lengths sum to N in (4), and their shifts sum to -1. On the STRICT chamber 0<s<r<N all three shifted endpoints are positive and sum to d=N-1. Thus (4) has ONE angle-energy weight, not a square-root amplitude weight and not its square. In (5) the lengths sum to 2N and the shifted endpoints sum to 2N-1. Boundary rows, including s=0, retain their literal empty products; a negative formal shifted endpoint is not declared a geometric angle. The full half-phase/sign accounting is in the reflection theorem and is not replaced by choosing the favorable chamber. For shifts in a fixed compact subset of (-1,0), lengths at most N-1, these T_N factors differ from the unshifted s_N factors by polynomial factors: separate the first factor and integrate the logarithmic derivative, bounded by the harmonic sums at the two root endpoints. If a shift approaches a divisor, retain its explicit factor. If L=N, T_N(N;delta)=|1-exp(2pi i delta)|, not the forbidden zero s_N(N). No uniform polynomial comparison through arbitrary exponentially close divisors is inferred. In particular, U fixed and u=U^(1/N) is only one parameter regime. A fixed semiclassical radius |u|!=1 has an exponentially varying Frobenius center. Equations (2)--(5) retain that regime rather than identifying it with the fixed-center estimate. ## 3. An explicit non-diagonal Bell Cauchy metric For the full positive array f in (2), give an exterior array b the norm squared sum f_(s,r)|b_(s,r)|^2. Its ORIGINAL source functional sum c_(s,r)b_(s,r) has exact Riesz norm squared sum |c_(s,r)|^2/f_(s,r)=kappa_N^2 sum f_(s,r). (6) Thus an explicit positive Gram exists in the Bell space; in the original doubled head coordinates it is a conjugate of diag(f) and is generally nondiagonal. It retains ALL sectors. The phase choice b=barc/|c| attains the corresponding weighted Cauchy bound, so (6) is a sharp local all-exterior statement. The coefficient c already belongs to a DOUBLED amplitude. Squaring its contraction again proves a fourth-power statement, not the desired |K|^2 estimate. Direct triangle comparison instead reads |sum c b|<=kappa_N sum f |b|. (7) If the actual remaining contraction has |b| bounded polynomially and the actual edge projector is diagonal in this SAME joint basis, (4)--(7) supply a one-power positive partition comparison. Those conditions on the remaining original contraction are not proved here. Introducing a dephasing or discarding (5) does not establish them. Normalization (6) is also explicit rather than assumed tame. ## 4. A stronger Gram balances the actual source AND co-source There is a useful quantitative alternative which does not require the Fermat equation. For the literal P,L in either orientation, when u^N!=1 and v!=0, finite cancellation gives L_a P_a=(1-u)/(1-u Q_s^a). Define H_a=|L_a|/|P_a|>0, U_a=(L_aP_a)/|L_aP_a|. Then EXACTLY L=P^* H U, U unitary diagonal, P^*H P=L H^(-1)L^* =S_N(u):=|1-u|sum_(a=0)^d 1/|1-u Q_s^a|. (8) This is a prescribed positive inner product, constructed from the known cyclic source frames, not from a knot value. For every specified exterior A, |L A P|<=S_N(u)||A||_H. (9) The phase U in (8) is compulsory; no positive pivotal trace is claimed. If the actual rows/columns are Gamma_L L,Gamma_R P, their balanced source norm squared is |Gamma_L Gamma_R|S_N. The Gamma product is part of (9), even when exponential. There is an elementary radius-uniform estimate S_N(u)<=2N^2 max(1,|u|^N)/|1-u^N|. (10) Indeed (1-u^N)/(1-uQ_s^a)=sum_(k=0)^d(uQ_s^a)^k. Its absolute value is at most N max(1,|u|^d). Sum over a and use |1-u|<=1+|u|. This proves (10) for arbitrary N-dependent radii. A polynomial lower bound on the NORMALIZED central separation |1-u^N|/max(1,|u|^N) makes this source cost polynomial. It is not a lower bound on that separation when a source pole approaches the contour. On the doubled head, use H tensor H. The original doubled source and co-source both have norm squared S_N^2. In the unitary Bell basis its Gram is explicitly Bell^*(H tensor H)Bell, generally NONDIAGONAL. Formula (4) of the reflection theorem preserves the magnitudes of P,L, so this H is invariant under the source antiinvolution, and its compulsory co-source clock is unitary for H as well. No small-root or fixed-radius argument is needed. The phase-ratio observables are unitary in the flat cyclic metric; they need not be unitary for H. Nor is a diagonal H at one quad chart automatically the diagonal metric at the next chart. Transporting this Gram and retaining its off-diagonal terms is essential. A flat diagonal edge projector need not be contractive in the transported source metric. The [selected corner-sector theorem](phase_ratio_corner_sector_metric.md) proves a precise boundary exception: the doubled metric is scalar on the actual corner's clock-sum sector for real cap parameters, and has polynomial condition number there throughout the complex cap disk. Orthogonal projectors restricted to that sector therefore have a tame norm. This does not discard the other regularized-cap sectors or prove that an interior crossing preserves the selected sector. ## 5. Polynomial cost at EVERY actual normalized cap In the literal cap orientation Q_s=Q, put epsilon=v^N, u=Q^(-j)(1-epsilon)^(1/N), |epsilon|<=rho=1/16. For j>=1 use the ORIGINAL normalized frames Phat_j=v^(N-j)P/alpha_j, Lhat_j=v^j L/beta_j, alpha_j beta_j=N(1-Q^(-j)). For j=0 use P,L without those factors. Let Hhat_j be their balanced positive metric as in (8). Their source norm squared is Shat_j=|epsilon| |1-u|/[N|1-Q^(-j)|] sum_a1/|1-uQ^a|, j>=1, Shat_0=S_N(u). (11) Uniformly in N,j, and the marked punctured epsilon disk, Shat_j<=C[1+|epsilon|(1+log N)], lim_(epsilon->0)Shat_j=1. (12) Proof. Write delta=(1-epsilon)^(1/N). The marked logarithm gives |delta-1|<=2|epsilon|/N. The resonant denominator is bounded below by |epsilon|/[N(1+rho)] from epsilon=(1-delta)sum_(k=0)^d delta^k. Every other denominator |1-delta Q^k| is at least 3min(k,N-k)/N. Their reciprocal sum is O(N(1+logN)). For j>=1, |1-u|/|1-Q^(-j)|<=2, giving (12). For j=0 the resonant term in S_N is exactly one and the others have the same bound. The resonant term tends to one in every case and the other terms vanish. This proof keeps the actual alpha_j,beta_j, whose separate sizes need not be polynomial. Independent input/output caps may use different Hhat metrics. Their original matrix element is bounded by the geometric mean of these source costs times the operator norm from Hhat_in to Hhat_out. Tensor products preserve this statement. The actual corner source is obtained by Cauchy evaluation of Phat,Lhat at zero; on |v|=rho^(1/N), each normalized dv/v circle has mass one. Thus these cap source factors cost only polynomially in the original whole residue presentation. The INTERIOR word norm between those metrics, and all additional retained scalar lines, remain to be bounded. This does not turn (12) into a knot-volume bound by itself. ## 6. Off-Fermat/current packets are not erased Let Delta=1-u^N-v^N and F_d=product_(a=1)^d(1-uQ^(-a)). The normalized column satisfies B P=Delta e_0/F_d even off the Fermat curve. Its exact Bell equations acquire c_sr-u c_(s,r+1)-vQ^(-r)c_(s-1,r)=h_s, c_sr-baruQ^s c_(s,r+1)-barv c_(s-1,r)=k_sr, h_s=(Delta/F_d)barP_s/sqrtN, k_sr=(barDelta/barF_d)Q^(-rs)P_s/sqrtN. Consequently the recurrence behind (1) is replaced by [u-t baru Q^(s-r)]c_(s,r+1) =[1-tQ^(-r)]c_sr-h_s+tQ^(-r)k_sr. (13) Variation of constants retains the finite sum of both displayed sources, with the actual cyclic closure determinant. Resonant closure does not select a free homogeneous coefficient. Thus (2)--(5) are exact Fermat-source formulas; extending them to a complete inhomogeneous beta packet requires the currents (13), not setting their central Delta to zero. The positive metric (8)--(10) itself remains exact off the Fermat locus. [Audit](../experiments/audit_phase_ratio_bell_weights.py): pointwise shifted-factorial profiles and Parseval normalization, varying radii/centers, source-balanced metrics and actual cap constants, and the full off-Fermat source corrections.

title: A tame phase-ratio projector on the actual doubled corner sector
text: # A tame phase-ratio projector on the actual doubled corner sector 29 October 2026. This is a boundary metric theorem for the ORIGINAL normalized Fermat cap, with all source normalizers retained. On its selected doubled clock sector, every flat orthogonal projector is exactly contractive for real cap parameters and polynomially bounded throughout a fixed complex cap disk. It does not prove that an interior crossing preserves that sector, or identify the character constraints of a triangulation edge. ## 1. The actual source and its periodic positive metric Let N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2pi i/N), and 0<|epsilon|<=rho=1/16. Use the marked root delta=(1-epsilon)^(1/N), u=Q^(-j)delta, v^N=epsilon, 0<=j<N. (1) Any marked Nth root v is allowed. In the literal cap orientation, P_a=v^a/product_(r=1)^a(1-uQ^r), L_a=v^(-a)product_(r=0)^(a-1)(1-uQ^r), 0<=a<N, h_a=|L_a|/|P_a|. (2) These are the original source frames of [the source-balanced Gram theorem](phase_ratio_bell_weights_and_source_gram.md). Because 1-u^N=v^N, both P and L, and hence h, extend N-periodically. Their EXACT recurrence is h_(a+1)/h_a=|1-uQ^a| |1-uQ^(a+1)|/|v|^2. (3) For j>=1 the actual cap normalization is Phat_a=v^(N-j)P_a/alpha_j, Lhat_a=v^j L_a/beta_j, alpha_j=F_(N-j), beta_j=N/F_(d-j), F_r=product_(k=1)^r(1-Q^k), alpha_j beta_j=N(1-Q^(-j)). (4) For j=0 retain P,L unchanged. Consequently the actual balanced metric Hhat=diag(|Lhat_a|/|Phat_a|) is a single positive scalar multiple of H=diag(h_a). The scalar in question is exactly |v|^(2j-N)|alpha_j/beta_j|; it has NOT been assumed tame or omitted from the original source. It cancels in every operator norm below. The literal source cost is still Phat^* Hhat Phat=Lhat Hhat^(-1)Lhat^* =|epsilon| |1-u|/[N|1-Q^(-j)|] sum_a 1/|1-uQ^a|, j>=1, (5) and |1-u| sum_a 1/|1-uQ^a| for j=0. In particular it is bounded by C(1+|epsilon|(1+log N)), as proved in the linked Gram note. No normalizer has been replaced by a chosen unit source. At fixed N, Phat and Lhat both tend to the coordinate corner e_j as epsilon tends to zero on their marked root cover. For the resonant entry of Phat, (1-delta)/epsilon tends to 1/N and the remaining denominator factors together with F_(N-j) multiply to N. For Lhat, its j-th numerator is exactly beta_j at epsilon=0. Every other entry has a strictly positive residual power of v. The j=0 assertion follows directly from (2). ## 2. The doubled sector and the exact projector criterion Give the doubled head the product metric G=H tensor H. Its clock sum sectors are V_s=span{|a,s-a mod N>:0<=a<N}, G|_(V_s)=diag(g_a), g_a=h_a h_(s-a). (6) The ORIGINAL conjugate double may equivalently be written using the source-exact antiunitary reflection of [the reflection theorem](phase_ratio_double_and_fermat_source.md). That reflection preserves h and adds only its specified diagonal unitary chirp. Thus it has the same metric (6), and the doubled corner e_j tensor bare_j belongs to V_(2j mod N). The clock-sector projector is diagonal and commutes with G, so it is contractive on the entire doubled space. Inside V_s the phase-ratio shift S^(-1) tensor S has the Fourier eigenvectors w_(s,r)=N^(-1/2)sum_a Q^(ra)|a,s-a>, 0<=r<N. Unit-modulus scalar marks change the eigenvalues, not these projectors. A rank-one flat character projector Pi_(s,r)=w w^* has the EXACT restricted metric norm ||Pi_(s,r)||_G =[(N^(-1)sum_a g_a)(N^(-1)sum_a g_a^(-1))]^(1/2). (7) Indeed a rank-one map xy^* has weighted norm ||G^(1/2)x|| ||G^(-1/2)y||. Formula (7) is independent of r and equals one precisely when g is constant. More generally, a flat orthogonal projector Pi is contractive in a positive metric G precisely when [Pi,G]=0. Necessity follows by applying contractivity to x+t y with x in its range and y in its kernel, and varying complex t: it forces their G-orthogonality. Sufficiency follows by the resulting orthogonal splitting. In general ||Pi||_G<=sqrt(cond G). ## 3. Exact contractivity and its complex extension **Theorem.** For the actual normalized cap (1)--(4), every flat orthogonal projector whose range and domain lie in V_(2j mod N) satisfies ||Pi||_(Hhat tensor Hhat) <=exp[8|epsilon|(1+log N)] <=e^(8rho)N^(8rho). (8) Here the norm means the restriction to that sector, or equivalently the extension by zero on its orthogonal complement. If epsilon is real, the norm of every nonzero such projector is EXACTLY one. In particular this applies to all shift-character projectors and their orthogonal sums on the selected doubled corner sector. Proof. Put z_k=|1-delta Q^k|, periodically in k. Applying (3) to the two reflected indices gives, for 1<=ell<N, g_(j+ell)/g_j =(z_ell/z_(-ell)) product_(k=1)^(ell-1)(z_k/z_(-k))^2, g_j=h_j^2, s=2j mod N. (9) The potentially arbitrarily small resonant chord z_0 cancels EXACTLY. If epsilon is real then delta is real and positive, including when epsilon<0 and delta>1. Thus z_k=z_(-k) and every g_a=h_j^2. The metric is scalar on this sector, proving exact contractivity without a limiting argument. For complex epsilon the marked logarithm gives |delta-1|<=2|epsilon|/N. For k!=0 mod N, with m=min(k,N-k), |1-Q^k|>=4m/N, |z_(+/-k)/|1-Q^k|-1|<=|epsilon|/(2m)=:t_k<=1/32. It follows that |log(z_k/z_(-k))| <=log((1+t_k)/(1-t_k))<=3|epsilon|/(2m). (10) Since sum_(k=1)^(N-1)1/min(k,N-k)<=2(1+log N), equations (9)--(10) give |log(g_a/h_j^2)|<=8|epsilon|(1+log N). Thus the restricted condition number is at most exp[16|epsilon|(1+log N)]. The general projector estimate of section 2 proves (8). Replacing H by Hhat only multiplies the doubled metric by a common positive scalar, so the proof retains all alpha,beta factors in (4). This also proves uniformity for epsilon depending arbitrarily on N, even exponentially close to zero. If |epsilon|log N tends to zero, the upper bound tends to one. The opposite root orientation follows by Q->Q^(-1) and the corresponding reflected cap labels; the same real chord estimates and source normalization proof apply. ## 4. Exact scope at the original source The theorem controls a genuine boundary sector selected by the original corner limit, not an arbitrarily chosen geometric sector. For epsilon!=0 the complete cap column has nonzero entries in every coordinate, so its conjugate double also has other V_s components. These components cannot be discarded inside a Cauchy cap contour. A general V_s has the exact norm (7), with no scalar metric conclusion unless its own reflected products are constant. Nor has a crossing been proved to preserve the local sector s=2j, or a change to an adjacent Fermat chart proved contractive in this metric. Global total-degree conservation does not imply those local assertions. If a specified physical/edge projector acts inside the selected sector as a flat orthogonal projector, (8) bounds that projector with the actual cap metric. Identifying all interior edge projectors and controlling their intervening transport remain separate requirements. All off-Fermat beta currents and both Bell half-phase chambers of the linked notes remain in the complete original source. ## 5. Independent finite audit [The audit](../experiments/audit_phase_ratio_corner_sector_metric.py) checks the literal normalized frames, the alpha beta product, periodic recurrence, reflected product (9), and all cap labels at a range of levels and real/complex cap parameters. It also compares (7) with direct weighted singular values of character projectors and their nontrivial sums. The tests include cap parameters exponentially small in N; none substitutes epsilon=0 before constructing the metric. The accompanying result file is written only after all assertions pass. Fresh replay: PASS 710 actual normalized cap sectors, 664 direct weighted character/sum-projector checks, and 12 opposite-root cases. Python compilation also passes. The numerical checks supplement the uniform reflected-chord proof; they do not establish interior preservation of the selected sector.

title: A pointed Hermitian reflection for the actual cyclic source
text: # A pointed Hermitian reflection for the actual cyclic source 29 October 2026. The phase-ratio double has a genuine source-compatible realization: inverse conjugation of the quad coordinates is implemented by an explicit ANTIUNITARY on the cyclic Fermat source, together with a face swap. Its full normalizer is retained, and the construction is valid at arbitrary radii. It agrees exactly with the pointed Fourier quad rotations. It also extends to inhomogeneous cyclic packets, with their source currents transformed rather than removed. The same diagonal reflection fixes the actual fused arbitrary-plat corner functional. Thus a whole original squared scalar has an exact reflected doubled-word presentation. This does not yet identify its contraction with a positive angle partition: the local joint spectral source and all original sewing/co-source factors remain explicit. ## 1. Conventions and a radius-independent antiinvolution Let N>=2, q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2. Use a sign sigma=+1 or -1 and set q_s=q^sigma, Q_s=Q^sigma, D_s e_a=Q_s^a e_a, S e_a=e_(a+1 modN), X=u D_s, Y=v S, B=I-X-Y. The literal cap-source convention has sigma=+1. The cyclic quad convention with Z_i Z_(i+1)=Q Z_(i+1)Z_i has sigma=-1. Define H_s(u,v)=(u',v')=(1/baru, q_s^(-1)barv/baru), A_(s,a)=(-q_s)^a Q_s^[a(a+1)/2], J_s=diag(A_(s,a)^(-1)), Theta_s=J_s conjugation. (1) All powers are ordinary integer expressions; no division by two modulo N is used. Since A_(s,N)=1, the chirp is cyclic, including its endpoint. It is unitary, Theta_s^2=I and H_s^2=id. If u^N+v^N=1, then u'^N+v'^N=1. The central shape U=u^N is sent to 1/barU, which preserves the upper half-plane. The exact matrix identity, with NO Fermat hypothesis, is B(u',v') J_s=-J_s barX^(-1) barB(u,v). (2) Indeed J_s S J_s^(-1)=-q_s^(-1)D_s^(-1)S; multiply barB on the left by -barX^(-1) and use this equality. The extra invertible left factor in (2) is not silently replaced by a similarity. ## 2. Actual right and left source frames, including their normalizers Use the literal normalized frames from the cap/source construction, with the indicated root orientation: F_a(u)=product_(r=1)^a(1-u Q_s^r), P_a(u,v)=v^a/F_a(u), L_a(u,v)=v^(-a)product_(r=0)^(a-1)(1-u Q_s^r), P_0=L_0=1. (3) They are the actual P,L of the cap theorem when sigma=+1. Whenever these expressions are defined, finite-product reflection gives P(u',v')=J_s barP(u,v), L(u',v')=barL(u,v) D_s^(-1)J_s^(-1). (4) For the right formula factor each denominator as 1-baru^(-1)Q_s^r=-baru^(-1)Q_s^r(1-baru Q_s^(-r)). Together with v'=q_s^(-1)barv/baru this gives precisely the chirp in (1). The same calculation starting at r=0 gives the COMPULSORY clock D_s^(-1) in the left formula. Both transformations preserve the Euclidean norm in this cyclic frame EXACTLY, at arbitrary radii. The cancellation uses the full Fermat/shift normalizer v'. It is not a small-root-log argument. For example |F_a(u)/F_a(1/baru)|=|u|^a can be exponentially large when a is proportional to N, but the corresponding v-power cancels it in (4). No assertion that a geometric clock radius is 1+O(1/N) is needed. For an arbitrary retained operator C, the paired scalar identity is bar[L C P]=L(u',v') D_s [J_s barC J_s^(-1)]P(u',v'). (5) Thus the actual co-source carries a unitary clock insertion. It is not merely the unshifted natural left source at the reflected point. Every external scalar Gamma is conjugated and retained. In particular Theta_s(Gamma P)=barGamma P'; it is not reset to one. There is also an exact check on polynomial normalization. Let Delta=1-u^N-v^N and Ptilde=F_d(u)P, d=N-1. Then B Ptilde=Delta e_0, Delta'=-barDelta/baru^N, F_d(u')=baru^(-d)barF_d(u), Ptilde(u',v')=baru^(-d)J_s barPtilde(u,v). (6) If the actual column is expressed in the polynomial Ptilde frame, the power baru^d must therefore stay in its transformed Gamma. It can be exponential; (4) does not license deleting it. The same warning applies to the actual cap residue constants and Jacobians. Those are retained by ordinary coordinate substitution. At a literal corner Theta_s e_d=-q_s e_d and Theta_s e_0=e_0, so its pointed normalization changes only by the specified unit phase, not an unknown central normalizer. ## 3. Pointed quad rotations compose coherently Use the original normalized Fourier matrix F_s and quad adapter (F_s)_(k,a)=Q_s^(ka)/sqrtN, W_s=F_s A_s, rho_s(u,v)=(q_s v/u,1/u). Then EXACTLY Theta_s W_s Theta_s=W_s^(-1), H_s rho_s H_s=rho_s^(-1). (7) The matrix proof is J_s barW_s barJ_s =A_s^(-1)F_s^(-1)=W_s^(-1). The parameter proof is direct substitution. No projective phase or central deck was discarded. Using q instead of q_s^(-1) in (1) with sigma=+1 would insert a root-of-unity deck; keeping the orientation makes (7) exact. If W_s P(p)=c(p)P(rho_s p) is the actual pointed source rotation, P_0=1 fixes c. Equations (4),(7) force c(H_s rho_s p) barc(p)=1. (8) Thus the exact source Gamma of a reflected pointed rotation is its reciprocal conjugate, including its nontrivial modulus. This is a genuine normalization identity, not a new unit-norm choice. The left-source clock in (4), and the corresponding clock in (5), must still be used on sewn output faces. ## 4. Full currents survive the reflection For ANY inhomogeneous packet B f=eta, (2) gives B' Theta_s f=-Theta_s(X^(-1)eta). (9) When B is invertible this is also an exact resolvent identity; meromorphic continuation keeps its poles and residues. It neither sets Delta=0 nor deletes a current proportional to Delta. Thus a local source decomposition into a balanced residue and a current is reflected LINEARLY with both parts retained. For example the complete Newton packet f_j=B_N(u,vQ^j) obeys (I-uR+vD_Q R)f=(1-u^N+v^N)1, with (Rf)_j=f_(j+1). The two terms uR and -vD_Q R form a finite Weyl pair, of central powers u^N and -v^N. A fixed unitary Weyl change puts it in the form of (9). Its source must undergo the SAME change and the factor X^(-1) in (9); no claim that the reflected packet is the same standard B_N with its source reset is made. In particular this is not a proof that the inhomogeneous beta current vanishes. The full-Psi split and its marked scalar normalizer remain part of the original packet. ## 5. The inverse-reflected triad and its positive joint basis Put Z0=X, Z1=Y^(-1), Z2=-X^(-1)Y. Their cyclic commutation parameter is Q_s^(-1), and their ordered product is -Q_s^(-1). At the reflected point, (Z0',Z1',Z2')= (J_s barZ0^(-1)J_s^(-1), J_s barZ2^(-1)J_s^(-1), J_s barZ1^(-1)J_s^(-1)). (10) Thus inverse conjugation comes with the 1<->2 face swap. The unitary map I tensor J_s takes P tensor barP to P tensor P' and takes the phase-ratio observables Z_i tensor barZ_i^(-1) to Z_i tensor Z'_(tau(i)), tau=(1 2). This is a source-compatible interpretation of the inverse factor, not arbitrary inversion of the original bra. For sigma=-1 the phase-ratio observables commute, are unitary even for complex u,v, and have ordered product Q. A joint orthonormal basis is |s,r>=N^(-1/2)sum_a Q^(ra)|a,s-a moduloN>. Its first two eigenvalues are (u/baru)Q^(-s) and (barv/v)Q^r; the third is Q divided by their product. This gives a genuine positive joint spectral norm. It is not yet a positive angle state or its geometric edge projector. Indeed the ORIGINAL conjugate source in this basis has coefficients c_(s,r)=N^(-1/2)sum_a Q^(-ra)P_a barP_(s-a). (11) The two source equations, BEFORE any positivity or projection, imply on the Fermat locus c_(s,r+1)=[1-(v/barv)Q^(-r)] /[u-(v/barv)baru Q^(s-r)] c_(s,r). (12) On the open family with Im(u^N)>0 and principal root marks u=(u^N)^(1/N),v=(1-u^N)^(1/N), every factor in (12) is nonzero. To check it, write alpha=Arg(u^N)>0,beta=Arg(v^N)<0. The third positive central quad angle gives -pi<beta-alpha<0. Neither beta nor beta-alpha is a multiple of pi. For each fixed s the Fourier transform in (11) is not identically zero, since all P_a barP_(s-a) are nonzero. Equation (12) therefore proves that EVERY c_(s,r) is nonzero at every N. Here u^N is a Frobenius center, not a claim about a fixed semiclassical clock radius. No tame geometric-contour estimate is inferred from choosing this center independent of N. In particular the positive half-phase square roots do not automatically select one affine tetrahedral charge. For this open family write alpha_i for the three positive CENTRAL quad arguments, sum alpha_i=pi, and let r0=-s modN, r1=r, r2=s-r modN, 0<=ri<N. The inverse-ratio upper-half-plane square roots have angles beta_i=pi-(alpha_i+pi ri)/N. Their product is q^d on the sum ri=0 or2N sectors and q^(-1) on the sum ri=N sector. Both occur with NONZERO source coefficients. Only the sum2N sector has sum beta_i=pi*d/N; the sum0 sector has sum 3pi-pi/N. Extra physical windows or source constraints are therefore indispensable. They cannot be inferred from the commuting phase-ratio algebra alone. A proposed local Cauchy norm supported ONLY on the desired angle sector is not continuous on this whole cyclic source: a discarded Bell basis vector has zero proposed norm but a nonzero source pairing in (11). This rules out that unqualified ALL-EXTERIOR local norm substitution, not a global comparison after the actual co-source or compensated length metric is used. ## 6. The whole original pointed scalar has a reflected double Use the already proved arbitrary-plat fused source K_N=chi_N N^(1-k) <e_out|B_beta|e_in>. Each input pair is (d,0); each ordinary output pair is (0,d), and the marked output pair is (d,0). On EVERY such pair the eigenvalue of J_s tensor J_s is J_(s,d)J_(s,0)=-q_s. Consequently the input and output corner eigenvalues of J_tot=J_s^(tensor2k) are equal. Hence EXACTLY barK_N=barChi_N N^(1-k) <e_out|J_tot barB_beta J_tot^(-1)|e_in>. (13) This proves a source-exact reflected doubled-word presentation of |K_N|^2, with no normalization by an unknown period. All kernel currents, original Cartan factors and external lines are conjugated and retained. On every standard cyclic quad chart, (10) identifies the inverse-reflected variables; (7) makes the pointed S3 changes compatible. It does not prove that every global cyclic/cluster adapter is unitary, or that all geometric edge isotypic constraints have been selected by this source. If an ordered edge word is reflected with reversed face order, its character transforms chi_e to 1/barchi_e. Existing UNIT characters, including the desired full-clock character, are preserved; a free character has not thereby been chosen. Nor may an exponentially conditioned physical-to-cyclic frame be discarded. The unitarity assertions here are in the specified cyclic flat metric, with the actual source/co-source transformed together. Thus the reflection is a constructive norm-compatible piece of a special-inner-product comparison. A positive angle majorant still requires the actual geometric tensor/wiring map and its controlled current or defect estimate. [Audit](../experiments/audit_phase_ratio_fermat_source.py): exact reflected generators and sources, arbitrary-radius and inhomogeneous normalizers, pointed dihedral identities, phase-ratio spectra/source recurrence, and original complete signed plat sources.

title: A positive determinant period of the actual pointed quantum A-operator
text: # A positive determinant period of the actual pointed quantum A-operator Research note, 27 October 2026. This gives an exact finite algebraic period on the actual A-operator side for every knot. It uses any specified nonzero all-level annihilator and finitely many fixed small-color jets. Its value is a positive ratio of polynomial coefficients of two matrices of fixed bandwidth. Neither the operator's root-level kernel rank nor a separate nonvanishing source-overlap hypothesis is required for the identity. The original Kashaev volume conjecture becomes a precise growth statement for this ratio, equation (6.2). That growth statement is not proved here. Positivity of Gram coefficients is not a substitute for estimating their ratio or relating it to the marked regulator. ## 1. The actual operator, and a fixed amount of pointing Use the actual reduced quantum periods from [the all-level theorem](all_level_a_period.md). A nonzero actual all-level meridian annihilator exists by the independent [finite-cut proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md). Fix one, clear its denominators, and write A=sum_(i=0)^d a_i(q,M) T^i, T M=q M T, a_i in Q[q^(+/-1),M^(+/-1)], a_d!=0. (1.1) The same argument works over a fixed coefficient number field. All original normalization and meridian conventions are retained. The finite small-color pointing gives the exact generic identities sum_i a_i(q,-q^j) C_(j+i)(q)=0, j>=1, C_N(q_N)=<K>_N, q_N=exp(pi i/N). (1.2) Here C_j is the reduced j-dimensional highest-weight cut, with unknot value one. No large-color Jones asymptotic is an input. Equation (1.2) is the repo's own polynomial-rigidity consequence of the actual root states and quotient colors. Remove a common power of q-1 from the coefficients first, so A_cl(M,L)=sum_i a_i(1,M)L^i is nonzero. This changes neither the generic annihilation nor the original root periods. Let A_q be the q-exponent span of a_d, D its M-exponent span, and s its number of monomials. Choose a fixed j_*>=A_q+1 and put B=D(s-1). (1.3) For sufficiently large N, the total order of zeros at q_N in a_d(q,-q^j), j_*<=j<=N-d, is at most B. Briefly, its root specialization has at most D distinct zeros on that color orbit, and any nonzero Laurent polynomial with s monomials has vanishing order at most s-1. The latter is the Vandermonde argument in the all-level note. The choice j_*>A_q prevents a coefficient from vanishing identically on one of the color trajectories. Only the jets through order B of C_(j_*),...,C_(j_*+d-1) will be used. This is a fixed list, independent of N. A smaller starting color is allowed when direct factorization verifies that a_d(q,-q^j) is not identically zero for every subsequent j; the bound A_q+1 is a sufficient uniform choice. ## 2. A finite banded system retains every singular step Put t=q/q_N-1, n_c=N-j_*+1 and n=(B+1)n_c. For each color j_*<=j<=N introduce its truncated jet y_j(t)=sum_(r=0)^B y_(j,r)t^r mod t^(B+1). Define the square n by n matrix M_N by these equations: * For the first d colors, prescribe their B-jets to be the actual fixed-color jets at q_N. * For j_*<=j<=N-d, impose (1.2) modulo t^(B+1), with q=q_N(1+t). Call the right side b_N. It is supported only in the first d color blocks; its norm is bounded as N grows. These fixed Laurent polynomials and their bounded-order jets are analytic near q=1. The matrix has lower block bandwidth d and block size B+1. Its initial diagonal blocks are I; each later diagonal block is truncated multiplication by a_d(q,-q^j). A monomial q^a M^c on the j-th trajectory contributes (-1)^c q_N^(a+cj) binom(a+cj,r) (2.1) to its r-th jet. Thus every entry is O(N^B) and the matrix has fixed bandwidth and size O(N). Negative exponents in (2.1) use the ordinary generalized binomial coefficient. Let R_N select the constant coefficient y_(j,0) from each block. The actual color jets give a solution of M_N y=b_N. (2.2) Although higher jets in a truncated solution may not be unique, every constant color value is unique. Indeed the difference of two solutions has zero initial jets through order B. At a step whose leading coefficient has zero order m, division in the Laurent-series field lowers the known valuation by at most m. Induction gives valuation at least B+1-sum_(previous steps)m >=1. The argument can be performed on arbitrary polynomial lifts: every recurrence error is divisible by t^(B+1), so the same valuation induction applies. Consequently ker M_N subset ker R_N, R_N y=f_N=(C_(j_*)(q_N),...,C_N(q_N))^t (2.3) for every solution of (2.2). No division at the singular value itself was used. The nullity nu_N=dim ker M_N is at most B. In fact a leading coefficient with order m has a multiplication block of nullity m (the total budget ensures m<=B). A lower block triangular matrix has rank at least the sum of the ranks of its diagonal blocks: select invertible minors of each diagonal block and combine them. Their combined minor is lower block triangular with nonzero determinant. Summing the block nullities proves the assertion. An exact per-level pole budget may replace B in this construction. The theorem uses the uniform bound so its block size is fixed. ## 3. The pointed norm is a Gram coefficient ratio For the fixed complex embedding at q_N let dagger be the ordinary Hermitian transpose. Write P=M_N^dagger M_N, g=M_N^dagger b_N, beta=b_N^dagger b_N, Q_N(lambda)=det(P+lambda I), D_N(lambda,z)=det[ P+lambda I+z R_N^dagger R_N g; g^dagger beta ]. (3.1) The variables lambda,z are ordinary commuting polynomial variables. They have no relation to a peripheral longitude. In particular, D_N here is not the root monodromy polynomial of the norm-torsor note. Define G_N(A,j_*)=[lambda^nu_N z]D_N(lambda,z) /[lambda^nu_N]Q_N(lambda). (3.2) **Exact pointed Gram theorem.** The denominator is positive and G_N(A,j_*)=||f_N||^2 =sum_(j=j_*)^N |C_j(q_N)|^2. (3.3) For large N its numerator is positive too: any one of the fixed initial colors tends to the unknot value 1 at q=1. Thus (3.2) is a well-defined positive algebraic period, even at a level where the complete Kashaev value might vanish. Here is a direct proof which also explains the specified coefficient. Use an orthonormal decomposition C^n=(ker M_N)^perp plus ker M_N. On it P=diag(P_r,0), P_r positive definite. By (2.3), R_N is zero on the kernel. Also g has no kernel component. Hence D_N has a factor lambda^nu_N, and its remaining block has size r+1. Let y_0 be the minimum-norm solution of (2.2). Then g=P_r y_0, beta=y_0^dagger P_r y_0. At lambda=0 the Schur complement of P_r+z R_N^dagger R_N is zero at z=0. Its derivative there is y_0^dagger R_N^dagger R_N y_0=||f_N||^2. Therefore the coefficient in the numerator is det(P_r)||f_N||^2, whereas the denominator coefficient is det(P_r). This proves (3.3), without any special-fiber rank-one assumption or pseudoinverse overlap estimate. ## 4. Both polynomial coefficient families are positive Every coefficient of Q_N(lambda) and D_N(lambda,z) is nonnegative real. For the latter form the rectangular matrix Z(lambda,z)=[ M_N b_N; sqrt(z) R_N 0; sqrt(lambda) I 0 ]. (4.1) Its Gram matrix is exactly the bordered matrix in (3.1). The Cauchy--Binet formula writes its determinant as a sum over row sets of squared absolute determinants. In each summand the chosen identity and R rows contribute a definite monomial in lambda,z. Its coefficient is nonnegative. The same proof with the last column and the R rows omitted applies to Q_N. This is positivity of the displayed coefficient periods. It does not assert that the original crossing coefficients are positive, or that every complex minor has been estimated. It removes a separate arbitrary choice of a source overlap from the statement: the original overlap is already contained in the pointed border. All data in (3.1) come from the specified actual A-operator and its fixed small-color jets. No color near N is an input. Conjugation of cyclotomic coefficients uses q_N->q_N^(-1), including the conjugates of the actual initial jets. These matrices still have fixed bandwidth. The matrix P has bounded block bandwidth, and g is supported in the initial blocks: because b_N is supported on the identity initial equations, M_N^dagger b_N is just that same padded initial vector. Placing the last row and column first keeps a bandwidth bounded in terms of d and B, independently of N. The size is O(N), the nullity is bounded, and all entries grow at most polynomially. ## 5. Independence of the operator presentation If two actual all-level operators are used with a common sufficiently large starting color j_*, their ratios (3.2) are identical, by (3.3). Their orders, jet bounds, singular steps and matrix sizes can differ. The equality is exact and retains their distinct lattice presentations. Starting at two different fixed colors changes G_N only by finitely many bounded small-color terms. In particular the construction is not a largest-root prescription, and it does not require an equality between the root-central characteristic and the classical A-polynomial. Multiplying an annihilator by a harmless or singular left factor changes its finite jet system but leaves the exact ratio unchanged when the same pointing and valid pole budget are used. ### A uniformly bounded jet lattice and its classical symbol The polynomial growth in individual jet entries is removable without changing the period. Set S_N=direct_sum_(j=j_*)^N diag(1,N^(-1),...,N^(-B)), M_tilde=S_N M_N S_N^(-1), b_tilde=S_N b_N. (5.1) Since R_N S_N^(-1)=R_N, the pointed Gram theorem applied to these scaled data gives exactly the same G_N. This is a genuine change of lattice and source, not an inference from invariance of an unpointed norm. In the new matrix a jet coefficient of order r is divided by N^r. Formula (2.1) shows that every entry, the matrix operator norm, and the source norm are now bounded uniformly in N. The bandwidth, size O(N), and nullity bound are unchanged. The source border remains confined to a fixed number of initial blocks. This also identifies the bulk symbol of the positive determinant problem directly from the actual A-operator. Write x=j/N, M(x)=-exp(pi i x), delta_M=M partial_M, and let J be the (B+1)-dimensional nilpotent subdiagonal shift. For fixed r, the scaled coefficient in (2.1) tends uniformly to (-1)^c exp(pi i c x) (cx)^r/r!. Thus the banded interior recurrence has block symbol, up to the harmless scalar Fourier factor L^(-d), A_B(x,L)=sum_(i=0)^d sum_(r=0)^B x^r/r! [delta_M^r a_i(1,M)]_(M=M(x)) J^r L^i. (5.2) It is lower triangular in jet degree and satisfies det A_B(x,L)=A_cl(M(x),L)^(B+1). (5.3) No additional classical curve is introduced by the jet repair. For |L|=1 the Hermitian bulk Gram symbol is A_B^dagger A_B, with determinant |A_cl(M(x),L)|^(2(B+1)). The initial equations and source border are explicitly retained boundary terms. These are statements about the chosen actual operator's symbol. They do not assert that its classical polynomial has already been identified with A_K, or estimate the small boundary singular values of the finite matrices. Even a strictly positive bulk Gram symbol need not bound those finite boundary singular values away from zero; the growing-recurrence example below exhibits this. ### The actual quantum period is a positive regularized response There is a canonical convex quadratic problem for these same scaled data, with the original source retained. For real z>=0 put Phi_N(z)=min_y {||M_tilde y-b_tilde||^2+z||R_N y||^2}. (5.4) On the orthogonal complement of ker M_tilde its minimizer is unique. If P_r,Q_r,g_r denote the restrictions of M_tilde^dagger M_tilde, R_N^dagger R_N and M_tilde^dagger b_tilde, respectively, then Phi_N(z)=beta-g_r^dagger(P_r+z Q_r)^(-1)g_r, Phi_N(0)=0, Phi_N'(0)=G_N(A,j_*). (5.5) The second identity follows from the proof of (3.3). Thus the period is an ordinary derivative of an algebraic response function, specified by finite matrices and a fixed source. The positive gradient flow y'=-(P_r+zQ_r)y+g_r solves (5.4) for each fixed N; its existence is not an assumption about a chosen knot state. The source dependence can also be retained in a positive spectral measure. Set H=P_r^(-1/2)Q_r P_r^(-1/2), u=P_r^(-1/2)g_r. For its orthonormal eigenbasis H e_a=h_a e_a put w_a=|e_a^dagger u|^2. Then exactly Phi_N(z)=sum_a w_a z h_a/(1+z h_a), G_N=sum_a w_a h_a, sum_a w_a=beta=O(1). (5.6) All h_a,w_a are nonnegative. The response is increasing and concave in z. The weights record the original source and cannot be dropped in favor of an extremal eigenvalue. Equations (5.4)--(5.6) supply an actual quantum variational problem and its rigid algebraic response for arbitrary knots. Relating this response to the geometric angle-volume optimization and proving its exponential rate remain the geometric part of the conjecture. ## 6. The desired A-polynomial/volume identity, with the original invariant The independently proved positive ordinary-color bound in [the regular-period note](regularized_kashaev_period.md#2-a-positive-trace-bounds-all-the-ordinary-colors) gives |C_j(q_N)|=O_K(N^(b-1)) for 1<=j<N, where b is any fixed knot-braid strand count. Therefore G_N(A,j_*)=|<K>_N|^2+O_K(N^(2b-1)), G_N(A,j_*)>=|<K>_N|^2. (6.1) This is also the earlier positive cyclic trace norm H_N, with its fixed small-color prefix removed: G_N(A,j_*)=N H_N-sum_(j=1)^(j_*-1)|C_j(q_N)|^2. The new content relative to that norm formulation is the explicit positive polynomial-coefficient ratio from the actual operator, its uniformly bounded banded jet lattice and its response function. No new knot state is being introduced. For a hyperbolic knot with positive volume V, its original volume conjecture is consequently equivalent to the polynomial-period identity lim_(N->infinity) (pi/N) log G_N(A,j_*)=V. (6.2) Equivalently the marked regulator norm of the existing torsor gives (2/N)log G_N(A,j_*)-log||P_hyp|| ->0, log||P_hyp||=2V/pi. (6.3) The equivalence uses only the polynomial remainder in (6.1): a positive exponential norm dominates that remainder in either direction. It does not presume that <K>_N is eventually nonzero. If (6.2) were proved, eventual nonvanishing would follow from (6.1). This is a positive determinant-period formulation with the actual quantum A-operator on the left, the original finite pointing retained, and no restriction on bridge number or alternatingness. It is an exact algebraic reduction of the required theorem, not a proof of its exponential estimate. That estimate and its link with the geometric A-curve's marked regulator are still necessary. Fixed bandwidth and polynomial matrix entries alone do not imply a polynomial bound on (3.2): a constant-coefficient recurrence y_j=c y_(j-1) already has a determinant ratio growing as sum |c|^(2j). Small singular values and the source border can encode an exponential rate. No estimate of those determinants is inferred from their construction or from positivity. [Audit](../experiments/audit_pointed_a_gram_period.py). [Results](../experiments/pointed_a_gram_period_results.json). The subsequent [tempered leading-divisor theorem](tempered_a_growth_bound.md) gives a one-sided exponential estimate for this period under its explicit operator hypotheses. It proves the complete leading-germ normalization and a direct matrix-product upper bound through eigenvalue collisions. Its largest-root integral is not identified with the selected volume; the source and sharp lower estimate remain.

title: A polynomial unfolding of the actual pointed cyclic source
text: # A polynomial unfolding of the actual pointed cyclic source Research theorem, 27 October 2026. There is an explicit whole algebraic unfolding of the original cyclic boundary. Allow its cyclic repair to acquire a characteristic polynomial, while keeping the actual highest vector, normalized output row and aligned rank-one multiplicative relation. The resulting sourced moduli chart is a principal open subset of affine (N-1)-space over the Q-line. Every matrix and the full co-source have polynomial formulas. A unipotent conjugation, requiring no quantum-gap division, trivializes the clock and retains the residual spectral polynomial in the transformed co-source. This is a source-specific chart of the existing framed multiplicative-commutator problem. It is not a new definition of the knot invariant, nor a proof that its residual polynomial is the knot's geometric A-polynomial. That requires the actual crossing-word and peripheral transport. ## 1. Keep the source and relax just the fixed cyclic polynomial Let R be any commutative coefficient ring and Q a unit. Let E be locally free of rank N, N at least two. Consider invertible X,Y, a vector v, and rows w,ell satisfying Q inverse X Y X inverse Y inverse=I+v w, (1) Xv=v, ell v=1, ell Y=ell. (2) Require the actual source-orbit chart: v,Yv,...,Y^(N-1)v is a basis. These hypotheses retain the normalized source v ell; in particular its image is aligned with the moment vector v. They relax the additional actual finite-head equation Y^N=I. The row w in (1) is the moment covector; ell is the original co-source and must not be replaced by w. In this canonical basis write Y e_j=e_(j+1), 0<=j<N-1, Y e_(N-1)=sum_(i=0)^(N-1) t_i e_i. (3) Then t_0 is a unit, ell=(1,...,1), and sum_i t_i=1. (4) Conversely choose arbitrary t_1,...,t_(N-1), set t_0=1-sum_(i>0)t_i and invert t_0. Define x_0=1 and x_m=(1-Q^m)t_(N-m) +sum_(l=1)^(m-1)t_(N-m+l)x_l, 1<=m<N. (5) The UNIQUE possible clock is X_(i,j)=Q^i x_(j-i) if i<=j, and zero if i>j. (6) It is invertible: det X=Q^(N(N-1)/2). The unique row w is the zeroth row of Q inverse X Y X inverse Y inverse minus I. All other rows of that matrix vanish. Consequently (3)-(6) are a complete construction and classification over R, including bases with nilpotents. They do not require Q^N-1 or any 1-Q^j to be invertible. Here is the entry proof. Equations (2) and cyclicity first fix the zeroth column of X and the row ell. Equation (1) is equivalent to saying that XY-QYX has image in Rv. In its nonzero-index rows, the first N-1 columns force (6) inductively: until the final column the additional companion term contains X_(N-1,j)=0. For i=N-m>0 the final-column equation, divided only by the unit Q^i, is x_m=sum_(l=0)^(m-1)t_(N-m+l)x_l-Q^m t_(N-m), which is exactly (5). Conversely that recurrence kills every nonzero-index row. Invertibility of X,Y then gives (1) and w. The final-column output equation ell Y=ell is precisely (4). Thus the sourced quotient in this cyclic chart is EXACTLY Spec R[t_1,...,t_(N-1), (1-sum_(i>0)t_i) inverse]. (7) If a free basis of E is included in the data, the representation chart is GL_N times (7). There are no residual stabilizers: an automorphism fixing Y and v fixes its full cyclic basis. In particular the sourced chart is smooth and flat over the whole Q-unit base, of relative dimension N-1. This follows from the displayed coordinate ring, not from a nonroot generic smoothness theorem. The surrounding [framed moment scheme](actual_resonant_framed_moment_smoothness.md) also has a direct root Jacobian proof and a cyclic-vector quotient of relative dimension 2N. The present formulas describe its full sourced subchart globally, rather than merely near that root. ## 2. The pointed spectral factor and a polynomial Hilbert-90 gauge The companion characteristic polynomial and its reversed form are chi(z)=z^N-sum_i t_i z^i, h(z)=z^N chi(1/z) =1-sum_(m=1)^N t_(N-m)z^m. (8) Because chi(1)=0, there are monic and constant-one polynomials chi_red and h_red, respectively, with chi(z)=(z-1)chi_red(z), h(z)=(1-z)h_red(z), h_red(z)=z^(N-1)chi_red(1/z). (9) Let L be the actual finite lowering shift, L e_j=e_(j-1) for j>0 and L e_0=0. Thus L^N=0. Put B=diag(1,Q,...,Q^(N-1)), G=h(L). (10) G is upper unipotent, with polynomial inverse: its nonconstant part is nilpotent. Equations (5)-(6) imply the exact WHOLE identity X=G B G inverse. (11) To verify this without matrix inversion, let x(z)=sum_(m=0)^(N-1)x_m z^m. Recurrence (5) is equivalent to h(z)x(z)=h(Qz) modulo z^N. Thus X=B h(QL)h(L) inverse. Since B L B inverse=Q inverse L, B h(QL)=h(L)B, which proves (11). This is an explicit finite polynomial coboundary, rather than a comparison obtained after truncating a quantum jet or choosing a singular eigenbasis. In particular no factors 1-Q^j or 1-Q^N have been canceled. The source is transported exactly as well: G inverse v=v, ell G=e_0^t h_red(L). (12) Indeed Gv=v and ell(I-L)=e_0^t, while (9) holds at L. Therefore the coefficients of the residual spectral factor remain in the actual transformed co-source. For every whole operator C, ell C v=[e_0^t h_red(L)] [G inverse C G] v. (13) The new transport is G inverse Y G, and every crossing, cap and inserted current has to be conjugated with it. Trivializing X alone does not erase the co-source polynomial. If the original period carries an external peripheral/dimension line, retain that SAME line on both sides of (13), including its norm-zero ratios. ## 3. The actual finite head is a regular section, not a singular limit The actual data are recovered by EQUALITY at t_0=1, t_i=0 for i>0, chi(z)=z^N-1, h(z)=1-z^N, h_red(z)=1+z+...+z^(N-1). (14) Then G=I, X=B, Y=P is the original cyclic repair, and w=(Q^-N-1)e_0^t, ell=e_0^t sum_(j=0)^(N-1)L^j=(1,...,1). (15) This is exactly the original orbit co-source of [the moment/source theorem](actual_rank_one_multiplicative_moment_and_orbit_source.md). The finite head itself still uses its two explicit endpoint deletions; unfolding P has not changed those actual matrices. Conversely Y^N=I FORCES (14): applying it to v and using its cyclic basis gives t_0=1 and t_i=0 for i>0. This works over every commutative base, without a distinct-eigenvalue or characteristic zero hypothesis. The fixed cyclic source is cut out by the N-1 ordinary coordinate equations t_i=0 in the smooth chart (7). It is a flat section over Q. The earlier aligned rigidity theorem is precisely this section, with the defect projector retained. The determinant of (1) supplies another retained character: 1+w v=Q^-N. (16) At a primitive N-th root the matrix v w therefore has square zero, even when w is nonzero elsewhere on the unfolded fiber. The actual section has w=0 there, and its divided normal still recovers e_0 e_0^t. Square-zero boundary monodromy does not imply nilpotence of the full braid image; the previously proved semisimple braid sector is unaffected. ## 4. Finitely many mixed source moments recover the polynomial This chart has a concrete comparison test. The uninserted source moments ell Y^j v are all one, so they cannot distinguish ANY of the residual spectral polynomials. Keep the clock insertion and define instead m_j=ell X Y^j v, 0<=j<N, m_0=1. The canonical columns give m_j=sum_(l=0)^j Q^(j-l)x_l, x_j=m_j-Qm_(j-1), 1<=j<N. (17) If the usual finite-head units 1-Q^m, 1<=m<N, are inverted, equation (5) then gives the UNIQUE recursive reconstruction t_(N-m)=[x_m-sum_(l=1)^(m-1)t_(N-m+l)x_l]/(1-Q^m). (18) Finally t_0=1-sum_(i>0)t_i. The mixed moment map is therefore a polynomial coordinate change over this head localization, with polynomial inverse there; it is not just a pointwise injectivity assertion. The determinant of its Jacobian, in the ordered variables t_(N-1),...,t_1, is exactly product_(m=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^m), (19) because (5) is triangular in this order and (17) is unit triangular. At a primitive N-th root (19) is N. These formulas construct a finite algebraic test for a proposed source-transport comparison and retain its whole normal derivatives. They do not yield a uniform bound on the inverse matrix's condition number; its other entries depend on the retained polynomial. For the actual fixed finite repair P one simply has m_j=Q^j and recovers chi=z^N-1. A different polynomial cannot be assigned to that same transport by relabeling its spectral factor. An actual quantum meridian transport would have to supply its own mixed moments and satisfy the sourced equations before this test could be applied to it. ## 5. What this gives to the A-torsor program There is now a fully explicit algebraic sourced family, its spectral polynomial with a FORCED pointed factor z-1, and a whole comparison carrying the remaining polynomial into the co-source. This supplies functions and a flat scheme before quantum jets. It also makes precise why an unpointed spectral equation and a bare diagonal clock omit selected-period data. Nothing here identifies chi_red with A_K. The coefficients t_i are arbitrary source-transport coordinates until an ACTUAL crossing word or quantum meridian transport produces them. No such new transport is substituted for the original P. The identity (13) compares a given full operator exactly; it does not determine its scalar period or give a growing-N norm bound. An upper-unipotent gauge can have large condition number, so its determinant one is not a subexponential estimate. In particular [the actual Fourier cancellation theorem](actual_fourier_source_cancellation.md) continues to apply. A nonzero formal block with the regulator action can lie in the zero-source current sector. To prove the volume conjecture the actual word class, source polynomial and independent normal/norm divisors must be carried into the marked regulator period. The present theorem is an exact algebraic source unfolding and polynomial comparison; it does not prove that final selected norm. The underlying multiplicative-commutator terminology is covered by [Chalykh--Fairon's one-loop quiver presentation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1704.05814). Only its defining equation is used; the classification and all gauge/source formulas above follow from the entry proof. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_companion_source_shell.py) and [saved results](../experiments/companion_source_shell_results.json) check the universal formulas at six symbolic levels and twelve full generic/primitive-root moment fibers. The [independent proof audit](companion_source_shell_independent_audit.md) checks the chart, periodic section, polynomial gauge and retained co-source separately. The [actual meridian compatibility audit](actual_meridian_companion_source_compatibility.md) now proves a universal mismatch if one tries to use the invariant's meridian orbit state directly as this normalized highest source. Its canonical highest residual has pairing K_N. This chart remains a comparison tool; a division by that unknown value cannot serve as the requested geometric-period proof.

title: Markov reduction of the actual source and its geometric determinant line
text: # Markov reduction of the actual source and its geometric determinant line Research note, 26 October 2026. This continues the invariant's own quantum A/torsor program. The source is the original reduced Kashaev/ADO cut. No comparison with Jones, a custom state, or a published regulator theorem is used. We prove an exact finite source contraction, a uniform geometric Gaussian reduction, and explicit Markov chain equivalences for the linearized holonomy complex. The selected global period's volume norm remains unproved. **Uniform compatibility theorem.** Let beta be any braid whose closure is a knot, at any N>=2 with the original quantum cut normalization. For either Markov stabilization: 1. The actual finite cut contracts exactly to the old cut as a whole meridian germ, with its full modified dimension. 2. At every nondegenerate geometric critical chart, the added quadratic period complex is the old complex plus one explicit acyclic rank-one pair. Its variable principal amplitude cancels the determinant of that pair. 3. At every irreducible fixed-trace representation with ker(dF-I) equal to the infinitesimal conjugation orbit, the linearized holonomy complex is the old one plus an explicit acyclic rank-two pair, and its torsion is unchanged. It is also invariant under braid conjugation and braid relations. The proof below has arbitrary N, braid and representation. The finite computations in the audit validate the formulas; they are not the proof or an assumption on knot examples. This is a uniform structural lemma for the intended volume theorem, not the volume theorem itself. ## 1. The full finite source has an exact contraction Use q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, x=-M/q, the original checked crossings B_+,B_-=B_+^(-1), pivot g=K^(1-N), and theta=x^(1-N). For every N>=2 and every whole color germ, ptr_g(B_+)=theta I, ptr_g(B_-)=theta^(-1)I. (1.1) Thus the zero-framed Markov contraction is identity. The full modified dimension d_N(M) on the remaining cut is unchanged; no peripheral factor is evaluated separately. Here is a coefficient proof, in the original finite basis. It uses the independently derived coefficients in [the actual crossing note](relative_octahedral_period.md#1-exact-formulas-for-both-actual-crossings). Integer-index conservation makes either partial trace diagonal. For the positive crossing, write k=a-b. Its diagonal entry divided by theta is x^(-2a) Q^(a(a-1)) sum_(k=0)^a (-1)^k Q^(k(k-1)/2+(1-a)k) {a choose k}_Q (t;Q)_k, t=Q^(1-a)x^2. (1.2) The sum equals t^a. To prove this, expand t^a in the Newton basis P_k=(t;Q)_k and use t P_k=Q^(-k)(P_k-P_(k+1)). Induction and the Gaussian binomial recursion give precisely the coefficients in (1.2). Its prefactor cancels t^a, proving the first identity. For the negative crossing put n=N-1-a. Root reflection gives {a+k choose k}_Q =(-1)^k Q^(ak+k(k+1)/2){n choose k}_Q. Invert the k Pochhammer factors. With w=Q^a x^(-2), the remaining diagonal sum becomes x^(2a+1-N) Q^(-a(a+1)) sum_(k=0)^n {n choose k}_Q w^(-k)(w;Q)_k. The last sum is w^(-n). Equivalently, sum_k {n choose k}_Q w^(n-k)(w;Q)_k=1; induction follows from {n+1 choose k}_Q=Q^k{n choose k}_Q+{n choose k-1}_Q and P_(k+1)=(1-wQ^k)P_k. The x exponent is then N-1 and the remaining Q exponent is -aN. This proves the second identity in (1.1), for the whole meridian function. ## 2. The regular geometric contraction has one critical variable Use the actual balanced coefficients, with position variables A,B, transfer C and Y=M^2, as in [the principal density calculation](actual_cut_residue_and_principal_density.md). Closing the added strand imposes B=A/C for B_+, B=AC for B_-. The original internal shift ratios give the respective stationary multipliers R_+=-(1-YC/A)(1-B)/[B(1-C)], R_-=(1-AC)(1-Y/B)/[A(1-C)]. On the nondegenerate chart R_sign=1 has the unique solution D=1+Y-A, C_+=A D/Y, C_-=Y/(A D), B_+=B_-=Y/D. (2.1) The excluded factors are actual chart divisors, including A=1,Y and D=0; they are not deleted from the quantum source. Let c=Log C and hold a=Log A fixed. The trace-phase Hessian in its single remaining internal variable is h_+=D^2/[(A-1)(A-Y)], h_-=-h_+. (2.2) These follow by taking (0,-1,1) and (0,1,1) directional derivatives in (Log A,Log B,Log C) of the actual phase Hessian. They are units on the stated regular chart. The original principal amplitudes include their closing pivot and zero-framing factors. Their squares are b_+^2=a_+^2/B^2, b_-^2=Y^2 a_-^2/B^2. Substitution of (2.1) gives exactly b_+^2=h_+, b_-^2=h_-, b_sign^2/(-h_sign)=-1. (2.3) Thus all input- and meridian-dependent factors cancel from the one-variable Gaussian contraction. The remaining minus sign belongs to the fixed Gaussian/quantum normalization line; it is not a new adjustable peripheral multiplier. The full finite normalization is fixed by (1.1). We retain that line rather than evaluating an infinite compact product at a root of unity. The cut-momentum and meridian character multipliers both equal one at (2.1). This follows by multiplying the two input shift ratios for the former and substituting in the actual meridian half-step ratio for the latter. Locally the critical phase therefore differs by a base-only term and integer stationary windings. Those windings are retained characters equal to one on the actual integer lattice. The base-only term has its specified original normalization. ## 3. An explicit map on the quadratic period complexes Let X be the old phase coordinates and let v be the column derivative of c_sign(A(X),Y). For a fixed meridian, partial_(Log A)c_sign =sign*(1+Y-2A)/D. After the stated integer flattening, the critical added phase has no X-dependent value. Its Hessian adjoining the old quadratic form H is consequently H_new=[H+h v v^t -h v; -h v^t h]. (3.1) The unit-determinant change c_tilde=c-c_sign(X) gives U=[I 0;v^t 1], U^t H_new U=diag(H,h). (3.2) This is a chain equivalence of the two-term quadratic complexes. It identifies the old kernel with the graph (xi,v^t xi) and adds the acyclic pair [k --h--> k]. The determinant factor is h. Equation (2.3) supplies its actual amplitude correction, including the universal sign. This proves stabilization compatibility of the variable geometric normal determinant line for every regular irreducible critical representation. It is not a claim that the selected global relative cycle has already been pushed through an arbitrary pole divisor. ## 4. Markov chain equivalences for the holonomy complex We can now prove that the finite-dimensional scalar in the [density note, equation (6.4)](actual_cut_residue_and_principal_density.md#an-invariant-finite-dimensional-complex-for-the-reduction) is invariant under Markov moves on its regular locus. Let X be the product of the noncentral fixed-trace meridian classes. At an irreducible fixed point H of the Hurwitz map F, use 0 -> sl_2 --a--> T_H X --(dF-I)--> T_H X --m--> sl_2 -> 0, a(xi)=([xi,H_j])_j, m(V)=dP(V)P^(-1), P=H_b...H_1. (4.1) It is acyclic when ker(dF-I)=im a. The earlier note proves injectivity of a, surjectivity of m and the well-defined torsion T_beta=det[a,V]/det[(dF-I)V,W], mW=I. For stabilization put A=H_b and append a new meridian Z. Writing G=F(H), the two extended maps are F_+(H,Z)=(G_<b, G_b^(-1) Z G_b, G_b), F_-(H,Z)=(G_<b, Z, Z G_b Z^(-1)). Their fixed-point schemes are exactly F(H)=H,Z=H_b. This follows by eliminating Z directly and holds over Artin rings, not just on reduced points. At such a point write w=(dF(V))_b and use the domain coordinate u=z-w. In the output use V'_b=V_b+Ad_(A^(-1)) z, V'_<b=V_<b, keeping the new last coordinate z. Both are triangular changes of determinant one. The middle differential becomes diag(dF-I,-I) for F_+, diag(dF-I,-Ad_A|_(T_A orbit)) for F_-. (4.2) The infinitesimal conjugation maps to (a,0). The extended product is P_new=Z P, and its transformed last map is m_new(V',z)=Ad_A m(V'). (4.3) Indeed the z term in d(ZP)(ZP)^(-1) cancels precisely against the correction in V'_b. Equations (4.2)--(4.3) are an explicit chain equivalence with the old complex and one acyclic two-dimensional pair. Both Ad_A on sl_2 and Ad_A on its tangent conjugacy orbit have determinant one; the latter also follows from invariance of dK wedge de/e. The signs in -I have even dimension. Therefore T_(beta stabilized)(H,H_b)=T_beta(H) (4.4) for either sign, and regularity is preserved. Braid conjugation is also a chain equivalence: a Hurwitz coordinate change is equivariant and preserves P. Its derivative changes both middle bases equally, so the torsion ratio is unchanged. Braid relations are identities of the Hurwitz maps. Thus this scalar is invariant under the braid presentation moves, with its meridian trace and irreducible representation marked. No equality with a separately defined Reidemeister torsion is used or asserted. ## 5. Consequence for the actual A/torsor program The actual finite source contraction, its geometric Gaussian pair, and the holonomy deformation complex now all have explicit stabilization maps. This is a compatibility for structures attached to the same invariant. It avoids assuming that two arbitrary periods with the same A-symbol coincide. The subsequent [uniform principal-density proof](quantum_source_bridge_extension.md) now compares the variable Gaussian determinant line with (4.1), including its kernel, cut co-source and explicit presentation-parity character. The base-only quantum normalization line and transport of the selected global relative period remain separate.
