These local contractions do not prove that its geometric block survives with subexponential comparison factor across levels. That norm statement is still the required volume theorem. [Audit](../experiments/audit_pointed_markov_reduction.py). [Results](../experiments/pointed_markov_reduction_results.json).

title: A pointed Newton--Green bound for the full figure-eight Fourier energy
text: # A pointed Newton--Green bound for the full figure-eight Fourier energy 28 October 2026. The actual affine rank-two figure-eight operator has an exact positive Green presentation in its Newton lattice. Its central determinant is elementary and its boundary-source response has a uniform polynomial bound. Keeping the Newton evaluation metric then gives the sharp upper exponent for the FULL root-color Fourier energy, instead of the doubled largest-root integral of the earlier homogeneous estimate. The Green estimate is uniform for a checkable class of fixed-width boundary sources, with the broader finite-order pointed UL criterion in Section 3.1. Its application to the figure-eight is an independently proved known prototype, not a new knot class. No claim that arbitrary knot A-operators have this Newton form is made. ## 1. The specified ACTUAL affine operator and its Newton lattice Use the already independently derived operator in `peripheral_normal_period.md`, Section 9: C=c_- T^(-1)+c_0+c_+T, T Y=Q Y T, D=Y(Y+1)(Q-Y^2)(QY^2-1), g=Q^2Y^2-QY^4+QY^3+QY-Q+Y^2, c_-=Y^2(Q-Y)(QY^2-1), c_0=-(Y-1)^2(Y+1)g, c_+=Y^2(QY-1)(Q-Y^2). Set Q=exp(2pi i/N), U=Y^N, h=Y+Y^(-1), d=N-1, and a_r=Q^r+Q^(-r), s_r=2-a_r=4sin^2(pi r/N), t_0=1, t_k=product_(r=1)^k(h-a_r), c=t_N=U+U^(-1)-2. (1) The product identity in (1) follows by writing every factor as (Y-Q^r)(1-Q^rY)/(-Q^rY), or by the monic Chebyshev polynomial. For generic U, the conjugates Q^jY+Q^(-j)Y^(-1) are distinct: equality for j!=k would give Y^2=Q^(-j-k), hence U^2=1. Thus the t_0,...,t_d are a basis of the degree-N field extension C(Y)/C(U). Put A=D^(-1)C over this GENERIC field. This division is performed before the complete fiber; D's zeros at special orbit points have not been replaced by numerical values. The rational telescoping certificate gives, exactly, A t_0=3-h, A t_k=-(h-2)(t_k-t_(k-1)), 1<=k<=d. (2) Indeed its certificate coefficient is (Y-1)^2 Q^k/((Y-Q^k)(1-YQ^k))=-(h-2)/(h-a_k). Multiplying by t_k cancels that last factor, including its whole germ. Multiplication by h sends t_k to t_(k+1)+a_(k+1)t_k; at the last column use t_N=c and a_N=2. Therefore A has the following matrix in the Newton basis, with coincident entries added for small N: diagonal: 1+s_(k+1), 0<=k<d; last diagonal 1, subdiagonal: -1, superdiagonal: -s_(k+1), row k, column k+1, extra corner: -c in row 0, column d. (3) Its coefficients are regular in c. This explicitly defines the free Newton lattice through c=0, retaining the double-point jets when the ordinary orbit evaluation basis coalesces. Its generic relation to the actual operator was proved first; (3) is not a replacement quantization. ## 2. Exact central determinant and the retained source All row sums of (3) vanish except the first, which is 1-c. Hence A(c) 1=(1-c)e_0. (4) The determinant is affine in c. The cofactor of the corner (0,d) is exactly one: deleting its row and column leaves an upper triangular matrix with diagonal -1, and the cofactor sign cancels its determinant sign. At c=1, (4) gives a kernel. Consequently, at EVERY level, det A(c)=1-c=3-U-U^(-1), det C=Norm(D)*(3-U-U^(-1)). (5) No large-period or classical-curve assumption enters (5). The original affine source is C F_N=D(3-U-U^(-1)). In this lattice it is exactly (1-c)e_0, so (4) gives its solution with ALL Newton coefficients one. This is the already identified original whole state F_N(Y)=sum_(k=0)^d t_k(Y). (6) The equality with the original knot cut is the earlier all-level four-plat source theorem. No value of K_N was used to normalize A, its source, the determinant, or the Newton basis. ## 3. Uniform Green bound for fixed-width boundary sources At c=0 write A_0=A(0). It is a killed birth-death matrix: its offdiagonal entries are nonpositive, its row sums are zero except the killing rate one at state zero, and every s_r is positive for 1<=r<N. A direct Green formula proves positivity and the quantitative estimate, so no general Markov-chain theorem is needed. Let A_0 v=g. Write w_i=v_i-v_(i-1), 1<=i<=d. Then w_i-s_(i+1)w_(i+1)=g_i, 1<=i<d, w_d=g_d, v_0-s_1 w_1=g_0. (7) Backward substitution gives the inverse. In particular for g=e_j, v_k=product_(r=1)^j s_r +sum_(i=1)^min(k,j) product_(r=i+1)^j s_r, j>=1, A_0^(-1)e_0=1. (8) Empty products equal one. All entries are nonnegative. If g is supported on states 0,...,J, where J is fixed independently of N, then s_r<=4 gives ||A_0^(-1)g||_2 <=sqrt(N)(J+1)^(3/2)4^J ||g||_2. (9) Thus the source-restricted inverse is polynomially bounded, even though the inverse on unrestricted bulk sources can be exponentially large. For general c the exact rank-one formula is A(c)^(-1)g=A_0^(-1)g +[c/(1-c)]1 [e_d^t A_0^(-1)g]. (10) Its only central denominator is the explicit 1-c in (5). This is the boundary matching certificate which a mere half-orbit fold does not automatically provide. The actual source (1-c)e_0 cancels it as a whole and remains exactly (6). ### 3.1 A broader pointed UL criterion The mechanism is not confined to nonnegative coefficients. In fact A_0=T_s(I-S), where S is the nilpotent lower shift and T_s is upper bidiagonal with diagonal one and superdiagonal -s_(k+1). For a boundary-supported source, T_s^(-1) never sends its support past that same fixed boundary window; (I-S)^(-1) then only takes partial sums. Thus (9) remains valid for complex s_r with |s_r|<=4, without a positivity assertion. More generally fix integers r>=1 and J>=0. Suppose an ACTUAL pointed Newton-frame operator is L_N=U_N(I-S_N)^r, (10a) where U_N is upper triangular and invertible. In its first J+1 rows and columns assume |(U_N)_(ij)|<=N^a and |(U_N)_(ii)|>=N^(-a), for a fixed a>=0. For every original source g supported in 0,...,J, ||L_N^(-1)g||_2 <=binom(N+r-1,r)(J+1)^(J+1) N^(a(2J+1))||g||_2. (10b) Proof: the first J+1 coordinate space is invariant under U_N and its inverse, so inversion uses only that finite block. Write its inverse as the finite Neumann sum after separating the diagonal. Its norm is at most (J+1)^(J+1)N^(a(2J+1)). On the other factor, (I-S_N)^(-r)=sum_(k=0)^(N-1)binom(r+k-1,k)S_N^k, whose operator norm is at most binom(N+r-1,r). This proves (10b). Fixed r,J,a give a polynomial bound even if the unrestricted inverse of U_N or L_N is exponential. This is an independently checkable finite-order OPERATOR AND SOURCE condition, not a condition on the desired value. Any comparison to it must preserve the actual boundary source and track its evaluation metric; an exponentially conditioned basis cannot be silently dropped. An additional fixed-rank central boundary update is governed by its explicit Schur matrix I-V^t L_N^(-1)U. Formula (10) is precisely the rank-one instance with Schur factor 1-c. No polynomial inverse of that Schur matrix is asserted without a separate algebraic certificate. ## 4. The actual root metric gives an endpoint barrier The Newton lattice is NOT asserted isometric to the original orbit. Retain its evaluation matrix V_(j,k)=t_k(Q^j), 0<=j,k<N. (11) For j=0, t_k(1)=|F_k|^2, F_k=(Q;Q)_k. For 1<=j<N, t_k(Q^j)=0 if k>=min(j,N-j), |t_k(Q^j)|=|F_(j+k)| / (|1-Q^j| |F_(j-k-1)|) otherwise. (12) This follows by factoring each term into its two sine factors. The ordinary indices in the second line stay between zero and N-1, so no unmarked root wrap or division by F_N occurs. Let J_0(x)=integral_0^x log(2sin(pi t))dt, 0<=x<=1, and put Delta=max J_0-min J_0=2 Lambda(pi/6)/pi. (13) The endpoint-uniform factorial estimate, proved by extracting log t and log(1-t) and applying Stirling to the remainder, is log|F_k|=N J_0(k/N)+O(log N). Also |1-Q^j|>=2sin(pi/N)>=4/N. Equations (12) and the logarithmic endpoint modulus of continuity imply log max_(j,k)|V_(j,k)|<=N Delta+O(log N). (14) At j=0 this uses 2max J_0=Delta; elsewhere it uses the DIFFERENCE of the two endpoint values J_0((j+k)/N)-J_0((j-k-1)/N), bounded by Delta. This is an endpoint barrier, not a full-circle integral of the pointwise largest root. For ANY polynomially bounded fixed-width source g in (9), its Newton response r=A_0^(-1)g has polynomial norm. Keeping (11) gives ||V r||_2^2<=poly(N) exp(2N Delta). (15) The unitary root-color Fourier transform has exactly that same norm. For the actual source r=1, it is the FULL energy E_N=|K_N|^2+sum_(j=1)^(N-1)|C_j(q_N)|^2, with its original pointing. The independent ordinary-color audit bounds the second term by a polynomial, but (15) already bounds the entire norm directly. The actual marked regulator calibration gives Vol(4_1)=4Lambda(pi/6). Thus (15) yields limsup (pi/N)log E_N<=2pi Delta=Vol(4_1), (16) where the earlier homogeneous largest-root envelope was 2Vol(4_1). For this particular source the positive sum at j=0 also supplies the known matching lower rate by a bulk factorial term. This is a prototype calibration of the Green mechanism, not a new broad-class theorem. ### 4.1 Stress check: the metric estimate is uniform on the whole unit circle The upper exponent is not an artifact of sampling exactly at root nodes. Let G(t)=log|2sin(pi t)|, periodically extended, and let J_0 be its periodic primitive of mean-zero derivative. Uniformly for real u and 0<=k<N, sum_(r=1)^k G(u+r/N) <=N integral_0^(k/N)G(u+s)ds+O(log N). (16a) For completeness, partition the sampled interval into monotonicity pieces of G. Away from the at most bounded number of mesh cells adjacent to a zero of sin, the Riemann-sum error telescopes and is O(log N): the retained cell endpoints are at distance at least 1/N from that zero. In the removed cells every sampled value is at most log 2; the cell integrals are bounded below by -(log N+C)/N, including when a zero lies inside the cell. A sample arbitrarily close to zero can only DECREASE the sum. This proves the one-sided uniform estimate, with no root-separation assumption on u. For Y=exp(2pi i u), the two sine factors in t_k give from (16a) log|t_k(Y)| <=N[J_0(u+k/N)-J_0(u-k/N)]+O(log N) <=N Delta+O(log N), (16b) uniformly on the full unit circle, including all zeros by continuity. Thus the same sharp exponential metric bound applies to the continuous unit-circle Fourier norm as well as the original root-color norm. It also permits fixed q-tags in the arguments without changing the rate. Conversely the complete entry t_k(1)=|F_k|^2 at k/N near 5/6 has rate Delta. Hence the root evaluation matrix itself satisfies lim_(N->infinity) N^(-1)log||V_N||=Delta. (16c) All exponential scale in this pointed Green example is therefore carried by a specified, quantitatively estimated evaluation metric. It is not hidden by calling the Newton change of basis unitary. ## 5. Checkable class and genuine generalization requirement The estimate (9) is a uniform source-independent theorem for every birth-death matrix (3) with 0<=s_r<=4 and every fixed-width boundary source. The root-metric estimate (15) applies whenever the ACTUAL operator/source has the Newton representation (1)--(3), or a uniformly polynomially conditioned comparison preserving its boundary source and evaluation. Neither hypothesis is an assertion about the unknown scalar. They can be checked by finite operator identities, as above. For a general knot, Weyl symmetry alone neither supplies (3) nor controls a folded boundary determinant. The original ordinary-color bounds fix the polynomial tail, but do not prove that the pointed normal response is a tame boundary-source Green vector in a basis with a controlled geometric evaluation metric. Establishing such a source-exact basis or an analogous multichannel Green estimate would be a substantive next step. No new knot, bridge family, or general volume upper bound is claimed. [Audit](../experiments/audit_pointed_newton_green_barrier.py): actual generic-orbit conjugacy including all c/D factors, central determinant, boundary-source Green formulas and bounds, root-evaluation endpoint products, and exact full-energy Plancherel through the original colors.

title: Pointed recoupling and relative period descent
text: # Pointed recoupling and relative period descent Research note, 25 October 2026. This continues the structural program. The result is an exact comparison of selected algebraic vacua, their normalization lines and their classical Bloch labels under recoupling. It applies uniformly to finite recoupling diagrams. The remaining identification with the intrinsic knot period is stated in Section 7. Write C_(s,t) for the explicit pointed factorization in `pointed_steinberg_recoupling.md`, and set tau(s,t)=(1-st)/(1-t), f(s,t)=t(1-st)/(1-t)^2, h=(n-1)/2, det C_(s,t)=f(s,t)^(nh). All formulae are on the nondegenerate parameter locus. Local maps are defined over its algebraic function field and extend wherever their intrinsic sections are regular. No angle-positivity assumption is used. ## 1. The pointing extends to arbitrary matched affine transports The Steinberg family is a normalization of a larger pointed family. Let g=(lambda,mu) be an affine central character with lambda*mu nonzero. Choose nonzero endpoint roots a,b such that b^n=lambda*a^n+mu. On E_(g;a,b)=K[x]/(x^n-lambda), define X f=x f, Y f=(b-a x)f(omega^(-1)x). The norm is b^n-a^n*lambda=mu. The unit is the unique vacuum line for Y+aX-b, since this operator is (b-a x)(sigma^(-1)-1). Rescaling X'=aX/b,Y'=Y/b gives exactly the Steinberg module with parameter lambda*a^n/b^n. For g,h use endpoints c->d and a->c, respectively. Assume also mu_(gh)=mu_g+lambda_g*mu_h is nonzero, so that the composite and relative matrix algebras below are nondegenerate. The tensor coproduct preserves the pointing of their composite a->d: L_tot=L_g+X_1 L_h, f(x) -> f(x_1x_2). This follows from c matching on the two factors. The injections are strictly coassociative. Thus the pointed construction is not confined to affine characters fixing the point one. The same relative operators Z=Y_1Y_2^(-1), D=X_1+Z, C=ZX_2 have central character lambda_rel=mu_(gh)/mu_h, mu_rel=-mu_g*lambda_h/mu_h. Their compatible endpoints are c/a -> d/a. With L_rel=-C+(c/a)D-d/a, L_tot=L_g+X_1 L_h, L_rel=(L_g-Z L_h)/a, L_h=D^(-1)(L_tot-a L_rel). (1.1) These are exact identities at indeterminate quantum parameter. Normalizing the two endpoint modules gives the earlier C_(s,t), with s=lambda_g*c^n/d^n and t=lambda_h*a^n/c^n. The resulting factorization therefore preserves the selected unit, with all endpoint scalars known. For the unscaled monomial bases its determinant is [a^n*lambda_h*mu_(gh)/mu_h^2]^(nh). (1.2) Indeed the target basis rescaling has determinant (a/d)^(n^2 h), the source rescaling has determinant (ac/d^2)^(n^2 h), and f(s,t)=lambda_h*mu_(gh)*(ac/d)^n/mu_h^2. Substitution in the previous determinant formula gives (1.2). ## 2. The Racah map is the same explicit pointed factorization Consider three Steinberg modules E_r tensor E_s tensor E_t, with all nonempty consecutive products different from zero and one. Put a=tau(rs,t), b=tau(r,s), c=tau(r,st), d=tau(s,t). Then cd=a and tau(c,d)=b. Order the left decomposition as E_(rst) tensor E_a tensor E_b, and the right as E_(rst) tensor E_c tensor E_d. Their evaluation maps are I_L=(C_(r,s) tensor 1) P_23 (C_(rs,t) tensor 1), I_R=(1 tensor C_(s,t)) (C_(r,st) tensor 1). Here P_23 is the literal vector-space permutation. Exactly I_L=I_R (1 tensor C_(c,d)). (2.1) In particular the recoupling maps the product of the two distinguished multiplicity vacua to their product, with coefficient one. For a proof uniform in the quantum parameter, write Y_12=X_1Y_2+Y_1, Y_23=X_2Y_3+Y_2, Y_123=X_1X_2Y_3+X_1Y_2+Y_1. The two left relative pairs A,B and two right pairs C,D have X_A=Y_123 Y_3^(-1), X_B=Y_12 Y_2^(-1), X_C=Y_123 Y_23^(-1), X_D=Y_23 Y_3^(-1), Y_A=-Y_12 Y_3^(-1)X_3, Y_B=-Y_1Y_2^(-1)X_2, Y_C=-Y_1Y_23^(-1)X_2X_3, Y_D=-Y_2Y_3^(-1)X_3. Keeping these orders, direct multiplication gives X_A=X_C X_D, Y_A=X_C Y_D+Y_C, X_B=X_C+Y_CY_D^(-1), Y_B=-Y_CY_D^(-1)X_D. (2.2) For the first identity the intermediate Y_23 cancels. For the third, 1+X_2Y_3Y_2^(-1)=Y_23Y_2^(-1); the others follow by the same ordered products. These are exactly the two-factor factorization formulae of C_(c,d). Both sides of (2.1) preserve the unit in all three factors and intertwine the same full matrix algebra. The pointed uniqueness theorem proves equality, including its scalar. This identifies a recoupling operator with the explicit q-factorial kernel, rather than only defining it as a ratio of unspecified maps. ## 3. The normalization cocycle and the permutation sign The units obey the rational identity f(c,d)=-f(r,s)f(rs,t)/[f(r,st)f(s,t)]. (3.1) Let gamma_(s,t)^n=f(s,t)^(-h), so gamma C has determinant one. Put Gamma_L=gamma_(r,s)gamma_(rs,t) and Gamma_R=gamma_(r,st)gamma_(s,t). The recoupling from these normalized tree evaluations is exactly F_hat=(Gamma_L/Gamma_R) C_(c,d). (3.2) Its determinant is (-1)^h, not necessarily one. This is forced by the single permutation P_23 in (2.1): the flip on two n-dimensional factors, and its tensor extension, both have determinant (-1)^h for odd n. Dropping that sign would give a false normalization law. If one independently normalizes C_(c,d) by gamma_(c,d), the ratio epsilon=Gamma_L/[Gamma_R*gamma_(c,d)] satisfies epsilon^n=(-1)^h. For a Racah normalization with its correct signed determinant, take eta_(c,d)^n=(-1)^h*f(c,d)^(-h). Then Gamma_L/[Gamma_R*eta_(c,d)] is mu_n-valued. (3.3) It is constant on each irreducible lifted parameter component. This proves the rigidity statement with its actual hypotheses and records the root phase, rather than canceling it at a special value. ## 4. Descent of the selected finite period on a recoupling diagram For any binary tree T, iterating the pointed C maps gives an evaluation I_T into the same tensor product of leaf modules. It is invertible and takes the product vacuum to the product vacuum. For two trees the transition is I_(T')^(-1)I_T. Consequently F_(T',T'') F_(T,T')=F_(T,T''), and every loop is the identity. This proves exact pointed coherence, including the pentagon and disjoint recouplings. If the node maps are multiplied by their specified roots gamma, let Gamma_T be their product. The transition becomes F_hat_(T,T')=(Gamma_T/Gamma_(T'))F_(T,T'). (4.1) All higher coherence still holds by cancellation. The normalized product vacuum is transported with precisely this scalar. Thus the selected line, not just the unpointed module, descends on this recoupling groupoid with its normalization line. The conclusion is stable under every finite exterior contraction: a matrix identity may be tensored with any exterior tensors and paired along any chosen indices, retaining the same scalar. Sums are finite, so no face-rank or convergence assumption enters this step. It includes scalar periods and open boundary tensors, and does not require the resulting period to be nonzero. These are algebraic identities on their common parameter cover. They extend to every regular specialization of the corresponding sections. Generic units must first be retained and canceled in that identity; specializing a displayed fraction at a pole is not a definition of its section. ## 5. The Bloch label is the tetrahedral cross-ratio For the four cumulative points p_0=1, p_1=r, p_2=rs, p_3=rst, the cross-ratio in the recorded convention is z(r,s,t)=(1-rs)(1-st)/[(1-rst)(1-s)] =b/c=tau(c,d)/c. (5.1) Thus the recoupling has a natural tetrahedral Bloch label. Four consecutive parameters give five cumulative points; their alternating tetrahedral boundary is [z(s,t,u)]-[z(rs,t,u)]+[z(r,st,u)] -[z(r,s,tu)]+[z(r,s,t)]=0. (5.2) This is the same five-point relation established in the Bloch note, by deleting each of the five vertices. The classical regulator and the quantum pointed recoupling therefore have compatible local coherence diagrams. Equating their *global period classes* still requires the comparison in Section 7. ## 6. Intrinsic normalization lines from spinor brackets The extra affine-frame data in f must be distinguished from the cross-ratio (5.1). For four nonzero affine coordinates p_i, direct substitution gives the Racah unit f_R=-p_1p_2(p_0-p_2)(p_1-p_3) /[p_0p_3(p_1-p_2)^2]. (6.1) Choose nonzero homogeneous flag vectors v_i in K^2, and set lambda_ij=det(v_i,v_j). In the affine frame v_i=(p_i,1), remove the displayed vertex-frame factor to obtain f_bar=-lambda_02 lambda_13/lambda_12^2. (6.2) This is GL(2)-invariant. Under v_i -> a_i v_i it is multiplied by a_0a_3/(a_1a_2), so it is intrinsically a section of a decoration line, rather than an invariant number after forgetting those lines. The cross-ratio and its complement are z=lambda_02 lambda_13/(lambda_03 lambda_12), 1-z=-lambda_01 lambda_23/(lambda_03 lambda_12), by the elementary Plucker relation. Their n-th roots give the local Fermat norm cover on this flag torsor. There is also an exact shared-face normalization. On an ordered triangle put q_ijk=lambda_ik/lambda_jk^2. With the usual multiplicative coboundary, f_bar(0123)=-(delta q)(0123)^(-1). (6.3) Choose roots alpha_ijk^n=q_ijk^h on faces and define the tetrahedral root eta_0123=(delta alpha)(0123). Then eta_0123^n=(-1)^h*f_bar(0123)^(-h), (6.4) the signed Racah normalization of Section 3. Sharing the face roots, rather than choosing unrelated tetrahedral roots, makes their product over a 3-chain equal to the face product over its boundary. Interior face roots cancel. On the boundary of a 4-simplex it is one because delta^2=1. This proves strict compatibility of these scalar normalization sections with the five-term relation. The statement is valid for actual equivariant vector flags or for sections of their decoration lines with the corresponding transition functions. A PSL(2) lifting obstruction or nontrivial peripheral characters must remain in those line transitions; they are not set to one by choosing an affine chart. Such data can leave peripheral factors after gluing, exactly where a generic unit can specialize to a numerical multiplier. ## 7. The remaining global theorem We have proved selected-vacuum coherence on the recoupling parameter groupoid, algebraic transport through arbitrary finite exterior contractions, and relative descent of its normalization line on decorated flag charts. The local Bloch label has the same five-point coherence. These statements are uniform and use no knot census. The subsequent `affine_frame_period_transport.md` and `projective_frame_period_torsor.md` prove full matrix/frame covariance on the specified local root covers. They also prove that the selected unit must generally be transported to a nonconstant vector. A global knot period still needs an intrinsic decorated-character gluing construction, its peripheral lifts and its selected period class matched with the literature state. The exact local Faddeev comparison does not by itself identify that global cycle. The regulator comparison across levels also remains necessary for the volume conjecture.

title: Pointed Steinberg modules and a basis-free pentagon
text: # Pointed Steinberg modules and a basis-free pentagon Research note, 25 October 2026. This develops the algebraic recoupling theory suggested by the period torsor, rather than another knot case. Cyclic 6j-symbols already have this origin: Kashaev, [Quantum Dilogarithm as a 6j-Symbol](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9411147). The proofs below are direct; no novelty is claimed for the categorical pentagon. A particular published matrix normalization is not assumed. The subsequent [integral extension](cyclic_steinberg_lattice.md) extends the local algebraic factorization to every level, supplies the even-level determinant sign, and computes the recoupling lattice at simultaneous nilpotent degeneration. Its endpoint chain also accounts for the actual quantum-group Borel coproduct. The odd-level analytic and global normalization conventions below are not automatically extended by that local calculation. ## 1. A rigid local vacuum Fix odd n and a primitive n-th root omega in a characteristic-zero field K. For t and 1-t nonzero use the split cyclic algebra and module A_t=K<X,Y>/(XY=omega YX, X^n=t, Y^n=1-t), E_t=K[x]/(x^n-t), X f(x)=x f(x), Y f(x)=(1-x)f(omega^(-1)x). The norm identity in `heisenberg_period_torsor.md` proves the splitting. Its distinguished vector is the unit 1, since (X+Y-1)f=(1-x)[f(omega^(-1)x)-f(x)]. (1.1) As 1-x is a unit, the kernel is exactly K*1. Therefore X+Y-1 has rank n-1, and a -> a.1 identifies the pointed module with (E_t,1)=(A_t/A_t(X+Y-1),[1]). (1.2) A cyclic-dilogarithm matrix is a change between frames of this algebraic vacuum, rather than an additional choice of an analytic solution. Its determinant-normalized frames require the preceding Heisenberg cover. This module is the local Faddeev difference module itself. In the previously audited functional equation set q=exp(2pi i b^2), X=-q^(-1/2)exp(2pi b Z), (Y f)(Z)=f(Z-i b), where q^(-1/2)=exp(-pi i b^2). Then XY=qYX and exactly (X+Y-1)Phi_b=0. For b^2=1/n with odd n, X^n=exp(2pi sqrt(n) Z)=t and the dual functional equation gives Y^n Phi_b=(1-t)Phi_b. Moreover Y[f(X)Phi_b]=(1-X)f(q^(-1)X)Phi_b. Thus its central fibre is precisely (E_t,1), under f(x) -> f(X)Phi_b. This identifies the operator, parameter and vacuum, without an analytic limiting argument. The remaining central period multiplier is fixed by the exact identity in `rational_quantum_dilogarithm_torsor.md`; the module relation alone does not determine that multiplier. ## 2. Coproduct and central characters Use the quantum affine bialgebra B=K<X,X^(-1),Y>/(XY=omega YX), Delta X=X tensor X, Delta Y=X tensor Y+Y tensor 1. Multiplication verifies the relation after Delta. Both iterated coproducts send Y to X tensor X tensor Y+X tensor Y tensor 1+Y tensor 1 tensor 1, so Delta is coassociative exactly. The nondegenerate central fibre X^n=lambda,Y^n=mu is a full n by n matrix algebra after a splitting extension. The root-of-unity q-binomial identity gives (Delta X)^n=lambda_1 lambda_2, (Delta Y)^n=mu_1+lambda_1 mu_2. (2.1) This also holds for composite n: the intermediate q-binomial coefficients vanish because 1-omega^j is nonzero for 0<j<n. Thus central characters multiply by the affine-group law (lambda,mu)*(lambda',mu') =(lambda lambda',mu+lambda mu'). The Steinberg subfamily closes as (s,1-s)*(t,1-t)=(st,1-st). For it there is a canonical pointed B-linear injection m_(s,t):E_(st)->E_s tensor E_t, f(x)->f(x_1 x_2). (2.2) For Y the two terms combine to [x_1(1-x_2)+(1-x_1)]f(omega^(-1)x_1x_2), proving the assertion. These maps are strictly coassociative by substitution of x_1x_2x_3. ## 3. A pointed factorization with an explicit ideal certificate Assume s,t,1-s,1-t,1-st nonzero. In A_s tensor A_t put X_tot=X_1 X_2, Y_tot=X_1 Y_2+Y_1, Z=Y_1 Y_2^(-1), D=X_1+Z, C=Z X_2, tau=(1-st)/(1-t). The quantum torus relations alone imply X_tot Y_tot=omega Y_tot X_tot, DC=omega CD, [X_tot,D]=[X_tot,C]=[Y_tot,D]=[Y_tot,C]=0. Moreover X_tot^n=st, Y_tot^n=1-st, D^n=tau, (-C)^n=1-tau. (3.1) For the last pair, X_1Z=omega ZX_1, Z^n=(1-s)/(1-t), and C^n=t(1-s)/(1-t). Oddness gives (-C)^n=-C^n. These exhibit commuting copies of A_(st), A_tau. Their unital map from the simple matrix algebra A_(st) tensor A_tau is injective after a splitting extension and both sides have dimension n^4. The equality descends: A_s tensor A_t = A_(st) tensor A_tau. (3.2) The vacuum is preserved. Write L_i=X_i+Y_i-1. The exact identities are L_tot=X_tot+Y_tot-1=L_1+X_1 L_2, L_rel=D-C-1=L_1-Z L_2, (3.3) L_2=D^(-1)(L_tot-L_rel), L_1=L_tot-X_1 D^(-1)(L_tot-L_rel). Thus the generated left ideals coincide. These identities hold even at generic quantum parameter in the localized quantum torus; the root-of-unity equations (3.1) identify its finite central fibres. There is consequently a unique isomorphism of pointed modules C_(s,t):E_(st) tensor E_tau -> E_s tensor E_t, C_(s,t)(1 tensor 1)=1 tensor 1, (3.4) intertwining the two commuting algebras (3.2). Explicitly send x^a y^b to X_tot^a D^b(1 tensor 1). The factorized common vacuum kernel has dimension one and (3.3) puts the old unit in it. Simplicity and equal dimensions give invertibility; the unit fixes the scalar. This is a uniform statement about pointed modules, stronger than the existence of an unpointed intertwiner. It is not yet an identification of the global knot period across arbitrary triangulations. ### 3.1 The exact kernel and its normalization unit This factorization has an explicit finite-product kernel. In the commutative coordinate algebra E_s tensor E_t write w=x_1x_2, z=x_2. Then D f(w,z)=(w/z)f(w,z) +(1-w/z)/(1-omega z)*f(w,omega z). Induction, starting with f=1, gives D^b 1=product_(j=1)^b (1-omega^j w)/(1-omega^j z). Thus, in the monomial bases, the pointed Clebsch--Gordan map is C_(s,t)(u^a v^b) =w^a (omega w;omega)_b/(omega z;omega)_b. (3.5) No undetermined scalar remains. These are q-factorial ratios in the same local family as the earlier custom products, now with a specified module meaning, phase, and vacuum. Taking their magnitudes does not identify the entire earlier positive state with this tensor construction. Its determinant also has a uniform formula: det C_(s,t) =[t(1-st)/(1-t)^2]^(n(n-1)/2). (3.6) Here the target basis is x_1^i x_2^j and the source is u^a v^b, with the first index ordered first in both. To prove (3.6), first replace the target basis by w^a z^k. Its determinant is t^(n(n-1)/2): for each a, reducing z^(a+k) modulo z^n=t contributes t^a; its cyclic permutation has sign one for odd n. Over K(w), each column b of (3.5) is multiplied by N_b(w)=product_(j=1)^b(1-omega^j w). Its field norm is (1-st)^b. The product of these norms is (1-st)^(n(n-1)/2). The remaining columns are R_b(z)=1/(omega z;omega)_b. For b>=1, R_b(z)=product_(j=b+1)^n(1-omega^j z)/(1-t). Their degrees are n-b, while R_0=1. The triangular leading-coefficient calculation gives det(R_b in the z^k basis) =omega^[n(n^2-1)/3]/(1-t)^(n-1). The sign is one because its exponent is (n-1)^2. This determinant appears to the n-th power over K, so its phase disappears exactly. Combining the three factors proves (3.6). Writing h=(n-1)/2 and f=t(1-st)/(1-t)^2, a specified cyclic determinant normalization can be taken on the mu_n-cover gamma^n=f^(-h), C_normalized=gamma C_(s,t). (3.7) It has determinant one because dim C=n^2 and det C=f^(nh). Equation (3.7) specifies a particular mu_n subcover of the general mu_(n^2) determinant choices. It retains a nonconstant algebraic unit, not just an unspecified root-of-unity scalar. Compositions must carry this unit before any peripheral specialization. For fixed nondegenerate classical parameters this normalization also has a uniform size bound, with no choice of root affecting it: log|gamma|=-(n-1)/(2n)*log|f|. Thus any fixed finite recoupling diagram accumulates a bounded logarithmic contribution from these units as n varies. Self-dual finite Fourier measures add only explicit powers of n. After the states and their period classes are identified, these recorded changes cannot alter their exponential volume rate. This assertion applies at nonzero finite f; cancellation and specialization at a zero or pole must be performed in the generic period identity first. ## 4. Recoupling without integral limits or chosen matrices For arbitrary nondegenerate affine central characters g,h,gh, take splitting modules H_g,H_h,H_(gh) of dimension n and define W(g,h)=Hom_B(H_(gh),H_g tensor H_h). The tensor product is an n^2-dimensional module over the split matrix algebra of the product character, hence n copies of its n-dimensional irreducible module. Therefore dim W(g,h)=n and evaluation is an isomorphism W(g,h) tensor H_(gh) -> H_g tensor H_h. (4.1) This only uses the specified nondegenerate central fibre, not a semisimplicity assertion for all B-modules. For three characters composition gives two canonical isomorphisms W(g,h) tensor W(gh,k) -> Hom_B(H_(ghk),H_g tensor H_h tensor H_k), W(h,k) tensor W(g,hk) -> Hom_B(H_(ghk),H_g tensor H_h tensor H_k). Their ratio defines the basis-free recoupling map. For four characters every parenthesization identifies in the same way with Hom_B(H_(ghkl),H_g tensor H_h tensor H_k tensor H_l). Both compositions in the pentagon are the same map through this common space. This proves the pentagon exactly by coassociativity and composition. It requires neither analytic limits nor a choice of cyclic-dilogarithm branches. On the Steinberg subfamily W(s,t) is canonically a pointed Steinberg module E_tau: the commuting algebra of Section 3 acts by postcomposition and its distinguished vector is m_(s,t). Equations (3.3) put it in the relative vacuum line. This identifies (3.4) with the evaluation map (4.1). Choosing bases turns these recoupling maps into cyclic 6j matrices. Frames introduce exactly the factors and root choices that require normalization torsors. Literal equality to a particular matrix still requires its basis, roots, measure and determinant convention to match. ## 5. The global comparison that remains This supplies one uniform algebraic origin of the local 2--3 recoupling relation on the nondegenerate locus at every odd level. Individual knot integrals need not reprove this coherence statement. The finite face theorem evaluates singular presentations and edge reduction supplies the boundary module. The required intrinsic knot period still needs a functorial gluing construction joining these pieces, with its peripheral data, duality pairings and normalization line. Degenerate central fibres are not covered by the matrix-algebra argument and must be handled explicitly in that construction. The rational Faddeev identity fixes its local Heisenberg/dilogarithm period. Its global cycle and the regulator comparison remain separate obligations. Coassociativity proves coherence, but does not by itself prove the numerical volume-growth law. The next task is this global comparison, not more knot cases.

title: Pointed tetrahedron modules and all-level edge reduction
text: # Pointed tetrahedron modules and all-level edge reduction Research note, 26 October 2026. This constructs strict shape-ordering maps, including explicit pointed root intertwiners, and proves integral edge-lattice primitivity for link exteriors in S^3. It extends the earlier odd-level edge reduction to every N. In particular a positive geometric triangulation of a hyperbolic knot supplies a nonzero rank-N quantum boundary block at every level on the stated central cover, without a global branching assumption for this module construction. The projected tensor generator is specified, but its nonvanishing, its identification with the actual relative ADO source, and its marked Bloch-regulator norm are not proved. Shape-module order changes are not automatically tensor-face adapters for the full [Verma period](verma_tetrahedral_transport.md). The marked peripheral lattice at even N requires a separate distinction in Section 7. ## 1. A pointed shape module and its strict order changes For local parameter R use the quantum Laurent algebra A_R=<X^(+/-1),Y^(+/-1): XY=R YX>, D_R=A_R/A_R L, L=X+Y-1, with distinguished generator [1]. For an oriented tetrahedron R=Q^(-epsilon), epsilon=+/-1. Its shape triad is Z_0=X, Z_1=Y^(-1), Z_2=-X^(-1)Y, Z_0 Z_1 Z_2=-R^(-1). The cyclic ordering map and reflection are rho(X)=Y^(-1), rho(Y)=-Y^(-1)X, sigma(X)=Y, sigma(Y)=X, sigma(R)=R^(-1). (1.1) Reflection is understood either semilinearly in the local parameter or as a linear map to the oppositely oriented algebra. Exact noncommutative substitution gives rho^3=1, sigma^2=1, sigma rho sigma=rho^(-1), rho(L)=-Y^(-1)L, sigma(L)=L. (1.2) The unit in rho(L) is on the left. Thus these maps preserve the correct left ideal and give actual pointed module maps, with [1] sent to [1]. Their coherence is exact rather than projective. The ordinary S_4 action on the six cross-ratios factors through this S_3. This supplies shape-module changes under local vertex orderings. It does not assert that the Klein-four action on face tensor legs has been constructed merely because it is trivial on shape coordinates. The module is related directly to the compact tetrahedral operator. If psi(a)=P_Q(a)^(-1), then psi(Qa)=(1-a)psi(a). Multiplication by a and the shift a->Qa give X+Y-1 on this generator, with parameter R=Q^(-1). Multiplying by the exact monomial shear in the preceding note transports this relation to its tetrahedral kernel module. This is an algebraic statement about the local functional module, not a termwise root evaluation of psi. ## 2. Explicit pointed root intertwiners Let R=r^2 have order N, with r^N=-1. On the nondegenerate shape cover choose s,t satisfying s^N+t^N=1, st!=0. Use the clock/shift representation X e_a=s R^a e_a, Y e_a=t e_(a+1 mod N). It is the full matrix algebra. The kernel of L is one-dimensional: normalize p_0=1 and use p_a/p_(a-1)=t/(1-sR^a), 1<=a<N. (2.1) The last cyclic equation is exactly s^N+t^N=1. All components are nonzero. The left-ideal quotient D_R at this center is an N-dimensional simple module: a matrix L of rank N-1 gives a left-ideal quotient of dimension N, and a[1]->a p identifies it with this representation. The root cover itself has exact order changes rho:(s,t,r)->(t^(-1),r s/t,r), sigma:(s,t,r)->(t,s,r^(-1)). (2.2) They obey the same S_3 relations. The factor r in rho is required: its N-th power gives the minus sign in 1-t^(-N)=-s^N/t^N. There is an explicit canonical matrix adapter. For rho use (A,B)=(Y^(-1),-Y^(-1)X); for sigma use (A,B)=(Y,X). Let (s',t',r') be (2.2), and let p' be (2.1) at that target. Put P_0=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1)(A/s')^j, v=P_0 e_0, J e_a=(B/t')^a v. The spectral projector and cyclic arrows show that J is invertible and intertwines both clock/shift generators. Its kernel image Jp' is a nonzero multiple of p. Divide J by its zeroth component to impose Jp'=p. (2.3) This fixes its entire scalar. The module relations (1.2) imply that a composition for an S_3 relation commutes with the full matrix algebra; (2.3) makes that scalar one. Thus cyclic rotation three times, reflection twice, and the braid relation have exact pointed coherence at every N, including even and composite N. No determinant-normalized or unitary metric assertion is needed. The subsequent [Regge/cover calculation](regge_period_covers_and_a_curves.md#the-quantum-ordering-maps-are-explicit-gaussians) now writes these same adapters as explicit Gaussian Fourier matrices divided by their actual pointing scalar. It retains the quadratic Gauss phase in the unpointed order-three cycle, and gives the scalar's exact Hermitian norm as a ratio of the two kernel norms. This solves the finite ordering part; it is not a full face-tensor S_4 or global selected-state theorem. ## 3. The integral edge lattice, without a branching Let K be a connected oriented triangulated 3-dimensional pseudomanifold whose vertex links are closed orientable surfaces; this includes an ideal triangulation of a cusped manifold and ordinary finite vertices with sphere links. Let T,E,V denote the numbers of tetrahedra, global edges and vertices. Write Lambda=direct-sum_j Z^2, Omega=direct-sum_j epsilon_j [[0,1],[-1,0]]. In tetrahedron j the opposite pairs are (01,23), (02,13), (03,12). For a global edge e let a_e,b_e,c_e be its incidence counts in these pairs. Its vector in Lambda is beta(e)_j=epsilon_j(a_e-c_e,b_e-c_e). Let E_ed=im beta. This definition uses arbitrary local vertex orders and their orientation signs, not a global branching. The sign gives the physical edge equation when an odd local reordering inverts the corresponding ordered shape. Omitting it from the incidence calculation gives an integrally symplectically isomorphic lattice, by multiplication of that tetrahedron block by -1, so the rank and saturation statements are the same. Isotropy has a direct face proof. Assign values lambda and mu to global edges, and form the local opposite-pair sums a,b,c and u,v,w. After factoring out epsilon_j, their local symplectic contribution is (a-c)(v-w)-(b-c)(u-w). For three ordered edge values put omega(l,m)=sum_cyclic(l_i m_(i+1)-l_(i+1)m_i). The displayed contribution is exactly minus the alternating sum of omega over the four ordered faces. Each pair of nonopposite edges occurs on its unique face, which verifies the formula termwise. The face expressions cancel under the orientation-reversing face identifications. Therefore Omega(E_ed,E_ed)=0. (3.1) This argument is unaffected by arbitrary local reordering, because both the face orientation and the three-edge alternating form transform by the same permutation sign. ## 4. Exact saturation and the missing prime 2 Put h=dim H^1(K;F_2). The nonzero Smith entries of beta are 1 repeated E-V-h times, 2 repeated h times. (4.1) Here is an independent proof. Over any field of odd characteristic, a row dependence says a=b=c in each tetrahedron. These equations are equivalent to lambda_ij=t_i+t_j. The local t's are uniquely recovered from the three edge values of a face by division by 2. They therefore descend to one t at every global vertex. The vertex-sum map is injective, since a triangle's three zero endpoint sums force all its t's to vanish. Hence rank beta=E-V in every odd characteristic, as well as over Q. In characteristic two, a=b=c is instead equivalent to the four triangle sums being equal. Face pairing makes their common value one global constant sigma. Subtract sigma times the constant edge assignment. The result is exactly a simplicial 1-cocycle on K. Conversely every such cocycle and every sigma give a dependence. The constant assignment has triangle sum one and is independent of the cocycles. Thus dim ker(beta mod 2)=1+dim Z^1(K;F_2)=V+h. (4.2) It remains to exclude Smith factors 4,8,..., not merely odd factors. Work with a dependence lambda valued in Q/Z. Locally one can solve lambda_ij=t_i+t_j, since multiplication by 2 is surjective on Q/Z. Two choices on a paired face differ by the same element of order at most 2 at its three vertices. Therefore 2t descends to global vertex values u, and 2lambda_ij=u_i+u_j. This is the reduction of a rational vertex-sum dependence. By Smith normal form, the quotient of Q/Z-valued dependences by reductions of rational dependences is the dual of the torsion in Lambda/E_ed. The preceding calculation kills it by 2. All nonzero Smith entries therefore equal 1 or 2; (4.2) counts exactly h entries equal to 2. This proves (4.1). For an exterior of a link in S^3, H^1(K;F_2)=0. Attach cones to each boundary component to obtain K; finite sphere vertices do not affect H_1. The cone Mayer--Vietoris sequence identifies H_1(K) with the cokernel of H_1(boundary M)->H_1(M). The meridians generate H_1(M)=Z^c for a c-component link, so this cokernel vanishes, including over F_2. Consequently E_ed is primitive in Lambda for S^3 link exteriors. (4.3) For a knot all edge-row dependences are constants, and the sum of all edge rows is zero integrally. Deleting any one edge row therefore gives an integral basis of E_ed, with no index hidden at 2. Equation (4.3) strengthens the odd-level argument in the [earlier Heisenberg reduction](heisenberg_period_torsor.md). ## 5. Edge reduction at every root level Fix nondegenerate tetrahedral central shapes satisfying the classical edge equations, and choose the recorded central-root cover. The tensor product of the root tetrahedron modules is a split irreducible quantum-torus module W of dimension N^T. This follows directly from their clock/shift matrix units. Use lambda^2=Q, lambda^N=(-1)^(N-1), for example lambda=-q_N. Use A_j=Z_(0,j), B_j=Z_(1,j), so A_j B_j=Q^epsilon_j B_j A_j. These are the first two triad variables, rather than the original X,Y pair of Section 1. For integer vectors v=(a,b) the Weyl convention is W(v)=lambda^(-sum epsilon_j a_j b_j) A^a B^b. It has the exact multiplication with factor lambda^Omega and its N-th power is precisely its classical central monomial. These statements include all even-level signs. Shape identities such as Z_0 Z_1 Z_2=-Q^epsilon and their induced edge units are part of the specified characters, not discarded constants. Choose a basis e_1,...,e_r of the primitive isotropic E_ed and specified commuting edge characters c_i with c_i^N=W(e_i)^N. All dependencies and their units must be matched. Such characters have an explicit realization on the central-root cover: if s_j,t_j are the roots of X_j^N,Y_j^N in Section 2, then eta(e)=product_j s_j^(a_j)t_j^(-b_j) is a multiplicative root character for W(e). A different compatible prescribed lift differs by a mu_N-valued character. This labels the lifts; it does not select the actual ADO source lift by nonvanishing. Then U_i=c_i^(-1)W(e_i) commute and U_i^N=1. The exact projector is Pi_chi=product_i (1/N)sum_(a=0)^(N-1)chi_i^(-a)U_i^a, chi_i in mu_N. (5.1) Every nonidentity term has zero trace: primitivity implies that a nonzero linear combination of the e_i modulo N is nonzero in Lambda/N Lambda, and noncentral clock/shift monomials have zero trace. Therefore rank Pi_chi=N^(T-r) (5.2) for every compatible prescribed character and every N>=2. The coinvariant quotient is canonically the image of Pi_chi. This supplies nonzero reductions at all levels; it does not permit choosing a character to force the desired period. The saturated lattice B=E_ed^perp/E_ed is free and unimodular symplectic. One can extend E_ed to an integral symplectic basis: choose a primitive e, solve Omega(e,f)=1 by Bezout, split off that pair and continue. Its remaining pairs act on im Pi_chi. The N-th-power central characters are retained on the same root cover. Their nonidentity Weyl operators have zero trace on the reduced space, by inserting (5.1) in the full trace. The resulting N^(2(T-r)) trace-orthogonal matrices span its entire endomorphism algebra. This proves irreducibility for the saturated boundary algebra, with no inversion of 2 modulo N. For a torus-cusped link exterior, Euler characteristic gives T-r=c. The module has dimension N^c; for a knot it has dimension N. The assertion remains valid with finite sphere vertices, since their genus contribution is zero. ## 6. The gluing vector and its ordering compatibility Let p_j be the specified tetrahedron generator in its splitting frame. The reduction has a specified candidate vector s_(T,N,chi)=Pi_chi(p_1 tensor ... tensor p_T). (6.1) The later [factorial source-torsor theorem](factorial_source_torsor.md) identifies this local tetrahedron kernel, after reversing its index, with the pointed cyclic dilogarithm phi_a. The actual factorial boundary is p_a=nu^a phi_a, nu^N=1-h^N; this is a singular frame at the Kashaev wall h=1. Its full affine source and cut-root adapters are explicit. This supplies local relative data; it does not identify the nondegenerate geometric root fiber with that degenerate actual boundary fiber. This is the root block of the usual left/right quantum gluing quotient: first impose the tetrahedron left ideals, then the edge coinvariants. A centralizer of the edge action, including the saturated boundary algebra, acts on it. The pointed order-change maps of Sections 1--2 intertwine the whole edge operators and their transported characters. Hence they intertwine (5.1), carry (6.1) to its corresponding vector, and obey the same exact cocycle relations. This proves local shape-order independence of the module and its projected vector. A global branching is unnecessary for this module construction. The vector (6.1) can still be zero even though the reduction has the nonzero rank (5.2). The trace of a projector does not prove that it is nonzero on a particular tensor. Nor has this candidate gluing vector been identified with the selected relative Verma trace or actual ADO source. In particular the root tetrahedron module was obtained by its algebraic relation, not by evaluating the four singular compact factors separately. ## 7. The marked peripheral lattice and its integral half-longitude For a knot the saturated boundary lattice B is unimodular of rank two. The earlier audited unhalved meridian/longitude rows have symplectic pairing -2. Whenever these are the chosen marked vectors, their span has index two in B. This is a peripheral index; it does not contradict the primitivity of the edge lattice. The subsequent [integral half-longitude proof](integral_half_longitude.md) identifies the missing half using the knot marking itself: B=Z delta(mu) + Z ell, ell=delta(lambda)/2, Omega(delta(mu),ell)=-1. A mod-two dual-face cochain proves that delta(lambda) pairs evenly with every balanced integral vector, because the preferred longitude is nullhomologous in the exterior. Unimodularity gives the unique half in B. An explicit edge correction constructs its integer representative before specializing N. Thus the unhalved algebra is generated by Y,T^2 inside the saturated algebra generated by Y,T, with TY=q^2 YT. At odd N these give the same finite Weyl algebra. At even N the unhalved algebra has two sectors distinguished by Y^(N/2), each of dimension N/2 after central normalization, and T exchanges them. The scalar lift satisfies T^2=Lambda_hat only after the full edge character and the specified square root are retained. In particular changing T to -T at even N does not change T^N. The actual central longitude and source pointing must still be matched. The [even-meridian ADO normalization](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) records its separate full-state sign character; no arbitrary choice of a sector or square-root sign identifies the states. If h in (4.1) is nonzero for a different manifold, the edge lattice itself can also be nonprimitive. Already E=<2f> has compatible reductions of dimension gcd(2,N) and vanishing reductions for incompatible even-level characters. Lens-space examples verify this distinction in the audit. The S^3-link hypothesis in (4.3) is doing actual work. ## 8. Consequence for the ideal-triangulation route The audited positive triangulation theorem supplies nondegenerate classical shapes for every hyperbolic knot. Sections 1--6 then supply order-compatible pointed tetrahedron modules and a nonzero rank-N geometric boundary block at every level on the specified cover, without a global branching requirement for this reduction. This upgrades the earlier local central-support calculation to an actual nonzero geometric quantum module. Placing that block in the actual affine meridian source extension, matching its projected vector and boundary functional to the relative Verma period, and identifying the marked Bloch-regulator norm are still necessary. The marked peripheral scalar lift in Section 7 must be transported explicitly. No geometric factor of the minimal actual A-operator or noncancellation in the selected period follows from module rank alone. ## 9. Coverage and independent diagnostics The integral edge complex and its 2-primary phenomena belong to Neumann's existing triangulation framework; see the statement coverage in [Combinatorics of triangulations and the Chern--Simons invariant](https://www.math.columbia.edu/department/neumann/preprints/cspaper.pdf). No integral exactness proof from it is used above. The elementary face pairing, endpoint-potential and Q/Z arguments prove the needed lattice statements here. The abstracts of [Garoufalidis--Yu, 2403.12424](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12424) and [Panitch--Park, 2403.12850](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12850) cover quantum gluing quotients and quantum trace maps. Their comparison, move and state-identification proofs are not premises. No novelty claim is made for the general quantum gluing framework. The point here is the explicit ordering/root phases and the all-level reduction with the remaining selected-period issue kept separate. [The audit](../experiments/audit_pointed_tetrahedron_gluing.py) checks the abstract pointed S_3 maps, finite root adapters in both orientation parameters, the six-edge face identity, exact edge Smith forms and mod-2 cohomology with arbitrary tetrahedron relabelings, and finite projectors including even N. Closed nonprimitive examples and index-two peripheral sectors are included as scope checks. The [results](../experiments/pointed_tetrahedron_gluing_results.json) support the uniform proofs; no volume asymptotic is inferred. The saved full audit has 49 abstract Laurent checks, 18 pointed root-adapter cases through level 12 in both orientation parameters, 45 exact incidence/Smith/cohomology checks including arbitrary tetrahedron relabelings and nonprimitive closed examples, and 11 edge-projector checks. The figure-eight projector checks include the full saturated boundary trace basis at every listed level; the Whitehead-link checks have the predicted N^2 dimensions. Nine parity tests retain incompatible nonprimitive characters and the two marked peripheral sectors at even N. The full reproduction command in this workspace is PYTHONPATH=.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages python3 experiments/audit_pointed_tetrahedron_gluing.py --regina

title: Positive angle majorants: half-period gluing and the affine source charge
text: # Positive angle majorants: half-period gluing and the affine source charge 28 October 2026. Failure of a bare 2-to-3 identity does NOT disqualify the positive angle-factorial partition function as an upper comparison. For a fixed complete geometric triangulation its already proved exponential rate is the desired one, and fixed constants or polynomial measure corrections have zero exponential rate. There is a constructive distinction between the N-clock and the FULL 2N-clock q=exp(pi*i/N). On STRICT angle support, the full clock already forces the geometric edge lift by positivity and the total-angle identity. A second lemma shows that the AFFINE charge d=N-1 removes all winding aliases even on weak nonnegative support, provided the full clock selects edge residue 2d. The resulting positive norm has the sharp geometric upper exponent. These are genuine bounds for the stated angle tensors. An exact map from the full original source to those tensors has not yet been proved. A weak sum-N angle tensor, with zero angles permitted, does retain an exponentially excessive winding face even with the full 2N-clock. That is the precise boundary scope of the obstruction below; it must NOT be applied to the strict-support lemma. This does NOT disprove a subexponential upper comparison for the FULL original Kashaev scalar. No nonzero original-source coefficient is assigned to the bad winding. Such a comparison remains possible if the actual source removes or cancels it before positivity is taken. ## 1. The correct normalization for an upper comparison For a fixed complete positive ideal triangulation T let w_N(k)=product_i s_N(k_i)^(-1), s_N(a)=product_(j=1)^a 2sin(pi*j/N), and let P_N be its strict integral angle structures: each tetrahedral triple sums to N and each global edge sums to 2N. The positive model is Z_N(T)=sum_(k in P_N)w_N(k). On its allowed lattice progression, (pi/N)log Z_N(T)->Vol(M). (1) This is the independently proved positive-volume theorem in [the original comparison note](quantum_a_volume.md#5-a-broad-theorem-for-a-positive-angle-state-comparison). The desired upper comparison is |K_N|² <= exp(o(N)) Z_N(T), (2) or equivalently |K_N|<=exp(o(N))sqrt(Z_N(T)). The square root is essential: Z has the ENERGY rate Vol/pi, not the amplitude rate Vol/(2pi). Any unchanged full peripheral/dimension line multiplies both sides with its exact square modulus; at the marked complete point the known such lines have polynomial magnitude and do not change (1). They cannot remove an exponential gap. For a fixed T, (1) means (2) is equivalent, on that progression, to the sharp original-source exponential upper bound. Merely knowing (1) does not prove (2); the nontrivial input must be an independent source-preserving comparison. Conversely, a finite move multiplier 8, N, or any fixed-degree boundary unit is not an obstruction to (2). ## 2. Exact positive Fourier gluing gives a different norm Let H_N have orthonormal basis indexed by k_i in{0,...,N-1}, each tetrahedral triple summing EXACTLY to N. Zero angles are allowed in this finite vector space, because s_N(0)=1. The forbidden all-pi triple would require an entry N and is absent. Define the positive vector v_N=sum_k sqrt(w_N(k)) |k>. Let E be the actual integral edge-angle incidence matrix and mu,nu the marked peripheral angle rows. The geometric projection P_geo, with peripheral restrictions included, is the diagonal orthogonal projector onto E k=2N*1, mu k=nu k=0. (3) Write P_geo^edge for the projector imposing ONLY E k=2N*1. One may impose the same EXACT peripheral restrictions on both sides of a comparison, or omit them on both. No modular-to-exact peripheral conclusion is used below. On the strict coordinates its squared norm is the corresponding positive angle partition. Allowing zero angles on the SAME integer fiber still has maximum volume at most Vol(M), by the same continuous concavity argument; zeros alone are not the problem. Now use the finite root Q=exp(2pi*i/N), as in the actual quantum Fourier transform. The character average on a constraint row c is (1/N)sum_(r=0)^(N-1) Q^[r(c k-bN)] =1 if c k=bN modulo N, and0 otherwise. (4) It sees no difference between b=0,1,2. Multiplying (4) over the edge and peripheral rows gives the orthogonal projector P_cyc onto E k in N Z^edges, mu k,nu k in N Z. (5) Hence an INDEPENDENT finite-Fourier/Plancherel gluing of these positive angle tensors gives exactly ||P_cyc v_N||² =sum_(k satisfying5) w_N(k)=:Z_N^cyc(T), P_geo<=P_cyc. (6) This is an equality of positive Hilbert-space norms. Replacing this N-clock cyclic projector by the exact geometric projection decreases the norm; it is not an automatic upper-bound operation. A unitary Fourier change of basis does not alter this projection order. ### 2.1 The FULL 2N-clock is sufficient on strict support For a cusped ideal triangulation with torus cusps, the edge count equals the tetrahedron count t. Each quad angle is counted twice in the sum of all edge incidences, so for every tetrahedral sum-N state, sum_edges (E k)_e=2Nt. (6a) The full q-character average is (1/(2N))sum_(r=0)^(2N-1) q^[r((E k)_e-2N)] =1 iff (E k)_e=0 modulo2N. (6b) On STRICT support every edge sum is positive. Equation(6b) then makes every edge sum at least2N. Their total is exactly2Nt and there are t edges; hence EACH sum is exactly2N. Consequently P_(2N-edge-cyclic)=P_geo^edge on strict angle support. (6c) The equality remains true after imposing the SAME exact peripheral restrictions on both sides. The sum argument does not upgrade modular peripheral conditions to exact ones. Thus one does not need a separate EDGE integer-lift projector if an original-source comparison retains both the full 2N edge character and strict angle support. This conclusion is constructive and independent of a local Pachner equality. ### 2.2 The affine d-charge is stronger, including at zero angles There is an equally useful variant matching the original reflected trivalent source equation h0+h4+h2=d=N-1. Suppose nonnegative angle indices satisfy tetrahedral sum d, and the full q-character selects (E k)_e=2d modulo2N at EVERY edge. (6d) The least nonnegative representative of 2d is 2d, strictly positive for N>=2. Each edge sum is therefore at least2d, while their total is exactly2dt. Since the number of edges is t, all sums MUST equal 2d, even if some individual angles vanish. No bad winding sector survives. This is a finite support identity, not an asymptotic claim. Let Z_N^aff be the positive factorial sum over this nonnegative sum-d/full-clock space. Then Z_N^aff <=N^C exp[N Vol(M)/pi] (6e) for a fixed triangulation-dependent C (and trivially if the set is empty). Indeed k/d is an exact weak geometric angle structure. The geometric volume bound gives sum_i Lambda(pi*k_i/d)<=Vol(M). The uniform modulus of continuity |Lambda(x)-Lambda(y)| <=C |x-y|(1+|log|x-y||) follows by integrating its two logarithmic endpoint singularities. Since |k_i/N-k_i/d|<=1/N, it changes the volume by O(logN/N). The uniform sine-factorial estimate then bounds EVERY weight by N^C exp[N Vol(M)/pi], and there are at most N^(3t) states. This proves(6e), with the original zero-angle weights retained. On any allowed nonempty progression for the strict model(1), its rounding proof gives the quantitative lower bound Z_N(T)>=N^(-C')exp[N Vol(M)/pi]. Indeed the rounded geometric angles differ by O(1/N), remain in a fixed strict neighborhood, and their volume differs by O(1/N); the uniform factorial error is O(logN). Thus(6e) actually gives Z_N^aff<=N^C'' Z_N(T), and in particular Z_N^aff<=exp(o(N))Z_N(T). A source-preserving norm map to THIS affine angle space, of subexponential norm and with the actual full-clock residue(6d), WOULD give the requested upper comparison. No lower/survival theorem would be required for that step. The local actual trivalent d-charge is already established in the source notes. What is not established here is its global realization as the tetrahedral angle indices of an arbitrary geometric T, with the full edge character(6d) after all Fourier/Gaussian/source adapters. The subsequent [supporting-plane and defect theorem](positive_angle_supporting_plane_and_defect_bound.md) weakens this target further: O(1) TRUE integer edge-charge errors cost only a polynomial, and o(N) errors preserve the sharp volume upper exponent, with an explicit Gaussian deficit. This is not a statement about bounded changes of residues modulo2N. ## 3. A certified exponential gap on a complete geometric triangulation Use the actual positive nine-tetrahedron 5_2 triangulation and exact rational angle vector alpha from [the previously certified fixture](positive_geometric_alias_volume_counterexample.md). The new conclusion here is the positive NORM comparison (6), not a claim about the coefficient of that fixture in the original state. (7) For 20|N, k_N=N alpha is therefore a legitimate basis vector in P_cyc H_N, with BOTH original marked peripheral equations exact. Its edge sums are even multiples of N, so it also survives the FULL 2N-clock on WEAK sum-N support. It fails the exact geometric edge lift. The exact geometry and outward-rounded dilogarithm evaluation give 3.76403<V_alias<3.76404, 2.82812<Vol(M)<2.82813. (8) The uniform sine-factorial estimate, including k_i=0, implies log w_N(k_N)=N V_alias/pi+O(log N). Retaining this ONE nonnegative term in (6), and using (1) along a common allowed progression, proves the rigorous gap liminf (pi/N)log[Z_N^cyc(T)/Z_N(T)] >=V_alias-Vol(M)>.93590. (9) Here the common progression can be any multiple of20 and of a denominator of a strict rational geometric angle structure. Such a denominator exists: rational solutions of the fixed rational affine equations are dense in their real affine solution space, and a complete positive point has an open strict neighborhood. Thus the denominator Z_N(T) is nonempty on that progression. If peripheral rows are added to the denominator, either it is nonempty on a further progression and the same upper volume bound applies, or an attempted all-level comparison already encounters an empty denominator. For (9) it suffices to use the original edge-only Z_N(T) of (1). In amplitude norm the unavoidable loss of this cyclic relaxation is at least exp[N(V_alias-Vol)/(2pi)+o(N)]. Neither a finite fixed number of move constants nor any polynomial measure/source factor changes it. The defect in(7) is O(N), so shifting angle indices by O(1) to correct N-versus-N-1 conventions also cannot repair it. This is a triangulation-based positive Gram obstruction for the WEAK sum-N model, already after exact tetrahedral equations and both peripheral rows, and even with the full 2N-clock. The strict alias locus for this particular face is empty: its zero edge forces three flat tetrahedra. It does NOT contradict(6c) or the differently charged affine model(6d). It does not rely on an oversized raw crossing state or on positivity of an unnormalized local pentagon. ## 4. A useful exact local connection, and its limit For 1<=L<N and0<=a<=L, reflection gives s_N(L)s_N(N-L)=2N sin(pi*L/N). Consequently the modulus of a genuine Gaussian coefficient is EXACTLY a positive tetrahedral angle weight times a polynomial factor: |[L choose a]_Q| =2N sin(pi*L/N) /[s_N(a)s_N(L-a)s_N(N-L)]. (10) The three indices on the right sum to N. Formula(10) applies also at a=0,L, where the tetrahedron is flat. It connects the original root-factorial magnitudes to the positive model more directly than merely sharing the same dilogarithm asymptotic. It can be applied to the Gaussian blocks AFTER any independently proved exact fusion. It does not, by itself, prove that the resulting triples have the complete knot triangulation's GLOBAL edge constraints with the correct full character and affine residue. A coefficientwise Cauchy--Schwarz estimate, or a convex majorization of factorial magnitudes, does not specify those constraints. The full phases and relative source may supply them. Lemmas(6c),(6d) show that this is a more concrete sufficient target than independently imposing unwrapped winding after every Fourier transform. ## 5. What would still establish the requested majorant The 29 October [length-normalized star and Gram identities](actual_length_normalized_star_gram.md) now give exact local square-root weights with all normalizers retained. The [original singleton clock source](actual_length_gauge_clock_source.md) has polynomial Riesz norm at arbitrary signed braid width. These establish a genuine original-source Cauchy framework. The original paired factorial gauge really fixes the complete cup/cap source, and the existing [weighted Fourier theorem](actual_weighted_fourier_plat_energy.md) retains the compulsory dual metric. It does not presently produce a map from the full original source to the strict or affine angle space above for an arbitrary positive geometric triangulation. The normalized finite Fourier transform supplies a SPECIFIED modular character, so its modulus and affine residue matter. The dual metric cannot be silently flattened. Nor does merely remembering that the scalar q has order2N prove that the source map implements(6b) or(6d). For instance, on the N-dimensional cyclic head let S|a>=|a+1 moduloN> and T|a>=q^a|a>. Then exactly T S-q S T=2|0><N-1|. (11) The strict nilpotent shift has no such wrap term. Thus changing an N-cyclic clock to a half-period clock while dropping its endpoint current is not an exact basis change. The subsequent [source-exact half-clock dilation](actual_half_clock_source_dilation.md) now supplies a faithful 2N ambient physical window: its weighted E/F shifts, genuine dual turns, original N-normalization, unrolled H, half-Cartan, pivot and selected one-component cut are all retained. What remains to be proved is its map to geometric tetrahedral angle indices and the GLOBAL edge characters(6b) or(6d); physical degree conservation alone does not identify those characters. In the conventions of [the pointed module](pointed_tetrahedron_gluing.md), for positive orientation, Z0 Z1 Z2=-Q. Setting zeta_i=q^-1 Z_i gives EXACTLY zeta0 zeta1 zeta2=-q^-1=q^d. (12) Thus the d-charge is consistent with the original half-period ordering, rather than chosen solely to make an optimization work. The three quad operators do not commute, however, so(12) is not itself a joint positive angle basis or a full tensor gluing theorem. There is also a central-sign constraint on transporting this local rescaling globally. If a chosen edge corner word has valence v_e, rescaling every corner by q^-1 multiplies that word by q^(-v_e). For its NEW character to equal q^-2=q^(2d), its OLD character would have to be q^(v_e-2), in that same specified ordering. But zeta_i^N =-Z_i^N. At an ODD-valence edge, the proposed old character has (q^(v_e-2))^N=-1, (13) so it cannot simply be imposed on that SAME geometric central fiber. title: A geometric supporting-plane bound for positive factorial energies with charge defects
text: # A geometric supporting-plane bound for positive factorial energies with charge defects 28 October 2026. Complete positive geometry gives a quantitative upper certificate for the angle-factorial model even when the edge charges are not exact. Bounded integer edge defects cost only a polynomial factor. Sublinear defects preserve the sharp volume exponent. There is also a uniform Gaussian deficit away from the complete angle point. This is a statement about the positive angle energy, with its specified normalization. It does not identify that energy with the original Kashaev period. In particular, the exact scalar in the original star--triangle identity is a FULL binomial, whereas the one-tetrahedron energy amplitude is its square root after division by N. Section 5 records that compulsory normalization distinction. ## 1. The complete geometric supporting plane Fix a finite complete positive ideal triangulation T with t tetrahedra. Let x* be its angle vector in units of pi, and put mu=min_i x*_i>0, V(x)=sum_i Lambda(pi*x_i), Lambda'(theta)=-log(2sin theta). Let A be the tetrahedral sum matrix and E the global edge-angle incidence matrix. Thus A x*=1, E x*=2*1, V(x*)=Vol(M). (1) No peripheral equation is required for the following upper bound. One may impose additional exact peripheral restrictions on the same angle variables; that only restricts the set being bounded. There is no claim that a modular peripheral condition becomes exact. Define the full coordinate gradient g_i=-pi*log(2sin(pi*x*_i)). There are FIXED real vectors lambda,eta such that g=A^t lambda+E^t eta. (2) Indeed, complete geometric gluing is stationary for volume on the angle slice Ax=1,Ex=2. One direct check uses fixed cusp horospheres and ideal Schlaefli: a tangent v with Av=Ev=0 has dV(v)=-(pi/2)sum_e ell_e(Ev)_e=0, with the SAME truncated global edge length ell_e on all incident tetrahedra. Hence g annihilates ker(A,E), and elementary real linear algebra proves (2). Equivalently one can fix a row basis of (A,E), solve (2) once, and retain that certificate. Row dependencies make the certificate nonunique but do not change its pairing with a consistent charge defect. For EVERY weak local angle point x>=0 with Ax=1, V(x)<=Vol(M)+eta dot(Ex-2) -c_*||x-x*||_2², c_*=pi³*mu/64>0. (3) Thus the supporting-plane linear terms telescope exactly into the integral edge defects. They are not independent per-tetrahedron errors and do not require estimating a different critical branch. ## 2. An explicit global quadratic deficit Here is a proof of the constant in(3), including boundary points. For one tetrahedron use independent coordinates x1,x2 and x3=1-x1-x2. Its negative Hessian is pi² [[cot(pi*x1)+cot(pi*x3), cot(pi*x3)], [cot(pi*x3), cot(pi*x2)+cot(pi*x3)]]. (4) Its determinant is pi^4, by the cotangent addition identity, and it is positive definite in the strict simplex. Along the FIRST HALF of the segment x_s=(1-s)x*+s x, every coordinate is at least mu/2 and at most1-mu. Consequently each cotangent has absolute value at most2/(pi*mu), so the trace of(4) is at most 8pi/mu. Its least eigenvalue is therefore at least pi³*mu/8. For a tetrahedral tangent v=(v1,v2,-v1-v2), ||v||_3²<=3(v1²+v2²). Thus its second derivative on that half-segment is at most -(pi³*mu/24)||v||_3². Integrate the Taylor remainder with weight1-s over0<=s<=1/2. Since the remaining part of the segment has nonpositive second derivative, V(x*)+g dot(x-x*)-V(x) >=(pi³*mu/64)||x-x*||². (5) For a boundary endpoint, apply the argument before reaching the endpoint and then use continuity of Lambda. Summing over tetrahedra gives(5) for the whole vector. Substitution of(2) and Ax=Ax*=1 proves(3). Global uniform strong concavity of the Hessian at every boundary point is NOT assumed; integrating its controlled first half is what gives the global deficit from the fixed interior x*. ## 3. The actual factorial weights and bounded edge-charge errors Use precisely s_N(k)=product_(r=1)^k 2sin(pi*r/N), w_N(k)=product_i s_N(k_i)^(-1), 0<=k_i<N. The uniform estimate, including k=0 and N-1, is log s_N(k)=-(N/pi)Lambda(pi*k/N)+O(log N). (6) For an explicit elementary error bound write log(2sin pi*x)=log x+log(1-x)+h(x), where h is smooth on[0,1]. The increasing log term has sum-integral error between0 and logN+1, the decreasing log term has absolute error at mostlogN, and h contributes at most its fixed total variation. Thus the constant in(6) is universal. In a fixed triangulation all weight errors are bounded by C_t logN+C'_t. Suppose A k=N*1 and let delta=E k-2N*1. Combining(3),(6) gives the finite-N Gaussian majorant w_N(k)<=C N^C_t exp[ N Vol(M)/pi+eta dot(delta)/pi -c_*||k-Nx*||²/(pi*N)]. (7) All original zero-angle weights are retained. In particular, for ANY set of such configurations with ||delta||_infty<=R_N, sum w_N(k)<=C N^C_t exp[N Vol(M)/pi+||eta||_1 R_N/pi]. (8) The number of configurations is at most N^(3t) and has been absorbed in the fixed polynomial. Thus O(1) edge defects cost only a polynomial factor; R_N=o(N) preserves the sharp geometric upper exponent. Exact full2N edge charge is sufficient but is NOT necessary for this positive-energy estimate. Here delta is the TRUE INTEGER difference E k-2N, not a distance between residues modulo2N. A bounded change of a residue need not give a bounded integer defect: for example the affine residue 2d changes to0 after adding only2, and0 permits zero or multiple edge windings. Thus robustness under bounded integer defects does not justify replacing the actual compatible quantum edge character by a nearby one. The source still has to supply the stated lift or an independent bound on its true supported defects. If ||k/N-x*||>=epsilon, the same sum has the extra factor exp[-N c_*epsilon²/pi]. More quantitatively a radius squared larger than a fixed multiple of(R_N+logN)/N controls the Gaussian tail relative to the complete geometric exponential rate. This is a consequence of the support-plane certificate, not a phase selection or an assertion about the original quantum cycle. The useful condition is even weaker than small defects in every edge: equation(7) controls any supported defect set for which sup eta dot(delta)=o(N), with the Gaussian deficit still retained. ## 4. Affine charge d=N-1 and further bounded local offsets For the source-compatible tetrahedral charge A k=d*1, set y=k/d and delta_d=E k-2d*1. Then Ay=1 and Ey-2=delta_d/d. Equation(3) applies exactly to y. The arguments k_i/N and k_i/d differ by at most1/N. Integrating the two logarithmic endpoint singularities of Lambda gives the uniform modulus |Lambda(u)-Lambda(v)| <=C |u-v|(1+|log|u-v||). It contributes only O(logN) to the logarithm of the weight. Therefore the affine version of(7) is w_N(k)<=C N^C_t exp[ N Vol(M)/pi+(N/(pi*d)) eta dot(delta_d) -(c_*N/(pi*d²))||k-dx*||²]. (9) Bounded or sublinear edge defects have the same conclusions as in(8), since N/d<=2 for N>=2. This retains flat tetrahedra and does not rely on endpoint vanishing. More generally let the local sums be N+u_j, |u_j|<=U_N<N/2, and normalize each tetrahedral triple by its own local sum. The normalized edge defects differ from delta/N by O(U_N/N), with constants determined by the fixed incidence matrix. The factorial action changes by at most C_t U_N[1+log(N/max(1,U_N))]. (10) Hence bounded local AND edge charge offsets still cost only a polynomial, and sublinear offsets still cost exp(o(N)). The Gaussian deficit in the normalized local angles remains valid. This extension requires the specified nonnegative angle support; it does not extend a factorial through a forbidden index N. On a common allowed nonempty progression, the strict geometric partition satisfies Z_N(T)>=N^(-C)exp[N Vol(M)/pi] by rounding the complete strict point in its integer kernel. Consequently the bounded-defect positive energies above are at most a fixed polynomial times Z_N(T); the sublinear-defect energies are at most exp(o(N))Z_N(T). ### 4.1 A bounded-defect comparison exists at EVERY level There is no lattice-progression obstruction for a sufficiently wide FIXED integer defect window. Put B=2 max_e sum_i E_(e,i), determined solely by the fixed edge incidence matrix, and define Z_N^B=sum_{k>=0, A k=d*1, ||E k-2d*1||_infty<=B} w_N(k). Then this sum is nonempty for every N>=2, and fixed constants give C^-1 N^-C exp[N Vol(M)/pi] <= Z_N^B <= C N^C exp[N Vol(M)/pi]. (10a) For nonemptiness, in each complete tetrahedral triple set k_1=floor(d x*_1), k_2=floor(d x*_2), k_3=d-k_1-k_2. All entries lie in[0,d]. Their errors relative to d x* lie in (-1,0] for the first two and [0,2) for the third. Hence every edge defect has absolute value at most B. This constructs an admissible state at each N, without a rationality assumption on x*. For large N it is strictly positive and k/N=x*+O(1/N). Smoothness of the coordinate Lobachevsky sum near x* and (6) give a single weight exp[N Vol(M)/pi+O(logN)], proving the lower bound. The upper bound is (9) summed with the fixed defect bound B. Increasing C handles the finitely many remaining levels. Thus this bounded-defect positive model has the desired energy rate at all levels, independently of any exact-fiber progression. It may be used as an upper comparison target. Its polynomial two-sided estimate still proves nothing about K_N until an exact original-source comparison is established; neither nonemptiness nor rounding constructs that comparison or enforces the true edge lift. ## 5. The exact affine local weight is not its amplitude square root There is a particularly direct connection to the original charged star. If a+b+c=d, root reflection gives w_N(a,b,c)=1/[s_N(a)s_N(b)s_N(c)] =|[a+b choose a]_Q|/N. (11) The exact ORIGINAL source-preserving balanced star--triangle identity in [the general fusion theorem](actual_general_flow_fusion.md) has scalar modulus |[a+b choose a]_Q|, with its full phase and typed outer factors retained. It is the FULL binomial, namely N w_N, not the normalized energy amplitude sqrt(w_N). For example at a=b=c=d/3, N=1 modulo3, the scalar divided by sqrt(w_N) has modulus sqrt(N*|[a+b choose a]_Q|), log of this ratio=N v_3/(2pi)+O(logN). (12) Here v_3=3Lambda(pi/3) is the regular ideal tetrahedron volume. Thus a uniform local one-tetrahedron comparison which simply replaces this scalar by sqrt(w_N) pays an exponential cost. Two-tetrahedron assignments, a genuinely different doubled contraction, or the exact exponentially varying internal gauges could compensate it. Their compensation at the ORIGINAL full source has to be proved; it cannot be inferred from the factorial identity(11) or absorbed into an unknown knot normalization. This warning does not disprove the requested upper comparison. It keeps its amplitude/energy and source normalizations explicit. The subsequent [exact length-frame calculation](actual_length_normalized_star_gram.md) now supplies a constructive compensation: b_L=N^(1/4)B_L/sqrt(s_L) makes a balanced star scalar N^(-1/2) times its retained phase, and parallel fusion produces a polynomial times sqrt(w_N). The [original singleton clock co-source](actual_length_gauge_clock_source.md) also has polynomial norm in that frame. Thus the flat-frame ratio in (12) is not an obstruction to a properly transported metric. The compulsory dual anchor weights and the coherent global state norm remain; [every diagonal clock metric fails the sharp budget in an actual complete figure-eight sector](actual_figure_eight_clock_gram_obstruction.md).
