The gauge can carry a zero or pole on that divisor. The source, cut functional, and full ADO sign line must be transported in their specified lattices. A rational generic comparison fixes neither an arbitrary root-central scalar nor the nonzero coefficient of the selected regulator period. Those require the original pointing. This theorem is a new sufficient descent tool for that comparison problem, not the volume theorem. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_q_parameter_curvature.py). [Results](../experiments/q_parameter_curvature_results.json).

title: Quantitative descent of the actual phase up to its boundary currents
text: # Quantitative descent of the actual phase up to its boundary currents 28 October 2026. Saturation gives more than a bound at exact critical points: on a slowly expanding regular window it gives a polynomial lower bound for the gradient everywhere above the volume level. Normalized gradient descent consequently costs only exp(o(N)) in that window. The full quantum dilogarithm has a uniform symbol estimate on the same slowly shrinking angular strips. This is a quantitative REGULAR-REGION statement for the actual full phase, at arbitrary fixed word width. It does not remove the original relative boundary currents. Descent can reach a shape/coordinate boundary, a logarithmic chart seam, or a quantum-pole exclusion before reaching the volume sublevel. Such exit currents must be retained. A claim of the full sharp knot bound still requires their estimate or exact cancellation. ## 1. The fixed phase and its algebraic critical equations Use the full logarithmic coordinates of [the marked critical-action calculation](actual_wall_critical_regulator.md), including every Gaussian and cap coordinate. On a recorded local sheet, W(Z)=sum_a epsilon_a Li_2(A_a(Z)) +Z^t C Z/2+i kappa^t Z+c, A_a(Z)=sigma_a exp(v_a^t Z), phi=Im W, R=sum_a epsilon_a D(A_a), rho=Re Z. The actual signed monomial vectors v_a and quadratic form C have the integral/rational structure specified there; any required fixed algebraic coordinate cover is retained. Branches and their integer logarithmic marks are matched. In particular c has real imaginary-free normalization, and the exact off-critical identity is phi-R=rho^t Im(partial W). (1) Write x_i=exp Z_i. In these actual coordinates the exponentiated full critical equations are rational functions of the torus coordinates on the fixed cover: H_i(x)=exp(partial_i W), H_i(x)=1. (2) One can instead use a fixed nonsingular linear combination of the derivatives if a coordinate cover requires it; all norm comparisons then have fixed constants. It is necessary to use the ORIGINAL exponentiated equations, not powers that introduce additional solution components. Integer changes of the recorded flattening do not change (2). Clear denominators to obtain f_i(x). Let D(x) contain the torus coordinate factors, all cleared denominators, all singular graph factors, and the shape exclusions. The regular critical locus is the zero locus of the f_i in D!=0. Its JOINT shape-image closure Y in (P^1)^s is the saturated closure of [the critical compactification](saturated_critical_regulator_compactification.md). The already proved input is |R|<=V on Y, V=Vol(S^3 minus K). (3) This is a statement about the actual full equations. Replacing them by an anchor-only, constrained endpoint, or unsaturated cleared system is not permitted in the following argument. ## 2. A finite saturation certificate separates high regulator values Take finitely many multihomogeneous equations G_l for Y in the product of projective lines. For their affine pullbacks g_l(x)=G_l(A(x),1), the localized radical ideal condition gives finite certificates D^(k_l) g_l^(s_l)=sum_i h_(li)(x) f_i(x), (4) after clearing any additional fixed rational denominators. Here k_l>=0 and s_l>=1 are fixed integers, and h_(li) are fixed polynomials. The power s_l cannot in general be omitted: the original critical ideal need not be radical. Formula (4) is an ordinary ideal-membership certificate. Its existence follows by taking the radical in the localized coordinate ring; it can also be produced and checked by polynomial arithmetic for a specified word. Normalize every G_l on unit homogeneous representatives, so |G_l|_norm is a continuous function on the compact product (P^1)^s. For any fixed eta>0 the compact set B_eta={shape tuples: R>=V+eta} is disjoint from Y. Therefore either B_eta is empty, or max_l |G_l|_norm >= mu_eta>0 on B_eta. (5) This uses compactness and the defining equations only, not an effective Lojasiewicz exponent or an assumption of isolated critical points. At finite shapes the affine value |G_l(A,1)| is at least its normalized value: the removed homogeneous normalization factor is a product of positive powers of sqrt(1+|A_a|^2), each at least one. ## 3. Polynomial gradient lower bound on a mild regular window Fix a finite analytic chart with its recorded logarithmic branches. For L>=2 let Omega_L impose |x_i|, |x_i|^(-1)<=L, |d_a(x)|^(-1)<=L for each individual excluded polynomial factor d_a of D. Further fixed chart restrictions, including selected-strip or quantum-pole exclusions, may be imposed. The upper bounds on all fixed polynomials on Omega_L are powers of L. Also |rho|<=sqrt(dim Z) log L. There are constants c_eta>0 and B<infinity, depending on the fixed word, chart and eta but not L, such that phi>=V+eta, Z in Omega_L ==> ||partial W(Z)||>=c_eta L^(-B). (6) Proof. If ||partial W||>=eta/(2 sqrt(dim Z) log L), this already implies (6), after increasing B and decreasing c_eta. Otherwise (1) gives R>=V+eta/2, so (5) supplies a g_l of modulus at least mu_(eta/2). For ||partial W||<=1, |exp(partial_i W)-1|<=e|partial_i W|. Clearing its denominator thus gives |f_i(x)|<=C L^a ||partial W||. The certificate (4), the denominator lower bounds and polynomial upper bounds give mu_(eta/2)^(s_l)<=C L^b ||partial W||. There are only finitely many certificates, so their largest exponent and smallest positive constant give (6). The case ||partial W||>1 is immediate. If B_(eta/2) is empty, the first alternative is the only one. This proves the claim uniformly even near nonisolated critical components and their genuine saturated degenerations. The same window gives a polynomial Hessian bound. Locally, partial^2 W=C+sum_a epsilon_a v_a v_a^t A_a/(1-A_a), ||partial^2 W||<=C L^a. (7) Higher fixed derivatives have the same type of bound. These bounds do not depend on the choice of an integer logarithmic mark, which changes only the linear part of W. Taking L=N^epsilon in (6)--(7) proves a quantitative exclusion of high-action approximate critical points in this window. The point is the exponent B*epsilon, which can be made smaller than any fixed positive number by choosing epsilon sufficiently small. This is stronger than merely excluding a convergent high-action critical sequence on a fixed compact set. ## 4. Subexponential cost of regular descent Regard the logarithmic chart as a real Euclidean domain. Holomorphy gives ||grad phi||=||partial W||. On phi>=V+eta use the vector field X=-grad phi/||grad phi||^2. (8) Then d phi(X)=-1 exactly. Equations (6)--(7) imply, for another fixed B, ||X||+||DX||<=C_eta L^B. (9) Extend it smoothly in a slightly larger regular chart as needed, with a cutoff which is one on the region being used; before a chart exit this does not change the flow. A cutoff over an inverse-power collar still has derivative bounded by a fixed power of L. Suppose the initial chain has mass exp(o(N)) and initial action at most O(log^2 N), as holds for bounded branches and logarithmic radii O(log N). Up to its first exit or its arrival at phi=V+eta, the available flow time is T_N=O(log^2 N). The usual variational equation, d(D F_t)/dt=DX(F_t) D F_t, and direct integration of its norm imply ||D F_t||<=exp(C_eta L^B T_N). (10) For L=N^epsilon, choose epsilon>0 so that B*epsilon<1. Every fixed dimensional fixed-time flow image, and the entire time-parametrized sweep before exit, then have mass exp(o(N)). The sweep gains only the additional factor T_N(1+sup||X||). No polynomial bound on this mass is needed for the exponential-rate problem. At the TARGET ACTION level the hitting-time map is also controlled: the time is exactly phi(Z)-V-eta, whose derivative has a polynomial bound in the recorded window. An arbitrary excluded-factor boundary is different. Its first-hit time can have an unbounded derivative at a grazing contact. Formula (10) must not be asserted for that first-hit map without an additional argument. A regular collar level chosen by coarea on the sweep controls the exit current; all such currents and any original chain boundary must remain in the period identity. More precisely, the [independent coarea construction](quantitative_regular_phase_descent_coarea_audit.md) uses H(u,z)=F_(u tau(z))(z), where tau=(phi(z)-V-eta)_+, and the running maximum m(u,z)=max_(v<=u) rho(H(v,z)) of a Lipschitz nested-window exhaustion. Coarea on the PARAMETER cylinder selects a legal level r in (1,2) such that its entire slice, pushed forward with multiplicity, has mass exp(o(N)). If the initial chain and its boundary have that mass bound, the exact period identity is integral_C omega = integral_C_low omega +integral_E_r omega-integral_B_r omega. (10a) Here B_r is the original-boundary sweep and E_r is the COMPLETE exit-associated slice. The latter can contain grazing curtains which have returned to the interior after touching the collar. It must not be relabeled as a current supported entirely on the collar hypersurface. All three currents have controlled mass; only C_low has the proved low-action support. The running maximum handles re-entry without a first-hit-time derivative or discarded curtain. Thus this statement bounds interior transport and its action-level endpoint. It is not a license to omit a boundary current or to cross an actual quantum pole. The latter is an excluded exit even if the classical shape is algebraically regular there. ## 5. The full quantum symbol on shrinking strips The defining-integral proof in [the literature-state audit](literature_state_volume.md#21-a-uniform-complex-remainder-on-an-entire-horizontal-strip) can be made quantitative in the strip width. For 0<b<=1 and |Im z|<=pi-delta, 0<delta<=1, log Phi_b(z/(2 pi b)) =Li_2(-exp z)/(2 pi i b^2)+R_b(z), |R_b(z)|<=C b^2 (delta^(-1)+log(2/delta)). (11) The constant is independent of Re z. Here are the bounds in that integral argument. With c=-b^2/24 and K_b(t)=[1/sinh(b^2 t)-1/(b^2 t)]/(4t sinh t), H_b(t)=K_b(t)-c exp(-t)/t, one has |H_b(t)|<=C b^2 for 0<t<=1 and |H_b(t)|<=C b^2 exp(-t) for t>=1. Consequently its weighted L1 norm with weight exp((1-delta/pi)t) is at most C b^2/delta. The remaining explicit arctan(z/pi) is bounded by C log(2/delta) on this strip, uniformly in Re z. Inserting these in the exact remainder integral proves (11). For the ACTUAL full function Psi_epsilon, substitute b^2=1/N and its recorded half-step shift. Taylor's formula uses |exp z/(1-exp z)|<=C/delta on the smaller angular strip. Hence, for 2pi/N<=delta<=1 and delta<=epsilon Im z<=2pi-delta, log Psi_epsilon(z) =Li_2(exp z)/(epsilon*2pi*i/N) +(1/2)Log(1-exp z)+O(1/(N delta)). (12) All logarithms are the same selected-strip continuations as in the exact definition. For the derivative estimate use a disk of radius delta/4. At the threshold delta=2pi/N one must return to (11), rather than reapply (12) with an inadmissibly smaller delta: throughout that disk the shifted Phi argument has strip margin at least 3delta/4-pi/N>=delta/4. Its remainder and the half-step Taylor remainder are therefore still O(1/(N delta)) throughout the disk. Cauchy's formula gives, for every fixed k, |partial_z^k remainder|<=C_k/(N delta^(k+1)). (13) In particular delta=N^(-epsilon), with epsilon small, is allowed. A fixed product of these full functions, original monomial factors, Gaussian factors and rational source amplitudes has the actual W as its leading phase with subexponential amplitude on this window. This last assertion applies only where its rational denominators and selected logarithmic strips are retained. It does not analytically continue a finite cyclic atom across a Stokes boundary, and does not drop the full-function moment ray corrections. ## 6. Consequence and exact remaining task The final LOW-ACTION CHAIN obtained from an original scalar cycle by the controlled transport above, with the stated initial mass bound, has contribution bounded by exp(N(V+eta)/(2pi)+o(N)). (14) This follows from (10), (12) and the triangle inequality on that final chain. The exact Stokes identity expresses the original initial period as its low-action contribution PLUS the retained exit-associated and original-boundary sweep contributions. Even if every interior point of an initial chain reaches the target level, its own boundary sweep cannot be omitted. Estimate (14) by itself is not an estimate for that initial chain's complete period. It requires no assertion that the selected geometric saddle has nonzero coefficient, and is uniform over all fixed knot words to which the actual phase construction applies. The original period itself also contains the exit/boundary currents created or retained in that transport. Equation (14) becomes the desired whole-source bound ONLY after those currents have been controlled at the same rate. The entire all-transfer-endpoint corner has a separate subexponential estimate in [the total-transfer packet theorem](actual_total_transfer_endpoint_packets.md). Mixed endpoint/bulk currents, simultaneous coordinate/shape exits, and source seams are not thereby estimated. They remain the concrete obstruction, rather than an unquantified cost of regular interior gradient descent. The shrinking-strip calculation, including both signs and the exact half-step normalization, has a separate [independent integral audit](shrinking_strip_full_psi_independent_audit.md). It corrected the displayed Hessian sign and supplied the derivative argument at the smallest permitted strip width; both are incorporated above. No computational sample is used to prove (6), (10) or (12).

title: A coarea audit of regular phase descent
text: # A coarea audit of regular phase descent 28 October 2026. This proves the boundary-mass assertion needed in Section 4 of [quantitative regular phase descent](quantitative_regular_phase_descent.md). It does not estimate the exponential size of the boundary periods. In particular, the boundary current below includes grazing curtains; its support need not be contained in a single physical collar hypersurface. ## 1. Precise transport statement Let C be a compact oriented piecewise smooth p-chain, with integer multiplicities, in a recorded logarithmic chart. The same argument applies to compact integral currents. Both M(C) and M(partial C) are assumed to be exp(o(N)). Let phi be the actual phase and a its target value. Suppose C lies in {rho<1}, where rho is a Lipschitz exhaustion and {rho<=2} is contained in a legal regular chart. All actual quantum poles and all chart seams which cannot be crossed are excluded from this chart. On {rho<=2, phi>=a}, let X satisfy d phi(X)=-1. Extend X to a globally defined smooth bounded vector field in a slightly larger real chart. The extension is only a device for defining a complete flow Phi_t; it must agree with X on the displayed region. Suppose, for the available time T_N, that sup |X| <= B_N, sup |DX| <= K_N, T_N=O(log^2 N), K_N T_N=o(N), and that B_N, Lip(rho), and the first derivatives of phi on the initial chain are exp(o(N)). In the application these are fixed powers of L=N^epsilon, with epsilon sufficiently small. Define tau(z)=max(phi(z)-a,0), 0<=tau<=T_N, H(u,z)=Phi_(u tau(z))(z), 0<=u<=1, m(u,z)=max_(0<=v<=u) rho(H(v,z)). (1) There is a level r in (1,2) for which the following currents are defined, have mass exp(o(N)), and satisfy partial T_r = C_low,r - C - B_r + E_r. (2) Here T_r is the transported truncated cylinder, C_low,r is supported in {phi<=a}, B_r is the transported side coming from the ORIGINAL boundary partial C, and E_r is the complete exit-associated current. The image of every term on the right lies in the legal closed window {rho<=r}. Thus a closed p-form omega on that window obeys the exact identity integral_C omega = integral_(C_low,r) omega + integral_(E_r) omega - integral_(B_r) omega. (3) The orientation of B_r is specified below. When C is closed it is absent. Formula (3) retains all relative boundary data; it is not a bound on the last two integrals by their mass alone. ## 2. Running maxima and quantitative slicing Orient S=[0,1] x C with du first. Then partial S = {1} x C - {0} x C - [0,1] x partial C. The variational equation and differentiation of u tau(z) give a local Lipschitz bound |DH| <= Lambda_N, Lambda_N <= const exp(K_N T_N) (1+B_N(T_N+Lip(tau))). (4) All fixed powers of Lambda_N are exp(o(N)). The positive-part definition of tau is Lipschitz and causes no difficulty. Bounds can equivalently be read in local parametrizations and integrated with their multiplicities. The running maximum in (1) is also Lipschitz. Indeed, write it as m(u,z)=max_(0<=v<=1) rho(H(vu,z)). Every function in this maximum has the same local Lipschitz bound, at most const Lip(rho) Lambda_N. The supremum inherits that bound. This argument does not differentiate a maximizing time or a first-hit time. Let Q_N be this bound. Coarea on the PARAMETER cylinder gives integral_1^2 M(<S,m,r>) dr <= Q_N M(S). (5) For almost every r, restriction to {m<r} is a finite-perimeter current and its boundary is partial(S restricted to {m<r}) = (partial S) restricted to {m<r} + <S,m,r>. (6) One may choose a common such r with M(<S,m,r>) <= 2 Q_N M(S). (7) The harmless factor 2 leaves a positive-measure choice of levels; the almost-everywhere current identities can therefore be imposed at the same time. A finite collection of chains or charts is handled by applying coarea to the sum of their unsigned slicing masses. Define T_r = H_#(S restricted to {m<r}), E_r = H_#<S,m,r>, C_low,r = H(1,.)_#(C restricted to {m(1,.)<r}), B_r = H_#(([0,1] x partial C) restricted to {m<r}). The u=0 face is all of C because rho(C)<1. Equations (6) and the product orientation give (2), including its minus sign on B_r. Pushforward commutes with boundary. In particular, (2) includes the boundary of the retained subset of the u=1 face; it is not permissible to discard it separately. For m(1,z)<r the entire trajectory up to tau(z) remains in the region where the extension is the actual normalized descent. Consequently its endpoint has phase a if phi(z)>a, and is unchanged with phase at most a otherwise. This proves the stated support of C_low,r. Monotonicity of m in u makes {m<r} an initial time interval in each fibre. There is no re-entry ambiguity, even if the physical trajectory later re-enters the window in the extended flow. Finally, mass pushforward and (7) give M(T_r) <= Lambda_N^(p+1) M(S), M(E_r) <= 2 Lambda_N^p Q_N M(S), M(C_low,r) <= Lambda_N^p M(C), M(B_r) <= Lambda_N^p M(partial C). (8) These are bounds on parametrized currents WITH their multiplicities. No inference from the size of an image set or from cancellation of its parametrization is used. All quantities in (8) are exp(o(N)). Stokes applied to the legal image of T_r proves (3). ## 3. Why the exit current includes curtains It is in general false that E_r is supported on {rho=r}. A local model is rho(H(t,z))=z-(t-t_0)^2. For t>=t_0 its running maximum is z. At z=r, the parameter slice {m=r} therefore includes the whole interval t>=t_0, although the physical value of rho is strictly less than r after t_0. These portions are grazing curtains in the boundary of the first-exit truncated cylinder. Coarea bounds their mass together with all other slice pieces. This distinction is essential. The construction proves controlled regular transport into a low-action chain PLUS an exit-associated current. It does not prove that this latter current has low action, or that its contribution is determined by data on one collar hypersurface. An additional estimate or an exact source cancellation is still required for a sharp full-period upper bound. ## 4. Audit verdict The saturation certificate and normalized-gradient estimates in Sections 2--4 of the root note support the interior transport assertion. Equations (1)--(8) supply the missing coarea argument without a first-hit derivative bound. They require a legal collar with the recorded derivative bounds, and retention of the complete exit-associated and original-boundary currents. No new general upper or lower volume bound follows from this boundary-mass result alone.

title: The actual quantum source at every bridge
text: # The actual quantum source at every bridge Research note, 27 October 2026. This continues the [arbitrary-bridge classical contraction](arbitrary_bridge_source_reduction.md) using the original finite quantum matrices. It computes all four balanced turns, a literal marked closure, their cyclic boundary sources and a flat completion under the actual meridian half-step. All formulas hold for arbitrary N and arbitrary bridge count. The completion needs two bulk channels: a single cap's bulk norm changes sign under the half-step. Keeping only the squared step would miss this. The explicit three-dimensional system below keeps that sign and the boundary source, including at the Kashaev color. This is finite quantum boundary transport. The selected knot period's comparison with the geometric regulator remains unproved. ## 1. The original caps lose their factorials exactly Fix q=exp(pi i/N), Q=q^2, N>=2 and x=-M/q. Write F_a=(Q;Q)_a and w_a=v_a/F_a, both on V(x) and its standard dual color V(x^(-1)Q^(-1)). No unrolled weight lift is changed. The existing actual turn matrices have c_a=(-x)^a Q^(a(a+1)/2), g_b=x^(1-N) Q^(-b). (1.1) For 0<=a<N, cancellation in the full product F_(N-1)=N gives F_a F_(N-1-a)=N (-1)^a Q^(a(a+1)/2). (1.2) Indeed F_(N-1)/F_(N-1-a)=product_(r=1)^a(1-Q^(-r)) =(-1)^a Q^(-a(a+1)/2)F_a. Thus the actual balanced left cap and cup are simply ev_L(w_a^dual tensor w_b) =x^a/N delta_(a+b,N-1), coev_L(1)=sum_a N x^(-a) w_(N-1-a) tensor w_a^dual. (1.3) The actual right cap and cup are ev_R(w_b tensor w_a^dual) =x^a g_b/N delta_(a+b,N-1), coev_R(1)=sum_a N x^(-a)g_(N-1-a)^(-1) w_a^dual tensor w_(N-1-a). (1.4) On their support the right-cap coefficient is (Q x^(1-N)/N)(Qx)^a. (1.5) The coefficients (1.3)--(1.4) are whole identities in the original finite matrices. The unbalanced J_x, its exact double dual g and all four snake identities were independently proved in [the pivotal duality note](relative_pivotal_duality.md). Equations (1.2)--(1.5) do not change their normalization. In particular, every cup contributes exactly N and every cap 1/N, in addition to the displayed monomials and pivots. ## 2. A marked nilpotent defect gives the reduced closure In this same balanced basis the actual cut source and co-source are psi_a=1, phi_a=1/N, e=psi phi, e^2=e, Tr(e)=1. If the cut operator is C=F_N(M) I, the original reduced evaluation is Tr(e C)=F_N(M). A fully closed ordinary pivotal network instead has Tr(g C)=0. To implement the original selected cut as a marked closed network, insert the specified operator D=g^(-1)e, D_(a,b)=x^(N-1)Q^a/N. (2.1) Then, for every matrix C, not just scalar ones, Tr(g D C)=Tr(e C). (2.2) Moreover rank D=1, D^2=0, Tr(gD)=1, D g D=D. (2.3) The nilpotence follows from sum_a Q^a=0. This defect is completely fixed by the original pivot and boundary projector. It is not an ordinary Hopf-intertwining local coupon, and its transport through a crossing must carry the actual operator, not replace it by the same local matrix on another strand. The marked right cap is particularly simple. Insert D on its primal input. Its array, with primal index b and dual index a, is ev_R^D(w_b tensor w_a^dual)=x^a/N^2, (2.4) with no diagonal-support constraint. Directly, the only summand in ev_R(D w_b tensor w_a^dual) has c=N-1-a, and g_c D_(c,b)=1/N. Contracting (2.4) with coev_L in (1.3) gives the unknot value one, whereas the unmarked cap gives Tr g=0. Consequently any k-bridge plat can express the original reduced knot evaluation with k cups, k-1 ordinary caps and one marked cap. The exact scalar from these turns is N^k (1/N)^(k-1) (1/N^2)=1/N. (2.5) All monomials, dual colors, crossing matrices and zero-framing corrections are still present. Formula (2.5) explains the same cut average 1/N for arbitrary k. It does not divide a zero quantum dimension or introduce one modified trace for each bridge. If the unreduced ADO evaluation is used, its whole d_N(M) remains the same separate factor. ## 3. A bridge has an explicit cyclic boundary source On a cap's support use a as the independent index; b=N-1-a. Let T f(a)=f(a+1 mod N) and let e_partial be the delta function at a=N-1. Each of (1.3)--(1.5), and the corresponding cup, has the form v_a=kappa lambda^a, (3.1) with kappa a specified nonzero monomial times N or 1/N and lambda a specified Q-power times x or x^(-1). There are exact identities (T-lambda)v=kappa(1-lambda^N)e_partial, v=kappa sum_(j=0)^(N-1)lambda^(N-1-j)T^j e_partial. (3.2) The second identity follows by inspecting its a-th coefficient. Equivalently (T-lambda)sum lambda^(N-1-j)T^j=1-lambda^N. There is no division by 1-lambda^N. The vector remains nonzero and has prescribed anchor v_0=kappa on that divisor as well. For a left cap lambda=x. At x=-M/q its source factor is 1-x^N=1+(-1)^N M^N. (3.3) At M=1 this is 2 at even N and 0 at odd N. Those values do not allow its whole meridian function to be discarded. In the odd case (3.1) becomes a pointed homogeneous eigenvector; it does not become the zero vector. The inverse-lambda cups retain their corresponding 1-x^(-N) factors. For disjoint bridges all T_i commute. Applying any subset of the operators T_i-lambda_i to their tensor source gives exactly the product of the displayed boundary factors and the corresponding corner deltas, with all other bridge factors unchanged. This is the entire cubical family of boundary intersections, not only the single-corner terms. For the marked cap (2.4), the primal index b is free. Its shift in b has multiplier one, and the dual-index shift has (T_a-x)ev_R^D=(1-x^N)delta_(a,N-1) tensor 1_b/N^2. (3.4) Thus its removal of the ordinary cap relation is part of the actual selected source. It cannot be replaced by an unmarked inverse-meridian cap when comparing period complexes. ### The principal cap equations are the inverse-meridian equations This paragraph concerns the q->1 principal symbol, not a fixed root's center. Let U be the primal position and V the dual position. The support in (1.3) gives UV=1 at the symbol. Write p_P,p_D for their balanced momenta. The cup coefficient x^(-a) gives p_D/p_P=x^(-1). A cap is a co-source, so its phase has the opposite momentum sign; the leading x^a factor gives the same relation. The right pivotal monomials and their base-only meridian phases are still retained, as in the existing actual action calculation. This has a direct matrix verification. For one balanced meridian use K=x/U, e=(1-x^2/U)p_P/x, f=(1-U)/p_P, b_+=[K e;0 1], b_-=[1 0;-Kf K]. (3.5) For its dual use x_D=x^(-1), position V and momentum p_D. Substituting V=U^(-1),p_D=p_P/x gives exactly b_(+,D)b_(+,P)=I, b_(-,D)b_(-,P)=I. (3.6) Indeed K_D=K^(-1),e_D=-K^(-1)e,f_D=-Kf. Under the already proved prefix transformation H_j=B_(-,j-1)^(-1)G_j B_(-,j-1), equation (3.6) is precisely the inverse-meridian cap in the arbitrary-plat representation scheme. This checks the cap from the actual quantum coefficients, rather than assigning a classical inverse relation independently. The marked cap (2.4) instead imposes p_P=1,p_D=x^(-1), with no position constraint of its own. At every bottom cup both total Borel products are I. Each crossing preserves them. All ordinary top caps also have product I. Therefore the two products at the remaining marked pair must be I; on the regular chart this restores V=U^(-1). The extra marked equation p_P=1 is exactly the fixed inverse-eigenflag: direct substitution gives G_P(1,1)^t=x^(-1)(1,1)^t. (3.7) Conversely (3.7) forces p_P=1 when its stated shape factors are units. It follows that the regular principal critical scheme of the actual pointed plat is the knot representation scheme with this selected peripheral flag fixed to 1. The inverse maps are the same rational prefix/Gauss maps already proved for crossings. The identities hold over Artin rings on that chart, since every inverse used is a unit there. The retained meridian is M=-x at the symbol, so the selected actual eigenvalue is M^(-1), consistent with the original cut convention. Thus every bridge's quantum turn, boundary source and principal holonomy constraint now come from the same finite matrices. This does not perform the remaining selected global period pairing. ## 4. The actual meridian half-step forces a second bulk channel Put A=Q^a and let delta x=qx, delta A=A. This is the actual M->qM step, not its square. First normalize kappa=1 and lambda=x. The internal bulk monodromy of T-lambda is X=x^N. The half-step sends X to -X. Therefore an invertible commuting meridian transport cannot preserve a two-dimensional affine system whose internal monodromy has only eigenvalues X and 1: its characteristic polynomial would have to be both (z-X)(z-1) and (z+X)(z-1). This fails over the generic coefficient field. There is an explicit minimal three-dimensional completion. Put v_0(a,x)=x^a, v_1(a,x)=(qx)^a, w=(v_0,v_1,1)^t, B_T=[x 0 (1-X)e_partial; 0 qx (1+X)e_partial; 0 0 1], B_delta=[0 1 0; A 0 0; 0 0 1]. (4.1) Then T w=B_T w, delta w=B_delta w, T(B_delta) B_T=delta(B_T) B_delta. (4.2) For the last identity use T(A)=QA and QA e_partial=e_partial. The first bulk channel goes to the second, and delta v_1=A v_0. The two boundary factors 1-X and 1+X are swapped. Both matrices are invertible for x!=0, even at X=1 or X=-1; their determinants are qx^2 and -A. The internal N-fold monodromy has eigenvalues X,-X,1. Hence three is the least possible generic rank for a flat completion retaining this bulk sector and its trivial source. The preceding spectral argument is a rank obstruction, not a choice of an extra physical state. The selected cap is still its specified first component v_0 with its anchor. There are two bulk channels because the meridian transports their central characters. For a turn with lambda=q^s x^epsilon, epsilon=+1 or -1, and kappa=c x^r (c fixed under delta), replace x,qx by lambda,q^epsilon lambda, replace A by A^epsilon, and multiply B_delta by q^r. The third selected component is then kappa, and the first two are kappa lambda^a and kappa(q^epsilon lambda)^a. The same direct calculation proves flatness. This covers the actual cups, caps and marked cap, with their full normalizations. No inverse of 1+X or 1-X occurs. ### The equivalent pointed norm-one frame The three-dimensional assertion keeps the unmodified bulk norm and its source as separate data. It is not a claim that a known cap vector intrinsically needs three components. There is also an explicit rank-one norm torsor which includes the last transition in its multiplier. On the supported orbit put h(A)=sum_(a=0)^(N-1) q^a e_a(A), h^2=A, T(h)=q h (1-2e_partial), a_T=lambda[1+(lambda^(-N)-1)e_partial], a_delta=q^r h^epsilon. (4.3) Every displayed multiplier is a unit when lambda!=0. The last internal multiplier is lambda^(1-N), so Norm_T(a_T)=1, T(v)=a_T v, delta(v)=a_delta v, T(a_delta) a_T=delta(a_T) a_delta. (4.4) To check the mixed square, use the ordinary q^epsilon factor off the cut and T(h)(N-1)=1 at the cut. Equations (4.3)--(4.4) also follow from a_T=T(v)/v and a_delta=delta(v)/v with the explicit anchored unit v=kappa lambda^a. Thus this cap's Hilbert-90 frame and full half-step transport are solved exactly, including at lambda^N=1. The boundary defect is recoverable as (a_T-lambda)v=kappa(1-lambda^N)e_partial. It is encoded in the retained cut multiplier, rather than discarded. For fixed q, h is a specified polynomial in A of degree <N; its two square-root choices are not interchangeable. Its cut sign is exactly what the two bulk channels in (4.1) record. The meridian transport has 2N-fold norm one, and the entire frame is fixed by v_0=kappa. This gives the explicit torsor description of every turn alongside its affine-source presentation. ## 5. All bridges share one half-step, rather than independent parity choices The construction has a uniform simultaneous version. For k bridges let lambda_i=q^(s_i)x^(epsilon_i), epsilon_i in {+1,-1}, A_i=Q^(a_i), X_i=lambda_i^N and kappa=c x^r the full retained monomial normalization. Use a component u_empty=kappa, and for each nonempty subset I of {1,...,k} use two components u_(I,b)=kappa product_(i in I) (q^(b epsilon_i)lambda_i)^(a_i), b=0,1. (5.1) There are 2^(k+1)-1 components, independent of N. The equations retain two synchronized half-step channels for each nonempty subset, sharing one empty-subset source. Set u_(empty,0)=u_(empty,1)=u_empty. Their internal equations are T_i u_(I,b)=u_(I,b), i notin I, T_i u_(I,b)=q^(b epsilon_i)lambda_i u_(I,b) +(1-(-1)^b X_i)e_(partial,i)u_(I\{i},b), i in I. (5.2) The full meridian step is delta u_empty=q^r u_empty, delta u_(I,0)=q^r u_(I,1), delta u_(I,1)=q^r product_(i in I)A_i^epsilon_i u_(I,0). (5.3) These are commuting flat transport matrices. For distinct internal directions, lowering subsets commutes and their coefficients depend only on their own clock. To check a mixed square with delta, use T_i(A_i)=QA_i and QA_i e_(partial,i)=e_(partial,i), just as in (4.2); after lowering I the remaining product is exactly that in (5.3) for I\{i}. The empty subset has the same retained scalar character q^r. This proves flatness for every k and N. The actual simultaneous bridge source is the component u_({1,...,k},0), with the known diagonal-support embeddings and, at the distinguished cap, its extra constant primal factor. Thus the source intersections and actual half-step transport have a finite explicit description for unbounded bridge number. The exponential dependence here is on k, not on the root level N. Their determinant line has no boundary denominator. With R_k=2^(k+1)-1 the explicit matrices give det B_(T_i)=(q^epsilon_i lambda_i^2)^(2^(k-1)), det B_delta=-q^(r R_k) product_i A_i^(epsilon_i 2^(k-1)). (5.4) The first identity counts the 2^(k-1) subsets containing i. For the second, each nonempty-subset block has determinant -product_(i in I)A_i^epsilon_i and every i occurs 2^(k-1) times. All are units. In fact B_delta^(2N)=I, and its determinant has meridian norm one. These statements retain the actual half-step characters, with no division by a factor that becomes 0 or 2 at completeness. ## 6. Exact propagation through the actual crossing word Let B_N(x) be any actual oriented braid operator in the plat, using the original R matrices and the literal turned matrices J_V^(-1)C^t J_W where appropriate. They are invertible; same-color formulas cannot be substituted on a dual-colored turn. For the cup vector U and any finite boundary equation L U=b, the transported equations and source are exactly (B_N L B_N^(-1))(B_N U)=B_N b. (6.1) For several source channels apply B_N to all components. If delta U=C_delta U, the meridian transport becomes delta(B_N U)=delta(B_N) C_delta B_N^(-1)(B_N U). (6.2) For an internal cyclic shift replace delta(B_N) by T_i B_N T_i^(-1). Consequently all commuting squares in Sections 4--5 survive; this is an identity in the finite matrix algebra, including the corner projectors. The co-source is transported by B_N^(-t). Its pairing with the source is unchanged. No central character, corner source, pivot or selected normalization is replaced by a scalar chosen after specialization. Equations (1.3)--(6.2), together with the marked cap, specify the original quantum boundary data for arbitrary k. They go beyond assigning unnamed b_s to the classical contraction. They do not yet prove that those full finite data descend to its geometric normal deformation complex, or that their selected scalar has the regulator's norm. ## 7. Boundary norms at completeness and the remaining volume problem At M=1 the balanced g is unitary, e is an orthogonal projector and D=g^(-1)e has operator norm one. The actual cups have norm N^(3/2), ordinary caps N^(-1/2), and the marked cap N^(-1). For a fixed k-bridge presentation their product has norm N^(k-1/2). (7.1) The zero-framing character has modulus one. In these specified balanced bases, Cauchy--Schwarz therefore gives |F_N(1)| <= N^(k-1/2) ||B_N(1)||. (7.2) The same control retains bounded meridian jets. Write u=Log M. Every coefficient in the tensor of all turns is a monomial in M; its total exponent has absolute value at most 2kN. Consequently, for each fixed j, its j-th u derivative has norm at most (2kN)^j N^(k-1/2). (7.3) This estimates the actual whole boundary germ, rather than only its value at M=1. The unchanged unreduced peripheral factor is d_N(e^u)=i^(N+3) sinh(u)/sinh(Nu). (7.4) The fixed-order Taylor coefficients of N i^(-N-3)d_N(e^u) are polynomials in N of degree at most their order. The j-th derivative of d_N at zero is therefore O_j(N^(j-1)); the odd derivatives vanish. Thus retaining that whole germ also preserves polynomial boundary-jet control. No factor 1+M^N or 1-M^N has been evaluated and canceled separately in deriving these bounds. If the zero-framing monomial is included with the boundary data, replace 2k in (7.3) by 2k+|w|, where w is the fixed diagram's writhe. Its value at completeness has modulus one. This is a uniform polynomial boundary bound. It does not give a lower bound on the selected matrix coefficient or rule out an exponentially small overlap. Any volume proof through the A-torsor must still control that coupling and compare the resulting pointed period with the calibrated geometric action. The nonzero boundary vectors, flat completion and fixed normalization proved here do not supply that remaining theorem by themselves. [Audit](../experiments/audit_quantum_bridge_cap_source.py). [Results](../experiments/quantum_bridge_cap_source_results.json).

title: Quantum-factorial frames and the cyclotomic source boundary
text: # Quantum-factorial frames and the cyclotomic source boundary Research proof, 27 October 2026. Moving the quantum parameter together with the integral color gives an actual finite representation on the whole path. A symmetric quantum-factorial frame makes its principal compact-source map a smooth sphere twist, with the correct clock. The singularity of a different natural polynomial frame is carried by an exact diagonal quantum-factorial gauge, whose norm has exponential size. Thus a singular source chart need not be an intrinsic obstruction. The retained inverse eigenflag has a different issue: two explicitly computed boundary bubbles remain even in the smooth frame. All these statements precede a quantum-geometric period comparison. In particular, this does not prove a selected hyperbolic contribution or volume growth. ## 1. Two actual frames on one integral-color path Put n=N-1 and, for 0<=lambda<=1, q=exp(pi*i lambda/N), Q=q^2, s=2pi*i lambda, m=q^N=exp(s/2), M=-m, rho=q-q^(-1). The actual common-Verma wall M Q^(-N)-M^(-1) is identically zero. Its N-dimensional head therefore is a genuine quotient, even when Q^N!=1. This assertion is about the module, not about pivotal cups or a generic ADO invariant. The other wall 1-Q^N remains present. Write [k]_q=(q^k-q^(-k))/rho, with its removable value k at q=1. For the standard q-spin highest-weight basis u_j with F_std u_j=u_(j+1), two frames are p_j=u_j/(n)_j, f_j=u_j/[n]_q^(fall,j), 0<=j<=n. Here (n)_j is the ordinary falling factorial. Thus p_j=R_j f_j, R_j=product_(k=N-j)^(N-1) [k]_q/k. (1) All factors are strictly positive on this real path, including their removable lambda=0 values. These changes of frame are exact and invertible at finite N, including the cyclotomic endpoint. Use the symmetric Gauss pair Ecal=rho E_std, F_G=rho F_std. In the f-frame, with J z^j=jz^j and D_q z^j=q^jz^j, they are Ecal=(D_q-D_q^(-1))/z, F_G=z(q^n D_q^(-1)-q^(-n)D_q), K=q^n D_q^(-2). (2) Their entries are rho[j]_q and rho[n-j]_q. The symmetric standard operators E_std,F_std have removable continuation at q=1. The literal common-Verma Hopf normalization is instead E_actual=Ecal/rho^2=rho^(-1)E_std, F_actual=F_G=rho F_std. This opposite Hopf scaling leaves E_actual tensor F_actual and the actual universal R unchanged. It must not be confused with identifying the individual ordinary and balanced generators. The finite Gauss pair and actual R extend regularly at q=1; the displayed Hopf rescaling itself need not. In the p-frame the same Gauss generators have entries Ecal p_j=rho [j]_q[N-j]_q/(N-j) p_(j-1), F_G p_j=rho(n-j)p_(j+1). The diagonal relation (1) conjugates these formulas exactly; it also conjugates every crossing, source and inserted matrix. A rank-one coupon psi phi becomes R^(-1)psi phi R. It must not be replaced by the original constant coupon after a frame change. The [global q-difference source theorem](integral_color_global_q_difference_source.md) gives its exact balanced frame and crossing comparison, including the normalization just specified. The exact comparison to the ordinary-falling head, including all such coupons and the pivotal adapter, is in [the actual coherent-symbol theorem](integral_color_coherent_symbols_and_uniform_poles.md), Section 6. That note also proves uniform C^l generator convergence on the whole compact sphere, including its poles. This is distinct from a full crossing-word asymptotic estimate. ## 2. The whole function in the frame torsor Set b_lambda(x)=sin(pi lambda x)/(pi lambda x), S_lambda(T)=integral_(1-T)^1 log b_lambda(x) dx. (3) Use b_0=1 and the positive real logarithm for lambda<1. At lambda=1 the endpoint logarithm is integrable. For T=j/N, uniformly for all 0<=lambda<=1 and 0<=j<N, (1/N)log R_j=S_lambda(j/N)+O((1+log N)/N). (4) Indeed [k]_q/k=b_lambda(k/N)/b_lambda(1/N). The denominator has logarithm O(N^(-2)), uniformly. For the numerator, write log b_lambda(x)=log(1-lambda x)+g(lambda x), g(y)=log[sin(pi y)/(pi y(1-y))]. The removable function g is C^1 on [0,1]. Its Riemann sums have uniform error O(N^(-1)). Monotonicity bounds the logarithmic part by its last grid value and its final-interval integral, each at most O((1+log N)/N). This proves (4), including both endpoints, without assuming a regular Taylor expansion at lambda=1. This is a dilogarithmic whole function. For s=2pi*i lambda put J_s(x)=2sinh(sx/2)/(sx)=b_lambda(x), B_s(x)=s x^2/4+Li_2(exp(-sx))/s-x Log(sx)+x. On the marked branch continuous from 0<lambda<1, dB_s/dx=Log J_s(x), S_lambda(T)=B_s(1)-B_s(1-T). (5) The endpoint x=0 is interpreted continuously. The logarithms in (5) are marked together, so its right side is real on this path. Equation (5) describes the scalar frame period before its quantum jets. It is not the knot's complete Bloch regulator. At lambda=1 the conditioning is already exponentially large. The elementary sine product gives exactly R_n=N/[(2sin(pi/N))^(N-1)(N-1)!], lim (1/N)log cond(R)=log(2pi)-1. (6) For this real path [k]_q/k<=1, so 1=R_0>=R_j>=R_n>0; cond(R)=1/R_n in the coordinate Euclidean metric or any common diagonal coherent metric. To prove the sine product, factor (z^N-1)/(z-1) at z=1 and take absolute values. Stirling's formula, or integral bounds for log((N-1)!), then gives (6). The same rate follows directly from S_1(1)=integral_0^1 log[sin(pi x)/(pi x)]dx=1-log(2pi). Consequently, an exact change of frame may move an exponential norm into its source or metric. Algebraic invertibility does not justify discarding that norm in the volume problem. ## 3. The symmetric frame has a smooth clock-preserving source map On the compact-source surface use coordinates (v,a), T=va and Omega=dv wedge da=dlog v wedge dT. Its real sphere has T=|v|^2/(1+|v|^2). At fixed lambda the coherent principal symbols of (2) are k=m exp(-sT), e=2sinh(sT/2)/v, f=2v sinh(s(1-T)/2). (7) They obey ef=m+m^(-1)-k-k^(-1). In particular H=[[k,e],[kf,m+m^(-1)-k]], det H=1. The m-eigenflag of H is z_+=(m-k)/e=exp(s(1-T)/2)v. (8) Both formulas continue at the poles. Thus the compact-source map to the eigenflag-marked Grothendieck family is the shear Psi_s(v,a)=(r v,a/r), r=exp(s(1-T)/2). It keeps T and the actual principal clock exp(sT) unchanged and obeys Psi_s^*Omega=Omega exactly. The local generator for the change of log v, using the primitive log v dT, is W_s(T)=s(T/2-T^2/4), W_s'(T)=Log r. (9) For imaginary s on the specified path |r|=1 on the real sphere. Hence Psi_s maps that sphere to itself, including lambda=1. It is a regular area-preserving sphere twist. This is a concrete principal clock-preserving map, stronger than the earlier exponential-current detour that changed the clock. The p-frame instead has e_p=J_s(1-T)e and f_p=f/J_s(1-T). Its source coordinates relate by v_f=v_p/J_s(1-T), T_f=T_p. (10) This is also symplectic wherever defined; its generator has derivative -Log J_s(1-T)=-S_lambda'(T). It explains the apparent p-frame flag factor s(1-T)/(1-exp[-s(1-T)]). Its pole at lambda=1,T=0 is carried by the genuine factorial frame torsor (1), rather than by a singularity of (8). The finite frame is invertible there; its nonuniform classical limit is quantified by (4)--(6). Source and metric changes remain essential. ### An exact finite quantization of the smooth shear There is an actual finite star automorphism behind (8), not merely a principal coordinate formula. On the polynomial frame set U_j=q^[Nj-j(j+1)/2]=m^j q^[-j(j+1)/2], U_0=1. (10a) All exponents are integers. This diagonal matrix is unitary for real lambda in any of the common diagonal coordinate/coherent metrics. It commutes with the entire finite clock Q^J, K, all index moments and both diagonal endpoint projectors. Conjugation gives the exact finite automorphism sigma_A -> sigma_(U A U^(-1)) of the already specified coherent star algebra. Its inverse, products, trace and all pointed word pairings are literal matrix identities, with the coupon and its dual conjugated as well. For the coordinate operators a_hat=J_-/n, b_hat=J_+/n, T_hat=J/n, where J_+ z^j=(n-j)z^(j+1), their exact symbols are sigma_(U a_hat U^(-1)) =m^(-1)q a [1+(q-1)T]^(n-1), sigma_(U b_hat U^(-1)) =m q^(-1)b [1+(q^(-1)-1)T]^(n-1), sigma_(U T_hat U^(-1))=T. (10b) The binomial derivative identity proves both first formulas. Uniformly on the compact sphere, they tend in every fixed derivative norm to a/r, r b, T. Thus this exact star automorphism quantizes precisely Psi_s. It is not the literal pullback by Psi_s on finite symbols; that pullback need not preserve their finite-dimensional space. Its whole diagonal phase is Log U_j=N W_s(j/N)-s j/(4N), (10c) with the marked logarithm from q=exp(s/(2N)). The subleading term is retained rather than replacing this phase by its leading quadratic generator. It also equals the actual balanced frame map at the roots. In the basis-vector convention of the global q-difference theorem, h_j=D_j w_j, D_j=(-1)^j q^[j(j+1)/2]/{n choose j}_q. For every parameter on the path one has exactly D_j U_j=M^j/{n choose j}_q, D^(-1)=U diag({n choose j}_q/M^j). (10d) At q_N, {N-1 choose j}_(q_N)=1 and M=1. Therefore U(q_N)=D(q_N)^(-1). (10e) So the actual root crossing, source, cups, caps and weighted word are transported by this unitary finite star map. Away from the root the last factor in (10d) remains present, with all its source and quantum-normal data; U alone is not the whole balanced frame map there. Finally its top phase is the original normalization phase: U_n=q^[N(N-1)/2], U_n(q_N)=i^(N-1)=i^(N+3)=epsilon_N. (10f) This is an exact comparison with the phase already fixed in the full modified dimension, not a phase chosen to fit volume. The rest of that dimension, the root-normal pivotal adapter and the knot's selected regulator period are separate data. ## 4. The retained inverse eigenflag has two boundary bubbles Changing the eigenvalue mark is not the same operation as changing polynomial frames. For the actual meridian mu=-H, the inverse eigenvalue M^(-1) corresponds to H-eigenvalue m^(-1). Its flag is z_-=-exp(-sT/2) sinh(s(1-T)/2)/sinh(sT/2) v. (11) For 0<lambda<1, z_- sends the north source pole to infinity and the south pole to zero. Its projection degree is -1. At lambda=1, for every 0<T<1, it equals z_+ and extends as the smooth degree +1 map z_+=-exp(-pi*i T)v. This difference consists of two explicit negative bubbles, not a contradiction about the full meridian matrix, which extends. To see this without a limiting stationary-phase argument, let u_lambda(T)=|z_-|^2/(1+|z_-|^2) =T sin^2(pi lambda(1-T)) / [T sin^2(pi lambda(1-T))+(1-T)sin^2(pi lambda T)]. For lambda<1 its endpoint values are u(0)=1,u(1)=0. Pointwise in the interior u_lambda->T as lambda->1. The pullback of the normalized flag sphere form is du_lambda wedge dphi/(2pi). For any smooth test function, angular averaging and integration by parts therefore prove the weak-current identity z_-^*omega_flag -> omega_Gamma-delta_north-delta_south. (12) For example, against a radial test h(T) the limit is exactly integral_0^1 h(T)dT-h(0)-h(1). Dominated convergence applies to u_lambda in [0,1], so it also proves (12) for general smooth tests after angular averaging. The local profiles fix both signs. For epsilon=1-lambda: v=epsilon zeta near north: z_- -> -1/bar(zeta), 1/v=epsilon zeta near south: z_- -> bar(zeta). Both are maps of degree -1 on their compactified bubble spheres. Thus the inverse-eigenflag/source boundary survives in the frame where the m-eigenflag is perfectly smooth. Switching marks must carry the full source and peripheral character; merely equating the two flags at the complete central eigenvalue loses (12). ## 5. Scope for the actual A-period This supplies an exact finite quantum-factorial frame torsor and a genuine principal compact-source map matching the moving-q clock. Equations (10a)--(10f) give an exact finite star quantization and identify its root restriction with the actual balanced frame. They do not give a global continuation or quantum-geometric pushforward of the internal knot component. The latter may meet other critical branches. The actual root-pivot K^(1-N) and ordinary integral-color pivot K also differ offroot by K^(-N), with the accompanying twist factor. The adapter is a weight-dependent whole clock, not a scalar. It becomes scalar at the marked root; its normal jets do not. The literature-defined invariant and all its factors remain fixed. The [whole Gamma-source theorem](whole_gamma_frame_profile.md) now also resolves the residual in (10d) on the scaled quantum normal. Its middle-index factor is exactly a marked holomorphic unit times the actual meridian Weyl half-adapter, with their resonance zeros aligned by a specified parameter change. The opposite Gamma profiles give the centered whole source character H(z)=2sinh(z/2)/z. The [regular-profile theorem](scaled_meridian_regular_profile.md) retains that character and the unknown knot-dependent regular coefficient, with uniform division through its resonance zeros. Rivin's unique positive algebraic optimizer supplies the marked classical branch. Equations (1)--(12) provide source and period transport data near its shell. One still must prove that the whole knot pushforward carries the original selected source to that branch with its regulator norm. Neither uniqueness of the critical shapes nor the smooth shear proves this statement. Verification: [independent audit script](../experiments/audit_quantum_factorial_frames.py) and [results](../experiments/quantum_factorial_frames_results.json). The [independent proof audit](quantum_factorial_frames_independent_audit.md) checks the whole frame function, metric rate, source normalization, both bubbles and the exact finite star map, including its root phase.

title: Independent audit of the actual quantum-factorial frames
text: # Independent audit of the actual quantum-factorial frames Audit, 27 October 2026. [quantum_factorial_frames_and_cyclotomic_source.md](quantum_factorial_frames_and_cyclotomic_source.md) passes the uniform frame-period, marked primitive, conditioning and eigenflag-current checks. The exact balanced-source comparison in [integral_color_global_q_difference_source.md](integral_color_global_q_difference_source.md) also checks. ## 1. Exact frame orientation and actual source The basis identity \(p_j=R_jf_j\) implies \(A_p=R^{-1}A_fR\); the printed coupon transformation has that orientation. The positive factors are the exact ratios of q-falling to ordinary falling factorials. The regular balanced basis multiplier of the global q-difference note is the inverse of the coordinate-conjugation multiplier in [the source detour audit](integral_color_source_detour_audit.md). Indeed \[ {n\choose j}_{\rm sym}=q^{-j(n-j)}{n\brack j}_{Q} \] identifies the two formulas exactly, including endpoint phases. The source column, dual row and cup/cap transformations in the regular basis all follow with their printed inverse factors. The normalization distinction is substantive and is explicit in the global-source note. The symmetric Gauss pair is \((\rho E_q,\rho F_q)\). Relative to the original balanced convention \((\rho^2E,F)\), this is a common Hopf rescaling, or equivalently the indicated weight-dependent change of integral lattice. Its \(E\otimes F\) factor cancels in the universal crossing; its Cartan and diagonal pivot stay unchanged. The ordinary integral generators and the literal balanced generators need not both have the same regular \(q=1\) lattice. This distinction cannot be omitted from a comparison of source jets. The reciprocal polynomial chart \(J_n\) gives the stated global q-difference formulas. A particular old balanced Weyl map, if used, must additionally be conjugated by its actual diagonal frame. It need not equal the bare reciprocal matrix in the new coordinates. ## 2. Uniform scalar frame period and its marked primitive The Riemann-sum estimate is uniform, including the resonant endpoint. Writing \[ \log b_\lambda(x)=\log(1-\lambda x)+g(\lambda x) \] leaves a \(C^1\) function \(g\) on the whole closed interval. Its normalized sum error is \(O(1/N)\). Monotonicity controls the logarithmic sum away from its last interval by \(O(\log N/N)\); the final interval has integral bounded by \(O((1+\log N)/N)\), uniformly even as \(\lambda\to1\). The denominator \(b_\lambda(1/N)\) contributes only \(O(N^{-2})\) to the normalized logarithm. This proves the claimed estimate. Direct differentiation of the marked dilogarithm expression gives \[ B_s'(x) =sx/2+\log(1-e^{-sx})-\log(sx) =\log\!\left(\frac{2\sinh(sx/2)}{sx}\right). \] With the common continuation mark this is real on the specified imaginary-\(s\) path. At \(s=0\) the common additive singular constant in \(B_s\) cancels in its difference; the period tends to zero. No unmarked dilogarithm constant is being discarded. The endpoint sine product gives precisely \[ R_n=\frac{N}{(2\sin(\pi/N))^{N-1}(N-1)!}. \] All factors satisfy \(0<[k]_q/k\le1\), so the condition number is \(R_n^{-1}\). The limit \(\log(2\pi)-1\) follows with the printed sign. This conditioning is the same in a common diagonal metric. ## 3. Canonical shears and the two negative inverse-flag bubbles The scalar products of the principal symbols give the stated Casimir. Solving their two eigenline equations gives exactly the printed plus and inverse flag factors. The plus shear fixes \(T=va\), preserves \(dv\wedge da\), and on the real sphere only changes its angle. Its generating function in the stated primitive \(\log v\,dT\) has derivative \(s(1-T)/2\), as claimed. For the Chern primitive \(-a\,dv\), the corresponding primitive difference instead is \(d(sT^2/4)\); these conventions are compatible through the exact change of primitive. The p-to-f principal shear has logarithmic shift \(-\log J_s(1-T)=-S_\lambda'(T)\), matching the actual factorial-period sign. Its nonuniform endpoint explains why the old p-frame plus bubble is not an invariant obstruction. For the inverse flag, the latitude lies in \([0,1]\), tends to \(T\) in the interior, and has endpoint values \(1,0\) below resonance. Integration by parts against the angularly averaged test function gives the weak limit \(\omega_\Gamma-\delta_{T=0}-\delta_{T=1}\). The local maps are \(-1/\bar\zeta\) and \(\bar\zeta\), each of degree \(-1\), fixing both signs independently. ## 4. Scope of the valid interpolation The exact ordinary integral-color closure uses \(K\) and its ordinary twist. The frozen root closure has its different whole-clock adapter, explicitly retained in both notes. The root pivot is not an off-root pivotal element merely because the module quotient exists. The smooth principal shear alone does not identify its literal pullback with finite star transport. A specified diagonal matrix conjugation does give an exact inner star automorphism, with its source transformed too; it does not construct a global geometric A-branch. Exponential frame conditioning, actual inverse-eigenflag marking, endpoint currents and source coupons remain. The nearby-principal-root resonances of the actual scalar color further prohibit a uniformly nonvanishing positive WKB approximation along the whole real path. ## 5. The exact finite unitary shear The added diagonal shear is also correct. Put \[ U_j=q^{Nj-j(j+1)/2},\qquad \widehat a=J_-/n,\quad\widehat b=J_+/n,\quad \widehat T=J/n. \] The two adjacent ratios are \(q^{j-N}\) and \(q^{N-j-1}\). Binomial summation therefore gives exactly \[ \sigma_{U\widehat aU^{-1}} =m^{-1}q\,a[1+(q-1)T]^{n-1},\qquad \sigma_{U\widehat bU^{-1}} =mq^{-1}\,b[1+(q^{-1}-1)T]^{n-1}, \] and \(\widehat T\) is fixed. Here \(a=z/(1+vz)\) and \(b=v/(1+vz)\) are the two normalized off-diagonal coordinates. Their principal limits are \(a/r,rb\), with \(r=e^{s(1-T)/2}\), giving precisely the source shear. For real \(\lambda\), every \(U_j\) has modulus one. This makes conjugation unitary in any common diagonal coherent metric and leaves the diagonal pivots unchanged. It is an exact automorphism of the finite symbol algebra with its star product; only its principal limit is the literal pullback by the smooth source map. Sources and inserted matrices still transform by that same conjugation. For the regular balanced basis multiplier, \[ D_{{\rm basis},j}U_j =\frac{M^j}{{n\choose j}_{\rm sym}}, \qquad M=-q^N. \] At the root this is one, so \(U=D_{\rm basis}^{-1}\). Off the root its residual q-binomial gauge remains; it is not a uniformly bounded scalar normalization. Finally \[ U_n=q^{N(N-1)/2}\big|_{q=q_N} =i^{N-1}=i^{N+3}=\epsilon_N. \] This exact endpoint phase uses the marked path. It does not permit dropping the other pivotal, ribbon or source characters.

title: Exact longitude insertion and the regulator action of the actual state
text: # Exact longitude insertion and the regulator action of the actual state Research note, 26 October 2026. This continues the [marked braid correspondence](marked_braid_holonomy.md) and [complete fundamental-cycle comparison](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md). It proves an exact meridian-shift insertion formula in the actual finite state, identifies its classical coordinate with the preferred longitude, and fixes the norm of a compatible geometric logarithmic action. The selected finite period's geometric contribution is still unproved; this is not a proof of the volume conjecture. The construction uses the literature ADO state already fixed in [the normalization audit](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). It introduces neither an ordering of an arbitrary classical polynomial nor a replacement state. ## 1. The meridian shift is an exact finite insertion Fix a b-strand braid closing to a knot, with writhe w. Put q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^alpha, M=-qx, kappa_D=w-b+1. The permutation of a knot braid is a b-cycle, hence kappa_D is even. The actual reduced zero-framed state F_N(M) is the cut scalar. In the balanced factorial basis it can equally be written with a constant cut vector and normalized average. Every nonzero term then has matching cut input and output indices: total integer weight is conserved at every crossing. Denote the resulting closed state set by S_N and its full weight, including trace, framing, and 1/N, by W_N(x;s). For a crossing with input a,b and shift k use A=Q^a,B=Q^b,C=Q^k,X=x^2. Define the rational functions tau_+=BC/x * (1-QX/A)/(1-QXC/A), tau_-=x/A * (1-QX/B)/(1-QXC/B). (1.1) Then, exactly at every level N>=2, F_N(qM)=sum_(s in S_N) L_D(q,x;s) W_N(x;s), L_D=q^(-kappa_D) x^(-w) product_crossings tau_sign^(-1). (1.2) The insertion is a fixed rational expression in q,x and the internal monomials. Its formula does not grow with N. Its meaning at a zero or pole is the cancelled whole term, as specified in Section 2, not evaluation of separate quotients. ### Direct proof, including the square-root and framing factors The exact coefficients in the preceding notes give r_+(qx)/r_+(x) =q^(-a-b-k)(1-QXC/A)/(1-QX/A), r_-(qx)/r_-(x) =q^(a+b-k)(1-QXC/B)/(1-QX/B). (1.3) If c is the first output index, respectively b+k or b-k, both equations become r_sign(qx)=x^(-sign)q^(c-a) r_sign(x)/tau_sign. (1.4) The factor q^(c-a), sometimes written as a square root of a shape monomial, telescopes without a sign ambiguity. Let J(a_1,...,a_b)=-sum_j j*a_j. For either crossing, c+d=a+b as an equality of integers, and J_out-J_in=c-a. Every closed state therefore has product_crossings q^(c-a)=1. (1.5) This uses the actual unwrapped indices and their finite support; it does not infer a sign by taking a square root after cyclic specialization. The pivotal trace contributes q^((1-N)(b-1)) under x->qx, and the residual zero-framing factor contributes q^(w(N-1)). Their product is gamma_N=q^((N-1)kappa_D)=q^(-kappa_D), (1.6) because q^N=-1 and kappa_D is even. Combining (1.4)--(1.6) proves (1.2). No summation index was shifted, so no endpoint term is omitted. Away from the roots the auxiliary finite cut lift has the same identity with gamma_N in place of q^(-kappa_D), or with z^kappa_D q^(-kappa_D) when z=q^N. That central factor must be retained before q^N=-1. There is a useful cancellation in (1.2). Put Y=M^2=QX. Then L_D=q^(-kappa_D) product_positive (1-YC/A)/(BC(1-Y/A)) product_negative A(1-YC/B)/(1-Y/B). (1.7) Thus the insertion uses the squared meridian, with no residual x or square root. Its N-fold cyclic norm is exactly one on every closed state. The [squared-meridian descent](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) proves F_N(-M)=F_N(M), descends the actual minimal operator to Y, and retains the full ADO state's even-level sign. Its natural root norm extension has degree N rather than 2N. ## 2. Cancellation at the ideal color and higher shifts Write r_sign=J_sign(z_sign;Q)_k, where J_sign denotes the explicit monomial times Gaussian binomial in the actual formula, defined without dividing by the Pochhammer. Put z_+=QX/A, z_-=QX/B. Adjacent product cancellation proves r_+/tau_+=(x/(BC)) J_+ (Qz_+;Q)_k, r_-/tau_-=(A/x) J_- (Qz_-;Q)_k. (2.1) These are finite Laurent expressions in x, even when the individual ratios in (1.1) are singular. For k=0 both Pochhammers are one; for k>0 cancel the first factor and add the last. This proves the extension of (1.2) to M=1 while retaining its whole meridian germ. For j>=0 there is the exact ordered-insertion identity F_N(q^j M)=sum_s W_N(x;s) product_(r=0)^(j-1)L_D(q,q^r x;s). (2.2) The local cancelled forms are r_+ product_r tau_+(q^r x)^(-1) =J_+ (Q^j z_+;Q)_k (x/(BC))^j q^(j(j-1)/2), r_- product_r tau_-(q^r x)^(-1) =J_- (Q^j z_-;Q)_k (A/x)^j q^(-j(j-1)/2). (2.3) They follow by telescoping a finite rectangular product. The external multiplier for the right side of (2.3), when summed with the old trace and framing weights, is gamma_N^j x^(-jw)q^(-w j(j-1)/2). All these formulas preserve even and composite levels and all finite support endpoints. For a specified Ore operator P=sum_j a_j(q,M)T^j, TM=qMT, its action on F_N is consequently the same actual period with the inserted expression sum_j a_j(q,M) product_(r=0)^(j-1)L_D(q,q^r x;s). (2.4) Thus T is an actual quantum peripheral insertion in the literature state. Equation (2.4) neither assumes that its classical polynomial annihilates each individual state nor identifies the minimal operator's classical components. ### The full ADO normalization remains explicit For N_N(M)=d_N(M)F_N(M), use the already proved gauge g(q,M)=d_N(qM)/d_N(M) =-q^(-1)(q^2M^2-1)/(M^2-1). Its insertion is g(q,M)L_D. This retains the entire factor d_N=i^(N+3)M^(N-1)/(1+M^2+...+M^(2N-2)). The full state may have poles elsewhere on the root orbit, so its identities are meromorphic whole-germ identities. At a generic classical meridian g->-1; the full and reduced classical shift variables therefore differ by a sign. No numerical specialization erases that marked distinction. ## 3. Its classical symbol is the preferred longitude Let q->1 in the rational insertion, with the internal coordinates held fixed. Then x=-M and ell_intr=x^(-w)/T_over, T_over=product t_sign, t_+=BC/x*(1-x^2/A)/(1-x^2C/A), t_-=x/A*(1-x^2/B)/(1-x^2C/B). (3.1) The exact cancellation (1.5) fixes the sign of this symbol. There is no remaining arbitrary square root. Here is a vector proof of its marking. In the balanced physical coordinates of the previous note, K=x/A, e=(x^(-1)-K)p, f=(1-A)/p. The raw meridian matrix G=b_-^(-1)b_+ obeys G (p,1)^t=x^(-1)(p,1)^t. Thus the canonical momentum p is the raw projective eigenflag. After the prefix transport B_(-,j-1), use the global vectors v_j=B_(-,j-1)^(-1)(p_j,1)^t. Their actual meridians mu_j=-H_j have eigenvalue M^(-1) on these vectors. Direct substitution in both crossing maps gives v'_under=-mu_over^(-sign) v_under, v'_over=t_sign v_over. (3.2) For example at a positive crossing, H_1^(-1)b_(-,1)^(-1)=b_(+,1)^(-1), whose second row is (0,1). Hence its under-vector is already normalized with scalar one before replacing H_1 by -mu_1. The over scalar is p'_2/p_1, exactly t_+ in (3.1). The inverse crossing gives t_- and the same minus sign. This proves (3.2) as a rational identity, with the prefix transports included. Follow the single knot through its braid and closure. Let W be the left-ordered product of mu_over^(-sign) encountered at the underpasses. Each crossing supplies one minus sign, and each supplies one factor t_sign at its overpass. Since the critical tuple closes, (3.2) gives 1=(-1)^c T_over * eigenvalue(W), (3.3) where c is the crossing number. The positively oriented blackboard parallel has holonomy W^(-1): its Wirtinger word lists mu_over^(sign) in encounter order, the inverse of this left-ordered vector transport. Its linking number is w. Therefore the preferred longitude is lambda=W^(-1)mu^(-w). (3.4) This also follows by pushing the parallel curve along the diagram: an underpass contributes its over-meridian with the crossing sign, and removing the writhe removes mu^w. On the selected M^(-1)-flag, (3.3)--(3.4) give eigenvalue(lambda)=(-1)^c M^w T_over =x^w T_over=ell_intr^(-1), (3.5) using c congruent to w modulo two. On the other peripheral flag, with meridian eigenvalue M, the eigenvalue is ell_intr. Consequently (M,ell_intr) is the marked preferred peripheral pair. (3.6) The source's cut flag and the flag in (3.6) are explicitly different at generic M. At completeness they coalesce, and the rational identity extends on the augmented chart. This fixes the Weyl inversion that a wedge calculation alone could not detect. The geometric peripheral image of the actual classical critical correspondence is therefore the marked geometric A-curve in these variables. This is a statement about that critical correspondence. It is not a claim that every minimal annihilator of its selected quantum period retains this component. ## 4. A source-compatible logarithmic action Put h=Log Q=2pi*i/N and u=Log M. Use independent integral state variables k_i, with t_i=Q^(k_i), xi_i=Log t_i. The actual incidence/weight-conservation lattice is integral; its kernel has an integral basis. Choose these coordinates before passing to logarithms, retaining any N-dependent purely imaginary affine offsets. The leading action derived from the actual coefficients has the form S=G(xi,u)+sum_j eps_j Li_2(z_j), (4.1) where z_j are monomials with modulus-one constants, and G is a quadratic form with real coefficients, a purely imaginary linear term, and a real constant. The real constant includes the retained Li_2(1) and framing constants. For example, in a positive crossing with a=Log A,b=Log B, c=Log C, the balanced expression uses G_+=ab+(a-b)c-c^2/2-u(a+b+c)-pi*i(a+b), Phi_+=Li_2(B)+Li_2(C)+Li_2(M^2/A) -Li_2(BC)-Li_2(M^2C/A)-Li_2(1). The negative expression uses G_-=-ab+u(a+b-c)+pi*i(a+b-c), Phi_-=Li_2(A)+Li_2(C)+Li_2(M^2/B) -Li_2(AC)-Li_2(M^2C/B)-Li_2(1). These signs follow from Log x=u+pi*i in the actual formulas. The pivotal term is 2pi*i sum_(closed legs)Log A_j and the remaining framing term is 2pi*i*kappa_D*u-2pi^2*kappa_D. Subleading terms remain in the exact quantum weights; (4.1) only describes their already specified leading logarithmic action. On an exponentiated critical branch, partial_(xi_i)S=2pi*i*n_i, n_i in Z. The integers are locally constant on its logarithmic cover. Define S_flat=S-2pi*i sum_i n_i xi_i. (4.2) This is compatible with the *same* actual discrete period: at every actual state, on its unwrapped lift xi_i=h k_i, exp((S_flat-S)/h)=exp(-2pi*i sum_i n_i k_i)=1. (4.3) No coefficient or boundary factor is changed. Equation (4.3) is a discrete character identity; it is not a claim that this character is an ordinary rational gauge for generic q. It identifies permissible logarithmic action sheets of the same finite data. In particular it does not choose a global steepest descent cycle or its coefficient. After restriction to this log-critical branch, dS_flat=2v du, v=Log ell_intr. (4.4) The factor two is forced by the actual meridian half-step u->u+h/2 and by (1.3), not inferred from an analogy with a classical polynomial. ## 5. An exact logarithmic identity fixes the geometric action norm For the same compatible logarithms and dilogarithms, D(beta)=Im S-sum_i Re xi_i Im(partial_(xi_i)S) -Re u Im(partial_u S). (5.1) Here beta is the actual crossing Bloch sum. To prove this, write Log z_j=sum_i m_ji xi_i+m_ju u+i theta_j. The Bloch--Wigner identity gives D(beta)=Im Phi+sum_j eps_j Re Log z_j Im Log(1-z_j). Differentiation of Phi gives minus the corresponding linear combinations of Log(1-z_j). Finally a real quadratic G with purely imaginary linear term and real constant satisfies Im G=sum_i Re xi_i Im(partial_i G)+Re u Im(partial_u G). Substitution proves (5.1). Compatible continuation of Li_2 and Log(1-z) preserves the identity: their monodromy terms cancel in D, and their remaining constants are real. Apply (4.2). All internal derivatives vanish on the branch, and (4.4) yields Im S_flat=D(beta)+2 Re u Im v. (5.2) At the complete color u=0 the previous fundamental-cycle proof gives the fully calibrated value Im S_flat=Vol(M). (5.3) Thus an admissible geometric action sheet of the actual coefficients has the required exponential: for h=2pi*i/N, (2pi/N)log|exp(S_flat/h)|=Vol(M) (5.4) at the complete point. This evaluates the specified geometric exponential. It is not an asymptotic formula for F_N(1). ## 6. The action period is the marked regulator norm Define R_intr=S_flat-u v, U=2u, V=2v. Equations (4.4) and (5.2) give exactly dR_intr=-(U dV-V dU)/4, Im R_intr=D(beta)+(Re U Im V-Re V Im U)/4. (6.1) Hence the period exp(2R_intr/(pi*i)), with the invariant Heisenberg norm already fixed in the regulator note, satisfies log||P_intr||=2D(beta)/pi. (6.2) There is no free imaginary additive constant: the retained action and the exact identity (5.1) fix it. A real phase constant remains part of the full complex-period comparison. The functions in the geometric triangulation's full peripheral rows are m=M^2,l=ell_intr^2. Indeed a peripheral matrix diag(M,M^(-1)) fixing infinity acts on its horospherical coordinate by multiplication by M^2, and similarly for the longitude. Thus both the actual crossing sum and the positive triangulation satisfy delta beta=-2M wedge ell_intr. Their regulator difference has zero differential on the connected geometric branch. It is zero at completeness by the fundamental-cycle comparison. Therefore D(beta) is the marked geometric regulator on that branch, on compatible nondegenerate chart overlaps. Equations (6.1)--(6.2) identify the connection and norm of its logarithmic action period. At a complete longitude value -1, v may equal pi*i rather than zero. Centering it requires the corresponding explicit character in S_flat; the regulator line's deck multiplier and invariant norm account for that change. It is not silently replaced by a longitude value +1. Likewise the full ADO gauge in Section 2 changes the classical shift sign; its meridian germ remains a separate piece of the exact quantum pointing. ## 7. What this establishes, and the remaining theorem There are now three actual-state comparisons: 1. The root-level meridian shift is the exact rational longitude insertion (1.2), with all endpoints, roots, and framing retained. 2. Its classical critical coordinate is the preferred longitude on the M-eigenflag, with the cut's inverse flag recorded. 3. The compatible geometric logarithmic action has the marked regulator connection and norm, and its complete imaginary value is Vol(M). The selected finite period still needs a theorem showing a nonzero geometric contribution of subexponential normalization, and controlling the other contributions. An exponentiated critical point, an allowed logarithmic character, and (5.3) do not prove its coefficient in that period is nonzero. They also do not prove a geometric factor in every minimal annihilator of the actual sum. The root-level rational V=1 sector is not being equated with the geometric central curve. The unchanged target is (4/N)log|F_N(1)|-log||P_hyp|| ->0. No version of the original volume conjecture is asserted here. ## 8. Coverage and verification Classical meridian/longitude potential interpretations already have coverage in, for example, [Sawabe, potential functions with arbitrary colors](https://msp.org/pjm/2023/322-1/pjm-v322-n1-p08-p.pdf). The geometric action/regulator framework is also within the previously recorded optimistic-limit coverage. The calculations above were derived independently from the fixed actual weights; no proof from those sources is a premise, and no novelty claim is made for the classical conclusion. The [audit](../experiments/audit_quantum_longitude_action.py) and [results](../experiments/quantum_longitude_action_results.json) check both rational eigenvector transports and the exact integer telescoping identity; 53,262 local cancelled shift identities at generic q and roots; and 80 inserted periods against the independently assembled actual dense matrices. These include the Kashaev color, both crossing signs, two successive shifts, and even/composite levels. An exact trefoil calculation fixes the longitude sign, inversion, and framing: the M-flag value is -M^(-6), and the inverse flag has -M^6. It is a peripheral calibration, not a torus-knot volume argument. The actual positive and negative potentials satisfy (5.1) in high-precision checks. A figure-eight complete/deformed calibration in three frames checks the preferred-longitude word, the five integer stationary windings, (5.2)--(6.2), and the complete action value. The proofs are the rational and logarithmic calculations above, not inference from these samples.

title: The quantum matrix torsor and the transport of its base
text: # The quantum matrix torsor and the transport of its base Research proof, 27 October 2026. On the dense full-cyclic chart, the actual cyclotomic-normal algebra has an explicit whole quantum-torus matrix cover. An actual crossing algebra map then splits, constructively, into a matrix intertwiner and an automorphism of the quantized leaf. The matrix part has no local lifting obstruction. The base transport and the selected source are separate data, and the latter has an exact comparison residual below. This extends the root-level [regular holonomy line](regular_holonomy_braiding.md) and [closed-braid period line](closed_braid_period_line.md). Those notes already construct the root Hom line and its cut. The new issue here is the noncommutative base of the actual [full-cyclic Rees module](irregular_rees_full_cyclic_module.md), before setting its normal parameter to zero. No selected-period or volume identity is inferred from smoothness. ## 1. A commutative base cannot support the full cyclic normal family Let R be a commutative ring, and let K,E be invertible N by N matrices with KE=Q EK. Taking determinants gives Q^N=1 in R. (1.1) In particular a full-cyclic E, for which E^N is a unit, cannot deform as an N-dimensional matrix representation over a flat commutative q-normal base with Q^N!=1. This remains true at a nonsingular point of the classical center. A commutative quantum implicit-function argument for such finite matrices would start with an impossible ambient family. The actual Rees construction avoids (1.1): its entries are operators on the Fock variable. The base itself is quantized. The construction below identifies the corresponding matrix cover without a formal order-by-order choice of matrix entries. ## 2. An exact whole quantum-torus matrix cover Work over a characteristic-zero field containing a marked primitive N-th root zeta. Keep Q variable and put c=Q/zeta. On the open set K Ecal!=0, fix the quantum Casimir Omega. The relation F Ecal=Omega-qK-q^(-1)K^(-1) eliminates F. Thus the actual localized algebra is the quantum torus A_Q=<K^(+/-1),Ecal^(+/-1): K Ecal=Q Ecal K>. (2.1) Its Laurent monomials are independent: one may either use their normal-order multiplication directly, or represent K by multiplication and Ecal by the Q-shift. This also proves flatness in Q on this chart. Choose nonzero root coordinates k_*,e_* and marked roots k_*^(1/N), e_*^(1/N). Let B_c=<u^(+/-1),v^(+/-1): u v=c v u>. (2.2) Let D,S be constant clock and shift matrices with D h_j=zeta^j h_j, S h_j=h_(j+1 mod N), D S=zeta S D, D^N=S^N=I. There is an exact map, for the whole variable Q, K=k_*^(1/N) D u, Ecal=e_*^(1/N) S v, (2.3) from A_Q to Mat_N(B_c). Indeed the two commutation factors multiply to zeta*c=Q. Distinct K^a Ecal^b have distinct scalar Laurent powers u^a v^b, so the map is injective. Its central powers at the root are K^N=k_* u^N, Ecal^N=e_* v^N. (2.4) Adjoining these marked quantum N-th roots gives the full matrix cover: D and S are recovered from (2.3), and their finite Fourier projectors and arrows give every matrix unit. Explicitly, p_0=(1/N)sum_(r=0)^(N-1)D^r, E_ij=S^i p_0 S^(-j). (2.5) Conversely (2.3), the quantum roots u,v, and (2.5) generate exactly Mat_N(B_c). This is a noncommutative cover before the root is taken. The marked cross relations include u Ecal=c Ecal u and K v=c v K; choosing arbitrary N-th roots without these cross relations would not specify this cover. It is not an etale cover of a nonexistent commutative generic center. At Q=zeta, B_c becomes the commutative root-coordinate cover of the regular fixed-Casimir leaf, and (2.3) is its ordinary matrix splitting. This construction is compatible with the dense full-cyclic color chart already obtained from the actual Verma source. It covers its Ecal^N!=0 open set.
