Another chart is needed at an Ecal^N zero; the identity singularity of the fixed-Casimir leaf has not been removed by declaring this open set dense. ### 2.1 The exact local logarithmic algebra For comparison with the actual normal parameter, put d=N(Q^N-1), H=N Log(Q^N)=N Log(1+d/N). Thus H=d+O(d^2), and Q=zeta exp(H/N^2) on the marked branch. Set X=N Log u, P=N Log v. In the completed local algebra, (2.2) is exactly [X,P]=H, (2.6) and K=k_*^(1/N)D exp(X/N), Ecal=e_*^(1/N)S exp(P/N). (2.7) One can check (2.6) directly inside the original completed quantum torus. Its logarithms X=Log(K^N/k_*), P=Log(Ecal^N/e_*) satisfy exp(ad X)P=P+H. The operator ad X raises the complete local filtration, so taking its formal logarithm gives [X,P]=H. The operators D=k_*^(-1/N)K exp(-X/N), S=e_*^(-1/N)Ecal exp(-P/N) commute with X,P, have N-th powers one, and obey DS=zeta SD. This recovers (2.7), including its matrix units, from the actual algebra itself. Completion may be taken with weights X=P=1,H=2; all normal-order products then have finite coefficients at each weight. In particular the divided commutator has {X,P}=1. Its symplectic form is -dX wedge dP, exactly the fixed-leaf Gauss form -dLog k wedge dLog e in the Rees calculation. On a connected formal chart the center of this quantum base is the constant ring k[[H]]: commuting a normal-ordered series with X and P forces its P and X derivatives, respectively, to vanish. Additional fixed peripheral parameters belong to that constant ring. ## 3. Constructive matrix Hensel splitting of an actual map Here is the algebra statement needed for crossing transport. It works over a noncommutative base. **Matrix/base splitting.** Let B_s,B_t be complete rings, with a central ideal of definition containing d, and let alpha:Mat_m(B_s) -> Mat_m(B_t) be a continuous algebra isomorphism. Suppose a specified root frame G_0 identifies the two systems of matrix units modulo d. Then there is an invertible G and a base isomorphism theta:B_s->B_t such that alpha(a)=G theta_entry(a) G^(-1). (3.1) This requires the given actual alpha. Classical nonsingularity by itself does not choose theta. Proof and exact formula: lift G_0 to any invertible G_* and replace alpha by alpha'=Ad_(G_*^-1)alpha. Now alpha'(E_ij)=E_ij modulo d. Define the finite sum G'=sum_(i=1)^m alpha'(E_i1) E_1i. (3.2) It is I modulo d and therefore invertible. Matrix-unit multiplication gives, for every a,b, alpha'(E_ab)G'=G'E_ab. Consequently beta=Ad_(G'^-1)alpha' fixes all E_ij. The centralizer of these matrix units is exactly the set of scalar matrices bI, even when B_t is noncommutative. Therefore beta(bI)=theta(b)I for an isomorphism theta; multiplying by E_ij proves (3.1) with G=G_*G'. This proves existence and gives the intertwiner explicitly. In particular the base map is also extracted by a finite formula: theta(b)=[G^(-1)alpha(bI)G]_(1,1). (3.3) The calculation is not restricted to a Taylor truncation: whenever alpha, the marked matrix units, and G_* belong to a specified whole function algebra, (3.2) belongs to that algebra too. Inverting its unit gives the same whole local formula. The formal theorem alone does not prove that this inverse or the quantum-root branches extend globally across their divisors. At a chosen regular root place the marked quantum roots of Section 2 lift under an actual regular alpha by Hensel functional calculus. For an element with scalar invertible root value, the derivative of W^N-a in the unknown W is multiplication by N W_0^(N-1), a unit. The unique branch obtained this way is the one reducing to the marked scalar N-th root, not one of the non-scalar finite-order roots. Uniqueness enforces the required quantum cross relations as well. For example, writing a=K^N,b=Ecal^N gives ab=c^(N^2)ba. Conjugating the marked root u by b and taking its N-th power shows b u b^(-1)=c^(-N)u. Conjugating the marked root v by u and repeating the argument gives u v u^(-1)=c v. The same proof gives u Ecal=c Ecal u and K v=c v K. These equalities use the marked branches with the same scalar root values modulo d. Thus alpha locally lifts to the specified matrix cover, and (3.2) then applies. This constructs a local function germ; it does not replace the branch and localization data of a whole cover. Apply this to the actual rational R-conjugation on the pair of localized full-cyclic colors, with m=N^2. At an admissible point where its denominators and the chosen input/output cyclic charts are units, it yields an explicit semilinear crossing object (3.5) below. Its classical base map is the actual root holonomy map. The procedure constructs an intertwiner of the actual algebra transport; it does not select the scalar normalization or the original R-source kernel from that algebra transport alone. ### 3.1 Precisely which torsor is a line? For fixed alpha and fixed theta, two G in (3.1) differ by a unit of Z(B_t). Indeed their ratio commutes with all matrix units, so is bI; commuting also with all scalar matrices forces b central. If only the matrix-unit equations are fixed, the freedom is B_t^x, not Z(B_t)^x. Changing G to G bI changes theta to theta' = Ad_(b^-1) theta. (3.4) This distinction matters. At the root the whole base is commutative and the Hom object is an ordinary line over the leaf. Before the root, fixing the full quantum base transport usually reduces its scalar freedom to functions of Q and the fixed peripheral parameters. A nonconstant root rescaling can instead change the subleading base transport through (3.4), while leaving its classical map unchanged. There is a semilinear module map R_theta(v)=G theta_entry(v), (3.5) which satisfies R_theta(av)=alpha(a)R_theta(v). This is a genuine linear intertwiner over the constants, with the specified right-base semilinearity. It need not be represented by a regular scalar operator on the original Fock representation. ### 3.2 No matrix obstruction can hide a base obstruction If a regular unit in Mat_m(B) implements an inner automorphism, its induced action on the scalar commutative algebra B/dB is the identity: the root scalar matrices are central. Hence a crossing with a nonidentity classical leaf map cannot be implemented by such a regular inner unit on a fixed fiber. It must be understood semilinearly between the transported fibers, or implemented after an irregular enlargement, as the actual quantum factorial does. The infinitesimal form is equally explicit. An O-linear derivation D of Mat_m(O) is inner, with H_D=sum_i D(E_i1)E_1i, D(E_ab)=[H_D,E_ab]. (3.6) The proof differentiates the matrix-unit identities; the term E_a1 D(E_11)E_1b vanishes by differentiating E_11^2=E_11. A general derivation decomposes into its derivation on O and (3.6). Thus a matrix correction can remove a lifting error precisely after its base derivation has been accounted for. Even a smooth symplectic base does not select the higher corrections. For [P,X]=d, all maps X->X+d a,P->P have the same classical identity. They are distinct exact automorphisms, implemented by exp(aP) on a formal coordinate chart. Classical uniqueness of an algebraic gluing point does not choose among them, or choose a central scalar factor of its intertwiner. ## 4. Composition, scalar cocycles, and what Hilbert 90 removes Suppose actual crossing maps alpha_g have been split as in (3.1). For composable g,h write alpha_(gh)=alpha_g alpha_h. The two matrix parts satisfy G_g theta_g(G_h)=G_(gh) b_(g,h), b_(g,h) in B^x, theta_(gh)=Ad_(b_(g,h)) theta_g theta_h. (4.1) To prove that b is a scalar matrix, compare the two sides on each matrix unit. This yields (4.1) without assuming a strict scalar cocycle in advance. Associativity gives the exact coherence identity b_(gh,k) b_(g,h) =b_(g,hk) theta_g(b_(h,k)). (4.2) If the base lifts have also been chosen coherently, so that theta_(gh)=theta_g theta_h, the b_(g,h) lie in Z(B)^x. Only then does this become the usual scalar cocycle. In particular equality of classical center maps does not make the two quantum base maps equal or make their relative transport scalar. An actual universal R identity can trivialize the corresponding cocycle; smoothness of the classical place alone cannot do so. For completeness the generic finite-Galois descent of such a scalar line has an elementary proof. Over a finite Galois field extension L/K let gamma(G)=a_gamma G, with a_(gamma delta)=a_gamma gamma(a_delta). Choose t in L such that b=sum_gamma a_gamma gamma(t) is nonzero. Such t exists because distinct field automorphisms are linearly independent: a minimal nontrivial relation, evaluated at tx and subtracted from its value at t times one chosen automorphism of x, would give a shorter relation. Reindexing gives gamma(b)=a_gamma^(-1)b. Therefore bG is Galois invariant. This is the needed Hilbert-90 calculation, with its scalar marking explicit. It works over the generic function field, or the constant Laurent-series field of the quantized leaf. It does not prove that b is a unit on an entire integral chart, trivialize a global line bundle, or normalize the actual cut. Those assertions have divisors and source data of their own. ## 5. The actual dilogarithm moves the quantum base The separation above locates the resonant factor of the actual crossing. For the uncheck nilpotent factor Theta=P_Q(q Ecal_1 F_2), P_Q(z)=(z;Q)_infinity, put X=-e_1 f_2, with e_i=Ecal_i^N,f_i=F_i^N. The root-normal logarithm has polar part Li_2(X)/d. This follows coefficientwise: in -sum_(m>=1)z^m/[m(1-Q^m)] only m=N r have poles, and their leading coefficient is z^(Nr)/(r^2 d). The precise regular matrix factor and its marked source are retained in [the explicit crossing regularization](rees_whole_crossing_source_factorization.md). The actual divided brackets on the two leaves give {Li_2(X),k_1}=k_1 Log(1-X), {Li_2(X),k_2}=-k_2 Log(1-X), {Li_2(X),e_1}={Li_2(X),f_2}=0. (5.1) Since X is constant along this Hamiltonian field, its time-one map is exactly k_1 -> k_1(1+e_1 f_2), k_2 -> k_2/(1+e_1 f_2), e_1 -> e_1, f_2 -> f_2, e_2 -> e_2+e_1/k_2-e_1 k_2/(1+e_1 f_2), f_1 -> f_1+f_2 k_1-f_2/[k_1(1+e_1 f_2)]. (5.2) For the last two equations, the vector field is e_2 dot=(k_2^(-1)-k_2)Log(1-X)/f_2, f_1 dot=(k_1-k_1^(-1))Log(1-X)/e_1. Insert k_1(t)=k_1(1-X)^t,k_2(t)=k_2(1-X)^(-t) and integrate. The formulas are rational and therefore extend from the log chart to the indicated divisor open set. These are the center formulas for Theta alone. Composing with the actual Cartan automorphism changes the relevant X to -e_1 f_2 k_2/k_1 and gives the full divisor D_c=1+e_1 f_2 k_2/k_1 of the root holonomy crossing. Thus the resonant function has a specific base action; a finite regular inner matrix factor cannot supply that action by itself. This is a statement about the actual crossing, not an identification of its selected braid closure with the geometric fundamental-class period. The [Rees-to-Gauss transgression](rees_gauss_period_transgression.md) is also exact, but has a different role. Its primitives theta_source=u dp and theta_Gauss=-Log(k/a)dLog e are explicitly chosen polarizations. Their dilogarithm difference gauges those prequantum primitives. This does not assert that exp(W/d) is the actual R, the actual source, or a selected horizontal section. The joint-meridian correction there must remain part of any such comparison. ## 6. The source obstruction is an explicit residual, not a matrix lift First suppose psi,phi are a column and row over the transported base algebras, so that their coupons are B-linear matrices. Their exact transport under (3.5) is psi_t=G theta(psi_s), phi_t=theta(phi_s)G^(-1), (6.1) and phi_t psi_t=theta(phi_s psi_s). For their coupons Gamma=psi phi, the exact comparison with an independently specified target coupon is Delta_Gamma=G theta(Gamma_s)-Gamma_t G. (6.2) Vanishing of (6.2) is equivalent to preservation of the rank-one source projector. For these B-linear coupons it is unchanged, up to an invertible scalar, by rescaling G through Z(B)^x. It is therefore not removable by the remaining scalar freedom of the intertwiner torsor. Matching the actual source vector and co-source is stronger still: their common rank-one coefficient must be the allowed central unit, with the prescribed normalization. For the actual finite cut, Gamma contains vacuum evaluation and is not a regular matrix-valued function on the leaf. One must first extend theta to its Fock/source module or construct the corresponding kernel. The source (6.2) is otherwise not even defined in the regular coefficient algebra. For such operator-valued coupons the scalar invariance just proved requires the scalar to commute with the source operator as well. The generic quantum center consists of the constant parameters, which do commute with this actual vacuum coupon. At the root the center enlarges to functions on the leaf, and those functions need not commute with vacuum evaluation. Arbitrary root-leaf units cannot be substituted for the allowed quantum scalars. In the actual Rees construction its entries are eta^(i-j) exp(-u/d)/N times evaluation at u=0, eta^N=d. (6.3) Every internal finite-head projector also carries exp(-u/d). Their finite normal jets have the recorded pole bounds and ramified flags; replacing them by regular leaf functions would change the period. The matrix splitting proves neither an extension across this irregular source nor the vanishing of (6.2). There is also a separate scalar evaluation obstruction. For an intertwiner line L and a cut functional ell:L->R, a normalized section ell(J)=1 exists locally if and only if ell of a local frame is a unit. Smoothness and invertibility of the frame do not imply it. An exact two-dimensional example, which can be tensored with any smooth symplectic base, is J=[[0,1],[-1,0]], Gamma=(1/2)[[1,1],[1,1]]. Here J is invertible and defines a perfectly regular inner algebra transport, but Tr(Gamma J)=0 and J Gamma-Gamma J!=0. This is not a knot counterexample. It disproves the inference from a nonsingular algebraic place and a lifted intertwiner to a nonzero selected source. ## 7. What is now constructive and what remains for the knot At an admissible smooth full-cyclic place, the actual rational crossing map and the marked quantum-root cover determine a local semilinear crossing object by (2.3), (3.2), and (3.5). Its matrix deformation is explicit. Its classical leaf transport is forced by the actual algebra map; its actual resonant dilogarithm gives (5.2). When base transport is made coherent the remaining ambiguity is an ordinary central-unit torsor, with the generic descent proved above. The missing pointed comparison has a precise target: extend that base transport to the actual vacuum/source lattice, retain every internal projector, and prove the corresponding residual (6.2) vanishes with the required scalar evaluation. Nonsingularity of the Rivin algebraic place supplies none of these source equations by itself. Conversely this result does not exclude a whole cyclotomic rigidity theorem after those actual equations and marks are supplied. The normal direction d at a fixed N remains distinct from the large-level direction H_N=2 pi i/N. The original finite auxiliary state is regular at its fixed root. Irregular factors in (6.3) can cancel polar phases in a whole contraction; regularity does not determine the eventual N-growth or select a geometric saddle. The [exact algebra audit](../experiments/audit_quantum_matrix_base_intertwiner_torsor.py) checks the noncommutative cover, the finite matrix-unit construction with a noncentral base gauge, the phase vector field, and the source counterexample. These checks supplement the proofs above. The [independent proof audit](quantum_matrix_torsor_independent_audit.md) also verifies the matrix cover, quantum-root cross relations, local logarithmic scale, matrix/base splitting, weak cocycle, and generic Hilbert-90 descent. [Independent matrix/base audit](quantum_matrix_torsor_independent_audit.md) checks the whole cover, logarithmic scale, matrix-unit construction, base/scalar freedom, weak cocycle order and Hilbert-90 convention.

title: Independent audit of the quantum matrix/base torsor
text: # Independent audit of the quantum matrix/base torsor Audit, 27 October 2026. Sections 2--4 of [quantum_matrix_base_intertwiner_torsor.md](quantum_matrix_base_intertwiner_torsor.md) pass this independent proof check. The noncommutative base and weak-composition conventions are essential. No tests were rerun. For \(DS=\zeta SD\), \(uv=(Q/\zeta)vu\), the two commutation factors give exactly \(KE=QEK\). Distinct Laurent monomials retain distinct \(u,v\) degrees, proving injectivity of the proposed map. Adjoining the marked quantum roots with their stated cross relations recovers \(D,S\), and their Fourier projectors give every matrix unit. This is a noncommutative matrix cover, rather than a commutative generic finite-dimensional representation. The logarithmic scale is correct: \[ H=N\log(Q^N)=N^2\log(Q/\zeta),\qquad [X,P]=H,\quad X=N\log u,\ P=N\log v. \] For an independent derivation, the original \(N\)-th powers give \(\exp(\operatorname{ad}X)P=P+H\). Since \(H\) is central, applying the formal logarithm leaves only the first difference and gives \([X,P]=H\). The recovered \(D,S\) commute with both logarithms, have order \(N\), and obey \(DS=\zeta SD\). The resulting Poisson form is \(-dX\wedge dP\), as stated. The local root-lifting argument also preserves the quantum cross relations. To make this explicit, suppose \[ ab=c^{N^2}ba,\quad u^N=a,\quad v^N=b,\quad c=Q/\zeta, \] with the roots marked by their scalar values at the regular root place. Conjugation and uniqueness of these marked roots imply \[ b u b^{-1}=c^{-N}u,\qquad u v u^{-1}=cv. \] The first identity follows by taking the marked \(N\)-th root of \(b a b^{-1}=c^{-N^2}a\); the second follows by taking that of \(u b u^{-1}=c^Nb\). The same calculation gives the mixed relations with \(K,E\). Thus the Hensel lift extends the whole quantum cover, not merely its two power equations. For the matrix splitting, \[ G'=\sum_i\alpha'(E_{i1})E_{1i} \] satisfies \(\alpha'(E_{ab})G'=\alpha'(E_{a1})E_{1b}=G'E_{ab}\). Its unit reduction makes it invertible. Conjugating by its inverse therefore fixes every matrix unit, whose centralizer consists exactly of scalar matrices over the possibly noncommutative base. This proves the entrywise base isomorphism and the printed semilinear module map. Holding that base map fixed leaves only central units; holding only the matrix-unit transport fixed leaves arbitrary base units. These two torsors must remain distinct. The order in the coherence formulas checks directly. From \[ G_g\theta_g(G_h)=G_{gh}b_{g,h} \] one gets \(\theta_{gh}=\operatorname{Ad}_{b_{g,h}}\theta_g\theta_h\). Associating a triple matrix product in the two ways gives \[ b_{gh,k}b_{g,h} =b_{g,hk}\theta_g(b_{h,k}), \] with exactly the printed order. Central scalar cocycles arise only after coherent base maps have been specified. The stated Hilbert-90 sum transforms by \(a_\gamma^{-1}\), so it descends the generic line with the given cocycle convention. The result constructs a local whole matrix/base transport from an actual regular algebra isomorphism. It does not infer that isomorphism, its coherent quantum base lift, source preservation, or a nonzero selected evaluation from classical smoothness. The separate source qualification in Section 6 is necessary.

title: Whole quantum-normal crossing response and the marked geometric action
text: # Whole quantum-normal crossing response and the marked geometric action Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual crossing coefficients have a uniform whole-function comparison between the integral quantum normal and the fixed-root positive-meridian normal on every compact bulk-flow chart. The difference is an order-one shape-dependent function. It is not a small matrix perturbation, and the Gamma diagonal source comparison alone cannot intertwine the crossings. For an arbitrary knot braid, the complete original Cartan, framing and pivotal factors cancel in a precise way. The remaining bulk insertion is the Euler derivative minus the actual leading action. At a marked flattened critical point it is the negative action itself. This gives a universal comparison of the leading formal geometric blocks, retaining their full source conventions. It does not compare the selected global periods or resolve their endpoint contributions. The exact scalar source-line comparison is [the whole Gamma theorem](whole_gamma_frame_profile.md), and its all-head extension is [the full-head source transport](full_head_gamma_source_transport.md). The independent local crossing analysis is recorded in [the actual crossing ratio calculation](actual_crossing_q_normal_meridian_ratio.md). ## 1. Two actual normal paths and the exact crossings Put c=2pi*i, H_0=c/N and use a in a fixed complex compact set. Define H=H_0+ca/N^2, b=a/(1+a/N), H b=ca/N, q_col=exp(H/2), Q_col=exp(H), M_col=exp(Hb/2)=-q_col^N, q_0=exp(H_0/2), Q_0=exp(H_0), M_+=exp(H_0b/2). (1) The meridian M_+ is the Weyl inverse of the argument used in the exact Gamma half-source comparison. It is not replaced by M_col. Retain the actual x=-M/q mark as Log x=c/2+H(b-1)/2 on the color path, and with H_0 on the root path. This fixes the Cartan half-character; it is not a principal-log reset. At input integer positions i,j the actual stripped positive coefficient sends `(i,j)` to `(j+k,i-k)` and is r_+=(-1)^k x^(-i-j-k) Q^[ij+(i-j)k-k(k+1)/2] {j+k choose k}_Q (M^2 Q^(-i);Q)_k. (2) The negative coefficient sends `(i,j)` to `(j-k,i+k)` and is r_-=x^(i+j-k) Q^(-ij) {i+k choose k}_Q (M^2 Q^(-j);Q)_k. (3) These are the actual canceled common-Verma formulas, with the original common Cartan unit separated and then restored below. No recurrences or asymptotic invariant identity are assumed. Write u=i/N, v=j/N, t=k/N. For positive crossings fix a compact flow domain with u<=1-epsilon, u-t>=epsilon, v>=0, t>=0, v+t<=1-epsilon. (4) For negative crossings interchange u and v in (4). These are literal head-flow domains. The Pochhammer factors stay away from both cyclotomic endpoints; factorial sums at zero are handled by their removable functions. All coefficients in the comparison are nonzero there for sufficiently large N and a in the prescribed compact set. ## 2. The exact whole bulk response Define the single-valued function on real -1<x<1 by F(x)=integral_0^x c y/(1-exp(-cy))dy, F(0)=0. (5) Its integrand has removable value one at zero. It has the corresponding analytic continuation to a marked zero-free crossing chart. Put B_+(u,v,t)=c[uv+(u-v)t-t^2/2] +F(v+t)-F(v)-F(t)+F(t-u)-F(-u), B_-(u,v,t)=-cuv +F(u+t)-F(u)-F(t)+F(t-v)-F(-v). (6) Then uniformly on (4) and on compact complex a-sets, r_(sign),col/r_(sign),root =exp[a B_sign(u,v,t)](1+O(1/N)). (7) The ratio is a whole function of a on these compact normal sets. Its expansion does not divide by a vanishing integer normal factor. Formula (7) is before summing over the flow indices. Here is a uniform proof. For a quantum factorial with m/N=x, partial_H Log(Q;Q)_m =-sum_(r=1)^m r exp(Hr)/(1-exp(Hr)). After division by N^2 this is a Riemann sum whose limit is F(x)/c. The summand normalized by N has a removable limit at r=0. Its second H derivative is O(N^3), uniformly below the far cyclotomic endpoint. Since H-H_0=ca/N^2, Taylor's formula with a uniform remainder gives (Q_col;Q_col)_m/(Q_0;Q_0)_m =exp[a F(x)](1+O(1/N)). (8) For the Pochhammer in (2), take the same logarithmic derivative at arguments b-i+r. Its range is uniformly separated from zero and from -N by (4). The same Taylor/Riemann calculation gives `exp{a[F(t-u)-F(-u)]}(1+O(1/N))`. The b-shift is O(1) in each argument and changes this limit only by O(1/N). The Gaussian coefficient is the factorial quotient in (8). Finally the explicit Q monomial gives the quadratic term in (6), while the x ratio contributes only O(1/N). This proves (7). The proof for (3) is identical with its displayed support. The original positive common Cartan unit is C(H,b)=exp{H[c/H+b-1]^2/4}. Indeed the unrolled color is `c/H+b-1`, equal to N-1 on the integral path and N-1+b on the fixed-root path. Therefore C(H,b)/C(H_0,b)=exp(-ca/4)(1+O(1/N)). (9) For a negative crossing use its inverse. This scalar cannot be omitted from a crossing comparison; its cancellation in the complete zero-framed word is the next step. ## 3. Why the scalar Gamma source map does not already intertwine R At k=0 the stripped positive coefficient is simply r_+(i,j,0)=x^(-i-j)Q^(ij). Its exact ratio on (1) is exp{(H-H_0)[ij-(b-1)(i+j)/2]}. (10) A diagonal conjugation on the two input/output strands multiplies a checked crossing at equal inputs i=j by one: the corresponding output is the same pair. This remains true for different diagonal gauges on the two strands. A common scalar can match i=j=0, but then cannot also match (10) at another i=j for generic a. For i/N approaching a nonzero bulk u the ratio in (10) tends to `exp(ca u^2)`, whereas at i=j=0 it is one. Restoring the common Cartan scalar changes both by the same factor and does not repair this. Thus the actual Gamma diagonal source maps, alone, cannot extend to a scalar-adjusted diagonal crossing intertwiner. A nontrivial Cartan/base transport is necessary. This is an exact local obstruction, not a knot example or a claim that all possible source/base extensions are impossible. ## 4. The complete source cancels the nongeometric bulk terms Let beta be any fixed b_strand-strand braid closing to a knot, with writhe w and kappa_D=w-b_strand+1. This integer is even. Let n=N-1 and let `sum_closed i` denote the initial closed-strand index sum. Restoring the exact common Cartan line, auxiliary root pivot `K^(1-N)`, root-compatible twist, and the original cut 1/N gives the literal array weight W_aux=(1/N)x^(n kappa_D) Q^(n sum_closed i) product_crossings r_sign. (11) To verify (11), the product of common crossing scalars and the inverse zero-framing twist is x^(nw). Each closed pivot is `x^(-n)Q^(n i)`. Their product gives (11). Thus no isolated Cartan scalar or numerical ideal-point multiplier was removed. For the color path versus root path in (1), the prefactor x^(n kappa_D) has ratio 1+O(1/N), while the Q prefactor has ratio `exp[ca sum_closed(i/N)](1+O(1/N))`. The genuine ordinary integral cap/twist is not this frozen root auxiliary source. Their exact adapter, proved in [the integral-source audit](integral_color_source_detour_audit.md), is W_aux,col/W_int,col =q_col^(Nn kappa_D)(Q_col^N)^(sum_closed i). (12) Its root value is one by knot parity. Its whole normal limit is `exp{ca[kappa_D/2+sum_closed(i/N)]}`. Consequently the original pivot-dependent position terms cancel, and (7) gives W_int,col/W_aux,root =exp{a B_beta(flow)}(1+O(1/N)), B_beta=sum_crossings B_sign-c kappa_D/2. (13) This is uniform for every fixed word on a common compact interior flow chart. Every original projection is retained; on the two actual walls the finite head is respectively the genuine quotient or submodule. The common-Verma excursion factor delta*w vanishes on both paths. External full modified dimensions, if one passes from reduced to full states, remain their specified separate factors, as in the regular-profile and Gamma-source notes. Equation (13) is an actual whole-array insertion comparison. It does not interchange the finite sum with a limit and does not bound the contribution of flows outside that compact chart. ## 5. The insertion is the Euler derivative minus the actual action Choose a marked primitive L(x)=integral_0^x Log(1-exp(cy))dy. Its logarithmic singularity at zero is integrable. Consistent branch changes add linear terms. Integration by parts gives F(x)=x L'(x)-L(x). (14) The leading stripped log-weights per N are A_+=-c(u+v)/2+c[uv+(u-v)t-t^2/2] +L(v+t)-L(v)-L(t)+L(t-u)-L(-u), A_-=c(u+v-t)/2-cuv +L(u+t)-L(u)-L(t)+L(t-v)-L(-v). (15) The signs in these linear terms follow directly from the marked Log x=c/2+O(1/N) and the actual `(-1)^k` in (2). Let E be the Euler field in these scaled position/transfer variables. Equations (6) and (14) prove B_sign=(E-1)A_sign. (16) For the whole root array (11), the leading log-weight per N is A_beta=sum_crossings A_sign +c kappa_D/2+c sum_closed(i/N). (17) The initial closed positions and all intermediate positions are homogeneous integral-linear functions of the actual free flow coordinates: follow the one braid-permutation cycle from the cut. Therefore the free-flow Euler field gives exactly B_beta=(E-1)A_beta. (18) The constant `c kappa_D/2` in (17) must be kept. Its exponential at complete integer N is one, but its Euler contribution is exactly the nontrivial normal term in (13). Resetting it would destroy the whole comparison. ## 6. The actual marked geometric block has a universal normal action factor On the existing regular actual critical chart choose the marked linear flattening so `d A_flat=0` at the chosen geometric point. Subtracting an integral linear character does not change `(E-1)A_beta`. Thus (18) gives there B_beta|_crit=-A_flat|_crit=-S_geo/c. (19) Here S_geo is the marked Log Q action of the actual state, with its original Bloch-regulator and source signs. Equations (13) and (19) give the leading formal geometric-block comparison block_int,col/block_aux,root has normal multiplier exp(-a S_geo/c). (20) The interpretation of (20) is precise. The finite-array uniform proof is on the real bulk charts (4). At the complex geometric point use the already constructed actual local proper-ratio/WKB branch and its analytic marked continuation. The two phases have the same leading critical scheme and transverse Hessian; (13) inserts the nonzero amplitude `exp(a B_beta)`. Ordinary nondegenerate transverse Gaussian contraction therefore evaluates its leading multiplier at the critical point, giving (20). The two framing directions remain external as in the partial support theorem. The marked action is constant along this critical framing torsor, so the factor is independent of that framing. This is a formal local block assertion, not an analytic continuation of the finite sum inferred from real lattice estimates. In the recorded geometric Log Q convention `Re(S_geo/c)=Vol/(2pi)`. For real a the modulus of (20) is therefore `exp[-a Vol/(2pi)]`, without a new adjustable Cartan or ideal-point scalar. The exact Gamma half-source remains necessary at the framing and resonance boundaries. Its zeros are not supplied by the nonvanishing exponential (20). No selected global geometric contribution, endpoint/carry cancellation, full normal-profile identity, or volume limit is proved by this block comparison. ## 7. Audit [audit_quantum_normal_bulk_response.py](../experiments/audit_quantum_normal_bulk_response.py) and its [results](../experiments/quantum_normal_bulk_response_results.json) evaluate the literal finite crossing products at 85-digit precision for N=16 through 256 and compact real/complex normal parameters. They check both signs, the original common Cartan line, and the complete source/framing cancellation for several even knot-parity values of kappa_D. They also check the exact diagonal obstruction at N=2,3,5,16 and the marked Euler/dilog primitive on positive and negative bulk intervals. These checks confirm the formulas and their O(1/N) error scale. The uniform proof is the Taylor/Riemann argument in Section 2; the arbitrary-word source cancellation is exact (11)--(12). No knot-specific example or selected-sum asymptotic is used.

title: Uniform comparison of the geometric Gaussian and holonomy density lines
text: # Uniform comparison of the geometric Gaussian and holonomy density lines Research note, 27 October 2026. This closes the variable principal determinant comparison previously checked for 4_1 and 5_2. The argument uses the actual local mixed-Hessian amplitudes, an explicit endpoint cut complex, and a telescoping canonical moment-map formula. It works for an arbitrary knot braid and any regular nondegenerate critical representation in the stated chart. No bound on bridge number or crossing word, and no published torsion identity, is assumed. This is a local principal-density theorem. The base-only quantum normalization line, square-root phases, integral source lattice and selected finite period remain the original ones. This does not prove their global geometric period pairing or the volume conjecture. ## 1. Statement and the exact scope Use the original balanced phase coordinates q_j=Log A_j, P_j=Log p_j, with Omega=sum_j dq_j wedge dP_j. Let beta be a b-strand braid with m crossings whose closure is a knot. Write F for its canonical map, also the actual Hurwitz map after the already proved prefix/Gauss coordinate transformation. At its chosen fixed representation suppose the holonomy complex is acyclic: 0 -> sl_2 --A--> V --D--> V --M--> sl_2 -> 0, D=dF-I, M(v)=dP(v)P^(-1), P=H_b...H_1. (1.1) All actual crossing shape factors and chart denominators are units. Thus ker D=im A, and A is injective. Let T_beta be the determinant ratio det[A,V_c]/det[D V_c,W], with M W=I, as in the existing note. On the actual inverse-eigenflag framing chart use F_M(r,s)=[r 1-r;s -kappa-s], kappa=M_mer-M_mer^(-1), Delta=s+kappa*r, K_1=-(M_mer+s), Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[Delta(M_mer+s)]. (1.2) Here M_mer denotes the meridian eigenvalue; the roman M in (1.1) is the product differential. The distinction is kept below. Let Omega_raw be the squared-coordinate-normalized variable Gaussian two-form from the actual coefficient phase, with denominator det(-H_perp) and all variable amplitude factors retained. Its parity-normalized version is Omega_beta^2=(-1)^(b-1)Omega_raw^2, the convention used in the two prototype audits. **Principal-density theorem.** Under these explicit regularity hypotheses, as a rational identity on the entire framing chart, Omega_beta^2=-(T_beta/2) Omega_cut^2. (1.3) Equivalently the unnormalized variable square is Omega_raw^2=(-1)^b (T_beta/2)Omega_cut^2. Thus the presentation parity is explicit; it has not been suppressed as a harmless numerical factor or assigned to an unknown quantum phase. The proof below does not identify a square-root phase or evaluate a base-only compact quantum product at a root. Those data are separate marked normalization lines, just as in the prototype. ## 2. The actual cut removes precisely one conjugation direction Let beta_0=sum_j dq_j. Since product Gauss decomposition gives P_11=product_j K_j and A_j=x/K_j at fixed meridian, beta_0=-dP_11/P_11. (2.1) The canonical braid map preserves beta_0. Write P=[a b;c d], a!=0. In the ordered sl_2 basis (h,e,f), with matrices h=diag(1,-1), e=E_12, f=E_21, (2.1) becomes beta_0=b_0 M, b_0=(-1,-c/a,0). (2.2) Let lambda=dLog p_1 be the actual cut momentum covector at p_1=1. The cut meridian has K_1=-(M_mer+s), e_1=kappa+s and x=-M_mer; hence lambda(delta G_1)=(delta K_1+delta e_1)/(kappa+s). For xi=[u v;w -u], delta G_1=[xi,G_1]. Since G_1(1,1)^t=x^(-1)(1,1)^t, direct multiplication gives lambda(A xi)=2u+v-w=:ell(xi). (2.3) This row is independent of braid, meridian and framing. Its kernel is the Lie algebra fixing the selected projective eigenflag 1. The endpoint cut differential is the square map D_cut: V -> ker(beta_0) direct_sum k, v |-> (D v,lambda(v)). (2.4) Its kernel is A ker ell, of dimension two. Its cokernel is ker b_0, via (w,z)->M w. This is exactly the retained framing and co-source; the three product dependencies have not been discarded. Indeed D v=f, lambda(v)=c has a solution precisely when M f=0 (with f already in ker beta_0). Choose a right inverse R_D for D onto ker M, and u in sl_2 with ell(u)=1. A specified solution is v=R_D f+A u[c-lambda(R_D f)], (2.5) unique modulo A ker ell. A co-source eta evaluates it as eta(R_D f)+eta(Au)[c-lambda(R_D f)] plus its value on the retained two framing directions. Thus the cut source and the affine dual constant are explicit, even before any Gaussian or geometric specialization. ## 3. Exact torsion of the endpoint cut complex Give ker beta_0 its trailing-normal volume: for beta_0(v_0)=1, vol_(ker beta_0)(w_1,...,w_(n-1)) =vol_V(w_1,...,w_(n-1),v_0), n=2b. Let K be a 3 by 2 basis of ker ell and ell(u)=1. Let Z be a 3 by 2 basis of ker b_0 and b_0(z_0)=1. Use A K as kernel basis and Z as cokernel coordinates of (2.4). Then T_cut(K,Z)=-det[K,u]/det[Z,z_0] * T_beta. (3.1) To prove this, use [A u,V_c] as the complement of A K, and W Z as a lift of the two-dimensional cokernel. The cut images are (0,1) and (D V_c,lambda V_c). Subtract multiples of the first column to remove lambda V_c. Moving (0,1) to the end contributes (-1)^(n-1)=-1. The remaining target determinant is the volume of [D V_c,W Z] in ker beta_0. Adjoining W z_0 identifies this with det[Z,z_0] det[D V_c,W]. The domain determinant is det[K,u] det[A,V_c], proving (3.1). For the natural bases K=(h+2f,e+f), u=e, Z=(e-(c/a)h,f), z_0=-h, both three-dimensional determinants are -1. Thus T_cut(K,Z)=-T_beta. This is a determinant identity with a specified kernel and co-source, not an identification obtained only from equality of critical sets. ## 4. A canonical moment-map identity which telescopes at every strand Use physical coordinates G_j=[K_j e_j;K_j f_j K_j^(-1)+e_j f_j], K_j+K_j^(-1)+e_j f_j=x+x^(-1), Omega=-sum_j dK_j wedge de_j/(K_j e_j). (4.1) The second expression is exactly the actual balanced canonical form. Let P_j=H_j...H_1=[a_j b_j;c_j d_j], with P_0=I. The prefix Gauss map gives the elementary recurrences a_j=K_j a_(j-1), b_j=K_j b_(j-1)+e_j, c_j=K_j(c_(j-1)+f_j). (4.2) For simultaneous conjugation xi=[u v;w -u], its induced physical action on G_j is commutation by the traceless part of zeta_j=[u+(v c_(j-1)+w b_(j-1))/(2a_(j-1)) v/a_(j-1); w/a_(j-1) -u-(v c_(j-1)+w b_(j-1))/(2a_(j-1))]. This follows by differentiating B_-(P)=[1 0;-P_21 P_11] and G_j=B_-(P_(j-1)) H_j B_-(P_(j-1))^(-1). A scalar trace term does not affect the commutator. For local traceless coefficients (U,V,W), contraction of (4.1) is iota_[zeta,G] Omega_j =2U dK/K+V(df+f dK/K)+W de/K. (4.3) Here df=(K^(-2)-1)dK/e-f de/e follows from the fixed trace. After inserting zeta_j, its coefficient of v is dc_j/a_j-dc_(j-1)/a_(j-1); its coefficient of w is db_j/a_j-db_(j-1)/a_(j-1). Its coefficient of u is 2dLog K_j. The sums telescope, giving the uniform identity iota_(A xi) Omega=(2u da+v dc+w db)/a. (4.4) In right-trivialized product coordinates M=(delta P)P^(-1), equation (4.4) is A^t Omega=R(P) M, R(P)=[2 2c/a 0;-c/a 0 1;b/a d/a 0], det R(P)=-2/a^2. (4.5) In particular it is independent of crossing number and presentation. The factor two is fixed by the h=diag(1,-1) convention; it is not an adjustable normalization of torsion. For the bases K,Z in Section 3, K^t R Z=[2/a^2 0;(c/a)^2+1/a^2 1], det(K^t R Z)=2/a^2. (4.6) The canonical self-dual cokernel associated to a tangent v in ker D_cut is (w,z)->Omega(v,w). It is well-defined and annihilates the cut image because F is symplectic and Fv=v. It is injective: Omega(v,ker beta_0)=0 would force v proportional to the Hamiltonian vector of beta_0, which is -A h/2 and has nonzero lambda value. Thus (4.6) gives the exact conversion from the product co-source to this canonical Gaussian co-source. ## 5. Canonical generating families give the same determinant line This section proves the Gaussian-to-endpoint comparison, retaining the source/cokernel pairing. It applies to the actual phase but is pure linear algebra of its quadratic part. At crossing t, write its generating function S_t(a,u,tau), where a is the first input position, u the first output position, and tau is the conserved sum of the two positions. The actual transfer coordinate is c_t with u=b+sign(t)c_t. Its mixed Hessian is V_t=(S_t)_(au), the exact unit computed from the actual coefficients. The graph equations are P_1=P_2-(S_t)_a, P'_2=P_2+(S_t)_tau, P'_1=P'_2+(S_t)_u. (5.1) They imply dS_t=P'_1 dq'_1+P'_2 dq'_2-P_1 dq_1-P_2 dq_2. For the whole word, let q be the b initial positions and c the m transfers. The final positions are q_out=P_perm q+R c, where P_perm is the braid permutation matrix and R is integral. Let S(q,c) be the sum of the local generating phases. If p denotes final momentum, the generating family gives p_in=P_perm^t p-S_q, r_int=S_c-R^t p=0. (5.2) At fixed q the Jacobian in (c,p) is J_in=[-S_qc P_perm^t;S_cc -R^t]. (5.3) It is invertible and det J_in=(-1)^(m(b-1)) product_t V_t. (5.4) For a direct induction append one crossing. Changing its variables (c_new,p_out) into (p_old,r_new) leaves the old equations unchanged. On its two active strands, at fixed input positions, the active 3 by 3 Jacobian has rows [-sign*(V+S_tau,u) 0 1], [-sign*(S_uu+S_tau,u) 1 0], [S_uu -sign sign]. Its determinant is -V. The b-2 unchanged momenta give the full determinant (-1)^(b-1)V. Starting from the empty word proves (5.4). Close positions 2,...,b. The closure matrix C on (q,c) has rank b-1. Its cofactor on q_2,...,q_b is P_perm-I with one row/column removed, of determinant +/-1 because the knot permutation is one cycle. This supplies the actual integral free coordinates z=(q_1,c), of dimension d=m+1. Denote the restricted phase Hessian by H. Let L_cut be the coordinate matrix of (2.4), with rows (q_out-q)_2,...,(q_out-q)_b, (p_out-p_in)_1,...,(p_out-p_in)_b, (p_in)_1. (5.5) The endpoint target is expressed in these coordinates. Its trailing- normal volume is the negative of their coordinate volume: the basis (e_qj-e_q1 for j>1, all e_pj) followed by e_q1 has determinant -1. For regular H, exact Jacobian elimination gives det L_cut=(-1)^(m+b-1) det H/product V_t =det H/product V_t. (5.6) Here is the sign calculation. On (q,c,p), use output equations (position closure, p_out-p_in, (p_in)_1, r_int). Their determinant is det L_cut det J_in, by the change to (q,p_in,r_int). Adding its first momentum-difference row to the cut row replaces (p_in)_1 by p_1. Reordering to (S_q-C_q^t rho,S_c-C_c^t rho, closure,p_1) has sign (-1)^(mb), where rho=(p_2,...,p_b). Eliminating p_1 has sign (-1)^(b-1). The remaining bordered matrix is [S'' -C^t;C 0]. The integral cofactor changes it, with determinant one squared, to H plus b-1 blocks [0 -1;1 0], each determinant one. This proves the first equality of (5.6). Knot parity m=b-1 mod 2 gives the second equality. ### The rank-two kernel and its co-source are also matched For a symmetric H with kernel basis B (the actual derivatives in r,s), define its torsion using cokernel rows B^t. It is T_H=det(B_chi)^2/det H_perp, (5.7) where chi is any two coordinates with invertible B_chi. This follows by adjoining the other coordinate columns as a complement and using a right inverse of B^t. It is independent of chi. The kernel map to the endpoint is explicit. Put w=(q,c)=E z for the integral closed-flow embedding. For B in ker H solve uniquely C^t rho=S'' E B, and send B to v=(q, p), with p_1=0 and p_j=rho_j for j>1. The q part is the initial-position part of E B. These equations give p_in=p_out, and yield exactly the kernel of L_cut. Thus the kernel uses the same r,s framing, not a rescaled substitute. To verify the cokernel, perturb the generating phase by epsilon f, where f is any quadratic form in the free closed-flow coordinates, extended as a quadratic form in (q,c). The position map and closure matrix stay unchanged, so total-position conservation and beta_0 are preserved. Differentiating the generating identity in (5.1) gives on two cut-fixed kernel tangents u,v Omega(u,(partial_epsilon F)v) =Hess(f)(B_u,B_v). (5.8) An explicit equation check fixes the sign without a boundary-form convention. At fixed input tangent v, write the internal and final- momentum variations as (tau,pi). Differentiating (5.2) gives P_perm^t pi-S_qc tau=f_q(B_v), S_cc tau-R^t pi=-f_c(B_v). Pair the first equation with q_u and subtract the second paired with c_u. Position closure gives P_perm q_u+R c_u=q_u, while the tangent internal equation gives q_u^t S_qc+c_u^t S_cc=p_u^t R. The resulting left side is q_u^t pi-p_u^t R tau=Omega(u,(partial_epsilon F)v); the right side is B_u^t Hess(f) B_v. This proves (5.8) with its positive sign and its specified kernel/co-source identification. Choose f nondegenerate on the two-dimensional kernel. In the leading epsilon^2 determinant coefficient, (5.8) is precisely the pairing used for both Hessian cokernel B^t and endpoint cokernel Omega(u,-). The unit J_in(epsilon) contributes only its constant determinant. The negative endpoint target volume in (5.5) and (5.6) therefore give (product_t V_t) T_H=-T_cut^Omega(r,s). (5.9) No limiting convergence is involved: this is extraction of the leading coefficient of a finite determinant polynomial (or a regular rational matrix germ). It also verifies the kernel/cokernel map, which cannot be inferred merely from det H=det L_cut=0 on a Morse--Bott locus. ## 6. The universal factor is -1/2 For the actual framing F_M(r,s), its infinitesimal conjugation columns are the traceless parts of -F_M^(-1)partial_r F_M and -F_M^(-1)partial_s F_M. In the fixed basis K=(h+2f,e+f) their 2 by 2 coefficient matrix has determinant det C_frame=-1/(2Delta). (6.1) This is direct multiplication of the displayed F_M. The framing changes both the kernel and its canonical self-dual cokernel, so it contributes det(C_frame)^2. Combining (3.1), (4.6) and (6.1) gives T_cut^Omega(r,s) =-T_beta * (2/a^2)/(4Delta^2) =-T_beta/(2a^2 Delta^2). (6.2) The original actual amplitude identity already proved in the [principal-density note](actual_cut_residue_and_principal_density.md) is a_beta^2=(product_(j=2)^b K_j^2) product_t V_t, product_(j=2)^b K_j^2=a^2/K_1^2. (6.3) Its Gaussian denominator is det(-H_perp), so Omega_raw^2=(-1)^(m-1) a_beta^2 T_H. Insert (5.9), then normalize by (-1)^(b-1). Because m+b-1 is even, Omega_beta^2=(a^2/K_1^2) T_cut^Omega(r,s) =-T_beta/(2Delta^2 K_1^2) (dr wedge ds)^2 =-(T_beta/2) Omega_cut^2. This proves (1.3) uniformly. Every scalar comes from an explicit Jacobian, source constraint or original pivotal factor. The argument does not set a peripheral factor to its value before forming these maps, and does not choose a square-root sign from an identity of squares. ## 7. Remaining quantum assertion The local geometric principal coefficient is now the same holonomy torsion/cut density for every regular knot braid, beyond the two prototype fields. The selected finite quantum period still has to be pushed to this normal block with its actual lattice, period mark and base-only normalization. A principal-density identity does not prove that the selected global cycle has a nonzero component there, or give its archimedean norm across levels. Those remain the volume theorem. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_uniform_cut_density_comparison.py). [Results](../experiments/uniform_cut_density_comparison_results.json).

title: The complete quantum period as a marked fibre after ramified Weyl descent
text: # The complete quantum period as a marked fibre after ramified Weyl descent Research note, 26 October 2026. The complete Kashaev value, previously written as a first normal derivative, is an ordinary linear evaluation on a specified descended lattice. This is an exact algebraic construction at each level, with the first-order information retained in the lattice. It is not an asymptotic argument or an identification with the Bloch regulator. A comparison that fixes only the ordinary root fibre can still change the period; an explicit example below exhibits the missing marking. The input is the [actual Weyl theorem](actual_weyl_descent.md), including the primitive normal operator's half-root and sign. The [actual peripheral calculation](actual_peripheral_fusion.md) fixes its boundary lattice. No different state or quantization is introduced. ## 1. The actual orbit and its two involutions Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, Y=M^2, and the central coordinate U=Y^N. The actual normal state is v_N(Y)=(Y-1)F_N(Y). At a regular operator specialization write B=sum_j b_j(q,Y)T^j, T Y=QY T, B J=J' B, J=-Y R, J'=sigma*q^(dm)*Y^m*T^d R, R h(Y)=h(Y^(-1)), sigma in {1,-1}, m in Z. (1.1) These quantum symmetries are proved for the actual primitive minimal normal operator. The state satisfies J v_N=v_N. All statements below also apply to a specified nonminimal operator with the checked same kind of intertwiner; their rank conclusions must be checked separately. Near U=1 choose the algebraic roots Y_r(U)=Q^r U^(1/N), 0<=r<N, U^(1/N)|_(U=1)=1. Let B_N(U) be the matrix acting on the orbit values. Its entries are (B_N(U))_(r,r+j)=b_j(q,Q^r U^(1/N)), (1.2) with coincident columns added modulo N. The quantum involutions on orbit vectors act semilinearly over U->U^(-1): (J_U h)(U)=U^(1/N)*J_0*h(U^(-1)), (J'_U h)(U)=U^(m/N)*J'_0*h(U^(-1)), (J_0)_(r,-r)=-Q^r, (J'_0)_(r,-r-d)=sigma*q^(dm)*Q^(mr). (1.3) All indices are modulo N. Direct multiplication gives J_0^2=J'_0^2=I. They are unitary in the orbit metric. This includes even levels; the q^(dm) in the second involution has not been replaced by a guessed Q-power. The semilinear identity corresponding to (1.1) is B_N(U) U^(1/N) J_0 =U^(m/N) J'_0 B_N(U^(-1)). (1.4) ## 2. Linearizing the ramification, with explicit algebraic frames Use the marked rational parameter z=(U-1)/(U+1), U=(1+z)/(1-z), s=z^2. Then U inversion is exactly z->-z. The completed local rings are R_z=C[[z]] and R_s=C[[s]]. Choose the units Gamma_in=U^(1/(2N)), Gamma_out=U^(m/(2N)), both equal to one at z=0. They are algebraic roots, unramified there. Thus the formal calculation may equally be performed on an etale local algebraic cover with these specified roots. Set x_N=Gamma_in^(-1)*v_N, B_tilde=Gamma_out^(-1)*B_N*Gamma_in =U^((1-m)/(2N))*B_N. Equations (1.3)--(1.4) become x_N(z)=J_0 x_N(-z), B_tilde(z)J_0=J'_0 B_tilde(-z). (2.1) This is an explicit linearization, rather than a presumed unramified descent theorem. Write E_+,E_- for the two eigenspaces of J_0 and E'_+,E'_- for those of J'_0. ## 3. The descended lattice retains the negative first coefficient An invariant vector has a unique form x(z)=a(s)+z b(s), a(s) in R_s E_+, b(s) in R_s E_-. Consequently its invariant lattice is the free R_s-module Lambda_in=R_s E_+ direct-sum z R_s E_-. (3.1) The symbol z e_- is a generator of the second summand as an R_s-module. Its class is nonzero in Lambda_in/s Lambda_in, even though its value as a function at z=0 is zero. There is the exact special-fibre sequence 0 -> E_- -> Lambda_in/s Lambda_in -> E_+ -> 0. (3.2) The last map records the ordinary value a(0); the kernel records the coefficient b(0). Evaluating first at z=0 and then taking the J_0 invariants retains only E_+ and discards that kernel. The two operations are therefore different. There is also an intrinsic filtration. The invariants of z times the original lattice are F_(1/2)Lambda_in=s R_s E_+ direct-sum z R_s E_-. Its special fibre is the subspace E_- in (3.2). This is the elementary weight-one-half parabolic structure of the ramified double cover. The output lattice is constructed identically using E'_+,E'_-. ### The descended actual operator Use constant eigenframes for the four eigenspaces. Equation (2.1) forces the exact block form B_tilde(z)=[ A(s) z C(s) ] [ z D(s) E(s) ]. Therefore its map on the invariant lattices is B_desc(s)=[ A(s) s C(s) ] [ D(s) E(s) ], B_desc(0)=[ A(0) 0 ] [ D(0) E(0) ]. (3.3) The blocks may be rectangular; the total matrix is N by N. If B_N(U)=B_0+(U-1)B_1+..., then B_tilde_z(0)=2B_1+(1-m)B_0/N. (3.4) Thus D(0) is its block from E_+ to E'_-. The negative block E(0) is exactly B_0 restricted from E_- to E'_-, the operator previously called B_-. This construction is functorial. If an equivariant matrix G(z) has the analogous blocks, its descended matrix is obtained by the same replacement of z C by s C and z D by D. Substitution shows (G_1 G_2)_desc=(G_1)_desc (G_2)_desc. In particular an invertible equivariant lattice comparison descends to an invertible comparison preserving the filtration in (3.2). This proves the needed elementary descent directly. ## 4. The original Kashaev value is a special-fibre evaluation For the actual state, let (a_0,b_0) be the class of x_N in the fibre of (3.1). The ordinary part is already specified: a_0=v_0, (v_0)_r=(Q^r-1)C_r(q), 1<=r<N, (v_0)_0=0, (a_0)_1/(Q-1)=1. (4.1) The last equality is the fixed ordinary-color anchor. It shows that the actual section is primitive at the branch point; it has not been multiplied by a vanishing central factor. Let e_0 be the complete-coordinate vector. It lies in E_-. Since dU/dz=2 at zero and Gamma_in,z(0)=1/N, differentiating the explicit algebraic frame gives x_N,z(0)=2v_N,U(1)-v_0/N=b_0, K_N=F_N(1)=(N/2)*e_0^* b_0, N_N(1)=(eta_N/2)*e_0^* b_0, eta_N=i^(N+3). (4.2) The final equation is the complete full ADO period. Thus its value is an ordinary linear functional on a specified algebraic fibre. The derivative notation is no longer needed to evaluate it once the descended lattice is retained. Its first-order data have not been removed; they are the second summand in that fibre. This statement uses no kernel-rank or sector-injectivity hypothesis. It applies to the actual state for every knot and N. At fixed N, the state, its frames, a(s), b(s), and this evaluation are algebraic. Their presentations vary with N; this is not a fixed-degree algebraic normalization across all levels or a growth bound. ### The affine source is a lifting equation in the same fibre The actual equation descends to A(0)a_0=0, E(0)b_0=-D(0)a_0. (4.3) For this particular a_0, (3.4) and B_0 a_0=0 give D(0)a_0=2B_1 a_0. Thus the second equation is exactly the preceding normal-source equation, with its reflection sector built into the algebraic fibre. Its set of lifts b_0, if nonempty, is an affine torsor under ker E(0). The actual state supplies a point. If E(0) is injective, this point and the period are determined by the source alone. More generally the scalar is unique when e_0^* annihilates ker E(0). These are the previous precise conditions; ramified descent does not prove them automatically. When the generic kernel over C((s)) is a line, its saturated intersection with Lambda_in is a free rank-one R_s-module. The actual section (4.1) generates it, because its anchor is a unit. This supplies a pointed line whose fibre and (4.2) remain defined even if B_desc(0) itself has an extra kernel. One must specialize the saturated kernel lattice, rather than replace it by the possibly larger kernel of the special matrix. Generic rank one is an additional hypothesis for this operator-only description; the actual state-defined line does not require it. The subsequent [torsion initial-rank theorem](torsion_initial_rank.md) supplies a finite sufficient condition for this generic line. A rational-coefficient actual annihilator with exactly one occupied binomial torsion curve in its initial form has generic rational rank one at all sufficiently large levels, even with non-toric remaining factors. Its primitive minimal actual right factor inherits the rank. This is an operator certificate, not a claim that every knot operator satisfies it; the special-sector rank and marked regulator norm remain additional questions. ## 5. Identity on the ordinary fibre does not fix this marking There is a sharp two-dimensional example. Use J_0=diag(1,-1), B_tilde(z)=[ 0 0 ], x(z)=(1,-z)^t. [ z 1 ] Then B_tilde*x=0 and the equivariance (2.1) holds. The descended operator is [[0,0],[1,1]], and the descended fibre vector is (1,-1). Its second coordinate is the retained normal period. For any c, the equivariant invertible frame change G(z)=[ 1 0 ], G(0)=I, [ cz 1 ] descends to G_desc(0)=[[1,0],[c,1]]. It sends that fibre vector to (1,c-1). Hence a frame change that is identity on the ordinary root fibre, and preserves the lattice and its filtration, can change the normal period by an arbitrary scalar. Transporting the period functional along with G restores its value; omitting that transport loses precisely the extra marking. This is an algebraic example about comparisons, not a knot counterexample. It shows why ordinary-fibre agreement or a normalization of a determinant does not alone identify the selected source period. ## 6. A parity obstruction to the optional injectivity condition The dimensions of the domain sectors are dim E_-=(N+1)/2 if N is odd, N/2 if N is even, tr J_0=-1 if N is odd, 0 if N is even. The range trace, including the full half-root, is exactly tr J'_0=sum_(0<=r<N, 2r+d=0 mod N) sigma*(-1)^(m*(d+2r)/N). (6.1) Only fixed coordinates contribute to the trace, and q^N=-1 gives the displayed sign. Consequently E(0):E_->E'_- cannot be injective whenever tr J'_0>tr J_0. For even N this obstruction occurs precisely when d and m are even and sigma=+1. For odd N>d, it occurs precisely when sigma*(-1)^m=+1 for odd d, or sigma=+1 for even d. The general formula (6.1) also covers the finitely many smaller levels. These are diagnostics for the proposed first-order inversion, not restrictions already proved for every primitive knot operator. If the obstruction occurs, one must keep the saturated kernel and the further source/lifting data; assuming sector injectivity would be false for that signature. ## 7. Metric and the remaining regulator comparison Choose orthonormal constant frames of E_+,E_-. Along |U|=1 the specified Gamma_in is unitary. Orthogonality then gives exactly ||v_N(U)||^2=||a(s)||^2+|z|^2||b(s)||^2. (7.1) The regular metric on the descended fibre records the coefficients as ||a_0||^2+||b_0||^2. This is a renormalization of the vanishing negative-weight part; it is not the result of setting z=0 in the original orbit norm. The Kashaev functional has norm N/2, and the full ADO functional has norm 1/2. Neither gives a lower bound on its overlap with the actual vector. The specified functional remains essential. The positive triangulation and [actual classical action](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md) already supply the marked Bloch period with norm logarithm 2Vol/pi. The quantum object to compare now has an explicit algebraic special fibre, its filtration, ordinary anchor, and functional (4.2). A geometric comparison must carry that marked source period; matching only an unpointed module or its ordinary fibre does not suffice. The target becomes (4/N)log|e_0^* b_0| -> 2Vol/pi, equivalent to the original statement because e_0^*b_0=2K_N/N. No such norm comparison or nonzero geometric contribution is proved here. Ramified descent identifies the exact object to compare; it does not establish its volume growth. The subsequent [threaded-character theorem](ado_threaded_shadow.md) also fixes interior data on this marked fibre. Every 2N-threaded loop acts by two at U=1 on both a_0 and b_0, and null-homologous loops act by two on the full family. A commutator separates this character from fixed hyperbolic central data. An actual source extension carrying a compatible separating observable can select its horizontal source-one point by a spectral projector, without a further rank assumption; the extension and its marked regulator norm have not been constructed by that criterion alone. ## 8. Coverage and checks The later [Frobenius Verma-period construction](frobenius_verma_period.md) gives an explicit alternate root realization F_N/Delta_K(U), retaining the entire Alexander factor. Reciprocity and Delta_K(1)=1 give 1/Delta_K(U)=1+O(z^2), z=(U-1)/(U+1). Consequently both marked fiber coordinates a_0,b_0 and the complete period functional above are unchanged. This is a specified central gauge, including its polar divisor away from the complete fiber; it is not an arbitrary normalization of the period. This elementary ramified descent belongs to existing parabolic-bundle theory. Coverage includes Borne, [Fibres paraboliques et champ des racines](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0604458), and Biswas--Borne, [Tamely ramified torsors and parabolic bundles](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06733). Only their abstracts and scope were consulted; no descent or torsor proof from either is used above, and no novelty claim is made for the general framework. The concrete contribution here is the explicit linearization and marked fibre for the fixed ADO state, including its half-root, source, metric and parity signatures. [The audit](../experiments/audit_ramified_weyl_fibre.py) checks 18 actual knot cut polynomials through z-order five at levels 2 through 7, recovering their exact complete values without a rank assumption. Eleven tests of the previously certified finite cyclotomic operator check the descended equation through s-order two and its special rank, at even/composite/odd levels through 18. Equality with the actual figure-eight cut is tested only at the seven listed levels through 8; an all-level state equality is not inferred. Another 528 signatures check the trace and dimension formulas, and exact symbolic examples check functoriality and the change-of-frame obstruction in Section 5. [Results](../experiments/ramified_weyl_fibre_results.json) are algebraic diagnostics, not an asymptotic proof.

title: Rational Faddeev periods: folding, gluing support and polar cycles
text: # Rational Faddeev periods: folding, gluing support and polar cycles Research note, 25 October 2026. This gives an exact multidimensional period representative for the rational Gaussian--Faddeev integral class already used in the state notes. It fixes the contour by construction. It also proves why replacing that period by a sum over gluing solutions needs a further polar-cycle theorem. Garoufalidis--Kashaev, [Evaluation of state integrals at rational points](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.6062), Section 2.1, gives the one-dimensional quasi-periodic folding method. The multidimensional identities below are proved directly. Their stated one-dimensional evaluation theorem is not assumed in higher dimensions. This note does not claim a volume theorem for all alternating knots. ## 1. The exact finite translation data Fix a positive integer n, delta=2pi i, omega=exp(2pi i/n), and the audited meromorphic function F_n(z)=Phi_(1/sqrt(n))(z/(2pi sqrt(n))-c_b). Use its exact equations F_n(z+delta)=F_n(z)/(1-exp(z/n)), F_n(z+n delta)=F_n(z)/(1-exp z). (1.1) Let A be an integral symmetric d by d matrix, v_j integral columns, epsilon_j integers, and rho,xi_j arbitrary parameters. Define f_n(z)=exp[i z^T A z/(4pi n)+rho^T z] product_j F_n(v_j^T z+xi_j)^epsilon_j. t_i=exp z_i, a_j=exp xi_j, x_j=exp((v_j^T z+xi_j)/n). For m>=0 put R_m(x)=product_(r=0)^(m-1)(1-omega^r x)^(-1); define the negative m by the inverse translation recurrence. For k in Z^d, direct substitution gives the rational finite-shift ratio r_k=f_n(z+delta k)/f_n(z) =exp[-k^T A z/n-pi i k^T A k/n+2pi i rho^T k] product_j R_(v_j^T k)(x_j)^epsilon_j. (1.2) The exponential of the linear z term is a monomial in exp(z_i/n). The phase in (1.2) uses its stated analytic square-root convention; it is not discarded as an unnamed power of omega. All ratios are rational on the finite root cover after retaining their constant phases. They satisfy r_(k+l)(z)=r_k(z)r_l(z+delta k) exactly. The coarse n-step multiplier is H_i(t)=chi_i product_l t_l^(-A_il) product_j(1-a_j t^v_j)^(-epsilon_j v_ji), chi_i=exp(2pi i n rho_i-pi i n A_ii). (1.3) Every H_i is invariant under all small translations delta e_l. Nothing in (1.3) specializes a peripheral parameter or suppresses a norm factor. The formulae hold at composite n as well. The previous Heisenberg normalization theorems use odd n; folding itself does not. ## 2. This class contains the specified rational literature integrands Take exactly the integrand from `general_annihilator_and_volume.md`, with boundary variable t_0, internal variables t, Q_b=b+b^(-1): I_b=exp[pi i (t_0,t)^T H(t_0,t)+Q_b pi c^T(t_0,t)+C(b)] product_j Phi_b(v_j0 t_0+v_j,int^T t+i Q_b rho_j)^epsilon_j. Here the H,c,v,rho data are rational and fixed as in that note. Choose an integer L clearing the internal exponents so that A=L^2 H_int,int and v'_j=L v_j,int are integral. At b^2=1/n set t=L z/(2pi sqrt(n)), rho'_n=L[(n+1)c_int/(2n)+i t_0 H_int,0/sqrt(n)], xi_j=2pi sqrt(n) v_j0 t_0+2pi i(n+1)(rho_j+1/2), C_n=C(b)+pi i H_00 t_0^2+Q_b pi c_0 t_0. Then, with the literal scaled source contour Gamma_n, J_b(t_0)=exp(C_n) [L/(2pi sqrt(n))]^d integral_(Gamma_n) f_n(z) dz. (2.1) This is an exact change of variables, including its Jacobian. Additional normalizations already attached to J remain attached. No alternative solution of a quantum A-operator has been chosen. For the literature peripheral coordinate Q=exp(-2pi b t_0), the factor exp xi_j is a_j=Q^(-n v_j0) exp[2pi i(n+1)(rho_j+1/2)]. (2.2) Rational powers require the same finite peripheral covers as in the annihilator note. Equations (2.1)--(2.2) retain Q, n, all phases, and the full generic peripheral factors. The central t values in this change of variables are not held fixed along a semiclassical shape path. ## 3. Multidimensional folding with the source contour retained Let T_i act by z->z+delta e_i, and N_i=1+T_i+...+T_i^(n-1). Initially assume no H_i is identically one; see the regularized specialization below for that case. On the translation orbit of f_n, T_i^n=H_i. Since the H_i commute with every T_l, the following is a pointwise meromorphic identity: K_n(z)=sum_(k in {0,...,n-1}^d) f_n(z+delta k) / product_i(1-H_i(t)), product_i(1-T_i) K_n=f_n. (3.1) Its proof is the telescoping equality (1-T_i)N_i=1-T_i^n in each coordinate. This uses the full unnormalized orbit sum; replacing it by an average would introduce the missing factor n^d. Consequently, wherever the indicated corner integrals exist, integral_Gamma f_n dz =sum_(e in {0,1}^d) (-1)^|e| integral_(Gamma+delta e) K_n dz. (3.2) Use the same orientation of dz_1 wedge ... wedge dz_d and the literal scaled source Gamma in (2.1). There is no guess of a preferred Bethe cycle in (3.2). There is also a common-excision version when K_n has new poles on one of those contours. Pull every corner back to Gamma, cut off the same compact parameter domain, and excise the same neighborhoods of the poles of all its corner terms. On that common domain (3.1) gives equality exactly. At each fixed cutoff first remove the common excisions, and then remove the cutoff as in the original integral. This defines a regularized alternating pairing equal to its value. The corner terms must not be regularized independently. If their poles do not meet the contours and the tails vanish, this reduces to the ordinary cubical cycle with vertical caps removed at infinity. The exact rational Faddeev identity factors f_n into algebraic cyclic coefficients and the continuous Heisenberg/dilogarithm period. The same is true of K_n because the finite r_k are rational. Thus (K_n, the folded source contour with its matched excisions) is an explicit period pairing for the chosen realization. It retains the polar-cycle data that the unpointed finite boundary module omits. If a coarse multiplier is identically one, introduce independent auxiliary units u_i near one by multiplying f_n by exp[sum_i Log(u_i)z_i/(n delta)]. Its coarse multipliers become u_i H_i, so (3.1) applies generically. When the source has a holomorphic exponential-moment germ, as proved for the charged state class in the existing notes, the original period is the regular evaluation at u=1 of the whole folded pairing. Individual corner terms need not have a regular value there. These are auxiliary moment parameters, not a replacement definition of the quantum state. ## 4. The algebraic gluing support is a Koszul reduction There is a precise algebraic reason that H_i=1 appears. Let R be a coefficient ring containing the H_i and the required inverse monomials, without inverting 1-H_i. On the free rank-n module V_i with basis e_j, let T_i e_j=e_(j+1), with T_i e_(n-1)=H_i e_0. Then [V_i --(1-T_i)--> V_i] is chain equivalent to [R --(1-H_i)--> R]. (4.1) For a direct proof, use source columns e_0,...,e_(n-2),sum_j e_j, and target columns e_0-e_1,...,e_(n-2)-e_(n-1),e_0. Both changes are unimodular. The map becomes diag(1,...,1,1-H_i). Its unit summands are contractible. No division by n or 1-H_i has been used. Tensoring (4.1) gives a chain equivalence Koszul(1-T_1,...,1-T_d; tensor_i V_i) ~ Koszul(1-H_1,...,1-H_d;R). (4.2) Concretely, write g_i=1-H_i. The degree-zero homology of the right side is exactly R/(g_1,...,g_d), the ordinary algebra of the gluing locus. If the g_i form a regular sequence, all its higher homology vanishes, so the ordinary quotient suffices. Keeping the complex retains the extra information when this regularity fails, for example because some gluing equations are redundant. Singularity of the zero set alone does not imply nonzero higher Koszul homology. Thus Koszul is bookkeeping for the simultaneous constraints and their relations, not an additional knot invariant or a construction of the period torsor. In a regular neighborhood one may work directly with the gluing quotient; the integration cycle and regulator data still have to be supplied separately. At H_i=1, in characteristic zero the average n^(-d)product_i N_i is the projector to the joint invariant line. The algebraic assertion does not imply that an ordinary noncompact contour integral factors through these coinvariants. Moving a contour can cross poles, and multiplying by an internal rational function can introduce poles or destroy decay. In particular one cannot invert 1-H_i and then argue that the period vanishes. The cycle pairing and its polar boundary are essential in this pushforward. ## 5. The local gluing-point residue and its regulator factor Write chi_i=exp eta_i on a chosen logarithmic sheet and put W(z)=-(1/2)z^T A z+eta^T z +sum_j epsilon_j Li_2(a_j exp(v_j^T z)). Then exp(partial_i W)=H_i and Hess W=-A+sum_j epsilon_j xcentral_j/(1-xcentral_j) v_j v_j^T, xcentral_j=a_j exp(v_j^T z). (5.1) This is a uniform, symmetric logarithmic gluing Jacobian. Suppose p is an isolated solution H_i=1, f_n is regular there, and det Hess W is nonzero. The local Leray residue is exactly Res_p K_n dz =(-1)^d [sum_k f_n(p+delta k)]/det Hess W(p). (5.2) Indeed the derivative of (1-H_i) with respect to z_j is -partial_i partial_j W at p. The residue convention is the integral over increasing ordered arguments of (1-H_i), divided by (2pi i)^d. Formula (5.2) fixes the Jacobian and its sign. Singular points need the full local residue algebra rather than an inverse Hessian. Here is the exact regulator content of a summand, without an n-limit. For a logarithmic lift of p, write zeta_j=v_j^T z+xi_j, w_j=Log(1-exp zeta_j), and choose integers k with -Az-sum_j epsilon_j v_j w_j+eta=2pi i k. Choose eta=2pi i n rho-pi i n diag(A) literally, so that rho=diag(A)/2+eta/(2pi i n). The continuous exponent in f_n from the local rational formula is i S/(2pi n), where S=(1/2)z^T A z+sum_j epsilon_j[Li_2(exp zeta_j)+zeta_j w_j]-eta^T z. At p the gluing equation gives S=sum_j epsilon_j[Li_2(exp zeta_j)+(1/2)zeta_j w_j] -(1/2)eta^T z-pi i k^T z +(1/2)sum_j epsilon_j xi_j w_j. (5.3) The omitted algebraic prefactor is explicitly exp(diag(A)^T z/2) product_j(1-exp zeta_j)^epsilon_j /product_j D_n(exp(zeta_j/n))^epsilon_j. Thus the critical-point term contains the Rogers/Heisenberg period, cyclic coefficients, source/peripheral terms and the full Jacobian. It is not just the Bloch norm or just a positive factorial weight. ## 6. A uniform source-pole cancellation criterion The actual divisor orders can be derived without a zero/pole theorem from the literature. F_n is holomorphic and nonzero in 0<Im z<2pi(n+1), by its defining integral. Iterating the n-step equation (1.1) shows that its only zeros and poles are at z=delta ell, ell in Z, and ord_(delta ell) F_n=-floor((ell-1)/n). (6.1) Indeed the points ell=1,...,n lie in the nonvanishing strip. A coarse shift by n reduces the order by one, which proves the formula at every other integer. Every point can be translated into the strip, so there are no additional divisors. Suppose all epsilon_j are positive. Let the source contour be the horizontal plane z=x+i lambda with gamma_j=(v_j^T lambda+Im xi_j)/(2pi) in (0,n+1). For the unit folding tube z=x+i(lambda+2pi s), s in [0,1]^d, each orbit summand has total shifts k+s in [0,n]^d. Put P_j=sum_i max(v_ji,0). Its local F_n pole order in this tube is at most P_j: an encountered integer ell obeys ell<gamma_j+n P_j<n(P_j+1)+1, so (6.1) gives floor((ell-1)/n)<=P_j. With multiplicity epsilon_j the bound is epsilon_j P_j. First assume distinct binomial divisors D_j:1-a_j t^v_j=0 have no common component. At a generic point of D_j away from the remaining zeros of 1-H_i, the order of H_i is -epsilon_j v_ji. Thus product_i(1-H_i)^(-1) has a zero of order epsilon_j P_j, which cancels the source pole of every orbit summand. The same proof allows common components if all their v_j are positive multiples of one primitive vector on that component; the orders then add with the same signs. This is the polar coorientation condition. Consequently K_n has no source-divisor poles in the folding tube, away from its remaining 1-H_i divisors. The assertion is divisorial; on the complement of the latter divisors, normality removes residual codimension-two singularities. It is uniform in d,n and the number of factors. It uses the strict strip inequalities, positive multiplicities, and the stated coorientation, not a knot census. Distinctness of the binomial components is a generic source/peripheral condition when it is not forced to fail by the coefficient data. This criterion is not asserted for every knot realization. Full peripheral parameters must remain available when testing it. Even when source poles cancel, a multivariate cycle-localization and tail argument is still needed before summing only the common H_i=1 residues. Independent auxiliary shifts xi_j -> xi_j+alpha_j make these binomial components distinct generically, after factors with v_j=0 have been retained as external scalars. For finitely many integral vectors, coincidence of components is a finite set of algebraic relations among the a_j. The generic shifted family therefore satisfies the criterion whenever its source strip inequalities persist. If the original charged integral has a holomorphic germ in those shifts, its value is the regular specialization of the whole period. A gluing point of the shifted family can meet the polar boundary in this specialization; its period must not be discarded by evaluating only the open gluing equations of the special fiber. ## 7. A Faddeev counterexample to automatic gluing-point localization For any odd n consider the absolutely convergent period f_n(z)=exp(z/(2n))/(1+exp(z/n))=1/[2cosh(z/(2n))]. It is an exponential times a ratio of the literature functions: f_n(z)=exp(z/(2n)) *Phi_b(z/(2pi sqrt(n))+i b/2) /Phi_b(z/(2pi sqrt(n))-i b/2), b=1/sqrt(n). The audited functional equation proves this identity. Nevertheless H=f_n(z+n delta)/f_n(z)=-1, so there are no H=1 points. Its period is integral_R f_n(z) dz=n pi, (7.1) as follows by exp(z/n)=u and the beta integral, or by the elementary sech integral. The folded kernel is (1/2)sum_(k=0)^(n-1)f_n(z+delta k). In 0<Im z<2pi it has the pole z=pi i from k=(n-1)/2. Its residue is -i n/2, and the contour theorem gives n pi exactly. Inverting the denominator Phi with the audited inversion equation also writes this example using two positive F_n factors: f_n(z)=exp[i pi(2/n-n)/12] exp[-i z^2/(4pi n)] *F_n(z+pi i(n+2))F_n(-z+pi i(n+2)). Both source heights are (n+2)/2 in (0,n+1). But their central divisors are 1+t=0 and 1+t^(-1)=0, the same component with opposite v vectors. Their norm orders cancel. Thus positive factors alone do not suffice; the coorientation hypothesis in Section 6 has a concrete role. This boundary contribution can itself be recovered as a regular generic gluing period. In the positive-pair expression independently shift the two F_n arguments by alpha and beta. Write a=-exp alpha, b=-exp beta. The coarse multiplier and its unique generic gluing root are H(t)=-(t-b)/(1-a t), t_*=(1-b)/(a-1). (7.2) For small generic shifts, the two source divisors are distinct and Section 6 cancels them in K_n. In a fixed small circle about z=pi i there is exactly one remaining pole, at the logarithmic lift of t_*. On the circle the family is holomorphic in the shifts through their zero value, where it equals the unshifted K_n. Its Cauchy integral is therefore a holomorphic germ in alpha,beta. The generic gluing residue has the regular value -i n/2 at alpha=beta=0, although t_* then lands on the removed divisor t=-1. Its corresponding period has value n pi. This is an evaluation of a regular period germ, not a gluing point of the open special fiber. It illustrates concretely why the comparison object must retain boundary/nearby-cycle data. The supplied manuscript makes the analogous distinction in Section 9.4: a boundary character can lose geometric period data that survive on a space retaining the periods or their scale. No assertion that the two period problems are equivalent is being made from that analogy. Thus a genuine Gaussian--Faddeev type period can have a nonzero folded source-pole contribution with no gluing solutions. This is not a counterexample to the volume conjecture or to admissible geometric states; it disproves an unrestricted inference from quasi-periodicity to localization solely on H=1. The pole exclusion must be proved for the chosen state rather than supplied by its boundary algebra. ## 8. The remaining uniform comparison The selected source realization now has the exact folded period (3.2), and the algebraic gluing support and local residues are identified. A finite sum of the residues (5.2) requires proving that this specific folded cycle is homologous to the corresponding sum of local Leray cycles, with no remaining polar or infinity contributions. Its integer coefficients are cycle data, not consequences of Hilbert 90. The finite recoupling/root descent must additionally match this relative period, its measure and its transported cycle. Neither the Koszul equivalence nor the local regulator expression supplies that identification. The quantum norm comparison with the classical boundary period, and its all-alternating scope, remain the objective.

title: The finite cover and the dilogarithm period are parts of one local object
text: # The finite cover and the dilogarithm period are parts of one local object Research note, 25 October 2026. This reconstructs the b^2=1/n case of Garoufalidis--Kashaev, [Evaluation of state integrals at rational points](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.6062), Theorem 1.9. The formula is standard; its proof is supplied here to fix the object and its normalization without adopting that theorem as a premise. It explains which data a proposed algebraic torsor must retain in comparing the finite cyclic construction with the Faddeev state already used here. ## 1. An exact identity, for every positive integer n Set b=1/sqrt(n), c_b=i(b+b^(-1))/2, omega=exp(2pi i/n), and F_n(z)=Phi_b(z/(2pi sqrt(n))-c_b), D_n(X)=product_(j=1)^(n-1)(1-omega^j X)^(j/n). Initially take Re z<0 and 0<Im z<2pi(n+1). Define all logarithms by their convergent series in exp(z/n), with D_n(0)=1. Then exactly F_n(z)= exp[i Li_2(exp z)/(2pi n)] (1-exp z)^(1+i z/(2pi n)) / D_n(exp(z/n)). (1.1) The formula extends by continuation with its recorded branches. The left side is meromorphic in z; arbitrary independent branch choices on the right do not give that same meromorphic function. ## 2. Independent residue proof Start from the independently audited defining integral for Phi. Substitute its integration variable w=sqrt(n)*t. The exponential shift by -c_b cancels the corresponding factors in the two hyperbolic sines, giving log F_n(z)=integral_(R+i0) exp(-i z t/pi)/[(exp(2t)-1)(exp(2nt)-1)] dt/t.
