Its f-image and the convex hull of its three f-vertices lie in a ball of radius L D_R. The geodesic homotopy has length at most 2 L D_R and derivative bounds depending only on R,L. Its volume is at most a finite constant C(R,L). Thus every b_rho in (5) is Haar-integrable. No uniform bound as R tends to infinity is needed. All FOUR ordered regular faces are congruent by orientation-preserving isometries of H^3. Naturality of the chosen parametrization and homotopy, followed by right-Haar invariance, therefore makes their averages equal. The alternating sum in (5) has two plus and two minus signs and averages to zero. Consequently [v_R/Vol(M)] V(rho)=integral c_rho(g) dmu(g). (6) By Section 2, |c_rho(g)|<=v_3. Therefore |V(rho)|<=Vol(M) v_3/v_R. Letting R tend to infinity proves the SHARP bound |V(rho)|<=Vol(M). (7) The proof did not use an unproved equality between an ordinary measure-homology cycle and a fundamental class. Equations (4)-(6) are direct integrals; finite regular face congruence cancels the only straightening error. It also did not need a controlled norm for an exponentially conditioned quantum face frame. ## 4. Apply it to all regular FULL critical values of the actual period Use the actual cotangent/fusion and coupled-cap equations from [the full scalar period](actual_full_psi_scalar_flow_cycle.md), and the exact regulator identity in [the critical-wall calculation](actual_wall_critical_regulator.md). At a regular full critical point Z, the actual crossing/cap equations give a framed representation rho of the knot group. At the complete meridian its peripheral image is boundary-parabolic. Indeed a noncentral parabolic meridian has parabolic centralizer; if the meridian is central in PSL_2, normal generation makes the entire representation trivial. The actual crossing certificate is representation-independent: its finite oriented-chain proof uses the Wirtinger relations, unipotent meridian action, and generic auxiliary region flags, not the geometric embedding. Degenerate developed configurations are normalized to zero, as specified in [the fundamental-cycle proof](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md). Together with (3) it gives sum_j epsilon_j D(A_j)=V(rho). (8) For an interior ray/cut mark, the action has the retained integer form W_m=W+2*pi*i sum_j m_j Log A_j. The proved identity is Im W_m -sum_j epsilon_j D(A_j) =Re Z dot Im(gradient W_m). (9) At a FULL critical point the right side vanishes. The original real phase constants and scalar line are retained in the cited calibration. Equations (7)-(9) therefore prove |Im W_m(Z_critical)|<=Vol(M) (10) for every such regular full critical point, including nongeneric, nongeometric and integer-marked embeddings on that regular chart. No positivity of the individual developed tetrahedra is required. The oversized weak alias-face example is not a counterexample: a maximum on a constrained angle face need not solve the full critical equations of this actual knot representation. ## 5. Regular cap-endpoint stationary values are exactly zero There is a further class of non-full source strata to which the same argument DOES extend. Use the exact coupled interval sources, and write their logarithmic variables as p_c=2*pi*i*s_c. Consider any stationary point of a regular stratum where one or more s_c are fixed at 0 or 1. Require stationarity in ALL remaining variables, including head, Gaussian and interior cap variables. The phase, its logarithmic marks and its physical canonical/Hurwitz maps must remain regular on this stratum. No assertion below applies to an infinite position or an undefined logarithmic shape chart. All ACTION coordinates, including auxiliary fusion positions, must be finite and regular; bounded physical meridian matrices alone do not supply this hypothesis. In (9) the only potentially nonzero gradient entries are now those of endpoint p_c. But Re p_c=0 both at p_c=0 and at p_c=2*pi*i. Their weighted contribution vanishes EXACTLY. Therefore Im W_m=sum_j epsilon_j D(A_j) (11) even though stationarity in these endpoint variables was not imposed. The missing equation partial_(p_c)W=0 would have required the paired position ratio to be one. It is not needed for the following argument. Differentiate the actual source phase in its two adjacent head coordinates, using the input or covector orientation as appropriate. At complete color the two PHYSICAL momenta are p_1=p_c, p_2=2*pi*i-p_c, B_1=exp(p_c), B_2=exp(-p_c). (12) This formula follows from the retained degree d=N-1, whose leading affine charge is one. It uses neither partial_(p_c)W=0 nor the paired position relation z_2=-z_1. At either endpoint, B_1=B_2=1. For finite nonzero physical positions, the actual complete generators K=-B^(-1), f=(1-B)z, e=z^(-1)(B^(-1)-1) give K=-1, e=f=0 and hence G=-I on both incident heads. Their based meridians are also central, so their paired cap product is I regardless of the position ratio. The other stationary equations give the actual Hurwitz transport; the remaining interior caps give their ordinary inverse-meridian relations. Thus these data still define the knot representation. For a ONE-component knot, all oriented meridians are conjugate up to inverse. One central meridian makes every PSL_2 meridian the identity; the Wirtinger generators then make the entire PSL_2 representation trivial. Its volume is zero, as is its marked fundamental Bloch regulator. This last assertion can also be checked without choosing eigenflags of a central matrix: every physical Gauss meridian then has clocks A=B=1 and e=f=0, so C_+=C_-=1 in the original five-argument coefficient symbol. Every one of its Bloch--Wigner arguments is 1 and contributes zero, by the continuous normalization D(1)=0. The exact nine-to-five regulator identity gives the same zero in every regular continuation. Equations (8) and (11) prove Im W_m=0 (13) on every such regular cap-endpoint stationary stratum. The proof allows simultaneous endpoints and any number of remaining interior caps. In charts where centrality forces an atomic degeneration, there is no regular solution; no singular extension is being claimed. The ordinary-cap integrated source can still cancel exactly, as in K_N(Q^(-1))=0. This is a bound on stationary VALUES, not a claim that the corresponding integrated source coefficient is nonzero. ## 6. Exact critical degenerations are safe; arbitrary boundary strata are not covered An EXACT sequence of full regular critical points obeys (10) pointwise even if its coordinates, frames or matrices escape. Every finite limit of its imaginary critical values still lies in [-Vol(M),Vol(M)]. The bounded continuous Bloch--Wigner function also extends to the degenerate shape values 0,1,infinity by zero, so exact critical degenerations do not create a larger regulator value. No compactness of the representation matrices is needed for this statement. An approximate logarithmic gradient tending to zero at infinity is weaker. Equation (9) has the weight Re Z; its error need not vanish unless the weighted residual does. Moreover approximate primitive gluing equations at infinity need not approach the saturated closure of their exact representation scheme. Neither claim follows just from polynomiality or local Zariski rigidity. A singular or escaping cap endpoint, a ray endpoint, or another critical point of a boundary restriction may have fewer equations than a full critical point. Outside Section 5 it cannot be declared a knot representation using (10). The [Markov ray normalization example](actual_markov_ray_normalization_and_pruning.md) further shows why some equal-exponent boundary pieces must first be grouped by exact operator identities rather than assigned a strict gap individually. Thus (10) closes the regular critical-VALUE part of the desired sharp upper bound. To conclude limsup N^(-1)log|K_N|<=Vol(M)/(2*pi), one still needs a source-preserving global stationary/compactification theorem placing every unpruned contributing asymptotic stratum under this bound, or cancelling/eliminating the remaining strata. The present proof does not assert that last theorem. ## 7. A whole-source quantitative cutoff at very deep zero ends There is a separate global tail estimate directly from the EXACT scalar flow cycle. It applies to every fixed original word, before or after a valid normalization-cell pruning. Retain its external line chi_(beta,N) explicitly. Let T_N(delta) denote the sum of the ABSOLUTE integrals over all circle/ray components on which at least one radial coordinate lies in 0<r_j<delta. There are constants C,B,L depending on the fixed word and fixed compact cap paths, but not on N or delta, such that for 0<delta<=1/2, T_N(delta)<=|chi_(beta,N)| C N^B exp(CN) delta(1+|log delta|)^L. (14) Here is the proof. The source-faithful LP radius bound is N^B exp(CN(1+sum|xi|)) product_radial r_j^(-d). The EXACT shifted full-Psi ray measure has modulus sqrt(1+r_j) r_j^(N-1)dr_j/(2*pi). Since d=N-1, the powers cancel exactly. With interval cap sources only a fixed power of 1+sum|log r_j|+sum|xi| remains. In particular this cancellation retains the affine +1; replacing d by N would lose the conclusion. The full-Psi factors on the finitely many fixed outer circles have a coarse uniform bound exp(CN), with a possible harmless fixed power of N. One elementary justification uses the compact finite-product estimate (7b)-(7c) on two vertical logarithmic lines Re z=+/-L away from zero. It extends along those lines through the ends of a full turn, because their nonzero real parts keep the regularized summand away from its other poles. The exact real-axis moduli (10) and top-turn monodromy bound the two horizontal sides. The maximum principle on the intervening rectangle then gives the same exponential bound on every required circle. Lower-half lifts introduce only the retained factor 1-t^N, again at most exp(CN) on a fixed circle. Thus this is a bound for the actual full functions, not an assumed endpoint-uniform small-disk asymptotic. The normalized Gaussian integral of exp(CN sum|xi|-N||xi||^2/2), with a fixed polynomial in |xi|, is bounded by exp(C'N) times a fixed polynomial in N. Finally integral_0^delta(1+|log r|)^L dr <=C_L delta(1+|log delta|)^L. Integrate the other radial variables on (0,1], whose corresponding logarithmic moments are finite; any fixed exterior segments are absorbed in the exp(CN) constant using their retained radial powers. Take the finite union over j. This proves (14), including all original coupled sources and all matched relative components. In particular, with delta_N=exp(-aN), limsup N^(-1)log[T_N(delta_N)/|chi_(beta,N)|] <=C-a. (15) Taking a sufficiently large fixed a makes this tail exponentially small at any prescribed finite scale. This does not prove the sharp upper bound: the retained region r_j>=exp(-aN) still permits logarithmic head coordinates of order N, and layers such as r~1/N remain. The same-volume normalization rays are compatible with (14). Neither fixed-domain compactness nor domination by the regular critical values follows from this cutoff alone. ## 8. Literature coverage only The representation-volume inequality and stronger rigidity statements are established territory; see the abstract of [Francaviglia, Hyperbolic volume of representations of fundamental groups of cusped 3-manifolds](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0305275). The independently supplied argument above is not a novelty claim for that inequality. Its role here is to justify its application to the actual nine-atom period and its retained integer cut marks without assuming a published proof. No proof technique from that paper was used as an input to this derivation.

title: Regular simple cut-wall stationarity is full stationarity
text: # Regular simple cut-wall stationarity is full stationarity 28 October 2026. A regular simple wall of the ACTUAL global radius homotopy has a free radial coordinate. Together with its remaining head angles, Gaussian paths and interior cap paths, its tangent vectors span the full complex tangent space. Therefore complex phase stationarity on this wall is automatically full holomorphic stationarity. On a regular all-pole branch this removes the extra "full critical" hypothesis from the regular simple-wall value bound. This does not identify the original geometric-thimble coefficient. It does not cover simultaneous corners of the one-parameter homotopy, dependent walls, endpoints, nonsmooth flow cells or escaping variables. Nor does a maximum of only the real exponential rate imply the complex stationarity used here. The [audit](../experiments/audit_regular_cut_wall_total_reality.py) and [results](../experiments/regular_cut_wall_total_reality_results.json) verify the implicit radial identity and the exact complex Jacobians, including arbitrary radial dependence of the head radii and the distinction between a free multiwall chart and a one-parameter corner. ## 1. The actual simple-wall radial coordinate is free Use the global head-radius homotopy (4) in [the exact cut-wall pushforward](actual_full_psi_cut_wall_pushforward.md). For a simple ray pole, write T_j=Log t_j=tau+i epsilon*pi, tau=log r, U=Log A_j=a.Z+b.E+i*pi*nu, Z=rho+i theta. (1) Here a is the primitive nonzero integer head-incidence row; E denotes the Gaussian log variables. The original atomic ratio connects two different retained head segments. All other moment and Gaussian parameters are denoted y for the moment. The radii are independent of HEAD ANGLES. On a smooth flow cell set rho_s=(1-s)lambda_0(tau,y)+s lambda_*(y). The pole's real equation is F(s,tau,y)=a.rho_s+Re(b.E)-tau=0. (2) A REGULAR SIMPLE crossing means F_s is nonzero and 0<s<1; all other pole factors are regular on this local stratum. The real implicit function theorem solves s=s(tau,y). Thus tau is a genuinely free local parameter, not a constrained boundary value. In particular a.rho_tau=1. (3) The imaginary pole equation is a.theta+Im(b.E)+pi*nu=epsilon*pi. It leaves n-1 independent head angles. The dependence of lambda_0 on tau and on the other moment radii causes no difficulty: it enters the implicit function and off-diagonal derivatives, while (3) remains exact. ## 2. The unreduced residue chain is maximal totally real Complete a to complex linear head coordinates (U,Y), keeping E as an additional independent coordinate. Let V be a real basis of ker a. On the wall choose theta=theta_0(E)+V phi, phi in R^(n-1), U=tau+i epsilon*pi. (4) Every other moment T_k follows its original circle or ray, with a nonzero tangent derivative; each Gaussian E follows a regular complex path, and each interior cap variable p=2*pi*i*s follows its regular complex path. Order the complex coordinates as (U, T_other, E, p, Y) and the real parameters as (tau, moment parameters, Gaussian parameters, cap parameters, phi). Their complex Jacobian is block triangular. Its diagonal consists of 1, the nonzero moment/Gaussian/cap path derivatives, and i C V, where C is the chosen complementary head-coordinate matrix. The matrix C V is invertible. Thus the Jacobian is NONZERO. All head-radius derivatives in tau or the other base variables occur only in lower off-diagonal blocks. The residue chain is therefore maximal totally real in its complex residue manifold. For a holomorphic phase S on that manifold, dS vanishing on all real tangent directions consequently implies dS=0 on the full complex tangent space. This follows by multiplying its complex derivative row by the invertible Jacobian. It requires stationarity of the COMPLEX phase, not just a stationary real-part envelope. This unreduced statement concerns the phase with independent other moment variables and their Cauchy poles. It does NOT yet identify it with the nine-atom W(A), or infer actual knot holonomy before those other atomic variables are pushed forward. ## 3. The regular all-pole branch gives the actual nine-atom conclusion Now restrict to a regular local branch on which the OTHER atomic moments are pushed to their Cauchy poles, with no additional local wall crossing. In a regular simple cut stratum these other pole arguments are off their negative-ray cuts. Their circle Cauchy reductions can retain the head variables; locally freeze the radius labels at the circle radii while taking these normal residues. Their normal degree is one, but no global thimble-degree claim is made. The remaining cycle has head profile rho(tau,E) independent of the free head angles, with a.rho+Re(b.E)=tau. Its coordinates are now (U,E,p,Y) and its parameters (tau, Gaussian paths, cap paths,phi). The same block-triangular proof gives a nonzero complex Jacobian. Thus an INTERIOR stationary point of the actual wall action W_m on this regular simple-wall chain automatically satisfies gradient W_m=0. (5) Here W_m is the genuine nine-atom action with its integer norm charge, Gaussian and original coupled cap phases. This is precisely the case covered by [the calibrated critical regulator](actual_wall_critical_regulator.md) and [the sharp representation-volume bound](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md). Consequently every such regular simple-wall interior stationary value satisfies |Im W_m|<=Vol(M). (6) No extra independent "full critical" assumption is required for these regular simple interiors. Additional local pole crossings, rank-deficient Cauchy reductions and endpoints are excluded from this inference. ## 4. Several genuinely free independent walls The linear-algebra statement extends if k wall rows form a real rank-k matrix A and the stratum ACTUALLY has k free radial variables tau=(tau_1,...,tau_k), with A.rho+ell(E)=tau, A.theta+arg(E)=constant. Choose n-k remaining angles in ker A. In coordinates consisting of the k logarithmic wall monomials, the Gaussian/cap variables and a complementary head basis, the Jacobian has diagonal blocks I_k, the nonzero path derivatives and i I_(n-k). It is invertible, so restricted complex stationarity is full stationarity there too. Rank A=k ALONE does not establish these free radial parameters in the actual common tube current. A simultaneous k-fold intersection of our SINGLE-parameter radius homotopy imposes k real modulus equations on k radii and the one homotopy parameter. In general this leaves only one free radial combination and k-1 further relations. It is a corner stratum, not the free multiwall chart just proved. Dependent walls, tangential crossings F_s=0, intersections on a flow cell edge, terminal homotopy faces, cap/ray endpoints and escapes still need their own source-preserving resolution. Nothing here deletes any of their original currents. ## 5. Transverse intersections: no extra exact corner residue, but a growth caveat There is a useful exact-current refinement. Suppose k distinct atomic pole divisors meet the homotopy TRANSVERSELY as 2k real equations, at a finite smooth point. Use their complex normal values q_1,...,q_k as real normal coordinates on that homotopy. On a compact patch the form has a smooth numerator divided by q_1...q_k. In a region where all |q_j| are comparable to epsilon, a rounded simultaneous tube boundary has 2k-1 normal real tangent directions. Its pulled-back form scales at most epsilon^(2k-1-k)=epsilon^(k-1). For k>=2 its integral tends to zero at fixed N. On each simple wall, the other transverse factors 1/q_j are locally L1 because their normal directions have two real dimensions. Hence the exact total current can be described by simple-wall residues with these L1 kernels; there is no additional independent transverse corner residue. This argument requires actual real transversality of the restricted pole equations, not just distinct divisors or a claimed independence of the moment labels. This DOES NOT remove transverse intersections from asymptotic growth. Local L1 meromorphic singularities can carry an exponential rate without a full holomorphic critical point. For real a>0 and c, I_N=integral_R^2 exp(N(c-x^2-y^2+i*a*x))/(x+i*y) dxdy =2*pi*i/(N*a) exp(N*c)(1-exp(-N*a^2/4)). (7) The pole is locally L1, and its real normal map (x,y)->x+i*y is transverse. The only regular holomorphic critical value of S(Z)=c-Z_1^2-Z_2^2+i*a*Z_1 is c-a^2/4. On the complex pole divisor Z_1+i Z_2=0 its restriction is c+a Z_2, with NO critical point. Nevertheless (7) has exponential rate c, arising at the real chain's pole intersection. Thus L1 integrability and absence of an independent exact corner term do not give a sharp exponential bound from the regular critical values alone. For a direct proof of (7), use polar coordinates. The angular integral is 2*pi*i J_1(N*a*r), obtained by differentiating the angular definition of J_0. Integration by parts reduces the radial integral to the two-dimensional Gaussian Fourier identity and gives integral_0^infinity exp(-N*r^2)J_1(N*a*r)dr =(1-exp(-N*a^2/4))/(N*a). Everything is absolutely integrable, including the pole. The audit checks the resulting identity independently. This is a LOCAL ANALYTIC countermodel, not a claimed knot-source counterexample. It shows precisely why a further source identity or phase-specific bound is required before eliminating transverse meromorphic intersections from the remaining growth analysis.

title: A regular holonomy-braiding line through the actual ADO color
text: # A regular holonomy-braiding line through the actual ADO color Research note, 26 October 2026. This supplies local quantum data for the [triangulation comparison](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md), continuing the [marked braid calculation](marked_braid_holonomy.md). It constructs the unrestricted quantum holonomy automorphism, a regular splitting module through the actual Kashaev color, and an explicitly anchored intertwiner line. Its restriction to the nilpotent meridian section gives the original zero-framed knot evaluation with its full peripheral factor. It does not construct the global relative source extension or identify its selected period with the Bloch regulator. Holonomy braidings have existing literature coverage; Section 8 records it. The algebra calculations below reconstruct the needed local facts without using a published holonomy-braiding proof. The subsequent [semicyclic carry-braiding theorem](semicyclic_carry_braiding.md) now gives a global explicit formula on E^N=0: its uncheck finite Euler sum retains the wrap phi_2/K_1^N. Four elementary conjugations, the Casimirs and the center powers prove all six generator equations. A common highest-weight flag fixes strict braid coherence without a determinant ambiguity on that locus. The transported center maps are the Frobenius block matrices; their common fixed line gives genuine braid actions on all integral recoupling charts and the original entire scalar cut operator. This is a special reducible-character source, not an extension of that highest-weight argument to E^N!=0 or an identification with the geometric regulator. ## 1. Rational conjugation survives when a universal matrix does not Put q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), N>=2. Use the unrestricted algebra with KE=QE K, KF=Q^(-1)FK, [E,F]=(K-K^(-1))/rho, Delta E=E_1 K_2+E_2, Delta F=F_1+K_1^(-1)F_2. There is no unrolled H on a general cyclic module. To derive rational formulas, first use a generic parameter and the formal series R=D Theta, D=q^(H_1 H_2/2), Theta=sum_(n>=0) c_n (E_1 F_2)^n, c_n=q^(n(n-1)/2)rho^n/[n]_q! . (1.1) Writing P_Q(t)=(t;Q)_infinity as a formal series, elementary coefficient comparison gives Theta=P_Q(q rho^2 E_1 F_2), P_Q(Qt)=P_Q(t)/(1-t). Thus conjugation on generators has rational expressions even though the series (1.1) cannot itself be specialized on general cyclic modules. Set, with the displayed multiplication order, u=q rho^2 E_1 K_1^(-1) K_2 F_2, H=(1-u)^(-1), G=(1-Q^(-1)u)^(-1). The automorphism r is K'_1=K_1(1-Q^(-1)u), K'_2=K_2 H, E'_1=E_1 K_2, F'_2=K_1^(-1)F_2, E'_2=K_1 E_2+E_1-E_1 K_2^2 H, F'_1=F_2+F_1 K_2^(-1)-G K_1^(-2)F_2. (1.2) For K, commute K through P_Q and use its functional equation. E_1 and F_2 commute with Theta, so their images follow from D. For the other two images use r(Delta a)=Delta^op a. This last identity is independently checked from c_(n+1)[n+1]_q=q^n rho c_n, [E,F^n]=[n]_q F^(n-1) (q^(1-n)K-q^(n-1)K^(-1))/rho. Substitution cancels adjacent series coefficients; the F equation is the same calculation with E,F and K,K^(-1) interchanged. No root-level infinite series is used in (1.2). There is an explicit rational inverse. From the primed generators set u=q rho^2 E'_1 F'_2, with H,G as above. Then K_1=K'_1 G, K_2=K'_2(1-u), E_1=E'_1 K_2^(-1), F_2=K_1 F'_2, E_2=K_1^(-1)(E'_2-E_1+E_1 K_2^2 H), F_1=(F'_1-F_2+G K_1^(-2)F_2)K_2. (1.3) These equations also specify the necessary localizations. Here is a direct coherence proof. If AB=QBA, expansion of (A+B)^n gives the ordered Gaussian coefficients and hence Theta(A+B)=Theta(A)Theta(B). After commuting the Cartan factors, the two instances needed are (A,B)=(E_1 K_2 F_3,E_2 F_3) and (E_1 K_2^(-1)F_3,E_1 F_2). They give (Delta tensor id)R=R_13 R_23, (id tensor Delta)R=R_13 R_12. Applying the intertwining identity to the first equation proves R_12 R_13 R_23=R_23 R_13 R_12. Consequently the rational conjugations (1.2) satisfy the corresponding three-factor identity. The identities involve only rational functions of the generators and q after conjugation. Clear their denominators and specialize: they hold at each root where the indicated denominators are invertible. This proves coherence of the automorphisms rather than assuming an infinite universal matrix exists at that root. ## 2. Exact root center and its peripheral marking Write k_i=K_i^N, e_i=E_i^N, f_i=F_i^N and Omega=rho^2 FE+qK+q^(-1)K^(-1), C_0=2, C_1=z, C_(n+1)=z C_n-C_(n-1). Multiplying the N shifted FE factors proves C_N(Omega)=rho^(2N)ef-k-k^(-1). (2.1) For example the polynomial identity behind this calculation is product_(j=0)^(N-1)(z-qKQ^j-q^(-1)K^(-1)Q^(-j)) =C_N(z)+K^N+K^(-N), using q^N=-1. Both individual Casimirs are fixed by r. Ordered multiplication gives u^N=-rho^(2N)e_1 f_2 k_2/k_1. Retain the entire central divisor D_c=1-u^N=1+rho^(2N)e_1 f_2 k_2/k_1. (2.2) All factors 1-Q^j u become invertible after D_c is inverted: their product is D_c. No parity-dependent scalar is discarded. The center map of (1.2) is k'_1=k_1 D_c, k'_2=k_2/D_c, e'_1=e_1 k_2, f'_2=f_2/k_1, e'_2=k_1 e_2+e_1-e_1 k_2^2/D_c, f'_1=f_2+f_1/k_2-f_2/(k_1^2 D_c). (2.3) For the last two formulas, take the N-th powers of the coproduct intertwining equations. The mixed Gaussian-binomial coefficients vanish because Q has order N, including composite N. Use balanced center coordinates epsilon=rho^N E^N, varphi=-rho^N F^N. Then k+k^(-1)+epsilon*varphi=-C_N(Omega) and D_c=1-epsilon_1 varphi_2 k_2/k_1. Equations (2.3) have the same form in these balanced variables. For the checked algebra map Ad_(PR)=tau composed with r, its point map applies (2.3) to swapped inputs, by contravariance. For inputs (k,e,f),(l,g,h), with c=1-k g f/l, that point map is ((l c, k g, f+h/k-f/(l^2 c)), (k/c, l e+g-k^2 g/c, f/l)). (2.4) This is exactly the inverse holonomy map (4.7) in the [marked braid note](marked_braid_holonomy.md). The inverse is required by pullback; replacing it by the positive critical map changes the convention. The previously derived Borel-factorization/prefix change therefore identifies (2.4) with inverse Hurwitz transport. In those coordinates put G(k,e,f)=[[k,e],[kf,k^(-1)+ef]]. At the actual ideal color a=N-1, x_0=q^a, k_0=x_0^N=delta=(-1)^(N-1), Omega_0=-2, e=f=0. The marked meridian is mu=delta G. It is the identity at this augmentation. On the actual nilpotent color section x=x_0 M it has eigenvalues M^N,M^(-N); its squared eigenvalue coordinate is U=M^(2N), as in the [actual threading calculation](ado_threaded_shadow.md). This fixes the sign rather than silently changing the root character. ## 3. A regular three-parameter splitting module Work near (x,epsilon_0,phi_0)=(x_0,0,0), where epsilon_0 and phi_0 now denote the raw central powers E^N,F^N, not the balanced variables of Section 2. Choose the unique algebraic Hensel branch omega near -2 satisfying C_N(omega)=rho^(2N)epsilon_0 phi_0-x^N-x^(-N). It exists because C_N'(-2)=delta N^2 is a unit in characteristic zero. Thus the full center is smooth on this cover at the actual color; fixing omega=-2 first would instead produce a singular quadratic cone at the augmentation. For 1<=j<N define a_j=(omega-qxQ^(-j)-q^(-1)x^(-1)Q^j)/rho^2, P=product_(j=1)^(N-1)a_j. Every a_j specializes to [j]_q^2, a unit. On a basis v_0,...,v_(N-1) set K v_j=xQ^(-j)v_j, F v_j=v_(j+1) (j<N-1), F v_(N-1)=phi_0 v_0, E v_j=a_j v_(j-1) (j>0), E v_0=(epsilon_0/P)v_(N-1). (3.1) The product identity (2.1) gives the missing FE diagonal at j=0. The differences of the other diagonals give [E,F], and K gives the remaining relations. Thus (3.1) has the specified Casimir and central powers. At epsilon_0=phi_0=0 the chosen omega is qx+q^(-1)x^(-1), so these are exactly the actual nilpotent ADO E,F,K matrices. At x=x_0 they give the Kashaev color. General cyclic members have no H satisfying the unrolled weight rule; none is asserted. This is a splitting module, including at the nilpotent point. Indeed the distinct K eigenvalues give spectral projectors p_j. For adjacent nonwrapping indices, F and a_j^(-1)E give inverse matrix units. Their products give all matrix units. Conversely reduce any returning path using FE, EF and the specified full E and F cycles. Its p_0 corner is a scalar. Hence the central quotient on this chart is End of the free module (3.1). This proves the needed splitting directly, including the special fiber. ## 4. A concrete Hom line and its anchor For a pair of source modules use (2.3) for the target center and choose x'_1=x_1 D_c^(1/N), x'_2=x_2 D_c^(-1/N), with D_c^(1/N)=1 at the ideal pair. Keep the individual Casimirs. The target modules are again (3.1). Source matrices transformed by (1.2), and these target matrices, are two splitting representations with the same center. Their intertwiners form a rank-one Hom module. There is an explicit generator. For each transformed K'_i form P_i=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1)(K'_i/x'_i)^j. Let lambda_0=q^((N-1)^2/2), using the already specified square root of q, and v=P_1 P_2(lambda_0 v_0 tensor v_0). Define the columns of I by I(v_r tensor v_s)=(F'_1)^r(F'_2)^s v. (4.1) The matrix-unit description proves all six intertwining equations. At the ideal pair the transformed algebra is conjugated by the actual full R, and R(v_0 tensor v_0)=lambda_0(v_0 tensor v_0). Consequently (4.1) equals that actual R at this point. In particular I is invertible on the formal neighborhood. This constructs the Hom frame using the K cover and ordinary units; no roots of E^N or F^N are required. At the base det I=1. Set I_bar=(det I)^(-1/N^2) I, (4.2) using the root with value one there. This is a specified finite algebraic cover and a pointed line, not a free scalar choice. For a triple, the rational Yang--Baxter identity identifies the two target splitting modules. The two products of the framed intertwiners differ by a scalar. Each pair map has determinant one, so its embedding on a triple also has determinant one. Thus the scalar has N^3-th power one. It equals one at the ideal triple, where the actual finite R satisfies Yang--Baxter (the generic highest-weight identity specializes without denominators [N]_q). In the formal neighborhood a root of unity with this value is one. This proves strict local holonomy coherence on the specified cover. Global continuation must retain its root cover and phases; this argument alone gives no globally normalized tangle invariant. ## 5. Exact restriction to the original knot period For the same nilpotent color on both strands, write R^0 for the actual uncheck R with its common Cartan factor q^(alpha^2/2) removed. The formula (4.1) restricts to I=lambda_0 R^0. Its diagonal entries before the common factor are x^(-r-s)q^(2rs), whence det R^0=x^(-N^2 a)q^(N^2 a^2/2), a=N-1. Writing x=x_0 M, the root of det I selected above is M^(-a). Therefore I_bar=x^a q^(-a^2/2) R^0. (5.1) At M=1 this is the actual full R. For the residual normalization R^0 the actual same-color twist is theta_0=x^(-a). For (5.1) take theta_bar=q^(-a^2/2). Their ratio is exactly the crossing scalar x^a q^(-a^2/2). On a knot braid of writhe w, multiplying crossings contributes this scalar to the power w; the zero-framing twist correction contributes its inverse. The pivot and cut pairing are unchanged. Thus the reduced and full zero-framed knot periods are exactly the original ones throughout this nilpotent meridian germ. In particular F_N(1)=<K>_N still holds. This statement concerns the same-color cut evaluation. It does not assert that the constant theta_bar is a ribbon twist on every mixed cyclic object. Nor does it change the full ADO factor d_N(M)=i^(N+3) M^(N-1)/(1+M^2+...+M^(2N-2)). The [rank-one meridian wall](marked_braid_holonomy.md) and its whole ratio at M=1 must still be retained in a global source construction. ## 6. What this contributes to the ideal-triangulation route The audited ideal-triangulation theorem supplies a complete positive geometric representative beta_T and its marked Bloch regulator. The [crossing fundamental-cycle calculation](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) already identifies the complete classical crossing class with beta_T. The construction here supplies actual local quantum holonomy data and a Hom line regular through the color used by the original invariant. It therefore provides a local object to transport when comparing a diagram decomposition and an ideal triangulation. It supplies neither the relative gluing source nor its chosen global contraction. In particular the actual root augmentation mu=I and the complete hyperbolic meridians are different central data. The [threaded separator](ado_threaded_shadow.md) rules out simply equating their homogeneous eigenlines while preserving the interior observables. A regular local family of crossing modules does not prove that the corresponding closed knot representations lie on one component, or identify their evaluations. The required comparison is of pointed relative source extensions, including their cut/cap data, full meridian wall, peripheral factors, and selected evaluation. It must also specify the trajectory between fixed semiclassical shapes and root-central coordinates. Positivity and local Yang--Baxter coherence alone do not prove nonzero geometric contribution, exclude cancellation, or bound the norm of the unknown comparison period. The volume identity (4/N)log|F_N(1)| -> log||P_hyp||=2Vol(M)/pi remains unproved. The subsequent [closed-braid note](closed_braid_period_line.md) constructs the admissible global braid Hom line and a literal scalar cut functional from these local data. A grading calculation identifies its entire upper triangular reducible period with the actual ADO meridian value. It also proves that the formal central augmentation neighborhood is abelian and identifies the Alexander attachment divisor. This advances the global braid construction; the relative triangulation source, opposite-weight geometric coupling and regulator norm remain unproved. ## 7. Independent exact diagnostics [The audit](../experiments/audit_regular_holonomy_braiding.py) checks 14 generic cyclic automorphism cases, including every commutator, the rational inverse, coproduct transport, Casimirs and central powers. Six three-factor tests check the quantum Yang--Baxter maps. Six tests construct the matrix-unit intertwiner and check all six generators. Fourteen actual nilpotent/ideal cases check exact conjugation, the anchored frame and determinant root; thirty knot cut evaluations check the compensating twist. Nine third-order deformation tests, through level 15, check the Hensel module and both central powers. The balanced-center sign and inverse holonomy convention are also checked symbolically. Even and composite levels are included. See [the results](../experiments/regular_holonomy_braiding_results.json). These diagnostics support the algebraic proofs, not a global period identification or volume estimate. ## 8. Literature coverage, not proof premises [Kashaev--Reshetikhin, math/0202212](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0202212) already constructs root-of-unity holonomy R-matrices. The abstract of [McPhail-Snyder--Reshetikhin, 2509.02354v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02354v2) announces an explicit four-dilogarithm factorization and holonomy Yang--Baxter equation. The abstract of [McPhail-Snyder, 2509.02365v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02365v3) announces invariants with flat-connection input and a phase-free geometric twist of Kashaev's invariant. These establish prior coverage of the general framework, not the selected original-state period comparison needed here. Their proofs, factorization and global normalization claims are not premises of Sections 1--6. The fixed-Casimir polynomial in the [older recoupling note](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md) is a specialization/lattice lift; that note does not assert a generic braiding for it. Equations (1.2)--(2.3) use a different construction: the individual unrestricted central characters change by the holonomy map. The coherence proof here gives no generic Yang--Baxter identity for that fixed polynomial extension.

title: The regular meridian centralizer and the actual normalization line
text: # The regular meridian centralizer and the actual normalization line Research note, 26 October 2026. There is a smaller commutative group relevant to the framed geometric period: the centralizer of the regular marked meridian. It is multiplicative away from the parabolic fiber and additive on that fiber. Its framing torsor, invariant differential and power adapters can all be computed exactly. The actual ADO modified dimension is the inverse Lie factor of one such adapter, with its original phase. The group model G^(lambda) is an existing definition, already recorded in [the uniform source-base note](uniform_frobenius_source_base.md#3-the-deformation-group-is-an-existing-definition), from [Mezard--Romagny--Tossici, Section 1.2](https://arxiv.org/html/1104.2222v1#S1.SS2). Here its parameter is the meridian eigenvalue gap, rather than the quantum gap rho. The matrix calculations below supply the geometric application without importing a classification proof. This identifies the peripheral normalization line, not the selected global quantum period or its Bloch-regulator norm. ## 1. The centralizer is a smooth commutative group model On the marked meridian eigenvalue cover put kappa=M-M^(-1), mu_M=[M 1;0 M^(-1)]. This meridian is regular even at M=1, where it is a nontrivial unipotent. Commutation of a general invertible matrix with mu_M forces its lower-left entry to zero and a-d=kappa*b. Normalize the lower diagonal entry to one in PGL_2. The projective image of this GL_2 centralizer is J_M={C_b=[1+kappa*b b;0 1]:1+kappa*b!=0}, b*b'=b+b'+kappa*b*b', b^(-1)=-b/(1+kappa*b). (1.1) It is commutative. Its generic multiplicative coordinate is y=1+kappa*b; its kappa=0 fiber is the additive b-line. Its invariant relative differential is omega_J=db/(1+kappa*b). (1.2) These facts are identities of the smooth open affine-line group scheme. A limit of diagonalizing matrices is unnecessary. The PGL convention is explicit; fixed SL_2 sign characters remain separate marked data. On the open set M+M^(-1)!=0 this is also the full PGL_2 centralizer: a projectively commuting lift can only commute with mu_M, since conjugation preserves its nonzero trace. At trace zero there is an additional anticommuting component. For example, at M=i the invertible matrix [1 0;-2i -1] conjugates mu_i to -mu_i. All statements here use the commutative regular centralizer (1.1); near the complete meridian M=1 the distinction disappears. This geometric meridian centralizer is distinct from the large quantum commutant End_(U_q)(V^(tensor b)) computed in [the intrinsic cut atlas](intrinsic_cut_and_meridian_atlas.md). Its commutativity does not contradict the genuine SL_2 sector of the full actual braid transport. ## 2. The framing torsor has an explicit quotient by this group Use the same two framing coordinates as in the actual critical correspondence, with F_M(r,s)=[r 1-r;s -kappa-s], Delta=s+kappa*r !=0, F_M(1,1)^t=(1,-kappa)^t. The latter vector is the M^(-1) eigenvector of mu_M. Direct conjugation gives F_M^(-1) mu_M F_M =[M+s -kappa-s;s M^(-1)-s]=mu_s. (2.1) In particular this boundary meridian is independent of r. Left multiplication by C_b acts on the frame by r -> r+b Delta, s -> s, Delta -> Delta(1+kappa*b). (2.2) Where s!=0, r=0 is a section and b=r/s is the torsor coordinate. Thus r is the residual centralizer direction, while s records the boundary coadjoint coordinate. At completeness the action is r->r+bs. These statements hold for every representation in the marked chart, independently of its knot presentation. The initial position coordinate on the classical critical chart of the actual balanced state is A_cut=M/(M+s), (2.3) because x=-M and the raw K is -(M+s). At fixed M an invariant framing two-form adapted to this original cut coordinate is Omega_cut=(dr/Delta) wedge dlog A_cut =-dr wedge ds/[Delta(M+s)]. (2.4) Its fundamental centralizer vector is V_J=Delta partial_r. Direct differentiation gives Lie_(V_J) Omega_cut=0, contraction_(V_J) Omega_cut=dlog A_cut. (2.5) At M=1 this is -dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)]. It is not an arbitrary choice of Haar measure on the two-dimensional framing group: it uses its one-dimensional centralizer and the specified cut coordinate. If t=r/s, then it is -dt wedge ds/(1+s). Equation (2.5) is a canonical algebraic reduction of this form. It does not yet prove that the actual selected finite period implements that contraction or divides out a group volume. ## 3. The marked A-curve supplies a second section of J_M Let ell be the centered longitude eigenvalue, with ell(1)=1; retain the original preferred-longitude sign separately. Any SL_2 longitude commuting with mu_M has the form lambda=[ell (ell-ell^(-1))/kappa;0 ell^(-1)]. (3.1) Normalize its lower diagonal entry in PGL_2. Its section of the same group (1.1) is b_lambda=(ell^2-1)/kappa, b_mu=M, 1+kappa*b_lambda=l=ell^2, 1+kappa*b_mu=m=M^2. (3.2) On the normalized smooth geometric branch, b_lambda|_(M=1)=dlog ell/dlog M=tau_cusp. (3.3) This is an ordinary value of a regular function: both numerator and denominator in (3.2) have simple first meridian terms. The positive cusp shape selects the geometric direction. The geometric A-equation in these coordinates is exactly A_geo(M^2,1+kappa*b_lambda)=0. (3.4) Its strict transform removes the common kappa power; the exceptional polynomial is its tangent-cone equation in b_lambda. Distinct slopes separate there. Normalization still retains the branch mark if several branches have the same tangent. The group model alone does not supply the marked central regulator constant or its volume. ## 4. Powers give the actual ADO normalization, including its phase Define the Laurent polynomial u_n(M)=(M^n-M^(-n))/(M-M^(-1)), u_0=0, u_1=1, u_(n+1)=(M+M^(-1))u_n-u_(n-1). Matrix multiplication gives exactly mu_M^n=[M^n u_n(M);0 M^(-n)]. (4.1) At M=1 the polynomial has value n, and at M=-1 it has value (-1)^(n-1)n. The original full ADO factor is therefore d_N(M)=eta_N/u_N(M), eta_N=i^(N+3). (4.2) This is precisely the previously fixed formula, since u_N=M^(1-N)(1+M^2+...+M^(2N-2)). It is an exact algebraic evaluation, with its whole meridian germ and phase retained. For a power degree D, let H_D=diag(u_D(M),1). Wherever u_D!=0, it is the canonical meridian normalization adapter: H_D^(-1) mu_M^D H_D=mu_(M^D), H_D^(-1) C_b^(kappa) H_D =C_(b/u_D)^(kappa_D), kappa_D=M^D-M^(-D)=kappa*u_D(M). (4.3) Its map on the centralizer Lie coordinate is multiplication by 1/u_D. Thus the actual dimension line is eta_N times this determinant line for D=N. At the parabolic fiber the adapter is diag(D,1), so the original value eta_N/N follows without separately evaluating two zero factors. ### The same adapter is a determinant and residue map There is an intrinsic spectral-algebra version. Put B_M=R[T]/(T^2-(M+M^(-1))T+1). The regular matrix mu_M is cyclic: the vectors e_2,mu_M e_2 form a basis of determinant -1 at every M. An operator commuting with mu_M is therefore uniquely a+b mu_M. This identifies its GL_2 centralizer with B_M^times, including the nonreduced fiber B_1=R[epsilon]/(epsilon^2), epsilon=T-1. Its norm is Norm(a+bT)=a^2+(M+M^(-1))ab+b^2. The PGL normalization of (1.1) is the class of (1-b/M)+bT; its norm is 1+kappa*b. Adjoining the marked square root of that norm gives its SL_2 lift. This is a spectral unit torsor, with its quadratic root retained. For a degree D power define phi_D:B_(M^D)->B_M, T'->T^D. The Cayley--Hamilton relation gives, integrally, T^D=u_D(M)T-u_(D-1)(M), Mat(phi_D)=[1 -u_(D-1);0 u_D], det(phi_D)=u_D(M). (4.4) Use the canonical algebraic residue Res_M(a+bT)=b. Its Gram matrix in 1,T is [[0,1],[1,M+M^(-1)]], with determinant -1 even at the dual-number fiber. Equation (4.4) gives the exact comparison of these functionals: Res_M(phi_D(f))=u_D(M) Res_(M^D)(f), (d_D(M)/eta_D) Res_M(phi_D(f)) =Res_(M^D)(f). (4.5) The same map also preserves the spectral norm exactly: Norm_(B_M)(phi_D(a+bT')) =a^2+(M^D+M^(-D))ab+b^2 =Norm_(B_(M^D))(a+bT'). (4.6) Indeed mu_M^D has determinant one and the indicated trace, so the determinant of aI+b mu_M^D is that polynomial. The norm torsor and the residue co-source therefore have compatible cover maps, including at the dual-number fiber. Thus the normalization line and its residue co-source are compared together. At M=1, phi_D(epsilon')=D epsilon; the original 1/D factor is its exact dual correction. This does not identify B_M with the knot's entire quantum-A spectral algebra or its two-Casimir source: it proves the specified peripheral determinant and residue-line identity. The adapter becomes singular at a nontrivial torsion root where mu_M^D is scalar. The regularized lattices in [the resonant-source calculation](cyclic_source_connection_and_resonant_flags.md) must be retained there; a regular matrix conjugation through that point is not asserted. The actual root-central augmentation is still the identity representation in the earlier threaded-character test. We have not identified it with the nontrivial geometric parabolic mu_1 or with mu_M^N. Equations (4.2)--(4.3) identify the peripheral scalar line and its adapter only. ## 5. The source normalization composes exactly across cover degrees Taking powers in two orders gives u_(DN)(M)=u_D(M)u_N(M^D) =u_N(M)u_D(M^N). (5.1) The original phases satisfy eta_(DN)/(eta_D eta_N)=i^((D-1)(N-1)). Consequently the exact dimension tower is d_(DN)(M)=i^((D-1)(N-1)) d_D(M)d_N(M^D). (5.2) Its phase factors obey the associative three-degree cocycle identity, by expanding their integer exponents. This includes even and composite degrees. For example d_(2N)(M)/d_N(M) =i^N M^N/(1+M^(2N)). (5.3) The peripheral factor becomes i^N/2 only after M=1. This is a verified power-composition factor; identifying a move's multiplier still requires its actual source adapter. The paired actual source comparison has a simpler strict law. Its previously proved scalar is Gamma_N=gamma_N(M)gamma_N(M^(-1)) =d_N(M)/(N eta_N)=1/[N u_N(M)]. It therefore satisfies the exact identity Gamma_(DN)(M)=Gamma_D(M) Gamma_N(M^D). (5.4) This supplies a coherent peripheral paired line across power covers. It is not an identification of the tensor spaces or selected knot periods at levels D,N,DN. The actual root meridian step is compatible as well: d_N(q_N M)/d_N(M) =-kappa(q_N M)/kappa(M), (5.5) because (q_N M)^N=-M^N. Thus this line has exactly the original ADO difference cocycle, not a newly chosen gauge. ## 6. Covers also transform the framing coordinate For the connected meridional D-cover, the longitude is unchanged while M'=M^D. Equations (3.2) and (4.3) give b'_lambda=b_lambda/u_D, tau'_cusp=tau_cusp/D. The actual boundary coadjoint coordinate changes differently. The Cayley--Hamilton power formula in (2.1) gives mu_s^D=mu_(s'), evaluated at M'=M^D, s'=u_D(M)s. The normalized cover frame is F_(M^D)(r,u_D s)=u_D H_D^(-1) F_M(r,s). (6.1) In particular A'_cut=M^D/(M^D+u_D s), (6.2) which is generally different from A_cut^D. This distinguishes the internal position coordinate from the peripheral eigenvalue m, whose cover map really is m'=m^D. Pulling back the two-form (2.4) yields exactly Omega'_cut/Omega_cut=(M+s)/(M^D+u_D s). (6.3) Thus a cover comparison must keep both the Lie adapter and the specified cut-coordinate Jacobian. The regulator's degree-D law from the A-curve cover note does not replace this local source data. ## 7. Relation with the actual normal density The exact figure-eight calculation on the full two-variable framing chart now gives Omega_actual^2=-tau_cusp/[6 s^2(1+s)^2] (dr wedge ds)^2. It has precisely the dependence of Omega_cut^2 at M=1, with a representation-dependent scalar -tau_cusp/6. The old tests against dr ds/s and dr ds/s^2 did not test the centralizer/cut form (2.4). The [two-variable audit](../experiments/audit_full_framing_density.py) retains both free variables, the actual coefficient amplitude, the two Hessian null vectors and its transverse determinant in Q(sqrt(-3))(s,r). The exact identity proves independence of r; no interpolation or finite-field inference is used. [Results](../experiments/full_framing_density_results.json). The displayed density law is not asserted for every knot. The uniform conclusions proved here are the geometric centralizer, its framing quotient, its marked longitude section, and the exact original normalization and cover composition laws. Establishing that the actual source implements the reduction (2.5), and then transporting the selected period to its geometric regulator line, remains necessary for the original volume conjecture. ## 8. At the additive fiber the relative boundary is essential The quotient form specifies a sharper requirement on the source. On the chart s!=0 put t=r/s. At M=1 one has Omega_cut=dt wedge dlog A_cut =d(t dlog A_cut), A_cut=1/(1+s). (8.1) Thus its ordinary closed two-periods vanish on this chart. Commutativity of the centralizer does not give a nonzero absolute period by itself. Its relative boundary data cannot be discarded during the proposed reduction. For a concrete relative cycle let gamma be a closed curve in the s-plane avoiding 0,-1, and take the oriented chain Gamma=[t_0,t_1] times gamma. Stokes' theorem gives exactly integral_Gamma Omega_cut =(t_1-t_0) integral_gamma dlog A_cut. (8.2) For a positive small circle around s=-1 the last integral is -2 pi i; around s=0 it is zero. The endpoint separation is part of the relative source, rather than a consequence of the invariant two-form. Setting it to one specifies a normalization, which must be compared with the actual cut. The rectangular cycle here is a model relative class; it has not been identified with that selected quantum cut. Off the parabolic fiber the same chart has Omega_cut=db/(1+kappa*b) wedge dlog A_cut, b=r/s, kappa Omega_cut=dlog(1+kappa*b) wedge dlog A_cut. (8.3) The multiplicative fiber has an absolute logarithmic circle; the additive fiber does not. This elementary change is why one must transport a relative source or its regularized lattice, not just a class of ordinary closed cycles. It agrees with the earlier need to retain resonant normal jets, without identifying the different source constructions. The subsequent [actual cut-residue calculation](actual_cut_residue_and_principal_density.md) now identifies beta=dlog A_cut in the original finite cut pairing, with its canonical representative, pole packet and normal carry retained. It also derives the principal crossing determinant and pivotal-volume factors uniformly. The remaining relative pushforward is not supplied by this exact boundary co-source identification. [The audit](../experiments/audit_regular_meridian_centralizer.py) checks the group, frame, longitude, invariant-density and cover identities, including the full normalization phases. [Results](../experiments/regular_meridian_centralizer_results.json).

title: The regular ADO period, its bounded source, and a cyclic trace
text: # The regular ADO period, its bounded source, and a cyclic trace Research note, 26 October 2026. This isolates a canonical regular period of the actual literature state. All its polar data come from ordinary colors and have polynomial size at the specified principal root. The regular period at completeness is exactly a weighted field trace on the squared-meridian cyclic algebra. Any specified actual all-level operator gives it a rootwise affine equation with a source in a fixed finite-dimensional Laurent space, with polynomially bounded coefficients. These statements hold for every knot. They neither prove that this source couples to the geometric branch nor establish the volume limit. They do not identify this rootwise source with a fixed generic rational source or import a published volume theorem. ## 1. The actual pointing and the statement Fix a b-strand braid closing to a zero-framed knot. The parameters and state are those of [the ADO audit](kashaev_ado_pointing.md): q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q_N=q_N^2, Y=M^2, F_N(Y) in C[Y,Y^(-1)], F_N(1)=K_N=<K>_N, F_N(Q_N^j)=C_j(q_N), 1<=j<N. (1.1) The evenness and operator descent to Y were proved in [the squared-meridian note](even_meridian_norm_descent.md). The integer-color identities are the independently proved [quotient-color pointing](root_orbit_pointing.md). Here C_j has unknot value one; it is used to control exact polar data, not through a Jones asymptotic assumption. Put zeta_j=Q_N^j and S_N(Y)=1+Y+...+Y^(N-1). There is a unique polynomial P_N of degree at most N-2 with P_N(zeta_j)=C_j(q_N), 1<=j<N. Define p_N(Y)=P_N(Y)/S_N(Y), R_N(Y)=(F_N(Y)-P_N(Y))/S_N(Y). (1.2) Then R_N is Laurent polynomial. With eta_N=i^(N+3), the exact full ADO state decomposes as N_N(M)=eta_N M^(N-1) R_N(M^2) +eta_N M^(N-1) p_N(M^2). (1.3) The second term has every polar principal part of the full state away from M=0 and infinity. The first term is regular there. This prescription is canonical in the marked Y-coordinate: p_N has precisely those simple principal parts, is regular at zero, and tends to zero at infinity. The main conclusions, proved below, are: * All C_j(q_N), 1<=j<N, satisfy the uniform bound |C_j(q_N)|<=[j]_(q_N)^(b-1)<=D_N, where D_N=sin(pi/N)^(1-b)<=(N/2)^(b-1). * |p_N(1)|<=D_N. Thus the regular full period and the full ADO value at completeness differ by a polynomially bounded quantity. * Exactly R_N(1)=(1/N) Tr_(C(Y)/C(U))(Y F_N(Y))|_(U=1), U=Y^N. (1.4) * A specified actual all-level operator, after a fixed rational gauge and denominator clearing, gives an affine equation for R_N. Its source has Laurent support in a fixed interval and coefficients O(D_N), independently of N. The last claim concerns meridian functions at each root. No corresponding bound on q-derivatives transverse to the root is inferred. ## 2. A positive trace bounds all the ordinary colors We reconstruct the finite algebra needed for the bound. Assume N>=3, theta=pi/N, and put delta=2cos(theta), mu_a=sin((a+1)theta)/sin(theta), 0<=a<=N-2. All mu_a are positive; with mu_(-1)=mu_(N-1)=0 they obey mu_(a-1)+mu_(a+1)=delta*mu_a. Let H_m have the orthonormal basis of length-m walks on the chain 0,...,N-2 starting at zero. On a walk a, define U_i to be zero unless a_(i-1)=a_(i+1)=c. Otherwise it replaces the middle height a_i by a neighbor a_i' of c, with matrix entry (U_i)_(a',a)=sqrt(mu_(a_i')mu_(a_i))/mu_c. (2.1) Direct multiplication gives U_i*=U_i, U_i^2=delta U_i, U_i U_(i+1) U_i=U_i, and commuting distant generators. For the square use the displayed neighbor sum. In the adjacent product the middle heights are forced at its two outer steps and the square-root ratios cancel, leaving the single U_i entry. Thus these are actual Temperley--Lieb matrices. The braid matrix B_i=q_N^(1/2) I-q_N^(-1/2) U_i (2.2) is unitary: its two eigenvalues are q_N^(1/2) and -q_N^(-3/2). The braid relation follows by expanding and using the three local Temperley--Lieb relations. The nonnormalized positive trace is tau_m(A)=sum_walks mu_(a_m) A_(a,a). (2.3) Endpoint preservation makes it tracial. The neighbor sum gives tau_(m+1)(A tensor I)=delta*tau_m(A), and (2.1) gives tau_(m+1)((A tensor I)U_m)=tau_m(A). These identities determine the diagram trace: every Temperley--Lieb diagram at the next level is in the span of the included algebra and A U_m B, and cyclicity reduces the latter trace to the preceding level. In particular this trace agrees with the algebraic closure trace. Here is its connection with the fixed actual R. On the ordinary two-dimensional color, after retaining the common Cartan scalar, R_checked=q^(1/2) I-q^(-1/2) U, where U is zero on 00 and 11 and has block U|_(01,10)=[ q -1 ; -1 q^(-1) ]. (2.4) This follows by substituting E v_1=v_0 into the actual finite R. It obeys U^2=(q+q^(-1))U and the adjacent relation. With K=diag(q,q^(-1)), its partial quantum trace is I. Thus the actual quantum trace has precisely the two trace recursions above and equals (2.3), even though (2.4) itself is not Hermitian in the unmodified tensor basis. For completeness the j-color is represented by the idempotent p_(j-1). The recursion, within the requisite tensor power, is p_0=p_1=I, p_(m+1)=p_m tensor I -[m]/[m+1]*(p_m tensor I)U_m(p_m tensor I). (2.5) The Temperley--Lieb relations inductively give p_m U_i=U_i p_m=0 for i<m and (p_m U_m p_m)^2=([m+1]/[m])p_m U_m p_m; substituting this last identity in (2.5) verifies idempotence at the next step. All coefficients are real and denominators nonzero in the range used here. Hence these idempotents are orthogonal projections in (2.1). The trace recursion and delta*[m+1]-[m]=[m+2] give tau_m(p_m)=[m+1]. (2.6) This also verifies the actual color rather than assigning it by name. For generic q the common kernel of the U_i in V_1^(tensor m) has one vector at each weight: each adjacent exchange imposes the q-ratio read from (2.4), and adjacent exchanges connect all words of that weight. These m+1 vectors are F^r(v_0 tensor ... tensor v_0), with E F^r=[r][m-r+1]F^(r-1). Thus the image is exactly the ordinary (m+1)-dimensional highest-weight color. This identity specializes for m<=N-2, when all needed denominators remain nonzero. Cabling the actual finite R and restricting to these images gives its color R by the coproduct identity; equivalently expand the coproduct powers by the q-binomial formula. This is the same color comparison proved in [the degree note](adequacy_and_algebraic_periods.md#3-passing-from-parallel-strands-to-the-actual-color). For a b-strand braid colored by j<N, the tensor product P of these projections has positive trace [j]^b. The cabled braid is unitary, preserves P, and its framing correction has modulus one. On the image of P each diagonal entry of a unitary has modulus at most one. The positive trace therefore gives |C_j(q_N)|<=tau(P)/[j]=[j]^(b-1). (2.7) This is uniform in j,N. For N=2 only j=1 occurs and the statement is immediate. Since sin(pi/N)>=2/N, the D_N bound in Section 1 follows. At j=N the positive trace of the corresponding projection is zero; division by [N] is unavailable. Nothing here bounds the Kashaev color. ## 3. The exact principal parts and the regular remainder At a root zeta_j of S_N, S_N'(zeta_j)=N*zeta_j^(-1)/(zeta_j-1). Lagrange interpolation gives P_N(Y)=sum_(j=1)^(N-1) C_j(q_N) *S_N(Y)/((Y-zeta_j)S_N'(zeta_j)), p_N(Y)=sum_(j=1)^(N-1) C_j(q_N)*zeta_j*(zeta_j-1)/(N*(Y-zeta_j)). (3.1) The roots are simple and F_N-P_N vanishes at all of them. Since S_N(0)=1, division in the Laurent ring proves R_N is Laurent polynomial. It also gives the whole wall value R_N(zeta_j)=(F_N'(zeta_j)-P_N'(zeta_j))/S_N'(zeta_j). (3.2) The full state's phase, its monomial M^(N-1), and every divisor in S_N remain in (1.3). This is an identity of meridian germs, not a replacement of any factor by its numerical value at M=1. In particular both summands retain parity (-1)^(N-1) on the M-cover. Putting Y=1 in (3.1) gives P_N(1)=-sum_(j=1)^(N-1) zeta_j C_j(q_N), p_N(1)=-(1/N)sum_(j=1)^(N-1) zeta_j C_j(q_N), |p_N(1)|<=D_N, K_N=N R_N(1)+P_N(1). (3.3) The interpolation coefficients themselves are [Y^r]P_N=(1/N)sum_j C_j(q_N)(zeta_j^(-r)-zeta_j), 0<=r<=N-2. (3.4) They have modulus at most 2D_N. More usefully, every Taylor coefficient of the proper polar function at zero satisfies [Y^r]p_N=(1/N)sum_j C_j(q_N)(1-zeta_j)zeta_j^(-r), |[Y^r]p_N|<=2D_N, r>=0. (3.5) This direct formula avoids estimating a growing Vandermonde inverse. The subsequent [actual Weyl-descent proof](actual_weyl_descent.md) now proves C_(N-j)=C_j for every knot in these conventions. It rewrites (3.5) as an exact sine-matrix moment and improves its bound to D_N. Thus the bounded Laurent source has an explicit Weyl structure, without a new quantum-state definition. Its geometric coupling and cross-level norm remain unproved. ## 4. Any actual operator supplies a bounded rootwise source Take the specified actual all-level reduced operator in squared-meridian coordinates, P_hat=sum_(j=0)^d a_j(q,Y)T^j, T Y=q^2Y T. Existence and descent were proved in the [finite-state](finite_sum_annihilator.md) and [even-meridian](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) notes. Let f=Y-1. Choose and retain a fixed nonzero clearing factor c(q,Y) so that A_hat=c*f*P_hat*f^(-1) belongs to C[q^(+/-1),Y^(+/-1)][T]. (4.1) At the actual root U=Y^N is shift-invariant, and F_N/S_N=f F_N/(U-1). Therefore exactly A_hat(F_N/S_N)=0, A_hat R_N=b_N, b_N=-A_hat p_N. (4.2) This is the full ADO normalization after extracting its explicitly known eta_N M^(N-1). Equivalently this extraction twists the full shift by kappa=-q^(-1), retaining its N-cyclic sign (-1)^(N-1). It is not a new chosen knot state. Write the Laurent support of all coefficients of A_hat as contained in [r_-,r_+]. The source b_N is Laurent polynomial: (4.2) also equals A_hat R_N, which has no finite nonzero poles. At zero every shifted p_N is O(1); at infinity every shifted p_N is O(Y^(-1)). Hence b_N in span{Y^r : r_-<=r<=r_+-1}. (4.3) This finite-dimensional space is independent of N. Empty intervals mean the source is zero; nonvanishing or geometric coupling is not being assumed. There is also a uniform bound on its coefficients. If a_(j,e)(q) is the coefficient of Y^e in A_hat's j-th term, the coefficient of Y^k in -A_hat p_N is a sum of -a_(j,e)(q_N)*Q_N^(j*(k-e))*[Y^(k-e)]p_N, k-e>=0. Equation (3.5) and |Q_N|=1 bound it by 2D_N sum_(j,e)|a_(j,e)(q_N)|=O_A(D_N). (4.4) The sum is bounded because A_hat is fixed and Laurent polynomial in q. The argument holds at all sufficiently large levels where the specified annihilation identity applies. Every fixed meridian jet of b_N at Y=1 has the same polynomial bound, since its Laurent support is fixed. Restoring the full monomial contributes only the corresponding fixed powers of N to such jets. This removes a rational-source-factorization hypothesis from this *rootwise* construction. It does not prove that the coefficients of b_N come from a single rational function b(q,Y), that its generic difference-extension class is the earlier one, or that q-jets of those coefficients are bounded. The latter are not controlled by principal-root unitarity. The individual rootwise affine equation has the rational particular solution R_N, so it splits over that root field. This does not split the generic all-level extension: the source coefficients and the selected sections have not been algebraized in q. The cross-level period and its regulator norm remain the issue. There is a useful pointed uniqueness statement under a separate rank hypothesis. Suppose the rational homogeneous solutions of A_hat form the one-dimensional C(U)-line generated by u_N=F_N/S_N. Then every rational solution of (4.2) regular at both Y=Q_N and Y=1 has the same value R_N(1). Indeed the difference of two such solutions is c(U)u_N. The anchor C_1=1 makes u_N have a nonzero simple pole at Y=Q_N, so regularity there forces c to vanish at U=1. Since u_N is regular at Y=1, the difference has value zero there. Thus this source and its two meridian lattices determine the complete period without a remaining central scalar. Rank one is sufficient, not asserted for every actual knot operator. ## 5. The complete regular period is an intrinsic cyclic trace Let E_N=C(Y), K_N^cent=C(U), U=Y^N. The extension is cyclic with sigma(Y)=Q_NY, and Tr_(E_N/K_N^cent)(Y F_N(Y)) =sum_(j=0)^(N-1) Q_N^j Y F_N(Q_N^jY). (5.1) It is Laurent polynomial in U; its whole value at U=1 is defined. Equations (1.1) and (3.3) give t_N:=R_N(1)=(1/N)Tr(Y F_N)|_(U=1). (5.2) Thus the regularized complete value is already an algebraic period pairing on the actual cyclic object. The functional uses the marked monomial Y, not a selected eigenvalue with largest modulus. An anchored central rescaling F_N->c(U)F_N, c regular and c(1)=1, preserves it. An unpointed Hilbert-90 module alone still does not supply F_N. More generally every Fourier coefficient t_(N,r)=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1) zeta_j^(-r)F_N(zeta_j) satisfies |t_(N,r)-K_N/N|<=D_N. The particular r=N-1 is (5.2). If the target volume is positive, exponential growth with that rate for K_N is equivalent to the same growth for any of these coefficients: their differences from K_N/N are polynomial, and log N/N tends to zero. This is an equivalence of the conjecture, not a proof of either side. ## 6. A positive trace norm gives another exact formulation On S_1=C[Y]/(Y^N-1), define the involution by conjugating coefficients and sending Y to Y^(-1). At the actual principal root it preserves the cyclic structure. The pointed state has the positive squared trace norm H_N=(1/N)Tr_(S_1/C)(F_N^* F_N) =|K_N|^2/N+(1/N)sum_(j=1)^(N-1)|C_j(q_N)|^2, 0<=H_N-|K_N|^2/N<=D_N^2. (6.1) For a hyperbolic knot with volume V>0, the following statements are equivalent: (2pi/N)log|K_N| -> V, (2pi/N)log|t_N| -> V, (pi/N)log H_N -> V. (6.2) For example the first implication uses (3.3): a polynomial term is exponentially smaller than a sequence of positive exponential rate. The converse follows from the same identity. The norm equivalence follows directly from the positive identity (6.1). Equivalently the regulator target log||P_hyp||=2V/pi becomes (4/N)log|t_N|-log||P_hyp|| ->0, (2/N)log H_N-log||P_hyp|| ->0. (6.3) The positivity here controls the semisimple tail. It does not estimate the complete regular period or prove its geometric coefficient. ## 7. Why a regularized period is needed at the complete point The anchor and evenness give F_N(q_N)=F_N(-q_N)=1. Therefore a nonvanishing geometric WKB amplitude uniformly valid across both M=1 and M=q_N cannot directly describe the reduced state if it has positive volume growth. Indeed a holomorphic geometric action with a nonzero finite shift multiplier, and an amplitude whose ratio at those points tends to a nonzero number, would give a nonzero finite limit for F_N(q_N)/F_N(1). The anchor would then exclude positive exponential growth of F_N(1). The exact decomposition explains how such an inference fails: F_N(Y)=S_N(Y)R_N(Y)+P_N(Y). (7.1) The regular term is multiplied by a function with S_N(1)=N and S_N(zeta_j)=0 for every ordinary orbit color. The actual full ADO normalization precisely removes that function, leaving the regular period R_N and the controlled polar part. The zeros and poles occur at spacing O(1/N); a coefficientwise formal branch cannot erase their whole meridian germs. This uses the exact original factors, including the sign character, rather than an asymptotic replacement. The [geometric action proof](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md) and [triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md) now provide the marked regulator connection and norm to compare with t_N or H_N. What remains is proving that this specified regular quantum period has that norm. Bounded source coefficients alone do not prove its coupling, noncancellation, or the geometric factor's survival in the summed operator. No volume conjecture is claimed here. The subsequent [normal-period construction](peripheral_normal_period.md) keeps the factor Y-1 in the polynomial quantum module. Its complete full ADO value is the first normal derivative of (Y-1)F_N across U=1. A boundary-column argument gives a necessary factor condition for positive volume growth. Under the stated rank, or checked Weyl-sector invertibility, condition that derivative is an exact inverse-matrix period with known bounded source. It equals R_N(1) plus the controlled p_N(1), with the full phase retained. Its norm comparison is still additional work. ## 8. Coverage and independent verification Positive Temperley--Lieb path traces and unitary braid matrices are existing theory; [Aharonov--Jones--Landau](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0511096) is one explicit coverage source. The connection of root-of-unity nonsemisimple invariants with derivatives already has coverage in [Murakami](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.1287), while the ADO/integer-color unification is covered by [Willetts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.09854). No proof, completion theorem, or asymptotic result from those sources is a premise here. Partial-fraction interpolation and cyclic field traces are standard algebra; no novelty claim is made for them. [The audit](../experiments/audit_regularized_kashaev_period.py) compares 30 positive colored path traces with independently assembled actual highest-weight cut states, checks 62 principal-root color bounds including colors next to the truncation wall, and checks the ADO quotient-color identification at the small levels. Ten exact finite- field Laurent cut calculations verify all polar divisions, every ordinary-color value, the cancelled wall derivatives, and the weighted cyclic trace identity. All checks passed. The uniform arguments above, rather than these finite samples, prove the statements. Results are in [the audit output](../experiments/regularized_kashaev_period_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_regularized_kashaev_period.py

title: What cyclotomic descent can identify with the regulator connection
text: # What cyclotomic descent can identify with the regulator connection Focused applicability audit, 27 October 2026. The marked Bloch regulator has an algebraic logarithmic connection, but its exact finite quantum step is not thereby rational in Q,Y. An absolute rational unipotent family with identity cyclotomic curvature cannot supply that regulator connection in a regular Q->1 limit. This remains true even if its initial rational gauge has poles at Q=1. The appropriate possible use of zero-curvature descent is a relative comparison between two already specified period realizations, with their sources and markings. No construction of that actual comparison or volume theorem is asserted here. ## 1. A rational-coboundary confluence lemma Let k be an infinite characteristic-zero field and put h=Q-1, D=Y partial_Y. Suppose a rational matrix C(Q,Y) is regular at Q=1 as a matrix over k(Y)[[h]], with C(Q,Y)=I+h A(Y)+O(h^2). (1.1) Assume it is a generic rational coboundary in the column convention: C(Q,Y)=G(Q,QY)G(Q,Y)^(-1), G in GL_d(k(Q,Y)). (1.2) Then the differential equation D v=A(Y)v has a fundamental matrix in GL_d(k(Y)). A pole of the initial G at Q=1 does not evade this conclusion. **Proof.** Introduce an independent anchor Z, fixed by sigma and D, and normalize on the right: Ghat(Q,Y;Z)=G(Q,Y)G(Q,Z)^(-1). (1.3) It obeys the same transport and Ghat(Q,Z;Z)=I. Its Laurent expansion in h has finite principal part. Its coefficients are rational in Y,Z and regular at Y=Z over k(Z). To see the last point, take a common rational denominator before expanding. Its first nonzero h coefficient as a polynomial in Y is nonzero at the generic value Y=Z. The extra normalization denominator is independent of Y and has the same property at generic Z. Thus expansion and evaluation at Y=Z commute. If Ghat had a negative leading order -r, r>0, the coefficient G_(-r) would satisfy D G_(-r)=A G_(-r), G_(-r)(Z;Z)=0. (1.4) This follows by comparing order h^(1-r) in sigma(Ghat)=C Ghat. The coefficients of A(Y)/Y are regular at the generic anchor. Expanding at Y=Z, the formal differential equation uniquely determines all coefficients from the constant term, so the zero initial value makes G_(-r)=0. This contradicts its leading-order choice. Hence Ghat is regular at Q=1. Its constant matrix G_0(Y;Z) has G_0(Z;Z)=I and satisfies D G_0=A G_0. (1.5) It is generically invertible. Specialize Z to a value in k avoiding the finitely many rational denominator and determinant exceptions. This gives a fundamental matrix over k(Y), proving the lemma. The same argument can be expressed analytically at a generic complex anchor. The independent-anchor proof avoids an assumption of uniform Laurent expansion at an accidentally degenerate numeric anchor. The anchor condition matters. For the scalar G=Y-Q one has C=Q(Y-1)/(Y-Q)=1+h Y/(Y-1)+O(h^2). Normalization at the fixed anchor Y=1 gives Ghat=1-(Y-1)/h and remains singular. That anchor is a pole of the limiting connection; it is excluded by the generic construction. At an independent Z the normalized limit is (Y-1)/(Z-1), the required rational fundamental solution. ## 2. Consequence of full cyclotomic curvature identity The full rank-one and upper-triangular descent theorems construct a rational G satisfying (1.2) when the specified rational triangular transport has identity whole cyclotomic curvature. If that transport also has the regular form (1.1), the lemma shows that its entire classical differential limit is rationally gauge trivial. Here the coefficient-field and full-root hypotheses are those in [the descent theorem](additive_unipotent_cyclotomic_descent.md): principal roots suffice for rational coefficients by Galois descent; over a number field one must supply the additional whole-root or coefficient-conjugate marking stated there. The statement is about the full differential module, not the residue of every displayed matrix entry in every gauge. A rational singular gauge can change individual residues and higher pole terms. What is excluded is a nontrivial marked logarithmic extension such as the regulator's first additive logarithm block below. There is an exact root-normal version as well. For every sufficiently large root where G is defined, take the module T=C^(-1)sigma_Q. The gauge v=G w changes it to sigma_Q. By the gauge law of [the first quantum-normal construction](first_quantum_normal_connection.md), the descended operator pi L_1/N^2 is therefore the trivial connection U partial_U in that invariant frame, U=Y^N. This assertion does not need a regular Q=1 gauge. It holds at each regular finite root. It does not make an arbitrary pointed source section horizontal. Nor does it identify generic kernels with special central-fiber kernels at rank jumps. Those remain source/lattice questions. ## 3. The marked regulator is not a rationally trivial connection On the normalized marked A-curve let m be the nonconstant meridian function and l the longitude function in the recorded conventions. The Heisenberg period equations are dU=dm/m, dV=dl/l, dH=U dl/l. (3.1) More precisely Pi=[1 U H;0 1 V;0 0 1] obeys the right equation dPi=Pi Omega, with Omega_12=dm/m, Omega_23=dl/l, and other entries zero. In the column convention the fundamental matrix is Pi^t and its connection matrix is Omega^t. These equations define an algebraic flat connection on the curve, with its fundamental-class mark fixing the central period. Already dm/m has no rational primitive on the curve: at a zero or pole of m its residue is ord_p(m)!=0, whereas an exact differential of a rational function has residue zero. A nonconstant meromorphic function on the compact normalized curve has such a divisor. The same obstruction survives every finite algebraic cover. The pullback residue is multiplied by the nonzero ramification index; it remains nonzero in characteristic zero. Thus Log m is not an algebraic function on any finite cover. Equivalently the rank-two additive block d(v_1)=v_2 dm/m, d(v_2)=0 (3.2) has no rational fundamental matrix, even on a finite cover. A horizontal rational vector with v_2!=0 would supply the forbidden primitive. This block obstructs rational triviality of the full marked Heisenberg connection. Directly in its recorded right convention, suppose K were a rational fundamental matrix for dK=K Omega. Its first column f_1 is a nonzero constant vector, and its second column obeys d f_2=f_1 dm/m. A constant row functional a with a f_1=1 would give the forbidden rational primitive a f_2. This avoids any choice of a splitting of the rank-three filtration. Consequently the regulator connection cannot be identified, preserving its flat structure and meridian marking, with an absolute rational triangular family satisfying both identity cyclotomic curvature and the regular confluence hypothesis (1.1). The finite-root normal connection of an absolute rational coboundary is likewise trivial and does not already give the marked regulator connection. These are global function-field obstructions. In a small analytic disk at m=1, or its formal completion, Log m is a perfectly valid primitive. Local formal triviality is not generic rational or finite-algebraic triviality. Algebraicity of the complete gluing shape does not remove this distinction. ## 4. A rational deformation can carry logarithms if curvature is retained The obstruction is not to a rational deformation of the differential connection. A simple Heisenberg example makes the missing condition explicit. On the torus chart take m=Y, l=Y^r for an integer r, and A=E_12+r E_23, A^3=0. The logarithmic connection is d v=A v dlog Y. The rational matrix C_rat(Q)=exp((Q-1)A) =I+(Q-1)A+(Q-1)^2 A^2/2 (4.1) has that regular differential limit. Its exact root curvature is C_rat(zeta_N)^N =exp(N(zeta_N-1)A), (4.2) which is not identity for N>=2 when A!=0. Its limit is exp(2pi*i A), the nontrivial logarithmic monodromy. All central Heisenberg terms are retained in this formula. The exact horizontal step of that same differential connection, on the chosen logarithmic sheet, is instead C_exact(Q)=exp((Log Q)A). (4.3) It contains Log Q and is not rational or algebraic in Q. Already its first superdiagonal is Log Q. This cannot be made a rational function by a rational additive gauge: such a change adds a rational function to that entry. The residue of dQ/Q on a finite cover also directly excludes an algebraic Log Q. Thus a rational algebraic connection does not furnish a rational exact q-step. Formula (4.1) gives a genuine confluence construction, while (4.3) gives exact connection transport; they are distinct whole objects. This torus example isolates the logarithmic issue and is not a replacement knot state or a hyperbolic volume model. ## 5. The precise possible use of comparison descent The zero-curvature theorems can be applied to a specified relative comparison whose own transport has identity curvature. They should not be applied to trivialize the absolute regulator period. Two period realizations may carry the same nontrivial logarithmic and central periods while their relative algebraic comparison descends. Its source, cut anchor and integral lattice still must be matched. Equality or conjugacy of the two absolute curvature matrices is insufficient. On a Hom module its curvature acts on a comparison matrix P by P |-> H_act P H_geo^(-1); even H_act=H_geo does not make this action identity on all matrices. One needs a specified comparison line or filtered subobject on which that relative action is identity, or an actual curvature-intertwining section together with the necessary descent data.
