Nor is the naive product C_geo^(-1) C_act in general the transport matrix of this Hom module. The descent theorem applies only after this relative zero-curvature object has been constructed. Likewise the actual geometric quantum action has an exponential scale exp(W/Log Q). It need not be a regular unipotent confluence of the form (1.1). Singular or derived limits outside the lemma's hypotheses require their own maps and normal source complexes; they are not justified by a scalar norm equation. The actual first-normal source constructed from the finite-sum central derivative and the Fourier--Mellin source are genuine data available for that comparison. No equality with the regulator source or its nonzero selected period is inferred here. [Exact confluence/gauge audit](../experiments/audit_regulator_curvature_obstruction.py). [Results](../experiments/regulator_curvature_obstruction_results.json).

title: Majorization, exact regulator conservation, and pointed energy
text: # Majorization, exact regulator conservation, and pointed energy 28 October 2026. Majorization gives a sharp general product inequality, but by itself it pays the pointwise singular-value envelope. There is a stronger, useful strict-convexity statement: a bistochastic mixing map which fixes the regulator observable can mix only equal-regulator channels. That property makes the exponential action weights telescope and gives an endpoint bound for the ORIGINAL source energy. The actual quantum connection has not been proved to possess this property. ## 1. The general log-majorization inequality For invertible d by d matrices A_j let s_1>=...>=s_d be their singular values and P=A_(m-1)...A_0. For every 1<=r<=d, sum_(i<=r)log s_i(P) <=sum_j sum_(i<=r)log s_i(A_j). (1) Indeed the product of the top r singular values is the operator norm of the r-th exterior power. Apply the elementary product-norm bound there. At r=d equality holds, by multiplicativity of the determinant. Thus log s(P) is majorized by the decreasing vector with entries sum_j log s_i(A_j). For completeness, the convex-function implication needs no imported inequality. The partial-sum inequalities imply sum_i (u_i-t)_+ <=sum_i (v_i-t)_+ for every t, because each side is the maximum over r of its top-r sum minus rt. Every convex piecewise linear function is a linear function plus a positive combination of these hinge functions. Approximation proves sum f(u_i)<=sum f(v_i) for every convex f. Taking f(t)=exp(pt), p>0, yields the corresponding Schatten bound. This is sharp with only the individual singular spectra specified: positive diagonal matrices whose decreasing singular directions are aligned attain equality. It cannot be generally improved by changing the convex function. On a regular slowly varying recurrence with a tame supplied instantaneous eigenbasis, the transformed steps are diag(lambda_i(x_j))+O(1/N). For eigenvalues bounded away from zero, their singular logarithms are the decreasing log|lambda_i|+O(1/N). Consequently (1) yields the integral of the POINTWISE sorted root moduli. It does not yield the maximum complete marked-branch action. For r=1 this is the safe classical spectral envelope already proved for the actual source. All exterior-power refinements retain the same limitation at r=1. The actual source costs are not part of a singular-spectrum list: |ell^*P s|<=||ell|| ||s|| s_1(P). In the actual macroscopic theorem, s is the entire ordinary-color packet on the denominator-avoiding complex circle and has proved polynomial norm. That fact makes (1) an original-source upper bound; it does not supply a new branch-selection inequality. ## 2. Strict convexity gives a stronger exact rigidity Let C be a nonnegative doubly stochastic matrix and r a real vector. One has the EXACT variance identity sum_(i,k) C_(ik)(r_i-r_k)^2 =2 r dot (r-Cr). (2) The two quadratic terms on expansion use the row and column sums. In particular, if Cr=r, every term on the left vanishes: C_(ik)>0 => r_i=r_k. (3) This is also the equality case of strict convexity of t^2 under doubly stochastic averaging. Merely preserving the TOTAL mean of r does not give (3); every doubly stochastic matrix preserves that mean. There is a noncommutative version directly suited to an energy. Let Phi(X)=sum_a K_a X K_a^* be a bistochastic Kraus channel: sum_a K_a^*K_a=I, sum_a K_aK_a^*=I. For a Hermitian regulator observable R, sum_a ||R K_a-K_a R||_HS^2 =2 Tr[R(R-Phi(R))] =2 Tr[R(R-Phi^*(R))]. (4) Expansion proves this identity: the two square terms each give Tr R^2, and the cross term is Tr[R Phi(R)]. Thus if either the Schroedinger or Heisenberg channel fixes R, EVERY Kraus operator commutes with R and with exp(tR). In an eigenbasis of R, all mixing is inside equal-regulator blocks. This is substantially stronger than conservation of one scalar mean in one selected state. For reference, a bistochastic channel also majorizes the eigenvalues of every positive input. For a rank-r projection Q, Tr[Q Phi(rho)]=Tr[Phi^*(Q)rho], where 0<=Phi^*(Q)<=I and Tr Phi^*(Q)=r. Diagonalizing rho bounds this trace by the sum of its top r eigenvalues; maximize over Q. This proves the usual convex energy inequalities directly. The NEW information required for (3) or (4) is the fixed regulator observable, not bistochasticity alone. ## 3. Exact telescoping with the original source retained Here is a concrete sufficient condition for endpoint control. It is an algebraic transport theorem, not a claim about an unverified knot connection. Let r_j be specified real diagonal action vectors and G_j=diag(exp(N r_(i,j))). Suppose the diagonal propagation is D_j=G_(j+1) A_j G_j^(-1), A_j diagonal, ||A_j||<=exp(epsilon_j), sum_j epsilon_j=o(N). (5) Unitary diagonal phases may be included in A_j. Suppose the ACTUAL energy evolution is rho_(j+1)=D_j Phi_j(rho_j)D_j^*, (6) where Phi_j is bistochastic and fixes diag(r_j) as in (4). These are conditions on specified local connection maps; no unknown terminal product or Kashaev value enters their definition. They imply Tr[G_m^(-1)rho_m G_m^(-1)] <=exp(2sum_j epsilon_j) Tr[G_0^(-1)rho_0 G_0^(-1)]. (7) Proof. By (4) each K_(a,j) commutes with G_j. Write rhohat_j=G_j^(-1)rho_j G_j^(-1). Then EXACTLY rhohat_(j+1)=A_j Phi_j(rhohat_j) A_j^*. Take the trace, use positivity and trace preservation, and iterate. This is the desired partial-sum telescoping: all intermediate action potentials cancel, including at equal-regulator mixing events. For a genuine amplitude recurrence the special case is one UNITARY Kraus operator U_j. If [U_j,diag(r_j)]=0 and A_j=I, the whole product is exactly P=G_m (U_(m-1)...U_0)G_0^(-1). (8) If the zero anchor gives G_0=I, the singular values of P are EXACTLY the endpoint exp(N r_(i,m)), up to ordering. Thus every top-r log-majorization bound telescopes to an endpoint sum, not an integral of separately sorted local increments. For the ORIGINAL pure input rho_0=s s^* and output ell, (7) gives ell^*rho_m ell <=exp(2sum epsilon_j) ||G_m ell||^2 ||G_0^(-1)s||^2. (9) When the actual evolution is coherent, rho_m=P s s^*P^*, its left side is exactly |ell^*P s|^2. No replacement of that evolution by an artificial mixture is implicit in (9). The general positive-output energy has the same bound with its specified output Gram matrix in place of ell ell^*. All actual external factors and original source normalizations remain outside this estimate unchanged. In particular a zero regulator anchor, polynomial original source and co-source norms, and r_(i,m)<=Vol(K)/(2pi) give the sharp desired UPPER rate. No nonzero overlap or lower rate follows. Introducing an artificial dephasing or a Kraus average does NOT establish premise (6). For the original coherent scalar one must prove its amplitude evolution or its exact selected Plancherel energy has that positive channel representation. Nor does regulator invariance under finite character-cover monodromy over a FIXED normalized peripheral point, or equality at a ramification point, imply invariance under the quantum connection. A meridian loop which ends on a different longitude sheet can have a different regulator. A bounded number of subexponentially bounded connection matrices supported only in equal-action blocks also suffices in (8), with a subexponential norm factor; more generally their summed logarithmic norm cost must be o(N). They need not be unitary. Genuine representation ramification supplies equality of the calibrated values on a colliding block. Proving that the actual quantum connection has only those blocks, with that bound, remains the analytic/source requirement. ## 4. Approximate conservation needs the right accuracy Formula (4) gives a quantitative diagnostic. If ||Phi^*(R)-R||_HS<=eta and ||R||_HS<=B, then sum_a ||[R,K_a]||_HS^2<=2B eta. (10) Across a pair of regulator eigenvalues separated by g, the total squared Kraus mass is at most 2B eta/g^2. Hence polynomial approximate conservation gives only polynomial off-block suppression. After conjugation by exp(NR), a transition from r_k to r_i carries exp[N(r_k-r_i)]. A polynomial error need not survive that factor. For example a bound from (10) alone would need eta exponentially smaller than exp[-2N(r_k-r_i)] for an upward weighted transition. The fixed point property or an actual action barrier is essential. The independently proved Gaussian model makes this quantitative: its off-diagonal coupling can be 1/N, its complete marked branch actions are zero, but its selected growth is a/4-theta^2/(4a)>0. Discarding coherent phases costs still more. If W_N(theta)=b_N sum_(k=0)^(N-1) exp[a k(N-k)/N+i k theta], exact finite Fourier orthogonality gives (1/N)sum_(ell=0)^(N-1)|W_N(2pi ell/N)|^2 =b_N^2 sum_(k=0)^(N-1)exp[2a k(N-k)/N]. (11) The square-root energy rate is a/4, exactly the scalar envelope, whereas fixed theta in (0,min(a,pi)) has the smaller coherent rate. Thus a positive phase-averaged energy can destroy the conversion penalty that one is trying to use. Equation (11) is a phase-variable example, NOT the actual root-color Plancherel energy: that actual identity retains its special ordinary-color polynomial remainder. ## 5. The knot-specific test suggested by majorization The useful test is stronger than convex ordering of root moduli: construct the ACTUAL connection on a calibrated representation packet and prove that its positive energy map is bistochastic and fixes the regulator observable, or prove directly that its entries are confined to equal-calibrated-action blocks with subexponential cost. The exact rigidity (2)--(4) then supplies the missing no-upward-action mixing statement and the source estimate (7)--(9). The [complex representation-path theorem](complex_peripheral_action_and_conversion_bound.md) already supplies calibrated equality at genuine normalized ramification and an absolute endpoint volume bound. The [two-bridge midpoint theorem](two_bridge_midpoint_regulator_anchor.md) supplies the zero anchor on every genuine component of that class. The finite quantum connection, its possible nodal jumps, and its exact selected energy are still to be identified and bounded. General log-majorization or Karamata does not manufacture those facts from eigenvalues alone. [Audit](../experiments/audit_regulator_majorization.py): exterior-power partial sums, the bistochastic variance identity, regulator-fixed quantum channels, exact pointed action telescoping, and the finite Gaussian phase-Plancherel distinction. Coverage only: product log-majorization is established matrix theory; see [Gowda, Some log and weak majorization inequalities](https://userpages.umbc.edu/~gowda/papers/trGOW20-02.pdf). The exterior-power, convexity, channel and source calculations used here are proved above independently.

title: Relative framing transgression and the literal finite cut projector
text: # Relative framing transgression and the literal finite cut projector Research note, 27 October 2026. This constructs an explicit relative boundary complex whose source and co-source are the original finite cut projector e and marked defect D. The marked meridian supplies the relative fiber endpoints; no Haar-volume division is introduced. There are two exact presentations: an intrinsic finite-root residue model and a smaller logarithmic residue model using the original canonical representatives. Their chain projection is literally e. This realizes the finite boundary source. It does not identify the internal quantum pushforward with the geometric Gaussian framing pushforward. In particular it does not prove survival of the geometric block in the selected global period or the volume conjecture. ## 1. The classical form needs a relative source At the complete meridian M=1, use the original framing chart Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)], V=s partial_r, A=1/(1+s), t=r/s. Then V=partial_t and beta=dlog A=-ds/(1+s), Omega_cut=dt wedge beta, iota_V Omega_cut=beta. (1.1) The ordinary two-form is exact: Omega_cut=d(t beta). This primitive is not harmless for a relative source, because its endpoint values are different. The relative endpoints have a marked geometric meaning. The regular meridian centralizer in the existing note is C_b=[1+kappa*b b;0 1], with kappa=M-M^(-1), and its action at M=1 is r->r+b s. The meridian itself is the centralizer section b=M, so at M=1 it translates t to t+1. A choice of initial framing section therefore gives the relative pair t=0,t=1. Replacing that section by t_0(A) translates both endpoints together. Since (dt-dt_0) wedge beta=dt wedge beta, the transgressed source below is independent of this choice on its invariant forms whenever the section change is regular on the retained source chart. A section with a pole at an added root requires its own boundary lattice data; no extension through that pole is inferred here. The geometric invertible-framing chart has s!=0, so A!=1. For the finite cut source we use the explicit extension F_tilde=A^1_t times G_m,A. It agrees with the framing chart at A!=1. Its added A=1 divisor is boundary source data, not an assertion that the original geometric frame remains invertible there. The generic meridian has a further marked period which must not be silently replaced by one. At fixed M, t=r/s gives Omega_cut=[dt/(1+kappa*t)] wedge dlog A, A=M/(M+s), V=(1+kappa*t)partial_t. The meridian sends t=0 to t=M. On its specified local logarithmic branch its relative centralizer period is L(M)=integral_0^M dt/(1+kappa*t) =Log(M^2)/kappa, L(1)=1. (1.2) This is a marked regular period, not a rational function. The centralizer power adapter already proved in the existing note gives L(M^N)=[N/u_N(M)]L(M), u_N(M)=(M^N-M^(-N))/(M-M^(-1)). (1.3) Indeed the adapted power map is t'=[(1+kappa*t)^N-1]/(kappa*u_N), and it pulls back the invariant differential to (N/u_N)dt/(1+kappa*t). Formula (1.3) retains exactly the actual modified-dimension factor 1/u_N. The generic centralizer also has an absolute multiplicative cycle, absent in the additive fiber. We do not identify its entire generic relative de Rham group with the polynomial additive resolution below. The finite source coefficients themselves retain their full M dependence throughout. ## 2. A relative complex with an explicit contraction For any characteristic-zero vector space E define a two-term complex R(E)^1=E[t], R(E)^2=E[t] direct_sum E direct_sum E, delta h=(partial_t h,h(0),h(1)). (2.1) All other degrees are zero. Define L(a,b_0,b_1)=integral_0^1 a(t)dt-b_1+b_0, i(f)=(f,0,0). (2.2) The integral is polynomial antiderivation over a characteristic-zero field; no analytic convergence or contour choice is used. We have L delta=0 and L i=I. Moreover the explicit degree-minus-one map H(a,b_0,b_1)(t) =b_0+integral_0^t [a(u)-L(a,b_0,b_1)]du (2.3) satisfies delta H+H delta=I-iL. Therefore H^1 R(E)=0, H^2 R(E)=E, R(E) equivalent to E[-2]. (2.4) Every linear map E->E' acts coefficientwise on this complex and commutes with delta,L,i,H. This naturality will retain every actual finite quantum matrix, source and cut. Geometrically, (2.1) is the relative de Rham complex along t=0,1 after taking a residue quotient in the A direction. A pair of the form (a(t)dt wedge omega,b_0 omega,b_1 omega) represents its degree two element, where omega is the chosen logarithmic normal form. The relative differential is (d omega,restriction omega-d eta). It gives precisely (2.1). The transgression is (2.2). In particular (dt wedge beta,0,0) gives a nonzero relative class: its image is beta. The ordinary primitive t beta has endpoint pair (0,beta), so its relative coboundary is (dt wedge beta,0,beta), whose transgression vanishes. Ordinary exactness does not kill the sourced relative class. ## 3. The intrinsic finite-root residue realization Fix the actual N>=2 and Q primitive of order N, over a field k containing its roots. Let C_N=k[A,A^(-1)]/(A^N-1), D_N={A^N=1}, omega_N=A^(N-1)dA/(A^N-1) =(1/N)dlog(A^N-1). (3.1) On F_tilde take logarithmic forms along A^1_t times D_N modulo forms regular along that divisor, and take their relative cone for t=0,1. The quotient has terms C_N[t] omega_N in degree one and C_N[t] dt wedge omega_N in degree two; differentiation is partial_t. Its relative complex is exactly R(C_N). The actual state f in C_N is the class i(f). Its cut functional is Phi_N(a,b_0,b_1)=(1/N)Tr_(C_N/k) L(a,b_0,b_1). (3.2) To see its literal residue meaning, first transgress in t and then sum residues at the N points of D_N. At A=Q^j, Res_(A=Q^j) f omega_N=f(Q^j)/N. Thus for an actual boundary vector f, Phi_N i(f)=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1) f(Q^j) =phi_N(f), (3.3) the original balanced co-source. This is intrinsic to the finite algebra: replacing a representative by (A^N-1)g changes its form by one regular at D_N, hence changes no residue class. For a whole normal family retain U and use C_U=k[U,U^(-1),A]/(A^N-U). If f is regular at U=1, then Tr_dR(f dlog A)=(Tr f/N)dlog U, Tr_dR(f omega_N)=(Tr f/N)dlog(U-1), Res_(U=1)Tr_dR(f omega_N)=phi_N(f|_(U=1)). (3.4) Here omega_N is pulled back as (1/N)dlog(U-1). The factor U-1 is retained before specialization. Equation (3.4) is also a direct trace/residue realization of the source's normal direction. ## 4. The logarithmic zero-residue source and the exact projector Let R(k) be the same relative complex with logarithmic normal form beta=dA/A along the added A=0 source boundary of the A-line. This added boundary is not a new geometric critical point. For a finite state use its original canonical representative f_tilde(A)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) f_j A^j. Transgression followed by Res_(A=0) sends (dt wedge f_tilde beta,0,0) to f_0. Root orthogonality gives f_0=phi_N(f). (4.1) Thus the original canonical representative defines a strict cochain map R(C_N)->R(k), applying phi_N to every coefficient. Its section R(k)->R(C_N) applies the constant vector psi=1. Their composition on R(C_N) is the coefficientwise chain map e=psi phi_N=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1) S^j, S f(A)=f(QA). (4.2) This is the literal original finite cut projector, not just a map with the same scalar norm. In the evaluation basis A=Q^a, its matrix has every entry 1/N. It has rank one and e^2=e on H^2. The averaging identity and idempotence also hold strictly on the two-term resolution; rank one here refers to its finite H^2. The two residue presentations agree by (3.3)--(4.1). They are not an identification of their unweighted ambient differential forms. In the D_N residue model the appropriate normal source is omega_N=[A^N/(A^N-1)] beta. (4.3) The unweighted beta is regular along D_N and has zero image in that particular quotient. In the A=0 model beta already is its logarithmic source. The chain map in (4.2), with the prescribed canonical representatives, is the exact comparison between them. Neither formula permits evaluating the source's pole first and then discarding its normal class. ## 5. The original pivot and marked defect lift unchanged In the same balanced evaluation basis, the original pivot is g(A)=x^(1-N)A^(-1), x=-M/q. This section first works in C_N, where A^N=1, so the displayed formula equals the literal power K^(1-N) for K=xA^(-1). Multiplication by g and g^(-1) gives coefficientwise chain maps on R(C_N). Define D=g^(-1)e. (5.1) Then on H^2, identified with the original color space, and also coefficientwise on its resolution, gD=e, D^2=0, DgD=D, Tr_(H^2)(gD)=1. (5.2) Indeed phi_N(g^(-1))=x^(N-1)phi_N(A)=0 for N>=2. In the evaluation basis (5.1) has the original matrix D_(a,b)=x^(N-1)Q^a/N. For every finite cut matrix C, Tr_(H^2)(g D C)=Tr_(C_N)(e C) =phi_N(C psi). (5.3) Every such C lifts coefficientwise and commutes with the explicit relative contraction (2.3). Hence arbitrary finite internal matrix composition and contraction commute with this boundary realization. The same applies when tensoring the cut leg with the remaining finite color spaces. This is exact finite linear algebra at every level, not a semiclassical or knot-by-knot assertion. The marked defect is still not an ordinary Hopf-intertwining coupon. This lift does not authorize moving D unchanged through a crossing. The whole full-ADO factor d_N(M), with its phase, pole, residue and normal jet, remains a separate marked line multiplying (5.3). In particular the 1/N from the cut source and the value eta_N/N of the modified dimension at completeness are distinct normalizations. For a whole C_U normal extension, one must distinguish the reduced representative g_red=x^(1-N)A^(-1) from the literal clock power g_lit=(xA^(-1))^(1-N)=U g_red. Their defects are respectively D_red=g_red^(-1)e and D_lit=U^(-1)D_red. Both products equal e, so the cut comparisons above remain exact. Their physical normal derivatives do differ: D_phys g_red=-g_red, while D_phys g_lit=(N-1)g_lit, with opposite rates for the two defects. Thus the U adapter is retained whenever a normal pivot jet is compared; a coefficientwise root representative is not relabeled as the literal clock power away from U=1. See the exact [Mellin lift comparison](fock_cyclic_normal_mellin_map.md), Section 2. ## 6. The representative carry and deleted-root obstruction remain The map (4.1) is linear and is not an algebra map. Canonical representatives satisfy the actual carry identity A f_tilde-(Af)_tilde=f_(N-1)(A^N-1). (6.1) In particular phi_N(Af)=f_(N-1), although Res_(A=0) A f_tilde beta is zero. Taking f=A^(N-1) gives phi_N(Af)=1 while phi_N(A)phi_N(f)=0. Thus the zero-residue source is compatible with multiplication only through the retained canonical carry. With U retained, its term is U f_(N-1); no normal source is removed. The open geometric framing chart A!=1 also cannot by itself carry the whole finite cut. The idempotent epsilon_1=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1) A^j is killed by localization at A-1 but satisfies phi_N(epsilon_1)=1/N. Thus phi_N does not descend through C_N->C_N[(A-1)^(-1)]. This is a precise source obstruction to deleting the excluded framing point. It is distinct from the projector e in (4.2), although both involve a finite average. Epsilon_1 is multiplication by one root's idempotent; e is averaging the shift and has constant image. There is now a precise repair after adjoining the actual matrix Ward differential. The [source localization theorem](ward_source_localization.md) replaces the boundary representative by P=1-epsilon_1, e_S=[N/(N-1)]P e P. Its matrix cut row has the same Ward class as the original cut, while its color co-source factors through A-1 localization. An explicit chain retraction and homotopy extend this comparison to the combined relative-Ward complex. With U retained, the deleted branch is marked by alpha(U)^N=U, alpha(1)=1, and removed as a whole regular idempotent summand; every normal carry is retained. The original color co-source's obstruction above remains valid on R(C_N) alone. The repair uses Ward currents and changes its representative with the exact factor N/(N-1). This is a boundary comparison. Compressing two internal operators separately omits the excursion L C(I-P)D J, so the theorem does not authorize deletion inside crossings or an internal geometric Gaussian comparison without those additional currents. ## 7. What is still needed for the internal geometric pushforward This gives a concrete relative boundary object, explicit chain projection and contraction, and literal realizations of psi,phi,e,D. The marked meridian rather than an arbitrary group volume supplies its relative centralizer interval. Absolute exactness of the classical framing form is therefore not by itself a vanishing argument for a source-compatible relative period. The finite boundary resolution is natural for every actual matrix, so ordinary finite internal elimination respects it. Its auxiliary relative coordinate t is not thereby identified with the zero mode r/s produced by the internal semiclassical Gaussian pushforward. Constructing that comparison, including (6.1), the missing root idempotent, and the normal divisor (4.3), remains necessary. In particular a constant geometric principal density would have nonzero image under this relative functional if the internal pushforward were proved to give this class. The boundary model does not prove that premise or select a global thimble. It supplies the explicit cochain target and the exact source defects that the missing map must transport. ### Finite contraction and formal Gaussian reduction are different maps The exact naturality statement is the commuting finite diagram R(C_N) tensor V_rest --lift(C)--> R(C_N) tensor V_rest | L | L v v C_N tensor V_rest --C--> C_N tensor V_rest, with the analogous inclusion and explicit homotopy. Thus actual whole finite internal contraction really does induce a chain map on this boundary resolution. What has not been constructed is a comparison from this diagram to the formal Gaussian normal module at a geometric critical representation, sending the auxiliary relative t to its internal framing zero mode r/s and intertwining the canonical carry. There is a concrete failure of the naive source map. The functions A^N and one are equal in C_N, whereas Res_(A=0) A^N dlog A=0, Res_(A=0) dlog A=1. (7.1) Consequently unreduced rational framing functions followed by the ordinary zero residue do not define a map out of the finite cut algebra. Canonical reduction, or its full normal-U source, must precede that operation. On the actual q trajectory h=Log Q, N=2pi*i/h, this lost character is A^N=exp((2pi*i/h)Log A). It is not a coefficientwise formal unit in h at a fixed classical shape. A local formal Gaussian contraction does not automatically transport its finite-root relation to one. The meromorphic extension of the principal framing two-form alone does not repair (7.1). Hence the present result establishes a compatible nonzero relative principal class and an exact finite source resolution. Calling it an actual nonzero *selected geometric formal summand* would require the additional commuting microlocal/source map just described. No such summand or global selected thimble is inferred here. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_relative_framing_source.py). [Results](../experiments/relative_framing_source_results.json).

title: The actual crossing, its ideal octahedron, and its relative source
text: # The actual crossing, its ideal octahedron, and its relative source Research note, 26 October 2026. This makes part of the [triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md) explicit. The crossing is the already fixed ADO crossing, with its Kashaev specialization. Its five quantum-dilogarithm factors give an actual ideal octahedron at the classical level. At finite levels its factorials have a canonical cyclic boundary source. The missing transition coefficient is exactly the denominator in the full ADO modified dimension, including its meridian dependence. These are uniform algebraic identities, not a different definition of the knot invariant. They do not prove that the resulting global relative period equals the marked geometric regulator. Octahedral potentials and crossing decompositions already have substantial literature coverage; Section 8 separates that coverage from the calculations proved here. ## 1. Exact formulas for both actual crossings Use the conventions independently fixed in [the ADO audit](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) and [the finite cut lift](finite_sum_annihilator.md): Q=q^2, x=q^alpha, X=x^2, M=-qx, Y=M^2=QX. Initially q is generic in the auxiliary finite cut lift; its truncated matrices are not claimed to give a representation or knot invariant away from the roots. Remove the common Cartan scalar q^(alpha^2/2) as in those notes; the known pivotal and writhe factors remain in the actual cut contraction. Put F(a)=(Q;Q)_a, (u;Q)_k=product_(r=0)^(k-1)(1-uQ^r), {a choose k}_Q=F(a)/(F(k)F(a-k)). For 0<=a,b<N, the positive checked crossing sends (a,b) to (b+k,a-k), 0<=k<=min(a,N-1-b). Its coefficient is exactly r^+_(a,b,k)=(-1)^k x^(-a-b-k) Q^(ab+(a-b)k-k(k+1)/2) {a choose k}_Q (QX/Q^a;Q)_k. (1.1) The negative checked crossing sends (a,b) to (b-k,a+k), 0<=k<=min(b,N-1-a), with coefficient r^-_(a,b,k)=x^(a+b-k) Q^(-ab) {b choose k}_Q (QX/Q^b;Q)_k. (1.2) Here is a direct derivation, including the phases. The E^k coefficient on v_a is [a]_q!/[a-k]_q! times product_(r=0)^(k-1)[alpha-a+1+r]_q =(-x^(-1))^k q^(k(a-1)-k(k-1)/2) (q-q^(-1))^(-k) (QX/Q^a;Q)_k. Also {a choose k}_q=q^(-k(a-k)){a choose k}_Q. Multiply by q^(k(k-1)/2)(q-q^(-1))^k/[k]_q! and by the Cartan factor at (a-k,b+k). This gives (1.1). For the inverse series, use (-1)^k q^(-k(k-1)/2) instead. After interchanging a,b at the input, its additional signs and all additional k-dependent q powers cancel. This gives (1.2). Thus the inverse crossing is checked independently, not inferred from an orientation slogan. ## 2. Five quantum tetrahedron factors For |Q|<1 write P_Q(u)=(u;Q)_infinity. Its elementary equation is P_Q(Qu)=P_Q(u)/(1-u). Set A=Q^a, B=Q^b, C=Q^k. The non-Gaussian factor of (1.1) is exactly {a choose k}_Q (QX/A;Q)_k = P_Q(QA/C) P_Q(QC) P_Q(QX/A) / (P_Q(QA) P_Q(QXC/A) P_Q(Q)). (2.1) To prove this, substitute F(j)=P_Q(Q)/P_Q(Q^(j+1)) and (u;Q)_k=P_Q(u)/P_Q(uQ^k). There are five variable tetrahedron factors and a fixed normalization P_Q(Q). For (1.2), replace A by B in (2.1). At a root of unity the individual infinite products in (2.1) are not being evaluated. First compress (2.1) to the finite products in (1.1); only those finite products are specialized. This prescription retains the normalization and both endpoints. For comparison with a classical period, let h=Log Q and use logarithms a_0=Log A, b_0=Log B, c_0=Log C, u=Log x on a chosen continuation cover. The leading dilogarithmic expression is Phi(A,C,X)=Li_2(A/C)+Li_2(C)+Li_2(X/A) -Li_2(A)-Li_2(XC/A)-Li_2(1). (2.2) It follows directly from the product, not an asymptotic theorem about a knot: expanding Log(1-z) in its disk gives Log P_Q(z)=-sum_(m>=1) z^m/(m(1-Q^m)), whose leading coefficient at Q=exp(h) is Li_2(z)/h. Analytic continuation retains the logarithmic branches. Equivalently the same symbol is read off from the exact contiguity equation below. The positive crossing has leading action G_++Phi, where G_+=a_0 b_0+(a_0-b_0)c_0-c_0^2/2 -u(a_0+b_0+c_0)+pi*i*c_0. (2.3) The exact scalar also has the subleading term -c_0/2, from k(k+1). The negative crossing uses G_-=-a_0 b_0+u(a_0+b_0-c_0), and Phi(B,C,X). In particular none of the Gaussian, sign, or boundary frame factors is silently discarded. For example (1.1) gives the exact rational identity r^+_(k+1)/r^+_k = -A/(QBCx) * (1-A/C)(1-QXC/A)/(1-QC). (2.4) Interpret this as r^+_(k+1)=the displayed ratio times r^+_k when r^+_k=0. Its commuting symbol is exp(partial_(c_0)(G_++Phi)). For the inverse crossing the ratio is x^(-1)(1-B/C)(1-QXC/B)/(1-QC). (2.5) The other positive-crossing contiguities retain the peripheral convention explicitly: r^+_(a+1,b,k)/r^+_(a,b,k) = (BC/x) (1-QA)(1-X/A) /((1-QA/C)(1-XC/A)), r^+_(a,b+1,k)/r^+_(a,b,k)=A/(Cx), r^+_(a,b,k)(qx)/r^+_(a,b,k)(x) = q^(-a-b-k)(1-QXC/A)/(1-QX/A). (2.6) They follow by cancelling adjacent factors in the finite Pochhammers, on the interior of both index supports. At a zero, retain the cross-multiplied equations. The meridian shift M->qM is x->qx, hence a half-step u->u+h/2 when h=Log Q. The last symbol in (2.6) is therefore exp(partial_u(G_++Phi)/2), with the square root (ABC)^(-1/2)=q^(-a-b-k) fixed by the original q convention. An internal Q-shift and a meridian q-shift must not be silently identified. These rational symbols provide local data for a global geometric-curve comparison, rather than assuming that comparison from an ordering of the classical A-polynomial. For a single crossing, k is determined by its external indices. One must not impose this ratio=1 there. Edge/stationary equations arise only for the variables actually contracted in a global state. ## 3. An explicit ideal octahedron, with no guessed shapes On the Zariski open set where the following six points are distinct and finite denominators are nonzero, take ideal vertices infinity, 0, 1, C, A, Z, Z=C(A-X)/(A-CX). (3.1) Use the cross-ratio convention r(v0,v1,v2,v3)=(v3-v1)(v2-v0)/((v3-v0)(v2-v1)), r(infinity,0,1,z)=z. The following ordered tetrahedra have the indicated shapes: | Ordered tetrahedron | Shape | | --- | --- | | (infinity,0,1,C) | C | | (infinity,0,C,A) | A/C | | (infinity,0,A,1) | 1/A | | (1,C,0,Z) | X/A | | (1,C,Z,infinity) | A/(XC) | All five cross-ratios follow by substitution in (3.1). The six internal triangular faces cancel with opposite boundary signs. In the displayed order the tetrahedra attach along 0,1,2,1,2 previous faces; each two-face attachment is along adjacent faces. This shells a 3-ball. Its boundary consists of eight triangles with the octahedral graph. Its opposite vertex pairs are (infinity,0), (1,C), (A,Z). The internal edges (infinity,0) and (1,C) each have valence three. Their shape products are exactly C(A/C)(1/A)=1, C(X/A)(A/(XC))=1. (3.2) In the rational oriented pre-Bloch group of [the Bloch-lift note](bloch_lift_and_boundary_torsor.md), this chain is beta_oct=[C]+[A/C]+[1/A]+[X/A]+[A/(XC)] =[A/C]+[C]+[X/A]-[A]-[XC/A]. (3.3) Thus (2.1) carries precisely the Bloch symbol of this octahedron. This is a local chain identity. It does not identify the globally selected knot period with the geometric embedding. The logarithmic frame remains additional data. For z=(A/C,C,X/A,A,XC/A) and eps=(1,1,1,-1,-1), define on the chosen logarithmic cover R_signed=sum_j eps_j (Li_2(z_j) +Log(z_j)Log(1-z_j)/2-pi^2/6). Since sum eps_j=1, the exact expression (2.2) obeys G_++Phi=R_signed+G_+ -sum_j eps_j Log(z_j)Log(1-z_j)/2. (3.4) Passing from inverted shapes in (3.3) to this signed expression at the level of a flattened Rogers period also requires its branch constants. Equation (3.4) retains a boundary/Heisenberg frame correction; its exponential need not have norm one. The rational symbol by itself cannot remove that correction. The five tetrahedra need not all be positive. In fact the local maximizer below has C=-1, so the central tetrahedron is flat. This diagrammatic subdivision is not automatically the positive triangulation supplied by the audited existence theorem. ## 4. The relative source of a finite quantum factorial Here is an exact root-level descent calculation. Let omega be a primitive N-th root, with no primeness or parity assumption. Define p_a(Y)=product_(r=1)^a(1-omega^r Y), 0<=a<N, S_N(Y)=1+Y+...+Y^(N-1), h_N(Y)=1/S_N(Y). The endpoint is p_(N-1)(Y)=S_N(Y), (4.1) because product_(r=0)^(N-1)(1-omega^rY)=1-Y^N. Work in S=K[t]/(t^N-1), with omega in K and N invertible. Its components are t=omega^a, and sigma f(t)=f(omega t). Let p(t;Y) interpolate the values p_a(Y). Put e_partial(t)=(1/N)sum_(r=0)^(N-1)(omega t)^r. (4.2) This is the idempotent supported at t=omega^(-1), or a=N-1. Then exactly, before any division, (sigma-(1-omega Yt))p=Y^N e_partial. (4.3) For a<N-1 this is the defining factorial recurrence. At the remaining component its left side is p_0-(1-Y)p_(N-1)=1-(1-Y)S_N(Y)=Y^N. It is useful to retain the cut interpretation. Extend p_a by zero off 0<=a<N in the integer index. Before cyclic identification, the defect is delta_(a,-1)-(1-Y^N)delta_(a,N-1). Closing the orbit identifies these two index positions and leaves exactly the source Y^N e_partial. Erasing the endpoints would incorrectly give a homogeneous tetrahedron equation. There is also a direct affine-resolvent interpretation. The unpatched homogeneous cyclic multiplier is H_raw=product_(a=0)^(N-1)(1-omega^(a+1)Y)=1-Y^N. Starting the cut at a=0, the augmented transfer around the orbit is exactly U_cyc = [ 1-Y^N Y^N ] . [ 0 1 ] Indeed the source occurs in the last transition, and its coefficient is Y^N. The marked fixed vector is (1,1). Thus the homogeneous block has central equation V+Y^N-1=0, while the source extension has the additional V=1 sector. This is a concrete instance of the distinction in [the triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md), derived from the actual finite factorial. The full cyclic linear system, including its exceptional components, has determinant det(sigma-(1-omega Yt))=(-1)^(N-1)Y^N. (4.3a) To check this, its matrix is a directed cyclic shift minus a diagonal. Only the full shift permutation and the diagonal permutation contribute to its determinant. For Y!=0 it is invertible, so (4.3) determines p uniquely even when S_N(Y)=0. In other words, the relative polynomial solution is regular where the homogeneous unit completion below acquires poles. At Y=1 the unpatched transition itself has a zero; the same cyclic system remains invertible. No inverse of that individual zero transition is needed for this conclusion. The source has the exact wall relation (1-omega t)e_partial=0. Consequently the original primitive is annihilated by the fixed-degree relative operator (1-omega t)(sigma-1+omega Yt). (4.3b) Its commuting support has a tetrahedron component L=1-Yt and a boundary component t=1. The latter must not be divided away at the root fiber t^N=1. Here sigma shifts the *internal factorial index*, not the meridian M. Neither (4.3b) nor the level-dependent projector (4.2) is being declared to be the knot's meridian A-operator. A global pushforward identifying the source class is still required. After localizing at S_N(Y), p is a unit: every p_a divides p_(N-1)=S_N. The unique unit transition agreeing with 1-omega Yt away from the cut and having cyclic norm one is a_tilde_N(t;Y)=1-omega Yt+Y^N h_N(Y)e_partial(t). (4.4) Its value at the cut is h_N(Y), since (1-Y)+Y^N h_N=h_N. All other components are unchanged. Consequently sigma p=a_tilde_N p, Norm_(S/K)(a_tilde_N)=S_N(Y)h_N(Y)=1. (4.5) This proves uniqueness as well: the product of the other N-1 transitions is S_N(Y), forcing the missing transition to be its inverse. The pointing p_0=1 fixes the Hilbert-90 primitive itself. For the reciprocal primitive g=p^(-1), the unpatched equation is ((1-omega Yt)sigma-1)g =-Y^N h_N(Y)e_partial. (4.6) At Y=1 all p_a remain units, and (4.4) becomes a_tilde_N(t;1)=1-omega t+e_partial(t)/N. (4.7) Thus the apparent zero transition is replaced by 1/N, derived from the relative recurrence, not inserted as an arbitrary scalar. At the other zeros of S_N(Y), the unit completion has a genuine pole. Equation (4.3) still holds polynomially there. Whole germs or an integral lattice are required for specialization; the rational unit formula alone does not cross those divisors. ## 5. This is the actual meridian normalization At q_N=exp(pi*i/N), set omega=Q^(-1) and Y=M^2. Then H_N(a;M^2)=(Q^(-1)M^2;Q^(-1))_a, (QX/A;Q)_k=H_N(a;M^2)/H_N(a-k;M^2). (5.1) The numerator in (1.1) is therefore a quotient of precisely the relative primitives just constructed. The Q-Gaussian binomial uses the same construction with omega=Q, Y=1. Formula (1.2) uses (5.1) with a replaced by b. At a zero of a denominator in (5.1), cancel back to the original finite Pochhammer before evaluation. No 0/0 value is assigned to the separate primitives. The independently audited full-state normalization is d_N(M)=eta_N M^(N-1)/S_N(M^2), eta_N=i^(N+3). By (4.4), this says exactly d_N(M)=eta_N M^(N-1) * (the missing cyclic transition at Y=M^2). (5.2) In particular d_N(1)=eta_N/N. The dependence on M is retained throughout. Its shift gauge is also recovered directly: h_N(QY)/h_N(Y)=(1-QY)/(1-Y), d_N(qM)/d_N(M) =-q^(-1)(q^2M^2-1)/(M^2-1). (5.3) The algebraic source before the unit completion is M^(2N) times the boundary idempotent. Both that central factor and the phase eta_N remain part of the data. For example the normalization tower has the exact factorization S_(ab)(Y)=S_a(Y)S_b(Y^a), h_(ab)(Y)=h_a(Y)h_b(Y^a). (5.4) Factors such as 1+Y are therefore meaningful peripheral functions; they become numerical multipliers only after specialization. Equation (5.4) concerns this normalization, not an unaudited identity between global states at different levels. ## 6. What the triangulation theorem can now compare For any fixed braid, substitute (1.1)--(1.2) into its existing finite cut contraction, keeping the pivotal and writhe factors. Equations (2.1) and (5.1) give a relative tetrahedral presentation of the *same* actual state. There is no state-comparison assumption in this substitution. The source in (4.3) and the transition in (5.2) are thus extracted from the actual literature state. The audited positive ideal triangulation supplies a different presentation of the geometric fundamental class, with beta_T=sum[z_j], Im(z_j)>0, D(beta_T)=Vol(M). The comparison distinguishes three global stages: 1. The subsequent [crossing fundamental-cycle proof](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) identifies the complete rational diagrammatic Bloch class with the marked fundamental class, including the additional diagram vertices and degree-one cusp cycle. The generic meridian correction and different eigenflags are retained. 2. Transport the *relative source, pointing, and logarithmic frame* through that comparison to the positive triangulation. A classical five-term identity does not prove this quantum transport. An unpointed homogeneous tetrahedron module loses (4.3), while separate evaluation can lose (5.2). The subsequent [factorial source torsor](factorial_source_torsor.md) supplies flat local source matrices in both index and meridian directions, their full cut-root transport, and the actual singular cyclic-dilogarithm lattice. The global tensor source and its wall intersections must still be transported. 3. Establish the norm comparison of the selected global relative period with the marked regulator. Local factorization alone does not rule out exponentially significant cancellation in the actual oscillatory contraction. The comparison must also specify the all-level parameter trajectory. It cannot simply substitute geometric shapes as fixed root-central characters: [the two-regime calculation](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md) shows why that has a different local normalization from holding semiclassical small coordinates fixed. Likewise, colored-move invariance with one specified representation does not by itself change its character to the geometric one. This locates precisely where the ideal triangulation theorem helps: it supplies a positive geometric representative for the regulator lift. The present calculation provides actual local quantum data on the other side of that comparison. It does not make the three global identifications automatic. Alternatingness is not needed for any identity in Sections 1--5; it could still help control the global gluing and selected cycle. The [nonzero actual annihilator proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md) already constructs an all-level A-operator from the finite cut state. The additional task is to identify its relevant source block and period with the geometric block, not to declare an arbitrarily quantized classical A-polynomial to be the operator. The subsequent [marked braid holonomy proof](marked_braid_holonomy.md) now identifies the actual cut state's classical critical correspondence with framed knot representations. It uses an exact factorial boundary/basis change, derives the meridian conjugation rule from both actual crossing symbols, and supplies nondegenerate charts through every hyperbolic representation. The framing torsor splits algebraically, and the crossing Bloch sum has the expected global boundary wedge and complete-frame regulator rigidity. The [crossing fundamental-cycle proof](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) now identifies the complete rational crossing class with the marked idealized fundamental class and its volume regulator. Generic peripheral/flattening identification and the quantum source and selected-period comparisons in items 1--3 above remain necessary. ## 7. An unconditional local norm statement, and its precise limit At the Kashaev color x=q_N^(N-1), QX=1. The finite identity (Q^(-a);Q)_k=(-1)^k Q^(-ak+k(k-1)/2) F(a)/F(a-k) reduces (1.1) to r^+_(a,b,k)=x^(-a-b-k)Q^(b(a-k)-k) F(a)^2/(F(a-k)^2 F(k)). (7.1) Every prefactor in (7.1) has modulus one. Hence exactly |r^+_(a,b,k)|=|F(a)|^2/(|F(a-k)|^2 |F(k)|), and the inverse crossing has the same modulus with a replaced by b. Thus a positive factorial weight appears in each actual entry. The global contraction still retains its phases. Uniformly for 0<=r<N, log|F(r)|=-N D(exp(2pi*i*r/N))/(2pi)+O(log N). (7.2) Here is an elementary uniform proof. Set f(s)=log(2sin(pi*s)). On [0,1/2] it is increasing. The difference between the right Riemann sum and N integral_0^(r/N) f is nonnegative. Its first interval contributes O(1), since f(s)-log(2pi*s) is bounded there, and all subsequent differences telescope to at most f(r/N)-f(1/N)=O(log N). For r>N/2 use reflection f(1-s)=f(s), integral_0^1 f=0, and the exact product |F(N-1)|=N. The change of one endpoint interval is O(log N). Finally d D(exp(2pi*i*s))/ds=-2pi*f(s), proving (7.2). For the admissible pairs s=a/N, t=k/N in 0<=t<=s<=1 this gives uniformly (2pi/N)log|r^+|=V(s,t)+O(log N/N), V(s,t)=2D(exp(2pi*i*(s-t)))+D(exp(2pi*i*t)) -2D(exp(2pi*i*s)). (7.3) At X=1, V(s,t) is exactly D(beta_oct) in (3.3). Its maximum is v_oct=4 D(i)=4 Catalan, at (s,t)=(3/4,1/2). For completeness, its two interior critical equations are sin(pi*s)=sin(pi*(s-t)), (2sin(pi*(s-t)))^2=2sin(pi*t). The first gives 2s-t=1 and the second then gives t=1/2. On t=0 the value is zero; on s=t or s=1 it is -D(exp(2pi*i*t)). The absolutely convergent Fourier series of D on the unit circle bounds this boundary value by pi^2/6, whereas 4 Catalan>32/9. Consequently the displayed unique interior point is the global maximum. Its four nonflat shapes are i; the central shape is -1. A fixed braid with c crossings has at most N^B cut states for a constant B depending only on the diagram. Pivotal and framing factors at this color have modulus one. The triangle inequality therefore proves for the actual original invariant log|<K>_N| <= N*c*v_oct/(2pi)+O_D(log N). (7.4) This is an octahedral upper bound, already within known coverage, and generally larger than the desired hyperbolic volume. It does not prove the lower bound, the exact volume rate, or equality with the earlier positive factorial model. Positivity of a geometric triangulation is not positivity of this contraction. ## 8. Coverage and verification Coverage was checked after deriving the displayed identities: * [Cho, optimistic limits and complex volumes](https://doi.org/10.1017/S144678871600001X) covers diagrammatic octahedral potentials, four/five-term subdivisions, and classical complex-volume evaluations. An optimistic potential evaluation is distinct from a theorem about the actual invariant's growth. * [Suzuki, universal quantum invariant and colored ideal triangulations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.08262) covers a Heisenberg-double reconstruction of the universal invariant on colored ideal triangulations. Its abstract concerns colored moves; that coverage is not being used as a theorem transporting the present meridian source and period to arbitrary positive geometric data. * [Garoufalidis--Le, asymptotics of the colored Jones function](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508100) covers octahedral growth upper bounds, with a stronger crossing count adjustment than (7.4). No proof from it is used here. These prevent a novelty claim for the octahedral interpretation or upper bound. The purpose of the present computation is to exhibit, in one fixed set of actual ADO conventions, the complete relative recurrence and its exact meridian normalization, so that the proposed regulator comparison has specified input. [The audit](../experiments/audit_relative_octahedral_period.py) and [its results](../experiments/relative_octahedral_period_results.json) check 17,754 entries against the actual positive/inverse matrices at generic q and at roots, for N=2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,12,15; the exact contiguity and Kashaev square-factorial identities; the five symbolic cross-ratios and oriented face cancellations; ten convergent five-atom identities away from roots; thirty polynomial source specializations, including eleven polar ones; the norm-one completions and their modified-dimension identification; the nonsingular relative cyclic resolvent even on the completion's polar divisor; and the normalization distribution identity. Numerical checks of the uniform estimate and the local maximum are supplementary to the proofs above. No global volume-limit claim is inferred from the numerical tests. The subsequent [regular holonomy-braiding construction](regular_holonomy_braiding.md) supplies local quantum transport compatible with the actual nilpotent color and its evaluation. It retains the full central divisor and uses an explicitly anchored Hom line, rather than substituting a generic cyclic state into the knot contraction. This adds local data for the proposed triangulation comparison; the relative source and its global gluing/evaluation are still required. The later [pointed tetrahedral calculation](verma_tetrahedral_transport.md) proves a quantum operator version for the untruncated Verma presentation: four monomial dilogarithm factors, an exactly normalized formal tetrahedral pentagon, and a root-period preservation theorem for finite formal rewrites with the actual boundary lattice retained. This is separate from merely matching the classical five-term symbol. Its required tensor assignment on a positive geometric triangulation and selected regulator norm are still unproved.

title: Oriented turns and duality of the actual relative source
text: # Oriented turns and duality of the actual relative source Research note, 26 October 2026. This supplies explicit oriented duality for the actual semicyclic modules, including its double-dual pivot, and dualizes the retained affine source and carry lattices. Caps necessarily meet a degenerate fusion character. The correct dual lattice and a perfect finite linking form retain the state directions that a generic cyclic fusion chart would lose there. This is a construction within the prescribed quantum-group/ADO definitions, not another knot invariant. It gives turns and source pairings on an already specified actual tensor network. It does not assign all geometric tetrahedron face modules, identify the global relative gluing period, or prove its Bloch-regulator norm. ## 1. The exact semicyclic dual Use [the genuine source module](semicyclic_carry_braiding.md) V(x,phi), N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2: K v_a=x Q^(-a)v_a, E v_a=e_a(x)v_(a-1), E v_0=0, e_a(x)=[a]_q (x q^(1-a)-x^(-1)q^(a-1))/(q-q^(-1)), F v_a=v_(a+1), F v_(N-1)=phi v_0. The actual coproducts and antipodes are Delta E=E tensor K+1 tensor E, Delta F=F tensor 1+K^(-1) tensor F, S(E)=-E K^(-1), S(F)=-K F, S(K)=K^(-1). On the ordinary linear dual the generator matrices are rho(S(h))^t. Put k=x^N and define x_dual=x^(-1)Q^(-1), phi_dual=-k phi, c_a(x)=(-x)^a Q^(a(a+1)/2), J_x v_a=c_a(x) v_(N-1-a)^*. (1.1) Then J_x is an isomorphism V(x_dual,phi_dual) -> V(x,phi)^*. (1.2) Here is a direct verification. The reversed K-inverse weights are x^(-1)Q^(N-1-a)=x_dual Q^(-a). For a<N-1 the dual F arrow is -x Q^(a+1)c_a/c_(a+1)=1. Its wrap is -x phi c_(N-1)=-x^N phi, since c_(N-1)=x^(N-1). The dual E coefficient is e_(N-a)(x)=e_a(x_dual), obtained by q^N=-1 and [N-a]_q=[a]_q. The top dual vector is killed by E. These verify all generators, without a generic simplicity argument. In particular the central factor -k is retained at both parities. When phi=0 the actual unrolled weight is also retained. If the source highest weight is alpha, its dual highest weight is alpha_dual=2(N-1)-alpha. (1.3) This has the K-root in (1.1), but the chosen H-lift in (1.3) must be used for the full Cartan and twist factors. For phi!=0 the statement concerns the root quantum group with E,F,K; no unrolled H-action on a wrapping weight string is asserted. At the Kashaev color x=q^(N-1), x_dual=x and c_a=q^(a^2). This is the self-duality already used in the [ADO comparison](kashaev_ado_pointing.md), now with a fixed normalization throughout the semicyclic family. ## 2. Double duality fixes the actual pivot exactly Dualizing the parameters in (1.1) twice returns (x,phi). The composition from the twice-dual standard frame to V** is J_x^(-t) J_(x_dual)=K^(1-N)=:g. (2.1) There is no scalar in (2.1). In the ordinary V**=V vector-space identification its a-th diagonal entry is c_a(x_dual)/c_(N-1-a)(x) =x^(1-N)Q^(a(N-1)), which is exactly g on v_a. The signs cancel using Q^(N(N-1)/2)=(-1)^(N-1). This proves (2.1) uniformly at even and composite levels. Also S^2=Ad K=Ad g at the root, since K^N is central. Thus the ordinary matrix double dual in these specific frames has precisely the literature pivot used by the actual cut state. It is not an independently selected determinant normalization. In standard dual coordinates the left cap and cup are ev(v_a_dual tensor v_b)=c_a delta_(a+b,N-1), coev(1)=sum_a c_a^(-1) v_(N-1-a) tensor v_a_dual. (2.2) The right cap and cup are ev_right(v_b tensor v_a_dual)=c_a g_b delta_(a+b,N-1), coev_right(1)=sum_a c_a^(-1)g_(N-1-a)^(-1) v_a_dual tensor v_(N-1-a). (2.3) The antipode identities make these actual Hopf module maps. The four snake identities follow by contracting the single matched index; c_a and its inverse cancel, as do the right g factors. Closing an endomorphism A with (2.2)--(2.3) gives exactly Tr(g A), with the original pivotal convention. For a map A:V->W its turned map in these coordinates is A_dual=J_V^(-1) A^t J_W. (2.4) This is contravariant under composition. For tensor products the dual factors reverse order; the corresponding literal flip is included. Thus turning a specified matrix identity, including an allowed tetrahedral rewrite inside the actual network, preserves it with its full scalar. One must use the turned map (2.4), rather than insert a same-color formula on a dual color. These statements give oriented turns on the actual colored network. They do not identify an independently assigned geometric tetrahedron face module with one of these duals, or establish unrestricted S_4 symmetries of an unassigned face tensor. ## 3. A cap forces a fusion wall The need for the relative source is already visible in the central character. On V_dual tensor V the q-binomial identity for the actual coproduct gives (Delta K)^N=k^(-1)k=1, (Delta F)^N=phi_dual+k phi=0. (3.1) The reversed order V tensor V_dual gives the same zero, since phi+k^(-1)phi_dual=0. Consequently the composite is on the degenerate Borel fusion character even when phi!=0. A cyclic factorization requiring a nonzero total F^N cannot be evaluated at this cap by forgetting the wall. The explicit maps (2.2) and (2.3) remain defined there and provide its canonical duality. There is a second exact check: Tr g=x^(1-N) sum_(a=0)^(N-1) Q^(-a)=0. (3.2) Thus closing the distinguished scalar cut F_N(M)I with an ordinary pivotal cap gives zero. The selected reduced cut and the actual modified trace must be retained. In particular the full factor remains the already specified d_N(M)=eta_N M^(N-1)/S_N(M^2), S_N(Y)=(1-Y^N)/(1-Y), eta_N=i^(N+3), (3.3) with its whole boundary germ. At M=1 it is eta_N/N. It is not obtained by multiplying the identically zero ordinary closure by a finite rational factor. Modified dimensions in this setting are existing literature definitions; no replacement is proposed. The later [actual meridian source](meridian_casimir_source.md) identifies a further operator built from these very cups and caps. At the Kashaev color their rank-one composition Pi has Pi^2=0 and actual pivotal partial trace identity. It is the nilpotent part of the complete two-color Casimir projector with the fixed factor (-1)^N(q-q^(-1))^2. The actual meridian source residue and the nontrivial pure-braid action are explicit multiples of Pi. This uses the full pivot above; an ordinary scalar closure or the reduced eigenline alone would lose that source test. ## 4. Dualizing the affine quantum-A source retains a co-source This duality has a direct form for the [inhomogeneous quantum-A system](affine_quantum_a_period.md). On a common difference base write sigma(w)=U w, U=[C c;0 1], w=(v,1)^t. The dual column has transport U_dual=U^(-t), explicitly U_dual=[ C^(-t) 0 ], [ -c^t C^(-t) 1 ]. (4.1) Indeed U_dual^t U=I, so the pairing of a dual horizontal column with w is sigma-invariant. Equation (4.1) reverses the extension: the source quotient becomes a trivial submodule, with the displayed nonzero lower off-diagonal term. This term is called the co-source here only to indicate that reversal. Deleting it is not dualizing the specified extension. For a source line with multiplier d instead of 1 the lower row is [-d^(-1)c^t C^(-t),d^(-1)]. Thus a nontrivial source line is dualized too, rather than first replaced by a trivial quotient. This applies to the full two-direction factorial extension and to its tensor sources. If a comparison is w'=A_aug w, the corresponding dual comparison is A_aug^(-t). Their paired period is unchanged exactly. The same construction works in every commuting shift direction; inverse transpose carries each flatness equation to its dual. For the [factorial source](factorial_source_torsor.md) the internal matrix [a b;0 1] therefore has dual [ a^(-1) 0 ], [ -b/a 1 ]. (4.2) The meridian source norm V=(1-UC)/(1-U) becomes V^(-1) on the dual. Interior dual pairings cancel these full functions and their specified comparison roots before any specialization. The raw non-scalar cut loop is also paired with its full inverse transpose; its off-diagonal source is not omitted. Unpaired boundary factors, including (3.3), remain in the selected period. This is an algebraic explanation for internal normalization cancellation when the actual duality data match; it is not a repair of an unrelated positive factorial model. At a zero of a, (4.2) can have a pole. Its extension on a lattice is handled by dualizing the retained lattice, not by evaluating that displayed fraction separately. ## 5. The dual carry source and its perfect linking pairing Let R=k[[epsilon]], F=k((epsilon)), and use the two lattices proved in [the carry construction](carry_recoupling_lattice.md): L=Lambda_leaf=direct_sum_i R e_i, C=Lambda_carry=direct_sum_i epsilon^(-kappa_i) R e_i, kappa_i=floor((i_1+...+i_b)/N). For any lattice A let A_sharp={ell in V* : ell(A) subset R}. Then duality reverses the inclusion: C_sharp=direct_sum_i epsilon^(kappa_i) R e_i^* subset L_sharp=direct_sum_i R e_i^*. (5.1) Put Q=C/L and Q_dual=L_sharp/C_sharp. There is a canonical perfect R-balanced linking pairing Q times Q_dual -> F/R, (c mod L,ell mod C_sharp) -> ell(c) mod R. (5.2) It is well defined: adding a member of L or C_sharp changes the value by an element of R. In the displayed diagonal bases each positive kappa contributes R/(epsilon^kappa) times R/(epsilon^kappa) -> F/R, (f,g) -> epsilon^(-kappa) f g mod R. (5.3) This is nondegenerate on both sides, as can be checked on the lowest nonzero coefficient of either input. It proves perfectness. Equivalently Q_dual=Ext_R^1(Q,R), by dualizing 0->L->C->Q->0; both lattice modules are free and Hom_R(Q,R)=0. For the fixed normal coordinate epsilon, the residue of (5.2) against d epsilon is the finite k-valued pairing (f,g) -> [epsilon^(kappa-1)] f g. (5.4) In bases 1,epsilon,...,epsilon^(kappa-1) its matrix is the anti-diagonal identity. Only jets of order at most floor(b(N-1)/N)-1<=b-2 occur, independently of N for fixed b. The F/R pairing is intrinsic; the scalar residue convention uses the marked normal coordinate, which is retained. In particular there is a perfect pairing Tor_1^R(Q,k) times (Q_dual/epsilon Q_dual) -> k. (5.5) On each summand, the Tor class is the socle epsilon^(kappa-1) and the dual residual class is represented by 1, so (5.4) equals one. The connecting map identifies this Tor class with the actual leaf direction killed by L/epsilon->C/epsilon. Thus (5.5) gives a canonical cap for those lost directions, rather than treating their ordinary image as the whole state. Its dimension is N^b-binomial(N+b-1,b). ## 6. Integral recoupling and turned contractions For every tree the actual evaluation has I_T=J_kappa M_T, M_T in GL_(N^b)(R), J_kappa=diag(epsilon^(-kappa_i)). Its dual evaluation is forced by preservation of the pairing: I_T_dual=(I_T^(-1))^t=J_kappa^(-1) M_T^(-t). (6.1) It has image C_sharp. The actual source in the tree chart is B_T=I_T^(-1)L, and its full dual source is B_T_sharp=I_T^t L_sharp. (6.2) These statements follow directly by evaluating the pairing. They distinguish the dual of the basic carry lattice from the larger dual of the actual source. The row ell I_T can have poles in a basic tree frame while still belonging to B_T_sharp and evaluating integrally on B_T. Replacing it by an arbitrary regular vacuum row can lose (5.5). A tree change I_(T')^(-1)I_T transports its dual by inverse transpose. All compositions, loops and paired interior maps cancel exactly. The same holds for a genuine braid map preserving both lattices and its appropriately typed dual. Because J_x in (1.1) has unit entries whenever x is a unit, its orientation change preserves the original leaf lattice at the nilpotent boundary. Equations (6.1)--(6.2), rather than a new unit pointing, specify its recoupled dual source. For an already specified finite actual network these maps therefore give consistent cups, caps, oriented turns and dual affine sources, with the entire cut evaluation retained. This resolves this part of the exterior data needed to use the [root tetrahedral pentagon](cyclic_tetrahedron_pentagon.md). It does not supply every face identification on the positive geometric triangulation, a comparison of its projected source with the actual one, or the selected Bloch-regulator norm. The carry normal coordinate is not thereby identified with the meridian normal coordinate or a regulator realization. ### 6.1 Reversing a triangle fixes its relative algebra The ordered relative operators for two quantum affine modules are D=X_1+Y_1 Y_2^(-1), Z=-Y_1 Y_2^(-1)X_2, DZ=QZD. Reverse the tensor factors and replace each by its Hopf dual. Construct D_rev,Z_rev by the same ordered formula in that reversed product. After the literal flip identifying its underlying dual vector space with the dual of the old product, the exact operator identities are D_rev^t=-Z^(-1)D, Z_rev^t=Q Z^(-1). (6.3) For example put S(Y_i)=-X_i^(-1)Y_i. Transposing the reversed formula gives D_rev^t=X_2^(-1)+S(Y_1)^(-1)S(Y_2) =X_2^(-1)(1+Y_1^(-1)X_1Y_2)=-Z^(-1)D. The second calculation gives -X_1^(-1)Y_1^(-1)X_1X_2^(-1)Y_2=QZ^(-1). This proves the phase and ordering without an unrecorded face-orientation convention. If D^N=lambda_R and Z^N=mu_R, (6.3) gives (lambda_R,mu_R) -> (-lambda_R/mu_R,1/mu_R). (6.4) On a normalized Steinberg face lambda_R+mu_R=1 this is an ordinary cross-ratio shape change. Its operator lift includes the transpose and Q in (6.3); central shapes alone do not determine the turned vector or covector. ### 6.2 The triangle face pairing is induced, with its scalar fixed Let g,h have matched endpoints c->d and a->c. Assume their three affine characters are nondegenerate. Use the existing pointed factorization maps C_gh:E_gh tensor R_gh -> E_g tensor E_h, C_rev:E_(gh)^(-1) tensor R_rev -> E_(h^(-1)) tensor E_(g^(-1)). Their columns are the already proved finite expressions X_total^i D^j(1 tensor 1); no new quantum kernel is chosen. Let J_g,J_h,J_total be the endpoint caps with the actual source normalization of Section 7. Their edge root markings are retained. A product total mark is one local source choice; globally the total cap is the already assigned cap of that edge, including its prescribed dual mark. With P the literal flip, form B=C_gh^t (J_g tensor J_h) P C_rev. (6.5) There is a unique invertible face pairing M_gh such that B=J_total tensor M_gh. (6.6) To prove this, (6.5) intertwines the total algebra with its Hopf dual, since each endpoint pairing and both C maps do. After removing J_total on that factor, it commutes with the full matrix algebra of E_(gh)^(-1). Its commutant is I tensor End(R), so it equals I tensor M_gh. Every matrix in (6.5) is invertible, proving invertibility of M_gh. In particular its entire scalar is determined. An explicit finite formula is M_gh=(1/N)Tr_total[(J_total^(-1) tensor I)B]. (6.7) Equation (6.3) proves that M_gh intertwines the reversed relative module with the indicated transposed relative operators. Thus the face algebra as well as its pairing has been specified. Its reversed unit becomes M_gh e_0, which can be a nonconstant covector in the old monomial dual frame. This vector is retained in selected periods. These pairings are coherent on every specified recoupling diagram. For a tree T write B_T=I_T^t B_leaf I_(T,reverse). If F=I_(T')^(-1)I_T and F_rev is the corresponding reverse tree change, then exactly B_T=F^t B_(T') F_rev. (6.8) Substitution proves (6.8) with scalar one. Consequently the face pairings transported by these C maps respect the recoupling pentagon, without an independent face scalar or a reset of its unit vector. At a wall, whole identities are interpreted on the actual paired lattices of (6.1)--(6.2) and their retained source quotients. No separate invertible specialization of every generic matrix is assumed. This constructs dual face data for the matched-endpoint recoupling network. It does not identify every independently assigned geometric tetrahedron face with that network, establish all uncolored tetrahedron ordering moves, or identify its selected positive geometric source. Those are the remaining global comparison questions. The subsequent [oriented source calculation](oriented_tetrahedron_source.md) now treats shared edge marks, exact full reversal and cyclic face orderings with these caps. The raw cyclic rotation has a non-scalar inverse-pivot defect; an explicit Weyl and central correction with its cubic phase gives coherent face orderings preserving M. A separate full tetrahedron vertex test still fails for the bare tensor, with an exact N=2 counterexample. Thus these face constructions do not yet justify a direct uncolored geometric tetrahedron assignment. ## 7. A cyclic endpoint cap matches the actual source frame There is also a direct comparison with the matched endpoint modules used by the pointed tetrahedral recoupling. Use the quantum affine Hopf algebra XY=QYX, Delta X=X tensor X, Delta Y=X tensor Y+Y tensor 1, S(X)=X^(-1), S(Y)=-X^(-1)Y. For g=(lambda,mu), with nonzero lambda,mu, take the existing endpoint module E_(g;a,b)=k[z]/(z^N-lambda), X f=z f, Y f=(b-a z)f(Q^(-1)z), b^N=lambda a^N+mu. (7.1) Its inverse affine character is g^(-1)=(lambda^(-1),-mu/lambda), with reversed endpoints b->a. Write tau for the normalized field-algebra trace, tau(f)=(1/N)Tr(multiplication by f). The explicit duality map J_B is the pairing <f,h>_B=tau_z( f(z^(-1))h(z)/(a-b/z) ), f in E_(g^(-1);b,a), h in E_(g;a,b). (7.2) The denominator is a unit when mu!=0, so this is a perfect pairing. X-duality follows by multiplication by z^(-1). For Y-duality change z to Qz in the trace. The weight w(z)=1/(a-b/z) obeys w(z)(a-b/z)=w(Qz)(a-b/(Qz))=1, which proves the antipode pairing equation. Thus the pointed unit on the inverse endpoint module is transported to a specified weighted trace functional, rather than reset to an arbitrary unit covector. The unnormalized endpoint double dual is J_B^(-t) J_(B,inverse)=-X^(-1). (7.3) For a proof, the weight for the inverse endpoint pairing, expressed back in z, is 1/(b-a z)=-z^(-1)w(z). This gives (7.3) directly. The sign is therefore part of the endpoint normalization; it cannot be silently identified with a different pivotal frame. Now make the actual quantum-group comparison. Set lambda=x^(-N), mu=phi, r_i=x^(-1)Q^i, d_i=product_(s=1)^i(b-a x^(-1)Q^s). The evaluation matrix H_(ij)=r_i^j identifies polynomials with functions at the N roots. In that basis Y has entry b-a r_i from i-1 to i. Consequently the exact frame A_g=H^(-1)diag(d_0,...,d_(N-1)) (7.4) takes the actual K^(-1),F_phi matrices to X,Y. Its dual counterpart A_inverse uses x_dual=x^(-1)Q^(-1) and the reversed endpoints. Both frames are invertible when mu!=0. The actual vector v_0 maps to the idempotent supported at r_0. The endpoint unit has actual coordinates sum_i d_i^(-1)v_i. These are the specified vector transports to use in a period; module duality alone does not identify the two selected lines. The transported endpoint unit solves (F_phi+a K^(-1)-b)sum_i d_i^(-1)v_i=0 exactly. The paired cap in the actual bases is exactly A_g^t J_B A_inverse=c(x;a,b) J_x, c(x;a,b)=-1/(N xQ) product_(s=1)^(N-2)(b-a x^(-1)Q^s). (7.5) To prove (7.5), both matrices intertwine the same K,F algebra, which is the full matrix algebra when phi!=0. Their ratio is scalar. The entry pairing the dual zeroth vector with the original (N-1)st vector is d_(N-1)/(N(a-bxQ)). Cancel its last factor b-a x^(-1)Q^(-1) to get (7.5). This determines the full scalar from the actual source frame, with no determinant-root choice. The finite product also gives c(x_dual;b,a)=-x^N c(x;a,b). (7.6) For example, reverse the exponents s=1,...,N-2 and use Q^(N(N-1)/2)=(-1)^(N-1). Thus the source-normalized endpoint pairing J_B/c has double dual (J_B/c)^(-t) (J_(B,inverse)/c_inverse) =lambda X^(-1)=X^(N-1). (7.7) Under the actual Hopf identification X=K^(-1), this is precisely K^(1-N). Equations (7.5)--(7.7) prove that the cyclic endpoint cap, with its finite-factorial source frame, has the actual pivotal normalization at every parity. The normalization is a full function on the marked endpoint cover before any peripheral evaluation. The nilpotent boundary shows concretely why the source must be retained. Choose a=x and let b tend algebraically to 1, so phi=b^N-1. On the original side d_i=(Q;Q)_i at b=1, all nonzero for i<N. The inverse endpoint frame instead has diagonal factors d'_j=x^j product_(s=1)^j(1-bQ^(s+1)). At b=1 its last factor d'_(N-1) vanishes simply; the other diagonal factors are nonzero. At the same time (7.2) has a simple pole in its root component z=x^(-1). The complete product (7.5), after cancellation, has the regular value [A_g^t J_B A_inverse]_(b=1) =J_x/[x(1-Q)]. (7.8) Indeed product_(s=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^s)=N gives c(x;x,1)=1/[x(1-Q)]. Thus the whole cap is nondegenerate even though its separate inverse endpoint frame has rank N-1 after ordinary specialization. The missing last column in (7.8) comes from multiplying the simple pole by the first normal coefficient of d'_(N-1). Deleting that coefficient gives a zero last column and cannot yield the actual cap. This is an explicit instance of the linking pairing (5.2)--(5.5), with a single normal source direction. No analytic limiting argument or replacement of the actual invariant is involved. There is also uniform normalization control on this actual boundary. At the Kashaev color |x|=1, (7.8) gives exactly |c(x;x,1)|=1/(2 sin(pi/N)), N/(2pi)<=|c(x;x,1)|<=N/4. (7.9) The elementary bounds 2/N<=sin(pi/N)<=pi/N prove the inequalities. The nonzero entries of J_x and of the actual pivot all have modulus one there; a cap or cup has operator norm sqrt(N). The scalar endpoint comparisons and their inverses have polynomial size. A fixed finite composition of these turn maps has an operator norm bounded by a fixed power of N. Such an upper bound gives no lower bound for the value of a cap on a specified tensor. Nonvanishing and cancellation in the selected global contraction, and the norm of an arbitrary moving endpoint frame, remain separate. The selected endpoint units also have a literal relative period interpretation. Equation (7.2) gives <1,1>_B=-a^(N-1)lambda/mu, <1,1>_(B/c)=-a^(N-1)lambda/(mu c). (7.10) To prove it, use tau((b-a z)^(-1))=b^(N-1)/(b^N-a^N lambda) and z/(az-b)=(1/a)(1-b/(b-az)). These are finite algebraic trace identities. For a=x, mu=b^N-1 the exact normal coefficient is therefore [mu <1,1>_(B/c)]_(mu=0)=-(1-Q). (7.11) This is nonzero at every N>=2. It is an evaluation of the regularized algebraic period, equivalently the residue of <1,1>_(B/c) d mu. In the normal coordinate b-1 its leading polar coefficient has the additional factor 1/N; the two normal coordinates are not conflated. This identifies a specific local source as a marked cyclic period residue, with its normalization fixed by the actual pivot. The internal cap coordinate mu has not thereby been identified with a peripheral meridian coordinate or with a global Bloch-regulator realization. This closes a marked local duality comparison between the cyclic endpoint module used in recoupling and the actual quantum-group source. Its tensor products, duals and already specified exterior contractions transport with their full factors. It does not yet identify all geometric tetrahedron face data or the selected global source on a positive ideal triangulation. ## 8. Coverage and independent checks Duality, pivotal traces and torsion linking pairings are standard structures; no novelty is claimed. The actual pivot and state definitions are those already fixed from [Brown--Dimofte--Garoufalidis--Geer, 2005.08176](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08176). The abstract of [Geer--Patureau-Mirand--Turaev, 0711.4229](https://arxiv.org/abs/0711.4229) already covers nonzero modified dimensions when ordinary dimensions vanish, including the nilpotent quantum-sl(2) invariants containing Kashaev's invariant. The independent calculations here concern the exact source frame, pivot, duality maps and lattice pairing in the current conventions; no published modified-trace proof is a premise. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_relative_pivotal_duality.py) checks 36 duality cases at generic/Kashaev colors and nilpotent/ nonzero wraps for N=2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,12. It verifies all generator intertwinings, all four snake identities, Hopf caps/cups, the exact double-dual pivot, the forced central degeneration and the zero ordinary bubble. Explicit turns recover the entire scalar cut in 30 actual braid cases, with the original pivot and framing. Nine two-direction factorial extensions have flat dual sources, reciprocal full meridian norms and the paired non-scalar cut loops. Eighteen cyclic endpoint caps match the actual dual frame with their explicit finite-factorial scalar and exact pivot; their complete nilpotent cap remains nondegenerate with the lost first normal coefficient retained. Ten carry quotients have perfect balanced residue forms and perfect lost-fiber pairings. All pass. Nine reversed triangle algebras verify (6.3)--(6.4), including the exact Q and transpose. Nine induced face pairings verify (6.5)--(6.7), their invertibility, scalar and both relative generator intertwinings. Their unit transport also exhibits the required nonconstant covector. These checks all pass. [Results](../experiments/relative_pivotal_duality_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_relative_pivotal_duality.py The subsequent [source flag carry extension](source_flag_carry_extension.md) now extends ordered source/tree frames through the marked source infinity on the common carry lattice. Its maps preserve the actual sublattice and transport the full dual by inverse transpose, so the linking form and lost normal directions remain paired there. The original whole cut and all peripheral factors are retained. It does not separately specialize a polar endpoint cap or identify the global geometric source and regulator norm. The uniform proofs above, rather than the finite samples, establish the stated dualities. The global marked geometric period comparison and the volume conjecture remain unproved.

title: Independent audit of the relative whole-word Green map
text: # Independent audit of the relative whole-word Green map Audit, 27 October 2026. The proof in [relative_word_green_transport.md](relative_word_green_transport.md) passes its weighted-source, Green-current and relative-map checks. No test rerun was required. Weighting a transfer coefficient by \(w_t^{k_t}\) does not alter integer-index conservation. After one-cut knot closure, every weighted array remains diagonal in that cut, so the original coupon equals normalized trace on the entire weighted family. Transfer and cut number moments are exactly Euler derivatives of these weights. For a knot closure, the one-cycle braid permutation expresses the other edge indices as integral-affine functions of the transfer indices and one cut index; for a general link one would retain additional initial-index weights. For the zero-extended array transform, \(Z_w[S_i f]=w_i^{-1}Z_w[f]\). Multiplication by \(S_i^{-1}p\) becomes \(p(E_w-e_i)\); therefore the stated Euler operator acts on the entire following Laurent factor and array transform. This gives exactly the printed Green current and commuting weight-current differential, including the support-shift terms. For any actual map \(O:V\to W\), differentiation of \[ O_{\rm rel}(\sigma)=e^{\sigma T_W}Oe^{-\sigma T_V} \] gives the bulk chain identity. Its endpoint maps are \(O\) and \(e^{T_W}Oe^{-T_V}\), with the stated orientations. These maps compose and tensor strictly. Multiplication by the inverse exponential in the transgression proves its naturality without requiring \(OT_V=T_WO\). The number lift is \(n-N\sigma T\), since \([n,T]=NT\). For \(a=w^N\), the exact clock lift follows from \(D_aT=aTD_a\): \[ e^{\sigma T}w^jD_ae^{-\sigma T} =w^je^{\sigma(1-a)T}D_a. \] Its Euler derivative at \(w=1\) recovers the same number lift. For the finite projection \(PT=0\), the relative projector is \(e^{\sigma T}P\); it is idempotent because \(Pe^{\sigma T}=P\). Under Mellin, multiplication by \(T\) becomes multiplication by \(u\), so its endpoint is the marked \(UP\). The Rees map commutes with \(u\), and the actual transformed projector consequently has relative factor \(e^{(\sigma-p/d)u}P\), with its head flags unchanged. Conjugating the fully head-projected word gives the stated whole-word coefficient and the same exponential. It does not create a regular cyclic vacuum or an infinite trace. These are exact source and current maps for the actual finite word. The note correctly retains the separate unresolved map from the geometric Gaussian coefficient space. Strict relative functoriality does not force its horizontal generator to have a nonzero image, erase its endpoint defects, or determine the selected norm.

title: A strict relative transport for the whole weighted word and its Green currents
text: # A strict relative transport for the whole weighted word and its Green currents Research proof, 27 October 2026. The actual complete finite word, with every intermediate head projector, has a strict Fock-relative extension. It carries the **whole weighted generating family** and hence every explicit least-moment Green current, rather than only the unweighted cut coupon. Its endpoint operators are specified exactly.
