For the actual clock B and cyclic repair P, with Z=Q^N and e=e_0 e_0^t, BPB inverse P inverse=Q[I+(Z inverse-1)e], original source matrix=e sum_(r=0)^(N-1)P^r. The [rank-one moment/source proof](actual_rank_one_multiplicative_moment_and_orbit_source.md) keeps its divided wall projector, the original orbit co-source and both actual endpoint deletions. The [aligned cyclic frame theorem](flat_cyclic_source_frame_and_scalar_period.md) classifies this whole source-cyclic chart directly: its endpoint-corrected function/shift algebra is Mat_N. Its unmarked frame ambiguity is a line bundle, removed by a vector marking. The defect must be aligned with the actual source; rank one and flatness alone do not impose that alignment. The scalar of a closed actual word is separate from the rigid frame. The geometric fiber also has a simpler global function. Factor U-V=u(a,b) and put (c,d)=(a,b)V inverse. With the original prefix sign sigma, the ACTUAL momentum is p=sigma[c(1-r)-ds]/[ar+bs]. The [Möbius theorem](mobius_fourier_framing_and_intrinsic_norm_pole.md) gives its inverse and identifies r=infinity with the intrinsic pole lambda=-sigma c/a, independent of the cut s. The whole principal density retains the norm 1-lambda^N. For the figure-eight prefix this pole has order six, and principal sampling is singular when six divides N even though the actual finite tensor is regular. The independent wall divisors 1-Q^N and 1-lambda^N therefore cannot be equated or canceled without their actual word/source map. Finally, the [actual zero-source Fourier current](actual_fourier_source_cancellation.md) is not an abstract countermodel. For the ORIGINAL two-cut tensor, W=[(I tensor B)T(I tensor B inverse)-T]/(Q-1) has zero second partial trace WHOLE, preserves its index support, and at a root has raw partial array J_W,j=[J_(j+1)-J_j]/(Q_N-1). Its formal geometric block on the good-A chart is nonzero, with the same regulator action: the leading amplitude is the derivative of the actual Fourier amplitude. Nevertheless its final source sum is exactly zero. The cyclic difference D has a centered inverse of norm at most one on the zero-source subspace, and abs(sum_j J_j)=sqrt(N) dist(J,im D). Thus the last selected norm is a norm in an exact source/current quotient. Local geometric support and Rivin algebraicity do not determine that quotient class. The next required construction must carry the actual original class, its independent wall/norm divisors and the marked relative boundary to the regulator line. No selected nonvanishing or volume limit is inferred from frame rigidity or a nonzero formal block alone. ## 39. The pointed source has an explicit polynomial unfolding before jets The [pointed companion theorem](pointed_companion_source_and_polynomial_hilbert90.md) now gives a stronger positive result than local root smoothness. Retain the source v,ell and aligned moment equation Q inverse XYX inverse Y inverse=I+v w, Xv=v, ell v=1, ell Y=ell. On the source-orbit chart v,Yv,...,Y^(N-1)v is a basis. Relaxing only the fixed finite cyclic equation Y^N=I gives an explicit principal open affine (N-1)-space over the whole Q-unit base. Y is companion with last column t_i, sum t_i=1 and t_0 a unit. The lower moment rows determine X by a polynomial recurrence; the top row then uniquely determines w. This is a scheme classification over arbitrary commutative bases, not a statement about individual jets or only field-valued points. The source forces an exact polynomial factor and its retained dual data. Put chi(z)=det(zI-Y)=(z-1)chi_red(z), h(z)=z^N chi(1/z)=(1-z)h_red(z), G=h(L), L^N=0 the actual lowering shift. Then, without any quantum-gap division, X=G B G inverse, G inverse v=v, ell G=e_0^t h_red(L). Thus clock trivialization carries the residual spectral polynomial into the co-source instead of deleting it. The actual fixed head is the regular section chi=z^N-1 and G=I, with its original orbit row and all peripheral factors retained. There is also a finite source-moment rigidity test. The mixed moments m_j=ell X Y^jv, 1<=j<N, recover all t_i by explicit triangular equations over the ordinary finite-head localization. Their Jacobian is product_(m=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^m), exactly N at a primitive N-th root. The pure moments ell Y^jv=1 cannot recover this polynomial. The theorem therefore supplies an actual finite algebraic test for a proposed transport/source comparison. For the original finite repair P the test recovers ONLY z^N-1. A geometric A-factor cannot be assigned to that same operator by changing its name. The actual quantum meridian transport must first be constructed with its full word/source and then tested by its own mixed moments. Neither the polynomial gauge nor its determinant one supplies a growing-level norm bound. The regulator comparison and the selected volume norm remain unproved. The explicit chart, gauge, retained co-source and moment reconstruction are the general algebraic progress here. ## 40. Actual horizontal transport and a universal complete cut The [actual open meridian theorem](actual_open_meridian_horizontal_source_transport.md) now derives the port character q^(-ell nu) from the unwrapped crossing potential. An actual SECOND-wire scaled Vandermonde W_(j,b)=(M^ell Q^j)^b removes it. Its whole inverse, both normal connections, full peripheral ratio and every alias power are retained. Partial trace is invariant on ALL tensors, so this is an exact source/current map. On the unit meridian arc it is an isometry of the root cyclic source complex. Its remaining meridian operator is the literal longitude insertion, including its Green/current terms. An [actual inverse-pair cut normalization](universal_resonant_cut_and_actual_source.md) now gives a general geometric simplification. Choose the first initial meridian U with nonzero lower-left entry relative to J. The preceding upper meridians are J by discreteness. Inverse Hurwitz moves carry U to the first slot; inserting those moves followed by their inverses preserves the original braid period. Cutting between them gives the actual prefix V=I and ell=0. All added coefficient atoms have a proved common regular open; the inverse graph is a nondegenerate normal stabilization. Writing U=I+c[-beta;1] * (1,beta), t=r+beta s, the actual complete momentum and density are p=1-1/t, r=1/(1-p)-beta s, Omega_cut=-p/[s(1-p)^2] dlog A_cut wedge dlog p. Thus the principal framing pole is the single fixed resonance p=1 for every complete discrete-faithful knot representation in the stated regular geometric model. It is not a finite quantum pole: the actual array is regular. Near p=1-zeta/N the framing escapes as r=N/zeta-beta s. The full source/current completion in this escaping region, and the global selected geometric coefficient, remain unproved. No replacement of that completion by the sampled principal density is made. The [actual meridian/shell audit](actual_meridian_companion_source_compatibility.md) and [Borel divided-cap period](actual_borel_regular_fusion_and_divided_cap_period.md) also distinguish genuine source transport from the auxiliary companion chart. The latter's root-center normal is abelian-local; it is not the hyperbolic critical branch. The next comparison must retain the actual word while crossing to that branch and controlling the marked escaping source. The three central gates in [the critical-path audit](critical_path_to_original_volume_conjecture.md) are still open.

title: Pointed descent on the central Kashaev fiber
text: # Pointed descent on the central Kashaev fiber Research note, 25 October 2026. This supplies a nonzero meridian anchor for the actual literature state and uses it to remove the central comparison ambiguity on the fiber containing the Kashaev evaluation. It also gives a cofactor formula for that evaluation from a specified quantum A-operator when its rational solution line has rank one. It does not prove that rank hypothesis for every knot or establish the regulator norm comparison. The subsequent [all-level A-period theorem](all_level_a_period.md) removes the rank and regular-orbit conditions from a different exact presentation. It uses cross-level polynomial rigidity, finitely many fixed small colors, and uniformly bounded q-jets. The [meridian-jet theorem](bounded_meridian_jets.md) gives the corresponding integral-kernel bound without assuming rank one. All conventions and the literature state are those independently fixed in [the ADO pointing note](kashaev_ado_pointing.md). The torsor and classical target remain those of [the primary A-polynomial formulation](a_polynomial_torsor_status.md). ## 1. An anchor at the trivial quotient color Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), and use M=-q^(alpha+1). The reduced literature period F_N is Laurent polynomial in M. For every knot, F_N(-q)=1, F_N(1)=<K>_N. (1.1) More generally, for 1<=j<=N, F_N(-q^j)=C_j(q), (1.2) where C_j is the normalized reduced j-dimensional highest-weight period, with unknot value one. It is the usual reduced colored-Jones normalization already compared directly in the crossing note. Here only fixed small j is needed to specify initial values; no Jones asymptotic or literature comparison theorem is a premise. ### Direct filtered-linear-algebra proof At alpha=j-1 the N-dimensional color has E v_a=[a]_q[j-a]_q v_(a-1), F v_a=v_(a+1), K v_a=q^(j-1-2a)v_a. The subspace U=span(v_j,...,v_(N-1)) is invariant under E,F,K,H. Its quotient W has dimension j and is exactly the standard j-color. The finite R and its inverse preserve U on each individual input strand and induce the usual R on the quotient. Terms of degree at least j vanish there. The pivotal matrix preserves U as well. The following elementary trace fact is the relevant functoriality. Use a basis adapted to U and its quotient on each strand of a braid whose closure is a knot. Along an underlying strand, a state that has entered U cannot leave U, since the crossing factors preserve the subspace. In the induced cut operator on W, the open strand starts and ends in the quotient. Partial trace identifies the other endpoints. The braid permutation is a single cycle, so every traced state contributing to this quotient block stays in W throughout. Thus the induced cut operator is precisely the cut operator with all strands colored by W. This assertion would need modification for a separate closed link component not attached to the cut. The two pivotal conventions on W differ by epsilon_j=(-1)^(j-1): K^(1-N)=epsilon_j*K, theta_ADO=epsilon_j*q^((j^2-1)/2). For a b-strand knot braid of writhe w, w and b-1 have the same parity. The total convention factor is therefore epsilon_j^(b-1-w)=1. This proves (1.2). In particular j=1 is the trivial quotient and gives the anchor in (1.1). For each fixed j, C_j(q) is analytic near q=1 and C_j(1)=1. This also follows directly from the finite matrices: [k]_q! tends to k!, R tends to the identity, the braid tends to its permutation, and the cut trace of a one-cycle permutation is the identity. These initial periods consequently have no level-dependent exponential normalization. The compatibility of integer colors and ADO is existing coverage; Willetts, [2003.09854](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.09854), states a more extensive unification. Its completion and recursion theorems are not used in the proof above. ## 2. Pointing kills the central scalar on the relevant fiber Let sigma(M)=qM with q of order n, E=C(M), K=C(u), u=M^n. If h and g span the same nonzero rational solution line, then g=c(u)h, c in K^*. (2.1) Suppose h is regular at M_0, h(M_0)!=0, and the corresponding germ of g is regular with g(M_0)=h(M_0). It follows that c is regular at u_0=M_0^n and c(u_0)=1. At every other point of that sigma-orbit where h is regular, g has the same value as h. This is an exact central-fiber statement, not a uniform growth bound. It permits arbitrarily level-dependent c; its value on this fiber has already been fixed by the pointing. For the literature state, n=2N and M_*=-q, M_+=1, M_* q^(N-1)=M_+, M_*^(2N)=M_+^(2N)=1. (2.2) Thus a comparison within the same rational solution line, normalized by the actual anchor F_N(M_*)=1, has no remaining central multiplier at the Kashaev point. ### A sufficient operator condition for the solution line Given a specified operator P and its cyclic module as in the intrinsic norm-torsor note, assume the row kernel of H-1 has dimension one over E. Then all rational solutions form a one-dimensional K-vector space, provided one nonzero solution exists. Indeed a solution h defines the E-linear pairing ell_h by ell_h(T^j e)=sigma^j h. It satisfies ell_h(H-1)=0. Two such pairings are E-proportional by the kernel hypothesis, so g=c(M)h. Their compatibility with T gives sigma(c)=c, hence c belongs to K. The hypothesis concerns geometric multiplicity one; it does not require H to be semisimple. It must be checked for the actual operator. ### An explicit period generator from Hilbert 90 This criterion also constructs a rational period from the operator. Write T=B*sigma on the cyclic module and choose a nonzero row w with wH=w. On this row line define Gamma(w)=sigma(w)B^(-1)=a*w. The identity sigma(H)=B^(-1)HB preserves the line, and Gamma^n(w)=wH^(-1)=w, so Norm(a)=1. The explicit Hilbert-90 sum f(c)=sum_(j=0)^(n-1) [a*sigma(a)*...*sigma^(j-1)(a)]*sigma^j(c) has a choice of c for which it is a unit and a*sigma(f)=f. Consequently ell=f*w obeys sigma(ell)=ell B. Its first component h is a nonzero rational solution of the original scalar operator. Changing c or the row frame changes h only by a central factor. Normalize on the specified root germs M_+(u)=u^(1/n), M_*(u)=-q*u^(1/n). Then for the reduced state <K>_N=[h(M_+(u))/h(M_*(u))]_(u=1), n=2N, (2.3) with common zeros and poles canceled as a whole germ. This is the explicit norm-torsor/Hilbert-90 version of the cofactor period below. It does not require equating D_n with the classical A-polynomial. The one-dimensional solution-line hypothesis cannot simply be omitted. For even N, the equation (T^2-1)h=0 admits both h=1 and g=1+c*(M^N+1). They have the same value one at M=-q, but their values at M=1 differ by 2c. This is an abstract equation, not a knot counterexample. It explains the need for either the verified line hypothesis or the finite initial-value data in Section 6. ## 3. The full ADO state is anchored by a central residue Write N_N(M)=d_N(M)F_N(M) and eta_N=i^(N+3), as before. At M_* the full state has a pole, so one must not replace the anchor by an undefined ordinary value. Instead (u-1)N_N(M)=eta_N*(M-M^(-1))*M^N*F_N(M), [(u-1)N_N]_(M=-q)=eta_N*(-1)^N*(q-q^(-1)). (3.1) The last quantity is nonzero. At M=1, by contrast, the whole full period is regular and N_N(1)=eta_N*<K>_N/N. The same central fiber therefore requires different meridian frames at its two marked points. To verify the residue, M_*^N=(-1)^(N+1) and M_*-M_*^(-1)=-(q-q^(-1)). Equation (1.1) then gives (3.1). If a rational comparison of full states preserves this residue, (2.1) again gives c(1)=1. It therefore preserves the regular full state value at M=1, and hence the Kashaev value. This is the same pointed descent with its actual peripheral lattice. ## 4. The root period can be read from the quantum A-operator Let P(q,M,T) be a specified reduced-state annihilator. At q=q_N, view it as a K-linear operator on E, using E=K[M]/(M^n-u), n=2N, basis 1,M,...,M^(n-1), X=multiplication by M, S=diag(1,q,...,q^(n-1)), A_n(u)=sum_j a_j(q_N,X)S^j. (4.1) This is an n by n matrix over K. Assume its generic nullity is one. It is a direct checkable condition on the given root-level A-module. Then its kernel is exactly K*F_N, since F_N is a nonzero solution. Work over the DVR O=C[u]_(u-1). The integral period lattice Lambda=ker_K(A_n) intersection O^n is free of rank one and saturated in O^n. The Laurent polynomial F_N is in this lattice and is primitive because F_N(M_*)=1. For any primitive generator w of Lambda, let e_+=(1,1,...,1), e_*=(1,M_*,...,M_*^(n-1)). The denominator e_* w(1) is nonzero and <K>_N=e_+ w(1)/(e_* w(1)). (4.2) This is the period pairing on a pointed projective kernel line. It contains no free normalization scalar. Clear rational denominators of A_n by a central scalar and choose any nonzero column w_raw of its adjugate. Generically its rank is n-1, so such a column spans the kernel. Divide out the common (u-1)-valuation to obtain w. Equivalently compute <K>_N=[(e_+ w_raw(u))/(e_* w_raw(u))]_(u=1), (4.3) as a whole central germ. This remains valid if all the displayed cofactors vanish at u=1 and the specialized matrix has a larger kernel. The saturated generic line, rather than the whole enlarged special kernel, specifies the period. A different nonzero column, or a central clearing denominator, gives the same ratio. The construction also applies to a specified finite system of annihilators, hence to the joint kernel of generators of a quantum A-ideal. If that joint kernel has dimension one, choose n-1 independent rows from the stacked matrix and take their signed maximal minors. They give the same projective kernel line and the same pointed ratio. Independence of the row choice follows from uniqueness of a one-dimensional kernel. No arbitrary favorable generator of an ideal is being substituted for the actual system. ## 5. The full-state formula retains one meridian jet The actual reduced/full gauge is multiplication by the nonzero rational function d_N over E. It is a K-linear isomorphism, so the generic rational kernel dimensions in these two normalizations agree. Their integral frames at u=1 differ, which is why the full state requires the jet below. For a full-state annihilator with generic rational nullity one, its integral kernel is generated by the primitive vector for R_N=(u-1)N_N. At M=1 this vector has zero evaluation. Its first meridian jet, rather than that zero value, gives the full state. Choose the root M_+(u)=u^(1/n) with value one, and M_*(u)=-q*u^(1/n). Let e_+(u),e_*(u) be their evaluation rows in the monomial basis. For a primitive generator w, j_+(w)=sum_(j=0)^(n-1)[w_j'(1)+(j/n)w_j(1)], <K>_N=N*(-1)^N*(q-q^(-1))*j_+(w)/(e_* w(1)). (5.1) This follows by differentiating R_N(M_+(u))=(u-1)N_N(M_+(u)) and using the nonzero residue (3.1) to fix the scalar at u=1. A derivative of that scalar does not contribute, since e_+w(1)=0. For any nonzero adjugate column the equivalent whole-germ formula is <K>_N=N*(-1)^N*(q-q^(-1))* [ e_+(u)w_raw(u) / ((u-1)e_*(u)w_raw(u)) ]_(u=1). (5.2) The specified root germs are essential here. Equations (4.3) and (5.2) give the same period under the actual reduced/full ADO gauge. This explains precisely where a first jet and the peripheral factor enter an intrinsic A-operator formulation. ## 6. A finite initial-value presentation when the orbit is regular There is another exact presentation that does not require a one-dimensional rational solution space. Suppose the scalar operator has order d and its coefficients and forward companion matrix are regular at the orbit points M_j=-q^j, j=1,...,N-d, with nonzero leading coefficient there. The equation propagates the initial vector (F_N(M_1),...,F_N(M_d))=(C_1(q),...,C_d(q)) (6.1) to F_N(M_N)=<K>_N by its ordered companion product. For fixed d the initial periods are the analytic, level-independent functions of q in Section 1. The quantum A-equation and this finite pointing specify the exact period on that orbit. At singular orbit points the stated propagation argument cannot simply divide by a vanishing coefficient; the integral lattice or additional compatibility must be retained. The subsequent all-level theorem supplies this compatibility from the actual integer-color identities. It first propagates rational functions in q and then evaluates the whole q-germ at q_N. Its jet bound is D(s-1), with D the leading M-span and s its support size; it does not assume the fixed-q meridian jets are bounded. ## 7. Remaining volume theorem Under the hypotheses of Section 4, (4.3) is an A-operator-only formula for the actual literature period. Consequently the requested volume conjecture is exactly the assertion that this pointed cofactor ratio has logarithmic growth Vol(S^3 minus K)/(2pi). No replacement invariant is being defined by a favorable quantization. This is not a proof of that growth statement. A nonzero actual all-level knot operator is now supplied by the [finite cut-state argument](finite_sum_annihilator.md). Its geometric classical symbol and comparison of the pointed period with the marked regulator still require proof in the desired knot class. Solution-rank and orbit-regularity conditions remain hypotheses of the particular formulas above; the all-level whole-germ presentation no longer needs them. The reference anchor removes the residual central normalization once the comparison line has been identified; it does not identify a geometric period with that line by itself. The independent checks in `experiments/audit_root_orbit_pointing.py` compare full and quotient colors directly and test the cofactor and lattice prescription, including a fiber where the matrix rank drops. They supplement the uniform arguments above.

title: The saturated critical variety has no excess-volume boundary
text: # The saturated critical variety has no excess-volume boundary 28 October 2026. The actual full-Psi period now has a calibrated regulator at every regular FULL critical point, including its integer cut marks. This note extends that conclusion to the entire shape compactification of those critical points. It also distinguishes this compactification from the much larger set obtained by retaining only cleared equations or weak angle constraints. The result concerns the ACTUAL critical variety. It does not assert that every endpoint of the original integration cycle lies in that variety. In particular it does not prove an upper bound for the whole period or its nonzero geometric coefficient. ## 1. The fixed algebraic object Fix the original signed knot diagram and its complete peripheral mark. Use the regular rational canonical graphs of its nine-atom crossings, with all original cap equations. Exponentiating the FULL critical equations gives a finite-type algebraic variety X over Q (with the specified finite sign/lift data). Invert all denominators used by these graphs and all shape factors z and 1-z. Retain only the components meeting this regular locus. Thus X describes genuine regular boundary-parabolic knot representations with their auxiliary frames; it is not a freely enlarged cleared gluing scheme. Every integer cut mark adds 2*pi*i times the logarithm of an actual monomial. It leaves these exponentiated equations unchanged. The exact [critical-action calculation](actual_wall_critical_regulator.md) gives Im W_m(x) = R(x) := sum_j epsilon_j D(z_j(x)) = Vol(rho_x), (1) whenever the marked lift is a FULL critical point. Here D is the single-valued Bloch--Wigner function and epsilon_j is the actual signed atom multiplicity. The scalar and peripheral normalization are those in that calculation. No change of source is made here. There are finitely many rational shape functions for this fixed word. Let Y be the Zariski closure of their JOINT image in (P^1)^s. Equivalently take the graph of all shape functions on X, close it in a projective compactification of X times (P^1)^s, and use the proper projection to the shape factors. Closing only over affine X and projecting would miss possible escaping limits and is not the operation intended here. Using the joint image prevents unrelated boundary values of different atoms from being assembled into a fictitious critical configuration. ## 2. The regulator is constant on each critical component Here is an elementary face calculation establishing the required constancy without a rigidity citation. Choose vector lifts v_i for an idealized tetrahedron and put p_ij=det(v_i,v_j). Work in the rational multiplicative group, so signs have zero class. In the six edge classes a=[p_01], b=[p_02], c=[p_03], d=[p_12], e=[p_13], f=[p_23], the convention of the actual fundamental-cycle note gives [z]=e+b-c-d, [1-z]=a+f-c-d. (2) Define the oriented triangular expression T(i,j,k)=[p_ij] wedge [p_jk] +[p_jk] wedge [p_ki] +[p_ki] wedge [p_ij]. (3) Expansion of the exterior products gives the exact identity [z] wedge [1-z] =-T(1,2,3)+T(0,2,3)-T(0,1,3)+T(0,1,2). (4) For a boundary-parabolic representation, decorate each lifted cusp vertex by its peripheral fixed vector. Peripheral SL2 eigenvalues are signs, so face transports preserve the determinant classes used above. Interior auxiliary vertices are decorated equivariantly. Summing (4) over the oriented idealized relative fundamental cycle cancels its paired faces. Hence its Bloch sum beta has delta(beta)=0 in the rational multiplicative wedge of the component's function field. An ordinary cusp-only ideal triangulation can be identically degenerate for a nonfaithful representation. To avoid taking the wedge of zero in that case, first barycentrically subdivide the abstract relative fundamental cycle and decorate its new free interior vertices generically and equivariantly. Each refined tetrahedron contains at most one original cusp vertex; its other vertices belong to distinct free vertex types. On the component's function field, adjoining independent generic decorations makes all the finitely many required determinants nonzero. Face transports still match. The extra vertex stars are interior balls: idealizing their decorations is the limit of the ordinary finite-vertex chain identity and changes no total regulator. The explicit crossing five-term certificate identifies the actual coefficient regulator with this same fundamental regulator. Thus the argument also covers components where the initial ideal triangulation is degenerate. For nontrivial meridians, peripheral parabolicity follows directly: in PSL2 the centralizer of a nonidentity unipotent consists of the unipotents fixing its unique point. The longitude commutes with the meridian. If a knot meridian is trivial, normal generation makes the entire representation trivial, with regulator zero. The differential identity dD(z)=log|z| dArg(1-z)-log|1-z| dArg z (5) factors through this multiplicative wedge. Thus dR=0 on the smooth regular part of each irreducible complex component of X. That part is connected. Continuity extends its constant value across its other regular points. There are only finitely many irreducible components, so the regular critical regulator takes a FINITE set of real values. This statement allows positive-dimensional components and does not assume that every representation is isolated. The same conclusion holds for the nine-atom sum: its regulator equals the five-symbol crossing regulator identically on each regular rational crossing graph, by the independently audited wedge/real-anchor proof. ## 3. Every genuine critical degeneration retains the same value The function D extends continuously to P^1(C), with value zero at 0, 1 and infinity. For example, for |z|<1/2 the convergent dilogarithm series and the logarithm bound give |D(z)| <= 2|z|(1+|log|z||). The identities D(1-z)=-D(z) and D(1/z)=-D(z) give the other two limits. Therefore the signed sum R extends continuously to all of (P^1)^s, including simultaneous zeros and poles of different atoms. The image of a regular algebraic component is constructible and dense in its Zariski closure; it is also dense in that closure in the complex topology. Indeed it contains a dense Zariski-open subset of the closure, and a proper complex algebraic subset has no analytic interior. Every point of that closure is consequently a limit of actual regular shape tuples. The extended R has the SAME constant value at every such limit. Combining this with the independently proved representation-volume bound in [the smearing argument](regular_critical_values_and_representation_volume_bound.md) gives |sum_j epsilon_j D(z_j)| <= Vol(M) (6) on ALL of Y, including its degenerate boundary. In fact each component of Y carries one of the finitely many values from Section 2. Components with different values cannot intersect in this joint shape compactification, since R is continuous there. This also covers an escaping sequence of genuine regular critical representations: compactness of (P^1)^s gives convergent shape subsequences, and none acquires a larger limiting regulator. It does not cover a sequence of approximate critical points with an uncontrolled gradient times an unbounded logarithmic coordinate. For those points the exact residual Im W-R=rho dot Im(gradient W) need not vanish. ## 4. Why saturation matters: an exact Pachner example The ordinary rational two-to-three shape map can be written w=xy, u=x(1-y)/(1-xy), v=y(1-x)/(1-xy). (7) Its cleared graph equations are f1=w-xy, f2=(1-w)u-x+w, f3=(1-w)v-y+w. (8) These equations alone contain the spurious surface x=y=w=1 with u,v arbitrary. Put g=uv-w(1-u)(1-v). Writing X0=w+(1-w)u and Y0=w+(1-w)v gives the exact certificate (1-w)g = -f1+f2*Y0+x*f3. (9) Consequently g belongs to (f1,f2,f3):(1-w)^infinity. Conversely, when w!=1, equation g=0 and x=X0,y=Y0 recover (7). The saturated graph therefore has the additional necessary equation g=0 even on its boundary. At w=1 it requires u+v=1. The collapsed three-tetrahedron regulator there is D(1)+D(u)+D(1-u)=0. In contrast, the unsaturated equations admit x=y=w=1, u=v=i. Their putative output regulator is 2D(i)>0, whereas the input regulator is zero. This point is excluded by g=2i-1!=0. Thus even ONE cleared Pachner graph can manufacture extra boundary volume. The failure has an exact algebraic certificate; it is not a question of numerical optimization or choice of a logarithmic lift. This example is not asserted to be the existing nine-tetrahedron oversized alias. The general consequence is sufficient: the certified oversized alias, once interpreted as its joint shape tuple, cannot belong to the saturated genuine critical closure if its regulator exceeds Vol(M). Weak angle compatibility never established that membership in the first place. ## 5. What this removes from the remaining problem Uncontrolled volume of a genuine critical degeneration is no longer an obstruction in this algebraic compactification. A proof of the quantum upper bound must still show that every exponentially relevant boundary contribution of the ORIGINAL relative cycle is supported on this critical closure, is canceled exactly, or obeys an independent estimate. Ordinary constrained endpoint maxima need not satisfy the full critical equations; they are not covered by (6). The lower bound also remains independent. A bounded list of possible critical rates does not show that the original cycle has a nonzero coefficient on the component with value Vol(M). The accompanying exact audit checks the universal exterior identity (4), the saturation certificate (9), elimination of the saturated Pachner graph, and the explicit false cleared-graph boundary point. These checks support the proofs above; no finite knot census is used to infer the general statement.

title: The whole meridian profile and its regular period are equivalent
text: # The whole meridian profile and its regular period are equivalent Research proof, 27 October 2026. The canonical actual polar subtraction gives a uniform comparison of the whole scaled meridian function and its regular period, including every fixed resonance center. The original full-state monomial supplies an even resonance factor exactly. Uniform division across its zeros is justified by a fixed boundary norm, not by pointwise division or a jet argument. The result is conditional only on the explicitly stated domination of the polynomial-size ordinary-color tail when normalized by the Kashaev value. It does not assert that this growth or a whole profile limit exists for a general hyperbolic knot. It also keeps the fixed-root meridian normal distinct from the moving-q integral-color normal. ## 1. Exact actual functions and the tail assumption used here Use the actual functions of [the regularized Kashaev period](regularized_kashaev_period.md): q_N=exp(pi*i/N), Q_N=q_N^2, Y=M^2, K_N=F_N(1), S_N(Y)=1+Y+...+Y^(N-1), F_N(Y)=S_N(Y)R_N(Y)+P_N(Y). (1) Here P_N is the unique polynomial of degree at most N-2 with `P_N(Q_N^j)=C_j(q_N)`, 1<=j<N, and R_N is Laurent polynomial. The ordinary-color theorem gives |C_j(q_N)|<=D_N, D_N<= (N/2)^(b-1), |[Y^r]P_N|<=2D_N, 0<=r<=N-2. (2) Work along any sequence with K_N nonzero and epsilon_N=N D_N/|K_N| ->0. (3) A positive exponential lower bound for |K_N| implies (3), but is stronger than needed here. Put c=2pi*i and use the entire scaled meridian coordinate M_N(z)=exp(z/(2N)), Y_N(z)=exp(z/N), U=Y_N(z)^N=exp(z). Define g_N(z)=F_N(Y_N(z))/K_N, pi_N(z)=P_N(Y_N(z))/K_N, r_N(z)=N R_N(Y_N(z))/K_N, rho_N(z)=M_N(z)^(N-1) r_N(z). (4) All these functions are entire in z. The retained monomial in rho_N is the original full-state normalization, not a newly chosen gauge. For any compact K in the z-plane and every nonnegative integer l, the coefficient formula (2) gives the direct bound sup_K |partial_z^l pi_N| <=2(N-1)D_N exp(max(0,sup_K Re z))/|K_N|. (5) Indeed each differentiated exponential contributes `(r/N)^l`, of modulus at most one. Thus the complete interpolation tail and all its fixed jets vanish locally uniformly under (3). No growing Vandermonde inverse or unproved q-normal estimate is involved. ## 2. The original full-state factor gives an exact even resonance function The symmetric geometric sum gives exactly H_N(z)=S_N(Y_N(z))/[N M_N(z)^(N-1)] =sinh(z/2)/[N sinh(z/(2N))]. (6) At apparent common zeros this is its entire continuation. It is even and H_N(0)=1. Hence (1) becomes the exact whole identity g_N=H_N rho_N+pi_N. (7) The uncentered geometric sum would instead tend to `(exp(z)-1)/z`. Its additional factor `exp(z/2)` is accounted for by the exact monomial in (4). Removing or ignoring that factor would give the wrong Weyl transformation for the regular coefficient. Put H(z)=2sinh(z/2)/z, H(0)=1. On every fixed disk, for all sufficiently large N, H_N(z)=H(z)B_N(z), B_N(z)=[z/(2N)]/sinh(z/(2N)), B_N=1+O_K(N^(-2)). (8) B_N is a holomorphic nonvanishing unit on that disk. Its poles are at the distant points cN times nonzero integers. Thus (8) is locally uniform, including all fixed zeros of H. Those zeros are exactly `z_k=ck`, nonzero integers k; they are simple. For N>|k| they are exact zeros of H_N as well. The full modified dimension from the actual state is d_N(M)=eta_N (M-M^(-1))/(M^N-M^(-N)), eta_N=i^(N+3). Therefore its complete Weyl-even scaled cocycle is exactly N d_N(M_N(z))/eta_N=1/H_N(z). (9) This retains both the actual phase eta_N and every finite root divisor. It is a whole meromorphic identity, not just its value at z=0. In particular the full normalized ADO profile is N calN_N(M_N(z))/(eta_N K_N) =g_N/H_N=rho_N+pi_N/H_N. (10) The last summand must be subtracted before claiming holomorphic uniformity at a resonance. A small nonzero residue still gives a pole. For example C_1=1 forces a nonzero pole at z=c at every finite level, even if its normalized residue tends to zero. There is also an exact actual half-source interpretation. The marked rational Weyl splitting beta_N from [the source Weyl-gluing theorem](twisted_cotangent_source_and_weyl_gluing.md) satisfies beta_N(M)beta_N(M^(-1))=c_N(M)^(-1), c_N(M)=N M^(N-1)/S_N(M^2). Thus, at this scaled meridian, without any limit or growth assumption, c_N(M_N(z))=H_N(z)^(-1), beta_N(M_N(z))beta_N(M_N(-z))=H_N(z). (10a) The odd/even-level phase and its unpaired even-level factor remain the original ones in beta_N. Hence the resonance factor is already the exact norm of the actual marked half-source, not an externally imposed entire function. ### 2.1 It is also the character of the original finite compact source On the actual N-dimensional source let J e_j=j e_j and n=N-1. Then exactly H_N(z)=(1/N)Tr exp[z(J-n/2)/N]. (10b) This is the finite sum (6), with its original 1/N. The compact coherent symbol is explicitly exp[-nz/(2N)] [1+(exp(z/N)-1)T]^n. Its original compact-source period is (10b), by the proved coherent trace formula. Uniformly for z in compact sets and 0<=T<=1 this symbol tends to `exp[z(T-1/2)]`. Consequently H(z)=integral_0^1 exp[z(T-1/2)]dT. (10c) Thus the resonance factor is at once an actual source character, the exact Weyl norm (10a), and the inverse full peripheral cocycle (9). No index theorem or identification of different quantum theories is needed for these equalities. ## 3. Uniform division is valid through every resonance center Choose radii 0<r<R with R not equal to 2pi times a positive integer. Let m_R=min_(|z|=R)|H(z)|>0. For all sufficiently large N, (8) gives `min_(|z|=R)|H_N(z)|>=m_R/2`. Whenever u_N/H_N has its holomorphic continuation to the disk of radius R, the maximum principle gives the fixed division bound ||u_N/H_N||_(|z|<=r) <=(2/m_R)||u_N||_(|z|=R). (11) There is no loss of control at an interior resonance. Its removable quotient is holomorphic before applying the maximum principle. For our exact numerator `u_N=g_N-pi_N`, this condition holds because (7) supplies the entire quotient rho_N. This proves the following equivalence under (3): * g_N converges locally uniformly on C to a holomorphic g; * rho_N converges locally uniformly on C to a holomorphic rho. The same proof is local on any open domain, using finitely many small boundaries avoiding its resonance zeros. The limits are necessarily related by g=H rho, g(0)=rho(0)=1. (12) For the nontrivial implication, at each fixed z_k the exact numerator vanishes for all large N. Equations (5) and local uniform convergence give g(z_k)=0, so g/H has a holomorphic removable continuation. Put rho=g/H. The numerator of rho_N-rho=(g_N-g-pi_N-(H_N-H)rho)/H_N is exactly divisible. Equations (5), (8), and (11) prove local uniform convergence, including all resonance centers. They also give the explicit estimate ||rho_N-rho||_(D_r) <=(2/m_R)[||g_N-g||_(boundary D_R) +||pi_N||_(boundary D_R) +||H_N-H||_(boundary D_R)||rho||_(boundary D_R)]. (13) The forward implication follows directly from (7). The same norms show that local boundedness of the two families is equivalent. In particular the regularization neither manufactures nor loses an unspecified normal-family assumption. At the centers the removable value can be recorded explicitly: rho_N(z_k)=[g_N'(z_k)-pi_N'(z_k)]/H_N'(z_k), H_N'(z_k)=(-1)^k/[2iN sin(pi k/N)], H'(z_k)=(-1)^k/(ck). (14) Thus fixed resonance derivatives and the regular quotient obey the same convergence. Higher derivatives follow either from Cauchy's formula after (13) or by repeated division. ## 4. Weyl symmetry and the regular coefficient The actual [Weyl theorem](actual_weyl_descent.md) gives `F_N(Y^(-1))=F_N(Y)`, hence g_N is exactly even. H_N is even as well. Equation (7) implies H_N(z)[rho_N(z)-rho_N(-z)]=pi_N(-z)-pi_N(z). The numerator is exactly divisible. Applying (11) and (5) proves, even without convergence of rho_N, rho_N(z)-rho_N(-z) ->0 locally uniformly. (15) Every profile rho in (12) is therefore even. It may still be algebraic: the example `rho=1, g=H` satisfies all these resonance, Weyl and normalization constraints. If rho is entire and algebraic over C(z), it is an even polynomial; these identities do not exclude such a regular coefficient. The required whole period factor is already nonalgebraic and supplies all the resonance zeros. By contrast the uncentered limit r satisfies `r(-z)=exp(z)r(z)`. A nonzero global r with this property cannot itself be algebraic. This is a normalization issue resolved by the original full-state monomial, not an obstruction to an algebraic centered coefficient. Also `rho_N(0)=N R_N(1)/K_N=1-P_N(1)/K_N ->1`. Thus R_N(1) is nonzero for all large N on the sequence (3), and using the intrinsic normalization M_N(z)^(N-1)R_N(Y_N(z))/R_N(1) gives the same local-uniform limits and the same equivalence. No division by an unproved nonzero period is made before (3). ## 5. Fixed-root and integral-color normal maps have the same U but different sources Compare the preceding path with the actual integral-color one qfrak_N(z)=exp(c/(2N)+z/(2N^2)), M=-qfrak_N(z)^N=exp(z/(2N)), Qfrak_N(z)^N=exp(z/N)=Y_N(z). (16) Thus M, Y and U=exp(z) agree exactly. The quantum parameter does not: q is fixed at q_N in (1)--(15), while it varies in (16). On the actual common module put delta=1-Q^N, w=M Q^(-N)-M^(-1). The two source paths are exactly fixed root: delta=0, w=M-M^(-1), integral color: delta=1-Y_N(z), w=0. (17) They are different legs of the two-wall geometry. The head-word excursion factor delta*w vanishes on both legs, but that does not identify their derivatives, pivots or selected contractions. The actual ordinary integral pivot/twist differs from the frozen root auxiliary source by the already computed route factor qfrak_N(z)^(Nn kappa_D) (Qfrak_N(z)^N)^(sum_closed j_a), kappa_D=writhe-b+1, n=N-1. Knot parity removes only its root value. In this normal coordinate the remaining whole insertion is exp{z[n kappa_D/(2N)+(sum_closed j_a)/N]}. (18) Its modulus and every fixed z derivative are bounded on compact z sets uniformly in N, since `0<=sum_closed j_a<=(b-1)n`. It remains a nonconstant source insertion. A bound on its individual weights does not control cancellations in a selected sum, so it cannot be deleted when comparing normalized profiles. There is also a q-normal contribution. For a specified auxiliary finite-word lift, the path derivative in (16) contains `q partial_q/(2N^2)` in addition to the fixed-root contribution `M partial_M/(2N)`, together with the actual source derivatives from (18). Neither (2) nor the polar bound (5) bounds that q-normal derivative of the selected quantum word. The integral-color sampling centers are accordingly different: z_(N,k)=-ckN/(N+k) ->-ck, C_N(qfrak_N(z_(N,k)))=C_k(q_(N+k)). (19) These are moving q-color resonances, whereas the fixed-root zeros in (14) are exactly ck at every sufficiently large level. Equations (16)--(19) specify the coordinate and source adapter needed for a comparison; they do not assert equality of the two selected profile functions. ## 6. Exact scope The tail bound, full-state cocycle, quotient norm and equivalence of whole/regular profile convergence are exact consequences of the actual regularized state. They hold through the resonance centers, and retain the marked monomial and full modified dimension. The independent [whole Gamma source comparison](whole_gamma_frame_profile.md) proves an actual function-level refinement, with no K_N growth assumption. If z=ca and Phi_a(T)=G(T)^(-a)/Gamma(1-a), G(T)=(exp(cT)-1)/c, its actual middle-index q-normal residual V_(N,L)(a) and the marked meridian half-source obey N^(-a)beta_N(M_N(ca)) ->Phi_(-a)(1/2), V_(N,L)(a)=u_N(a) beta_N(M_N(-c b)), b=a/(1+a/N), u_N(0)=1, u_N=1+O_K(1/N). (21) The unit is specified by nonvanishing J-products there and remains valid through resonance zeros. The reparametrization b aligns their finite moving and fixed zeros; it cannot be omitted in a unit comparison. Consequently Phi_a(T)Phi_(-a)(T)=H(ca). Thus (10a), (10b) and (21) match actual source functions and their norm, not only a formally similar entire function. These are scalar source-line comparisons. They do not identify the full selected knot modules, their regular period coefficients or the state profiles in (16). In particular the opposite and slightly reparametrized half-source coordinate in (21) is not the identical-M normal path used in (16). No positive volume growth, whole normal-family convergence, algebraicity of the regular coefficient, or equality of q-normal and meridian-normal sourced periods has been proved here. ## 7. Audit [audit_scaled_meridian_regular_profile.py](../experiments/audit_scaled_meridian_regular_profile.py) and its [results](../experiments/scaled_meridian_regular_profile_results.json) check the finite centered character, both marked half-source norms and full cocycle at 85-digit precision, including odd and even N=2 through 18. They check the interpolation coefficient and derivative bound for bounded nodal data, and removable quotient values at the exact positive and negative resonances. The quotient stress family is an explicitly declared universal Laurent-polynomial family satisfying the same interpolation divisibility; it is not asserted to be a knot invariant. The general-knot analytic proof is (5)--(14). A separate compact grid through N=128 checks the improved centered factor rate O(N^(-2)); no general-knot growth assumption is inferred from these audits.

title: A source-sensitive angular homotopy: proved bounds and the remaining cycle theorem
text: # A source-sensitive angular homotopy: proved bounds and the remaining cycle theorem 28 October 2026. This note records two proved analytic facts useful for transporting a selected angular source: an exponential boundary bound, and properness of the critical set for a particular lattice-equivalent phase homotopy. It also records the exact coefficient projection which kills the dominant scalar endpoint expansion in a natural prototype contour. These facts do not yet prove a selected geometric contribution. The double sum below is now the exact transform proved in [the finite five-crossing calculation](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md). Its original triple source and all normalizations are retained. Numerical homotopy continuation results are separated from the proved lemmas. The subsequent selected contour argument is in [the inner contour note](selected_inner_angular_contour.md); the homotopy observations here alone are not that source proof. ## 1. The finite source and its exact phase Let Q=exp(2 pi i/N), F_n=(Q;Q)_n. The candidate at completeness is Z_N=sum_(0<=j<=n<N) W_N(n,j), W_N(n,j)=Q^[-n(n+2)-j(n+1)] F_n^3/[F_j F_(n-j)]. (1) Put x=n/N, y=j/N and J(s)=integral_0^s log(2sin(pi r))dr. The actual factor phases give EXACTLY on this lattice W_N(n,j)=|W_N(n,j)| *exp{iN B(x,y)-pi i(3x+2y)}, B(x,y)=pi(3x+2y-x^2-xy-y^2). (2) The more immediate phase is -pi(x+x^2+xy+y^2). Its difference from B is 4pi x+2pi y, whose N-fold exponential is one at EVERY selected lattice point. This is a change of interpolation mark with no change of the original finite source at the endpoint. Define the actual finite homotopy of this candidate sum by Z_N(t)=sum |W_N(n,j)| *exp{it[N B(x,y)-pi(3x+2y)]}, 0<=t<=1. (3) At t=0 every summand is positive, and at t=1 (3) is exactly (1). This is a specified deformation of the entire finite source, not an inference from formal jets. It does not say that intermediate t is a knot invariant or a quantum-group parameter. On the holomorphic triangle T={ (x,y): 1/2<Re x<1, 0<Re y<Re x }, mark L(z)=Log(2sin(pi z)) by its real value on 0<z<1. The sine has positive real part throughout that strip, so this mark is holomorphic. Let J be its primitive agreeing with the real J above, and put A(x,y)=3J(x)-J(y)-J(x-y), S_t=A+i t B. The leading phase of (3) is S_t. Its derivatives are S_(t,x)=3L(x)-L(x-y)+it pi(3-2x-y), S_(t,y)=-L(y)+L(x-y)+it pi(2-x-2y). (4) The exact factorial interpolation supplies an actual analytic summand with these uniform leading terms; no scalar exterior Euler approximation is needed for that construction. ## 2. Strict real concavity and the actual boundary envelope On the REAL late triangle 1/2<x<1, 0<y<x, A is strictly concave. Indeed put a=cot(pi x), b=cot(pi y), c=cot(pi(x-y)). Then H_A/pi=[[3a-c,c],[c,-b-c]], b+c=sin(pi x)/[sin(pi y)sin(pi(x-y))]>0, a=(bc-1)/(b+c)<0. The lower diagonal is negative, and det H_A/pi^2=3-2bc>1. (5) Thus the real positive sum at t=0 has one nondegenerate late interior maximum. Its y-coordinate is x/2. If c_0=cos(pi x/2), the remaining equation is 32(1-c_0^2)c_0^3=1, which has one root in the interval corresponding to 1/2<x<1. Numerically x=0.78786562191785..., y=x/2. The phase maximum is about 0.6124533677523. These decimals are descriptive; the uniqueness follows from strict concavity and the boundary signs. Let c_*=max_(0<=s<=1)J(s)=J(5/6)=v_3/(2pi), where v_3 is the regular ideal tetrahedron volume. The uniform root-factorial estimate gives log|W_N(n,j)|=N A(n/N,j/N)+O(log N) (6) on the ENTIRE closed triangle, including its endpoint rows. The implied constant is independent of n,j,N. For x<=1/2, J(x)<=0 and J(s)>=-c_*, hence A(x,y)<=2c_*. On y=0 or y=x one has A=2J(x)<=2c_*. On x=1, J(y)+J(1-y)=0 and A=0. Therefore the complete low-n region and every triangular boundary face have absolute exponential envelope at most 2c_*=v_3/pi=0.32306594721945.... (7) By continuity the same statement, with arbitrarily small fixed error, holds in fixed collars of those faces. More precisely for every eta>0 there is delta>0 such that the portion outside K_delta={1/2+delta<=x<=1-delta, delta<=y<=x-delta} has absolute sum <=N^C exp[N(2c_*+eta)], uniformly for ALL 0<=t<=1 in the exact finite homotopy (3). This includes the number of lattice terms, which is only O(N^2). This is an actual absolute source bound for (1)--(3), rather than a bound on a proposed saddle coefficient. It places all possible contributions above that envelope in a fixed real interior subtriangle. A higher selected exponent is still to be proved, so this is not used as a relative error statement. ## 3. The good-gauge critical set cannot escape on a fixed real subtriangle **Properness lemma.** Fix delta>0 and let t range over [0,1]. All critical points of S_t with 1/2+delta<=Re x<=1-delta, delta<=Re y<=Re x-delta have uniformly bounded imaginary parts. In particular a sequence of such critical points cannot escape at imaginary infinity. Here is a proof retaining the affine forcing of the chosen mark. For 0<Re z<1 and Im z tending to either infinity, L(z)=-i pi sigma z+i pi sigma/2+o(1), sigma=sign(Im z), (8) uniformly on fixed real substrips. Suppose first that Im x, Im y and Im(x-y) all diverge in modulus along a subsequence. With signs sigma_x,sigma_y,sigma_d, equation (4) becomes grad S_t=-i pi M_sigma(t)(x,y)^t +i pi f_sigma(t)+o(1), M_sigma(t)=C_sigma+t[[2,1],[1,2]], C_sigma=[[3sigma_x-sigma_d,sigma_d], [sigma_d,-sigma_y-sigma_d]], f_sigma(t)=((3sigma_x-sigma_d)/2, (sigma_d-sigma_y)/2)^t+t(3,2)^t. (9) The real parts of x,y stay bounded. Any such critical sequence must therefore have a limiting t at which M is singular, and every null vector v of that limiting matrix must satisfy v^t f=0. This follows by taking the real part of (9)/(i pi) and then projecting onto v; it does not infer critical escape merely from a degenerate Hessian at infinity. The six consistent sign cones give the following determinants: (+++): (t+1)(3t-5), (++-): 3t^2+10t-1, (-+-): (t-1)(3t+1), (+-+): (t+1)(3t-1), (--+): 3t^2-10t-1, (---): (t-1)(3t+5). In the second cone the only root in [0,1] is alpha=(2sqrt(7)-5)/3; a null vector is (2alpha,1-alpha), and its forcing projection is (1-19alpha)/3, which is nonzero. In the fourth cone, t=1/3 and v=(1,-2), with v^t f=-4/3. The third and sixth cones have t=1 and v=(1,0), with v^t f=2. The other cones have no root in [0,1]. All full-cone escapes are therefore impossible. It remains to allow one of the three imaginary combinations to stay bounded. Passing to subsequences reduces to six cases. If Im x stays bounded while Im y tends to +infinity, the second component of (4), divided by i pi, is (1-t)x-2t y+(2t-1)+o(1). Its imaginary part forces t->0, and its real part then forces Re x->1, excluded by delta. For Im y->-infinity the corresponding expression is -(1+t)x-2t y+(1+2t), with the same contradiction. If Im y stays bounded and Im x->+infinity, the first component is -(1+t)(2x+y)+(1+3t)+o(1), whose imaginary part cannot vanish. For Im x->-infinity it is (1-t)(2x+y)+(3t-1)+o(1). The imaginary part forces t->1, and the real part then tends to 2, again impossible. Finally suppose Im(x-y) stays bounded and Im x,Im y diverge together. For positive infinity, the SUM of (4), divided by i pi, is -(3+3t)x+(1-3t)y+(1+5t)+o(1), whose imaginary part cannot vanish. For negative infinity it is (3-3t)x+(-1-3t)y+(-1+5t)+o(1). This forces t->1/3, where its real part is 2Re(x-y)+2/3>0. These cases exhaust all escapes and prove the lemma. It does not exclude finite degeneracies, additional bounded critical points or crossings of the REAL subtriangle's boundary; those are separate questions. ## 4. Exact endpoint annihilation in the natural coefficient contour The inner polynomial in (1) has the exact finite identity H_n(t)=sum_(j=0)^n {n choose j}_Q t^j =F_n [z^n]u_N(tz)u_N(z), n<N. (10) For any delta>0 and n<=(1-delta)N, the coefficient functional in (10) annihilates EVERY fixed number of terms of the exterior top-degree expansion of u_N(tz). Each such term has degree N-1-k in z, with k fixed, whereas the other atom has only nonnegative powers. Thus its contribution is exactly zero once N-1-k>n. This is a source identity, not an estimate. Consequently that coefficient can be governed by a scalar atom sector which is beyond every fixed order of the dominant exterior expansion. Uniform pointwise dominance before contraction cannot by itself identify this selected coefficient. For the geometric algebraic critical points of the candidate, the proper-ratio equations give Y^3+Y^2-1=0, X=Y/(1+Y-Y^2), (1-X)^3=X^3Y(1-Y), X Y^2+(1-X)Y-X=0. (11) At the corresponding formal saddle of (10), its two u arguments are 1-Y and 1-X/Y. Let rho be the real root of Y^3+Y^2-1, so 0<rho<1. For either nonreal root, |1-Y|^2=2+rho+rho^(-1)>4. (12) The full scalar u_N at that argument is therefore in the PROVED top-degree region of the [actual atom theorem](full_euler_atom_dilog_and_endpoint_regions.md). Equation (10) nevertheless kills its fixed-order top-degree expansion as just explained. A correct coefficient-contour comparison must retain that cancellation or use the marked factorial interpolation. Substitution of two bare u dilogarithm branches at (11) would not justify the selected source. ## 5. Numerical guide, not a cycle proof Implicit-ODE continuation of grad S_t=0 from the real positive maximum follows a bounded nondegenerate branch to x=0.86919340003238+0.09218763788516 i, y=0.61202243557853-0.02237715112442 i. Then exp(2pi i x),exp(2pi i y) solve (11). In the Riley field t^3+t^2+2t+1=0 they are Y=t^2+t+1, X=(t^2+2t+4)/5. The sampled continuation has Re(x-y)>=0.244, 1-Re x>=0.1308 and |det Hess S_t|>=27.09. These are numerical observations, not interval-certified bounds or a theorem excluding other critical points. The simpler lattice gauge B=pi(x-x^2-xy-y^2) does NOT follow this bounded branch: numerical continuation instead approaches a degenerate infinite branch. Hence a phase mark cannot be changed during a homotopy without checking it. The remaining theorem must show that the fixed finite source cycle in (3), equivalently its exact cotangent-residue contour, transports to the tracked geometric thimble with nonzero integer coefficient. Properness on fixed subtriangles, local saddle uniqueness and the real boundary envelope do not alone prove it. Possible finite degeneracies, competing bounded critical points, the outer real boundaries, and the exact Poisson/cotangent source still have to be controlled. No selected 5_2 volume theorem is claimed in this note. [Exact algebra and numerical continuation audit](../experiments/audit_selected_angular_source_homotopy.py) and [saved results](../experiments/selected_angular_source_homotopy_results.json).

title: A selected inner angular contour with coefficient one
text: # A selected inner angular contour with coefficient one 28 October 2026. The late inner block of the five-crossing source has a genuine noncancelling contour. This is a selected contour calculation, rather than the existence of a formal critical point. Its real-parameter version is proved below. A complex-parameter reduction gives explicit one-variable boundary tests for transporting the outer contour. The full outer selected asymptotic is not proved here. The exact whole-source transform is supplied separately by [the finite five-crossing transform](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md). The calculation below concerns its explicitly specified inner block and does not use a Jones formula or a published asymptotic proof. ## 1. The exact inner block and its continuous source Put Q=exp(2pi i/N), F_n=(Q;Q)_n and W_N(n,j)=Q^[-n(n+2)-j(n+1)] F_n^3/[F_j F_(n-j)], 0<=j<=n<N. Use the exact marked factorial interpolation Fhat_N(z). Its reflection and finite-shift identities are Fhat_N(z)Fhat_N(N-1-z) =N exp[pi i z(z-N+1)/N], Fhat_N(z+L)/Fhat_N(z)=(Q^(z+1);Q)_L (1) for nonnegative INTEGER L, with the stated analytic continuation. Thus, with L=N-1-n, the actual interpolation after the harmless lattice factor exp(2pi i z) is exactly W_N(n,z)exp(2pi i z) =C_(N,n) exp[-pi i z(z-N+1)/N] (Q^(z+1);Q)_L, C_(N,n)=F_n^3/N * exp[-2pi i n(n+2)/N -pi i n(n-N+1)/N]. (2) All constants in (2) are retained. It equals W_N(n,j) at every selected integer j. The right side is an ENTIRE finite-product function of z. Define its selected ordinary integral I_(N,n)=C_(N,n) integral_0^n exp[-pi i z(z-N+1)/N](Q^(z+1);Q)_L dz. (3) The separate [finite Abel--Plana comparison](source_preserving_inner_quadrature.md) controls the difference between the discrete inner sum and (3) by O_K(log N)|F_n|^2 for n/N in a compact late interval. The contour theorem below proves a positive exponential gap over precisely that endpoint scale; hence that comparison does not erase its selected saddle coefficient. ## 2. The selected critical point for real x Let 1/2<x<1, X=exp(2pi i x). The equation XY^2+(1-X)Y-X=0 (4) has a unique root with |Y|<1. Write it as Y=-R exp(i alpha), 0<R<1, 0<alpha<pi/2, y_s=Log(Y)/(2pi i)+1=b+i eta, b=1/2+alpha/(2pi), eta=-log(R)/(2pi)>0. Then 1/2<b<x. One direct verification uses beta=2pi(1-x), h=-log R and the identities sinh(h)cos(alpha)=sin^2(beta/2), cosh(h)sin(alpha)=sin(beta/2)cos(beta/2). (5) They give one positive h and alpha in (0,pi/2). For x>=3/4, b<x is immediate. For 1/2<x<3/4, the ratio of the equations in (5) gives alpha<pi-beta, hence again b<x. Let J be the holomorphic primitive of Log(2sin(pi z)) marked from 0<z<1. Up to an x-only constant the inner phase is Psi_x(y)=-J(y)-J(x-y) +pi i[(2-x)y-y^2]. (6) The chosen root solves Psi_x'(y_s)=0 in this mark. It is the continuation from the real late source, not the other quadratic root, whose real logarithmic coordinate lies outside (0,x). ## 3. The horizontal contour has a unique global maximum Shift the interval [0,x] to [0,x]+i eta. For y=s+i eta, d_s Re Psi_x(s+i eta) =1/2 log[(sin^2(pi(x-s))+sinh^2(pi eta)) / (sin^2(pi s)+sinh^2(pi eta))] +2pi eta=:F(s). (7) One has F(0)>0 and F(x)<0. The first is immediate. For the second, put S=sin^2(pi x), h=2pi eta, a=sinh h and c=cosh h. Equation (5) gives a^4+(1-S)a^2-S^2=0, 0<a<1. (8) The desired F(x)<0 is equivalent to S>a(a+c)(c-1)=:R_0. The polynomial P(z)=z^2+a^2z-a^2(1+a^2) is increasing for z>=0 and has positive root S. If v=exp(h), direct factorization gives P(R_0)=(v-1)^2(v+1)^2(v^2+1)(v^2-2v-1) (v^2-v+1)/(16v^4)<0, because 1<v<1+sqrt(2). This proves F(x)<0. The equation F(s)=0, after exponentiation and expansion of the two sine squares, is a constant plus one sine and one cosine of 2pi s. It has at most two zeros in an interval of length x<1, counting multiplicities. Opposite endpoint signs therefore force exactly one zero. It is s=b, the already known critical point, and it crosses from positive to negative. Thus y_s is a strict, nondegenerate GLOBAL maximum of the real part on this horizontal contour. The Gaussian square root is fixed by this actual left-to-right orientation. ## 4. Both connecting segments are lower Connect 0 to i eta, and x+i eta to x, using vertical segments. All endpoint values below use the one-sided J mark from 0<Re y<Re x; evaluating a principal dilogarithm directly on its cut can give the wrong value. On the left segment y=i tau, tau>0, the imaginary part of Psi_x'(y) is arg sin(pi(x-i tau))+pi(3/2-x)>0. Consequently Re Psi strictly decreases upward. Its maximum is the original endpoint y=0. On the right segment y=x+i tau, tau>0, one obtains d_tau Re Psi_x(x+i tau) =arg sin(pi(x+i tau))+pi(3x-3/2)>0. Indeed arg sin(pi(x+i tau))> -pi(x-1/2), leaving the positive lower bound pi(2x-1). Its maximum is therefore the horizontal endpoint x+i eta, strictly below the horizontal saddle. It remains to compare the LEFT original endpoint with the saddle. Restore the outer phase and define S(x,y)=3J(x)-J(y)-J(x-y) +pi i(3x+2y-x^2-xy-y^2), D(x)=Re S(x,y_s(x))-2J(x). (9) Then D(x)>0, 1/2<x<1. (10) Here is a direct proof. The critical equation gives D'(x)=log[|1-X|/(R|1-Y|)]. (11) Use S_0=sin^2(pi x), a=sinh h, c=cosh h as in (8). Formula (11) becomes D'(x)=1/2 log[2S_0 a/(ac+S_0)]+3h/2. (12) As a function of S_0 in (0,1), a and h are strictly increasing. Also c/S_0 is strictly decreasing. To verify the latter, put T=a^2; equation (8) gives T'=(T+2S_0)/(2T+1-S_0)>0, sign d_(S_0)(c/S_0) =sign[S_0 T'-2(1+T)]<0, since after clearing its positive denominator the numerator is S_0(T+2)-2(T+1)^2<0. Therefore 2S_0 a/(ac+S_0)=2/(c/S_0+1/a) is strictly increasing. The right side of (12) is strictly increasing in S_0. Since S_0 strictly decreases with x on (1/2,1), D''(x)<0. Finally D(1/2+)=D(1-)=0. At x=1 the limiting saddle is y=1/2, and J(1)=J(1/2)=0. At x=1/2 the saddle is y=1/2+i asinh(1)/(2pi); the one-sided identities Re J(1/2+i eta)=0 and Re J(-i eta)=-pi eta/2 make the two real terms cancel. Strict concavity proves (10). Thus every connector and the Abel--Plana endpoint scale is strictly below the selected saddle, uniformly when x lies in a compact subinterval of (1/2,1). ## 5. The resulting selected Gaussian, with its source coefficient Let P'(z)=Log(1-exp(2pi i z)), with its inherited strip mark, and put Phi_x(y)=P(y+1-x)-P(y)+pi i(y-y^2), a_x(y)=exp(-pi i y) / sqrt[(1-exp(2pi i y))(1-exp(2pi i(y+1-x)))]. For n/N=x in any compact K contained in (1/2,1), the selected integral (3) satisfies uniformly I_(N,n)=C_(N,n) sqrt(N) a_x(y_s) sqrt[2pi/(-Phi_x''(y_s))] exp[N Phi_x(y_s)] (1+O_K(1/N)). (13) Every displayed factor is nonzero. The multiplier of this Gaussian is ONE. This follows by an exact contour deformation of the entire integrand (2); no thimble intersection is guessed. For completeness, the finite product on the horizontal segment has the uniform Euler--Maclaurin expansion (Q^(Ny+1);Q)_(N-1-n) =exp{N[P(y+1-x)-P(y)]} / sqrt[(1-exp(2pi i y))(1-exp(2pi i(y+1-x)))] *(1+O_K(1/N)). Its arguments stay strictly inside the unit disk there, and away from one, uniformly on K. The quadratic Gaussian in (2) contributes exp[N pi i(y-y^2)]exp(-pi i y). The two connector bounds follow with a uniform O(log N) logarithmic product error, treating their simple endpoint zeros by rectangle sums. Their strict phase gap makes them exponentially negligible in (13). Ordinary one-variable complex Laplace expansion at the unique horizontal maximum then proves (13), including the orientation and coefficient one. Combined with the finite Abel--Plana endpoint bound stated in Section 1, the SAME selected Gaussian is the asymptotic of the original discrete inner sum, uniformly on real compact K. This is an inner source-selection theorem. Outer cancellation is a further operation and has not been suppressed by wording. ## 6. A complex-x reduction for the actual outer contour The following identities reduce the complex continuation to explicit one-variable boundary tests. Let x=u+i h, 1/2<u<1, |1/X|<=2, X=exp(2pi i x), T=1/X-1, v=(T+sqrt(T^2+4))/2, Re sqrt(T^2+4)>0, Y=-v, y_s=b+i lambda=Log(Y)/(2pi i)+1. The condition 0<Im T<2 is enough to make v lie in quadrant I; it cannot cross an axis without T becoming real or satisfying Im T>=2. Hence 1/2<b<min(u,3/4). The latter inequality follows from the ratio of real and imaginary parts of v-1/v=T when u<3/4; it is automatic when u>=3/4. The root has no collision on this domain. At the selected root, S_yy=-2pi i(v^2+1)/[v(v+1)], sign Re S_yy=sign(|v|^2-2Re v-1)<0. (14) For the last inequality write a=Re v>0, r=|v|^2. Then |1+v-1/v|^2=r+3+2a+(1-2a-4a^2)/r. At r=2a+1 its excess over four is (4a^2+2a+1)/(2a+1)>0, and it is strictly increasing for r>=2a+1. Thus |1/X|<=2 forces r<2a+1. In particular the selected root remains a nondegenerate strict horizontal maximum. On y=s+i lambda, 0<=s<=u, one has F(s)=d_s Re S =1/2 log[(sin^2(pi(u-s))+sinh^2(pi(h-lambda))) / (sin^2(pi s)+sinh^2(pi lambda))] +pi(h+2lambda). (15) There are at most two horizontal stationary points. Also F(0)>0. An exact proof of the latter is available directly from the root: put R=|v| and c=cos(arg v). After squaring the equivalent modulus inequality, its positive difference is 2(c+1)[(R-1)^2(R+1)+2R^2(1-c)]>0, after multiplication by a positive power of R. The sign, rather than that irrelevant positive scaling, is what is used. Together with (14), this shows that the maximum over the WHOLE horizontal segment is either the selected saddle or the right endpoint u+i lambda. Unlike the real-x case, F(u) can be positive; there can be a second stationary point, which is a minimum. The polygon 0 -> i lambda -> u+i lambda -> x has particularly simple connectors. The left phase is strictly decreasing as a function of its vertical parameter tau. Its maximum is therefore at tau=min(0,lambda). On the right put theta_u(tau)=arg sin(pi(u+i tau)). This is strictly decreasing. The vertical derivative of Re S is theta_u(tau)+pi(3u-5/2), tau<h, theta_u(tau)+pi(3u-3/2), tau>h. (16) Each connector segment is strictly concave. Its maximum is at an endpoint or the single stationary value obtained by solving theta_u(tau)=-pi(3u-c), c=5/2 or 3/2, when that value belongs to the segment. Explicitly tau=(1/pi)artanh[tan(pi(3u-c))/(-cot(pi u))], (17) with the actual arctangent range checked before using (17). Consequently an outer contour construction need only bound the selected outer action and these finitely many ONE-VARIABLE endpoint/stationary connector functions. No sampling of the whole two-dimensional polygon is required for a rigorous bound. At the geometric outer x, diagnostic values are Re S(x,y_s)=0.450109610025218..., max left connector=0.10745960674786..., max right connector=0.43978988922391.... The right maximum occurs at tau=0.04913510458548..., rather than at either endpoint. The exact formulas (14)--(17) reduce the whole-contour comparison to one real parameter. The following certificate completes those phase bounds; the displayed decimals above are not used as proof. ## 7. Rigorous bounds for the full inner polygons and outer source edges [The Arb certificate](../experiments/certify_selected_inner_contours.py) uses 192-bit outward-rounded acb/arb arithmetic. Its [saved result](../experiments/selected_inner_contour_certificate.json) reports `RIGOROUS_ARB_PASS`. Polynomial root isolation, every analytic function enclosure, every pass/fail comparison and every interval subdivision are certified balls; floats are used only for displaying already-proved bounds. Let x_g=u_g+i h_g be the exact cubic point from [the outer phase theorem](five_two_reduced_outer_contour_concavity.md), and put h(u)=min(h_g,h_g(1-u)/(1-u_g)). The certificate proves: * For .51<=u<=.99 on x=u+i h(u), ALL left inner connectors have phase below .200 and ALL right inner connectors have phase below .445. The two contour pieces require 523 and 734 dyadic parameter cells respectively. * On x=u-.1i, .51<=u<=.99, the maximum phase of the ENTIRE inner polygon, after adding the exact lower-kernel weight -.2pi, is below .400. This includes the selected horizontal saddle, the horizontal endpoint and both connectors; 187 parameter cells suffice. * For u in EACH of [.5099,.5101] and [.9899,.9901], every full inner polygon on the vertical outer source edges has phase below .440. On the upper edge 0<=h<=h(u) this is unweighted. On the lower edge -.1<=h<=0 it includes the actual kernel weight +2pi h. These four boxes require 388 further cells. The real u variable is kept as its whole Arb interval, so these are two-parameter box enclosures, not evaluations at just u=.51,.99. The total is 1832 verified cells. The same calculation encloses the selected cubic rate between .45010 and .45012. Thus all connector and lower-source bounds have a STRICT positive gap. The phase calibration is supplied by the separate [marked Bloch calculation](five_two_selected_bloch_calibration.md). Here is why the maximum reductions make this a full certificate. On each parameter cell the code encloses the selected quadratic root and checks its first-quadrant branch. Formula (14) and F(0)>0 imply that every horizontal maximum is either the saddle or its right endpoint. The left connector maximum is one of its two endpoints. On the right, the derivative is decreasing; the code includes both endpoints and the unique candidate (17) unless an interval sign proves it irrelevant. Ambiguous cases are subdivided. It therefore cannot omit an actual maximum. The interval cells cover both closed parameter ranges, including their common cubic endpoint. The [exact finite-height outer source formula](source_preserving_outer_finite_height_quadrature.md) uses precisely these weights and edges. Its half-integer real edges lie in the certified u boxes for every sufficiently large N (N>=10000 is sufficient for its specified rounding). The uniform factorial bound in that theorem includes BOTH inner endpoints, with only polynomial factors; hence a certified phase bound controls the actual whole inner function there. The upper kernel also has an explicit gap. On this window h(u)>.007. The outer theorem gives selected reduced phase at most the cubic value, and the remaining upper connectors are below .445. Consequently the full upper polygon, after its kernel weight -2pi h, is below .407. Combining the upper, lower and vertical bounds in the exact outer formula gives an outer discretization error O(N^(5/2)exp(.440N)). This is strictly below the selected cubic action. No outer alias or finite source edge is discarded by its formal symbol. These estimates supply the source-error and inner-contour inputs for combining the exact finite transform, selected saddle and marked volume calibration. They do not constitute a general knot theorem; extension to broader bridge networks requires analogous source-preserving reductions and contour bounds.

title: Genuine holonomy braiding on the common carry lattice
text: # Genuine holonomy braiding on the common carry lattice Research note, 26 October 2026. This replaces the frozen auxiliary crossing of [the carry-lattice construction](carry_recoupling_lattice.md) by an explicit genuine semicyclic holonomy braiding. A retained central factor corrects the wrap, the transported centers obey a linear braid map, and a common fixed center line gives a braid action on every recoupled integral source and its special fiber. The entire original ADO cut operator, not just its trace, is recovered with its meridian, pivot, twist and modified dimension unchanged. These are statements on the E^N=0 semicyclic locus. This locus represents reducible knot characters. No identification with the complete irreducible geometric character or its selected regulator norm follows. ## 1. The source modules and their fixed highest-weight flag Put q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), N>=2, and k=x^N. On V(x,phi), with basis v_0,...,v_(N-1), use K v_a=x Q^(-a)v_a, E v_a=e_a v_(a-1), E v_0=0, e_a=[a]_q (x q^(1-a)-x^(-1)q^(a-1))/rho, F_phi v_a=v_(a+1), a<N-1, F_phi v_(N-1)=phi v_0. (1.1) These are the regular modules already constructed on the semicyclic section of [the holonomy splitting chart](regular_holonomy_braiding.md): E^N=0, F^N=phi, K^N=k, Omega=rho^2 FE+qK+q^(-1)K^(-1)=qx+q^(-1)x^(-1). (1.2) The wrap of F never enters FE because E has no output v_(N-1). This directly checks that the Casimir and commutator are unchanged. For generic x the e_a, a>0, are units, and K projectors together with the nonwrap E,F arrows generate every matrix unit, for every phi. The vector v_0 is a fixed highest-weight flag throughout this locus. The rational holonomy automorphism r and its center map are the independently proved formulas in that linked note. Here its central divisor is identically one because E_1^N=0. In raw F-power coordinates the uncheck center transport is phi'_1=phi_1/k+(1-k^(-2))phi_2, phi'_2=phi_2/k. (1.3) The K roots and the individual Casimirs stay fixed. ## 2. An explicit global intertwiner, with the correct wrap factor Let D be diagonal on the pair: D v_(a,b)=x^(-a-b)Q^(ab) v_(a,b), c_n=q^(n(n-1)/2)rho^n/[n]_q!. Define R_(phi_1,phi_2) =D sum_(n=0)^(N-1)c_n E_1^n F_(2,phi_2/k)^n. (2.1) It maps V(x,phi'_1) tensor V(x,phi'_2) to V(x,phi_1) tensor V(x,phi_2), intertwining the target generators with r applied in the source. In particular the wrap is phi_2/k, not phi_2. At the Kashaev color, x_0=q^(N-1), k_0=(-1)^(N-1), so the missing factor is -1 at even levels. Before specialization it is the whole function x^(-N). All denominators [n]_q!, n<N, are nonzero. The series is a polynomial in a nilpotent operator, with constant term one; its inverse is the corresponding finite inverse Euler series. Thus (2.1) is invertible for every phi and x!=0. It fixes v_00. Here is a proof of every intertwining equation without assuming a published semicyclic R formula. Write Theta for the finite sum in (2.1), and U=q rho^2 E_1 F_(2,phi_2/k). The Euler coefficient identity gives Theta(QU)=Theta(U)/(1-U), U^N=0. (2.2) Consequently its K conjugations are exact finite identities. The Cartan factor satisfies D E_1 D^(-1)=E_1 K_2, D F_(2,phi_2/k) D^(-1)=K_1^(-1)F_(2,phi_2). (2.3) In the second equation a nonwrap has ratio x^(-1)Q^a; the wrap has ratio x^(N-1)Q^a and its factor phi_2/k restores exactly the same coefficient. This is the origin of the central correction. E_1 and F_(2,phi_2/k) commute with Theta. Combining (2.2)--(2.3) therefore intertwines E_1,F_2,K_1,K_2 with precisely their four rational holonomy images. No derivative or omitted Nth Euler coefficient is used. The remaining two generators are forced. On phi_2!=0, F_2 is invertible, so its Casimir and K determine E_2 uniquely. For the first factor, put the already matched K_1,E_1 in their standard weight-string basis. Its Casimir determines every nonwrap F_1 arrow. The weight relation allows only the remaining arrow v_(N-1)->v_0, with an arbitrary matrix on the spectator. F_1^N=phi'_1 fixes that matrix to phi'_1 times the identity. Both representations have the same Casimirs and (1.3) is the proved central map, so F_1 also agrees. This proves all six equations on a dense open set. The intertwiner and its inverse have only monomial x and fixed root denominators; the holonomy denominators are finite nilpotent inverses. Clearing them extends the identities to all phi and all defined colors, including the original nilpotent section. The uncheck determinant is independent of phi. Every wrap lowers integer residue degree, and every nonzero transfer lowers the first index before checking. Thus only the diagonal D contributes: det R=x^(-N^2(N-1)) Q^((N(N-1)/2)^2). (2.4) This is the original nilpotent determinant. Its anchored scalar normalization is therefore exactly the one in the existing holonomy note, with no new phi-dependent scalar. ## 3. Checked maps transport their centers Let P be the literal flip. As a map from the input pair with centers (u,v) to its transported output, the positive crossing is B^+(u,v)=P D sum_(n<N)c_n E_1^n F_(2,v)^n, (u,v) -> L_-(k)(u,v), L_-(k)=[[0,k],[k,1-k^2]]. (3.1) This follows by applying (2.1) at the swapped output centers. Its source correction phi_2/k then equals the input v exactly. Thus the old wrapped positive matrix can be used with the proper center transport; holding arbitrary centers fixed would use a different composition rule. The inverse crossing at input (u,v) is B^-(u,v)=Theta_(u/k)^(-1) D^(-1)P, (u,v) -> L_+(k)(u,v), L_+(k)=[[1-k^(-2),k^(-1)],[k^(-1),0]]. (3.2) The matrices L_- and L_+ are inverse. These are precisely the classical polynomial-block matrices of [the Frobenius Verma calculation](frobenius_verma_period.md). The quantum holonomy and Frobenius center transports now have the same explicit convention, rather than an unmarked identification. ## 4. Strict braid coherence on the semicyclic locus The rational holonomy automorphisms satisfy the three-factor identity by the earlier direct algebra proof. With (3.1)--(3.2) transporting the centers, the two braid composites intertwine the same split full matrix algebra with the same target centers. They differ by one scalar on the generic regular chart. Every crossing (2.1), checked crossing, and inverse fixes the tensor highest-weight vector v_00. Therefore the two composites both fix v_000, forcing that scalar to equal one. This proves the braid relation exactly, without an unspecified determinant phase. It holds over the entire semicyclic affine center chart by the same polynomial continuation as in Section 2, including even and composite N. Positive and negative maps are literal inverses when the intermediate centers are updated. The fixed highest-weight flag is essential to this argument. On the full cyclic locus with E^N!=0 that flag is absent; the general phase cover has not been removed by this special coherence theorem. ## 5. A common fixed line and the even-level endpoint mark For b strands the line phi_j=z k^(1-j), j=1,...,b, (5.1) is fixed by every embedded L_+ and L_-. Substitution in each two-by-two matrix proves this directly. Hence on this line the matrices are endomorphisms of one ordered tensor module and obey the ordinary braid relations. Retain the unit endpoint change c_j=x^(j-1), S_j v_a=c_j^a v_a, F_j^new=c_j F_j, E_j^new=c_j^(-1)E_j. (5.2) In the new leaf frame the F central parameters are all (F_j^new)^N=c_j^N phi_j=z. At M=1 these are exactly c_j=(-q)^(1-j), the previously derived actual coproduct endpoint marks. For even N their Nth powers remove the alternating raw center signs. This is an explicit root/meridian function, not a numerical choice made after evaluating M=1. Choose z=1-(1-epsilon)^N. After (5.2), all leaves have the same Borel parameter t_j=1-z=(1-epsilon)^N. The common carry theorem applies with every direction a_j=1. Every relative parameter specializes to tau_I(0)=|I|/|R| !=0,1. (5.3) The endpoint change is diagonal and a unit and thus commutes with the carry weights. Every genuine crossing and inverse preserves both leaf and carry lattices: a wrap still lowers residue degree by N and has one factor z. Therefore its conjugation to each basic recoupled source is integral. The braid identities hold over R before specialization, so they hold on every basic recoupled carry fiber as well as on its actual source sublattice. This upgrades the auxiliary trace construction to a genuine braid action in each integral recoupling chart. The arbitrary frozen-direction lift in the preceding note is not asserted to have this property; (5.1)--(5.2) supply it. The recoupling statement is a transport of linear modules and operators with the given endpoint frames. A complete assignment of colored tensor-face data to a positive geometric knot triangulation is still required. ## 6. The entire selected cut operator remains the actual ADO one The finite crossing matrices in (3.1)--(3.2) have no degree- increasing term. A wrap lowers the integer residue sum by N. This holds for any transported semicyclic parameters, not only the common fixed line. Close b-1 strands with the original diagonal pivot and keep the original open N-dimensional strand. For an entry from cut index a to a', closing the other strands makes the total degree change equal a'-a. On the other hand it is -N times the number of wraps.
