Since 0<=a,a'<N, the only possibility is a'=a and no wraps. Thus the whole cut operator has exactly its original nilpotent entries: C_(beta,N)(x;phi)=F_N(M) I_N, M=-qx. (6.1) All pivot and zero-framing twist factors are the original ones. At a closed center fixed point this is a literal semicyclic holonomy cut evaluation. The same finite matrix identity also holds before imposing center closure; that extra assertion does not define a new geometric-character invariant. Any vector/covector pair with value one can evaluate the scalar operator (6.1). This includes the original highest-weight cut and its already proved factorial/Whittaker frame. After a recoupling the corresponding insertion is transported as the full matrix; it is not reset independently in the new chart. The determinant normalization from (2.4) uses the original same-color scalar s=x^(N-1)q^(-(N-1)^2/2). Its compensating twist is s*x^(1-N)=q^(-(N-1)^2/2), exactly as on the nilpotent section. The zero-framed evaluation and its full factor remain exactly F_N(M), d_N(M)F_N(M), d_N(M)=i^(N+3)M^(N-1)/(1+M^2+...+M^(2N-2)). (6.2) All meridian germs, the Kashaev value, and the actual all-level meridian annihilator ideal are consequently retained. The raw k=x^N, its even-level sign, and the separately known full ADO shift sign have not been discarded or identified by fiat. ## 7. What this closes and what remains There is now an explicit genuine holonomy braiding through the actual semicyclic source, a common fixed center line with the correct endpoint marks, and an integral braid action compatible with every recoupling tree and the full actual cut operator. The scalar is fixed by a highest-weight flag and the wrap by its central character. These comparisons use actual operators and evaluations, not only matching algebra dimensions. The E^N=0 locus is preserved by the center maps. Its meridian holonomies are triangular after the existing prefix change, so its closed knot representations are reducible. The common fixed line does not represent complete irreducible hyperbolic holonomy. The previously constructed Alexander attachment points and mixed E/F deformation problem remain relevant. No Hilbert-90 change can remove that central-character distinction. Transport to the equivariant colored positive triangulation, identification of the meridian source with its marked Bloch period, and the selected regulator norm across N remain to be proved. The volume conjecture is not established here. The subsequent [four cyclic-atom theorem](four_cyclic_atoms.md) now writes the explicit crossing (2.1) as four literature cyclic dilogarithm matrices in changing central frames. Their norm roots and determinant normalizations, the Cartan map and one external root are all retained. A formal source anchor fixes the remaining finite scalar. This is an actual root-level operator factorization, not separate specialization of compact infinite products. It supplies local tetrahedron data while leaving the geometric global source and selected norm open. ## 8. Coverage and exact diagnostics This lies in the existing Kashaev--Reshetikhin holonomy-braiding and semicyclic quantum-group framework, whose statement coverage is recorded in [the regular holonomy note](regular_holonomy_braiding.md). The abstracts of [Kashaev--Reshetikhin, math/0202212](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0202212) and [McPhail-Snyder--Reshetikhin, 2509.02354v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02354v2) were checked for this coverage, including the latter's four-dilogarithm and holonomy Yang--Baxter scope. Their proofs are not used here. The root module is the literature quantum-group module (1.1), and the actual knot invariant is unchanged. No new general semicyclic invariant or novelty claim is made. The four-generator, Casimir, center and highest-weight arguments above give the proof without importing a published R-matrix or coherence proof. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_semicyclic_carry_braiding.py) checks all six generator intertwinings in 18 cases at nine levels through 12, retaining the wrap factor k^(-1). It checks ten dynamically transported braid/inverse cases and compares freezing the wrong centers. On the common fixed line it checks the genuine braid in both three-leaf carry frames and 60 original recoupled cut periods. It separately checks 30 entire scalar cut matrices with arbitrary transported centers, at generic and Kashaev colors. All passed. Results: [semicyclic_carry_braiding_results.json](../experiments/semicyclic_carry_braiding_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_semicyclic_carry_braiding.py The subsequent [braided source atlas](braided_source_groupoid.md) also handles varying centers through every tree/source chart, including the line data at source infinity. For that construction the explicit inverse endpoint factors c_j=x^(-j), j starting at zero, make the normalized total Y exactly the original coproduct of F. The normalized wraps are k^(-j)a_j and their center maps depend on U=k^2=M^(2N), preserving their total. This is a different coordinate choice from (5.2), whose purpose was to make the fixed line have equal wraps. All inverse/source factors remain explicit. The full arrows act on the relative factors and preserve the selected original cut. The actual meridian-source equation and nontrivial pure-braid jet are derived in the companion note; the complete geometric gluing and regulator norm remain unproved.

title: Actual sewing shifts are divided-Ward images of the wrap source
text: # Actual sewing shifts are divided-Ward images of the wrap source 28 October 2026. The unit shifts in the exact cyclic sewing have an explicit relation to the ORIGINAL integral divided Hopf adjoint. The relation holds on the actual balanced head, including an exact whole-q source profile. The large scalar powers cancel between the two ends of a transfer. Thus these shifts need not be assigned an auxiliary unipotent action. This does not yet give a geometric centralizer chain map. There is a first explicit obstruction to the simplest proposed extension: independent head adjoints are not the full mixed coproduct adjoint. Their difference has a nonzero ORIGINAL crossing-cap pairing. The internal geometric interval cannot be inferred by omitting it. ## 1. The literal integral head and its two wrap coupons Fix N>=2 and put `m=N-1`, `L=N(N-1)/2`, `rho=q-q^-1`. Use the actual integral color of highest weight m, with basis v_j, E^(a)v_j=[m-j+a choose a]_q v_(j-a), F^(a)v_j=[j+a choose a]_q v_(j+a), K v_j=q^(m-2j)v_j. (1) Terms outside the head are zero. Symmetric Gaussian coefficients are their Laurent-polynomial values, not quotients evaluated at a root. Let `B_+=|m><0|`, `B_-=|0><m|`. These are the literal missing cyclic-wrap matrix units. Write `J_+,J_-` for the unit truncated raising/lowering shifts and `J v_j=j v_j`. Use the FULL integral Hopf adjoints A_(E^(n))(C)=sum_(k=0)^n (-1)^k q^(-k(n-1)) E^(n-k) C E^(k) K^-n, A_(F^(n))(C)=sum_(k=0)^n (-1)^k q^(k(n-1)) F^(n-k)K^-k C K^k F^(k). (2) The mixed terms in (2) remain even when E^(N),F^(N) individually vanish on the N-dimensional head. These are linear adjoint images; no assertion that a single A_h is a square-zero differential is made. ## 2. Exact root identities in the ORIGINAL balanced basis At `q=exp(pi*i/N)` one has `[m choose k]_q=1` for every k. Indeed each numerator factor `[N-s]_q` equals `[s]_q`, with all factors below N nonzero. Direct substitution in (2) gives A_(E^(N))(B_+)=(-1)^m J_- q^J, A_(F^(N))(B_-)=-q^-1 J_+ q^-J (3) in the integral basis. For example only the k-th term contributes to entry `(k-1,k)` of the first identity. Its coefficient is `(-1)^k q^(-km) q^(-N(m-2k))=(-1)^m q^k`. For the second identity, entry `(j+1,j)` comes from `k=m-j` and has coefficient `-q^(-j-1)`. The original balanced crossing basis is the diagonal transport D_j=(-rho)^j q^(j(j+1)/2). (4) It gives exactly the original raising coefficients `1-Q^(j+1)` and balanced `Ecal=rho^2 E` coefficients `Q^-j-1`, with `Q=q^2`. Transport the actual adjoint and the wrap coupons by this same D, keeping their scalars. Equations (3)-(4) imply A^bal_(E^(N))(B_+)=-rho^(-N) q^-L J_-, A^bal_(F^(N))(B_-)=(-1)^m rho^N q^L J_+. (5) Hence on the actual two-head sewing edge, J_+ tensor J_- =(-1)^N A^bal_(F^(N))(B_-) tensor A^bal_(E^(N))(B_+). (6) The rho^N and quadratic phase factors cancel EXACTLY. The same statement with exchanged heads gives the other transfer. The marked x^-1 coefficient in each actual transfer remains attached. Neither endpoint wrap is reset or replaced by a new vacuum. Thus an actual divided-current description of every local sewing shift exists, at every N, before Gaussian contraction. It uses the mixed Hopf adjoint, rather than an ordinary commutator with the vanishing divided matrix. ## 3. The whole normal profile is explicit The root formulas cannot simply be differentiated as constants. Keep q generic and the same integral head and balanced frame. Put M_col=-q^N, G_j(q)=M_col^j [m choose j]_q, C_E(q)=(-rho)^(-N)q^(-Nm-L), C_F(q)=(-1)^m(-rho)^N q^(L+1-m^2). Then the exact WHOLE-q identities are A^bal_(E^(N))(B_+)=C_E(q) J_- diag(G_j(q)), A^bal_(F^(N))(B_-)=C_F(q) J_+ diag(G_j(q)). (7) To verify the first, its integral `(k-1,k)` coefficient is `(-1)^k q^(k(N+1)-Nm)[m choose k]_q`. The balanced-frame ratio and the wrap scalar in (4) change this into `C_E M_col^k[m choose k]_q`. For the second, put k=m-j in (2); its integral coefficient is `(-1)^(m-j)q^(-(m-j)m)[m choose j]_q`. The same frame calculation gives the displayed C_F G_j. At the root `G_j=1` and `C_E C_F=(-1)^N`. Off the root the diagonal profile is nonconstant and may have source divisors. It is tied to the already computed actual color-source profile: G_j=M_col^(2j) V_j, V_j=[m choose j]_q/M_col^j. (8) Thus the [whole-head Gamma/source comparison](full_head_gamma_source_transport.md) can transport this precise profile, with its extra character retained. Equation (7) itself does not invert G_j at a zero. Fractional source and dual lattices, all normal derivatives, and the original peripheral line remain necessary. The actual moment carry at these endpoints is also explicit. Let `S=J_++B_-` be the cyclic raising completion. For every polynomial p (indeed every function on the displayed finite arguments), entrywise multiplication proves p(J)S-S p(J+1)=[p(0)-p(N)]B_-, p(J)S^-1-S^-1 p(J-1)=[p(m)-p(-1)]B_+. (8a) In particular `[J,S]=S-NB_-` and `[J,S^-1]=-S^-1+NB_+`. Before taking moments, the whole position-clock identity is z^J S z^-J=z S+(z^(1-N)-z)B_-, z^J S^-1 z^-J=z^-1 S^-1+(z^(N-1)-z^-1)B_+. (8b) Euler derivatives in z recover every polynomial/logarithmic moment with its actual endpoint. The factors z^N are retained before specialization. For the two-head cyclic transfer A, [J_1+J_2,A] =Na[-B_-,1 tensor S_2^-1+S_1 tensor B_+,2]. (8c) The two corner contributions cancel where both wrap edges overlap. The nilpotent transfer has zero total-index commutator. Thus its sewing sources have exactly the N-step moment carry required to repair the cyclic completion. Equations (7)-(8c) retain that carry; they do not turn it into an ordinary derivation after cyclic specialization. ## 4. The first global mismatch has an actual nonzero cap row Equation (6) contains INDEPENDENT adjoints on the two heads. The original crossing intertwines the actual coproduct, whose divided formulas have all mixed terms. Those are different operations. The difference is already visible at N=2 without an asymptotic argument. Take `q=i`, `Q=-1`, `M=1`, `x=i`. In the original balanced basis, E=(1/2)E_01, F=2E_10, K=diag(i,-i), Delta E^(2)=(1/4)E_(00,11), Delta F^(2)=4E_(11,00). Let `C=B_- tensor B_+`. Direct use of (2) with the full coproduct matrices gives A^tot_(F^(2)E^(2))(C) =[[-i,0,0,0], [0,-i,1,0], [0,1,i,0], [0,0,0,i]]. (9) The independent product in (6) is `J_+ tensor J_-`, whose only nonzero entry is `(row2,column1)=1`. Denote their difference by D_mix. It is not a suppressed scalar or a zero source current. Keep the original stripped crossing R_0=[[1,0,0,0],[0,0,-i,0], [0,-i,2,0],[0,0,0,1]], and its original normalized average first cut with closed pivots `(-i,i)`. Exactly, Phi(D_mix R_0)=1/2, Phi(R_0 D_mix)=-1/2. (10) The actual common Cartan factor kappa multiplies these by kappa and is retained; restoring the other external factors does not make them zero. Thus the proposed replacement of the independent sewing image by a diagonal divided Ward generator drops an actual nonzero endpoint contribution. This rules out that replacement, not every corrected current construction. A valid tensor/chain fusion must carry D_mix and its counterparts, rather than use independent adjoint identities as if they already had coproduct naturality. ## 5. The geometric endpoint condition is now specific There is also a precise target on the ORIGINAL whole word, not only on a separate source cone. The already proved [actual Borel Ward calculation](actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction.md) gives the complete principal conjugation fields (ad_Ktot-I)/H -> A(h/2), ad_Ecal,tot/H -> A f_sl, ad_Ftot/H -> A e_sl, where `H=Log Q`. On the original inverse-eigenflag framing chart the compensated cut-Borel fields are `xi_1=2(r-1)partial_r+2s partial_s` and `xi_2=(2r-1)partial_r+2s partial_s`. Define the literal finite operator, with the specified LEFT multiplication, S_cut=-q K_1-1, W_cut=ad_Ftot-2(ad_Ktot-I)-ad_Ecal,tot, V_N(C)=S_cut W_cut(C). (11a) Its cut symbol is `S_cut -> A_cut^-1-1=s`, so `V_N/H -> s(xi_2-xi_1)=s partial_r=V_J`. It vanishes exactly on the unweighted actual braid word. The target classical ODE consequently has endpoint `r->r+s` at time one. This gives the principal generator; it is not a proof that an arbitrary finite exponential of V_N equals the retained quantum meridian endpoint. The target co-source row is explicit as well. For `Phi_A(C)=Tr(A C)` set `B=A S_cut`, in that order. Then Phi_A(V_N(C))=Tr[W_cut^vee(B) C], W_cut^vee(B)=B Ftot-Ktot Ftot B Ktot^-1 -2(Ktot^-1 B Ktot-B) -(Ktot^-1 B Ecal,tot-Ecal,tot Ktot^-1 B). (11b) Each term follows by cyclicity of the trace, so the original cut row and pivot need not be declared invariant. The whole weighted Ward formula transports (11a)-(11b) with the actual lower-moment Green currents: a moment polynomial p leaves its specified forward difference `Delta_t p`, not a zero endpoint. The normal clock/pivot adapters in the divided Ward theorem remain attached. These target data already exist; (6) does not by itself supply their source map. The actual paired Frobenius source already supplies a precise target generator. In the marked variables of [the unprojectivized source torsor](actual_unprojectivized_frobenius_borel_torsor.md), let `s=C alpha^2`, `r=(1+m_src)/2+D alpha^2`. The actual divided-source generator `e-h-f` has field `2 partial_msrc`; it fixes alpha. Hence its source-dependent multiple s(e-h-f) -> s partial_r=V_J. (11c) At fixed alpha its actual standard-vector group is `I+b s [[-1,1],[-1,1]]`. Its square-zero matrix gives an exact additive group law, and the paired dual parameter changes by `m_src -> m_src+2bs`. At b=1 the frame changes by `r -> r+s`, precisely the complete marked meridian endpoint. Thus the desired endpoint is not an unspecified abstract additive action. Equation (11c) is a theorem on that actual paired source family. Equations (6)-(8) identify the literal sewing currents and their whole normal profiles. The missing map must fuse the INDEPENDENT images in (6) into the FULL ordinary/divided coproduct current, carry the correction detected in (10) and all its Green-moment rows, and then identify its transverse Gaussian image with (11a)-(11c). The generic principal density `c_beta Omega_cut` and its nonzero logarithmic residue do not perform that fusion. No nonzero selected geometric image, equality of the relative coordinates, or volume lower bound is claimed from the two separate endpoint constructions. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_sewing_wrap_divided_ward.py). It checks root and generic-q identities at levels 2 through 12, the retained paired transfer signs, and (9)-(10) in characteristic zero. The displayed calculations prove the all-level identities independently of those tests.

title: Sewing the actual source residue with its conserved meridian charge
text: # Sewing the actual source residue with its conserved meridian charge Research note, 26 October 2026. The actual meridian source residue can be sewn through an arbitrary integral knot operator. With one helper strand it belongs to an explicit two-copy projective corner. Its lift through the meridian wall requires a cubic meridian color; keeping the remaining colors unchanged is obstructed at first order. The charged corner has a regular rational construction anchored to the original cup, cap, crossing and full modified cut. This identifies the sewn residue and a regular lift of its corner. It does not identify the entire polar source projector away from the wall, the global affine extension, or the selected Bloch period. The original volume conjecture remains unproved. ## 1. An adjacent crossing splits the actual cup/cap channel Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1), and the complete actual color V=V_(x_0), x_0=-q^(-1)=q^(N-1). Its pivot and zero-framing twist are the existing actual matrices and scalar g=K^(1-N), theta=x_0^(1-N). Use the original self-duality matrix and right cup/cap from [the actual meridian source](meridian_casimir_source.md): D_(N-1-a,a)=q^(a^2), cup=vec(D^(-t)), cap=vec(gD)^t, Pi=cup cap, cap cup=0. (1.1) These are E,F,K intertwiners; the cup and cap factor through the unit object and Pi has rank one. For b>=3 put W_0=V^(tensor b), P_0=V^(tensor(b-2)), i=cup tensor I_(P_0), c=cap tensor I_(P_0). Let B_23 be the original checked positive crossing on the second and third strands. Then c B_23 i=theta I_(P_0), c B_23^(-1) i=theta^(-1) I_(P_0). (1.2) Here is a direct scalar check. On the three active strands the compositions are intertwiners of the simple color V, so they are scalar. Evaluate the positive composition on v_(N-1). The actual R has only its zero-th summand when its second input is v_(N-1). The cap then forces the cup component v_0 tensor v_(N-1). The cup and cap coefficients cancel D and leave g_0=theta; the crossing coefficient on v_(N-1) tensor v_(N-1) is one, since x_0=q^(N-1). For the inverse composition evaluate on v_0. After the permutation its first input is v_0, so again only the zero-th summand remains; the cap forces v_(N-1) tensor v_0 and leaves g_(N-1)=theta^(-1). Tensoring the other strands proves (1.2). Define entirely specified maps beta=theta^(-1) B_23 i, alpha=theta^(-1)c B_23, Omega=alpha beta, alpha_prime=alpha-Omega c. Equations (1.1)--(1.2) imply alpha_prime i=I, alpha_prime beta=0, c i=0, c beta=I. Thus U=(i,beta):P_0^2->W_0 and R=(alpha_prime,c)^t give R U=I_(P_0^2), Pi_12 tensor I=U E_12 R. (1.3) The four maps U E_ij R are actual matrix units. Their corner is End_H(P_0^2), with the calibrated full trace inherited from W_0. This is an explicit splitting, including its twist unit. ## 2. The actual residue can be sewn through the whole knot operator Let u=Log M, R_0=C[[u]], x(M)=-M/q, W_b(M)=V_(x(M))^(tensor b). For any integral E,F,K intertwiner A(M) of W_b(M), use exactly the full modified cut mathfrak_t_W=d_N(M)t_W. This includes an actual knot braid with its original zero-framing scalar. The [integral projective cut theorem](integral_projective_cut_duality.md) identifies these traces with one calibrated symmetric PBW form. Its rectangular-matrix cyclicity gives, for projective P_0,W_0, mathfrak_t_W0(A(0)i c) =mathfrak_t_P0(c A(0)i). (2.1) This equality uses the same PBW scalar on both sides, so no dimension or phase is chosen during sewing. It also follows by embedding the two projectives in finite free modules and applying the termwise identity sum mu((XY)_ii)=sum mu((YX)_jj). Let E_last(M) be the actual last Casimir projector on the first two factors, tensored with the remaining identities. The existing source calculation gives [u E_last]_(M=1)=(-1)^N rho (Pi_12 tensor I)/4. Combining this with (2.1) proves the all-operator residue formula Res_(u=0) mathfrak_t_W(A(M)E_last(M)) du =(-1)^N rho/4 *mathfrak_t_P0(c A(0)i). (2.2) It holds for the entire sewn knot operator, not only an isolated crossing. In the original source coordinate U=M^(2N), keeping the full coefficient 1+U^(-1) gives [(U-1)(1+U^(-1))mathfrak_t_W(A E_last)]_(M=1) =(-1)^N N rho *mathfrak_t_P0(c A(0)i). (2.3) Indeed U-1=2Nu+O(u^2), while the full source coefficient has value two only after the polar product is combined. Its factor has not been dropped in (2.3). The sewn functional is nonzero as a functional on the complete centralizer. To see this uniformly, choose T in End_H(P_0) with mathfrak_t_P0(T)!=0, using its perfect trace pairing, and set A=U E_21(T)R. Then c A i=T. In particular its zero set is a proper linear hyperplane. This does not say that every specified knot operator avoids that hyperplane. As a concrete actual braid check, the positive stabilized unknot on b strands has mathfrak_t_P0(c A_unknot i)=d_N(1)theta^(-1)!=0 after its original zero-framing correction. Here B_12 i=i, the adjacent crossing contributes theta by (1.2), and the remaining positive Markov chain contributes theta^(b-3)d_N(1). The original correction is theta^(-(b-1)), giving precisely the displayed value. The helper strand is essential. At b=2 the remaining object is the nonprojective unit: mathfrak_t_(V tensor V)(Pi)=d_N(1)!=0, although cap cup=0. Extending (2.1) to that unit would be false. Every knot can be represented after actual Markov stabilization with b>=3, retaining the same reduced zero-framed invariant. ## 3. An unchanged lower-strand color cannot lift this source Write epsilon_N=x_0^N=(-1)^(N+1). The central K^N character of the original meridian family is k_W=epsilon_N^b M^(bN). The unmodified lower tensor power V_(x(M))^(tensor(b-2)) has character epsilon_N^(b-2)M^((b-2)N). These agree at M=1 but differ at first order. If an intertwiner lifting i existed, centrality would force (k_W-k_lower)i(M)=0. Its u coefficient is 2N epsilon_N^b i(0), which is nonzero. Hence no such lift exists, even over C[u]/(u^2). This is an obstruction from the actual central character, despite agreement of the complete modules and their point-source signs. The charge-preserving lower object is instead P_b(M)=V_(-M^3/q) tensor V_(-M/q)^(tensor(b-3)). (3.1) Its K^N character is exactly k_W, including the parity sign. The first surviving strand carries the charges of the two removed strands as well as its own. If all other surviving colors remain fixed and the replacement is x(M^c), equality of central characters forces c=3. Both P_b(M) and W_b(M) are projective over the same finite nilpotent algebra H_(k_W): each color is a Steinberg deformation at M=1, and tensoring preserves projectivity. Thus the complete split corner in (1.3) admits a regular lift. The next construction makes that lift rational and anchors it without an unspecified choice of scalar. ## 4. A regular rational construction of the charged corner It is enough to construct the maps on three strands and tensor the remaining factors. Put z=-M^3/q, k=z^N, c_z=qz+q^(-1)z^(-1). On W_3(M) use the actual total K,E,F and scaled Casimir Omega. Let P_k(t)=T_N(t)+k+k^(-1), e_z=[P_k(Omega)/(Omega-c_z)]/P_k'(c_z), pi_z=(1/N)sum_(r=0)^(N-1)(K/z)^r, e=e_z pi_z. (4.1) The quotient is polynomial division before evaluation. At M=1, c_z=-2 and P_k'(c_z)=(-1)^(N+1)N^2. It is therefore a unit in the meridian germ. The selected block is Mat_N(R_0), and its interior E,F chain coefficients e_a(z), 0<a<N, are units. These are the explicit block and matrix-unit calculations from the integral projectivity proof, applied to this actual branch. In particular e projects to the highest vectors of V_z. Let U_0^0=i, U_1^0=beta and R_0^0=alpha_prime, R_1^0=c on the complete three-strand module. With the fixed basis v_a of V_z, define h_j(M)=e(M)U_j^0 v_0, U_j(M)v_a=F^a h_j(M), R_j^pre(M)(w)_a =(v_0^t R_j^0)e(M)E^a w/ product_(r=1)^a e_r(z). (4.2) The empty product is one. These are rational functions of M, regular at M=1. The block matrix units F^a e E^b divided by the same chain products prove all E,F,K intertwinings. At M=1 they recover exactly U_j^0,R_j^0, including the original phase. Every composition R_i^pre U_j is a scalar multiple D_ij(M) of identity on V_z. The two-by-two matrix D has D(1)=I. Define R_i(M)=sum_j (D(M)^(-1))_ij R_j^pre(M). Then the full two-copy retraction identity holds exactly, R_i(M)U_j(M)=delta_ij I. (4.3) All denominators are units in the complete meridian germ. Tensoring these maps with the remaining V_(x(M)) factors constructs the claimed charged corner for every b>=3. The calibrated full cut is preserved on this corner: mathfrak_t_W(U A R)=mathfrak_t_(P_b^2)(A). (4.4) This follows from the same rectangular PBW trace identity as (2.1), or from the generic actual fusion weights followed by whole-germ continuation. Thus the corner and its trace pairing extend through the wall together. The nilpotent U E_12 R is a regular lift of Pi_12 tensor I. It is not the full generic projector E_last, whose rank and generic minimal polynomial are different. Equations (2.2)--(2.3) identify its residue, not every higher meridian coefficient of that projector. ## 5. The complete peripheral factor and source step must stay charged The first source color in (3.1) has full modified dimension d_N(M^3). Its exact ratio to the original cut normalization is d_N(M^3)/d_N(M) =(M^2+1+M^(-2))/(M^(2N)+1+M^(-2N)) =(Y+1+Y^(-1))/(U+1+U^(-1)). (5.1) The phase eta_N cancels in this ratio; it remains present in each dimension separately. The whole complete value is 3/3=1. Discarding the central denominator would instead introduce an incorrect factor three. Its other central zeros also matter away from the complete germ. The source step is charged as well: under M->qM its first meridian becomes M^3->q^3M^3. A source period in that color is pulled back by the third meridian step, with all its intermediate factors retained. Identifying it with a single uncharged step would change its period connection. This charge is not visible in the complete longitude sign: for L_c=+/-1, L_c^3=L_c. Consequently a point-source module and its complete shift character alone cannot establish the required global comparison. The actual source network must retain the meridian cocharacter on its surviving strands. For positive odd charges c_1,c_2,c_3 the same central-character argument replaces them by the surviving charge c_1+c_2+c_3; the total charge and strand parity are conserved. ## 6. Scope, coverage and independent checks The residue can now be sewn through any original knot operator, and its projective corner has an explicit integral rational lift with conserved meridian charge and calibrated full trace. This adds actual quantum data to the normalized local comparison in [the equivariant source note](equivariant_cut_source_transport.md). The original knot's value of the sewn functional can still vanish. Its geometric component and selected period have not been identified. Higher source jets, coherent transport through a positive triangulation, and the central pole lattice still need comparison. The residue formulas require integral surrounding operators; polar meridian-atlas transitions must first be combined in their whole germs and are not covered term by term by (2.3). Perfection of the bilinear trace does not provide a positive norm or a noncancellation bound. No volume limit is deduced here. Projective trace ideals and ribbon calculus have existing coverage, including [the modified-trace abstract](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.00321) already checked for scope. No proof from it is assumed. The curl calibration, charge obstruction, explicit rational corner and full source factors above are independently derived in our conventions. No novelty claim is made for projective splitting or trace cyclicity. [The audit](../experiments/audit_sewn_source_corner.py) checks eight actual complete source corners, including all E,F,K intertwinings and inherited full trace pairings. Twenty-eight original braid-word cases compare the literal Casimir source residue, with the full coefficient in (2.3), against the lower-strand cup/cap evaluation. The cases include both crossing signs and both root parities. Five independent linear solves verify the first-order charged intertwiner and the obstruction for charge one. Fifteen separate exact rational corner constructions check (4.1)--(4.4) at complete and generic colors, including their actual modified dimensions. The tests include even and odd composite levels; they validate the uniform algebraic arguments, not the unproved geometric selection or norm claim. [Results](../experiments/sewn_source_corner_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_sewn_source_corner.py The subsequent [adjacent-source normal form](adjacent_source_normal_form.md) now determines the full adjacent local projectors beyond these residues. Their charged two-channel overlap equals the actual pivotal cut moment, and the remaining projector terms are regular. The ordered integral numerators generate the local matrix algebra. A trace pole proves that the unscaled adjacent projectors cannot share one finite stable lattice. The full source comparison must retain those changes of lattice and its selected section; its global geometric period and norm remain unproved.

title: One shared face frame for pointed fusion and the standard matrix kernel
text: # One shared face frame for pointed fusion and the standard matrix kernel Research note, 26 October 2026. The preceding [standard matrix comparison](standard_matrix_dilog_source_comparison.md) has four explicit face factors for a tetrahedron. This note makes them compatible on a shared affine flag chart: there is one frame for each ordered triangular face. In that frame the actual dual pairing and corrected cyclic map are fixed Gaussian matrices times their retained source-normalized scalars. Every ordered tetrahedron is the standard kernel with an explicit clock/shift insertion and a specified scalar. This is a local gluing result for an already specified pointed network. It does not assert invariance of the bare uncolored tetrahedron under vertex permutations. The earlier counterexample in [the oriented-source note](oriented_tetrahedron_source.md) still applies. Equivariance on a knot's developing cover, global literature charge conditions, the actual source/cut comparison and the regulator norm remain to be established. ## 1. Shared roots and a face frame Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, and lambda_0=-q. Thus lambda_0^2=Q, lambda_0^N=(-1)^(N-1). On a finite affine flag chart choose distinct nonzero p_i=A_i^N. Orient each edge once and choose B_ij^N=p_i-p_j on that orientation. Define the reverse root by B_ji=q B_ij. Consequently, for an arbitrary ordered edge, r_ij=B_ji/B_ij is q or q^(-1), r_ji=r_ij^(-1). (1.1) The reversal prescription is made once per edge, not afresh on each triangle. It does not prescribe B_ji=q B_ij in both directions. For f=(i,j,k), the actual relative endpoint module has generators D_f^N=lambda_f=(p_i-p_k)/(p_j-p_k), Y_f=(v_f-u_f D_f)sigma^(-1), u_f=A_j/A_k, v_f=A_i/A_k. Here sigma(D_f)=Q D_f. Put beta_f=B_ik/B_jk, rho_f=(A_j/A_i) beta_f, a_f=(A_k/A_i) B_ji/B_jk, nu_f=B_ji/B_jk. (1.2) Then rho_f^N=t_f=(p_j/p_i)lambda_f and a_f^N=1-t_f. All these quantities and their indicated factorials are nonzero. Define phi_f(n)=(Q rho_f;Q)_n/a_f^n, H(beta)_(a,b)=(beta Q^a)^b, G_f=diag(phi_f^(-1)) H(beta_f). (1.3) The factorial is periodic in n. Let Z e_n=Q^n e_n and S e_n=e_(n+1). Direct evaluation gives G_f D_f G_f^(-1)=beta_f Z, G_f Y_f G_f^(-1)=nu_f S. (1.4) Indeed H(beta) evaluates polynomials at beta Q^a. In that basis Y_f is (v_f-u_f beta_f Z)S. The adjacent ratio phi_f(a)/phi_f(a-1)=(1-rho_f Q^a)/a_f cancels this coefficient and leaves v_f a_f=nu_f. Thus the same G_f works regardless of which tetrahedron contains the ordered face. ## 2. The actual face pairing is a fixed Gaussian times a fixed scalar Write bar f=(k,j,i). Let M_f be the actual pairing induced from the shared endpoint caps and pointed fusion maps, as in the [relative pivotal proof](relative_pivotal_duality.md). Its scalar is already fixed by those caps. In the new frames its matrix is M_f^st=G_f^(-t) M_f G_(bar f)^(-1). (2.1) The proved reversal anti-map on the raw relative generators is a(D)=-Y^(-1)D, a(Y)=QY^(-1). Substitute (1.4), retaining transpose and generator order. With c_f=-r_ik^(-1), the resulting two equations are M_f^st S=Q S M_f^st, M_f^st Z=c_f Z S M_f^st. (2.2) They determine every matrix entry from its (0,0) entry. Namely M_f^st=mu_f Mcal_f, mu_f=(M_f^st)_(0,0), Mcal_f(a,b)=Q^b c_f^n Q^(n(n+1)/2), n=a-b mod N. (2.3) For a direct proof, the first equation gives M_(a,b)=Q^b F_(a-b). The second gives F_n=c_f Q^n F_(n-1). Its cyclic consistency is c_f^N Q^(N(N+1)/2)=1. This proves (2.3) at every parity, without dividing by two modulo N. The Gaussian is a product of two invertible diagonal matrices and the Fourier matrix (Q^(-ab)). Since the original pairing is invertible, mu_f is nonzero. If r_ik=q, (2.3) is equivalently Mcal_f(a,b)=Q^b lambda_0^((a-b)^2). If r_ik=q^(-1), it is the transpose of this matrix. Thus its entire matrix dependence on the flag parameters has disappeared; mu_f is the actual remaining scalar function. It is not set to one. ## 3. The corrected cyclic map has the same property Write r f=(j,k,i). The preceding oriented-source proof constructed the actual cyclic map U_f=tau_N lambda_f L_f D_f^(-1), tau_N^3=Q, with exact cyclic and pairing coherence. Define U_f^st=G_(r f) U_f G_f^(-1). Its raw generator equations are D_(r f) U_f=-Q U_f D_f^(-1)Y_f and Y_(r f) U_f=Q U_f D_f^(-1). Therefore (1.4) gives Z U_f^st=crot_f U_f^st Z^(-1)S, S U_f^st=drot_f U_f^st Z^(-1), crot_f=-Q r_ik, drot_f=Q r_ik/r_jk. (3.1) Solving the entry recurrences yields U_f^st=xi_f Ucal_f, xi_f=(U_f^st)_(0,0), Ucal_f(a,b)=drot_f^(-a) crot_f^(-b) Q^(ab+b(b+1)/2). (3.2) The second equation of (3.1) first gives U_(a,b)=drot_f^(-a)Q^(ab) U_(0,b). The first then gives U_(0,b+1)=crot_f^(-1)Q^(b+1)U_(0,b). These are precisely (3.2). Again Ucal_f is a diagonal--Fourier--diagonal product and xi_f is nonzero. The chosen tau_N is retained in xi_f. Conjugating the already proved identities gives U_(r^2 f)^st U_(r f)^st U_f^st=I, (U_f^st)^t M_(r f)^st (U_(i,k,j)^st)^(-1)=M_f^st. (3.3) Thus the scalar functions in (2.3) and (3.2) obey the exact coherence relations forced by the Gaussian products. They are not independent normalizations assigned at the end of each move. ## 4. A standard kernel for every ordered tetrahedron For an ordered tetrahedron (i,j,k,l), name its faces A=(i,k,l), B=(i,j,k), C=(i,j,l), D=(j,k,l). Use their shared roots from (1.2). They satisfy rho_A=rho_C rho_D. Put alpha=rho_C, beta=rho_D, eta=rho_A, gamma=a_A/a_D, v=a_C/a_A, u=alpha/gamma. Then u^N+v^N=1. Define the marked integers e,d modulo N by Q^e=gamma/rho_B=r_ik/r_jk, Q^d=-lambda_0 gamma beta v/a_B=q/r_jk. (4.1) The first root defect uses the edges ik and jk; it does not use ij. Since every r is q or q^(-1), e is 0,1 or -1 and d is 0 or 1 modulo N. These are explicit orientation data. The central standard shape has the projective expression u^N=(p_i-p_l)(p_k-p_j)/((p_j-p_l)(p_k-p_i)). (4.1a) With the convention r(infinity,0,1,z)=z used in the crossing fundamental-cycle note, (4.1a) is r(p_i,p_j,p_k,p_l)^(-1). The reciprocal and the corresponding oriented tetrahedron order must be carried into any regulator comparison. They cannot be removed by calling both coordinates the geometric shape. The formula concerns the root center at fixed N; it does not specify the quantum-parameter trajectory of a selected period across N. Let R_raw be the actual pointed fusion of the raw face modules C and D, with total face A and relative face B. Let P exchange the total and relative input factors. The exact shared-frame formula is (G_C tensor G_D) R_raw (G_A^(-1) tensor G_B^(-1)) P =kappa phi_B(e) L0(u,v)(Z^d S^(-e) tensor I), kappa=(1/N)sum_(b=0)^(N-1) gamma^(-b)(Q eta;Q)_b/(Q beta;Q)_b. (4.2) Here kappa is the nonzero unit-fixed scalar from the preceding local comparison. At odd N, L0 is exactly the published basic matrix kernel without its h(u) prefactor. At every N it is the same existing pointed-fusion expression L0_(k,l)^(i,j)=Q^(kj)lambda_0^(k^2) Omega(u,v|i-k) delta_(i+j,l). This all-level expression does not extend the literature's odd-level charge definition by dividing by two at even N. Here is a direct derivation of (4.2). Normalize each raw endpoint module by X_tilde=(u_f/v_f)D_f and Y_tilde=Y_f/v_f. The polynomial basis change diag((u_f/v_f)^n) sends this normalized module to the raw one. These changes intertwine both the total and relative generators of the fusion, so the preceding four-frame comparison applies with parameters s=rho_C^N,t=rho_D^N. The total and two output factors then cancel against the shared face frames. The natural relative evaluation root is gamma rather than rho_B, so its evaluation map differs by S^(-e). Its remaining diagonal entry at k is D_gamma(k) lambda_0^(-k^2) phi_B(k+e), D_gamma(k)=(beta v)^k / product_(j=1)^k(1-gamma^(-1)Q^(-j)). Periodicity and finite-product cancellation give phi_B(k+e)=phi_B(e)(Q gamma;Q)_k/a_B^k, product_(j=1)^k(1-gamma^(-1)Q^(-j)) =(-gamma)^(-k)Q^(-k(k+1)/2)(Q gamma;Q)_k. Consequently that entry is exactly phi_B(e)(-lambda_0 gamma beta v/a_B)^k =phi_B(e)Q^(dk). This proves the whole clock/shift factor and its scalar, including at even and composite levels. If the tetrahedron order agrees with all its edge orientations, e=d=0 and (4.2) is kappa L0. ## 5. The scalar line and source evaluation are retained The scalar functions can be evaluated by the specified (0,0) entries; their determinant equations also give exact norm data: mu_f^N=det M_f / (det G_f det G_(bar f) det Mcal_f), xi_f^N=(det G_(r f) det U_f) / (det G_f det Ucal_f). (5.1) These equations do not authorize new phase choices. The original caps and trivalent tensors determine mu_f and xi_f themselves. For the normalized literature kernel L=h(u)L0, the multiplier in (4.2) is kappa phi_B(e)/h(u), with exactly the same Weyl insertion. Full integer-charge lifts and their non-phase multipliers remain as in the preceding comparison note. For any already specified finite contraction, (1.3), (2.1) and (3.2) are honest changes of bases. All interior inverse frames cancel. A source column p changes to G_f p; its cut row changes to ell G_f^(-1). A raw unit is therefore the generally nonconstant column (phi_f(n)^(-1))_n, not a new unit in the standard coordinates. At a source wall, the lattice and its normal quotient must move with the frame, using the retained carry/linking constructions. These observations prove preservation of a given contraction. They do not construct that contraction on an arbitrary positive geometric triangulation. Projective/deck equivariance, the global charge constraints, its actual source extension and selected cut must still be matched. In particular the fixed Gaussian matrices above have not been declared equal to a published choice with its scalar normalizations omitted. The audited ideal triangulation theorem supplies the desired geometric developing flags and marked fundamental-class period. This note supplies shared face algebra for a proposed quantum comparison. Equality of the actual and triangulation source classes, integral pointings and regulator norms does not follow from either existence statement alone. The subsequent [source-flag proof](source_flag_transport.md) makes the origin an extra marked point. Its finite-source transports are fixed by actual edge duality and preserve fusion, caps and cyclic maps exactly. It also expresses the normal chart and its non-scalar first coefficient as jets of that same source family. This supplies more of the local source comparison; the genuine degenerate edge lattice and selected global norm remain necessary. ## 6. Independent finite-field audit [The audit](../experiments/audit_standard_face_gluing.py) constructs four distinct affine flags and roots of all six edge differences in exact finite fields. For each N=2,3,4,5,6,9, it checks the 24 ordered face pairings and cyclic maps against (2.3),(3.2), retaining their actual scalars, and all 24 ordered tetrahedron identities (4.2), including the two root-defect formulas (4.1). Thus 144 pairings, 144 cyclic maps and 144 full ordered kernels passed. [Results](../experiments/standard_face_gluing_results.json). The uniform proofs above are separate from these finite tests. python3 experiments/audit_standard_face_gluing.py

title: Independent defining-integral audit of the shrinking-strip full-Psi estimate
text: # Independent defining-integral audit of the shrinking-strip full-Psi estimate 28 October 2026. The full-Psi estimates in Section 5 of [quantitative regular descent](quantitative_regular_phase_descent.md) are correct, with the explicit Cauchy-disk qualification below. The proof uses the defining integral and its exact subtraction formula; no published asymptotic theorem is assumed. It is a local selected-chart estimate, not a contour-crossing or whole-source boundary theorem. ## 1. Uniform kernel bound with the width displayed Use the exact remainder formula independently derived in [the defining-integral note](literature_state_volume.md#21-a-uniform-complex-remainder-on-an-entire-horizontal-strip): log Phi_b(z/(2pi b))=Li_2(-exp z)/(2pi i b^2)+R_b(z), R_b(z)=-2i[ integral_0^infinity H_b(t)sin(zt/pi)dt +c arctan(z/pi)]-i pi c, c=-b^2/24, K_b(t)=[1/sinh(b^2t)-1/(b^2t)]/[4t sinh t], H_b(t)=K_b(t)-c exp(-t)/t. (1) The constant and logarithm are the ones fixed by the original upper indentation and the left-half-plane anchor. In particular R_b(0)= i pi b^2/24; it is not an adjustable scalar normalization. For all v>0, 0<=1/v-1/sinh(v)<=v/6. (2) For 0<v<sqrt(6), the right inequality follows by expanding sinh(v)(1-v^2/6): the cubic coefficient is zero and every subsequent coefficient is negative, giving sinh(v)(1-v^2/6)<=v. Above sqrt(6) it follows already from 1/v<=v/6. Thus (2) is uniform. It gives |K_b(t)|<=b^2/[24sinh(t)]. For t>=1 this is O(b^2exp(-t)). For 0<t<=1, uniformly in 0<b<=1, K_b(t)=c/t+O(b^2t). Indeed 1/sinh(v)=1/v-v/6+O(v^3) uniformly for v=b^2t<=1; substitution gives c/sinh(t)+O(b^6t), followed by 1/sinh(t)=1/t+O(t). Consequently |H_b(t)|<=Cb^2 (0<t<=1), |H_b(t)|<=Cb^2exp(-t) (t>=1). (3) For 0<delta<=1, integration yields integral_0^infinity |H_b(t)|exp((1-delta/pi)t)dt <=Cb^2/delta. (4) This estimate has no dependence on Re z. On |Im z|<=pi-delta, |sin(zt/pi)|<=exp((1-delta/pi)t), so it controls the integral in (1) uniformly on the entire horizontal strip. For the remaining elementary term, put w=z/pi. Both 1+iw and 1-iw have positive real part at least delta/pi. On their principal branches, arctan(w)=[Log(1+iw)-Log(1-iw)]/(2i). The argument difference is bounded by pi, and the modulus ratio is between (delta/(2pi))^2 and its reciprocal. These bounds persist for arbitrarily large Re w. Hence |arctan(z/pi)|<=C log(2/delta). (5) Equations (1),(4),(5) prove the absolute uniform estimate |R_b(z)|<=Cb^2[delta^(-1)+log(2/delta)], |Im z|<=pi-delta, 0<b<=1, 0<delta<=1. (6) ## 2. The actual half-step for both signs Set b^2=1/N and h=2pi i/N. The actual positive full function has the recorded identification log Psi_+(z)=log Phi_b(w/(2pi b)), w=z-i pi(1+1/N). (7) For delta<=Im z<=2pi-delta and delta>=2pi/N, the distance of w to both edges +/-pi is at least delta-pi/N>=delta/2. The argument in the leading dilogarithm is exactly -exp(w)=exp(z-h/2). Write f(z)=Li_2(exp z) on the selected strip continuation from Re z negative. Then f'(z)=-Log(1-exp z) and f''(z)=exp z/(1-exp z). For y separated from 2pi Z by delta/2, |1-r exp(iy)|>=[delta/(2pi)](1+r), r>=0. This follows from |1-r exp(iy)|^2=(1-r)^2+4r sin^2(y/2) and sin(delta/4)>=delta/(2pi). Thus |f''|<=C/delta uniformly over all real parts, including on the whole half-step segment. Taylor's integral remainder and (6) give log Psi_+(z)=f(z)/h+(1/2)Log(1-exp z)+O(1/(Ndelta)). (8) The negative actual function is conjugate-reflected with all branches anchored in the same way. Reflection changes h to -h, but preserves the SIGN of the half-logarithm. Therefore both signs satisfy log Psi_epsilon(z) =Li_2(exp z)/(epsilon h) +(1/2)Log(1-exp z)+O(1/(Ndelta)), (9) on delta<=epsilon Im z<=2pi-delta. There is no hidden sign change or N-dependent normalizing constant in (9). ## 3. Derivatives down to the stated Ndelta threshold There is a small logical qualification when using Cauchy's estimate. At delta=2pi/N, one cannot simply apply a statement formulated only for margin >=2pi/N to every point of a disk with a smaller margin. Instead use the defining-integral proof again. For a center satisfying the hypotheses of (9), take the complex disk |z'-z|<=delta/4. Its signed angular margin is at least 3delta/4. After the ACTUAL half-step (7), its Phi strip margin is at least 3delta/4-pi/N>=delta/4. (10) Both the integral remainder and the Taylor remainder are therefore O(1/(Ndelta)) throughout this disk. The remainder in (9) is holomorphic there with its fixed selected branches. Cauchy's formula now proves for every fixed integer k>=0, |partial_z^k remainder|<=C_k/[Ndelta^(k+1)]. (11) This proves the derivative assertion without strengthening the threshold delta>=2pi/N or assuming a fixed strip width. ## 4. Source-chart scope and a harmless Hessian sign correction These estimates apply to the actual full Psi functions on their selected logarithmic strips and only to such local charts. A product estimate for the original network must retain every exponential N-dependent monomial/Gaussian/window factor in its specified leading action; rational amplitudes must obey the asserted denominator bounds. The moment-ray corrections and chart-exit currents are not discarded. No estimate here crosses a quantum pole, identifies a different sheet, or bounds a mixed endpoint/bulk period. One unrelated sign in Section 3 of the descent note needs correction. For its explicitly written W=sum epsilon Li_2(A)+Z^tCZ/2+linear, partial^2 W=C+sum epsilon v v^t A/(1-A), (12) rather than a minus sign. The polynomial Hessian N/L norm bound and every subsequent descent estimate use absolute values, so this correction changes none of those inequalities. I found no further error in the strip constants, the half-step normalization, or the claimed local-chart limitation. The separate global issue remains estimation of all original exit/boundary currents.

title: Both original crossing signs have the same flat Green transport
text: # Both original crossing signs have the same flat Green transport 28 October 2026. At complete color, the ORIGINAL negative crossing is the flip-conjugate of the positive crossing in the SAME balanced flat metric. The apparent diagonal comparison in an unbalanced frame cancels to a phase depending only on total integer degree. This transports the proved clock/ground Green system to negative crossings without an ill-conditioned factorial change of metric. All original Cartan, twist, pivotal and cap normalizations are retained. This is a local operator theorem; it gives no lower bound for the final scalar source pairing. ## 1. Exact antiunitary including the common Cartan phase Put q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=q^(N-1)=-q^(-1), rho=q-q^(-1), and eta=exp(pi*i/(2N)). Write the original crossings as R_+=kappa K_0^+, R_-=kappa^(-1)K_0^-, kappa=eta^((N-1)^2), |kappa|=1. Let P swap the two heads and let C be coefficientwise conjugation in the ORIGINAL balanced basis. Then EXACTLY R_-=P overline(R_+)P, K_0^-=P overline(K_0^+)P. (1) Thus J=P C is an antiunitary involution and R_-=J R_+ J^(-1). It is not an assertion that R_+ itself is unitary. Here is a direct proof fixing the frame and phase. In the real unbalanced basis, F is the real unit shift and E_j=[j]_q^2 is real at this complete color. The common-scalar-removed checked crossing is B=P D Theta, D_(a,b)=x^(-a-b)q^(2ab). D is unitary diagonal. The finite nilpotent Euler factor Theta has coefficients q^(k(k-1)/2)rho^k/[k]_q!. Conjugating them gives the ordinary inverse Euler coefficients; the finite q-binomial convolution proves overline(Theta)=Theta^(-1). Hence overline(B)=D^(-1)P B^(-1)P D. (2) The actual balanced gauge is g_j=(Q;Q)_j, up to a REAL nonzero diagonal. Since (Q;Q)_j=(-rho)^j q^(j(j+1)/2)[j]_q!, g_j/overline(g_j)=(-1)^j q^(j(j+1)), the residual pair phase after transporting (2) to the balanced frame is (g_a g_b)/(overline(g_a g_b)) D_(a,b) =q^((a+b)(a+b+2)). (3) This depends only on total INTEGER head degree a+b. The actual crossings and P preserve that degree, so this phase commutes with them and cancels from the conjugation relation. This proves (1). The full scalar obeys overline(kappa)=kappa^(-1), so there is no unrecorded sign or framing multiplier. No factorial modulus remains in the comparison and no unbalanced norm is used in the result. ## 2. Negative clock and ground families Take the proved original positive clock and ground operators K_m^+,H_m^+ from Section 8 of [the original source theorem](actual_rogers_sink_opposite_beta_source.md). Their clock is Q^(m J_second) immediately after C^(-1), and all indices are physical 0,...,N-1. Define the negative auxiliary families by the exact antiunitary transport K_m^-=P overline(K_m^+)P, H_m^-=P overline(H_m^+)P. (4) At m=0 this is the literal ORIGINAL negative crossing with its common scalar removed. These definitions transport a specified original clock insertion; they do not replace the negative crossing by its transpose or assume a new local metric. Both families are N-periodic in m. For an array X_(c,d;a,b) let the positive Green shift be (A_+ X)_(c,d;a,b)=x^(-1)X_(c,d-1;a-1,b) when a,d>=1, with zero outside the physical range. Its antiunitary transport is (A_- X)_(c,d;a,b)=x X_(c-1,d;a,b-1), (5) when b,c>=1, zero otherwise. In scalar kernel coordinates this is the monomial x z_first-output/z_second-input. The exact signed source Ward equations are K_m^+-A_+ K_(m+1)^+=H_m^+, K_m^--A_- K_(m+1)^-=H_m^-. (6) The second is the antiunitary image of the first, with all original support conditions transported, so no negative-current endpoint is discarded independently. For input (a,b), the negative ground output is (0,a+b), provided a+b<N, with coefficient Q^(-m a)x^a {a+b choose b}_(Q^(-1)) (Q^(-m)x^2;Q^(-1))_b. (7) It is zero if a+b>=N. This is the conjugate of the EXACT positive ground coefficient with its two input indices exchanged. In particular both ground channels have rank N and the same singular values. Their exponential bulk factorial weight has not disappeared. ## 3. Flat Green conditioning is identical for both signs Use the clock-family Hilbert space H_clock=direct_sum_(m mod N) HS(V_N tensor V_N), ||X||^2=sum_m ||X_m||_HS^2, (T_+ X)_m=A_+X_(m+1), (T_- X)_m=A_-X_(m+1). All head basis vectors have norm one. The clock advance is a permutation, and (5) is a partial permutation with a unit scalar, so ||T_+||<=1, ||T_-||<=1, T_+^N=T_-^N=0. (8) The nilpotence follows from the strictly increasing first input demand for the positive sign and second input demand for the negative sign. It concerns source transport, not the full braid image group. The exact inverses are finite: G_+=(1-T_+)^(-1)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1)T_+^j, G_-=(1-T_-)^(-1)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1)T_-^j, ||G_+||,||G_-||<=N, ||G_+^(-1)||,||G_-^(-1)||<=2. (9) Thus the local transformations have condition number at most 2N in the SAME metric for either sign. They reconstruct the original signed crossings from (6), with scalar kappa or kappa^(-1) respectively. For clarity, the family shifts are partial permutations with finite chains of length at most N; some chains have length exactly N. After unit phase gauges on each chain, 1-T is the elementary bidiagonal matrix. Its squared singular values on a chain of length L are 4 sin^2[(2j-1)pi/(4L+2)], j=1,...,L. Consequently the exact full family norms are ||G_+||=||G_-||=1/[2 sin(pi/(4N+2))], ||G_+^(-1)||=||G_-^(-1)||=2 cos(pi/(2N+1)). (10) The coarser bounds (9) already suffice for polynomial-cost tensor transport at fixed word length. These estimates do NOT lower-bound the final scalar period: the pulled-back original source can still be nearly orthogonal to the tensor of ground channels. ## 4. Original source and scope Equation (1) is used locally to represent the negative matrix at its actual four ports. It is NOT applied as a global conjugation of the word or to change the knot into its mirror. All original cups, caps, pivots, common Cartan and zero-framing lines stay in their prescribed places. In particular no metric change or scalar normalization is hidden in passing from positive to negative Green transport. The [exact root audit](../experiments/audit_signed_green_antiunitary_transport.py) checks the full original negative crossing, all negative clock Ward and ground coefficients, nilpotent reconstruction and original whole signed pivotal sources. Small bidiagonal singular-value checks verify (10) independently of the phase calculation; the proof of the all-N bounds is the explicit partial-permutation structure.

title: Fourier reduction of singular face matrices and the 6_2 state
text: # Fourier reduction of singular face matrices and the 6_2 state Research note, 25 October 2026. The local operators are the published charged Andersen--Kashaev kernels, with their Fourier and normalization identities independently proved in `faddeev_pentagon_audit.md`. We evaluate those kernels before extracting a boundary fiber. This does not replace them with the positive factorial model, and does not require inversion of the full face matrix. The results are a general reduction and volume theorem under explicit rank hypotheses, and complete finite geometric/peripheral certificates for its application to 6_2. Uniform membership for all two-bridge knots, global connecting paths, and the all-alternating conjecture remain open. The subsequent [cohomology proof](automatic_face_regularity.md) shows that both Fourier rank hypotheses hold for every globally branched ideal triangulation of a knot exterior in S^3. Thus they are no longer additional conditions in that setting. ## 1. A singular face matrix can give a regular reduced integral Use N ordered tetrahedra, 2N paired faces, signs epsilon, and selectors X_i. Put D=X_0-X_1+X_2, R=X_2-X_3, E=diag(epsilon). The existing full charged kernel contraction is integral delta(Dx) product_j f_j(-(Rx)_j) exp[-2pi i (X_0x)^T E R x] dx, (1.1) where f_j is the positive charged function or its conjugate. In the previous proper calculation, t=E R x gave an invertible coordinate system on ker D. That is sufficient but not necessary. Assume rank D=N. Choose rational matrices G,F with DG=I and columns of F a basis of ker D. Write x=G u+F z, and define T=E R F, U=X_0 F, k=dim ker T, rank T=N-k. Choose K a basis of ker T and a complement Z, so [Z K] is invertible. Writing z=Z a+K b gives t=P a, P=T Z. The phase is -2pi i a^T P^T U Z a -2pi i b^T C a, C=K^T U^T P. (1.2) **Additional rank hypothesis:** rank C=k. Choose CJ=I and V a basis of ker C. With a=J c+V s, the b integral is delta(c), and the result is c_X integral_R^d exp(2pi i s^T Q_red s) product_j f_j(epsilon_j(Ss)_j) ds, d=N-2k, S=P V, Q_red=-sym(S^T U Z V), c_X=|det[G F] det[Z K] det[J V]|. (1.3) All displayed determinants are retained. In particular, a numerical specialization is not used to discard a normalization factor. In (1.3) we have reversed the remaining real coordinates s after the delta integration. The dynamical variable is then t=-E R x=S s; the quadratic is unchanged and the Lebesgue Jacobian is one. This fixes the sign needed for the subsequent common-Phi convention. **Distributional justification.** The delta(Dx) is an ordinary independent linear delta measure. The remaining product of positive charged functions, pulled back by the injective map P, is Schwartz in a; the quadratic chirp preserves Schwartz space. Fourier integration in b gives delta(Ca), whose pullback is defined because C is surjective. Equivalently insert exp(-pi eta |b|^2): its b integral is eta^(-k/2)exp(-pi|Ca|^2/eta), and the ordinary Gaussian approximate-identity limit after a=Jc+Vs gives (1.3). The Schwartz bounds justify that limit. Positive Gaussian regularizations in all face variables give the same Fourier distribution by completing the kernel Gaussian and applying the same argument. This is an evaluation of (1.1), not a divergent integral treated as absolutely convergent. The reduced integral itself is absolutely convergent. Its value is independent of the chosen rational bases with exactly the determinants in (1.3). For k=0 the calculation gives the earlier proper expression: Q_ambient=Q_f and c_X/|det S|=1/|det script-A|. ## 2. Stokes still gives the edge identities Let a_e,b_e,c_e denote local opposite-pair edge incidences and A_ed,B_ed the literature edge matrices of `face_edge_stokes_identity.md`. For an arbitrary assignment lambda to global edges, put on an ordered triangle i<j<k phi(lambda)_ijk=lambda_jk-lambda_ik. Then D phi=0 and E R phi=B_ed^T lambda. The same face cancellation as in the previous note, now without an inverse face matrix, gives B_ed^T lambda in im S, S^T A_ed^T = S^T G_ambient B_ed^T, (2.1) G_ambient=-2 Q_ambient+P_+, P_+=(E+I)/2. Here Q_ambient is any real symmetric extension of Q_red from im S. For completeness, write phi=F z_lambda. The Stokes cancellation gives U^T B_ed^T lambda=T^T(lambda_01-lambda_02), U z_lambda=lambda_23-lambda_13. If b is a ker T direction, the first equality implies K^T U^T B_ed^T lambda=0, so B_ed^T lambda is in im S. Differentiating the quadratic (1.2) along this direction gives -2 S^T Q_ambient B_ed^T lambda=S^T(a(lambda)-b(lambda)). Adding P_+ gives (2.1). Changes of lift by ker T vanish in this calculation precisely because S satisfies the Fourier constraints. ## 3. A complete-geometry volume theorem for the full tensor Assume the two rank hypotheses of Section 1 and a complete positive geometric ideal structure. Choose its actual physical angles as the charges. Use b>0 for the quantum parameter, Q_b=b+b^(-1), h=Q_b^(-2). Write a,c for physical angle vectors in radians and put d_angle=pi 1-a, C_angle=E c, H=Q_ambient-P_+/2, W=2 Q_ambient d_angle-C_angle. Applying the exact inversion identity to the reduced tensor and setting y=i d_angle+S z gives the dynamical integrand exp[(i y^T H y+W^T y)/(2pi h)] product_j Phi_b(y_j/(2pi sqrt(h))). (3.1) The Jacobian is (Q_b/(2pi))^d, multiplied by c_X. All omitted factors in this display are the explicit unit phases of Section 6 below. **Lemma (decoration).** If z_j are the positive literature shape parameters, set u=log|z| and w=log|z''|. There is a real global edge vector lambda with u=-B_ed^T lambda/2, w=A_ed^T lambda/2. (3.2) Choose consistently scaled horospheres on the complete cusp(s), and let lambda_e be the signed length of the segment on e between them. The formula is the cross-ratio modulus identity. For the negative ordering with vertices (infinity,0,1,z), take unit horosphere factors: the nonzero finite edge contributions are lambda_13=2log|z| and lambda_23=2log|1-z|. Thus u=(b_e-c_e)lambda/2 and w=(a_e-b_e)lambda/2. Changing the ordering gives exactly (3.2) with the columnwise epsilon convention. Horosphere changes add vertex terms and cancel in both formulas. By (2.1), Re y_*=-u lies in im S, where y_*=-Log z+i pi 1, Im y_*=d_angle. It is therefore on the actual integration plane. The real part of the ambient classical gradient at this point is zero: in a positive tetrahedron it is d_angle-c-Arg z''=0, and in a negative tetrahedron it is c-Arg z''=0. Its imaginary part on im S is zero by (3.2) and (2.1). Hence y_* is a full critical point on the reduced plane. For the classical phase F_0(y)=i y^T H y+W^T y-i sum_j Li_2(-exp y_j), the Bloch--Wigner identity gives Re F_0(y_*)=-sum_j D(z_j)=-Vol(M). Its real Hessian on real directions in im S is -S^T diag[Im(e^y/(1+e^y))] S, which is negative definite because 0<Im y_j<pi. Thus the critical point is unique on its horizontal plane, has a nonzero Gaussian coefficient, and has the global linear tail bound proved by the ray argument in `literature_state_volume.md`. The independently derived uniform Phi remainder and the exact h versus b^2 correction apply to the same N factors. The implicit-function and contour arguments therefore apply in dimension d. They prove lim_(h->0+) -2pi h log|Z_AK(X,complete angles;b)|=Vol(M). (3.3) The normalized full tensor is nonzero for sufficiently small h. This theorem does not assume B invertible, a FAMED longitude identity, or a formal absence of cancellations. It is a theorem for the specified kernel contraction under the displayed rank/geometric hypotheses; it does not assert global triangulation invariance. ## 4. The explicit singular chart for 6_2 Use the folded word RRLR, hence Conway [3,1,2]=11/3, and the ordered faces returned by `certify_six_two.py`. The signs are (+,+,-,-,-,+). The 12 by 12 stacked face matrix has rank 11. Nevertheless rank D=6, k=1, rank C=1, d=4 and c_X=1. A determinant-one change of the reduced coordinates gives the especially simple affine shape plane y=(u,v,i pi-u-v,i pi-u-v,w,z), z_coord=(u,v,w,z). Thus the singularity imposes actual linear relations; it does not prevent an integral representation of the same charged tensor. The normal cusp cycles computed from the face pairings give H_1(M)=Z, alpha of linking number 1, beta of linking number 6, intersection alpha.beta=1, and [beta-6alpha]=boundary_2*(-2,-3,-7,3,0,3)^T. Consequently l=beta-6alpha is the primitive preferred longitude up to sign. This is an integral cellular certificate. Its angle rows are recorded in the script; the affine offset and its zero branch are checked independently. The optional combinatorial isomorphism to the marked canonical 6_2 triangulation calibrates alpha to the standard meridian and l to the standard longitude, with zero affine correction. Its cusp matrix from the imported arbitrary basis is [[6,-1],[1,0]]. A positive rational reference angle structure, in units of pi, is (5,1,1 | 5,1,1 | 4,2,1 | 4,1,2 | 5,1,1 | 1,5,1)/7. Its longitude is zero. On the entire balanced affine angle space, the imaginary affine plane above is fixed; the angle-dependent linear term varies only with the longitude. Its coefficient is (lambda/2) p, p=(-1,-1,-1,1)^T, x=p^T z_coord=-u-v-w+z, gamma=0. The imaginary part of x is exactly the angular holonomy of alpha. All these claims are rational matrix identities on the complete affine angle space, rather than identities checked only at one structure. ## 5. An exact complete-geometry certificate for 6_2 In the native all-positive shape convention the layer shapes are (a,a,b,b,c,c), with P(c)=c^5-3c^4+5c^3-5c^2+4c-1=0, a=c^3-2c^2+2c-1, b=2c^4-5c^3+8c^2-7c+6. The root is isolated by the rational Rouché disc |c-(1186078+874646 i)/10^6|<10^(-5). The Taylor remainder bound divided by the lower bound for the linear term is less than 0.086 (the exact test is less than 1/10). Thus there is exactly one root in the disc. Rational image enclosures put every shape in the upper half-plane. The eight native multiplicative edge/peripheral equations reduce to zero modulo P. Rational atan2 and Machin bounds fix their logarithmic branches. All dihedral angles are greater than 1/4 radian. The source Gaussian uses the opposite global orientation from this native shape convention. Choose the quad in each newly ordered tetrahedron first, then uniformly replace its positive shape q by 1/conj(q). In terms of the lower root t=conj(c), the positive **literature** shape parameters for our six ordered tetrahedra are (1/a(t),1/a(t),1/b(t),1/b(t),1-t,1/t). (5.1) This distinction preserves angles and Bloch--Wigner volume but changes logarithmic moduli. Inverting tetrahedra individually according only to their signs would give the wrong saddle. The script independently reduces all six literature Neumann--Zagier edge equations and the two normal peripheral equations using (5.1) modulo P(t). It also fixes the affine-plane branch y_0+y_1+y_2=i pi and y_2=y_3. These give a complete positive ideal structure without relying on a numerical solver. Its volume is V=2[D(a)+D(b)+D(c)] =4.4008325161230461014... . ## 6. The selected boundary state and its exact tensor normalization Define the following state by disintegrating the Fourier-reduced existing tensor along x=-u-v-w+z. With z=x+u+v+w, put J_6_2(h,x)=(2pi sqrt(h))^(-4) integral I_b(u,v,w,z) du dv dw, I_b=exp[(i z_coord^T H_red z_coord+pi v_lin^T z_coord)/(2pi h)] product_(j=1)^6 Phi_b(y_j/(2pi sqrt(h))), v_lin=(-2,-2,-1,1)^T, H_red = [ -3/2 -3/2 -3/2 1/2 ] [ -3/2 -3/2 -3/2 1/2 ] [ -3/2 -3/2 -2 1 ] [ 1/2 1/2 1 -1/2 ]. (6.1) The contour is the horizontal fiber through the complete saddle at x=0, continued for small x. The positive coarea Jacobian is one when eliminating z, since its coefficient in x is one. Equivalently the exponent after substitution is [i(-(u+v)^2-(u+v)w-w^2/2+xw-x^2/2) +pi(x-u-v)]/(2pi h), and the Phi arguments have numerators u, v, i pi-u-v, i pi-u-v, w, x+u+v+w. This is not the printed FAMED formula evaluated with det script-A=0. It is a fiber of the original charged-operator contraction, providing the type of factorization used in the existing AK formulation. Here is its exact phase convention. For balanced physical angles let Q_ambient be the rational extension in the certificate and set d_angle=pi 1-a, C_angle=E c, W=2 Q_ambient d_angle-C_angle, Theta=C_angle^T d_angle-d_angle^T Q_ambient d_angle, k(a,c)=a c/(4pi)+(a-c)/12-pi/24, beta0=(0,0,1,1,0,0)^T, kappa=-beta0^T H beta0+(W^T beta0)/pi, K=sum_j epsilon_j k(a_j,c_j)-pi N_+/12 +Theta/(2pi)+pi kappa/2. The exact inversion and charged Fourier identities now give Z_AK(X,angles;b)=i exp(i K/h) integral_(R+i mu) J_6_2(h,x)exp(lambda x/(4pi h)) dx. (6.2) At the rational reference angles kappa=27/35. Thus removing the constant from the displayed compact integrand has the recorded multiplier exp(27pi i/(70h)); it is included in K in (6.2). Choosing the existing AK level ell=-4K/pi removes precisely that phase. The root i is exp(pi i N/12) for N=6. No peripheral variable has been specialized in (6.2). The strip, tail, and Fourier--Laplace uniqueness arguments of the previous phase note apply to this reduced integral. The map from balanced angles to (mu,lambda) has rank two. Thus the fixed normalization in (6.2) recovers this selected fiber uniquely from that normalized tensor function. General identification with fibers from arbitrary triangulations still requires compatible connecting paths. ## 7. Volume and the quantum A-operator for this state There is also a direct critical-equation check, independent of the general decoration lemma in Section 3. Let g=(1/i)grad F_0 in the four coordinates of (6.1), and use the exact edge/normal-curve matrices from the certificate. They give all edge equations as linear combinations of g with zero logarithmic offset. Their coefficient matrix has rank three. Adding the preferred-longitude row gives rank four. Therefore the complete shapes (5.1) force g=0. The meridian relation is H_alpha=x+b_alpha^T g, H_l=b_l^T g, b_alpha^T p=0, b_l^T p=2. (7.1) In particular x=0 at completeness. The restricted Hessian on its three-dimensional fiber has negative definite real part. The same uniform Phi remainder, complex saddle, and tail proof as before gives lim_(h->0+) -2pi h log|J_6_2(h,0)|=Vol(S^3\6_2). (7.2) For clarity, the critical value is not inferred from the exponentiated equations alone. In the affine coordinates y=i pi beta0+S z_coord, the exact Bloch--Wigner identity is Re F_0 = Re z_coord . Re grad F_0 + sum_j D(-exp y_j). At the certified critical point this is -sum_j D(z_j). Strict concavity and the nonzero Gaussian coefficient control cancellation. The state is nonzero for all sufficiently small h. All Phi arguments and Gaussian coefficients in (6.1) are rational linear/quadratic data. The independently proved finite-product, dimension-count, and exponential-moment argument therefore gives a nonzero minimal boundary annihilator in the Andersen--Malusà convention: t_0=x/(2pi sqrt(h)), q=exp(2pi i b^2), Q=exp(-2pi b t_0), E:t_0 -> t_0-i b, E Q=q Q E. At a constrained saddle grad F_0=i xi p/2, equations (7.1) yield H_alpha=x, H_l=xi, Q=exp(-H_alpha), E=exp(H_l/2). Thus Q^(-1) and E^2 are the PSL(2) meridian and longitude eigenvalue ratios. Conversion to conventional SL(2) A-polynomial variables must also record the lift signs, including the possible negative longitude lift at completeness. The geometric peripheral factor thus divides its nonzero classical symbol by the uniform saddle argument already proved. A full explicit minimal-operator coefficient list and equality to the Jones AJ operator are not being asserted. Generic factors are retained before any Q=1 specialization. ## 8. Reproducibility and remaining uniform work Run the exact core with python3 experiments/reduce_singular_faces.py python3 experiments/certify_six_two.py and the separate standard-marking calibration with .venv/bin/python experiments/certify_six_two.py --topology The finite word scan python3 experiments/reduce_singular_faces.py --scan-length 7 checks 81 one-component folded R/L words. They all pass the two rank hypotheses, fixed-support angle test, rank-one longitude variation test, and rank B_ed=d-1. The rank hypotheses now have the uniform cohomological proof in the subsequent note. The additional finite angle tests remain evidence for the general boundary construction, rather than a proof of it. The scan also includes singular charts: the alternating word RLRLRLRL reduces from fourteen tetrahedral factors to ten integration variables. The exact algorithm and analytic theorem now handle the singularity which prevented the previous proper-chart approach. `check_singular_state_volume.py` additionally checks the correctly oriented classical saddle and evaluates the finite-b three-dimensional integral numerically. The recorded maximum classical gradient is below 7e-16. At b=0.24 and b=0.16, changing the quadrature order from 36 to 56 changes the normalized complex amplitude by approximately 5.7e-4 and 1.4e-4 respectively. These are coarse numerical diagnostics; the proof and all root/branch decisions use the exact certificates.

title: The actual six-crossing source: a proved triple reduction and the missing finite transform
text: # The actual six-crossing source: a proved triple reduction and the missing finite transform 28 October 2026. This note reduces the ORIGINAL six-crossing four-plat, with every turn and framing factor retained, to a three-index finite sum. The proof uses literal finite transfer elimination and the independently proved terminating three-factor q-Chu identity. It does not assume a colored-Jones formula. The attractive Rogers/Newton expansion in Section 4 remains **unproved**. It matches the direct finite tests and its classical characteristic is exactly the independently derived longitude quartic. Neither fact proves the finite transform. Accordingly this note supplies no verified actual quantum color operator for 6_1 and no new volume estimate. ## 1. The marked plat and its source Use the conventions of the [actual four-crossing proof](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md): Q is any primitive Nth root, d=N-1, x=-M/q, Q=q², Y=Qx²=M², and xvee=x^-1 Q^-1. The actual action order is sigma2, sigma1^-1, sigma1^-1, sigma1^-1, sigma2, sigma2. The braid word, with rightmost action first, is sigma2² sigma1^-3 sigma2. Its rational-tangle slope is T² U³ T (0,1)^t=(9,4)^t, T=[[1,1],[0,1]], U=[[1,0],[1,1]]. (1) This is the 9/4 handedness, mirror to the 9/5 convention in the [independent longitude calculation](six_one_classical_spectral_envelope_obstruction.md). We keep this handedness throughout the source calculation; mirroring replaces Q by Q^-1 in the final scalar. Top colors/orientations are (x,xvee,xvee,x), (+,-,-,+). Cut the fourth leg with the ORIGINAL left-trace coupon D0=g E00. As in the earlier proof, the input is (a,d-a,d,0), with coefficient N² x^(a-2d). (2) The oriented writhe is 2. With A=alpha, B=2d-alpha, the full mixed Cartan exponent minus the actual framing exponent is exactly dB: sum_crossings sign*alpha_i alpha_j/2 -2*(A²-2dA)/2 = dB. (3) Thus the retained common factor is xvee^d. The final colors are (xvee,x,xvee,x), so BOTH caps are ev_L. No ordinary quantum dimension is divided out and no turn is moved through a crossing. ## 2. Forced transfers give an actual four-index sum The surviving transfer list is (0,k,ell,r,a,0), 0<=a, k, a+k<=d, 0<=ell<=k, 0<=r<=d-a-k+ell. (4) Indeed the first transfer is zero because its second input is d. After the three negative crossings the state is (d-k+ell-r, a+k-ell+r, d-a, 0). If the fourth positive transfer is j<=a, the final second cap forces the last transfer j-a. Hence j=a and the last transfer is zero. The final state is (d-k+ell-r, k-ell+r, d, 0). The two cap factors multiply to x^(2d-k+ell-r)/N². This exponent is important; replacing it by x^d gives the wrong source. Write G_m=(Q/Y;Q)_m and let brackets denote Gaussian binomials. Direct multiplication of the literal mixed entries, (2), the two caps, and (3), followed only by reflection of [d choose a], gives F_N(Y)=sum_(4) W(a,k,ell,r), W=Y^(d-2a-k+r) Q^[1+a+2k(a+k+1)-ell(a+2k)+ell²] [a+k choose k] [d-k+ell choose ell] [a+k-ell+r choose r] (Q/Y)_k (Y Q^(-a-k))_ell (Q^(k-ell+1)/Y)_r (Y Q^(-a-k+ell-r))_a. (5) Here and below all Pochhammers have base Q. The root relation used to reduce integer exponents is d=-1 modulo N; no half-power root sign is discarded. All binomial factorial indices lie between 0 and d. ## 3. A proved three-index source The actual same period is F_N(Y)=sum_(m=0)^d sum_(b=0)^m sum_(r=0)^(d-b) Y^(m-b) Q^(b²) [m choose b] [d-b choose r] G_m (Q^(b+1)/Y)_r (Q^(-2b-m-r-1))_b. (6) Proof. In (5) put n=a+k, m=a+k-ell+r, b=n-ell. The new support is 0<=m,n<=d, 0<=a<=b<=min(m,n). Reflect [d-k+ell choose ell] and invert the two Y-positive Pochhammers. The four original Pochhammers combine to G_m (Q^(b-a+1)/Y)_(n-b) (Q^(b+1)/Y)_(n-b), with sign (-1)^a. The binomials become [n choose b][m choose b][b choose a]. The whole scalar is (-1)^a Y^(d+m-2b) Q^[1+n+b+2b²+a(a-3)/2-a(2b+m)]. (7) For fixed m,b,a, sum n=b+l. Set K=d-b, A=Q^(b-a+1)/Y and B=Q^(b+1)/Y. The n-dependent part is Q^b sum_(l=0)^K (Q^-K)_l(A)_l(B)_l Q^l/F_l =Q^b sum_(r=0)^K [K choose r] B^(K-r)A^r(B)_r. (8) This is the symmetric form of the terminating three-factor identity proved in [the five-crossing finite transform, Section 1](five_two_cyclotomic_transform_proof.md). It applies at every primitive root because K<N and every denominator F_l is nonzero. Now B^(K-r)A^r=B^K Q^(-ar). Combining B^K with (7) gives the factor Y^(m-b)Q^(b²), leaving the a-sum sum_(a=0)^b [b choose a] (-1)^a Q^[a(a-1)/2-a(2b+m+r+1)] =(Q^(-2b-m-r-1))_b. (9) The finite q-binomial theorem proves (9). This gives (6). All operations are identities of whole Laurent polynomials in Y, so fixed-root meridian jets and the original modified-dimension germ, if attached, are retained. No conclusion about moving-q normal jets is drawn from differentiation of this root identity. ## 4. The exact finite identity still required for the simple recurrence Put T_n(Y)=product_(j=1)^n(Y+Y^-1-Q^j-Q^-j), J_n(t)=sum_(j=0)^n t^(j(j+1)) [n choose j]_t. The candidate remaining identity is (6) ?= sum_(n=0)^d J_n(Q^-1) T_n(Y). (10) Equivalently J_n(Q^-1)=sum_j [n choose j]_Q Q^(-j(n+1)). The direct source tests agree, but (8)--(9) do not prove (10). No existing note supplies the additional extra-sigma1^-1 transform. There is a useful exact algebraic target if (10) is proved. The Rogers polynomials satisfy generically J_0=1, J_1=1+t², J_n=(1+t-t^n+t^(2n))J_(n-1) -t(1-t^(n-1))J_(n-2). (11) This recurrence has a separate elementary formal generating-series proof in [the multichannel note](actual_multichannel_newton_green_transport.md). For the MIRRORED candidate c_n=J_n(Q), its forward operator in u=Q^n, Ec_n=c_(n+1), Eu=QuE, is E²-[1+Q-Q²u+Q⁴u²]E+Q(1-Qu). (12) It is monic and has stable classical order. It is an exact operator on the stated Rogers sequence, but is NOT asserted here to be an actual 6_1 coefficient operator. If (10) is proved for all primitive roots and whole Y, ordinary-color pointing at infinitely many levels and Laurent polynomial rigidity promote these coefficients to the generic actual ordinary-color Newton sequence. This avoids assuming an off-root lift. At Q=1 the coefficient characteristic is 1-(2-u+u²)V+(1-u)V²=0, V=E^-1. Under the independently proved classical Newton map u=(YL+1)/(Y+L), V=Y+Y^-1-u-u^-1, its numerator is EXACTLY the normalized quartic (3) of the independent 9/5 longitude calculation, multiplied by Y^4; the denominator is Y²(Y+L)²(YL+1)². This is checked symbolically. The unmirrored version of (12) gives L reversed. This match is a useful consistency check and does not substitute for (10). Even after (10), a polynomial color-shift operator and its full inhomogeneous source must be obtained by the quantum Newton transform with denominators and unilateral endpoints retained. Generic noncommutative fraction-field conjugacy alone does not certify the classical leading coefficient of a particular cleared color operator. ## 5. Reproduction and precise output Run ```sh python3 experiments/audit_six_one_actual_source_recurrence_port.py ``` The audit constructs the literal six original mixed crossings and every source factor independently of (5), checks the route identity (5), the finite intermediate (7), and (6). It labels (10) as unproved and tests it separately. It also verifies the generic Rogers recurrence and the exact classical quartic transform. The uniform proofs of (5)--(9) are the finite calculations above; the tests are diagnostics rather than an all-N proof of (10). The usable new result is the actual three-index source (6). The specific remaining source identity is (10). A general classical-order theorem, a verified actual 6_1 quantum color operator, phase-aware product asymptotics, and a broad selected geometric coefficient are still open.

title: A modulus-only switch on the independently derived 6_1 longitude curve
text: # A modulus-only switch on the independently derived 6_1 longitude curve 28 October 2026. This note tests the remaining classical inequality in [the macroscopic actual-source spectral upper bound](actual_macroscopic_a_spectral_upper_bound.md). It proves that the largest-modulus longitude root switches between two distinct analytic branches already on the 6_1 two-bridge curve. The switch is exact and transverse. Consequently, a theorem that simply identifies the pointwise largest-modulus root with one distinguished geometric branch cannot hold for this curve. This does **not** invalidate the spectral upper bound, which makes no such identification. An actual all-level quantum annihilator with this classical companion has not been verified here. The integral values below are labelled numerical diagnostics; no rigorous volume calibration or general sharp upper bound is claimed. ## 1. The curve from the two meridians, without a polynomial table Use the p=9,q=5 two-bridge presentation, with alternating exponents `(+,-,-,+,+,-,-,+)`, and matrices \[ A=\begin{pmatrix}M&1\\0&M^{-1}\end{pmatrix},\qquad B=\begin{pmatrix}M&0\\-z&M^{-1}\end{pmatrix},\quad W=(AB^{-1}A^{-1}B)^2. \] The relation is \(WA=BW\).
