The actual density theorem fixes the weight-zero ratio c_beta after the original cut-density factors have been combined. It does not identify a separately normalized transverse Gaussian with K_Y^(1/2) alone. These line statements retain the original square-root phases and do not equate ordinary coherent clutch with quantum dressing. The coherent vector line is the dual O(-(N-1)); its coefficient wave line is O(N-1). Their distinction avoids a sign ambiguity in the table. Pairing the actual source and co-source and retaining the incidence denominator gives the globally defined compact kernel, whose normalized trace period is already exact. There is a useful representation-theoretic check of the boundary weight. On the SL2 sign cover, (3.3) lifts as eta^(-1/2)g, so for n=N-1, Sym^n(g_SL2)=eta^(-n/2)Sym^n(g). (5.2) Its leading coefficient is the rank-one coherent operator of the two boundary flags. At v=a=0 the eigenvalues are eta^(1/2), eta^(-1/2), and the powers are eta^((n-2j)/2). This yields precisely the source normal pole and torus weight in the table. For odd n the single source requires its SL2 sign mark; the End kernel and paired compact period descend to PGL2 for every N. Equation (5.2) is the standard polynomial coherent-line clutch. It is not proved here to be the actual unrestricted quantum-group dressing of a physical Gauss frame. Ordinary SL2 Möbius action on coherent coordinates and the actual quantum dressing are different constructions until a source-preserving network map has been supplied. The exact actual result in this note is (4.6), which uses the independently checked physical diagonal gauge and principal Gaussian density, not this unproved identification. ## 6. Physical-symbol and residue sections remain separately marked The compact source also has the physical map of Section 1. Under the actual bridge coordinates it is reached by the logarithmic centralizer section r_*(A)=1-Log A/(2pi*i), a=p(1-r_*)=p Log A/(2pi*i). (6.1) The mark at the north pole is r_*=1 and that at the south pole is r_*=0. A logarithm deck shift changes r_* by -1 and its old frame coordinate b=(1-r)/s by +1/s; the relative comparison coordinate (r_*-r)/s has the opposite jump. Thus the global source needs the logarithmic transition, not a single split B1 section. The r,s,p note retains its boundary primitive and sign. The associated boundary coordinate T=va=1-r and the physical symbol coordinate Log A/(2pi*i) agree on the marked section (6.1). They are not identical functions on the full three-dimensional framing family. In particular taking an arbitrary framing section or identifying the old two B1 coordinates with the two compact leaf coordinates would change the comparison. More precisely the physical section is the graph eta=(1-exp(-2pi*i va))/v inside Y; eta on Y is otherwise independent. This graph meets E_exc at the analytic identity locus, not along all of X. For finite v!=0 that locus has va in Z; at v=0 its removable condition is a=0. On the real compact sphere only the two poles occur. Therefore the nonzero residue class on E_exc is not yet the image of the actual physical compact-cycle pairing. A relative cycle or source-chain comparison is still necessary. Equivariant descent supplies the global principal class (4.6) and fixes its line weights. It does not fix the scalar of a whole actual quantum source or ensure that unrestricted logarithmic Green transgressions preserve that class. The remaining operation is a marked relative pushforward with the actual source, caps, Weyl transitions and normal jets retained, rather than another choice of a local geometric optimum. The [exact universal audit](../experiments/audit_springer_centralizer_boundary_source.py) checks the matrix transitions, compact flag and form maps, actual Gaussian adapter, normal weights and coherent rank-one boundary. The [independent resolved-boundary audit](resolved_framing_boundary_independent_audit.md) also verifies the centralizer nonextension, matrix compactification, line bundles and principal Gaussian residue with the physical-cycle and quantum-dressing qualifications retained. The [independent global boundary audit](resolved_framing_boundary_independent_audit.md) checks the torsor obstruction, compactification, exact Haar adapter and marked principal residue, including its selected-cycle limitation.

title: The actual pointed fusion map in the literature charged matrix frames
text: # The actual pointed fusion map in the literature charged matrix frames Research note, 26 October 2026. This gives an exact local comparison between the pointed cyclic fusion map used in the actual source construction and the literature basic/charged matrix dilogarithm. It retains four face frames, the input permutation, the scalar fixed by the selected unit, and the full integer-charge multiplier. At the nilpotent source the same identity gives a regular standard kernel on the normal chart. The fractional face powers combine to the integer carry pole. The normal kernel shape is a ratio of normal directions; for recoupling it is their ordinary projective cross-ratio. These are algebraic evaluations at fixed N, not a volume limit. The definitions compared below are the displayed definitions in [Baseilhac--Benedetti, Section 2.1.2, equations (3) and the following kernel](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0306283v2#S2.SS1.SSS2). Only definitions and scope are used from that source. Its proofs of symmetrization, tetrahedral invariance and global state identification are not premises. This note proves local identities directly. It does not repair the failed full vertex-order test merely by naming the charged tensor, construct the required global charged source, or prove the volume conjecture. ## 1. Definitions and compatible roots Let N=2m+1>=3, r=m+1, Q=exp(2pi*i/N), so 2r=1 modulo N. The odd-level restriction is part of the literature definition being compared. Section 9 computes the same existing fusion map at even levels without claiming that this source defines an even charged tensor. For u^N+v^N=1, with uv!=0, put Omega(u,v|n)=product_(j=1)^n v/(1-uQ^j). It extends periodically to every integer n. Let g_N(u)=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-uQ^(-j))^j, h(u)^N=g_N(u)/g_N(1). (1.1) Here h is the literature g(u)/g(1), with its compatible Nth roots retained; g_N is its unambiguous Nth-power product. The basic kernel without that scalar and the published normalized kernel are L0(u,v)_(k,l)^(i,j) =Q^(kj+r k^2) Omega(u,v|i-k) delta_(i+j,l), L(u,v)=h(u)L0(u,v). (1.2) All indices are modulo N. In this note (i,j) are output indices and (k,l) are input indices, in precisely the displayed order. For the pointed fusion C_(s,t) choose nonzero compatible roots alpha^N=s, beta^N=t, eta=alpha beta, a_s^N=1-s, a_t^N=1-t, a_st^N=1-st, gamma=a_st/a_t, v=a_s/a_st, u=alpha/gamma. (1.3) Assume s,t,1-s,1-t,1-st are nonzero. Then tau=gamma^N=(1-st)/(1-t), u^N=s/tau, v^N=(1-s)/(1-st), u^N+v^N=1. The relations a_st=gamma a_t and a_s=gamma v a_t are part of the marked cover. Arbitrarily independent roots would miss their face factors. The shape in (1.2) is w_0=u^N=s/tau. It is the reciprocal of the cross-ratio label tau/s used by the earlier recoupling note. The corresponding orientation and index conventions must be retained in a regulator comparison. ## 2. Exact four-face factorization For a variable z and norm root a, write phi_(z,a)(j)=(Qz;Q)_j/a^j, Phi_s=diag phi_(alpha,a_s), Phi_t=diag phi_(beta,a_t), Phi_st=diag phi_(eta,a_st). These are the existing pointed cyclic-factorial frames. Define the other input-face frame and the quadratic phase by D_tau(k)=(beta v)^k / product_(j=1)^k(1-gamma^(-1)Q^(-j)), Gamma_N(k)=Q^(-r k^2). (2.1) They are periodic: (beta v)^N=1-gamma^(-N). Each denominator is nonzero on the stated chart. Let P exchange the total and relative input factors. In evaluation bases at the marked roots, the exact pointed fusion identity is C_eval=kappa (Phi_s tensor Phi_t) L0(u,v) (D_tau Gamma_N tensor Phi_st^(-1))P, kappa=(1/N)sum_(b=0)^(N-1) gamma^(-b)(Q eta;Q)_b/(Q beta;Q)_b. (2.2) Thus the comparison with the normalized literature L has scalar kappa/h(u), not an unspecified proportionality. It is fixed by the original pointed fusion map. The Gaussian and input flip in (2.2) are essential. Each remaining matrix is a function on a single face with its specified norm root; no new local quantum function has been introduced. Here is a direct proof. The known pointed polynomial kernel is C_(s,t)(U^a V^b) =w^a (Qw;Q)_b/(Qz;Q)_b, w=x_1x_2, z=x_2. Passing to evaluation bases gives delta_(l,i+j) times f_k(i,j)=(1/N)sum_b gamma^(-b)Q^(-kb) (Q alpha beta Q^(i+j);Q)_b/(Q beta Q^j;Q)_b. (2.3) Set x=alpha Q^i, z=beta Q^j. The finite-product recurrence in b and its cyclic closure give f_k/f_(k-1)=z (gamma Q^k-Qx)/(gamma Q^k-1). (2.4) Every numerator and denominator here is a unit on the chart. Divide f_k by D_tau(k)Q^(jk)Omega(u,v|i-k). Equation (2.4) makes the result independent of k. The relative Y-intertwining equation next gives the row ratio B_(i-1,j+1)/B_(i,j) =gamma v (1-beta Q^(j+1))/(1-alpha Q^i). Consequently B_(i,j)=phi_s(i)phi_t(j)A_(i+j). The total Y-intertwining equation reduces to A_l/A_(l-1)=gamma a_t/(1-eta Q^l). It follows that A_l=kappa/phi_st(l). The value at i=j=k=0 is exactly the finite sum in (2.2). The chirp in (2.1) cancels the k^2 phase in (1.2), proving the formula entry by entry. Invertibility of the pointed fusion and its face frames proves kappa!=0; if its value were zero the same recurrences would make the whole matrix zero. ## 3. The published normalization has determinant one: a rigidity proof First L0 is invertible directly. At fixed l its block is a pair of diagonal matrices times the circulant with entries H_n=Q^(r n^2)Omega(u,v|n). For its finite Fourier coefficients Hhat_a, the defining recurrence gives Hhat_a=(u+vQ^(1-r-a))Hhat_(a-1). (3.1) The multipliers are nonzero, and their product is u^N+v^N=1. If one Fourier coefficient vanished they would all vanish, contradicting H_0=1. This proves invertibility at composite levels as well. The exact root translations of L0, proved in Section 5, imply that Delta(u,v)=det L0(u,v) [g_N(u)/g_N(1)]^N is invariant under independent u->Qu and v->Qv. The clock and shift determinants are one at odd N. Thus Delta belongs to C(z), z=u^N, the invariant field of the Fermat cover. It is a regular unit away from z=0,1,infinity. It is therefore of the form constant*z^a*(1-z)^b for integers a,b. At u=0,v=1 the Gaussian circulant remains invertible, so a=0. At u=1,v=0, Omega(n)=0 for 1<=n<N and Omega(0)=1. The kernel is the permutation (k,l)->(k,l-k) with coefficient Q^(kl+(r-1)k^2). Its determinant is one: the permutation sign is one at odd N and the sum of those exponents is divisible by N. Also h(1)=1. This gives b=0 and the constant one. Hence exactly det L(u,v)=1. (3.2) This proves the normalization by an explicit invariant-unit argument and boundary evaluation, rather than a borrowed matrix-dilogarithm theorem. ## 4. The remaining scalar is a specified normalization torsor Put S=N(N-1)/2=Nm, and let F_s,F_t,F_st,F_D be the products of the diagonal entries of Phi_s,Phi_t,Phi_st,D_tau. The already proved polynomial fusion determinant and the two Vandermonde changes give det C_eval=[t/(1-t)]^S. For example the Vandermonde ratio is gamma^(-NS), which converts the polynomial-basis determinant to this expression. The input flip has determinant (-1)^m. The chirp determinant raised to N is one, including when 3 divides N. Equation (3.2) therefore gives the exact scalar norm (kappa/h(u))^(N^2) =(-1)^m [t/(1-t)]^(Nm) [F_st/(F_s F_t F_D)]^N. (4.1) The source value (2.2) and the chosen branch of h fix its remaining phase. Equation (4.1) is not permission to discard the scalar or choose independent roots at different moves. It makes its modulus and normalization line explicit from the four face factors. For compatible roots with bounded fixed logarithms of s,t, 1-s,1-t,1-st as N varies, (4.1) also gives log|kappa/h(u)|=O(log N). (4.2) Indeed a cyclic-factorial product has log-modulus log|F_s|=N log|(1-s)/(1-alpha)| -N log|D_N(alpha)|-m log|1-s|, where D_N(alpha)=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-alpha Q^j)^(j/N). The fixed-log root bound proved in [the triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md#4-keep-central-and-semiclassical-shapes-distinct) is log|D_N(exp(w/N))|=O(log N). It gives O(N log N) for each F; the inverse-Q input frame obeys the same estimate. Substitution in (4.1) proves (4.2), with upper and lower polynomial bounds. This concerns these marked trajectories. It does not bound an arbitrary moving root frame or the selected contraction of the knot state. ## 5. Charges act through the finite Heisenberg torsor Let Z e_j=Q^j e_j and S e_j=e_(j+1). Finite-product cancellation gives, for every a,b modulo N, Omega(uQ^a,vQ^b|n) =Q^(bn)Omega(u,v|n+a)/Omega(u,v|a). Substitution in (1.2) proves the full operator identity Omega(u,v|a)L0(uQ^a,vQ^b) =(Z^b S^(-a) tensor S^a)L0(u,v) (Z^(a-b) tensor I). (5.1) No scalar is suppressed. The scalar normalization obeys g_N(uQ^a)/g_N(u)=Omega(u,v|a)^N. Thus on the compatible cover h_a=Omega(u,v|a)h_0, (5.1) is the corresponding identity for normalized L. Other normalization-root lifts retain their finite phase. For the matrix operation W_(a,b) on the right of (5.1), W_(c,d) W_(a,b)=Q^(bc)W_(a+c,b+d). (5.2) This follows from S^(-c)Z^b=Q^(bc)Z^b S^(-c). In particular the two root generators have central commutator Q. The root transport is the finite Heisenberg extension, with its central root retained, rather than an unmarked pair of roots. Its Weyl matrices are unitary for complex Q on the unit circle. To apply the literature charged definition, let w_0=z, w_1=(1-z)^(-1), w_2=1-z^(-1). For a chosen log branch and flattening f, its root formula is w_j'=exp[(Log w_j+(f_j-epsilon c_j)(N+1)pi*i)/N], c_0+c_1+c_2=1, epsilon=+/-1. Relative to the unshifted roots of w_0 and w_1^(-1), put a=r(f_0-epsilon c_0), b=-r(f_1-epsilon c_1), u_c=uQ^a, v_c=vQ^b. The published charged tensor is exactly R_(epsilon,c)=sigma_(epsilon,c)L(u_c,v_c)^epsilon, sigma_(epsilon,c)=u_c^(-m c_1)v_c^(-m c_0). (5.3) Equation (5.1) expresses this definition in the original matrix frame by explicit four-leg Weyl operators. For a negative tensor their order and inverses are reversed; the prefactor in (5.3) is still retained as printed. No published symmetry proof is assumed in this calculation. The integral charges must not be reduced modulo N in the prefactor. A lift (c_0,c_1)->(c_0+N b_0,c_1+N b_1), with c_2 adjusted, leaves u_c,v_c unchanged but multiplies the full tensor by z^(-m b_1)(1-z)^(-m b_0). (5.4) These are central functions, not generally phases. For fixed integer charges and fixed z the exact modulus is log|sigma_c|=-m/N [c_1 log|z|+c_0 log|1-z|]. (5.5) It is bounded across N under that qualification. The Weyl root shifts preserve the local normalized kernel's singular values; (5.5) supplies its remaining scalar norm. This operator statement supplies no lower bound for an arbitrary selected global contraction. ## 6. The selected source is explicit in the standard frames The pointed fusion sends the product unit to the product unit. In evaluation coordinates these are constant vectors. Equation (2.2) consequently says L0(u,v)p_standard =kappa^(-1)(Phi_s tensor Phi_t)^(-1)1, p_standard=(D_tau Gamma_N tensor Phi_st^(-1))1. (6.1) The flip fixes that constant input. In general p_standard is not the constant vector. This gives the selected source in the standard matrix definition, rather than identifying two unpointed kernels and resetting their boundary vectors. For a positive charged tensor (5.3), substituting (5.1) in (2.2) gives the original map with four transported leg frames and scalar kappa/[h(u)sigma_c]. For the inverse original map the corresponding scalar is h(u)/[kappa sigma_c], with the inverted leg order. These formulas retain the complete peripheral functions before specialization. Any already specified finite recoupled actual network can make this substitution with its full source, covectors, caps and scalar lines. Its period is then unchanged exactly. This is a local equivalence with the literature definition. It is not a proof that the independently prescribed face pairings, charges and selected vector of a global geometric state are the transformed ones in (6.1). ## 7. The normal chart gives a nondegenerate standard tetrahedron At fixed N take alpha=1-epsilon a, beta=1-epsilon b, a b(a+b)!=0, s=alpha^N, t=beta^N. Algebraic evaluation of the ratios at epsilon=0 gives gamma^N=(a+b)/b, u^N=b/(a+b), v^N=a/(a+b), kappa_0=(1-u^N)/(N(1-u)). (7.1) The last formula is the finite geometric sum obtained from (2.2), since its Pochhammer quotient becomes one. All these standard kernel parameters are nondegenerate, and kappa_0 is nonzero. This is an evaluation on the normal chart, not an N->infinity calculation. The singular face roots in (2.2) recombine integrally. On its support l=i+j modulo N put kappa_carry=floor((i+j)/N). Writing p_i(alpha)=(Qalpha;Q)_i, exactly phi_s(i)phi_t(j)/phi_st(l) =[p_i(alpha)p_j(beta)/p_l(eta)] gamma^(l-i)v^(-i)(1-t)^(-kappa_carry). (7.2) Use a_st=gamma a_t, a_s=gamma v a_t and a_t^N=1-t to prove (7.2). Thus the fractional powers cancel to the integer carry. Every other displayed kernel factor is a unit at the normal point. Multiplying row (i,j) by (1-t)^kappa_carry gives a regular source frame. Its determinant is exactly t^(N(N-1)/2), hence one at t=1. Its actual normal matrix, for l=i+j modulo N, is C0_(ij,lk)=kappa_0 [(Q;Q)_i(Q;Q)_j/(Q;Q)_l] gamma^(l-i)v^(-i)D_tau(k)Q^(jk) Omega(u,v|i-k). (7.3) There are N(N-1)/2 carry-one rows. They are the retained relative source directions of the two-lattice construction; evaluating only an ordinary unscaled image loses them. The independent valuation calculation in the audit checks (7.3) directly from the original finite-product Fourier sum, as well as its determinant and unit pointing. For three normal leaf directions a,b,c the standard recoupling shape is z_normal=(a+b+c)b/[(a+b)(b+c)]. (7.4) It is the cross-ratio in the literature convention of the four cumulative normal flags 0,a,a+b,a+b+c. This follows by substituting the first-order products in s/tau for the two recoupling trees. It explains how geometric flag coordinates can occur on the exceptional source chart even though the leaf central parameters coalesce. A global geometric developing configuration must still be matched to the actual equivariant source, its gluing and its marked cut. Arbitrary local normal ratios do not establish that comparison. In particular (7.4) does not turn a reducible root-central character into the complete hyperbolic one or prove the selected regulator norm. ## 8. Verification and scope [The independent audit](../experiments/audit_standard_matrix_dilog_comparison.py) compares the torus-defined fusion matrix and its evaluated four-face expression at N=2,3,...,12,15. At the six odd levels it is the literal literature kernel. All four frame factors, the flip, chirp, nonzero kappa, selected source and determinant norm agree. It checks 874 root translations, 108 odd-level positive/negative charged definitions, their full integer-charge lifts, the Heisenberg commutator and the compatible cyclic-g normalization. All twelve normal source frames also match the independent leading-valuation calculation with their exact determinant phases. All checks pass. [Results](../experiments/standard_matrix_dilog_comparison_results.json). python3 experiments/audit_standard_matrix_dilog_comparison.py The uniform proofs are finite products, intertwinings, Fourier recurrences and invariant-unit rigidity. Their coverage overlaps existing cyclic 6j and charged matrix dilogarithm theory; no novelty is claimed. The new role in these notes is the explicit actual source, full scalar and normal lattice in the published tensor coordinates. The failed bare vertex-order prescription still needs a global source-compatible charged replacement. Equality of the selected knot period with the marked Bloch-regulator period and its all-level norm remain unproved. ## 9. The same existing fusion map at even levels There is an all-level algebraic expression, without dividing by two modulo an even N. Put q=exp(pi*i/N), lambda_0=-q. Then lambda_0^2=Q, lambda_0^N=(-1)^(N-1), Gamma_N(k)=lambda_0^(-k^2). The quadratic phase is periodic in k modulo N. Replace Q^(r k^2) in L0 by lambda_0^(k^2), and the input chirp by this Gamma_N. Equations (2.2), (2.3)--(2.4), (5.1)--(5.2) and the full normal-source calculation then hold at every N. They are exact matrices of the already defined pointed quantum-group fusion, rather than a separately chosen invariant. At odd N, lambda_0=Q^r, so the expression is exactly the literature kernel already compared. The Gaussian Fourier recurrence is now Hhat_a=(u+v lambda_0^(-1)Q^(1-a))Hhat_(a-1). Its product is one because lambda_0^N=(-1)^(N-1), proving invertibility at all levels. The same invariant-unit proof gives the exact determinant det L^(lambda_0)=delta_N, delta_N=1 for odd N, delta_N=(-1)^(N/2) for even N. (9.1) For completeness, the clock and shift determinant signs cancel in their N-dimensional tensor extensions. At u=1,v=0 the remaining boundary permutation and phase have determinant Q^(S^2), S=N(N-1)/2, which is exactly delta_N. This proves (9.1) without dropping the even-level sign. The evaluated fusion and the normal carry frame similarly have det C_eval=delta_N[t/(1-t)]^S, det C_normal=delta_N at the source. (9.2) In the scalar norm formula (4.1), replace (-1)^m by chi_N, where chi_N=(-1)^((N-1)/2) for odd N and chi_N=1 for even N. The input flip and the chirp's tensor determinant cancel at even N. All the phase factors are thus accounted for in the existing source map. The charge prescription (5.3) was read from an odd-level definition and is not asserted at even N by this observation. In particular its flattening/charge parity cannot be extended by silently treating one half modulo an even level. The all-level source expression is available for the required comparison, while the global charged construction and its selected regulator norm still require proof. The subsequent [shared face proof](shared_standard_face_gluing.md) now makes the four-face expression compatible on one affine flag chart. Its frame depends only on the ordered triangle and shared edge roots. Actual face pairings and corrected cyclic maps become fixed Gaussian matrices with retained scalar functions; the full ordered kernel includes an explicit orientation clock/shift and pointing factor. This establishes local gluing data for a specified network, while its equivariant global charges, actual source/cut and selected regulator norm still require comparison.

title: What the present notes add, and what they do not
text: # What the present notes add, and what they do not Research comparison, 26 October 2026. The user's requested direction is to identify the intrinsic period torsor and prove a uniform structural statement. Individual knot certificates are validation, not the main mechanism. This comparison distinguishes independent verification from a new mathematical construction; no novelty claim is made. **Latest target clarification.** The intended route proves Kashaev's volume growth through the quantum A-module or torsor attached to the actual invariant. The classical A-polynomial should emerge as its appropriate geometric support, with source and peripheral factors retained. Relating it to Jones is separate. The comparison with the previous work in this repo is in [the primary status, Section 0](a_polynomial_torsor_status.md#0-comparison-with-the-previous-work-in-this-repo). The auxiliary [direct classical A-period construction](a_polynomial_volume_limits.md) now supplies such a marked-root limit under a connectedness criterion, independently verified for the hyperbolic twist family. Its finite samples are not canonical; it is not presented as a standard quantum A-state or a new classical regulator theorem. Coverage for exact polynomials and volume functions includes [Guilloux--Marche, 1804.01395](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01395). The integer-norm construction, rounding estimate, cover product law and twist-curve algebra are independently proved in the note. The later [doubled-phase proof](doubled_phase_rivin_optimizer.md) works directly with the normalized geometric and conjugate places. It makes the unique constrained Rivin optimizer algebraic in its two multiplicative boundary phases and writes its marked volume potential as the central period of one fixed two-step Heisenberg connection. This is a refinement of the repo's earlier meridian etaleness and boundary Monge--Ampere calculation. It is not a new claim that classical volume potentials exist, and no Ronkin, Harnack or dimer equivalence is inferred. All formulas are derived in the note without using the coverage papers' proofs. The [critical-source trace theorem](irreducible_critical_source_and_whole_norm.md) adds a finite nonvanishing criterion through irreducible descent and exact source moments. It also proves polynomial norm bounds for a fixed whole algebraic density along the actual root-source arc. The [whole unit/level-weight theorem](whole_torsor_unit_weights_and_irregular_type.md) separately records why finite type of a connection does not bound its amplified horizontal periods. These are elementary trace and function estimates, not claims that the actual quantum source has already descended to the geometric critical field. The subsequent source work now gives actual maps: [centralizer normal moments and endpoints](centralizer_normal_residue_and_actual_cut_moments.md), an [exact dual whole clock](dual_clock_normal_cut_source.md), and a [degree-N divided source in an actual high integral color](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md). Quantum Frobenius and Steinberg tensor-product constructions are established representation theory; the high-color note uses their standard integral divided-power definitions and proves every needed coefficient and even/odd sign directly. Its specific role here is the literal wall row, first-normal block arrows, original knot-period adapter and source germ. The whole-clock proof similarly derives its dual Toeplitz polynomial and affine normal clutch explicitly. No general quantum source/geometry equivalence is inferred from these maps; the inserted-network and Gaussian naturality remain the parts to prove. The [intrinsic diagonal wall-source theorem](cyclotomic_diagonal_wall_current_source.md) subsequently constructs its finite Fourier constraint, exact endpoint-completed ladder and regular whole-source gauge. The [first-normal crossing theorem](high_color_first_normal_r_and_frobenius_degree.md) supplies the universal resonant factor and quadratic divided degree, with a general braid-word extension. These are actual matrix/source identities, not a proposed positive replacement state. The [memory-clock refinement](actual_memory_clock_and_normal_transfer.md) retains first-normal block carries while explicitly reducing its root clock identity to the earlier position-clock factorization. The clock-dependent source gauge retains whole dilations; no bounded differential degree after that gauge or geometric Gaussian/current equivalence is inferred. The later [all-normal filtration proof](high_color_all_normal_frobenius_filtration.md) extends the actual matrix bound to every finite order: normal depth j uses degree at most 2j and at most 2j+1 rotated source descendants. The [unprojectivized actual source](actual_unprojectivized_frobenius_borel_torsor.md) then uses the earlier standard Borel formulas on a marked actual Sym^N source/dual cover. Its additional content is the retained weight-N scale, its literal old-clock normal detector, and the framing two-form recovered from scale plus an actual descendant. It is not a novelty claim for Borel groups, pure-power cones or Kummer covers. The network Gaussian/current intertwiner remains to be constructed. The original-Kashaev torsor work remains the main construction. The later AK meridian state studied in several notes is another comparison object. The claimed AK results here do not prove the original conjecture without a comparison of its distinguished period. The subsequent [coverage audit](hyperbolic_class_coverage.md) records current statements. The user also separately authorized a proof audit of Ge's geometric existence argument; its core is now checked in [the geometric audit](ge_geometric_triangulation_audit.md). The principal direction remains an intrinsic A-module/period-torsor construction. The subsequent [intrinsic norm-torsor note](intrinsic_quantum_a_norm_torsor.md) constructs that module-comparison line directly from root-of-unity monodromy, proves its cyclic norm equation, and extends it by a finite cyclic lattice sum. This is standard semilinear descent proved explicitly, not a claim that the selected Kashaev period has now been identified. Subsequently, the [crossing proof](kashaev_crossing_and_period_lattice.md) independently verifies the known enhanced Kashaev/quantum-group comparison at every level. The [ADO pointing proof](kashaev_ado_pointing.md) identifies its actual meridian normalization line, including the peripheral factor and regular specialization. This supplies a literature pointing; it does not yet identify its norm with the geometric regulator. In particular, root-level central support and the classical geometric A-curve must be distinguished. The [regular cyclic/Steinberg calculation](cyclic_steinberg_lattice.md) subsequently identifies an all-level regular quantum-group family, the nilpotent Kashaev vacuum, matched endpoint rescalings for the actual Borel coproduct, and the two-step recoupling lattice at simultaneous degeneration. The [normalization tower](cyclotomic_normalization_tower.md) proves all-level distribution, a local Kummer certificate, and a local regulator estimate without a Habiro-ring theorem. This is independent verification of local representation and finite-product identities, not a new global quantum invariant or a knot volume theorem. The [Casimir comparison](casimir_braiding_and_recoupling_lattice.md) subsequently proves that the product-coordinate injection intertwines E as well as the Borel action. It derives the actual crossing as a confluent Casimir polynomial, with its inverse and writhe phase, and matches it on the integral recoupling lattice. The pivotal closing trace is an explicit spectral-jet functional. The relative spectral algebra is nonreduced: its units and normalization torsor retain nilpotent jets. A finite logarithmic Hilbert-90 argument extends descent to that Artin base. These are independent local calculations within existing projective braid theory, not a new volume theorem. Following the user's return to the A-polynomial direction, the [formal A-curve construction](formal_a_curve_period_torsor.md) now derives a branch of the specified operator by noncommutative Hensel lifting, its gauge-covariant period differential, and its leading regulator action with peripheral conversions explicit. Formal q-difference solutions already occur in Garoufalidis--Geronimo; their analytic theorems are not used. The ordinary-double-point calculation retains the colliding pair as a regular rank-two formal connection. The [central normalization theorem](algebraic_central_normalization.md) also proves polynomial bounds for whole-germ values from a fixed finite algebraic central presentation. These are algebraic formal and normalization results, not an identification of the actual Kashaev period or a new knot-family volume theorem. The [root-orbit pointing calculation](root_orbit_pointing.md) subsequently proves the nonzero anchor F_N(-q)=1 and the fixed integer-color specializations by a filtered cut-trace argument. These specializations overlap existing ADO/Jones unification coverage; no completion theorem is adopted. It then derives an operator-only cofactor expression on a one-dimensional rational solution line, using the saturated generic kernel and its actual reference pointing. The full-state formula retains the central residue and first meridian jet. This removes an unfixed central scalar at the Kashaev fiber once the common line is known; it does not prove the geometric identification or a volume growth theorem. The [all-level A-period theorem](all_level_a_period.md) now gives a rank-independent exact presentation from any specified actual annihilator and finitely many fixed small colors. The ADO-to-trace recursion inclusion is already stated in Brown--Dimofte--Garoufalidis--Geer; it is reconstructed here from the independently proved color identity and infinitely many polynomial zeroes. Sparse-polynomial multiplicity bounds control the whole-q-germ jet order uniformly. The [meridian version](bounded_meridian_jets.md) derives the Smith bound by elementary degree counting and integral companion propagation. These overlap existing q-difference desingularization theory; no novelty or volume theorem is inferred. They remove the earlier rank/regularity restriction from exact period recovery, while geometric growth still needs proof. The subsequent [finite cut-state argument](finite_sum_annihilator.md) independently supplies the missing nonzero actual all-level meridian annihilator for every knot. It proves the needed proper-product shift bound on boundary strata as well as in the interior, repairs zero direct summation by finite moments, and strips a common central operator factor before q^N=-1. This reconstructs existing recursion coverage; it is not a new invariant or a general classical-symbol theorem. The [affine source construction](affine_quantum_a_period.md) now uses the literature inhomogeneous A-equation, retaining its source as an extension class modulo sigma-C. Cyclic affine averaging and the nonresonant resolvent are direct linear descent. Normalized trace proves that a finite stable algebraic cover cannot kill this class. These are standard affine difference-module constructions, not a newly defined quantum knot invariant. The [adequacy proof](adequacy_and_algebraic_periods.md) reconstructs the known quadratic degree span by extreme states, cabling and Chebyshev threading. A valuation argument excludes a fixed algebraic meridian trace. With the stated actual-source and either cyclotomic or formal nonresonance test this forces nonsplitting, including for the proposed adequate knot class. Polynomiality of perturbative color coefficients is reconstructed from the one-cycle cut trace, without using stronger MMR results. None of this identifies the source class or its norm with the marked regulator. The two equal spectral-radius lobes of the classical figure-eight curve show why a maximum-eigenvalue norm calculation would not supply that identification. The [triangulation bridge](triangulation_regulator_bridge.md) places the positive geometric triangulation theorem at this comparison step. It gives the marked Bloch lift and geometric gluing branch; the local root-binomial calculation gives exact central support. The actual relative source and selected period must still be identified. The proof distinguishes fixed semiclassical shapes from fixed root centers, including an explicit polynomial bound for the local cyclic normalization in the latter regime. The QHI link and geometric-character patterns are kept distinct by their definitions; no unaudited comparison theorem is imported. The [actual relative octahedral calculation](relative_octahedral_period.md) subsequently factors both actual crossings into five quantum dilogarithm atoms and proves their octahedral cross-ratio and face identities. This overlaps the existing octahedral-potential coverage of Cho and universal-invariant/colored-triangulation coverage of Suzuki; neither is used as a proof premise. The calculation also derives the finite factorial's polynomial boundary source, its invertible cyclic resolvent, and the exact missing transition 1/S_N(M^2) in the full ADO dimension. This concretely supplies local relative data for the proposed comparison. The local octahedral growth bound overlaps Garoufalidis--Le and is not a volume-conjecture theorem. Internal-index descent still needs a global comparison with the meridian source and marked regulator. The [marked braid holonomy calculation](marked_braid_holonomy.md) now supplies the actual-state classical critical correspondence. Its factorial basis change transports the boundary vector and changes crossing symbols by a cancelling boundary coboundary. An explicit rank-one E-wall and cyclic central defect recover the entire modified dimension. The derived crossing map is conjugate to meridian Hurwitz action, so the global critical scheme has nondegenerate charts through every hyperbolic representation. Its residual Borel framing torsor is split, and a direct wedge calculation gives a frame-independent complete regulator for the crossing sum. Holonomy braidings already occur in Kashaev--Reshetikhin; representation-associated critical solutions are covered by Cho. These are independently reconstructed with the actual source conventions, with no novelty claim. Survival of the geometric branch under quantum elimination and its contribution to the actual period are still unproved. The [crossing fundamental-cycle calculation](crossing_fundamental_cycle.md) now identifies the complete rational crossing Bloch sum with the marked idealized fundamental class. It reconstructs the classical shadow-volume coverage of Inoue--Kabaya and Cho in the fixed actual ADO conventions, with an explicit three-five-term certificate, four-tetrahedron face pairing, orientation, and peripheral degree. The generic meridian defect is retained. This closes the complete classical regulator comparison in these notes, with no novelty claim or imported proof. It does not prove quantum source transport, integral flattenings, a minimal-operator classical factor, or the original selected volume limit. The [exact longitude/action proof](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md) continues this comparison within the same finite state. It proves the meridian-shift insertion, its preferred-longitude marking including the inverse cut flag, and the calibrated regulator norm of a compatible logarithmic action. Classical potential/longitude derivatives already have coverage in [Sawabe, arbitrary-color potential functions](https://msp.org/pjm/2023/322-1/pjm-v322-n1-p08-p.pdf). No proof from that source is used. The integer-position cancellation, finite pole cancellation, and discrete-character lift specify precisely which exact state and logarithmic action these calculations use. They do not show that the geometric action contributes to the selected sum. The [squared-meridian descent](even_meridian_norm_descent.md) applies elementary sign symmetry, Ore minimality and cyclic norms to these fixed data. It descends the actual operator to Y=M^2 and retains the full ADO state's N-cyclic sign (-1)^(N-1). The norm-torsor construction itself remains the preceding Hilbert-90 construction; no new general descent principle or classical-symbol theorem is claimed. The [regular-period construction](regularized_kashaev_period.md) uses standard positive Temperley--Lieb path traces, reconstructed directly from the actual fundamental crossing, to bound every ordinary root color uniformly. Positive path models already have explicit coverage in [Aharonov--Jones--Landau](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0511096). Partial fractions then isolate a canonical regular ADO period and identify its complete value with a weighted cyclic field trace. A fixed actual operator gives this period a rootwise source in a bounded Laurent window with polynomially bounded coefficients. The broader root-of-unity derivative/nonsemisimple framework has coverage in [Murakami](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.1287). No proof or asymptotic claim from either source is used. These results specify the actual quantum scalar for comparison; they do not prove a generic rational source or its geometric regulator norm. The [peripheral normal-period calculation](peripheral_normal_period.md) applies the ordinary-color bound to a cleared actual operator. It proves that a coefficient nonzero on the complete column would force polynomial Kashaev growth. Retaining the corresponding delta quotient gives a first normal derivative and, under the explicit rank condition, an inverse-matrix formula with bounded source. These use standard delta modules, lifting obstructions and linear algebra. Quantum-torus Weyl reciprocity already appears in [Le's lectures, Section 5.9](https://letu.math.gatech.edu/Papers/Lectures_Luminy_2014_new.pdf). The checked weighted involutions isolate the relevant source sector; no general ADO state symmetry or AJ conclusion is assumed. The operator calibration has an exact telescoping certificate and finite actual-state checks at the levels recorded, not an inferred all-level comparison or a broad volume proof. The [actual Weyl-descent proof](actual_weyl_descent.md) now reconstructs the reflected-meridian identity of the actual ADO state from the Chevalley turnover, including the cups, caps, pivot and residual framing factor. Its symmetry has existing coverage in [Martel--Willetts, 2112.15204](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.15204). Primitive minimality then gives the unitary monomial reciprocity of the actual normal operator; the balanced-operator framework already has the Le coverage above. No proof from those sources is assumed. The new calculation removes the extra quantum-Weyl hypothesis from the canonical normal-period formulation, describes the bounded source by sine moments, and checks generator-metric invariance. It does not prove the root-sector inverse norm or the geometric factor's survival. | Part of the current notes | Existing construction or result | Actual status here | | --- | --- | --- | | Compact product and its Faddeev completion | Andersen--Kashaev's product formula | Independently verified standard identity; no new quantum function | | Face/edge cochain relation, including singular matrices | Kambampati, Sections 4--8 | Substantially the same correspondence, with independent local and homological proofs | | Gaussian/Fourier reduction | Standard linear symplectic reduction and the AK tensor | Explicit measures and phases audited; this is a coordinate computation of that reduction | | Ordinary meridian fiber and positive geometric saddle | AK, Ben Aribi--Wong, Wong | Needed proofs reconstructed; the theorem for its stated realizations is not a proof of the intrinsic all-knot conjecture | | Moving-plane inverse Fourier state | A metaplectic reformulation of the same tensor | A uniform extension recorded here with explicit level and local factorization; full intrinsic state identification remains unproved | | Minimal annihilator by finite products, moments and descent | Andersen--Malusa's annihilator convention and quantum holonomicity questions | An elementary existence argument for the specified integral class; no equality to the full A-polynomial is claimed | | Twist, 6_2, 6_3, and move certificates | Particular realizations of these constructions | Exact checks and applications; they do not supply the missing uniform theory | | Positive factorial state and naive cone transfer | Earlier custom candidates | Volume criteria proved; global quantum-state equivalence not established | | Explicit pointed recoupling and projective frame cover | Cyclic 6j-symbols and Baseilhac--Benedetti matrix dilogarithms | Direct proofs of vacuum, determinant, full matrix covariance and anchored root phases in the specified frames; no novelty or published-normalization equality inferred | | Rational quantum functions on character covers | Baseilhac--Benedetti, 2015, Theorem 1.1 and Section 4 | Existing global framework; its theorem is not being assumed as a proof for the selected AK period or its volume growth | | Equivariant denominator roots and scalar descent | Equivariant-line induction and relative group cohomology; same peripheral cover in the QHI framework | Direct formulas for coherent roots and a degree-four obstruction proof; the relative degree-three phase is retained | | Boundary period with volume norm | Classical Chern--Simons line and Bloch regulator, including Baseilhac--Benedetti Section 4.4 | Connection and norm derived explicitly with the affine reference term; the quantum norm comparison remains unproved | | Rational-state folding and local gluing residues | Garoufalidis--Kashaev's one-dimensional quasi-periodic method, Koszul reduction and Leray residues | Direct multidimensional folding proof with the actual source contour and measures; uniform pole criterion and regular boundary-period specialization; no all-knot cycle-localization theorem inferred | The following sources are relevant to the proposed torsor. They are used to identify definitions and compare scope, not as unaudited proof premises: * Faddeev--Kashaev, [Quantum Dilogarithm, hep-th/9310070](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9310070), Section 3, already defines the cyclic function by its spectral recurrence and determines it up to scalar. Its determinant normalization and parameter-dependent pentagon are therefore not new definitions here. * Kashaev, [Quantum Dilogarithm as a 6j-Symbol, hep-th/9411147](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9411147), already gives the cyclic-representation and recoupling origin of the quantum dilogarithm. The basis-free coassociativity proof reconstructed in `pointed_steinberg_recoupling.md` is standard representation theory, not a new pentagon principle. Its explicit left-ideal certificates specify the pointed vacuum used in this reformulation. * Ishibashi, [Cyclic quantum Teichmuller theory, 2501.02316v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.02316v3), interprets the coefficients and central characters in quantum cluster mutations. Its global constructions concern surface groupoids and mapping-class operators; this is not an automatic theorem for the selected boundary period of every knot complement. * Ishibashi's [correction, 2610.23572v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23572v1), Sections 1.1--1.2 and 2.1, explicitly adds the determinant-root cover and retains a possible mu_n pentagon scalar. Our local determinant cover agrees with that corrected spectral definition after a change of variables. Its claimed strict global lifts have not been adopted as a premise. * Banerjee--Merel, [The Heisenberg covering of the Fermat curve, 2210.04439](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.04439), studies the covering geometry already present here. We derive the deck transformations directly; the underlying Heisenberg cover is known. * Garoufalidis--Kashaev, [Evaluation of state integrals at rational points, 1411.6062](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.6062), Theorem 1.9, already gives an exact rational-parameter local Faddeev formula. The companion torsor note reconstructs its b^2=1/n case. Their stated global evaluation theorem is for one-dimensional integrals; it has not been used as a theorem for arbitrary knot state integrals. * Baseilhac--Benedetti, [Classical and quantum dilogarithmic invariants, math/0306283](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306283), Sections 3 and 5 and Appendix 8, is the closest matrix-level comparison: cyclic Borel recoupling, matrix dilogarithms, root branches, tetrahedral symmetries and scalar normalization. The bare recoupling pentagon is only one part of this existing construction. The present notes prove their own stated identities without adopting those global proofs. * Baseilhac--Benedetti, [Analytic families of quantum hyperbolic invariants, 1212.4261v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.4261v3), Theorem 1.1, already states rational functions on degree-n^2 covers of a Zariski open part of the geometric augmented-character component, with bulk and boundary weights. Section 4.4 describes the classical Chern--Simons line, its connection and parallel section over the peripheral curve. Thus algebraic character covers and classical period sections are existing theory, not a missing definition newly invented here. Their asymptotic problem still depends on the selected weights and periods; this work is not an automatic volume theorem. ## The structural change made here `heisenberg_period_torsor.md` presents the local normalization as an explicit H_n-torsor over the classical central shape t. The norm relation is the Steinberg relation, and the third root makes the first two deck transformations fail to commute by a central phase. This identifies the same finite Heisenberg structure behind the cyclic operator and its cover. The coordinate-free finite face contraction is proved for every finite level, including composite levels and nonfree support groups. Its measure is exactly |W|^(-1/2), and its support and quadratic form follow from one ideal-cohomology vanishing. This replaces separate rational nullspace cases by a single finite-character argument. It is an application of finite Fourier duality, not a claim to have invented that theory. The boundary module is obtained by primitive isotropic edge reduction and is irreducible of dimension n, independent of face projection rank. Its unpointed intertwiner line is rigid. The selected intrinsic boundary period remains to be identified; the subsequent local pointed results below do not already supply that global identification. The pointed recoupling note goes further at the local algebraic level: the quantum tetrahedron has the canonical vacuum A/A(X+Y-1). The audited Faddeev shift equation identifies its root-of-unity central fibre with this pointed module exactly, including the choice X=-q^(-1/2)exp(2pi b Z). Thus the algebraic vacuum is a representation of the existing local difference object, rather than a separate quantum definition selected for its asymptotic behavior. Its factorization preserves the vacuum by two exact left-ideal identities at generic quantum parameter. The associated q-factorial kernel has determinant [t(1-st)/(1-t)^2]^(n(n-1)/2), so its normalization unit is explicit before any peripheral specialization. Coassociativity proves the basis-free pentagon uniformly. This does not yet identify all global period sections or their growth with the classical regulator. The exact rational Faddeev formula also exhibits a continuous Heisenberg dilogarithm period in addition to the finite root cover. Thus the correct comparison object needs its flat connection and period/cycle data. A plain algebraic G_m-torsor does not retain all of those data. `pointed_period_descent.md` explicitly identifies the Racah operator with the same q-factorial factorization, fixes the permutation sign, and makes the scalar normalization a shared-face coboundary. This proves selected-vacuum coherence through every finite recoupling diagram. `affine_frame_period_transport.md` proves a necessary correction to the proposed pointing: unit vacua in two endpoint frames are generally different vectors under the central intertwiner. It constructs their exact norm-one transport and proves full affine covariance. `projective_frame_period_torsor.md` then proves that a fractional linear change rescales triangle generators by D_j/D_i and D_k/D_i. These rescalings commute with all four ordered Racah operator embeddings. The remaining comparison is consequently a scalar; determinant roots make it mu_(n^2)-valued and an identity-frame anchor fixes it on its irreducible lifted component. Shared-face roots preserve the pentagon. This supplies a local projective period system with its actual vector transport, uniformly at all odd levels. The proof uses precisely stated Hilbert-90 and Zariski-rigidity hypotheses and retains the deck phases. These results reconstruct and clarify part of the existing cyclic matrix framework. The new global question for this project is the exact identification of its selected period with the prescribed literature quantum-A state, followed by compatibility across levels with the Bloch regulator. Constructing another algebraic character cover would not alone establish either comparison. There is also an exact parameter condition on that last comparison. Section 5.1 of the rational Faddeev note substitutes the actual state argument at b^2=1/n and obtains t_n=exp((n+1)y), with a recorded omega deck shift of its chosen n-th root. Thus a fixed semiclassical shape does not mean a fixed finite central character. This distinction must be preserved in any claimed compatibility between the two period models. `bloch_lift_and_boundary_torsor.md` identifies a further missing datum: the tetrahedral symbol is a lift of the boundary wedge, with delta beta=-(1/2)m wedge l in the recorded unhalved conventions. Its Bloch-Wigner regulator is the volume exactly. Thus the target includes the Bloch-period lift, rather than only an unpointed split boundary algebra. The wedge and five-term arguments are uniform. The [actual peripheral-fusion calculation](actual_peripheral_fusion.md) now reconstructs the fundamental-color boundary action directly from the fixed unrolled matrices. Explicit adjacent-color projectors give the full modified-dimension ratios; heterogeneous double crossing fixes the meridian sign. The complete fusion wall retains a square-zero Casimir residue of rank N-1 and pivotal trace identity. Its actual cabled-knot coefficient and the normal Kashaev functional are specified derivatives. General unrolled/projective representation coverage is in [Costantino--Geer--Patureau-Mirand, 1406.0410](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.0410), and the torus skein/quantum-torus framework is covered by [Frohman--Gelca, math/9806107](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9806107). Derivative/radical-center knot invariants also have coverage in [Murakami, 1406.1287](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.1287). Their abstracts establish coverage only; no proof is imported. The actual threading formulas are independently proved, and no universal degree-2N Frobenius map or new general spectral projector theorem is claimed. ## What would constitute the new global theorem The [arbitrary-bridge sourced reduction](arbitrary_bridge_source_reduction.md) now replaces the recent one-variable twist diagnostic by a 2k-plat construction with arbitrary k and word. Plat intersections and their volume/torsion forms have existing coverage in Dubois's [2005 paper](https://www.numdam.org/articles/10.5802/aif.2136/) and [2006 paper](https://msp.org/agt/2006/6-1/agt-v6-n1-p13-p.pdf). It does not assume the published torsion comparison or identify the full selected quantum source. The uniform proof has no bridge-number or alternatingness restriction; the tests also include nonacyclic endpoints and make no knot-recognition claims. No novelty is claimed for ribbon turns, geometric sums or Hilbert 90. The selected crossing/source coupling remains the missing global norm step, rather than another boundary normalization choice. Its new role here is a bounded-bandwidth finite jet system, valid without rank-one root kernels, whose source border recovers the original selected norm. Jet rescaling makes its norm uniformly bounded; its characteristic is a power of the chosen operator's classical symbol. A positive quadratic response has precisely this period as its derivative. Cauchy--Binet, Schur complements and quadratic response theory are standard algebra; no novelty is claimed for them. The source, jet budget, classical-symbol calculation and exact link to the original knot period are proved directly. The hyperbolic-volume growth of this determinant ratio remains unproved. The [tempered leading-divisor estimate](tempered_a_growth_bound.md) now proves a source-preserving upper bound for actual operator periods under its explicit analytic-divisor hypotheses. The direct proof keeps the finite jet budget and exact cyclic zeros, then uses an adapted norm for a continuous fixed-size matrix family. No eigenvalue noncollision theorem is invoked. Existing coverage includes [Garoufalidis--Geronimo](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0405331), whose abstract states regularity assumptions; those theorem claims are not proof inputs. The geometric leading-edge roots of unity have coverage in [Cooper--Culler--Gillet--Long--Shalen, 5.10](https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~culler/papers/PlaneCurves/curves.pdf); the present deduction is directly from our Bloch boundary wedge and multiplicative valuation residue. The statement is an upper estimate, and the explicit source countercheck rules out inferring a selected volume formula from root moduli alone. `equivariant_roots_and_phase_descent.md` supplies a further global part of the finite-level theory. Equivariant root lines on Gamma/P are classified by roots of the peripheral character; the explicit induced multiplier satisfies the cocycle law. Triangle determinant roots can be chosen multiplicatively on their free orbits. The remaining Racah phase is a configuration three-cocycle. A relative free resolution and H^4(W,partial W;mu_(n^2))=0 produce a correction with both equivariance and pentagon coherence. Its residual choices form the relative fundamental-class phase torsor H^3(W,partial W;mu_(n^2)). This is a uniform scalar descent theorem, not an identification of a selected analytic integration cycle or a proof of arbitrary admissible-path connectivity. The degree-n^2 classification concerns the peripheral root line; no degree for the complete period cover is inferred. The same relative argument works for generic F^*-valued discrepancies, provided the parameter field is fixed and the operator comparison has already made them scalar. It retains a residual F^* period class and all peripheral units; specialization to a numerical multiplier cannot identify that class or fix its normalization. `boundary_regulator_period.md` directly constructs the continuous target. The logarithmic boundary line has multiplier exp(bU-aV), connection -(U dV-V dU)/(2pi i), and an invariant norm. An explicit centering term for the affine edge equations gives a parallel period satisfying log||P||=2D(beta)/pi, including all branch terms. At completeness this is 2Vol/pi. This agrees with the existing classical Chern--Simons framework. The still-unproved quantum comparison is precisely 4h_n log|J_n|+log||P_hyp|| -> 0 with h_n=n/(n+1)^2, for the prescribed literature state and the full requested knot class. `rational_period_pushforward.md` now fixes a concrete representative for that chosen realization. Cubical telescoping gives the folded source period. A unimodular Koszul reduction identifies the algebraic gluing equations H_i=1, while the local Leray residue contains the full symmetric gluing Hessian and Rogers-period terms. These algebraic statements do not themselves remove polar cycle data. The same note proves a source-pole cancellation criterion for positive factors with consistent polar coorientation. Independent auxiliary argument shifts achieve generic distinctness when used in a holomorphic period germ. A direct Faddeev-ratio example shows why the specialization must retain that germ: its generic gluing root reaches a removed polar divisor, yet its residue has a regular nonzero value. This is a model of boundary specialization, not a counterexample to the volume conjecture. The supplied manuscript's Section 9.4 provides a related warning that ordinary limiting characters can discard period data. An equivalence of those different period problems is not assumed from the analogy. What remains here is transport/localization of the selected global cycle, matching it with the finite recoupling realization, and the norm comparison across levels. The one-dimensional evaluation theorem in 1411.6062 has not been promoted to a multidimensional theorem by citation. The intended advance is a triangulation-independent **pointed boundary splitting module with its Heisenberg/dilogarithm period torsor**, together with its regulator comparison. It must be built on the intrinsic decorated character space, identify the literature state, and prove the requested volume statement uniformly. The current notes do not yet prove this theorem. Neither renaming a known local cover nor adding more knot examples would do so. The [whole-period rigidity note](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) adds a finite reconstruction criterion to the existing source-base and sparse-multiplicity arguments. It keeps q^N as well as M^N and their relative logarithmic connection before specializing. The root-only slice q^N=-1 is not stable under a quantum-normal derivative. Two Vandermonde inversions and level interpolation reconstruct any fixed bounded algebraic residual from mixed cyclotomic jets; a finite algebra norm extends the criterion to a chosen etale shape branch. These are elementary algebraic arguments, with no novelty claim. They provide a certificate for an already specified pointed map; they do not construct the unknown global quantum period comparison or infer its existence from Rivin's classical optimizer. The [rank-one divisor-flow theorem](cyclotomic_divisor_descent.md) then removes the assumed levelwise gauge bound for a fixed split-divisor class. The closest coverage found is cyclotomic q-curvature and parameterized generic difference-Galois groups in [Di Vizio--Hardouin, 1205.1692](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.1692) and [1205.1694](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.1694). Only their abstracts are used for this coverage statement; none of their proofs or theorems is a premise of our restricted descent proof. A comparison line satisfying its divisor and norm hypotheses has not yet been constructed for the actual selected knot period. For coverage, the torus skein/noncommutative-torus connection appears in [Frohman--Gelca](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9806107), and related Askey--Wilson, skein and R-matrix structures are surveyed in [Crampe et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.14815). [Habiro's completion paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0209324) advertises cyclotomic functions determined by their root data. Only these abstracts were consulted for this coverage statement. The explicit weighted source lattice, normal cut and banded identities here are proved in the repo; no published theorem is invoked to infer their geometric support or volume norm. The basis and invariant-division-ring setting have existing coverage: cyclotomic expansions are discussed in [Berest--Gallagher--Samuelson](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.04415), and [Fryer](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.5071) advertises fixed q-division rings for finite monomial automorphism groups. Only their abstracts were used for coverage here; the specific identities and source arguments are proved directly. Neither general quantum rationality nor cyclotomic interpolation by itself selects the volume branch. There is now a proved [partial geometric-support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md) from the actual finite arrays: two framing indices remain external, and formal transverse-only contraction satisfies the same certificate and least-moment identity as the finite partial sum. This yields a certified operator with a geometric classical factor, rather than adding one to an annihilator. It does not prove the geometric factor survives the final selected framing contraction. Its shifted function, endpoint polynomial, explicit head Ward correction and marked Green carry are retained before normal restriction. These supply new explicit steps in this repo's source construction. Jackson calculus, confluent interpolation and Serre duality themselves are established mathematics; no novelty is claimed for them. For coverage, Kashaev's original [cyclic 6j-symbol paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9411147) already places the cyclic dilogarithm in the Weyl/Borel framework, and his [1995 crossing paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9504020) states its R-matrix link construction.
