title: A tame paired Fermat frame for the original whole source
text: # A tame paired Fermat frame for the original whole source 28 October 2026. Pairing the actual cap heads before changing frame removes the exponential factorial norm found in independent-head Fermat frames. The paired source, its marked dual, and a full invertible frame are explicit. The frame and inverse are uniformly bounded on one fixed central neighborhood, for every level. Conjugating the whole actual word and all currents gives a pointwise identity of the ORIGINAL invariant, including its full meridian family and scalar lines. This is a theorem about the selected boundary source. It does not factor the new crossing into a positive geometric tetrahedron kernel, or identify its Cartan charge with a new Pachner edge winding. ## 1. The actual charged channel and the paired source Fix N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2pi i/N). On the original relative dual pair the actual Cartan is Q^(-1-D), D=a+b, 0<=a,b<=d. Its invariant channel is EXACTLY H_d=span{|j,d-j>:0<=j<=d}, D+1=N. (1) Indeed Q^(-1-D)=1 and 0<=D<=2N-2 force D=N-1. The projector onto this channel is the actual finite Cartan average, not a new positivity projection. The [original source reduction](actual_rogers_bridge_transport.md) uses the input/marked corner e_+=|d,0> and ordinary output corner e_-=|0,d> in this channel. Put epsilon=a^N and delta=(1-epsilon)^(1/N), delta(0)=1. Take the ORIGINAL normalized cap frames from [the exact cap theorem](actual_cap_pachner_wall_charge.md), using the SAME a on the two heads, and project their tensor product to (1). In the basis indexed by j this gives V_j(epsilon)= epsilon / [(1-Q)(Q^2 delta;Q)_j (Q delta;Q)_(d-j)], W_j(epsilon)= (Q delta;Q)_j (delta;Q)_(d-j)/N. (2) These are removable formulas at epsilon=0, with V(0)=e_+, W(0)=e_+^t, V_d=R=(1-Q delta)/(1-Q), W_d=A=epsilon/[N(1-delta)] =(1+delta+...+delta^(N-1))/N. (3) All j<d entries vanish at zero. Replacing j by d-j gives V_-,W_- with limits e_-,e_-^t. Write V_+=V,W_+=W. To derive (2), the normalized input factors are (P_hat_d)_j=a^(j+1)/[(1-Q)(Q^2 delta;Q)_j], (P_hat_0)_(d-j)=a^(d-j)/(Q delta;Q)_(d-j). Their powers multiply to a^N=epsilon. The normalized output factors have powers a^(d-j) and a^(-(d-j)), which cancel. This proves central descent directly, including the exact affine charge. It also proves equality with the original corners at zero. No assertion that epsilon is the actual semicyclic or meridian normal parameter is needed. In the fixed old current frame, F_rel V is generally nonzero away from zero. Section 4 transports that current as well as the source; it does not silently claim V is an invariant vector of the unchanged current. ## 2. Pairing cancels the exponential factorial profiles For |epsilon|<=rho<=1/16, one has |delta-1|<=2rho/N, |1-Q^r|>=4 dist(r,N Z)/N. (4) There is an EXACT symmetry before estimating any long product: V_j=V_(d-1-j), W_j=W_(d-1-j), 0<=j<d. (5) Indeed, writing A_l=(Q delta;Q)_l, the two expressions are V_j=epsilon R/[A_(j+1)A_(d-j)] and W_j=(1-delta)A_j A_(d-j-1)/N. The symmetry swaps their two factors. It lets us estimate only j=ell-1 with ell=min(j+1,N-j-1)<=N/2. The consecutive ratios in (2) are V_(j+1)/V_j=(1-delta Q^(-j-1))/(1-delta Q^(j+2)), W_(j+1)/W_j=(1-delta Q^(j+1))/(1-delta Q^(-j-2)). (6) Their unperturbed magnitudes telescope from j=0 to ell-1, giving |1-Q|/|1-Q^ell|<=pi/(2ell). Each normalized factor at root distance s<=ell has relative error at most rho/(2s), so its logarithmic magnitude changes by at most rho/s. The numerator and denominator errors therefore sum to at most 2rho(1+log ell), with NO log N loss. Moreover V_0=(1-delta)/(1-Q), W_0=epsilon/[N(1-delta Q^-1)], |V_0|,|W_0|<=|epsilon|/2. Combining these statements gives the uniform tail estimate |V_j|,|W_j| <= (pi |epsilon|/4) exp(2rho) ell_j^(-1+2rho), j<d. (7) At rho=1/16 the squared power is -7/4. Every ell occurs at most twice, and sum_(ell>=1)ell^(-7/4)<=1+4/3. Hence the total off-corner squared norm is less than .015. Together with |R|<=1+rho/2 and |A|<=1+rho, this proves sup_(|epsilon|<=1/16) ||V_+/-||_2,||W_+/-||_2<=3 (8) for EVERY N. In fact the displayed estimates give norms below 1.1. The simple bound 3 suffices for all subsequent constants. This fixed CENTRAL disc corresponds to |a|=(1/16)^(1/N), near one, rather than the individual-head micro-collar |a|<=1/(16N). The Cartan-charge pairing is essential to the cancellation. More precisely ||V-e_+|| and ||W-e_+^t|| are O(|epsilon|), uniformly in N on this disc. This includes the endpoints by (3). The same holds in the reversed orientation. ## 3. The exact paired normalizer is a known algebraic unit The full paired value is G(epsilon)=W V = R (2-epsilon)/(1+delta) = R (1+delta^N)/(1+delta). (9) For a direct proof, for j<d put r=j+1 and multiply (2): W_j V_j = epsilon(1-delta)R / [N(1-delta Q^r)(1-delta Q^-r)]. The missing endpoint is W_dV_d=RA. The finite root identity sum_(r=0)^(N-1) 1/[(1-delta Q^r)(1-delta Q^-r)] = N(1+delta^N)/[(1-delta^N)(1-delta^2)] (10) follows by multiplying the two convergent geometric series first for |delta|<1, taking the root sum, and then rational continuation. Subtract its r=0 term. Its contribution exactly cancels RA, giving (9). Removable values extend the calculation to zero. On |epsilon|<=1/16, R and G are bounded units: for example |R-1|<=rho/2 and |G-1|<1/8. In particular G(0)=1. This scalar is computed from the known source alone. It is NOT a normalization by an unknown knot period. Its entire factor (2-epsilon)/(1+delta) must be retained. Equation (9) also holds for W_-V_-. It does not normalize the cross-oriented pairing W_-V_+, which vanishes at zero. Dividing by that latter pairing would destroy the ordinary zero-dimensional cup-cap behavior and is not permitted here. For real 0<epsilon<1, there is also an exact positive Hermitian structure. Reflection of complementary root factors gives W=(A/conjugate(R)) V^*, W/G=V^*/||V||^2, ||V||^2=|R|^2(2-epsilon)/[(1+delta)A]. (9a) For j<d, use conjugate((Q delta;Q)_(j+1))= epsilon/[(1-delta)(Q delta;Q)_(d-j-1)] and the analogous identity for d-j. Substitution in (2) proves (9a); the endpoint follows from (3). Hence V W/G is an ORTHOGONAL rank-one projector on this real interval. Its diagonal is the explicit probability distribution pi_j=epsilon(1-delta^2) / [N(2-epsilon)|1-delta Q^(j+1)|^2]. (9b) This describes the paired boundary functional. Ordinary output caps have the other orientation, and the transformed word remains complex. No positivity or noncancellation of the knot scalar follows. The paired source also has a fixed-order exact cyclic equation. Let A_clk act by Q^j and let (Tf)_j=f_(j+1 mod N), so T A_clk=Q A_clk T. Direct ratios in (2), including the wrap, give [(1-delta Q^2 A_clk)T -(1-delta Q^-1 A_clk^-1)] V=0, W[(1-delta Q^-1 A_clk^-1)T^-1 -(1-delta Q A_clk)]=0. (9c) The two finite operators have different ordering, as the actual marked co-source requires. Their regular classical symbol is the Gaussian relation p=-A_clk^-1. The dilogarithmic factorial profiles cancel in this paired boundary relation. At A_clk=1 its factors cannot be divided out; the exact equations retain the cap wall. The [degree/cap audit](actual_degree_carry_and_cap_winding_obstruction.md) proves these ratios and their wrapped endpoint identities. ## 4. An explicit full invertible frame of uniformly bounded norm Use either matched orientation, with reference corner e and v=V_+/- , w=W_+/- /G. Then wv=1 and e^t v=R!=0. Define on H_d g=v e^t+(I-vw)(I-ee^t), g^-1=I-v e^t/R+e w. (11) Direct multiplication gives g e=v, e^t g^-1=w, det g=R, g(0)=I, rank(g-I)<=2, rank(g^-1-I)<=2. (12) For instance decompose an input as ae+z with e^t z=0. The output is z+v(a-wz), and e^t applied to it determines a-wz because R!=0. This gives precisely the inverse in (11). On the disc (8), the bounds above imply the uniform estimates ||g||<=15, ||g^-1||<=8. (13) Both matrices in fact differ from the identity by O(|epsilon|), uniformly in N. They are algebraic meromorphic functions of epsilon,delta,Q, regular on the stated marked disc. Extend g by the identity on all other total-degree channels in the two-head space. This retains its norm bounds and commutes with total degree and with the actual Cartan clock. This is a full matrix frame, not only an isomorphism of one line. The construction does not assert that g commutes with the old raising and lowering currents. They are transported by the same conjugation, which is necessary for a pointed network identity. These are bounds for whole algebraic functions on an N-independent disc. They do not require truncating the source to a fixed list of Taylor coefficients or shrinking its central neighborhood. The norm is the fixed Euclidean norm in the ORIGINAL relative-head basis of the exact Rogers presentation. Conjugating back by a physical fusion matrix C_x need not preserve these estimates; that separate matrix can be exponentially conditioned. The new source frame adds no exponential cost within this specified exact presentation, and the scalar equality in Section 5 is independent of the metric. ## 5. Pointwise transport of the whole original arbitrary-plat invariant Use the literal original fused word B_beta, with EVERY degree channel retained, and its known source formula P_(beta,N)=chi_beta N^(1-k) <e_out|B_beta|e_in>. (14) At each chosen horizontal slice form a tensor product Gamma of the paired frames (11), extended off H_d as above. For an actual letter or coupon O between consecutive slices use O'=Gamma_next O Gamma_previous^-1. (15) The actual currents, sewing maps, projectors, and any other insertions use the same prescription. Internal frames cancel exactly, giving B'_beta=Gamma_out B_beta Gamma_in^-1. At the boundary use the original input orientation e_+ on each pair, the ordinary output e_- on k-1 pairs, and the marked output e_+ on the remaining pair. Then, POINTWISE in every allowed auxiliary parameter, P_(beta,N)=chi_beta N^(1-k) (tensor_out W_sigma/G) B'_beta (tensor_in V_+). (16) This follows from (12), not from a limiting argument or a proposed triangulation invariant. The original full meridian dependence and original scalar lines remain those of B_beta and chi_beta. With unnormalized output rows W, retain the explicit additional factor product_out G^-1 in (16). No cross-oriented source pairing is divided out. No independent head coherent frame H or M is substituted for g. Those frames have the exponential norms proved in the four-line note; the present paired, charge-preserving frame has the different explicit bounds (13). For a fixed bridge number its tensor norms remain bounded independently of N. At an actual input dual pair, (15) carries F_rel to a current annihilating V_+ exactly, since F_rel e_+=0. For an ordinary OUTPUT the sided identity is (W_-/G)F'_rel=0, because e_-^t F_rel=0. The marked output is not an ordinary Hopf cap. Thus the relevant auxiliary completion's Ward defect is resolved by an explicit full current transport. This does not identify epsilon with a semicyclic normal parameter, nor turn intermediate non-dual pairs into dual ones. ## 6. Normal residue corrections have uniformly bounded source cost For completeness, the paired source also supplies an exact finite-jet regularization of singular terms. With one common central variable set J(epsilon)=V(epsilon)W(epsilon), or use its explicit normalized version J/G. These rank-one kernels have uniformly bounded trace norm on (8). Hence ||[epsilon^r]J||_1 <=9*16^r. (17) For an actual matrix expansion O(epsilon)=sum_(r=-p)^infinity O_r epsilon^r with fixed pole order, the paired constant-term functional is exactly CT tr(OJ)=sum_(r=0)^p tr(O_(-r) J_r), |CT tr(OJ)|<=9 sum_(r=0)^p 16^r ||O_(-r)||. (18) The normalized kernel has another absolute constant. Independent input and output central parameters, or a fixed number of pairs, give the corresponding product Cauchy bounds. Central descent of the paired source is proved in Section 1; descent or bounded deck support of a transformed operator must still be checked. Equations (17)--(18) specify a linear regularization which agrees with the original cap on every assembled holomorphic word. It preserves any exact meromorphic matrix identity to which it is applied on one common domain. They do not assert that every singular summand has the same value as an older independent-head residue prescription. Such a comparison retains its actual Ward/sewing corrections. The stronger pointwise identity (16) does not depend on making that termwise identification. ## 7. What remains on the main critical path The original paired source is now represented by a genuine tame pointed frame, with its affine charge, dual scalar and currents all explicit. This is the part of boundary transport proved here. The new crossing in (15) has not been identified with the positive geometric tetrahedron kernels. The three angular clocks of a Pachner edge have not been proved to represent the charge D+1. In particular (16) neither removes the certified oversized weak alias face nor proves that the geometric scalar survives. A nonzero bulk component of V can still cancel against the exact transformed kernel. The general volume conjecture remains open. The independent checks are in [the paired-source audit](../experiments/audit_paired_actual_cap_source_independent.py). They compare literal two-head cap products and the actual Cartan projector, source bounds, the full normalizer, and the full frame identities. The uniform assertions follow from the proofs above.

title: A general A-operator growth bound with the cyclic source retained
text: # A general A-operator growth bound with the cyclic source retained Research note, 27 October 2026. This gives a one-sided exponential estimate for the original pointed period, under explicit conditions on a specified actual quantum A-operator. The proof allows eigenvalue collisions, nonnormal matrices and exactly vanishing leading columns. It uses the finite jet source, rather than assuming a regular growing solution of a classical recurrence. There is no bridge-number bound. The estimate is an upper bound, not the volume conjecture. Its classical largest-root integral can be strictly larger than the selected period's rate. Sections 6--7 make that limitation explicit. ## 1. The Bloch boundary relation forces roots of unity at a leading edge This general algebraic property already follows from our marked Bloch relation; no published K-theory proof is needed here. On the function field of a geometric gluing curve, or a finite augmented cover of its peripheral curve, the existing calculation gives sum_j epsilon_j z_j wedge (1-z_j)=-2 M wedge L in wedge^2(F^* tensor Q). (1.1) For a discrete valuation v and units after uniformizer extraction, define the multiplicative residue tau_v(f,g)=(-1)^(v(f)v(g)) [f^v(g)/g^v(f)]_residue. (1.2) It is multiplicative in each input, and alternating after tensoring the target with Q. Directly tau_v(z,1-z)=1: when v(z)>0 the residue of 1-z is 1; when v(1-z)>0 that of z is 1; when v(z)<0 the quotient z/(1-z) has residue -1, and the two sign exponents sum to v(z)^2+v(z), which is even. The remaining unit case is immediate. Thus (1.2) applied to (1.1) makes tau_v(M,L) torsion. At a place where M has finite nonzero residue M_0 and L has a pole, this says that M_0^v(L) is a root of unity. Hence M_0 is a root of unity. If the valuation is first defined on the peripheral curve, extend it to the finite gluing field; the valuation order is multiplied by its positive ramification index and the same conclusion follows. This keeps the marked lifts. Every nonzero root of the leading L coefficient of a geometric A-factor gives a point (M_0,infinity) of its projective closure. A place on the normalization above that point has v(M)=0 and v(L)<0, so the preceding argument applies. The same conclusion holds in the squared meridian Y=M^2. Thus that leading coefficient has only roots of unity in C^*, apart from its Laurent monomial. This is the leading-edge part of the usual temperedness property. This proof concerns the geometric peripheral factor supported by (1.1). It does not identify a given actual quantum operator's classical symbol with that factor, remove additional operator factors, or prove a quantum deformation is unramified. ## 2. Conditions for a source-preserving growth estimate Use a specified even-meridian actual all-level annihilator A=sum_(i=0)^d a_i(q,Y) T^i, T Y=q^2 Y T, Y=M^2, a_i in C[q^(+/-1),Y^(+/-1)]. (2.1) Even descent for the original state was proved in [the signed norm note](even_meridian_norm_descent.md). Clear denominators and remove a common power of q-1. Assume: 1. a_0(1,Y) and p(1,Y), p=a_d, are nonzero Laurent polynomials. 2. Every zero of p(1,Y) on |Y|=1 is a root of unity. 3. Near each such zero zeta the zero divisor of p(q,Y) splits into analytic branches Y=lambda_r(q), lambda_r(1)=zeta, with multiplicity allowed. Its local remaining factor is a unit. The third condition holds for simple classical roots, and for products of the usual binomials 1-zeta q^a Y^b. It is a genuine condition: a ramified Puiseux branch is not silently treated as analytic. Roots away from the unit circle require no such condition. The theorem does not claim these conditions for every knot's unknown minimal operator. They are directly checkable operator data. Let A_cl(Y,L)=sum a_i(1,Y)L^i and, outside the finite leading-zero set, let R(theta)=max{|L|:A_cl(exp(i theta),L)=0}, E(A)=integral_0^(2pi) log R(theta) dtheta. (2.2) The logarithmic singularities at the excluded finite set are integrable, as shown in Section 5. No selected source is replaced by a choice of the largest root in the definition of the invariant. **Pointed growth theorem.** Under conditions 1--3, the original Kashaev value recovered from this actual operator satisfies limsup_(N->infinity) (2pi/N)log|<K>_N| <= E(A). (2.3) Zero values on the left are interpreted as log 0=-infinity. For the positive pointed Gram period of the previous note, limsup_(N->infinity) (pi/N)log G_N <= max(0,E(A)). (2.4) We prove these statements below. Neither is an equality assertion. ## 3. A fixed-size positive transport keeps every singular step Use the exact generic color recurrence and bounded q-jet budget B from [the pointed Gram construction](pointed_a_gram_period.md). Write V_j=(C_j,...,C_(j+d-1))^t. Before specializing any root, p(q,q^(2j)) V_(j+1)=N_j(q) V_j, (3.1) where N_j has p on its superdiagonal and last row (-a_0,...,-a_(d-1)), evaluated at Y=q^(2j). Put q=q_N(1+t) and use the scaled variable s=N t. Let K_(N,j) be the lower Toeplitz lift of N_j(q_N(1+s/N)) through s-degree B. Its size is d(B+1), independent of N, and its entries are uniformly bounded. Let m_j be the actual order of p(q,q^(2j)) at q_N and define eta_j=[s^m_j]p(q_N(1+s/N),q_N^(2j)(1+s/N)^(2j)), beta_N=sum_(j=j_*)^(N-d)m_j <= B. (3.2) The fixed small-color jet column u_N is bounded. Multiplying (3.1) in the generic field and only then taking the indicated coefficient gives the exact formula <K>_N=e_(beta_N,d)^t K_(N,N-d)...K_(N,j_*)u_N / product_j eta_j. (3.3) Indeed the unlifted numerator is (product_j p_j)V_(N-d+1). The product has first nonzero s-coefficient product_j eta_j in degree beta_N, and the color column is regular. Thus (3.3) does not divide by a vanishing specialized leading coefficient. There is an exact positive transport of its squared norm. With rho_0=u_N u_N^dagger propagate rho_(j+1)=K_(N,j) rho_j K_(N,j)^dagger, |<K>_N|^2=Tr(E_(beta_N,d)rho_final) /product_j |eta_j|^2. (3.4) The last effect is its specified rank-one coordinate projector. All phases and jet couplings remain in the matrices and source. This is a positive matrix transport, not an entrywise-positive recurrence or a license to drop the source. The denominator is the same whole leading germ used in the original A-period. ## 4. The leading germ has a controlled logarithmic product Under conditions 2--3 one has sum_j log|eta_j|=N I_p+O(log N), I_p=(1/(2pi))integral_0^(2pi)log|p(1,exp(i theta))|dtheta. (4.1) Here is a proof retaining exact root zeros. Away from a fixed neighborhood of the classical unit-circle zeros, p(q_N,Y)/p(1,Y) is uniformly 1+O(1/N). Near a zero zeta, each analytic root branch moves by O(1/N). At grid points with distance at least K/N from zeta, choose K large enough so the root displacement is less than half that distance. Factoring locally gives a log-modulus error O(1/(N distance)). Summation over these points costs O(log N). Only a bounded number of points lie within K/N of zeta. Because zeta is a root of unity, write zeta=exp(2pi i a/r). On each residue class of N modulo r, every such point is j=aN/r+k, Y_j=zeta q_N^(2k), (4.2) where k is in a fixed finite set of rational numbers; use both endpoint representations a/r=0,1 when zeta=1. Its ordinary value is a fixed analytic germ p(q,zeta q^(2k)) at q=1. Unless identically zero, that germ has a finite order, so its nonzero value at q_N is bounded above and below by powers of N. For an exactly zero value use the q-jet along the actual color trajectory. A coefficient of fixed jet degree is a finite sum of terms c zeta^b q_N^(u+2bk) N^(-m) binom(u+2b(aN/r+k),m). (4.3) Here u is the q-exponent of the monomial and b its Y-exponent. Formula (4.3) is meromorphic in 1/N with a finite-order pole or zero. The finite-monomial Vandermonde bound from the jet theorem bounds the first nonzero degree m. For each of the finitely many residue classes and offsets, that leading coefficient is therefore bounded above and below by powers of N for all sufficiently large N. If all bounded-degree germs vanished identically, their evaluations would violate that Vandermonde bound on every large actual trajectory. Thus exact zeros, including coalescing analytic branches, cost only O(log N) at this bounded number of points. The fixed discarded initial and final colors have the same control. Finally the classical grid product itself has the claimed mean. Factor p(1,Y) over C. Off-circle roots contribute N times their circle mean plus O(1), by the identity product_(Y^N=1)(Y-lambda) =(-1)^N(lambda^N-1). A unit-circle root of unity either has zeta^N!=1, giving a nonzero value in a finite set, or is a grid root. In the latter case omitting its zero factor gives modulus N by differentiating Y^N-1 at zeta. Multiplicities and the fixed removed points add O(log N). Combining these facts proves (4.1). The analytic-branch condition is used exactly in the O(1/N) displacement above. Classical temperedness alone does not prove it. In particular, if p(1,Y) is a Laurent monomial times cyclotomic factors with leading scalar of modulus one, then I_p=0. The entire product of leading germs is then bounded above and below by powers of N. Individual factors may still vanish or become numerical multipliers at a root. Their complete germs, rather than those separate numerical values, give this conclusion. ## 5. A direct upper bound for slowly varying matrix products We need only the following elementary norm lemma. Suppose bounded matrices K_(N,j) tend uniformly to a continuous matrix K(x), x=j/N, of fixed dimension. If log rho(K(x)) is integrable, then limsup (1/N)log||product_j K_(N,j)|| <=integral_0^1 log rho(K(x)) dx. (5.1) For completeness first fix epsilon>0 and set a(x)=rho(K(x))+epsilon. The matrix H(x)=sum_(n>=0)(K(x)^dagger)^n K(x)^n/a(x)^(2n) converges uniformly, is continuous, satisfies H>=I and is bounded above on the compact interval. Uniform convergence follows, for example, by unitary triangularization: bounded upper triangular matrices of fixed size have power growth bounded by a fixed polynomial times (rho+epsilon/2)^n, uniformly with constants depending on epsilon and the dimension. Its induced norm obeys ||K(x)v||_(H(x))<=a(x)||v||_(H(x)). Uniform convergence of K_(N,j) and uniform continuity of H make each step cost at most a(j/N)+o(1), and the change between the two neighboring H norms costs 1+o(1), uniformly. Multiplying, taking logarithms, and dividing by N yields integral log(rho+epsilon). Let epsilon decrease to zero. In the present application integrability and the passage to that limit follow from the polynomial lower bound on rho stated below. No diagonalization through an eigenvalue collision and no spectral-gap hypothesis enters this upper bound. For our lifted matrices the limit K(x) is lower triangular in jet degree, with the same diagonal block at every degree: N_0(x)=[0 p 0 ...; ...; -a_0 -a_1 ... -a_(d-1)] at q=1,Y=exp(2pi i x). Therefore rho(K(x))=rho(N_0(x)). Where p!=0 its eigenvalues are p(1,Y)L_i(Y), so log rho(K(x))=log|p(1,Y)|+log R(2pi x). (5.2) Both sides are integrable. Indeed the characteristic coefficients of N_0 are a_i p^(d-1-i), and a_0 p^(d-1) is nonzero by condition 1. Their finite-order zeros give a polynomial lower bound on rho near its finitely many possible zeros. This justifies the limiting norm argument as well as the integral in (2.2). Apply (5.1) to (3.3). The input is bounded, the selected coordinate has norm one, and (4.1) subtracts I_p from the growth rate. Equation (5.2) gives (2.3). The polynomial ordinary-color remainder in the Gram theorem then gives (2.4). This proves the pointed upper bound. ## 6. The source prevents turning this bound into a volume formula An exact countercheck is the unknot with the actual annihilator (T-c)(T-1), c>1, C_j(q)=1 for every color. All conditions above hold. The entropy is E=2pi log c, but the selected period is identically one and has zero rate. Its source is entirely in the L=1 line; the positive evolution (3.4) retains this fact. The same left multiplication can be applied to an actual hyperbolic knot operator and can enlarge E arbitrarily without changing its pointed period. Thus source reachability and a sharp estimate cannot be inferred from root moduli alone. Even full classical temperedness does not fix this source issue. Let C(Y,L) be the figure-eight geometric polynomial displayed below, and form the dummy left factor C(Y,T). The operator C(Y,T)(T-1) is an actual annihilator of the unknot's constant period. Its classical symbol is (L-1)C(Y,L), whose edge polynomials are cyclotomic, yet its selected period is still one. This is not claimed to be a standard quantum figure-eight operator; it is an exact countercheck on any argument using only the tempered characteristic polynomial and omitting the actual source. There is also a useful geometric calibration. For the figure-eight geometric polynomial in Y,L, A_geo=L^2-(Y^2-Y-2-Y^(-1)+Y^(-2))L+1, put c(theta)=1+cos theta-cos(2theta). Then log R is arcosh c(theta) on (0,2pi/3) and (4pi/3,2pi), and is zero on the remaining arc. Hence E(A_geo)=2 integral_0^(2pi/3)arcosh c(theta)dtheta =2 Vol(4_1). (6.1) The last equality is the already calibrated [classical cone/regulator identity](quantum_a_volume.md#34-the-figure-eight-knot-a-complete-example), not an identification of that note's custom transfer state with Kashaev. This factor of two shows why the full-circle largest-root integral is not the desired selected volume. The quantum boundary and resonance data must choose the appropriate action; (2.3) does not prove that selection or its lower bound. ## 7. Coverage and remaining scope The leading-edge root-of-unity statement has existing coverage in [Cooper--Culler--Gillet--Long--Shalen, Proposition 5.10](https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~culler/papers/PlaneCurves/curves.pdf). The direct residue proof in Section 1 uses only our recorded Bloch boundary relation. Existing regular q-difference asymptotics include [Garoufalidis--Geronimo](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0405331), whose abstract specifies noncollision and nonvanishing assumptions. Only their stated scope was used for coverage; none of their proofs is a premise for Sections 3--5. The new step relative to the previous repo notes is a one-sided estimate for the actual pointed A-period that retains the complete cyclic leading germ, a bounded number of singular jets, and its fixed source, while allowing eigenvalue collisions. It requires the explicit leading-divisor hypotheses in Section 2. It neither proves those hypotheses for every knot operator nor proves a sharp geometric rate. Identifying and estimating the source-selected geometric action is still the central unresolved part of the volume conjecture. [Audit](../experiments/audit_tempered_a_growth.py). [Results](../experiments/tempered_a_growth_results.json).

title: Tetrahedral order changes and a calibrated figure-eight move
text: # Tetrahedral order changes and a calibrated figure-eight move Research note, 25 October 2026. The definitions are the Gaussian kernels and charged operators of Andersen–Kashaev, [arXiv:1109.6295v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6295v2), Sections 4–7. We reconstruct the needed symmetries from the independently proved Fourier formula, rather than assuming the source's Fundamental Lemma or its global invariance theorem. The phase conventions are those of `peripheral_phase_and_state.md`. This note calibrates an actual move between the three-tetrahedron twist-family realization of 4_1 and the two-tetrahedron realization used for its audited minimal annihilator. Its statement is for generic boundary x, before setting the complete value x=0. Throughout, b>0, h=(b+b^(-1))^(-2), and q=exp(2pi i b^2). ## 1. Coherent changes of triangle ordering Define the published kernels A(x,y)=delta(x+y)exp[pi i(x^2+1/12)], B(x,y)=exp[pi i(x-y)^2]. As operators, A is reflection followed by a unit-modulus chirp, and B=M_+ Fourier M_+, where M_+(x)=exp(pi i x^2) and Fourier has kernel exp(-2pi i xy). Thus A,B are unitary and preserve Schwartz space, with adjoints given by their conjugate symmetric kernels. These assertions do not require a quantum-dilogarithm identity. For a triangle whose orientation is reversed, identify its space with its conjugate dual using the antiunitary maps R_A=A conjugation and R_B=B conjugation. They represent its two adjacent vertex transpositions. Indeed R_A^2=R_B^2=1. Their product is the linear operator V=A B^*, V(x,y)=exp(pi i/12)exp(-pi i y^2-2pi i xy). Completing a square in the middle integral of V^2 supplies the Fresnel factor exp(-pi i/4). The third product leaves delta(x-y), with total scalar exp(3pi i/12-pi i/4)=1. Therefore V^3=1. The two involutions and this relation give an *exact* representation of S_3, with the odd permutations antiunitary because they reverse orientation. In particular, the triangle basis change is determined by its vertex permutation, independently of a chosen word. The pi/12 in A is essential to this scalar calculation. All Fresnel and plane-wave integrals here can be regularized by a positive Gaussian. Their limits are the ordinary Fourier delta and Fresnel integral with the displayed normalization, not unspecified projective equalities. ## 2. The three tetrahedral generators Use a,beta,c>0 with a+beta+c=1/2 for the charges, and write f_(a,c)(r)=exp(-pi i/12)psi_(c,beta)(r), K_(a,c)(x,y;u,v) =delta(x+y-u)f_(a,c)(v-y)exp[2pi i x(v-y)]. The Fourier and inversion identities in the pentagon audit give the following three exact kernel identities, where bars denote adjoints: integral Abar(v,s)K_(a,c)(x,s;u,t)A(t,y) dsdt =Kbar_(a,beta)(x,y;u,v), integral Abar(u,s)K_(a,c)(s,x;v,t)B(t,y) dsdt =Kbar_(beta,c)(x,y;u,v), integral Bbar(u,s)K_(a,c)(s,y;t,v)B(t,x) dsdt =Kbar_(a,beta)(x,y;u,v). (2.1) Here is a direct verification, including the possible convergence issue. Put r=v-y. In the first identity the two A delta functions set s=-v,t=-y. On x=u+v, its coefficient reduces to exp(-pi i/12)psi_(c,beta)(r)exp[pi i r(r+2u)]. In the second identity the A delta sets s=-u and the tetrahedron delta gives x=u+v. After shifting t by x, its remaining integral is precisely Fourier inversion of the Schwartz function psi_(a,c); its coefficient is the same expression with psi_(a,c) in place of psi_(c,beta). This integral is absolutely convergent. In the third identity the tetrahedron delta sets t=s+y. Its quadratic terms cancel and the last integral is integral exp[2pi i s(u+v-x)]ds=delta(u+v-x). With exp(-pi epsilon s^2) inserted, the left side is epsilon^(-1/2)exp[-pi(u+v-x)^2/epsilon], so the distributional limit has coefficient exactly 1. The remaining smooth coefficient is again the first displayed expression. The defining inversion and conjugation formula for psi identifies these three expressions with their claimed adjoint kernels. There is no extra phase in (2.1). These are precisely the adjacent tetrahedral vertex swaps (01),(12),(23). The charges transform respectively as (a,beta,c)->(a,c,beta), (beta,a,c), (a,c,beta). The first swap changes the first two vertices in its incident faces 2,3, so it uses A on both. The middle swap uses A on face 0 and B on face 3. The last uses B on faces 0,1. This identifies the operators with actual face vertex permutations. Section 1 makes their compositions coherent; their actions on opposite edge pairs and on face labels are the ordinary permutation actions of S_4. The identities for a negative tetrahedron are the adjoints of (2.1). ## 3. Gluing through these order changes For a face and its oppositely oriented copy, simultaneous changes of basis preserve the pairing. For an even permutation this is unitarity; for an odd one, the bra and ket are interchanged as well as conjugated. Internal face adapters therefore cancel. A non-order-preserving intermediate face gluing is represented by its unique S_3 adapter from Section 1, rather than being silently replaced by an increasing vertex map. For the proper contractions of the previous notes this cancellation has a direct regularized justification. A paired B and B^* integration gives integral exp(-pi epsilon x^2) B(x,t)Bbar(x,s) dx =exp[pi i(t^2-s^2)]epsilon^(-1/2) exp[-pi(t-s)^2/epsilon]. It tends to delta(t-s); paired A kernels give that delta directly. After the independent face constraints are eliminated, invertibility of the original full face matrix lets one use the N dynamical arguments and the adapter errors t-s as independent coordinates. The dynamical functions are Schwartz, and the errors have normalized Gaussian weights. Rescale each error by sqrt(epsilon). Translations of the dynamical coordinates preserve their L1 norms, and their Schwartz bounds justify dominated convergence. Quadratic chirps have modulus one. The same argument applies to the plane-wave delta in the third rule (2.1). Thus changing face frames inside a finite proper contraction preserves its value, with these prescribed limits. This argument does not claim that an arbitrary trace of a bounded operator is trace class. Properness and the explicit Gaussian resolution supply the needed finite-dimensional justification here. One may consequently put a positive bipyramid into the canonical pentagon ordering, apply the audited identity, and return to the desired boundary orders. When both endpoint face contractions are proper, this gives their tensor identity with its retained pentagon scalar. It is unnecessary to assume that the intermediate canonical vertex order extends to one global branching of the closed triangulation. ## 4. The actual figure-eight bipyramid Start with the p=0 even twist face family: U=(r,v,s,g), V=(s,g,e,u), W=(u,v,r,e), signs=(+,-,-). Its degree-three edge has local representatives U_02,V_03,W_02. The incident internal faces are v,g,e. Gluing only these faces, before any boundary identification, gives the following five-vertex bipyramid: | Tetrahedron | Global vertices at its local 0,1,2,3 | Canonical local order | Pentagon label | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | U | (1,0,3,4) | (1,0,2,3) | 2 | | V | (1,2,0,3) | (2,0,1,3) | 0 | | W | (1,2,3,4) | (0,1,2,3) | 4 | The apices are 1,3 and the equator vertices are 0,2,4. All three canonical signs are negative, so this is the *adjoint* pentagon, not the original all-positive operator word. The remaining boundary faces r,s,u retain their original vertex maps. Replace the three tetrahedra by canonical tetrahedra 1=(0,1,2,4) and 3=(0,2,3,4), sharing their equatorial face h. Their face tuples are (r,h,s,u), (u,r,h,s). To obtain increasing face maps, reorder their vertices by (0,1,3,2) and (0,3,1,2), respectively. The result is X_2: (r,h,u,s), (u,s,r,h), signs=(+,-). (4.1) The boundary maps, including the nontrivial intermediate one, are computed from the original pairings in the script. In the canonical ordering the u gluing has full permutation (3,1,2,0); its induced triangular permutation is a cyclic rotation. It must be carried by the corresponding V or V^2 adapter. The coherent triangle rules account for it exactly. After the two reorders above all four face maps are increasing. This is a 3–2 replacement of the embedded abstract ball before boundary pairing, so it identifies the same knot exterior. Optional Regina checks recognize (4.1) as the standard two-tetrahedron figure-eight triangulation; the homeomorphism argument does not rely on that finite recognition. ## 5. Full angle and peripheral transport Write the old physical triples as (a_U,b_U,c_U), and similarly for V,W. The old canonical charges are half the following angles divided by pi: a_0=b_V/(2pi), c_0=a_V/(2pi), a_2=a_U/(2pi), c_2=b_U/(2pi), a_4=a_W/(2pi), c_4=c_W/(2pi). The balanced edge equations give c_2=c_0+a_4+a_0+c_4. All five free charges are positive and 1/2-(a_0+a_2+a_4+c_0+c_4)=c_U/(2pi)>0. Thus the entire positive angle space lies in the convergent charged pentagon chamber; no continuation through a pole is being assumed. In the ordered triangulation (4.1), the new triples are a'_1=a_U+b_V, b'_1=a_V+a_W, c'_1=pi-a_U-b_V-a_V-a_W, a'_2=b_V+c_W, b'_2=a_U+a_W, c'_2=pi-a_U-a_W-b_V-c_W. (5.1) They are positive, and both new edge weights are 2pi. The new face and peripheral matrices are exactly Q_f=diag(1,-1), H=diag(1/2,-1), A=[[1,-2],[0,4]], B=[[-1,-1],[0,2]], nu/pi=(-1,2), c_0/pi=(1,-1), p=(-1,1). Here the standard peripheral holonomies are mu_2=a'_1-a'_2, lambda_2=2(a'_2-b'_2). Pulling back (5.1) gives, on the entire old balanced angle space, mu_2=-mu_3, lambda_2=-lambda_3. (5.2) The old meridian and preferred longitude are independently certified in the topological note. The bipyramid homeomorphism transports them; cusp angle holonomy is preserved by the corresponding diagonal changes on its vertex links. Identity (5.2), with zero constant branch correction, records the resulting orientation convention. Matching the old curves therefore uses the negative of the displayed new longitude row, giving p=(1,-1) and the same c_0=(pi,-pi). This reverses the fiber variable and changes the printed prefactor: the matched state is -J_2(h,-x). ## 6. The exact phase certificate and state identity Use K_X from the peripheral-phase note. The adjoint pentagon multiplier is exp(i rho/h), where rho=pi P/12, P=(a_V+a_U+c_W)/pi-1/2. Direct substitution of (5.1) into the two K polynomials gives K_2-K_3+rho=11pi/12. (6.1) This identity holds for every balanced angle vector. In particular its longitude slope is zero. The script checks all coefficients on the four-dimensional affine angle space, not one special geometric point. For matched peripheral orientations the two coarea orientation signs are both -1, and N_2-N_3=-1. Applying the exact transform formula and its uniqueness theorem consequently gives J_3(h,x)=-exp[-pi i/12+11pi i/(12h)]J_2(h,-x). (6.2) Here J_3,J_2 are the literal printed FAMED states with the chosen eliminated coordinates: U for J_3 and the first tetrahedron for J_2. Use the increasing lexicographic face-label orders of the scripts; the corresponding face determinants are +1 and -1. Their p_1^2 factors are both 1. The equality is on their common horizontal holomorphic band around the complete meridian. Positive angle chambers overlap under (5.1), so the Fourier–Laplace comparison has an open longitude interval and requires no extrapolation from a complete-point test. ## 7. Reflection and the same selected minimal operator There is also an orientation-preserving automorphism of (4.1): interchange its two tetrahedra, with vertex maps (1,3,0,2), (2,0,3,1). These commute with every actual face pairing. Their induced angle map interchanges the tetrahedra and swaps a,b in each. The peripheral action is (mu,lambda)->(-mu,-lambda), and direct substitution on the full balanced angle space gives K(alpha')=K(alpha). Tetrahedral equivariance and the same transform uniqueness therefore show J_2(h,x)=J_2(h,-x). (7.1) Thus (6.2) is also an exact scalar equivalence at the same boundary x. Both the reflection and its scalar normalization were proved for the selected integrals, not inferred from a reciprocal classical A-polynomial. For clarity the known minimal order-two operator of J_2, in the natural Andersen–Malusà b-shift convention, has coefficients R=q^4 Q^4-q^3 Q^3-q(q^2+1)Q^2-qQ+1, b_0=q^2 Q^2(q^3 Q^2-1), b_1=q^(1/2)(q^2 Q^2-1)R, b_2=q^3 Q^2(q Q^2-1). The previous Ore and minimality proofs concern this same literature state after its recorded scalar gauge. Reflection sends (Q,E) to (Q^(-1),E^(-1)). Left multiplication by E^2 returns nonnegative shift degrees; its exact coefficient identity is b_(2-k)(q^(-2)Q^(-1))=-q^(-6)Q^(-6)b_k(Q), k=0,1,2. Only this Laurent monomial unit is removed. All nonmonomial peripheral factors, including those vanishing at the complete value, remain. Equation (6.2) now proves that the three- and two-tetrahedron states have the same primitive minimal operator and the same volume law. No colored Jones polynomial or arbitrarily chosen recurrence solution enters this comparison. ## 8. Checks and remaining scope Run `.venv/bin/python experiments/audit_figure_eight_move.py --regina` for the exact combinatorial, entire-angle-space, phase, reflection and operator certificates and the optional independent triangulation recognition. Without Regina use `python3 experiments/audit_figure_eight_move.py`. The independent integral comparison is in `python3 experiments/compare_figure_eight_realizations.py`. The latter compares four generic/complete boundary cases at two b values, using tensor Hermite orders 256 and 384. Its maximum relative discrepancy from (6.2) is below 1.2e-12, with refinement difference below 3.3e-10. It also checks the evenness (7.1) independently. These are numerical diagnostics of the separately proved identities. The argument audits the ordering changes needed in this concrete positive move and provides reusable local rules for other proper positive moves. Together with the endpoint moment theorem in the peripheral-phase note, these rules give selected-state annihilator invariance along certified proper positive paths between compatible geometric endpoints. It does not supply connecting paths for arbitrary triangulations, justify every nonproper contraction, or prove geometric FAMED certificates for all alternating knots. The positive factorial comparison model still needs its own generic boundary move law; its factor-eight test is not resolved by a different model's calibrated identity.

title: One extra quantum region degree, with an exact original crossing port
text: # One extra quantum region degree, with an exact original crossing port 28 October 2026. The third classical certificate changes the region flag in the literal middle configuration. Its two projective coordinates do not form a quantum torus on the original two heads. This note constructs a genuine quantum-torus extension with one extra region degree whose **typed matrix elements** are exactly those physical coordinates. The extension has a fixed vacuum source. It also proves an exact vacuum-port formula for the other original crossing factor. A complete marked full-Phi pentagon can be applied BEFORE the auxiliary contraction; summing every intermediate index still gives that original factor and hence the original R. No knot value defines the auxiliary source. The complete developed geometric face-order table for the third certificate is not inferred from these two facts. In particular, different matrix elements are not multiplied as though compression were an algebra homomorphism. The subsequent [physical THIRD theorem](literal_third_full_phi_certificate.md) now supplies that literal face/source certificate by a different construction on the original two heads: inverse actual flag transport and opposite-root FIRST, with its full reflected input adapter. It also explains the forced degenerate clock in this auxiliary vacuum port. The auxiliary identities below remain valid; they are not used as the missing regular geometric face table. ## 1. The actual third-region coordinates Use complete original heads and marks Q=exp(2pi*i/N), x=-q^(-1), k=x^N=(-1)^(N-1), Z=Z_1, Z_2, X=xS_2S_1^(-1), S_1^N=mu, S_2^N=k mu, XZ=QZX, XZ_2=Q^(-1)Z_2X, X^N=Z^N=Z_2^N=1. The actual total lowering current gives the normalized last region flag in the middle configuration's homogeneous frame as R=1-n_R, n_R=(1-Z_2)X=x f_2 S_1^(-1). (1) The root binomial product gives n_R^N=0, so R is a unit. Normalizing this new region to one changes the two projective coordinates to X'=Z_2X R^(-1), Z'=1-R(1-Z). (2) Their failure to satisfy X'Z'=QZ'X' cannot be repaired by renaming them as a new quantum-torus pair. We instead retain the missing face degree explicitly. ## 2. An honest extended quantum torus Add an auxiliary head with W|j>=Q^j|j>, S|j>=|j+1>, S|d>=k|0>, WS=QSW, W^N=1, S^N=k. It commutes with the physical heads. Put a=Z_2X and A=a tensor S^(-1), B=1 tensor W-Q^(-1)1 tensor WS+Z tensor S. (3) Then exactly AB=QBA, A^N=B^N=1. (4) For the commutator, A has quantum degree one against each of the three displayed summands of B. For the central powers, a^N=k and S^N=k give A^N=1. In the displayed order the three summands of B pairwise Q-commute. Their root binomial powers give 1-S^N+Z^NS^N=1. These calculations include even and composite levels. The face normalization has a periodic quantum lift. Define U_j=P(Q^j n_R)^(-1)P(n_R) =product_(r=0)^(j-1)(1-Q^r n_R), U=sum_(j=0)^d U_j tensor |j><j|, (5) where P is the original finite Euler polynomial. Every factor is invertible since n_R is nilpotent. Moreover U_0=1, U_1=R, U_N=1. (6) Thus there is no omitted auxiliary wrap or independently chosen norm root. Let Atilde=UAU^(-1), Btilde=UBU^(-1). Its typed matrix elements are <0|Atilde|1>=Z_2X R^(-1)=X', (<0|+<1|)Btilde|0>=1-R+RZ=Z'. (7) The Q^(-1) coefficient in (3) is essential: WS sends |0> to Q|1>, so its off-diagonal contribution in (7) is exactly -R. For every physical operator O, <0|U(O tensor 1)U^(-1)|0>=O. (8) Hence this controlled face extension can be inserted with its fixed vacuum without changing an original physical operator or any of its external source conventions. The ports in (7) have different incoming/outgoing types. When words are composed one must sum every intermediate auxiliary index. Equation (4) applies before that sum. It does not assert that multiplying the two entries in (7) preserves the same commutator after compression. ## 3. An explicit quantum triangle source The simple B in (3) is not an unspecified similarity. Set L=(1-Q ZW^(-1))S, C_B=P(L). (9) Then L^N=0, B=C_B W C_B^(-1), [A,C_B]=0, <0|C_B|0>=1. (10) Indeed L W=Q^(-1)WL and the finite Euler shift gives P(L)W P(L)^(-1)=W(1-Q^(-1)L)=B. The product around its clock orbit is proportional to 1-Z^N=0. Direct commutation gives [A,L]=0. The last identity follows because fewer than N raises from input zero cannot return to zero. Thus this source has fixed augmentation one, not a normalization chosen from a knot invariant. For h<N its complete input column is <h|C_B|0>=p_h(Z;Q^(-1))_h, p_h=(-1)^hQ^(h(h-1)/2)/F_h. (11) All factors and endpoint zeros in this column remain part of the source. ## 4. The other original R factor is an exact coherent vacuum port The original crossing has R_0=D P(n_-)P(n), n=(Q-Z^(-1))X=e_1S_2, n_-=-(Q-Z^(-1))a=-e_1Z_2S_2. Set a_eff=Q a Z^(-1), e_aux=(Q-W^(-1))S^(-1), n_0=a_eff e_aux. (12) The auxiliary e_aux is a unit scalar times the literal complete nilpotent raising/lowering matrix. Then exactly P(n_-)=<0|P(n_0)C_B|0>. (13) Here the whole intermediate auxiliary sum has been performed, not suppressed. For a finite proof, the original Euler coefficient cancels the h-fold lowering matrix coefficient to give <0|P(n_0)|h>=a_eff^h. Together with (11), the right side of (13) is sum_h p_h a_eff^h(Z;Q^(-1))_h. The actual physical relations aZ=QZa imply n_-^h=a_eff^h(Z;Q^(-1))_h, which proves (13) term by term. This is an exact all-level finite q-binomial bridge from a genuine auxiliary source to the original crossing factor. The polarization factor a_eff=QaZ^(-1) is forced by this calculation and is retained explicitly. Equation (13) can be conjugated by the U of (5) on the full extended space without changing its vacuum port, since U_0=1. Thus the same source extension contains both the actual third-region coordinate ports (7) and an original-R operator port. ## 5. A full marked pentagon before the complete auxiliary contraction Use the marked full-Phi clock on the auxiliary head, with its fixed scalar and top lift: F_W=phi_N diag_j[1/F_j], phi_N=sqrt(N)exp{i pi[1/4-(N+N^(-1))/12]}. Let P_0=P(n_0), H_0=P_0^(-1)WP_0, and F_H0=P_0^(-1)F_WP_0. Exactly as in the literal middle identity, since n_0W=QWn_0 and its missing arrow is the actual input zero, P_0 F_H0^(-1) =F_H0^(-1)P_0 P(-n_0H_0). (14) Inserting (14) into (13), while retaining its interface and source, gives the exact full physical factor P(n_-)=<0| U [F_H0^(-1)P_0P(-n_0H_0) F_H0 C_B] U^(-1)|0>. (15) Every intermediate auxiliary index in this product is summed. The source F_H0 C_B|0> is not replaced by a scalar vacuum. Its full-Phi scalar, both radial pieces and every finite boundary current are retained. Consequently substituting (15) for P(n_-) in the displayed R_0 gives the ORIGINAL crossing as a matrix identity, before choosing a cut entry or a closing tangle. Its common Cartan/framing/peripheral line and the original cups and caps therefore remain unchanged. The factors phi_N in F_H0 and its inverse cancel because those exact interfaces occur on opposite sides in (15), not because a phase has been dropped. Each nilpotent Euler factor can be represented by its exact full-Psi circle/radial moment. The controlled operator (5) is likewise a ratio of two such finite Euler factors in n_RQ^(J_aux), with its inverse and vacuum edge fixed. Factorial conjugations reduce n_R to xS_1^(-1) tensor J_+ with unit coefficients; the joint physical/auxiliary clock similarly gives the single missing edge of L. Thus these are finite relative full-Phi kernels with their original coefficient sources, not bare functional substitutions. ## 6. What this proves and what still needs its face table The extra region degree resolves the actual failure of projective coordinate renaming: (7) comes from an honest extended quantum torus, with an explicit periodic source-preserving controlled transport. The same construction has a fixed coherent vacuum port for the actual second crossing factor, and its complete marked pentagon still gives that original factor after ALL auxiliary sums. This is stronger than a coordinate compression or an equality of unmarked generic kernels. The precise developed geometric face-order table linking the pentagon in (14) to all five third- certificate flags still must be checked. In particular A in (3) and the forced a_eff in (12) are different typed polarization coordinates; one cannot erase their QZ^(-1) relation. Nor can one replace products by products of the compressed entries (7). These are the remaining explicit face data, not a claim that the original operator or source comparison in (15) is conditional. No global selected cycle, geometric intersection degree or volume lower bound is asserted. ## 7. Exact audit Run python3 experiments/audit_third_region_quantum_face_extension.py The audit checks ten complete/wrap families through N=6 over exact prime fields. It verifies the extended torus and its centers, both coordinate ports, C_B's source augmentation and clock intertwiner, the complete physical port (13), the marked pentagon BEFORE auxiliary contraction, and the entire original R after (15), using the independent original E/Cartan crossing evaluator. It never multiplies compressed coordinates in place of the full auxiliary word.

title: Torsion rigidity of the initial form and a finite generic-rank certificate
text: # Torsion rigidity of the initial form and a finite generic-rank certificate Research note, 26 October 2026. A rational root-level knot state forces root-of-unity zeros of a fixed extremal coefficient polynomial. An elementary cyclotomic argument reduces these zeros, outside an explicit finite range, to finitely many binomial torsion curves contained in that polynomial. A unique occupied curve gives generic rational rank one at all sufficiently large levels. This extends the earlier pure-binomial initial-form test to an initial form with an arbitrary non-toric remainder. The argument is uniform and uses no knot census or asymptotic estimates. It supplies a finite sufficient condition for the operator-only line in [the ramified-fibre construction](ramified_weyl_fibre.md). It does not prove that every knot operator satisfies that condition, retain a geometric classical factor, or establish the regulator norm. ## 1. The initial rank bound, with the rational-coefficient scope fixed Let L=sum_j a_j(q,Y)T^j be a specified actual polynomial annihilator, T Y=q^2 Y T. In this note the cleared coefficients are in Q[q^(+/-1),Y^(+/-1)]. Such an actual operator is supplied by the [finite cut-state construction](finite_sum_annihilator.md), whose linear equations and finite products have rational coefficients. To pass from its M coordinate to Y=M^2, clear denominators and separate the even and odd parts of P(M) and P(-M); both annihilate the actual even state, and at least one is nonzero after the possible left unit M is removed. The fixed normal gauge Y-1 also has rational coefficients. These operations retain the specified state and all meridian factors. No claim is made that every minimal generator after extending constants to C has rational coefficients. Let r be the least Y exponent in its coefficient list, and set P(q,Z)=sum_j [Y^r]a_j(q,Y)*Z^j !=0. (1.1) Multiplying by an initial shift or a Laurent monomial allows polynomial notation; no meridian factor is discarded. At q_N=exp(pi*i/N), put Q_N=q_N^2, U=Y^N. The preceding [triangular-matrix proof](peripheral_normal_period.md#7-a-fixed-initial-form-bounds-the-rational-root-period-rank) gives, whenever the initial form specializes nontrivially, dim_(C(U)) ker L_N <=#{0<=k<N:P(q_N,Q_N^k)=0}. (1.2) Indeed the matrix of Y^(-r)L on 1,Y,...,Y^(N-1) is integral at U=0 and lower triangular modulo U, with these entries on its diagonal. The principal minor on the nonzero diagonal indices is nonzero. This proves (1.2), counting distinct roots, not multiplicity. The original state has a nonzero rational solution at every regular level, by its ordinary-color anchor. Thus the right side is at least one at those levels. We now control it using the fixed polynomial P. ## 2. An elementary root-of-unity lemma Suppose sum_(i=1)^h c_i eta_i=0 is a minimal vanishing relation, c_i in Q^*, eta_i roots of unity. Minimal means no proper nonempty subsum is zero. Then every ratio eta_i/eta_j has order dividing R_h=product_(primes p<=h) p. (2.1) Here is an independent proof of the needed form of Mann's lemma. Divide by eta_1 and let n be the least common multiple of the orders of the remaining roots. If p^nu exactly divides n, write the roots using a p^nu-th root rho and roots of order prime to p. If nu>=2, the extension from the cyclotomic field of order n/p to that of order n has degree p. Group the relation by the powers rho^j, 0<=j<p. Linear independence makes each grouped coefficient zero. Minimality forces all terms into one group. Their ratios then have order dividing n/p, a contradiction. Thus n is squarefree. If nu=1, the degree over the prime-to-p cyclotomic field is p-1. The sole relation between 1,rho,...,rho^(p-1) has all coefficients equal. If p>h, at least one group is empty, so all grouped coefficients must be zero. Minimality again forces one group and removes p from n, a contradiction. Hence each prime divisor of n is at most h. This proves (2.1), including p=2. The cyclotomic degrees used here are phi(n)/phi(n/p); no torsion-point theorem is a proof premise. ## 3. A finite list of candidate curves, with an effective exception bound Write the collected nonzero terms of P as P(q,Z)=sum_(i=1)^S c_i q^(a_i)Z^(b_i), c_i in Q^*. A monomial has no torus zeros, so assume S>=2 and put R=R_S. At a torsion zero (q,Z), partition the terms into minimal vanishing subrelations. Any pair in one such relation satisfies (q^(a_i-a_j) Z^(b_i-b_j))^R=1. (3.1) Thus all torsion zeros lie on a finite, explicitly specified list of binomial curves. For each support difference put g=gcd(|a_i-a_j|,|b_i-b_j|), (a,b)=((a_i-a_j)/g,(b_i-b_j)/g). Its candidate curves are C_(a,b,eta):q^a Z^b=eta, eta^(Rg)=1. (3.2) The exponent vector is primitive. Each such curve is irreducible over C. It is contained in P=0 exactly when its Laurent binomial divides P. This is a finite algebraic factor test, not an inference from a finite list of levels. ### Bounding the isolated exceptions Choose integers c,d with ad-bc=1. The curve has the parametrization q=eta^d t^(-b), Z=eta^(-c)t^a, t=q^c Z^d. If it is not contained in P=0, the substituted P is a nonzero Laurent polynomial in t over Q(eta). Its exponent width is at most W_(a,b)=max_i(-b*a_i+a*b_i)-min_i(-b*a_i+a*b_i). At an intersection, multiplying by a Laurent monomial gives a nonzero polynomial of degree at most W_(a,b). Width zero gives no intersection. If eta has order e, then [Q(q):Q] <= [Q(eta,t):Q] <= W_(a,b)*phi(e) <= W_(a,b)*phi(Rg). (3.3) Define E(P) to be the maximum of W_(a,b)*phi(Rg) over support pairs. Also let V(P) be the maximum Rg over the vertical pairs b=0, or zero if there are none. Contained vertical curves have q of order at most V(P). Therefore, if phi(2N)>E(P), 2N>V(P), (3.4) every zero P(q_N,Q_N^k)=0 belongs to a contained *nonvertical* curve from (3.2). Conversely every grid point on a contained curve is a zero. This proves the required classification beyond an explicit finite range. For a cruder bound stated using N alone, phi(n)^2>=n/2: in the prime factorization, each factor p^(a-2)(p-1)^2 is at least one, except the possible factor 1/2 from p=2,a=1. Hence phi(2N)>=sqrt(N), and N>max(E(P)^2,V(P)/2) suffices for (3.4). ## 4. Exact periodic counting, retaining the half-root Write a contained nonvertical curve as q^a Z^b=exp(2pi*i*h/t), gcd(h,t)=1, using h=0,t=1 for the root one. On the specified grid its equation is a+2bk = 2N*h/t mod 2N. (4.1) There are no roots unless t divides 2N. If it does, the count is gcd(|b|,N), if 2*gcd(|b|,N) divides 2N*h/t-a; 0, otherwise. (4.2) This follows by solving the elementary linear congruence in (4.1). The count is periodic in N, for example with period 2|b|t. It keeps the order-2N parameter q_N and the order-N parameter Q_N distinct. For instance Z=q has no grid points at any N, while Z=-q has one at odd N and none at even N. Dropping the half-root would lose this distinction. Distinct contained nonvertical curves have disjoint grid roots outside another explicit finite range. If their primitive exponent vectors have nonzero determinant Delta, their intersection gives q^Delta=eta^(b') eta'^(-b), so ord(q) divides |Delta|*lcm(ord(eta),ord(eta')). Parallel distinct curves are disjoint. Thus, outside a fixed range, the number in (1.2) is exactly the sum of (4.2) over the distinct contained curves. It is a computable periodic function of N. Multiplicities of the binomial factors do not enter this distinct-root count. ## 5. Consequences for actual operators First, a fixed P attached to an actual rational root period at infinitely many unbounded levels must contain a nonvertical binomial torsion curve. Otherwise (3.4) would rule out all such levels. An initial polynomial without such a factor cannot be the initial form of the specified all-level rational knot state. For an all-level state, the eventual periodic count in Section 4 must be nonzero on every residue class. This is a finite necessary test for a proposed rational-coefficient quantum operator. It does not require evaluating a growing root monodromy matrix. Second, suppose the only occupied contained curve at all sufficiently large N is Z=q^(2s), for a fixed integer s. Other contained curves with no grid points are harmless; arbitrary non-toric factors are allowed. Equations (1.2)--(4.2) give dim_(C(U)) ker L_N <=1. The actual nonzero state gives the opposite inequality. Hence dim_(C(U)) ker L_N=1 for all sufficiently large N. (5.1) More generally the same conclusion holds whenever the finite periodic count is exactly one. This is a finite sufficient generic-rank certificate, extending the pure-binomial test. If a primitive minimal actual operator B over C(q,Y) is a right factor of the certified L, then ker B_N is contained in ker L_N at the cofinite set where the factorization specializes. It also contains the actual state. Thus (5.1) proves generic rank one for B_N as well; no rational-constant-field descent of B is needed. This supplies the operator-only pointed saturated line of [the ramified Weyl fibre](ramified_weyl_fibre.md) for every actual operator meeting the finite certificate. It does not prove injectivity on its special negative sector or a bound on the complete period. ### A rigid comparison criterion once the common operator is constructed Suppose a second period is explicitly represented by a regular vector v'_N(U) in the same marked orbit lattice, satisfies B_N v'_N=0 and the same Weyl equivariance, and has the same ordinary anchor (v'_N(1))_1/(Q_N-1)=1. If (5.1) holds for B_N, linear algebra over the local fraction field gives v'_N=h(U)v_N. The first ordinary coordinate of v_N is a unit at U=1, so h is regular there and h(1)=1. Weyl equivariance makes h(U)=h(U^(-1)). Hence its germ is a unit in R_s with value one. On the descended special fibre (a'_0,b'_0)=(a_0,b_0). The complete functional therefore gives exactly the same full ADO value; no separate asymptotic comparison of those two vectors is needed. This argument permits analytic germs as well as algebraic ones, provided they extend in the specified lattice. The requirements are substantive: the second realization must be put in this same kernel and marked lattice with the same functional. An abstract unpointed module isomorphism does not supply them, as the ramified shear example shows. No geometric triangulation period satisfying these conditions has been constructed here. ### The condition is algebraically broad, with the scope kept explicit For fixed monomial support the candidate list (3.2) is finite. Containing any designated curve is a finite set of linear conditions on the coefficients, obtained by the substitution in Section 3. Requiring that none of the other occupied curves be contained removes a finite union of closed linear conditions. Where nonempty, the single-occupied-curve condition is therefore Zariski open relative to the family retaining the designated curve. This is a class of actual *operator certificates*, not a proof that all hyperbolic, adequate, or alternating knot operators lie in it. Establishing such a diagram-independent containment and the geometric regulator norm remains separate work. ## 6. An actual operator example with an isolated rank jump For the unknot normal state v_N=Y-1, let B=(Y-1)T-(q^2Y-1), C=1-q+T, L=C*B. These are actual all-level annihilators of that state. The initial form of L is (1-Z)(1-q+Z). The first factor is the persistent curve Z=1. The second is non-toric and has the grid zero Z=q^2 at q=exp(pi*i/3), N=3. At that level B maps Y to (1-Q)Y and C kills Y, so the kernel of L has the two independent vectors 1,Y. At the other levels C is invertible on the monomial root basis, and B has rank N-1 by (1.2) with initial form 1-Z. Indeed a grid zero of C would require |q-1|=1, which on q=exp(pi*i/N), N>=2, forces N=3. Thus the generic rational rank is two at N=3 and one otherwise. This illustrates why non-toric initial factors can create isolated exceptions but do not require a case-by-case large-level argument. It is an operator example for a known state, not a hyperbolic volume-conjecture counterexample or proof. ## 7. Coverage and verification Root-of-unity relations have existing coverage in Mann, [On linear relations between roots of unity](https://doi.org/10.1112/S0025579300005210), Mathematika 12 (1965), 107--117. The general torsion-coset framework also belongs to the established theory of algebraic tori. The coverage check used the publication metadata and scope, not its proof. Sections 2--4 provide the needed proof from elementary cyclotomic degrees, Laurent substitution, and congruences. No novelty is claimed for the general root-of-unity lemma or torsion classification. The application is the uniform finite rank test for the specified quantum operator and its marked period line. [The independent audit](../experiments/audit_torsion_initial_rank.py) uses polynomial division by Phi_(2N) over Q, rather than numerical roots, for 490 level cases. Its examples include persistent, sporadic, vertical, parity-dependent, and unoccupied cosets. The matrix test constructs the actual unknot annihilator above at 29 levels and detects its isolated rank jump. Its [results](../experiments/torsion_initial_rank_results.json) are diagnostics of the uniform algebraic proof. They contain no geometric period or volume estimate.

title: Where the geometric ideal triangulation enters the period comparison
text: # Where the geometric ideal triangulation enters the period comparison Research note, 26 October 2026. This answers the user's question about the role of the ideal triangulation theorem in identifying the source extension with the marked Bloch regulator. It gives the common geometric input, an exact local quantum/central calculation, and the precise comparison still required. No new definition of the knot invariant or identification with a geometric-character state is made. ## 1. What the audited triangulation theorem supplies The [independent Ge audit](ge_geometric_triangulation_audit.md), relative to the standard Epstein--Penner decomposition, supplies a complete positive geometric ideal triangulation T of every finite-volume cusped hyperbolic manifold. For the knot complement M, its tetrahedra have marked shapes z_j with Im(z_j)>0 and fundamental-class lift beta_T=sum_j [z_j], D(beta_T)=Vol(M). (1.1) Thus the geometric starting point is available without alternatingness. The edge equations and marked peripheral monomials give, in the conventions already audited, delta beta_T=-(1/2)m wedge l. (1.2) The complete positive point selects the volume embedding and orientation. This is precisely the lift that the boundary equation alone omits. On an augmented representation chart, develop each ideal vertex using the representation and its chosen peripheral eigenflag and take tetrahedral cross-ratios. The face identifications give the edge equations and peripheral holonomies as identities. Positivity at the complete point ensures nondegeneracy there and hence on a Zariski open neighborhood of that point. This realizes the geometric peripheral branch in the gluing coordinates, keeping the augmented cover when one is required. The five-term calculation in [the Bloch-lift note](bloch_lift_and_boundary_torsor.md) proves invariance under the oriented five-vertex chain relation. The [regulator note](boundary_regulator_period.md) gives dR=-(Log(m)dLog(l)-Log(l)dLog(m))/4, log||P_hyp||=2Vol(M)/pi. (1.3) The same triangulation therefore supplies both the geometric gluing branch of the peripheral A-curve and its marked regulator period. An existence theorem for positive shapes does not specify a quantum boundary vector or source cycle. ## 2. The exact local quantum calculation At a primitive n-th root omega, take the quantum torus X Y=omega Y X, and the tetrahedron relation (X+Y-1)v=0. The finite q-binomial expansion gives (X+Y)^n=X^n+Y^n. (2.1) For completeness, induction gives the ordered Gaussian-binomial coefficients. For 0<k<n their formula has a numerator 1-omega^n and only nonzero denominator factors 1-omega^r, 0<r<n. Those coefficients vanish even when n is composite. Hence (X^n+Y^n-1)v=0. (2.2) The root center has the ordinary tetrahedron equation s+t=1, s=X^n,t=Y^n. This is an exact algebraic statement. It does not require a semiclassical estimate or an assumed quantum-Frobenius theorem for an arbitrary A-operator. Since the equation is central, it annihilates the whole cyclic tetrahedron module generated by v. Here n is the order of the tetrahedral quantum-torus parameter. The actual ADO parameter q_N has order 2N, while tetrahedron conventions often use omega=q_N^2 of order N. A comparison must convert these parameters and the full peripheral monomial lattice explicitly. This local equation alone does not fix that conversion or the factor in the regulator action. The monomial phases can also be retained at every parity. Choose lambda with lambda^2=omega, lambda^n=(-1)^(n-1), W(a,b)=lambda^(-ab) X^a Y^b. Then direct commutation gives W(a,b)W(c,d)=lambda^(ad-bc)W(a+c,b+d), W(a,b)^n=(X^n)^a(Y^n)^b. (2.3) For several tetrahedra use the product convention. Isotropic integral edge vectors therefore give commuting edge operators, whose n-th powers are exactly the corresponding classical monomials. If an edge equation is W(e)=c_e, its central equation is the monomial=c_e^n. The full c_e, including its chosen roots and phases, remains part of the gluing data. Using z''=1-z^(-1) instead of 1-z also requires the sign in z''=-(1-z)/z. It belongs in the classical edge character and its specified quantum root. Equations (2.2)--(2.3) do not erase it. For the actual parameter omega=Q_N=q_N^2 there is a uniform compatible choice lambda=-q_N: lambda^2=Q_N and lambda^N=(-1)^(N-1). Its inverse is exactly the constant character kappa=-q_N^(-1) in the full ADO shift gauge. This records a compatible root convention at every parity; it is not by itself a comparison of the quantum states. Using lambda=q_N at odd N instead would change W(a,b)^N by (-1)^(ab), as the local audit detects. Concretely, start with the tensor product of the tetrahedron modules and form edge coinvariants by the images (W(e)-c_e)V. Use the centralizer of the edge operators for the descended action; it contains the marked peripheral operators. The central relation W(e)^n-c_e^n acts by zero on these coinvariants, by factoring it through W(e)-c_e. Their central support therefore satisfies the classical gluing constraints and maps into their peripheral elimination curve. Localizing at the chosen geometric component selects the branch represented by (1.1). This is a support statement; by itself it does not prove nonvanishing of the global reduction, equality of two annihilator ideals, or identification of their periods. The later [pointed tetrahedron gluing theorem](pointed_tetrahedron_gluing.md) does establish nonvanishing of the root reduction for S^3 knot exteriors: its saturated boundary module has dimension N at every level, including even N. Integral edge primitivity and strict shape-ordering maps remove a global branching requirement for this module construction. The later [integral half-longitude theorem](integral_half_longitude.md) identifies its saturated boundary lattice using the marked meridian and half the preferred longitude. This gives TY=q^2 YT without dividing by two modulo an even level. Its scalar lift retains the edge character and the actual central longitude. The projected generator's actual ADO period and regulator norm are not identified by these module and lattice statements. ## 3. Why the affine source is useful here After converting to one quantum-parameter and peripheral-lattice convention, suppose the geometric gluing module is the homogeneous block C of an actual source extension sigma(v)=C v+c, U=[C c;0 1]. At a root its augmented monodromy is [H s;0 1], so exactly det(V-U_cyc)=(V-1)det(V-H). (3.1) The actual rational ADO period has a V=1 sector. The geometric block need not: if I-H is invertible, its source-normalized period is (I-H)^(-1)s, as proved in [the affine extension note](affine_quantum_a_period.md). Thus the geometric block and the rational period can belong to one extension without being the same unpointed homogeneous module. This avoids a literal identification that is generically impossible. The proposed uniform twist formula and its missing determinant map are stated explicitly. This is a concrete source/determinant step in the actual A-torsor construction. The selected global source still needs to be pushed to that residue with its norm controlled across levels. The original volume conjecture is not inferred from the local formula. ## 35. Every bridge can be reduced, with arbitrary bridge number The [arbitrary-plat reduction](arbitrary_bridge_source_reduction.md) now gives a uniform replacement for the twist relator. For every 2k-plat and every crossing word, exact scheme substitutions remove all intermediate transport variables. Its endpoint complex is 0 -> sl_2 -> T(O^k) -> direct_sum_i N_(A_i) -> sl_2 -> 0, dimensions (3,2k,2k,3). The two end maps retain conjugation and the three product dependencies. The explicit triangular chain equivalence carries every inhomogeneous crossing source forward, carries the dual affine constant, and has determinant one. It is valid before assuming endpoint acyclicity. At the complete hyperbolic point, the positive triangulation input gives acyclicity: a fixed-parabolic infinitesimal representation develops ideal vertices, its shapes have zero variation by the marked gluing Jacobian, and face propagation makes it conjugation. Thus this step applies to arbitrary bridge number, without alternatingness. The original finite quantum cut also admits a pointed plat expression by its already verified matrix turns, retaining all dual colors and the whole peripheral factor. The classical contraction is not yet a comparison of that full quantum affine extension with the geometric period. Establishing that comparison and its selected regulator norm remains necessary for the volume theorem. ## 36. Every quantum bridge has an explicit pointed source frame The [actual bridge-cap theorem](quantum_bridge_cap_source.md) now calculates the boundary input to Section 35 from the original matrices. In the balanced basis the left cap is x^a/N on a+b=N-1 and its cup is N x^(-a). The marked pivotal defect D=g^(-1)e satisfies D^2=0 and Tr(gD)=1; its cap is x^a/N^2 with the other index free. For every k-bridge plat, the exact turn normalization is 1/N. The boundary source is retained as (T-lambda)v=kappa(1-lambda^N)e_partial, with its polynomial resolvent and nonzero prescribed anchor on the norm-one divisor. The actual M->qM step exchanges bulk characters x^N and -x^N. An explicit three-channel flat system retains both and the source; an equivalent anchored rank-one norm torsor includes the final cyclic multiplier. The simultaneous construction and determinant characters are proved for arbitrary k, including all corner intersections. The principal cap symbols give inverse meridians, and the marked cap gives the original inverse peripheral flag. All boundary norms and fixed-order meridian jets grow polynomially at completeness, including the unchanged whole d_N germ. The remaining quantum issue concerns coupling through the crossing operator and transport to the marked geometric regulator period. The boundary calculation gives no lower bound on that selected matrix coefficient and does not prove its volume norm. ## 37. The selected A-period has a positive bounded-matrix formulation The [pointed A-Gram theorem](pointed_a_gram_period.md) now gives an exact polynomial-period expression for the actual norm, with arbitrary knot and bridge number. A fixed all-level annihilator and finitely many fixed-color jets determine a banded O(N)-size system. The jet budget retains every singular step; its nullity is uniformly bounded and its constant-color projection is unique. The selected norm is a ratio of two Gram polynomial coefficients, both nonnegative, and equals sum_(j=j_*)^N|C_j(q_N)|^2. After an explicit jet-lattice rescaling all matrix and source norms are uniformly bounded. Its interior characteristic polynomial is A_cl(M,L)^(B+1), up to the specified scalar Fourier factor, where A_cl is the actual chosen quantum operator's classical symbol. No identification of that symbol with A_K is assumed. The same period is the derivative at zero of a positive quadratic regularization with the original source. This supplies a concrete quantum flow/response problem. Its exponential norm, and the comparison with the geometric A-curve's calibrated Bloch regulator, remain the required theorem. The exact identity does not establish that estimate or infer it from a bulk determinant alone. ## 38. A source-preserving one-sided growth estimate The [tempered leading-divisor theorem](tempered_a_growth_bound.md) now turns the exact finite-jet period into a fixed-size matrix transport with its actual source and coordinate effect. Its squared norm has an exact positive matrix evolution. Analytic unit-circle root branches with root-of-unity classical values make the complete leading-germ product have logarithmic rate equal to its circle mean, including exactly vanishing root factors. These hypotheses are stated explicitly, rather than assumed for every knot operator. A direct adapted-norm argument then proves a largest-root upper bound, allowing nonnormal matrices and eigenvalue collisions. The leading-edge root-of-unity property of the geometric A-factor follows independently from the recorded Bloch wedge by its explicit valuation residue; no published K-theory theorem is used for that deduction. This is one-sided. The actual unknot with an added growing left factor has zero selected rate despite a positive root-modulus integral. The figure-eight geometric polynomial has full-circle integral 2Vol, emphasizing the missing source selection. A matching selected action and lower estimate remain necessary for the original volume theorem. ## 39. Whole comparisons have a faithful cyclotomic jet test The [whole-period reconstruction theorem](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) now supplies a precise part of the user's functions-before-jets proposal. The positive complete optimizer is already a marked etale algebraic gluing place; its nilpotent shape lifts are unique. On the quantum side one must retain both v=q^N and w=M^N before taking jets. The root-only value v=-1 discards a nonzero normal derivative. Keeping t=1/N gives commuting logarithmic derivatives and an exact meridian shift sigma(w)=vw. Exponent separation and two Vandermonde matrices reconstruct a fixed bounded algebraic comparison from a uniform number of mixed quantum and meridian jets at finitely many levels. An algebraic norm extends the test to a marked shape cover. It tests the intertwiner, its inverse, sources, cuts and any specified period connection, once their fixed whole presentations are supplied. This is a reconstruction theorem for maps, not their existence and not a claim that algebraic shapes make the full period algebraic. The whole pointed source comparison and selected regulator norm remain the required theorem for the original volume conjecture.
