The subsequent [divisor-flow descent](cyclotomic_divisor_descent.md) constructs a fixed rational gauge from all-level cyclic norms for two stated rank-one divisor classes, including moving algebraic zeros with unramified nonresonant limiting values. Its support bound is derived rather than assumed for individual root gauges. An explicit half-root alias shows why the quantum parameter and normal directions matter. The even closed lift supplies a nonzero actual operator over Q=q^2 by the finite-sum proof, with its full ADO sign line retained. No generic comparison with the geometric period, or selected volume theorem, follows without its remaining source and norm hypotheses. ## 40. Whole source descent and the actual residue period The [full rank-one descent](full_rank_one_cyclotomic_descent.md) now treats arbitrary rational Q-coefficients, including ramified zeros and poles at Q=1. Whole cyclic norm identities force one generic rational gauge. Its weighted sequence argument also gives [additive and unipotent descent](additive_unipotent_cyclotomic_descent.md): vanishing whole cyclic source sums force rational source solutions, and a finite upper triangular filtration solves the entire transport. The Heisenberg central coordinate is included explicitly. The [actual Fourier--Mellin source](fourier_mellin_actual_source.md) constructs the nonzero generic affine source from fixed colors of the original state. Its selected root fiber is a whole rational function by [exact integral-color periodicity](cyclotomic_mellin_residue.md), and K_N=Res_infinity Z_N dX/X. This is an exact actual period, not an alternative positive model. The [principal-density comparison](quantum_source_bridge_extension.md) is now uniform for arbitrary knot braids on the regular critical locus. Its presentation parity is explicit and its normalized Gaussian/holonomy ratio is -1/2. For 4_1 the [whole selected source](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md) is proved at every level; direct evaluation of the original [Bloch class](figure_eight_bloch_specialization.md) gives its volume action, and the actual period has leading coefficient 3^(-1/4)N^(3/2) and first correction 11pi/(36sqrt(3)N). For the general target, these are separate established pieces. The remaining theorem must construct the actual quantum/geometric pointed comparison and prove its whole cyclotomic transport and selected regulator norm. The descent theorem solves that rational comparison once these identities hold; it does not infer them from the positive triangulation or from classical algebraicity alone. ## 41. Geometric support is proved before the last framing contraction The [partial geometric-support theorem](partial_geometric_support_theorem.md) now uses the actual normalized-average coefficient model, leaving two literal integer flow coordinates as external framing parameters. Its finite-array proof constructs a nonzero meridian operator. The same certificate acts on the nondegenerate transverse formal Gaussian, so its first nonzero classical symbol contains A_geo. The proof retains both framing directions and their source; it does not invoke a shift-invariant functional on their unresolved relative period. The [independent audit](partial_geometric_support_independent_audit.md) checks this precise scope. The [actual Newton transform](newton_actual_source_canonical_transform.md) also gives a generic coefficient recurrence and exact selected whole-germ period from finite actual pointing. In its classical chart the [geometric resolution](newton_resolution_and_regulator_cut.md) turns completeness into a transverse stationary cut intersection, with u=(tau+1)/(tau-1), e=(1-tau^2)/4. The source's first normal factor N and the trace-to-trace factor N^2 are both explicit. The remaining theorem must preserve the geometric period through the last actual framing contraction and establish its selected regulator norm. No minimal scalar operator or volume conclusion is inferred from the proved partial support theorem. ## 42. The local quantum restrictions now have a whole functional lift The [Ward unfolding](unfolded_ward_factorial_and_regulator.md) reconstructs a unique rational-coefficient quantum factorial from the actual jets at all sufficiently large roots. Its logarithmic cyclotomic pole is -Li_2(z^N)/N^2, and its marked regular part is the normalized cyclic gauge with its exact norm-root correction. Thus the local dilogarithm period is recovered from one whole function, rather than independently chosen levelwise primitives. On a genuine moving complete-color tensor representation, the same pole evaluates to exp[(-t)^N J_b/N], with J_b^b=0. The [fusion theorem](divided_ward_factorial_fusion.md) proves its associative block transport, including every even-level character. The [norm-root group transfer](cyclic_ward_norm_root_period.md) also carries the marked peripheral path and evaluates its period as Log(M^2)/(M-M^(-1)), with the full N/u_N adapter. The [divided-adjoint source](divided_adjoint_marked_edge_pairing.md) realizes the literal original knot cut by an exact normalized missing-edge insertion. Its generic pivotal naturality and ordered tensor insertion are proved. The [complete-color calculation](complete_color_divided_ward_and_fusion.md) retains the distinct q and meridian normals and the pivot/twist moments between those routes. These local function and source transfers do not yet construct the final geometric pushforward. The [independent audits](divided_ward_bridge_independent_audit.md) verify these formulas, while the [global function/source audit](global_period_rigidity_function_audit.md) distinguishes their exact local rigidity from the still-required selected geometric period and its archimedean norm.

title: Uniform face, angle and quantum-state certificates for the twist families
text:
# Uniform face, angle and quantum-state certificates for the twist families Research note, 25 October 2026. This note reconstructs the geometric and finite matrix arguments for the explicit face families used in the literature. The quantum asymptotic and annihilator arguments are in `literature_state_volume.md` and `general_annihilator_and_volume.md`. Source conventions are Ben Aribi–Guéritaud–Piguet-Nakazawa, *Geometric triangulations and the Teichmüller TQFT volume conjecture for twist knots*, [arXiv:1903.09480v5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1903.09480v5), especially Sections 4, 5 and 8; and the later FAMED definition and integral (4.5) in [arXiv:2410.10776v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.10776v2). We do not use their geometricity or asymptotic theorem as a black box. The face pairings, the geometry of their angle maximum, and the Gaussian/edge identity below are explicit. The subsequent [topological and peripheral audit](twist_topology_and_peripherals.md) reconstructs their identification with the twist diagrams and independently certifies the meridian and preferred longitude. Global quantum move identities remain separate work; this qualification remains part of the scope of the final triangulation-independent knot theorem. All semiclassical limits are for each fixed p. The constants and strip gaps may depend on p; no simultaneous p->infinity, b->0 estimate is asserted. ## 1. The two ordered face families Let p>=0. There are p+3 tetrahedra T_1,...,T_p,U,V,W and 2p+6 faces e_1,...,e_(p+1), f_1,...,f_p, v,r,s,g,u. Set f_0=e_1. A tuple lists faces opposite the ordered vertices 0,1,2,3. Pair equal face labels by the order-preserving map on their three vertices. | Tetrahedron | Odd family | Even family | | --- | --- | --- | | T_j | (e_j,e_(j+1),f_j,f_(j-1)) | same | | U | (r,v,s,g) | same | | V | (g,s,f_p,u) | (s,g,f_p,u) | | W | (u,r,v,e_(p+1)) | (u,v,r,e_(p+1)) | The signs are (+,...,+,-,-,-) in the odd family and (+,...,+,+,-,-) in the even family. The literature identifies these with X_(2p+3) and X_(2p+2), respectively. The p=0 even member is the three-tetrahedron subdivision of the figure-eight decomposition; the p=0 odd member is the three-tetrahedron 5_2 example. An edge angle a is attached to 01 and 23, b to 02 and 13, and c to 03 and 12. Following the face pairings gives the chain weights c_(j-1)+2b_j+c_(j+1), 1<=j=1: s: 2a_U+b_V+c_V+a_W+b_W, 0: 2a_1+c_1+2a_2+...+2a_p+a_V+c_W. Odd family: p: c_(p-1)+2b_p+b_U+b_V+a_W, p+1: c_p+b_U+2c_U+a_V+c_V+b_W+c_W. Even family: p: c_(p-1)+2b_p+b_U+2c_U+a_V+b_V+a_W+c_W, p+1: c_p+b_U+c_V+b_W. Each weight is 2pi. Their sum is twice the sum of all tetrahedral angles, so one edge equation is redundant. The chains above can be checked directly by crossing each face with the two endpoints of the local edge. Every one of the 6(p+3) edge occurrences appears once in this list. The same local crossing rule gives the p=0 matrices recorded in Section 5 below. The executable face construction in `experiments/twist_family_certificates.py` does the edge identifications from the vertex maps, rather than using the listed weights as an input. It also checks the oriented face gluings, one ideal vertex, and the Euler characteristic zero of its link in finite examples. For the uniform geometric argument, a connected torus link is the topological input supplied by this ordered face family; the edge cycles and orientation can also be followed inductively along the chain. ## 2. A positive angle structure for every p Angles in the following formulas have their usual radian units. For p>=1 set epsilon=pi/[12(p+1)^2]. For j

=1 the reduced odd endpoint constraints are c_(p-1)+2b_p+3B=2pi, c_p+A+3C=pi, and the reduced even endpoint constraints are c_(p-1)+2b_p+A+3C=pi, c_p+3B=2pi. In both cases the earlier chain equations remain, and c_0=0. These reductions follow by substitution in the full edge weights; the redundant 0 equation then holds automatically. ### 3.3 Odd family At a symmetric maximum, c_p=pi would imply A=C=0, B=pi, contradicting the first endpoint constraint. If c_p=0, the convex nonnegative sequence (0,c_1,...,c_p) is identically zero, because c_(j-1)-2c_j+c_(j+1)=2a_j>=0, j0 by forward induction, starting from b_1=pi-c_2/2>=pi/2. Descending induction then gives b_j0, and each following step uses positivity of the next tetrahedron. By Section 3.1 every chain tetrahedron is positive. For p=1 the chain inductions are empty and the endpoint argument is unchanged. For p=0 the reduced condition is A+3C=pi. Its interior contains positive triples. Its boundary has either a flat non-taut triple or zero total volume, so its maximum is interior as well. ### 3.4 Even family The second endpoint equation gives B=(2pi-c_p)/3 in [pi/3,2pi/3]. Thus U is positive by Section 3.1. The chain forward induction gives b_j>0 for j0. For p=1 the same c_p=0 contradiction follows directly from the endpoints. Thus the only remaining possible flat tetrahedron is (a_p,b_p,c_p)=(0,0,pi). Suppose this occurs. Write r=c_(p-1), or r=0 if p=1. The endpoint equations give U=((pi+r)/2, pi/3, pi/6-r/2), 0<=r=2 perturb the last two chain triples and U by the following column increments, multiplied by small t>0: T_(p-1): (-1,+1,0), T_p: (+2,0,-2), U: (-1,+2/3,+1/3), and propagate the same aligned U change to V,W. These preserve every angle and edge equation. For p=1 omit the first increment. T_p stays flat and contributes zero volume on the path; all other affected tetrahedra remain positive. Direct differentiation gives exp(-V'(0+)) = [sin b_(p-1)/sin a_(p-1)] sin^2 B sin C / sin^3 A, (3.1) with the bracket absent for p=1. The chain equations and convexity give a_(p-1) in [pi/6,pi/2], so the bracket is at most 2. Also sin^2 B sin C/sin^3 A = (3/4) sin(pi/6-r/2)/cos^3(r/2) <=3/8. For the inequality, its logarithmic derivative in t=r/2 is -cot(pi/6-t)+3tan t<=0 on [0,pi/6). Therefore (3.1) is at most 3/4<1, or 3/8<1 for p=1. This gives V'(0+)>0, contradicting the maximum. The maximum is consequently positive in every tetrahedron. For p=0 the symmetric constraints reduce to B=2pi/3, A+C=pi/3. The strictly concave symmetric volume is maximized at A=C=pi/6, an interior point. ### 3.5 Why an interior maximum gives a complete hyperbolic metric Here is the needed direction of the usual Casson–Rivin argument, reconstructed from its multipliers. At an interior maximum on the full angle polytope, there are a multiplier lambda_T for each tetrahedron and mu_e for each global edge such that for opposite local edges e,e' carrying angle theta, -log(2sin theta)=lambda_T+mu_e+mu_e'. (3.2) This is ordinary linear algebra: the derivative is orthogonal to the kernel of the affine constraint matrix. Independence of all constraint rows is not required. Realize the unique positive ideal tetrahedron with each prescribed angle triple. At its ideal vertex v scale the Euclidean cusp triangle by exp(lambda_T+sum_(w!=v) mu_(vw)). Its side opposite the corner along vw then has length exp(mu_(va)+mu_(vb)-mu_(ab))/2, where v,a,b are the vertices of the face containing that side. This follows from (3.2) and the Euclidean sine rule. The expression depends only on the three global edges of that face. Hence it matches on paired faces. All cusp triangles therefore glue isometrically. Around a global edge their angles sum to 2pi, so the cusp surface has no cone singularities. The face isometries preserve these horosphere cuts; the possible dilation in the edge holonomy is consequently 1, while its rotation is 2pi. The tetrahedra glue to a nonsingular hyperbolic metric. The compact torus cusp section is flat and gives a complete cusp end. This proves a complete finite-volume metric, whose volume is the sum of the ideal tetrahedral volumes. This argument supplies positive complete geometric shapes without relying on a numerical maximizer or on the source's geometricity theorem. ## 4. The face Gaussian for every p, from elementary elimination Use the current FAMED spectral variables t_j,t_U,t_V,t_W, and the equations script-A f+script-B t=0, with script-B's lower block the tetrahedral sign matrix. The chain face equations give f_j=e_1-sum_(k<=j)t_k, e_(j+1)=e_j+f_j. The end equations force f_p=t_U in both parities, hence e_1=t_U+sum_k t_k, f_j=t_U+sum_(k>j)t_k, e_j=j t_U+sum_k min(j,k)t_k. Odd end solution: u=t_U-t_V, s=t_V-t_U, g=t_V-2t_U, v=(p+1)t_U+sum_k k t_k+t_W, r=(p+2)t_U+sum_k k t_k-t_V+t_W. Even end solution: u=s=t_U-t_V, g=2t_U-t_V, r=(p+1)t_U+sum_k k t_k+t_W, v=(p+2)t_U+sum_k k t_k-t_V+t_W. The homogeneous equations have only the zero solution, so script-A is invertible for every p, including p=0. The same elimination uses only unit pivots, so its determinant has absolute value 1. Taking the symmetric part of the selected x_0 face variables gives Q_f: (Q_f)_ij=min(i,j), (Q_f)_(iU)=i, (Q_f)_(iV)=(Q_f)_(iW)=0, 1<=i,j<=p, and the U,V,W block odd: [[p+2,-3/2,1],[-3/2,1,-1/2],[1,-1/2,0]], even: [[p+1, 1/2,1],[ 1/2,-1,-1/2],[1,-1/2,0]]. Thus G=-2Q_f+diag((epsilon+1)/2) is explicit. In the chain block G_ij=-2min(i,j)+delta_ij and G_(iU)=-2i. Its end blocks are odd: [[-2p-4,3,-2],[3,-2,1],[-2,1,0]], even: [[-2p-1,-1,-2],[-1,2,1],[-2,1,0]]. ## 5. Edge and peripheral matrices, with no assumed inverse formula At a positive tetrahedron the angles a,b,c correspond to z,z'',z'; at a negative one they correspond to z,z',z''. Convert the actual edge incidences accordingly to G_0,G',G'', and set A_edge=G_0-G', B_edge=G''-G'. Direct substitution of the displayed G in each chain and end row gives A_edge=B_edge G. The preferred-longitude rows used in the source, independently identified by normal curves and integral boundary certificates in the topological companion note, are odd: a_l=(...,2,-2,2), b_l=(...,0,2,2), even: a_l=(...,-2,4,2), b_l=(...,0,2,0). They too satisfy a_l=b_l G. Their branch constant is nu_l=2pi. For p>=1, take edge rows s,0,1,...,p-1,p+1 and this longitude row. In B they read s: -v_W, 0: -v_1+v_W, k: 2v_k-v_(k-1)-v_(k+1), 1<=k=0 are thus covered by explicit matrix certificates. For later exact normalization comparisons, the vector c/pi=B^(-1)(nu/pi)-G1 has chain entries i(2p-i+1), V entry -1, W entry 1, and U entry p^2+p+2 in the odd family or p^2+p+4 in the even family. Here each edge branch constant is 2-sum_j G'_ej, in units of pi. ## 6. Comparison with the older published twist-state formulas The FAMED state has all Phi factors in the numerator. Transform to the older spectral variables y'_j by z_j=-y'_j (chain), z_W=y'_W, odd: z_U=y'_U, z_V=y'_U+x_0, even: z_U=-y'_U, z_V=x_0-y'_U, where z here denotes *spectral integration coordinates*, not complex tetrahedron shapes, and x=2pi sqrt(hbar)x_0. Inverting the chain factors, and the U factor in the even case, uses the exact identity Phi_b(-y')=zeta_b exp(pi i y'^2)/Phi_b(y'), zeta_b=exp(i pi(b^2+b^(-2))/12). Consequently the exact FAMED integral equals C_X zeta_b^r/(2pi sqrt(hbar)) times J_derived(hbar,x_0), where r=p for odd parity and r=p+1 for even parity, and C_X is the explicit orientation constant of the chosen published fiber convention. Its absolute value is 1 in these unimodular face families. No exponential factor of nonunit modulus has been dropped at the complete point. The reduced Gaussian on y'_1,...,y'_p,y'_U,y'_W has chain block min(i,j), chain-U entries -i in the odd case and +i in the even case, and U,W block odd: [[p,1/2],[1/2,0]], even: [[p+1,-1/2],[-1/2,0]]. The extra quadratic boundary term is odd: x_0(x_0-y'_U-y'_W), even: x_0(y'_U-y'_W-x_0). (6.1) The linear vector, divided by pi, has chain entries -i(2p-i+1), W entry 1, U entry p^2+p+1 in the odd case and -(p^2+p+3) in the even case, and the extra boundary term is -pi x_0/sqrt(hbar). These formulas follow by ordinary quadratic substitution using Sections 4–5. **A version-specific discrepancy.** In arXiv:1903.09480v5, the even theorem statement and its concluding state formula print the *odd* boundary quadratic x_0(x_0-y'_U-y'_W). The preceding derivation explicitly computes the even expression in (6.1). Our direct face-matrix calculation agrees with that derivation. The difference depends on the internal variable y'_U, so it is not an overall scalar peripheral factor. Both expressions agree at x_0=0, which is why this discrepancy does not change their complete-point volume limit. The exact generic-boundary definition used here is the later FAMED integral (4.5), retaining its own published convention. The final journal version has not been checked for this discrepancy. ## 7. What follows, and what remains to audit For every member of these explicit ordered face families, Sections 2–5 provide the positive complete geometric and finite matrix certificates required by the independent state-integral theorem. Thus its published FAMED state has the hyperbolic volume limit. In the Andersen–Malusà b-shift algebra acting on its explicitly rescaled spectral variable, it also has a nonzero annihilator and a primitive minimal operator, by the dimension-count and moment proof. The classical symbol contains the geometric peripheral curve with the stated lift and orientation conventions. At the complete boundary value, the older displayed twist states have the same limit because their exact ratio to the derived state is a unit-modulus phase times a power of sqrt(hbar). Therefore no arbitrary recurrence boundary condition or colored Jones sequence has been used. The subsequent topological note reconstructs the diagram-to-face-family construction and independently identifies the peripheral curves. It gives a three-arc marked-edge-germ certificate for the actual meridian, a ten-arc auxiliary curve, and an integral boundary certificate for the preferred longitude. Exact angle-constraint identities show that the longitude branch correction is zero in both parities. Thus these results apply to the stated literature realizations of the named twist knots. The exact global state transformations needed to identify arbitrary triangulations and the broader alternating-knot extension remain open. Run `python3 experiments/twist_family_certificates.py` for exact diagnostics on p=0,...,8 in both parities. They recompute edge classes, link counts, face matrices, positive angle equations, and the FAMED and peripheral matrix identities from the face tuples. The proofs above, rather than the finite sample, establish the displayed algebraic and angle statements for all p.

title: Twist-knot identification and exact peripheral certificates
text: # Twist-knot identification and exact peripheral certificates Research note, 25 October 2026. This supplements the uniform geometric and matrix proof in [twist_family_audit.md](twist_family_audit.md). The ordered face data come from Ben Aribi–Guéritaud–Piguet-Nakazawa, [arXiv:1903.09480v5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1903.09480v5), Figures 7–14 and 17–23. We reconstruct the local topological operations below. We do not use their identification of a preferred longitude, geometricity theorem, or quantum asymptotic theorem as premises. There are two different kinds of evidence here. The local constructions and the formulas with arbitrary p give the arguments for the whole family. The exact script and Regina recognition at the end are independent finite diagnostics of the transcribed data. Finite recognition alone would not establish an infinite-family knot identification. ## 1. Ordered triangulations and their marked extensions Use p>=0, f_0=e_1, and the face tuples and signs from Section 1 of the geometric note. In particular, T_j=(e_j,e_(j+1),f_j,f_(j-1)), U=(r,v,s,g), odd: V=(g,s,f_p,u), W=(u,r,v,e_(p+1)), even: V=(s,g,f_p,u), W=(u,v,r,e_(p+1)). Every face pairing maps the three vertices in increasing order. The ideal triangulation is denoted X_p. Its compact marked extension Y_p is obtained by adding Z=(m,m,s,s'), changing V's face 1 from s to s' in the odd case, or U's face 2 from s to s' in the even case. The marked knot edge is Z_23. Pairing the two m faces uses the full vertex permutation (01); it fixes 2 and 3. These conventions also cover p=0, without any chain tetrahedron. ### 1.1 Reconstruction from the twist diagram Let K_n be the twist knot with a two-crossing clasp and an alternating n-crossing twist region, with the mirror convention fixed by the oriented diagram in Figures 7 and 17 of the source. Thus odd: n=2p+3, even: n=2p+2. In particular K_2 is 4_1, K_3 is 5_2, and K_4 is 6_1. The parameter n is not the total crossing number of this reduced diagram: that number is n+2. Here is a reconstruction of the diagram-to-face-data argument. It is useful to distinguish actual local changes of a decomposition from any quantum move identity; only topology is involved in this subsection. 1. Put vertices at the middle of the diagram arcs, with one additional vertex on the clasp arc, and draw a quadrilateral around each crossing. The two knot arcs at that crossing are opposite edges of an embedded crossing tetrahedron. Replace this block by an interval: the two knot edges become its ends, while its four lateral edges become the interval. The local quotient has the same regular neighborhood as the original block, with the four exterior sectors in the same cyclic order. One can see this by shrinking transverse disk sections inside a collar and expanding the adjacent collar by the same amount. Reversing the operation expands the interval back to the crossing block and restores the two knot arcs. Thus the resulting quotient and its marked curve describe the same pair (S^3,K_n). The crossing information is retained in the cyclic attachment of the exterior sectors. 2. After these disjoint local replacements, the regions above and below the projection are two balls. Their boundary face pairs are D,E,m,r,s. The arrow identifications are read by following one sector of each crossing: successive arrows in the long twist region alternate. Glue the two balls along the disk E. The result is one ball with paired faces D,m,r,s and one surviving marked knot edge. This is a disk gluing of two balls, rather than an assumption about a face-pairing quotient. 3. The repeated reduction in the twist region is a disk cut and regluing. Split a paired face F into a residual face and a triangle; isolate the adjacent ball with two triangular faces and one bigon; rotate this ball and reglue it along the triangular disk; then merge the residual face with the bigon. Each operation has its inverse, and the rotating ball misses the marked knot edge. This proves preservation of the pair. The effect on the boundary is to replace two successive twist edges by one long edge and move the triangle u upward by one level. These are exactly the labeled attachments in source Figure 10. Repeat p times. 4. In the odd case the residual pair of (p+2)-gons G is triangulated by a fan. The successive layers have boundary face tuples (e_j,e_(j+1),f_j,f_(j-1)). The clasp region has four tetrahedra; reading the faces opposite 0,1,2,3 gives U=(r,v,s,g), V=(g,s',f_p,u), W=(u,r,v,e_(p+1)), Z=(m,m,s,s'). This reads the common triangular face at each layer, so it is unchanged when an additional level is added to the fan. For p=0 the fan is absent and the last two boundary faces have the common name f_0=e_1. 5. In the even case the same p disk reductions leave the opposite clasp attachment. Separate off the ball along the quadrilateral formed by the two adjacent G faces and change its diagonal. Both diagonals triangulate the same ball relative to its exterior boundary. The fan still has the preceding T_j tuples. Reading the residual clasp gives U=(r,v,s',g), V=(s,g,f_p,u), W=(u,v,r,e_(p+1)), Z=(m,m,s,s'). This is the diagonal change visible in source Figure 21. For p=0 the intervening bigon is collapsed in its collar, so the same tuples with f_0=e_1 apply. No negative or zero number of layers is used. All the face maps in this reading preserve the increasing order of their three vertices. The signs in the geometric note follow by orienting the ball and each tetrahedron. This gives a construction of Y_p as the marked pair (S^3,K_n), rather than an inference from its homology or from a finite list of recognized manifolds. ### 1.2 Why removing Z gives the knot complement The quotient of Z by its m pairing is a ball. Its unpaired faces 2 and 3 are two disks meeting along their common equator 01: in each disk the two radial sides have been identified. Their centers are 3 and 2 respectively. The edge 23 is the unknotted proper arc joining these centers. Removing a small neighborhood of that arc gives the product between the two punctured disks. Absorbing this product into a collar identifies the punctured disks. The equator vertices map 0->0, 1->1 and the centers map 3->2. Composing with the two external face maps gives precisely the increasing vertex map between the two s faces in X_p, in both parities. Thus drilling the marked edge and deflating this product gives X_p, with no change to the remaining tetrahedra. In particular X_p triangulates S^3 minus K_n. The same local description explains the topology of the cusp. The vertex link in Y_p is a sphere; deleting the two marked-edge germs and adjoining the tube around the open edge makes a torus. The computation in Section 3 uses this description to identify the meridian without a linking-number guess. ## 2. A separate uniform homology check Orient each dual face edge from its first to its second occurrence in the ordered tetrahedron list. A spanning tree in the dual graph is e_2,...,e_(p+1),r,s. After contracting it, the generators are e_1,f_1,...,f_p,v,g,u. All edge relations below are abelianized boundaries of the actual dual edge disks; each is determined by crossing the consecutive faces incident to the edge. For p>=1 put f_0=e_1. The relations, up to reversing individual disk orientations, are f_j-f_(j-1)=0 (1<=j<p), f_p-f_(p-1)-g+v=0, g-v-f_p=0, -v-g=0, sum_(j=1)^p f_j+u+2e_1=0. (2.1) These formulas hold in both parities. The first two relations involving f_p add to -f_(p-1)=0. Back substitution then gives e_1=f_1=...=f_(p-1)=0, v=-g, f_p=2g, u=-2g. Every elimination has a unit integral pivot. There is no remaining relation on g and no torsion; hence H_1(X_p;Z)=Z. For p=0 the three relations are -v-g=0, v-2e_1+u-g=0, v-g-e_1=0, and give v=-g,e_1=-2g,u=-2g, again with no relation on g. The single dual 1-chain g-s before tree contraction will be the meridian. Thus its class is the displayed generator, not a multiple of it. Homology by itself would not identify this class with the meridian of the knot; that requires the next local argument. The chain T_1,...,T_p by itself is also a useful diagnostic. For p>=1 it is a layered solid torus with top faces 1 and 2. If A is its boundary edge 01/23 and B is 02/13, their images in its H_1 are a and (p+1)a; edge 03 has image (p+2)a. For p=1 the two face relations give B=2A and 03=3A. Adding a layer leaves A unchanged, sends the new B to the previous 03, and sends the new 03 to A plus that previous 03. This proves the formulas inductively. Its meridian slope is (p+1)A-B and its three unoriented meridional cuts are (1,p+1,p+2). This solid-torus description does not assert that the fixed three-tetrahedron clasp piece is a two-cusped link exterior. ## 3. The actual meridian, from the marked edge A cusp normal walk is listed as (tetrahedron, vertex, exit face). The entry face is determined by the preceding step. Define odd: mu=((U,1,3),(V,2,1)), even: mu=((U,1,3),(V,2,0)). (3.1) Thus U_1 enters through s and leaves through g; V_2 returns through s. This is a simple two-arc curve. Its dual 1-chain is g-s. To verify that it is a meridian, lift it to the spherical vertex link of Y_p before drilling. Insert one arc in Z_1 at the s crossing. The resulting closed three-arc walks are odd: ((U,1,3),(V,2,1),(Z,1,2)), even: ((U,1,3),(V,2,0),(Z,1,3)). (3.2) They separate the two germs of the marked edge Z_23. Here is a constant-size certificate that can be checked directly from the face tuples. One side contains the three whole link triangles odd: U_3,W_3,Z_3, even: U_3,W_3,Z_2, and, in both parities, the following corner regions of the three cut triangles: U_1: corner 0; V_2: the region containing corners 0 and 1; Z_1: corner 0. There are thirteen local corners in this region: nine in whole triangles and four in the cut pieces. Each non-cut edge is matched within the region; its only boundary is (3.2). In the odd case it contains germ (Z,3;2) but not (Z,2;3); in the even case it contains (Z,2;3) but not (Z,3;2). All these triangles are in the fixed clasp block; no chain tetrahedron enters the certificate. On the sphere, the simple curve (3.2) therefore bounds a disk containing just one marked-edge germ. After the two germs are removed and the tube is attached, it is precisely a meridian. Deflation gives (3.1). This proves the meridian claim independently of the source cusp drawing. ## 4. A preferred longitude without a diagrammatic linking count The following auxiliary simple normal walks beta stay in the fixed clasp block. Each row is (tetrahedron, vertex, exit face), read cyclically: | Step | Odd beta | Even beta | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | (U,0,1) | (U,0,1) | | 2 | (W,0,1) | (W,0,2) | | 3 | (U,1,2) | (U,1,2) | | 4 | (V,2,3) | (V,2,3) | | 5 | (W,3,1) | (W,3,1) | | 6 | (U,3,2) | (U,3,2) | | 7 | (V,3,0) | (V,3,1) | | 8 | (U,2,0) | (U,2,0) | | 9 | (W,2,0) | (W,1,0) | | 10 | (V,1,0) | (V,0,1) | The cusp is oriented by the oriented complement. Direct normal-arc intersection gives mu . beta = +1 (odd), -1 (even). (4.1) For an entirely rational check, place the vertices of each cusp triangle at (0,0),(1,0),(0,1) in increasing order. Put mu's endpoints one-third of the way along each side and beta's endpoints two-thirds of the way along it. The increasing face maps match these positions across triangles. Count the transverse interior segment intersections with triangle orientation -epsilon_t(-1)^v. This evaluates (4.1) using only the two triangles visited by mu. It also avoids coincident-arc conventions. Their dual face chains are odd: [beta]=-r+v+2s-2g, even: [beta]=2s-2g. Using (2.1), beta has homology class -3[mu] in the odd case and -2[mu] in the even case. Define on the peripheral torus odd: lambda=beta+3mu, even: lambda=beta+2mu. (4.2) There is a direct integral boundary certificate, with no division or specialization. The dual disk at U_01 has oriented face word s u v^(-1) r u^(-1) g^(-1) in the odd case. Its abelian boundary is s-v+r-g. Consequently the odd lambda chain -r+v-s+g is minus this boundary. In the even case lambda's dual chain is already zero. Thus both classes in (4.2) are null-homologous in the complement. Equation (4.1) makes each lambda primitive. Since mu is the actual meridian, these are preferred longitudes, with the orientation specified by (4.1). This argument replaces a crossing-sign linking count. ## 5. Angular branches and the exact longitude rows Let a,b,c be the local edge angles, in radians, assigned to opposite edge pairs 01/23,02/13,03/12. For a normal arc at (t,v) entering face i and leaving face j, let k be the unused vertex. Its signed corner-angle contribution is epsilon_t (-1)^v sign((i,j,k) relative to the sorted other vertices) times the angle at edge vk. (5.1) This follows by orienting the vertex link triangle and following its oriented incoming and outgoing sides. It fixes the signs rather than assigning an unsigned sum to a normal walk. Applying it gives h_mu = a_U-a_V (odd), h_mu = a_V-a_U (even), h_beta = -b_U-c_U-a_V-b_V+c_V+2a_W+c_W (odd), h_beta = a_V-b_V+c_V+a_W-b_W-c_W (even). Put T_t=a_t+b_t+c_t and let omega_s=2a_U+b_V+c_V+a_W+b_W. The target longitude formulas are h_lambda=2(a_U-a_V+c_V-b_W) (odd), h_lambda=2(-a_U+a_V-b_V+a_W) (even). (5.2) These follow from (4.2) with exact constraint certificates: odd: (5.2)-(h_beta+3h_mu)=T_U+2T_V-T_W-omega_s, even: (5.2)-(h_beta+2h_mu)=-T_V+T_W. On the balanced angle space T_t=pi and omega_s=2pi, both right sides are exactly zero. In particular no unnoticed multiple of 2pi is needed to match the source formula. This is stronger than equality modulo angular holonomy. For the shape convention in the geometric note, a,b,c correspond to z,z'',z' at positive tetrahedra and z,z',z'' at negative ones. Using T_W=pi in the odd case and T_V=pi in the even case converts (5.2) to h_lambda=a_l Arg z+b_l Arg z''-2pi, with chain entries zero and the U,V,W rows odd: a_l=(2,-2,2), b_l=(0,2,2), even: a_l=(-2,4,2), b_l=(0,2,0). (5.3) Thus the longitude rows and the branch constant nu_l=2pi used in the geometric and Gaussian certificates are now independently identified. The natural spectral boundary coordinate x=y_V-y_U has angular meridian a_U-a_V in both parities. It reverses mu in the even case; its intersection with the chosen preferred longitude is consequently +1 in both cases. ## 6. Consequence and the remaining scope For every fixed p>=0 in both parities, the uniform topological identification, the independently identified peripheral rows, and the geometric certificates in the companion note apply to the same literature integral. Therefore the state defined by FAMED equation (4.5), with the explicit spectral rescaling and b-shift convention in [general_annihilator_and_volume.md](general_annihilator_and_volume.md), has a primitive minimal boundary annihilator and satisfies lim_(b->0+) -2pi hbar log|J_(X_p)(hbar,0)| = Vol(S^3 minus K_n), hbar=b^2/(1+b^2)^2. (6.1) Its classical symbol contains the geometric peripheral component in the recorded eigenvalue-ratio/lift convention. The limiting state normalization is fixed by the literature integral. This is a statement for these explicit literature realizations. The identification of all triangulations or all purported standard knot states requires the global quantum transformations with their generic peripheral factors and contours. It does not follow from the topological disk operations used in Section 1. No equality of the entire classical symbol with the full A-polynomial is inferred here. The all-alternating-knot extension also remains open in this program; the positive geometric and matrix certificates have been supplied here for the twist families. A Menasco decomposition alone does not supply those certificates or an exact quantum move identity. Run the exact cellular and normal-curve checks with python3 experiments/twist_topology_audit.py and the optional independent 3-manifold recognition with .venv/bin/python experiments/twist_topology_audit.py --regina The latter uses Regina 7.4.1 and SymPy 1.14. It recognizes Y_p as S^3, checks X_p has one ideal torus cusp and H_1=Z, recognizes Z as a ball, and checks the layered-solid-torus cuts for p=1,...,8. Both modes check the eighteen cases p=0,...,8 in both parities against the uniform homology, marked-germ, intersection, integral-boundary and zero-branch certificates. The source figures specify the input drawings; the local reconstruction and the all-p certificates, rather than these finite checks, justify the family statement.

title: The compact source torsor and its actual Weyl gluing
text: # The compact source torsor and its actual Weyl gluing Research proof, 27 October 2026. The fixed compact source is a nontrivial cotangent torsor with an explicit Chern transition. The actual finite root module has a meridian-dependent Weyl adapter whose square is exactly the full modified-dimension function times its recorded scalar. The resulting order-two cocycle has a marked rational splitting at every level, including even levels. Quantum/dynamical Weyl operators have existing coverage; see the scope of [Etingof--Varchenko](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0011001). We use that reference for coverage, not a proof or a claim that its precise normalization equals the one below. The cotangent torsor is identified directly by its transition equations (1)--(2). The already proved [actual Weyl descent](actual_weyl_descent.md) gives state reciprocity. The new calculations identify the compact source transition and the explicit balanced-basis scalar cocycle with our full peripheral factor. These are source and gluing theorems. They do not identify the actual global geometric period or prove its volume norm. ## 1. An explicit twisted cotangent torsor Use the [compact source](compact_coherent_source_period.md) X=(P1 times P1) minus {s_0t_0+s_1t_1=0}, omega_0=dw wedge dz/(1+wz)^2. Project to the first P1. On its affine chart w define the fiber coordinate b=z/(1+wz). Each fiber is an affine line, including the value z=infinity when allowed. On the second chart put w'=1/w, b'=1/(w'+z). The exact overlap formulas are b'=w-w^2 b, dw' wedge db'=dw wedge db=omega_0. (1) In particular X is a torsor under the cotangent bundle O(-2), with the affine term w retained. For the local primitives lambda=-b dw, lambda'=-b' dw' one has d lambda=d lambda'=omega_0, lambda'-lambda=dlog w. (2) This is the connection torsor of O(1), in this explicit transition convention. It is not the split total cotangent bundle. On the marked real sphere z=bar(w), lambda is the Chern connection form -bar(w)dw/(1+|w|^2), and integral_Gamma omega_0=-2pi*i, integral_Gamma[-omega_0/(2pi*i)]=1. (3) Thus the sign agrees with c1(O(1))=1. Equation (2), rather than a globally defined primitive, records the nonzero source class. There is a useful obstruction to an incorrect global comparison. On a split framing chart with global tau and invertible A, Omega_cut=dtau wedge dlog A=d(tau dlog A) is exact. No globally regular map from X to this split chart can pull Omega_cut back to a nonzero multiple of omega_0 in cohomology: pullback preserves exactness and (3) forbids it. A nonzero whole comparison must retain a twisted transition, a divisor residue or its equivalent marked relative class. Equality of local two-forms does not supply that data. ## 2. The actual complete head patches globally Let N>=2, n=N-1, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2. At complete color M=1 identify the actual balanced head with H^0(P1,O(n)), by e_j=w^j. Its exact generators on this space are K=-(1/q)D_(Q^-1), Ecal=w^(-1)(D_(Q^-1)-1), F=w(1-QD_Q), D_Q f(w)=f(Qw). (4) The E numerator cancels at w=0. The F coefficient on w^n is 1-Q^(n+1)=1-Q^N=0, so all three preserve this finite section space. They are exactly the finite matrices, not an independent quantization. The line transition is f_infinity(u)=u^n f_zero(1/u), u=1/w. It transforms the shift to D_Q^(w) -> Q^n D_(Q^-1)^(u)=Q^(-1)D_(Q^-1)^(u). Consequently the generators in the second chart are (K,Ecal,F) -> (K_u^(-1),-F_u,-Ecal_u). (5) Equivalently let C e_j=e_(n-j). Direct matrix multiplication gives C K C=K^(-1), C Ecal C=-F, C F C=-Ecal. The original constant source vector, average co-source, and coupon e_ij=1/N are fixed by C. Thus the actual complete source has this exact Weyl gluing, not just a matching semiclassical two-form. The source level also has a precise half-form description: O(N-1)=O(N) tensor K_(P1)^(1/2), K_(P1)^(1/2)=O(-1), dim H^0(O(N-1))=N. (6) This is a bundle identity with the unique half-canonical line on P1. In the physical convention Omega_phys=2pi*i omega_0, h_N=2pi*i/N, its prequantum curvature is Omega_phys/h_N=N omega_0, with the Chern sign of (3). Thus the root level N and the actual section degree N-1 differ by this specified half-form factor. No limit is required for (4)--(6). ## 3. The balanced Weyl matrix at generic meridian Keep the actual root finite head with meridian M, and write K_M e_j=-(M/q)Q^(-j)e_j, E_M e_j=(M Q^(-j)-M^(-1))e_(j-1), j>0, E_M e_0=0, F e_j=(1-Q^(j+1))e_(j+1), j<n, F e_n=0. Here E_M is Ecal, not the unscaled Chevalley E. Put P_j=(Q;Q)_j, P_j(M^2)=(M^2 Q;Q)_j, D_M e_j=M^j P_j/P_j(M^2) e_j, W_M=D_M C. (7) Work on the marked open where the displayed denominators and numerators are units; in particular they are units near M=1. Then the actual generator comparison is W_M K_M W_M^(-1)=K_(M^-1)^(-1), W_M E_M W_M^(-1)=-F, W_M F W_M^(-1)=-E_(M^-1). (8) For E after reversing the basis, its raising coefficient is M Q^(j+1)-M^(-1). The adjacent ratio of D is D_(j+1)/D_j=M(1-Q^(j+1))/(1-M^2Q^(j+1)), giving -(1-Q^(j+1)). The F equation follows from the inverse ratio and 1-Q^(-j)=-Q^(-j)(1-Q^j). The K equation is immediate from Q^n=Q^(-1). This proves (8) including both endpoints. On full unrolled colors the same matrix sends H_M to -H_(M^-1), with the meridian lift alpha'=2n-alpha retained. Termwise substitution in the actual universal R therefore gives the Chevalley turnover with reversed tensor order. The original Cartan half-character, cups, caps and twist transform as in the generator proof of actual Weyl descent. This does not discard the stripped-Cartan multiplier recorded there. ## 4. The square is the full peripheral function Following each reversed basis vector twice gives W_(M^-1) W_M=c_N(M) I, c_N(M)=N M^(N-1)/S_N(M^2), S_N(Y)=1+Y+...+Y^(N-1). (9) For a direct proof the j-th diagonal product is D_(M^-1,j) D_(M,n-j). Using Q^(N-r)=Q^(-r) pairs its suffix factors and proves independence of j. At j=0 it is D_(M,n)=M^n (Q;Q)_n/(M^2Q;Q)_n =N M^n/S_N(M^2), since (Q;Q)_(N-1)=N and (M^2Q;Q)_(N-1)=S_N(M^2). This is exactly the already fixed full modified-dimension adapter: c_N(M)=(N/eta_N)d_N(M), eta_N=i^(N+3). (10) It is invariant under M inversion and has value one at M=1. Its whole meridian germ is not constant. On M=exp(u), c_N(exp u)=N sinh(u)/sinh(Nu) =1-(N^2-1)u^2/6+O(u^4). (11) Thus even where the ideal-point multiplier equals one, its peripheral normal data must not be reset. Formula (10) ties the Weyl cocycle to the specified period normalization, rather than an arbitrary projective scalar. ## 5. A marked rational splitting at odd and even levels The cocycle in (9) can be solved explicitly, with its divisors kept. For N=2m+1 put beta_N(M)=(M^2Q;Q)_m/(Q;Q)_m. For N=2m put beta_N(M)=[(1+iM)/(1+i)] (M^2Q;Q)_(m-1)/(Q;Q)_(m-1). (12) The specified i is in the root coefficient field at even N; its phase is retained. In both cases beta_N(1)=1 and beta_N(M) beta_N(M^(-1))=c_N(M)^(-1). (13) To prove this, pair Q^r with Q^(-r). For odd N all nonzero residues pair, and (Q;Q)_m^2=N(-1)^m Q^(m(m+1)/2). For even N the unpaired residue is Q^m=-1, so (Q;Q)_(m-1)^2=(N/2)(-1)^(m-1)Q^(m(m-1)/2). The remaining scalar norm is (1+iM)(1+i/M)/(1+i)^2=(1+M^2)/(2M), precisely the missing factor. These identities prove (13). Therefore Wtilde_M=beta_N(M) W_M, Wtilde_(M^-1) Wtilde_M=I. (14) This is a marked rational norm splitting, not a permission to omit c_N or beta_N from an exact comparison. Their zero/pole divisors are part of the integral source lattice. On the M=1 chart the splitting is regular and fixes the original complete source. ## 6. Relation to the remaining geometric boundary theorem The actual source now has an explicit cotangent-torsor cocycle, complete quantum chart gluing, and generic-meridian Weyl scalar whose norm and full modified-dimension role are known exactly. This solves the order-two source gluing problem on its stated charts, uniformly in the knot and level. Equations (7)--(14) are identities of whole meridian functions at the fixed quantum root. They do not assert the same finite-matrix relations off the root Q^N=1. A q-normal extension must retain the actual two-wall source and its corrections before differentiating. It does not assert that the standard polynomial SL2 action on H^0(O(N-1)) equals the actual quantum dressing of every geometric framing. The actual finite Weyl adapter (8) is proved; a general unipotent dressing and its source-normal comparison require their own derivation. Nor does (14) select which internal geometric stationary component contributes to the original period. The global regulator/selected-norm comparison remains to be proved. [Exact source and cocycle checks](../experiments/audit_twisted_source_weyl_gluing.py) and [results](../experiments/twisted_source_weyl_gluing_results.json) verify all three generator comparisons, the full scalar square and marked norm splitting in 78 actual root-module cases at N=2,...,14. They also check the cotangent transition and full peripheral germ. The [independent audit](twisted_source_weyl_independent_audit.md) confirms the proof, normalizations, phases and endpoints. The [geometric framing compactification](springer_centralizer_boundary_source.md) now produces this same twisted cotangent torsor by rescaling its centralizer coordinate. Its nonzero principal Gaussian residue is computed in [the explicit gauge calculation](compact_framing_gauge_and_boundary_residue.md). The physical selected-cycle comparison remains separate from that exceptional-divisor residue.

title: Independent audit of the twisted source and balanced Weyl cocycle
text: # Independent audit of the twisted source and balanced Weyl cocycle Audit, 27 October 2026. The proof in [twisted_cotangent_source_and_weyl_gluing.md](twisted_cotangent_source_and_weyl_gluing.md) passes this independent sign, scalar and endpoint check. No tests were rerun. The cotangent transition is \(b'=w-w^2b,\ w'=1/w\), so \(dw'\wedge db'=dw\wedge db\) and \(-b'dw'=-b\,dw+d\log w\). On the compact sphere the local primitive is the \(O(1)\) Chern connection, with curvature period \(-2\pi i\) and positive normalized class \(-\omega_0/(2\pi i)\). The complete finite section formulas preserve \(O(N-1)\), and its reciprocal coordinate change gives precisely \((K,E,F)\mapsto(K^{-1},-F,-E)\). The half-form bundle identity and its physical curvature scale also agree with these signs. For the generic meridian comparison, let \[ d_j(M)=M^j\frac{(Q;Q)_j}{(M^2Q;Q)_j},\qquad W_M=D_MC. \] After reversal the raising coefficient of \(E_M\) is \((M^2Q^{j+1}-1)/M\). Multiplication by \[ \frac{d_{j+1}}{d_j} =\frac{M(1-Q^{j+1})}{1-M^2Q^{j+1}} \] gives exactly \(-(1-Q^{j+1})\). The inverse ratio and \(1-Q^{-j}=-Q^{-j}(1-Q^j)\) give \(-E_{M^{-1}}\) for the other generator. The clock and both zero endpoint coefficients match too. At the unrolled level, \(\alpha'=2(N-1)-\alpha\) gives exactly \(H\mapsto-H'\); this is the retained lift, not merely an equality modulo \(2N\). The diagonal product of two Weyl matrices is \(d_j(M^{-1})d_{N-1-j}(M)\). Its ratio between consecutive \(j\)'s is one, so its scalar is its \(j=0\) value: \[ c_N(M)=\frac{N M^{N-1}}{S_N(M^2)}. \] Here the two full products are \((Q;Q)_{N-1}=N\) and \((M^2Q;Q)_{N-1}=S_N(M^2)\), with no phase missing. This is invariant under \(M\mapsto M^{-1}\), equals one at completeness, and has exactly \(N\sinh u/\sinh(Nu)\) as its whole \(M=e^u\) germ. The marked full dimension function therefore gives the printed \(c_N=(N/\eta_N)d_N\). For odd levels, pairing \(Q^r,Q^{-r}\) in the norm of the half product leaves \(S_N(M^2)/(NM^{N-1})\). For even levels the paired product omits \(1+M^2\), and the missing scalar is exactly \[ \frac{(1+iM)(1+i/M)}{(1+i)^2} =\frac{1+M^2}{2M}. \] The two printed factorial identities supply their respective factors \(N\) and \(N/2\). Thus both rational splittings satisfy \(\beta(M)\beta(M^{-1})=c_N(M)^{-1}\), including \(N=2\). For even \(N=2m\), the marked \(q^m=i\) places the chosen phase in the specified root coefficient field. Both splittings equal one at \(M=1\), where \(D_M=I\) and the original complete source is fixed by reversal. The result is an explicit splitting, not a uniqueness assertion: norm-one gauge changes can give other rational splittings. Its zero/pole divisors and its nonconstant meridian germs remain part of the source lattice. The note correctly retains these data and does not infer generic coupon invariance, an arbitrary unipotent dressing, a geometric stationary coefficient, or the volume norm from the order-two gluing alone.

title: A zero regulator anchor for every two-bridge component
text: # A zero regulator anchor for every two-bridge component 28 October 2026. For every two-bridge knot, all SL2(C) representations with meridian eigenvalue M=+i or -i have finite projective image and marked representation volume zero. The nonabelian character branches have finite limits there. Consequently the macroscopic source point x=1/2, M=-exp(pi i x), supplies a common ZERO geometric anchor for every genuine peripheral component of this class. This proves a geometric input for the whole-source transport problem. It does not identify an actual quantum operator with the peripheral curve or estimate its branch conversion. ## 1. The group relation forces a finite image Use a two-bridge presentation, p=2m+1 odd, G=<a,b | a w=w b>, w=b^(epsilon_1)a^(epsilon_2)... b^(epsilon_(2m-1))a^(epsilon_(2m)), epsilon_j in {+1,-1}. (1) The generators are the two bridge meridians; the signs encode the rational tangle. The argument below works for every sign word of this form which presents the knot, so it does not require a restriction on continued-fraction length or twist parameters. If rho(a) has eigenvalues i,-i, Cayley-Hamilton gives rho(a)^2=-I. The same is true of rho(b), since meridians are conjugate. In PSL2(C), write their images as A,B. Then A²=B²=1, and every sign in w disappears: A(BA)^m=(BA)^m B. (2) Set R=AB. Since BA=R^-1 and A R A=R^-1, (2) becomes R^m A=R^(-(m+1))A, hence R^p=1. (3) Every word in A,B reduces to R^j or R^j A. Thus the projective image has at most 2p elements. Its inverse image in SL2(C) has at most 4p elements. This applies to reducible representations as well as irreducible ones, and uses no unitarity assumption. The image is metabelian: its subgroup above <R> is cyclic (R^p=+/-I in a lift), and its commutator subgroup lies there. The preferred knot longitude lies in G'': choose a Seifert surface and express its boundary as a product of commutators of surface generators. Their push-offs have zero linking number with the knot, so each generator lies in G'. Hence rho(longitude)=I. (4) In particular all these midpoint peripheral points have L=1 in the original preferred-longitude eigenvalue convention. A changed framing must retain its meridian correction rather than reuse (4) unchanged. ## 2. The ABSOLUTE representation volume is zero A finite group of hyperbolic isometries fixes a point c in H3. One elementary construction is to sum its orbit of a future unit timelike vector in the hyperboloid model and normalize that timelike sum. Use the constant equivariant map c on a truncated core. On each cusp, choose a peripheral fixed ideal point xi and extend along the ray from c to xi, depending only on the cusp height. The ray is peripheral invariant because both endpoints are fixed. These choices extend equivariantly to all lifted cusps. Every cusp and its interpolating collar have rank at most one; the core has rank zero. The pullback of the hyperbolic volume form therefore vanishes everywhere. By the independently proved choice-independence of the [general peripheral volume](general_peripheral_representation_volume_bound.md), this is the SAME absolutely marked regulator used by the Bloch chain: R(rho)=Vol(rho)=0. (5) No additive shift of a primitive is used to arrange (5). ## 3. No character branch escapes at this meridian For an irreducible pair with M!=+/-1, put A_M=[M,1;0,M^-1], B_(M,z)=[M,0;-z,M^-1]. (6) To justify this form, choose the M-eigenline of the first meridian and the M^-1-eigenline of the second as the two coordinate lines. If they coincide the pair is reducible. Otherwise the first upper off-diagonal entry is nonzero for an irreducible pair and may be normalized to one. The remaining entry defines z. Let W be the word in (1). The top-right entry of A_M W-W B_(M,z) is P(M,z)=W_22+(M-M^-1)W_12. (7) It is a polynomial in z of degree m, with leading coefficient (-1)^m product_(j=1)^(2m) epsilon_j in {+1,-1}. (8) Here is a direct leading-term proof. Each pair B^epsilon A^delta has z-leading matrix -epsilon e_2 (M^delta,delta). Multiplying these rank-one matrices shows that W_22 has the coefficient (8), while W_12 has degree at most m-1. This proves (8), independently of M. Every actual irreducible representation satisfies P=0. On a compact M-neighborhood of +i or -i, the other coefficients are bounded Laurent polynomials in M. The elementary monic polynomial root bound then bounds z uniformly. Thus the matrices (6) have convergent subsequences at the midpoint and their limits still satisfy the full group relation. Their limits are the finite-image representations of Section 1. There is a stronger local check. At M=i, inverse meridians differ from positive meridians by -I, so W is a sign times (BA)^m. Put t=tr(AB)=-2-z and define U_0=1, U_1=t, U_(r+1)=t U_r-U_(r-1). Equation (7) becomes, up to that same sign, P(i,z)=U_m(t)-U_(m-1)(t). (9) The identity follows from the determinant-one matrix recurrence for BA, or directly from P_0=1, P_1=t-1. Its m roots are distinct: t=2 cos((2j-1)pi/p), j=1,...,m. (10) Indeed U_m(2cos theta)-U_(m-1)(2cos theta) =cos(p theta/2)/cos(theta/2), with endpoint values obtained by limits. This also follows from the finite sine-sum formula for U_m. At M=-i one obtains the same roots, since replacing M by -M negates both meridian matrices after a constant diagonal conjugation. Thus each actual local branch through the midpoint has an ordinary finite analytic representative (possibly after taking its character normalization), not an escaping Riley parameter. The monic equation is finite over C[M,M^-1]; every one-dimensional nonvertical component of the actual relation locus reaches M=i and M=-i. More explicitly, a dominating irreducible component is closed in this finite scheme, so its image is a closed dense subset of C*, hence all of C*. No assertion about a vertical component is needed for a meridian transport curve. The volume is continuous at these limits. One can check this without assuming cross-ratios stay nondegenerate: M remains away from +/-1, so the peripheral eigenlines and axis vary continuously on each local branch. Choose the axis cusp maps continuously; their volume forms vanish on the cusp. The equivariant interpolation over the fixed finite compact core varies continuously, so its finite volume integral does too. Hence every such branch has limiting marked regulator zero. Reducible representations have zero regulator throughout and cause no additional endpoint case. ## 4. Consequence for COMPLEX conversion paths Combine (5) and the finite-limit statement with the [complex peripheral action identity](complex_peripheral_action_and_conversion_bound.md). For any path which genuinely lifts to a connected representation/Bloch curve, starts at this midpoint and ends at unit meridian, |Im integral Log(L) dLog(M²)| <= Vol(S³ minus K). (11) Ramification points on the normalized lifted curve are allowed. For the quantum step h=2pi i/N, the corresponding exponential action has growth at most Vol/(2pi). This controls all such lifted paths for the entire hyperbolic two-bridge class, rather than selected twist examples. It does NOT prove that every contribution of the original quantum recurrence admits this path description, nor that the number and prefactors of those contributions are subexponential. Those are the remaining analytic/source requirements. ## 5. Coverage and checks The trace-free slice and binary-dihedral representations are established subjects; coverage includes [Nagasato--Yamaguchi](https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.0714). No proof from that source is used here. The group reduction, monic matrix calculation, finite limit and zero-volume argument are supplied above; no novelty is claimed for the representation classification. [Audit](../experiments/audit_two_bridge_midpoint_anchor.py) checks the generic leading coefficients, actual two-bridge sign words, the trace-free polynomial recurrence, and the exact finite-order relation. An independent agent reviewed the entire proof, including the longitude marking and finite-limit argument: PASS. The fresh root audit checks 84 generic sign words and 41 two-bridge midpoint sign words, with simple roots and the exact finite-order relation.

title: Two actual flow cuts give a strict matrix and coherent Green complex
text:
# Two actual flow cuts give a strict matrix and coherent Green complex Research construction, 27 October 2026. Once two actual physical edge positions a,b have been retained, their zero-extended array is one matrix with independent row and column clocks. Both finite Green currents, all boundary rows/columns/corners, and the ORIGINAL 1/N co-source have an exact Laurent/coherent realization. This does not identify a physical single-port Hopf action with matrix multiplication, and does not assume that the geometric Gaussian commutes with the construction. The physical existence, four-port ordering and integral flow-chart choice are supplied by [the actual two-cut reconstruction](actual_two_cut_framing_port_reconstruction.md). The second cut is an INTERNAL IDENTITY edge: no new pivot is inserted there. All original pivots, caps and scalar peripheral factors remain in the actual array. Only a diagonal transport ALREADY present on that edge may be absorbed in its definition. ## 1. The actual array, source and independent clocks Let f(a,b) be a finite zero-extended array on Z^2 over the original coefficient algebra, after the specified other finite sums. All flow constraints and their zero entries are retained. On the head window 0<=a,b<N put J_ab=f(a,b), and n=N-1. The actual selected state is head-supported, and its period is \[ \Phi(J)= rac1N\sum_{a,b=0}^{n}J_{ab}. 	ag{1} \] There is no second factor 1/N. In particular this is the original rank-one average matrix row Tr(eJ), e_ab=1/N, rather than Tr(J)/N. The matrix is a reshaped DOUBLE-DIAGONAL four-port array, not an ordinary open-knot endomorphism. No scalarity condition J=cI is imposed on it. Let A=diag(1,Q,...,Q^n). The two actual characters are exactly \[ A_1J=AJ,\qquad A_2J=JA. 	ag{2} \] Both remain independent before the final source pairing. Their whole q-germs, including Q^N, are retained before root evaluation. ## 2. Exact shifts and every boundary term Let Ue_j=e_(j+1), j<n, and Ue_n=0. Define endpoint rows and columns r_+(b)=f(N,b), r_-(b)=f(-1,b), c_+(a)=f(a,N), c_-(a)=f(a,-1), restricted to the other head index. Then literal coordinate translations have the matrix formulas \[  egin{split} \Pi S_a^+f&=U^tJ+e_n r_+,& \Pi S_a^-f&=UJ+e_0r_-,\ \Pi S_b^+f&=JU+c_+e_n^t,& \Pi S_b^-f&=JU^t+c_-e_0^t. \end{split} 	ag{3} \] Here Pi is head-window restriction; these are coordinate-array translations, not physical single-port raising/lowering actions. The endpoint rows themselves translate and have endpoints. For example \[ \Pi S_a^+S_b^+f=U^tJU+e_n r_+U+U^tc_+e_n^t +f(N,N)e_ne_n^t. 	ag{4} \] More generally choose L_+=U^t,L_-=U, R_+=U,R_-=U^t, e_+=e_n,e_-=e_0 and t_+=N,t_-=-1. Then \[ \Pi S_a^\epsilon S_b^\eta f =L_\epsilon JR_\eta+e_\epsilon r_\epsilon R_\eta +L_\epsilon c_\eta e_\eta^t +f(t_\epsilon,t_\eta)e_\epsilon e_\eta^t. 	ag{5} \] The corner term is required for the two translations to commute. Longer words keep the corresponding finite strips and corners; there is no fixed finite head matrix representation of all translations without this tail data. The co-source versions of (3) are equally explicit: \[ \Phi(\Pi(S_a^+-1)f)= rac1N\sum_{b=0}^n[f(N,b)-f(0,b)], \] \[ \Phi(\Pi(S_a^--1)f)= rac1N\sum_{b=0}^n[f(-1,b)-f(n,b)], 	ag{6} \] with the analogous two column formulas. A clock on an endpoint uses Q^N or Q^(-1), not one substituted from its root value. The exact Weyl relation S_a^+ A_1=Q A_1 S_a^+, and its three counterparts, includes these endpoint coefficients. ## 3. A whole Laurent kernel retains the tails strictly Define the finite Laurent polynomial \[ \mathscr F_f(x,y)=\sum_{a,b\in\mathbb Z}f(a,b)x^ay^b. 	ag{7} \] This map is injective and has the exact operator dictionary \[ S_a^+\leftrightarrow x^{-1},\quad S_a^-\leftrightarrow x, \quad S_b^+\leftrightarrow y^{-1},\quad S_b^-\leftrightarrow y, \] \[ A_1\leftrightarrow[x\mapsto Qx],\quad A_2\leftrightarrow[y\mapsto Qy],\quad a\leftrightarrow x\partial_x,\quad b\leftrightarrow y\partial_y. 	ag{8} \] Consequently arbitrary ordered clock/shift words and every retained polynomial Green moment are transported exactly. External meridian Ore operators act on the coefficient algebra with their original order. Q derivatives of a dilation include its Euler chain-rule term; the source's normal terms are not frozen before differentiation. If an external Ore shift changes a chosen source/basis frame L, its transported operator is L_after O sigma(L_before^(-1)), with the specified semilinear coefficient action. It is not ordinary conjugation by a frame which the Ore shift has changed. For head-supported states (1) is exactly \[ \Phi_{full}(f)= rac{\mathscr F_f(1,1)}N = rac1N\operatorname{Res}_{x=1}\operatorname{Res}_{y=1}  rac{\mathscr F_f(x,y)\,dx\,dy}{(x-1)(y-1)}. 	ag{9} \] The same expression on currents sums ALL their finite tails. It equals the head row plus the explicit outside-window sum divided by N. Thus it kills both full zero-extended differences, while (6) records exactly the boundary removed by restricting to the head. No cyclic interpretation of either actual coordinate is used. ## 4. Explicit two-current complex and its contraction Write d_x=x^(-1)-1,d_y=y^(-1)-1. The actual two-flow Green complex on finite Laurent kernels has \[ d_1(P,Q)=d_xP+d_yQ,\qquad d_2(H)=(d_yH,-d_xH),\qquad\Phi_{full}d_1=0. 	ag{10} \] All actual finite certificate identities map to this complex coefficientwise. Define P_xF=F(1,y), P_yF=F(x,1), and \[ H_xF= rac{F-P_xF}{x^{-1}-1},\qquad H_yF= rac{F-P_yF}{y^{-1}-1}. 	ag{11} \] The quotients are Laurent POLYNOMIALS: their numerator vanishes at the indicated source point. In the original array, for example, H_af(a,b)=-sum_(k>=a)[f(k,b)-delta_(k,0)sum_u f(u,b)]; this is a finite sequence. Put \[ h_0(F)=(H_xF,P_xH_yF),\qquad h_1(P,Q)=-H_xQ. 	ag{12} \] Direct substitution gives \[ d_1h_0F=F-F(1,1),\quad h_0d_1+d_2h_1=I,\quad h_1d_2=I. 	ag{13} \] Thus both currents and their common corner/syzygy have a specified finite contracting homotopy. There is no inferred Gaussian or Stokes operation in this identity. If the section is chosen as the literal matrix identity, let E_N(x,y)=sum_(a=0)^n(xy)^a, so Phi(E_N)=1, and let Gamma=h_0(E_N-N). Replace h_0 by \[ h_0^{I}(F)=h_0(F)-\Gamma\Phi_{full}(F). 	ag{14} \] Then d_1h_0^I=I-E_N Phi_full, while the other identities remain unchanged. The 1/N in the ORIGINAL source is therefore preserved by the pointed complex; it has not become 1/N^2. This section is a specified homotopy anchor, not a claim that every physical two-cut tangle has identity matrix. ## 5. Global P1 kernel and the literal source/co-source The core polynomial (7) has bidegree at most (n,n), hence is a section of O(n) external_tensor O(n) on P1_x times P1_y. A single matrix operator kernel uses the dual coordinate w=y^(-1): \[ \mathcal K_J(z,w)=\sum_{a,b=0}^nJ_{ab}z^a w^{-b-1}\,dw. 	ag{15} \] In the monomial identification of the actual head basis with H^0(P1,O(n)), its input factor is the explicit Serre-dual Cech class in H^1(P1,O(-n-2)). The ACTUAL head ket and row are psi(w)=sum_(b=0)^n w^b and evaluation at z=1 divided by N. Thus \[ \Phi(J)= rac1N\operatorname{Res}_{w=0} \mathcal K_J(1,w)\psi(w). 	ag{16} \] This keeps the original uniform ket/dual, rather than replacing them by binomial coherent weights or compact ordinary trace. If a binomial-normalized coherent frame is desired, its diagonal source and dual adapter must be carried explicitly. No positivity, metric isometry or asymptotic phase is inferred from this vector space identification. Both clocks and the shifts act on (15) as in (8); for the input clock its action is the ONE-FORM pullback w->w/Q, which includes the differential factor. This avoids a spurious factor Q in the right clock. On the coefficient of dw the input index b is -w partial_w-1; the missing -1 would give the wrong moment. Matrix composition, when it is actually used, is exactly \[ \mathcal K_{JH}(z,w)=\operatorname{Res}_{u=0} \mathcal K_J(z,u)\mathcal K_H(u,w), \] with the input/output differential factors retained. It is not pointwise multiplication of symbols, nor a claim that the physical four-port tangle composes by the reshaped matrix product. The full tails in (7) are meromorphic sections with possible poles only at zero and infinity in each coordinate. Keep them as such, or as the corresponding relative Cech cochains with their explicit boundary rows. Projecting them to the finite H^0/Serre quotient would discard the terms (3)--(6). The whole residue (9) is regular on these finite Laurent sections and preserves them. This gives one global meromorphic matrix/coherent Green complex for both actual coordinate currents, with no hypothetical extra Fr flag. Here is an explicit principal-part/Cech description of the tails. For O(n) on U_0 and U_infinity use the transition z^n and write every finite meromorphic section uniquely as \[ p(z)=p_{<0}(z)+p_{[0,n]}(z)+p_{>n}(z). \] The first and last summands are respectively the finite principal parts at zero and infinity; the middle one is H^0(O(n)). This is the global-section form of 0->O(n)->O(n)(*0+*infinity)->principal_parts->0. Exactness is immediate from the displayed Laurent splitting. Two coordinates give N-by-N core, four strips and four corner principal parts. The two one-step rules are, for a core polynomial, \[ \Pi(z^{-1}p)= rac{p-p(0)}z,\qquad \Pi(zp)=zp-p_nz^{n+1}. 	ag{16a} \] The discarded monomials are precisely the outgoing principal parts; the incoming ones give the last row or first row in (3). Tensoring these splits gives the explicit corner formula (5). Thus this is a strict global meromorphic/relative-Cech lift of the actual finite tail data, rather than an appeal to a different cohomology class with the same scalar value. Its source evaluates ALL nine regions at (1,1) with the one factor 1/N. ## 6. One-cut restriction and the physical Hopf distinction Closing the second identity cut gives the original one-cut array p_a=sum_b J_ab, hence C_one=diag(p_a) and \[ \Phi(J)=\operatorname{Tr}(C_{one})/N. 	ag{17} \] The second clock and current cannot in general be reconstructed from C_one: matrices with zero row sums can have nonzero weighted row sums after right multiplication by A. Keeping J avoids exactly that loss. Neither its two clocks nor its arbitrary off-diagonal entries are subject to an ordinary open-knot Schur condition. The ACTUAL physical single-port Hopf actions of the four-port tangle need not descend to J. They can create off-diagonal port bands, whose source uses the corresponding original cut pairing. Equations (2)--(8) concern simultaneous coordinate translations of the scalar/charge-zero flow array, not that separate Hopf diagram. The necessary port-band current extension is therefore retained as an additional map; it is not asserted by this matrix reshape. Their exact bands and current audit are recorded in [the physical port-band calculation](two_cut_port_band_current_audit.md). The finite two-flow certificate now has an exact global coherent and sourced relative complex. Establishing that the nondegenerate geometric Gaussian pushforward is a map into this complex, with the same marked endpoint/carry data, remains a theorem to prove. No such commutation, nonzero selected geometric contribution or volume limit is inferred here. ## 7. An exact band involution and the identity-cut residue sign A nontrivial geometric deck which fixes BOTH position clocks cannot be an exact source-preserving involution on the bare matrix J. Indeed the two operators L_A,R_A have jointly simple eigenvectors E_ab. A linear map commuting with both is a Schur multiplier E_ab->w_ab E_ab. Since Phi(E_ab)=1/N, preserving the original source forces every w_ab=1. An anti-source map similarly gives only -I. This is a fixed-level obstruction, not a prohibition on a transform with nontrivial internal/band multiplicity or only semiclassically fixed clocks. The retained PHYSICAL PORT BANDS have such multiplicity. In the actual band convention put \[ J^{\mu,
u}_{a,b}=T_{a+\mu,b+
u;a,b},\qquad (\mathcal I J)^{\mu,
u}_{a,b} =J^{-\mu,-
u}_{a+\mu,b+
u}. 	ag{18} \] This is simply input/output transpose of the full four-port tensor. It is exactly involutive and preserves the actual full source N^(-1) sum_(mu,a,b) J^(mu,0)_(a,b), with zero-extended bounds. It is not asserted to be a symmetry of the actual knot word. It exchanges input/output clocks; the CENTERED clocks Q^(a+mu/2), Q^(b+nu/2) are fixed exactly. Their square-root mark is the original q with q^2=Q. They restrict to the physical position clocks on the zero band. Simultaneous coordinate translations in a,b commute with this involution. The finite Laurent band kernel and its exact transformation are \[ F_T(x,y;\xi,\eta)=\sum J^{\mu,
u}_{a,b}x^ay^b\xi^\mu\eta^
u, \qquad F_{\mathcal IT}(x,y;\xi,\eta) =F_T(x,y;x/\xi,y/\eta). 	ag{19} \] The original second identity-cut co-source is the eta constant term of F_T(1,1;1,eta)/N. Its period form is \[ 	heta_T=F_T(1,1;1,\eta) rac{d\eta}{N\eta}. \] For inversion iota(eta)=eta^(-1) the natural ONE-FORM identity is \[ \iota^*	heta_T=-	heta_{\mathcal IT}. 	ag{20} \] Thus the scalar coefficient source is even, but its Cech residue orientation line is canonically odd: inversion exchanges zero and infinity, and Res_infinity(theta_T)=-Res_0(theta_T). This sign follows from the literal identity-cut residue, rather than from an assigned choice of geometric orientation. Equations (18)--(20) give a candidate source sign line for a geometric deck with anti-invariant density. To use it one must still prove that the geometric deck lifts to this actual port involution and transport the whole R/word and source frames. Transposition swaps left and right insertions and reverses operator order; no unchanged single-port Hopf row or unproved Weyl symmetry is inferred. The fixed-clock bare-matrix obstruction and the full-band candidate are distinct, exact statements. [Exact shifts, source, global-kernel and two-current audit](../experiments/audit_two_cut_matrix_green_and_coherent_source.py). The [results](../experiments/two_cut_matrix_green_and_coherent_source_results.json) pass fourteen root/whole-Q families N=2,...,8 and 742 head-plus-tail matrix units. They check every signed shift/corner, whole boundary clock, literal 1/N source and both current homotopies. An additional 1956 physical four-port matrix units check the candidate band involution, centered clocks and source; the residue orientation sign is checked symbolically. These tests do not identify that involution with the geometric deck or establish a Gaussian map.

title: Independent audit of the two physical cuts, bands and selected source
text: # Independent audit of the two physical cuts, bands and selected source 27 October 2026. The two-cut route gives a genuine two-position source/current model. It escapes the one-cut diagonal obstruction, has a unimodular flow chart, and supplies canonical nonzero LOCAL Gaussian blocks for bounded port offsets. The global selected-class comparison still needs its specified endpoint/projector and sheet data. The assertions below distinguish these operations explicitly. ## 1. Integral physical coordinates and the original source The existence/lattice proof in [the actual two-cut construction](actual_two_cut_framing_port_reconstruction.md) passes independently. Edge differentials here mean logarithmic physical-clock differentials on the classical critical scheme; integer labels define the underlying flow lattice. If all edge differentials lay in the span of the first cut differential, so would all transfer differentials, contradicting the two-dimensional critical framing tangent space. A second independent physical edge therefore exists on an open chart. For a connected graph G with circulation lattice L, the kernel of evaluating a set S of edge flows is the circulation lattice of G minus S. Incidence ranks give exactly \[ \operatorname{rank}\mathrm{ev}_S=|S|+1-c(G\setminus S). \] Rank two for the chosen pair implies that its complement is connected. A spanning tree avoiding both edges gives an integral fundamental-cycle basis with these two flows as literal coordinates. Thus there is no finite lattice index, congruence loss, extra cover or Jacobian factor. All zero-extension support conditions move with that integer change of variables. Opening the second identity wire means replacing it by the literal matrix unit E_bd. Summing E_bb restores its identity. Every original pivotal/turn/framing/peripheral tensor stays in its original place; no second pivotal weight is added. The reconstruction T_(a,b)^(c,d) and its double diagonal J_ab therefore have the exact source \[ F_N=\frac1N\sum_{a,b}J_{ab}. \tag{1} \] Use RAW coefficients for J. If the old Green array already includes 1/N, multiply its partial reshape by N before applying (1). There is no second normalization 1/N. J is a linear reshaping, not the two-leg operator algebra. For example diagonal extraction of the identity on H tensor H is the all-ones matrix, whose source value in (1) is N, while the actual two-cut unknot is the swap tensor and gives J=I, value one. A trace-center or multiplicative statement about J cannot silently be imported from the original four-port operator. ## 2. The whole two-flow Green/source complex passes The [matrix/Laurent/coherent construction](two_cut_matrix_green_and_coherent_source.md) passes independently. The four signed shift formulas retain the correct row/column tails, and their composition retains the common corner. Its Laurent kernel includes ALL finite tails. Consequently source evaluation F(1,1)/N kills full zero-extended differences, while window restriction has precisely its displayed boundary rows. For d_x=x^-1-1,d_y=y^-1-1 the displayed h_0,h_1 satisfy all three contraction identities with their printed signs. The identity-matrix anchor is correct too: Gamma=h_0(E_N-N) has differential E_N-N, so subtracting Gamma times the ORIGINAL source changes the section to E_N without changing the other identities. It does not introduce 1/N^2 or declare every physical tangle to have that anchor. The P1 kernel uses the literal uniform source and dual, not binomial coherent weights. Its input clock is a ONE-FORM pullback w to w/Q: the differential factor cancels the extra Q, giving exactly Q^b. The finite Laurent principal parts remain in their nine tensor regions; projecting to a finite Serre quotient would discard the tails and is not done. The generating variables are dual weights, not physical positions: \[ \mathscr F(x,y)=\sum J_{ab}x^ay^b,\qquad Q^a\leftrightarrow[x\mapsto Qx],\quad S_a^+\leftrightarrow x^{-1}. \tag{2} \] Rivin's physical coordinates are A=Q^a,B=Q^b. Identifying (x,y) with (A,B) would change the problem. Source evaluation at x=y=1 is the original zero-weight framing pairing. ## 3. Actual port currents have an exact band extension For fixed literal port order retain \[ J^{p,q}_{ab}=T_{a+p,b+q;a,b}, \] with zero values outside all four physical ranges. If E e_j=e_j^{E}e_(j-1) and F e_j=f_j e_(j+1), direct matrix multiplication gives the first-port commutator identities \[ \begin{split} [E_1,T]^{p,q}_{ab} &=e^E_{a+p+1}J^{p+1,q}_{ab} -e^E_aJ^{p+1,q}_{a-1,b},\\ [F_1,T]^{p,q}_{ab} &=f_{a+p-1}J^{p-1,q}_{ab} -f_aJ^{p-1,q}_{a+1,b}. \tag{3} \end{split} \] The second-port formulas interchange (a,p) and (b,q). Arbitrary port matrices have the stated sums of such shifted bands. This is a lossless finite current map, including the genuine endpoint coefficients and all original phase marks. For every current tensor the ORIGINAL source is \[ \Phi^{(2)}(T)=\sum_{p,a,b}(e_0)_{a,a+p}J^{p,0}_{ab}. \tag{4} \] In the balanced frame (e_0)_ij=1/N. A homogeneous cut degree d selects p=d; only a conserving scalar kernel selects p=q=0. Thus (1) may not be used as the source of every off-diagonal Hopf current. The actual two-cut unknot already proves that a single-port E action does not descend to ordinary left EJ: its diagonal extraction is zero, whereas EJ=E is nonzero. The actual insertion identity (3.1) in the main construction passes: A and B intertwine their ACTUAL intermediate coproducts, so the true adjoint of A X B is A(ad X)B, and the genuine pivotal cap is natural. Its E prefix terms and F cancellations have the correct order and weight k_X. For weighted words retain their extra crossing currents; for the frozen cap retain its exact moment-clock defect. A naive Delta on the reshaped J is not used. In a specified parallel two-leg Delta convention, the source of an ordinary E row needs only J^(0,0) and J^(-1,+1); F needs J^(0,0) and J^(+1,-1). This follows by (3) applied to the actual coproduct. A word of r ordinary E/F generators accesses exchange bands |p|<=r. For arbitrary boundary ordering this statement must first be transported by its actual opposite/dual/braided port dictionary. The literal cut tensor is NOT automatically an End(V tensor V) Delta-intertwiner. General divided-N rows and large bands are not covered by a fixed bounded-band assertion. ## 4. The bounded-band Gaussian construction is genuinely positive The interior theorem in Section5 of the main construction also passes independently. Removing both cuts leaves a connected internal graph. Any balanced fixed boundary offset has an integral tree particular flow. Every other solution differs by an internal cycle, with the same free transverse chords. For offsets fixed independently of N, each original local position/transfer changes by bounded integers. Actual proper factorial/Cartan ratios are therefore finite products of known rational shifts. Their principal symbols are units on the regular shape chart, with the original common compact, peripheral, phase and half-density lines retained. The two physical coordinates give a nondegenerate transverse Hessian. The original Gaussian of that proper-ratio insertion has the same marked action and a nonzero leading amplitude. Its value is independent of a FIXED bounded particular-flow choice by the exact transverse translation identity. An N-cycle is a finite logarithmic-deck move and needs its additional period mark.
