The explicit interior port/current identities consequently have a canonical LOCAL cochain pushforward, not merely a dimension count. Original support and endpoint rows remain their separate relative summand; this theorem does not evaluate them. The nearest-band principal ratios are also correct in the ACTUAL balanced/factorial frame. Its canonical boundary form uses p_new=(1-A)p_old. Holding inputs fixed and shifting outputs by (p,q) changes the principal action by p Log p_cut+q Log p_e. The cut value is one, giving \[ R_{(+1,-1),0}=p_e^{-1},\qquad R_{(-1,+1),0}=p_e. \tag{5} \] Internal tree contributions cancel by critical momentum matching. Using the old momentum without its frame factor would change (5). ## 5. A reviewed physical two-parabolic chart and its sign target In a common ACTUAL physical chart, take a normalized cut meridian g_0=[[1,1],[0,1]], a trace-two meridian g_e=[[a,b],[c,d]], h=a-d, and F=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]]. Then \[ P=F E_{11}F^{-1} =\begin{pmatrix}r&r(1-r)/s\\s&1-r\end{pmatrix},\quad k_e=\operatorname{Tr}(g_eP) =d+hr+bs+c r(1-r)/s. \] Let A=1/(1+s), B=1/k_e, tau=r/s and D=c+sh-2cr. Direct differentiation and trace/determinant identities give \[ D^2=c^2+4cs(1-B^{-1}),\qquad \Omega_{cut}=\frac{d\log A\wedge d\log B}{BD}. \tag{6} \] If c=0, trace2 and determinant1 force a=d=1, and B depends only on s, contradicting an independent pair. Thus a rank-two chart has c!=0. The quadratic discriminant is generically nonsquare (its pole at B=0 is simple), and the deck is r to 1+sh/c-r. It flips D and Omega. Ordinary field trace of the coefficient1/(BD) is consequently ZERO. The symmetric matrix Q=[[h/c,1],[1,0]] has determinant -1 and satisfies g_0Q=Qg_0^t, g_eQ=Qg_e^t. Thus the same deck is P to QP^tQ^-1. This is a bilinear transpose statement, not an assertion of a positive Hermitian structure or an already proved quantum-Weyl symmetry of the whole word. In the moving cut frame the ACTUAL factorial momentum form is \[ g_{cut}=\begin{pmatrix}1+s&-s\\s&1-s\end{pmatrix},\quad g_e^{cur}=\begin{pmatrix}k&(1-k)p_e\\(k-1)/p_e&2-k\end{pmatrix}. \] If these are the displayed matrices in that same physical frame, with c=Tr(g_cut g_e^cur)-2 fixed, put z=s(k-1). Then exactly \[ c=z(2-p_e-p_e^{-1}),\qquad D=-z(p_e-p_e^{-1}). \] One may also verify D=-Tr([g_0,g_e]P). On the regular z!=0, p_e!=0 chart, the deck is precisely p_e to p_e^-1. Formula (5) therefore gives a genuine actual LOCAL odd-band observable \[ R_{(+1,-1),0}-R_{(-1,+1),0}=D/z. \] Its product with (6) is the nonzero even density dlog A wedge dlog B/(Bz). This does not say the original q=0 identity-cap source inserts that observable or selects that sign cycle. That is a specified remaining source-parity test. The physical dictionary is essential: in the existing marked holonomy construction H_j=B_(minus,prefix)^-1 G_j B_(minus,prefix). A developed meridian cannot be substituted for a physical Gauss matrix solely because both have trace two. The conditional chart consequence above requires the actual prefix/port adapter. There is an alternative finite parity-moment test where a third physical meridian clock is available in the SAME frame. For g_f with entries a',b',c',d', h'=a'-d' and W=c'h-ch' nonzero, \[ r=\frac{c'k_e-c k_f-(c'd-cd')-(c'b-cb')s}{W}. \tag{7} \] Thus D is a rational combination of three actual clock observables; its moment can be inserted through the retained internal-edge coupling, with no extra pivot. If the descended quadratic field is F(D), Delta=D^2, and lambda=Tr((a_0+a_1D) times -), then \[ \lambda(1/(BD))=\lambda(D)/(B\Delta). \tag{8} \] The actual odd moment lambda(D), rather than a chosen field-trace normalization, is the coefficient to test. Formula (7) has the same physical-prefix qualification as (6). ## 6. The exact remaining selected-class square Two physical cuts now give both external difference directions and their complete finite matrix/source complex. The old one-cut obstruction does not apply. Local transverse Gaussian transport also has both physical base variables and the bounded band currents just proved. These are genuine improvements. The whole selected comparison still needs the ORIGINAL internal finite head projections. In the known relative/Rees diagram their actual maps are, with all head flags retained, \[ P_t^{rel}(\sigma) =e^{(\sigma-p/d)u}P_t. \tag{9} \] Opening a second identity edge does not remove the remaining internal projectors. A proposed whole geometric pushforward Gamma must intertwine (9) and both endpoints, in addition to the actual crossings and the selected two-cut tail/co-source. Its elementary defect is the specifically typed expression \[ E_O=\Gamma_{out}O_{act,rel} -O_{geo,rel}\Gamma_{in}. \] For a word its residual is the finite telescoping sum \[ \sum_t O_{geo,>t}\,E_{O_t}\,O_{act,<t}. \tag{10} \] The internal source equation (9), not a generic formal Morse assertion, is a concrete remaining test. Its irregular factor cannot be silently replaced by a regular vacuum. The exact whole Fermat-trace source is one available explicit function for this comparison, with its original norm, trace and power characters. Equations (9)--(10) do not assert an obstruction to constructing Gamma. They identify what the new external matrix/coherent map does not yet prove. Extending it through these specified internal maps and proving the selected sign/orientation would give the desired whole source-class comparison; neither selected survival nor volume growth follows just from local nonzero Gaussian bands. ## 7. The actual prefix correction passes, including the parity signs The later [prefix-adapted two-position proof](prefix_adapted_two_position_framing_cover.md) passes independently. It resolves the physical-prefix qualification in Section 5. For U=mu_j...mu_1 and V=mu_(j-1)...mu_1, the actual second clock is k=ell_U/ell_V. With C=U-kV the correct density is \[ \Omega_{cut}=\frac{\ell_V}{BD}\,d\log A\wedge d\log B, \qquad D=\partial_\tau\ell_C. \tag{11} \] The Section 5 density with numerator one is a special chart, not a formula for every physical internal edge. Direct quadratic root summation gives \[ \operatorname{Tr}(\ell_V/D) =\frac{c_Vh_U-h_Vc_U}{(c_U-kc_V)^2}. \tag{12} \] It can be nonzero; the actual figure-eight prefix in the main note has c_Vh_U-h_Vc_U=2u+1 for u squared plus u plus one equal to zero. The claimed rational primitive of the resulting trace form also has the correct sign. A nonzero field trace is not a selected period. The signed triangular reconstruction gives exactly beta=(-1)^j e_j and gamma=(-1)^j K_j f_j, because both triangular prefix adapters cancel out of these off-diagonal entries. Thus \[ \beta=(-1)^j(k-M^{-1})p,\qquad \gamma=(-1)^{j+1}(k-M)/p. \] At M=1, Tr(JC) fixes beta-gamma and differentiation gives D=s(beta+gamma). Hence the deck sends beta,gamma to -gamma,-beta, and p to p inverse, with D=(-1)^j s(k-1)(p-p inverse). This independently checks the parity j in its nearest-band and density formulas. The generic-meridian twisted reciprocal formula follows by using the actual cut meridian entries M inverse minus k_0 and k_0 minus M in this same trace equation; it also passes. Finally the literal inverse signed prefix is (q/M)^(j-1) product_(i<j) Q^(J_i). It is an actual finite diagonal clock observable with its peripheral factor, not a postselected scalar. Its principal symbol removes ell_V from (11). The note correctly keeps its ordered crossing/current transport and does not claim that it commutes through the whole word. ## 8. The finite identity cap has a marked orientation presentation [The marked cap-cover identity](identity_cut_orientation_cover_and_marked_source.md) now supplies an exact positive source comparison before any Gaussian: \[ F(\eta)\frac{d\eta}{N\eta} =[(\eta-\eta^{-1})F(\eta)] \frac{d(\eta+\eta^{-1})} {N((\eta+\eta^{-1})^2-4)}. \tag{13} \] The original cap marks eta=0, equivalently the preimage of u=infinity with v/u tending to -1. Its exact residue has all finite negative odd-band tails, with partial-sum endpoint (F_0-F_(-2K-2))/N. The compensating measure and this endpoint prevent replacing the original state by an arbitrary odd observable. The total form has no new branch-point poles. No global tensor involution is assumed. The principal prefix formula identifies eta=p inverse and gives Omega_cut/ell_V=[(k-1)/(A_1-A_0)] dlog A wedge d eta/eta on its regular coordinate chart, where A_0=c_U+s Tr U and A_1=c_V+s Tr V. This checks the principal density and its full rational Jacobian. Transporting the entire marked residue through the actual internal projectors and transverse Gaussian remains the global comparison. The new independent exact audit passes 21 literal actual signed braid tensors, seven literal-unknot levels and all 8,771 port matrix units at those levels, including their whole clocks and finite endpoints. See the linked cap-cover note and its reproducible script/results. The same note now records an important exact GEOMETRIC boundary check. Its eta_geo=p inverse differs from the finite Fourier-band variable eta_F. The relation eta_F p=1 is principal Fourier incidence, not an ordinary source-coordinate change or a map of the cap cycle. In the geometric relation u=p+p inverse, eta_geo=0 forces k to one and selects D=A_0-A_1. If c_U-c_V is nonzero, the prefix root r and ell_V stay finite. The full density multiplier ell_V(k-1)/(A_1-A_0) is O(eta), so Omega_cut has zero logarithmic residue there. This does not identify that boundary with the image of the original eta_F cap. For the actual figure-eight prefix at s=1 the limiting data are r=-2 and ell_V=2+3u_shape, with c_U-c_V=1 and A_0-A_1=3+u_shape. If a proposed source transform assigns the cap to this geometric boundary, a nonzero image needs its retained polar, endpoint or escaping block amplitude; the geometric residue functional is equation (19) of the cap-cover note. The finite identity (13) does not by itself imply that an interior regular Gaussian density has the original nonzero cap. This is a concrete remaining source coefficient, rather than a choice of an odd cycle by hand.

title: Independent audit of the actual two-head cyclic sewing
text: # Independent audit of the actual two-head cyclic sewing 28 October 2026. The exact five-term resolvent and the two-sector SMALL-CIRCLE period reduction in [the sewing theorem](exact_quantum_quad_source_transport.md) are correct, including the coincident-wall fibre. A balancing gauge gives a useful local matrix estimate. It does not turn the original period into a positive pairing or license the old Hankel deformation term by term. There is an explicit source-visible pole witness in the ORIGINAL positive crossing: its two sewn cross pieces have nonzero double poles absent from the nilpotent resolvent. Their contributions must accompany any subsequent cut deformation. ## 1. Resolvent order and the coincident wall On a total-index residue fibre choose basis b_n, n=0,...,N-1. Let S be cyclic raising, A=aS, z=a/t, and h=k+1. For h<N the actual truncated transfer deletes the arrows N-1 to 0 and h-1 to h. With U=[b_0,b_h], its deleted operator is UU^t A. Woodbury therefore gives R_T=R_A-R_A U (I+U^t A R_A U)^-1 U^t A R_A. Direct cyclic summation gives (I+U^t A R_A U)^-1 =C_h(z)=[[1,-z^(N-h)],[-z^h,1]]. All orders in the displayed formula matter. At h=N the two columns of U coincide, so a rank-two Woodbury inverse is NOT available. Nevertheless the SAME compressed expression remains correct, because U C_N(z) U^t=(1-z^N)b_0 b_0^t. This is exactly the single-deleted-edge formula. Thus the global five-term expression and its two cross terms are valid for every fibre without double-counting the physical wall. R_A and the two diagonal sewing terms are holomorphic at t=0. Multiplying by the marked analytic inverse-D germ and integrating on rho<min(1,|a|) kills those three terms entrywise. Other word factors do not alter that conclusion, since they use different integration variables. Consequently the at most 2^(3m) surviving cross-sector networks retain the ORIGINAL source exactly on the original product of small circles. ## 2. The balancing gauge and its quantitative scope Retain a continuous Log z and put D_h=diag(1,z^(h-N/2)), w=z^(N/2). Then exactly D_h^-1 C_h D_h=[[1,-w],[-w,1]], det C_h=1-z^N. (1) The original physical scalar is a=x^-1 or Q^-1 x^-1. On an actual inverse-D cut t=Q^(-epsilon j)r and at M=1, z^N=(-1)^(N+1) r^(-N). (2) For odd N, w is one of the two real values +/-r^(-N/2). The balanced C has positive eigenvalues 1+/-r^(-N/2) for r>1. For even N, w is purely imaginary, and the Hermitian part of the balanced C is EXACTLY identity. Both statements retain the root phase; z^N has not been replaced by a positive number. The gauge condition number is kappa(D_h)=r^|h-N/2|. On the actual radial scale r=exp(s/N), it is bounded by exp(s/2), uniformly in h and N when s is bounded. This includes h=N, although U then has repeated columns. For odd N the smallest balanced eigenvalue is 1-exp(-s/2), which tends to zero at the radial endpoint. At fixed r>1 the gauge can instead have exponential condition number; the stated bound is a scaled local estimate, not a uniform estimate on the entire radial ray. Moreover the two-sector Cauchy reduction keeps only C's OFFDIAGONAL part. Its balanced version is [[0,-w],[-w,0]]: indefinite for odd N and with zero Hermitian part for even N. Thus the positive diagonal of full C belongs to terms whose original small-circle periods vanish. Positivity of full C does not itself prove a lower bound for their remaining cross-sector contraction. The actual co-source is also a pivotal linear pairing, not the positive quadratic form used by an accretivity estimate. ## 3. Added cyclic poles change the required relative cycle Every cyclic R_A has poles at t^N=a^N, while R_T has only its nilpotent pole at zero. The five-term formula cancels all added poles. Discarding its analytic-at-zero terms preserves the small circle period but does NOT preserve global holomorphy. At completeness a^N=(-1)^(N+1). Thus for odd N the added poles lie at N-th roots of unity: most hit D-cut endpoints, and t=1 is an added pole where D itself is regular. For even N they lie at the interlaced half-roots, off those cuts. Separate cross pieces can have double poles. Their old radial-cut integrals may be nonintegrable when the pole hits a branch endpoint. Pole residues or the corresponding marked finite-part chains must be retained. Matrix balancing in Section 2 does not remove this change of relative cycle. ## 4. An exact ORIGINAL positive-crossing source witness Take N=2, M=1, Q=-1, q=i, x=i. In the opposite-root realization of the actual U_+ factor, a=Q^-1 x^-1=i. Use the ORIGINAL fusion C and Gaussian D=I from the strict crossing factorization, and the original averaged first-cut functional Phi with pivotal entries (-i,i). Keep its common Cartan scalar and external line separately, unchanged. Let R_cross(t) be the sum of the two cross terms, and R_T the actual transfer resolvent. Exact source contraction gives Phi(C R_T(t) C^-1)=2i/t^2, Phi(C R_cross(t) C^-1) =-2i(t-1)(t+1)/[t^2(t^2+1)^2]. (3) The leading double-pole coefficient of the second expression at EACH of t=i and t=-i is i. These poles are source-visible inside an actual positive crossing, rather than only in an arbitrary matrix entry. The original inverse-D germ here is f(t)=(1+t)^(-1/2). Both small-circle periods are exactly -i. The uncorrected old D-cut integral for the sewn expression, on t=-r, would instead be (2i/pi) integral_1^infinity (r^2-1)/[r^2(r^2+1)^2] (r-1)^(-1/2)dr. It is purely POSITIVE imaginary and therefore cannot equal -i. The missing cyclic-pole contributions are essential, even in this smallest actual-source example. The original normalization multiplies both expressions by the same retained nonzero factor; it cannot correct the mismatch. The missing ordinary residues are explicitly Res_(t=i) f(t)B(t)dt=(-9-i)/(4sqrt(1+i)), Res_(t=-i) f(t)B(t)dt=(9-i)/(4sqrt(1-i)). Their sum is approximately 1.0596435755300515788i. The raw cut integral is approximately 0.0596435755300515788i. The correct contour identity is cut MINUS these pole residues, which gives the original value -i. ## 5. Audit conclusion The exact small-circle sewing is a real finite-sector reduction. The balanced 2-by-2 matrix has a controlled condition number on the natural radial scale and the stated parity-dependent sign. Neither statement supplies a convergent termwise old-cut sewing or a positive selected scalar. A usable geometric comparison must carry the new cyclic poles and the original cross-sector source through the transform, including its endpoint corrections. There is a canonical linear repair when cyclic poles have order at most two, as they do in each transfer variable. At a D-cut endpoint alpha, put x=r-1 and write the remaining cut integrand as x^(-u)f(x), where f(x)=b_-2 x^(-2)+b_-1 x^(-1)+O(1). Its finite part is integral_0^1 x^(-u)[f-b_-2 x^(-2)-b_-1 x^(-1)]dx +integral_1^infinity x^(-u)f dx -b_-2/(u+1)-b_-1/u. Use these marked finite parts on the branch cuts and subtract the ordinary residues at unbranched cyclic poles. This gives the original small-circle period exactly. The constants follow from analytic continuation of the two elementary power integrals. The small endpoint arcs cancel their fractional divergences and have no additional finite residue: on the normalized cover a residue exponent would require j to be a multiple of N. Coordinatewise finite parts commute for this word because its ordered matrix source is a finite sum of products of one-variable rational factors. The tensor prescription retains the required corner subtractions. It preserves the source, while still not making its resulting scalar a positive quadratic pairing. The completed [regularized cut theorem](cyclic_sewing_regularized_cut_cycle.md) passes this independent proof review. In particular its derivative identity has the positive factor 1/[u...(u+p-1)] for p=1,2. At every integration-by-parts step the boundary term at infinity is O(x^(-(N-1)/2)), and its zero-end finite constant vanishes because u is nonintegral. The final derivative integral converges at both ends. Its whole-word tensor prescription follows from the finite sum of products of one-variable factors, with only coordinate pole loci. The unit-circle/completeness scope excludes new poles in the interior of a radial cut. No additional boundary term was found, and the theorem explicitly leaves geometric coupling open. [Exact and quantitative audit](../experiments/audit_two_head_cyclic_sewing_independent.py) and [saved results](../experiments/two_head_cyclic_sewing_independent_results.json).

title: The actual unfolded atom requires its cyclotomic divisors and second nome
text: # The actual unfolded atom requires its cyclotomic divisors and second nome Research proof, 27 October 2026. The original unfolded Ward factorial is not horizontal in a rank-one meromorphic line at the physical parameter origin. Its cyclotomic singularities already accumulate there. A two-nome difference-period object cancels the local root pole and has an exact cyclic/source factorization, but it also does not become an ordinary meromorphic line at the origin. It has explicit accumulating zeros on another parameter ray. The positive result is a whole exceptional-slope evaluation of the actual Ward atom, including its Kummer norm character, and an exact two-nome root formula retaining the original cyclic gauge and Heisenberg period. No published analytic-continuation or quantum dilogarithm proof is a premise. Use H=Log Q throughout. The physical root is H_N=2pi i/N. The earlier ADO parameter h=Log q is H/2. A fixed-root normal epsilon=H-H_N is a different parameter from the varying H_N. ## 1. The function is fixed by the actual Ward jets The literal finite source has f_N(z)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) z^j/(Q_N;Q_N)_j. Its all-level rational-coefficient unfolding was proved uniquely to be \[ F(Q,z)=\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{z^j}{(Q;Q)_j},\qquad F(Q,Qz)=(1-z)F(Q,z),\quad F(Q,0)=1. \] For |Q|<1, |z|<1, coefficient comparison or iteration gives \[ F(Q,z)=\frac1{(z;Q)_\infty},\qquad \log F(Q,z)=\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{z^m}{m(1-Q^m)}. \tag{1} \] These are the actual unfolded source functions of [the Ward construction](unfolded_ward_factorial_and_regulator.md), not an unrelated function chosen for its growth. The finite nilpotent head itself only uses the first N coefficients; scalar root values with nonnilpotent z require the retained central/source data below. ## 2. Cyclotomic singularities exclude the strict meromorphic-line target Fix a primitive n-th root zeta and Q=zeta exp(epsilon). On a closed sector around the negative real epsilon ray, uniformly for |z|<=r<1 with n FIXED, \[ \log F(\zeta e^\epsilon,z) =-\frac{\operatorname{Li}_2(z^n)}{n^2\epsilon} +\log D_n(z)-\frac12\operatorname{Log}(1-z^n)+O(\epsilon), \quad D_n(z)=\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}(1-\zeta^jz)^{j/n}. \tag{2} \] All marks start at z=0. Here is an analytic justification of the coefficient calculation already recorded in the Ward note. Separate m divisible by n in (1). Nonresonant denominators are uniformly bounded away from zero on the stated sector: for m|epsilon| small, use the distance of the finitely many nontrivial n-th roots from one; otherwise their radial modulus gives a uniform bound. Their termwise difference from epsilon=0 is O(m|epsilon|), so the z-series remainder is O(epsilon). For the resonant terms use \[ \frac1{1-e^u}=-\frac1u+\frac12+O(u) \] uniformly on the same negative sector. For large u the error bound O(|u|) still holds; summing against r^(kn) justifies the uniform remainder. The weighted finite-root sum gives the displayed D_n constant. Thus (2) is a genuine sectorial estimate, not merely a formal Laurent calculation. For fixed 0<z<1, every H_(m,n)=2pi i m/n, gcd(m,n)=1, has the nonzero polar logarithm in (2). Along epsilon=-t, log|F|=Li_2(z^n)/(n^2t)+O(1). These singularities accumulate at H=0. A nonzero horizontal frame of a meromorphic rank-one H-line would be holomorphic and nonzero at every sufficiently small H_(m,n)!=0, a contradiction. Finite ramification does not help. A fixed algebraic/Puiseux gauge has only finite-order behavior there and cannot cancel this exponential singularity. Removing only exp(-Li_2(z)/H) also leaves every nonzero cyclotomic point unchanged as a singularity. This disproves automatic applicability of the strict one-variable meromorphic-line criterion to the ORIGINAL UNFOLDED ATOM. It does not prove that singularities cannot cancel in a completed whole word or selected period; that cancellation would need its actual source theorem. ## 3. The actual norm is an exceptional normal-slope evaluation Retain U independently and form the WHOLE ratio \[ R(Q,z,U)=F(Q,zU)/F(Q,z). \tag{3} \] The bare generic restriction U=1 is one. Instead put Q=zeta_n exp(epsilon), U=exp(t n epsilon). For fixed n, t in a compact subset of C, and |z|<=r<1, the same sectorial argument gives \[ \log R(Q,z,U)=t\operatorname{Log}(1-z^n)+O(\epsilon), \qquad R\longrightarrow(1-z^n)^t. \tag{4} \] Proof. Nonresonant terms in the difference of (1) tend to zero uniformly. For m=kn the term is z^(kn)(exp(tkn^2 epsilon)-1)/[kn(1-exp(kn epsilon))], whose limit is -t z^(kn)/k. Uniform Taylor bounds near zero and exponential bounds away from zero, absorbed into a slightly larger r<1, justify the summed O(epsilon). This proves (4). At the ACTUAL slope t=1, U=Q^n and Ward iteration gives EXACTLY \[ R(Q,z,Q^n)=(z;Q)_n,\qquad R(Q_n,z,1)_{slope=1}=1-z^n. \tag{5} \] Thus the original finite cyclic norm is an exceptional normal-slope value, not the result of first imposing U=1 generically. It retains factors such as 1+M^n when they arise from the actual z substitution. For rational t=a/b, b>0, retain the telescope \[ \prod_{j=0}^{b-1}R(Q,zU^j,U)=F(Q,zU^b)/F(Q,z). \tag{6} \] Here U^b=Q^(an), so for a>=0 the right side is the finite product (z;Q)_(an), and negative a gives its specified reciprocal product. Its root value is (1-z^n)^a. The marked individual exceptional period nu therefore satisfies nu^b=(1-z^n)^a, with nu=1 at z=0. Equation (6) does NOT assert R^b equals that finite product away from the exceptional restriction: its arguments are different. This is a fixed-n sectorial exceptional period and Kummer norm statement. It is not a holomorphic regular extension across an entire complex blowup neighborhood, where other cyclotomic divisors still accumulate. No fixed-n limit is interchanged with a growing-n limit. ## 4. A two-nome flat difference object made from exact products Let z=e^x and define, for Re H<0, \[ Q=e^H,\quad \widetilde Q=e^{4\pi^2/H},\quad y=e^{2\pi i x/H},\quad w=\widetilde Q y, \] \[ \Psi(H,x)=\frac{(w;\widetilde Q)_\infty}{(z;Q)_\infty} =\frac{F(Q,z)}{F(\widetilde Q,w)}. \tag{7} \] Both nomes have modulus<1. The numerator product is entire in w; the log-series quotient is used on the smaller common chart |w|<1. Elementary product cancellation proves the exact two transports \[ \Psi(H,x+H)=(1-z)\Psi(H,x),\qquad \Psi(H,x+2\pi i)=(1-y)\Psi(H,x). \tag{8} \] The two shifts commute, since each multiplier is fixed by the other shift. In whole independent coordinates (Q,Qtilde,z,y), the automorphisms are z->Qz and y->Qtilde^(-1)y, respectively. Equations (8) are a rank-one flat algebraic DIFFERENCE presentation over that fixed finite-type base. The product (7) supplies one marked horizontal period. It is not thereby an algebraic section or an ordinary meromorphic differential line in H. The second factor is invariant under x->x+H. It is a genuine difference-constant for the original Ward equation. On the left upper H sector, x->-infinity along the real axis makes both z,w tend to zero, specifying the product mark Psi->1. That extra period/source datum must not be inferred from the first equation alone. ## 5. Exact physical-root value and the full source factor Now fix N and H=H_N+epsilon, H_N=2pi i/N. Write X=z^N and mark V=Log(1-X), nu=(1-X)^(1/N). The exact normal identities are \[ \widetilde H=4\pi^2/H+2\pi iN, \quad\frac1{\widetilde H} =\frac1{N^2\epsilon}+\frac1{2\pi iN}, \quad w=Xe^{\gamma\widetilde H},\quad \gamma=1-x/(2\pi i). \tag{9} \] For x in a compact marked subset of Re x<0, use (2) on the numerator atom and its n=1 case on the dual atom. The entire negative Laurent part of the two logarithms is the same simple pole -Li_2(X)/(N^2 epsilon), and cancels. Their exact constant difference gives the sectorial root value \[ \boxed{\ \Psi_N(x)=D_N(z) \exp\!\left(\frac{\operatorname{Li}_2(X)}{2\pi iN}\right) (1-X)^{x/(2\pi i)-1}.\ } \tag{10} \] For clarity the dual constant is -Li_2(X)/(2pi iN)+(gamma-1/2)V; subtracting it from log D_N- V/2 proves (10), including its sign. The estimate is O(epsilon) on the stated sector. This establishes the finite marked root value, not an unproved holomorphic H-extension around the whole root. Use the ACTUAL determinant-normalized cyclic source gauge \[ g_{D,N}=D_N/\nu^{(N-1)/2},\quad S(X)=\operatorname{Li}_2(X)+(Nx)V. \] Then the COMPLETE factorization is \[ \boxed{\ \Psi_N=g_{D,N}\, \exp(S(X)/(2\pi iN))\,\nu^{-(N+1)/2}.\ } \tag{11} \] Every determinant root, its half-power mark, and the logarithmic period is retained. In the actual cyclic Ward substitution z=-t e one has X=-kappa_N t^N, so 1-X=1+kappa_N t^N is exactly the ORIGINAL norm, not an arbitrarily dropped central factor. The source/transport check is decisive. Under x->x+H_N, g_D multiplies by (1-z)/nu, while S changes by 2pi i V. Their factors in (11) combine to 1-z, exactly (8). Under x->x+2pi i, g_D returns to itself and S changes by 2pi iN V, giving 1-X. Thus the n-step quotient is precisely the finite product (5), with its central norm and branch marks still present. The raw finite polynomial also retains its affine source: \[ f_N(Q_Nz)-(1-z)f_N(z)=z^N/N. \tag{12} \] On the nilpotent quotient z^N=0, (11) has central factor congruent to one and g_D reduces to f_N. This is a canonical projection in the logarithmic z-jet ring: the Log z terms first occur with z^N. It is not a literal evaluation of Log of a nilpotent matrix. For moving tensor sources or nonzero central norm, (11)--(12) must be retained. Nilpotent-jet agreement does not prove that the two-nome completion preserves the actual whole normal source. The formula has the established rational quantum-dilogarithm coverage described in [the existing finite/continuous torsor note](rational_quantum_dilogarithm_torsor.md). Its proof here is the exact original Ward product and the two normal identities (9), without adopting that literature's proof. ## 6. The completion still is not an ordinary meromorphic H-line Fix real x<0. The function (7) has exact SIMPLE zeros \[ H_k=(x-2\pi i)/k\longrightarrow0. \tag{13} \] Indeed Re H_k<0, both nomes have modulus<1, and w(H_k)=exp(2pi i k)=1. Only the numerator's first factor 1-w vanishes; the remaining product and the denominator are nonzero, since |Q|,|Qtilde|,|z|<1. Moreover w'(H_k)!=0. This proves simplicity directly. A nonzero horizontal frame of a rank-one meromorphic line at zero cannot have these accumulating interior zeros. A fixed algebraic Puiseux gauge cannot remove them. Thus the completion does NOT repair the strict one-parameter criterion globally either. This does not prevent a finite polar ASYMPTOTIC along the physical positive-imaginary sequence. On a fixed marked compact annulus 0<rho<=|z|<=r<1, the actual finite sum for log D_N and elementary trapezoid bounds give \[ \log D_N(z)=-\operatorname{Li}_2(z)/H_N -\tfrac12\operatorname{Log}(1-z)+O(1/N). \] The central factor in (10) is exponentially small in its logarithm on this chart, because X=z^N. Therefore \[ \log\Psi_N(x)=-\operatorname{Li}_2(z)/H_N -\tfrac12\operatorname{Log}(1-z)+O(1/N). \tag{14} \] For a direct proof of the leading integral, expand integral_0^1 t Log(1-z exp(2pi it))dt=-Li_2(z)/(2pi i); the endpoint correction is the displayed -Log(1-z)/2. Uniform derivative bounds on |z|<=r give the error. This is a statement about the specified root sequence and chart, not an ordinary meromorphic H-germ or a global geometric-knot norm. ## 7. The usable target for the whole-period program The strict selected meromorphic-line polar-character theorem remains a valid sufficient condition. It cannot be inferred from the actual local q-factorial atom: both its original and completed forms give explicit obstructions. The natural exact local target instead keeps the cyclotomic divisors, the independent power/normal direction of (3)--(6), the two-nome difference presentation (8), and the central Heisenberg/norm-root period (11). The completion is not permission to replace the already selected Kashaev source by a convenient periodic factor. It has the same finite nilpotent jets but additional difference-constant period data. A knot comparison must carry those data, every peripheral factor, the actual internal projectors and its selected contraction. No topological invariant, global source descent, or volume conjecture is proved by this local construction. [Exact source identities and high-precision root/zero audit](../experiments/audit_unfolded_atom_two_nome_source.py). The audit passes at 80 decimal digits: 21 fixed-root expansions, 24 exceptional-slope limits, nine exact rational-slope telescopes, four generic two-nome shift pairs, 14 physical-root constants with both marked source transports, 12 exact finite-field affine-source polynomials, six accumulating simple zeros, and 12 independently bounded physical-root sequence cases. The two normal-coordinate identities in (9) also pass symbolic verification. The [saved results](../experiments/unfolded_atom_two_nome_source_results.json) record every case. These finite checks support the proofs above; they do not assert uniformity in growing n for the fixed-n normal limits. [Independent proof audit](unfolded_atom_two_nome_independent_audit.md) checks the sectorial estimate, full root constant, norm-root power, two transports, accumulating simple zeros and trapezoid endpoint.

title: Independent audit of the whole Ward atom and its two-nome completion
text: # Independent audit of the whole Ward atom and its two-nome completion 27 October 2026. Independent proof pass of [the cyclotomic-divisor and two-nome construction](unfolded_atom_cyclotomic_divisors_and_two_nome_source.md), especially Sections 2, 3, 5 and 6. The fixed-level sectorial nature of the assertions is necessary and is stated in that note. This audit does not promote its finite root formula to an ordinary meromorphic parameter germ, a whole selected-knot source, or a volume theorem. ## 1. Fixed-level sectorial expansions and the normal-slope norm For a fixed primitive n-th root, split the absolutely convergent logarithm sum into m divisible by n and its complement. In a closed negative-real epsilon sector the nonresonant denominators have a uniform positive bound: for m times absolute epsilon small this is the finite root separation, and for it large the radial modulus is bounded below. Their differences from the root value are bounded by a constant times m times absolute epsilon. For the resonant terms the bound \[ \left|\frac1{1-e^u}+\frac1u-\frac12\right|\leq C|u| \] holds on that sector, using its Taylor expansion near zero and radial bounds outside a disk. Geometric decay in z then sums the errors. This proves the displayed O(epsilon) estimate uniformly on |z| at most r less than one, with n fixed. Its constant may depend on n; it does not give an estimate for growing n. Putting U=exp(t n epsilon), each resonant term of the log ratio has limit -t z^(kn)/k. The nonresonant difference is O(epsilon). Uniformity for compact t follows after absorbing exp(C m absolute epsilon) into a slightly larger z disk. Thus the exceptional value is exactly (1-z^n)^t with its z=0 mark. At t=1 the actual identity F(Q,zQ^n)/F(Q,z)=(z;Q)_n proves its norm interpretation without an interchange of two limits. The rational-slope telescope uses its different shifted arguments; it is not an off-exceptional identity claiming that the first ratio raised to a power is that product. ## 2. The root completion constants, including the source half-power Write c=2 pi i, H=c/N+epsilon, X=exp(Nx), V=Log(1-X). Direct inversion, not an asymptotic approximation, gives \[ \widetilde H=4\pi^2/H+cN,\quad \frac1{\widetilde H}=\frac1{N^2\epsilon}+\frac1{cN},\quad w=X\exp(\gamma\widetilde H),\quad \gamma=1-x/c. \] The first-nome constant after its polar term is log D_N minus V/2. The dual n=1 atom has constant -Li_2(X)/(cN)+(gamma-1/2)V. Subtracting these two constants cancels their entire simple polar asymptotic term and gives \[ \Psi_N=D_N\exp(\operatorname{Li}_2(X)/(cN))(1-X)^{x/c-1}. \] With nu=(1-X)^(1/N), g_D=D_N/nu^((N-1)/2) and S=Li_2(X)+(Nx)V this is precisely \[ \Psi_N=g_D\exp(S/(cN))\nu^{-(N+1)/2}. \] Both half-power factors are required: their combined exponent is -N on nu, producing the factor (1-X) inverse in the preceding formula. The first shift x to x+c/N changes S by cV and changes g_D by (1-z)/nu, which combine to the original Ward multiplier 1-z. The second shift x to x+c gives the multiplier 1-X. All these signs and the original central norm 1-X pass independently. The stated conclusion is the radial/sectorial fixed-N value; the calculation alone does not prove holomorphic extension around a whole root neighborhood. ## 3. Exact accumulating zeros are a decisive parameter obstruction For fixed real x less than zero, put H_k=(x-c)/k. Its real part is negative, so both infinite products in the actual defining ratio converge. Since 4 pi squared plus 2 pi i x equals c(x-c), one has w(H_k)=exp(ck)=1. Only the numerator factor 1-w vanishes: every remaining numerator factor is 1-Qtilde^j with modulus of Qtilde less than one, and the denominator has modulus of z and Q less than one. The derivative of w at H_k is nonzero. These are therefore exact simple zeros, accumulating at H=0 inside its product domain. A nonzero horizontal solution of a meromorphic rank-one connection at zero is nonzero at every sufficiently small nonzero ordinary point, by uniqueness of its scalar differential equation. Such a solution cannot have these zeros. A finite algebraic ramification and a fixed nonzero Puiseux meromorphic gauge do not remove them. The uncompleted atom already has accumulating nonzero cyclotomic exponential singularities. These two explicit facts forbid an automatic ordinary meromorphic-line interpretation of either atom. They do not prohibit cancellations in a fully specified word/source. ## 4. The physical-root leading estimate has the stated sign For g(t)=t Log(1-z exp(ct)), elementary trapezoid summation gives sum_(j=1)^(N-1) g(j/N)=N integral_0^1 g-(g(0)+g(1))/2+O(1/N). Termwise integration on |z| less than one gives integral g=-Li_2(z)/c. Thus log D_N=-Li_2(z)/H_N-Log(1-z)/2+O(1/N), uniformly on a fixed marked compact z chart. The remaining logarithm in the exact completion formula is exponentially small there because X=z^N. The note's physical-root estimate follows with its negative one-half logarithmic term. It does not supply a selected geometric knot period or a uniform estimate across the accumulating divisors.

title: Unfolding the actual Ward jets gives a marked dilogarithm period
text: # Unfolding the actual Ward jets gives a marked dilogarithm period Research proof, 27 October 2026. A product-preserving fixed-N formalization with reduced scalar symbols is obstructed under the regularity hypotheses of [the fixed-root audit](fixed_root_formal_ward_obstruction.md). Their coherent all-level factorial jets do admit an unfolding. This note constructs it and identifies its cyclotomic pole, regular part, norm-root gauge, and local Heisenberg regulator by direct formulas. This is a theorem about the literal Ward factorial block. It does not identify the selected full knot contraction with a geometric period, or prove the volume conjecture. No published asymptotic or quantum-dilogarithm theorem is a premise of the proof. ## 1. The actual jets and a faithful all-level unfolding Let Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N), N>=2. The actual nilpotent Ward block has the finite factorial gauge f_N(z)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) z^j/(Q_N;Q_N)_j, with z=-t e and e^N=0. Every denominator in this formula is nonzero. Its constant term is one. The literal relation is f_N(Q_N z)=(1-z)f_N(z) mod z^N. (1) Consider a proposed unfolding F(Q,z)=sum_j c_j(Q)z^j with each c_j rational in Q and regular at Q_N for all sufficiently large N. If its restrictions modulo z^N give these actual jets at every sufficiently large level, then necessarily c_j(Q)=1/(Q;Q)_j. (2) Indeed fix j and use every N>j outside the finite exceptional set. The rational function c_j(Q)-1/(Q;Q)_j vanishes at infinitely many distinct Q_N, so is zero. Existence is the displayed series F(Q,z)=sum_(j>=0) z^j/(Q;Q)_j. (3) Thus all-level rational coefficient data, rather than a chosen levelwise continuation, determine one formal function. No bound on the degrees of c_j as j grows was assumed. The same argument works for any specified family of nilpotent jets with such a rational coefficient unfolding; it proves uniqueness, not existence for an arbitrary family or for an unspecified whole knot period. Coefficient comparison gives the exact equation and normalization F(Q,Qz)=(1-z)F(Q,z), F(Q,0)=1. (4) Over Q(Q)[[z]], these conditions also determine F uniquely. For |Q|<1 it agrees with the ordinary convergent quantum factorial F(Q,z)=1/(z;Q)_infinity near z=0. This analytic statement follows directly by iterating (4), or from the coefficient identity below; it is not used to justify a root specialization of the infinite product. The nilpotent jets in (1) do not on their own define a value of F at a root for nonnilpotent z. The cyclotomic pole must first be retained. The rational coefficient hypothesis excludes arbitrary unrelated periodic factors at different levels; it is not a claim that any transseries or multivalued modular completion is thereby fixed without additional markings. ## 2. The formal logarithm and its exact cyclotomic pole Take the z-adic logarithm, with constant term zero. Equation (4) gives directly log F(Q,z)=sum_(m>=1) z^m/[m(1-Q^m)]. (5) There is no convergence assumption in (5). For fixed m it is a rational identity in Q. Fix a primitive root zeta of order N and write Q=zeta exp(h). The expansion is coefficientwise in z, with one possible h^(-1) term. Put X=z^N. Terms m not divisible by N are regular in h. For m=kN, 1/(1-exp(kN h))=-1/(kN h)+1/2+O(h). Consequently the polar coefficient is exactly A_(-1)(X)=[h^(-1)]log F=-Li_2(X)/N^2. (6) Here Li_2(X)=sum_(k>=1)X^k/k^2 is first a formal power series. On a marked punctured curve it has its usual analytic continuation fixed from this germ. Formula (6) is a coefficient evaluation, not a limiting assertion about a selected knot sequence. This gives a useful logarithmic-coordinate interpretation. Passing to the N-th cyclotomic resonance retains the terms with indices divisible by N. Their denominators supply a second factor kN, so the resonant logarithm coefficient is a dilogarithm. Keeping only a bare nilpotent special fiber would miss exactly this term. ## 3. The regular part is the marked cyclic dilogarithm Define, with the z=0 branch fixed, D_N(z)=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-zeta^j z)^(j/N). Its formal logarithm is well defined. The elementary weighted root sum is sum_(j=1)^(N-1) j zeta^(jm) =N/(zeta^m-1) for N not dividing m, =N(N-1)/2 for N dividing m. For the first equality, differentiate the finite geometric sum and evaluate at the nontrivial N-th root zeta^m. This identity and (5) give the entire constant coefficient: [h^0]log F=log D_N(z)-(1/2)Log(1-X). (7) Indeed the nonresonant terms give log D_N minus its resonant part, and the resonant constant term is Li_1(X)/(2N). Combining them gives precisely (7), with its sign and factor one half. In a formal exponential line the first two coefficients are therefore F(zeta exp(h),z) =exp(-Li_2(X)/(N^2 h)) D_N(z)(1-X)^(-1/2)(1+O(h)). (8) Equation (8) is a coefficientwise formal statement in z and h. It is not a uniform rootwise asymptotic estimate or a permission to evaluate a divergent infinite product first. All logarithmic and square-root branches are continued from z=0 together. ## 4. Identification with the actual normalized norm-root gauge Use the actual cyclic Ward order near M=1, kappa=M-M^(-1), kappa_N=M^N-M^(-N), A_N=R[e]/(e^N-(-1)^(N+1)kappa_N), sigma(e)=zeta e, z=-t e. Then X=z^N=-kappa_N t^N, and the full determinant character is 1-X=1+kappa_Nt^N=Norm(1+t e). (9) Mark nu=(1-X)^(1/N) by nu=1 at the nilpotent fiber. The cyclic product satisfies the exact transport and norm identities D_N(zeta z)/D_N(z)=(1-z)/nu, Norm D_N(z)=nu^(N(N-1)/2). (10) The first follows by subtracting its two logarithms using the weighted root sum; the second follows by multiplying all its deck translates. Both identities hold on the common marked root cover, not with independent fractional powers chosen per factor. Define g_D=D_N(z)/nu^((N-1)/2). (11) It has Norm g_D=1 and sigma g_D=((1+t e)/nu)g_D. At kappa=0 it has constant coefficient one and reduces exactly to the actual finite factorial gauge f_N(-t e): equation (1) determines that nilpotent unit coefficient by coefficient. The [norm-root transfer theorem](cyclic_ward_norm_root_period.md) constructs a meridian-regular norm-one gauge with precisely these properties. Their ratio is sigma invariant, hence scalar in R; its N-th power is one and its identity mark is one. Thus the two gauges agree exactly on the completed marked cover. This identifies the actual normalized Ward gauge with the defined cyclic dilogarithm, rather than only comparing their norms. For even N the half power in (11) has its identity square-root mark. The disconnected phase sheets are retained, not equated. Formula (7) may now be written particularly simply as [h^0]log F=log g_D-(1/2)Log nu. (12) The meridian-regular unit interpretation of (10)--(12) is over the characteristic-zero cyclotomic coefficient field, retaining all factorial denominators. No arithmetic integrality at those denominators is asserted. ## 5. The local Heisenberg regulator is reconstructed On the marked logarithmic cover of X away from 0,1,infinity put U=Log X, V=Log(1-X), S=Li_2(X)+UV, R=Li_2(X)+(1/2)UV. Direct differentiation gives dS=U dV, dR=(1/2)(U dV-V dU). (13) Thus U/N, V/N and S/N^2 are the coordinates of the usual Heisenberg period matrix Pi_N=[1 U/N S/N^2; 0 1 V/N; 0 0 1]. The right connection Pi_N^(-1)dPi_N has entries dU/N and dV/N on the first superdiagonal and zero central entry, by (13); equivalently dPi_N=Pi_N Omega_N. More explicitly, U/N=Log z, V/N=Log nu, S/N^2=-A_(-1)+Log z Log nu, R/N^2=-A_(-1)+(1/2)Log z Log nu. (14) Equations (6), (9), and the actual norm-root mark therefore reconstruct the full local flat period from the unfolded Ward factorial and its source. Its real regulator is D(X)=Im Li_2(X)+Re(U) Im(V), dD=Re(U)d Im(V)-Re(V)d Im(U). (15) This is the Bloch--Wigner local regulator, with the same marked logs. Individual Li_2 pole coefficients alone omit the displayed logarithmic metric term. No knot fundamental-class constant or orientation is supplied merely by this local calculation. These logarithmic formulas live on the generic marked punctured cover. They do not assign Log(0) to the nilpotent special fiber; there the regular jet and its divided source are kept instead. The actual divided cyclic source is tied to the pole by an explicit first-normal identity. Since kappa_N=N kappa+O(kappa^2), formula (6), with X=-kappa_Nt^N, gives partial_kappa A_(-1)|_(kappa=0)=t^N/N. The literal polynomial source from the cyclic Ward block obeys [(sigma f_N(-t e)-(1+t e)f_N(-t e))/kappa]_(kappa=0) =-t^N=-N partial_kappa A_(-1)|_(kappa=0). (16) This directly compares the actual normal source with the unfolded cyclotomic period coefficient. The same scalar t^N is the first-normal group-transfer character B_0(1+t e). The source, norm-root transfer, and period pole are three specified realizations of this one local normal datum. ### 5.1 The resonant pole is an exact divided-power tensor correction There is also an operator realization of this pole on the genuine integral complete-color lift. It is important to use that lift here, rather than suppose that a fixed-root typical color is a generic-q quantum-group module. On b factors let C(Q) be the total actual raising operator. Its individual factors have N-th power zero for every generic Q. The q-multinomial formula then shows that J_b(Q)=C(Q)^N/(1-Q^N) is regular at Q_N. Denote its root value by J_b. It lowers total integer position by N, so J_b^b=0. The [divided Ward fusion proof](divided_ward_factorial_fusion.md) gives the matrix definitions, all root characters, and arbitrary-block associativity. The following derivation identifies its correction directly with the whole function (3). Since C(Q) is nilpotent for generic Q, evaluating (5) at -t C(Q) involves only finitely many terms. For m<N its root value is the corresponding coefficient of log f_N(-t C). For m>=N not divisible by N, C(Q)^m has a factor 1-Q^N while its denominator is a unit, so the term vanishes at the root. For m=kN with k>=2 the numerator has k such factors and the denominator only one, so it also vanishes. The remaining term, m=N, is exactly (-t)^N J_b/N. Consequently [F(Q,-t C(Q))]_root =exp[(-t)^N J_b/N] f_N(-t C). (16a) Here the exponential terminates before its b-th power. Equivalently, if A_i are the individual raising operators dressed by all later K factors, q-binomial expansion gives product_(i=b,...,1) f_N(-t A_i) =exp[(-t)^N J_b/N] f_N(-t C). (16b) Thus the exact finite tensor defect is the evaluated resonant logarithm of the all-level function. In the coordinate of (6), C(Q)^N=(1-Q^N)J_b(Q)=-N h J_b+O(h^2). Substituting this into -Li_2((-t C(Q))^N)/(N^2 h) gives the same (-t)^N J_b/N; all its higher dilogarithm powers vanish after specialization. This comparison uses the moving representation and retains its first normal. Substituting C^N=0 before taking the quotient would delete the entire correction. This is a general tensor theorem, with a nilpotence bound independent of N for fixed b. It is not a scalar growth theorem. Ordinary pivotal closure kills a degree-N lowering insertion. A marked missing-edge insertion can compensate that degree, and its divided Hopf-adjoint pairing with the literal cut is computed in the fusion note. A source comparison must retain that relative pairing before contraction. ## 6. A controlled norm theorem on an actual cyclic gauge chart The local reconstruction also admits an analytic norm estimate. This is a different parameter direction from the fixed-root h in (6)--(8): now N varies, Q_N=exp(2pi*i/N), and hbar_N=2pi*i/N. Fix 0<r<1 and use the branches continued from z=0. Uniformly for |z|<=r, Log g_(D,N)(z) =-Li_2(z)/hbar_N-(1/2)Log(1-z)+O_r(1/N). (17) To prove it, put f_z(x)=x Log(1-z exp(2pi*i*x)). The function and its first two x derivatives are uniformly bounded on this compact chart. The finite product is Log D_N(z)=sum_(j=1)^(N-1) f_z(j/N). Trapezoidal Euler summation therefore gives Log D_N=N integral_0^1 f_z(x)dx -(1/2)Log(1-z)+O_r(1/N). Termwise integration of the absolutely convergent logarithmic series gives integral_0^1 f_z=-Li_2(z)/(2pi*i). The normalization in (11) changes this by O_r(r^N), since Log nu_N=Log(1-z^N)/N. This proves (17), with both upper and lower norm control. It is an estimate of the specific marked cyclic gauge already identified in Section 4, not a choice of a new quantum state. For example an explicit bound for the absolute remainder in (17) is B_r/(12N)+r^N/[2(1-r^N)], B_r=4pi r/(1-r)+4pi^2 r/(1-r)^2. The displayed B_r bounds |f_z''|. The ordinary composite trapezoidal remainder, multiplied by N, gives its first term; |Log(1-z^N)|<=r^N/(1-r^N) gives the second. Thus no interchange of a divergent infinite root product and a limit is used. In particular its inverse has rate (2pi/N)log|g_(D,N)(z)^(-1)| -> Im Li_2(z). (18) The full local regulator uses the logarithmic metric term in (15). On a marked chart define the metrized inverse gauge by ||g_(D,N)^(-1)(z)||_reg =|g_(D,N)^(-1)(z)| exp[(N/(2pi))Log|z| Arg(1-z)]. (19) Then (2pi/N)log||g_(D,N)^(-1)(z)||_reg -> D(z), (20) with O_r(1/N) error on fixed compact marked subcharts. At z=0 the metric extends by continuity if needed. Formula (19) is the explicit metric on the local Heisenberg period line determined by (15); it is not an additional factor inserted into the actual Kashaev invariant. A global knot comparison must still show that its quantum period carries this metric with the prescribed signs and logarithmic transition functions. ## 7. What the local identification does not imply globally This replaces the obstructed fixed-N multiplicative comparison by an explicit coherent all-level function and its marked cyclotomic period. It proves an exact local source/gauge/regulator identification for a block built from the actual quantum matrices. To use it for the knot, the local transfer currents and their inserted moments must still be transported through the full source-preserving contraction. The selected cycle and cross-level metric cannot be inferred from agreement of local factors. For example, ordinary finite factorial ratios are regular at their roots because their polar terms cancel; extracting a pole from an individual infinite factor and forgetting that cancellation would not be a valid knot-period argument. The actual Newton period, the partially summed geometric block, and its marked knot Bloch action already exist in the other notes. Their remaining comparison must use the unfolded source complex, retaining the normal edge and all peripheral factors. Neither global source survival nor the general volume conjecture is asserted here. [Exact coefficient audit](../experiments/audit_unfolded_ward_factorial_regulator.py). [Results](../experiments/unfolded_ward_factorial_regulator_results.json). [Independent proof audit](unfolded_ward_factorial_independent_audit.md). [Independent moving-representation and cut audit](divided_ward_bridge_independent_audit.md). The [global function/source audit](global_period_rigidity_function_audit.md) records the extra selected-period information still required beyond this exact local function reconstruction.

title: Independent audit of the unfolded Ward factorial
text: # Independent audit of the unfolded Ward factorial Research audit, 27 October 2026. The formulas in [the unfolding theorem](unfolded_ward_factorial_and_regulator.md) pass an independent coefficientwise proof check. This audit does not assert a global network-period identity. ## 1. All-level uniqueness Fix a coefficient index `j`. For all sufficiently large `N>j`, the actual nilpotent jet prescribes the value `c_j(Q_N)=1/(Q_N;Q_N)_j`; neither denominator vanishes there. A nonzero rational function has finitely many zeros, while the `Q_N` are infinitely many distinct points. Thus the coefficient is uniquely `1/(Q;Q)_j`. The exceptional set can depend on `j`. No common bound in `j` on degrees or exceptional levels is required. This proves uniqueness in the specified rational coefficient class, and the displayed universal factorial supplies existence in this case. ## 2. Cyclotomic pole and constant The formal logarithm is log F(Q,z)=sum_(m>=1) z^m/[m(1-Q^m)]. Put `Q=zeta exp(h)`, with `zeta` primitive of order `N` and `X=z^N`. For `m=kN`, 1/[m(1-exp(mh))]=-1/(m^2 h)+1/(2m)+O(h). The pole is therefore `-Li_2(X)/N^2`. The resonant constant is `Li_1(X)/(2N)=-Log(1-X)/(2N)`. For `D_N=product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-zeta^j z)^(j/N)`, the coefficient of `z^m` in its logarithm is -1/(mN) sum_(j=1)^(N-1) j zeta^(jm). For nonresonant `m`, this equals `1/[m(1-zeta^m)]`, exactly the constant of `log F`. For `m=kN`, it is `-(N-1)/(2kN)`, so the whole resonant part of `log D_N` is `(N-1)Log(1-X)/(2N)`. Subtracting `Log(1-X)/2` leaves precisely the resonant constant of `log F`. This checks the sign and every factor of `N` in the pole and regular part. The parameter `h=Log(Q/zeta)` here is a fixed-root deformation parameter. It is not the earlier large-level parameter `Log q` with `q_N=exp(pi*i/N)`. ## 3. Norm-root gauge and its uniqueness The marked cyclic product satisfies D_N(zeta z)/D_N(z)=(1-z)/(1-X)^(1/N), product_(a=0)^(N-1) D_N(zeta^a z) =(1-X)^((N-1)/2). Both follow directly by rearranging the marked logarithms, hence hold for even and composite `N` as well. With `nu=(1-X)^(1/N)`, the gauge g_D=D_N/nu^((N-1)/2) has norm one and the required normalized cyclic transport. Its nilpotent specialization has constant one and solves the same coefficient recurrence as the literal actual factorial. It therefore equals that finite factorial modulo `e^N`. The ratio of this gauge and the previously constructed norm-root gauge is sigma invariant, hence scalar in the completed base: the basis `1,e,...,e^(N-1)` has distinct sigma eigenvalues. Its norm is its `N`-th power. The identity marking forces this scalar to be one. This proves equality on the completed common marked cover, rather than merely equality of norms. The even-`N` square root is fixed by the same identity mark. For the actual cyclic sign `e^N=(-1)^(N+1)kappa_N`, substitution `z=-te` gives `X=-kappa_N t^N` and `1-X=1+kappa_N t^N`, with no remaining parity sign. ## 4. Period and source conventions For `S=Li_2(X)+UV`, `U=Log X`, `V=Log(1-X)`, direct differentiation gives `dS=U dV`. Thus the stated Heisenberg matrix has `Pi^(-1)dPi` with zero central entry; equivalently its right equation is `dPi=Pi Omega`. The opposite Maurer--Cartan convention would require a different central coordinate. Since `d kappa_N/d kappa=N` at completion, partial_kappa[-Li_2(-kappa_N t^N)/N^2]_(kappa=0)=t^N/N. The actual divided affine source is `-t^N`, exactly minus `N` times this normal derivative. The local Bloch--Wigner logarithmic metric term is retained by the displayed regulator formula. ## 5. Identity-meridian formal rigidity is already available [The closed-braid period note](closed_braid_period_line.md), Section 4, already proves that an Artinian representation with every meridian congruent to identity factors through knot abelianization. Its induction is valid: if all meridians agree modulo `m^r` and lie in `I+m`, their pairwise commutators lie in `m^(r+1)`. A Wirtinger crossing then equates consecutive understrand meridians modulo `m^(r+1)`. A knot has one connected understrand cycle, so all agree at the next order. Nilpotence terminates the induction. For matrix groups this argument does not require characteristic zero. More generally it applies whenever the identity congruence filtration satisfies `[G_r,G_s] subset G_(r+s)`. For the present `SL_2` application it proves the stated Artin functor equality and the claimed formal inability to reach nonabelian geometry from the identity representation. It says nothing analogous about a noncentral parabolic meridian or a different residual representation.

title: A uniform Frobenius base for the source and its marked period
text: # A uniform Frobenius base for the source and its marked period Research note, 26 October 2026. This places the actual scalar source coefficients at all levels on one difference base, retaining the Frobenius coordinate and root phases. A standard multiplicative-to- additive group model resolves the quantum--meridian point. The normalized two-channel source algebra extends there. A second marked chart evaluates the original central-pole normalization as a whole. The resulting Frobenius period is explicit and regular in h^2. This is the universal root-center period, not the knot's selected Bloch period. The global source comparison and volume conjecture remain unproved. ## 1. Keep the Frobenius coordinate independent before restricting a root Use the fixed literature parameter q_N=exp(pi*i/N) and meridian M. Introduce independent coordinates q,M,w and the finite phase cover zeta^4=1, U=w^2, sigma(q)=q, sigma(M)=qM, sigma(w)=-w, sigma(zeta)=zeta. (1.1) The actual root graph is Gamma_N: q=q_N, w=M^N, zeta=i^(1-N). (1.2) It is sigma-stable because q_N^N=-1. The phases are exactly zeta_N=q_N^(N(1-N)/2), epsilon_N=(-1)^N=-zeta_N^2, eta_N=i^(N+3)=zeta_N^3. No phase is reset independently at a level. The coefficient field on each phase component is C(q,M,w), with constant field C(q,U). (1.3) For a proof, sigma^2 fixes w and scales M by q^2. A rational invariant in M cannot have a finite nonzero pole, since its infinite q^2 orbit would also be poles. It is therefore Laurent in M, and invariance forces all nonzero M exponents to vanish. The remaining sigma invariance is w->-w, giving C(q,w^2). Adjoining the shift T gives the exact relations TM=qMT, Tw=-wT. Under (1.2), the second is the ordinary root identity T M^N=q_N^N M^N T. Thus this base extends the literature coefficient algebra and recovers it at each specified root. It does not impose monodromy one on a quantum-A module. Here w is a half-Frobenius meridian coordinate; it is not the geometric longitude or the norm-torsor spectral variable. The original normalization functions are now fixed rational functions: rho=q-q^(-1), f=M-M^(-1), d=zeta^3 f/(w-w^(-1)), C_cut=-zeta U/[(U-1)(U+1)], epsilon=-zeta^2, delta=rho(M^2-M^(-2)), nu=epsilon rho^2, A=epsilon rho(M+M^(-1)) *(qM^2-q^(-1)M^(-2))/(w+w^(-1)). (1.4) They restrict to the actual full ADO dimension, cut line and adjacent-source overlap. Direct substitution gives sigma(d)/d=-f(qM)/f(M), sigma(C_cut)=C_cut. The central divisor U=1 and the half-root sign of w are retained. ## 2. Root graphs give a genuine algebraic rigidity test On each fixed phase component, the union of Gamma_N for infinitely many N in its residue class modulo four is Zariski dense. Indeed clear denominators of a proposed identity and write P(q,M,w)=sum_(a,b) f_(a,b)(q)M^a w^b. Let D_M be the span of its finitely many M exponents. If N>D_M, the exponents a+Nb for distinct pairs (a,b) are distinct. Restriction to Gamma_N is therefore zero only if every f_(a,b)(q_N) is zero. Infinitely many distinct q_N force these fixed polynomials to vanish. This proves the density assertion, including complex coefficients and every phase component. There is a finite-degree version over a number field K. After clearing denominators let D_q be the q degree and D_M the M exponent span. If N>D_M, phi(2N)>[K:Q] D_q, (2.1) then an exact whole-graph identity at that one level proves the generic identity on that phase component. The algebraic degree of q_N over K is at least phi(2N)/[K:Q], so each polynomial f_(a,b) has degree too small to vanish at q_N unless it is zero. For K=Q(i), the sufficient bound is phi(2N)>2D_q. The graph must lie in the domain of the cleared comparison. The degree hypotheses are essential: w-M^N vanishes on a single graph, and a cyclotomic polynomial vanishes at its q_N. Neither satisfies the relevant strict bound. Checking only M=1,w=1, or a few unspecified meridian samples, is not a whole-graph certificate. The actual knot period is not assumed to have this fixed rational presentation or these degree bounds. The test concerns source coefficients and proposed algebraic comparison maps once their bounds have been established. ## 3. The deformation group is an existing definition The standard group scheme G^(lambda)=Spec R[t,1/(1+lambda t)] is recalled in [Mezard--Romagny--Tossici, Section 1.2](https://arxiv.org/html/1104.2222v1#S1.SS2). We use this definition with lambda=rho and M=1+rho*t. Its group law and inverse follow directly by multiplying M: t*tprime=t+tprime+rho*t*tprime, t^(-1)=-t/(1+rho*t). (3.1) For rho invertible it is G_m, while its rho=0 fiber is G_a. This is existing group-scheme theory. Only the abstract and this definition were consulted; no isogeny, extension, or classification proof from that source is assumed here. Symmetric source coordinates near M=1 are s=(M-M^(-1))/rho, c=M+M^(-1), c^2-rho^2 s^2=4, M=(c+rho*s)/2. (3.2) This is the selected c=2 chart of the same deformation, since s=t(2+rho*t)/(1+rho*t). Its group law is (s,c)*(sprime,cprime) =((s cprime+c sprime)/2, (c cprime+rho^2 s sprime)/2). (3.3) Multiplication preserves the displayed norm; associativity follows either by expansion or by the M multiplication law. On the exceptional identity fiber rho=0,c=2 it becomes addition of s. This resolves the ideal (rho,M-1) in the meridian chart. The original meridian step is multiplication by (1,q+q^(-1)): sigma(s)=((q+q^(-1))s+c)/2, sigma(c)=(rho^2 s+(q+q^(-1))c)/2. (3.4) It preserves c^2-rho^2s^2 and has determinant one. Meridian inversion is (s,c,w)->(-s,c,w^(-1)); direct multiplication gives the relation inversion*sigma*inversion=sigma^(-1). At the exceptional identity fiber the action is exactly sigma(s)=s+1, sigma(w)=-w. (3.5) Charge is the ordinary multiplication map of this group. For the cubic source it is (M,w)->(M^3,w^3), equivalently s->s(c^2-1), c->c^3-3c. It intertwines the original meridian step with the third source step, retaining the charge from the actual projective source construction. ## 4. The normalized adjacent source extends over the exceptional fiber Let p=q^(-1)M^2-qM^(-2), r=sigma(p), and k=q+q^(-1). On (3.2), p/rho=(k s c-(c^2-2))/2=:p_hat, r/rho=(k s c+(c^2-2))/2=:r_hat. (4.1) Their difference is c^2-2, a unit near c=2. Thus the old point ideal (p,r) pulls back to the principal ideal (rho); its proper transform has no residual point. This resolves the nonfree rank-one factor (u,h) in the earlier cyclic source lattice. The exceptional factor rho remains a specified line and divisor; principalizing the ideal does not discard that source datum. Normalize the source numerators by their recorded factor nu: d_hat=delta/nu=epsilon*s*c, a_hat=A/nu=c*r_hat/(w+w^(-1)). (4.2) Here epsilon^2=1 on the phase cover. These are regular on the chosen chart with w+w^(-1) invertible. The two coefficient matrices from the actual source become t_1_hat=[d_hat a_hat;0 0], t_2_hat=[0 0;a_hat d_hat]. On the exceptional identity fiber, d_hat=2 epsilon*s, a_hat=2(2s+1)/(w+w^(-1)). (4.3) At s=0,w=1 their matrix-algebra generators have nonzero units: a_hat=1 and a_hat^2-d_hat^2=1. Thus their multiplicity algebra and local scalar comparison torsor extend over the joint quantum--meridian degeneration. This resolves the shrinking fixed-level unit in the preceding normal-form note. It is the two-channel coefficient algebra that extends; the N-dimensional color factor and full knot section have not been algebraized. The original numerator matrices are exactly nu*t_i_hat on every root graph. The original projectors are t_i_hat/d_hat, so this normalization retains their full germs and defines no new state. The full affine factor has the uniform expression (1+w^(-2))*a_hat/d_hat =epsilon*w^(-1)*r_hat/s. (4.4) Its exceptional value is epsilon*w^(-1)(2s+1)/s. The pole at s=0 and the central cap at w^2=1 stay in the relative model; normalizing the numerators has not discarded either of them. The earlier obstruction to a common lattice for both unscaled projectors is consequently still present. ## 5. One marked Frobenius period realizes every prescribed root Put h=Log q and retain the original Tate mark tau=pi*i, so N h_N=tau. On the identity chart let u(h,s)=arsinh(s sinh h), M=exp(u), log w_per=(tau/h)arsinh(s sinh h). (5.1) This is the selected solution of M-M^(-1)=rho*s with M=1 at s=0. The quotient in (5.1) is regular at h=0, since u is odd in h. More precisely log w_per=tau*s+tau*(s-s^3)h^2/6+O(h^4). It is analytic in h^2 locally for bounded s. At h=h_N it is exactly N Log M, so w_per=M^N as a whole germ. Translation by q gives u->u+h, hence w_per->exp(tau)w_per=-w_per. Thus this one period section respects the original meridian action and recovers (1.2), rather than choosing unrelated sections at different levels. At the exceptional fiber it is the horizontal period dlog w_per=tau ds, w_per(0)=1, w_per=exp(tau*s). (5.2) This is an algebraic line with connection and a marked horizontal period, not a rational function of s. A regular algebraic group homomorphism G_a->G_m is constant: its defining function is an invertible polynomial, hence constant, and its identity value is one. Thus the nonzero Tate marking cannot be replaced by an algebraic character on the exceptional additive fiber. Retaining the period comparison is necessary even though its coefficient group and connection are algebraic. All normalized scalar source formulas in (4.1)--(4.3), and the source step (3.4), are even in h after this period section is substituted on a fixed phase component. Indeed c=2sqrt(1+s^2 sinh^2 h), k=2cosh h, and w_per are all even in h. This parity does not assert parity or regularity of the knot's geometric exponential exp(S/h). ## 6. The pole normalization becomes a marked regular evaluation The point s=0,w=1 alone does not evaluate d/rho: its expression is zeta^3*s/(w-w^(-1)). Retain the second chart w=1+s*ell, ell invertible. (6.1) Then the whole normalized dimension and cap are regular: d/rho=zeta^3*w/[ell(w+1)], s*C_cut=-zeta*w^2/[ell(w+1)(w^2+1)]. (6.2) Their complete values are zeta^3/(2ell) and -zeta/(4ell). The actual graph fixes the slope, not only the point: ell_N=(dw/ds)|_(s=0)=N rho_N/2. (6.3) Combining (6.2)--(6.3) recovers exactly d_N(1)=zeta_N^3/N. On the uniform period section this slope is ell(h)=tau*sinh h/h, d(h,0)=zeta^3*h/tau. (6.4) Thus the central normalization is a regular evaluation on a marked chart, including its transverse root-graph direction. No separate zero or pole was evaluated. At the exceptional fiber ell=tau; the period marking fixes that value. The meridian translates this marked chart to the other cap charts. Its orbit is not a single invariant point; those arrows remain in the lattice/source groupoid. This construction does not make all adjacent projector arrows integral on one lattice. ## 7. Scope and verification This supplies a uniform difference base for the actual source coefficients, its standard group deformation, a regular normalized two-channel algebra, and one marked Frobenius period with exact root restrictions. It also gives an algebraic rigidity test for bounded comparisons. These replace levelwise coefficient choices by specified functions and period data. The horizontal section above is the universal Frobenius period. It is not the knot's marked Bloch regulator. An actual global source/section comparison with the positive triangulation still has to be constructed, with all matrix and lattice transitions. The root-graph density theorem does not apply to an unknown comparison without its fixed presentation and degree bounds. The source coefficient algebra does not determine the scalar coefficient of the geometric exponential in the selected period. The subsequent [whole-period reconstruction](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) extends this root-only base by an independent v=q^N and t=1/N. Its action is sigma(w)=vw, with commuting derivatives D_q=q partial_q+t^(-1)v partial_v and D_M=M partial_M+t^(-1)w partial_w. The slice v=-1 recovers the base here but is not preserved by D_q. Thus quantum-normal jets require this extension before specialization. Bounded mixed jets then reconstruct any proposed fixed algebraic comparison, including one on a marked etale shape cover. This does not algebraize the full knot state or construct the missing map. The [fixed central normalization theorem](algebraic_central_normalization.md) controls a comparison factor once its fixed finite algebraic presentation is proved. It does not supply that global comparison. The volume conjecture remains unproved. The subsequent [common Frobenius/regulator period space](common_frobenius_regulator_period_space.md) now puts this Frobenius mark and the geometric regulator action over one explicit logarithmic Heisenberg connection. Its additional Tate period J recovers all four root phases; unlike a frozen phase sheet it carries the q-direction connection. The full complete cap is -i J h/(pi*i), and the geometric exponential retains its volume term. Adjoining the rational Frobenius coordinate preserves an existing nonsplit source class, by a Laurent-coefficient retraction. Thus the common period space does not by itself supply the missing actual source comparison. [The audit](../experiments/audit_uniform_source_base.py) verifies the group law, Weyl and meridian matrices, normalized source and cap identities, and period-section translation through h^6. Four phase sheets verify bounded-degree exponent separation and cyclotomic factor degrees. Fourteen root levels verify the original phases and marked complete normalization, with 28 generic scalar root-graph specializations. These are source-base checks, not quantum-volume experiments. [Results](../experiments/uniform_source_base_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_uniform_source_base.py

title: A uniform norm group and sourced relation complex for twist knots
text: # A uniform norm group and sourced relation complex for twist knots Research note, 27 October 2026. This proves the one-relator side of the determinant reduction suggested by the 4_1 and 5_2 prototypes. The twist parameter remains arbitrary throughout. The construction comes from the actual knot-group relation, with its return-map sign and matrix normal direction retained. It does not assign a replacement quantum state or establish the selected Kashaev period's volume growth. ## 1. Uniform statement Use the signed twist presentation G_k=<a,b | a w^k=w^k b>, w=ab^(-1)a^(-1)b, k in Z, k!=0. The hyperbolic members have k<=-1 or k>=2. Set A=[1 1;0 1], B=[1 0;t 1], W=AB^(-1)A^(-1)B, z=t^2+2, v=1+t, P_k(t)=S_(k-1)(z), f_k(t)=v S_(k-1)(z)-S_(k-2)(z), (1.1) where S_(-1)=0,S_0=1,S_(j+1)=z S_j-S_(j-1), extended to all integer indices. **Theorem.** For every k!=0: 1. The pair (f_k,P_k) is obtained by powers of one explicit norm-one unit in a quadratic algebra. Its norm identity is f_k^2+t(t-2)f_k P_k-t^3 P_k^2=1. 2. The matrix return relator has an exact quadratic normal form in f_k. On t!=0, its full matrix equation generates the scheme-theoretic ideal (f_k), retaining its first jet. 3. The polynomial f_k is monic with constant term one and is squarefree, even modulo 2. The classes of t and P_k are integral units in Z[t]/(f_k). 4. At every parabolic root, the sourced relation complex is acyclic. With the orbit-volume and matrix-source marks specified below, its torsion is exactly T_k^rel=-2/[P_k(t) f_k'(t)]. (1.2) 5. The weighted residue on the full integral Riley algebra is a perfect pairing. Its branch coefficient is 1/[P_k(t)f_k'(t)], including all conjugate places. This theorem is uniform in k. The comparison T_k^rel=T_beta with the braid complex is proved by the existing exact prototype calculations for k=-1,2; a general presentation and quantum-source comparison is still required. No general Gaussian-density or volume identity is inferred merely by giving the relation torsion the same name. ## 2. A single quadratic norm group solves the twist transport Put b=t(t-2) and introduce the quadratic algebra E=Q(t)[y]/(y^2-b y-t^3). The norm of F+P y is N(F+P y)=F^2+b F P-t^3 P^2. (2.1) Let u=1+t+y. Direct multiplication gives N(u)=1, and multiplication by u in the basis 1,y is U=[1+t t^3;1 t^2-t+1], det U=1, Tr U=t^2+2. (2.2) Consequently (f_k,P_k)^t=U^k(1,0)^t (2.3) for every integer k. This follows either from the Chebyshev recurrence or from U^2-z U+I=0 and the initial values (f_0,P_0)=(1,0), (f_1,P_1)=(1+t,1). Taking norms proves f_k^2+b f_k P_k-t^3 P_k^2=1. (2.4) This is transport in an existing quadratic norm-one group, with a specified unit and source point. It is not the root-of-unity norm torsor of the quantum A-operator. The generic splitting cover has discriminant t^2(t^2+4). Twisting the diagram is not a manifold cover; those operations are not being identified. The algebra has a literal matrix realization: Y=W^(-1)-vI, Tr Y=b, det Y=-t^3, u -> W^(-1), W^(-k)=f_k I+P_k Y. (2.5) Thus (2.3) is the spectral transport of the meridian commutator itself, rather than a chosen auxiliary recurrence. ## 3. Exact matrix relator and its normal direction The base identity A W-W B=v(A-B), followed by Cayley--Hamilton, gives A W^k-W^k B=f_k(A-B). (3.1) Define V=(A-B)B^(-1)=[-t 1;-t 0], Z=(A-B)B^(-1)Y=[-t^2 2t(t-1);0 t^2], V^#=Tr(V)I-V=[0 -1;t -t]. The inverse return relation is A W^k B^(-1)W^(-k)=I+P_k f_k Z+f_k^2 V. Its inverse, with the same output-minus-input convention as dF-I in the braid complex, is R_k=W^k B W^(-k)A^(-1) =I-P_k f_k Z+f_k^2 V^#. (3.2) These are exact identities. The first follows from (3.1) and (2.5). For the second use determinant one and adj(I+X)=I+Tr(X)I-X in dimension two. In particular Tr R_k=2-t f_k^2, R_k-I=-P_k f_k Z modulo f_k^2, Tr Z=0, det Z=-t^4. (3.3) The trace alone loses the first normal direction. The marked matrix equation retains it in the nonzero vector Z. For completeness, the full ideal of entries of R_k-I in Q[t,t^(-1)] is (f_k). The entries give P_k f_k and f_k^2, since t is a unit. Equation (2.4) gives (f_k,P_k)=(1), so these two generators generate f_k itself. The converse inclusion is immediate from (3.2). This is a statement about schemes, including nilpotent test rings. ## 4. All parabolic roots are simple; the source unit is integral For k>0, f_k has degree 2k-1 and leading coefficient one. For k=-h<0 it has degree 2h and leading coefficient one, using S_(-j-2)=-S_j. Since S_j(2)=j+1, f_k(0)=k-(k-1)=1. (4.1) To prove squarefreeness uniformly, work over F_2. Put P(t)=overline(S_(k-1)(t)), Q(t)=overline(S_(k-2)(t)). Frobenius and t^2+2=t^2 give overline(f_k)=(1+t)P(t)^2+Q(t)^2, overline(f_k')=P(t)^2. Consecutive Chebyshev polynomials are coprime over every field: their recurrence reduces a common divisor to the pair S_0=1,S_(-1)=0. Thus gcd(overline(f_k),overline(f_k'))=1. Since f_k is monic, its resultant with its derivative is an odd nonzero integer. All characteristic-zero roots are therefore simple, without a genericity hypothesis. Let B_k=Z[t]/(f_k). Equation (4.1) makes t an integral unit. Equation (2.4) gives, in this algebra, t^3 P_k^2=-1, P_k^(-1)=-t^3 P_k. (4.2) Thus the source factor is an integral unit, not a factor silently canceled only at generic complex points. ## 5. The sourced relation complex and its normalization Let O be the noncentral trace-two conjugacy class in SL_2. At a parabolic root, the pair (A,B) is irreducible because t!=0. PGL_2 conjugation has an injective three-dimensional tangent, and its quotient on O times O has coordinate t=Tr(AB)-2. Let L be the one-dimensional matrix normal line spanned by Z in (3.3), with the specified generator Z. Differentiating the return relation on the fixed-trace pair space gives the complex 0 -> sl_2 --a--> T_(A,B)(O times O) --dR_k--> L -> 0, a(xi)=([xi,A],[xi,B]), dR_k=-P_k f_k'(t) dt times Z. (5.1) The derivative kills conjugation because R_k=I. It is nonzero in the remaining direction by Sections 3--4. The complex is therefore acyclic at every root of f_k. The source normalization is explicit. Use the ordered sl_2 basis H=diag(1,-1), E=E_12, F=E_21. On a fixed trace class use nu=dK wedge de/e for the matrix entries K=G_11,e=G_12. At A use (A_11,A_12); at B use (B_11,B_21), so nu_B=-dB_11 wedge dB_21/t. Both forms are invariant under conjugation. In the four tangent coordinates (A_11,A_12,B_11,B_21), the conjugation columns and the normal vector partial_t are [a(H),a(E),a(F),partial_t] =[0 0 -1 0;2 0 0 0;0 t 0 0;-2t 0 0 1]. Its determinant is -2t. The product orbit volume has coefficient -1/t, so its value on these columns is 2. The last differential in (5.1), expressed in the marked Z basis, is -P_k f_k'. Therefore the torsion is exactly T_k^rel=2/(-P_k f_k')=-2/(P_k f_k'). (5.2) Changing the complement by a conjugation column changes neither determinant. Conjugating the pair transports all the stated volume and source marks, so the scalar is frame invariant. Reversing the return relation would reverse the sign; no unmarked sign is being ignored. ## 6. A perfect residue pairing on the entire integral algebra For a monic degree-d polynomial f define Res_f(h) to be the coefficient of t^(d-1) in the remainder of h modulo f. Set lambda_k(h)=Res_(f_k)(P_k^(-1)h). (6.1) The pairing (g,h)->Res_f(gh) on Z[t]/(f) is perfect: its matrix in 1,t,...,t^(d-1) has zeros below its anti-diagonal and ones on that diagonal. Its determinant is (-1)^(d(d-1)/2). Multiplication by the integral unit P_k^(-1) preserves perfection, proving the claim for lambda_k as well. No localization at a discriminant prime is needed for the whole algebra. After splitting into the distinct complex root lines, Lagrange interpolation gives lambda_k(h)=sum_(f_k(t_j)=0) h(t_j)/(P_k(t_j)f_k'(t_j)). (6.2) Hence the branch coefficient is exactly -T_k^rel/2. It is a canonical weighted residue in a finite integral algebra, with its conjugate branches retained. ## 7. What this settles and what it does not The denominator and the -2 source normalization are now proved uniformly on the actual twist relator side. The commutator transport, exact normal form, all-root regularity and integral residue pairing have proofs for arbitrary k. They are not conclusions inferred from the prototypes. The existing prototype computation proves T_k^rel=T_beta and Omega_beta^2=-(T_beta/2)Omega_cut^2 for k=-1,2. For arbitrary k, the next required map is the determinant- and source-preserving reduction from the braid period complex to (5.1), including its quantum lattice. The classical group relation alone does not supply that map. Even after that map, the actual global quantum source must have its regulator norm controlled across levels. This note does not prove the original volume conjecture, or replace Kashaev by the classical residue (6.1).
