The general program now uses the [arbitrary-bridge sourced complex](arbitrary_bridge_source_reduction.md), with unrestricted bridge number and crossing word. The calculation above is retained as a one-relator diagnostic. A separate executable uniform-twist audit is not attached to this proof text.

title: An actual cut with a universal complete framing pole
text: # An actual cut with a universal complete framing pole Research theorem, 27 October 2026. For every complete discrete-faithful knot representation, an exact inverse-pair insertion in the ORIGINAL braid places a noncommuting meridian on the first slot at a second physical cut. The actual prefix there is V=I. Its Fourier momentum is a Möbius coordinate whose inverse framing map and density have pole p=1, independent of the knot and first framing phase. The added crossings have a nonempty regular atom chart, so the existing nonzero geometric normal block persists. This is an actual source-preserving choice of presentation and cut. It does not replace the selected source by sampling its principal density. That density is resonant at EVERY level. Controlling its whole quantum completion and the original selected class remains the missing geometric-period theorem. Subsequent exact source calculation: the [complete first-slot localization theorem](universal_resonant_fourier_source_completion.md) proves J_(a,j)=P_N delta_(j,0) for EVERY first input, and in fact L(X_j)=P_N X_j. Thus the original regular Fourier rows j!=0 vanish identically at completeness. The missing geometric-period comparison concerns the resonant row. An [actual all-strand Euler/Cauchy formula](all_strand_euler_cauchy_cap.md) now supplies its finite source as an exact coefficient or two-point divided difference, with the entire word retained. ## 1. Choose a meridian that does not fix the reference cusp Fix a b-strand braid presenting the knot and the complete marked holonomy. Normalize the reference meridian to J=[[1,1],[0,1]]. Write its initial developed meridians as mu_1=J,...,mu_b, using the signed convention of [the actual prefix dictionary](prefix_adapted_two_position_framing_cover.md). Some mu_i has nonzero lower-left entry, since otherwise the representation is reducible. Choose the first such i. Every preceding mu_j is J, not merely another upper triangular matrix. Indeed mu_j=g J g inverse. If mu_j has lower-left zero, its unique fixed point is infinity, hence g also fixes infinity. In a torsion-free discrete projective group containing J, every upper triangular word has diagonal ratio one. Otherwise suitable conjugates of J, or their commutators with J, tend nontrivially to the identity; a nontrivial finite-order ratio gives projective torsion. This is the elementary discreteness argument already proved in the Fourier framing theorem. Such a g commutes with J. Put U=mu_i. It is nontrivial trace-two unipotent, with c=U_21 nonzero, and has the unique form U=I+c[-beta;1] * (1,beta), beta=(U_22-1)/c. (1) The rows/columns in (1) have zero contraction, so this expression retains determinant one and the actual meridian orientation. ## 2. Move it with a literal inverse pair, preserving every source factor Use inverse Hurwitz moves (X,Y) -> (Y,YXY inverse). Let P be the braid whose ACTION order is sigma_(i-1) inverse,...,sigma_1 inverse. It moves U left unchanged past the preceding J's. Insert the action words P then P inverse before the original action word beta_braid. The matrix order is R_beta_braid R_P inverse R_P=R_beta_braid. (2) The second cut is the FIRST physical slot between P and P inverse. At that level its developed meridian is exactly U; its physical prefix products are therefore V=I, U=mu_i, prefix sign sigma=-1. (3) The original first cut and its reference J are untouched. Closing the second cut with its original identity gives (2). The first output row, fixed-input source, all original pivotal caps and full d_N(M) line remain the original ones. Strand number and writhe are unchanged; the presentation acquires at most 2(b-1) crossings, independently of N. At an actual root use the genuine signed crossing matrices and their inverses. For a whole auxiliary q-normal calculation use the specified whole inverse matrices BEFORE specialization, so (2) is still an exact matrix identity and preserves all its jets. No inverse is obtained by first deleting a central norm factor. The second cut is at slot ell=0. The EXACT open meridian insertion therefore has no endpoint q^(-ell nu) character, by [the actual horizontal transport theorem](actual_open_meridian_horizontal_source_transport.md). Its Fourier dilation and scaled-frame correction are identity. The original gamma_N, x=-M/q and full meridian ratio g_N are still retained; their absence is not implied by ell=0. ## 3. The added crossings have a nonempty regular geometric chart Use the actual complete framing matrix F(r,s)=[[r,1-r],[s,-s]], s nonzero, t=r+beta s. For h preceding J's set a_h=ell_(J^h)=1+hs, b_h=ell_(U J^h) =a_h+(c/s)(1-t)(t+hs). (4) One negative move carrying U left across J has actual physical positions A,B and transfer C A=a_h/a_(h+1), B=a_(h+1)/b_(h+1), C=a_(h+1)b_h/[b_(h+1)a_h]. (5) Its five balanced coefficient atoms at completeness are A, C, 1/B, AC, C/B =a_h/a_(h+1), C, b_(h+1)/a_(h+1), b_h/b_(h+1), b_h/a_h. (6) All are different from zero and one on a NONEMPTY Zariski open. For an explicit proof, in addition to their denominator factors exclude 1-t, t+hs, t+(h+1)s, s+c(1-t). The differences from one in (6) have these nonzero factors, and C-1=-c(1-t)^2/[b_(h+1)a_h]. (7) Every displayed factor is a nonzero rational function because c is nonzero. The finite intersection over h=0,...,i-2 is nonempty over the infinite marked representation field. It also intersects any existing nonempty regular framing open for the original word. Reversing a move has A'=B/C,B'=AC,C'=1/C. Its positive atoms are AC, 1/C, C/B, A, 1/B, so the inverse path introduces no new nondegeneracy condition. This verifies admissibility of the ACTUAL new crossings rather than assuming that an arbitrary identity insertion is regular. On this common open the added critical equations are the actual crossing graph followed by its inverse. Intermediate states eliminate uniquely over local Artin rings; the marked critical scheme is the original one. Thus its two framing tangent modes and regular Morse--Bott property are unchanged. Equivalently, each inverse pair is a generating-family stabilization: in regular input/output position coordinates its added normal block has form [[0,mu],[mu,*]] with mu a unit. Its determinant is -mu^2. The explicit local mixed coefficients are C/(1-C) for the negative move and 1/(1-C') for its positive inverse, C'=1/C; they are negatives of each other and are units on (6). The original nonzero normal Gaussian therefore persists. Fourier polarizing the new cut removes the remaining framing mode as in the proved bordered-Hessian theorem. This proves persistence, not equality of every old and new formal coefficient in arbitrary Gaussian frames. The marked fundamental cycle/action calibration remains the same, since the actual inverse path adds a cancelling relative cycle. All Gaussian phases and source lines must still be transported. ## 4. The complete momentum and leading density are universal Direct conjugation of (1) gives F inverse U F =I+(c/s)[1-t;-t] * (t,1-t). Its first diagonal is k=1+(c/s)t(1-t). With the ACTUAL slot-one prefix sign -1, the balanced momentum is p=-[(F inverse U F)_12]/(k-1) =1-1/t, r=1/(1-p)-beta s. (8) Consequently (A_cut,p), A_cut=1/(1+s), are birational framing coordinates, with partial_r p=1/t^2 nonzero. No new quadratic framing cover or arbitrary change of the finite band source is introduced. The actual Fourier stationary incidence is xi=p inverse because this second cut has ell=0. The original geometric framing density is exactly Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)] =-p/[s(1-p)^2] dlog A_cut wedge dlog p. (9) Its only principal-density momentum pole is p=1, corresponding to r=infinity. At a root that point belongs to EVERY finite Fourier grid. This theorem is on the COMPLETE M=1 fiber; it does not assert a single generic-M double-pole model or freeze its normal splitting. ## 5. What has become universal, and what is still missing For the principal rational coefficient alone, the regular nodes p=Q_N^j, j=1,...,N-1, have the exact sum sum_(j=1)^(N-1) -Q_N^j/[s(1-Q_N^j)^2] =(N^2-1)/(12s). (10) This is the elementary inverse-sine-square identity already used in the source-current norm proof. It is NOT the original period: the omitted node p=1 is a pole of this coefficient, while the actual finite tensor and its raw Fourier array are regular. No principal sampling is justified at that node, and the local Gaussian expansion is not uniform near it. Higher coefficients and the full source can retain other shape-chart exclusions. Equation (8) specifies the escaping scale explicitly. If p=1-zeta/N, then r=N/zeta-beta s. (11) The fixed-label nodes near zero therefore leave every fixed compact framing chart as N grows. A fixed-r formal expansion cannot decide their selected contribution. The full quantum boundary layer, together with its actual word and current terms, must be retained. Equation (10) provides neither its missing value nor a no-cancellation theorem. More strongly, the exact actual localization just cited says the regular-node contribution of the ORIGINAL array is zero, even though the sum of this isolated PRINCIPAL coefficient is (10). That principal sum is therefore not a bulk approximation to the actual complete array. The geometric formal block can be nonzero while its exact regular-node source value vanishes. The critical-path gain is concrete: an actual source-preserving presentation now removes the prefix-dependent leading pole and the port meridian half-step for ANY complete discrete-faithful knot representation on its regular geometric branch. The chosen leading pole is the single fixed resonance p=1. This supplies a uniform location and scale for the next source comparison. It does not by itself reduce all remaining shape/global issues to a knot-independent cap or prove gate C, D or E of [the critical-path audit](critical_path_to_original_volume_conjecture.md). [Exact source, atom and normal-Hessian tests](../experiments/audit_universal_resonant_cut.py) and [saved results](../experiments/universal_resonant_cut_results.json) support the direct proof. The [independent proof audit](universal_resonant_cut_independent_audit.md) checks the actual placement, admissible chart, prefix momentum and scope of the normal-block persistence. The separate [word/source audit](universal_resonant_cut_word_audit.md) also records the explicit mixed-Hessian stabilization and a carefully scoped meridian-germ calculation with its split poles.

title: Independent audit of the actual universal resonant cut
text: # Independent audit of the actual universal resonant cut 27 October 2026. The construction in [the universal-cut theorem](universal_resonant_cut_and_actual_source.md) passes under its stated complete discrete-faithful and original regular geometric-chart hypotheses. It is an actual presentation/cut change, not only a conjugation of an abstract representation. The complete principal pole and port half-character become universal. The global selected-period comparison remains unproved. ## 1. The unchanged meridian can be moved by the specified actual word The initial braid meridians generate the knot group. If they all had lower-left entry zero, the representation would be reducible. Choose the first U with c=U_21 nonzero. A preceding upper parabolic is conjugate to J within the discrete faithful group. Its conjugator must fix infinity. An upper word with diagonal ratio not one either gives nontrivial translations tending to identity under conjugation, or has nontrivial finite projective order. Discreteness and torsion freeness exclude both. Its ratio is one, so it commutes with J and the preceding meridian is EXACTLY J. In the actual Hurwitz convention the NEGATIVE adjacent move is (J,U) -> (U,U J U^-1). Thus the indicated sequence carries U LEFT UNCHANGED. Placing this sequence P and then its inverse BEFORE the old action word means the literal operator R_beta R_P^-1 R_P. This order matters. Opening the first physical identity wire between the two words supplies the claimed prefix V=I and signed first-slot index -1. The original cut, its input/output source and all existing caps remain in place. Actual R inverses, including their full Cartan/scalar marks, give identity reclosure at every level. The added writhe is zero. The original d_N(M) line is unchanged as a rational map/lattice, not replaced by its complete value. The same inverse identity holds in the supplied whole finite auxiliary lift, hence with all its normal derivatives. None of these identities requires extending an auxiliary source-frame deformation to a knot representation. The cut is at slot ell=0, so the actual open meridian endpoint factor q^(-ell nu) is one. This removes that PORT character only. The original x=-M/q, gamma_N framing power, full g_N and every independent peripheral power remain, just as stated in the note. ## 2. Every added atom is regular on a nonempty common open Write U=I+c[-beta;1] * (1,beta), t=r+beta s, a_h=1+hs, b_h=a_h+(c/s)(1-t)(t+hs). The displayed b_h equals (F^-1 U J^h F)_11 by direct multiplication. Before each negative move the prefixes are J^h,J^(h+1),U J^(h+1), so its actual clocks and transfer are exactly A=a_h/a_(h+1), B=a_(h+1)/b_(h+1), C=a_(h+1)b_h/[b_(h+1)a_h]. The five atoms are A,C,1/B,AC,C/B. Besides their nonzero numerator and denominator factors, their differences from one are controlled by 1-A=s/a_(h+1), 1-C=c(1-t)^2/[b_(h+1)a_h], b_h-a_h=(c/s)(1-t)(t+hs), b_(h+1)-a_(h+1)=(c/s)(1-t)(t+(h+1)s), b_(h+1)-b_h=s+c(1-t). Each excluded function is nonzero because c is nonzero and t,s are independent framing coordinates. Their finite product therefore defines a nonempty Zariski open. The framing surface is irreducible, so it intersects the original nonempty regular chart. This is a general nonemptiness proof, not inference from the figure-eight tests. For the inverse positive move, A'=B/C,B'=AC,C'=1/C. Its atoms are AC,1/C,C/B,A,1/B. Thus it adds no further conditions. All inverse paths are actual reversed graphs of these same moves. For a two-POSITION transverse chart also exclude 1-2t, since the new clock has r derivative (c/s)(1-2t). This is another nonzero factor and leaves a nonempty open. The Fourier (A,p) chart itself has derivative 1/t^2 and resolves that position caustic. ## 3. The Morse normal block persists on this open The existing actual phase/critical dictionary is an isomorphism of the exponentiated critical scheme with the framed representation germ on its unit-atom charts, including local Artin rings. Adding the crossing graphs and their inverses eliminates their intermediate states uniquely and recovers the OLD fixed representation equations. Thus the new critical germ still has precisely its two B_1 tangent modes. The added 2 length(P) flow variables increase the Hessian rank by that same number. Every VARIABLE principal amplitude is a unit on the constructed open, with its original base-only line retained separately, so its transverse formal Gaussian block remains nonzero. The generating-family stabilization wording has an explicit twist unit, not an additional unproved determinant hypothesis. In the original input/output position coordinates the exact mixed Hessians from the actual coefficients are V_-=C/(1-C), V_+=1/(1-C'). For C'=1/C these satisfy V_+=-V_-. They are units on the atom open C!=0,1. Consequently the extra cross block has the indicated form [[0,mu],[mu,*]], with mu a unit up to its unit coordinate factor, and determinant -mu^2. No additional excluded function or singular quantum-gap division is required here. More explicitly, the inverse-pair generating phase can be written F(y,q)-F(y,q+delta)+S_open(z,delta), with its actual inverse marks. The y equation forces delta=0 because F_yq is a unit; the delta equation then fixes y from the old momentum. Its reduced critical phase is S_open(z,0)=S_old(z), and the added (y,delta) Hessian has determinant -F_yq^2. The intermediate position and net displacement are unimodular integer coordinates in the two added transfers. This gives the direct stabilization proof recorded in the separate [word/source audit](universal_resonant_cut_word_audit.md). The original marked action calibration continues to apply to the new admissible diagram. The inverse path cancels its canonical graph and relative contribution, with the fixed phase/base line retained. This does NOT prove equality of every old/new formal coefficient in arbitrary frames, nor a global Gaussian/source pushforward. Finite matrix inversion alone would not justify those stronger statements. ## 4. The new complete prefix and density are genuinely universal Direct multiplication gives F^-1 U F=I+(c/s)[1-t;-t] * (t,1-t), k=1+(c/s)t(1-t). With the ACTUAL balanced/factorial momentum and first-slot sign, p=-(F^-1UF)_12/(k-1)=1-1/t, r=1/(1-p)-beta s. Thus at completeness the framing map is birational, without a new quadratic cover, and Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/[s(1+s)] =-p/[s(1-p)^2]dlog A_cut wedge dlog p. The pole p=1 belongs to the INVERSE framing map and density; the momentum p(r) itself has its pole at t=0. The universal density pole is at r=infinity and lies outside the proved fixed regular framing chart. At xi=p^-1 it is the fixed Fourier node xi=1, present at every N. This exact principal formula has not been promoted to a generic-M double-pole formula or a substitute for the full quantum source. The regular-node sum (N^2-1)/(12s) is correct. It excludes precisely the singular node and is not the selected knot period. Higher coefficients, original shape-chart exclusions and relative current endpoints still need their whole completion. The source-preserving word change therefore gives a useful uniform critical target, but does not close gates C, D or E. The main note's [exact actual audit](../experiments/audit_universal_resonant_cut.py) checks its identities and normal examples. The proofs above supply the general admissibility and persistence arguments independently of those examples.

title: Independent word/source audit of the universal first-slot cut
text: # Independent word/source audit of the universal first-slot cut 27 October 2026. Proof pass of [the universal resonant-cut theorem](universal_resonant_cut_and_actual_source.md). The inverse-pair insertion is an actual source-preserving presentation change. On the established regular geometric critical branch its added crossings have a nonempty regular chart and preserve a nonzero normal block. This is not a claim about the contribution of the resonant node to the final selected finite sum. ## 1. The chosen meridian really moves left unchanged At the complete faithful discrete representation all positively oriented meridians are conjugate to J. If such a conjugate fixes infinity, its conjugating group element also fixes infinity, since J has only that fixed point. An upper triangular group word has diagonal ratio one: a ratio of absolute value different from one contracts conjugates of J toward the identity; an infinite-order unit ratio gives nontrivial such commutators approaching identity; a nontrivial finite-order ratio gives projective torsion. These contradict discreteness/torsion-freeness. Hence that conjugator commutes with J and the meridian is exactly J, not a scaled translation. The first nonupper initial meridian U therefore has only J's before it. Negative Hurwitz moves (J,U) to (U,UJU inverse), so U passes left UNCHANGED at every step. The already crossed strands behind it do not change the prefixes before its next move. This proves the stated finite action word and V=I at the FIRST physical slot. The sign sigma=-1 is the first PREFIX index, while the physical slot for the endpoint half-character is ell=0. These are distinct index conventions with the correctly stated different values. These meridians describe the q-to-one geometric critical representation. They are not the identity Frobenius-central meridians at the actual fixed-root augmentation. No center-deformation identification is needed or implied by this presentation change. ## 2. The exact finite tensor and source are unchanged In action order insert the chosen braid P followed by P inverse before the old word. In matrix order the closed operator is R_old R_P inverse R_P=R_old. Opening the new edge gives the literal coupon tensor ptr[R_old R_P inverse E_bd^(0) R_P]. Summing E_bb restores that exact identity. This leaves the first input/output source and all original pivotal caps in their original places. There is no new pivot, color, trace normalization or source vector. The writhe and strand number are unchanged. The full twist, half-Cartan scalar lines and d_N(M) must be kept in both R_P and its inverse; their common factors cancel as a matrix identity, not as separately evaluated numerical norm values. The specified whole finite inverse exists on the auxiliary q/M lift as well, so the same presentation identity preserves its normal jets. Topological invariance of an unrelated off-root lift is unnecessary. The internal cut is at ell=0. The exact half-character q^(-ell nu) is therefore one, while the actual longitude insertion, gamma_N and complete peripheral ratio still remain. In particular opening BETWEEN inverse matrices prevents canceling their inserted path weights before the second edge is reclosed. The new partial array is a real changed partial family with the same final state. ## 3. Admissibility is verified on the actual coefficient atoms Write U=I+c[-beta;1] * (1,beta), c nonzero, and t=r+beta s. At the step with h left J's put \[ a_h=1+hs,\qquad b_h=a_h+(c/s)(1-t)(t+hs). \] The four physical positions and negative transfer follow by the actual triangular prefix reconstruction, yielding exactly the five atoms in the main theorem. Their differences from one are controlled by the displayed finite list of factors. In particular \[ C-1=-c(1-t)^2/(b_{h+1}a_h),\quad b_{h+1}-b_h=s+c(1-t), \] \[ b_h-a_h=(c/s)(1-t)(t+hs). \] All are nonzero rational functions on the two-dimensional framing torsor; for example b_h has nonzero quadratic r coefficient -c/s. Their finite product is nonzero in its function field. The common regular open therefore is nonempty and intersects the old regular geometric framing open. Inverse positive atoms are permutations/ inversions of the same regular atoms, so they introduce no new identical-zero condition. This is stronger than just assuming that an arbitrary Reidemeister-II insertion has a regular shape chart. The first/second physical position pair can fail at its ordinary projection caustic. This does not invalidate the Fourier block: on this regular chart p=1-1/t has p_r=1/t squared, so the pair (A_cut,p) is etale. The bordered-Hessian theorem needs that pair, not an everywhere invertible old two-position projection. ## 4. The inverse insertion is a genuine Morse stabilization The actual crossing generating phase has a UNIT mixed Hessian on the regular atom chart, by the previously proved generating-family calculation. Fix its conserved total position and denote that phase by F(y,q), with y the intermediate first output and q the input. The inverse phase is -F(y,q+delta), with its actual inverse marks; any recorded base phase is retained. The surrounding old network has its ordinary open extension S_open(z,delta), with S_open(z,0)=S_old(z). Thus the enlarged local phase is \[ F(y,q)-F(y,q+\delta)+S_{open}(z,\delta). \tag{1} \] At delta=0 the y equation is automatic. The delta equation fixes y uniquely by the old momentum because F_yq is a unit. Its (y,delta) Hessian is \[ \begin{pmatrix}0&-F_{yq}\\-F_{yq}&*\end{pmatrix}, \qquad\det=-F_{yq}^2\ne0. \tag{2} \] The reduced critical phase is precisely S_old. Schur elimination therefore makes the enlarged Hessian congruent to its old Hessian plus (2). The original two-dimensional framing kernel is unchanged; it is not a newly assumed Gaussian complement. The intermediate position and net displacement are integer coordinates with determinant plus or minus one in the two added transfers, so this stabilization does not introduce a lattice factor or fractional cover. For a longer P the inverse pairs cancel successively from the middle. The common regular chart from Section 3 allows this induction. Equivalently the exact canonical graph followed by its inverse eliminates uniquely over local Artin rings. The critical scheme remains the original framed representation germ. This proves the Morse--Bott and nonzero normal-block assertion in the main theorem. It does not assert equality of every formal coefficient in arbitrary Gaussian gauges. All inverse flattenings, density/base lines and fixed phases must still be transported. The positive statement is on the existing REGULAR geometric branch. It does not manufacture a regular branch for an arbitrary originally degenerate diagram or for unrelated representation components. ## 5. Universal pole and its precise source limitation The raw actual first-slot conjugation gives p=1-1/(r+beta s), r=1/(1-p)-beta s, and \[ \Omega_{cut}=-\frac p{s(1-p)^2} d\log A_{cut}\wedge d\log p. \] The orientation agrees directly with Omega_cut=-dr wedge ds/ [s(1+s)]. The pole is exactly p=1, not a rescaling chosen after evaluating the state. The finite regular-node sum equals (N squared minus one)/(12s), with the main theorem's sign. This normalization places the escaping point at EVERY level's pointed Fourier node. It does not remove the resonance. The actual finite tensor is regular there, whereas the principal Gaussian density is not. Its full source, the nonuniform boundary layer and all higher shape-chart exclusions are still required. The exact presentation change and persistent nonzero partial block do not prove that this block survives the final selected source. ## Appendix: a checked first-slot meridian germ, with a split density pole This appendix does not extend the main complete Gaussian/source theorem to generic M. It computes the raw physical momentum and the explicitly defined invariant form in [the regular-centralizer chart](regular_meridian_centralizer.md), Section 2. Its normalization is A_cut=M/(M+s), Delta=s+(M-M inverse)r and Omega=-dr wedge ds/[Delta(M+s)]. The actual balanced symbol in the marked braid note has x=-M, e=(k-M inverse)p and physical mu=-G. Hence at the first slot p=-(F_M inverse U F_M)_12/(k-M inverse); its minus sign is fixed, not inferred by continuity. Let kappa=M-M inverse and \[ U=\begin{pmatrix}M-c\beta&\kappa\beta-c\beta^2\\ c&M^{-1}+c\beta\end{pmatrix},\quad F_M=\begin{pmatrix}r&1-r\\s&-\kappa-s\end{pmatrix}. \] Then D=U-M inverse I has rank one. Direct matrix calculation gives \[ p=1-\frac{1-\kappa\beta}{r+\beta s},\qquad r=\frac{1-\kappa\beta}{1-p}-\beta s, \tag{3} \] on the regular chart, and for THAT invariant form \[ \Omega=-\frac p{(1-p)[s(1-p)+\kappa]} d\log A_{cut}\wedge d\log p. \tag{4} \] The momentum Möbius pole stays p=1, but the density has two simple poles, p=1 and p=1+kappa/s. They coalesce to the main theorem's double pole at M=1. Thus even this special first-slot calculation does not justify retaining a generic single-double- pole filter. An additional Gaussian-density/source comparison, if needed away from completeness, has not been supplied by (3)-(4). [The exact symbolic check](../experiments/audit_first_slot_meridian_germ.py) and [its output](../experiments/first_slot_meridian_germ_results.json) verify the raw conjugated momentum, complete bubble atoms and the density's full meridian dependence. The root main theorem's actual R/source and Hessian tests are linked from that theorem.

title: Exact complete localization of the original first-slot Fourier source
text: # Exact complete localization of the original first-slot Fourier source Research theorem, 27 October 2026. At an actual root, the first-slot cut in the [universal resonant presentation](universal_resonant_cut_and_actual_source.md) has the exact ORIGINAL finite Fourier array J_(a,j)(1)=P_N(1) delta_(j,0) (1) for EVERY physical first input a. This includes the original all-ones output row, the original pivotal caps, twists and full peripheral dimension line. No division by P_N and no nonvanishing assertion are used. The result is a consequence of the actual Hopf rows, rather than an approximation by the geometric principal density. In fact the entire channel obeys L(X_j)=P_N X_j at completeness, as proved below; this is stronger than the selected scalar rows. Consequently the regular Fourier labels j!=0 have zero selected finite value at completeness. A nonzero local geometric formal block at those labels does not establish that it contributes to the original period. The resonant value P_N remains to be evaluated. In particular, (1) supplies neither its volume exponent nor a new scalar formula independent of the original word. ## 1. The actual channel and its source Fix N>=2, q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, and retain the original meridian M. In the balanced head put B=diag(Q^a), K=x B^-1, x=-M/q, F_(a+1,a)=1-Q^(a+1), Ecal_(a-1,a)=M Q^(-a)-M^-1. (2) All missing entries are zero. Ecal is the fixed scalar multiple of E used in the actual balanced crossing conventions. Its coproduct and antipode have the same form as those of E. Cut a braid at its FIRST physical slot between two actual words A and Bword; both words intertwine the true iterated coproduct. The original second-cut coupon X defines the actual linear channel L(X)=d_N theta^(-w) ptr_g[ A (X tensor I) Bword ]. (3) Here ptr_g closes every strand except the original first open strand using g=K^(1-N), in the original order. The displayed external factors may instead be recorded in their original external line; the SAME convention must then be used for P_N and J throughout. The universal presentation inserts a word P and its literal inverse, so A Bword is exactly the original braid operator. It changes none of the factors in (3), including their actual rational-map/lattice specializations. The [root scalar-closure proof](actual_one_index_fourier_source_and_ward_reduction.md), Section 1, gives L(I)=P_N(M) I. (4) There is an elementary version of that proof: the cut commutes with K and F; the distinct K eigenvalues make it diagonal, and its F commutator makes successive diagonal entries equal because 1-Q^a!=0 for 0<a<N. Thus no generic irreducibility or division by an unknown scalar period is needed. With the full line in (3), P_N=d_N F_N; with that line recorded externally, P_N=F_N. At M=1, F_N(1) is the fixed original Kashaev invariant. Set ell=1^t, and use the actual root Fourier projectors X_j=V^-1 E_(j,j) V, (X_j)_(b,d)=Q^[j(d-b)]/N, V_(j,b)=Q^(jb), 0<=j<N. The original one-index Fourier source is EXACTLY Y_j=L(X_j), J_(a,j)=ell Y_j e_a. (5) This follows by expanding the second-wire conjugation and retaining the all-ones first output row. Since sum_j X_j=I, (4) gives sum_j J_(a,j)=P_N (6) for every a. The 1/N in X_j is the Fourier inverse. There is no additional exterior factor in (6). ## 2. Why the first-slot channel intertwines the actual Hopf adjoint For the actual coproduct convention, Delta Ecal=Ecal tensor K+1 tensor Ecal, Delta F=F tensor 1+K^-1 tensor F, S(Ecal)=-Ecal K^-1, S(F)=-K F. The induced action on an endomorphism is ad_K X=K X K^-1, ad_Ecal X=(Ecal X-X Ecal)K^-1, ad_F X=F X-K^-1 X K F. (7) For the FIRST tensor factor, direct substitution in the coproduct gives ad_h^(total)(X tensor I)=(ad_h X) tensor I, h=K,Ecal,F. (8) For example the Ecal commutator is [Ecal,X] tensor K_other, which becomes [Ecal,X]K^-1 tensor I after multiplying by the total K^-1. For F the extra term cancels as K^-1 X tensor F_other -K^-1 X K K^-1 tensor F_other=0. This verifies the position requirement. An arbitrary later-slot embedding is not substituted for (8). Multiplication on either side by an actual braid intertwiner commutes with (7). The original pivotal partial trace is also an adjoint intertwiner. One can check the latter directly, without assuming scalarity: on the closed tensor factor write K_o,E_o,F_o for its total generators and g_o for its original product pivot. At the actual root, [g_o,K_o]=0, g_o E_o g_o^-1=K_o E_o K_o^-1, g_o F_o g_o^-1=K_o F_o K_o^-1. Weighted partial-trace cyclicity cancels the closed-factor terms in (7), using precisely these identities. The remaining terms are ad_h of the partial trace. Equivalently these are the direct evaluation/coevaluation identities checked in [the closed-braid construction](closed_braid_period_line.md), Section 2. Scalars d_N and theta^(-w) commute with this calculation. Consequently L(ad_h X)=ad_h L(X), h=K,Ecal,F. (9) Equations (8)--(9) apply to the literal cut of any word of the specified equal original color, not only to an inverse-pair example. The inverse-pair construction is what simultaneously provides this first slot and the desired noncommuting geometric meridian while preserving the original selected period. Everything so far is an ACTUAL root identity. It makes no off-root q scalarity or compressed auxiliary Hopf assertion. ## 3. Complete cyclic generator formulas Let S be the cyclic raising shift S e_a=e_(a+1 mod N). The Fourier projectors satisfy S X_j=X_j S=eta_j X_j, eta_j=Q^j, B^-1 X_j B=X_(j+1). (10) All Fourier labels in this note are cyclic. At M=1 the missing physical endpoints in (2) have zero coefficients. Therefore, as exact finite matrices, F=S(I-QB), Ecal=S^-1(B^-1-I). (11) There is no replacement of a nonzero endpoint by a cyclic arrow. Substituting (10)--(11) into (7) gives ad_K X_j=X_(j+1), ad_Ecal X_j=x^-1 eta_j^-1 (Q^-1 X_(j+1)-X_j), ad_F X_j=eta_j X_j-eta_(j-1) X_(j-1). (12) For instance [S^-1(B^-1-I),X_j]B has its two X_j B terms cancel; the remaining terms are eta_j^-1(Q^-1 X_(j+1)-X_j). For the F row, the two S B terms cancel by B X_j=X_(j-1)B. These prove all formulas in (12) within the original finite balanced head. The first row of (12) and (9) imply Y_(j+1)=B^-1 Y_j B. (13) In particular their diagonal entries are independent of j. Summing (13) and using (4) proves (Y_j)_(a,a)=P_N/N. This latter identity also holds for generic M and will retain the full scalar period in the endpoint equation below. ## 4. Highest-input localization, followed by all-input propagation First take the actual input a=0. Since Ecal e_0=0 and ell Ecal=ell(B^-1-I) at M=1, (13) gives ell (ad_Ecal Y_j)e_0 =x^-1[J_(0,j+1)-J_(0,j)]. Apply (9) to the Ecal row of (12) and compare the two expressions. The resulting exact scalar recurrence is (eta_j-Q^-1)J_(0,j+1) =(eta_j-1)J_(0,j). (14) At j=0 its right side is zero and 1-Q^-1 is a unit, so J_(0,1)=0. For j=1,...,N-2 the coefficient eta_j-Q^-1 is nonzero, and induction gives J_(0,j)=0 for every j!=0. Equation (6) then gives J_(0,0)=P_N. This proof never divides by P_N and remains valid when the original invariant vanishes. For every physical input a, use (13), the F row of (12), and F e_a=(1-Q^(a+1))e_(a+1). They give (1-eta_j)J_(a,j) =(Q^(a+1)-Q^-1 eta_j)J_(a,j-1) +(1-Q^(a+1))J_(a+1,j-1). (15) At a=N-1 the last term is zero; it is not an added cyclic physical-input column. The candidate P_N delta_(j,0), constant in a, satisfies (15). Subtract it and call the difference D. The result just proved is D_(0,j)=0 for all j. If D_(a,j)=0 for all j and a<N-1, (15) forces (1-Q^(a+1))D_(a+1,j-1)=0. Every coefficient is a unit. Induction in a proves D=0, which is the stated theorem (1). The proof also works at M=-1, since then Ecal=-S^-1(B^-1-I); its extra common sign cancels in (14). There is a useful full-matrix corollary. Define the Fourier rows r_k=ell B^-k, which form a basis of the dual head. By (13), r_k Y_j=ell Y_(j+k) B^-k =P_N delta_(j+k,0) r_k. Directly from (5), r_k X_j=delta_(j+k,0)r_k as well. Hence L(X_j)=P_N X_j, (19) L(h(S))=P_N h(S) for EVERY element h(S) of the finite cyclic-shift algebra. This identity also uses no nonzero-period assumption. It concerns this commutative subalgebra of coupons, not the full endomorphism algebra or the generic-M channel. ## 5. The meridian endpoint and word data are retained off completeness Keep the actual root Q but allow M to vary. Put kappa=M-M^-1, W=E_(N-1,0). The exact finite Ecal matrix is Ecal=S^-1(MB^-1-M^-1 I)-kappa W. (16) The last term subtracts the cyclic arrow at the original physical endpoint. It is nonzero off completeness. The F row, K row, (13), (15) and (Y_j)_(0,0)=P_N/N remain exact. Define the ACTUAL inserted endpoint source R_j=ell L([W,X_j]B)e_0. (17) Repeating the preceding Ecal calculation with (16) gives M(eta_j-Q^-1)J_(0,j+1) +(M-M^-1 eta_j)J_(0,j) =kappa eta_j(P_N/N-R_j). (18) Indeed the cyclic part of ad_Ecal X_j is x^-1 M eta_j^-1(Q^-1 X_(j+1)-X_j), while its missing-arrow correction is -x^-1 kappa[W,X_j]B. On the output side, ell Ecal=ell(MB^-1-M^-1 I)-kappa e_0^t. This proves (18), including both its original scalar source and its actual inserted endpoint source. Deleting (17) before differentiation would alter the original meridian normal equation. There is no universal generic-M profile determined by P_N alone for all original words. The exact finite-field audit includes the same first-slot inverse-pair cut on the one-positive-crossing unknot and positive trefoil. At N=3, M=3 over F_157, their highest rows divided by their respective NONZERO full periods are unknot: [117,62,136], trefoil: [52,122,141]. Both sums are one modulo 157. The different rows disprove such a universal rational identity across these original words; this is not a separate claim about all hyperbolic knots or about a particular complex asymptotic boundary profile. It records why the whole word/source in (17)--(18) cannot be replaced by a knot-independent cap simply because (1) holds on the complete fiber. ## 6. Critical-path consequence and verification On this actual source-preserving cut ALL of the selected complete finite period is at j=0. Thus the nonzero geometric normal block on a regular p!=1 chart is not yet a nonzero image of the final selected scalar source: the complete finite rows at j!=0 vanish exactly. Sampling their nonzero geometric principal coefficient and summing it is not an evaluation of the actual finite array. The remaining issue is a source-compatible geometric transform of the resonant row and its whole endpoint/peripheral completion, not proving that an unspecified regular Fourier row survives. Its regulator exponent, subexponential coefficient and global norm estimate are still unproved in general. The current theorem does not close C, D or E of [the critical-path audit](critical_path_to_original_volume_conjecture.md). The [exact original-matrix audit](../experiments/audit_universal_resonant_fourier_source.py) checks every matrix unit against all three Hopf-adjoint generators, the generic-M endpoint equation (18), all-input equation (15), complete delta localization and full matrix projector identity (19). Its [saved results](../experiments/universal_resonant_fourier_source_results.json) report PASS on 36 signed-word/cut cases at N=2,...,6, comprising 598 matrix input units and three generator checks per unit. The full d_N, original pivots and twists are retained in every case. These finite tests support the direct proof above; they are not used as a proof for untested knots or as an asymptotic estimate.

title: Pointed tetrahedral transport of the Verma root period
text: # Pointed tetrahedral transport of the Verma root period Research note, 26 October 2026. This factors the actual untruncated Verma crossing into four compact quantum dilogarithms, derives a scalar-one algebraic tetrahedral pentagon, and proves that finite formal pentagon rewrites preserve its selected root period after compression to the Verma lattice. It retains the boundary frame, its entire norm character and its poles. Individual compact products are not evaluated at roots of unity. The resulting root period is still the one independently identified in the [Frobenius Verma note](frobenius_verma_period.md): V_N(M)=F_N(M)/Delta_K(M^(2N)). This supplies local operator moves for the proposed triangulation comparison. It does not establish that an arbitrary positive geometric triangulation carries the required colored network and pointing, or identify its selected quantum period with the Bloch regulator. The volume conjecture remains unproved. ## 1. A pointed compact pentagon For generic Q put P_Q(t)=(t;Q)_infinity =sum_(n>=0)(-1)^n Q^(n(n-1)/2)t^n/(Q;Q)_n. Use it as a formal series. Its constant term is one and P_Q(Qt)=P_Q(t)/(1-t). If AB=QBA, Gaussian expansion gives P_Q(A+B)=P_Q(A)P_Q(B). (1.1) For XY=QYX, conjugation by P_Q(Y) sends X to X(1-Q^(-1)Y)=X-YX. The two summands X and -YX satisfy the commutation required in (1.1). Consequently P_Q(Y)P_Q(X)=P_Q(X)P_Q(-YX)P_Q(Y). (1.2) This proves the pentagon directly from the series and its shift equation. It is an equality with scalar one, fixed by the constant term. The ordered middle argument -YX, including its Q phase in an X-before-Y monomial basis, is part of the identity. To make completions unambiguous, attach formal variables u,v to X,Y. The middle argument has tag uv. Every coefficient is finite in the (u,v)-adic completion of the quantum Laurent algebra. Inverses of P are defined in the same completion. No analytic branch or root-level value of an individual infinite product is assumed. ## 2. A tetrahedral operator, including its shear and phase On Laurent monomials in z_1,...,z_b let Z_i multiply by z_i and S_i f(z)=f(...,Qz_i,...). Put x_i=Z_i, y_i=S_i^(-1), so x_i y_i=Q y_i x_i. Define a monomial shear (C_ij f)(z)=f(...,z_i z_j,...,z_j,...), a_ij=-Q x_i x_j^(-1)y_j, T_ij(t)=C_ij P_Q(t a_ij)^(-1). (2.1) The shear conjugates x_i to x_i x_j and y_j to y_i^(-1)y_j. Its exact monomial action gives C_12 C_13 C_23=C_23 C_12. Move the dilogarithms past these shears in the two products below. On the left their arguments become A,-AC,C; on the right they become C,A, where A=u a_12, C=v a_23, CA=QAC. Indeed the transformed a_13 has coefficient -Q uv, whereas AC has coefficient Q uv. Inverting (1.2) therefore proves T_12(u)T_13(uv)T_23(v)=T_23(v)T_12(u). (2.2) This is the algebraic three-to-two tetrahedral operator identity with its exact shear and scalar. It is not a claim that the uncolored geometric triangulation theorem supplies the extra tensor data needed to apply it globally. For a direct coefficient check, T_ij(t) sends a Laurent monomial of exponent vector n to vectors with n'_i=n_i+m, n'_j=n_j+n_i, coefficient=t^m(-1)^m Q^(m(m+1)/2-m n_j)/(Q;Q)_m, summed over m>=0. Tagged coefficients are finite. Omitting the Q in a_ij already violates (2.2); it is not a removable scalar normalization. ## 3. Four factors for the actual Verma crossing Use the same infinite Verma basis v_a=z^a, x=q^alpha, Q=q^2, rho=q-q^(-1). On one factor put S v_a=Q^a v_a and Z v_a=v_(a+1). Then K=xS^(-1), F=Z, rho^2 E=qx Z^(-1)(1-S^(-1))(1-Q^(-1)x^(-2)S). The right side kills v_0 and preserves the polynomial Verma module. Let G=P_Q(x^(-2)S), initially as a tagged formal diagonal operator. The functional equation gives rho^2 E=qx G[Z^(-1)(1-S^(-1))]G^(-1). (3.1) For a pair set A=Z_1^(-1)Z_2, S=S_1 and W=x^(-2)S, U=Qx A, V=-Qx A S^(-1). Here AS=QSA and VU=QUV. The formal universal uncheck R, with its common Cartan scalar removed, is D times its nilpotent series, where D(v_a tensor v_b)=x^(-a-b)Q^(ab)v_a tensor v_b. Using the independently derived R coefficients and (3.1) gives R^0=D P_Q(W)P_Q(V)P_Q(U)P_Q(W)^(-1). (3.2) Indeed the middle product is P_Q(U+V), with U+V=Qx A(1-S^(-1)); its action terminates on each polynomial input before the diagonal conjugation. Equation (3.2) is therefore the actual Verma operator, not a replacement cyclic crossing. Two applications of (1.2) remove the diagonal G: P_Q(W)P_Q(V)=P_Q(V)P_Q(-WV)P_Q(W), P_Q(W)P_Q(U)P_Q(W)^(-1)=P_Q(U)P_Q(-WU). Since -WV=x^(-1)A and -WU=-x^(-1)AS, the four-monomial formula is R^0=D P_Q(-Qx AS^(-1))P_Q(x^(-1)A) P_Q(Qx A)P_Q(-x^(-1)AS). (3.3) The checked crossing is the usual flip times (3.3). Its inverse is the inverse word, with the same external conventions. All Cartan, flip and zero-framing factors remain in the period. ## 4. Compression fixes the boundary lattice The individual factors in (3.3) can send a polynomial input to infinitely many negative powers of z_1. The complete product has an elementary cancellation. Introduce a color tag h and a transfer tag d in (3.2): replace W by hW and U,V by dU,dV. In (3.3) this tags the second and fourth arguments by hd, and the first and third by d. After grouping the whole product, the coefficient sending (a,b) to (a-n,b+n), before the checked flip, is exactly d^n x^(-a-b+n)Q^((a-n)b){a choose n}_Q (h x^(-2)Q^(a-n);Q)_n, 0<=n<=a, (4.1) and is zero for n>a. Here the Gaussian coefficient is a polynomial, not a divided-factorial value at a root. For a uniform proof, first expand P_Q(d(U+V)). Its n-th power acts by the factor product_(j=0)^(n-1)(1-Q^(-a+j)), which vanishes for n>a. Combining this factor with the Euler coefficient gives d^n x^n Q^(-n(a-n)){a choose n}_Q. The diagonal ratio from G is (h x^(-2)Q^(a-n);Q)_n. Applying D at the output gives (4.1). This is also the direct untruncated crossing coefficient of the preceding note at h=d=1. Every fixed homogeneous total-index sector of the combined operator is thus a finite matrix of Laurent polynomials in q,x and polynomials in h,d. The inverse has the same property, by the terminating inverse R series. Its determinant is the invertible Cartan monomial times that of a unipotent triangular matrix. The combined operator preserves the original polynomial Verma lattice. Neither this fact nor its root specialization is obtained by specializing its four compact factors separately. ## 5. A precise pointed transport theorem Start with the Verma braid operator and a fixed cut, pivot and grading insertion as in the [graded trace construction](frobenius_verma_period.md). Expand its crossings and inverses by (3.2) or (3.3), with independent auxiliary tags for the occurrences. Permit a finite sequence of the formal pentagon identities, their inverse identities, exact monomial/shear identities and cancellations of adjacent inverse factors, with their argument tags and external leg identifications transported throughout. These are equalities of the external operator, before taking its trace. Then compress the entire rewritten operator to the original Verma lattice, set its tags to one, and specialize q=q_N. The resulting graded cut period and its rational continuation at tau=1 are exactly the original ones: rewritten V_beta(q_N,x;tau)=V_beta(q_N,x;tau), rewritten V_N(M)=F_N(M)/Delta_K(M^(2N)). (5.1) Here is the proof, including the otherwise missing specialization step. All factors have positive auxiliary tag degree, so every rewrite is defined in a common formal completion of the Laurent module. The initial complete operator has the polynomial matrix entries of Section 4. Formal operator equality forces the rewritten complete entries to equal those polynomials, including the vanishing of every forbidden negative-index transfer. Thus setting the tags to one and specializing q use a known regular polynomial entry. No root limit of an individual factor is used. Each coefficient of the cut grading tau sums only finitely many input and intermediate indices after this compression. The coefficientwise period identity follows. At a root the initial period has the rational formula proved in the preceding note. Two rational functions with the same series at tau=0 are equal; hence their entire rational continuations, poles and regular whole specializations agree. This proves (5.1), including the Kashaev fiber and its marked normal coordinate. Multiplying by the full d_N(M) retains the full ADO normalization as before. This theorem transports the actual selected period under the specified formal operator moves. It does not assert that every Pachner or face-permutation operation on arbitrary ideal triangulations has already been assigned such an operator identity. For such an application the coloring, polarization, turns and boundary identifications must be constructed and checked. ## 6. The relative norm torsor at the Kashaev boundary Normalize the diagonal operator in (3.2) on v_0. Its finite ratio is g_a=P_Q(x^(-2)Q^a)/P_Q(x^(-2)) =1/(x^(-2);Q)_a, g_0=1. The finite expression specifies its meromorphic root frame even though the two infinite products individually have no such value. For q=q_N and U=M^(2N)=x^(2N), g_(a+1)/g_a=(1-x^(-2)Q^a)^(-1), g_(NA+r)=(1-U^(-1))^(-A)g_r, 0<=r<N. (6.1) This is an explicit rank-one cyclic norm character Norm((1-x^(-2)Q^a)^(-1))=(1-U^(-1))^(-1). It is invertible away from its divisor; at U=1 its meromorphic filtered lattice, with pole order A on the A-th polynomial block, must be retained. Every finite total-index filtration has finite pole order. At the actual Kashaev color x=q_N^(N-1), x^(-2)=Q, so the first N frame entries are g_r=1/(Q;Q)_r, 0<=r<N. They are exactly the factorial frame of the already fixed [actual cut boundary](marked_braid_holonomy.md). The next entry has a pole. The combined crossing is regular nevertheless by (4.1), and the complete rational trace is regular there because Delta_K(1)=1. Evaluating this diagonal frame separately at its pole would lose the prescribed boundary data. The middle arguments in pentagons also retain nontrivial central norms. If XY=QYX and Q has order N, direct ordered multiplication gives (-YX)^N=-X^N Y^N (6.2) at every parity. Thus its binomial norm factor is 1+X^N Y^N, which can specialize to a numerical multiplier. In the tetrahedral operator (2.1), a_ij^N=-Z_i^N Z_j^(-N)S_j^(-N), with the same sign. Such factors must be carried as functions before a whole boundary specialization. The strict formal identities above do not justify discarding them or repair a different numerical state model by fiat. The subsequent [factorial source-torsor calculation](factorial_source_torsor.md) identifies this frame directly with the literature cyclic primitive. For h=Q^(-1)x^(-2), write p_a(h)=(Qh;Q)_a=nu^a phi_a(h), nu^N=1-U^(-1). Then the exact Verma frame is g_a=1/p_a(h)=nu^(-a) phi_a(h)^(-1). Its block pole character in (6.1) is the N-step transport of this same singular cyclic frame. The new two-direction affine extension and cut-root adapters retain its source channel and the full endpoint factors. They do not supply the remaining global colored/polarized network or its selected regulator norm. The subsequent [four cyclic-atom proof](four_cyclic_atoms.md) now constructs a finite root counterpart for the genuine semicyclic crossing: each atom is the literature alternate cyclic dilogarithm, acting between explicitly transported centers. Two independent Fermat norm roots and their inverses restore the external clocks. Their determinant normalization, an external root and the actual source anchor fix the whole crossing scalar. This is not a termwise evaluation of (3.3); the finite cyclic atoms include the required center transport and boundary frame. Recombination has exactly the original regular crossing and full cut period. The subsequent [root tetrahedral pentagon](cyclic_tetrahedron_pentagon.md) constructs the corresponding finite cyclic move with monomial shears and changing centers. Compatible roots give the same final clock/shift frame on both paths; a determinant and formal zero-tag anchor fix the scalar to one on the stated lifted component. This supplies an exact root move for specified exterior contractions, rather than a separate specialization of the compact infinite factors. The global geometric tensor presentation and selected regulator norm are still missing. ## 7. Role in the regulator comparison There are now actual four-factor crossing data, an algebraic tetrahedral pentagon and a pointed root-period transport theorem for finite formal operator rewrites. The cyclic norm character and its relative lattice are explicit. These are local algebraic inputs for a triangulation presentation of the source period. The positive geometric triangulation supplies the marked classical Bloch fundamental class, as already audited. To apply Section 5 to it requires a compatible colored/polarized tensor presentation and a move transport of the cut and its relative gluing data. Existence of positive tetrahedra alone does not supply that presentation or a global branching. Nor does the operator move identity show that a chosen hyperbolic character contribution is the selected quantum period or has its regulator norm. The original distinction between root-central and semiclassical shape coordinates remains in force. In particular (5.1) preserves the actual state and its source; it does not equate its abelian interior root character with the different fixed hyperbolic character separated in the [threading note](ado_threaded_shadow.md). The needed comparison remains a relative marked-period theorem. Its norm statement and the volume conjecture are not proved here. The subsequent [pointed tetrahedron gluing construction](pointed_tetrahedron_gluing.md) does resolve local order coherence and nonvanishing at the root module level. Integral edge primitivity gives a nonzero saturated rank-N boundary block for S^3 knots at all N. It also specifies the projected tetrahedron generator, without proving that vector nonzero or identifying it with the selected relative Verma trace. The full tensor-face presentation and marked regulator norm are still additional comparisons. ## 8. Coverage and exact diagnostics [Kashaev, q-alg/9503005](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9503005) already covers a canonical Heisenberg-double pentagon and reconstruction of Yang--Baxter solutions. The abstract of [Suzuki, 1612.08262](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.08262) covers a Heisenberg-double construction on colored ideal triangulations and colored moves. These are coverage of the framework, not proof premises or an unrestricted geometric-triangulation comparison. The earlier consulted [four-dilogarithm holonomy-R coverage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02354) also prevents a novelty claim for the general factorization idea. The formulas and polynomial-specialization proof above are reconstructed directly in the fixed actual Verma conventions. [The audit](../experiments/audit_verma_tetrahedral_transport.py) checks the compact pentagon symbolically, the tagged tetrahedral operator on Laurent monomials, forbidden-transfer cancellations in the four-factor product, root-specialized compressed entries and their actual ADO restrictions, the full meromorphic frame, and the period through the grading using independent finite ADO and classical Burau data. See [the results](../experiments/verma_tetrahedral_transport_results.json). These diagnostics verify the stated constructions and not the remaining global geometric or regulator-norm theorem. The saved checks include 28 symbolic compact-pentagon coefficients, 81 Laurent inputs and 1,215 coefficients for the tagged tetrahedral operator, 49 symbolic four-factor compressions with 21 forbidden transfers canceled, 3,360 compressed root entries, nine full pole lattice levels through 12, and 210 graded coefficients in 30 transported trace cases. Even and composite levels and the exact Kashaev boundary are included.

title: Exact Ward cancellation of cyclic wall currents, with the marked charge retained
text: # Exact Ward cancellation of cyclic wall currents, with the marked charge retained 28 October 2026. The original all-plat Ward corner has an explicit co-source homotopy. Under cyclic completion it produces a rank-two commutator wall current. That current is canceled exactly by the corresponding sewing defect, before asymptotics or closure. For an assembled word the typed defects telescope. This gives a finite relative-cycle comparison for the Ward reduction; it does not identify nonlinear positive-angle boundary prisms with those currents. The surviving marked wall has charge one. It is not permitted to delete the only source carrier. ## 1. An explicit original co-source homotopy Use the literal arbitrary-plat conventions in [the Rogers transport theorem](actual_rogers_bridge_transport.md). Put d=N-1. After the k-1 ordinary caps the remaining dual pair has total integer degree d. On that fiber let p=|d,0>, ell=<d,0|, mu(a)=x^(d-a)(-1)^a Q^(-a(a+1)/2) F_a^2/N^2. The first color x here is the remaining pair's actual color. In particular mu(d)=1. Let F_rel=S_a be the ACTUAL total lowering operator in fusion coordinates. It sends the degree-d fiber to degree d+1. Define a row on the latter fiber by nu(a+1,d-a)=mu(a), 0<=a<d. Then, on the entire degree-d fiber, exactly mu-ell=nu F_rel. (1) This is an actual co-source homotopy, not just vanishing on a single vector. Since the full original remaining vector v satisfies F_rel v=0, equation (1) proves mu v=ell v. It is the explicit current behind the Ward corner. All meridian powers in mu and nu remain functions. For a general nonintertwining coupon or a separated cyclic sector, F_rel v need not vanish. Its omitted term is precisely nu F_rel v. ## 2. Cyclic completion has a rank-two Ward defect Consider the positive actual Euler transfer T=a J_+ tensor J_-, A=a S tensor S^-1, with the literal truncated shifts J and cyclic S. The two residue fibers relevant to F_rel are k=d and k=0. In either cyclic basis the operator A is aS. Between them F_rel is the strict raising shift J_+. Consequently its typed cyclic defect is Delta=F_rel A_in-A_out F_rel =a (|1><d|-|0><d-1|). (2) For N=2 this is the same two distinct matrix units; no generic rank assertion or separated-wall assumption is required. The ACTUAL transfer has no such defect: F_rel T_in=T_out F_rel, because J_+ on the first head commutes with J_+ tensor J_-. Writing R_A=(t-A)^(-1), R_T=(t-T)^(-1), and E=R_T-R_A, the resolvent identity gives the exact rational equations F_rel R_A,in-R_A,out F_rel=R_A,out Delta R_A,in, F_rel E_in-E_out F_rel=-R_A,out Delta R_A,in. (3) Thus the cyclic Ward defect and its sewing Ward defect cancel POINTWISE. This is more than equality after a particular trace. The full central polynomial t^N-a^N and its poles remain in (3). On a cut meeting such poles one must use the matched residue and finite-part prescription already proved in [the sewing cycle theorem](cyclic_sewing_regularized_cut_cycle.md). Equation (3) does not authorize retaining only the old branch cuts. Every common Cartan line multiplies the same two equations. The negative crossing and other residue fibers have the same typed identity with their literal operators; no replacement inverse or scalar normalization is used. ## 3. The full original marker detects the Ward current For one actual dual cup, input colors are (x,y), y=x^(-1)Q^(-1), and the checked positive core is D u_N(aJ_+ tensor J_-) with a=x^(-1). The output marked row is mu_y. The Gaussian D depends only on the second head, so it commutes with F_rel as a typed map. Since T p=0, the ORIGINAL marked resolvent is exactly mu_y D R_T,in(t) p=1/t. (4) Thus every holomorphic functional-calculus germ f gives the original value f(0). In particular the actual Euler germ has f(0)=1. Together with the original Cartan/framing line this is the original one-bridge normalization, not a newly assigned scalar. Set g_mu=mu_y D R_A,in p and g_ell=ell R_A,in p. Equation (1) and the first equation of (3), with F_rel p=0, give g_mu-g_ell=nu D_out R_A,out Delta R_A,in p. (5) This is the exact missing current when somebody applies the Ward corner separately to a cyclic sector. The right-hand side can be nonzero and has source-visible cyclic poles. The corner cyclic term is especially simple: g_ell=t^(N-1)/(t^N-a^N). Its marked relative wall is 1/t-g_ell=-a^N/[t(t^N-a^N)]. (6) Its residue at zero is one, its residues at the N cyclic poles are -1/N each, and it has zero residue at infinity. Hence even after full zero-current Ward reduction a nonzero augmented wall survives. A source-free cyclic resolvent is holomorphic at zero and has zero original small-circle period. It cannot be the replacement for (4) with the wall removed. ## 4. Exact residue contraction with polynomial cost Let beta_j=aQ^j. In the input fiber write S for its cyclic shift, and put c_r=mu_y D S^r p, 0<=r<N, c_0=1. The ORIGINAL cyclic residues are exactly w_j=Res_(beta_j) g_mu(t)dt =(1/N)sum_(r=0)^(N-1)c_r Q^(-jr), sum_j w_j=1. (7) The corner residues are 1/N. Their difference is an explicit cyclic boundary. With (S_res J)_j=J_(j+1), put J_j=(1/N)sum_(r=1)^(N-1) c_r Q^(-jr)/(Q^(-r)-1). Then (S_res-1)J=w-(1/N)1. (8) The zero-average inverse H of S_res-1 satisfies the genuine chain contraction Delta_res H=H Delta_res=I-Pi_0, ||H||_(ell2)<=1/[2sin(pi/N)]<=N/4, ||H||_(ell-infinity)<=N. (9) These are the flat norms on the ACTUAL scalar cyclic-residue coordinates j=0,...,N-1. They are not norms asserted invariant under an exponentially conditioned fusion frame. The first bound is the unitary Fourier spectral calculation. For the second, a zero-sum input g has a cumulative primitive P_j=sum_(h<j)g_h. Both j and N-j bound its absolute size, so |P_j|<=N||g||_infinity/2. Subtract its mean to impose zero average. This proves the stated N bound. No inverse is applied to the constant character; Pi_0 retains its marked augmentation. Equations (5)--(9) are an actual Ward/cyclic residue comparison. With a nonconstant analytic test function f, summation by parts retains the dual difference of f, and its cut/pole terms. Thus (8) does not permit deleting these currents before their full relative pairing. For f=1 all nonconstant residues cancel exactly. ## 5. Large individual residues occur in this original unit source At the canonical unit root and any unit meridian, for 1<=r<N, |c_r|=|F_(r-1)|^2/N^2. (10) Indeed S^r p has first index r-1 and second index N-r; the Gaussian has modulus one, and the actual marked row is mu_y(n)=y^(d-n)|F_n|^2/N^2. This also proves uniformity over all unit meridians, not only one complete numerical value. Finite Fourier inversion gives the two-sided inequalities (max_r |c_r|)/N <= max_j |w_j| <= max_r |c_r|. The already independently proved figure-eight factorial estimate therefore yields lim_N (1/N)log max_j|w_j|=Vol(4_1)/(2pi)>0, (11) whereas sum_j w_j is EXACTLY one. This is an original-source cancellation example satisfying all the actual zero-current Ward equations. It is neither an arbitrary normalization counterexample nor a claim that this unknot has positive volume. The polynomial homotopy bound (9) is entirely compatible with (11): it controls the cost relative to the original coefficient norm; it does not replace exponential input coefficients by polynomial ones without their exact cancellation. ## 6. Whole-word cancellation and the precise surviving class For arbitrary finite typed factors O_j:V_(j-1)->V_j, retain the actual transported lowering operators F_j and define delta_j=F_j O_j-O_j F_(j-1). Their original ordered product W obeys the exact identity F_L W-W F_0 =sum_j O_L...O_(j+1) delta_j O_(j-1)...O_1. (12) The original cups have F_0 p=0; the original assembled word and ordinary caps intertwine. Therefore the TOTAL co-source change from mu to the Ward corner is zero. In a cyclic/sewn realization (3) supplies the local rational defect cancellation. With its complete matched contours, every cyclic residue and ramified finite-part contribution is carried through (12). This statement is linear in the exact rational forms and does not assume an unmarked deformation of a small circle into branch cuts. It follows that the FULL original fused corner can use the purely cyclic cross-sewing representation with its explicit relative boundary source. This is obtained by applying the Ward co-source homotopy to the assembled original network and then the local exact resolvent expansion, or by retaining all the currents in the opposite order; (3) and (12) equate the procedures. The total sum of marker-reduction Ward currents is removable. The unit augmented class (6) is NOT removable. In particular a sectorwise corner replacement without (5) is not this theorem. All of (1)--(12) are covariant under a literal full tensor/frame change, with F, the source, every sewing map and every current transformed together. An isomorphism of cyclic kernel lines alone does not supply that full change. In particular this note does not identify arbitrary nonlinear positive-quad angular boundary prisms with the currents in (12), nor prove that the retained cusp class couples to a geometric critical point. The complementary [compactified quad transport](cap_wall_fermat_quad_residue_transport.md) constructs an actual divisor-residue image of the cup. That local transition can carry the augmentation; it must still respect the cyclic-pole and source-current data above in a whole positive chart comparison. [Original-matrix and wall-current audit](../experiments/audit_ward_cyclic_wall_contraction.py). The audit passes fourteen original complete/generic dual-cup families, twelve assembled two- and three-slot original Euler words with every cyclic/sewing sector retained, eight chain-contraction norm cases, and six source-scale grids through N=1280. In the assembled words the separate marker changes are nonzero, their commutator-current sum is exactly zero, and the original unit source is retained. The proofs above are uniform; these finite tests independently fix operator order and the two different residue fibers in (3) and (5).

title: Deleting cut roots preserves the pointed relative Ward class
text: # Deleting cut roots preserves the pointed relative Ward class Research proof, 27 October 2026. The original cut covector does not descend after deleting the root `A=1`. A different literal finite cut does descend, and its matrix functional is explicitly cochain homotopic to the original on the actual Ward complex. The equivalence extends to the relative boundary resolution and to a marked whole normal family. It is a boundary/source comparison, not a rule for compressing crossings or a geometric Gaussian source-survival theorem. ## 1. The localized source and its exact normalization Fix `N>=2`, `Q` primitive of order `N`, and the original evaluation color `V=C_N=k[A^+/-1]/(A^N-1)`. In its evaluation basis the source is `psi=(1,...,1)^t`, the co-source is `phi=(1/N)(1,...,1)`, and `e=psi phi`. Let `S` be any nonempty set of retained roots, `m=|S|=N-s>0`, and let `P` be multiplication by its characteristic idempotent. Define psi_S=P psi, phi_S=(N/m)phi P, e_S=psi_S phi_S=(N/m)P e P. (1) One has `phi_S psi_S=1`, `e_S^2=e_S`, and `Tr e_S=1`. The literal new matrix cut is Phi_S(C)=Tr(e_S C)=(1/m)sum_(a,b in S) C_(a,b). (2) The factor `N/(N-s)` is retained exactly, for every `s<N`. The original pivot and marked defect remain available via `Phi(C)=Tr(g D C)`; equation (2) changes the boundary representative, not the original numerical invariant on closed tangles. The entire external full-ADO factor remains unchanged. For deletion only of `A=1`, let `epsilon_1=(1/N)sum_(j<N)A^j` and `P=1-epsilon_1`. The new color co-source is intrinsically phi_S(f)=[N phi(f)-f(1)]/(N-1). (3) It kills the deleted root's entire idempotent summand and factors through `C_N[(A-1)^(-1)]=P C_N`. Thus it removes the previously displayed localization obstruction for this new representative. ## 2. The actual Ward homotopy, on all matrices Use the actual root matrices `K,F` and the split image Ward complex from [the Ward contraction](actual_borel_ward_cut_contraction.md): W_N^0=End(V), W_N^1=im delta_N, delta_N(C)=([K,C],[F,C]), h_N delta_N=I-i_N p_N, delta_N h_N=I, p_N(C)=Tr(C)/N, i_N(c)=c I. Both `Phi` and `Phi_S` take value one on `I`. Consequently Phi_S-Phi=(Phi_S-Phi) h_N delta_N. (4) This is an explicit all-matrices cochain homotopy, with the known finite denominators in `h_N`. Every actual closed cut tangle is Ward closed and equals `F_N(M)I`. Hence Phi_S(C_K)=Phi(C_K)=F_N(M). (5) This holds wherever that original root-color cut operator is defined, as a meromorphic whole germ in `M`; no scalar or peripheral factor is replaced by its value at completeness. The distinction between the two source complexes matters. In the color relative complex `R(C_N)` alone, `phi_S` and `phi` are not homotopic: its top cohomology is `C_N`, and they have different values on `epsilon_1`. Equation (4) uses the **matrix Ward** differential. It must not be presented as a homotopy in the old color relative complex without that additional differential. ## 3. An explicit localized Ward complex and retraction Order the retained labels as `a_1<...<a_m`. Put `V_S=P V` and `K_S=K|_(V_S)`. If several interior roots were deleted, the ordinary compression of `F` can be disconnected. Instead use the specified skip-transport matrix (F_S)_(a_(j+1),a_j)=product_(r=a_j)^(a_(j+1)-1)(1-Q^(r+1)), 1<=j<m. (6) All these coefficients are units. This is the original F transport along the unique retained linear interval between the two labels. For deletion only of label zero it is ordinary compressed `F`. For `m=1` it is zero, as appropriate to a one-dimensional space. The distinct `K_S` eigenvalues and the connected nonzero path (6) give `ker delta_S=k I_S`. The same entrywise and cumulative formulas give its explicit split image Ward complex `W_S` and contraction `h_S`, with normalized row `p_S=Tr/m`. Let `L:V->V_S` be restriction and `J:V_S->V` be inclusion, so `JL=P,LJ=I_S`. Define c_0(C)=L C J, c_1=delta_S c_0 h_N. (7) Then `c_1 delta_N=delta_S c_0`: the only omitted term is `delta_S c_0 i_N p_N=0`. Thus (7) is a genuine chain map, not an assumed rowwise compression of Ward currents. It sends `I_N` to `I_S` and induces the identity on scalar cohomology. A section is equally explicit. Set s_0(T)=J T L+p_S(T)(I_N-P), s_1=delta_N s_0 h_S. (8) It is a chain map, sends `I_S` to `I_N`, and `c s=I` in both degrees. With `H=(I-s_0 c_0)h_N` in degree one, direct multiplication gives H delta_N=I-s_0 c_0, delta_N H=I-s_1 c_1. (9) Therefore deleting any `s<N` roots gives an explicit homotopy retraction of these Ward complexes. The localized cut on `W_S` composed with `c_0` is exactly (2). This construction transports currents as well as the scalar class. It does not turn `V_S` into the original quantum-group module. The skip matrix is a Ward transport operator; no coproduct, crossing intertwining, or Hopf-pivotal property is inferred for it. ## 4. The relative source map is strict after adjoining Ward currents For a coefficient space `E`, the existing relative source resolution is `R(E)=R(k) tensor E`, where R(E)^1=E[t], R(E)^2=E[t] direct_sum E direct_sum E, d_R h=(partial_t h,h(0),h(1)). Its contraction is natural for every linear coefficient map. Apply it degreewise to `W_N` and `W_S` and use the usual total differential `d_R tensor I+(-1)^degR I tensor delta`. Equations (7)--(9) extend to actual relative-Ward chain maps and homotopies. The two cut rows extend to maps into `R(k)`; their homotopy is explicitly r tensor x -> (-1)^deg(r) r tensor [(Phi_S-Phi)h_N](x). Thus the **combined** relative-Ward complex has the same nonzero pointed line after deletion. This is a precise relative source extension of (4), rather than just equality on one knot value. ## 5. The whole normal and its branch mark can be retained Let `R=k[[U-1]]`, and retain the actual finite color normal algebra C_U=R[A]/(A^N-U). Mark the unique root `alpha(U)^N=U`, `alpha(1)=1`. Its evaluation branches are `A=alpha(U)Q^a`. The idempotent epsilon_0(U)=(1/N)sum_(j=0)^(N-1)(A/alpha(U))^j is regular and projects onto the marked branch reducing to `A=1`. Put `P(U)=1-epsilon_0(U)`. The exact whole-normal co-source is phi_S,U(f)=[Tr_(C_U/R)(f)-f(alpha(U))]/(N-1) =Tr_(P(U)C_U/R)(P(U)f)/(N-1). (10) It is regular, normalized on `P(U)`, and retains every normal coefficient. Since `A-1` is a unit on the retained summands, (10) factors through `A-1` localization. The marked deleted branch is removed as a whole; its punctured generic remnant is not used to divide away its normal contribution. For a canonical representative `f_tilde=sum_(j<N)f_j A^j`, equation (10) reads `[N f_0-f_tilde(alpha)]/(N-1)`. Multiplication still has the exact carry A f_tilde-(Af)_tilde=f_(N-1)(A^N-U). The source is linear, and this carry remains necessary. Deletion repairs the excluded-root obstruction; it does not make a trace functional into a ring map or erase the normal `U`. The same marked construction works for any subset of branches. In the split evaluation lattice one can use `K_aa=x alpha^(-1)Q^(-a)` and the interior path entries `F_(a+1,a)=1-alpha Q^(a+1)`. They specialize to the original matrices. Distinct K differences and these interior path entries are units over `R`. A separately specified cyclic wrap can also be retained; it does not enter the interior entries used by the Ward contraction. The retractions above therefore extend over this whole formal boundary normal family, with their normalization `N/(N-s)` unchanged. No Hopf or internal-network extension is inferred from this boundary construction. ## 6. Compression has an exact composition defect For arbitrary matrices `C,D`, one has c_0(CD)-c_0(C)c_0(D)=L C(I-P)D J. (11) The right side records an excursion through the deleted root sector. It is generally nonzero. Thus independently compressing each crossing, turn, or cap does not reproduce compression of the whole actual network. Nor is `c_0` multiplicative or an ordinary quantum-group intertwiner. The current map (7) is the specific repair in the split Ward complex; it supplies no local R-matrix replacement or strict tensor functor. The old statement that the **original** co-source fails to descend is still correct. The new result is that its pointed relative-Ward class has a literal representative supported on the geometric open chart, with an exact normalization and a marked whole-normal extension. A source-compatible internal Gaussian comparison can use this representative and its homotopy. Such a comparison must still transport the excursion currents, carries, and the other retained divisors. Nonzero geometric-source survival and the volume conjecture do not follow just from deleting the root. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_ward_source_localization.py) and [results](../experiments/ward_source_localization_results.json) check the source homotopy and explicit chain retraction on matrix units, for every nonempty retained subset at seven levels. They also retain a nonzero compression-excursion defect and the marked whole-normal carry. [Independent proof audit](ward_source_localization_independent_audit.md).

title: Independent audit of pointed relative Ward localization
text: # Independent audit of pointed relative Ward localization Audit, 27 October 2026. The proof in [ward_source_localization.md](ward_source_localization.md) is sound as a boundary/source homotopy statement. No crossing, coproduct, Hopf-pivotal, or multiplicative compression is claimed or supplied. No new matrix tests were needed. ## 1. Source normalization and the chain maps For a nonempty retained set of size \(m\), the formulas \(\psi_S=P\psi,\ \phi_S=(N/m)\phi P\) give \(\phi_S\psi_S=1\). Hence \(e_S\) is rank one, idempotent, and has trace one. The new row and the original row both take value one on \(I_N\). Therefore their difference equals that difference composed with \(h_N\delta_N\), exactly as claimed. This requires the matrix Ward differential; it does not descend to a homotopy in the color relative complex alone. The compressed \(K\) eigenvalues are distinct. Every skip coefficient is a product of \(1-Q^r\) with \(1\le r<N\); it is nonzero. Thus the retained path is connected and the split image Ward complex has kernel precisely \(kI_S\). For \[ c_1=\delta_Sc_0h_N,\qquad s_1=\delta_Ns_0h_S, \] the identities \(c_0i_N=i_S,\ s_0i_S=i_N,\ c_0s_0=I\) give the chain-map equations directly. In particular \[ c_1s_1 =\delta_Sc_0(I-i_Np_N)s_0h_S =\delta_Sh_S=I \] on the image complex. With the stated order \(H=(I-s_0c_0)h_N\), one gets \[ H\delta_N=I-s_0c_0,\qquad \delta_NH=I-s_1c_1. \] These calculations remain valid for \(m=1\), where the retained degree-one image is zero. ## 2. The relative sign and the whole normal For total differential \(d_R\otimes I+(-1)^pI\otimes\delta\), \(p=\deg_R\), the induced Ward homotopy is \((-1)^pI\otimes H\). Its two \(d_R\) contributions cancel; its remaining terms are \(I\otimes(\delta H+H\delta)\). The displayed relative sign is therefore correct. The marked root \(\alpha(U)^N=U,\ \alpha(1)=1\) exists uniquely over \(k[[U-1]]\). Root orthogonality gives the specified regular idempotent and \[ \phi_{S,U}(f)= \frac{\operatorname{Tr}(f)-f(\alpha)}{N-1}. \] For a degree-\(<N\) representative the trace is \(Nf_0\); the carry \(f_{N-1}(A^N-U)\) is consequently retained. There is a useful subtlety which the proof handles correctly: localizing \(C_U\) at \(A-1\) does not literally delete the entire marked branch over the punctured normal base. That branch has \(\alpha-1\) invertible after \(U-1\) is inverted. The new functional instead kills the marked summand as a whole and extends by zero there. It is regular on the retained summands, where \(A-1\) is a unit. The extended \(K\)-differences and interior \(F\)-entries are units over the formal base, so the boundary Ward retractions extend regularly. An extra cyclic wrap does not change the interior reconstruction on the split image complex. This is not an internal Hopf extension. ## 3. There is an explicit obstruction to network compression The composition defect is exactly \[ c_0(CD)-c_0(C)c_0(D)=LC(I-P)DJ. \] For retained \(i,j\) and deleted \(d\), choose \(C=E_{i,d}\), \(D=E_{d,j}\). Both separate compressions are zero, whereas \(c_0(CD)=E_{i,j}\). Thus even the most elementary excursion forbids treating the retraction as a local crossing replacement or tensor functor. The proof states this limitation explicitly. The resulting representative is supported on the \(A\ne1\) cut chart. Other geometric chart divisors and the internal Gaussian/source map remain separate. ## 4. Additional check of the off-root product and pivot moment The two-normal distinction in [the complete-color divided Ward note](complete_color_divided_ward_and_fusion.md), section 7, also checks directly. In the generic balanced lift, \[ \epsilon_a=MQ^{-a-1}-M^{-1},\qquad F_{a+1,a}=1-Q^{a+1}. \] Subtracting adjacent diagonal products gives the usual \(\rho(K-K^{-1})\) at every interior vertex. The absent last edge leaves exactly \[ [\mathcal E,F]-\rho(K-K^{-1}) =-(1-Q^N)(MQ^{-N}-M^{-1})E_{N-1,N-1}. \] Hence the root wall and the integral-color wall are different normals, even though the defect vanishes on both. On the integral color \(m=N-1\), each of the \(b-1\) closed pivot ratios contributes \(q^{-Nm+2Na_j}\). The inverse-writhe twist ratio contributes \(q^{Nm\ell}\). Their product is exactly \[ q^{Nm(\ell-b+1)+2N\sum_{\rm closed}a_j}. \] Knot parity makes its root value one. Its logarithmic derivative still contains the closed-position moment; there is no equality of off-root jets merely from the root scalar equality. The current notes retain that moment and use the genuine generic pivot before divided specialization, so no adapter is omitted.

title: The weaving reflection source has expanding nonordinary channels
text: # The weaving reflection source has expanding nonordinary channels 28 October 2026. A bounded negative correction would be enough to evade the exact indefinite-Gram obstruction at the leading exponential scale. This note tests a specific way to obtain that correction: ordinary-color unitary traces and finitely many of their source jets.
