The ORIGINAL five-strand weaving source does not admit that particular reflection-positive decomposition. Its retained projective source has nonreal EXPANDING moment channels, not only the constant channel seen at N=2. This is a fixed-root, word-growth theorem. It is NOT a disproof of a polynomial-in-N correction for each fixed knot, an asymptotic positive formula valid only at large N, or a word-dependent scalar norm. Those would require additional arguments. In particular nothing below identifies the negative source terms with the bounded ordinary-color tail of the [regular meridian period](regularized_kashaev_period.md). ## 1. The exact arbitrary-width reflection pairing At complete color the ORIGINAL balanced crossing matrices are symmetric: R_plus^t=R_plus, R_minus^t=R_minus. For example the positive coefficient with input (a,b), output (c,j), c=a+b-j, is kappa x^(-b-j) Q^(jb) F_c F_a/(F_(a-j)F_bF_j). Transposing exchanges (a,b) with (c,j); c-b=a-j makes this coefficient identical. The negative statement follows by inversion. The proved [complete antiunitary identity](signed_green_antiunitary_transport.md) therefore gives R_minus=P R_plus^dagger P, including kappa. Let the width p be odd. Put U=product_(i odd)R_i^+, and let J reverse the p head factors. Since the odd crossings are disjoint, V=product_(i even)R_i^-=J U^dagger J, B=VU=J U^dagger J U, B^dagger J=J B. (1) The actual first-cut source is F=P_0 tensor g^(tensor(p-1)); the equivalent averaged marked row may be used only through its already proved whole-source identity. With the original writhe-zero framing and its external line retained, the reduced weave moments are k_n=Tr(F B^n), h(X,Y)=Tr(F J X^dagger J Y), h(B^i,B^j)=k_(i+j). (2) Thus a definite reflection subspace containing these half-states would give a positive Hankel form on the sequence (k_n). Equations (1)--(2) are an actual source pairing. They do not assert that the involution J, or its original marked co-source, is positive. For p=5 the time-ordered braid block is [1,3,-2,-4]. Its physical over and under encounters alternate, and its strand permutation is a five-cycle. In particular the closures at n=5m+2 are knots. The scalar is the original reduced Kashaev value. Restoring the full ADO dimension line multiplies every moment at this fixed N by the same known nonzero scalar; it changes none of the poles below. ## 2. An exact selected-source computation at N=3 Put omega=Q=exp(2 pi i/3). Then x=omega and g_a=omega^(1-a). The two positive and two negative common Cartan factors cancel in B. Its entries lie in Z[omega]. The audit constructs this literal operator and its original source exactly, rather than sampling its spectrum numerically. The resulting rational generating function is G(z)=sum_(n>=0) k_n z^n=A(z)/D(z), (3) where A and D are COPRIME integer polynomials and deg D=43. The full coefficient lists are saved in the audit certificate. The denominator is D=-(z-1)^3 P4a^2 P4b P8^2 P12, P4a=z^4-17z^3+55z^2-17z+1, P4b=z^4-5z^3+7z^2-5z+1, P8=z^8-19z^7+126z^6-380z^5+557z^4 -380z^3+126z^2-19z+1, P12=z^12-57z^11+1032z^10-8306z^9+34071z^8 -75492z^7+95323z^6-75492z^5+34071z^4 -8306z^3+1032z^2-57z+1. (4) The first moments are 0,1,217,15349,707317,26955828,936961969,... . This is not an inferred finite recurrence. After discovering its coefficients, the audit verifies the reversed denominator polynomial as an EXACT annihilating matrix identity on every source-supported integer-degree block. It then verifies the numerator and coprimeness. Cayley--Hamilton-style multiplication of that displayed identity proves (3) at ALL n, independently of any finite fit. The ordinary source includes only first-head index zero, hence supports total integer degrees 0,...,8. The exact arithmetic represents a+b omega by the integer matrix [[a,-b],[b,a-b]], so the calculation uses neither floating eigenvalues nor approximate cancellation. The local matrices and pivot are also checked directly against the existing independently assembled ORIGINAL balanced crossing. ## 3. The retained source couples to nonreal expanding modes Exact rational root isolation places a root z_0 of P8 in .41<Re z_0<.42, .11<Im z_0<.13. (5) In particular |z_0|<1. Numerically z_0 is approximately .4133686+.1189402i, giving |1/z_0| approximately 2.324825. The numerical values are explanatory only; (5) proves expansion. Since gcd(A,P8)=1, this is a genuine DOUBLE pole of the selected whole source. Its moment contribution has the form (a+b n)lambda^n with b!=0 and lambda=1/z_0. It survives on the all-knot subsequence n=5m+2. Indeed the exact fifth-power resultant is Res_z(P8(z),w-z^5) =w^8-58634w^7+98866981w^6-2511273890w^5 +449769171292w^4-2511273890w^3 +98866981w^2-58634w+1. (6) This polynomial is squarefree and coprime to the corresponding resultant of D/P8^2. Thus no two relevant fifth powers collide and cancel the selected double pole. The box (5) also proves Im(z_0^5)>0: for z_0=x+iy it is y(5x^4-10x^2y^2+y^4), whose lower bound on that box is positive. Consequently the generating series of k_(5m+2) has a NONREAL pole strictly inside the unit disk. This selected-source assertion is stronger than noticing nonreal eigenvalues in the ambient transfer matrix. Such eigenvalues could have been invisible to the marked cap; coprimeness in (3) proves that these are visible. ## 4. What this rules out, and what it leaves open An ordinary-color braid action in the positive path model is unitary. At fixed N, its closing trace is therefore uniformly bounded as the weave repetition varies. Finitely many fixed-order analytic jets of those finite matrices have at most polynomial growth in the repetition: differentiating a product chooses only polynomially many factors, with the remaining zero-order factors unitary. Their generating functions are analytic in |z|<1. Suppose the reflection form (2), restricted even to nonempty half-states B^(1+5i), split into a positive form plus such an ordinary-color/finite-unitary-jet correction. Then the sequence k_(5m+2) would differ by a polynomially bounded sequence from a positive Hankel moment sequence. This is impossible because of the nonreal pole just proved. Here is an elementary justification, avoiding a spectral-positivity assumption about B. A positive Hankel sequence a_m of exponential size defines the inner product <X^i,X^j>=a_(i+j) on polynomials. Multiplication T by X is symmetric. Iterated Cauchy--Schwarz gives ||Tf||<=||f||^(1-2^(-j)) ||T^(2^j)f||^(2^(-j)). The exponential moment bound makes ||T^n f||<=C_f R^n, so letting j tend to infinity proves ||Tf||<=R||f||. Thus T extends to a bounded self-adjoint operator on the Hilbert completion. Its scalar resolvent <1,(I-zT)^(-1)1> is analytic at EVERY nonreal z. One may verify the usual resolvent fact directly from ||(T-w)f||>=|Im w| ||f|| and the same inequality for its adjoint. It agrees near zero with the moment series. Subtracting a polynomially bounded sequence changes that series by a function analytic in the unit disk, which cannot remove the nonreal pole in (5)--(6). This is the contradiction. The conclusion concerns a source-compatible REFLECTION/HANKEL decomposition with a correction uniformly polynomial in repetition. The nonordinary source radical cannot be bounded in that way just by invoking ordinary-color unitarity. It retains expanding channels. It remains possible that, for each fixed knot as N tends to infinity, a different marked extension has a polynomially bounded negative part; this fixed-N computation does not decide that question. Likewise a nonlinear or word-dependent norm formula need not give the Hankel form (2), and is not excluded. The positive cyclic norm already known for all knots is a different construction. No broad volume theorem, asymptotic counterexample, or positivity failure for the scalar values themselves follows here. ## 5. Reproducible certificate python3 experiments/audit_weaving_source_expanding_reflection_channels.py The certificate contains the exact numerator/denominator lists, the matrix-recurrence verification, the rational isolating rectangle, and the disjoint fifth-power resultants. The whole proof uses the original local matrices, source, word and ordinary-color unitarity already independently derived in this repository.

title: Weighted complete-crossing norms and the actual Green-source gap
text: # Weighted complete-crossing norms and the actual Green-source gap 28 October 2026. The ORIGINAL complete crossing has a uniform compact variational formula for its exponential norm in real boundary metrics. At the flat metric its unique maximum is the regular octahedral point and its rate is 2 Catalan/pi. The COMPLETE Green source, including its carry, has a much smaller explicit metric exponent. This proves an open weighted operator-norm gap for both signs. This is a norm comparison. It does not assert noncancellation of the original closed scalar period or replace the actual exterior source by a norm-maximizing vector. The [audit](../experiments/audit_weighted_crossing_source_gap.py) and [results](../experiments/weighted_crossing_source_gap_results.json) check literal weighted R/source norms, endpoint-uniform factorial estimates and signed metric-rate diagnostics. The weighted optimizer in that script is a diagnostic; the rigorous variational formula, flat maximum and explicit gap chamber are proved below. ## 1. The actual coefficient and metric Put q=exp(pi*i/N), Q=q^2, x=-q^(-1), F_k=(Q;Q)_k and d=N-1. The exact positive Green reconstruction, with original unit scalar kappa retained, has input (a,b), output (a+b-j,j), and coefficient kappa*x^(-b-j)Q^(jb) F_(a+b-j)F_a/[F_(a-j)F_bF_j], (1) when 0<=j<=a<N, 0<=b<N and a+b-j<N; otherwise it is zero. Every displayed factor is nonzero on this range. This is the ORIGINAL crossing coefficient, independently checked against its gate word, not a positive surrogate. Give input and output basis vectors real exponential metrics W_in|a,b>=exp(rho_a*a+rho_b*b)|a,b>, W_out|c,e>=exp(rho_c*c+rho_d*e)|c,e>, R_(+,rho)=W_out R_+ W_in^(-1). (2) Set p=rho_c-rho_a, q_w=rho_c-rho_b, r=rho_d-rho_a. The symbol q_w is a REAL weight, distinct from the root q. With alpha=(a-j)/N, beta=b/N, gamma=j/N, the exact boundary-metric exponent in (1) is N(p alpha+q_w beta+r gamma). ## 2. Uniform factorial and Laplace estimates Define the continuous function J(s)=integral_0^s log(2 sin(pi t))dt, 0<=s<=1. Uniformly for 0<=k<N, log|F_k|=N J(k/N)+O(log N). (3) One direct proof writes log(2 sin(pi t))=log t+log(1-t)+b(t), where b extends smoothly to [0,1]. Stirling bounds on the two finite factorial sums give O(log N) uniformly, including k=0 and k=N-1; the smooth remainder has bounded Riemann-sum error. Thus no fixed distance from a factorial endpoint is needed. Let D={alpha,beta,gamma>=0: alpha+beta<=1, alpha+gamma<=1}, f=J(alpha+beta)+J(alpha+gamma)-J(alpha)-J(beta)-J(gamma), M(p,q_w,r)=max_D [f+p alpha+q_w beta+r gamma]. (4) Then for EVERY compact real metric set K, log||R_(+,rho)||_HS=N M(p,q_w,r)+O_K(log N). (5) The same formula holds for operator norm, with another O_K(log N). Indeed the positive sum of squared matrix entries lies between its largest summand and N^3 times that summand. Equation (3) approximates each logarithm by the phase in (4) with O(log N) error. Conversely shrink any point of D by 1-1/N and round its coordinates DOWN to the 1/N grid. The resulting physical indices obey both upper bounds N-1 and lie O(1/N) away. The uniform modulus of continuity of J is O(eta(1+|log eta|)), so the maximal phase changes by O_K(log N/N). This proves the uniform two-sided estimate (5). Finally ||R||_op<=||R||_HS<=N||R||_op, so their rates agree. There is also an exact finite separable formula useful for computation. Set A_N(k;s)=sum_(t=0)^(d-k) |F_(k+t)/F_t|^2 exp(2s t). Then the ACTUAL weighted squared HS norm is exactly ||R_(+,rho)||_HS^2=sum_(k=0)^d |F_k|^(-2) exp(2p k) A_N(k;q_w)A_N(k;r). (5a) This takes O(N^2) positive real operations without evaluating a new invariant or assuming that the original scalar sum is positive. For the negative crossing the exact balanced antiunitary identity is R_-=P overline(R_+)P, including its original Cartan phase. Therefore (5) applies with both input weights and both output weights swapped: p_-=rho_d-rho_b, q_-=rho_d-rho_a, r_-=rho_c-rho_b. (6) No factorial metric conversion is used. All estimates are uniform on compact sets and hold for the literal two signs. ## 3. The unique flat maximum and its value For fixed 0<alpha<1 put g_alpha(t)=J(alpha+t)-J(t). On 0<t<1-alpha, g_alpha'=log[sin(pi(alpha+t))/sin(pi t)], g_alpha''=-pi sin(pi alpha) /[sin(pi(alpha+t))sin(pi t)]<0. Thus the unique maximizers in beta and gamma at zero weights are both (1-alpha)/2. The mean of log(2 sin(pi t)) is zero and J(1-s)=-J(s). The reduced maximum is consequently F(alpha)=-4J((1-alpha)/2)-J(alpha), F'(alpha)=log cot(pi alpha/2). (7) It increases to alpha=1/2 and decreases afterward; its endpoint values are zero. Hence the unique maximum on the ENTIRE domain is (alpha,beta,gamma)=(1/2,1/4,1/4), M(0,0,0)=-4J(1/4)=2G/pi, (8) where G=sum_(n>=0)(-1)^n/(2n+1)^2 is Catalan's constant. To obtain the last equality independently, expand log|1-r exp(2*pi*i*t)| for r<1, integrate its absolutely convergent Fourier series, and let r tend to one in L^1. This gives J(1/4)=-G/(2*pi). Equivalently 2G/pi=v_8/(2*pi), where v_8=4G is the volume of the regular ideal octahedron. Only the explicit Catalan value is needed for the norm theorem. In particular log||R_+||=log||R_-||=N*(2G/pi)+O(log N). (9) The maximizing Hessian is -pi[[2,1,1],[1,2,0],[1,0,2]], negative definite. Thus the maximum and M vary smoothly for sufficiently small weights. No global concavity for arbitrary weights is assumed. ## 4. A one-dimensional computation for arbitrary real weights For every 0<alpha<1, strict concavity gives the exact inner optima beta_*(alpha;q_w) =Arg(exp(-q_w)-exp(-pi*i*alpha))/pi, gamma_*(alpha;r) =Arg(exp(-r)-exp(-pi*i*alpha))/pi. (10) Both lie strictly between zero and 1-alpha. Thus M is the maximum over the SINGLE interval alpha in [0,1] of (4) evaluated at (10). Its endpoint values are max(0,q_w)+max(0,r) at alpha=0 and p at alpha=1. This is an explicit computable variational problem, including weighted maxima that reach the boundary. Uniqueness is not asserted for arbitrary weights. ## 5. Sharp complete Green-source exponent with its carry retained Use the actual COMPLETE Green source L=G_out+G_in+G_top from [the sharp endpoint theorem](actual_crossing_shared_face_fourier_source.md#9-exact-flat-metric-norm-of-the-complete-green-source). This is the weighted crossing source of that theorem, NOT the unweighted exponentially large fusion-ground channel H_m. Its exact complete coefficients are unit phases on the following supports: * G_out maps (a,b) to(a+b,0), a>=1 and a+b<N. * G_in maps (a,0) to(a-e,e), 1<=e<=a<N. * G_top is one rank-one block on pair degree N, with input(a,N-a) and output(N-e,e), 1<=a,e<N, and unit-modulus input/output factors. Put L_rho=W_out L W_in^(-1). For either operator or HS norm, log||L_rho||=N delta(rho)+O_K(log N), delta(rho)=max(0,max(rho_c,rho_d)-min(rho_a,rho_b)). (11) Here is the full endpoint proof. The rank-one carry has norm equal to the product of its weighted vector norms. Its output components have magnitudes exp[rho_c(N-e)+rho_d e], and its input covector components exp[-rho_a a-rho_b(N-a)]. The allowed grids approach both ends within 1/N, so its logarithmic norm is N(max rho_out-min rho_in)+O_K(log N), uniformly even at tied weights. The ground-output triangular support gives rate max(0,p,q_w). The ground-input triangular support gives rate max(0,p,r). The degree-one ground entry supplies the lower rate zero even if every metric difference is negative. Both triangular rates are at most delta. Different total-degree blocks isolate the top carry, and different second-output supports isolate the two lower-degree ground terms, so cancellation cannot remove the maximal component. Projection onto those supports bounds each component by the whole operator; the reverse bound is their triangle sum. This proves (11), including the carry and BOTH ground sources. The same assertion for HS follows also by their disjoint matrix-entry supports. Negative crossing sources are transported by the same flip-conjugation; delta is unchanged by the swaps, proving (11) for both signs. The norms of the COMPLETE Green source are only polynomial at the flat metric. The carry fixes the sharp positive exponent when output radii dominate input radii. It has not been omitted as a negligible degree-N correction. ## 6. An explicit open radius chamber for the relative source norm gap Evaluate (4) at its unweighted maximizing point. This gives M_+(rho)>=2G/pi+L_+(rho), L_+=(3rho_c+rho_d-3rho_a-rho_b)/4, M_-(rho)>=2G/pi+L_-(rho), L_-=(rho_c+3rho_d-rho_a-3rho_b)/4. (12) Consequently the following strict, explicit piecewise-linear chamber contains the flat metric: delta(rho)<2G/pi+min(L_+(rho),L_-(rho)). (13) On every compact subset with a margin eta>0, equations (5), (6), and (11) prove for BOTH crossing signs ||L_(sigma,rho)||/||R_(sigma,rho)|| <=N^C exp(-N eta). (14) One convenient radius cube is |rho_i|<=epsilon, with 0<epsilon<G/(2*pi). Then delta<=2epsilon and L_+,L_->=-2epsilon. Hence (14) holds uniformly with any eta<2G/pi-4epsilon. The fixed explicit choice epsilon=1/10 even permits eta=4/25 without relying on a decimal evaluation: the alternating series gives G>8/9, and pi<22/7 implies 2G/pi-2/5>82/495>4/25. A common additive shift of all four rho_i leaves every comparison unchanged, so this can also be viewed as a chamber of radius RATIOS rather than a fixed overall scale. These are relative operator/HS norm gaps for the actual sourced crossing equation. Contracting through the rest of a knot can select a subspace far below the norm-maximizing octahedral profile. No scalar volume limit or source-angle lower bound follows from (14) alone.

title: Whole clock functions require an endpoint extension
text: # Whole clock functions require an endpoint extension Independent algebraic proof and actual-source audit, 27 October 2026. The exact endpoint-completed Jackson current retains its input function, rather than only that function's finite matrix value. There is a precise obstruction to forgetting the function and an explicit flat tower that retains the additional endpoints. This is the usual infinite-order quantum-shift phenomenon; no novelty claim is made for the algebraic simplicity statement. ## 1. The actual whole current and its retained function On one actual Frobenius residue string, let \[ C_Q=c Z^R,\quad 0\le R\le N,\quad Z=Q^N, \quad eC_Q=ZC_Qe,\quad fC_Q=Z^{-1}C_Qf. \] Here c=Q^s for the original physical clock. The actual divided e(q),f(q) have nonzero interior arrow coefficients at the root. Invert just those finite arrows and set the absent endpoint arrow to zero. This defines regular ORIGINAL whole germs e^dagger,f^dagger with \[ e^\dagger e=I-P_0,\qquad f^\dagger f=I-P_N. \tag{1} \] No inverse of the whole nilpotent matrix is asserted. For a RETAINED function g, the exact whole current is \[ \mathcal J_Z(g)= \frac{-e^\dagger[e,g(ZC_Q)] +P_0 f^\dagger[f,g(C_Q)]}{1-Z} =\frac{g(C_Q)-g(ZC_Q)}{1-Z}. \tag{2} \] The full proof and its actual matrix/source implementation are in [the endpoint-completed normal clock current](endpoint_completed_normal_clock_euler_current.md). For an independent check of the order, put D=g(C_Q)-g(ZC_Q). The first numerator is (I-P_0)D, and the second is P_0(I-P_N)D=P_0D. Their sum is D. This also identifies precisely where the lower endpoint is repaired. Polynomials and Laurent polynomials are always allowed. Rational or marked analytic functions require their denominators or domains at EVERY shifted spectrum used in (2). The root value is C_0 g'(C_0), with any explicit coefficient parameter held fixed. An additional coefficient derivative is a separate operation. The inverse arrows are regular actual q-germs because their root coefficients are r-R+1 and R+1, respectively (with r=N here), times fixed nonzero root units. This is not a generic module inverse or a Hopf-natural contraction on arbitrary tensor summands. ## 2. No finite-dimensional compatible function quotient at generic Z Let K be a characteristic-zero field, let Z in K^times have infinite multiplicative order, and put F=K[x,x^-1]. The shift is sigma(g)(x)=g(Zx), fixing K. Then **Claim.** A nonzero ideal I with sigma(I) contained in I is F. Consequently F has no nonzero finite-dimensional quotient carrying the induced whole shift or Jackson operator D_Z=(1-sigma)/(1-Z). Proof. Write I=(p), multiplying its Laurent generator by a unit to make p an ordinary polynomial with nonzero constant term. The divisibility p(x)|p(Zx), and equality of degrees, give p(Zx)=a p(x) for a nonzero scalar a. If p has positive degree, choose a root r over an algebraic closure. It is nonzero. Then all Z^j r, j>=0, are roots, contradicting their infinitude. Thus p is a nonzero constant and I=F. This also proves sigma(I)=I; one-sided stability was sufficient. Because 1-Z is a field unit, Jackson stability and shift stability are equivalent. The statement concerns a COMPATIBLE FUNCTION-ALGEBRA quotient at generic Z. It does not prohibit finite root modules, finite matrix representations, or the actual cyclic/Steinberg source. Evaluation on a finite spectral string is perfectly valid; it simply forgets the endpoint value needed for the next shift. ## 3. The actual minimal-polynomial certificate and its normal order For the actual spectral string let \[ P_N(x)=\prod_{r=0}^N(x-cZ^r). \] Then P_N(C_Q)=0 exactly, whereas \[ P_N(ZC_Q)=P_N(cZ^{N+1})P_N^{\rm top},\qquad P_N(cZ^{N+1})= c^{N+1}Z^{N(N+1)/2}\prod_{j=1}^{N+1}(Z^j-1). \tag{3} \] Here P_N^top denotes the last BLOCK PROJECTOR, not the polynomial. Every other entry of P_N(ZC_Q) is zero. Thus the retained function P_N and the zero function have the SAME actual matrix value, but their currents differ. With delta=1-Z, (2)--(3) give \[ \mathcal J_Z(P_N)=(-1)^N c_0^{N+1}(N+1)! \delta^N P_N^{\rm top}+O(\delta^{N+1}). \tag{4} \] The defect is invisible to every normal truncation below order N. This is an exact reason why a bounded-order jet calculation cannot discard the whole clock function. It does not contradict bounded-jet reconstruction in a separately fixed bounded-complexity pole lattice: the degree of P_N grows with N. ## 4. A flat confluent tower supplies the missing endpoints There is a constructive integral alternative to an impossible fixed finite quotient. Let R=k[[delta]], Z=1-delta, and c in R^times. Put \[ P_L(x)=\prod_{r=0}^L(x-cZ^r),\qquad A_L=R[x,x^{-1}]/(P_L),\quad L\ge0. \tag{5} \] The polynomial is monic with unit constant term, so A_L is R-free of rank L+1. Forgetting the last endpoint gives A_L to A_(L-1). The exact Jackson operator induces \[ D_Z:A_L\longrightarrow A_{L-1}. \tag{6} \] Indeed D_Z P_L is integral: every coefficient of P_L(x)-P_L(Zx) is divisible by 1-Z. Over k((delta)) it vanishes at c,cZ,...,cZ^(L-1), so is divisible by the monic P_(L-1). Monic division shows the quotient is already integral over R. The same argument applies to a multiple of P_L, or directly to the Jackson product formula. Thus (6) is independent of a representative. At the root, \[ A_L/delta A_L=k[x]/(x-c_0)^{L+1},\qquad D_Z\longmapsto x\partial_x:A_{L,0}\to A_{L-1,0}. \tag{7} \] These are CONFLUENT jet lattices. They are not the ordinary root matrix image: the latter sets C_0=c_0 I and kills all positive powers of x-c_0. For example x-c_0 has zero ambient root matrix value, but its Jackson image has root value c_0 I. For the actual original interval L=N, one extra endpoint suffices for one whole Jackson action; j actions use A_(N+j) to A_N. The compatible inverse tower retains all such endpoint values without divided Vandermonde or idempotent denominators. It is an infinite completed FUNCTION object, not an extra finite quantum color or a tensor-intertwining theorem. The functions supplied to it must still be the specified actual whole functions, with their marks; arbitrary formal sections are not substituted for them. ### The exact spectral index and its flat source extension The integral distinction from the ambient finite matrix values can be computed exactly. Use the Newton basis \[ p_j(x)=\prod_{u=0}^{j-1}(x-cZ^u),\quad 0\le j\le L. \] The monomial-to-Newton change of basis is unitriangular. Its evaluation matrix V_(rj)=p_j(cZ^r), r=0,...,L, is lower triangular: \[ V_{rj}=c^jZ^{j(j-1)/2} \prod_{k=r-j+1}^r(Z^k-1) =\delta^j W_{rj}\quad(r\ge j). \tag{8} \] At the root W_(rj)=(-c_0)^j(r)_j, with falling factorial (r)_j. Its diagonal entries (-c_0)^j j! are units. Thus W is invertible over R and the evaluation map A_L to R^(L+1) has EXACT Smith factors \[ 1,\delta,\ldots,\delta^L, \qquad v_\delta(\det V)=L(L+1)/2. \tag{9} \] This identifies the confluent source lattice lost by ordinary ambient root evaluation. The kernel of forgetting the last endpoint is explicitly \[ 0\longrightarrow R\,P_{L-1}\longrightarrow A_L \longrightarrow A_{L-1}\longrightarrow0. \tag{10} \] Multiplication by x acts on this rank-one line by cZ^L. Its sole nonzero generic spectral value is at the new endpoint, namely \[ P_{L-1}(cZ^L)=c^LZ^{L(L-1)/2}\prod_{j=1}^L(Z^j-1), \] of exact order L, with leading coefficient (-c_0)^L L!. There is a second, different exact sequence giving an integral Jackson primitive: \[ 0\longrightarrow R\cdot1\longrightarrow A_L \xrightarrow{D_Z}A_{L-1}\longrightarrow0. \tag{11} \] Indeed D_Z x^j=[j]_Z x^j and [j]_Z is a root unit for 1<=j<=L. The classes x,...,x^L form a basis of A_(L-1), because x is a unit there. This proves surjectivity. If a degree-at-most-L representative g has D_Z g=0 in the target, D_Z g must be a scalar multiple of P_(L-1); its zero constant term and the unit constant term of P_(L-1) force that scalar to vanish. Thus g is constant. The whole primitive requires no division by delta. Both actions are explicit in the same Newton basis: \[ x p_j=p_{j+1}+cZ^j p_j,\qquad D_Zp_j=[j]_Z x p_{j-1}\quad(j\ge1). \tag{11a} \] The first identity makes the retained clock a bidiagonal matrix; at delta=0 it is the single Jordan block c_0 I plus its nilpotent shift. The second follows by factoring p_j(Zx)=Z^j(x-cZ^{-1})p_{j-1}(x). These give constructive finite flow equations on the confluent lattice, without diagonalizing by singular idempotents. The root of every [j]_Z is the nonzero scalar j, so the primitive is regular at the marked root at each fixed L. Its whole rational formulas retain the other zeros of [j]_Z; no common growing-L analytic neighborhood or bound is asserted. These regular FUNCTION lattices are not every actual regular matrix insertion. For example the original block-number matrix R is regular, while the marked function Log(x/c)/Log Z representing it on this spectrum contains a divided normal factor. Saturating the evaluation lattice allows such functions but can introduce poles in their Jackson currents: already g=(x-c)/delta has a regular finite matrix value and D_Z g=x/delta. Therefore fractional normal/current lattices and their endpoint compensations remain part of the data. Equations (9)--(11) do not discard those factors or assert that every matrix coefficient is a regular scalar function of the clock. ## 5. The root primitive has a tame actual coherent norm In the original divided basis, the Fr coherent metric is \(\|v_k\|^2=\binom Nk\). The normalized inverse-arrow lengths are \[ \frac1{\sqrt{(k+1)(N-k)}}\quad(e^\dagger),\qquad \frac1{\sqrt{k(N-k+1)}}\quad(f^\dagger). \] Their largest values occur at the extreme arrows. Consequently \[ \|e^\dagger_0\|=\|f^\dagger_0\|=N^{-1/2}, \quad\|P_0\|=\|P_N\|=1. \tag{12} \] This positive bound is for the ROOT inverse-arrow operators in the specified actual Frobenius metric. It gives neither a uniform whole normal-neighborhood estimate nor a norm bound for arbitrary inserted functions and all full braiding operators. In particular it does not remove the separate exponential endpoint-row norms computed in [the actual relative source period](actual_frobenius_relative_endpoint_period.md). The integrated row can still have cancellations; all endpoint and source normalization factors remain. The conclusions are therefore compatible: a tame finite root primitive exists, while exact whole functional transport requires the additional endpoint extension. A comparison with the actual network's geometric framing currents must preserve that extension, its true co-source and the ordinary/divided Hopf endpoint terms. [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_whole_clock_endpoint_extension.py) checks the integral confluent tower, the actual spectral-polynomial defect and its sign/order, and the root primitive norms. The independent [confluent-lattice audit](../experiments/audit_whole_clock_confluent_lattice.py) checks the Newton evaluation, Smith factors, primitive kernel and new-endpoint line explicitly.

title: The whole original Fermat source as a toric residue, with its wire seams
text: # The whole original Fermat source as a toric residue, with its wire seams 28 October 2026. The exact balanced Fourier crossing theorem gives a single scalar period for the ORIGINAL complete knot source. Its co-source is an explicit rational function of bounded degree on the finite Fermat grids. This note computes its root-grid Jacobian and the different Jacobian of a wire-pole pushforward. The latter has coefficient one, but its other relative currents need not vanish. In fact an exact local calculation shows that sewing a balanced full-Psi block off its original central grid REGENERATES the beta/Rogers current. Thus the residue formula does not by itself identify the original period with a positive geometric cycle. All frame changes below are reversible finite changes of basis. All original cups, ordinary caps, the FULL marked row, pivots and external scalar lines are retained. The proofs use the exact crossing theorem, not a new invariant or a favorable source. ## 1. Exact bounded-degree rational co-source Put N>=2, d=N-1, Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), x=-exp(-pi*i/N), and s=x^N=(-1)^(N+1). On a port with central coordinate C choose a marked root r^N=C and the finite grid z=r Q^k. The normalized frame is F(r)_(k,a)=z^a/sqrt(N), F(r)^(-1)_(a,k)=z^(-a)/sqrt(N), 0<=a,k<N. (1) The [exact balanced crossing](actual_balanced_fourier_crossing_kernel.md) and its complete antiunitary mirror apply independently at every signed crossing. Join their ports with the actual frame adapters. No matching of distinct central grids is implicit. Let K_N(t)=sum_(a=0)^d t^a. For an output port x0^N=C and the next input y^N=D the adapter is exactly E(y,x0)=[1-D/C]/[N(1-y/x0)]. (2) The pivot on the actual oriented head is g_a=x^(1-N)Q^(-a)=(x/s)Q^(-a), so its adapter is E_g(y,x0)=(x/s)[1-D/C]/[N(1-Q^(-1)y/x0)]. (3) At a removable collision the original finite K_N is understood. The unpivoted first trace, where present, has its ORIGINAL external normalization; it is not absorbed into (3). For completeness, use the actual physical pair sources proved in [the coupled-cap theorem](actual_coupled_caps_interval_source.md): p(a,b)=N x^(a-d) delta_(a+b,d), m(a,b)=N^(-1)(x^(-1)Q^(-1))^a delta_(a+b,d), m_mark(a,b)=x^b/N^2, ALL 0<=a,b<N. (4) If z_i^N=C_i, their transformed entries are the following exact rational functions ON THE GRIDS: (F_1 tensor F_2)p =(x/s)(C_2-s C_1)/(z_2-x z_1), m(F_1^(-1) tensor F_2^(-1)) =z_1 z_2(C_1-s C_2) /[N^2 C_1 C_2(z_1-x^(-1)Q^(-1)z_2)], m_mark(F_1^(-1) tensor F_2^(-1)) =z_1 z_2(C_1-1)(C_2-s) /[N^3 C_1 C_2(z_1-1)(z_2-x)]. (5) In particular the marked source in (5) is the FULL row in (4), not its restriction to an invariant fiber after some decomposition. The first two formulas follow from K_N and z_i^d=C_i/z_i. The marked row gives N^(-3)K_N(z_1^(-1))K_N(x/z_2), which gives the last formula. These computations fix every N and Q factor. For a fixed diagram the product of (2), (3), (5) is therefore a rational function of degree bounded independently of N, after its explicit powers of N and the actual unit phases are separated. The central parameters are fixed nonzero constants. On the generic source chart require the corresponding numerator differences in (2), (5) to be nonzero. This is a finite list of proper algebraic conditions and can be arranged by the independent local frames. One may insert another reversible frame on a wire if needed; the added grid variable and BOTH adapters are then retained. On compact subsets of this generic central chart, each entry of this rational source and its reciprocal has at most polynomial size in N. Indeed the moduli of all marked Nth roots are uniformly bounded above and below, each numerator difference stays nonzero, and |1-y/x0| >= c/N if C!=D, and likewise for the shifted denominators in (5). To see the last bound, use (1-t^N)/(1-t)=sum_(a=0)^d t^a and the fixed nonzero central numerator. The elementary upper bound on this sum is O(N) because |t|^N is fixed. Thus no exponential source gauge is hidden in this initial regular chart. An ambient rational unit is not a geometric thimble coefficient. ## 2. The exact single toric residue of the whole source Expand the complete transformed word, including (5), as its finite sum over all port labels. Write it as P_N=chi_N sum_(z_i^N=C_i, all i) H_N(z) A_N(z). (6) Here H_N is the product of the exact signed four-full-Psi crossing entries (including their Gaussian and actual local constants); A_N is the rational co-source from Section 1. The external original line chi_N is unchanged. No new normalization of the sum is used. Let f_i=z_i^N-C_i. The coordinate algebra T_N=C[z_1^(+/-1),...,z_n^(+/-1)]/(f_1,...,f_n) is finite etale. Its source is the actual finite trace in (6), not a postulated trace on a geometric critical algebra. At a grid point det(d f_i/d z_j)=N^n product_i z_i^(N-1). (7) Choose the continued local full-Psi germs which give the specified grid entries. With coordinate order fixed as dz_1 wedge ... wedge dz_n, the exact period is P_N=chi_N Res_(all f_i=0) H_N(z) A_N(z) product_i [N z_i^(N-1) dz_i/(z_i^N-C_i)]. (8) The normalized residue is the sum of the local product-circle integrals divided by (2*pi*i)^n. Every grid point has coefficient ONE, by (7). The same statement holds with N C_i/z_i in place of N z_i^(N-1); these numerators agree on the grid. Such a change of off-grid extension need not preserve individual zero/infinity boundary terms during a later contour deformation. Equation (8) is a specified original cycle and a single period. It does not turn the grid algebra into the classical gluing algebra. Different off-grid holomorphic extensions with the same grid values have the same small residues and can have different critical schemes. Any proposed deformation to a geometric shape cycle must therefore transport the whole form, source and relative boundaries, not just its sampled values. ## 3. Wire-pole pushforward and its exact Jacobian Keep one wire with x0^N=C, y^N=D, C!=D. Let f(x0) denote the complete remaining local field, with its actual logarithmic marks. Its Fourier interpolation is I_(C->D) f(y) =sum_(x0^N=C) [1-D/C]/[N(1-y/x0)] f(x0) =sum_(x0^N=C) Res_x0 omega, omega=(C-D)f(x0) dx0/[(x0^N-C)(x0-y)]. (9) The grid residue in (9) is (2) times f. The DISTINCT wire collision pole x0=y has Res_(x0=y) omega=-f(y). (10) Thus pushing the grid contours across the collision gives a coefficient-one substitution x0=y. No color, Gaussian or root Jacobian is missing. It is a different residue calculation from (7). More precisely, on any marked branch domain U containing the grid points and y, with all additional poles and branch lips retained, the residue theorem gives I_(C->D) f(y) =f(y)+(1/(2*pi*i)) integral_(boundary U) omega -sum_(other poles in U) Res omega. (11) The boundary includes the logarithmic cut lips and any zero/infinity or endpoint circles needed to specify that branch domain. There is no assumption that they vanish. If f is a polynomial of degree<N, one can take U approaching the sphere, the integral at infinity vanishes, and (11) is ordinary polynomial interpolation. For a full function these hypotheses generally fail. For a collection of wire edges whose undirected graph is a forest, successive collision residues eliminate one variable at a time with the same coefficient one. Retain one variable in each component; with leaf-first orientation their coordinate incidence matrix is triangular with diagonal one. All non-wire branches in (11) are still present. For an edge closing a cycle there is no additional independent leaf variable; a closure condition or a remaining residue has to be retained. In particular the forest calculation does not dispose of the closed knot source. ## 4. Sewing recreates the exact original beta current Fix v and choose the old central grid C=1+v^N, C!=0. On that grid the EXACT original Newton source identity is B_N(x0,v)=S_N(x0,v), B_N(u,v)=S_N(u,v)+(1-u^N+v^N)I_N(u,v). (12) The functions and marks in (12) are those of [the normalized beta source](actual_trivalent_quantum_beta_source.md). Choose the grid germs by that identity, away from its exceptional divisors. The polynomial B_N has degree<N in its first argument. For y^N=D, its interpolation theorem and (12) therefore imply the EXACT identity I_(C->D)[ S_N(.,v)|_(x0^N=C) ](y) =B_N(y,v) =S_N(y,v)+(C-D)I_N(y,v). (13) Consequently the aggregate non-wire term in (11), for this source, is exactly boundary integral - other-pole residues =(C-D)I_N(y,v). (14) This is an identified beta source, rather than an unspecified remainder defined by a putative global asymptotic. Its coefficient is the difference between the two central wire parameters. The current is generally nonzero; it is not killed by the old balance C=1+v^N after y has moved off that grid. The Rogers sink is identical in structure. On its old grid C=1-v^N, use the independently proved R_N(u,v)=T_N(u,v)+(1-u^N-v^N)J_N(u,v). Since R_N also has degree<N in u, the corresponding exact formula is I_(C->D)[ T_N(.,v)|_(x0^N=C) ](y) =R_N(y,v)=T_N(y,v)+(C-D)J_N(y,v). (15) It retains the opposite-root contour and the full norm of [the Rogers source](actual_rogers_sink_opposite_beta_source.md). Apparent C=D collisions are interpreted by the finite interpolation and the continued complete source, not by dividing (14) by C-D. Thus balancing the local blocks and then gluing by only the collision residues is not in general an exact source operation. The omitted seam is the original current in a different polarization. Its exact logarithmic continuation can itself carry a regular geometric sector, as proved in [the current connection](actual_beta_current_connection_and_monodromy.md). Neither its vanishing nor an exponential gap follows from local balancing or from the unit residue (10). ## 5. Interior adapters and bulk logarithmic seams are different The [propagated-frame theorem](propagated_balanced_frames_and_boundary_source.md) makes every INTERIOR finite Fourier adapter the identity on an open braid. Thus at most the braid width many nontrivial frame adapters remain at its boundary. This exact statement does not imply that the off-grid bulk full-Psi continuation has no logarithmic seams. Here is an explicit sewn test, using the independently verified [four-port characters](balanced_crossing_deck_characters.md). Sew two positive crossings with central port data M_1=M(A,B,C,D), M_2=M(C,D,E,F). The internal C and D variables have whole-product characters nu_C=-s E(A-C)/[D(C-E)], nu_D=-s B(F-D)/[C(D-B)]. (16) For example nu_C is mu_c of the first crossing times mu_a of the second; C-sD=-s(D-sC) cancels the common local factor. No wire adapter was introduced. After the propagated pair of crossings the external centers return to their original values, so set E=A,F=B. Then, as identities of the WHOLE bulk product away from divisors, nu_C=sA/D, nu_D=sB/C. (17) These characters equal one on the original internal grids C=sB, D=sA, but do not equal one during arbitrary off-grid motion. The whole product has a bulk seam even though it has no interior Fourier adapter. This example also permits an exact, but limited, dual-character residue transformation. Write c,d for the actual internal variables and put f_c=c^N-sB, f_d=d^N-sA, G_c=nu_C-1=-f_d/d^N, G_d=nu_D-1=-f_c/c^N. (18) The change from (f_c,f_d) to (G_c,G_d) is invertible near every nonzero grid point. Its coefficient matrix and determinant are L=[[0,-d^(-N)],[-c^(-N),0]], det L=-(cd)^(-N). Consequently the exact local Grothendieck transformation rule is Res_f H dc wedge dd/(f_c f_d) =Res_G H det(L) dc wedge dd/(G_c G_d). (19) At a grid point the two coordinate Jacobians are respectively N^2 c^(N-1)d^(N-1) and -N^2/(cd). Their ratio is exactly det L, including its sign; the residue contours use their respective ordered defining functions. Thus (19) has no missing Jacobian. But the zero sets in (18) are EXACTLY the same finite grid. This calculation replaces its defining equations; it does not transform the source to a different classical geometric cycle. In particular nu_C=nu_D=1 pins the two internal centers at their original values when A,B are fixed. Also, the first defect in (18) cancels the OPPOSITE grid denominator f_d in a seam form. The resulting regular current is not zero merely because its numerator vanished on the grid. Formula (13) gives a fully normalized source example of that same cancellation mechanism. The source-deformation problem therefore includes both the remaining boundary Fourier co-source and the bulk logarithmic seams of the chosen off-grid continuation. Neither is removed by the telescoping of interior finite changes of basis. ## 6. What is fixed and what is still required Equations (5)--(8) give the entire original co-source and a single finite etale residue period, without an exponentially unspecified matrix source. Equations (9)--(15) compute what an actual wire-pole pushforward adds. Iterated forest collision residues have exact degree one, but the independent non-wire currents remain and can be identified explicitly on the elementary trivalent blocks. The remaining theorem is an actual deformation or exact regrouping of this complete relative source onto the geometric shape cycle, with its geometric coefficient proved nonzero and the other total sectors controlled. A nonzero rational density on the grid, or a unit collision Jacobian, does not prove that theorem. No volume limit for a broad knot class is claimed here. ## 7. Reproducible audit python3 experiments/audit_whole_fermat_toric_residue_and_wire_source.py The audit checks the normalized source table via its unnormalized finite Fourier form (so every square-root normalization is explicit), the original whole signed plat contraction, the toric Jacobians, the wire/extra-pole residue identity, both exact current regeneration identities using independent full-Psi evaluations, the sewn characters (16)--(17), and the exact dual-character Jacobian in (19).

title: An actual whole Frobenius source is a Fermat-cover trace
text: # An actual whole Frobenius source is a Fermat-cover trace Research proof, 27 October 2026. Integral divided powers give a whole algebraic source polynomial whose root value is the actual binomial coherent source. Its Kummer-cover trace, norm and first quantum-normal flag transport are explicit. This supplies a source object before taking jets, with every power and phase retained. This is a choice of whole coupons in the ORIGINAL integral color. An explicit root-identity pair gauge compares it with the previously specified divided-exponential coupons. Operators and all partial sources must be transported by that gauge. No equality with a new state model, controlled growing-level norm, or selected geometric period is inferred. ## 1. Actual divided powers and the whole polynomial Fix N>=2, m=N(N+1)-1 and a residue string 0<=s<N in D_m(q). Use the constant actual sign frame \[ w_{k,s}=\beta_{k,s}u_{kN+s},\qquad \beta_{k,s}=(-1)^{Nk(k-1)/2+ks},\quad 0\le k\le N. \] Symmetric Gaussian coefficients below are integral Laurent polynomials, with the original divided-power formulas \[ F^{(r)}u_j={j+r\brack r}_q u_{j+r},\qquad E^{(r)}u_j={m-j+r\brack r}_q u_{j-r}. \] Put L_s=m-s and epsilon_s=(-1)^(N-1+s). Define \[ A_{k,s}(q)=\epsilon_s^k{L_s\brack kN}_q,\qquad P_s(q,t)=\sum_{k=0}^N A_{k,s}(q)t^k. \tag{1} \] Here t is a SOURCE-FLAG coupling. It is not the knot meridian, the classical longitude, or a quantum-A spectral coordinate. The literal constant-frame ket psi_s=sum_k w_(k,s) is made from actual divided powers as \[ \psi_s=\sum_k\frac{\beta_{k,s}}{{s+kN\brack kN}_q} F^{(kN)}u_s. \tag{2} \] Every denominator is a unit at q_N: its root value is (-1)^(ks). The homogeneous dual is also an actual divided-power row: \[ \widetilde\lambda_s(q;c,d)= \sum_k\epsilon_s^k\beta_{k,s}c^{N-k}d^k u_s^*E^{(kN)}. \] Its value on w_(k,s) is A_(k,s)c^(N-k)d^k. Thus its pairing with the ket is the homogeneous polynomial \[ B_s(q;c,d)=\sum_k A_{k,s}(q)c^{N-k}d^k, \quad B_s(q;1,t)=P_s(q,t). \tag{3} \] Normalize by this ORIGINAL pairing unit on its marked chart. At c=d=1 the normalized dual has coefficients A_k/P_s(q,1). The root value P_s(q_N,1)=2^N is retained, not set to one before normalization. Scaling the ket by alpha^N and the dual inversely retains the unprojectivized source line. ## 2. Exact trace and norm on the root cover Let zeta_N be the marked N-th root of unity, independent of the variable q. Work on the Kummer cover x^N=epsilon_s t and set \[ \Pi_s(q,x)=\prod_{r=0}^{L_s-1} (1+q^{L_s-1-2r}x). \] Multiplication of the factors gives the symmetric Gaussian identity Pi_s=sum_j {L_s choose j}_q x^j. Averaging the deck transformations x->zeta_N x kills exactly the degrees not divisible by N. Hence \[ \boxed{\ P_s(q,t)=\frac1N\operatorname{Tr}_{x^N=\epsilon_st} \Pi_s(q,x).\ } \tag{4} \] This is an exact polynomial identity before normal specialization. It is valid even at t=0 as an identity of coefficients; the cover is etale on t!=0. The 1/N is part of the source construction. The full norm is equally explicit. Put Z=Q^N=q^(2N) and theta_s=(-1)^s q^[N(L_s-1)]. The elementary deck product gives \[ \boxed{\ \mathcal N_s(q,t):=\operatorname{Norm}\Pi_s =\prod_{r=0}^{L_s-1}(1+\theta_s Z^{-r}t).\ } \tag{5} \] Indeed Norm(1+a x)=1-(-a)^N epsilon_s t, and (-1)^N epsilon_s=-(-1)^s. No peripheral sign or central power has been removed in (5). This is a finite factorial in the WHOLE power coordinate Z, distinct from its value Z=1. On a marked cover let nu_s^N=mathcal N_s, with nu_s=1 at t=0. Then c_s=Pi_s/nu_s has norm one and \[ P_s=\nu_s\,\frac{\operatorname{Tr}c_s}{N}. \tag{6} \] Thus the source polynomial is a selected trace in a concrete norm torsor. A norm-one statement about c_s does not by itself give the trace in (6); both are specified here. Zeros of the norm or trace remain part of the lattice/domain data. There is an exact power-parameter law for the SAME source product. Put q_hat=-q^N, so q_hat^2=Z and q_hat=1 at the marked root. Since L_s-1 has parity s, (5) becomes \[ \operatorname{Norm}\Pi_s(q,x) =\prod_{r=0}^{L_s-1}(1+\widehat q^{L_s-1-2r}t) =\sum_{j=0}^{L_s}{L_s\brack j}_{\widehat q}t^j. \tag{6a} \] Thus the Kummer norm is the identical finite Gaussian product at the power parameter -q^N. Its chosen root restriction is a classical binomial product. This is an algebraic identity; it does not assert a modular-group action or equate different knot states. The norm and selected trace also retain different normal data. Write v=Log Z with v=0 at the marked root. Pairing the symmetric exponents in (6a) gives \[ [\partial_v\log\mathcal N_s]_0=0,\qquad [v^2]\log\mathcal N_s =\frac{t L_s(L_s^2-1)}{24(1+t)^2}. \tag{6b} \] Indeed their sum is zero and their squared sum is L_s(L_s^2-1)/12. The source trace in (9) generally has a nonzero FIRST normal on middle residue strings. That information is in its specified cyclic trace, even though the norm's first derivative vanishes. ## 3. Its actual root restriction and normalization Write L_s=N^2+b_s, b_s=N-1-s. At q_N every block of N factors in Pi_s contributes EXACTLY 1+t: the sign from q_N^N=-1 cancels epsilon_s as in (1). There are N full blocks. The remaining polynomial has degree b_s<N, so its deck average is one. Therefore \[ P_s(q_N,t)=(1+t)^N,\qquad A_{k,s}(q_N)={N\choose k}. \tag{7} \] One can also verify (7) by cancelling the root zero factors in the Gaussian product. Its symmetric phase is (-1)^[k(N-1-s)], which epsilon_s^k cancels for every s and every parity of N. Equations (5)--(6) keep a useful fractional head correction: \[ \mathcal N_s(q_N,t)=(1+t)^{L_s},\quad \nu_s(q_N,t)=(1+t)^{N+b_s/N},\quad \frac{\operatorname{Tr}c_s(q_N)}N=(1+t)^{-b_s/N}. \tag{8} \] All branches have the same mark at t=0. The product is (7). Dropping either factor would change the source character. In particular the original selected dual gives the endpoint E_(N,0) the value 2^(-N), with the full N-th power still visible. ## 4. First normal equals an explicit flag connection Use delta=1-Q^N and q=q_N(1-delta)^(1/(2N)). Set \[ \ell_s=-\frac12\sum_{a=1}^{s} \frac{q_N^a+q_N^{-a}}{q_N^a-q_N^{-a}}. \] Then the actual Gaussian polynomial has the exact first derivative \[ [\partial_\delta A_{k,s}]_0=k\ell_s{N\choose k},\qquad [\partial_\delta P_s]_0=\ell_s N t(1+t)^{N-1}. \tag{9} \] Here is a direct cancellation proof. Split the symmetric Gaussian product into arguments divisible by N and the remaining residues. Ratios of the vanishing q-integers have zero first relative logarithmic derivative: after their simple zeros cancel they are ratios of odd sinh functions. For each of the k nonzero residue blocks, cyclic reindexing leaves N sum_(a<=b_s) cot_q(a) in the q-log derivative. Pairing residues a and N-a makes that sum equal N sum_(a<=s) cot_q(a). Finally q partial_q=-2N partial_delta at the root. This gives (9), including its sign. At the normalized selected point t=1, the dual's first derivative is \[ [\partial_\delta\lambda_s(w_k)]_0 =2^{-N}{N\choose k}\ell_s(k-N/2). \tag{10} \] More generally it is ell_s t partial_t of the normalized root dual. Thus the first normal is a concrete source-flag transport. The same ell_s is the original head connection in [the whole Jackson current](endpoint_completed_normal_clock_euler_current.md). It vanishes for s=0,N-1; middle strings retain it. Higher normals remain those of the WHOLE polynomial (4), with no assertion that they are all a single flag reparameterization. ## 5. Exact pivotal/moment character and the original coupon gauge On this residue string J=kN+s. The frozen-pivot adapter Z^J has the exact source generating function \[ \lambda_s(q,t)Z^J\psi_s =Z^s\frac{P_s(q,tZ^N)}{P_s(q,t)}. \tag{11} \] This retains all cap/Green moments and both power coordinates. At the root its value is one, while its normal derivatives must be taken from (11), including both moving q-Gaussian coefficients. The frozen root binomial formula cannot be substituted before those derivatives. No growing-N scaled profile is asserted. Finally compare this source pair (psi_f,lambda_f) with the previous actual divided-exponential pair (psi_c,lambda_c), both normalized to one. They have the SAME root pair by (7). Let P_i=psi_i lambda_i and put \[ G=\psi_f\lambda_c+(I-P_f)(I-P_c). \] Its root is I, so it is an invertible regular rational germ, and \[ G\psi_c=\psi_f,\qquad\lambda_fG=\lambda_c. \tag{12} \] All arbitrary inserted operators must become G T G^(-1), connections include their derivative gauge term, and every source, dual, projector and peripheral adapter is carried along. This is an actual whole coupon comparison, not an inference from matching root numbers or a replacement of the source in a partial word. It supplies neither the missing geometric-current pushforward nor the selected hyperbolic-volume estimate. [Exact actual divided-source and cover audit](../experiments/audit_whole_frobenius_source_fermat_trace.py).

title: A whole Gamma profile of the actual retained quantum-factorial source
text: # A whole Gamma profile of the actual retained quantum-factorial source Research proof, 27 October 2026. The exact residual in the actual balanced-to-symmetric source frame has a uniform whole-function profile on the N^2-scaled quantum normal. It includes its integer resonance zeros and all fixed holomorphic jets. A middle-index residual is also exactly a holomorphic unit times the independently fixed actual meridian Weyl half-adapter, after a necessary parameter reparametrization that aligns their zeros. The opposite profiles multiply to the entire centered meridian factor already present in the full modified dimension. No growth assumption on the knot invariant is used. These are actual scalar source/frame comparisons, not an asserted equivalence of the whole q-normal and meridian-normal knot modules. The retained residual is established in [the exact clock-shear audit](exact_clock_shear_star_automorphism_audit.md) and [the actual polynomial source](integral_color_global_q_difference_source.md). The actual meridian half-adapter is the marked rational function of [the Weyl-gluing theorem](twisted_cotangent_source_and_weyl_gluing.md). ## 1. The actual residual and its marked normal Put c=2pi*i, n=N-1 and retain the symmetric q-binomial. On the actual integral-color family the residual after removing the quadratic clock shear is exactly V_(N,j)(q)={N-1 choose j}_q/M^j, M=-q^N. (1.1) Use the whole scaled normal H=Log Q=c/N+z/N^2, q=exp(H/2), z=ca, M=exp(z/(2N)), b=a_N=a/(1+a/N). (1.2) The marking M=-q^N gives the stated exponential since exp(c/2)=-1. The exact identity H b=z/N is important. All powers N^a below mean exp(a log N) with the real logarithm of the positive integer. For every j<N, V_(N,j)(a) =exp(-Hbj/2) product_(r=1)^j sinh[H(r-b)/2]/sinh(Hr/2). (1.3) Indeed sinh[H(N-r)/2]=sinh[H(r-b)/2], because HN=c+z/N. There is no omitted sign. Equation (1.3) is an equality of the original finite residual, not a model chosen to reproduce its jets. Set J(x)=2sinh(x/2)/x, J(0)=1. Then (1.3) separates exactly as V_(N,j)=exp(-Hbj/2) product_(r=1)^j(1-b/r) product_(r=1)^j J(H(r-b))/J(Hr). (1.4) Zeros in the first product must not be removed by logarithms. ## 2. Uniform whole-profile theorem Define the marked chord function for 0<T<1 by G(T)=(exp(cT)-1)/c =exp(pi*i T)sin(pi T)/pi, Log G(T)=log[sin(pi T)/pi]+pi*i T. (2.1) For every compact K in the complex a-plane and every delta>0, there is C_(K,delta) such that, for all sufficiently large N, sup_(a in K, delta<=j/N<=1-delta) |N^a V_(N,j)(a)-Phi_a(j/N)| <=C_(K,delta) log N/N, (2.2) Phi_a(T)=G(T)^(-a)/Gamma(1-a). (2.3) The convergence is absolute and locally uniform in complex a. It includes every positive integer a, where the limiting function vanishes. It is not a relative-error assertion at those zeros. In particular if j_N/N->T in (0,1), then N^a V_(N,j_N)->Phi_a(T) locally uniformly in a. ### 2.1 An elementary Euler-product lemma, including zeros For b in a fixed complex compact set and j sufficiently large, E_j(b)=j^b product_(r=1)^j(1-b/r) =1/Gamma(1-b)+O(1/j), (2.4) uniformly and absolutely. One direct proof uses (1-b/r)exp(b/r)=1+O_K(r^(-2)). For r beyond a fixed compact-dependent threshold choose the logarithm near one. Its tails sum uniformly to O(1/j). Also sum_(r<=j)1/r-log j=gamma+O(1/j). Therefore E_j converges at the stated rate to the entire Euler product exp(-gamma b)product_(r>=1)(1-b/r)exp(b/r). (2.5) The finitely many possible zero factors are kept as factors, so this proof remains valid at positive integers. For completeness (2.5) is the reciprocal of the Euler Gamma function, not an imported asymptotic formula. For Re b<1 repeated integration by parts gives I_j(b)=integral_0^1 t^(-b)(1-t)^j dt =1/[(j+1-b)product_(r<=j)(1-b/r)]. After u=jt, dominated convergence gives j^(1-b)I_j(b)->integral_0^infinity u^(-b)exp(-u)du=Gamma(1-b). Near zero use a fixed integrable power on each compact subset of Re b<1; away from zero use (1-u/j)^j<=exp(-u). Thus the entire product (2.5) agrees with 1/Gamma(1-b) on that half-plane and defines its entire continuation. This proves (2.4) independently of a Gamma-ratio or Stirling theorem. ### 2.2 The nonzero J product has a uniform logarithm For T=j/N in the stated interval, all Hr and H(r-b) stay in a fixed zero-free neighborhood of the segment c[0,1-delta] once N is large. Choose L(x)=Log J(x), L(0)=0. Its first two derivatives are bounded there. Taylor expansion with its uniform remainder and a Riemann sum give sum_(r<=j)[L(H(r-b))-L(Hr)] =-Hb sum_(r<=j)L'(Hr)+O(1/N) =-b L(Hj)+O(1/N) =-a L(cT)+O(1/N). (2.6) The Riemann sum can be integrated along the straight complex segment from zero to Hj; the same derivative bound gives its O(1/N) error. Exponentiating proves that the J product is J(cT)^(-a)(1+O(1/N)), uniformly on K and the indicated interval. Finally b=a+O_K(1/N), N^a j^(-b)=T^(-a)[1+O_K(log N/N)], exp(-Hbj/2)=exp(-caT/2) exactly. Combining these identities, (2.4) and (2.6) proves (2.2), since T J(cT)exp(cT/2)=G(T). The proof never divides by Gamma^-1 near a resonance zero. ## 3. The profile retains the entire normal resonance data For fixed T, Phi_a(T) is entire in a. The finite normalized functions in (2.2) are holomorphic too. Cauchy's formula therefore gives convergence of every fixed a-derivative on smaller compact sets. This packages the large root-normal jets in one whole function, rather than assuming a finite jet controls the source. The exact numerator zeros are at b=r, equivalently a=N r/(N-r), 1<=r<=j. (3.1) They approach the positive-integer zeros of (2.3), but they are not located exactly at those integers at finite N. At a=-k, k>=0, the profile is instead Phi_(-k)(T)=G(T)^k/k!, V_(N,j)(-k)~N^k G(T)^k/k!. (3.2) This is a polynomial source scale in N. No complete knot-growth assumption appears in either (3.1) or (3.2). As a check on the known exact first normal, partial_a Log V_(N,j)|_(a=0) =-log N-Log G(T)-gamma+o(1). (3.3) Since q partial_q=(2N^2/c)partial_a in this normal, (3.3) agrees with the exact cotangent sum of the clock-shear audit. The N^2 log N term is real source data, resolved by (2.3). ## 4. The actual meridian Weyl half-adapter has the opposite profile Keep the actual fixed root Q_N=exp(c/N), and put M(a)=exp(ca/(2N)). The already specified rational half-adapter is, with its even-level mark i retained, beta_N(M)=(M^2Q_N;Q_N)_L/(Q_N;Q_N)_L, N odd, beta_N(M)=[(1+iM)/(1+i)] (M^2Q_N;Q_N)_L/(Q_N;Q_N)_L, N even, L=(N-1)/2 odd, L=N/2-1 even. (4.1) It is not a newly normalized scalar: beta_N(1)=1 and the actual Weyl norm identity fixes it as in the cited gluing theorem. For each factor there is the exact identity (1-exp[H_0(r+a)])/(1-exp(H_0r)) =exp(H_0a/2)(1+a/r) J(H_0(r+a))/J(H_0r), H_0=c/N. (4.2) Apply the same proof as Section 2 with b=-a, now without the a_N drift. The even prefactor in (4.1) is 1+O_K(1/N). Thus, uniformly on every compact complex a-set, including its zeros, N^(-a) beta_N(exp(ca/(2N))) =G(1/2)^a/Gamma(1+a)+O_K(1/N) =Phi_(-a)(1/2)+O_K(1/N). (4.3) The same whole Gamma half-profile is therefore derived separately from an actual q-normal frame and an actual fixed-root meridian source adapter. No logarithm of a vanishing factor is used. ## 5. An exact finite scalar source bridge aligns their zeros There is a stronger comparison before taking any limit. Let H,b be as in (1.2), choose L as in (4.1), and put M_tilde=exp(-H_0 b/2). Define the explicit unit u_N(a)=exp[-(H-H_0)bL/2] product_(r=1)^L J(H(r-b))J(H_0r)/[J(Hr)J(H_0(r-b))], (5.1) and at even N divide its right-hand side by (1+iM_tilde)/(1+i). Then exactly V_(N,L)(a)=u_N(a) beta_N(M_tilde). (5.2) All J factors in (5.1) are units on fixed compact a-sets for sufficiently large N: their arguments remain near c[0,1/2], which misses the first nonzero J zero. The even prefactor is a unit near M=1. In particular (5.2) is valid through integer resonances; it was not defined by dividing its two vanishing sides. It has u_N(0)=1 and u_N=1+O_K(1/N) (5.3) locally uniformly and holomorphically. Proof: in (1.4), take j=L. The corresponding beta product has the exact factorization exp(-H_0bL/2)product_(r<=L)(1-b/r) J(H_0(r-b))/J(H_0r), times the even prefactor if appropriate. The zero polynomial product cancels as a common factor of the two expressions; what remains is precisely (5.1). For (5.3), H-H_0=O_K(N^-2). The exponent in (5.1) is O(1/N). The logarithm of each J cross ratio is also O_K(N^-2), by differentiating the bounded smooth difference L(H(r-b))-L(Hr) with respect to H. Summing L terms is O(1/N). The even prefactor differs from one by O(1/N). The reparametrization b=a_N is essential. Comparing directly to beta_N(exp(-H_0a/2)) would put its zeros at a=r, while the q-normal frame zeros are (3.1). A claimed uniform unit ratio without that adjustment would be false near integer zeros. This is an exact holomorphic scalar source-line comparison with its origin mark, phase, zeros and unit all specified. It is not an intertwiner of the full q-normal and meridian-normal knot states, their quantum clocks, or their selected regular parts. The [full-head source theorem](full_head_gamma_source_transport.md) extends this comparison to every color by using the complementary actual Weyl chart in the upper half. Its comparison unit is uniformly I+O(1/N) in any common diagonal metric, including the resonance divisors. Its source and dual fractional lattices are retained; the potentially singular source factors themselves are not declared units. The same coordinate also matches the retained central power, with the meridian reflection explicit. On the integral-color leg M_col=exp(Hb/2), while M_tilde=exp(-H_0b/2). Therefore chi_H(M_col)=exp[-2c Log(M_col)/H] =exp(-cb)=M_tilde^(2N). (5.4) Here chi_H is the geometric whole flux character of [the Gauss-wall calculation](gauss_wall_flux_and_actual_peripheral_character.md). The target inverse-power character is its reciprocal, as required by the opposite meridian orientation. Equation (5.4) matches specified scalar characters; it does not assert that this geometric lift is an unspecified off-root auxiliary-matrix center. ## 6. Opposite profiles give the exact universal meridian function The actual finite Weyl scalar is c_N(M)=N M^(N-1)/S_N(M^2), beta_N(M)beta_N(M^(-1))=c_N(M)^(-1). (6.1) At M=exp(z/(2N)), the exact centered inverse norm is H_N(z)=c_N(M)^(-1) =sinh(z/2)/[N sinh(z/(2N))]. (6.2) It has its removable entire values at the apparent common zeros. On each fixed compact z-set it tends uniformly, with O(N^-2) error, to H(z)=2sinh(z/2)/z. Multiplying the two limits in (4.3) therefore proves independently Phi_a(T)Phi_(-a)(T) =1/[Gamma(1-a)Gamma(1+a)] =sin(pi a)/(pi a) =H(ca), (6.3) for every T in (0,1), with entire continuation at all a. The T factors cancel. In particular the actual c_N tends meromorphically to Gamma(1-a)Gamma(1+a), locally uniformly away from its poles. Its inverse and the beta norm converge to the entire H. This orientation is retained. For completeness the finite norm input to this reflection identity does not require a published proof. At odd N pair residues r and N-r in the beta factors; their numerator is the full product (M^2Q;Q)_(N-1)=S_N(M^2), and their denominator is N with the displayed phase. The leftover M power is M^(-(N-1)), giving (6.1). At even N the unpaired residue is Q^(N/2)=-1; its factor is supplied exactly by (1+iM)(1+i/M)/(1+i)^2=(1+M^2)/(2M). The same product argument gives (6.1). These are the actual marked finite identities already audited in the gluing construction. The entire difference identities are G(T)Phi_(a+1)(T)=-a Phi_a(T), (a+1)H(c(a+1))=-a H(ca). (6.4) They follow from the Gamma recurrence and hold even at their zeros; ratio notation would exclude those points. These rank-one shifts agree with the retained inverse meridian-norm half-step character. The half-adapter with a->-a has shift factor G(T)/(a+1). The [centered regular-profile theorem](scaled_meridian_regular_profile.md) keeps H_N and the whole knot-dependent regular part separately. Equality of the universal factor (6.3) does not identify that regular part or prove a growth or convergence theorem for it. The subsequent [full-head source transport](full_head_gamma_source_transport.md) extends the finite comparison to every head index, using the actual Weyl complement in the upper half. The interior profile here is unchanged; a naive upper prefix would introduce different zero divisors and is not that source extension. ## 7. Coverage and precise novelty A repository search found earlier factorial-frame periods and normal jets, but no existing derivation of (2.2), (4.3), or the zero-preserving actual comparison (5.2). The Gamma reflection factor itself is classical, not a new identity. For background coverage, [Iritani's survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.15938) uses it in Gamma-class factorizations and integral flat-section structures. That coverage is not used as a proof or as an identification of this knot source with quantum cohomology. The contribution here is the independent whole-function derivation from the actual retained q-binomial residual, its uniformity through the shifted integer resonances, and its exact marked unit comparison to the already fixed actual meridian half-adapter. These statements do not assume the volume conjecture or any K_N growth hypothesis. The [audit](../experiments/audit_whole_gamma_frame_profile.py) checks finite hyperbolic factorizations, zero alignment, the exact unit, both parities of the actual beta norm, uniform compact profiles and the paired entire function. The [independent normal-profile audit](gamma_residual_normal_profile_independent_audit.md) also checks the whole zero-preserving unit and its uniform bound.

title: A whole actual high-color Ward contraction by grid flow
text: # A whole actual high-color Ward contraction by grid flow Research theorem, 27 October 2026. Four ACTUAL integral quantum-group words give a pole-free contraction of the full high-color matrix Ward complex onto its scalar line. The construction uses two diagonal spectra and a connected grid of nonvanishing ordinary and divided arrows. Every denominator is a unit at the marked root; no power of 1-Q^N is inverted. The original cut source has an explicit whole cochain homotopy to normalized trace, including the formerly resonant Frobenius corner. The result is a finite actual source/current contraction. It does not identify a partial geometric Gaussian module with this matrix complex, and does not identify low-color and high-color normal jets. Whole source units and the frozen pivotal cap correction remain part of any such comparison. ## 1. Four actual words and the whole coefficient ring Fix N>=2, r>=1, D=N(r+1), m=D-1. Use the ACTUAL integral Weyl color D_m(q) in the constant sign basis w_(R,S), 0<=R<=r, 0<=S<N, of [the high-color construction](high_integral_color_frobenius_wall_source.md). The integer position is j=NR+S. Write K=q^m Q^(-J), Q=q^2, F=the original ordinary lowering generator, L=F^(N)=F^N/[N]_q!, H=tau [E^(N),F^(N)], tau=(-1)^(Nr-1). (1.1) The divided matrices in (1.1) are their regular integral Gaussian matrices, not singular quotients specialized separately. All four are actual U_q words. In particular their coproducts retain the mixed ordinary/divided terms; neither H nor L is declared to have a primitive tensor coproduct. K is diagonal with entries k_(R,S)=q^(m-2NR-2S). Both divided matrices preserve S and shift R by one, so H is diagonal for ALL q; denote its entries by h_(R,S)(q). At the marked root q_N=exp(pi i/N), Q_N=q_N^2, K_0=q_N^m I_Fr tensor diag(Q_N^(-S)), H_0=diag(r-2R) tensor I_head, F_0=I_Fr tensor F_St, L_0=f_r tensor I_head, (1.2) where F_St has entries [S+1]_(q_N), and (f_r)_(R+1,R)=R+1. The sign basis is the actual one proving (1.2); no additional q-factorial head gauge is needed. Work in the rational local coefficient ring at q_N, enlarged only by the original source units and the following finitely many units: * k_(R,S)-k_(T,U) for S!=U; * h_(R,S)-h_(T,S) for R!=T; * the selected nonwrap F arrows and L arrows below. Their root values are respectively q_N^m(Q_N^(-S)-Q_N^(-U)), 2(T-R), [S+1]_(q_N), R+1, all nonzero. Thus this is a whole rational localization before normal completion. The wall delta=1-Q^N is never inverted. ## 2. Off-diagonal recovery separates the two actual spectra For a four-tuple of matrices X=(X_K,X_H,X_F,X_L), define O(X) to have zero diagonal and O(X)_(R,S;T,U)= (X_K)_(R,S;T,U)/(k_(R,S)-k_(T,U)), S!=U, (X_H)_(R,S;T,S)/(h_(R,S)-h_(T,S)), R!=T. (2.1) The two cases are disjoint. Consequently, for every matrix C, O([K,C],[H,C],0,0)=C_off. (2.2) The K row resolves every different head residue. The H row resolves the repeated K eigenvalues between different Fr blocks, including the extreme corner (r,0). Its root gap there is -2r. This is the whole full-grid extension of [the actual wall unit](actual_divided_ward_closure_and_green_caps.md). ## 3. Diagonal recovery is an explicit finite tree flow Choose the comb tree rooted at (0,0). It consists of every horizontal nonwrap edge (R,S)->(R,S+1), 0<=R<=r, 0<=S<N-1, and the vertical trunk (R,0)->(R+1,0), 0<=R<r. There are D-1 edges and every vertex has a unique root path. For a horizontal edge e:u->v put a_e(q)=F_(v,u); for a vertical edge put a_e(q)=L_(v,u). These are exactly the actual units of Section 1. Define the current gradient d_e(X)=(X_F)_(v,u)/a_e on horizontal edges, d_e(X)=(X_L)_(v,u)/a_e on vertical edges. (3.1) Both F and L have one possible incoming and outgoing arrow at each vertex in their respective direction. Hence, even if C has off-diagonal entries, d_e([K,C],[H,C],[F,C],[L,C])=C_(u,u)-C_(v,v). (3.2) No off-diagonal subtraction is needed in this four-row version. For an edge e let T_e be its child subtree and n_e its number of vertices. Let Q_e be the diagonal matrix (Q_e)_(v,v)=n_e/D-1_(v in T_e). It has trace zero. The explicit tree-flow primitive is G(X)=sum_e d_e(X) Q_e. (3.3) Indeed, if b_v=-sum_(e on root->v) d_e, then G_v=b_v-D^(-1)sum_w b_w. Applying (3.2) yields G(delta C)=C_diag-(Tr C/D)I. (3.4) For this comb, a horizontal edge (R,S)->(R,S+1) has subtree {(R,U):U>S}, so n_e=N-1-S. A vertical trunk edge (R,0)->(R+1,0) has every row T>R as its subtree, so n_e=N(r-R). Thus (3.3) is a fully specified finite formula. ## 4. The actual Ward complex has a strong whole contraction Define delta C=([K,C],[H,C],[F,C],[L,C]), p(C)=Tr C/D, i(c)=cI, h(X)=O(X)+G(X). (4.1) Equations (2.2) and (3.4) prove the exact WHOLE identity h delta=I-i p, p h=0, delta i=0, p i=1. (4.2) In particular the common Ward kernel is precisely the scalar line, without invoking Schur irreducibility. Define the degree-one term of the Ward complex to be the ACTUAL image W^0=End(D_m), W^1=im(delta). Then delta h=I on W^1, so (i,p,h) is a strong contraction onto the scalar line in degree zero. The image is a direct summand of the unrestricted four-row space, since delta h is its explicit idempotent projector. No claim is made that the unrestricted codomain End(D_m)^4 has zero cokernel. Every map is rational and regular at q_N. The same identities hold after arbitrary finite normal truncation or formal completion, with all Leibniz convolutions retained. Unlike inversion of a root memory-Cartan gap, (4.2) is not obtained by inverting delta. ## 5. The original cut is attached by its exact source row Let Phi_A(C)=Tr(A(q)C) be ANY specified whole actual cut coupon. Put rho(q)=Phi_A(I)=Tr A. Applying it to (4.2) gives Phi_A-rho p=b_A delta, b_A(X)=Phi_A(h(X)). (5.1) This retains the original source, dual and every normalization unit exactly. For an actually normalized coupon, rho=1; if its raw source uses a normalization unit, that unit is retained in A, not inferred from its root value. In entries the degree-one row is b_A(X)=sum_(S!=U,R,T) A_(T,U;R,S) (X_K)_(R,S;T,U) /(k_(R,S)-k_(T,U)) +sum_(R!=T,S) A_(T,S;R,S) (X_H)_(R,S;T,S) /(h_(R,S)-h_(T,S)) +sum_e Tr(A Q_e) d_e(X). (5.2) In particular this applies to the original correlated coupon e_D, whose root source is the literal selected sum over (R,S)=(R,R mod N) and whose row has coefficients 2^(-N) binom(N,R), for r=N. The diagonal alias at R=0,N and its old endpoint normalization remain part of A. The root wall has original value 2^(-N), not the uniform interval value 1/(N+1). Equation (5.1) makes their difference an ACTUAL Ward boundary using H, rather than incorrectly declaring it a boundary in the smaller resonant memory-Borel complex. The original root row can be made still more explicit. Write p_R=2^(-N)binom(N,R), S_R=R mod N. Its only two distinct selected vertices having the SAME head residue are (0,0) and (N,0). Therefore its H-row part in (5.2) is exactly 2^(-N)/(2N) * [(X_H)_(0,0;N,0) -(X_H)_(N,0;0,0)]. (5.3) This is the original wall weight, with its original sign, rather than an interval-average substitute. The diagonal-flow coefficient Tr(e_D Q_e) is also explicit. On the horizontal edge in row R after S it is (N-1-S)/D-p_R 1_(S_R>S), and on the vertical trunk edge after R it is (N-R)/(N+1)-sum_(T>R)p_T. (5.4) The whole formulas remain (5.1)--(5.2) with the actual supplied source entries and their normalization units; (5.3)--(5.4) only display their root values, not a chosen off-root extension. If the network is expressed in the controlled Fourier/source frame, conjugate all four actual words, all rows, h, and A by that same whole matrix. Equation (5.1) is preserved. Conjugating the coupon alone and keeping the old current operators would be a different source problem. The ordinary pivotal cap transports the actual Hopf-adjoint rows with their full divided coproducts. A commutator row is converted by [rho(h),C]=sum_(h) D_(h_1)(C)rho(h_2). Thus [the all-word current/cap formulas](actual_divided_ward_closure_and_green_caps.md) give an explicit global endpoint for each actual word in (4.1). For the frozen ADO cap retain its whole adapter chi^(-1)ptr_K M_(Z^J) and its recorded defect rows. This grid contraction does not make those Green or cap endpoints zero. ## 6. A polynomial root bound in the actual hybrid metric Use the root positive metric ||w_(R,S)||^2=binom(r,R) with the ordinary integral head basis orthonormal. Give End the induced Hilbert--Schmidt norm, and the four-row domain the orthogonal product norm. This is an explicitly stated root metric, not a bound on an unretained q-factorial change of basis. K is unitary at the root. Its inverse-gap norm in (2.1) is at most 1/[2 sin(pi/N)] <= N/4. The H inverse-gap norm is at most 1/2. The two off-diagonal pieces occupy disjoint supports. For a horizontal tree edge the metric-normalized actual arrow has size [S+1]_(q_N)>=1. For a vertical edge its size is sqrt((R+1)(r-R))>=sqrt(r)>=1. Hence the Euclidean norm of the selected gradient vector is bounded by the combined Hilbert--Schmidt norms of X_F and X_L. Before centering, the root-path integration matrix has one entry -1 for each edge on a vertex path. Its squared Frobenius norm is sum_(R=0)^r sum_(S=0)^(N-1)(R+S) =D(r+N-1)/2. Centering is an orthogonal projection. Since the off-diagonal and diagonal outputs are orthogonal, this gives, for example, ||h_0|| <= max(1/[2 sin(pi/N)], 1/2, sqrt(D(r+N-1)/2)). (6.1) For r=N the bound is O(N^(3/2)). It is uniform in the word length because h is a cut contraction, not a product of crossing norms. There is no claim of an N-independent complex neighborhood on which every whole rational unit has this root bound. The ORIGINAL root correlated coupon e_D is an orthogonal rank-one projector in this hybrid metric: its selected source has squared norm sum_R binom(N,R)=2^N, and its original dual is that metric dual divided by 2^N. Consequently its functional norm is one. Equation (5.1) therefore gives ||b_(e_D),0|| <= ||h_0||, (6.2) a polynomial source-homotopy bound, INCLUDING the old memory wall. The full external modified-dimension line multiplies both sides and is never suppressed. A source comparison through some other nonunitary whole gauge requires its own norm adapter; the present bound concerns the specified actual hybrid frame. The ORIGINAL controlled root head-shift/Fourier matrix with its literal 1/N normalization is a scalar N^(-1/2) times a unitary map. Its conjugation is therefore isometric, so simultaneous transport of operators, current maps and coupon preserves this bound. ## 7. Two actual words suffice, with an explicit row correction There is also a shorter whole presentation. Put A=H+K/2, B=F+L. At the root A has simple full-grid spectrum. If R!=T then |Delta H+Delta K/2|>=2|R-T|-1>=1. If R=T and S!=U the gap is |Q_N^(-S)-Q_N^(-U)|/2>=sin(pi/N). Hence every off-diagonal A gap is a whole unit. Recover C_off entrywise from [A,C]. Next subtract Z=[B,C]-[B,C_off]=[B,C_diag]. The N-step and one-step arrows in B occupy distinct positions for N>=2. Read the same comb-edge gradients from Z and apply (3.3). This gives an explicit two-row contraction with the SAME scalar trace projection. Its off-diagonal subtraction is essential; simply reading a tree edge of [B,C] can include other entries of C. The four-row form has the cleaner bound and source formulas above. Both presentations use actual integral U_q words. They supply a whole finite Ward target and its original co-source homotopy; a nonzero map from the sourced geometric current complex into this target is still the necessary geometric comparison. Exact audits: [script](../experiments/audit_whole_high_color_ward_grid.py) and [results](../experiments/whole_high_color_ward_grid_results.json). The proof has a separate [independent audit](high_color_wall_source_independent_audit.md).

title: Whole algebraic comparisons and their cyclotomic jets
text: # Whole algebraic comparisons and their cyclotomic jets Research note, 27 October 2026. This follows the user's proposal that Rivin's optimizer and quantum restrictions should be treated as parts of a whole period object. It proves a finite reconstruction theorem for algebraic comparison maps, including a quantum-normal direction which the earlier root-only source base does not record. The argument is exponent separation, Vandermonde inversion and a finite-algebra norm. No published rigidity or arithmetic module theorem is assumed. This does not construct the missing comparison of the actual selected Kashaev period with the geometric regulator period. The volume conjecture remains unproved. In particular, the theorem below requires a fixed algebraic presentation or a bounded space of possible maps; it does not assert algebraicity of a quantum period from its classical saddle. ## 1. What is algebraic about the Rivin optimum Let X be the nondegenerate gluing variety of a positive complete ideal triangulation, with shapes z_j, marked meridian M and longitude L. Its equations are monomial equations in z_j and 1-z_j, with integer exponents and the recorded peripheral signs. They define an algebraic variety over Q after inverting the shape denominators. Use the normalized geometric component, with its selected complete lift. The [positive rigidity proof](geometric_rigidity_and_cyclic_source.md) shows that its marked-meridian Jacobian is invertible at the complete geometric point. Consequently: * the complete shapes are algebraic numbers; * the local shape branch is algebraic over Q(M), and hence over the function field of its marked A-curve; * after shrinking a suitable algebraic neighborhood and retaining the chosen place, the branch is an etale algebraic germ over M; * every nilpotent thickening of that chosen place has a unique shape lift once its meridian lift is specified. The last assertion follows directly by Newton lifting.
