At each square- zero extension the correction is the unique solution of J delta z=-r, where J is the invertible gluing Jacobian and r is the residual. Repeating this through powers of the nilpotent ideal proves existence and uniqueness, with no convergence assertion needed. The [Rivin calculation](rivin_flow_and_quantum_source.md) independently proves strict concavity and stationarity at this geometric point. Thus positivity selects the same branch among the algebraic solutions. At the complete lift M=+1 or -1; the specified longitude sign and fundamental-class mark are still retained. M and L are not independent parameters on this curve. These statements concern shapes. Their arguments, logarithms and dilogarithm periods are not thereby algebraic functions. For example, the algebraic Gaussian coefficient and the action exp(S/h) are distinct parts of the period. The already marked action has Im S_complete=Vol(X)/2, h_N=pi*i/N. This gives log|exp(S_complete/h_N)|=N Vol(X)/(2pi). Establishing its contribution to the actual selected finite period is the remaining quantum assertion. For coverage, [Futer--Gueritaud, 1004.0440](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.0440) describes the Casson--Rivin angle polytope and its critical-point criterion. Our rigidity and concavity proofs are in the linked notes. ## 2. Retain both power coordinates before taking quantum jets Work over any characteristic-zero coefficient field k. Put B=Spec k[t,t^(-1),q^(+/-1),M^(+/-1),v^(+/-1),w^(+/-1)]. Here t=1/N on the N-th restriction, and the power graphs are Gamma_N: t=1/N, v=q^N, w=M^N. (2.1) The actual cyclotomic point on this graph is q=q_N=exp(pi*i/N), M=1, v=-1, w=1. (2.2) The other meridian lift is handled in the same way. The finite phase cover of [the source base](uniform_frobenius_source_base.md) can be retained component by component, using levels in its specified residue class modulo four. None of its phases is reset here. The exact meridian shift on B is sigma(q)=q, sigma(M)=qM, sigma(v)=v, sigma(w)=vw, sigma(t)=t. (2.3) It preserves every Gamma_N. The two relative logarithmic derivatives which preserve these graphs are D_q=q partial_q+t^(-1)v partial_v, D_M=M partial_M+t^(-1)w partial_w. (2.4) They commute and satisfy the exact identities D_M sigma=sigma D_M, D_q sigma=sigma(D_q+D_M). (2.5) These follow by checking the five coordinate generators and extending by the product rule. Their pullbacks to Gamma_N are exactly q d/dq and M d/dM. Equivalently, the power coordinates are marked horizontal sections of the algebraic relative equations t dlog v=dlog q, t dlog w=dlog M, (2.6) with t fixed. Equations (2.6) specify a connection; their horizontal sections need not be rational functions for nonintegral 1/t. Setting v=-1 recovers the earlier root-only action w->-w. That closed slice is not preserved by D_q: D_q(v+1)=-1/t on it. In particular, replacing q^N by -1 before differentiating destroys quantum-normal information. The root values of v+1 are zero at every level, while their first quantum derivatives are -N. This is a refinement of the old source base, not an assertion that an N-dimensional cyclic Weyl representation extends off its root. The actual whole q-germs must still be supplied by the specified color/quantum-period construction. ## 3. Finite cyclotomic jets detect a whole bounded presentation Write a Laurent polynomial on B in the form P=sum_(a,b,c,d) p_(a,b,c,d)(t) q^a v^b M^c w^d, deg_t p_(a,b,c,d)<=D. (3.1) A Laurent power of t can be cleared first. Let S be the number of distinct pairs (a,b), R the number of distinct pairs (c,d), A the span of the a exponents, and C the span of the c exponents. These are bounds of the fixed presentation, independent of N. **Finite reconstruction theorem.** Choose D+1 distinct positive integers N>max(A,C). At each chosen N, suppose (D_q^i D_M^j P)(1/N,q_N,1,-1,1)=0 for 0<=i<S, 0<=j<R. (3.2) Then P=0 on B. The same conclusion holds if these jets vanish for infinitely many sufficiently large N. The number of derivatives is independent of N. No lower bound on the algebraic degree of q_N is needed, and k need not be a number field. **Proof.** On Gamma_N the exponents are lambda_(a,b)=a+Nb, mu_(c,d)=c+Nd. The lambda values are pairwise distinct when N>A: equality with b!=b' would give N<=|a-a'|. The same argument separates the mu values when N>C. Fill missing pairs with zero coefficients and form the S by R matrix A_N of coefficients p_(a,b,c,d)(1/N). Let V_lambda and V_mu be the Vandermonde matrices with rows indexed by derivative order, and put W=diag(q_N^lambda). The rectangular jet matrix in (3.2) is exactly J_N=V_lambda W A_N V_mu^t. (3.3) All three outer factors are invertible: characteristic is zero, the exponent lists are distinct, and q_N!=0. Hence J_N=0 implies A_N=0. Every p coefficient vanishes at D+1 distinct values 1/N; its degree bound makes it identically zero. This proves the theorem. If the full meridian family rather than its M=1 jets is known, its distinct M exponents can be compared directly; the R meridian jets are then unnecessary. Sparse supports can also reduce the rectangular test, but (3.2) gives a simple uniform sufficient bound. The theorem applies to rational residuals by clearing their fixed denominators. At a pole one must specify the regularized whole map and lattice before testing, rather than separately evaluating a vanishing numerator and denominator. Increasing the allowable support increases the required jet bound. For example (v+1)^s defeats all quantum jets of order less than s, and a polynomial in t vanishing at the tested levels defeats an insufficient number of level tests. The same proof handles any fixed number of power coordinates, including q^(N^2) from Gaussian phases. Write v_j=q^(N^j), w_j=M^(N^j), and use D_q(v_j)=t^(-j)v_j, D_M(w_j)=t^(-j)w_j. Exponents are now fixed-degree integer polynomials in N. Distinct such polynomials have distinct values for all sufficiently large N. The same two Vandermonde matrices and interpolation in t apply, with a fixed bound on the excluded levels. This retains a whole chosen phase lift; a phase's values at the roots alone do not determine its quantum-normal derivatives. ## 4. The same detection works on a fixed algebraic shape cover Let A be a finite free integral algebra over a localization of the coordinate ring of B, with fraction field K. A fixed algebraic shape branch is of this form after suitable localization. Consider a regular element f of A. At each tested cyclotomic point, choose an etale place, so it lifts uniquely to its two-variable formal q,M neighborhood, as in Section 1. Take the norm n(f), the determinant of multiplication by f on A. It has a fixed rational presentation on B. If the chosen lift of f vanishes in the rectangular jet ring, then the same is true of n(f). Indeed that etale place splits off a rank-one factor after formal base change, and multiplication determinants factor as n(f)=f_selected * det(m_f on the complementary factor). The complementary determinant is regular. Apply Section 3 with support and degree bounds of the cleared norm. It follows that n(f)=0 identically. Since K is a field, the norm of a nonzero element cannot be zero, and hence f=0. For a finite algebra with several integral components, apply this argument on the marked component; one selected component does not test all the others. A rational f must first have its poles cleared in the prescribed lattice. A finite number of shifted algebraic expressions can be treated in their finite compositum. We do not assume that the classical shape cover itself admits a finite algebraic lift of every q-shift. Thus algebraic shape coefficients do not require an independent unbounded list of Taylor coefficients. Nilpotent restrictions are faithful tests of a fixed whole comparison once its presentation and chosen algebraic place have been supplied. ## 5. Consequence for a pointed quantum comparison Suppose two specified finite-rank quantum objects have algebraic coefficient matrices, with their actual sources, cuts and integral lattices. Suppose a proposed comparison C and proposed inverse E are given on a fixed algebraic presentation. The intertwining, inverse, source and cut identities have residuals such as C B_1-B_2 sigma(C), CE-I, EC-I, C s_1-s_2, ell_2 C-ell_1. (5.1) If differential period connections are part of the specified objects, their residuals must also be checked: D_i C+C Omega_(1,i)-Omega_(2,i) C, i=q,M. (5.2) The maps C and E must be regular as maps of the prescribed lattices on their marked charts. This condition retains the peripheral zero and pole factors; it is not inferred from nonzero fiber values. Each cleared residual in (5.1)--(5.2) has a fixed algebraic norm. The finite jet test with the resulting bounds therefore proves all these identities for the whole objects. This is a finite certificate criterion for an already constructed comparison, not an existence theorem for C or E. In particular, equality of all fixed-root connection restrictions would not test a term proportional to dq. The quantum-normal jets and D_q in (5.2) are what test that direction. A classical optimizer, or a levelwise Hilbert-90 trivialization without bounded presentation, does not supply (5.1)--(5.2). ### A bounded family of jet intertwiners also proves generic existence There is an existence consequence which does not require proposing C in advance. It has a substantial uniformity hypothesis, stated here. Let F=k(q,t,v), and fix a finite-dimensional F-space of matrix functions of M,w, with a fixed Laurent support and denominator. Use this as the space of possible comparisons. The matrix entries of the two objects, their sources and cuts have fixed algebraic presentations. Include the meridian differential equation if it is specified and its unknown coefficients are constant for D_M. For rational coefficient objects, expanding the difference, source, cut and meridian identities in this fixed space gives a finite affine linear system H(q,t,v) u=b(q,t,v). (5.3) All unknown coefficients u are in F; sigma fixes F. For algebraic coefficient objects, a system of the form (5.3) is an additional descent requirement: testing one algebraic place alone does not imply coefficientwise equality in a generic algebraic basis. The theorem here assumes the displayed finite system and jet solutions to it. Clear the fixed denominators of (5.3). The assertion concerns regular charts of the prescribed lattices, so the candidate map denominators are units on the test germs. Other boundary factors need their stated lattice charts first. Let r be the generic rank of H. Take bounds for the t degrees and q,v supports of every r-minor of H and every (r+1)-minor of [H|b]. Such bounds are finite and can be obtained before choosing a comparison. Use D+1 levels for their t-degree bound and B quantum jets for their support bound as in Section 3. Use enough meridian jets to recover the coefficients in (5.3). **Bounded-comparison existence theorem.** Suppose at all these levels there are solutions in the fixed comparison space to order B in the quantum parameter, satisfying the pointing identities to that order. Suppose their leading matrices are invertible as rational meridian matrices. Then there is a generically invertible comparison in that space over F satisfying all of (5.3) exactly. Here order B means equality modulo epsilon^B, where q=q_N(1+epsilon), v=-(1+epsilon)^N. B is the number of jets, so the orders tested are 0 through B-1. It is enough to take B at least the largest number of distinct q,v exponent pairs in the stated minors. The size of the bound depends on the fixed comparison space, not on N. Maps at different levels need not be interpolated or assumed coherent beforehand. **Proof.** A jet solution makes every (r+1)-minor of [H|b] vanish modulo epsilon^B. Indeed its last column is a linear combination of the H columns plus a remainder of order B, and every (r+1)-minor of H is identically zero. Section 3, now with no meridian variables, makes these augmented minors identically zero. Therefore (5.3) is generically consistent and has a rational affine family of solutions, computable by Gaussian elimination. Choose a nonzero r-minor Delta of H. At one of the tested levels its whole power-graph pullback is nonzero; otherwise reconstruction would give Delta=0. Its order k at q_N is at most S_Delta-1 by the same sparse Vandermonde argument. In particular k<B. At that level retain the free coordinates of a jet solution and solve the pivot equations exactly over the Laurent-series field in epsilon. The pivot inverse has pole order at most k, so the correction is O(epsilon^(B-k)). It preserves the leading matrix. The exact specialized affine solution family consequently contains an invertible matrix. Its determinant is thus not the zero polynomial in its free parameters. The generic rational affine family has the same property. Since F is infinite, free parameters can be chosen in F outside that determinant's proper zero locus. This gives the claimed invertible rational comparison. For r=0 the same argument first gives b=0; an invertible matrix in the proposed space can be chosen directly. The zero-size pivot has order zero. This is an existence theorem for the difference/meridian/pointing identities encoded in (5.3). A q-direction period-connection identity contains derivatives of the unknown coefficients and is not an affine algebraic system of this form. It must be established for the constructed comparison by (5.2), or by a separate flatness and uniqueness argument with its hypotheses proved. Nor does generic invertibility prove regularity of C and its inverse on every boundary chart. There is one useful sufficient condition for the q-connection check. Suppose the two supplied period connections and semilinear shifts obey nabla_M T=T nabla_M, nabla_q T=T(nabla_q+nabla_M), (5.4) and their marked sources satisfy nabla_q s_i=0. Suppose s_1 is cyclic for T_1. If C already intertwines T and nabla_M and sends s_1 to s_2, then it automatically intertwines nabla_q. Indeed E=nabla_(q,2) C-C nabla_(q,1) is linear over the coefficient field; (5.4) and the meridian identity give E T_1=T_2 E. Also E s_1=0. Hence E kills every T_1^j s_1, which span the module, and E=0. The same proof works if nabla_q s_i is a specified common expression in T_i,nabla_(M,i),s_i already respected by C. Existence of these connections, their compatibility and this source law are hypotheses; they are not inferred from an A-symbol. The unresolved knot-specific input is a bounded comparison space and its sufficiently deep source-preserving jet intertwiners. Classical etaleness alone does not provide them. If that input is proved, however, generic algebraic existence follows from the finite rank argument above; a comparison matrix need not be guessed from a list of knot examples. The subsequent [divisor-flow descent theorem](cyclotomic_divisor_descent.md) supplies such a bound for a stated rank-one class. If the comparison coefficient has a fixed product of linear factors in known q-shift orbits, equality of its full cyclic norm characters at every large level forces zero divisor charge in each orbit. A finite cumulative flow then constructs one rational generic gauge with an explicit degree bound. No bounds for the separate levelwise gauges are assumed. A second theorem treats moving algebraic zeros and poles under explicit unramified and nonresonance hypotheses, using uniqueness of exponential sequences with meromorphic coefficients. It also records an exact half-root alias counterexample and a direct construction of a nonzero actual annihilator over Q=q^2. Establishing the comparison line's stated hypotheses and norm compatibility remains necessary. ## 6. Relation to the existing work and the volume target The earlier [uniform source base](uniform_frobenius_source_base.md) already proves whole-root-graph Zariski density for fixed rational functions of q,M,M^N and the finite phases. The [all-level period proof](all_level_a_period.md) already uses sparse Vandermonde multiplicity bounds for singular companion steps. The addition here is the simultaneous power-coordinate base for q^N and M^N, its differential/shift compatibility, and the finite reconstruction of whole algebraic maps from both quantum and meridian jets, extended to marked etale shape covers by a norm. The bounded-comparison theorem further gives generic existence from jet solutions in a fixed finite comparison space, by rank minors and a controlled pivot lift, without a precomputed matrix. No novelty claim is made for these elementary algebraic arguments. This supplies a rigorous part of the proposed functions-before-jets approach. The actual missing construction is the whole pointed quantum comparison, with its period marking. Rivin optimization and algebraic gluing supply its geometric place; they do not by themselves algebraize the quantum period or choose its global source. The [central normalization theorem](algebraic_central_normalization.md) already proves that a nonzero factor from a fixed finite algebraic central presentation has log norm O(log N), after whole-germ specialization. Thus a comparison of that type would have controlled normalization. Neither its existence nor the actual period's geometric exponential component is inferred here. The action and the nonzero algebraic principal density are established in the geometric notes; their selected finite-period contribution remains the outstanding theorem. [Exact audit](../experiments/audit_whole_period_rigidity.py). [Results](../experiments/whole_period_rigidity_results.json). Reproduce with: python3 experiments/audit_whole_period_rigidity.py The subsequent [full rank-one proof](full_rank_one_cyclotomic_descent.md) removes the earlier unramified and nonresonance restrictions for rational Q-coefficients. Weighted exponential--Puiseux uniqueness detects all moving divisor orbits, including poles tending to zero or infinity at Q=1. The [additive/unipotent extension](additive_unipotent_cyclotomic_descent.md) then treats source differences and upper triangular rational comparison systems. Its generic gauge is constructed from whole cyclic transport, without a supplied bound for unrelated levelwise gauges. The actual comparison's transport identities and its source/cut lattice remain inputs rather than consequences of classical etaleness. ## 7. Actual clock transport requires functions before finite evaluation There is now an exact instance of this distinction on the ORIGINAL high-color source. Put C_Q=Q^S Z^R, Z=Q^N, with Frobenius index 0<=R<=N. Its actual whole divided matrices e_q,f_q obey e_q C_Q=Z C_Q e_q, f_q C_Q=Z^(-1) C_Q f_q. Their nonzero interior arrows are units at the marked root. Let e_q^dagger,f_q^dagger be their finite inverse arrows, retaining the endpoint projections P_0,P_top. Then e_q^dagger e_q=I-P_0, f_q^dagger f_q=I-P_top. For a retained rational function g whose denominators are invertible at BOTH C_Q and Z C_Q, the endpoint-completed current is exactly [-e_q^dagger[e_q,g(Z C_Q)] +P_0 f_q^dagger[f_q,g(C_Q)]]/(1-Z) =[g(C_Q)-g(Z C_Q)]/(1-Z). (7.1) The proof and original-matrix checks are in [the whole Jackson-current theorem](endpoint_completed_normal_clock_euler_current.md). The quotient is regular at Z=1 and gives C g'(C). The shifted argument in the first commutator is essential. Keeping only g(C_Q) does not specify (7.1): the finite evaluation kernel need not be preserved by g(x)->g(Zx). For example, on one head string set c=Q^s and p_N(x)=product_(R=0)^N(x-c Z^R). Then p_N(C_Q)=0 on that string, whereas p_N(Z C_Q)=c^(N+1) Z^[N(N+1)/2] product_(k=1)^(N+1)(Z^k-1) P_top. (7.2) After division by 1-Z its first nonzero normal order is N. Consequently every fixed normal depth eventually misses this endpoint. The degree of p_N grows with N, so this example respects the FIXED-presentation hypothesis of Section 3. It does not contradict the independent bounded-lattice Mellin uniqueness theorem either. [The function-algebra audit](whole_clock_function_algebra_and_endpoint_extension.md) also proves the general algebraic reason: for generic Z of infinite multiplicative order, the Laurent function algebra has no nonzero proper finite-codimension ideal preserved by x->Zx. Thus a whole function algebra with its relative endpoint data is the appropriate object for this current; a finite functional-calculus quotient loses part of its transport. At the cyclotomic fiber the finite matrix representation remains valid. The same audit supplies an explicit positive construction. Over R=k[[delta]], Z=1-delta, take the monic spectral lattices A_L=R[x,x^(-1)]/product_(r=0)^L(x-cZ^r). They are free of rank L+1, and their whole Jackson maps give an exact primitive sequence 0 -> R*1 -> A_L -> A_(L-1) -> 0. One extra endpoint per current suffices. In their Newton bases the evaluation lattice has exact Smith factors 1,delta,...,delta^L; the root algebra is the confluent (x-c_0)^(L+1) jet algebra. Thus finite ambient matrix evaluation and its integral function lattice carry different root data. This establishes flatness and solvability for this clock complex. The full pointed knot/geometric comparison is a further complex with its own flatness condition. The source has a compatible global [P1/Serre model](global_frobenius_cech_source_and_endpoints.md) and an [actual relative interval](actual_frobenius_relative_endpoint_period.md). Its retained pairing density gives a rational whole comparison of the interval co-source with a normalized uniform row. These are explicit source constructions before taking any normal jets. The full braid coefficient currents and their Gaussian pushforward must still respect them. In particular an abstractly matching Borel action, or agreement of its root two-form, does not supply that last intertwining identity. At the finite cut a further [whole degree-elevation map](degree_elevation_actual_head_ward_map.md) now supplies such a current/co-source comparison for the actual two-row head K/F complex. Its explicit matrix formula and retained whole diagonal gauges preserve the image complex, while an explicit trace homotopy carries the original cut row. The map is linear and not multiplicative; equality of this cut complex does not assert transport of the full ordered crossing network or its geometric relative period.

title: Independent check of the whole-comparison rigidity arguments
text: # Independent check of the whole-comparison rigidity arguments Audit, 27 October 2026. I checked the proofs in [whole-period rigidity](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md) and [cyclotomic divisor descent](cyclotomic_divisor_descent.md), including their stated hypotheses, without importing a published q-curvature theorem. No counterexample to the stated reconstruction, bounded comparison, or divisor-descent theorems was found. ## 1. Finite reconstruction and algebraic norms The rectangular jet identity is correct. After the power substitution, the two exponent lists are a+Nb and c+Nd. The strict bounds on N separate these lists. The two Vandermonde matrices and the diagonal q_N-power matrix are invertible, and interpolation at D+1 distinct values of 1/N kills every coefficient. No number-field degree bound for q_N is needed. The algebraic-norm extension is valid for the stated finite free integral algebra and a regular element. At a selected etale place, one may first extend the residue field to its separable closure; the chosen formal branch then splits off as a rank-one factor. The norm is its product with the regular complementary determinant, so vanishing in a rectangular Artin jet quotient passes to the norm. Nonzero field elements have nonzero norms. This does not extend the argument to arbitrary independently chosen root-level covers. ## 2. Bounded-comparison existence The rank-minor argument is valid for the explicitly supplied affine linear system over F=k(q,t,v). A jet solution kills the augmented minors to the required order. Fixed support and degree bounds then make them zero identically. A nonzero generic-rank minor survives as a whole q-germ at one of the tested levels. Its sparse multiplicity bound makes its inverse's pole order strictly smaller than the jet budget, so exact pivot repair preserves the invertible leading map. This exact specialized solution lies in the specialization of the generic affine solution family: the selected pivot remains nonzero over the Laurent-series field, so the rank has not dropped there. Consequently the generic determinant polynomial is nonzero, and the infinite coefficient field supplies an invertible rational member. For rank zero, the minors force b=0 and the invertible test member shows that the proposed matrix space has a nonzero determinant polynomial. This also proves the stated rank-zero conclusion. The restrictions in the note are material. The finite system must really be coefficientwise; a test at one algebraic place does not by itself prove coefficientwise equality in an algebraic basis. Candidate denominators must be regular units in the chosen test charts. The q-connection equation involves derivatives of unknown coefficients and is not included in the finite affine system. The later cyclic-source lemma correctly supplies a sufficient condition for that additional compatibility. ## 3. Moving algebraic divisors and rational descent The exponential-sequence independence lemma is correct. At the largest modulus and least Laurent order, Cesaro orthogonality of distinct unit-circle phases kills every alleged nonzero leading coefficient. This includes root-of-unity phase ratios because the identity holds at every sufficiently large integer. Under the finite nonresonance condition, the first d power sums separate the limiting-root groups. Padding to d elements with zero then makes Newton identities sufficient even before the group sizes are known equal. All actual germs are units, so the padded zeroes are distinguished and the group sizes agree. Equality of the paired exponentials forces a constant integral logarithmic difference and therefore the claimed q^(2k) ratio. The half-root convention and the derivative formula for k are consistent. The gauge constructed over the splitting field descends rationally. There is also a short alternative justification for that final step. Remove its Y^(k_0) part and normalize the product gauge f_0 at Y=0 to one. For any splitting-field Galois automorphism tau, both f_0 and tau(f_0) have the same sigma-coboundary. Their quotient is a sigma-invariant rational function of Y and hence a coefficient-field constant. Its value at Y=0 is one, so tau(f_0)=f_0. This proves the descent without any additional choice of branch pairings. The explicit half-root alias coefficient is a genuine obstruction to dropping the divisor/parameter hypotheses. Its transport is identity at every selected q_N, while its q=1 value prevents a generic rational coboundary. Thus the printed scope qualifications are necessary and do not merely reflect missing estimates. ## 4. Verification and limit of the audit Both diagnostic scripts were rerun. They verify their claimed exact finite checks; these are validation of formulas, not a replacement for the uniform arguments above. No actual/geometric knot-period comparison, integral-lattice extension at every polar chart, or volume-conjecture proof is established by this audit.

title: The whole selected period: its polar character controls the volume rate
text: # The whole selected period: its polar character controls the volume rate Research theorem and scope audit, 27 October 2026. The user's proposal is to construct the function or torsor first and regard quantum jets as its restrictions. The classical part of that proposal is already proved in [the doubled-phase optimizer](doubled_phase_rivin_optimizer.md) and [whole cyclotomic reconstruction](whole_period_cyclotomic_rigidity.md). This note gives a different sufficient quantum target: a meromorphic connection on the **whole selected period line**, with the correct polar character. Algebraicity of every quantum amplitude is unnecessary for this criterion. Existence of that line for the actual knot period is not asserted here; the general volume conjecture remains unproved. **Applicability audit.** The subsequent [actual atom theorem](unfolded_atom_cyclotomic_divisors_and_two_nome_source.md) proves that neither the original unfolded Ward factorial nor its two-nome completion is an ordinary meromorphic H-line at H=0. Accumulating cyclotomic singularities and exact interior zeros give the obstructions. Thus this sufficient criterion is not an established model for the actual local quantum factors. The usable whole object keeps its difference transports, cyclotomic divisors and independent power/source normal. A completed selected word could still have additional cancellations, but those have not been proved here. ## 1. What the classical optimizer supplies For a positive ideal triangulation at a nondegenerate complete point, the monomial shape equations and peripheral equations are defined over Q, with their sign characters retained. The fixed-meridian shape Jacobian is invertible. Therefore the normalized selected shape germ is algebraic and etale over its meridian germ. Its shapes are algebraic over the function field of the marked geometric A-curve, and the complete shapes are algebraic numbers. Here M and L satisfy A(M,L)=0; they are not two independent deformation parameters. At completeness the specified SL2 meridian lift has M=+1 or -1 and the longitude lift retains its prescribed sign. Strict concavity of the volume on its affine positive angle slice selects this geometric solution. It does not assert that an arbitrary ideal triangulation has a positive interior optimum. The independent arguments, including the nonzero Jacobian, are in the linked notes. For literature coverage of the critical-point formulation, see [Futer--Gueritaud, 1004.0440](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.0440); no proof from that paper is used as a premise here. The algebraic coordinates are the shapes, not their arguments or the dilogarithm value. The latter is a marked regulator period of an algebraic connection. The fundamental-class and peripheral marks fix the additive constant in the action. In the actual q convention used here, h = Log q, h_N = pi*i/N, Im S_geo = Vol(S^3 minus K)/2. (1.1) Consequently the character exp(S_geo/h_N) has precisely the desired volume rate. This character and an ordinary leading Gaussian coefficient are different data. The question is whether the ORIGINAL selected quantum period has this character, with only lower-rate factors remaining. ## 2. A finite polar-character theorem for a whole rank-one line Let L be a rank-one meromorphic connection at h=0. After a specified finite ramification h=s^e, choose a meromorphic frame and write the horizontal scalar equation as dP = omega P, omega = sum_(j=-m)^infinity a_j s^j ds. (2.1) Meromorphic here means a convergent Laurent germ with FINITE polar part. Fix one sector and logarithmic sheet containing the physical ray. Suppose P is a nonzero horizontal section there. Integrating (2.1), exactly rather than asymptotically, gives P(s) = C s^rho exp(B(s) + H(s)), rho = a_(-1), B(s) = sum_(r=1)^(m-1) b_r s^(-r), b_r = -a_(-r-1)/r, (2.2) where C is nonzero and H is holomorphic at zero. If m<2 the sum is empty. These equations follow simply by differentiating the right side. No summation of a divergent formal series is involved. Choose the marked root kappa with kappa^e=pi*i and put s_N = kappa N^(-1/e), s_N^e = h_N. (2.3) Then the exact norm expansion is (2*pi/N) log|P(s_N)| = 2*pi sum_r Re(b_r kappa^(-r)) N^(r/e-1) + O(log N/N). (2.4) Indeed B(s_N) is the finite displayed sum; H(s_N) is bounded; and log|s_N^rho| equals Re(rho) log|s_N| minus the bounded marked argument times Im(rho). The constant C contributes O(1/N). Thus the rate depends only on a finite polar character of the whole connection. In particular: * Terms r<e have zero limiting contribution, even though their exponentials need not be algebraic or polynomially bounded. * The r=e term contributes 2 Im(b_e), since kappa^e=pi*i. * Terms r>e contribute a divergent real power unless their real coefficients on the marked physical ray vanish. Distinct r give distinct powers, so they cannot cancel each other. It follows that the limit equals a specified V if and only if Re(b_r kappa^(-r))=0 for all r>e, 2 Im(b_e)=V, (2.5) with b_e=0 when absent. This is a criterion for the norm on this particular marked ray. It allows higher polar terms which are pure phase there; no uniform assertion on adjacent sectors is inferred. ## 3. The criterion belongs to the line, not to a chosen Taylor frame A fixed nonzero meromorphic frame change P -> g(s)P changes omega by dlog g. Write g=s^nu u(s), where nu is an integer and u is a holomorphic unit. Then dlog g = nu ds/s + dlog u. It has no polar term of order two or higher. Consequently B(s) in (2.2) is unchanged, and the scalar norm changes by O(log N). The criterion is invariant under every such frame change, including zeros and poles of fixed order. Changing the ramification root changes B and kappa compatibly and leaves B(s_N) unchanged. The quotient by the geometric character is particularly useful. The character has P_geo = exp(S_geo/h) = exp(S_geo s^(-e)), omega_geo = -e S_geo s^(-e-1) ds. (3.1) If L tensor P_geo^(-1) admits a logarithmic connection at s=0 in a meromorphic frame, then its entire B is zero. For a nonzero selected horizontal section the theorem therefore gives (2*pi/N) log|P(s_N)| = Vol(S^3 minus K) + O(log N/N). (3.2) A logarithmic quotient is a clean sufficient condition, stronger than necessary. A quotient whose polar primitive has degree below e still has zero limiting rate, with the finite fractional-power error given by (2.4). This weakens the earlier amplitude requirement that the whole comparison coefficient itself belong to a fixed finite algebraic extension. For example exp(1/s) with e=2 is not algebraic and grows as exp(O(sqrt N)) on a suitable ray, but it does not affect the volume limit. ## 4. Why this is a substantive quantum theorem to prove The hypothesis concerns the WHOLE selected period, not only the nonzero rank-one Gaussian germ at a geometric critical point. The source and co-source must put the actual finite Kashaev values in the proposed line, with the original finite endpoint and polar data. A local block, or the existence of an unpointed abstract line, does not imply that statement. More precisely, the application requires ONE common horizontal section v(s) and a FIXED nonzero meromorphic cut lambda(s), with the original scalar equal to lambda(s_N)v(s_N). The theorem is applied to that scalar in its induced meromorphic frame. A nonzero anchor fixes its integration constant. Arbitrarily varying level rows, or an essential exponential hidden in lambda, are not covered. Also the differential equation supplied by a quantum A-operator is in the meridian direction. A factor exp(C/h), independent of the meridian, preserves that operator equation and changes the h connection by -C dh/h^2. It changes the normalized rate by 2 Im C. The already specified Kashaev source does not admit this arbitrary renormalization; the example shows why the full period connection and its action anchor contain data beyond the A-operator alone. All of (1.1)--(3.2) uses the fixed complete peripheral slice. With a moving meridian one must first pull back the FULL connection along the actual marked peripheral path. One must also retain S_geo(M(s))/h, not replace its differential by the fixed-meridian partial derivative. Even the flat extra term d((M-M_0)/h^2) restricts to zero on M=M_0 but becomes d(1/h) along M=M_0+h, changing a leading character. If S_geo(M(h))-S_geo(M_0)=O(h), the action replacement changes the norm by O(1); a finite-Puiseux motion may give larger, still sublinear, corrections that (2.4) must retain. Marked root phases also remain part of the comparison. For example q^(N^2)=exp(-pi^2/h) on h=pi*i/N. Its polar character is nonzero but pure phase on that ray, and hence has zero norm contribution. It satisfies the weaker real-character test (2.5); it need not give a logarithmic quotient before that recorded phase is absorbed. It is also not legitimate to define omega=dlog P for any interpolated function and declare the hypothesis automatic. For example, if A!=B and C_1 C_2!=0, the entire punctured function P(h) = C_1 exp(A/h) + C_2 exp(B/h) has infinitely many zeros accumulating at h=0: h_k = (A-B)/(Log(-C_2/C_1)+2*pi*i*k), omitting a possible zero denominator. Its logarithmic derivative therefore has infinitely many poles accumulating at zero and is not a meromorphic germ at zero. A finite cover does not remove this obstruction. Two local rank-one characters are not a single whole meromorphic selected line. One may instead need a higher-rank period object and its actual source projection. Nor does finite type of an algebraic torsor imply a logarithmic quotient. The previously proved whole unit example Q_N=exp(2*pi*i/N), u(Q)=1+i(Q-1), C_N=u(Q_N)^(N^2) has u(1)=1 but (1/N)log|C_N| -> -2*pi. In the present coordinate its one whole logarithm is F(h) = -pi^2 h^(-2) Log(1+i(exp(2h)-1)). Its polar primitive is -2*i*pi^2/h. Thus its connection really has an additional leading irregular character, and (2.4) detects the rate change -4*pi^2 in the normalization 2*pi/N. It is not a counterexample to the theorem. This example is not claimed to preserve the actual knot source. ## 5. The revised cyclotomic rigidity target The proposed route can now be phrased without computing an infinite list of quantum Taylor coefficients: 1. Use the normalized geometric A-curve, its algebraic optimizer, and its marked regulator connection as the whole geometric object. 2. Construct the whole period object selected by the actual quantum source and cut; carry its endpoints, peripheral units and pole lattice. Determine whether its selected geometric contribution descends to a rank-one line of the type above. 3. Prove equality of the leading polar character with (3.1), and prove the selected pairing is nonzero. A logarithmic quotient would give the stronger error estimate (3.2). 4. Use exact cyclotomic restrictions to certify identities of the whole algebraic transport and source maps. The existing reconstruction theorem applies once their fixed presentation is supplied. It does not by itself assert existence of this period connection or preservation of its marked polar character. This is a different sufficient target from proving all amplitude coefficients algebraic and then estimating them. It has a weaker amplitude requirement conditional on the stronger structural input of a whole selected rank-one line. It does not establish that the actual knot object satisfies the target. If only a local geometric summand is obtained, its global coefficient and the other summands must still be controlled; formula (3.2) cannot be applied to the entire selected invariant in that situation. [Symbolic audit](../experiments/audit_whole_selected_line_polar_character.py) checks the polar integration, ramification and frame laws, lower-rate characters, the amplified-unit example, and the accumulating zeros. The [independent proof audit, Section 6](doubled_phase_and_critical_source_independent_audit.md#6-the-whole-selected-line-polar-criterion) checks the constants, physical-ray criterion and whole-period scope.

title: A controlled one-variable lemniscate for the whole original source
text: # A controlled one-variable lemniscate for the whole original source 28 October 2026. The full original knot scalar, with ALL clocks and outer phases retained, has a one-variable coefficient presentation whose selected lemniscate has polynomial logarithmic mass. This bypasses the unproved arbitrary-anchor interior-flow mass estimate for this particular whole-source presentation. It does not prove a sharp geometric bound for the selected lemniscate level. Taking the largest modulus of all critical values is unnecessary and can be substantially worse. No coefficient below is defined by the unknown value K_N. The input is the whole original meridian cut polynomial computed from the finite R, followed by explicit monic polynomial operations. It may be expensive, but is a specified source construction rather than a favorable replacement invariant. ## 1. Exact full-source Hadamard master Fix a zero-framed one-component knot diagram, or a fixed braid presenting it. Use its original reduced reciprocal meridian polynomial F_N(Y), at Q=exp(2pi i/N), with F_N(1)=K_N, F_N(Q^j)=C_j(q_N), C_1=1. The actual finite-cut and Weyl theorems give F_N in C[Y,Y^-1], reciprocal under Y inversion. Put h=Y+Y^-1 and expand by MONIC Newton division, F_N(Y)=sum_(n=0)^D a_(N,n) T_n(Y), T_n(Y)=product_(r=1)^n(h-Q^r-Q^-r). (1) Repeated nodes cause no division here: the T_n are monic polynomials in h. The whole original polynomial is the input; one does not reconstruct a missing coefficient from K_N. All original scalar and framing factors remain those of that input. At the root, T_N=Y^N+Y^-N-2 and T_(n+N)=T_N T_n. Consequently terms n>=N vanish at EVERY root-color point Y=Q^j. With d=N-1 set A_N(z)=sum_(n=0)^d a_(N,n) z^n, w_n=T_n(1)=|(Q;Q)_n|^2, W_N(z)=sum_(n=0)^d w_n z^(d-n), f_N(z)=A_N(z)W_N(z)/z^d. (2) Then the exact original scalar is K_N=CT_z f_N(z)=(2pi i)^(-1)integral f_N(z)dz/z. (3) This retains every coefficient phase; it is not the absolute Newton envelope. The truncation also retains all original root-color values, so their audited Plancherel identity remains applicable. The first Newton node is Q+Q^-1. Thus a_(N,0)=F_N(Q)=1. Also w_0=1 and w_d=N^2. If m=degree A_N, the polynomial P_N=A_N W_N has P_N(0)=N^2, degree P_N=d+m, leading coefficient a_(N,m). (4) If m=0, A_N=1 and (3) is exactly K_N=1. This one-pole case is treated separately; no proper-two-pole assertion is made for the unknot case. Otherwise f_N has genuine poles of orders d and m at zero and infinity. ## 2. Arithmetic size bounds come from the original finite word For a fixed original diagram there are constants C,L such that: * the Laurent degree of F_N is at most C N; * its coefficients, and all their cyclotomic conjugates, have modulus at most exp(C N), after a harmless fixed power of N is absorbed in C; * multiplying every coefficient by N^L makes it integral in the cyclotomic integer ring of the retained root field, of degree at most 4N. Here is a direct justification. Each finite R term has a bounded number of root factorial denominators, each with index below N, times a product of at most N binomials in the meridian. The complement identity F_a F_(d-a)=N times a unit root clears each inverse factorial with ONE factor N, not N factors. Every conjugate root product has modulus at most 2^N; each binomial expansion has coefficient sum at most 2^N. The fixed diagram uses a fixed number of such factors and only a polynomial number of state paths in N. Pivot exponents and the retained zero-framing normalization have meridian degree O(N). The common quadratic Cartan cancels against its prescribed zero-framing factor, leaving the explicit meridian monomial, not an uncontrolled analytic scalar. Thus the asserted degree, denominator and conjugate bounds follow from the finite defining matrices. In the Gaussian-polynomial cut formula the denominators can in fact be cleared integrally; the weaker N^L statement suffices here. Passing from reciprocal Laurent polynomials to h-polynomials uses the integer recurrence Y^r+Y^-r=C_r(h), C_(r+1)=hC_r-C_(r-1). Its coefficient norm is exponential in r. Monic Newton conversion introduces only the complete homogeneous polynomials in the nodes Q^r+Q^-r. In every conjugate their modulus is at most two, and |h_(j-n)(a_1,...,a_(n+1))| <=binom(j,n)2^(j-n). Consequently every coefficient of A_N and P_N still has all conjugates bounded by exp(C' N), with the same fixed N-denominator budget. This includes confluent nodes. No small Vandermonde divisor occurs. If a_(N,m)!=0, apply the field norm to the nonzero integral element N^L a_(N,m). Its norm is a nonzero integer. Bounding all other conjugates above gives |a_(N,m)|>=exp(-C'' N^2). (5) Constants depend on the fixed original diagram, not its invariant value. ## 3. The source selects a pole-separating level, not every critical value For m>=1 view f=f_N as a rational function on the sphere. For any R>0, every connected component of {|f|>R}, with poles included, contains a pole. Otherwise its closure avoids both poles and is compact; the maximum principle for f would contradict |f|>R inside and |f|=R on its boundary. There are therefore at most TWO such components. For sufficiently large R they are disjoint neighborhoods of zero and infinity. For sufficiently small R the superlevel is the sphere with small disjoint zero neighborhoods removed, so the two poles are in the same component. Define R_sep to be their merger threshold: R_sep=inf{R>0: the superlevel components of 0 and infinity are distinct}. (6) Separation persists as R increases. Thus for every regular level R>R_sep the zero component is bounded in the plane. It has a unique OUTER boundary circle Gamma_R lying in |f|=R and winding once around zero. Any additional boundary circles surround holes without zero and have winding zero. Their periods of f dz/z vanish individually. Hence Gamma_R ALONE, with multiplicity one and the original positive orientation, represents (3). There is no integer boundary-matrix inversion or accumulated cell multiplicity in this construction. Connectivity can change only at a nonzero critical level, since between regular levels the compact level annulus admits the ordinary gradient trivialization. Thus R_sep is the modulus of a regular critical value of f. It can be smaller than the largest critical modulus; inaccessible criticals are not included merely because they are algebraic roots of f'. The definition (6) is a marked algebraic connectivity condition independent of K_N. It is equivalent to the least level supporting a pole-separating closed curve, but (6) specifies it using the actual two pole components. ## 4. The selected circle has polynomial logarithmic length Let Dp=degree P_N<=2N-2. Every radial ray meets the real algebraic curve |P_N(z)|^2-R^2|z|^(2d)=0 at most 2Dp times. Every fixed-radius circle also meets it at most 2Dp times: the highest angular harmonic has the nonzero product of the leading coefficient of P_N and its constant N^2, so it cannot vanish identically on such a circle. One-dimensional coarea gives integral_(Gamma_R)|dz/z| <=4pi Dp+2Dp log(r_max/r_min). (7) The radii have a uniform quantitative bound. The critical equation is zP_N'-dP_N=0; its leading coefficient is m a_(N,m) and its constant is -dN^2. The coefficient bounds and (5), followed by the elementary Cauchy polynomial root bound and its reversed-polynomial version, put all its roots between exp(-C N^2) and exp(C N^2). It follows that the largest regular critical modulus is at most exp(C N^3). For |w|=R, every point of the level is a root of P_N(z)-w z^d. Because m>=1, its leading coefficient remains a_(N,m), and its constant remains N^2, independent of w. For R_sep<R<=R_sep+1, the same root bounds therefore give |log|z||<=C N^3. (8) This estimate is uniform as R decreases to R_sep; no inverse critical value separation or inverse R-R_sep is used. Equations (7)--(8) prove (2pi)^(-1)integral_(Gamma_R)|dz/z|<=C N^4. (9) The circles are explicit components of degree-O(N) algebraic curves, with coefficient one. Thus this is controlled ORIGINAL-source transport, not merely a conditional estimate for a prospective chain. ## 5. Whole-source estimate and its exact remaining scope Define R_src=R_sep when m>=1 and R_src=1 in the one-pole case m=0. Integrate (3) on Gamma_R, use (9), and take regular R down to R_sep. There is a constant C depending only on the fixed original diagram with |K_N|<=C N^4 R_src. (10) The audited ordinary-color theorem and exact root-color Plancherel identity then give a corresponding positive whole-energy bound E_N=|K_N|^2+poly(N) <=poly(N) max(1,R_src^2). (11) ALL clocks, original Newton coefficients and outer phases are inside f_N; none were separately estimated before this contour was constructed. This does not establish an upper bound by knot volume. The critical points of a product of finite generating polynomials need not be genuine stationary points of a single classical WKB branch: branch cancellation or anti-Stokes interfaces can create extra critical values. The largest critical envelope already overshoots in simple prototypes. Even the selected R_src is not proved to have the hyperbolic-volume rate for general knots. The required remaining theorem must estimate THIS marked level with its exact source, or refine its cycle further; it cannot simply identify every finite polynomial critical point with a knot representation. As a check, for the figure-eight the actual A_N=1+z+...+z^d and every coefficient of W_N is positive. Thus R_src<=max_(|z|=1)|f_N(z)| =f_N(1)=N K_N. Together with (10), the selected level has the same known exponential rate as K_N in this prototype. This does not extend the positivity argument to the complex five-crossing coefficients. [Audit](../experiments/audit_whole_source_hadamard_lemniscate.py): exact original Laurent cuts, monic confluent Newton conversion, all-color truncation, Hadamard source equality and known one-pole treatment. Numerical connectivity diagnostics are kept separate from the proof and are not used to assert a geometric barrier or a new volume theorem.

title: Whole-source Newton transport and the finite-root normal lattice
text: # Whole-source Newton transport and the finite-root normal lattice This note proves a boundary quantum-torus calculation, retaining the whole meridian variable and its normal directions. It does **not** yet assert that an arbitrary marked crossing or bridge recoupling has been realized by these operators. In particular, it does not prove the remaining triple-to-cyclotomic transform in [the \(5_2\) source reduction](five_two_whole_source_reduction.md). No literature proof is used. Comparisons with torus skeins or rank-one Askey--Wilson algebras supply background terminology only. The [independent lattice/cut audit](source_lattice_independent_audit.md) gives a second ring proof and checks the physical derivative convention. ## 1. A source basis and three banded operators Initially let \(Q\) be an indeterminate and work in \(k[Y,Y^{-1}]\), where \(k=\mathbb Q(Q)\). Set \[ X=Y+Y^{-1},\qquad t_n(Y)=\prod_{r=1}^n(X-Q^r-Q^{-r}),\qquad v_n(Y)=(1-Y)t_n(Y). \] The lower-case \(t_n\) is a Newton polynomial. The upper-case \(T\) denotes the shift \[ (Tf)(Y)=f(QY),\qquad TY=QYT. \] The following product fixes every factor and power: \[ v_n(Y)=-Y^{n+1}(Q^{-n}/Y;Q)_{2n+1}. \tag{1.1} \] Define \[ S=T+QT^{-1},\qquad Z=YT+QY^{-1}T^{-1}, \] and \[ a_n=Q^n+Q^{-n},\quad \gamma_n=Q^{n+1}+Q^{-n},\quad \delta_n=Q^{-2n}(1-Q^{2n})(1-Q^{2n+1}). \] With \(v_{-1}=0\), the exact Laurent-polynomial identities are \[ \boxed{Xv_n=v_{n+1}+a_{n+1}v_n,} \tag{1.2} \] \[ \boxed{Sv_n=\gamma_n v_n+\delta_n v_{n-1},} \tag{1.3} \] \[ \boxed{Zv_n=Q^{n+1}v_{n+1} +(1+Q)Q^{2n+1}v_n+Q^n\delta_n v_{n-1}.} \tag{1.4} \] These hold over \(\mathbb Z[Q,Q^{-1}]\). They therefore specialize at every nonzero \(Q\), including \(Q=-1\), without a \(1-Q^2\) denominator. ### Proof The first identity is the defining Newton recurrence. Let \[ (Jf)(Y)=-Yf(Y^{-1}). \] Then \(J^2=1\), \(Jv_n=v_n\), and \[ JTJ=QT^{-1},\qquad JYJ=Y^{-1}. \] Thus \(S,Z\) preserve the \(J\)-fixed Laurent polynomials. These are exactly \((1-Y)k[X]\): evaluation at \(Y=1\) gives divisibility by \(1-Y\), and after division the quotient is invariant under \(Y\leftrightarrow Y^{-1}\). For generic \(Q\), (1.1) shows that \(Sv_n\) is divisible by \(v_{n-1}\). The quotient is invariant under inversion and has Laurent degree at most one, so it is affine in \(X\). Comparing the top coefficient \(v_n=-Y^{n+1}+\cdots\) gives the coefficient \(\gamma_n\) of \(v_n\). Evaluation at \(Y=Q^n\) then gives \[ \delta_n =\frac{v_n(Q^{n+1})}{v_{n-1}(Q^n)} =Q^{2n+1}(1-Q^{-2n})(1-Q^{-2n-1}) =Q^{-2n}(1-Q^{2n})(1-Q^{2n+1}). \] For \(n=0\), (1.3) is directly \(S(1-Y)=(1+Q)(1-Y)\). This proves (1.3) generically and hence as an integral Laurent identity. Finally, \[ (1-Q^2)Z=XS-QSX. \tag{1.5} \] Substituting (1.2)--(1.3) and cancelling this polynomial factor before specialization gives (1.4). It does not divide by \(1-Q^2\) after setting \(Q=-1\). ## 2. The exact finite-root corner Let \(Q\) now be a primitive \(N\)-th root, \(N\ge2\), in a characteristic-zero field \(k\). Introduce \[ A=k[U,U^{-1}],\qquad B=A[Y]/(Y^N-U)=k[Y,Y^{-1}]. \tag{2.1} \] The last equality specifies the \(A\)-algebra structure \(U=Y^N\). The power basis is \(1,Y,\ldots,Y^{N-1}\). The shift \(T\) is \(A\)-linear and \(T^N=1\). Put \[ W=U+U^{-1}-2=\frac{(U-1)^2}{U}. \] There is the exact product identity \[ t_N=W,\qquad t_{n+N}=Wt_n,\qquad v_{n+N}=Wv_n. \tag{2.2} \] Indeed \[ Y^Nt_N(Y)=\prod_{r=1}^N(Y-Q^r)(Y-Q^{-r}) =(Y^N-1)^2, \] and the factors repeat with period \(N\). Define \[ L=\bigoplus_{n=0}^{N-1}A v_n\subset B. \tag{2.3} \] Independence is proved in section 3. Equations (1.2)--(1.4), with \(v_N=Wv_0\), give banded \(N\times N\) matrices on this whole-source lattice. In column convention, the columns \(0\le n<N-1\) are exactly (1.2)--(1.4), while the last columns are \[ Xv_{N-1}=Wv_0+2v_{N-1}, \tag{2.4} \] \[ Sv_{N-1}=\gamma_{N-1}v_{N-1} +\delta_{N-1}v_{N-2}, \tag{2.5} \] \[ Zv_{N-1}=Wv_0+(1+Q)Q^{-1}v_{N-1} +Q^{-1}\delta_{N-1}v_{N-2}. \tag{2.6} \] At \(n=0\), the lower term is zero since \(\delta_0=0\). For \(N=2\), contributions in the same row are added. The corner \(Wv_0\) is retained. It vanishes to order two at \(U=1\), rather than being identically zero; deleting it changes second and higher normal jets. ## 3. The normal lattice and its saturation The involution \(J\) acts on \(B=k[Y,Y^{-1}]\), but is **semilinear** over \(A\): \[ J(a(U)f)=a(U^{-1})Jf. \tag{3.1} \] It becomes \(A\)-linear modulo \(U^2-1\). There is the exact characterization \[ \boxed{L=\{f\in B:Jf-f\in(U^2-1)B\}.} \tag{3.2} \] In particular, \[ \boxed{(U^2-1)B\subset L\subset B.} \tag{3.3} \] Since the Newton polynomials are monic, this \(A\)-span is independent of the choice of primitive \(Q\): \[ L=(1-Y)\operatorname{span}_A\{1,X,\ldots,X^{N-1}\}. \tag{3.4} \] ### Proof of (3.2)--(3.3) Every \(J\)-fixed Laurent polynomial is \((1-Y)\) times a polynomial in \(X\). Expand in the monic Newton basis and fold using (2.2); it belongs to \(L\). The inclusion from left to right in (3.2) follows from (3.1) and \(a(U^{-1})-a(U)\in(U^2-1)A\). For any \(h\in B\), use its \(k\)-linear \(J\)-eigenspace decomposition \(h=h_++h_-\). We have \(h_+\in L\), and \[ J\big((U-U^{-1})h_-\big)=(U-U^{-1})h_-. \] Thus \((U-U^{-1})h_-\in L\); multiplication by the unit \(U\) shows \((U^2-1)h_-\in L\). This proves (3.3). If \(Jf-f\in(U^2-1)B\), then \(f_-=(f-Jf)/2\in(U^2-1)B\subset L\), and \(f_+\in L\). This proves (3.2). ### Independence and determinant Over an algebraic closure of \(k(U)\), write \(y_j=Q^j y\), \(y^N=U\), and \(x_j=y_j+y_j^{-1}\). The \(x_j\) are distinct away from \(U^2=1\): equality for distinct \(i,j\) would force \(y_i y_j=1\), hence \(U^2=1\). Also \(1-y_j\ne0\) away from \(U=1\). The monic Newton evaluation matrix multiplied by \(\operatorname{diag}(1-y_j)\) is therefore invertible generically. This proves independence over \(A\) and spanning over \(k(U)\). Let \(M_N\) be the coefficient matrix of \(v_0,\ldots,v_{N-1}\) in \(1,Y,\ldots,Y^{N-1}\), with increasing columns. Then \[ \begin{aligned} \det M_N &=\prod_j(1-y_j)\prod_{i<j}\frac{x_j-x_i}{y_j-y_i}\\ &=(1-U)\prod_{i<j}(1-(y_i y_j)^{-1})\\ &=\boxed{\begin{cases} (1-U)(1-U^{-2})^{(N-1)/2},&N\text{ odd},\\ -U(1-U^{-2})^{N/2},&N\text{ even}. \end{cases}} \tag{3.5} \end{aligned} \] For odd \(N\), each residue \(i+j\pmod N\) occurs \((N-1)/2\) times among unordered distinct pairs. For \(N=2m\), even residues occur \(m-1\) times and odd residues \(m\) times. Their products are \(1-U^{-1}\) and \(1+U^{-1}\), respectively, giving the displayed even sign. The Smith factors over the PID \(A\), up to units, are \[ \begin{array}{c|c} N=2m&1\ (m\text{ times}),\quad U^2-1\ (m\text{ times}),\\ N=2m+1&1\ (m\text{ times}),\quad U-1,\quad U^2-1\ (m\text{ times}). \end{array} \tag{3.6} \] To see the multiplicities, reduce (3.2) at \(U=\pm1\), where \(J\) is an ordinary involution. Evaluation on reciprocal pairs of roots gives \[ \dim\operatorname{im}(L\longrightarrow B/(U-1)B) =\begin{cases}(N-1)/2,&N\text{ odd},\\N/2,&N\text{ even}.\end{cases} \tag{3.7} \] At \(Y=1\), a fixed function must vanish; at \(Y=-1\), there is no condition. At \(U=-1\), the rank is \((N+1)/2\) for odd \(N\), and \(N/2\) for even \(N\). Inclusion (3.3), or these ranks together with (3.5), shows that all nontrivial local Smith exponents are one. Crucially, \(L/(U-1)L\) has dimension \(N\), whereas its image in \(B/(U-1)B\) has only the dimension in (3.7). The lost directions are retained by first normal jets of the embedding \(L\subset B\). For another description, let \(C_n(Y+Y^{-1})=Y^n+Y^{-n}\). On the abstract fiber \(L/(U-1)L\), both the characteristic and minimal polynomials of the \(X\) matrix equal \(C_N(x)-2\). Indeed \(v_0\) is a cyclic vector by the Newton recurrence. The repeated roots give size-two Jordan blocks. On \(B/(U-1)B\), multiplication by \(X\) is diagonalizable by evaluation at the distinct \(N\)-th roots. The two fibers must not be identified. ## 4. Cleared recovery of the clock and shift Define integer polynomials by \[ C_0(x)=2,\quad C_1(x)=x,\quad C_{n+1}(x)=xC_n(x)-C_{n-1}(x), \] \[ P_{-1}(x)=0,\quad P_0(x)=1,\quad P_{n+1}(x)=xP_n(x)-P_{n-1}(x). \] Thus \(P_j(x)=\mathcal U_j(x/2)\), and \[ P_{N-1}(X)(Y-Y^{-1})=U-U^{-1},\qquad P_{N-1}(X)Y^{-1}=P_{N-2}(X)+U^{-1}. \tag{4.1} \] Write \(D=U-U^{-1}\). On the original regular power lattice \(B\), the following are exact cleared operator identities: \[ \boxed{DY=C_{N+1}(X)-U^{-1}X,} \tag{4.2} \] \[ \boxed{DY^{-1}=C_{N-1}(X)-U^{-1}X,} \tag{4.3} \] \[ \boxed{DT=P_{N-1}(X)Z -(P_{N-2}(X)+U^{-1})S,} \tag{4.4} \] \[ \boxed{QD T^{-1}=(P_{N-2}(X)+U)S-P_{N-1}(X)Z.} \tag{4.5} \] For (4.2), expand \(C_{N+1}(X)=UY+U^{-1}Y^{-1}\); (4.3) is analogous. For (4.4), use \(Z-Y^{-1}S=(Y-Y^{-1})T\) and (4.1). Subtracting (4.4) from \(DS\) gives (4.5). Operator order is as displayed; the polynomials in \(X\) multiply on the left. Thus \(X,S,Z\) recover the full quantum-torus action over \(k(U)\), and recover its cleared equations over \(A\). Dividing by \(D\) and then substituting \(U=1\) is not a recovery rule. Use the regular action on \(B\), or retain the compatible lattice and normal jets, before specialization. There is a uniform denominator bound. For any \(A\)-linear endomorphism \(R\) of \(B\), \[ DR(L)\subset L, \tag{4.6} \] since \(R(L)\subset B\) and \(DB=(U^2-1)B\) up to a unit. Its matrix in the \(v_n\) basis therefore has at most a simple pole at each of \(U=1,-1\), independently of its clock/shift word length. Higher poles appearing in products of (4.2)--(4.5) cancel. This applies to an operator already proved regular and \(A\)-linear on \(B\); it supplies neither hypothesis for an uncomputed crossing. For reference, clock and shift generate all \(A\)-linear endomorphisms of \(B\). The projectors \[ E_j=\frac1N\sum_{\ell=0}^{N-1}Q^{-j\ell}T^\ell \] project onto \(AY^j\), and \(Y^{i-j}E_j\) are matrix units. ## 5. Reciprocal sources and the marked cut If an actual marked source calculation gives a reciprocal Laurent polynomial \(F(Y)=F(Y^{-1})\), then \[ f(Y)=(1-Y)F(Y)\in L. \tag{5.1} \] This follows from whole reciprocity, rather than ordinary-color interpolation. For a finite Newton expansion \(F=\sum_n c_n t_n\), every tail folds exactly: \[ f=\sum_{r=0}^{N-1} \left(\sum_{a\ge0}c_{r+aN}W^a\right)v_r. \tag{5.2} \] Terms with index \(r+aN\) start at normal order \(2a\) at \(U=1\); vanishing at the point does not discard them as whole functions. Define the marked cut on \(L\subset k[Y,Y^{-1}]\) by \[ \operatorname{cut}(f)=-\left.\frac{df}{dY}\right|_{Y=1}. \tag{5.3} \] This derivative follows \(U=Y^N\). It is **not** the derivative at fixed \(U\) of a chosen power-basis representative. Every \(f\in L\) vanishes at \(Y=1\), so \[ \operatorname{cut}((U-1)f)=0,\qquad \operatorname{cut}(v_n)=t_n(1) =\prod_{r=1}^n(2-Q^r-Q^{-r}). \tag{5.4} \] Thus cut factors through the full abstract fiber \(L/(U-1)L\). If \(f=\sum_{n<N}b_n(U)v_n\), then \[ \boxed{F(1)=\operatorname{cut}(f) =\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}b_n(1) \prod_{r=1}^n(2-Q^r-Q^{-r}).} \tag{5.5} \] Cut need not factor through the image in \(B/(U-1)B\). For \(N=3\), \(Q+Q^{-1}=-1\), and \[ v_1=(1-Y)(Y+Y^{-1}+1)=\frac{1-U}{Y}. \] Its image in \(B/(U-1)B\) is zero, but its cut is \(3\). This is an exact example of the normal data required by the selected period. More generally, \(v_{\lfloor N/2\rfloor}\) has zero image in that power fiber: the factors \(t_{\lfloor N/2\rfloor}\) cover every nontrivial reciprocal pair of roots, and \(1-Y\) kills \(Y=1\). Its cut is nonzero, and is positive at the principal complex root. Thus this phenomenon already occurs among exactly \(J\)-fixed whole sources at every level. Equations (5.1)--(5.5) do not determine uncomputed Newton coefficients. For the actual figure-eight source proved in [the figure-eight source identity](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md), the coefficients are \(b_n=1\). For the actual \(5_2\) triple sum, the proposed coefficient transform remains unproved. ## 6. A whole annihilator can be put in the banded algebra This section is conditional on an actual source annihilator, not on a conjectured recurrence or its geometric interpretation. Let \(\mathcal Q=k\langle Y^{\pm1},T^{\pm1}\rangle/(TY-QYT)\). Conjugation by \(J\) induces the involution \[ \theta(Y)=Y^{-1},\qquad\theta(T)=QT^{-1}. \] Its fixed algebra is exactly the algebra generated by \(X,S,Z\). Here is an elementary proof. Its fixed vector space is spanned by \(1\) and the orbit sums \[ E_{a,b}=Y^aT^b+Q^bY^{-a}T^{-b}. \] They obey \[ XE_{a,b}=E_{a+1,b}+E_{a-1,b},\qquad E_{a,b}S=E_{a,b+1}+QE_{a,b-1}, \] \[ E_{1,-1}=Q^{-1}(XS-Z),\qquad E_{-a,b}=Q^bE_{a,-b}. \] Starting from \(E_{0,0}=2\), \(E_{1,0}=X\), \(E_{0,1}=S\), \(E_{1,1}=Z\), these recurrences generate every orbit sum. The proof works before or after root specialization in characteristic zero. At \(Q=1\), the commuting symbols obey \(x^2+s^2+z^2-xsz-4=0\), as direct substitution of \(x=Y+Y^{-1}\), \(s=T+T^{-1}\), \(z=YT+Y^{-1}T^{-1}\) shows. This identifies the classical fixed algebra with the Weyl quotient of the boundary torus; it does not choose a longitude convention for \(T\). Suppose \(F\) is reciprocal and an actual nonzero quantum-torus operator \(P\) annihilates it. For \(f=(1-Y)F\), conjugate to \((1-Y)P(1-Y)^{-1}\) in the rational-coefficient shift algebra and clear its finitely many \(Y\)-denominators by left multiplication. This gives a nonzero Laurent operator \(R\in\mathcal Q\) with \(Rf=0\). Since \(Jf=f\), also \(\theta(R)f=0\). If \(R+\theta(R)\ne0\), this is a nonzero invariant annihilator. Otherwise \(R\) is anti-invariant and \[ (Y-Y^{-1})R \] is a nonzero invariant annihilator. Nonzeroness uses the fact that the abstract quantum torus is a domain, also at roots of unity; no quotient by \(T^N-1\) is taken in this domain assertion. By the fixed-algebra result, the resulting annihilator is a noncommutative polynomial in \(X,S,Z\). It therefore acts by a finite-band expression in the whole source basis, with the exact corner in section 2. This proves an operator-existence statement whenever the actual annihilator and reciprocity have been established. It does not select a particular operator, prove that its classical symbol is the geometric \(A\)-component, or prove a regulator/volume statement. For the actual reduced knot family these hypotheses have already been established in the repository: [actual Weyl descent, section 1](actual_weyl_descent.md) proves reciprocity at every level for every knot, and [squared-meridian descent, section 2](even_meridian_norm_descent.md), using [the finite-sum proof](finite_sum_annihilator.md), supplies a nonzero all-level annihilator over \(\mathbb Q(Q,Y)\). Clearing its finitely many denominators gives the Laurent input used here. The argument applies levelwise to \(f_N=(1-Y)F_N\) with this same operator and therefore gives a nonzero all-level annihilator in the algebra generated by \(X,S,Z\). This corollary has no hyperbolicity, alternatingness, or bridge-number restriction. It remains an existence statement, without a selected geometric symbol or a volume estimate. ## 7. Reproducible checks [The audit script](../experiments/audit_whole_source_newton_transport.py) independently checks the integral Laurent identities, exact finite-root matrix intertwining, determinants and fiber ranks, and cleared clock/shift recovery. The saved JSON reports checks; proofs are supplied above. The completed audit passes 78 generic integral Laurent identities, 148 orbit-sum identities, and 108 exact finite-root checks at \(N=2,\ldots,10\), including the un-specialized \(U\) corners. The subsequent [actual Newton transform](newton_actual_source_canonical_transform.md) constructs generic coefficients and their recurrence from actual fixed colors, proves quantum birationality, and retains the selected whole parameter-germ period. The [source/monodromy chain map](source_lattice_monodromy_chainmap.md) also transports its scalar source and physical normal cut. The [geometric resolution](newton_resolution_and_regulator_cut.md) proves transversality of the marked geometric branch to the resolved complete cut curve, retaining both peripheral normal scales.

title: Whole torsor units, level weights, and the finite jet depth for a norm
text: # Whole torsor units, level weights, and the finite jet depth for a norm Independent function-level theorem, 27 October 2026. There is a sharp distinction between a fixed algebraic comparison section and a horizontal period on a fixed finite-type algebraic connection. A classically normalized algebraic unit can change a leading regulator rate when the level character amplifies its first unseen jet. Conversely a finite jet depth suffices once that character weight is bounded. These are statements about whole functions, not independently chosen levelwise tails. They complement [exact cyclotomic Mellin uniqueness](mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness.md). No modification below is asserted to preserve the actual knot source. ## 1. A sharp unit/weight theorem Let \(t_N=1/N\). Suppose holomorphic units \(u_j(t)\) on one common marked neighborhood satisfy, uniformly in their index, \[ u_j(t)=1+O(t^k),\qquad k\ge1. \] The number of factors may depend on \(N\). For integer characters \(m_{N,j}\) assume the total weight bound \[ \sum_j |m_{N,j}|\le C N^d . \] Then the whole scalar comparison \[ a_N=\prod_j u_j(t_N)^{m_{N,j}} \] satisfies \[ |\log|a_N||\le C' N^{d-k},\qquad \frac1N\log|a_N|=O(N^{d-k-1}). \tag{1} \] Thus it has subexponential norm whenever \(k\ge d\). Proof: choose the logarithm with \(\log u_j(0)=0\). Uniformity and the convergent logarithm imply \(|\log u_j(t)|\le C''|t|^k\) on a smaller common neighborhood. Sum these bounds with the absolute character weights. Both positive and negative exponents are covered. In particular (1) bounds the comparison and its inverse, so multiplying a nonzero selected scalar by it preserves every existing leading exponential rate. It does not estimate an internal sum with cancelling coefficients. The threshold is sharp for \(d\ge2\). If one unit has \(\log u(t)=\alpha t^{d-1}+O(t^d)\) and \(m_N/N^d\to\kappa\), then \[ \frac1N\log|u(t_N)^{m_N}| \longrightarrow\kappa\,\operatorname{Re}\alpha . \tag{2} \] For a quadratic character weight \(O(N^2)\), agreement through the first physical-arc Taylor coefficient, \(u=1+O(t^2)\), therefore suffices. Classical agreement \(u(0)=1\) alone does not. The uniform remainder and total weight are substantive hypotheses. They cannot be inferred from separate algebraicity at each level or from a common classical value. ## 2. A single algebraic unit can change the leading rate Put \(c=2\pi i\), \(Q_N=e^{c/N}\), and take the whole rational unit \[ u(Q)=1+i(Q-1)\in\mathbb Q(i)(Q),\qquad u(1)=1. \] For all sufficiently large \(N\), it is nonzero and \[ \log u(e^{ct})=-2\pi t+O(t^2). \] Consequently \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N \log|u(Q_N)^{N^2}|=-2\pi . \tag{3} \] Its inverse has the opposite rate. The coefficient \(i\) is a fixed algebraic constant, as permitted on a marked geometric coefficient field. All root values in (3) are algebraic numbers. There is also a rational-coefficient example: \(u(Q)=(1+Q)/2\). Since \[ u(Q_N)=e^{\pi i/N}\cos(\pi/N), \] one has \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N \log|u(Q_N)^{N^3}|=-\pi^2/2 . \tag{4} \] The first complex logarithmic term in this example is a phase; its first real term is quadratic. More generally, for every fixed \(J\ge0\), take \[ u(Q)=1+i^{-(J+1)}(Q-1)^{J+1}. \] It agrees with one through all ordinary Q-jets of order \(J\) at \(Q=1\). Nevertheless \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N \log|u(Q_N)^{N^{J+2}}|=(2\pi)^{J+1}. \tag{5} \] Thus a finite jet budget controls a norm only after the level character weight is controlled. This is a single whole algebraic unit, rather than a separately assigned \(a^Nz^N\) tail. ## 3. Finite type of a connection is not bounded algebraic section complexity The preceding amplified functions occur on a fixed finite-type algebraic connection. Work over the punctured \(t\)-base and the open where \(u(Q)\ne0\). Introduce coordinates \(L,W\), with \(W\ne0\), and the algebraic differential laws \[ dL=\frac{du}{u},\qquad d\log W=t^{-d}\frac{du}{u} -d\,t^{-d-1}L\,dt . \tag{6} \] This is a full flat connection: on its horizontal sections the right side for \(d\log W\) is \(d(t^{-d}L)\). Equivalently the two mixed derivatives commute directly. There is no claim that the naive product translation on \(L,W\) makes (6) a regular principal connection at \(t=0\). On the marked branch \(L=\Log u\), its horizontal period is \[ W=\exp(t^{-d}\Log u). \] Restricting \(t=1/N\) gives exactly \(u(Q)^{N^d}\). The connection has fixed algebraic rank and presentation, while its marked horizontal period is not generally an algebraic function of the base. Its singularity at \(t=0\) retains the large character and cannot be omitted. Therefore a claim of finite-type algebraic torsor or connection does not by itself supply the bounded algebraic comparison SECTION required by the existing reconstruction and norm theorems. Conversely (1) identifies a finite sufficient jet depth when the relevant character degrees are known. This does not refute the flat pointed-comparison lifting lemma: (6) is singular at the classical boundary and does not give a regular pointed comparison there. It also does not preserve the actual finite-level source equation or its pointing. Such source conditions are precisely what can exclude (3)--(5). ## 4. Which jets and which functions The three distinct uniqueness assertions should remain separate: * If two functions are holomorphic at the same ordinary point and all their Taylor coefficients agree, they are the same analytic germ. Marked continuation then fixes them on a connected common continuation domain. * Equality of asymptotic formal power series at an irregular puncture is weaker. Exponentially flat sectorial differences can remain, as proved in [the earlier function audit](global_period_rigidity_function_audit.md). * Varying finite-dimensional root fibers are not one analytic function unless a whole family has been constructed. Here exact source and pole conditions are decisive: [the bounded-jet Mellin theorem](mellin_cyclotomic_jet_uniqueness.md) proves equality of the entire rational root function from orders \(0,\ldots,D(s-1)\), in its specified finite X-window and cyclotomic numerator lattice. The Taylor order in (1) is along the physical arc \(t\mapsto(t,Q=e^{ct})\) at \(t=0\). It must not be confused with a quantum-normal Taylor derivative at a fixed root \(Q=Q_N(1+\epsilon)\), where \(N\) is held fixed. Exact root-normal source identities and bounded whole presentations can relate these data; classical shape etaleness alone cannot. ## 5. Consequence for the optimizer/torsor proposal The algebraic Rivin optimizer fixes the chosen shape branch and its local critical field. A marked Bloch primitive then fixes the geometric action, with its original peripheral signs. The new doubled-phase optimizer also gives an algebraic positive Hessian. These are meaningful whole geometric data. What remains is a source-compatible comparison, not another classical uniqueness argument. One concrete sufficient route is now finite: construct a candidate whole root Mellin function with the ACTUAL cyclotomic numerator lattice and ACTUAL source equation through the fixed quantum order of the bounded-jet theorem. That theorem then identifies it exactly with the selected actual root function, including its residue. To infer its norm from a regulator factor, its remaining comparison units must either belong to the bounded algebraic section class already covered by norm control, or satisfy an explicit level-weight estimate such as (1). Finite-type period connections and classical unit normalization alone are insufficient by (3)--(6). No existence of that comparison, selected geometric coefficient, global dominance, or volume limit is claimed here. The complementary [doubled-phase theorem](doubled_phase_rivin_optimizer.md) constructs the whole classical period connection explicitly, and the [critical-source theorem](irreducible_critical_source_and_whole_norm.md) gives a finite criterion for a genuinely descended source density with polynomial norm bounds. Their proofs are recorded in the [independent audit](doubled_phase_and_critical_source_independent_audit.md).

title: An exact whole-translation and gluing-source test
text: # An exact whole-translation and gluing-source test Research reduction, 27 October 2026. The new whole-clock endpoint maps preserve the functions and carries needed by a comparison. The existing cyclic/Koszul reduction still needs an actual co-source calculation. This note supplies the signed local norm table and the precise orbit/moment pairing to compute next. It proves neither a nonzero global geometric contribution nor a volume bound. ## 1. The exact signed crossing norms Use the ORIGINAL coefficient ratios of [the actual geometric normal period](actual_geometric_normal_period.md), with Q primitive of order N, x=-M/q_N, Y=M^2 and Q x^2=Y. For one local crossing write \[ U=A^N,\quad V=B^N,\quad W=C^N,\quad P=Y^N,\quad X=x^N. \] The norm of a ratio is the product over the N shifts of its OWN variable, fixing the other two. The exact results are \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} &\text{positive crossing}&\text{negative crossing}\\ \hline A&\displaystyle\frac{VW}{X}\frac{1-P/U}{1-PW/U} &\displaystyle\frac{X}{V}\frac{1-UW}{1-U}\\[4pt] B&\displaystyle\frac{U}{WX}\frac{1-VW}{1-V} &\displaystyle\frac{X}{U}\frac{1-P/V}{1-PW/V}\\[4pt] C&\displaystyle-\frac{U}{VWX} \frac{(1-VW)(1-PW/U)}{1-W} &\displaystyle\frac1X\frac{(1-UW)(1-PW/V)}{1-W}. \end{array} \tag{1} \] This is an identity of rational functions on their common open chart. It is proved by the elementary identity prod_(j=0)^(N-1)(1-Q^j z)=1-z^N. The positive C ratio has an additional Gaussian product. Its exact phase is (-1)^N Q^(-N(N+1)/2)=-1, which gives the displayed minus sign for EVERY N, including even N. No unspecified phase remains. The full periphery is retained: \[ X=(-1)^{N+1}M^N,\qquad X^2=P. \tag{2} \] The table uses Frobenius-power variables U,V,W,P. They must not be silently identified with fixed semiclassical shape coordinates or with the original M. The exact moving-central-character issue in [the rational period torsor](rational_quantum_dilogarithm_torsor.md) still applies. Closure combines these local transport factors along the already specified integral free-flow lattice, with its original pivot and zero-framing factors. It does not replace them by one. They are nonconstant rational gluing characters off the gluing equations. A finite dominant cover cannot turn such a character H into a root of unity: pullback is injective on function fields, so H^r=1 after pullback would imply H^r=1 beforehand. Finite phases can kill the Gaussian signs; they do not kill the rational norm transport in (1). On the gluing quotient H=1 is instead an actual equation, whose regularity is a different assertion. There is also an essential whole-quantum distinction. If T_i=r_i(q,mathbf A) sigma_(Q,i), its EXACT N-step operator is \[ T_i^N=H_{i,N}(q,\mathbf A)\,\sigma_{Z,i}, \qquad Z=Q^N. \tag{3} \] Only at Z=1 does sigma_Z become the identity and the coefficient specialize to (1). The new [flat endpoint tower](whole_clock_function_algebra_and_endpoint_extension.md) retains that displacement; it does not license dropping it before all actual normal coefficients and endpoint rows are transported. ## 2. What the source-sensitive cyclic reduction actually asks For one unit scalar orbit let T e_j=r_j e_(j+1), with the last edge returning to e_0, and put \[ s_0=1,\quad s_j=\prod_{u=0}^{j-1}r_u,\quad H=\prod_{u=0}^{N-1}r_u . \] The basis v_j=s_j e_j gives the standard companion transport T v_j=v_(j+1), T v_(N-1)=H v_0. It is unimodular precisely on the chart where the r_j are units. Direct telescoping gives \[ (1-T)\omega=(1-H)e_0,\qquad \omega=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}s_j e_j. \tag{4} \] At H=1 the invariant line has generator omega. For the ORIGINAL transported co-source Lambda its exact coefficient is \[ a_N=\Lambda(\omega) =\sum_j s_j\Lambda(e_j). \tag{5} \] For d commuting translations on the finite root cover, the same calculation gives the joint generator \[ \omega=\prod_{i=1}^d(1+T_i+\cdots+T_i^{N-1})e_{\rm mark}. \tag{6} \] Its coefficients are the specified cocycle products, including all finite phases. Original sum versus average factors N^d stay as given by the actual source; (6) is the UNNORMALIZED orbit. The source-sensitive test is to compute Lambda_rel(omega) on the marked Rivin/gluing branch, with Lambda_rel the actual whole relative co-source. In a relative complex this means pairing its bulk, endpoint and carry components, not just an ordinary row chosen after discarding boundaries. The derivative rows must also be compared. For an ordinary row lambda the literal defect is \[ b_j=\lambda_j-r_j\lambda_{j+1},\qquad \sum_j s_j b_j=(1-H)\lambda_0, \tag{7} \] with the cyclic convention at the last edge. These b_j are the actual co-source boundary data to transport through the reduction. The regular-sequence theorem in [the rational period pushforward](rational_period_pushforward.md) eliminates higher constraint homology. It does not prove that (5) is a unit or that the source in (7) is the desired geometric one. For example unit weights r_0=-1,r_1=u-1 have H=1-u, a unique etale gluing point u=0, and flat free orbit module. The normalized pointing lambda=(1,1)/2, psi=(1,1) still has lambda psi=1 but lambda omega=0 there. Transporting BOTH source and dual under a rephasing preserves this zero. This two-state diagnostic is not a knot counterexample; it rules out the proposed inference from flatness and regular sequence alone. ## 3.
