Exact moment and carry data required for the actual test For the ACTUAL uncollapsed word introduce its existing independent couplings w_i for each free flow and retain \[ \omega(\mathbf w;p)=\sum_{\mathbf k\in[0,N-1]^d} \mathbf w^{\mathbf k}r_{\mathbf k}(p) e_{\mathbf k}. \tag{8} \] The precise algebraic/relative moments to calculate are \[ a_{N,\alpha}(p)= \left[\prod_i(N^{-1}w_i\partial_{w_i})^{\alpha_i} \Lambda_{\rm act,rel}(\omega(\mathbf w;p)) \right]_{\mathbf w=1}. \tag{9} \] The actual source maps are independent of these transfer couplings, so the derivatives in (9) insert the literal normalized free-flow moments. Raw Green moments retain their corresponding N powers. This is the whole generating-family identity of [the strict word transport](relative_word_green_transport.md), not an ordinary-color interpolation or a WKB definition of the moments. Equation (8) denotes the TRANSPORTED actual coupons. In a splitting using head indices and Frobenius blocks, their exponent is the original full index/difference, with its marked offset and memory carry; it must not be replaced by the residual deck index alone. The identification of those coefficients with an open cyclic geometric chart is part of the test, not an asserted source equality. To compare (8)--(9) with the actual source, retain at least: - All original head projectors, phases, pivot, source pairing units and the full external peripheral/modified-dimension line. - The shifted value g(ZC) in every whole Jackson current and the added top spectral endpoint in its flat function tower. - The literal endpoint P(J+N), rather than P(J), for every marked logarithmic moment; polynomial degree h makes this finite but does not make the endpoint zero. - The actual memory carry w^((N+1)Delta R), with its recorded crossing sign. At w=exp(z/N) its limit is a nontrivial e^(z Delta R). - The explicit off-diagonal head-current correction to Jackson, and every charged head neighbor at the requested quantum-normal depth. Scalar character differentiation does not replace them. These conditions are the specific next calculation. The positive Rivin point supplies a reduced algebraic evaluation place for the coefficients and the transverse regular sequence. It does not supply the actual transported Lambda_rel or its value on (6). Proving that actual value is the specified nonzero geometric relative period would advance the full theorem. A local norm table or a nonzero result alone would still not establish uniform cross-level growth or global dominance. [The exact local-norm audit](../experiments/audit_actual_signed_crossing_norms.py) checks all six ORIGINAL ratios, including even-level Gaussian signs and full peripheral powers. No asymptotic formula is used.

title: A whole two-period transport lattice preserves the actual finite coefficients
text: # A whole two-period transport lattice preserves the actual finite coefficients Research construction, 27 October 2026. The standard two-nome product already constructed in the repository defines a flat rank-one DIFFERENCE object over four independent coordinates. Its finite first-period transports are exactly the Pochhammer factors in the ORIGINAL crossing matrices. Consequently every actual finite word and its original source have a realization in this whole transport algebra before quantum jets are taken. This statement concerns transport ratios, not replacement of the selected knot state by a value or integral of the completed function. The singular transport lattice, its central norm and the full peripheral factor are retained. No meromorphic differential connection at H=0 or selected volume asymptotic is asserted. ## 1. The algebraic difference object precedes any analytic restriction Work over a characteristic-zero constant field k_0 and put K=k_0(Q,Qtilde,z,w), with FOUR independent coordinates. The commuting base automorphisms are sigma(z)=Qz, sigma(w)=w, tau(z)=z, tau(w)=Qtilde^(-1)w, and both fix the two nomes. On the free line L=K e define sigma_L(e)=(1-z)e, tau_L(e)=(1-w)e. (1.1) They commute: sigma(1-w)=1-w and tau(1-z)=1-z. This is the flat two-period difference presentation. It is a fixed finite-type rational/birational presentation, not an assertion that its period section is an algebraic function of the base. The integral lattice matters. Over R=k_0[Q^+-1,Qtilde^+-1,z,w], retain R e. This also retains the z=w=0 source mark and nilpotent jets; its torus localization is available when needed. The positive maps in (1.1) are injective semilinear maps over this domain; their coefficients may vanish on a divisor. Their inverses are rational maps with the specified poles. One may invert all translated factors to obtain a genuine Z^2 difference torsor, but that localization is NOT the original lattice at a zero of one of those factors. At such a point keep the line, its actual vanishing transport maps and their normal/source data. One analytic marked period, on Re H<0, is the existing product Q=exp H, Qtilde=exp(4pi^2/H), z=exp x, w=exp(2pi i x/H), Psi(H,x)=(Qtilde*w;Qtilde)_infinity/(z;Q)_infinity. (1.2) Both nomes have modulus less than one. Product cancellation gives Psi(x+H)=(1-z)Psi(x), Psi(x+2pi i)=(1-w)Psi(x). (1.3) The extra Qtilde in the numerator is essential for the second equation. In the [two-nome atom note](unfolded_atom_cyclotomic_divisors_and_two_nome_source.md) our w is its y, and its numerator argument is Qtilde*y. That note supplies and marks (1.2) by exact products. Nothing here derives a unique completion from the first Ward equation. ## 2. Every finite transport is the original finite product Define t_n(z) by sigma_L^n(e)=t_n(z)e, first over K. Direct iteration gives for EVERY integer n t_n(z)=product_(j=0)^(n-1)(1-Q^j z), n>=0, t_(-n)(z)=1/product_(j=1)^n(1-Q^(-j)z), n>0. (2.1) They satisfy the exact cocycle identity t_(m+n)(z)=t_m(z)t_n(Q^m z). (2.2) For any nonzero marked period of (1.1), in a domain where its values are defined meromorphically, Psi(H,x+nH)/Psi(H,x)=t_n(exp x). (2.3) The right side gives the rational continuation of the RATIO, even when neither individual period has a root value. A sigma- periodic completion factor cancels in (2.3) exactly. In particular (z;Q)_n=t_n(z), (Q;Q)_n=t_n(Q), {a choose k}_Q=t_a(Q)/[t_k(Q)t_(a-k)(Q)]. (2.4) These are identities of whole finite products before evaluation. The physical q with Q=q^2 and the original half-Cartan root characters are retained on their specified covers when actual coefficients are pulled back; the new notation does not erase them. For instance the actual balanced positive crossing is, with its original unwrapped support and full Cartan line retained, r_+=(-1)^k x_1^(-b-2k)x_2^(-a+k) Q^(ab+(a-b)k-k(k+1)/2) {b+k choose k}_Q t_k(Qx_1^2 Q^(-a)), and the negative one is r_-=x_1^b x_2^(a-k)Q^(-ab) {a+k choose k}_Q t_k(Qx_2^2 Q^(-b)). (2.5) Their derivation, original Cartan factors and exact cups/caps are in [the actual crossing calculation](figure_eight_whole_source_identity.md), Section 2. Here (2.4) realizes every factor in (2.5) by the universal period transport. It does not omit their common scalar. ## 3. Universal finite-word preservation, with the actual lattice Take the ORIGINAL finite coefficient array at fixed level, with all actual crossing coefficients, cup/cap factors, pivots, framing and meridian lifts, cut row and full modified dimension. Replace each finite Pochhammer by (2.1), and each Gaussian by (2.4), on its specified support. Keep every monomial, phase and original normalization factor unchanged. The resulting transport word equals the original coefficient as a whole rational function in its actual q/M variables and clock characters. Its value is independent of the extra two-period completion: each local first-period ratio already descends from the four-coordinate period object to Q,z. This equality is preserved by finite products, sums, matrix contractions and literal insertion of all actual index moments. It therefore gives EXACTLY the original finite state, including its source and every whole normal derivative. This is a uniform finite-word identity for arbitrary braids/cups/plats; it does not assume a triangulation move or a new state integral identity. At a singular factor evaluate the CANCELLED WHOLE coefficient in the original lattice. Do not evaluate the numerator and denominator period separately. The ordinary actual root support has factorial denominators of length below N, hence those factors are nonzero there. A vanishing norm or a supplied source ratio may require the original relative/normal lattice instead. For example the actual finite Ward gauge is f_N(z)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) z^j/t_j(Q_N). Its EXACT affine source is f_N(Q_N z)-(1-z)f_N(z)=z^N/N. (3.1) Indeed adjacent coefficients cancel and t_(N-1)(Q_N)=N. The nonzero source must not be replaced by a homogeneous cyclic equation. Nor does the transport equality mean that f_N itself is the scalar function Psi_N; the latter has additional central period/source data, explicitly computed in the atom note. The new conclusion compared with [rational-state folding](rational_period_pushforward.md) is this actual finite-word preservation and singular-lattice statement. The two-nome definitions and their rational-point factorization are already part of the repository and established literature. ## 4. Commensurate periods keep the cyclic norm as central transport At the marked physical H_N=2pi i/N the analytic power restriction is Q=Q_N, Qtilde=1, w=z^N. (4.1) The two periods obey NH_N=2pi i. On the base sigma^N and tau are both identity after (4.1), but their LINE maps are sigma_L^N(e)=t_N(z)e=(1-z^N)e=tau_L(e). (4.2) The equality t_N=1-z^N uses primitiveness, with no primality or odd-level assumption. It is NOT sigma_L^N=I. The nontrivial central tau transport is exactly the finite cyclic source norm. Off the divisor 1-z^N=0, the commensurability loop sigma_L^N tau_L^(-1) is trivial, as it must be. If nu^N=1-z^N with the original mark nu=1 at z=0, the normalized small-step transport (1-z)/nu has cyclic norm one. This is the finite Kummer/Hilbert-90 part. It is obtained only after adjoining nu and inverting its zero divisor. At z^N=1, the original transport in (4.2) is noninvertible, while the normalized map requires division by zero. The original line lattice and its vanishing/normal source must remain; the norm-one gauge is not a regular replacement there. ## 5. The original peripheral norm and its whole quantum adapter The full original peripheral factor is d_N(M)=epsilon_N (M-M^(-1))/(M^N-M^(-N)) =epsilon_N M^(N-1)(1-M^2)/(1-M^(2N)). (5.1) Keep epsilon_N and any specified whole phase lift exactly. At the root, (4.2) identifies its denominator with t_N(M^2). Thus its central norm is a transport factor of the same object, including all factors such as 1+M^n on their actual marked substitutions. No such factor is replaced by its numerical complete-point value. There is a necessary WHOLE qualification. The actual fixed-N power coordinate W=M^(2N) is independent before restriction. Under the actual half-meridian step M->qM it obeys W -> Q^N W, whereas the independent dual-nome coordinate w in (1.1) is fixed by sigma. The two markings agree at (4.1); they are not an off-root equivariant identification. The actual source and its q/M power-graph derivatives must therefore be retained. In particular the alternative first-period norm lift d_N^tr(Q,M)=epsilon_N M^(N-1)t_1(M^2)/t_N(M^2) agrees with (5.1) at Q_N but is generally DIFFERENT as a whole q-germ. Their exact ratio is C_N(Q,M)=d_N^tr/d_N=(1-M^(2N))/(M^2;Q)_N. (5.2) The whole regular continuation near M=1 is obtained by canceling their common 1-M^2 factor before evaluation. At a generic regular M and Q=Q_N, D_Q log C_N=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) j M^2 Q_N^j/(1-M^2 Q_N^j). (5.3) For N=2 this is already visible: d_2=epsilon_2 M/(1+M^2), d_2^tr=epsilon_2 M/(1-QM^2). Their values agree at Q=-1, but (5.3) at M=1 is -1/2. The phase lift cancels from this comparison if it is the SAME actual lift on both sides. Thus replacing the original peripheral denominator by a cyclic Pochhammer before differentiating loses an actual normal source term. More generally the cancelled whole function at M=1 is C_N=N/product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-Q^j). Since Re[Q_N^j/(1-Q_N^j)]=-1/2 for 1<=j<N, its actual physical-root normal satisfies Re[D_Q log C_N]_(Q_N,M=1)=-N(N-1)/4. (5.4) Thus an adapter whose root value is exactly one can still have quadratically growing quantum-normal data. This does not change its root value; it explains why that value cannot replace its whole marked source in a quantum-jet comparison. One may record (5.1) in the universal TWO-period base as the formal transport ratio epsilon_N M^(N-1)(1-z)/(1-w), with z=M^2 and w=W. This records its whole rational source factor; it does not identify its fixed-N power-graph dynamics with the analytic modular restriction away from the root. Alternatively keep (5.1) separately, which is what finite-word preservation in Section 3 does. Either way, no original factor has been changed. ## 6. Fixed-n exceptional slopes are compatible, but not a global blowup The atom note proves independently, for n FIXED, Q=zeta_n exp(eps) in a closed negative-real eps sector and U=exp(t n eps), F(Q,zU)/F(Q,z) -> (1-z^n)^t, (6.1) with its logarithm marked from z=0, uniformly on |z|<=r<1 and compact t sets. The resonant terms m=kn in the exact logarithm give -t z^(kn)/k; nonresonant terms vanish. Exponential bounds and a slightly larger r<1 give the stated uniform remainder. For t=a/b the EXACT telescope uses shifted arguments, product_(j=0)^(b-1) R(Q,zU^j,U)=F(Q,zU^b)/F(Q,z). On U^b=Q^(an) its root value is (1-z^n)^a, and the marked individual exceptional period has nu^b=(1-z^n)^a. It is NOT the assertion R^b equals that finite product away from the exceptional restriction. Nor is (6.1) a regular holomorphic extension across an entire complex blowup neighborhood, where other cyclotomic divisors still accumulate. No n-growing limit is interchanged with this fixed-n statement. This local exceptional/source result, the whole difference presentation and the actual finite transport identities fit one period object. They do not prove that its analytic completion preserves the selected global knot contraction. The latter still requires its original period/cycle, all internal projectors and the source/co-source comparison, rather than only equal nilpotent jets or equal cyclic norms. Exact transport/source audits: [script](../experiments/audit_whole_two_period_transport.py) and [results](../experiments/whole_two_period_transport_results.json). The argument and the cancelled peripheral-normal adapter have a separate [independent proof audit](whole_two_period_transport_independent_audit.md).

title: Independent audit of actual finite transport and the peripheral normal adapter
text: # Independent audit of actual finite transport and the peripheral normal adapter Proof audit, 27 October 2026, of [the whole two-period transport construction](whole_two_period_transport_and_actual_coefficients.md). Its algebraic identities, singular-lattice treatment and actual-source scope pass. This audit does not identify the analytic two-nome period with a selected whole knot period. ## 1. The free lattice and its actual first-period ratios On the four-coordinate Laurent domain, the maps sigma(e)=(1-z)e and tau(e)=(1-w)e commute: their base automorphisms commute and each fixes the other's multiplier. Both positive maps are injective before specialization. Their rational inverses have the specified translated-factor poles. Thus the genuine invertible difference torsor is a localization, whereas the original free line with its vanishing maps is retained at norm zero. Iteration gives t_n(z)=(z;Q)_n for n>=0, and the stated reciprocal product for negative n. Directly splitting the product proves t_(m+n)(z)=t_m(z)t_n(Q^m z) for all integers. These ratios depend only on Q,z; every sigma-periodic completion cancels from them. The Gaussian ratio of three factorial transports is its original rational Gaussian polynomial, with cancellation performed before singular evaluation. Consequently the finite-word substitution changes no matrix entry: the original monomial, Cartan and framing characters, support, cup/cap, pivot, modified dimension, source and moment insertions remain exactly where they were. Products, finite sums and normal derivatives preserve the identity. This verifies an exact rational transport realization, rather than an identity of completed analytic state contractions. At a primitive N-th root, the polynomial identity product_(j=0)^(N-1)(1-Q_N^j z)=1-z^N proves sigma^N(e)=tau(e)=(1-z^N)e on the marked commensurate base. The line map is not the identity. A Kummer norm-one gauge divides by nu with nu^N=1-z^N, and so cannot replace the original lattice on its zero divisor. The actual affine finite Ward source z^N/N is also retained. No primality or odd-N assumption is used here. ## 2. The whole peripheral source requires its adapter Set t=M^2 and keep the SAME original phase lift on both dimension factors. The exact quotient is C_N(Q,M)=d_N^tr/d_N=(1-t^N)/(t;Q)_N. At a generic regular M it equals one at Q=Q_N. Near M=1 its regular continuation is obtained BEFORE evaluation: C_N=(1+t+...+t^(N-1))/product_(j=1)^(N-1)(1-tQ^j). The denominator is N at (Q_N,t=1), so the ratio is a regular unit there with value one. Holding M fixed and using D_Q=Q partial_Q gives D_Q log C_N=sum_(j=1)^(N-1) j t Q^j/(1-tQ^j). The sign is positive because this differentiates the reciprocal product. At N=2, Q=-1, M=1 it is -1/2. Therefore the two dimension lifts agree at the root but have different quantum-normal jets. The phase cancels only because its actual whole lift was kept the same on both sides. Other norm-zero points may involve moving zero/pole intersections; the local regularity statement above is specifically near M=1. The note correctly retains the original rational lattice instead of asserting a global unit adapter across every such point. Finally, the actual fixed-N power W=M^(2N) satisfies W->Q^N W under M->qM, while sigma fixes the independent dual coordinate w. Their root values agree, but their whole normal dynamics do not. Keeping the original d_N unchanged, as the construction does, avoids imposing a false off-root equivariant identification. The separate fixed-n exceptional-slope theorem is consistent with this calculation: its rational-slope statement is a telescope over shifted arguments, not an off-root equality R^b=(z;Q)_(aN).

title: Polynomially conditioned signed Green transport with the original source
text: # Polynomially conditioned signed Green transport with the original source 28 October 2026. The physical crossing Green equation has a useful whole-word consequence: its complete clock-family transport and inverse have polynomial norms for every fixed signed diagram and every bridge count. The original contraction is transported as a functional, rather than replaced by a positive contraction or a geometric quotient. This is an ambient source-transport theorem. It does NOT give a lower bound for the restriction of that functional to geometric data. In fact the complete ground data already contain the original positive crossing entries by an isometric reindexing. That fact sharply limits what can be deduced from the norm theorem alone. ## 1. The actual signed clock families Fix N>=2, Q=exp(2*pi*i/N), q=exp(pi*i/N), x=-q^(-1), and F_a=(Q;Q)_a. Use the SAME balanced finite heads V=C^N as in the [literal crossing source](actual_trivalent_layer_crossing_source.md). Keep the original unit-modulus Cartan scalar kappa external. Give End(V tensor V) its flat Hilbert--Schmidt norm, and put E_N = direct_sum_(m in Z/N) End(V tensor V), ||X||^2 = sum_m ||X_m||_HS^2. The [physical Green theorem](actual_rogers_sink_opposite_beta_source.md#8-the-actual-shared-head-source-combines-the-currents-into-a-ground-channel) constructs ACTUAL internal-clock insertions K_m^+, and their full retained ground sources H_m^+, with K_m^+ - A_+ K_(m+1)^+ = H_m^+, (A_+ X)_(c,d;a,b) = x^(-1) X_(c,d-1;a-1,b). (1) An out-of-range index on the right means zero. In particular A_+ retains both physical barriers. It is a partial coordinate shift times a unit scalar, so ||A_+||<=1 and A_+^N=0. The [signed transport proof](signed_green_antiunitary_transport.md) shows that at this COMPLETE color the balanced negative crossing is obtained by flip and complex conjugation: R_- = P overline(R_+) P. (2) This includes kappa, since its conjugate is its inverse. For clarity, the proof starts from the original unbalanced crossing conjugation relation with its Cartan diagonal D. The balanced basis change has g_j/overline(g_j)=(-1)^j q^(j(j+1)). Its residual diagonal on a pair (a,b) is q^((a+b)(a+b+2)), depending ONLY on total integer degree. It therefore commutes with both the crossing and the flip, and cancels from the conjugation relation. No exponentially sized factorial gauge is used as an isometry. Consequently K_m^-=P overline(K_m^+)P and H_m^-=P overline(H_m^+)P are actual negative-crossing clock families, and their equation is (1) with (A_- X)_(c,d;a,b) = x X_(c-1,d;a,b-1). (3) The label m names the conjugated original insertion; it does not reassign its physical clock orientation. Again ||A_-||<=1 and A_-^N=0 in the SAME flat metric. These assertions concern the complete color; a fixed nonunit color cannot be included by silently treating |x| as one. ## 2. A bounded inverse on the entire clock space Define T_s on E_N by (T_s X)_m=A_s X_(m+1), s=+,-. The clock shift is a cyclic isometry and commutes with A_s. Hence T_s^N=0, ||T_s||<=1, G_s=(1-T_s)^(-1)=sum_(j=0)^(N-1) T_s^j, ||G_s||<=N, ||G_s^(-1)||<=2. (4) Thus the full actual family satisfies K^s=G_s H^s. This is an isomorphism on ALL of E_N, not only on vectors meeting a guessed geometric support condition. It preserves the currents already combined into the explicit H_m; none is set to zero. Nilpotence here has index N. What makes (4) useful is the contraction bound on EACH power, not nilpotence by itself. A nilpotent matrix with exponentially large entries would not give (4). For a fixed word with r signed crossings put E_W = tensor_(v=1)^r E_N, G_W = tensor_(v=1)^r G_(s_v), k_W = tensor_v K^(s_v), h_W = tensor_v H^(s_v). The tensor Hilbert norm gives the general, all-bridge theorem k_W=G_W h_W, ||G_W||<=N^r, ||G_W^(-1)||<=2^r. (5) In particular this change of the COMPLETE data has zero exponential conditioning cost as N tends to infinity for any fixed word. Neither the word nor its bridge count is allowed to grow with N in this claim. ## 3. Carry the specified original co-source Let L_W be the EXACT original linear tensor contraction: evaluate each external clock label at zero, connect the original head indices in their original order, and apply the specified cups, caps, pivotal weights and external normalization line. In a braid presentation the same statement uses its original selected cut and pivotal closure. No new trace or averaging is substituted for that selected functional. The original scalar is therefore K_N(W)=L_W(k_W)=(L_W composed with G_W)(h_W). (6) Define L_W^G=L_W composed with G_W. Equations (4)--(5) imply, for the dual norm on the FULL ambient tensor space, 2^(-r)||L_W|| <= ||L_W^G|| <= N^r||L_W||. (7) The lower inequality follows from L_W=L_W^G composed with G_W^(-1), so it requires no positivity assertion. The fixed original complete source has polynomial coefficients and polynomially many tensor entries: balanced pivotal entries have unit modulus, and the original cup/marked-cap normalizations are fixed powers of N times unit color phases. Thus its norm is polynomially bounded for a fixed diagram. The exact external factors are retained in L_W on BOTH sides of (7). For any vector h and nonzero L_W, the elementary Hilbert-space identity dist(v,ker L)=|L(v)|/||L|| now gives 2^(-r) dist(h,ker L_W^G) <= dist(G_W h,ker L_W) <= N^r dist(h,ker L_W^G). (8) This quantifies preservation of the actual cancellation problem. It does not replace distance by ||h||. A tensor can be large and belong to the exact kernel. Nor does (7) give a lower bound for L_W^G RESTRICTED to a geometric submodule or to the actual ground-support subspace; that restriction can vanish. ## 4. The complete ground data have an exact visible-support metric The positive sources are, for alpha+beta<N, H_m^+|alpha,beta> = Q^(m beta) x^(-beta) {alpha+beta choose alpha}_Q (Q^(m+1);Q)_alpha |alpha+beta,0>. (9) Choose 0<=m<N. The coefficient vanishes if alpha+m>=N, because the displayed Pochhammer then contains 1-Q^N. Every remaining entry maps, under the mth Green term, to the original crossing entry with input (alpha+m,beta), output (alpha+beta,m), and changes only by the unit scalar x^(-m). Distinct entries in (9) give distinct crossing entries, and every nonzero original crossing entry is obtained this way. Therefore, exactly, sum_m ||H_m^+||_HS^2 = ||R_+/kappa||_HS^2. (10) Flip-conjugation gives the identical negative statement. In particular (sum_m ||K_m^s||_HS^2)^(1/2) <= N ||R_s||_HS. (11) Here |kappa|=1. Equation (11) controls ALL these internal clock responses despite the factorial frames in their definition. For a fixed signed word, (5) and (10) give the analogous tensor bound ||k_W|| <= N^r product_v ||R_(s_v)||_HS. This does not bound the clock-inserted SCALAR by the uninserted knot scalar: contraction can cancel, and (8) is the exact distinction. The endpoint channel is not of lower exponential order. Already H_0 has the norm computed in the local source note, ||H_0||^2=max_(t<N)|F_t|^2 sum_(b=0)^t |F_b|^(-2), with a strictly positive exponential rate. The ground presentation therefore transports the original bulk difficulty; it does not prove that all nonground or current contributions are negligible. ## 5. What remains on the critical path We now have an exact polynomially conditioned signed transport with the ORIGINAL functional, without dropping peripheral or endpoint/current terms. This answers a specified transport-norm question for this presentation. It does not identify a geometric quotient, prove that L_W^G is nonzero on the marked Bloch-regulator sector, or bound the total remainder by a smaller exponential. Those are still necessary for the requested volume limit. In particular (5) is not completion of the general source-coefficient gate: that gate concerns a geometric projection, whereas (5) concerns the complete ambient data. The [audit](../experiments/audit_whole_word_ground_green_transport.py) and [results](../experiments/whole_word_ground_green_transport_results.json) verify signed finite transport, nilpotence, the visible-support isometry, and the unchanged original contraction on a nonfactorable ambient test as well as actual crossing tensors. The all-N statements follow from the index and operator proofs above. ## 6. A global bound with several actual gluing-source insertions The [complete crossing normal source](actual_crossing_shared_face_fourier_source.md) is a different operator from the unweighted H_m in (9). At complete color it obeys the sharp flat bound ||L||=N-1 for N>=3 and sqrt(2) for N=2. Flip-conjugation defines the opposite signed insertion in the same metric. Since its rank is at most N^2, its Hilbert--Schmidt norm is O(N^2); every original scalar factor is still attached. The [uniform weighted crossing estimate](weighted_crossing_source_gap.md) proves at zero weights log ||R_+||_HS = log ||R_-||_HS = N v_8/(2*pi)+O(log N), where v_8=4 Catalan is the regular ideal octahedron volume. This constant is an exact local norm rate, not the volume of the knot. For a fixed original word with r crossings, replace any s distinct crossing slots by these actual L operators (or their signed versions), and retain its SAME original source. The polynomial source norm and tensor norm inequality give unconditionally |L_W(tensor with s such insertions)| <= N^C exp[N (r-s)v_8/(2*pi)]. (12) Here C depends on the fixed diagram, not on N. This is valid for every bridge count and every placement of the specified insertions. It does not assert they form a nilpotent ideal: in particular their degree-N carry contains a nonzero idempotent. Consequently these terms are exponentially smaller than a POSITIVE target of rate V/(2*pi) whenever (r-s)v_8<V. This is a precise sufficient condition, not a claim that the current decomposition of the original invariant already has that many insertions. A single local source replacement generally leaves a bound much larger than Vol(K). Equation (12) controls some whole-source terms, but neither bounds the remaining invariant sharply nor proves its geometric lower bound.

title: A sourced primitive gauge for the whole actual word and its meridian boundary
text: # A sourced primitive gauge for the whole actual word and its meridian boundary 27 October 2026. The k=1 source sector can be gauged on the ENTIRE actual word to a fixed, unit Frobenius density. Its resulting Euler orientation is the one with a quadratic classical boundary position. Thus that orientation, which is incorrect for the unsplit original cap, is legitimate for this precisely transported primitive sector. The exact quantum clock equations and meridian adapter retain the adjacent boundary divisors. No equality of the full invariant with one primitive sector is asserted. The source decomposition and all normalizations are those of [the actual all-strand Fourier traces](actual_source_fourier_twisted_traces.md). This note supplies a concrete word/source transgression, rather than identifying a sector with a geometric period without a source map. ## 1. The whole-word identity fixes the density and Euler orientation Use the common right coefficient algebra B=Mat_r(A_0), r=N^(b-2), with A_0=<H,f | H^N=1,Hf=Q^-1 fH,f^N=0>. Its actual Frobenius functional is T=sum tau on diagonal entries, with tau(f^a e_j)=delta_(a,N-1), nu(H)=QH, nu(f)=f, T(ab)=T(b nu(a)). Write z=xf, u=u_N(z), u_Q=u_N(Qz), v=u^-1, v_Q=u_Q^-1, J=[(1-z)(1-Qz)]^-1. Scalar functions of z below mean the same block-diagonal element in B. Let A be the COMPLETED actual word coefficient matrix, including every off-diagonal tail transition. The original Euler source uses b=u^-1 A u. In the primitive k=1 sector its actual density simplifies to C_1=Q^-1 H J I_r, C_1^0=Q^-1 H I_r. The diagonal tail phases really are independent of the tail label in this sector; this follows from -j+(j-1)=-1 in the original marked Fourier resolution. Let g=v v_Q=[u u_Q]^-1. Then the following identities are exact at every original root: nu(g)=g, g^-1 C_1 g=C_1^0, c:=g^-1 b g=u_Q A u_Q^-1, Phi_1(b)=T(C_1 b)=T(C_1^0 c). (1) For the density identity use g(Qz)=J(z)g(z) and Hh(z)=h(Q^-1z)H. For the trace identity, T is invariant under conjugation by a unit fixed by nu: T(g^-1 a g)=T(a). The last equality follows by applying that fact to C_1 b. There is no extra factor of Q from an ordinary cyclic rotation; T is a Nakayama-twisted trace. Equation (1) preserves full word composition: conjugation is applied to the complete matrix A, or to every factor before multiplication. It never discards off-diagonal tail channels. The original scalar period remains chi_W gamma_0/N times the sum of ALL Fourier sectors. The k=1 term in that sum is exactly chi_W gamma_0 T(C_1^0 c)/N. The other sectors have not been proved negligible or identified with this one. For two physical/fused heads with actual fusion C, right multiplication reverses coefficient composition. Consequently the new-to-physical basis for c is C R_(u_Q), (2) and in the common multi-head module it is the corresponding common fusion followed by this same block-diagonal right multiplication. Indeed (C R_(u_Q))^-1 W (C R_(u_Q))=R_c. This is the opposite Euler orientation to C R_(u^-1), the basis of the unsplit cap. The density change in (1) is essential for (2) to represent an ACTUAL source sector. ## 2. The exact primitive-sector clock equations Keep the relative clocks D_a=diag(Q^a), D_j=diag(Q^j), right shift R_f and z=x R_f. Put U_Q=R_(u_Q). Direct nilpotent Euler cancellation gives the ordered finite matrix identities U_Q D_a U_Q^-1=(1-Qz)^-1 D_a, U_Q D_j U_Q^-1=(1-z)D_j, U_Q^-1 D_a U_Q=(1-Qz)D_a=:A', U_Q^-1 D_j U_Q=(1-z)^-1 D_j=:J', A'J'=D_aD_j. (3) The factors 1-z and 1-Qz are units in this nilpotent algebra. Let U_phys=diag(Q^u) on the physical first head and define its primitive-basis version U_prim=(C U_Q)^-1 U_phys(C U_Q). Conjugating the EXACT fusion clock equation yields (1-U_prim^-1 A')z=(1-Q A')(1-J'). (4) This equation includes every wrapped and top-degree endpoint of the original fusion. The apparent denominator 1-U_prim^-1 A' is nilpotent, just as in the original fusion relation. Thus (4) is an exact polynomial transport equation, not an inverse formula in the finite root representation. On the regular commutative principal chart, put delta=1-z and let A,J denote its undressed relative clock values. At Q=1, (3) becomes A'=A delta,J'=J/delta. In the rational fusion chart this gives D_-=J-AJ delta+(A-1)delta^2, U=A z delta^2/D_-, V=J D_-/(z delta^2), delta^-2 U -> A/J, delta^2 V -> J^2. (5) Therefore the quadratic classical boundary exists on the correctly sourced primitive sector, even though it does not arise from the unsplit cap's orientation. Equation (5) alone does not mark U as the internal second meridian of the geometric cut. Here V is the FUSED tail clock, and UV=AJ stays a unit on the stated fixed-A,J chart. A geometric framing can have a nonunit total braid-axis clock, so matching the valuation of one position does not identify the full representation/source map. There is also a necessary order-of-limits qualification. Equation (3) retains 1-Qz. If delta=epsilon*zeta and Q=exp(2pi*i*epsilon), 1-Qz=epsilon*(zeta-2pi*i)+O(epsilon^2). Thus setting Q=1 before that boundary rescaling loses a leading term. Formula (5) is a regular classical chart followed by a classical boundary limit. It is not a uniform quantum boundary profile or a Gamma normalization formula. ## 3. The full primitive meridian gauge increment is controlled At fixed Q use the original meridian x=-M/q and sigma(M)=qM. Keep the same abstract coefficient basis, so sigma(z)=qz. Define D_N(z)=sigma(g)g^-1=g(qz)g(z)^-1. For the actual half-step adapters B_N=u(qz)/u(z), A_N=B_N^-1, the exact factorization is D_N(z)=A_N(z)A_N(Qz), D_N(z)^-1=B_N(z)B_N(Qz). (6) Using [the proved half-step bounds](actual_euler_meridian_half_step.md), in the same flat right-regular metric on |M|=1, ||D_N|| <= 64N, ||D_N^-1|| <= (1+6pi)^2. (7) The gauge g itself has exponential condition number, but its one-step meridian increment has polynomial condition number. Both statements concern a specified coefficient metric, without an unproved transfer through physical fusion. For any actual whole-word family b(M), let c(M)=g(M)^-1 b(M)g(M). The fiberwise meridian equation is EXACTLY sigma(c)=D_N^-1 [g^-1 sigma(b)g]D_N. (8) In particular the sector density C_1^0 is independent of M, but one must retain the two-sided D_N in (8). Omitting it is not permitted by the fact that (1) is an inner change at each fiber. The original chi_W(M), gamma_0(M) and full peripheral ratio still multiply their original fiber values. At a peripheral pole their whole rational-map/source-lattice product must be combined before evaluation; they are not replaced by numerical complete values. The actual longitude insertion of the original finite state remains the one in [the marked longitude theorem](quantum_longitude_and_regulator_action.md). Its internal inserted network need not commute with the Borel action at the original color. Equation (8) does not assert that such a coupon is an element of B. It transports the actual uninserted word families at M and qM, and any supplied two-fiber linear network map can be conjugated on BOTH fibers before its original source pairing. This distinction retains the current terms required by the full geometric comparison. There are actual-word witnesses for the increment in (8). For the positive one-crossing word at generic M=3, using the original balanced color matrices, the correct and omitted-adapter k=1 source values are, respectively, N=3 over F_1009: 439 and 293, N=4 over F_1009: 630 and 956. The known external factors are identical in each comparison and are nonzero on that generic chart. A single sector is not a knot invariant, but altering only this term while retaining the rest of the prescribed Fourier sum changes the original source value. ## 4. Regular action transgression and the marked longitude On the regular multiplication-symbol chart where the actual gauge has the proved action F(z)=2Li_2(z), conjugating a word kernel by g changes its phase by S_new(z_out,z_in)=S_old(z_out,z_in) -F(z_out)+F(z_in). (9) The transported co-source kernel has the OPPOSITE boundary term. For a full kernel/co-source composition these terms cancel before taking critical values. This is a whole-word statement: applying the gauge to successive kernels also telescopes at every internal node. On a common marked logarithmic chart no imaginary constant is introduced by (9), since identical endpoint branches cancel. For the primitive k=1 trace, its bare twisting automorphism Ad_(C_1^0) composed with nu shifts logarithms only by O(h); its principal canonical twist is the identity. This does NOT prove that T(C_1^0 .) has a nonzero regular co-source there: T detects the nilpotent top degree, and a regular geometric realization of that source remains a separate construction. Whenever a source-compatible regular kernel branch is supplied, the cancellation above preserves its critical action and its meridian derivative. If that branch is already identified with the marked geometric critical branch, the longitude derivative and Bloch-regulator action from the marked longitude theorem remain the same after (1). The corresponding one-step scalar symbol is also explicit. The actual normal-form estimate for g gives, uniformly on |z|<=1/4, D_N(z)=(1-z)^-1(1+O(1/N)). (10) To prove this for the CANONICAL polynomial D_N, not an invalid quotient of polynomial evaluations, take its finite logarithm: log D_N=sum_(a=1)^(N-1) (1+q^(2a))z^a/[a(1+q^a)] modulo z^N. On each fixed disk of radius<1 its ordinary polynomial right-hand side tends to -log(1-z), with error O(1/N). For a<=N/2 the coefficient difference from 1/a is O(1/N); the upper half is bounded by 2/(N-a) times a geometric tail. The logarithm is uniformly bounded on |z|<=1/2. Cauchy's Taylor-tail bound for its exponential is therefore O(2^-N) on |z|<=1/4. This proves (10) for the canonical finite polynomial. Its leading action also agrees with 2[Li_2(qz)-Li_2(z)]/h=-log(1-z)+O(h). This is a real boundary/longitude correction for an UNTRANSPORTED word kernel; the co-source supplies its inverse in the complete period. Formula (8) is its finite, ordered counterpart. One cannot discard it and keep only the bulk longitude symbol. This transgression does NOT prove that the actual finite sector selects the regular marked geometric graph, that the other Fourier sectors cancel subexponentially, or that the full boundary profile has been transported. In particular the original highest-input source lies at a fusion wall; a generic regular interior chart does not itself move that source through the wall. Thus the geometric identification and global growth gates remain open. ## 5. Verification [The exact audit](../experiments/audit_whole_word_primitive_source_gauge.py) and [saved results](../experiments/whole_word_primitive_source_gauge_results.json) check the whole-word density equality, the opposite Euler basis, all ordered clocks in (3)-(4), the exact meridian factorization, and generic actual-word omitted-adapter witnesses. They retain the entire actual signed word before extracting source diagonal blocks. The symbolic check verifies (5), the adjacent boundary shift and the retained product of both position clocks. The direct proofs above are all-level; tests check conventions and source scope.

title: Independent first-loop audit for the actual compact coefficient model
text: # Independent first-loop audit for the actual compact coefficient model Proof audit, 27 October 2026. This checks the universal Wick coefficient and the original crossing, color-half-step and pivot contributions used in the figure-eight cap calculation. The coefficient is a transverse FORMAL block in the stated physical slice. Its geometric coordinate eta_geo=p_e^(-1) is independent of the finite band-Fourier variable eta. Transport of the latter's entire marked contour/endpoint is a separate assertion; see [the exact Fourier audit](finite_band_fourier_cap_and_independent_clock.md). ## 1. Wick signs and multiplicities Write the local integral formally as exp(S/H) a_0(1+H a_1+...), put G=(S'')^(-1), and use Gaussian covariance -H G. Repeated indices below are summed. Dividing the first coefficient by its leading amplitude gives z_1=a_1-G_ij a_(0,ij)/(2a_0) +(a_(0,l)/a_0)S_ijk G_ij G_kl/2 +S_ijkl G_ij G_kl/8 -S_ijk S_lmn G_il G_jm G_kn/12 -S_ijk S_lmn G_ij G_lm G_kn/8. (1) The amplitude second derivative contracts one covariance, giving the minus sign. The amplitude-linear/cubic and quartic vertices contract two covariances, giving the positive signs.
